# Preface

## About this book

A pada is a short song sung in kirtana; at its close the poet usually names himself (the signature, *bhanita*). Sri
Chaitanya Mahaprabhu (1486–1533) was surrounded by poets: Vasu, Madhava and Govinda Ghosha sang before Him in Navadvipa
and Puri, and Narahari Sarkar, Murari Gupta, Ramananda Vasu and others made songs about His lilas while He was still
present. These padas are the earliest witnesses to the Lord in Bengali, and in them one hears the living voice of His
companions: the rapture of the Navadvipa kirtanas, the grief of Nadia after the sannyasa, the longing for Nilachala.

The padas lie scattered through later anthologies. We have gathered those which research (above all Bimanbihari
Majumdar, *Sri-Chaitanya-chariter upadan*, ch. 2) assigns to Mahaprabhu's contemporaries, established their text from
several editions and translated them into Russian and English — 754 padas in all. The book has three parts.

- **Part I. Padas of the Contemporaries** (chapters 1–16) — the core of the collection: padas signed by the Lord's
  contemporaries, from the *Padakalpataru*, the *Bhakti-ratnakara*, the *Gaura-pada-tarangini* and other collections;
  first the padas Majumdar dates to the Lord's lifetime, then by poets and themes.
- **Part II. Appendix: Padas Signed "Narahari" from the Gaura-pada-tarangini** (chapters 17–26). Two poets sang
  under this name: Narahari Sarkar of Srikhanda, the Lord's companion, and Narahari Chakravarti (18th c.), author of the
  *Bhakti-ratnakara*. Whose each pada is, is stated in its heading; how we distinguish the two poets is explained in the
  introductory note to chapter 17.
- **Part III. Nagari Padas** (chapters 27–34) — songs in which the women of Nadia speak of Gaura in amorous feeling
  (*nagari-bhava*). They are translated in full and faithfully to their authors, but the Gaudiya Vaishnava tradition —
  Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja, Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati — does not accept the worship of Gaura in this
  mood: Gaura is Krishna Himself in the mood and lustre of Radha, come to taste Her love as a devotee, not to enjoy. This
  is set out in the introductory note to chapter 27, and every sharp passage has a short note. Concluding notes to the
  section stand at the end of chapters 33 and 34.

## Sources

The text of the padas is established from editions in the public domain; where a pada is found in several
collections, the base text follows the oldest or most correct one, and the variants are given in the notes and in the
Russian full edition.

- **PK** — *Padakalpataru* of Gokulananda Sena (Vaishnavadasa), 18th c.; ed. Satishchandra Ray, Bangiya Sahitya
  Parishat, 1915–1931, vols. 1–5 (the pada number is the running number of this edition; a "pallava" is its section).
  Ray records manuscript readings; their sigla are in the list of abbreviations.
- **BR** — *Bhakti-ratnakara* of Narahari Chakravarti (18th c.); eds. 1888, 1912/1913, 1960 (Gaudiya Mission), 2006.
  Its chapters are "waves" (*taranga*).
- **GPT1, GPT2** — *Gaura-pada-tarangini*, compiled by Jagadbandhu Bhadra: 1st ed. 1903, 2nd ed. 1934.
- **PS** — *Padamrita-samudra* of Radhamohana Thakura (18th c.); ed. 1878.
- **KGC** — *Kshanada-gita-chintamani* of Vishvanatha Chakravarti (17th–18th c.); ed. 1925.
- **GCC** — *Gaura-charita-chintamani* of Narahari Chakravarti; ed. Haridasa Dasa, 1947. Its chapters are "kiranas"
  (rays).
- **GCd** — *Gita-chandrodaya* of Narahari Chakravarti; ed. 1948.

For dating and attribution we have consulted Majumdar, but his arguments are given only briefly, in our own words; the
editors' prefaces and notes are not translated.

## Principles of the translation

**Faithfulness to the author.** Each pada is translated as it stands — line for line, without rhyme, keeping the
song's images and tone; nothing is added and nothing softened. Where an author speaks otherwise than the Gaudiya
Vaishnava tradition teaches, the translation stays exact and a note explains how the passage is to be understood. The
measure of interpretation is Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati.

**Theology.** The Lord is not subject to maya (His "maya" is yogamaya, His internal energy); He is not born but
appears; the Deity is the Lord Himself, not an image; the prema of Radha and the gopis and the Lord's bhava are not
worldly passion. Pronouns referring to the Lord are capitalised (Me, My, Mine; "I" is unchanged), also in His own
speech and in speech in the mood of Radha.

**Attribution and authority.** The heading of each pada gives its source, its lila and, where needed, its attribution.
We grade the reliability of the attribution on a scale A–D:

- **A** — a contemporary of the Lord with a reliable signature (confirmed by several witnesses or by Majumdar);
- **B** — a recognised later author of established authorship (above all the padas of Narahari Chakravarti from his
  BR, GCC and GCd: a later poetic elaboration of the lila accepted by the tradition), or a contemporary with a probable
  but not certain attribution;
- **C** — author not established or attribution disputed (the pada is known only from GPT, the signatures differ
  between sources, it is unclear which of the two Naraharis is meant);
- **D** — authenticity doubtful (a forgery, an anachronism, another's couplet bearing the signature).

The heading marks "**probably Sarkar**", "**probably Chakravarti**", "**not established**" concern the padas signed
"Narahari" and say to which of the two poets we incline.

**Numbering.** The padas in each chapter are numbered; a couplet (in a tripadi, a stanza) is marked "pada.couplet":
**1.1**, **1.2**, … **2.1**. The refrain (*dhruva*) is marked "(Refrain)" and counts as a separate unit; the kirtana
singers' insertions in some padas of Lochana Dasa are given in brackets. Notes are numbered within each chapter; a
reference "ch. 22, no. 7" means pada 7 of chapter 22, "n. 36 of chapter 22" — note 36 of that chapter. Labels like
VG-…, NG-…, NS-…, LD-… are the numbers of our working catalogue of padas (from the initials of the poet or section);
they are kept in the notes so that a pada can be found in the project materials.

**Transliteration.** Bengali words are given in IAST, with the inherent vowel written in full; ব is rendered *b*
(but *v* after a consonant: স্ব *sv*, দ্ব *dv*), ঁ is *m̐*, ং is *ṃ*, ড় is *ṛ*, য় is *y*.

## How to read the full version

The book appears in two forms. The **standard** version gives the translation with notes. In the **full** version
each couplet is preceded by:

1. the Bengali original (medieval spelling; Vrajabuli as in the source);
2. a transliteration in IAST;
3. a word-for-word translation;
4. the translation.

The readings of the witnesses are recorded in the notes; their full apparatus appears in the Russian full edition, and
references to variants "in the full version of the book" point to it.

## Abbreviations

- **CC** — *Chaitanya-charitamrita* of Krishnadasa Kaviraja (Adi, Madhya, Antya — its parts; the number is the chapter).
- **CB** — *Chaitanya-bhagavata* of Vrindavana Dasa (Adi, Madhya, Antya).
- **Murari** — *Sri-Krishna-Chaitanya-charitamrita* (*Kadacha*) of Murari Gupta (prakrama.sarga.verse).
- **Lochana** — *Chaitanya-mangala* of Lochana Dasa (Sutra-, Adi-, Madhya-, Antya-khanda; references follow the parts
  of our translation).
- **GGD** — *Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika* of Kavi Karnapura.
- *Bhag.* — *Srimad-Bhagavatam* (canto.chapter.verse).
- **BRS** — *Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu* of Rupa Gosvami.
- **PK, BR, GPT1, GPT2, PS, KGC, GCC, GCd** — see "Sources".
- **PVP** — *Prachina vaishnava padavali*, vol. 1, collected by Chandranatha Bandyopadhyaya, 1922 (a late anthology,
  not an independent witness).
- **M.**, **Majumdar** — Bimanbihari Majumdar, *Sri-Chaitanya-chariter upadan*; **M-1961** — a reference to its pages
  and pada numbers (ed. 1961).
- **ka, kha, gha, cha** (ক, খ, ঘ, চ) — manuscripts of PK in S. Ray's apparatus; **P-R-Sa** (প-র-সা) — the manuscript
  of the Bangiya Sahitya Parishat.
- **VG-, NG-, NS-, LD-** etc. — numbers of the working catalogue of padas.
- **IA** — Internet Archive (identifier of a scan).
- **sect.** — a section of GPT (e.g. sect. 3.2); **no.** — the number of a pada in a GPT section or in PK; **pallava**,
  **wave**, **kirana** — sections of PK, BR, GCC.
- **ch.**, **no.**, **n.** — chapter, pada, note of this book.

# Part I. Padas of the Contemporaries

---

# Chapter 1. Padas Dated to the Lord's Lifetime (after Majumdar)

*Padas by Sri Chaitanya's companions which Bimanbihari Majumdar (*Sri-Chaitanya-chariter upadan*, ch. 2) assigns to the
Lord's lifetime, arranged in the order of events: from Nimai's journey to East Bengal, through the Navadvipa kirtanas of
1509 and the sannyasa, to the first years of separation (the padas of the Puri period follow in the next chapter). The text follows the *Padakalpataru* (PK), the *Bhakti-ratnakara* (BR) and
the *Gaura-pada-tarangini* (GPT); the Bengali original, variants and word-for-word translation are in the full version of the book.*

## 1. Govinda Ghosha — "gorā gelā pūrvadeśa…" (PK 1597)
*Lila: Vishvambhara in East Bengal; in Navadvipa His dear ones pine for Him. According to Majumdar it was composed while
the Lord was away, before Gaya: if so, it is the earliest surviving pada about Gaura. Raga pahida.*[^01-1]

গোরা গেলা পূর্বদেশ নিজগণ পাই ক্লেশ
বিলাপয়ে কত পরকার ।
কান্দে দেবী লক্ষ্মীপ্রিয়া শুনিতে বিদরে হিয়া
দিবসে মানয়ে অন্ধকার ॥

*gorā gelā pūrvadeśa nijagaṇa pāi kleśa*
*bilāpaye kata parakāra |*
*kānde debī lakṣmīpriyā śunite bidare hiyā*
*dibase mānaye andhakāra ||*

*Word for word:* gora gela purvadesha — Gora went to the Eastern land; nijagana pai klesha — His own people, in anguish; bilapaye kata parakara — lament in so many ways; kande devi lakshmipriya — Devi Lakshmipriya weeps; shunite bidare hiya — to hear it the heart breaks; dibase manaye andhakara — by day she sees darkness

**1.1.** Gora has gone to the Eastern land, and His own people, in anguish,
lament in so many ways.
Devi Lakshmipriya weeps — to hear it the heart breaks;
broad day is darkness to her.[^01-2]

হরি হরি গৌরাঙ্গ-বিচ্ছেদ নাহি সহে ।
পুন সেই গোরা-মুখ দেখিয়া ঘুচিবে দুখ
এখন পরাণ যদি রহে ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*hari hari gaurāṅga-biccheda nāhi sahe |*
*puna sei gorā-mukha dekhiyā ghucibe dukha*
*ekhana parāṇa yadi rahe || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* hari hari — Hari, Hari! (a cry of grief); gauranga-bichchheda — separation from Gauranga; nahi sahe — cannot be borne; puna sei gora-mukha — once more that face of Gora; dekhiya — seeing; ghuchibe dukha — the sorrow will go; ekhana parana — life now; yadi rahe — if it lasts

**1.2.** *(Refrain)* Hari, Hari! Separation from Gauranga cannot be borne!
Once more we shall see Gora's face, and the sorrow will go —
if only life holds out till then.

শচীর করুণা শুনি কান্দয়ে অখিল প্রাণী
মালিনী প্রবোধ করে তায় ।
নদীয়া-নাগরীগণ কান্দে তারা অনুক্ষণ
বসন ভূষণ নাহি ভায় ॥

*śacīra karuṇā śuni kāndaye akhila prāṇī*
*mālinī prabodha kare tāya |*
*nadīyā-nāgarīgaṇa kānde tārā anukṣaṇa*
*basana bhūṣaṇa nāhi bhāya ||*

*Word for word:* shachira karuna shuni — hearing Shachi's piteous weeping; kandaye akhila prani — every living being weeps; malini prabodha kare taya — Malini consoles her; nadiya-nagari-gana — the townswomen of Nadia; kande tara anukshana — they weep incessantly; basana bhushana — clothes and ornaments; nahi bhaya — give no pleasure

**1.3.** Hearing Shachi's piteous weeping, every living being weeps;
Malini consoles her.[^01-3]
The townswomen of Nadia weep without cease;
neither clothes nor ornaments please them.

সুরধুনী-তীরে যাইতে দেখিব গৌরাঙ্গ পথে
কত দিনে হবে শুভ দিন ।
চাঁদ-মুখের বাণী শুনি জুড়াবে তাপিত প্রাণী
গোবিন্দ ঘোষের দেহ ক্ষীণ ॥

*suradhunī-tīre yāite dekhiba gaurāṅga pathe*
*kata dine habe śubha dina |*
*cām̐da-mukhera bāṇī śuni juṛābe tāpita prāṇī*
*gobinda ghoṣera deha kṣīṇa ||*

*Word for word:* suradhuni-tire yaite — going to the bank of the Suradhuni (Ganga); dekhiba gauranga pathe — we shall see Gauranga on the way; kata dine habe — after how many days will come; shubha dina — the auspicious day; chanda-mukhera bani shuni — hearing the words of [His] moon-face; jurabe tapita prani — the burning soul will be cooled; gobinda ghoshera deha kshina — Govinda Ghosha's body is wasting away

**1.4.** When, going to the bank of the Suradhuni, shall we see Gauranga on the way —
after how many days will that auspicious day come?
We shall hear the words of His moonlike face, and the burning soul will be cooled…
Govinda Ghosha's body is wasting away.

[^01-1]: Govinda Ghosha was the eldest of the three Ghosha brothers (Govinda, Madhava, Vasudeva), kirtana singers of the
Lord (CC Adi 10, Madhya 13). The journey to East Bengal: CB Adi 14, CC Adi 16, Murari 1.11.5–16, Lochana
(*Chaitanya-mangala*, Adi-khanda, part 12, vv. 61–103). Majumdar's argument: the pada has no hint of Nimai's divinity or of kirtana — the poet
knows Him only as a youth he has seen on the bank of the Ganga; such simplicity is natural only in verses made before the
change at Gaya. In PK the pada stands as a gaura-chandrika (prelude) to the section on "distant separation" (Krishna's
departure for Mathura).
[^01-2]: Lakshmipriya was the Lord's first wife. According to CB (Adi 14) and Murari (1.11.17–20), while the Lord was in East
Bengal she left this world, bitten by the "serpent of separation"; the pada finds her still alive, pining for her husband.
[^01-3]: Malini, the wife of Srivasa Pandita, was a close friend of Shachi.

## 2. Vasu Ghosha — "śaṅkha dundubhi-nāda…" (BR, p. 893; PK 1536)
*Lila: the abhisheka-bathing of the Lord in Srivasa's house (the mahaprakasha), 1509. According to Majumdar, the song of
an eyewitness; raga bhupali (PK), suhai (BR).*[^01-4]

শঙ্খ দুন্দুভি-নাদ বাজয়ে সুস্বরে ।
গোরাচাঁদের অভিষেক করে সহচরে ॥

*śaṅkha dundubhi-nāda bājaye susvare |*
*gorācām̐dera abhiṣeka kare sahacare ||*

*Word for word:* shankha — conchs; dundubhi-nada — the roll of kettledrums; bajaye susvare — sound melodiously; gorachandera — of Gorachand; abhisheka — the ceremonial bathing; kare sahachare — the companions perform

**2.1.** Conchs and the roll of kettledrums sound melodiously:
the companions perform the abhisheka of Gorachand.

গন্ধ চন্দন শিলা ধূপ দীপ জ্বালি ।
নগরের নাগরীগণ আনে অর্ঘ্য-থালি ॥

*gandha candana śilā dhūpa dīpa jvāli |*
*nagarera nāgarīgaṇa āne arghya-thāli ||*

*Word for word:* gandha chandana shila — fragrant sandal, the [grinding] stone; dhupa — incense; dipa jvali — lighting lamps; nagarera nagari-gana — the women of the town; ane — bring; arghya-thali — platters of arghya

**2.2.** Fragrant sandal on the stone, incense, lamps alight;
the women of the town bring platters of arghya.[^01-5]

নদীয়ার লোক যত দেখি আনন্দিত ।
ঘন জয় জয় দিয়া সভে গায় গীত ॥

*nadīyāra loka yata dekhi ānandita |*
*ghana jaya jaya diyā sabhe gāya gīta ||*

*Word for word:* nadiyara loka yata — all the people of Nadia; dekhi anandita — rejoice to see it; ghana jaya jaya diya — crying "Jaya, jaya!" again and again; sabhe gaya gita — all sing songs

**2.3.** All the people of Nadia look on and rejoice;
again and again they cry "Jaya, jaya!" and sing songs.

গোরাচাঁদের মুখ সভে করে নিরীক্ষণে ।
গোরা-অভিষেক-রস বাসু ঘোষ গানে ॥

*gorācām̐dera mukha sabhe kare nirīkṣaṇe |*
*gorā-abhiṣeka-rasa bāsu ghoṣa gāne ||*

*Word for word:* gorachandera mukha — Gorachand's face; sabhe kare nirikshane — all gaze upon; gora-abhisheka-rasa — the sweetness of Gora's bathing; basu ghosha gane — Vasu Ghosha sings

**2.4.** All gaze upon the face of Gorachand;
Vasu Ghosha sings the sweetness of Gora's abhisheka.

[^01-4]: Vasudeva (Vasu) Ghosha was the youngest of the Ghosha brothers and the most prolific of Gaura's singers. The great
bathing of the Lord in Srivasa's house: CB Madhya 9; Murari 2.12; Lochana (*Chaitanya-mangala*, Madhya-khanda, part 9, vv. 93–113); Karnapura,
*Chaitanya-chandrodaya*, act 1. In the *Bhakti-ratnakara* (wave 12) Narahari Chakravarti cites precisely this pada as an
eyewitness's testimony, though he had Murari, CB and CC to hand — and on this Majumdar rests its early date. In PK it
stands as a gaura-chandrika to the snana-yatra (the bathing of Jagannatha at the full moon of Jyeshtha).
[^01-5]: Arghya is a respectful offering of water (with flowers, rice and durva grass). Majumdar notes that the pada keeps a
detail the biographies pass over — the part women took in the rite.

## 3. Vasu Ghosha — "taila haridrā āra kuṅkuma kastūrī…" (PK 1537)
*Lila: the same abhisheka — the anointing, bathing and dressing of the Lord. Raga varadi.*[^01-6]

তৈল হরিদ্রা আর কুঙ্কুম কস্তূরী ।
গোরা-অঙ্গে লেপন করে নব নব নারী ॥

*taila haridrā āra kuṅkuma kastūrī |*
*gorā-aṅge lepana kare naba naba nārī ||*

*Word for word:* taila — oil; haridra — turmeric; ara kunkuma kasturi — and kunkuma, musk; gora-ange — on Gora's body; lepana kare — apply; naba naba nari — women, one after another

**3.1.** Oil, turmeric, kunkuma and musk
the women, one after another, apply to Gora's body.

সুবাসিত জল আনি কলসে পূরিয়া ।
সুগন্ধি চন্দন আদি তাহে মিশাইয়া ॥

*subāsita jala āni kalase pūriyā |*
*sugandhi candana ādi tāhe miśāiyā ||*

*Word for word:* subasita jala ani — bringing scented water; kalase puriya — filling the pitchers; sugandhi chandana adi — fragrant sandal and the like; tahe mishaiya — mixing into it

**3.2.** Bringing scented water, they fill the pitchers
and mix fragrant sandal and other things into it.

জয় জয় দিয়া জল ঢালে গোরা-গায় ।
শ্রীঅঙ্গ মোছাঞা কেহ বসন পরায় ॥

*jaya jaya diyā jala ḍhāle gorā-gāya |*
*śrīaṅga mochāñā keha basana parāya ||*

*Word for word:* jaya jaya diya — crying "Jaya, jaya!"; jala dhale gora-gaya — they pour water over Gora's body; shri-anga mochhana — wiping the holy body; keha basana paraya — someone dresses [Him] in garments

**3.3.** Crying "Jaya, jaya!" they pour the water over Gora's body;
wiping the holy body, someone dresses Him in garments.

সিনান-মণ্ডপে দেখ গোরা নটরায় ।
মনের হরিষে বাসুদেব ঘোষ গায় ॥

*sināna-maṇḍape dekha gorā naṭarāya |*
*manera hariṣe bāsudeba ghoṣa gāya ||*

*Word for word:* sinana-mandape — in the bathing pavilion; dekha — behold!; gora nataraya — Gora, king of dancers; manera harishe — with joy at heart; vasudeva ghosha gaya — Vasudeva Ghosha sings

**3.4.** Behold, in the bathing pavilion — Gora, king of dancers!
With joy at heart Vasudeva Ghosha sings.

[^01-6]: In PK (and in GPT1) this pada follows directly on the preceding one; Majumdar assigns it to the same abhisheka of
1509 (PK 1536, 1537, 1571 — the "historical" padas of Vasu Ghosha). "King of dancers" (nata-raya) is a frequent name
for Gaura, the leader of the dancers in kirtana, among the kirtana poets.

## 4. Govinda, Madhava and Vasu Ghosha — "basilā gaurāṅgacandra ratna-siṃhāsane…" (PK 1538)
*Lila: after the abhisheka the Lord on the throne: the feast, Shachi's arati, the worship of the devotees. Signed by all
three Ghosha brothers.*[^01-7]

বসিলা গৌরাঙ্গচন্দ্র রত্ন-সিংহাসনে ।
শ্রীবাস পণ্ডিত অঙ্গে লেপয়ে চন্দন ॥

*basilā gaurāṅgacandra ratna-siṃhāsane |*
*śrībāsa paṇḍita aṅge lepaye candana ||*

*Word for word:* basila gauranga-chandra — Gaurangachandra sat; ratna-simhasane — on the jewelled throne; shribasa pandita — Srivasa Pandita; ange lepaye chandana — anoints His body with sandal

**4.1.** Gaurangachandra sat upon the jewelled throne;
Srivasa Pandita anoints His body with sandal.

গদাধর দিল গলে মালতীর মালা ।
রূপের ছটায় দশ দিগ হৈল আলা ॥

*gadādhara dila gale mālatīra mālā |*
*rūpera chaṭāya daśa diga haila ālā ||*

*Word for word:* gadadhara dila gale — Gadadhara placed on His neck; malatira mala — a garland of malati; rupera chhataya — by the radiance of His beauty; dasha diga haila ala — the ten directions were lit up

**4.2.** Gadadhara placed a garland of malati on His neck;
by the radiance of His beauty all ten directions were lit.

বহু উপহার যত মিষ্টান্ন পকার ।
নিত্যানন্দ সহ বসি করিল ভোজন ॥

*bahu upahāra yata miṣṭānna pakāra |*
*nityānanda saha basi karila bhojana ||*

*Word for word:* bahu upahara — many offerings; yata mishtanna pakara — every kind of sweet dish; nityananda saha basi — sitting with Nityananda; karila bhojana — He ate

**4.3.** Many offerings, every kind of sweet dish
He ate, sitting together with Nityananda.

তাম্বূল ভক্ষণ করি বসিলা সিংহাসনে ।
শচী দেবী আইলেন মালিনীর সনে ॥

*tāmbūla bhakṣaṇa kari basilā siṃhāsane |*
*śacī debī āilena mālinīra sane ||*

*Word for word:* tambula bhakshana kari — having chewed tambula (betel); basila simhasane — He sat on the throne; shachi devi ailena — Shachi-devi came; malinira sane — with Malini

**4.4.** Having chewed tambula, He sat on the throne again;
Shachi-devi came together with Malini.

পঞ্চদীপ জ্বালি তেঁহ আরাত্রিক কৈল ।
নিরমঞ্ছন করি শিরে ধান্য দূর্বা দিল ॥

*pañcadīpa jvāli tem̐ha ārātrika kaila |*
*niramañchana kari śire dhānya dūrvā dila ||*

*Word for word:* panchadipa jvali — lighting the five-wicked lamp; tenha aratrika kaila — she performed arati; nirmanchhana kari — waving [it] round; shire — on His head; dhanya durva dila — she placed paddy and durva grass

**4.5.** Lighting the five-wicked lamp, she performed arati,
waved [the flame] round Him and placed paddy and durva on His head.[^01-8]

তৎক্ষণ করে সভে পুষ্প বরিষণ ।
অদ্বৈত আচার্য দেই তুলসী চন্দন ॥

*tatkṣaṇa kare sabhe puṣpa bariṣaṇa |*
*advaita ācārya dei tulasī candana ||*

*Word for word:* tatkshana — at that moment; kare sabhe pushpa barishana — all shower flowers; advaita acharya — Advaita Acharya; dei tulasi chandana — offers tulasi and sandal

**4.6.** At that moment all shower Him with flowers;
Advaita Acharya offers tulasi and sandal.

দেখিতে আইসে দেব নরে এক সঙ্গে ।
নিত্যানন্দ ডাহিনে বসিয়া দেখে রঙ্গে ॥

*dekhite āise deba nare eka saṅge |*
*nityānanda ḍāhine basiyā dekhe raṅge ||*

*Word for word:* dekhite aise — come to see; deba nare eka sange — gods and men together; nityananda dahine basiya — Nityananda, sitting on the right; dekhe range — watches with delight

**4.7.** Gods and men come together to see it;
Nityananda, sitting at His right, watches with delight.

গোরা-অভিষেক এই অপরূপ লীলা ।
গোবিন্দ মাধব বাসু প্রেমেতে ভাসিলা ॥

*gorā-abhiṣeka ei aparūpa līlā |*
*gobinda mādhaba bāsu premete bhāsilā ||*

*Word for word:* gora-abhisheka — Gora's bathing; ei aparupa lila — this matchless lila; gobinda madhava basu — Govinda, Madhava [and] Vasu; premete bhasila — floated away in prema

**4.8.** This is the matchless lila of Gora's abhisheka:
Govinda, Madhava and Vasu floated away in prema.

[^01-7]: Majumdar cites this pada together with the preceding ones as a description of the same abhisheka in Srivasa's
house; from the signature "Govinda, Madhava, Vasu" (as in Vasu Ramananda) he infers that Govinda was the eldest. The
Lord sitting on Vishnu's throne in Srivasa's house, accepting offerings and receiving the devotees' worship: CB Madhya 9;
CC Adi 17.
[^01-8]: Paddy (dhanya) and durva grass placed on the head are a Bengali mother's blessing.

## 5. Ramachandra — "pahu mora gaurāṅga rāya…" (BR, p. 919; PK 2186)
*Lila: the Lord in Navadvipa in the mood of Radha, with Gadadhara and Narahari beside Him. According to Majumdar, the
song of an eyewitness (Narahari Chakravarti cites it as testimony). Raga shri (PK), suhai (BR).*[^01-9]

পহু মোর গৌরাঙ্গ রায় ।
শিব শুক বিরিঞ্চি যার গুণ গায় ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*pahu mora gaurāṅga rāya |*
*śiba śuka biriñci yāra guṇa gāya || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* pahu mora — my Lord; gauranga raya — Gauranga Raya; shiva shuka virinchi — Shiva, Shuka, Brahma; yara guna gaya — whose qualities sing

**5.1.** *(Refrain)* My Lord is Gauranga Raya,
whose glories Shiva, Shuka and Brahma sing!

কমলা যাহার ভাবে সদাই আকুলি ।
সেই পহু বাহু তুলি কান্দে হরি বলি ॥

*kamalā yāhāra bhābe sadāi ākuli |*
*sei pahu bāhu tuli kānde hari bali ||*

*Word for word:* kamala — Kamala (Lakshmi); yahara bhabe — in love for whom; sadai akuli — is ever restless; sei pahu — that same Lord; bahu tuli — raising His arms; kande hari bali — weeps, crying "Hari!"

**5.2.** He for whom Kamala ever pines,[^01-10]
that very Lord raises His arms, weeps and cries out, "Hari!"

যে অঙ্গ হেরি হেরি অনঙ্গ ভেল কাম ।
সো অব কীর্তন-ধূলি-ধূসর অবিরাম ॥

*ye aṅga heri heri anaṅga bhela kāma |*
*so aba kīrtana-dhūli-dhūsara abirāma ||*

*Word for word:* ye anga — the body which; heri heri — beholding again and again; ananga bhela kama — Kama became bodiless; so aba — that now; kirtana-dhuli-dhusara — grey with the dust of kirtana; abirama — unceasingly

**5.3.** The body at whose sight Kamadeva became bodiless[^01-11]
is now ever grey with the dust of kirtana.

খেণে রাধা রাধা বলি উঠে চমকিয়া ।
গদাধর নরহরি রহে মুখ চাঞা ॥

*kheṇe rādhā rādhā bali uṭhe camakiyā |*
*gadādhara narahari rahe mukha cāñā ||*

*Word for word:* khene — now and then; radha radha bali — crying "Radha, Radha!"; uthe chamakiya — He starts up; gadadhara narahari — Gadadhara [and] Narahari; rahe mukha chana — stand gazing at [His] face

**5.4.** Now and again He starts up, crying, "Radha, Radha!" —
Gadadhara and Narahari stand gazing at His face.

পুরব-নিবিড়-প্রেম-পুলকিত অঙ্গ ।
রামচন্দ্র কহে কে না বুঝে ও না রঙ্গ ॥

*puraba-nibiṛa-prema-pulakita aṅga |*
*rāmacandra kahe ke nā bujhe o nā raṅga ||*

*Word for word:* puraba-nibira-prema — with the deep love of old; pulakita anga — His body thrills; ramachandra kahe — says Ramachandra; ke na bujhe — who would not understand; o na ranga — that play

**5.5.** His body thrills with the deep love of former days.
Says Ramachandra: who would not understand this play?

[^01-9]: Who this Ramachandra was is unclear: Majumdar rejects Ramachandra Puri, Ramachandra the brahmana and Ramachandra
Khan, and suggests Ramachandra Kaviraja of Nityananda's branch (not Narottama's friend, whom Narahari Chakravarti would
not have passed off as an eyewitness). In BR (wave 12) the pada stands among testimonies to the Navadvipa pastimes,
directly after Govinda Ghosha's pada on the Lord's dancing with Narahari. Narahari Sarakara Thakura (of Shrikhanda) was a
singer of Gaura's moods; Majumdar confirms his presence with the Lord in Navadvipa from the padas of other
contemporaries. Cf. CC Adi 17 (Radha's mood in Navadvipa).
[^01-10]: Kamala is Lakshmi, the consort of Narayana. Here she is only mentioned as longing for the Lord; cf. *Bhag.* 10.16.36
(Lakshmi longs for the dust of Krishna's feet).
[^01-11]: The Lord's beauty put Kama (Kamadeva, the god of love) to shame, and he was as if bereft of his body (Ananga, "the
Bodiless", is his name). The "love of former days" (v. 5.5) is Radha's love for Krishna, which the Lord tastes in the
form of Gaura. BR reads: "He gazes at the faces of Narahari and Gadadhara."

## 6. Murari Gupta — "gadādhara-aṅge pahu aṅga helāiyā…" (BR, p. 922; PK 2121)
*Lila: the Lord in Radha's mood, leaning on Gadadhara, listens to the song of Vrindavana. According to Majumdar, composed in
1509 under the immediate impression of Nimai's moods. Raga patamanjari (PK), kamoda (BR).*[^01-12]

গদাধর-অঙ্গে পহু অঙ্গ হেলাইয়া ।
বৃন্দাবন-গুণ গান বিভোর হইয়া ॥

*gadādhara-aṅge pahu aṅga helāiyā |*
*bṛndābana-guṇa gāna bibhora haiyā ||*

*Word for word:* gadadhara-ange — against Gadadhara's body; pahu — the Lord; anga helaiya — leaning His body; vrindavana-guna gana — the song of Vrindavana's glories; bibhora haiya — being absorbed

**6.1.** Leaning His body against Gadadhara,
the Lord is lost in the song of Vrindavana's glories.

খেণে হাসে খেণে কান্দে বাহ্য নাহি জানে ।
রাধার ভাবে আকুল প্রাণ গোকুল পড়ে মনে ॥

*kheṇe hāse kheṇe kānde bāhya nāhi jāne |*
*rādhāra bhābe ākula prāṇa gokula paṛe mane ||*

*Word for word:* khene hase — now He laughs; khene kande — now He weeps; bahya nahi jane — unaware of the outer world; radhara bhabe — in Radha's mood; akula prana — His heart restless; gokula pare mane — Gokula comes to His mind

**6.2.** Now He laughs, now He weeps, unaware of the outer world;
in Radha's mood His heart is restless — Gokula comes to His mind.

অনন্ত অনঙ্গ জিনি দেহের বলনি ।
কত কোটি চাঁদ কান্দে হেরি মুখখানি ॥

*ananta anaṅga jini dehera balani |*
*kata koṭi cām̐da kānde heri mukhakhāni ||*

*Word for word:* ananta ananga jini — surpassing countless Kamadevas; dehera balani — the grace of His body; kata koti chanda — so many millions of moons; kande — weep; heri mukhakhani — seeing His face

**6.3.** The grace of His form surpasses countless Kamadevas;
millions of moons weep to see His face.

ত্রিভুবন দরবিত এ দোঁহার রসে ।
না জানি মুরারি গুপ্ত বঞ্চিত কোন দোষে ॥

*tribhubana darabita e dom̐hāra rase |*
*nā jāni murāri gupta bañcita kona doṣe ||*

*Word for word:* tribhubana — the three worlds; darabita — melt; e donhara rase — in the rasa of these two; na jani — I know not; murari gupta — Murari Gupta; banchita — is deprived; kona doshe — for what fault

**6.4.** The three worlds melt in the rasa of these two.[^01-13]
I know not for what fault Murari Gupta is left without it.

[^01-12]: Murari Gupta, the Lord's companion from childhood, wrote the Sanskrit biography (the "Kadacha"); apart from it only
a few Bengali padas are his. Narahari Chakravarti cites this one in BR (wave 12) among eyewitness testimonies.
Majumdar's argument: the pada was written in 1509, when Nimai's moods were still new; the signature of the poet, lamenting
that he himself is "deprived" of this rasa, is an eyewitness's humility. Cf. CC Adi 17.
[^01-13]: "These two" are Gaura and Gadadhara. According to the *Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika* (vv. 147–153) Gadadhara Pandita is a
manifestation of Radha in Gaura's lila; the Lord, Himself in Radha's mood, remembers Gokula beside him.

## 7. Paramananda (Gupta) — "gorā-tanu dhūlāya loṭāya…" (PK 2120)
*Lila: in Navadvipa the Lord, dressed as Natavara (Krishna the dancer), calls for Radha and asks for the flute; the
companions caution the singers. According to Majumdar, an eyewitness's testimony from 1509. Raga kalyani.*[^01-14]

গোরা-তনু ধূলায় লোটায় ।
ডাকে রাধা রাধা বলি গদাধর কোলে করি
পীত বসন বংশী চায় ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*gorā-tanu dhūlāya loṭāya |*
*ḍāke rādhā rādhā bali gadādhara kole kari*
*pīta basana baṃśī cāya || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* gora-tanu — Gora's body; dhulaya lotaya — rolls in the dust; dake radha radha bali — He calls, "Radha, Radha!"; gadadhara kole kari — embracing Gadadhara; pita basana — the yellow garment; vamshi chaya — and the flute He asks for

**7.1.** *(Refrain)* Gora's body rolls in the dust.
Embracing Gadadhara, He calls, "Radha, Radha!" —
and asks for the yellow garment and the flute.

ধরি নটবর-বেশ সমুখে বান্ধিয়া কেশ
তাহে শোভে ময়ূরের পাখা ।
ত্রিভঙ্গ ভঙ্গিমা করি সঘনে বলয়ে হরি
চাহে গোরা কদম্বের শাখা ॥

*dhari naṭabara-beśa samukhe bāndhiyā keśa*
*tāhe śobhe mayūrera pākhā |*
*tribhaṅga bhaṅgimā kari saghane balaye hari*
*cāhe gorā kadambera śākhā ||*

*Word for word:* dhari natavara-besha — wearing the dress of Natavara (the best of dancers); samukhe bandhiya kesha — binding His hair in front; tahe shobhe mayurera pakha — a peacock feather shines on it; tribhanga bhangima kari — standing thrice-bent; saghane balaye hari — again and again He cries "Hari!"; chahe gora kadambera shakha — Gora looks for the kadamba branch

**7.2.** Dressed as Natavara, His hair bound up in front
and a peacock feather shining in it,
standing thrice-bent, He cries again and again, "Hari!" —
and Gora looks about for the kadamba branch.

শুনি বৃন্দাবন-গুণ রসে উনমত মন
সখী-বৃন্দ কোথা গেল হায় ।
না বুঝিয়া রস-বোধ প্রিয় সব পারিষদ
গৌরাঙ্গ বলিয়া গুণ গায় ॥

*śuni bṛndābana-guṇa rase unamata mana*
*sakhī-bṛnda kothā gela hāya |*
*nā bujhiyā rasa-bodha priya saba pāriṣada*
*gaurāṅga baliyā guṇa gāya ||*

*Word for word:* shuni vrindavana-guna — hearing of Vrindavana's glories; rase unamata mana — His mind is maddened with rasa; sakhi-vrinda kotha gela haya — "Where have the sakhis gone, alas!"; na bujhiya rasa-bodha — not grasping [His] mood; priya saba parishada — all the dear companions; gauranga baliya guna gaya — sing His glories, calling Him "Gauranga"

**7.3.** Hearing of Vrindavana's glories, His mind maddened with rasa, [He asks,]
"Where have the sakhis gone, alas?"
Not grasping His mood, all the dear companions
sing His glories, calling Him "Gauranga".

কেহো বলে সাবধান না করিহ রস-গান
উথলিলে না ধরে ধরণী ।
নিজ মন-আনন্দে কহয়ে পরমানন্দে
কেবা দেহে ধরিবে পরাণি ॥

*keho bale sābadhāna nā kariha rasa-gāna*
*uthalile nā dhare dharaṇī |*
*nija mana-ānande kahaye paramānande*
*kebā dehe dharibe parāṇi ||*

*Word for word:* keho bale — someone says; sabadhana — take care!; na kariha rasa-gana — do not sing songs of rasa; uthalile — if [prema] surges up; na dhare dharani — the earth will not hold it; nija mana-anande — in the joy of his heart; kahaye paramanande — says Paramananda; keba dehe dharibe parani — who will keep life in the body?

**7.4.** And someone says, "Take care! Do not sing songs of rasa:
if [prema] surges up, the earth will not hold it!"
In the joy of his heart says Paramananda:
"Who then will keep life in the body?"

[^01-14]: The signature is "Paramananda". S. Ray ascribed the padas bearing it to Kavi Karnapura (Paramananda Sena); Majumdar
separates six Vrajabuli padas by a certain Paramananda of Vrindavana and gives the rest, this and the next among them, to
Paramananda Gupta, in whose house Nityananda stayed (CB, Antya-khanda) — Karnapura was not yet born in 1509. His argument for
the date: only a close companion could know the detail "do not sing songs of rasa", and the Lord did not wear the
Natavara dress in Puri — hence Navadvipa. The attribution to Paramananda Gupta is Majumdar's conjecture. Cf. Murari
2.15.3 (the Lord asks for His flute).

## 8. Paramananda (Gupta) — "śacīra nandana gorācānda…" (PK 2528)
*Lila: in Navadvipa the Lord in the mood of new love (anuraga); the same mood overcomes His companions. According to
Majumdar, an eyewitness's pada.*[^01-15]

শচীর নন্দন গোরাচান্দ ।
সকল-ভুবন-মোহন ফান্দ ॥

*śacīra nandana gorācānda |*
*sakala-bhubana-mohana phānda ||*

*Word for word:* shachira nandana — Shachi's son; gorachanda — Gorachand; sakala-bhubana — of all the worlds; mohana phanda — the enchanting snare

**8.1.** Shachi's son, Gorachand,
is the enchanting snare of all the worlds.

নব অনুরাগ-ভাবে ভেল ভোর ।
অনুখণ কঞ্জ-নয়নে বহে লোর ॥

*naba anurāga-bhābe bhela bhora |*
*anukhaṇa kañja-nayane bahe lora ||*

*Word for word:* naba anuraga-bhabe — in the mood of ever-new love; bhela bhora — He is lost; anukhana — incessantly; kanja-nayane — from His lotus eyes; bahe lora — tears flow

**8.2.** In the mood of new love He is lost to Himself:
incessantly tears flow from His lotus eyes.

পুলকে পূরিত তনু গদ গদ বোল ।
খেণে থির করি চিত খেণে অতি লোল ॥

*pulake pūrita tanu gada gada bola |*
*kheṇe thira kari cita kheṇe ati lola ||*

*Word for word:* pulake purita tanu — His body full of thrills; gada gada bola — His speech faltering; khene thira kari chita — now steadying His heart; khene ati lola — now utterly unsteady

**8.3.** His body is full of thrills, His speech falters;
now He steadies His heart, now He is utterly unsettled.

ঐছে বিভাবিত সহচর সঙ্গ ।
পরমানন্দ কহে প্রেম-তরঙ্গ ॥

*aiche bibhābita sahacara saṅga |*
*paramānanda kahe prema-taraṅga ||*

*Word for word:* aichhe — likewise; bibhabita — are overcome; sahachara sanga — the companions with Him; paramananda kahe — says Paramananda; prema-taranga — waves of prema

**8.4.** Likewise the companions with Him are overcome [by this mood].
Says Paramananda: these are waves of prema.

[^01-15]: Only in PK, as a gaura-chandrika to the section "anuraga". Majumdar regards this pada too as an eyewitness's: in it
the Lord's mood overcomes His companions as well. (In the catalogue the first line of this pada had been given wrongly,
from a line of a different, neighbouring song.)

## 9. Vasu Ghosha — "cām̐cara cikura cūṛā cāru bhāle…" (BR, pp. 934–935)
*Lila: Nimai in the dress of Natavara (Krishna the dancer), 1509. According to Majumdar, something seen with his own eyes.
Raga kamoda.*[^01-16]

চাঁচর চিকুর চূড়া চারু ভালে ।
বেড়িয়াছে মালতীর মালে ॥

*cām̐cara cikura cūṛā cāru bhāle |*
*beṛiyāche mālatīra māle ||*

*Word for word:* chanchara chikura — curling hair; chura — the topknot; charu bhale — above the lovely brow; beriyachhe — is wound round; malatira male — with a garland of malati

**9.1.** His curling hair is bound in a topknot above the lovely brow
and wound with a garland of malati;

তাহে দিয়া ময়ূরের পাখা ।
সপত্র সহিত ফুলশাখা ॥

*tāhe diyā mayūrera pākhā |*
*sapatra sahita phulaśākhā ||*

*Word for word:* tahe diya — setting in it; mayurera pakha — a peacock feather; sapatra sahita phulashakha — and a flowering sprig with its leaves

**9.2.** in it is set a peacock feather
and a flowering sprig with its leaves.

কষিত কাঞ্চন জিনি অঙ্গ ।
কটি-মাঝে বসন সুরঙ্গ ॥

*kaṣita kāñcana jini aṅga |*
*kaṭi-mājhe basana suraṅga ||*

*Word for word:* kashita kanchana jini — surpassing assayed gold; anga — His body; kati-majhe — about His waist; basana suranga — a bright-coloured cloth

**9.3.** His body outshines assayed gold,
about His waist is a bright-coloured cloth;

চন্দন-তিলক শোভে ভালে ।
আজানুলম্বিত বনমালে ॥

*candana-tilaka śobhe bhāle |*
*ājānulambita banamāle ||*

*Word for word:* chandana-tilaka — a sandal tilaka; shobhe bhale — shines on His brow; ajanu-lambita — hanging to the knees; banamale — a garland of forest flowers

**9.4.** a sandal tilaka shines on His brow,
a garland of forest flowers hangs to His knees.

নটবর-বেশ গোরাচাঁদ ।
রমণীগণের কিবা ফাঁদ ॥

*naṭabara-beśa gorācām̐da |*
*ramaṇīgaṇera kibā phām̐da ||*

*Word for word:* natavara-besha — in the dress of Natavara; gorachanda — Gorachand; ramaniganera — for the women; kiba phanda — what a snare!

**9.5.** Gorachand in the dress of Natavara —
what a snare for the women!

তা দেখিয়া বাসুদেব কান্দে ।
প্রাণ মোর থির নাহি বান্ধে ॥

*tā dekhiyā bāsudeba kānde |*
*prāṇa mora thira nāhi bāndhe ||*

*Word for word:* ta dekhiya — seeing this; vasudeva kande — Vasudeva weeps; prana mora — my heart; thira nahi bandhe — finds no rest

**9.6.** Seeing this, Vasudeva weeps:
my heart can find no rest.

[^01-16]: This and the next two padas of Vasu Ghosha are known only from the *Bhakti-ratnakara* (wave 12): Narahari
Chakravarti introduces them as songs composed at the very places in Navadvipa that are shown to Srinivasa Acharya on
his circuit of Navadvipa ("here, under this kadamba, Gora, dressed as Natavara and standing thrice-bent, played the
flute"). Majumdar takes them as describing what was seen with one's own eyes in 1509. "A snare for the women" (9.5) is a
poetic image of the Lord's irresistible beauty (Krishna the Natavara captivates the gopis); Vrindavana Dasa stresses that
in this incarnation the Lord never so much as glanced at another man's wife, and the Gaudiya tradition does not accept
the worship of Gaura in the spirit of "Gaura-nagari".

## 10. Vasu Ghosha — "soṅari puruba-līlā tribhaṅga hailā…" (BR, p. 935)
*Lila: Gora, remembering His former lila, plays the flute on the bank of the Ganga. Raga dhanashi.*[^01-17]

সোঙরি পুরুব-লীলা ত্রিভঙ্গ হইলা ।
মোহন মুরলী গোরা অধরে ধরিলা ॥

*soṅari puruba-līlā tribhaṅga hailā |*
*mohana muralī gorā adhare dharilā ||*

*Word for word:* songari — remembering; puruba-lila — His former lila; tribhanga haila — He stood thrice-bent; mohana murali — the enchanting flute; gora adhare dharila — Gora held to His lips

**10.1.** Remembering His former lila, He stood thrice-bent,
and Gora raised the enchanting flute to His lips.

মুরলীর রন্ধ্রে ফুঁক দিলা গোরাচাঁদ ।
অঙ্গুলি চালাঞা করে সুললিত গান ॥

*muralīra randhre phum̐ka dilā gorācām̐da |*
*aṅguli cālāñā kare sulalita gāna ||*

*Word for word:* muralira randhre — into the flute's opening; phunka dila gorachanda — Gorachand blew; anguli chalana — moving His fingers; kare sulalita gana — plays a most lovely song

**10.2.** Gorachand blew into the flute's opening
and, moving His fingers, played a most lovely song.

নগরের লোক যত শুনিয়া মোহিত ।
সুরধুনী-তীরে তরু লতা পুলকিত ॥

*nagarera loka yata śuniyā mohita |*
*suradhunī-tīre taru latā pulakita ||*

*Word for word:* nagarera loka yata — all the townspeople; shuniya mohita — are enchanted to hear it; suradhuni-tire — on the Ganga's bank; taru lata pulakita — trees and creepers thrill

**10.3.** All the townspeople are enchanted to hear it;
on the bank of the Suradhuni the trees and creepers thrill.

বাসুদেব ঘোষ তাহা কি বলিতে জানে ।
ভুবন মোহিল গোরা মুরলীর গানে ॥

*bāsudeba ghoṣa tāhā ki balite jāne |*
*bhubana mohila gorā muralīra gāne ||*

*Word for word:* vasudeva ghosha — Vasudeva Ghosha; taha ki balite jane — what can he say of it?; bhubana mohila gora — Gora enchanted the world; muralira gane — with the song of the flute

**10.4.** What can Vasudeva Ghosha say of it?
With the song of His flute Gora enchanted the world.

[^01-17]: Cf. Murari 2.15.3 (the Lord asks for His flute); CC Adi 17 (the Lord in Krishna's mood in Navadvipa). The pada is
also in GPT2.

## 11. Vasu Ghosha — "pūrvalīlā gorācām̐dera manete paṛila…" (BR, p. 935)
*Lila: the goshtha-lila in Navadvipa — the Lord in the mood of a cowherd boy calls the cows; with Him are Nityananda,
Ramai, Sundarananda, Gauridasa. Raga tori.*[^01-18]

পূর্বলীলা গোরাচাঁদের মনেতে পড়িল ।
শাঙলি ধবলি বলি সঘনে ডাকিল ॥

*pūrvalīlā gorācām̐dera manete paṛila |*
*śāṅali dhabali bali saghane ḍākila ||*

*Word for word:* purvalila — His former lila; gorachandera manete parila — came to Gorachand's mind; shangali dhabali bali — "Shangali! Dhavali!" [calling the cows]; saghane dakila — He called again and again

**11.1.** His former lila came to Gorachand's mind,
and He began to call aloud: "Shangali! Dhavali!"

শিঙা বেণু মুরলী করিয়া জয়ধ্বনি ।
হৈ হৈ করিয়া ঘন ফিরায় পাঁচনী ॥

*śiṅā beṇu muralī kariyā jayadhvani |*
*hai hai kariyā ghana phirāya pām̐canī ||*

*Word for word:* shinga venu murali — horn, venu, murali; kariya jaya-dhvani — sounding in triumph; hai hai kariya — shouting "hai, hai!"; ghana phiraya panchani — keeps twirling the cowherd's stick

**11.2.** Sounding horn, venu and murali in triumph,
shouting "hai, hai!" He keeps twirling the cowherd's stick.

রামাই সুন্দর আর সঙ্গে নিত্যানন্দ ।
গৌরীদাস আদি সভে হইলা আনন্দ ॥

*rāmāi sundara āra saṅge nityānanda |*
*gaurīdāsa ādi sabhe hailā ānanda ||*

*Word for word:* ramai — Ramai; sundara — Sundara(nanda); ara sange nityananda — and Nityananda with them; gauridasa adi sabhe — Gauridasa and all the others; haila ananda — were filled with bliss

**11.3.** Ramai, Sundara, and Nityananda with them,
Gauridasa and all the others were filled with bliss.

বাসুদেব ঘোষে কহে মনের হরিষে ।
গোষ্ঠলীলা গোরাচাঁদ করিলা প্রকাশে ॥

*bāsudeba ghoṣe kahe manera hariṣe |*
*goṣṭhalīlā gorācām̐da karilā prakāśe ||*

*Word for word:* vasudeva ghoshe kahe — says Vasudeva Ghosha; manera harishe — with joy at heart; goshtha-lila — the pastime of the pastures; gorachanda karila prakashe — Gorachand revealed

**11.4.** With joy at heart Vasudeva Ghosha says:
Gorachand has revealed the goshtha-lila.

[^01-18]: Shangali and Dhavali are names of Krishna's cows ("the dark one", "the white one"); venu and murali are kinds of flute.
Sundara is Sundarananda; Gauridasa Pandita (of Ambika-Kalna) — companions of Nityananda, cowherd boys of Vraja according
to the *Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika* (Gauridasa is Subala). "Ramai" is probably Abhirama (Ramadasa), the cowherd Shridama
according to GGD; the identification is not certain. Majumdar's argument: this pada explains why Nityananda's companions
lived in the mood of cowherds (as CB describes) — they had seen the Lord's goshtha-lila.

## 12. Vamshivadana — "śacīra nandana gorā o cām̐da-bayāne…" (PK 2564)
*Lila: the same goshtha-lila: Nityananda sounds the horn, Gauridasa and Abhirama come running. According to Majumdar, more
detailed than Vasu's and bearing "the stamp of an eyewitness"; 1509. Raga bhatiyari.*[^01-19]

শচীর নন্দন গোরা ও চাঁদ-বয়ানে ।
ধবলী শাঙলী বলি ডাকে ঘনে ঘনে ॥

*śacīra nandana gorā o cām̐da-bayāne |*
*dhabalī śāṅalī bali ḍāke ghane ghane ||*

*Word for word:* shachira nandana gora — Gora, the son of Shachi; o chanda-bayane — with that moonlike mouth; dhabali shangali bali — "Dhavali! Shangali!"; dake ghane ghane — calls again and again

**12.1.** Gora, the son of Shachi, with that moonlike mouth
calls again and again: "Dhavali! Shangali!"

বুঝিয়া ভাবের গতি নিত্যানন্দ রায় ।
শিঙ্গার শবদ করি বদনে বাজায় ॥

*bujhiyā bhābera gati nityānanda rāya |*
*śiṅgāra śabada kari badane bājāya ||*

*Word for word:* bujhiya bhabera gati — understanding the course of [His] mood; nityananda raya — Nityananda Raya; shingara shabada kari — making the sound of a horn; badane bajaya — sounds it with his mouth

**12.2.** Understanding where His mood is leading, Nityananda Raya
sounds a call with His mouth, imitating a horn.

নিতাই-চাঁদের মুখে শিঙ্গার নিসান ।
শুনিয়া ভকতগণ প্রেমে অগেয়ান ॥

*nitāi-cām̐dera mukhe śiṅgāra nisāna |*
*śuniyā bhakatagaṇa preme ageyāna ||*

*Word for word:* nitai-chandera mukhe — from Nitaichand's mouth; shingara nisana — the call of the horn; shuniya bhakatagana — hearing it, the devotees; preme ageyana — are senseless with prema

**12.3.** Hearing the horn-call from Nitaichand's mouth,
the devotees fall senseless with prema.

ধাইল পণ্ডিত গৌরীদাস যার নাম ।
ভাইয়া রে ভাইয়া রে বলি ধায় অভিরাম ॥

*dhāila paṇḍita gaurīdāsa yāra nāma |*
*bhāiyā re bhāiyā re bali dhāya abhirāma ||*

*Word for word:* dhaila pandita — ran the pandita; gauridasa yara nama — named Gauridasa; bhaiya re bhaiya re bali — crying "Brother, brother!"; dhaya abhirama — Abhirama runs

**12.4.** Up ran the pandita whose name is Gauridasa,
and Abhirama runs, crying, "Brother, brother!"

দেখিয়া গৌরাঙ্গ-রূপ প্রেমার আবেশ ।
শিরে চূড়া শিখি-পাখা নটবর-বেশ ॥

*dekhiyā gaurāṅga-rūpa premāra ābeśa |*
*śire cūṛā śikhi-pākhā naṭabara-beśa ||*

*Word for word:* dekhiya gauranga-rupa — seeing Gauranga's form; premara abesha — [all are] seized by prema; shire chura shikhi-pakha — on His head a topknot with a peacock feather; natavara-besha — the dress of Natavara

**12.5.** Seeing Gauranga's form, all are seized by prema:
on His head a topknot with a peacock feather, the dress of Natavara,

চরণে নূপুর সাজে সর্বাঙ্গে চন্দন ।
বংশীবদন কহে চল গোবর্ধন ॥

*caraṇe nūpura sāje sarvāṅge candana |*
*baṃśībadana kahe cala gobardhana ||*

*Word for word:* charane nupura saje — anklets adorn His feet; sarvange chandana — sandal on all His limbs; vamshivadana kahe — says Vamshivadana; chala gobardhana — come, to Govardhana!

**12.6.** anklets ringing on His feet, sandal on all His limbs.
Says Vamshivadana: "Come, let us go to Govardhana!"

[^01-19]: Vamshivadana (Vamshi) was a companion of the Lord, and after the sannyasa the guardian of Vishnupriya and Shachi in
Navadvipa. In PK the pada is a gaura-chandrika to the section "going out to the pastures" (goshtha-gamana). Majumdar
notes that the pada explains why GGD calls Gauridasa Subala and Abhirama Shridama. He dates it to 1509 (the OCR of his
book has "1507", probably a misprint).

## 13. Vasu Ghosha — "gaurāṅgacām̐dera mane ki bhāba uṭhila…" (PK 1368; BR, pp. 935–936)
*Lila: the Lord in Krishna's mood remembers the dana-lila and "collects a toll" on the roads of Nadia. According to
Majumdar, seen with his own eyes, 1509. Raga suhai (PK), kamoda (BR).*[^01-20]

গৌরাঙ্গচাঁদের মনে কি ভাব উঠিল ।
নদীয়ার মাঝে গোরা দান সিরজিল ॥

*gaurāṅgacām̐dera mane ki bhāba uṭhila |*
*nadīyāra mājhe gorā dāna sirajila ||*

*Word for word:* gauranga-chandera mane — in Gaurangachand's heart; ki bhaba uthila — what a mood arose!; nadiyara majhe — in the midst of Nadia; gora dana sirajila — Gora set up a toll

**13.1.** What a mood arose in Gaurangachand's heart!
In the midst of Nadia Gora set up a toll.

কি রসের দান চাহে গোরা দ্বিজমণি ।
বেত্র দিয়া আগুলিয়া রাখয়ে তরুণী ॥

*ki rasera dāna cāhe gorā dvijamaṇi |*
*betra diyā āguliyā rākhaye taruṇī ||*

*Word for word:* ki rasera dana — a toll of what rasa; chahe — demands; gora dvijamani — Gora, the jewel of brahmanas; betra diya — with a cane; aguliya rakhaye — barring the way, holds back; taruni — the young women

**13.2.** A toll of what rasa does Gora, the jewel of brahmanas, demand?
Barring the way with a cane, He holds back the young women.

দান দেহ দান দেহ বলি গোরা ডাকে ।
নগরের নাগরী সব পড়িল বিপাকে ॥

*dāna deha dāna deha bali gorā ḍāke |*
*nagarera nāgarī saba paṛila bipāke ||*

*Word for word:* dana deha dana deha — "Pay the toll, pay the toll!"; bali gora dake — Gora calls out; nagarera nagari saba — all the women of the town; parila bipake — were in a fix

**13.3.** "Pay the toll, pay the toll!" Gora calls,
and the women of the town were in a fix.

কৃষ্ণ-অবতারে আমি সাধিয়াছি দান ।
সে ভাব পড়িল মনে বাসু ঘোষে গান ॥

*kṛṣṇa-abatāre āmi sādhiyāchi dāna |*
*se bhāba paṛila mane bāsu ghoṣe gāna ||*

*Word for word:* krishna-abatare — in the Krishna-avatara; ami sadhiyachhi dana — I collected the toll; se bhaba parila mane — that mood came to [His] mind; basu ghoshe gana — Vasu Ghosha sings

**13.4.** "In the Krishna-avatara I collected the toll" —
that mood came back to His mind, sings Vasu Ghosha.

[^01-20]: The dana-lila is Krishna's pastime of stopping the gopis, together with His cowherd friends, on their way to
Govardhana and demanding a "toll" for their milk and butter; it is a lila of pure prema, not of worldly passion. Here
the Lord, seized by Krishna's mood, re-enacts it: Majumdar sees in the pada the explanation of Gadadhara Dasa's mood
("who will buy Gora?"). The reading "taruṇī" ("young women", BR, PK) Majumdar holds correct, "taraṇī" ("boat", GPT) not.
Vrindavana Dasa stresses that in this incarnation the Lord never so much as glanced at another man's wife; the Gaudiya
tradition (Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja, Bhaktisiddhanta) does not accept the worship of Gaura in the spirit
of "Gaura-nagari".

## 14. Shivananda Sena — "holi khelata gaurakiśora…" (BR, pp. 944–945)
*Lila: Holi in Navadvipa: the Lord in Krishna's mood with Gadadhara; Narahari sings of Vraja, Mukunda, Murari and Vasu
dance. According to Majumdar, apparently 1509. Raga kamoda; Vrajabuli.*[^01-21]

হোলি খেলত গৌরকিশোর ।
রসবতী নারী গদাধর কোর ॥

*holi khelata gaurakiśora |*
*rasabatī nārī gadādhara kora ||*

*Word for word:* holi khelata — plays Holi; gaura-kishora — the youthful Gaura; rasabati nari — the beloved full of rasa; gadadhara — Gadadhara; kora — in His embrace

**14.1.** The youthful Gaura plays Holi;
in His embrace is Gadadhara, the beloved full of rasa.[^01-22]

স্বেদবিন্দু মুখে পুলক শরীর ।
ভাবভরে গলতহি লোচনে নীর ॥

*svedabindu mukhe pulaka śarīra |*
*bhābabhare galatahi locane nīra ||*

*Word for word:* sveda-bindu mukhe — drops of sweat on His face; pulaka sharira — His body thrilling; bhaba-bhare — under the weight of the mood; galatahi lochane nira — tears stream from His eyes

**14.2.** Drops of sweat on His face, His body thrilling,
under the weight of the mood tears stream from His eyes.

ব্রজরস গায়ত নরহরি সঙ্গে ।
মুকুন্দ মুরারি বাসু নাচত রঙ্গে ॥

*brajarasa gāyata narahari saṅge |*
*mukunda murāri bāsu nācata raṅge ||*

*Word for word:* braja-rasa — of the rasa of Vraja; gayata — they sing; narahari sange — together with Narahari; mukunda murari basu — Mukunda, Murari, Vasu; nachata range — dance with delight

**14.3.** They sing of the rasa of Vraja together with Narahari;
Mukunda, Murari and Vasu dance with delight.

খেনে খেনে মুরছই পণ্ডিত কোর ।
হেরইতে সহচর সুখে ভেল ভোর ॥

*khene khene murachai paṇḍita kora |*
*heraite sahacara sukhe bhela bhora ||*

*Word for word:* khene khene — again and again; murachhai — He swoons; pandita kora — in the Pandita's (Gadadhara's) arms; heraite sahachara — seeing it, the companions; sukhe bhela bhora — are lost in joy

**14.4.** Again and again He swoons in the Pandita's arms;
seeing it, the companions are lost in joy.

নিকুঞ্জ-মন্দির পহু কয়ল বিথার ।
ভূমে পড়ি কহে কাঁহা মুরলী হামার ॥

*nikuñja-mandira pahu kayala bithāra |*
*bhūme paṛi kahe kām̐hā muralī hāmāra ||*

*Word for word:* nikunja-mandira — a bower-temple; pahu kayala bithara — the Lord laid out; bhume pari — falling to the ground; kahe — He says; kanha murali hamara — where is My flute?

**14.5.** The Lord laid out a bower-temple,
falls to the ground and says: "Where is My flute?

কাঁহা গোবর্ধন যমুনাক কূল ।
কাঁহা মালতী যূথী চম্পক ফুল ॥

*kām̐hā gobardhana yamunāka kūla |*
*kām̐hā mālatī yūthī campaka phula ||*

*Word for word:* kanha gobardhana — where is Govardhana?; yamunaka kula — the Yamuna's bank?; kanha malati yuthi champaka phula — where the malati, yuthi and champaka flowers?

**14.6.** Where is Govardhana, where the Yamuna's bank?
Where are the malati, yuthi and champaka flowers?"

শিবানন্দ কহে পহু শুনি রসবাণী ।
যাঁহা পহু গদাধর তাঁহা রসখানি ॥

*śibānanda kahe pahu śuni rasabāṇī |*
*yām̐hā pahu gadādhara tām̐hā rasakhāni ||*

*Word for word:* shivananda kahe — says Shivananda; pahu shuni rasabani — hearing the Lord's words of rasa; yanha pahu gadadhara — where the Lord and Gadadhara are; tanha rasa-khani — there is a mine of rasa

**14.7.** Says Shivananda, hearing the Lord's words full of rasa:
where the Lord and Gadadhara are, there is a mine of rasa.

[^01-21]: Shivananda Sena of Kumarahatta was the father of Kavi Karnapura and later led the Gaudiya devotees to Puri every
year (CC Madhya 1, Antya 12). The pada is known from BR (wave 12) and GPT; it is not in PK. Its historical value,
according to Majumdar, is the list of the companions of the Navadvipa kirtanas; it is also confirmed by Vasu Ghosha's
pada on Holi with Gadadhara (BR, pp. 942–943). Holi (dola) is the spring festival of colours at the full moon of
Phalguna, the day of the Lord's appearance.
[^01-22]: "The beloved" (rasavati nari) is Gadadhara in Radha's mood (GGD 147: Gadadhara Pandita is Radha), and the Lord is
in Krishna's mood. This is the spiritual lila of Radha and Krishna remembered by the Lord and His companion, not a
worldly feeling.

## 15. Govinda Ghosha — "prāṇera mukunda he ki āji śunilum̐ ācambita…" (PK 1606)
*Lila: the first news that the Lord will leave Navadvipa; Gadadhara runs to Mukunda. According to Majumdar, late January
1510, a few days before the sannyasa. Raga pahida.*[^01-23]

প্রাণের মুকুন্দ হে কি আজি শুনিলুঁ আচম্বিত ।
কহিতে পরাণ যায় মুখে নাহি বাহিরায়
শ্রীগৌরাঙ্গ ছাড়িবে নবদ্বীপ ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*prāṇera mukunda he ki āji śunilum̐ ācambita |*
*kahite parāṇa yāya mukhe nāhi bāhirāya*
*śrīgaurāṅga chāṛibe nabadvīpa || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* pranera mukunda he — O Mukunda, dear as life; ki aji shunilun achambita — what have I suddenly heard today!; kahite parana yaya — to say it, life departs; mukhe nahi bahiraya — it will not leave the lips; shri-gauranga chharibe nabadvipa — Sri Gauranga will leave Navadvipa

**15.1.** *(Refrain)* "O Mukunda, dear as life! What have I suddenly heard today!
To say it, life departs; it will not leave my lips:
Sri Gauranga will leave Navadvipa!

ইহা ত না জানি মোরা সকালে মিলিলুঁ গোরা
অবনত-মাথে আছে বসি ।
নিঝরে নয়ান ঝরে বুক বাহি ধারা পড়ে
মলিন হৈয়াছে মুখ-শশী ॥

*ihā ta nā jāni morā sakāle mililum̐ gorā*
*abanata-māthe āche basi |*
*nijhare nayāna jhare buka bāhi dhārā paṛe*
*malina haiyāche mukha-śaśī ||*

*Word for word:* iha ta na jani mora — this we did not know; sakale mililun gora — in the morning I came to Gora; abanata-mathe achhe basi — He sits with bowed head; nijhare nayana jhare — tears stream from His eyes; buka bahi dhara pade — streams run down His chest; malina haiyachhe mukha-shashi — the moon of His face has grown pale

**15.2.** We knew nothing. In the morning I came to Gora —
He sits with bowed head;
tears stream from His eyes and run in rivulets down His chest,
the moon of His face has grown pale.

দেখিয়া তখনি প্রাণ সদা করে আনছান
সুধাইতে নাহি অবসর ।
ক্ষণেকে সম্বিত হৈল তবে মুঞি নিবেদিল
শুনিয়া দিলেন এ উত্তর ॥

*dekhiyā takhani prāṇa sadā kare ānachāna*
*sudhāite nāhi abasara |*
*kṣaṇeke sambita haila tabe muñi nibedila*
*śuniyā dilena e uttara ||*

*Word for word:* dekhiya takhani — seeing it, at once; prana sada kare anachhana — my heart was in turmoil; sudhaite nahi abasara — there was no chance to ask; kshaneke sambita haila — after a moment He came to Himself; tabe muni nibedila — then I asked; shuniya dilena e uttara — hearing, He gave this answer

**15.3.** Seeing this, my heart was at once in turmoil,
but there was no chance to ask.
After a moment He came to Himself; then I asked —
and, hearing me, He gave this answer.

আমি ত বিবশ হৈয়া তাঁরে কিছু না কহিয়া
ধাইয়া আইলুঁ তুয়া পাশ ।
এই ত কহিলুঁ আমি যে করিতে পার তুমি
মোর নাহি জীবনের আশ ॥

*āmi ta bibaśa haiyā tām̐re kichu nā kahiyā*
*dhāiyā āilum̐ tuyā pāśa |*
*ei ta kahilum̐ āmi ye karite pāra tumi*
*mora nāhi jībanera āśa ||*

*Word for word:* ami ta bibasha haiya — I, overwhelmed; tanre kichhu na kahiya — saying nothing to Him; dhaiya ailun tuya pasha — ran to you; ei ta kahilun ami — so I have told you; ye karite para tumi — do what you can; mora nahi jibanera asha — I have no hope of living

**15.4.** And I, overwhelmed, saying nothing to Him,
ran to you.
So I have told you; do what you can —
I have no hope of living."

শুনিয়া মুকুন্দ কান্দে হিয়া থির নাহি বান্ধে
গদাধরের বদন হেরিয়া ।
এ গোবিন্দ ঘোষে কয় ইহা যেন নাহি হয়
তবে মুঞি যাইমু মরিয়া ॥

*śuniyā mukunda kānde hiyā thira nāhi bāndhe*
*gadādharera badana heriyā |*
*e gobinda ghoṣe kaya ihā yena nāhi haya*
*tabe muñi yāimu mariyā ||*

*Word for word:* shuniya mukunda kande — hearing it, Mukunda weeps; hiya thira nahi bandhe — his heart finds no rest; gadadharera badana heriya — looking at Gadadhara's face; e gobinda ghoshe kaya — says this Govinda Ghosha; iha yena nahi haya — may this not happen!; tabe muni yaimu mariya — or else I shall die

**15.5.** Hearing this, Mukunda weeps, his heart finds no rest,
as he looks into Gadadhara's face.
Says this Govinda Ghosha: may this not happen!
Or else I shall die.

[^01-23]: In PK the pada is headed "spoken by Pandita Gosvami", i.e. by Gadadhara Pandita: in the pada he tells Mukunda Datta
of the Lord's words, and Mukunda weeps looking into his face; the signature is Govinda Ghosha's. Majumdar takes the
heading as a tradition going back to Gadadhara himself and dates the pada to the end of January 1510. In PK it opens the
section "separation to come". Cf. CB Madhya 26, Murari 2.18.17–23: the devotees learn of the Lord's decision to take
sannyasa.

## 16. Govinda Ghosha — "hede re nadīyābāsī kāra mukha cāo…" (PK 1622)
*Lila: the day the Lord leaves Navadvipa for sannyasa. According to Majumdar, written on that very day (1510). Raga
suhai.*[^01-24]

হেদে রে নদীয়াবাসী কার মুখ চাও ।
বাহু পসারিয়া গোরাচাঁদেরে ফিরাও ॥

*hede re nadīyābāsī kāra mukha cāo |*
*bāhu pasāriyā gorācām̐dere phirāo ||*

*Word for word:* hede re nadiya-basi — O people of Nadia!; kara mukha chao — whose face are you looking to?; bahu pasariya — stretching out your arms; gorachandere phirao — bring Gorachand back

**16.1.** O people of Nadia! Whose face are you looking to?
Stretch out your arms — bring Gorachand back!

তো-সভারে কে আর করিবে নিজ কোরে ।
কে যাচিয়া দিবে প্রেম দেখিয়া কাতরে ॥

*to-sabhāre ke āra karibe nija kore |*
*ke yāciyā dibe prema dekhiyā kātare ||*

*Word for word:* to-sabhare — all of you; ke ara karibe nija kore — who else will take into his arms; ke yachiya dibe prema — who will offer prema unasked; dekhiya katare — seeing the afflicted

**16.2.** Who else will take you all into His arms?
Who, seeing the afflicted, will offer them prema unasked?

কি শেল হিয়ায় হায় কি শেল হিয়ায় ।
পরাণ-পুতলী নবদ্বীপ ছাড়ি যায় ॥

*ki śela hiyāya hāya ki śela hiyāya |*
*parāṇa-putalī nabadvīpa chāṛi yāya ||*

*Word for word:* ki shela hiyaya — what a spear in the heart!; haya — alas; parana-putali — the darling of our life; nabadvipa chhari yaya — is leaving Navadvipa

**16.3.** What a spear in the heart, alas, what a spear in the heart!
The darling of our life is leaving Navadvipa.

আর না যাইব মোরা গৌরাঙ্গের পাশ ।
আর না করিব মোরা কীর্তন-বিলাস ॥

*āra nā yāiba morā gaurāṅgera pāśa |*
*āra nā kariba morā kīrtana-bilāsa ||*

*Word for word:* ara na yaiba mora — no more shall we go; gaurangera pasha — to Gauranga; ara na kariba mora — no more shall we; kirtana-bilasa — delight in kirtana

**16.4.** No more shall we go to Gauranga,
no more shall we delight in kirtana.

কান্দয়ে ভকতগণ বুক বিদরিয়া ।
পাষাণ গোবিন্দ ঘোষ না যায় মরিয়া ॥

*kāndaye bhakatagaṇa buka bidariyā |*
*pāṣāṇa gobinda ghoṣa nā yāya mariyā ||*

*Word for word:* kandaye bhakatagana — the devotees weep; buka bidariya — their hearts breaking; pashana gobinda ghosha — stony Govinda Ghosha; na yaya mariya — does not die

**16.5.** The devotees weep, their hearts breaking;
only stony Govinda Ghosha does not die.

[^01-24]: In PK the pada stands in the section "words of the devotees of Navadvipa in separation from Gaura". The Lord's
leaving home at night at the end of Magha 1510 and crossing the Ganga towards Katwa: CB Madhya 28, CC Adi 17, Murari
3.1.6–7.

## 17. Vamshi(vadana) — "āra nā heriba prasara kapāle…" (PK 1855)
*Lila: Navadvipa's grief after the sannyasa; the weeping of Shachi and Vishnupriya. According to Majumdar, soon after the
sannyasa (1510). Raga gandhara.*[^01-25]

আর না হেরিব প্রসর কপালে
অলকা-তিলক-কাচ ।
আর না হেরিব সোনার কমলে
নয়ন-খঞ্জন নাচ ॥

*āra nā heriba prasara kapāle*
*alakā-tilaka-kāca |*
*āra nā heriba sonāra kamale*
*nayana-khañjana nāca ||*

*Word for word:* ara na heriba — no more shall I see; prasara kapale — on the broad brow; alaka-tilaka-kacha — the adornment of curls and tilaka; ara na heriba — no more shall I see; sonara kamale — on the golden lotus [of His face]; nayana-khanjana nacha — the dance of the wagtail eyes

**17.1.** No more shall I see on the broad brow
the adornment of curls and tilaka,
no more see on the golden lotus [of His face]
the dance of the wagtail eyes.

আর না নাচিবে শ্রীবাস-মন্দিরে
ভকত-চাতক লৈয়া ।
আর না নাচিবে আপনার ঘরে
আমরা দেখিব চাঞা ॥

*āra nā nācibe śrībāsa-mandire*
*bhakata-cātaka laiyā |*
*āra nā nācibe āpanāra ghare*
*āmarā dekhiba cāñā ||*

*Word for word:* ara na nachibe — no more will He dance; shribasa-mandire — in Srivasa's house; bhakata-chataka laiya — with His chataka-bird devotees; ara na nachibe apanara ghare — no more will He dance in His own house; amara dekhiba chana — for us to watch

**17.2.** No more will He dance in Srivasa's house
with His chataka-bird devotees,
no more will He dance in His own house
for us to gaze at Him.

আর কি দুভাই নিমাই নিতাই
নাচিবেন এক ঠাঞি ।
নিমাই করিয়া ফুকরি সদাই
নিমাই কোথায় নাই ॥

*āra ki dubhāi nimāi nitāi*
*nācibena eka ṭhāñi |*
*nimāi kariyā phukari sadāi*
*nimāi kothāya nāi ||*

*Word for word:* ara ki dubhai — will the two brothers ever again; nimai nitai — Nimai and Nitai; nachibena eka thani — dance together?; nimai kariya phukari sadai — I keep crying "Nimai!"; nimai kothaya nai — but Nimai is nowhere

**17.3.** Will the two brothers, Nimai and Nitai,
ever dance together again?
I keep crying, "Nimai!" —
but Nimai is nowhere.

নিদয় কেশব-ভারতী আসিয়া
মাথায় পাড়িল বাজ ।
গৌরাঙ্গ-সুন্দর না দেখি কেমনে
রহিব নদীয়া মাঝ ॥

*nidaya keśaba-bhāratī āsiyā*
*māthāya pāṛila bāja |*
*gaurāṅga-sundara nā dekhi kemane*
*rahiba nadīyā mājha ||*

*Word for word:* nidaya keshava-bharati — pitiless Keshava Bharati; asiya — coming; mathaya parila baja — brought down a thunderbolt on our heads; gauranga-sundara na dekhi — not seeing beautiful Gauranga; kemane rahiba nadiya majha — how shall I stay in Nadia?

**17.4.** Pitiless Keshava Bharati came
and brought down a thunderbolt on our heads.
How, not seeing beautiful Gauranga,
shall I stay on in Nadia?

কেবা হেন জন আনিবে এখন
আমার গৌর রায় ।
শাশুড়ী বধূর রোদন শুনিতে
বংশী গড়াগড়ি যায় ॥

*kebā hena jana ānibe ekhana*
*āmāra gaura rāya |*
*śāśuṛī badhūra rodana śunite*
*baṃśī gaṛāgaṛi yāya ||*

*Word for word:* keba hena jana — who is there; anibe ekhana — who will bring now; amara gaura raya — my Gaura Raya?; shashuri badhura rodana — the weeping of mother-in-law and daughter-in-law; shunite — hearing; vamshi garagari yaya — Vamshi rolls on the ground

**17.5.** Who is there now to bring back
my Gaura Raya?
Hearing the weeping of mother-in-law and daughter-in-law,
Vamshi rolls in the dust.[^01-26]

[^01-25]: The signature is "Vamshi". The PK index ascribes the pada to Vamshidasa; Majumdar distinguishes Vamshidasa (a disciple
of Srinivasa Acharya, 17th century) from Vamshivadana and assigns this pada to Vamshivadana, who looked after Shachi and
Vishnupriya — hence the poet's grief at hearing "the weeping of mother-in-law and daughter-in-law". One manuscript
(according to GPT) has a signature of Vasu Ghosha, so the attribution is not beyond doubt. Keshava Bharati was the
sannyasi who gave the Lord sannyasa at Katwa; "pitiless" is the reproach of those who love, not a condemnation (cf. CB
Madhya 28).
[^01-26]: The mother-in-law and daughter-in-law are Shachi and Vishnupriya, the Lord's second wife.

## 18. Ramananda (Vasu) — "pāpī māghe pahum̐ kayala sannyāsa…" (PK 1711; GPT1, p. 390)
*Lila: longing for the Lord in the spring of 1510, soon after the sannyasa. According to Majumdar, written a few days
after the sannyasa. Raga suhai; Vrajabuli.*[^01-27]

পাপী মাঘে পহুঁ কয়ল সন্ন্যাস ।
তবহিঁ গেও মঝু জীবন-আশ ॥

*pāpī māghe pahum̐ kayala sannyāsa |*
*tabahim̐ geo majhu jībana-āśa ||*

*Word for word:* papi maghe — in the accursed month of Magha; pahun kayala sannyasa — my Lord took sannyasa; tabahin geo — then went; majhu jibana-asha — my hope of life

**18.1.** In the accursed month of Magha my Lord took sannyasa —
and then my hope of life departed too.

দিনে দিনে খিণ তনু ঝরয়ে নয়ান ।
গোরা বিনে কত দিন ধরিব পরাণ ॥

*dine dine khiṇa tanu jharaye nayāna |*
*gorā bine kata dina dhariba parāṇa ||*

*Word for word:* dine dine khina tanu — day by day my body wastes; jharaye nayana — my eyes stream; gora bine — without Gora; kata dina dhariba parana — how many days shall I keep my life?

**18.2.** Day by day my body wastes, my eyes stream;
how many days without Gora shall I keep my life?

অবহুঁ বসন্ত সবহুঁ সুখময় ।
এ ছার কঠিন প্রাণ বাহির না হয় ॥

*abahum̐ basanta sabahum̐ sukhamaya |*
*e chāra kaṭhina prāṇa bāhira nā haya ||*

*Word for word:* abahun basanta — now it is spring; sabahun sukhamaya — all are happy; e chhara kathina prana — this wretched, hard life; bahira na haya — does not leave [the body]

**18.3.** Now it is spring, and all are happy —
yet this wretched, hard life will not leave me.

যত যত পিরিতি কয়ল পহুঁ মোর ।
সোঙরিতে জিউ অব কণ্ঠহিঁ ডোর ॥

*yata yata piriti kayala pahum̐ mora |*
*soṅarite jiu aba kaṇṭhahim̐ ḍora ||*

*Word for word:* yata yata piriti — all the love; kayala pahun mora — my Lord showed; songarite — remembering [it]; jiu aba kanthahin dora — my life now hangs by a thread at my throat

**18.4.** All the love my Lord showed me! —
I remember it, and my life hangs by a thread at my throat.[^01-28]

কহে রামানন্দ সেই মোর প্রাণনাথ ।
কবে নিরখিব আর গদাধর সাথ ॥

*kahe rāmānanda sei mora prāṇanātha |*
*kabe nirakhiba āra gadādhara sātha ||*

*Word for word:* kahe ramananda — says Ramananda; sei mora prananatha — He is the lord of my life; kabe nirakhiba ara — when shall I see [Him] again; gadadhara satha — together with Gadadhara?

**18.5.** Says Ramananda: He is the lord of my life.
When shall I see Him again beside Gadadhara?

[^01-27]: The signature is "Ramananda". Majumdar (who knew the pada only from GPT) argues that this is not Ramananda Raya (who
did not know the Lord before the sannyasa and could not pine for Him beside Gadadhara) but Vasu Ramananda of Kulinagrama,
a descendant of Maladhara Vasu, Gunaraja Khan (CC Madhya 15). His argument for the date: "now it is spring" — the pada was made in
Phalguna–Chaitra, some weeks after the sannyasa taken at the end of Magha (January–February 1510). The reading "māghe"
("in Magha") is given by PK and GPT1; Majumdar (in the OCR of his book) has "māthe". In PK the pada is a gaura-chandrika to
the section "separation in spring".
[^01-28]: The reading "kaṇṭhahim̐ ḍora" follows the PK scan; in GPT the line is corrupt. The sense: life "has risen to the
throat" (is about to leave the body).

## 19. Shivananda Sena — "dayāmaya gaurahari naidyā-līlā sāṅga kari…" (GPT1, p. 382)
*Lila: from Shantipura the Lord leaves for Puri and tells the devotees of Gauda to come to Him once a year. According to
Majumdar, written right after the Lord's departure (1510). Raga mangala.*[^01-29]

দয়াময় গৌরহরি নৈদ্যা-লীলা সাঙ্গ করি
হায় হায় কি কপাল মন্দ ।
গেলা নাথ নীলাচলে এ দাসেরে একা ফেলে
না ঘুচিল মোর ভববন্ধ ॥

*dayāmaya gaurahari naidyā-līlā sāṅga kari*
*hāya hāya ki kapāla manda |*
*gelā nātha nīlācale e dāsere ekā phele*
*nā ghucila mora bhababandha ||*

*Word for word:* dayamaya gaurahari — merciful Gaurahari; naidya-lila sanga kari — having ended the Nadia-lila; haya haya — alas, alas; ki kapala manda — what ill fate!; gela natha nilachale — the Lord went to Nilachala; e dasere eka phele — leaving this servant alone; na ghuchila mora bhababandha — my worldly bonds were not cut

**19.1.** Merciful Gaurahari, having ended the Nadia-lila —
alas, alas, what ill fate! —
my Lord has gone to Nilachala, leaving this servant alone:
my worldly bonds were not cut.

আদেশ করিলা যাহা নিচয় পালিব তাহা
কিন্তু একা কিরূপে রহিব ।
পুত্র পরিবার যত লাগিবে বিষের মত
তোমা বিনা কি মতে গোঙাব ॥

*ādeśa karilā yāhā nicaya pāliba tāhā*
*kintu ekā kirūpe rahiba |*
*putra paribāra yata lāgibe biṣera mata*
*tomā binā ki mate goṅāba ||*

*Word for word:* adesha karila yaha — what You have commanded; nichaya paliba taha — I shall surely carry out; kintu eka kirupe rahiba — but how shall I live alone?; putra paribara yata — sons and all the family; lagibe bishera mata — will be like poison to me; toma vina ki mate gongaba — how shall I pass my days without You?

**19.2.** What You have commanded I shall surely carry out,
but how shall I live alone?
My sons and all my family will be like poison to me:
how shall I pass my days without You?

গৌড়ীয় যাত্রিক সনে বৎসরান্তে দরশনে
কহিলা যাইতে নীলাচলে ।
কিরূপে সহিয়া রব সম্বৎসর কাটাইব
যুগশত জ্ঞান করি তিলে ॥

*gauṛīya yātrika sane batsarānte daraśane*
*kahilā yāite nīlācale |*
*kirūpe sahiyā raba sambatsara kāṭāiba*
*yugaśata jñāna kari tile ||*

*Word for word:* gaudiya yatrika sane — with the pilgrims from Gauda; batsarante darashane — at the year's end, for darshana; kahila yaite nilachale — You told me to come to Nilachala; kirupe sahiya raba — how shall I endure; sambatsara kataiba — how shall I pass a year; yugashata jnana kari tile — when a moment seems a hundred yugas

**19.3.** You told me to come to Nilachala
with the pilgrims of Gauda at the year's end, for darshana.
How shall I endure, how pass a whole year,
when a moment seems a hundred yugas?

হও প্রভু কৃপাবান্ কর অনুমতি দান
নিতি নিতি হেরি পদদ্বন্দ্ব ।
যদি না আদেশ কর অহে প্রভু বিশ্বম্ভর
আত্মঘাতী হবে শিবানন্দ ॥

*hao prabhu kṛpābān kara anumati dāna*
*niti niti heri padadvandva |*
*yadi nā ādeśa kara ahe prabhu biśvambhara*
*ātmaghātī habe śibānanda ||*

*Word for word:* hao prabhu kripaban — be merciful, Lord; kara anumati dana — grant permission; niti niti heri padadvandva — that I may see Your feet every day; yadi na adesha kara — if You do not command it; ahe prabhu vishvambhara — O Lord Vishvambhara; atmaghati habe shivananda — Shivananda will take his own life

**19.4.** Be merciful, Lord, grant me leave
to see Your feet every day.
If You do not command it, O Lord Vishvambhara,
Shivananda will take his own life.

[^01-29]: The pada is known only from GPT (signature "Shivananda"). Majumdar's argument: the words "my sons and all my family will be
like poison to me" and "how shall I live through the year until the next journey with the Gaudiyas" make sense only
directly after the Lord's departure from Shantipura for Puri; later, when the journeys had become a custom, they would
not have been written. The Lord's instruction to the devotees of Gauda to come to Puri every year: CC Madhya 3, CB Antya
1. "Will take his own life" is a hyperbole of separation, common in Bengali padas; cf. the devotees' threats to give up
their lives in separation from the Lord in CC (Madhya 3).

## 20. Narahari (Sarakara) — "sonā śatabāna jini gaurāṅga āmāra…" (PK 1729)
*Lila: the first chaturmasya after the sannyasa — the devotees do not know where the Lord is. According to Majumdar,
written during the first chaturmasya (1510). Raga suhai.*[^01-30]

সোনা শতবান জিনি গৌরাঙ্গ আমার ।
কি হয়ে চামর সে না কুন্তলের ভার ॥

*sonā śatabāna jini gaurāṅga āmāra |*
*ki haye cāmara se nā kuntalera bhāra ||*

*Word for word:* sona shatabana jini — surpassing gold refined a hundred times; gauranga amara — my Gauranga; ki haye chamara — what is a chamara whisk; se na kuntalera bhara — beside that mass of His hair

**20.1.** My Gauranga outshines gold refined a hundred times —
what is a chamara whisk beside that thick mass of His hair?

কি লাগিয়া মুড়াইলা গেলা কোন দেশে ।
কার ঘরে রহিলেন ইহ চতুর্মাসে ॥

*ki lāgiyā muṛāilā gelā kona deśe |*
*kāra ghare rahilena iha caturmāse ||*

*Word for word:* ki lagiya muraila — why did He shave [His head]; gela kona deshe — to what land has He gone?; kara ghare rahilena — in whose house has He stayed; iha chaturmase — this chaturmasya?

**20.2.** Why did He shave His head, to what land has He gone?
In whose house is He spending this chaturmasya?

সোঙরি সোঙরি হিয়া বিদরিয়া যায় ।
কোথা গেলা পরাণ-পুতলী গোরা রায় ॥

*soṅari soṅari hiyā bidariyā yāya |*
*kothā gelā parāṇa-putalī gorā rāya ||*

*Word for word:* songari songari — remembering, remembering; hiya bidariya yaya — the heart breaks; kotha gela — where has He gone; parana-putali gora raya — Gora Raya, dear as life itself?

**20.3.** I remember and remember, and my heart breaks:
where has Gora Raya gone, dear as life itself?

কান্দয়ে ভকতগণ ছাড়য়ে নিশ্বাস ।
ধৈরজ ধরিতে নারে নরহরি দাস ॥

*kāndaye bhakatagaṇa chāṛaye niśvāsa |*
*dhairaja dharite nāre narahari dāsa ||*

*Word for word:* kandaye bhakatagana — the devotees weep; chharaye nishvasa — and heave sighs; dhairaja dharite nare — cannot keep patience; narahari dasa — Narahari Dasa

**20.4.** The devotees weep and heave sighs;
Narahari Dasa cannot keep his patience.

[^01-30]: The signature is "Narahari Dasa". Narahari Sarakara Thakura of Shrikhanda was a companion of the Lord and a singer of
His moods; Majumdar assigns to him the padas in plain Bengali known from PK (not only from GPT). In PK the pada is a
gaura-chandrika to the section "separation in the rainy season"; Majumdar dates it to the first chaturmasya after the
sannyasa (1510), when the Lord was travelling in the South. According to CC (Madhya 9) He spent that chaturmasya at
Shrirangam, in the house of Venkata Bhatta.

## 21. Shivananda Sena — "jaya jaya paṇḍita gosāñi…" (PK 2355)
*Lila: Gadadhara Pandita gives up his vow to live in the Kshetra and his service of Gopinatha to follow the Lord to Gauda
(1514). According to Majumdar, composed at that very time. Raga patamanjari.*[^01-31]

জয় জয় পণ্ডিত গোসাঞি ।
যার কৃপা-বলে সে চৈতন্য-গুণ গাই ॥

*jaya jaya paṇḍita gosāñi |*
*yāra kṛpā-bale se caitanya-guṇa gāi ||*

*Word for word:* jaya jaya — glory, glory; pandita gosani — to Pandita Gosani (Gadadhara)!; yara kripa-bale — by the power of whose mercy; se chaitanya-guna gai — I sing Chaitanya's glories

**21.1.** Glory, glory to Pandita Gosani!
By the power of his mercy I sing Chaitanya's glories.

হেন সে গৌরাঙ্গচন্দ্রে যাহার পিরিতি ।
গদাধর-প্রাণনাথ যাহে নাম-খ্যাতি ॥

*hena se gaurāṅgacandre yāhāra piriti |*
*gadādhara-prāṇanātha yāhe nāma-khyāti ||*

*Word for word:* hena se gaurangachandre — for that Gaurangachandra; yahara piriti — whose love [is such] that; gadadhara-prananatha — "Lord of Gadadhara's life"; yahe nama-khyati — by that name He became famed

**21.2.** So does he love Gaurangachandra
that He is famed by the name "Lord of Gadadhara's life".

গৌরগত-প্রাণ প্রেম কে বুঝিতে পারে ।
ক্ষেত্র-বাস কৃষ্ণ-সেবা যার লাগি ছাড়ে ॥

*gauragata-prāṇa prema ke bujhite pāre |*
*kṣetra-bāsa kṛṣṇa-sebā yāra lāgi chāṛe ||*

*Word for word:* gauragata-prana — whose life is given to Gaura; prema — [his] love; ke bujhite pare — who can understand?; kshetra-basa — residence in the Kshetra (Puri); krishna-seba — service to Krishna; yara lagi chhare — for whose sake he gave up

**21.3.** Who can understand the love of one whose life is given to Gaura,
who for His sake gave up life in the Kshetra and the service of Krishna?[^01-32]

গদাইর গৌরাঙ্গ গৌরাঙ্গের গদাধর ।
শ্রীরাম জানকী যেন এক-কলেবর ॥

*gadāira gaurāṅga gaurāṅgera gadādhara |*
*śrīrāma jānakī yena eka-kalebara ||*

*Word for word:* gadaira gauranga — Gadai's Gauranga; gaurangera gadadhara — Gauranga's Gadadhara; shrirama janaki — Sri Rama and Janaki; yena eka-kalebara — as if one body

**21.4.** Gadai's Gauranga, Gauranga's Gadadhara:
like Sri Rama and Janaki — one body.

যেন এক-প্রাণ রাধা বৃন্দাবন-চন্দ ।
তেন গৌর গদাধর প্রেমের তরঙ্গ ॥

*yena eka-prāṇa rādhā bṛndābana-canda |*
*tena gaura gadādhara premera taraṅga ||*

*Word for word:* yena eka-prana — as one soul; radha vrindavana-chanda — Radha and the Moon of Vrindavana; tena gaura gadadhara — so are Gaura and Gadadhara; premera taranga — waves of prema

**21.5.** As Radha and the Moon of Vrindavana are one soul,
so Gaura and Gadadhara are waves of one prema.

কহে শিবানন্দ পহু যার অনুরাগে ।
শ্যাম-তনু গৌর হৈয়া প্রেম মাগে ॥

*kahe śibānanda pahu yāra anurāge |*
*śyāma-tanu gaura haiyā prema māge ||*

*Word for word:* kahe shivananda — says Shivananda; pahu yara anurage — the Lord, in love for whom (Radha); shyama-tanu — dark of body; gaura haiya — becoming golden; prema mage — begs for prema

**21.6.** Says Shivananda: in love for Her the Lord,
dark of body, became golden and begs for prema.[^01-33]

[^01-31]: Gadadhara Pandita (Gadai) took in Puri the vow of kshetra-sannyasa (never to leave the Kshetra) and served the
Deity of Tota-Gopinatha. When in 1514 the Lord set out for Gauda (on His way to Vrindavana), Gadadhara followed Him,
abandoning both vow and service, and only at Cuttack did the Lord persuade him to go back — CC Madhya 16. Majumdar's
argument: later, knowing from CC that the Lord sent Gadadhara back, no one would have written "for His sake he gave up
life in the Kshetra" — the pada is contemporary with the event (1514/15).
[^01-32]: "The service of Krishna" is the service of the Deity Gopinatha in Puri.
[^01-33]: "In love for Her" — for Radha: Krishna (Shyama, the dark one) took on Radha's golden form to taste Her love.
Majumdar sees in the last verse an echo of Svarupa Damodara's teaching (CC Adi 1.5–6, 4). Gadadhara is Radha (GGD 147).

## 22. Vasu Ghosha — "ājukāra svapana-kathā śuna lo mālinī sai…" (BR, pp. 982–983)
*Lila: Shachi tells Malini her dream: Nimai, unable to stay in Nilachala, came home. According to Majumdar, an
eyewitness's pada from the years of separation (about 1514/15). Raga kamoda.*[^01-34]

আজুকার স্বপন-কথা শুন লো মালিনী সই
নিমাই আসিয়াছিল ঘরে ।
আঙ্গিনাতে দাঁড়াইয়া গৃহ পানে চাঞা চাঞা
মা বৈলা ডাকিয়াছিল মোরে ॥

*ājukāra svapana-kathā śuna lo mālinī sai*
*nimāi āsiyāchila ghare |*
*āṅgināte dām̐ṛāiyā gṛha pāne cāñā cāñā*
*mā bailā ḍākiyāchila more ||*

*Word for word:* ajukara svapana-katha — the tale of today's dream; shuna lo malini sai — listen, friend Malini; nimai asiyachhila ghare — Nimai came home; anginate daraiya — standing in the courtyard; griha pane chana chana — gazing and gazing at the house; ma baila dakiyachhila more — He called me, "Mother!"

**22.1.** Listen, friend Malini, to the dream I had today:
Nimai came home.
Standing in the courtyard, gazing and gazing at the house,
He called me: "Mother!"

গৃহেতে শয়নে ছিনু অচেতনে বাহির হনু
নিমাইর গলার সাড়া পাঞা ।
মায়ের চরণধূলি নিল নিমাই শিরে তুলি
মা বোলে কান্দিয়া কান্দিয়া ॥

*gṛhete śayane chinu acetane bāhira hanu*
*nimāira galāra sāṛā pāñā |*
*māyera caraṇadhūli nila nimāi śire tuli*
*mā bole kāndiyā kāndiyā ||*
