*Word for word:* grihete shayane chhinu — I was lying in the house; achetane bahira hanu — beside myself, I came out; nimaira galara sara pana — hearing Nimai's voice; mayera charana-dhuli — the dust of his mother's feet; nila nimai shire tuli — Nimai took and put on His head; ma bole kandiya kandiya — weeping and weeping, says "Mother"

**22.2.** I was lying in the house — and, beside myself, came out,
hearing Nimai's voice.
Nimai put the dust of His mother's feet on His head,
and weeps and weeps: "Mother!"

তোর প্রেমে বন্দী হৈয়া বেড়াইনু ভরমিয়া
রহিতে নারিনু নীলাচলে ।
তোরে দেখিবার তরে আইনু নদীয়াপুরে
কান্দিতে কান্দিতে ইহা বোলে ॥

*tora preme bandī haiyā beṛāinu bharamiyā*
*rahite nārinu nīlācale |*
*tore dekhibāra tare āinu nadīyāpure*
*kāndite kāndite ihā bole ||*

*Word for word:* tora preme bandi haiya — captive to your love; berainu bharamiya — I wandered about; rahite narinu nilachale — I could not stay in Nilachala; tore dekhibara tare — to see you; ainu nadiyapure — I came to Nadia; kandite kandite iha bole — weeping, He says this

**22.3.** "Captive to your love, I wandered about —
I could not stay in Nilachala.
To see you I have come to Nadia" —
so He says, weeping.

আইস মোর বাছা বুলি হিয়ার উপরে তুলি
হেন বেলে নিদ দূরে গেল ।
পুন না দেখিয়া তারে পরাণ কেমন করে
কান্দিয়া রজনী পোহাইল ॥

*āisa mora bāchā buli hiyāra upare tuli*
*hena bele nida dūre gela |*
*puna nā dekhiyā tāre parāṇa kemana kare*
*kāndiyā rajanī pohāila ||*

*Word for word:* aisa mora bachha buli — saying "Come, my child!"; hiyara upare tuli — I lifted Him to my breast; hena bele — at that moment; nida dure gela — sleep went away; puna na dekhiya tare — not seeing Him again; parana kemana kare — how my heart aches!; kandiya rajani pohaila — the night passed in tears

**22.4.** "Come to me, my child!" — I lifted Him to my breast —
and at that moment sleep left me.
Not seeing Him again, how my heart aches!
The night passed in tears.

কান্দিতে কান্দিতে শচী মুরছি পড়ল ক্ষিতি
মালিনী কান্দয়ে উভরায় ।
কি বলিব হায় হায় এ দুখ না সহে গায়
বাসু কেনে মরিয়া না যায় ॥

*kāndite kāndite śacī murachi paṛala kṣiti*
*mālinī kāndaye ubharāya |*
*ki baliba hāya hāya e dukha nā sahe gāya*
*bāsu kene mariyā nā yāya ||*

*Word for word:* kandite kandite shachi — weeping and weeping, Shachi; murachhi parala kshiti — fell fainting to the ground; malini kandaye ubharaya — Malini wails aloud; ki baliba haya haya — what can I say, alas!; e dukha na sahe gaya — this pain cannot be borne; basu kene mariya na yaya — why does Vasu not die?

**22.5.** Weeping and weeping, Shachi fell fainting to the ground;
Malini wails aloud.
What can I say — alas, alas! — this pain cannot be borne:
why does Vasu not die?

[^01-34]: The pada is known from BR (wave 12): Narahari Chakravarti cites it in the account of Shachi's house, to which
Nityananda comes. Majumdar values this and the next pada as testimonies which the later biographers left out, as if they
"diminished" the sannyasa. Cf. CC Antya 3: the Lord says that He comes unseen to eat what Shachi cooks. *Addendum (chapter
05):* the same pada is found in PK — no. 2270 (vol. 3, PDF p. 293, printed p. 282; 21st pallava, raga vibhasa; MS
P-R-Sa no. 2374) and in GPT1 (p. 386, no. 11, raga pahida) — signed by Vasudeva Ghosha and with a different
last stanza: "Since then my soul weeps, my heart finds no rest: what shall I do, tell me, what way is there? Says Vasudeva
Ghosha: Gauranga is yours — otherwise would you always see Him?" Stanzas 22.1–22.4 in PK have minor variants (see the full version of the book). PK 2268 "biraha-bikala māya…", which the stage-1 catalogue took for this pada (VG-138), is a pada of Premadasa.

## 23. Vasu Ghosha — "āola nadīyāra loka gaurāṅga dekhite…" (GPT1, p. 413)
*Lila: the sannyasi Chaitanya comes to Nadia (1514/15); the people of Navadvipa and Mother Shachi see Him. Raga shri.*[^01-35]

আওল নদীয়ার লোক গৌরাঙ্গ দেখিতে ।
আনন্দে আকুল চিত না পারে চলিতে ॥

*āola nadīyāra loka gaurāṅga dekhite |*
*ānande ākula cita nā pāre calite ||*

*Word for word:* aola nadiyara loka — the people of Nadia came; gauranga dekhite — to see Gauranga; anande akula chita — their hearts overwhelmed with joy; na pare chalite — they cannot walk

**23.1.** The people of Nadia came to see Gauranga:
their hearts so overwhelmed with joy they cannot walk.

চিরদিনে গোরাচাঁদের বদন দেখিয়া ।
ভুখিল চকোর আঁখি রহয়ে মাতিয়া ॥

*ciradine gorācām̐dera badana dekhiyā |*
*bhukhila cakora ām̐khi rahaye mātiyā ||*

*Word for word:* chiradine — after so long; gorachandera badana dekhiya — seeing Gorachand's face; bhukhila chakora ankhi — the hungry chakora-eyes; rahaye matiya — remain intoxicated

**23.2.** Seeing Gorachand's face after so long,
their hungry chakora-eyes are intoxicated.

আনন্দে ভকতগণ হেরিয়া বিভোর ।
জননী ধাইয়া গোরাচাঁদে করে কোর ॥

*ānande bhakatagaṇa heriyā bibhora |*
*jananī dhāiyā gorācām̐de kare kora ||*

*Word for word:* anande bhakatagana — the devotees, in joy; heriya bibhora — are lost in gazing; janani dhaiya — the mother, running up; gorachande kare kora — embraces Gorachand

**23.3.** The devotees are lost in joy, gazing at Him;
the mother runs up and embraces Gorachand.

মরণ-শরীরে যেন পাইল পরাণ ।
গৌরাঙ্গ নদীয়াপুরে বাসু ঘোষ গান ॥

*maraṇa-śarīre yena pāila parāṇa |*
*gaurāṅga nadīyāpure bāsu ghoṣa gāna ||*

*Word for word:* marana-sharire — into a dying body; yena paila parana — as if life returned; gauranga nadiyapure — Gauranga in Nadia; basu ghosha gana — Vasu Ghosha sings

**23.4.** As if life had returned to a dying body:
Gauranga is in Nadia, sings Vasu Ghosha.

[^01-35]: The pada is in GPT (GPT1, p. 413, no. 31) and in PK — no. 1991 (vol. 3, PDF p. 190, section "The joy of all Vraja: first Navadvipa", raga shri, reading "dhāola" — "came running" for "āola" — "came"; established in chapter 4); it is not in BR. Majumdar sees in it a testimony to the coming of the sannyasi Lord
to the neighbourhood of Navadvipa on His way to Gauda (1514/15), told by Murari (4.14.3–11) and Lochana (Shesha-khanda);
CC (Madhya 1) and CB (Antya 3) speak of His stay at Kuliya, opposite Navadvipa. The chakora is a bird that, in poetic
tradition, feeds on moonlight.

## 24. Krishnadasa — "ṭhākura paṇḍitera bāṛī gorā nāce phiri phiri…" (PK 2358)
*Lila: the Lord and Nityananda at Ambika with Gauridasa Pandita; Gauridasa begs Them to stay, and the Lord tells him to
serve Their Deities. According to Majumdar, a contemporary testimony that the worship of the Lord's Deity began in His
lifetime. Raga bhatiyari.*[^01-36]

ঠাকুর পণ্ডিতের বাড়ী গোরা নাচে ফিরি ফিরি
নিত্যানন্দ বলে হরি হরি ।
কান্দি গৌরীদাস বলে পড়ি প্রভুর পদ-তলে
কভু না ছাড়িবে মোর বাড়ী ॥

*ṭhākura paṇḍitera bāṛī gorā nāce phiri phiri*
*nityānanda bale hari hari |*
*kāndi gaurīdāsa bale paṛi prabhura pada-tale*
*kabhu nā chāṛibe mora bāṛī ||*

*Word for word:* thakura panditera bari — in Thakura Pandita's house; gora nache phiri phiri — Gora dances, whirling round; nityananda bale hari hari — Nityananda cries "Hari, Hari!"; kandi gauridasa bale — weeping, Gauridasa says; pari prabhura pada-tale — falling at the Lord's feet; kabhu na chharibe mora bari — "Never leave my house!"

**24.1.** In Thakura Pandita's house Gora dances, whirling round;
Nityananda cries, "Hari, Hari!"
Weeping, Gauridasa falls at the Lord's feet and says:
"Never leave my house!

আমার বচন রাখ অম্বিকানগরে থাক
এই নিবেদন তুয়া পায় ।
যদি ছাড়ি যাবে তুমি নিশ্চয় মরিব আমি
রহিব সে নিরখিয়া কায় ॥

*āmāra bacana rākha ambikānagare thāka*
*ei nibedana tuyā pāya |*
*yadi chāṛi yābe tumi niścaya mariba āmi*
*rahiba se nirakhiyā kāya ||*

*Word for word:* amara bachana rakha — grant my request; ambika-nagare thaka — stay in Ambika; ei nibedana tuya paya — this is my plea at Your feet; yadi chhari yabe tumi — if You leave; nishchaya mariba ami — I shall surely die; rahiba se nirakhiya kaya — looking at whom shall I live?

**24.2.** Grant my request — stay in Ambika:
this is my plea at Your feet.
If You go away, I shall surely die:
looking at whom shall I live then?

তোমরা যে দুটি ভাই থাক মোর এই ঠাঞি
তবে সভার হয় পরিত্রাণ ।
পুন নিবেদন করি না ছাড়িহ গৌরহরি
তবে জানি পতিত-পাবন ॥

*tomarā ye duṭi bhāi thāka mora ei ṭhāñi*
*tabe sabhāra haya paritrāṇa |*
*puna nibedana kari nā chāṛiha gaurahari*
*tabe jāni patita-pābana ||*

*Word for word:* tomara ye duti bhai — you two brothers; thaka mora ei thani — stay here with me; tabe sabhara haya paritrana — then all will be delivered; puna nibedana kari — again I pray; na chhariha gaurahari — do not leave [me], Gaurahari; tabe jani patita-pabana — then I shall know You are the saviour of the fallen

**24.3.** If You two brothers stay here with me,
then everyone will be delivered.
Again I pray: do not leave me, Gaurahari —
then I shall know that You are the saviour of the fallen."

প্রভু কহে গৌরীদাস ছাড়হ এমত আশ
প্রতিমূর্তি সেবা করি দেখ ।
তাহাতে আছিয়ে আমি নিশ্চয় জানিহ তুমি
সত্য মোর এই বাক্য রাখ ॥

*prabhu kahe gaurīdāsa chāṛaha emata āśa*
*pratimūrti sebā kari dekha |*
*tāhāte āchiye āmi niścaya jāniha tumi*
*satya mora ei bākya rākha ||*

*Word for word:* prabhu kahe gauridasa — the Lord says, "Gauridasa!; chharaha emata asha — give up such a wish; pratimurti seba kari dekha — serve [My] image and see; tahate achhiye ami — I am present in it; nishchaya janiha tumi — know this for certain; satya mora ei bakya rakha — keep this true word of Mine"

**24.4.** The Lord says: "Gauridasa, give up such a wish:
serve My Deity and you will see —
I am present in it, know this for certain;
keep this true word of Mine."

এত শুনি গৌরীদাস ছাড়ি দীর্ঘ নিশ্বাস
ফুকরি ফুকরি পুন কান্দে ।
পুন সেই দুই ভাই প্রবোধ করয়ে তায়
তবু হিয়া থির নাহি বান্ধে ॥

*eta śuni gaurīdāsa chāṛi dīrgha niśvāsa*
*phukari phukari puna kānde |*
*puna sei dui bhāi prabodha karaye tāya*
*tabu hiyā thira nāhi bāndhe ||*

*Word for word:* eta shuni gauridasa — hearing this, Gauridasa; chhari dirgha nishvasa — heaving a long sigh; phukari phukari puna kande — again weeps aloud; puna sei dui bhai — again the two brothers; prabodha karaye taya — console him; tabu hiya thira nahi bandhe — yet his heart finds no rest

**24.5.** Hearing this, Gauridasa heaved a long sigh
and again weeps aloud.
Again the two brothers console him,
yet his heart finds no rest.

কহে দীন কৃষ্ণদাস চৈতন্য-চরণে আশ
দুই ভাই রহিলা তথায় ।
ঠাকুর পণ্ডিতের প্রেমে বন্দী হৈলা দুই জনে
ভকত-বৎসল তেঞি গায় ॥

*kahe dīna kṛṣṇadāsa caitanya-caraṇe āśa*
*dui bhāi rahilā tathāya |*
*ṭhākura paṇḍitera preme bandī hailā dui jane*
*bhakata-batsala teñi gāya ||*

*Word for word:* kahe dina krishnadasa — says lowly Krishnadasa; chaitanya-charane asha — whose hope is Chaitanya's feet; dui bhai rahila tathaya — the two brothers stayed there; thakura panditera preme — by Thakura Pandita's love; bandi haila dui jane — both became captives; bhakata-batsala tenyi gaya — hence they are sung as loving to their devotees

**24.6.** Says lowly Krishnadasa, whose hope is Chaitanya's feet:
the two brothers stayed there.
Both were taken captive by Thakura Pandita's love —
hence They are sung as "loving to Their devotees".[^01-37]

[^01-36]: Krishnadasa was the younger brother of Gauridasa Pandita, of Nityananda's branch (according to Majumdar). Gauridasa
Pandita (here "Thakura Pandita") was a companion of Nityananda, Subala according to GGD; at Ambika-Kalna he served the
Deities of Gaura-Nitai. Cf. Murari 4.14.12–14. Majumdar's argument: the pada is a contemporary's testimony that the
worship of the Lord's Deity began in His lifetime. The next pada of PK (2359) continues the story.
[^01-37]: "The two brothers stayed there" — the Lord and Nityananda remained at Ambika in Their Deity forms, in which, by
Their own word, They Themselves are present: the Deity is not an image but the Lord Himself, manifest through the
devotee's love.

## 25. Chandrashekhara — "kṣaṇeka rahiyā caliyā uṭhiyā paṇḍita jagadānanda…" (PK 1854)
*Lila: Jagadananda Pandita comes from Nilachala to Navadvipa, to Shachi and Vishnupriya. According to Majumdar, written
"before one's eyes", in the Lord's lifetime.*[^01-38]

ক্ষণেক রহিয়া চলিয়া উঠিয়া
পণ্ডিত জগদানন্দ ।
প্রবেশি নগরে দেখে ঘরে ঘরে
লোক সব নিরানন্দ ॥

*kṣaṇeka rahiyā caliyā uṭhiyā*
*paṇḍita jagadānanda |*
*prabeśi nagare dekhe ghare ghare*
*loka saba nirānanda ||*

*Word for word:* kshaneka rahiya — after pausing a while; chaliya uthiya — rising and going on; pandita jagadananda — Pandita Jagadananda; prabeshi nagare — entering the town; dekhe ghare ghare — sees that in every house; loka saba nirananda — all the people are joyless

**25.1.** After pausing a while, Pandita Jagadananda
rose and went on.
Entering the town, he sees that in every house
all the people are joyless.

না মেলে পসার না করে আহার
কারো মুখে নাহি হাসি ।
নগরে নাগরী কান্দয়ে গুমরি
থাকয়ে বিরলে বসি ॥

*nā mele pasāra nā kare āhāra*
*kāro mukhe nāhi hāsi |*
*nagare nāgarī kāndaye gumari*
*thākaye birale basi ||*

*Word for word:* na mele pasara — the shops are not open; na kare ahara — no one eats; karo mukhe nahi hasi — no smile on any face; nagare nagari — the women of the town; kandaye gumari — weep with stifled sobs; thakaye birale basi — sit apart in solitude

**25.2.** The shops are not open, no one eats,
no face has a smile.
The women of the town weep with stifled sobs,
sitting apart, alone.

দেখিয়া নগর ঠাকুরের ঘর
প্রবেশ করল যাই ।
আধ মরা হেন ভূমে অচেতন
পড়িয়া আছেন আই ॥

*dekhiyā nagara ṭhākurera ghara*
*prabeśa karala yāi |*
*ādha marā hena bhūme acetana*
*paṛiyā āchena āi ||*

*Word for word:* dekhiya nagara — having seen the town; thakurera ghara — the Lord's house; prabesha karala yai — he went and entered; adha mara hena — as if half dead; bhume achetana — senseless on the ground; pariya achhena ai — lies Ai (Mother Shachi)

**25.3.** Having seen the town, he went
and entered the Lord's house.
As if half dead, senseless,
Ai lies on the ground.[^01-39]

প্রভুর রমণী সেহ অনাথিনী
প্রভুরে হইয়া হারা ।
পড়িয়া আছেন মলিন বসন
মুদল-নয়ানে ধারা ॥

*prabhura ramaṇī seha anāthinī*
*prabhure haiyā hārā |*
*paṛiyā āchena malina basana*
*mudala-nayāne dhārā ||*

*Word for word:* prabhura ramani — the Lord's wife; seha anathini — she too, forsaken; prabhure haiya hara — having lost the Lord; pariya achhena — lies; malina basana — in faded clothes; mudala-nayane dhara — tears from closed eyes

**25.4.** And the Lord's wife, forsaken,
having lost the Lord,
lies in faded clothes,
tears flowing from her closed eyes.

দাস দাসী সব আছয়ে নীরব
দেখিয়া পথিক-জন ।
সোধাইছে তারে কহ দেখি মোরে
কোথা হৈতে আগমন ॥

*dāsa dāsī saba āchaye nīraba*
*dekhiyā pathika-jana |*
*sodhāiche tāre kaha dekhi more*
*kothā haite āgamana ||*

*Word for word:* dasa dasi saba — all the servants and maids; achhaye niraba — are silent; dekhiya pathika-jana — seeing the traveller; sodhaichhe tare — they ask him; kaha dekhi more — tell me now; kotha haite agamana — where have you come from?

**25.5.** All the servants and maids are silent;
seeing the traveller,
they ask him: "Tell us now,
where have you come from?"

পণ্ডিত কহেন মোর আগমন
নীলাচলপুর হৈতে ।
গৌরাঙ্গ-সুন্দর পাঠাইল মোরে
তোমা সভারে দেখিতে ॥

*paṇḍita kahena mora āgamana*
*nīlācalapura haite |*
*gaurāṅga-sundara pāṭhāila more*
*tomā sabhāre dekhite ||*

*Word for word:* pandita kahena — the Pandita says; mora agamana — I have come; nilachalapura haite — from Nilachala; gauranga-sundara pathaila more — beautiful Gauranga sent me; toma sabhare dekhite — to see you all

**25.6.** The Pandita says: "I have come
from Nilachala.
Beautiful Gauranga sent me
to see you all."

শুনিয়া বচন সজল নয়ন
শচীরে কহল গিয়া ।
আর এক জন চলিল তখন
শ্রীবাস-মন্দিরে ধাঞা ॥

*śuniyā bacana sajala nayana*
*śacīre kahala giyā |*
*āra eka jana calila takhana*
*śrībāsa-mandire dhāñā ||*

*Word for word:* shuniya bachana — hearing these words; sajala nayana — with tearful eyes; shachire kahala giya — they went and told Shachi; ara eka jana — and another; chalila takhana — set off at once; shribasa-mandire dhana — running to Srivasa's house

**25.7.** Hearing these words, with tearful eyes
they went and told Shachi,
and another set off at once
running to Srivasa's house.

শুনিয়া শ্রীবাস মালিনী উল্লাস
যত নবদ্বীপ-বাসী ।
মরা হেন ছিল অমনি ধাইল
পরাণ পাইল আসি ॥

*śuniyā śrībāsa mālinī ullāsa*
*yata nabadvīpa-bāsī |*
*marā hena chila amani dhāila*
*parāṇa pāila āsi ||*

*Word for word:* shuniya shribasa — hearing it, Srivasa; malini ullasa — Malini overjoyed; yata nabadvipa-basi — and all the people of Navadvipa; mara hena chhila — had been as if dead; amani dhaila — at once they ran; parana paila asi — coming, they came back to life

**25.8.** Hearing it, Srivasa, Malini in delight,
and all the people of Navadvipa,
who had been as if dead, came running at once —
and, coming, came back to life.

মালিনী আসিয়া শচী বিষ্ণুপ্রিয়া
উঠাইল যতন করি ।
তাহারে কহিল পণ্ডিত আইল
পাঠাইল গৌরহরি ॥

*mālinī āsiyā śacī biṣṇupriyā*
*uṭhāila yatana kari |*
*tāhāre kahila paṇḍita āila*
*pāṭhāila gaurahari ||*

*Word for word:* malini asiya — Malini, coming; shachi vishnupriya — Shachi [and] Vishnupriya; uthaila yatana kari — gently raised; tahare kahila — told them; pandita aila — the Pandita has come; pathaila gaurahari — Gaurahari has sent him

**25.9.** Malini came and gently raised
Shachi and Vishnupriya
and told them: "The Pandita has come;
Gaurahari has sent him."

শুনি শচী আই সচকিত চাই
দেখিলেন পণ্ডিতেরে ।
কহে তার ঠাই আমার নিমাই
আসিয়াছে কত দূরে ॥

*śuni śacī āi sacakita cāi*
*dekhilena paṇḍitere |*
*kahe tāra ṭhāi āmāra nimāi*
*āsiyāche kata dūre ||*

*Word for word:* shuni shachi ai — hearing it, Mother Shachi; sachakita chai — looked up with a start; dekhilena panditere — saw the Pandita; kahe tara thai — says to him; amara nimai — my Nimai; asiyachhe kata dure — how far off has He come?

**25.10.** Hearing it, Mother Shachi looked up with a start
and saw the Pandita.
She says to him: "My Nimai —
how far off is He now?"

দেখি প্রেমসীমা স্নেহের মহিমা
পণ্ডিত কান্দিয়া কয় ।
সেই গোরা-মণি যুগে যুগে জানি
তুয়া প্রেম-বশ হয় ॥

*dekhi premasīmā snehera mahimā*
*paṇḍita kāndiyā kaya |*
*sei gorā-maṇi yuge yuge jāni*
*tuyā prema-baśa haya ||*

*Word for word:* dekhi prema-sima — seeing the utmost of love; snehera mahima — the greatness of a mother's tenderness; pandita kandiya kaya — the Pandita says, weeping; sei gora-mani — that jewel Gora; yuge yuge jani — I know, age after age; tuya prema-basha haya — is subdued by your love

**25.11.** Seeing the utmost of love, the greatness of a mother's tenderness,
the Pandita says, weeping:
"That jewel Gora, I know, age after age
is subdued by your love."

হেন নীত রীত গৌরাঙ্গ-চরিত
সভাকারে শুনাইয়া ।
পণ্ডিত রহিলা নদীয়া নগরে
সভাকারে সুখ দিয়া ॥

*hena nīta rīta gaurāṅga-carita*
*sabhākāre śunāiyā |*
*paṇḍita rahilā nadīyā nagare*
*sabhākāre sukha diyā ||*

*Word for word:* hena nita rita — such ways and doings; gauranga-charita — Gauranga's life; sabhakare shunaiya — telling everyone; pandita rahila nadiya nagare — the Pandita stayed in the town of Nadia; sabhakare sukha diya — giving joy to all

**25.12.** Having told everyone
of Gauranga's ways and doings,
the Pandita stayed on in the town of Nadia,
giving joy to all.

চন্দ্রশেখর পশুর সোসর
বিষয়-বিষেতে প্রীত ।
গৌরাঙ্গ-চরিত পরম অমৃত
তাহাতে না লয় চিত ॥

*candraśekhara paśura sosara*
*biṣaya-biṣete prīta |*
*gaurāṅga-carita parama amṛta*
*tāhāte nā laya cita ||*

*Word for word:* chandrashekhara — Chandrashekhara; pashura sosara — like a beast; bishaya-bishete prita — fond of the poison of sense-objects; gauranga-charita — Gauranga's life; parama amrita — supreme nectar; tahate na laya chita — his heart does not take to it

**25.13.** Chandrashekhara, no better than a beast,
is fond of the poison of sense-objects:
to Gauranga's life, the supreme nectar,
his heart does not take.

[^01-38]: The signature is "Chandrashekhara"; by tradition (S. Ray) this is Chandrashekhara Acharya, the Lord's maternal
uncle; the attribution is traditional but not proven. In PK the pada continues the preceding one (PK 1853, signed
"Madhavi Dasa"), in which Jagadananda walks from Puri wondering whether he will find Shachi. Jagadananda's journeys to
Shachi at the Lord's bidding: CC Antya 12. Majumdar's argument: the restraint in mentioning the Lord's wife (her name is
not given — only "the Lord's wife") is a mark of a contemporary; Vrindavana Dasa does the same.
[^01-39]: Ai ("mother") — so Mother Shachi was called in Navadvipa.

## 26. Narahari (Sarakara) — "rase tanu ḍhara ḍhara gaurakiśora bara…" (PK 2259)
*Theme: the truth of Gaura — Shyama became Gaura to play with Radha; the poet fears to reveal the secret. According to
Majumdar, written before Svarupa Damodara's kadacha, i.e. in the Lord's lifetime. Raga pahida (GPT).*[^01-40]

রসে তনু ঢর ঢর গৌরকিশোর বর
নাম তার শ্রীকৃষ্ণচৈতন্য ।
এ সব নিগূঢ় কথা কহিতে অন্তরে ব্যথা
ভক্ত বিনা নাহি জানে অন্য ॥

*rase tanu ḍhara ḍhara gaurakiśora bara*
*nāma tāra śrīkṛṣṇacaitanya |*
*e saba nigūṛha kathā kahite antare byathā*
*bhakta binā nāhi jāne anya ||*

*Word for word:* rase tanu dhara dhara — His body brimming with rasa; gaura-kishora bara — the most excellent youthful Gaura; nama tara shri-krishna-chaitanya — His name is Sri Krishna Chaitanya; e saba nigudha katha — these hidden matters; kahite antare byatha — to tell them pains the heart; bhakta vina nahi jane anya — none but the devotees know

**26.1.** The most excellent youthful Gaura, His body brimming with rasa —
His name is Sri Krishna Chaitanya.
To speak these hidden things pains the heart:
none but the devotees know them.

দ্বাপর যুগেতে শ্যাম কলিতে চৈতন্য নাম
গর্গ-বাক্য ভাগবতে লিখি ।
মনে করি অনুমান শ্যাম হইল গৌরাঙ্গ
রাধাকৃষ্ণ-তনু তার সাথী ॥

*dvāpara yugete śyāma kalite caitanya nāma*
*garga-bākya bhāgabate likhi |*
*mane kari anumāna śyāma haila gaurāṅga*
*rādhākṛṣṇa-tanu tāra sāthī ||*

*Word for word:* dvapara yugete shyama — in the Dvapara-yuga, Shyama; kalite chaitanya nama — in Kali, the name Chaitanya; garga-bakya bhagabate likhi — [so] Garga's words are written in the Bhagavata; mane kari anumana — I have reasoned in my heart; shyama haila gauranga — Shyama has become Gauranga; radha-krishna-tanu tara sathi — the body of Radha and Krishna is His companion (witness)

**26.2.** In the Dvapara-yuga Shyama, in Kali the name Chaitanya:
so Garga's words are written in the *Bhagavata*.[^01-41]
I have reasoned in my heart: Shyama has become Gauranga,
and the body of Radha and Krishna bears witness to it.[^01-42]

অন্তরেতে শ্যাম-তনু বাহিরে গৌরাঙ্গ তনু
অদ্ভুত চৈতন্যের লীলা ।
রাই সঙ্গে খেলাইতে কুঞ্জ-রস বিলাইতে
অনুরাগে গৌর-তনু হৈলা ॥

*antarete śyāma-tanu bāhire gaurāṅga tanu*
*adbhuta caitanyera līlā |*
*rāi saṅge khelāite kuñja-rasa bilāite*
*anurāge gaura-tanu hailā ||*

*Word for word:* antarete shyama-tanu — within, the dark body; bahire gauranga tanu — without, the golden body; adbhuta chaitanyera lila — wondrous is Chaitanya's lila; rai sange khelaite — to play with Rai (Radha); kunja-rasa bilaite — to distribute the rasa of the bowers; anurage gaura-tanu haila — out of love He became golden

**26.3.** Within, the dark body; without, the golden:
wondrous is Chaitanya's lila!
To play with Rai and to share the rasa of the bowers,
out of love He became golden.

কহিবার কথা নহে কহিলে কি জানি হয়ে
না কহিলে মনে বড় তাপ ।
চিত্তে অনুমান করি গৌরাঙ্গ হৃদয়ে ধরি
নরহরি করয়ে বিলাপ ॥

*kahibāra kathā nahe kahile ki jāni haye*
*nā kahile mane baṛa tāpa |*
*citte anumāna kari gaurāṅga hṛdaye dhari*
*narahari karaye bilāpa ||*

*Word for word:* kahibara katha nahe — it is not a thing to be told; kahile ki jani haye — if told, who knows what may happen; na kahile mane bara tapa — if not told, the heart burns; chitte anumana kari — reasoning in his heart; gauranga hridaye dhari — holding Gauranga in his heart; narahari karaye bilapa — Narahari laments

**26.4.** This is not to be told: tell it, and who knows what may happen;
leave it untold, and the heart burns.
Reasoning in his heart and holding Gauranga in his heart,
Narahari laments.

[^01-40]: The signature is "Narahari"; Majumdar assigns the pada to Narahari Sarakara. In PK it stands in the section on the
sannyasa, in GPT among the opening padas (mangalacharana). Majumdar's argument: this truth (Krishna became Gaura for
Radha's sake) was later set forth openly by Svarupa Damodara in his kadacha and after him by Krishnadasa Kaviraja (CC Adi
1.5–6, 4); the poet's fear of revealing the secret would be unintelligible after that — so the pada was written in the
Lord's lifetime.
[^01-41]: *Bhag.* 10.8.13: Garga, naming Krishna, says that in other yugas He took white, red and yellow colours, and now has
become dark (krishna). The Gaudiya tradition sees in the "yellow" (pita) a reference to Gaura.
[^01-42]: The reading "sāthī" (PK, GPT) means "companion"; the sense may require "sākhī" (witness). Within He is Shyama
(Krishna), without He is clad in Radha's golden radiance (cf. CC Adi 4).

# Chapter 2. Padas of the Puri Period

*Padas by contemporaries on the Lord's life in Puri after the sannyasa, in the order of events: the arrival in Nilachala
and Sarvabhauma's house, the darshan of Jagannatha, sankirtana on the seashore, Radha's mood in the company of Svarupa
Damodara and Ramananda Raya, the states of separation (dasha), the Gambhira, and the divine madness of prema
(divya-unmada). Majumdar (*Sri-Chaitanya-chariter upadan*, ch. 2) regards the Puri padas of Narahari Sarakara, Vasu Ghosha
and Vasu Ramananda as the testimony of those who came to the Lord every year with the pilgrims from Gauda. The text
follows the *Padakalpataru* (PK) and the *Gaura-pada-tarangini* (GPT1 — 1st ed., 1903; GPT2 — 2nd ed., 1934); the Bengali
original, variants and word-for-word translation are in the full version of the book.*

## 1. Madhavi Dasa — "kalaha kariyā chhalā…" (PK 2239)
*Lila: the arrival in Puri (1510). Making a quarrel His pretext, the Lord goes on ahead to Jagannatha; Nityananda and the
devotees follow His footprints; at the Lion Gate Nitai questions the people of Nilachala; the Lord enters the house of the
Bhattacharya (Sarvabhauma). Raga varadi (PK), suhai (GPT).*[^02-1]

কলহ করিয়া ছলা আগে পহু চলি গেলা
ভেটিবারে নীলাচল-রায় ।
যতেক ভকতগণ হৈয়া সকরুণ-মন
পদ-চিহ্ন-অনুসারে ধায় ॥

*kalaha kariyā chalā āge pahu cali gelā*
*bheṭibāre nīlācala-rāya |*
*yateka bhakatagaṇa haiyā sakaruṇa-mana*
*pada-cihna-anusāre dhāya ||*

*Word for word:* kalaha kariya chhala — making a quarrel the pretext; age pahu chali gela — the Lord went on ahead; bhetibare nilachala-raya — to meet the Lord of Nilachala; yateka bhakatagana — all the devotees; haiya sakaruna-mana — their hearts full of grief; pada-chihna-anusare — following the footprints; dhaya — run

**1.1.** Making a quarrel His pretext, the Lord went on ahead
to see the Lord of Nilachala.
All the devotees, their hearts full of grief,
run after Him, following His footprints.[^02-2]

নিতাই বিরহ-অনলে ভেল ধন্দ ।
আঠারনালাতে হৈতে কান্দিতে কান্দিতে পথে
যায় নিতাই অবধৌত-চন্দ ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*nitāi biraha-anale bhela dhanda |*
*āṭhāranālāte haite kāndite kāndite pathe*
*yāya nitāi abadhauta-canda || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* nitai — Nitai; biraha-anale — in the fire of separation; bhela dhanda — became bewildered; atharanala-te haite — from Atharanala; kandite kandite pathe — weeping and weeping on the road; yaya nitai — goes Nitai; abadhauta-chanda — the moon of avadhutas

**1.2.** *(Refrain)* Nitai, in the fire of separation, is as if in a daze.
From Atharanala, weeping and weeping on the road,
goes Nitai, the moon of avadhutas.[^02-3]

সিংহ-দুয়ারে গিয়া মরমে বেদনা পাইয়া
দাঁড়াইল নিত্যানন্দ রায় ।
হরে কৃষ্ণ হরি বলে দেখিয়াছ সন্ন্যাসীরে
নীলাচল-বাসীরে সোধায় ॥

*siṃha-duyāre giyā marame bedanā pāiyā*
*dām̐ṛāila nityānanda rāya |*
*hare kṛṣṇa hari bale dekhiyācha sannyāsīre*
*nīlācala-bāsīre sodhāya ||*

*Word for word:* simha-duyare giya — coming to the Lion Gate; marame bedana paiya — with pain in his heart; daraila nityananda raya — Nityananda Raya stopped; hare krishna hari bale — crying "Hare Krishna, Hari!"; dekhiyachha sannyasire — "have you seen a sannyasi?"; nilachala-basire sodhaya — he asks the people of Nilachala

**1.3.** Coming to the Lion Gate, with pain in His heart,
Nityananda Raya stopped.
Crying "Hare Krishna, Hari!" He asks the people of Nilachala:
"Have you seen a sannyasi?

জাম্বুনদ-হেম জিনি গৌর-বরণ-খানি
অরুণ বসন শোভে গায় ।
প্রেম-ভরে গরগর আঁখিযুগ ঝর ঝর
হরি হরি বোল বলি ধায় ॥

*jāmbunada-hema jini gaura-baraṇa-khāni*
*aruṇa basana śobhe gāya |*
*prema-bhare garagara ām̐khiyuga jhara jhara*
*hari hari bola bali dhāya ||*

*Word for word:* jambunada-hema jini — surpassing the gold of the Jambu river; gaura-barana-khani — His golden form; aruna basana shobhe gaya — a red cloth shines on His body; prema-bhare garagara — brimming with prema; ankhi-yuga jhara jhara — tears stream from both eyes; hari hari bola boli dhaya — He runs, crying "Hari, Hari!"

**1.4.** His golden form surpasses the gold of the Jambu river,
a red cloth shines on His body;
brimming with prema, He sheds tears from both eyes
and runs, crying 'Hari, Hari!'"[^02-4]

ছাড়ি নাগরালি-বেশে ভ্রমে পহু দেশে দেশে
এবে ভেল সন্ন্যাসীর বেশ ।
মাধবী দাসেতে কয় অপরূপ গোরা রায়
ভট্ট-গৃহে করল প্রবেশ ॥

*chāṛi nāgarāli-beśe bhrame pahu deśe deśe*
*ebe bhela sannyāsīra beśa |*
*mādhabī dāsete kaya aparūpa gorā rāya*
*bhaṭṭa-gṛhe karala prabeśa ||*

*Word for word:* chhari nagarali-beshe — leaving the dress of a nagara; bhrame pahu deshe deshe — the Lord wanders from land to land; ebe bhela sannyasira besha — now [He wears] the garb of a sannyasi; madhavi dasete kaya — Madhavi Dasa says; aparupa gora raya — the wondrous Gora Raya; bhatta-grihe karala prabesha — entered the house of the Bhattacharya

**1.5.** Leaving the dress of a nagara, the Lord wanders from land to land —
now He wears the garb of a sannyasi.
Madhavi Dasa says: the wondrous Gora Raya
has entered the house of the Bhattacharya.[^02-5]

[^02-1]: The signature in PK is "mādhabī dāsa" (Madhavi Dasa). Who this poet was is not established: Majumdar does not name
him among the contemporaries; some identify the poet with Madhavi Devi of Puri, the sister of Shikhi Mahiti, whom the
Lord counted among Radha's closest maidservants (CC Antya 2), but there is no proof — the attribution is doubtful. GPT1
and GPT2 give the same pada with different readings in almost every line and with another ending — the signature of
Govinda Dasa ("Govinda Dasa says: I saw His entry into Sarvabhauma's house"). In PK the pada opens the 21st pallava
("The sannyasa of Sri Gauranga, etc."). The events: CC Madhya 5–6; CB Antya 2; Murari 3.10–3.11; Lochana, Shesha-khanda.
[^02-2]: The "quarrel": according to CC (Madhya 5) and CB (Antya 2), Nityananda broke the Lord's sannyasa staff, and the
Lord, as if angered, went on ahead alone. The poet calls the quarrel a "pretext": the Lord Himself wished to come first
to Jagannatha (and to Sarvabhauma).
[^02-3]: Atharanala is the bridge of eighteen arches at the entrance to Puri; here, according to CC (Madhya 5), the Lord
learned that His staff had been broken and went on ahead alone. An avadhuta is a wanderer above outward rules; so
Nityananda is called.
[^02-4]: Jambunada is the gold of the river Jambu, the finest gold (Puranas). The red cloth is the saffron garb of a
sannyasi. According to CC (Madhya 6), on seeing Jagannatha the Lord fell senseless in the temple, and Sarvabhauma had
Him carried to his house; when Nityananda and the companions came to the Lion Gate, people told them of the sannyasi
who had been taken to the Bhattacharya's.
[^02-5]: The first line of this couplet ("Leaving the dress of a nagara…") is absent from the "P-R-Sa" manuscript.
"Nagarali" is the manner and dress of a nagara (an elegant young townsman): a hint at the Lord's Navadvipa form as it
is sung by the poets of nagari-bhava. Vrindavana Dasa stresses that in this incarnation the Lord did not so much as
glance at another man's wife; the Gaudiya tradition (Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja, Bhaktisiddhanta) does not
accept the worship of Gaura in the spirit of "Gaura-nagari".

## 2. Madhavi — "nityānanda saṅgati mukunda gadādhare…" (PK 2240)
*Lila: the sequel to the previous pada — the companions find the Lord in Sarvabhauma's house; the people of Nilachala
gaze at Him. Raga — the same (varadi).*[^02-6]

নিত্যানন্দ সঙ্গতি মুকুন্দ গদাধরে ।
দেখিলেন গৌরচন্দ্র সার্ব্বভৌম-ঘরে ॥

*nityānanda saṅgati mukunda gadādhare |*
*dekhilena gauracandra sārvvabhauma-ghare ||*

*Word for word:* nityananda sangati — together with Nityananda; mukunda gadadhare — Mukunda and Gadadhara; dekhilena gaurachandra — beheld Gaurachandra; sarvabhauma-ghare — in Sarvabhauma's house

**2.1.** Together with Nityananda, Mukunda and Gadadhara
beheld Gaurachandra in Sarvabhauma's house.

প্রতপ্ত কাঞ্চন-কান্তি অরুণ বসন ।
প্রেমে ছল ছল দুই অরুণ নয়ন ॥

*pratapta kāñcana-kānti aruṇa basana |*
*preme chala chala dui aruṇa nayana ||*

*Word for word:* pratapta kanchana-kanti — the lustre of molten gold; aruna basana — a red cloth; preme chhala chhala — brimming with tears of prema; dui aruna nayana — two reddish eyes

**2.2.** His lustre is like molten gold, His cloth is red;
His two reddish eyes brim with tears of prema.

আজানুলম্বিত ভুজ চন্দনে ভূষিত ।
উন্নত নাসিকা ঊর্দ্ধ-তিলক-শোভিত ॥

*ājānulambita bhuja candane bhūṣita |*
*unnata nāsikā ūrddha-tilaka-śobhita ||*

*Word for word:* ajanulambita bhuja — arms reaching to the knees; chandane bhushita — adorned with sandal; unnata nasika — a high nose; urdhva-tilaka-shobhita — graced with the urdhva-tilaka

**2.3.** His arms reach to His knees, adorned with sandal;
His nose is high, His brow graced with the urdhva-tilaka.

গোপীনাথ বাণীনাথ সার্ব্বভৌম কাশী ।
গোরা-রূপ দেখে যত নীলাচল-বাসী ॥

*gopīnātha bāṇīnātha sārvvabhauma kāśī |*
*gorā-rūpa dekhe yata nīlācala-bāsī ||*

*Word for word:* gopinatha — Gopinatha [Acharya]; vaninatha — Vaninatha; sarvabhauma — Sarvabhauma; kashi — Kashi [Mishra]; gora-rupa dekhe — gaze at Gora's form; yata nilachala-basi — all the people of Nilachala

**2.4.** Gopinatha, Vaninatha, Sarvabhauma, Kashi —
all the people of Nilachala gaze at Gora's form.[^02-7]

দক্ষিণে নিতাই বসি বামে গদাধর ।
মিলিলেন গোরাচাঁদের যত অনুচর ॥

*dakṣiṇe nitāi basi bāme gadādhara |*
*mililena gorācām̐dera yata anucara ||*

*Word for word:* dakshine nitai basi — on the right sits Nitai; bame gadadhara — on the left Gadadhara; mililena — have gathered; gorachandera yata anuchara — all the followers of Gorachand

**2.5.** Nitai sits on the right, Gadadhara on the left:
all the followers of Gorachand have gathered.

যে দেখয়ে গোরা-মুখ সেই প্রেমে ভাসে ।
মাধবি বঞ্চিত হৈল নিজ কর্ম্ম-দোষে ॥

*ye dekhaye gorā-mukha sei preme bhāse |*
*mādhabi bañcita haila nija karmma-doṣe ||*

*Word for word:* ye dekhaye gora-mukha — whoever sees Gora's face; sei preme bhase — floats in prema; madhavi banchita haila — Madhavi was left out; nija karma-doshe — through the fault of [Madhavi's] own deeds

**2.6.** Whoever sees Gora's face floats in prema;
Madhavi alone is left out — through the fault of Madhavi's own deeds.[^02-8]

[^02-6]: The signature is "mādhabi" (MS "ka": "mādhabī"; "P-R-Sa": "mādhaba"); on the poet see note 1. In GPT (GPT1, p. 402) the
pada follows the pada on Sarvabhauma seeing the Lord's forms. Cf. CC Madhya 6: Nityananda, Mukunda, Gadadhara (and
Jagadananda) come to Sarvabhauma's house, where the Lord lies senseless.
[^02-7]: Gopinatha Acharya, Sarvabhauma's brother-in-law (his sister's husband), had known the Lord in Navadvipa; Vaninatha
Raya was the brother of Ramananda Raya; Kashi is evidently Kashi Mishra, in whose house the Lord later lived. According
to CC (Madhya 10), the Lord met Vaninatha and Kashi Mishra after His return from the South; the poet gathers them into a
single scene.
[^02-8]: A formula of humility usual in a bhanita: the poet laments being deprived of what was given to others.

## 3. Narahari (Sarakara) — "dekhi gorā nīlāchala-nātha…" (PK 799)
*Lila: the darshan of Jagannatha — the Lord, in a gopi's mood, reproaches Krishna. In PK it is the gaura-chandrika to
the section "reproaches to Krishna" (akshepanuraga). According to Majumdar, an eyewitness description unequalled in
literature. Raga suhai.*[^02-9]

দেখি গোরা নীলাচল-নাথ ।
নিজ পারিষদগণ সাথ ॥

*dekhi gorā nīlācala-nātha |*
*nija pāriṣadagaṇa sātha ||*

*Word for word:* dekhi — seeing; gora — Gora; nilachala-natha — the Lord of Nilachala; nija parishada-gana satha — with His own associates

**3.1.** Seeing the Lord of Nilachala,
Gora, together with His own associates,

বিভোর হইলা গোপী-ভাবে ।
কহে পহু করিয়া আক্ষেপে ॥

*bibhora hailā gopī-bhābe |*
*kahe pahu kariyā ākṣepe ||*

*Word for word:* bibhora haila — was overwhelmed; gopi-bhabe — by a gopi's mood; kahe pahu — the Lord says; kariya akshepe — reproachfully

**3.2.** was overwhelmed by a gopi's mood,
and, reproaching, the Lord says:

আমি তোমা না দেখিলে মরি ।
উলটি না চাহ তুমি ফিরি ॥

*āmi tomā nā dekhile mari |*
*ulaṭi nā cāha tumi phiri ||*

*Word for word:* ami toma na dekhile mari — I perish without seeing You (I cannot live without You); ulati na chaha tumi phiri — yet You do not turn round to look

**3.3.** "Without You I cannot live,
yet You will not even turn round to look at Me!

করিলা পিরিতিময় ফাঁদ ।
হাতে দিলা আকাশের চাঁদ ॥

*karilā piritimaya phām̐da |*
*hāte dilā ākāśera cām̐da ||*

*Word for word:* karila piritimaya phanda — You set a snare made of love; hate dila akashera chanda — You put the moon of the sky into my hands

**3.4.** You wove a snare of love —
You put the moon of the sky into My hands;

এবে তোমা দেখিতে সন্দেশ ।
কহে গোরা করিয়া আবেশ ॥

*ebe tomā dekhite sandeśa |*
*kahe gorā kariyā ābeśa ||*

*Word for word:* ebe toma dekhite — now to see You; sandesha — [is only] tidings, hearsay; kahe gora — says Gora; kariya abesha — possessed by the mood

**3.5.** and now to see You is only tidings and hearsay," —
so says Gora, overwhelmed by the mood.[^02-10]

ছলছল অরুণ নয়ান ।
রসরস বিরস বয়ান ॥

*chalachala aruṇa nayāna |*
*rasarasa birasa bayāna ||*

*Word for word:* chhalachhala — brimming with tears; aruna nayana — the reddish eyes; rasarasa — [once] full of sweetness; birasa bayana — the face has grown wan

**3.6.** His reddish eyes are brimming with tears,
His face, so full of sweetness, has grown wan.

অপরূপ গৌরাঙ্গ-বিলাস ।
কহে কিছু নরহরি দাস ॥

*aparūpa gaurāṅga-bilāsa |*
*kahe kichu narahari dāsa ||*

*Word for word:* aparupa — wondrous; gauranga-bilasa — Gauranga's play; kahe kichhu — tells a little; narahari dasa — Narahari Dasa

**3.7.** Wondrous is Gauranga's play —
Narahari Dasa has told a little of it.

[^02-9]: The signature is "Narahari Dasa"; Majumdar ascribes the pada to Narahari Sarakara of Shrikhanda and places it among
the Puri padas written in the Lord's lifetime. GPT (GPT1, p. 299, no. 23) has the same pada with minor variants. In
Radha's mood the Lord sees Krishna Himself in Jagannatha — cf. CC Madhya 13 (at the Ratha-yatra: "You are the same, I am
the same…") and Antya 14 (darshan at the Garuda-stambha). The gopi's reproaches are a manifestation of the highest prema,
not of worldly resentment.
[^02-10]: The reading "sandeśa" (PK, GPT) means "tidings", "news"; a similar line of Chandidasa reads "sandeha" ("doubtful").
The sense is the same: the meeting that was once so close has become unattainable.

## 4. Vasu Ramananda — "nāchaye chaitanya chintāmaṇi…" (PK 2082)
*Lila: the Lord dances in the sankirtana. According to Majumdar, Puri: the Lord is called here by His sannyasa name —
"Chaitanya". Raga pathamanjari.*[^02-11]

নাচয়ে চৈতন্য চিন্তামণি ।
বুক বাহি পড়ে ধারা মুকুতা-গাঁথুনি ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*nācaye caitanya cintāmaṇi |*
*buka bāhi paṛe dhārā mukutā-gām̐thuni || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* nachaye — dances; chaitanya — Chaitanya; chintamani — the chintamani gem; buka bahi — flowing down the chest; pare dhara — streams fall; mukuta-ganthuni — [like] strung pearls

**4.1.** *(Refrain)* Chaitanya dances — the chintamani gem;
streams of tears flow down His chest like strings of pearls.

প্রেমে গদগদ হৈয়া ধরণী লোটায় ।
হুহুঙ্কার দিয়া খেণে উঠিয়া দাঁড়ায় ॥

*preme gadagada haiyā dharaṇī loṭāya |*
*huhuṅkāra diyā kheṇe uṭhiyā dām̐ṛāya ||*

*Word for word:* preme gadagada haiya — in prema, His voice choked; dharani lotaya — He rolls on the ground; huhunkara diya — with a thundering cry; khene uthiya daraya — suddenly He rises and stands

**4.2.** In prema, His voice choked, He rolls on the ground;
suddenly, with a thundering cry, He rises to His full height.

ঘন ঘন দেন পাক ঊর্দ্ধ বাহু করি ।
পতিত জনারে পহু বোলায় হরি হরি ॥

*ghana ghana dena pāka ūrddha bāhu kari |*
*patita janāre pahu bolāya hari hari ||*

*Word for word:* ghana ghana dena paka — again and again He whirls; urdhva bahu kari — raising His arms; patita janare — the fallen people; pahu bolaya hari hari — the Lord makes say "Hari, Hari"

**4.3.** Again and again He whirls, arms raised,
and makes the fallen say "Hari, Hari!"[^02-12]

হরিনাম করে গান জপে অনুক্ষণ ।
বুঝিতে না পারে কেহ বিরল লক্ষণ ॥

*harināma kare gāna jape anukṣaṇa |*
*bujhite nā pāre keha birala lakṣaṇa ||*

*Word for word:* harinama kare gana — He sings the name of Hari; jape anukshana — repeats it ceaselessly; bujhite na pare keha — no one can understand; birala lakshana — the rare signs

**4.4.** He sings the name of Hari, ceaselessly repeating it —
no one can fathom these rare signs.

অপার মহিমা গুণ জগ-জনে গায় ।
বসু রামানন্দে তাহে প্রেম-ধন চায় ॥

*apāra mahimā guṇa jaga-jane gāya |*
*basu rāmānande tāhe prema-dhana cāya ||*

*Word for word:* apara mahima guna — boundless glory and virtues; jaga-jane gaya — the people of the world sing; basu ramanande — Vasu Ramananda; tahe — of Him; prema-dhana chaya — begs the treasure of prema

**4.5.** His boundless glory and virtues the whole world sings;
Vasu Ramananda begs Him for the treasure of prema.

[^02-11]: Vasu Ramananda was from Kulinagrama, a descendant of Maladhara Vasu (Gunaraja Khan); according to CC (Madhya 15),
the Lord charged the people of Kulinagrama — Satyaraja Khan and Ramananda Vasu — to bring silk ropes every year for the
Ratha-yatra. Majumdar regards him as a contemporary and an eyewitness. In GPT2 the pada is given twice (the section
"dance and kirtana", nos. 17 and 74); in the second instance the first couplet is marked as the refrain. Cf. CC Madhya 11,
13 (the Lord's kirtanas in Puri).
[^02-12]: The chintamani is the wish-fulfilling gem. "Makes the fallen say the name": the Lord gives the holy name to all
without distinction.

## 5. Narahari (Sarakara) — "tribhubana-manohara śachīra nandana mora…" (PK 2241)
*Lila: from the sannyasa to Nilachala — the Lord leaves His former appearance and gives away the holy name and prema;
sankirtana on the seashore with Svarupa, Rupa, Ramananda, Govinda and Paramananda Puri. According to Majumdar, a pada by
an eyewitness of the Puri period. Raga bhatiyari.*[^02-13]

ত্রিভুবন-মনোহর শচীর নন্দন মোর
নদীয়া নগরে যার বাস ।
সকল সম্পদ ছাড়ি সন্ন্যাস গ্রহণ করি
নীলাচলে জগন্নাথ পাশ ॥

*tribhubana-manohara śacīra nandana mora*
*nadīyā nagare yāra bāsa |*
*sakala sampada chāṛi sannyāsa grahaṇa kari*
*nīlācale jagannātha pāśa ||*

*Word for word:* tribhubana-manohara — enchanter of the three worlds; shachira nandana mora — Shachi's son, my [Lord]; nadiya nagare yara basa — who lived in the town of Nadia; sakala sampada chhari — leaving all wealth; sannyasa grahana kari — taking sannyasa; nilachale jagannatha pasha — in Nilachala, near Jagannatha

**5.1.** The enchanter of the three worlds, Shachi's son, my Lord,
who lived in the town of Nadia,
gave up all His wealth and took sannyasa —
and He is in Nilachala, near Jagannatha.

যে চাঁচর কেশ দেখি মোহ যায় রতি-পতি
মুণ্ডন করিল হেন কেশ ।
কনক অঙ্গদ বালা মণি মুকুতার মালা
তেয়াগিলা সে মোহন বেশ ॥

*ye cām̐cara keśa dekhi moha yāya rati-pati*
*muṇḍana karila hena keśa |*
*kanaka aṅgada bālā maṇi mukutāra mālā*
*teyāgilā se mohana beśa ||*

*Word for word:* ye chanchara kesha dekhi — those curling locks, seeing which; moha yaya rati-pati — Rati's husband (Kamadeva) loses his wits; mundana karila hena kesha — such locks He had shaved; kanaka angada bala — golden armlets and bracelets; mani mukutara mala — necklaces of gems and pearls; teyagila se mohana besha — He abandoned that enchanting dress

**5.2.** Those curling locks at the sight of which Rati's husband himself loses his wits —
such locks He has had shaved;
golden armlets and bracelets, necklaces of gems and pearls —
all that enchanting dress He has abandoned.[^02-14]

জীবে হৈয়া দয়াবান সভে দিয়া হরিনাম
পরম পাতকী উদ্ধারয়ে ।
দেবের দুর্ল্লভ যে লক্ষ্মী আদি বাঞ্ছে সে
প্রেম পতিতে বিতরয়ে ॥

*jībe haiyā dayābāna sabhe diyā harināma*
*parama pātakī uddhāraye |*
*debera durllabha ye lakṣmī ādi bāñche se*
*prema patite bitaraye ||*

*Word for word:* jibe haiya dayabana — compassionate to living beings; sabhe diya harinama — giving all the name of Hari; parama pataki uddharaye — He delivers the greatest sinners; debera durlabha ye — that which is rare for the gods; lakshmi adi banchhe se — which Lakshmi and others long for; prema patite bitaraye — that prema He gives away to the fallen

**5.3.** Compassionate to all living beings, giving everyone the name of Hari,
He delivers the greatest sinners;
the prema rare even for the gods, which Lakshmi and others long for,
He gives away to the fallen.

সকল ভকত সঙ্গে সংকীর্ত্তন-মহারঙ্গে
বিহার করয়ে সিন্ধু-তীরে ।
স্বরূপ রূপ রামানন্দ গোবিন্দ পরমানন্দ
মিলিলা সকল সহচরে ॥

*sakala bhakata saṅge saṃkīrttana-mahāraṅge*
*bihāra karaye sindhu-tīre |*
*svarūpa rūpa rāmānanda gobinda paramānanda*
*mililā sakala sahacare ||*

*Word for word:* sakala bhakata sange — with all the devotees; sankirtana-maharange — in the great joy of sankirtana; bihara karaye sindhu-tire — He roams along the seashore; svarupa — Svarupa; rupa — Rupa; ramananda — Ramananda; gobinda — Govinda; paramananda — Paramananda [Puri]; milila sakala sahachare — all the companions gathered

**5.4.** With all the devotees, in the great joy of sankirtana,
He roams along the seashore;
Svarupa, Rupa, Ramananda, Govinda, Paramananda —
all the companions have gathered.[^02-15]

কহে দাস নরহরি আমার গৌরহরি
রাধার পিরিতে হৈল হেন ।
এমন প্রেমের বন্যা জগত হইল ধন্যা
বঞ্চিত হইলুঁ মুঞি কেন ॥

*kahe dāsa narahari āmāra gaurahari*
*rādhāra pirite haila hena |*
*emana premera banyā jagata haila dhanyā*
*bañcita hailum̐ muñi kena ||*

*Word for word:* kahe dasa narahari — Narahari Dasa says; amara gaurahari — my Gaurahari; radhara pirite — out of love for Radha; haila hena — became so; emana premera banya — by such a flood of prema; jagata haila dhanya — the world was blessed; banchita hailun munyi kena — why am I left out?

**5.5.** Narahari Dasa says: my Gaurahari
became so out of love for Radha.
By such a flood of prema the whole world is blessed —
why then am I alone left out?[^02-16]

[^02-13]: The signature is "Narahari Dasa". Majumdar names the pada twice: as PK 2241 (kirtana on the seashore) and, by a
misprint, as "PK 1241" (the line about armlets and necklaces — his argument that the Lord's "dress" in the Navadvipa padas
is no invention). GPT1 (p. 403, no. 4) has the same pada with minor variants. In PK it stands in the 21st pallava ("The
sannyasa of Sri Gauranga, etc."), immediately after Madhavi's two padas.
[^02-14]: Rati's husband is Kamadeva, the god of love. The shaven locks: the sannyasa at Katwa (CC Adi 17; CB Madhya 28;
Lochana, Madhya-khanda).
[^02-15]: Svarupa Damodara and Ramananda Raya were the Lord's inseparable companions in the last years (CC Madhya 2; Antya 14–20);
Rupa Gosvami came to Puri (CC Antya 1); Govinda was the Lord's servant; Paramananda Puri, a disciple of
Madhavendra Puri, lived with the Lord in Puri (CC Madhya 10). "Rupa" is absent from MSS "ka", "kha", "cha" ("Svarupa"
without "Rupa"); "P-R-Sa" reads "Svarupa and others".
[^02-16]: "Became so out of love for Radha": cf. CC Adi 1.6 and 4 — Krishna took on Radha's lustre and mood in order to
taste Her love. A bhanita with the words "why then am I alone left out" is Narahari's habitual formula of humility (cf.
PK 2259 in chapter 1).

## 6. Narahari (Sarakara) — "rāmānanda svarūpera sane…" (PK 820)
*Lila: the Lord with Svarupa and Ramananda, in the mood of Radha who has heard Krishna's flute. In PK it is the
gaura-chandrika to the section "reproaches to the flute" (akshepanuraga). According to Majumdar, Puri, an eyewitness.
Raga suhini (PK), suhai (GPT).*[^02-17]

রামানন্দ স্বরূপের সনে ।
বসি গোরা ভাবে মনে মনে ॥

*rāmānanda svarūpera sane |*
*basi gorā bhābe mane mane ||*

*Word for word:* ramananda svarupera sane — with Ramananda and Svarupa; basi — sitting; gora bhabe mane mane — Gora muses within Himself

**6.1.** Sitting with Ramananda and Svarupa,
Gora is lost in thought.

চমকি কহয়ে আলি আলি ।
ক্ষণে রহিয়া বাঁশীরে দেয় গালি ॥

*camaki kahaye āli āli |*
*kṣaṇe rahiyā bām̐śīre deya gāli ||*

*Word for word:* chamaki kahaye — with a start He says; ali ali — "friend, friend!"; kshane rahiya — at times, falling silent; banshire deya gali — He rails at the flute

**6.2.** With a start He cries: "Friend, friend!" —
and at times, falling silent, He rails at the flute.

পুন কহে স্বরূপের পাশে ।
বাঁশী মোর জাতিকুল নাশে ॥

*puna kahe svarūpera pāśe |*
*bām̐śī mora jātikula nāśe ||*

*Word for word:* puna kahe svarupera pashe — again He says beside Svarupa (to Svarupa); banshi mora jatikula nashe — the flute destroys my family and honour

**6.3.** And again He says to Svarupa:
"The flute destroys My family and My honour.

ধ্বনি কাণে পশিয়া রহিল ।
বধির সমান মোরে কৈল ॥

*dhvani kāṇe paśiyā rahila |*
*badhira samāna more kaila ||*

*Word for word:* dhvani kane pashiya rahila — the sound entered my ears and stayed; badhira samana more kaila — it made me like one deaf

**6.4.** Its sound has entered My ears and stayed there —
it has deafened Me."[^02-18]

নরহরি মনে মনে হাসে ।
দেখি এই গৌরাঙ্গ-বিলাসে ॥

*narahari mane mane hāse |*
*dekhi ei gaurāṅga-bilāse ||*

*Word for word:* narahari mane mane hase — Narahari smiles within himself; dekhi ei gauranga-bilase — seeing this play of Gauranga

**6.5.** Narahari smiles within himself,
seeing this play of Gauranga.

[^02-17]: The signature is "Narahari"; Majumdar ascribes the pada to Narahari Sarakara and to the Puri period. In GPT1 (p. 299,
no. 24) it follows directly on "Seeing the Lord of Nilachala" (PK 799). In the last years Svarupa Damodara and Ramananda
Raya sustained the Lord with songs and verses answering to His mood (CC Madhya 2; Antya 14–17); on Krishna's flute heard by the
Lord in Radha's mood, see CC Antya 15–17.
[^02-18]: Radha's words: the sound of Krishna's flute draws the gopis out of their homes, making them forget their duty to
family and their good name. This is the language of pure prema, not of worldly passion.

## 7. Narahari (Sarakara) — "āre mora gaurakiśora. puruba prema-rase bhora…" (PK 840)
*Lila: holding the hands of Svarupa Damodara and Ramananda Raya, the Lord laments: "No one understands My heart." In PK
it is the gaura-chandrika to the section "reproaches to a friend" (akshepanuraga). According to Majumdar, Puri, an
eyewitness. Raga suhai.*[^02-19]

আরে মোর গৌরকিশোর ।
পুরুব প্রেম-রসে ভোর ॥

*āre mora gaurakiśora |*
*puruba prema-rase bhora ||*

*Word for word:* are — ah!; mora gaurakishora — my young Gaura; puruba prema-rase — in the rasa of a former love; bhora — lost, absorbed

**7.1.** Ah, my young Gaura —
lost in the rasa of a former love!

স্বরূপ দামোদর রামরায় ।
করে ধরি করে হায় হায় ॥

*svarūpa dāmodara rāmarāya |*
*kare dhari kare hāya hāya ||*

*Word for word:* svarupa damodara — Svarupa Damodara; ramaraya — Ramaraya (Ramananda Raya); kare dhari — holding by the hands; kare haya haya — He cries "alas, alas!"

**7.2.** Holding the hands of Svarupa Damodara and Ramaraya,
He cries: "Alas, alas!"

কহে মৃদু গদগদ ভাষ ।
ঘন বহে দীঘ নিশাস ॥

*kahe mṛdu gadagada bhāṣa |*
*ghana bahe dīgha niśāsa ||*

*Word for word:* kahe mridu gadagada bhasha — He speaks softly, His voice breaking; ghana bahe digha nishvasa — long sighs come again and again

**7.3.** He speaks softly, His voice breaking,
and again and again heaves long sighs.

মরম না বুঝে কেহো মোর ।
কহে পহু হইয়া বিভোর ॥

*marama nā bujhe keho mora |*
*kahe pahu haiyā bibhora ||*

*Word for word:* marama na bujhe keho mora — no one understands my heart; kahe pahu — says the Lord; haiya bibhora — beside Himself

**7.4.** "No one understands My heart," —
says the Lord, beside Himself.

কেনে বা এ প্রেম বাঢ়াইলুঁ ।
জীয়ন্তে পরাণ খোয়াইলুঁ ॥

*kene bā e prema bāṛhāilum̐ |*
*jīyante parāṇa khoyāilum̐ ||*

*Word for word:* kene va — why then; e prema badhailun — did I let this love grow; jiyante — while still alive; parana khoyailun — I have lost my life (heart)

**7.5.** "Why did I let this love grow?
I am still alive — yet My heart is already lost."[^02-20]

নিঝরে ঝরয়ে দু নয়ান ।
নরহরি মলিন বয়ান ॥

*nijhare jharaye du nayāna |*
*narahari malina bayāna ||*

*Word for word:* nijhare jharaye — pour like a cascade; du nayana — [from] both eyes; narahari — Narahari; malina bayana — with a sorrowful face

**7.6.** Tears pour unceasingly from both eyes;
Narahari's face is sorrowful.

[^02-19]: The signature is "Narahari"; Majumdar (whose text misprints "PK 804") cites the third line ("Svarupa Damodara,
Ramaraya…") as proof that the pada describes Puri. GPT1 (p. 299, no. 26) has it with minor variants. A pada by
Chaitanyadasa, PK 1985, opens with the same line — but there it is the joy of meeting: "I have found the young Lord of
Vraja." Cf. CC Antya 14–20 (at night the Lord reveals His mood to Svarupa and Ramananda) and Antya 20 (Shikshashtaka 8:
Radha's words).
[^02-20]: Words in Radha's mood: love for Krishna in separation burns so fiercely that the heart seems already lost. The
line conveys the force of vipralambha, not worldly despair.

## 8. Narahari (Sarakara?) — "prema kari kulabatī sane…" (GPT1, pp. 309–310)
*Lila: the Lord, in the mood of Radha as khandita (wounded by Her beloved's faithlessness), complains to Svarupa of Kanu,
who did not come to the tryst. Only in GPT (section "khandita, mana"). Raga suhai.*[^02-21]

প্রেম করি কুলবতী সনে ।
এত কি শঠতা কানুর মনে ॥

*prema kari kulabatī sane |*
*eta ki śaṭhatā kānura mane ||*

*Word for word:* prema kari — having loved; kulabati sane — a wife of a noble house; eta ki shathata — so much deceit; kanura mane — in Kanu's heart

**8.1.** Having loved a wife of a noble house —
how much deceit there is in Kanu's heart!

বংশীনাদে সঙ্কেত করিল ।
ঘরের বাহির মুই আইল ॥

*baṃśīnāde saṅketa karila |*
*gharera bāhira mui āila ||*

*Word for word:* vamshi-nade — with the sound of the flute; sanketa karila — He gave the sign; gharera bahira mui aila — I came out of my house

**8.2.** With the sound of His flute He gave the sign —
and I came out of My house.[^02-22]

কহে পুন হইবে মিলন ।
তাই মুই আইনু কুঞ্জবন ॥

*kahe puna haibe milana |*
*tāi mui āinu kuñjabana ||*

*Word for word:* kahe — He said; puna haibe milana — there will be a meeting again; tai mui ainu — so I came; kunjabana — to the bower-grove

**8.3.** He said: "We shall meet again," —
so I came to the bower-grove.

বেশ বনাইনু কত মতে ।
আশা করি বঞ্চিনু কুঞ্জেতে ॥

*beśa banāinu kata mate |*
*āśā kari bañcinu kuñjete ||*

*Word for word:* besha banainu — I adorned myself; kata mate — in so many ways; asha kari — in hope; banchinu kunjete — I passed [the night] in the bower

**8.4.** In so many ways I adorned Myself,
and in hope I spent the night in the bower.

কিন্তু কানু বঞ্চিয়া আমারে ।
রজনী বঞ্চিল কার ঘরে ॥

*kintu kānu bañciyā āmāre |*
*rajanī bañcila kāra ghare ||*

*Word for word:* kintu kanu — but Kanu; banchiya amare — deceiving me; rajani banchila — spent the night; kara ghare — in whose house?

**8.5.** But Kanu, deceiving Me,
spent the night — in whose house?

স্বরূপেরে এত কহি গোরা ।
অভিমানে কাঁদে হৈয়া ভোরা ॥

*svarūpere eta kahi gorā |*
*abhimāne kām̐de haiyā bhorā ||*

*Word for word:* svarupere eta kahi — having said this to Svarupa; gora — Gora; abhimane kande — weeps in wounded love (abhimana); haiya bhora — beside Himself

**8.6.** Having said this to Svarupa, Gora
weeps in wounded love, beside Himself.

নরহরি তা হেরিয়া কাঁদে ।
কেমনে কঠিন হিয়া বাঁধে ॥

*narahari tā heriyā kām̐de |*
*kemane kaṭhina hiyā bām̐dhe ||*

*Word for word:* narahari ta heriya kande — Narahari, seeing this, weeps; kemane — how; kathina hiya bandhe — is he to steady (harden) his heart

**8.7.** Narahari, seeing this, weeps:
how is he to steady his heart?

[^02-21]: The signature is "Narahari". The pada is in neither PK nor BR — only in GPT1 and GPT2 (identically); so by
Majumdar's criterion (1959) its authenticity is not proven: padas known only from GPT he regards as unreliable.
B. B. Majumdar in a later work (1961) accepts it as a pada of Narahari Sarakara, known from the collection of Advaitadasa
Pandita Babaji. The language is simple, without Vrajabuli, and there is no sambhoga — this fits the marks of Narahari's
genuine padas named by Majumdar. The khandita is one of the eight heroines of rasa-shastra; in Radha's mood the Lord
speaks to Svarupa as Radha to Lalita (cf. CC Antya 14–19).
[^02-22]: "I came" — in the original "mui āila" (a 3rd-person form with "I", so in both editions of GPT). The speech is
Radha's; the poet conveys what the Lord says in Her mood. Radha's jealousy and wounded pride (mana) are a manifestation
of the highest prema, not of a worldly feeling.

## 9. Narahari (Sarakara) — "gaura sundara mora…" (PK 853)
*Lila: the Lord, sitting in solitude, in Radha's mood reproaches Kamadeva. In PK it is the gaura-chandrika to the section
"reproaches to Kandarpa" (akshepanuraga). Raga tudi (PK), pahadi (GPT1).*[^02-23]

গৌর সুন্দর মোর ।
কি লাগি একলে বসিয়া বিরলে
নয়নে গলয়ে লোর ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*gaura sundara mora |*
*ki lāgi ekale basiyā birale*
*nayane galaye lora || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* gaura sundara mora — my beautiful Gaura; ki lagi — why; ekale basiya birale — sitting alone in solitude; nayane galaye lora — tears flow from His eyes

**9.1.** *(Refrain)* My beautiful Gaura!
Why, sitting alone in solitude, does He shed tears?

হরি-অনুরাগে আকুল অন্তর
গদগদ মৃদু কহে ।
সকল অকাজ করে মনসিজ
এত কি পরাণে সহে ॥

*hari-anurāge ākula antara*
*gadagada mṛdu kahe |*
*sakala akāja kare manasija*
*eta ki parāṇe sahe ||*

*Word for word:* hari-anurage — through love for Hari; akula antara — the heart is shaken; gadagada mridu kahe — He speaks softly, His voice breaking; sakala akaja kare — does every harm; manasija — Manasija (Kamadeva); eta ki parane sahe — can the soul bear so much?

**9.2.** His heart is shaken by love for Hari;
He speaks softly, His voice breaking:
"How much harm Manasija does —
can the soul bear so much?

অবলা-শরীর করে জরজর
মনের মাঝারে পশি ।
কহিতে ঐছন পুরুব-বচন
অবনত মুখ-শশী ॥

*abalā-śarīra kare jarajara*
*manera mājhāre paśi |*
*kahite aichana puruba-bacana*
*abanata mukha-śaśī ||*

*Word for word:* abala-sharira — the body of a weak [woman]; kare jarajara — he has tormented; manera majhare pashi — entering the depth of the heart; kahite aichhana — saying such; puruba-bachana — words of the former [lila]; abanata mukha-shashi — the moonlike face is lowered

**9.3.** The body of a weak woman he has tormented,
entering the very depth of the heart."
Saying such words from the former lila,
He lowers His moonlike face.[^02-24]

প্রলাপের পারা কিবা কহে গোরা
মরম কেহো না জানে ।
পুরুব-চরিত সদা বিভাবিত
দাস নরহরি ভণে ॥

*pralāpera pārā kibā kahe gorā*
*marama keho nā jāne |*
*puruba-carita sadā bibhābita*
*dāsa narahari bhaṇe ||*

*Word for word:* pralapera para — as in pralapa (incoherently, as in a trance); kiba kahe gora — Gora says something; marama keho na jane — no one knows [His] heart's secret; puruba-charita — the former deeds; sada bibhabita — [He is] ever absorbed in them; dasa narahari bhane — sings Narahari Dasa

**9.4.** Incoherently, as if in a trance, Gora says something —
no one knows the secret of His heart;
He is ever absorbed in His former deeds, —
sings Narahari Dasa.

[^02-23]: The signature is "Narahari Dasa"; Majumdar mentions the pada among Narahari Sarakara's gaura-chandrikas in the
akshepanuraga sections of PK; B. B. Majumdar (1961) also gives it as Sarakara's. GPT1 (p. 292, no. 51) has it with
variants. No place is named; the mood of separation from Krishna that the pada describes is, according to CC, the mood of
the last years in Puri (Antya 14–20).
[^02-24]: Manasija ("born of the mind") is Kamadeva. The scriptures call the gopis' love "kama" in name only: "the prema of
the gopis became known as 'kama'" (*Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu* 1.2.285; CC Madhya 8) — there is not a trace of
self-seeking desire in it. "Words from the former lila": Radha's speeches in separation from Krishna.

## 10. Narahari (Sarakara) — "ki lāgi dhulāya dhūsara soṇāra baraṇa gaura-deha…" (PK 1902)
*Lila: the mood of separation — the Lord's body has grown wan (malinangata, one of the ten states of separation). In PK
it is in the section "The ten states" (dasha-dasha). Raga malashi-vala (PK), suhai (GPT1).*[^02-25]

কি লাগি ধুলায় ধূসর সোণার
বরণ গৌর-দেহ ।
আসন ভূষণ সকল তেজল
না জানি কাহার লেহ ॥

*ki lāgi dhulāya dhūsara soṇāra*
*baraṇa gaura-deha |*
*āsana bhūṣaṇa sakala tejala*
*nā jāni kāhāra leha ||*

*Word for word:* ki lagi — why; dhulaya dhusara — grey with dust; sonara barana gaura-deha — Gaura's golden body; asana bhushana — seat and adornments; sakala tejala — He gave up entirely; na jani kahara leha — I know not for whose love

**10.1.** Why has Gaura's golden body
turned grey with dust?
His seat and adornments He has given up entirely:
I know not for whose love.

হরি হরি মলিন গৌরাঙ্গচান্দে ।
উহু উহু করি ফুকরি ফুকরি
উরে পাণি হানি কান্দে ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*hari hari malina gaurāṅgacānde |*
*uhu uhu kari phukari phukari*
*ure pāṇi hāni kānde || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* hari hari — Hari, Hari! (a cry of grief); malina gaurangachande — Gaurangachand has grown wan; uhu uhu kari — moaning "uhu, uhu"; phukari phukari — crying aloud; ure pani hani — striking His breast with His hand; kande — He weeps

**10.2.** *(Refrain)* Hari, Hari! Gaurangachand has grown wan!
Moaning "uhu, uhu", crying aloud,
He beats His breast with His hand and weeps.

ঘামে তিতি গেল সব কলেবর
ছাড়য়ে দীঘ নিশ্বাস ।
রাইয়ের পিরিতি হেন তেন রীতি
কহে নরহরি দাস ॥

*ghāme titi gela saba kalebara*
*chāṛaye dīgha niśvāsa |*
*rāiyera piriti hena tena rīti*
*kahe narahari dāsa ||*

*Word for word:* ghame titi gela — is drenched with sweat; saba kalebara — the whole body; chharaye digha nishvasa — He heaves long sighs; raiyera piriti — of Rai's love; hena tena riti — such is the way; kahe narahari dasa — says Narahari Dasa

**10.3.** His whole body is drenched with sweat,
He heaves long sighs.
Such is the way of Rai's love, —
says Narahari Dasa.[^02-26]

[^02-25]: The signature is "Narahari Dasa"; Majumdar quotes the line "Moaning 'uhu, uhu'…" among Narahari Sarakara's padas on
the mood of separation (biraha). GPT1 (p. 311, no. 11) has it with variants. The ten states (dasha) of separation
according to rasa-shastra (*Ujjvala-nilamani*): anxious brooding, sleeplessness, agitation, emaciation, wanness of the
body (malinangata), incoherent speech (pralapa), sickness, the madness of prema (unmada), swoon (moha), and the last, extreme state. In PK the pada
is headed: "Now — wanness of the body. Sri Mahaprabhu, overcome by this mood".
[^02-26]: "The way of Rai's love": the Lord experiences Radha's separation from Krishna (CC Antya 14–20); this is no worldly
pining but the highest stage of prema — mahabhava.

## 11. Narahari (Sarakara) — "soṇāra baraṇa gaurāṅgasundara pāṇḍura bhai gela deha…" (PK 1908)
*Lila: the mood of separation — "sickness" (vyadhi-dasha): pallor, trembling, sweat, tears, incoherent speech. Raga
kamoda.*[^02-27]

সোণার বরণ গৌরাঙ্গসুন্দর
পাণ্ডুর ভৈ গেল দেহ ।
শীতে ভীত যেন কাঁপায়ে সঘন
সোঙরি পুরব লেহ ॥

*soṇāra baraṇa gaurāṅgasundara*
*pāṇḍura bhai gela deha |*
*śīte bhīta yena kām̐pāye saghana*
*soṅari puraba leha ||*

*Word for word:* sonara barana — golden-hued; gaurangasundara — beautiful Gauranga; pandura bhai gela deha — His body turned pale; shite bhita yena — as if from cold; kapaye saghana — He trembles again and again; sonari puraba leha — remembering a former love

**11.1.** Golden, beautiful Gauranga —
His body has turned pale;
as if from cold, He trembles again and again,
remembering a former love.

কিছু না কহই দীঘ নিশ্বাসই
চিত্রের পুতলী পারা ।
নয়নযুগল বাহি পড়ে জল
যেন মন্দাকিনী-ধারা ॥

*kichu nā kahai dīgha niśvāsai*
*citrera putalī pārā |*
*nayanayugala bāhi paṛe jala*
*yena mandākinī-dhārā ||*

*Word for word:* kichhu na kahai — He says nothing; digha nishvasai — He sighs long; chitrera putali para — like a painted doll; nayana-yugala bahi — from both eyes; pare jala — tears fall; yena mandakini-dhara — like the streams of the Mandakini

**11.2.** He says nothing, only heaves long sighs —
like a painted doll;
from both His eyes tears stream
like the currents of the Mandakini.[^02-28]

ঘামে তিতি গেল সব কলেবর
না জানি কেমন তাপে ।
কখন সঙ্গীত কখন রোদন
কিবা করে পরলাপে ॥

*ghāme titi gela saba kalebara*
*nā jāni kemana tāpe |*
*kakhana saṅgīta kakhana rodana*
*kibā kare paralāpe ||*

*Word for word:* ghame titi gela — drenched with sweat; saba kalebara — the whole body; na jani kemana tape — who knows from what fever; kakhana sangita — now singing; kakhana rodana — now sobbing; kiba kare paralape — He murmurs something incoherent (paralapa = pralapa)

**11.3.** His whole body is drenched with sweat —
who knows from what fever;
now He sings, now He sobs,
He murmurs something incoherent.

কহে নরহরি মোর গৌরহরি
চাহয়ে রঙ্কের পারা ।
হরি হরি বোলে ভুজযুগ তোলে
মরম বুঝিবে কারা ॥

*kahe narahari mora gaurahari*
*cāhaye raṅkera pārā |*
*hari hari bole bhujayuga tole*
*marama bujhibe kārā ||*

*Word for word:* kahe narahari — Narahari says; mora gaurahari — my Gaurahari; chahaye rankera para — gazes (or: begs) like a beggar; hari hari bole — cries "Hari, Hari"; bhuja-yuga tole — raises both arms; marama bujhibe kara — who will fathom [His] heart?

**11.4.** Narahari says: my Gaurahari
gazes about like a beggar;
He cries "Hari, Hari", raising both His arms —
who will fathom His heart?

[^02-27]: The signature is "Narahari"; B. B. Majumdar (1961) gives the pada as Narahari Sarakara's. GPT1 (pp. 317–318, no. 17)
has it with minor variants. In PK it is in the section "The ten states", under the heading "The state of sickness
(vyadhi). Sri Gaurachandra, accordingly".
[^02-28]: The Mandakini is the heavenly Ganga. "A painted doll": stillness (stambha), one of the sattvika-bhavas.

## 12. Vasu Ramananda — "āre mora gaurakiśora. sahachara-kandhe pahum̐…" (PK 1924; GPT1, p. 318)
*Lila: the mood of separation — "the ninth state": leaning on His companions' shoulders, the Lord falls senseless and,
naming Mathura, calls: "O Natha!" According to Majumdar, Puri. Raga pahida (GPT1).*[^02-29]

আরে মোর গৌরকিশোর ।
সহচর-কন্ধে পহুঁ ভুজযুগ আরোপিয়া
নবমী দশায় ভেল ভোর ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*āre mora gaurakiśora |*
*sahacara-kandhe pahum̐ bhujayuga āropiyā*
*nabamī daśāya bhela bhora || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* are mora gaurakishora — ah, my young Gaura!; sahachara-kandhe — on the companions' shoulders; pahu — the Lord; bhuja-yuga aropiya — resting both arms; nabami dashaya — in the ninth state; bhela bhora — lost Himself

**12.1.** *(Refrain)* Ah, my young Gaura!
Resting His arms on His companions' shoulders,
the Lord, in the ninth state, has lost Himself.[^02-30]

পড়িয়া ক্ষিতির পরে মুখে বাক্য নাহি সরে
সাহসে পরশে নাহি কেহ ।
সোণার গৌরহরি কহে হায় মরি মরি
তন্তুক দোসর ভেল দেহ ॥

*paṛiyā kṣitira pare mukhe bākya nāhi sare*
*sāhase paraśe nāhi keha |*
*soṇāra gaurahari kahe hāya mari mari*
*tantuka dosara bhela deha ||*

*Word for word:* pariya kshitira pare — fallen on the ground; mukhe bakya nahi sare — no word leaves His mouth; sahase parashe nahi keha — no one dares to touch Him; sonara gaurahari — golden Gaurahari; kahe haya mari mari — says "Alas, woe is me, woe!" (a cry of anguish); tantuka dosara — the twin of a thread; bhela deha — the body has become

**12.2.** Fallen on the ground, He cannot utter a word;
no one dares to touch Him.
Golden Gaurahari says: "Alas, alas for Me!" —
His body has become thin as a thread.

থীর নয়ন করি মথুরার নাম ধরি
রোয়ে পহু হা নাথ বলিয়া ।
বসু রামানন্দ ভণে গৌরাঙ্গ এমন কেনে
না বুঝিলুঁ কিসের লাগিয়া ॥

*thīra nayana kari mathurāra nāma dhari*
*roye pahu hā nātha baliyā |*
*basu rāmānanda bhaṇe gaurāṅga emana kene*
*nā bujhilum̐ kisera lāgiyā ||*

*Word for word:* thira nayana kari — with a fixed gaze; mathurara nama dhari — naming Mathura; roye pahu — the Lord weeps; ha natha baliya — crying "O Natha!"; basu ramananda bhane — Vasu Ramananda says; gauranga emana kene — why is Gauranga so; na bujhilun kisera lagiya — I have not understood for what reason

**12.3.** With a fixed gaze, naming Mathura,
the Lord weeps: "O Natha!"
Vasu Ramananda says: why is Gauranga so —
I have not understood for what reason.[^02-31]

[^02-29]: The signature is "Vasu Ramananda". In PK the pada stands in the section "The ten states" (no. 1924), but the
available scan of PK vol. 3 lacks printed pp. 147–150, and only the last couplet survives (on p. 151); the full text is
given from GPT1 (no. 20, p. 318), where the pada follows the previous one (PK 1908). Majumdar (who misprints it "PK
1920") assigns the pada to Puri: the body "like a thread" and the weeping with the name of Mathura describe the mood of
the last years, not of Navadvipa.
[^02-30]: The ninth of the ten states of separation is moha, swoon (see note 25).
[^02-31]: Radha, in separation from Krishna who has gone to Mathura, calls Him "Natha" — "Lord" (cf. CC Antya 19–20;
Madhavendra Puri's verse "Ayi dina-dayardra natha…", which the Lord loved to repeat — CC Madhya 4, Antya 8).

## 13. Narahari (Sarakara) — "gambhīrā bhitare gorā rāya…" (PK 1643)
*Lila: the Gambhira — a sleepless night: the Lord laments, weeps, trembles, rubs His face against the walls and cries:
"Where is the Lord of My life?" In PK — "lamentation in the state of mere sleeplessness" (kevala-jagarana-dasha).
According to Majumdar, the quintessence of the Antya-lila of the *Chaitanya-charitamrita*. Raga — the same as that of
the preceding pada (PK).*[^02-32]

গম্ভিরা ভিতরে গোরা রায় ।
জাগিয়া রজনি পোহায় ॥

*gambhirā bhitare gorā rāya |*
*jāgiyā rajani pohāya ||*

*Word for word:* gambhira bhitare — inside the Gambhira; gora raya — Gora Raya; jagiya — keeping awake; rajani pohaya — passes the night

**13.1.** In the Gambhira Gora Raya
passes the night without sleep.

খেণে খেণে করয়ে বিলাপ ।
খেণে রোয়ত খেণে কাঁপ ॥

*kheṇe kheṇe karaye bilāpa |*
*kheṇe royata kheṇe kām̐pa ||*

*Word for word:* khene khene karaye bilapa — again and again He laments; khene royata — now He weeps; khene kanpa — now He trembles

**13.2.** Again and again He laments,
now He weeps, now He trembles.

খেণে ভিতে মুখ শির ঘসে ।
কোই না রহু পহু-পাশে ॥

*kheṇe bhite mukha śira ghase |*
*koi nā rahu pahu-pāśe ||*

*Word for word:* khene bhite — now against the wall; mukha shira ghase — He rubs His face and head; koi na rahu — no one stays; pahu-pashe — beside the Lord

**13.3.** Now He rubs His face and head against the wall —
no one is beside the Lord.[^02-33]

খেণে কান্দে তুলি দুই হাথ ।
কোথায় আমার প্রাণনাথ ॥

*kheṇe kānde tuli dui hātha |*
*kothāya āmāra prāṇanātha ||*

*Word for word:* khene kande — now He weeps; tuli dui hatha — raising both hands; kothaya amara prananatha — where is the Lord of my life?

**13.4.** Now He weeps, raising both His arms:
"Where is the Lord of My life?"

নরহরি কহে মোর গোরা ।
রাই-প্রেমে হইলা বিভোরা ॥

*narahari kahe mora gorā |*
*rāi-preme hailā bibhorā ||*

*Word for word:* narahari kahe — Narahari says; mora gora — my Gora; rai-preme — in Rai's love; haila bibhora — is lost

**13.5.** Narahari says: my Gora
is lost in the love of Rai.

[^02-32]: The signature is "Narahari"; Majumdar places the pada among Narahari Sarakara's Puri padas. Neither the archive.org
OCR nor the new recognition of PK contains the text — it has been read from the scan (vol. 3, printed p. 30); GPT1
(p. 314, no. 5) and GPT2 have it with variants. The Gambhira is the small inner room in Kashi Mishra's house where the
Lord spent His last years (CC Antya 6, 14–20).
[^02-33]: According to CC (Antya 19), one night the Lord, in the agony of separation, rubbed His face against the walls of
the Gambhira until it was covered with wounds; after that Svarupa asked Shankara Pandita to sleep at the Lord's feet.
Here is the same state: "no one is beside Him".

## 14. Narahari (Sarakara) — "gaurāṅga-chāndera bhāba kahane nā yāya…" (PK 832)
*Lila: in solitude the Lord tells His companions: "I will throw Myself into the sea." In PK it is the gaura-chandrika to
the section "reproaches to oneself" (akshepanuraga). According to Majumdar, Puri: the pada foreshadows the Lord's fall
into the sea. Raga tudi.*[^02-34]

গৌরাঙ্গ-চান্দের ভাব কহনে না যায় ।
বিরলে বসিয়া পহু করে হায় হায় ॥

*gaurāṅga-cāndera bhāba kahane nā yāya |*
*birale basiyā pahu kare hāya hāya ||*

*Word for word:* gauranga-chandera bhaba — Gaurangachand's mood; kahane na yaya — cannot be told; birale basiya — sitting in solitude; pahu kare haya haya — the Lord moans "alas, alas!"

**14.1.** Gaurangachand's mood cannot be put into words:
sitting in solitude, the Lord moans: "Alas, alas!"

প্রিয় পারিষদগণ পুছয়ে তাহারে ।
কহে মুঞি ঝাঁপ দিব সমুদ্র মাঝারে ॥

*priya pāriṣadagaṇa puchaye tāhāre |*
*kahe muñi jhām̐pa diba samudra mājhāre ||*

*Word for word:* priya parishada-gana — the dear companions; puchhaye tahare — question Him; kahe — He says; munyi jhanpa diba — I will leap; samudra majhare — into the sea

**14.2.** His dear companions question Him —
He says: "I will throw Myself into the sea!"[^02-35]

করিলুঁ দারুণ প্রেম আপনা আপনি ।
দু কুলে কলঙ্ক হৈল না যায় পরাণি ॥

*karilum̐ dāruṇa prema āpanā āpani |*
*du kule kalaṅka haila nā yāya parāṇi ||*

*Word for word:* karilun daruna prema — I began a cruel love; apana apani — by my own will; du kule kalanka haila — disgrace fell on both families; na yaya parani — yet life does not depart (goes on)

**14.3.** "By My own will I began this cruel love:
disgrace has fallen on both families — and still life goes on."[^02-36]

এত কহি গোরাচান্দ ছাড়য়ে নিশ্বাস ।
মরম বুঝিয়া কহে নরহরিদাস ॥

*eta kahi gorācānda chāṛaye niśvāsa |*
*marama bujhiyā kahe naraharidāsa ||*

*Word for word:* eta kahi — having said this; gorachanda chharaye nishvasa — Gorachand heaves a sigh; marama bujhiya — understanding [His] heart; kahe narahari-dasa — Narahari Dasa speaks

**14.4.** Having said this, Gorachand sighs deeply;
understanding His heart, Narahari Dasa speaks.

[^02-34]: The signature is "Narahari Dasa"; Majumdar ascribes the pada to Narahari Sarakara and to Puri. GPT1 (p. 299, no. 25)
has it with variants. In PK the pada stands as the gaura-chandrika to the words of Radha reproaching Herself for Her love
of Krishna.
[^02-35]: Instead of "into the sea", MS "ka" of PK, GPT1 and GPT2 read "into the waters of the Yamuna", MSS "cha" and
"P-R-Sa" — "into the Yamuna". In Radha's mood the sea is the Yamuna to the Lord: according to CC (Antya 18), one night the
Lord, taking the sea for the Yamuna, threw Himself into it, and a fisherman drew Him out with his net. The PK reading
("into the sea") points to Puri; the reading "into the Yamuna" conveys Radha's words.
[^02-36]: "Both families" (du kule) — the father's family and the husband's; the words of Radha as parakiya. Her readiness to
give up everything for Krishna is the highest expression of prema, not worldly despair.

## 15. Vasu Ghosha — "siṃhadvāra teji gorā samudra āṛe dhāya…" (PK 1662)
*Lila: the divine madness of prema (divya-unmada): the Lord runs from the Lion Gate towards the sea, asking everyone:
"Where is Krishna?", and falls senseless. In PK — the section "Divya-unmada. Here — Sri Mahaprabhu". According to
Majumdar, an eyewitness's testimony whose vividness is matched only by Raghunatha Dasa. Raga suhai.*[^02-37]

সিংহদ্বার তেজি গোরা সমুদ্র আড়ে ধায় ।
কোথা কৃষ্ণ কোথা কৃষ্ণ সভারে সুধায় ॥

*siṃhadvāra teji gorā samudra āṛe dhāya |*
*kothā kṛṣṇa kothā kṛṣṇa sabhāre sudhāya ||*

*Word for word:* simhadvara teji — leaving the Lion Gate; gora — Gora; samudra are dhaya — runs towards the sea; kotha krishna kotha krishna — "where is Krishna, where is Krishna?"; sabhare sudhaya — He asks everyone

**15.1.** Leaving the Lion Gate, Gora runs towards the sea,
asking everyone: "Where is Krishna? Where is Krishna?"

চৌদিকে ভকতগণ হরি-গুণ গায় ।
মাঝে কনয়া-গিরি ধূলায় লুটায় ॥

*caudike bhakatagaṇa hari-guṇa gāya |*
*mājhe kanayā-giri dhūlāya luṭāya ||*

*Word for word:* chaudike bhakatagana — all around the devotees; hari-guna gaya — sing the glories of Hari; majhe — in the middle; kanaya-giri — a golden mountain; dhulaya lutaya — rolls in the dust

**15.2.** All around, the devotees sing the glories of Hari,
and in their midst a golden mountain rolls in the dust.

আছাড়িয়া পড়ে অঙ্গ ভূমে গড়ি যায় ।
দীঘল শরীর গোরা পড়ি মুরছায় ॥

*āchāṛiyā paṛe aṅga bhūme gaṛi yāya |*
*dīghala śarīra gorā paṛi murachāya ||*

*Word for word:* achhariya pare anga — the body falls headlong; bhume gari yaya — rolls on the ground; dighala sharira gora — tall-bodied Gora; pari murachhaya — falls senseless

**15.3.** He falls headlong, He rolls on the ground;
tall Gora falls senseless.[^02-38]

উত্তান-শয়ন মুখে ফেনা বাহিরায় ।
বাসুদেব ঘোষের হিয়া বিদরিয়া যায় ॥

*uttāna-śayana mukhe phenā bāhirāya |*
*bāsudeba ghoṣera hiyā bidariyā yāya ||*

*Word for word:* uttana-shayana — lying on His back; mukhe phena bahiraya — foam comes from His mouth; vasudeva ghoshera hiya — Vasudeva Ghosha's heart; bidariya yaya — is breaking

**15.4.** He lies on His back, foam comes from His mouth;
Vasudeva Ghosha's heart is breaking.

[^02-37]: The signature is "Vasudeva Ghosha". Majumdar counts the pada among Vasu Ghosha's historical padas (the run to the
sea in Puri). GPT1 (p. 314, no. 6) and GPT2 have it with minor variants. The Lion Gate (Simha-dvara) is the main, eastern
gate of Jagannatha's temple. Cf. CC Antya 14 (seeing the sand hill Chataka-parvata, the Lord took it for Govardhana and
ran towards it) and Antya 17–18; Raghunatha Dasa's *Gauranga-stava-kalpataru*. In PK (no. 1663) and GPT (no. 7) there
follows a pada on how the Lord, coming to Himself, sees Svarupa and Ramaraya before Him: in PK it is unsigned, in the
"P-R-Sa" MS it bears the signature of Govinda Dasa, in GPT that of Vasu Ghosha; it is not included in this chapter.
[^02-38]: Falling, trembling, foam at the mouth, unconsciousness are sattvika-bhavas and manifestations of mahabhava,
described in CC as well (Antya 14, 17); this is not illness but the working of the highest prema.
