# Chapter 3. Padas of Radha's Mood: Navadvipa, Sannyasa, Puri

*Narahari Sarakara's Navadvipa padas in which the Lord experiences Radha's mood (in the *Padakalpataru* they stand as
gaura-chandrikas to the sections on purvaraga, vasakasajja, vipralabdha and khandita) and which Majumdar
(*Sri-Chaitanya-chariter upadan*, ch. 2) regards as descriptions of real moods seen by an eyewitness; padas by Ananta and
Gauridasa on Gaura and Nitai, on the sannyasa and on Nityananda's "market"; then Puri and Navadvipa in the years of
separation: Sarvabhauma, the waiting for the Lord and a dream of His return, Radha's mood in the company of Svarupa, the
divine madness of prema. The text follows the *Padakalpataru* (PK), the *Bhakti-ratnakara* (BR), the
*Kshanada-gita-chintamani* (KGC) and the *Gaura-pada-tarangini* (GPT1 — 1st ed., 1903; GPT2 — 2nd ed., 1934); the
Bengali original, variants and word-for-word translation are in the full version of the book.*

## 1. Narahari (Sarakara) — "gaurāṅga ṭhekila pāke…" (PK 2122; BR, p. 924)
*Lila: Navadvipa — the Lord in Krishna's mood: the Ganga seems to Him the Yamuna, a flowering garden — Vrindavana; He asks
for yellow cloth and a flute and embraces Gadadhara. According to Majumdar — an eyewitness's pada (1509). Raga mallar
(PK, KGC, GPT), ashavari (BR).*[^03-1]

গৌরাঙ্গ ঠেকিল পাকে ।
ভাবের আবেশে রাধা রাধা বলি ডাকে ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*gaurāṅga ṭhekila pāke |*
*bhābera ābeśe rādhā rādhā bali ḍāke || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* gauranga — Gauranga; thekila pake — was caught in a whirlpool (a noose); bhabera abeshe — absorbed in bhava; radha radha boli dake — calls "Radha, Radha!"

**1.1.** *(Refrain)* Gauranga is caught in a whirlpool:
absorbed in bhava, He calls, "Radha, Radha!"[^03-2]

সুরধুনী দেখি পহু যমুনার ভানে ।
ফুল-বন দেখি বৃন্দাবন পড়ে মনে ॥

*suradhunī dekhi pahu yamunāra bhāne |*
*phula-bana dekhi bṛndābana paṛe mane ||*

*Word for word:* suradhuni dekhi — seeing the Suradhuni (the Ganga); pahu — the Lord; yamunara bhane — takes it for the Yamuna; phula-bana dekhi — seeing a flower garden; vrindavana pare mane — remembers Vrindavana

**1.2.** Seeing the Suradhuni, the Lord takes it for the Yamuna;
seeing a flowering garden, He remembers Vrindavana.

পূরব-আবেশেতে তিরিভঙ্গ হয়ে ।
পীত বসন আর মুরলী চাহয়ে ॥

*pūraba-ābeśete tiribhaṅga haye |*
*pīta basana āra muralī cāhaye ||*

*Word for word:* puraba-abeshete — in the mood of [His] former [lila]; tiribhanga haye — bending in three places; pita basana — yellow cloth; ara murali — and the flute; chahaye — asks for

**1.3.** In the mood of His former lila He stands bent in three places
and asks for yellow cloth and a flute.[^03-3]

প্রিয় গদাধর পহু করিয়া ত কোলে ।
কোথা ছিলা কোথা ছিলা গদগদ বোলে ॥

*priya gadādhara pahu kariyā ta kole |*
*kothā chilā kothā chilā gadagada bole ||*

*Word for word:* priya gadadhara — the beloved Gadadhara; pahu — the Lord; kariya ta kole — taking into His embrace; kotha chhila kotha chhila — "where were you? where were you?"; gadagada bole — says in a faltering voice

**1.4.** Taking His beloved Gadadhara into His embrace,
the Lord says in a faltering voice, "Where were you? Where were you?"

ভাব বুঝি পণ্ডিত রহে বাম পাশে ।
না বুঝয়ে এহ রঙ্গ নরহরি দাসে ॥

*bhāba bujhi paṇḍita rahe bāma pāśe |*
*nā bujhaye eha raṅga narahari dāse ||*

*Word for word:* bhaba bujhi — understanding the mood; pandita — the Pandita (Gadadhara); rahe bama pashe — stays at the left side; na bujhaye — does not fathom; eha ranga — this play; narahari dase — Narahari Dasa

**1.5.** Understanding His mood, the Pandita stays at His left.
Narahari Dasa does not fathom this play.[^03-4]

[^03-1]: The signature is "Narahari Dasa". Narahari Chakravarti quotes the pada in BR (wave 12, p. 924) with the note "a song
of Sri Narahari Sarakara Thakura" — the only pada signed "Narahari" in BR that he expressly ascribes to Sarakara, and Majumdar
puts it first among Narahari's Navadvipa padas. It is also found in KGC (27th kshanada, as a gaura-chandrika) and in GPT1
(p. 280, no. 9); in PK it stands in the section "The form of Sri Gauranga, etc." In BR it is preceded by the words: "By this
road Gora goes to the bank of the Suradhuni… He calls, 'Radha, Radha!'" Cf. CC Antya 18: in Puri the sea seems to the
Lord to be the Yamuna.
[^03-2]: Pak — a whirlpool, a noose: the Lord is as if drawn into the whirlpool of bhava. Suradhuni ("the river of the gods") is
the Ganga.
[^03-3]: The threefold-bending pose (tribhanga), yellow cloth (pitambara) and flute are Krishna's form; the "former lila" is His
Vrindavana lila. Here the Lord is in Krishna's mood, while Gadadhara Pandita, according to the *Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika*
(vv. 147–153), is a manifestation of Radha in Gaura's lila.
[^03-4]: Krishna's left side is Radha's place. Instead of "the Lord taking into His embrace", PK manuscripts ka, kha, gha, cha,
KGC and GPT read simply "taking into His embrace", BR — "clasping Gadadhara to His breast". The humble "does not fathom" in
the signature is Narahari's usual formula.

## 2. Narahari (Sarakara) — "mo mena manu gorācāndere dekhiyā…" (PK 103)
*Lila: Navadvipa — Gaura walks along the road to the Ganga; a young townswoman tells how she saw Him. In PK — a
gaura-chandrika to purvaraga (love dawning at first sight). According to Majumdar — Narahari Sarakara's pada about a real
mood, though it contains expressions of nagari-bhava. Raga dhanashi.*[^03-5]

মো মেন মনু গোরাচান্দেরে দেখিয়া ।
অপরূপ রূপ কাচা কাঞ্চন জিনিয়া ॥

*mo mena manu gorācāndere dekhiyā |*
*aparūpa rūpa kācā kāñcana jiniyā ||*

*Word for word:* mo — I; mena (mene) manu — as if died (?); gorachandere dekhiya — seeing Gorachand; aparupa rupa — a wondrous form; kancha kanchana jiniya — surpassing pure (unworked) gold

**2.1.** Seeing Gorachand, I all but died:[^03-6]
wondrous is His form — it outshines pure gold.

খেনে শীঘ্রগতি চলে মারে মালসাট ।
খেনে থির হৈয়া চলে সুরধুনী-বাট ॥

*khene śīghragati cale māre mālasāṭa |*
*khene thira haiyā cale suradhunī-bāṭa ||*

*Word for word:* khene — now; shighra-gati chale — walks swiftly; mare malsat — slaps His shoulders (like a wrestler); khene thira haiya — now, grown calm; chale suradhuni-bat — walks along the road to the Suradhuni

**2.2.** Now He walks swiftly, slapping His shoulders like a wrestler,
now, grown calm, He steps slowly along the road to the Suradhuni.[^03-7]

অরুণ নয়ানে ঘন চাহে অনিবার ।
হানিলে নয়ান-বাণ হিয়ার মাঝার ॥

*aruṇa nayāne ghana cāhe anibāra |*
*hānile nayāna-bāṇa hiyāra mājhāra ||*

*Word for word:* aruna nayane — with reddish eyes; ghana chahe anibara — gazes again and again, unceasingly; hanile nayana-bana — shot the arrows of His glances; hiyara majhara — into the midst of the heart

**2.3.** With His reddish eyes He gazes again and again, unblinking —
and has driven the arrows of His glances into the very heart.

আজানুলম্বিত ভুজ দোলে দুই দিগে ।
যুবতি যৌবন দিতে চাহে অনুরাগে ॥

*ājānulambita bhuja dole dui dige |*
*yubati yaubana dite cāhe anurāge ||*

*Word for word:* ajanulambita bhuja — arms reaching to the knees; dole dui dige — sway on both sides; yubati — young women; yaubana dite chahe — long to give [their] youth; anurage — in love

**2.4.** His arms, reaching to the knees, sway on either side;
young women, in love, long to give Him their youth.[^03-8]

খেনে মন্দ মন্দ হাসি খেনে উতরোল ।
না বুঝিয়া নরহরি হইল বিভোর ॥

*khene manda manda hāsi khene utarola |*
*nā bujhiyā narahari haila bibhora ||*

*Word for word:* khene manda manda hasi — now smiling softly; khene utarola — now in loud joy; na bujhiya — not understanding; narahari haila bibhora — Narahari became lost in rapture

**2.5.** Now He smiles softly, now He shouts for joy;
not fathoming it, Narahari is lost in rapture.

[^03-5]: The signature is "Narahari". In PK the pada is the second gaura-chandrika to the section "Purvaraga — the age of
transition" (after a pada by Radhamohana); in GPT1 — p. 170, no. 41 (raga dhanashi). Majumdar discusses it among the nine
Navadvipa padas of Narahari Sarakara in PK and cites the line "With His reddish eyes He gazes again and again".
[^03-6]: The opening is obscure: "mo mena manu" (PK; ms. ka and GPT1 — "mo mene manu"). We translate tentatively: "mo" — "I",
"manu" — an old form for "I died" (cf. "malum̐"); "I think I perished" is also possible. The sense is the shock of seeing Gaura.
[^03-7]: "Slapping one's shoulders" (mālasāṭa mārā) is the gesture of a wrestler challenging to a bout; in another pada of GPT the
Lord does the same in kirtana ("now He slaps His shoulders, now calls 'Krishna!', now 'Radha!'"). The Suradhuni is the Ganga.
[^03-8]: The words about young women belong to the language of nagari-bhava (Gaura as the nagara, the beloved of the
townswomen); we translate them faithfully to the author. Vrindavana Dasa stresses that in this incarnation the Lord never
looked at another man's wife; the Gaudiya tradition (Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja, Bhaktisiddhanta) does not
accept the worship of Gaura in the spirit of "gaura-nagari". In PK the pada is a gaura-chandrika: it sets the tone for
Radha's purvaraga, and the attraction here is an image of prema for Krishna, not of a worldly feeling.

## 3. Narahari (Sarakara) — "ki lāgiyā mora gaura-sundara…" (PK 307)
*Lila: Navadvipa — the Lord in the mood of Radha as vasakasajja (the heroine who adorns herself and the bower while
awaiting her beloved) dresses Himself and waits for Krishna. In PK — a gaura-chandrika to "vasakasajja in spring".
According to Majumdar — a description of a real mood; the Lord's dress and ornaments in the Navadvipa padas are not
invented. Raga dhanashi.*[^03-9]

কি লাগিয়া মোর গৌর-সুন্দর
বসিয়া গৃহের মাঝে ।
বসন আসন রতন-ভূষণ
সাজয়ে অঙ্গের মাঝে ॥

*ki lāgiyā mora gaura-sundara*
*basiyā gṛhera mājhe |*
*basana āsana ratana-bhūṣaṇa*
*sājaye aṅgera mājhe ||*

*Word for word:* ki lagiya — why; mora gaura-sundara — my beautiful Gaura; basiya grihera majhe — sitting in the house; basana asana — clothes, seat; ratana-bhushana — jewelled ornaments; sajaye angera majhe — arranges on His body

**3.1.** Why does my beautiful Gaura
sit in the house
and, preparing clothes, a seat and jewelled ornaments,
adorn His body with them?

আপন বপুর ছাহ হেরিয়া
চমকি উঠয়ে মনে ।
কি লাগি অবহুঁ না মিলল পহুঁ
এত না বিলম্ব কেনে ॥

*āpana bapura chāha heriyā*
*camaki uṭhaye mane |*
*ki lāgi abahum̐ nā milala pahum̐*
*eta nā bilamba kene ||*

*Word for word:* apana bapura chhaha heriya — seeing the shadow of His own body; chamaki uthaye mane — starts in His heart; ki lagi — why; abahun na milala pahun — has the Lord not come even now; eta na bilamba kene — why such delay

**3.2.** Seeing the shadow of His own body,
He starts in His heart:
"Why has the Lord not come even now?
Why does He delay so long?"[^03-10]

কহে নরহরি মোর গৌরহরি
ভাবিয়া রাইয়ের দশা ।
সজল নয়ানে চাহে পথ পানে
কহে গদ গদ ভাষা ॥

*kahe narahari mora gaurahari*
*bhābiyā rāiyera daśā |*
*sajala nayāne cāhe patha pāne*
*kahe gada gada bhāṣā ||*

*Word for word:* kahe narahari — Narahari says; mora gaurahari — my Gaurahari; bhabiya raiyera dasha — thinking of Rai's condition; sajala nayane — with tearful eyes; chahe patha pane — looks at the road; kahe gada gada bhasha — speaks in a faltering voice

**3.3.** Narahari says: my Gaurahari,
thinking of Rai's condition,
looks at the road with tear-filled eyes
and speaks in a faltering voice.

[^03-9]: The signature is "Narahari". In GPT1 (p. 306, no. 22) with minor variants (section "vasakasajja"). Majumdar adduces
the pada as an example that Narahari's gaura-chandrikas are not conventional preludes but descriptions of moods he saw;
that the Lord wore ornaments in Navadvipa is attested by the sannyasa pada PK 2241 (chapter 2, no. 5): "golden
armlets… — all that enchanting attire He gave up."
[^03-10]: A shadow mistaken for the beloved's step is a usual trait of the vasakasajja in rasa-shastra: Radha starts at every
rustle, thinking Krishna has come. The Lord experiences Her waiting; this is a manifestation of prema, not of worldly
longing.

## 4. Narahari (Sarakara) — "hema darapaṇi gaurāṅga-lābaṇi…" (PK 316)
*Lila: Navadvipa — the Lord in the mood of Radha as vipralabdha (the deceived heroine whose beloved did not come to the
tryst) rolls in the dust, calls "Lord of My life!" and weeps before His companions. In PK — a gaura-chandrika to
"vipralabdha in spring". According to Majumdar — a pada of vipralambha (separation). Raga bhairavi.*[^03-11]

হেম দরপণি গৌরাঙ্গ-লাবণি
ধূলায় ধূসর কাঁতি ।
আসন বসন তেজিয়া রোদন
ব্রজ-বিলাসিনী ভাঁতি ॥

*hema darapaṇi gaurāṅga-lābaṇi*
*dhūlāya dhūsara kām̐ti |*
*āsana basana tejiyā rodana*
*braja-bilāsinī bhām̐ti ||*

*Word for word:* hema darapani — a golden mirror; gauranga-labani — Gauranga's beauty; dhulaya dhusara kanti — the lustre grey with dust; asana basana tejiya — leaving seat and clothes; rodana — weeping; braja-bilasini bhanti — like a beauty of Vraja

**4.1.** Gauranga's beauty is like a golden mirror,
yet its lustre is grey with dust;
leaving His seat and clothes, He weeps
like a beauty of Vraja.

হরি হরি বলি প্রাণনাথ করি
ধরণী ধরিয়া উঠে ।
কোথা না যাইব কাহারে কহিব
পরাণ ফাটিয়া উঠে ॥

*hari hari bali prāṇanātha kari*
*dharaṇī dhariyā uṭhe |*
*kothā nā yāiba kāhāre kahiba*
*parāṇa phāṭiyā uṭhe ||*

*Word for word:* hari hari boli — crying "Hari, Hari!"; prananatha kari — calling [Him] Lord of life; dharani dhariya uthe — rises holding the ground; kotha na yaiba — where shall I go; kahare kahiba — whom shall I tell; parana phatiya uthe — the heart is bursting

**4.2.** Crying "Hari, Hari!", calling Him Lord of His life,
He rises, leaning on the ground:
"Where shall I go? Whom shall I tell?
My heart is breaking!"

সহচরগণে করিয়া রোদনে
কহয়ে বদন তুলি ।
আমার পরাণ করয়ে যেমন
বেদন কাহারে বলি ॥

*sahacaragaṇe kariyā rodane*
*kahaye badana tuli |*
*āmāra parāṇa karaye yemana*
*bedana kāhāre bali ||*

*Word for word:* sahacharagane — to the companions; kariya rodane — weeping; kahaye badana tuli — speaks raising His face; amara parana karaye yemana — what my heart is going through; bedana kahare boli — to whom shall I tell the pain

**4.3.** Weeping, He speaks to His companions,
raising His face:
"What is happening to My heart —
to whom can I tell this pain?"

নরহরি দাসে গদ গদ ভাষে
কহয়ে গৌরাঙ্গ মোর ।
আন ছলে বুলে উদ্ধারে সকলে
সদা রাধা-প্রেমে ভোর ॥

*narahari dāse gada gada bhāṣe*
*kahaye gaurāṅga mora |*
*āna chale bule uddhāre sakale*
*sadā rādhā-preme bhora ||*

*Word for word:* narahari dase — Narahari Dasa; gada gada bhashe — in a faltering voice; kahaye — says; gauranga mora — my Gauranga; ana chhale bule — wanders under another pretext; uddhare sakale — delivers all; sada radha-preme bhora — ever drunk with Radha's love

**4.4.** Narahari Dasa says in a faltering voice:
my Gauranga
wanders under another pretext, delivering all —
yet He Himself is ever drunk with Radha's love.[^03-12]

[^03-11]: The signature is "Narahari Dasa". S. Ray notes that the pada is found in only one PK manuscript (kha) and placed it in
the text because the other sections of this pallava open with gaura-chandrikas. In GPT1 (p. 307, no. 27) with minor
variants. B. B. Majumdar (1961) gives the pada from a Baranagar manuscript with the reading "aśana basana" ("food and clothes")
instead of "āsana basana" ("seat and clothes").
[^03-12]: Cf. CC Adi 4: the external reason for the Lord's appearance is to give the world the holy name and prema, the internal
one — to taste Radha's love. Narahari expresses the same thought: delivering the world is the "pretext", while the Lord's
heart is ever in Radha's prema.

## 5. Narahari (Sarakara) — "āre mora āre mora gaurāṅga rāya…" (PK 408)
*Lila: Navadvipa — the Lord in the mood of Radha as khandita (the heroine whose beloved comes at dawn bearing the marks of a
tryst with another) angrily reproaches Krishna. In PK — a gaura-chandrika to the section "Khandita — the impatient
(adhira) madhya". According to Majumdar — Narahari Sarakara's pada of the khandita. Raga suhai.*[^03-13]

আরে মোর আরে মোর গৌরাঙ্গ রায় ।
পুরুব প্রেমভরে মৃদু চলি যায় ॥

*āre mora āre mora gaurāṅga rāya |*
*puruba premabhare mṛdu cali yāya ||*

*Word for word:* are mora are mora — ah, my, ah, my; gauranga raya — Gauranga Raya; puruba prema-bhare — full of former love; mridu chali yaya — walks slowly

**5.1.** Ah, my, ah, my Gauranga Raya!
Full of His former love, He walks with slow steps.

অরুণ নয়ন মুখ বিরস হইয়া ।
কোপে কহয়ে পহুঁ গদ-গদ হিয়া ॥

*aruṇa nayana mukha birasa haiyā |*
*kope kahaye pahum̐ gada-gada hiyā ||*

*Word for word:* aruna nayana — eyes reddened; mukha birasa haiya — face darkened; kope kahaye pahun — in anger the Lord says; gada-gada hiya — His heart trembling (haltingly)

**5.2.** His eyes have reddened, His face has darkened;
in anger, His heart trembling, the Lord speaks haltingly:

জানলুঁ তোহারে তোর কপট পিরীতি ।
যা সঞে বঞ্চিলা নিশি তাহা কর নতি ॥

*jānalum̐ tohāre tora kapaṭa pirīti |*
*yā sañe bañcilā niśi tāhā kara nati ||*

*Word for word:* janalun tohare — I know You; tora kapata piriti — Your false love; ya sanne banchila nishi — with whom You spent the night; taha kara nati — to her bow down

**5.3.** "I know You, I know Your false love!
Go and bow to her with whom You spent the night."[^03-14]

এত কহি গৌরাঙ্গের গর-গর মন ।
ভাবের তরঙ্গে যেন নিশি-জাগরণ ॥

*eta kahi gaurāṅgera gara-gara mana |*
*bhābera taraṅge yena niśi-jāgaraṇa ||*

*Word for word:* eta kahi — having said this; gaurangera gara-gara mana — Gauranga's mind is overwhelmed; bhabera tarange — in the waves of bhava; yena nishi-jagarana — as if after a night's vigil

**5.4.** Having said this, Gauranga is wholly overcome by bhava:
in the waves of bhava He is as if after a sleepless night.

কহে নরহরি রাধার ভাবে হৈল হেন ।
পাই আশোয়াস বঞ্চিত হৈল যেন ॥

*kahe narahari rādhāra bhābe haila hena |*
*pāi āśoyāsa bañcita haila yena ||*

*Word for word:* kahe narahari — Narahari says; radhara bhabe — in Radha's mood; haila hena — He became thus; pai ashoyasa — having received assurance; banchita haila yena — as if deceived

**5.5.** Narahari says: in Radha's mood He has become
like one who was given a promise and deceived.

[^03-13]: The signature is "Narahari". In GPT1 (p. 309, no. 4) with minor variants (section "khandita, mana"). Majumdar cites
the line "I know You, I know Your false love". The khandita is one of the eight heroines of rasa-shastra
(*Ujjvala-nilamani*).
[^03-14]: The words of Radha as khandita to Krishna, who has come in the morning from Her rival. Radha's jealousy and pique
(mana) are a manifestation of the highest prema, not a worldly feeling; the Lord experiences them in Her mood.

## 6. Narahari (Sarakara) — "gorā pahum̐ birale basiyā…" (PK 421)
*Lila: Navadvipa — the Lord in the mood of Radha as khandita sits alone after a sleepless night and weeps: "Having given Me
hope, You deceived Me all night." In PK — a gaura-chandrika to "khandita — the composed-impatient (dhira-adhira) madhya".
According to Majumdar — Narahari Sarakara's pada of the khandita. Raga gandhara.*[^03-15]

গোরা পহুঁ বিরলে বসিয়া ।
অবনত বদন করিয়া ॥

*gorā pahum̐ birale basiyā |*
*abanata badana kariyā ||*

*Word for word:* gora pahun — Lord Gora; birale basiya — sitting alone; abanata badana kariya — lowering His face

**6.1.** Lord Gora, sitting alone,
has lowered His face.

ভাবাবেশে ঢুলু ঢুলু আঁখি ।
রজনি জাগিল হেন সাখি ॥

*bhābābeśe ḍhulu ḍhulu ām̐khi |*
*rajani jāgila hena sākhi ||*

*Word for word:* bhababeshe — in bhava; dhulu dhulu ankhi — eyes drooping; rajani jagila — kept awake all night; hena sakhi — such is the witness

**6.2.** In bhava His eyes are heavy with sleep —
the sleepless night is witness to it.

বিরস-বদনে কহে বাণী ।
আশা দিয়া বঞ্চিল রজনী ॥

*birasa-badane kahe bāṇī |*
*āśā diyā bañcila rajanī ||*

*Word for word:* birasa-badane — with a faded face; kahe bani — speaks words; asha diya — having given hope; banchila rajani — [You] deceived [me] all night

**6.3.** With a faded face He says:
"Having given Me hope, You deceived Me all night."

কান্দিয়া কহয়ে গোরা রায় ।
এ দুখ সহনে নাহি যায় ॥

*kāndiyā kahaye gorā rāya |*
*e dukha sahane nāhi yāya ||*

*Word for word:* kandiya kahaye — weeping, says; gora raya — Gora Raya; e dukha — this pain; sahane nahi yaya — cannot be borne

**6.4.** Weeping, Gora Raya says:
"I cannot bear this pain."

কাতরে কহয়ে সবিষাদ ।
নরহরি মাগে পরসাদ ॥

*kātare kahaye sabiṣāda |*
*narahari māge parasāda ||*

*Word for word:* katare — sorrowfully; kahaye sabishada — speaks full of grief; narahari mage — Narahari begs; parasada — for grace (prasada)

**6.5.** He laments, full of grief;
Narahari begs for grace.[^03-16]

[^03-15]: The signature is "Narahari". In GPT1 (p. 309, no. 5) with minor variants, immediately after the preceding pada
(PK 408). Majumdar cites the lines "Having given Me hope, You deceived Me all night, — weeping, says Gora Raya".
[^03-16]: "Begs for grace" — in the original "begs for prasada" (parasāda): the Lord's mercy.

## 7. Ananta Dasa — "āpāda-mastaka prema-dhārā barikhata…" (PK 2208)
*Praise of Gauranga: from head to foot He pours streams of prema; at His qualities wood and stone melt, beasts and birds
weep; the poet asks only one thing — to sing of Gauranga, wandering from land to land. In PK — the section "Sri Gaurachandra —
in another way". Majumdar names the pada among Ananta's padas on Gauranga's mood. Raga mangala.*[^03-17]

আপাদ-মস্তক প্রেম-ধারা বরিখত
চৌদিগে ঝলকত কিরণে ।
মত্ত গজেন্দ্র জিনি গমন সুলাবণি
চাঁদ উদয় করু চরণে ॥

*āpāda-mastaka prema-dhārā barikhata*
*caudige jhalakata kiraṇe |*
*matta gajendra jini gamana sulābaṇi*
*cām̐da udaya karu caraṇe ||*

*Word for word:* apada-mastaka — from foot to head; prema-dhara barikhata — rains streams of prema; chaudige jhalakata kirane — rays flash all around; matta gajendra jini — surpassing an intoxicated lordly elephant; gamana sulabani — a lovely gait; chanda udaya karu charane — moons rise at the feet

**7.1.** From head to foot He pours down streams of prema,
His rays flash in every direction;
His gait is lovelier than a lordly elephant's,
moons rise at His feet.[^03-18]

কেমন বিধাতা সে গৌরাঙ্গ-চাঁদের দে
গঢ়িল আপন তনু দঢ়িয়া ।
কেমন কেমন তার কাষ্ঠ-পাষাণ-হিয়া
তখনি না গেল কেনে গলিয়া ॥

*kemana bidhātā se gaurāṅga-cām̐dera de*
*gaṛhila āpana tanu daṛhiyā |*
*kemana kemana tāra kāṣṭha-pāṣāṇa-hiyā*
*takhani nā gela kene galiyā ||*

*Word for word:* kemana bidhata se — what kind of Creator is he; gauranga-chandera de(ha) — Gaurangachand's body; garila — fashioned; apana tanu dariya — himself remaining firm; kemana kemana tara — what kind is his; kashtha-pashana-hiya — heart of wood and stone; takhani na gela kene galiya — why did it not melt at once

**7.2.** What kind of Creator, having fashioned Gaurangachand's body,
remained firm himself?
What kind of heart is his — of wood and stone —
that it did not melt at once?[^03-19]

আমার গৌরাঙ্গের গুণে দারু পাষাণ কিবা
গলিয়া গলিয়া পড়ে অবনী ।
অরণ্যের মৃগ পাখী ঝুরিয়া ঝুরিয়া কান্দে
নাহি কান্দে হেন নাহি পরাণী ॥

*āmāra gaurāṅgera guṇe dāru pāṣāṇa kibā*
*galiyā galiyā paṛe abanī |*
*araṇyera mṛga pākhī jhuriyā jhuriyā kānde*
*nāhi kānde hena nāhi parāṇī ||*

*Word for word:* amara gaurangera gune — by my Gauranga's qualities; daru pashana kiba — wood and stone, what of them; galiya galiya pare abani — melting, flow to the earth; aranyera mriga pakhi — beasts and birds of the forest; jhuriya jhuriya kande — weep and weep; nahi kande hena nahi parani — there is no creature that does not weep

**7.3.** At my Gauranga's qualities wood and stone —
what of wood and stone! — melt and flow down to the earth;
the beasts and birds of the forest weep and weep:
there is no living being that does not weep.

যেমন তেমন কুলে জনম হউক মোর
যেমন তেমন দেহ পাইয়া ।
অনন্ত দাসের মন ঠাকুর গৌরাঙ্গের গুণ
দেশে দেশে ফিরি যেন গাইয়া ॥

*yemana temana kule janama hauka mora*
*yemana temana deha pāiyā |*
*ananta dāsera mana ṭhākura gaurāṅgera guṇa*
*deśe deśe phiri yena gāiyā ||*

*Word for word:* yemana temana kule — in whatever family; janama hauka mora — may I be born; yemana temana deha paiya — receiving whatever body; ananta dasera mana — Ananta Dasa's wish; thakura gaurangera guna — Thakura Gauranga's qualities; deshe deshe phiri — wandering from land to land; yena gaiya — that [I may] sing

**7.4.** In whatever family I may be born,
whatever body I may receive, —
Ananta Dasa's one wish is to sing of Thakura Gauranga's qualities,
wandering from land to land.

[^03-17]: The signature is "Ananta Dasa". According to Majumdar, Ananta Dasa was a poet of Advaita's branch and a contemporary
of the Lord; PK has 32 padas with his signature. In GPT1 (p. 39, no. 41) and GPT2 with variants.
[^03-18]: The moons at His feet are the Lord's toenails, shining like moons.
[^03-19]: PK: "…fashioned Gaurangachand's body, remaining firm himself" (daṛhiyā); the P-R-Sa manuscript and GPT2 read "dhariyā",
and GPT "Gaurangachand" (cām̐dere ye): "…fashioned Gaurangachand, taking on his own body". The image of the Creator (bidhi) who "sculpted" beauty is a
poetic convention (poets speak so of Radha and Krishna too); the Lord's body is not created — it is eternal, full of being,
knowledge and bliss ("ishvarah paramah krishnah sac-cid-ananda-vigrahah", *Brahma-samhita* 5.1).

## 8. Ananta Dasa — "dekha dekha aparūpa gaurāṅga nitāi…" (PK 2336)
*Praise of Gaura and Nitai — the two brothers who purify the fallen: They give prema to all without distinction and weep on
seeing the fallen. In PK — the section "The form and qualities of Sri Chaitanya and Nityananda". According to Majumdar it
"sounds like the word of a contemporary". Raga kamoda.*[^03-20]

দেখ দেখ অপরূপ গৌরাঙ্গ নিতাই ।
অখিল জীবের ভাগ্যে অবনী বিহরে গো
পতিত-পাবন দোন ভাই ॥

*dekha dekha aparūpa gaurāṅga nitāi |*
*akhila jībera bhāgye abanī bihare go*
*patita-pābana dona bhāi ||*

*Word for word:* dekha dekha — look, look; aparupa gauranga nitai — the wondrous Gauranga and Nitai; akhila jibera bhagye — by the good fortune of all beings; abani bihare go — wander the earth; patita-pabana dona bhai — the two brothers who purify the fallen

**8.1.** *(Refrain)* Look, look: the wondrous Gauranga and Nitai!
By the good fortune of all living beings there wander the earth
the two brothers who purify the fallen.

যারে দেখে তার ঠামে যাচিয়া বিলায় প্রেমে
উত্তম অধম নাহি মানে ।
এ তিন ভুবনের লোক নাহি জরা মৃত্যু শোক
প্রেম-অমৃত করি পানে ॥

*yāre dekhe tāra ṭhāme yāciyā bilāya preme*
*uttama adhama nāhi māne |*
*e tina bhubanera loka nāhi jarā mṛtyu śoka*
*prema-amṛta kari pāne ||*

*Word for word:* yare dekhe — whomever They see; tara thame — to him; yachiya bilaya preme — entreating, They distribute prema; uttama adhama nahi mane — make no distinction of high and low; e tina bhubanera loka — the people of the three worlds; nahi jara mrityu shoka — no old age, death or sorrow; prema-amrita kari pane — having drunk the nectar of prema

**8.2.** Whomever They see, They give prema to him, entreating him,
making no distinction between high and low;
the people of the three worlds, drinking the nectar of prema,
know neither old age, nor death, nor sorrow.

কলপ-বিরিখি সিন্ধু না যাচয়ে এক বিন্দু
ছি ছি কিয়ে তাহাতে উপমা ।
পতিত দেখিয়া কান্দে দোঁহে থির নাহি বান্ধে
যাচয়ে অমূল্য ভক্তি প্রেমা ॥

*kalapa-birikhi sindhu nā yācaye eka bindu*
*chi chi kiye tāhāte upamā |*
*patita dekhiyā kānde dom̐he thira nāhi bāndhe*
*yācaye amūlya bhakti premā ||*

*Word for word:* kalapa-birikhi — the wish-fulfilling tree; sindhu — the ocean; na yachaye eka bindu — do not offer even a drop [unasked]; chhi chhi kiye tahate upama — shame to compare them; patita dekhiya kande — seeing the fallen, They weep; donhe thira nahi bandhe — Both cannot restrain Themselves; yachaye amulya bhakti prema — entreating, They give priceless bhakti and prema

**8.3.** The wish-fulfilling tree and the ocean will not give a drop unasked —
shame even to compare them with Them!
Seeing the fallen, Both weep, unable to restrain Themselves,
and, entreating, give priceless bhakti and prema.[^03-21]

এমন দয়াল দুহুঁ যে না ভজে হেন পহু
সে ছারের জীবনে কি আশ ।
ন্যাসী বিপ্র হইলেহ অসুরে গণন সেহ
অনন্ত দাসের এই ভাষ ॥

*emana dayāla duhum̐ ye nā bhaje hena pahu*
*se chārera jībane ki āśa |*
*nyāsī bipra haileha asure gaṇana seha*
*ananta dāsera ei bhāṣa ||*

*Word for word:* emana dayala duhun — such merciful Two; ye na bhaje hena pahu — who does not worship such Lords; se chharera jibane — in that wretch's life; ki asha — what hope; nyasi bipra haileha — even if he be a sannyasi or brahmana; asure ganana seha — he is counted among the asuras; ananta dasera ei bhasha — this is Ananta Dasa's word

**8.4.** If someone does not serve such merciful Lords —
what hope is there in his wretched life?
Even if he be a sannyasi or a brahmana, he is counted among the asuras:
such is the word of Ananta Dasa.[^03-22]

[^03-20]: The signature is "Ananta Dasa". In GPT1 (p. 39, no. 42, raga shri or kamoda) and GPT2 with minor variants; there the
pada immediately follows the preceding one (PK 2208).
[^03-21]: "Entreating" (yāciyā): the Lord and Nityananda Themselves beg people to accept the name and prema (cf. CB Madhya
13: Nitai and Haridasa go from house to house begging, "Sing Krishna's name"; CC Adi 7). Instead of "Both" (dom̐he)
manuscript ka reads "body" (deha): "Their body knows no rest".
[^03-22]: Cf. *Bhagavad-gita* 7.15: the deluded do not surrender to the Lord, "having taken shelter of the nature of the asuras".

## 9. Ananta Acharya — "jaya śacīnandana jaga-jībana sāra…" (PK 2285)
*Lila: from the appearance to Nilachala — the Lord of Goloka descends in Navadvipa, teaches the dharma of the age —
sankirtana, accepts sannyasa from Keshava Bharati, shows the six-armed form in Utkala and settles in Nilachala. In PK —
the section "The sannyasa of Sri Gauranga, etc." According to Majumdar — probably a pada by Ananta Acharya, who lived in
Navadvipa; an important detail: the Lord Himself "gave the mantra" to Bharati. Raga shri (as for the preceding PK pada).*[^03-23]

জয় শচীনন্দন জগ-জীবন সার ।
জীবনে মরণে গোরা ঠাকুর আমার ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*jaya śacīnandana jaga-jībana sāra |*
*jībane maraṇe gorā ṭhākura āmāra || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* jaya — glory; shachinandana — to the Son of Shachi; jaga-jibana sara — the essence of the world's life; jibane marane — in life and in death; gora thakura amara — Gora is my Lord

**9.1.** *(Refrain)* Glory to the Son of Shachi, the essence of the world's life!
In life and in death Gora is my Lord.

আসিয়া গোলোক-নাথ পারিষদগণ সাথ
নবদ্বীপে অবতীর্ণ হৈয়া ।
স্থাপিয়া যুগের কর্ম্ম নিজ-সংকীর্ত্তন ধর্ম্ম
বুঝাইলা নাচিয়া গাইয়া ॥

*āsiyā goloka-nātha pāriṣadagaṇa sātha*
*nabadvīpe abatīrṇa haiyā |*
*sthāpiyā yugera karmma nija-saṃkīrttana dharmma*
*bujhāilā nāciyā gāiyā ||*

*Word for word:* asiya — coming; goloka-natha — the Lord of Goloka; parishadagana satha — with His associates; nabadvipe abatirna haiya — having descended in Navadvipa; sthapiya yugera karma — establishing the work of the age; nija-sankirtana dharma — the dharma of His own sankirtana; bujhaila nachiya gaiya — explained it by dancing and singing

**9.2.** Coming with His associates, the Lord of Goloka
descended in Navadvipa;
establishing the dharma of the age — His own sankirtana —
He explained it by dancing and singing.

ধরি রূপ হেম-গৌর পরিলা কৌপীন ডোর
অরুণ-কিরণ বহির্ব্বাস ।
করে কমণ্ডলু দণ্ড ধরিলা গৌরাঙ্গচন্দ্র
ছাড়ি বিষ্ণুপ্রিয়া-অভিলাষ ॥

*dhari rūpa hema-gaura parilā kaupīna ḍora*
*aruṇa-kiraṇa bahirvvāsa |*
*kare kamaṇḍalu daṇḍa dharilā gaurāṅgacandra*
*chāṛi biṣṇupriyā-abhilāṣa ||*

*Word for word:* dhari rupa hema-gaura — [He] of golden form; parila kaupina dora — put on the kaupina and cord; aruna-kirana bahirvasa — an outer cloth like the morning rays; kare kamandalu danda — in His hands the kamandalu and staff; dharila gaurangachandra — Gaurangachandra took; chhari vishnupriya-abhilasha — leaving Vishnupriya's hopes

**9.3.** He of golden form put on the kaupina and the cord,
an upper cloth the colour of the morning rays;
Gaurangachandra took the kamandalu and staff in His hands,
casting aside Vishnupriya's hopes.[^03-24]

অখিলের গুরু হরি ভারতীরে গুরু করি
মন্ত্র দিয়া করিলা গ্রহণ ।
নিন্দুক পাষণ্ড ছিল বহু নিন্দা পূর্ব্বে কৈল
ভজিল বলিয়া নারায়ণ ॥

*akhilera guru hari bhāratīre guru kari*
*mantra diyā karilā grahaṇa |*
*ninduka pāṣaṇḍa chila bahu nindā pūrvve kaila*
*bhajila baliyā nārāyaṇa ||*

*Word for word:* akhilera guru hari — Hari, the guru of all; bharatire guru kari — making Bharati His guru; mantra diya — giving [him] the mantra; karila grahana — accepted [it]; ninduka pashanda chhila — those who were scoffers and unbelievers; bahu ninda purve kaila — who had reviled much before; bhajila boliya narayana — worshipped [Him] as Narayana

**9.4.** Hari, the guru of the whole world, made Bharati His guru:
having given him the mantra, He received it from him.[^03-25]
The scoffers and unbelievers, who had once reviled Him much,
began to worship Him as Narayana.[^03-26]

যাইয়া উৎকল-দেশে নাম কৈল উপদেশে
ষড়্‌ভুজ দেখাঞা প্রকাশ ।
অনন্ত আচার্য্যে কয় সঙ্গে সব মহাশয়
লৈয়া কৈল নীলাচলে বাস ॥

*yāiyā utkala-deśe nāma kaila upadeśe*
*ṣaṛbhuja dekhāñā prakāśa |*
*ananta ācāryye kaya saṅge saba mahāśaya*
*laiyā kaila nīlācale bāsa ||*

*Word for word:* yaiya utkala-deshe — going to the land of Utkala; nama kaila upadeshe — taught the name; shadbhuja dekhanya prakasha — revealing the six-armed form; ananta acharye kaya — Ananta Acharya says; sange saba mahashaya laiya — taking with Him all the great souls; kaila nilachale basa — made His dwelling in Nilachala

**9.5.** Going to the land of Utkala, He taught the holy name,
manifesting the six-armed form.
Ananta Acharya says: with all the great souls
He made His dwelling in Nilachala.[^03-27]

[^03-23]: The signature is "Ananta Acharya"; in S. Ray's index of poets it is the only pada of Ananta Acharya in PK. Majumdar
considers it probably a pada of Ananta Acharya of Advaita's branch, who lived in Navadvipa (CC Adi 12). In GPT1
(pp. 19–20, no. 53) and GPT2 with minor variants; the refrain there (and in PK manuscripts ka, kha, cha) begins "The Son of
Shachi…" without "Glory".
[^03-24]: The kaupina is the sannyasi's loincloth; the kamandalu, a water-pot; the staff (danda), the sign of sannyasa.
"Vishnupriya's hopes" — in the original "vishnupriya-abhilasha": the Lord left His wife, who hoped to keep Him at home
(CC Adi 17; Lochana, Madhya-khanda).
[^03-25]: According to CB (Madhya 28), the Lord spoke into Keshava Bharati's ear a mantra He said He had heard in a dream, and
then received it from him as from a guru; thus He, the guru of the world, showed the example of a disciple's humility. Cf.
Murari 3.2.
[^03-26]: Cf. CC Adi 17: the Lord accepted sannyasa so that those who had reviled Him in Navadvipa, by bowing to a sannyasi,
would be freed from their offences; a sannyasi is honoured as Narayana.
[^03-27]: Utkala is Orissa. The six-armed form the Lord showed to Sarvabhauma (CB Antya 3; see the next pada). Instead of
"with" (laiyā) the P-R-Sa manuscript reads "in lila" (līlā).

## 10. Gauridasa Pandita — "pahu mora nityānanda rāya…" (PK 2313)
*Praise of Nityananda — the "market of the holy name" (hat-pattan): Nityananda is king of the market on the Ganga's bank,
Ramai carries out His orders, Haridasa is the kotwal, Krishnadasa the weighman, Srivasa the scribe; Vishvambhara and
Gadadhara trade in the Acharya's courtyard; Gauridasa, sitting near the king, hears of the market's glory. In PK — the
section "The qualities of Sri Nityananda". According to Majumdar — the first pada of the hat-pattan genre, written after
the sannyasa (the Lord is called "Chaitanya"). Raga shri.*[^03-28]

পহু মোর নিত্যানন্দ রায় ।
মথিয়া সকল তন্ত্র হরি-নাম মহামন্ত্র
করে ধরি জীবেরে বুঝায় ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*pahu mora nityānanda rāya |*
*mathiyā sakala tantra hari-nāma mahāmantra*
*kare dhari jībere bujhāya || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* pahu mora — my Lord; nityananda raya — Nityananda Raya; mathiya sakala tantra — having churned all the scriptures; hari-nama mahamantra — the great mantra, the name of Hari; kare dhari — holding by the hand; jibere bujhaya — explains to the living beings

**10.1.** *(Refrain)* My Lord is Nityananda Raya!
Having churned all the tantras, the great mantra — the name of Hari —
He explains to living beings, holding them by the hand.

চৈতন্য-অগ্রজ নাম ত্রিভুবন-অনুপাম
সুরধুনী-তীরে করি থানা ।
হাট করি পরবন্ধ রাজা হৈলা নিত্যানন্দ
পাষণ্ডী-দলন বীর-বানা ॥

*caitanya-agraja nāma tribhubana-anupāma*
*suradhunī-tīre kari thānā |*
*hāṭa kari parabandha rājā hailā nityānanda*
*pāṣaṇḍī-dalana bīra-bānā ||*

*Word for word:* chaitanya-agraja nama — His name is "Chaitanya's elder brother"; tribhubana-anupama — peerless in the three worlds; suradhuni-tire kari thana — setting up a post on the Suradhuni's bank; hata kari parabandha — arranging a market in due form; raja haila nityananda — Nityananda became king; pashandi-dalana bira-bana — [with] the hero's banner crushing the unbelievers

**10.2.** His name is "Chaitanya's elder brother", He has no equal in the three worlds;
on the bank of the Suradhuni He set up a post;
arranging a market in due form, Nityananda became its king,
with the hero's banner that crushes the unbelievers.[^03-29]

রামাই সুপাত্র হৈয়া রাজ-আজ্ঞা চালাইয়া
কোতোয়াল হৈলা হরিদাস ।
কৃষ্ণদাস হৈলা দাড়্যা কেহো যাইতে নারে ভাঁড়্যা
লিখন পড়ন শ্রীনিবাস ॥

*rāmāi supātra haiyā rāja-ājñā cālāiyā*
*kotoyāla hailā haridāsa |*
*kṛṣṇadāsa hailā dāṛyā keho yāite nāre bhām̐ṛyā*
*likhana paṛana śrīnibāsa ||*

*Word for word:* ramai supatra haiya — Ramai, a worthy servant; raja-ajna chalaiya — executing the royal orders; kotoyala haila haridasa — Haridasa became the kotwal; krishnadasa haila darya — Krishnadasa became the weighman (?); keho yaite nare bhanrya — no one can pass by cheating; likhana parana shrinibasa — writing and reading — Srinivasa (Srivasa)

**10.3.** Ramai, a worthy servant, carries out the royal orders,
Haridasa became the kotwal;
Krishnadasa became the weighman — no one can slip past by cheating;
the writing and reading is Srinivasa's.[^03-30]

পসারিয়া বিশ্বম্ভর আর প্রিয় গদাধর
আচার্য্য-চত্বরে বিকি কিনি ।
গৌরীদাস হাসি হাসি রাজার নিকটে বসি
হাটের মহিমা কিছু শুনি ॥

*pasāriyā biśvambhara āra priya gadādhara*
*ācāryya-catvare biki kini |*
*gaurīdāsa hāsi hāsi rājāra nikaṭe basi*
*hāṭera mahimā kichu śuni ||*

*Word for word:* pasariya — traders; vishvambhara — Vishvambhara; ara priya gadadhara — and the beloved Gadadhara; acharya-chatvare — in the Acharya's courtyard; biki kini — selling and buying; gauri-dasa hasi hasi — Gauridasa, smiling; rajara nikate basi — sitting near the king; hatera mahima kichhu shuni — hearing a little of the market's glory

**10.4.** The traders are Vishvambhara and the beloved Gadadhara:
in the Acharya's courtyard there is buying and selling.
Gauridasa, smiling, sits near the king
and hears a little of the market's glory.[^03-31]

[^03-28]: The signature is "Gauridasa". Gauridasa Pandita of Ambika (Kalna) was a companion of the Lord and of Nityananda;
Jayananda praises his poetry; PK has only two padas with his signature (161 and 2313). In GPT1 (p. 420, no. 20) with
minor variants. "Hat-pattan" ("opening a market") is a genre of padas where the preaching of the holy name is pictured
as a market at which prema is given away; later poems also belong to it. Majumdar regards Gauridasa's pada as the first
example of the genre and dates it after the sannyasa: Nityananda is called "Chaitanya's elder brother". Cf. CC Madhya 15
and Murari 4.21–4.22: the Lord sends Nityananda from Puri to preach in Gauda.
[^03-29]: Tantras here means the scriptures in general. A post (thānā) — a guard station. "The hero's banner that crushes the
unbelievers": Nityananda is Balarama, and His preaching is a victory over the pashandas.
[^03-30]: Ramai is probably Ramai Pandita (Sri Rama Pandita), Srivasa's younger brother, or Abhirama (Ramadasa), Nityananda's
companion; a kotwal is the chief of the town watch; Haridasa is Haridasa Thakura. "Weighman" — in the original "dāṛyā"
(mss. "ḍāṛyā", "ḍeṛyā"): the meaning is unclear — the one who holds the scales (dām̐ṛi) or a gatekeeper; "by cheating"
(bhām̐ṛyā) — manuscript cha reads "bhem̐ṛyā", P-R-Sa "chāṛyā" ("let off"). Krishnadasa is probably Gauridasa's younger
brother, the author of PK 2358 (chapter 1, no. 24). Srinivasa is Srivasa Pandita (Srinivasa is his full name).
[^03-31]: The Acharya is Advaita Acharya. Vishvambhara is the Lord Himself (His name before sannyasa). The humble "hears a
little" in the signature: the poet is merely present at this play.

## 11. Vasu Ghosha — "acaitanya śrīcaitanya sārvvabhauma-ghare…" (GPT1, p. 402)
*Lila: Puri, 1510 — the Lord lies unconscious in Sarvabhauma's house; Sarvabhauma sees Him in the forms of the avataras, and
when the Lord stands up in the six-armed form, he falls at His feet. Only in GPT (section "Antya-lila"). Raga suhai.*[^03-32]

অচৈতন্য শ্রীচৈতন্য সার্ব্বভৌম-ঘরে ।
গোপীনাথ পাশে বসি পদসেবা করে ॥

*acaitanya śrīcaitanya sārvvabhauma-ghare |*
*gopīnātha pāśe basi padasebā kare ||*

*Word for word:* achaitanya — unconscious; shri-chaitanya — Sri Chaitanya; sarvabhauma-ghare — in Sarvabhauma's house; gopinatha pashe basi — Gopinatha, sitting beside; pada-seba kare — serves [His] feet

**11.1.** Sri Chaitanya lies unconscious in Sarvabhauma's house;
Gopinatha, sitting beside Him, massages His feet.[^03-33]

সার্ব্বভৌম প্রভুমুখ আছে নিরখিয়া ।
ইনি কোন্ বস্তু কিছু না পায় ভাবিয়া ॥

*sārvvabhauma prabhumukha āche nirakhiyā |*
*ini kon bastu kichu nā pāya bhābiyā ||*

*Word for word:* sarvabhauma — Sarvabhauma; prabhu-mukha achhe nirikhiya — keeps gazing at the Lord's face; ini kon bastu — what Being He is; kichhu na paya bhabiya — cannot make out at all, pondering

**11.2.** Sarvabhauma gazes unblinking at the Lord's face
and cannot make out Who He is.

নরসিংহরূপ প্রভুর দেখে একবার ।
বটুক বামনরূপ দেখে পুনর্ব্বার ॥

*narasiṃharūpa prabhura dekhe ekabāra |*
*baṭuka bāmanarūpa dekhe punarvvāra ||*

*Word for word:* narasimha-rupa prabhura — the Lord's Nrisimha form; dekhe ekabara — sees once; batuka vamana-rupa — the form of the boy Vamana; dekhe punarvara — sees again

**11.3.** Now he sees the Lord in the form of Nrisimha,
now again in the form of the boy Vamana;

পুন দেখে মৎস্য কূর্ম্ম বরাহ আকার ।
পুন ভৃগুরাম হস্তে ভীষণ কুঠার ॥

*puna dekhe matsya kūrmma barāha ākāra |*
*puna bhṛgurāma haste bhīṣaṇa kuṭhāra ||*

*Word for word:* puna dekhe — then he sees; matsya kurma varaha akara — the forms of Matsya, Kurma, Varaha; puna bhrigurama — then Bhrigurama; haste bhishana kuthara — with a fearsome axe in hand

**11.4.** now he sees the forms of Matsya, Kurma, Varaha,
now Bhrigurama with a fearsome axe in His hand;

দূর্ব্বাদলশ্যামরূপ দেখয় কখন ।
কখন মুরলীধর নীরদবরণ ॥

*dūrvvādalaśyāmarūpa dekhaya kakhana |*
*kakhana muralīdhara nīradabaraṇa ||*

*Word for word:* durvadala-shyama-rupa — a form dark as a durva blade; dekhaya kakhana — at times he sees; kakhana murali-dhara — at times the Holder of the flute; nirada-barana — the colour of a rain-cloud

**11.5.** at times he sees a form dark as a blade of durva grass,
at times the Holder of the flute, the colour of a rain-cloud.[^03-34]

এ সব দেখিয়া তাঁর সন্দেহ ঘুচিল ।
ষড়্‌ভুজরূপে প্রভু উঠি দাণ্ডাইল ॥

*e saba dekhiyā tām̐ra sandeha ghucila |*
*ṣaṛbhujarūpe prabhu uṭhi dāṇḍāila ||*

*Word for word:* e saba dekhiya — seeing all this; tanra sandeha ghuchila — his doubt was dispelled; shadbhuja-rupe — in the six-armed form; prabhu uthi dandaila — the Lord rose and stood

**11.6.** Seeing all this, he gave up his doubts;
the Lord rose and stood in the six-armed form.[^03-35]

শচীর দুলাল যেই সেই ননীচোর ।
অন্তরেতে কালা কানু বাহিরেতে গৌর ॥

*śacīra dulāla yei sei nanīcora |*
*antarete kālā kānu bāhirete gaura ||*

*Word for word:* shachira dulala yei — he who is Shachi's darling; sei nani-chora — is that Butter-thief; antarete kala kanu — within, the dark Kanu; bahirete gaura — without, Gaura

**11.7.** Shachi's darling is that very Butter-thief:
within — the dark Kanu, without — Gaura.[^03-36]

ভূমে পড়ি দণ্ডবৎ করে সার্ব্বভৌম ।
বাসু ঘোষ বলে আর কেন মিছা ভ্রম ॥

*bhūme paṛi daṇḍabat kare sārvvabhauma |*
*bāsu ghoṣa bale āra kena michā bhrama ||*

*Word for word:* bhume pari — falling to the ground; dandabat kare sarvabhauma — Sarvabhauma prostrates himself; basu ghosha bale — Vasu Ghosha says; ara kena michha bhrama — why any more vain delusion

**11.8.** Falling to the ground, Sarvabhauma prostrates himself.
Vasu Ghosha says: why any more vain delusion?

[^03-32]: The signature is "Vasu Ghosha". The pada is neither in PK nor in BR — only in GPT1 (p. 402, no. 2 of the section
"Antya-lila") and GPT2; by Majumdar's criterion Vasu Ghosha's padas known only from GPT are unreliable, and the attribution
remains doubtful. In GPT the pada stands between Madhavi's two padas on the Lord's arrival in Puri (PK 2239, 2240; chapter
02, nos. 1–2). Cf. CC Madhya 6, CB Antya 3, Murari 3.11–3.12.
[^03-33]: Gopinatha Acharya, Sarvabhauma's brother-in-law, had known the Lord already in Navadvipa. According to CC (Madhya 6),
the Lord fell unconscious on seeing Jagannatha, and Sarvabhauma had Him carried to his house.
[^03-34]: The forms of the avataras: Nrisimha, Vamana (the boy brahmana), Matsya, Kurma, Varaha, Parashurama (Bhrigurama);
"dark as durva grass" — Ramachandra; the Holder of the flute — Krishna.
[^03-35]: The six-armed form (with Rama's bow, Krishna's flute, and the sannyasi's staff and water-pot) the Lord showed to
Sarvabhauma according to CB (Antya 3); according to CC (Madhya 6) — first a four-armed form, then Krishna's two-armed form
with the flute.
[^03-36]: The Butter-thief is Krishna. Cf. *Tattva-sandarbha* (2): "antah krishnam bahir gauram" — "Krishna within, Gaura
without"; CC Adi 1, 4.

## 12. Narahari (Sarakara) — "āoba gaura punahi nadiyāpura…" (PK 1970)
*Lila: Navadvipa in the years when the Lord lives in Puri: the devotees dream of His return — to see His face and His
kirtana again. In PK — a gaura-chandrika to the section "Bhavollasa" (Radha's joy at the news of Krishna's return), headed
"The words of the devotees, the residents of Navadvipa". Raga dhanashi.*[^03-37]

আওব গৌর পুনহি নদিয়াপুর
হোয়ত মনহি উলাস ।
ঐছে আনন্দ-কন্দ কিয়ে হেরব
করবহি কির্ত্তন-বিলাস ॥

*āoba gaura punahi nadiyāpura*
*hoyata manahi ulāsa |*
*aiche ānanda-kanda kiye heraba*
*karabahi kirttana-bilāsa ||*

*Word for word:* aoba gaura — Gaura will come; punahi nadiyapura — again to the town of Nadia; hoyata manahi ulasa — the heart will rejoice; aichhe ananda-kanda — such a root of bliss; kiye heraba — shall we see; karabahi kirtana-bilasa — [His] play in kirtana

**12.1.** Gaura will come again to the town of Nadia —
and the heart will be filled with joy.
Shall we really see again that fountain of bliss,
His play in kirtana?

হরি হরি কব হাম হেরব সো মুখ-চাঁদ ।
বিরহ-পয়োধি কবহুঁ দিন পঙরব
টুটব হৃদয়ক ধাঁধ ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*hari hari kaba hāma heraba so mukha-cām̐da |*
*biraha-payodhi kabahum̐ dina paṅaraba*
*ṭuṭaba hṛdayaka dhām̐dha || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* hari hari — Hari, Hari; kaba hama heraba — when shall I see; so mukha-chanda — that moon-face; biraha-payodhi — the ocean of separation; kabahun dina pangaraba — when shall I swim across; tutaba hridayaka dhandha — the heart's bewilderment will break

**12.2.** *(Refrain)* Hari, Hari! When shall I see that moon-like face?
When shall I swim across the ocean of separation,
and the heart's bewilderment be dispelled?

কুন্দন-কনক-কাঁতি কব হেরব
যজ্ঞকি সূত্র বিরাজ ।
বাহুযুগল তুলি হরি হরি বোলব
নটন ভকতগণ মাঝ ॥

*kundana-kanaka-kām̐ti kaba heraba*
*yajñaki sūtra birāja |*
*bāhuyugala tuli hari hari bolaba*
*naṭana bhakatagaṇa mājha ||*

*Word for word:* kundana-kanaka-kanti — the lustre of the purest gold; kaba heraba — when shall I see; yajnaki sutra biraja — the sacred thread shining; bahuyugala tuli — raising both arms; hari hari bolaba — He will cry "Hari, Hari"; natana bhakatagana majha — dancing amid the devotees

**12.3.** When shall I see a lustre like the purest gold
and the gleaming sacred thread?
Raising both arms, He will cry "Hari, Hari!",
dancing amid the devotees.[^03-38]

এত কহি নয়ন মুন্দি রহু সব জন
গৌর-প্রেমে ভেল ভোর ।
নরহরি দাস আশ কব পূরব
হেরব গৌরকিশোর ॥

*eta kahi nayana mundi rahu saba jana*
*gaura-preme bhela bhora |*
*narahari dāsa āśa kaba pūraba*
*heraba gaurakiśora ||*

*Word for word:* eta kahi — having said this; nayana mundi rahu saba jana — all stayed with eyes closed; gaura-preme bhela bhora — drunk with love for Gaura; narahari dasa — Narahari Dasa; asha kaba puraba — when will the hope be fulfilled; heraba gaura-kishora — to see youthful Gaura

**12.4.** Having said this, all fell still with closed eyes,
drunk with love for Gaura.
Narahari Dasa: when will the hope be fulfilled —
to see the youthful Gaura?

[^03-37]: The signature is "Narahari Dasa". Majumdar does not discuss this pada; its attribution to Narahari Sarakara is likely
(simple language) but not proven. In GPT1 (p. 411, no. 27) with variants, in the section on the years in Puri; there
instead of "will come" (āoba) it reads "is coming" (āota). In PK the pada follows a gaura-chandrika by Radhamohana to the
same section.
[^03-38]: The Lord wore the sacred thread (upavita) before sannyasa; on accepting sannyasa He gave it up. The Navadvipa
devotees remember His former form — as they saw Him in the kirtanas of 1509.

## 13. Narahari (Sarakara) — "locane jharajhara ānanda-lora…" (PK 1707)
*Lila: Navadvipa in the years of separation: the poet sees in a dream how Gaura, after a long separation, has come to
Navadvipa and strolls among the devotees; on waking he weeps. In PK — a gaura-chandrika to the section "Telling of a dream"
(svapna-rasodgara), headed "Here — Sri Mahaprabhu". Raga suhai.*[^03-39]

লোচনে ঝরঝর আনন্দ-লোর ।
স্বপনহি পেখলুঁ গৌর কিশোর ॥

*locane jharajhara ānanda-lora |*
*svapanahi pekhalum̐ gaura kiśora ||*

*Word for word:* lochane — from the eyes; jharajhara ananda-lora — stream tears of joy; svapanahi pekhalun — in a dream I saw; gaura kishora — the youthful Gaura

**13.1.** Tears of joy stream from my eyes:
in a dream I saw the youthful Gaura.

চিরদিনে আওল নবদ্বিপ মাঝ ।
বিহরয়ে আনন্দে ভকত-সমাজ ॥

*ciradine āola nabadvipa mājha |*
*biharaye ānande bhakata-samāja ||*

*Word for word:* chiradine — after a long time; aola nabadvipa majha — came into Navadvipa; biharaye anande — strolls joyfully; bhakata-samaja — in the assembly of devotees

**13.2.** After so many days He came to Navadvipa
and joyfully strolls in the circle of devotees.

কি কহব রে সখি রজনিক সূখ ।
চিরদিনে হেরলুঁ গোরা-চান্দ-মূখ ॥

*ki kahaba re sakhi rajanika sūkha |*
*ciradine heralum̐ gorā-cānda-mūkha ||*

*Word for word:* ki kahaba re sakhi — what shall I tell you, friend; rajanika sukha — of the night's bliss; chiradine heralun — after a long time I saw; gora-chanda-mukha — Gora's moon-face

**13.3.** What shall I tell you, friend, of the bliss of that night!
After so many days I saw Gora's moon-like face.

বিরহে আকুল যত নদিয়ার লোক ।
গোরা-মুখ হেরি দুরে গেল সব শোক ॥

*birahe ākula yata nadiyāra loka |*
*gorā-mukha heri dure gela saba śoka ||*

*Word for word:* birahe akula — tormented by separation; yata nadiyara loka — all the people of Nadia; gora-mukha heri — seeing Gora's face; dure gela saba shoka — all sorrow went far away

**13.4.** All the people of Nadia, tormented by separation,
saw Gora's face — and all their sorrow went far away.

পুন না দেখিয়া হিয়া বিদরিয়া যায় ।
নরহরি দাস কান্দি ধূলায় লোটায় ॥

*puna nā dekhiyā hiyā bidariyā yāya |*
*narahari dāsa kāndi dhūlāya loṭāya ||*

*Word for word:* puna na dekhiya — now, not seeing [Him]; hiya bidariya yaya — the heart breaks; narahari dasa — Narahari Dasa; kandi dhulaya lotaya — weeping, rolls in the dust

**13.5.** And now, not seeing Him, the heart is breaking:
Narahari Dasa weeps, rolling in the dust.[^03-40]

[^03-39]: The signature is "Narahari Dasa". Majumdar does not discuss the pada. In GPT1 (p. 410, no. 25) with minor variants,
in the section on the years in Puri, next to padas on the Lord's meeting with the Navadvipa devotees. In PK the section
"telling of a dream" consists of Radha's words relating to a friend Her dream of meeting Krishna; the gaura-chandrika
transfers them to Gaura. Cf. Shachi's dream of Nimai's coming (Vasu Ghosha, chapter 1, no. 22) and the Lord's visit to
Navadvipa in 1514 (CC Madhya 16).
[^03-40]: Waking after a dream of meeting is a usual motif of separation: the joy of the dream makes separation still keener.

## 14. Vasu Ghosha — "svarūpera kare dhari gorārāya…" (GPT1, p. 310)
*Lila: Puri — the Lord in Radha's mood, holding Svarupa's hand, reviles "Shyama, the friend": He ruined Her honour and went
to another. Only in GPT (section "Khandita, mana"). Raga suhai.*[^03-41]

স্বরূপের করে ধরি গোরারায় ।
গালি কত পাড়ে শ্যাম বন্ধুয়ায় ॥

*svarūpera kare dhari gorārāya |*
*gāli kata pāṛe śyāma bandhuyāya ||*

*Word for word:* svarupera kare dhari — holding Svarupa's hand; goraraya — Gora Raya; gali kata pare — heaps abuse; shyama bandhuyaya — on Shyama the friend

**14.1.** Holding Svarupa's hand, Gora Raya
heaps abuse on Shyama, the friend:

সে শঠ লম্পট রতিচোর ।
কত না দুর্গতি করে মোর ॥

*se śaṭha lampaṭa raticora |*
*kata nā durgati kare mora ||*

*Word for word:* se shatha — that cheat; lampata — rake; rati-chora — thief of love; kata na durgati kare mora — how many woes He causes me

**14.2.** "That cheat, that rake, that thief of love —
how many woes He has brought on Me!

কুলমান সকলি নাশিল ।
পতি-গেহে আনল ভেজাইল ॥

*kulamāna sakali nāśila |*
*pati-gehe ānala bhejāila ||*

*Word for word:* kula-mana sakali nashila — ruined family and honour altogether; pati-gehe — in the husband's house; anala bhejaila — kindled a fire

**14.3.** He ruined My family and My honour,
He set fire to My husband's house;

শেষে কালা মোহে পরিহরি ।
কেলি করে লৈয়া অন্য নারী ॥

*śeṣe kālā mohe parihari |*
*keli kare laiyā anya nārī ||*

*Word for word:* sheshe — in the end; kala — the Dark One; mohe parihari — abandoning me; keli kare laiya anya nari — sports with another woman

**14.4.** and in the end, the Dark One left Me
and sports with another.[^03-42]

মুই কি হইনু তার পর ।
ইহা কহি গৌরহরি কাঁদিয়া ফাঁফর ॥

*mui ki hainu tāra para |*
*ihā kahi gaurahari kām̐diyā phām̐phara ||*

*Word for word:* mui ki hainu tara para — have I become a stranger to Him; iha kahi — saying this; gaurahari — Gaurahari; kandiya phanphara — weeps in despair

**14.5.** Have I become a stranger to Him?" —
saying this, Gaurahari sobs in despair.

বাসু কহে কি বুঝিব আমি ।
যার লাগি কাঁদ পহুঁ সেই ধন তুমি ॥

*bāsu kahe ki bujhiba āmi |*
*yāra lāgi kām̐da pahum̐ sei dhana tumi ||*

*Word for word:* basu kahe — Vasu says; ki bujhiba ami — what can I understand; yara lagi kanda pahun — for whom You weep, Lord; sei dhana tumi — that treasure is You

**14.6.** Vasu says: what can I understand?
The One You weep for, Lord, is You Yourself.[^03-43]

[^03-41]: The signature is "Vasu". The pada is neither in PK nor in BR — only in GPT1 (p. 310, no. 8) and GPT2 (sec. 4.6, no.
8); Majumdar considers Vasu Ghosha's padas known only from GPT unreliable, and two padas signed Vasu in which Svarupa
accompanies the Lord in Navadvipa or on the Yamuna outright spurious (Svarupa came to the Lord only in Puri). Here, to judge
by Svarupa's presence, the scene is Puri, but the attribution remains doubtful. In GPT the pada follows the pada of
Narahari (?) "prema kari kulabatī sane" (chapter 2, no. 8). Svarupa Damodara in the Lord's mood is Radha's friend Lalita
(CC Antya 14–19; *Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika*).
[^03-42]: "Another" — Radha's rival (Chandravali). Radha's abuse in mana is the language of the highest prema, not of worldly
jealousy; the Lord experiences it in Radha's mood.
[^03-43]: Cf. CC Adi 4: Krishna accepted Radha's mood and lustre to taste His own sweetness and Radha's love for Him. The poet
says: the Krishna You seek is You Yourself.

## 15. Narahari (Sarakara) — "kanaka-campaka gorācānde…" (PK 849)
*Lila: the Lord in Radha's mood reproaches the Creator (bidhi): "Who has driven Me mad? Why did he make such a union?" In PK
— a gaura-chandrika to the section "reproaches to the Creator" (akshepanuraga). Raga suhai.*[^03-44]

কনক-চম্পক গোরাচান্দে ।
ভূমিতে পড়িয়া কেন কান্দে ॥

*kanaka-campaka gorācānde |*
*bhūmite paṛiyā kena kānde ||*

*Word for word:* kanaka-champaka — the colour of the golden champaka; gorachande — Gorachand; bhumite pariya — fallen on the ground; kena kande — why does He weep

**15.1.** Gorachand, the colour of the golden champaka —
why does He weep, fallen on the ground?

ক্ষেণে উঠি কহে হরি হরি ।
কে করিল আমারে বাউরি ॥

*kṣeṇe uṭhi kahe hari hari |*
*ke karila āmāre bāuri ||*

*Word for word:* kshene uthi — now rising; kahe hari hari — cries "Hari, Hari"; ke karila amare bauri — who has made me mad

**15.2.** Now He rises and cries, "Hari, Hari!
Who has driven Me mad?"

আজানুলম্বিত বাহু তুলি ।
বিধিরে পাড়য়ে সদা গালি ॥

*ājānulambita bāhu tuli |*
*bidhire pāṛaye sadā gāli ||*

*Word for word:* ajanulambita bahu tuli — raising arms that reach to the knees; bidhire paraye sada gali — keeps reviling the Creator

**15.3.** Raising His arms that reach to the knees,
He keeps reviling the Creator:

কহে ধিক্ বিধির বিধানে ।
এমত যোটনা করে কেনে ॥

*kahe dhik bidhira bidhāne |*
*emata yoṭanā kare kene ||*

*Word for word:* kahe dhik — says: shame; bidhira bidhane — on the Creator's decrees; emata yotana kare kene — why did he make such a union

**15.4.** "Shame on the Creator's decrees!
Why did he make such a union?"[^03-45]

কোন ভাবে কহে গোরারায় ।
নরহরি সোধিয়া বেড়ায় ॥

*kona bhābe kahe gorārāya |*
*narahari sodhiyā beṛāya ||*

*Word for word:* kona bhabe — in what mood; kahe goraraya — Gora Raya speaks; narahari sodhiya beraya — Narahari goes about asking

**15.5.** With what feeling does Gora Raya say this? —
Narahari goes about asking everyone.

[^03-44]: The signature is "Narahari". Majumdar does not discuss this pada separately, but he calls Narahari Sarakara's
gaura-chandrikas in the PK sections on akshepanuraga (853, 799, 820, 832, 840) descriptions of the Lord's real moods. In GPT1
(p. 300, no. 27) and GPT2 the pada comes immediately after PK 840 ("Ah, my youthful Gaura!", chapter 2, no. 7), among the
Puri padas. The pada itself does not name the place.
[^03-45]: "Union" (yoṭanā; ms. ka "yoṭana", kha "yoṭinā"; GPT "joṭana"): Radha reproaches the Creator because Her love for Krishna
has been joined with the bonds of family and duty and brings only suffering. The madness (bāuri) here is the madness of
prema. Instead of "Shame…" PK reads "bahe dhik" — apparently a misprint for "kahe dhik" ("says: shame…"), as in GPT.

## 16. Narahari (Sarakara) — "āre mora gaura kiśora. nāhi jāne dibāniśi…" (PK 1746)
*Lila: the mood of separation — the Lord does not distinguish day from night, laughs without cause, sings aloud asking,
"Where is the Lord of My life?", trembles, leaps, dances, speaks incoherently, weeps with closed eyes. In PK — a
gaura-chandrika to the section "Separation in the winter season" (hemanta and shishira). According to Majumdar — Narahari
Sarakara's pada of viraha ("laughter without cause"). Raga pahida.*[^03-46]

আরে মোর গৌর কিশোর ।
নাহি জানে দিবানিশি কারণ বিহনে হাসি
মনের ভরমে পহুঁ ভোর ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*āre mora gaura kiśora |*
*nāhi jāne dibāniśi kāraṇa bihane hāsi*
*manera bharame pahum̐ bhora || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* are mora gaura kishora — ah, my youthful Gaura; nahi jane dibanishi — knows not day or night; karana bihane hasi — laughing without cause; manera bharame — in the bewilderment of the mind; pahun bhora — the Lord is lost

**16.1.** *(Refrain)* Ah, my youthful Gaura!
Not knowing day from night, He laughs without cause —
the Lord is lost in the bewilderment of His heart.

ক্ষেণে উচ্চ-স্বরে গায় কারে পহুঁ কি সুধায়
কোথায় আমার প্রাণনাথ ।
ক্ষেণে শীতে অঙ্গ কম্প ক্ষেণে ক্ষেণে দেই লম্ফ
কাঁহা পাঙ যাঙ কার সাথ ॥

*kṣeṇe ucca-svare gāya kāre pahum̐ ki sudhāya*
*kothāya āmāra prāṇanātha |*
*kṣeṇe śīte aṅga kampa kṣeṇe kṣeṇe dei lampha*
*kām̐hā pāṅa yāṅa kāra sātha ||*

*Word for word:* kshene uccha-svare gaya — now sings aloud; kare pahun ki sudhaya — whom, what does the Lord ask; kothaya amara prananatha — where is the Lord of my life; kshene shite anga kampa — now the body trembles as with cold; kshene kshene dei lampha — now He leaps; kanha pana — where shall I find; yana kara satha — where go, with whom

**16.2.** Now He sings aloud — of whom, of what does the Lord ask? —
"Where is the Lord of My life?"
Now His whole body trembles as with cold, now He leaps:
"Where shall I find Him? Where shall I go? With whom?"[^03-47]

ক্ষেণে ঊর্দ্ধবাহু করি নাচি বুলে ফিরি ফিরি
ক্ষেণে ক্ষেণে করয়ে প্রলাপ ।
ক্ষেণে আঁখিযুগ মুন্দে হা নাথ বলিয়া কান্দে
ক্ষেণে ক্ষেণে করয়ে সন্তাপ ॥

*kṣeṇe ūrddhabāhu kari nāci bule phiri phiri*
*kṣeṇe kṣeṇe karaye pralāpa |*
*kṣeṇe ām̐khiyuga munde hā nātha baliyā kānde*
*kṣeṇe kṣeṇe karaye santāpa ||*

*Word for word:* kshene urdhva-bahu kari — now raising His arms; nachi bule phiri phiri — dances whirling round and round; kshene kshene karaye pralapa — now again and again speaks incoherently; kshene ankhiyuga munde — now closes His eyes; ha natha boliya kande — weeps crying "O Natha!"; kshene kshene karaye santapa — now again and again is in torment

**16.3.** Now, raising His arms, He dances, whirling and whirling,
now again and again He speaks incoherently;
now He closes His eyes and weeps, "O Natha!",
now again and again He is in torment.

কহে দাস নরহরি আরে মোর গৌরহরি
রাধার পিরিতে হৈল হেন ।
ঐছন করিয়া চিতে কলিযুগ উদ্ধারিতে
বঞ্চিত হইলুঁ মুঞি কেন ॥

*kahe dāsa narahari āre mora gaurahari*
*rādhāra pirite haila hena |*
*aichana kariyā cite kaliyuga uddhārite*
*bañcita hailum̐ muñi kena ||*

*Word for word:* kahe dasa narahari — Narahari Dasa says; are mora gaurahari — ah, my Gaurahari; radhara pirite haila hena — became thus through Radha's love; aichhana kariya chite — so resolving in His heart; kaliyuga uddharite — to deliver the age of Kali; banchita hailun muni kena — why am I left out

**16.4.** Narahari Dasa says: ah, my Gaurahari
has become like this from Radha's love.
He resolved in His heart to deliver the age of Kali —
why then am I left out?[^03-48]

[^03-46]: The signature is "Narahari Dasa". Majumdar cites the line "Now He sings aloud — of whom, of what does the Lord ask?"
among Narahari Sarakara's viraha padas. In GPT1 (p. 315, no. 8) and GPT2 (sec. 4.7, no. 8) the pada stands immediately after
PK 1662 and 1663 (no. 17 of this chapter), among the padas on the divine madness of prema; there instead of "speaks
incoherently" (pralāpa) it reads "laments" (bilāpa), with a note of the reading "pralāpa". In PK the pada is preceded by the
heading "Separation befitting winter. Here — Sri Gaurachandra".
[^03-47]: Radha's words in separation: She seeks Krishna and does not know where to go. Trembling is a sattvika-bhava; in PK
the pada opens the section on winter separation, and trembling "as with cold" matches the season. This is the madness of
prema (divya-unmada) described in CC Antya 14–20, not worldly longing.
[^03-48]: Cf. CC Adi 4. The formula "why then am I left out" is Narahari's usual signature (cf. PK 2241, chapter 2, no. 5).

## 17. Unsigned (Vasu Ghosha? Govinda Dasa?) — "cetana pāiyā gorā rāya…" (PK 1663)
*Lila: a continuation of PK 1662 (Vasu Ghosha, chapter 2, no. 15): the Lord, coming to Himself after running to the sea,
sees Svarupa and Ramaraya before Him and laments: "Where is My Krishna with the flute at His lips? I saw Him just now!" In PK
— the section "Divya-unmada". Raga shri.*[^03-49]

চেতন পাইয়া গোরা রায় ।
ভূমে পড়ি ইতি উতি চায় ॥

*cetana pāiyā gorā rāya |*
*bhūme paṛi iti uti cāya ||*

*Word for word:* chetana paiya — regaining consciousness; gora raya — Gora Raya; bhume pari — lying on the ground; iti uti chaya — looks here and there

**17.1.** Coming to His senses, Gora Raya,
lying on the ground, looks this way and that.

সম্মুখে স্বরূপ রাম রায় ।
দেখি পহুঁ করে হায় হায় ॥

*sammukhe svarūpa rāma rāya |*
*dekhi pahum̐ kare hāya hāya ||*

*Word for word:* sammukhe — in front; svarupa rama raya — Svarupa [and] Ramaraya; dekhi — seeing [them]; pahun kare haya haya — the Lord cries "Alas, alas!"

**17.2.** Before Him are Svarupa and Ramaraya;
seeing them, the Lord cries, "Alas, alas!

কাঁহা মোর মুরলী-বদন ।
এখনি পাইলুঁ দরশন ॥

*kām̐hā mora muralī-badana |*
*ekhani pāilum̐ daraśana ||*

*Word for word:* kanha mora murali-badana — where is my flute-faced one; ekhani pailun darashana — just now I had His sight

**17.3.** Where is My Krishna with the flute at His lips?
I saw Him just now!

ওহে নাথ পরম-করুণ ।
কৃপা করি দেহ দরশন ॥

*ohe nātha parama-karuṇa |*
*kṛpā kari deha daraśana ||*

*Word for word:* ohe natha — O Lord; parama-karuna — supremely merciful; kripa kari — be gracious; deha darashana — grant Your sight

**17.4.** O Lord, supremely merciful,
be gracious, show Yourself!"[^03-50]

এত বিলাপয়ে গোরাচান্দে ।
দেখিয়া ভকতগণ কান্দে ॥

*eta bilāpaye gorācānde |*
*dekhiyā bhakatagaṇa kānde ||*

*Word for word:* eta bilapaye — thus laments; gorachande — Gorachand; dekhiya — seeing [this]; bhakatagana kande — the devotees weep

**17.5.** So laments Gorachand;
seeing this, the devotees weep.

[^03-49]: In PK the pada is unsigned; in the P-R-Sa manuscript "Govinda Dasa" stands instead of "the devotees" ("seeing this,
Govinda Dasa weeps"), so that the pada is signed by Govinda Dasa; in GPT1 (p. 315, no. 7) and GPT2 (sec. 4.7, no. 7) a sixth
couplet is added with Vasu Ghosha's signature: "Vasu Ghosha says: my Gora is drunk with love for Krishna". The attribution
is disputed: it may be a continuation of Vasu Ghosha's PK 1662, but the witnesses disagree. Ramaraya is Ramananda Raya. Cf.
CC Antya 14: coming to Himself after running to Chataka-parvata, the Lord says to Svarupa, "Why have you brought Me here? I
just saw Krishna…"; Antya 17–18.
[^03-50]: "Krishna with the flute at His lips" — in the original "murali-badana", "He whose face bears the flute". The Lord
speaks in the mood of Radha, who has just seen Krishna and lost Him again.

## 18. Narahari — "gaurāṅga ke jāne mahimā tomāra…" (PK 2293)
*Praise of Gauranga, the avatara who purifies the fallen in the age of Kali: from the ocean of Shyama, as if by churning,
the sweet Gauranga appeared, and a downpour of prema flooded the three worlds. In PK — the last pada of the section "The
sannyasa of Sri Gauranga, etc." Raga varadi ("the same" as for the preceding PK pada), dhanashri (GPT).*[^03-51]

গৌরাঙ্গ কে জানে মহিমা তোমার ।
কলিযুগ উদ্ধারিতে পতিত-পাবন অবতার ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*gaurāṅga ke jāne mahimā tomāra |*
*kaliyuga uddhārite patita-pābana abatāra || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* gauranga — Gauranga; ke jane mahima tomara — who knows Your greatness; kaliyuga uddharite — to deliver the age of Kali; patita-pabana avatara — the avatara who purifies the fallen

**18.1.** *(Refrain)* Gauranga, who knows Your greatness?
To deliver the age of Kali You appeared — the avatara who purifies the fallen.

শ্যাম-মহোদধি কেমনে বিধাতা
মথিয়া সে কত কাল ।
কত সুধা-রস তাহে নিরমিয়া
উপজল গৌরাঙ্গ রসাল ॥

*śyāma-mahodadhi kemane bidhātā*
*mathiyā se kata kāla |*
*kata sudhā-rasa tāhe niramiyā*
*upajala gaurāṅga rasāla ||*

*Word for word:* shyama-mahodadhi — the great ocean of Shyama; kemane bidhata — how the Creator; mathiya se kata kala — churned for so long; kata sudha-rasa — how much nectar; tahe niramiya — making from it; upajala gauranga rasala — the sweet Gauranga arose

**18.2.** How long the Creator
churned the ocean of Shyama!
How much nectar he made from it —
and the sweet Gauranga appeared.[^03-52]

ত্রিভুবনে প্রেম- বাদর হইল
গৌর-প্রেম-বরিষণে ।
দীন হীন জন ও রসে মগন
নরহরি গুণ-গানে ॥

*tribhubane prema- bādara haila*
*gaura-prema-bariṣaṇe |*
*dīna hīna jana o rase magana*
*narahari guṇa-gāne ||*

*Word for word:* tribhubane — in the three worlds; prema-badara haila — a downpour of prema came; gaura-prema-barishane — by the rain of Gaura's love; dina hina jana — the lowly and wretched; o rase magana — are drowned in that rasa; narahari guna-gane — [so] Narahari sings His qualities

**18.3.** In the three worlds a downpour of prema came —
the rain of Gaura's love;
the lowly and wretched are drowned in that rasa, —
so Narahari sings of His qualities.

[^03-51]: The signature is "Narahari". Majumdar does not discuss the pada; in the stage-1 catalogue another pada ("nīlācale yave
majhu nātha" — in GPT1 signed by Vaishnava Dasa) was wrongly linked to PK 2293. The language and imagery (churning, a downpour
of prema) are closer to later stutis; the pada may also belong to Narahari Chakravarti — its attribution to Sarakara is not
established. In GPT1 (p. 28, no. 6) and GPT2 with the variant "mathiyā se karatāla" instead of "mathiyā se kata kāla".
[^03-52]: The image is the churning of the Milk Ocean, from which the amrita appeared. "The Creator" (bidhi) is a poetic figure:
Gauranga is not created — He is Shyama (Krishna) Himself, who accepted Radha's lustre and mood (CC Adi 4).

# Chapter 4. Gaura's Form, Navadvipa, the Sannyasa and the Return

*Padas of contemporaries which Majumdar (*Sri-Chaitanya-chariter upadan*, ch. 2) regards as eyewitness testimony, in the
order of the lilas: the six-armed form and the beauty of Gorachand in Navadvipa, Radha's mood in Gadadhara's lap, the
swing festival on the bank of the Ganga, the goshtha-lila, praise of Gaura and Nityananda; then Vasu Ghosha's cycle on the
sannyasa (the last night at home, the lament of Shachi and Vishnupriya, Katwa, Keshava Bharati, the shorn curls, the
lament of Nadia), the dance of the Lord as a sannyasi, and the Lord's return to the neighbourhood of Navadvipa (1514/15).
The text follows the *Padakalpataru* (PK), the *Bhakti-ratnakara* (BR), the *Kshanada-gita-chintamani* (KGC) and the
*Gaura-pada-tarangini* (GPT1 — 1st ed., 1903; GPT2 — 2nd ed., 1934); the Bengali original, variants and word-for-word
translation are in the full version of the book.*

## 1. Ananta Dasa — "kām̐cā se soṇāra tanu…" (PK 2167)
*Lila: Navadvipa — the Lord's six-armed form (shad-bhuja): Rama's bow and arrows, Krishna's flute, the sannyasi's staff and
waterpot. In PK the pada is headed "Then the form that revealed six arms, in Navadvipa". Majumdar mentions this pada when
speaking of Ananta Dasa, a poet of Advaita's branch and a contemporary of the Lord. Raga tirotha-dhanashi.*[^04-1]

কাঁচা সে সোণার তনু ডগমগি অঙ্গ ।
চাঁদ-বদনে হাসি অমিয়া-তরঙ্গ ॥

*kām̐cā se soṇāra tanu ḍagamagi aṅga |*
*cām̐da-badane hāsi amiyā-taraṅga ||*

*Word for word:* kancha se sonara tanu — a body like pure gold; dagamagi anga — the whole body quivering (glowing); chanda-badane — on the moon-face; hasi — a smile; amiya-taranga — waves of nectar

**1.1.** His body is like pure gold, all of it quivering;
on His moon-face a smile — waves of nectar.

অবনি-বিলম্বিত বনি বনমাল ।
সৌরভে বেঢ়ল মধুকর-জাল ॥

*abani-bilambita bani banamāla |*
*saurabhe beṛhala madhukara-jāla ||*

*Word for word:* abani-bilambita — hanging down to the earth; bani banamala — a lovely forest garland; saurabhe — by the fragrance; bedhala — surrounded; madhukara-jala — swarms of bees

**1.2.** A forest garland hangs down to the very earth;
drawn by its fragrance, swarms of bees surround it.

উত ছয় ভুজ পর খর শর-চাপ ।
হেরইতে রিপুগণ থরহরি কাঁপ ॥

*uta chaya bhuja para khara śara-cāpa |*
*heraite ripugaṇa tharahari kām̐pa ||*

*Word for word:* uta — there (?); chhaya bhuja para — upon the six arms (on the [upper] of the six arms); khara shara-chapa — sharp arrows and a bow; heraite — on seeing; ripugana — the enemies; tharahari kapa — tremble and shake

**1.3.** Of the six arms the upper ones hold sharp arrows and a bow —
at the sight of them enemies tremble.[^04-2]

দুরবা-দল-তুল নখ-বিধু সাজ ।
মণিময় কঙ্কণ বলয় বিরাজ ॥

*durabā-dala-tula nakha-bidhu sāja |*
*maṇimaya kaṅkaṇa balaya birāja ||*

*Word for word:* duraba-dala-tula — like blades of durva grass; nakha-bidhu saj — moon-like nails adorn [them]; manimaya kankana balaya — jewelled bracelets and armlets; biraj — shine

**1.4.** These arms are the colour of durva grass, their nails like moons;
bracelets and armlets of jewels shine on them.

তদধহিঁ দুহুঁ কর জলধর-শ্যাম ।
তহিঁ শোভে মোহন মুরলি অনুপাম ॥

*tadadhahim̐ duhum̐ kara jaladhara-śyāma |*
*tahim̐ śobhe mohana murali anupāma ||*

*Word for word:* tadadhahi — below them; duhu kara — two hands; jaladhara-shyama — dark as a rain-cloud; tahi — in them; shobhe — shines; mohana murali — the enchanting flute; anupama — matchless

**1.5.** Below, two arms dark as a thundercloud;
in them gleams the matchless, enchanting flute.

নখ-মণি বিধু জিনি তলহি সুরঙ্গ ।
মণি-অভরণ তাহে মুরছে অনঙ্গ ॥

*nakha-maṇi bidhu jini talahi suraṅga |*
*maṇi-abharaṇa tāhe murache anaṅga ||*

*Word for word:* nakha-mani — the jewel-nails; bidhu jini — outshine the moon; talahi suranga — the palms are red; mani-abharana tahe — the jewelled ornaments on them; murachhe ananga — Ananga (Kamadeva) swoons

**1.6.** The jewel-nails outshine the moon, the palms are red;
seeing the jewelled ornaments on them, Ananga himself swoons.[^04-3]

তদধহি করহি কমণ্ডলু দণ্ড ।
যাহে কলি-কলমষ পাষণ্ড খণ্ড ॥

*tadadhahi karahi kamaṇḍalu daṇḍa |*
*yāhe kali-kalamaṣa pāṣaṇḍa khaṇḍa ||*

*Word for word:* tadadhahi — lower still; karahi — in the hands; kamandalu danda — the waterpot and staff; yahe — by which; kali-kalamasha — the filth of Kali; pashanda — the godless; khanda — are shattered

**1.7.** Lower still, hands with the waterpot and the staff,
which shatter the filth of Kali and the godless.[^04-4]

গিম সঞে উরে মণি মোতি বিলোল ।
শ্রীবৎসাঙ্কিত কৌস্তভ দোল ॥

*gima sañe ure maṇi moti bilola |*
*śrībatsāṅkita kaustabha dola ||*

*Word for word:* gima sanye ure — at the throat and on the breast; mani moti bilola — jewels and pearls sway; shribatsankita — [the breast] marked with the Shrivatsa; kaustubha dola — the Kaustubha swings

**1.8.** At the throat and on the breast jewels and pearls sway;
the Kaustubha swings, the breast is marked with the Shrivatsa.

মলয়জময় উর পরিসর পীন ।
নাভি গভির কটি কেশরি-খীণ ॥

*malayajamaya ura parisara pīna |*
*nābhi gabhira kaṭi keśari-khīṇa ||*

*Word for word:* malayajamaya — anointed with sandal; ura parisara pina — the broad, full chest; nabhi gabhira — the navel deep; kati keshari-khina — the waist slender as a lion's

**1.9.** The broad chest is anointed with sandal;
the navel is deep, the waist slender as a lion's.

বসন সুরঙ্গ চরণ-পরিযন্ত ।
পদ-নখ-নীছনি দাস অনন্ত ॥

*basana suraṅga caraṇa-pariyanta |*
*pada-nakha-nīchani dāsa ananta ||*

*Word for word:* basana suranga — the red cloth; charana-pariyanta — down to the feet; pada-nakha-nichhani — self-offering to the toenails; dasa ananta — Ananta Dasa

**1.10.** The red cloth falls to His very feet;
Ananta Dasa offers himself to the nails of His feet.[^04-5]

[^04-1]: The signature is "Dasa Ananta". In PK the pada stands last in the 18th pallava ("The form of Sri Gauranga, etc.";
vol. 3, PDF p. 256, printed p. 245; MS P-R-Sa no. 2274); in GPT1 — p. 141, no. 89; in GPT2 — sect. 3.1, twice (nos. 44 and
89), with minor variants. The Lord revealed the six-armed form to Nityananda in Navadvipa (CB Madhya 5; Murari 2.8) and
to Sarvabhauma in Puri (CC Madhya 6). Majumdar regards Ananta Dasa as a contemporary; PK has 32 padas with his signature.
[^04-2]: Bow and arrows are the form of Ramachandra, and the colour of durva grass (a dark greenish hue) is the colour of His
body. PK reads "uta chaya bhuja para" ("there, of the six arms…"), GPT "ubhadvaya bhujapara" ("on the two raised arms");
the sense is the same.
[^04-3]: The middle pair of arms holding the flute, dark as a cloud, is Krishna's form. Ananga ("the bodiless") is Kamadeva,
the god of love.
[^04-4]: The lowest pair of arms holds the staff (danda) and waterpot (kamandalu) of a sannyasi: the form of Gaura Himself.
For "the godless" (pāṣaṇḍa) MSS "ka", "ca" read "filth" (kaluṣa); so also GPT: "the filth, the sin of Kali".
[^04-5]: Nichhani (nichani) is the custom of waving something round a beloved person to ward off harm from him and then giving it
away; the poet "offers himself" in such an offering to the nails of the Lord's feet. MSS "ka", "ca", P-R-Sa read "nichani".

## 2. Govinda Ghosha — "gorācām̐da kibā tomāra badana-maṇḍala…" (PK 1029)
*Lila: Gorachand's form — a song of the Lord's beauty in Navadvipa. In PK it opens the section "Delight in the form"
(rupa-ullasa) as a gaura-chandrika. According to Majumdar, Govinda Ghosha, the eldest of the Ghosha brothers, conveys his
own impression of Gauranga's form. Raga dhanashi.*[^04-6]

গোরাচাঁদ কিবা তোমার বদন-মণ্ডল ।
কনক-কমল কিয়ে শরদ-পূর্ণিমা-শশী
নিশি দিশি করে ঝলমল ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*gorācām̐da kibā tomāra badana-maṇḍala |*
*kanaka-kamala kiye śarada-pūrṇimā-śaśī*
*niśi diśi kare jhalamala || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* gorachand — Gorachand; kiba — how wondrous; tomara badana-mandala — the orb of Your face; kanaka-kamala — a golden lotus; kiye — or; sharada-purnima-shashi — the full autumn moon; nishi dishi — night and day; kare jhalamala — shines

**2.1.** *(Refrain)* Gorachand, how wondrous is the orb of Your face!
Is it a golden lotus, is it the full autumn moon —
it shines by night and by day.

তোমার বরণখানি জনু হরিতাল জিনি
কিয়ে থির বিজুরী জিনিয়া ।
কিয়ে নব গোরোচনা কিয়ে দশবান সোণা
মনমথ-মন-মোহনিয়া ॥

*tomāra baraṇakhāni janu haritāla jini*
*kiye thira bijurī jiniyā |*
*kiye naba gorocanā kiye daśabāna soṇā*
*manamatha-mana-mohaniyā ||*

*Word for word:* tomara barana-khani — the colour of Your body; janu — as if; haritala jini — surpassing orpiment; kiye thira bijuri jiniya — or surpassing a motionless lightning; kiye naba gorochana — is it fresh gorochana; kiye dashabana sona — is it gold of the finest assay; manamatha-mana-mohaniya — enchanting the mind of Manmatha

**2.2.** The colour of Your body outshines yellow haritala
and seems to surpass a motionless lightning;
is it fresh gorochana, is it gold of the finest assay —
You enchant the mind of Manmatha himself.[^04-7]

খগপতি জিনি নাসা অমিয়া-মধুর ভাষা
তুলনা না হয় ত্রিভুবনে ।
আকর্ণ নয়ান-বাণ ভুরু-ধনু-সন্ধান
কটাক্ষে হানয়ে নারী-মনে ॥

*khagapati jini nāsā amiyā-madhura bhāṣā*
*tulanā nā haya tribhubane |*
*ākarṇa nayāna-bāṇa bhuru-dhanu-sandhāna*
*kaṭākṣe hānaye nārī-mane ||*

*Word for word:* khagapati jini nasa — a nose surpassing [the beak of] the king of birds (Garuda); amiya-madhura bhasha — speech sweet as nectar; tulana na haya tribhubane — no comparison in the three worlds; akarna nayana-bana — eyes reaching to the ears are arrows; bhuru-dhanu-sandhana — brows a drawn bow; katakshe hanaye — pierces with sidelong glances; nari-mane — the hearts of women

**2.3.** Your nose is lovelier than Garuda's beak, Your speech sweet as nectar —
there is none like You in the three worlds.
Eyes reaching to the ears are arrows, brows a drawn bow:
with a sidelong glance You pierce the hearts of women.[^04-8]

আজানুলম্বিত ভুজ বিলেপিত মলয়জ
অঙ্গুরী বলয়া তাহে সাজে ।
সিংহ জিনি মধ্য সরু হেম-রম্ভা জিনি উরু
চরণে নূপুর বঙ্করাজে ॥

*ājānulambita bhuja bilepita malayaja*
*aṅgurī balayā tāhe sāje |*
*siṃha jini madhya saru hema-rambhā jini uru*
*caraṇe nūpura baṅkarāje ||*

*Word for word:* ajanulambita bhuja — arms reaching to the knees; bilepita malayaja — anointed with sandal; anguri balaya — rings and bracelets; tahe saje — shine on them; simha jini madhya saru — a waist slenderer than a lion's; hema-rambha jini uru — thighs surpassing golden plantain stems; charane nupura bankaraje — on the feet, anklets (bankaraj)

**2.4.** Arms reaching to the knees are anointed with sandal,
and rings and bracelets shine on them.
The waist is slenderer than a lion's, the thighs like golden plantain stems,
on the feet are anklets.

জিনি ময়মত্ত হাতী হংসরাজ জিনি গতি
দেখিয়ে এ হেন রূপ-রাশি ।
কহয়ে গোবিন্দ ঘোষ গোর মনে সন্তোষ
নিছনি যাইয়ে হেন বাসি ॥

*jini mayamatta hātī haṃsarāja jini gati*
*dekhiye e hena rūpa-rāśi |*
*kahaye gobinda ghoṣa gora mane santoṣa*
*nichani yāiye hena bāsi ||*
