*Word for word:* jini mayamatta hati — surpassing a maddened elephant; hamsaraj jini gati — a gait surpassing the king of swans; dekhiye — seeing; e hena rupa-rashi — such a treasury of beauty; kahaye gobinda ghosha — Govinda Ghosha says; gora mane santosha — with joy at heart for Gora (?); nichhani yaiye — I would offer myself up; hena basi — so I feel

**2.5.** The gait is lovelier than a maddened elephant's and the king of swans';
seeing such a treasury of beauty,
Govinda Ghosha speaks, with joy in his heart for Gora:
"I would give myself up for Him."[^04-9]

[^04-6]: The signature is "Govinda Ghosha". In PK (vol. 2, PDF p. 225, printed p. 212; MS P-R-Sa no. 1455) the pada comes
under the heading "Now, delight in the form. Sri Gaurachandra" and opens the songs on the beauty of Radha and Krishna. It is
not in GPT. Majumdar names PK 1029 and 2146 (no. 3) among Govinda Ghosha's padas on Gaura's form.
[^04-7]: Haritala is orpiment, a golden-yellow paint; gorochana is a yellow pigment used for tilaka; "gold of ten van"
(daśabān) is gold refined many times, of the finest assay. Manmatha is Kamadeva: the Lord's beauty enchants the god of love
himself (cf. Krishna's name Madana-mohana). MS P-R-Sa reads "tanu" ("body") for "janu" ("as if").
[^04-8]: "You pierce the hearts of women" (MSS "kha", "gha", P-R-Sa: "the heart of a woman") is a stock image of the poetics
of describing beauty; we translate faithfully. Vrindavana Dasa stresses that in this incarnation the Lord never looked at
another man's wife; worship of Gaura in the spirit of "Gaura-nagari" is not accepted by the Gaudiya tradition (Vrindavana
Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja, Bhaktisiddhanta).
[^04-9]: The words "gora mane santoṣa" also allow the reading "and Gora is pleased at heart"; our rendering is tentative.
"Give myself up" (nichani jāiye) — see note 5. For "maddened" (mayamatta) MSS "ka", "kha" read "madamatta" (same sense).

## 3. Govinda Ghosha — "kanayā kaṣila mukha-śobhā…" (PK 2146)
*Lila: Gaura's form — the causeless smile, the yellow silk, a bee flying to His feet. According to Majumdar, an
eyewitness's impression of Gauranga's form. Raga sindhura.*[^04-10]

কনয়া কষিল মুখ-শোভা ।
হেরইতে জগ-মন লোভা ॥

*kanayā kaṣila mukha-śobhā |*
*heraite jaga-mana lobhā ||*

*Word for word:* kanaya kashila — gold tried on the touchstone; mukha-shobha — the beauty of the face; heraite — on seeing; jaga-mana lobha — the mind of the world longs

**3.1.** The beauty of His face is like gold tried on the touchstone;
one glance, and the mind of the whole world is filled with longing.

বিনি হাসে গোরা-মুখ হাস ।
পরিধান পীত পটবাস ॥

*bini hāse gorā-mukha hāsa |*
*paridhāna pīta paṭabāsa ||*

*Word for word:* bini hase — smiles without cause; gora-mukha hasa — Gora's face, the smile; paridhana — wearing; pita patabasa — yellow silk garments

**3.2.** Without any cause Gora's face smiles;
He is clad in yellow silk.[^04-11]

অঙ্গের সৌরভ-লোভ পাইয়া ।
নবীন ভ্রমরী আইল ধাইয়া ॥

*aṅgera saurabha-lobha pāiyā |*
*nabīna bhramarī āila dhāiyā ||*

*Word for word:* angera saurabha-lobha paiya — drawn by the fragrance of the body; nabina bhramari — a young bee; aila dhaiya — came flying

**3.3.** Drawn by the fragrance of His body,
a young bee has come flying;

ঘুরি ঘুরি বুলে পদ-তলে ।
গুণ গুণ শবদ রসালে ॥

*ghuri ghuri bule pada-tale |*
*guṇa guṇa śabada rasāle ||*

*Word for word:* ghuri ghuri bule — circles round and round; pada-tale — at the feet; guna guna shabada — a humming sound; rasale — sweet

**3.4.** round and round it circles at His feet,
humming sweetly.

গোবিন্দ ঘোষের মনে জাগে ।
গোরা না দেখিলে বিষ লাগে ॥

*gobinda ghoṣera mane jāge |*
*gorā nā dekhile biṣa lāge ||*

*Word for word:* gobinda ghoshera mane jage — in Govinda Ghosha's heart it awakens; gora na dekhile — if I do not see Gora; bisha lage — [all] tastes of poison

**3.5.** In Govinda Ghosha's heart it awakens:
if I do not see Gora, everything tastes of poison.

[^04-10]: The signature is "Govinda Ghosha". PK: 18th pallava "The form of Sri Gauranga, etc." (vol. 3, PDF p. 248, printed
p. 237; MS P-R-Sa no. 2253); GPT1 — p. 116, no. 17; GPT2 — sect. 3.1, no. 17 (almost without variants). Majumdar quotes
from it the lines "without cause Gora's face smiles" and "if I do not see Gora, everything tastes of poison".
[^04-11]: "Without cause" (bini) — the smile comes not from an outward occasion but from inner joy. Yellow silk (pita-pata) is
Krishna's garment; in Navadvipa the Lord, in Krishna's mood, asked for yellow cloth (cf. PK 2122, chapter 3, no. 1). MS
P-R-Sa: "mukhe" ("on the face").

## 4. Govinda Ghosha — "śrīdāma sudāma saṅge ye rasa karilum̐ raṅge…" (PK 2128; BR, p. 919)
*Lila: Navadvipa — the Lord remembers the pastimes of Vrindavana and, crying "The flute, the flute!", falls senseless into
Gadadhara's lap; then, in Radha's mood, He repeats Her name and calls Lalita and Vishakha. Around Him are Vasu Ghosha,
Ramananda, Srivasa, Jagadananda, Narahari. According to Majumdar — an eyewitness's testimony; he cites the line about
Narahari as proof that Narahari Sarakara was with the Lord already in Navadvipa. Raga mangala (PK, GPT), dhanashi (BR).*[^04-12]

শ্রীদাম সুদাম সঙ্গে যে রস করিলুঁ রঙ্গে
বলি পহু করে উতরোল ।
মুরলী মুরলী করি মুরছিত গৌরহরি
পড়ে পহু গদাধর-কোল ॥

*śrīdāma sudāma saṅge ye rasa karilum̐ raṅge*
*bali pahu kare utarola |*
*muralī muralī kari murachita gaurahari*
*paṛe pahu gadādhara-kola ||*

*Word for word:* shridama sudama sange — with Shridama and Sudama; ye rasa karilu range — the pastimes (rasa) I enjoyed with delight; boli — saying; pahu kare utarola — the Lord cries out in agitation; murali murali kari — crying "the flute, the flute"; murachhita gaurahari — Gaurahari swoons; pare pahu gadadhara-kola — the Lord falls into Gadadhara's lap

**4.1.** "The pastimes I enjoyed so gladly with Shridama and Sudama!.." —
saying this, the Lord cries out in agitation.
Crying "The flute, the flute!", Gaurahari loses consciousness,
and the Lord falls into Gadadhara's lap.[^04-13]

রাস-রস বৃন্দাবন প্রিয় সখা সখীগণ
উপজয়ে প্রেম-তরঙ্গ ।
বাসুঘোষ রামানন্দ শ্রীবাস জগদানন্দ
মাতে পহু নরহরি সঙ্গ ॥

*rāsa-rasa bṛndābana priya sakhā sakhīgaṇa*
*upajaye prema-taraṅga |*
*bāsughoṣa rāmānanda śrībāsa jagadānanda*
*māte pahu narahari saṅga ||*

*Word for word:* rasa-rasa — the rasa-lila; vrindavana — Vrindavana; priya sakha sakhigana — dear friends and girl-companions; upajaye prema-taranga — waves of prema arise; basughosha ramananda shribasa jagadananda — Vasu Ghosha, Ramananda, Srivasa, Jagadananda; mate pahu — the Lord is intoxicated; narahari sanga — together with Narahari

**4.2.** The rasa-lila, Vrindavana, the dear friends and girl-companions —
waves of prema rise.
Vasu Ghosha, Ramananda, Srivasa, Jagadananda —
with Narahari the Lord is intoxicated.[^04-14]

রাধা-ভাবে বিভোরা বরণ হইল গোরা
রাধা নাম জপে অনুক্ষণ ।
ললিতা বিশাখা বলি পহু যান গড়াগড়ি
কাহাঁ মোর গিরি গোবর্দ্ধন ॥

*rādhā-bhābe bibhorā baraṇa haila gorā*
*rādhā nāma jape anukṣaṇa |*
*lalitā biśākhā bali pahu yāna gaṛāgaṛi*
*kāhām̐ mora giri gobarddhana ||*

*Word for word:* radha-bhabe bibhora — absorbed in Radha's mood; barana haila gora — the complexion became golden; radha nama jape anukshana — ceaselessly repeats Radha's name; lalita vishakha boli — crying "Lalita, Vishakha"; pahu yana garagari — the Lord rolls on the ground; kaha mora giri gobardhana — where is My hill Govardhana

**4.3.** Absorbed in Radha's mood, He has become golden — Gora —
and ceaselessly repeats Radha's name.
Crying "Lalita, Vishakha!", the Lord rolls on the ground:
"Where is My hill Govardhana?

কাহাঁ যমুনার তট কাহাঁ মোর বংশীবট
বলি পুন হরল চেতন ।
এ দীন গোবিন্দ ঘোষে তা পাওল লব-লেশে
ধিক রহু ঐছন জীবন ॥

*kāhām̐ yamunāra taṭa kāhām̐ mora baṃśībaṭa*
*bali puna harala cetana |*
*e dīna gobinda ghoṣe tā pāola laba-leśe*
*dhika rahu aichana jībana ||*

*Word for word:* kaha yamunara tata — where is the bank of the Yamuna; kaha mora vamshivata — where is My Vamshivata; boli — saying; puna harala chetana — again loses consciousness; e dina gobinda ghoshe — this poor Govinda Ghosha; ta paola laba-leshe — received but a particle of it; dhika rahu aichhana jibana — shame on such a life

**4.4.** Where is the bank of the Yamuna? Where is My banyan Vamshivata?" —
saying this, He again loses consciousness.
Poor Govinda Ghosha received but a particle of this —
shame on such a life![^04-15]

[^04-12]: The signature is "Govinda Ghosha". PK: vol. 3, PDF pp. 239–240 (printed pp. 228–229), 18th pallava, right after
Shivananda Sena's pada PK 2127; MS P-R-Sa no. 2235; after it PK notes "Such is the description of absorption in bhava".
Narahari Chakravarti quotes the pada in BR (wave 12; ed. 1913, p. 919; ed. 1960, vv. 2997–3000) among the testimonies to
the Lord's moods in Navadvipa; GPT1 — pp. 281–282, no. 15; GPT2 — sect. 4.3, no. 15. Majumdar quotes the line about Vasu
Ghosha, Ramananda, Srivasa, Jagadananda and Narahari after BR. In the stage-1 catalogue the first line of the next pada
(PK 2129) was wrongly assigned to PK 2128.
[^04-13]: Shridama and Sudama are Krishna's cowherd friends in Vraja; BR and GPT read "Shridama and Subala". The Lord in
Krishna's mood remembers His pastimes with His friends. Gadadhara Pandita, according to the *Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika*, is a
manifestation of Radha in Gaura's lila (cf. chapter 3, no. 1).
[^04-14]: "Ramananda" is probably Ramananda Vasu of Kulinagrama (the Lord met Ramananda Raya only after His sannyasa). BR and
GPT read "the Lord dances with Narahari". Majumdar sees in the line proof that Narahari Sarakara was a companion of the Lord
already in Navadvipa.
[^04-15]: "In Radha's mood… became golden" — cf. CC Adi 4: Krishna took on Radha's lustre and mood to taste Her love.
Vamshivata is the banyan in Vrindavana under which Krishna played the flute. BR and GPT1 read "nā pāyala labaleśe" — "did
not receive even a particle"; P-R-Sa, BR and GPT — "e chāra jībana" — "this wretched life". The signature is the usual
formula of humility.

## 5. Vasu Ghosha — "dekhata jhulata gauracandra…" (PK 1550)
*Lila: Navadvipa — the swing festival (jhulana) in the bright fortnight of Shravana: the devotees swing Gaurachandra, the
townspeople come running at the cries of "Hari, Hari!". In PK — the gaura-chandrika opening the section on the swinging
of Radha and Krishna. According to Majumdar — a pada about an event Vasu Ghosha saw himself. Raga jayajayanti.*[^04-16]

দেখত ঝুলত গৌরচন্দ্র
অপরূপ দ্বিজমণিয়া ।
বিধির অবধি রূপ নিরুপম
কষিল কাঞ্চন জিনিয়া ॥

*dekhata jhulata gauracandra*
*aparūpa dvijamaṇiyā |*
*bidhira abadhi rūpa nirupama*
*kaṣila kāñcana jiniyā ||*

*Word for word:* dekhata — behold; jhulata gaurachandra — Gaurachandra swings; aparupa dvijamaniya — the wondrous jewel among the twice-born; bidhira abadhi — the utmost of the Creator['s making]; rupa nirupama — a matchless form; kashila kanchana jiniya — outshining tested gold

**5.1.** Behold: Gaurachandra is swinging,
the wondrous jewel among the twice-born;
the utmost of the Creator's making, a matchless form
that outshines tested gold.

ঝুলায়ত কত ভকতবৃন্দ
গৌরচন্দ্র বেড়িয়া ।
আনন্দে সঘন জয় জয় রব
উথলে নগর ভরিয়া ॥

*jhulāyata kata bhakatabṛnda*
*gauracandra beṛiyā |*
*ānande saghana jaya jaya raba*
*uthale nagara bhariyā ||*

*Word for word:* jhulayata — swing [Him]; kata bhakatabrinda — many devotees; gaurachandra bediya — surrounding Gaurachandra; anande — in joy; saghana — again and again; jaya jaya raba — cries of "Jaya!"; uthale nagara bhariya — surging, filling the town

**5.2.** Many devotees push the swing,
surrounding Gaurachandra;
in joy the cries of "Jaya!" sound again and again,
overflowing the town in a wave.[^04-17]

নয়ন-কমল মুখ নিরমল
শরদ-চাঁদ জিনিয়া ।
নগরের লোক ধায় এক-মুখ
হরি হরি ধ্বনি শুনিয়া ॥

*nayana-kamala mukha niramala*
*śarada-cām̐da jiniyā |*
*nagarera loka dhāya eka-mukha*
*hari hari dhvani śuniyā ||*

*Word for word:* nayana-kamala — lotus-eyes; mukha niramala — a spotless face; sharada-chanda jiniya — outshining the autumn moon; nagarera loka — the townspeople; dhaya eka-mukha — run all in one direction (in a throng); hari hari dhvani shuniya — hearing the cries of "Hari, Hari"

**5.3.** Eyes like lotuses, a spotless face
that outshines the autumn moon;
the townspeople come running in a throng,
hearing the cries of "Hari, Hari!".

ধন্য কলিযুগ গোরা অবতার
সুরধুনী ধনি ধনিয়া ।
গোরাচান্দ বিনে আন নাহি মনে
বাসুঘোষে কহে জানিয়া ॥

*dhanya kaliyuga gorā abatāra*
*suradhunī dhani dhaniyā |*
*gorācānda bine āna nāhi mane*
*bāsughoṣe kahe jāniyā ||*

*Word for word:* dhanya kaliyuga — blessed is the Kali age; gora avatara — Gora's descent; suradhuni dhani dhaniya — blessed, blessed the Suradhuni (Ganga); gorachanda bine — apart from Gorachand; ana nahi mane — nothing else is in the heart; basughoshe kahe janiya — Vasu Ghosha says, having understood

**5.4.** Blessed is the Kali age, blessed Gora's descent,
blessed, blessed the Suradhuni!
Nothing but Gorachand is in the heart —
so says Vasu Ghosha, having understood this.[^04-18]

[^04-16]: The signature is "Vasu Ghosha". PK: vol. 2, PDF p. 456 (printed p. 441), 30th pallava of the 3rd shakha ("The
swing lila"), under the heading "Now, the swinging game in the bright fortnight of Shravana. Jhulana. Here — Sri
Gaurachandra"; MS P-R-Sa no. 2015. In GPT (GPT1, pp. 323–324, no. 8; GPT2, section on the jhulana, no. 8) the pada is
shorter — three couplets: after the first two comes "Eyes like lotuses… outshines the autumn moon; / with Gadadhara He
swings joyfully — seeing it, Shiva-Ram is blessed", i.e. the signature of the poet Shivarama. Majumdar counts PK 1550
among Vasu Ghosha's historically valuable padas describing what the poet saw himself (the jhulana); we accept the
signature of Vasu after PK.
[^04-17]: The end of the couplet is damaged in the PK scan; we read "uthale nagara bhariyā" ("overflowing the town in a
wave"); GPT: "uṭhata nāgara nadīyā" ("[the din] rises in the town of Nadia").
[^04-18]: The Suradhuni is the Ganga, on whose bank the swing was set up. "Having understood this" — having understood that
Gaura is the Lord Himself.

## 6. Narahari — "āju racita naba ratana-him̐ḍora…" (PK 1559)
*Lila: Navadvipa — the jhulana: on the bank of the Ganga, under a tall tree, a new jewelled swing has been set up; the
companions swing Gaura, sing and dance to the drums, the people of Nadia come running, the gods shower the Lord with
flowers. In PK — a gaura-chandrika in the same section on the jhulana. Raga imana-beloyara.*[^04-19]

আজু রচিত নব রতন-হিঁডোর ।
সুরধুনি-তীর তুঙ্গ-তরু-তল তহিঁ
রসময় গৌর কিশোর ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*āju racita naba ratana-him̐ḍora |*
*suradhuni-tīra tuṅga-taru-tala tahim̐*
*rasamaya gaura kiśora || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* aju — today; rachita — has been set up; naba ratana-hindora — a new jewelled swing; suradhuni-tira — on the bank of the Suradhuni; tunga-taru-tala — under a tall tree; tahi — there; rasamaya gaura kishora — the young Gaura, full of rasa

**6.1.** *(Refrain)* Today a new jewelled swing has been set up;
there, on the bank of the Suradhuni, under a tall tree, —
the young Gaura, full of rasa.

পরিকর সুঘড় ঝুলায়ত লহু লহু
গাওত তান সরস রস মাতি ।
উঘটত খোল খোল তক থৈ থৈ
নাচত মধুর বাওত বহু ভাতি ॥

*parikara sughaṛa jhulāyata lahu lahu*
*gāota tāna sarasa rasa māti |*
*ughaṭata khola khola taka thai thai*
*nācata madhura bāota bahu bhāti ||*

*Word for word:* parikara sughara — the skilful companions; jhulayata lahu lahu — gently swing [Him]; gaota tana — sing melodies; sarasa rasa mati — intoxicated with sweet rasa; ughatata — call out [the rhythmic syllables]; khola khola taka thai thai — "khol, khol, tak, thai-thai"; nachata madhura — dance sweetly; baota bahu bhati — play in many ways

**6.2.** The skilful companions gently push the swing
and sing melodies, intoxicated with sweet rasa;
they call out the syllables of the rhythm — "khol, khol, tak, thai-thai" —
dance sweetly and play in every manner.[^04-20]

নদীয়া নগর না রহু কোই ঘর
তেজি চলত চৌদিশে নরনারী ।
অধিক উছাহ হোয়ত হিয়ে পহুঁক
হাস-মিলিত মুখ-চাঁদ নেহারি ॥

*nadīyā nagara nā rahu koi ghara*
*teji calata caudiśe naranārī |*
*adhika uchāha hoyata hiye pahum̐ka*
*hāsa-milita mukha-cām̐da nehāri ||*

*Word for word:* nadiya nagara — in the town of Nadia; na rahu koi ghara — no one stays at home; teji — leaving [them]; chalata chaudishe nara-nari — men and women come from all sides; adhika uchhaha hoyata hiye — joy grows ever greater in the heart; pahuka — the Lord's; hasa-milita mukha-chanda nehari — beholding the smiling moon-face

**6.3.** In the town of Nadia no one has stayed at home:
from every side men and women come;
the joy in their hearts grows ever greater
as they behold the Lord's smiling moon-face.

সুরগণ গগনে মগন গণ সহ সুখে
বরিখত কুসুম করত জয়কার ।
নরহরি ভণত ভুবন উমতায়ল
কো কহুঁ অদভুত রঙ্গ অপার ॥

*suragaṇa gagane magana gaṇa saha sukhe*
*barikhata kusuma karata jayakāra |*
*narahari bhaṇata bhubana umatāyala*
*ko kahum̐ adabhuta raṅga apāra ||*

*Word for word:* suragana gagane — the gods in the sky; magana — immersed [in bliss]; gana saha — with their retinues; sukhe — joyfully; barikhata kusuma — shower flowers; karata jayakara — cry "Jaya"; narahari bhanata — Narahari says; bhubana umatayala — the world has gone mad [with joy]; ko kahu — who can tell; adabhuta ranga apara — the wondrous, boundless play

**6.4.** The gods in the sky with their retinues, in bliss,
shower flowers and cry "Jaya!";
Narahari says: the world has gone mad with joy —
who can describe this wondrous, boundless play?[^04-21]

[^04-19]: The signature is "Narahari". PK: vol. 2, PDF p. 460 (printed p. 445), 30th pallava, the third pada of the section
on the jhulana after the padas of Shivarama (PK 1556–1557, the swinging of Radha and Krishna) and Uddhava Dasa (PK 1558,
Gaura swinging with Gadadhara); MS P-R-Sa no. 2103. GPT1 — p. 326, no. 16 (raga imana); GPT2 — section on the jhulana,
no. 16. S. Ray's index of poets assigns PK 1557 to Narahari, but that is Shivarama's pada on the swinging of Radha and
Krishna; the gaura-pada signed Narahari in this section is PK 1559. The attribution to Narahari Sarakara is not proven: the
signature "Narahari" is also borne by padas of Narahari Chakravarti, and the language here is Vrajabuli, which according
to Majumdar is absent from Sarakara's genuine padas.
[^04-20]: The khol is a clay drum (mridanga); "tak, thai-thai" are rhythmic syllables of the dance. For "play" (bāota) MS
P-R-Sa reads "bājāyata" (same sense).
[^04-21]: "Has gone mad" (umatāyala) — intoxicated with the joy of prema at the sight of the Lord.

## 7. Chaitanyadasa — "gaurāṅga-cāndera mane ki bhāba uṭhila…" (PK 1169)
*Lila: Navadvipa — the goshtha-lila: seeing Gauridasa, the Lord remembers His play as a cowherd boy, asks for the milking
rope and the milk pail, calls the cows Dhavali and Shangali and His friends Shridama and Sudama; Nityananda embraces Him. In
PK — the gaura-chandrika to the goshthashtami festival. According to Majumdar — the same goshtha-lila (Gauridasa, the
milking rope) as in Vasu Ghosha. Raga bhupali.*[^04-22]

গৌরাঙ্গ-চান্দের মনে কি ভাব উঠিল ।
পুরুব-চরিত্র বুঝি মনেতে পড়িল ॥

*gaurāṅga-cāndera mane ki bhāba uṭhila |*
*puruba-caritra bujhi manete paṛila ||*

*Word for word:* gauranga-chandera mane — in Gaurangachand's heart; ki bhaba uthila — what bhava has arisen; puruba-charitra — the former deeds; bujhi — it seems; manete parila — came to mind

**7.1.** What bhava has arisen in the heart of Gaurangachand?
It seems He has remembered His former deeds.

গৌরীদাস-মুখ হেরি উলসিত হিয়া ।
আনহ ছান্দন ডুরি বোলে ডাক দিয়া ॥

*gaurīdāsa-mukha heri ulasita hiyā |*
*ānaha chāndana ḍuri bole ḍāka diyā ||*

*Word for word:* gauridasa-mukha heri — seeing Gauridasa's face; ulasita hiya — the heart rejoices; anaha chhandana duri — "bring the milking rope"; bole daka diya — He says, calling aloud

**7.2.** Seeing Gauridasa's face, He rejoices at heart
and calls aloud: "Bring the milking rope!

আজি শুভ দিন চল গোঠেরে যাইব ।
আজি হৈতে গো-দোহন আরম্ভ করিব ॥

*āji śubha dina cala goṭhere yāiba |*
*āji haite go-dohana ārambha kariba ||*

*Word for word:* aji shubha dina — today is an auspicious day; chala gothere yaiba — come, let us go to the pasture; aji haite — from today; go-dohana arambha kariba — I shall begin milking the cows

**7.3.** Today is an auspicious day — let us go to the pasture:
from today I shall begin to milk the cows.

ধবলী সাঙলী কোথা শ্রীদাম সুদাম ।
দোহনের ভাণ্ড মোর হাতে দেহ রাম ॥

*dhabalī sāṅalī kothā śrīdāma sudāma |*
*dohanera bhāṇḍa mora hāte deha rāma ||*

*Word for word:* dhabali shangali — Dhavali and Shangali (cows); kotha — where; shridama sudama — Shridama and Sudama; dohanera bhanda — the milk pail; mora hate deha — give into My hands; rama — Rama (Balarama — Nityananda)

**7.4.** Where are Dhavali and Shangali? Where are Shridama and Sudama?
Give the milk pail into My hands, Rama!"[^04-23]

ভাবাবেশে বেয়াকুল শচীর নন্দন ।
নিত্যানন্দ আসি কোলে করে সেই ক্ষণ ॥

*bhābābeśe beyākula śacīra nandana |*
*nityānanda āsi kole kare sei kṣaṇa ||*

*Word for word:* bhababeshe beyakula — beside Himself with bhava; shachira nandana — the son of Shachi; nityananda asi — Nityananda, coming; kole kare sei kshana — at once embraces [Him]

**7.5.** Beside Himself with bhava is the son of Shachi;
and at once Nityananda comes and embraces Him.

চৈতন্যদাসেতে বলে ছান্দনের দড়ি ।
হারাইল গৌরীদাস গোপী কৈল চুরি ॥

*caitanyadāsete bale chāndanera daṛi |*
*hārāila gaurīdāsa gopī kaila curi ||*

*Word for word:* chaitanyadasete bale — Chaitanyadasa says; chhandanera dari — the milking rope; haraila gauridasa — Gauridasa has lost; gopi kaila churi — the gopis have stolen [it]

**7.6.** Chaitanyadasa says: the milking rope
Gauridasa has lost — the gopis have stolen it.[^04-24]

[^04-22]: The signature is "Chaitanyadasa". PK: vol. 2, PDF p. 286, 20th pallava of the 3rd shakha, the first pada of the
section "Goshthashtami-yatra", under the heading "Sri Gaurachandra"; MS P-R-Sa no. 1700. GPT1 — p. 331, no. 32 (raga
bhupala); GPT2 — no. 32 — with minor variants. Goshthashtami (Kartika, eighth day of the bright fortnight) is the festival
of Krishna's first going out to herd the cows. Majumdar regards Chaitanyadasa (probably of Gadadhara's branch) as a
contemporary and compares the pada with the goshtha-lila in Vasu Ghosha (BR, p. 935; chapter 1, no. 11) and Vamshivadana
(PK 2564; chapter 1, no. 12).
[^04-23]: Dhavali ("the white one") and Shangali (śāṅalī, "the dark one"; GPT — Shamali, the same sense) are Krishna's cows.
"Rama" is Balarama: so the Lord addresses Nityananda, who in Krishna's lila is Balarama. Shridama and Sudama are Krishna's
cowherd friends.
[^04-24]: A playful signature: Gauridasa Pandita in Krishna's lila is the cowherd boy Subala (according to the
*Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika*), and in Vraja the gopis hide the milking rope to delay Krishna. GPT and MS P-R-Sa read "ḍuri"
for "daṛi" (same sense).

## 8. Nayanananda — "kali-ghora-timire garāsala jaga-jana…" (PK 2204)
*Praise of Gaura: when the darkness of Kali had swallowed the world and people had abandoned dharma, the Creator granted,
without any sadhana, the chintamani gem — Gora, the Lord of great mercy; learning without worship of Gauranga is useless.
Raga shri (PK), suhai (GPT).*[^04-25]

কলি-ঘোর-তিমিরে গরাসল জগ-জন
ধরম করম রহু দূর ।
অসাধনে চিন্তামণি বিহি মিলাওল আনি
গোরা বড় দয়ার ঠাকুর ॥

*kali-ghora-timire garāsala jaga-jana*
*dharama karama rahu dūra |*
*asādhane cintāmaṇi bihi milāola āni*
*gorā baṛa dayāra ṭhākura ||*

*Word for word:* kali-ghora-timire — the dense darkness of Kali; garasala jaga-jana — has swallowed the people of the world; dharama karama rahu dura — dharma and righteous deeds remain far off; asadhane — without sadhana, without effort; chintamani — the chintamani gem; bihi milaola ani — the Creator brought and bestowed; gora bara dayara thakura — Gora, the Lord of great mercy

**8.1.** The dense darkness of Kali has swallowed the people of the world,
dharma and righteous deeds remain far away;
without any effort the Creator brought and bestowed the chintamani gem —
Gora, the Lord of great mercy.[^04-26]

ভাই রে ভাই গোরা-গুণ কহনে না যায় ।
কত শত-আনন কত চতুরানন
বরণিয়া ওর না পায় ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*bhāi re bhāi gorā-guṇa kahane nā yāya |*
*kata śata-ānana kata caturānana*
*baraṇiyā ora nā pāya || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* bhai re bhai — brother, O brother; gora-guna kahane na yaya — Gora's virtues cannot be told; kata shata-anana — however many hundred-mouthed ones; kata chaturanana — however many four-faced ones; baraniya ora na paya — describing, they find no end

**8.2.** *(Refrain)* Brother, brother, Gora's virtues cannot be told:
however many hundred-mouthed ones, however many four-faced ones there are —
describing them, they find no end.[^04-27]

চারি বেদ ষড় দরশন পড়িয়া যে
সে যদি গৌরাঙ্গ নাহি ভজে ।
কিবা তার অধ্যয়ন লোচন-বিহীন যেন
দরপণে কিবা তার কাজে ॥

*cāri beda ṣaṛa daraśana paṛiyā ye*
*se yadi gaurāṅga nāhi bhaje |*
*kibā tāra adhyayana locana-bihīna yena*
*darapaṇe kibā tāra kāje ||*

*Word for word:* chari beda — the four Vedas; shara darashana — the six darshanas; pariya ye — who has studied; se yadi gauranga nahi bhaje — if he does not worship Gauranga; kiba tara adhyayana — what use is his study; lochana-bihina yena — as to one without eyes; darapane kiba tara kaje — what use to him is a mirror

**8.3.** One who has studied the four Vedas and six darshanas
but does not worship Gauranga —
what use is his learning? As a mirror to the blind,
so is all his knowledge to him.[^04-28]

বেদ বিদ্যা দুই কিছুই না জানত
সে যদি গৌরাঙ্গ জানে সার ।
নয়নানন্দ ভণে সেই সে সকল জানে
সর্ব্ব সিদ্ধি করতলে তার ॥

*beda bidyā dui kichui nā jānata*
*se yadi gaurāṅga jāne sāra |*
*nayanānanda bhaṇe sei se sakala jāne*
*sarvva siddhi karatale tāra ||*

*Word for word:* beda bidya dui — the Vedas and learning, both; kichhui na janata — knows nothing of; se yadi gauranga jane sara — if he knows Gauranga as the essence; nayanananda bhane — says Nayanananda; sei se sakala jane — he indeed knows all; sarva siddhi karatale tara — all perfections are in the palm of his hand

**8.4.** One who knows neither the Vedas nor learning
but knows that Gauranga is the essence of all —
says Nayanananda — he knows everything,
all perfections lie in the palm of his hand.

[^04-25]: The signature is "Nayanananda". PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 270 (printed p. 259), 20th pallava ("Sri Gaurachandra — another
manner"), raga the same as that of the preceding pada (shri); MS P-R-Sa no. 2312. GPT1 — p. 32, no. 18 (raga suhai);
GPT2 — sect. 1.3, no. 18. Nayanananda (Nayana Mishra) is the nephew and disciple of Gadadhara Pandita; Majumdar counts him
among the contemporary poets. In the stage-1 catalogue a GPT-only pada signed Narahari, "gorā baṛa dayāra ṭhākura" (NS-009),
was wrongly linked to PK 2204: the words "Gora, the Lord of great mercy" occur here too, but PK 2204 is Nayanananda's
pada.
[^04-26]: Chintamani is the wish-fulfilling gem. "Without any effort" (asādhane) — without sadhana: Gaura bestows prema by
causeless mercy, without asking about qualification (cf. CC Adi 8).
[^04-27]: "The hundred-mouthed" — Ananta-Shesha, who ever sings of the Lord with a thousand mouths; "the four-faced" — the
Brahmas of the universes.
[^04-28]: PK: "as to the eyeless [a mirror] — what is a mirror to him?"; GPT: "what is the blind man to do with a mirror?". The
six darshanas are the six philosophical schools (nyaya, vaisheshika, sankhya, yoga, mimamsa, vedanta).

## 9. Raya Ananta — "preme matta nityānanda…" (KGC, 11th kshanada)
*Praise of Nityananda: intoxicated with prema, He walks swaying, rolls on the ground with the name of Hari and weeps looking
at the face of His brother, Gaura; Advaita, seeing Him, roars; the companions sing the names of Hari and Gaura. Raga
kamoda (KGC), mangala (GPT).*[^04-29]

প্রেমে মত্ত নিত্যানন্দ সহজে আনন্দ-কন্দ
ঢুলিয়া ঢুলিয়া চলি যায় ।
ভায়ার ভাবেতে মত্ত জানেন সকল তত্ত্ব
হরি বলি অবনী লোটায় ॥

*preme matta nityānanda sahaje ānanda-kanda*
*ḍhuliyā ḍhuliyā cali yāya |*
*bhāyāra bhābete matta jānena sakala tattva*
*hari bali abanī loṭāya ||*

*Word for word:* preme matta nityananda — Nityananda, intoxicated with prema; sahaje ananda-kanda — by nature the source of bliss; dhuliya dhuliya chali yaya — walks swaying, swaying; bhayara bhabete matta — intoxicated with His brother's mood; janena sakala tattva — knowing all truths; hari boli abani lotaya — crying "Hari" rolls on the ground

**9.1.** Nityananda, intoxicated with prema, the source of natural bliss,
walks swaying, swaying;
intoxicated with His brother's mood, knowing all truths,
crying "Hari!" He rolls on the ground.[^04-30]

নিতাইর গোরা-প্রেমে গড়া তনুখানি ।
ভাইয়ার মুখ হেরি লুলিয়া লুলিয়া পড়ে
ধারা বহে সিঞ্চয়ে ধরণী ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*nitāira gorā-preme gaṛā tanukhāni |*
*bhāiyāra mukha heri luliyā luliyā paṛe*
*dhārā bahe siñcaye dharaṇī || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* nitaira gora-preme gara tanukhani — Nitai's body is moulded of love for Gora; bhaiyara mukha heri — looking at His brother's face; luliya luliya pare — limply sinks down; dhara bahe — streams flow; sinchaye dharani — watering the earth

**9.2.** *(Refrain)* Nitai's body is moulded of love for Gora;
looking at His brother's face, He sinks down limply,
and streams of tears flow, watering the earth.[^04-31]

অদ্বৈত আনন্দ-কন্দ হেরি নিতাইর মুখ-চন্দ
হুঙ্কার পুলক শোভে তায় ।
হরি হরি বোল বলে পুন গৌর গৌর বলে
প্রিয় পারিষদে গুণ গায় ॥

*advaita ānanda-kanda heri nitāira mukha-canda*
*huṅkāra pulaka śobhe tāya |*
*hari hari bola bale puna gaura gaura bale*
*priya pāriṣade guṇa gāya ||*

*Word for word:* advaita ananda-kanda — Advaita, the source of bliss; heri nitaira mukha-chanda — seeing Nitai's moon-face; hunkara pulaka shobhe taya — roars and bristling hair adorn him; hari hari bola bale — they cry "Hari, Hari"; puna gaura gaura bale — and again "Gaura, Gaura"; priya parishade guna gaya — the dear companions sing [His] virtues

**9.3.** Advaita, the source of bliss, seeing Nitai's moon-face,
roars, and His body bristles with rapture;
they cry "Hari, Hari!", and again "Gaura, Gaura!" —
the dear companions sing His virtues.

গোলোকের প্রেম-বন্যা অবনী করল ধন্যা
অতুল অপার রস-সিন্ধু ।
মাতিল জগত ভরি নিতাই চৈতন্য করি
রায় অনন্ত মাগে বিন্দু ॥

*golokera prema-banyā abanī karala dhanyā*
*atula apāra rasa-sindhu |*
*mātila jagata bhari nitāi caitanya kari*
*rāya ananta māge bindu ||*

*Word for word:* golokera prema-banya — the flood of Goloka's prema; abani karala dhanya — has blessed the earth; atula apara rasa-sindhu — a matchless, boundless ocean of rasa; matila jagata bhari — the world is intoxicated, filled; nitai chaitanya kari — [with the names] "Nitai — Chaitanya"; raya ananta mage bindu — Raya Ananta begs a drop

**9.4.** The flood of Goloka's prema has blessed the earth —
a matchless, boundless ocean of rasa;
the world is intoxicated, filled with the names "Nitai — Chaitanya";
Raya Ananta begs but a drop.[^04-32]

[^04-29]: The signature is "Raya Ananta" (rāya ananta). The pada is known from KGC (11th kshanada — Krishna-ekadashi, no. 2,
a gaura-chandrika marked "of Sri Nityananda"; p. 83) and GPT (GPT1 — pp. 429–430, no. 52; GPT2 — sect. 6.1, no. 52); it had
not previously been found in PK (see below). B. B. Majumdar (1961) identifies the "Raya Ananta" of KGC with Ananta of Advaita's branch, a contemporary of the
Lord; the identification is not proven. The text follows KGC (checked against the scan).
Full PK check (chapter 16): the pada is also in PK — **PK 2328** (vol. 3, 22nd pallava, PDF pp. 313–314, label "॥৩৫॥২৩২৮॥", MS P-R-Sa no. 2432); PK signature "ananta nā pāila eka bindu" (MSS ka, kha: "rāya ananta māge eka bindu").
[^04-30]: "The source of natural bliss" (sahaje ānanda-kanda) — Nityananda ("eternal bliss") by His very nature. "Knowing all
truths" — Nityananda (Balarama) knows the hidden truth about Gaura.
[^04-31]: "Brother" (bhāiyā) is Gaura; for "looking at His brother's face" GPT reads "looking at Gadadhara's face".
[^04-32]: Goloka is Krishna's supreme abode; "the flood of Goloka's prema" is the prema that Gaura and Nitai brought to the
earth. GPT: "begs a single drop".

## 10. Vasu Ghosha — "śacīra mandire āsi duyārera pāśe basi…" (PK 2221)
*Lila: the last night in Navadvipa — Vishnupriya wakes, does not find the Lord and comes to Shachi; Shachi and her
daughter-in-law search for Nimai with a lamp, the people of Nadia question passers-by; someone has seen Him on the road to
Kanchananagara (Katwa). According to Majumdar — a pada of Vasu Ghosha's cycle on the sannyasa ("Nimai-sannyasa"): a
historical picture with poetic exaggerations. Raga bibhasa-karuna.*[^04-33]

শচীর মন্দিরে আসি দুয়ারের পাশে বসি
ধীরে ধীরে কহে বিষ্ণুপ্রিয়া ।
শয়ন-মন্দিরে ছিলা নিশিভাগে কোথা গেলা
মোর মুণ্ডে বজর পাড়িয়া ॥

*śacīra mandire āsi duyārera pāśe basi*
*dhīre dhīre kahe biṣṇupriyā |*
*śayana-mandire chilā niśibhāge kothā gelā*
*mora muṇḍe bajara pāṛiyā ||*

*Word for word:* shachira mandire asi — coming to Shachi's rooms; duyarera pashe basi — sitting by the door; dhire dhire kahe vishnupriya — softly Vishnupriya says; shayana-mandire chhila — [He] was in the bedchamber; nishibhage kotha gela — where did He go in the night; mora munde bajara pariya — bringing down a thunderbolt on my head

**10.1.** Coming to Shachi's rooms, sitting down by the door,
softly Vishnupriya speaks:
"He was in the bedchamber — where has He gone in the night,
bringing down a thunderbolt upon my head?

গৌরাঙ্গ জাগয়ে মনে নিদ্রা নাহি দুনয়নে
শুনিয়া উঠিলা শচী মাতা ।
আউদড়-কেশে ধায় বসন না রহে গায়
শুনিয়া বধূর মুখের কথা ॥

*gaurāṅga jāgaye mane nidrā nāhi dunayane*
*śuniyā uṭhilā śacī mātā |*
*āudaṛa-keśe dhāya basana nā rahe gāya*
*śuniyā badhūra mukhera kathā ||*

*Word for word:* gauranga jagaye mane — Gauranga is awake in [my] heart; nidra nahi dunayane — no sleep in both eyes; shuniya uthila shachi mata — hearing, mother Shachi rose; audara-keshe dhaya — she runs with dishevelled hair; basana na rahe gaya — her cloth does not stay on her body; shuniya badhura mukhera katha — hearing her daughter-in-law's words

**10.2.** Gauranga is awake in my heart, there is no sleep in my eyes…" —
hearing this, Mother Shachi rose;
with dishevelled hair she runs, her cloth slipping off —
hearing her daughter-in-law's words.[^04-34]

তুরিতে জ্বালিয়া বাতি দেখিলেন ইতি উতি
কোন ঠাঞি উদ্দেশ না পাইয়া ।
বিষ্ণুপ্রিয়া বধূ সাথে কান্দিতে কান্দিতে পথে
ডাকে শচী নিমাঞি বলিয়া ॥

*turite jvāliyā bāti dekhilena iti uti*
*kona ṭhāñi uddeśa nā pāiyā |*
*biṣṇupriyā badhū sāthe kāndite kāndite pathe*
*ḍāke śacī nimāñi baliyā ||*

*Word for word:* turite jvaliya bati — quickly lighting a lamp; dekhilena iti uti — she looked here and there; kona thanyi uddesha na paiya — finding no trace anywhere; vishnupriya badhu sathe — with her daughter-in-law Vishnupriya; kandite kandite pathe — weeping and weeping on the road; dake shachi nimanyi boliya — Shachi calls "Nimai!"

**10.3.** Quickly lighting a lamp, she looked here and there,
but nowhere found a trace;
together with her daughter-in-law Vishnupriya, weeping and weeping on the road,
Shachi calls: "Nimai!"

শুনিয়া নদীয়ার লোকে কান্দে উচ্চস্বরে শোকে
যারে তারে পুছেন বারতা ।
এক জন পথে যায় দশ জন পুছে তায়
গৌরাঙ্গ দেখ্যাছ যাইতে কোথা ॥

*śuniyā nadīyāra loke kānde uccasvare śoke*
*yāre tāre puchena bāratā |*
*eka jana pathe yāya daśa jana puche tāya*
*gaurāṅga dekhyācha yāite kothā ||*

*Word for word:* shuniya nadiyara loke — hearing, the people of Nadia; kande uchchasvare shoke — weep aloud in grief; yare tare puchhena barata — ask anyone for news; eka jana pathe yaya — one man goes along the road; dasha jana puchhe taya — ten ask him; gauranga dekhyachha yaite kotha — have you seen where Gauranga went

**10.4.** Hearing this, the people of Nadia weep aloud in grief,
asking everyone for news:
if one man goes along the road, ten ask him:
"Have you seen where Gauranga went?"

সে বলে দেখ্যাছি পথে কেহো ত নাহিক সাথে
কাঞ্চননগর-পথে ধায় ।
কহে বাসু ঘোষ ভাষা শচীর এমন দশা
পাছে জানি মস্তক মুড়ায় ॥

*se bale dekhyāchi pathe keho ta nāhika sāthe*
*kāñcananagara-pathe dhāya |*
*kahe bāsu ghoṣa bhāṣā śacīra emana daśā*
*pāche jāni mastaka muṛāya ||*

*Word for word:* se bale — he says; dekhyachhi pathe — I saw [Him] on the road; keho ta nahika sathe — no one is with Him; kanchananagara-pathe dhaya — He hastens on the road to Kanchananagara; kahe basu ghosha bhasha — Vasu Ghosha says; shachira emana dasha — such is Shachi's state; pachhe jani mastaka muraya — what if He shaves His head

**10.5.** He answers: "I saw Him on the road — no one was with Him,
He hastens along the road to Kanchananagara."
Vasu Ghosha says: such is Shachi's state —
"What if He shaves His head!"[^04-35]

[^04-33]: The signature is "Vasu Ghosha". PK: vol. 3, PDF pp. 275–276 (printed pp. 264–265), 21st pallava ("Sri Gauranga's
sannyasa, etc."), the fourth pada of the pallava — after Lochana Dasa's padas PK 2219 (before dawn the Lord goes to the
Ganga and on to Kanchananagara) and PK 2220 (Vishnupriya wakes and does not find the Lord); MS P-R-Sa no. 2326. GPT1 —
p. 372, no. 20 (raga bibhasa or karuna), GPT2 — sect. 5.3, no. 20: one couplet longer (at the beginning: "She touched the
bed with her hand — and a thunderbolt fell on her head…") and with another signature ("Vasu says: ah, my Sri Gaurahari —
what if He shaves His head!"). The events — CB Madhya 28; CC Adi 17; Murari 3.1; Lochana, Madhya-khanda. Majumdar includes
PK 2221–2223, 2225, 2226, 2229 in Vasu Ghosha's sannyasa cycle. In the stage-1 catalogue the first line of PK 2220 (a pada
of Lochana Dasa) was wrongly assigned to PK 2221.
[^04-34]: Vishnupriya thought of the Lord all night: "Gauranga is awake in my heart". GPT: "…no sleep in the eyes — hearing
this, mother Shachi awoke".
[^04-35]: Kanchananagara (Kantaka-nagara) is Katwa, where the Lord took sannyasa from Keshava Bharati. "Shaves His head" —
takes sannyasa.

## 11. Vasu Ghosha — "sakala mahānta meli sakāle sināna kari…" (PK 2222)
*Lila: the morning after the Lord's departure — the devotees come to see Gauranga, but He is gone: Vishnupriya lies
prostrate, Shachi weeps at the gate and asks who taught her son sannyasa. Raga pahida.*[^04-36]

সকল মহান্ত মেলি সকালে সিনান করি
আইলা গৌরাঙ্গ দেখিবারে ।
গৌরাঙ্গ গিয়াছে ছাড়ি বিষ্ণুপ্রিয়া আছে পড়ি
শচী কান্দে বাহির দুয়ারে ॥

*sakala mahānta meli sakāle sināna kari*
*āilā gaurāṅga dekhibāre |*
*gaurāṅga giyāche chāṛi biṣṇupriyā āche paṛi*
*śacī kānde bāhira duyāre ||*

*Word for word:* sakala mahanta meli — all the great souls together; sakale sinana kari — having bathed in the morning; aila gauranga dekhibare — came to see Gauranga; gauranga giyachhe chhari — Gauranga has gone, leaving [home]; vishnupriya achhe pari — Vishnupriya lies prostrate; shachi kande bahira duyare — Shachi weeps at the outer gate

**11.1.** All the great souls together, having bathed in the morning,
came to see Gauranga.
Gauranga has gone, leaving home; Vishnupriya lies prostrate,
Shachi weeps at the outer gate.[^04-37]

শচী কহে শুন মোর নিতাই গুণমণি ।
কেবা আসি দিলে মন্ত্র কে শিখাইলে কোন তন্ত্র
কিবা হৈল কিছুই না জানি ॥

*śacī kahe śuna mora nitāi guṇamaṇi |*
*kebā āsi dile mantra ke śikhāile kona tantra*
*kibā haila kichui nā jāni ||*

*Word for word:* shachi kahe — Shachi says; shuna mora nitai gunamani — listen, my Nitai, jewel of virtues; keba asi dile mantra — who came and gave a mantra; ke shikhaile kona tantra — who taught what tantra; kiba haila — what has happened; kichhui na jani — I know nothing

**11.2.** Shachi says: "Listen, my Nitai, jewel of virtues:
who came and gave Him a mantra, who taught Him what tantra?
What has happened — I know nothing.[^04-38]

গৃহ মাঝে শুয়্যা ছিলুঁ ভাল মন্দ না জানিলুঁ
কিবা করি গেল রে ছাড়িয়া ।

*gṛha mājhe śuyyā chilum̐ bhāla manda nā jānilum̐*
*kibā kari gela re chāṛiyā |*

*Word for word:* griha majhe shuyya chhilu — I was asleep in the house; bhala manda na janilu — knowing neither good nor ill; kiba kari — what has [He] done; gela re chhariya — going away and leaving [me]

**11.3.** I was asleep in the house, knowing nothing —
what has He done, going away and leaving me?

কিবা নিঠুরাই কৈল পাথারে ভাসাঞা গেল
রহিব কাহার মুখ চাঞা ।

*kibā niṭhurāi kaila pāthāre bhāsāñā gela*
*rahiba kāhāra mukha cāñā |*

*Word for word:* kiba nithurai kaila — what cruelty He has done; pathare bhasanya gela — He went, casting [me] adrift on a shoreless sea; rahiba kahara mukha chanya — whose face shall I look to [to live]

**11.4.** What cruelty He has done! He has cast me adrift on a shoreless sea —
whose face shall I look to now?"

বাসুদেব ঘোষ ভাষা শচীর এমন দশা
মরা হেন রহিল পড়িয়া ।

*bāsudeba ghoṣa bhāṣā śacīra emana daśā*
*marā hena rahila paṛiyā |*

*Word for word:* vasudeva ghosha bhasha — Vasudeva Ghosha says; shachira emana dasha — such is Shachi's state; mara hena rahila pariya — she lies as if dead

**11.5.** Vasudeva Ghosha says: such is Shachi's state —
she lies as if dead;

শিরে করাঘাত মারি ঈশানে দেখায় ঠারি
গোরা গেল নদীয়া ছাড়িয়া ॥

*śire karāghāta māri īśāne dekhāya ṭhāri*
*gorā gela nadīyā chāṛiyā ||*

*Word for word:* shire karaghata mari — striking her head with her hand; ishane dekhaya thari — she shows Ishana by signs; gora gela nadiya chhariya — Gora has gone, leaving Nadia

**11.6.** striking her head with her hand, she gestures to Ishana:
"Gora has gone, leaving Nadia."[^04-39]

[^04-36]: The signature is "Vasudeva Ghosha". PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 276 (printed p. 265), 21st pallava, no. 5; MS P-R-Sa no. 2327,
P-R 40.34. GPT1 — p. 373, no. 22; GPT2 — sect. 5.3, no. 22 (OCR "21"). MS P-R gives a number of lines differently (see the full version of the book).
[^04-37]: Great souls (mahānta) — the senior devotees. MS P-R: "all went to Gora", "[Vishnupriya] senseless on the ground".
[^04-38]: "Nitai" — so the main text of PK and MS P-R; MSS "kha", P-R-Sa and GPT read "Nimai": Shachi addresses her departed son.
"Mantra" and "tantra" mean initiation into sannyasa: Shachi does not know who gave her son the mantra (according to CB Madhya
28, the Lord Himself whispered the sannyasa mantra into Keshava Bharati's ear and then received it from him).
[^04-39]: Ishana is the old servant in the house of Shachi and Vishnupriya. "Gestures" — in her grief she cannot speak.

## 12. Vasu Ghosha — "kāñcananagare eku bṛkṣa manohara…" (PK 2223)
*Lila: Katwa (Kanchananagara) — Gauranga sits under a tree on the bank of the Ganga; the townspeople come running, struck by
His beauty and resolve; Keshava Bharati appears, the Lord bows to him and asks for the gift of devotion. Raga shri.*[^04-40]

কাঞ্চননগরে একু বৃক্ষ মনোহর ।
সুরধুনী-তীরে ছায়া শীতল সুন্দর ॥

*kāñcananagare eku bṛkṣa manohara |*
*suradhunī-tīre chāyā śītala sundara ||*

*Word for word:* kanchananagare — in Kanchananagara; eku briksha manohara — a lovely tree; suradhuni-tire — on the bank of the Suradhuni; chhaya shitala sundara — a cool, beautiful shade

**12.1.** In Kanchananagara there is a lovely tree;
on the bank of the Suradhuni — a cool and beautiful shade.

তার তলে বসিলেন গৌরাঙ্গ সুন্দর ।
কাঞ্চনের কান্তি জিনি দীপ্তি কলেবর ॥

*tāra tale basilena gaurāṅga sundara |*
*kāñcanera kānti jini dīpti kalebara ||*

*Word for word:* tara tale — beneath it; basilena gauranga sundara — the beautiful Gauranga sat; kanchanera kanti jini — outshining the lustre of gold; dipti kalebara — [His] body shines

**12.2.** Beneath it the beautiful Gauranga sat down;
His body shines brighter than the lustre of gold.

নগরের লোক ধায় যুবক যুবতী ।
সতী ছাড়ে নিজ পতি জপ ছাড়ে যতি ॥

*nagarera loka dhāya yubaka yubatī |*
*satī chāṛe nija pati japa chāṛe yati ||*

*Word for word:* nagarera loka dhaya — the townspeople run; yubaka yubati — young men and young women; sati chhare nija pati — the wife leaves her own husband; japa chhare yati — the ascetic leaves his japa

**12.3.** The townspeople come running — young men and young women;
the wife leaves her husband, the ascetic leaves his japa.[^04-41]

কেহো বলে এ নাগর যেনা দেশে ছিল ।
সে দেশের পুরুষ নারী কেমনে বাঁচিল ॥

*keho bale e nāgara yenā deśe chila |*
*se deśera puruṣa nārī kemane bām̐cila ||*

*Word for word:* keho bale — someone says; e nagara — this nagara (elegant youth); yena deshe chhila — in what land he lived; se deshera purusha nari — the men and women of that land; kemane bachila — how have they survived

**12.4.** Someone says: "In what land did this young nagara live?
How do the men and women of that land go on living now?"[^04-42]

কেহ বলে নিজ নারীর গলে পদ দিয়া ।
আসিয়াছে জননীর পরাণ বধিয়া ॥

*keha bale nija nārīra gale pada diyā |*
*āsiyāche jananīra parāṇa badhiyā ||*

*Word for word:* keha bale — someone says; nija narira gale pada diya — treading on his own wife's throat; asiyachhe — he has come; jananira parana badhiya — killing his mother's life

**12.5.** Someone says: "He has come, treading on His wife's throat
and killing His mother's life."[^04-43]

হেন কালে কেশব ভারতী মহামতি ।
দেখিয়া তাহারে প্রভু করিলা প্রণতি ॥

*hena kāle keśaba bhāratī mahāmati |*
*dekhiyā tāhāre prabhu karilā praṇati ||*

*Word for word:* hena kale — at that time; keshava bharati mahamati — the magnanimous Keshava Bharati; dekhiya tahare — seeing him; prabhu karila pranati — the Lord bowed down

**12.6.** At that time the magnanimous Keshava Bharati came;
seeing him, the Lord bowed down to him:

কৃষ্ণ-দাস কর গোসাঞি দেহ ভক্তি বর ।
বাসু ঘোষ কহে মুণ্ডে পড়িল বজর ॥

*kṛṣṇa-dāsa kara gosāñi deha bhakti bara |*
*bāsu ghoṣa kahe muṇḍe paṛila bajara ||*

*Word for word:* krishna-dasa kara — make [Me] Krishna's servant; gosanyi — Gosai (master); deha bhakti bara — grant the boon of devotion; basu ghosha kahe — Vasu Ghosha says; munde parila bajara — a thunderbolt has fallen on the head

**12.7.** "Make Me Krishna's servant, Gosai, grant Me the gift of devotion!"
Vasu Ghosha says: a thunderbolt has fallen on the head.[^04-44]

[^04-40]: The signature is "Vasu Ghosha". PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 276 (printed p. 265), 21st pallava, no. 6; MS P-R-Sa no. 2328. In
GPT1 (pp. 368–369, no. 10, raga shri) and GPT2 (sect. 5.3, no. 10) the pada is longer: women stand with pitchers on their
hips, the lame run leaning on sticks; the townspeople praise the mother who bore Him and plead: "Go back home, do not
become a sannyasi, do not shave Your hair"; the Lord answers: "Bless Me, mothers and fathers: I shall give My head to
Krishna's feet"; the signature — "May a thunderbolt fall on the head!". Kanchananagara (Kantaka-nagara) is Katwa; the
events — CB Madhya 28, CC Adi 17, Murari 3.2.
[^04-41]: A hyperbole: the Lord's beauty draws everyone away from their usual occupations; this is wonder at the sight of the
Lord, not worldly attraction.
[^04-42]: Nagara (nāgara) — an elegant young townsman; so the people of Katwa speak of the Lord. MS "gha": "enā gaura" ("this
Gaura"), P-R-Sa: "enā nāgara".
[^04-43]: That is, leaving His young wife and His mother in mortal grief. GPT: "has come having killed mother and father".
[^04-44]: Cf. CB Madhya 28: the Lord asks Keshava Bharati for sannyasa as a mercy, to attain service to Krishna. "A
thunderbolt" — the poet's grief: the sannyasa is settled.

## 13. Vasu Ghosha — "muṛāiyā cām̐cara cule snāna kari gaṅgā-jale…" (PK 2225)
*Lila: the sannyasa at Katwa — having shaved His curly locks and bathed in the Ganga, the Lord asks for red garments;
Keshava Bharati gives two pieces of red cloth and a kaupina; the Lord asks the devotees to bless Him "that the sannyasa may
not become a mockery and that in Vraja I may attain the Lord of Vraja", and runs off, heedless of direction. According to
Majumdar — an episode omitted by the biographers; the "Nimai-sannyasa" cycle is a historical picture with poetic
exaggerations. Raga pahida.*[^04-45]

মুড়াইয়া চাঁচর চুলে স্নান করি গঙ্গা-জলে
বলে দেহ অরুণ বসন ।
গৌরাঙ্গের বচন শুনিয়া ভকতগণ
উচ্চ-স্বরে করয়ে রোদন ॥

*muṛāiyā cām̐cara cule snāna kari gaṅgā-jale*
*bale deha aruṇa basana |*
*gaurāṅgera bacana śuniyā bhakatagaṇa*
*ucca-svare karaye rodana ||*

*Word for word:* muraiya chachara chule — having shaved the curly locks; snana kari ganga-jale — having bathed in the Ganga's water; bale deha aruna basana — He says: "Give red garments"; gaurangera bachana — Gauranga's words; shuniya bhakatagana — hearing, the devotees; uchcha-svare karaye rodana — weep aloud

**13.1.** Having shaved His curly locks and bathed in the water of the Ganga,
He says: "Give Me red garments."
Hearing Gauranga's words, the devotees
weep aloud.

অরুণ দুই খানি কানি ভারতী দিলেন আনি
আর দিল একটি কৌপীন ।
মস্তকে পরশ করি পরিলেন গৌরহরি
আপনাকে মানে অতি দীন ॥

*aruṇa dui khāni kāni bhāratī dilena āni*
*āra dila ekaṭi kaupīna |*
*mastake paraśa kari parilena gaurahari*
*āpanāke māne ati dīna ||*

*Word for word:* aruna dui khani kani — two pieces of red cloth; bharati dilena ani — Bharati brought and gave; ara dila ekati kaupina — and gave one kaupina; mastake parasha kari — touching [them] to the head; parilena gaurahari — Gaurahari put [them] on; apanake mane ati dina — regarding Himself as most lowly

**13.2.** Two pieces of red cloth Bharati brought and gave,
and also gave one kaupina;
touching them to His head, Gaurahari put them on,
regarding Himself as utterly lowly.[^04-46]

তোমরা বান্ধব মোর এই আশীর্ব্বাদ কর
নিজ-কর দিয়া মোর মাথে ।
করিলাম সন্ন্যাস নহে যেন উপহাস
ব্রজে যেন পাই ব্রজ-নাথে ॥

*tomarā bāndhaba mora ei āśīrvvāda kara*
*nija-kara diyā mora māthe |*
*karilāma sannyāsa nahe yena upahāsa*
*braje yena pāi braja-nāthe ||*

*Word for word:* tomara bandhaba mora — you are My friends; ei ashirvada kara — give this blessing; nija-kara diya mora mathe — placing your hands on My head; karilama sannyasa — I have taken sannyasa; nahe yena upahasa — let it not be a mockery; braje yena pai braja-nathe — that in Vraja I may attain the Lord of Vraja

**13.3.** "You are My friends; give Me this blessing,
laying your hands upon My head:
I have taken sannyasa — let it not become a mockery,
let Me attain the Lord of Vraja in Vraja!"[^04-47]

এত কহি গৌররায় ঊর্দ্ধমুখ করি ধায়
দিগ বিদিগ নাহি মানে ।
ভক্ত-জনার পাছে পাছে লোটাঞা লোটাঞা কাছে
বাসু ঘোষ হাকান্দ কান্দনে ॥

*eta kahi gaurarāya ūrddhamukha kari dhāya*
*diga bidiga nāhi māne |*
*bhakta-janāra pāche pāche loṭāñā loṭāñā kāche*
*bāsu ghoṣa hākānda kāndane ||*

*Word for word:* eta kahi gauraraya — saying this, Gaura Raya; urdhvamukha kari dhaya — runs with His face raised; diga bidiga nahi mane — heeding neither the quarters nor the points between; bhakta-janara pachhe pachhe — following the devotees; lotanya lotanya kachhe — rolling and rolling nearby; basu ghosha hakanda kandane — Vasu Ghosha weeps and sobs

**13.4.** Saying this, Gaura Raya runs, His face raised to the sky,
heedless of the quarters and the points between;
following the devotees, rolling and rolling on the ground beside them,
Vasu Ghosha weeps and sobs.[^04-48]

[^04-45]: The signature is "Vasu Ghosha". PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 277 (printed p. 266), 21st pallava, no. 8; MS P-R-Sa no. 2330.
GPT1 — p. 370, no. 14; GPT2 — sect. 5.3, no. 14 (with minor variants); in GPT it is followed (no. 15) by another pada with
the same signature and similar lines ("You are the best of Vaishnavas, give Me this blessing… that going to Vraja I may
attain the Lord of Vraja"). Majumdar quotes the lines "You are My friends, give Me a blessing…" as an example of a detail
that the later biographers omitted for fear of diminishing the Lord's divinity. The preceding pada in PK (no. 2224, on the
shaving of the head) bears the signature of Rasikananda, a later poet, not Vasu Ghosha.
[^04-46]: The kaupina is a sannyasi's loincloth. "Touching them to His head" — respectfully receiving the sannyasi's garments
from the guru. The Lord's humility is an example for sannyasis (cf. CC Adi 17).
[^04-47]: The Lord plays the role of a devotee and asks for a blessing as befits a seeker: for Him sannyasa is a way to the
service of Krishna in Vraja, not renunciation for its own sake. Cf. CC Madhya 3: after the sannyasa the Lord, in ecstasy,
longs for Vrindavana.
[^04-48]: "Heedless of direction" — in ecstasy the Lord runs, thinking He is going to Vrindavana (CC Madhya 3; CB Antya 1).

## 14. Vasu Ghosha — "āre mora gaurāṅga nāyara…" (PK 2226)
*Lila: after the sannyasa — the Lord, His waterpot tied at His waist, runs wherever His eyes lead and does not turn at
Nitai's call; Nitai pleads: "All the sinners You have saved will count for something if You save me." Raga bhatiyari (PK),
suhai (GPT).*[^04-49]

আরে মোর গৌরাঙ্গ নায়র ।
প্রেম-জলে তিতিল সোণার কলেবর ॥

*āre mora gaurāṅga nāyara |*
*prema-jale titila soṇāra kalebara ||*

*Word for word:* are mora gauranga nayara — ah, my Gauranga, beloved hero; prema-jale titila — drenched with the tears of prema; sonara kalebara — the golden body

**14.1.** *(Refrain)* Ah, my Gauranga, my beloved hero!
His golden body is drenched with the tears of prema.[^04-50]

কটিতে করঙ্গ বান্ধি দিগ-পথে ধায় ।
প্রেমের ভাইয়া নিতাই ডাকে ফিরিয়া না চায় ॥

*kaṭite karaṅga bāndhi diga-pathe dhāya |*
*premera bhāiyā nitāi ḍāke phiriyā nā cāya ||*

*Word for word:* katite karanga bandhi — tying the waterpot at the waist; diga-pathe dhaya — runs along the roads in every direction; premera bhaiya nitai — Nitai, the brother in prema; dake — calls; phiriya na chaya — [He] does not turn round

**14.2.** His waterpot tied at His waist, He runs along the roads in every direction;
Nitai, His brother in prema, calls Him — He does not turn round.

নিতাই বলে যত যত পাতকী তরাইলে ।
সে সব সফল হবে আমা উদ্ধারিলে ॥

*nitāi bale yata yata pātakī tarāile |*
*se saba saphala habe āmā uddhārile ||*

*Word for word:* nitai bale — Nitai says; yata yata pataki taraile — however many sinners You have saved; se saba saphala habe — all that will bear fruit; ama uddharile — if You save me

**14.3.** Nitai says: "However many sinners You have saved —
all that will bear fruit if You save me.[^04-51]

যত যত অবতার অবনীর মাঝে ।
পতিত-পাবন নাম তোমারে সে সাজে ॥

*yata yata abatāra abanīra mājhe |*
*patita-pābana nāma tomāre se sāje ||*

*Word for word:* yata yata avatara — however many incarnations; abanira majhe — upon the earth; patita-pabana nama — the name Purifier of the Fallen; tomare se saje — befits You alone

**14.4.** Of all the incarnations that have been on earth,
to You alone the name Purifier of the Fallen is fitting."

বাসুদেব ঘোষে কহে মুঞি অভাগিয়া ।
মোরে না ছাড়িহ দয়া পতিত দেখিয়া ॥

*bāsudeba ghoṣe kahe muñi abhāgiyā |*
*more nā chāṛiha dayā patita dekhiyā ||*

*Word for word:* vasudeva ghoshe kahe — Vasudeva Ghosha says; munyi abhagiya — I am ill-starred; more na chhariha daya — do not withhold mercy from me; patita dekhiya — seeing [me] fallen

**14.5.** Vasudeva Ghosha says: I am ill-starred —
seeing me fallen, do not withhold Your mercy from me.[^04-52]

[^04-49]: PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 277 (printed p. 266), 21st pallava, no. 9; MS P-R-Sa no. 2331, P-R 14.1. The last couplet (with
Vasudeva Ghosha's signature) is only in MS P-R-Sa; in the other MSS of PK the pada is unsigned. In GPT1 (p. 371, no. 17,
raga suhai) and GPT2 (sect. 5.3, no. 17) there are four couplets; there the signature is woven into the plea: "Vasu says:
Lord, however many sinners You have saved — it will be more if You save me." In the stage-1 catalogue this pada is entered
twice: VG-061 (after GPT) and VG-137 (PK 2226, with a wrong first line taken from PK 2224).
[^04-50]: Nayara (nāyara, from nāgara) — beloved, hero; GPT: "sundara" ("beautiful"), with the variant "nāyara".
[^04-51]: Nityananda speaks out of humility, as a devotee. According to CC (Madhya 3) and CB (Antya 1), after the sannyasa the
Lord wandered for three days in ecstasy through Radha-desha, and Nityananda followed Him and brought Him to Shantipura.
[^04-52]: "Ill-starred" (abhāgiyā) is the usual formula of humility in a signature.

## 15. Vasu Ghosha — "ki lāgiyā daṇḍa dhare aruṇa basana pare…" (PK 2229)
*Lila: Navadvipa after the sannyasa — the devotees are bewildered and grieve: why has the Lord taken the staff and red
garments, shaved His head and, weeping "Radha, Radha", left His homeland; Srivasa sobs, Gadadhara can scarcely live,
tears stream from Mukunda's eyes. According to Majumdar — a pada of the sannyasa cycle. Raga bhatiyari.*[^04-53]

কি লাগিয়া দণ্ড ধরে অরুণ বসন পরে
কি লাগিয়া মুড়াইল কেশ ।
কি লাগিয়া মুখ-চাঁদে রাধা রাধা বলি কান্দে
কি লাগি ছাড়িল নিজ দেশ ॥

*ki lāgiyā daṇḍa dhare aruṇa basana pare*
*ki lāgiyā muṛāila keśa |*
*ki lāgiyā mukha-cām̐de rādhā rādhā bali kānde*
*ki lāgi chāṛila nija deśa ||*

*Word for word:* ki lagiya — why; danda dhare — holds a staff; aruna basana pare — wears red garments; muraila kesha — shaved His hair; mukha-chande — with His moon-face; radha radha boli kande — weeps, crying "Radha, Radha"; ki lagi chharila nija desha — why did He leave His native land

**15.1.** Why does He hold a staff, why has He put on red garments,
why has He shaved His hair?
Why, weeping "Radha, Radha!" with His moon-face,
why has He left His native land?[^04-54]

শ্রীবাসের উচ্চরায় পাষাণ মিলাঞা যায়
গদাধর না জিয়ে পরাণে ।
বহিছে তপত ধারা যেন মন্দাকিনী পারা
মুকুন্দের ও দুই নয়ানে ॥

*śrībāsera uccarāya pāṣāṇa milāñā yāya*
*gadādhara nā jiye parāṇe |*
*bahiche tapata dhārā yena mandākinī pārā*
*mukundera o dui nayāne ||*

*Word for word:* shribasera uchcharaya — at Srivasa's loud cries; pashana milanya yaya — stones melt; gadadhara na jiye parane — Gadadhara cannot live; bahichhe tapata dhara — hot streams flow; yena mandakini para — like the Mandakini; mukundera o dui nayane — from both of Mukunda's eyes

**15.2.** At Srivasa's loud weeping stones melt;
Gadadhara has no strength to live;
hot streams flow, like the Mandakini,
from both of Mukunda's eyes.[^04-55]

সকল মহান্ত ঘরে বিধাতা বুঝাই ফিরে
তমু স্থির নাহি হয় কেহ ।
জ্বলন্ত অনল হেন রমণী ছাড়িল কেন
কি লাগি তেজিল তার লেহ ॥

*sakala mahānta ghare bidhātā bujhāi phire*
*tamu sthira nāhi haya keha |*
*jvalanta anala hena ramaṇī chāṛila kena*
*ki lāgi tejila tāra leha ||*

*Word for word:* sakala mahanta ghare — at the houses of all the great souls; bidhata bujhai phire — they go round consoling: "[it was] the Creator['s will]"; tamu sthira nahi haya keha — yet no one is calmed; jvalanta anala hena ramani — a wife like a blazing flame; chharila kena — why did He leave; ki lagi tejila tara leha — why did He reject her love

**15.3.** They go round the houses of all the great souls, consoling: "So the Creator ordained," —
but no one can be calm:
"A wife like a blazing flame — why did He leave her?
Why did He reject her love?"[^04-56]

কি কব দুখের কথা কহিতে মরমে ব্যথা
না দেখি বিদরে মোর হিয়া ।
দিবানিশি নাহি জানি বিরহে আকুল প্রাণী
বাসু ঘোষ পড়ে মুরছিয়া ॥

*ki kaba dukhera kathā kahite marame byathā*
*nā dekhi bidare mora hiyā |*
*dibāniśi nāhi jāni birahe ākula prāṇī*
*bāsu ghoṣa paṛe murachiyā ||*

*Word for word:* ki kaba dukhera katha — what can I say of the grief; kahite marame byatha — speaking brings pain to the depths of the heart; na dekhi — not seeing [Him]; bidare mora hiya — my heart is torn; dibanishi nahi jani — knowing neither day nor night; birahe akula prani — the soul distraught in separation; basu ghosha pare murachhiya — Vasu Ghosha falls senseless

**15.4.** What can I say of the grief? To speak is pain in the depths of the heart;
not seeing Him, my heart is torn apart.
Knowing neither day nor night, in the anguish of separation
Vasu Ghosha falls senseless.

[^04-53]: The signature is "Vasu Ghosha". PK: vol. 3, PDF pp. 278–279 (printed pp. 267–268), 21st pallava, no. 12; MS P-R-Sa
no. 2334. GPT1 — p. 374, no. 26; GPT2 — sect. 5.3, no. 26 (almost without variants).
[^04-54]: After the sannyasa the Lord is in Radha's mood: for Him sannyasa is a way of service to Krishna (cf. note 47).
[^04-55]: The Mandakini is the heavenly Ganga. Srivasa, Gadadhara and Mukunda are the Lord's closest companions in Navadvipa.
[^04-56]: "Consoling: 'So the Creator ordained'" — our understanding of the line "sakala mahānta ghare bidhātā bujhāi phire"
(MSS "ka", "gha", "ca": "bujhāiyā", "kha": "bujhāite"). "Like a blazing flame" — radiant with beauty and purity (of
Vishnupriya); one may also understand "He left His wife — [now] burning like the fire [of separation]".

## 16. Vasu Ghosha — "hari hari ki nā haila nadīyā nagare…" (PK 2228)
*Lila: the lament of the women of Nadia after the sannyasa (nagari-bhava): Keshava Bharati has struck their hearts as with
a thunderbolt; the sannyasis have robbed them of their treasure; how will Vishnupriya survive now; Nadia, which was joy,
has become like Gokula after Krishna's departure. According to Majumdar — a pada of nagari-bhava. Raga pahida.*[^04-57]

হরি হরি কি না হৈল নদীয়া নগরে ।
কেশব ভারতী আসি বজর পাড়িল গো
রসবতীর পরাণের ঘরে ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*hari hari ki nā haila nadīyā nagare |*
*keśaba bhāratī āsi bajara pāṛila go*
*rasabatīra parāṇera ghare || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* hari hari — Hari, Hari; ki na haila — what has not befallen; nadiya nagare — the town of Nadia; keshava bharati asi — Keshava Bharati, coming; bajara parila go — brought down a thunderbolt; rasabatira paranera ghare — upon the house of the souls of those full of rasa

**16.1.** *(Refrain)* Hari, Hari! What has not befallen the town of Nadia!
Keshava Bharati came and hurled a thunderbolt
upon the house of the souls of those full of rasa.[^04-58]

গিরি পুরী ভারতী আসিয়া করিল যতি
আঁচলের রতন কাড়ি নিল ।
প্রিয় সহচরী সঙ্গে যে সাধ করিলুঁ রঙ্গে
সে সব স্বপন সম ভেল ॥

*giri purī bhāratī āsiyā karila yati*
*ām̐calera ratana kāṛi nila |*
*priya sahacarī saṅge ye sādha karilum̐ raṅge*
*se saba svapana sama bhela ||*

*Word for word:* giri puri bharati — Giri, Puri, Bharati (orders of sannyasis); asiya karila yati — came and made [Him] an ascetic; anchalera ratana — the jewel from the end of the cloth; kari nila — they snatched away; priya sahachari sange — with dear companions; ye sadha karilu range — what we longed for in joy; se saba svapana sama bhela — all that has become like a dream

**16.2.** Giri, Puri, Bharati came and made Him an ascetic —
they snatched the jewel from the end of our cloth.
All that we and our dear companions longed for in joy —
all of it has become like a dream.[^04-59]

কিশোর বয়েস বেশ মাথায় চাঁচর কেশ
মুখে হাসি আছে মিশাইয়া ।
আমরা পরের নারী পরাণ ধরিতে নারি
কেমনে বাঁচিবে বিষ্ণুপ্রিয়া ॥

*kiśora bayesa beśa māthāya cām̐cara keśa*
*mukhe hāsi āche miśāiyā |*
*āmarā parera nārī parāṇa dharite nāri*
*kemane bām̐cibe biṣṇupriyā ||*

*Word for word:* kishora bayesa besha — the youthful age, the attire; mathaya chachara kesha — curly locks on the head; mukhe hasi achhe mishaiya — a smile blended with the face; amara parera nari — we are others' wives; parana dharite nari — we cannot keep life in us; kemane bachibe vishnupriya — how will Vishnupriya survive

**16.3.** The youthful age, the attire, the curly locks on His head,
the smile lighting up His face…
We are others' wives, and even we cannot keep life in us —
how then will Vishnupriya survive?[^04-60]

সুরধুনী-তীরে তরু কদম্বখণ্ডিতে চারু
প্রাণ কান্দে কেতকী দেখিয়া ।
নদীয়া আনন্দ ছিল গোকুলের পারা হৈল
বাসু ঘোষ মরয়ে কান্দিয়া ॥

*suradhunī-tīre taru kadambakhaṇḍite cāru*
*prāṇa kānde ketakī dekhiyā |*
*nadīyā ānanda chila gokulera pārā haila*
*bāsu ghoṣa maraye kāndiyā ||*

*Word for word:* suradhuni-tire taru — the trees on the bank of the Suradhuni; kadambakhandite charu — lovely in the kadamba groves; prana kande — the heart weeps; ketaki dekhiya — seeing the ketaki; nadiya ananda chhila — Nadia was joy; gokulera para haila — has become like Gokula; basu ghosha maraye kandiya — Vasu Ghosha dies weeping

**16.4.** The trees on the bank of the Suradhuni, lovely in the kadamba groves —
the heart weeps seeing the ketaki.
Nadia was joy — and has become like Gokula;
Vasu Ghosha is dying, weeping.[^04-61]

[^04-57]: The signature is "Vasu Ghosha". PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 278 (printed p. 267), 21st pallava, no. 11; MS P-R-Sa no. 2333,
P-R 40.105. GPT1 — p. 373, no. 24; GPT2 — sect. 5.3, no. 24. Majumdar counts PK 2228 among Vasu Ghosha's padas of
nagari-bhava. The pada is put into the mouths of the women of Nadia; we translate faithfully to the author. Vrindavana Dasa
stresses that in this incarnation the Lord never looked at another man's wife; worship of Gaura in the spirit of
"Gaura-nagari" is not accepted by the Gaudiya tradition (Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja, Bhaktisiddhanta).
[^04-58]: "Those full of rasa" (rasabatī) — the women of Nadia, whose hearts are given to Gaura. MS P-R-Sa and GPT read
"kuliśa" for "bajara" (thunderbolt; same sense).
[^04-59]: Giri, Puri, Bharati are names of orders of sannyasis; Keshava Bharati belonged to the Bharati order. "The jewel from
the end of the cloth" — what one keeps tied in the end of one's sari.
[^04-60]: "Others' wives" — married women for whom Gaura is not a husband; the words convey the force of their grief. MSS
P-R-Sa, P-R and GPT: "how will Vishnupriya pass [her life]" (bañcibe).
[^04-61]: Gokula after Krishna's departure for Mathura is an image of inconsolable separation. Kadamba and ketaki blossom in the
rainy season and recall Krishna. The second half of the first line is read variously: PK "kadambakhaṇḍite cāru", MSS "ka",
"kha", "ca" "…baru", P-R-Sa "kadamba khaṇḍita uru", GPT "kadambakhaṇḍete uru".

## 17. Madhava Ghosha — "nāce pahu kaladhauta-gorā…" (PK 2289)
*Lila: the dance of the Lord as a sannyasi — golden Gora in a kaupina and a red outer cloth, a garland at His throat, in
tears of prema and bristling with rapture, trembling like a plantain tree at dawn. The place is not named; in PK the pada
stands in the pallava on the sannyasa. According to Majumdar — one of Madhava Ghosha's four padas on the Lord's sannyasa.
Raga mayura.*[^04-62]

নাচে পহু কলধৌত-গোরা ।
অবিরত পূর্ণ-কল মুখ-বিধু মণ্ডল
নিরবধি প্রেম-রসে ভোরা ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*nāce pahu kaladhauta-gorā |*
*abirata pūrṇa-kala mukha-bidhu maṇḍala*
*nirabadhi prema-rase bhorā || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* nache pahu — the Lord dances; kaladhauta-gora — golden Gora; abirata — ceaselessly; purna-kala — full [moon]; mukha-bidhu mandala — the orb of the moon-face; nirabadhi — ever; prema-rase bhora — intoxicated with the rasa of prema

**17.1.** *(Refrain)* The Lord dances — golden Gora;
ceaselessly, like the full moon, shines the orb of His face;
ever is He intoxicated with the rasa of prema.

অরুণ-কমল-পাখী জিনি রাঙ্গা দুটি আঁখি
ভ্রমরযুগল দুটি তারা ।
সোণার ভূধরে যৈছে সুর-নদী বহে ঐছে
বুক বাহি পড়ে প্রেম-ধারা ॥

*aruṇa-kamala-pākhī jini rāṅgā duṭi ām̐khi*
*bhramarayugala duṭi tārā |*
*soṇāra bhūdhare yaiche sura-nadī bahe aiche*
*buka bāhi paṛe prema-dhārā ||*

*Word for word:* aruna-kamala-pakhi jini — outshining the petals of a red lotus; ranga duti ankhi — the two red eyes; bhramarayugala duti tara — the two pupils a pair of bumblebees; sonara bhudhare yaichhe — as on a golden mountain; sura-nadi bahe aichhe — a heavenly river flows, so; buka bahi pare prema-dhara — streams of prema flow down the breast

**17.2.** His two red eyes outshine the petals of a red lotus,
the two pupils are a pair of bumblebees;
as a heavenly river runs down a golden mountain,
so streams of prema flow down His breast.

কেশরীর কটি জিনি তাহাতে কৌপীন খিণি
অরুণ বরণ বহির্ব্বাস ।
গলায় দোনার মালা ভূষণ করিল আলা
নাসা তিল-কুসুম বিকাশ ॥

*keśarīra kaṭi jini tāhāte kaupīna khiṇi*
*aruṇa baraṇa bahirvvāsa |*
*galāya donāra mālā bhūṣaṇa karila ālā*
*nāsā tila-kusuma bikāśa ||*

*Word for word:* kesharira kati jini — outshining a lion's waist; tahate kaupina khini — on it a slender kaupina; aruna barana bahirvasa — a red outer cloth; galaya donara mala — at the throat a garland (?); bhushana karila ala — the ornaments glow; nasa tila-kusuma bikasha — the nose an opening sesame flower

**17.3.** His waist is slenderer than a lion's, on it a slender kaupina,
the outer cloth is red in colour;
at the throat a garland, the ornaments glow with light,
the nose is like an opening sesame flower.[^04-63]

কনক-মৃণাল-যুগ সুবলিত দুটি ভুজ
কর-যুগ কঞ্জের বিলাস ।
রাতা-উতপল-ফুল পদ নহে সমতুল
পরশনে মহীর উল্লাস ॥

*kanaka-mṛṇāla-yuga subalita duṭi bhuja*
*kara-yuga kañjera bilāsa |*
*rātā-utapala-phula pada nahe samatula*
*paraśane mahīra ullāsa ||*

*Word for word:* kanaka-mrinala-yuga — a pair of golden lotus stalks; subalita duti bhuja — the two shapely arms; kara-yuga kanjera bilasa — the two hands, the play of lotuses; rata-utapala-phula — the red lotus; pada nahe samatula — is no match for the feet; parashane mahira ullasa — at their touch the earth rejoices

**17.4.** The two arms are like a pair of golden lotus stalks,
the two hands — the play of lotuses;
the red lotus cannot compare with His feet —
at their touch the earth rejoices.

আপাদ মস্তক গায় পুলকে পূরিত তায়
যৈছে নীপ-ফুল অতি শোভা ।
প্রভাতে কদলী জনু সঘনে কম্পিত তনু
মাধব ঘোষের মনলোভা ॥

*āpāda mastaka gāya pulake pūrita tāya*
*yaiche nīpa-phula ati śobhā |*
*prabhāte kadalī janu saghane kampita tanu*
*mādhaba ghoṣera manalobhā ||*

*Word for word:* apada mastaka gaya — the body from feet to head; pulake purita taya — is filled with bristling rapture; yaichhe nipa-phula ati shobha — like a kadamba flower in full beauty; prabhate kadali janu — like a plantain at dawn; saghane kampita tanu — the body trembles again and again; madhava ghoshera manalobha — captivating the heart of Madhava Ghosha

**17.5.** From feet to head His body bristles with rapture,
like a kadamba flower in full beauty;
like a plantain at dawn His body trembles again and again, —
captivating the heart of Madhava Ghosha.[^04-64]

[^04-62]: The signature is "Madhava Ghosha". PK: vol. 3, PDF pp. 299–300 (printed pp. 288–289), 21st pallava, no. 72, under the
heading "Another manner"; MS P-R-Sa no. 2393. In GPT1 — p. 153, no. 123 (raga mayura), with the reading "nāce pahu abadhūta
gorā" ("the Lord dances — Gora the avadhuta"); in GPT2 — twice: sect. 3.1, no. 123 (likewise) and sect. 4.2, no. 38
("kaladhauta"). MSS "ka", "kha", "ca" of PK also read "abadhauta" — "avadhuta" (a wanderer above all rules). Majumdar counts
PK 2289 among Madhava Ghosha's four padas on the Lord's sannyasa. In the stage-1 catalogue this pada is entered three times
(MG-001, MG-002, MG-007).
[^04-63]: "Donā" (donāra mālā) — the meaning is unclear (perhaps a garland of dona leaves or flowers); MS P-R-Sa: "at the
throat a garland sways" (dolaye). The sesame flower is a traditional comparison for a beautiful nose.
[^04-64]: Bristling hair (pulaka) and trembling are sattvika-bhavas, signs of prema; the kadamba flower with its protruding
filaments is an image of a body bristling with rapture. The editor of PK suggests the reading "prabāte" — "in the wind"
instead of "prabhāte" — "at dawn".

## 18. Vasu Ghosha — "eta dine sadaya haila more bidhi…" (PK 1994)
*Lila: the Lord's return to the neighbourhood of Navadvipa (1514/15) — the words of a devotee who sees Gora again after a
long separation. In PK — a gaura-chandrika to "samriddhiman-sambhoga" (the fullness of the joy of Radha and Krishna's
meeting after a long separation), marked "words of the devotees". According to Majumdar — an eyewitness's pada on the
Lord's return to Navadvipa. Raga suhai.*[^04-65]

এত দিনে সদয় হইল মোরে বিধি ।
আনি মিলায়ল মোরে গোরা গুণ-নিধি ॥

*eta dine sadaya haila more bidhi |*
*āni milāyala more gorā guṇa-nidhi ||*

*Word for word:* eta dine — at last (after so many days); sadaya haila more bidhi — the Creator has had mercy on me; ani milayala more — has brought and united me with; gora guna-nidhi — Gora, the treasury of virtues

**18.1.** At last the Creator has had mercy on me:
he has brought and given me Gora, the treasury of virtues.

এত দিনে মিটল দারুণ দুখ ।
নয়ন সফল ভেল দেখি চাঁদ-মুখ ॥

*eta dine miṭala dāruṇa dukha |*
*nayana saphala bhela dekhi cām̐da-mukha ||*

*Word for word:* eta dine — at last; mitala daruna dukha — the cruel grief is over; nayana saphala bhela — the eyes have found their purpose; dekhi chanda-mukha — seeing the moon-face

**18.2.** At last the cruel grief is over:
my eyes have found their purpose, seeing the moon-face.

চির-উপবাসী ছিল লোচন মোর ।
চাঁদ পাওল যেন তৃষিত চকোর ॥

*cira-upabāsī chila locana mora |*
*cām̐da pāola yena tṛṣita cakora ||*

*Word for word:* chira-upabasi chhila — long had been fasting; lochana mora — my eyes; chanda paola — has found the moon; yena trishita chakora — as a thirsty chakora

**18.3.** Long have my eyes been fasting —
as if a thirsty chakora had found the moon.[^04-66]

বাসুদেব ঘোষে গায় গোরা-পরবন্ধ ।
লোচন পাওল যেন জনমের অন্ধ ॥

*bāsudeba ghoṣe gāya gorā-parabandha |*
*locana pāola yena janamera andha ||*

*Word for word:* vasudeva ghoshe gaya — Vasudeva Ghosha sings; gora-parabandha — the song (composition) about Gora; lochana paola — has gained eyes; yena janamera andha — as one blind from birth

**18.4.** Vasudeva Ghosha sings the song of Gora:
as if one blind from birth had gained his eyes.

[^04-65]: The signature is "Vasudeva Ghosha". PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 191 (printed p. 180), the first pada of the 13th pallava of
the 4th shakha ("The outpouring of rasa of samriddhiman-sambhoga. Here — Sri Gaurachandra: words of the devotees"); MS P-R
26.1 (raga bibhasa in it). GPT1 — p. 413, no. 33 (raga suhai); GPT2 — sect. 5.5, no. 33. On the same page of GPT1 (no. 31)
stands Vasu Ghosha's pada "The people of Nadia came to see Gauranga" (chapter 1, no. 23), which Majumdar quotes from GPT,
p. 413; it is also in PK — no. 1991 (vol. 3, PDF p. 190, reading "dhāola" — "came running") — a correction to chapter 1.
Majumdar counts PK 1991, 1994 and 2273 among Vasu Ghosha's padas on the Lord's return to Navadvipa: on His way to Gauda
(1514/15) the Lord stopped at Kuliya opposite Navadvipa, and crowds flocked to Him (CC Madhya 1, 16; CB Antya 3).
[^04-66]: The chakora is a bird which, according to poetic tradition, feeds on moonlight. MS P-R: "my eyes fasted greatly".

## 19. Vasu Ghosha — "sannyāsī haiyā gelā puna yadi bāhuṛilā…" (PK 2273)
*Lila: having taken sannyasa, the Lord returned to Gauda (1514/15) but did not come to the town of Nadia; Vishnupriya's
grief: "Akrura was better — he took Krishna only to Mathura, whence news comes, but Bharati has made You a stranger in
foreign lands." According to Majumdar — a pada on the Lord's return to Navadvipa. Raga pahida.*[^04-67]

সন্ন্যাসী হইয়া গেলা পুন যদি বাহুড়িলা
নাহি আইলা নদীয়া নগরে ।
হৃদয়ে হৃদয়ে ধরি নিজ পর এক করি
চাঁদ-মুখ দেখিবার তরে ॥

*sannyāsī haiyā gelā puna yadi bāhuṛilā*
*nāhi āilā nadīyā nagare |*
*hṛdaye hṛdaye dhari nija para eka kari*
*cām̐da-mukha dekhibāra tare ||*

*Word for word:* sannyasi haiya gela — having become a sannyasi, He went; puna yadi bahurila — even when He returned; nahi aila nadiya nagare — He did not come to the town of Nadia; hridaye hridaye dhari — pressing heart to heart; nija para eka kari — making one's own and others one; chanda-mukha dekhibara tare — for the seeing of the moon-face

**19.1.** "Having become a sannyasi, He went away; and even when He returned,
He did not come to the town of Nadia,
to press heart to heart, making no difference between one's own and others,
and to let us see His moon-face.[^04-68]

হরি হরি গৌরাঙ্গ এমন কেনে হৈলা ।
সভারে সদয় হৈয়া মুঞি নারীরে বঞ্চিয়া
এ শোক-সাগরে ভাসাইলা ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*hari hari gaurāṅga emana kene hailā |*
*sabhāre sadaya haiyā muñi nārīre bañciyā*
*e śoka-sāgare bhāsāilā || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* hari hari — Hari, Hari; gauranga emana kene haila — Gauranga, why have You become like this; sabhare sadaya haiya — being merciful to all; munyi narire banchiya — depriving me, a woman; e shoka-sagare bhasaila — You have cast [me] adrift on this ocean of grief

**19.2.** *(Refrain)* Hari, Hari! Gauranga, why have You become like this?
To all You are merciful — only me, a woman, You have deprived
and cast into this ocean of grief.

এ নব যৌবন-কালে মুড়াইয়া চাঁচর চুলে
না জানি সাধিলা কোন সিধি ।
কি ছার পুরাণ সে পশুবৎ পণ্ডিত যে
গৌরাঙ্গ-সন্ন্যাসে দিল বিধি ॥

*e naba yaubana-kāle muṛāiyā cām̐cara cule*
*nā jāni sādhilā kona sidhi |*
*ki chāra purāṇa se paśubat paṇḍita ye*
*gaurāṅga-sannyāse dila bidhi ||*

*Word for word:* e naba yaubana-kale — in this early youth; muraiya chachara chule — having shaved the curly locks; na jani — I do not know; sadhila kona sidhi — what perfection You sought; ki chhara purana se — what worthless purana; pashubat pandita ye — what beast-like pandita; gauranga-sannyase dila bidhi — enjoined sannyasa on Gauranga

**19.3.** In this early youth, having shaved Your curly locks —
I do not know what perfection You were seeking.
What worthless purana, what beast-like pandita
enjoined sannyasa on Gauranga?[^04-69]

অক্রুর আছিল ভাল রাজ-বলে লৈয়া গেল
রাখিল সে মথুরা-নগরী ।
নিতি লোক আইসে যায় তাহাতে সম্বাদ পায়
ভারতী করিল দেশান্তরী ॥

*akrura āchila bhāla rāja-bale laiyā gela*
*rākhila se mathurā-nagarī |*
*niti loka āise yāya tāhāte sambāda pāya*
*bhāratī karila deśāntarī ||*

*Word for word:* akrura achhila bhala — Akrura was better; raja-bale laiya gela — took [Him] away at the king's word; rakhila se mathura-nagari — kept [Him] in the city of Mathura; niti loka aise yaya — every day people come and go; tahate sambada paya — from them one gets news; bharati karila deshantari — Bharati has made [You] a stranger in far lands

**19.4.** Akrura was better: at the king's word he took [Krishna] away
and kept Him in the city of Mathura;
every day people come and go — from them one gets news;
but Bharati has made You a stranger in foreign lands."[^04-70]

এত বলি বিষ্ণুপ্রিয়া মরমে বেদনা পাইয়া
ধরণীরে মাগয়ে বিদার ।
বাসুদেব ঘোষে কয় মো সম পামর নয়
তমু হিয়া বিদরে আমার ॥

*eta bali biṣṇupriyā marame bedanā pāiyā*
*dharaṇīre māgaye bidāra |*
*bāsudeba ghoṣe kaya mo sama pāmara naya*
*tamu hiyā bidare āmāra ||*

*Word for word:* eta boli vishnupriya — saying this, Vishnupriya; marame bedana paiya — pained to the depths of her heart; dharanire magaye bidara — begs the earth to split open; vasudeva ghoshe kaya — Vasudeva Ghosha says; mo sama pamara naya — there is no wretch like me; tamu hiya bidare amara — and yet my heart is breaking

**19.5.** Saying this, Vishnupriya, pained to the depths of her heart,
begs the earth to open.
Vasudeva Ghosha says: there is no wretch like me —
and yet my heart is breaking.[^04-71]

[^04-67]: The signature is "Vasudeva Ghosha". PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 294 (printed p. 283), 21st pallava, no. 56; MS P-R-Sa no. 2377.
The same pada is printed in PK once more — no. 1801 (vol. 3, PDF p. 111), in the section on separation, before "The twelve
months of Sri Radhika's separation". GPT1 — p. 389, no. 23 (raga pahida); GPT2 — no. 23. Majumdar counts PK 2273 among the
padas on the Lord's return to Navadvipa; cf. CC Madhya 16 (the Lord at Kuliya) and chapter 1, nos. 22–23.
[^04-68]: The stanza also allows another understanding: "…[we] waited, pressing heart to heart, making no difference between
one's own and others, to see the moon-face." MSS "gha", "ca", PK 1801 and GPT: "tāra mukha" — "His face".
[^04-69]: These are Vishnupriya's words of grief, not the poet's judgement on the shastras: the sannyasa was the will of the Lord
Himself, accepted for the deliverance of living beings (CC Adi 17; CB Madhya 26). We read "ki chāra purāṇa se, paśubat
paṇḍita ye" after PK 1801 and MSS "ka", "kha", "ca", P-R-Sa; the main text of PK 2273 has "ki chāra parāṇa ye, paśubata
paṇḍita se" ("what worthless life…"), GPT "ki jāni parāṇa ye" ("I know not what life…").
[^04-70]: Akrura, at the order of King Kamsa, took Krishna and Balarama from Vraja to Mathura (Bhag. 10.39). "A stranger in
foreign lands" (deśāntarī) — one who has gone to distant parts.
[^04-71]: "Begs the earth to open" (dharaṇīre māgaye bidāra) — like Sita; MS P-R-Sa: "bidāya" ("begs the earth for leave to
depart"). The signature is a formula of humility.
