# Chapter 5. Praise of Gaura, the Pastimes of Navadvipa, Separation, and Nityananda in Gauda

*Padas of contemporaries which Majumdar (*Sri-Chaitanya-chariter upadan*, ch. 2) assigns to the Lord's own time, in the
order of the lilas: praise of Gaura (Paramananda); a kirtana festival in Advaita's house (Parameshvara Dasa); the Lord's
pastimes with Gadadhara and His companions in Navadvipa, which Narahari Chakravarti cites in the *Bhakti-ratnakara* as the
testimony of the eyewitness Vasu Ghosha (the battle of flowers, the game of dice, the water play, the rasa, the spring
festival of colours); the Lord's ecstatic moods (Shivananda, Chaitanyadasa); the separation of Navadvipa after the
sannyasa (Paramananda, Vasu Ghosha, Chaitanyadasa, Madhava Ghosha); and Nityananda in Gauda (Kanu Thakura). The text
follows the *Padakalpataru* (PK), the *Bhakti-ratnakara* (BR), the *Kshanada-gita-chintamani* (KGC) and the
*Gaura-pada-tarangini* (GPT1 — 1st ed., 1903; GPT2 — 2nd ed., 1934); the Bengali original, variants and word-for-word
translation are in the full version of the book.*

## 1. Paramananda (Gupta) — "gorā-abatāre yāra nā haila bhakati-sāra…" (PK 2202)
*Lila: praise of Gaura — a call to worship the feet of Gorachand, the Purifier of the fallen. In PK the pada stands in the
20th pallava among padas on Gaura's mercy; in GPT, among the mangalacharanas (songs of blessing that open a kirtana).
According to Majumdar it is one of the padas signed "Paramananda" which he ascribes to Paramananda Gupta, the Lord's
companion in Navadvipa — perhaps a fragment of his lost *Gauranga-vijaya*. Raga kamoda.*[^05-1]

গোরা-অবতারে যার না হৈল ভকতি-সার
আর তার না দেখি উপায় ।
রবির কিরণে যার আঁখি পরসন্ন নৈল
বিধাতা বঞ্চিত ভেল তায় ॥

*gorā-abatāre yāra nā haila bhakati-sāra*
*āra tāra nā dekhi upāya |*
*rabira kiraṇe yāra ām̐khi parasanna naila*
*bidhātā bañcita bhela tāya ||*

*Word for word:* gora-abatare — in the descent of Gora; yara na haila — in whom there arose no; bhakati-sara — essence of devotion (var. bhakati-rasa — taste of devotion); ara tara na dekhi upaya — I see no other means for him; rabira kirane — in the rays of the sun; yara ankhi parasanna naila — whose eyes did not brighten; bidhata — the Creator; banchita bhela taya — has deprived him

**1.1.** One in whom the essence of devotion did not awaken in the descent of Gora —
for him I see no other means:
one whose eyes did not brighten in the rays of the sun
has been deprived by the Creator.[^05-2]

ভজ গোরাচাঁদের চরণ ।
এ তিন ভুবনে ভাই দয়ার ঠাকুর নাই
গোরা বড় পতিত-পাবন ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*bhaja gorācām̐dera caraṇa |*
*e tina bhubane bhāi dayāra ṭhākura nāi*
*gorā baṛa patita-pābana || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* bhaja — worship; gorachandera charana — the feet of Gorachand; e tina bhubane — in these three worlds; bhai — brother; dayara thakura nai — there is no [such] Lord of mercy; gora bara patita-pabana — Gora is the great purifier of the fallen; (dhru) — refrain

**1.2.** *(Refrain)* Worship the feet of Gorachand!
In the three worlds, brothers, there is no such Lord of mercy:
Gora is the great Purifier of the fallen.

হেম-জলদ কিয়ে প্রেম-সরোবর
করুণা-সিন্ধু অবতার ।
হেন অবতার পাইয়া যে জন শীতল নহে
কি জানি কেমন মন তার ॥

*hema-jalada kiye prema-sarobara*
*karuṇā-sindhu abatāra |*
*hena abatāra pāiyā ye jana śītala nahe*
*ki jāni kemana mana tāra ||*

*Word for word:* hema-jalada — a golden rain-cloud; kiye — or; prema-sarobara — a lake of prema; karuna-sindhu avatara — the descent, an ocean of mercy; hena avatara paiya — having found such a descent; ye jana shitala nahe — whoever is not cooled; ki jani kemana mana tara — I do not know what kind of heart he has

**1.3.** Is He a golden cloud, or a lake of prema —
the descent, an ocean of mercy!
Whoever, having found such a descent, is not cooled —
I do not know what kind of heart he has.

ভব তরিবারে হরি- নাম-মন্ত্র ভেলা করি
আপনে গৌরাঙ্গ করে পার ।
তবে যে ডুবিয়া মরে কেবা উদ্ধারিবে তারে
পরমানন্দের পরিহার ॥

*bhaba taribāre hari- nāma-mantra bhelā kari*
*āpane gaurāṅga kare pāra |*
*tabe ye ḍubiyā mare kebā uddhāribe tāre*
*paramānandera parihāra ||*

*Word for word:* bhaba taribare — to cross [the ocean of] worldly existence; hari-nama-mantra bhela kari — making the mantra of Hari's name a raft; apane gauranga kare para — Gauranga Himself ferries across; tabe ye dubiya mare — if anyone still drowns; keba uddharibe tare — who will rescue him?; paramanandera parihara — [this is] Paramananda's plea

**1.4.** To cross the ocean of worldly existence, making the mantra of Hari's name a raft,
Gauranga Himself ferries [all] across.
If anyone still drowns and perishes — who will save him?
This is Paramananda's plea.[^05-3]

[^05-1]: Signature: "Paramananda". PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 269 (printed p. 258), 20th pallava ("Sri Gaurachandra — another
mode"), no. 19; MS P-R-Sa no. 2310. GPT1 — p. 16, no. 40 (raga kamoda); GPT2 — sect. 1.2, no. 40. Majumdar divides the
twelve PK padas signed "Paramananda" into Vrajabuli padas of a later poet of Vrindavana and Bengali padas which he ascribes
to Paramananda Gupta — the Lord's companion in whose house Nityananda stayed (CB); he regards PK 2202, 2119, 672 and 1693
as possibly fragments of his lost *Gauranga-vijaya-gita*, mentioned by Jayananda. The attribution is conjectural (S. Ray
assigned these padas to Karnapura, Paramananda Sena).
[^05-2]: "Essence of devotion" (bhakati-sāra); MSS "ka", "kha", "cha" and GPT: "the taste of devotion" (bhakati-rasa). The image: Gaura
is the sun; whoever stays blind at His rising can be helped by nothing else.
[^05-3]: "Plea" (parihāra) — the poet's humble entreaty. The raft of the holy name is an image of the nama-sankirtana which the
Lord brought (CC Adi 3, 7).

## 2. Paramananda (Gupta) — "paraśa-maṇira sane ki diba tulanā re…" (PK 672)
*Lila: praise of Gaura: neither the touchstone, nor the moon, nor the wish-fulfilling tree can be compared with Him — He
gave away prema without waiting to be asked. In PK the pada is the gaura-chandrika to the section "rasodgara-anuraga"
(Radha recalls Her meeting with Krishna). According to Majumdar — possibly from Paramananda Gupta's *Gauranga-vijaya*.
Raga vibhasa.*[^05-4]

পরশ-মণির সনে কি দিব তুলনা রে
পরশ ছোঁয়াইলে হয় সোণা ।
আমার গৌরাঙ্গের গুণে নাচিয়া গাইয়া রে
রতন হইল কত জনা ॥

*paraśa-maṇira sane ki diba tulanā re*
*paraśa chom̐yāile haya soṇā |*
*āmāra gaurāṅgera guṇe nāciyā gāiyā re*
*ratana haila kata janā ||*

*Word for word:* parasha-manira sane — with the touchstone; ki diba tulana re — what comparison can I give?; parasha chhonyaile — at the touch [of the stone]; haya sona — [iron] becomes gold; amara gaurangera gune — by the qualities of my Gauranga; nachiya gaiya re — dancing and singing; ratana haila kata jana — how many people became jewels!

**2.1.** What can be compared with the touchstone? —
at its touch [iron] turns to gold;
but by the virtues of my Gauranga, dancing and singing,
how many people have become jewels![^05-5]

শচীর নন্দন বনমালী ।
এ তিন ভুবনে যার তুলনা দিবার নাই
গোরা মোর পরাণ-পুতলী ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*śacīra nandana banamālī |*
*e tina bhubane yāra tulanā dibāra nāi*
*gorā mora parāṇa-putalī || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* shachira nandana — the son of Shachi; vanamali — wearing a forest garland; e tina bhubane — in the three worlds; yara tulana dibara nai — to whom nothing can be compared; gora mora parana-putali — Gora, the darling (doll) of my life; (dhru) — refrain

**2.2.** *(Refrain)* The son of Shachi, wearing the forest garland,
He to whom nothing in the three worlds can be compared —
Gora, the darling of my life.[^05-6]

গৌরাঙ্গ-চাঁদের ছাঁদে ও চাঁদ কলঙ্কী রে
এমন করিতে নারে আলো ।
অকলঙ্ক পূর্ণ-চাঁদ উদয় নদিয়া-পুরে
মনের আন্ধার দূরে গেলো ॥

*gaurāṅga-cām̐dera chām̐de o cām̐da kalaṅkī re*
*emana karite nāre ālo |*
*akalaṅka pūrṇa-cām̐da udaya nadiyā-pure*
*manera āndhāra dūre gelo ||*

*Word for word:* gauranga-chandera chhande — beside the form of the moon Gauranga; o chanda kalanki re — that moon is spotted; emana karite nare alo — cannot give such light; akalanka purna-chanda — the spotless full moon; udaya nadiya-pure — has risen in the town of Nadia; manera andhara dure gelo — the darkness of the heart has gone far away

**2.3.** Beside the form of the moon Gauranga that moon is spotted:
it cannot shine like this.
A spotless full moon has risen in the town of Nadia —
and the darkness of the heart has gone far away.

এ গুণে সুরভি সুর- তরু সম নহে রে
মাগিলে সে পায় কোন জন ।
না মাগিতে অখিল ভুবন ভরি জনে জনে
যাচিয়া দেওল প্রেম-ধন ॥

*e guṇe surabhi sura- taru sama nahe re*
*māgile se pāya kona jana |*
*nā māgite akhila bhubana bhari jane jane*
*yāciyā deola prema-dhana ||*

*Word for word:* e gune — in this quality; surabhi — the Surabhi [cow]; sura-taru — the tree of the gods (wish-fulfilling tree); sama nahe re — are not equal [to Him]; magile — [only] on asking; se paya kona jana — does someone receive; na magite — unasked; akhila bhubana bhari — filling the whole world; jane jane — to each person; yachiya deola prema-dhana — He gave, even entreating, the wealth of prema

**2.4.** In this virtue neither [the cow] Surabhi nor the tree of the gods equals Him:
from them only one who asks receives;
but He, unasked, filled the whole world —
to each person, entreating, He gave the wealth of prema.[^05-7]

গোরাচাঁদের তুলনা গোরাচাঁদ গোসাঞি রে
বিচার করিয়া দেখ সভে ।
পরমানন্দের মনে এ বড় আকুতি রে
গৌরাঙ্গের দয়া হবে কবে ॥

*gorācām̐dera tulanā gorācām̐da gosāñi re*
*bicāra kariyā dekha sabhe |*
*paramānandera mane e baṛa ākuti re*
*gaurāṅgera dayā habe kabe ||*

*Word for word:* gorachandera tulana — the comparison for Gorachand; gorachanda gosani re — is the Lord Gorachand [Himself]; bichara kariya dekha sabhe — consider and see, all of you; paramanandera mane — in Paramananda's heart; e bara akuti re — this is the great longing; gaurangera daya habe kabe — when will Gauranga's mercy come?

**2.5.** Gorachand can be compared only with the Lord Gorachand Himself —
consider, all of you, and you will see.
In Paramananda's heart there is a great longing:
when will Gauranga's mercy come?

[^05-4]: Signature: "Paramananda". PK: vol. 2, PDF pp. 61–62, 6th pallava, no. 9 ("Then — rasodgara-anuraga. Sri
Gaurachandra"); MSS P-R-Sa no. 1147, P-R 22.27. GPT1 — p. 138, no. 78 (raga vibhasa). In MS P-R the stanzas stand in
another order, and the last runs differently and is signed with the name of Nayanananda: "Gaurangachand cannot be
compared — consider in your hearts and see; in Nayanananda's heart there is great joy: ponder Gora's virtues" (see VAR).
The attribution to Paramananda (Ray's index, Majumdar) is therefore not wholly secure.
[^05-5]: The touchstone (parasha-mani) only turns iron into gold, but the songs of Gauranga's virtues have made "jewels" of
many people. MS P-R adds before this stanza: "How can I forget the lilas of Gaurangachand! At my Gauranga's virtues beasts
and birds weep, stones melt and crumble."
[^05-6]: "Darling of my life" (parāṇa-putalī, lit. "the little doll of my life") — what is dearest of all. MS P-R lacks the refrain.
[^05-7]: Surabhi is the wish-fulfilling cow; the tree of the gods (kalpa-vriksha) is the wish-fulfilling tree: they give only
what is asked of them. Cf. CC Adi 7 (the Lord gives prema to all without discrimination). MS P-R: "unasked, He Himself
gave".

## 3. Paramananda (Gupta) — "gorā mora dayāra abadhi guṇanidhi…" (PK 2119)
*Lila: Navadvipa — Gauranga roams the bank of the Ganga leaning on the shoulders of devotees; He weeps, repeating
"Haribol"; His body is covered with thrills, and the earth cannot hold Him. In PK — in the 18th pallava (the form of Sri
Gauranga); in KGC — the first pada of the 14th kshanada. According to Majumdar — possibly from Paramananda Gupta's
*Gauranga-vijaya*. Raga shri.*[^05-8]

গোরা মোর দয়ার অবধি গুণনিধি ।
সুরধুনী-তীরে নদীয়া নগরে
গৌরাঙ্গ বিহরে নিরবধি ॥

*gorā mora dayāra abadhi guṇanidhi |*
*suradhunī-tīre nadīyā nagare*
*gaurāṅga bihare nirabadhi ||*

*Word for word:* gora mora — my Gora; dayara abadhi — the limit of mercy; gunanidhi — the treasury of virtues; suradhuni-tire — on the bank of the Suradhuni (Ganga); nadiya nagare — in the town of Nadia; gauranga bihare — Gauranga sports (roams); nirabadhi — ceaselessly

**3.1.** My Gora is the limit of mercy, the treasury of virtues:
on the bank of the Suradhuni, in the town of Nadia,
Gauranga sports ceaselessly.

ভুজ-যুগ আরোপিয়া ভকতের কান্ধে ।
চলিতে না পারে গোরা হরিবোল বলিয়া কান্দে ॥

*bhuja-yuga āropiyā bhakatera kāndhe |*
*calite nā pāre gorā haribola baliyā kānde ||*

*Word for word:* bhuja-yuga aropiya — placing both arms; bhakatera kandhe — on the shoulders of devotees; chalite na pare gora — Gora cannot walk; haribola baliya kande — He weeps, saying "Haribol"

**3.2.** Placing both arms on the shoulders of devotees,
Gora cannot walk — He weeps, repeating "Haribol".

প্রেমে ছল ছল নয়ান-যুগল
কত নদী বহে ধারে ।
পুলকে পূরল সব কলেবর
ধরণী ধরিতে নারে ॥

*preme chala chala nayāna-yugala*
*kata nadī bahe dhāre |*
*pulake pūrala saba kalebara*
*dharaṇī dharite nāre ||*

*Word for word:* preme chhala chhala — brimming with tears of prema; nayana-yugala — the two eyes; kata nadi bahe dhare — how many rivers flow in streams!; pulake purala — filled with thrills; saba kalebara — the whole body; dharani dharite nare — the earth cannot hold [Him]

**3.3.** Both eyes brim with tears of prema —
how many rivers flow in streams!
His whole body is covered with thrills —
the earth cannot hold Him.

সঙ্গে পারিষদ ফিরে নিরন্তর
হরি হরি বোল বলে ।
সখার কান্ধে ভুজ-যুগ দিয়া
হেলিতে দুলিতে চলে ॥

*saṅge pāriṣada phire nirantara*
*hari hari bola bale |*
*sakhāra kāndhe bhuja-yuga diyā*
*helite dulite cale ||*

*Word for word:* sange parishada — the associates with Him; phire nirantara — move about ceaselessly; hari hari bola bale — say "Hari, Hari!"; sakhara kandhe — on His friends' shoulders; bhuja-yuga diya — placing both arms; helite dulite chale — He walks, swaying and rocking

**3.4.** His associates go with Him ceaselessly,
crying, "Hari, Hari!"
Placing both arms on His friends' shoulders,
He walks, swaying and rocking.

ভুবন ভরিয়া প্রেম উভারিল
পতিত-পাবন নাম ।
শুনিয়া ভরসা পরমানন্দের
মনেতে না লয় আন ॥

*bhubana bhariyā prema ubhārila*
*patita-pābana nāma |*
*śuniyā bharasā paramānandera*
*manete nā laya āna ||*

*Word for word:* bhubana bhariya — filling the world; prema ubharila — He poured out prema; patita-pabana nama — [His] name is "Purifier of the fallen"; shuniya — hearing [this]; bharasa paramanandera — Paramananda's hope; manete na laya ana — his heart accepts nothing else

**3.5.** Filling the world, He poured out prema —
His name is "Purifier of the fallen".
Hearing this, Paramananda has taken hope:
his heart accepts nothing else.[^05-9]

[^05-8]: Signature: "Paramananda". PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 237 (printed p. 226), 18th pallava, no. 11; MS P-R-Sa no. 2227. In PK
the pada stands immediately before Paramananda's pada "gorā-tanu dhūlāya loṭāya" (PK 2120; chapter 1, no. 7). GPT1 — p. 279,
no. 6 (raga shri; the first line is the refrain); GPT2 — twice (sect. 1.3, no. 16; 4.3, no. 6). KGC — 14th kshanada, no. 1
(pp. 106–107; raga dhanashi) — with minor variants: "Gora is the limit of mercy" (without "my"), "Gorachand cannot walk —
He weeps, repeating 'Hari, Hari'". Cf. CB Madhya 23 (the Lord with His devotees in kirtana along the bank of the Ganga).
[^05-9]: "Poured out" (ubhārila; KGC ubhārala) — lit. "made overflow". MSS "kha", "gha", P-R-Sa read in 3.4 "hilite" ("swaying").

## 4. Parameshvara Dasa — "eka dina pahum̐ hāsi advaita-mandire āsi…" (PK 23)
*Lila: the Lord comes to Advaita's house and with Nityananda and Advaita discusses a great festival; Sita Thakurani speaks
sweet words; the Lord orders that all singers and musicians be invited, that a full water-pot, banana trees and garlands
be set up, and that in the evening the "khol-mangala" be performed — the blessing of the mridanga before the kirtana. In PK
— the first pada of the section "Adhivasa of the sankirtana". According to Majumdar (following S. Ray) — an eyewitness
description. Raga dhanashi.*[^05-10]

এক দিন পহুঁ হাসি অদ্বৈত-মন্দিরে আসি
বসিলেন শচীর কুমার ।
নিত্যানন্দ করি সঙ্গে অদ্বৈত বসিয়া রঙ্গে
মহোৎসবের করিলা বিচার ॥

*eka dina pahum̐ hāsi advaita-mandire āsi*
*basilena śacīra kumāra |*
*nityānanda kari saṅge advaita basiyā raṅge*
*mahotsabera karilā bicāra ||*

*Word for word:* eka dina — one day; pahun hasi — the Lord, smiling; advaita-mandire asi — coming to Advaita's house; basilena shachira kumara — the son of Shachi sat down; nityananda kari sange — taking Nityananda with Him; advaita basiya range — Advaita, sitting joyfully; mahotsabera karila bichara — they deliberated on a great festival

**4.1.** One day the Lord, smiling, came to Advaita's house —
and the son of Shachi sat down;
with Nityananda, and with Advaita joyfully seated beside Him,
He deliberated on a great festival.

শুনিয়া আনন্দে হাসি সীতা ঠাকুরাণী আসি
কহিলেন মধুর বচন ।
তা শুনি আনন্দ মনে মহোৎসবের বিধানে
বোলে কিছু শচীর নন্দন ॥

*śuniyā ānande hāsi sītā ṭhākurāṇī āsi*
*kahilena madhura bacana |*
*tā śuni ānanda mane mahotsabera bidhāne*
*bole kichu śacīra nandana ||*

*Word for word:* shuniya — hearing; anande hasi — laughing with joy; sita thakurani asi — Sita Thakurani came; kahilena madhura bachana — she spoke sweet words; ta shuni — hearing that; ananda mane — with a joyful heart; mahotsabera bidhane — about the arrangement of the festival; bole kichhu shachira nandana — the son of Shachi says something

**4.2.** Hearing of this, laughing with joy, Sita Thakurani came
and spoke sweet words.
Hearing them, joyfully, about the arrangement of the festival
the son of Shachi says:

শুন ঠাকুরাণি সীতা বৈষ্ণব আনিয়ে এথা
আমন্ত্রণ করিয়া যতনে ।
যেবা গায় যেবা বায় আমন্ত্রণ করি তায়
পৃথক্ পৃথক্ জনে জনে ॥

*śuna ṭhākurāṇi sītā baiṣṇaba āniye ethā*
*āmantraṇa kariyā yatane |*
*yebā gāya yebā bāya āmantraṇa kari tāya*
*pṛthak pṛthak jane jane ||*

*Word for word:* shuna thakurani sita — listen, mistress Sita; vaishnava aniye etha — let us bring Vaishnavas here; amantrana kariya yatane — inviting them with care; yeba gaya — whoever sings; yeba baya — whoever plays; amantrana kari taya — inviting them; prithak prithak jane jane — each one separately

**4.3.** "Listen, mistress Sita: let us bring Vaishnavas here,
inviting them with care;
whoever sings, whoever plays — let us invite them all,
each one separately."

এত বলি গোরা রায় আজ্ঞা দিল সভাকায়
বৈষ্ণব করহ আমন্ত্রণ ।
খোল করতাল লৈয়া অগুরু চন্দন দিয়া
পূর্ণ-ঘট করহ স্থাপন ॥

*eta bali gorā rāya ājñā dila sabhākāya*
*baiṣṇaba karaha āmantraṇa |*
*khola karatāla laiyā aguru candana diyā*
*pūrṇa-ghaṭa karaha sthāpana ||*

*Word for word:* eta bali — saying this; gora raya — Gora Raya; ajna dila sabhakaya — commanded everyone; vaishnava karaha amantrana — invite the Vaishnavas; khola karatala laiya — taking the khol and karatalas; aguru chandana diya — [anointing them] with aloe-wood and sandal; purna-ghata karaha sthapana — set up the full water-pot

**4.4.** Saying this, Gora Raya commanded everyone:
"Invite the Vaishnavas;
take the khol and karatalas, anoint them with aloe-wood and sandal,
set up the full water-pot;

আরোপণ কর কলা তাহে বান্ধি ফুলমালা
কীর্তন-মণ্ডলী কুতূহলে ।
মাল্য চন্দন গুয়া ঘৃত মধু দধি দিয়া
খোল-মঙ্গল সন্ধ্যাকালে ॥

*āropaṇa kara kalā tāhe bāndhi phulamālā*
*kīrtana-maṇḍalī kutūhale |*
*mālya candana guyā ghṛta madhu dadhi diyā*
*khola-maṅgala sandhyākāle ||*

*Word for word:* aropana kara kala — plant banana trees; tahe bandhi phulamala — tying flower garlands on them; kirtana-mandali kutuhale — [prepare] the kirtana circle with delight; malya chandana guya — garlands, sandal, areca nuts; ghrita madhu dadhi diya — with ghee, honey and curd; khola-mangala sandhyakale — the blessing of the khol at evening

**4.5.** plant banana trees, tie flower garlands to them,
joyfully prepare the circle for kirtana;
with garlands, sandal, areca nuts, ghee, honey and curd,
in the evening perform the khol-mangala."[^05-11]

শুনিয়া প্রভুর কথা প্রীতে বিধি কৈল যথা
নানা উপহার গন্ধবাসে ।
সভে হরি হরি বোলে খোল-মঙ্গল করে
পরমেশ্বর দাস রসে ভাষে ॥

*śuniyā prabhura kathā prīte bidhi kaila yathā*
*nānā upahāra gandhabāse |*
*sabhe hari hari bole khola-maṅgala kare*
*parameśvara dāsa rase bhāṣe ||*

*Word for word:* shuniya prabhura katha — hearing the Lord's words; prite — lovingly; bidhi kaila yatha — they did as instructed; nana upahara gandhabase — [with] various offerings and fragrances; sabhe hari hari bole — all say "Hari, Hari!"; khola-mangala kare — they perform the khol-mangala; parameshvara dasa rase bhashe — Parameshvara Dasa tells [this], full of rasa

**4.6.** Hearing the Lord's words, lovingly they did all as instructed,
with various offerings and fragrances.
All cry "Hari, Hari!" and perform the khol-mangala —
so, full of rasa, sings Parameshvara Dasa.[^05-12]

[^05-10]: Signature: "Parameshvara Dasa". PK: vol. 1, PDF p. 31 (printed p. 24), 1st shakha, no. 23, under the heading "Then
— the adhivasa of the sankirtana"; MS P-R-Sa no. 23. GPT1 — p. 246, no. 26 (raga dhanashi), signed "Parameshvari Dasa";
after it in GPT1 (no. 27) comes another pada with the same signature, on the "seven groups" of the kirtana with fourteen
mridangas. Parameshvara Dasa was a companion of Nityananda (CC Adi 11; CB, Antya-khanda), and later of Jahnava-devi.
Majumdar, following S. Ray, regards the pada as an eyewitness description. Where this house of Advaita was — in Navadvipa
or in Shantipura — the pada does not say.
[^05-11]: The full water-pot (purna-ghata), banana trees and garlands are the usual adornment of a festival ground. The khol is
the Bengali clay mridanga; the "khol-mangala" is the rite of blessing the mridanga before a kirtana: it is anointed with
sandal, garlanded, and auspicious substances are offered to it. MSS "ga", "gha", "cha", P-R-Sa read in 4.3: "whoever plays
[instruments]" (ye bājāya).
[^05-12]: MS "ga" and GPT1 read in 4.1: "…seated in Advaita's house, the son of Shachi said". GPT1 ends: "Parameshvari Dasa is
immersed in rasa" (rase bhāse) instead of "sings" (lit. "tells", bhāṣe).

## 5. Vasu Ghosha — "phulabana gorācām̐da dekhiyā nayane…" (PK 1525; BR, p. 936)
*Lila: Navadvipa, 1509 — seeing a flowering grove, the Lord remembers the battle of flowers; crying "Jaya!", His
companions shower Him with flowers; Gadadhara and Nityananda are with Him. In the *Bhakti-ratnakara* the guide shows
Srinivasa Acharya this flower garden in Navadvipa and quotes the pada as testimony; in PK it is the gaura-chandrika to
the section "Phula-dola" (the spring play with flowers). According to Majumdar — seen with the poet's own eyes (1509).
Raga tudi (in BR, kamoda).*[^05-13]

ফুলবন গোরাচাঁদ দেখিয়া নয়নে ।
ফুলের সমর গোরার পড়ি গেল মনে ॥

*phulabana gorācām̐da dekhiyā nayane |*
*phulera samara gorāra paṛi gela mane ||*

*Word for word:* phulabana — the flower grove; gorachanda dekhiya nayane — Gorachand, seeing with His eyes; phulera samara — the battle of flowers; gorara pari gela mane — came to Gora's mind (BR var.: phula bala — "an army of flowers"; gora balila bachane — Gora said in words)

**5.1.** Seeing with His eyes the flowering grove,
Gorachand remembered the battle of flowers.[^05-14]

ঘন জয় জয় দিয়া পারিষদগণে ।
গোরা-গায়ে ফুল পেলি মারে জনে জনে ॥

*ghana jaya jaya diyā pāriṣadagaṇe |*
*gorā-gāye phula peli māre jane jane ||*

*Word for word:* ghana jaya jaya diya — again and again crying "Jaya, jaya!"; parishadagane — the associates; gora-gaye — at Gora's body; phula peli mare — throw flowers; jane jane — one after another

**5.2.** Again and again crying "Jaya, jaya!", the associates
one after another throw flowers at Gora.

প্রিয় গদাধর সঙ্গে আর নিত্যানন্দ ।
ফুলের সমরে গোরার হইল আনন্দ ॥

*priya gadādhara saṅge āra nityānanda |*
*phulera samare gorāra haila ānanda ||*

*Word for word:* priya gadadhara sange — with Him the dear Gadadhara; ara nityananda — and Nityananda; phulera samare — in the battle of flowers; gorara haila ananda — Gora was filled with joy

**5.3.** With Him are the dear Gadadhara and Nityananda;
in the battle of flowers Gora was filled with joy.

গদাধর সঙ্গে পহুঁ করয়ে বিলাস ।
বাসুদেব ঘোষ এই করল প্রকাশ ॥

*gadādhara saṅge pahum̐ karaye bilāsa |*
*bāsudeba ghoṣa ei karala prakāśa ||*

*Word for word:* gadadhara sange — with Gadadhara; pahun karaye bilasa — the Lord sports; vasudeva ghosha — Vasudeva Ghosha; ei karala prakasha — has revealed this

**5.4.** With Gadadhara the Lord sports —
this Vasudeva Ghosha has told.[^05-15]

[^05-13]: Signature: "Vasudeva Ghosha". PK: vol. 2, PDF p. 446, no. 101, under the heading "Then — phula-dola. Here — Sri
Mahaprabhu"; MS P-R-Sa no. 2070. BR, wave 12 (ed. 1912/1913, p. 936; ed. 1960, vv. 3224–3229): before the pada Narahari
Chakravarti writes: "One day, looking at this flower garden, [the Lord] says with a smile: 'A battle of flowers would be
good!' — and His dear companions, taking bunches of flowers, fight with flowers while all look on." GPT1 — p. 342, no. 69
(raga tudi); GPT2 — sect. 5.1, no. 69. Majumdar calls this and the following padas of BR (pp. 936–943) — the battle of
flowers, the game of dice, the water play, the holi with Gadadhara — scenes the poet saw himself; they are confirmed by
Shivananda Sena's holi pada (chapter 1, no. 14), where Vasu is named among the dancers. In the stage-1 catalogue the pada
was wrongly linked with PK 1186 (that is Vasu Ghosha's goshtha pada — another recension of the pada in chapter 1, no. 11).
[^05-14]: BR: "Seeing with His eyes an army of flowers, Gora said: 'A battle of flowers!'" (phula bala … balila bacane). In Navadvipa
the Lord was often absorbed in the moods of Krishna-lila (cf. chapter 1, nos. 9–13).
[^05-15]: Here and in the following padas Gadadhara is the chief partner in the Lord's play. In Gaudiya Vaishnava theology
Gadadhara Pandita is a manifestation of Sri Radha (*Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika* 147–153), and these pastimes reflect the lilas
of Radha and Krishna: pure prema, in which there is nothing mundane. BR: "…with Gadadhara Gora sports — Vasudeva Ghosha
reveals [this] rasa"; MS "gha": "Vasudeva Ghosha has revealed this rasa".

## 6. Vasu Ghosha — "gaurāṅgacām̐dera mane ki bhāba paṛila…" (BR, pp. 936–937)
*Lila: Navadvipa, 1509 — sitting in the flower garden, the Lord plays dice (pasha-sari) with Gadadhara; both are immersed
in the rasa of the game. The pada is known from BR and GPT. According to Majumdar — seen with the poet's own eyes. Raga
kamoda.*[^05-16]

গৌরাঙ্গচাঁদের মনে কি ভাব পড়িল ।
পাশা সারী লইয়া গোরা খেলা সিরজিল ॥

*gaurāṅgacām̐dera mane ki bhāba paṛila |*
*pāśā sārī laiyā gorā khelā sirajila ||*

*Word for word:* gaurangachandera mane — in the heart of Gaurangachand; ki bhaba parila — what feeling arose; pasha sari laiya — taking dice and pieces; gora khela sirajila — Gora started a game

**6.1.** What feeling arose in the heart of Gaurangachand! —
taking dice and pieces, Gora started a game.

গদাধর সঙ্গে গোরা খেলে পাশা সারী ।
ফেলিতে লাগিলা পাশা হারি জিনি বলি ॥

*gadādhara saṅge gorā khele pāśā sārī |*
*phelite lāgilā pāśā hāri jini bali ||*

*Word for word:* gadadhara sange — with Gadadhara; gora khele pasha sari — Gora plays at dice; phelite lagila pasha — they began to throw the dice; hari jini bali — saying "I lose — I win"

**6.2.** With Gadadhara Gora plays at dice;
they began to throw the dice, saying: "I lose — I win!"

দুয়া চারি বলি দান ফেলে গদাধর ।
পঞ্চ তিন করি ডারে গৌরাঙ্গসুন্দর ॥

*duyā cāri bali dāna phele gadādhara |*
*pañca tina kari ḍāre gaurāṅgasundara ||*

*Word for word:* dua chari bali — calling "two, four!"; dana phele gadadhara — Gadadhara throws [his] turn; pancha tina kari — [calling] "five, three!"; dare gaurangasundara — Gaurangasundara casts (var.: dake — calls out)

**6.3.** "Two, four!" — Gadadhara throws his turn;
"Five, three!" — Gaurangasundara casts.[^05-17]

দুই জন মগ্ন হৈল পাশা-খেলা-রসে ।
জয় জয় দিয়া গায় বাসুদেব ঘোষে ॥

*dui jana magna haila pāśā-khelā-rase |*
*jaya jaya diyā gāya bāsudeba ghoṣe ||*

*Word for word:* dui jana — the two; magna haila — were immersed; pasha-khela-rase — in the rasa of the dice game; jaya jaya diya — crying "Jaya, jaya!"; gaya vasudeva ghoshe — Vasudeva Ghosha sings

**6.4.** The two were immersed in the rasa of the dice game;
crying "Jaya, jaya!", Vasudeva Ghosha sings.

[^05-16]: Signature: "Vasudeva Ghosha". BR, wave 12 (ed. 1912/1913, pp. 936–937; ed. 1960, vv. 3230–3234): "One day
Gaurahari with Gadadhara, sitting in this flower garden, plays at dice." GPT1 — p. 354, no. 32 (raga dhanashi), with minor
variants ("the Lord began the game"). The pada was not previously found in PK (see the end of this note). The game of dice (pasha-khela) is a well-known lila of
Radha and Krishna; on Gadadhara see note 15.
Full PK check (chapter 16): another recension of the pada is in PK — **PK 2668** (vol. 4, 30th pallava, ashtakaliya: "atha pāśā-krīṛā. tatra śrī-gauracandro yathā," PDF p. 114, label "॥১৯৫॥২৬৬৮॥"; "gaurāṅgacām̐dera mane ki bhāba haila / pāśā śārī laiyā pahu khelā ārambhila…," signature "jaya jaya diyā gāya bāsudeba ghoṣe").
[^05-17]: The players' cries name the throw they want. BR-1960, BR-2006 and GPT1: "'Five, three!' — calls out…" (ḍāke); GPT1
here names the Lord "Rasika-nagara" ("the connoisseur of rasa", a name of Krishna).

## 7. Vasu Ghosha — "jalakeli gorācāndera maneta paṛila…" (PK 1108; BR, p. 937)
*Lila: Navadvipa, 1509 — the Lord remembers the water play and goes down into the Ganga with His companions; all splash
one another; Gauranga splashes Gadadhara. In BR the guide shows Srinivasa that very ghat; in PK it is the gaura-chandrika
to the section "Water play". According to Majumdar — seen with the poet's own eyes. Raga saranga (in BR, mayura).*[^05-18]

জলকেলি গোরাচান্দের মনেত পড়িল ।
পারিষদগণ সঞে জলেতে নামিল ॥

*jalakeli gorācāndera maneta paṛila |*
*pāriṣadagaṇa sañe jalete nāmila ||*

*Word for word:* jalakeli — water play; gorachandera maneta parila — came to Gorachand's mind; parishadagana sanye — with His associates; jalete namila — He went down into the water

**7.1.** The water play came to Gorachand's mind —
with His associates He went down into the water.

কারো অঙ্গে কেহো কেহো জল পেলি মারে ।
গৌরাঙ্গ পেলিয়া জল মারে গদাধরে ॥

*kāro aṅge keho keho jala peli māre |*
*gaurāṅga peliyā jala māre gadādhare ||*

*Word for word:* karo ange — at someone's body; keho keho — someone; jala peli mare — splashes water; gauranga peliya jala — Gauranga, throwing water; mare gadadhare — splashes Gadadhara

**7.2.** Someone splashes water on someone;
Gauranga, scooping up water, splashes Gadadhara.[^05-19]

জল-ক্রীড়া করে গোরা হরষিত-মনে ।
হুলাহুলি বোলাবুলি করে জনে জনে ॥

*jala-krīṛā kare gorā haraṣita-mane |*
*hulāhuli bolābuli kare jane jane ||*

*Word for word:* jala-krida kare gora — Gora sports in the water; harashita-mane — with a joyful heart; hulahuli — joyful shouting; bolabuli — calling to one another; kare jane jane — everyone does

**7.3.** With a joyful heart Gora sports in the water;
all shout with joy, all call to one another.

গৌরাঙ্গচান্দের লীলা কহনে না যায় ।
বাসুদেব ঘোষে তহি গোরা-গুণ গায় ॥

*gaurāṅgacāndera līlā kahane nā yāya |*
*bāsudeba ghoṣe tahi gorā-guṇa gāya ||*

*Word for word:* gaurangachandera lila — the lila of Gaurangachand; kahane na yaya — cannot be told; vasudeva ghoshe tahi — Vasudeva Ghosha there; gora-guna gaya — sings Gora's virtues

**7.4.** The lila of Gaurangachand cannot be told in words;
Vasudeva Ghosha sings of it — of Gora's virtues.

[^05-18]: Signature: "Vasudeva Ghosha". PK: vol. 2, PDF p. 261, 16th pallava, no. 17, under the heading "Here — water play.
Sri Gaurachandra befitting it"; MS P-R-Sa no. 1606. BR, wave 12 (ed. 1912/1913, p. 937; ed. 1960, vv. 3235–3239): "One
day at this ghat the Lord with His companions plays in the water, remembering the former [lila]." GPT1 — p. 351, no. 25
(raga tudi); GPT2 — sect. 5.2, no. 25.
[^05-19]: BR: "…Gadadhara splashes water on Gora's body." Krishna's water play (jala-keli) with Radha and the gopis is one of
the lilas of Vraja; on Gadadhara see note 15.

## 8. Vasu Ghosha — "bṛndābana-līlā gorāra manete paṛila…" (PK 1253; BR, p. 941)
*Lila: Navadvipa — the Lord remembers the lila of Vrindavana: the Ganga becomes for Him the Yamuna, the flowering grove
Vrindavana, His companions the gopis; bringing together khols and karatalas, He dances in the midst of the kirtana,
revealing the rasa of the rasa dance. In BR the guide tells Srinivasa: "Here Gaurachandra revealed great bliss, overcome
by the former rasa of the rasa dance"; in PK it is the gaura-chandrika to the section "The great rasa on the autumn full
moon". Raga tudi (in BR, kamoda).*[^05-20]

বৃন্দাবন-লীলা গোরার মনেতে পড়িল ।
যমুনার ভাব সুরধুনীরে করিল ॥

*bṛndābana-līlā gorāra manete paṛila |*
*yamunāra bhāba suradhunīre karila ||*

*Word for word:* vrindavana-lila — the lila of Vrindavana; gorara manete parila — came to Gora's mind; yamunara bhaba — the feeling [for] the Yamuna (BR var.: yamunara bhana — taking [it] for the Yamuna); suradhunire karila — He turned upon the Suradhuni (Ganga)

**8.1.** The lila of Vrindavana came to Gora's mind:
the Suradhuni became for Him the Yamuna.[^05-21]

ফুলবন দেখি বৃন্দাবনের সমান ।
সহচরগণ গোপীগণ অনুমান ॥

*phulabana dekhi bṛndābanera samāna |*
*sahacaragaṇa gopīgaṇa anumāna ||*

*Word for word:* phulabana dekhi — seeing the flower grove; brindabanera samana — as like Vrindavana; sahacharagana — His companions; gopigana anumana — [He] takes to be the gopis

**8.2.** He saw the flowering grove as like Vrindavana,
and took His companions for the gopis.

খোল করতাল গোরা সুমেলি করিয়া ।
তার মাঝে নাচে গোরা জয় জয় দিয়া ॥

*khola karatāla gorā sumeli kariyā |*
*tāra mājhe nāce gorā jaya jaya diyā ||*

*Word for word:* khola karatala — khols and karatalas; gora sumeli kariya — Gora, bringing together; tara majhe — in their midst; nache gora — Gora dances; jaya jaya diya — amid cries of "Jaya, jaya!"

**8.3.** Bringing together khols and karatalas,
in their midst Gora dances amid cries of "Jaya, jaya!"

ঢলঢল গোরাতনু কাঞ্চন জিনিয়া ।
আজানুলম্বিত ভুজ নব কমনিয়া ॥

*ḍhalaḍhala gorātanu kāñcana jiniyā |*
*ājānulambita bhuja naba kamaniyā ||*

*Word for word:* dhaladhala goratanu — Gora's softly radiant body; kanchana jiniya — outshining gold; ajanulambita bhuja — arms reaching to the knees; naba kamaniya — youthful and lovely

**8.4.** *(Only in BR)* Gora's body glows softly, outshining gold;
His youthful, lovely arms reach to the knees.

বাসুদেব ঘোষ তাহে করয়ে বিলাস ।
রাস-রস গোরাচাঁদ করিলা প্রকাশ ॥

*bāsudeba ghoṣa tāhe karaye bilāsa |*
*rāsa-rasa gorācām̐da karilā prakāśa ||*

*Word for word:* vasudeva ghosha — Vasudeva Ghosha; tahe karaye bilasa — delights in that; rasa-rasa — the rasa of the rasa dance; gorachanda karila prakasha — Gorachand revealed

**8.5.** Vasudeva Ghosha delights in this:
Gorachand revealed the rasa of the rasa dance.[^05-22]

[^05-20]: Signature: "Vasudeva Ghosha". PK: vol. 2, PDF pp. 317–318, the first pada of the 24th pallava ("Then — the great
rasa on the autumn full moon. Sri Gaurachandra befitting it"); the end of the pada and its number are smudged in the scan
— by sequence it is no. 1 / 1253, which agrees with Ray's index and with Majumdar (PK 1253 is in his list of Vasu's padas
"on bhava"). BR, wave 12 (ed. 1912/1913, p. 941; ed. 1960, vv. 3291–3296). GPT1 — p. 335, no. 46 (raga tudi). Couplet 8.4
is found only in BR. Majumdar, listing the pastimes on BR pp. 936–943, does not name this pada specifically, but it
belongs to the same series.
[^05-21]: BR: "He took the Suradhuni for the Yamuna" (yamunāra bhāṇa, "the semblance of the Yamuna"); PK and GPT: "He turned His
feeling for the Yamuna upon the Suradhuni" (yamunāra bhāba). Suradhuni ("the river of the gods") is the Ganga.
[^05-22]: In these pastimes the Lord relishes the moods of Krishna-lila; in the kirtana His companions become, as it were, the
gopis — this is prema, pure and transcendental, not mundane feeling. The Gaudiya acharyas (Krishnadasa Kaviraja,
Bhaktisiddhanta) teach that Mahaprabhu is Krishna who has accepted Radha's mood and lustre to taste Her love (CC Adi 1, 4);
in Navadvipa He at times displayed the moods of Krishna Himself as well (cf. chapter 1, nos. 9–13). BR: "…Lord Gora
reveals the rasa of the rasa."

## 9. Vasu Ghosha — "dekha dekha ṛtu-rāja basanta samaya…" (PK 1425; BR, pp. 942–943)
*Lila: Navadvipa, spring — the Lord plays with coloured powder (phagu) with His companions; Srivasa leads the musicians,
Haridasa dances with upraised arms; Gadadhara is beside Him. In PK — the first pada of the section "Spring play on
Vasanta-panchami" (gaura-chandrika); in BR — among the padas on spring in Navadvipa, after padas of Narahari Chakravarti.
According to Majumdar — the holi with Gadadhara, seen with the poet's own eyes (1509). Raga vasanta.*[^05-23]

দেখ দেখ ঋতু-রাজ বসন্ত সময় ।
সহচর সঙ্গে বিহরে গোরা রায় ॥

*dekha dekha ṛtu-rāja basanta samaya |*
*sahacara saṅge bihare gorā rāya ||*

*Word for word:* dekha dekha — look, look; ritu-raja basanta samaya — the time of spring, king of seasons; sahachara sange — with His companions; bihare gora raya — Gora Raya sports

**9.1.** Look, look: the time of spring, the king of seasons —
Gora Raya sports with His companions.

ফাগু খেলে গোরাচান্দ নদীয়া নগরে ।
যুবতীর চিত হরে নয়নের শরে ॥

*phāgu khele gorācānda nadīyā nagare |*
*yubatīra cita hare nayanera śare ||*

*Word for word:* phagu khele gorachanda — Gorachand plays with coloured powder (phagu); nadiya nagare — in the town of Nadia; yubatira chita hare — He steals the hearts of young women; nayanera share — with the arrows of His eyes

**9.2.** Gorachand plays with coloured powder in the town of Nadia,
stealing the hearts of young women with the arrows of His eyes.[^05-24]

সহচর মেলি ফাগু দেয় গোরা-গায় ।
কুঙ্কুম পিচকা লেই কেহ কেহ ধায় ॥

*sahacara meli phāgu deya gorā-gāya |*
*kuṅkuma picakā lei keha keha dhāya ||*

*Word for word:* sahachara meli — the companions together; phagu deya gora-gaya — throw powder on Gora's body; kunkuma pichaka lei — taking squirts of kunkuma; keha keha dhaya — some run about

**9.3.** The companions together throw powder on Gora's body;
some run about with squirts of kunkuma.[^05-25]

নানা যন্ত্রে সুমেলি করিয়া শ্রীনিবাস ।
গদাধর আদি সঙ্গে করয়ে বিলাস ॥

*nānā yantre sumeli kariyā śrīnibāsa |*
*gadādhara ādi saṅge karaye bilāsa ||*

*Word for word:* nana yantre — the various instruments; sumeli kariya — bringing into harmony; shrinibasa — Srinivasa (Srivasa); gadadhara adi sange — with Gadadhara and others; karaye bilasa — [the Lord] sports

**9.4.** Srinivasa has brought the various instruments into harmony;
with Gadadhara and others [the Lord] sports.

হরি বলি বাহু তুলি নাচে হরিদাস ।
বাসুদেব ঘোষ রস করিল প্রকাশ ॥

*hari bali bāhu tuli nāce haridāsa |*
*bāsudeba ghoṣa rasa karila prakāśa ||*

*Word for word:* hari bali — crying "Hari!"; bahu tuli — raising his arms; nache haridasa — Haridasa dances; vasudeva ghosha — Vasudeva Ghosha; rasa karila prakasha — has revealed [this] rasa

**9.5.** Crying "Hari!", with upraised arms, Haridasa dances;
this rasa Vasudeva Ghosha has told.

[^05-23]: Signature: "Vasudeva Ghosha". PK: vol. 2, PDF p. 395, no. 1, under the heading "Then — spring play on
Vasanta-panchami. Here — Sri Mahaprabhu"; MS P-R-Sa no. 1978. BR, wave 12 (ed. 1912/1913, pp. 942–943; ed. 1960,
vv. 3321–3324): the guide tells Srinivasa that Gaurachandra with His companions sported here in spring with great joy and
that "here there was a wonderful game of phagu"; in BR the pada begins with the second couplet. GPT1 — pp. 337–338, no. 54
(raga vasanta); GPT2 — sect. 5.1, no. 54. Phagu is the red powder which people throw on one another at the spring
festivals (Vasanta-panchami, dola-yatra or holi).
[^05-24]: The words about young women are the language of nagari-bhava (Gaura as the nagara, the beloved of the town's
women); we translate faithfully to the author. Vrindavana Dasa stresses that in this incarnation the Lord never glanced at
another man's wife; worship of Gaura in the spirit of "Gaura-nagari" is not accepted by the Gaudiya tradition (Vrindavana
Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja, Bhaktisiddhanta).
[^05-25]: Kunkuma is a red powder (saffron); the squirt (pichaka, pichkari) is for coloured water. BR: "…run about with squirts
of sandal-water"; GPT1: "…run after [Him] with squirts [of flower-water]".

## 10. Shivananda Sena — "soṇāra baraṇa gorā prema-binodiyā…" (PK 2127)
*Lila: Navadvipa — golden Gora has flooded Nadia with prema; leaning on Govinda, He listens to the glories of Vrindavana
and, crying "Radha, Radha!", falls unconscious; Shivananda weeps, not comprehending the Lord's bhava. In PK — in the 18th
pallava, immediately after Yadunatha Dasa's pada on the Lord's bhava (PK 2126). According to Majumdar the pada conveys the
bewilderment of the devotees at the sight of Gauranga's ecstasies. Raga gauri.*[^05-26]

সোণার বরণ গোরা প্রেম-বিনোদিয়া ।
প্রেম-জলে ভাসাওল নগর নদীয়া ॥

*soṇāra baraṇa gorā prema-binodiyā |*
*prema-jale bhāsāola nagara nadīyā ||*

*Word for word:* sonara barana gora — golden-hued Gora; prema-binodiya — sporting in (delighting in) prema; prema-jale — with the waters of prema; bhasaola nagara nadiya — flooded the town of Nadia

**10.1.** Golden Gora, rapt in prema,
has flooded the town of Nadia with the waters of prema.

পরিসর বুক বাহি পড়ে প্রেম-ধার ।
নাহি জানে দিবানিশি প্রেমে মাতোয়ারা ॥

*parisara buka bāhi paṛe prema-dhāra |*
*nāhi jāne dibāniśi preme mātoyārā ||*

*Word for word:* parisara buka bahi — down His broad chest; pare prema-dhara — fall streams of prema; nahi jane dibanishi — He knows neither day nor night; preme matoara — intoxicated with prema

**10.2.** Down His broad chest stream torrents of prema;
intoxicated with prema, He knows neither day nor night.

গোবিন্দের অঙ্গে পহুঁ অঙ্গ হেলাইয়া ।
বৃন্দাবন-গুণ শুনে মগন হইয়া ॥

*gobindera aṅge pahum̐ aṅga helāiyā |*
*bṛndābana-guṇa śune magana haiyā ||*

*Word for word:* gobindera ange — against Govinda's body; pahun anga helaiya — the Lord, leaning His body; vrindavana-guna shune — listens to the glories of Vrindavana; magana haiya — absorbed

**10.3.** Leaning on Govinda,
the Lord, absorbed, listens to the glories of Vrindavana.[^05-27]

রাধা রাধা বলি পহুঁ পড়ে মুরছিয়া ।
শিবানন্দ কান্দে পহুঁর ভাব না বুঝিয়া ॥

*rādhā rādhā bali pahum̐ paṛe murachiyā |*
*śibānanda kānde pahum̐ra bhāba nā bujhiyā ||*

*Word for word:* radha radha bali — saying "Radha, Radha"; pahun pare murachhiya — the Lord falls fainting; shivananda kande — Shivananda weeps; pahunra bhaba na bujhiya — not understanding the Lord's bhava

**10.4.** "Radha, Radha!" cries the Lord and falls unconscious;
Shivananda weeps, not comprehending the Lord's bhava.[^05-28]

[^05-26]: Signature: "Shivananda". PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 239 (printed p. 228), 18th pallava, no. 19; MS P-R-Sa no. 2234. GPT1 —
p. 281, no. 14 (raga gauri), also immediately after Yadunatha's pada "gadādhara narahari kare dhari gaurahari" (GPT1 no. 13). Shivananda
Sena of Kumarahatta, the father of Kavi-Karnapura, led the devotees of Gauda to Puri every year; Majumdar regards his padas
as written during the Lord's lifetime.
[^05-27]: Govinda — probably Govinda Ghosha, the kirtana singer, singing to the Lord of Vrindavana; if the pada describes Puri,
Govinda the Lord's servant. Cf. the padas of Murari Gupta "Leaning against Gadadhara…" and of Paramananda "Gora's body
rolls in the dust" (chapter 1, nos. 6–7).
[^05-28]: The Lord is Krishna who has accepted Radha's bhava; His cry "Radha, Radha!" and His swoon are manifestations of
mahabhava (CC Adi 4). The words "not comprehending the bhava" are the poet's humility: the depth of this bhava is beyond
the grasp even of His intimate companions.

## 11. Chaitanyadasa — "āre mora gaura kiśora…" (PK 1985)
*Lila: the Lord's bhava — youthful Gaura, rapt in the rasa of former love, says with tears of joy: "I have found the Youth
of Vraja, all My sorrow is gone"; His companions laugh with joy. In PK it is the gaura-chandrika to the section
"Samriddhiman-sambhoga" (the fullness of union after long separation). The place is not named. Majumdar compares the pada
with the Lord's words in the *Chaitanya-charitamrita*: "I have found the Lord of My life…". Raga suhai.*[^05-29]

আরে মোর গৌর কিশোর ।
পুরব প্রেম-রসে ভোর ॥

*āre mora gaura kiśora |*
*puraba prema-rase bhora ||*

*Word for word:* are mora — O my; gaura kishora — youthful Gaura; puraba prema-rase — in the rasa of former love; bhora — absorbed

**11.1.** O my youthful Gaura,
rapt in the rasa of former love!

দু নয়নে আনন্দ-লোর ।
কহে পহুঁ হইয়া বিভোর ॥

*du nayane ānanda-lora |*
*kahe pahum̐ haiyā bibhora ||*

*Word for word:* du nayane — in both eyes; ananda-lora — tears of joy; kahe pahun — the Lord says; haiya bibhora — beside Himself [with prema]

**11.2.** In both eyes, tears of joy;
beside Himself with prema, the Lord says:

পাওলুঁ বরজ-কিশোর ।
সব দুখ দূরে গেও মোর ॥

*pāolum̐ baraja-kiśora |*
*saba dukha dūre geo mora ||*

*Word for word:* paolun — I have found; baraja-kishora — the Youth of Vraja; saba dukha — all sorrow; dure geo mora — of Mine has gone far away

**11.3.** "I have found the Youth of Vraja —
all My sorrow has gone far away;

চির দিনে পায়লুঁ পরাণ ।
যৈছন অমিয়া-সিনান ॥

*cira dine pāyalum̐ parāṇa |*
*yaichana amiyā-sināna ||*

*Word for word:* chira dine — after a long time; paylun parana — I have found [My] life; yaichhana — as if; amiya-sinana — a bath in nectar

**11.4.** after long days I have found My life —
as if bathed in nectar."[^05-30]

হেরি সহচরগণ হাস ।
গাওই চৈতন্য দাস ॥

*heri sahacaragaṇa hāsa |*
*gāoi caitanya dāsa ||*

*Word for word:* heri — seeing [this]; sahacharagana hasa — the companions laugh (with joy); gaoi chaitanya dasa — Chaitanya Dasa sings

**11.5.** Seeing this, the companions laugh with joy —
so sings Chaitanya Dasa.

[^05-29]: Signature: "Chaitanya Dasa". PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 188 (printed p. 177), 12th pallava, no. 17, under the heading "Then
— samriddhiman-sambhoga. Here — Sri Mahaprabhu". GPT1 — p. 413, no. 30 (raga suhai; on the same page are Vasu Ghosha's padas
nos. 31 and 33: chapter 1, no. 23; chapter 4, no. 18). Majumdar assigns Chaitanyadasa probably to Gadadhara's branch; he
compares the language of the pada with the padas of Narahari and Shivananda (cf. Narahari's pada with the same opening —
chapter 2, no. 7), and its sense with CC Madhya 1 and 13: "I have found the Lord of My life, for whom I was wasting away,
burnt by the fire of Madana" — the Lord's words at the Ratha-yatra.
[^05-30]: "The Youth of Vraja" (baraja-kiśora) is Krishna. These are the Lord's words in Radha's bhava as She finds Krishna after
long separation; the joy of this meeting is pure prema, not mundane feeling.

## 12. Paramananda (Gupta) — "ki karilā gorācām̐da nadiyā chāṛiyā…" (PK 1693)
*Lila: after the sannyasa — the grief of the devotees of Navadvipa: Murari, Mukunda and Srivasa will not survive the
separation, Advaita has despaired; with a straw between his teeth the poet begs the Lord to come to Nadia at least once. In
PK — the gaura-chandrika to the gopis' messages to Krishna in Mathura. According to Majumdar — probably a fragment of
Paramananda Gupta's *Gauranga-vijaya-gita*, written during the Lord's lifetime. Raga suhai.*[^05-31]

কি করিলা গোরাচাঁদ নদিয়া ছাড়িয়া ।
মরয়ে ভকতগণ তোমা না দেখিয়া ॥

*ki karilā gorācām̐da nadiyā chāṛiyā |*
*maraye bhakatagaṇa tomā nā dekhiyā ||*

*Word for word:* ki karila gorachanda — what have You done, Gorachand; nadiya chhariya — leaving Nadia; maraye bhakatagana — the devotees are dying; toma na dekhiya — not seeing You

**12.1.** What have You done, Gorachand, leaving Nadia!
The devotees are dying, not seeing You.

কীর্তন-বিলাস আদি যে করিলা সুখ ।
সোঙরি সোঙরি সভার বিদরয়ে বুক ॥

*kīrtana-bilāsa ādi ye karilā sukha |*
*soṅari soṅari sabhāra bidaraye buka ||*

*Word for word:* kirtana-bilasa adi — the sports of kirtana and the rest; ye karila sukha — the joy You gave; sonari sonari — remembering again and again; sabhara bidaraye buka — everyone's heart is breaking

**12.2.** The sports of kirtana and all the joy You gave —
remembering them again and again, everyone's heart is breaking.

মুরারি মুকুন্দ না জিয়ব শ্রীনিবাস ।
আচার্য্য অদ্বৈত ভেল জীবন নৈরাশ ॥

*murāri mukunda nā jiyaba śrīnibāsa |*
*ācāryya advaita bhela jībana nairāśa ||*

*Word for word:* murari mukunda — Murari, Mukunda; na jiyaba shrinibasa — Srinivasa (Srivasa) will not live; acharya advaita — Advaita Acharya; bhela jibana nairasha — has despaired of life

**12.3.** Murari, Mukunda, Srinivasa will not live;
Advaita Acharya has despaired of life.

নদিয়ার লোক সব কাতর হইয়া ।
ছটফট করে প্রাণ তোমা না দেখিয়া ॥

*nadiyāra loka saba kātara haiyā |*
*chaṭaphaṭa kare prāṇa tomā nā dekhiyā ||*

*Word for word:* nadiyara loka saba — all the people of Nadia; katara haiya — in anguish; chhatphat kare prana — their hearts writhe; toma na dekhiya — not seeing You

**12.4.** All the people of Nadia are in anguish —
their hearts writhe, not seeing You.

কহয়ে পরমানন্দ দন্তে তৃণ ধরি ।
এক বার নদিয়া চল প্রভু গৌরহরি ॥

*kahaye paramānanda dante tṛṇa dhari |*
*eka bāra nadiyā cala prabhu gaurahari ||*

*Word for word:* kahaye paramananda — says Paramananda; dante trina dhari — holding a straw between his teeth; eka bara — just once; nadiya chala — come to Nadia; prabhu gaurahari — Lord Gaurahari

**12.5.** Says Paramananda, holding a straw between his teeth:
"Come to Nadia just once, Lord Gaurahari!"[^05-32]

[^05-31]: Signature: "Paramananda". PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 66 (printed p. 55), 6th pallava, no. 32 ("And again — Sri
Gaurachandra"), among the padas on the messengers to Krishna in Mathura: as the gopis call Krishna back to Vraja, so the
devotees call Gaura to Nadia; MS P-R-Sa no. 916. In the 21st pallava of PK, after Madhava Ghosha's pada PK 2277 (no. 17
below), the compiler refers to this pada again: "'What have You done, Gorachand, leaving Nadia' etc. — given above."
GPT1 — p. 385, no. 7 (raga suhai); GPT2 — sect. 5.4, no. 7. On the attribution see note 1.
[^05-32]: Holding a straw between the teeth is a sign of utter humility before one who is being entreated. GPT1: "This time come
to Nadia". The devotees' wish was fulfilled in 1514/15, when the Lord came to Kuliya opposite Navadvipa (CC Madhya 1, 16;
chapter 1, no. 23; chapter 4, nos. 18–19).

## 13. Vasu Ghosha — "hari hari gorā kothā gela…" (PK 1856)
*Lila: after the sannyasa — a devotee's lament: "Had I known that Gora would leave, I would have kept Him, binding His life
to mine"; how will Gadadhara and Damodara live? In PK — in the 10th pallava ("Various separations"), immediately after
Vamshi's pada "No more shall I see…" (PK 1855; chapter 1, no. 17). According to Majumdar — one of Vasu Ghosha's padas on
the sannyasa. Raga suhai.*[^05-33]

হরি হরি গোরা কোথা গেল ।
মরমে পশিল শেল বাহির না হৈল ॥

*hari hari gorā kothā gela |*
*marame paśila śela bāhira nā haila ||*

*Word for word:* hari hari — Hari, Hari! (a cry of grief); gora kotha gela — where has Gora gone?; marame pashila shela — a spear has pierced the heart; bahira na haila — and does not come out

**13.1.** Hari, Hari! Where has Gora gone?
A spear has pierced my heart — and does not come out.

কাহারে কহিব দুখ না নিঃসরে বাণী ।
অনুখণ পড়ে মনে গোরা গুণমণি ॥

*kāhāre kahiba dukha nā niḥsare bāṇī |*
*anukhaṇa paṛe mane gorā guṇamaṇi ||*

*Word for word:* kahare kahiba dukha — to whom shall I tell my grief?; na nihsare bani — words do not come out; anukhana pare mane — He comes to mind ceaselessly; gora gunamani — Gora, the jewel of virtues

**13.2.** To whom shall I tell my grief? Words do not leave my lips;
ceaselessly I remember Gora, the jewel of virtues.

মো যদি জানিতাম গোরা যাবে রে ছাড়িয়া ।
পরাণে পরাণ দিয়া রাখিতাম বান্ধিয়া ॥

*mo yadi jānitāma gorā yābe re chāṛiyā |*
*parāṇe parāṇa diyā rākhitāma bāndhiyā ||*

*Word for word:* mo yadi janitama — if I had known; gora yabe re chhariya — that Gora would leave [us]; parane parana diya — giving life for life (heart to heart); rakhitama bandhiya — I would have kept [Him] bound

**13.3.** Had I known that Gora would leave us,
I would have kept Him, binding His life to mine.[^05-34]

গদাধর দামোদর কেমনে বাঁচিবে ।
এত দিনে বাসুঘোষ পরাণে মরিবে ॥

*gadādhara dāmodara kemane bām̐cibe |*
*eta dine bāsughoṣa parāṇe maribe ||*

*Word for word:* gadadhara damodara — Gadadhara, Damodara; kemane banchibe — how will they live?; eta dine — now at last; basughosha — Vasu Ghosha; parane maribe — will die

**13.4.** How will Gadadhara and Damodara live?
Now Vasu Ghosha will die.[^05-35]

[^05-33]: Signature: "Vasu Ghosha". PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 131 (printed p. 120), 10th pallava, no. 5. In GPT1 (p. 385, no. 8, raga
suhai) the pada is signed "Radhamohana Dasa" (a poet of the early 18th c., compiler of the *Padamrita-samudra*), but the
compiler of GPT notes that in one manuscript the signature reads "Now Vasu Ghosha will die"; PK gives Vasu's signature. The
attribution is therefore not beyond doubt.
[^05-34]: Lit. "giving life for life, I would have kept [Him] bound". MSS "ka", "kha", "cha": "jānitāṅa" (same meaning).
[^05-35]: Gadadhara is Gadadhara Pandita; Damodara is probably Damodara Pandita, the Lord's companion in Navadvipa (CC Adi 10).
MSS "ka", "kha", "cha": "…how shall I live… I shall die" (bām̐ciba, mariba). The signature is a formula of grief: the poet will
not survive the separation.

## 14. Chaitanyadasa — "mohe bihi biparīta bhela…" (PK 463)
*Lila: a devotee's remorse: Gora, the darling of his life, has gone, and the poet, having found Him, did not serve Him. In
PK — the gaura-chandrika to the section "Kalahantarita" (the heroine who has rebuffed her beloved in a quarrel and
repents); the pada is composed in the voice of such a heroine. According to Majumdar — testimony of the poet's personal
closeness to Gaura. Raga suhai.*[^05-36]

মোহে বিহি বিপরীত ভেল ।
অভিমানে মোহে উপেখি পহুঁ গেল ॥

*mohe bihi biparīta bhela |*
*abhimāne mohe upekhi pahum̐ gela ||*

*Word for word:* mohe — towards me; bihi biparita bhela — the Creator has turned against [me]; abhimane — through wounded pride; mohe upekhi — disregarding me; pahun gela — the Lord has gone

**14.1.** The Creator has turned against me:
through my wounded pride the Lord, disregarding me, has gone.[^05-37]

কি করিব কহ না উপায় ।
কেমনে পাইব সেই মোর গোরা রায় ॥

*ki kariba kaha nā upāya |*
*kemane pāiba sei mora gorā rāya ||*

*Word for word:* ki kariba — what shall I do?; kaha na upaya — tell me a way; kemane paiba — how shall I find; sei mora gora raya — that Gora Raya of mine

**14.2.** What shall I do? Tell me, what way is there?
How shall I find again my Gora Raya?

কি করিতে কি না জানি হৈল ।
পরাণ-পুতলি গোরা মোরে ছাড়ি গেল ॥

*ki karite ki nā jāni haila |*
*parāṇa-putali gorā more chāṛi gela ||*

*Word for word:* ki karite ki na jani haila — I meant one thing, and I know not what has happened; parana-putali gora — Gora, the darling of my life; more chhari gela — has gone, leaving me

**14.3.** I meant one thing — I know not what has happened:
Gora, the darling of my life, has gone, leaving me.

কে জানে যে এমন হইবে ।
আঁচলে বান্ধিতে ধন সায়রে পড়িবে ॥

*ke jāne ye emana haibe |*
*ām̐cale bāndhite dhana sāyare paṛibe ||*

*Word for word:* ke jane — who knew; ye emana haibe — that it would be so; anchale bandhite — while tying it in the end of my sari; dhana — the treasure; sayare paribe — would fall into the ocean

**14.4.** Who knew it would be so:
the treasure I was tying in the end of my sari would fall into the ocean!

চৈতন্যদাসের সেই হৈল ।
পাইয়া গৌরাঙ্গচান্দ না ভজি তেজিল ॥

*caitanyadāsera sei haila |*
*pāiyā gaurāṅgacānda nā bhaji tejila ||*

*Word for word:* chaitanyadasera — with Chaitanyadasa; sei haila — that is what happened; paiya gaurangachanda — having found Gaurangachand; na bhaji — not serving [Him]; tejila — he lost (let go)

**14.5.** So it happened with Chaitanyadasa:
having found Gaurangachand, he did not serve Him — and lost Him.[^05-38]

[^05-36]: Signature: "Chaitanyadasa". PK: vol. 1, PDF pp. 314–315 (printed pp. 303–304), the first pada of the 15th pallava,
under the heading "Another kind of kalahantarita. Sri Gaurachandra befitting it"; MS P-R-Sa no. 652. GPT1 — p. 313, no. 21
(raga suhai).
[^05-37]: The pada is composed in the voice of the kalahantarita — the heroine who in wounded pride (abhimana) has rebuffed her
beloved and now repents. The poet applies this image from Radha's lila to himself: having found Gaura, he did not serve
Him, and Gora went away (evidently the sannyasa is meant). This is the language of the gaura-chandrika, not of mundane
relations; the "wounded pride" here is the bitter self-reproach of a devotee.
[^05-38]: "Lost" (tejila, lit. "let go, gave up"). MS P-R-Sa: "Just so it happened…" (sei se); MSS "kha", "gha" in 14.3: "left me"
(mohe).

## 15. Vasu Ghosha — "gorā-guṇe prāṇa kānde ki buddhi kariba…" (PK 2280)
*Lila: after the sannyasa — the lament of Navadvipa: who else will show mercy to the fallen and, entreating, give away the
name of Hari? Without Gora all Nadia has become empty. In PK — in the 21st pallava, in the section "The longing of the
devotees". According to Majumdar — one of Vasu Ghosha's padas on the sannyasa. Raga suhai.*[^05-39]

গোরা-গুণে প্রাণ কান্দে কি বুদ্ধি করিব ।
গৌরাঙ্গ গুণের নিধি কোথা গেলে পাব ॥

*gorā-guṇe prāṇa kānde ki buddhi kariba |*
*gaurāṅga guṇera nidhi kothā gele pāba ||*

*Word for word:* gora-gune — for Gora's virtues; prana kande — the heart weeps; ki buddhi kariba — what can I devise?; gauranga gunera nidhi — Gauranga, the treasury of virtues; kotha gele paba — where shall I go to find [Him]?

**15.1.** For Gora's virtues my heart weeps — what can I devise?
Where shall I go to find Gauranga, the treasury of virtues?[^05-40]

কে আর করিবে দয়া পতিত দেখিয়া ।
দুর্লভ হরির নাম কে দিবে যাচিয়া ॥

*ke āra karibe dayā patita dekhiyā |*
*durlabha harira nāma ke dibe yāciyā ||*

*Word for word:* ke ara karibe daya — who else will show mercy; patita dekhiya — on seeing the fallen?; durlabha harira nama — the rare name of Hari; ke dibe yachiya — who will give it, entreating [us to take it]?

**15.2.** Who else will show mercy, seeing the fallen?
Who, entreating, will give the rare name of Hari?

অকিঞ্চন দেখি কেবা উঠিবে কান্দিয়া ।
গোরা বিনু শূন্য হৈল সকল নদীয়া ॥

*akiñcana dekhi kebā uṭhibe kāndiyā |*
*gorā binu śūnya haila sakala nadīyā ||*

*Word for word:* akinchana dekhi — seeing the destitute; keba uthibe kandiya — who will burst into tears?; gora binu — without Gora; shunya haila — has become empty; sakala nadiya — all Nadia

**15.3.** Who will burst into tears, seeing the destitute?
Without Gora all Nadia has become empty.[^05-41]

বাসুদেব ঘোষ কান্দে গুণ সোঙরিয়া ।
কেমনে রহিবে প্রাণ গোরা না দেখিয়া ॥

*bāsudeba ghoṣa kānde guṇa soṅariyā |*
*kemane rahibe prāṇa gorā nā dekhiyā ||*

*Word for word:* vasudeva ghosha kande — Vasudeva Ghosha weeps; guna sonariya — remembering [His] virtues; kemane rahibe prana — how will life remain?; gora na dekhiya — not seeing Gora

**15.4.** Vasudeva Ghosha weeps, remembering His virtues:
how is one to live, not seeing Gora?

[^05-39]: Signature: "Vasudeva Ghosha". PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 296 (printed p. 285), 21st pallava, no. 63, after Vasu's pada "How
many days more until I see Gorachand's face…" (PK 2279) under the common heading "Then — the longing of the devotees";
MS P-R-Sa nos. 1041 and 2384 (the pada is written in it twice); MS "kha" lacks it. GPT1 — p. 387, no. 15 (raga suhai).
Majumdar lists PK 2280 among Vasu Ghosha's padas on the sannyasa.
[^05-40]: MSS "gha", "cha": "the treasury of mercy" (dayāra nidhi).
[^05-41]: "The destitute" (akiñcana) — the humble one who has nothing but hope in the Lord. MS P-R-Sa: "Who will burst into
tears, seeing such a person? Without Gora the town of Nadia has become empty."

## 16. Madhava Ghosha — "tachu dukhe dukhī eka priya-sakhī…" (PK 2276)
*Lila: the years of separation (the Lord in Puri) — a friend of Vishnupriya, sharing her grief, as if maddened by
separation from Gaura, runs to the bank of the Ganga, to the place where the Lord used to sit, and in her raving words
seems to see Gaura in Nilachala. In PK — in the 21st pallava, after Madhava Dasa's pada on Vishnupriya's grief (PK 2275).
According to Majumdar — an imagined scene; the authorship of Madhava Ghosha for this and the next two padas is doubtful.
Raga dhanashi.*[^05-42]

তছু দুখে দুখী এক প্রিয়-সখী
গৌর-বিরহে ভোরা ।
সহিতে নারিয়া চলিল ধাইয়া
যেমত বাউরী পারা ॥

*tachu dukhe dukhī eka priya-sakhī*
*gaura-birahe bhorā |*
*sahite nāriyā calila dhāiyā*
*yemata bāurī pārā ||*

*Word for word:* tachhu dukhe dukhi — grieving with her grief; eka priya-sakhi — a dear friend; gaura-birahe bhora — overwhelmed by separation from Gaura; sahite nariya — unable to bear it; chalila dhaiya — ran off; yemata bauri para — like one gone mad

**16.1.** A dear friend, grieving with her grief,
overwhelmed by separation from Gaura,
unable to bear it, ran off
as if gone mad.[^05-43]

নদীয়া নগরে সুরধুনী-তীরে
যেখানে বসিতা পহুঁ ।
তাহাঁই যাইয়া গদগদ হৈয়া
কি কহয়ে লহু লহু ॥

*nadīyā nagare suradhunī-tīre*
*yekhāne basitā pahum̐ |*
*tāhām̐i yāiyā gadagada haiyā*
*ki kahaye lahu lahu ||*

*Word for word:* nadiya nagare — in the town of Nadia; suradhuni-tire — on the bank of the Suradhuni; yekhane basita pahun — where the Lord used to sit; tahani yaiya — going there; gadagada haiya — choked with emotion; ki kahaye lahu lahu — she softly says something

**16.2.** In the town of Nadia, on the bank of the Suradhuni,
where the Lord used to sit —
going there, in a choking voice
she softly says something.

সে সব প্রলাপ- বচন শুনিতে
পাষাণ মিলাঞা যায় ।
নীলাচল-পুরে ঐছন গৌরে
যাইয়া দেখিতে পায় ॥

*se saba pralāpa- bacana śunite*
*pāṣāṇa milāñā yāya |*
*nīlācala-pure aichana gaure*
*yāiyā dekhite pāya ||*

*Word for word:* se saba pralapa-bachana — those words of raving; shunite — on hearing; pashana milanya yaya — stone melts away; nilachala-pure — in the city of Nilachala; aichhana gaure — Gaura thus (var. yaichhana — as if); yaiya dekhite paya — having gone, she sees

**16.3.** At those raving words
even a stone would melt:
as if, having gone to Nilachala,
she sees Gaura there.[^05-44]

আঁখি ঝরঝর হিয়া গরগর
কহয়ে কান্দিয়া কথা ।
মাধব ঘোষের হিয়া বেয়াকুল
শুনিতে মরমে বেথা ॥

*ām̐khi jharajhara hiyā garagara*
*kahaye kāndiyā kathā |*
*mādhaba ghoṣera hiyā beyākula*
*śunite marame bethā ||*

*Word for word:* ankhi jharajhara — eyes streaming; hiya garagara — heart overflowing; kahaye kandiya katha — she speaks weeping; madhava ghoshera hiya — Madhava Ghosha's heart; beyakula — is distraught; shunite marame betha — hearing, there is pain deep within

**16.4.** Her eyes stream, her heart overflows —
weeping, she speaks;
Madhava Ghosha's heart is distraught:
to hear it is pain deep within.

[^05-42]: Signature: "Madhava Ghosha". PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 295 (printed p. 284), 21st pallava, no. 59; MS P-R-Sa no. 2380.
"Her" (tachu) refers to Vishnupriya, of whom the preceding pada in PK, by Madhava Dasa, "All my life I prided myself on
Gaura…" (PK 2275), speaks. GPT1 — p. 399, no. 32 (raga dhanashi), reading "your grief" (tuyā dukhe). Majumdar accepts Madhava
(Madhavananda) Ghosha, brother of Govinda and Vasu and the finest kirtana singer (CB Antya 5), as the Lord's contemporary,
but regards his padas on the sannyasa as late: PK 2276 is an imagined scene of the grief of Nadia's women, and PK 2278 was
probably written much later. The attribution of PK 2276–2278 to Madhava Ghosha is therefore doubtful.
[^05-43]: "As if gone mad" (yemata bāurī pārā) — the madness of grief in separation from Gaura, that is, of a devotee's prema.
[^05-44]: MSS "ka", "kha", "gha", "cha" and GPT1 read "yaichana" — "as if"; the main text of PK has "aichana" ("[Gaura] thus").

## 17. Madhava Ghosha — "abalā se biṣṇupriyā tuyā guṇa soṅariyā…" (PK 2277)
*Lila: the years of separation — the poet addresses the Lord: Vishnupriya, remembering His virtues, lies unconscious, her
friends holding cotton to her nostrils; the people of Nadia, old Shachi and the companions are barely alive — "Come to
Nadia, O best of the knowers of rasa!" According to Majumdar — Madhava Ghosha's pada on the grief of Shachi and
Vishnupriya. Raga pahida.*[^05-45]

অবলা সে বিষ্ণুপ্রিয়া তুয়া গুণ সোঙরিয়া
মুরছি পড়ল খিতি-তলে ।
চৌদিগে সখীগণ হেরি করে রোদন
তুলা ধরি নাসার উপরে ॥

*abalā se biṣṇupriyā tuyā guṇa soṅariyā*
*murachi paṛala khiti-tale |*
*caudige sakhīgaṇa heri kare rodana*
*tulā dhari nāsāra upare ||*

*Word for word:* abala se vishnupriya — the helpless Vishnupriya; tuya guna sonariya — remembering Your virtues; murachhi parala khiti-tale — fell fainting to the ground; chaudige sakhigana — her friends all around; heri kare rodana — seeing [this], weep; tula dhari nasara upare — holding cotton to her nostrils

**17.1.** The helpless Vishnupriya, remembering Your virtues,
fell unconscious to the ground;
her friends around, seeing this, weep,
holding a wisp of cotton to her nostrils.[^05-46]

তুয়া বিরহানলে অন্তর জরজর
দেহ ছাড়া হইল পরাণি ।
নদীয়া-নিবাসী যত তারা ভেল মুরছিত
না দেখিয়া তুয়া মুখখানি ॥

*tuyā birahānale antara jarajara*
*deha chāṛā haila parāṇi |*
*nadīyā-nibāsī yata tārā bhela murachita*
*nā dekhiyā tuyā mukhakhāni ||*

*Word for word:* tuya birahanale — in the fire of separation from You; antara jarajara — her heart is worn out; deha chhara haila parani — life has [all but] left her body; nadiya-nibasi yata — all the dwellers of Nadia; tara bhela murachhita — have fainted; na dekhiya tuya mukhakhani — not seeing Your face

**17.2.** In the fire of separation from You her heart is worn out —
life barely stays in her body.
All the dwellers of Nadia have fainted,
not seeing Your face.

শচী বৃদ্ধ আধ-মরা দেহে প্রাণ নাহি তারা
তার প্রতি নাহি তোর দয়া ।
নদীয়ার সঙ্গিগণ কেমনে ধরিবে প্রাণ
কেমনে ছাড়িলা তার মায়া ॥

*śacī bṛddha ādha-marā dehe prāṇa nāhi tārā*
*tāra prati nāhi tora dayā |*
*nadīyāra saṅgigaṇa kemane dharibe prāṇa*
*kemane chāṛilā tāra māyā ||*

*Word for word:* shachi briddha — old Shachi; adha-mara — half-dead; dehe prana nahi tara — there is no life in her body; tara prati nahi tora daya — You have no pity for her; nadiyara sangigana — the companions in Nadia; kemane dharibe prana — how will they keep alive?; kemane chharila tara maya — how did You give up Your affection for them?

**17.3.** Old Shachi is half-dead — there is no life in her body —
and You have no pity for her!
How will Your friends in Nadia keep alive?
How did You give up Your affection for them?[^05-47]

যত সহচর তোর সভাই বিরহে ভোর
শ্বাস রহে দরশন আশে ।
হেদে হে রসিকবর চলহ নদীয়া-পুর
কহে দীন মাধব ঘোষে ॥

*yata sahacara tora sabhāi birahe bhora*
*śvāsa rahe daraśana āśe |*
*hede he rasikabara calaha nadīyā-pura*
*kahe dīna mādhaba ghoṣe ||*

*Word for word:* yata sahachara tora — all Your companions; sabhai birahe bhora — all are overwhelmed by separation; shvasa rahe darashana ashe — their breath remains in the hope of seeing [You]; hede he rasikabara — O best of the knowers of rasa!; chalaha nadiya-pura — come to the town of Nadia; kahe dina madhava ghoshe — says the lowly Madhava Ghosha

**17.4.** All Your companions are overwhelmed by separation:
their breath is held only by the hope of seeing You.
O best of the knowers of rasa, come to the town of Nadia! —
says the lowly Madhava Ghosha.[^05-48]

[^05-45]: Signature: "Madhava Ghosha". PK: vol. 3, PDF pp. 295–296 (printed pp. 284–285), 21st pallava, no. 60; MS P-R-Sa
no. 2381. GPT1 — p. 400, no. 33 (raga pahida); GPT2 — sect. 5.4, no. 33. Majumdar cites the pada as "PK 1277" (a misprint
for 2277); on the doubts about the attribution see note 42. Immediately after this pada the compiler of PK refers to
Paramananda's pada "What have You done, Gorachand, leaving Nadia" (no. 12).
[^05-46]: Cotton is held to the nostrils to see whether there is any breath. "Life barely stays in her body" (17.2) — lit.
"life has become separate from the body": a poetic exaggeration of a swoon; MS P-R-Sa: "[separation] has separated [her]
life".
[^05-47]: The reproach "no pity" and the familiar address (tora) are the language of grief and intimacy, not a judgement on the
Lord: in leaving His home the Lord did not abandon His own (cf. CC Madhya 3 and 16 — the meetings with Shachi in Shantipura
and Kuliya). "Affection" is in the original "maya" (māyā) in its everyday Bengali sense of "tender attachment, love", not
the illusory energy: the Lord is not subject to maya. MS P-R-Sa has "Shachi, who…" (śacīya ye) instead of "old Shachi".
[^05-48]: "Knower of rasa" (rasikabara) — an address to Gaura as to Krishna. MSS: "the breath flows" (vahe; P-R-Sa and GPT1), "the hope
of touching [You]" (paraśana; "gha"), "this Madhava" (P-R-Sa).

## 18. Madhava Ghosha — "gaurāṅga jhāṭa kari calaha nadīyā…" (PK 2278)
*Lila: the years of separation — the poet begs Gauranga to come quickly to Nadia: Vishnupriya, remembering His former
love, has fainted; Nadia and the companions weep in the dust. According to Majumdar — probably written long after the
sannyasa. Raga shri.*[^05-49]

গৌরাঙ্গ ঝাট করি চলহ নদীয়া ।
প্রাণ-হীন হইল অবলা বিষ্ণুপ্রিয়া ॥

*gaurāṅga jhāṭa kari calaha nadīyā |*
*prāṇa-hīna haila abalā biṣṇupriyā ||*

*Word for word:* gauranga — O Gauranga; jhata kari — quickly; chalaha nadiya — come to Nadia; prana-hina haila — has become lifeless; abala vishnupriya — the helpless Vishnupriya

**18.1.** Gauranga, come quickly to Nadia:
the helpless Vishnupriya is as if lifeless.[^05-50]

তোমার চরিত যত পুরব-পিরীত ।
সোঙরি সোঙরি এবে ভেল মুরছিত ॥

*tomāra carita yata puraba-pirīta |*
*soṅari soṅari ebe bhela murachita ||*

*Word for word:* tomara charita yata — all Your deeds; puraba-pirita — the former love; sonari sonari — remembering again and again; ebe bhela murachhita — she has now fainted

**18.2.** All Your deeds, the former love —
remembering them again and again, she has now fainted.

সে হেন নদীয়াপুর সে সব সঙ্গিয়া ।
ধূলায় পড়িয়া কান্দে তোমা না দেখিয়া ॥

*se hena nadīyāpura se saba saṅgiyā |*
*dhūlāya paṛiyā kānde tomā nā dekhiyā ||*

*Word for word:* se hena nadiyapura — that same town of Nadia; se saba sangiya — all those companions; dhulay pariya kande — weep, fallen in the dust; toma na dekhiya — not seeing You

**18.3.** That same town of Nadia, all those companions
weep, fallen in the dust, not seeing You.

কহয়ে মাধব ঘোষ শুন গৌরহরি ।
তিলেক বিলম্বে আমি আগে যাব মরি ॥

*kahaye mādhaba ghoṣa śuna gaurahari |*
*tileka bilambe āmi āge yāba mari ||*

*Word for word:* kahaye madhava ghosha — says Madhava Ghosha; shuna gaurahari — hear, Gaurahari; tileka bilambe — if You delay a moment; ami age yaba mari — I shall die first

**18.4.** Says Madhava Ghosha: "Listen, Gaurahari:
delay but a moment — and I shall die first."

[^05-49]: Signature: "Madhava Ghosha". PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 296 (printed p. 285), 21st pallava, no. 61; MS P-R-Sa no. 2382.
GPT1 — p. 400, no. 34 (raga shri). Majumdar supposes that the pada was written long after the sannyasa: hardly anyone in
the Lord's lifetime would have called Him back like this, and the mention of Vishnupriya's "former love" seems to him
discourteous; this is only a conjecture. On the doubts about the attribution see note 42. In the stage-1 catalogue the
first line was read "gaurāṅga bāṭa kari" — the scan has "jhāṭa kari" ("quickly").
[^05-50]: "As if lifeless" (prāṇa-hīna) — lit. "has lost life": an exaggeration of a swoon, as in 17.2. "The former love" (18.2)
is the intimacy of the years of the Lord's household life; the love and grief of Vishnupriya, the Lord's eternal companion,
are revered by the Gaudiya tradition as pure prema.

## 19. Kanu Dasa — "āre mora pahum̐ nitāicām̐da…" (PK 2327)
*Lila: Nityananda in Gauda (after 1515) — He sings and dances, absorbed in bhava, sprinkles the suffering people with His
glance, tells of His Brother; His fair body is covered with thrills like a kadamba flower; the devotees sing around Him. In
PK — in the 22nd pallava ("Description of the virtues of Sri Nityananda"); in KGC — in the 10th kshanada. According to
Majumdar — a pada on Nityananda's preaching in Gauda. Raga deshaga.*[^05-51]

আরে মোর পহুঁ নিতাইচাঁদ ।
ঘরে ঘরে দিল প্রেমের ফাঁদ ॥

*āre mora pahum̐ nitāicām̐da |*
*ghare ghare dila premera phām̐da ||*

*Word for word:* are mora pahun — O my Lord; nitaichanda — Nitaichand; ghare ghare — in every house; dila premera phanda — has set the snare of prema

**19.1.** O my Lord Nitaichand!
In every house He has set the snare of prema.

তাপিত অখিল সকল জনে ।
সিঞ্চিত করল নয়ন-কোণে ॥

*tāpita akhila sakala jane |*
*siñcita karala nayana-koṇe ||*

*Word for word:* tapita akhila sakala jane — all the scorched people everywhere; sinchita karala — He sprinkled; nayana-kone — with the corners of His eyes (His glance)

**19.2.** All the people scorched by the world's heat
He has sprinkled with the corners of His eyes.[^05-52]

অপার করুণা গৌড়-দেশে ।
নাচিয়া বুলয়ে ভাব-আবেশে ॥

*apāra karuṇā gauṛa-deśe |*
*nāciyā bulaye bhāba-ābeśe ||*

*Word for word:* apara karuna — boundless mercy; gauda-deshe — in the land of Gauda; nachiya bulaye — dancing, He wanders; bhaba-abeshe — absorbed in bhava

**19.3.** Boundless mercy in the land of Gauda:
He dances and wanders, absorbed in bhava.

গদগদ কহে ভাইয়ার কথা ।
প্রেম-জলে ডুবে নয়ন রাতা ॥

*gadagada kahe bhāiyāra kathā |*
*prema-jale ḍube nayana rātā ||*

*Word for word:* gadagada kahe — in a choked voice He tells; bhaiyara katha — of [His] Brother; prema-jale dube — drown in the waters of prema; nayana rata — the reddened eyes

**19.4.** In a choking voice He tells of His Brother;
His reddened eyes drown in the waters of prema.[^05-53]

আরকত গোরা সুন্দর-তনু ।
পুলক কদম্ব-কেশর জনু ॥

*ārakata gorā sundara-tanu |*
*pulaka kadamba-keśara janu ||*

*Word for word:* arakata — reddish-glowing; gora sundara-tanu — fair, beautiful body; pulaka — the thrills; kadamba-keshara janu — like the filaments of a kadamba flower

**19.5.** His fair, beautiful body glows reddish,
the thrills like the filaments of a kadamba.

বিবিধ ভূষণে ভূষিত অঙ্গ ।
ভকত মিলিয়া গায়ত রঙ্গ ॥

*bibidha bhūṣaṇe bhūṣita aṅga |*
*bhakata miliyā gāyata raṅga ||*

*Word for word:* bibidha bhushane — with various ornaments; bhushita anga — the body is adorned; bhakata miliya — the devotees together; gayata ranga — sing joyfully

**19.6.** His body is adorned with various ornaments;
the devotees together sing joyfully.

ঢুলিতে ঢুলিতে কত না ভাতি ।
কমল-চরণে খঞ্জন-গতি ॥

*ḍhulite ḍhulite kata nā bhāti |*
*kamala-caraṇe khañjana-gati ||*

*Word for word:* dhulite dhulite — swaying; kata na bhati — in how many ways!; kamala-charane — with lotus feet; khanjana-gati — with the gait of a wagtail

**19.7.** Swaying — in how many ways!
His lotus feet step like a wagtail.[^05-54]

করুণা শুনিয়া বাঢ়ল আশ ।
প্রেম মাগে পদে এ কানুদাস ॥

*karuṇā śuniyā bāṛhala āśa |*
*prema māge pade e kānudāsa ||*

*Word for word:* karuna shuniya — hearing of [His] mercy; badhala asha — hope has grown; prema mage pade — at [His] feet begs for prema; e kanudasa — this Kanudasa

**19.8.** Hearing of His mercy, hope has grown:
at His feet this Kanudasa begs for prema.

[^05-51]: Signature: "Kanudasa". PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 313 (printed p. 302), 22nd pallava, no. 34; MS P-R-Sa no. 2431. KGC — 10th
kshanada, no. 2 (pp. 76–77; raga shri), with a different order of couplets (19.7 after 19.3) and the signature "Kanu
Dasa"; GPT1 — p. 431, no. 58 (raga barari); GPT2 — sect. 6.1, no. 58. Majumdar identifies Kanudasa and Kanurama Dasa (their
language is the same) with Kanu Thakura — son of Purushottama Dasa and grandson of Sadashiva Kaviraja, of Nityananda's
branch (CC Adi 11). Nityananda preached in Gauda at the Lord's command after 1515 (CC Madhya 15; CB Antya 5).
[^05-52]: The world's heat is the threefold suffering; Nityananda's glance is the cool water of mercy.
[^05-53]: "Brother" (bhāiyā) is Gauranga: telling of Him, Nityananda weeps. Cf. the cry "Brother, brother!" (bhāiyā re) in padas of
the same pallava of PK (2319, 2326).
[^05-54]: The wagtail (khanjana) is an image of a graceful, light gait. MSS "ka", "kha", "cha", P-R-Sa in 19.3: "wanders"
(vulena — honorific form); KGC and GPT1: "absorbed in prema", "absorbed in bhava".

## 20. Kanurama Dasa — "dayā kara more nitāi dayā kara more…" (PK 2321)
*Lila: a prayer to Nityananda: You gave prema to all without distinction — why then am I unhappy? You are the Lord of our
family. In PK — in the 22nd pallava ("Description of the virtues of Sri Nityananda"). According to Majumdar, "the Lord of
the family" points to three generations of the poet's family at Nityananda's feet. Raga patamanjari.*[^05-55]

দয়া কর মোরে নিতাই দয়া কর মোরে ।
অগতির গতি নিতাই সাধু লোকে বোলে ॥

*dayā kara more nitāi dayā kara more |*
*agatira gati nitāi sādhu loke bole ||*

*Word for word:* daya kara more nitai — have mercy on me, Nitai; agatira gati nitai — Nitai is the refuge of those without refuge; sadhu loke bole — say the saintly people

**20.1.** Have mercy on me, Nitai, have mercy on me!
Nitai is the refuge of those without refuge, say the saints.

জয় প্রেম-ভক্তি-দাতা পতাকা তোমার ।
উত্তম অধম কিছু না কৈল বিচার ॥

*jaya prema-bhakti-dātā patākā tomāra |*
*uttama adhama kichu nā kaila bicāra ||*

*Word for word:* jaya prema-bhakti-data — "Glory to the Giver of prema-bhakti!"; pataka tomara — is Your banner; uttama adhama — the high and the low; kichhu na kaila bichara — You made no distinction at all

**20.2.** "Glory to the Giver of prema-bhakti!" proclaims Your banner;
You made no distinction at all between high and low.[^05-56]

প্রেম-দানে জগ-জীবের মন কৈলা সুখী ।
তুমি যদি দয়ার ঠাকুর আমি কেনে দুখী ॥

*prema-dāne jaga-jībera mana kailā sukhī |*
*tumi yadi dayāra ṭhākura āmi kene dukhī ||*

*Word for word:* prema-dane — by the gift of prema; jaga-jibera mana — the hearts of the world's beings; kaila sukhi — You made happy; tumi yadi dayara thakura — if You are the Lord of mercy; ami kene dukhi — why am I unhappy?

**20.3.** By the gift of prema You made happy the hearts of all beings in the world;
if You are the Lord of mercy, why am I unhappy?

কানুরাম দাসে বোলে কি বলিব আমি ।
এ বড় ভরসা মোর কুলের ঠাকুর তুমি ॥

*kānurāma dāse bole ki baliba āmi |*
*e baṛa bharasā mora kulera ṭhākura tumi ||*

*Word for word:* kanurama dase bole — says Kanurama Dasa; ki baliba ami — what can I say?; e bara bharasa mora — this is my great hope; kulera thakura tumi — You are the Lord of our family

**20.4.** Says Kanurama Dasa: what can I say?
This is my great hope: You are the Lord of our family.[^05-57]

[^05-55]: Signature: "Kanurama Dasa". PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 311 (printed p. 300), 22nd pallava, no. 28; MS P-R-Sa no. 2425. GPT1 —
p. 431, no. 57 (raga patamanjari), immediately before PK 2327 (no. 19). In the stage-1 catalogue the first line had not been
recognized (KD-009). Majumdar: Kanurama Dasa = Kanudasa = Kanu Thakura; "the Lord of our family" — the poet's grandfather
Sadashiva Kaviraja, his father Purushottama Dasa and he himself — three generations at Nityananda's feet.
[^05-56]: "Banner" (patākā; MSS "ka", "kha": patakā) — the image of Nityananda as a victorious king whose banner proclaims the giving
of prema. GPT1: "…You make no distinction".
[^05-57]: MSS in 20.3: "the hearts of the world's people" (jaga janera — "ka"; jagat jībera — "kha"); "You are the Lord of mercy" (without
"if" — "ka"); "You, such a Lord of mercy — why am I…" ("kha", "cha").

# Chapter 6. Kirtanas and Gaura's Form in Navadvipa, the Lord's Ecstasy, Nityananda, Separation, and Nilachala

*Padas of contemporaries known from the *Padakalpataru* (PK), the *Bhakti-ratnakara* (BR) and the
*Kshanada-gita-chintamani* (KGC), in the order of the lilas: the Navadvipa kirtana through the eyes of Vasu Ramananda;
praise of the Gaura-avatara (Narahari, Yadunatha Dasa); Gaura's form (Shankara Ghosha, Vasudeva Datta, Ramananda); the
kirtana festival in Advaita's house (Vamshivadana); the Lord's dance in kirtana (Chaitanyadasa, Narahari, Ramananda); the
