Lord's ecstatic moods (Yadunatha Dasa, Vamshidasa); pastimes on the Ganga — the boat and the swing (Ramananda);
Nityananda's dance in Srivasa's courtyard (Shankara Ghosha); Navadvipa after the sannyasa (Murari, Madhavi Dasa); kirtana
and the festival of colours in Nilachala (Ramananda, Madhavi Dasa); and the poet's prayer (Ramananda). The text follows PK, BR, KGC and the
*Gaura-pada-tarangini* (GPT1 — 1st ed., 1903; GPT2 — 2nd ed., 1934); the Bengali original, variants and word-for-word
translation are in the full version of the book.*

## 1. Vasu Ramananda — "caudige gobinda-dhvani śuni pahum̐ hāse…" (BR, p. 952; KGC 29.1)
*Lila: a kirtana in Navadvipa: on every side the cry "Govinda!" resounds; the Lord laughs and dances together with
Nityananda; Govinda, Madhava and Vasu (the Ghosha brothers) and Mukunda sing. Narahari Chakravarti cites the pada in the
*Bhakti-ratnakara* among the testimonies to the Navadvipa kirtanas. According to Majumdar it is the pada of an eyewitness
of the Navadvipa kirtana (1509); from the order of the names "Govinda — Madhava — Vasu" he infers that Govinda Ghosha was
the eldest. Raga dhanashi (BR), mangala (KGC, GPT).*[^06-1]

চৌদিগে গোবিন্দধ্বনি শুনি পহুঁ হাসে ।
কম্পিত অধরে গোরা গদ গদ ভাষে ॥

*caudige gobindadhvani śuni pahum̐ hāse |*
*kampita adhare gorā gada gada bhāṣe ||*

*Word for word:* caudige — on every side; gobinda-dhvani — the cry "Govinda!"; śuni — hearing; pahum̐ hāse — the Lord laughs; kampita adhare — with trembling lips; gorā — Gora (Gaura); gada gada bhāṣe — speaks falteringly

**1.1.** On every side — "Govinda!"; hearing it, the Lord laughs;
with trembling lips Gora speaks in a faltering voice.[^06-2]

নাচয়ে গৌরাঙ্গ যার সঙ্গে নিত্যানন্দ ।
অবনী ভাসল প্রেমে বাঢ়ল আনন্দ ॥

*nācaye gaurāṅga yāra saṅge nityānanda |*
*abanī bhāsala preme bāṛhala ānanda ||*

*Word for word:* nācaye gaurāṅga — Gauranga dances; yāra saṅge nityānanda — with whom [dances] Nityananda; abanī bhāsala preme — the earth is flooded with prema; bāṛhala ānanda — bliss swelled

**1.2.** Gauranga dances, and with Him Nityananda;
the earth is flooded with prema, and bliss has swelled.

গোবিন্দ মাধব বাসু গায়েন মুকুন্দ ।
ভুলিল কীর্তনরসে পায়া নিজবৃন্দ ॥

*gobinda mādhaba bāsu gāyena mukunda |*
*bhulila kīrtanarase pāyā nijabṛnda ||*

*Word for word:* gobinda mādhaba bāsu — Govinda, Madhava, Vasu (the Ghosha brothers); gāyena mukunda — and Mukunda sings; bhulila — He forgot [Himself]; kīrtana-rase — in the taste of kirtana; pāyā (= pāiyā) nija-bṛnda — having found His own (companions)

**1.3.** Govinda, Madhava, Vasu and Mukunda sing;
having found His own, He forgot Himself in the taste of kirtana.[^06-3]

রঙ্গিয়া সঙ্গিয়া সে অমিয়া-রসে ভোর ।
বসু রামানন্দ তাহে লুবধ চকোর ॥

*raṅgiyā saṅgiyā se amiyā-rase bhora |*
*basu rāmānanda tāhe lubadha cakora ||*

*Word for word:* raṅgiyā — joyful; saṅgiyā — companions; se amiyā-rase bhora — are drunk with the nectarean taste; basu rāmānanda — Vasu Ramananda; tāhe — in this; lubadha cakora — a thirsting chakora

**1.4.** The joyful companions are drunk with the nectarean taste,
and Vasu Ramananda in this is a thirsting chakora.[^06-4]

[^06-1]: Signature: "Vasu Ramananda". BR, 12th wave: 1913 ed. (Murshidabad), p. 952 ("again dhanashi"; the 1912 ed. the
same), 1960 ed. vv. 3426–3429, 2006 ed. vv. 3426–3429; in BR the pada stands in a series of padas on the Navadvipa
kirtana, near the pada of Chaitanyadasa (below, no. 10). A second recension: KGC, 29th kshanada (shukla-chaturdashi), no. 1
(pp. 229–230, raga mangala); GPT1 — p. 270, no. 73 (Majumdar's "p. 27" is evidently a misprint); GPT2 — sect. 4.2, no. 73.
In it the first and the last half-lines agree, but the middle differs (see note 3 and VAR); Majumdar considered the GPT
text corrupt. The pada is not in PK. Majumdar: Vasu Ramananda of Kulinagrama, a descendant of Maladhara Vasu, was a
contemporary of the Lord (CC Madhya 15).
[^06-2]: "Govinda!" (govinda-dhvani) — the name of Krishna sung in kirtana; perhaps also a hint at the lead singer Govinda
Ghosha. Gora is Gaura. "Trembling lips… faltering voice" are signs of ecstasy (sattvika-bhavas).
[^06-3]: "Having found His own" (pāyā = pāiyā nija-bṛnda) — His companions. In KGC and GPT, instead of 1.2–1.3: "Splendidly
Gauranga dances, and with Him Nityananda; the earth is flooded with prema, Ramananda sings. To Mukunda, Murari, Vasu He
says: 'Come here!' — for your virtues the Darling of [our] life weeps" (GPT: "Murari, Mukunda, come…"); and instead of the
first line of 1.4: "All the other devotees are drunk with bliss". The double mention of Ramananda (in 1.2 and in the
signature) argues for the BR recension.
[^06-4]: The chakora is a bird which, by poetic convention, feeds on moonlight: the poet greedily drinks the nectar of Gaura's
moonlike face.

## 2. Narahari — "anupāma gorā-abatāra…" (PK 2288)
*Praise of the Gaura-avatara: the Lord spread through all lands the taste of ninefold bhakti, making no distinction of
caste; in the age of Kali, where people sin, the holy name easily carries them across — what in other ages was attained
with great toil through sacrifice, japa, meditation and worship. In PK it stands in the 21st pallava, next to padas on
Gaura the sannyasi. Raga varadi.*[^06-5]

অনুপাম গোরা-অবতার ।
নবধা ভকতি-রস বিস্তারিলা সব দেশ
না করিলা জাতির বিচার ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*anupāma gorā-abatāra |*
*nabadhā bhakati-rasa bistārilā saba deśa*
*nā karilā jātira bicāra || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* anupāma — peerless; gorā-abatāra — the descent of Gora; nabadhā bhakati-rasa — the taste of ninefold bhakti; bistārilā saba deśa — He spread through all lands; nā karilā jātira bicāra — made no distinction of caste

**2.1.** *(Refrain)* Peerless is the descent of Gora!
The taste of ninefold bhakti He spread through all lands,
making no distinction of caste.[^06-6]

এমন ঠাকুর ভজ দূর কর সব কাজ
ছাড় সব মিছা অভিলাষ ।
চৈতন্যচাঁদের গুণে আলো কৈল ত্রিভুবনে
অনায়াসে হৈল পরকাশ ॥

*emana ṭhākura bhaja dūra kara saba kāja*
*chāṛa saba michā abhilāṣa |*
*caitanyacām̐dera guṇe ālo kaila tribhubane*
*anāyāse haila parakāśa ||*

*Word for word:* emana ṭhākura bhaja — worship such a Lord; dūra kara saba kāja — cast aside all concerns; chāṛa saba michā abhilāṣa — give up all false desires; caitanya-cām̐dera guṇe — by the virtues of Chaitanyachand; ālo kaila tribhubane — the three worlds were lit; anāyāse haila parakāśa — effortlessly He was manifest

**2.2.** Worship such a Lord, cast aside all [other] concerns,
give up all false desires.
By the virtues of Chaitanyachand the three worlds are lit —
effortlessly He revealed Himself.

চৈতন্য-কলপতরু অখিল-জীবের গুরু
গোলোক-বৈভব সব সঙ্গে ।
জীবেরে মলিন দেখি হৈয়া সকরুণ-আঁখি
হরি-নাম বিলাইল রঙ্গে ॥

*caitanya-kalapataru akhila-jībera guru*
*goloka-baibhaba saba saṅge |*
*jībere malina dekhi haiyā sakaruṇa-ām̐khi*
*hari-nāma bilāila raṅge ||*

*Word for word:* caitanya-kalapataru — Chaitanya, the wish-fulfilling tree; akhila-jībera guru — the guru of all beings; goloka-baibhaba saba saṅge — all the splendour of Goloka with Him; jībere malina dekhi — seeing the beings defiled; haiyā sakaruṇa-ām̐khi — with compassionate eyes; hari-nāma bilāila raṅge — joyfully gave out the name of Hari

**2.3.** Chaitanya is a wish-fulfilling tree, the guru of all living beings;
with Him is all the splendour of Goloka.
Seeing the living beings defiled, with compassionate eyes
He joyfully gave out the name of Hari.

যজ্ঞ জপ ধ্যান পূজা অন্য যুগে যত প্রজা
সাধিলেক অতি বড় দুখে ।
এই যে কলি-যুগ-নরে যত পাপ তাই করে
নাম লৈয়া তরি গেল সুখে ॥

*yajña japa dhyāna pūjā anya yuge yata prajā*
*sādhileka ati baṛa dukhe |*
*ei ye kali-yuga-nare yata pāpa tāi kare*
*nāma laiyā tari gela sukhe ||*

*Word for word:* yajña japa dhyāna pūjā — sacrifice, japa, meditation, worship; anya yuge yata prajā — all the people of other ages; sādhileka ati baṛa dukhe — accomplished with very great toil; ei ye kali-yuga-nare — these people of the Kali age; yata pāpa tāi kare — however much sin they commit; nāma laiyā tari gela sukhe — taking the name, crossed over with ease

**2.4.** Sacrifice, japa, meditation, worship — all that people did in other ages
they accomplished with very great toil.
But these people of the age of Kali, however much they sin —
taking the name, they crossed over with ease.[^06-7]

করুণা-বিগ্রহ সার তুলনা কি দিব আর
পতিতের পূরাইল আশ ।
কিছু না বুঝিয়া চিতে কান্দিয়া কান্দিয়া পথে
গুণ গায় নরহরি দাস ॥

*karuṇā-bigraha sāra tulanā ki diba āra*
*patitera pūrāila āśa |*
*kichu nā bujhiyā cite kāndiyā kāndiyā pathe*
*guṇa gāya narahari dāsa ||*

*Word for word:* karuṇā-bigraha sāra — the essence, compassion embodied; tulanā ki diba āra — with whom else can He be compared?; patitera pūrāila āśa — fulfilled the hopes of the fallen; kichu nā bujhiyā cite — understanding nothing in his heart; kāndiyā kāndiyā pathe — weeping and weeping on the road; guṇa gāya narahari dāsa — Narahari Dasa sings [His] virtues

**2.5.** He is the essence, compassion embodied; with whom else can He be compared?
He fulfilled the hopes of the fallen.
Understanding nothing in his heart, weeping and weeping on the road,
Narahari Dasa sings His virtues.[^06-8]

[^06-5]: Signature: "Narahari Dasa". PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 299 (printed p. 288), 21st pallava, no. 71 (mark "॥৭১॥২২৮৮॥"); raga
varadi; MS P-R-Sa no. 2392. GPT1 — p. 28, no. 5 (raga varadi); GPT2 — sect. 1.3, no. 5. In Ray's index of poets it is
among the padas of Narahari. Majumdar does not discuss this pada; its simple Bengali without heaped ornament fits his
criteria for the genuine padas of Narahari Sarakara, but the attribution (Sarakara or Narahari Chakravarti) is unproven.
[^06-6]: The nine forms of bhakti — hearing, chanting, remembering, etc. (Bhag. 7.5.23–24). "Making no distinction of caste"
— cf. CC Adi 7 on the distribution of prema to all without discrimination. GPT: "spreading [it] with the taste of bhakti
through all lands, He made no distinction of caste".
[^06-7]: Cf. Bhag. 12.3.52: what was attained in Satya-yuga by meditation, in Treta by sacrifice, in Dvapara by worship, is
attained in Kali-yuga by chanting the name of Hari. GPT1 in 2.4: "but in this darkness of Kali, however much people sin —
taking the name, they cross over with ease".
[^06-8]: "Understanding nothing in his heart" — the poet's humility: he cannot grasp the Lord's greatness and only weeps as
he sings. MS P-R-Sa: "weeping, weeping"; "with whom can He be compared" (tāra for āra).

## 3. Narahari (?) — "pāsarā nā yāya āmāra gorācām̐dera līlā…" (PK 2344)
*Praise of Gaura: the pastimes of Gorachand cannot be forgotten — by His virtues beasts and birds weep and stones melt;
the name inaccessible to Brahma He gave out to the three worlds. In PK the pada has no signature (its last line speaks of
Nityananda); in GPT it bears the signature of Narahari Dasa. In PK it stands in the 25th pallava ("Description of the form
and virtues of Sri Chaitanya and Nityananda"). Raga vibhasa.*[^06-9]

পাসরা না যায় আমার গোরাচাঁদের লীলা ।
যাহার গুণে পশুপাখী ঝুরে সদা দুটি আঁখি
গলিয়া গলিয়া পড়ে শিলা ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*pāsarā nā yāya āmāra gorācām̐dera līlā |*
*yāhāra guṇe paśupākhī jhure sadā duṭi ām̐khi*
*galiyā galiyā paṛe śilā || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* pāsarā nā yāya — cannot be forgotten; āmāra gorācām̐dera līlā — the pastimes of my Gorachand; yāhāra guṇe — by whose virtues; paśu-pākhī — beasts and birds; jhure sadā duṭi ām̐khi — ever weep from both eyes; galiyā galiyā paṛe śilā — stones melt and melt

**3.1.** *(Refrain)* I cannot forget the pastimes of my Gorachand!
By His virtues beasts and birds ever weep from both eyes,
and stones melt and melt.

যাহার নামের লাগি মহেশ হইলা যোগী
বিরিঞ্চি ভাবয়ে অনুক্ষণে ।
ব্রহ্মার দুর্লভ নাম সুলভ করিয়া পহু
যাচিয়া দেয়ল ত্রিভুবনে ॥

*yāhāra nāmera lāgi maheśa hailā yogī*
*biriñci bhābaye anukṣaṇe |*
*brahmāra durlabha nāma sulabha kariyā pahu*
*yāciyā deyala tribhubane ||*

*Word for word:* yāhāra nāmera lāgi — for the sake of whose name; maheśa hailā yogī — Mahesha (Shiva) became a yogi; biriñci bhābaye anukṣaṇe — Virinchi (Brahma) meditates incessantly; brahmāra durlabha nāma — the name hard for Brahma to obtain; sulabha kariyā pahum̐ — the Lord, making it easy to obtain; yāciyā deyala tribhubane — entreating, gave it to the three worlds

**3.2.** For the sake of His name Mahesha became a yogi,
Virinchi meditates [on Him] incessantly.
The name inaccessible even to Brahma the Lord made easy to obtain —
and Himself, entreating, gave it to the three worlds.[^06-10]

গৌরাঙ্গ-অঙ্গ শোভে পুলক-কদম্ব তাহে
অপরূপ শ্রীঅঙ্গের শোভা ।
আনন্দে বিভোর ঠাকুর নিত্যানন্দ
দেখিয়া কনকের আভা ॥

*gaurāṅga-aṅga śobhe pulaka-kadamba tāhe*
*aparūpa śrīaṅgera śobhā |*
*ānande bibhora ṭhākura nityānanda*
*dekhiyā kanakera ābhā ||*

*Word for word:* gaurāṅga-aṅga śobhe — Gauranga's body shines; pulaka-kadamba tāhe — on it hair standing on end like kadamba blossoms; aparūpa śrī-aṅgera śobhā — wondrous the beauty of the holy body; ānande bibhora — lost in bliss; ṭhākura nityānanda — Thakura Nityananda; dekhiyā kanakera ābhā — seeing the golden radiance

**3.3.** Gauranga's body shines, and on it the hair stands on end like kadamba blossoms:
wondrous is the beauty of His holy body!
In bliss Thakura Nityananda is lost to Himself,
seeing that golden radiance.[^06-11]

[^06-9]: PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 319 (printed p. 308), 25th pallava, no. 13 (mark "॥১৩॥২৩৪৪॥"), headed "again in another way"; raga
vibhasa; MS P-R-Sa no. 2448. There is no signature in PK. GPT1 — p. 28, no. 7, and GPT2 — sect. 1.3, no. 7 (both raga
vibhasa) give the last line with a signature: "In bliss Narahari Dasa is lost to himself, seeing that golden radiance".
The PK line is shorter than the tripadi metre requires (one member is missing), while the GPT line fits it; perhaps PK
preserved a line in which the poet's name was lost. The attribution to Narahari (still less to Sarakara) is unproven.
[^06-10]: Mahesha is Shiva; Virinchi is Brahma. "Entreating" (yāciyā) — the Lord Himself offers the name without waiting to be
asked (cf. CC Adi 3).
[^06-11]: Hair standing on end "like kadamba blossoms" is one of the sattvika-bhavas. MSS: "on the body of holy Gauranga"
("ka").

## 4. Yadunatha Dasa — "aparūpa cām̐da udaya nadiyāpure…" (PK 2191)
*Praise of Gaura: a wondrous Moon has risen in Nadia, and darkness has left the three worlds; the Lord whom Shesha,
Shankara, Narada and Brahma praise rolls on the ground in bliss on hearing His own virtues; from His eyes flows an ocean of
the nectar of prema. According to M-1961 it is a pada of Yadunatha Dasa (Kavichandra), a fellow countryman of Jagannatha
Mishra and a contemporary of the Lord. Raga dhanashi.*[^06-12]

অপরূপ চাঁদ উদয় নদিয়াপুরে
তিমির নাহি রে ত্রিভুবনে ।
অবনিতে অখিল জিবের শোক নাশল
নিগম-নিগূঢ় প্রেম-দানে ॥

*aparūpa cām̐da udaya nadiyāpure*
*timira nāhi re tribhubane |*
*abanite akhila jibera śoka nāśala*
*nigama-nigūṛha prema-dāne ||*

*Word for word:* aparūpa cām̐da — a wondrous moon; udaya nadiyāpure — has risen in the town of Nadia; timira nāhi re tribhubane — there is no darkness in the three worlds; abanite — on earth; akhila jibera śoka nāśala — destroyed the sorrow of all beings; nigama-nigūṛha prema-dāne — by giving the prema hidden in the Vedas

**4.1.** A wondrous Moon has risen in the town of Nadia —
there is no more darkness in the three worlds!
On earth He destroyed the sorrow of all living beings,
bestowing the prema hidden in the Vedas.

আরে মোর গৌরাঙ্গসুন্দর রায় ।
ভকত-হৃদয়-কুমুদ পরকাশল
অকিঞ্চন-জিবের উপায় ॥

*āre mora gaurāṅgasundara rāya |*
*bhakata-hṛdaya-kumuda parakāśala*
*akiñcana-jibera upāya ||*

*Word for word:* āre mora gaurāṅgasundara rāya — O my Gaurangasundara Raya; bhakata-hṛdaya-kumuda parakāśala — made the lilies of the devotees' hearts unfold; akiñcana-jibera upāya — the salvation of the destitute

**4.2.** *(Refrain)* O my Gaurangasundara Raya!
He made the lilies of the devotees' hearts unfold —
the salvation of the destitute.[^06-13]

শেষ শঙ্কর নারদ চতুরানন
নিরবধি যার গুণ গায় ।
সো পহু নিরুপম নিজ-গুণ শুনইতে
আনন্দে ধরণী লোটায় ॥

*śeṣa śaṅkara nārada caturānana*
*nirabadhi yāra guṇa gāya |*
*so pahu nirupama nija-guṇa śunaite*
*ānande dharaṇī loṭāya ||*

*Word for word:* śeṣa śaṅkara nārada caturānana — Shesha, Shankara, Narada, the Four-faced; nirabadhi yāra guṇa gāya — incessantly sing whose virtues; so pahu nirupama — that incomparable Lord; nija-guṇa śunaite — hearing His own virtues; ānande dharaṇī loṭāya — rolls on the ground in bliss

**4.3.** Shesha, Shankara, Narada, the Four-faced One
incessantly sing His virtues;
and this incomparable Lord, hearing His own virtues,
rolls on the ground in bliss.[^06-14]

অরুণ নয়ানে বরুণ-আলয়
বহয়ে প্রেম-সুধা-জল ।
যদুনাথ দাস বলে যেন সোণার কমলে
প্রসবিছে মুকুতার ফল ॥

*aruṇa nayāne baruṇa-ālaya*
*bahaye prema-sudhā-jala |*
*yadunātha dāsa bale yena soṇāra kamale*
*prasabiche mukutāra phala ||*

*Word for word:* aruṇa nayāne — from the reddish eyes; baruṇa-ālaya — an ocean (abode of Varuna); bahaye prema-sudhā-jala — flows the nectar-water of prema; yadunātha dāsa bale — Yadunatha Dasa says; yena soṇāra kamale — as if a golden lotus; prasabiche mukutāra phala — were bearing pearls

**4.4.** From His reddish eyes there flows, [like] an ocean,
the nectarean water of prema.
Yadunatha Dasa says: it is as if from a golden lotus
pearls were being born.[^06-15]

[^06-12]: Signature: "Yadunatha Dasa". PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 265 (printed p. 254), no. 8 (mark "॥৮॥২১৯১॥"); raga dhanashi; MS
P-R-Sa no. 2299. GPT1 — p. 35, no. 27 (raga dhanashi); GPT2 — sect. 1.3 (OCR 18989). Yadunatha Kavichandra was the youngest
son of Ratnagarbha Acharya, a fellow countryman and friend of Jagannatha Mishra (CB Adi 2; CC Adi 11 — in the branch of
Nityananda); B. B. Majumdar (*Padas of the Sixteenth Century*, 1961) considers him a contemporary who wrote of Gaura's
moods as an eyewitness, and distinguishes him from Yadunandana. Cf. his padas below (nos. 14–15).
[^06-13]: Gaura is the moon whose rays make the night-lilies (kumuda) — the devotees' hearts — unfold. "The destitute"
(akiñcana) — those who have nothing but devotion.
[^06-14]: Shesha (Ananta) is the thousand-mouthed serpent; Shankara is Shiva; the Four-faced One is Brahma. MS "gha": "the
Name" instead of "Narada". Cf. Bhag. 10.14 (Brahma's praise).
[^06-15]: "Ocean" (baruṇa-ālaya — "abode of Varuna"): the tears of prema flow in streams. The image of the last line: the
tears on Gaura's golden face are pearls "born" of a golden lotus. GPT1: "Yadunatha Dasa says: by the [good] fortune
(lit. the fruit of karma) of the living beings He brings forth these pearls".

## 5. Shankara Ghosha — "dekha dekha sundara śacī-nandanā…" (KGC 24.1)
*Gaura's form in Navadvipa: arms reaching to the knees, the gait of an intoxicated elephant, a garland of malati, a face
lovelier than the autumn moon, eyes full of the tears of prema's bliss; with His companions He ceaselessly plays and sings
"Hari, Hari". According to M-1961 it is a pada of Shankara Ghosha, a mridanga player and a contemporary of the Navadvipa
period. Raga beloyar.*[^06-16]

দেখ দেখ সুন্দর শচী-নন্দনা ।
আজানুলম্বিত ভুজ বাহু সুবলনা ॥

*dekha dekha sundara śacī-nandanā |*
*ājānulambita bhuja bāhu subalanā ||*

*Word for word:* dekha dekha — look, look; sundara śacī-nandanā — the beautiful Son of Shachi; ājānulambita — reaching to the knees; bhuja bāhu subalanā — His arms beautifully formed

**5.1.** Look, look: the beautiful Son of Shachi!
His arms reach to the knees, beautifully formed.[^06-17]

ময়মত্ত হাতী ভাতি গতি চলনা ।
কিয়ে মালতী-মালা গোরা-অঙ্গে দোলনা ॥

*mayamatta hātī bhāti gati calanā |*
*kiye mālatī-mālā gorā-aṅge dolanā ||*

*Word for word:* mayamatta hātī bhāti — like an intoxicated elephant; gati calanā — the gait, the walk; kiye mālatī-mālā — and the garland of malati; gorā-aṅge dolanā — sways on Gora's body

**5.2.** His gait is like that of an intoxicated elephant;
a garland of malati sways on Gora's body.

শরদ-চাঁদ জিনি সুন্দর-বয়না ।
প্রেম-আনন্দ-বারি-পূরিত-নয়না ॥

*śarada-cām̐da jini sundara-bayanā |*
*prema-ānanda-bāri-pūrita-nayanā ||*

*Word for word:* śarada-cām̐da jini — surpassing the autumn moon; sundara-bayanā — of beautiful face; prema-ānanda-bāri-pūrita-nayanā — with eyes filled with the water of prema's bliss

**5.3.** His face is lovelier than the autumn moon,
His eyes are filled with the water of prema's bliss.

সহচর লই সঙ্গে অনুখণ খেলনা ।
নবদ্বীপ মাঝে গোরা হরি হরি বলনা ॥

*sahacara lai saṅge anukhaṇa khelanā |*
*nabadvīpa mājhe gorā hari hari balanā ||*

*Word for word:* sahacara lai saṅge — taking His companions along; anukhaṇa khelanā — ceaselessly plays; nabadvīpa mājhe — in the midst of Navadvipa; gorā hari hari balanā — Gora says "Hari, Hari"

**5.4.** Taking His companions along, He ceaselessly plays:
in the midst of Navadvipa Gora sings "Hari, Hari!"

অভয় চরণারবিন্দে মকরন্দ-লোভনা ।
কহয়ে শঙ্কর ঘোষ অখিল-লোক-তারণা ॥

*abhaya caraṇārabinde makaranda-lobhanā |*
*kahaye śaṅkara ghoṣa akhila-loka-tāraṇā ||*

*Word for word:* abhaya caraṇārabinde — with lotus feet that grant fearlessness; makaranda-lobhanā — enticing with honey; kahaye śaṅkara ghoṣa — says Shankara Ghosha; akhila-loka-tāraṇā — the Deliverer of all the worlds

**5.5.** His lotus feet, which grant fearlessness, entice with their honey —
says Shankara Ghosha — He is the Deliverer of all the worlds.[^06-18]

[^06-16]: Signature: "Shankara Ghosha". KGC: 24th kshanada (shukla-navami), no. 1 ("to Sri Gaurachandra"), p. 192; raga
beloyar. The pada is not in PK or GPT; its only witness is the anthology of Vishvanatha Chakravarti (late 17th c.).
Shankara Ghosha was a mridanga player, a companion of the Lord; Devakinandana in the *Vaishnava-vandana* praises his
humility and the playing of the dampha with which he delighted the Lord. B. B. Majumdar (1961) counts him among the poets
who were companions of Nimai Pandita in Navadvipa.
[^06-17]: Arms reaching to the knees (ājānulambita) are one of the marks of a great personality (mahapurusha); cf. CC Adi 3 on
the Lord's marks.
[^06-18]: The lines of the pada are a chain of epithets in -nā (subalanā, calanā, dolanā…); the last is "the Deliverer of all
the worlds" (akhila-loka-tāraṇā). "Entice with their honey" (makaranda-lobhanā) — the image of devotees as bees thirsting
for the honey of the feet.

## 6. Vasudeva Datta (?) — "aparūpa gorā naṭarāja…" (KGC 22.1; PK 2925)
*The form of Gaura, the "king of dancers", in Navadvipa: curling locks, a sandal tilaka, arms lovelier than an elephant's
trunk, on His chest a necklace as if the Ganga were falling from the peak of Sumeru, crimson feet with moonlike nails. In
KGC it bears the signature of Vasudeva Datta, in PK and GPT that of Govinda Dasa. According to M-1961 it is the only pada
of Vasudeva Datta; Majumdar prefers the KGC attribution, since Vishvanatha Chakravarti is two or three generations older
than the compiler of PK, Vaishnavadasa. Raga kedara.*[^06-19]

অপরূপ গোরা নটরাজ ।
প্রকট প্রেম-বিনোদ নব নাগর
বিহরে নবদ্বীপ মাঝ ॥

*aparūpa gorā naṭarāja |*
*prakaṭa prema-binoda naba nāgara*
*bihare nabadvīpa mājha ||*

*Word for word:* aparūpa — wondrous; gorā naṭarāja — Gora, king of dancers; prakaṭa — manifest; prema-binoda — sporting in prema; naba nāgara — the young Nagara (refined lover — an epithet of Krishna); bihare nabadvīpa mājha — plays in Navadvipa

**6.1.** *(Refrain)* Wondrous Gora, king of dancers!
The young Nagara made manifest, sporting in prema,
plays in Navadvipa.[^06-20]

কুটিল কুন্তল গন্ধ পরিমল
চন্দন তিলক ললাট ।
হেরি কুলবতী লাজ-মন্দির-
দুয়ারে দেওই কপাট ॥

*kuṭila kuntala gandha parimala*
*candana tilaka lalāṭa |*
*heri kulabatī lāja-mandira-*
*duyāre deoi kapāṭa ||*

*Word for word:* kuṭila kuntala — curling locks; gandha parimala — fragrance; candana tilaka lalāṭa — a sandal tilaka on the brow; heri — seeing; kulabatī — chaste wives; lāja-mandira-duyāre — at the door of the temple of modesty; deoi kapāṭa — bolt the doors

**6.2.** His curling locks are fragrant,
on His forehead a tilaka of sandal.
Seeing [Him], chaste wives
bolt the doors of the temple of modesty.[^06-21]

করিবর-কর জিনি বাহুর সুবলনি
দোসরি গজ-মতি-হারা ।
সুমেরু-শিখরে যৈছন ঝাঁপিয়া
বহই সুরধুনী-ধারা ॥

*karibara-kara jini bāhura subalani*
*dosari gaja-mati-hārā |*
*sumeru-śikhare yaichana jhām̐piyā*
*bahai suradhunī-dhārā ||*

*Word for word:* karibara-kara jini — surpassing the trunk of a royal elephant; bāhura subalani — the lovely roundness of the arms; dosari gaja-mati-hārā — a double necklace of elephant-pearls; sumeru-śikhare — from the peak of Sumeru; yaichana jhām̐piyā — as if rushing down; bahai suradhunī-dhārā — flows the stream of the Suradhuni (the Ganga)

**6.3.** His arms are lovelier than the trunk of a royal elephant,
a double necklace of elephant-pearls —
as if, rushing down from the peak of Sumeru,
the stream of the Suradhuni were flowing.[^06-22]

রাতুল অতুল চরণ-যুগল
নখ-মণি বিধু উজোর ।
ভকত ভ্রমরা সৌরভে আকুল
বাসুদেব দত্ত রহু ভোর ॥

*rātula atula caraṇa-yugala*
*nakha-maṇi bidhu ujora |*
*bhakata bhramarā saurabhe ākula*
*bāsudeba datta rahu bhora ||*

*Word for word:* rātula atula caraṇa-yugala — crimson peerless feet; nakha-maṇi — gem-like nails; bidhu ujora — radiant moons; bhakata bhramarā — the devotee-bees; saurabhe ākula — maddened by the fragrance; bāsudeba datta rahu bhora — Vasudeva Datta is enraptured

**6.4.** Crimson, peerless feet,
gem-like nails — radiant moons;
the devotee-bees are maddened by the fragrance —
Vasudeva Datta is enraptured.[^06-23]

[^06-19]: Signature: "Vasudeva Datta" (KGC: 22nd kshanada, shukla-saptami, no. 1, "to Sri Gaurachandra", p. 171; raga
kedara). PK 2925 (vol. 4, PDF pp. 207–208, printed pp. 198–199; 33rd pallava — "The eightfold eternal lila",
gaura-chandrika to a description of sambhoga; mark "॥১১॥২৯২৫॥"; raga kedara) has the signature "Govinda Dasa" and an extra
stanza (see VAR); so too GPT1 (p. 121, no. 31) and GPT2 (sect. 3.1, no. 31). Vasudeva Datta was the elder brother of
Mukunda Datta, a great singer (CC Adi 10; Madhya 11, 15). The attribution is disputed.
[^06-20]: "Nagara" — "the refined lover", a traditional epithet of Krishna; here of Gaura as Krishna Himself appearing in
Navadvipa ("young" — PK MSS "ka", "kha", "gha", "ca" and KGC: nava nāgara; the main PK text has simply nāgara).
[^06-21]: The image (as in padas about Krishna) speaks of the irresistibility of the Lord's beauty: at the sight of Him women
hide behind the doors of modesty. This is not a description of worldly passion, nor a basis for worshipping Gaura in the
mood of "gaura-nagari", which the Gaudiya Vaishnava tradition (Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja, Bhaktisiddhanta
Sarasvati) does not accept: in Navadvipa, according to CB (Adi 15), the Lord did not even jest with women; He is Krishna
come in the mood of Radha, tasting Her prema.
[^06-22]: Elephant-pearls (gaja-mati) — according to tradition, pearls from the frontal globes of an elephant. Sumeru is the
golden mountain: Gaura's golden chest, down which the white necklace flows like the Ganga.
[^06-23]: In PK instead of this stanza: "I beheld the crimson feet, the nails a pair of moon-gems; maddened by the fragrance is
the swarm of bees — the mind of Govinda Dasa is enraptured".

## 7. Ramananda — "dekha dekha adabhuta sundara śacisuta…" (PK 2162)
*Gaura's form: His body, trembling with prema, outshines rays of gold; His lips sing "Hari, Hari"; drops of sandal on His
brow; His locks curl like bees round a golden lotus; tears flow from His eyes like pearls from a loosened string; He has
plunged the world into the ocean of the taste of singing His names and virtues. Signature "Ramananda" (without "Vasu"):
the attribution to Vasu Ramananda is likely but unproven. Raga gandhara.*[^06-24]

দেখ দেখ অদভুত সুন্দর শচিসুত
অপরূপ বিহি-নিরমাণ ।
ডগমগি হিরণ-কিরণ জিনি তনু-রুচি
হরি হরি বোলত বয়ান ॥

*dekha dekha adabhuta sundara śacisuta*
*aparūpa bihi-niramāṇa |*
*ḍagamagi hiraṇa-kiraṇa jini tanu-ruci*
*hari hari bolata bayāna ||*

*Word for word:* dekha dekha — look, look; adabhuta sundara śacisuta — the wondrous, beautiful Son of Shachi; aparūpa bihi-niramāṇa — an extraordinary creation of the Creator; ḍagamagi — trembling; hiraṇa-kiraṇa jini — surpassing rays of gold; tanu-ruci — the radiance of the body; hari hari bolata bayāna — the lips say "Hari, Hari"

**7.1.** Look, look at the wondrous, beautiful Son of Shachi —
an extraordinary creation of the Creator!
The radiance of His trembling body outshines rays of gold,
His lips utter "Hari, Hari".

ভালহি মলয়জ-বিন্দু বিরাজিত
তছু পর অলকা হিলোল ।
কনক-সরোজ চাঁদ জিনি উজোর
তহি বেড়ি অলিকুল দোল ॥

*bhālahi malayaja-bindu birājita*
*tachu para alakā hilola |*
*kanaka-saroja cām̐da jini ujora*
*tahi beṛi alikula dola ||*

*Word for word:* bhālahi malayaja-bindu birājita — on the brow gleam drops of sandal; tachu para alakā hilola — above them the locks sway; kanaka-saroja cām̐da jini ujora — shining brighter than a golden lotus and the moon; tahi beṛi alikula dola — round it circles a swarm of bees

**7.2.** Drops of sandal gleam on His brow,
above them His locks sway;
[His face] shines brighter than a golden lotus and the moon,
and round it circles a swarm of bees.

দুনয়ন অরুণ কমল-দল-গঞ্জন
খঞ্জন জিনিয়া চকোর ।
যৈছন শিথিল গাঁথন মোতি-ফল
তৈছে বহত ঘন লোর ॥

*dunayana aruṇa kamala-dala-gañjana*
*khañjana jiniyā cakora |*
*yaichana śithila gām̐thana moti-phala*
*taiche bahata ghana lora ||*

*Word for word:* dunayana aruṇa — two reddish eyes; kamala-dala-gañjana — shaming lotus petals; khañjana jiniyā cakora — surpassing the wagtail and the chakora; yaichana śithila gām̐thana moti-phala — like pearls from a loosened string; taiche bahata ghana lora — so flow abundant tears

**7.3.** His two reddish eyes put lotus petals to shame,
surpass the wagtail and the chakora;
like pearls from a loosened string,
so flow His abundant tears.[^06-25]

নিজ গুণ নাম গান রস-সায়রে
জগ-জন নিমগন কেল ।
দিন-হিন রামানন্দ তহিঁ বঞ্চিত
কিঞ্চিত পরশ না ভেল ॥

*nija guṇa nāma gāna rasa-sāyare*
*jaga-jana nimagana kela |*
*dina-hina rāmānanda tahim̐ bañcita*
*kiñcita paraśa nā bhela ||*

*Word for word:* nija guṇa nāma gāna rasa-sāyare — in the ocean of the taste of singing His own virtues and names; jaga-jana nimagana kela — He plunged the people of the world; dina-hina rāmānanda — wretched Ramananda; tahim̐ bañcita — is deprived in this; kiñcita paraśa nā bhela — not a drop touched [him]

**7.4.** Into the ocean of the taste of singing His virtues and names
He has plunged the people of the world;
wretched Ramananda alone is deprived —
not even a drop has touched him.[^06-26]

[^06-24]: Signature: "Ramananda". PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 253 (printed p. 242), 18th pallava, no. 54 (mark "॥৫৪॥২১৬২॥"); raga
gandhara; MS P-R-Sa no. 2269. GPT1 — twice: p. 124, no. 40, and p. 137, no. 76 (both raga gandhara); GPT2 — sect. 3.1,
no. 76 (and no. 40). In Ray's index of poets "Ramananda" (11 padas) is kept apart from "Vasu Ramananda" (7 padas); Majumdar
ascribes to Vasu Ramananda only one pada signed "Ramananda" (PK 1711, chapter 1, no. 18). The padas of this group (PK 1417,
2060, 2096, 2162, 2163, 2257, 2615, 3057) are in Vrajabuli and Bengali, like the undisputed padas of Vasu Ramananda (PK
2082, 1924); there is also the signature "Ramananda Dasa" (PK 2096, 2615). Hence authority C. In the stage-1 catalogue the
first line of PK 2160 (Shekhara Raya) had been attached to PK 2162.
[^06-25]: The wagtail (khañjana) and the chakora are images of lively, beautiful eyes. MSS: "trembling" (ḍagamaga — "ka"),
"string" (gām̐thala — "ka", "kha").
[^06-26]: MS "kha": "gave" (debe) and "not" (nāhi). GPT1, p. 137: "…how many wretched ones He saved, while Ramananda in this is
deprived — not a drop has touched him".

## 8. Ramananda — "dekhata bekata gaura adabhuta…" (PK 2163)
*Gaura's form and dance on the bank of the Ganga: He recalls the virtues of the Vraja-lila and cannot stand still; His
body thrills, tears flow; intoxicated by the devotees' singing, He dances skilfully and cries "Haribol". Signature:
"Ramananda". Raga tudi.*[^06-27]

দেখত বেকত গৌর অদভুত
উজোর সুরধুনি-তীর ।
জাম্বুনদ-তনু বসন জিনিয়া ভানু
সুন্দর সুঘড় সুধীর ॥

*dekhata bekata gaura adabhuta*
*ujora suradhuni-tīra |*
*jāmbunada-tanu basana jiniyā bhānu*
*sundara sughaṛa sudhīra ||*

*Word for word:* dekhata — look; bekata — manifest; gaura adabhuta — wondrous Gaura; ujora suradhuni-tīra — lighting up the bank of the Suradhuni (the Ganga); jāmbunada-tanu — His body jambunada gold; basana jiniyā bhānu — His garment outshining the sun; sundara sughaṛa sudhīra — beautiful, well-formed, composed

**8.1.** Look: manifest is wondrous Gaura,
lighting up the bank of the Suradhuni!
His body is jambunada gold, His garment outshines the sun;
beautiful, well-formed, composed.[^06-28]

ব্রজ-লীলা গুণ সোঙরি সোঙরি ঘন
রহই না পারই থীর ।
পুলকে পূরল তনু ফুটল কদম্ব জনু
ঝরঝর নয়নক নীর ॥

*braja-līlā guṇa soṅari soṅari ghana*
*rahai nā pārai thīra |*
*pulake pūrala tanu phuṭala kadamba janu*
*jharajhara nayanaka nīra ||*

*Word for word:* braja-līlā guṇa — the virtues of the Vraja-lila; soṅari soṅari ghana — recalling and recalling; rahai nā pārai thīra — cannot stand still; pulake pūrala tanu — the body filled with thrills; phuṭala kadamba janu — as if a kadamba had blossomed; jharajhara nayanaka nīra — tears stream from the eyes

**8.2.** Recalling and recalling the virtues of the Vraja-lila,
He cannot stand still;
His body is covered with thrills, as if a kadamba had blossomed,
tears stream from His eyes.

অবিরত ভকত গান-রসে উনমত
কম্বু-কণ্ঠ ঘন দোল ।
পুলকে পূরল জীব সুনিপুণ নাচত
সঘনে বলয়ে হরিবোল ॥

*abirata bhakata gāna-rase unamata*
*kambu-kaṇṭha ghana dola |*
*pulake pūrala jība sunipuṇa nācata*
*saghane balaye haribola ||*

*Word for word:* abirata bhakata gāna-rase unamata — intoxicated by the taste of the devotees' ceaseless singing; kambu-kaṇṭha ghana dola — often sways His conch-like neck; pulake pūrala jība — the beings are filled with thrills; sunipuṇa nācata — dances skilfully; saghane balaye haribola — again and again cries "Haribol"

**8.3.** Intoxicated by the taste of the devotees' ceaseless singing,
He sways His conch-like neck;
a thrill has seized the living beings; skilfully He dances
and again and again cries: "Haribol!"[^06-29]

দেব দেব অধিদেব জন-বল্লভ
পতিত-পাবন অবতার ।
কলিযুগ-কাল-ব্যাল-ভয়ে কাতর
রামানন্দে কর পার ॥

*deba deba adhideba jana-ballabha*
*patita-pābana abatāra |*
*kaliyuga-kāla-byāla-bhaye kātara*
*rāmānande kara pāra ||*

*Word for word:* deba deba adhideba — God of gods, Lord of gods; jana-ballabha — Beloved of the people; patita-pābana abatāra — the descent who purifies the fallen; kaliyuga-kāla-byāla-bhaye kātara — tormented by fear of the serpent of time in the age of Kali; rāmānande kara pāra — carry Ramananda across

**8.4.** God of gods, Lord of gods, Beloved of the people,
descent who purifies the fallen!
Ramananda, tormented by fear of the serpent of time in the age of Kali —
carry him across [the ocean of existence]!

[^06-27]: Signature: "Ramananda". PK: vol. 3, PDF pp. 253–254 (printed pp. 242–243), 18th pallava, no. 55; on the scan the
mark is "॥৫৫॥২১৬৪॥" — evidently a misprint (no. 55 follows PK 2162 = no. 54; in Ray's index the Ramananda pada is 2163);
raga tudi; MS P-R-Sa no. 2270. GPT1 — p. 124, no. 41 (raga tudi); GPT2 — sect. 3.1, no. 41 and no. 77. In the stage-1
catalogue the second GPT2 copy (no. 77) was wrongly ascribed to Paramananda (PA-004). On the attribution see note 24.
[^06-28]: Jambunada is celestial gold (from the river Jambu). MS P-R-Sa: "of beautiful, well-formed body" (śarīra for
sudhīra).
[^06-29]: "Conch-like neck" (kambu-kaṇṭha) — a neck with three lines, a mark of beauty. MSS "ka", "kha", "ca", P-R-Sa and
GPT1: "hearing, He dances again" (śuni puna for sunipuṇa); "ka": "the devotees (bhakata-gaṇa) are intoxicated with the
taste".

## 9. Vamshi(vadana) — "jaya jaya nabadvīpa mājha…" (PK 26)
*Lila: the eve of a kirtana festival in Navadvipa: at Gauranga's bidding Advaita prepares the "khol-mangala" — the
consecration of the mridanga; having called the Vaishnavas, they perform the adhivasa of the great festival; Nitai gives
out garlands and sandal, Govinda plays the mridanga, Advaita the kartals, Haridasa sings, Srivasa holds the tune, Gora
dances. Cf. the pada of Parameshvara Dasa, PK 23 (chapter 5, no. 4), on the same festival in Advaita's house. Raga
kamoda.*[^06-30]

জয় জয় নবদ্বীপ মাঝ ।
গৌরাঙ্গ-আদেশ পাঞা ঠাকুর অদ্বৈত যাঞা
করে খোল-মঙ্গলের সাজ ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*jaya jaya nabadvīpa mājha |*
*gaurāṅga-ādeśa pāñā ṭhākura advaita yāñā*
*kare khola-maṅgalera sāja || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* jaya jaya — glory, glory; nabadvīpa mājha — in the midst of Navadvipa; gaurāṅga-ādeśa pāñā — having received Gauranga's bidding; ṭhākura advaita yāñā — Thakura Advaita, having come; kare khola-maṅgalera sāja — prepares the khol-mangala (consecration of the mridanga)

**9.1.** *(Refrain)* Glory, glory [to the festival] in the midst of Navadvipa!
At Gauranga's bidding Thakura Advaita has come
and prepares the khol-mangala.[^06-31]

আনিয়া বৈষ্ণব সব হরিবোল কলরব
মহোৎসবের করে অধিবাস ।
আপনি নিতাই ধন দেই মালাচন্দন
করে প্রিয় বৈষ্ণব সম্ভাষ ॥

*āniyā baiṣṇaba saba haribola kalaraba*
*mahotsabera kare adhibāsa |*
*āpani nitāi dhana dei mālācandana*
*kare priya baiṣṇaba sambhāṣa ||*

*Word for word:* āniyā baiṣṇaba saba — having brought all the Vaishnavas; haribola kalaraba — the clamour of "Haribol"; mahotsabera kare adhibāsa — they perform the adhivasa of the great festival; āpani nitāi dhana — Nitai Himself, the treasure; dei mālācandana — gives garlands and sandal; kare priya baiṣṇaba sambhāṣa — greets the dear Vaishnavas

**9.2.** Having brought all the Vaishnavas, amid the clamour of "Haribol!",
they perform the adhivasa of the great festival.
Nitai Himself, [our] treasure, gives garlands and sandal,
greeting the dear Vaishnavas.[^06-32]

গোবিন্দ মৃদঙ্গ লৈয়া বায়ে তা তা থৈয়া থৈয়া
করতালে অদ্বৈত চপল ।
হরিদাস করে গান শ্রীবাস ধরয়ে তান
নাচে গোরা কীর্তন-মঙ্গল ॥

*gobinda mṛdaṅga laiyā bāye tā tā thaiyā thaiyā*
*karatāle advaita capala |*
*haridāsa kare gāna śrībāsa dharaye tāna*
*nāce gorā kīrtana-maṅgala ||*

*Word for word:* gobinda mṛdaṅga laiyā — Govinda, taking the mridanga; bāye tā tā thaiyā thaiyā — plays "ta-ta thaiya-thaiya"; karatāle advaita capala — nimble on the kartals is Advaita; haridāsa kare gāna — Haridasa sings; śrībāsa dharaye tāna — Srivasa holds the tune; nāce gorā kīrtana-maṅgala — Gora dances at the blessing of the kirtana

**9.3.** Govinda, taking the mridanga, plays: "ta-ta thaiya-thaiya",
nimble on the kartals is Advaita;
Haridasa sings, Srivasa holds the tune —
Gora dances at the blessing of the kirtana.[^06-33]

চৌদিকে বৈষ্ণবগণ হরি বোলে ঘনে-ঘন
কালি হবে কীর্তন মহোৎসব ।
আজি খোল-মঙ্গলি রাখিয়ে আনন্দ করি
বংশী বলে দেহ জয় রব ॥২৬॥

*caudike baiṣṇabagaṇa hari bole ghane-ghana*
*kāli habe kīrtana mahotsaba |*
*āji khola-maṅgali rākhiye ānanda kari*
*baṃśī bale deha jaya raba ||26||*

*Word for word:* caudike baiṣṇaba-gaṇa — all round the Vaishnavas; hari bole ghane-ghana — cry "Hari" again and again; kāli habe kīrtana mahotsaba — tomorrow will be the great festival of kirtana; āji khola-maṅgali — today the khol-mangala; rākhiye ānanda kari — we have performed (lit. we keep), rejoicing; baṃśī bale — says Vamshi; deha jaya raba — raise the cry "Glory!"

**9.4.** All round the Vaishnavas cry "Haribol!" again and again —
tomorrow there will be the great festival of kirtana.
"Today we have joyfully performed the khol-mangala," —
says Vamshi: "Cry out 'Glory!'"

[^06-30]: Signature: "Vamshi". PK: vol. 1, PDF p. 32 (printed p. 21), 1st pallava ("Mangalacharana"), no. 26 (mark "॥২৬॥");
raga kamoda; MS P-R-Sa no. 26. GPT1 — p. 247, no. 30 (raga kamoda); GPT2 — sect. 4.1, no. 30. In the stage-1 catalogue
the PK number was given wrongly (45; corrected in stage 1b). In PK the pada stands in a series of padas on the adhivasa of kirtana (PK 23 —
Parameshvara Dasa, 24 and 25 — Vrindavana Dasa). Majumdar ascribes the signature "Vamshi" to Vamshivadana (the guardian of
Vishnupriya), distinguishing him from the later Vamshidasa, a disciple of Srinivasa.
[^06-31]: The khol is the clay mridanga of Bengali kirtana; the khol-mangala is the consecration of the mridanga on the eve of
a kirtana (sandal, garlands, auspicious articles), and the adhivasa is the rite of "installation" that precedes a
festival. In PK 23 the same festival is described as arranged by Advaita and Sita Thakurani at the Lord's direction.
[^06-32]: MS "ga": "having given garlands and sandal".
[^06-33]: "Ta-ta thaiya-thaiya" imitates the rhythm of the mridanga. Govinda — evidently Govinda Ghosha or Govinda Datta (a
kirtaniya, CC Madhya 13). "Plays" (bāye) — so Ray corrects the reading of all the manuscripts, bāje ("sounds"), considering
it a scribal error.

## 10. Chaitanyadasa — "mahābhuja nācata caitanya rāya…" (PK 664; BR, p. 951)
*Lila: the Lord's dance in kirtana: His golden body is full of bhavas; hearing His own names and virtues He loses Himself in
the dance; Nadia has forgotten its sorrow; the rain of prema has watered the whole world, and only the poet is deprived.
Narahari Chakravarti cites the pada in the *Bhakti-ratnakara* among the testimonies to the Navadvipa kirtanas, next to the
pada of Vasu Ramananda (no. 1). In PK it is a gaura-chandrika to the "rasodgara". Raga vibhasa (PK), suhai (BR).*[^06-34]

মহাভুজ নাচত চৈতন্য রায় ।
কে জানে কত কত ভাব শত শত
সোনার বরণ গোরা-গায় ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*mahābhuja nācata caitanya rāya |*
*ke jāne kata kata bhāba śata śata*
*sonāra baraṇa gorā-gāya || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* mahābhuja — long-armed (mighty-armed); nācata caitanya rāya — Chaitanya Raya dances; ke jāne — who knows; kata kata bhāba śata śata — how many bhavas, hundreds upon hundreds; sonāra baraṇa gorā-gāya — on Gora's golden body

**10.1.** *(Refrain)* Long-armed, Chaitanya Raya dances!
Who knows how many bhavas, hundreds upon hundreds,
are on Gora's golden body!

প্রেমে ঢর ঢর অঙ্গ নিরমল
পুলক-অঙ্কুর-শোভা ।
আর কি কহব অশেষ অনুভব
হেরইতে জগ-মন-লোভা ॥

*preme ḍhara ḍhara aṅga niramala*
*pulaka-aṅkura-śobhā |*
*āra ki kahaba aśeṣa anubhaba*
*heraite jaga-mana-lobhā ||*

*Word for word:* preme ḍhara ḍhara — brimming with prema; aṅga niramala — the pure body; pulaka-aṅkura-śobhā — the beauty of sprouts of thrill; āra ki kahaba — what more shall I say; aśeṣa anubhaba — of the countless anubhavas; heraite jaga-mana-lobhā — at the sight the mind of the world is drawn

**10.2.** His body, moist with prema, pure,
is adorned with sprouts of thrill;
what more shall I say of the countless anubhavas? —
at the sight [of Him] the mind of the world is drawn.[^06-35]

শুনিয়া নিজ-গুণ নাম-কীর্তন
বিভোর নটন-বিভঙ্গ ।
নদিয়া-পুর-লোক পাসরিল দুখ শোক
ভাসল প্রেম-তরঙ্গ ॥

*śuniyā nija-guṇa nāma-kīrtana*
*bibhora naṭana-bibhaṅga |*
*nadiyā-pura-loka pāsarila dukha śoka*
*bhāsala prema-taraṅga ||*

*Word for word:* śuniyā nija-guṇa — hearing His own virtues; nāma-kīrtana — the kirtana of the names; bibhora naṭana-bibhaṅga — lost in the curves of the dance; nadiyā-pura-loka — the people of the town of Nadia; pāsarila dukha śoka — forgot grief and sorrow; bhāsala prema-taraṅga — float on the waves of prema

**10.3.** Hearing His own virtues, the kirtana of the names,
He loses Himself in the curves of the dance;
the people of the town of Nadia have forgotten grief and sorrow,
they float on the waves of prema.

রতন বিতরণ প্রেম-রস বরিখণ
অখিল ভুবন সিঞ্চিত ।
চৈতন্যদাস গানে অতুল প্রেম-দানে
মুঞি সে হইলুঁ বঞ্চিত ॥১॥৬৬৪॥

*ratana bitaraṇa prema-rasa barikhaṇa*
*akhila bhubana siñcita |*
*caitanyadāsa gāne atula prema-dāne*
*muñi se hailum̐ bañcita ||1||664||*

*Word for word:* ratana bitaraṇa — giving out the jewel; prema-rasa barikhaṇa — raining the taste of prema; akhila bhubana siñcita — the whole world is watered; caitanya-dāsa gāne — Chaitanyadasa sings; atula prema-dāne — in the peerless gift of prema; muñi se hailum̐ bañcita — I alone have remained deprived

**10.4.** Giving out the jewel, raining the taste of prema,
He has watered the whole world;
Chaitanyadasa sings: in this peerless gift of prema
I alone have remained deprived.[^06-36]

[^06-34]: Signature: "Chaitanyadasa". PK: vol. 2, PDF p. 57 (printed p. 44), 6th pallava, no. 1 (mark "॥১॥৬৬৪॥"), "Then the
rasodgara; Sri Gaurachandra, according to the kirtana befitting what precedes and follows"; raga vibhasa; MS P-R-Sa
no. 1139 and MS P-R. BR, 12th wave: 1913 ed., p. 951; 1960 ed. vv. 3418–3421 (raga suhai); 2006 ed. the same. In BR stanzas
10.2 and 10.3 are transposed and 10.4 begins differently (see note 36). GPT2 — sect. 4.2, no. 1. Majumdar does not discuss
the pada; in his view Chaitanyadasa was probably a contemporary from the branch of Gadadhara. The fact that Narahari
Chakravarti cites the pada as testimony makes it one of the early sources.
[^06-35]: "Anubhavas" (anubhaba) — outward manifestations of inner feelings (tears, thrills, trembling). MS P-R: "of the body"
(aṅgera for aṅkura); P-R-Sa: "endless anubhavas" (aśeṣānubhāba).
[^06-36]: BR and MS P-R: "With a merciful glance, with a rain of nectar He has watered the whole world". In MS P-R the
signature is "Vasu Ghosha", and instead of "in this peerless gift of prema" — "[He] has no equal"; MS "ka": "He came to give
prema".

## 11. Narahari — "nāce śacīsuta līlā adabhuta…" (PK 2097)
*Lila: the dance of Shachi's Son in kirtana: His gait sways, He leans on Gadadhara, raising His arms He cries "Hari,
Hari", intoxicated with His own taste; from His reddish eyes tears pour day and night; to all — the lame, the blind, the
fallen — He has given prema, entreating them to accept it. Raga mayura.*[^06-37]

নাচে শচীসুত লীলা অদভুত
চলনি ডগমগি ভঙ্গিয়া ।
সঙ্গে কত কত ভকত গাওত
হিলন গদাধর-অঙ্গিয়া ॥

*nāce śacīsuta līlā adabhuta*
*calani ḍagamagi bhaṅgiyā |*
*saṅge kata kata bhakata gāota*
*hilana gadādhara-aṅgiyā ||*

*Word for word:* nāce śacīsuta — the Son of Shachi dances; līlā adabhuta — wondrous lila; calani ḍagamagi bhaṅgiyā — a swaying gait, the curves; saṅge kata kata bhakata gāota — with Him so many devotees sing; hilana gadādhara-aṅgiyā — leaning on Gadadhara's body

**11.1.** Shachi's Son dances — wondrous is His lila! —
His gait sways, the curves [of the dance];
with Him so many, so many devotees sing —
He leans on Gadadhara.

আজানুবাহু তুলি বোলয়ে হরি হরি
আপনি নিজ রসে মাতিয়া ।
বদন-মণ্ডল চাঁদ ঝলমল
দশন মোতিম-পাঁতিয়া ॥

*ājānubāhu tuli bolaye hari hari*
*āpani nija rase mātiyā |*
*badana-maṇḍala cām̐da jhalamala*
*daśana motima-pām̐tiyā ||*

*Word for word:* ājānu-bāhu tuli — raising His arms that reach to the knees; bolaye hari hari — cries "Hari, Hari"; āpani nija rase mātiyā — Himself intoxicated with His own taste; badana-maṇḍala cām̐da jhalamala — the circle of His face shines like the moon; daśana motima-pām̐tiyā — His teeth a row of pearls

**11.2.** Raising His arms that reach to the knees, He cries "Hari, Hari",
Himself intoxicated with His own taste;
the circle of His face shines like the moon,
His teeth a string of pearls.[^06-38]

কষিত কাঞ্চন- কিরণ ঝলমল
সতত কীর্তন-রঙ্গিয়া ।
অরুণ-নয়ানে বরুণ-আলয়
অঝরে ঝরে দিন রাতিয়া ॥

*kaṣita kāñcana- kiraṇa jhalamala*
*satata kīrtana-raṅgiyā |*
*aruṇa-nayāne baruṇa-ālaya*
*ajhare jhare dina rātiyā ||*

*Word for word:* kaṣita kāñcana-kiraṇa jhalamala — gleaming with the radiance of touchstone-tested gold; satata kīrtana-raṅgiyā — ever delighting in kirtana; aruṇa-nayāne — from the reddish eyes; baruṇa-ālaya — an ocean; ajhare jhare dina rātiyā — pours unceasingly day and night

**11.3.** He gleams like gold tested on the touchstone,
ever delighting in kirtana;
from His reddish eyes, [like] an ocean,
[water] pours unceasingly day and night.

পঙ্গু অন্ধ যত পতিত দুর্গত
দেওল সভে প্রেম যাচিয়া ।
করুণা দেখি মনে ভরসা বাঢ়ল
দাস নরহরি-ছাতিয়া ॥৩৯॥২০৯৭॥

*paṅgu andha yata patita durgata*
*deola sabhe prema yāciyā |*
*karuṇā dekhi mane bharasā bāṛhala*
*dāsa narahari-chātiyā ||39||2097||*

*Word for word:* paṅgu andha yata — all the lame and blind; patita durgata — the fallen, the wretched; deola sabhe prema yāciyā — He gave prema to all, entreating; karuṇā dekhi mane — seeing [His] mercy, in the heart; bharasā bāṛhala — hope has grown; dāsa narahari-chātiyā — in the breast of Narahari Dasa

**11.4.** To the lame, the blind, to all the fallen and wretched
He has given prema, entreating [them to accept it];
seeing His mercy, hope has grown strong
in the breast of Narahari Dasa.

[^06-37]: Signature: "Narahari Dasa". PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 229 (printed p. 218), 17th pallava ("Sri Gauranga's dance"), no. 39 (mark
"॥৩৯॥২০৯৭॥"); raga mayura; MS P-R-Sa no. 2206. GPT1 — pp. 256–257, no. 26 (raga mayura); GPT2 — sect. 4.2, no. 26. In
Ray's index of poets it is among the padas of Narahari; Majumdar does not discuss it. The attribution to Sarakara is likely
(simple language) but unproven.
[^06-38]: "Intoxicated with His own taste" (āpani nija rase mātiyā) — cf. CC Adi 4: the Lord came to taste His own sweetness
and Radha's love for Him. MSS "kha", "gha", P-R-Sa: "intoxicated with His own taste" (āpana); P-R-Sa in 11.1: "so many
people" (jana).

## 12. Ramananda Dasa — "āre mora nācata gaurakiśora…" (PK 2096)
*Lila: the dance of young Gaura: His body brighter than gold, His face lovelier than the autumn moon, a tilaka of
gorochana, locks like bees on a lotus, drops of sweat, streams of tears; He Himself "strung" His virtues into the kirtana
which His companions sing, and brought in the khol and kartals to crush godlessness. Signature: "Ramananda Dasa". Raga
vibhasa.*[^06-39]

আরে মোর নাচত গৌরকিশোর ।
হিরণ-কিরণ জিনি ও তনু সুন্দর
দশ দিশ সকল উজোর ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*āre mora nācata gaurakiśora |*
*hiraṇa-kiraṇa jini o tanu sundara*
*daśa diśa sakala ujora || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* āre mora — ah, my; nācata gaura-kiśora — young Gaura dances; hiraṇa-kiraṇa jini — brighter than rays of gold; o tanu sundara — that beautiful body; daśa diśa sakala ujora — has lit up all ten directions

**12.1.** *(Refrain)* Ah, my young Gaura dances!
His beautiful body, brighter than rays of gold,
has lit up all ten directions.

শরদ-চাঁদ জিনি ঝলমল বদনহি
গোরোচন-তিলক সুভাল ।
কুঞ্চিত চারু চিকুর তহিঁ লোলত
কমলে কিয়ে অলি-জাল ॥

*śarada-cām̐da jini jhalamala badanahi*
*gorocana-tilaka subhāla |*
*kuñcita cāru cikura tahim̐ lolata*
*kamale kiye ali-jāla ||*

*Word for word:* śarada-cām̐da jini — brighter than the autumn moon; jhalamala badanahi — the face shines; gorocana-tilaka subhāla — a lovely tilaka of gorochana on the brow; kuñcita cāru cikura — curling, charming locks; tahim̐ lolata — sway upon it; kamale kiye ali-jāla — like a swarm of bees on a lotus

**12.2.** His face shines brighter than the autumn moon,
on His brow a lovely tilaka of gorochana;
His curling, charming locks sway upon it,
like a swarm of bees on a lotus.[^06-40]

নাসা তিলফুল বিম্ব অধর-তল
চুয়ত বিন্দু বিন্দু ঘাম ।
তরুণ অরুণ সরসিজ জিনি লোচন
ধারা বহে অবিরাম ॥

*nāsā tilaphula bimba adhara-tala*
*cuyata bindu bindu ghāma |*
*taruṇa aruṇa sarasija jini locana*
*dhārā bahe abirāma ||*

*Word for word:* nāsā tilaphula — the nose a sesame flower; bimba adhara-tala — the lips a bimba fruit; cuyata bindu bindu ghāma — drop by drop the sweat trickles; taruṇa aruṇa sarasija jini locana — eyes lovelier than a young red lotus; dhārā bahe abirāma — streams flow ceaselessly

**12.3.** His nose a sesame flower, His lips a bimba fruit,
drop by drop the sweat trickles;
His eyes lovelier than a young red lotus,
ceaselessly flow streams [of tears].

গাঁথিয়া আপন গুণ পরকাশ কীর্তন
গাওত সহচরবৃন্দে ।
খোল করতাল যতন করি সিরজিল
পাষণ্ড-দলন-অনুবন্ধে ॥

*gām̐thiyā āpana guṇa parakāśa kīrtana*
*gāota sahacarabṛnde |*
*khola karatāla yatana kari sirajila*
*pāṣaṇḍa-dalana-anubandhe ||*

*Word for word:* gām̐thiyā āpana guṇa — stringing His own virtues; parakāśa kīrtana — revealed the kirtana; gāota sahacara-bṛnde — the hosts of companions sing; khola karatāla — the khol and kartals; yatana kari sirajila — He carefully created; pāṣaṇḍa-dalana-anubandhe — for the purpose of crushing godlessness

**12.4.** Stringing His own virtues, He revealed the kirtana —
the hosts of His companions sing it;
the khol and kartals He carefully created
to crush godlessness.[^06-41]

অবনীতে অদভুত প্রভু শচীনন্দন
পতিত-পাবন অবতার ।
দীন হীন মূঢ়মতি রামানন্দ দাস অতি
পহু মোরে কর ভব পার ॥৩৮॥২০৯৬॥

*abanīte adabhuta prabhu śacīnandana*
*patita-pābana abatāra |*
*dīna hīna mūṛhamati rāmānanda dāsa ati*
*pahu more kara bhaba pāra ||38||2096||*

*Word for word:* abanīte adabhuta prabhu śacīnandana — on earth the wondrous Lord, the Son of Shachi; patita-pābana abatāra — the descent who purifies the fallen; dīna hīna mūṛhamati — lowly, wretched, foolish; rāmānanda dāsa ati — Ramananda Dasa, utterly; pahum̐ more kara bhaba pāra — Lord, carry me across [the ocean of] existence

**12.5.** On earth is the wondrous Lord, the Son of Shachi,
the descent who purifies the fallen!
Lowly, wretched, foolish Ramananda Dasa [prays]:
Lord, carry me across [the ocean of] existence!

[^06-39]: Signature: "Ramananda Dasa". PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 229 (printed p. 218), 17th pallava, no. 38 (mark "॥৩৮॥২০৯৬॥"); raga vibhasa; MS
P-R-Sa no. 2205. GPT1 — p. 256, no. 25 (raga vibhasa); GPT2 — sect. 4.2, no. 25. On the attribution see note 24: the
signature "Ramananda Dasa" may belong either to Vasu Ramananda or to another poet.
[^06-40]: Gorochana is a yellow pigment for tilaka. "A swarm of bees on a lotus" — dark locks on the golden face.
[^06-41]: GPT1: "Having accomplished (sādhiyā) His virtues, revealing the kirtana…". The khol (mridanga) and kartals are the
instruments of sankirtana; "godlessness" (pāṣaṇḍa) — the opponents of bhakti, against whom the kirtana procession in
Navadvipa was directed (CB Madhya 23). MS "ka": "revealing" (parakāśe).

## 13. Ramananda — "nācata gaura naṭabara rasiyā…" (PK 2060)
*Lila: Gaura the dancer dances, finding no limit to the ocean of prema; remembering Vrindavana, He sighs deeply and,
laughing, calls "Rai, Rai!"; not concealing His secret, He stands bent in three places and plays the flute; He roars like a
lion and rolls on the ground. In PK it is in the 17th pallava ("Sri Gauranga's dance"). Signature: "Ramananda" (GPT:
"lowly Ramananda"). Raga beloyar.*[^06-42]

নাচত গৌর নটবর রসিয়া ।
প্রেম-পয়োধি অবধি নাহি পাওত
দিবস রজনি ফিরত ভাসি ভাসিয়া ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*nācata gaura naṭabara rasiyā |*
*prema-payodhi abadhi nāhi pāota*
*dibasa rajani phirata bhāsi bhāsiyā || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* nācata gaura — Gaura dances; naṭabara — the best of dancers; rasiyā — full of rasa; prema-payodhi — the ocean of prema; abadhi nāhi pāota — finds no limit; dibasa rajani phirata bhāsi bhāsiyā — day and night He moves about, floating and rocking

**13.1.** *(Refrain)* Gaura dances, the best of dancers, full of rasa;
finding no limit to the ocean of prema,
day and night He floats, rocking [on its waves].

সোঙরি বৃন্দাবন শ্বাস ছাড়ে ঘন ঘন
রাই রাই বলে হাসি হাসিয়া ।
নিজ-মন-মরম ভরম নাহি রাখত
রহত ত্রিভঙ্গ বাজাওত বাঁশিয়া ॥

*soṅari bṛndābana śvāsa chāṛe ghana ghana*
*rāi rāi bale hāsi hāsiyā |*
*nija-mana-marama bharama nāhi rākhata*
*rahata tribhaṅga bājāota bām̐śiyā ||*

*Word for word:* soṅari bṛndābana — remembering Vrindavana; śvāsa chāṛe ghana ghana — sighs deeply again and again; rāi rāi bale — says "Rai, Rai" (Radha); hāsi hāsiyā — laughing; nija-mana-marama bharama nāhi rākhata — keeps no secret of His heart; rahata tribhaṅga — stands bent in three places; bājāota bām̐śiyā — plays the flute

**13.2.** Remembering Vrindavana, again and again He sighs deeply,
laughing, He repeats: "Rai, Rai!"
Keeping no secret of His heart,
He stands bent in three places and plays the flute.[^06-43]

মত্ত সিংহসম ঘন ঘন গরজন
চঞ্চল পদ-নখ-শশিয়া ।
কটি-তটে অরুণ-বরণ বর অম্বর
খেণে খেণে উড়ত পড়ত খসি খসিয়া ॥

*matta siṃhasama ghana ghana garajana*
*cañcala pada-nakha-śaśiyā |*
*kaṭi-taṭe aruṇa-baraṇa bara ambara*
*kheṇe kheṇe uṛata paṛata khasi khasiyā ||*

*Word for word:* matta siṃha-sama — like an intoxicated lion; ghana ghana garajana — roars again and again; cañcala pada-nakha-śaśiyā — the restless moons of the toenails; kaṭi-taṭe — on the hips; aruṇa-baraṇa bara ambara — a fine crimson cloth; kheṇe kheṇe uṛata paṛata khasi khasiyā — again and again flies up, falls, slipping down

**13.3.** Like an intoxicated lion He roars again and again,
the moons of the nails of His restless feet flash;
on His hips a fine crimson cloth —
again and again it flies up, falls, slips down.

পুলকাঞ্চিত সব গৌর-কলেবর
কাটত অখিল পাপ-পুণ্য-ফাঁসিয়া ।
ধরণি উপরে খেণে লুঠত বৈঠত
উঠত রামানন্দ-ভয় নাশিয়া ॥২॥২০৬০॥

*pulakāñcita saba gaura-kalebara*
*kāṭata akhila pāpa-puṇya-phām̐siyā |*
*dharaṇi upare kheṇe luṭhata baiṭhata*
*uṭhata rāmānanda-bhaya nāśiyā ||2||2060||*

*Word for word:* pulakāñcita saba gaura-kalebara — Gaura's whole body covered with thrills; kāṭata akhila pāpa-puṇya-phām̐siyā — cuts through all the nooses of sin and piety; dharaṇi upare kheṇe luṭhata baiṭhata — now rolls on the ground, now sits; uṭhata — rises; rāmānanda-bhaya nāśiyā — destroying Ramananda's fear

**13.4.** Gaura's whole body is covered with thrills —
He cuts through all the nooses of sin and piety;
now He rolls on the ground, now sits,
now rises, destroying Ramananda's fear.[^06-44]

[^06-42]: Signature: "Ramananda". PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 215 (printed p. 204), 17th pallava ("Sri Gauranga's dance"), no. 2 (mark
"॥২॥২০৬০॥"), after the heading "Then Sri Gaurachandra befitting every time"; raga beloyar; MS P-R-Sa no. 2169. GPT1 —
p. 249, no. 4 (raga beloyar); GPT2 — sect. 4.2, no. 4 (signature "dīna rāmānanda"). On the attribution see note 24.
[^06-43]: "Rai" is Radha. "Bent in three places" (tribhaṅga) — the pose of Krishna playing the flute: Gaura reveals Himself in
the mood of Krishna (cf. PK 2120, chapter 1, no. 7: the Lord in the dress of Natavara). Gaudiya Vaishnava siddhanta sees
in this not imitation but a manifestation of His nature: Gaura is Krishna Himself, come in the mood of Radha (CC Adi 4).
MS P-R-Sa: "in the tribhangi pose" (tribhaṅgī).
[^06-44]: "The nooses of sin and piety" — the bonds of karma, both sinful and pious: prema frees one from both. MS "kha": "like
a lion" (siṃha yena); "gha": "the fear of existence" (bhababhaya). GPT: "He rolls, rises, sits — destroying the fear of
lowly Ramananda".

## 14. Yadunatha Dasa — "āmāra gaurāṅga jāne premera marama…" (PK 2125)
*Lila: Radha's mood: Gauranga knows the inmost essence of prema; absorbed in meditation, He has taken on Radha's colour; as
soon as He utters "Ra", His whole body quivers; as soon as He utters "dha", He sheds tears; His mind is immersed in the
manifestation of the mood of Gauri — Radha. Raga suhai.*[^06-45]

আমার গৌরাঙ্গ জানে প্রেমের মরম ।
ভাবিতে ভাবিতে ভেল রাধার বরণ ॥

*āmāra gaurāṅga jāne premera marama |*
*bhābite bhābite bhela rādhāra baraṇa ||*

*Word for word:* āmāra gaurāṅga — my Gauranga; jāne premera marama — knows the inmost essence of prema; bhābite bhābite — meditating and meditating; bhela rādhāra baraṇa — took on Radha's colour

**14.1.** My Gauranga knows the inmost essence of prema:
meditating and meditating, He has taken on Radha's colour.[^06-46]

রা বোল বলিতে পূর্ণিত কলেবর ।
ধা বোল বলিতে বহে নয়নের জল ॥

*rā bola balite pūrṇita kalebara |*
*dhā bola balite bahe nayanera jala ||*

*Word for word:* rā bola balite — as He utters "Ra"; pūrṇita kalebara — His body is overwhelmed; dhā bola balite — as He utters "dha"; bahe nayanera jala — tears flow from His eyes

**14.2.** As soon as He utters "Ra" — His whole body is overwhelmed;
as soon as He utters "dha" — tears flow from His eyes.

ধারা ধরণী সঘনে বহি যায় ।
পুলকে পূরিত তনু জপে নাম তায় ॥

*dhārā dharaṇī saghane bahi yāya |*
*pulake pūrita tanu jape nāma tāya ||*

*Word for word:* dhārā dharaṇī saghane bahi yāya — the streams run incessantly over the ground; pulake pūrita tanu — the body full of thrills; jape nāma tāya — repeats that name

**14.3.** Streams [of tears] run incessantly over the ground;
His body, covered with thrills, repeats that name.

মন নিমগন গৌরী-ভাবের প্রকাশ ।
এক মুখে কি কহব যদুনাথ দাস ॥১৭॥২১২৫॥

*mana nimagana gaurī-bhābera prakāśa |*
*eka mukhe ki kahaba yadunātha dāsa ||17||2125||*

*Word for word:* mana nimagana — the mind is immersed; gaurī-bhābera prakāśa — in the manifestation of Gauri's (Radha's) mood; eka mukhe ki kahaba — what can one tell with a single mouth; yadunātha dāsa — Yadunatha Dasa

**14.4.** His mind is immersed in the manifestation of Gauri's mood —
how can one tell of it with a single mouth, [says] Yadunatha Dasa?[^06-47]

[^06-45]: Signature: "Yadunatha Dasa". PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 239 (printed p. 228), no. 17 (mark "॥১৭॥২১২৫॥"), immediately before
PK 2126 (no. 15) and PK 2127 (Shivananda, chapter 5, no. 10); raga suhai; MS P-R-Sa no. 2232. GPT1 — p. 36, no. 29 (raga
suhai), in a series of Yadunatha's padas (no. 27 = PK 2191, no. 4). This pada was not in the stage-1 catalogue (found during
verification). On the author see note 12.
[^06-46]: "Has taken on Radha's colour": Gaura's golden form is Radha's radiance, with which Krishna has covered Himself,
accepting Her mood (CC Adi 4: "the Lord adorned with the mood and radiance of Radha"). This is the mood of pure prema, not a
worldly feeling. GPT1: "haila" (became) instead of "bhela".
[^06-47]: Gauri ("the golden one") is a name of Radha. MSS "kha", "ca": "nigamana" instead of "nimagana"; GPT1: "…to Yadunatha
Dasa".

## 15. Yadunatha Dasa — "gadādhara narahari kare dhari gaurahari…" (PK 2126; BR, pp. 918–919)
*Lila: Gaurahari, holding the hands of Gadadhara and Narahari, rolls on the ground in prema and loudly sings the virtues of
Vrindavana; remembering His pastimes in Nidhuvana, He weeps: "Yamuna!"; He recalls the friendship of Subala, the words of
Vrinda, the love of Lalita and Vishakha: "Where is the Queen of My life? Where is Govardhana? Where are My flute and yellow
garments?" Narahari Chakravarti cites the pada in the *Bhakti-ratnakara* among the testimonies to the Lord's moods in
Navadvipa, next to the pada of Govinda Ghosha (PK 2128). According to M-1961 it is an eyewitness pada. Raga gandhara (PK),
kamoda (BR).*[^06-48]

গদাধর নরহরি করে ধরি গৌরহরি
প্রেমাবেশে ধরণী লোটায় ।
কহিলে না হয় তত ফুকরি ফুকরি পহু
বৃন্দা-বিপিন-গুণ গায় ॥

*gadādhara narahari kare dhari gaurahari*
*premābeśe dharaṇī loṭāya |*
*kahile nā haya tata phukari phukari pahu*
*bṛndā-bipina-guṇa gāya ||*

*Word for word:* gadādhara narahari kare dhari — holding the hands of Gadadhara and Narahari; gaurahari — Gaurahari; premābeśe dharaṇī loṭāya — rolls on the ground in the ecstasy of prema; kahile nā haya tata — words cannot express it; phukari phukari pahum̐ — the Lord, crying aloud; bṛndā-bipina-guṇa gāya — sings the virtues of Vrinda's forest

**15.1.** Holding the hands of Gadadhara and Narahari, Gaurahari
rolls on the ground in the ecstasy of prema;
words cannot express it: the Lord, crying aloud,
sings the virtues of Vrinda's forest.

নিজ লীলা নিধুবন সোঙরিয়া উচাটন
কান্দে পহু যমুনা বলিয়া ।
নয়নে বহিছে কত সুরধুনী-ধারা মত
দর দর শ্রীবুক বাহিয়া ॥

*nija līlā nidhubana soṅariyā ucāṭana*
*kānde pahu yamunā baliyā |*
*nayane bahiche kata suradhunī-dhārā mata*
*dara dara śrībuka bāhiyā ||*

*Word for word:* nija līlā nidhubana — His own pastimes in Nidhuvana; soṅariyā ucāṭana — remembering, in agitation; kānde pahum̐ yamunā baliyā — the Lord weeps, calling "Yamuna"; nayane bahiche kata — so many [tears] flow from the eyes; suradhunī-dhārā mata — like streams of the Suradhuni (the Ganga); dara dara śrī-buka bāhiyā — running down the holy breast

**15.2.** Remembering His pastimes in Nidhuvana, in agitation
the Lord weeps, calling: "Yamuna!"
From His eyes, like streams of the Suradhuni, [tears] flow,
running down His holy breast.[^06-49]

সুবলের শুদ্ধ সখ্য বৃন্দাদেবীর প্রিয় বাক্য
ললিতার ললিত সুস্নেহ ।
বিশাখার প্রেম-কথা সোঙরি মরমে বেথা
কহি কহি না ধরয়ে দেহ ॥

*subalera śuddha sakhya bṛndādebīra priya bākya*
*lalitāra lalita susneha |*
*biśākhāra prema-kathā soṅari marame bethā*
*kahi kahi nā dharaye deha ||*

*Word for word:* subalera śuddha sakhya — Subala's pure friendship; bṛndā-debīra priya bākya — Vrinda-devi's sweet words; lalitāra lalita susneha — Lalita's tender love; biśākhāra prema-kathā — Vishakha's talk of prema; soṅari marame bethā — recalling, with pain in the heart; kahi kahi nā dharaye deha — speaking and speaking, He cannot hold up His body

**15.3.** Subala's pure friendship, Vrinda-devi's sweet words,
Lalita's tender love,
Vishakha's talk of prema — recalling them, with pain in His heart,
speaking and speaking, He cannot stand.[^06-50]

কাঁহা মোর প্রাণেশ্বরী কাঁহা গোবর্ধন-গিরি
কাঁহা মোর বংশী পীত বাস ।
প্রেম-সিন্ধু উথলিল জগত ভরিয়া গেল
না বুঝিল যদুনাথ দাস ॥১৮॥২১২৬॥

*kām̐hā mora prāṇeśvarī kām̐hā gobardhana-giri*
*kām̐hā mora baṃśī pīta bāsa |*
*prema-sindhu uthalila jagata bhariyā gela*
*nā bujhila yadunātha dāsa ||18||2126||*

*Word for word:* kām̐hā mora prāṇeśvarī — where is the Queen of My life; kām̐hā gobardhana-giri — where is Govardhana Hill; kām̐hā mora baṃśī pīta bāsa — where are My flute and yellow garments; prema-sindhu uthalila — the ocean of prema overflowed; jagata bhariyā gela — the world was flooded; nā bujhila yadunātha dāsa — Yadunatha Dasa did not comprehend

**15.4.** "Where is the Queen of My life? Where is Govardhana Hill?
Where are My flute and yellow garments?"
The ocean of prema overflowed, flooding the whole world —
only Yadunatha Dasa did not comprehend [it].[^06-51]

[^06-48]: Signature: "Yadunatha Dasa". PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 239 (printed p. 228), no. 18 (mark "॥১৮॥২১২৬॥"); raga gandhara
("shri-gandhara"); MS P-R-Sa no. 2233. BR, 12th wave: 1913 ed., pp. 918–919 ("again kamoda"); 1960 ed. vv. 2993–2996. GPT1 —
p. 281, no. 13; GPT2 — sect. 4.3, no. 13. In the stage-1 catalogue the pada was listed under Shivananda Sena (ShS-002) with
the PK number 2123 — wrongly. B. B. Majumdar (1961) sees in it an eyewitness testimony to the Lord's mood in Navadvipa.
[^06-49]: Nidhuvana is a grove in Vrindavana, the place of Radha and Krishna's most intimate pastimes. Here the Lord, in the
mood of Krishna, recalls His pastimes in Vraja (cf. PK 2128, chapter 4, no. 4, and Narahari's PK 2122, chapter 3, no. 1).
[^06-50]: Subala is a friend of Krishna; Vrinda-devi is the goddess of Vrindavana, the arranger of His pastimes; Lalita and
Vishakha are Radha's closest friends. BR: "Lalita's tender love" (sneha), "recalling, with pain in the heart" (soṅari marama
bethā).
[^06-51]: "The Queen of My life" (prāṇeśvarī) is Radha. "Did not comprehend": the poet's humility — he cannot contain that ocean.
Cf. the similar ending in Govinda Ghosha (PK 2128).

## 16. Vamshidasa — "bhābābeśe gorācām̐da bibhora haiyā…" (PK 2851)
*Lila: the mood of a cowherd friend: Gorachand in ecstasy calls Shridama, Subala, Vasudama, "brother Balarama", calls the
cows Dhavali and Shangali and, crying "Kalindi! Yamuna!", floats in tears of prema. In PK it is a gaura-chandrika to the
"morning lila" in the section of the "eightfold eternal lila". Signature: "Vamshidasa". Raga bhatiyari.*[^06-52]

ভাবাবেশে গোরাচাঁদ বিভোর হইয়া ।
ক্ষেণে ক্ষেণে ডাকে ভাইয়া শ্রীদাম বলিয়া ॥

*bhābābeśe gorācām̐da bibhora haiyā |*
*kṣeṇe kṣeṇe ḍāke bhāiyā śrīdāma baliyā ||*

*Word for word:* bhābābeśe — in the ecstasy of His mood; gorācām̐da bibhora haiyā — Gorachand, lost to Himself; kheṇe kheṇe ḍāke — again and again calls; bhāiyā śrīdāma baliyā — saying "Brother Shridama!"

**16.1.** In the ecstasy of His mood Gorachand, lost to Himself,
again and again calls: "Brother Shridama!"

ক্ষেণে ডাকে সুবলেরে ক্ষেণে বসুদাম ।
ক্ষেণে ডাকে ভাই মোর দাদা বলরাম ॥

*kṣeṇe ḍāke subalere kṣeṇe basudāma |*
*kṣeṇe ḍāke bhāi mora dādā balarāma ||*

*Word for word:* kheṇe ḍāke subalere — now calls Subala; kheṇe basudāma — now Vasudama; kheṇe ḍāke — now calls; bhāi mora dādā balarāma — "My brother, elder brother Balarama"

**16.2.** Now He calls Subala, now Vasudama,
now He calls: "My brother, elder brother Balarama!"[^06-53]

ধবলি শাঙলি বলি করয়ে ফুকার ।
পুরল পুলকে অঙ্গ বহে প্রেম-ধার ॥

*dhabali śāṅali bali karaye phukāra |*
*purala pulake aṅga bahe prema-dhāra ||*

*Word for word:* dhabali śāṅali bali — saying "Dhavali! Shangali!" (names of cows); karaye phukāra — calls out loudly; purala pulake aṅga — the body is covered with thrills; bahe prema-dhāra — streams of prema flow

**16.3.** He calls out: "Dhavali! Shangali!" —
His body covered with thrills, streams of prema flow.

কালিন্দি যমুনা বলি প্রেম-জলে ভাসে ।
পুরব পড়িল মনে কহে বংশীদাসে ॥১৪॥২৮৫১॥

*kālindi yamunā bali prema-jale bhāse |*
*puraba paṛila mane kahe baṃśīdāse ||14||2851||*

*Word for word:* kālindi yamunā bali — crying "Kalindi! Yamuna!"; prema-jale bhāse — floats in the waters of prema; puraba paṛila mane — the past came to mind; kahe baṃśīdāse — says Vamshidasa

**16.4.** Crying "Kalindi! Yamuna!", He floats in the waters of prema:
the past has come back to His mind, says Vamshidasa.[^06-54]

[^06-52]: Signature: "Vamshidasa". PK: vol. 4, PDF p. 181 (printed p. 172), "Then the morning lila", no. 14 (mark
"॥১৪॥২৮৫১॥"); raga bhatiyari. GPT1 — p. 282, no. 19 (raga bhatiyari); GPT2 — sect. 4.3, no. 19. S. Ray considered "Vamshidasa"
and "Vamshivadana" one poet; Majumdar separates Vamshidasa — a disciple of Srinivasa Acharya (a later poet) — from
Vamshivadana, the guardian of Vishnupriya. Hence the attribution to a contemporary is doubtful (C).
[^06-53]: Shridama, Subala, Vasudama are Krishna's cowherd friends; Balarama is His elder brother. Cf. Gaura's goshtha-lila in
the padas of Vamshivadana (PK 2564, chapter 1, no. 12) and Chaitanyadasa (PK 1169, chapter 4, no. 7): in Navadvipa the Lord
reveals the mood of Krishna the cowherd.
[^06-54]: Dhavali ("the white one") and Shangali ("the dark one") are Krishna's cows; Kalindi is the Yamuna, daughter of the
Sun. "The past" — the pastimes of Vraja.

## 17. Ramananda — "āre mora āre mora gaurāṅga rāya…" (PK 1417)
*Lila: the boat play on the Ganga: Gauranga, having become a young boatman, plays in a boat with His companions and dear
Gadadhara, as once [Krishna on the Yamuna]; the boat nearly sinks in the gusts of wind, and Gora laughs; on both banks the
people of Nadia watch and cry "Haribol". In PK it is a gaura-chandrika to the "boat play" (nauka-vilasa) of Radha and
Krishna on the Yamuna. Signature: "Ramananda". Raga dhanashi.*[^06-55]

আরে মোর আরে মোর গৌরাঙ্গ রায় ।
সুরধুনী মাঝে যাইয়া নবীন নাবিক হইয়া
সহচর মিলিয়া খেলায় ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*āre mora āre mora gaurāṅga rāya |*
*suradhunī mājhe yāiyā nabīna nābika haiyā*
*sahacara miliyā khelāya || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* āre mora āre mora — O my, O my; gaurāṅga rāya — Gauranga Raya; suradhunī mājhe yāiyā — going out into the middle of the Suradhuni (the Ganga); nabīna nābika haiyā — having become a young boatman; sahacara miliyā khelāya — plays together with His companions

**17.1.** *(Refrain)* O my, O my Gauranga Raya!
Going out into the middle of the Suradhuni, having become a young boatman,
He plays together with His companions.

প্রিয় গদাধর সঙ্গে পূরব রভস-রঙ্গে
নৌকায় বসিয়া করে কেলি ।
ডুবু ডুবু করে না বহয়ে বিষম বা
দেখি হাসে গোরা বনমালী ॥

*priya gadādhara saṅge pūraba rabhasa-raṅge*
*naukāya basiyā kare keli |*
*ḍubu ḍubu kare nā bahaye biṣama bā*
*dekhi hāse gorā banamālī ||*

*Word for word:* priya gadādhara saṅge — with dear Gadadhara; pūraba rabhasa-raṅge — in the merriment of the former play; naukāya basiyā kare keli — seated in the boat, sports; ḍubu ḍubu kare nā — the boat (nā = nau) is about to sink; bahaye biṣama vā — a fierce wind blows; dekhi hāse gorā banamālī — seeing it, Gora who wears the forest garland laughs

**17.2.** With dear Gadadhara, in the merriment of the former play,
seated in the boat, He sports;
the boat is about to sink, a fierce wind blows —
seeing it, Gora, who wears the forest garland, laughs.[^06-56]

কেহো করে উতরোল ঘন ঘন হরিবোল
দু কূলে নদীয়ার লোক দেখে ।
ভুবন-মোহন নায়্যা দেখিয়া বিবশ হৈয়া
যুবতী ভুলিল লাখে লাখে ॥

*keho kare utarola ghana ghana haribola*
*du kūle nadīyāra loka dekhe |*
*bhubana-mohana nāyyā dekhiyā bibaśa haiyā*
*yubatī bhulila lākhe lākhe ||*

*Word for word:* keho kare utarola — someone makes a din; ghana ghana haribola — "Haribol" again and again; du kūle nadīyāra loka dekhe — on both banks the people of Nadia watch; bhubana-mohana nāyyā — the world-enchanting Boatman; dekhiyā bibaśa haiyā — seeing, enraptured; yubatī bhulila lākhe lākhe — hundreds of thousands of young wives forgot themselves

**17.3.** Someone makes a din, crying "Haribol" again and again,
on both banks the people of Nadia watch;
seeing the world-enchanting Boatman, enraptured,
hundreds of thousands of young wives forgot themselves.[^06-57]

জগজন-চিত্ত-চোর গৌরসুন্দর মোর
যে করে তাহাই পরতেক ।
কহে দীন রামানন্দে এ হেন আনন্দ-কন্দে
বঞ্চিত রহিলুঁ মুঞি এক ॥৯॥১৪১৭॥

*jagajana-citta-cora gaurasundara mora*
*ye kare tāhāi parateka |*
*kahe dīna rāmānande e hena ānanda-kande*
*bañcita rahilum̐ muñi eka ||9||1417||*

*Word for word:* jagajana-citta-cora — thief of the hearts of the world's people; gaurasundara mora — my Gaurasundara; ye kare tāhāi parateka — whatever He does is before the eyes; kahe dīna rāmānande — lowly Ramananda says; e hena ānanda-kande — in such a fount of bliss; bañcita rahilum̐ muñi eka — I alone have remained deprived

**17.4.** The thief of the hearts of the world's people is my Gaurasundara:
whatever He does is before everyone's eyes.
Lowly Ramananda says: in such a fount of bliss
I alone have remained deprived.

[^06-55]: Signature: "Ramananda". PK: vol. 2, PDF p. 391 (printed p. 378), "Then the boat play on the Yamuna. Fixing the mind on
the feet of Sri Radha and Krishna, listen. First — Sri Mahaprabhu", no. 9 (mark "॥৯॥১৪১৭॥"); raga dhanashi; MS P-R-Sa
no. 1963. GPT1 — pp. 333–334, no. 43 (raga dhanashi); GPT2 — sect. 5.1 (OCR 38886). On the attribution see note 24.
[^06-56]: "The former play" (pūraba rabhasa) — Krishna's play with Radha in a boat on the Yamuna. "Who wears the forest
garland" (banamālī) is an epithet of Krishna. MS "kha": "laughing".
[^06-57]: Cf. note 21: the image speaks of the Lord's irresistible beauty, not of worldly passion; the Gaudiya Vaishnava
tradition does not accept worship of Gaura in the mood of "gaura-nagari". MSS "ka", "gha": "having gathered" (meliyā);
"kha": "that" (tāi).

## 18. Ramananda Dasa — "suradhuni-tire āju gaura kiśora…" (PK 2615)
*Lila: jhulana on the bank of the Ganga: the companions have woven a swing of flowers, Gaura swings together with
Gadadhara; Mukunda, Madhava, Vasu and Haridasa sing of former pastimes. In PK it is a gaura-chandrika to the "swing lila" in
the section of the "eightfold eternal lila". Signature: "Ramananda Dasa". Raga saranga.*[^06-58]

সুরধুনি-তিরে আজু গৌর কিশোর ।
ঝুলন রঙ্গ-রসে পহু ভেল ভোর ॥

*suradhuni-tire āju gaura kiśora |*
*jhulana raṅga-rase pahu bhela bhora ||*

*Word for word:* suradhuni-tire — on the bank of the Suradhuni (the Ganga); āju gaura kiśora — today young Gaura; jhulana raṅga-rase — in the taste of the swing play; pahum̐ bhela bhora — the Lord is lost

**18.1.** Today on the bank of the Suradhuni is young Gaura:
the Lord is lost in the taste of the swing play.

বিবিধ কুসুমে সভে রচই হিন্দোল ।
সব সহচরগণ আনন্দে ভোল ॥

*bibidha kusume sabhe racai hindola |*
*saba sahacaragaṇa ānande bhola ||*

*Word for word:* bibidha kusume — out of various flowers; sabhe racai hindola — all weave a swing; saba sahacara-gaṇa — all the companions; ānande bhola — are drunk with bliss

**18.2.** Out of various flowers they have all woven a swing;
all the companions are drunk with bliss.

ঝুলয়ে গৌর পুন গদাধর সঙ্গ ।
তাহে কত উপজয়ে প্রেম-তরঙ্গ ॥

*jhulaye gaura puna gadādhara saṅga |*
*tāhe kata upajaye prema-taraṅga ||*

*Word for word:* jhulaye gaura — Gaura swings; puna gadādhara saṅga — and with Him Gadadhara; tāhe kata upajaye prema-taraṅga — how many waves of prema arise thereby

**18.3.** Gaura swings, and with Him Gadadhara:
how many waves of prema arise thereby!

মুকুন্দ মাধব বাসু হরিদাস মেলি ।
গাওত পুরব রভস-রস-কেলি ॥

*mukunda mādhaba bāsu haridāsa meli |*
*gāota puraba rabhasa-rasa-keli ||*

*Word for word:* mukunda mādhaba bāsu haridāsa meli — Mukunda, Madhava, Vasu, Haridasa together; gāota puraba rabhasa-rasa-keli — sing of the joyful play of former times

**18.4.** Mukunda, Madhava, Vasu, Haridasa together
sing of the joyful play of former times.[^06-59]

নদিয়া নগরে কত ঐছে বিলাস ।
রামানন্দ দাস করত সোই আশ ॥১৪॥২৬১৫॥

*nadiyā nagare kata aiche bilāsa |*
*rāmānanda dāsa karata soi āśa ||14||2615||*

*Word for word:* nadiyā nagare — in the town of Nadia; kata aiche bilāsa — how many such pastimes; rāmānanda dāsa — Ramananda Dasa; karata soi āśa — cherishes that hope

**18.5.** How many such pastimes in the town of Nadia! —
Ramananda Dasa cherishes the hope [of seeing them].

[^06-58]: Signature: "Ramananda Dasa". PK: vol. 4, PDF p. 94 (printed pp. 84–85), 30th pallava ("The eightfold eternal lila"),
"Then the swing lila", no. 14 (mark "॥১৪॥২৬১৫॥"); raga saranga. GPT1 — p. 326, no. 18 (raga saranga); GPT2 — sect. 5.1,
no. 18. In the stage-1 catalogue (RM-009) the PK number was not given. Cf. the jhulana padas of Vasu Ghosha (PK 1550) and
Narahari (PK 1559) — chapter 4, nos. 5–6. On the attribution see note 24.
[^06-59]: Mukunda is Mukunda Datta; Madhava and Vasu are the Ghosha brothers; Haridasa is Haridasa Thakura. "The play of former
times" — the swing of Radha and Krishna in Vraja. MSS "ka", "ca" in 18.2: "lost to themselves" (bibhora); so too GPT1.

## 19. Shankara Ghosha (?) — "śrībāsa-aṅgane binoda bandhāne…" (KGC 30.2)
*Lila: Nityananda's dance in Srivasa's courtyard: men and gods, men and women run to see; the devotees sing, the khol and
kartals sound; in the midst, intoxicated with the mood of "Brother", Nitai dances in the guise of a wrestler, leaps and
roars, watering the earth with a rain of prema; Advaita roars, Srivasa weeps holding His feet, Mukunda sobs embracing
Gadadhara. In KGC it is a pada on Nityananda signed by Shankara Ghosha; in GPT the same pada is about Gauranga and signed by
Vrindavana Dasa. Raga mangala.*[^06-60]

শ্রীবাস-অঙ্গনে বিনোদ বন্ধানে
নাচে নিত্যানন্দ রায় ।
মনুজ দৈবত পুরুষ যোষিত
সবাই দেখিতে ধায় ॥

*śrībāsa-aṅgane binoda bandhāne*
*nāce nityānanda rāya |*
*manuja daibata puruṣa yoṣita*
*sabāi dekhite dhāya ||*

*Word for word:* śrībāsa-aṅgane — in Srivasa's courtyard; binoda bandhāne — to a wondrous rhythm; nāce nityānanda rāya — Nityananda Raya dances; manuja daibata — men and gods; puruṣa yoṣita — males and females; sabāi dekhite dhāya — all run to see

**19.1.** In Srivasa's courtyard, to a wondrous rhythm,
Nityananda Raya dances;
men and gods, males and females —
all run to see.

ভকত-মণ্ডল গাওত মঙ্গল
বাজে খোল করতাল ।
মাঝে উনমত নিতাই নাচত
ভাইয়ার ভাবে মাতোয়ার ॥

*bhakata-maṇḍala gāota maṅgala*
*bāje khola karatāla |*
*mājhe unamata nitāi nācata*
*bhāiyāra bhābe mātoyāra ||*

*Word for word:* bhakata-maṇḍala gāota maṅgala — the circle of devotees sings an auspicious song; bāje khola karatāla — the khol and kartals sound; mājhe unamata nitāi nācata — in the midst, beside Himself (with prema), Nitai dances; bhāiyāra bhābe mātoyāra — intoxicated with the mood of "Brother"

**19.2.** The circle of devotees sings an auspicious song,
the khol and kartals sound;
in the midst, beside Himself with prema, Nitai dances,
intoxicated with the mood of "Brother".[^06-61]

হেম-স্তম্ভ-জিনি বাহু সুবলনি
সিংহ জিনি কটিদেশ ।
চন্দ্র বদন কমল নয়ন
মদন-মোহন বেশ ॥

*hema-stambha-jini bāhu subalani*
*siṃha jini kaṭideśa |*
*candra badana kamala nayana*
*madana-mohana beśa ||*

*Word for word:* hema-stambha-jini — surpassing golden pillars; bāhu subalani — the roundness of the arms; siṃha jini kaṭideśa — a waist slimmer than a lion's; candra badana — a moon face; kamala nayana — lotus eyes; madana-mohana beśa — a form that enchants Cupid

**19.3.** His arms lovelier than golden pillars,
His waist slimmer than a lion's;
His face a moon, His eyes lotuses,
a form that enchants Cupid.

গরজে পুন পুন লম্ফ ঘন ঘন
মল্লবেশ ধরি নাচই ।
অরুণ-লোচনে প্রেম-বরিখণে
অবনী-মণ্ডল সিঞ্চই ॥

*garaje puna puna lampha ghana ghana*
*mallabeśa dhari nācai |*
*aruṇa-locane prema-barikhaṇe*
*abanī-maṇḍala siñcai ||*
