*Word for word:* garaje puna puna — roars again and again; lampha ghana ghana — leaps again and again; mallabeśa dhari nācai — dances in the guise of a wrestler; aruṇa-locane — from the reddish eyes; prema-barikhaṇe — with a rain of prema; abanī-maṇḍala siñcai — waters the circle of the earth

**19.4.** Again and again He roars, again and again He leaps,
in the guise of a wrestler He dances;
from His reddish eyes, with a rain of prema,
He waters the circle of the earth.[^06-62]

ধরণী-মণ্ডলে প্রেমের বাদর
করল অবধূত-চান্দ ।
না জানে নর-নারী ভুবন দশ-চারি
রূপ হেরি হেরি কান্দ ॥

*dharaṇī-maṇḍale premera bādara*
*karala abadhūta-cānda |*
*nā jāne nara-nārī bhubana daśa-cāri*
*rūpa heri heri kānda ||*

*Word for word:* dharaṇī-maṇḍale — upon the circle of the earth; premera bādara — a downpour of prema; karala abadhūta-cānda — the Avadhuta-moon (Nityananda) poured; nā jāne — unaware of themselves; nara-nārī bhubana daśa-cāri — the men and women of the fourteen worlds; rūpa heri heri kānda — weep gazing and gazing at His beauty

**19.5.** Upon the circle of the earth a downpour of prema
has the Avadhuta-moon poured;
the men and women of the fourteen worlds, forgetting themselves,
weep, gazing and gazing at His beauty.

শান্তিপুর-নাথ গরজে অবিরত
দেখিয়া প্রেমের বিকার ।
ধরিয়া শ্রীচরণ করয়ে রোদন
পণ্ডিত শ্রীবাস উদার ॥

*śāntipura-nātha garaje abirata*
*dekhiyā premera bikāra |*
*dhariyā śrīcaraṇa karaye rodana*
*paṇḍita śrībāsa udāra ||*

*Word for word:* śāntipura-nātha — the Lord of Shantipura (Advaita); garaje abirata — roars without cease; dekhiyā premera bikāra — seeing the transformations of prema; dhariyā śrī-caraṇa — holding the holy feet; karaye rodana — weeps; paṇḍita śrībāsa udāra — magnanimous Pandita Srivasa

**19.6.** The Lord of Shantipura roars without cease,
seeing the transformations of prema;
holding the holy feet, magnanimous
Pandita Srivasa weeps.

মুকুন্দ কুতূহলী কান্দয়ে ফুলি ফুলি
ধরিয়া গদাধর-কোর ।
নয়নে বহে প্রেম ঠাকুর অভিরাম
সঘনে হরি হরি বোল ॥

*mukunda kutūhalī kāndaye phuli phuli*
*dhariyā gadādhara-kora |*
*nayane bahe prema ṭhākura abhirāma*
*saghane hari hari bola ||*

*Word for word:* mukunda kutūhalī — Mukunda, rejoicing; kāndaye phuli phuli — sobs and sobs; dhariyā gadādhara-kora — embracing Gadadhara; nayane bahe prema — prema flows from the eyes; ṭhākura abhirāma — [of] Thakura Abhirama; saghane hari hari bola — again and again "Hari, Hari"

**19.7.** Mukunda, rejoicing, sobs and sobs,
embracing Gadadhara;
from the eyes of Thakura Abhirama prema flows,
again and again resounds "Hari, Hari!"[^06-63]

না জানে দিবানিশি প্রেম-রসে ভাসি
সকল সহচর-বৃন্দে ।
শঙ্কর ঘোষ দাস করত প্রতি আশ
নিতাই-চরণারবিন্দে ॥

*nā jāne dibāniśi prema-rase bhāsi*
*sakala sahacara-bṛnde |*
*śaṅkara ghoṣa dāsa karata prati āśa*
*nitāi-caraṇārabinde ||*

*Word for word:* nā jāne dibāniśi — knowing neither day nor night; prema-rase bhāsi — floating in the taste of prema; sakala sahacara-bṛnde — all the companions; śaṅkara ghoṣa dāsa — Shankara Ghosha Dasa; karata prati āśa — cherishes hope; nitāi-caraṇārabinde — in Nitai's lotus feet

**19.8.** Knowing neither day nor night, in the taste of prema float
all the companions;
Shankara Ghosha Dasa cherishes hope
in Nitai's lotus feet.

[^06-60]: Signature: "Shankara Ghosha Dasa". KGC: 30th kshanada (purnima), no. 2 ("to Sri Nityanandachandra"), pp. 239–241;
raga mangala. GPT1 — p. 275, no. 88, and GPT2 — sect. 4.2, no. 88 (raga mangala): "In Srivasa's courtyard… Gauranga Raya
dances", without stanza 19.3, with a different ending: "Knowing neither day nor night, in the taste of prema float all the
companions; Vrindavana Dasa reveals prema at Nitai's lotus feet". B. B. Majumdar (1961) cites the pada as Shankara Ghosha's
(after KGC). The attribution is disputed (C): KGC is older than GPT, but a later substitution of the signature is possible
in the KGC recension too.
[^06-61]: "The mood of 'Brother'" (bhāiyāra bhābe) — Nityananda's love for Gauranga, His Brother (cf. chapter 5, note 53). GPT:
"the khol and kartals sound" (bājata).
[^06-62]: "In the guise of a wrestler" (mallabeśa) — Nityananda reveals the mood of Balarama. GPT in 19.5: "…all men and women,
seeing the beauty of the Lord of the world, weep".
[^06-63]: Abhirama Thakura is a companion of Nityananda (in Vraja, Shridama). GPT: "again and again resounds 'Brother,
brother!'". The Lord of Shantipura is Advaita Acharya.

## 20. Murari (?) — "premābeśe prabhure rākhiyā śāntipure…" (PK 2231)
*Lila: after the sannyasa: leaving the Lord, overwhelmed by prema, in Shantipura, Nityananda comes to Nadia; thinking of
Shachi's grief, He rolls on the ground on the way; arriving at the house, He stands before the mother, sighing heavily — His
heart breaks to tell of His Brother's sannyasa: "Gaura has taken sannyasa and come to Shantipura; He has sent Me to fetch
you." Shachi, Nitai and all Nadia weep. According to Majumdar, Murari Gupta's authorship is unproven: in one of the
manuscripts known to the compiler of GPT the same pada bears the name of Vasu Ghosha. Raga suhai.*[^06-64]

প্রেমাবেশে প্রভুরে রাখিয়া শান্তিপুরে ।
নিত্যানন্দ প্রভু আইলা নদীয়া নগরে ॥

*premābeśe prabhure rākhiyā śāntipure |*
*nityānanda prabhu āilā nadīyā nagare ||*

*Word for word:* premābeśe prabhure — the Lord, overwhelmed by prema; rākhiyā śāntipure — leaving in Shantipura; nityānanda prabhu āilā — Lord Nityananda came; nadīyā nagare — to the town of Nadia

**20.1.** Leaving the Lord, overwhelmed by prema, in Shantipura,
Lord Nityananda came to the town of Nadia.

ভাবিয়া শচীর দুখ নিত্যানন্দ রায় ।
পথ মাঝে অবনীতে গড়াগড়ি যায় ॥

*bhābiyā śacīra dukha nityānanda rāya |*
*patha mājhe abanīte gaṛāgaṛi yāya ||*

*Word for word:* bhābiyā śacīra dukha — thinking of Shachi's grief; nityānanda rāya — Nityananda Raya; patha mājhe — in the middle of the road; abanīte gaṛāgaṛi yāya — rolls on the ground

**20.2.** Thinking of Shachi's grief, Nityananda Raya
rolls on the ground in the middle of the road.

ক্ষণেকে সম্বরি নিতাই আইলেন ঘরে ।
শুনি শচী ঠাকুরাণী আইলা বাহিরে ॥

*kṣaṇeke sambari nitāi āilena ghare |*
*śuni śacī ṭhākurāṇī āilā bāhire ||*

*Word for word:* kṣaṇeke sambari — barely composing Himself; nitāi āilena ghare — Nitai came to the house; śuni — hearing; śacī ṭhākurāṇī āilā bāhire — Shachi Thakurani came outside

**20.3.** Barely composing Himself, Nitai came to the house;
hearing it, Shachi Thakurani came outside.

দাঁড়াঞা মায়ের আগে ছাড়য়ে নিশ্বাস ।
প্রাণ বিদরয়ে ভাইয়ের কহিতে সন্ন্যাস ॥

*dām̐ṛāñā māyera āge chāṛaye niśvāsa |*
*prāṇa bidaraye bhāiyera kahite sannyāsa ||*

*Word for word:* dām̐ṛāñā māyera āge — standing before the mother; chāṛaye niśvāsa — sighs heavily; prāṇa bidaraye — the heart breaks; bhāiyera kahite sannyāsa — to tell of His Brother's sannyasa

**20.4.** Standing before the mother, He sighs heavily:
His heart breaks to tell of His Brother's sannyasa.

সন্ন্যাস করিয়া গৌর আইলা শান্তিপুরে ।
আমারে পাঠাঞা দিল তোমা লইবারে ॥

*sannyāsa kariyā gaura āilā śāntipure |*
*āmāre pāṭhāñā dila tomā laibāre ||*

*Word for word:* sannyāsa kariyā gaura — Gaura, having taken sannyasa; āilā śāntipure — came to Shantipura; āmāre pāṭhāñā dila — sent Me; tomā laibāre — to fetch you

**20.5.** "Gaura has taken sannyasa and come to Shantipura;
He has sent Me to fetch you."[^06-65]

শচী কান্দে নিতাই কান্দে নদীয়া-নিবাসী ।
সভারে ছাড়িয়া নিমাই হইলা সন্ন্যাসী ॥

*śacī kānde nitāi kānde nadīyā-nibāsī |*
*sabhāre chāṛiyā nimāi hailā sannyāsī ||*

*Word for word:* śacī kānde — Shachi weeps; nitāi kānde — Nitai weeps; nadīyā-nibāsī — the people of Nadia [weep]; sabhāre chāṛiyā — leaving everyone; nimāi hailā sannyāsī — Nimai has become a sannyasi

**20.6.** Shachi weeps, Nitai weeps, the people of Nadia weep:
"Leaving everyone, Nimai has become a sannyasi!"

কহয়ে মুরারি গোরাচাঁদ না দেখিলে ।
নিশ্চয় মরিব প্রবেশিব গঙ্গা-জলে ॥১৪॥২২৩১॥

*kahaye murāri gorācām̐da nā dekhile |*
*niścaya mariba prabeśiba gaṅgā-jale ||14||2231||*

*Word for word:* kahaye murāri — Murari says; gorācām̐da nā dekhile — if I do not see Gorachand; niścaya mariba — I shall surely die; prabeśiba gaṅgā-jale — I shall enter the waters of the Ganga

**20.7.** Murari says: if I do not see Gorachand,
I shall surely die — I shall enter the waters of the Ganga.[^06-66]

[^06-64]: Signature: "Murari". PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 279 (printed p. 268), 21st pallava ("Sri Gauranga's sannyasa etc."), no. 14
(mark "॥১৪॥২২৩১॥"); raga suhai; MS P-R-Sa no. 2336. GPT1 — p. 378, no. 40 (raga dhanashi; in Majumdar "pp. 373–374"), GPT2 —
sect. 5.3, no. 40: longer, with three extra couplets (see note 65); in a note GPT1 gives a signature "according to some
books": "Vasu Ghosha says: do not weep, mother Shachi — for the sake of the living beings your Gaura will become the Giver of
prema". In PK the pada is followed by PK 2232 (signature "wretched Vallabha"): the women of Nadia agree to go to Advaita's
house. Cf. CC Madhya 3; CB Antya 1; Murari, *Kadacha* (book 3).
[^06-65]: In GPT after 20.4: "Seeing Nitai, Shachi fell: 'Where is my Nimai?' — 'Do not weep, mother Shachi, hear Me: Lord
Gaura, the treasure of virtues, has taken sannyasa'"; after 20.5: "Hearing of the sannyasa from Nitai's lips, Shachi fell
senseless to the ground. Nityananda raised her: 'Come to Shantipura — your Nimai is in Advaita's house'".
[^06-66]: The poet's grief, not a vow: thus padas of separation express that life without the Lord is unbearable.

## 21. Madhavi Dasa — "nīlācala haite śacīre dekhite…" (PK 1853)
*Lila: Jagadananda comes from Nilachala to see Shachi; from afar Nadia seems to him like Gokula in separation: leaves fall
out of season, the sun does not shine, birds with closed eyes do not eat and weep, repeating Gorachand's name, cows stand
silent on the road — and the Pandita falls to the ground. Continued in Chandrashekhara's pada PK 1854 (chapter 1, no. 25).
Signature: "Madhavi Dasa". Raga dhanashi (GPT).*[^06-67]

নীলাচল হৈতে শচীরে দেখিতে
আইসে জগদানন্দ ।
রহি কথো দূরে দেখে নদীয়ারে
গোকুলপুরের ছন্দ ॥

*nīlācala haite śacīre dekhite*
*āise jagadānanda |*
*rahi katho dūre dekhe nadīyāre*
*gokulapurera chanda ||*

*Word for word:* nīlācala haite — from Nilachala; śacīre dekhite — to see Shachi; āise jagadānanda — Jagadananda comes; rahi katho dūre — stopping at some distance; dekhe nadīyāre — sees Nadia; gokulapurera chanda — like Gokula

**21.1.** From Nilachala, to see Shachi,
Jagadananda comes;
stopping at a distance, he sees Nadia —
it is like Gokula.[^06-68]

ভাবয়ে পণ্ডিত রায় ।
পাই কি না পাই শচীরে দেখিতে
এই অনুমানে যায় ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*bhābaye paṇḍita rāya |*
*pāi ki nā pāi śacīre dekhite*
*ei anumāne yāya || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* bhābaye paṇḍita rāya — Pandita Raya reflects; pāi ki nā pāi — shall I find or not; śacīre dekhite — to see Shachi; ei anumāne yāya — with this thought he goes

**21.2.** *(Refrain)* Pandita Raya reflects:
"Shall I find Shachi or not?" —
with this thought he walks on.

তরু লতা যত দেখে শত শত
অকালে খসিছে পাতা ।
রবির কিরণ না হয় স্ফুটন
মেঘগণ দেখে রাতা ॥

*taru latā yata dekhe śata śata*
*akāle khasiche pātā |*
*rabira kiraṇa nā haya sphuṭana*
*meghagaṇa dekhe rātā ||*

*Word for word:* taru latā yata — all the trees and creepers; dekhe śata śata — he sees hundreds and hundreds; akāle khasiche pātā — leaves fall out of season; rabira kiraṇa nā haya sphuṭana — the sun's rays do not break through; megha-gaṇa dekhe rātā — he sees the clouds crimson

**21.3.** Trees and creepers — hundreds and hundreds — he sees:
out of season their leaves are falling;
the sun's rays do not break through,
the clouds seem crimson.

ডালে বসি পাখী মুদি দুটি আঁখি
ফল জল তেয়াগিয়া ।
কান্দয়ে ফুকরি ডুকরি ডুকরি
গোরাচাঁদ নাম লৈয়া ॥

*ḍāle basi pākhī mudi duṭi ām̐khi*
*phala jala teyāgiyā |*
*kāndaye phukari ḍukari ḍukari*
*gorācām̐da nāma laiyā ||*

*Word for word:* ḍāle basi pākhī — birds sitting on the branches; mudi duṭi ām̐khi — closing both eyes; phala jala teyāgiyā — giving up fruit and water; kāndaye phukari ḍukari ḍukari — weep, crying and sobbing; gorācām̐da nāma laiyā — repeating Gorachand's name

**21.4.** Birds sitting on the branches, both eyes closed,
having given up fruit and water,
weep, crying aloud,
repeating the name of Gorachand.

ধেনু যূথে যূথে দাঁড়াইয়া পথে
কারো মুখে নাহি রা ।
মাধবী দাসের ঠাকুর পণ্ডিত
পড়িল আছাড়ে গা ॥২॥১৮৫৩॥

*dhenu yūthe yūthe dām̐ṛāiyā pathe*
*kāro mukhe nāhi rā |*
*mādhabī dāsera ṭhākura paṇḍita*
*paṛila āchāṛe gā ||2||1853||*

*Word for word:* dhenu yūthe yūthe — cows in herds; dām̐ṛāiyā pathe — standing on the road; kāro mukhe nāhi rā — not a sound from any; mādhabī dāsera ṭhākura paṇḍita — Thakura Pandita, [master] of Madhavi Dasa; paṛila āchāṛe gā — crashed to the ground

**21.5.** Cows stand in herds on the road —
not a sound from any of them;
Thakura Pandita, [the master] of Madhavi Dasa,
crashed to the ground.[^06-69]

[^06-67]: Signature: "Madhavi Dasa". PK: vol. 3, PDF pp. 129–130 (printed pp. 118–119), 10th pallava ("Separation of various
kinds"), no. 2 (mark "॥২॥১৮৫৩॥"), headed "the same raga"; MSS according to the apparatus: "ka", "gha", "ca". GPT1 — p. 407,
no. 17 (raga dhanashi); GPT2 — sect. 5.5, no. 17. It is followed in PK and GPT1 (no. 18, pp. 407–408) by Chandrashekhara's
pada PK 1854 on Jagadananda entering Shachi's house (in GPT1 with an extra couplet about the faithful servant Ishana; the
stage-1 catalogue entry ChSh-001 lacked the GPT1 reference). In the stage-1 catalogue the first line of PK 1853 was given
from its third line ("rahi katho dūre…"). Cf. CC Antya 12 (Jagadananda's journeys to Navadvipa on the Lord's commission). The
attribution to Madhavi (Madhavi Devi of Puri or another poet) is not established.
[^06-68]: "Like Gokula" (gokulapurera chanda) — Nadia after Gaura's departure resembles Gokula after Krishna's departure for
Mathura. MS "ka": "how many" (kata for katho, so too GPT).
[^06-69]: "[The master] of Madhavi Dasa" (mādhabī dāsera ṭhākura paṇḍita) — the poet calls Jagadananda his master (thakura),
i.e. he was evidently his follower. MS "gha": "sees" (dekhi), "sobbing" (ḍukuri); "ka", "ca": "of anyone" (kāra); GPT1: "fell,
crashing down" (āchāṛi).

## 22. Ramananda — "bhāla bhāli nāce gaurāṅga raṅgiyā…" (PK 2257)
*Lila: the Lord's kirtana — evidently in Nilachala: Gauranga dances, Nitai supports Him from behind; Murari, Mukunda and Vasu
sing to the kartals and mridangas; the Lord asks: "Speak, speak, Narahari!" and looks at Gadadhara; coming up to Svarupa and
Rupa, He asks for the flute and stands in the tribhanga pose; Advaita rejoices, mighty Kashishvara supports Him. The
presence of Svarupa, Rupa and Kashishvara points to Nilachala, where the Gaudiyas came for the Ratha-yatra. Signature:
"Ramananda". Raga dhanashi.*[^06-70]

ভাল ভালি নাচে গৌরাঙ্গ রঙ্গিয়া ।
প্রেমে মত্ত হুহুঙ্কারে কলি-কলমষ হরে
পিছে বুলে নিতাই ধরিয়া ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*bhāla bhāli nāce gaurāṅga raṅgiyā |*
*preme matta huhuṅkāre kali-kalamaṣa hare*
*piche bule nitāi dhariyā || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* bhāla bhāli — splendidly, splendidly; nāce gaurāṅga raṅgiyā — joyful Gauranga dances; preme matta — intoxicated with prema; huhuṅkāre — with a roar; kali-kalamaṣa hare — destroys the filth of Kali; piche bule nitāi dhariyā — behind walks Nitai, supporting [Him]

**22.1.** *(Refrain)* Splendidly, splendidly joyful Gauranga dances!
Intoxicated with prema, with His roar He destroys the filth of Kali;
behind Him Nitai walks, supporting [Him].

করতাল মৃদঙ্গ বায় সভে উচ্চস্বরে গায়
মুরারি মুকুন্দ বাসু সঙ্গে ।
পদ শুনি গোরা রায় ধরণী না পড়ে পায়
প্রেম-সিন্ধু উছলে তরঙ্গে ॥

*karatāla mṛdaṅga bāya sabhe uccasvare gāya*
*murāri mukunda bāsu saṅge |*
*pada śuni gorā rāya dharaṇī nā paṛe pāya*
*prema-sindhu uchale taraṅge ||*

*Word for word:* karatāla mṛdaṅga bāya — kartals and mridangas sound; sabhe uccasvare gāya — all sing aloud; murāri mukunda bāsu saṅge — with Him Murari, Mukunda, Vasu; pada śuni gorā rāya — hearing the pada, Gora Raya; dharaṇī nā paṛe pāya — His feet do not touch the ground; prema-sindhu uchale taraṅge — the ocean of prema surges in waves

**22.2.** Kartals and mridangas sound, all sing aloud —
with Him Murari, Mukunda, Vasu;
hearing the pada, Gora Raya [dances] —
His feet do not touch the ground —
the ocean of prema surges in waves.[^06-71]

পুছে পহু গৌরহরি কহ কহ নরহরি
বামে গদাধর পানে চায় ।
প্রিয় গদাধর ধন্য প্রাণ যার চৈতন্য
গদাইর গৌরাঙ্গ লোকে গায় ॥

*puche pahu gaurahari kaha kaha narahari*
*bāme gadādhara pāne cāya |*
*priya gadādhara dhanya prāṇa yāra caitanya*
*gadāira gaurāṅga loke gāya ||*

*Word for word:* puche pahu gaurahari — Lord Gaurahari asks; kaha kaha narahari — "speak, speak, Narahari"; bāme gadādhara pāne cāya — looks at Gadadhara on the left; priya gadādhara dhanya — blessed is dear Gadadhara; prāṇa yāra caitanya — whose life is Chaitanya; gadāira gaurāṅga loke gāya — "Gadai's Gauranga", people sing

**22.3.** Lord Gaurahari asks: "Speak, speak, Narahari!" —
and looks at Gadadhara on His left;
blessed is dear Gadadhara, whose life is Chaitanya:
"Gadai's Gauranga," people sing.[^06-72]

স্বরূপ রূপ কাছে আসি কহে দেহ মোহন বাঁশী
ক্ষেণে রহে ত্রিভঙ্গ হইয়া ।
বচন-অমিয়া রাশি ক্ষেণে লহু লহু হাসি
হরি বোলে দুবাহু তুলিয়া ॥

*svarūpa rūpa kāche āsi kahe deha mohana bām̐śī*
*kṣeṇe rahe tribhaṅga haiyā |*
*bacana-amiyā rāśi kṣeṇe lahu lahu hāsi*
*hari bole dubāhu tuliyā ||*

*Word for word:* svarūpa rūpa kāche āsi — coming up to Svarupa and Rupa; kahe deha mohana bām̐śī — says "Give the enchanting flute"; kṣeṇe rahe tribhaṅga haiyā — now stands bent in three places; bacana-amiyā rāśi — speech a heap of nectar; kṣeṇe lahu lahu hāsi — now softly, softly laughing; hari bole dubāhu tuliyā — cries "Hari", raising both arms

**22.4.** Coming up to Svarupa and Rupa, He says: "Give Me the enchanting flute!" —
now He stands bent in three places;
His speech a heap of nectar; now, softly, softly laughing,
He raises both arms and cries "Hari".[^06-73]

জয় জয় দ্বিজমণি উঠিল মঙ্গল-ধ্বনি
অদ্বৈতের বাড়ল আনন্দ ।
কাশীশ্বর মহাবলী অদ্বৈত রাখয়ে ধরি
হেরি হরষিত রামানন্দ ॥৪০॥২২৫৭॥

*jaya jaya dvijamaṇi uṭhila maṅgala-dhvani*
*advaitera bāṛala ānanda |*
*kāśīśvara mahābalī advaita rākhaye dhari*
*heri haraṣita rāmānanda ||40||2257||*

*Word for word:* jaya jaya dvijamaṇi — "glory, glory to the Jewel of the twice-born"; uṭhila maṅgala-dhvani — an auspicious cry rose up; advaitera bāṛala ānanda — Advaita's bliss increased; kāśīśvara mahābalī — mighty Kashishvara; advaita rākhaye dhari — supports Advaita; heri haraṣita rāmānanda — seeing it, Ramananda rejoices

**22.5.** "Glory, glory to the Jewel of the twice-born!" — an auspicious cry rose up,
Advaita's bliss increased;
mighty Kashishvara supports Advaita,
and Ramananda, seeing it, rejoices.[^06-74]

[^06-70]: Signature: "Ramananda". PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 289 (printed p. 278), 21st pallava, after the heading "Then a description of
Sri Gauranga's form in sankirtana", no. 40 (mark "॥৪০॥২২৫৭॥"); raga dhanashi; MS P-R-Sa no. 2362. GPT1 — p. 261, no. 42 (raga
dhanashi); GPT2 — sect. 4.2, no. 42. The next PK pada, 2258, "nāce śacīnandana bhakata-jībana-dhana", which GPT gives with the
signature of Narahari (catalogue NS-007), is signed by Lochana Dasa in PK. On the attribution to Ramananda see note 24.
[^06-71]: "The pada" — the song the kirtaniyas sing. This tripadi line has three members.
[^06-72]: "Gadai's Gauranga" (gadāira gaurāṅga) — "Gadadhara's Gauranga", a set expression for the inseparability of the Lord and
Gadadhara Pandita.
[^06-73]: Svarupa Damodara lived with the Lord in Puri; Rupa Gosvami came to Puri in 1516–1517 (CC Antya 1). MS P-R-Sa: "Coming up
to Svarupa, He says: 'Do give Me the enchanting flute!'" (svarūpera… deha nā) — without Rupa. The request for the flute and
the tribhanga pose are the mood of Krishna (cf. note 43).
[^06-74]: "The Jewel of the twice-born" (dvijamaṇi) is Gaura. Kashishvara was the Lord's mighty servant in Puri, who cleared a
path for Him through the crowd (CC Adi 10).

## 23. Madhavi Dasa — "ānande nācata saṅge bhakata…" (PK 2290)
*Lila: the festival of colours (phagu) in Nilachala: young Gaura dances with the devotees, they shower one another with
coloured powder; the women of Puri run to see, the people of Nilachala watch the play with delight; kartals and khol sound.
Signature: "Madhavi Dasa". Raga vasanta.*[^06-75]

আনন্দে নাচত সঙ্গে ভকত
গৌরকিশোর-রাজ ।
ফাগু উঝালি করে ফেলাফেলি
নীলাচল-পুরী মাঝ ॥

*ānande nācata saṅge bhakata*
*gaurakiśora-rāja |*
*phāgu ujhāli kare phelāpheli*
*nīlācala-purī mājha ||*

*Word for word:* ānande nācata — dances in bliss; saṅge bhakata — with the devotees; gaura-kiśora-rāja — the young king Gaura; phāgu ujhāli — scattering phagu powder; kare phelāpheli — they shower one another; nīlācala-purī mājha — in the midst of the city of Nilachala

**23.1.** In bliss, with the devotees, dances
the young king Gaura:
scattering phagu powder, they shower one another
in the midst of the city of Nilachala.[^06-76]

শুনিয়া নাগরী প্রেমেত আগরি
ধাইয়া চলিল বাটে ।
হেরিয়া গৌরে পড়িয়া ফাঁফরে
বদন চাহিয়া থাকে ॥

*śuniyā nāgarī premeta āgari*
*dhāiyā calila bāṭe |*
*heriyā gaure paṛiyā phām̐phare*
*badana cāhiyā thāke ||*

*Word for word:* śuniyā nāgarī — hearing, the townswomen; premeta āgari — full of love; dhāiyā calila bāṭe — ran out to the road; heriyā gaure — seeing Gaura; paṛiyā phām̐phare — bewildered; badana cāhiyā thāke — keep gazing at [His] face

**23.2.** Hearing of it, the women, full of love,
ran out to the road;
seeing Gaura, they were bewildered
and could not take their eyes off [His] face.[^06-77]

দু বাহু তুলিয়া বেড়ায় নাচিয়া
ভকত-গণের সঙ্গ ।
নীলাচল-বাসী মনে অভিলাষী
কৌতুকে দেখয়ে রঙ্গ ॥

*du bāhu tuliyā beṛāya nāciyā*
*bhakata-gaṇera saṅga |*
*nīlācala-bāsī mane abhilāṣī*
*kautuke dekhaye raṅga ||*

*Word for word:* du bāhu tuliyā — raising both arms; beṛāya nāciyā — goes about dancing; bhakata-gaṇera saṅga — with the devotees; nīlācala-bāsī — the people of Nilachala; mane abhilāṣī — full of longing; kautuke dekhaye raṅga — watch the play with delight

**23.3.** Raising both arms, He goes about dancing
together with the devotees;
the people of Nilachala, full of longing [to see],
watch the play with delight.

বাজে করতাল বোলে ভালি ভাল
আর বাজে তাহে খোল ।
মাধবি দাস মনেতে উল্লাস
সদা বলে হরি বোল ॥৭৩॥২২৯০॥

*bāje karatāla bole bhāli bhāla*
*āra bāje tāhe khola |*
*mādhabi dāsa manete ullāsa*
*sadā bale hari bola ||73||2290||*

*Word for word:* bāje karatāla — the kartals sound; bole bhāli bhāla — they cry "splendid, splendid"; āra bāje tāhe khola — and the khol sounds as well; mādhabi dāsa — Madhavi Dasa; manete ullāsa — rejoices in his heart; sadā bale hari bola — ceaselessly cries "Haribol"

**23.4.** The kartals sound, [people] cry "Splendid, splendid!",
and the khol sounds as well;
Madhavi Dasa rejoices in his heart
and ceaselessly cries "Haribol".

[^06-75]: Signature: "Madhavi Dasa". PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 300 (printed p. 289), 21st pallava, no. 73 (mark "॥৭৩॥২২৯০॥"); raga
vasanta; MS P-R-Sa no. 2394. GPT1 — p. 260, no. 39 (raga vasanta); GPT2 — sect. 4.2, no. 39. On the attribution see note 67.
[^06-76]: Phagu is the red powder (abir) with which people shower one another at the spring festival of Holi (Dola-yatra; the
Phalguna full moon is the day of the Lord's appearance). MS P-R-Sa: "city" (pura for purī).
[^06-77]: MS P-R-Sa: "having come, all look" (āsiyā sakali dekhe). On such images see note 21.

## 24. Ramananda — "hari hari aiche ki hoyaba hāmāra…" (PK 3057)
*The poet's prayer: "Hari, Hari! Will I have such fortune — to see Gaura's pastimes with His companions in Nadia: dance and
kirtana on the bank of the Ganga, the Lord in His place in Srivasa's house — Nityananda on the right holding the parasol,
Gadadhara on the left; someone will take me there, and I shall see His moonlike face; and when, calling His mother, He comes
home to dine…" In PK it stands among the prayer-padas (prarthana). Signature: "Ramananda". The raga is the same as that of
the preceding pada.*[^06-78]

হরি হরি ঐছে কি হোয়ব হামার ।
সহচর-সঙ্গে রঙ্গে পহুঁ গৌরক
হেরব নদিয়া-বিহার ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*hari hari aiche ki hoyaba hāmāra |*
*sahacara-saṅge raṅge pahum̐ gauraka*
*heraba nadiyā-bihāra || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* hari hari — Hari, Hari; aiche ki hoyaba hāmāra — will I have such; sahacara-saṅge — with the companions; raṅge — joyfully; pahum̐ gauraka — of Lord Gaura; heraba nadiyā-bihāra — shall I see the pastimes in Nadia

**24.1.** *(Refrain)* Hari, Hari! Will I have such [fortune] —
joyfully, together with the companions, Lord Gaura's
pastimes in Nadia to behold?

সুরধুনি-তীরে নটন-রসে পহুঁ মোর
কীর্তন করব বিলাস ।
সো কিয়ে হাম নয়ন ভরি হেরব
পূরব চির-অভিলাষ ॥

*suradhuni-tīre naṭana-rase pahum̐ mora*
*kīrtana karaba bilāsa |*
*so kiye hāma nayana bhari heraba*
*pūraba cira-abhilāṣa ||*

*Word for word:* suradhuni-tīre — on the bank of the Suradhuni (the Ganga); naṭana-rase — in the taste of dancing; pahum̐ mora — my Lord; kīrtana karaba bilāsa — will sport in kirtana; so kiye hāma nayana bhari heraba — shall I see it, filling my eyes; pūraba cira-abhilāṣa — the long-held desire will be fulfilled

**24.2.** On the bank of the Suradhuni, in the taste of dancing, my Lord
will sport in kirtana —
shall I see it, filling my eyes?
My long-held desire will be fulfilled.

শ্রীবাস-ভবনে যব নিজ-গণ সঙ্গহি
বৈঠব আপন ঠামে ।
ডাহিনে নিত্যানন্দ ছত্র ধরি
পণ্ডিত গদাধর বামে ॥

*śrībāsa-bhabane yaba nija-gaṇa saṅgahi*
*baiṭhaba āpana ṭhāme |*
*ḍāhine nityānanda chatra dhari*
*paṇḍita gadādhara bāme ||*

*Word for word:* śrībāsa-bhabane — in Srivasa's house; yaba nija-gaṇa saṅgahi — when with His own; baiṭhaba āpana ṭhāme — He sits in His place; ḍāhine nityānanda — on the right Nityananda; chatra dhari — holding the parasol; paṇḍita gadādhara bāme — Pandita Gadadhara on the left

**24.3.** When in Srivasa's house, with His own,
He sits in His place,
Nityananda on the right holding the parasol,
Pandita Gadadhara on the left —

তব কোই মোহে লেই তাঁহা যায়ব
হেরব সো মুখ-চন্দ ।
পুলকহি সকল অঙ্গ পরিপূরব
পাওব প্রেম-আনন্দ ॥

*taba koi mohe lei tām̐hā yāyaba*
*heraba so mukha-canda |*
*pulakahi sakala aṅga paripūraba*
*pāoba prema-ānanda ||*

*Word for word:* taba koi mohe lei tām̐hā yāyaba — then someone will lead me there; heraba so mukha-canda — I shall see that moonlike face; pulakahi sakala aṅga paripūraba — my whole body will be covered with thrills; pāoba prema-ānanda — I shall attain the bliss of prema

**24.4.** then someone will take me and lead me there,
and I shall see that moonlike face;
my whole body will be covered with thrills,
and I shall attain the bliss of prema.

জননি সম্বোধনে যব ঘরে আওব
করবহুঁ ভোজন পান ।
রামানন্দ আনন্দে কি হেরব
সফল করব দু নয়ান ॥৭৩॥৩০৫৭॥

*janani sambodhane yaba ghare āoba*
*karabahum̐ bhojana pāna |*
*rāmānanda ānande ki heraba*
*saphala karaba du nayāna ||73||3057||*

*Word for word:* janani sambodhane — calling His mother; yaba ghare āoba — when He comes home; karabahum̐ bhojana pāna — and eats and drinks; rāmānanda ānande ki heraba — what Ramananda will behold in bliss; saphala karaba du nayāna — will make both eyes fruitful

**24.5.** When, calling His mother, He comes home
and sits to eat and drink —
what Ramananda will behold in bliss!
Then my two eyes will not have been in vain.[^06-79]

[^06-78]: Signature: "Ramananda". PK: vol. 4, PDF p. 253 (printed p. 244), among the prayer-padas, no. 73 (mark
"॥৭৩॥৩০৫৭॥"); "the same raga"; MS P-R-Sa no. 2554. GPT1 — pp. 491–492 (sect. 7, "Prarthana"; first line "hari hari aiche
bhāgya hoyaba hāmāra" — "will I have such good fortune"). On the attribution see note 24. A prayer in the form of a longing
to see the pastimes of Navadvipa is common among later poets (cf. the prarthanas of Narottama Dasa); but it may also be the
word of a contemporary yearning after the sannyasa for the days of Navadvipa. MSS "ka", "kha", "ca", P-R-Sa in 24.1: "to me"
(āmāra for hāmāra).
[^06-79]: "Calling His mother" (janani sambodhane) — MS "ka": "with address to the mother" (sambodhana). GPT1: "…then I shall see
[it] and make both eyes fruitful".

# Chapter 7. Praise of Nitai and Chaitanya, the Appearance of Nityananda and Gaura, Nimai's Childhood, the Abhisheka, Kirtanas, the Sannyasa, Nilachala, the Deities at Ambika, Prayers

*Padas of contemporaries known from the *Padakalpataru* (PK), in the order of the lilas: praise of Nitai and Chaitanya
and of the sankirtana (Krishnadasa); Nityananda's appearance at Ekachakra (Krishnadasa); Gaura's appearance and His
childhood play in Shachi's house (Vasu Ghosha); the Govardhana of bhakti in Navadvipa (Chaitanyadasa); the abhisheka in
Srivasa's house (Krishnadasa); the dance of the Lord hearing of Vrindavana (Ramachandra); Nityananda's dance (Vasu
Ramananda); separation in autumn (Krishnadasa); the sannyasi Lord on the seashore (Ramananda); Nilachala (Paramananda);
the Deities of Gaura and Nitai in Gauridasa's house at Ambika (Krishnadasa); and Krishnadasa's prayers. The text follows
PK, checked against the scans, with the variants of the *Bhakti-ratnakara* (BR) and the *Gaura-pada-tarangini* (GPT1 —
1st ed., 1903; GPT2 — 2nd ed., 1934); the Bengali original, variants and word-for-word translation are in the full version of the book.*

## 1. Krishnadasa — "prema-sindhu gorā rāy…" (PK 2343)
*Praise of Nitai and Chaitanya: Gaura is an ocean of prema, Nitai the wave upon it; Rupa and Sanatana, diving into this
ocean, bring up jewels and string them on the thread of bhakti; the kirtana of the lilas is a blossoming lotus forest.
In PK it stands in the 23rd pallava (the form and qualities of Chaitanya and Nityananda). Raga dhanashi.*[^07-1]

প্রেম-সিন্ধু গোরা রায় নিতাই-তরঙ্গ তায়
করুণা-বাতাস চারি পাশে ।
প্রেম উথলিয়া পড়ে জগত হাফান ছাড়ে
তাপ তৃষ্ণা সভাকার নাশে ॥

*prema-sindhu gorā rāya nitāi-taraṅga tāya*
*karuṇā-bātāsa cāri pāśe |*
*prema uthaliyā paṛe jagata hāphāna chāṛe*
*tāpa tṛṣṇā sabhākāra nāśe ||*

*Word for word:* prema-sindhu — the ocean of prema; gorā rāy — Gora Raya; nitāi-taraṅga tāy — Nitai the wave upon it; karuṇā-bātāsa — the wind of compassion; cāri pāśe — on all four sides; prema uthaliyā paṛe — prema surges and spills over; jagata hāphān chāṛe — the world draws breath (sighs with relief); tāpa tṛṣṇā — heat and thirst; sabhākāra nāśe — are destroyed for all

**1.1.** An ocean of prema is Gora Raya, Nitai the wave upon it,
on all four sides — the wind of compassion.
Prema surges and spills over — the world draws breath again:
everyone's heat and thirst are gone.[^07-2]

দেখ দেখ নিতাই চৈতন্য দয়াময় ।
ভক্ত-হংস-চক্রবাকে পিব পিব বলি ডাকে
পাইয়া বঞ্চিত কেন হয় ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*dekha dekha nitāi caitanya dayāmaya |*
*bhakta-haṃsa-cakrabāke piba piba bali ḍāke*
*pāiyā bañcita kena haya || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* dekha dekha — behold, behold; nitāi caitanya dayāmaya — the merciful Nitai and Chaitanya; bhakta-haṃsa-cakrabāke — the swans and chakravakas, the devotees; piba piba bali ḍāke — call, saying "Drink, drink!"; pāiyā — having found; bañcita kena haya — why does one stay deprived

**1.2.** *(Refrain)* Behold, behold the merciful Nitai and Chaitanya!
To the swans and chakravakas — the devotees — They call: "Drink, drink!"
Having found such a thing, why stay deprived?[^07-3]

ডুবি রূপ সনাতন তোলে নানা রত্ন ধন
যতনে গাঁথিয়া তার মালা ।
ভক্তি-লতা-সূত্র করি লেহ জীব কণ্ঠ ভরি
দূরে যাবে তপনের জ্বালা ॥

*ḍubi rūpa sanātana tole nānā ratna dhana*
*yatane gām̐thiyā tāra mālā |*
*bhakti-latā-sūtra kari leha jība kaṇṭha bhari*
*dūre yābe tapanera jvālā ||*

*Word for word:* ḍubi — diving; rūpa sanātana — Rupa and Sanatana; tole nānā ratna dhana — bring up many jewel-treasures; yatane gāṃthiyā tāra mālā — carefully stringing a garland of them; bhakti-latā-sūtra kari — making the creeper of bhakti the thread; leha jība — take it, souls; kaṇṭha bhari — filling (adorning) the neck; dūre yābe tapanera jvālā — the burning of the sun will go away

**1.3.** Diving, Rupa and Sanatana bring up many treasures, jewels,
and carefully string a garland of them.
Making the creeper of bhakti the thread — take it, souls, adorn your necks:
the scorching heat of the sun will go.[^07-4]

লীলা-রস সংকীর্ত্তন বিকসিত পদ্ম-বন
জগত ভরিল যার বাসে ।
ফুটিল কুসুম বন মাতিল ভ্রমরগণ
পাইয়া বঞ্চিত কৃষ্ণদাসে ॥

*līlā-rasa saṃkīrttana bikasita padma-bana*
*jagata bharila yāra bāse |*
*phuṭila kusuma bana mātila bhramaragaṇa*
*pāiyā bañcita kṛṣṇadāse ||*

*Word for word:* līlā-rasa saṅkīrtana — the sankirtana of the taste of the lilas; bikasita padma-bana — a blossoming lotus forest; jagata bharila — the world was filled; yāra bāse — with whose fragrance; phuṭila kusuma bana — the flower forest bloomed; mātila bhramara-gaṇa — the bees became intoxicated; pāiyā — having found; bañcita kṛṣṇadāse — Krishnadasa is deprived

**1.4.** The sankirtana of the taste of the lilas is a blossoming lotus forest,
whose fragrance has filled the world.
The forest of flowers has bloomed, the bees are intoxicated —
yet Krishnadasa, having found it, has stayed deprived.[^07-5]

[^07-1]: Signature: "Krishnadasa". PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 319 (printed p. 308), 23rd pallava, no. 12 (mark "॥১২॥২৩৪৩॥"); raga
dhanashi; ms. P-R-Sa no. 2447. GPT1 — pp. 32–33, no. 19 (raga dhanashi); GPT2 — sect. 1.3, no. 19. Which Krishnadasa wrote
the pada is not established: PK gathers under this signature padas of different poets (including Krishnadasa Kaviraja);
the mention of Rupa and Sanatana dates it not earlier than 1514–1516. Majumdar does not discuss it.
[^07-2]: "The world draws breath again" (jagata hāphān chāṛe) — like one exhausted by the heat breathing with relief; ms.
"ka" and GPT1 — hākāla ("the world cries out"). Ms. "kha": "sin" (pāpa) instead of "heat".
[^07-3]: Hamsa-swans and chakravakas are water birds living on the ocean of prema; the image continues the ocean metaphor.
[^07-4]: Rupa and Sanatana Gosvami are disciples of the Lord whose books opened the treasures of bhakti. Ms. "gha": "the
thread of a book" (grantha) instead of "creeper". "The heat of the sun" is worldly suffering; GPT1: "your burning will go".
[^07-5]: The humility usual with Vaishnava poets: the poet considers himself deprived of what is being given to all.

## 2. Krishnadasa — "nabadvīpe śuni siṃhanāda…" (PK 2089)
*The sankirtana in Navadvipa as a battle: Gaurachandra is the great chariot-warrior, Nityananda the general, Advaita the
vanguard; the enemies are bound with a noose of the rope of prema; the Lord, mounted on the elephant of Kali, sets up
outposts on every side. In PK it stands in the 17th pallava (the dance and pastimes of Gauranga). Raga ramakeli.*[^07-6]

নবদ্বীপে শুনি সিংহনাদ ।
সাজল বৈষ্ণবগণ করি হরি সংকীর্ত্তন
মূঢ়মতি গণিল প্রমাদ ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*nabadvīpe śuni siṃhanāda |*
*sājala baiṣṇabagaṇa kari hari saṃkīrttana*
*mūṛhamati gaṇila pramāda || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* nabadvīpe — in Navadvipa; śuni — is heard; siṃhanāda — a lion's roar; sājala baiṣṇaba-gaṇa — the Vaishnavas arrayed themselves; kari hari saṅkīrtana — performing the sankirtana of Hari; mūṛhamati — the fools; gaṇila pramāda — reckoned it a calamity

**2.1.** *(Refrain)* In Navadvipa a lion's roar was heard!
The Vaishnavas arrayed themselves, starting the sankirtana of Hari —
the fools took it for a calamity.[^07-7]

গৌরচন্দ্র মহারথী নিত্যানন্দ সেনাপতি
অদ্বৈত যুদ্ধের আগুয়ান ।
প্রেম-ডোর ফাঁস করি বান্ধিল অনেক ঐরি
নিরন্তর গর্জ্জে হরিনাম ॥

*gauracandra mahārathī nityānanda senāpati*
*advaita yuddhera āguyāna |*
*prema-ḍora phām̐sa kari bāndhila aneka airi*
*nirantara garjje harināma ||*

*Word for word:* gauracandra mahārathī — Gaurachandra the great chariot-warrior; nityānanda senāpati — Nityananda the general; advaita yuddhera āguyāna — Advaita the vanguard of the battle; prema-ḍora phāṃsa kari — making a noose of the rope of prema; bāndhila aneka airi — they bound many foes; nirantara garjje hari-nāma — unceasingly thunders the name of Hari

**2.2.** Gaurachandra is the great chariot-warrior, Nityananda the general,
Advaita at the head of the army.
With a noose of the rope of prema they bound many foes;
unceasingly thunders the name of Hari.

শ্রীচৈতন্য করে রণ কলি-গজে আরোহণ
পাষণ্ড-দলন বীর-বানা ।
কলি-জীব তরাইতে আইল প্রভু অবনীতে
চৌদিকে চাপিয়া দিল থানা ॥

*śrīcaitanya kare raṇa kali-gaje ārohaṇa*
*pāṣaṇḍa-dalana bīra-bānā |*
*kali-jība tarāite āila prabhu abanīte*
*caudike cāpiyā dila thānā ||*

*Word for word:* śrīcaitanya kare raṇa — Sri Chaitanya wages battle; kali-gaje ārohaṇa — mounted on the elephant of Kali; pāṣaṇḍa-dalana — the crusher of godlessness; bīra-bānā — [in] the array of a hero; kali-jība tarāite — to deliver the souls of the Kali age; āila prabhu abanīte — the Lord came to the earth; caudike cāpiyā dila thānā — set up outposts all around

**2.3.** Sri Chaitanya wages the battle, mounted on the elephant of Kali,
in the array of a hero, the crusher of godlessness.
To deliver the souls of the Kali age the Lord came to the earth
and set up outposts on all four sides.[^07-8]

উত্তম অধম জন সভে পাইল প্রেম-ধন
নিতাই-চৈতন্য-কৃপা-লেশে ।
সমুখে শমন দেখি কৃষ্ণদাস বড় দুখী
না পাইয়া প্রেমের উদ্দেশে ॥

*uttama adhama jana sabhe pāila prema-dhana*
*nitāi-caitanya-kṛpā-leśe |*
*samukhe śamana dekhi kṛṣṇadāsa baṛa dukhī*
*nā pāiyā premera uddeśe ||*

*Word for word:* uttama adhama jana — high and low people; sabhe pāila prema-dhana — all obtained the treasure of prema; nitāi-caitanya-kṛpā-leśe — by a particle of the mercy of Nitai and Chaitanya; samukhe śamana dekhi — seeing Yama before him; kṛṣṇadāsa baṛa dukhī — Krishnadasa is very sorrowful; nā pāiyā premera uddeśe — not having found a trace of prema

**2.4.** High and low — all obtained the treasure of prema
by a particle of the mercy of Nitai and Chaitanya.
But Krishnadasa, seeing Yama before him, grieves deeply:
he has not found even a trace of prema.[^07-9]

[^07-6]: Signature: "Krishnadasa". PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 226 (printed p. 215), 17th pallava, no. 31 (mark "॥৩১॥২০৮৯॥"); raga
ramakeli; ms. P-R-Sa no. 2198; after the pada a PK rubric: here the pada "kali timira ghora…" is also sung. GPT1 — p. 274,
no. 85 (raga ramakeli); GPT2 — sect. 4.2. The catalogue's former first line ("kali-jība tarāite…") is the beginning of
the third stanza. Which Krishnadasa it is has not been established.
[^07-7]: "A lion's roar" is the thundering kirtana; "the fools" (mūṛhamati) are the opponents of the kirtana in Navadvipa
(cf. CB Madhya 23).
[^07-8]: "Mounted on the elephant of Kali" (kali-gaje ārohaṇa): the Kali age, subdued, serves the Lord as His war elephant;
mss. "ka", "kha", "ca": "mounted on an elephant" (kari-gaje). GPT1: "Nityananda is the charioteer" (sārathi) instead of
"the general". The Lord crushes godlessness (pāṣaṇḍa) not with weapons but with the holy name: cf. CC Adi 17 — the
Kazi subdued by the kirtana.
[^07-9]: Yama is the lord of death. The self-abasement usual with Vaishnava poets.

## 3. Krishnadasa — "jaya jaya mahāprabhu jaya gauracandra…" (PK 2847)
*A nama-kirtana: glory to Mahaprabhu, His parents, Navadvipa, the Ganga, the Lord's consorts and His devotees. In PK
it is the gaura-chandrika to the morning lila (32nd pallava, the "eightfold lila"). Raga "kau".*[^07-10]

জয় জয় মহাপ্রভু জয় গৌরচন্দ্র ।
জয় বিশ্বম্ভর জয় করুণার সিন্ধু ॥

*jaya jaya mahāprabhu jaya gauracandra |*
*jaya biśvambhara jaya karuṇāra sindhu ||*

*Word for word:* jaya jaya mahāprabhu — glory, glory to Mahaprabhu; jaya gauracandra — glory to Gaurachandra; jaya biśvambhara — glory to Vishvambhara; jaya karuṇāra sindhu — glory to the ocean of mercy

**3.1.** Glory, glory to Mahaprabhu, glory to Gaurachandra!
Glory to Vishvambhara, glory to the ocean of mercy!

জয় শচীসুত জয় পণ্ডিত নিমাঞি ।
জয় মিশ্র পুরন্দর জয় শচী আই ॥

*jaya śacīsuta jaya paṇḍita nimāñi |*
*jaya miśra purandara jaya śacī āi ||*

*Word for word:* jaya śacīsuta — glory to the Son of Shachi; jaya paṇḍita nimāñi — glory to Pandita Nimai; jaya miśra purandara — glory to Mishra Purandara; jaya śacī āi — glory to Mother Shachi

**3.2.** Glory to the Son of Shachi, glory to Pandita Nimai!
Glory to Mishra Purandara, glory to Mother Shachi!

জয় জয় নবদ্বীপ জয় সুরধুনী ।
জয় লক্ষ্মী বিষ্ণুপ্রিয়া প্রভুর গৃহিণী ॥

*jaya jaya nabadvīpa jaya suradhunī |*
*jaya lakṣmī biṣṇupriyā prabhura gṛhiṇī ||*

*Word for word:* jaya jaya nabadvīpa — glory, glory to Navadvipa; jaya suradhunī — glory to the Suradhuni (the Ganga); jaya lakṣmī biṣṇupriyā — glory to Lakshmi and Vishnupriya; prabhura gṛhiṇī — the Lord's consorts

**3.3.** Glory, glory to Navadvipa, glory to the Suradhuni!
Glory to Lakshmi and Vishnupriya, the Lord's consorts![^07-11]

জয় জয় নবদ্বীপ-বাসী ভক্তগণ ।
জয় জয় নিত্যানন্দ অদ্বৈত-চরণ ॥

*jaya jaya nabadvīpa-bāsī bhaktagaṇa |*
*jaya jaya nityānanda advaita-caraṇa ||*

*Word for word:* jaya jaya nabadvīpa-bāsī bhakta-gaṇa — glory, glory to the devotees dwelling in Navadvipa; jaya jaya nityānanda advaita-caraṇa — glory, glory to the feet of Nityananda and Advaita

**3.4.** Glory, glory to the devotees who dwell in Navadvipa!
Glory, glory to the feet of Nityananda and Advaita!

নিত্যানন্দ-পদ-দ্বন্দ্ব সদা করি আশ ।
নাম-সংকীর্ত্তন গাইল কৃষ্ণদাস ॥

*nityānanda-pada-dvandva sadā kari āśa |*
*nāma-saṃkīrttana gāila kṛṣṇadāsa ||*

*Word for word:* nityānanda-pada-dvandva — the two feet of Nityananda; sadā kari āśa — ever hoping [for]; nāma-saṅkīrtana — the nama-sankirtana; gāila kṛṣṇadāsa — Krishnadasa sang

**3.5.** Ever hoping for the two feet of Nityananda,
Krishnadasa has sung this nama-sankirtana.[^07-12]

[^07-10]: Signature: "Krishnadasa". PK: vol. 4, PDF pp. 179–180 (printed pp. 170–171), 32nd pallava, "Now the morning
lila. Sri Gaurachandra", no. 10 (mark "॥১০॥২৮৪৭॥"); raga "kau" (an abbreviation; so also GPT1). GPT1 — pp. 22–23,
no. 62 (without couplet 3.3); GPT2 — sect. 1.2, no. 62. The attribution is not established; the hope placed in Nityananda's feet
in the signature points rather to a poet of Nityananda's branch than to Krishnadasa Kaviraja.
[^07-11]: Mishra Purandara is Jagannatha Mishra, the Lord's father. Suradhuni is the Ganga. Lakshmi is Lakshmipriya, the
Lord's first consort; Vishnupriya the second.
[^07-12]: Nama-sankirtana — the singing of the Lord's names.

## 4. Krishnadasa — "rāṛhadeśe nāma ekacakrā grāma…" (PK 1116)
*Nityananda's appearance: in Radha-desha, in the village of Ekachakra, in the house of Hadai Pandita, on the bright
thirteenth of Magha, Haladhara was born; Hadai celebrates his son's birth, the earth sways with joy; Advaita in
Shantipura perceives that Rama, Krishna's elder brother, has appeared. In PK: "Then the appearance of Shri
Nityananda-chandra" (3rd shakha, 18th pallava, the "janma-lila"). Raga shri.*[^07-13]

রাঢ়দেশে নাম একচক্রা গ্রাম
হাড়াই পণ্ডিত-ঘর ।
শুভ মাঘ-মাসি শুক্লা ত্রয়োদশী
জনমিলা হলধর ॥

*rāṛhadeśe nāma ekacakrā grāma*
*hāṛāi paṇḍita-ghara |*
*śubha māgha-māsi śuklā trayodaśī*
*janamilā haladhara ||*

*Word for word:* rāṛhadeśe — in Radha-desha; nāma ekacakrā grāma — the village named Ekachakra; hāṛāi paṇḍita-ghara — the house of Hadai Pandita; śubha māgha-māsi — in the auspicious month of Magha; śuklā trayodaśī — on the bright thirteenth; janamilā haladhara — Haladhara (Balarama) was born

**4.1.** In Radha-desha, in the village named Ekachakra,
in the house of Hadai Pandita,
in the auspicious month of Magha, on the bright thirteenth,
Haladhara was born.[^07-14]

হাড়াই পণ্ডিত অতি হরষিত
পুত্র-মহোৎসব করে ।
ধরণী-মণ্ডল করে টলমল
আনন্দ নাহিক ধরে ॥

*hāṛāi paṇḍita ati haraṣita*
*putra-mahotsaba kare |*
*dharaṇī-maṇḍala kare ṭalamala*
*ānanda nāhika dhare ||*

*Word for word:* hāṛāi paṇḍita — Hadai Pandita; ati haraṣita — overjoyed; putra-mahotsaba kare — holds a festival for his son; dharaṇī-maṇḍala — the circle of the earth; kare ṭalamala — sways; ānanda nāhika dhare — cannot contain the bliss

**4.2.** Hadai Pandita, filled with joy,
holds a festival for his son.
The circle of the earth sways,
unable to contain the bliss.

শান্তিপুর-নাথ মনে হরষিত
করি কিছু অনুমান ।
অন্তরে জানিলা বুঝি জনমিলা
কৃষ্ণের অগ্রজ রাম ॥

*śāntipura-nātha mane haraṣita*
*kari kichu anumāna |*
*antare jānilā bujhi janamilā*
*kṛṣṇera agraja rāma ||*

*Word for word:* śāntipura-nātha — the Lord of Shantipura (Advaita); mane haraṣita — rejoicing at heart; kari kichu anumāna — divining something; antare jānilā — He knew within; bujhi janamilā — surely there is born; kṛṣṇera agraja rāma — Rama, Krishna's elder brother

**4.3.** The Lord of Shantipura, rejoicing,
divined something:
in His heart He knew: surely there is born
Rama, the elder brother of Krishna.[^07-15]

বৈষ্ণবের মন হৈল পরসন্ন
আনন্দ-সাগরে ভাসে ।
এ দীন পামর হইবে উদ্ধার
কহে দুখী কৃষ্ণদাসে ॥

*baiṣṇabera mana haila parasanna*
*ānanda-sāgare bhāse |*
*e dīna pāmara haibe uddhāra*
*kahe dukhī kṛṣṇadāse ||*

*Word for word:* baiṣṇabera mana — the hearts of the Vaishnavas; haila parasanna — became serene; ānanda-sāgare bhāse — float in an ocean of bliss; e dīna pāmara — this wretched sinner; haibe uddhāra — will be delivered; kahe dukhī kṛṣṇadāse — says the unhappy Krishnadasa

**4.4.** The hearts of the Vaishnavas grew serene,
they float in an ocean of bliss.
"Even this wretched sinner will be delivered,"
says the unhappy Krishnadasa.[^07-16]

[^07-13]: Signature: "Krishnadasa". PK: vol. 2, PDF p. 265 (printed p. 252), 3rd shakha, 18th pallava (the "janma-lila"),
section "tataḥ śrīnityānandacandrābirbhābaḥ", no. 5 (mark "॥৫॥১১১৬॥"); raga shri; ms. P-R-Sa no. 1614. GPT1 — p. 416, no. 7
(raga shri); GPT2 — sect. 6.1, no. 7. In the catalogue the pada was listed as PK 1117 (PK 1117 is the next pada, below,
no. 5). Which Krishnadasa it is has not been established.
[^07-14]: Radha-desha (Rarh) is the region west of the Ganga. Hadai Pandita (Hadai Ojha) is Nityananda's father. Haladhara
("bearer of the plough") is Balarama: Nityananda is Balarama Himself. Magha is January–February; the same date is in the
*Advaita-prakasha*. Ms. "ka" and P-R-Sa: "Radha-desh" (without the locative ending).
[^07-15]: The Lord of Shantipura is Advaita Acharya. Rama is Balarama, Krishna's elder brother.
[^07-16]: "Unhappy" (dukhī) is the poet's humble name for himself.

## 5. Krishnadasa — "bhubana-ānanda-kanda balarāma nityānanda…" (PK 1117)
*Praise of Nityananda, descended in the Kali age: He is golden like the champaka, the nails of His fingers are a row of
moons, His face eclipses the full moon, His arms reach His knees; bee-devotees hover at His lotus feet. In PK it is the
next pada of the same section. Raga suhai.*[^07-17]

ভুবন-আনন্দ-কন্দ বলরাম নিত্যানন্দ
অবতীর্ণ হৈলা কলি-কালে ।
ঘুচিল সকল দুখ দেখিয়া ও চান্দমুখ
ভাসে লোক আনন্দ-হিলোলে ॥

*bhubana-ānanda-kanda balarāma nityānanda*
*abatīrṇa hailā kali-kāle |*
*ghucila sakala dukha dekhiyā o cāndamukha*
*bhāse loka ānanda-hilole ||*

*Word for word:* bhubana-ānanda-kanda — the root of the world's bliss; balarāma nityānanda — Balarama Nityananda; abatīrṇa hailā kali-kāle — descended in the Kali age; ghucila sakala dukha — all sorrows vanished; dekhiyā o cāndamukha — seeing that moon-face; bhāse loka — people float; ānanda-hilole — on waves of bliss

**5.1.** The root of the world's bliss, Balarama Nityananda,
has descended in the Kali age.
All sorrows are gone: seeing that moon-face,
people float on waves of bliss.[^07-18]

জয় জয় নিত্যানন্দ রাম ।
কনক-চম্পক-কাঁতি অঙ্গুলে চান্দের পাঁতি
রূপে জিতল কোটি কাম ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*jaya jaya nityānanda rāma |*
*kanaka-campaka-kām̐ti aṅgule cāndera pām̐ti*
*rūpe jitala koṭi kāma || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* jaya jaya nityānanda rāma — glory, glory to Nityananda-Rama; kanaka-campaka-kāṃti — the lustre of the golden champaka; aṅgule cāndera pāṃti — on the fingers a row of moons (the nails); rūpe jitala koṭi kāma — by beauty conquered millions of Kamadevas

**5.2.** *(Refrain)* Glory, glory to Nityananda-Rama!
His lustre is that of the golden champaka, on His fingers a row of moons;
by His beauty He has conquered millions of Kamadevas.[^07-19]

ও মুখ-মণ্ডল দেখি পূর্ণ-চন্দ্র কিসে লেখি
দিঘল নয়ান ভাঙু ধনু ।
আজানুলম্বিত ভুজ তল থল-পঙ্কজ
কটি খীণ করি-অরি জনু ॥

*o mukha-maṇḍala dekhi pūrṇa-candra kise lekhi*
*dighala nayāna bhāṅu dhanu |*
*ājānulambita bhuja tala thala-paṅkaja*
*kaṭi khīṇa kari-ari janu ||*

*Word for word:* o mukha-maṇḍala dekhi — seeing that face; pūrṇa-candra kise lekhi — how could I reckon the full moon (with it); dighala nayāna — long eyes; bhāṅu dhanu — eyebrows like bows; ājānulambita bhuja — arms reaching the knees; tala thala-paṅkaja — palms like land-lotuses; kaṭi khīṇa — a slender waist; kari-ari janu — like that of the elephant's enemy (the lion)

**5.3.** Seeing that face, to what can the full moon compare?
Long eyes, eyebrows like bows.
Arms reaching the knees, palms like land-lotuses,
a waist slender as a lion's.[^07-20]

চরণ-কমল-তলে ভকত-ভ্রমর বুলে
আধ বাণী অমিয়া প্রকাশ ।
ইহ কলিযুগ-জীবে উদ্ধার হইবে এবে
কহে দীন দুখী কৃষ্ণদাস ॥

*caraṇa-kamala-tale bhakata-bhramara bule*
*ādha bāṇī amiyā prakāśa |*
*iha kaliyuga-jībe uddhāra haibe ebe*
*kahe dīna dukhī kṛṣṇadāsa ||*

*Word for word:* caraṇa-kamala-tale — at the lotus feet; bhakata-bhramara bule — the bee-devotees hover; ādha bāṇī — half-words; amiyā prakāśa — reveal nectar; iha kaliyuga-jībe — for the souls of this Kali age; uddhāra haibe ebe — there will now be deliverance; kahe dīna dukhī kṛṣṇadāsa — says the humble, unhappy Krishnadasa

**5.4.** At His lotus feet the bee-devotees hover;
His half-words pour out nectar.
"Now the souls of this Kali age will be delivered,"
says the humble, unhappy Krishnadasa.[^07-21]

[^07-17]: Signature: "Krishnadasa". PK: vol. 2, PDF pp. 265–266 (printed pp. 252–253), 18th pallava, no. 6 (mark
"॥৬॥১১১৭॥"); raga suhai (P-R-Sa: shri); ms. P-R-Sa no. 1615. GPT1 — p. 416, no. 8 (raga suhai); GPT2 — sect. 6.1, no. 8.
Which Krishnadasa it is has not been established.
[^07-18]: Mss. "ka", "kha": haila (the same form, "descended"); P-R-Sa: "in an ocean of bliss" (sāgare) instead of "on waves".
[^07-19]: According to Ray's apparatus, the refrain is marked only in ms. P-R-Sa; in GPT1 too it stands after the first
stanza. Kamadeva is the god of love: the Lord's beauty surpasses that of millions of Kamadevas.
[^07-20]: "As a lion's" — literally "as the elephant's enemy's" (kari-ari); ms. "ka": airi, "ca": vairi (same meaning).
[^07-21]: Ms. "kha": "bringing nectar" (āniyā). Ms. "ka": "are delivered" (haila), P-R-Sa: haiba ("will be delivered");
GPT1: "the souls of the Kali age are all delivered".

## 6. Vasu Ghosha — "jaya jaya kalaraba nadiyā nagare…" (PK 1121; BR, p. 763)
*Gaura's appearance: in Nadia cries of "Jaya!" resound; at the full moon of Phalguna, under the Phalguni nakshatra,
Gora was born to Shachi; as in the Dvapara age Krishna appeared to Yashoda, so now He has appeared in Nadia to deliver
the souls of the Kali age. Narahari Chakravarti cites the pada in the *Bhakti-ratnakara* in the account of the Lord's
appearance. According to Majumdar, Vasu Ghosha's padas on the Lord's birth and childhood are poetic invention: Vasu was
not in Navadvipa at that time. Raga tudi (BR: basanta).*[^07-22]

জয় জয় কলরব নদিয়া নগরে ।
জনম লভিলা গোরা শচীর উদরে ॥

*jaya jaya kalaraba nadiyā nagare |*
*janama labhilā gorā śacīra udare ||*

*Word for word:* jaya jaya kalaraba — cries of "Glory, glory!"; nadiyā nagare — in the city of Nadia; janama labhilā gorā — Gora took birth (appeared); śacīra udare — from Shachi's womb

**6.1.** Glory, glory! — cries resound in the city of Nadia:
Gora has appeared from Shachi's womb.[^07-23]

ফাল্গুন-পূর্ণিমা তিথি নক্ষত্র ফাল্গুনি ।
শুভক্ষণে জনমিলা গোরা দ্বিজমণি ॥

*phālguna-pūrṇimā tithi nakṣatra phālguni |*
*śubhakṣaṇe janamilā gorā dvijamaṇi ||*

*Word for word:* phālguna-pūrṇimā tithi — on the full-moon day of Phalguna; nakṣatra phālguni — under the Phalguni nakshatra; śubha-kṣaṇe — at an auspicious moment; janamilā gorā dvijamaṇi — Gora was born, the jewel of the twice-born

**6.2.** At the full moon of Phalguna, under the Phalguni nakshatra,
at an auspicious moment Gora was born, the jewel of the twice-born.

পূর্ণিমার চন্দ্র জিনি কিরণ প্রকাশ ।
দূরে গেল অন্ধকার পাইয়া নৈরাশ ॥

*pūrṇimāra candra jini kiraṇa prakāśa |*
*dūre gela andhakāra pāiyā nairāśa ||*

*Word for word:* pūrṇimāra candra jini — surpassing the full moon; kiraṇa prakāśa — a radiance shone forth; dūre gela andhakāra — the darkness went far away; pāiyā nairāśa — having fallen into despair

**6.3.** His radiance eclipsed the full moon —
the darkness, losing hope, went far away.[^07-24]

দ্বাপরে নন্দের ঘরে কৃষ্ণ অবতার ।
যশোদা-উদরে জন্ম বিদিত সংসার ॥

*dvāpare nandera ghare kṛṣṇa abatāra |*
*yaśodā-udare janma bidita saṃsāra ||*

*Word for word:* dvāpare — in the Dvapara age; nandera ghare — in Nanda's house; kṛṣṇa abatāra — the descent of Krishna; yaśodā-udare janma — birth from Yashoda; bidita saṃsāra — known to the world

**6.4.** In the Dvapara age Krishna appeared in Nanda's house —
the whole world knows of His birth from Yashoda.

শচীর উদরে এবে জন্ম নদীয়াতে ।
কলিযুগের জীব সব নিস্তার করিতে ॥

*śacīra udare ebe janma nadīyāte |*
*kaliyugera jība saba nistāra karite ||*

*Word for word:* śacīra udare — from Shachi; ebe janma nadīyāte — now the birth in Nadia; kaliyugera jība saba — all the souls of the Kali age; nistāra karite — to deliver

**6.5.** Now He has been born to Shachi in Nadia
to deliver all the souls of the Kali age.

বাসুদেব ঘোষ কহে মনে করি আশা ।
গৌর-পদ-দ্বন্দ্ব মনে করিয়া ভরোসা ॥

*bāsudeba ghoṣa kahe mane kari āśā |*
*gaura-pada-dvandva mane kariyā bharosā ||*

*Word for word:* bāsudeba ghoṣa kahe — says Vasudeva Ghosha; mane kari āśā — cherishing hope at heart; gaura-pada-dvandva — the two feet of Gaura; mane kariyā bharosā — making them his trust at heart

**6.6.** So says Vasudeva Ghosha, cherishing hope in his heart,
trusting in his mind in the two feet of Gaura.[^07-25]

[^07-22]: Signature: "Vasudeva Ghosha". PK: vol. 2, PDF p. 267 (printed p. 254), 18th pallava, no. 10 (mark "॥১০॥১১২১॥");
raga tudi; ms. P-R-Sa no. 1619. BR, 12th wave: 1912/1913 eds. — p. 763 ("tathāhi gīte basantaḥ"), 1960 ed. — vv.
895–900; in BR lines 6.3–6.5 differ (see VAR). GPT1 — p. 51, no. 2 (raga tudi or karuna); GPT2 — sect. 2.1, no. 2.
Majumdar: Vasu's padas on the birth and childhood (PK 1121, 1150, 1151, 1161 and others) are the poet's invention; we
translate them as a poetic contemplation of lilas known from the biographies (CB Adi 2–5; CC Adi 13–14).
[^07-23]: "From Shachi's womb" is the ordinary language of the biographies about the Lord's appearance: the Lord is not born
like a conditioned soul but manifests Himself, as Krishna appeared to Devaki (Bhag. 10.3; CC Adi 13). BR: "Gorachand was
born".
[^07-24]: The Lord appeared during a lunar eclipse (CC Adi 13.89–98); the poet plays on this: the moon was dimmed before His
radiance.
[^07-25]: Vasudeva Ghosha is Vasu Ghosha. Mss. "ka", "kha", P-R-Sa: bharasā (the same). BR: "sings Vasudeva Ghosha…
trusting in the two feet of Lord Gora".

## 7. Vasu Ghosha — "gorā-rūpe ki diba tulanā…" (PK 1137)
*Gaura's form: neither gold of the highest assay, nor lightning in a cloud, nor a garland of champakas, nor the golden
ketaki, nor gorochana can compare with Him; the fragrance of His body surpasses kunkuma. In PK it is the gaura-chandrika
to the festival of Sri Radha's birth; no raga is given.*[^07-26]

গোরা-রূপে কি দিব তুলনা ।
তুলনা নহিল যে কষিল বান সোণা ॥

*gorā-rūpe ki diba tulanā |*
*tulanā nahila ye kaṣila bāna soṇā ||*

*Word for word:* gorā-rūpe — to Gora's form; ki diba tulanā — what comparison shall I give; tulanā nahila — does not compare; ye kaṣila bāna sonā — even gold of the highest assay (tested on the touchstone)

**7.1.** To what shall I compare the form of Gora?
Even gold of the highest assay does not compare with it.[^07-27]

মেঘের বিজুরী নহে রূপের উপাম ।
তুলনা নহিল রূপে চম্পকের দাম ॥

*meghera bijurī nahe rūpera upāma |*
*tulanā nahila rūpe campakera dāma ||*

*Word for word:* meghera bijurī — lightning in a cloud; nahe rūpera upāma — is no likeness of the form; tulanā nahila rūpe — does not compare with the form; campakera dāma — a garland of champakas

**7.2.** Lightning in a cloud is no likeness of this form;
a garland of champakas does not compare with it.

তুলনা নহিল স্বর্ণ-কেতকীর দল ।
তুলনা নহিল গোরোচনা নিরমল ॥

*tulanā nahila svarṇa-ketakīra dala |*
*tulanā nahila gorocanā niramala ||*

*Word for word:* tulanā nahila — does not compare; svarṇa-ketakīra dala — the petal of the golden ketaki; gorocanā niramala — pure gorochana

**7.3.** The petal of the golden ketaki does not compare,
pure gorochana does not compare.[^07-28]

কুঙ্কুম জিনিয়া অঙ্গ-গন্ধ মনোহরা ।
বাসু কহে কি দিয়া গড়িল বিধি গোরা ॥

*kuṅkuma jiniyā aṅga-gandha manoharā |*
*bāsu kahe ki diyā gaṛila bidhi gorā ||*

*Word for word:* kuṅkuma jiniyā — surpassing kunkuma; aṅga-gandha manoharā — the fragrance of the body is captivating; bāsu kahe — says Vasu; ki diyā gaṛila bidhi gorā — out of what did the Creator fashion Gora

**7.4.** The fragrance of His body, surpassing kunkuma, captivates the heart.
Says Vasu: out of what did the Creator fashion Gora?[^07-29]

[^07-26]: Signature: "Vasu". PK: vol. 2, PDF p. 274 (printed p. 261), 18th pallava, "Now the festival of Sri Radhika's birth.
There — Sri Gaurachandra", no. 11 (mark "॥১১॥১১৩৭॥"); according to Ray's apparatus — ms. P-R-Sa nos. 371 and 1641 and ms.
P-R no. 21 (the pada recurs in the manuscripts). GPT1 — p. 110, no. 1 (raga shri; the beginning of the section on the
Lord's form); GPT2 — sect. 3.1, no. 1. According to Majumdar, PK 1030 = 1137 (the pada stands twice in PK); he counts it
among Vasu's padas on Gaura's form.
[^07-27]: "Gold of the highest assay" (kaṣila bāna sonā) — gold tested on the touchstone; P-R: another reading (kaṣida kāṃcā).
Mss. "ka", "kha", "ca" and GPT1: "likeness" (upamā) instead of "comparison".
[^07-28]: Ketaki is the screw-pine with golden flowers; gorochana is a bright yellow pigment. P-R-Sa and P-R, instead of
"golden": "with the form" (rūpera, rūpe).
[^07-29]: Kunkuma is saffron. P-R-Sa, P-R: "the form, so captivating" (rūpa ati) instead of "the fragrance of the body".

## 8. Vasu Ghosha — "eka mukhe ki kahaba gorācāndera līlā…" (PK 1141)
*The infant Gaura crawls about the courtyard: saliva trickles down His little face, His lips are redder than a ripe
bimba, on His little arms are bracelets, on His feet anklets, on His neck a tiger's claw amulet, on His back a golden
chain with a silken tassel. In PK: "Now parental love befitting infancy. Sri Gaurachandra" (the beginning of the 19th
pallava). Raga tudi.*[^07-30]

এক মুখে কি কহব গোরাচান্দের লীলা ।
হামাগুড়ি যায় নানা রঙ্গে শচীর বালা ॥

*eka mukhe ki kahaba gorācāndera līlā |*
*hāmāguṛi yāya nānā raṅge śacīra bālā ||*

*Word for word:* eka mukhe — with one mouth; ki kahaba — what can I tell; gorācāndera līlā — the lilas of Gorachand; hāmāguṛi yāya — crawls on all fours; nānā raṅge — in many games; śacīra bālā — Shachi's child

**8.1.** With one mouth how can I tell the lilas of Gorachand?
Shachi's Child crawls on all fours, starting all kinds of games.[^07-31]

লালে মুখ ঝর ঝর দেখিতে সুন্দর ।
পাকা বিম্বফল জিনি সুরঙ্গ অধর ॥

*lāle mukha jhara jhara dekhite sundara |*
*pākā bimbaphala jini suraṅga adhara ||*

*Word for word:* lāle — with saliva; mukha jhara jhara — the little face trickles; dekhite sundara — lovely to see; pākā bimba-phala jini — surpassing a ripe bimba fruit; suraṅga adhara — red lips

**8.2.** Saliva trickles down His little face — how lovely it is!
His lips are redder than a ripe bimba fruit.[^07-32]

অঙ্গদ বলয়া শোভে সুবাহু-যুগলে ।
চরণে মগরা খাড়ু বাঘনখ গলে ॥

*aṅgada balayā śobhe subāhu-yugale |*
*caraṇe magarā khāṛu bāghanakha gale ||*

*Word for word:* aṅgada balayā — armlets and bracelets; śobhe subāhu-yugale — shine on the two lovely arms; caraṇe — on the feet; magarā khāṛu — makara-headed anklets; bāghanakha gale — a tiger's claw on the neck

**8.3.** On His lovely little arms are armlets and bracelets;
on His feet makara-headed anklets, on His neck a tiger's claw.[^07-33]

সোণার শিকলী পিঠে পাটের থোপনা ।
বাসুদেব ঘোষ কহে নিছনি আপনা ॥

*soṇāra śikalī piṭhe pāṭera thopanā |*
*bāsudeba ghoṣa kahe nichani āpanā ||*

*Word for word:* soṇāra śikalī piṭhe — a golden chain on the back; pāṭera thopanā — a silken tassel; bāsudeba ghoṣa kahe — says Vasudeva Ghosha; nichani āpanā — I give myself (the nichhani rite)

**8.4.** On His back a golden chain with a silken tassel.
Says Vasudeva Ghosha: "I give my very self for Him."[^07-34]

[^07-30]: Signature: "Vasudeva Ghosha". PK: vol. 2, PDF p. 275 (printed p. 262), 3rd shakha, 19th pallava, "atha
bātsalyaṃ kaumārakālocitaṃ yathā. śrīgauracandraḥ", no. 1 (mark "॥১॥১১৪১॥"); raga tudi; ms. P-R-Sa no. 1648. GPT1 — p. 62,
no. 2 (raga tudi); GPT2 — sect. 2.2, no. 2. Among Vasu's childhood padas Majumdar names "PK 1140" — evidently PK 1141:
PK 1140 is a pada of Uddhava Dasa on Radha's birth. On his assessment see note 22.
[^07-31]: P-R-Sa instead of the second line: "crawling, He plays in all kinds of ways".
[^07-32]: Mss. "ka", "ca": nāle (the same, "saliva"). Mss. "ka", "kha", "gha", "ca": "lovely" (sundara) instead of "red"
(suraṅga). The bimba is a fruit with a bright red skin, a common comparison for lips.
[^07-33]: Armlets (aṅgada) and bracelets (balayā), makara-headed anklets (magarā khāṛu), the tiger's claw (bāghanakha) are
common ornaments and amulets of children in Bengal.
[^07-34]: "I give my very self" (nichani āpanā) — the nichhani rite: one waves something around a beloved one and gives it
away (here — oneself) for his welfare.

## 9. Vasu Ghosha — "kiye hāma pekhaluṃ kanaka-putaliyā…" (PK 1150; BR, p. 774)
*The boy Gaura dances in Shachi's courtyard, all covered with dust, amid naked boys, crying "Hari, Hari!"; His mother
listens to the jingling of His anklet bells. Narahari Chakravarti cites the pada in the *Bhakti-ratnakara*: Srinivasa,
in Navadvipa, is told how Vishvambhara danced in this courtyard. In PK: "Now parental love befitting childhood and
boyhood. Sri Gaurachandra". Raga mayur (BR: kamoda).*[^07-35]

কিয়ে হাম পেখলুঁ কনক-পুতলিয়া ।
শচীর আঙ্গিনায় নাচে ধুলি-ধূসরিয়া ॥

*kiye hāma pekhalum̐ kanaka-putaliyā |*
*śacīra āṅgināya nāce dhuli-dhūsariyā ||*

*Word for word:* kiye hāma pekhaluṃ — what have I seen; kanaka-putaliyā — a golden doll; śacīra āṅgināya — in Shachi's courtyard; nāce — dances; dhuli-dhūsariyā — grey with dust

**9.1.** What a golden doll I have seen!
In Shachi's courtyard He dances, all grey with dust.[^07-36]

চৌদিকে দিগম্বর বালকে বেঢ়িয়া ।
তার মাঝে গোরা নাচে হরি হরি বলিয়া ॥

*caudike digambara bālake beṛhiyā |*
*tāra mājhe gorā nāce hari hari baliyā ||*

*Word for word:* caudike — on all sides; digambara bālake — naked boys; beṛhiyā — surrounding; tāra mājhe — in their midst; gorā nāce — Gora dances; hari hari baliyā — saying "Hari, Hari"

**9.2.** On all sides naked boys surround Him,
and in their midst Gora dances, saying "Hari, Hari!"

রাতুল কমল-পদে ধায় দ্বিজমণিয়া ।
জননী শুনয়ে ভাল নূপুরের ধ্বনিয়া ॥

*rātula kamala-pade dhāya dvijamaṇiyā |*
*jananī śunaye bhāla nūpurera dhvaniyā ||*

*Word for word:* rātula kamala-pade — on reddish lotus feet; dhāya — runs; dvijamaṇiyā — the jewel of the twice-born; jananī śunaye bhāla — the mother gladly listens; nūpurera dhvaniyā — to the jingling of the anklet bells

**9.3.** On reddish lotus feet the jewel of the twice-born runs about;
His mother listens with joy to the jingling of His anklet bells.[^07-37]

বাসুদেব ঘোষে কহে শিশু-রস জানিয়া ।
ধন্য নদিয়ার লোক নবদ্বীপ ধনিয়া ॥

*bāsudeba ghoṣe kahe śiśu-rasa jāniyā |*
*dhanya nadiyāra loka nabadvīpa dhaniyā ||*

*Word for word:* bāsudeba ghoṣe kahe — says Vasudeva Ghosha; śiśu-rasa jāniyā — knowing the taste of childhood; dhanya nadiyāra loka — blessed are the people of Nadia; nabadvīpa dhaniyā — blessed is Navadvipa

**9.4.** Says Vasudeva Ghosha, who knows the taste of the childhood play:
"Blessed are the people of Nadia, blessed is Navadvipa!"[^07-38]

[^07-35]: Signature: "Vasudeva Ghosha". PK: vol. 2, PDF p. 279 (printed p. 266), 19th pallava, no. 10 (mark
"॥১০॥১১৫০॥"); raga mayur (mss. "gha", "ca": maur). BR, 12th wave: 1913 ed. — p. 774 ("gīte rāgaḥ kāmoda"), 1960 ed. —
vv. 1035–1038. GPT1 — p. 63, no. 4 (raga beloar — dashakoshi); GPT2 — sect. 2.2, no. 4. On Majumdar's assessment see
note 22.
[^07-36]: "What… I have seen" (kiye hāma pekhaluṃ) is a Vrajabuli turn of phrase.
[^07-37]: "The jewel of the twice-born" is the young brahmana Nimai; GPT1: "the sun-jewel" (dinamaṇiyā); BR: "on radiant lotus
feet". In 9.2 mss. "gha", "ca": beṛiyā (the same, "surrounding"); ms. "gha": "Gaura". Ms. "ka": "the sweet jingle of the
bells".
[^07-38]: BR after the pada: "O Srinivasa, in this courtyard Vishvambhara danced in all kinds of ways — a wonderful sight".

## 10. Vasu Ghosha — "śacīra āṅgināya nāce biśvambhara rāy…" (PK 1151; BR, p. 774)
*Hide-and-seek: Vishvambhara dances in the courtyard and, laughing, hides from His mother, covering His face with the
end of His cloth: "I have hidden!" — Shachi plays along: "Vishvambhara, I cannot see You!"; holding the end of her sari,
He skips along with the gait of a wagtail. In BR it comes right after the previous pada. The same raga (BR: vibhasa).*[^07-39]

শচীর আঙ্গিনায় নাচে বিশ্বম্ভর রায় ।
হাসি হাসি ফিরি ফিরি মায়েরে লুকায় ॥

*śacīra āṅgināya nāce biśvambhara rāya |*
*hāsi hāsi phiri phiri māyere lukāya ||*

*Word for word:* śacīra āṅgināya — in Shachi's courtyard; nāce biśvambhara rāy — Vishvambhara Raya dances; hāsi hāsi — laughing; phiri phiri — turning about; māyere lukāy — hides from His mother

**10.1.** In Shachi's courtyard Vishvambhara Raya dances;
laughing, turning about, He hides from His mother.

বয়ানে বসন দিয়া বোলে লুকাইলুঁ ।
শচী বোলে বিশ্বম্ভর আমি না দেখিলুঁ ॥

*bayāne basana diyā bole lukāilum̐ |*
*śacī bole biśvambhara āmi nā dekhilum̐ ||*

*Word for word:* bayāne basana diyā — putting the cloth over His face; bole lukāiluṃ — says, "I have hidden"; śacī bole — Shachi says; biśvambhara — Vishvambhara; āmi nā dekhiluṃ — I have not seen (cannot see)

**10.2.** Covering His face with His cloth, He says: "I have hidden!"
Shachi says: "Vishvambhara, I cannot see You!"[^07-40]

মায়ের অঞ্চল ধরি চঞ্চল-চরণে ।
নাচিয়া নাচিয়া যায় খঞ্জন-গমনে ॥

*māyera añcala dhari cañcala-caraṇe |*
*nāciyā nāciyā yāya khañjana-gamane ||*

*Word for word:* māyera añcala dhari — holding the end of His mother's sari; cañcala-caraṇe — on restless feet; nāciyā nāciyā yāya — goes dancing along; khañjana-gamane — with the gait of a wagtail

**10.3.** Holding the end of His mother's sari, on restless little feet
He goes skipping with the gait of a wagtail.[^07-41]

বাসুদেব ঘোষে কহে অপরূপ শোভা ।
শিশু-রূপ দেখি হয় জগ-মন-লোভা ॥

*bāsudeba ghoṣe kahe aparūpa śobhā |*
*śiśu-rūpa dekhi haya jaga-mana-lobhā ||*

*Word for word:* bāsudeba ghoṣe kahe — says Vasudeva Ghosha; aparūpa śobhā — a wondrous beauty; śiśu-rūpa dekhi — seeing the form of the Child; haya jaga-mana-lobhā — the world's mind is filled with longing

**10.4.** Says Vasudeva Ghosha: "A wondrous beauty!
Seeing the form of the Child, the world is filled with longing."

[^07-39]: Signature: "Vasudeva Ghosha". PK: vol. 2, PDF p. 279 (printed p. 266), 19th pallava, no. 11 (mark "॥১১॥১১৫১॥");
"tathā rāga" (mayur); ms. P-R-Sa no. 1657. BR, 12th wave: 1913 ed. — p. 774 ("gīti bibhāṣaḥ"), 1960 ed. — vv. 1040–1043.
GPT1 — p. 63, no. 5 (beloar — dashakoshi); GPT2 — sect. 2.2, no. 5.
[^07-40]: P-R-Sa: "on the face" (badane) — the same meaning.
[^07-41]: The wagtail (khañjana) is a bird with a lively, skipping gait; a common poetic comparison.

## 11. Vasu Ghosha — "gorā nāce śacīra dulāliyā…" (PK 1161; BR, pp. 774–775)
*Shachi's darling Gora dances, the boys around Him clap their hands: "Haribol!"; on His head a red cap, on His neck golden
beads, His mother has lovingly tied His little dhoti; the poet exclaims: "Take Him in your arms — Gora is the life of my
life!" In BR it is the third pada of the same series. In PK: "Now the rasa of parental love, another mode. Shri
Gaurachandra" (the beginning of the 20th pallava). Raga bhatiyari (BR: bhatyali).*[^07-42]

গোরা নাচে শচীর দুলালিয়া ।
চৌদিকে বালক মেলি সভে দেই করতালি
হরিবোল হরিবোল বলিয়া ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*gorā nāce śacīra dulāliyā |*
*caudike bālaka meli sabhe dei karatāli*
*haribola haribola baliyā || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* gorā nāce — Gora dances; śacīra dulāliyā — Shachi's darling; caudike bālaka meli — the boys gathering around; sabhe dei karatāli — all clap their hands; haribola haribola baliyā — saying "Haribol, Haribol"

**11.1.** *(Refrain)* Gora dances, Shachi's darling;
the boys have gathered around, all clap their hands,
saying "Haribol, Haribol!"

সুরঙ্গ চতুনা মাথে গলায় সোণার কাঁঠি ।
সাধ করিয়া মায় পরাইছে ধড়া গাছি আঁটি ॥

*suraṅga catunā māthe galāya soṇāra kām̐ṭhi |*
*sādha kariyā māya parāiche dhaṛā gāchi ām̐ṭi ||*

*Word for word:* suraṅga catunā māthe — a red cap on the head; galāya soṇāra kāṃṭhi — golden beads on the neck; sādha kariyā — lovingly (as she fancied); māy parāiche — the mother has put on; dhaṛā gāchi āṃṭi — a little dhoti, tied tight

**11.2.** On His head a red cap, on His neck golden beads;
with love His mother has tied His little dhoti tight.[^07-43]

সুন্দর চাঁচর কেশ সুবলিত তনু ।
ভুবন-মোহন বেশ ভুরু কাম-ধনু ॥

*sundara cām̐cara keśa subalita tanu |*
*bhubana-mohana beśa bhuru kāma-dhanu ||*

*Word for word:* sundara cāṃcara keśa — lovely curling hair; subalita tanu — a well-formed body; bhubana-mohana beśa — a dress charming the world; bhuru kāma-dhanu — eyebrows like Kamadeva's bow

**11.3.** Lovely curling hair, a well-formed body;
a dress that charms the world, eyebrows — Kamadeva's bow.

রজত কাঞ্চন নানা অভরণ
অঙ্গে মনোহর সাজে ।
রাতা-উতপল চরণ-যুগল
তুলিতে নূপুর বাজে ॥

*rajata kāñcana nānā abharaṇa*
*aṅge manohara sāje |*
*rātā-utapala caraṇa-yugala*
*tulite nūpura bāje ||*

*Word for word:* rajata kāñcana — silver and gold; nānā abharaṇa — many ornaments; aṅge manohara sāje — adorn the body charmingly; rātā-utapala — red lotuses; caraṇa-yugala — the pair of feet; tulite — as He lifts them; nūpura bāje — the anklet bells ring

**11.4.** Silver and golden ornaments
adorn His body charmingly.
As He lifts His feet — red lotuses —
the anklet bells ring.

শচীর অঙ্গনে নাচয়ে সঘনে
বোলে আধ আধ বাণী ।
বাসুদেব ঘোষে বোলে ধর ধর কর কোলে
গোরা মোর পরাণের পরাণি ॥

*śacīra aṅgane nācaye saghane*
*bole ādha ādha bāṇī |*
*bāsudeba ghoṣe bole dhara dhara kara kole*
*gorā mora parāṇera parāṇi ||*

*Word for word:* śacīra aṅgane — in Shachi's courtyard; nācaye saghane — dances again and again; bole ādha ādha bāṇī — babbles half-words; bāsudeba ghoṣe bole — says Vasudeva Ghosha; dhara dhara — hold Him, hold Him; kara kole — take Him in your arms; gorā mora parāṇera parāṇi — Gora is the life of my life

**11.5.** In Shachi's courtyard He dances and dances,
babbling half-words.
Says Vasudeva Ghosha: "Hold Him, hold Him, take Him in your arms —
Gora is the life of my life!"[^07-44]

[^07-42]: Signature: "Vasudeva Ghosha". PK: vol. 2, PDF pp. 282–283 (printed pp. 269–270), 3rd shakha, 20th pallava, "atha
bātsalyarasaḥ prakārāntaraṃ yathā. śrīgauracandraḥ", no. 1 (mark "॥১॥১১৬১॥"); raga bhatiyari; ms. P-R-Sa no. 1680. BR,
12th wave: 1913 ed. — pp. 774–775 ("punaḥ rāga bhāṭyāli"), 1960 ed. — vv. 1044–1048. GPT1 — p. 63, no. 3 (raga
bhatiyari); GPT2 — sect. 2.2, no. 3. The catalogue's former first line ("śacīra aṅgane nācaye saghane") is the
beginning of the last stanza.
[^07-43]: "Cap" (catunā) — a child's cap; ms. "ca": catulā. "Beads" (kāṃṭhi) — a string of beads. Ms. "ka": parāñāche (the
same, "has tied").
[^07-44]: Ms. "ka": "Gora, Gora is the life of my life"; BR: "Gora is like the life of my life".

## 12. Chaitanyadasa — "dekha dekha aparūpa gaurāṅga-bilāsa…" (PK 1242)
*An allegory: in Navadvipa Gauranga again manifests the lila of lifting Govardhana. He bids the people of Kali worship
the "Govardhana" of pure bhakti: the nine kinds of bhakti are its peaks, the five rasas its fruits, pulaka, tears and
trembling its adornment. The "Indra" of the Kali age, on the "Airavata" of irreligion, sends a downpour of lust,
lightnings of anger and a hail of greed, but Gauranga lifts the mountain of bhakti; Kali, put to shame, begs forgiveness
and vows not to touch those who sing the Lord's glory. In PK it is the gaura-chandrika to the "Govardhana-yatra" (3rd
shakha, 23rd pallava). Raga gandhara (P-R-Sa: dhanashi).*[^07-45]

দেখ দেখ অপরূপ গৌরাঙ্গ-বিলাস ।
পুন গিরি-ধারণ পুরব লীলা-ক্রম
নবদ্বীপে করিলা প্রকাশ ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*dekha dekha aparūpa gaurāṅga-bilāsa |*
*puna giri-dhāraṇa puraba līlā-krama*
*nabadvīpe karilā prakāśa || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* dekha dekha — behold, behold; aparūpa gaurāṅga-bilāsa — the wondrous play of Gauranga; puna giri-dhāraṇa — again the lifting of the hill; puraba līlā-krama — in the order of the former lila; nabadvīpe karilā prakāśa — He manifested in Navadvipa

**12.1.** *(Refrain)* Behold, behold the wondrous play of Gauranga!
Again the lifting of the hill — in the order of the former lila —
He has manifested in Navadvipa.[^07-46]

শুদ্ধ ভক্তি গোবর্দ্ধন পূজা কর জগ-জন
এই বিধি দিলা কলি মাঝে ।
শ্রবণাদি নব অঙ্গ কল্পতরুময় শৃঙ্গ
পঞ্চ-রস ফল তাহে সাজে ॥

*śuddha bhakti gobarddhana pūjā kara jaga-jana*
*ei bidhi dilā kali mājhe |*
*śrabaṇādi naba aṅga kalpatarumaya śṛṅga*
*pañca-rasa phala tāhe sāje ||*

*Word for word:* śuddha bhakti gobarddhana — the Govardhana of pure bhakti; pūjā kara jaga-jana — worship, people of the world; ei bidhi dilā kali mājhe — this law He gave in the Kali age; śrabaṇādi naba aṅga — the nine limbs beginning with hearing; kalpatarumaya śṛṅga — peaks like wish-fulfilling trees; pañca-rasa phala — the five rasas are the fruits; tāhe sāje — adorn them

**12.2.** "People of the world, worship the Govardhana of pure bhakti!" —
such is the law He gave in the Kali age.
The nine branches of bhakti beginning with hearing are its peaks, like wish-fulfilling trees;
the five rasas are the fruits that adorn them.[^07-47]

পুলক-অঙ্কুর শোভা অশ্রু-জল মনোলোভা
মন্দ বায়ু বেপথু সুন্দর ।
নিজেন্দ্রিয়-উপচারে সেব সেই গিরিবরে
প্রেম-মণি পাবে ইষ্ট-বর ॥

*pulaka-aṅkura śobhā aśru-jala manolobhā*
*manda bāyu bepathu sundara |*
*nijendriya-upacāre seba sei giribare*
*prema-maṇi pābe iṣṭa-bara ||*

*Word for word:* pulaka-aṅkura śobhā — sprouts of pulaka are its beauty; aśru-jala manolobhā — tears captivate the heart; manda bāyu — a gentle breeze; bepathu sundara — lovely trembling; nijendriya-upacāre — with one's own senses as offerings; seba sei giribare — serve that best of hills; prema-maṇi pābe — you will obtain the jewel of prema; iṣṭa-bara — the desired boon

**12.3.** Sprouts of pulaka are its beauty, streams of tears captivate the heart,
a gentle breeze is its lovely trembling.
Serve this best of hills, offering it your own senses as gifts —
you will obtain the jewel of prema, the desired boon.[^07-48]

দেখিয়া লোকের গতি কলিযুগ-সুরপতি
কোপে তনু কম্পিত হইল ।
অধরম-ঐরাবতে কুমতি-ইন্দ্রাণী সাথে
সসৈন্যেতে সাজিয়া আইল ॥

*dekhiyā lokera gati kaliyuga-surapati*
*kope tanu kampita haila |*
*adharama-airābate kumati-indrāṇī sāthe*
*sasainyete sājiyā āila ||*

*Word for word:* dekhiyā lokera gati — seeing the ways of people; kaliyuga-surapati — the king of the gods of the Kali age; kope tanu kampita haila — his body shook with anger; adharama-airābate — on the Airavata of irreligion; kumati-indrāṇī sāthe — with Indrani, evil-mindedness; sasainyete sājiyā āila — came arrayed with his army

**12.4.** Seeing how people lived, the king of the gods of the Kali age
shook with anger.
On the Airavata of irreligion, together with Indrani — evil-mindedness —
he came with his army arrayed.[^07-49]

কাম-মেঘ বরিষণে ক্রোধ-বজ্র নিক্ষেপণে
লোকের হইল বড় ডর ।
লোভ-মোহ-শিলাঘাতে মাৎসর্য্যাদি-খর-বাতে
ধৈর্য্য ধর্ম্ম উড়ে নিরন্তর ॥

*kāma-megha bariṣaṇe krodha-bajra nikṣepaṇe*
*lokera haila baṛa ḍara |*
*lobha-moha-śilāghāte mātsaryyādi-khara-bāte*
*dhairyya dharmma uṛe nirantara ||*

*Word for word:* kāma-megha bariṣaṇe — by the downpour of the clouds of lust; krodha-bajra nikṣepaṇe — by the hurling of thunderbolts of anger; lokera haila baṛa ḍara — great fear came upon people; lobha-moha-śilāghāte — by blows of the stones of greed and delusion; mātsaryādi-khara-bāte — by harsh winds of envy and the rest; dhairya dharma uṛe nirantara — steadfastness and dharma are ceaselessly blown away

**12.5.** The clouds of lust poured down, the thunderbolts of anger were hurled —
a great fear seized the people.
Under the blows of the stones of greed and delusion, under the harsh winds of envy and the rest,
steadfastness and dharma are ceaselessly blown away.[^07-50]

জানিয়া জীবের ভয় শ্রীগৌরাঙ্গ দয়াময়
উপায় চিন্তিলা মনে মনে ।
ভক্ত-ভাব-সারোদ্ধার নিজে করি অঙ্গীকার
ভক্তি-গিরি করিলা ধারণে ॥

*jāniyā jībera bhaya śrīgaurāṅga dayāmaya*
*upāya cintilā mane mane |*
*bhakta-bhāba-sāroddhāra nije kari aṅgīkāra*
*bhakti-giri karilā dhāraṇe ||*

*Word for word:* jāniyā jībera bhaya — knowing the fear of the living beings; śrīgaurāṅga dayāmaya — the merciful Sri Gauranga; upāya cintilā mane mane — conceived a means in His heart; bhakta-bhāba-sāroddhāra — the essence of a devotee's bhava; nije kari aṅgīkāra — Himself accepting; bhakti-giri karilā dhāraṇe — lifted the mountain of bhakti

**12.6.** Seeing the fear of the living beings, the merciful Sri Gauranga
conceived a means in His heart:
Himself accepting the essence of a devotee's bhava,
He lifted the mountain of bhakti.[^07-51]

তাহার আশ্রয়ে লোক পাসরিল দুঃখ শোক
কলি-ভয় খণ্ডিল সকলে ।
তবে কলি-দেবরাজ পাঞা পরাভব-লাজ
স্তুতি করে চরণ-কমলে ॥

*tāhāra āśraye loka pāsarila duḥkha śoka*
*kali-bhaya khaṇḍila sakale |*
*tabe kali-debarāja pāñā parābhaba-lāja*
*stuti kare caraṇa-kamale ||*

*Word for word:* tāhāra āśraye — under its shelter; loka pāsarila duḥkha śoka — people forgot grief and sorrow; kali-bhaya khaṇḍila sakale — the fear of Kali was dispelled for all; tabe kali-debarāja — then Kali, the king of the gods; pāñā parābhaba-lāja — feeling the shame of defeat; stuti kare caraṇa-kamale — offers praise to the lotus feet

**12.7.** Under its shelter people forgot grief and sorrow,
everyone's fear of Kali was dispelled.
Then Kali, the king of the gods, ashamed of his defeat,
offers praise to the lotus feet.

অপরাধ ক্ষমাইয়া কহে কিছু দীন হৈয়া
যত জীব প্রভুর আশ্রয় ।
যেবা তব গুণ গায় তাহে মোর নাহি দায়
এই সত্য করিল নিশ্চয় ॥

*aparādha kṣamāiyā kahe kichu dīna haiyā*
*yata jība prabhura āśraya |*
*yebā taba guṇa gāya tāhe mora nāhi dāya*
*ei satya karila niścaya ||*

*Word for word:* aparādha kṣamāiyā — having begged forgiveness for the offence; kahe kichu dīna haiyā — says humbly; yata jība prabhura āśraya — all souls are under the Lord's shelter; yebā taba guṇa gāya — whoever sings Your qualities; tāhe mora nāhi dāya — over him I have no claim; ei satya karila niścaya — this vow he firmly made

**12.8.** Having begged forgiveness for his offence, he humbly says:
"All souls are under the Lord's shelter;
whoever sings Your glory — over him I have no claim," —
this he solemnly confirmed.[^07-52]

প্রভু তারে দয়া কৈল ধন্য কলি নাম থুইল
অদ্যাপিহ ঘোষয়ে সংসার ।
চৈতন্যদাসেতে বলে গোবর্দ্ধন-লীলা-ছলে
যুগে যুগে জীবের উদ্ধার ॥

*prabhu tāre dayā kaila dhanya kali nāma thuila*
*adyāpiha ghoṣaye saṃsāra |*
*caitanyadāsete bale gobarddhana-līlā-chale*
*yuge yuge jībera uddhāra ||*

*Word for word:* prabhu tāre dayā kaila — the Lord showed him mercy; dhanya kali nāma thuila — gave him the name "Blessed Kali"; adyāpiha ghoṣaye saṃsāra — to this day the world proclaims it; caitanyadāsete bale — says Chaitanyadasa; gobarddhana-līlā-chale — under the guise of the Govardhana lila; yuge yuge jībera uddhāra — from age to age the deliverance of souls

**12.9.** The Lord showed him mercy — "Blessed Kali" became his name,
and to this day the world proclaims it.
Says Chaitanyadasa: under the guise of the Govardhana lila —
from age to age the deliverance of souls.[^07-53]

[^07-45]: Signature: "Chaitanyadasa" ("caitanyadāsete bale"). PK: vol. 2, PDF pp. 312–313 (printed pp. 299–300), 3rd shakha,
23rd pallava, "atha gobarddhana-yātrā. taducita-śrīgauracandraḥ", no. 1 (mark "॥১॥১২৪২॥"); raga gandhara (P-R-Sa:
dhanashi); ms. P-R-Sa no. 1776. In the catalogue this pada was wrongly listed as PK 1243 by Krishnadasa (KR-013); PK 1243
