is the next pada, on the Govardhana-puja in Vraja, signed "Krishnadasa" (Krishna-lila; not translated). The pada was not
found in GPT1. Chaitanyadasa was, according to Majumdar, a contemporary of the Lord (cf. chapters 4–6); the allegorical
form, however, suggests rather a later author.
[^07-46]: Krishna lifted Govardhana, protecting Vraja from Indra's wrath (Bhag. 10.24–25); the poet sees in Gauranga's
preaching of bhakti a "repetition" of that lila.
[^07-47]: The nine kinds of bhakti are hearing, chanting, remembering and so on (Bhag. 7.5.23–24). The five rasas are shanta,
dasya, sakhya, vatsalya, madhurya. Mss. "ka", "kha", "ca", P-R-Sa: "limbs" (aṅga) instead of "peaks" (śṛṅga).
[^07-48]: Pulaka is the bristling of the body's hair in ecstasy; tears and trembling are also sattvika-bhavas. Serving the
Lord of the senses with the senses is the definition of bhakti (Narada-pancharatra, quoted in *Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu*
1.1.12).
[^07-49]: Airavata is Indra's elephant, Indrani his consort: here "the king of the gods" is Kali himself, the personified age.
[^07-50]: Ms. "kha", P-R-Sa: mahā (the same, "great").
[^07-51]: "Accepting the essence of a devotee's bhava" — in this avatara the Lord accepts the mood of His devotee (CC Adi 4).
[^07-52]: Mss. "ka", "kha", "ca": khemāiyā (a dialect form of "having begged forgiveness").
[^07-53]: "Blessed Kali" (dhanya kali) — cf. Bhag. 11.5.36 and 12.3.52: the wise praise the Kali age, for in it the highest
goal is attained by sankirtana.

## 13. Krishnadasa — "ānande bhakatagaṇa dei jaya-raba…" (PK 1570)
*Gaura's abhisheka in Srivasa's house: the devotees cry "Jaya!", Gauranga is bathed with panchagavya, panchamrita and
the water of a hundred pots; He sits on a jewelled platform; Advaita and Nityananda float in prema, Mukunda, Murari and
others sing, Haridasa dances crying "Hari!"; the men and women of Nadia see it all with their own eyes. In PK: "Now the
abhisheka-vilasa. First, that of Sri Gaurachandra" (3rd shakha, 31st pallava). Raga suhai.*[^07-54]

আনন্দে ভকতগণ দেই জয়-রব ।
শ্রীবাস পণ্ডিত-ঘরে মহামহোৎসব ॥

*ānande bhakatagaṇa dei jaya-raba |*
*śrībāsa paṇḍita-ghare mahāmahotsaba ||*

*Word for word:* ānande — in bliss; bhakata-gaṇa — the devotees; dei jaya-raba — raise the cry "Jaya!"; śrībāsa paṇḍita-ghare — in the house of Srivasa Pandita; mahā-mahotsaba — a great festival

**13.1.** In bliss the devotees raise the cry "Jaya!";
in the house of Srivasa Pandita there is a great festival.

পঞ্চগব্য পঞ্চামৃত শত ঘট জলে ।
গৌরাঙ্গের অভিষেক করে কুতূহলে ॥

*pañcagabya pañcāmṛta śata ghaṭa jale |*
*gaurāṅgera abhiṣeka kare kutūhale ||*

*Word for word:* pañcagabya — with panchagavya; pañcāmṛta — with panchamrita; śata ghaṭa jale — with the water of a hundred pots; gaurāṅgera abhiṣeka kare — perform the abhisheka of Gauranga; kutūhale — joyfully

**13.2.** With panchagavya, panchamrita, the water of a hundred pots
they joyfully perform the abhisheka of Gauranga.[^07-55]

রতন-বেদীর পর বসি গোরাচান্দ ।
অপরূপ রূপ সে রমণী-মন-ফাঁদ ॥

*ratana-bedīra para basi gorācānda |*
*aparūpa rūpa se ramaṇī-mana-phām̐da ||*

*Word for word:* ratana-bedīra para — on the jewelled platform; basi gorācānda — Gorachand sits; aparūpa rūpa se — that wondrous beauty; ramaṇī-mana-phāṃda — a snare for the hearts of women

**13.3.** On the jewelled platform sits Gorachand;
a wondrous beauty — a snare for the hearts of women.[^07-56]

শান্তিপুর-নাথ আর নিত্যানন্দ রায় ।
হেরিয়া গৌরাঙ্গ মুখ প্রেমে ভাসি যায় ॥

*śāntipura-nātha āra nityānanda rāya |*
*heriyā gaurāṅga mukha preme bhāsi yāya ||*

*Word for word:* śāntipura-nātha — the Lord of Shantipura (Advaita); āra nityānanda rāy — and Nityananda Raya; heriyā gaurāṅga mukha — gazing at Gauranga's face; preme bhāsi yāy — float away in prema

**13.4.** The Lord of Shantipura and Nityananda Raya,
gazing at Gauranga's face, float away in prema.[^07-57]

মুকুন্দ মুরারি আদি সুমধুর গায় ।
হরি বলি হরিদাস নাচিয়া বেড়ায় ॥

*mukunda murāri ādi sumadhura gāya |*
*hari bali haridāsa nāciyā beṛāya ||*

*Word for word:* mukunda murāri ādi — Mukunda, Murari and others; sumadhura gāy — sing sweetly; hari bali — crying "Hari"; haridāsa nāciyā beṛāy — Haridasa dances all around

**13.5.** Mukunda, Murari and others sing sweetly;
crying "Hari!", Haridasa dances all around.

কহে কৃষ্ণদাস গোরাচাঁদের অভিষেক ।
নদীয়ার নরনারী দেখে পরতেক ॥

*kahe kṛṣṇadāsa gorācām̐dera abhiṣeka |*
*nadīyāra naranārī dekhe parateka ||*

*Word for word:* kahe kṛṣṇadāsa — says Krishnadasa; gorācāṃdera abhiṣeka — the abhisheka of Gorachand; nadīyāra naranārī — the men and women of Nadia; dekhe parateka — see with their own eyes

**13.6.** Says Krishnadasa: the abhisheka of Gorachand
the men and women of Nadia see with their own eyes.[^07-58]

[^07-54]: Signature: "Krishnadasa". PK: vol. 2, PDF p. 465 (printed p. 452), 3rd shakha, 31st pallava,
"athābhiṣeka-bilāsaḥ. ādau śrīgauracandrasya", no. 2 (mark "॥২॥১৫৭০॥"); raga suhai; ms. P-R-Sa no. 2114. GPT1 — p. 239,
no. 5 (raga suhai); GPT2 — sect. 4.1, no. 5. The catalogue's former first line ("ratana-bedīra para…") is the
beginning of the third couplet. The next pada of PK (1571) is Vasu Ghosha's pada on the abhisheka (chapter 1, no. 2).
Which Krishnadasa it is has not been established. On the Lord's abhisheka in Srivasa's house see CB Madhya 9.
[^07-55]: Panchagavya — the five products of the cow; panchamrita — the five nectars (milk, curd, ghee, honey, sugar); the
Deity is bathed with them at the abhisheka.
[^07-56]: The image (as in the padas on Krishna) speaks of the Lord's irresistible beauty, not of mundane passion; worship of
Gaura in the mood of "gaura-nagari" is not accepted by the Gaudiya Vaishnava tradition (Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa
Kaviraja, Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati): in Navadvipa, according to CB (Adi 15), the Lord did not even jest with women.
[^07-57]: The Lord of Shantipura is Advaita. Mss. "ka", "kha", P-R-Sa: "having seen" (heri); P-R-Sa: "form" (rūpa) instead
of "face".
[^07-58]: "With their own eyes" (parateka = pratyakṣa).

## 14. Ramachandra — "dekha śacīnandana jagata-jībana-dhana…" (PK 2064)
*The Lord's dance: the Son of Shachi, the treasure of the world's life, ceaselessly gives out prema; in ecstasy He dances,
crying "Hari"; hearing of Vrindavana's glories, He rolls on the ground and laughs; Kashishvara, Abhirama, Pandita
Purushottama and Narahari Dasa sing His glory; at the sound of the khol and karatalas children and wealthy alike come
running. In PK it stands in the 17th pallava (the dance and pastimes of Gauranga). Raga "the same" (tathā rāga).*[^07-59]

দেখ শচীনন্দন জগত-জীবন-ধন
অনুখণ প্রেম-ধন জগ-জনে যাচে ।
ভাবে বিভোর বর গৌর-তনু পুলকিত
সঘনে বোলাঞা হরি গোরা পহুঁ নাচে ॥

*dekha śacīnandana jagata-jībana-dhana*
*anukhaṇa prema-dhana jaga-jane yāce |*
*bhābe bibhora bara gaura-tanu pulakita*
*saghane bolāñā hari gorā pahum̐ nāce ||*

*Word for word:* dekha śacīnandana — behold, the Son of Shachi; jagata-jībana-dhana — the treasure of the world's life; anukhaṇa — ceaselessly; prema-dhana jaga-jane yāce — offers the people the treasure of prema; bhābe bibhora bara — the Best One, rapt in bhava; gaura-tanu pulakita — His golden body thrilling; saghane bolāñā hari — crying "Hari" again and again; gorā pahuṃ nāce — Lord Gora dances

**14.1.** Behold: the Son of Shachi, the treasure of the world's life,
ceaselessly offers people the treasure of prema.
Rapt in bhava, the Best One — His golden body thrilling —
crying "Hari" again and again, Lord Gora dances.[^07-60]

সব অবতার-সার গোরা অবতার ।
হেম-বরণ জিনি নিরুপম তনুখানি
অরুণ নয়নে বহে প্রেমক ধার ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*saba abatāra-sāra gorā abatāra |*
*hema-baraṇa jini nirupama tanukhāni*
*aruṇa nayane bahe premaka dhāra || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* saba abatāra-sāra — the essence of all avataras; gorā abatāra — the Gora-avatara; hema-baraṇa jini — surpassing the colour of gold; nirupama tanukhāni — the peerless body; aruṇa nayane — from reddish eyes; bahe premaka dhāra — flow streams of prema

**14.2.** *(Refrain)* The essence of all avataras is the Gora-avatara!
His peerless body surpasses the colour of gold,
from His reddish eyes flow streams of prema.

বৃন্দাবন-গুণ শুনি লুঠত সে দ্বিজ-মণি
ভাব-ভরে গরগর পহুঁ মোর হাসে ।
কাশীশ্বর অভিরাম পণ্ডিত পুরুষোত্তম
গুণ গান করতহি নরহরি দাসে ॥

*bṛndābana-guṇa śuni luṭhata se dvija-maṇi*
*bhāba-bhare garagara pahum̐ mora hāse |*
*kāśīśvara abhirāma paṇḍita puruṣottama*
*guṇa gāna karatahi narahari dāse ||*

*Word for word:* bṛndābana-guṇa śuni — hearing Vrindavana's glories; luṭhata se dvija-maṇi — that jewel of the twice-born rolls on the ground; bhāba-bhare garagara — overflowing with bhava; pahuṃ mora hāse — my Lord laughs; kāśīśvara abhirāma — Kashishvara, Abhirama; paṇḍita puruṣottama — Pandita Purushottama; guṇa gāna karatahi — sing His glory; narahari dāse — [and] Narahari Dasa

**14.3.** Hearing Vrindavana's glories, this jewel of the twice-born rolls on the ground;
overflowing with bhava, my Lord laughs.
Kashishvara, Abhirama, Pandita Purushottama
sing His glory, and with them Narahari Dasa.[^07-61]

খোল করতাল শুনি কিবা শিশু কিবা ধনী
ধায়ত সবহুঁ প্রেম-প্রতিআশে ।
এমন গৌর-গুণ যাক জাগয়ে মন
তাকর সেবক রামচন্দ্র দাসে ॥

*khola karatāla śuni kibā śiśu kibā dhanī*
*dhāyata sabahum̐ prema-pratiāśe |*
*emana gaura-guṇa yāka jāgaye mana*
*tākara sebaka rāmacandra dāse ||*

*Word for word:* khola karatāla śuni — hearing the khol and karatalas; kibā śiśu kibā dhanī — children and wealthy alike; dhāyata sabahum̐ — all come running; prema-pratiāśe — in hope of prema; emana gaura-guṇa — such qualities of Gaura; yāka jāgaye mana — whose heart is awakened [to]; tākara sebaka — his servant; rāmacandra dāse — is Ramachandra Dasa

**14.4.** Hearing the khol and karatalas, children and wealthy alike
come running — all in hope of prema.
Whoever's heart is awakened to such qualities of Gaura —
his servant is Ramachandra Dasa.[^07-62]

[^07-59]: Signature: "Ramachandra Dasa". PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 217 (printed p. 206), 4th shakha, 17th pallava, no. 6 (mark
"॥৬॥২০৬৪॥"); "tathā rāga"; ms. P-R-Sa no. 2173. GPT1 — p. 250, no. 6 (raga beloar; without stanza 14.4, i.e. without
the signature); GPT2 — sect. 4.2, no. 6. According to Majumdar, Ramachandra is probably Ramachandra Kaviraja of
Nityananda's branch (not his namesake, the friend of Narottama), a companion of the Lord: Narahari Chakravarti cites
another pada of his (PK 2186 = BR p. 919, chapter 1) as the testimony of an eyewitness.
[^07-60]: "Lord Gora" (gorā pahuṃ); ms. "kha", P-R-Sa: "crying 'Hari, Hari', the Lord dances".
[^07-61]: Kashishvara is a servant of the Lord (according to CC a disciple of Ishvara Puri, later in Puri); Abhirama Thakura
is a companion of Nityananda; Pandita Purushottama is a companion of the Lord (CC Adi 10–11 names several Purushottamas);
Narahari Dasa is Narahari Sarakara. The place (Navadvipa or Puri) cannot be determined with certainty from the list of
companions.
[^07-62]: The khol is the clay drum of kirtana, the karatalas are hand cymbals.

## 15. Vasu Ramananda — "aruṇa basane bidita bhubane…" (PK 2331)
*Nityananda's dance: in red garments, with a dancer's turban, He dances, looking around and crying "Hari, Hari"; His gait
is that of a mighty elephant, His anklet bells ring; in ecstasy He knows no directions and roars "Gaura!"; the devotees
roll on the ground gazing at His moon-face, and Vasu Ramananda weeps, clasping Nitai's feet. In PK it is the last pada of
the 22nd pallava (on Nityananda). The same raga (suhai).*[^07-63]

অরুণ বসনে বিদিত ভুবনে
শিরে নটপটি পাগিয়া ।
চৌদিগে হেরি হেরি বোলয়ে হরি হরি
নাচত কতহুঁ ভঙ্গিয়া ॥

*aruṇa basane bidita bhubane*
*śire naṭapaṭi pāgiyā |*
*caudige heri heri bolaye hari hari*
*nācata katahum̐ bhaṅgiyā ||*

*Word for word:* aruṇa basane — in red garments; bidita bhubane — renowned in the world; śire naṭapaṭi pāgiyā — with a dancer's gay turban on His head; caudige heri heri — looking around on every side; bolaye hari hari — cries "Hari, Hari"; nācata katahuṃ bhaṅgiyā — dances in all manner of ways

**15.1.** In red garments, renowned in the world,
with a dancer's turban on His head,
looking around on every side He cries "Hari, Hari!" —
and dances in all manner of ways.[^07-64]

নিতাইসুন্দর নাচে ।
অরুণ-নয়ানে ও চাঁদ-বদনে
কত বা মাধুরি আছে ॥

*nitāisundara nāce |*
*aruṇa-nayāne o cām̐da-badane*
*kata bā mādhuri āche ||*

*Word for word:* nitāisundara nāce — lovely Nitai dances; aruṇa-nayāne — in the reddish eyes; o cāṃda-badane — in that moon-face; kata vā mādhuri āche — how much sweetness there is

**15.2.** *(Refrain)* Lovely Nitai dances!
In those reddish eyes, in that moon-face —
how much sweetness there is![^07-65]

চলন সুন্দর মত্ত করিবর
নূপুর ঝনন কারিয়া ।
ভাবে অবশ নাহি দিগ পাশ
গৌর বলি হুঙ্কারিয়া ॥

*calana sundara matta karibara*
*nūpura jhanana kāriyā |*
*bhābe abaśa nāhi diga pāśa*
*gaura bali huṅkāriyā ||*

*Word for word:* calana sundara — lovely is the gait; matta karibara — [like] a mighty elephant's; nūpura jhanana kāriyā — making the anklets jingle; bhābe abaśa — overcome by bhava; nāhi diga pāśa — knowing no directions; gaura bali huṅkāriyā — roaring out "Gaura"

**15.3.** Lovely is His gait — like a mighty elephant's,
His anklet bells jingle.
Overcome by bhava, knowing no directions,
He roars out: "Gaura!"[^07-66]

যতেক ভকত ধরণী লুঠত
ও চাঁদ-বদন হেরিয়া ।
বসু রামানন্দে কাঁদে নিরানন্দে
নিতাই চরণ ধরিয়া ॥

*yateka bhakata dharaṇī luṭhata*
*o cām̐da-badana heriyā |*
*basu rāmānande kām̐de nirānande*
*nitāi caraṇa dhariyā ||*

*Word for word:* yateka bhakata — all the devotees; dharaṇī luṭhata — roll on the ground; o cāṃda-badana heriyā — gazing at that moon-face; basu rāmānande kāṃde — Vasu Ramananda weeps; nirānande — disconsolate; nitāi caraṇa dhariyā — clasping Nitai's feet

**15.4.** All the devotees roll on the ground
gazing at that moon-face.
And Vasu Ramananda weeps, disconsolate,
clasping the feet of Nitai.

[^07-63]: Signature: "Vasu Ramananda". PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 315 (printed p. 304), 4th shakha, 22nd pallava, no. 38 (mark
"॥৩৮॥২৩৩১॥"); "tathā rāga" (after the preceding pada — suhai); ms. P-R-Sa no. 2435. Not found in GPT1 or KGC. In Ray's
index of poets it stands among the padas of Vasu Ramananda. The red garments, turban and jingling ornaments recall the
description of Nityananda in Gauda after 1515 (CB Antya 5–6), but the pada names no place.
[^07-64]: A dancer's turban (naṭapaṭi pāga) — a gay turban, as worn by Krishna-Natavara. Mss. "ka", "ca": "Hari, Hari"
instead of "looking around" (heri heri).
[^07-65]: Ms. "gha": kata nā (the same meaning).
[^07-66]: According to Ray's apparatus, the lines "Lovely is His gait… jingle" were omitted by scribal error in mss. "ka",
"kha", "ca" and P-R-Sa.

## 16. Krishnadasa — "śarata-cānda jini gorā-mukha cānda…" (PK 1743)
*Separation in autumn: Gauranga, whose face surpasses the autumn moon, gazes at the autumn moon and weeps, remembering the
happiness of the autumn season, sobbing aloud; the heart breaks at the sight of His face, even a fool loses his
composure; all the dear companions weep. In PK it is the gaura-chandrika to "separation befitting autumn": "Shri
Mahaprabhu, overcome by that bhava" (8th pallava). Raga sindhura.*[^07-67]

শরত-চান্দ জিনি গোরা-মুখ চান্দ ।
শারদ-নিশাকর হেরি হেরি কান্দ ॥

*śarata-cānda jini gorā-mukha cānda |*
*śārada-niśākara heri heri kānda ||*

*Word for word:* śarata-cānda jini — surpassing the autumn moon; gorā-mukha cānda — the moon-face of Gora; śārada-niśākara — the autumn moon; heri heri kānda — gazing and gazing, weeps

**16.1.** The moon-face of Gora, surpassing the autumn moon,
gazes at the autumn moon — and weeps.[^07-68]

সময় শরদ সুখ সোঙরি সোঙরি ।
কান্দয়ে গৌরাঙ্গ পহুঁ ফুকরি ফুকরি ॥

*samaya śarada sukha soṅari soṅari |*
*kāndaye gaurāṅga pahum̐ phukari phukari ||*

*Word for word:* samaya śarada sukha — the happiness of the autumn season; soṅari soṅari — remembering again and again; kāndaye gaurāṅga pahuṃ — Lord Gauranga weeps; phukari phukari — sobbing aloud

**16.2.** Remembering again and again the happiness of autumn,
Lord Gauranga weeps, sobbing aloud.[^07-69]

বিদরিয়া যায় হিয়া সে মুখ দেখিতে ।
মূঢ় যেহো নারে সেহো ধৈরজ ধরিতে ॥

*bidariyā yāya hiyā se mukha dekhite |*
*mūṛha yeho nāre seho dhairaja dharite ||*

*Word for word:* bidariyā yāy hiyā — the heart breaks; se mukha dekhite — at the sight of that face; mūṛha yeho — even one who is a fool; nāre seho dhairaja dharite — even he cannot keep his composure

**16.3.** The heart breaks at the sight of that face;
even a fool cannot keep his composure.

কান্দিয়া আকুল যত প্রিয় অনুচর ।
কৃষ্ণদাস কহে মুঞি বড়ই পামর ॥

*kāndiyā ākula yata priya anucara |*
*kṛṣṇadāsa kahe muñi baṛai pāmara ||*

*Word for word:* kāndiyā ākula — weeping, distraught; yata priya anucara — all the dear companions; kṛṣṇadāsa kahe — Krishnadasa says; muñi baṛai pāmara — I am a great sinner

**16.4.** All the dear companions weep in distress.
Krishnadasa says: "I am a great sinner."

[^07-67]: Signature: "Krishnadasa". PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 92 (printed p. 81), 4th shakha, 8th pallava ("separation befitting
spring and the other seasons"), "atha śaratkālocita-birahaḥ. tadbhābākrāntaḥ śrīmahāprabhuḥ", no. 33 (mark
"॥৩৩॥১৭৪৩॥"); raga sindhura; ms. P-R-Sa no. 967. Not found in GPT1. Which Krishnadasa it is has not been established.
[^07-68]: Autumn is the time of the rasa ("the autumn nights", Bhag. 10.29.1). The Lord's weeping is separation in Radha's
mood — pure prema, not worldly longing (CC Antya 14–20).
[^07-69]: P-R-Sa: "the face of autumn" (mukha) instead of "happiness".

## 17. Ramananda — "dekha dekha jība gaurāṅgacām̐dera līlā…" (PK 2248)
*The sannyasi Lord: He who in a moment enchanted hundreds of thousands of gopis has exchanged His yellow garments for the
kaupina and the staff; leaving the happiness of the Kalindi's bank, He stands awesome on the seashore; in the Rama-avatara
He held the bow, in Gokula He played the flute, and now, out of compassion for souls, He has taken the sannyasi's staff;
the poet says: this is no sannyasi's garb, but the armour of a hero crushing godlessness. In PK it stands in the 21st
pallava (Gauranga's sannyasa). Raga varadi.*[^07-70]

দেখ দেখ জীব গৌরাঙ্গচাঁদের লীলা ।
লাখে লাখে গোপী নিমিখে ভুলায়্যা
কি লাগি সন্ন্যাসী হৈলা ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*dekha dekha jība gaurāṅgacām̐dera līlā |*
*lākhe lākhe gopī nimikhe bhulāyyā*
*ki lāgi sannyāsī hailā || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* dekha dekha jība — behold, behold, souls; gaurāṅgacām̐dera līlā — the lila of Gaurangachand; lākhe lākhe gopī — hundreds of thousands of gopis; nimikhe bhulāyyā — enchanting in a moment; ki lāgi sannyāsī hailā — why did He become a sannyasi

**17.1.** *(Refrain)* Behold, souls, the lila of Gaurangachand!
He who in the twinkling of an eye enchanted hundreds of thousands of gopis —
why has He become a sannyasi?[^07-71]

পীত বসন ছাড়ি ডোর কৌপীন পরি
বাকুয়া করিলা দণ্ড ।
কালিন্দীর তীরে সুখ পরিহরি
সিন্ধু-তীরে পরচণ্ড ॥

*pīta basana chāṛi ḍora kaupīna pari*
*bākuyā karilā daṇḍa |*
*kālindīra tīre sukha parihari*
*sindhu-tīre paracaṇḍa ||*

*Word for word:* pīta basana chāṛi — leaving the yellow garments; ḍora kaupīna pari — putting on the string and kaupina; bākuyā karilā daṇḍa — made the crooked (?) into a staff; kālindīra tīre — on the Kalindi's bank; sukha parihari — abandoning happiness; sindhu-tīre — on the seashore; paracaṇḍa — awesome

**17.2.** Leaving His yellow garments, putting on the string and kaupina,
the crooked He has made a straight staff.
Leaving the happiness of the Kalindi's bank,
awesome is He on the shore of the sea.[^07-72]

রাম-অবতারে ধনুক ধরিলা
গোকুলে পূরিলা বাঁশী ।
এবে জীব লাগি করুণা করিয়া
দণ্ড ধরিয়া সন্ন্যাসী ॥

*rāma-abatāre dhanuka dharilā*
*gokule pūrilā bām̐śī |*
*ebe jība lāgi karuṇā kariyā*
*daṇḍa dhariyā sannyāsī ||*

*Word for word:* rāma-abatāre — in the Rama-avatara; dhanuka dharilā — He held the bow; gokule pūrilā bām̐śī — in Gokula He filled the flute [with sound]; ebe jība lāgi — now for the sake of souls; karuṇā kariyā — out of compassion; daṇḍa dhariyā sannyāsī — taking the staff, [He is] a sannyasi

**17.3.** In the Rama-avatara He held the bow,
in Gokula He filled the flute with sound,
and now, out of compassion for souls,
taking the staff, He has become a sannyasi.[^07-73]

ধরি নব দণ্ড লইলা করঙ্গ
সিন্ধু-তীরে কৈলা থানা ।
রামানন্দে কয় সন্ন্যাসীর বেশ নয়
পাষণ্ড-দলন বীর-বানা ॥

*dhari naba daṇḍa lailā karaṅga*
*sindhu-tīre kailā thānā |*
*rāmānande kaya sannyāsīra beśa naya*
*pāṣaṇḍa-dalana bīra-bānā ||*

*Word for word:* dhari naba daṇḍa — taking a new staff; lailā karaṅga — He took a water-pot; sindhu-tīre kailā thānā — made His abode on the seashore; rāmānande kaya — says Ramananda; sannyāsīra beśa naya — it is not a sannyasi's garb; pāṣaṇḍa-dalana bīra-bānā — [but] the array of a hero crushing godlessness

**17.4.** Taking a new staff and a water-pot,
He has settled on the shore of the sea.
Says Ramananda: this is no sannyasi's garb —
it is the armour of a hero crushing godlessness.[^07-74]

[^07-70]: Signature: "Ramananda". PK: vol. 3, PDF pp. 285–286 (printed pp. 274–275), 4th shakha, 21st pallava (Gauranga's
sannyasa), no. 31 (mark "॥৩১॥২২৪৮॥"); raga varadi; ms. P-R-Sa no. 2353. GPT1 — p. 18, no. 49 (raga varadi); GPT2 — sect.
1.2, no. 49. In the catalogue (RM-001) this pada was confused with the preceding PK 2247 ("goloka chāṛiyā pahu kene vā
abanī"): that one is signed in PK "Govinda Dasa", in GPT "Nayanananda", and Ramananda is only mentioned in it ("Raya
Ramananda weeps"). The attribution of PK 2248 to Vasu Ramananda is not proven (the signature is only "Ramananda"); by its
content the pada was written after the sannyasa, about the Lord in Puri.
[^07-71]: The gopis are Krishna's friends in Vraja; their prema is pure, without a trace of the mundane — the highest love of
God.
[^07-72]: "The crooked" (bākuyā) — the reading is unclear; probably "crooked" (bām̐kuyā): Krishna, who stood "bent in three
places" (tribhanga) with the flute, now holds the straight staff of a sannyasi. The Kalindi is the Yamuna. "Awesome"
(paracaṇḍa = pracaṇḍa).
[^07-73]: Mss. "ka", "kha", "ca", P-R-Sa: "holding the bow" (dhariyā).
[^07-74]: The staff (danda) and the water-pot (karaṅga, kamandalu) are the sannyasi's belongings; mss. "ka", "kha", P-R-Sa:
"taking along" (laiyā saṅge) instead of "taking a water-pot". "The armour of a hero" (bīra-bānā — a warrior's array): the
Lord's sannyasa is a weapon against godlessness; cf. note 8.

## 18. Paramananda — "śrīnityānanda caitanya hare…" (PK 2971)
*A nama-kirtana in Vrajabuli: the Son of Shachi, descended in Nadia, first of all spread the holy name; He dances in
kirtana, Gadadhara at His left; tears of prema wash away the darkness of Kali; He embraces all without distinction;
living in Nilachala, He beholds the Lord of the Yadus (Jagannatha); He goes from house to house for the sake of the
fallen, offering prema. In PK it is unsigned, in the 34th pallava (nama-sankirtana); in GPT the last line carries
Paramananda's signature. Ragini "kau", tala madhyaman (according to ms. "gha").*[^07-75]

শ্রীনিত্যানন্দ চৈতন্য হরে ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*śrīnityānanda caitanya hare || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* śrīnityānanda caitanya hare — Sri Nityananda, Chaitanya, Hari

**18.1.** *(Refrain)* Sri Nityananda, Chaitanya, Hari!

শচি-নন্দন নদিয়া অবতারি
উজ্জ্বল-বরণ গৌর-রূপ-ধারি
আগে নাম জগতে পরচারি
সকরুণ ঐছে পতিত-জন-তারি—কোহে ।

*śaci-nandana nadiyā abatāri*
*ujjvala-baraṇa gaura-rūpa-dhāri*
*āge nāma jagate paracāri*
*sakaruṇa aiche patita-jana-tāri—kohe |*

*Word for word:* śaci-nandana — the Son of Shachi; nadiyā abatāri — descended in Nadia; ujjvala-baraṇa — of radiant hue; gaura-rūpa-dhāri — bearing the form of Gaura; āge nāma jagate paracāri — first spreading the name in the world; sakaruṇa aiche — so compassionately; patita-jana-tāri — saving the fallen; kohe — who [else]?

**18.2.** The Son of Shachi, descended in Nadia,
having taken the form of Gaura of radiant hue,
first of all spread the holy name in the world —
who else so compassionately saves the fallen?[^07-76]

সংকীর্ত্তন-রস-নৃত্য-বিহারি
অবিরল-পুলক ভকত-হিত-কারি
হাসত নাচত গাওত ভোরি
ত্রিভুবন-জন বোলত বলিহারি—মোহে ॥

*saṃkīrttana-rasa-nṛtya-bihāri*
*abirala-pulaka bhakata-hita-kāri*
*hāsata nācata gāota bhori*
*tribhubana-jana bolata balihāri—mohe ||*

*Word for word:* saṅkīrttana-rasa-nṛtya-bihāri — delighting in dance in the taste of sankirtana; abirala-pulaka — with unbroken pulaka; bhakata-hita-kāri — the benefactor of the devotees; hāsata nācata gāota bhori — laughs, dances, sings, enraptured; tribhubana-jana bolata balihāri — the people of the three worlds cry "Glory!"; mohe — He enchants

**18.3.** He who delights in dance in the taste of sankirtana,
all thrilled with unbroken pulaka, the benefactor of the devotees,
laughs, dances and sings, enraptured —
the people of the three worlds cry "Glory!" — so He enchants.[^07-77]

ভাবে বিবশ ভই হোত ত্রিভঙ্গী
বামে গদাধর রাজত রঙ্গী
চৌদিশ উপনিত শোভিত সঙ্গী
শচি-নন্দন বৃন্দাবন-রঙ্গী—শোহে ।

*bhābe bibaśa bhai hota tribhaṅgī*
*bāme gadādhara rājata raṅgī*
*caudiśa upanita śobhita saṅgī*
*śaci-nandana bṛndābana-raṅgī—śohe |*

*Word for word:* bhābe bibaśa bhai — overcome by bhava; hota tribhaṅgī — stands in the tribhanga pose; bāme gadādhara rājata raṅgī — at the left shines the joyful Gadadhara; caudiśa upanita — gathered on all sides; śobhita saṅgī — the shining companions; śaci-nandana bṛndābana-raṅgī — the Son of Shachi, who delights in Vrindavana; sohe — shines

**18.4.** Overcome by bhava, He stands in the tribhanga pose;
at His left shines the joyful Gadadhara;
on all sides the companions have gathered and shine —
so glows the Son of Shachi, who delights in Vrindavana.[^07-78]

অবিরত নয়নে বহত প্রেম-ধারা
সীঁচত মোছত কলি-অন্ধিয়ারা
করত আলিঙ্গন নাহি বিচারা
নিরুপম গুণ বপু-ভাব অপারা—হো হে ॥

*abirata nayane bahata prema-dhārā*
*sīm̐cata mochata kali-andhiyārā*
*karata āliṅgana nāhi bicārā*
*nirupama guṇa bapu-bhāba apārā—ho he ||*

*Word for word:* abirata nayane — unceasingly from the eyes; bahata prema-dhārā — flow streams of prema; sīṃcata — sprinkling; mochata kali-andhiyārā — wash away the darkness of Kali; karata āliṅgana — He embraces; nāhi bicārā — without distinction; nirupama guṇa bapu-bhāba apārā — peerless qualities, form and bhava, boundless; ho he — oh!

**18.5.** Unceasingly streams of prema flow from His eyes;
sprinkling, they wash away the darkness of Kali.
He embraces all without distinction —
peerless are His qualities, form and bhava, boundless![^07-79]

নীলাচলে বসত শচিনন্দন
দরশন করত দেব যদুনন্দন
অঙ্গে বিলেপিত শোভিত চন্দন
রূপক সবহিঁ করত অভিনন্দন—জোহে ।

*nīlācale basata śacinandana*
*daraśana karata deba yadunandana*
*aṅge bilepita śobhita candana*
*rūpaka sabahim̐ karata abhinandana—johe |*

*Word for word:* nīlācale basata — in Nilachala dwells; śacinandana — the Son of Shachi; daraśana karata — beholds; deba yadunandana — God, the Lord of the Yadus (Jagannatha); aṅge bilepita — anointed on the body; śobhita candana — radiant sandal paste; rūpaka sabahim̐ karata abhinandana — all hail His form with delight; johe — [He who]

**18.6.** In Nilachala dwells the Son of Shachi
and beholds God, the Lord of the Yadus;
His body anointed with radiant sandal paste —
His whole form calls forth delight.[^07-80]

মধুর মধুর হরি-নাম বোলত
পতিতনকে লিয়ে ঘরে ঘরে ডোলত
করুণাময় প্রভু প্রেমহি যাচত
জগ-জনকে ভয় দূরহি ভাজত—ভো হে ॥

*madhura madhura hari-nāma bolata*
*patitanake liye ghare ghare ḍolata*
*karuṇāmaya prabhu premahi yācata*
*jaga-janake bhaya dūrahi bhājata—bho he ||*

*Word for word:* madhura madhura hari-nāma bolata — sweetly, sweetly utters the name of Hari; patitanake liye — for the sake of the fallen; ghare ghare ḍolata — goes from house to house; karuṇāmaya prabhu — the merciful Lord; premahi yācata — Himself offers prema; jaga-janake bhaya — the fear of the world's people; dūrahi bhājata — drives far away; bho he — oh!

**18.7.** Sweetly, sweetly He utters the name of Hari,
for the fallen He goes from house to house;
the merciful Lord Himself offers prema —
the fear of the world's people He drives away.[^07-81]

[^07-75]: PK: vol. 4, PDF pp. 221–222 (printed pp. 212–213), 4th shakha, 34th pallava (nama-sankirtana), no. 14 (mark
"॥১৪॥২৯৭১॥"); "rāgiṇī kau — tāla madhyamāna" (according to Ray, this heading is only in ms. "gha"). In PK there is no
signature: the last line is "jaga-janake bhaya dūrahi bhājata" ("He drives away the fear of the world's people"). GPT1 —
p. 403, no. 5 (raga dhanashi; the section on Puri), where the same line reads "paramānandaka bhaya dūrahi bhāgata" ("He
drives away Paramananda's fear") — Paramananda's signature; the catalogue's attribution (PA-007) rests on it. The
catalogue connected Paramananda with PK 2966 and 2974: PK 2966 is a pada of Gopala Dasa on Radha and Krishna; PK 2974
("hare hare govinda hare") does bear Paramananda's signature, but it is a nama-kirtana to Krishna without gaura-lila (not
translated). Majumdar ascribes Paramananda's Vrajabuli padas to Paramananda of Vrindavana, a follower of Rupa, not to
Paramananda Gupta; authority C.
[^07-76]: The last words of the stanzas (kohe, mohe, sohe…) are Hindi exclamatory endings ("who?", "enchants", "shines"),
usual in Vrajabuli nama-kirtanas.
[^07-77]: "Glory!" (balihāri) — literally "I give myself for Him".
[^07-78]: Tribhanga is the "thrice-bent" pose of Krishna with the flute; "who delights in Vrindavana" (bṛndābana-raṅgī) is
Krishna. Ms. "gha": another reading instead of "gathered" (ota nita).
[^07-79]: Ms. "gha": "tears of prema flow" (bahata premajala); "ka", "kha", "ca": siṃcata (the same, "sprinkling"); "ka":
mohata, "kha": mocata ("wash away"); "ka", "kha": kara (the same, "embraces").
[^07-80]: The Lord of the Yadus (yadunandana) is Jagannatha. GPT1: "beholds every day".
[^07-81]: "Himself offers prema" (premahi yācata) — He gives it without waiting to be asked. Ms. "ka": "fallen people"
(patitaloka); "ka", "kha": līye (the same, "for the sake of").

## 19. Krishnadasa — "ākula dekhiyā tāre kahe gaura dhīre dhīre…" (PK 2359)
*The continuation of PK 2358 (chapter 1, no. 24). Seeing Gauridasa distraught, the Lord softly says: "We have stayed with
you"; He comes to the Pandita with two Deities, and four stand before Gauridasa — the Lord, Nityananda and Their Deities;
the Lord bids him keep whichever two he wishes and promises, for the sake of his faith, to eat at his house, asking for
food; Gauridasa cooks, and all four partake; having thus turned his heart, the Lord left Both with him in Their Deities,
while the two brothers Themselves went to Nilachala. In PK it stands in the section on Gauridasa Pandita (24th pallava,
"the character of Gaura's devotees"). The same raga (bhatiyari).*[^07-82]

আকুল দেখিয়া তারে কহে গৌর ধীরে ধীরে
আমরা থাকিলাম তোর ঠাঞি ।
নিশ্চয় জানিহ তুমি তোমার এ ঘরে আমি
রহিলাম এই দুই ভাই ॥

*ākula dekhiyā tāre kahe gaura dhīre dhīre*
*āmarā thākilāma tora ṭhāñi |*
*niścaya jāniha tumi tomāra e ghare āmi*
*rahilāma ei dui bhāi ||*

*Word for word:* ākula dekhiyā tāre — seeing him distraught; kahe gaura dhīre dhīre — Gaura says softly, softly; āmarā thākilāma tora ṭhāñi — We have stayed with you; niścaya jāniha tumi — know it for certain; tomāra e ghare āmi — in this house of yours We; rahilāma ei dui bhāi — have stayed, these two brothers

**19.1.** Seeing him distraught, Gaura says softly, softly:
"We have stayed with you.
Know it for certain: in this house of yours
We have stayed, the two brothers."[^07-83]

এতেক প্রবোধ দিয়া দুই প্রতিমূর্ত্তি লৈয়া
আইল পণ্ডিত বিদ্যমান ।
চারি জনে দাঁড়াইল পণ্ডিত বিস্ময় ভেল
ভাবে অশ্রু বহয়ে নয়ান ॥

*eteka prabodha diyā dui pratimūrtti laiyā*
*āila paṇḍita bidyamāna |*
*cāri jane dām̐ṛāila paṇḍita bismaya bhela*
*bhābe aśru bahaye nayāna ||*

*Word for word:* eteka prabodha diyā — having consoled him thus; dui pratimūrtti laiyā — taking two Deities (pratimurti); āila paṇḍita bidyamāna — came before the Pandita; cāri jane dāṃṛāila — four stood there; paṇḍita bismaya bhela — the Pandita was amazed; bhābe aśru bahaye nayāna — tears of bhava flow from his eyes

**19.2.** Having consoled him thus, taking two Deities,
the Lord appeared before the Pandita.
Four stood there side by side — the Pandita was amazed,
tears of bhava flow from his eyes.[^07-84]

পুন প্রভু কহে তারে তোর ইচ্ছা হয় যারে
সেই দুই রাখ নিজ ঘরে ।
তোমার প্রতীত লাগি তোর ঠাঞি খাব মাগি
সত্য সত্য জানিহ অন্তরে ॥

*puna prabhu kahe tāre tora icchā haya yāre*
*sei dui rākha nija ghare |*
*tomāra pratīta lāgi tora ṭhāñi khāba māgi*
*satya satya jāniha antare ||*

*Word for word:* puna prabhu kahe tāre — again the Lord says to him; tora icchā haya yāre — whichever you wish; sei dui rākha nija ghare — keep those two in your house; tomāra pratīta lāgi — for the sake of your faith; tora ṭhāñi khāba māgi — I will eat at your house, asking; satya satya jāniha antare — know in your heart: true, true

**19.3.** Again the Lord says to him: "Whichever you wish,
those two keep in your house.
For the sake of your faith I will eat at your house, asking for food —
know it in your heart: it is true, true."

শুনিয়া পণ্ডিত-রাজ করিলা রন্ধন-কাজ
চারি জনে ভোজন করিলা ।
পুষ্প-মাল্য বস্ত্র দিয়া তাম্বূলাদি সমর্পিয়া
সর্ব্ব অঙ্গে চন্দন লেপিলা ॥

*śuniyā paṇḍita-rāja karilā randhana-kāja*
*cāri jane bhojana karilā |*
*puṣpa-mālya bastra diyā tāmbūlādi samarpiyā*
*sarvva aṅge candana lepilā ||*

*Word for word:* śuniyā paṇḍita-rāja — hearing this, the king of panditas; karilā randhana-kāja — set about cooking; cāri jane bhojana karilā — the four partook of the meal; puṣpa-mālya bastra diyā — giving flower garlands and clothes; tāmbūlādi samarpiyā — offering betel and the rest; sarvva aṅge candana lepilā — anointed the whole body with sandal

**19.4.** Hearing this, the king of panditas set about cooking —
and the four partook of the meal.
Offering flower garlands and clothes, presenting betel and the rest,
he anointed Their whole bodies with sandal paste.

নানা মতে পরতীত করায়্যা ফিরাল্যা চিত
দোঁহারে রাখিল নিজ ঘরে ।
পণ্ডিতের প্রেম লাগি দুই ভাই খায় মাগি
দোঁহে গেলা নীলাচল-পুরে ॥

*nānā mate paratīta karāyyā phirālyā cita*
*dom̐hāre rākhila nija ghare |*
*paṇḍitera prema lāgi dui bhāi khāya māgi*
*dom̐he gelā nīlācala-pure ||*

*Word for word:* nānā mate — in every way; paratīta karāyyā — instilling faith; phirālyā cita — turning his heart; doṃhāre rākhila nija ghare — kept Both in his house; paṇḍitera prema lāgi — for the Pandita's love; dui bhāi khāy māgi — the two brothers eat, asking; doṃhe gelā nīlācala-pure — Both went to the city of Nilachala

**19.5.** Having strengthened his faith in every way and turned his heart,
the Lord left Both in his house.
For the Pandita's love the two brothers eat there, asking for food —
while They Themselves went to the city of Nilachala.[^07-85]

পণ্ডিত করয়ে সেবা যখন যে ইচ্ছা যেবা
সেই মত করয়ে বিলাস ।
হেন প্রভু গৌরীদাস তার পদ করি আশ
কহে দীন হীন কৃষ্ণদাস ॥

*paṇḍita karaye sebā yakhana ye icchā yebā*
*sei mata karaye bilāsa |*
*hena prabhu gaurīdāsa tāra pada kari āśa*
*kahe dīna hīna kṛṣṇadāsa ||*

*Word for word:* paṇḍita karaye sebā — the Pandita serves; yakhana ye icchā yebā — whenever They wish for whatever; sei mata karaye bilāsa — so They sport; hena prabhu gaurīdāsa — such is the master Gauridasa; tāra pada kari āśa — hoping for his feet; kahe dīna hīna kṛṣṇadāsa — says the humble, lowly Krishnadasa

**19.6.** The Pandita serves Them: whenever They wish for whatever,
so They sport.
Such is my master Gauridasa; hoping for his feet,
says the humble, lowly Krishnadasa.[^07-86]

[^07-82]: Signature: "Krishnadasa". PK: vol. 3, PDF pp. 324–325 (printed pp. 313–314), 4th shakha, 24th pallava, no. 7
(mark "॥৭॥২৩৫৯॥"); "tathā rāga" (after PK 2358 — bhatiyari); ms. P-R-Sa no. 2463. GPT1 — p. 406, no. 15 (raga kamoda;
right after PK 2358 = GPT1 no. 14); GPT2 — sect. 5.5, no. 15 (in the catalogue GD-003, wrongly ascribed to Gauridasa and
to PK 2360). The first line in the catalogue (KR-011, "nityānandacāṃda…") is the end of PK 2357. According to Majumdar,
Krishnadasa is Gauridasa's younger brother; he dates PK 2358 to the Lord's lifetime, and this pada directly continues it.
Cf. Murari 4.14.12–17.
[^07-83]: Ms. "kha": "seeing" (dekhite); "ka": "with you" (tomāra); GPT1: "We have stayed, the two brothers, as captives"
(bandī).
[^07-84]: The four are the Lord, Nityananda and Their two Deities (so also GPT1's note). Ms. "ka": "murti, murti" (mūrtti
mūrtti). The Deity is not a statue but the Lord Himself, manifesting Himself out of love for His devotee: the Lord shows
Gauridasa that He and His Deity are one.
[^07-85]: Ms. "ka", P-R-Sa: "then" (sei) instead of "whenever". "Asking for food" (khāy māgi) — the Lord Himself asks
Gauridasa for food, reciprocating his love.
[^07-86]: "Master" (prabhu) is Gauridasa, the poet's elder brother and, it seems, his teacher.

## 20. Krishnadasa — "dekha dui bhāi gaura nitāi…" (PK 1576)
*The abhisheka of Gaura and Nitai in Gauridasa's house: the two brothers sit on the altar as if the moon and the sun had
come down from the sky; Thakura Pandita with his people pours scented water over Them to the sound of conches, bells,
gongs, flutes, vinas, khols and karatalas; having bathed and dressed Them, he seats Them on a throne, performs puja,
feeds Them, offers betel and sandal, puts on garlands and performs arati. In PK the pada concludes a series of padas,
in the section on the abhisheka (31st pallava), about the festival at Gauridasa's: in the two preceding ones (signed
"Svarupa") the Lord and Nityananda promise Gauridasa in a dream to come and stay in his temple, he prepares the
festival, and They come. Raga varadi.*[^07-87]

দেখ দুই ভাই গৌর নিতাই
বসিলা বেদীর পরে ।
গগন তেজিয়া আসিলা নামিয়া
যেন শশি-দিবাকরে ॥

*dekha dui bhāi gaura nitāi*
*basilā bedīra pare |*
*gagana tejiyā āsilā nāmiyā*
*yena śaśi-dibākare ||*

*Word for word:* dekha dui bhāi — behold the two brothers; gaura nitāi — Gaura and Nitai; basilā bedīra pare — sit upon the altar; gagana tejiyā — leaving the sky; āsilā nāmiyā — have come down; yena śaśi-dibākare — like the moon and the sun

**20.1.** Behold: the two brothers, Gaura and Nitai,
sit upon the altar,
as if the moon and the sun, leaving the sky,
had come down to the earth.[^07-88]

হেরি হরষিত ঠাকুর পণ্ডিত
নিজগণ লৈয়া সাথে ।
জল সুবাসিত ঘট ভরি কত
ঢালয়ে দোঁহার মাথে ॥

*heri haraṣita ṭhākura paṇḍita*
*nijagaṇa laiyā sāthe |*
*jala subāsita ghaṭa bhari kata*
*ḍhālaye dom̐hāra māthe ||*

*Word for word:* heri haraṣita — seeing it, rejoices; ṭhākura paṇḍita — Thakura Pandita (Gauridasa); nijagaṇa laiyā sāthe — taking his people along; jala subāsita — scented water; ghaṭa bhari kata — filling many pots; ḍhālaye doṃhāra māthe — pours it over the heads of Both

**20.2.** Seeing it, Thakura Pandita rejoices;
taking his people along,
filling many pots with scented water,
he pours it over the heads of Both.

শঙ্খ ঘণ্টা কাঁসী বেণু বীণা বাঁশী
খোল করতাল বায় ।
জয় জয় বোল হরি হরি রোল
চৌদিগে ভকত গায় ॥

*śaṅkha ghaṇṭā kām̐sī beṇu bīṇā bām̐śī*
*khola karatāla bāya |*
*jaya jaya bola hari hari rola*
*caudige bhakata gāya ||*

*Word for word:* śaṅkha ghaṇṭā kāṃsī — conches, bells, gongs; beṇu bīṇā bām̐śī — flutes, vinas, pipes; khola karatāla bāy — khols and karatalas sound; jaya jaya bola — cries of "Jaya, jaya"; hari hari rola — shouts of "Hari, Hari"; caudige bhakata gāy — on all sides the devotees sing

**20.3.** Conches, bells, gongs, flutes, vinas, pipes,
khols and karatalas sound;
cries of "Jaya, jaya!", shouts of "Hari, Hari!" —
on all sides the devotees sing.[^07-89]

সিনান করায়্যা বসন পরায়্যা
বসাইলা সিংহাসনে ।
ধূপ দীপ জ্বালি লৈয়া অর্ঘ্যথালী
পূজা কৈলা দুই জনে ॥

*sināna karāyyā basana parāyyā*
*basāilā siṃhāsane |*
*dhūpa dīpa jvāli laiyā arghyathālī*
*pūjā kailā dui jane ||*

*Word for word:* sinān karāyyā — having bathed [Them]; basana parāyyā — having dressed [Them]; basāilā siṃhāsane — seated [Them] on the throne; dhūpa dīpa jvāli — lighting incense and lamps; laiyā arghya-thālī — taking a plate of arghya; pūjā kailā dui jane — worshipped the two

**20.4.** Having bathed and dressed Them,
he seated Them on the throne.
Lighting incense and lamps, taking a plate of arghya,
he performed the puja of Both.[^07-90]

উপহারগণ করায়্যা ভোজন
তাম্বুল চন্দন শেষে ।
ফুল-হার দিয়া আরাত্রি করিয়া
প্রণমিল কৃষ্ণদাসে ॥

*upahāragaṇa karāyyā bhojana*
*tāmbula candana śeṣe |*
*phula-hāra diyā ārātri kariyā*
*praṇamila kṛṣṇadāse ||*

*Word for word:* upahāragaṇa — with all the offerings; karāyyā bhojana — having fed [Them]; tāmbula candana śeṣe — at the end, betel and sandal; phula-hāra diyā — putting on flower garlands; ārātri kariyā — performing arati; praṇamila kṛṣṇadāse — Krishnadasa bowed down

**20.5.** Having fed Them with all kinds of offerings,
at the end — betel and sandal;
putting on flower garlands and performing arati,
Krishnadasa bowed down [before Them].

[^07-87]: Signature: "Krishnadasa". PK: vol. 2, PDF p. 467 (printed p. 454), 3rd shakha, 31st pallava, no. 8 (mark
"॥৮॥১৫৭৬॥"); raga varadi; ms. P-R-Sa no. 2146. GPT1 — p. 241, no. 12 (raga varadi); GPT2 — sect. 4.1, no. 12. The pada
belongs to the same story as PK 2358–2360 (here nos. 19, 21), but PK places it in the section on the abhisheka. Which
Krishnadasa it is, is not stated; by the theme, probably Gauridasa's younger brother.
[^07-88]: Mss. "ka", "kha", "gha", "ca": nāmilā āsiyā (the same, "came down"); "ka", "kha": "night and the sun" (niśā)
instead of "the moon".
[^07-89]: P-R-Sa: bāje (the same, "sound"), gāhe (the same, "sing").
[^07-90]: Arghya is a respectful offering of water with flowers and rice. P-R-Sa: arghyathālī (the same).

## 21. Krishnadasa — "śrībṛndābana nāma ratna-cintāmaṇi-dhāma…" (PK 2360)
*Praise of Gauridasa: in Vrindavana, the abode of chintamani jewels, beside Krishna and Balarama, was Subala-chandra —
now he has become Gauridasa and lives in Ambika; Nitai and Chaitanya accepted his service, and all four partook of his
food; as Subala once subdued Rama and Kanu, so now this has become manifest; knowing nothing but Nitai and Chaitanya, he
kept the two brothers Themselves in his house. In PK it is the next pada of the same section. The same raga
(bhatiyari).*[^07-91]

শ্রীবৃন্দাবন নাম রত্ন-চিন্তামণি-ধাম
তাহে কৃষ্ণ বলরাম পাশ ।
সুবলচন্দ্র নাম ছিল এবে গৌরীদাস হৈল
অম্বিকা নগরে যার বাস ॥

*śrībṛndābana nāma ratna-cintāmaṇi-dhāma*
*tāhe kṛṣṇa balarāma pāśa |*
*subalacandra nāma chila ebe gaurīdāsa haila*
*ambikā nagare yāra bāsa ||*

*Word for word:* śrībṛndābana nāma — [the place] named Sri Vrindavana; ratna-cintāmaṇi-dhāma — the abode of chintamani jewels; tāhe kṛṣṇa balarāma pāśa — there beside Krishna and Balarama; subalacandra nāma chila — he was named Subala-chandra; ebe gaurīdāsa haila — now he has become Gauridasa; ambikā nagare yāra bāsa — who lives in the city of Ambika

**21.1.** There is Sri Vrindavana, the abode of chintamani jewels;
there, beside Krishna and Balarama,
was he, named Subala-chandra — now he has become Gauridasa
and lives in the city of Ambika.[^07-92]

নিতাই চৈতন্য যার সেবা কৈল অঙ্গীকার
চারি মূর্ত্তি ভোজন করিল ।
পুরবে সুবল জনু বশ কৈল রাম কানু
পরতেক এখন রহিল ॥

*nitāi caitanya yāra sebā kaila aṅgīkāra*
*cāri mūrtti bhojana karila |*
*purabe subala janu baśa kaila rāma kānu*
*parateka ekhana rahila ||*

*Word for word:* nitāi caitanya yāra — Nitai and Chaitanya, whose; sebā kaila aṅgīkāra — accepted the service; cāri mūrtti bhojana karila — four murtis (the Lord, Nityananda and Their Deities) partook; purabe subala janu — as formerly Subala; baśa kaila rāma kānu — subdued Rama and Kanu; parateka ekhana rahila — so now it has become manifest

**21.2.** Nitai and Chaitanya accepted his service —
four murtis partook of his food.
As Subala once subdued Rama and Kanu,
so now it has become manifest.[^07-93]

নিতাই চৈতন্য বিনে আর কিছু নাহি জানে
কে কহিবে প্রেমের বড়াই ।
সাক্ষাতে রাখিল ঘরে হেন কে করিতে পারে
নিতাই চৈতন্য দুই ভাই ॥

*nitāi caitanya bine āra kichu nāhi jāne*
*ke kahibe premera baṛāi |*
*sākṣāte rākhila ghare hena ke karite pāre*
*nitāi caitanya dui bhāi ||*

*Word for word:* nitāi caitanya bine — apart from Nitai and Chaitanya; āra kichu nāhi jāne — he knows nothing else; ke kahibe premera baṛāi — who can tell the greatness of [his] prema; sākṣāte rākhila ghare — he kept in his house in person; hena ke karite pāre — who else could do so; nitāi caitanya dui bhāi — Nitai and Chaitanya, the two brothers

**21.3.** Nothing but Nitai and Chaitanya does he know —
who can tell the greatness of his prema?
He kept in his house before his very eyes —
who else could do so? — Nitai and Chaitanya, the two brothers.

প্রেমে লম্ফ ঝম্প যার পুলকিত হুহুঙ্কার
খেণেকে রোদন খেণে হাস ।
তাঁর পাদ পদ্ম রেণু ভূষণ করিয়া তনু
কহে দীনহীন কৃষ্ণদাস ॥

*preme lampha jhampa yāra pulakita huhuṅkāra*
*kheṇeke rodana kheṇe hāsa |*
*tām̐ra pāda padma reṇu bhūṣaṇa kariyā tanu*
*kahe dīnahīna kṛṣṇadāsa ||*

*Word for word:* preme lampha jhampa yāra — he who in prema leaps and bounds; pulakita huhuṅkāra — thrilled, roaring; khaṇeke rodana khaṇe hāsa — now weeping, now laughing; tāṃra pāda padma reṇu — the dust of his lotus feet; bhūṣaṇa kariyā tanu — making it the body's adornment; kahe dīnahīna kṛṣṇadāsa — says the humble, lowly Krishnadasa

**21.4.** In prema he leaps and bounds, thrilled all over, he roars,
now he weeps, now he laughs.
Adorning his body with the dust of his lotus feet,
says the humble, lowly Krishnadasa.

[^07-91]: Signature: "Krishnadasa". PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 325 (printed p. 314), 24th pallava, no. 8 (mark "॥৮॥২৩৬০॥"); "tathā
rāga"; ms. P-R-Sa no. 2464. GPT1 — p. 458, no. 19 (raga bhatiyari; the section on the companions); GPT2 — sect. 6.3. After
the pada a section on Rupa and Sanatana begins in PK.
[^07-92]: Subala is a cowherd friend of Krishna in Vraja; according to the *Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika* (128), Gauridasa is
Subala. In P-R-Sa "named" and "abode" are interchanged. Chintamani is the wish-fulfilling jewel: according to the
scriptures, Vrindavana is made of them.
[^07-93]: The four murtis are the Lord and Nityananda and Their Deities (cf. no. 19); ms. "ka": "forms" (mūrtte). Rama
and Kanu are Balarama and Krishna.

## 22. Krishnadasa — "nitāi caitanya doṃhe baṛa abatāra…" (PK 2991)
*A prayer of repentance: Nitai and Chaitanya are the greatest avataras, none will be more generous than They; They
delivered mlecchas, chandalas and blasphemers; yet the poet has gained nothing — he did not worship Their feet, he himself
put poison into his mouth; the whole world drowned in the prema of the gaura-kirtana, but not a drop touched him. In PK
it stands in the 36th pallava (prayers). Raga shri.*[^07-94]

নিতাই চৈতন্য দোঁহে বড় অবতার ।
এমন দয়াল দাতা না হইবে আর ॥

*nitāi caitanya dom̐he baṛa abatāra |*
*emana dayāla dātā nā haibe āra ||*

*Word for word:* nitāi caitanya doṃhe — Nitai and Chaitanya, both; baṛa abatāra — are great avataras; emana dayāla dātā — such merciful givers; nā haibe āra — there will never be again

**22.1.** Nitai and Chaitanya — Both are great avataras;
such merciful givers there will never be again.[^07-95]

ম্লেচ্ছ চণ্ডাল নিন্দুক পাষণ্ডাদি যত ।
করুণায় উদ্ধার করিলা কত কত ॥

*mleccha caṇḍāla ninduka pāṣaṇḍādi yata |*
*karuṇāya uddhāra karilā kata kata ||*

*Word for word:* mleccha caṇḍāla — mlecchas, chandalas; ninduka pāṣaṇḍādi yata — blasphemers, the godless and all the rest; karuṇāya uddhāra karilā — delivered by Their mercy; kata kata — so very many

**22.2.** Mlecchas, chandalas, blasphemers, the godless —
how many of them They delivered by Their mercy![^07-96]

হেন অবতারে মোর কিছুই না হৈল ।
হায় রে দারুণ প্রাণ কি সুখে রহিল ॥

*hena abatāre mora kichui nā haila |*
*hāya re dāruṇa prāṇa ki sukhe rahila ||*

*Word for word:* hena abatāre — in such an avatara; mora kichui nā haila — nothing at all came to me; hāy re — alas; dāruṇa prāṇa — cruel life; ki sukhe rahila — in what contentment you remain

**22.3.** In such an avatara nothing at all fell to my lot —
alas, cruel life, in what contentment you abide!

যত যত অবতার হইল ভুবনে ।
হেন অবতার ভাই না হয় কখনে ॥

*yata yata abatāra haila bhubane |*
*hena abatāra bhāi nā haya kakhane ||*

*Word for word:* yata yata abatāra — however many avataras; haila bhubane — came into the world; hena abatāra — such an avatara; bhāi — brother; nā haya kakhane — never comes

**22.4.** However many avataras have come into the world —
one like this, brother, never comes.

হেন প্রভুর পদ-দ্বন্দ্ব না করি ভজন ।
হাতে তুলি মুখে বিষ করিলুঁ ভক্ষণ ॥

*hena prabhura pada-dvandva nā kari bhajana |*
*hāte tuli mukhe biṣa karilum̐ bhakṣaṇa ||*

*Word for word:* hena prabhura pada-dvandva — the two feet of such a Lord; nā kari bhajana — not worshipping; hāte tuli — lifting with my hand; mukhe biṣa — poison to my mouth; kariluṃ bhakṣaṇa — I ate

**22.5.** Not worshipping the two feet of such a Lord,
with my own hand I raised poison to my mouth and ate it.[^07-97]

গৌর-কীর্ত্তনে প্রেমে জগত ডুবিল ।
হায় রে অভাগার বিন্দু পরশ নহিল ॥

*gaura-kīrttane preme jagata ḍubila |*
*hāya re abhāgāra bindu paraśa nahila ||*

*Word for word:* gaura-kīrttane — in the gaura-kirtana; preme jagata ḍubila — the world drowned in prema; hāy re — alas; abhāgāra — the unfortunate one; bindu paraśa nahila — not a drop touched

**22.6.** The world drowned in the prema of the gaura-kirtana —
alas, not a drop has touched the unfortunate one.

কান্দে কৃষ্ণদাস কেশ ছিঁড়ি নিজ-করে ।
ধিক্ ধিক্ অভাগিয়া কেনে নাহি মরে ॥

*kānde kṛṣṇadāsa keśa chim̐ṛi nija-kare |*
*dhik dhik abhāgiyā kene nāhi mare ||*

*Word for word:* kānde kṛṣṇadāsa — Krishnadasa weeps; keśa chiṃṛi nija-kare — tearing his hair with his own hand; dhik dhik — shame, shame; abhāgiyā — the unfortunate one; kene nāhi mare — why does he not die

**22.7.** Krishnadasa weeps, tearing his hair:
"Shame, shame! Why does the unfortunate one not die?"

[^07-94]: Signature: "Krishnadasa". PK: vol. 4, PDF p. 228 (printed p. 219), 36th pallava (prarthana), no. 7 (mark
"॥৭॥২৯৯১॥"); raga shri; ms. P-R-Sa no. 2500. GPT1 — p. 14, no. 34 (raga shri); GPT2 — sect. 1.2, no. 34. Which Krishnadasa
it is has not been established.
[^07-95]: Ms. "gha": dayālu (the same, "merciful").
[^07-96]: Mlecchas are foreigners and unbelievers; chandalas are untouchables. P-R-Sa: "hundreds" (śata) instead of "how
many".
[^07-97]: Ms. "ka" and GPT1: "lotus feet" (pādapadma).

## 23. Krishnadasa — "adoṣa-daraśī mora prabhu nityānanda…" (PK 2992)
*A prayer to Nityananda: Lord Nityananda sees no fault in people, yet the poet did not worship His feet; at the news of
Nitai's mercy even stone melts, but his heart does not soften; Nitai and Chaitanya do not count offences and give prema
to all alike. In PK it is the next pada. The same raga (shri).*[^07-98]

অদোষ-দরশী মোর প্রভু নিত্যানন্দ ।
না ভজিলুঁ হেন প্রভুর চরণারবিন্দ ॥

*adoṣa-daraśī mora prabhu nityānanda |*
*nā bhajilum̐ hena prabhura caraṇārabinda ||*

*Word for word:* adoṣa-daraśī — who sees no fault; mora prabhu nityānanda — my Lord Nityananda; nā bhajiluṃ — I did not worship; hena prabhura caraṇārabinda — the lotus feet of such a Lord

**23.1.** My Lord Nityananda sees no fault in anyone —
yet I did not worship the lotus feet of such a Lord.

হায় রে না জানি মুঞি কেমন অসুর ।
পাইয়া না ভজিলুঁ হেন দয়ার ঠাকুর ॥

*hāya re nā jāni muñi kemana asura |*
*pāiyā nā bhajilum̐ hena dayāra ṭhākura ||*

*Word for word:* hāy re — alas; nā jāni — I do not know; muñi kemana asura — what kind of demon I am; pāiyā — having found; nā bhajiluṃ — I did not worship; hena dayāra ṭhākura — so merciful a Master

**23.2.** Alas, I myself do not know what kind of demon I am:
having found so merciful a Master, I did not worship Him.[^07-99]

হায় রে অভাগার প্রাণ কি সুখে আছহ ।
নিতাই বলিয়া কেনে মরিয়া না যাহ ॥

*hāya re abhāgāra prāṇa ki sukhe āchaha |*
*nitāi baliyā kene mariyā nā yāha ||*

*Word for word:* hāy re abhāgāra prāṇa — alas, life of the unfortunate one; ki sukhe āchaha — in what contentment do you abide; nitāi baliyā — crying "Nitai"; kene mariyā nā yāha — why do you not die

**23.3.** Alas, life of the unfortunate one, in what contentment do you abide?
Why do you not die crying "Nitai"?

নিতাইর করুণা শুনি পাষাণ মিলায় ।
হায় রে দারুণ হিয়া না দরবে তায় ॥

*nitāira karuṇā śuni pāṣāṇa milāya |*
*hāya re dāruṇa hiyā nā darabe tāya ||*

*Word for word:* nitāira karuṇā śuni — hearing of Nitai's mercy; pāṣāṇa milāya — stone melts; hāy re — alas; dāruṇa hiyā — the cruel heart; nā darabe tāya — does not soften at it

**23.4.** At the news of Nitai's mercy stone melts —
but my cruel heart, alas, does not soften at it.

নিতাই চৈতন্য অপরাধ নাহি মানে ।
যারে তারে নিজ-প্রেম-ভক্তি করে দানে ॥

*nitāi caitanya aparādha nāhi māne |*
*yāre tāre nija-prema-bhakti kare dāne ||*

*Word for word:* nitāi caitanya — Nitai and Chaitanya; aparādha nāhi māne — do not count offences; yāre tāre — to all and sundry; nija-prema-bhakti kare dāne — give Their own prema-bhakti

**23.5.** Nitai and Chaitanya do not count offences —
to all and sundry They give Their prema-bhakti.

তাঁর নাম লইতে না গলয়ে মোর হিয়া ।
কৃষ্ণদাস কহে মুঞি বড় অভাগিয়া ॥

*tām̐ra nāma laite nā galaye mora hiyā |*
*kṛṣṇadāsa kahe muñi baṛa abhāgiyā ||*

*Word for word:* tāṃra nāma laite — uttering His name; nā galaye mora hiyā — my heart does not melt; kṛṣṇadāsa kahe — Krishnadasa says; muñi baṛa abhāgiyā — I am most unfortunate

**23.6.** When I utter His name, my heart does not melt.
Krishnadasa says: "I am the most unfortunate of all."[^07-100]

[^07-98]: Signature: "Krishnadasa". PK: vol. 4, PDF p. 228 (printed p. 219), 36th pallava, no. 8 (mark "॥৮॥২৯৯২॥"); "tathā
rāga" (shri); ms. P-R-Sa no. 2501. GPT1 — p. 433, no. 63 (raga shri; the section on Nityananda); GPT2 — sect. 6.1, no. 63.
[^07-99]: Mss. "ka", "kha": kemata (the same, "what kind of").
[^07-100]: Ms. "ca", P-R-Sa: "is not touched" (lāgaye) instead of "does not melt" (galaye).

## 24. Krishnadasa — "jaya jaya nityānanda rāy…" (PK 3006)
*A prayer to Nityananda: the poet confesses his sins and reminds the Lord of His name "Purifier of the fallen": if He
rejects the sinner, that name will bear a stain; He once delivered even yavanas — He will not push him away either, if He
does not despise him. In PK it stands in the 36th pallava. The same raga.*[^07-101]

জয় জয় নিত্যানন্দ রায় ।
অপরাধ পাপ মোর তাহার নাহিক ওর
উদ্ধারহ নিজ করুণায় ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*jaya jaya nityānanda rāya |*
*aparādha pāpa mora tāhāra nāhika ora*
*uddhāraha nija karuṇāya || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* jaya jaya nityānanda rāy — glory, glory to Nityananda Raya; aparādha pāpa mora — my offences and sins; tāhāra nāhika ora — have no end; uddhāraha nija karuṇāya — deliver [me] by Your own mercy

**24.1.** *(Refrain)* Glory, glory to Nityananda Raya!
My offences and sins have no end —
deliver me by Your own mercy!

আমার অসত মতি তোমার নামে নাহি রতি
কহিতে না বাসি মুখে লাজ ।
জনমে জনমে কত করিয়াছি আত্ম-ঘাত
অতয়ে সে মোর এই কাজ ॥

*āmāra asata mati tomāra nāme nāhi rati*
*kahite nā bāsi mukhe lāja |*
*janame janame kata kariyāchi ātma-ghāta*
*ataye se mora ei kāja ||*

*Word for word:* āmāra asata mati — my mind is wicked; tomāra nāme nāhi rati — I have no attraction to Your name; kahite nā bāsi mukhe lāja — I feel no shame to say it; janame janame kata — in how many births; kariyāchi ātma-ghāta — I have destroyed myself; ataye se mora ei kāja — therefore such are my deeds

**24.2.** My mind is wicked, I have no attraction to Your name —
I am not even ashamed to say it.
How many births in a row have I destroyed myself —
that is why such are my deeds.[^07-102]

তুমি ত করুণা-সিন্ধু পাতকী জনার বন্ধু
এবার করহ যদি ত্যাগ ।
পতিত-পাবন নাম নির্ম্মল সে অনুপাম
তাহাতে লাগয়ে বড় দাগ ॥

*tumi ta karuṇā-sindhu pātakī janāra bandhu*
*ebāra karaha yadi tyāga |*
*patita-pābana nāma nirmmala se anupāma*
*tāhāte lāgaye baṛa dāga ||*

*Word for word:* tumi ta karuṇā-sindhu — You are indeed an ocean of mercy; pātakī janāra bandhu — the friend of sinners; ebāra karaha yadi tyāga — if this time You reject [me]; patita-pābana nāma — the name "Purifier of the fallen"; nirmala se anupāma — pure and peerless; tāhāte lāgaye baṛa dāga — on it will fall a great stain

**24.3.** You are an ocean of mercy, the friend of sinners;
if this time You reject me,
then on Your peerless, pure name "Purifier of the fallen"
there will be a great stain.

পুরুবে যবন আদি কত কত অপরাধী
তরায়্যাছ শুনিয়াছি কাণে ।
কৃষ্ণদাস অনুমানি ঠেলিতে নারিবে তুমি
যদি ঘৃণা না করহ মনে ॥

*purube yabana ādi kata kata aparādhī*
*tarāyyācha śuniyāchi kāṇe |*
*kṛṣṇadāsa anumāni ṭhelite nāribe tumi*
*yadi ghṛṇā nā karaha mane ||*

*Word for word:* purube — formerly; yabana ādi — yavanas and others; kata kata aparādhī — so many offenders; tarāyyācha — You delivered; śuniyāchi kāṇe — I have heard with my ears; kṛṣṇadāsa anumāni — Krishnadasa reckons; ṭhelite nāribe tumi — You will not be able to push away; yadi ghṛṇā nā karaha mane — if You do not despise [him] in Your heart

**24.4.** I have heard with my own ears: You once delivered
yavanas and so many offenders.
Krishnadasa reckons: You will not be able to push him away,
if You do not despise him in Your heart.[^07-103]

[^07-101]: Signature: "Krishnadasa". PK: vol. 4, PDF p. 233 (printed p. 224), 36th pallava, no. 22 (mark "॥২২॥৩০০৬॥"); "tathā
rāga" (the raga of this series of padas is not named separately); ms. P-R-Sa no. 2515. GPT1 — pp. 432–433, no. 62 (raga
suhai; the section on Nityananda); GPT2 — sect. 6.1, no. 62. Which Krishnadasa it is has not been established.
[^07-102]: "Destroyed myself" (ātmaghāta) — lived forgetting the Lord, to the harm of the soul.
[^07-103]: Yavanas are foreign Muslims; cf. the Lord's mercy to the Kazi in Navadvipa (CC Adi 17).
