# Chapter 9. Vasu Ghosha: the Lord's Bhavas, Separation, Nityananda, Prayers

*Padas of Vasu (Vasudeva) Ghosha known from the *Padakalpataru* (PK), in the order of the lilas: Gaura in the
kirtana of Navadvipa, His form, His rest and the boat play on the Ganga; the Lord in Krishna's mood and in the mood of
Radha pining in separation (gaura-chandrikas to the sections of PK on impending and accomplished separation); the
devotees' longing for Gaura who has gone; praise of Nityananda; stavas and prarthanas — prayers to Gauranga. Majumdar
regards Vasu Ghosha as an eyewitness of the Navadvipa kirtanas and counts these padas among his padas on the Lord's
bhava, on Nityananda and among his stavas. The text follows PK, checked against the scans, with the manuscript
variants from PK's apparatus, the *Gaura-pada-tarangini* (GPT1 — 1st ed., 1903; GPT2 — 2nd ed., 1934) and the
*Kshanada-gita-chintamani* (KGC); the Bengali original, variants and word-for-word translation are in the full version of the book.*

## 1. Vasu Ghosha — "nabadvīpe udaya karilā dvija-rāja…" (PK 1494)
*Gaura in the kirtana of Navadvipa: the moon risen in the darkness of Kali among the stars, His companions; grey with
dust, He sways on the waves of bhava, sings "Hari, Hari" and stands still in the tribhanga pose; at His left is
Gadadhara; remembering Vrindavana, the Lord weeps and pours a downpour of the holy name upon the world. In PK it is the
gaura-chandrika to the section "the spring rasa." Raga dhanashi or vasanta.*[^09-1]

নবদ্বীপে উদয় করিলা দ্বিজ-রাজ ।
কলি-তিমির ঘোর গোরাচাঁদে উজোর
পারিষদ-তারাগণ মাঝ ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*nabadvīpe udaya karilā dvija-rāja |*
*kali-timira ghora gorācām̐de ujora*
*pāriṣada-tārāgaṇa mājha || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* nabadvīpe — in Navadvipa; udaya karilā — has risen; dvija-rāja — the king of the twice-born (the moon; the best of brahmanas); kali-timira ghora — the darkness of Kali is dense; gorācām̐de ujora — lit up by Gorachand (Gorachand shines); pāriṣada-tārā-gaṇa — the stars, His companions; mājha — amid

**1.1.** *(Refrain)* In Navadvipa the king of the twice-born has risen[^09-2] —
dense is the darkness of Kali, but Gorachand shines
amid the stars — His companions.

কীর্ত্তনে ঢর ঢর অঙ্গ ধূলি-ধূসর
হালত ভাব-তরঙ্গে ।
করে করতাল ধরি বোলত হরি হরি
খেণে খেণে রহই ত্রিভঙ্গে ॥

*kīrttane ḍhara ḍhara aṅga dhūli-dhūsara*
*hālata bhāba-taraṅge |*
*kare karatāla dhari bolata hari hari*
*kheṇe kheṇe rahai tribhaṅge ||*

*Word for word:* kīrttane — in kirtana; ḍhara ḍhara — brimming over (with love); aṅga — body; dhūli-dhūsara — grey with dust; hālata — sways; bhāba-taraṅge — on the waves of bhava; kare — in His hands; karatāla dhari — holding karatalas; bolata hari hari — says (sings) "Hari, Hari"; khene khene — again and again; rahai tribhaṅge — stands bent in three places

**1.2.** In kirtana, brimming over with love, grey all over with dust,
He sways on the waves of bhava;
karatalas in His hands, He sings, "Hari, Hari!" —
and again and again stands still, bent in three places.[^09-3]

বামে প্রিয় গদাধর কান্ধের উপরে তার
সুবলিত বাহু আজানে ।
সোঙরি বৃন্দাবন আকুল অনুখণ
ধারা বহে অরুণ-নয়ানে ॥

*bāme priya gadādhara kāndhera upare tāra*
*subalita bāhu ājāne |*
*soṅari bṛndābana ākula anukhaṇa*
*dhārā bahe aruṇa-nayāne ||*

*Word for word:* bāme — at the left; priya gadādhara — dear Gadadhara; kāndhera upare tāra — on his shoulder; subalita bāhu — the graceful (rounded) arm; ājāne — reaching to the knees; soṅari bṛndābana — remembering Vrindavana; ākula anukhaṇa — ceaselessly yearning; dhārā bahe — streams flow; aruṇa-nayāne — from the reddish eyes

**1.3.** At His left is dear Gadadhara,
and on his shoulder rests the Lord's graceful arm that reaches to the knees.[^09-4]
Remembering Vrindavana, ceaselessly yearning,
He sheds streams of tears from His reddish eyes.

আঁখিযুগ ঝর ঝর যেন নব জলধর
দশন বিজুরী জিনি ছটা ।
বাসুদেব ঘোষ গীতে কলি-জীব উদ্ধারিতে
বরিখল হরি-নাম-ঘটা ॥

*ām̐khiyuga jhara jhara yena naba jaladhara*
*daśana bijurī jini chaṭā |*
*bāsudeba ghoṣa gīte kali-jība uddhārite*
*barikhala hari-nāma-ghaṭā ||*

*Word for word:* ām̐khi-yuga — both eyes; jhara jhara — pour and pour; yena naba jaladhara — like a fresh raincloud; daśana — teeth; bijurī jini chaṭā — their radiance outshines lightning; bāsudeba ghoṣa gīte — in Vasudeva Ghosha's song (Vasudeva Ghosha sings); kali-jība uddhārite — to deliver the souls of Kali; barikhala — has rained; hari-nāma-ghaṭā — a downpour (profusion) of Hari's name

**1.4.** His eyes pour and pour like a fresh raincloud,
His teeth shine brighter than lightning.
Vasudeva Ghosha sings: to deliver the souls of the age of Kali,
He has rained a downpour of Hari's name.[^09-5]

[^09-1]: Signature: "Vasudeva Ghosha." PK: vol. 2, PDF p. 432 (printed p. 419), 3rd shakha, 27th pallava, section "atha bāsantī
rāsalīlā । taducita-śrīgauracandra" (gaura-chandrika to the spring rasa), no. 70 (mark "॥৭০॥১৪৯৪॥"); raga dhanashi or vasanta;
MS P-R-Sa no. 2044. GPT1 — p. 131, no. 59 (raga dhanashi). Majumdar counts PK 1494 among Vasu's padas on the Lord's
bhava.
[^09-2]: "Dvija-raja," "king of the twice-born," is both the moon and the best of brahmanas: Gaura is a brahmana risen
over Navadvipa like the moon.
[^09-3]: Tribhanga is the pose of Krishna playing the flute (bent at the neck, waist and knee): in kirtana the Lord
spontaneously assumes Krishna's form.
[^09-4]: Gadadhara Pandita, according to the *Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika*, is a manifestation of Radha; he stands at Gaura's
left as Radha stands at Krishna's left. MS "kh": "ājāno"; P-R-Sa: "ajāne" (the same).
[^09-5]: MS "kh": "pours" (barikhata). P-R-Sa: "like" (yena) instead of "brighter than" (jini).

## 2. Vasu Ghosha — "cala dekhi giyā gorā ati manohare…" (PK 973)
*Gaura's form in Nadia: "Come, let us go and see Gora!" — His body brighter than tested gold, His arms reaching to the
knees like golden pillars, a red cloth at His waist, a garland of malati down to His feet; the poet is ready to give
his life for Him. In PK it is the gaura-chandrika to the section "anuraga: setting out to the tryst by night." Raga
suhai.*[^09-6]

চল দেখি গিয়া গোরা অতি মনোহরে ।
অপরূপ রূপ গোরা নদীয়া নগরে ॥

*cala dekhi giyā gorā ati manohare |*
*aparūpa rūpa gorā nadīyā nagare ||*

*Word for word:* cala dekhi giyā — come, let us go and see; gorā — Gora; ati manohare — exceedingly beautiful; aparūpa rūpa — the wondrous form; gorā — of Gora; nadīyā nagare — in the town of Nadia

**2.1.** Come, let us go and see Gora, beautiful beyond words:
wondrous is Gora's form in the town of Nadia!

ঢল ঢল কষিল কাঞ্চন জিনি অঙ্গ ।
কে দেখি ধৈরজ ধরে নয়ান-তরঙ্গ ॥

*ḍhala ḍhala kaṣila kāñcana jini aṅga |*
*ke dekhi dhairaja dhare nayāna-taraṅga ||*

*Word for word:* ḍhala ḍhala — tender, radiant (shimmering); kaṣila kāñcana — tested gold (tried on the touchstone); jini — surpassing; aṅga — body; ke dekhi — who, seeing; dhairaja dhare — keeps composure; nayāna-taraṅga — the waves of the eyes

**2.2.** His body, tender and radiant, outshines tested gold;
who, seeing the waves of His eyes, can keep his composure?

আজানুলম্বিত ভুজ কনকের স্তম্ভ ।
অরুণ বসন কটি বিপুল নিতম্ব ॥

*ājānulambita bhuja kanakera stambha |*
*aruṇa basana kaṭi bipula nitamba ||*

*Word for word:* ājānu-lambita — reaching down to the knees; bhuja — arms; kanakera stambha — golden pillars; aruṇa basana — red cloth; kaṭi — at the waist; bipula nitamba — broad hips

**2.3.** His arms reach to His knees like golden pillars,
a red cloth is at His waist, broad are His hips.[^09-7]

মালতীর মালা গলে আপাদ দোলনি ।
বাসু কহে চল দিব পরাণ নিছনি ॥

*mālatīra mālā gale āpāda dolani |*
*bāsu kahe cala diba parāṇa nichani ||*

*Word for word:* mālatīra mālā — a garland of malati; gale — on the neck; āpāda dolani — swaying down to the feet; bāsu kahe — says Vasu; cala — come; diba parāṇa nichani — I will give my life as nichhani (as an offering waved around Him)

**2.4.** A garland of malati sways on His neck down to His feet.
Says Vasu: "Come — I will give my life for Him!"[^09-8]

[^09-6]: Signature: "Vasu." PK: vol. 2, PDF p. 200 (printed p. 187), 3rd shakha, 12th pallava, section "tataḥ punaśca
abhisārānurāgaḥ rātrau yathā । śrīgauracandraḥ," no. 1 (mark "॥১॥৯৭৩॥"); raga suhai; MS P-R-Sa no. 1423. The same pada stands in
PK a second time — PK 2176 (vol. 3, PDF pp. 259–260, printed pp. 248–249; 19th pallava, no. 9; MS P-R-Sa no. 2284), in
the section of padas spoken by the women of Nadia, with the ending "Says Vasu: 'I will go and offer [Him] my youth'";
so too in GPT1 (p. 161, no. 15, raga shri), among padas in nagari-bhava. Majumdar counts PK 973 among the padas on the
Lord's form and PK 2176 under nagari-bhava. The PK 973 recension is translated here; the 2176 recension belongs to
nagari-bhava: worship of Gaura in the spirit of "Gaura-nagari" is not accepted by the Gaudiya tradition (Vrindavana
Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja, Bhaktisiddhanta).
[^09-7]: Long arms, a broad chest and broad hips are marks of a great personality (mahapurusha) according to the
samudrika-shastra; so too Vrindavana Dasa and Krishnadasa Kaviraja describe the Lord's form.
[^09-8]: Literally "I will give my life as nichhani" — a rite in which something precious is waved around a beloved
person to ward off misfortune and then given away; here the poet gives his very life.

## 3. Vasu Ghosha — "śutiyāche gorācām̐da śayana-mandire…" (PK 656)
*Gorachand lies in His bedchamber on a wondrous couch, languid; it is as if the Creator had strained lightning from
the clouds and put all rasa into Him; Vasudeva Ghosha looks on in joy. In PK it is the gaura-chandrika to the section
"languor after the play" (rasalasa). Raga vibhasa.*[^09-9]

শুতিয়াছে গোরাচাঁদ শয়ন-মন্দিরে ।
বিচিত্র পালঙ্ক শেজ অতি মনোহরে ॥

*śutiyāche gorācām̐da śayana-mandire |*
*bicitra pālaṅka śeja ati manohare ||*

*Word for word:* śutiyāche — lies (asleep); gorācām̐da — Gorachand; śayana-mandire — in the bedchamber; bicitra pālaṅka — on a wondrous couch; śeja — bed; ati manohare — very lovely

**3.1.** Gorachand lies in His bedchamber
on a wondrous couch, on a lovely bed.

আলসে অবশ-তনু গোরা নটরায় ।
কি কহব অঙ্গ-শোভা কহনে না যায় ॥

*ālase abaśa-tanu gorā naṭarāya |*
*ki kahaba aṅga-śobhā kahane nā yāya ||*

*Word for word:* ālase — from languor; abaśa-tanu — His body limp; gorā naṭarāya — Gora, the king of dancers; ki kahaba — what shall I say; aṅga-śobhā — the beauty of His body; kahane nā yāya — cannot be told

**3.2.** Languid is the body of Gora, the king of dancers —
how can I tell the beauty of His body? It cannot be told![^09-10]

মেঘের বিজুরী কিবা ছানিয়া যতনে ।
কত রস দিয়া বিধি কৈল নিরমাণে ॥

*meghera bijurī kibā chāniyā yatane |*
*kata rasa diyā bidhi kaila niramāṇe ||*

*Word for word:* meghera bijurī — the lightning of the clouds; kibā — as if; chāniyā yatane — straining (kneading) it with care; kata rasa diyā — putting in so much rasa; bidhi — the Creator; kaila niramāṇe — fashioned (Him)

**3.3.** As if lightning had been carefully strained from the clouds —
so much rasa did the Creator put in, fashioning Him!

অতি মনোহর শেজ বিচিত্র বালিশে ।
বাসুদেব ঘোষে দেখে মনের হরিষে ॥

*ati manohara śeja bicitra bāliśe |*
*bāsudeba ghoṣe dekhe manera hariṣe ||*

*Word for word:* ati manohara śeja — a most lovely bed; bicitra bāliśe — with wondrous pillows; bāsudeba ghoṣe — Vasudeva Ghosha; dekhe — looks on; manera hariṣe — with joy in his heart

**3.4.** A lovely bed, wondrous pillows —
Vasudeva Ghosha looks on with joy in his heart.

[^09-9]: Signature: "Vasudeva Ghosha." PK: vol. 2, PDF p. 51 (printed p. 38), 3rd shakha, section "atha rasālasa । taducita-śrīgauracandra,"
no. 1 (mark "॥১॥৬৫৬॥"); raga vibhasa; MS P-R-Sa no. 1131. GPT1 — pp. 361–362, no. 53 (raga vibhasa). According to PK's
index of first lines (vol. 5), the same pada stands in PK a second time — PK 2474 (vol. 4, the section on the night and
morning plays); in the scan of vol. 4 (IA 354459) the leaf with PK 2474–2478 is missing between PDF pp. 44
and 45, so its variants have not been checked. The catalogue wrongly linked PK 656 to the GPT pada "nācata śacītanaya
gaurasundara…" (VG-057). Majumdar counts PK 656 among Vasu's padas on the Lord's bhava. PK's section "rasalasa" is about the
languor of Radha and Krishna after the night's play; the gaura-chandrika shows the Lord wearied by the night's kirtana
and bhava.
[^09-10]: MSS "gh," "c": "Gaura lies" (śutiyā āchena gaura) instead of "Gorachand lies"; "k," "c": "in absorption" (ābeśe),
"gh": "in languor" (alase) instead of "languid" (ālase; GPT1 — "ābeśe," with "ālase" in a note); P-R-Sa: "how can I tell the
beauty of His body" (ki kaba aṅgera śobhā), "says Vasudeva Ghosha" (kaya) instead of "looks on" (dekhe).

## 4. Vasu Ghosha — "nā jāniye gorācām̐dera kona bhāba mane…" (PK 1409)
*The boat play on the Ganga: Gorachand goes to the bank with His companions, steps into a boat with Gadadhara and
steers it Himself; everyone cries "We are sinking!" and bails out water, and, remembering the former play, floats in
the waters of prema, while the Lord, looking at Gadadhara, gently smiles. In PK it is the gaura-chandrika to the
section "the boat play" (nauka-vilasa). Raga tudi.*[^09-11]

না জানিয়ে গোরাচাঁদের কোন ভাব মনে ।
সুরধুনী-তীরে গেলা সহচর সনে ॥

*nā jāniye gorācām̐dera kona bhāba mane |*
*suradhunī-tīre gelā sahacara sane ||*

*Word for word:* nā jāniye — I do not know; gorācām̐dera — of Gorachand; kona bhāba mane — what bhava in the heart; suradhunī-tīre — to the bank of the Suradhuni (the Ganga); gelā — went; sahacara sane — with His companions

**4.1.** I do not know what bhava is in Gorachand's heart:
He went with His companions to the bank of the Suradhuni.[^09-12]

প্রিয় গদাধর আদি সঙ্গে ত করিয়া ।
নৌকায় চড়িলা গৌর প্রেমাবেশ হৈয়া ॥

*priya gadādhara ādi saṅge ta kariyā |*
*naukāya caṛilā gaura premābeśa haiyā ||*

*Word for word:* priya gadādhara ādi — dear Gadadhara and others; saṅge ta kariyā — taking with Him; naukāya caṛilā — stepped into a boat; gaura — Gaura; premābeśa haiyā — overwhelmed by prema

**4.2.** Taking with Him dear Gadadhara and others,
Gaura stepped into a boat, overwhelmed by prema.

আপনে কাণ্ডারী হৈয়া বায় নৌকাখানি ।
ডুবিল ডুবিল বলি সিঞ্চে সভে পানি ॥

*āpane kāṇḍārī haiyā bāya naukākhāni |*
*ḍubila ḍubila bali siñce sabhe pāni ||*

*Word for word:* āpane — Himself; kāṇḍārī haiyā — becoming the helmsman; bāya naukākhāni — steers the boat; ḍubila ḍubila bali — crying "we are sinking, sinking"; siñce — bail out (splash); sabhe — all; pāni — water

**4.3.** Becoming the helmsman Himself, He steers the boat;
"We are sinking, sinking!" all cry, and bail out the water.

পারিষদগণ সবে হরি হরি বোলে ।
পুরব সোঙরি কেহো ভাসে প্রেম-জলে ॥

*pāriṣadagaṇa sabe hari hari bole |*
*puraba soṅari keho bhāse prema-jale ||*

*Word for word:* pāriṣada-gaṇa sabe — all the companions; hari hari bole — call out "Hari, Hari"; puraba soṅari — remembering the former (play); keho — some; bhāse — float; prema-jale — in the waters of prema

**4.4.** All the companions call out, "Hari, Hari!" —
remembering the former play, some float in the waters of prema.[^09-13]

গদাধর-মুখ হেরি মৃদু মৃদু হাসে ।
বাসুদেব ঘোষে কহে মনের উল্লাসে ॥

*gadādhara-mukha heri mṛdu mṛdu hāse |*
*bāsudeba ghoṣe kahe manera ullāse ||*

*Word for word:* gadādhara-mukha heri — looking into Gadadhara's face; mṛdu mṛdu hāse — smiles ever so gently; bāsudeba ghoṣe kahe — says Vasudeva Ghosha; manera ullāse — with jubilation in his heart

**4.5.** Looking into Gadadhara's face, He smiles ever so gently —
so says Vasudeva Ghosha, with jubilation in his heart.

[^09-11]: Signature: "Vasudeva Ghosha." PK: vol. 2, PDF p. 388 (printed p. 375), 3rd shakha, 26th pallava, section "atha
naukā-bilāsa । taducita śrīmahāprabhu," no. 1 (mark "॥১॥১৪০৯॥"); raga tudi; MS P-R-Sa no. 1925. GPT1 — p. 333, no. 38 (raga tudi;
among the padas on the dana-lila). Majumdar counts PK 1409 among Vasu's padas on the Lord's bhava. Compare Ramananda's
pada on the same play (PK 1417, chapter 6).
[^09-12]: Suradhuni, "the river of the gods," is the Ganga.
[^09-13]: "The former play" is Krishna's play with Radha and the gopis in a boat on the Yamuna (nauka-lila): the Lord at
the helm is Krishna, Gadadhara is Radha. MSS "k," "c," P-R-Sa: "Himself" — āpani (the same); P-R-Sa: "guides" (bahe) instead
of "steers" (bāya), "with joy" (hariṣe) instead of "with jubilation" (ullāse). GPT1: "smiles to Himself" (mane mane hāse).

## 5. Vasu Ghosha — "āre mora gorā dvijamaṇi…" (PK 54)
*The Lord in the mood of Krishna stricken with purvaraga: "Radha, Radha!" Gora calls, weeps and rolls on the ground,
chants Radha's name with great devotion, rivers of tears flow from His eyes, and again and again He loses
consciousness. In PK it is the gaura-chandrika to the section "Sri Krishna's purvaraga." Raga suhai, tala
jayajayanti.*[^09-14]

আরে মোর গোরা দ্বিজমণি ।
রাধা রাধা বলি কান্দে লোটায় ধরণী ॥

*āre mora gorā dvijamaṇi |*
*rādhā rādhā bali kānde loṭāya dharaṇī ||*

*Word for word:* āre mora — O my; gorā — Gora; dvijamaṇi — jewel of the twice-born (brahmanas); rādhā rādhā bali — saying "Radha, Radha"; kānde — weeps; loṭāya dharaṇī — rolls on the ground

**5.1.** O my Gora, jewel of the twice-born!
"Radha, Radha!" He calls, weeps and rolls on the ground.

রাধা নাম জপে গোরা পরম যতনে ।
সুরধুনী-ধারা বহে অরুণ নয়ানে ॥

*rādhā nāma jape gorā parama yatane |*
*suradhunī-dhārā bahe aruṇa nayāne ||*

*Word for word:* rādhā nāma jape — chants Radha's name; gorā — Gora; parama yatane — with great devotion; suradhunī-dhārā — streams of the Suradhuni (the Ganga); bahe — flow; aruṇa nayāne — from the reddish eyes

**5.2.** Gora chants Radha's name with great devotion,
and streams of the Suradhuni flow from His reddish eyes.[^09-15]

খেনে খেনে গোরা-অঙ্গ ভূমে গড়ি যায় ।
রাধা নাম বলি খেনে খেনে মুরুছায় ॥

*khene khene gorā-aṅga bhūme gaṛi yāya |*
*rādhā nāma bali khene khene muruchāya ||*

*Word for word:* khene khene — again and again; gorā-aṅga — Gora's body; bhūme gaṛi yāya — rolls on the ground; rādhā nāma bali — uttering Radha's name; muruchāya — swoons

**5.3.** Again and again Gora's body rolls on the ground,
again and again, uttering Radha's name, He swoons.

পুলকে পূরল তনু গদগদ বোল ।
বাসু কহে গোরা কেন এত উতরোল ॥

*pulake pūrala tanu gadagada bola |*
*bāsu kahe gorā kena eta utarola ||*

*Word for word:* pulake pūrala tanu — the body is filled with gooseflesh (pulaka); gadagada bola — faltering speech; bāsu kahe — says Vasu; gorā kena — why is Gora; eta utarola — so agitated

**5.4.** His body is thrilled with gooseflesh, His voice falters.
Says Vasu: "Why is Gora so agitated?"

[^09-14]: Signature: "Vasu." PK: vol. 1, PDF p. 51 (printed p. 40), 1st shakha, section "śrīkṛṣṇasya pūrvvarāgaḥ । taducita-śrīmahāprabhuḥ,"
no. 1 (mark "॥১॥৫৪॥"); "suhai । jayajayantī." GPT1 — p. 297, no. 16 (jayajayanti). Majumdar counts PK 54 among Vasu's padas on
the Lord's bhava. Usually the Lord abides in Radha's mood, but His companions also saw His mood of Krishna longing for
the gopis (cf. CC Adi 17: the Lord chants "Gopi, gopi!").
[^09-15]: Streams of the Suradhuni (the Ganga) are His tears. MS "kh" and GPT1: "how many Suradhunis flow…". Line 5.2 is
repeated by Radhamohana Dasa in his pada on Gaura and Gauridasa (GPT1, p. 290, no. 43).

## 6. Vasu Ghosha — "sakala bhakata meli ānande hulāhuli…" (PK 2041)
*In the morning the devotees come with joyful cries to see Gauranga, but He has not slept all night and His face is
wan; rising, He sits down again on the ground, alone, apart; the devotees are alarmed, not understanding what bhava
has risen in His heart; one washes His face, another tidies His hair. In PK it is the gaura-chandrika "on the next
day" to the section "recollections of the complete union." Raga pahida.*[^09-16]

সকল ভকত মেলি আনন্দে হুলাহুলি
আইলা গৌরাঙ্গ-দরশনে ।
গৌরাঙ্গ শুতিয়া আছে কেহু ত নাহিক কাছে
নিশি জাগি মলিন বদনে ॥

*sakala bhakata meli ānande hulāhuli*
*āilā gaurāṅga-daraśane |*
*gaurāṅga śutiyā āche kehu ta nāhika kāche*
*niśi jāgi malina badane ||*

*Word for word:* sakala bhakata meli — all the devotees together; ānande hulāhuli — with joyful cries; āilā — came; gaurāṅga-daraśane — to see Gauranga; gaurāṅga śutiyā āche — Gauranga is lying down; kehu ta nāhika kāche — no one is near; niśi jāgi — having stayed awake all night; malina badane — with a wan face

**6.1.** All the devotees together, with joyful cries,
came to see Gauranga.
Gauranga is lying down, no one is near Him;
He has stayed awake all night, His face is wan.

ইহ বড় অদভুত রঙ্গ ।
উঠিয়া গৌর হরি ভূমিতে বসিলা ফেরি
না বৈসয়ে কাহুক সঙ্গ ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*iha baṛa adabhuta raṅga |*
*uṭhiyā gaura hari bhūmite basilā pheri*
*nā baisaye kāhuka saṅga || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* iha baṛa adabhuta raṅga — here is a great wonder; uṭhiyā — rising; gaura hari — Gaura Hari; bhūmite — on the ground; basilā pheri — sat down again; nā baisaye — does not sit; kāhuka saṅga — with anyone

**6.2.** *(Refrain)* Here is a great wonder:
rising, Gaura Hari sat down again on the ground,
and sits with no one beside Him.[^09-17]

দেখিয়া ভকতগণ চমকিত হৈল মন
বিরস বদন কি কারণে ।
সভে কহে হায় হায় কিছুই না বুঝা যায়
কি ভাব উঠিল আজি মনে ॥

*dekhiyā bhakatagaṇa camakita haila mana*
*birasa badana ki kāraṇe |*
*sabhe kahe hāya hāya kichui nā bujhā yāya*
*ki bhāba uṭhila āji mane ||*

*Word for word:* dekhiyā bhakatagaṇa — seeing, the devotees; camakita haila mana — were alarmed at heart; birasa badana — the cheerless face; ki kāraṇe — for what reason; sabhe kahe hāya hāya — all say "alas, alas"; kichui nā bujhā yāya — nothing can be understood; ki bhāba uṭhila — what bhava has risen; āji mane — today in the heart

**6.3.** Seeing this, the devotees were alarmed:
why is His face so cheerless?
All say, "Alas, alas! Nothing can be understood —
what bhava has risen in His heart today?"

কেহু লহু লহু করে মুখানি পাখালে নীরে
কেহ করে কেশ সম্বরণ ।
কিছু না জানিয়ে মোরা ভাবের মূরতি গোরা
বাসুঘোষ মলিন-বদন ॥

*kehu lahu lahu kare mukhāni pākhāle nīre*
*keha kare keśa sambaraṇa |*
*kichu nā jāniye morā bhābera mūrati gorā*
*bāsughoṣa malina-badana ||*

*Word for word:* kehu lahu lahu kare — someone gently; mukhāni pākhāle nīre — washes the face with water; keha kare keśa sambaraṇa — someone tidies the hair; kichu nā jāniye morā — we know nothing; bhābera mūrati gorā — Gora is bhava embodied; bāsughoṣa — Vasu Ghosha; malina-badana — with a sad face

**6.4.** One gently washes His face with water,
another tidies His hair.
"We know nothing: Gora is bhava embodied" —
and sad is Vasu Ghosha's face.[^09-18]

[^09-16]: Signature: "Vasu Ghosha." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 210 (printed p. 199), 4th shakha, 16th pallava ("samriddhiman
sambhoga: recollections"), section "atha dināntare śrīmadgauracandro yathā," no. 18 (mark "॥১৮॥২০৪১॥"); raga pahida. GPT1 — p. 312,
no. 17 (pahida), just before the section on separation; in GPT2 — in the section on the antya-lila (the catalogue had
it twice: VG-080 and VG-122). The place is not named. Majumdar counts PK 2041 among Vasu's padas on the Lord's bhava.
The PK section shows Radha, on the next day, recalling the night of union with Krishna; the gaura-chandrika shows the
Lord absorbed in such recollections.
[^09-17]: MSS "k," "kh": "Gauranga" instead of "Gaura"; "k," "kh," "c" and GPT1: "having sat" (basiyā) instead of "sat." In MS "k"
there is a lacuna mark in place of the word "with joyful cries" (hulāhuli).
[^09-18]: "Bhava embodied" (bhābera mūrati): the Lord, in whom Radha's bhava manifests in its fullness.

## 7. Vasu Ghosha — "āju kene gorācām̐dera birasa bayāna…" (PK 1598)
*The Lord in the mood of Radha foreseeing separation: Gorachand's face is cheerless, He asks, "Who has come?" and
weeps; the devotees around have fainted, not understanding the cause; crying "Hari, Hari," Gora sighs heavily. In PK it
is the gaura-chandrika to the section "impending separation." Raga suhai, tala kandarpa.*[^09-19]

আজু কেনে গোরাচাঁদের বিরস বয়ান ।
কে আইল কে আইল বলি ঝরয়ে নয়ান ॥

*āju kene gorācām̐dera birasa bayāna |*
*ke āila ke āila bali jharaye nayāna ||*

*Word for word:* āju kene — why today; gorācām̐dera — Gorachand's; birasa bayāna — cheerless face; ke āila ke āila bali — saying "who has come? who has come?"; jharaye nayāna — the eyes stream with tears

**7.1.** Why is Gorachand's face so cheerless today?
"Who has come? Who has come?" He says, and tears stream down.[^09-20]

চৌদিগে ভকতগণ কাঁদি অচেতন ।
গৌরাঙ্গ এমন কেনে না বুঝি কারণ ॥

*caudige bhakatagaṇa kām̐di acetana |*
*gaurāṅga emana kene nā bujhi kāraṇa ||*

*Word for word:* caudige — all around; bhakatagaṇa — the devotees; kām̐di acetana — weeping, have fainted; gaurāṅga emana kene — why Gauranga is so; nā bujhi kāraṇa — we do not understand the cause

**7.2.** All around, the devotees, weeping, have fainted:
why Gauranga is so, they cannot understand.[^09-21]

সে মুখ চাহিতে হিয়া কেমন জানি করে ।
কত সুরধুনী-ধারা আঁখিযুগে ঝরে ॥

*se mukha cāhite hiyā kemana jāni kare |*
*kata suradhunī-dhārā ām̐khiyuge jhare ||*

*Word for word:* se mukha cāhite — looking at that face; hiyā kemana jāni kare — the heart feels I know not how (is wrung); kata suradhunī-dhārā — how many streams of the Suradhuni; ām̐khi-yuge jhare — pour from both eyes

**7.3.** To look at that face — the heart is wrung:
how many Suradhunis pour from His eyes!

হরি হরি বলি গোরা ছাড়য়ে নিশ্বাস ।
শিরে কর হানে বাসু গদগদ ভাষ ॥

*hari hari bali gorā chāṛaye niśvāsa |*
*śire kara hāne bāsu gadagada bhāṣa ||*

*Word for word:* hari hari bali — crying "Hari, Hari"; gorā chāṛaye niśvāsa — Gora heaves sighs; śire kara hāne — strikes his head with his hand; bāsu — Vasu; gadagada bhāṣa — with faltering speech

**7.4.** Crying "Hari, Hari," Gora sighs heavily;
Vasu strikes his head with his hand and speaks, faltering with tears.

[^09-19]: Signature: "Vasu." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 18 (printed p. 7), 4th shakha, 2nd pallava, section "atha bhābī birahaḥ ।
tadbhābākrāntaḥ śrīmahāprabhuḥ" ("impending separation; Sri Mahaprabhu, overwhelmed by this bhava"), no. 1 (mark "॥১॥১৫৯৮॥");
"suhai । kandarpatāla"; MS P-R-Sa no. 806. GPT1 — p. 313, no. 1 (suhai, kandarpa) — the first pada of the section on
separation. Majumdar counts PK 1598 among Vasu's padas on the Lord's bhava.
[^09-20]: The PK section: Radha learns that Akrura has come for Krishna to take Him to Mathura; the Lord in Radha's mood
asks, "Who has come?" GPT1: "'Who has come? Who has come?' — and tears stream down" (kari instead of vali).
[^09-21]: MS "k": "kena" (the same, "why"); "gh": "they cannot understand His heart" (bujhilu mana) instead of "cannot understand
the cause"; "k": "before Him" (samukha) instead of "that face" (se mukha); MS "kh" lacks the word "jāni" ("is wrung," literally
"I know not how"); P-R-Sa: "weep" (jhure) instead of "pour" (jhare).

## 8. Vasu Ghosha — "roi roi jape gorā kṛṣṇa-nāma-madhu…" (PK 1634)
*The Lord in the mood of Radha separated from Krishna: weeping, Gora chants the honeyed name of Krishna; He whose feet
Shiva and Brahma do not attain sits under a tree, having left all company and all comforts; His golden body is adorned
with the treasures of bhava; seeing Him, all weep. In PK it is the gaura-chandrika to the section "accomplished
separation." Raga suhai.*[^09-22]

রোই রোই জপে গোরা কৃষ্ণ-নাম-মধু ।
অমিয়া বরিখে যেন নিরমল বিধু ॥

*roi roi jape gorā kṛṣṇa-nāma-madhu |*
*amiyā barikhe yena niramala bidhu ||*

*Word for word:* roi roi — weeping and weeping; jape — chants; gorā — Gora; kṛṣṇa-nāma-madhu — the honey of Krishna's name; amiyā barikhe — showers nectar; yena — as if; niramala bidhu — a spotless moon

**8.1.** Weeping and weeping, Gora chants the honey of Krishna's name —
as if a spotless moon were showering nectar.[^09-23]

শিব বিহি নাহি পায় যার পদ ভজি ।
তরুতলে বৈঠল সব সঙ্গ তেজি ॥

*śiba bihi nāhi pāya yāra pada bhaji |*
*tarutale baiṭhala saba saṅga teji ||*

*Word for word:* śiba bihi — Shiva and Brahma; nāhi pāya — do not attain; yāra pada bhaji — whose feet, worshipping; tarutale — under a tree; baiṭhala — sat down; saba saṅga teji — forsaking all company

**8.2.** He whose feet Shiva and Brahma do not attain by worship
has sat down under a tree, forsaking all company.[^09-24]

ছাড়িয়া সকল সুখ ভেল অশকতি ।
শাতকুম্ভ-কলেবর ভাব-বিভূতি ॥

*chāṛiyā sakala sukha bhela aśakati |*
*śātakumbha-kalebara bhāba-bibhūti ||*

*Word for word:* chāṛiyā sakala sukha — leaving all comforts; bhela aśakati — grew weak (became powerless); śātakumbha-kalebara — golden body; bhāba-bibhūti — the treasures (adornments) of bhava

**8.3.** Leaving all comforts, He has grown weak;
His golden body is adorned with the treasures of bhava.[^09-25]

দেখিয়া সকল লোক অনুখণ কান্দে ।
বাসুদেব ঘোষ হিয়া থির নাহি বান্ধে ॥

*dekhiyā sakala loka anukhaṇa kānde |*
*bāsudeba ghoṣa hiyā thira nāhi bāndhe ||*

*Word for word:* dekhiyā — seeing; sakala loka — all the people; anukhaṇa kānde — weep ceaselessly; bāsudeba ghoṣa — Vasudeva Ghosha's; hiyā thira nāhi bāndhe — heart finds no rest

**8.4.** Seeing Him, all the people weep ceaselessly;
Vasudeva Ghosha's heart can find no rest.

[^09-22]: Signature: "Vasudeva Ghosha." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 37 (printed p. 26), 4th shakha, 4th pallava, section "atha
bhūta-birahaḥ । nāyikā proṣitabhartṛkā । tadbhābākrāntaḥ śrīgauracandro yathā" ("accomplished separation; the heroine whose beloved has
gone abroad; Sri Gaurachandra, overwhelmed by this bhava"), no. 1 (mark "॥১॥১৬৩৪॥"); raga suhai (P-R: sindhura); MS P-R-Sa
no. 857, MS P-R no. 40.19. GPT2 — in the section on separation (the catalogue had it as VG-043 and VG-115; one pada).
Not found in GPT1. Majumdar counts PK 1634 among Vasu's padas on the Lord's bhava. Sitting under a tree, having left
all company — the Lord after His sannyasa.
[^09-23]: MSS "k," "kh," "c," P-R-Sa and GPT2: "as if a spotless moon were pouring nectar" (jharaye; "k," "kh," "gh," "c," P-R-Sa and
GPT2 — vimala, "spotless," instead of niramala, the same).
[^09-24]: MSS "k," "c": "whose feet they do not attain by devotion (bhakti)"; P-R: "by seeking" (khuji).
[^09-25]: MS P-R: "He left all comforts, renouncing strength" (chāṛala saba sukha tejiyā śakati); "k," "kh," P-R: "went" (gela) instead of
"has grown weak" (bhela aśakati — literally "became powerless"). The treasures of bhava are the sattvika-bhavas: tears,
trembling, gooseflesh and the other signs of prema. P-R: "the heart finds no rest" (sthira).

## 9. Vasu Ghosha — "birale basiyā ekeśvare…" (PK 1635)
*The Lord as a sannyasi in separation: alone, in solitude, He ceaselessly chants the name of Hari; His body, once
anointed with sandal, now cares for nothing but dust; He has left the pastimes with Lakshmi and lives under a tree, has
left the flute and taken the sannyasi's staff; He knows neither day nor night. In PK it is the second gaura-chandrika
to the section "accomplished separation." Raga suhai.*[^09-26]

বিরলে বসিয়া একেশ্বরে ।
হরিনাম জপে নিরন্তরে ॥

*birale basiyā ekeśvare |*
*harināma jape nirantare ||*

*Word for word:* birale — in solitude; basiyā — sitting; ekeśvare — alone; hari-nāma jape — chants the name of Hari; nirantare — ceaselessly

**9.1.** In solitude He sits alone
and ceaselessly chants the name of Hari.

সুগন্ধি চন্দন মাখা গায় ।
ধূলা বিনু আন নাহি ভায় ॥

*sugandhi candana mākhā gāya |*
*dhūlā binu āna nāhi bhāya ||*

*Word for word:* sugandhi candana — with fragrant sandal; mākhā gāya — anointed body; dhūlā binu — except dust; āna nāhi bhāya — nothing else pleases

**9.2.** His body was anointed with fragrant sandal —
now nothing pleases Him but dust.[^09-27]

ছাড়ি পহুঁ লখিমী-বিলাস ।
এবে ভেল তরুতলে বাস ॥

*chāṛi pahum̐ lakhimī-bilāsa |*
*ebe bhela tarutale bāsa ||*

*Word for word:* chāṛi — leaving; pahum̐ — the Lord; lakhimī-bilāsa — the pastimes with Lakshmi; ebe — now; bhela — has become; tarutale bāsa — a dwelling beneath a tree

**9.3.** The Lord has left the pastimes with Lakshmi —
now His dwelling is beneath a tree.[^09-28]

ছাড়িয়া মোহন করে বাঁশী ।
দণ্ড ধরি হইলা সন্ন্যাসী ॥

*chāṛiyā mohana kare bām̐śī |*
*daṇḍa dhari hailā sannyāsī ||*

*Word for word:* chāṛiyā — leaving; mohana — the enchanting; kare — from His hand; bām̐śī — flute; daṇḍa dhari — taking the staff; hailā sannyāsī — became a sannyasi

**9.4.** Leaving the enchanting flute from His hands,
He has taken the staff and become a sannyasi.

রাতি দিবস নাহি জান ।
বাসু কহে বিদরে পরাণ ॥

*rāti dibasa nāhi jāna |*
*bāsu kahe bidare parāṇa ||*

*Word for word:* rāti dibasa — night and day; nāhi jāna — He does not know; bāsu kahe — says Vasu; bidare parāṇa — the heart is breaking

**9.5.** He knows neither day nor night.
Says Vasu: "The heart is breaking!"[^09-29]

are swollen with weeping"; "Making prema His treasure, / He has taken all the destitute with Him"; the ending — "He
bathes in the waters of prema. / Says Vasu: 'The heart is breaking!'"

## 10. Vasu Ghosha — "majhu mane lāgala śela…" (PK 451)
*A lament for Gaura who has turned away from His lover: a spear has pierced the heart, life has become fruitless; if
one is never again to see Gora's face, what joy is there in life? Without Gora life cannot be held. In PK it is the
gaura-chandrika to the section "repentance after a quarrel" (kalahantarita). Raga pathamanjari.*[^09-30]

মঝু মনে লাগল শেল ।
গৌর বিমুখ ভৈ গেল ॥

*majhu mane lāgala śela |*
*gaura bimukha bhai gela ||*

*Word for word:* majhu mane — in my heart; lāgala śela — a spear has struck; gaura — Gaura; bimukha bhai gela — has turned away

**10.1.** A spear has pierced my heart:
Gaura has turned away from me.

জনম বিফল মোর ভেল ।
দারুণ বিহি দুখ দেল ॥

*janama biphala mora bhela |*
*dāruṇa bihi dukha dela ||*

*Word for word:* janama biphala mora bhela — my life has become fruitless; dāruṇa bihi — the cruel Creator; dukha dela — has given grief

**10.2.** My life has become fruitless —
a cruel Creator has sent me grief.

কাহে কহব ইহ দুখ ।
কহইতে বিদরয়ে বুক ॥

*kāhe kahaba iha dukha |*
*kahaite bidaraye buka ||*

*Word for word:* kāhe kahaba — to whom shall I tell; iha dukha — this grief; kahaite — in speaking; bidaraye buka — the breast is torn apart

**10.3.** To whom shall I tell this grief?
When I begin to speak, my breast is torn apart.[^09-31]

আর না হেরব গোরা-মুখ ।
তবে জীবনে কিয়ে সুখ ॥

*āra nā heraba gorā-mukha |*
*tabe jībane kiye sukha ||*

*Word for word:* āra nā heraba — if I shall no more see; gorā-mukha — Gora's face; tabe — then; jībane — in life; kiye sukha — what joy

**10.4.** If I am never again to see Gora's face,
what joy is there for me in life?[^09-32]

বাসুদেব ঘোষ রস গান ।
গোরা বিনে না রহে পরাণ ॥

*bāsudeba ghoṣa rasa gāna |*
*gorā bine nā rahe parāṇa ||*

*Word for word:* bāsudeba ghoṣa — Vasudeva Ghosha; rasa gāna — sings the rasa; gorā bine — without Gora; nā rahe parāṇa — life does not remain

**10.5.** Vasudeva Ghosha sings this rasa:
without Gora life cannot be held.

[^09-30]: Signature: "Vasudeva Ghosha." PK: vol. 1, PDF p. 307 (printed p. 296), 2nd shakha, section "punaśca kalahāntaritā ।
taducita-śrīgauracandraḥ," no. 1 (mark "॥১॥৪৫১॥"); raga pathamanjari (P-R: suhai); MS P-R-Sa no. 640, P-R no. 22.1. GPT1 — p. 312,
no. 19 (pathamanjari), following a pada of Radhamohana on the Lord in the mood of mana and separation; GPT2 — in the
section of the laments of Shachi and Vishnupriya after the sannyasa (no. 16). Whose words these are, the author does
not say; the PK section shows Radha repenting that in anger She rejected Krishna. We translate it as the lament of a
devoted soul separated from Gaura. Majumdar does not discuss this pada.

tell this grief" (hāma kāhe kahabahim̐ dukha).
[^09-32]: MSS "k," "g," "c," P-R: "taba"; P-R-Sa: "tabahi" (the same: "then"); P-R: "kibā sukha" (the same).

## 11. Vasu Ghosha — "kata dine heraba gorācām̐dera mukha…" (PK 2279)
*The devotees' longing for Gaura after the sannyasa: when shall we see Gorachand's face, when will the Lord embrace
us, when will our ears hear His words? The people of Nadia weep, not seeing Gora. In PK it is the section "the
devotees' longing" in the pallava on Gauranga's sannyasa. Raga suhai.*[^09-33]

কত দিনে হেরব গোরাচাঁদের মুখ ।
কবে মোর মনের মিটব সব দুখ ॥

*kata dine heraba gorācām̐dera mukha |*
*kabe mora manera miṭaba saba dukha ||*

*Word for word:* kata dine — after how many days (when); heraba — shall I see; gorācām̐dera mukha — Gorachand's face; kabe — when; mora manera — of my heart; miṭaba — will be stilled; saba dukha — all the sorrow

**11.1.** When shall I see Gorachand's face?
When will all the sorrow of my heart be stilled?

কত দিনে গোরা পহু করবহি কোর ।
কত দিনে সদয় হইবে বিধি মোর ॥

*kata dine gorā pahu karabahi kora |*
*kata dine sadaya haibe bidhi mora ||*

*Word for word:* kata dine — when; gorā pahu — the Lord Gora; karabahi kora — will clasp in His embrace; sadaya haibe — will be kind; bidhi mora — my fate (my Creator)

**11.2.** When will the Lord Gora clasp me in His embrace?
When will fate be kind to me?[^09-34]

কত দিনে শ্রবণের হবে শুভ দিন ।
চাঁদ-মুখের বচন শুনিব নিশিদিন ॥

*kata dine śrabaṇera habe śubha dina |*
*cām̐da-mukhera bacana śuniba niśidina ||*

*Word for word:* kata dine — when; śrabaṇera — for the ears; habe śubha dina — will the auspicious day come; cām̐da-mukhera bacana — the words of the Moon-faced One; śuniba niśidina — I shall hear night and day

**11.3.** When will the auspicious day dawn for my ears —
to hear day and night the words of the Moon-faced One?

বাসুঘোষ কহে গোরা-গুণ সোঙরিয়া ।
ঝুরয়ে নদীয়ার লোক গোরা না দেখিয়া ॥

*bāsughoṣa kahe gorā-guṇa soṅariyā |*
*jhuraye nadīyāra loka gorā nā dekhiyā ||*

*Word for word:* bāsughoṣa kahe — says Vasu Ghosha; gorā-guṇa soṅariyā — remembering Gora's virtues; jhuraye — weep; nadīyāra loka — the people of Nadia; gorā nā dekhiyā — not seeing Gora

**11.4.** Says Vasu Ghosha, remembering Gora's virtues:
the people of Nadia weep, not seeing Gora.[^09-35]

Gauranga, etc."), section "atha bhaktagaṇasya utkaṇṭhā yathā," no. 62 (mark "॥৬২॥২২৭৯॥"); raga suhai; MS P-R-Sa no. 2383, P-R no. 41.11.
GPT1 — p. 387, no. 14 (suhai); GPT2 — sect. 5.4, no. 14. Majumdar counts PK 2279 among Vasu's stavas and prarthanas.
Next in PK (2280) comes Vasu's pada "gorā-guṇe prāṇa kānde…" (chapter 5).

Gora's face [sorrow] will cease" (gorāmukha daraśe ṭuṭaba); P-R-Sa, P-R: "kore," "more" (the same).
[^09-35]: MSS "k," "kh," "gh," "c," P-R-Sa and GPT1: "śrabaṇe haibe" (the same); P-R: "sings" (gāya) instead of "says," "the Lord's" (pahum̐) instead of "Gora's"; instead of "the
people of Nadia weep" — MS "kh": "how can life be kept [, not seeing Gora]" (kemane rahibe prāṇa); P-R: "weeping, the eyes are
dying" (jhuriyā maraye ām̐khi).

## 12. Vasu Ghosha — "nitāi kebala patita janāra bandhu…" (PK 2314)
*Praise of Nitai: He alone is the friend of the fallen, an ocean of jewels amid the destitute; in separation from Gaura
He looks all around and calls, "Lord Gora Raya!" and falls unconscious; His companions take Him in their arms and weep;
tears of prema flow from His reddish eyes, with a thundering voice He calls, "Brother, brother!" and the earth trembles
under His steps; He gave the world prema through sankirtana — why then has Vasu been left out? In PK it stands in the
pallava "Description of Sri Nityananda's virtues." Raga sindhura.*[^09-36]

নিতাই কেবল পতিত জনার বন্ধু ।
জীবের চির পুণ্য-ফলে বিহি আনি মিলাইলে
রঙ্ক মাঝে রতনের সিন্ধু ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*nitāi kebala patita janāra bandhu |*
*jībera cira puṇya-phale bihi āni milāile*
*raṅka mājhe ratanera sindhu || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* nitāi kebala — Nitai alone; patita janāra bandhu — the friend of fallen people; jībera cira puṇya-phale — by the fruit of the living beings' age-old pious deeds; bihi āni milāile — the Creator brought and granted; raṅka mājhe — amid poverty; ratanera sindhu — an ocean of jewels

**12.1.** *(Refrain)* Nitai alone is the friend of fallen people.
By the fruit of the living beings' age-old pious deeds the Creator has granted them,
amid their poverty, an ocean of jewels.[^09-37]

দিগ নেহারিয়া যায় ডাকে পহু গোরা রায়
ধরণীতে পড়ে মুরছিয়া ।
প্রিয় সহচর মেলে নিতাইরে করি কোলে
কান্দে চাঁদ-বদন হেরিয়া ॥

*diga nehāriyā yāya ḍāke pahu gorā rāya*
*dharaṇīte paṛe murachiyā |*
*priya sahacara mele nitāire kari kole*
*kānde cām̐da-badana heriyā ||*

*Word for word:* diga nehāriyā yāya — looking in all directions He goes; ḍāke pahu gorā rāya — calls "Lord Gora Raya"; dharaṇīte paṛe muruchiyā — falls unconscious to the ground; priya sahacara mele — the dear companions gather; nitāire kari kole — taking Nitai in their arms; kānde — weep; cām̐da-badana heriyā — gazing at the moonlike face

**12.2.** Looking all around, He goes and calls, "Lord Gora Raya!" —
and falls unconscious to the ground.
His dear companions gather, take Nitai in their arms
and weep, gazing at His moonlike face.

নব-কঞ্জারুণ আঁখি প্রেমে ছল ছল দেখি
সুমেরু বাহিয়া মন্দাকিনী ।
মেঘ-গভীর-স্বরে ভাই ভাই রব করে
পদ-ভরে কম্পিত মেদিনী ॥

*naba-kañjāruṇa ām̐khi preme chala chala dekhi*
*sumeru bāhiyā mandākinī |*
*megha-gabhīra-svare bhāi bhāi raba kare*
*pada-bhare kampita medinī ||*

*Word for word:* naba-kañjāruṇa ām̐khi — eyes red as a fresh lotus; preme chala chala dekhi — seen brimming with tears of prema; sumeru bāhiyā mandākinī — the Mandakini streaming down Sumeru; megha-gabhīra-svare — with a voice deep as the thunder of clouds; bhāi bhāi raba kare — cries "brother, brother"; pada-bhare — under the weight of His steps; kampita medinī — the earth trembles

**12.3.** His eyes, red as a fresh lotus, brim with tears of prema —
as if the Mandakini were streaming down Sumeru.[^09-38]
With a voice deep as the thunder of clouds He calls, "Brother, brother!" —
under the weight of His steps the earth trembles.

নিতাই করুণাময় জীবে দিল প্রেমাশ্রয়
হেন দয়া জগতে বিদিত ।
নিজ-নাম-সংকীর্ত্তনে উদ্ধারিলা জগ-জনে
বাসু কেনে হইল বঞ্চিত ॥

*nitāi karuṇāmaya jībe dila premāśraya*
*hena dayā jagate bidita |*
*nija-nāma-saṃkīrttane uddhārilā jaga-jane*
*bāsu kene haila bañcita ||*

*Word for word:* nitāi karuṇāmaya — merciful Nitai; jībe dila premāśraya — gave the living beings the shelter of prema; hena dayā — such mercy; jagate bidita — is known to the world; nija-nāma-saṃkīrttane — by the sankirtana of His own (dear) name; uddhārilā jaga-jane — delivered the people of the world; bāsu kene — why has Vasu; haila bañcita — been left out

**12.4.** Merciful Nitai gave the living beings the shelter of prema —
such mercy is known to all the world.
Through the sankirtana of the name so dear to Him He delivered the people of the world —
why then has Vasu been left out?[^09-39]

Nityananda's virtues"), no. 21 (mark "॥২১॥২৩১৪॥"); raga sindhura; MS P-R-Sa no. 2418. KGC 27.2 (sindhura; "of Shri
Nityananda-chandra"); GPT1 — pp. 423–424, no. 31 (sindhura); GPT2 — sect. 6.1, no. 31. Majumdar counts PK 2314 among
Vasu's padas on Nityananda.
[^09-37]: MS "kh": "to the living beings" (jībe); P-R-Sa: "jība" (the same). KGC: "the Creator brought and joined [to them]" (bidhi
āni milāola); GPT1: "amid poverty, an ocean of love" (pirītera sindhu).

body. MSS "k," "kh," "gh," "c," KGC and GPT1: "red as gunja berries" (guñjāruṇa). MS "kh": "meli," P-R-Sa: "mile" (the same:
"gather"); P-R-Sa: "holding" (kare) instead of "take in their arms." KGC and GPT1: "and the Lord [Nitai] weeps, gazing at
the moonlike face," "with thunderous sound again He calls, 'Brother!'"

KGC: "He gave the living beings prema unknown even to the Creator; by His own virtues, giving prema, He flooded the three
worlds — / only Vasudeva Ghosha is left out"; so too GPT1.

## 13. Vasu Ghosha — "saṃkīrtane nityānanda nāce…" (PK 2315)
*Nityananda dances in sankirtana with His dear companions near Him, while Govinda and Madhava Ghosha sing; embracing
the fallen, He weeps and says, "I owe you much — take the wares of prema! I will destroy your misfortunes and give you
prema with interest"; Vasu pines in tears, remembering such mercy. In PK it is the next pada of the same pallava. Raga
shri.*[^09-40]

সংকীর্তনে নিত্যানন্দ নাচে ।
প্রিয় পারিষদগণ কাছে ॥

*saṃkīrtane nityānanda nāce |*
*priya pāriṣadagaṇa kāche ||*

*Word for word:* saṃkīrtane — in sankirtana; nityānanda nāce — Nityananda dances; priya pāriṣadagaṇa — the dear companions; kāche — near

**13.1.** In sankirtana Nityananda dances,
His dear companions near Him.

গোবিন্দ-মাধব-ঘোষের গান ।
শুনি কেবা ধরয়ে পরাণ ॥

*gobinda-mādhaba-ghoṣera gāna |*
*śuni kebā dharaye parāṇa ||*

*Word for word:* gobinda-mādhaba-ghoṣera gāna — the song of Govinda and Madhava Ghosha; śuni — hearing; kebā dharaye parāṇa — who could keep hold of life

**13.2.** Hearing the song of Govinda and Madhava Ghosha,
who could keep hold of life?[^09-41]

পতিতের গলায় ধরিয়া ।
কান্দে পহু সকরুণ হৈয়া ॥

*patitera galāya dhariyā |*
*kānde pahu sakaruṇa haiyā ||*

*Word for word:* patitera galāya dhariyā — embracing the fallen by the neck; kānde pahu — the Lord (Nitai) weeps; sakaruṇa haiyā — full of compassion

**13.3.** Embracing the fallen by the neck,
the Lord weeps, full of compassion.

গদগদ কহে পতিতেরে ।
শুনি যাহা পাষাণ বিদরে ॥

*gadagada kahe patitere |*
*śuni yāhā pāṣāṇa bidare ||*

*Word for word:* gadagada kahe — with faltering voice says; patitere — to the fallen; śuni yāhā — hearing which; pāṣāṇa bidare — stones split

**13.4.** With a faltering voice He speaks to the fallen —
hearing it, stones split apart:[^09-42]

তো সভার ধারি বহু ধার ।
ধর ধর প্রেমের পসার ॥

*to sabhāra dhāri bahu dhāra |*
*dhara dhara premera pasāra ||*

*Word for word:* to sabhāra — to all of you; dhāri bahu dhāra — I owe much (am in debt); dhara dhara — take, take; premera pasāra — the wares of prema

**13.5.** "I owe a great debt to all of you —
take, take the wares of prema!

তো সভার দুর্গতি নাশিব ।
ব্যাজের সহিতে প্রেম দিব ॥

*to sabhāra durgati nāśiba |*
*byājera sahite prema diba ||*

*Word for word:* to sabhāra durgati — your misfortunes; nāśiba — I will destroy; byājera sahite — with interest; prema diba — I will give prema

**13.6.** I will destroy all your misfortunes,
I will give you prema — and with interest besides!"[^09-43]

তারা প্রেমে চাহে মুখ-চাঁদে ।
গলায় ধরিয়া তার কান্দে ॥

*tārā preme cāhe mukha-cām̐de |*
*galāya dhariyā tāra kānde ||*

*Word for word:* tārā preme cāhe — they gaze with love; mukha-cām̐de — at the moonlike face; galāya dhariyā — embracing by the neck; tāra — them; kānde — (He) weeps

**13.7.** With love they gaze at His moonlike face,
and He, embracing them by the neck, weeps.

সে হেন করুণা সোঙরিয়া ।
বাসুঘোষ মরয়ে ঝুরিয়া ॥

*se hena karuṇā soṅariyā |*
*bāsughoṣa maraye jhuriyā ||*

*Word for word:* se hena karuṇā — such mercy; soṅariyā — remembering; bāsughoṣa — Vasu Ghosha; maraye jhuriyā — pines away (dies) weeping

**13.8.** Remembering such mercy,
Vasu Ghosha pines away in tears.

[^09-40]: Signature: "Vasu Ghosha." PK: vol. 3, PDF pp. 308–309 (printed pp. 297–298), 4th shakha, 22nd pallava, no. 22 (mark
"॥২২॥২৩১৫॥"); raga shri; MS P-R-Sa no. 2419. Not found in GPT1 or KGC. Majumdar counts PK 2315 among Vasu's padas on
Nityananda.
[^09-41]: Govinda and Madhava Ghosha, Vasu's brothers, were kirtana singers. According to the *Chaitanya-bhagavata*
(Antya 5) the Ghosha brothers were the singers in Nityananda's kirtanas in Gauda; the pada pictures these kirtanas. MS "k": "ghoṣe" (the same).
[^09-42]: MS "gh": "patitere" (the same).
[^09-43]: MS "k": "tā sabhāra" (the same: "to all of you") instead of "to sabhāra" in 13.5 and 13.6. "With interest" — byāja.

## 14. Vasu Ghosha — "jaya jaya jagannātha śacīra nandana…" (PK 2192)
*Praise of Gaura — Jagannatha, the son of Shachi: in Nilachala He holds the conch, disc, club and lotus, in Nadia the
staff and water pot of a sannyasi; formerly He slew Ravana and manifested the splendour of the pastimes of Goloka, now
in Radha's mood He has come as Gora and preached the name Hare Krishna; He is Gaura, He is Krishna, He is Jagannatha.
In PK it stands in the pallava "Sri Gaurachandra — another mode." Raga tirota.*[^09-44]

জয় জয় জগন্নাথ শচীর নন্দন ।
ত্রিভুবন করে যার চরণ বন্দন ॥

*jaya jaya jagannātha śacīra nandana |*
*tribhubana kare yāra caraṇa bandana ||*

*Word for word:* jaya jaya — glory, glory; jagannātha — to Jagannatha (the Lord of the universe); śacīra nandana — the son of Shachi; tribhubana — the three worlds; kare yāra caraṇa bandana — whose feet worship

**14.1.** Glory, glory to Jagannatha, the son of Shachi,
whose feet the three worlds worship!

নীলাচলে শঙ্খ-চক্র-গদা-পদ্ম-ধর ।
নদীয়ানগরে দণ্ড-কমণ্ডলু-কর ॥

*nīlācale śaṅkha-cakra-gadā-padma-dhara |*
*nadīyānagare daṇḍa-kamaṇḍalu-kara ||*

*Word for word:* nīlācale — in Nilachala; śaṅkha-cakra-gadā-padma-dhara — holding conch, disc, club and lotus; nadīyā-nagare — in the town of Nadia; daṇḍa-kamaṇḍalu-kara — with staff and water pot in hand

**14.2.** In Nilachala He holds the conch, disc, club and lotus,
in the town of Nadia — the staff and water pot in His hands.[^09-45]

কেহো বলে পুরবেতে রাবণ বধিলা ।
গোলোকের বৈভব লীলা প্রকাশ করিলা ॥

*keho bale purabete rābaṇa badhilā |*
*golokera baibhaba līlā prakāśa karilā ||*

*Word for word:* keho bale — some say; purabete — formerly; rābaṇa badhilā — He slew Ravana; golokera baibhaba līlā — the splendid pastimes of Goloka; prakāśa karilā — He manifested

**14.3.** Some say that formerly He slew Ravana;
He manifested the splendour of the pastimes of Goloka.[^09-46]

শ্রীরাধার ভাবে এবে গোরা-অবতার ।
হরেকৃষ্ণ নাম গৌর করিলা প্রচার ॥

*śrīrādhāra bhābe ebe gorā-abatāra |*
*harekṛṣṇa nāma gaura karilā pracāra ||*

*Word for word:* śrī-rādhāra bhābe — in the mood of Sri Radha; ebe — now; gorā-abatāra — the Gora-avatara; hare-kṛṣṇa nāma — the name "Hare Krishna"; gaura karilā pracāra — Gaura preached

**14.4.** And now, in the mood of Sri Radha, He is the Gora-avatara:
Gaura has preached the name "Hare Krishna."[^09-47]

বাসুদেব ঘোষ বলে করি যোড় হাত ।
সেই গৌর সেই কৃষ্ণ সেই জগন্নাথ ॥

*bāsudeba ghoṣa bale kari yoṛa hāta |*
*sei gaura sei kṛṣṇa sei jagannātha ||*

*Word for word:* bāsudeba ghoṣa bale — says Vasudeva Ghosha; kari yoṛa hāta — with folded palms; sei gaura — He is Gaura; sei kṛṣṇa — He is Krishna; sei jagannātha — He is Jagannatha

**14.5.** Vasudeva Ghosha says with folded palms:
He is Gaura, He is Krishna, He is Jagannatha.

[^09-44]: Signature: "Vasudeva Ghosha." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 265 (printed p. 254), 4th shakha, 20th pallava, no. 9 (mark
"॥৯॥২১৯২॥"); raga tirota; MS P-R-Sa no. 2300. GPT1 — p. 4, no. 3 (tirota); GPT2 — sect. 1.2, no. 3. The catalogue listed the
pada twice: VG-001 (from GPT, wrongly linked to PK 2151) and VG-131 (PK 2192, only the ending). Majumdar counts PK 2192
among Vasu's stavas and prarthanas.
[^09-45]: Nilachala is Puri: Jagannatha is the Lord Himself (Vishnu with four emblems); in Nadia He is a sannyasi with a
staff (danda) and water pot (kamandalu).
[^09-46]: Slaying Ravana is Rama's lila; the pastimes of Goloka are Krishna's lila. MSS "k," "kh," "gh," "c": "purube" (the
same: "formerly").
[^09-47]: "The name 'Hare Krishna'" is the maha-mantra "Hare Krishna Hare Krishna Krishna Krishna Hare Hare / Hare Rama Hare
Rama Rama Rama Hare Hare." MS "kh": "ei" instead of "sei" in 14.5; GPT1: "He who is Gaura is Krishna, is Jagannatha" (yei
gaura sei kṛṣṇa).

## 15. Vasu Ghosha — "gaurāṅga nahita ki mene haita…" (PK 2345)
*Had there been no Gauranga, who would have revealed to the world the glory of Radha and the summit of the rasa of
prema, the way into the sweetness of Vrindavana and devotion in the mood of the maidens of Vraja? In the ocean of
worldly existence there is none more merciful than He; the poet reproaches himself for his heart of stone. In PK it
stands in the pallava on the form and virtues of Chaitanya and Nityananda.*[^09-48]

গৌরাঙ্গ নহিত কি মেনে হইত
কেমনে ধরিত দে ।
রাধার মহিমা প্রেম-রস-সীমা
জগতে জানাইত কে ॥

*gaurāṅga nahita ki mene haita*
*kemane dharita de |*
*rādhāra mahimā prema-rasa-sīmā*
*jagate jānāita ke ||*

*Word for word:* gaurāṅga nahita — had there been no Gauranga; ki mene haita — what would have been; kemane dharita de — how would [we] have kept the body (lived); rādhāra mahimā — the glory of Radha; prema-rasa-sīmā — the summit of the rasa of prema; jagate jānāita ke — who would have made known to the world

**15.1.** Had there been no Gauranga, what would have become of us?
How would we have lived?
The glory of Radha, the summit of the rasa of prema —
who would have made it known to the world?[^09-49]

মধুর বৃন্দা- বিপিন-মাধুরি-
প্রবেশ চাতুরি-সার ।
বরজ-যুবতি- ভাবের ভকতি
শকতি হইত কার ॥

*madhura bṛndā- bipina-mādhuri-*
*prabeśa cāturi-sāra |*
*baraja-yubati- bhābera bhakati*
*śakati haita kāra ||*

*Word for word:* madhura bṛndā-bipina-mādhuri — the sweetness of the sweet forest of Vrinda; prabeśa cāturi-sāra — the essence of the art of entering; baraja-yubati-bhābera bhakati — devotion in the mood of the young maidens of Vraja; śakati haita kāra — who would have had the power

**15.2.** The very essence of the art of entering
the sweetness of the sweet forest of Vrinda,
devotion in the mood of the young maidens of Vraja —
who would have had the power for it?[^09-50]

গাও পুন পুন গৌরাঙ্গের গুণ
সরল হইলা মন ।
এ ভব-সাগরে এমন দয়াল
না দেখিয়ে এক জন ॥

*gāo puna puna gaurāṅgera guṇa*
*sarala hailā mana |*
*e bhaba-sāgare emana dayāla*
*nā dekhiye eka jana ||*

*Word for word:* gāo puna puna — sing again and again; gaurāṅgera guṇa — Gauranga's virtues; sarala hailā mana — O mind, becoming simple; e bhaba-sāgare — in this ocean of worldly existence; emana dayāla — one so merciful; nā dekhiye eka jana — not one is seen

**15.3.** Sing then again and again of Gauranga's virtues,
O my mind, becoming simple!
In this ocean of worldly existence one so merciful
is not to be found — not one.

গৌরাঙ্গ বলিয়া না গেল গলিয়া
কেমনে ধরিল দে ।
বাসুর হিয়া পাষাণ দিয়া
কেমনে গড়িয়াছে ॥

*gaurāṅga baliyā nā gela galiyā*
*kemane dharila de |*
*bāsura hiyā pāṣāṇa diyā*
*kemane gaṛiyāche ||*

*Word for word:* gaurāṅga baliyā — saying "Gauranga"; nā gela galiyā — did not melt; kemane dharila de — how does he keep the body (live); bāsura hiyā — Vasu's heart; pāṣāṇa diyā — of stone; kemane gaṛiyāche — how have they fashioned

**15.4.** Saying "Gauranga," he has not melted —
how does he still live?
Surely of stone they have fashioned
the heart of Vasu![^09-51]

[^09-48]: Signature: "Vasu." PK: vol. 3, PDF pp. 319–320 (printed pp. 308–309), 4th shakha, 23rd pallava ("Description of
the form and virtues of Sri Chaitanya and Nityananda"), no. 14 (mark "॥১৪॥২৩৪৫॥"); "tathā rāga"; MS P-R-Sa no. 2449. Majumdar
counts PK 2345 among Vasu's stavas and prarthanas. In GPT1 (pp. 12–13, no. 30, raga vibhasa) and GPT2 (sect. 1.2, no. 30)
it bears the signature "Narahari" and ends in the first person: "Saying 'Gauranga,' I have not melted — how do I still
live? Surely of stone they have fashioned the heart of Narahari" (in the catalogue — NG-002). The attribution is
disputed: PK (and MS P-R-Sa) give Vasu, GPT gives Narahari.
[^09-49]: "How would we have lived" — literally "how would [we] have kept the body" (kemane dharita de). MSS "k," "gh": "kemane"
instead of "ki mene" ("how would it have been"); "kh": "ki mane" (the same); GPT: "tabe ki haita" ("what then would have been").
Cf. CC Adi 3–4: the Lord came to taste Radha's prema and to give the world raganuga-bhakti.
[^09-50]: "The maidens of Vraja" are the gopis. Devotion in their mood (raganuga-bhakti) the Lord gave the world through
Rupa, Sanatana and His other companions.
[^09-51]: MS P-R-Sa: "becoming simple" — haiyā (the same; the main text has hailā).

## 16. Vasu Ghosha — "gaurāṅga tumi more dayā nā chāṛiha…" (PK 3007)
*A prarthana to Gauranga: "Do not withdraw Your mercy from me, keep me at Your reddish feet; for them I have left
everything and bidden farewell to kin on both sides; give me the shade of Your feet." In PK it is the section "prayer
again," on Sri Gaurachandra. Raga shri.*[^09-52]

গৌরাঙ্গ তুমি মোরে দয়া না ছাড়িহ ।
আপন করিয়া রাঙ্গা চরণে রাখিহ ॥

*gaurāṅga tumi more dayā nā chāṛiha |*
*āpana kariyā rāṅgā caraṇe rākhiha ||*

*Word for word:* gaurāṅga tumi — Gauranga, You; more — me; dayā nā chāṛiha — do not withdraw mercy; āpana kariyā — making Your own; rāṅgā caraṇe — at the reddish feet; rākhiha — keep

**16.1.** Gauranga, do not withdraw Your mercy from me;
making me Your own, keep me at Your reddish feet.

তোমার চরণ লাগি সব তেয়াগিলুঁ ।
শীতল চরণ পাঞা শরণ লইলুঁ ॥

*tomāra caraṇa lāgi saba teyāgilum̐ |*
*śītala caraṇa pāñā śaraṇa lailum̐ ||*

*Word for word:* tomāra caraṇa lāgi — for the sake of Your feet; saba teyāgilum̐ — I have left everything; śītala caraṇa pāñā — finding the cool feet; śaraṇa lailum̐ — I have taken shelter

**16.2.** For the sake of Your feet I have left everything;
finding Your cool feet, I have taken shelter in them.

এ কুলে ও কুলে মুঞি দিলুঁ তিলাঞ্জলি ।
রাখিহ চরণে মোরে আপনার বলি ॥

*e kule o kule muñi dilum̐ tilāñjali |*
*rākhiha caraṇe more āpanāra bali ||*

*Word for word:* e kule o kule — to this kin and that (this shore and that); muñi dilum̐ tilāñjali — I have given tilanjali (bidden farewell forever); rākhiha caraṇe more — keep me at Your feet; āpanāra bali — calling me Your own

**16.3.** To this kin and to that I have bidden farewell forever —
keep me at Your feet, calling me Your own.[^09-53]

বাসুদেব ঘোষে বলে চরণে ধরিয়া ।
কৃপা করি রাখ মোরে পদ-ছায়া দিয়া ॥

*bāsudeba ghoṣe bale caraṇe dhariyā |*
*kṛpā kari rākha more pada-chāyā diyā ||*

*Word for word:* bāsudeba ghoṣe bale — says Vasudeva Ghosha; caraṇe dhariyā — clasping the feet; kṛpā kari — in mercy; rākha more — keep me; pada-chāyā diyā — giving the shade of Your feet

**16.4.** Vasudeva Ghosha says, clasping Your feet:
in Your mercy, shelter me in the shade of Your feet.

[^09-52]: Signature: "Vasudeva Ghosha." PK: vol. 4, PDF p. 233 (printed p. 224), 4th shakha, 36th pallava, section "punaḥ
prārthanā । tatra śrīgauracandraḥ," no. 23 (mark "॥২৩॥৩০০৭॥"); raga shri; MS P-R-Sa no. 2516. Not found in GPT1, GPT2 or KGC.
Majumdar counts PK 3007 among Vasu's stavas and prarthanas. MS "k": "You will not withdraw… You will keep" (chāṛibe,
rākhibe).
[^09-53]: "To this kin and to that" (e kule o kule) — to family and to the world, to this shore and to that: to all worldly and
heavenly hopes. "Bidden farewell forever" — literally "given tilanjali" (the funeral offering of water with sesame).

## 17. Vasu Ghosha — "āre mora gaurāṅga soṇā…" (PK 3008)
*A prarthana to Gauranga: "O my gold, Gauranga, how much I prayed — and found You; I have no one of my own — keep me at
Your feet; give the nectar of prema and the shade of Your cool feet to one tormented." In PK it is the next pada of
the same section. Raga shri.*[^09-54]

আরে মোর গৌরাঙ্গ সোণা ।
পাইয়াছি তোমারে কত করিয়া কামনা ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*āre mora gaurāṅga soṇā |*
*pāiyāchi tomāre kata kariyā kāmanā || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* āre mora — O my; gaurāṅga soṇā — Gauranga, gold; pāiyāchi tomāre — I have found You; kata kariyā kāmanā — after so much longing

**17.1.** *(Refrain)* O my Gauranga, my gold!
How much I prayed — and I have found You.

আপনা বলিয়া মোর নাহি কোন জনা ।
রাখিহ চরণ-তলে করিয়া আপনা ॥

*āpanā baliyā mora nāhi kona janā |*
*rākhiha caraṇa-tale kariyā āpanā ||*

*Word for word:* āpanā baliyā — to call my own; mora nāhi kona janā — I have no one; rākhiha caraṇa-tale — keep beneath Your feet; kariyā āpanā — making me Your own

**17.2.** I can call no one my own —
keep me beneath Your feet, making me Your own.[^09-55]

তোমার বদন কিবা চাঁদের তুলনা ।
দেহ প্রেম-সুধা-রস রহুক ঘোষণা ॥

*tomāra badana kibā cām̐dera tulanā |*
*deha prema-sudhā-rasa rahuka ghoṣaṇā ||*

*Word for word:* tomāra badana — Your face; kibā cām̐dera tulanā — what but the moon to compare it with; deha prema-sudhā-rasa — give the nectar-rasa of prema; rahuka ghoṣaṇā — let it be proclaimed

**17.3.** Your face — with what can it be compared? Only with the moon.
Give the nectar-rasa of prema, and let it be proclaimed abroad.[^09-56]

কমল জিনিয়া তোমার শীতল চরণ ।
বাসুঘোষে দেহ ছায়া এ তাপিত জন ॥

*kamala jiniyā tomāra śītala caraṇa |*
*bāsughoṣe deha chāyā e tāpita jana ||*

*Word for word:* kamala jiniyā — surpassing the lotus; tomāra śītala caraṇa — Your cool feet; bāsughoṣe deha chāyā — give shade to Vasu Ghosha; e tāpita jana — this one tormented by heat

**17.4.** Cooler than the lotus are Your feet —
give their shade, then, to Vasu Ghosha, tormented by the heat.

"॥২৪॥৩০০৮॥"); MS P-R-Sa no. 2517. Not found in GPT1, GPT2 or KGC. Majumdar counts PK 3008 among Vasu's stavas and
prarthanas.
[^09-55]: MS "kh": "balite" (the same: "to call"); "k": "rākhaha" (the same).
[^09-56]: "Let it be proclaimed abroad" (rahuka ghoṣaṇā) — let all the world know of Your mercy to the unworthy.

# Chapter 10. Nayanananda and Balarama Dasa: the Gaura-avatara, the Kirtanas of Navadvipa, Gaura and Gadadhara, Shantipura

*Padas of Nayanananda (Nayana Mishra), the nephew and disciple of Gadadhara Pandita, and padas signed by Balarama Dasa,
in the order of the lilas: praise of the Gaura-avatara; the kirtanas of Navadvipa, where Gaura dances beside
Gadadhara; Gauranga's form; His bhava — the Lord weeps gazing at Gadadhara's face; a spring night on the Ganga and the spring swing; Shantipura after
the sannyasa and the departure for Nilachala; Nityananda in Gauda. Majumdar counts Nayanananda among the Lord's
contemporaries: like his other padas, the pada on Gaura and Gadadhara ("premera gṛhiṇī se paṇḍita gadādhare") is cited
by Narahari Chakravarti in the *Bhakti-ratnakara* as testimony; for Balarama Dasa Majumdar accepts three padas from the
*Bhakti-ratnakara* (many padas of a later Balarama Dasa bear the same signature, so the attribution of the rest is
doubtful). The text follows the *Padakalpataru* (PK), checked against the scans, with the manuscript variants from PK's
apparatus, the *Bhakti-ratnakara* (BR), the *Gaura-pada-tarangini* (GPT1 — 1st ed., 1903; GPT2 — 2nd ed., 1934) and the
*Kshanada-gita-chintamani* (KGC); the Bengali original, variants and word-for-word translation are in the full version of the book.*

## 1. Balarama Dasa — "kaliyuga-matta-mataṅgaja-maradane…" (PK 617)
*Praise of the Gaura-avatara: the age of Kali is a mad elephant, Gaura is the king of lions who has appeared in the
mountain cave of Navadvipa; at the roar of sankirtana sins and the mystic perfections flee, and on the wretched He
hangs necklaces of the pearls of the holy name. The gaura-chandrika at the opening of PK's 3rd shakha. Raga kamoda.*[^10-1]

কলিযুগ-মত্ত-মতঙ্গজ-মরদনে
কুমতি-করিণি দুর গেল ।
পামর দুরগত নাম-মোতি শত-
দাম কণ্ঠ ভরি দেল ॥

*kaliyuga-matta-mataṅgaja-maradane*
*kumati-kariṇi dura gela |*
*pāmara duragata nāma-moti śata-*
*dāma kaṇṭha bhari dela ||*

*Word for word:* kaliyuga — of the Kali age; matta-mataṅgaja — of the mad elephant; maradane — at the crushing; kumati-kariṇi — the she-elephant of evil thinking; dura gela — went far away; pāmara — to the low; duragata — to the wretched; nāma-moti — pearls of the Name; śata-dāma — a hundred-stranded necklace; kaṇṭha bhari — filling the neck; dela — gave (put on)

**1.1.** When the mad elephant of the Kali age was crushed,
the she-elephant of evil thinking fled far away;
on the low and the wretched He hung, as much as their necks would hold,
hundred-stranded necklaces of the pearls of the Name.[^10-2]

অপরূপ গৌর বিরাজ ।
শ্রীনবদ্বীপ-নগর-গিরি-কন্দরে
উয়ল কেশরি-রাজ ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*aparūpa gaura birāja |*
*śrīnabadvīpa-nagara-giri-kandare*
*uyala keśari-rāja || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* aparūpa — wondrously; gaura — Gaura; birāja — shines; śrī-nabadvīpa-nagara — of the city of Sri Navadvipa; giri-kandare — in the mountain cave; uyala — has risen; keśari-rāja — the king of lions

**1.2.** *(Refrain)* Wondrously shines Gaura:
in the mountain cave of the city of Sri Navadvipa
the king of lions has risen!

সংকীর্ত্তন-রণ হুঙ্কৃতি শুনইতে
দুরিত দীপি-গণ ভাগি ।
ভয়ে আকুল অণিমাদি মৃগীকুল
পুণবত গরব তেয়াগি ॥

*saṃkīrttana-raṇa huṅkṛti śunaite*
*durita dīpi-gaṇa bhāgi |*
*bhaye ākula aṇimādi mṛgīkula*
*puṇabata garaba teyāgi ||*

*Word for word:* saṅkīrttana-raṇa — the battle (cry) of sankirtana; huṅkṛti — the roar; śunaite — on hearing; durita — the sins; dīpi-gaṇa — the leopards; bhāgi — flee; bhaye ākula — frantic with fear; aṇimādi — anima and the rest (the perfections); mṛgīkula — the herd of does; puṇabata — (merits?, the word is unclear); garaba — the pride; teyāgi — abandoning

**1.3.** Hearing the battle roar of sankirtana,
the leopards — the sins — run away;
the does — anima and the other perfections — are frantic with fear,
abandoning the pride of their merits.[^10-3]

ত্যাগ যাগ যম তিরিথি বরত সম
শশ জম্বুকি জরি যাতি ।
বলরাম দাস কহ অতয়ে সে জগ মাহ
হরি-ধনি শবদ খেয়াতি ॥

*tyāga yāga yama tirithi barata sama*
*śaśa jambuki jari yāti |*
*balarāma dāsa kaha ataye se jaga māha*
*hari-dhani śabada kheyāti ||*

*Word for word:* tyāga — renunciation; yāga — sacrifices; yama — the vows of yama; tirithi — pilgrimages; barata — fasts (vows); sama — like; śaśa — hares; jambuki — jackals; jari — scorched; yāti — flee; balarāma dāsa kaha — Balarama Dasa says; ataye — therefore; se — that; jaga māha — in the world; hari-dhani śabada — the sound of Hari's name; kheyāti — is renowned

**1.4.** Renunciation, sacrifices, the vows of yama, pilgrimages, fasts —
like hares and jackals they flee as if scorched.
Balarama Dasa says: that is why in the world
only the sound of Hari's name is renowned.[^10-4]

[^10-1]: Signature: "Balarama Dasa." PK: vol. 2, PDF p. 14 (printed p. 1), opening of the 3rd shakha, section "śrīgauracandra"
(gaura-chandrika), no. 1 (label "॥১॥৬১৭॥"); raga kamoda; P-R-Sa MS no. 1091. GPT1 — p. 25, no. 1 (kamoda). The catalogue's link
to the *Bhakti-ratnakara* (BR p. 901) is mistaken: there it is a different pada signed by Narahari — "bali-kali-matta-mataṅgaja-maradana
gaurasiṃha nācata nadīyāya". The pada is in elaborate Vrajabuli; which of the Balarama Dasas wrote it is not established.
[^10-2]: MS "ka": "the elephant (like) Yama"; P-R-Sa: "mataṅgajamabadane" (corrupt). GPT1 in a note: "the elephant's roar." MSS "ka",
"ca": "far" (dūra). MS "ka": "pearl" (motima); so also GPT1. "Hundred-stranded necklaces" — śata-dāma, a necklace of many strands.
[^10-3]: Anima (the power of becoming minute) and the other eight siddhis are the mystic perfections of yoga; before
sankirtana they lose their worth, like does before a lion. The word "puṇabata" (here "merits," from puṇya) is unclear; MS
"ka" has "pumabata," "kha," "gha," "ca" "pumarata," P-R-Sa "patharata." MSS "ka," "kha," "ca," P-R-Sa: "islands" (dvīpagaṇa) instead of
"leopards" (dīpigaṇa); MSS "ka," "gha," "ca": "forest" (bana), "kha": "in the forest" instead of "battle" (raṇa).
[^10-4]: MS "ca": "like" (sama); MS "ka": "moon" (śaśi) instead of "hare." MSS "ka," "ca": "Hari" instead of "sound" (dhani). The
thought: nama-sankirtana is the dharma of the age of Kali (cf. CC Adi 3, 17), and all other means give way before it.

## 2. Balarama Dasa — "baṛa abatāra bhāi baṛa abatāra…" (PK 2207 = BR p. 956)
*The great incarnation: Gaura distributes the storehouse of prema to the fallen; women of noble families dance in the
sankirtana; the one whom all drove away as untouchable is now the one whose foot-dust the gods beg for; even yavanas
sing the holy name. Raga shri (BR — dhanashi).*[^10-5]

বড় অবতার ভাই বড় অবতার ।
পতিতেরে বিলাওল প্রেমের ভাণ্ডার ॥

*baṛa abatāra bhāi baṛa abatāra |*
*patitere bilāola premera bhāṇḍāra ||*

*Word for word:* baṛa abatāra — a great incarnation; bhāi — brothers; patitere — to the fallen; bilāola — gave away; premera bhāṇḍāra — the storehouse of prema

**2.1.** A great incarnation, brothers, a great incarnation!
To the fallen He has given away the storehouse of prema.

বড় অপরূপ গোরাচাঁদের লীলা ।
রাজা হৈয়া কান্ধে করে বৈষ্ণবের দোলা ॥

*baṛa aparūpa gorācām̐dera līlā |*
*rājā haiyā kāndhe kare baiṣṇabera dolā ||*

*Word for word:* baṛa aparūpa — how wondrous; gorācām̐dera līlā — Gorachand's pastimes; rājā haiyā — being a king; kāndhe kare — holds on the shoulder; baiṣṇabera dolā — a Vaishnava's palanquin

**2.2.** How wondrous are Gorachand's pastimes:
a king — and he carries a Vaishnava's palanquin on his shoulder![^10-6]

হেন অবতারের উপমা দিতে নারি ।
সংকীর্ত্তন মাঝে নাচে কুলের বৌহারী ॥

*hena abatārera upamā dite nāri |*
*saṃkīrttana mājhe nāce kulera bauhārī ||*

*Word for word:* hena abatārera — for such an incarnation; upamā dite nāri — I cannot give a likeness; saṅkīrttana mājhe — amid the sankirtana; nāce — dance; kulera bauhārī — the wives (and daughters) of noble families

**2.3.** No likeness can be found for such an incarnation:
amid the sankirtana the wives of noble families dance.[^10-7]

সর্ব্ব লোক ছাড়ে যারে অপরশ বলি ।
দেবগণ মাগে এবে তার পদধূলি ॥

*sarvva loka chāṛe yāre aparaśa bali |*
*debagaṇa māge ebe tāra padadhūli ||*

*Word for word:* sarva loka — all people; chāṛe — shun; yāre — whom; aparaśa bali — calling him "untouchable"; debagaṇa — the gods; māge — beg; ebe — now; tāra padadhūli — the dust of his feet

**2.4.** The one whom everyone shunned, saying, "Do not touch!" —
from him the gods now beg the dust of his feet.

যবনেহ নাচে গায় লয় হরিনাম ।
হেন অবতারে সে বঞ্চিত বলরাম ॥

*yabaneha nāce gāya laya harināma |*
*hena abatāre se bañcita balarāma ||*

*Word for word:* yabaneha — even the yavanas; nāce gāya — dance, sing; laya harināma — take Hari's name; hena abatāre — in such an incarnation; se — he; bañcita — deprived; balarāma — Balarama

**2.5.** Even yavanas dance, sing and take the name of Hari —
yet in such an incarnation Balarama is left out.[^10-8]

prakārāntara," no. 24 (label "॥২৪॥২২০৭॥"); raga shri; P-R-Sa MS no. 2315, P-R 9.15. BR, 12th wave (1913 ed., pp. 956–957, "punardhānaśī"):
the pada is sung within the account of Navadvipa. Majumdar cites it among the BR testimonies of Balarama Dasa (the detail of
the noble wives dancing in the sankirtana is new). The catalogue had assigned it to PK 2208, which is a pada of Ananta Dasa.
GPT2 — sec. 1.3, no. 36.
[^10-6]: Who this "king" is, the pada does not say: perhaps the Lord Himself, the King of all, who serves His devotees, or a king
(Prataparudra) humbly serving the Vaishnavas. BR: "a Vaishnava's bag (jholā)" instead of "palanquin (dolā)"; MS P-R: "bears"
(bahe) instead of "holds."
[^10-7]: MS P-R: "in sankirtana people dance, having abandoned all (other) dharmas." BR: "nāpi" (corrupt), "bom̐hāri."
[^10-8]: BR: "all people" (saba loka) instead of "sarvva loka." A yavana is a non-Hindu (a Muslim); cf. the conversion of Chand Kazi
(CB Madhya 23; CC Adi 17).

## 3. Nayanananda — "jaya re jaya re gorā śrīśacī-nandana…" (PK 2)
*Glory to Gora, the son of Shachi, dancing His auspicious dance: Srivasa, Ramananda, Mukunda and Vasu sing; the
mridanga and the mandiras resound; one anoints Gora with sandal paste, another puts on Him a malati garland; some call
Him Rama, others the Kandarpa dear to Radha, but the poet knows only this: He is Gadadhara's life. A mangalacharana —
the second pada of PK. Raga kamoda.*[^10-9]

জয় রে জয় রে গোরা শ্রীশচী-নন্দন
মঙ্গল নটন সুঠান রে ।
কীর্ত্তন-আনন্দে শ্রীবাস রামানন্দে
মুকুন্দ বাসু গুণ-গান রে ॥

*jaya re jaya re gorā śrīśacī-nandana*
*maṅgala naṭana suṭhāna re |*
*kīrttana-ānande śrībāsa rāmānande*
*mukunda bāsu guṇa-gāna re ||*

*Word for word:* jaya re jaya re — glory, glory; gorā — to Gora; śrī-śacī-nandana — the son of Sri Shachi; maṅgala naṭana — in the auspicious dance; suṭhāna — beautiful; re — (refrain particle); kīrttana-ānande — in the bliss of kirtana; śrībāsa rāmānande — Srivasa and Ramananda; mukunda bāsu — Mukunda and Vasu; guṇa-gāna — sing His virtues

**3.1.** Glory, glory to Gora, the son of Sri Shachi,
beautiful in His auspicious dance!
In the bliss of kirtana Srivasa and Ramananda,
Mukunda and Vasu sing His virtues.[^10-10]

দাং দ্রিমিকি দ্রিমি মাদল বাজত
মধুর মঞ্জীর রসাল রে ।
শঙ্খ করতাল ঘণ্টারব ভেল
মিলল পদতলে তাল রে ॥

*dāṃ drimiki drimi mādala bājata*
*madhura mañjīra rasāla re |*
*śaṅkha karatāla ghaṇṭāraba bhela*
*milala padatale tāla re ||*

*Word for word:* dāṃ drimiki drimi — (the sound of the madal); mādala bājata — the madal sounds; madhura — sweetly; mañjīra — the mandiras (small cymbals); rasāla — ring delightfully; śaṅkha — conch; karatāla — karatalas; ghaṇṭāraba — the ringing of bells; bhela — arises; milala — blended; padatale tāla — with the rhythm of the feet

**3.2.** "Dang drimiki drimi" — the madal sounds,
the mandiras ring sweetly,
conch, karatalas and bells resound,
blending with the rhythm of His feet.[^10-11]

কো দেই গোরা-অঙ্গে সুগন্ধি চন্দন
কো দেই মালতী-মাল রে ।
পিরিতি-ফুল-শরে মরম ভেদল
ভাবে সহচর ভোর রে ॥

*ko dei gorā-aṅge sugandhi candana*
*ko dei mālatī-māla re |*
*piriti-phula-śare marama bhedala*
*bhābe sahacara bhora re ||*

*Word for word:* ko dei — one applies; gorā-aṅge — to Gora's body; sugandhi candana — fragrant sandal paste; ko dei — one puts on; mālatī-māla — a malati garland; piriti-phula-śare — by the flower-arrow of love; marama bhedala — the heart is pierced; bhābe — in bhava; sahacara — the companions; bhora — are lost

**3.3.** One anoints Gora's body with fragrant sandal paste,
another puts on Him a malati garland;
pierced to the heart by the flower-arrow of love,
the companions are lost in bhava.[^10-12]

কোই বোলে গোরা জানকী-বল্লভ
রাধার প্রিয় পাঁচবাণ রে ।
নয়নানন্দ মনে আন নাহি জানে
আমারি গদাধরের প্রাণ রে ॥

*koi bole gorā jānakī-ballabha*
*rādhāra priya pām̐cabāṇa re |*
*nayanānanda mane āna nāhi jāne*
*āmāri gadādharera prāṇa re ||*

*Word for word:* koi bole — some say; gorā — Gora; jānakī-ballabha — the beloved of Janaki (Rama); rādhāra priya — dear to Radha; pām̐cabāṇa — the Five-arrowed One (Kandarpa); nayanānanda mane — in Nayanananda's heart (mind); āna nāhi jāne — knows nothing else; āmāri gadādharera prāṇa — the life of my Gadadhara

**3.4.** Some say Gora is the beloved of Janaki,
others — the Five-arrowed One dear to Radha;
Nayanananda's heart knows nothing else:
He is the life of my Gadadhara.[^10-13]

[^10-9]: Signature: "Nayanananda." PK: vol. 1, PDF p. 13 (printed p. 2), 1st shakha, 1st pallava (mangalacharana), no. 2 (label
"॥২॥"); raga kamoda; P-R-Sa MS no. 1, P-R 1.3 and 38.1 (raga "kamoda-mallara," P-R "mallara"). KGC — 30th kshanada (purnima),
no. 1, gaura-chandrika (kedara); GPT1 — p. 4, no. 4 (kedara or mangala); GPT2 — sec. 1.2, no. 4. The catalogue gave the PK
number as "45" (PK 45 is a pada of Radhamohana on Radha's purvaraga).
[^10-10]: MS P-R: "suṭhāna re," "guṇa-gāna re" (with the refrain particle "re"); KGC lacks "re." Srivasa is the master of the
house where the night kirtanas of Navadvipa were held; Ramananda here is probably Vasu Ramananda; Mukunda is the singer
Mukunda Datta; Vasu is Vasudeva (Vasu) Ghosha.
[^10-11]: The syllables imitate the madal (mridanga): MSS "ka," "kha," "gha," "ca": "dāṃ drimiki drimi drimi"; P-R-Sa: "tā drimi ki
drimi"; P-R 1.3: "drimiki drimiki drimi"; P-R 38.1: "dāṃ drimi drimi," "mandirā"; KGC: "drāṃ drimiki drimi." Mandiras are
small cymbals.
[^10-12]: In the PK scan the epithet of the sandal paste is partly illegible; "fragrant" (sugandhi) follows KGC and GPT1. MS P-R
38.1: "One anoints Gora's body with sandal paste, (one offers) fragrant karabira," "kora re" instead of "bhora re." MSS "kha,"
"gha," "ca," P-R, P-R-Sa: "the (female) companions" (sahacari). The flower-arrow is Kamadeva's weapon; here it is the hearts pierced
by love for the Lord.
[^10-13]: MSS "kha," "gha," P-R, P-R-Sa: "say" (bale); "ka": "says" (kahata), so also KGC. The beloved of Janaki (Sita) is Rama. The
Five-arrowed One is Kamadeva; "the Five-arrowed One dear to Radha" is Krishna as the transcendental Madana (aprakrita-madana,
CC Madhya 8), not the worldly god of desire. Gadadhara Pandita, according to the *Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika*, is a manifestation
of Radha; Nayanananda calls Gaura the life of his Gadadhara. MSS "ka," P-R-Sa: "āmāra"; P-R: "hāmāri."

## 4. Balarama Dasa — "bhāla raṅge nāce mora śacīra dulāla…" (BR p. 837)
*Gaura dances in the kirtana of Navadvipa: sandal paste all over His body, His garland swaying, pearls on His chest,
His ankle bells ringing; the kinnaras learn singing from Him, the gandharvas contemplate His dance; the lotuses shrink
before His eyes. Raga dhanashi.*[^10-14]

ভাল রঙ্গে নাচে মোর শচীর দুলাল ।
সব অঙ্গে চন্দন দোলয়ে বনমাল ॥

*bhāla raṅge nāce mora śacīra dulāla |*
*saba aṅge candana dolaye banamāla ||*

*Word for word:* bhāla raṅge — beautifully, joyfully; nāce — dances; mora — my; śacīra dulāla — Shachi's darling; saba aṅge — on all the body; candana — sandal paste; dolaye — sways; banamāla — the garland

**4.1.** How beautifully my darling of Shachi dances!
Sandal paste over all His body, His garland swaying.

বিশাল হৃদয়ে গজমুকুতার হার ।
পদতলে তাল উঠে নূপুর-ঝঙ্কার ॥

*biśāla hṛdaye gajamukutāra hāra |*
*padatale tāla uṭhe nūpura-jhaṅkāra ||*

*Word for word:* biśāla hṛdaye — on the broad chest; gaja-mukutāra hāra — a necklace of "elephant" pearls; padatale — beneath the feet; tāla uṭhe — the rhythm rises; nūpura-jhaṅkāra — the ringing of the ankle bells

**4.2.** On His broad chest is a necklace of "elephant" pearls,
to the rhythm of His feet the ankle bells ring out.[^10-15]

ছন্দ-বিছন্দে কত জানে অঙ্গভঙ্গি ।
নদীয়া-নগরে নাই এত বড় রঙ্গী ॥

*chanda-bichande kata jāne aṅgabhaṅgi |*
*nadīyā-nagare nāi eta baṛa raṅgī ||*

*Word for word:* chanda-bichande — in measure and out of measure; kata — how many; jāne — He knows; aṅga-bhaṅgi — bends of the body; nadīyā-nagare — in the city of Nadia; nāi — there is not; eta baṛa raṅgī — so great an artist (merrymaker)

**4.3.** How many bends of the body He knows, in measure and out of measure —
in all the city of Nadia there is no such artist![^10-16]

কিন্নর করয়ে শিক্ষা শুনি মৃদু গান ।
গন্ধর্ব্ব তাণ্ডব হেরি ধরয়ে ধিয়ান ॥

*kinnara karaye śikṣā śuni mṛdu gāna |*
*gandharvva tāṇḍaba heri dharaye dhiyāna ||*

*Word for word:* kinnara — the kinnaras; karaye śikṣā — learn; śuni — hearing; mṛdu gāna — the soft singing; gandharva — the gandharvas; tāṇḍaba heri — seeing the tandava; dharaye dhiyāna — sink into meditation

**4.4.** The kinnaras learn from hearing His soft singing,
the gandharvas, seeing His tandava, sink into meditation.[^10-17]

পঙ্কজ সঙ্কোচ পায় দেখিয়া নয়নে ।
হাসিতে বিজুরি-ছটা পড়য়ে দশনে ॥

*paṅkaja saṅkoca pāya dekhiyā nayane |*
*hāsite bijuri-chaṭā paṛaye daśane ||*

*Word for word:* paṅkaja — the lotus; saṅkoca pāya — shrinks; dekhiyā nayane — seeing (His) eyes; hāsite — when He smiles; bijuri-chaṭā — the radiance of lightning; paṛaye daśane — falls from His teeth

**4.5.** The lotus shrinks on seeing His eyes,
when He smiles, His teeth shed the radiance of lightning.

বান্ধুলি জিনিয়া রাঙা ওটখানি হাস ।
ও-রূপ হেরিয়া কান্দে বলরাম দাস ॥

*bāndhuli jiniyā rāṅā oṭakhāni hāsa |*
*o-rūpa heriyā kānde balarāma dāsa ||*

*Word for word:* bāndhuli jiniyā — surpassing the bandhuli flower; rāṅā — red; oṭakhāni — the lips; hāsa — the smile; o-rūpa heriyā — gazing at that form; kānde — weeps; balarāma dāsa — Balarama Dasa

**4.6.** His lips are redder than the bandhuli flower — and that smile!
Gazing at this form, Balarama Dasa weeps.[^10-18]

[^10-14]: Signature: "Balarama Dasa." BR, 12th wave: 1913 ed. (Murshidabad), pp. 837–838 ("gīte yathā — dhānaśī"); 1960 ed., vv.
1884–1889. The pada is not in PK or GPT1. In Narahari Chakravarti it is sung in the account of the path by which the Lord went
with kirtana from Srivasa's house to the Ganga and back; Majumdar cites it among the three BR padas of Balarama Dasa.
[^10-15]: Gaja-mukta is the pearl believed to be born in an elephant's head — the finest pearl. 1913 ed.: "jhañcāra," 1960 ed.: "jhaṅkāra"
(ringing).
[^10-16]: Chhanda-bichhanda — dancing in measure and with departures from it (syncopations).
[^10-17]: The kinnaras and gandharvas are celestial singers and musicians. Tandava is the vigorous male dance.
[^10-18]: Bandhuli (bandhuka) is a bright red flower. "oṭakhāni" — "the lips" (oṭha, oṣṭha); 1913 ed.: "…oṭakhāni hāma" (corrupt), 1960 ed.:
"oṭakhāni hāsa."

## 5. Balarama Dasa — "hari hari maṅgala bharala khiti-maṇḍala…" (PK 2065)
*Gaura dances, spreading through the world the storehouse of rasa — the kirtana of His own virtues; His form robs
