Manmatha of his senses; the Name that Shiva and Brahma seek in the depths of the heart He strings into a necklace and
gives to the fallen. Raga mangala.*[^10-19]

হরি হরি মঙ্গল ভরল খিতি-মণ্ডল
রসময় রতন-পসার ।
নিজ গুণ-কীর্ত্তন প্রেম-রতন ধন
অনুখণ করু পরচার ॥

*hari hari maṅgala bharala khiti-maṇḍala*
*rasamaya ratana-pasāra |*
*nija guṇa-kīrttana prema-ratana dhana*
*anukhaṇa karu paracāra ||*

*Word for word:* hari hari — Hari, Hari; maṅgala — with blessing; bharala — is filled; khiti-maṇḍala — the circle of the earth; rasamaya — full of rasa; ratana-pasāra — a shop of treasures; nija guṇa-kīrttana — the kirtana of His own virtues; prema-ratana dhana — the wealth of the jewel of prema; anukhaṇa — ceaselessly; karu paracāra — He spreads abroad

**5.1.** Hari, Hari! The circle of the earth is filled with blessing —
a shop of the treasures of rasa has opened:
the kirtana of His own virtues, the jewel of prema
He ceaselessly spreads abroad.

নাচত নটবর গৌর কিশোর ।
অনুখণ ভাবে বিভাবিত অন্তর
প্রেম-সুখের নাহি ওর ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*nācata naṭabara gaura kiśora |*
*anukhaṇa bhābe bibhābita antara*
*prema-sukhera nāhi ora || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* nācata — dances; naṭabara — the skilful dancer; gaura kiśora — youthful Gaura; anukhaṇa — ceaselessly; bhābe bibhābita — stirred by bhava; antara — the heart; prema-sukhera — to the joy of prema; nāhi ora — there is no end

**5.2.** *(Refrain)* The skilful dancer, youthful Gaura, dances;
His heart is ceaselessly stirred by bhava,
there is no end to the joy of prema.

কুন্দন-কনয়-বিরাজিত কলেবর
বিহি সে করল নিরমাণ ।
মনমথ মুরছিত অঙ্গহি অঙ্গ কত
রূপ দেখি হরল গেয়ান ॥

*kundana-kanaya-birājita kalebara*
*bihi se karala niramāṇa |*
*manamatha murachita aṅgahi aṅga kata*
*rūpa dekhi harala geyāna ||*

*Word for word:* kundana-kanaya — like pure gold; birājita — shining; kalebara — the body; bihi — the Creator; se — it; karala niramāṇa — fashioned; manamatha — Manmatha (Kamadeva); murachita — fainted; aṅgahi aṅga — in every limb; kata rūpa — so much beauty; dekhi — seeing; harala geyāna — lost his wits

**5.3.** That body, shining like pure gold —
it is the Creator who fashioned it![^10-20]
Manmatha has fainted: in every limb there is such
beauty that, seeing it, he has lost his wits.

যা কর ভজন শিব চতুরানন
করু মন-মরম সন্ধান ।
হেন নাম-হার যতন করি গাঁথই
পতিত জনেরে করে দান ॥

*yā kara bhajana śiba caturānana*
*karu mana-marama sandhāna |*
*hena nāma-hāra yatana kari gām̐thai*
*patita janere kare dāna ||*

*Word for word:* yā kara bhajana — whom (they) worship; śiba caturānana — Shiva and the Four-faced One (Brahma); karu — make; mana-marama sandhāna — a search in the depths of the heart; hena nāma-hāra — such a necklace of the Name; yatana kari — carefully; gām̐thai — strings; patita janere — to fallen people; kare dāna — gives

**5.4.** The Name that Shiva and the Four-faced One worship,
seeking it in the depths of the heart —
of such a Name He carefully strings a necklace
and gives it to the fallen.

অন্ধকার-কূপে মগন দেখিয়া জীব
নবদ্বীপে পহু পরকাশ ।
প্রেম-রতন ধন জগ ভরি বিতরল
বঞ্চিত বলরাম দাস ॥

*andhakāra-kūpe magana dekhiyā jība*
*nabadvīpe pahu parakāśa |*
*prema-ratana dhana jaga bhari bitarala*
*bañcita balarāma dāsa ||*

*Word for word:* andhakāra-kūpe — in a dark well; magana — sunk; dekhiyā — seeing; jība — the souls; nabadvīpe — in Navadvipa; pahu — the Lord; parakāśa — appeared; prema-ratana dhana — the treasure of prema; jaga bhari — filling the world; bitarala — gave away; bañcita — deprived; balarāma dāsa — Balarama Dasa

**5.5.** Seeing the souls sunk in a dark well,
the Lord appeared in Navadvipa;
the treasure of prema He gave away, filling the world —
only Balarama Dasa is left out.

[^10-19]: Signature: "Balarama Dasa." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 217 (printed p. 206), 4th shakha, 17th pallava "śrīgaurāṅgera nṛtyādi līlā"
(Gauranga's dance and other pastimes), no. 7 (label "॥৭॥২০৬৫॥"); raga mangala; P-R-Sa MS no. 2174. GPT1 — p. 274, no. 86
(mangala); GPT2 — sec. 4.2, no. 86. Majumdar does not discuss the pada; its attribution to one of the Balarama Dasas is not
established. MS "kha": "kara" instead of "karu" (5.4).
[^10-20]: "The Creator fashioned" is a poetic figure of wonder: the Lord's body is eternal and spiritual (sac-cid-ananda), not
created by Brahma.

## 6. Balarama Dasa — "nācata gaura sunāgara-maṇiyā…" (PK 2066)
*Gaura's dance: a golden body, reddish garments, tears like rain, a merciful glance that drowns the world in the ocean
of prema; He embraces the fallen, and at His leaps and roars the hearts of the godless tremble. The raga is not named
("the same raga" — mangala).*[^10-21]

নাচত গৌর সুনাগর-মণিয়া ।
খঞ্জন-গঞ্জন পদযুগ-রঞ্জন
রণরণি মঞ্জির মঞ্জুল-ধ্বনিয়া ॥

*nācata gaura sunāgara-maṇiyā |*
*khañjana-gañjana padayuga-rañjana*
*raṇaraṇi mañjira mañjula-dhvaniyā ||*

*Word for word:* nācata — dances; gaura — Gaura; sunāgara-maṇiyā — the jewel of refined youths; khañjana-gañjana — putting the wagtails to shame; padayuga-rañjana — the delightful pair of feet; raṇaraṇi — "ran-ran"; mañjira — the ankle bells; mañjula-dhvaniyā — ring sweetly

**6.1.** *(Refrain)* Gaura dances, the jewel of refined youths;
His feet, which put the wagtails to shame, delight the eye,
His ankle bells ring with a sweet "ran-ran."[^10-22]

সহজই কাঞ্চন- কাঁতি কলেবর
হেরইতে জগ-জন-মন-মোহনিয়া ।
তহিঁ কত কোটি মদন-মন মুরছল
অরুণ-কিরণ কিয়ে অম্বর বনিয়া ॥

*sahajai kāñcana- kām̐ti kalebara*
*heraite jaga-jana-mana-mohaniyā |*
*tahim̐ kata koṭi madana-mana murachala*
*aruṇa-kiraṇa kiye ambara baniyā ||*

*Word for word:* sahajai — naturally; kāñcana-kām̐ti — of golden lustre; kalebara — the body; heraite — on seeing; jaga-jana-mana-mohaniyā — enchanting the hearts of all the world's people; tahim̐ — thereupon; kata koṭi — so many millions; madana-mana murachala — Madanas fainted; aruṇa-kiraṇa kiye — as if the rays of dawn; ambara baniyā — the garments worn

**6.2.** His body has a natural golden lustre —
whoever looks, the whole world is enchanted;
millions of Madanas faint at it;
His garments are like the rays of dawn.

ডগ মগ দেহ থেহ নাহি বান্ধই
দুহুঁ দিঠি-মেহ সঘনে বরিখণিয়া ।
প্রেমক সায়রে ভুবন মজাওই
লোচন-কোণে করুণ নিরখণিয়া ॥

*ḍaga maga deha theha nāhi bāndhai*
*duhum̐ diṭhi-meha saghane barikhaṇiyā |*
*premaka sāyare bhubana majāoi*
*locana-koṇe karuṇa nirakhaṇiyā ||*

*Word for word:* ḍaga maga deha — the body sways; theha nāhi bāndhai — cannot steady itself; duhum̐ diṭhi-meha — the two eyes, (like) clouds; saghane barikhaṇiyā — rain unceasingly; premaka sāyare — in the ocean of prema; bhubana majāoi — He drowns the world; locana-koṇe — with the corners of the eyes; karuṇa nirakhaṇiyā — glancing mercifully

**6.3.** His body sways, He cannot stand steady,
His two eyes pour like clouds unceasingly;
He drowns the world in the ocean of prema,
glancing mercifully from the corners of His eyes.

ও রসে ভোর ওর নাহি পায়ই
পতিত কোরে ধরি ভুবন বিয়াপি ।
কহ বলরাম লক্ষ ঘন হুঙ্কৃতি
হেরি পাষণ্ড-হৃদয় অতি কাঁপি ॥

*o rase bhora ora nāhi pāyai*
*patita kore dhari bhubana biyāpi |*
*kaha balarāma lakṣa ghana huṅkṛti*
*heri pāṣaṇḍa-hṛdaya ati kām̐pi ||*

*Word for word:* o rase bhora — absorbed in that rasa; ora nāhi pāyai — finds no limit; patita — the fallen; kore dhari — embracing; bhubana biyāpi — pervading the world; kaha balarāma — Balarama says; lakṣa — the leaps; ghana huṅkṛti — the thunderous roars; heri — seeing; pāṣaṇḍa-hṛdaya — the hearts of the godless; ati kām̐pi — tremble greatly

**6.4.** Absorbed in that rasa, He knows no limit,
He embraces the fallen and fills the world.
Balarama says: seeing His leaps and thunderous roars,
the hearts of the godless tremble.[^10-23]

[^10-21]: Signature: "Balarama." PK: vol. 3, PDF pp. 217–218 (printed pp. 206–207), 17th pallava, no. 8 (label "॥৮॥২০৬৬॥"); P-R-Sa
MS no. 2175. GPT1 — p. 250, no. 7 ("yathārāga"); GPT2 — sec. 4.2, no. 7. Its attribution to one of the Balarama Dasas is not
established.
[^10-22]: Sunagara-mani, "the jewel of refined youths," is an epithet of Krishna; the poet sees Krishna Himself in the dancing
Gaura. The wagtail (khañjana) is an image of nimble, light feet or eyes.
[^10-23]: P-R-Sa: "on the earth" (bhūtala) instead of "in the world" (bhubana). "lakṣa" is a leap (cf. "lakṣe lakṣe" in BR). GPT1: "majāyai,"
"pāoi," "aruṇakiraṇa ambara baniyā" (without "kiye").

## 7. Balarama Dasa — "gobinda mādhaba śrīnibāsa rāmānande…" (PK 2067 = BR p. 922)
*Kirtana in Navadvipa: Govinda, Madhava, Srinivasa (Srivasa), Ramananda, Murari and Mukunda sing; hearing of His
former (Vrindavana) pastimes the Lord falls senseless and rolls in the dust; seeing Gadadhara, He weeps; He calls out,
"Shripada!" — and Nityananda, understanding the secret of His heart, weeps too. Raga mallara-kamoda (BR — dhanashi).*[^10-24]

গোবিন্দ মাধব শ্রীনিবাস রামানন্দে ।
মুরারি মুকুন্দ মেলি গায় নিজ-বৃন্দে ॥

*gobinda mādhaba śrīnibāsa rāmānande |*
*murāri mukunda meli gāya nija-bṛnde ||*

*Word for word:* gobinda mādhaba — Govinda, Madhava; śrīnibāsa rāmānande — Srinivasa, Ramananda; murāri mukunda — Murari, Mukunda; meli — joining together; gāya — sing; nija-bṛnde — as their own choir

**7.1.** Govinda, Madhava, Srinivasa, Ramananda,
Murari and Mukunda sing together, as their own choir.[^10-25]

শুনিয়া পুরব-গুণ উনমত হৈয়া ।
কীর্ত্তন-আনন্দে পহু পড়ে মুরছিয়া ॥

*śuniyā puraba-guṇa unamata haiyā |*
*kīrttana-ānande pahu paṛe murachiyā ||*

*Word for word:* śuniyā — hearing; puraba-guṇa — of the former virtues; unamata haiyā — becoming maddened; kīrttana-ānande — in the bliss of kirtana; pahu — the Lord; paṛe murachiyā — falls senseless

**7.2.** Hearing of His former virtues, maddened,
in the bliss of kirtana the Lord falls senseless.

কিয়ে অপরূপ কথা কহনে না যায় ।
গোলোকের নাথ হৈয়া ধুলায় লোটায় ॥

*kiye aparūpa kathā kahane nā yāya |*
*golokera nātha haiyā dhulāya loṭāya ||*

*Word for word:* kiye aparūpa kathā — what a wonder; kahane nā yāya — cannot be told; golokera nātha haiyā — being the Lord of Goloka; dhulāya loṭāya — rolls in the dust

**7.3.** What a wonder — words cannot tell it:
the Lord of Goloka rolls in the dust![^10-26]

ভাবে গরগর চিত গদাধর দেখি ।
কান্দিয়া আকুল পহু ছলছল আঁখি ॥

*bhābe garagara cita gadādhara dekhi |*
*kāndiyā ākula pahu chalachala ām̐khi ||*

*Word for word:* bhābe garagara — overflowing with bhava; cita — the heart; gadādhara dekhi — seeing Gadadhara; kāndiyā ākula — weeping in longing; pahu — the Lord; chalachala ām̐khi — eyes brimming with tears

**7.4.** His heart is overflowing with bhava — He sees Gadadhara
and weeps in longing, His eyes brimming with tears.

শ্রীপাদ বলিয়া পহু ভূমে পড়ি কান্দে ।
বুঝিয়া মরম-কথা কান্দে নিত্যানন্দে ॥

*śrīpāda baliyā pahu bhūme paṛi kānde |*
*bujhiyā marama-kathā kānde nityānande ||*

*Word for word:* śrīpāda baliyā — calling "Shripada!"; pahu — the Lord; bhūme paṛi — falling to the ground; kānde — weeps; bujhiyā — understanding; marama-kathā — the secret of the heart; kānde nityānande — Nityananda weeps

**7.5.** "Shripada!" the Lord calls, falls to the ground and weeps;
understanding the secret of His heart, Nityananda weeps.[^10-27]

দেখিয়া ত্রিবিধ লোক কান্দে গোরা-রসে ।
এ সুখে বঞ্চিত ভেল বলরাম দাসে ॥

*dekhiyā tribidha loka kānde gorā-rase |*
*e sukhe bañcita bhela balarāma dāse ||*

*Word for word:* dekhiyā — seeing; tribidha loka — people of three kinds; kānde — weep; gorā-rase — (drunk) with Gora's rasa; e sukhe — of this joy; bañcita bhela — has been deprived; balarāma dāse — Balarama Dasa

**7.6.** Seeing this, people of all three kinds weep, drunk with Gora's rasa,
but of this joy Balarama Dasa has been deprived.

[^10-24]: Signature: "Balarama Dasa." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 218 (printed p. 207), 17th pallava, no. 9 (label "॥৯॥২০৬৭॥"); raga
mallara-kamoda; P-R-Sa MS no. 2176. BR, 12th wave (1913 ed., p. 922, "punardhānaśī"), right after Balarama's pada "…nā darabe balarāma
pāṣāṇa-hṛdaya". GPT1 — p. 275, no. 87 (shri-mallara); GPT2 — sec. 4.2, no. 87. Majumdar cites the pada as testimony of Balarama
Dasa: a kirtana with the Ghosha brothers, Srivasa, Vasu Ramananda, Murari and Mukunda.
[^10-25]: Govinda and Madhava are the Ghosha brothers, the singers of Navadvipa; Srinivasa is Srivasa Pandita; Ramananda is
Vasu Ramananda; Murari is Murari Gupta; Mukunda is Mukunda Datta. MS "ka," BR, GPT1: "mili" (together) instead of "meli."
[^10-26]: MSS "ka," "ca," P-R-Sa: "goloka-" (without the case ending); so also GPT1. In BR this couplet is followed by the refrain
mark (dhru).
[^10-27]: Shripada is the Lord's respectful way of addressing Nityananda. MSS "ka," "kha," "gha," "ca": "to the ground" (dharaṇī) instead
of "bhūme"; BR: "prabhu bhūme"; GPT1: "śrīpāda bali pahum̐ dharaṇī paṛi kām̐de." BR: "gadādhare dekhi" (7.4).

## 8. Nayanananda — "maṇḍalī raciyā sahacare…" (PK 2068)
*The companions have formed a circle, and in the middle Gora dances: with Him are Gadadhara and Nityananda; from house to
house He, Shyamasundara Himself, distributes love and devotion and with sankirtana offers everyone the treasure of
prema; men dance in the mood of women, women in the mood of men. The poet and his friends seek shelter at Gadadhara's
feet. Raga kedara.*[^10-28]

মণ্ডলী রচিয়া সহচরে ।
তার মাঝে গোরা নটবরে ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*maṇḍalī raciyā sahacare |*
*tāra mājhe gorā naṭabare || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* maṇḍalī raciyā — forming a circle; sahacare — the companions; tāra mājhe — in its middle; gorā naṭabare — Gora, the best of dancers

**8.1.** *(Refrain)* The companions have formed a circle,
in the middle is Gora, the best of dancers.

নাচে বিশ্বম্ভর সঙ্গে গদাধর
নাচে নিত্যানন্দ রায় ।
পুরব-কৌতুক ভুঞ্জে প্রেম-সুখ
স্বভাবে বুঝিয়া পায় ॥

*nāce biśvambhara saṅge gadādhara*
*nāce nityānanda rāya |*
*puraba-kautuka bhuñje prema-sukha*
*svabhābe bujhiyā pāya ||*

*Word for word:* nāce biśvambhara — Vishvambhara dances; saṅge gadādhara — with Him Gadadhara; nāce nityānanda rāya — Nityananda Raya dances; puraba-kautuka — (recalling) the former pastimes; bhuñje — they taste; prema-sukha — the joy of prema; svabhābe — by one's own nature; bujhiyā pāya — grasps

**8.2.** Vishvambhara dances, with Him Gadadhara,
Nityananda Raya dances;
recalling their former pastimes, they taste the joy of prema —
each grasps it according to his own nature.[^10-29]

ঘরে ঘরে শ্যাম- সুন্দর-মূরতি
পিরীতি ভকতি দিয়া ।
করে সংকীর্ত্তন যাচে প্রেম-ধন
সব সহচর লৈয়া ॥

*ghare ghare śyāma- sundara-mūrati*
*pirīti bhakati diyā |*
*kare saṃkīrttana yāce prema-dhana*
*saba sahacara laiyā ||*

*Word for word:* ghare ghare — from house to house; śyāma-sundara-mūrati — the form of Shyamasundara (Shyamasundara Himself); pirīti bhakati diyā — giving love and devotion; kare saṅkīrttana — performs sankirtana; yāce prema-dhana — begs (all) to take the treasure of prema; saba sahacara laiyā — with all the companions

**8.3.** From house to house — Shyamasundara Himself in person —
He gives away love and devotion;
He performs sankirtana and begs all to take the treasure of prema,
together with all His companions.[^10-30]

পুরুষ নাচে প্রকৃতি-ভাবে
পুরুষ-ভাবে যুবতী ।
যার যেই ভাব পাইয়া স্বভাব
নাচে কত শত জাতি ॥

*puruṣa nāce prakṛti-bhābe*
*puruṣa-bhābe yubatī |*
*yāra yei bhāba pāiyā svabhāba*
*nāce kata śata jāti ||*

*Word for word:* puruṣa nāce — men dance; prakṛti-bhābe — in the mood of women; puruṣa-bhābe — in the mood of men; yubatī — young women; yāra yei bhāba — whatever bhava one has; pāiyā svabhāba — having found one's own nature; nāce — dance; kata śata jāti — people of hundreds of castes

**8.4.** Men dance in the mood of women,
young women in the mood of men;
each having found his own bhava, his own nature,
people of every caste dance.[^10-31]

কহে নয়নানন্দ নদীয়া-আনন্দ
আনন্দে ভুবন ভোরা ।
দুখিত-জীবন মাধব-নন্দন-
চরণে শরণ মোরা ॥

*kahe nayanānanda nadīyā-ānanda*
*ānande bhubana bhorā |*
*dukhita-jībana mādhaba-nandana-*
*caraṇe śaraṇa morā ||*

*Word for word:* kahe nayanānanda — Nayanananda says; nadīyā-ānanda — the bliss of Nadia; ānande — with bliss; bhubana bhorā — the world is drunk; dukhita-jībana — with lives full of sorrow; mādhaba-nandana-caraṇe — at the feet of Madhava's son; śaraṇa — shelter; morā — we

**8.5.** Nayanananda says: the bliss of Nadia —
the whole world is drunk with bliss.
We whose life is full of sorrow take shelter
at the feet of Madhava's son.[^10-32]

[^10-28]: Signature: "Nayanananda." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 218 (printed p. 207), 17th pallava, no. 10 (label "॥১০॥২০৬৮॥"); raga kedara;
P-R-Sa MS nos. 2177 and 2213. GPT1 — pp. 250–251, no. 8 (kedara); GPT2 — sec. 4.2, no. 8. PK 2104 (vol. 3, PDF p. 231, no. 46) is
another recension of the same pada (after P-R-Sa no. 2213): "…nāce nityānanda bhāyā। pūraba-kautuka bhuñje prema-sukha saba sahacara laiyā,"
after which Raya refers back to PK 2068.
[^10-29]: "Former pastimes" are the pastimes of Vrindavana. P-R-Sa: "sabhāre" (to all) instead of "svabhābe" (by one's own nature); PK 2104
and GPT1 (in a note): "brother Nityananda" (bhāyā, bhāiyā).
[^10-30]: Shyamasundara, "the dark beauty," is Krishna: the poet sees in Gaura Krishna Himself going from house to house. P-R-Sa:
"merciful to all" (sabhāre sadaya haiyā) instead of "together with all His companions."
[^10-31]: In the ecstasy of kirtana the devotees forget the worldly distinction of sex: each dances in the bhava that has opened
within him. P-R-Sa: "dance" (nācata), "women" (prakṛti) instead of "young women" (yubatī).
[^10-32]: "Madhava's son" is Gadadhara Pandita, the son of Madhava Mishra; Nayanananda is his nephew and disciple. MSS "ka," "kha,"
P-R-Sa: "duḥkhita"; "gha": "jībajana" (souls). GPT1: "duḥkhita jībana, mādhabanandana, caraṇe śaraṇa morā."

## 9. Nayanananda — "duhum̐ duhum̐ piriti ārati nāhi ṭuṭe…" (PK 2069 = BR p. 925)
*Gaura and Gadadhara dance, drunk with each other's love: Gauranga with Gadadhara's rasa, Gadadhara with Gauranga's
pastimes; they are like Sita and Rama, like Radha and Kanu; in Nadia reigns the joy of the kirtana of prema, and the
mistress of the house of prema is Pandita Gadadhara, while Shachi's son is the touchstone of prema. Raga pathamanjari
(BR — kamoda).*[^10-33]

দুহুঁ দুহুঁ পিরিতি আরতি নাহি টুটে ।
পরশে পরম কত কত সুখ উঠে ॥

*duhum̐ duhum̐ piriti ārati nāhi ṭuṭe |*
*paraśe parama kata kata sukha uṭhe ||*

*Word for word:* duhum̐ duhum̐ — for each other; piriti ārati — love and longing; nāhi ṭuṭe — never break off; paraśe — at the touch; parama — supreme; kata kata sukha — so much joy; uṭhe — arises

**9.1.** Their love and longing for each other never break off,
at their touch so much supreme joy arises![^10-34]

নাচয়ে গৌরাঙ্গ মোর গদাধর-রসে ।
গদাধর নাচে পুন গৌরাঙ্গ-বিলাসে ॥

*nācaye gaurāṅga mora gadādhara-rase |*
*gadādhara nāce puna gaurāṅga-bilāse ||*

*Word for word:* nācaye gaurāṅga mora — my Gauranga dances; gadādhara-rase — in Gadadhara's rasa; gadādhara nāce — Gadadhara dances; puna — in turn; gaurāṅga-bilāse — in Gauranga's play

**9.2.** My Gauranga dances, drunk with Gadadhara's rasa,
and Gadadhara dances, drunk with Gauranga's play.

প্রকৃতি পুরুষ কিবা জানকী শ্রীরাম ।
রাধা-কানু এই কিবা রতি দেব কাম ॥

*prakṛti puruṣa kibā jānakī śrīrāma |*
*rādhā-kānu ei kibā rati deba kāma ||*

*Word for word:* prakṛti puruṣa — the female and male principles; kibā — are they not; jānakī śrīrāma — Janaki and Sri Rama; rādhā-kānu — Radha and Kanu; ei — this; kibā — or; rati deba kāma — Rati and the god Kama

**9.3.** Prakriti and purusha — are they not Janaki and Sri Rama?
Are they not Radha with Kanu, Rati with the god Kama?[^10-35]

অনন্ত অনঙ্গ জিনি অঙ্গের বলনি ।
উপমা মহিমা-সীমা কি বলিতে জানি ॥

*ananta anaṅga jini aṅgera balani |*
*upamā mahimā-sīmā ki balite jāni ||*

*Word for word:* ananta anaṅga jini — surpassing countless Anangas; aṅgera balani — the grace (curve) of the limbs; upamā — a likeness; mahimā-sīmā — for the limit of greatness; ki balite jāni — how can I tell

**9.4.** The grace of their limbs surpasses countless Anangas —
how can I find a likeness for the limit of their greatness?

মুখে চাঁদ কি বর্ণিব নিতি জীয়ে মরে ।
কর-পদে পদ্ম কিবা হিম-ভরে ঝরে ॥

*mukhe cām̐da ki barṇiba niti jīye mare |*
*kara-pade padma kibā hima-bhare jhare ||*

*Word for word:* mukhe — beside the face; cām̐da — the moon; ki barṇiba — what shall I describe; niti — every day; jīye mare — lives and dies; kara-pade — beside the hands and feet; padma kibā — what is the lotus; hima-bhare — under the weight of frost; jhare — falls apart

**9.5.** What to say of the moon beside His face — every day it is born and dies;
what is the lotus beside His hands and feet — it falls apart under the weight of frost![^10-36]

প্রেম-কীর্ত্তন-সুখ নদীয়া নগরে ।
প্রেমের গৃহিণী সে পণ্ডিত গদাধরে ॥

*prema-kīrttana-sukha nadīyā nagare |*
*premera gṛhiṇī se paṇḍita gadādhare ||*

*Word for word:* prema-kīrttana-sukha — the joy of the kirtana of prema; nadīyā nagare — in the city of Nadia; premera gṛhiṇī — the mistress of the house of prema; se — she; paṇḍita gadādhare — Pandita Gadadhara

**9.6.** The joy of the kirtana of prema is in the city of Nadia;
the mistress of the house of prema is Pandita Gadadhara.[^10-37]

প্রেম-পরশ-মণি শচীর নন্দন ।
উদ্ধারিল জগ-জন দিয়া প্রেম-ধন ॥

*prema-paraśa-maṇi śacīra nandana |*
*uddhārila jaga-jana diyā prema-dhana ||*

*Word for word:* prema-paraśa-maṇi — the touchstone of prema; śacīra nandana — Shachi's son; uddhārila — delivered; jaga-jana — the people of the world; diyā prema-dhana — giving the treasure of prema

**9.7.** The touchstone of prema is Shachi's son:
He delivered the people of the world by giving them the treasure of prema.

কহে নয়নানন্দ দোঁহার বিহার ।
শুনিতে হরয়ে মন ইথে কি বিচার ॥

*kahe nayanānanda dom̐hāra bihāra |*
*śunite haraye mana ithe ki bicāra ||*

*Word for word:* kahe nayanānanda — Nayanananda tells; dom̐hāra bihāra — of the play of the two; śunite — on hearing; haraye mana — the heart is captivated; ithe — in this; ki bicāra — what is there to reason

**9.8.** Nayanananda tells of the play of these two:
hearing of it, the heart is captivated — what is there to reason about?[^10-38]

[^10-33]: Signature: "Nayanananda." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 219 (printed p. 208), 17th pallava, no. 11 (label "॥১১॥২০৬৯॥"); raga
pathamanjari; P-R-Sa MS nos. 2178 and 2460. BR, 12th wave (1913 ed., p. 925, "punaḥ kāmodaḥ"): Narahari Chakravarti cites the pada in
the account of Navadvipa as testimony ("ohe śrīnibāsa kichu kahila nā haya। suradhunītīre gorā raṅge bilasaya"). GPT1 — p. 251, no. 9
(pathamanjari); GPT2 — sec. 4.2, no. 9. Majumdar counts the pada among the testimonies of the closeness of Gauranga and Gadadhara
(catalogue: NN-029 = NN-015). In the catalogue the padas NS-005, BD-018 and BD-022 had been wrongly linked to PK 2069. PK 2356 (24th pallava, vol. 3, PDF p. 324) repeats the same pada.
[^10-34]: MS "gha," GPT1: "the heart" (marama) instead of "supreme" (parama); BR: "paraśe parama sukha jāni kata uṭhe."
[^10-35]: Prakriti and purusha are the female and male principles: Gadadhara, the manifestation of Radha (the pleasure energy,
hladini-shakti), and Gaura, Krishna Himself. Rati and Kama (Kamadeva) are the deities of love; the poet's comparisons are
images of beauty and intimacy, not of worldly passion: according to Gaudiya teaching, Krishna is the transcendental Madana
(aprakrita-madana, CC Madhya 8). BR, GPT1: "Radha and Kanu at play (keli)"; BR: "purusha and prakriti."
[^10-36]: The moon wanes and waxes; the lotus withers in the winter frost — but the Lord's face, hands and feet are always
beautiful. MS "ka": "the moon-face" (mukha-cām̐da); "gha": "karapada"; BR: "What likeness is the moon? Every day it is born and dies;
the hands and feet — lotuses? (Lotuses) fall apart from the frost."
[^10-37]: "The mistress of the house of prema" (premera gṛhiṇī) is Gadadhara as the manifestation of Radha. BR: "prema-saṅkīrtana-sukha."
[^10-38]: MSS "kha," "gha," P-R-Sa: "behāra" (the same). BR: "kahaye nayanānanda ānanda bihāra" ("…the play of bliss"). MS "ka," P-R-Sa:
"prema-parama-maṇi" instead of "prema-paraśa-maṇi" (9.7); BR: "uddhārilā jagajane."

## 10. Nayanananda — "kīrttana mājhe kīrttana-naṭa-rāja…" (PK 2070)
*Amid the kirtana is the king of the kirtana dancers: a garland on His neck with bees humming over it, a moon of sandal
paste on His forehead; this dancing Vishvambhara is Krishna Himself: within Krishna, without the form of Radha,
incomparable gold; He takes on His lap Gadadhara, the Lakshmi of prema. Raga bhatiyari.*[^10-39]

কীর্ত্তন মাঝে কীর্ত্তন-নট-রাজ ।
কীর্ত্তন-কৌতুক সব নাগরালি-সাজ ॥

*kīrttana mājhe kīrttana-naṭa-rāja |*
*kīrttana-kautuka saba nāgarāli-sāja ||*

*Word for word:* kīrttana mājhe — amid the kirtana; kīrttana-naṭa-rāja — the king of kirtana dancers; kīrttana-kautuka — (for) the play of kirtana; saba — all; nāgarāli-sāja — the attire of an elegant youth

**10.1.** Amid the kirtana is the king of the kirtana dancers,
for the play of kirtana — all the finery of an elegant youth.[^10-40]

গলায় দোলার মালা মধুকর-গান ।
কপালে চন্দন-চাঁদ ভুরু ফুল-বাণ ॥

*galāya dolāra mālā madhukara-gāna |*
*kapāle candana-cām̐da bhuru phula-bāṇa ||*

*Word for word:* galāya — on the neck; dolāra mālā — a swaying garland; madhukara-gāna — the song of bees; kapāle — on the forehead; candana-cām̐da — a moon of sandal paste; bhuru — the brows; phula-bāṇa — flower-arrows

**10.2.** On His neck sways a garland, the bees sing over it,
on His forehead is a moon of sandal paste, His brows are flower-arrows.

দেখ ভাই অতি অপরূপ ।
এই বিশ্বম্ভর নাচে কৃষ্ণের স্বরূপ ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*dekha bhāi ati aparūpa |*
*ei biśvambhara nāce kṛṣṇera svarūpa || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* dekha bhāi — look, brothers; ati aparūpa — a great wonder; ei biśvambhara — this Vishvambhara; nāce — dances; kṛṣṇera svarūpa — Krishna's own form

**10.3.** *(Refrain)* Look, brothers, what a wonder:
this dancing Vishvambhara is Krishna in His own form!

কৃষ্ণ কৃষ্ণ অন্তরে পরম-রস কোণা ।
বাহিরে রাধার রূপ নিরুপম সোণা ॥

*kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa antare parama-rasa koṇā |*
*bāhire rādhāra rūpa nirupama soṇā ||*

*Word for word:* kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa — "Krishna, Krishna"; antare — within; parama-rasa — the supreme rasa; koṇā — in a hidden corner (?); bāhire — without; rādhāra rūpa — Radha's form; nirupama sonā — incomparable gold

**10.4.** Within — "Krishna, Krishna," the hidden supreme rasa,
without — the form of Radha, incomparable gold.[^10-41]

প্রকৃতি-পুরুষ-সুখ রসে রসে এক ।
প্রেম-অবতার এই দেখ পরতেক ॥

*prakṛti-puruṣa-sukha rase rase eka |*
*prema-abatāra ei dekha parateka ||*

*Word for word:* prakṛti-puruṣa-sukha — the joy of prakriti and purusha; rase rase — rasa with rasa; eka — one; prema-abatāra — the incarnation of prema; ei — this; dekha parateka — see with your own eyes

**10.5.** The joy of prakriti and purusha — rasa with rasa — has become one:
see with your own eyes — here is the incarnation of prema!

প্রেম-লখিমিনী কোলে কৈল গদাধর ।
প্রেমানন্দে নিত্যানন্দ প্রাণ-সহোদর ॥

*prema-lakhiminī kole kaila gadādhara |*
*premānande nityānanda prāṇa-sahodara ||*

*Word for word:* prema-lakhiminī — the Lakshmi of prema; kole kaila — took on His lap; gadādhara — Gadadhara; premānande — in the bliss of prema; nityānanda — Nityananda; prāṇa-sahodara — His own brother, dear as life

**10.6.** Gadadhara, the Lakshmi of prema, He took on His lap;
in the bliss of prema is Nityananda, His own brother, dear as life.[^10-42]

নয়নানন্দে কহে প্রেম নিগূঢ় বিচার ।
অমিয়া-পুতলী যেন অমিয়া-আকার ॥

*nayanānande kahe prema nigūṛha bicāra |*
*amiyā-putalī yena amiyā-ākāra ||*

*Word for word:* nayanānande kahe — Nayanananda tells; prema nigūṛha bicāra — the hidden truth of prema; amiyā-putalī — a doll of nectar; yena — as if; amiyā-ākāra — a form of nectar

**10.7.** Nayanananda tells of the hidden secret of prema:
He is like a doll of nectar, a form made of nectar.[^10-43]

[^10-39]: Signature: "Nayanananda." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 219 (printed p. 208), 17th pallava, no. 12 (label "॥১২॥২০৭০॥"); raga
bhatiyari; P-R-Sa MS no. 2179. GPT1 — p. 260, no. 41 (bhatiyari); GPT2 — sec. 4.2, no. 41. The linking of pada NS-021 (Narahari) to
PK 2070 is mistaken.
[^10-40]: "Nāgarāli-sāj" — the attire of a nagara, an elegant youth: an epithet of Krishna the dancer, not the language of
nagari-bhava. MSS "ka," "kha": "sways" (dolaye) instead of "dolāra" (10.2).
[^10-41]: Cf. the teaching of Krishnadasa Kaviraja (CC Adi 1.5–6; Adi 4): Sri Chaitanya is Krishna who has accepted the bhava and
the lustre of Radha. MSS "ka," "kha," "gha," "ca": "antara" (within); "ka," "kha," "gha," "ca": "paraśa" instead of "parama"; "gha": "kanā" (a
particle) instead of "koṇā" ("a corner," i.e. something hidden — the reading is unclear).
[^10-42]: The Lakshmi of prema (prema-lakhiminī) is Gadadhara, the manifestation of Radha.
[^10-43]: MS "ka": "nigurṇa," "ca": "niguna," P-R-Sa: "niguni," GPT1: "niguṇa" — slips for "nigūṛha" (hidden); the subject is the secret of
prema, not "qualitylessness" (nirguna) — the Lord has spiritual qualities.

## 11. Nayanananda — "sajanī aparūpa dekha siyā…" (PK 2071)
*Gaura dances in Krishna's mood: He stands still in the tribhanga pose, looks for the flute, ties His hair into a topknot
like Krishna, calls "Krishna, Krishna!", strikes His chest and says, "I am that very Lord"; the Ganga seems to Him the
Yamuna, Navadvipa — Gokula and Mathura. Raga dhanashi.*[^10-44]

সজনী অপরূপ দেখ সিয়া ।
নাচয়ে গৌরাঙ্গচাঁদ হরিবোল বলিয়া ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*sajanī aparūpa dekha siyā |*
*nācaye gaurāṅgacām̐da haribola baliyā || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* sajanī — friend; aparūpa — a wonder; dekha siyā — come and see; nācaye — dances; gaurāṅgacām̐da — Gaurangachand; haribola baliyā — chanting "Hari-bol"

**11.1.** *(Refrain)* Friend, come and see what a wonder:
Gaurangachand dances, chanting "Hari-bol"!

সুগন্ধি চন্দন-সার গন্ধ করবীর মাল
গোরা-অঙ্গে দোলে হিলোলিয়া ।
পুরব পরোক্ষ-ভাব পরতেক দেখ লাভ
সেই এই গোরা বিনোদিয়া ॥

*sugandhi candana-sāra gandha karabīra māla*
*gorā-aṅge dole hiloliyā |*
*puraba parokṣa-bhāba parateka dekha lābha*
*sei ei gorā binodiyā ||*

*Word for word:* sugandhi candana-sāra — the fragrant choicest sandal paste; gandha karabīra māla — the scented karabira garland; gorā-aṅge — on Gora's body; dole hiloliyā — sway in waves; puraba — formerly; parokṣa-bhāba — hidden from sight; parateka dekha — see before your eyes; lābha — what a gain; sei ei — that very — this; gorā binodiyā — charming Gora

**11.2.** The fragrant choicest sandal paste, the scented karabira garland
sway in waves on Gora's body.
What was hidden from sight before — see, here it is before your eyes, what a gain!
He is that very One — this charming Gora.[^10-45]

ত্রিভঙ্গ হইয়া রহে মধুর মুরলী চাহে
বান্ধে চূড়া চাচর চিকুরে ।
কৃষ্ণ কৃষ্ণ বলি ডাকে মালসাট মারে বুকে
ক্ষণে বোলে মুঞি সে ঠাকুরে ॥

*tribhaṅga haiyā rahe madhura muralī cāhe*
*bāndhe cūṛā cācara cikure |*
*kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa bali ḍāke mālasāṭa māre buke*
*kṣaṇe bole muñi se ṭhākure ||*

*Word for word:* tribhaṅga haiyā rahe — stands bent in three places; madhura muralī cāhe — looks for the sweet flute; bāndhe cūṛā — ties a topknot; cācara cikure — of curly hair; kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa bali ḍāke — calls "Krishna, Krishna"; mālasāṭa māre buke — slaps His chest (like a wrestler); kṣaṇe — suddenly; bole — says; muñi se ṭhākure — I am that Lord

**11.3.** He stands still, bent in three places, looks for the sweet flute,
ties a topknot of His curly hair;
He calls, "Krishna, Krishna!" — slaps His chest like a wrestler,
and suddenly says, "I am that very Lord!"[^10-46]

জাহ্নবী যমুনা-ভ্রম তীর-তরু বৃন্দাবন
নবদ্বীপ গোকুল মথুরা ।
কহে নয়নানন্দ সেই সখা সখীবৃন্দ
কালা তনু এবে হৈল গোরা ॥

*jāhnabī yamunā-bhrama tīra-taru bṛndābana*
*nabadvīpa gokula mathurā |*
*kahe nayanānanda sei sakhā sakhībṛnda*
*kālā tanu ebe haila gorā ||*

*Word for word:* jāhnabī — the Jahnavi (Ganga); yamunā-bhrama — (mistaken) for the Yamuna; tīra-taru — the trees on the bank; bṛndābana — Vrindavana; nabadvīpa — Navadvipa; gokula mathurā — Gokula and Mathura; kahe nayanānanda — Nayanananda says; sei — the same; sakhā sakhībṛnda — friends and girlfriends; kālā tanu — the dark body; ebe — now; haila gorā — has become Gora (golden)

**11.4.** The Jahnavi He takes for the Yamuna, the trees on her bank for Vrindavana,
Navadvipa for Gokula and Mathura.
Nayanananda says: the same friends and girlfriends —
and the dark body has now become Gora.[^10-47]

[^10-44]: Signature: "Nayanananda." PK: vol. 3, PDF pp. 219–220 (printed pp. 208–209), 17th pallava, no. 13 (label "॥১৩॥২০৭১॥");
raga dhanashi; P-R-Sa MS no. 2180. GPT1 — p. 251, no. 10 (dhanashi); GPT2 — sec. 4.2, no. 10. The address "friend" (sajanī) is a
usual opening of a pada; the speaker is not named. PK 2123 (18th pallava, vol. 3, PDF p. 238; P-R-Sa MS no. 2230) is another recension
of the same pada: "rādhā rādhā bali ḍāke… bale muñi sabhāra ṭhākura" ("He calls, 'Radha, Radha!'… says, 'I am the Lord of all'"), closing
"baraṇakhāni kāra bhābe gorā" ("by whose bhava has the form become golden").
[^10-45]: "Hidden before" — the pastimes of Vraja, formerly beyond sight, are now revealed before the eyes in Gaura.
[^10-46]: Tribhanga is Krishna's pose with the flute; chura is Krishna's topknot. "Mālasāṭ" is a slap of the palm on the arm or
chest, as wrestlers do. In Krishna's mood the Lord speaks of Himself as Krishna — cf. CB Madhya 8–9 (the mahaprakasha).
[^10-47]: The Jahnavi is the Ganga. Gaura's companions are the same as Krishna's companions in Vraja (*Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika*);
"the dark body" is Krishna who has become golden Gaura. MSS "gha," "ca," GPT1: "the trees on the bank" (tīre taru); "ka," "ca,"
GPT1: "in Navadvipa" (nabadvīpe).

## 12. Nayanananda — "nāce śacīra nandana dulāliyā…" (PK 2073)
*Shachi's darling son dances — the ocean of all rasas, Gadadhara's dearest friend: a tilaka of musk, a topknot, a face
like a golden moon, a smile that captivates the young women of the town; on His neck a forest garland, on Him yellow
garments. Raga bhatiyari.*[^10-48]

নাচে শচীর নন্দন দুলালিয়া ।
সকল রসের সিন্ধু গদাধর-প্রাণবন্ধু
নিরবধি বিনোদ রঙ্গিয়া ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*nāce śacīra nandana dulāliyā |*
*sakala rasera sindhu gadādhara-prāṇabandhu*
*nirabadhi binoda raṅgiyā || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* nāce — dances; śacīra nandana — Shachi's son; dulāliyā — the darling; sakala rasera sindhu — the ocean of all rasas; gadādhara-prāṇa-bandhu — the friend dear as life to Gadadhara; nirabadhi — ever; binoda raṅgiyā — merry in play

**12.1.** *(Refrain)* Shachi's darling son dances,
the ocean of all rasas, the friend dearer than life to Gadadhara,
ever merry in His play.

কস্তুরী-তিলক মাঝে মোহন চূড়াটী সাজে
অলকাবলিত বর শোভা ।
কনক বদন-শশী অমিয়া মধুর হাসি
নবীন নাগরী মন-লোভা ॥

*kasturī-tilaka mājhe mohana cūṛāṭī sāje*
*alakābalita bara śobhā |*
*kanaka badana-śaśī amiyā madhura hāsi*
*nabīna nāgarī mana-lobhā ||*

*Word for word:* kastūrī-tilaka mājhe — amid a tilaka of musk; mohana cūṛāṭī — a charming topknot; sāje — is adorned; alakābalita — framed by curls; bara śobhā — wondrous beauty; kanaka badana-śaśī — the face, a golden moon; amiyā madhura hāsi — a nectarean sweet smile; nabīna nāgarī — of young town women; mana-lobhā — captivating the hearts

**12.2.** Amid a tilaka of musk is a charming topknot,
wondrously framed by curls;
His face is a golden moon, His sweet nectarean smile
captivates the hearts of the young women of the town.[^10-49]

গোরা-গলে বনমালা অতি অপরূপ লীলা
কনক-অঙ্গুরী অঙ্গ ভুজে ।
পিয়ল বসন জোরা অখিল-মরম-চোরা
নয়নানন্দ পদাম্বুজে ॥

*gorā-gale banamālā ati aparūpa līlā*
*kanaka-aṅgurī aṅga bhuje |*
*piyala basana jorā akhila-marama-corā*
*nayanānanda padāmbuje ||*

*Word for word:* gorā-gale — on Gora's neck; banamālā — the forest garland; ati aparūpa līlā — a wondrous play; kanaka-aṅgurī — golden rings; aṅga(da) — armlets; bhuje — on the arms; piyala basana jorā — a pair of yellow garments; akhila-marama-corā — the thief of all hearts; nayanānanda — Nayanananda; padāmbuje — at the lotus feet

**12.3.** On Gora's neck is a forest garland — a wondrous play —
golden rings and bracelets on His arms;
He wears a pair of yellow garments — the thief of all hearts;
Nayanananda is at His lotus feet.[^10-50]

[^10-48]: Signature: "Nayanananda." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 220 (printed p. 209), 17th pallava, no. 15 (label "॥১৫॥২০৭৩॥"); raga bhatiyari;
P-R-Sa MS no. 2182. GPT1 — p. 153, no. 125 (bhatiyari); GPT2 — sec. 3.1, no. 125. The preceding pada PK 2072 is Uddhava Dasa's
("uddhaba dāsa tāra kīṭa").
[^10-49]: The words about young women are the language of nagari-bhava (Gaura as the nagara, the beloved of the town's
women); we translate faithfully to the author. Vrindavana Dasa stresses that in this incarnation the Lord never glanced at
another man's wife; worship of Gaura in the spirit of "Gaura-nagari" is not accepted by the Gaudiya tradition (Vrindavana
Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja, Bhaktisiddhanta). GPT1: "alakā balita baṛa śobhā" ("…great beauty").
[^10-50]: The forest garland (vanamala) and yellow garments (pitambara) are Krishna's attire. GPT1: "piṅgala" (yellowish) garments;
"maje nayanānanda-padāmbuje" — "…Nayanananda is immersed in (His) lotus feet."

## 13. Nayanananda — "mukhakhāni pūrṇimāra śaśī…" (PK 2102)
*Gora dances, binding the hearts of all souls with prema: His face is the full moon, His lips move all the time as if
chanting a mantra; the moon weeps on seeing the beauty of His face, the sun on seeing the clouds of His eyes; streams of
prema run down His chest. The poet asks: shall I see Gora beside Gadadhara again? Raga dhanashi.*[^10-51]

মুখখানি পূর্ণিমার শশী কিবা মন্ত্র জপে ।
বিম্ব-বিড়ম্বিতাধর সদাই কেনে কাঁপে ॥

*mukhakhāni pūrṇimāra śaśī kibā mantra jape |*
*bimba-biṛambitādhara sadāi kene kām̐pe ||*

*Word for word:* mukhakhāni — the face; pūrṇimāra śaśī — the full moon; kibā mantra jape — what mantra does He chant; bimba-biṛambita-adhara — the lips that mock the bimba (fruit); sadāi — always; kene kām̐pe — why do they tremble

**13.1.** His face is a full moon: what mantra is He chanting?
Why do His lips, which mock the bimba fruit, always tremble?[^10-52]

গোরা নাচে নটন-রঙ্গিয়া ।
অখিল জীবের মন বান্ধে প্রেম দিয়া ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*gorā nāce naṭana-raṅgiyā |*
*akhila jībera mana bāndhe prema diyā || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* gorā nāce — Gora dances; naṭana-raṅgiyā — merry in the dance; akhila jībera mana — the hearts of all souls; bāndhe — binds; prema diyā — with prema

**13.2.** *(Refrain)* Gora dances, merry in the dance,
the hearts of all souls He binds with prema.

চান্দ কান্দয়ে মুখ-ছান্দ দেখিয়া ।
তপন কান্দয়ে আঁখি-জলদ হেরিয়া ॥

*cānda kāndaye mukha-chānda dekhiyā |*
*tapana kāndaye ām̐khi-jalada heriyā ||*

*Word for word:* cānda kāndaye — the moon weeps; mukha-chānda — the beauty (shape) of the face; dekhiyā — seeing; tapana kāndaye — the sun weeps; ām̐khi-jalada — the clouds of the eyes; heriyā — beholding

**13.3.** The moon weeps seeing the beauty of His face,
the sun weeps seeing the clouds of His eyes.[^10-53]

কাঁচা কাঞ্চন জিনি নবাঞ্চল গোরা ।
বুক বাহি পড়ে প্রেম-রসের যে ধারা ॥

*kām̐cā kāñcana jini nabāñcala gorā |*
*buka bāhi paṛe prema-rasera ye dhārā ||*

*Word for word:* kām̐cā kāñcana jini — surpassing fresh (unwrought) gold; nabāñcala (?) — (unclear word); gorā — Gora; buka bāhi — down the chest; paṛe — flow; prema-rasera — of the rasa of prema; ye dhārā — the streams

**13.4.** Gora is brighter than fresh, unwrought gold,
streams of the rasa of prema run down His chest.[^10-54]

কহয়ে নয়নানন্দ মনের উল্লাসে ।
পুন কি দেখিব গোরা গদাধর পাশে ॥

*kahaye nayanānanda manera ullāse |*
*puna ki dekhiba gorā gadādhara pāśe ||*

*Word for word:* kahaye nayanānanda — Nayanananda says; manera ullāse — in the joy of his heart; puna — again; ki dekhiba — shall I see; gorā — Gora; gadādhara pāśe — beside Gadadhara

**13.5.** Nayanananda says in the joy of his heart:
shall I see Gora beside Gadadhara again?[^10-55]

[^10-51]: Signature: "Nayanananda." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 231 (printed p. 220), 17th pallava, no. 44 (label "॥৪৪॥২১০২॥"); raga dhanashi;
P-R-Sa MS no. 2211. GPT1 — p. 154, no. 126 (dhanashri); GPT2 — sec. 3.1, no. 126.
[^10-52]: The bimba is a bright red fruit, the usual comparison for lips. The Lord's lips move — He is ceaselessly chanting the
holy name. MSS "ka," "kha," "gha," "ca," GPT1: "bimba biṛambita adhara."
[^10-53]: The clouds of His eyes are His eyes full of tears. MS "gha": "chāna" instead of "chānda" (beauty, shape), "haiyā" instead of
"heriyā."
[^10-54]: "nabāñcala" is unclear; GPT1: "Gora of new rasa" (naba rasera gorā). MSS "ka," "kha," "ca," GPT1: "of touch" (paraśera) instead of "of
rasa" (rasera); "gha": "rasera."
[^10-55]: The poet's question betrays longing: it seems he can no longer see Gaura beside Gadadhara in Navadvipa.

## 14. Nayanananda — "kinā se sukhera sarobare…" (PK 2103)
*Vishvambhara's dance is a lake of joy from which the waves of prema splash over the brim: the earth cannot hold His
feet, His face is a golden moon pouring nectar; His companions are royal swans, bees and chakoras; the treasure of
bhakti has come without effort to all the poor and wretched — Vrindavana has become the town of Nadia. The raga is not
named ("the same raga" — dhanashi).*[^10-56]

কিনা সে সুখের সরোবরে ।
প্রেমের তরঙ্গ উথলিয়া পড়ে ধারে ॥

*kinā se sukhera sarobare |*
*premera taraṅga uthaliyā paṛe dhāre ||*

*Word for word:* kinā se — what a; sukhera sarobare — lake of joy; premera taraṅga — the waves of prema; uthaliyā — surging; paṛe dhāre — splash over the brim

**14.1.** What a lake of joy!
The waves of prema surge and splash over the brim.

নাচত পহু বিশ্বম্ভরে ।
প্রেম-ভরে পদ ধরে ধরণী না ধরে ॥

*nācata pahu biśvambhare |*
*prema-bhare pada dhare dharaṇī nā dhare ||*

*Word for word:* nācata — dances; pahu biśvambhare — the Lord Vishvambhara; prema-bhare — drunk with prema; pada dhare — He steps; dharaṇī nā dhare — the earth cannot hold (Him)

**14.2.** The Lord Vishvambhara dances;
drunk with prema He steps — and the earth cannot hold His feet.[^10-57]

বয়ান কনয়া-চান্দ ছান্দে ।
কত সুধা বরিখয়ে থির নাহি বান্ধে ॥

*bayāna kanayā-cānda chānde |*
*kata sudhā barikhaye thira nāhi bāndhe ||*

*Word for word:* bayāna — the face; kanayā-cānda — a golden moon; chānde — in shape; kata sudhā — how much nectar; barikhaye — it pours; thira nāhi bāndhe — there is no holding it

**14.3.** His face is shaped like a golden moon:
how much nectar it pours — there is no holding it!

রাজহংস প্রিয় সহচরে ।
কেহ ভেল মধুকর কেহ বা চকোরে ॥

*rājahaṃsa priya sahacare |*
*keha bhela madhukara keha bā cakore ||*

*Word for word:* rājahaṃsa — royal swans; priya sahacare — the dear companions; keha bhela madhukara — some became bees; keha vā cakore — others chakoras

**14.4.** His companions are royal swans;
some have become bees, others chakora birds.[^10-58]

নব নব নটন-লহরী ।
প্রেম-লছমি নাচে নদিয়া-নগরী ॥

*naba naba naṭana-laharī |*
*prema-lachami nāce nadiyā-nagarī ||*

*Word for word:* naba naba — ever new; naṭana-laharī — waves of dance; prema-lachami — the Lakshmi of prema; nāce — dances; nadiyā-nagarī — the town of Nadia

**14.5.** Ever new waves of dance —
the Lakshmi of prema dances, the very town of Nadia.[^10-59]

নব নব ভকতি-রতনে ।
অযতনে পাইল সব দীন হীন জনে ॥

*naba naba bhakati-ratane |*
*ayatane pāila saba dīna hīna jane ||*

*Word for word:* naba naba — ever new; bhakati-ratane — jewels of bhakti; ayatane — without effort; pāila — obtained; saba dīna hīna jane — all the poor and wretched people

**14.6.** Ever new jewels of bhakti
all the poor and wretched have gained without effort.

নয়নানন্দ কহয়ে সুখ-সারে ।
সেই বৃন্দাবন ভেল নদীয়া নগরে ॥

*nayanānanda kahaye sukha-sāre |*
*sei bṛndābana bhela nadīyā nagare ||*

*Word for word:* nayanānanda kahaye — Nayanananda tells; sukha-sāre — of the essence of joy; sei bṛndābana — that very Vrindavana; bhela — has become; nadīyā nagare — the town of Nadia

**14.7.** Nayanananda tells the essence of joy:
that very Vrindavana has become the town of Nadia.

[^10-56]: Signature: "Nayanananda." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 231 (printed p. 220), 17th pallava, no. 45 (label "॥৪৫॥২১০৩॥"); P-R-Sa MS no.
2212. GPT1 — p. 31, no. 16 (dhanashi); GPT2 gives the pada twice (sec. 1.3, no. 16; sec. 4.2, no. 31).
[^10-57]: MS "gha": "from the weight (of prema)" (bhare) instead of "steps" (dhare). GPT1: "premabhare pada dhare dharaṇī nā dhare."
[^10-58]: The bees cling to the Lord's lotus feet, the chakoras (birds that drink moonlight) to the moon of His face.
[^10-59]: MS "ka": "lachimā." GPT1: "prema lachimā nāce nadīyā-nāgarī" — "…the town-woman of Nadia dances." The PK reading "nadiyā-nagarī" (the
town of Nadia) is adopted.

## 15. Nayanananda — "dekha dekha gorā-naṭa raṅga…" (PK 2106)
*An auspicious kirtana — a circle of the great rasa where the former, Vrindavana days come alive: Nityananda, Advaita,
Srivasa, Mukunda, Murari, Ramananda and Vakreshvara dance; Gora dances with Gadadhara, the mridanga resounds. In the
Lord of Navadvipa are all the incarnations: each sees his own bhava before his eyes. Raga mangala.*[^10-60]

দেখ দেখ গোরা-নট রঙ্গ ।
কীর্ত্তন মঙ্গল মহারাস-মণ্ডল
উপজিল পুরব-প্রসঙ্গ ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*dekha dekha gorā-naṭa raṅga |*
*kīrttana maṅgala mahārāsa-maṇḍala*
*upajila puraba-prasaṅga || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* dekha dekha — look, look; gorā-naṭa raṅga — at the dance of Gora the dancer; kīrttana maṅgala — the auspicious kirtana; mahārāsa-maṇḍala — the circle of the great rasa; upajila — has come alive; puraba-prasaṅga — the former (Vrindavana) story

**15.1.** *(Refrain)* Look, look at the dance of Gora the dancer!
An auspicious kirtana — the circle of the great rasa,
in it the former days have come alive.[^10-61]

নাচে পহু নিত্যানন্দ ঠাকুর অদ্বৈতচন্দ্র
শ্রীনিবাস মুকুন্দ মুরারি ।
রামানন্দ বক্রেশ্বর আর যত সহচর
প্রেম-সিন্ধু আনন্দ-লহরী ॥

*nāce pahu nityānanda ṭhākura advaitacandra*
*śrīnibāsa mukunda murāri |*
*rāmānanda bakreśvara āra yata sahacara*
*prema-sindhu ānanda-laharī ||*

*Word for word:* nāce — dances; pahu nityānanda — the Lord Nityananda; ṭhākura advaitacandra — Thakura Advaitachandra; śrīnibāsa mukunda murāri — Srinivasa, Mukunda, Murari; rāmānanda bakreśvara — Ramananda, Vakreshvara; āra yata sahacara — and all the other companions; prema-sindhu — an ocean of prema; ānanda-laharī — waves of bliss

**15.2.** The Lord Nityananda dances, Thakura Advaitachandra,
Srinivasa, Mukunda, Murari,
Ramananda, Vakreshvara and all the other companions —
an ocean of prema, waves of bliss.

ঠাকুর পণ্ডিত গায় গোবিন্দ আনন্দে বায়
নাচে গোরা গদাধর সঙ্গে ।
দ্রিমিকি দ্রিমিকি থৈয়া তা থৈয়া তা থৈয়া থৈয়া
বাজত মোহন মৃদঙ্গে ॥

*ṭhākura paṇḍita gāya gobinda ānande bāya*
*nāce gorā gadādhara saṅge |*
*drimiki drimiki thaiyā tā thaiyā tā thaiyā thaiyā*
*bājata mohana mṛdaṅge ||*

*Word for word:* ṭhākura paṇḍita gāya — Thakura Pandita sings; gobinda ānande bāya — Govinda plays in bliss; nāce gorā — Gora dances; gadādhara saṅge — with Gadadhara; drimiki… thaiyā — (imitation of the mridanga); bājata — sounds; mohana mṛdaṅge — the enchanting mridanga

**15.3.** Thakura Pandita sings, Govinda plays in bliss,
Gora dances together with Gadadhara;
"drimiki drimiki thaiyā, tā thaiyā, tā thaiyā thaiyā" —
the enchanting mridanga sounds.[^10-62]

যত যত অবতারে সুখময় সুখ-সারে
এই মোর নবদ্বীপ-নাথে ।
যার যেই নিজ ভাব পরতেকে দেখ সব
নয়নানন্দের রহু চিতে ॥

*yata yata abatāre sukhamaya sukha-sāre*
*ei mora nabadvīpa-nāthe |*
*yāra yei nija bhāba parateke dekha saba*
*nayanānandera rahu cite ||*

*Word for word:* yata yata abatāre — all the incarnations; sukhamaya sukha-sāre — full of joy, the essence of joy; ei mora nabadvīpa-nāthe — in this Lord of Navadvipa of mine; yāra yei nija bhāba — whatever bhava one has; parateke dekha saba — see it all before your eyes; nayanānandera rahu cite — may it abide in Nayanananda's heart

**15.4.** All the incarnations, full of joy, the essence of joy,
are in this Lord of Navadvipa of mine:
whatever bhava one has — see it all before your eyes.
May this abide in Nayanananda's heart![^10-63]

[^10-60]: Signature: "Nayanananda." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 232 (printed p. 221), 17th pallava, no. 48 (label "॥৪৮॥২১০৬॥"); raga mangala;
P-R-Sa MS no. 2215. GPT1 — p. 258, no. 33 (mangala); GPT2 — sec. 4.2, no. 33. The preceding pada PK 2105
("gorā nāce naba naba raṅgiyā") is unsigned in PK, and in MS P-R it has additional stanzas with Lochana's signature; it does not belong
to Nayanananda. The linking of pada NS-016 ("jhulata rasamaya gaurakiśora") to PK 2106 is mistaken.
[^10-61]: The maha-rasa is Krishna's circle dance with the gopis; Gaura's kirtana is like it. "The former days" are the pastimes of
Vrindavana.
[^10-62]: Who is called "Thakura Pandita" is unclear (perhaps Srivasa Pandita). Govinda is probably Govinda Ghosha or a
mridanga player among the companions. MS "gha": "bājāyata" (plays). The syllables imitate the mridanga.
[^10-63]: Gaura is the source of all incarnations (cf. CC Adi 2: Krishna is the avatari, the source of the avatars): each devotee sees
in Him the One he worships. GPT1: "…nayanānandera rahu cite."

## 16. Nayanananda — "nācaye gaurāṅga gadādhara-mukha cāñā…" (PK 2179)
*Gauranga dances gazing at Gadadhara's face: looking at each other, both are lost, they embrace, tremble and shed tears —
body, mind and speech are one in them, one life; the town women of Nadia watch from afar and grasp the secret in their
hearts. Raga varadi.*[^10-64]

নাচয়ে গৌরাঙ্গ গদাধর-মুখ চাঞা ।
অন্তরে পরশ-রস উথলিল হিয়া ॥

*nācaye gaurāṅga gadādhara-mukha cāñā |*
*antare paraśa-rasa uthalila hiyā ||*

*Word for word:* nācaye gaurāṅga — Gauranga dances; gadādhara-mukha cāñā — gazing at Gadadhara's face; antare — within; paraśa-rasa — the rasa of touch; uthalila hiyā — flooded the heart

**16.1.** Gauranga dances, gazing at Gadadhara's face;
within, the rasa of touch has risen and flooded His heart.

দুহুঁ মুখ নিরখিতে দুহুঁ ভেল ভোর ।
দুহুঁ ভেল রস-নিধি অমিয়া চকোর ॥

*duhum̐ mukha nirakhite duhum̐ bhela bhora |*
*duhum̐ bhela rasa-nidhi amiyā cakora ||*

*Word for word:* duhum̐ mukha nirakhite — looking into each other's faces; duhum̐ bhela bhora — both were lost; duhum̐ bhela — both became; rasa-nidhi — an ocean of rasa; amiyā cakora — (and) a chakora (drinking) nectar

**16.2.** Looking into each other's faces, both are lost:
each has become for the other an ocean of rasa — and a chakora drinking nectar.[^10-65]

বুকে বুকে মিলি দুহেঁ কয়লহি কোর ।
কাঁপি পুলক দুহুঁ ঝাঁপই লোর ॥

*buke buke mili duhem̐ kayalahi kora |*
*kām̐pi pulaka duhum̐ jhām̐pai lora ||*

*Word for word:* buke buke mili — chest to chest; duhem̐ kayalahi kora — the two embraced; kām̐pi — trembling; pulaka — (with) hair on end; duhum̐ — both; jhām̐pai lora — are covered with tears

**16.3.** Chest to chest, the two have embraced,
they tremble, their hair stands on end, both are flooded with tears.[^10-66]

তনু মন বাণী দুহুঁ একই পরাণ ।
প্রতি অঙ্গে পিরিতি-অমিয়া নিরমাণ ॥

*tanu mana bāṇī duhum̐ ekai parāṇa |*
*prati aṅge piriti-amiyā niramāṇa ||*

*Word for word:* tanu mana bāṇī — body, mind, speech; duhum̐ — of both; ekai parāṇa — one life; prati aṅge — every limb; piriti-amiyā — of the nectar of love; niramāṇa — made

**16.4.** Body, mind and speech in both are one life;
every limb of theirs is made of the nectar of love.

পণ্ডিতে মণ্ডিত ভেল গোরা নট-রাজ ।
দূর সঞে দেখে সব নাগরী-সমাজ ॥

*paṇḍite maṇḍita bhela gorā naṭa-rāja |*
*dūra sañe dekhe saba nāgarī-samāja ||*

*Word for word:* paṇḍite maṇḍita bhela — was adorned by the Pandita; gorā naṭa-rāja — Gora, the king of dancers; dūra sañe — from afar; dekhe — watch; saba nāgarī-samāja — all the town women

**16.5.** Gora, the king of dancers, is adorned by the Pandita;
from afar all the town women are watching.[^10-67]

নদীয়া-নাগরীগণ বুঝিল মরমে ।
যার পরসাদে পাই প্রেম-রতনে ॥

*nadīyā-nāgarīgaṇa bujhila marame |*
*yāra parasāde pāi prema-ratane ||*

*Word for word:* nadīyā-nāgarīgaṇa — the town women of Nadia; bujhila marame — grasped in their hearts; yāra parasāde — by whose grace; pāi — I obtain; prema-ratane — the jewel of prema

**16.6.** The town women of Nadia have grasped in their hearts
the One by whose grace I obtain the jewel of prema.

গদাধর-প্রেম-বশ গৌর রসিয়া ।
কহয়ে নয়নানন্দ এ রসে ভাসিয়া ॥

*gadādhara-prema-baśa gaura rasiyā |*
*kahaye nayanānanda e rase bhāsiyā ||*

*Word for word:* gadādhara-prema-baśa — subdued by Gadadhara's love; gaura rasiyā — rasa-drunk Gaura; kahaye nayanānanda — Nayanananda says; e rase bhāsiyā — floating in this rasa

**16.7.** Subdued by Gadadhara's love is the rasa-drunk Gaura —
so says Nayanananda, floating in this rasa.

[^10-64]: Signature: "Nayanananda." PK: vol. 3, PDF pp. 260–261 (printed pp. 249–250), 4th shakha, 19th pallava "śrīgaurāṅgera rūpa —
nāgarī ukti" (Gauranga's form — the words of the town women), no. 12 (label "॥১২॥২১৭৯॥"); raga varadi; P-R-Sa MS no. 2287. GPT1 —
p. 259, no. 35 (varadi); GPT2 — sec. 4.2, no. 35.
[^10-65]: The chakora is a bird believed to drink moonlight: each of the two is both the moon and the one who drinks its nectar.
[^10-66]: The embrace of Gaura and Gadadhara is an expression of prema: Gadadhara is the manifestation of Radha, and their love
sings of the spiritual prema of Radha and Krishna, not of a worldly feeling. MSS "ka," "kha": "duhum̐"; "gha": "dohe" (16.3, 16.4).
[^10-67]: Raya placed the pada in the section of the nagaris' (town women's) words; here the town women only watch from afar
and grasp the secret of the love of Gaura and Gadadhara. The words about young women are the language of nagari-bhava
(Gaura as the nagara, the beloved of the town's women); we translate faithfully to the author. Vrindavana Dasa stresses that
in this incarnation the Lord never glanced at another man's wife; worship of Gaura in the spirit of "Gaura-nagari" is not
accepted by the Gaudiya tradition (Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja, Bhaktisiddhanta). MSS "ka," "kha," P-R-Sa: without
"all" (saba).

## 17. Nayanananda — "o rūpa sundara gaura kiśora…" (PK 2115)
*The beauty of youthful Gaura, at which one cannot gaze enough: He is prema itself made visible, a golden mountain strewn
with flowers; thirsting for the prema of her who is full of rasa, He is beyond the meditation of Shiva, Shuka and Ananta;
the poet is a bee at His lotus feet. Raga suhai.*[^10-68]

ও রূপ সুন্দর গৌর কিশোর ।
হেরইতে নয়নে আরতি নাহি ওর ॥

*o rūpa sundara gaura kiśora |*
*heraite nayane ārati nāhi ora ||*

*Word for word:* o rūpa sundara — how beautiful the form; gaura kiśora — of youthful Gaura; heraite nayane — gazing with the eyes; ārati — to the longing; nāhi ora — there is no end

**17.1.** How beautiful is the form of youthful Gaura —
however much I gaze, there is no end to the longing to gaze.

কর পদ সুন্দর অধর সুরাগ ।
নব অনুরাগিণি নব অনুরাগ ॥

*kara pada sundara adhara surāga |*
*naba anurāgiṇi naba anurāga ||*

*Word for word:* kara pada sundara — beautiful hands and feet; adhara surāga — red lips; naba anurāgiṇi — (for) the new girl in love; naba anurāga — a new love

**17.2.** Beautiful are His hands and feet, red are His lips;
for the new girl in love — a new love.[^10-69]

লোল বিলোচন লোলত লোর ।
রসবতি-হৃদয়ে বান্ধল প্রেম-ডোর ॥

*lola bilocana lolata lora |*
*rasabati-hṛdaye bāndhala prema-ḍora ||*

*Word for word:* lola bilocana — restless eyes; lolata lora — restlessly the tears flow; rasabati-hṛdaye — to the heart of her who is full of rasa (Radha); bāndhala — has tied; prema-ḍora — with the cord of prema

**17.3.** His eyes are restless, restlessly His tears flow;
to the heart of her who is full of rasa He has tied Himself with the cord of prema.

পরতেক প্রেম কিয়ে মনমথ-রাজ ।
কাঞ্চন-গিরি কিয়ে কুসুম-সমাজ ॥

*parateka prema kiye manamatha-rāja |*
*kāñcana-giri kiye kusuma-samāja ||*

*Word for word:* parateka prema — prema made visible; kiye — or; manamatha-rāja — King Manmatha; kāñcana-giri — a golden mountain; kiye — or; kusuma-samāja — a gathering of flowers

**17.4.** Is this prema itself made visible — or King Manmatha?
A golden mountain — or a gathering of flowers?[^10-70]

তছু প্রেম-লম্পট শ্রীগৌরাঙ্গ রায় ।
শিব শুক অনন্ত ধেয়ানে নাহি পায় ॥

*tachu prema-lampaṭa śrīgaurāṅga rāya |*
*śiba śuka ananta dheyāne nāhi pāya ||*

*Word for word:* tachu prema-lampaṭa — thirsting for her prema; śrī-gaurāṅga rāya — Sri Gauranga Raya; śiba śuka ananta — Shiva, Shuka, Ananta; dheyāne nāhi pāya — do not reach in meditation

**17.5.** Thirsting for her prema is Sri Gauranga Raya —
He whom Shiva, Shuka and Ananta do not reach in meditation.[^10-71]

পুলক-পটল-বলয়িত সব অঙ্গ ।
প্রেমবতি-আলিঙ্গনে লহরি-তরঙ্গ ॥

*pulaka-paṭala-balayita saba aṅga |*
*premabati-āliṅgane lahari-taraṅga ||*

*Word for word:* pulaka-paṭala — with layers of thrilling hair; balayita — ringed; saba aṅga — the whole body; premabati-āliṅgane — in the embrace of her who is full of prema; lahari-taraṅga — wave upon wave

**17.6.** His whole body is ringed with layers of thrilling hair;
in the embrace of her who is full of prema — wave upon wave.

তছু পদ-পঙ্কজ অলি সহকার ।
কহ নয়নানন্দ চীত বিহার ॥

*tachu pada-paṅkaja ali sahakāra |*
*kaha nayanānanda cīta bihāra ||*

*Word for word:* tachu pada-paṅkaja — His lotus feet; ali — (for) the bee; sahakāra — the flowering mango; kaha nayanānanda — Nayanananda says; cīta bihāra — the heart's delight

**17.7.** His lotus feet are a flowering mango for the bee:
so says Nayanananda — in them is his heart's delight.[^10-72]

[^10-68]: Signature: "Nayanananda." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 236 (printed p. 225), 4th shakha, 18th pallava "śrīgaurāṅgera rūpa prabhṛti"
(Gauranga's form, etc.), no. 7 (label "॥৭॥২১১৫॥"); raga suhai; P-R-Sa MS no. 2223. GPT1 — twice: p. 136, no. 74 and p. 278, no. 2
(suhai); GPT2 — sec. 3.1, no. 74 and sec. 4.3, no. 2. In GPT1 (p. 136) it is preceded (no. 73) by a pada signed by Narahari, "suradhunītīre gaura
naṭanāgara" (wrongly ascribed to Nayanananda in the catalogue — NN-006).
[^10-69]: "The new girl in love" (naba-anurāgiṇī), "her who is full of rasa" (rasabatī), "her who is full of prema" (premabatī) are
Radha; behind this in the pada stands also Gadadhara, Her manifestation. Gaura is Krishna who longs to taste Radha's prema
and has accepted Her bhava (CC Adi 1.6; Adi 4); this is spiritual prema, not worldly passion.
[^10-70]: Manmatha (Kamadeva) is the god of love; the Lord is the transcendental Madana who surpasses him (CC Madhya 8).
[^10-71]: "Thirsting" (lampaṭa) — of the Lord thirsting for the prema of His devotee. MS P-R-Sa: "achu," "Ananta and others" (anantādi),
"nā" instead of "nāhi."
[^10-72]: Sahakara is the flowering mango tree, beloved of bees. MS P-R-Sa: "balaithe"; "kha," "ca," P-R-Sa: "lahali" (17.6); "ka": "kahala,"
"gha": "kahaye." GPT1: "…kayala nayanānanda citabihāra" — "Nayanananda has made (them) the pleasure-ground of his heart."

## 18. Nayanananda — "āota piriti muratimaya sāgara…" (PK 2116)
*The pastimes in Nadia: the Lord is an ocean of love in person; in Him is all the wealth of Vaikuntha and Vrindavana;
blessed has become the Ganga in which He bathes; in every house and temple, under every grove and in every flowering
garden are His pastimes; Vishvambhara has fulfilled the hopes of all. Raga bala-dhanashi.*[^10-73]

আওত পিরিতি মুরতিময় সাগর
অপরূপ পহু দ্বিজ-রাজ ।
নব নব ভকত ভকতি নব রতন সু-
বাচত নটন-সমাজ ॥

*āota piriti muratimaya sāgara*
*aparūpa pahu dvija-rāja |*
*naba naba bhakata bhakati naba ratana su-*
*bācata naṭana-samāja ||*

*Word for word:* āota — comes; piriti-muratimaya — of love embodied; sāgara — an ocean; aparūpa pahu — the wondrous Lord; dvija-rāja — the king of the twice-born; naba naba bhakata — ever new devotees; bhakati — devotion; naba ratana — new treasures; su-bācata (?) — glorious (?); naṭana-samāja — the circle of dancers

**18.1.** He comes — an ocean, love itself embodied,
the wondrous Lord, the king of the twice-born;
ever new devotees, new devotion, new treasures —
glorious is the circle of dancers.[^10-74]

ভালি ভালি নদিয়া-বিহার ।
সকল বৈকুণ্ঠ-বৃন্দাবন-সম্পদ
সকল সুখের সুখ-সার ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*bhāli bhāli nadiyā-bihāra |*
*sakala baikuṇṭha-bṛndābana-sampada*
*sakala sukhera sukha-sāra || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* bhāli bhāli — splendid, splendid; nadiyā-bihāra — the pastimes in Nadia; sakala baikuṇṭha-bṛndābana-sampada — all the wealth of Vaikuntha and Vrindavana; sakala sukhera — of all joys; sukha-sāra — the essence of joy

**18.2.** *(Refrain)* Splendid, splendid are the pastimes in Nadia!
All the wealth of Vaikuntha and Vrindavana,
the essence of the joy of all joys.

ধনি ধনি অতি ধনি অব ভেল সুরধুনি
আনন্দে বহে রস-ধার ।
স্নান পান অবগাহ আলিঙ্গন
সঙ্গম কত কত বার ॥

*dhani dhani ati dhani aba bhela suradhuni*
*ānande bahe rasa-dhāra |*
*snāna pāna abagāha āliṅgana*
*saṅgama kata kata bāra ||*

*Word for word:* dhani dhani ati dhani — blessed, blessed, thrice blessed; aba bhela — now has become; suradhuni — the Suradhuni (Ganga); ānande — in bliss; bahe rasa-dhāra — flows with streams of rasa; snāna pāna abagāha — bathing, drinking, immersion; āliṅgana — embrace; saṅgama — meeting (touching); kata kata bāra — how many times

**18.3.** Blessed, blessed, thrice blessed now has the Suradhuni become:
in bliss she flows with streams of rasa;
bathing, drinking, immersion, embrace —
how many, many times she meets Him![^10-75]

প্রতি পুর মন্দির প্রতি তরুকুল-তল
প্রতি ফুল-বিপিন বিলাস ।
কহে নয়নানন্দ প্রেমে বিশ্বম্ভর
সভাকার পূরল আশ ॥

*prati pura mandira prati tarukula-tala*
*prati phula-bipina bilāsa |*
*kahe nayanānanda preme biśvambhara*
*sabhākāra pūrala āśa ||*

*Word for word:* prati pura mandira — in every house and temple; prati tarukula-tala — under every grove; prati phula-bipina — in every flowering garden; bilāsa — pastimes; kahe nayanānanda — Nayanananda says; preme biśvambhara — Vishvambhara with prema; sabhākāra — of all; pūrala āśa — fulfilled the hopes

**18.4.** In every house, in every temple, under every grove,
in every flowering garden are His pastimes.
Nayanananda says: Vishvambhara with prema
has fulfilled the hopes of all.

[^10-73]: Signature: "Nayanananda." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 236 (printed p. 225), 18th pallava, no. 8 (label "॥৮॥২১১৬॥"); raga
bala-dhanashi; P-R-Sa MS no. 2224. GPT1 — p. 32, no. 17 (bala-dhanashi); GPT2 — sec. 1.3, no. 17.
[^10-74]: "The king of the twice-born" is both the moon and the best of brahmanas. The end of the stanza is unclear ("su- / bācata");
GPT1: "naba naba bhakata, naba rasa yābata, naba tanu ratana samāja" — "ever new devotees, all new rasa, a gathering of new
precious bodies."
[^10-75]: The Suradhuni is the Ganga. The river is blessed because the Lord bathes in her, drinks her water and immerses Himself
in her: her "embrace" and "meeting" with Him are an image of the Ganga's happiness at touching the Lord. GPT1: "…āliṅgana saṅgama,
kata kata bāra."

## 19. Nayanananda — "gadādhara-mukha heri kibā uṭhe mane…" (PK 2114)
*The Lord's bhava: gazing at Gadadhara's face, He remembers the joys of the groves of Vrindavana, pines like a poor man
who has lost a touchstone, weeps, "Hari, Hari!", sways and falls to the ground. The poet asks: from whose love comes such
turmoil? Raga pathamanjari.*[^10-76]

গদাধর-মুখ হেরি কিবা উঠে মনে ।
সোঙরি সে সব সুখ নিকুঞ্জ বৃন্দাবনে ॥

*gadādhara-mukha heri kibā uṭhe mane |*
*soṅari se saba sukha nikuñja bṛndābane ||*

*Word for word:* gadādhara-mukha heri — gazing at Gadadhara's face; kibā uṭhe mane — what rises in the heart; soṅari — remembering; se saba sukha — all those joys; nikuñja bṛndābane — in the groves of Vrindavana

**19.1.** Gazing at Gadadhara's face — what rises in His heart?
He remembers all those joys in the groves of Vrindavana.

ঝুরয়ে সদাই মন সে গুণ শুনিয়া ।
হারাইল দুখী যেন পরশ-মণিয়া ॥

*jhuraye sadāi mana se guṇa śuniyā |*
*hārāila dukhī yena paraśa-maṇiyā ||*

*Word for word:* jhuraye sadāi mana — the heart pines ceaselessly; se guṇa śuniyā — hearing of those virtues; hārāila — has lost; dukhī — a poor man; yena — as if; paraśa-maṇiyā — the touchstone

**19.2.** Hearing of those virtues, His heart pines ceaselessly —
like a poor man who has lost a touchstone.

হরি হরি বলে পহু কান্দিতে কান্দিতে ।
না জানি কাহার ভাব উপজিল চিতে ॥

*hari hari bale pahu kāndite kāndite |*
*nā jāni kāhāra bhāba upajila cite ||*

*Word for word:* hari hari bale — says "Hari, Hari"; pahu — the Lord; kāndite kāndite — weeping and weeping; nā jāni — who can tell; kāhāra bhāba — whose bhava; upajila cite — has arisen in the heart

**19.3.** "Hari, Hari!" says the Lord, weeping and weeping;
who can tell whose bhava has arisen in His heart?

টলমল করয়ে সোণার বরণখানি ।
ঢুলিয়া ঢুলিয়া পড়ে লোটায় ধরণী ॥

*ṭalamala karaye soṇāra baraṇakhāni |*
*ḍhuliyā ḍhuliyā paṛe loṭāya dharaṇī ||*

*Word for word:* ṭalamala karaye — sways unsteadily; soṇāra baraṇakhāni — the golden form; ḍhuliyā ḍhuliyā — reeling and reeling; paṛe — falls; loṭāya dharaṇī — rolls on the ground

**19.4.** His golden form sways unsteadily;
reeling and reeling, He falls and rolls on the ground.

কহয়ে নয়নানন্দ গদাধর আগে ।
এত পরমাদ হৈল কার অনুরাগে ॥

*kahaye nayanānanda gadādhara āge |*
*eta paramāda haila kāra anurāge ||*

*Word for word:* kahaye nayanānanda — Nayanananda says; gadādhara āge — before Gadadhara; eta paramāda — such turmoil; haila — has come; kāra anurāge — from whose love

**19.5.** Nayanananda says before Gadadhara:
from whose love comes such turmoil?[^10-77]

[^10-76]: Signature: "Nayanananda." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 235 (printed p. 224), 18th pallava, no. 6 (label "॥৬॥২১১৪॥"); raga pathamanjari.
GPT1 — p. 278, no. 1 (pathamanjari; section "bhavavesha and pralapa"). A pada on Radha's bhava in the Lord: Gadadhara awakens
in Him the memory of Vrindavana.
[^10-77]: The answer is implied: it is the love (anuraga) of Radha, whose bhava the Lord has accepted; Gadadhara is Her
manifestation.

## 20. Balarama Dasa — "gaura manohara nāgara-śekhara…" (PK 2113)
*Gaura's form and bhava: at the sight of Him countless Kamas faint, the autumn moon weeps gazing at His face; He
ceaselessly chants His own name, and on looking at Gadadhara's face He cries, "Rai, Rai!" and falls to the ground,
seized by the fever of separation; weeping, He takes the fallen by the hand. Raga todi.*[^10-78]

গৌর মনোহর নাগর-শেখর ।
হেরইতে মুরছই অসিম কুসুম-শর ॥

*gaura manohara nāgara-śekhara |*
*heraite murachai asima kusuma-śara ||*

*Word for word:* gaura manohara — enchanting Gaura; nāgara-śekhara — the crown of elegant youths; heraite — on seeing (Him); murachai — faint; asima kusuma-śara — countless Flower-arrowed Ones

**20.1.** Gaura, the enchanting crown of elegant youths:
seeing Him, countless Flower-arrowed Ones faint.[^10-79]

কাঞ্চন রুচিতর রুচিত কলেবর ।
মুখ হেরি রোয়ত শরদ-সুধাকর ॥

*kāñcana rucitara rucita kalebara |*
*mukha heri royata śarada-sudhākara ||*

*Word for word:* kāñcana — than gold; rucitara — brighter; rucita — shining; kalebara — the body; mukha heri — gazing at the face; royata — weeps; śarada-sudhākara — the autumn moon

**20.2.** His body shines brighter than gold —
gazing at His face, the autumn moon weeps.

জিনি মদ-কুঞ্জর গতি অতি মন্থর ।
অধর-সুধারস মধুর হসিত ঝর ॥

*jini mada-kuñjara gati ati manthara |*
*adhara-sudhārasa madhura hasita jhara ||*

*Word for word:* jini mada-kuñjara — surpassing a drunken elephant; gati ati manthara — the gait is very slow; adhara-sudhārasa — the nectar of the lips; madhura hasita — a sweet smile; jhara — flows

**20.3.** His gait is slower than a drunken elephant's;
from the nectar of His lips flows a sweet smile.[^10-80]

নিজ নাম মন্তর জপয়ে নিরন্তর ।
ভাবে অবশ তনু গরগর অন্তর ॥

*nija nāma mantara japaye nirantara |*
*bhābe abaśa tanu garagara antara ||*

*Word for word:* nija nāma mantara — the mantra of His own name; japaye nirantara — chants ceaselessly; bhābe abaśa tanu — the body helpless in bhava; garagara antara — the heart overflowing

**20.4.** Ceaselessly He chants the mantra of His own name,
His body is helpless in bhava, His heart overflowing.[^10-81]

হেরি গদাধর-মুখ অতি কাতর ।
রাই রাই করি পড়ই ধরণি পর ॥

*heri gadādhara-mukha ati kātara |*
*rāi rāi kari paṛai dharaṇi para ||*

*Word for word:* heri gadādhara-mukha — looking at Gadadhara's face; ati kātara — in great anguish; rāi rāi kari — crying "Rai, Rai"; paṛai — falls; dharaṇi para — to the ground

**20.5.** Looking at Gadadhara's face, He is in great anguish:
"Rai, Rai!" He cries and falls to the ground.[^10-82]

লোচন-জলধর বরিখয়ে ঝরঝর ।
মরমে ভরল খর বিষম বিরহ-জ্বর ॥

*locana-jaladhara barikhaye jharajhara |*
*marame bharala khara biṣama biraha-jvara ||*

*Word for word:* locana-jaladhara — the clouds of the eyes; barikhaye jharajhara — pour in torrents; marame bharala — has filled the heart; khara biṣama — sharp, cruel; biraha-jvara — the fever of separation

**20.6.** The clouds of His eyes pour in torrents,
His heart is filled with the sharp, cruel fever of separation.

অতি রসে গরগর না চিনে আপন পর ।
রোয়ত করে ধরি পতিত নীচতর ॥

*ati rase garagara nā cine āpana para |*
*royata kare dhari patita nīcatara ||*

*Word for word:* ati rase garagara — overflowing with rasa; nā cine — does not recognise; āpana para — His own and others; royata — weeping; kare dhari — taking by the hand; patita nīcatara — the fallen and the lowest

**20.7.** Overflowing with rasa, He does not know His own from others:
weeping, He takes by the hand the fallen and the lowest.[^10-83]

ও রস-সাগরে মগন সুরাসুর ।
বিন্দু না পরশল বলরাম দাস পর ॥

*o rasa-sāgare magana surāsura |*
*bindu nā paraśala balarāma dāsa para ||*

*Word for word:* o rasa-sāgare — in that ocean of rasa; magana — plunged; surāsura — gods and asuras; bindu nā paraśala — not a drop touched; balarāma dāsa para — Balarama Dasa

**20.8.** Gods and asuras have plunged into this ocean of rasa —
not a drop has touched Balarama Dasa.[^10-84]

[^10-78]: Signature: "Balarama Dasa." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 235 (printed p. 224), 18th pallava, no. 5 (label "॥৫॥২১১৩॥"); raga todi; P-R-Sa MS
no. 2221, P-R 14.76. GPT1 — p. 141 (todi; without the couplet 20.6b–20.7a); GPT2 — sec. 3.1. The pada was not in the catalogue
(new row BD-042); its attribution to one of the Balarama Dasas is not established.
[^10-79]: "Nāgara-śekhara," "the crown of elegant youths," is an epithet of Krishna. The Flower-arrowed One (kusuma-śara) is
Kamadeva.
[^10-80]: MS "gha": "ruciratara"; "ka," "kha," "ca," P-R-Sa: "racita" (20.2). MSS "ka," "kha," "gha," "ca," P-R-Sa, GPT1: "drunken" (matta)
instead of "mada"; "ka," "kha," "gha," "ca," P-R-Sa: "rasa" instead of "sudhārasa."
[^10-81]: Gaura chants the names of Krishna — His own name. MSS P-R-Sa, P-R: "antara" instead of "mantara"; "ka," "ca," P-R-Sa, P-R: "bharama,"
"kha": "marama" instead of "antara" (at the end of the line).
[^10-82]: Rai is Radha: in Krishna's mood the Lord, seeing Gadadhara, calls Radha and pines in separation from Her. The PK scan has
"rāha rāi" (a misprint); GPT1: "rāi rāi."
[^10-83]: MS "gha," P-R: "jarajara" instead of "garagara."
[^10-84]: MS P-R: "of joy" (sukha) instead of "of rasa," "people" (narinara) instead of "gods and asuras."

## 21. Nayanananda — "kāndaye mahāprabhu gadādhara saṅge…" (PK 2181)
*Mahaprabhu weeps together with Gadadhara at the very first mention of their former love; remembering the joys of the
groves, both are filled with prema, they come to greet each other with sandal paste, garlands, tulasi and durva grass,
embrace and float in rasa; the three worlds are maddened by their ecstasy. Raga varadi.*[^10-85]

কান্দয়ে মহাপ্রভু গদাধর সঙ্গে ।
পহিলহি পুরুব পিরিতি-পরসঙ্গে ॥

*kāndaye mahāprabhu gadādhara saṅge |*
*pahilahi puruba piriti-parasaṅge ||*

*Word for word:* kāndaye mahāprabhu — Mahaprabhu weeps; gadādhara saṅge — together with Gadadhara; pahilahi — at the very first; puruba piriti-parasaṅge — mention of the former love

**21.1.** Mahaprabhu weeps together with Gadadhara —
at the very first mention of their former love.

সোঙরি সে সব সুখ নিকুঞ্জ-কাননে ।
উপজল দুহুঁ প্রেম-ভাব মনে মনে ॥

*soṅari se saba sukha nikuñja-kānane |*
*upajala duhum̐ prema-bhāba mane mane ||*

*Word for word:* soṅari — remembering; se saba sukha — all those joys; nikuñja-kānane — in the forest groves; upajala — arose; duhum̐ — in both; prema-bhāba — the bhava of prema; mane mane — at heart

**21.2.** Remembering all those joys in the forest groves,
both were filled at heart with the bhava of prema.

সুগন্ধি চন্দন মালা তুলসী দূর্ব্বা লৈয়া ।
দুহুঁ দোহাঁ সম্ভাষণে মিলিল আসিয়া ॥

*sugandhi candana mālā tulasī dūrvvā laiyā |*
*duhum̐ dohām̐ sambhāṣaṇe milila āsiyā ||*

*Word for word:* sugandhi candana — fragrant sandal paste; mālā — garlands; tulasī dūrvvā laiyā — taking tulasi and durva; duhum̐ dohām̐ — the two, each other; sambhāṣaṇe — to greet; milila āsiyā — came together

**21.3.** With fragrant sandal paste, garlands, tulasi and durva
the two came together to greet each other.[^10-86]

হাসি হাসি পরশি পরশি করু কোর ।
দুহুঁ রসে ভাসল না বুঝল ওর ॥

*hāsi hāsi paraśi paraśi karu kora |*
*duhum̐ rase bhāsala nā bujhala ora ||*

*Word for word:* hāsi hāsi — smiling; paraśi paraśi — touching again and again; karu kora — they embrace; duhum̐ rase bhāsala — both float in rasa; nā bujhala ora — find no shore (limit)

**21.4.** Smiling, touching again and again, they embrace;
both float in rasa, finding no shore.[^10-87]

না জানি পুরুষ নারী না জানি ভকত ।
দোঁহার আবেশে তিন লোক উনমত ॥

*nā jāni puruṣa nārī nā jāni bhakata |*
*dom̐hāra ābeśe tina loka unamata ||*

*Word for word:* nā jāni — one cannot tell; puruṣa nārī — (who is) man, (who) woman; nā jāni bhakata — nor (who is) devotee; dom̐hāra ābeśe — by the ecstasy of the two; tina loka — the three worlds; unamata — are maddened

**21.5.** One cannot tell who is man, who woman, who devotee;
by the ecstasy of the two the three worlds are maddened.

কহয়ে নয়নানন্দ নিগূঢ় বিচার ।
অমিয়া-পুতলী যেন অমিয়া-আকার ॥

*kahaye nayanānanda nigūṛha bicāra |*
*amiyā-putalī yena amiyā-ākāra ||*

*Word for word:* kahaye nayanānanda — Nayanananda tells; nigūṛha bicāra — the hidden secret; amiyā-putalī — a doll of nectar; yena — as if; amiyā-ākāra — a form of nectar

**21.6.** Nayanananda tells of the hidden secret:
He is like a doll of nectar, a form made of nectar.[^10-88]

[^10-85]: Signature: "Nayanananda." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 261 (printed p. 250), 19th pallava (section of the nagaris' words), no. 14
(label "॥১৪॥২১৮১॥"); raga varadi ("tathā rāga"); P-R-Sa MS no. 2289. GPT1 — p. 282, no. 17 (section "bhavavesha and pralapa"); GPT2 —
sec. 4.3, no. 17.
[^10-86]: Tulasi and durva grass are articles of worship: Gaura and Gadadhara greet each other like worshippers. MS "ka": "duhum̐"
instead of "dohām̐"; "kha," "gha" lack the word.
[^10-87]: The embrace is an expression of the prema of Radha and Krishna revealed in Gaura and Gadadhara (cf. no. 16), not of a
worldly feeling. MS "ka": "bujhinu," "ca," GPT1: "bujhilum̐" ("…I did not grasp the limit").
[^10-88]: The couplet repeats the close of PK 2070 (no. 10.7).

## 22. Nayanananda — "madhu-ṛtu-yāmini suradhuni-tīra…" (PK 1495)
*A spring night on the bank of the Ganga: the moon shines, the Malaya breeze blows; Gaura, the king of dancers, dances
in kirtana with His companions, with Him Narahari and Gadadhara, khol and karatalas resound, the cuckoos and bees sing.
The gaura-chandrika to PK's section on the spring rasa. Raga suhai.*[^10-89]

মধু-ঋতু-যামিনি সুরধুনি-তীর ।
উজোর সুধাকর মলয়-সমীর ॥

*madhu-ṛtu-yāmini suradhuni-tīra |*
*ujora sudhākara malaya-samīra ||*

*Word for word:* madhu-ṛtu-yāmini — a spring night; suradhuni-tīra — the bank of the Suradhuni; ujora — shines; sudhākara — the moon; malaya-samīra — the Malaya breeze

**22.1.** A spring night, the bank of the Suradhuni,
the moon shines, the Malaya breeze blows.[^10-90]

সহচর সঙ্গে গৌর নট-রাজ ।
বিহরয়ে নিরুপম কীর্ত্তন মাঝ ॥

*sahacara saṅge gaura naṭa-rāja |*
*biharaye nirupama kīrttana mājha ||*

*Word for word:* sahacara saṅge — with the companions; gaura naṭa-rāja — Gaura, the king of dancers; biharaye — plays; nirupama kīrttana mājha — amid the incomparable kirtana

**22.2.** With His companions Gaura, the king of dancers,
plays amid the incomparable kirtana.

খোল করতাল-ধ্বনি নটন-হিলোল ।
ভুজ তুলি ঘন ঘন হরি হরি বোল ॥

*khola karatāla-dhvani naṭana-hilola |*
*bhuja tuli ghana ghana hari hari bola ||*

*Word for word:* khola karatāla-dhvani — the sounds of khol and karatalas; naṭana-hilola — waves of dance; bhuja tuli — raising the arms; ghana ghana — again and again; hari hari bola — "Hari, Hari!" (they call)

**22.3.** The sounds of khol and karatalas, waves of dance,
arms raised, again and again they call, "Hari, Hari!"

নরহরি গদাধর বিহরই সঙ্গ ।
নাচত গাওত কতহুঁ বিভঙ্গ ॥

*narahari gadādhara biharai saṅga |*
*nācata gāota katahum̐ bibhaṅga ||*

*Word for word:* narahari gadādhara — Narahari and Gadadhara; biharai saṅga — play together (with Him); nācata gāota — dance and sing; katahum̐ bibhaṅga — bending in every way

**22.4.** Narahari and Gadadhara play together with Him,
they dance and sing, bending in every way.

কোকিল মধুকর পঞ্চম ভাষ ।
নয়নানন্দ-পহু করয়ে বিলাস ॥

*kokila madhukara pañcama bhāṣa |*
*nayanānanda-pahu karaye bilāsa ||*

*Word for word:* kokila madhukara — the cuckoos and bees; pañcama bhāṣa — sing on the fifth note; nayanānanda-pahu — Nayanananda's Lord; karaye bilāsa — is at play

**22.5.** The cuckoos and bees sing on the fifth note —
Nayanananda's Lord is at play.[^10-91]

[^10-89]: Signature: "Nayanananda" ("nayanānanda-pahu," "Nayanananda's Lord"). PK: vol. 2, PDF p. 432 (printed p. 419), 3rd shakha, 27th pallava,
section "atha bāsantī rāsalīlā । taducita-śrīgauracandra" (gaura-chandrika to the spring rasa), no. 71 (label "॥৭১॥১৪৯৫॥"), right after Vasu
Ghosha's PK 1494 (chapter 9, no. 1); raga suhai; P-R-Sa MS no. 2045. Not found by OCR in GPT1; GPT (GPT1 p. 336, no. 48) has a
different pada of Raya Shekhara with the same lines "sahacara saṅge gaura naṭarāja। biharaye nirupama kīrtana mājha" (in the catalogue NS-018,
wrongly linked there to PK 1495). The pada was not in the catalogue (new row NN-030).
[^10-90]: The Suradhuni is the Ganga. The Malaya breeze is the warm southern wind of spring, said by poets to blow from the Malaya
hills.
[^10-91]: Panchama is the fifth note of the scale; the cuckoo sings on the panchama — a sign of spring.

## 23. Nayanananda — "ko kahum̐ ājuka ānanda-ora…" (PK 1449)
*The spring swing festival: in a flowering garden young Gaura swings, with Him Nityananda and Gadadhara, the Lord of
Shantipura sings, the companions shower Gora with red powder; all the people of Nadia come running. The gaura-chandrika
to PK's section on the spring swing and holi. Raga vasanta.*[^10-92]

কো কহুঁ আজুক আনন্দ-ওর ।
ফুল-বনে দোলত গৌর কিশোর ॥

*ko kahum̐ ājuka ānanda-ora |*
*phula-bane dolata gaura kiśora ||*

*Word for word:* ko kahum̐ — who can tell; ājuka — of today's; ānanda-ora — the limit of joy; phula-bane — in the flowering garden; dolata — swings; gaura kiśora — young Gaura

**23.1.** Who can tell how boundless today's joy is!
In a flowering garden young Gaura swings.

নিত্যানন্দ গদাধর সঙ্গে ।
শান্তিপুর-নাথ গাওই রঙ্গে ॥

*nityānanda gadādhara saṅge |*
*śāntipura-nātha gāoi raṅge ||*

*Word for word:* nityānanda gadādhara saṅge — with Nityananda and Gadadhara; śāntipura-nātha — the Lord of Shantipura; gāoi raṅge — sings merrily

**23.2.** With Him are Nityananda and Gadadhara,
the Lord of Shantipura sings merrily.[^10-93]

সহচর ফাগু পেলই গোরা-গায় ।
ধায়ই শুনি সব লোক নদিয়ায় ॥

*sahacara phāgu pelai gorā-gāya |*
*dhāyai śuni saba loka nadiyāya ||*

*Word for word:* sahacara — the companions; phāgu — phagu (red powder); pelai — throw; gorā-gāya — on Gora's body; dhāyai — run; śuni — hearing; saba loka nadiyāya — all the people in Nadia

**23.3.** The companions shower Gora with phagu;
hearing of it, all the people of Nadia come running.[^10-94]

খোল-করতাল-ধ্বনি হরি হরি বোল ।
নয়নানন্দে আনন্দে বিভোর ॥

*khola-karatāla-dhvani hari hari bola |*
*nayanānande ānande bibhora ||*

*Word for word:* khola-karatāla-dhvani — the sounds of khol and karatalas; hari hari bola — "Hari, Hari!"; nayanānande — Nayanananda; ānande bibhora — is lost in bliss

**23.4.** The sounds of khol and karatalas, "Hari, Hari!" —
Nayanananda is lost in bliss.

[^10-92]: Signature: "Nayanananda." PK: vol. 2, PDF pp. 406–407 (printed pp. 393–394), 3rd shakha, section "atha bāsantī dolā hori-bilāsa ।
