tatra śrīgauracandra" (the spring swing and holi; gaura-chandrika), no. 25 (label "॥২৫॥১৪৪৯॥"); raga vasanta; P-R-Sa MS no. 2002.
GPT1 — p. 343, no. 70 (basanta); GPT2 — sec. 5.1, no. 70. The Dola-yatra is the spring swing festival on the full moon of Phalguna
(the day of the Lord's appearance).
[^10-93]: The Lord of Shantipura is Advaita Acharya. P-R-Sa: "Gadadhara and others" (gadādhara ādi).
[^10-94]: Phagu (phag) is the red powder people throw at each other at the spring festivals. MS "ka": "smear" (lepai), P-R-Sa: "phelaye";
GPT1: "phāgu lepata." GPT1 in 23.4: "nayanānanda dīna ānande bibhola" ("poor Nayanananda…").

## 24. Nayanananda — "ācāryya-mandire bhikṣā kariyā caitanya…" (PK 2234)
*Shantipura after the sannyasa: Chaitanya takes His meal in Advaita's house and dances in the sankirtana in the
reddish robes of a sannyasi; Mukunda and Madhavananda sing; Advaita dances clapping His hands: "After so many days Gora is
in my house!" The poet, standing behind Gadadhara, sighs: what was, what has become, what is yet to be. Raga suhai.*[^10-95]

আচার্য্য-মন্দিরে ভিক্ষা করিয়া চৈতন্য ।
পতিত পাতকী দুখী করিলেন ধন্য ॥

*ācāryya-mandire bhikṣā kariyā caitanya |*
*patita pātakī dukhī karilena dhanya ||*

*Word for word:* ācāryya-mandire — in the Acharya's house; bhikṣā kariyā — having accepted alms (a meal); caitanya — Chaitanya; patita — the fallen; pātakī — the sinful; dukhī — the wretched; karilena dhanya — blessed

**24.1.** Having accepted alms in the Acharya's house, Chaitanya
has blessed the fallen, the sinful and the wretched.

চন্দনে শোভিত অঙ্গ অরুণ বসন ।
সংকীর্ত্তন মাঝে নাচে অদ্বৈত-জীবন ॥

*candane śobhita aṅga aruṇa basana |*
*saṃkīrttana mājhe nāce advaita-jībana ||*

*Word for word:* candane śobhita — adorned with sandal paste; aṅga — the body; aruṇa basana — reddish garments; saṅkīrttana mājhe — amid the sankirtana; nāce — dances; advaita-jībana — Advaita's life

**24.2.** His body anointed with sandal paste, His garments reddish —
amid the sankirtana dances Advaita's life.[^10-96]

মুকুন্দ মাধবানন্দ গায় উচ্চস্বরে ।
নিতাই চৈতন্য নাচে অদ্বৈত-মন্দিরে ॥

*mukunda mādhabānanda gāya uccasvare |*
*nitāi caitanya nāce advaita-mandire ||*

*Word for word:* mukunda mādhabānanda — Mukunda and Madhavananda; gāya uccasvare — sing aloud; nitāi caitanya — Nitai and Chaitanya; nāce — dance; advaita-mandire — in Advaita's house

**24.3.** Mukunda and Madhavananda sing at the top of their voices,
Nitai and Chaitanya dance in Advaita's house.[^10-97]

আচার্য্য গোসাঞি নাচে দিয়া করতালি ।
চির দিনে মোর ঘরে গোরা বনমালী ॥

*ācāryya gosāñi nāce diyā karatāli |*
*cira dine mora ghare gorā banamālī ||*

*Word for word:* ācāryya gosāñi — Acharya Gosani; nāce — dances; diyā karatāli — clapping His hands; cira dine — after so many days; mora ghare — in my house; gorā banamālī — Gora-Vanamali

**24.4.** Acharya Gosani dances, clapping His hands:
"After so many days — Gora-Vanamali in my house!"[^10-98]

কহয়ে নয়নানন্দ গদাধরের পাছে ।
কিবা ছিল কিবা হৈল আর কিবা আছে ॥

*kahaye nayanānanda gadādharera pāche |*
*kibā chila kibā haila āra kibā āche ||*

*Word for word:* kahaye nayanānanda — Nayanananda says; gadādharera pāche — behind Gadadhara; kibā chila — what was; kibā haila — what has become; āra kibā āche — and what is yet to be (what remains)

**24.5.** Nayanananda says, standing behind Gadadhara:
what was, what has become, and what is yet to be![^10-99]

[^10-95]: Signature: "Nayanananda." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 280 (printed p. 269), 4th shakha, 21st pallava "śrīgaurāṅgera sannyāsa ityādi"
(Gauranga's sannyasa, etc.), no. 17 (label "॥১৭॥২২৩৪॥"); raga suhai; P-R-Sa MS no. 2339. GPT1 — p. 381, no. 48 (suhai); GPT2 — sec.
5.3, no. 48. In the catalogue the one pada is entered twice: NN-021 (the first line, wrongly with no. 2235) and NN-027 (the
second line). PK 2235 ("dhara dhara dhara dhara re nitāi") is a pada signed "Murari," not Nayanananda's. Cf. CC Madhya 3; CB Antya 1.
[^10-96]: Reddish (saffron) robes are a sannyasi's garments. "Advaita's life" is Chaitanya.
[^10-97]: Mukunda is Mukunda Datta; Madhavananda is probably Madhava Ghosha. MS "gha": "advaitera ghare."
[^10-98]: Vanamali, "wearer of the forest garland," is a name of Krishna. MSS "ka," "kha," P-R-Sa: "cira dina."
[^10-99]: "Behind Gadadhara" — as his companion and disciple: the poet places himself among the witnesses. The sigh is for Nimai's
former life in Navadvipa, for the sannyasa and for the coming separation.

## 25. Nayanananda — "sakala bhakata ṭhāñi haiyā bidāya…" (PK 2236)
*The farewell in Shantipura: Gaura Raya takes leave of all the devotees, bows to His mother, receives her permission,
takes leave of Advaita and with "Haribol!" sets out for Nilachala; in the Acharya's house weeping arises. Raga suhai.*[^10-100]

সকল ভকত ঠাঞি হইয়া বিদায় ।
নীলাচল দেখিতে চলিল গৌর রায় ॥

*sakala bhakata ṭhāñi haiyā bidāya |*
*nīlācala dekhite calila gaura rāya ||*

*Word for word:* sakala bhakata ṭhāñi — from all the devotees; haiyā bidāya — having taken leave; nīlācala dekhite — to see Nilachala; calila — set out; gaura rāya — Gaura Raya

**25.1.** Having taken leave of all the devotees,
Gaura Raya set out to see Nilachala.

মায়ের চরণ বন্দি অনুমতি লৈয়া ।
অদ্বৈত আচার্য্য ঠাঞি বিদায় হইয়া ॥

*māyera caraṇa bandi anumati laiyā |*
*advaita ācāryya ṭhāñi bidāya haiyā ||*

*Word for word:* māyera caraṇa bandi — bowing at His mother's feet; anumati laiyā — receiving permission; advaita ācāryya ṭhāñi — from Advaita Acharya; bidāya haiyā — taking leave

**25.2.** Bowing at His mother's feet, receiving her permission,
taking leave of Advaita Acharya,

চলিলা গৌরাঙ্গ পহু বলি হরিবোল ।
আচার্য্য-মন্দিরে উঠে ক্রন্দনের রোল ॥

*calilā gaurāṅga pahu bali haribola |*
*ācāryya-mandire uṭhe krandanera rola ||*

*Word for word:* calilā — set out; gaurāṅga pahu — the Lord Gauranga; bali haribola — saying "Haribol"; ācāryya-mandire — in the Acharya's house; uṭhe — arose; krandanera rola — the sound of weeping

**25.3.** the Lord Gauranga set out, saying, "Haribol!" —
in the Acharya's house the sound of weeping arose.[^10-101]

গৌরাঙ্গ গৌরাঙ্গ বলি কান্দয়ে সভায় ।
কান্দয়ে নয়নানন্দ ধুলায় লোটায় ॥

*gaurāṅga gaurāṅga bali kāndaye sabhāya |*
*kāndaye nayanānanda dhulāya loṭāya ||*

*Word for word:* gaurāṅga gaurāṅga bali — crying "Gauranga, Gauranga"; kāndaye sabhāya — all weep; kāndaye nayanānanda — Nayanananda weeps; dhulāya loṭāya — rolling in the dust

**25.4.** "Gauranga, Gauranga!" all weep,
Nayanananda weeps, rolling in the dust.[^10-102]

[^10-100]: Signature: "Nayanananda." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 281 (printed p. 270), 21st pallava, no. 19 (label "॥১৯॥২২৩৬॥"); raga suhai; P-R-Sa
MS no. 2341. GPT1 — p. 381, no. 49 (suhai; the first three couplets, without signature); GPT2 — sec. 5.3, no. 49. Cf. CC Madhya 3;
CB Antya 1.
[^10-101]: GPT1: "the sound of kirtana arose" (kīrtanera rola) instead of "weeping" (krandanera rola).
[^10-102]: According to PK's apparatus, the last couplet with the signature is found only in the P-R-Sa manuscript; the attribution
to Nayanananda is therefore not fully secure.

## 26. Balarama Dasa — "anukṣaṇa aruṇa-nayana ghana ghūrata…" (BR p. 975)
*Nityananda in Gauda (Saptagrama, the house of Uddharana Datta): His reddish eyes roll ceaselessly and pour nectar, He
dances sprinkling the world with prema, now weeps, now laughs, falls senseless with "Hari" on His lips, runs crying
"Gaura, Gaura!" and gives the jewel of prema to the destitute and the lowest. Raga dhanashi.*[^10-103]

অনুক্ষণ অরুণ-নয়ন ঘন ঘূরত
টপকত লোর বিথার ।
কিয়ে ঘন অরুণ বরুণালয় সঞ্চরু
অমিয়া বরিষে অনিবার ॥

*anukṣaṇa aruṇa-nayana ghana ghūrata*
*ṭapakata lora bithāra |*
*kiye ghana aruṇa baruṇālaya sañcaru*
*amiyā bariṣe anibāra ||*

*Word for word:* anukṣaṇa — ceaselessly; aruṇa-nayana — the reddish eyes; ghana ghūrata — roll constantly; ṭapakata lora — the tears drip; bithāra — spreading; kiye — as if; ghana aruṇa — a red cloud; baruṇālaya — over the ocean; sañcaru — drifting; amiyā bariṣe — pours nectar; anibāra — unceasingly

**26.1.** Ceaselessly His reddish eyes roll,
His tears stream down and spread;
as if a red cloud drifting over the ocean
were pouring nectar without cease.

নাচে রে নিতাই বরচাঁদ ।
সিঞ্চই প্রেম-সুধা-রস জগজনে
অদভুত নটন-সুছাঁদ ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*nāce re nitāi baracām̐da |*
*siñcai prema-sudhā-rasa jagajane*
*adabhuta naṭana-suchām̐da || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* nāce re — dances; nitāi — Nitai; bara-cām̐da — the beautiful moon; siñcai — sprinkles; prema-sudhā-rasa — with the nectar-rasa of prema; jagajane — the people of the world; adabhuta — wondrous; naṭana-suchām̐da — the beauty of the dance

**26.2.** *(Refrain)* Nitai dances, the beautiful moon,
sprinkling the people of the world with the nectar-rasa of prema —
wondrous is the beauty of His dance!

পদতলে বলিত মণি-মঞ্জরী
চলত হি টলমল অঙ্গ ।
মেরু-শিখর কিয়ে তনু অনুপাম রে
ঝলমল ভাব-তরঙ্গ ॥

*padatale balita maṇi-mañjarī*
*calata hi ṭalamala aṅga |*
*meru-śikhara kiye tanu anupāma re*
*jhalamala bhāba-taraṅga ||*

*Word for word:* padatale — on the feet; balita — fastened; maṇi-mañjarī — jewelled anklets; calata hi — as He moves; ṭalamala aṅga — the body sways; meru-śikhara kiye — like the peak of Meru; tanu anupāma — the incomparable body; re — (particle); jhalamala — sparkle; bhāba-taraṅga — the waves of bhava

**26.3.** On His feet are jewelled anklets,
as He moves His whole body sways;
His body is incomparable, like the peak of Meru,
and the waves of bhava sparkle.[^10-104]

রোয়ত হসত চলত গতি মন্থর
হরি বুলি মুরছি বিভোর ।
খেনে খেনে গৌর গৌর বলি ধায়ই
আনন্দে গরজত ঘোর ॥

*royata hasata calata gati manthara*
*hari buli murachi bibhora |*
*khene khene gaura gaura bali dhāyai*
*ānande garajata ghora ||*

*Word for word:* royata — weeps; hasata — laughs; calata gati manthara — walks slowly; hari buli — saying "Hari"; muruchi — falls senseless; bibhora — lost to the world; khene khene — again and again; gaura gaura bali — crying "Gaura, Gaura"; dhāyai — runs; ānande — in bliss; garajata ghora — roars terribly

**26.4.** He weeps, laughs, walks slowly,
with "Hari!" on His lips He falls senseless, lost to the world;
again and again He runs crying "Gaura, Gaura!"
and in bliss roars terribly.

পামর পঙ্গু অধম জড় আতুর
দীন অবধি নাহি মান ।
অবিরত দুর্লভ প্রেম-রতন-ধন
যাচি জগতে করু দান ॥

*pāmara paṅgu adhama jaṛa ātura*
*dīna abadhi nāhi māna |*
*abirata durlabha prema-ratana-dhana*
*yāci jagate karu dāna ||*

*Word for word:* pāmara — the low; paṅgu — the lame; adhama — the fallen; jaṛa — the dull; ātura — the sick; dīna — the wretched; abadhi nāhi — no limit; māna — makes (no) distinction; abirata durlabha — ever unattainable; prema-ratana-dhana — the treasure, the jewel of prema; yāci — offering of Himself; jagate — to the world; karu dāna — gives freely

**26.5.** The low, the lame, the fallen, the dull, the sick —
there is no end of the wretched, yet He makes no distinction:
the ever unattainable treasure, the jewel of prema,
He Himself offers to the world and gives away freely.

অবিচল দুলহ প্রেম-ধন বিতরণে
নিখিল তাপ দূরে গেল ।
দীন হীন সবহি মনোরথ পূরল
অবলাউ উনমত ভেল ॥

*abicala dulaha prema-dhana bitaraṇe*
*nikhila tāpa dūre gela |*
*dīna hīna sabahi manoratha pūrala*
*abalāu unamata bhela ||*

*Word for word:* abicala — steadfast; dulaha — rare; prema-dhana bitaraṇe — at the giving of the treasure of prema; nikhila tāpa — all sufferings; dūre gela — went far away; dīna hīna sabahi — of all the poor and wretched; manoratha pūrala — the desires were fulfilled; abalāu — even the women; unamata bhela — became maddened

**26.6.** When He gave away the steadfast, rare treasure of prema,
all the world's sufferings went far away;
the desires of all the poor and wretched were fulfilled,
even the women became maddened.[^10-105]

ঐছন করুণ-নয়ন অবলোকনে
কাহ না রহু দুরদিন ।
বলরাম দাস তাহে ভেল বঞ্চিত
দারুণ হৃদয় কঠিন ॥

*aichana karuṇa-nayana abalokane*
*kāha nā rahu duradina |*
*balarāma dāsa tāhe bhela bañcita*
*dāruṇa hṛdaya kaṭhina ||*

*Word for word:* aichana — such; karuṇa-nayana abalokane — by the merciful glance; kāha nā rahu — no one was left with; duradina — dark days; balarāma dāsa — Balarama Dasa; tāhe — in this; bhela bañcita — was left out; dāruṇa hṛdaya — a cruel heart; kaṭhina — hard

**26.7.** By such a merciful glance
no one was left with dark days —
yet Balarama Dasa was left out:
cruel is his heart, and hard.

[^10-103]: Signature: "Balarama Dasa." BR, 12th wave: 1913 ed. (Murshidabad), pp. 974–975 ("gīte yathā — dhānaśī"); 1960 ed., vv.
3738–3744; 2006 ed., vv. 3738–3744. In Narahari Chakravarti the pada is sung in the account of Saptagrama: Nityananda comes to
Uddharana Datta's house and "is ever immersed in dance and kirtana." By OCR it is not found in GPT1 (on PK see below); GPT2 — sec. 6.1, no. 15
(in the catalogue BD-028, "GPT only"). Majumdar does not discuss the pada. Cf. CB Antya 5 (Nityananda in Gauda, Saptagrama).
Full PK check (chapter 16): the pada is also in PK — **PK 2301** (vol. 3, 22nd pallava, PDF pp. 303–304, label "॥৮॥২৩০১॥", MS P-R-Sa no. 2405; signature "balarāma dāsa kāhe bhela bañcita dāruṇa hṛdaya-kaṭhina").
[^10-104]: 1913 ed.: "padatala tāla-balita maṇi mañjarī"; 1960 ed.: "padatalatale balita muṇimañjarī" (OCR). Meru is the golden mountain.
[^10-105]: 1913 ed.: "abalāu unamata bhela" — "even the women (abalā) became maddened."

# Chapter 11. Balarama Dasa, Yadunandana, Kanu Dasa and Others: Praise of Gaura, His Bhavas in Navadvipa, the Sannyasa, Nityananda in Gauda

*This chapter completes the core — padas of the Lord's contemporaries known from the *Padakalpataru* (PK), the
*Bhakti-ratnakara* (BR) and the *Kshanada-gita-chintamani* (KGC), excluding padas in nagari-bhava. Here are the
remaining padas signed by Balarama Dasa; padas of Yadunandana Chakravarti (a disciple of Gadadhara Dasa) cited by
Narahari Chakravarti in the *Bhakti-ratnakara*; and padas of Kanu Dasa (Kanu Thakura), Raya Ananta, Murari and
Krishnadasa, in the order of the lilas: praise of the Gaura-avatara and of Nitai-Chaitanya; Gaura's form and His bhavas in
the kirtanas of Navadvipa, when, holding Gadadhara's hand, He speaks of Radha and Vrindavana; the lament over the
sannyasa; Shachi in Shantipura; the Lord in Nilachala; Nityananda, sent to Gauda, with Shachi; Gaura's bliss after long separation. Majumdar counts among the
Lord's contemporaries Balarama Dasa (on the strength of three BR padas, translated in chapter 10) and Yadunandana (on the
strength of his BR padas); the signature "Balarama Dasa" in PK covers padas of several poets, so the attribution of the
rest is doubtful. The text follows PK, checked against the scans, with the manuscript variants from PK's apparatus, BR,
the *Gaura-pada-tarangini* (GPT1 — 1st ed., 1903; GPT2 — 2nd ed., 1934) and KGC; the Bengali original, variants and
word-for-word translation are in the full version of the book.*

## 1. Balarama Dasa — "baraṇa-āśrama kiñcana akiñcana…" (PK 2212)
*Praise of the Gaura-avatara: making no distinction of varnas and ashramas, of rich and destitute, Gaura gives away the
prema inaccessible to Shiva and Brahma; sinners, beasts and birds weep; kings, yogis and jnanis abandon their own — only
the poet's heart seems made of stone. Raga suhai.*[^11-1]

বরণ-আশ্রম কিঞ্চন অকিঞ্চন
কার কোন দোষ নাহি মানে ।
শিব-বিরিঞ্চির অগোচর প্রেম-ধন
যাচিয়া বিলায় জগ-জনে ॥

*baraṇa-āśrama kiñcana akiñcana*
*kāra kona doṣa nāhi māne |*
*śiba-biriñcira agocara prema-dhana*
*yāciyā bilāya jaga-jane ||*

*Word for word:* baraṇa-āśrama — varnas and ashramas; kiñcana — those who have; akiñcana — those who have not; kāra — whose; kona doṣa — any fault; nāhi māne — takes no account; śiba-biriñcira — of Shiva and Brahma; agocara — inaccessible; prema-dhana — the treasure of prema; yāciyā — offering of Himself; bilāya — distributes; jaga-jane — to the people of the world

**1.1.** Making no distinction of varnas and ashramas, of those who have and those who have not,
He takes no account of anyone's faults;
the treasure of prema, inaccessible to Shiva and Brahma,
He distributes to the people of the world, offering it Himself.[^11-2]

করুণার সাগর গৌর-অবতার
নিছনি লইয়া মরি ।
কে জানে কিবা গুণ কিবা সে মাধুরী
প্রাণ কান্দে পাসরিতে নারি ॥

*karuṇāra sāgara gaura-abatāra*
*nichani laiyā mari |*
*ke jāne kibā guṇa kibā se mādhurī*
*prāṇa kānde pāsarite nāri ||*

*Word for word:* karuṇāra sāgara — an ocean of mercy; gaura-abatāra — the incarnation of Gaura; nichani laiyā mari — I would die taking (His) misfortune on myself; ke jāne — who knows; kibā guṇa — what qualities; kibā se mādhurī — what that sweetness; prāṇa kānde — my soul weeps; pāsarite nāri — I cannot forget

**1.2.** An ocean of mercy is the incarnation of Gaura:
I would give my life to turn misfortune away from Him![^11-3]
Who knows what His qualities are, what His sweetness is?
My soul weeps — I cannot forget.

পামর পাষণ্ড আদি দীন হীন খীণ জাতি
গুণ শুনি কান্দে জগ-জন ।
অগেয়ান পশু পাখী তারা কান্দে ঝরে আঁখি
কি দিয়া বান্ধিল সভার মন ॥

*pāmara pāṣaṇḍa ādi dīna hīna khīṇa jāti*
*guṇa śuni kānde jaga-jana |*
*ageyāna paśu pākhī tārā kānde jhare ām̐khi*
*ki diyā bāndhila sabhāra mana ||*

*Word for word:* pāmara — the low; pāṣaṇḍa — the godless; ādi — and the rest; dīna — the poor; hīna — the wretched; khīṇa jāti — the weak and low-born; guṇa śuni — hearing of the qualities; kānde — weeps; jaga-jana — the whole world; ageyāna — unreasoning; paśu pākhī — beasts and birds; tārā kānde — they too weep; jhare ām̐khi — (tears) pour from the eyes; ki diyā — with what; bāndhila — has bound; sabhāra mana — the hearts of all

**1.3.** The low, the godless, the poor, the wretched, the weak and the low-born —
hearing of His qualities, the whole world weeps;
even unreasoning beasts and birds weep, tears pour from their eyes:
with what has He bound the hearts of all?[^11-4]

রাজা ছাড়ে রাজা-ভোগ যোগী ছাড়ে ধ্যান যোগ
জ্ঞানী কান্দে ছাড়ি জ্ঞান-রস ।
কেবা বলরাম-হিয়া গঢ়িল পাষাণ দিয়া
হেন রস না কৈল পরশ ॥

*rājā chāṛe rājā-bhoga yogī chāṛe dhyāna yoga*
*jñānī kānde chāṛi jñāna-rasa |*
*kebā balarāma-hiyā gaṛhila pāṣāṇa diyā*
*hena rasa nā kaila paraśa ||*

*Word for word:* rājā chāṛe — the king abandons; rājā-bhoga — royal pleasures; yogī chāṛe — the yogi abandons; dhyāna yoga — meditation and yoga; jñānī kānde — the jnani weeps; chāṛi — abandoning; jñāna-rasa — the taste of knowledge; kebā — who; balarāma-hiyā — Balarama's heart; gaṛhila — fashioned; pāṣāṇa diyā — out of stone; hena rasa — this rasa; nā kaila paraśa — did not touch

**1.4.** The king abandons royal pleasures, the yogi meditation and yoga,
the jnani weeps, abandoning the taste of knowledge.
Who, then, fashioned Balarama's heart out of stone,
that this rasa has not touched it?

[^11-1]: Signature: "Balarama" ("kebā balarāma-hiyā…"). PK: vol. 3, PDF pp. 272–273 (printed pp. 261–262), 20th pallava, no. 29
(label "॥২৯॥২২১২॥"); raga suhai; P-R-Sa MS no. 2320. GPT1 — p. 38, no. 38; GPT2 — sec. 1.3, no. 38. The catalogue (BD-010)
assigns the pada to PK 2214 — a mistake: PK 2214 is a pada of Govinda Dasa, "kundana-kanaya-kalebara-kāti", and PK 2213, which
follows ours (Govinda Dasa, "patita heri kānde…"), repeats its line "baraṇa-āśrama kiñcana akiñcana". Which of the Balarama
Dasas wrote the pada has not been established.
[^11-2]: "Those who have and those who have not" — kiñcana akiñcana. On the prema which the Lord gives away without
distinguishing the worthy and the unworthy, cf. CC Adi 7.
[^11-3]: "nichani laiyā mari" is a set phrase of love: "I would die taking on myself (the beloved's misfortune)"; nichhani is
a rite by which misfortune is turned away from a beloved.
[^11-4]: "The weak" — khīṇa; MS "ka", P-R-Sa: khala ("the wicked"). "The low-born" — jāti ("by birth"); P-R-Sa: mati ("the weak
in understanding").

## 2. Balarama Dasa — "dekha dekha aparūpa gaura-carita…" (PK 2286)
*Gaura's pastimes are like those of Vamana: the Lord of Gokula has appeared again, and Prataparudra, like Bali, gave Him
body, mind and all his possessions, asuras such as Jagai and Madhai bowed to His feet; Advaita is Bhagiratha, who brought
down the Ganga of bhakti, Nityananda is Shiva, who received it; in it all the devotees bathe, and the fallen attain the
supreme abode. Raga kamoda.*[^11-5]

দেখ দেখ অপরূপ গৌর-চরিত ।
সো গোকুল-পতি অব পরকাশল
পুন কিয়ে বামন-রীত ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*dekha dekha aparūpa gaura-carita |*
*so gokula-pati aba parakāśala*
*puna kiye bāmana-rīta || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* dekha dekha — look, look; aparūpa — wondrous; gaura-carita — Gaura's deeds; so gokula-pati — that Lord of Gokula; aba parakāśala — has now appeared; puna kiye — is it not again; bāmana-rīta — the manner of Vamana

**2.1.** *(Refrain)* Look, look — wondrous are Gaura's deeds!
That very Lord of Gokula has now appeared —
was it not so that Vamana once appeared?[^11-6]

নিরখি প্রতাপ প্রতাপরুদ্র বলি
তনু মন সরবস দেল ।
জগাই মাধাই আদি অসুরগণ
চরণ প্রবণ নিজ কেল ॥

*nirakhi pratāpa pratāparudra bali*
*tanu mana sarabasa dela |*
*jagāi mādhāi ādi asuragaṇa*
*caraṇa prabaṇa nija kela ||*

*Word for word:* nirakhi — seeing; pratāpa — the majesty; pratāparudra — Prataparudra; bali — (like) Bali; tanu mana — body and mind; sarabasa — all possessions; dela — gave; jagāi mādhāi ādi — Jagai, Madhai and the rest; asura-gaṇa — the asuras; caraṇa prabaṇa — bowed to the feet; nija kela — made His own

**2.2.** Seeing His majesty, Prataparudra, like Bali,
gave Him body, mind and all he possessed;
Jagai, Madhai and the other asuras
He brought to bow at His feet.[^11-7]

যছু পদ সহ অদ্বৈত-ভগীরথ
ভকতি-গঙ্গ-পরবাহ ।
নিত্যানন্দ গিরিশ দেই আনল
বাম-হিমাচল মাহ ॥

*yachu pada saha advaita-bhagīratha*
*bhakati-gaṅga-parabāha |*
*nityānanda giriśa dei ānala*
*bāma-himācala māha ||*

*Word for word:* yachu pada — from whose feet; saha — together with; advaita-bhagīratha — Advaita as Bhagiratha; bhakati-gaṅga-parabāha — the stream of the Ganga of bhakti; nityānanda giriśa — Nityananda is Girisha (Shiva); dei — receiving (it); ānala — brought (down); bāma-himācala māha — into the … Himalaya (the sense of "bāma" is unclear)

**2.3.** From His feet, with Advaita as Bhagiratha,
flowed the stream of the Ganga of bhakti;
Nityananda is Girisha: He received it
and brought it down into the Himalaya…[^11-8]

যছু অবগাহনে অখিল ভকতগণে
বিলসই প্রেম-আনন্দ ।
পামর পতিত পরম পদ পায়ল
বঞ্চিত বলরাম মন্দ ॥

*yachu abagāhane akhila bhakatagaṇe*
*bilasai prema-ānanda |*
*pāmara patita parama pada pāyala*
*bañcita balarāma manda ||*

*Word for word:* yachu abagāhane — bathing in it; akhila bhakata-gaṇe — all the devotees; bilasai — revel; prema-ānanda — in the bliss of prema; pāmara patita — the low and fallen; parama pada — the supreme abode; pāyala — attained; bañcita — left out; balarāma manda — worthless Balarama

**2.4.** Bathing in it, all the devotees
revel in the bliss of prema;
the low and the fallen attained the supreme abode —
only worthless Balarama is left out.[^11-9]

[^11-5]: Signature: "Balarama" ("bañcita balarāma manda"). PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 298 (printed p. 287), 21st pallava "The sannyasa of
Sri Gauranga and so on", no. 69 (label "॥৬৯॥২২৮৬॥"); raga kamoda; P-R-Sa MS no. 2390. GPT1 — p. 46, no. 66; GPT2 — sec.
1.3, no. 66. The catalogue (BD-013) assigns the pada to PK 1245 — wrongly: PK 1245 is Krishna-lila (Govardhana, signed
"Chaitanyadasa"). The pada follows Ananta Acharya's PK 2285 (chapter 3, no. 9).
[^11-6]: Vamana is the Lord's incarnation as a dwarf brahmana who begged three steps of land from Bali, king of the asuras,
and covered the universe with them (Bhag. 8.18–21). The comparison: Gaura, like Vamana, "begs" — and receives everything.
[^11-7]: Prataparudra is the king of Orissa (CC Madhya 11–14); Bali gave himself to Vamana. Jagai and Madhai are the wicked
brothers of Navadvipa delivered by the Lord (CB Madhya 13). "Brought to bow at His feet" — caraṇa prabaṇa nija kela; MS "ka":
prabale, "kha", "gha", "cha": prabaṇe.
[^11-8]: The Ganga flowed from Vamana's foot, Bhagiratha brought it down to earth, and Shiva (Girisha, "lord of the
mountains") received it on his head (Bhag. 9.9). So too Advaita called the Lord down, and Nityananda received and spread
the stream of bhakti. The end of the line is unclear: PK reads "bāma-himācala māha", MSS "cha", P-R-Sa "rāma-himācala"; P-R-Sa
reads "nityānanda gīma" instead of "nityānanda giriśa, dei". MSS "ka", "kha": "path" (patha) instead of "feet" (pada); "kha",
P-R-Sa: "devotee" (bhakata) instead of "bhakti".
[^11-9]: "The supreme abode" — parama pada; MSS "ka", "kha" and GPT1: "the supreme mercy" (parama dayā).

## 3. Raya Ananta — "nitāi caitanya duṭī bhāi dayāra abadhi…" (KGC 28.2)
*Nitai and Chaitanya, two brothers, are the limit of mercy: the prema inaccessible to Shiva and Brahma and sought in vain
by the four Vedas They give away unceasingly; the fallen of the age of Kali, crying "Nitai-Chaitanya", dance and sing.
Raga shri.*[^11-10]

নিতাই চৈতন্য দুটী ভাই দয়ার অবধি ।
শিব ব্রহ্মার দুর্লভ প্রেম যাচে নিরবধি ॥

*nitāi caitanya duṭī bhāi dayāra abadhi |*
*śiba brahmāra durlabha prema yāce nirabadhi ||*

*Word for word:* nitāi caitanya — Nitai and Chaitanya; duṭī bhāi — two brothers; dayāra abadhi — the limit of mercy; śiba brahmāra — of Shiva and Brahma; durlabha prema — the inaccessible prema; yāce — give away (offering it); nirabadhi — without end

**3.1.** Nitai and Chaitanya, two brothers, are the limit of mercy:
the prema inaccessible to Shiva and Brahma They give away without end.

চারি বেদে অন্বেষয়ে যে প্রেম পাইতে ।
হেন প্রেম দুটী ভাই যাচে অবিরতে ॥

*cāri bede anveṣaye ye prema pāite |*
*hena prema duṭī bhāi yāce abirate ||*

*Word for word:* cāri bede — the four Vedas; anveṣaye — search; ye prema — the prema which; pāite — to attain; hena prema — such prema; duṭī bhāi — the two brothers; yāce — give away; abirate — unceasingly

**3.2.** The prema which the four Vedas search for, to attain it —
such prema the two brothers give away unceasingly.

পতিত দুর্গত যত কলি-হত যারা ।
নিতাই চৈতন্য বলি নাচে গায় তারা ॥

*patita durgata yata kali-hata yārā |*
*nitāi caitanya bali nāce gāya tārā ||*

*Word for word:* patita — the fallen; durgata — the wretched; yata — as many as; kali-hata — struck down by Kali; yārā — those who; nitāi caitanya bali — crying "Nitai-Chaitanya"; nāce gāya — dance and sing; tārā — they

**3.3.** The fallen, the wretched, as many as are struck down by Kali —
crying "Nitai-Chaitanya!" they dance and sing.[^11-11]

ভুবন-মঙ্গল ভেল সঙ্কীর্তন-রসে ।
রায় অনন্ত কাঁদে না পাইয়া শেষে ॥

*bhubana-maṅgala bhela saṅkīrtana-rase |*
*rāya ananta kām̐de nā pāiyā śeṣe ||*

*Word for word:* bhubana-maṅgala — the good of the world; bhela — has come about; saṅkīrtana-rase — in the rasa of sankirtana; rāya ananta — Raya Ananta; kām̐de — weeps; nā pāiyā — not obtaining; śeṣe — at the last (GPT1 "leśe" — not a particle)

**3.4.** The good of the whole world has come about in the rasa of sankirtana —
Raya Ananta weeps: not a drop of it has come to him.[^11-12]

[^11-10]: Signature: "Raya Ananta" ("rāya ananta"). KGC: 28th kshanada, no. 2 (1925 ed., p. 223; scan PDF p. 257), a
gaura-chandrika to Radha-Krishna lila, raga shri. GPT1 — p. 40, no. 43 (raga mangala); GPT2 — sec. 1.3, no. 43. The pada
was not previously found in PK (see below). According to B. B. Majumdar, the "Raya Ananta" of KGC is Ananta Acharya of Advaita's branch (cf. chapter 4,
no. 9).
Full PK check (chapter 16): the pada is also in PK — **PK 2337** (vol. 3, 23rd pallava, PDF p. 317, label "॥৬॥২৩৩৭॥"; signature "rāya ananta kānde nā pāiyā leśe").
[^11-11]: GPT1, GPT2: "the fallen, the wretched, the sinful, struck down by Kali" (patita durgata pāpī kalihata yārā).
[^11-12]: "Not a drop of it has come to him" follows GPT1 (nā pāiyā leśe, "not obtaining a particle"); KGC reads śeṣe ("at
the end": "weeps, not obtaining [it] at the last").

## 4. Krishnadasa — "soṅaro naba gauracanda…" (PK 1085)
*Remembering the youthful Gaurachandra — the moon of Navadvipa, Krishna Himself: the moon-face, eyes full of prema, locks
dressed with flowers, earrings, the Kaustubha, red garments, sandal; the king of serpents holds an umbrella over Him,
Lakshmi serves His feet, the devotees sing His glory; at the end the poet places his hope in Nitai too, the giver of
prema. Raga bhairavi.*[^11-13]

সোঙরো নব গৌরচন্দ
নাগর বনয়ারি ।
নবদ্বীপ-ইন্দু করুণা-সিন্ধু
ভক্ত-বৎসলকারী ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*soṅaro naba gauracanda*
*nāgara banayāri |*
*nabadvīpa-indu karuṇā-sindhu*
*bhakta-batsalakārī || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* soṅaro — I remember; naba — the youthful; gauracanda — Gaurachandra; nāgara — the graceful (youth); banayāri — Vanamali (Krishna); nabadvīpa-indu — the moon of Navadvipa; karuṇā-sindhu — the ocean of mercy; bhakta-batsala-kārī — tenderly loving the devotees

**4.1.** *(Refrain)* I remember the youthful Gaurachandra —
the graceful Vanamali,
the moon of Navadvipa, the ocean of mercy,
tenderly loving His devotees.[^11-14]

বদন-চন্দ অধর রঙ্গ
নয়নে গলত প্রেম-তরঙ্গ
চন্দ্র কোটি ভানু কোটি
শোভা নিছয়ারি ।
কুসুম-শোভিত চাঁচর চিকুর
ললাটে তিলক নাসিকা উজোর
দশন মোতিম অমিয়া হাস
দামিনি ঘনয়ারি ॥

*badana-canda adhara raṅga*
*nayane galata prema-taraṅga*
*candra koṭi bhānu koṭi*
*śobhā nichayāri |*
*kusuma-śobhita cām̐cara cikura*
*lalāṭe tilaka nāsikā ujora*
*daśana motima amiyā hāsa*
*dāmini ghanayāri ||*

*Word for word:* badana-canda — the moon-face; adhara raṅga — red lips; nayane — from the eyes; galata — stream; prema-taraṅga — waves of prema; candra koṭi — millions of moons; bhānu koṭi — millions of suns; śobhā — the beauty; nichayāri — I offer as a gift to ward off harm; kusuma-śobhita — dressed with flowers; cām̐cara cikura — the curling locks; lalāṭe tilaka — tilaka on the brow; nāsikā ujora — the shining nose; daśana motima — teeth are pearls; amiyā hāsa — the smile is nectar; dāmini — lightning; ghanayāri — (in) a cloud

**4.2.** His face is the moon, His lips are red,
waves of prema stream from His eyes;
the beauty of millions of moons, of millions of suns
I offer to Him as a gift to ward off harm.
His locks, dressed with flowers,
the tilaka on His brow, His shining nose,
His teeth are pearls, His smile nectar,
like lightning in a cloud.[^11-15]

মকর-কুণ্ডল ঝলকে গণ্ড
মণি-কৌস্তুভ-দীপ্ত কণ্ঠ
অরুণ বসন করুণ বচন
শোভা অতি ভারি ।
মাল্য-চন্দন-চর্চিত অঙ্গ
লাজে লজ্জিত কোটি অনঙ্গ
অঙ্গদ বলয়া রতন-নূপুর
যজ্ঞ-সূত্রধারি ॥

*makara-kuṇḍala jhalake gaṇḍa*
*maṇi-kaustubha-dīpta kaṇṭha*
*aruṇa basana karuṇa bacana*
*śobhā ati bhāri |*
*mālya-candana-carcita aṅga*
*lāje lajjita koṭi anaṅga*
*aṅgada balayā ratana-nūpura*
*yajña-sūtradhāri ||*

*Word for word:* makara-kuṇḍala — makara earrings; jhalake — flash; gaṇḍa — (on) the cheeks; maṇi-kaustubha-dīpta — lit by the Kaustubha gem; kaṇṭha — the neck; aruṇa basana — red garments; karuṇa bacana — merciful words; śobhā ati bhāri — beauty beyond measure; mālya-candana-carcita — anointed with sandal and garlanded; aṅga — the body; lāje lajjita — put to shame; koṭi anaṅga — millions of Kamadevas; aṅgada — armlets; balayā — bracelets; ratana-nūpura — jewelled anklets; yajña-sūtra-dhāri — wearing the sacred thread

**4.3.** Makara earrings flash on His cheeks,
His neck is lit by the Kaustubha gem,
red garments, merciful words —
beauty beyond measure.
His body anointed with sandal, in garlands —
millions of Kamadevas are put to shame;
bracelets on arms and wrists, jewelled anklets,
the sacred thread upon Him.[^11-16]

ছত্র ধরত ধরণিধরেন্দ্র
গাওত যশ ভকতবৃন্দ
কমলা-সেবিত পাদদ্বন্দ্ব
বলিয়ে বলিহারি ।
কহত দান কৃষ্ণদাস
গৌর-চরণে করত আশ
পতিত-পাবন নিতাই চান্দ
প্রেম দানকারী ॥

*chatra dharata dharaṇidharendra*
*gāota yaśa bhakatabṛnda*
*kamalā-sebita pādadvandva*
*baliye balihāri |*
*kahata dāna kṛṣṇadāsa*
*gaura-caraṇe karata āśa*
*patita-pābana nitāi cānda*
*prema dānakārī ||*

*Word for word:* chatra dharata — holds the umbrella; dharaṇi-dharendra — the king of the bearers of the earth (Shesha); gāota yaśa — sing the glory; bhakata-bṛnda — the host of devotees; kamalā-sebita — served by Kamala (Lakshmi); pāda-dvandva — the two feet; baliye balihāri — I offer myself in sacrifice; kahata — says; dāna (dīna) — humble; kṛṣṇadāsa — Krishnadasa; gaura-caraṇe — in Gaura's feet; karata āśa — placing his hope; patita-pābana — the saviour of the fallen; nitāi cānda — Nitaichand; prema dānakārī — the giver of prema

**4.4.** The king of the bearers of the earth holds an umbrella over Him,
the host of devotees sings His glory;
to the two feet served by Kamala
I offer myself in sacrifice.
Says humble Krishnadasa,
placing his hope in Gaura's feet:
the saviour of the fallen, Nitaichand,
is the giver of prema.[^11-17]

[^11-13]: Signature: "Krishnadasa" ("kahata dāna kṛṣṇadāsa"; GPT1 reads "dīna", "humble"; "dāna" in PK is apparently a misprint).
PK: vol. 2, PDF pp. 251–252 (printed pp. 238–239), 15th pallava, section "rasālasopayuktarūpaṃ" (the form befitting the
languor after the rasa), "śrīgauracandraḥ" — a gaura-chandrika to Radha-Krishna lila, no. 23 (label "॥২৩॥১০৮৫॥"); raga
bhairavi; P-R-Sa MS no. 1494. GPT1 — p. 136, no. 75 (bhairava, ektala). In the catalogue (KR-006) the pada stood without a
first line, marked as probably Krishna-lila: it is a gaura-pada. Which Krishnadasa wrote it has not been established (C).
[^11-14]: "The graceful Vanamali" — nāgara banayāri: nagara is a graceful youth skilled in love; Banvari (Vanamali, "wearing the
forest garland") is a name of Krishna. Gaura is Krishna Himself (CC Adi 1–4). MSS "ka", "kha", "gha", "cha":
"Gaurasundara" instead of "Gaurachandra"; GPT1: "Remember the youthful Gaurasundara…" (soṅara).
[^11-15]: "I offer to Him as a gift to ward off harm" — nichayāri (from nichhani: everything beautiful is offered up to turn
misfortune away from the beloved). MSS "ka", "kha": "the beauty of His face" (mukhaśobhā). "Like lightning in a cloud" —
dāmini ghanayāri; the sense of the second word is not wholly clear.
[^11-16]: The Kaustubha is the gem on the breast of Vishnu-Krishna. MSS "ka", "kha", "gha", "cha" and GPT1: "sandal" (candana)
instead of "armlets" (aṅgada); MS "kha": tarala instead of ratana.
[^11-17]: "The king of the bearers of the earth" is Ananta-Shesha, the serpent who bears the universes; he serves the Lord as
His umbrella. Kamala is Lakshmi. Instead of the first line GPT1 reads "the devotees run and sing…" (dhārata gāota bhakatabṛnda)
and adds: "majestically He walks, slowly, slowly". MSS "ka", "kha", "gha", "cha": baliyā instead of baliye.

## 5. Balarama Dasa — "kothāya āchila gorā emana sundara…" (PK 2110)
*Gaura's form: where was such a beauty until now? He has charmed the whole town of Nadia: His hair dressed with flowers,
bees hovering above it, pearls on His breast, sandal and kunkuma, the forest garland, a gliding gait, the ringing of
anklets. Raga shri.*[^11-18]

কোথায় আছিল গোরা এমন সুন্দর ।
ও রূপে মুগধ কৈল নদীয়া নগর ॥

*kothāya āchila gorā emana sundara |*
*o rūpe mugadha kaila nadīyā nagara ||*

*Word for word:* kothāya — where; āchila — was; gorā — Gora; emana sundara — such a beauty; o rūpe — with that form; mugadha kaila — charmed; nadīyā nagara — the town of Nadia

**5.1.** Where was such a beauty — Gora — until now?
With this form He has charmed the town of Nadia.

বান্ধিয়া চিকণ কেশ দিয়া নানা ফুলে ।
রঙ্গণ মালতী যূথী বান্ধুলী বকুলে ॥

*bāndhiyā cikaṇa keśa diyā nānā phule |*
*raṅgaṇa mālatī yūthī bāndhulī bakule ||*

*Word for word:* bāndhiyā — dressing; cikaṇa keśa — the glossy hair; diyā nānā phule — with flowers of every kind; raṅgaṇa — rangana; mālatī — malati; yūthī — yuthi; bāndhulī — bandhuli; bakule — bakula

**5.2.** His glossy hair is dressed with flowers of every kind —
rangana, malati, yuthi, bandhuli, bakula.[^11-19]

মধু-লোভে মধুকর তাহে কত উড়ে ।
ও রূপ দেখিতে প্রাণ নাহি রহে ধড়ে ॥

*madhu-lobhe madhukara tāhe kata uṛe |*
*o rūpa dekhite prāṇa nāhi rahe dhaṛe ||*

*Word for word:* madhu-lobhe — thirsting for honey; madhukara — bees; tāhe — over them; kata uṛe — how many hover; o rūpa dekhite — gazing at that form; prāṇa — life; nāhi rahe — does not stay; dhaṛe — in the body

**5.3.** Thirsting for honey, how many bees hover over them!
Gazing at this form, life will not stay in the body.

মণি-মুকুতার হার ঝলমল বুকে ।
প্রতি অঙ্গে আভরণ বিজুরী চমকে ॥

*maṇi-mukutāra hāra jhalamala buke |*
*prati aṅge ābharaṇa bijurī camake ||*

*Word for word:* maṇi-mukutāra hāra — a necklace of gems and pearls; jhalamala — glitters; buke — on the breast; prati aṅge — on every limb; ābharaṇa — ornaments; bijurī camake — flash like lightning

**5.4.** A necklace of gems and pearls glitters on His breast,
on every limb ornaments flash like lightning.

কুঙ্কুমে লেপিত অঙ্গ চন্দন মিশালে ।
আজানুলম্বিত ভুজ বনমালা গলে ॥

*kuṅkume lepita aṅga candana miśāle |*
*ājānulambita bhuja banamālā gale ||*

*Word for word:* kuṅkume lepita — anointed with kunkuma; aṅga — the body; candana miśāle — mixed with sandal; ājānu-lambita — reaching to the knees; bhuja — the arms; banamālā — the forest garland; gale — on the neck

**5.5.** His body is anointed with kunkuma mixed with sandal,
His arms reach to His knees, the forest garland is on His neck.

মন্থর চলনি গতি দুদিগে হেলনি ।
অমিয়া উথলে কিবা গ্রীবার দোলনি ॥

*manthara calani gati dudige helani |*
*amiyā uthale kibā grībāra dolani ||*

*Word for word:* manthara calani gati — a gliding gait; dudige helani — swaying to both sides; amiyā uthale — nectar wells up; kibā — as if; grībāra dolani — the swaying of the neck

**5.6.** A gliding gait, swaying now to one side, now to the other —
as if nectar welled up when His neck sways.

চলিতে মধুর-নাদে নূপুর বাজে পায় ।
বলরাম দাস বলে নিছনি যাঙ তায় ॥

*calite madhura-nāde nūpura bāje pāya |*
*balarāma dāsa bale nichani yāṅa tāya ||*

*Word for word:* calite — as He walks; madhura-nāde — with a sweet sound; nūpura — the anklets; bāje pāya — ring on the feet; balarāma dāsa bale — Balarama Dasa says; nichani yāṅa tāya — I give myself for Him

**5.7.** As He walks, the anklets on His feet ring sweetly —
Balarama Dasa says: I give myself for Him.[^11-20]

[^11-18]: Signature: "Balarama Dasa." PK: vol. 3, PDF pp. 233–234 (printed pp. 222–223), 18th pallava, section "atha
śrīgauracandrasya rūpādibarṇanaṃ" (description of Sri Gaurachandra's form), no. 2 (label "॥২॥২১১০॥"); raga shri; P-R-Sa MS no.
2218. GPT1 — p. 110, no. 2; GPT2 — sec. 3.1, no. 2. The catalogue (BD-014) listed it as "GPT only": the PK number was found
on the scan. The preceding PK 2109 ("gaura-baraṇa maṇi-ābharaṇa nāṭuyā-mohana beśa", with the same signature; BD-017) is in
nagari-bhava (deferred).
[^11-19]: Rangana (ixora), malati and yuthi (kinds of jasmine), bandhuli (pentapetes, a red flower), bakula (mimusops). GPT1:
pārulī (the patali flower) instead of bāndhulī.
[^11-20]: "I give myself for Him" — nichani yāṅa tāya (see note 3).

## 6. Balarama Dasa — "kusume khacita ratane racita…" (PK 2164)
*The form of Gaura the dancer: His hair dressed with flowers and gems, bees above it; a sandal tilaka, locks, earrings;
at His glances the women of Nadia lose their peace; lips, smile, speech are nectar; jasmine garlands, gold and diamonds,
red garments; the gait of an elephant, feet that outshine the lotus, nails that outshine the moon. Raga tori.*[^11-21]

কুসুমে খচিত রতনে রচিত
চিকণ চিকুর-বন্ধ ।
মধুতে মুগধ সৌরভে লুবধ
খুবধ মধুপ বৃন্দ ॥

*kusume khacita ratane racita*
*cikaṇa cikura-bandha |*
*madhute mugadha saurabhe lubadha*
*khubadha madhupa bṛnda ||*

*Word for word:* kusume khacita — dressed with flowers; ratane racita — studded with gems; cikaṇa — glossy; cikura-bandha — tresses; madhute mugadha — drunk with honey; saurabhe lubadha — greedy for fragrance; khubadha — agitated (whirling); madhupa bṛnda — swarms of bees

**6.1.** Dressed with flowers, studded with gems —
His glossy tresses;
drunk with honey, greedy for fragrance,
swarms of bees whirl above them.

ললাট-ফলক পটীর-তিলক
কুটিল অলকা সাজে ।
তাণ্ডবে পণ্ডিত কুণ্ডলে মণ্ডিত
গণ্ড-মণ্ডল রাজে ॥

*lalāṭa-phalaka paṭīra-tilaka*
*kuṭila alakā sāje |*
*tāṇḍabe paṇḍita kuṇḍale maṇḍita*
*gaṇḍa-maṇḍala rāje ||*

*Word for word:* lalāṭa-phalaka — the tablet of the brow; paṭīra-tilaka — a sandal tilaka; kuṭila alakā — curling locks; sāje — adorn; tāṇḍabe paṇḍita — skilled in the tandava dance; kuṇḍale maṇḍita — adorned with earrings; gaṇḍa-maṇḍala — the rounded cheeks; rāje — shine

**6.2.** On the tablet of His brow is a tilaka of sandal,
curling locks adorn it;
skilled in the tandava dance, adorned with earrings —
His rounded cheeks shine.

ও রূপ দেখিয়া সতী কুলবতী
ছাড়ল কুলের লাজ ।
ধরম করম সরম ভরম
মাথাতে পড়িল বাজ ॥

*o rūpa dekhiyā satī kulabatī*
*chāṛala kulera lāja |*
*dharama karama sarama bharama*
*māthāte paṛila bāja ||*

*Word for word:* o rūpa dekhiyā — seeing that form; satī kulabatī — chaste wives of noble families; chāṛala — abandoned; kulera lāja — the shame before their kin; dharama — dharma; karama — duties; sarama — modesty; bharama — honour; māthāte — on the head; paṛila bāja — thunder fell

**6.3.** Seeing this form, the chaste wives of noble families
abandoned their shame before their kin:
dharma, duties, modesty, honour —
as though struck by thunder.[^11-22]

অপাঙ্গ-ইঙ্গিতে ভাঙর ভঙ্গিতে
অনঙ্গ-রঙ্গিত সঙ্গ ।
মদন-কদন হোয়ল সদন
জগত-যুবতি-অঙ্গ ॥

*apāṅga-iṅgite bhāṅara bhaṅgite*
*anaṅga-raṅgita saṅga |*
*madana-kadana hoyala sadana*
*jagata-yubati-aṅga ||*

*Word for word:* apāṅga-iṅgite — by hints of sidelong glances; bhām̐ṅara bhaṅgite — by the play of the brows; anaṅga-raṅgita — tinged with Ananga; saṅga — the company (all around); madana-kadana — the longing of Kama; hoyala sadana — has become the abode; jagata-yubati-aṅga — the limbs (hearts) of the young women of the world

**6.4.** By the hints of sidelong glances, by the play of the brows,
all around is tinged with Ananga;
the longing of Kama has made its abode
in the hearts of the young women of the world.

অধর বন্ধুক মাধ্বীক-অধিক
আধ মধুর হাসি ।
বোলনি অলসে কলসে কলসে
বময়ে অমিয়া-রাশি ॥

*adhara bandhuka mādhvīka-adhika*
*ādha madhura hāsi |*
*bolani alase kalase kalase*
*bamaye amiyā-rāśi ||*

*Word for word:* adhara — the lips; bandhuka — bandhuka flowers; mādhvīka-adhika — sweeter than honey-wine; ādha madhura hāsi — a sweet half-smile; bolani — the speech; alase — unhurried; kalase kalase — pitcher after pitcher; bamaye — pours out; amiyā-rāśi — streams of nectar

**6.5.** His lips are bandhuka flowers, sweeter than honey-wine
is His half-smile;
His speech, unhurried, pitcher after pitcher
pours out streams of nectar.

কুন্দ-দাম ঠামহি ঠাম
কুসুম-সুষম-পাঁতি ।
ততহিঁ লোলুপ মধুপী মধুপ
উড়িয়া পড়য়ে মাতি ॥

*kunda-dāma ṭhāmahi ṭhāma*
*kusuma-suṣama-pām̐ti |*
*tatahim̐ lolupa madhupī madhupa*
*uṛiyā paṛaye māti ||*

*Word for word:* kunda-dāma — garlands of jasmine; ṭhāmahi ṭhāma — here and there; kusuma-suṣama-pām̐ti — rows of lovely flowers; tatahi̐ — there; lolupa — greedy; madhupī madhupa — female and male bees; uṛiyā paṛaye — fly down; māti — intoxicated

**6.6.** Garlands of jasmine here and there,
rows of lovely flowers;
greedy bees, male and female,
fly down to them, intoxicated.

হিরণ হীর বিজুরী থীর
শোহন মোহন দেহে ।
অরুণ-কিরণ- হরণ বসন
বরণে যুবতী মোহে ॥

*hiraṇa hīra bijurī thīra*
*śohana mohana dehe |*
*aruṇa-kiraṇa- haraṇa basana*
*baraṇe yubatī mohe ||*

*Word for word:* hiraṇa — gold; hīra — diamonds; bijurī thīra — motionless lightning; śohana — adorn; mohana dehe — the enchanting body; aruṇa-kiraṇa-haraṇa — outshining the red rays of dawn; basana — the garments; baraṇe — by their colour; yubatī mohe — captivate the young women

**6.7.** Gold, diamonds, motionless lightning
adorn His enchanting body;
garments that outshine the red rays of dawn
captivate the young women with their colour.

কাম চমক ঠাম ঠমক
কুন্দন-কনক-গোরা ।
মত্ততা-সিন্ধুর- গমন-মন্থর
হেরিয়া ভুবন ভোরা ॥

*kāma camaka ṭhāma ṭhamaka*
*kundana-kanaka-gorā |*
*mattatā-sindhura- gamana-manthara*
*heriyā bhubana bhorā ||*

*Word for word:* kāma camaka — astonishing Kama; ṭhāma ṭhamaka — bearing and poise; kundana-kanaka-gorā — Gora like pure gold; mattatā-sindhura — of a maddened elephant; gamana-manthara — the slow gait; heriyā — gazing; bhubana bhorā — the world is enraptured

**6.8.** His bearing and poise astonish Kama —
Gora, like pure gold;
His gait is slow, like a maddened elephant's —
gazing at Him, the world forgets itself.

কঞ্জ-চরণ খঞ্জন-গঞ্জন
মঞ্জু মঞ্জীর ভাষ ।
ইন্দু-নিন্দন নখর-ছন্দন
বনি বলরাম দাস ॥

*kañja-caraṇa khañjana-gañjana*
*mañju mañjīra bhāṣa |*
*indu-nindana nakhara-chandana*
*bani balarāma dāsa ||*

*Word for word:* kañja-caraṇa — the lotus feet; khañjana-gañjana — putting wagtails to shame; mañju — soft; mañjīra bhāṣa — the ringing of the anklets; indu-nindana — outshining the moon; nakhara-chandana — the nails; bani — describes; balarāma dāsa — Balarama Dasa

**6.9.** His lotus feet put the wagtails to shame,
softly His anklets ring;
His nails outshine the moon —
so Balarama Dasa describes Him.[^11-23]

[^11-21]: Signature: "Balarama Dasa" ("bani balarāma dāsa"). PK: vol. 3, PDF pp. 254–255 (printed pp. 243–244), 18th pallava, no. 56
(label "॥৫৬॥২১৬৪॥"; the preceding pada of Ramananda, PK 2163, is by a misprint also labelled "২১৬৪"); raga tori; P-R-Sa MS no.
2271. GPT1 — p. 125, no. 42, and p. 140, no. 86 (the same pada twice); GPT2 — sec. 3.1, nos. 42 and 86. The catalogue (BD-016)
gives PK 2165 (a mistake: PK 2165 is Narottama Dasa, "kāñcana darapaṇa baraṇa sugorā re").
[^11-22]: The words about the women of Nadia who, seeing Gaura, lose their shame and peace are an image of the poetics of
describing beauty and the language of nagari-bhava (Gaura as the nagara, the beloved of the town's women); we translate
faithfully to the author. Vrindavana Dasa stresses that in this incarnation the Lord never glanced at another man's wife;
worship of Gaura in the spirit of "Gaura-nagari" is not accepted by the Gaudiya tradition (Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa
Kaviraja, Bhaktisiddhanta). MSS "ka", "kha": "with thrills" (pulake) instead of "with earrings" (kuṇḍale); "gha", "cha",
P-R-Sa: bhaṅgita instead of bhaṅgite. The last word of 6.4 is unclear on the scan (sardana?); we read it with GPT1 as sadana
("abode"); MS "gha": sohana instead of hoyala.
[^11-23]: The wagtail (khañjana) is an image of nimble, graceful feet. "Describes" — bani (from barṇana?); MSS "ka", P-R-Sa: bali
("says"). MSS "gha", "cha": lulupa instead of lolupa (6.6); P-R-Sa: kundala instead of kundana (6.8). GPT1 (6.1): kṣubdha
("agitated") instead of khubadha.

## 7. Balarama Dasa — "sahajai kāñcana-kānti kalebara…" (PK 2145)
*Gaura dancing, overwhelmed by Radha's prema: a body the colour of gold, before which millions of Madanas swoon; He
lingers, falls to the ground, trembles, roars, sheds tears and, embracing the fallen, bathes them in His tears. Raga
beloar.*[^11-24]

সহজই কাঞ্চন-কান্তি কলেবর
হেরইতে জগ-জন-মন-মোহনিয়া ।
তঁহি কত কোটী মদন মুরছায়ল
অরুণ-কিরণ-হর অম্বর বনিয়া ॥

*sahajai kāñcana-kānti kalebara*
*heraite jaga-jana-mana-mohaniyā |*
*tam̐hi kata koṭī madana murachāyala*
*aruṇa-kiraṇa-hara ambara baniyā ||*

*Word for word:* sahajai — by nature; kāñcana-kānti — of golden lustre; kalebara — the body; heraite — gazing; jaga-jana-mana-mohaniyā — enchanting the hearts of the people of the world; tām̐hi — before it; kata koṭī madana — how many millions of Madanas; murachāyala — swoon; aruṇa-kiraṇa-hara — outshining the red rays; ambara — the garment; baniyā — adorned

**7.1.** His body by nature is the colour of gold:
gazing at Him, the people of the world lose their hearts;
before Him how many millions of Madanas swoon!
His garment outshines the red rays of dawn.

রাই-প্রেম-ভরে গমন সুমন্থর
অন্তর গরগর পড়ই ধরণিয়া ।
স্বেদ কম্প ঘন ঘন পুলকাবলি
ঘন হুহুঙ্কার করত গরজনিয়া ॥

*rāi-prema-bhare gamana sumanthara*
*antara garagara paṛai dharaṇiyā |*
*sveda kampa ghana ghana pulakābali*
*ghana huhuṅkāra karata garajaniyā ||*

*Word for word:* rāi-prema-bhare — overwhelmed by Rai's prema; gamana sumanthara — walks very slowly; antara garagara — the heart brimming; paṛai dharaṇiyā — falls to the ground; sveda — sweat; kampa — trembling; ghana ghana — again and again; pulakābali — waves of thrills; ghana huhuṅkāra — again and again the roar "hum"; karata garajaniyā — utters, roaring

**7.2.** Overwhelmed by Rai's prema, He walks slowly, slowly,
His heart brimming over — He falls to the ground;
sweat, trembling, again and again wave upon wave of thrills,
again and again He roars: "Hum! Hum!"[^11-25]

ডগমগ দেহ থেহ নাহি বান্ধই
দুহুঁ দিঠি-মেহ সঘনে বরখণিয়া ।
ও রসে ভোর ওর নাহি পায়ই
পতিত কোরে ধরি লোর সিচনিয়া ॥

*ḍagamaga deha theha nāhi bāndhai*
*duhum̐ diṭhi-meha saghane barakhaṇiyā |*
*o rase bhora ora nāhi pāyai*
*patita kore dhari lora sicaniyā ||*

*Word for word:* ḍagamaga deha — the body sways; theha nāhi bāndhai — cannot stand firm; duhum̐ diṭhi-meha — the clouds of both eyes; saghane — unceasingly; barakhaṇiyā — pour rain; o rase bhora — drunk with that rasa; ora nāhi pāyai — finds no end; patita kore dhari — clasping the fallen to the breast; lora sicaniyā — bathing them in tears

**7.3.** His body sways, He cannot stand firm,
from both cloud-like eyes the rain pours unceasingly;
drunk with that rasa, He finds no end to it,
clasping the fallen to His breast, He bathes them in tears.

হরি হরি বোলি রোই কত বিলপই
বঞ্চিত বলরাম দিবস রজনিয়া ॥

*hari hari boli roi kata bilapai*
*bañcita balarāma dibasa rajaniyā ||*

*Word for word:* hari hari boli — crying "Hari, Hari"; roi — weeping; kata bilapai — how much He laments; bañcita — left out; balarāma — Balarama; dibasa rajaniyā — day and night

**7.4.** Crying "Hari, Hari," how much He weeps and laments! —
only Balarama is left out, day and night.[^11-26]

[^11-24]: Signature: "Balarama" ("bañcita balarāma"). PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 247 (printed p. 236), 18th pallava, no. 37 (label
"॥৩৭॥২১৪৫॥"); raga beloar; P-R-Sa MS no. 2252. The pada follows Vasu Ghosha's PK 2143 and 2144 (chapter 8). GPT1 — p. 116,
no. 16 (beloar); GPT2 — sec. 3.1, no. 16. The catalogue (BD-015) gives PK 788: a mistake (PK 788 is a pada of Govinda Dasa,
"tapata-kāñcana-kānti kalebara").
[^11-25]: "Rai's prema" — rāi-prema: the Lord appeared in Radha's bhava and complexion to taste Her love for Krishna (CC Adi
4). MSS "kha", "gha": "immersed" (magana) instead of "walks" (gamana); "ka", "kha": kara instead of karata.
[^11-26]: Instead of the last couplet GPT1 reads: "Crying 'Hari, Hari,' He weeps and laments, mad with bliss day and night;
hearing the sound 'Hari, Hari,' the world was saved — only lowly Balarama Dasa is left out."

## 8. Balarama Dasa — "bihare āju rasika-rāja…" (PK 2111)
*Gaurachandra, the king of rasikas, sports in Nadia: beauty outshining millions of Kamadevas, a moon-face, smile and speech
of nectar; remembering the groves of Vraja He loses Himself, stumbles, falls into the arms of the fallen, repeats "Rai,
Rai!" — all drink the nectar of prema except the poet. Raga turi.*[^11-27]

বিহরে আজু রসিক-রাজ
গৌরচন্দ্র নদিয়া মাঝ
কুঞ্জ কেশরপুঞ্জ উজোর
কনক-রুচির-কাঁতিয়া ।
কোটি কাম রূপ-ধাম
ভুবনমোহন লাবণি ঠাম
হেরত জগত-যুবতি উমতি
ধৈরজ ধরম তেজিয়া ॥

*bihare āju rasika-rāja*
*gauracandra nadiyā mājha*
*kuñja keśarapuñja ujora*
*kanaka-rucira-kām̐tiyā |*
*koṭi kāma rūpa-dhāma*
*bhubanamohana lābaṇi ṭhāma*
*herata jagata-yubati umati*
*dhairaja dharama tejiyā ||*

*Word for word:* bihare — sports; āju — today; rasika-rāja — the king of rasikas; gauracandra — Gaurachandra; nadiyā mājha — in Nadia; kuñja (?) keśara-puñja — a cluster of nagakeshara flowers; ujora — shining; kanaka-rucira-kām̐tiyā — with the lovely lustre of gold; koṭi kāma — of millions of Kamadevas; rūpa-dhāma — the abode of beauty; bhubana-mohana — enchanting the world; lābaṇi ṭhāma — loveliness; herata — seeing; jagata-yubati — the young women of the world; umati — in turmoil; dhairaja dharama — composure and dharma; tejiyā — abandon

**8.1.** Today the king of rasikas,
Gaurachandra, sports in Nadia:
shining like a cluster of nagakeshara flowers,
with the lovely lustre of gold.
The abode of the beauty of millions of Kamadevas,
loveliness that enchants the world —
seeing Him, the young women of the world in turmoil
abandon composure and dharma.[^11-28]

অসিম পুণিম-শরদ-চন্দ-
কিরণ-দমন-বদন-ছন্দ
কুন্দ-কুসুম নিন্দি সুষম
মঞ্জু দশন-পাঁতিয়া ।
বিম্বু-অধরে মধুর হাসি
বময়ে কতহিঁ অমিয়া-রাশি
শুধই সীধু-নিকর নিঝর
বচন ঐছন ভাতিয়া ॥

*asima puṇima-śarada-canda-*
*kiraṇa-damana-badana-chanda*
*kunda-kusuma nindi suṣama*
*mañju daśana-pām̐tiyā |*
*bimbu-adhare madhura hāsi*
*bamaye katahim̐ amiyā-rāśi*
*śudhai sīdhu-nikara nijhara*
*bacana aichana bhātiyā ||*

*Word for word:* asima — boundless; puṇima-śarada-canda — of the full autumn moon; kiraṇa-damana — outshining the rays; badana-chanda — the charm of the face; kunda-kusuma nindi — putting kunda flowers to shame; suṣama — lovely; mañju daśana-pām̐tiyā — the row of lovely teeth; bimbu-adhare — on the bimba lips; madhura hāsi — a sweet smile; bamaye — pours out; katahi̐ — so many; amiyā-rāśi — streams of nectar; śudhai — flows; sīdhu-nikara — torrents of sweet drink; nijhara — like a cascade; bacana — the words; aichana bhātiyā — in such a manner

**8.2.** A face whose charm outshines the rays
of the boundless full autumn moon;
a row of lovely teeth
puts the kunda flowers to shame;
on His bimba lips a sweet smile
pouring out so many streams of nectar;
His words, likewise, flow
in torrents of sweet drink.[^11-29]

মধুর বরজ-বিপিন-কুঞ্জ
মধুর পিরিতি-আরতি-পুঞ্জ
সোঙরি সোঙরি অধিক অবশ
মুগধ দিবস রাতিয়া ।
ভাবে অবশ অলস ধন্দ
চলত চলত খলত মন্দ
পতিত-কোর পড়ত ভোর
নিবিড় আনন্দে মাতিয়া ॥

*madhura baraja-bipina-kuñja*
*madhura piriti-ārati-puñja*
*soṅari soṅari adhika abaśa*
*mugadha dibasa rātiyā |*
*bhābe abaśa alasa dhanda*
*calata calata khalata manda*
*patita-kora paṛata bhora*
*nibiṛa ānande mātiyā ||*

*Word for word:* madhura — sweet; baraja-bipina-kuñja — the groves of the forests of Vraja; piriti-ārati-puñja — heaps of love and longing; soṅari soṅari — remembering, remembering; adhika abaśa — more and more lost to Himself; mugadha — rapt; dibasa rātiyā — day and night; bhābe abaśa — overcome by bhava; alasa — languid; dhanda — bewildered; calata calata — walking, walking; khalata manda — slowly stumbles; patita-kora — into the arms of the fallen; paṛata — falls; bhora — enraptured; nibiṛa ānande — with deep bliss; mātiyā — intoxicated

**8.3.** The sweet groves of the forests of Vraja,
the sweet heaps of love and longing —
remembering, remembering them, He loses Himself more and more,
rapt day and night.
Overcome by bhava, languid, bewildered,
He walks, walks — and slowly stumbles;
enraptured, He falls into the arms of the fallen,
intoxicated with deep bliss.[^11-30]

অরুণ নয়ানে করুণ চাই
সঘনে জপয়ে রাই রাই
নটত উমত লুঠত ভ্রমত
ফুটত মরম ছাতিয়া ।
উত্তম মধ্যম অধম জীব
সবহুঁ প্রেম-অমিয়া পীব
তহিঁ বলরাম বঞ্চিত একলে
সাধু ঠামে অপরাধিয়া ॥

*aruṇa nayāne karuṇa cāi*
*saghane japaye rāi rāi*
*naṭata umata luṭhata bhramata*
*phuṭata marama chātiyā |*
*uttama madhyama adhama jība*
*sabahum̐ prema-amiyā pība*
*tahim̐ balarāma bañcita ekale*
*sādhu ṭhāme aparādhiyā ||*

*Word for word:* aruṇa nayāne — with reddened eyes; karuṇa cāi — gazes with compassion; saghane — unceasingly; japaye — repeats; rāi rāi — "Rai, Rai"; naṭata — dances; umata — mad (with prema); luṭhata — rolls; bhramata — wanders; phuṭata — bursts; marama chātiyā — the breast (with what is) in the heart; uttama madhyama adhama jība — high, middling and low beings; sabahum̐ — all; prema-amiyā pība — drink the nectar of prema; tahim̐ — therein; balarāma bañcita ekale — Balarama alone is left out; sādhu ṭhāme — towards the sadhus; aparādhiyā — having offended

**8.4.** With reddened eyes He gazes, full of compassion,
unceasingly He repeats: "Rai, Rai!";
He dances, mad with prema, rolls on the ground, wanders —
His breast bursting with what is in His heart.
The high, the middling, the low beings —
all drink the nectar of prema;
Balarama alone is left out,
having offended the sadhus.[^11-31]

[^11-27]: Signature: "Balarama" ("tahim̐ balarāma bañcita ekale"). PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 234 (printed p. 223), 18th pallava, no. 3 (label
"॥৩॥২১১১॥"); raga turi (todi); P-R-Sa MS nos. 1430 and 2219. GPT1 — p. 110, no. 3 (turi). The pada is not in the catalogue
(in chapter 10 it was noted from Ray's footnote to PK 2066 as "outside the catalogue"); new row BD-043.
[^11-28]: Nagakeshara (keśara) is a flower with golden stamens; "cluster" — puñja (the word kuñja at the start of the line is
unclear). The words about young women are the language of nagari-bhava; we translate faithfully to the author (see note
22). MS "gha": murati instead of yubati.
[^11-29]: Bimba is a red fruit; kunda is white jasmine. MS "ka": "a face outshining Madana" (madana badana); P-R-Sa: "badana madana";
instead of chanda ("charm") MS "ka": basana, "kha": sadana, "gha", P-R-Sa: badana. MS "ka": nikare; P-R-Sa: racana (instead of bacana?).
[^11-30]: The idea: Gaura in Krishna's bhava remembers the pastimes in Vraja (cf. CC Madhya 2). P-R-Sa: "the love of the young
(gopis)" (yubati piriti) instead of "love and longing" (piriti-ārati). MSS "ka", "kha", "cha", P-R-Sa: "in ecstasy" (ābeśe)
instead of "by bhava"; P-R-Sa: "dances" (naṭata) instead of the second "walks".
[^11-31]: "Rai" is Radha. Cf. chapter 10, no. 20 (PK 2113: "Rai, Rai!" at the sight of Gadadhara). "Having offended the sadhus"
— sādhu ṭhāme aparādhiyā: the poet sees the cause of his being left out in an offence against the devotees. P-R-Sa: "red"
(aruṇa) instead of "full of compassion" (karuṇa).

## 9. Balarama Dasa — "ābeśe abaśa aṅga dhīre dhīre cale…" (PK 2081)
*The Lord dances in kirtana: hearing the story of His former pastimes of love, He falls senseless, weeps at the sight of
the fallen, rolls on the ground crying "Hari!"; because of His bhava householders abandon the happiness of home — only the
poet remains indifferent to this rasa. Raga shri.*[^11-32]

আবেশে অবশ অঙ্গ ধীরে ধীরে চলে ।
ভাব-ভরে গর গর আঁখি নাহি মেলে ॥

*ābeśe abaśa aṅga dhīre dhīre cale |*
*bhāba-bhare gara gara ām̐khi nāhi mele ||*

*Word for word:* ābeśe — in ecstasy; abaśa aṅga — with limbs overcome; dhīre dhīre cale — walks slowly, slowly; bhāba-bhare — with the weight of bhava; gara gara — brimming; ām̐khi nāhi mele — does not open His eyes

**9.1.** Overcome by ecstasy, He walks slowly, slowly,
brimming with bhava, He does not open His eyes.

নাচে পহুঁ রসিক সুজান ।
যার গুণে দরবয়ে দারু পাষাণ ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*nāce pahum̐ rasika sujāna |*
*yāra guṇe darabaye dāru pāṣāṇa || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* nāce — dances; pahum̐ — the Lord; rasika sujāna — the connoisseur of rasa; yāra guṇe — by whose qualities; darabaye — melt; dāru pāṣāṇa — wood and stone

**9.2.** *(Refrain)* The Lord dances, the connoisseur of rasa,
by whose qualities wood and stone melt.

পুরুব-চরিত যত পিরিতি-কাহিনী ।
শুনি পহুঁ মুরছিত লোটায় ধরণী ॥

*puruba-carita yata piriti-kāhinī |*
*śuni pahum̐ murachita loṭāya dharaṇī ||*

*Word for word:* puruba-carita — the former deeds; yata — all; piriti-kāhinī — the tales of love; śuni — hearing; pahum̐ — the Lord; murachita — senseless; loṭāya dharaṇī — rolls on the ground

**9.3.** All the tales of former deeds, of love —
hearing them, the Lord rolls senseless on the ground.[^11-33]

পতিত হেরিয়া কান্দে নাহি বান্ধে থীর ।
কত শত ধারা বহে নয়নের নীর ॥

*patita heriyā kānde nāhi bāndhe thīra |*
*kata śata dhārā bahe nayanera nīra ||*

*Word for word:* patita heriyā — seeing the fallen; kānde — weeps; nāhi bāndhe thīra — cannot calm Himself; kata śata dhārā — in hundreds of streams; bahe — flow; nayanera nīra — the water of the eyes

**9.4.** Seeing the fallen, He weeps, He cannot calm Himself,
in hundreds of streams the tears pour from His eyes.

পুলকে মণ্ডিত কিবা ভুজযুগ তুলি ।
লুলিয়া লুলিয়া পড়ে হরি হরি বলি ॥

*pulake maṇḍita kibā bhujayuga tuli |*
*luliyā luliyā paṛe hari hari bali ||*

*Word for word:* pulake maṇḍita — covered with thrills; kibā — (particle); bhuja-yuga tuli — raising both arms; luliyā luliyā — swaying; paṛe — falls; hari hari bali — crying "Hari, Hari"

**9.5.** Covered with thrills, raising both arms,
crying "Hari, Hari," swaying, He falls.

কুলবতীর ঝুরে মন ঝুরে দুটি আঁখি ।
ঝুরিয়া ঝুরিয়া কান্দে বনের পশু পাখী ॥

*kulabatīra jhure mana jhure duṭi ām̐khi |*
*jhuriyā jhuriyā kānde banera paśu pākhī ||*

*Word for word:* kulabatīra — of chaste wives; jhure mana — the heart pines; jhure duṭi ām̐khi — both eyes pine; jhuriyā jhuriyā — pining; kānde — weep; banera paśu pākhī — the beasts and birds of the forests

**9.6.** The hearts of chaste wives pine, their eyes pine,
pining, the beasts and birds of the forests weep.[^11-34]

যার ভাবে গৃহ-বাসী ছাড়ে গৃহ-সুখ ।
বলরাম দাস সবে একলে বিমুখ ॥

*yāra bhābe gṛha-bāsī chāṛe gṛha-sukha |*
*balarāma dāsa sabe ekale bimukha ||*

*Word for word:* yāra bhābe — because of whose bhava; gṛha-bāsī — householders; chāṛe — abandon; gṛha-sukha — the happiness of home; balarāma dāsa — Balarama Dasa; sabe — (among) all; ekale — alone; bimukha — indifferent

**9.7.** Because of His bhava householders abandon the happiness of home —
Balarama Dasa alone is indifferent to it all.[^11-35]

[^11-32]: Signature: "Balarama Dasa." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 223 (printed p. 212), 17th pallava, no. 23 (label "॥২৩॥২০৮১॥"); raga
shri; P-R-Sa MS no. 1181 (?) and 2190, P-R 4.1. KGC — 3rd kshanada, no. 1 (p. 16; raga varari), a gaura-chandrika. GPT1 —
p. 289, no. 41; GPT2 — sec. 4.2, no. 16, and 4.3, no. 41. According to B. B. Majumdar, signatures of this type ("everyone —
but I am indifferent") belong to the later Balarama Dasa; attribution C.
[^11-33]: "Former deeds" — puruba-carita: Krishna's pastimes in Vraja sung by the devotees; hearing them, the Lord is plunged into
bhava (cf. CB Madhya 8). MS P-R: "attentive" (abahita) instead of "senseless". In KGC the refrain stands after 9.4.
[^11-34]: The words about "chaste wives" are an image of how every living being pines for Gaura (see note 22). MS P-R: "young
wives" (kulabadhū), "in the heart" (mane); MS "gha": "understanding, understanding, they weep in their hearts" (bujhiyā bujhiyā
mane kānde) instead of "pining, they weep".
[^11-35]: MSS P-R-Sa, P-R: "Balarama Dasa is indifferent to such rasa" (hena rase balarāma dāsa bimukha); KGC: "Balarama Dasa alone among
all is indifferent to this rasa" (balarāma dāsa sabe e rase bimukha).

## 10. Balarama Dasa — "bhābabhare gara gara cita…" (BR pp. 921–922)
*The Lord in the kirtana of Navadvipa: brimming with bhava, He now rises, now sits, weeps over His former love — why is
the Lord of Goloka in the midst of sankirtana? — makes no distinction of His own and others, holding Gadadhara's hand
cries out what is in His heart, and falls into the arms of the devotees. Raga suhai.*[^11-36]

ভাবভরে গর গর চিত ।
খেনে উঠে খেনে বসে না পায় সম্বিৎ ॥

*bhābabhare gara gara cita |*
*khene uṭhe khene base nā pāya sambit ||*

*Word for word:* bhāba-bhare — with the fullness of bhava; gara gara — brimming; cita — the heart; khene uṭhe — now rises; khene base — now sits; nā pāya sambit — cannot come to His senses

**10.1.** His heart brims with bhava:
now He rises, now He sits — He cannot come to His senses.

অতিরসে নাহি বাঁধে থেহ ।
সোঙরি সোঙরি কাঁদে পুরুব সনেহ ॥

*atirase nāhi bām̐dhe theha |*
*soṅari soṅari kām̐de puruba saneha ||*

*Word for word:* ati-rase — from the excess of rasa; nāhi bām̐dhe theha — cannot stand firm; soṅari soṅari — remembering, remembering; kām̐de — weeps; puruba saneha — (over) the former love

**10.2.** From the excess of rasa He cannot stand firm,
remembering, remembering, He weeps over His former love.[^11-37]

নাচে পহুঁ গোরা নটরাজ ।
কি লাগি গোলোক-পতি সঙ্কীর্তন মাঝ ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*nāce pahum̐ gorā naṭarāja |*
*ki lāgi goloka-pati saṅkīrtana mājha || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* nāce — dances; pahum̐ — the Lord; gorā naṭarāja — Gora, the king of dancers; ki lāgi — why; goloka-pati — the Lord of Goloka; saṅkīrtana mājha — in the midst of sankirtana

**10.3.** *(Refrain)* The Lord dances — Gora, the king of dancers:
why is the Lord of Goloka in the midst of sankirtana?[^11-38]

নিজ পর কিছু নাহি জানে ।
দীনহীন অধম উত্তম নাহি মানে ॥

*nija para kichu nāhi jāne |*
*dīnahīna adhama uttama nāhi māne ||*

*Word for word:* nija para — own and other; kichu nāhi jāne — knows not at all (does not distinguish); dīna-hīna — the poor and wretched; adhama uttama — the low and the high; nāhi māne — does not distinguish

**10.4.** He does not know who is His own and who is another,
the poor, the wretched, the low and the high He does not distinguish.[^11-39]

প্রিয় গদাধর-কর ধরি ।
মরম কথাটি কহে ফুকরি ফুকরি ॥

*priya gadādhara-kara dhari |*
*marama kathāṭi kahe phukari phukari ||*

*Word for word:* priya gadādhara-kara dhari — holding the hand of dear Gadadhara; marama kathāṭi — the word of His heart; kahe — tells; phukari phukari — crying out again and again

**10.5.** Holding the hand of His dear Gadadhara,
He tells what is in His heart, crying out again and again.

ডগমগ আনন্দ-হিল্লোলে ।
লুলিয়া লুলিয়া পড়ে ভকতের কোলে ॥

*ḍagamaga ānanda-hillole |*
*luliyā luliyā paṛe bhakatera kole ||*

*Word for word:* ḍagamaga — swaying; ānanda-hillole — in waves of bliss; luliyā luliyā — reeling; paṛe — falls; bhakatera kole — into the arms of the devotees

**10.6.** Swaying in waves of bliss,
He sinks, reeling, into the arms of the devotees.[^11-40]

গোরা-রসে সব রসময় ।
না দরবে বল-পাষাণ হৃদয় ॥

*gorā-rase saba rasamaya |*
*nā darabe bala-pāṣāṇa hṛdaya ||*

*Word for word:* gorā-rase — through Gora's rasa; saba rasamaya — everything is full of rasa; nā darabe — does not melt; bala-pāṣāṇa hṛdaya — the stony heart of Bala (Balarama)

**10.7.** Through Gora's rasa everything is full of rasa —
only Balarama's stony heart does not melt.[^11-41]

[^11-36]: Signature: "Bala(rama)" ("nā darabe bala-pāṣāṇa hṛdaya"). BR, 12th wave: 1913 ed., pp. 921–922 ("punaḥ suhai"), 1960 ed., vv.
3022–3028 — in Narahari Chakravarti's account to Srinivasa of the places of Navadvipa ("here Gaurachandra danced in
sankirtana"); in BR the pada stands before padas of Balarama (PK 2067; chapter 10, no. 7) and Murari (PK 2121; chapter 1, no. 6).
KGC — 17th kshanada, no. 1 (p. 125; raga deshaga), a gaura-chandrika. GPT1 — p. 271, no. 77 (dhanashi). Not previously found in PK (see below). In the
catalogue — BD-041.
Full PK check (chapter 16): the pada is also in PK — **PK 635** (vol. 2, 3rd shakha, gaura-chandrika to "svayaṃ dautya," PDF p. 30, label "॥১॥৬৩৫॥", raga dhanashi, MS P-R-Sa no. 1112; repeated as PK 909); signature "nā darabe balarāma pāṣāṇa-hṛdaya."
[^11-37]: "Former love" — the love of Krishna and Radha in Vraja: the Lord in His bhava remembers it.
[^11-38]: Goloka is Krishna's supreme abode. The footnote in BR, and KGC: "the Lord of Gokula" (gokula-pati).
[^11-39]: The couplet is only in BR (KGC and GPT1 lack it). In the 1913 ed. the middle of the line is effaced on the scan; we
read it from the 1960 ed.: "dīnahīna adhama uttama nāhi māne".
[^11-40]: KGC: "into the arms of the Pandita" (paṇḍitera kole), i.e. of Gadadhara Pandita; GPT1: "into the arms of the fallen"
(patitera kola).
[^11-41]: "Balarama" — BR: "Vala-" (bala-pāṣāṇa hṛdaya, "Vala's stony heart"); KGC: "Balarama" (balarāma pāṣāṇa-hṛdaya); GPT1: "Balarama's
hard heart" (balarāma kaṭhina hṛdaya).

## 11. Kanu Dasa — "nija-nāmāmṛte matta anukṣaṇa…" (PK 2117)
*Gauranga's wondrous pastimes: intoxicated with the nectar of His own name, He makes everyone drink it, the lowly above
all; now He says, "I am the Lord," now, "I am the servant"; now He strides like a maddened lion, now stands stunned in
bhava, slaps His arms, roars with laughter, weeps, and sees before Him Shyamasundara, bent in three places. Raga
vibhasa.*[^11-42]

নিজ-নামামৃতে মত্ত অনুক্ষণ ।
পিয়ায় সভারে নাম বিশেষে হীন জন ॥

*nija-nāmāmṛte matta anukṣaṇa |*
*piyāya sabhāre nāma biśeṣe hīna jana ||*

*Word for word:* nija-nāmāmṛte — with the nectar of His own name; matta — intoxicated; anukṣaṇa — ever; piyāya — makes drink; sabhāre — all; nāma — the Name; biśeṣe — above all; hīna jana — the lowly

**11.1.** Ever intoxicated with the nectar of His own name,
He makes all drink the Name, the lowly above all.

অতি অরুণিত আঁখি আধ আধ বোলে ।
কান্দে উচ্চনাদে যারে তারে করে কোলে ॥

*ati aruṇita ām̐khi ādha ādha bole |*
*kānde uccanāde yāre tāre kare kole ||*

*Word for word:* ati aruṇita ām̐khi — the eyes deeply reddened; ādha ādha bole — speaks haltingly; kānde ucca-nāde — weeps aloud; yāre tāre — whomever He meets; kare kole — embraces

**11.2.** His eyes reddened, He speaks haltingly,
weeps aloud and embraces whomever He meets.

অপরূপ গৌরাঙ্গ-বিলাস ।
খেণে বলে মুঞি পহুঁ খেণে বলে দাস ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*aparūpa gaurāṅga-bilāsa |*
*kheṇe bale muñi pahum̐ kheṇe bale dāsa || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* aparūpa — wondrous; gaurāṅga-bilāsa — Gauranga's pastimes; kheṇe bale — now He says; muñi pahum̐ — "I am the Lord"; khene bale dāsa — now He says "(I am) the servant"

**11.3.** *(Refrain)* Wondrous are Gauranga's pastimes:
now He says, "I am the Lord," now He says, "I am the servant."[^11-43]

খেণে মত্ত সিংহ-গতি খেণে ভাব-স্তম্ভ ।
খেণে ধরু ধরণী পাইয়া অঙ্গ-সঙ্গ ॥

*kheṇe matta siṃha-gati kheṇe bhāba-stambha |*
*kheṇe dharu dharaṇī pāiyā aṅga-saṅga ||*

*Word for word:* khene — now; matta siṃha-gati — with the gait of a maddened lion; bhāba-stambha — stupor in bhava; dharu dharaṇī — embraces the earth; pāiyā aṅga-saṅga — as though finding an embrace

**11.4.** Now He strides like a maddened lion, now stands stunned in bhava,
now embraces the earth, as though He had found an embrace.[^11-44]

খেণে মালশাট মারে অট্ট অট্ট হাসে ।
খেণেকে রোদন খেণে গদ গদ ভাষে ॥

*kheṇe mālaśāṭa māre aṭṭa aṭṭa hāse |*
*kheṇeke rodana kheṇe gada gada bhāṣe ||*

*Word for word:* mālaśāṭa māre — slaps His arms (like a wrestler); aṭṭa aṭṭa hāse — roars with laughter; kheṇeke rodana — now weeping; gada gada bhāṣe — speaks in a faltering voice

**11.5.** Now He slaps His arms like a wrestler and roars with laughter,
now He weeps, now He speaks in a faltering voice.

খেণে দেখে শ্যামসুন্দর তিরিভঙ্গ ।
কানুদাস কহে কেবা বুঝে ও না রঙ্গ ॥

*kheṇe dekhe śyāmasundara tiribhaṅga |*
*kānudāsa kahe kebā bujhe o nā raṅga ||*

*Word for word:* dekhe — sees; śyāmasundara — Shyamasundara; tiribhaṅga — bent in three places; kānudāsa kahe — Kanu Dasa says; kebā bujhe — who understands; o nā raṅga — that play

**11.6.** Now He sees Shyamasundara, bent in three places —
Kanu Dasa says: who can understand this play?[^11-45]

[^11-42]: Signature: "Kanu Dasa" ("kānudāsa kahe"). PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 236 (printed p. 225), 18th pallava, no. 9 (label
"॥৯॥২১১৭॥"); raga vibhasa; P-R-Sa MS no. 2225. GPT1 — p. 278, no. 4 (vibhasa). The preceding PK 2116 is Nayanananda's
(chapter 10, no. 18). In the catalogue — KD-010. Kanu Dasa is Kanu Thakura, son of Purushottama Dasa and grandson of
Sadashiva Kaviraja, of Nityananda's branch (Majumdar).
[^11-43]: The Lord showed now the bhava of His own divinity, now the bhava of a devotee (cf. CB Madhya 9: the mahaprakasha in
Srivasa's house; the Lord, coming to Himself, calls Himself the servant of the devotees). MS "ka": "the Lord is
intoxicated" (pahu matta) instead of "intoxicated" (11.1); "gha", "cha": "speaks" (bola) instead of the second "ādha".
[^11-44]: The sense of the second line is not wholly clear: "kheṇe dharu dharaṇī pāiyā aṅga-saṅga" — apparently in His bhava the Lord
embraces the earth as though embracing the Beloved.
[^11-45]: Slapping one's arms (mālasāṭa) is a wrestler's gesture. Shyamasundara bent in three places (tribhanga) is Krishna with
the flute: in Radha's bhava the Lord sees Krishna before Him. MSS "ka", "kha": "seeing" (dekhi); P-R-Sa: "who would not
understand" (ke nā).

## 12. Yadunandana — "dekha dekha gorācānde…" (BR p. 909)
*Gaura, dancing, speaks of His former love: in the bhava of youth He tells of the banks of the Yamuna and the wanderings
in the forests, Himself tells of Radha, holding Gadadhara's hand, weeps, laughs, rushes like a maddened elephant, and begs
for the treasure of prema: He is the enchanter of Gokula. Raga bhupali.*[^11-46]

দেখ দেখ গোরাচান্দে ।
কাঞ্চন রঞ্জন বরণ মদন-
মোহন নটন ছান্দে ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*dekha dekha gorācānde |*
*kāñcana rañjana baraṇa madana-*
*mohana naṭana chānde || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* dekha dekha — look, look; gorācānde — at Gorachand; kāñcana rañjana — outshining gold; baraṇa — His colour; madana-mohana — enchanting Madana; naṭana chānde — His dancing

**12.1.** *(Refrain)* Look, look at Gorachand:
His colour outshines gold, His dancing
enchants Madana.

পুরুব পিরিতি কহে ।
কিশোর বয়সে ভাবের আবেশে
পুলক পূরল দেহে ॥

*puruba piriti kahe |*
*kiśora bayase bhābera ābeśe*
*pulaka pūrala dehe ||*

*Word for word:* puruba piriti — of the former love; kahe — speaks; kiśora bayase — in youthful age; bhābera ābeśe — in the ecstasy of bhava; pulaka pūrala — thrills filled; dehe — the body

**12.2.** He speaks of His former love:
in the bhava of youth
His body is filled with thrills.

কে জানে মরম বেথা ।
যমুনা পুলিন বন বিহরণ
কহয়ে সে সব কথা ॥

*ke jāne marama bethā |*
*yamunā pulina bana biharaṇa*
*kahaye se saba kathā ||*

*Word for word:* ke jāne — who knows; marama bethā — the pain of the heart; yamunā pulina — the banks of the Yamuna; bana biharaṇa — wanderings in the forests; kahaye — tells; se saba kathā — all those things

**12.3.** Who knows the pain of His heart?
The banks of the Yamuna, the wanderings through the forests —
of all this He speaks.

নীরজ নয়নে নীর ।
রাধার কাহিনী কহয়ে আপুনি
তিলেক না রহে থির ॥

*nīraja nayane nīra |*
*rādhāra kāhinī kahaye āpuni*
*tileka nā rahe thira ||*

*Word for word:* nīraja nayane — in the lotus eyes; nīra — tears; rādhāra kāhinī — the story of Radha; kahaye āpuni — He tells Himself; tileka nā rahe thira — not for a moment remains still

**12.4.** His lotus eyes are full of tears,
He Himself tells of Radha —
not for a moment can He be still.[^11-47]

গদাধর করে ধরি ।
কাঁদন মাখন কহিতে বচন
বোলে হরি হরি হরি ॥

*gadādhara kare dhari |*
*kām̐dana mākhana kahite bacana*
*bole hari hari hari ||*

*Word for word:* gadādhara kare dhari — holding Gadadhara's hand; kām̐dana mākhana — steeped in weeping; kahite bacana — speaking words; bole hari hari hari — cries "Hari, Hari, Hari"

**12.5.** Holding Gadadhara's hand,
He speaks words steeped in weeping
and cries: "Hari, Hari, Hari!"

ভাবে জর জর তনু ।
ছুটল মাতল কুঞ্জর গমনে
বনের দলনু যনু ॥

*bhābe jara jara tanu |*
*chuṭala mātala kuñjara gamane*
*banera dalanu yanu ||*

*Word for word:* bhābe — with bhava; jara jara tanu — the body is spent; chuṭala — rushed; mātala kuñjara gamane — with the gait of a maddened elephant; banera dalanu — trampling of the forest; janu — as though

**12.6.** His body is spent with bhava;
He rushes forward with the gait of a maddened elephant,
as though trampling the forest.

খেনে হাসে কান্দে নাচে ।
অধর কম্পিত রহয়ে চকিত
খেনে প্রেমধন যাচে ॥

*khene hāse kānde nāce |*
*adhara kampita rahaye cakita*
*khene premadhana yāce ||*

*Word for word:* khene hāse kānde nāce — now laughs, weeps, dances; adhara kampita — the lips tremble; rahaye cakita — stands startled; khene — now; prema-dhana yāce — begs for the treasure of prema

**12.7.** Now He laughs, now weeps, now dances;
His lips tremble, He stands still, startled,
now He begs for the treasure of prema.

এ যদুনন্দন কহে ।
তুমি কি না জান গোকুলমোহন
গৌরাঙ্গ ভুবন মোহে ॥

*e yadunandana kahe |*
*tumi ki nā jāna gokulamohana*
*gaurāṅga bhubana mohe ||*

*Word for word:* e yadunandana kahe — Yadunandana says; tumi ki nā jāna — do you not know; gokula-mohana — the enchanter of Gokula; gaurāṅga — Gauranga; bhubana mohe — captivates the world

**12.8.** Yadunandana says:
do you not know? The enchanter of Gokula
is Gauranga, who captivates the world.[^11-48]

[^11-46]: Signature: "Yadunandana" ("e yadunandana kahe"). BR, 12th wave: 1913 ed., p. 909 ("kācicca bhūpāliḥ"), 1960 ed., vv.
2862–2869. GPT1 — p. 294, no. 5 (bhupali). Not found in PK. In BR the pada belongs to a series of padas by Yadunandana
Chakravarti, a disciple of Gadadhara Dasa (BR pp. 904–910), which Narahari Chakravarti puts into the mouths of the women of
Nadia, "full of anuraga", talking about Gaura as He goes to the Ganga; most of these padas are in nagari-bhava (deferred),
but this one is about the Lord's bhava in kirtana.
[^11-47]: The Lord in Krishna's bhava remembers the pastimes in Vraja and Radha (cf. chapter 10, no. 9).
[^11-48]: "You" is the friend whom the poet addresses (the frame of BR). Gokulamohana ("the enchanter of Gokula") is Krishna:
Gaura is Krishna Himself. GPT1: "as though crushing hosts of monkeys" (bānara dalana janu, per OCR) instead of "as though
trampling the forest" (12.6).

## 13. Yadunandana — "chala chala cāru nayana yugala…" (BR pp. 922–923 = PK 2246)
*Gaura, the ocean of mercy: His eyes pour rivers of tears, He roars in a thunderous voice, embraces the fallen, sings
songs of the rasa, calls "Radha, Radha!" and embraces Gadadhara, asks for the flute and the peacock feather, gazing into
Svarupa's face. Raga kamoda.*[^11-49]

ছল ছল চারু নয়ন যুগল
কত নদী বহে ধারে ।
পুলকে পূরল গোরা-কলেবর
ধরণি ধরিতে নারে ॥

*chala chala cāru nayana yugala*
*kata nadī bahe dhāre |*
*pulake pūrala gorā-kalebara*
*dharaṇi dharite nāre ||*

*Word for word:* chala chala — brimming with tears; cāru nayana yugala — the lovely eyes; kata nadī — how many rivers; bahe dhāre — flow in streams; pulake pūrala — filled with thrills; gorā-kalebara — Gora's body; dharaṇi — the earth; dharite nāre — cannot hold

**13.1.** His lovely eyes are brimming with tears —
how many rivers flow in streams!
Gora's body is filled with thrills —
the earth cannot hold Him.

পহুঁ করুণাসাগর গোরা ।
ভাবের ভরেতে অঙ্গ টলমল
গমনে ভুবন ভোরা ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*pahum̐ karuṇāsāgara gorā |*
*bhābera bharete aṅga ṭalamala*
*gamane bhubana bhorā || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* pahum̐ — the Lord; karuṇā-sāgara — the ocean of mercy; gorā — Gora; bhābera bharete — in the fullness of bhava; aṅga ṭalamala — the body sways; gamane — as He walks; bhubana bhorā — the world is enraptured

**13.2.** *(Refrain)* The Lord — Gora, the ocean of mercy:
in the fullness of bhava
His body sways; as He walks, the world forgets itself.

খেনে খেনে কত করুণা করয়ে
গরজে গভীর নাদে ।
অধম দেখিয়া আকুল হৃদয়
ধরিয়া ধরিয়া কাঁদে ॥

*khene khene kata karuṇā karaye*
*garaje gabhīra nāde |*
*adhama dekhiyā ākula hṛdaya*
*dhariyā dhariyā kām̐de ||*

*Word for word:* khene khene — again and again; kata karuṇā karaye — how much mercy He shows; garaje gabhīra nāde — roars in a deep voice; adhama dekhiyā — seeing the lowly; ākula hṛdaya — with heart in turmoil; dhariyā dhariyā — clasping, clasping; kām̐de — weeps

**13.3.** Again and again how much mercy He shows,
roaring in a thunderous voice;
seeing the lowly, His heart full of turmoil,
He clasps and clasps them and weeps.[^11-50]

চরণকমল অতি সুচঞ্চল
অথির তাহার রীত ।
বদনকমলে গদ গদ স্বরে
গায় রাসকেলি-গীত ॥

*caraṇakamala ati sucañcala*
*athira tāhāra rīta |*
*badanakamale gada gada svare*
*gāya rāsakeli-gīta ||*

*Word for word:* caraṇa-kamala — the lotus feet; ati sucañcala — most restless; athira tāhāra rīta — unsteady their manner; badana-kamale — from the lotus mouth; gada gada svare — in a faltering voice; gāya — sings; rāsa-keli-gīta — songs of the rasa dance

**13.4.** His lotus feet are most restless,
unsteady is their gait;
from His lotus mouth, in a faltering voice,
He sings songs of the rasa.[^11-51]

আহা আহা করি ভুজ যুগ তুলি
বোলে হরি হরি বোল ।
রাধা রাধা বলি ডাকে উচ্চ করি
দেই গদাধরে কোল ॥

*āhā āhā kari bhuja yuga tuli*
*bole hari hari bola |*
*rādhā rādhā bali ḍāke ucca kari*
*dei gadādhare kola ||*

*Word for word:* āhā āhā kari — crying "Aha! Aha!"; bhuja yuga tuli — raising both arms; bole — says; hari hari bola — "sing 'Hari, Hari'"; rādhā rādhā bali — crying "Radha, Radha"; ḍāke ucca kari — calls aloud; dei gadādhare kola — embraces Gadadhara

**13.5.** Crying "Aha! Aha!", raising both arms,
He says: "Sing 'Hari, Hari'!";
loudly calling "Radha, Radha!",
He embraces Gadadhara.

মুরলী মুরলী খেনে খেনে বুলি
স্বরূপ-মুখ নেহারে ।
শিখিপুচ্ছ বুলি উঠে ফুলি ফুলি
যদু কি বুঝিতে পারে ॥

*muralī muralī khene khene buli*
*svarūpa-mukha nehāre |*
*śikhipuccha buli uṭhe phuli phuli*
*yadu ki bujhite pāre ||*
