*Word for word:* muralī muralī — "the flute, the flute"; khene khene — again and again; buli — saying; svarūpa-mukha nehāre — gazes into Svarupa's face; śikhi-puccha buli — saying "the peacock feather"; uṭhe phuli phuli — chokes with sobs; yadu — Yadu; ki bujhite pāre — can he understand

**13.6.** Again and again saying, "The flute! The flute!" —
He gazes into Svarupa's face;
saying, "The peacock feather!" — He chokes with sobs:
can Yadu understand this?[^11-52]

[^11-49]: Signature: "Yadu" ("yadu ki bujhite pāre"). BR, 12th wave: 1913 ed., pp. 922–923 ("punaḥ kāmodaḥ"), right after Murari's
PK 2121. PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 285 (printed p. 274), 21st pallava, no. 29 (label "॥২৯॥২২৪৬॥", the second digit damaged on the scan), raga shri, P-R-Sa MS no. 2351 —
without the first stanza and **without a signature** (last line: "who can tell it?"). GPT1 — p. 285, no. 27 (kamoda; signed
Yadu) and p. 46, no. 65 (the PK recension, unsigned). KGC (26th kshanada, no. 1, pp. 207–208, raga varari) joins the first
stanza of Prasada Dasa's pada "keśera beśe bhulila deśe" (PK 2085) to 13.1–13.5 of our pada — without 13.6 and without a
signature. A variant signed "Govinda-dasiya" — GPT1 p. 10, no. 23. The pada was not in the catalogue; RM-005 ("keśera
beśe…", supposedly Ramananda's) is a pada of Prasada Dasa.
[^11-50]: PK: "losing His head" (ākula haiyā) instead of "His heart full of turmoil" (ākula hṛdaya).
[^11-51]: "Songs of the rasa" follows BR (rāsakeli-gīta, songs of the rasa dance); PK and GPT1 (no. 65): "songs full of rasa"
(rasamaya gīta). Instead of "unsteady is their gait" (athira tāhāra rīta) PK reads "like red lotuses" (rātā-utapala-rīta).
[^11-52]: In Krishna's bhava the Lord seeks His flute and peacock feather. Svarupa is Svarupa Damodara, the Lord's closest
companion in Puri (before his sannyasa, Purushottama Acharya, who knew the Lord already in Navadvipa, CC Madhya 10); PK places
the pada among the pastimes after the sannyasa, BR among the places of Navadvipa. PK: "who knows what bhava rises in Him,
who can tell it?" (ki bhāba uṭhaye ke tāhā kahite pāre).

## 14. Yadunandana — "kīrtana-lampaṭa ghana ghana nāṭa…" (BR pp. 923–924)
*Gaura, greedy for kirtana, dances untiringly; seeing nothing for His tears, He walks leaning on the hand of Gadadhara Dasa,
cannot tell water from land, repeats the name of Hari, sings, and, seeing the fallen, clasps them to His breast; Brahma and
Shiva bow at His feet. Raga abhiri.*[^11-53]

কীর্তন-লম্পট ঘন ঘন নাট ।
চলইতে আঁখিজলে না হেরই বাট ॥

*kīrtana-lampaṭa ghana ghana nāṭa |*
*calaite ām̐khijale nā herai bāṭa ||*

*Word for word:* kīrtana-lampaṭa — greedy for kirtana; ghana ghana — again and again; nāṭa — dances; calaite — walking; ām̐khi-jale — for tears; nā herai bāṭa — does not see the way

**14.1.** Greedy for kirtana, He dances again and again,
He walks — and for His tears cannot see the way.

সুন্দর গৌরকিশোর ।
পুরুব পিরিতি-রসে ভৈ গেল ভোর ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*sundara gaurakiśora |*
*puruba piriti-rase bhai gela bhora || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* sundara — beautiful; gaura-kiśora — youthful Gaura; puruba piriti-rase — in the rasa of former love; bhai gela bhora — is rapt

**14.2.** *(Refrain)* Beautiful youthful Gaura
is rapt in the rasa of former love.

বলিতে না পারে মুখে আধেক বাণী ।
চলিতে ধরয়ে দাস-গদাধর-পাণি ॥

*balite nā pāre mukhe ādheka bāṇī |*
*calite dharaye dāsa-gadādhara-pāṇi ||*

*Word for word:* balite nā pāre — cannot utter; mukhe — with the mouth; ādheka bāṇī — even half a word; calite — walking; dharaye — holds; dāsa-gadādhara-pāṇi — the hand of Gadadhara Dasa

**14.3.** He cannot utter even half a word,
He walks holding the hand of Gadadhara Dasa.[^11-54]

অরুণ চরণতল না বাঁধয়ে থেহ ।
কিবা জল কিবা থল কিবা বন গেহ ॥

*aruṇa caraṇatala nā bām̐dhaye theha |*
*kibā jala kibā thala kibā bana geha ||*

*Word for word:* aruṇa caraṇa-tala — the red soles; nā bām̐dhaye theha — find no footing; kibā jala — is it water; kibā thala — is it land; kibā bana geha — forest or house

**14.4.** His red soles find no footing:
is it water, is it land, a forest or a house?

জপে হরি হরি নাম আলাপে আভীরী ।
সুমাধুরী করযুগে কিবা ভঙ্গি করি ॥

*jape hari hari nāma ālāpe ābhīrī |*
*sumādhurī karayuge kibā bhaṅgi kari ||*

*Word for word:* jape — repeats; hari hari nāma — the name "Hari, Hari"; ālāpe ābhīrī — sings (the raga) abhiri; sumādhurī — lovely; kara-yuge — with both hands; kibā bhaṅgi kari — what gestures He makes

**14.5.** He repeats the name "Hari, Hari", sings abhiri —
what gestures His lovely hands display![^11-55]

কিবা লাগি কিবা করে কেবা জানে ওর ।
পতিত দুর্গত দেখি ধরি করে কোর ॥

*kibā lāgi kibā kare kebā jāne ora |*
*patita durgata dekhi dhari kare kora ||*

*Word for word:* kibā lāgi — why; kibā kare — what He does; kebā jāne ora — who knows the end of it; patita durgata dekhi — seeing the fallen and wretched; dhari kare kora — clasps to the breast

**14.6.** Why He does what He does — who can fathom it?
Seeing the fallen and wretched, He clasps them to His breast.

অজ ভব আদি দেব পদে করে নতি ।
যদু কহে কৃপা বিনে কে জানিবে মতি ॥

*aja bhaba ādi deba pade kare nati |*
*yadu kahe kṛpā bine ke jānibe mati ||*

*Word for word:* aja bhaba ādi deba — Aja, Bhava and the other gods; pade kare nati — bow at the feet; yadu kahe — Yadu says; kṛpā bine — without mercy; ke jānibe mati — who will fathom (His) mind

**14.7.** Aja, Bhava and the other gods bow at His feet —
Yadu says: without mercy who can fathom His mind?[^11-56]

[^11-53]: Signature: "Yadu" ("yadu kahe"). BR, 12th wave: 1913 ed., pp. 923–924 ("gīte yathā — ābhīrī"), 1960 ed., vv. 3047–3053; in
Narahari Chakravarti's account: "along this path Gorachand slowly walked… in kirtana He danced in many ways". GPT1 — pp.
285–286, no. 28 (abhiri). Not found in PK. The pada was not in the catalogue.
[^11-54]: Gadadhara Dasa is a companion of the Lord (CC Adi 10), the guru of Yadunandana Chakravarti.
[^11-55]: Abhiri is a raga (the pada itself is marked with it); "sings abhiri" — ālāpe ābhīrī (sings the alap in raga abhiri).
[^11-56]: Aja is Brahma, Bhava is Shiva. "Mind" follows the 1960 ed. and GPT1 (mati); the 1913 ed. has "māta". 1913 ed.: "dhāri kare
kora" (14.6).

## 15. Yadunandana — "dāsa-gadādhara-prāṇa gorā…" (BR p. 924)
*Gora, the life of Gadadhara Dasa, is rapt in the memory of His former pastimes: His body is lightning, tears stream from
His eyes, His face is a golden lotus, He trembles, leaps with the cry "Hari!", rolls on the ground like a golden mountain;
the world drowns in prema — only the poet is left out. Raga dhanashi.*[^11-57]

দাস-গদাধর-প্রাণ গোরা ।
পুরুব চরিতে ভেল ভোরা ॥

*dāsa-gadādhara-prāṇa gorā |*
*puruba carite bhela bhorā ||*

*Word for word:* dāsa-gadādhara-prāṇa — the life of Gadadhara Dasa; gorā — Gora; puruba carite — in the former pastimes; bhela bhorā — is rapt

**15.1.** Gora — the life of Gadadhara Dasa —
is rapt in His former pastimes.

বিজুরি-বরণ তনু চোরা ।
কমল-নয়নে বহে লোরা ॥

*bijuri-baraṇa tanu corā |*
*kamala-nayane bahe lorā ||*

*Word for word:* bijuri-baraṇa — of the colour of lightning; tanu — the body; corā — a thief (of hearts); kamala-nayane — from the lotus eyes; bahe lorā — tears flow

**15.2.** His body, the colour of lightning, steals hearts,
from His lotus eyes tears flow.

কনক-কমল মুখ-কাঁতি ।
হাসিতে খসয়ে মণি মোতি ॥

*kanaka-kamala mukha-kām̐ti |*
*hāsite khasaye maṇi moti ||*

*Word for word:* kanaka-kamala — a golden lotus; mukha-kām̐ti — the radiance of the face; hāsite — when He smiles; khasaye — tumble out; maṇi moti — gems and pearls

**15.3.** The radiance of His face is a golden lotus,
when He smiles, gems and pearls tumble out.

বিপুল পুলক-ভরে কম্প ।
হরি হরি বুলি দেই ঝম্প ॥

*bipula pulaka-bhare kampa |*
*hari hari buli dei jhampa ||*

*Word for word:* bipula pulaka-bhare — with abundant thrills; kampa — trembling; hari hari buli — crying "Hari, Hari"; dei jhampa — leaps

**15.4.** With abundant thrills He trembles,
crying "Hari, Hari", He leaps.

না জানে অহর্নিশি নিজ-রসে ।
সঘনে চিকুর চির খসে ॥

*nā jāne aharniśi nija-rase |*
*saghane cikura cira khase ||*

*Word for word:* nā jāne — notices nothing; aharniśi — day and night; nija-rase — in His own rasa; saghane — again and again; cikura — the hair; cira — the garments; khase — come loose

**15.5.** Day and night He notices nothing in His rasa,
again and again His hair and garments come loose.[^11-58]

ঘন ঘন মহি গড়ি যায় ।
হেমগিরি ধরণি লোটায় ॥

*ghana ghana mahi gaṛi yāya |*
*hemagiri dharaṇi loṭāya ||*

*Word for word:* ghana ghana — again and again; mahi gaṛi yāya — rolls on the ground; hema-giri — a golden mountain; dharaṇi loṭāya — rolls on the earth

**15.6.** Again and again He rolls on the ground —
a golden mountain rolling on the earth.

ভাসল ভুবন প্রেম-রসে ।
যদু এড়াইল দীন দোষে ॥

*bhāsala bhubana prema-rase |*
*yadu eṛāila dīna doṣe ||*

*Word for word:* bhāsala bhubana — the world floats; prema-rase — in the rasa of prema; yadu — Yadu; eṛāila — has missed; dīna — worthless; doṣe — by (his) fault

**15.7.** The world floats in the rasa of prema —
only Yadu, worthless, has missed it by his own fault.[^11-59]

[^11-57]: Signature: "Yadu" ("yadu eṛāila dīna doṣe"). BR, 12th wave: 1913 ed., p. 924 ("punardhānaśī"), 1960 ed., vv. 3054–3060 —
before Narahari Sarakara's pada "gaurāṅga ṭhekilā pāke" (chapter 3, no. 1). Not found in PK or GPT1. According to Majumdar it is one of
Yadunandana's padas cited in BR as testimony (BR p. 924; in the catalogue YN-007).
[^11-58]: "Hair and garments" — cikura cira (chikura, hair; chira, cloth).
[^11-59]: "Has missed" — eṛāila; "worthless, by his own fault" — dīna doṣe (1913 and 1960 eds.).

## 16. Balarama Dasa — "naṭabara rasika ramaṇi-manomohana…" (PK 2249)
*A lament over the sannyasa: Krishna, the best of dancers, who enchanted the hearts of the gopis, covering His dark form
with a golden one, has appeared to the world — and this Beloved of Radha, who wore garments marked with kunkuma from Her
breast, now lives under a tree as a sannyasi: what siddhi does He seek? Raga sindhura.*[^11-60]

নটবর রসিক রমণি-মনোমোহন
কত শত বেশ বিলাস ।
শ্যাম বরণ পর গৌর কলেবর
অখিল ভুবন পরকাশ ॥

*naṭabara rasika ramaṇi-manomohana*
*kata śata beśa bilāsa |*
*śyāma baraṇa para gaura kalebara*
*akhila bhubana parakāśa ||*

*Word for word:* naṭabara — the best of dancers; rasika — the knower of rasa; ramaṇi-mano-mohana — enchanting the hearts of young women; kata śata beśa bilāsa — in hundreds of attires and pastimes; śyāma baraṇa para — over the dark form; gaura kalebara — a golden body; akhila bhubana — to the whole world; parakāśa — has appeared

**16.1.** The best of dancers, the knower of rasa, the enchanter of young hearts,
in hundreds of attires and pastimes —
over His dark form clad in a golden body,
He has appeared to the whole world.[^11-61]

দেখ দেখ অদভুত পহুক বিলাস ।
রঙ্গিণি-সঙ্গ-রঙ্গ-রস-রঙ্গিত
হেন জন করিল সন্ন্যাস ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*dekha dekha adabhuta pahuka bilāsa |*
*raṅgiṇi-saṅga-raṅga-rasa-raṅgita*
*hena jana karila sannyāsa || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* dekha dekha — look, look; adabhuta — wondrous; pahuka bilāsa — the Lord's play; raṅgiṇi-saṅga-raṅga-rasa-raṅgita — steeped in the rasa of play with the playful (Beloved); hena jana — such a One; karila sannyāsa — has taken sannyasa

**16.2.** *(Refrain)* Look, look — wondrous is the Lord's play:
He who was steeped in the rasa of play with His playful Beloved —
such a One has taken sannyasa![^11-62]

নায়রি-কুচ-তট-কুঙ্কুম-মণ্ডিত
বসন বেশ ধরু সাধে ।
গোরিক থোরি বদন-বিধু চুম্বন
হৃদয় গহন উনমাদে ॥

*nāyari-kuca-taṭa-kuṅkuma-maṇḍita*
*basana beśa dharu sādhe |*
*gorika thori badana-bidhu cumbana*
*hṛdaya gahana unamāde ||*

*Word for word:* nāyari-kuca-taṭa-kuṅkuma-maṇḍita — marked with kunkuma from the Beloved's breast; basana beśa — garments; dharu sādhe — wore gladly; gorika — of the Fair One (Radha); thori — a little (?); badana-bidhu — the moon-like face; cumbana — touching with the lips; hṛdaya gahana — in the depth of the heart; unamāde — in the frenzy (of prema)

**16.3.** He who gladly wore garments
marked with kunkuma from His Beloved's breast,
who in the depth of His heart, in the frenzy of prema, longed
to touch with His lips Her moon-like face —

তাকর গাঢ় আলিঙ্গন সঙ্গমে
পুলকিত অতি অবসাধে ।
মনসিজ-সমরে পরাভব অন্তরে
তেঁ অতি করয়ে বিষাদে ॥

*tākara gāṛha āliṅgana saṅgame*
*pulakita ati abasādhe |*
*manasija-samare parābhaba antare*
*tem̐ ati karaye biṣāde ||*

*Word for word:* tākara — Her; gāṛha āliṅgana saṅgame — in the close embrace; pulakita — thrilled with rapture; ati abasādhe — to exhaustion; manasija-samare — in the contest of love; parābhaba — defeated; antare — in the heart; tem̐ — therefore; ati karaye biṣāde — grieved greatly

**16.4.** who in Her close embrace
thrilled all over with rapture,
who, defeated in the contest of love,
grieved in His heart —[^11-63]

মরকত-বরণ রতন-মণি-ভূষণ
তেজি অব তরু-তলে বাস ।
লম্পট-গুরুবর কোন সিধি সাধয়ে
না বুঝই বলরাম দাস ॥

*marakata-baraṇa ratana-maṇi-bhūṣaṇa*
*teji aba taru-tale bāsa |*
*lampaṭa-gurubara kona sidhi sādhaye*
*nā bujhai balarāma dāsa ||*

*Word for word:* marakata-baraṇa — the emerald hue; ratana-maṇi-bhūṣaṇa — jewelled ornaments; teji — abandoning; aba — now; taru-tale bāsa — lives beneath a tree; lampaṭa-gurubara — the first of fickle lovers; kona sidhi sādhaye — what siddhi does He seek; nā bujhai — does not understand; balarāma dāsa — Balarama Dasa

**16.5.** now, abandoning His emerald hue and jewelled ornaments,
lives beneath a tree.
The first of fickle lovers — what siddhi does He seek?
Balarama Dasa does not understand.[^11-64]

[^11-60]: Signature: "Balarama Dasa" ("nā bujhai balarāma dāsa"). PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 286 (printed p. 275), 21st pallava "The sannyasa
of Sri Gauranga and so on", no. 32 (label "॥৩২॥২২৪৯॥"); raga sindhura; P-R-Sa MS no. 2354. GPT1 — p. 19, no. 52; GPT2 — sec.
1.2, no. 52. In the catalogue — BD-006 (number corrected in chapter 7). The next pada, PK 2250 ("gopīgaṇa-kuca-kuṅkume
bañcita…"), is signed "Natavara" (in the P-R-Sa MS "Balarama"); not included in this chapter.
[^11-61]: "Over His dark form a golden body": Krishna appeared covered by Radha's golden radiance (CC Adi 4; "Krishna within,
Gaura without"). MSS "ka", "kha", "cha": bibaraṇa instead of baraṇa; Ray thinks the original reading was "śyāmari baraṇa" and in his
note compares the line with PK 2259 ("antarete śyāma-tanu bāhire gaurāṅga").
[^11-62]: The pada speaks of Krishna's transcendental pastimes with Radha: Their love is pure prema, having nothing in common
with mundane passion (Bhaktisiddhanta: aprakrita-shringara). The poet contrasts Krishna, the Beloved of Vraja, with Krishna
become the sannyasi Gaura.
[^11-63]: "Defeated in the contest of love": Krishna is defeated by Radha's love; to taste it He appeared as Gaura (CC Adi 4).
MSS "ka", "kha", "cha", P-R-Sa: "in union" (saṅgama); MS "ka": "with great joy" (atiśaya sādhe), P-R-Sa: "ati apasādhe"; so too
GPT1: "pulakita atiśaya sādhe"; MS "gha": manabhaba instead of manasija.
[^11-64]: "Emerald hue" — Krishna's dark form. "The first of fickle lovers" — lampaṭa-gurubara (literally "the foremost teacher of
rakes"): a tender reproach in the spirit of the gopis, who call Krishna a deceiver (Bhag. 10.31, 10.47); we translate
faithfully to the author.

## 17. Balarama Dasa — "hari hari e baṛa bismaya lāge mane…" (PK 2251)
*A lament over the sannyasa: He whose body was darker than a new cloud has become Gauranga; the head that wore a crown with
a peacock feather is shaven; the eyes that charmed Radha are full of tears; He who sported with the gopas and gopis now
does not hear even the name of a woman; the hands that held the flute hold a staff; instead of yellow silk — saffron
garments. Raga shri.*[^11-65]

হরি হরি এ বড় বিস্ময় লাগে মনে ।
জিনি নব জলধর পূর্বে যার কলেবর
সে এবে গৌরাঙ্গ ভেল কেনে ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*hari hari e baṛa bismaya lāge mane |*
*jini naba jaladhara pūrve yāra kalebara*
*se ebe gaurāṅga bhela kene || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* hari hari — Hari, Hari; e baṛa bismaya — great wonder; lāge mane — (fills) the heart; jini naba jaladhara — outshining a new cloud; pūrve yāra kalebara — whose body formerly; se ebe — He now; gaurāṅga bhela kene — why has He become Gauranga

**17.1.** *(Refrain)* Hari, Hari! Great wonder fills my heart:
He whose body once outshone a new cloud —
why has He now become Gauranga?

শিখি-পুচ্ছ গুঞ্জা-বেড়া মনোহর যার চূড়া
সে মস্তকে কেশ-শূন্য দেখি ।
যার বাঁকা চাহনিতে মোহে রাধিকার চিতে
এবে প্রেমে ছলছল আঁখি ॥

*śikhi-puccha guñjā-beṛā manohara yāra cūṛā*
*se mastake keśa-śūnya dekhi |*
*yāra bām̐kā cāhanite mohe rādhikāra cite*
*ebe preme chalachala ām̐khi ||*

*Word for word:* śikhi-puccha — with a peacock feather; guñjā-beṛā — wreathed in gunja; manohara — lovely; yāra cūṛā — whose crown; se mastake — on that head; keśa-śūnya dekhi — I see (it) without hair; yāra bām̐kā cāhanite — by whose crooked glance; mohe rādhikāra cite — Radhika's heart is captivated; ebe — now; preme chalachala ām̐khi — eyes full of tears of prema

**17.2.** He whose crown was lovely, with a peacock feather, wreathed in gunja —
that head I see without hair.
He whose crooked glance captivated Radhika's heart —
His eyes are now full of tears of prema.

সদা গোপ গোপী সঙ্গে বিলসয়ে রস-রঙ্গে
এবে নারী-নাম না শুনয়ে ।
ভুজযুগে বংশী ধরি আকর্ষয়ে ব্রজ-নারী
সেই ভুজে দণ্ড কেনে লয়ে ॥

*sadā gopa gopī saṅge bilasaye rasa-raṅge*
*ebe nārī-nāma nā śunaye |*
*bhujayuge baṃśī dhari ākarṣaye braja-nārī*
*sei bhuje daṇḍa kene laye ||*

*Word for word:* sadā — always; gopa gopī saṅge — with the gopas and gopis; bilasaye rasa-raṅge — sported, delighting in rasa; ebe — now; nārī-nāma nā śunaye — does not hear even the name of a woman; bhuja-yuge — with both hands; baṃśī dhari — holding the flute; ākarṣaye braja-nārī — drew the women of Vraja; sei bhuje — in those hands; daṇḍa kene laye — why takes a staff

**17.3.** He who always sported with the gopas and gopis, delighting in rasa —
now does not hear even the name of a woman.
He who, holding the flute in both hands, drew the women of Vraja —
why does He take a staff in those hands?[^11-66]

পিয়ল পাটের ধটি শোভা করে যার কটি
তাহে কেনে অরুণ বসন ।
না পায়্যা ভাবের ওর বলরাম দাস ভোর
বিষাদ ভাবয়ে মনে মন ॥

*piyala pāṭera dhaṭi śobhā kare yāra kaṭi*
*tāhe kene aruṇa basana |*
*nā pāyyā bhābera ora balarāma dāsa bhora*
*biṣāda bhābaye mane mana ||*

*Word for word:* piyala pāṭera dhaṭi — yellow silk cloth; śobhā kare yāra kaṭi — adorned whose hips; tāhe kene — why on Him; aruṇa basana — saffron (reddish) garments; nā pāyyā bhābera ora — not finding the bottom of the bhava; balarāma dāsa bhora — Balarama Dasa, bewildered; biṣāda bhābaye mane mana — ponders sorrowfully in his heart

**17.4.** He whose hips were adorned with yellow silk —
why does He wear saffron garments?
Finding no bottom to this bhava, Balarama Dasa, bewildered,
ponders a sorrowful thought in his heart.[^11-67]

[^11-65]: Signature: "Balarama Dasa." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 287 (printed p. 276), 21st pallava, no. 34 (label "॥৩৪॥২২৫১॥"); raga
shri; P-R-Sa MS no. 2356. GPT1 — p. 19, no. 51; GPT2 — sec. 1.2, no. 51. The catalogue (BD-005) listed it as "GPT only": the
PK number was found on the scan.
[^11-66]: Gunja are red-and-black berries from which the cowherds of Vraja make necklaces. GPT1: "He who was always with the
gopis, speaking with them in many playful ways…" (sadā gopī saṅge rahe, nānā raṅge kathā kahe). A sannyasi does not listen to
talk of women — thus the Lord strictly kept the rules of sannyasa (CC Antya 2).
[^11-67]: MS P-R-Sa: "grievous" (biṣama) instead of "wonder" (bismaya) in 17.1.

## 18. Balarama Dasa — "rūpa koṭi kāma jini…" (PK 2252)
*A lament over the sannyasa: He whose beauty outshines millions of Kamadevas, who sports in Goloka, the son of the king of
Vraja, the treasure of the gopis' lives — why does He roll on the ground and weep in the midst of sankirtana? He who
sported with Radha, Chandravali and hundreds of young cowherd girls is now a sannyasi with a staff; abandoning His graceful
attire, He goes from land to land seeking out the fallen. Raga sindhura.*[^11-68]

রূপ কোটি কাম জিনি বিদগধ-শিরোমণি
গোলোকে বিহরে কুতূহলে ।
ব্রজ-রাজ-নন্দন গোপিকার প্রাণ-ধন
কি লাগি লোটায় ভূমি-তলে ॥

*rūpa koṭi kāma jini bidagadha-śiromaṇi*
*goloke bihare kutūhale |*
*braja-rāja-nandana gopikāra prāṇa-dhana*
*ki lāgi loṭāya bhūmi-tale ||*

*Word for word:* rūpa — in beauty; koṭi kāma jini — outshining millions of Kamadevas; bidagadha-śiromaṇi — the crest-jewel of the skilful; goloke bihare — sports in Goloka; kutūhale — full of delight; braja-rāja-nandana — the son of the king of Vraja; gopikāra prāṇa-dhana — the treasure of the gopis' lives; ki lāgi — why; loṭāya bhūmi-tale — rolls on the ground

**18.1.** He whose beauty outshines millions of Kamadevas, the crest-jewel of the skilful,
who sports in Goloka full of delight —
the son of the king of Vraja, the treasure of the gopis' lives —
why does He roll on the ground?

হরি হরি কি শেল রহিল মোর বুকে ।
কি লাগি রসিক-রাজ কান্দে সংকীর্তন মাঝ
না বুঝিয়া মলুঁ মন-দুখে ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*hari hari ki śela rahila mora buke |*
*ki lāgi rasika-rāja kānde saṃkīrtana mājha*
*nā bujhiyā malum̐ mana-dukhe || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* hari hari — Hari, Hari; ki śela — what a spear; rahila mora buke — has lodged in my breast; ki lāgi — why; rasika-rāja — the king of rasikas; kānde — weeps; saṃkīrtana mājha — in the midst of sankirtana; nā bujhiyā — not understanding; malum̐ — I am dying; mana-dukhe — of grief

**18.2.** *(Refrain)* Hari, Hari! What a spear has lodged in my breast:
why does the king of rasikas weep in the midst of sankirtana?
Not understanding it, I am dying of grief.

সঙ্গে বিলসই যার রাধা চন্দ্রাবলী আর
কত শত বরজ-কিশোরী ।
এবে পহু বুকে বুক না দেখে নারীর মুখ
কি লাগি সন্ন্যাসী দণ্ড-ধারী ॥

*saṅge bilasai yāra rādhā candrābalī āra*
*kata śata baraja-kiśorī |*
*ebe pahu buke buka nā dekhe nārīra mukha*
*ki lāgi sannyāsī daṇḍa-dhārī ||*

*Word for word:* saṅge — with; bilasai — sported; yāra — with whom; rādhā candrābalī āra — Radha and Chandravali and; kata śata — hundreds; baraja-kiśorī — young girls of Vraja; ebe pahu — now the Lord; buke buka — breast to breast (?); nā dekhe nārīra mukha — does not look at a woman's face; ki lāgi — why; sannyāsī daṇḍa-dhārī — a sannyasi bearing a staff

**18.3.** He with whom Radha and Chandravali sported,
and hundreds of young girls of Vraja —
now the Lord, breast to breast, does not look at a woman's face:
why is He a sannyasi with a staff?[^11-69]

ছাড়ি নাগরালি-বেশ ভ্রমে পহু দেশ দেশ
পতিত চাহিয়া ঘরে ঘরে ।
চিন্তামণি নিজ-গুণে উদ্ধারিলা জগ-জনে
বলরাম দাস রহু দূরে ॥

*chāṛi nāgarāli-beśa bhrame pahu deśa deśa*
*patita cāhiyā ghare ghare |*
*cintāmaṇi nija-guṇe uddhārilā jaga-jane*
*balarāma dāsa rahu dūre ||*

*Word for word:* chāṛi — abandoning; nāgarāli-beśa — the graceful attire; bhrame pahu deśa deśa — the Lord wanders from land to land; patita cāhiyā — seeking the fallen; ghare ghare — in every house; cintāmaṇi nija-guṇe — by His chintamani-like qualities; uddhārilā — saved; jaga-jane — the people of the world; balarāma dāsa — Balarama Dasa; rahu dūre — remains far away

**18.4.** Abandoning His graceful attire, the Lord goes from land to land,
seeking out the fallen in every house;
by His qualities, like a chintamani, He has saved the people of the world —
only Balarama Dasa remains far away.[^11-70]

[^11-68]: Signature: "Balarama Dasa." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 287 (printed p. 276), 21st pallava, no. 35 (label "॥৩৫॥২২৫২॥"); raga
sindhura; P-R-Sa MS no. 2357. GPT1 — p. 19, no. 50 (a footnote in GPT1 gives a manuscript variant signed by Vasu Ghosha);
GPT2 — sec. 1.2, no. 50. In the catalogue — BD-004.
[^11-69]: Chandravali is a gopi, Radha's rival. The sense of "buke buka" ("breast to breast") is unclear: probably the Lord
embraces the devotees in kirtana but does not look at women. GPT1: "nā dekhena nārīmukha". MS P-R-Sa: "many" (bahu) instead of
"the Lord" (pahu) in 18.4.
[^11-70]: The chintamani is the wish-fulfilling touchstone. MS P-R-Sa: "by the gift of the chintamani of the Name"
(nāma-cintāmaṇi-dāne) instead of "by His qualities, like a chintamani" (cintāmaṇi nija-guṇe).

## 19. Murari — "dhara dhara dhara dhara re nitāi…" (PK 2235)
*Shantipura after the sannyasa: Shachi watches her sannyasi son dancing in kirtana in Advaita's house and begs Nitai,
Advaita and Srivasa to support Him when He falls and to stop the kirtana — the night is already far gone. Raga
ramakeli.*[^11-71]

ধর ধর ধর ধর রে নিতাই
আমার গৌরাঙ্গ ধর ।
আছাড়-সময়ে অনুজ বলিয়া
বারেক করুণা কর ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*dhara dhara dhara dhara re nitāi*
*āmāra gaurāṅga dhara |*
*āchāṛa-samaye anuja baliyā*
*bāreka karuṇā kara || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* dhara dhara — hold, hold; re nitāi — O Nitai; āmāra gaurāṅga dhara — hold my Gauranga; āchāṛa-samaye — when He falls; anuja baliyā — as Your younger brother; bāreka — just once; karuṇā kara — show mercy

**19.1.** *(Refrain)* "Hold Him, hold Him, hold Him, hold Him, Nitai,
hold my Gauranga!
When He falls, remember that He is Your younger brother,
show mercy just once!"[^11-72]

আচার্য্য গোসাঞি দেখিহ নিমাই
আমার আঁখির তারা ।
না জানি কি খেণে নাচিতে কীর্তনে
পরাণে হইব হারা ॥

*ācāryya gosāñi dekhiha nimāi*
*āmāra ām̐khira tārā |*
*nā jāni ki kheṇe nācite kīrtane*
*parāṇe haiba hārā ||*

*Word for word:* ācāryya gosāñi — Acharya Gosani; dekhiha nimāi — take care of Nimai; āmāra ām̐khira tārā — the pupil of my eyes; nā jāni — I do not know; ki kheṇe — at what moment; nācite kīrtane — while (He) dances in kirtana; parāṇe haiba hārā — I shall lose my life

**19.2.** "Acharya Gosani, take care of Nimai —
the pupil of my eyes!
I do not know at what moment, while He dances in kirtana,
I shall lose my life."[^11-73]

শুনহ শ্রীবাস করাছে সন্ন্যাস
ভূমি-তলে গড়ি যায় ।
সোণার বরণ ননীর পুতলী
বেথা না লাগয়ে গায় ॥

*śunaha śrībāsa karāche sannyāsa*
*bhūmi-tale gaṛi yāya |*
*soṇāra baraṇa nanīra putalī*
*bethā nā lāgaye gāya ||*

*Word for word:* śunaha śrībāsa — listen, Srivasa; karāche sannyāsa — (He) has taken sannyasa; bhūmi-tale gaṛi yāya — rolls on the ground; soṇāra baraṇa — golden in colour; nanīra putalī — a doll of butter; bethā nā lāgaye gāya — may His body not be hurt

**19.3.** "Listen, Srivasa: He has taken sannyasa —
He rolls on the ground;
golden in colour, a little doll of butter —
may He not be hurt!"

শুন ভক্তগণ রাখহ কীর্তন
হইল অধিক নিশা ।
কহয়ে মুরারি শুন গৌরহরি
দেখহ মায়ের দশা ॥

*śuna bhaktagaṇa rākhaha kīrtana*
*haila adhika niśā |*
*kahaye murāri śuna gaurahari*
*dekhaha māyera daśā ||*

*Word for word:* śuna bhakta-gaṇa — listen, devotees; rākhaha kīrtana — stop the kirtana; haila adhika niśā — the night is far gone; kahaye murāri — Murari says; śuna gaurahari — listen, Gaurahari; dekhaha māyera daśā — see the state of Your mother

**19.4.** "Listen, devotees, stop the kirtana —
the night is far gone!"
Murari says: listen, Gaurahari,
see what Your mother is going through![^11-74]

[^11-71]: Signature: "Murari" ("kahaye murāri śuna gaurahari"). PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 280 (printed p. 269), 21st pallava, no. 18 (label
"॥১৮॥২২৩৫॥"); raga ramakeli; P-R-Sa MS no. 2340. The preceding PK 2233 (Vallabha Dasa) and PK 2234 (Nayanananda, chapter 10,
no. 24) concern the same stay of the Lord in Advaita's house. GPT1 — p. 380, no. 46 (ramakeli or turi). In chapter 10 the
pada was found to have been wrongly counted as Nayanananda's (NN-021/027 = PK 2234); the Murari section of the catalogue had
no row for it. Whether this Murari is Murari Gupta is not proven (Majumdar doubts other padas signed "Murari" too);
attribution C. Cf. Shachi in Shantipura — CC Madhya 3, CB Antya 1.
[^11-72]: "Your younger brother" — anuja: Shachi sees in Nityananda Nimai's elder brother (a second Vishvarupa, as it were; cf. Shachi's dream of the two
brothers, Krishna and Balarama, CB Madhya 8). MSS "ka", "kha", "cha", P-R-Sa: "hold, hold" (twice); "ka", "kha", "cha": "my Gora"; "gha": "my Gaura".
[^11-73]: MSS "ka", "kha", "cha", P-R-Sa: "take care of Nitai" (nitāi) instead of "Nimai"; P-R-Sa: "of my eyes" (nayana), "some day"
(kakhane) instead of "at what moment".
[^11-74]: "A little doll of butter" — nanīra putalī: so tender, to a mother's feeling, is His body. Shachi's last words and the poet's
signature merge: Murari asks the Lord to have pity on His mother.

## 20. Balarama Dasa — "gaurasundara pahum̐ nadīyā udaya kari…" (PK 2244)
*Gaura rose in Nadia and filled the world with prema, saving the low and fallen with the holy name; He weeps seeing
Gadadhara, holding the hands of Svarupa and Ramananda, rolls in the dust crying "Shripada!", and Nityananda, embracing
Him, weeps; the blind and the deaf go mad with His qualities, high and low become bhagavatas. Raga ramakeli.*[^11-75]

গৌরসুন্দর পহুঁ নদীয়া উদয় করি
ভুবন ভরিয়া প্রেম-দান ।
পামর পাষণ্ড আদি দীন হীন ক্ষীণ জাতি
উদ্ধারিল দিয়া হরি-নাম ॥

*gaurasundara pahum̐ nadīyā udaya kari*
*bhubana bhariyā prema-dāna |*
*pāmara pāṣaṇḍa ādi dīna hīna kṣīṇa jāti*
*uddhārila diyā hari-nāma ||*

*Word for word:* gaurasundara pahum̐ — the Lord Gaurasundara; nadīyā udaya kari — rising in Nadia; bhubana bhariyā — filling the world; prema-dāna — with the gift of prema; pāmara pāṣaṇḍa ādi — the low, the godless and the rest; dīna hīna kṣīṇa jāti — the poor, the wretched, the weak and low-born; uddhārila — saved; diyā hari-nāma — giving the name of Hari

**20.1.** The Lord Gaurasundara, rising in Nadia,
filled the world with the gift of prema;
the low, the godless, the poor, the wretched, the weak and low-born
He saved, giving them the name of Hari.

ঠাকুর গৌরাঙ্গের গুণ শুনিতে পরাণ কান্দে ।
অগেয়ান যত জন দেখিয়া সুথির-মন
হরিবোল বলি মন বান্ধে ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*ṭhākura gaurāṅgera guṇa śunite parāṇa kānde |*
*ageyāna yata jana dekhiyā suthira-mana*
*haribola bali mana bāndhe || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* ṭhākura gaurāṅgera guṇa — the qualities of Thakura Gauranga; śunite — hearing; parāṇa kānde — the soul weeps; ageyāna yata jana — all the ignorant; dekhiyā — seeing (Him); suthira-mana — their minds made steady; haribola bali — crying "Haribol"; mana bāndhe — bind their hearts (to Him)

**20.2.** *(Refrain)* Hearing of the qualities of Thakura Gauranga, my soul weeps.
All the ignorant, seeing Him, their minds made steady,
cry "Haribol!" and give Him their hearts.[^11-76]

গদাধর দেখি কান্দে মন থির নাহি বান্ধে
করে ধরি স্বরূপ রামানন্দে ।
পহু মোর শ্রীপাদ বলি লোটায় ধরণী-ধূলি
কোলে করি কান্দে নিত্যানন্দে ॥

*gadādhara dekhi kānde mana thira nāhi bāndhe*
*kare dhari svarūpa rāmānande |*
*pahu mora śrīpāda bali loṭāya dharaṇī-dhūli*
*kole kari kānde nityānande ||*

*Word for word:* gadādhara dekhi — seeing Gadadhara; kānde — weeps; mana thira nāhi bāndhe — cannot calm His mind; kare dhari — holding the hands; svarūpa rāmānande — of Svarupa and Ramananda; pahu mora — my Lord; śrīpāda bali — crying "Shripada"; loṭāya dharaṇī-dhūli — rolls in the dust of the earth; kole kari — embracing (Him); kānde nityānande — Nityananda weeps

**20.3.** Seeing Gadadhara, He weeps, He cannot calm Himself,
holding the hands of Svarupa and Ramananda;
my Lord, crying "Shripada!", rolls in the dust of the earth —
embracing Him, Nityananda weeps.[^11-77]

অন্ধ বধির যত গোরা-গুণে উনমত
দিগ বিদিগ নাহি জানে ।
ভাব-ভরে গরগর না চিনে আপন পর
নিস্তার করয়ে জনে জনে ॥

*andha badhira yata gorā-guṇe unamata*
*diga bidiga nāhi jāne |*
*bhāba-bhare garagara nā cine āpana para*
*nistāra karaye jane jane ||*

*Word for word:* andha badhira yata — all the blind and deaf; gorā-guṇe — by Gora's qualities; unamata — maddened; diga bidiga nāhi jāne — know not the quarters of the sky; bhāba-bhare garagara — brimming with bhava; nā cine āpana para — not knowing own and others; nistāra karaye — delivers; jane jane — person after person

**20.4.** The blind, the deaf — all are maddened by Gora's qualities,
they know not the quarters of the sky;
brimming with bhava, not knowing His own and others,
He delivers one person after another.

বাহু তুলি হরি বোলে পতিত লইয়া কোলে
গোরা-প্রেমে জগ-জন ভাসে ।
উত্তম অধম যত তারা হৈল ভাগবত
বঞ্চিত বলরাম দাসে ॥

*bāhu tuli hari bole patita laiyā kole*
*gorā-preme jaga-jana bhāse |*
*uttama adhama yata tārā haila bhāgabata*
*bañcita balarāma dāse ||*

*Word for word:* bāhu tuli — raising the arms; hari bole — cries "Hari"; patita laiyā kole — embracing the fallen; gorā-preme — in Gora's prema; jaga-jana bhāse — the world floats; uttama adhama yata — all the high and the low; tārā haila bhāgabata — have become bhagavatas; bañcita — left out; balarāma dāse — Balarama Dasa

**20.5.** Raising His arms, He cries "Hari", embracing the fallen —
the world floats in Gora's prema;
the high and the low — all have become bhagavatas,
only Balarama Dasa is left out.[^11-78]

[^11-75]: Signature: "Balarama Dasa" ("bañcita balarāma dāse"). PK: vol. 3, PDF pp. 283–284 (printed pp. 272–273), 21st pallava, no.
27 (label "॥২৭॥২২৪৪॥"); raga ramakeli; P-R-Sa MS no. 2349. GPT1 — p. 45, no. 63 (ramakeli); GPT2 — sec. 1.3, no. 63. In the
catalogue — BD-011; the same PK 2244 was wrongly given for YN-001, "praphullita kanaka-kamala mukhamaṇḍala" (that is GPT1 p. 118, no. 24,
signed "Vijayananda Dasa", in GPT2 "Yadunandana Dasa"; not in PK). The preceding PK 2243, "jībe emana dayā kothāo nā dekhi", is
signed "Vasudasa".
[^11-76]: GPT1: "seeing Him, their minds unsteady" (athira mana) instead of "their minds made steady" (suthira-mana).
[^11-77]: Gadadhara (Pandita), Svarupa Damodara, Ramananda Raya and Nityananda are the Lord's companions in Puri. Shripada is a
respectful address to a sannyasi: so the Lord called Nityananda. MSS "ka", "kha", "cha": "the Lord" (pahu) instead of "mind"
(mana): "the Lord cannot calm Himself"; "ka": "Ramananda", "Nityananda" (without case endings).
[^11-78]: A bhagavata is a devotee of the Lord. MSS "ka", "kha", "cha", P-R-Sa: "embracing the pandits" (paṇḍita) instead of "the
fallen" (patita).

## 21. Balarama Dasa — "āpanāra guṇa śuni āpanā pāsare…" (PK 2245)
*Hearing of His own qualities, Gaura forgets Himself: His saffron garments slip off, He embraces the fallen, weeping He
begs Nityananda for the dust of His feet, Nitai weeps "my brother!"; Gadadhara, Ramananda, Vasu, Srivasa, Mukunda and
Murari weep; young and old rejoice, beasts and birds weep. Raga varari.*[^11-79]

আপনার গুণ শুনি আপনা পাসরে ।
অরুণ অম্বর খসে তাহা না সম্বরে ॥

*āpanāra guṇa śuni āpanā pāsare |*
*aruṇa ambara khase tāhā nā sambare ||*

*Word for word:* āpanāra guṇa śuni — hearing His own qualities; āpanā pāsare — forgets Himself; aruṇa ambara — the saffron garment; khase — slips; tāhā nā sambare — He does not set it right

**21.1.** Hearing of His own qualities, He forgets Himself,
His saffron garment slips — He does not set it right.

নাহি দিগ বিদিগ নাহি নিজ পর ।
ধরিয়া ধরিয়া কান্দে পতিত পামর ॥

*nāhi diga bidiga nāhi nija para |*
*dhariyā dhariyā kānde patita pāmara ||*

*Word for word:* nāhi diga bidiga — no quarters of the sky; nāhi nija para — no own and other; dhariyā dhariyā — clasping, clasping; kānde — weeps; patita pāmara — (over) the fallen and the low

**21.2.** For Him there are no quarters of the sky, no own and other:
clasping, clasping them, He weeps over the fallen and the low.[^11-80]

শ্রীপাদ বলিয়া পহু কান্দে উচ্চ স্বরে ।
কত শত ধারা বহে নয়ন-কমলে ॥

*śrīpāda baliyā pahu kānde ucca svare |*
*kata śata dhārā bahe nayana-kamale ||*

*Word for word:* śrīpāda baliyā — crying "Shripada"; pahu — the Lord; kānde ucca svare — weeps aloud; kata śata dhārā — in hundreds of streams; bahe — flow; nayana-kamale — from the lotus eyes

**21.3.** Crying "Shripada!", the Lord weeps aloud,
in hundreds of streams the tears pour from His lotus eyes.

কান্দিয়া কান্দিয়া পহু মাগে পদ-ধূলি ।
ভূমে পড়ি কান্দে নিতাই ভাইয়া ভাইয়া বলি ॥

*kāndiyā kāndiyā pahu māge pada-dhūli |*
*bhūme paṛi kānde nitāi bhāiyā bhāiyā bali ||*

*Word for word:* kāndiyā kāndiyā — weeping, weeping; pahu māge — the Lord begs; pada-dhūli — the dust of the feet; bhūme paṛi — falling on the ground; kānde nitāi — Nitai weeps; bhāiyā bhāiyā bali — saying "brother, brother"

**21.4.** Weeping, weeping, the Lord begs for the dust of His feet;
fallen on the ground, Nitai weeps, saying: "My brother, brother!"[^11-81]

প্রিয় গদাধর কান্দে রায় রামানন্দে ।
দেখিয়া গৌরাঙ্গ-মুখ থির নাহি বান্ধে ॥

*priya gadādhara kānde rāya rāmānande |*
*dekhiyā gaurāṅga-mukha thira nāhi bāndhe ||*

*Word for word:* priya gadādhara — dear Gadadhara; kānde — weeps; rāya rāmānande — Raya Ramananda; dekhiyā gaurāṅga-mukha — seeing Gauranga's face; thira nāhi bāndhe — cannot calm themselves

**21.5.** Dear Gadadhara and Raya Ramananda weep,
seeing Gauranga's face, they cannot calm themselves.

কান্দে বাসু শ্রীবাস মুকুন্দ মুরারি ।
আনন্দে চলয়ে যত বাল বৃদ্ধ নারী ॥

*kānde bāsu śrībāsa mukunda murāri |*
*ānande calaye yata bāla bṛddha nārī ||*

*Word for word:* kānde — weep; bāsu — Vasu; śrībāsa — Srivasa; mukunda — Mukunda; murāri — Murari; ānande — in bliss; calaye — go; yata — all; bāla bṛddha nārī — children, old men, women

**21.6.** Vasu, Srivasa, Mukunda and Murari weep;
in bliss all go along — children, old men, women.[^11-82]

হেন অবতার ভাই কোথাও না দেখি ।
ভুবন মগন সুখে কান্দে পশু পাখী ॥

*hena abatāra bhāi kothāo nā dekhi |*
*bhubana magana sukhe kānde paśu pākhī ||*

*Word for word:* hena abatāra — such an incarnation; bhāi — brothers; kothāo nā dekhi — I have seen nowhere; bhubana magana sukhe — the world is sunk in happiness; kānde paśu pākhī — beasts and birds weep

**21.7.** Such an incarnation, brothers, I have seen nowhere:
the world is sunk in happiness, beasts and birds weep.

অন্ধ বধির জড় সভে আনন্দিত ।
বলরাম দাস সবে এ রসে বঞ্চিত ॥

*andha badhira jaṛa sabhe ānandita |*
*balarāma dāsa sabe e rase bañcita ||*

*Word for word:* andha badhira jaṛa — the blind, the deaf, the dull; sabhe ānandita — all are in bliss; balarāma dāsa — Balarama Dasa; sabe — (of) all; e rase bañcita — is left out of this rasa

**21.8.** The blind, the deaf, the dull — all are in bliss,
Balarama Dasa alone of all is left out of this rasa.[^11-83]

[^11-79]: Signature: "Balarama Dasa." PK: vol. 3, PDF pp. 284–285 (printed pp. 273–274), 21st pallava, no. 28 (label "॥২৮॥২২৪৫॥");
raga varari; P-R-Sa MS no. 2350. GPT1 — p. 45, no. 64, and p. 289, no. 40; GPT2 — sec. 1.3, no. 64, and 4.3, no. 40. The
catalogue (BD-012) listed it as "GPT only": the PK number was found on the scan.
[^11-80]: MS P-R-Sa: "for Him there are no quarters of the sky" (diga bidiga tāhe nāhi).
[^11-81]: In the humility of a devotee the Lord begs Nityananda for the dust of His feet, and Nityananda calls Him brother (cf.
CB Antya 5–6). GPT1 (p. 289): "fallen on the ground, He weeps: 'Nitai, Nitai, brother!'".
[^11-82]: Vasu is Vasu Ghosha or Vasudeva Datta; Srivasa, Mukunda (Datta) and Murari (Gupta) are companions from Navadvipa who
came to the Lord in Puri. MSS "ka", "kha", "cha", P-R-Sa: "Srinivasa" (śrīnibāsa); "as if" (yena) instead of "all" (yata).
[^11-83]: MS "gha": "such an incarnation I have never seen anywhere" (āra kabhu nāhi dekhi) in 21.7. GPT1: "only Balarama Dasa is left
out of this rasa" (balarāma dāsa mātra e rase bañcita).

## 22. Balarama Dasa — "prabhu kahe nityānanda saba jība haila andha…" (PK 2261)
*The Lord sends Nityananda to Gauda: all souls have gone blind and have not received the name of Hari — let Nityananda
mercifully give the Name to everyone He sees: sinners, slanderers, disputants, students turned away from bhakti,
children, men and women — and flood Gauda with the prema of sankirtana. Raga varari.*[^11-84]

প্রভু কহে নিত্যানন্দ সব জীব হৈল অন্ধ
কেহো ত না পাইল হরি-নাম ।
এক নিবেদন তোরে নয়ানে দেখিবে যারে
কৃপা করি লওয়াইবে নাম ॥

*prabhu kahe nityānanda saba jība haila andha*
*keho ta nā pāila hari-nāma |*
*eka nibedana tore nayāne dekhibe yāre*
*kṛpā kari laoyāibe nāma ||*

*Word for word:* prabhu kahe — the Lord says; nityānanda — Nityananda; saba jība haila andha — all souls have gone blind; keho ta nā pāila hari-nāma — no one has received the name of Hari; eka nibedana tore — one request of You; nayāne dekhibe yāre — whom You see with Your eyes; kṛpā kari — mercifully; laoyāibe nāma — make them repeat the Name

**22.1.** The Lord says: "Nityananda, all souls have gone blind,
no one has received the name of Hari.
I have one request of You: whomever You see with Your eyes,
mercifully make them repeat the Name.

কৃতপাপী দুরাচার নিন্দুক পাষণ্ড আর
কেহো যেন বঞ্চিত না হয় ।
শমন বলিয়া ভয় জীবে যেন নাহি হয়
সুখে যেন হরি-নাম লয় ॥

*kṛtapāpī durācāra ninduka pāṣaṇḍa āra*
*keho yena bañcita nā haya |*
*śamana baliyā bhaya jībe yena nāhi haya*
*sukhe yena hari-nāma laya ||*

*Word for word:* kṛta-pāpī — hardened sinners; durācāra — the wicked; ninduka — slanderers; pāṣaṇḍa āra — and the godless; keho yena bañcita nā haya — let no one be left out; śamana baliyā bhaya — fear of Yama; jībe yena nāhi haya — let souls not have; sukhe — joyfully; yena hari-nāma laya — let them repeat the name of Hari

**22.2.** Hardened sinners, the wicked, slanderers, the godless —
let not one of them be left out;
let souls not fear that Yama will come —
let them joyfully repeat the name of Hari.

কুমতি তার্কিক জন পড়ুয়া অধমগণ
জন্মে জন্মে ভকতি-বিমুখ ।
কৃষ্ণ-প্রেম দান করি বালক পুরুষ নারী
খণ্ডাইহ সবাকার দুখ ॥

*kumati tārkika jana paṛuyā adhamagaṇa*
*janme janme bhakati-bimukha |*
*kṛṣṇa-prema dāna kari bālaka puruṣa nārī*
*khaṇḍāiha sabākāra dukha ||*

*Word for word:* kumati tārkika jana — evil-minded disputants; paṛuyā adhama-gaṇa — low students; janme janme — birth after birth; bhakati-bimukha — turned away from bhakti; kṛṣṇa-prema dāna kari — giving prema for Krishna; bālaka puruṣa nārī — children, men and women; khaṇḍāiha sabākāra dukha — free all from suffering

**22.3.** Evil-minded disputants, low students,
turned away from bhakti birth after birth —
giving prema for Krishna to children, men and women,
free them all from suffering.

সংকীর্তন প্রেম-রসে ভাসাইহ গৌড় দেশে
পূর্ণ কর সভাকার আশ ।
হেন কৃপা-অবতারে উদ্ধার নহিল যারে
কি করিবে বলরাম দাস ॥

*saṃkīrtana prema-rase bhāsāiha gauṛa deśe*
*pūrṇa kara sabhākāra āśa |*
*hena kṛpā-abatāre uddhāra nahila yāre*
*ki karibe balarāma dāsa ||*

*Word for word:* saṃkīrtana prema-rase — with the prema and rasa of sankirtana; bhāsāiha gauṛa deśe — flood the land of Gauda; pūrṇa kara sabhākāra āśa — fulfil the hope of all; hena kṛpā-abatāre — by such an incarnation of mercy; uddhāra nahila yāre — whom (He) did not save; ki karibe balarāma dāsa — what can Balarama Dasa do

**22.4.** Flood the land of Gauda with the prema and rasa of sankirtana,
fulfil the hope of all."
Whom such an incarnation of mercy did not save —
what can Balarama Dasa do?[^11-85]

[^11-84]: Signature: "Balarama Dasa." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 290 (printed p. 279), 21st pallava, section "tatra nityānandacandrasya
gauṛe preraṇaṃ yathā" (the sending of Nityananda to Gauda), no. 44 (label "॥৪৪॥২২৬১॥"); raga varari; P-R-Sa MS no. 2366. GPT1 —
pp. 403–404, no. 6 (varari); GPT2 — sec. 5.5, no. 6. The catalogue (BD-026) listed it as "GPT only": the PK number was found
on the scan. Cf. CC Madhya 15 (the Lord sends Nityananda to preach in Gauda), CB Antya 5.
[^11-85]: MS "kha": "give" (diha) instead of "make them repeat" (laoyāibe) in 22.1; "gha": pāṣaṇḍi; "ka": "flooded" (bhāsāila); "kha":
karā.

## 23. Balarama Dasa — "birale nitāi pāñā…" (PK 2262; fuller in GPT1)
*The Lord alone with Nityananda: "Go to the bank of the Suradhuni and, taking pity on souls, give them the name of Hari; I
have come to give away the Name and prema at Advaita's call, and You are My chief helper; having delivered Nilachala, I
shall go south with Govinda — You hasten to Gauda." Raga varari.*[^11-86]

বিরলে নিতাই পাঞা হাতে ধরি বসাইয়া
মধুর কথা কহে ধীরে ধীরে ।
জীবেরে সদয় হইয়া হরি-নাম লওয়াও গিয়া
যাও নিতাই সুরধুনী-তীরে ॥

*birale nitāi pāñā hāte dhari basāiyā*
*madhura kathā kahe dhīre dhīre |*
*jībere sadaya haiyā hari-nāma laoyāo giyā*
*yāo nitāi suradhunī-tīre ||*

*Word for word:* birale — in private; nitāi pāñā — finding Nitai; hāte dhari — taking His hand; basāiyā — seating (Him); madhura kathā — sweet words; kahe dhīre dhīre — speaks softly; jībere sadaya haiyā — taking pity on souls; hari-nāma laoyāo giyā — go and make them repeat the name of Hari; yāo nitāi — go, Nitai; suradhunī-tīre — to the bank of the Suradhuni (the Ganga)

**23.1.** Finding Nitai alone, taking His hand and seating Him,
the Lord softly speaks sweet words to Him:
"Taking pity on souls, go and make them repeat the name of Hari —
go, Nitai, to the bank of the Suradhuni."

নাম-প্রেম বিতরিতে অদ্বৈতের হুঙ্কারেতে
অবতীর্ণ হইনু ধরায় ।
তারিতে কলির জীব করিতে তাদের শিব
তুমি মোর প্রধান সহায় ॥

*nāma-prema bitarite advaitera huṅkārete*
*abatīrṇa hainu dharāya |*
*tārite kalira jība karite tādera śiba*
*tumi mora pradhāna sahāya ||*

*Word for word:* nāma-prema bitarite — to give away the Name and prema; advaitera huṅkārete — at Advaita's thunderous call; abatīrṇa hainu dharāya — I have descended to earth; tārite kalira jība — to save the souls of Kali; karite tādera śiba — to bring them good; tumi mora pradhāna sahāya — You are My chief helper

**23.2.** "To give away the Name and prema, at Advaita's thunderous call
I have descended to earth;
to save the souls of the Kali age, to bring them good —
You are My chief helper."[^11-87]

নীলাচল উদ্ধারিয়া গোবিন্দেরে সঙ্গে লৈয়া
দক্ষিণ-দেশেতে যাব আমি ।
শ্রীগৌড়-মণ্ডল-ভার করিতে নাম প্রচার
ত্বরা নিতাই যাও তথা তুমি ॥

*nīlācala uddhāriyā gobindere saṅge laiyā*
*dakṣiṇa-deśete yāba āmi |*
*śrīgauṛa-maṇḍala-bhāra karite nāma pracāra*
*tvarā nitāi yāo tathā tumi ||*

*Word for word:* nīlācala uddhāriyā — having delivered Nilachala; gobindere saṅge laiyā — taking Govinda with Me; dakṣiṇa-deśete yāba āmi — I shall go to the southern country; śrī-gauṛa-maṇḍala-bhāra — the charge of Sri Gauda-mandala; karite nāma pracāra — to preach the Name; tvarā — quickly; nitāi — Nitai; yāo tathā tumi — go there Yourself

**23.3.** "Having delivered Nilachala, taking Govinda with Me,
I shall go to the southern country;
the charge of Sri Gauda-mandala — preaching the Name —
quickly, Nitai, go there Yourself."[^11-88]

মো হৈতে না হবে যাহা তুমি ত পারিবে তাহা
প্রেমদাতা পরম দয়াল ।
বলরাম কহে পহুঁ দোঁহার সমান দুহুঁ
তার মোরে আমি ত কাঙ্গাল ॥

*mo haite nā habe yāhā tumi ta pāribe tāhā*
*premadātā parama dayāla |*
*balarāma kahe pahum̐ dom̐hāra samāna duhum̐*
*tāra more āmi ta kāṅgāla ||*

*Word for word:* mo haite nā habe yāhā — what cannot be done by Me; tumi ta pāribe tāhā — that You will be able to do; prema-dātā — the giver of prema; parama dayāla — most merciful; balarāma kahe — Balarama says; pahum̐ — Lords; dom̐hāra samāna duhum̐ — You both are equal; tāra more — deliver me; āmi ta kāṅgāla — I am but a beggar

**23.4.** "What I cannot do, You will be able to do:
You are the giver of prema, the most merciful."
Balarama says: Lords, You both are equal —
deliver me: I am but a beggar.[^11-89]

[^11-86]: PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 291 (printed p. 280), 21st pallava, no. 45 (label "॥৪৫॥২২৬২॥"); the same raga (varari); P-R-Sa MS no.
2367. PK has only the first stanza (23.1), **without a signature**; Ray notes that in the P-R-Sa MS the next pada, PK 2263
("caitanya-ādeśa pāiyā…", signed Premadasa), is written as the end of this one, and thinks this right, but in MSS "ka", "kha",
"gha", "cha" they are separate. The full text with Balarama's signature is in GPT1, p. 404, no. 7 (varari); 23.2–23.4 are
translated from GPT1 (scan PDF p. 663). Attribution C. In the catalogue — BD-027.
[^11-87]: Advaita called on the Lord to appear for the deliverance of the world (CC Adi 3; CB Adi 2).
[^11-88]: Govinda is perhaps Kala Krishnadasa or Govinda, the Lord's servant; according to CC (Madhya 7) the Lord went south with
Kala Krishnadasa and sent Nityananda to Gauda later (Madhya 15) — the poet tells the events differently; we translate
faithfully to the author.
[^11-89]: "You both are equal" — dom̐hāra samāna duhum̐: Gaura and Nitai are equally merciful.

## 24. Kanu Dasa — "nadīyā nagare gelā nityānanda rāya…" (PK 2264)
*Nityananda comes to Nadia and falls at Shachi's feet; embracing Him, she weeps; He consoles her with talk of Gauranga:
"Your son is well and happy, He sent me to see you and bowed many times to your feet: Gauranga is bound by your love."
Raga suhai.*[^11-90]

নদীয়া নগরে গেলা নিত্যানন্দ রায় ।
দণ্ডবৎ হৈয়া পড়ে শচী মাতার পায় ॥

*nadīyā nagare gelā nityānanda rāya |*
*daṇḍabat haiyā paṛe śacī mātāra pāya ||*

*Word for word:* nadīyā nagare — to the town of Nadia; gelā — came; nityānanda rāya — Nityananda Raya; daṇḍabat haiyā — like a rod; paṛe — falls; śacī mātāra pāya — at the feet of Mother Shachi

**24.1.** Nityananda Raya came to the town of Nadia,
fell like a rod at the feet of Mother Shachi.

তারে কোলে করি শচী কান্দয়ে করুণে ।
নয়ানের জলে ভিজে অঙ্গের বসনে ॥

*tāre kole kari śacī kāndaye karuṇe |*
*nayānera jale bhije aṅgera basane ||*

*Word for word:* tāre kole kari — embracing Him; śacī kāndaye karuṇe — Shachi weeps piteously; nayānera jale — with the water of her eyes; bhije — are soaked; aṅgera basane — the garments on her body

**24.2.** Embracing Him, Shachi weeps piteously,
the tears from her eyes soak her garments.

ফুকরি ফুকরি কান্দে কাতর হিয়ায় ।
গৌরাঙ্গের কথা কহি প্রবোধয়ে তায় ॥

*phukari phukari kānde kātara hiyāya |*
*gaurāṅgera kathā kahi prabodhaye tāya ||*

*Word for word:* phukari phukari — crying out, crying out; kānde — weeps; kātara hiyāya — with an anguished heart; gaurāṅgera kathā kahi — telling of Gauranga; prabodhaye tāya — consoles her

**24.3.** Crying out, crying out, she weeps with an anguished heart —
with talk of Gauranga He consoles her.

নিত্যানন্দ বলে মাতা থির কর মন ।
কুশলে আছয়ে সুখে তোমার নন্দন ॥

*nityānanda bale mātā thira kara mana |*
*kuśale āchaye sukhe tomāra nandana ||*

*Word for word:* nityānanda bale — Nityananda says; mātā — mother; thira kara mana — calm your heart; kuśale āchaye sukhe — is well and happy; tomāra nandana — your son

**24.4.** Nityananda says: "Mother, calm your heart:
your son is well and happy.

তোমারে দেখিতে মোরে পাঠাইয়া দিল ।
তোর পদযুগে কত প্রণতি করিল ॥

*tomāre dekhite more pāṭhāiyā dila |*
*tora padayuge kata praṇati karila ||*

*Word for word:* tomāre dekhite — to see you; more pāṭhāiyā dila — sent me; tora pada-yuge — to your feet; kata praṇati karila — bowed many times

**24.5.** He sent me to see you,
many times He bowed to your feet."

কানুদাস কহে মাতা কহি তোর ঠাঞি ।
তোমার প্রেমে বান্ধা আছে গৌরাঙ্গ গোসাঞি ॥

*kānudāsa kahe mātā kahi tora ṭhāñi |*
*tomāra preme bāndhā āche gaurāṅga gosāñi ||*

*Word for word:* kānudāsa kahe — Kanu Dasa says; mātā — mother; kahi tora ṭhāñi — I tell you; tomāra preme — by your love; bāndhā āche — is bound; gaurāṅga gosāñi — Gauranga Gosani

**24.6.** Kanu Dasa says: "Mother, this I tell you:
Gauranga Gosani is bound by your love."[^11-91]

[^11-90]: Signature: "Kanu Dasa" ("kānudāsa kahe"). PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 291 (printed p. 280), 21st pallava, no. 47 (label
"॥৪৭॥২২৬৪॥"); raga suhai; P-R-Sa MS no. 2368. GPT1 — pp. 404–405, no. 10 (suhai); GPT2 — sec. 5.5, no. 10. In the catalogue —
KD-008. Cf. CB Antya 5–6 (Nityananda in Navadvipa with Shachi).
[^11-91]: Kanu Dasa's words continue Nityananda's speech. GPT1: "pāṭhāiyā dilā", "karilā" (honorific forms) in 24.5.

## 25. Krishnadasa — "ciradine gorācām̐dera ānanda apāra…" (PK 2018)
*After long separation — Gorachand's boundless bliss: He tells the devotees of His former pastimes, His body is covered
with thrills, like a kadamba bud with golden filaments; hearing the words from His lips, the devotees are consoled. In
GPT1 it stands among the padas on the Lord's return to the devotees of Nadia.*[^11-92]

চিরদিনে গোরাচাঁদের আনন্দ অপার ।
কহয়ে ভকতগণে পুরব-বিহার ॥

*ciradine gorācām̐dera ānanda apāra |*
*kahaye bhakatagaṇe puraba-bihāra ||*

*Word for word:* ciradine — after a long time; gorācām̐dera — Gorachand's; ānanda apāra — boundless bliss; kahaye — tells; bhakata-gaṇe — the devotees; puraba-bihāra — of the former pastimes

**25.1.** After a long time boundless is Gorachand's bliss:
He tells the devotees of His former pastimes.[^11-93]

পুলকে পূরল তনু আপাদ-মস্তক ।
সোণার কেশর জনু কদম্ব-কোরক ॥

*pulake pūrala tanu āpāda-mastaka |*
*soṇāra keśara janu kadamba-koraka ||*

*Word for word:* pulake pūrala — filled with thrills; tanu — the body; āpāda-mastaka — from head to foot; soṇāra keśara — with golden filaments; janu — like; kadamba-koraka — a kadamba bud

**25.2.** From head to foot His body is filled with thrills —
like a kadamba bud with golden filaments.

ভাবে ভরল মন গদগদ ভাষ ।
অনেক যতনে বিহি পূরায়ল আশ ॥

*bhābe bharala mana gadagada bhāṣa |*
*aneka yatane bihi pūrāyala āśa ||*

*Word for word:* bhābe bharala mana — the heart is full of bhava; gadagada bhāṣa — the speech falters; aneka yatane — after so much striving; bihi — Providence; pūrāyala āśa — has fulfilled the hope

**25.3.** His heart is full of bhava, His speech falters:
after so much striving Providence has fulfilled the hope.[^11-94]

শচীর নন্দন গোরা জাতি প্রাণ ধন ।
শুনি চাঁদ-মুখের কথা জুড়াইল মন ॥

*śacīra nandana gorā jāti prāṇa dhana |*
*śuni cām̐da-mukhera kathā juṛāila mana ||*

*Word for word:* śacīra nandana gorā — Gora, the son of Shachi; jāti — honour (of kin); prāṇa — life; dhana — wealth; śuni — hearing; cām̐da-mukhera kathā — the words of the moon-like lips; juṛāila mana — the heart was consoled

**25.4.** Gora, the son of Shachi, is our honour, life and wealth:
hearing the words from His moon-like lips, the heart is consoled.

গোরাচাঁদের লীলায় যার হইল বিশ্বাস ।
দুখী কৃষ্ণদাস তার দাস-অনুদাস ॥

*gorācām̐dera līlāya yāra haila biśvāsa |*
*dukhī kṛṣṇadāsa tāra dāsa-anudāsa ||*

*Word for word:* gorācām̐dera līlāya — in Gorachand's pastimes; yāra haila biśvāsa — whoever has come to faith; dukhī kṛṣṇadāsa — wretched Krishnadasa; tāra dāsa-anudāsa — the servant of his servants

**25.5.** Whoever has come to faith in Gorachand's pastimes —
wretched Krishnadasa is the servant of his servants.

[^11-92]: Signature: "Krishnadasa" ("dukhī kṛṣṇadāsa"). PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 201 (printed p. 190), opening of the 15th pallava,
section "atha samṛddhimat-sambhogasya rasodgāraḥ — tatra śrīgauracandro yathā" (a gaura-chandrika to Radha's account of full union
after separation), no. 1 (label "॥১॥২০১৮॥"); no raga given. GPT1 — p. 413, no. 32 (shri), right after Vasu Ghosha's pada
"āola nadīyāra loka gaurāṅga dekhite" (chapter 1, no. 23). In the catalogue (KR-003) the pada was listed under nagari-bhava (by
the GPT2 section 3.2) without a first line — it is not a nagari pada. Which Krishnadasa wrote it has not been established
(C).
[^11-93]: "Former pastimes" — puraba-bihāra: Krishna's pastimes in Vraja (in PK the pada introduces Radha's account of Her union
with Krishna).
[^11-94]: It can also be understood as the words of the Lord Himself in Radha's bhava: "after so much striving Providence has
fulfilled My hope." MSS "ka", "kha": jine ("outshining") instead of janu ("like") in 25.2.
