# Chapter 12. Vasu Ghosha: Padas from the *Gaura-pada-tarangini* — Appearance and Childhood, Sannyasa, the Lament of Nadia, Nilachala

*This chapter opens the group of padas known only from the *Gaura-pada-tarangini* (GPT1 — 1st ed. by Jagadbandhu
Bhadra, 1903; GPT2 — 2nd ed., 1934), excluding padas in nagari-bhava. Here are padas signed by Vasu (Vasudeva) Ghosha, in
the order of the lilas: praise of the Gaura-avatara; Gauranga's appearance on the night of the lunar eclipse, the
name-giving, His first steps and "the moon from the sky"; the Lord's morning in Navadvipa and the jhulana; Vishnupriya's
forebodings, the sannyasa at Katwa, the lament of Shachi and the devotees, the Lord with Advaita in Shantipura and His
departure for Nilachala; the lament of Shachi and Vishnupriya; the Lord in Nilachala, His bhava of Radha, and the festival
at Shrikhanda. Two padas were found in the *Padakalpataru* (PK) without a signature (nos. 1 and 15) — there the text
follows PK; no. 27 is an abridged recension of a pada by Govinda Dasa (PK 1463). Ten padas (nos. 1, 3–5, 9–12, 14, 17) were
missing from the stage-1 catalogue: they were found in a full check of the signatures of GPT1 (the catalogue section on Vasu
Ghosha has been supplemented). Majumdar considers the GPT unreliable for attributing padas to Vasu Ghosha: Jagadbandhu included spurious
ones as well; the childhood padas he regards as the poet's invention, and the festival at Shrikhanda (no. 29) and the
pada about Svarupa (no. 28) as forgeries. The attribution of all the padas of this chapter is therefore provisional. The
Bengali original, the variants of GPT1/GPT2 and PK, and the word-for-word translation are in the full version of the book.*

## 1. Vasu Ghosha — "abatāra baṛa abatāra kailā baṛa…" (PK 2347; GPT1 no. 68)
*Praise of the Gaura-avatara: there was no such mercy in any yuga; in every house there is the weeping of prema, the
name of Hari is proclaimed; Gaura has brought a boat laden with prema to the landing and opened a market; Jagai and
Madhai are saved by the name.*[^12-1]

অবতার বড় অবতার কৈলা বড় ।
এমন করুণা কোন যুগে নাহি কর ॥

*abatāra baṛa abatāra kailā baṛa |*
*emana karuṇā kona yuge nāhi kara ||*

*Word for word:* abatāra — incarnation; baṛa — great; abatāra kailā — You made an incarnation; baṛa — great; emana karuṇā — such mercy; kona yuge — in any age; nāhi kara — You do not show (GPT: nāhi āra — there is no other)

**1.1.** A great incarnation, a great incarnation You have made!
Such mercy You have shown in no other yuga.

প্রতি ঘরে ঘরে শুনি প্রেমের কান্দনা ।
কলি-যুগে হরি-নাম রহিল ঘোষণা ॥

*prati ghare ghare śuni premera kāndanā |*
*kali-yuge hari-nāma rahila ghoṣaṇā ||*

*Word for word:* prati ghare ghare — in every house; śuni — I hear; premera kāndanā — the weeping of prema; kali-yuge — in the age of Kali; hari-nāma — the name of Hari; rahila ghoṣaṇā — remained proclaimed

**1.2.** In every house the weeping of prema is heard;
in the age of Kali the name of Hari is proclaimed.[^12-2]

সুখ-সায়রের ঘাটে দিয়া প্রেমের ভরা ।
ভাল হাট পাত্যাছ গৌর প্রেমের পসরা ॥

*sukha-sāyarera ghāṭe diyā premera bharā |*
*bhāla hāṭa pātyācha gaura premera pasarā ||*

*Word for word:* sukha-sāyarera ghāṭe — at the landing of the ocean of happiness; diyā — bringing in; premera bharā — a boatload of prema; bhāla hāṭa — a fine market; pātyācha — You have set up; gaura — Gaura; premera pasarā — wares of prema

**1.3.** To the landing of the ocean of happiness You have brought a boat full of prema;
a fine market You have opened, Gaura — with wares of prema![^12-3]

জগাই মাধাই তারা ছিল দুই ভাই ।
হরি-নামে উদ্ধারিলা চৈতন্য গোসাঞি ॥

*jagāi mādhāi tārā chila dui bhāi |*
*hari-nāme uddhārilā caitanya gosāñi ||*

*Word for word:* jagāi mādhāi — Jagai and Madhai; tārā chila — they were; dui bhāi — two brothers; hari-nāme — by the name of Hari; uddhārilā — delivered; caitanya gosāñi — Chaitanya Gosani

**1.4.** Jagai and Madhai — they were two brothers:
by the name of Hari Chaitanya Gosani saved them.[^12-4]

বাসুদেব ঘোষে কহে না হবে এমন ।
কলি-যুগে ধন্য নাম চৈতন্য-রতন ॥

*bāsudeba ghoṣe kahe nā habe emana |*
*kali-yuge dhanya nāma caitanya-ratana ||*

*Word for word:* bāsudeba ghoṣe kahe — Vasudeva Ghosha says; nā habe emana — there will not be such (again); kali-yuge — in the age of Kali; dhanya nāma — blessed is the name; caitanya-ratana — the jewel Chaitanya

**1.5.** Vasudeva Ghosha says: there will be no other such;
in the age of Kali blessed is the name — the jewel Chaitanya.

[^12-1]: PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 320 (printed p. 309), 4th shakha, last pada of the 23rd pallava (mark "॥১৬॥২৩৪৭॥"), MS P-R-Sa
no. 2451 — **without a signature** (in PK the pada ends at 1.4; it is preceded by PK 2346, signed by Balarama Dasa). GPT1 —
pp. 46–47, no. 68 (raga yatharaga), with the closing couplet 1.5 — the signature of Vasudeva Ghosha; GPT2 — sec. 1.3,
no. 68. Text of 1.1–1.4 follows PK, 1.5 follows GPT. The attribution to Vasu Ghosha is known only from GPT (a new catalogue
entry, VG-154). The first line reads differently in the PK manuscripts and in GPT ("abatāra kailā baṛa baṛa" etc.), see the full version of the book.
[^12-2]: "The weeping of prema" (premera kāndanā) — tears of love for God in kirtana, not worldly grief. The name of Hari as the
dharma of the age of Kali — CC Adi 3, 17.
[^12-3]: Images of trade: the boat (bharā — a boat's cargo; in the PK manuscripts bhārā, "load") comes in to the landing, and Gaura
opens a market (hāṭa) whose "wares" are prema, given away freely. Cf. the padas about the "market" of Nityananda and Gaura
(hāṭa-pattana).
[^12-4]: Jagai and Madhai — the villainous brothers of Navadvipa, saved by the Lord and Nityananda (CB Madhya 13; CC Adi 17).

## 2. Vasu Ghosha — "nadīyā-ākāśe āsi udila gaurāṅga-śaśī…" (GPT1 p. 51, no. 3)
*The appearance of Gauranga: in the sky of Nadia the moon Gauranga has risen, and the moon of the sky, out of shame,
has smeared its face with soot — the eclipse; conches and drums sound in every house; Jagannatha Mishra and Shachi are
beside themselves with joy; in the darkness of the eclipse gods mingle with men, celestial women together with the women
of Nadia gaze at the Child; the father gives gifts to the poor. Raga kalyana.*[^12-5]

নদীয়া-আকাশে আসি উদিল গৌরাঙ্গ-শশী
ভাসিল সকলে কুতূহলে ।
লাজেতে গগন-শশী মাখিল বদনে মসি
কাল পেয়ে গ্রহণের ছলে ॥

*nadīyā-ākāśe āsi udila gaurāṅga-śaśī*
*bhāsila sakale kutūhale |*
*lājete gagana-śaśī mākhila badane masi*
*kāla peye grahaṇera chale ||*

*Word for word:* nadīyā-ākāśe — in the sky of Nadia; āsi — coming; udila — rose; gaurāṅga-śaśī — the moon Gauranga; bhāsila — floated (in joy); sakale — all; kutūhale — in delight; lājete — out of shame; gagana-śaśī — the moon of the sky; mākhila — smeared; badane — on its face; masi — soot; kāla peye — seizing the moment; grahaṇera chale — under pretext of an eclipse

**2.1.** In the sky of Nadia a moon has risen — Gauranga,
and all are drowned in delight;
and the moon of the sky, out of shame, has smeared its face with soot,
seizing the moment — as if in an eclipse.[^12-6]

বামাগণ উচ্চস্বরে জয় জয় ধ্বনি করে
ঘরে ঘরে বাজে ঘণ্টা শাঁখ ।
দামামা দগড় কাঁসি সানাই ভেঁউড় বাঁশী
তুড়ী ভেড়ী আর জয়ঢাক ॥

*bāmāgaṇa uccasvare jaya jaya dhvani kare*
*ghare ghare bāje ghaṇṭā śām̐kha |*
*dāmāmā dagaṛa kām̐si sānāi bhem̐uṛa bām̐śī*
*tuṛī bheṛī āra jayaḍhāka ||*

*Word for word:* bāmāgaṇa — the women; uccasvare — aloud; jaya jaya dhvani kare — raise the cry "jaya, jaya"; ghare ghare — in every house; bāje — sound; ghaṇṭā — bells; śām̐kha — conches; dāmāmā — kettledrums; dagaṛa — dagar drums; kām̐si — gongs; sānāi — shehnais; bhem̐uṛa — bheur horns; bām̐śī — flutes; tuṛī bheṛī — turi and bheri trumpets; āra — and; jayaḍhāka — the great victory drum

**2.2.** The women cry aloud: "Jaya, jaya!" —
in every house bells and conches sound;
kettledrums, drums, gongs, shehnais, horns and flutes,
turi and bheri trumpets and the great victory drum.[^12-7]

মিশ্র জগন্নাথ মন মহানন্দে নিমগন
শচীর সুখের সীমা নাই ।
দেখিয়া নিমাইর মুখ ভুলিলা প্রসব-দুখ
অনিমিখে পুত্র-মুখ চাই ॥

*miśra jagannātha mana mahānande nimagana*
*śacīra sukhera sīmā nāi |*
*dekhiyā nimāira mukha bhulilā prasaba-dukha*
*animikhe putra-mukha cāi ||*

*Word for word:* miśra jagannātha — Jagannatha Mishra; mana — (his) mind; mahānande — in great bliss; nimagana — immersed; śacīra — Shachi's; sukhera sīmā nāi — joy has no limit; dekhiyā — seeing; nimāira mukha — Nimai's face; bhulilā — she forgot; prasaba-dukha — the pains of childbirth; animikhe — unblinking; putra-mukha — at her son's face; cāi — gazing

**2.3.** Jagannatha Mishra is immersed in great bliss,
Shachi's joy knows no bounds:
seeing Nimai's face, she has forgotten the pains of childbirth
and, unblinking, gazes at her son's face.[^12-8]

গ্রহণের অন্ধকারে কেহ না চিনয়ে কারে
দেব-নরে হৈল মিশামিশি ।
নদীয়া-নাগরী সঙ্গে দেবনারী আসি রঙ্গে
হেরিছে গৌরাঙ্গ-রূপরাশি ॥

*grahaṇera andhakāre keha nā cinaye kāre*
*deba-nare haila miśāmiśi |*
*nadīyā-nāgarī saṅge debanārī āsi raṅge*
*heriche gaurāṅga-rūparāśi ||*

*Word for word:* grahaṇera andhakāre — in the darkness of the eclipse; keha nā cinaye kāre — no one recognizes anyone; deba-nare — gods and men; haila miśāmiśi — mingled; nadīyā-nāgarī saṅge — together with the townswomen of Nadia; debanārī — celestial women; āsi raṅge — coming joyfully; herichhe — behold; gaurāṅga-rūparāśi — the whole beauty of Gauranga

**2.4.** In the darkness of the eclipse no one recognizes anyone —
gods have mingled with men;
together with the women of Nadia, celestial women, coming joyfully,
behold the beauty of Gauranga.[^12-9]

পুত্রের বদন দেখি জগন্নাথ মহাসুখী
করে দান দরিদ্র সকলে ।
ভুবন আনন্দময় গৌরবিধু সমুদয়
বাসু কহে জীব-ভাগ্যফলে ॥

*putrera badana dekhi jagannātha mahāsukhī*
*kare dāna daridra sakale |*
*bhubana ānandamaya gaurabidhu samudaya*
*bāsu kahe jība-bhāgyaphale ||*

*Word for word:* putrera badana dekhi — seeing his son's face; jagannātha mahāsukhī — Jagannatha, overjoyed; kare dāna — gives gifts; daridra sakale — to all the poor; bhubana ānandamaya — the world is full of bliss; gaurabidhu samudaya — the rising of the moon Gaura; bāsu kahe — says Vasu; jība-bhāgyaphale — as the fruit of the good fortune of living beings

**2.5.** Gazing at his son's face, Jagannatha, overjoyed,
gives gifts to all the poor.
The world is full of bliss — the moon Gaura has risen:
this, says Vasu, is the fruit of the good fortune of living beings.

[^12-5]: GPT1 — p. 51, no. 3 (raga kalyana), checked against the scan (PDF pp. 310–311); GPT2 — sec. 2.1, no. 3. The pada is not in
PK, BR, KGC or PS. The preceding pada of GPT (no. 2, "jaya jaya kalaraba nadiyā nagare") is PK 1121, translated in chapter 7 (no. 6).
Majumdar regards Vasu's padas on the Lord's birth and childhood as the poet's invention: Vasu was not in Navadvipa at that
time (and the attribution of this pada is moreover known only from GPT). The Lord's appearance on the phalguna purnima
during a lunar eclipse, when everyone was chanting the name of Hari — CC Adi 13; CB Adi 2.
[^12-6]: A play of images: the moon Gauranga has eclipsed the moon of the sky, and it has hidden its face "out of shame" — this is
how the poet explains the eclipse on the night of the Lord's appearance.
[^12-7]: The shehnai (sānāi) is a wind instrument like an oboe; the bheur (bhem̐uṛa) is a horn; the turi and bheri are trumpets.
[^12-8]: The Lord's appearance is not the birth of a conditioned soul: He comes by His own will, in His eternal form, and Mother
Shachi, like Devaki and Yashoda, only in the sweetness of love experiences it as the birth of a son (CC Adi 13; Bhag. 10.3).
The words about "the pains of childbirth" convey her motherly experience in the humanlike lila.
[^12-9]: "The women of Nadia" (nadīyā-nāgarī) here are simply townswomen who came to see the Child, not "nagaris" in the sense of
nagari-bhava. The gods who came in human guise to see the newborn Lord — CB Adi 2.

## 3. Vasu Ghosha — "miśra purandara kichu mane bicāriyā…" (GPT1 p. 62, no. 1)
*The name-giving: Purandara Mishra calls the family priest and gives him gifts, and the priest places the arghya and his
blessing on the Child's head; Shachi asks that her son be given the name "Nimai". Raga suhai.*[^12-10]

মিশ্র পুরন্দর কিছু মনে বিচারিয়া ।
পুরোহিত দ্বিজবরে আনিলা ডাকিয়া ॥

*miśra purandara kichu mane bicāriyā |*
*purohita dvijabare ānilā ḍākiyā ||*

*Word for word:* miśra purandara — Purandara Mishra; kichu mane bicāriyā — having considered something in his mind; purohita dvijabare — the excellent brahmana, the family priest; ānilā ḍākiyā — called and brought

**3.1.** Purandara Mishra, having considered something,
called to him the family priest, the best of brahmanas.

ধন রত্ন অলঙ্কার দ্বিজবরে দিল ।
স্বস্তি-বচন বলি দান তুলি নিল ॥

*dhana ratna alaṅkāra dvijabare dila |*
*svasti-bacana bali dāna tuli nila ||*

*Word for word:* dhana ratna alaṅkāra — wealth, jewels, ornaments; dvijabare dila — he gave to the brahmana; svasti-bacana bali — pronouncing the blessing "svasti"; dāna tuli nila — (the brahmana) accepted the gift

**3.2.** Wealth, jewels and ornaments he gave to the brahmana;
the brahmana, pronouncing his blessing, accepted the gift.

অর্ঘ্য আশীষ দ্বিজ ধরি নিজ হাতে ।
সন্তোষে তুলিয়া দিল গোরাচাঁদের মাথে ॥

*arghya āśīṣa dvija dhari nija hāte |*
*santoṣe tuliyā dila gorācām̐dera māthe ||*

*Word for word:* arghya āśīṣa — the arghya and the blessing; dvija — the brahmana; dhari nija hāte — taking in his own hands; santoṣe — gladly; tuliyā dila — placed; gorācām̐dera māthe — on Gorachand's head

**3.3.** The arghya and the blessing the brahmana took in his own hands
and gladly placed them on Gorachand's head.[^12-11]

শচী ঠাকুরাণী কিছু কহিতে লাগিল ।
সাত পুত্রের এই পুত্র বিধি মোরে দিল ॥

*śacī ṭhākurāṇī kichu kahite lāgila |*
*sāta putrera ei putra bidhi more dila ||*

*Word for word:* śacī ṭhākurāṇī — Shachi Thakurani; kichu kahite lāgila — began to speak; sāta putrera ei putra — this son (worth) seven sons; bidhi more dila — Providence gave me

**3.4.** Shachi Thakurani began to speak:
"Providence has given me this son — He is to me as seven sons.[^12-12]

নিমাই বলিয়া নাম দেহ দ্বিজবর ।
বাসুদেব ঘোষ কহে জুড়ি দুই কর ॥

*nimāi baliyā nāma deha dvijabara |*
*bāsudeba ghoṣa kahe juṛi dui kara ||*

*Word for word:* nimāi baliyā — as "Nimai"; nāma deha — give the name; dvijabara — O best of brahmanas; bāsudeba ghoṣa kahe — says Vasudeva Ghosha; juṛi dui kara — joining both palms

**3.5.** Give Him the name 'Nimai', O best of brahmanas!" —
so, joining his palms, says Vasudeva Ghosha.

[^12-10]: GPT1 — p. 62, section "Childhood pastimes" (bālyalīlā), no. 1 (raga suhai), checked against the scan (PDF p. 321); GPT2 —
sec. 2.2, no. 1. The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS; it was missing from the catalogue (new entry VG-155). On Majumdar's view
of Vasu's padas on the Lord's childhood — note 5. Purandara is another name of Jagannatha Mishra. According to CB (Adi 3–4)
and CC (Adi 13–14), the name "Nimai" was given to the Child by the women (born under a nim tree — as a protection), while
at the name-giving ceremony the brahmanas named Him Vishvambhara; in the poem it is Shachi herself who asks for the name
"Nimai".
[^12-11]: Arghya — a respectful offering (water, rice, durva grass); here it is placed on the child's head as a blessing.
[^12-12]: "sāta putrera ei putra" — lit. "this son is (as) seven sons": an expression of the priceless worth of an only child. It may
also allude to the children Shachi lost before the Lord's appearance (according to CC Adi 13 — eight daughters).

## 4. Vasu Ghosha — "māyera aṅguli dhari śiśu gaurahari…" (GPT1 p. 63, no. 6)
*The first steps: holding His mother's finger, little Gaurahari toddles step by step, pulls her by the hand, stumbles and
falls; Shachi wants to take Him in her arms, but He, being stubborn, rolls on the ground; the mother wipes Him and kisses
Him. Raga beloar (tala dashakoshi).*[^12-13]

মায়ের অঙ্গুলি ধরি শিশু গৌরহরি ।
হাটি হাটি পায় পায় যায় গুড়ি গুড়ি ॥

*māyera aṅguli dhari śiśu gaurahari |*
*hāṭi hāṭi pāya pāya yāya guṛi guṛi ||*

*Word for word:* māyera aṅguli dhari — holding his mother's finger; śiśu gaurahari — the child Gaurahari; hāṭi hāṭi pāya pāya — step by step; yāya guṛi guṛi — goes toddling

**4.1.** Holding His mother's finger, the child Gaurahari
toddles forward step by step.

টানি লৈঞা মার হাত চলে ক্ষণে জোরে ।
পদ আধ যাইতে ঠেকাড় করি পড়ে ॥

*ṭāni laiñā māra hāta cale kṣaṇe jore |*
*pada ādha yāite ṭhekāṛa kari paṛe ||*

*Word for word:* ṭāni laiñā — pulling; māra hāta — his mother's hand; cale kṣaṇe jore — now walks fast; pada ādha yāite — going half a step; ṭhekāṛa kari paṛe — stumbles and falls

**4.2.** Pulling His mother by the hand, He suddenly walks faster —
and, before going half a step, stumbles and falls.

শচীমাতা কোলে লৈতে যায় ধূলি ঝারি ।
আখুটি করিয়া গোরা ভূমে দেয় গড়ি ॥

*śacīmātā kole laite yāya dhūli jhāri |*
*ākhuṭi kariyā gorā bhūme deya gaṛi ||*

*Word for word:* śacīmātā — mother Shachi; kole laite yāya — goes to take Him in her arms; dhūli jhāri — brushing off the dust; ākhuṭi kariyā — throwing a tantrum; gorā — Gora; bhūme deya gaṛi — rolls on the ground

**4.3.** Mother Shachi, brushing off the dust, goes to take Him in her arms —
but Gora, throwing a tantrum, rolls on the ground.

আহা আহা বলি মাতা মুছায় অঞ্চলে ।
কোলে করি চুমা দেয় বদন-কমলে ॥

*āhā āhā bali mātā muchāya añcale |*
*kole kari cumā deya badana-kamale ||*

*Word for word:* āhā āhā bali — saying "ah, ah"; mātā muchāya añcale — the mother wipes Him with the end of her sari; kole kari — taking Him in her arms; cumā deya — kisses; badana-kamale — the lotus face

**4.4.** Saying "ah, ah", the mother wipes Him with the end of her sari,
takes Him in her arms and kisses the lotus of His face.

বাসু কহে এ ছাবাল ধূলায় লোটাবা ।
স্নেহভরে তুমি মাগো কত ঠেকাইবা ॥

*bāsu kahe e chābāla dhūlāya loṭābā |*
*snehabhare tumi māgo kata ṭhekāibā ||*

*Word for word:* bāsu kahe — Vasu says; e chābāla — this child; dhūlāya loṭābā — will roll in the dust; snehabhare — in the fullness of affection; tumi māgo — you, mother; kata ṭhekāibā — how much will you hold Him back

**4.5.** Vasu says: this child will roll in the dust —
how long, mother, will you hold Him back out of tenderness?[^12-14]

[^12-13]: GPT1 — p. 63, no. 6 (raga beloar, tala dashakoshi), checked against the scan (PDF p. 322); GPT2 — sec. 2.2, no. 6. The pada
is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS; new catalogue entry VG-156. The neighbouring GPT padas (nos. 2–5) are PK 1141, 1161, 1150, 1151
(translated in chapter 7, nos. 8–11). On Majumdar's view — note 5.
[^12-14]: The Lord's childhood play in the dust — CB Adi 4; Murari 1.6. The sweetness of these pastimes lies in Shachi's motherly
love (vatsalya), which keeps her from seeing her Son's majesty.

## 5. Vasu Ghosha — "pūrṇimā-rajanī cām̐da gagane udaya…" (GPT1 pp. 63–64, no. 7)
*The moon from the sky: on the night of the full moon little Nimai, seeing the moon, cries: "Give me the moon, mother!";
the moon does not come, and in despair He falls in the dust; Shachi gives Him a picture of Radha and Krishna — and He is
happy: in it, says the poet, the Lord sees His own face. Raga beloar (tala dashakoshi).*[^12-15]

পূর্ণিমা-রজনী চাঁদ গগনে উদয় ।
চাঁদ হেরি গোরাচাঁদের হরিষ-হৃদয় ॥

*pūrṇimā-rajanī cām̐da gagane udaya |*
*cām̐da heri gorācām̐dera hariṣa-hṛdaya ||*

*Word for word:* pūrṇimā-rajanī — the night of the full moon; cām̐da — the moon; gagane udaya — rises in the sky; cām̐da heri — seeing the moon; gorācām̐dera — Gorachand's; hariṣa-hṛdaya — heart rejoices

**5.1.** On the night of the full moon the moon rose in the sky;
seeing the moon, Gorachand rejoiced in His heart.

চাঁদ দে মা বলি শিশু কাঁদে উভরায় ।
হাত তুলি শচী ডাকে আয় চাঁদ আয় ॥

*cām̐da de mā bali śiśu kām̐de ubharāya |*
*hāta tuli śacī ḍāke āya cām̐da āya ||*

*Word for word:* cām̐da de mā — "give me the moon, mother"; bali — saying; śiśu kām̐de ubharāya — the child cries aloud; hāta tuli — raising her hand; śacī ḍāke — Shachi calls; āya cām̐da āya — "come, moon, come"

**5.2.** "Give me the moon, mother!" — the child cries aloud;
raising her hand, Shachi calls: "Come, moon, come!"

না আসে নিঠুর চাঁদ নিমাই ব্যাকুল ।
কাঁদিয়া ধূলায় পড়ে হাতে ছিঁড়ে চুল ॥

*nā āse niṭhura cām̐da nimāi byākula |*
*kām̐diyā dhūlāya paṛe hāte chim̐ṛe cula ||*

*Word for word:* nā āse — does not come; niṭhura cām̐da — the cruel moon; nimāi byākula — Nimai is distraught; kām̐diyā — weeping; dhūlāya paṛe — falls in the dust; hāte chim̐ṛe cula — tears His hair with His hands

**5.3.** The cruel moon does not come — Nimai is distraught:
weeping, He falls in the dust and tears His hair.

রাধাকৃষ্ণ-চিত্র এক মিশ্র-গৃহে ছিল ।
পুত্র শান্তাইতে শচী তাহা হাতে দিল ॥

*rādhākṛṣṇa-citra eka miśra-gṛhe chila |*
*putra śāntāite śacī tāhā hāte dila ||*

*Word for word:* rādhākṛṣṇa-citra eka — a picture of Radha-Krishna; miśra-gṛhe chila — was in Mishra's house; putra śāntāite — to soothe her son; śacī tāhā hāte dila — Shachi gave it into His hands

**5.4.** In Mishra's house there was a picture of Radha and Krishna:
to soothe her son, Shachi gave it into His hands.

চিত্র পাঞা গোরাচাঁদের মনে বড় সুখ ।
বাসু কহে পটে পহুঁ হের নিজ-মুখ ॥

*citra pāñā gorācām̐dera mane baṛa sukha |*
*bāsu kahe paṭe pahum̐ hera nija-mukha ||*

*Word for word:* citra pāñā — getting the picture; gorācām̐dera mane — in Gorachand's heart; baṛa sukha — great joy; bāsu kahe — Vasu says; paṭe — in the picture; pahum̐ — O Lord; hera nija-mukha — behold Your own face

**5.5.** Getting the picture, Gorachand rejoiced with all His heart;
Vasu says: in the picture, Lord, You behold Your own face.[^12-16]

[^12-15]: GPT1 — pp. 63–64, no. 7 (raga beloar, tala dashakoshi), checked against the scan (PDF pp. 322–323); GPT2 — sec. 2.2, no. 7.
The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS; new catalogue entry VG-157. On Majumdar's view — note 5. The child asking for the moon is
a well-known motif of Krishna's childhood pastimes as well (cf. the story of the moon in a bowl of water).
[^12-16]: The sense of the signature: Gaura is Krishna Himself, who has taken the bhava and complexion of Radha (CC Adi 1.5; 4);
therefore in the picture of Radha and Krishna He sees Himself: in the Child's play the poet reveals the secret of Gaura — Radha and Krishna in one form (cf. the
verse of Svarupa Damodara, CC Adi 1.5).

## 6. Vasu Ghosha — "uṭha uṭha gorācām̐da niśi pohāila…" (GPT1 p. 347, no. 11)
*The awakening of Gaura: the night is over, Nadia has woken, the cuckoo is calling, the dawn has risen, the lotuses have
opened — how long will You sleep, Gora, in the languor of prema? Raga dhanashi.*[^12-17]

উঠ উঠ গোরাচাঁদ নিশি পোহাইল ।
নদীয়ার লোক সব জাগিয়া উঠিল ॥

*uṭha uṭha gorācām̐da niśi pohāila |*
*nadīyāra loka saba jāgiyā uṭhila ||*

*Word for word:* uṭha uṭha — rise, rise; gorācām̐da — Gorachand; niśi pohāila — the night is over; nadīyāra loka saba — all the people of Nadia; jāgiyā uṭhila — have woken and risen

**6.1.** Rise, rise, Gorachand — the night is over;
all the people of Nadia have woken and risen.

কোকিলার কুহু-রব সুললিত ধ্বনি ।
কত নিদ্রা যাও ওহে গোরা গুণমণি ॥

*kokilāra kuhu-raba sulalita dhvani |*
*kata nidrā yāo ohe gorā guṇamaṇi ||*

*Word for word:* kokilāra kuhu-raba — the cuckoo's "kuhu"; sulalita dhvani — a charming sound; kata nidrā yāo — how long You sleep; ohe gorā — O Gora; guṇamaṇi — jewel of virtues

**6.2.** The cuckoo calls "kuhu" — how charming its voice;
how long will You sleep, O Gora, jewel of virtues?

অরুণ উদয় ভেল কমল প্রকাশ ।
শশধর তেজল কুমুদিনী-বাস ॥

*aruṇa udaya bhela kamala prakāśa |*
*śaśadhara tejala kumudinī-bāsa ||*

*Word for word:* aruṇa udaya bhela — the dawn has risen; kamala prakāśa — the lotuses have opened; śaśadhara tejala — the moon has left; kumudinī-bāsa — the abode of the night lilies

**6.3.** The dawn has risen, the lotuses have opened;
the moon has left the abode of the night lilies.[^12-18]

বাসুদেব ঘোষ কহে মনের হরিষে ।
কত নিদ্রা যাও গোরা প্রেমের অলসে ॥

*bāsudeba ghoṣa kahe manera hariṣe |*
*kata nidrā yāo gorā premera alase ||*

*Word for word:* bāsudeba ghoṣa kahe — Vasudeva Ghosha says; manera hariṣe — with joy in his heart; kata nidrā yāo — how long You sleep; gorā — Gora; premera alase — in the languor of prema

**6.4.** Vasudeva Ghosha, with joy in his heart, says:
how long will You sleep, Gora, in the languor of prema?

[^12-17]: GPT1 — p. 347, section "the eight periods of the day" (ashtakaliya), no. 11 (raga dhanashi); GPT2 — sec. 5.2, no. 11. The
pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS. Ashtakaliya songs are a meditation on the Lord's daily pastimes hour by hour; Majumdar
does not discuss such padas.
[^12-18]: The night lilies (kumudini) open under the moon and close at dawn; the lotuses do the opposite.

## 7. Vasu Ghosha — "bāyasa kokilakula ghughu dahiyāla-raba…" (GPT1 p. 351, no. 24)
*Morning and bath: the birds call, the companions call Gora; He rises, rubs His eyes, performs the morning duties, slowly
anoints Himself with fragrant oil and goes with everyone to the Ganga. Raga dhanashi.*[^12-19]

বায়স কোকিলকুল ঘুঘু দহিয়াল-রব ।
তা সহ মিলিয়া ডাকে পরিকর সব ॥

*bāyasa kokilakula ghughu dahiyāla-raba |*
*tā saha miliyā ḍāke parikara saba ||*

*Word for word:* bāyasa — crows; kokilakula — cuckoos; ghughu — doves; dahiyāla-raba — the calls of magpie-robins; tā saha miliyā — together with them; ḍāke — call; parikara saba — all the companions

**7.1.** Crows, cuckoos, doves and magpie-robins are calling,
and together with them all the companions call Him.

অলস তেজিয়া গোরা উঠে শেজ হৈতে ।
আঁখি কচালিয়া হাতে চায় চারি ভিতে ॥

*alasa tejiyā gorā uṭhe śeja haite |*
*ām̐khi kacāliyā hāte cāya cāri bhite ||*

*Word for word:* alasa tejiyā — casting off drowsiness; gorā uṭhe — Gora rises; śeja haite — from the bed; ām̐khi kacāliyā hāte — rubbing His eyes with His hands; cāya cāri bhite — looks all around

**7.2.** Casting off drowsiness, Gora rises from His bed,
rubs His eyes with His hands and looks all around.

পরিকর সহ গোরা প্রাতঃকৃত্য সারি ।
অঙ্গেতে সুগন্ধি তৈল মাখে ধীরি ধীরি ॥

*parikara saha gorā prātaḥkṛtya sāri |*
*aṅgete sugandhi taila mākhe dhīri dhīri ||*

*Word for word:* parikara saha — with the companions; gorā — Gora; prātaḥkṛtya sāri — finishing the morning duties; aṅgete — on His body; sugandhi taila — fragrant oil; mākhe dhīri dhīri — slowly rubs

**7.3.** Having finished the morning duties with His companions,
Gora slowly anoints His body with fragrant oil.

তৈল মাখি যায় সবে গঙ্গা-অভিমুখে ।
বাসুঘোষ স্নানলীলা গায় মনসুখে ॥

*taila mākhi yāya sabe gaṅgā-abhimukhe |*
*bāsughoṣa snānalīlā gāya manasukhe ||*

*Word for word:* taila mākhi — anointed with oil; yāya sabe — all go; gaṅgā-abhimukhe — toward the Ganga; bāsughoṣa — Vasu Ghosha; snānalīlā — the lila of bathing; gāya manasukhe — sings with a happy heart

**7.4.** Anointed with oil, they all go toward the Ganga;
Vasu Ghosha joyfully sings the lila of bathing.

[^12-19]: GPT1 — p. 351, section ashtakaliya, no. 24 (raga dhanashi); GPT2 — sec. 5.2, no. 24. The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS.
The next GPT pada (no. 25, "jalakeli gorācām̐dera manete paṛila", the water play) is PK 1108, translated in chapter 5 (no. 7). The
dahiyal (dahiyāla) is the magpie-robin (Copsychus saularis), a songbird of Bengal.

## 8. Vasu Ghosha — "jhulata gorācām̐da sundara raṅgiyā…" (GPT1 p. 326, no. 17)
*Jhulana: Gorachand swings on the swing, overflowing with prema; in the bhava of Radha tears stream down His face;
understanding His bhava, Gadadhara swings at His left; "The flute!" Gora exclaims, gazing into his face. Raga
dhanashi.*[^12-20]

ঝুলত গোরাচাঁদ সুন্দর রঙ্গিয়া ।
প্রেমভরে হৈয়া ডগমগিয়া ॥

*jhulata gorācām̐da sundara raṅgiyā |*
*premabhare haiyā ḍagamagiyā ||*

*Word for word:* jhulata — swings; gorācām̐da — Gorachand; sundara raṅgiyā — beautiful and joyous; premabhare — in the fullness of prema; haiyā ḍagamagiyā — overflowing

**8.1.** Gorachand swings, beautiful and joyous,
overflowing with the fullness of prema.

রাধার ভাবেতে ধারা বয়ানেতে ভাসে ।
ভাব বুঝি গদাধর ঝুলে বাম পাশে ॥

*rādhāra bhābete dhārā bayānete bhāse |*
*bhāba bujhi gadādhara jhule bāma pāśe ||*

*Word for word:* rādhāra bhābete — in the bhava of Radha; dhārā — streams (of tears); bayānete bhāse — flood His face; bhāba bujhi — understanding the bhava; gadādhara — Gadadhara; jhule bāma pāśe — swings at the left side

**8.2.** In the bhava of Radha streams of tears flood His face;
understanding His bhava, Gadadhara swings at His left.[^12-21]

মুরলী বলিয়া চাহে বদন হেরিয়া ।
বাসু ঘোষ গায় গোরাগুণ সোঙরিয়া ॥

*muralī baliyā cāhe badana heriyā |*
*bāsu ghoṣa gāya gorāguṇa soṅariyā ||*

*Word for word:* muralī baliyā — saying "the flute!"; cāhe — looks; badana heriyā — gazing at the face; bāsu ghoṣa gāya — Vasu Ghosha sings; gorāguṇa soṅariyā — remembering Gora's qualities

**8.3.** "The flute!" He exclaims, gazing into Gadadhara's face;
Vasu Ghosha sings, remembering Gora's qualities.

[^12-20]: GPT1 — p. 326, section "festivals of the year", no. 17 (raga dhanashi), checked against the scan (PDF p. 585); GPT2 —
sec. 5.1, no. 17. The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS. Vasu's other pada on the jhulana (PK 1550, where Gaura sits on the
swing with Gadadhara; according to Majumdar, an eyewitness testimony) is translated in chapter 4 (no. 5). Jhulana is the
swing festival of Radha and Krishna in the month of shravana.
[^12-21]: The bhava of Radha is pure prema, Radha's love for Krishna; in it the Lord tastes the sweetness of His own love (CC Adi 4).
The left side is Radha's place beside Krishna; Gadadhara, the Lord's eternal companion, understands His mood. The cry "The
flute!" is a remembrance of Krishna's flute that has seized the Lord in this bhava.

## 9. Vasu Ghosha — "biṣṇupriyā saṅginīre pāiyā birale…" (GPT1 p. 367, no. 4)
*Vishnupriya's foreboding: alone with a friend, she says that Nadia seems desolate to her today, the right side of her
body twitches, her earring has fallen, on the bank of the Suradhuni the trees have wilted, the current has stopped, the cuckoo
is silent; the poet fears that Gora may leave Navadvipa. Raga dhanashi.*[^12-22]

বিষ্ণুপ্রিয়া সঙ্গিনীরে পাইয়া বিরলে ।
ব্যাকুল হিয়ায় গদ গদ কিছু বলে ॥

*biṣṇupriyā saṅginīre pāiyā birale |*
*byākula hiyāya gada gada kichu bale ||*

*Word for word:* biṣṇupriyā — Vishnupriya; saṅginīre — her companion; pāiyā birale — finding alone; byākula hiyāya — with an anxious heart; gada gada — faltering; kichu bale — says something

**9.1.** Vishnupriya, finding her friend alone,
with an anxious heart, faltering, says:

আজি কেন নদীয়া উদাস লাগে মোরে ।
অঙ্গে নাহি পাই সুখ দুটী আঁখি ঝুরে ॥

*āji kena nadīyā udāsa lāge more |*
*aṅge nāhi pāi sukha duṭī ām̐khi jhure ||*

*Word for word:* āji kena — why today; nadīyā — Nadia; udāsa lāge more — seems desolate to me; aṅge nāhi pāi sukha — I find no ease in my body; duṭī ām̐khi jhure — both eyes weep

**9.2.** "Why does Nadia seem desolate to me today?
There is no ease in my body, both my eyes weep.

নাচিছে দক্ষিণ অঙ্গ দক্ষিণ-নয়ন ।
খসিয়া পড়িল মোর কর্ণের ভূষণ ॥

*nāciche dakṣiṇa aṅga dakṣiṇa-nayana |*
*khasiyā paṛila mora karṇera bhūṣaṇa ||*

*Word for word:* nāchiche — twitches; dakṣiṇa aṅga — the right side of the body; dakṣiṇa-nayana — the right eye; khasiyā paṛila — slipped and fell; mora karṇera bhūṣaṇa — my ear ornament

**9.3.** The right side of my body twitches, my right eye;
my earring has slipped and fallen.[^12-23]

সুরধুনী-পুলিনে মলিন তরুলতা ।
ভ্রমর না খায় মধু শুকাইল পাতা ॥

*suradhunī-puline malina tarulatā |*
*bhramara nā khāya madhu śukāila pātā ||*

*Word for word:* suradhunī-puline — on the bank of the Suradhuni (the Ganga); malina — wilted; tarulatā — the trees and creepers; bhramara — the bees; nā khāya madhu — do not drink honey; śukāila pātā — the leaves have withered

**9.4.** On the bank of the Suradhuni the trees and creepers have wilted,
the bees do not drink honey, the leaves have withered.

স্থগিত হইল কেন জাহ্নবীর ধারা ।
কোকিলের রব নাহি হৈল মূক পারা ॥

*sthagita haila kena jāhnabīra dhārā |*
*kokilera raba nāhi haila mūka pārā ||*

*Word for word:* sthagita haila kena — why has it stopped; jāhnabīra dhārā — the current of the Jahnavi; kokilera raba nāhi — there is no cuckoo's call; haila mūka pārā — it has become as if mute

**9.5.** Why has the current of the Jahnavi stopped?
The cuckoo is not heard — as if it had grown mute."

এই বড় ভয় লাগে বাসুর হিয়া মাঝে ।
নবদ্বীপ ছাড়ে পাছে গোরা দ্বিজরাজে ॥

*ei baṛa bhaya lāge bāsura hiyā mājhe |*
*nabadvīpa chāṛe pāche gorā dvijarāje ||*

*Word for word:* ei baṛa bhaya lāge — this great fear arises; bāsura hiyā mājhe — in Vasu's heart; nabadvīpa chāṛe — leaves Navadvipa; pāche — lest; gorā dvijarāje — Gora, the king of brahmanas

**9.6.** A great fear has settled in Vasu's heart:
lest Gora, the king of brahmanas, leave Navadvipa!

(including this one and the next) are missing from it. The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS; new catalogue entry VG-158. The

## 10. Vasu Ghosha — "pāgalinī biṣṇupriyā bhijā bastra cule…" (GPT1 p. 367, no. 6)
*Vishnupriya, as if distraught, runs home in wet clothes and, weeping, tells Shachi of the ill omens: while she was
bathing her nose ring fell into the water, her right eye twitches, she keeps seeing a snake on her right; the poet: today
the lord of your life will leave Navadvipa. Raga dhanashi.*[^12-24]

পাগলিনী বিষ্ণুপ্রিয়া ভিজা বস্ত্র চুলে ।
ত্বরা করি বাড়ী আসি শাশুড়ীরে বলে ॥

*pāgalinī biṣṇupriyā bhijā bastra cule |*
*tvarā kari bāṛī āsi śāśuṛīre bale ||*

*Word for word:* pāgalinī — like one distraught; biṣṇupriyā — Vishnupriya; bhijā bastra cule — with wet clothes and hair; tvarā kari — hurriedly; bāṛī āsi — coming home; śāśuṛīre bale — says to her mother-in-law

**10.1.** Vishnupriya, as if distraught, with wet clothes and wet hair,
hurriedly comes home and speaks to her mother-in-law —

বলিতে না পারে কিছু কাঁদিয়া ফাঁফর ।
শচী বোলে মাগো এত কি লাগি কাতর ॥

*balite nā pāre kichu kām̐diyā phām̐phara |*
*śacī bole māgo eta ki lāgi kātara ||*

*Word for word:* balite nā pāre kichu — cannot say anything; kām̐diyā phām̐phara — breathless with weeping; śacī bole — Shachi says; māgo — my dear; eta ki lāgi kātara — why are you so distressed

**10.2.** but she cannot say anything, breathless with weeping.
Shachi says: "My dear, why are you so distressed?"

বিষ্ণুপ্রিয়া বলে আর কি কব জননি ।
চারিদিকে অমঙ্গল কাঁপিছে পরাণি ॥

*biṣṇupriyā bale āra ki kaba janani |*
*cāridike amaṅgala kām̐piche parāṇi ||*

*Word for word:* biṣṇupriyā bale — Vishnupriya says; āra ki kaba — what more shall I say; janani — mother; cāridike — on all sides; amaṅgala — ill omens; kām̐piche parāṇi — my soul trembles

**10.3.** Vishnupriya says: "What more can I say, mother?
On all sides there are ill omens — my soul trembles.

নাহিতে পড়িল জলে নাকের বেশর ।
ভাঙ্গিবে কপাল মাথে পড়িবে বজর ॥

*nāhite paṛila jale nākera beśara |*
*bhāṅgibe kapāla māthe paṛibe bajara ||*

*Word for word:* nāhite — while bathing; paṛila jale — fell into the water; nākera beśara — my nose ring; bhāṅgibe kapāla — my fortune will break; māthe paṛibe bajara — a thunderbolt will fall on my head

**10.4.** As I was bathing, my nose ring fell into the water:
my fortune will break, a thunderbolt will fall on my head.[^12-25]

থাকি থাকি প্রাণ কাঁদে নাচে ডানি আঁখি ।
দক্ষিণে ভুজঙ্গ যেন রহি রহি দেখি ॥

*thāki thāki prāṇa kām̐de nāce ḍāni ām̐khi |*
*dakṣiṇe bhujaṅga yena rahi rahi dekhi ||*

*Word for word:* thāki thāki — again and again; prāṇa kām̐de — my soul weeps; nāce ḍāni ām̐khi — my right eye twitches; dakṣiṇe — on the right; bhujaṅga — a snake; yena — as if; rahi rahi dekhi — I keep seeing

**10.5.** Again and again my soul weeps, my right eye twitches,
on my right I keep seeing as if a snake."

কাঁদি কহে বাসুঘোষ কি কহিব সতি ।
আজি নবদ্বীপ ছাড়ি যাবে প্রাণপতি ॥

*kām̐di kahe bāsughoṣa ki kahiba sati |*
*āji nabadvīpa chāṛi yābe prāṇapati ||*

*Word for word:* kām̐di kahe bāsughoṣa — weeping, Vasu Ghosha says; ki kahiba — what shall I say; sati — O faithful wife; āji — today; nabadvīpa chāṛi — leaving Navadvipa; yābe prāṇapati — the lord of your life will go

**10.6.** Weeping, Vasu Ghosha says: "What shall I say, O faithful wife?
Today the lord of your life will leave Navadvipa."

not in PK, BR, KGC or PS; new catalogue entry VG-159. The night before the Lord's departure and Vishnupriya's grief — CC Adi 17;

[^12-25]: The nose ring (beśara) is a sign of a married woman; its loss is an ill omen for the husband.

## 11. Vasu Ghosha — "prabhu kahe nijaguṇe deota sannyāsa…" (GPT1 p. 369, no. 11)
*Katwa: the Lord asks Keshava Bharati to give Him sannyasa; the people of Katwa try to dissuade Him, Bharati recalls
that the scriptures allow sannyasa after fifty; the Lord replies: if death comes earlier, when will there be the company
of saints? Bharati agrees, the barber is called; he does not dare touch the Lord's head — the Lord tells him to give up
his trade and promises him a happy life by Krishna's grace. Raga shri.*[^12-26]

প্রভু কহে নিজগুণে দেওত সন্ন্যাস ।
হৈয় না সন্ন্যাসী নিমাই না মুড়াও কেশ ॥

*prabhu kahe nijaguṇe deota sannyāsa |*
*haiya nā sannyāsī nimāi nā muṛāo keśa ||*

*Word for word:* prabhu kahe — the Lord says; nijaguṇe — by your own grace; deota sannyāsa — give sannyasa; haiya nā sannyāsī — do not become a sannyasi; nimāi — Nimai; nā muṛāo keśa — do not shave Your hair

**11.1.** The Lord says: "By your grace give Me sannyasa!"
— "Do not become a sannyasi, Nimai, do not shave Your hair!" —

কাঞ্চন-নগরের লোক সব মানা করে ।
সন্ন্যাস না কর বাছা ফিরা যাও ঘরে ॥

*kāñcana-nagarera loka saba mānā kare |*
*sannyāsa nā kara bāchā phirā yāo ghare ||*

*Word for word:* kāñcana-nagarera loka saba — all the people of Kanchana-nagara; mānā kare — dissuade; sannyāsa nā kara — do not take sannyasa; bāchā — dear child; phirā yāo ghare — go back home

**11.2.** so all the people of Kanchana-nagara try to dissuade Him:
"Do not take sannyasa, dear child, go back home!"[^12-27]

পঞ্চাশের ঊর্দ্ধ হৈলে রাগের নিবৃত্তি ।
তবে ত সন্ন্যাস দিতে শাস্ত্রে অনুমতি ॥

*pañcāśera ūrddha haile rāgera nibṛtti |*
*tabe ta sannyāsa dite śāstre anumati ||*

*Word for word:* pañcāśera ūrddha haile — when one is past fifty; rāgera nibṛtti — the cessation of passion; tabe ta — only then; sannyāsa dite — to give sannyasa; śāstre anumati — the scriptures permit

**11.3.** "When one is past fifty and the passions have ceased,
only then do the scriptures allow sannyasa to be given."[^12-28]

এ বোল শুনিয়া প্রভু বলে এই বাণী ।
তোমার সাক্ষাতে গুরু কি বলিতে জানি ॥

*e bola śuniyā prabhu bale ei bāṇī |*
*tomāra sākṣāte guru ki balite jāni ||*

*Word for word:* e bola śuniyā — hearing these words; prabhu bale ei bāṇī — the Lord speaks thus; tomāra sākṣāte — before you; guru — O guru; ki balite jāni — what do I know to say

**11.4.** Hearing this, the Lord speaks thus:
"What do I know to say before you, O guru?

পঞ্চাশ হইতে যদি হয়ত মরণ ।
তবে আর সাধু-সঙ্গ হইবে কখন ॥

*pañcāśa haite yadi hayata maraṇa |*
*tabe āra sādhu-saṅga haibe kakhana ||*

*Word for word:* pañcāśa haite — before fifty; yadi hayata maraṇa — if death should come; tabe āra — then; sādhu-saṅga — the company of saints; haibe kakhana — when will it be

**11.5.** If death should come before fifty,
when then will there be the company of saints?"

এ বোল শুনিয়া কহে ভারতী গোসাঞি ।
সন্ন্যাস দিব রে তোরে শুন রে নিমাই ॥

*e bola śuniyā kahe bhāratī gosāñi |*
*sannyāsa diba re tore śuna re nimāi ||*

*Word for word:* e bola śuniyā — hearing this; kahe bhāratī gosāñi — Bharati Gosani says; sannyāsa diba re tore — I will give you sannyasa; śuna re nimāi — listen, Nimai

**11.6.** Hearing this, Bharati Gosani says:
"I will give You sannyasa — listen, Nimai!"

এ কথা শুনিয়া প্রভুর আনন্দ উল্লাস ।
নাপিত ডাকাইল তবে মুড়াইতে কেশ ॥

*e kathā śuniyā prabhura ānanda ullāsa |*
*nāpita ḍākāila tabe muṛāite keśa ||*

*Word for word:* e kathā śuniyā — hearing this; prabhura ānanda ullāsa — the Lord's joy and delight; nāpita ḍākāila — they called the barber; tabe — then; muṛāite keśa — to shave the hair

**11.7.** Hearing this, the Lord was filled with joy and delight;
then they called the barber to shave His head.

নাপিত বলয়ে প্রভো করি নিবেদন ।
এরূপ মনুষ্য নাহি এ তিন ভুবন ॥

*nāpita balaye prabho kari nibedana |*
*erūpa manuṣya nāhi e tina bhubana ||*

*Word for word:* nāpita balaye — the barber says; prabho — O Lord; kari nibedana — I humbly submit; erūpa manuṣya nāhi — there is no such person; e tina bhubana — in the three worlds

**11.8.** The barber says: "Master, I humbly submit:
there is no such person in the three worlds!

তব শিরে হাত দিয়া ছোঁব কার পায় ।
যে বোল সে বোল প্রভো কাঁপে মোর কায় ॥

*taba śire hāta diyā chom̐ba kāra pāya |*
*ye bola se bola prabho kām̐pe mora kāya ||*

*Word for word:* taba śire — on Your head; hāta diyā — having put my hand; chom̐ba kāra pāya — whose feet shall I touch; ye bola se bola — say what you will; prabho — O Lord; kām̐pe mora kāya — my body trembles

**11.9.** Having touched Your head with my hand, whose feet shall I touch then?
Say what you will, Master — my whole body trembles.

কার পায় হাত দিয়া কামাইব নিতি ।
অধম নাপিত জাতি মোর এই রীতি ॥

*kāra pāya hāta diyā kāmāiba niti |*
*adhama nāpita jāti mora ei rīti ||*

*Word for word:* kāra pāya hāta diyā — touching whose feet; kāmāiba niti — shall I shave every day; adhama nāpita jāti — the low barber caste; mora ei rīti — this is my custom

**11.10.** Touching whose feet shall I now shave every day?
I am a barber of low caste — such is my custom."[^12-29]

এ বোল শুনিয়া কহে বিশ্বম্ভর রায় ।
না করিও নিজবৃত্তি ঠাকুর কহয় ॥

*e bola śuniyā kahe biśvambhara rāya |*
*nā kario nijabṛtti ṭhākura kahaya ||*

*Word for word:* e bola śuniyā — hearing this; kahe biśvambhara rāya — Vishvambhara Raya says; nā kario nijabṛtti — do not follow your trade; ṭhākura kahaya — the Lord says

**11.11.** Hearing this, Vishvambhara Raya speaks,
the Lord says: "Do not follow your trade any longer.

কৃষ্ণের প্রসাদে জন্ম গোয়াইবা সুখে ।
অন্তকালেতে গতি হবে বিষ্ণুলোকে ॥

*kṛṣṇera prasāde janma goyāibā sukhe |*
*antakālete gati habe biṣṇuloke ||*

*Word for word:* kṛṣṇera prasāde — by Krishna's grace; janma goāibā sukhe — you will pass your life happily; antakālete — at the end; gati habe — your destination will be; biṣṇuloke — the abode of Vishnu

**11.12.** By Krishna's grace you will pass your life in happiness,
and at the end your way will lead to the abode of Vishnu."

কাঞ্চন-নগরের লোক সদয় হৃদয় ।
বাসুঘোষ জোড় হাতে ভারতীরে কয় ॥

*kāñcana-nagarera loka sadaya hṛdaya |*
*bāsughoṣa joṛa hāte bhāratīre kaya ||*

*Word for word:* kāñcana-nagarera loka — the people of Kanchana-nagara; sadaya hṛdaya — are kind-hearted; bāsughoṣa — Vasu Ghosha; joṛa hāte — with joined palms; bhāratīre kaya — speaks to Bharati

**11.13.** The people of Kanchana-nagara are kind-hearted;
Vasu Ghosha, with joined palms, speaks to Bharati…

[^12-26]: GPT1 — p. 369, section "sannyasa", no. 11 (raga shri), checked against the scan (PDF p. 628); GPT2 — p. 236, sec. 5.3, no. 11
(scan PDF p. 525). The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS; new catalogue entry VG-160. The preceding GPT pada (no. 10, "kāñcana nagare
eka bṛkṣa manohara", with the double signature of Krishnadasa and Vasu) is PK 2223 (VG-136), translated in chapter 4 (no. 12). The sannyasa at
Katwa — CB Madhya 28; CC Adi 17, Madhya 3; Lochana, Madhya-khanda; Murari 2.18. Keshava Bharati is the Lord's sannyasa-guru.
[^12-27]: Kanchana-nagara is Katwa (Kantaka-nagara) on the Ganga, where the Lord took sannyasa.
[^12-28]: Apparently the words of Keshava Bharati (GPT1 gives them in quotation marks without naming the speaker): sannyasa was usually
taken in old age, after the stages of grihastha and vanaprastha. The Lord's answer (11.4–11.5) is the word of a man seeking sannyasa: the Lord, who teaches by His own
example, speaks of the brevity of human life, not of Himself — time has no power over Him.
[^12-29]: The barber's trade is shaving and paring nails, touching people's feet; having touched the Lord's head, he can no longer
touch the feet of others (the same motif in Lochana, where the barber is called Haridasa (in the 1983 ed.), and in Govinda's *Karcha*, where he is
Deva).

## 12. Vasu Ghosha — "madhuśīla bale gosāñi nā bhām̐ṛāo more…" (GPT1 p. 369, no. 12)
*Continuation: the barber Madhushil says to the Lord: "Do not deceive me — I know You are God Himself; I shall do Your
will, but first place Your feet on my head"; the Lord places His foot on his head. Raga shri.*[^12-30]

মধুশীল বলে গোসাঞি না ভাঁড়াও মোরে ।
তুমি ব্রহ্মা তুমি বিষ্ণু জানিনু অন্তরে ॥

*madhuśīla bale gosāñi nā bhām̐ṛāo more |*
*tumi brahmā tumi biṣṇu jāninu antare ||*

*Word for word:* madhuśīla bale — Madhushil says; gosāñi — O Gosani; nā bhām̐ṛāo more — do not deceive me; tumi brahmā tumi biṣṇu — You are Brahma, You are Vishnu; jāninu antare — I know it in my heart

**12.1.** Madhushil says: "Gosani, do not deceive me:
You are Brahma, You are Vishnu — I know it in my heart.[^12-31]

পূরাব তোমার ইচ্ছা তুমি ইচ্ছাময় ।
পালিব তোমার আজ্ঞা নাহিক সংশয় ॥

*pūrāba tomāra icchā tumi icchāmaya |*
*pāliba tomāra ājñā nāhika saṃśaya ||*

*Word for word:* pūrāba tomāra icchā — I shall fulfil Your wish; tumi icchāmaya — You are all-willing; pāliba tomāra ājñā — I shall obey Your order; nāhika saṃśaya — without doubt

**12.2.** I shall fulfil Your wish — You are all-powerful;
I shall obey Your order without doubt.

বলিতেছ কৃষ্ণের প্রসাদে রব সুখে ।
মরণের পরে গতি হবে বিষ্ণুলোকে ॥

*balitecha kṛṣṇera prasāde raba sukhe |*
*maraṇera pare gati habe biṣṇuloke ||*

*Word for word:* balitecha — You say; kṛṣṇera prasāde — by Krishna's grace; raba sukhe — I shall live happily; maraṇera pare — after death; gati habe biṣṇuloke — I shall go to the abode of Vishnu

**12.3.** You say: by Krishna's grace I shall live happily,
and after death my way will lead to the abode of Vishnu.

যে কৃষ্ণ রাখিবে সুখে সেই কৃষ্ণ তুমি ।
তব পদ বিষ্ণুলোক কিবা জানি আমি ॥

*ye kṛṣṇa rākhibe sukhe sei kṛṣṇa tumi |*
*taba pada biṣṇuloka kibā jāni āmi ||*

*Word for word:* ye kṛṣṇa — the Krishna who; rākhibe sukhe — will keep me happy; sei kṛṣṇa tumi — that Krishna is You; taba pada — Your feet; biṣṇuloka — the abode of Vishnu; kibā jāni āmi — what else do I know

**12.4.** The Krishna who will keep me in happiness — that is You;
Your feet are my abode of Vishnu: what else do I know?

মুড়াব চাঁচর কেশ হাত দিব মাথে ।
কিন্তু প্রভু শ্রীচরণ দেও আগে মাথে ॥

*muṛāba cām̐cara keśa hāta diba māthe |*
*kintu prabhu śrīcaraṇa deo āge māthe ||*

*Word for word:* muṛāba — I shall shave; cām̐cara keśa — the curly hair; hāta diba māthe — I shall put my hand on Your head; kintu prabhu — but, Lord; śrīcaraṇa deo — place Your holy feet; āge māthe — first on my head

**12.5.** I shall shave Your curly hair, I shall touch Your head with my hand —
but first, Lord, place Your holy feet on my head."

মধুর বচনে প্রভু দিলা শিরে পদ ।
বাসু কহে যার কাছে তুচ্ছ ব্রহ্মপদ ॥

*madhura bacane prabhu dilā śire pada |*
*bāsu kahe yāra kāche tuccha brahmapada ||*

*Word for word:* madhura bacane — at the sweet words; prabhu dilā śire pada — the Lord placed His foot on his head; bāsu kahe — Vasu says; yāra kāche — before which; tuccha brahmapada — the post of Brahma is trifling

**12.6.** At these sweet words the Lord placed His foot on his head —
the foot, says Vasu, before which the post of Brahma is trifling.

[^12-30]: GPT1 — p. 369, no. 12 (raga shri), checked against the scan (PDF p. 628); GPT2 — p. 236, sec. 5.3, no. 12. The pada is not in
PK, BR, KGC or PS; new catalogue entry VG-161. The barber's name is Madhushil (madhuśīla; Shil is a surname of the barber caste).
[^12-31]: "You are Brahma, You are Vishnu" — the simple words of a barber who has recognized God in the Lord; according to Gaudiya
teaching Gaura is Krishna Himself, the Supreme Lord, the source of both Vishnu and Brahma (CC Adi 2) — which the barber himself
says in 12.4: "that Krishna is You".

## 13. Vasu Ghosha — "prabhura muṇḍana dekhi kānde yata paśu pākhī…" (GPT1 p. 370, no. 15)
*After the shaving: beasts, birds and people weep, a cow runs to the Lord with grass in her teeth, all stand silent like
trees; the Lord, in kaupina and with staff, asks the Vaishnavas to bless Him so that His sannyasa may not become a mockery
and He may attain the Lord of Vraja in Vraja, and runs crying "Where is Vrindavana?" through the land of Rarh, with
Nityananda beside Him. Raga pahida.*[^12-32]

প্রভুর মুণ্ডন দেখি কান্দে যত পশু পাখী
আর কান্দে যত শ্রীনিবাসী ।
বৎস নাহি দুগ্ধ খায় তৃণ দন্তে গাভী ধায়
নেহালে গৌরাঙ্গ-মুখ আসি ॥

*prabhura muṇḍana dekhi kānde yata paśu pākhī*
*āra kānde yata śrīnibāsī |*
*batsa nāhi dugdha khāya tṛṇa dante gābhī dhāya*
*nehāle gaurāṅga-mukha āsi ||*

*Word for word:* prabhura muṇḍana dekhi — seeing the Lord shaven; kānde yata paśu pākhī — all the beasts and birds weep; āra kānde — and weep; yata śrīnibāsī — all the dwellers (of the holy place); batsa nāhi dugdha khāya — the calf does not drink milk; tṛṇa dante — with grass in its teeth; gābhī dhāya — the cow runs; nehāle — gazes; gaurāṅga-mukha āsi — coming, at Gauranga's face

**13.1.** Seeing the Lord shaven, all the beasts and birds weep,
all the dwellers of the holy place weep;[^12-33]
the calf does not drink milk, the cow, with grass in her teeth,
runs and gazes at Gauranga's face.

আছে লোক দাঁড়াইয়া গৌরাঙ্গ-মুখ চাহিয়া
কারো মুখে নাহি সরে বাণী ।
দু-নয়নে জল সরে গৌরাঙ্গের মুখ হেরে
বৃক্ষবৎ হৈল সব প্রাণী ॥

*āche loka dām̐ṛāiyā gaurāṅga-mukha cāhiyā*
*kāro mukhe nāhi sare bāṇī |*
*du-nayane jala sare gaurāṅgera mukha here*
*bṛkṣabat haila saba prāṇī ||*

*Word for word:* āche loka dām̐ṛāiyā — people stand; gaurāṅga-mukha cāhiyā — looking at Gauranga's face; kāro mukhe — from no one's mouth; nāhi sare bāṇī — comes a word; du-nayane jala sare — tears flow from both eyes; gaurāṅgera mukha here — they gaze at Gauranga's face; bṛkṣabat haila — have become like trees; saba prāṇī — all beings

**13.2.** People stand looking at Gauranga's face —
no one can utter a word;
tears flow from both eyes as they gaze at Gauranga's face —
all beings have become still as trees.

ডোর কৌপীন পরি মস্তকে মুণ্ডন ডুরি
মায়া ছাড়ি হৈল উদাসীন ।
বৈসে ডগমগি হৈয়া করেতে দণ্ড লইয়া
প্রভু কহে আমি দীন হীন ॥

*ḍora kaupīna pari mastake muṇḍana ḍuri*
*māyā chāṛi haila udāsīna |*
*baise ḍagamagi haiyā karete daṇḍa laiyā*
*prabhu kahe āmi dīna hīna ||*

*Word for word:* ḍora kaupīna pari — putting on the cord and kaupina; mastake muṇḍana — with shaven head; ḍuri — (meaning unclear); māyā chāṛi — leaving maya (worldly ties); haila udāsīna — became detached; baise ḍagamagi haiyā — sits, overflowing (with prema); karete daṇḍa laiyā — taking the staff in His hand; prabhu kahe — the Lord says; āmi dīna hīna — I am poor and lowly

**13.3.** Putting on the cord and kaupina, with shaven head,
leaving maya, He has become detached;[^12-34]
He sits, overflowing with prema, taking the staff in His hand,
and says: "I am poor and lowly.

তোমরা বৈষ্ণববর এই আশীর্বাদ কর
দুই হাত দিয়া মোর মাথে ।
করিলাম সন্ন্যাস নহে যেন উপহাস
ব্রজে গেলে পাই ব্রজনাথে ॥

*tomarā baiṣṇababara ei āśīrvāda kara*
*dui hāta diyā mora māthe |*
*karilāma sannyāsa nahe yena upahāsa*
*braje gele pāi brajanāthe ||*

*Word for word:* tomarā baiṣṇababara — you, the best of Vaishnavas; ei āśīrvāda kara — bless (Me) thus; dui hāta diyā mora māthe — placing both hands on My head; karilāma sannyāsa — I have taken sannyasa; nahe yena upahāsa — may it not become a mockery; braje gele — going to Vraja; pāi brajanāthe — may I attain the Lord of Vraja

**13.4.** You, the best of Vaishnavas, give Me this blessing,
placing both hands on My head:
I have taken sannyasa — may it not become a mockery;
may I, going to Vraja, attain the Lord of Vraja!"[^12-35]

এত বলি গোরা রায় প্রেমে ঊর্দ্ধমুখে ধায়
কোথা বৃন্দাবন বলি কাঁদে ।
ভ্রমে প্রভু রাঢ় দেশে নিত্যানন্দ তান পাশে
বাসু ঘোষ উচ্চস্বরে কাঁদে ॥

*eta bali gorā rāya preme ūrddhamukhe dhāya*
*kothā bṛndābana bali kām̐de |*
*bhrame prabhu rāṛha deśe nityānanda tāna pāśe*
*bāsu ghoṣa uccasvare kām̐de ||*

*Word for word:* eta bali — saying this; gorā rāya — Gora Raya; preme — in prema; ūrddhamukhe dhāya — runs with face upturned; kothā bṛndābana — "where is Vrindavana?"; bali kām̐de — saying, weeps; bhrame prabhu — the Lord wanders; rāṛha deśe — in the land of Rarh; nityānanda tāna pāśe — Nityananda beside Him; bāsu ghoṣa — Vasu Ghosha; uccasvare kām̐de — weeps aloud

**13.5.** Saying this, Gora Raya runs in prema with His face upturned
and weeps: "Where is Vrindavana?"
The Lord wanders through the land of Rarh, Nityananda beside Him;
Vasu Ghosha weeps aloud.[^12-36]

[^12-32]: GPT1 — pp. 370–371, section "sannyasa", no. 15 (raga pahida), checked against the scan (PDF p. 629); GPT2 — sec. 5.3, no. 15.
The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS. The couplet about the blessing (13.4) coincides almost word for word with Vasu's pada PK 2225
(VG-059; chapter 4, no. 13), which Majumdar considers part of the historical cycle "Nimai-sannyasa": this is a "double" of that
pada, known only from GPT.
[^12-33]: śrīnibāsī — lit. "dwellers of Shri (the holy place)"; the sense of the word is unclear (perhaps the people of Katwa or of
Nadia).
[^12-34]: "Leaving maya" — here "maya" in the everyday sense: family, home, worldly attachments that the Lord leaves on taking
sannyasa; the Lord Himself is never under the power of maya. The word "ḍuri" after "shaven head" is unclear (omitted in the
translation).
[^12-35]: The Lord, taking the role of a devotee, prays for a blessing — to attain Krishna; cf. CC Madhya 3 (the verse of the Avanti
brahmana, which the Lord recites on taking sannyasa).
[^12-36]: After the sannyasa the Lord wandered for three days in a trance through the land of Rarh, seeking Vrindavana, and Nityananda
led Him to the Ganga and to Shantipura — CC Madhya 3; CB Antya 1.

## 14. Vasu Ghosha — "gaurāṅge sannyāsa diyā bhāratī kām̐dilā…" (GPT1 p. 371, no. 18)
*Having given Gauranga sannyasa and the name Sri Krishna Chaitanya, Keshava Bharati weeps; the Lord asks him for the
blessing of love for Krishna, and Bharati replies: "You are my guru, I see Krishna in You; only for the sake of worldly
custom do You call me guru." Raga dhanashi.*[^12-37]

গৌরাঙ্গে সন্ন্যাস দিয়া ভারতী কাঁদিলা ।
শ্রীকৃষ্ণচৈতন্য নাম নিমাইয়েরে দিলা ॥

*gaurāṅge sannyāsa diyā bhāratī kām̐dilā |*
*śrīkṛṣṇacaitanya nāma nimāiyere dilā ||*

*Word for word:* gaurāṅge sannyāsa diyā — having given sannyasa to Gauranga; bhāratī kām̐dilā — Bharati wept; śrīkṛṣṇacaitanya nāma — the name Sri Krishna Chaitanya; nimāiyere dilā — he gave to Nimai

**14.1.** Having given Gauranga sannyasa, Bharati wept;
the name "Sri Krishna Chaitanya" he gave to Nimai.

প্রভু কহে গুরু মোর পূরাহ মন-সাধ ।
কৃষ্ণে মতি হউক এই দেও আশীর্বাদ ॥

*prabhu kahe guru mora pūrāha mana-sādha |*
*kṛṣṇe mati hauka ei deo āśīrvāda ||*

*Word for word:* prabhu kahe — the Lord says; guru mora — O My guru; pūrāha mana-sādha — fulfil My heart's desire; kṛṣṇe mati hauka — may My mind be in Krishna; ei deo āśīrvāda — give this blessing

**14.2.** The Lord says: "My guru, fulfil the desire of My heart:
bless Me, that My mind may be in Krishna."

ভারতী কাঁদিয়া বোলে মোর গুরু তুমি ।
আশীর্বাদ কি করিব কৃষ্ণ দেখি আমি ॥

*bhāratī kām̐diyā bole mora guru tumi |*
*āśīrvāda ki kariba kṛṣṇa dekhi āmi ||*

*Word for word:* bhāratī kām̐diyā bole — Bharati, weeping, says; mora guru tumi — You are my guru; āśīrvāda ki kariba — what blessing shall I give; kṛṣṇa dekhi āmi — I see Krishna

**14.3.** Bharati, weeping, says: "You are my guru;
what blessing shall I give? I see Krishna.

ভুবন ভুলাও তুমি সব নাটের গুরু ।
রাখিতে লৌকিক মান মোরে কহ গুরু ॥

*bhubana bhulāo tumi saba nāṭera guru |*
*rākhite laukika māna more kaha guru ||*

*Word for word:* bhubana bhulāo tumi — You bewilder the world; saba nāṭera guru — the master of every play; rākhite laukika māna — to keep up worldly custom; more kaha guru — You call me guru

**14.4.** You bewilder the whole world, You are the master of every play;
only to keep up worldly custom do You call me guru.[^12-38]

আমার সন্ন্যাস আজি হইল সফল ।
বাসু কহে দেখিলাম চরণ-কমল ॥

*āmāra sannyāsa āji haila saphala |*
*bāsu kahe dekhilāma caraṇa-kamala ||*

*Word for word:* āmāra sannyāsa — my sannyasa; āji haila saphala — today has borne fruit; bāsu kahe — Vasu says; dekhilāma caraṇa-kamala — I have seen the lotus feet

**14.5.** My sannyasa has today borne fruit!"
Vasu says: "I have seen the lotus feet."

[^12-37]: GPT1 — p. 371, no. 18 (raga dhanashi); GPT2 — sec. 5.3, no. 18. The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS; new catalogue entry
VG-162. The name "Sri Krishna Chaitanya" — CC Madhya 3, CB Madhya 28; cf. Govinda's *Karcha*, where Bharati inwardly recognizes the Lord as God.
[^12-38]: "You bewilder the world" (bhubana bhulāo) — of the lila of the Lord, who hides His majesty in the role of a devotee and a disciple;
"the master of every play" (nāṭera guru) — He Himself arranges His lila. This is not "maya" over the Lord: by His own will He shows
the form of a sannyasi in order to teach the world.

## 15. Vasu Ghosha — "svapane giyāchilum̐ kṣīroda-sāyare…" (PK 2269; GPT1 no. 25)
*Shachi's lament: in a dream she went to the ocean of milk, but even there did not find the treasure of virtues; she set up
a market, but fate did not let her trade; where did Keshava Bharati in sannyasi garb come from? She raised her son to be a
pandit — who has taken Him away to a distant land? Shachi calls: "Nimai, come!" Raga pahida.*[^12-39]

স্বপনে গিয়াছিলুঁ ক্ষীরোদ-সায়রে
তথা না পাইলুঁ গুণ-নিধি ।
পাতিয়া হাট খানি বেসাইতে না দিলে
বিবাদে লাগিল বিধি ॥

*svapane giyāchilum̐ kṣīroda-sāyare*
*tathā nā pāilum̐ guṇa-nidhi |*
*pātiyā hāṭa khāni besāite nā dile*
*bibāde lāgila bidhi ||*

*Word for word:* svapane giyāchilum̐ — in a dream I went; kṣīroda-sāyare — to the ocean of milk; tathā nā pāilum̐ — there I did not find; guṇa-nidhi — the treasure of virtues; pātiyā hāṭa khāni — having set up the market; besāite nā dile — (fate) did not let me trade; bibāde lāgila bidhi — Providence turned hostile

**15.1.** "In a dream I went to the ocean of milk —
and even there I did not find the treasure of virtues;
I set up a market — but I was not let to trade:
Providence has turned against me.[^12-40]

কোথা হৈতে আইল কেশব ভারতী
ধরিয়া সন্ন্যাসি-বেশ ।
পড়ায়্যা শুনায়্যা পণ্ডিত করিলুঁ
কেবা লৈয়া গেল দূরদেশ ॥

*kothā haite āila keśaba bhāratī*
*dhariyā sannyāsi-beśa |*
*paṛāyyā śunāyyā paṇḍita karilum̐*
*kebā laiyā gela dūradeśa ||*

*Word for word:* kothā haite āila — from where came; keśaba bhāratī — Keshava Bharati; dhariyā sannyāsi-beśa — wearing the sannyasi's garb; paṛāyyā śunāyyā — teaching and instructing; paṇḍita karilum̐ — I made (him) a pandit; kebā laiyā gela — who has taken (him) away; dūradeśa — to a distant land

**15.2.** From where did this Keshava Bharati come
in the garb of a sannyasi?
I taught Him, instructed Him, raised Him a pandit —
who, then, has taken Him away to a distant land?"

শচী মায় ডাকে নিমাই আয় রে ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*śacī māya ḍāke nimāi āya re || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* śacī māya ḍāke — mother Shachi calls; nimāi āya re — "Nimai, come!"

**15.3.** *(Refrain)* Mother Shachi calls: "Nimai, come!"

শূন্য ঘরেতে যাদুধন ।
বাসু ঘোষ কহে ঐ গোরাচাঁদ মায়ের জীবন ॥

*śūnya gharete yādudhana |*
*bāsu ghoṣa kahe ai gorācām̐da māyera jībana ||*

*Word for word:* śūnya gharete — to the empty house; yādudhana — my treasure; bāsu ghoṣa kahe — Vasu Ghosha says; ai gorācām̐da — that Gorachand; māyera jībana — is the mother's life

**15.4.** "My treasure, (come back) to the empty house!"
Vasu Ghosha says: "That Gorachand is the mother's life."[^12-41]

[^12-39]: PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 293 (printed p. 282), 21st pallava "The sannyasa of Sri Gauranga etc.", no. 52 (mark "॥৫২॥২২৬৯॥"), MS P-R-Sa
no. 2373 — **without a signature**, with the refrain "śacī māya ḍāke nimāi āya re"; in MS P-R-Sa the refrain is longer: "…what has he
plotted with Bharati — he goes away, killing his mother." GPT1 — p. 374, no. 25 (raga pahida), checked against the scan (PDF
p. 633); GPT2 — sec. 5.3, no. 25: with a closing line and Vasu's signature (15.4). Text of 15.1–15.3 follows PK, 15.4 follows GPT.
The attribution to Vasu is known only from GPT.
[^12-40]: The ocean of milk (Kshiroda) is the abode of Vishnu; Shachi seeks her son where the Lord dwells. The "market" is an image of a
settled life, of family (cf. no. 1: the market of Gaura's prema).
[^12-41]: Shachi's lament in the spirit of vatsalya: motherly love, in which there is no room for thoughts of the Son's majesty, is
lofty prema (CC Adi 4).

## 16. Vasu Ghosha — "nadīyā chāṛiyā gela gaurāṅga sundare…" (GPT1 p. 374, no. 27)
*Gauranga has left Nadia, and the devotees sink in an ocean of grief: Advaita, Srivasa, Gadadhara, Vasudeva Datta, Murari,
Vakreshvara, Vasudeva and Narahari weep, Raghunandana rolls in the dust, Haridasa weeps with closed eyes, Nityananda —
looking at Shachi; the poet remembers the blissful kirtanas of Nadia. Raga suhai (tala somtal).*[^12-42]

নদীয়া ছাড়িয়া গেল গৌরাঙ্গ সুন্দরে ।
ডুবল ভকত সব শোকের সাগরে ॥

*nadīyā chāṛiyā gela gaurāṅga sundare |*
*ḍubala bhakata saba śokera sāgare ||*

*Word for word:* nadīyā chāṛiyā gela — has left Nadia and gone; gaurāṅga sundare — beautiful Gauranga; ḍubala bhakata saba — all the devotees have sunk; śokera sāgare — in the ocean of grief

**16.1.** Beautiful Gauranga has left Nadia —
all the devotees have sunk in an ocean of grief.

কাঁদিছে অদ্বৈতাচার্য শ্রীবাস গদাধর ।
বাসুদেব দত্ত কাঁদে মুরারি বক্রেশ্বর ॥

*kām̐diche advaitācārya śrībāsa gadādhara |*
*bāsudeba datta kām̐de murāri bakreśvara ||*

*Word for word:* kām̐diche — weep; advaitācārya — Advaita Acharya; śrībāsa — Srivasa; gadādhara — Gadadhara; bāsudeba datta kām̐de — Vasudeva Datta weeps; murāri — Murari; bakreśvara — Vakreshvara

**16.2.** Advaita Acharya, Srivasa and Gadadhara weep;
Vasudeva Datta, Murari and Vakreshvara weep.

বাসুদেব নরহরি কাঁদে উচ্চ রায় ।
শ্রীরঘুনন্দন কাঁদি ধূলায় লোটায় ॥

*bāsudeba narahari kām̐de ucca rāya |*
*śrīraghunandana kām̐di dhūlāya loṭāya ||*

*Word for word:* bāsudeba narahari — Vasudeva and Narahari; kām̐de ucca rāya — weep aloud; śrīraghunandana — Sri Raghunandana; kām̐di — weeping; dhūlāya loṭāya — rolls in the dust

**16.3.** Vasudeva and Narahari weep aloud;
Sri Raghunandana, weeping, rolls in the dust.[^12-43]

কাঁদিছেন হরিদাস দু-আঁখি মুদিয়া ।
কাঁদে নিত্যানন্দ শচীর মুখ নিরখিয়া ॥

*kām̐dichena haridāsa du-ām̐khi mudiyā |*
*kām̐de nityānanda śacīra mukha nirakhiyā ||*

*Word for word:* kām̐dichena haridāsa — Haridasa weeps; du-ām̐khi mudiyā — closing both eyes; kām̐de nityānanda — Nityananda weeps; śacīra mukha nirakhiyā — looking at Shachi's face

**16.4.** Haridasa weeps, closing both eyes;
Nityananda weeps, looking at Shachi's face.

সুখময় কীর্তন করিত নদীয়ায় ।
সোঙরি সে সব বাসুর হিয়া ফাটি যায় ॥

*sukhamaya kīrtana karita nadīyāya |*
*soṅari se saba bāsura hiyā phāṭi yāya ||*

*Word for word:* sukhamaya kīrtana — the blissful kirtana; karita nadīyāya — (He) used to hold in Nadia; soṅari se saba — remembering all that; bāsura hiyā — Vasu's heart; phāṭi yāya — breaks

**16.5.** Blissful kirtanas He used to hold in Nadia —
remembering all that, Vasu's heart breaks.

[^12-42]: GPT1 — p. 374, no. 27 (raga suhai, tala somtal), checked against the scan (PDF p. 633); GPT2 — sec. 5.3, no. 27. The pada is not
in PK, BR, KGC or PS. The lament of Navadvipa after the Lord's departure — CB Antya 1; CC Madhya 3. The poet gathers all the companions
into one picture of grief, without regard to where each was (Nityananda, for instance, was with the Lord at Katwa).
[^12-43]: "Vasudeva" is apparently the poet himself (Vasudeva Ghosha), beside Narahari Sarakara of Shrikhanda; Raghunandana is Narahari's
nephew, then still a child.

## 17. Vasu Ghosha — "śuniyā māyera bāṇī kahe prabhu guṇamaṇi…" (GPT1 pp. 379–380, no. 44)
*Shantipura: hearing His mother's lament, the Lord consoles her: birth after birth she is His mother and He her child; so it
was with Dhruva's mother, with Kaushalya, and with Yashoda when Krishna went to Mathura; let her worship Krishna; when she
weeps and calls, He will come. Shachi is silent in tears; the poet begs the Lord to return to Nadia. Raga pahida.*[^12-44]

শুনিয়া মায়ের বাণী কহে প্রভু গুণমণি
শুন মাতা আমার বচন ।
জন্মে জন্মে মাতা তুমি তোমার বালক আমি
এই সব বিধির লিখন ॥

*śuniyā māyera bāṇī kahe prabhu guṇamaṇi*
*śuna mātā āmāra bacana |*
*janme janme mātā tumi tomāra bālaka āmi*
*ei saba bidhira likhana ||*

*Word for word:* śuniyā māyera bāṇī — hearing His mother's words; kahe prabhu guṇamaṇi — the Lord, jewel of virtues, says; śuna mātā — listen, mother; āmāra bacana — to My words; janme janme — birth after birth; mātā tumi — you are (My) mother; tomāra bālaka āmi — I am your child; ei saba — all this; bidhira likhana — is the writing of destiny

**17.1.** Hearing His mother's words, the Lord, the jewel of virtues, says:
"Listen, mother, to My words:
birth after birth you are My mother and I am your child;
all this is written by Providence.

ধ্রুবের জননী ছিল পুত্রকে বৈরাগ্য দিল
ভজে তেঁই দেব চক্রপাণি ।
রঘুনাথ ছাড়ি ভোগে বনে বনে ফিরে লোকে
ঝুরে সদা কৌশল্যা জননী ॥

*dhrubera jananī chila putrake bairāgya dila*
*bhaje tem̐i deba cakrapāṇi |*
*raghunātha chāṛi bhoge bane bane phire loke*
*jhure sadā kauśalyā jananī ||*

*Word for word:* dhrubera jananī chila — there was Dhruva's mother; putrake bairāgya dila — she gave her son detachment; bhaje tem̐i — therefore he worships; deba cakrapāṇi — the Lord who holds the disc; raghunātha — Raghunatha (Rama); chāṛi bhoge — leaving enjoyments; bane bane phire — wanders from forest to forest; loke — (so) people (say); jhure sadā — ever weeps; kauśalyā jananī — mother Kaushalya

**17.2.** There was Dhruva's mother — she gave her son detachment,
and therefore he worships the Lord who holds the disc;
Raghunatha, leaving all pleasures, wanders from forest to forest —
and mother Kaushalya, they say, ever weeps.[^12-45]

তবে শেষে দ্বাপরে কৃষ্ণ গেলা মধুপুরে
ঘরে নন্দরাণী নন্দ পিতা ।
সর্ব্ব পরে এই হয়ে এ কথা অন্যথা নহে
মিথ্যা শোক কর শচী মাতা ॥

*tabe śeṣe dvāpare kṛṣṇa gelā madhupure*
*ghare nandarāṇī nanda pitā |*
*sarvva pare ei haye e kathā anyathā nahe*
*mithyā śoka kara śacī mātā ||*

*Word for word:* tabe śeṣe — then at last; dvāpare — in Dvapara; kṛṣṇa gelā madhupure — Krishna went to Mathura; ghare — at home (remained); nandarāṇī — Nanda's queen (Yashoda); nanda pitā — father Nanda; sarvva pare — with everyone; ei haye — so it happens; e kathā anyathā nahe — this is not otherwise; mithyā śoka kara — you grieve in vain; śacī mātā — mother Shachi

**17.3.** And then, in Dvapara, Krishna went to Mathura,
and Nanda's queen and father Nanda remained at home.
So it is with everyone, it is not otherwise:
in vain you grieve, Mother Shachi.

বিধাতা-নির্বন্ধ যাহা কেবা খণ্ডাইবে তাহা
এত জানি স্থির কর মন ।
ভজ কৃষ্ণ কর সার আর নাহি সংসার
পাইয়া পরম পদধন ॥

*bidhātā-nirvandha yāhā kebā khaṇḍāibe tāhā*
*eta jāni sthira kara mana |*
*bhaja kṛṣṇa kara sāra āra nāhi saṃsāra*
*pāiyā parama padadhana ||*

*Word for word:* bidhātā-nirvandha yāhā — what is ordained by the Creator; kebā khaṇḍāibe tāhā — who will undo it; eta jāni — knowing this; sthira kara mana — steady your heart; bhaja kṛṣṇa — worship Krishna; kara sāra — make (it) the essence; āra nāhi saṃsāra — there is no more samsara; pāiyā — attaining; parama padadhana — the treasure of the supreme abode

**17.4.** Who will undo what the Creator has ordained?
Knowing this, steady your heart.
Worship Krishna, make this the essence of life —
and there is no more samsara: you will attain the treasure of the supreme abode.

রোদন করিলে তুমি ডাকিলে আসিব আমি
এই দেহ তোমার পালিত ।
আশীর্বাদ কর মোরে যাই নীলাচলপুরে
তুমি চিত্তে কর সন্নিহিত ॥

*rodana karile tumi ḍākile āsiba āmi*
*ei deha tomāra pālita |*
*āśīrvāda kara more yāi nīlācalapure*
*tumi citte kara sannihita ||*

*Word for word:* rodana karile tumi — when you weep; ḍākile — call; āsiba āmi — I shall come; ei deha — this body; tomāra pālita — was nurtured by you; āśīrvāda kara more — bless Me; yāi nīlācalapure — I go to Nilachala; tumi citte — you, in your heart; kara sannihita — keep (Me) near

**17.5.** When you weep and call Me — I shall come:
this body was nurtured by you.
Bless Me — I am going to Nilachala;
keep Me near in your heart."[^12-46]

প্রভু-স্তুতি-বাণী কহে শচী নির্ব্বাচনে রহে
পড়ে জল নয়ন বহিয়া ।
বাসু কহে গৌরহরি এই নিবেদন করি
পুনরপি চলহ নদীয়া ॥

*prabhu-stuti-bāṇī kahe śacī nirvvācane rahe*
*paṛe jala nayana bahiyā |*
*bāsu kahe gaurahari ei nibedana kari*
*punarapi calaha nadīyā ||*

*Word for word:* prabhu-stuti-bāṇī kahe — the Lord speaks words of comfort; śacī nirvvācane rahe — Shachi remains speechless; paṛe jala — tears fall; nayana bahiyā — flowing from her eyes; bāsu kahe — Vasu says; gaurahari — O Gaurahari; ei nibedana kari — thus I pray; punarapi calaha nadīyā — go back to Nadia again

**17.6.** The Lord speaks words of comfort, and Shachi remains silent,
and tears flow from her eyes.
Vasu says: "Gaurahari, thus I pray:
go back to Nadia again!"

[^12-44]: GPT1 — pp. 379–380, section "sannyasa", no. 44 (raga pahida), checked against the scan (PDF pp. 638–639); GPT2 — sec. 5.3,
no. 44 (only the first line is recognized in the OCR). The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS; new catalogue entry VG-163. The pada
answers Shachi's lament in the preceding GPT pada (no. 43, "nitāi kariyā āge…") — this is PK 2233 with the signature of Vallabha
Dasa (in GPT — Vasu; according to Jagadbandhu's note, other collections have a different signature). The meeting with Shachi in
Shantipura and the Lord's answer, "I shall always come when you call" — CC Madhya 3; CB Antya 1. "Birth after birth you are My mother" — of the eternal relationship: Shachi is the Lord's eternal mother (in Krishna's lila — Yashoda; CC Adi 13).
[^12-45]: Suniti, Dhruva's mother, instructed her son to seek refuge in the Lord (Bhag. 4.8); Kaushalya is the mother of Rama
(Raghunatha), who went into exile in the forest.
[^12-46]: According to CC Madhya 3, Shachi herself asks her son to live in Puri so that she may have news of Him; the Lord promises to come
at her call (and, according to CC, comes to eat her offerings).

## 18. Vasu Ghosha — "nānāna prakāre prabhu māyere sāntvāya…" (GPT1 p. 380, no. 45)
*Shantipura: the Lord consoles His mother, Sita, Advaita's wife, reasons with Shachi; in Advaita's courtyard there is kirtana,
Gaura dances embracing Nitai, Advaita follows with outstretched arms lest the Lord fall; Shantipura has become like Navadvipa;
Shachi is outwardly sad, but in her heart she is blissful; for ten days the Lord stays with Advaita. Raga dhanashi.*[^12-47]

নানান প্রকারে প্রভু মায়েরে সান্ত্বায় ।
অদ্বৈত-ঘরণী সীতা শচীরে বুঝায় ॥

*nānāna prakāre prabhu māyere sāntvāya |*
*advaita-gharaṇī sītā śacīre bujhāya ||*

*Word for word:* nānāna prakāre — in many ways; prabhu māyere sāntvāya — the Lord consoles His mother; advaita-gharaṇī sītā — Sita, Advaita's wife; śacīre bujhāya — reasons with Shachi

**18.1.** In many ways the Lord consoles His mother;
Sita, Advaita's wife, reasons with Shachi.

শচীর সহিত যত নদীয়ার লোক ।
সুদৃষ্টি মেলিয়া প্রভু জুড়াইল শোক ॥

*śacīra sahita yata nadīyāra loka |*
*sudṛṣṭi meliyā prabhu juṛāila śoka ||*

*Word for word:* śacīra sahita — together with Shachi; yata nadīyāra loka — all the people of Nadia; sudṛṣṭi meliyā — casting a gracious glance; prabhu juṛāila śoka — the Lord soothed the grief

**18.2.** Shachi and all the people of Nadia
the Lord comforted with His gracious glance.

শান্তিপুর ভরিয়া উঠিল হরিধ্বনি ।
অদ্বৈতের আঙ্গিনায় নাচে গৌরমণি ॥

*śāntipura bhariyā uṭhila haridhvani |*
*advaitera āṅgināya nāce gauramaṇi ||*

*Word for word:* śāntipura bhariyā — filling Shantipura; uṭhila haridhvani — rose the cry of "Hari"; advaitera āṅgināya — in Advaita's courtyard; nāce gauramaṇi — the jewel Gaura dances

**18.3.** Over Shantipura rose the cry of "Hari!" —
in Advaita's courtyard the jewel Gaura dances.

প্রেমে টলমল করে স্থির নহে চিত ।
নিতাই ধরিয়া কাঁদে নিমাই পণ্ডিত ॥

*preme ṭalamala kare sthira nahe cita |*
*nitāi dhariyā kām̐de nimāi paṇḍita ||*

*Word for word:* preme ṭalamala kare — reels in prema; sthira nahe cita — the heart is not still; nitāi dhariyā — holding Nitai; kām̐de nimāi paṇḍita — Nimai Pandita weeps

**18.4.** He reels in prema, His heart knows no rest;
embracing Nitai, Nimai Pandita weeps.

অদ্বৈত পসারি বাহু ফিরে পাছে পাছে ।
আছাড় খাইয়া গোরা ভূমে পড়ে পাছে ॥

*advaita pasāri bāhu phire pāche pāche |*
*āchāṛa khāiyā gorā bhūme paṛe pāche ||*

*Word for word:* advaita pasāri bāhu — Advaita, with outstretched arms; phire pāche pāche — follows behind; āchāṛa khāiyā — crashing down; gorā bhūme paṛe — Gora falls to the ground; pāche — lest

**18.5.** Advaita, with outstretched arms, follows behind Him,
lest Gora crash down to the ground.

চৌদিকে ভকতগণ বোলে হরি হরি ।
শান্তিপুর হৈল যেন নবদ্বীপ পুরী ॥

*caudike bhakatagaṇa bole hari hari |*
*śāntipura haila yena nabadvīpa purī ||*

*Word for word:* caudike — on all sides; bhakatagaṇa bole hari hari — the devotees cry "Hari, Hari"; śāntipura haila — Shantipura became; yena nabadvīpa purī — like the city of Navadvipa

**18.6.** On all sides the devotees cry "Hari, Hari!" —
Shantipura has become like the city of Navadvipa.

প্রভু-সঙ্গে কোটিচন্দ্র দেখিয়ে আভাস ।
এ ডোর কৌপীন তাহে প্রেমের প্রকাশ ॥

*prabhu-saṅge koṭicandra dekhiye ābhāsa |*
*e ḍora kaupīna tāhe premera prakāśa ||*

*Word for word:* prabhu-saṅge — about the Lord; koṭicandra — (the radiance of) millions of moons; dekhiye ābhāsa — a glow is seen; e ḍora kaupīna — this cord and kaupina; tāhe — in them; premera prakāśa — prema is manifest

হেন রূপ প্রেমাবেশ দেখি শচী মায় ।

*hena rūpa premābeśa dekhi śacī māya |*
*bāhire duḥkhita kintu ānanda hiyāya ||*

*Word for word:* hena rūpa — such a form; premābeśa — the ecstasy of prema; dekhi śacī māya — seeing, mother Shachi; bāhire duḥkhita — is outwardly sorrowful; kintu ānanda hiyāya — but in her heart is bliss

is outwardly sorrowful, but in her heart is bliss.

বুঝায় শচীর মন অবধূত রায় ।

*bujhāya śacīra mana abadhūta rāya |*
*saṃkīrtana samāpiyā prabhure basāya ||*

*Word for word:* bujhāya śacīra mana — calms Shachi's heart; abadhūta rāya — the Avadhuta (Nityananda); saṃkīrtana samāpiyā — ending the sankirtana; prabhure basāya — seats the Lord

**18.9.** The Avadhuta calms Shachi's heart;
ending the sankirtana, He seats the Lord.[^12-48]

এইরূপ দশ দিন অদ্বৈতের ঘরে ।
ভোজন-বিলাসে প্রভু আনন্দ অন্তরে ॥

*eirūpa daśa dina advaitera ghare |*
*bhojana-bilāse prabhu ānanda antare ||*

*Word for word:* eirūpa — thus; daśa dina — ten days; advaitera ghare — in Advaita's house; bhojana-bilāse — in the delights of the meals; prabhu ānanda antare — the Lord is blissful at heart

the Lord, blissful at heart, enjoys the meals.

বাসুদেব ঘোষ কয় চরণে ধরিয়া ।

*Word for word:* bāsudeba ghoṣa kaya — Vasudeva Ghosha says; caraṇe dhariyā — clasping the feet; advaitera ei āśā — this hope of Advaita; nā diba chāṛiyā — I will not let go

**18.11.** Vasudeva Ghosha says, clasping His feet:
"This hope of Advaita I will not let go!"[^12-49]

## 19. Vasu Ghosha — "prabhu karuṇa-svare bhakata prabodha kare…" (GPT1 pp. 380–381, no. 47)
*The farewell in Shantipura: the Lord, weeping, with joined palms, begs the devotees not to withdraw their mercy from Him: He has
left Navadvipa, Shachi and Vishnupriya and with their consent wishes to live in Nilachala — people travelling between
Nilachala and Nadia will bring news of Him; embracing Advaita and taking the dust of Shachi's feet, He departs, and Shantipura is
filled with weeping. Raga shri-gandhara.*[^12-50]

প্রভু করুণ-স্বরে ভকত প্রবোধ করে
কহে কথা কান্দিতে কান্দিতে ।
দুটী হাত জোড় করি নিবেদয়ে গৌরহরি
সবে দয়া না ছাড়িহ চিতে ॥

*prabhu karuṇa-svare bhakata prabodha kare*
*kahe kathā kāndite kāndite |*
*duṭī hāta joṛa kari nibedaye gaurahari*
*sabe dayā nā chāṛiha cite ||*

*Word for word:* prabhu karuṇa-svare — the Lord in a plaintive voice; bhakata prabodha kare — consoles the devotees; kahe kathā — speaks words; kāndite kāndite — weeping and weeping; duṭī hāta joṛa kari — joining both palms; nibedaye gaurahari — Gaurahari entreats; sabe — all of you; dayā nā chāṛiha cite — do not abandon mercy in your hearts

**19.1.** The Lord in a plaintive voice consoles the devotees,
speaking as He weeps and weeps;
joining His palms, Gaurahari entreats:
"Do not withdraw your mercy from Me in your hearts!

ছাড়ি নবদ্বীপ-বাস পরিনু অরুণ-বাস
শচী বিষ্ণুপ্রিয়ারে ছাড়িয়া ।
মনে মোর এই আশ করি নীলাচলে বাস
তোমা সবার অনুমতি লৈয়া ॥

*chāṛi nabadvīpa-bāsa parinu aruṇa-bāsa*
*śacī biṣṇupriyāre chāṛiyā |*
*mane mora ei āśa kari nīlācale bāsa*
*tomā sabāra anumati laiyā ||*

*Word for word:* chāṛi nabadvīpa-bāsa — leaving My dwelling in Navadvipa; parinu aruṇa-bāsa — I have put on saffron cloth; śacī biṣṇupriyāre chāṛiyā — leaving Shachi and Vishnupriya; mane mora ei āśa — in My heart is this hope; kari nīlācale bāsa — to live in Nilachala; tomā sabāra anumati laiyā — with the consent of you all

**19.2.** Leaving My life in Navadvipa, I have put on saffron cloth,
I have left Shachi and Vishnupriya;
in My heart is one hope — to live in Nilachala
with the consent of you all.

নীলাচল নদীয়াতে লোক করে যাতায়াতে
তাহাতে পাইবা তত্ত্ব মোর ।
এত বলি গৌরহরি নমো নারায়ণ স্মরি
অদ্বৈতে ধরিয়া দিল কোর ॥

*nīlācala nadīyāte loka kare yātāyāte*
*tāhāte pāibā tattva mora |*
*eta bali gaurahari namo nārāyaṇa smari*
*advaite dhariyā dila kora ||*

*Word for word:* nīlācala nadīyāte — between Nilachala and Nadia; loka kare yātāyāte — people come and go; tāhāte — through them; pāibā tattva mora — you will get news of Me; eta bali gaurahari — saying this, Gaurahari; namo nārāyaṇa smari — uttering "namo narayana"; advaite dhariyā — taking hold of Advaita; dila kora — embraced Him

**19.3.** Between Nilachala and Nadia people come and go —
through them you will have news of Me."
Saying this, Gaurahari, uttering "namo narayana",
took hold of Advaita and embraced Him.[^12-51]

শচীরে প্রবোধ দিয়া তাঁর পদধূলি লৈয়া
নিরপেক্ষ যাত্রা প্রভু কৈল ।
বাসুদেব ঘোষ বলে গোরা যায় নীলাচলে
শান্তিপুর ক্রন্দনে ভরিল ॥

*śacīre prabodha diyā tām̐ra padadhūli laiyā*
*nirapekṣa yātrā prabhu kaila |*
*bāsudeba ghoṣa bale gorā yāya nīlācale*
*śāntipura krandane bharila ||*

*Word for word:* śacīre prabodha diyā — consoling Shachi; tām̐ra padadhūli laiyā — taking the dust of her feet; nirapekṣa yātrā prabhu kaila — the Lord set out without looking back; bāsudeba ghoṣa bale — Vasudeva Ghosha says; gorā yāya nīlācale — Gora goes to Nilachala; śāntipura krandane bharila — Shantipura was filled with weeping

**19.4.** Consoling Shachi, taking the dust of her feet,
the Lord set out on His way without looking back.
Vasudeva Ghosha says: Gora goes to Nilachala —
Shantipura was filled with weeping.
