## 20. Vasu Ghosha — "advaita-bilāpe prabhu hailā bikala…" (GPT1 p. 382, no. 53)
*Advaita's lament: moved by His weeping, the Lord in tears says to Him: "Why such bewilderment? You Yourself determined the course of
My lila; if I do not go to Nilachala, the lila will be spoiled and all You wished for will be in vain: how then will the name of
Hari be preached? Do not grieve like an ordinary man: I am always with You." Advaita is comforted. Raga dhanashi.*[^12-52]

অদ্বৈত-বিলাপে প্রভু হইলা বিকল ।
শ্রাবণের ধারা সম চক্ষে ঝরে জল ॥

*advaita-bilāpe prabhu hailā bikala |*
*śrābaṇera dhārā sama cakṣe jhare jala ||*

*Word for word:* advaita-bilāpe — at Advaita's lament; prabhu hailā bikala — the Lord was overwhelmed; śrābaṇera dhārā sama — like the downpour of shravana; cakṣe jhare jala — tears pour from His eyes

**20.1.** At Advaita's lament the Lord was overwhelmed:
like the downpour of shravana, tears pour from His eyes.

কহেন অদ্বৈতাচার্য্য এত কেন ভ্রম ।
তুমি স্থির করিয়াছ মোর লীলাক্রম ॥

*kahena advaitācāryya eta kena bhrama |*
*tumi sthira kariyācha mora līlākrama ||*

*Word for word:* kahena advaitācāryya — (the Lord) says (to) Advaita Acharya; eta kena bhrama — why such bewilderment; tumi sthira kariyācha — You have determined; mora līlākrama — the course of My lila

**20.2.** He says to Advaita Acharya: "Why such bewilderment?
You Yourself have determined the course of My lila.[^12-53]

নীলাচলে নাহি গেলে পণ্ড হবে লীলা ।
বিফল হইবে সব তুমি যা চাহিলা ॥

*nīlācale nāhi gele paṇḍa habe līlā |*
*biphala haibe saba tumi yā cāhilā ||*

*Word for word:* nīlācale nāhi gele — if I do not go to Nilachala; paṇḍa habe līlā — the lila will be spoiled; biphala haibe saba — all will be fruitless; tumi yā cāhilā — that You wished for

**20.3.** If I do not go to Nilachala, the lila will be spoiled,
all that You wished for will be in vain.

কিরূপেতে হরিনাম হইবে প্রচার ।
কিরূপে ভুবনের লোক পাইবে নিস্তার ॥

*kirūpete harināma haibe pracāra |*
*kirūpe bhubanera loka pāibe nistāra ||*

*Word for word:* kirūpete — how; harināma haibe pracāra — will the name of Hari be preached; kirūpe — how; bhubanera loka — the people of the world; pāibe nistāra — will find deliverance

**20.4.** How then will the name of Hari be preached?
How will the people of the world find deliverance?

প্রাকৃত লোকের প্রায় শোক কেন কর ।

I am always with You — believe this."

প্রভু-বাক্যে অদ্বৈত পাইলা পরিতোষ ।

*prabhu-bākye advaita pāilā paritoṣa |*
*jaya gaurāṅgera jaya kahe bāsu ghoṣa ||*

*Word for word:* prabhu-bākye — at the Lord's words; advaita pāilā paritoṣa — Advaita was comforted; jaya gaurāṅgera jaya — glory, glory to Gauranga; kahe bāsu ghoṣa — says Vasu Ghosha

**20.6.** At the Lord's words Advaita was comforted.
"Glory, glory to Gauranga!" says Vasu Ghosha.

কান্দে বধূ বিষ্ণুপ্রিয়া ধূলায় অঙ্গ আছাড়িয়া

## 22. Vasu Ghosha — "hede re nadīyāra cām̐da bāchā re nimāi…" (GPT1 p. 383, no. 2)
*Shachi, embracing her son by the neck and kissing Him, implores: she, unfortunate, has no one else; He has abandoned His
old mother and left Vishnupriya in her care; all Nadia weeps — let Him come home and sing kirtana with Srivasa, Haridasa,
Murari, Mukunda and Vasu; she will call the brahmanas, and He will be given the sacred thread again. Raga suhai.*[^12-56]

হেদে রে নদীয়ার চাঁদ বাছা রে নিমাই ।
অভাগিনী তোর মায়ের আর কেহ নাই ॥

*hede re nadīyāra cām̐da bāchā re nimāi |*
*abhāginī tora māyera āra keha nāi ||*

*Word for word:* hede re — O; nadīyāra cām̐da — moon of Nadia; bāchā re nimāi — my child Nimai; abhāginī — unfortunate; tora māyera — your mother has; āra keha nāi — no one else

**22.1.** "O moon of Nadia, my child Nimai!
Your unfortunate mother has no one else."

এত বলি ধরি শচী গৌরাঙ্গের গলে ।
স্নেহভরে চুম্ব দেয় বদন-কমলে ॥

*eta bali dhari śacī gaurāṅgera gale |*
*snehabhare cumba deya badana-kamale ||*

*Word for word:* eta bali — saying this; dhari śacī — Shachi, holding; gaurāṅgera gale — Gauranga by the neck; snehabhare — in the fullness of affection; cumba deya — kisses; badana-kamale — the lotus face

**22.2.** Saying this, Shachi embraced Gauranga by the neck
and, in the fullness of affection, kisses the lotus of His face.

মুই বৃদ্ধ মাতা তোর মোরে ফেলাইলা ।
বিষ্ণুপ্রিয়া বধূ দিলা গলায় গাঁথিয়া ॥

*mui bṛddha mātā tora more phelāilā |*
*biṣṇupriyā badhū dilā galāya gām̐thiyā ||*

*Word for word:* mui bṛddha mātā tora — I, your old mother; more phelāilā — you have abandoned me; biṣṇupriyā badhū — the daughter-in-law Vishnupriya; dilā galāya gām̐thiyā — you have hung on my neck

**22.3.** "Me, Your old mother, You have abandoned,
and the daughter-in-law Vishnupriya You have hung upon my neck.

তোর লাগি কাঁদে সব নদীয়ার লোক ।
ঘরেরে চল রে বাছা দূরে যাকু শোক ॥

*tora lāgi kām̐de saba nadīyāra loka |*
*gharere cala re bāchā dūre yāku śoka ||*

*Word for word:* tora lāgi — for you; kām̐de saba nadīyāra loka — all the people of Nadia weep; gharere cala re bāchā — come home, my child; dūre yāku śoka — let the grief go far away

**22.4.** For You all the people of Nadia weep;
come home, my child — let the grief go far away.

শ্রীনিবাস হরিদাস যত ভক্তগণ ।
তা সবারে লৈয়া বাছা করহ কীর্তন ॥

*śrīnibāsa haridāsa yata bhaktagaṇa |*
*tā sabāre laiyā bāchā karaha kīrtana ||*

*Word for word:* śrīnibāsa haridāsa — Srinivasa (Srivasa), Haridasa; yata bhaktagaṇa — all the devotees; tā sabāre laiyā — with all of them; bāchā — my child; karaha kīrtana — perform kirtana

**22.5.** Srinivasa, Haridasa and all the devotees —
with all of them, my child, perform kirtana.

মুরারি মুকুন্দ বাসু আর হরিদাস ।
এ সব ছাড়িয়া কেন করিলা সন্ন্যাস ॥

*murāri mukunda bāsu āra haridāsa |*
*e saba chāṛiyā kena karilā sannyāsa ||*

*Word for word:* murāri mukunda bāsu — Murari, Mukunda, Vasu; āra haridāsa — and Haridasa; e saba chāṛiyā — leaving all these; kena karilā sannyāsa — why did you take sannyasa

**22.6.** Murari, Mukunda, Vasu and Haridasa —
why, leaving them all, did You take sannyasa?

যে করিলা সে করিলা চল রে ফিরিয়া ।
পুন যজ্ঞসূত্র দিব ব্রাহ্মণে ডাকিয়া ॥

*ye karilā se karilā cala re phiriyā |*
*puna yajñasūtra diba brāhmaṇe ḍākiyā ||*

*Word for word:* ye karilā se karilā — what you did, you did; cala re phiriyā — come back; puna yajñasūtra diba — I will give (you) the sacred thread again; brāhmaṇe ḍākiyā — calling the brahmanas

**22.7.** What You did, You did — come back!
I shall call the brahmanas, and You will be given the sacred thread again."[^12-57]

বাসুদেব ঘোষে কয় শুন মোর বাণী ।
পুনরায় নৈদ্যা চল গৌর গুণমণি ॥

*bāsudeba ghoṣe kaya śuna mora bāṇī |*
*punarāya naidyā cala gaura guṇamaṇi ||*

*Word for word:* bāsudeba ghoṣe kaya — Vasudeva Ghosha says; śuna mora bāṇī — listen to my word; punarāya naidyā cala — go back again to Nadia; gaura guṇamaṇi — Gaura, jewel of virtues

**22.8.** Vasudeva Ghosha says: "Listen to my word:
go back again to Nadia, Gaura, jewel of virtues!"

[^12-56]: GPT1 — p. 383, no. 2 (raga suhai), checked against the scan (PDF p. 642); GPT2 — sec. 5.4, no. 2. The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or
PS. Shachi holds her son in her arms — apparently at the meeting in Shantipura (CC Madhya 3); "Srinivasa" (śrīnibāsa) here is

motherly love (vatsalya), unaware of the Son's majesty.

## 23. Vasu Ghosha — "kām̐de debī biṣṇupriyā nija aṅga āchāṛiyā…" (GPT1 pp. 387–388, no. 17)
*Vishnupriya's lament: rolling on the ground, she says: "My lord, You have cast me adrift in boundless waters; at whose word did
You take sannyasa? Even Raghunatha went to the forest together with Janaki; even Krishna, going to Mathura, sent Uddhava to the
gopis and so preserved their lives. I shall give this body to the Ganga." Raga pahida.*[^12-58]

কাঁদে দেবী বিষ্ণুপ্রিয়া নিজ অঙ্গ আছাড়িয়া
লোটাঞা লোটাঞা ক্ষিতিতলে ।
ওহে নাথ কি কহিলে পাথারে ভাসাঞা গেলে
কাঁদিতে কাঁদিতে ইহা বলে ॥

*kām̐de debī biṣṇupriyā nija aṅga āchāṛiyā*
*loṭāñā loṭāñā kṣititale |*
*ohe nātha ki kahile pāthāre bhāsāñā gele*
*kām̐dite kām̐dite ihā bale ||*

*Word for word:* kām̐de debī biṣṇupriyā — Devi Vishnupriya weeps; nija aṅga āchāṛiyā — flinging herself down; loṭāñā loṭāñā — rolling and rolling; kṣititale — on the ground; ohe nātha — O my lord; ki kahile — what have you said; pāthāre bhāsāñā gele — you left (me) adrift in the boundless waters; kām̐dite kām̐dite ihā bale — weeping, she says this

**23.1.** Devi Vishnupriya weeps, flinging herself down,
rolling and rolling on the ground.
"O my lord, what have You done? You have cast me adrift in boundless waters and gone!" —
so she says, sobbing.

এ ঘর জননী ছাড়ি মোরে অনাথিনী করি
কার বোলে করিলা সন্ন্যাস ।
বেদেও শুনি রঘুনাথ লইয়া জানকী সাথ
তবে সে করিলা বনবাস ॥

*e ghara jananī chāṛi more anāthinī kari*
*kāra bole karilā sannyāsa |*
*bedeo śuni raghunātha laiyā jānakī sātha*
*tabe se karilā banabāsa ||*

*Word for word:* e ghara jananī chāṛi — leaving this house and your mother; more anāthinī kari — making me helpless; kāra bole — at whose word; karilā sannyāsa — did you take sannyasa; bedeo śuni — even in the Vedas I hear; raghunātha — Raghunatha; laiyā jānakī sātha — taking Janaki with him; tabe se karilā banabāsa — only then went to live in the forest

**23.2.** "Leaving this house and Your mother, making me helpless,
at whose word did You take sannyasa?
Even in the Vedas I hear: Raghunatha
went to the forest only taking Janaki with Him.[^12-59]

পূরুবে নন্দের বালা যবে মধুপুর গেলা
এড়িয়া সকল গোপীগণে ।
উদ্ধবেরে পাঠাইয়া নিজ-তত্ত্ব জানাইয়া
রাখিলেন তা সবার প্রাণে ॥

*pūrube nandera bālā yabe madhupura gelā*
*eṛiyā sakala gopīgaṇe |*
*uddhabere pāṭhāiyā nija-tattva jānāiyā*
*rākhilena tā sabāra prāṇe ||*

*Word for word:* pūrube — formerly; nandera bālā — Nanda's son; yabe madhupura gelā — when he went to Mathura; eṛiyā sakala gopīgaṇe — leaving all the gopis; uddhabere pāṭhāiyā — sending Uddhava; nija-tattva jānāiyā — making known news of himself; rākhilena tā sabāra prāṇe — preserved their lives

**23.3.** And formerly the son of Nanda, when He went to Mathura,
leaving all the gopis,
sent Uddhava to them, gave them news of Himself —
and so preserved their lives.[^12-60]

চাঁদমুখ না দেখিব আর পদ না সেবিব
না করিব সে সুখবিলাস ।
এ দেহ গঙ্গায় দিব তোমার শরণ নিব
বাসুর জীবনে নাহি আশ ॥

*cām̐damukha nā dekhiba āra pada nā sebiba*
*nā kariba se sukhabilāsa |*
*e deha gaṅgāya diba tomāra śaraṇa niba*
*bāsura jībane nāhi āśa ||*

*Word for word:* cām̐damukha nā dekhiba — I shall not see the moon-face; āra pada nā sebiba — no more shall I serve the feet; nā kariba se sukhabilāsa — there will be no more that happy life; e deha gaṅgāya diba — I shall give this body to the Ganga; tomāra śaraṇa niba — I shall take refuge in you; bāsura jībane nāhi āśa — Vasu has no hope of life

**23.4.** No more shall I see the moon-face, no more serve Your feet,
there will be no more that happy life;
this body I shall give to the Ganga, I shall take Your refuge."
Vasu has no hope of life.[^12-61]

[^12-58]: GPT1 — pp. 387–388, no. 17 (raga pahida), checked against the scan (PDF pp. 646–647); GPT2 — sec. 5.4, no. 17. The pada is not in
PK, BR, KGC or PS. Below the text Jagadbandhu gives three variants (without naming the source): "mui", "eṛi", "rāmāyaṇe" (see the full version of the book).
[^12-59]: Variant (GPT1 note): "in the Ramayana" instead of "in the Vedas". Rama took Sita (Janaki) with Him into His forest exile.
[^12-60]: Uddhava, sent by Krishna from Mathura to Vraja with a message for the gopis (Bhag. 10.46–47). Vishnupriya reproaches the Lord: He
has not left her even a message. Her lament is the lament of a wife in separation; Vishnupriya herself, according to tradition,
afterwards lived under a strict vow, chanting the holy name.
[^12-61]: "I shall give my body to the Ganga" is an image of the utmost despair of separation, not the description of an event.

## 24. Vasu Ghosha — "hede re parāṇa nilajiyā…" (GPT1 p. 388, no. 21)
*Vishnupriya reproaches her "shameless" life for not leaving the body: Gauranga has left her, He has become a sannyasi and gone —
the happiness of this life is over. Raga bhupali.*[^12-62]

হেদে রে পরাণ নিলজিয়া ।
এখন না গেলি তনু তেজিয়া ॥

*hede re parāṇa nilajiyā |*
*ekhana nā geli tanu tejiyā ||*

*Word for word:* hede re — O; parāṇa nilajiyā — shameless life; ekhana nā geli — have you not yet gone; tanu tejiyā — leaving the body

**24.1.** "O my shameless life,
you have still not left the body!

গৌরাঙ্গ ছাড়িয়া গেছে মোর ।
আর কি গৌরব আছে তোর ॥

*gaurāṅga chāṛiyā geche mora |*
*āra ki gauraba āche tora ||*

*Word for word:* gaurāṅga chāṛiyā geche mora — Gauranga has left me; āra ki gauraba āche tora — what honour do you still have

**24.2.** Gauranga has left me —
what honour do you still have?

আর কি গৌরাঙ্গচাঁদে পাবে ।
মিছা প্রেম-আশ-আশে রবে ॥

*āra ki gaurāṅgacām̐de pābe |*
*michā prema-āśa-āśe rabe ||*

*Word for word:* āra ki gaurāṅgacām̐de pābe — will you ever find Gaurangachand again; michā prema-āśa-āśe rabe — in vain you will live in hope of love

**24.3.** Will you ever find Gaurangachand again?
In vain you will live in hope of love.

সন্ন্যাসী হইয়া পহুঁ গেল ।
এ জনমের সুখ ফুরাইল ॥

*sannyāsī haiyā pahum̐ gela |*
*e janamera sukha phurāila ||*

*Word for word:* sannyāsī haiyā pahum̐ gela — becoming a sannyasi, my lord has gone; e janamera sukha phurāila — the happiness of this life is over

**24.4.** Becoming a sannyasi, my lord has gone —
the happiness of this life is over."

কাঁদি বিষ্ণুপ্রিয়া কহে বাণী ।
বাসু কহে না রহে পরাণি ॥

*kām̐di biṣṇupriyā kahe bāṇī |*
*bāsu kahe nā rahe parāṇi ||*

*Word for word:* kām̐di biṣṇupriyā kahe bāṇī — weeping, Vishnupriya speaks; bāsu kahe — Vasu says; nā rahe parāṇi — life will not remain

**24.5.** So, weeping, Vishnupriya speaks.
Vasu says: life will not remain.

## 25. Vasu Ghosha — "dhika yāu e chāra jībane…" (GPT1 p. 389, no. 22)
*Lament in separation: fie on this worthless life — where has Gora, the life of my life, gone? I shall not see the moon-face nor
hear His words; gone is the happiness He gave — a spear has remained in my heart; day and night I think only of the pauper's
treasure — His reddish feet; fate has turned away. Raga vibhasa.*[^12-63]

ধিক যাউ এ ছার জীবনে ।
পরাণের পরাণ গোরা গেল কোন্‌খানে ॥

*dhika yāu e chāra jībane |*
*parāṇera parāṇa gorā gela konkhāne ||*

*Word for word:* dhika yāu — fie on; e chāra jībane — this worthless life; parāṇera parāṇa — the life of my life; gorā gela konkhāne — where has Gora gone

**25.1.** Fie on this worthless life!
Where has Gora gone, the life of my life?

গোরা বিনু প্রাণ মোর আকুল বিকল ।
নিরবধি আঁখির জল করে ছল ছল ॥

*gorā binu prāṇa mora ākula bikala |*
*nirabadhi ām̐khira jala kare chala chala ||*

*Word for word:* gorā binu — without Gora; prāṇa mora ākula bikala — my soul is distraught and overwhelmed; nirabadhi — ceaselessly; ām̐khira jala — the tears of my eyes; kare chala chala — brim over

**25.2.** Without Gora my soul is distraught and overwhelmed,
ceaselessly tears brim over in my eyes.

না হেরিব চাঁদমুখ না শুনিব বাণী ।
মনে করে গোরা বিনু পশিব ধরণী ॥

*nā heriba cām̐damukha nā śuniba bāṇī |*
*mane kare gorā binu paśiba dharaṇī ||*

*Word for word:* nā heriba cām̐damukha — I shall not see the moon-face; nā śuniba bāṇī — I shall not hear the words; mane kare — I think; gorā binu — without Gora; paśiba dharaṇī — I shall enter the earth

**25.3.** I shall not see the moon-face, I shall not hear His words —
I think: without Gora I shall enter the earth.

গেল সুখ সম্পদ যত পহুঁ কৈল ।
শেল সমান মোর হৃদয়ে রহি গেল ॥

*gela sukha sampada yata pahum̐ kaila |*
*śela samāna mora hṛdaye rahi gela ||*

*Word for word:* gela sukha — gone is the happiness; sampada yata — all the wealth; pahum̐ kaila — that my lord bestowed; śela samāna — like a spear; mora hṛdaye rahi gela — has remained in my heart

**25.4.** Gone is the happiness and all the wealth my lord bestowed —
like a spear (the separation) has remained in my heart.

গোরা বিনু নিশি দিশি আর নাহি মনে ।
নিরবধি চিন্ত মুই নিধনিয়ার ধনে ॥

*gorā binu niśi diśi āra nāhi mane |*
*nirabadhi cinta mui nidhaniyāra dhane ||*

*Word for word:* gorā binu — apart from Gora; niśi diśi — night and day; āra nāhi mane — nothing else is in my mind; nirabadhi — ceaselessly; cinta mui — I think; nidhaniyāra dhane — of the pauper's treasure

**25.5.** Apart from Gora, night and day nothing else is in my mind:
ceaselessly I think of the pauper's treasure.[^12-64]

রাতুল চরণতল অতিশয় শোভা ।
যাহা লাগি মন মোর অতিশয় লোভা ॥

*rātula caraṇatala atiśaya śobhā |*
*yāhā lāgi mana mora atiśaya lobhā ||*

*Word for word:* rātula caraṇatala — the reddish soles of the feet; atiśaya śobhā — exceedingly beautiful; yāhā lāgi — for which; mana mora — my heart; atiśaya lobhā — intensely longs

**25.6.** The reddish soles of His feet are exceedingly beautiful —
for them my heart intensely longs.

ডাহিনে আছিল বিহি এবে ভেল বাম ।
কহে বাসুদেব ঘোষ না রহে পরাণ ॥

*ḍāhine āchila bihi ebe bhela bāma |*
*kahe bāsudeba ghoṣa nā rahe parāṇa ||*

*Word for word:* ḍāhine āchila bihi — fate was favourable; ebe bhela bāma — now has turned adverse; kahe bāsudeba ghoṣa — says Vasudeva Ghosha; nā rahe parāṇa — life will not remain

**25.7.** Fate was favourable — now it has turned away.
Says Vasudeva Ghosha: life will not remain.

## 26. Vasu Ghosha — "śuniyā bhakata-dukha bidariyā yāya buka…" (GPT1 pp. 409–410, no. 23)
*Hearing of the devotees' sorrow, the Lord comes with His companions to Nadia in the twinkling of an eye; Gadadhara lies
senseless, Narahari beside him; the Lord, rolling on the ground, cries out: "What have I done! May lightning strike the
sannyasa — I will not go to Nilachala, I shall stay with the devotees!" — and loses consciousness; the companions lay Him in
Gadadhara's lap, and both float in bliss. Raga dhanashi.*[^12-65]

শুনিয়া ভকত-দুখ বিদরিয়া যায় বুক
চলে গোরা সহচর সাথে ।
তুরিতে গমন যার নিমেষে যোজন পার
ভকত-মিলন নদীয়াতে ॥

*śuniyā bhakata-dukha bidariyā yāya buka*
*cale gorā sahacara sāthe |*
*turite gamana yāra nimeṣe yojana pāra*
*bhakata-milana nadīyāte ||*

*Word for word:* śuniyā bhakata-dukha — hearing of the devotees' sorrow; bidariyā yāya buka — His heart breaks; cale gorā — Gora goes; sahacara sāthe — with His companions; turite gamana yāra — He whose going is swift; nimeṣe yojana pāra — crosses a yojana in a moment; bhakata-milana nadīyāte — the meeting with the devotees in Nadia

**26.1.** Hearing of the devotees' sorrow, His heart breaking,
Gora goes with His companions;
He whose going is swift crosses a yojana in a moment —
and here is the meeting with the devotees in Nadia.[^12-66]

গদাধর পড়িয়াছে নরহরি তার কাছে
আর কার মুখে নাহি বাণী ।
দেখিয়া ভকত-দশা কহে গদাধর-ভাষা
ধরণী লোটাঞা ন্যাসী মুনি ॥

*gadādhara paṛiyāche narahari tāra kāche*
*āra kāra mukhe nāhi bāṇī |*
*dekhiyā bhakata-daśā kahe gadādhara-bhāṣā*
*dharaṇī loṭāñā nyāsī muni ||*

*Word for word:* gadādhara paṛiyāche — Gadadhara has fallen (senseless); narahari tāra kāche — Narahari beside him; āra kāra mukhe nāhi bāṇī — no one else can speak; dekhiyā bhakata-daśā — seeing the devotees' state; kahe gadādhara-bhāṣā — speaks words to Gadadhara (?); dharaṇī loṭāñā — rolling on the ground; nyāsī muni — the sannyasi sage

**26.2.** Gadadhara lies senseless, Narahari is beside him,
no one else can speak.
Seeing the devotees' state, the sannyasi sage, rolling on the ground,
speaks to Gadadhara:[^12-67]

হায় কি করিলাম কাজ সন্ন্যাসে পড়ুক বাজ
মোর বড় হৃদয় পাষাণ ।
নাহি যাব নীলাচলে থাকিব ভকত-মেলে
ইহা বলি হরল গেয়ান ॥

*hāya ki karilāma kāja sannyāse paṛuka bāja*
*mora baṛa hṛdaya pāṣāṇa |*
*nāhi yāba nīlācale thākiba bhakata-mele*
*ihā bali harala geyāna ||*

*Word for word:* hāya — alas; ki karilāma kāja — what have I done; sannyāse paṛuka bāja — may lightning strike the sannyasa; mora baṛa hṛdaya pāṣāṇa — My heart is like stone; nāhi yāba nīlācale — I will not go to Nilachala; thākiba bhakata-mele — I shall stay among the devotees; ihā bali — saying this; harala geyāna — He lost consciousness

**26.3.** "Alas, what have I done! May lightning strike the sannyasa:
My heart is like stone!
I will not go to Nilachala — I shall stay with the devotees."
Saying this, He lost consciousness.

সঙ্গে সহচর ছিল ধাই গৌরাঙ্গ নিল
রাখিলেন গদাধর-কোরে ।
পরশ পাইয়া দুহুঁ কথা কহে লহু লহু
ভাসিলেন আনন্দ-পাথারে ॥

*saṅge sahacara chila dhāi gaurāṅga nila*
*rākhilena gadādhara-kore |*
*paraśa pāiyā duhum̐ kathā kahe lahu lahu*
*bhāsilena ānanda-pāthāre ||*

*Word for word:* saṅge sahacara chila — the companions who were with Him; dhāi — running up; gaurāṅga nila — lifted Gauranga; rākhilena gadādhara-kore — laid Him in Gadadhara's lap; paraśa pāiyā — feeling the touch; duhum̐ — both; kathā kahe lahu lahu — speak softly; bhāsilena ānanda-pāthāre — floated in an ocean of bliss

**26.4.** The companions who were with Him ran up, lifted Gauranga
and laid Him in Gadadhara's lap;
feeling each other's touch, both speak softly, softly
and float in an ocean of bliss.

শ্রীগৌরাঙ্গ-মুখ দেখি শীতল হইল আঁখি
পরশেতে হিয়া জুড়াইল ।
আর না ছাড়িয়া দিব হিয়ার মাঝারে থোব
বাসু ঘোষের আনন্দ বাড়িল ॥

*śrīgaurāṅga-mukha dekhi śītala haila ām̐khi*
*paraśete hiyā juṛāila |*
*āra nā chāṛiyā diba hiyāra mājhāre thoba*
*bāsu ghoṣera ānanda bāṛila ||*

*Word for word:* śrīgaurāṅga-mukha dekhi — seeing Sri Gauranga's face; śītala haila ām̐khi — the eyes were cooled; paraśete — by the touch; hiyā juṛāila — the heart was soothed; āra nā chāṛiyā diba — I shall not let Him go again; hiyāra mājhāre thoba — I shall keep Him within my heart; bāsu ghoṣera ānanda bāṛila — Vasu Ghosha's bliss increased

**26.5.** The eyes were cooled, seeing the face of Sri Gauranga,
by the touch the heart was soothed:
"I shall not let Him go again — I shall keep Him in my heart!" —
and Vasu Ghosha's bliss increased.

[^12-65]: GPT1 — pp. 409–410, section "antya-lila" (the final pastimes), no. 23 (raga dhanashi), checked against the scan (PDF pp. 668–669);
GPT2 — sec. 5.5, no. 23. The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS. In GPT the pada stands before Vasu's pada on the coming of the people of
Nadia to the Lord (no. 24 = PK 2041, chapter 9, no. 6), i.e. it concerns the Lord's coming to Navadvipa on His way to Vrindavana
(1514/15; CC Madhya 16; CB Antya 3). The poet depicts this meeting in his own way: with him Gadadhara is in Nadia (according to CC
Madhya 16 Gadadhara accompanied the Lord from Puri to Cuttack) and the Lord resolves to stay.
[^12-66]: "Crosses a yojana in a moment" — hearing the devotees' call, the Lord comes to them, however long the way; the power of His love
for His devotees.
[^12-67]: The reading "gadādhara-bhāṣā" (lit. "Gadadhara's speech") is found in both editions of GPT; possibly a corruption of "gadagada bhāṣā" ("in a
choked voice").

## 27. Vasu Ghosha — "āju re kanakācala nīlācale gorā…" (GPT1 p. 341, no. 64)
*Phagu in Nilachala: Gora, like a golden mountain, is lost in the play of colours together with Govinda; on His neck sways a garland of
bakula, red with colour; the devotees, red with colour, sing sweetly; bhavas spread over His body, His eyes are half-closed in waves of
prema; looking at Gadadhara, He smiles softly. Raga todi.*[^12-68]

আজু রে কনকাচল নীলাচলে গোরা ।
গোবিন্দের সঙ্গে ফাগু-রঙ্গে ভেল ভোরা ॥

*āju re kanakācala nīlācale gorā |*
*gobindera saṅge phāgu-raṅge bhela bhorā ||*

*Word for word:* āju re — today; kanakācala — a golden mountain; nīlācale gorā — Gora in Nilachala; gobindera saṅge — together with Govinda; phāgu-raṅge — in the play of colours; bhela bhorā — is lost (in bliss)

**27.1.** Today Gora, a golden mountain, in Nilachala
together with Govinda is lost in the play of colours.[^12-69]

কণ্ঠে লোহিত দোলে বকুলকি মাল ।
অরুণ ভকতগণ গাওয়ে রসাল ॥

*kaṇṭhe lohita dole bakulaki māla |*
*aruṇa bhakatagaṇa gāoye rasāla ||*

*Word for word:* kaṇṭhe — on His neck; lohita dole — reddened, swings; bakulaki māla — the garland of bakula flowers; aruṇa bhakatagaṇa — the reddened devotees; gāoye rasāla — sing sweetly

**27.2.** On His neck sways a garland of bakula, red with colour;
the devotees, red with colour, sing sweetly.

কত কত ভাব উঠে বিথারল অঙ্গ ।
নয়ন ঢুলু ঢুলু প্রেম-তরঙ্গ ॥

*kata kata bhāba uṭhe bithārala aṅga |*
*nayana ḍhulu ḍhulu prema-taraṅga ||*

*Word for word:* kata kata bhāba uṭhe — so many bhavas arise; bithārala aṅga — spread over His body; nayana ḍhulu ḍhulu — the eyes half-closed; prema-taraṅga — waves of prema

**27.3.** So many bhavas arise — they have spread over all His body;
His eyes are half-closed in waves of prema.

গদাধরে হেরিয়া লহু লহু হাসে ।
সো নাহি সমুঝল বাসুদেব ঘোষে ॥

*gadādhare heriyā lahu lahu hāse |*
*so nāhi samujhala bāsudeba ghoṣe ||*

*Word for word:* gadādhare heriyā — looking at Gadadhara; lahu lahu hāse — smiles softly; so nāhi samujhala — that (smile) did not understand; bāsudeba ghoṣe — Vasudeva Ghosha

**27.4.** Looking at Gadadhara, He smiles softly, softly —
that smile Vasudeva Ghosha did not understand.

[^12-68]: GPT1 — p. 341, section "festivals of the year", no. 64 (raga todi), checked against the scan (PDF p. 600); GPT2 — sec. 5.1, no. 64. The
pada repeats almost word for word — shorter and with the signature of Vasudeva Ghosha — the pada of **Govinda Dasa** PK 1463
("nīlācale kanakācala gorā…", vol. 2; = GPT1 p. 341, no. 66; also in PS), which Jagadbandhu placed right here, one pada later. Probably this is
a recension of Govinda Dasa's pada which, by mistake or by singers' custom, received Vasu's signature; the attribution to Vasu Ghosha is
highly doubtful. Another pada on the phagu in Nilachala is by Madhavi Dasa (PK 2290; chapter 6).
[^12-69]: Govinda is Krishna; in Puri, at the festival of Dola-yatra, His festival Deity (Dola-Govinda) is sprinkled with coloured powder.
Perhaps the poet means the Lord's play with the Deity at this festival.

## 28. Vasu Ghosha — "svarūpera kare dhari bale kām̐di gaurahari…" (GPT1 pp. 306–307, no. 25)
*The Lord in the bhava of Radha disappointed in Her waiting (vipralabdha): holding Svarupa's hand, He weeps — the night has passed in
vain, the moon has set, Shyama has not come; the bed of flowers has wilted, the garland has withered; "Come, Svarupa, to the Suradhuni, let us
set all this afloat; let honour and family be lost — I shall throw Myself into the water"; the poet: where can the pain of this heart be
eased? Raga kamoda.*[^12-70]

স্বরূপের করে ধরি বলে কাঁদি গৌরহরি
বিহনে আমার শ্যাম রায় ।
বিফলে বঞ্চিলুঁ নিশি অস্তমিত ভেল শশী
এ পরাণ ফাটি মঝু যায় ॥

*svarūpera kare dhari bale kām̐di gaurahari*
*bihane āmāra śyāma rāya |*
*biphale bañcilum̐ niśi astamita bhela śaśī*
*e parāṇa phāṭi majhu yāya ||*

*Word for word:* svarūpera kare dhari — holding Svarupa's hand; bale kām̐di gaurahari — weeping, Gaurahari says; bihane — without; āmāra śyāma rāya — My Shyama; biphale bañcilum̐ niśi — I have spent the night in vain; astamita bhela śaśī — the moon has set; e parāṇa phāṭi majhu yāya — My heart is breaking

**28.1.** Holding Svarupa's hand, weeping, Gaurahari says:
"My Shyama is not with Me!
In vain have I spent the night — the moon has set;
My heart is breaking.

কোথায় আমার শ্যাম বঁধু ।
ফুল-শেজ বাসি ভেল ফুলহার শুখাওল
না মিলল শ্যাম-প্রেমমধু ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*kothāya āmāra śyāma bam̐dhu |*
*phula-śeja bāsi bhela phulahāra śukhāola*
*nā milala śyāma-premamadhu || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* kothāya āmāra śyāma bām̐dhu — where is My beloved Shyama; phula-śeja bāsi bhela — the bed of flowers has gone stale; phulahāra śukhāola — the garland has withered; nā milala — was not found; śyāma-premamadhu — the honey of Shyama's love

**28.2.** *(Refrain)* Where is My beloved Shyama?
The bed of flowers has wilted, the garland has withered —
I have not tasted the honey of Shyama's love.

চল রে স্বরূপ চল যাই সুরধুনী-জল
এ সকল দেই ভাসাইয়া ।
গেল যাক কুলমান আর না রাখিব প্রাণ
তেজিব সলিলে ঝাঁপ দিয়া ॥

*cala re svarūpa cala yāi suradhunī-jala*
*e sakala dei bhāsāiyā |*
*gela yāka kulamāna āra nā rākhiba prāṇa*
*tejiba salile jhām̐pa diyā ||*

*Word for word:* cala re svarūpa — come, Svarupa; cala yāi — let us go; suradhunī-jala — to the waters of the Suradhuni (the Ganga); e sakala dei bhāsāiyā — let us set all this afloat; gela yāka kulamāna — let family honour be gone; āra nā rākhiba prāṇa — I shall not keep My life; tejiba salile — I shall give it up in the water; jhām̐pa diyā — leaping in

**28.3.** Come, Svarupa, let us go to the waters of the Suradhuni —
let us set all this afloat.
Let honour and family be lost — I shall live no more:
I shall leap into the water and give up My life.[^12-71]

আমার সে কালশশী কার কুঞ্জে বঞ্চে নিশি
কাঁহে মুঝে ভেলত বৈমুখ ।
বাসুদেব ঘোষ কহে এ দুখে পরাণ দহে
কাঁহা মিটায়ব হিয়া-দুখ ॥

*āmāra se kālaśaśī kāra kuñje bañce niśi*
*kām̐he mujhe bhelata baimukha |*
*bāsudeba ghoṣa kahe e dukhe parāṇa dahe*
*kām̐hā miṭāyaba hiyā-dukha ||*

*Word for word:* āmāra se kālaśaśī — that dark moon of Mine; kāra kuñje bañce niśi — in whose bower does He spend the night; kām̐he mujhe — why from Me; bhelata baimukha — has He turned away; bāsudeba ghoṣa kahe — says Vasudeva Ghosha; e dukhe parāṇa dahe — in this sorrow the heart burns; kām̐hā miṭāyaba hiyā-dukha — where shall I ease the pain of the heart

**28.4.** That dark moon of Mine — in whose bower does He spend the night?
Why has He turned away from Me?"
Says Vasudeva Ghosha: in this sorrow the heart burns —
where can the pain of this heart be eased?[^12-72]

[^12-70]: GPT1 — pp. 306–307, section on the vipralabdha, no. 25 (raga kamoda), checked against the scan (PDF pp. 565–566); GPT2 — sec. 4.5,
no. 25. The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS. Majumdar considers that the pada does not belong to Vasu: Svarupa Damodara was not the Lord's
companion in Navadvipa (at that time he was called Purushottama Acharya), while the Suradhuni (the Ganga) here points to Navadvipa. Cf. another GPT pada
with the same signature and the same opening, "svarūpera kare dhari gorārāya" (chapter 3, no. 14). Such bhavas of the Lord in Puri, in the
company of Svarupa — CC Antya 14–19.
[^12-71]: Radha's words in separation: "let honour and family be lost" is a sign of prema that gives up for Krishna everything the world
values; this is not worldly passion but the highest, pure love (CC Adi 4). The Lord in the bhava of Radha speaks Her words (Svarupa in
this lila is Radha's friend Lalita). "I shall leap into the water" is the utmost expression of separation
(vipralambha), in which prema reaches its peak.
[^12-72]: "The dark moon" (kālaśaśī) is Krishna; the kunja is a bower-grove in Vrindavana.

## 29. Vasu Ghosha — "ki ānanda khaṇḍapure ṭhākura naraharira ghare…" (GPT1 p. 353, no. 30)
*The festival at Shrikhanda: in the house of Narahari Thakura all the mahantas gather, the twelve gopalas, the sixty-four mahantas and the
six Gosvamis; Srinivasa seats everyone according to rank, in the middle — Gaurahari between the two Prabhus, Nityananda and Advaita;
Raghunandana serves the food, Mahaprabhu puts a mouthful into Nitai's mouth, Narahari and Gadadhara feed each other; after the meal
Srinivasa gives out garlands and sandal. Raga dhanashi.*[^12-73]

কি আনন্দ খণ্ডপুরে ঠাকুর নরহরির ঘরে
মহোৎসবের কে করে আনন্দ ।
সকল মহান্ত আসি প্রেমানন্দ-রসে ভাসি
নিরখয়ে গৌরমুখচন্দ ॥

*ki ānanda khaṇḍapure ṭhākura naraharira ghare*
*mahotsabera ke kare ānanda |*
*sakala mahānta āsi premānanda-rase bhāsi*
*nirakhaye gauramukhacanda ||*

*Word for word:* ki ānanda — what bliss; khaṇḍapure — in Shrikhanda; ṭhākura naraharira ghare — in the house of Thakura Narahari; mahotsabera — of the festival; ke kare ānanda — who (can tell) the joy; sakala mahānta āsi — all the mahantas, coming; premānanda-rase bhāsi — floating in the rasa of the bliss of prema; nirakhaye gauramukhacanda — gaze at the moon of Gaura's face

**29.1.** What bliss in Shrikhanda, in the house of Narahari Thakura!
Who can describe the joy of this festival?
All the mahantas have come and, floating in the rasa of the bliss of prema,
gaze at the moon of Gaura's face.

দ্বাদশ গোপাল আর চৌষট্টি মহান্ত সাথ
আর ক্রমে ছয়টী গোসাঞি ।
শাখা উপশাখা যত আইল সকল ভক্ত
আনন্দেতে গৌরগুণ গাই ॥

*dvādaśa gopāla āra cauṣaṭṭi mahānta sātha*
*āra krame chayaṭī gosāñi |*
*śākhā upaśākhā yata āila sakala bhakta*
*ānandete gauraguṇa gāi ||*

*Word for word:* dvādaśa gopāla — the twelve gopalas; āra — and; cauṣaṭṭi mahānta sātha — with the sixty-four mahantas; āra krame — and in order; chayaṭī gosāñi — the six Gosvamis; śākhā upaśākhā yata — all the branches and sub-branches; āila sakala bhakta — all the devotees came; ānandete gauraguṇa gāi — joyfully singing Gaura's qualities

**29.2.** The twelve gopalas and with them the sixty-four mahantas,
and then the six Gosvamis;
all the branches and sub-branches — all the devotees have come,
joyfully singing Gaura's qualities.[^12-74]

শ্রীনিবাস জনে জনে বসাইল স্থানে স্থানে
বসিল মহান্ত সারি সারি ।
যার যৈছে অনুমানে বসাইল স্থানে স্থানে
দুই প্রভুর মধ্যে গৌরহরি ॥

*śrīnibāsa jane jane basāila sthāne sthāne*
*basila mahānta sāri sāri |*
*yāra yaiche anumāne basāila sthāne sthāne*
*dui prabhura madhye gaurahari ||*

*Word for word:* śrīnibāsa — Srinivasa; jane jane — each one; basāila sthāne sthāne — seated in their places; basila mahānta sāri sāri — the mahantas sat in rows; yāra yaiche anumāne — according to each one's standing; basāila — he seated; dui prabhura madhye — between the two Prabhus; gaurahari — Gaurahari

**29.3.** Srinivasa seated each one in his place —
the mahantas sat in rows;
according to each one's standing he seated them all,
and between the two Prabhus — Gaurahari.

দক্ষিণেতে নিত্যানন্দ বামেতে অদ্বৈতচন্দ
তার বামে গদাধরাচার্য্য ।
ভোজনে বসিলা সভে রঘুনন্দন আসি তবে
করে পরিবেশনের কার্য্য ॥

*dakṣiṇete nityānanda bāmete advaitacanda*
*tāra bāme gadādharācāryya |*
*bhojane basilā sabhe raghunandana āsi tabe*
*kare paribeśanera kāryya ||*

*Word for word:* dakṣiṇete nityānanda — on the right Nityananda; bāmete advaitacanda — on the left Advaitachandra; tāra bāme — to His left; gadādharācāryya — Gadadhara Acharya; bhojane basilā sabhe — all sat down to the meal; raghunandana āsi tabe — then Raghunandana came; kare paribeśanera kāryya — does the serving

**29.4.** On the right — Nityananda, on the left — Advaitachandra,
and to His left — Gadadhara Acharya.
All sat down to the meal; then Raghunandana came
and began to serve the food.

মহাপ্রভু সুখোল্লাসে করে লৈয়া এক গ্রাসে
দেন প্রভু নিতাইর মুখে ।
এইরূপ পরস্পর নরহরি গদাধর
ভোজন করয়ে প্রেমসুখে ॥

*mahāprabhu sukhollāse kare laiyā eka grāse*
*dena prabhu nitāira mukhe |*
*eirūpa paraspara narahari gadādhara*
*bhojana karaye premasukhe ||*

*Word for word:* mahāprabhu sukhollāse — Mahaprabhu in joyful delight; kare laiyā eka grāse — taking a mouthful in His hand; dena prabhu nitāira mukhe — the Lord puts it in Nitai's mouth; eirūpa paraspara — thus one another; narahari gadādhara — Narahari and Gadadhara; bhojana karaye premasukhe — eat in the happiness of prema

**29.5.** Mahaprabhu in joyful delight, taking a mouthful in His hand,
puts it into Nitai's mouth;
so also Narahari and Gadadhara feed
each other in the happiness of prema.

ভোজনান্তে জয়ধ্বনি জয় গৌর দ্বিজমণি
সভে মিলি কৈল আচমন ।
শ্রীনিবাস সুখোল্লাসে করে লৈয়া মুখবাসে
সভে দিল মাল্য চন্দন ॥

*bhojanānte jayadhvani jaya gaura dvijamaṇi*
*sabhe mili kaila ācamana |*
*śrīnibāsa sukhollāse kare laiyā mukhabāse*
*sabhe dila mālya candana ||*

*Word for word:* bhojanānte — after the meal; jayadhvani — the cry; jaya gaura dvijamaṇi — "glory to Gaura, jewel of brahmanas!"; sabhe mili kaila ācamana — all together rinsed their mouths; śrīnibāsa sukhollāse — Srinivasa in joyful delight; kare laiyā mukhabāse — taking mouth-fresheners in his hands; sabhe dila mālya candana — gave everyone garlands and sandal

**29.6.** After the meal — the cry: "Glory to Gaura, jewel of brahmanas!" —
and all together rinsed their mouths.
Srinivasa in joyful delight, taking mouth-fresheners,
gave everyone garlands and sandal.

নরহরি ঠাকুর ধন্য যার গৃহে শ্রীচৈতন্য
নিত্যানন্দ সহিত আপনি ।
তা দেখি বৈষ্ণবগণ হরি বোলে ঘন ঘন
বাসু মাগে চরণ দুখানি ॥

*narahari ṭhākura dhanya yāra gṛhe śrīcaitanya*
*nityānanda sahita āpani |*
*tā dekhi baiṣṇabagaṇa hari bole ghana ghana*
*bāsu māge caraṇa dukhāni ||*

*Word for word:* narahari ṭhākura dhanya — blessed is Narahari Thakura; yāra gṛhe — in whose house; śrīcaitanya — Sri Chaitanya; nityānanda sahita āpani — Himself together with Nityananda; tā dekhi — seeing this; baiṣṇabagaṇa — the Vaishnavas; hari bole ghana ghana — cry "Hari!" again and again; bāsu māge caraṇa dukhāni — Vasu begs for the two feet

**29.7.** Blessed is Narahari Thakura, in whose house Sri Chaitanya
is present Himself — together with Nityananda!
Seeing this, the Vaishnavas cry "Hari!" again and again —
Vasu begs for His two feet.[^12-75]

[^12-73]: GPT1 — p. 353, section ashtakaliya, no. 30 (raga dhanashi), checked against the scan (PDF p. 612); GPT2 — sec. 5.2, no. 30. The pada is
not in PK, BR, KGC or PS. Majumdar cites it as an example of forgery in GPT: the participation of the six Gosvamis is impossible — they
never left Vrindavana together; moreover, the festival is arranged by Srinivasa Acharya, who came to Shrikhanda only after the Lord's
departure (*Bhakti-ratnakara*, *Prema-vilasa*). The attribution to Vasu Ghosha is unreliable (D).
[^12-74]: The twelve gopalas are companions of Nityananda (in the bhava of the cowherd boys of Vraja); the sixty-four mahantas are
devotee-preachers in Bengal (a later tradition); the six Gosvamis are Rupa, Sanatana, Jiva, Gopala Bhatta, Raghunatha Bhatta and
Raghunatha Dasa. "Branches and sub-branches" — the image of the tree of Chaitanya (CC Adi 10–12).
[^12-75]: The presence of Chaitanya and Nityananda "Themselves" at a festival arranged by Srinivasa is understood in the tradition as Their
appearance (avirbhava) in the devotees' kirtana: thus, according to the *Bhakti-ratnakara* and the *Narottama-vilasa*, the Lord with His
companions appeared at the festival in Kheturi. The poet, however, describes the festival as if the Lord were present in person, together
with Gadadhara, Advaita and Narahari.

---

# Chapter 13. Balarama Dasa, Murari, Yadunatha, Ananta, Ramachandra: Padas from the *Gaura-pada-tarangini* — from Krishna's Resolve to the Prayers

*This chapter continues the group of padas known from the *Gaura-pada-tarangini* (GPT1 — 1st ed. by Jagadbandhu Bhadra,
1903; GPT2 — 2nd ed., 1934), excluding padas in nagari-bhava. Here are padas signed by Balarama Dasa, Yadunatha Dasa, Murari,
Ananta (Raya Ananta) and Ramachandra, in the order of the GPT sections (that is, of the lilas): the nandi prologue (Krishna's
resolve to appear as Gaura), praise of the Gaura-avatara and wonder at the sannyasa, Gaura and Gadadhara, childhood plays,
the kirtanas of Navadvipa, the bhava of Radha, the Lord's morning, the people of Nadia in Shantipura, the waiting for His
return, praise of Nityananda and Advaita, the books of Jiva Gosvami, and prayers. Checking against the *Padakalpataru* (PK)
showed that nine padas listed as "GPT only" or missing from the catalogue altogether are in PK (nos. 4–7, 9, 15, 19–21) —
there the text follows PK with the GPT variants; no. 4 is signed by Vasu Ghosha in PK, no. 5 by "Natavara," no. 8 is
Balarama's pada PK 2201 (formerly misidentified with Lochana's pada PK 2203; corrected in the full PK check of chapter 16). Seven padas (nos. 4, 5, 8, 9, 19, 20, 25) were missing from
the stage-1 catalogue: they were found in a full check of the signatures of GPT1. Majumdar considers the GPT unreliable for
attribution; padas of several poets are known under the signature "Balarama Dasa"; the "Ramachandra" of nos. 24–25 is, by his
own words, a grandson of Vamshivadana who lived after the Lord's departure. The attribution of the padas of this chapter is
therefore provisional. The full PK check (chapter 16) found nos. 16 (PK 2512) and 18 (PK 1976) in PK as well;
their variants have been added. The Bengali original, the variants of GPT1/GPT2, PK and KGC, and the word-for-word translation are in the full version of the book.*

## 1. Balarama Dasa — "śunaite rāi bacana adharāmṛta…" (GPT1 p. 2, no. 2)
*Prologue (nandi) of the *Gaura-pada-tarangini*: having heard Radha tell of Her dream in which She saw a golden youth,
Krishna reveals to Her that He Himself will take that form: three desires — to know what Her prema is like, what its
sweetness is, and what happiness She tastes — were not fulfilled in Vraja; taking Her bhava and lustre, making Her prema
His guru, He will rise in Nadia.*[^13-1]

শুনইতে রাই-বচন অধরামৃত বিদগধ রসময় কান ।
আপনাক ভাবে ভাব প্রকাশিতে ধনী অনুমতি ভেল জান ॥

*śunaite rāi-bacana adharāmṛta bidagadha rasamaya kāna |*
*āpanāka bhābe bhāba prakāśite dhanī anumati bhela jāna ||*

*Word for word:* śunaite — hearing; rāi-bacana — Rai's words; adharāmṛta — nectar of the lips; bidagadha — clever; rasamaya — full of rasa; kāna — Kanu (Krishna); āpanāka bhābe — in His own self; bhāba prakāśite — to reveal the bhava; dhanī — the fair one (Radha); anumati bhela — consent was given; jāna — know

**1.1.** Hearing the nectar of Rai's words, the clever Kanu, full of rasa,
received, know it, the fair one's consent — to reveal Her bhava in His own self.[^13-2]

সুন্দরি যে কহিলে গৌর-স্বরূপ ।
কোই নাহি জানয়ে কেবল তুয়া প্রেম বিনা মোহে করবি হেন রূপ ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*sundari ye kahile gaura-svarūpa |*
*koi nāhi jānaye kebala tuyā prema binā mohe karabi hena rūpa || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* sundari — beautiful one; ye kahile — which you spoke of; gaura-svarūpa — the form of Gaura; koi nāhi jānaye — no one knows; kebala tuyā prema binā — except only your prema; mohe karabi — you will make Me; hena rūpa — such a form

**1.2.** "Beautiful one, the form of Gaura you have spoken of
no one knows: only by your prema will you make Me such."

কৈছন তুয়া প্রেমা কৈছন মধুরিমা কৈছন সুখে তুহুঁ ভোর ।
এ তিন বাঞ্ছিত ধন ব্রজে নহিল পূরণ কি কহব না পাইয়া ওর ॥

*kaichana tuyā premā kaichana madhurimā kaichana sukhe tuhum̐ bhora |*
*e tina bāñchita dhana braje nahila pūraṇa ki kahaba nā pāiyā ora ||*

*Word for word:* kaichana — what; tuyā premā — your prema; madhurimā — sweetness; kaichana sukhe — in what happiness; tuhum̐ bhora — you are absorbed; e tina bāñchita dhana — these three longed-for treasures; braje — in Vraja; nahila pūraṇa — were not fulfilled; ki kahaba — what shall I say; nā pāiyā ora — not finding the end

**1.3.** "What your prema is like, what its sweetness, in what happiness you are absorbed —
these three longed-for treasures were not fulfilled in Vraja; what can I say — I have found no end to them.[^13-3]

ভাবিয়া দেখিনু মনে তোহারি স্বরূপ বিনে এ সুখ আস্বাদ কভু নয় ।
তুয়া ভাব কান্তি ধরি তুয়া প্রেম গুরু করি নদীয়াতে করব উদয় ॥

*bhābiyā dekhinu mane tohāri svarūpa bine e sukha āsvāda kabhu naya |*
*tuyā bhāba kānti dhari tuyā prema guru kari nadīyāte karaba udaya ||*

*Word for word:* bhābiyā dekhinu mane — pondering I saw in My mind; tohāri svarūpa bine — without your form; e sukha — this joy; āsvāda kabhu naya — is never tasted; tuyā bhāba kānti dhari — taking your bhava and lustre; tuyā prema guru kari — making your prema guru; nadīyāte — in Nadia; karaba udaya — I shall rise

**1.4.** Having pondered, I have understood: except in your very form this joy can never be tasted.
Taking your bhava and lustre, making your prema My guru, I shall rise in Nadia.

সাধব মনের সাধা ঘুচাব মনের বাধা জগতে বিলাব প্রেম-ধন ।
বলরাম দাসে কয় প্রভু মোর দয়াময় না ভজিনু মুঞি নরাধম ॥

*sādhaba manera sādhā ghucāba manera bādhā jagate bilāba prema-dhana |*
*balarāma dāse kaya prabhu mora dayāmaya nā bhajinu muñi narādhama ||*

*Word for word:* sādhaba — I shall fulfil; manera sādhā — the heart's longing; ghucāba — I shall remove; manera bādhā — the heart's obstacle; jagate — in the world; bilāba — I shall distribute; prema-dhana — the treasure of prema; balarāma dāse kaya — Balarama Dasa says; prabhu mora dayāmaya — my Lord is merciful; nā bhajinu — did not worship; muñi narādhama — I, lowest of men

**1.5.** I shall fulfil My heart's longing, remove My heart's obstacle, distribute to the world the treasure of prema."
Balarama Dasa says: my Lord is all-merciful — and I, lowest of men, have not served Him.

[^13-1]: GPT1 — printed p. 2, section "Nandi, or Prelude" (nāndī vā pūrvābhāsa), no. 2, no raga given; checked against the IA scan
in.ernet.dli.2015.477854 (PDF p. 261); GPT2 — sec. 1.1, no. 2. The pada is not in the *Padakalpataru* (PK), the
*Bhakti-ratnakara* (BR), the *Kshanada-gita-chintamani* (KGC) or the *Padamrita-samudra* (PS). Padas nos. 2–4 are a dialogue
of Krishna and Radha continuing no. 1 (Radha's dream of a golden youth, signed by Jagadananda) and concluded by no. 5
(Vaishnava Dasa). Majumdar considers the GPT unreliable for attribution; padas of several poets are known under the
signature "Balarama Dasa," and this pada on the purpose of the Gaura-avatara contains nothing pointing to an eyewitness —
the attribution is provisional (C).
[^13-2]: Kanu (Kan) is Krishna. "To reveal Her bhava in Himself" is what Krishnadasa Kaviraja names as the cause of the
Gaura-avatara: Krishna, taking Radha's bhava and lustre, tastes His own sweetness (CC Adi 1.5–6; 4).
[^13-3]: The three desires — CC Adi 1.6 and 4: to know the greatness of Radha's love, the sweetness of Himself which Radha
tastes, and the happiness She feels. The poet puts this theological motif into Krishna's mouth almost word for word.

## 2. Balarama Dasa — "bām̐dhu he śunaite kām̐pai dehā…" (GPT1 p. 2, no. 3)
*Radha's reply: at this news Her body trembles — He is the life of Vraja; like a fish without water or a serpent
without its jewel, Vraja cannot live a moment without Him; will He, leaving Her, reveal prema with His brother and friends
on the bank of another river?*[^13-4]

বঁধু হে শুনইতে কাঁপই দেহা ।
তুহুঁ ব্রজ-জীবন তুয়া বিনু কৈছন ব্রজপুর বাঁধব থেহা ॥

*bam̐dhu he śunaite kām̐pai dehā |*
*tuhum̐ braja-jībana tuyā binu kaichana brajapura bām̐dhaba thehā ||*

*Word for word:* bām̐dhu he — O beloved; śunaite — hearing; kām̐pai dehā — the body trembles; tuhum̐ braja-jībana — You are the life of Vraja; tuyā binu — without You; kaichana — how; brajapura — Vraja; bām̐dhaba thehā — will keep its footing

**2.1.** "Beloved, hearing this my whole body trembles.
You are the life of Vraja: without You how will Vraja keep its footing?

জল বিনু মীন ফণী মণি বিনু তেজয়ে আপন পরাণ ।
তিল আধ তুহারি দরশ বিনু তৈছন ব্রজপুর-গতি তুহুঁ জান ॥

*jala binu mīna phaṇī maṇi binu tejaye āpana parāṇa |*
*tila ādha tuhāri daraśa binu taichana brajapura-gati tuhum̐ jāna ||*

*Word for word:* jala binu mīna — a fish without water; phaṇī maṇi binu — a serpent without its jewel; tejaye āpana parāṇa — gives up its own life; tila ādha — for half a sesame-seed's time (half a moment); tuhāri daraśa binu — without the sight of You; taichana — just so; brajapura-gati — the fate of Vraja; tuhum̐ jāna — You know

**2.2.** As a fish without water, as a serpent without its jewel gives up its life,
so Vraja without the sight of You for even half a moment — You know what its state will be.

সকল সমাধি কোন সিধি সাধবি পাওবি কোনহি সুখ ।
কিয়ে আন জন তুয়া মরমহি জানব ইথে লাগি বিদরয়ে বুক ॥

*sakala samādhi kona sidhi sādhabi pāobi konahi sukha |*
*kiye āna jana tuyā maramahi jānaba ithe lāgi bidaraye buka ||*

*Word for word:* sakala samādhi — having finished everything; kona sidhi sādhabi — what perfection will You attain; pāobi — will You gain; konahi sukha — what happiness; kiye — will; āna jana — other people; tuyā maramahi jānaba — know Your heart; ithe lāgi — for this; bidaraye buka — the breast is torn

**2.3.** Having finished everything, what perfection will You attain, what happiness will You find?
Will others know Your heart? For this my breast is torn.

বৃন্দাবন-কুঞ্জ নিকুঞ্জহি নিবসসি তুহুঁ বর-নাগর কান ।
অহনিশি তুহারি দরশ বিনু ঝুরব তেজব সবহুঁ পরাণ ॥

*bṛndābana-kuñja nikuñjahi nibasasi tuhum̐ bara-nāgara kāna |*
*ahaniśi tuhāri daraśa binu jhuraba tejaba sabahum̐ parāṇa ||*

*Word for word:* bṛndābana-kuñje — in the groves of Vrindavana; nikuñjahi — in the bowers; nibasasi — You dwell; tuhum̐ — You; bara-nāgara — best of lovers; kāna — Kanu; ahaniśi — day and night; tuhāri daraśa binu — without the sight of You; jhuraba — will pine; tejaba — will give up; sabahum̐ parāṇa — all their lives

**2.4.** You dwell in the groves and bowers of Vrindavana, You, Kanu, best of lovers;
day and night, without the sight of You, all will pine and give up their lives.

অগ্রজ সঙ্গে রঙ্গে যমুনা-তটে সখা সঞে করবি বিলাস ।
পাসরবি মুঝে কিয়ে প্রেম প্রকাশবি না বুঝয়ে বলরাম দাস ॥

*agraja saṅge raṅge yamunā-taṭe sakhā sañe karabi bilāsa |*
*pāsarabi mujhe kiye prema prakāśabi nā bujhaye balarāma dāsa ||*

*Word for word:* agraja saṅge — with the elder brother; raṅge — joyfully; yamunā-taṭe — on the Yamuna's bank; sakhā sañe — with friends; karabi bilāsa — You will sport; pāsarabi mujhe — You will forget me (GPT2: parihari — abandoning); kiye — will; prema prakāśabi — You reveal prema; nā bujhaye balarāma dāsa — Balarama Dasa does not understand

**2.5.** With Your elder brother, with Your friends You will sport on the river bank —
and forgetting me You will reveal prema?" Balarama Dasa does not understand.[^13-5]

[^13-4]: GPT1 — p. 2, no. 3, no raga (scan PDF p. 261); GPT2 — sec. 1.1, no. 3. In 2.5 GPT1 reads "pāsarabi mujhe" (you will forget
me), GPT2 "parihari mujhe" (abandoning me). Radha's anguish is not worldly sorrow but the highest prema (mahabhava) by which
Vraja lives; the fear of separation is inseparable from it (CC Madhya 2).
[^13-5]: "Elder brother" — Balarama, who appeared in the Gaura-lila as Nityananda; "friends" — the cowherd boys who became
the Lord's associates. The "river bank" (yamunātaṭa) is in the poem the bank of the Yamuna; in the Gaura-lila its place is
taken by the Ganga of Navadvipa. Radha's fear is answered by Krishna in the next pada: He will not leave Vraja (3.4) — in
Bhaktisiddhanta's teaching Navadvipa and Vraja are non-different, and Gaura is Radha and Krishna in one form (CC Adi
4.55–56).

## 3. Balarama Dasa — "śunaha sundari majhu abhilāṣa…" (GPT1 p. 2, no. 4)
*Krishna's reply: He will reveal the prema of Vraja; with all the cowherd men and boys He will sport in Nadia; the two
bodies will merge into one, and He will ceaselessly repeat Her name; He will never leave Vraja — without Vraja prema is
not attained.*[^13-6]

শুনহ সুন্দরি মঝু অভিলাষ ।
ব্রজপুর-প্রেম করব পরকাশ ॥

*śunaha sundari majhu abhilāṣa |*
*brajapura-prema karaba parakāśa ||*

*Word for word:* śunaha — hear; sundari — beautiful one; majhu abhilāṣa — My desire; brajapura-prema — the prema of Vraja; karaba parakāśa — I shall reveal

**3.1.** "Hear, beautiful one, My desire:
the prema of Vraja I shall reveal to the world.

গোপ গোপাল সব জন মেলি ।
নদীয়া-নগর পরে করবহুঁ কেলি ॥

*gopa gopāla saba jana meli |*
*nadīyā-nagara pare karabahum̐ keli ||*

*Word for word:* gopa gopāla — cowherd men and boys; saba jana meli — gathering all; nadīyā-nagara pare — in the town of Nadia; karabahum̐ keli — I shall sport

**3.2.** Gathering all the cowherd men and boys,
in the town of Nadia I shall begin My play.

তনু তনু মেলি হোই এক ঠাম ।
অবিরত বদনে বোলব তব নাম ॥

*tanu tanu meli hoi eka ṭhāma |*
*abirata badane bolaba taba nāma ||*

*Word for word:* tanu tanu meli — the bodies joining; hoi eka ṭhāma — becoming one; abirata — ceaselessly; badane — with My lips; bolaba — I shall utter; taba nāma — your name

**3.3.** Our bodies, joined, will become one,
and My lips will ceaselessly repeat your name.

ব্রজপুর পরিহরি কবহুঁ না যাব ।
ব্রজ বিনু প্রেম না হোয়ব লাভ ॥

*brajapura parihari kabahum̐ nā yāba |*
*braja binu prema nā hoyaba lābha ||*

*Word for word:* brajapura parihari — abandoning Vraja; kabahum̐ nā yāba — I shall never go; braja binu — without Vraja; prema nā hoyaba lābha — prema will not be attained

**3.4.** Leaving Vraja, I shall never go away:
without Vraja prema is not attained.

ব্রজপুর-ভাবে পূরব মন-কাম ।
অনুভবি জানল দাস বলরাম ॥

*brajapura-bhābe pūraba mana-kāma |*
*anubhabi jānala dāsa balarāma ||*

*Word for word:* brajapura-bhābe — with the bhava of Vraja; pūraba — I shall fulfil; mana-kāma — the heart's desire; anubhabi — realizing; jānala — knew; dāsa balarāma — Balarama Dasa

**3.5.** With the bhava of Vraja I shall fulfil My heart's desire" —
this Balarama Dasa has known by realization.[^13-7]

[^13-6]: GPT1 — p. 2, no. 4, no raga (scan PDF p. 261; the last line is smudged in the scan, the reading "anubhabi jānala" is
confirmed by GPT2); GPT2 — sec. 1.1, no. 4.
[^13-7]: "Two bodies will become one" — Gaura is Radha and Krishna united in one form (CC Adi 1.5; 4.55); "repeat Her name" —
the Lord in Navadvipa and Puri cries "Radha, Radha!" "The heart's desire" (mana-kāma) is the thirst to taste Radha's love,
not worldly lust.

## 4. Vasu Ghosha (in GPT1 — Balarama Dasa) — "purabe bāndhila cūṛā ebe keśa-hīna…" (PK 2255; GPT1 p. 18, no. 47)
*The Lord's sannyasa as Krishna's transformation: formerly He tied His hair in a top-knot — now His head is shaven;
instead of the milk-pail in His left hand — the sannyasi's water-pot; in the Treta-yuga He held the bow, in the
Dvapara the flute, in the Kali-yuga He took the staff; Balarama has become an avadhuta, Kanai a sannyasi. Raga
gandhara.*[^13-8]

পুরবে বান্ধিল চূড়া এবে কেশ-হীন ।
নটবর-বেশ ছাড়ি পরিলা কৌপীন ॥

*purabe bāndhila cūṛā ebe keśa-hīna |*
*naṭabara-beśa chāṛi parilā kaupīna ||*

*Word for word:* purabe — formerly; bāndhila cūṛā — tied a top-knot; ebe — now; keśa-hīna — without hair; naṭabara-beśa — the dress of the best of dancers; chāṛi — leaving; parilā kaupīna — put on the kaupina

**4.1.** Formerly He tied His hair in a top-knot — now He is without hair;
leaving the dress of the best of dancers, He has put on the kaupina.

গাবি-দোহন-ভাণ্ড ছিল বাম করে ।
করঙ্গ ধরিলা গোরা সেই অনুসারে ॥

*gābi-dohana-bhāṇḍa chila bāma kare |*
*karaṅga dharilā gorā sei anusāre ||*

*Word for word:* gābi-dohana-bhāṇḍa — the pail for milking cows; chila bāma kare — was in the left hand; karaṅga — the sannyasi's water-pot; dharilā gorā — Gora took; sei anusāre — after that pattern

**4.2.** A pail for milking the cows was in His left hand —
after that very pattern Gora has taken the sannyasi's water-pot.[^13-9]

ত্রেতায় ধরিল ধনু দ্বাপরেত বাঁশী ।
কলিযুগে দণ্ড ধরি হইলা সন্ন্যাসী ॥

*tretāya dharila dhanu dvāpareta bām̐śī |*
*kaliyuge daṇḍa dhari hailā sannyāsī ||*

*Word for word:* tretāya — in the Treta-yuga; dharila dhanu — held the bow; dvāpareta — in the Dvapara; bām̐śī — the flute; kaliyuge — in the Kali-yuga; daṇḍa dhari — taking the staff; hailā sannyāsī — became a sannyasi

**4.3.** In the Treta-yuga He held the bow, in the Dvapara the flute;
in the Kali-yuga, taking the staff, He has become a sannyasi.

বাসুঘোষ কহে শুন নদীয়া-নিবাসী ।
বলরাম অবধৌত কানাই সন্ন্যাসী ॥

*bāsughoṣa kahe śuna nadīyā-nibāsī |*
*balarāma abadhauta kānāi sannyāsī ||*

*Word for word:* bāsughoṣa kahe — Vasu Ghosha says (GPT1: balarāma kahe — Balarama says); śuna — listen; nadīyā-nibāsī — people of Nadia; balarāma — Balarama; abadhauta — avadhuta; kānāi — Kanai (Krishna); sannyāsī — sannyasi

**4.4.** Vasu Ghosha says: listen, people of Nadia:
Balarama is an avadhuta, Kanai a sannyasi![^13-10]

[^13-8]: PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 288 (printed p. 277), 21st pallava "The sannyasa of Sri Gauranga, etc.," label "॥৩৮॥২২৫৫॥", raga
gandhara, MS P-R-Sa no. 2310 — signed by **Vasu Ghosha** (4.4: "bāsughoṣa kahe…"). GPT1 — p. 18, section "Mangalacharana,"
no. 47 (gandhara), checked against the scan (PDF p. 277): the same pada, but in 4.4 "balarāma kahe śuna nadīyānibāsī," i.e. signed by
Balarama; the compiler of GPT1 himself noted that a manuscript and PK ascribe it to Vasu Ghosha. GPT2 — sec. 1.2, no. 47.
The pada was missing from the stage-1 catalogue (new row); the attribution to Vasu Ghosha (per PK) is preferable: the
signature "Balaram" in GPT1 probably arose from the second half of 4.4, where Balarama's name refers to Nityananda.
[^13-9]: Kaupina — the loincloth of the renunciant; karanga (karaṅga) — the sannyasi's water-pot (kamandalu). The poet sets the
marks of Krishna the cowherd beside those of Gaura the sannyasi: the milk-pail in His left hand has "become" the water-pot.
[^13-10]: Avadhuta — a renunciant above outward rules; so Nityananda was called, who is Balarama (CC Adi 5; CB Adi 9). Kanai
(Kanu) is Krishna, appearing as Gauranga. The Lord's sannyasa is not the renunciation of a conditioned soul but a lila
for the deliverance of the people of Kali-yuga (CC Adi 17; CB Madhya 26).

## 5. Balarama Dasa (in PK — "Natavara") — "gopīgaṇa-kuca-kuṅkume bañcita…" (PK 2250; GPT1 p. 18, no. 48)
*Wonder at the Lord's sannyasa: He whom the maidens of Vraja embraced, whose body was coloured with their kunkuma, is
now in saffron cloth, covered with thrills, with streams of tears of prema; the dark-bodied Dancer of Vrindavana has
become a pauper begging prema from house to house. Raga dhanashi (in GPT1 — kedara).*[^13-11]

গোপীগণ-কুচ-কুঙ্কুমে বঞ্চিত অরুণ বসন শোভে অঙ্গে ।
কাঞ্চন-নিন্দিত কান্তি কলেবর রাই-পরশ-রস-রঙ্গে ॥

*gopīgaṇa-kuca-kuṅkume bañcita aruṇa basana śobhe aṅge |*
*kāñcana-nindita kānti kalebara rāi-paraśa-rasa-raṅge ||*

*Word for word:* gopīgaṇa-kuca-kuṅkume — of the kunkuma of the gopis' breasts; bañcita — bereft (GPT1: rañjita — coloured); aruṇa basana — ruddy cloth; śobhe aṅge — shines on the body; kāñcana-nindita — putting gold to shame; kānti — lustre; kalebara — body; rāi-paraśa-rasa-raṅge — by the joy of Rai's touch

**5.1.** Bereft of the kunkuma from the gopis' breasts, He has a ruddy cloth shining on His body;
His body, whose lustre puts gold to shame, is from the joy of Rai's touch.[^13-12]

দেখ দেখ অপরূপ গৌর-বিলাস ।
লাখ যুবতি-রতি যো গুরু লম্পট সো অব করল সন্ন্যাস ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*dekha dekha aparūpa gaura-bilāsa |*
*lākha yubati-rati yo guru lampaṭa so aba karala sannyāsa || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* dekha dekha — look, look; aparūpa — wondrous; gaura-bilāsa — the play of Gaura; lākha yubati-rati — of the love of hundreds of thousands of young maidens; yo guru lampaṭa — who was the foremost lover (teacher of love); so aba — he now; karala sannyāsa — has taken sannyasa

**5.2.** Look, look — the wondrous play of Gaura!
He who was the teacher of love to hundreds of thousands of young maidens has now taken sannyasa.[^13-13]

যো ব্রজ-বধূগণ দৃঢ় ভুজ-বন্ধন অবিরত রহত অগোর ।
সো তনু পুলকে পূরিত অব ঢর ঢর নয়নে গলয়ে প্রেম-লোর ॥

*yo braja-badhūgaṇa dṛṛha bhuja-bandhana abirata rahata agora |*
*so tanu pulake pūrita aba ḍhara ḍhara nayane galaye prema-lora ||*

*Word for word:* yo — whom; braja-badhūgaṇa — the maidens of Vraja; dṛṛha bhuja-bandhana — in the firm bond of arms; abirata — ceaselessly; rahata agora — held enclosed; so tanu — that body; pulake pūrita — filled with thrills; aba — now; ḍhara ḍhara — streaming; nayane — from the eyes; galaye prema-lora — tears of prema flow

**5.3.** He whom the maidens of Vraja ceaselessly held in their firm embrace
is now all thrilling with goosebumps, and tears of prema stream from His eyes.

যো নটবর ঘন-শ্যাম-কলেবর বৃন্দা-বিপিন-বিহারী ।
কহয়ে নটবর সো অব অকিঞ্চন ঘরে ঘরে প্রেম-ভিখারী ॥

*yo naṭabara ghana-śyāma-kalebara bṛndā-bipina-bihārī |*
*kahaye naṭabara so aba akiñcana ghare ghare prema-bhikhārī ||*

*Word for word:* yo naṭabara — that best of dancers; ghana-śyāma-kalebara — with a body dark as a rain-cloud; bṛndā-bipina-bihārī — roaming the forest of Vrinda; kahaye naṭabara — says Natavara (P-R-Sa, GPT1: balarāma — Balarama); so aba — he now; akiñcana — a pauper; ghare ghare — from house to house; prema-bhikhārī — a beggar of prema

**5.4.** That best of dancers, with a body dark as a rain-cloud, who roamed the forest of Vrinda —
says Natavara — now, a pauper, begs prema from house to house.[^13-14]

[^13-11]: PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 286 (printed p. 275), 21st pallava, label "॥৩৩॥২২৫০॥", raga dhanashi, MSS P-R-Sa no. 2355 and P-R no. 12 —
signature "kahaye naṭabara" (according to Ray's apparatus, P-R-Sa reads "balarāma"). GPT1 — pp. 18–19, no. 48 (kedara), checked
against the scan (PDF p. 277): "kahaye balarāma naṭabara so aba…" — signed by Balarama. GPT2 — sec. 1.2, no. 48. In PK the pada follows
PK 2249 of Balarama (chapter 11, no. 16), where it was noted that PK 2250 is signed "Natavara" and had not been
translated; it was missing from the catalogue (new row). Attribution to Balarama — per P-R-Sa and GPT1 (C).
[^13-12]: The first half-line in PK reads "kuṅkume bañcita" ("bereft of the kunkuma"): formerly Krishna's body was ruddy with the
gopis' kunkuma, now the sannyasi's cloth is ruddy; GPT1 reads "kuṅkume rañjita" ("coloured with kunkuma"). Gaura's golden
lustre comes from Radha's touch: He has taken Her complexion (CC Adi 4).
[^13-13]: "Guru-lampata" (guru lampaṭa) — literally "the foremost of lovers": the language of madhurya-rasa. The gopis' love for
Krishna is not worldly passion but the purest prema, only called "kama" (CC Madhya 8; Adi 4.165–171); the contrast in the
pada stresses that the same Krishna, the Lord of Vraja, has become a renunciant.
[^13-14]: "Natavara" — in PK apparently the poet's name (or an epithet of Krishna taken by a scribe for a signature); in P-R-Sa
and GPT1 — "Balarama." "A beggar of prema" — the Lord, who Himself distributes prema, in the mood of a devotee begs it of
everyone (CC Adi 7).

## 6. Yadunatha Dasa — "gaura-baraṇa tanu sundara sukhamaya…" (PK 2180; GPT1 p. 36, no. 28)
*Gaura and Gadadhara in Navadvipa: a golden body full of bliss, a heart full of compassion; at Gaura's left is the
beloved Gadadhara, and the hidden rasa is revealed, as if the circle of the rasa; in Nadia there are so many moons that the
darkness has gone far away; Gaura and Gadadhara are a lake of prema that has overflowed the earth. Raga the same as that of
the preceding PK pada (in GPT1 — kamoda).*[^13-15]

গৌর-বরণ তনু সুন্দর সুখময় সদয়-হৃদয় রসাল রে ।
কুন্দ করবির গাঁথন থরে-থর দোলনি বনি বন-মাল রে ॥

*gaura-baraṇa tanu sundara sukhamaya sadaya-hṛdaya rasāla re |*
*kunda karabira gām̐thana thare-thara dolani bani bana-māla re ||*

*Word for word:* gaura-baraṇa tanu — a golden-hued body; sundara — beautiful; sukhamaya — full of bliss (GPT1: sudhāmaya — full of nectar); sadaya-hṛdaya — a compassionate heart; rasāla — abode of rasa; re — (refrain particle); kunda karabira — of jasmine and oleander; gām̐thana thare-thara — woven row upon row; dolani — swaying; bani bana-māla — a forest garland

**6.1.** A golden-hued body — beautiful, full of bliss; a compassionate heart — an abode of rasa;
a garland of jasmine and oleander, woven row upon row, sways — a forest garland.

গৌর-বামে বর প্রিয় গদাধর নিগুঢ় রস পরকাশ রে ।
রাস-মণ্ডল ঐছে ভানল প্রেমে গদ গদ ভাষ রে ॥

*gaura-bāme bara priya gadādhara niguṛha rasa parakāśa re |*
*rāsa-maṇḍala aiche bhānala preme gada gada bhāṣa re ||*

*Word for word:* gaura-bāme — at Gaura's left; bara — the best; priya gadādhara — beloved Gadadhara; niguṛha rasa — the hidden rasa; parakāśa — revealed; rāsa-maṇḍala — the circle of the rasa; aiche — as if; bhānala — shone forth; preme — with prema; gada gada bhāṣa — faltering speech

**6.2.** At Gaura's left is the best one, the beloved Gadadhara: the hidden rasa is revealed;
as if the circle of the rasa had shone forth — and their speech falters with prema.[^13-16]

নদিয়া-নগরে চাঁদ কত কত দূরে গেও অন্ধিয়ার রে ।
কতহুঁ উয়ল দীপ নিরমল ইথেহুঁ লখই না পার রে ॥

*nadiyā-nagare cām̐da kata kata dūre geo andhiyāra re |*
*katahum̐ uyala dīpa niramala ithehum̐ lakhai nā pāra re ||*

*Word for word:* nadiyā-nagare — in the town of Nadia; cām̐da kata kata — so many moons; dūre geo — has gone far; andhiyāra — the darkness; katahum̐ — however many; uyala — have risen (been lit); dīpa niramala — spotless lamps; ithehum̐ — even these; lakhai nā pāra — cannot be discerned

**6.3.** In the town of Nadia so many moons — the darkness has gone far away;
however many spotless lamps are lit — beside them they cannot even be discerned.

গৌর গদাধর প্রেম-সরোবর উথলি মহিতল পূর রে ।
দাস যদুনাথ বিধি-বিড়ম্বিত পরশ না পাই ঝুর রে ॥

*gaura gadādhara prema-sarobara uthali mahitala pūra re |*
*dāsa yadunātha bidhi-biṛambita paraśa nā pāi jhura re ||*

*Word for word:* gaura gadādhara — Gaura and Gadadhara; prema-sarobara — a lake of prema; uthali — overflowing; mahitala pūra — filled the earth; dāsa yadunātha — Dasa Yadunatha; bidhi-biṛambita — cheated by fate; paraśa nā pāi — not getting a touch; jhura — weeps

**6.4.** Gaura and Gadadhara are a lake of prema: overflowing, it has filled the earth;
Dasa Yadunatha, cheated by fate, not getting even a touch of it, weeps.[^13-17]

[^13-15]: PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 261 (printed p. 250), label "॥১৩॥২১৮০॥", raga "tathā" (the same as PK 2179), MS P-R-Sa no. 2288. GPT1 — p. 36,
no. 28 (kamoda), checked against the scan (PDF p. 295); GPT2 — sec. 3.1 (OCR, line 25224). In the catalogue (YD-006) the pada was
listed as "GPT only"; it is found in PK — **core**. In PK it stands among Nayanananda's padas on Gaura and Gadadhara. On Yadunatha
Dasa (Kavichandra), a fellow villager of Jagannatha Mishra, see the catalogue (CB Madhya 1; CC Adi 11); other padas signed
"Yadunatha Dasa" in PK are PK 2125, 2126, 2191 (chapter 6).
[^13-16]: Gadadhara Pandita is the Lord's eternal associate, in whom Vaishnavas see a manifestation of Radha (GGD 147–153); the
"hidden rasa" is their prema, not worldly intimacy. The "circle of the rasa" is the image of Krishna's rasa-lila showing
through the kirtana of Gaura and Gadadhara.
[^13-17]: "Cheated by fate" is the usual formula of humility in a poet's signature.

## 7. Balarama Dasa — "yata yata abatāra-sāra…" (PK 2346; GPT1 p. 38, no. 37)
*Praise of the Gaura-avatara: among all incarnations the incarnation of Gora is renowned; prema for Krishna, inaccessible
even to Brahma, the Lord distributed down to the chandalas; the flood of prema has drowned foreigners and unbelievers, beasts
and birds sing and weep in kirtana — only Balarama has been left out. Raga bhatiyari.*[^13-18]

যত যত অবতার-সার ।
ঘুষিতে রহিল আমার গোরা অবতার ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*yata yata abatāra-sāra |*
*ghuṣite rahila āmāra gorā abatāra || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* yata yata — of all and all; abatāra-sāra — the essence of incarnations; ghuṣite rahila — remained proclaimed; āmāra gorā abatāra — my incarnation of Gora

**7.1.** Of all and all the incarnations the essence —
renowned has remained my incarnation of Gora!

ব্রহ্মার দুর্লভ কৃষ্ণ-প্রেম নাম-ধন ।
আচণ্ডালে দিয়া পহু ভরিল ভুবন ॥

*brahmāra durlabha kṛṣṇa-prema nāma-dhana |*
*ācaṇḍāle diyā pahu bharila bhubana ||*

*Word for word:* brahmāra durlabha — hard for even Brahma to obtain; kṛṣṇa-prema — prema for Krishna; nāma-dhana — the treasure of the Name; ācaṇḍāle diyā — giving down to the chandalas; pahu — the Lord; bharila bhubana — filled the world

**7.2.** Prema for Krishna and the treasure of the Name, hard for even Brahma to obtain,
the Lord gave down to the chandalas and filled the world with them.

ম্লেচ্ছ পাষণ্ড আদি প্রেমের বন্যায় ।
ডুবিয়া সকল লোক হাসে নাচে গায় ॥

*mleccha pāṣaṇḍa ādi premera banyāya |*
*ḍubiyā sakala loka hāse nāce gāya ||*

*Word for word:* mleccha — foreigners; pāṣaṇḍa — unbelievers; ādi — and others; premera banyāya — in the flood of prema; ḍubiyā — immersed; sakala loka — all people; hāse nāce gāya — laugh, dance, sing

**7.3.** In the flood of prema foreigners, unbelievers and the rest —
all people, immersed, laugh, dance and sing.

পশু পক্ষী ব্যাঘ্র মৃগ জলচরগণে ।
হাসে কান্দে নাচে গায় করয়ে কীর্তনে ॥

*paśu pakṣī byāghra mṛga jalacaragaṇe |*
*hāse kānde nāce gāya karaye kīrtane ||*

*Word for word:* paśu pakṣī — beasts and birds; byāghra mṛga — tigers and deer; jalacaragaṇe — the creatures of the waters; hāse kānde nāce gāya — laugh, weep, dance, sing; karaye kīrtane — perform kirtana

**7.4.** Beasts and birds, tigers, deer, the creatures of the waters
laugh, weep, dance, sing and perform kirtana.

স্বর্গ মর্ত্য পাতাল ডুবিল গোরা-প্রেমে ।
বঞ্চিত হইল একা দাস বলরামে ॥

*svarga martya pātāla ḍubila gorā-preme |*
*bañcita haila ekā dāsa balarāme ||*

*Word for word:* svarga martya pātāla — heaven, earth and the netherworlds; ḍubila — have drowned; gorā-preme — in prema for Gora (GPT1: saba grāme — all the villages); bañcita haila — was left out; ekā — alone; dāsa balarāma — Dasa Balarama

**7.5.** Heaven, earth and the netherworlds have drowned in prema for Gora —
left out has been only Dasa Balarama.

[^13-18]: PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 320 (printed p. 309), 23rd pallava, label "॥১৫॥২৩৪৬॥", raga bhatiyari, MS P-R-Sa no. 2450; it is followed in PK by
PK 2347 (chapter 12, no. 1). GPT1 — p. 38, no. 37 (bhatiyari), checked against the scan (PDF p. 297); GPT2 — sec. 1.3, no. 37. In the
catalogue (BD-009) the pada was listed as "GPT only"; it is found in PK — **core** (C). A chandala is an outcaste beyond the
varnas; the gift of prema to all without distinction — CC Adi 7; CB Madhya 13.

## 8. Balarama Dasa — "saba abatāra sāra gorā abatāra…" (PK 2201; GPT1 p. 38, no. 39)
*Praise of the Gaura-avatara: such mercy there has never been; the Lord, entreating, gave prema to the humble and fallen;
whoever does not serve such a treasure of mercy drinks poison with his own hands and will not be saved even in millions of
kalpas. Raga shri.*[^13-19]

সব অবতার-সার গোরা অবতার ।
এমন করুণা কভু না দেখিয়ে আর ॥

*saba abatāra-sāra gorā abatāra |*
*emana karuṇā kabhu nā dekhiye āra ||*

*Word for word:* saba abatāra-sāra — the essence of all incarnations; gorā abatāra — the incarnation of Gora; emana karuṇā — such mercy; kabhu nā dekhiye āra — is never seen elsewhere

**8.1.** The essence of all incarnations is the incarnation of Gora:
such mercy is seen nowhere else.

দীন হীন অধম পতিত জনে জনে ।
যাচিঞা যাচিঞা পহু দিলা প্রেম-ধনে ॥

*dīna hīna adhama patita jane jane |*
*yāciñā yāciñā pahu dilā prema-dhane ||*

*Word for word:* dīna hīna — to the humble and destitute; adhama — the low; patita — the fallen; jane jane — to each one; yāciñā yāciñā — entreating and entreating; pahu — the Lord; dilā prema-dhane — gave the treasure of prema

**8.2.** To the humble, the destitute, the low, the fallen — to each one
the Lord, entreating and entreating, gave the treasure of prema.

এমন দয়ার নিধি যেবা না ভজিল ।
আপনার হাতে তুলি গরল খাইল ॥

*emana dayāra nidhi yebā nā bhajila |*
*āpanāra hāte tuli garala khāila ||*

*Word for word:* emana dayāra nidhi — such a treasure of mercy; yebā nā bhajila — whoever did not serve; āpanāra hāte tuli — lifting with his own hand; garala khāila — drank poison

**8.3.** Whoever does not serve such a treasure of mercy
has lifted poison with his own hand and drunk it.

যে জন বঞ্চিত হৈল হেন অবতারে ।
কোটি কলপে তার নাহিক উদ্ধারে ॥

*ye jana bañcita haila hena abatāre |*
*koṭi kalape tāra nāhika uddhāre ||*

*Word for word:* ye jana — whoever; bañcita haila — was left out; hena abatāre — at such an incarnation; koṭi kalape — even in millions of kalpas; tāra nāhika uddhāre — there is no deliverance for him

**8.4.** Whoever has been left out at such an incarnation
will find no deliverance even in millions of kalpas.

মুঞি সে অধম হেন পহুঁ না ভজিয়া ।
কহে বলরাম এবে মরিনু পুড়িয়া ॥

*muñi se adhama hena pahum̐ nā bhajiyā |*
*kahe balarāma ebe marinu puṛiyā ||*

*Word for word:* muñi se adhama — I, the low one; hena pahu — such a Lord; nā bhajiyā — not serving; kahe balarāma — says Balarama; ebe — now; marinu puṛiyā — I perish, burning

**8.5.** And I, low as I am, have not served such a Lord —
says Balarama: now I am burning and perishing.[^13-20]

[^13-19]: GPT1 — p. 38, no. 39 (shri), checked against the scan (PDF p. 297); GPT2 — sec. 1.3, no. 39. **The pada is in PK — PK 2201**
(vol. 3, 20th pallava "Śrī-Gauracandra — prakārāntara," PDF p. 269, printed p. 258, label "॥১৮॥২২০১॥", raga "tathā", MS P-R-Sa no. 2309) —
with the same signature of Balarama ("…kahe balarāma ebe marinu puṛiyā" — "now I am burning"). The earlier statement that 8.1–8.4 are
the beginning of Lochana Dasa's pada PK 2203 was mistaken: PK 2203 begins "ke yābe ke yābe bhāi bhaba-sindhu pāra" (MS P-R-Sa
no. 2311) and merely stands near this pada (corrected in the full PK check, chapter 16). Balarama's signature is attested both in PK and
in GPT — C. The pada was missing from the stage-1 catalogue (row BD-045).
[^13-20]: "Burning and perishing" (PK: marinu puṛiyā; GPT: paṛiyā — "fallen and perishing") is a formula of penitence in the signature (cf. 7.5); the poet speaks of himself, not of the Lord.

## 9. Balarama Dasa — "nabadvīpa-gagane uyala dina rāti…" (PK 2196; GPT1 p. 39, no. 40)
*Gaura as a rain-cloud: in the sky of Navadvipa a cloud stands day and night, watering all that lives; a downpour of the
nectar of prema; foul weather has covered the world; the peacock-devotees dance, the frog-non-devotees croak in the water;
the creeper of bhakti has overspread the three worlds; the lightning of kirtana has burnt the forest of yoga, the thunder
has split knowledge; the serpent of karma is driven out, the chataka is satisfied; the earth has drowned — only Balarama
is left on the mountain of samsara. Raga kamoda.*[^13-21]

নবদ্বীপ-গগনে উয়ল দিন রাতি ।
ঘন-রসে সেচল থির-চর জাতি ॥

*nabadvīpa-gagane uyala dina rāti |*
*ghana-rase secala thira-cara jāti ||*

*Word for word:* nabadvīpa-gagane — in the sky of Navadvipa; uyala — rose; dina rāti — day and night; ghana-rase — with the cloud's rain of rasa; secala — watered; thira-cara jāti — beings unmoving and moving (GPT1: sthalacara — land-dwelling)

**9.1.** In the sky of Navadvipa a cloud has risen and stays day and night:
with a downpour of rasa it has watered all that lives — the unmoving and the moving.

দেখ দেখ গৌর জলদ-অবতার ।
বরিখয়ে প্রেম-অমিয়া অনিবার ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*dekha dekha gaura jalada-abatāra |*
*barikhaye prema-amiyā anibāra || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* dekha dekha — look, look; gaura — Gaura; jalada-abatāra — the incarnation of a rain-cloud; barikhaye — rains; prema-amiyā — the nectar of prema; anibāra — ceaselessly

**9.2.** Look, look: Gaura is the incarnation of a cloud,
ceaselessly raining the nectar of prema!

তব ধরি জগ ভরি দুরদিন ডোর ।
হরি-রসে ডগমগ জগ-জন ভোর ॥

*taba dhari jaga bhari duradina ḍora |*
*hari-rase ḍagamaga jaga-jana bhora ||*

*Word for word:* taba dhari — since then; jaga bhari — the whole world; duradina — foul weather; ḍora — wraps; hari-rase — with the rasa of Hari; ḍagamaga — swaying (intoxicated); jaga-jana — the people of the world; bhora — lost to themselves

**9.3.** Since then the whole world is wrapped in foul weather;
with the rasa of Hari the people of the world, intoxicated, have forgotten themselves.

নাচত উনমত ভকত-ময়ূর ।
অভকত-ভেক রোয়ত জলে বুর ॥

*nācata unamata bhakata-mayūra |*
*abhakata-bheka royata jale bura ||*

*Word for word:* nācata — dance; unamata — in frenzy; bhakata-mayūra — the peacock-devotees; abhakata-bheka — the frog-non-devotees; royata — wail (croak); jale bura — sunk in the water

**9.4.** In frenzy the peacock-devotees dance;
the non-devotees — the frogs — croak, sunk in the water.[^13-22]

ভকতি-লতা তিন ভুবনে বেয়াপ ।
উত্তম অধম প্রেম-ফল পাব ॥

*bhakati-latā tina bhubane beyāpa |*
*uttama adhama prema-phala pāba ||*

*Word for word:* bhakati-latā — the creeper of bhakti; tina bhubane — over the three worlds; beyāpa — has spread; uttama adhama — high and low; prema-phala pāba — received the fruit of prema

**9.5.** The creeper of bhakti has overspread the three worlds:
the fruit of prema the high and the low have received.

কীর্তন-কুলিশে যোগ-বন জারি ।
জ্ঞান সেও ঘন-গরজে বিদারি ॥

*kīrtana-kuliśe yoga-bana jāri |*
*jñāna seo ghana-garaje bidāri ||*

*Word for word:* kīrtana-kuliśe — with the thunderbolt of kirtana; yoga-bana — the forest of yoga; jāri — burning; jñāna seo — knowledge too; ghana-garaje — with the cloud's thunder; bidāri — splitting

**9.6.** With the thunderbolt of kirtana the forest of yoga is burnt,
and knowledge too the cloud's thunder splits apart.

চিত-বিল-নিকষিল করম-ভুজঙ্গ ।
নিরসল কলি-মদ-দহন-তরঙ্গ ॥

*cita-bila-nikaṣila karama-bhujaṅga |*
*nirasala kali-mada-dahana-taraṅga ||*

*Word for word:* cita-bila — from the hole of the heart; nikaṣila — was driven out; karama-bhujaṅga — the serpent of karma; nirasala — subsided; kali-mada-dahana-taraṅga — the waves of Kali's burning intoxication

**9.7.** From the hole of the heart the serpent of karma is driven out;
the waves of Kali's burning intoxication have subsided.

তাপিত-চাতক তিরপিত ভেল ।
দশ দিশ সবহুঁ নদিয়া বহি গেল ॥

*tāpita-cātaka tirapita bhela |*
*daśa diśa sabahum̐ nadiyā bahi gela ||*

*Word for word:* tāpita-cātaka — the scorched chataka; tirapita bhela — was satisfied; daśa diśa sabahum̐ — in all ten directions; nadiyā bahi gela — rivers flowed

**9.8.** The scorched chataka has drunk its fill;
in all ten directions rivers have flowed.

ডুবল অবনি কাহু নাহি ঠাম ।
সংসারাচলে রহু বলরাম ॥

*ḍubala abani kāhu nāhi ṭhāma |*
*saṃsārācale rahu balarāma ||*

*Word for word:* ḍubala abani — the earth drowned; kāhu nāhi ṭhāma — no place for anyone; saṃsārācale — on the mountain of samsara; rahu — remained; balarāma — Balarama

**9.9.** The earth has drowned, for no one is there any dry place —
on the mountain of samsara only Balarama is left.[^13-23]

[^13-21]: PK: vol. 3, PDF pp. 266–267 (printed pp. 255–256), 20th pallava, label "॥১৩॥২১৯৬॥", raga kamoda, MS P-R-Sa no. 2304. GPT1 — p. 39,
no. 40 (kamoda), checked against the scan (PDF p. 298); GPT2 — sec. 1.3, no. 40. The pada was missing from the catalogue (new row); **core** (PK, C).
**core** (PK, C).
[^13-22]: Images of the rainy season: peacocks dance at the sight of clouds, frogs croak in the water; so the Bhagavata describes the
rains in Vraja (Bhag. 10.20), and the poet transfers the images to Gaura's kirtana. "Croak" (royata) — literally "weep, wail."
[^13-23]: The chataka is a bird that drinks only rainwater — an image of the soul thirsting only for prema. "Rivers" (nadiyā) puns on
the name Nadia. "The mountain of samsara" — the poet is left "high and dry," not washed by the flood of prema (cf. 7.5).

## 10. Ananta (Raya Ananta?) — "gaura nabaghana premadhārā bariṣila…" (GPT1 p. 40, no. 44)
*Gaura's mercy as husbandry: the young cloud Gaura has rained down prema; the hard soil of evil thoughts is broken by the
ploughing of bhakti, and prema has sprouted in hearts; Nitai waters the shoot with the water of bhakti, and the tree of prema
grows day by day, bearing fruit for all. Raga suhai.*[^13-24]

গৌর নবঘন প্রেম-ধারা বরিষিল ।
তৃষিত তাপিত জীব তিরপিত ভেল ॥

*gaura nabaghana prema-dhārā bariṣila |*
*tṛṣita tāpita jība tirapita bhela ||*

*Word for word:* gaura nabaghana — Gaura, the young cloud; prema-dhārā bariṣila — rained streams of prema; tṛṣita tāpita jība — thirsty, scorched souls; tirapita bhela — were satisfied

**10.1.** Gaura, a young rain-cloud, has poured down streams of prema:
thirsty, scorched souls have drunk their fill.

দুর্মতি কঠিন মাটী ভক্তি-চাষে চূর ।
উপজিল জীব-হৃদে প্রেমের অঙ্কুর ॥

*durmati kaṭhina māṭī bhakti-cāṣe cūra |*
*upajila jība-hṛde premera aṅkura ||*

*Word for word:* durmati — of evil thoughts; kaṭhina māṭī — hard soil; bhakti-cāṣe — by the tillage of bhakti; cūra — broken; upajila — sprang up; jība-hṛde — in the hearts of living beings; premera aṅkura — a shoot of prema

**10.2.** The hard soil of evil thoughts is broken by the tillage of bhakti —
in the hearts of living beings a shoot of prema has sprung up.

সে অঙ্কুরে ভক্তি-বারি নিতাই সেচিল ।
দিনে দিনে প্রেম-তরু বাড়িয়া উঠিল ॥

*se aṅkure bhakti-bāri nitāi secila |*
*dine dine prema-taru bāṛiyā uṭhila ||*

*Word for word:* se aṅkure — that shoot; bhakti-bāri — with the water of bhakti; nitāi secila — Nitai watered; dine dine — day by day; prema-taru — the tree of prema; bāṛiyā uṭhila — grew up

**10.3.** That shoot Nitai watered with the water of bhakti,
and day by day the tree of prema grew higher.

ধরিল প্রেমের ফল সব জীব-তরে ।
অনন্ত বঞ্চিত ভেল নিজ কর্ম-ফেরে ॥

*dharila premera phala saba jība-tare |*
*ananta bañcita bhela nija karma-phere ||*

*Word for word:* dharila — bore; premera phala — fruits of prema; saba jība-tare — for all living beings; ananta — Ananta; bañcita bhela — was left out; nija karma-phere — by the turns of his own karma

**10.4.** It has borne the fruits of prema for all living beings —
Ananta has been left out by the turns of his own karma.
