[^13-24]: GPT1 — p. 40, no. 44 (suhai), checked against the scan (PDF p. 299); GPT2 — sec. 1.3, no. 44 (last word "kammaphere"). The pada is not
in PK, BR, KGC or PS (catalogue: AN-010; the signature given in the catalogue as "…karmadoṣe" reads "karmaphere" in the scan). In GPT it
follows the pada of Raya Ananta from KGC (no. 43, chapter 11, no. 3), and the signature "Ananta" here is probably the same poet's —
Ananta of Advaita's branch (per M-1961); attribution only by GPT (C). The image of Nityananda watering the shoot of devotion — cf.
the "tree of prema," CC Adi 9.

## 11. Murari — "śacīra āṅginā mājhe bhubanamohana sāje…" (GPT1 p. 77, no. 47)
*Childhood: in the middle of Shachi's courtyard, enchanting the world, little Gorachand crawls on all fours; holding His
mother's finger He toddles and falls; a tiger-claw swings at His neck, His chest is wet with dribble, on His moon-face is the
lightning of a smile; Shachi takes the dusty child to her breast, but He, crying, climbs down and rolls on the ground again;
Murari, laughing, says: this is no child for the lap — Gaurahari will become a sannyasi. Raga pahira.*[^13-25]

শচীর আঙ্গিনা মাঝে ভুবনমোহন সাজে গোরাচাঁদ দেয় হামাগুড়ি ।
মায়ের অঙ্গুলি ধরি ক্ষণে চলে গুড়ি গুড়ি আছাড় খাইয়া যায় পড়ি ॥

*śacīra āṅginā mājhe bhubanamohana sāje gorācām̐da deya hāmāguṛi |*
*māyera aṅguli dhari kṣaṇe cale guṛi guṛi āchāṛa khāiyā yāya paṛi ||*

*Word for word:* śacīra āṅginā mājhe — in the middle of Shachi's courtyard; bhubanamohana sāje — in a world-enchanting attire; gorācām̐da — Gorachand; deya hāmāguṛi — crawls on all fours; māyera aṅguli dhari — holding the mother's finger; kṣaṇe — now; cale guṛi guṛi — toddles; āchāṛa khāiyā — tripping; yāya paṛi — falls down

**11.1.** In the middle of Shachi's courtyard, in an attire that enchants the world, Gorachand crawls on all fours;
holding His mother's finger, now He toddles along — and, tripping, falls down.

বাঘনখ গলে দোলে বুক ভাসি যায় লোলে চাঁদমুখে হাসির বিজুলি ।
ধূলামাখা সর্ব গায় সহিতে কি পারে মায় বুকের উপরে লয় তুলি ॥

*bāghanakha gale dole buka bhāsi yāya lole cām̐damukhe hāsira bijuli |*
*dhūlāmākhā sarva gāya sahite ki pāre māya bukera upare laya tuli ||*

*Word for word:* bāghanakha — tiger-claw; gale dole — swings at the neck; buka bhāsi yāya — the chest is wet; lole — with dribble; cām̐damukhe — on the moon-face; hāsira bijuli — lightning of a smile; dhūlāmākhā — dust-smeared; sarva gāya — the whole body; sahite ki pāre māya — can the mother bear it; bukera upare — to the breast; laya tuli — lifts

**11.2.** A tiger-claw swings at His neck, His chest is wet with dribble, on His moon-face is the lightning of a smile;
covered all over with dust — can a mother bear it? — she lifts Him to her breast.

কাঁদিয়া আকুল তাতে নামে গোরা কোল হৈতে পুন ভূমে দেয় গড়াগড়ি ।
হাসিয়া মুরারি বোলে এ নহে কোলের ছেলে সন্ন্যাসী হইবে গৌরহরি ॥

*kām̐diyā ākula tāte nāme gorā kola haite puna bhūme deya gaṛāgaṛi |*
*hāsiyā murāri bole e nahe kolera chele sannyāsī haibe gaurahari ||*

*Word for word:* kām̐diyā — crying; ākula tāte — upset at this; nāme gorā — Gora climbs down; kola haite — from the lap; puna bhūme — again on the ground; deya gaṛāgaṛi — rolls about; hāsiyā murāri bole — Murari says, laughing; e nahe kolera chele — this is no child for the lap; sannyāsī haibe gaurahari — Gaurahari will become a sannyasi

**11.3.** Crying, displeased at this, Gora climbs down from her lap and rolls on the ground again;
Murari, laughing, says: "This is no child for the lap — Gaurahari will become a sannyasi."[^13-26]

[^13-25]: GPT1 — p. 77, section "Childhood plays," no. 47 (pahira), checked against the scan (PDF p. 336); GPT2 — sec. 2.2, no. 47. The pada
is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS. Catalogue: MU-001; the row MU-006 ("…hāsiyā murāri bole e nahe kolera chele," after Majumdar's reference to
GPT1 p. 77) is the same pada (a duplicate). Majumdar considers this pada doubtful: the signature merely names Murari, and he
ascribes the padas on the Lord's infancy to later imagination. The attribution to Murari Gupta is unproven (C). A tiger-claw
(bāghanakha) is an amulet on a child's neck.
[^13-26]: The first syllable of line 11.3 is cut off in the GPT1 scan ("[kām̐]diyā"), restored by sense and metre. Murari's words foretell
the sannyasa; in CB (Adi 4–5) the child's future greatness is spoken of by an astrologer and neighbours, while Murari is Nimai's
senior fellow student (CB, Adi-khanda).

## 12. Murari — "śacīra dulāla manoraṅge…" (GPT1 pp. 77–78, no. 48)
*Children's kirtana: Shachi's darling son plays with boys of His age; Gora is in the middle, the children around Him; holding
hands they whirl in time and clap; Gora cries "Hari, Hari!", the children echo, and Kali trembles; Murari is full of joy — the
reign of sin is over. Raga kamoda.*[^13-27]

শচীর দুলাল মনোরঙ্গে ।
খেলে সমবয় শিশু-সঙ্গে ॥

*śacīra dulāla manoraṅge |*
*khele samabaya śiśu-saṅge ||*

*Word for word:* śacīra dulāla — Shachi's darling; manoraṅge — with a joyful heart; khele — plays; samabaya śiśu-saṅge — with children of His age

**12.1.** Shachi's darling son, with a joyful heart,
plays with children of His own age.

মাঝে গোরা শিশু চারি পাশে ।
নাচে আর মৃদু মৃদু হাসে ॥

*mājhe gorā śiśu cāri pāśe |*
*nāce āra mṛdu mṛdu hāse ||*

*Word for word:* mājhe gorā — Gora in the middle; śiśu cāri pāśe — children all around; nāce — dances; āra — and; mṛdu mṛdu hāse — smiles gently

**12.2.** Gora is in the middle, the children all around;
He dances and smiles ever so gently.

হাতে হাতে করে ধরাধরি ।
তালে তালে নাচে ঘুরি ঘুরি ॥

*hāte hāte kare dharādhari |*
*tāle tāle nāce ghuri ghuri ||*

*Word for word:* hāte hāte — hand in hand; kare dharādhari — hold one another; tāle tāle — in time; nāce ghuri ghuri — dance whirling

**12.3.** Holding one another by the hand,
they whirl in time and dance.

ক্ষণে ঘন দেয় করতালি ।
ক্ষণে কেহ কহে ভালি ভালি ॥

*kṣaṇe ghana deya karatāli |*
*kṣaṇe keha kahe bhāli bhāli ||*

*Word for word:* kṣaṇe — now; ghana — thickly; deya karatāli — clap their hands; kṣaṇe keha — now someone; kahe bhāli bhāli — says "well done, well done"

**12.4.** Now they clap their hands together,
now someone cries: "Well done, well done!"

গোরা যবে বলে হরি হরি ।
শিশুগণ বলে সঙ্গে হরি ॥

*gorā yabe bale hari hari |*
*śiśugaṇa bale saṅge hari ||*

*Word for word:* gorā yabe bale — when Gora cries; hari hari — "Hari, Hari"; śiśugaṇa — the children; bale saṅge — cry along; hari — "Hari"

**12.5.** When Gora calls out "Hari, Hari!" —
the children call out "Hari!" along with Him.

ঘন ঘন হরিবোল শুনি ।
কাঁপে কলি পরমাদ গুণি ॥

*ghana ghana haribola śuni |*
*kām̐pe kali paramāda guṇi ||*

*Word for word:* ghana ghana — again and again; haribola śuni — hearing "Hari bol"; kām̐pe kali — Kali trembles; paramāda guṇi — reckoning disaster

**12.6.** Hearing "Hari bol!" again and again,
Kali trembles, sensing disaster.

মুরারি আনন্দে ভরপুর ।
পাপের রাজত্ব হৈল দূর ॥

*murāri ānande bharapura |*
*pāpera rājatva haila dūra ||*

*Word for word:* murāri — Murari; ānande bharapura — full of joy; pāpera rājatva — the reign of sin; haila dūra — has gone away

**12.7.** Murari is filled with joy:
the reign of sin is over.[^13-28]

[^13-27]: GPT1 — pp. 77–78, no. 48 (kamoda), checked against the scan (PDF pp. 336–337); GPT2 — sec. 2.2, no. 48. The pada is not in PK, BR,
KGC or PS. Catalogue: MU-007 (the first line given in the catalogue, "gorā sabe bale hari hari," after Majumdar's reference, is 12.5).
Majumdar allows that it may be an interpolation; the attribution to Murari Gupta is unproven (C).
[^13-28]: Murari's name in the last couplet is the poet's signature (or a mention of Murari Gupta as a witness). Little Nimai's games,
repeating the name of Hari with the children — CB Adi 4; CC Adi 14.

## 13. Yadunatha (?) — "nityānanda saṅge nāce prabhu gauracandra…" (GPT1 p. 271, no. 76)
*The kirtana of Gaura and Nityananda: the Lord dances with Nityananda, His associates after Him; the earth floats in tears; He
embraces the fallen and weeps, calls His devotees, embraces Gadai; He calls Govinda, Madhava and Vasu. Raga suhai.*[^13-29]

নিত্যানন্দ সঙ্গে নাচে প্রভু গৌরচন্দ্র ।
সঙ্গে সঙ্গে নাচে পারিষদ ভক্তবৃন্দ ॥

*nityānanda saṅge nāce prabhu gauracandra |*
*saṅge saṅge nāce pāriṣada bhaktabṛnda ||*

*Word for word:* nityānanda saṅge — with Nityananda; nāce — dances; prabhu gauracandra — the Lord Gaurachandra; saṅge saṅge — along after; nāce pāriṣada — the associates dance; bhaktabṛnda — the host of devotees

**13.1.** With Nityananda dances the Lord Gaurachandra,
and after Him dance His associates — the host of devotees.

অবনী ভাসিয়া যায় নয়নের জলে ।
দুবাহু তুলিয়া সভে হরি হরি বোলে ॥

*abanī bhāsiyā yāya nayanera jale |*
*dubāhu tuliyā sabhe hari hari bole ||*

*Word for word:* abanī bhāsiyā yāya — the earth floats away; nayanera jale — on the tears of the eyes; dubāhu tuliyā — raising both arms; sabhe — all; hari hari bole — cry "Hari, Hari"

**13.2.** The earth floats away on the tears of their eyes;
raising both arms, all cry: "Hari, Hari!"

ভাবে গর গর অঙ্গ কত ধারা বয় ।
পতিতের গলে ধরি রোদন করয় ॥

*bhābe gara gara aṅga kata dhārā baya |*
*patitera gale dhari rodana karaya ||*

*Word for word:* bhābe — with bhava; gara gara aṅga — the body quivers; kata dhārā baya — how many streams flow; patitera gale dhari — embracing the fallen by the neck; rodana karaya — sobs

**13.3.** His body quivers with bhava — how many streams flow!
Embracing the fallen by the neck, He sobs.

আপনার ভক্তগণে ডাকয়ে আপনে ।
গদাইর গলা ধরি কাঁদে ক্ষণে ক্ষণে ॥

*āpanāra bhaktagaṇe ḍākaye āpane |*
*gadāira galā dhari kām̐de kṣaṇe kṣaṇe ||*

*Word for word:* āpanāra bhaktagaṇe — His own devotees; ḍākaye āpane — He Himself calls; gadāira galā dhari — embracing Gadai by the neck; kām̐de kṣaṇe kṣaṇe — weeps again and again

**13.4.** His own devotees He Himself calls together,
and, embracing Gadai by the neck, He weeps again and again.

গোবিন্দ মাধব বাসু হের আইস বলি ।
যদু কহে কাঁদে প্রভুর পরাণ-পুতলী ॥

*gobinda mādhaba bāsu hera āisa bali |*
*yadu kahe kām̐de prabhura parāṇa-putalī ||*

*Word for word:* gobinda mādhaba bāsu — Govinda, Madhava, Vasu; hera āisa — come here; bali — calling; yadu kahe — Yadu says; kām̐de — weeps; prabhura parāṇa-putalī — the darling (lit. doll) of the Lord's life

**13.5.** "Govinda, Madhava, Vasu — come here!" He calls;
Yadu says: the darling of the Lord's life weeps.[^13-30]

[^13-29]: GPT1 — p. 271, no. 76 (suhai), checked against the scan (PDF p. 530); GPT2 — sec. 4.2, no. 76. The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS.
It is entered twice in the catalogue: YD-007 and YN-013 (a duplicate; the signature "yadu kahe" — Yadunatha or Yadunandana, not
established); C. Govinda, Madhava and Vasu are the Ghosha brothers, the Lord's kirtana singers (CC Adi 10; Madhya 11).
[^13-30]: "The darling of the Lord's life" (prabhura parāṇa-putalī, literally "the doll of the Lord's life") — probably Gadadhara (Gadai), named in 13.4.

## 14. Raya Ananta — "nadīyā-ākāśe saṃkīrtana-megha sāje…" (GPT1 p. 271, no. 79)
*Sankirtana as a thunderstorm: in the sky of Nadia the cloud of kirtana has gathered, khol and karatalas thunder, the roars
of "hum" are like thunderclaps; the two Lords rain down the name; the associates dance, and the lightning of bhava flashes;
Nadia and Shantipura are flooded with the rain of prema. Raga suhai.*[^13-31]

নদীয়া-আকাশে সংকীর্তন-মেঘ সাজে ।
খোল করতাল মুখে গভীর গরজে ॥

*nadīyā-ākāśe saṃkīrtana-megha sāje |*
*khola karatāla mukhe gabhīra garaje ||*

*Word for word:* nadīyā-ākāśe — in the sky of Nadia; saṃkīrtana-megha — the cloud of sankirtana; sāje — has gathered; khola karatāla — khol and karatalas; mukhe — with their voice; gabhīra garaje — thunder deeply

**14.1.** In the sky of Nadia the cloud of sankirtana has gathered:
khol and karatalas are its deep thunder.

হুহুঙ্কার বজ্রধ্বনি হয় মুহুর্মুহু ।
বরিখয়ে নাম-নীর ঘন দুই পহুঁ ॥

*huhuṅkāra bajradhvani haya muhurmuhu |*
*barikhaye nāma-nīra ghana dui pahum̐ ||*

*Word for word:* huhuṅkāra — the roar "hum-hum"; bajradhvani — thunderclaps; haya muhurmuhu — sound again and again; barikhaye — rain down; nāma-nīra — the water of the Name; ghana — clouds; dui pahum̐ — the two Lords

**14.2.** Roars of "hum-hum" — thunderclaps — sound again and again;
the two Lords, the clouds, pour down a rain of the Name.

নাচে গায় পারিষদ থমকে থমকে ।
ভাবের বিজুলী তায় সঘন চমকে ॥

*nāce gāya pāriṣada thamake thamake |*
*bhābera bijulī tāya saghana camake ||*

*Word for word:* nāce gāya — dance and sing; pāriṣada — the associates; thamake thamake — pausing now and then; bhābera bijulī — the lightning of bhava; tāya — in them; saghana camake — flashes again and again

**14.3.** The associates dance and sing, pausing now and then,
and in them the lightning of bhava flashes again and again.

প্রেমের বাদলে নৈদা শান্তিপুর ভাসে ।
রায় অনন্তের হিয়া না ভুলিল রসে ॥

*premera bādale naidā śāntipura bhāse |*
*rāya anantera hiyā nā bhulila rase ||*

*Word for word:* premera bādale — by the rain of prema; naidā — Nadia; śāntipura — Shantipura; bhāse — are flooded; rāya anantera hiyā — the heart of Raya Ananta; nā bhulila rase — did not lose itself in the rasa

**14.4.** By the rain of prema Nadia and Shantipura are flooded —
only the heart of Raya Ananta has not dissolved in this rasa.[^13-32]

[^13-31]: GPT1 — pp. 271–272, no. 79 (suhai), checked against the scan (PDF p. 531); GPT2 — sec. 4.2, no. 79. The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC
or PS (catalogue: AN-009, GPT only; C). The signature "Raya Ananta" is as in KGC 11.2 and 28.2 (chapters 4, 11): per M-1961 this is
Ananta of Advaita's branch.
[^13-32]: "The two Lords" — Gaura and Nityananda; "Shantipura" — Advaita's town: the kirtana has swept both places. Literally: "the heart
of Raya Ananta did not lose itself in the rasa."

## 15. Balarama Dasa — "hari hari gorā kene kānde…" (PK 2254; GPT1 p. 289, no. 39)
*Why does Gora weep? Having left the bank of the Kalindi and the plays by the kadamba, what does He seek on the shore of the
ocean? He who danced the rasa with millions of gopis now, having taken sannyasa, weeps; the eyes at whose glance Kamadeva
swooned pour out streams of tears; the head whose top-knot charmed the world is shaven; instead of yellow garments,
saffron; instead of the dark form, golden. The poet does not know the reason — the reason is she whose colour it is. Raga
suhai (in GPT1 — gandhara).*[^13-33]

হরি হরি গোরা কেনে কান্দে ।
না জানি ঠেকিলা গোরা কার প্রেম-ফান্দে ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*hari hari gorā kene kānde |*
*nā jāni ṭhekilā gorā kāra prema-phānde || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* hari hari — Hari, Hari!; gorā kene kānde — why does Gora weep; nā jāni — I do not know; ṭhekilā gorā — Gora was caught; kāra prema-phānde — in whose snare of love

**15.1.** Hari, Hari! Why does Gora weep?
I do not know in whose snare of love He has been caught.

তেজিয়া কালিন্দী-তীর কদম্ব-বিলাস ।
এবে সিন্ধু-তীরে কেনে কিবা অভিলাষ ॥

*tejiyā kālindī-tīra kadamba-bilāsa |*
*ebe sindhu-tīre kene kibā abhilāṣa ||*

*Word for word:* tejiyā — leaving; kālindī-tīra — the bank of the Kalindi; kadamba-bilāsa — the plays by the kadamba; ebe — now; sindhu-tīre — on the ocean shore; kene kibā abhilāṣa — what does He desire

**15.2.** Leaving the bank of the Kalindi and the plays by the kadamba,
what does He now desire on the shore of the ocean?

যে করিল শত কোটি গোপী সঙ্গে রাস ।
এবে সে কান্দয়ে কেনে করিয়া সন্ন্যাস ॥

*ye karila śata koṭi gopī saṅge rāsa |*
*ebe se kāndaye kene kariyā sannyāsa ||*

*Word for word:* ye karila — who performed; śata koṭi gopī saṅge — with millions of gopis; rāsa — the rasa; ebe se — now He; kāndaye kene — why does He weep; kariyā sannyāsa — having taken sannyasa

**15.3.** He who danced the rasa with millions of gopis —
now, having taken sannyasa, why does He weep?

যে আঁখি-ভঙ্গীতে কত অনঙ্গ মুরছে ।
এবে কত শত ধারা বাহিয়া পড়িছে ॥

*ye ām̐khi-bhaṅgīte kata anaṅga murache |*
*ebe kata śata dhārā bāhiyā paṛiche ||*

*Word for word:* ye ām̐khi-bhaṅgīte — at the play of which eyes; kata anaṅga murache — how many Anangas swooned; ebe — now; kata śata dhārā — hundreds of streams; bāhiyā paṛiche — are flowing down

**15.4.** Those eyes, at whose play Ananga himself swooned,
now pour out hundreds of streams.

যে মোহন চূড়া-ছাঁদে জগত মোহিত ।
সে মস্তক কেশ-শূন্য অতি বিপরীত ॥

*ye mohana cūṛā-chām̐de jagata mohita |*
*se mastaka keśa-śūnya ati biparīta ||*

*Word for word:* ye mohana cūṛā-chām̐de — by whose enchanting top-knot; jagata mohita — the world was charmed; se mastaka — that head; keśa-śūnya — hairless; ati biparīta — utterly reversed

**15.5.** That head whose enchanting top-knot captivated the world —
now without hair: everything turned upside down!

পীত বাস ছাড়ি কেনে অরুণ বসন ।
কালরূপ ছাড়ি কেনে গৌর বরণ ॥

*pīta bāsa chāṛi kene aruṇa basana |*
*kālarūpa chāṛi kene gaura baraṇa ||*

*Word for word:* pīta bāsa chāṛi — leaving the yellow garment; kene — why; aruṇa basana — saffron (ruddy) cloth; kāla-rūpa chāṛi — leaving the dark form; gaura baraṇa — golden hue

**15.6.** Why has He changed yellow garments for saffron cloth,
why has He changed the dark form for a golden hue?

কহে বলরাম দাসে না জানি কারণ ।
তাহার কারণ কিবা যাহার বরণ ॥

*kahe balarāma dāse nā jāni kāraṇa |*
*tāhāra kāraṇa kibā yāhāra baraṇa ||*

*Word for word:* kahe balarāma dāse — says Balarama Dasa; nā jāni kāraṇa — I do not know the reason; tāhāra kāraṇa kibā — its reason is indeed; yāhāra baraṇa — she whose colour it is

**15.7.** Balarama Dasa says: I do not know the reason —
the reason for it is she whose colour it is.[^13-34]

[^13-33]: PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 288 (printed p. 277), 21st pallava, label "॥৩৭॥২২৫৪॥", raga suhai, MS P-R-Sa no. 2309. GPT1 — p. 289, no. 39
(gandhara), checked against the scan (PDF p. 548); GPT2 — sec. 4.3, no. 39. In the catalogue (BD-024) the pada was listed as "GPT only"
(in chapter 8 the erroneous link to PK 764 — a pada of Vasu Ghosha with the same opening, translated in chapter 8 — was
corrected); it is found in PK — **core** (C). Kalindi is the Yamuna; the kadamba is the tree of Krishna's plays; the ocean shore is
Puri.
[^13-34]: The poet's answer: Gaura is Krishna who has taken Radha's colour and bhava, and He weeps from Her prema (CC Adi 4). Ananga
(Kamadeva) is the god of love; "swooned" — an image of Krishna's beauty, which captivates Cupid himself (Madana-mohana). The
Lord's sannyasa and tears are not the sorrow of a conditioned soul but prema.

## 16. Yadunatha Dasa — "prabhāte jāgila gorācām̐da…" (GPT1 p. 349, no. 18)
*The Lord's morning in Navadvipa: Gorachand has awoken, and all see Him quite different; His eyes, red with sleep, are
half-closed, He stretches like the golden bow of the god of love; the devotees come at dawn; having washed, Gaurahari sits
in the circle of His own. Raga suhai.*[^13-35]

প্রভাতে জাগিল গোরাচাঁদ ।
হেরই সকলে আন ছাঁদ ॥

*prabhāte jāgila gorācām̐da |*
*herai sakale āna chām̐da ||*

*Word for word:* prabhāte — at dawn; jāgila gorācām̐da — Gorachand awoke; herai sakale — all see; āna chām̐da — a different look

**16.1.** At dawn Gorachand awoke,
and all see Him quite different.

ঘুমে ঢুলু ঢুলু নয়ন রাতা ।
অলসে ঈষৎ মুদিত পাতা ॥

*ghume ḍhulu ḍhulu nayana rātā |*
*alase īṣat mudita pātā ||*

*Word for word:* ghume — with sleep; ḍhulu ḍhulu — drooping; nayana rātā — red eyes; alase — with languor; īṣat mudita pātā — lids half-closed

**16.2.** His eyes, reddened with sleep, keep closing,
the lids half-shut with languor.

অঙ্গুলি মুড়িয়া মোড়য়ে তনু ।
যৈছন অতনু কনক-ধনু ॥

*aṅguli muṛiyā moṛaye tanu |*
*yaichana atanu kanaka-dhanu ||*

*Word for word:* aṅguli muṛiyā — interlacing the fingers; moṛaye tanu — stretches the body; yaichana — like; atanu — the bodiless god of love; kanaka-dhanu — golden bow

**16.3.** Interlacing His fingers, He stretches His whole body —
like the golden bow of Ananga.[^13-36]

দেখিতে আওল ভকতগণে ।
মিলিল বিহানে হরিষ-মনে ॥

*dekhite āola bhakatagaṇe |*
*milila bihāne hariṣa-mane ||*

*Word for word:* dekhite āola — came to see; bhakatagaṇe — the devotees; milila bihāne — gathered in the morning; hariṣa-mane — with joyful hearts

**16.4.** The devotees came to see Him
and gathered joyfully in the morning.

মুখ পাখালিয়া গৌরহরি ।
বৈসে নিজগণ চৌদিকে বেড়ি ॥

*mukha pākhāliyā gaurahari |*
*baise nijagaṇa caudike beṛi ||*

*Word for word:* mukha pākhāliyā — having washed His face; gaurahari — Gaurahari; baise — sits; nijagaṇa — His own; caudike beṛi — surrounding on all sides

**16.5.** Having washed His face, Gaurahari
sits down — and His own surround Him on all sides.

নদীয়া-নগরে হেন বিলাস ।
যদুনাথ দেখে সদাই পাশ ॥

*nadīyā-nagare hena bilāsa |*
*yadunātha dekhe sadāi pāśa ||*

*Word for word:* nadīyā-nagare — in the town of Nadia; hena bilāsa — such plays; yadunātha dekhe — Yadunatha sees; sadāi pāśa — always, close by

**16.6.** Such are the plays in the town of Nadia;
Yadunatha sees them always, being close by.[^13-37]

[^13-35]: GPT1 — p. 349, section "Ashtakaliya" (morning), no. 18 (suhai), checked against the scan (PDF p. 608); GPT2 — sec. 5.1, no. 18. The
pada is not in BR, KGC or PS; **it is in PK — PK 2512** (vol. 4, 30th pallava "Aṣṭakālīya nitya-līlā," "atha dibāyāṃ yathā," raga
bibhasa, PDF p. 56, label "॥৩৯॥২৫১২॥"; found in the full PK check of chapter 16 — M-1961's reference is correct; catalogue: YD-003). PK
reads "herai sakale bayana chānda" ("all look upon the form of His face") and "yadunātha dekhe gadāi pāśa" ("Yadunatha sees it beside
Gadai," that is, Gadadhara); the main text is kept after GPT1, the PK readings are in the full version of the book. The preceding GPT pada (no. 17) is by Ghanashyama, the following (no. 19) by Narahari.
[^13-36]: Ananga is the god of love; the comparison with his bow is a traditional image of a slender, curving body.
[^13-37]: The signature seems to speak of the poet as an eyewitness of the Navadvipa plays; on this ground M-1961 considers Yadunatha
a contemporary of the Lord (Yadunatha Kavichandra is mentioned among the Lord's associates in CB). GPT only — C.

## 17. Murari — "calila nadīyāra loka gaurāṅga dekhite…" (GPT1 pp. 378–379, no. 42)
*After the sannyasa: at Nityananda's word the people of Nadia go to Shantipura to see Gauranga — Shachi in front, everyone
after her; on every lip is "Ha Gauranga!"; without Gauranga they were living dead and seem to have revived at Nitai's words;
Nadia is emptied, and behind them all goes Murari. Raga dhanashi.*[^13-38]

চলিল নদীয়ার লোক গৌরাঙ্গ দেখিতে ।
আগে শচী আর সবে চলিলা পশ্চাতে ॥

*calila nadīyāra loka gaurāṅga dekhite |*
*āge śacī āra sabe calilā paścāte ||*

*Word for word:* calila — set out; nadīyāra loka — the people of Nadia; gaurāṅga dekhite — to see Gauranga; āge śacī — Shachi in front; āra sabe — and all the rest; calilā paścāte — went behind

**17.1.** The people of Nadia set out to see Gauranga:
Shachi in front, and all the rest behind.

হা গৌরাঙ্গ হা গৌরাঙ্গ সবাকার মুখে ।
নয়নে গলয়ে ধারা হিয়া ফাটে দুঃখে ॥

*hā gaurāṅga hā gaurāṅga sabākāra mukhe |*
*nayane galaye dhārā hiyā phāṭe duḥkhe ||*

*Word for word:* hā gaurāṅga — "ha, Gauranga"; sabākāra mukhe — on everyone's lips; nayane galaye dhārā — streams flow from the eyes; hiyā phāṭe duḥkhe — the heart bursts with grief

**17.2.** "Ha Gauranga, ha Gauranga!" is on every lip;
streams pour from their eyes, the heart bursts with grief.

গৌরাঙ্গ বিহনে ছিল জীয়ন্তে মরিয়া ।
নিতাই-বচনে যেন উঠিল বাঁচিয়া ॥

*gaurāṅga bihane chila jīyante mariyā |*
*nitāi-bacane yena uṭhila bām̐ciyā ||*

*Word for word:* gaurāṅga bihane — without Gauranga; chila jīyante mariyā — were dead while living; nitāi-bacane — at Nitai's words; yena uṭhila bām̐ciyā — as if they rose up alive

**17.3.** Without Gauranga they had been living dead —
and at Nitai's words they seemed to come back to life.

হেরিতে গৌরাঙ্গ-মুখ মনে অভিলাষ ।
শান্তিপুর ধায় সবে হৈয়া ঊর্ধ্বশ্বাস ॥

*herite gaurāṅga-mukha mane abhilāṣa |*
*śāntipura dhāya sabe haiyā ūrdhvaśvāsa ||*

*Word for word:* herite — to see; gaurāṅga-mukha — Gauranga's face; mane abhilāṣa — desire in the heart; śāntipura dhāya — run to Shantipura; sabe — all; haiyā ūrdhvaśvāsa — breathless

**17.4.** In the heart one desire: to see Gauranga's face;
all hurry to Shantipura, breathless with running.

হইল পুরুষ-শূন্য নদীয়া-নগরী ।
সবাকার পাছে পাছে চলিল মুরারি ॥

*haila puruṣa-śūnya nadīyā-nagarī |*
*sabākāra pāche pāche calila murāri ||*

*Word for word:* haila puruṣa-śūnya — became empty of men; nadīyā-nagarī — the town of Nadia; sabākāra pāche pāche — behind them all; calila murāri — went Murari

**17.5.** The town of Nadia was emptied of its men;
behind them all, following, went Murari.[^13-39]

[^13-38]: GPT1 — pp. 378–379, section on the sannyasa, no. 42 (dhanashi), checked against the scan (PDF pp. 637–638); GPT2 — sec. 5.3, no. 42.
The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS (catalogue: MU-008). It continues no. 40 (PK 2231, "prabhure rākhiyā śāntipure," signed by Murari;
chapter 6, no. 20), where Nityananda comes to Nadia to call everyone to Shantipura. Majumdar considers Murari Gupta's authorship
unproven (C).
[^13-39]: Nityananda brought Shachi and the people of Navadvipa to Shantipura, to Advaita, where the Lord was after His sannyasa — CC
Madhya 3; CB Antya 1. "Behind them all went Murari" — Murari Gupta as a witness (or the poet's signature).

## 18. Yadunatha Dasa — "āsibe āmāra gaurāṅgasundara…" (GPT1 p. 412, no. 29)
*Waiting: my Gaurangasundara will come to Nadia! Seeing Him from afar I shall perform the auspicious rites — set out water-pots
with mango twigs, plant banana saplings, hang garlands; the women of Nadia will run to see, in every house "Hari, Hari!" will
resound; His mother will rush to Him, embrace Him, bathe Him in tears and take Him home; Yadunatha, looking on, will fall
down and take His lotus feet. Raga turi.*[^13-40]

আসিবে আমার গৌরাঙ্গসুন্দর নদীয়া-নগর মাঝ ।
দূরেতে দেখিয়া চমকিত হৈয়া করব মঙ্গল কাজ ॥

*āsibe āmāra gaurāṅgasundara nadīyā-nagara mājha |*
*dūrete dekhiyā camakita haiyā karaba maṅgala kāja ||*

*Word for word:* āsibe — will come; āmāra gaurāṅgasundara — my Gaurangasundara; nadīyā-nagara mājha — into the town of Nadia; dūrete dekhiyā — seeing from afar; camakita haiyā — thrilled; karaba maṅgala kāja — I shall perform auspicious rites

**18.1.** My Gaurangasundara will come to the town of Nadia!
Seeing Him from afar, thrilled, I shall perform the auspicious rites.

জল-ঘট ভরি আম-শাখা ধরি রাখি সারি সারি করি ।
কদলী আনিয়া রোপণ করিয়া ফুলমালা তাহে ধরি ॥

*jala-ghaṭa bhari āma-śākhā dhari rākhi sāri sāri kari |*
*kadalī āniyā ropaṇa kariyā phulamālā tāhe dhari ||*

*Word for word:* jala-ghaṭa bhari — filling water-pots; āma-śākhā dhari — setting mango twigs; rākhi sāri sāri kari — placing them in rows; kadalī āniyā — bringing banana saplings; ropaṇa kariyā — planting them; phulamālā tāhe dhari — hanging garlands on them

**18.2.** I shall fill water-pots, set mango twigs in them, and arrange them in rows;
I shall bring banana saplings, plant them, and hang garlands on them.

আওল শুনিয়া নারী নদীয়া আওব দেখিবার তরে ।
হরি হরি ধ্বনি জয় জয় বাণী উঠিবে সকল ঘরে ॥

*āola śuniyā nārī nadīyā āoba dekhibāra tare |*
*hari hari dhvani jaya jaya bāṇī uṭhibe sakala ghare ||*

*Word for word:* āola śuniyā — hearing that He has come; nārī nadīyā — the women of Nadia; āoba dekhibāra tare — will come to see; hari hari dhvani — cries of "Hari, Hari"; jaya jaya bāṇī — shouts of "jaya"; uṭhibe sakala ghare — will rise in every house

**18.3.** Hearing that He has come, the women of Nadia will come running to see;
cries of "Hari, Hari!" and "Jaya, jaya!" will rise in every house.

শুনিয়া জননী ধাইবে অমনি করিবে আপন কোরে ।
নয়নের জলে ধুই কলেবরে তুরিতে লইবে ঘরে ॥

*śuniyā jananī dhāibe amani karibe āpana kore |*
*nayanera jale dhui kalebare turite laibe ghare ||*

*Word for word:* śuniyā jananī — hearing, the mother; dhāibe amani — will at once rush; karibe āpana kore — will take Him in her arms; nayanera jale — with tears; dhui kalebare — washing His body; turite laibe ghare — will quickly take Him home

**18.4.** Hearing it, His mother will at once rush to Him and take Him in her arms;
bathing His body in her tears, she will quickly lead Him home.

যতেক ভকত দেখি হরষিত হইবে প্রেম-আনন্দ ।
যদুনাথ চাঞা পড়ি লোটাইয়া লইবে চরণারবিন্দ ॥

*yateka bhakata dekhi haraṣita haibe prema-ānanda |*
*yadunātha cāñā paṛi loṭāiyā laibe caraṇārabinda ||*

*Word for word:* yateka bhakata — all the devotees; dekhi haraṣita — rejoicing at the sight; haibe prema-ānanda — there will be the bliss of prema; yadunātha cāñā — Yadunatha, looking; paṛi loṭāiyā — falling prostrate; laibe caraṇārabinda — will take the lotus feet

**18.5.** All the devotees, seeing Him, will rejoice in the bliss of prema;
Yadunatha, looking on, will fall prostrate and take His lotus feet.[^13-41]

[^13-40]: GPT1 — p. 412, no. 29 (turi), checked against the scan (PDF p. 671); GPT2 — no. 29 (OCR, line 44957). The pada is not in
BR, KGC or PS; **it is in PK — PK 1976** (vol. 3, 12th pallava "Bhābollāsa," raga turi, PDF pp. 182–183, printed pp. 171–172, label
"॥৮॥১৯৭৬॥"; found in the full PK check of chapter 16; catalogue: YD-004; M-1961 mentions this pada under Yadunatha's name). The PK
signature reads "yadunātha yāñā paṛi loṭāiyā" ("Yadunatha, coming, will fall…"; GPT "cāñā," "looking"); the other PK readings are in the full version of the book. C. Water-pots with mango twigs
(pūrṇakumbha) and banana saplings at the entrance are Bengali rites of welcome.
[^13-41]: The pada is a dream of the Lord's return (cf. CC Madhya 16: the Lord comes to Gauda and meets His mother at Kuliya). The speaker
is a devotee of Nadia (perhaps the poet himself); the "women of Nadia" here are townswomen, not "nagaris" in the sense of
nagari-bhava.

## 19. Balarama Dasa — "rūpe guṇe anupamā lakṣmī-koṭi-manoramā…" (PK 2299; GPT1 pp. 426–427, no. 43; KGC 23.2)
*On Nityananda: He with whom countless maidens of Vraja sported in the rasa-lila — why has He become an avadhuta? The teacher
of all lovers, the wish-fulfilling tree of rasa — why does He wander in renunciation? Balarama, from whose chapters come
Sankarshana and Shesha, who dwells eternally in Goloka — why is He in the midst of sankirtana? Nityananda has plunged everyone
into the rasa of Gaura — only the poet is left aside. Raga kalyani (in KGC and GPT1 — gandhara).*[^13-42]

রূপে গুণে অনুপমা লক্ষ্মী-কোটি-মনোরমা ব্রজ-বধূ অযুতে অযুত ।
রাস-কেলি-রস-রঙ্গে বিহরে যাহার সঙ্গে সো পহু কি লাগি অবধূত ॥

*rūpe guṇe anupamā lakṣmī-koṭi-manoramā braja-badhū ayute ayuta |*
*rāsa-keli-rasa-raṅge bihare yāhāra saṅge so pahu ki lāgi abadhūta ||*

*Word for word:* rūpe guṇe anupamā — peerless in beauty and virtue; lakṣmī-koṭi-manoramā — more charming than millions of Lakshmis; braja-badhū — maidens of Vraja; ayute ayuta — tens of thousands; rāsa-keli-rasa-raṅge — in the joy of the rasa play; bihare yāhāra saṅge — with whom they sported; so pahu — that Lord; ki lāgi — why; abadhūta — an avadhuta

**19.1.** Peerless in beauty and virtue, more charming than millions of Lakshmis — the maidens of Vraja, tens of thousands —
He with whom they sported in the joy of the rasa-lila — why has that Lord become an avadhuta?[^13-43]

হরি হরি এ দুখ কহিব কার আগে ।
সকল নাগর-গুরু রসের কলপতরু সে বা কেন ফিরয়ে বৈরাগে ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*hari hari e dukha kahiba kāra āge |*
*sakala nāgara-guru rasera kalapataru se bā kena phiraye bairāge || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* hari hari — Hari, Hari!; e dukha — this sorrow; kahiba kāra āge — to whom shall I tell; sakala nāgara-guru — teacher of all lovers; rasera kalapataru — wish-fulfilling tree of rasa; se vā kena — why does He; phiraye bairāge — wander in renunciation

**19.2.** Hari, Hari! To whom shall I tell this sorrow?
The teacher of all lovers, the wish-fulfilling tree of rasa — why does He wander in renunciation?

সঙ্কর্ষণ শেষ যার অংশ কলা অবতার অনুখণ গোলোকে বিরাজে ।
কৃষ্ণের অগ্রজ নাম মহাপ্রভু বলরাম কেন নিতাই সংকীর্তন মাঝে ॥

*saṅkarṣaṇa śeṣa yāra aṃśa kalā abatāra anukhaṇa goloke birāje |*
*kṛṣṇera agraja nāma mahāprabhu balarāma kena nitāi saṃkīrtana mājhe ||*

*Word for word:* saṅkarṣaṇa śeṣa — Sankarshana and Shesha; yāra aṃśa kalā abatāra — incarnations of whose portions and parts; anukhaṇa goloke birāje — ever dwelling in Goloka; kṛṣṇera agraja nāma — called Krishna's elder brother; mahāprabhu balarāma — Mahaprabhu Balarama; kena nitāi — why is Nitai; saṃkīrtana mājhe — in the midst of sankirtana

**19.3.** Sankarshana and Shesha are incarnations of His chapters and parts; He dwells eternally in Goloka —
Krishna's elder brother, Mahaprabhu Balarama — why is Nitai in the midst of sankirtana?

শিব-বিহি-অগোচর আগম-নিগম-পর কলি-যুগে শ্রীনিত্যানন্দ ।
গৌর-রসে নিমগন করাইল জনে জন দূরে রহু বলরাম মন্দ ॥

*śiba-bihi-agocara āgama-nigama-para kali-yuge śrīnityānanda |*
*gaura-rase nimagana karāila jane jana dūre rahu balarāma manda ||*

*Word for word:* śiba-bihi-agocara — beyond the reach of Shiva and Brahma; āgama-nigama-para — beyond the agamas and nigamas; kali-yuge — in the Kali age; śrī-nityānanda — Sri Nityananda; gaura-rase nimagana — immersed in Gaura's rasa; karāila jane jana — every single person (KGC, GPT1: jaga-jana — the people of the world); dūre rahu — remained aside; balarāma manda — Balarama the unworthy

**19.4.** Beyond the reach of Shiva and Brahma, beyond the agamas and nigamas — in the Kali age, Sri Nityananda:
He has plunged every single person into the rasa of Gaura — aside has remained only Balarama, the unworthy.[^13-44]

[^13-42]: PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 303 (printed p. 292), 23rd pallava, label "॥৬॥২২৯৯॥", raga kalyani. KGC — 23rd kshanada, no. 2 (p. 180, gandhara;
tesseract kgc.txt, line 6326). GPT1 — pp. 426–427, section on Nityananda, no. 43 (pahira or gandhara); GPT2 — sec. 6.1, no. 43. In KGC
and GPT stanzas 19.3 and 19.4 are rearranged by half-lines (the second halves of 19.3 and 19.4 change places). The pada was missing
from the catalogue (new row); core (PK, KGC), C.
[^13-43]: Nityananda is Balarama; Balarama's rasa-lila with the maidens of Vraja — Bhag. 10.65 (Balarama, coming from Dvaraka to Vraja, spent
two spring months in the rasa-lila with the gopis). The question "why has He become an avadhuta" is poetic wonder, not doubt.
[^13-44]: According to CC (Adi 5) Nityananda-Balarama is the source of Sankarshana, Maha-Vishnu and Shesha. "Balarama, the unworthy" (balarāma manda)
is the poet himself; a play on names: Balarama-Nityananda has saved everyone, while the poet Balarama is left aside.

## 20. Balarama Dasa — "gajendra-gamane yāya sakaruṇa-diṭhe cāya…" (PK 2298; GPT1 p. 427, no. 44)
*The Avadhuta comes, an ocean of mercy: with the gait of a king of elephants, with compassion in His glance, shaking the earth; His
roar frightens the unbelievers, He floats in prema with the host of the immortals; this is Balarama, the son of Rohini, from whose
chapters come Sheshashayi and Sankarshana; now in the dress of a pauper He goes from land to land, saving the three worlds. If you
wish to attain the lilas of Vraja, serve His feet. Raga mangala.*[^13-45]

গজেন্দ্র-গমনে যায় সকরুণ-দিঠে চায় পদ-ভরে মহী টলমল ।
মত্ত-সিংহ জিনি কম্পমান মেদিনী পাষণ্ডীগণ শুনিয়া বিকল ॥

*gajendra-gamane yāya sakaruṇa-diṭhe cāya pada-bhare mahī ṭalamala |*
*matta-siṃha jini kampamāna medinī pāṣaṇḍīgaṇa śuniyā bikala ||*

*Word for word:* gajendra-gamane yāya — walks with the gait of a king of elephants; sakaruṇa-diṭhe cāya — looks with compassion; pada-bhare — at the weight of His steps; mahī ṭalamala — the earth sways; matta-siṃha jini — surpassing a maddened lion; kampamāna medinī — the earth trembles; pāṣaṇḍīgaṇa — the unbelievers; śuniyā bikala — hearing, lose strength

**20.1.** He walks with the gait of a king of elephants, He looks with compassion — at His steps the earth sways;
surpassing a maddened lion, He makes the earth tremble — the unbelievers, hearing it, lose their strength.

আওত অবধৌত করুণার সিন্ধু ।
প্রেমে গরগর মন করে হরি-সংকীর্তন পতিত-পাবন দীন-বন্ধু ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*āota abadhauta karuṇāra sindhu |*
*preme garagara mana kare hari-saṃkīrtana patita-pābana dīna-bandhu || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* āota — comes; abadhauta — the Avadhuta; karuṇāra sindhu — ocean of mercy; preme garagara mana — the mind overflowing with prema; kare hari-saṃkīrtana — performs Hari-sankirtana; patita-pābana — Purifier of the fallen; dīna-bandhu — Friend of the destitute

**20.2.** Here comes the Avadhuta — an ocean of mercy!
His mind overflowing with prema, He performs Hari-sankirtana — Purifier of the fallen, Friend of the destitute.

হুঙ্কার করিয়া চলে অচল সচল নড়ে প্রেমে ভাসে অমর-সমাজে ।
সহচরগণ সঙ্গে বিবিধ খেলন-রঙ্গে অলখিতে করে সব কাজে ॥

*huṅkāra kariyā cale acala sacala naṛe preme bhāse amara-samāje |*
*sahacaragaṇa saṅge bibidha khelana-raṅge alakhite kare saba kāje ||*

*Word for word:* huṅkāra kariyā cale — walks roaring; acala sacala naṛe — the unmoving and moving shake; preme bhāse — float in prema; amara-samāje — the host of the immortals; sahacaragaṇa saṅge — with His companions; bibidha khelana-raṅge — in the joy of many games; alakhite — unseen; kare saba kāje — does all the work

**20.3.** He walks roaring — the unmoving and the moving shake, the host of the immortals floats in prema;
with His companions, in the joy of many games, He unseen accomplishes every task.[^13-46]

শেষ-শায়ী সঙ্কর্ষণ অবতারী নারায়ণ যার অংশ-কলায় গণন ।
কৃপা-সিন্ধু ভক্তি-দাতা জগতের হিত-কর্তা সেই রাম রোহিণী-নন্দন ॥

*śeṣa-śāyī saṅkarṣaṇa abatārī nārāyaṇa yāra aṃśa-kalāya gaṇana |*
*kṛpā-sindhu bhakti-dātā jagatera hita-kartā sei rāma rohiṇī-nandana ||*

*Word for word:* śeṣa-śāyī — Sheshashayi; saṅkarṣaṇa — Sankarshana; abatārī nārāyaṇa — Narayana, source of incarnations; yāra aṃśa-kalāya gaṇana — are counted as His portions of portions; kṛpā-sindhu — ocean of mercy; bhakti-dātā — giver of bhakti; jagatera hita-kartā — benefactor of the world; sei rāma — that Rama; rohiṇī-nandana — son of Rohini

**20.4.** Sheshashayi, Sankarshana, Narayana — the source of incarnations — are counted as chapters of His chapters;
ocean of mercy, Giver of bhakti, Benefactor of the world — this is Rama, the son of Rohini.

যার লীলা লাবণ্য-ধাম আগমে নিগমে গান যার রূপ মদন-মোহন ।
এবে অকিঞ্চন-বেশে ফিরে পহু দেশে দেশে উদ্ধার করয়ে ত্রিভুবন ॥

*yāra līlā lābaṇya-dhāma āgame nigame gāna yāra rūpa madana-mohana |*
*ebe akiñcana-beśe phire pahu deśe deśe uddhāra karaye tribhubana ||*

*Word for word:* yāra līlā — whose lilas; lābaṇya-dhāma — abode of beauty; āgame nigame gāna — sung in agamas and nigamas; yāra rūpa madana-mohana — whose form enchants Madana; ebe — now; akiñcana-beśe — in the dress of one who owns nothing; phire pahu deśe deśe — the Lord wanders from land to land; uddhāra karaye tribhubana — saves the three worlds

**20.5.** Whose lilas are an abode of beauty, sung by the agamas and nigamas, whose form enchants Madana himself —
now in the dress of one who owns nothing the Lord goes from land to land and saves the three worlds.

ব্রজের বৈদগ্ধি-সার যত যত লীলা আর পাইবারে যদি থাকে মন ।
বলরাম দাসে কয় মনোরথ সিদ্ধি হয় ভজ ভজ শ্রীপাদ-চরণ ॥

*brajera baidagdhi-sāra yata yata līlā āra pāibāre yadi thāke mana |*
*balarāma dāse kaya manoratha siddhi haya bhaja bhaja śrīpāda-caraṇa ||*

*Word for word:* brajera baidagdhi-sāra — the essence of Vraja's refinement; yata yata līlā āra — all the other lilas; pāibāre yadi thāke mana — if you have the wish to attain; balarāma dāse kaya — says Balarama Dasa; manoratha siddhi haya — the wish is fulfilled; bhaja bhaja — serve, serve; śrīpāda-caraṇa — the feet of Shripada

**20.6.** If in your heart there is the wish to attain the lilas of Vraja, the essence of all refinement,
says Balarama Dasa, the wish will be fulfilled: serve, serve the feet of Shripada.[^13-47]

[^13-45]: PK: vol. 3, PDF pp. 302–303 (printed pp. 291–292), 23rd pallava, label "॥৫॥২২৯৮॥", raga mangala, MS P-R-Sa no. 2402. GPT1 — p. 427,
no. 44 (mangala); GPT2 — sec. 6.1, no. 44. The signature is garbled in the GPT1 OCR; by PK — "balarāma dāse kaya". The pada was missing from the
catalogue (new row); core (PK), C.
[^13-46]: "Unseen accomplishes every task" — Nityananda, playing with His companions, secretly fulfils the Lord's plan (the preaching of the
Name in Gauda).
[^13-47]: Shripada is a respectful name for Nityananda. According to CC (Adi 5–6) Nityananda's mercy is the way to the service of Radha and
Krishna in Vraja.

## 21. Balarama Dasa — "bandiba advaita śire ye ānilā dhīre dhīre…" (PK 2348; GPT1 p. 449, no. 35)
*Praise of Advaita: I bow to Advaita, who brought Mahaprabhu to the earth — the son of Nanda become the son of Shachi; He saved the
high and the low by the gift of bhakti; the flood of prema is from Nitai, Advaita its wave, the wind of Chaitanya has raised it to the
sky: the worlds of the nagas, men and gods have drowned, the flood of prema has filled Goloka — only Balarama has been left out. Raga
"tatha" (in GPT1 — mangala).*[^13-48]

বন্দিব অদ্বৈত শিরে যে আনিলা ধীরে ধীরে মহাপ্রভু অবনী মাঝার ।
নন্দের নন্দন যে শচীর নন্দন সে নিত্যানন্দ রায় সখা যার ॥

*bandiba advaita śire ye ānilā dhīre dhīre mahāprabhu abanī mājhāra |*
*nandera nandana ye śacīra nandana se nityānanda rāya sakhā yāra ||*

*Word for word:* bandiba advaita śire — I bow my head to Advaita; ye ānilā dhīre dhīre — who slowly brought; mahāprabhu — Mahaprabhu; abanī mājhāra — onto the earth; nandera nandana ye — who is the son of Nanda; śacīra nandana se — He is the son of Shachi; nityānanda rāya sakhā yāra — whose friend is Nityananda Raya

**21.1.** I bow my head to Advaita, who slowly, gradually brought Mahaprabhu to the earth —
Him who is the son of Nanda and also the son of Shachi, whose friend is Nityananda Raya.[^13-49]

প্রভু মোর অদ্বৈত গোসাঞি ।
উত্তম অধম জনে তরাইলা ভক্তি-দানে এমন দয়াল দাতা নাই ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*prabhu mora advaita gosāñi |*
*uttama adhama jane tarāilā bhakti-dāne emana dayāla dātā nāi || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* prabhu mora — my Lord; advaita gosāñi — Advaita Gosani; uttama adhama jane — high and low people; tarāilā bhakti-dāne — saved by the gift of bhakti; emana dayāla dātā nāi — there is no such merciful giver

**21.2.** My Lord is Advaita Gosani!
The high and the low He saved by the gift of bhakti — there is no other giver so merciful.

উত্তম অধম মেলি করাইলা কোলাকুলি অন্ধ বধির যত আছে ।
পঙ্গুয়া চলিল ধাঞা হরি হরি বোলাইয়া দু বাহু তুলিয়া তারা নাচে ॥

*uttama adhama meli karāilā kolākuli andha badhira yata āche |*
*paṅguyā calila dhāñā hari hari bolāiyā du bāhu tuliyā tārā nāce ||*

*Word for word:* uttama adhama meli — bringing high and low together; karāilā kolākuli — made them embrace; andha badhira yata āche — all the blind and the deaf; paṅguyā calila dhāñā — the lame set off running; hari hari bolāiyā — making them say "Hari, Hari"; du bāhu tuliyā — raising both arms; tārā nāce — they dance

**21.3.** He brought the high and the low together in embrace — and all the blind and the deaf;
the lame set off running and, making all call "Hari, Hari!", dance with both arms raised.

প্রেমের বন্যা নিতাই হৈতে অদ্বৈত তরঙ্গ তাতে চৈতন্য-বাতাসে উথলিল ।
আকাশে লাগিছে ঢেউ স্বর্গে নাহি বাঁচে কেউ সপ্ত পাতাল ভেদি গেল ॥

*premera banyā nitāi haite advaita taraṅga tāte caitanya-bātāse uthalila |*
*ākāśe lāgiche ḍheu svarge nāhi bām̐ce keu sapta pātāla bhedi gela ||*

*Word for word:* premera banyā — the flood of prema; nitāi haite — from Nitai; advaita taraṅga tāte — Advaita the wave in it; caitanya-bātāse uthalila — surged in the wind of Chaitanya; ākāśe lāgiche ḍheu — the waves touch the sky; svarge nāhi bām̐ce keu — in heaven no one escapes; sapta pātāla bhedi gela — pierced the seven netherworlds

**21.4.** The flood of prema is from Nitai, Advaita is a wave in it, the wind of Chaitanya raises it high;
the waves touch the sky, in heaven no one can escape — they have pierced the seven netherworlds.

ডুবিল যে নাগ-লোক নর-লোক সুর-লোক গোলোক ভরিল প্রেম-বন্যা ।
কেহ নাচে কেহ গায় কেহ হাসে কেহ ধায় বিশেষে ধরণী হৈল ধন্যা ॥

*ḍubila ye nāga-loka nara-loka sura-loka goloka bharila prema-banyā |*
*keha nāce keha gāya keha hāse keha dhāya biśeṣe dharaṇī haila dhanyā ||*

*Word for word:* ḍubila — drowned; nāga-loka — the world of nagas; nara-loka — the world of men; sura-loka — the world of gods; goloka bharila prema-banyā — the flood of prema filled Goloka; keha nāce keha gāya — some dance, some sing; keha hāse keha dhāya — some laugh, some run; biśeṣe dharaṇī haila dhanyā — the earth was especially blessed

**21.5.** The worlds of the nagas, of men and of gods have drowned, the flood of prema has filled Goloka;
some dance, some sing, some laugh, some run — and the earth is especially blessed.

হেন লীলা করে যেই অদ্বৈত আচার্য সেই অনন্ত অপার রস-ধাম ।
এমন প্রেমের বন্যা স্থাবর জঙ্গম ধন্যা বঞ্চিত হইল বলরাম ॥

*hena līlā kare yei advaita ācārya sei ananta apāra rasa-dhāma |*
*emana premera banyā sthābara jaṅgama dhanyā bañcita haila balarāma ||*

*Word for word:* hena līlā kare yei — he who performs such plays; advaita ācārya sei — is Advaita Acharya; ananta apāra rasa-dhāma — an endless, boundless abode of rasa; emana premera banyā — such a flood of prema; sthābara jaṅgama dhanyā — the unmoving and moving are blessed; bañcita haila balarāma — Balarama was left out

**21.6.** He who performs such plays is Advaita Acharya, an endless, boundless abode of rasa;
by such a flood of prema all the unmoving and the moving are blessed — Balarama alone has been left out.

[^13-48]: PK: vol. 3, PDF pp. 320–321 (printed pp. 309–310), beginning of the 24th pallava "Description of the qualities of Sri Advaita," label
"॥১॥২৩৪৮॥", raga "tathā", MSS P-R-Sa no. 2452 and P-R no. 18. GPT1 — pp. 449–450, section on the associates, no. 35 (mangala), checked against the
scan (PDF pp. 708–709); GPT2 — sec. 6.3, no. 35. In the catalogue (BD-029) it was listed as "GPT only"; it is found in PK — **core** (C).
[^13-49]: Advaita by His prayers (with Ganga water and tulasi leaves) called the Lord to the earth — CC Adi 3; CB Adi 2. "Slowly" (dhīre dhīre) — by
long worship.

## 22. Balarama Dasa — "bhābera ābeśe bahu sītāpati mora pahum̐…" (GPT1 p. 450, no. 36)
*Advaita announces the advent: absorbed in bhava, the husband of Sita sat in a yogic posture — and suddenly with a thunderous roar He
sprang up: "I have brought Him, brought Him to the earth! He who will save the world has risen in Nadia!" — and He dances; at His dance
the earth trembles, men and women dance with the Lord of Shantipura; Advaita's roar has pierced the seven heavens and resounded in the
Paravyoma — the three worlds have learned of Mahaprabhu's coming. Raga suhai.*[^13-50]

ভাবের আবেশে বহু সীতাপতি মোর পহুঁ যোগাসনে বসিয়া আছিলা ।
হঠাৎ কি ভাব মনে হুহুঙ্কার গরজনে অকস্মাৎ উঠি দাণ্ডাইলা ॥

*bhābera ābeśe bahu sītāpati mora pahum̐ yogāsane basiyā āchilā |*
*haṭhāt ki bhāba mane huhuṅkāra garajane akasmāt uṭhi dāṇḍāilā ||*

*Word for word:* bhābera ābeśe bahu — deeply absorbed in bhava; sītāpati mora pahum̐ — Sita's husband, my Lord; yogāsane basiyā āchilā — was sitting in a yogic posture; haṭhāt — suddenly; ki bhāba mane — what bhava in the heart; huhuṅkāra garajane — with a thunderous "hum-hum"; akasmāt uṭhi dāṇḍāilā — abruptly sprang up

**22.1.** Absorbed in bhava, the husband of Sita, my Lord, sat in a yogic posture;
suddenly — what bhava in His heart? — with a thunderous roar of "hum-hum" He abruptly sprang up.

আনিয়াছি আনিয়াছি অবনী-মণ্ডলী ।
জগত তারিবে যেই নদীয়া উদয় সেই ইহা বলি নাচে বাহু তুলি ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*āniyāchi āniyāchi abanī-maṇḍalī |*
*jagata tāribe yei nadīyā udaya sei ihā bali nāce bāhu tuli || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* āniyāchi āniyāchi — I have brought, I have brought; abanī-maṇḍalī — to the circle of the earth; jagata tāribe yei — He who will save the world; nadīyā udaya sei — has risen in Nadia; ihā bali — saying this; nāce bāhu tuli — dances with arms raised

**22.2.** "I have brought Him, brought Him to the circle of the earth!
He who will save the world has risen in Nadia!" — saying this He dances with arms upraised.

তাঁহার উদ্দণ্ড নৃত্যে ভূকম্পন হইল মর্ত্যে ধরণী ধরিতে নারে ভার ।
শান্তিপুর-নাথ সঙ্গে নরনারী নাচে রঙ্গে যেন ভেল আনন্দ-বাজার ॥

*tām̐hāra uddaṇḍa nṛtye bhūkampana haila martye dharaṇī dharite nāre bhāra |*
*śāntipura-nātha saṅge naranārī nāce raṅge yena bhela ānanda-bājāra ||*

*Word for word:* tām̐hāra uddaṇḍa nṛtye — at His violent dance; bhūkampana haila martye — the mortal world quaked; dharaṇī dharite nāre bhāra — the earth cannot bear the weight; śāntipura-nātha saṅge — with the Lord of Shantipura; naranārī nāce raṅge — men and women dance merrily; yena bhela ānanda-bājāra — as if a market of bliss arose

**22.3.** At His violent dance the mortal world quaked, the earth cannot bear the weight;
with the Lord of Shantipura men and women dance merrily — as if a market of bliss had opened.

অদ্বৈতের হুহুঙ্কারে সপ্ত স্বর্গ ভেদ কৈরে পরব্যোমে লাগিল ঝঙ্কার ।
মহাপ্রভু-আগমন জানিলেক ত্রিভুবন বলরামের আনন্দ অপার ॥

*advaitera huhuṅkāre sapta svarga bheda kaire parabyome lāgila jhaṅkāra |*
*mahāprabhu-āgamana jānileka tribhubana balarāmera ānanda apāra ||*

*Word for word:* advaitera huhuṅkāre — at Advaita's roar; sapta svarga bheda kaire — piercing the seven heavens; parabyome lāgila jhaṅkāra — a ringing reached the Paravyoma; mahāprabhu-āgamana — Mahaprabhu's coming; jānileka tribhubana — the three worlds learned; balarāmera ānanda apāra — boundless is Balarama's joy

**22.4.** At Advaita's roar the seven heavens are pierced, a ringing has reached the Paravyoma;
the three worlds have learned of Mahaprabhu's coming — boundless is Balarama's joy.[^13-51]

[^13-50]: GPT1 — p. 450, no. 36 (suhai), checked against the scan (PDF p. 709); GPT2 — sec. 6.3, no. 36. The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS
(catalogue: BD-030); C. Before it in GPT (no. 34) is a short unsigned pada on the joy of Advaita and Sita on the night of the Lord's
appearance.
[^13-51]: Paravyoma is the spiritual sky, Vaikuntha. Advaita, learning of the Lord's appearance, dances in Shantipura — CB Adi 2; CC Adi 13 (on
the night of the appearance Advaita and Haridasa dance in Shantipura).

## 23. Balarama Dasa — "rūpa sanātana saṅge śrījība gosāñi…" (GPT1 p. 466, no. 39)
*The books of Sri Jiva: together with Rupa and Sanatana, Sri Jiva Gosani wrote countless books on bhakti; for his purification the
poet names some: *Gopala-virudavali*, *Krishna-pada-chihna*, *Sri Madhava-mahotsava*, *Radha-pada-chihna*, *Gopala-champu*,
*Rasamrita-shesha*, *Kripambudhi-stava*, *Sapta-sandarbha*, *Sutramalika*, *Dhatu-sangraha*, *Krishnarchana*, *Sankalpa-kalpavriksha*,
*Harinamamrita-vyakarana*: he opened the gates of bhakti. Raga velaor.*[^13-52]

রূপ সনাতন সঙ্গে শ্রীজীব গোসাঞি ।
কত ভক্তি-গ্রন্থ লেখে লেখা-জোখা নাই ॥

*rūpa sanātana saṅge śrījība gosāñi |*
*kata bhakti-grantha lekhe lekhā-jokhā nāi ||*

*Word for word:* rūpa sanātana saṅge — together with Rupa and Sanatana; śrījība gosāñi — Sri Jiva Gosani; kata bhakti-grantha lekhe — writes so many books on bhakti; lekhā-jokhā nāi — beyond counting

**23.1.** Together with Rupa and Sanatana, Sri Jiva Gosani
wrote so many books on bhakti that they cannot be counted.

মনের বাসনা আত্মশুদ্ধির কারণ ।
কতিপয় গ্রন্থ-নাম করিব কীর্তন ॥

*manera bāsanā ātmaśuddhira kāraṇa |*
*katipaya grantha-nāma kariba kīrtana ||*

*Word for word:* manera bāsanā — the heart's wish; ātmaśuddhira kāraṇa — for self-purification; katipaya grantha-nāma — the names of a few books; kariba kīrtana — I shall glorify

**23.2.** Wishing in my heart to be purified,
I shall glorify the names of a few books.

গোপাল-বিরুদাবলী কৃষ্ণ-পদ-চিহ্ন ।
শ্রীমাধব-মহোৎসব রাধা-পদ-চিহ্ন ॥

*gopāla-birudābalī kṛṣṇa-pada-cihna |*
*śrīmādhaba-mahotsaba rādhā-pada-cihna ||*

*Word for word:* gopāla-birudābalī — Gopala-virudavali; kṛṣṇa-pada-cihna — Krishna-pada-chihna; śrī-mādhaba-mahotsaba — Sri Madhava-mahotsava; rādhā-pada-cihna — Radha-pada-chihna

**23.3.** *Gopala-virudavali*, *Krishna-pada-chihna*,
*Sri Madhava-mahotsava*, *Radha-pada-chihna*;

শ্রীগোপাল-চম্পূ আর রসামৃত-শেষ ।
কৃপাম্বুধি-স্তব সপ্ত-সন্দর্ভ বিশেষ ॥

*śrīgopāla-campū āra rasāmṛta-śeṣa |*
*kṛpāmbudhi-staba sapta-sandarbha biśeṣa ||*

*Word for word:* śrī-gopāla-campū — Sri Gopala-champu; āra — and; rasāmṛta-śeṣa — Rasamrita-shesha; kṛpāmbudhi-staba — Kripambudhi-stava; sapta-sandarbha — Sapta-sandarbha; biśeṣa — especially

**23.4.** *Sri Gopala-champu*, and *Rasamrita-shesha*,
*Kripambudhi-stava*, and especially the *Sapta-sandarbha*;

সূত্রমালা ধাতু-সংগ্রহ কৃষ্ণার্চন ।
সঙ্কল্প-কল্পবৃক্ষ হরিনাম-ব্যাকরণ ॥

*sūtramālā dhātu-saṃgraha kṛṣṇārcana |*
*saṅkalpa-kalpabṛkṣa harināma-byākaraṇa ||*

*Word for word:* sūtramālā — Sutramala; dhātu-saṃgraha — Dhatu-sangraha; kṛṣṇārcana — Krishnarchana; saṅkalpa-kalpabṛkṣa — Sankalpa-kalpavriksha; harināma-byākaraṇa — Harinama-vyakarana

**23.5.** *Sutramala*, *Dhatu-sangraha*, *Krishnarchana*,
*Sankalpa-kalpavriksha*, *Harinama-vyakarana*.

নিখিল লিখিলা গ্রন্থ কত কব নাম ।
খুলিলা ভক্তির দ্বার কহে বলরাম ॥

*nikhila likhilā grantha kata kaba nāma |*
*khulilā bhaktira dvāra kahe balarāma ||*

*Word for word:* nikhila — all; likhilā grantha — wrote the books; kata kaba nāma — how many names shall I tell; khulilā bhaktira dvāra — opened the gates of bhakti; kahe balarāma — says Balarama

**23.6.** All these books he wrote — how many names shall I tell?
He opened the gates of bhakti, says Balarama.[^13-53]

[^13-52]: GPT1 — p. 466, section on the associates and followers, no. 39 (velaor), checked against the scan (PDF p. 725); GPT2 — sec. 6.3, no. 39.
The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS (catalogue: BD-031). A pada on the writings of Jiva Gosvami (after the Lord's departure) is not
Gaura-lila in the narrow sense; a poet who lists Jiva's books lived no earlier than the end of the 16th century (C).
[^13-53]: Titles: *Gopala-virudavali*, *Madhava-mahotsava*, *Gopala-champu*, *Sankalpa-kalpavriksha*, *Hari-namamrita-vyakarana*,
*Sutramalika*, *Dhatu-sangraha* are well-known works of Jiva; *Rasamrita-shesha* is his supplement to the *Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu*;
*Krishnarchana-dipika* is a manual of worship; *Krishna-* and *Radha-pada-chihna* describe the marks on the feet; the *Sapta-sandarbha* is
probably the *Shat-sandarbha* (six sandarbhas) together with the *Krama-sandarbha*; the *Kripambudhi-stava* is perhaps one of Jiva's hymns.
Cf. CC Adi 10.85; Madhya 1.

## 24. Ramachandra — "hāhā mora ki chāra adṛṣṭa…" (GPT1 p. 492, no. 25)
*A prayer: alas, how wretched my lot — when Gaura appeared, I was not born; I did not see Gaurachandra, nor Nityananda, nor
Advaita, nor Thakura Sarakara, nor Srivasa and Gadai; the essence of all incarnations, the Sri Gauranga-avatara, I did not
see; I am the grandson of Vamshivadana, the Lord's dear associate — so why is Ramachandra so base? Raga dhanashi.*[^13-54]

হাহা মোর কি ছার অদৃষ্ট ।
যবে গৌর প্রকটিল আমার জনম নৈল তেঁই মুঞি অধম পাপিষ্ঠ ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*hāhā mora ki chāra adṛṣṭa |*
*yabe gaura prakaṭila āmāra janama naila tem̐i muñi adhama pāpiṣṭha || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* hāhā — alas, alas; mora ki chāra adṛṣṭa — how wretched my lot; yabe gaura prakaṭila — when Gaura appeared; āmāra janama naila — I was not born; tem̐i — therefore; muñi adhama pāpiṣṭha — I am low and sinful

**24.1.** Alas, alas, how wretched is my lot!
When Gaura appeared, I was not born — therefore I am low and sinful.

না হেরিনু গৌরচন্দ না হেরিনু নিত্যানন্দ না হেরিনু অদ্বৈত গোসাঞি ।
ঠাকুর শ্রীসরকার না হেরিনু পদ তার না হেরিনু শ্রীবাস গদাই ॥

*nā herinu gauracanda nā herinu nityānanda nā herinu advaita gosāñi |*
*ṭhākura śrīsarakāra nā herinu pada tāra nā herinu śrībāsa gadāi ||*

*Word for word:* nā herinu — I did not see; gauracanda — Gaurachandra; nityānanda — Nityananda; advaita gosāñi — Advaita Gosani; ṭhākura śrī-sarakāra — Thakura Sri Sarakara; pada tāra — his feet; śrībāsa gadāi — Srivasa and Gadai

**24.2.** I did not see Gaurachandra, did not see Nityananda, did not see Advaita Gosani;
the feet of Thakura Sarakara I did not see, did not see Srivasa and Gadai.

কি মোর কর্মের লেখা সে সব নহিল দেখা একা আমি কেন জনমিনু ।
সব অবতার-সার শ্রীগৌরাঙ্গ অবতার না দেখিনু কেন না মরিনু ॥

*ki mora karmera lekhā se saba nahila dekhā ekā āmi kena janaminu |*
*saba abatāra-sāra śrīgaurāṅga abatāra nā dekhinu kena nā marinu ||*

*Word for word:* ki mora karmera lekhā — what fate karma wrote for me; se saba nahila dekhā — none of them did I see; ekā āmi kena janaminu — why was I born alone; saba abatāra-sāra — the essence of all incarnations; śrī-gaurāṅga abatāra — the incarnation of Sri Gauranga; nā dekhinu — I did not see; kena nā marinu — why did I not die

**24.3.** What fate has karma written for me — none of them did I see; why was I born alone?
The essence of all incarnations, the incarnation of Sri Gauranga, I did not see — why did I not die?

প্রভুর প্রিয় স্বগণ ঠাকুর বংশীবদন সুত-সুত হও মুঞি তার ।
অহে গৌর নিত্যানন্দ তবে কেন মতি মন্দ রামচন্দ্র অতি দুরাচার ॥

*prabhura priya svagaṇa ṭhākura baṃśībadana suta-suta hao muñi tāra |*
*ahe gaura nityānanda tabe kena mati manda rāmacandra ati durācāra ||*

*Word for word:* prabhura priya svagaṇa — the Lord's dear associate; ṭhākura baṃśībadana — Thakura Vamshivadana; suta-suta — son's son; hao muñi tāra — I am his; ahe gaura nityānanda — O Gaura, O Nityananda; tabe kena mati manda — why then dull of mind; rāmacandra ati durācāra — Ramachandra, so wicked

**24.4.** The Lord's dear associate is Thakura Vamshivadana: I am his son's son.
O Gaura, O Nityananda! Why then is Ramachandra so dull of mind, so wicked?[^13-55]

[^13-54]: GPT1 — p. 492, section of prayers (prārthanā), no. 25 (dhanashi), checked against the scan (PDF p. 751); GPT2 — sec. 7, no. 25. The pada
is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS (catalogue: RC-003). The poet says plainly that he was born after the Lord's departure and that he is the
grandson of Vamshivadana (Vamshi Dasa) — this is **Ramachandra Gosvami** (Ramai), Vamshivadana's grandson and Jahnava's adopted son
(16th–17th c.), not a contemporary of the Lord; cf. the padas signed "Ramachandra" PK 2064, 2186 (chapters 1, 7), which sound like
eyewitness accounts — apparently another poet. Attribution by GPT (C).
[^13-55]: "Thakura Sarakara" is Narahari Sarakara of Shrikhanda. Vamshivadana Thakura is the Lord's associate, guardian of Shachi and Vishnupriya
after the sannyasa (according to tradition). "Dull of mind," "wicked" are the poet's formulas of humility about himself.

## 25. Ramachandra — "prabhura lāgiyā yāba kon deśe…" (GPT1 pp. 492–493, no. 26)
*A prayer of longing: to what land shall I go for the Lord, who will show me the way? Will I have the fortune to see Gauranga's
feet? Gora is my master, Gora my refuge, Gora my whole wealth; if I do not see Him, I shall give up this wretched life; let my soul,
becoming a bird, fly to where He is and serve Him; let my body mingle with the dust of His feet. Raga dhanashi.*[^13-56]

প্রভুর লাগিয়া যাব কোন্ দেশে কে মোরে সন্ধান কবে ।
গৌরাঙ্গ-চরণ দরশন পাব হেন ভাগ্য মোর হবে ॥

*prabhura lāgiyā yāba kon deśe ke more sandhāna kabe |*
*gaurāṅga-caraṇa daraśana pāba hena bhāgya mora habe ||*

*Word for word:* prabhura lāgiyā — for the Lord; yāba kon deśe — to what land shall I go; ke more sandhāna kabe — who will show me the way; gaurāṅga-caraṇa — Gauranga's feet; daraśana pāba — shall I see; hena bhāgya mora habe — will I have such fortune

**25.1.** For the Lord, to what land shall I go, who will show me the way?
Shall I see Gauranga's feet — will I have such fortune?

গোরা মোর পতি গোরা মোর গতি গোরা সরবস ধন ।
যদ্যপি তাঁহারে না পাই দেখিতে তেজিব ছার জীবন ॥

*gorā mora pati gorā mora gati gorā sarabasa dhana |*
*yadyapi tām̐hāre nā pāi dekhite tejiba chāra jībana ||*

*Word for word:* gorā mora pati — Gora is my master; gorā mora gati — Gora is my refuge; gorā sarabasa dhana — Gora is my whole wealth; yadyapi — if; tām̐hāre nā pāi dekhite — I cannot see Him; tejiba chāra jībana — I shall give up this wretched life

**25.2.** Gora is my master, Gora my refuge, Gora my whole wealth;
and if I cannot see Him, I shall give up this wretched life.

পাখী হৈয়া প্রাণ যাইবে উড়িয়া যে দেশে পহুঁর বাস ।
সতত পহুঁর নিকটে রহিবে হইয়া তাঁহার দাস ॥

*pākhī haiyā prāṇa yāibe uṛiyā ye deśe pahum̐ra bāsa |*
*satata pahum̐ra nikaṭe rahibe haiyā tām̐hāra dāsa ||*

*Word for word:* pākhī haiyā — becoming a bird; prāṇa — the soul; yāibe uṛiyā — will fly away; ye deśe pahum̐ra bāsa — to the land where the Lord dwells; satata — always; pahum̐ra nikaṭe rahibe — will stay near the Lord; haiyā tām̐hāra dāsa — becoming His servant

**25.3.** My soul, becoming a bird, will fly to the land where the Lord dwells,
and will always be near the Lord, having become His servant.

গৌরাঙ্গ-চরণ-ধূলিতে মিশিবে এ ছার শরীর মোর ।
কহে রামচন্দ্র পাদপদ্ম-মধু আস্বাদি রহিব ভোর ॥

*gaurāṅga-caraṇa-dhūlite miśibe e chāra śarīra mora |*
*kahe rāmacandra pādapadma-madhu āsvādi rahiba bhora ||*

*Word for word:* gaurāṅga-caraṇa-dhūlite — with the dust of Gauranga's feet; miśibe — will mingle; e chāra śarīra mora — this wretched body of mine; kahe rāmacandra — says Ramachandra; pādapadma-madhu — the honey of the lotus feet; āsvādi — tasting; rahiba bhora — I shall remain lost

**25.4.** With the dust of Gauranga's feet this wretched body of mine will mingle;
says Ramachandra: tasting the honey of His lotus feet, I shall lose myself.[^13-57]

[^13-56]: GPT1 — pp. 492–493, no. 26 (dhanashi), checked against the scan (PDF pp. 751–752); GPT2 — sec. 7, no. 26. The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or
PS; it was missing from the catalogue (new row RC-007). Its position next to no. 25 suggests the same Ramachandra (Vamshivadana's grandson);
attribution by GPT (C).
[^13-57]: "Master" (pati) — here "lord, refuge" in the spirit of dasya, not in the sense of nagari-bhava. "To what land shall I go for the Lord" —
the longing of a poet who lived after the Lord's departure; cf. Narottama Dasa's prayers to Gaura.

## 26. Balarama Dasa — "bhāi re sādhusaṅga kara sādhu haiyā…" (GPT1 pp. 515–516, no. 59)
*A prayer-instruction: brothers, keep the company of saints, becoming saints yourselves — you will cross the ocean of existence,
singing of Nitai and Chaitanya; having obtained, after eight million four hundred thousand births, the rare human body, do not waste
it; I wear beads and marks, but there is no trace of devotion in me — like the makal fruit: handsome outside, worthless within; sandal
makes all the trees around it like itself — but Balarama, without the company of saints, has remained in the well of existence. Raga
kamoda.*[^13-58]

ভাই রে সাধুসঙ্গ কর সাধু হৈয়া ।
এ ভব তরিয়া যাবে মহানন্দ-সুখ পাবে নিতাই চৈতন্য গুণ গাইয়া ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*bhāi re sādhusaṅga kara sādhu haiyā |*
*e bhaba tariyā yābe mahānanda-sukha pābe nitāi caitanya guṇa gāiyā || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* bhāi re — brothers; sādhusaṅga kara — keep the company of saints; sādhu haiyā — becoming saints; e bhaba tariyā yābe — you will cross this ocean of existence; mahānanda-sukha pābe — you will find great bliss; nitāi caitanya guṇa gāiyā — singing the glories of Nitai and Chaitanya

**26.1.** Brothers, keep the company of saints, becoming saints yourselves:
you will cross the ocean of existence and find great bliss, singing the glories of Nitai and Chaitanya.

চৌরাশী লক্ষ জনম ভ্রমণ করিয়া শ্রম ভালই দুর্লভ দেহ পাইয়া ।
মহতের দায় দিয়া ভক্তিপথে না চলিয়া জন্ম যায় অকারণ বৈয়া ॥

*caurāśī lakṣa janama bhramaṇa kariyā śrama bhālai durlabha deha pāiyā |*
*mahatera dāya diyā bhaktipathe nā caliyā janma yāya akāraṇa baiyā ||*

*Word for word:* caurāśī lakṣa janama — eighty-four lakhs of births; bhramaṇa kariyā śrama — weary of wandering; bhālai — at last; durlabha deha pāiyā — obtaining the rare body; mahatera dāya diyā — laying all upon the great (?); bhaktipathe nā caliyā — not walking the path of bhakti; janma yāya akāraṇa baiyā — life passes in vain

**26.2.** Weary of wandering through eight million four hundred thousand births, you have at last obtained the rare body;
laying all upon the great and not walking the path of bhakti, you let your life pass in vain.[^13-59]

মালা মুদ্রা করি বেশ ভজনের নাহি লেশ ফিরি আমি লোক দেখাইয়া ।
মাকালের ফল লাল দেখিতে সুন্দর ভাল ভাঙ্গিলে সে দেয় ফেলাইয়া ॥

*mālā mudrā kari beśa bhajanera nāhi leśa phiri āmi loka dekhāiyā |*
*mākālera phala lāla dekhite sundara bhāla bhāṅgile se deya phelāiyā ||*

*Word for word:* mālā mudrā kari beśa — wearing beads and marks; bhajanera nāhi leśa — no trace of devotion; phiri āmi loka dekhāiyā — I go about showing myself to people; mākālera phala lāla — the makal fruit is red; dekhite sundara bhāla — handsome and fine to look at; bhāṅgile se deya phelāiyā — broken open, it is thrown away

**26.3.** Wearing beads and marks, but having not a trace of devotion, I go about showing myself to people —
like the makal fruit: red, handsome and fine to look at, but break it open — fit only to be thrown away.

চন্দন-তরুর কাছে যত বৃক্ষ লতা আছে আত্ম-সম করয়ে বায়ু দিয়া ।
হেন সাধুসঙ্গ সার নাহি বলরাম ছার ভবকূপে রহিল পড়িয়া ॥

*candana-tarura kāche yata bṛkṣa latā āche ātma-sama karaye bāyu diyā |*
*hena sādhusaṅga sāra nāhi balarāma chāra bhabakūpe rahila paṛiyā ||*

*Word for word:* candana-tarura kāche — near the sandal tree; yata bṛkṣa latā āche — all the trees and creepers there are; ātma-sama karaye — it makes like itself; bāyu diyā — by its breeze; hena sādhusaṅga sāra — this essence, the company of saints; nāhi balarāma chāra — wretched Balarama has not; bhabakūpe rahila paṛiyā — remained fallen in the well of existence

**26.4.** The trees and creepers growing near the sandal tree it makes like itself by its breeze;
but this essence — the company of saints — wretched Balarama has not: he has remained in the well of existence.[^13-60]

[^13-58]: GPT1 — pp. 515–516, section of prayers, no. 59 (kamoda), checked against the scan (PDF pp. 774–775); GPT2 — sec. 7, no. 59. The pada is not in
PK, BR, KGC or PS (catalogue: BD-033). A prayer of general content; its refrain (the names of Nitai and Chaitanya) links it to Gaura, and so it
is translated; other prayers signed by Balarama without Gaura content are not translated (see the catalogue). C.
[^13-59]: 8,400,000 species of life — Padma Purana; CC Madhya 19. "Laying all upon the great" (mahatera dāya diyā) — the sense is not quite clear:
probably "relying on the mercy of the great but making no effort of one's own."
[^13-60]: The makal is a fruit handsome outside and inedible within — an image of feigned piety. The sandal tree that makes the neighbouring trees
fragrant is an image of the company of saints (sadhu-sanga), CC Madhya 22.

# Chapter 14. Vamshidasa, Nayanananda, Shivananda, Yadu, Govinda and Vasu Ghosha, Krishnadasa, Kanu Dasa and Others: Padas from the *Gaura-pada-tarangini* — Completing the "GPT Only" Group

*This chapter completes the group of padas by poets other than Narahari that are known from the *Gaura-pada-tarangini*
(GPT1 — 1st ed. by Jagadbandhu Bhadra, 1903; GPT2 — 2nd ed., 1934), excluding padas in nagari-bhava. The padas follow the
order of the lilas: mangalacharana and praise of the Gaura-avatara, Gaura's form, the abhisheka in Srivasa's house and the
adhivasa of the kirtana of the "seven groups," Gaura with Gauridasa in the bhava of Krishna and of Radha, the goshtha-bhava and the
festival of colours, the decision to take sannyasa and the lament after it, the Ratha-yatra in Puri, Nityananda (His marriage — in
a pada that Majumdar considers a forgery — His dance and His mercy), Ramananda Raya. Seven padas are signed "Yadu" (nos. 4, 5,
20–23, 26); five of them are also in the *Padakalpataru* (PK 2459, 2460, 1546, 1547, 2300; and PK 1548 without signature, no. 23) —
there the text follows PK with the GPT variants; who this "Yadu" is — Yadunatha Kavichandra, a contemporary of the Lord, or the
later Yadunandana — is not established. Checking against the text of GPT1 showed that the stage-1 catalogue had ascribed to Vamshi,
Gauridasa, Paramananda and Narahari a good many padas of other poets: of the seven padas of "Vamshi," six belong to others
(Vaishnava Dasa, Premadasa, Rajavallabha, Govinda Dasa, Vasu Ghosha, or are unsigned); instead, a goshtha-pada of Vamshidasa
(no. 15) is translated, and the pada "āhā mari kothā gela gorā kām̐cā sonā" (no. 19 — "Vamshi" in the catalogue) is signed by Vasu
Ghosha; the padas of "Gauridasa" are signed by Jagannatha Dasa and Chaitanyadasa, those of "Paramananda" by Vrindavana Dasa and
Gopala Dasa. Four padas (nos. 9, 17, 23, 26) were missing from the catalogue.
Majumdar considers the GPT unreliable for attribution; the attribution of all the padas of this chapter is therefore provisional
(C; D only where authenticity itself is in doubt: an added signature, a forgery). The Bengali original, the variants of GPT1/GPT2 and PK,
and the word-for-word translation are in the full version of the book.*

## 1. Vamshidasa — "jaya re jaya re mora gaurāṅga rāya…" (GPT1 p. 5, no. 8)
*Mangalacharana: glory to Gauranga, to Nityananda and to Gaura's devotees; the poet asks Sitanatha — Advaita Acharya — to
give him the shade of His feet and to keep his wicked mind there: he has no other hope. Raga kamoda.*[^14-1]

জয় রে জয় রে মোর গৌরাঙ্গ রায় ।
জয় নিত্যানন্দ চন্দ্র জয় গৌরভক্তবৃন্দ সীতানাথে দেহ পদছায় ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*jaya re jaya re mora gaurāṅga rāya |*
*jaya nityānanda candra jaya gaurabhaktabṛnda sītānāthe deha padachāya || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* jaya re — glory; mora — to my; gaurāṅga rāya — Gauranga Raya; nityānanda candra — Nityananda the moon; gaura-bhakta-bṛnda — the host of Gaura's devotees; sītānāthe — O Sitanatha (Sita's husband, Advaita); deha — give; pada-chāya — the shade of the feet

**1.1.** Glory, glory to my Gauranga Raya!
Glory to Nityananda the moon, glory to Gaura's devotees! Sitanatha, give me the shade of Your feet!

জয় জয় মোর আচার্য ঠাকুর অগতি পতিত অতি ।
করুণা করিয়া স্বচরণে রাখ এ মোর পাপিষ্ঠ মতি ॥

*jaya jaya mora ācārya ṭhākura agati patita ati |*
*karuṇā kariyā svacaraṇe rākha e mora pāpiṣṭha mati ||*

*Word for word:* jaya jaya — glory, glory; mora ācārya ṭhākura — to my Acharya Thakura; agati — helpless; patita ati — utterly fallen (am I); karuṇā kariyā — being merciful; sva-caraṇe — at Your own feet; rākha — keep; e mora — this my; pāpiṣṭha mati — sinful mind

**1.2.** Glory, glory to my Acharya Thakura! I am helpless, utterly fallen:
be merciful — keep this sinful mind of mine at Your feet.[^14-2]

তোমার চরণে ভরসা কেবল না দেখি আর উপায় ।
মোর দুষ্ট মনে রাখ শ্রীচরণে এই মাগোঁ তুয়া পায় ॥

*tomāra caraṇe bharasā kebala nā dekhi āra upāya |*
*mora duṣṭa mane rākha śrīcaraṇe ei māgom̐ tuyā pāya ||*

*Word for word:* tomāra caraṇe — in Your feet; bharasā kebala — only trust; nā dekhi — I do not see; āra upāya — another way; mora duṣṭa mane — my wicked mind; rākha śrī-caraṇe — keep at the holy feet; ei māgom̐ — this I beg; tuyā pāya — at Your feet

**1.3.** In Your feet alone I trust — I see no other way;
keep my wicked mind at Your holy feet — this I beg at Your feet.

সদা মনোরথ যে কিছু আমার সকল জানহ তুমি ।
কহে বংশীদাস পূর সব আশ কি আর কহিব আমি ॥

*sadā manoratha ye kichu āmāra sakala jānaha tumi |*
*kahe baṃśīdāsa pūra saba āśa ki āra kahiba āmi ||*

*Word for word:* sadā manoratha — constant desires; ye kichu āmāra — whatever is mine; sakala jānaha tumi — You know all; kahe baṃśīdāsa — says Vamshidasa; pūra saba āśa — fulfil all hopes; ki āra kahiba āmi — what more shall I say

**1.4.** Whatever I long for at all times — all of it You know.
Says Vamshidasa: fulfil all my hopes — what more shall I say?

[^14-1]: GPT1 — p. 5, section of mangalacharana, no. 8 (kamoda), checked against the scan IA in.ernet.dli.2015.477854 (PDF p. 264);
GPT2 — sec. 1.2, no. 8. The pada is not in PK, the *Bhakti-ratnakara* (BR), the *Kshanada-gita-chintamani* (KGC) or the
*Padamrita-samudra* (PS) (catalogue: VV-001). Under the signature "Vamshi, Vamshidasa" there are padas of Vamshivadana Thakura, the
Lord's associate, and of a later Vamshidasa (by Majumdar, PK 2851 is his; see chapter 6, no. 16); this pada is a prayer with no
sign of an eyewitness; attribution by GPT (C).
[^14-2]: "Acharya Thakura" — by the refrain (Sitanatha, the husband of Sita) this is Advaita Acharya. After the Lord's sannyasa
Vamshivadana lived with Shachi and Vishnupriya in Navadvipa (according to tradition); a prayer to Advaita is possible from him, but the pada
may also belong to a disciple of Advaita's line.

## 2. Nayanananda — "gorā mora guṇera sāgara…" (GPT1 p. 31, no. 15)
*Praise of Gaura in images: He is an ocean of virtues where waves of prema rise; a spotless moon pouring the nectar of the
holy name; the Himalayan peak from which the Ganga of prema flows; a wish-fulfilling tree; a new cloud that cools everyone; a
mine of bliss. Raga dhanashi.*[^14-3]

গোরা মোর গুণের সাগর ।
প্রেমের তরঙ্গ তায় উঠে নিরন্তর ॥

*gorā mora guṇera sāgara |*
*premera taraṅga tāya uṭhe nirantara ||*

*Word for word:* gorā mora — my Gora; guṇera sāgara — an ocean of virtues; premera taraṅga — waves of prema; tāya — in it; uṭhe — rise; nirantara — without cease

**2.1.** My Gora is an ocean of virtues:
in it waves of prema rise without cease.

গোরা মোর অকলঙ্ক শশী ।
হরিনাম-সুধা তাহে ক্ষরে দিবানিশি ॥

*gorā mora akalaṅka śaśī |*
*harināma-sudhā tāhe kṣare dibāniśi ||*

*Word for word:* akalaṅka śaśī — a spotless moon; harināma-sudhā — the nectar of Hari's name; tāhe — from it; kṣare — drips; dibāniśi — day and night

**2.2.** My Gora is a spotless moon:
day and night the nectar of Hari's name drips from it.

গোরা মোর হিমাদ্রি-শেখর ।
তাহা হৈতে প্রেম-গঙ্গা বহে নিরন্তর ॥

*gorā mora himādri-śekhara |*
*tāhā haite prema-gaṅgā bahe nirantara ||*

*Word for word:* himādri-śekhara — the peak of the Himalayas; tāhā haite — from it; prema-gaṅgā — the Ganga of prema; bahe — flows; nirantara — without cease

**2.3.** My Gora is the peak of the Himalayas:
from it the Ganga of prema flows without cease.

গোরা মোর প্রেম-কল্পতরু ।
যার পদচ্ছায়ে জীব সুখে বাস করু ॥

*gorā mora prema-kalpataru |*
*yāra padacchāye jība sukhe bāsa karu ||*

*Word for word:* prema-kalpataru — the wish-fulfilling tree of prema; yāra pada-chāye — in the shade of whose feet; jība — living beings; sukhe — happily; bāsa karu — dwell

**2.4.** My Gora is a wish-fulfilling tree that gives prema:
in the shade of His feet living beings dwell happily.

গোরা মোর নব জলধর ।
বরষি শীতল যাহে করে নারী-নর ॥

*gorā mora naba jaladhara |*
*baraṣi śītala yāhe kare nārī-nara ||*

*Word for word:* naba jaladhara — a new rain-cloud; baraṣi — raining; śītala kare — cools; yāhe — by which; nārī-nara — women and men

**2.5.** My Gora is a new rain-cloud:
pouring rain, He cools men and women.

গোরা মোর আনন্দের খনি ।
নয়নানন্দের প্রাণ যাহার নিছনি ॥

*gorā mora ānandera khani |*
*nayanānandera prāṇa yāhāra nichani ||*

*Word for word:* ānandera khani — a mine of bliss; nayanānandera prāṇa — Nayanananda's life; yāhāra — for whom; nichani — a ransom offered for the beloved

**2.6.** My Gora is a mine of bliss:
Nayanananda's life is given for Him as a ransom.[^14-4]

[^14-3]: GPT1 — p. 31, section of praise of the Gaura-avatara, no. 15 (dhanashi), checked against the scan (PDF p. 290); GPT2 — sec. 1.3,
no. 15. The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS (catalogue: NN-003). Nayanananda Mishra is the nephew and disciple of Gadadhara
Pandita; his padas on Gaura in PK were translated in chapters 4 and 10. This pada is known only from the GPT (C).
[^14-4]: "Given as a ransom" (nichani) — a rite in which something dear is waved around the beloved and given away to avert harm from
him: the poet gives his life for Gaura. In 2.1 GPT1 has "guṇera nāgara" (a misprint or misreading), GPT2 "guṇera sāgara": the image of an
ocean with waves requires "sagara."

## 3. Shivananda — "akhila bhubana bhari hari-rasa-bādara…" (GPT1 p. 35, no. 25)
*The cloud of Chaitanya: a downpour of Hari's rasa has filled the universe, and the devotees, like chataka birds, drink and ask
for more; the cloud was born on the full moon of Phalguna and flooded high and low with prema; the holy name became the
maha-mantra, prema was given out by handfuls, the fallen became bhagavatas, Jagai and Madhai were saved; the poet laments
that he has remained in forgetfulness. Raga mangala.*[^14-5]

অখিল ভুবন ভরি হরি-রস-বাদর বরিখয়ে চৈতন্য-মেঘে ।
ভকত চাতক যত পিবি পিবি অবিরত অনুখন প্রেম-জল মাগে ॥

*akhila bhubana bhari hari-rasa-bādara barikhaye caitanya-meghe |*
*bhakata cātaka yata pibi pibi abirata anukhana prema-jala māge ||*

*Word for word:* akhila bhubana bhari — filling the whole universe; hari-rasa-bādara — the downpour of Hari's rasa; barikhaye — pours; caitanya-meghe — from the cloud Chaitanya; bhakata — devotees; cātaka — chataka birds; yata — all; pibi pibi — drinking and drinking; abirata — without end; anukhana — every moment; prema-jala — the water of prema; māge — beg

**3.1.** Filling the universe, a downpour of Hari's rasa pours from the cloud of Chaitanya;
the devotees, like chataka birds, drink and drink without end, every moment begging for the water of prema.

ফাল্গুন-পূর্ণিমা তিথি মেঘের জনম তথি সেই মেঘে করল বাদর ।
উচা নীচ যত ছিল প্রেম-জলে ভাসাওল গোরা বড় দয়ার সাগর ॥

*phālguna-pūrṇimā tithi meghera janama tathi sei meghe karala bādara |*
*ucā nīca yata chila prema-jale bhāsāola gorā baṛa dayāra sāgara ||*

*Word for word:* phālguna-pūrṇimā tithi — the lunar day of the full moon of Phalguna; meghera janama — the cloud's birth; tathi — on that (day); sei meghe — that cloud; karala bādara — made a downpour; ucā nīca — high and low; yata chila — as many as there were; prema-jale — with the water of prema; bhāsāola — flooded; gorā baṛa dayāra sāgara — Gora is a great ocean of mercy

**3.2.** The full moon of Phalguna is the cloud's birthday; that cloud poured the downpour:
high and low — it flooded all with the water of prema: Gora is a great ocean of mercy.

জীবেরে করিয়া যন্ত্র হরিনাম মহামন্ত্র হাতে হাতে প্রেমের অঞ্জলি ।
অধম দুঃখিত যত তারা হৈল ভাগবত বাঢ়িল গৌরাঙ্গ-ঠাকুরালি ॥

*jībere kariyā yantra harināma mahāmantra hāte hāte premera añjali |*
*adhama duḥkhita yata tārā haila bhāgabata bāṛhila gaurāṅga-ṭhākurāli ||*

*Word for word:* jībere kariyā yantra — making living beings a yantra; harināma mahāmantra — Hari's name the great mantra; hāte hāte — from hand to hand; premera añjali — handfuls of prema; adhama — the low; duḥkhita — the wretched; yata — all; tārā haila bhāgabata — they became bhagavatas; bāṛhila — grew; gaurāṅga-ṭhākurāli — Gauranga's glory (lordship)

**3.3.** Making living beings His yantra and Hari's name the maha-mantra, He gave prema by handfuls from hand to hand;
all the low and wretched became bhagavatas — so Gauranga's glory grew.[^14-6]

জগাই মাধাই ছিল তারা প্রেমে উদ্ধারিল হেন জীবে বিলাওল দয়া ।
দাস শিবানন্দ বলে কেন রৈনু মায়া-ভোলে প্রভু মোরে দেহ পদছায়া ॥

*jagāi mādhāi chila tārā preme uddhārila hena jībe bilāola dayā |*
*dāsa śibānanda bale kena rainu māyā-bhole prabhu more deha padachāyā ||*

*Word for word:* jagāi mādhāi chila — there were Jagai and Madhai; tārā preme uddhārila — them He delivered with prema; hena — such; jībe — to living beings; bilāola dayā — distributed mercy; dāsa śibānanda bale — says Shivananda-dasa; kena rainu — why did I remain; māyā-bhole — in the forgetfulness of maya; prabhu — Lord; more deha pada-chāyā — give me the shade of the feet

**3.4.** There were Jagai and Madhai — them too He saved with prema: such mercy He showed to living beings.
Says Shivananda-dasa: why have I remained in the forgetfulness of maya? Lord, give me the shade of Your feet![^14-7]

[^14-5]: GPT1 — p. 35, no. 25 (mangala), checked against the scan (PDF p. 294); GPT2 — sec. 1.3, no. 25. The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or
PS. In the catalogue (SS-001) the first line was wrong: "iha kaliyuga dhana nityānanda caitanya" is the preceding GPT pada (no. 24), signed by
Haridasa; the pada signed "dāsa śibānanda" is no. 25. Whether this is Shivananda Sena, the father of Kavi Karnapura, is unclear (C);
Majumdar considers Shivananda Sena the author of padas on the Lord composed in His lifetime.
[^14-6]: The full moon of Phalguna is the day of the Lord's appearance (1486). "Yantra" and "mantra" — an image from ritual: as a sacred
diagram and a mantra serve worship, so living beings became the Lord's vessel and Hari's name the great mantra. The sense of the
