line is not quite clear. A footnote in GPT1 gives "durgata" (distressed) for "duḥkhita" (wretched). "Glory" (ṭhākurāli) — the Lord's
majesty, lordship.
[^14-7]: Jagai and Madhai — CB Madhya 13; CC Adi 17. "The forgetfulness of maya" (māyā-bhole) — the poet of himself: "maya" here in the
everyday sense — forgetting God and attachment to the world; it has nothing to do with the Lord.

## 4. Yadu — "eke se kanayā-kaṣila tanu…" (PK 2459; GPT1 p. 120, no. 27)
*Gauranga's form: His body like gold tested on the touchstone, outshining the moon; curls tied in a knot, garments of red silk;
raising His arms He stretches — and lightning seems to flash; the gaze slips over His body, over which waves run; all pride is
broken. Raga "the same" (in GPT1, "yatharaga").*[^14-8]

একে সে কনয়া-কষিল তনু ।
শশী-নিকলঙ্ক-দমন জনু ॥

*eke se kanayā-kaṣila tanu |*
*śaśī-nikalaṅka-damana janu ||*

*Word for word:* eke — first of all; se — that; kanayā-kaṣila — gold tested on the touchstone; tanu — body; śaśī-nikalaṅka — the spotless moon; damana — subduing; janu — as if

**4.1.** First of all, His body, like gold tested on the touchstone:
as if it subdues even the spotless moon.

তাহাতে লোটন চাঁচর কেশে ।
মাতায় রঙ্গিণী সুষমা-লেশে ॥

*tāhāte loṭana cām̐cara keśe |*
*mātāya raṅgiṇī suṣamā-leśe ||*

*Word for word:* tāhāte — besides; loṭana — a knot (of hair); cām̐cara keśe — with curly locks; mātāya — intoxicates; raṅgiṇī — playful fair ones; suṣamā-leśe — with a trace of beauty

**4.2.** And then — the curly locks tied in a knot:
even a trace of that beauty intoxicates the playful fair ones.[^14-9]

কিবা অপরূপ গৌরাঙ্গ-শোভা ।
এ-তিন-ভুবন-রঙ্গিণী-লোভা ॥

*kibā aparūpa gaurāṅga-śobhā |*
*e-tina-bhubana-raṅgiṇī-lobhā ||*

*Word for word:* kibā aparūpa — how wondrous; gaurāṅga-śobhā — Gauranga's beauty; e tina bhubana — of the three worlds; raṅgiṇī — of the fair ones; lobhā — coveted

**4.3.** How wondrous is Gauranga's beauty —
coveted by the fair women of the three worlds!

অরুণ পাটের বসন ছলে ।
তরুণী-হৃদয়-রাগ উছলে ॥

*aruṇa pāṭera basana chale |*
*taruṇī-hṛdaya-rāga uchale ||*

*Word for word:* aruṇa pāṭera basana — garment of red silk; chale — in the guise of; taruṇī-hṛdaya-rāga — the red (passion) of young hearts; uchale — overflows

**4.4.** In the guise of His red silk garment
the red passion of young hearts seems to overflow.

বাহু উঠাইয়া মোড়য়ে তনু ।
ছটায় বিজুরী ঝলকে জনু ॥

*bāhu uṭhāiyā moṛaye tanu |*
*chaṭāya bijurī jhalake janu ||*

*Word for word:* bāhu uṭhāiyā — raising the arms; moṛaye tanu — stretches the body; chaṭāya — in the radiance; bijurī — lightning; jhalake — flashes; janu — as if

**4.5.** Raising His arms, He stretches His whole body —
and in its radiance lightning seems to flash.

পিছলে লোচন চাহিলে অঙ্গ ।
তনুতে তনুতে তরঙ্গ-রঙ্গ ॥

*pichale locana cāhile aṅga |*
*tanute tanute taraṅga-raṅga ||*

*Word for word:* pichale — slips; locana — the gaze; cāhile aṅga — when one looks at the body; tanute tanute — all over the body; taraṅga-raṅga — the play of waves

**4.6.** The gaze cast upon His body slips off:
over all His body waves run in play.

কেশর-কুসুম-সুষম-দাম ।
যদু কহে সব ভাঙ্গল মান ॥

*keśara-kusuma-suṣama-dāma |*
*yadu kahe saba bhāṅgala māna ||*

*Word for word:* keśara-kusuma — of keshara flowers; suṣama-dāma — a lovely garland; yadu kahe — says Yadu; saba — all; bhāṅgala — is broken; māna — pride (the beloved's offended pride)

**4.7.** A lovely garland of keshara flowers —
says Yadu: all pride is broken.[^14-10]

[^14-8]: PK — vol. 4 (pt. 2), 4th shakha, 29th pallava, mark "॥২॥২৪৫৯॥," raga "tatha," checked against the scan IA 354459 (PDF p. 35,
printed p. 26); in PK the pada stands among the gaura-chandrikas to the description of beauty (before it, Premadasa's PK 2458;
after it, PK 2460 and the description of Radha's beauty, "atha śrīrādhāyāṃ yathā"). GPT1 — p. 120, section on Gaura's form, no. 27
("yatharaga"), scan PDF p. 379; GPT2 — sec. 3.1, no. 27. The pada is not in BR, KGC or PS (catalogue: YD-008). The signature "yadu" (Yadu)
may belong to Yadunatha Kavichandra, a contemporary of the Lord (M-1961 ascribes to him padas on Gaura's bhavas), or to the later
poet Yadunandana Dasa (17th c.); PK 2459–2460 show no sign of an eyewitness; C.
[^14-9]: "Playful fair ones" (raṅgiṇī), "young hearts" (4.4), "pride" (4.7) — the motif of the townswomen captivated by Gaura's beauty:
the language of nagari-bhava (Gaura as nagara); we translate faithfully to the author. Vrindavana Dasa stresses that in this
incarnation the Lord never looked at another man's wife; worship of Gaura in the spirit of "gaura-nagari" is not accepted by the
Gaudiya tradition (Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja, Bhaktisiddhanta). In PK the pada is a gaura-chandrika: it sets the tone
for the description of the beauty of Radha and Krishna, and the attraction here is an image of prema for Krishna, not of a worldly
feeling. "Knot" (loṭana) — hair gathered in a knot; "cām̐cara keśa" — curly locks.
[^14-10]: "Red silk… red passion" — a play on words: "raga" means both "red colour" and "attraction, love." Keshara — the nagakeshara flower
(or kadamba). "Pride is broken" (bhāṅgala māna) — "mana," the beloved's offended pride, melts before Gaura's beauty. PK manuscripts:
"ka" — "chāla," "uchāla," "araṅga" for "chale," "uchale," "taraṅga"; "kha, gha, cha" — "madana" for "damana" (4.1: "subdues Madana").

## 5. Yadu — "bikaca kanayā-kamala-kām̐ti…" (PK 2460; GPT1 p. 120, no. 28)
*Gauranga's form and bhava: the lustre of a full-blown golden lotus, a face like the full moon, teeth like pomegranate seeds,
lips redder than the bandhuli; He walks intoxicated with an unknown rasa, with the gait of a king of elephants; tears flow from
His reddish eyes; remembering His former love He weeps, thundering like a new cloud, and calls: "Where is Gadadhara?" Raga
"the same."*[^14-11]

বিকচ কনয়া-কমল-কাঁতি ।
বদন পূর্ণিমা-চাঁদের ভাতি ॥

*bikaca kanayā-kamala-kām̐ti |*
*badana pūrṇimā-cām̐dera bhāti ||*

*Word for word:* bikaca — full-blown; kanayā-kamala — golden lotus; kām̐ti — lustre; badana — face; pūrṇimā-cām̐dera — of the full moon; bhāti — radiance

**5.1.** A lustre like that of a full-blown golden lotus,
a face shining like the full moon.

দশন-শিখর-নিকর পাঁতি ।
অধর অরুণ বান্ধুলী আতি ॥

*daśana-śikhara-nikara pām̐ti |*
*adhara aruṇa bāndhulī āti ||*

*Word for word:* daśana — teeth; śikhara-nikara — a cluster of pomegranate seeds (rubies); pām̐ti — in a row; adhara — lips; aruṇa — red; bāndhulī — the bandhuli (flower); āti — surpassing

**5.2.** Teeth in an even row, like pomegranate seeds,
lips red — redder than the bandhuli flower.[^14-12]

মধুর মধুর গৌরাঙ্গ-শোভা ।
এ তিন-ভুবন-নয়ন-লোভা ॥

*madhura madhura gaurāṅga-śobhā |*
*e tina-bhubana-nayana-lobhā ||*

*Word for word:* madhura madhura — sweet, sweet; gaurāṅga-śobhā — Gauranga's beauty; e tina-bhubana-nayana — of the eyes of the three worlds; lobhā — coveted

**5.3.** Sweet, sweet is Gauranga's beauty —
coveted by the eyes of the three worlds.

কি জানি কি রসে সতত মাতি ।
গমন মন্থর গজেন্দ্র-ভাতি ॥

*ki jāni ki rase satata māti |*
*gamana manthara gajendra-bhāti ||*

*Word for word:* ki jāni — who knows; ki rase — with what rasa; satata māti — ever intoxicated; gamana — gait; manthara — slow; gajendra-bhāti — like a king of elephants

**5.4.** Who knows with what rasa He is ever intoxicated? —
His gait is slow, like a king of elephants'.

অরুণ নয়নে ঝরয়ে লোর ।
অমিয়া বমে কি চকোর জোর ॥

*aruṇa nayane jharaye lora |*
*amiyā bame ki cakora jora ||*

*Word for word:* aruṇa nayane — from the reddish eyes; jharaye — stream; lora — tears; amiyā — nectar; bame — pours out (lit. "vomits"); ki — is it that; cakora jora — a pair of chakoras

**5.5.** From His reddish eyes tears stream —
is it a pair of chakoras pouring out nectar?[^14-13]

সোঙরি কান্দয়ে পূরব-লেহ ।
যৈছন গরজে নবীন মেহ ॥

*soṅari kāndaye pūraba-leha |*
*yaichana garaje nabīna meha ||*

*Word for word:* soṅari — remembering; kāndaye — weeps; pūraba-leha — the former love; yaichana — as; garaje — thunders; nabīna meha — a new cloud

**5.6.** Remembering His former love, He weeps —
as a new cloud thunders.

কোথা গদাধর বলিয়া ডাকে ।
যদু কহে পহুঁ ঠেকিলা পাকে ॥

*kothā gadādhara baliyā ḍāke |*
*yadu kahe pahum̐ ṭhekilā pāke ||*

*Word for word:* kothā gadādhara — "where is Gadadhara?"; baliyā ḍāke — saying so, He calls; yadu kahe — says Yadu; pahum̐ — the Lord; ṭhekilā pāke — is caught in a whirlpool (a plight)

**5.7.** "Where is Gadadhara?" He calls.
Says Yadu: the Lord is caught in a whirlpool.[^14-14]

[^14-11]: PK — vol. 4 (pt. 2), 29th pallava, mark "॥৩॥২৪৬০॥," raga "tatha," checked against the scan (PDF pp. 35–36); GPT1 — p. 120, no. 28
("tatharaga"); GPT2 — sec. 3.1, no. 28. The pada is not in BR, KGC or PS (catalogue: YD-009); attribution as for the preceding (C).
[^14-12]: "Shikhara" (śikhara) — in poetics, a ruby the colour of a ripe pomegranate seed; PK manuscripts "ka, kha" and the GPT: "daśana sikara nikara"
(a row of drops), "cha": "śikara." Bandhuli — a red flower (Pentapetes phoenicea), a common image for lips. "Redder" (āti = ati; "ka, kha": "ati").
[^14-13]: Chakoras — birds that drink moonlight; Gaura's eyes are a pair of chakoras on the moon of His face. GPT: "āsiyā base ki cakora jorā" —
"has a pair of chakoras come and settled?"
[^14-14]: "Former love" — the love of Vrindavana: remembering His lila as Krishna, the Lord calls Gadadhara — the associate in whom the
tradition sees a manifestation of Radha (*Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika* 147–153). His tears and "thunder" are manifestations of prema,
not of worldly grief. "Caught in a whirlpool" (ṭhekilā pāke) — in the power of prema, unable to come out of it. PK MSS "ka, kha, cha": "lorā,"
"jorā"; "gha": "kānde ki."

## 6. Govinda Ghosha — "snāna kari śrīgaurāṅga basilena dibyāsane…" (GPT1 p. 240, no. 9)
*The abhisheka in Srivasa's house: after the bath Gauranga sits on a splendid seat with Nitai and Gadai to His right and left;
Advaita offers sweets and payasa, Srivasa runs to bring the dishes; Gora eats with Nitai and Gadai, Advaita gives Him tambula,
Narahari fans Him with a chamara, gazing at the three forms; Advaita places tulasi at His feet, saying "Krishnaya namah." Raga
mangala.*[^14-15]

স্নান করি শ্রীগৌরাঙ্গ বসিলেন দিব্যাসনে ডাইনে বামে নিতাই গদাই ।
অদ্বৈত সম্মুখে বসি মিষ্টান্ন পায়স করে শ্রীবাস যোগায় ধাই ধাই ॥

*snāna kari śrīgaurāṅga basilena dibyāsane ḍāine bāme nitāi gadāi |*
*advaita sammukhe basi miṣṭānna pāyasa kare śrībāsa yogāya dhāi dhāi ||*

*Word for word:* snāna kari — having bathed; śrī-gaurāṅga — Sri Gauranga; basilena — sat; dibyāsane — on a splendid seat; ḍāine bāme — to the right and left; nitāi gadāi — Nitai and Gadai; advaita sammukhe basi — Advaita, seated in front; miṣṭānna pāyasa — sweets and payasa; kare — in hand; śrībāsa — Srivasa; yogāya — serves; dhāi dhāi — running

**6.1.** Having bathed, Sri Gauranga sat on a splendid seat, with Nitai and Gadai to His right and left;
Advaita, seated before Him, holds sweets and payasa in His hands, Srivasa runs to and fro serving.

আহা মরি মরি কিবা অভিষেকানন্দ ।
নিতাই গদাই সহ ভোজনে বসিলা গোরা আনন্দে নেহারে ভক্তবৃন্দ ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*āhā mari mari kibā abhiṣekānanda |*
*nitāi gadāi saha bhojane basilā gorā ānande nehāre bhaktabṛnda || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* āhā mari mari — ah, ah (lit. "ah, I die"); kibā — what; abhiṣekānanda — the bliss of the abhisheka; nitāi gadāi saha — with Nitai and Gadai; bhojane basilā — sat down to eat; gorā — Gora; ānande — in bliss; nehāre — watch; bhakta-bṛnda — the devotees

**6.2.** Ah, ah, what bliss of the abhisheka!
With Nitai and Gadai Gora sat down to eat — the devotees watch in bliss.

ভোজন সমাপি গোরা করিলেন আচমন অদ্বৈত তাম্বূল দিল মুখে ।
নরহরি পাশে থাকি তিনরূপ নিরখিছে চামর ঢুলায় অঙ্গে সুখে ॥

*bhojana samāpi gorā karilena ācamana advaita tāmbūla dila mukhe |*
*narahari pāśe thāki tinarūpa nirakhiche cāmara ḍhulāya aṅge sukhe ||*

*Word for word:* bhojana samāpi — having finished the meal; gorā karilena ācamana — Gora rinsed His mouth; advaita tāmbūla dila mukhe — Advaita put tambula in His mouth; narahari pāśe thāki — Narahari, standing beside; tina-rūpa — the three forms; nirakhiche — gazes at; cāmara ḍhulāya — waves the chamara; aṅge — over the body; sukhe — joyfully

**6.3.** Having finished His meal, Gora rinsed His mouth, Advaita placed tambula in His mouth;
Narahari, standing beside, gazes at the three forms and joyfully fans Him with a chamara.[^14-16]

সচন্দন তুলসী-পত্র গোরার চরণে দিয়া আচার্য কৃষ্ণায় নমঃ বলে ।
কহে এ গোবিন্দ ঘোষ হরিধ্বনি ঘন ঘন করিতে লাগিল কুতূহলে ॥

*sacandana tulasī-patra gorāra caraṇe diyā ācārya kṛṣṇāya namaḥ bale |*
*kahe e gobinda ghoṣa haridhvani ghana ghana karite lāgila kutūhale ||*

*Word for word:* sacandana tulasī-patra — tulasi leaves with sandal; gorāra caraṇe diyā — placing at Gora's feet; ācārya — the Acharya (Advaita); kṛṣṇāya namaḥ bale — says "obeisance to Krishna"; kahe e gobinda ghoṣa — says Govinda Ghosha; hari-dhvani — the cry "Hari!"; ghana ghana — again and again; karite lāgila — began to make; kutūhale — rejoicing

**6.4.** Placing tulasi leaves with sandal at Gora's feet, the Acharya says: "Krishnaya namah!"
Says Govinda Ghosha: and all, rejoicing, began to call out "Hari!" again and again.[^14-17]

[^14-15]: GPT1 — p. 240, section of the abhisheka, no. 9 (mangala), checked against the scan (PDF p. 499); GPT2 — sec. 4.1, no. 9. The pada is not
in PK, BR, KGC or PS (catalogue: GG-008). The preceding GPT pada (no. 8) is PK 1538 with the signature of the three Ghosha brothers
(chapter 1, no. 4), on the same scene: Gauranga on the throne after the abhisheka, the meal with Nityananda, tulasi from Advaita; this
pada is its continuation with the signature of Govinda Ghosha alone. Govinda Ghosha is the Lord's associate, an eyewitness according to
Majumdar; but the pada is known only from the GPT (C).
[^14-16]: Gadai — Gadadhara Pandita. "The three forms" — Gaura, Nitai and Gadai; Narahari Sarakara, the Lord's associate from Shrikhanda,
served Him with the chamara (CB Madhya 9 names Narahari among those present; cf. chapter 1, nos. 3–4). The abhisheka and the "great
revelation" (mahaprakasha) in Srivasa's house — CB Madhya 9; Murari 2.12; CC Adi 17.
[^14-17]: "Krishnaya namah" — "obeisance to Krishna": Advaita worships Gaura as Krishna Himself. The Acharya — Advaita Acharya.

## 7. Vasu Ghosha — "jaya jaya dhvani uṭhe nadīyā-nagare…" (GPT1 p. 240, no. 10)
*The abhisheka: cries of "Jaya!" throughout Nadia; Advaita roars: "I have brought Him!" — and dances, Haridasa after Him;
Srivasa and his brothers dance; devotees come running from all sides. Raga dhanashi.*[^14-18]

জয় জয় ধ্বনি উঠে নদীয়া-নগরে ।
গোরা-অভিষেক আজি পণ্ডিতের ঘরে ॥

*jaya jaya dhvani uṭhe nadīyā-nagare |*
*gorā-abhiṣeka āji paṇḍitera ghare ||*

*Word for word:* jaya jaya dhvani — cries of "jaya, jaya"; uṭhe — rise; nadīyā-nagare — in the town of Nadia; gorā-abhiṣeka — Gora's abhisheka; āji — today; paṇḍitera ghare — in the Pandita's house

**7.1.** Cries of "Jaya, jaya!" have risen in the town of Nadia:
today is Gora's abhisheka in the Pandita's house.

এনেছি এনেছি বলে অদ্বৈত গোসাঞি ।
মহা হুহুঙ্কার ছাড়ে বাহ্যজ্ঞান নাই ॥

*enechi enechi bale advaita gosāñi |*
*mahā huhuṅkāra chāṛe bāhyajñāna nāi ||*

*Word for word:* enechi enechi — "I have brought, I have brought"; bale — says; advaita gosāñi — Advaita Gosani; mahā huhuṅkāra — a great roar; chāṛe — lets out; bāhya-jñāna nāi — no outer awareness

**7.2.** "I have brought Him, brought Him!" cries Advaita Gosani;
He lets out a great roar, oblivious of everything around.[^14-19]

বাহু তুলি নাচে নাড়া তাথিয়া তাথিয়া ।
পাছে পাছে হরিদাস ফিরেন নাচিয়া ॥

*bāhu tuli nāce nāṛā tāthiyā tāthiyā |*
*pāche pāche haridāsa phirena nāciyā ||*

*Word for word:* bāhu tuli — raising the arms; nāce — dances; nāṛā — "Nara" (Advaita); tāthiyā tāthiyā — "ta-theiya, ta-theiya" (rhythm syllables); pāche pāche — behind; haridāsa — Haridasa; phirena nāciyā — goes round dancing

**7.3.** Arms raised, "Nara" dances — "ta-theiya, ta-theiya!";
behind Him Haridasa goes round, dancing.

শ্রীবাস শ্রীপতি আর শ্রীনিধি শ্রীরাম ।
হর্ষভরে নৃত্য করে নয়নাভিরাম ॥

*śrībāsa śrīpati āra śrīnidhi śrīrāma |*
*harṣabhare nṛtya kare nayanābhirāma ||*

*Word for word:* śrībāsa śrīpati āra śrīnidhi śrīrāma — Srivasa, Shripati, and Shrinidhi and Shrirama; harṣa-bhare — in delight; nṛtya kare — dance; nayanābhirāma — a joy to the eyes

**7.4.** Srivasa, Shripati, Shrinidhi and Shrirama
dance in delight — a joy to the eyes.

জয় রে গৌরাঙ্গ জয় অদ্বৈত নিতাই ।
বলি ভক্তগণ আসে করি ধাওয়া ধাই ॥

*jaya re gaurāṅga jaya advaita nitāi |*
*bali bhaktagaṇa āse kari dhāoyā dhāi ||*

*Word for word:* jaya re gaurāṅga — glory to Gauranga; jaya advaita nitāi — glory to Advaita and Nitai; bali — crying; bhakta-gaṇa āse — the devotees come; kari dhāoyā dhāi — running together

**7.5.** "Glory to Gauranga, glory to Advaita and Nitai!" —
crying so, the devotees come running.

কেহ প্রেমে নাচে গায় কেহ প্রেমে হাসে ।
গোরা-অভিষেক-লীলা গায় বাসুঘোষে ॥

*keha preme nāce gāya keha preme hāse |*
*gorā-abhiṣeka-līlā gāya bāsughoṣe ||*

*Word for word:* keha preme nāce gāya — some dance and sing in prema; keha preme hāse — some laugh in prema; gorā-abhiṣeka-līlā — the lila of Gora's abhisheka; gāya bāsughoṣe — Vasu Ghosha sings

**7.6.** Some dance and sing in prema, some laugh in prema;
the lila of Gora's abhisheka is sung by Vasu Ghosha.

[^14-18]: GPT1 — p. 240, no. 10 (dhanashi), checked against the scan (PDF p. 499); GPT2 — sec. 4.1, no. 10. The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS
(catalogue: VG-165). The colloquial form "enechi, enechi" ("I have brought") is modern Bengali, unusual for the 16th century; by it the pada is
probably late or reworked; Majumdar warns that the GPT contains forgeries under Vasu's name; but this pada shows no sign of forgery. C.
[^14-19]: By His worship and His call Advaita "brought" the Lord to earth (CC Adi 3; CB Adi 2); for this the Lord called Him "Nara" (nāṛā, 7.3)
(CB, Madhya-khanda). "The Pandita" — Srivasa Pandita; Shripati, Shrinidhi and Shrirama are his brothers (CC Adi 10).

## 8. Vasu Ghosha — "gorā-abhiṣeka kathā adbhuta kathana…" (GPT1 p. 240, no. 11)
*The abhisheka: hearing the wonderful news, the devotees run to the Pandita's house and dance, crying "Glory to Gorachand!";
with them the whole universe dances — moon, sun, stars, Brahma, Indra, the gods, the nagas, the guardians of the quarters.
Raga dhanashi.*[^14-20]

গোরা-অভিষেক কথা অদ্ভুত কথন ।
শুনিয়া পণ্ডিত-ঘরে ধায় ভক্তগণ ॥

*gorā-abhiṣeka kathā adbhuta kathana |*
*śuniyā paṇḍita-ghare dhāya bhaktagaṇa ||*

*Word for word:* gorā-abhiṣeka kathā — the news of Gora's abhisheka; adbhuta kathana — a wonderful tale; śuniyā — hearing; paṇḍita-ghare — to the Pandita's house; dhāya — run; bhakta-gaṇa — the devotees

**8.1.** Wonderful is the news — of Gora's abhisheka:
hearing it, the devotees run to the Pandita's house.

ধাওয়া ধাই করি আসি নাচে কুতূহলে ।
দুবাহু তুলিয়া জয় গোরাচাঁদ বলে ॥

*dhāoyā dhāi kari āsi nāce kutūhale |*
*dubāhu tuliyā jaya gorācām̐da bale ||*

*Word for word:* dhāoyā dhāi kari āsi — running together; nāce — dance; kutūhale — joyfully; dubāhu tuliyā — raising both arms; jaya gorācām̐da bale — cry "Glory to Gorachand!"

**8.2.** Running together, they dance joyfully;
raising both arms, they cry: "Glory to Gorachand!"

চাঁদ নাচে সূর্য নাচে নাচে তারাগণ ।
ব্রহ্মা নাচে বায়ু নাচে সহস্রলোচন ॥

*cām̐da nāce sūrya nāce nāce tārāgaṇa |*
*brahmā nāce bāyu nāce sahasralocana ||*

*Word for word:* cām̐da nāce — the moon dances; sūrya nāce — the sun dances; nāce tārā-gaṇa — the stars dance; brahmā — Brahma; bāyu — Vayu; sahasra-locana — the Thousand-eyed (Indra)

**8.3.** The moon dances, the sun dances, the stars dance;
Brahma dances, Vayu dances, the Thousand-eyed dances.

অরুণ বরুণ নাচে সব সুরগণ ।
পাতালে বাসুকি নাচে নাচে নাগগণ ॥

*aruṇa baruṇa nāce saba suragaṇa |*
*pātāle bāsuki nāce nāce nāgagaṇa ||*

*Word for word:* aruṇa baruṇa nāce — Aruna and Varuna dance; saba sura-gaṇa — all the gods; pātāle — in the underworld; bāsuki nāce — Vasuki dances; nāce nāga-gaṇa — the nagas dance

**8.4.** Aruna and Varuna dance, all the gods;
in the underworld Vasuki dances, the nagas dance.

স্বর্গ নাচে মর্ত্য নাচে নাচয়ে পাতাল ।
পরম আনন্দে নাচে দশ দিক্পাল ॥

*svarga nāce martya nāce nācaye pātāla |*
*parama ānande nāce daśa dikpāla ||*

*Word for word:* svarga — heaven; martya — earth (the world of mortals); nācaye pātāla — the underworld dances; parama ānande — in supreme bliss; daśa dikpāla — the guardians of the ten quarters

**8.5.** Heaven dances, earth dances, the underworld dances;
in supreme bliss the guardians of the ten quarters dance.

আনন্দে ভকতগণ করে হুহুঙ্কার ।
এ বাসু ঘোষের মনে আনন্দ অপার ॥

*ānande bhakatagaṇa kare huhuṅkāra |*
*e bāsu ghoṣera mane ānanda apāra ||*

*Word for word:* ānande — in bliss; bhakata-gaṇa — the devotees; kare huhuṅkāra — roar out; e bāsu ghoṣera mane — in the heart of this Vasu Ghosha; ānanda apāra — boundless joy

**8.6.** In bliss the devotees roar out —
boundless is the joy in Vasu Ghosha's heart.[^14-21]

[^14-20]: GPT1 — p. 240, no. 11 (dhanashi), checked against the scan (PDF p. 499); GPT2 — sec. 4.1, no. 11. The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS.
In the catalogue (VG-031) it was listed under section 3.2, "nagari-bhava" — wrongly: it is the abhisheka, section 4.1, with no nagari
motif; it had not been translated. GPT only (C).
[^14-21]: The Thousand-eyed — Indra; Aruna — the charioteer of the Sun; Varuna — lord of the waters; Vasuki — king of the naga serpents. The
rejoicing of the whole universe at the Lord's revelation — cf. CB Madhya 9 (the gods come to see the mahaprakasha).

## 9. Krishnadasa — "abhiṣeke gauracām̐dera ānanda apāra…" (GPT1 p. 241, no. 13)
*The abhisheka: Gaurachand in boundless bliss tells the devotees of His former plays; His body thrills, His speech falters;
listening to Him, the devotees' hearts are comforted. Raga suhai.*[^14-22]

অভিষেকে গৌরচাঁদের আনন্দ অপার ।
কহয়ে ভকতগণে পূরব বিহার ॥

*abhiṣeke gauracām̐dera ānanda apāra |*
*kahaye bhakatagaṇe pūraba bihāra ||*

*Word for word:* abhiṣeke — at the abhisheka; gauracām̐dera — Gaurachand's; ānanda apāra — boundless bliss; kahaye — tells; bhakata-gaṇe — the devotees; pūraba bihāra — of the former plays

**9.1.** At the abhisheka boundless is Gaurachand's bliss:
He tells the devotees of His former plays.[^14-23]

পুলকে পূরল তনু আপাদ-মস্তক ।
সোনার কেশর জিনে কদম্ব-কোরক ॥

*pulake pūrala tanu āpāda-mastaka |*
*sonāra keśara jine kadamba-koraka ||*

*Word for word:* pulake — with thrill; pūrala tanu — the body was filled; āpāda-mastaka — from head to foot; sonāra keśara — golden filaments (hairs); jine — rival (lit. "surpass"); kadamba-koraka — a kadamba bud

**9.2.** From head to foot His body thrilled:
the golden hairs stood like a kadamba bud.

ভাবে তরল মন গদগদ ভাষ ।
অনেক যতনে বিধি পূরাওল আশ ॥

*bhābe tarala mana gadagada bhāṣa |*
*aneka yatane bidhi pūrāola āśa ||*

*Word for word:* bhābe — in bhava; tarala mana — the heart melts; gadagada bhāṣa — faltering speech; aneka yatane — with great effort; bidhi — fate (the Creator); pūrāola āśa — fulfilled the hope

**9.3.** The heart melts in bhava, the speech falters with emotion:
with great effort fate has fulfilled our hope.

শচীর নন্দন গোরা জাতি-প্রাণধন ।
শুনি চাঁদ-মুখের কথা জুড়াইল মন ॥

*śacīra nandana gorā jāti-prāṇadhana |*
*śuni cām̐da-mukhera kathā juṛāila mana ||*

*Word for word:* śacīra nandana gorā — Shachi's son Gora; jāti-prāṇa-dhana — the life-treasure of all (lit. "of the kin"); śuni — hearing; cām̐da-mukhera kathā — the words of the moonlike mouth; juṛāila mana — the heart was comforted

**9.4.** Shachi's son Gora is the treasure of the life of all:
hearing the words of His moonlike mouth, the heart was comforted.

গোরাচাঁদের লীলায় যার হইল বিশ্বাস ।
দুঃখী কৃষ্ণদাস তার দাস-অনুদাস ॥

*gorācām̐dera līlāya yāra haila biśvāsa |*
*duḥkhī kṛṣṇadāsa tāra dāsa-anudāsa ||*

*Word for word:* gorācām̐dera līlāya — in Gorachand's lila; yāra haila biśvāsa — whoever came to believe; duḥkhī kṛṣṇadāsa — wretched Krishnadasa; tāra dāsa-anudāsa — the servant of his servants

**9.5.** Whoever has come to believe in Gorachand's lila —
wretched Krishnadasa is the servant of his servants.

[^14-22]: GPT1 — p. 241, no. 13 (suhai), checked against the scan (PDF p. 500); GPT2 — sec. 4.1, no. 13. The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS; it was
missing from the catalogue (new row KR-020). The preceding GPT pada (no. 12, "dekha dui bhāi gaura nitāi") is Krishnadasa's PK 1576 (chapter 7).
The signature "Krishnadasa" in GPT and PK covers padas of several poets; attribution by GPT (C).
[^14-23]: "Former plays" — Krishna's lilas in Vraja and the deeds of earlier avataras: during the mahaprakasha the Lord revealed to each devotee
his past and His own former lilas (CB Madhya 9–10). In 9.4 "jāti-prāṇadhana" (lit. "the life-treasure of the kin/of all") — the sense is not
quite clear.

## 10. Vasu Ghosha — "aguru candana lepiyā gorā-gāya…" (GPT1 p. 243, no. 19)
*The abhisheka: Gora's body is anointed with aguru and sandal, the associates fan Him with chamaras and pour water over Him; they wipe
His face, put on Him a garland of malati, dress Him in red garments and ornaments; Vasudeva gazes at that form. Raga
dhanashi.*[^14-24]

অগুরু চন্দন লেপিয়া গোরা-গায় ।
প্রিয় পারিষদগণ চামর ঢুলায় ॥

*aguru candana lepiyā gorā-gāya |*
*priya pāriṣadagaṇa cāmara ḍhulāya ||*

*Word for word:* aguru candana — aguru and sandal; lepiyā — anointing; gorā-gāya — Gora's body; priya pāriṣada-gaṇa — the dear associates; cāmara ḍhulāya — wave chamaras

**10.1.** Having anointed Gora's body with aguru and sandal,
the dear associates fan Him with chamaras.

আনি সলিল কেহ ধরি নিজ করে ।
মনের মানসে ঢালে গৌরাঙ্গ-উপরে ॥

*āni salila keha dhari nija kare |*
*manera mānase ḍhāle gaurāṅga-upare ||*

*Word for word:* āni salila — bringing water; keha — someone; dhari nija kare — holding in his own hands; manera mānase — as the heart desires; ḍhāle — pours; gaurāṅga-upare — over Gauranga

**10.2.** Someone, bringing water and holding it in his own hands,
pours it over Gauranga as his heart desires.

চাঁদ জিনিয়া মুখ অধিক করি মাজে ।
মালতী ফুলের মালা গোরা-অঙ্গে সাজে ॥

*cām̐da jiniyā mukha adhika kari māje |*
*mālatī phulera mālā gorā-aṅge sāje ||*

*Word for word:* cām̐da jiniyā mukha — the face surpassing the moon; adhika kari — still more; māje — they wipe (polish); mālatī phulera mālā — a garland of malati flowers; gorā-aṅge sāje — adorns Gora's body

**10.3.** The face that outshines the moon they wipe to make it shine still more;
on Gora's body is a garland of malati flowers.

অরুণ বসন সাজে নানা আভরণে ।
বাসুদেব ওই রূপ করে নিরীক্ষণে ॥

*aruṇa basana sāje nānā ābharaṇe |*
*bāsudeba oi rūpa kare nirīkṣaṇe ||*

*Word for word:* aruṇa basana — red garments; sāje — adorn; nānā ābharaṇe — with various ornaments; bāsudeba — Vasudeva (Ghosha); oi rūpa — that form; kare nirīkṣaṇe — gazes at

**10.4.** Red garments and various ornaments shine on Him —
Vasudeva gazes at that form.

[^14-24]: GPT1 — p. 243, no. 19 (dhanashi), checked against the scan (PDF p. 502); GPT2 — sec. 4.1, no. 19. The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS
(catalogue: VG-164). GPT only (C). The bathing, anointing and dressing of the Lord at the abhisheka — cf. Vasu Ghosha's PK 1536–1537
(chapter 1, nos. 2–3) and CB Madhya 9.

## 11. Parameshvari Dasa — "prabhura ādeśa pāñā bhakata sakala…" (GPT1 p. 246, no. 27)
*The adhivasa of the kirtana: at the Lord's command the devotees form seven groups, led by Nityananda, Mukunda, Advaita, Gadadhara,
Vasu Ghosha, Murari and Narahari; fourteen madals and fourteen pairs of kartals resound; in the courtyard pots of curd mixed with
turmeric are broken, and with it they mark one another's foreheads. Raga dhanashi.*[^14-25]

প্রভুর আদেশ পাঞা ভকত সকল ।
সাত ভাগ হৈয়া গঠিল সাত দল ॥

*prabhura ādeśa pāñā bhakata sakala |*
*sāta bhāga haiyā gaṭhila sāta dala ||*

*Word for word:* prabhura ādeśa pāñā — receiving the Lord's command; bhakata sakala — all the devotees; sāta bhāga haiyā — dividing into seven parts; gaṭhila — formed; sāta dala — seven groups

**11.1.** Having received the Lord's command, all the devotees
divided into seven parts and formed seven groups.

এক দলের অধিপতি হৈলা নিত্যানন্দ ।
দ্বিতীয়ের মূলগায়ন হইলা মুকুন্দ ॥

*eka dalera adhipati hailā nityānanda |*
*dvitīyera mūlagāyana hailā mukunda ||*

*Word for word:* eka dalera adhipati — head of one (the first) group; hailā nityānanda — became Nityananda; dvitīyera — of the second; mūla-gāyana — the lead singer; hailā mukunda — became Mukunda

**11.2.** At the head of the first group was Nityananda;
the lead singer of the second was Mukunda.

তৃতীয়ের কর্তা হৈলা নিজে সীতাপতি ।
গদাধর চতুর্থের হৈলা অধিপতি ॥

*tṛtīyera kartā hailā nije sītāpati |*
*gadādhara caturthera hailā adhipati ||*

*Word for word:* tṛtīyera kartā — head of the third; hailā nije sītāpati — became Sitapati (Advaita) Himself; gadādhara — Gadadhara; caturthera — of the fourth; adhipati — leader

**11.3.** The head of the third was Sitapati Himself;
Gadadhara became the leader of the fourth.

পঞ্চমের বাসুঘোষ ষষ্ঠের মুরারি ।
সপ্তম দলের নেতা হৈলা নরহরি ॥

*pañcamera bāsughoṣa ṣaṣṭhera murāri |*
*saptama dalera netā hailā narahari ||*

*Word for word:* pañcamera — of the fifth; bāsughoṣa — Vasu Ghosha; ṣaṣṭhera — of the sixth; murāri — Murari; saptama dalera netā — leader of the seventh group; hailā narahari — became Narahari

**11.4.** Of the fifth — Vasu Ghosha, of the sixth — Murari;
the leader of the seventh group was Narahari.

একত্রে বাজিয়া উঠে চৌদ্দ মাদল ।
চৌদ্দ জোড়া করতালে মহা কোলাহল ॥

*ekatre bājiyā uṭhe caudda mādala |*
*caudda joṛā karatāle mahā kolāhala ||*

*Word for word:* ekatre — all at once; bājiyā uṭhe — resound; caudda mādala — fourteen madals; caudda joṛā karatāle — from fourteen pairs of kartals; mahā kolāhala — a great clamour

**11.5.** All at once fourteen madals thundered;
from fourteen pairs of kartals rose a great clamour.

আম্রসার সহ দধি পাত্রেতে রাখিয়া ।
অঙ্গনে ভাঙ্গিলা হরিদ্রা মিশাইয়া ॥

*āmrasāra saha dadhi pātrete rākhiyā |*
*aṅgane bhāṅgilā haridrā miśāiyā ||*

*Word for word:* āmrasāra saha — with amrasara (?); dadhi — curd; pātrete rākhiyā — setting in pots; aṅgane — in the courtyard; bhāṅgilā — broke; haridrā miśāiyā — mixing with turmeric

**11.6.** Setting curd with amrasara in pots,
in the courtyard they broke them, mixing it with turmeric.[^14-26]

হরিদ্রা-মিশ্রিত দধি লইয়া সকলে ।
প্রেমানন্দে দেয় ফোঁটা এ উহার ভালে ॥

*haridrā-miśrita dadhi laiyā sakale |*
*premānande deya phom̐ṭā e uhāra bhāle ||*

*Word for word:* haridrā-miśrita dadhi — curd mixed with turmeric; laiyā sakale — all, taking; premānande — in the bliss of prema; deya phom̐ṭā — put marks; e uhāra bhāle — on one another's foreheads

**11.7.** The curd mixed with turmeric all took up,
and in the bliss of prema they mark one another's foreheads.

এইরূপে কীর্তন-মঙ্গল অধিবাস ।
প্রেমানন্দে গায় পরমেশ্বরীদাস ॥

*eirūpe kīrtana-maṅgala adhibāsa |*
*premānande gāya parameśvarīdāsa ||*

*Word for word:* ei-rūpe — thus; kīrtana-maṅgala adhibāsa — the adhivasa, the blessing of the kirtana; premānande gāya — sings in the bliss of prema; parameśvarīdāsa — Parameshvari Dasa

**11.8.** Thus was the adhivasa — the blessing of the kirtana — performed;
in the bliss of prema sings Parameshvari Dasa.

[^14-25]: GPT1 — p. 246, no. 27 (dhanashi), checked against the scan (PDF p. 505; the catalogue had "p. 247"); GPT2 — sec. 4.1, no. 27. The pada
is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS (catalogue: PD-003). The signature "parameśvarīdāsa" is the same as that of the preceding GPT pada (no. 26 = PK 23,
the kirtana festival at Advaita's house, chapter 5, no. 4), which this pada continues. Parameshvari (Parameshvara) Dasa is an associate of
Nityananda, one of the twelve gopalas (CC Adi 11). By the user's decision it is translated though known only from the GPT (C).
[^14-26]: Madal (mridanga, khol) — a clay drum; kartals — hand cymbals. "Seven groups" (sāta dala, sampradayas) — as at the Ratha-yatra in Puri
(CC Madhya 13), where there were also seven groups and fourteen mridangas; here the poet carries that arrangement over to a kirtana in
Navadvipa. "Amrasara" (āmrasāra) — the sense is unclear (perhaps mango juice or treacle). Marking with turmeric and curd is a festive ritual
game (cf. the "dadhi-haridra" of the Nanda-utsava).

## 12. Vasu Ghosha — "gaurīdāsa saṅge kṛṣṇa-kathā-raṅge…" (GPT1 p. 291, no. 49)
*Gaura with Gauridasa: in a joyful talk about Krishna They embrace, intoxicated with bhava; Gauridasa puts a garland of champaka on
the Lord — and, looking at its golden colour, the Lord remembers Radha: "Gauridasa, Radha has come to My mind!" — and longs to see
Her. Raga dhanashi, tala dashakushi.*[^14-27]

গৌরীদাস সঙ্গে কৃষ্ণ-কথা-রঙ্গে বসিলা গৌরহরি ।
ভাবে হিয়া ভোর ঘন দেয় কোর দোঁহে গলা ধরাধরি ॥

*gaurīdāsa saṅge kṛṣṇa-kathā-raṅge basilā gaurahari |*
*bhābe hiyā bhora ghana deya kora dom̐he galā dharādhari ||*

*Word for word:* gaurīdāsa saṅge — with Gauridasa; kṛṣṇa-kathā-raṅge — in joyful talk of Krishna; basilā gaurahari — Gaurahari sat; bhābe hiyā bhora — the heart absorbed in bhava; ghana deya kora — again and again embrace; dom̐he — both; galā dharādhari — arms round each other's necks

**12.1.** With Gauridasa, joyfully talking of Krishna, Gaurahari sat;
the heart absorbed in bhava, again and again They embrace, arms round each other's necks.

ভাব সম্বরিয়া প্রভুরে বসাঞা গৌরীদাস গৃহ হৈতে ।
চম্পকের মাল আনিয়া তৎকাল গলে দিল আচম্বিতে ॥

*bhāba sambariyā prabhure basāñā gaurīdāsa gṛha haite |*
*campakera māla āniyā tatkāla gale dila ācambite ||*

*Word for word:* bhāba sambariyā — restraining the bhava; prabhure basāñā — seating the Lord; gaurīdāsa — Gauridasa; gṛha haite — from the house; campakera māla — a champaka garland; āniyā tatkāla — bringing at once; gale dila — put round the neck; ācambite — suddenly

**12.2.** Restraining the bhava and seating the Lord, Gauridasa
at once brought from the house a garland of champaka and suddenly put it round His neck.

চম্পকের হার চাহে বারে বার আমার গৌর রায় ।
রাধার বরণ হইল স্মরণ প্রেমধারা বহে গায় ॥

*campakera hāra cāhe bāre bāra āmāra gaura rāya |*
*rādhāra baraṇa haila smaraṇa premadhārā bahe gāya ||*

*Word for word:* campakera hāra — at the champaka garland; cāhe bāre bāra — looks again and again; āmāra gaura rāya — my Gaura Raya; rādhāra baraṇa — Radha's colour; haila smaraṇa — came to mind; prema-dhārā — a stream of prema; bahe gāya — flows over the body

**12.3.** At the champaka garland my Gaura Raya looks and looks:
He remembered Radha's colour — a stream of prema flows over His body.

প্রভু কহে বাস শুন গৌরীদাস মনেতে পড়িল রাধা ।
বাসু ঘোষ কয় রাই রসময় দেখিতে হইল সাধা ॥

*prabhu kahe bāsa śuna gaurīdāsa manete paṛila rādhā |*
*bāsu ghoṣa kaya rāi rasamaya dekhite haila sādhā ||*

*Word for word:* prabhu kahe — the Lord says; bāsa — (unclear; an address?); śuna gaurīdāsa — listen, Gauridasa; manete paṛila rādhā — Radha came to My mind; bāsu ghoṣa kaya — says Vasu Ghosha; rāi rasamaya — Rai, full of rasa; dekhite — to see; haila sādhā — a longing arose

**12.4.** The Lord says: "Listen, Gauridasa, Radha has come to My mind!"
Says Vasu Ghosha: a longing to see Rai, full of rasa, seized Him.[^14-28]

[^14-27]: GPT1 — p. 291, section on the Lord's bhava, no. 49 ("dhānaśrī daśakuśī"), checked against the scan (PDF p. 550); GPT2 — the same section, no. 49 (also in the
GPT2 index of first lines: "gaurīdāsa saṅge kṛṣṇakathāraṅge — bāsu ghoṣa"). The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS (catalogue: VG-166; the first line in
the catalogue, "kata kathā raṅge," is corrected from the scan to "kṛṣṇa kathā raṅge"). GPT only (C). Before it in the GPT stand padas of Radhamohana
Dasa (nos. 43–44) on the same theme: Gaura with Gauridasa, whom He calls Subala.
[^14-28]: Gauridasa Pandita in Krishna's lila is the cowherd Subala, Krishna's intimate friend and helper in His meetings with Radha
(*Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika* 128). The golden champaka garland reminds the Lord of golden Radha; here Gaura is in the bhava of Krishna
longing for Radha — this is the prema of Vraja, not a worldly feeling. "Listen" — the text has "prabhu kahe bāsa, śuna gaurīdāsa": the word "bāsa"
is unclear (by the rhyme, a form of address; possibly a corruption).

## 13. Vasu Ghosha — "gaurīdāsa kari saṅge ānandita tanu raṅge…" (GPT1 p. 292, no. 50)
*Gaura with Gauridasa on the bank of the Suradhuni: in bhava the Lord trembles, tears stream from His eyes, He looks into Gauridasa's face —
and suddenly falls senseless; Gauridasa lifts Him up: "What is Your sorrow?" — "It cannot be told: My heart is breaking." In the bhava
of Radha Gaurahari cannot restrain His heart. Raga bhatiyari, tala dashakushi.*[^14-29]

গৌরীদাস করি সঙ্গে আনন্দিত তনু রঙ্গে চলি যায় গোরা গুণমণি ।
ভাবে অঙ্গ থরহরি দুনয়নে বহে বারি চাহে গৌরীদাসের মুখখানি ॥

*gaurīdāsa kari saṅge ānandita tanu raṅge cali yāya gorā guṇamaṇi |*
*bhābe aṅga tharahari dunayane bahe bāri cāhe gaurīdāsera mukhakhāni ||*

*Word for word:* gaurīdāsa kari saṅge — taking Gauridasa along; ānandita — joyful; tanu raṅge — thrilled in body; cali yāya — goes; gorā guṇamaṇi — Gora, the jewel of virtues; bhābe aṅga tharahari — the body trembles from bhava; dunayane bahe bāri — tears flow from both eyes; cāhe — looks at; gaurīdāsera mukhakhāni — Gauridasa's face

**13.1.** Taking Gauridasa with Him, joyful, thrilled in body, goes Gora, the treasure of virtues;
from bhava His body trembles, tears stream from both eyes — He looks into Gauridasa's face.

আচম্বিতে অচৈতন্য প্রেমাবেশে শ্রীচৈতন্য পড়ি গেলা সুরধুনী-তীরে ।
গৌরীদাস ধীরে ধীরে ধরিয়া করিল কোরে কোন দুখ কহত আমারে ॥

*ācambite acaitanya premābeśe śrīcaitanya paṛi gelā suradhunī-tīre |*
*gaurīdāsa dhīre dhīre dhariyā karila kore kona dukha kahata āmāre ||*

*Word for word:* ācambite — suddenly; acaitanya — senseless; premābeśe — in the ecstasy of prema; śrī-caitanya — Sri Chaitanya; paṛi gelā — fell; suradhunī-tīre — on the bank of the Suradhuni (the Ganga); gaurīdāsa dhīre dhīre — Gauridasa gently; dhariyā karila kore — lifted into his arms; kona dukha — what sorrow; kahata āmāre — tell me

**13.2.** Suddenly losing consciousness in the ecstasy of prema, Sri Chaitanya fell on the bank of the Suradhuni;
Gauridasa gently lifted Him into his arms: "Tell me, what is Your sorrow?"

কহিবার কথা নয় কেমনে কহিব তায় মরি আমি বুক বিদরিয়া ।
বাসু কহে আহা মরি রাধা-ভাবে গৌরহরি ধরিতে নারয়ে নিজ হিয়া ॥

*kahibāra kathā naya kemane kahiba tāya mari āmi buka bidariyā |*
*bāsu kahe āhā mari rādhā-bhābe gaurahari dharite nāraye nija hiyā ||*

*Word for word:* kahibāra kathā naya — it is not a thing to be told; kemane kahiba tāya — how shall I tell it; mari āmi — I die; buka bidariyā — the heart (breast) breaking; bāsu kahe — says Vasu; āhā mari — ah!; rādhā-bhābe — in the bhava of Radha; gaurahari — Gaurahari; dharite nāraye — cannot hold; nija hiyā — His own heart

**13.3.** "It is not a thing to be told — how shall I tell it? My heart is breaking — I am dying."
Says Vasu: ah! — in the bhava of Radha Gaurahari cannot hold His heart.[^14-30]

[^14-29]: GPT1 — p. 292, no. 50 ("bhāṭiyāri daśakuśī"), checked against the scan (PDF p. 551); GPT2 — the same section, no. 50. The pada is not in PK, BR,
KGC or PS (catalogue: VG-167). GPT only (C).
[^14-30]: The bhava of Radha is pure prema, the torment of separation from Krishna (vipralambha); "I am dying" is the Lord's speech in that
bhava, an expression of the utmost intensity of prema, not of worldly grief (cf. CC Antya 14–20). Gauridasa is Subala (see above), the
confidant of the secrets of Radha and Krishna; therefore it is to him that the Lord almost discloses His torment.

## 14. Vasu Ghosha — "bṛndābanera bhābe gorā phirāya pām̐cani…" (GPT1 p. 330, no. 28)
*Goshtha-bhava in Navadvipa: in the bhava of Vrindavana Gora twirls a herding stick and calls the cows, "Ava, aba!"; Shachi is called to
come and see Gora going to the forest to tend the cows; Srivasa's wife runs, and the poet after her. Raga dhanashi.*[^14-31]

বৃন্দাবনের ভাবে গোরা ফিরায় পাঁচনি ।
আবা আবা রবে ডাকে গোরা গুণমণি ॥

*bṛndābanera bhābe gorā phirāya pām̐cani |*
*ābā ābā rabe ḍāke gorā guṇamaṇi ||*

*Word for word:* bṛndābanera bhābe — in the bhava of Vrindavana; gorā — Gora; phirāya pām̐cani — twirls the herding stick; ābā ābā rabe — with the call "aba, aba"; ḍāke — calls; gorā guṇamaṇi — Gora, the jewel of virtues

**14.1.** In the bhava of Vrindavana Gora twirls the herding stick;
"Ava, aba!" calls Gora, the jewel of virtues.

ভাবিছেন গোরাচাঁদ সেই ভাবাবেশে ।
বৃন্দাবনের ভাবে গোরার হইল আবেশে ॥

*bhābichena gorācām̐da sei bhābābeśe |*
*bṛndābanera bhābe gorāra haila ābeśe ||*

*Word for word:* bhābichena gorācām̐da — Gorachand is absorbed; sei bhābābeśe — in that bhava; bṛndābanera bhābe — by the bhava of Vrindavana; gorāra haila ābeśe — Gora is possessed

**14.2.** Gorachand is absorbed in that bhava:
the bhava of Vrindavana has taken hold of Gora.

শচী প্রতি কহে চল যাই দেখিবারে ।
বিপিনে যাইবে গোরা গোষ্ঠ করিবারে ॥

*śacī prati kahe cala yāi dekhibāre |*
*bipine yāibe gorā goṣṭha karibāre ||*

*Word for word:* śacī prati kahe — they say to Shachi; cala yāi dekhibāre — come, let us go and see; bipine yāibe gorā — Gora will go to the forest; goṣṭha karibāre — to tend the cows

**14.3.** They say to Shachi: "Come, let us see —
Gora is going to the forest to tend the cows!"

শ্রীবাসের ব্রাহ্মণী ধাইয়া চলিল ।
বাসুদেব ঘোষ কহে যাইতে হইল ॥

*śrībāsera brāhmaṇī dhāiyā calila |*
*bāsudeba ghoṣa kahe yāite haila ||*

*Word for word:* śrībāsera brāhmaṇī — Srivasa's wife (the brahmana lady); dhāiyā calila — set off running; bāsudeba ghoṣa kahe — says Vasudeva Ghosha; yāite haila — one had to go

**14.4.** Srivasa's wife set off running;
says Vasudeva Ghosha: I had to go too.[^14-32]

[^14-31]: GPT1 — p. 330, section of the year's festivals (goshtha-yatra), no. 28 (dhanashi), checked against the scan (PDF p. 589); GPT2 — sec. 5.1,
no. 28. The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS (catalogue: VG-170). GPT only (C). Gaura's goshtha-lila in Navadvipa is also described by Vasu
Ghosha in BR (p. 935) and PK 1186, 1353 (chapter 1).
[^14-32]: "Herding stick" (pām̐cani) — the stick for driving cows; "aba, aba" — the cowherds' call. Srivasa's wife is Malini, the Lord's nurse.

## 15. Vamshidasa — "śrīnandanandana śacīra dulāla cale goṭhe pāya pāya…" (GPT1 pp. 330–331, no. 30)
*Goshtha-lila in Navadvipa: Nanda's son, become Shachi's darling, goes to the pasture, Nityananda, Rohini's son, running ahead; Abhirama —
Shridama — drives the cows, Gauridasa — Subala — joins the band; Navadvipa has become Gokula, all the associates are dressed as cowherd
boys; the poet goes with them. Raga lalita.*[^14-33]

শ্রীনন্দনন্দন শচীর দুলাল চলে গোঠে পায় পায় ।
রোহিণী-কোঙর নিত্যানন্দ রায় ভাইয়ার অগ্রেতে ধায় ॥

*śrīnandanandana śacīra dulāla cale goṭhe pāya pāya |*
*rohiṇī-koṅara nityānanda rāya bhāiyāra agrete dhāya ||*

*Word for word:* śrī-nandanandana — Sri Nandanandana (Nanda's son); śacīra dulāla — Shachi's darling; cale goṭhe — goes to the pasture; pāya pāya — step by step; rohiṇī-koṅara — Rohini's son; nityānanda rāya — Nityananda Raya; bhāiyāra agrete — ahead of the Brother; dhāya — runs

**15.1.** Sri Nandanandana, Shachi's darling, goes to the pasture step by step;
Rohini's son, Nityananda Raya, runs ahead of His Brother.

শ্রীদাম সাঙ্গাইত অভিরাম স্বামী গাভী বৎস লৈয়া চলে ।
সুবল পণ্ডিত গৌরীদাস আসি তুরিত মিলিল দলে ॥

*śrīdāma sāṅgāita abhirāma svāmī gābhī batsa laiyā cale |*
*subala paṇḍita gaurīdāsa āsi turita milila dale ||*

*Word for word:* śrīdāma sāṅgāita — Shridama the friend; abhirāma svāmī — Abhirama Svami; gābhī batsa laiyā cale — goes driving cows and calves; subala — Subala; paṇḍita gaurīdāsa — Gauridasa Pandita; āsi — coming; turita — quickly; milila dale — joined the band

**15.2.** Shridama the friend — Abhirama Svami — drives the cows and calves;
Subala — Gauridasa Pandita — came and quickly joined the band.[^14-34]

নবদ্বীপ আজি গোকুল হইল যেন দ্বাপরের শেষ ।
পরিকর সবে লইল পাঁচনি ধরিয়া রাখাল বেশ ॥

*nabadvīpa āji gokula haila yena dvāparera śeṣa |*
*parikara sabe laila pām̐cani dhariyā rākhāla beśa ||*

*Word for word:* nabadvīpa āji — Navadvipa today; gokula haila — became Gokula; yena dvāparera śeṣa — as at the end of Dvapara(-yuga); parikara sabe — all the associates; laila pām̐cani — took herding sticks; dhariyā rākhāla beśa — putting on the dress of cowherds

**15.3.** Navadvipa today has become Gokula, as at the end of the Dvapara-yuga;
all the associates took up herding sticks, putting on the dress of cowherd boys.

আবা আবা রবে ছাইল গগন সুরগণ হেরি হাসে ।
তা সবার সহ গোঠেতে চলিল পামর এ বংশীদাসে ॥

*ābā ābā rabe chāila gagana suragaṇa heri hāse |*
*tā sabāra saha goṭhete calila pāmara e baṃśīdāse ||*

*Word for word:* ābā ābā rabe — with cries of "aba, aba"; chāila gagana — the sky was filled; sura-gaṇa heri hāse — the gods look and laugh; tā sabāra saha — together with them all; goṭhete calila — went to the pasture; pāmara e baṃśīdāse — this wretched Vamshidasa

**15.4.** Cries of "Ava, aba!" filled the sky — the gods look and laugh;
together with them all to the pasture went this wretched Vamshidasa.

[^14-33]: GPT1 — pp. 330–331, no. 30 (lalita), checked against the scan (PDF pp. 589–590); GPT2 — sec. 5.1, no. 30. The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or
PS. In the catalogue (VV-007) the preceding GPT pada (no. 29, "abhirāma ḍāke dvārete…") was listed under Vamshi, but it is unsigned (it ends with
the words "bāsu yāya niyā chātā" — "Vasu carries the umbrella"), does not belong to Vamshi and is not translated; the pada signed "baṃśīdāsa" is
no. 30. Attribution by GPT (C). Cf. Vamshivadana's goshtha-pada PK 2564 (chapter 1, no. 12).
[^14-34]: According to the *Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika*, Abhirama Thakura is Shridama and Gauridasa Pandita is Subala, Krishna's cowherd friends;
Nityananda is Balarama, Rohini's son. Vamshivadana himself, according to the GGD, is Krishna's flute.

## 16. Krishnadasa — "khelata phāgu gorā dvijarāja…" (GPT1 p. 339, no. 59)
*The festival of colours: Gora, king of the twice-born, plays with red powder (phagu) with Gadadhara and Narahari, with Nitai and Advaita;
Ramananda Raya plays with Sarvabhauma, Murari and Mukunda with Srivasa and Svarupa; in pairs they shower each other with phagu to cries
of "Hori, hori!"; some dance, some sing. Raga basanta, tala ekatali.*[^14-35]

খেলত ফাগু গোরা দ্বিজরাজ ।
গদাধর নরহরি দুহুঁক সমাজ ॥

*khelata phāgu gorā dvijarāja |*
*gadādhara narahari duhum̐ka samāja ||*

*Word for word:* khelata phāgu — plays phagu; gorā dvijarāja — Gora, king of the twice-born; gadādhara narahari — Gadadhara and Narahari; duhum̐ka samāja — with the circle of both

**16.1.** Gora, king of the twice-born, plays phagu
with the whole circle of Gadadhara and Narahari.

নিতাই অদ্বৈত সহ খেলই রসাল ।
ক্ষণে গালি ক্ষণে কেলি প্রেমে মাতোয়াল ॥

*nitāi advaita saha khelai rasāla |*
*kṣaṇe gāli kṣaṇe keli preme mātoyāla ||*

*Word for word:* nitāi advaita saha — with Nitai and Advaita; khelai rasāla — plays with relish; kṣaṇe gāli — now playful abuse; kṣaṇe keli — now sport; preme mātoyāla — drunk with prema

**16.2.** With Nitai and Advaita He plays with relish:
now playful abuse, now sport — all drunk with prema.[^14-36]

সার্বভৌম সঙ্গে খেলে রায় রামানন্দ ।
শ্রীবাস স্বরূপ সঙ্গে মুরারি মুকুন্দ ॥

*sārvabhauma saṅge khele rāya rāmānanda |*
*śrībāsa svarūpa saṅge murāri mukunda ||*

*Word for word:* sārvabhauma saṅge — with Sarvabhauma; khele — plays; rāya rāmānanda — Ramananda Raya; śrībāsa svarūpa saṅge — with Srivasa and Svarupa; murāri mukunda — Murari and Mukunda

**16.3.** With Sarvabhauma plays Ramananda Raya,
with Srivasa and Svarupa — Murari and Mukunda.

দোঁহে দোঁহে ফাগু খেলে হোরি হোরি ধ্বনি ।
গদাধর সহ খেলে গোরা দ্বিজমণি ॥

*dom̐he dom̐he phāgu khele hori hori dhvani |*
*gadādhara saha khele gorā dvijamaṇi ||*

*Word for word:* dom̐he dom̐he — in pairs; phāgu khele — play phagu; hori hori dhvani — with the cry "hori, hori"; gadādhara saha — with Gadadhara; khele gorā — Gora plays; dvijamaṇi — the jewel of the twice-born

**16.4.** In pairs they play phagu to cries of "Hori, hori!";
with Gadadhara plays Gora, the jewel of the twice-born.

কেহ নাচে কেহ গায় করতালি দিয়া ।
দীন কৃষ্ণদাসে কহে আনন্দে ভাসিয়া ॥

*keha nāce keha gāya karatāli diyā |*
*dīna kṛṣṇadāse kahe ānande bhāsiyā ||*

*Word for word:* keha nāce — some dance; keha gāya — some sing; karatāli diyā — clapping hands; dīna kṛṣṇadāse kahe — says humble Krishnadasa; ānande bhāsiyā — floating in bliss

**16.5.** Some dance, some sing, clapping their hands;
says humble Krishnadasa, floating in bliss.

[^14-35]: GPT1 — pp. 339–340, section of the year's festivals (dola, phagu), no. 59 (basanta, ekatali), checked against the scan (PDF pp. 598–599);
GPT2 — sec. 5.1, no. 59. The pada is not in BR, KGC or PS (catalogue: KR-004); on PK see below. Signature "dīna kṛṣṇadāsa" — attribution by GPT (C). The next
GPT pada (no. 60) is also signed by Krishnadasa (no. 17); no. 61 is Shivananda's (BR, chapter 5).
Full PK check (chapter 16): the pada is also in PK — **PK 1464** (vol. 2, PDF p. 413, label "॥৪০॥১৪৬৪॥", raga basanta, MS P-R-Sa no. 2017; PK: "khelata phāgu gorā dvija-rāja / gadādhara narahari dom̐hāra samāja… dīna kṛṣṇadāse kahe ānande bhāsiyā").
[^14-36]: Playful abuse (gāli) is a custom of the Holi festival. The poet brings together associates of Navadvipa and of Puri (Sarvabhauma,
Ramananda and Svarupa were with the Lord only in Nilachala); historically this is not a single scene but a song-image of the Lord's
festival with His associates.

## 17. Krishnadasa — "phāgu khelata gorā gadādhara saṅge…" (GPT1 p. 340, no. 60)
*The festival of colours: Gora plays with Gadadhara, the two showering each other with kunkuma and squirting from syringes; both are red
from head to foot with phagu — as if in Vraja Kanu and His beloved were playing; the devotees supply phagu, dance and sing; the poet
grieves that he was not born in that happy time. Raga basanta, tala ekatali.*[^14-37]

ফাগু খেলত গোরা গদাধর সঙ্গে ।
কুঙ্কুম মারত দুহুঁ দোঁহা অঙ্গে ॥

*phāgu khelata gorā gadādhara saṅge |*
*kuṅkuma mārata duhum̐ dom̐hā aṅge ||*

*Word for word:* phāgu khelata — plays phagu; gorā — Gora; gadādhara saṅge — with Gadadhara; kuṅkuma mārata — throw kunkuma; duhum̐ — both; dom̐hā aṅge — at each other's bodies

**17.1.** Gora plays phagu with Gadadhara:
the two shower each other with kunkuma.

মারে পিচকারি গুলি গুলাল ।
ফাগুমে দুহুঁ তনু লালহি লাল ॥

*māre picakāri guli gulāla |*
*phāgume duhum̐ tanu lālahi lāla ||*

*Word for word:* māre picakāri — squirt syringes; guli gulāla — balls of gulal; phāgume — with phagu; duhum̐ tanu — both bodies; lālahi lāla — red all over

**17.2.** They squirt from syringes, throw balls of gulal —
from the phagu both are red from head to foot.

খেলে ব্রজে জনু কানু পেয়ারী ।
দুহুঁ বদনে ঘন হোরি হোরি ॥

*khele braje janu kānu peyārī |*
*duhum̐ badane ghana hori hori ||*

*Word for word:* khele — play; braje janu — as if in Vraja; kānu peyārī — Kanu and (His) beloved; duhum̐ badane — on the lips of both; ghana — again and again; hori hori — "hori, hori"

**17.3.** They play as if in Vraja Kanu and His beloved;
on the lips of both, again and again: "Hori, hori!"[^14-38]

চৌদিকে ভকত ফাগু যোগায় ।
কোহি নাচত কোহি আনন্দে গায় ॥

*caudike bhakata phāgu yogāya |*
*kohi nācata kohi ānande gāya ||*

*Word for word:* caudike — on all sides; bhakata — the devotees; phāgu yogāya — supply phagu; kohi nācata — some dance; kohi ānande gāya — some sing in bliss

**17.4.** From all sides the devotees supply phagu:
some dance, some sing in bliss.

কৃষ্ণদাসক চিতে রহল শেল ।
হেন সুখ-সময়ে জনম না ভেল ॥

*kṛṣṇadāsaka cite rahala śela |*
*hena sukha-samaye janama nā bhela ||*

*Word for word:* kṛṣṇadāsaka cite — in Krishnadasa's heart; rahala śela — a thorn (spear) remained; hena sukha-samaye — in such a happy time; janama nā bhela — there was no birth

**17.5.** In Krishnadasa's heart a thorn has remained:
in such a happy time he was not born.

[^14-37]: GPT1 — p. 340, no. 60 (basanta, ekatali), checked against the scan (PDF p. 599); GPT2 — sec. 5.1, no. 60. The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or
PS; it was missing from the catalogue (new row KR-021). The poet says plainly that he was born after the Lord's departure — so this is not a
contemporary but a later poet with the same signature (C).
[^14-38]: Phagu (phāgu), gulal — the red powder of the Holi festival (dola-yatra); kunkuma — red powder. Gadadhara is, by tradition, a
manifestation of Radha (GGD 147–153); Gaura's play with Gadadhara reflects the plays of Radha and Krishna in Vraja; this is the prema of
Vraja, not a worldly amusement. "Hori" — the festival cry.

## 18. Govinda Ghosha — "prāṇera mukunda he tomarā ki sudhāo āmāya…" (GPT1 p. 366, no. 2)
*The Lord discloses to Mukunda His decision to take sannyasa: He left Goloka seeing the sufferings of living beings, but the panditas and
students do not accept His teaching; to save them He will shave His head and take sannyasa — then even the blasphemers will go mad with
the holy name and prema. Mukunda falls senseless; the poet begs the Lord not to end the lila in Nadia. Raga pahira.*[^14-39]

প্রাণের মুকুন্দ হে তোমরা কি সুধাও আমায় ।
যে দুঃখ মরমে পাই কহিবার নাহি ঠাঁই ইহা কহি কাঁদে গোরারায় ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*prāṇera mukunda he tomarā ki sudhāo āmāya |*
*ye duḥkha marame pāi kahibāra nāhi ṭhām̐i ihā kahi kām̐de gorārāya || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* prāṇera mukunda he — O Mukunda, (My) life; tomarā ki sudhāo āmāya — what are you asking Me; ye duḥkha marame pāi — the pain I feel in My heart; kahibāra nāhi ṭhām̐i — there is no one to tell (lit. "no place to tell"); ihā kahi — saying this; kām̐de gorārāya — Gora Raya weeps

**18.1.** "Mukunda, My life, what are you asking Me?
The pain I carry in My heart I have no one to tell," — saying this, Gora Raya weeps.

দেখিয়া জীবের দুখ ছাড়িনু গোলোক সুখ লভিলাম মনুষ্য জনম ।
পাইলাম কষ্ট যত তোমরা পাইলা তত হইল সব পণ্ড পরিশ্রম ॥

*dekhiyā jībera dukha chāṛinu goloka sukha labhilāma manuṣya janama |*
*pāilāma kaṣṭa yata tomarā pāilā tata haila saba paṇḍa pariśrama ||*

*Word for word:* dekhiyā jībera dukha — seeing the sufferings of living beings; chāṛinu goloka sukha — I left the bliss of Goloka; labhilāma manuṣya janama — I took a human birth; pāilāma kaṣṭa yata — as much hardship as I suffered; tomarā pāilā tata — so much you suffered; haila saba paṇḍa pariśrama — all the labour came to nothing

**18.2.** "Seeing the sufferings of living beings, I left the bliss of Goloka and took a human birth;
as much hardship as I have suffered, so much you too have suffered — and all the labour has gone for nothing.

পণ্ডিত পড়ুয়া যারা আমারে না মানে তারা মোর উপদেশ নাহি লয় ।
ভাবি হই বুদ্ধিহারা কিরূপে তরিবে তারা দূর হবে নরকের ভয় ॥

*paṇḍita paṛuyā yārā āmāre nā māne tārā mora upadeśa nāhi laya |*
*bhābi hai buddhihārā kirūpe taribe tārā dūra habe narakera bhaya ||*

*Word for word:* paṇḍita paṛuyā yārā — the panditas and students; āmāre nā māne tārā — they do not accept Me; mora upadeśa nāhi laya — do not take My teaching; bhābi hai buddhi-hārā — thinking, I lose My reason; kirūpe taribe tārā — how will they be saved; dūra habe narakera bhaya — (how) will the fear of hell go

**18.3.** The panditas and students do not accept Me, they do not take My teaching;
thinking of this I lose My reason: how will they be saved, how will they be rid of the fear of hell?

অনেক চিন্তার পর দঢ়াইনু এ অন্তর আমি ত্বরা ছাড়ি গৃহবাস ।
মস্তক মুণ্ডন করি এ ডোর কৌপীন পরি অবিলম্বে লইব সন্ন্যাস ॥

*aneka cintāra para daṛhāinu e antara āmi tvarā chāṛi gṛhabāsa |*
*mastaka muṇḍana kari e ḍora kaupīna pari abilambe laiba sannyāsa ||*

*Word for word:* aneka cintāra para — after much thought; daṛhāinu e antara — I made firm this heart (resolve); āmi tvarā chāṛi gṛhabāsa — I shall soon leave the life of the home; mastaka muṇḍana kari — shaving the head; e ḍora kaupīna pari — wearing the cord and kaupina; abilambe laiba sannyāsa — I shall take sannyasa without delay

**18.4.** After long thought I have made firm My heart: soon I shall leave the life of the home;
shaving My head, putting on the cord and the kaupina, without delay I shall take sannyasa.

তবে ত পাষণ্ডী সব শুনি হরি হরি রব নামে প্রেমে হইবে পাগল ।
সবে যাবে নিত্যধাম পূর্ণ হবে মনস্কাম অবতার হইবে সফল ॥

*tabe ta pāṣaṇḍī saba śuni hari hari raba nāme preme haibe pāgala |*
*sabe yābe nityadhāma pūrṇa habe manaskāma abatāra haibe saphala ||*

*Word for word:* tabe ta — then indeed; pāṣaṇḍī saba — all the blasphemers; śuni hari hari raba — hearing the cries "Hari, Hari"; nāme preme haibe pāgala — will go mad with the name and prema; sabe yābe nitya-dhāma — all will go to the eternal abode; pūrṇa habe manaskāma — the heart's desire will be fulfilled; abatāra haibe saphala — the descent will bear fruit

**18.5.** Then all the blasphemers, hearing the cries of 'Hari, Hari!', will go mad with the holy name and prema;
all will go to the eternal abode, My desire will be fulfilled, and My whole descent will bear fruit."[^14-40]

প্রভু যবে হেন কৈল মুকুন্দ মূর্ছিত হৈল কতক্ষণে সম্বিত পাইলা ।
শ্রীগোবিন্দ ঘোষে কয় এ তব উচিত নয় সাঙ্গ করা নদীয়ার লীলা ॥

*prabhu yabe hena kaila mukunda mūrchita haila katakṣaṇe sambita pāilā |*
*śrīgobinda ghoṣe kaya e taba ucita naya sāṅga karā nadīyāra līlā ||*

*Word for word:* prabhu yabe hena kaila — when the Lord spoke thus; mukunda mūrchita haila — Mukunda fainted; katakṣaṇe sambita pāilā — after a while came to himself; śrī-gobinda ghoṣe kaya — says Sri Govinda Ghosha; e taba ucita naya — it is not fitting for You; sāṅga karā — to end; nadīyāra līlā — the lila of Nadia

**18.6.** When the Lord spoke thus, Mukunda lost consciousness and only after a while came to himself;
says Sri Govinda Ghosha: "It is not fitting for You to end the lila in Nadia."

[^14-39]: GPT1 — p. 366, section "Presage of the sannyasa, the sannyasa, and the journey to Shantipura," no. 2 (pahira), checked against the scan
(PDF p. 625); GPT2 — sec. 5.3, no. 2 (nos. 1–8 of this section are missing from the GPT2 scan). The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS (catalogue: GG-009). It continues GPT pada no. 1 = PK 1606 of Govinda
Ghosha (Gadadhara brings the news to Mukunda, chapter 1, no. 15). Govinda Ghosha is the Lord's associate, an eyewitness according to Majumdar;
this pada is known only from the GPT (C).
[^14-40]: The reason for the sannyasa is the same as in CC Adi 17 (the Lord sees that the students and panditas of Navadvipa offend Him and do not
accept the holy name, and resolves to take sannyasa so that, honouring a sannyasi, they may be saved) and CB Madhya 26. "Blasphemers"
(pāṣaṇḍī) — those who reject bhakti. "Goloka" — Krishna's eternal abode; the Lord's descent is by His own will, not by the law of karma.

## 19. Vasu Ghosha — "āhā mari kothā gela gorā kām̐cā sonā…" (GPT1 p. 385, no. 6)
*A lament after the sannyasa: where has Gora — pure gold — gone? Life did not go out with the words; what use are eyes when their pupil is
gone; His face will be seen no more, His words heard no more; the poet laments that he did not die before. Raga dhanashi.*[^14-41]

আহা মরি কোথা গেল গোরা কাঁচা সোনা ।
কহিতে পরাণ কাঁদে পাসরি আপনা ॥

*āhā mari kothā gela gorā kām̐cā sonā |*
*kahite parāṇa kām̐de pāsari āpanā ||*

*Word for word:* āhā mari — ah!; kothā gela — where has gone; gorā kām̐cā sonā — Gora, pure (raw) gold; kahite — speaking; parāṇa kām̐de — the soul weeps; pāsari āpanā — forgetting myself

**19.1.** Ah! Where has Gora gone — pure gold?
As I speak, my soul weeps; I forget myself.

কহইতে বাণীর সনে পরাণ না গেল ।
কি সুখ লাগিয়া প্রাণ বাহির না হৈল ॥

*kahaite bāṇīra sane parāṇa nā gela |*
*ki sukha lāgiyā prāṇa bāhira nā haila ||*

*Word for word:* kahaite — while speaking; bāṇīra sane — together with the words; parāṇa nā gela — life did not go; ki sukha lāgiyā — for what happiness; prāṇa bāhira nā haila — the soul did not go out

**19.2.** While I spoke these words, life did not go out with them:
for the sake of what happiness has the soul not left the body?

নয়নের তারা গেলে কি কাজ নয়নে ।
আর না হেরিব গোরার সে চাঁদবদনে ॥

*nayanera tārā gele ki kāja nayane |*
*āra nā heriba gorāra se cām̐dabadane ||*

*Word for word:* nayanera tārā gele — if the pupil of the eye is gone; ki kāja nayane — what use are the eyes; āra nā heriba — I shall no more see; gorāra se cām̐da-badane — that moonlike face of Gora

**19.3.** If the pupil of the eye is gone, what use are the eyes?
No more shall I see Gora's moonlike face.

হাসিমুখে সুধামাখা বাণী না শুনিব ।
গৌরাঙ্গ গুণের নিধি কোথা গেলে পাব ॥

*hāsimukhe sudhāmākhā bāṇī nā śuniba |*
*gaurāṅga guṇera nidhi kothā gele pāba ||*

*Word for word:* hāsi-mukhe — from the smiling mouth; sudhā-mākhā bāṇī — words steeped in nectar; nā śuniba — I shall not hear; gaurāṅga guṇera nidhi — Gauranga, the treasury of virtues; kothā gele pāba — where shall I go to find

**19.4.** No more shall I hear from smiling lips words steeped in nectar;
where shall I find Gauranga, the treasury of virtues?

বাসু ঘোষ কহে গোরাগুণ সোঙরিয়া ।
মুঞি কেন সভার আগে না গেনু মরিয়া ॥

*bāsu ghoṣa kahe gorāguṇa soṅariyā |*
*muñi kena sabhāra āge nā genu mariyā ||*

*Word for word:* bāsu ghoṣa kahe — says Vasu Ghosha; gorā-guṇa soṅariyā — remembering Gora's virtues; muñi kena — why did I; sabhāra āge — before everyone; nā genu mariyā — not die (lit. "not go, dying")

**19.5.** Says Vasu Ghosha, remembering Gora's virtues:
why did I not die before everyone?[^14-42]

[^14-41]: GPT1 — p. 385, section of the lament after the sannyasa, no. 6 (dhanashi), checked against the scan (PDF p. 644); GPT2 — sec. 5.4, no. 6. The
pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS. In the catalogue it was listed under Vamshi (VV-008): in the GPT2 OCR (because of the two-column layout) the last
line of another pada — "…śāśuṛī badhūra rodana śuniyā, baṃśī gaṛāgaṛi yāya" (the end of Vamshi's PK 1855, GPT1 pp. 385–386, no. 9; chapter 1) — landed
next to it. The pada itself is signed by **Vasu Ghosha** (new row VG-173). GPT only (C).
[^14-42]: "Gone" — the Lord has left Navadvipa, having taken sannyasa (1510); there is no question of death. "Why did I not die" is the usual formula
of laments, for a devotee to whom separation from the Lord is harder than death.

## 20. Yadu — "aparūpa ratha-āge…" (PK 1546; GPT1 p. 321, no. 2)
*The Ratha-yatra: before the chariot Gora Raya dances, and all the blessed ones sing with Him; in bhava He knows neither day nor night and,
gazing at Jagannatha's face, dances overflowing with bliss; khols and kartals resound, cries of "Jaya!" from gods, men and sages rise to the
sky; the people of Nilachala and pilgrims from many lands swim in the ocean of prema. Raga imana.*[^14-43]

অপরূপ রথ-আগে ।
নাচে গোরা রায় সবে মিলি গায় যত যত মহাভাগে ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*aparūpa ratha-āge |*
*nāce gorā rāya sabe mili gāya yata yata mahābhāge || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* aparūpa — wondrous; ratha-āge — before the chariot; nāce gorā rāya — Gora Raya dances; sabe mili gāya — all sing together; yata yata mahābhāge — all the blessed ones, as many as there are

**20.1.** Wondrous — before the chariot
Gora Raya dances, and all the blessed ones, as many as there are, sing together.

ভাবেতে অবশ কি রাতি দিবস আবেশে কিছু না জানে ।
জগন্নাথ-মুখ দেখি মহাসুখ নাচে গর গর মনে ॥

*bhābete abaśa ki rāti dibasa ābeśe kichu nā jāne |*
*jagannātha-mukha dekhi mahāsukha nāce gara gara mane ||*

*Word for word:* bhābete abaśa — overcome by bhava; ki rāti dibasa — whether night or day; ābeśe kichu nā jāne — in ecstasy knows nothing; jagannātha-mukha dekhi — seeing Jagannatha's face; mahāsukha — in great bliss; nāce — dances; gara gara mane — with an overflowing heart

**20.2.** Overcome by bhava, He knows not whether it is night or day — in ecstasy He is aware of nothing;
gazing at Jagannatha's face, in great bliss He dances, His heart overflowing.

খোল করতাল কীর্তন রসাল ঘন ঘন হরিবোল ।
জয় জয় ধ্বনি সুর নর মুনি গগনে উঠয়ে রোল ॥

*khola karatāla kīrtana rasāla ghana ghana haribola |*
*jaya jaya dhvani sura nara muni gagane uṭhaye rola ||*

*Word for word:* khola karatāla — khols and kartals; kīrtana rasāla — sweet kirtana; ghana ghana haribola — ceaseless "Haribol"; jaya jaya dhvani — cries of "jaya, jaya"; sura nara muni — of gods, men and sages; gagane uṭhaye rola — the clamour rises to the sky

**20.3.** Khols and kartals, a sweet kirtana, ceaseless "Haribol!";
cries of "Jaya, jaya!" from gods, men and sages rise to the heavens.[^14-44]

নীলাচল-বাসী আর নানা দেশী লোকের উথলে হিয়া ।
প্রেমের পাথারে সভাই সাঁতারে দুখী যদু অভাগিয়া ॥

*nīlācala-bāsī āra nānā deśī lokera uthale hiyā |*
*premera pāthāre sabhāi sām̐tāre dukhī yadu abhāgiyā ||*

*Word for word:* nīlācala-bāsī — the people of Nilachala; āra nānā deśī loka — and folk from many lands; uthale hiyā — hearts overflow; premera pāthāre — in the ocean of prema; sabhāi sām̐tāre — all swim; dukhī yadu abhāgiyā — wretched Yadu is luckless

**20.4.** The hearts of the people of Nilachala and of folk from many lands overflow;
all swim in the ocean of prema — but wretched Yadu is luckless.

[^14-43]: PK — vol. 2, 3rd shakha, 29th pallava (the Ratha-yatra: "śrīgauracandrasya rathāgre nartanaṃ yathā"), mark "॥৩॥১৫৪৬॥," raga imana (MS P-R-Sa no. 2091 —
"imana kalyāṇa"), checked against the scan IA 336618 (PDF pp. 454–455; the end of the first stanza is effaced in the scan — given from GPT1). GPT1 —
p. 321, section of the Ratha-yatra, no. 2 (imana), scan PDF p. 580; GPT2 — sec. 5.1 (Ratha-yatra), no. 2. Before it in PK stand a pada of Vaishnava
Dasa (PK 1544) and an excerpt from CC Madhya 13 (PK 1545). In the catalogue — YD-010. Signature "dukhī yadu abhāgiyā"; who this Yadu is — Yadunatha
Kavichandra or the later Yadunandana — is not established; the pada, like the following ones, is close to the account of CC Madhya 13 and is probably
late (C).
[^14-44]: Khol — the mridanga; kartals — hand cymbals. "Haribol" — "Utter Hari's name!"

## 21. Yadu — "caudike mahānta meli karaye kīrtana keli…" (PK 1547; GPT1 p. 322, no. 3)
*The Ratha-yatra: on all sides seven kirtana groups, fourteen khols resound, Jagannatha rejoices; in the middle, among Nityananda, Advaita, Srivasa
and Haridasa, Gaurahari dances, the earth shakes under His steps, on His body the eight sattvika-bhavas; in ecstasy He dances, and Jagannatha moves
slowly after Him; grief and sorrow are gone, prema has flooded all that lives. Raga mangala, tala kandarpa.*[^14-45]

চৌদিকে মহান্ত মেলি করয়ে কীর্তন কেলি সাত সম্প্রদায় গায় গীত ।
বাজে চতুর্দশ খোল গগন ভেদিল রোল দেখি জগন্নাথ আনন্দিত ॥

*caudike mahānta meli karaye kīrtana keli sāta sampradāya gāya gīta |*
*bāje caturdaśa khola gagana bhedila rola dekhi jagannātha ānandita ||*

*Word for word:* caudike — on all sides; mahānta meli — great souls gathering; karaye kīrtana keli — engage in the sport of kirtana; sāta sampradāya gāya gīta — seven groups sing songs; bāje caturdaśa khola — fourteen khols sound; gagana bhedila rola — the roar pierced the sky; dekhi jagannātha ānandita — seeing, Jagannatha rejoices

**21.1.** On all sides great souls have gathered and give themselves to the sport of kirtana — seven groups sing songs;
fourteen khols resound, the roar has pierced the sky — seeing it, Jagannatha rejoices.

উনমত নিত্যানন্দ আচার্য অদ্বৈতচন্দ্র পণ্ডিত শ্রীবাস হরিদাস ।
এ সভারে সঙ্গে করি মাঝে নাচে গৌরহরি ভকত-মণ্ডল চারি পাশ ॥

*unamata nityānanda ācārya advaitacandra paṇḍita śrībāsa haridāsa |*
*e sabhāre saṅge kari mājhe nāce gaurahari bhakata-maṇḍala cāri pāśa ||*

*Word for word:* unamata nityānanda — maddened Nityananda; ācārya advaitacandra — Acharya Advaitachandra; paṇḍita śrībāsa haridāsa — Pandita Srivasa, Haridasa; e sabhāre saṅge kari — taking them all along; mājhe nāce gaurahari — in the middle Gaurahari dances; bhakata-maṇḍala cāri pāśa — the circle of devotees all around

**21.2.** Maddened Nityananda, Acharya Advaitachandra, Pandita Srivasa, Haridasa —
taking them all with Him, Gaurahari dances in the middle, and around Him the circle of devotees.

হরি হরি বোল বোলে পদভরে মহী দোলে নয়ানে বহয়ে জলধার ।
প্রেমের তরঙ্গ-রঙ্গ সুমেরু জিনিয়া অঙ্গ তাহে অষ্ট সাত্ত্বিক-বিকার ॥

*hari hari bola bole padabhare mahī dole nayāne bahaye jaladhāra |*
*premera taraṅga-raṅga sumeru jiniyā aṅga tāhe aṣṭa sāttvika-bikāra ||*

*Word for word:* hari hari bola bole — cry "Hari, Hari"; pada-bhare — under the steps; mahī dole — the earth sways; nayāne bahaye jala-dhāra — streams of tears flow from the eyes; premera taraṅga-raṅga — the play of waves of prema; sumeru jiniyā aṅga — a body surpassing Sumeru; tāhe — on it; aṣṭa sāttvika-bikāra — the eight sattvika transformations

**21.3.** They cry "Hari, Hari!" — under the steps the earth sways, from the eyes flow streams of tears;
waves of prema play on His body, surpassing Mount Sumeru — on it all eight sattvika-bhavas.[^14-46]

ভাবাবেশে গোরারায় নাচিতে নাচিতে যায় ধীরে ধীরে চলে জগন্নাথ ।
আনন্দ বিস্ময় মন দেখি প্রেম-সংকীর্তন নিজ পরিকরগণ সাথ ॥

*bhābābeśe gorārāya nācite nācite yāya dhīre dhīre cale jagannātha |*
*ānanda bismaya mana dekhi prema-saṃkīrtana nija parikaragaṇa sātha ||*

*Word for word:* bhābābeśe — in ecstasy; gorārāya — Gora Raya; nācite nācite yāya — goes dancing; dhīre dhīre cale jagannātha — slowly moves Jagannatha; ānanda bismaya mana — with a joyful, amazed heart; dekhi prema-saṃkīrtana — seeing the sankirtana of prema; nija parikara-gaṇa sātha — with His own associates

**21.4.** In ecstasy Gora Raya goes dancing — slowly, slowly moves Jagannatha;
amazed and joyful, He watches the sankirtana of prema of His own circle of associates.[^14-47]

দূরে গেল দুঃখ শোক প্রেমায় ভাসিল লোক স্থাবর জঙ্গম পশু পাখী ।
যে প্রেম-বিলাস-ধাম যদু কহে অনুপাম যে দেখিল সেই তার সাথী ॥

*dūre gela duḥkha śoka premāya bhāsila loka sthābara jaṅgama paśu pākhī |*
*ye prema-bilāsa-dhāma yadu kahe anupāma ye dekhila sei tāra sāthī ||*

*Word for word:* dūre gela — went away; duḥkha śoka — grief and sorrow; premāya bhāsila loka — prema flooded the people; sthābara jaṅgama — the unmoving and the moving; paśu pākhī — beasts and birds; ye prema-bilāsa-dhāma — this abode of the plays of prema; yadu kahe — says Yadu; anupāma — incomparable; ye dekhila — whoever saw; sei tāra sāthī — became its companion

**21.5.** Gone are grief and sorrow, prema has flooded the people — the unmoving and the moving, beasts and birds;
says Yadu: incomparable is this abode of the plays of prema — whoever saw it became its companion.

[^14-45]: PK — vol. 2, 29th pallava, mark "॥৪॥১৫৪৭॥," raga mangala, tala kandarpa (MS P-R-Sa no. 2092), checked against the scan (PDF p. 455); GPT1 — p. 322,
no. 3 ("maṅgala-kandarpatāla"), scan PDF p. 581; GPT2 — sec. 5.1, no. 3. In the catalogue — YD-011. The pada retells CC Madhya 13 (seven groups,
fourteen mridangas, eight sattvika-bhavas); attribution as for the preceding (C).
[^14-46]: The eight sattvika-bhavas — stupefaction, perspiration, horripilation, faltering of the voice, trembling, change of colour, tears, fainting
(CC Madhya 13). Sumeru — the golden mountain: an image of the Lord's golden body.
[^14-47]: The second line of this stanza ("ānanda bismaya mana…") is not in PK — the stanza is incomplete there; it is given from GPT1. "Amazed and joyful" —
according to CC Madhya 13, Jagannatha, seeing the Lord's dance, rejoices and slows the chariot; here it apparently refers to Jagannatha watching
the kirtana.

## 22. Yadu — "līlākārī jagannātha…" (GPT1 pp. 322–323, no. 5)
*The Ratha-yatra: halfway along, Jagannatha's chariot suddenly stops; gods, asuras and men pull it, the temple servants curse, at the king's order
hundreds of elephants are harnessed — it does not move a step; then Gora Raya goes behind and pushes the chariot with His head — and it races
off with the speed of the wind; the pilgrims rejoice, the poet is amazed at the power of the Two. Raga imana.*[^14-48]

লীলাকারী জগন্নাথ ।
চলিতে চলিতে যেয়ে অর্ধপথে রথ থামে অকস্মাৎ ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*līlākārī jagannātha |*
*calite calite yeye ardhapathe ratha thāme akasmāt || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* līlākārī jagannātha — Jagannatha is playing (performing lila); calite calite — as it goes along; yeye ardha-pathe — reaching halfway; ratha thāme akasmāt — the chariot suddenly stops

**22.1.** Jagannatha is playing:
midway along the road, as it goes, the chariot suddenly stops.

সুরাসুর নরে টানিল রথেরে তবু না চলয়ে রথ ।
পড়িছা পূজারি বেত্র হস্তে করি গালি পাড়ে কত মত ॥

*surāsura nare ṭānila rathere tabu nā calaye ratha |*
*paṛichā pūjāri betra haste kari gāli pāṛe kata mata ||*

*Word for word:* surāsura nare — gods, asuras and men; ṭānila rathere — pulled the chariot; tabu nā calaye ratha — still the chariot does not move; pariṛchā pūjāri — the superintendent and the priests; betra haste kari — canes in hand; gāli pāṛe — curse; kata mata — in every way

**22.2.** Gods, asuras and men pulled the chariot — and still it does not move;
the parichha and the pujaris, canes in hand, curse in every way.[^14-49]

রাজার আদেশে জোড়ে দুই পাশে শত শত করিবর ।
টানে রথ বলে তথাপি না চলে এক পদ রথবর ॥

*rājāra ādeśe joṛe dui pāśe śata śata karibara |*
*ṭāne ratha bale tathāpi nā cale eka pada rathabara ||*

*Word for word:* rājāra ādeśe — by the king's order; joṛe dui pāśe — they harness on both sides; śata śata karibara — hundreds of mighty elephants; ṭāne ratha bale — pull the chariot with force; tathāpi nā cale — yet it does not move; eka pada — (even) one step; rathabara — the best of chariots

**22.3.** At the king's order hundreds of mighty elephants are harnessed on both sides;
they pull the chariot with all their strength — yet the best of chariots does not move a single step.

তবে গোরারায় রথ পাছে যায় শিরেতে ঠেলিছে রথ ।
বায়ুর বেগেতে নিমেষ মাঝেতে চলিল যোজন শত ॥

*tabe gorārāya ratha pāche yāya śirete ṭheliche ratha |*
*bāyura begete nimeṣa mājhete calila yojana śata ||*

*Word for word:* tabe gorārāya — then Gora Raya; ratha pāche yāya — goes behind the chariot; śirete ṭheliche ratha — pushes the chariot with His head; bāyura begete — with the speed of the wind; nimeṣa mājhete — in an instant; calila yojana śata — it went a hundred yojanas

**22.4.** Then Gora Raya goes behind the chariot and pushes it with His head —
and with the speed of the wind, in a moment, it sped a hundred yojanas.

জয় গৌর বলি দুই বাহু তুলি করে রোল যাত্রিগণ ।
দুঁহার প্রভাব করি অনুভব যদুর বিস্মিত মন ॥

*jaya gaura bali dui bāhu tuli kare rola yātrigaṇa |*
*dum̐hāra prabhāba kari anubhaba yadura bismita mana ||*

*Word for word:* jaya gaura bali — crying "Glory to Gaura!"; dui bāhu tuli — raising both arms; kare rola yātri-gaṇa — the pilgrims shout; duṃhāra prabhāba — the power of the Two; kari anubhaba — perceiving; yadura bismita mana — Yadu's heart is amazed

**22.5.** "Glory to Gaura!" — raising both arms, the pilgrims cry;
grasping the power of the Two, Yadu was filled with wonder.[^14-50]

[^14-48]: GPT1 — pp. 322–323, no. 5 (imana), checked against the scan (PDF pp. 581–582); GPT2 — sec. 5.1, no. 5. The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS (catalogue: YD-013).
It retells CC Madhya 14 (the chariot stops, the king orders elephants to be harnessed, the Lord pushes it with His head). Signature "yadu"; a late pada
after the CC (C).
[^14-49]: "Is playing" (līlākārī) — the stopping of the chariot is the play of Jagannatha Himself. Parichha — the temple superintendent; pujaris — the
priest-servants.
[^14-50]: "A hundred yojanas" — poetic hyperbole (in the CC the chariot "rolled on, rumbling"). "The Two" — Jagannatha and Gaura.

## 23. Yadunatha Dasa — "caitanya nitāi āre dona bhāi nāce re…" (PK 1548 unsigned; GPT1 p. 323, no. 6)
*The Ratha-yatra: the two brothers, Chaitanya and Nitai, dance, khols and kartals sound; the golden lotus sways in the ocean of the nectar of
prema, and its wave touches all — high, middling and low; the seven groups sing aloud, and to each it seems that Gora Raya is dancing everywhere at
once; the poet begs a particle of mercy. Raga ramakeli, tala trayar.*[^14-51]

চৈতন্য নিতাই আরে দোন ভাই নাচে রে ।
খোল করতাল পঞ্চম রসাল তাথৈয়া তাথৈয়া বাজে রে ॥

*caitanya nitāi āre dona bhāi nāce re |*
*khola karatāla pañcama rasāla tāthaiyā tāthaiyā bāje re ||*

*Word for word:* caitanya nitāi — Chaitanya and Nitai; āre — oh!; dona bhāi — the two brothers; nāce re — dance; khola karatāla — khols and kartals; pañcama rasāla — the sweet fifth note; tāthaiyā tāthaiyā — "ta-theiya, ta-theiya"; bāje re — sounds

**23.1.** Chaitanya and Nitai — the two brothers — dance!
Khols and kartals, the sweet fifth note — "ta-theiya, ta-theiya" it sounds.

সোনার কমল করে টলমল প্রেম-সুধা-সিন্ধু মাঝে রে ।
উত্তম মধ্যম দীন হীন জন এ ঢেউ সভারে বাজে রে ॥

*sonāra kamala kare ṭalamala prema-sudhā-sindhu mājhe re |*
*uttama madhyama dīna hīna jana e ḍheu sabhāre bāje re ||*

*Word for word:* sonāra kamala — the golden lotus; kare ṭalamala — sways; prema-sudhā-sindhu mājhe — in the ocean of the nectar of prema; uttama madhyama — the high, the middling; dīna hīna jana — the wretched and low; e ḍheu — this wave; sabhāre bāje — strikes all

**23.2.** The golden lotus sways in the ocean of the nectar of prema;
high, middling, wretched and low — that wave touches all.[^14-52]

সাত সম্প্রদায় অতি উভরায় জগন্নাথ গায় রে ।
সভায় দেখিছে সর্বত্র নাচিছে এককালে গোরারায় রে ॥

*sāta sampradāya ati ubharāya jagannātha gāya re |*
*sabhāya dekhiche sarvatra nāciche ekakāle gorārāya re ||*

*Word for word:* sāta sampradāya — the seven groups; ati ubharāya — at the top of their voices; jagannātha gāya — sing to Jagannatha; sabhāya dekhiche — all see; sarvatra nāciche — dances everywhere; ekakāle — at the same time; gorārāya — Gora Raya

**23.3.** The seven groups sing to Jagannatha at the top of their voices;
all can see: Gora Raya is dancing everywhere at once.[^14-53]

অপূর্ব ঐশ্বর্য অপূর্ব মাধুর্য প্রকটিত এ লীলায় রে ।
যদুনাথ দাসে প্রেমানন্দে ভাসে পহুঁ-কৃপা-লব চায় রে ॥

*apūrva aiśvarya apūrva mādhurya prakaṭita e līlāya re |*
*yadunātha dāse premānande bhāse pahum̐-kṛpā-laba cāya re ||*

*Word for word:* apūrva aiśvarya — unprecedented majesty; apūrva mādhurya — unprecedented sweetness; prakaṭita — revealed; e līlāya — in this lila; yadunātha dāse — Yadunatha Dasa; premānande bhāse — floats in the bliss of prema; pahum̐-kṛpā-laba cāya — begs a particle of the Lord's mercy

**23.4.** Unprecedented majesty, unprecedented sweetness are revealed in this lila;
Yadunatha Dasa floats in the bliss of prema and begs from the Lord a particle of mercy.

[^14-51]: PK — vol. 2, 29th pallava, mark "॥৫॥১৫৪৮॥," ramakeli, tala trayar (MS P-R-Sa no. 2093; "tālatrayaṃ" is absent in MSS ka, kha, cha and P-R-Sa), checked
against the scan (PDF p. 455); PK has only 23.1–23.2, **without a signature**. GPT1 — p. 323, no. 6 (ramakeli), scan PDF p. 582 — with two more stanzas
(23.3–23.4) and the signature "yadunātha dāsa"; GPT2 — sec. 5.1, no. 6. It was missing from the catalogue (new row YD-015). GPT1 also attached the
signature "yadunātha dāsa" to verses of the CC (no. 4 = PK 1545; YD-012, excluded), so the signature and the additional stanzas of GPT1 are not beyond
doubt (D).
[^14-52]: The golden lotus is Gaura. "The fifth note" (pañcama) — the fifth degree of the scale, the voice of the kokila. MSS ka, kha, cha and P-R-Sa: "uttama adhama" for
"uttama madhyama"; P-R-Sa in 23.1: "caitanya nitāi re dona bhāi saṅge pariṣada nāce re" ("with the brothers the associates dance").
[^14-53]: According to CC Madhya 13 the Lord, dancing among the seven groups, appeared in all of them at once, and each group thought He was with it.

## 24. "Ramananda" — "ohe nitāi nīlācala nā chāṛiba āra…" (GPT1 p. 405, no. 13)
*The Lord tells Nityananda that He will not leave Nilachala again: Haridasa has wound up his lila, Advaita, Srinivasa, Puri, Damodara,
Vishvarupa and Krishnadasa are gone; He bids Nitai live as a householder — go to the Pandita, who will give Him two daughters — and be merciful
to the fallen; Gauda is His own abode. Holding Nitai's hand, the Lord weeps, repeating "Hari, Hari." Raga dhanashi.*[^14-54]

ওহে নিতাই নীলাচল না ছাড়িব আর ।
প্রাণের হরিদাস ছিল সেই লীলা সম্বরিল কার সঙ্গে করিব বিহার ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*ohe nitāi nīlācala nā chāṛiba āra |*
