*prāṇera haridāsa chila sei līlā sambarila kāra saṅge kariba bihāra || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* ohe nitāi — O Nitai; nīlācala nā chāṛiba āra — I shall not leave Nilachala any more; prāṇera haridāsa chila — there was Haridasa, dear as life; sei līlā sambarila — he wound up (his) lila; kāra saṅge — with whom; kariba bihāra — shall I play

**24.1.** "Nitai, I shall not leave Nilachala any more.
There was Haridasa, dear to Me as life — he has wound up his lila; with whom shall I now play?

অদ্বৈত শ্রীশ্রীনিবাস পুরী দামোদর দাস তারা গেল এ সুখ ছাড়িয়া ।
কেবা পাবে রস রঙ্গ ভ্রমিব কাহার সঙ্গ গেল বুকে পাষাণ চাপাঞা ॥

*advaita śrīśrīnibāsa purī dāmodara dāsa tārā gela e sukha chāṛiyā |*
*kebā pābe rasa raṅga bhramiba kāhāra saṅga gela buke pāṣāṇa cāpāñā ||*

*Word for word:* advaita śrī-śrīnibāsa — Advaita, Sri Srinivasa; purī — Puri; dāmodara dāsa — Damodara Dasa; tārā gela — they have gone; e sukha chāṛiyā — leaving this joy; kebā pābe rasa raṅga — who will share (lit. "get") rasa and play; bhramiba kāhāra saṅga — with whom shall I wander; gela buke pāṣāṇa cāpāñā — they went, laying a stone on the breast

**24.2.** Advaita, Sri Srinivasa, Puri, Damodara Dasa — they have gone, leaving this joy;
who will share rasa with Me, with whom shall I wander? They have gone, laying a stone upon My breast.[^14-55]

বিশ্বরূপ মোর ভাই তাহার উদ্দেশ নাই সেই গেল বৈরাগ্য করিয়া ।
কৃষ্ণদাস রসখান না শুনিব তার গান সেহ গেল বুকে শেল দিয়া ॥

*biśvarūpa mora bhāi tāhāra uddeśa nāi sei gela bairāgya kariyā |*
*kṛṣṇadāsa rasakhāna nā śuniba tāra gāna seha gela buke śela diyā ||*

*Word for word:* biśvarūpa mora bhāi — Vishvarupa, My brother; tāhāra uddeśa nāi — there is no trace of him; sei gela bairāgya kariyā — he went away, taking renunciation; kṛṣṇadāsa rasa-khāna — Krishnadasa, a mine of rasa; nā śuniba tāra gāna — I shall not hear his songs; seha gela buke śela diyā — he too went, driving a spear into the breast

**24.3.** Vishvarupa, My brother — there is no news of him: he went away, taking renunciation;
Krishnadasa, a mine of rasa — I shall hear his songs no more: he too has gone, driving a spear into My heart.

নিতাই কর গৃহবাস যাহ হে পণ্ডিত-পাশ তোমারে দেখিয়া সুখ পাবে ।
তোমারে যতন করি দিবে দুই কন্যা বরি নিজরূপ তাহাকে দেখাবে ॥

*nitāi kara gṛhabāsa yāha he paṇḍita-pāśa tomāre dekhiyā sukha pābe |*
*tomāre yatana kari dibe dui kanyā bari nijarūpa tāhāke dekhābe ||*

*Word for word:* nitāi kara gṛha-bāsa — Nitai, live as a householder; yāha he paṇḍita-pāśa — go to the Pandita; tomāre dekhiyā sukha pābe — seeing You, he will be happy; tomāre yatana kari — caring for You; dibe dui kanyā bari — will give You two daughters in marriage; nija-rūpa tāhāke dekhābe — You will show him Your own form

**24.4.** Nitai, live as a householder — go to the Pandita: seeing You, he will be happy;
with care he will give You two daughters in marriage — show him Your own form.[^14-56]

পতিত অধম মূর্খ ইহারে না দিবে দুখ করুণা করিবা সবা পানে ।
আপনা বলিয়া বলো জীবে দেখি দয়া করো করুণা ঘুষিবে ত্রিভুবনে ॥

*patita adhama mūrkha ihāre nā dibe dukha karuṇā karibā sabā pāne |*
*āpanā baliyā balo jībe dekhi dayā karo karuṇā ghuṣibe tribhubane ||*

*Word for word:* patita adhama mūrkha — the fallen, low, ignorant; ihāre nā dibe dukha — do not grieve them; karuṇā karibā sabā pāne — be merciful to all; āpanā baliyā balo — call them Your own; jībe dekhi dayā karo — seeing living beings, have pity; karuṇā ghuṣibe tribhubane — the mercy will be proclaimed in the three worlds

**24.5.** The fallen, the low, the ignorant — do not grieve them, be merciful to all;
call them Your own, have pity on living beings — Your mercy will be proclaimed in the three worlds.

সেহ মোর নিজ ধাম যশ রাখ বলরাম করুণা করিয়া প্রভু কাঁদে ।
নিতাইচাঁদের করে ধরি প্রভু বোলে হরি হরি রামানন্দ বুক নাহি বাঁধে ॥

*seha mora nija dhāma yaśa rākha balarāma karuṇā kariyā prabhu kām̐de |*
*nitāicām̐dera kare dhari prabhu bole hari hari rāmānanda buka nāhi bām̐dhe ||*

*Word for word:* seha mora nija dhāma — that is My own abode; yaśa rākha balarāma — keep the glory, Balarama; karuṇā kariyā — mercifully; prabhu kām̐de — the Lord weeps; nitāicām̐dera kare dhari — holding Nitaichand's hand; prabhu bole hari hari — the Lord says "Hari, Hari"; rāmānanda buka nāhi bām̐dhe — Ramananda's heart finds no rest

**24.6.** And that land is My own abode; keep My glory, Balarama," — saying this mercifully, the Lord weeps.
Holding Nitaichand's hand, the Lord says "Hari, Hari!" — Ramananda's heart finds no rest.[^14-57]

[^14-54]: GPT1 — p. 405, section on Nityananda in Gauda, no. 13 (dhanashi), checked against the scan (PDF pp. 664–665); GPT2 — sec. 5.5, no. 13 (GPT1
p. 405 — as cited by Majumdar). The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS (catalogue: RM-015). Signature "rāmānanda." **Majumdar considers the pada a
forgery composed to justify Nityananda's marriage**; it also departs from tradition: Advaita outlived the Lord, and the Lord sent Nityananda to
preach in Gauda long before Haridasa's departure (CC Madhya 15; Antya 11). We translate it as a text of the GPT without accepting it as
authentic (D).
[^14-55]: If "gone" is understood as departure from the world, this contradicts the CC and CB: Advaita and Svarupa Damodara were with the Lord to
the end of His lila; perhaps their leaving Puri is meant. "Puri" — probably Paramananda Puri; "Damodara Dasa" — Svarupa Damodara or Damodara
Pandita; "Krishnadasa, a mine of rasa" — it is unclear who is meant.
[^14-56]: "The Pandita" — Suryadasa Pandita (Sarakhel), father of Vasudha and Jahnava, whom Nityananda married (CC Adi 11; *Bhakti-ratnakara* 12).
"Show him Your own form" — Nityananda as Balarama. Nityananda's marriage and His householder life in Gauda are His own will, manifested at the
Lord's command for the sake of preaching; Nityananda, Balarama, is not subject to worldly attachments.
[^14-57]: "That land" (seha) — apparently Gauda, the land of Nityananda's preaching. "Balarama" — an address to Nityananda (He is Balarama). The signature
"Ramananda": according to Majumdar, neither Ramananda Raya nor Ramananda Vasu is the author of this pada.

## 25. Vasu Ghosha — "aruṇa-basane bibidha bhūṣaṇe śirete pāga laṭapaṭiyā…" (GPT1 p. 423, no. 30)
*Nityananda's dance: in red garments and ornaments, His turban slipping askew, He whirls, arms raised, crying "Hari, Hari!"; His gait is that of a
maddened elephant, His ankle-bells ring; in bhava, heedless of the quarters, He roars: "Gaura!"; the devotees roll on the ground, gazing at His
moonlike face. Raga bala-suhai.*[^14-58]

অরুণ-বসনে বিবিধ ভূষণে শিরেতে পাগ লটপটিয়া ।
চৌদিকে ফিরি ফিরি বাহুযুগ তুলি নাচত হরি হরি বলিয়া ॥

*aruṇa-basane bibidha bhūṣaṇe śirete pāga laṭapaṭiyā |*
*caudike phiri phiri bāhuyuga tuli nācata hari hari baliyā ||*

*Word for word:* aruṇa-basane — in red garments; bibidha bhūṣaṇe — in various ornaments; śirete pāga — the turban on the head; laṭapaṭiyā — slipping askew; caudike phiri phiri — whirling all around; bāhu-yuga tuli — raising both arms; nācata — dances; hari hari baliyā — crying "Hari, Hari"

**25.1.** In red garments, in various ornaments, the turban on His head slipping askew,
He whirls round and round, both arms raised — He dances, crying "Hari, Hari!"

নিতাই রঙ্গিয়া নাচে ।
অরুণ-নয়নে ও চাঁদবয়ানে কত না মাধুরী আছে ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*nitāi raṅgiyā nāce |*
*aruṇa-nayane o cām̐dabayāne kata nā mādhurī āche || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* nitāi raṅgiyā — merry Nitai; nāce — dances; aruṇa-nayane — in the reddish eyes; o cām̐da-bayāne — in that moonlike face; kata nā mādhurī āche — how much sweetness there is

**25.2.** Merry Nitai dances!
In the reddish eyes, in the moonlike face — how much sweetness!

চলন সুন্দর মত্ত করিবর নূপুর ঝঙ্কৃত করিয়া ।
ভাবে অবশ নাহি দিগপাশ গৌর বলি হুহুঙ্কারিয়া ॥

*calana sundara matta karibara nūpura jhaṅkṛta kariyā |*
*bhābe abaśa nāhi digapāśa gaura bali huhuṅkāriyā ||*

*Word for word:* calana sundara — lovely gait; matta karibara — (like) a maddened elephant; nūpura jhaṅkṛta kariyā — making the ankle-bells ring; bhābe abaśa — overcome by bhava; nāhi digapāśa — heedless of the quarters; gaura bali — crying "Gaura"; huhuṅkāriyā — roaring

**25.3.** Lovely is His gait — like a maddened elephant's, His ankle-bells ringing;
overcome by bhava, heedless of the quarters, He roars: "Gaura!"

যতেক ভকত ধরণী লোটত হেরিয়া ও চাঁদবয়ানিয়া ।
বাসুদেব ঘোষ কাতর বঞ্চিত মাগহুঁ প্রেমরস দানিয়া ॥

*yateka bhakata dharaṇī loṭata heriyā o cām̐dabayāniyā |*
*bāsudeba ghoṣa kātara bañcita māgahum̐ premarasa dāniyā ||*

*Word for word:* yateka bhakata — all the devotees; dharaṇī loṭata — roll on the ground; heriyā o cām̐da-bayāniyā — gazing at that moonlike face; bāsudeba ghoṣa — Vasudeva Ghosha; kātara bañcita — wretched, deprived; māgahum̐ — I beg; prema-rasa — the rasa of prema; dāniyā — from the Giver

**25.4.** All the devotees roll on the ground, gazing at that moonlike face;
Vasudeva Ghosha, wretched, deprived, begs the Giver for the rasa of prema.[^14-59]

[^14-58]: GPT1 — p. 423, section on Nityananda, no. 30 ("bālā suhai"), checked against the scan (PDF p. 682); GPT2 — sec. 6.1, no. 30. The pada is not in PK,
BR, KGC or PS (catalogue: VG-171). GPT only (C). The GPT1 footnotes give variants from an unnamed source: "bidita bhubane" ("known to the world") for
"bibidha bhūṣaṇe," "sundara" for "raṅgiyā," and a different last line — "basu rāmānande, kām̐de nirānande, nitāi caraṇa dhariyā" ("Vasu Ramananda weeps in sorrow,
clasping Nitai's feet"): there the pada is signed by Vasu Ramananda.
[^14-59]: "The Giver" (dāniyā) — Nityananda, the giver of prema. The turban (pāga) and red garments are the appearance of Nityananda the avadhuta in
Gauda (CB Antya 5).

## 26. Yadu — "nitāicām̐da dayāmaya…" (PK 2300; GPT1 p. 429, no. 51)
*Nityananda's mercy: never was there one so merciful to the people of Kali; His body now darkens, now brightens, now turns yellow; He laughs, He
weeps, unaware of Himself; He tries to say "Gora" and cannot; His eyes, red with love for Gaura, swim in tears; drowning Himself, He has flooded the
earth — only Yadu has remained on the mountain of worldly existence. Raga pathamanjari.*[^14-60]

নিতাইচাঁদ দয়াময় নিতাইচাঁদ দয়াময় ।
কলি-জীবে এত দয়া কভু নাহি হয় ॥

*nitāicām̐da dayāmaya nitāicām̐da dayāmaya |*
*kali-jībe eta dayā kabhu nāhi haya ||*

*Word for word:* nitāicām̐da dayāmaya — Nitaichand is merciful; kali-jībe — to the living beings of Kali; eta dayā — such mercy; kabhu nāhi haya — never is

**26.1.** Nitaichand is merciful, Nitaichand is merciful!
Such mercy to the living beings of Kali there never was.

খেণে কালা খেণে গোরা খেণে অঙ্গ পীত ।
খেণে হাসে খেণে কান্দে না পায় সম্বিত ॥

*kheṇe kālā kheṇe gorā kheṇe aṅga pīta |*
*kheṇe hāse kheṇe kānde nā pāya sambita ||*

*Word for word:* khene kālā — now dark; khene gorā — now fair; khene aṅga pīta — now the body yellow; khene hāse — now He laughs; khene kānde — now He weeps; nā pāya sambita — He does not come to Himself

**26.2.** Now He is dark, now fair, now His body turns yellow;
now He laughs, now He weeps — He is unaware of Himself.

খেণে গো গো করে গোরা বলিতে না পারে ।
গোরা-রাগে রাঙ্গা আঁখি জলেই সাঁতারে ॥

*kheṇe go go kare gorā balite nā pāre |*
*gorā-rāge rāṅgā ām̐khi jalei sām̐tāre ||*

*Word for word:* khene go go kare — now stammers "go… go…"; gorā balite nā pāre — cannot say "Gora"; gorā-rāge — from love for Gora; rāṅgā ām̐khi — red eyes; jalei sām̐tāre — swim in tears

**26.3.** Now He stammers "Go… go…" — He cannot say "Gora";
His eyes, red with love for Gora, swim in tears.

আপনি ভাসিয়া জলে ভাসাওল ক্ষিতি ।
এ ভব-অচলে যদু রহল অবধি ॥

*āpani bhāsiyā jale bhāsāola kṣiti |*
*e bhaba-acale yadu rahala abadhi ||*

*Word for word:* āpani bhāsiyā jale — Himself afloat in the waters; bhāsāola kṣiti — flooded the earth; e bhaba-acale — on this mountain of worldly existence; yadu rahala abadhi — Yadu remained to the end

**26.4.** Drowning Himself in those waters, He has flooded the earth —
only Yadu has remained on the mountain of worldly existence.[^14-61]

[^14-60]: PK — vol. 3, 4th shakha, 22nd pallava ("Description of the virtues of Sri Nityananda"), mark "॥৭॥২৩০০॥," pathamanjari, MS P-R-Sa no. 2404,
checked against the scan (PDF p. 303); GPT1 — p. 429, no. 51 (pathamanjari), scan PDF p. 688; GPT2 — sec. 6.1, no. 51. It was missing from the
catalogue (new row YD-016). Signature "yadu": Yadunatha Kavichandra or the later Yadunandana — not established (C).
[^14-61]: Changes of colour (vaivarnya), laughter and tears are the sattvika-bhavas of prema. "The mountain of worldly existence" (bhava-acala) — existence,
immovable like a mountain: the poet of himself, unmoved by the flood of prema. PK MSS "ka, kha, cha": "śīta" ("cold") for "pīta"; "gha": "galita."

## 27. Kanu Dasa — "preme mātoyārā nitāi nāgara…" (GPT1 p. 432, no. 60)
*Praise of Nityananda: lovely Nitai is intoxicated with prema, an ocean of incomparable prema and mercy; making no distinction between His own
and others, He gives prema beyond the injunctions of the Vedas, saves sinners, weeps for the fallen, gives prema generously as from an
inexhaustible treasury; the poet asks for a place at His feet. Raga dhanashi.*[^14-62]

প্রেমে মাতোয়ারা নিতাই নাগর ।
অতুলিত প্রেম দয়ার সাগর ॥

*preme mātoyārā nitāi nāgara |*
*atulita prema dayāra sāgara ||*

*Word for word:* preme mātoyārā — intoxicated with prema; nitāi nāgara — lovely Nitai; atulita prema — incomparable prema; dayāra sāgara — an ocean of mercy

**27.1.** Lovely Nitai is intoxicated with prema:
incomparable prema — an ocean of mercy.

প্রেমভরে অন্তর গর গর ।
না জানেন পহুঁ কে আপন পর ॥

*premabhare antara gara gara |*
*nā jānena pahum̐ ke āpana para ||*

*Word for word:* prema-bhare — with prema; antara gara gara — the heart brimming; nā jānena pahum̐ — the Lord does not know; ke āpana para — who is His own, who is other

**27.2.** His heart is brimming with prema:
the Lord does not distinguish who is His own and who is not.

হেন দয়া কোথা এ ধরণী পর ।
দেয় প্রেম বেদবিধি-অগোচর ॥

*hena dayā kothā e dharaṇī para |*
*deya prema bedabidhi-agocara ||*

*Word for word:* hena dayā kothā — where is such mercy; e dharaṇī para — on this earth; deya prema — He gives prema; beda-bidhi-agocara — beyond the reach of the Vedic injunctions

**27.3.** Where on earth is such mercy?
He gives prema beyond the reach of the Vedic injunctions.[^14-63]

পাতকী উদ্ধার কার্য নিরন্তর ।
পতিতের দুখে নেত্র ঝর ঝর ॥

*pātakī uddhāra kārya nirantara |*
*patitera dukhe netra jhara jhara ||*

*Word for word:* pātakī uddhāra — delivering sinners; kārya nirantara — ceaseless work; patitera dukhe — at the sufferings of the fallen; netra jhara jhara — the eyes stream

**27.4.** Delivering sinners is His ceaseless work;
for the sufferings of the fallen tears stream from His eyes.

যাচি প্রেম দেয় সবে অকাতর ।
অফুরন্ত যেন ভাণ্ডার সুন্দর ॥

*yāci prema deya sabe akātara |*
*aphuranta yena bhāṇḍāra sundara ||*

*Word for word:* yāci — offering of His own accord; prema deya sabe — gives prema to all; akātara — unstintingly; aphuranta — inexhaustible; yena bhāṇḍāra sundara — like a lovely treasury

**27.5.** Offering prema of His own accord, He gives it to all without stint —
like a lovely inexhaustible treasury.

কানু দাস কহে জুড়ি দুই কর ।
পদে দেহ স্থান এ দীন কিঙ্কর ॥

*kānu dāsa kahe juṛi dui kara |*
*pade deha sthāna e dīna kiṅkara ||*

*Word for word:* kānu dāsa kahe — says Kanu Dasa; juṛi dui kara — joining both palms; pade deha sthāna — give a place at the feet; e dīna kiṅkara — to this wretched servant

**27.6.** Says Kanu Dasa with joined palms:
give this wretched servant a place at Your feet.

[^14-62]: GPT1 — p. 432, section on Nityananda, no. 60 (dhanashi), checked against the scan (PDF p. 691); GPT2 — sec. 6.1, no. 60. The pada is not in PK, BR,
KGC or PS (catalogue: KD-004). Signature "kānu dāsa" — Kanu Thakura (Kanurama Dasa), son of Purushottama Dasa, associate of Jahnava (cf. PK 2327,
chapter 5); attribution by GPT (C).
[^14-63]: "Nagara" (nitāi nāgara) — here an epithet, "lovely, elegant," usual in praise of Nitai, not the motif of nagari-bhava. "Beyond the reach of the Vedic
injunctions" (bedabidhi-agocara) — the prema of Vraja is above the rules of Vedic dharma (CC Adi 4).

## 28. Kanu Dasa — "bidyānagarādhipa apāra sampadaśālī…" (GPT1 pp. 454–455, no. 9)
*Praise of Ramananda Raya: the ruler of Vidyanagara, owner of boundless wealth, received Gauranga in his house and gave Him the bee of his mind;
glory to Ramananda, with whom the Lord tasted boundless bliss; in a dialogue of questions and answers they established the goal and the path of the
living being; his padas of rasa are like a full-blown red lotus, the life of the rasikas; the poet begs for Ramananda's feet. Raga kamoda.*[^14-64]

বিদ্যানগরাধিপ অপার সম্পদশালী রামরায় পুরুষ-প্রধান ।
গৃহে পাইয়া শ্রীগৌরাঙ্গ আপনার মনোভৃঙ্গ তাঁর পদে করিলেক দান ॥

*bidyānagarādhipa apāra sampadaśālī rāmarāya puruṣa-pradhāna |*
*gṛhe pāiyā śrīgaurāṅga āpanāra manobhṛṅga tām̐ra pade karileka dāna ||*

*Word for word:* bidyānagarādhipa — the ruler of Vidyanagara; apāra sampada-śālī — possessor of boundless wealth; rāmarāya — Rama Raya; puruṣa-pradhāna — first among men; gṛhe pāiyā śrī-gaurāṅga — receiving Sri Gauranga in the house; āpanāra mano-bhṛṅga — the bee of his own mind; tām̐ra pade karileka dāna — gave to His feet

**28.1.** The ruler of Vidyanagara, owner of boundless wealth, Rama Raya, first among men,
receiving Sri Gauranga in his house, gave His feet the bee of his own mind.

ধন্য ধন্য রায় রামানন্দ ।
যাহার পাইয়া সঙ্গ প্রভু মোর শ্রীগৌরাঙ্গ ভুঞ্জিলেক অসীম আনন্দ ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*dhanya dhanya rāya rāmānanda |*
*yāhāra pāiyā saṅga prabhu mora śrīgaurāṅga bhuñjileka asīma ānanda || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* dhanya dhanya — glory, glory; rāya rāmānanda — to Raya Ramananda; yāhāra pāiyā saṅga — having his company; prabhu mora śrī-gaurāṅga — my Lord Sri Gauranga; bhuñjileka asīma ānanda — tasted boundless bliss

**28.2.** Glory, glory to Raya Ramananda!
With him my Lord Sri Gauranga tasted boundless bliss.

দোঁহে প্রশ্নোত্তর-ছলে স্বাধ্যায় নির্ণয় কৈলে জানি জীব-সাধন-সন্ধান ।
যাহার রসের পদ যেন ফুল্ল কোকনদ রসিক জনের সে পরাণ ॥

*dom̐he praśnottara-chale svādhyāya nirṇaya kaile jāni jība-sādhana-sandhāna |*
*yāhāra rasera pada yena phulla kokanada rasika janera se parāṇa ||*

*Word for word:* dom̐he — the two; praśnottara-chale — in the form of questions and answers; svādhyāya nirṇaya kaile — examined the sacred teaching; jāni — knowing; jība-sādhana-sandhāna — the path of sadhana for living beings; yāhāra rasera pada — whose padas of rasa; yena phulla kokanada — like a full-blown red lotus; rasika janera se parāṇa — the life of those who know rasa

**28.3.** The two, in the form of questions and answers, examined the sacred teaching — and learned what the path of sadhana is for living beings;
his padas of rasa are like a full-blown red lotus: the life of those who know rasa.[^14-65]

রামানন্দ-পদরজ শিরে ধরি সদা ভজ ভজনের সারাৎসার ধন ।
কানুদাস মতিহীন মধুর রসেতে দীন রামরায় দেও শ্রীচরণ ॥

*rāmānanda-padaraja śire dhari sadā bhaja bhajanera sārātsāra dhana |*
*kānudāsa matihīna madhura rasete dīna rāmarāya deo śrīcaraṇa ||*

*Word for word:* rāmānanda-pada-raja — the dust of Ramananda's feet; śire dhari — placing on the head; sadā bhaja — always serve; bhajanera sārātsāra dhana — the treasure, the essence of the essence of service; kānudāsa mati-hīna — Kanu Dasa, poor in wit; madhura rasete dīna — poor in madhura-rasa; rāmarāya — Rama Raya; deo śrī-caraṇa — give the holy feet

**28.4.** Always place the dust of Ramananda's feet on your head — and serve: this is the essence of the essence of service, the treasure.
Kanu Dasa, poor in wit, poor in madhura-rasa: Rama Raya, give me your holy feet!

[^14-64]: GPT1 — pp. 454–455, section on the associates, no. 9 (kamoda), checked against the scan (PDF pp. 713–714); GPT2 — sec. 6.3, no. 9 (in the GPT2 index:
"bidyānagarādhipa — kānudāsa"). The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS (catalogue: KD-005). Signature "kānudāsa"; attribution by GPT (C).
[^14-65]: The Lord's conversation with Ramananda Raya on the Godavari — CC Madhya 8 (the Lord's questions and Ramananda's answers on sadhya and sadhana — the
goal and the path). The GPT1 print has "svādhyāya nirṇaya" ("established [the meaning of] the study of scripture"); by sense one would expect "sādhyera
nirṇaya" ("established the goal"). Ramananda's padas are his verses on rasa (including the drama *Jagannatha-vallabha*, whose songs the Lord heard in
Puri, CC Madhya 2, Antya 5).

# Chapter 15. Krishnadasa, Kanu Dasa, Vasu Ghosha, Yadunandana, Nayanananda, Yadu, Ramananda, Chaitanyadasa: the rest of the "GPT only" group and finds of a full check of signatures

*This chapter completes the group of padas by the other poets (apart from Narahari) that are known from the "Gaura-pada-tarangini"
(GPT1 — 1st ed. by Jagadbandhu Bhadra, 1903; GPT2 — 2nd ed., 1934), without the padas in nagari-bhava. It contains padas missed by
earlier checks (in the OCR text of GPT1 some headings "N pada" lack the danda, and such padas merged with their neighbours) and finds
of a full manual re-check of the signatures of all contemporary poets throughout GPT1. Four of the finds turned out not to be "GPT
only": they are in the "Padakalpataru" (PK 2099 — Yadunandana, PK 2101 — Yadu, also in the "Bhakti-ratnakara", PK 2083 — unsigned,
PK 1867 — Chaitanyadasa); there the text is given from PK with the readings of GPT. The padas follow the order of the lilas: praise of
the Gaura-avatara, Advaita's call and the Lord's appearance, goshtha-bhava and the kirtanas of Navadvipa, Shachi's lament after the
sannyasa, the Lord's bhavas in Puri, Nityananda. The language of some padas (nos. 1, 3–5, 14) has New Bengali forms — by these they
are probably late; Majumdar in general considers GPT unreliable for attribution. Hence the attribution of padas known only from GPT is
conditional (C, the late ones included: late language alone does not indicate a forgery). The Bengali original, variant readings and word-for-word translation are in the full version of the book.*

## 1. Krishnadasa — "āre re ninduka bhāi…" (GPT1 p. 14, no. 35)
*Rebuke of a blasphemer: Gauranga is the essence of all avataras; when drunkenness, killing of the unborn and debauchery under the
guise of tantric religion had overrun Bharata and people had begun to worship yakshas, rakshasas and Vishahari, Sri Chaitanya
appeared in Navadvipa, gave everyone the name of Hari, saved Jagai and Madhai, united brahmanas with yavanas; whoever does not
believe this has no deliverance. Raga dhanashi.*[^15-1]

আরে রে নিন্দুক ভাই তোর কি রে বোধ নাই বৃথাই ধরিলা দোন আঁখি ।
সব অবতারসার শ্রীগৌরাঙ্গ অবতার তুমি তাহে রৈয়াছ উপেখি ॥

*āre re ninduka bhāi tora ki re bodha nāi bṛthāi dharilā dona ām̐khi |*
*saba abatārasāra śrīgaurāṅga abatāra tumi tāhe raiyācha upekhi ||*

*Word for word:* āre re — hey; ninduka bhāi — brother blasphemer; tora ki re bodha nāi — have you no understanding; bṛthāi — in vain; dharilā — you bear; dona ām̐khi — a pair of eyes; saba abatāra-sāra — the essence of all avataras; śrī-gaurāṅga abatāra — the avatara of Sri Gauranga; tumi tāhe — you Him; raiyācha upekhi — disregard

**1.1.** "Hey, brother blasphemer, have you no understanding at all? In vain you bear a pair of eyes!
The essence of all avataras is the avatara of Sri Gauranga — and you pass Him by with disregard.

সুরাপান অত্যাচার ভ্রূণহত্যা ব্যভিচার তন্ত্রধর্মে ভারত ব্যাপিল ।
যক্ষ রক্ষ বিষহরি নানা উপহার করি জীব সবে পূজিতে লাগিল ॥

*surāpāna atyācāra bhrūṇahatyā byabhicāra tantradharme bhārata byāpila |*
*yakṣa rakṣa biṣahari nānā upahāra kari jība sabe pūjite lāgila ||*

*Word for word:* surāpāna — drunkenness; atyācāra — violence; bhrūṇahatyā — killing of the unborn; byabhicāra — debauchery; tantra-dharme — under the guise of tantric religion; bhārata byāpila — overran Bharata; yakṣa rakṣa — yakshas, rakshasas; biṣahari — Vishahari (Manasa); nānā upahāra kari — with various offerings; jība sabe — all people; pūjite lāgila — began to worship

**1.2.** Drunkenness, violence, killing of the unborn, debauchery — under the guise of tantric religion they overran Bharata;
yakshas, rakshasas and Vishahari people began to worship with all kinds of offerings.[^15-2]

দেখিয়া জীবের দৈন্য প্রভু মোর শ্রীচৈতন্য নবদ্বীপে প্রকট হইলা ।
তারক ব্রহ্ম হরিনাম যাচি সবে করি দান ধর্মের সে গ্লানি ঘুচাইলা ॥

*dekhiyā jībera dainya prabhu mora śrīcaitanya nabadvīpe prakaṭa hailā |*
*tāraka brahma harināma yāci sabe kari dāna dharmera se glāni ghucāilā ||*

*Word for word:* dekhiyā — seeing; jībera dainya — the misery of the living beings; prabhu mora śrī-caitanya — my Lord Sri Chaitanya; nabadvīpe — in Navadvipa; prakaṭa hailā — appeared; tāraka brahma — the saving taraka-brahma; hari-nāma — the name of Hari; yāci — offering unasked; sabe kari dāna — giving to all; dharmera se glāni — that decline of dharma; ghucāilā — removed

**1.3.** Seeing the misery of the living beings, my Lord Sri Chaitanya appeared in Navadvipa:
the saving name of Hari — the taraka-brahma — He Himself offered and gave to all, and removed the decline of dharma.[^15-3]

জগাই মাধাই আদি দুষ্কৃতের নিরবধি হরিনামে করিলা উদ্ধার ।
ব্রাহ্মণ যবনে মিলি করাইলা কোলাকুলি পরতেকে দেখ একবার ॥

*jagāi mādhāi ādi duṣkṛtera nirabadhi harināme karilā uddhāra |*
*brāhmaṇa yabane mili karāilā kolākuli parateke dekha ekabāra ||*

*Word for word:* jagāi mādhāi ādi — Jagai, Madhai and others; duṣkṛtera nirabadhi — doing evil without end; hari-nāme — by the name of Hari; karilā uddhāra — saved; brāhmaṇa yabane mili — uniting brahmanas with yavanas; karāilā kolākuli — made them embrace; parateke — with your own eyes; dekha ekabāra — see but once

**1.4.** Jagai, Madhai and others who did evil without end He saved by the name of Hari;
He united brahmanas and yavanas — made them embrace: see it with your own eyes but once!

নাস্তিকে করিলা ভক্ত খঞ্জে কৈলা গতিশক্ত অন্ধের করিলা চক্ষুদান ।
কহে দীন কৃষ্ণদাস নহিলে ইথে বিশ্বাস তোর আর নাহি পরিত্রাণ ॥

*nāstike karilā bhakta khañje kailā gatiśakta andhera karilā cakṣudāna |*
*kahe dīna kṛṣṇadāsa nahile ithe biśvāsa tora āra nāhi paritrāṇa ||*

*Word for word:* nāstike — atheists; karilā bhakta — made devotees; khañje — the lame; kailā gati-śakta — made able to walk; andhera — to the blind; karilā cakṣu-dāna — gave sight; kahe dīna kṛṣṇadāsa — says lowly Krishnadasa; nahile ithe biśvāsa — if there is no faith in this; tora āra nāhi paritrāṇa — there is no more deliverance for you

**1.5.** He made atheists into devotees, gave the lame the power to walk, granted the blind their sight."
Says lowly Krishnadasa: if you do not believe this, there is no more deliverance for you.[^15-4]

[^15-1]: GPT1 — p. 14, section of mangalacharana, no. 35 (dhanashi), checked against the scan IA in.ernet.dli.2015.477854 (PDF p. 273);
GPT2 — sec. 1.2, no. 35. The pada is not in PK, the "Bhakti-ratnakara" (BR), the "Kshanada-gita-chintamani" (KGC) or the
"Padamrita-samudra" (PS); it was missing from the catalogue (new row KR-022). Under the signature "Krishnadasa" PK has 22 padas by
different poets. The denunciation of "tantric religion" and words like "killing of the unborn" (bhrūṇahatyā) point to a late origin
(18th–19th c.); C.
[^15-2]: Cf. Vrindavana Dasa's description of Navadvipa before the Lord's appearance: people worship yakshas with wine and meat and honour
Vishahari (CB Adi 2). Vishahari is Manasa, the goddess of snakes. "Tantric religion" here means the rites with wine and the like that
the poet denounces.
[^15-3]: "Taraka-brahma" — the name that carries one across the ocean of birth and death: the maha-mantra "Hare Krishna," which the
"Kali-santarana Upanishad" calls the destroyer of the taint of Kali. "Decline of dharma" echoes Bhagavad-gita 4.7–8.
[^15-4]: Jagai and Madhai — CB Madhya 13; CC Adi 17. "Brahmanas and yavanas embraced": the Lord accepted all without distinction of caste —
thus Haridasa Thakura, born in a Muslim family, was one of His closest associates (CB Adi 16); the Kazi became His devotee (CC Adi 17).

## 2. Krishnadasa — "śāntipurera buṛāmālī…" (GPT1 pp. 14–15, no. 36)
*An allegory of the tree of Chaitanya: the old gardener of Shantipur (Advaita) brought a seedling from the garden of Vaikuntha and gave
it to the gardener Nitai; in Nadia grew the tree of Chaitanya and bore two fruits — the Name and prema; Nitai gives them out to all,
down to chandalas and yavanas, whether they wish it or not; the poet laments that he did not see that tree and did not know the
merciful gardener. Raga suhai.*[^15-5]

শান্তিপুরের বুড়ামালী বৈকুণ্ঠ বাগান খালি করিয়া আনিল এক চারা ।
নিতাই মালীরে পাঞা চারা তার হাতে দিয়া যতনে রোপিতে কৈল নাড়া ॥

*śāntipurera buṛāmālī baikuṇṭha bāgāna khāli kariyā ānila eka cārā |*
*nitāi mālīre pāñā cārā tāra hāte diyā yatane ropite kaila nāṛā ||*

*Word for word:* śāntipurera — of Shantipur; buṛā-mālī — the old gardener; baikuṇṭha bāgāna khāli kariyā — emptying the garden of Vaikuntha; ānila eka cārā — brought a seedling; nitāi mālīre pāñā — finding the gardener Nitai; cārā tāra hāte diyā — putting the seedling in his hands; yatane ropite — to plant with care; kaila nāṛā — said Nara (Advaita)

**2.1.** The old gardener of Shantipur, emptying the garden of Vaikuntha, brought a single seedling;
finding the gardener Nitai, He put the seedling into His hands — "Plant it with care," said Nara.[^15-6]

নদীয়া উত্তম স্থান তাহাতে করি উদ্যান রোপিল চৈতন্য-তরু মালী ।
বাড়ে তরু দিনে দিনে শাখাপত্র অগণনে গজাইল যত্নে জল ঢালি ॥

*nadīyā uttama sthāna tāhāte kari udyāna ropila caitanya-taru mālī |*
*bāṛe taru dine dine śākhāpatra agaṇane gajāila yatne jala ḍhāli ||*

*Word for word:* nadīyā uttama sthāna — Nadia is the finest place; tāhāte kari udyāna — laying out a garden there; ropila caitanya-taru mālī — the gardener planted the tree of Chaitanya; bāṛe taru dine dine — the tree grows day by day; śākhā-patra agaṇane — branches and leaves past counting; gajāila — brought up; yatne jala ḍhāli — watering with care

**2.2.** Nadia is the finest place: laying out a garden there, the gardener planted the tree of Chaitanya;
the tree grows day by day, its branches and leaves past counting: watering it with care, He brought it up.

পাইয়া ভকতি-জল নাম-প্রেম দুই ফল প্রসবিল সে তরু সুন্দর ।
সেই দুই ফলের আশে জীব-পাখী নিত্য আসে কোলাহল করে নিরন্তর ॥

*pāiyā bhakati-jala nāma-prema dui phala prasabila se taru sundara |*
*sei dui phalera āśe jība-pākhī nitya āse kolāhala kare nirantara ||*

*Word for word:* pāiyā bhakati-jala — receiving the water of bhakti; nāma-prema dui phala — two fruits, the Name and prema; prasabila — bore; se taru sundara — that beautiful tree; sei dui phalera āśe — in hope of those two fruits; jība-pākhī — the birds, the living beings; nitya āse — come daily; kolāhala kare nirantara — chatter without cease

**2.3.** Receiving the water of bhakti, the beautiful tree bore two fruits — the Name and prema;
in hope of these two fruits the birds — the living beings — come every day and chatter without cease.

আনন্দে নিতাই মালী লইয়া মাথায় ডালি দুই ফল সবারে বিলায় ।

*Word for word:* ki mora karama phere — what a turn of my karma; nā herinu se tarure — I did not see that tree; nā cininu — did not know; se mālī dayāla — that merciful gardener; kṛṣṇadāsa durāśaya — Krishnadasa, full of bad desires; dante tṛṇa dhari kaya — holding a straw in his teeth, says; dhik dhik — shame, shame; e poṛā kapāla — on this burnt fate

[^15-8]: GPT1 — p. 448, section on Advaita, no. 32 (dhanashi), scan PDF pp. 707–708; GPT2 — sec. 6.2, no. 32. The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC
or PS; it was missing from the catalogue (new row KD-012). Signature "Kanu" (kānu); Kanu Thakura, the son of Purushottama, is a poet of
the next generation, and the language of the pada (sādhanā biphala, pāpabhārākrānta) is New Bengali: the pada is probably late; C.

[^15-9]: Advaita Acharya is Maha-Vishnu Himself; He appeared before the Lord in order to call Him down (CC Adi 3, 6; CB Adi 2). His "despair"
is not ignorance but compassion for the living beings and longing for the Lord's appearance, expressed in lila. The conversation of
the Lord with Advaita in Vaikuntha that is spoken of here is not described in CC or CB; CC (Adi 3) speaks of Advaita's resolve to call
Krishna by worship with Ganga water and tulasi. Haridasa Thakura came to Advaita in Shantipur (CB Adi 16).

in PK, BR, KGC or PS. In the catalogue (VV-007) the pada was listed as "unsigned," but the last line names Vasu (bāsu yāya niyā chātā) —
thus the poet often brings himself into the lila as a participant; new row VG-174. The colloquial language (halo, yeye, śune) points to a
late origin; C. Cf. other padas on Gaura's goshtha-bhava in Navadvipa: chapter 1, nos. 11–12; chapter 14, nos. 14–15.
[^15-13]: Abhirama Thakura (Ramadasa) is an associate of Nityananda, one of the twelve gopalas; the tradition sees in him Shridama, Krishna's
friend (Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika). In the pasture the cowherd friends hold an umbrella over Krishna; naming himself, the poet becomes
one of them.
[^15-14]: PK — vol. 3, 17th pallava ("śrīgaurāṅgera nṛtyādi līlā"), mark "॥৪১॥২০৯৯॥," raga "tathā" (mayura, as for PK 2097), MS P-R-Sa no. 2208,
checked against the scan (PDF p. 230, printed p. 219); GPT1 — p. 138, section on Gaura's beauty, no. 80 (mayura), scan PDF p. 397; GPT2 —
sec. 3.1, no. 80. The pada was missing from the catalogue (new row YN-014). Signature "yadunandana": Yadunandana Chakravarti, a disciple
of Gadadhara Dasa (by Majumdar a contemporary of the Lord; his padas are in BR, chapter 11), or the later Yadunandana Dasa (17th c.) —
not established; C.
[^15-15]: "A new cloud" is the form of Krishna, "a golden Madana" the form of Gaura: within the golden Gaura the dark Krishna is hidden.
Madana (Kamadeva) is an image of beauty; Krishna is Madana-mohana, "He who enchants Madana himself": the point is a beauty before which
the god of love is powerless, not worldly attraction. GPT1 has "sudhāya garala janu" ("as if poison in nectar") — apparently a misprint for
"gaṛala" ("moulded"). "Gives as a ransom" (nichiye) — a rite that averts misfortune from the beloved (cf. chapter 14, no. 2).

## 7. Nayanananda (?) — "nāce re bhāli gaurakiśora bara-raṅgiyā…" (PK 2083 unsigned; GPT1 p. 284, no. 23)
*A dance in Radha's bhava: young Gaura dances, His golden body quivering with prema; remembering Vrindavana, Govardhana and the bank of
the Yamuna, He falls and cries: "The flute!"; in Radha's bhava He takes on Radha's colour and repeats "Radha, Radha!" — and Gadadhara,
understanding the hint, smilingly takes his place at His left. Raga turi.*[^15-16]

নাচে রে ভালি গৌরকিশোর বর-রঙ্গিয়া ।
হেম-কিরণিয়া গৌরসুন্দর-তনু প্রেম-ভরে ভেল ডগমগিয়া ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*nāce re bhāli gaurakiśora bara-raṅgiyā |*
*hema-kiraṇiyā gaurasundara-tanu prema-bhare bhela ḍagamagiyā || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* nāce re bhāli — dances, ah, finely; gaura-kiśora — young Gaura; bara-raṅgiyā — finest of merry ones; hema-kiraṇiyā — shining with gold; gaura-sundara-tanu — the beautiful body of Gaura; prema-bhare — under the weight of prema; bhela ḍagamagiyā — quivered

**7.1.** He dances — ah, young Gaura, finest of merry ones!
The beautiful body of Gaura, shining like gold, quivers under the weight of prema.

বৃন্দাবন গোবর্ধন যমুনা-পুলিন বন সোঙরি সোঙরি পড়ে ঢুলিয়া ।
মুরলী মুরলী বলি ঘন ঘন ফুকরই রহল মুরলী-মুখ হেরিয়া ॥

*bṛndābana gobardhana yamunā-pulina bana soṅari soṅari paṛe ḍhuliyā |*
*muralī muralī bali ghana ghana phukarai rahala muralī-mukha heriyā ||*

*Word for word:* bṛndābana gobardhana — Vrindavana, Govardhana; yamunā-pulina bana — the bank and groves of the Yamuna; soṅari soṅari — remembering and remembering; paṛe ḍhuliyā — sways and falls; muralī muralī bali — crying "The flute! the flute!"; ghana ghana phukarai — cries again and again; rahala — stands still; muralī-mukha heriyā — as if gazing at the flute at the lips (or: at the face with the flute)

**7.2.** Remembering Vrindavana, Govardhana, the bank and the groves of the Yamuna, He sways and falls;
"The flute! the flute!" He cries again and again, and stands still, as if gazing at the flute at His lips.

শ্রীরাধার ভাবে গোরা রাধার বরণ ভেল রাধা রাধা বয়নক ভাষ ।
ইঙ্গিত বুঝিয়া প্রিয় গদাধর কৌতুকে রহল বাম পাশ ॥

*śrīrādhāra bhābe gorā rādhāra baraṇa bhela rādhā rādhā bayanaka bhāṣa |*
*iṅgita bujhiyā priya gadādhara kautuke rahala bāma pāśa ||*

*Word for word:* śrī-rādhāra bhābe — in the bhava of Sri Radha; gorā — Gora; rādhāra baraṇa bhela — took on Radha's colour; rādhā rādhā bayanaka bhāṣa — the word of His lips, "Radha, Radha"; iṅgita bujhiyā — understanding the hint; priya gadādhara — dear Gadadhara; kautuke — playfully; rahala bāma pāśa — stood at the left side

**7.3.** In the bhava of Sri Radha, Gora took on the colour of Radha; from His lips — "Radha, Radha!";
understanding the hint, His dear Gadadhara playfully took his place at the left.[^15-17]

## 8. Yadu — "gorā mora baṛai raṅgiyā…" (PK 2101; BR pp. 925–926; GPT1 p. 257, no. 30)
*Kirtana on the bank of the Suradhuni: Gaura dances in the midst of His associates — Gadadhara and Narahari on either side, and Srivasa,
Haridasa, Mukunda, Murari, Vasu, Ramai, Damodara and Jagadisha singing; "Hari! Hari!" is heard on all sides; seeing the moon of His
face, one forgets all torments. Raga suhini.*[^15-18]

গোরা মোর বড়ই রঙ্গিয়া ।
সুরধুনী-তীরে নব রঙ্গিয়া সঙ্গিয়া ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*gorā mora baṛai raṅgiyā |*
*suradhunī-tīre naba raṅgiyā saṅgiyā || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* gorā mora — my Gora; baṛai raṅgiyā — a great merry-maker; suradhunī-tīre — on the bank of the Suradhuni (the Ganga); naba raṅgiyā saṅgiyā — with new merry companions

**8.1.** *(Refrain)* My Gora is a great merry-maker:
on the bank of the Suradhuni — with new merry companions.

গাওত সহচর মন-মোহনিয়া ।
মাঝহি নাচত গৌর দ্বিজ-মণিয়া ॥

*gāota sahacara mana-mohaniyā |*
*mājhahi nācata gaura dvija-maṇiyā ||*

*Word for word:* gāota sahacara — the associates sing; mana-mohaniyā — enchanting hearts; mājhahi — in the midst; nācata gaura — dances Gaura; dvija-maṇiyā — the jewel among brahmanas

**8.2.** The associates sing, enchanting hearts;
in their midst dances Gaura — the jewel among brahmanas.

গদাধর নরহরি ডাহিন বাম ।
শ্রীনিবাস হরিদাস গায় হরিনাম ॥

*gadādhara narahari ḍāhina bāma |*
*śrīnibāsa haridāsa gāya harināma ||*

*Word for word:* gadādhara narahari — Gadadhara and Narahari; ḍāhina bāma — right and left; śrīnibāsa haridāsa — Srivasa and Haridasa; gāya harināma — sing the name of Hari

**8.3.** Gadadhara and Narahari — on the right and the left;
Srivasa and Haridasa sing the name of Hari.

মুকুন্দ মুরারি বাসু রামাই সঙ্গতি ।
গায় দামোদর জগদীশ মহামতি ॥

*mukunda murāri bāsu rāmāi saṅgati |*
*gāya dāmodara jagadīśa mahāmati ||*

*Word for word:* mukunda murāri bāsu rāmāi — Mukunda, Murari, Vasu, Ramai; saṅgati — together with Him; gāya dāmodara — Damodara sings; jagadīśa mahāmati — wise Jagadisha

**8.4.** With Him are Mukunda, Murari, Vasu, Ramai;
Damodara and wise Jagadisha sing.[^15-19]

চৌদিগে শুনিয়ে যে হরি হরি বোল ।
উথলিল প্রেম-সিন্ধু অমিয়া-হিল্লোল ॥

*caudige śuniye ye hari hari bola |*
*uthalila prema-sindhu amiyā-hillola ||*

*Word for word:* caudige śuniye — on all sides is heard; ye — lo; hari hari bola — the cry "Hari! Hari!"; uthalila prema-sindhu — the ocean of prema rose; amiyā-hillola — in waves of nectar

**8.5.** On all sides is heard: "Hari! Hari!" —
the ocean of prema has risen in waves of nectar.

দেখিয়া বদন-চাঁদ সব তাপ হরে ।
যদু কহে কেবা হেন এ রূপ পাসরে ॥

*dekhiyā badana-cām̐da saba tāpa hare |*
*yadu kahe kebā hena e rūpa pāsare ||*

*Word for word:* dekhiyā badana-cām̐da — seeing the moon of His face; saba tāpa hare — all torments vanish; yadu kahe — says Yadu; kebā hena — who such; e rūpa pāsare — would forget this beauty

**8.6.** Seeing the moon of His face, one is freed of all torments.
Says Yadu: who could forget such beauty?

## 9. Ramananda — "drāṃ drimiki drimi mādala bājata…" (GPT1 p. 335, no. 45)
*The Lord's dance in kirtana: the madala thunders, Srivasa and all the associates sing; His arms reach to His knees, His body is as of
gold, in red garments He shines like the morning sun; now He trembles, now His hair stands on end, now, raising His arms, He cries
"Hari! Hari!", cherishing His former prema; with Him are Nityananda, Advaita and the associates; at this play even a diamond softens.
Raga gandhara.*[^15-20]

দ্রাং দ্রিমিকি দ্রিমি মাদল বাজত কতহুঁ তাল সুতালুয়া ।
অখিল ভুবনক নাচ নাচত শ্রীবাস আদি সভে গানুয়া ॥

*drāṃ drimiki drimi mādala bājata katahum̐ tāla sutāluyā |*
*akhila bhubanaka nāca nācata śrībāsa ādi sabhe gānuyā ||*

*Word for word:* drāṃ drimiki drimi — (the sound of the drum); mādala bājata — the madala sounds; katahum̐ tāla sutāluyā — how many talas and well-matched rhythms; akhila bhubanaka nāca nācata — He dances the dance of the whole universe; śrībāsa ādi sabhe — Srivasa and all the others; gānuyā — are singers

**9.1.** "Drang-drimiki-drimi" thunders the madala: how many talas, how many well-matched rhythms!
He dances the dance of the whole universe — Srivasa and all the others sing.[^15-21]

জানু লম্বিত বাহুযুগল কলিত কলধৌত ঠানুয়া ।
অরুণ অম্বরে ভুবন ডগমগি যৈছে পাতর ভানুয়া ॥

*jānu lambita bāhuyugala kalita kaladhauta ṭhānuyā |*
*aruṇa ambare bhubana ḍagamagi yaiche pātara bhānuyā ||*

*Word for word:* jānu lambita bāhuyugala — arms reaching to the knees; kalita kaladhauta ṭhānuyā — a body as if of pure gold; aruṇa ambare — in red garments; bhubana ḍagamagi — the world trembles; yaiche pātara bhānuyā — like the morning sun

**9.2.** His arms reach to His knees, His body is as of pure gold;
in red garments — the whole world trembles: like the morning sun.

ক্ষণহি কম্পিত ক্ষণহি পুলকিত ক্ষণহি করযুগ চালনা ।
ক্ষণহি উচ করি বলই হরি হরি পূরুব প্রেম পালনা ॥

*kṣaṇahi kampita kṣaṇahi pulakita kṣaṇahi karayuga cālanā |*
*kṣaṇahi uca kari balai hari hari pūruba prema pālanā ||*

*Word for word:* kṣaṇahi kampita — now trembling; kṣaṇahi pulakita — now with hair on end; kṣaṇahi karayuga cālanā — now waving the arms; kṣaṇahi uca kari — now raising (them); balai hari hari — He cries "Hari! Hari!"; pūruba prema pālanā — cherishing the former prema

**9.3.** Now He trembles, now His hair stands on end, now He waves His arms;
now, raising them high, He cries: "Hari! Hari!" — cherishing His former prema.

চাঁদ অবধূত ঠাকুর অদ্বৈত সঙ্গে সহচর মিলিয়া ।
কহে রামানন্দ কুলিশ সরসয়ে দারু দরবিত কেলিয়া ॥

*cām̐da abadhūta ṭhākura advaita saṅge sahacara miliyā |*
*kahe rāmānanda kuliśa sarasaye dāru darabita keliyā ||*

*Word for word:* cām̐da abadhūta — the avadhuta moon (Nityananda); ṭhākura advaita — Thakura Advaita; saṅge sahacara miliyā — with them all the associates; kahe rāmānanda — says Ramananda; kuliśa sarasaye — the diamond softens; dāru darabita — wood melts; keliyā — at (this) play

**9.4.** The avadhuta moon, Thakura Advaita, and with them all the associates.
Says Ramananda: at this play a diamond softens and wood melts.

[^15-16]: PK — vol. 3, 17th pallava, mark "॥২৫॥২০৮৩॥," raga turi, MS P-R-Sa no. 2192, checked against the scan (PDF p. 223, printed p. 212); in PK
the pada is unsigned. GPT1 — p. 284, section on bhavavesha, no. 23 (turi), scan PDF p. 543: the second half of the last line is replaced by
the signature "kahe nayanānanda dāsa"; GPT2 — sec. 4.3, no. 23. The pada is not in BR, KGC or PS; it was missing from the catalogue (new row
NN-031). Nayanananda, the nephew of Gadadhara Pandita, is a contemporary poet (chapters 4, 10, 14); but his signature is found only in
GPT — the attribution is conditional (C).
[^15-17]: The pada passes from Krishna's mood (memory of Vrindavana, the call of the flute) to Radha's: Gaura is Krishna Himself who has taken
on Radha's bhava and golden colour (CC Adi 4). Gadadhara Pandita — the tradition sees in him a manifestation of Radha (Gaura-ganoddesha-
dipika 147–153); the left side is Radha's place beside Krishna. "As if gazing at the flute at His lips" (muralī-mukha heriyā) may also mean
"gazing at the face with the flute," that is, seeking Krishna with His eyes. PK MS "P-R-Sa": "rādhikāra" for "śrīrādhāra."
[^15-18]: PK — vol. 3, 17th pallava, mark "॥৪৩॥২১০১॥," raga suhini, MS P-R-Sa no. 2210, checked against the scan (PDF pp. 230–231, printed
pp. 219–220). BR — ed. 1912/1913, pp. 925–926 (12th wave, "gīte yathā kāmodaḥ"), ed. 1960, vv. 3077–3082: Narahari Chakravarti quotes the pada while
showing Srinivasa the places of Navadvipa, right after a pada of Nayanananda "duhum̐ duhum̐ piriti…" (PK 2069, chapter 10, no. 9). GPT1 — p. 257, section on dance
and kirtana, no. 30 (suhini), scan PDF p. 516; GPT2 — sec. 4.2, no. 30. The pada was missing from the catalogue (new row YD-017). Signature
"yadu": BR quotes nearby padas of Yadunandana Chakravarti, a disciple of Gadadhara Dasa; most probably it is he, though Yadunatha
Kavichandra is not excluded; B (the pada is in BR).
[^15-19]: Gadadhara Pandita, Narahari Sarakara, Srivasa Pandita, Haridasa Thakura, Mukunda Datta, Murari Gupta are the Lord's associates in
Navadvipa. Vasu is Vasudeva (Ghosha or Datta); Ramai — Shrirama Pandita, Srivasa's brother (or Ramai Pandita); Damodara — Damodara
Pandita; Jagadisha — Jagadisha Pandita. The night kirtanas of Navadvipa — CB Madhya 8; CC Adi 17.
[^15-20]: GPT1 — p. 335, section "rasa and maharasa," no. 45 (gandhara), scan PDF p. 594; GPT2 — sec. 5.1, no. 45. The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or
PS; it was missing from the catalogue (new row RM-017). Signature "Ramananda" without "Vasu": Vasu Ramananda or the later Ramananda
Dasa (see the catalogue) — not established; C. The kirtanas in Srivasa's house — CB Madhya 8.
[^15-21]: "The dance of the whole universe" (akhila bhubanaka nāca) — possibly "a dance in which the whole universe is drawn." "Former prema" — the
prema of Vrindavana, of Krishna's lila. The avadhuta moon is Nityananda. "A diamond (vajra) softens, wood melts" — even the hardest
hearts melt. "Like the morning sun": GPT1 has "pātara" (= prātara, "morning").

## 10. Vasu Ghosha — "paṛiyā dharaṇītale śoke śacī…" (GPT1 p. 372, no. 21)
*Shachi's lament after the Lord's departure: fallen on the ground, she complains of cruel fate — her priceless treasure has been
stolen; Gorachand's bracelets, necklace and bed lie abandoned, Nadia is plunged in darkness; she is ready to become a yogini and go in
search of Him, to sell herself as a maid to whoever will give her back Gauranga; the poet: do not weep, Shachi — for the sake of the
living beings Nimai has become a sannyasi. Raga karuna.*[^15-22]

পড়িয়া ধরণীতলে শোকে শচী কাঁদি বলে লাগিল দারুণ বিধি বাদে ।
অমূল্য রতন ছিল কোন্ বিধি হরি নিল পরাণ-পুতলী গোরাচাঁদে ॥

*paṛiyā dharaṇītale śoke śacī kām̐di bale lāgila dāruṇa bidhi bāde |*
*amūlya ratana chila kon bidhi hari nila parāṇa-putalī gorācām̐de ||*

*Word for word:* paṛiyā dharaṇītale — fallen on the ground; śoke śacī kām̐di bale — Shachi, weeping in grief, says; lāgila dāruṇa bidhi bāde — cruel fate has turned enemy; amūlya ratana chila — there was a priceless treasure; kon bidhi hari nila — what fate has stolen; parāṇa-putalī gorācām̐de — Gorachand, the darling doll of the soul

**10.1.** Fallen on the ground, Shachi weeps in grief and says: "Cruel fate has become my enemy!
I had a priceless treasure — what fate has stolen Gorachand, the darling doll of my soul?

অঙ্গের অঙ্গদবালা গোরাচাঁদের কণ্ঠমালা খাট পাট সোণার দুলিচা ।
সে সব রহিল পড়ি গৌর মোরে গেল ছাড়ি আমি প্রাণ ধরি আছি মিছা ॥

*aṅgera aṅgadabālā gorācām̐dera kaṇṭhamālā khāṭa pāṭa soṇāra dulicā |*
*se saba rahila paṛi gaura more gela chāṛi āmi prāṇa dhari āchi michā ||*

*Word for word:* aṅgera aṅgadabālā — the bracelets of His arms; gorācām̐dera kaṇṭhamālā — Gorachand's necklace; khāṭa pāṭa — bed, silk; soṇāra dulicā — the gold-woven rug; se saba rahila paṛi — all that lies abandoned; gaura more gela chāṛi — Gaura has left me; āmi prāṇa dhari āchi michā — I keep my life in vain

**10.2.** The bracelets from His arms, Gorachand's necklace, the bed, the silk, the gold-woven rug —
all lie abandoned: Gaura has left me, and I go on living in vain.

গৌরাঙ্গ ছাড়িয়া গেল নদীয়া আঁধার ভেল ছটফটি করে মোর হিয়া ।
যোগিনী হইয়া যাব গৌরাঙ্গ যথায় পাব কাঁদিব তার গলায় ধরিয়া ॥

*gaurāṅga chāṛiyā gela nadīyā ām̐dhāra bhela chaṭaphaṭi kare mora hiyā |*
*yoginī haiyā yāba gaurāṅga yathāya pāba kām̐diba tāra galāya dhariyā ||*

*Word for word:* gaurāṅga chāṛiyā gela — Gauranga has gone away; nadīyā ām̐dhāra bhela — Nadia has become dark; chaṭaphaṭi kare mora hiyā — my heart tosses; yoginī haiyā yāba — I shall become a yogini and go; gaurāṅga yathāya pāba — where I can find Gauranga; kām̐diba tāra galāya dhariyā — I shall weep holding His neck

**10.3.** Gauranga has gone — Nadia is plunged in darkness, my heart tosses about.
I shall become a yogini, I shall go where I can find Gauranga — I shall weep, my arms around His neck.

যে মোরে গৌরাঙ্গ দিব বিনামূলে বিকাইব হৈব তার দাসের অনুদাসী ।
বাসুদেব ঘোষে ভণে কাঁদ শচি কি কারণে জীব লাগি নিমাই সন্ন্যাসী ॥

*ye more gaurāṅga diba bināmūle bikāiba haiba tāra dāsera anudāsī |*
*bāsudeba ghoṣe bhaṇe kām̐da śaci ki kāraṇe jība lāgi nimāi sannyāsī ||*

*Word for word:* ye more gaurāṅga diba — whoever gives me Gauranga; bināmūle bikāiba — I shall sell myself without price; haiba tāra dāsera anudāsī — I shall be the maid of his servant; bāsudeba ghoṣe bhaṇe — says Vasudeva Ghosha; kām̐da śaci ki kāraṇe — why do you weep, Shachi; jība lāgi — for the sake of the living beings; nimāi sannyāsī — Nimai is a sannyasi

**10.4.** Whoever gives me back Gauranga — to him I shall sell myself without price, I shall be the maid of his servant."
Says Vasudeva Ghosha: why do you weep, Shachi? For the sake of the living beings Nimai has become a sannyasi.[^15-23]

## 11. Vasu Ghosha — "svarūpera mukhe śuni mānalīlā…" (GPT1 p. 290, no. 42)
*The Lord in Radha's bhava: hearing from Svarupa of the mana-lila, He is plunged into the bhava of the Loving One (Radha), dances crying
"Radha-kunda!", slowly walks to the bank of the "Yamuna," sits by the water and, His face bowed, is lost in thought; the poet: only one
who has realized rasa in the heart knows its essence. Raga dhanashi, tala dashakushi.*[^15-24]

ভাবাবেশে গৌরকিশোর ।
স্বরূপের মুখে শুনি মানলীলা দ্বিজমণি ভাবিনীর ভাবেতে বিভোর ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*bhābābeśe gaurakiśora |*
*svarūpera mukhe śuni mānalīlā dvijamaṇi bhābinīra bhābete bibhora || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* bhābābeśe — in bhavavesha; gaura-kiśora — young Gaura; svarūpera mukhe śuni — hearing from Svarupa's lips; māna-līlā — the mana-lila; dvija-maṇi — the jewel of brahmanas; bhābinīra bhābete bibhora — lost in the bhava of the Loving One (Radha)

**11.1.** *(Refrain)* Young Gaura is in bhavavesha:
hearing from Svarupa's lips of the mana-lila, the jewel of brahmanas was lost in the bhava of the Loving One.[^15-25]

রাধাকুণ্ড রাধাকুণ্ড বলি নাচে ভুজদণ্ড প্রেমধারা বহে দুনয়নে ।
না বুঝি ভাবের গতি ধীরে ধীরে করে গতি গজরাজ জিনিয়া গমনে ॥

*rādhākuṇḍa rādhākuṇḍa bali nāce bhujadaṇḍa premadhārā bahe dunayane |*
*nā bujhi bhābera gati dhīre dhīre kare gati gajarāja jiniyā gamane ||*

*Word for word:* rādhākuṇḍa rādhākuṇḍa bali — crying "Radha-kunda! Radha-kunda!"; nāce bhujadaṇḍa — dances with arms (flung up); prema-dhārā bahe dunayane — streams of prema flow from both eyes; nā bujhi bhābera gati — one cannot understand the course of the bhava; dhīre dhīre kare gati — slowly, slowly He walks; gajarāja jiniyā gamane — with a gait surpassing the king of elephants

**11.2.** "Radha-kunda! Radha-kunda!" — crying out, He dances with arms flung up; streams of prema flow from both His eyes.
One cannot understand where His bhava is drawing Him: slowly, slowly He walks, His gait surpassing the king of elephants.

যাইয়া যমুনাতটে বসি জলসন্নিকটে ভাবনা করয়ে মনে মনে ।
সে ভাব তরঙ্গ হেরি কিছুই বুঝিতে নারি রহিয়াছে হেঁট শ্রীবদনে ॥

*yāiyā yamunātaṭe basi jalasannikaṭe bhābanā karaye mane mane |*
*se bhāba taraṅga heri kichui bujhite nāri rahiyāche hem̐ṭa śrībadane ||*

*Word for word:* yāiyā yamunā-taṭe — going to the bank of the Yamuna; basi jala-sannikaṭe — sitting near the water; bhābanā karaye mane mane — He is lost in thought; se bhāba taraṅga heri — seeing the waves of that bhava; kichui bujhite nāri — I cannot understand anything; rahiyāche hem̐ṭa śrī-badane — He remains with His holy face bowed

**11.3.** Coming to the bank of the Yamuna, sitting right by the water, He is lost in thought;
seeing the waves of that bhava, I can understand nothing: He sits with His holy face bowed.

বাসুদেব ঘোষ ভণে অনুভব যার মনে রসিকে জানয়ে রস মর্ম ।
অনুভব নাহি যার বেদ্য নাহি হয় তার বৃথা তার হইল এ জনম ॥

*bāsudeba ghoṣa bhaṇe anubhaba yāra mane rasike jānaye rasa marma |*
*anubhaba nāhi yāra bedya nāhi haya tāra bṛthā tāra haila e janama ||*

*Word for word:* bāsudeba ghoṣa bhaṇe — says Vasudeva Ghosha; anubhaba yāra mane — one who has realization in the heart; rasike jānaye rasa marma — he, the connoisseur of rasa, knows the essence of rasa; anubhaba nāhi yāra — one who has no realization; bedya nāhi haya tāra — to him it is unknowable; bṛthā tāra haila e janama — his life has been in vain

**11.4.** Says Vasudeva Ghosha: one who has realization in his heart — he, the connoisseur of rasa, knows the essence of rasa;
one who has no realization — to him it is unknowable: his life has been in vain.

## 12. Vasu Ghosha — "svarūpera kāche gaurahari…" (GPT1 p. 306, no. 24)
*The Lord in the bhava of Radha disappointed in waiting (vipralabdha): weeping before Svarupa, He says that in vain He set the snares
of love — Kala-chand did not come to the kunja, the dew is falling, the night has passed for nothing; having said this, He rolls on the
ground. Raga suhai.*[^15-26]

স্বরূপের কাছে গৌরহরি ।
কাঁদি কহে ফুকরি ফুকরি ॥

*svarūpera kāche gaurahari |*
*kām̐di kahe phukari phukari ||*

*Word for word:* svarūpera kāche — before Svarupa; gaurahari — Gaurahari; kām̐di kahe — weeping speaks; phukari phukari — sobbing aloud

**12.1.** Before Svarupa Gaurahari,
weeping, speaks, sobbing aloud:

বৃথাই পাতিনু প্রেমফাঁদ ।
কুঞ্জে না আয়ল কালাচাঁদ ॥

*bṛthāi pātinu premaphām̐da |*
*kuñje nā āyala kālācām̐da ||*

*Word for word:* bṛthāi pātinu — in vain I laid; prema-phām̐da — the snares of love; kuñje nā āyala — did not come to the kunja; kālā-cām̐da — Kala-chand (Krishna)

**12.2.** "In vain I laid the snares of love —
Kala-chand did not come to the kunja.

টুপটাপ পড়িছে শিশির ।
রজনী ভেল ত সুগভীর ॥

*ṭupaṭāpa paṛiche śiśira |*
*rajanī bhela ta sugabhīra ||*

*Word for word:* ṭupaṭāpa paṛiche śiśira — drip-drip, the dew is falling; rajanī bhela ta sugabhīra — the night has grown very deep

**12.3.** Drip, drip — the dew is falling;
the night has grown very deep.

আশাপথ বৃথাই চাহিনু ।
বৃথা ইহ যামিনী যাপিনু ॥

*āśāpatha bṛthāi cāhinu |*
*bṛthā iha yāminī yāpinu ||*

*Word for word:* āśā-patha — the road of hope; bṛthāi cāhinu — in vain I watched; bṛthā iha yāminī yāpinu — in vain I spent this night

**12.4.** In vain I watched the road of hope,
in vain I spent this night."[^15-27]

ইহা কহি ধরণী লোটায় ।
বাসু ঘোষ করে হায় হায় ॥

*ihā kahi dharaṇī loṭāya |*
*bāsu ghoṣa kare hāya hāya ||*

*Word for word:* ihā kahi — having said this; dharaṇī loṭāya — rolls on the ground; bāsu ghoṣa kare hāya hāya — Vasu Ghosha moans "alas, alas"

**12.5.** Having said this, He rolls on the ground;
Vasu Ghosha moans: "Alas, alas!"

[^15-22]: GPT1 — p. 372, section on the sannyasa, no. 21 (karuna), checked against the scan (PDF p. 631); GPT2 — sec. 5.3, no. 21. The pada is not in
PK (including Vasu's sannyasa cycle PK 2221–2229, chapter 4), BR, KGC or PS; it was missing from the catalogue (new row VG-175). The
preceding pada of GPT (no. 20) is Vasu's PK 2221 (chapter 4, no. 10). GPT only; C.
[^15-23]: "I shall become a yogini" — I shall go as a wandering ascetic to find my son: so speaks a mother's love (vatsalya). "For the sake of the
living beings": the Lord took sannyasa so that even the proud, seeing a sannyasi, would bow before Him and receive prema (CC Adi 17;
CB Madhya 26). Shachi's grief after the sannyasa — CC Madhya 3; CB Antya 1.
[^15-24]: GPT1 — p. 290, section on bhavavesha, no. 42 (dhanashi, dashakushi), checked against the scan (PDF p. 549); GPT2 — sec. 4.3, no. 42. The
pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS; it was missing from the catalogue (new row VG-176). Svarupa Damodara was with the Lord in Puri and sang
Him songs in keeping with His bhava (CC Madhya 10; Antya 14–19); the "Yamuna" is apparently the sea or a river in Puri which the Lord in
His bhava takes for the Yamuna (cf. CC Antya 18). Majumdar doubts that GPT padas in which Svarupa is with the Lord belong to Vasu (see
chapter 12, no. 28); GPT only; C.
[^15-25]: The mana-lila is the play of Radha's offended pride (mana), the highest manifestation of Her love for Krishna. "The Loving One" (bhābinī)
is Radha. Radha's bhava is pure prema, not a worldly feeling; the Lord tastes it in order to know Radha's love (CC Adi 4). Radha-kunda is
Radha's pond near Govardhana.
[^15-26]: GPT1 — p. 306, section on Radha's moods (vasaka-sajja, vipralabdha), no. 24 (suhai), checked against the scan (PDF p. 565); GPT2 — sec. 4.5,
no. 24. The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS; it was missing from the catalogue (new row VG-177). The next pada of GPT (no. 25, "svarūpera kare
dhari…") was translated in chapter 12 (no. 28). GPT only; C.
[^15-27]: The Lord in Radha's bhava speaks Her words (Svarupa in this lila is
Radha's friend Lalita). Kala-chand, "the dark moon," is Krishna; a kunja is a bower in Vrindavana. The Lord's bhavas in Puri in Svarupa's
company — CC Antya 14–19.

## 13. Chaitanyadasa — "ki baliba bidhātāre e dukha sahāya…" (PK 1867; GPT1 p. 281, no. 12)
*The divine madness of prema (divyonmada): the poet does not know what to say to the Creator — seeing Gora's face, how can one still
live? The Lord sits with faded face, tears pour like the heavenly Ganga onto the peak of Sumeru; now He rubs His face and head, now He
leaps up and runs, now He falls senseless; His breath stops — all weep. Raga suhini.*[^15-28]

কি বলিব বিধাতারে এ দুখ সহায় ।
গোরা-মুখ হেরি কেনে পরাণ না যায় ॥

*ki baliba bidhātāre e dukha sahāya |*
*gorā-mukha heri kene parāṇa nā yāya ||*

*Word for word:* ki baliba bidhātāre — what shall I say to the Creator; e dukha sahāya — (who makes us) bear this pain; gorā-mukha heri — seeing Gora's face; kene parāṇa nā yāya — why does life not go

**13.1.** What shall I say to the Creator, who makes us bear this pain?
Seeing Gora's face, why does life not leave me?

মলিন বদনে বসি আঁখিযুগ ঝরে ।
আকাশ-গঙ্গার ধারা সুমেরু-শিখরে ॥

*malina badane basi ām̐khiyuga jhare |*
*ākāśa-gaṅgāra dhārā sumeru-śikhare ||*

*Word for word:* malina badane basi — sitting with a faded face; ām̐khi-yuga jhare — both eyes pour; ākāśa-gaṅgāra dhārā — a stream of the heavenly Ganga; sumeru-śikhare — on the peak of Sumeru

**13.2.** He sits with a faded face, tears pour from both His eyes —
like a stream of the heavenly Ganga onto the peak of Sumeru.

ক্ষণে মুখ শির ঘসে ক্ষণে উঠি ধায় ।
অতি দুরবল ভূমে পড়ি মুরছায় ॥

*kṣaṇe mukha śira ghase kṣaṇe uṭhi dhāya |*
*ati durabala bhūme paṛi murachāya ||*

*Word for word:* kṣaṇe mukha śira ghase — now rubs face and head; kṣaṇe uṭhi dhāya — now leaps up and runs; ati durabala — utterly weak; bhūme paṛi muracchāya — falls on the ground senseless

**13.3.** Now He rubs His face and head, now He leaps up and runs;
utterly spent, He falls to the ground senseless.

নাসায় নাহিক শ্বাস দেখি সভে কান্দে ।
চৈতন্যদাসের হিয়া থির নাহি বান্ধে ॥

*nāsāya nāhika śvāsa dekhi sabhe kānde |*
*caitanyadāsera hiyā thira nāhi bāndhe ||*

*Word for word:* nāsāya nāhika śvāsa — there is no breath in the nostrils; dekhi sabhe kānde — seeing it, all weep; caitanya-dāsera hiyā — the heart of Chaitanyadasa; thira nāhi bāndhe — cannot be calm

**13.4.** There is no breath in His nostrils — seeing this, all weep;
the heart of Chaitanyadasa cannot be calm.[^15-29]

## 14. Vasu Ghosha — "nitāi āmāra parama dayāla…" (GPT1 p. 424, no. 32)
*Nityananda's flood of prema: Nitai brought a flood of prema into the world, and it filled the rivers and canals; the wave carried away
sinners and sufferers alike, the devotees sport in it, some swim; Nadia and Shantipur went under — and started a boat race; Nitai
laughs, and the poet flounders in the waves. Raga sindhura.*[^15-30]

নিতাই আমার পরম দয়াল ।
আনিয়া প্রেমের বন্যা জগত করিল ধন্যা ভরিল প্রেমের নদীখাল ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*nitāi āmāra parama dayāla |*
*āniyā premera banyā jagata karila dhanyā bharila premera nadīkhāla || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* nitāi āmāra parama dayāla — my Nitai is supremely merciful; āniyā premera banyā — bringing a flood of prema; jagata karila dhanyā — blessed the world; bharila premera nadī-khāla — filled the rivers and canals with prema

**14.1.** *(Refrain)* My Nitai is supremely merciful:
bringing a flood of prema, He blessed the world — filled the rivers and canals with prema.

লাগিয়া প্রেমের ঢেউ বাকী না রহিল কেউ পাপী তাপী চলিল ভাসিয়া ।
সকল ভকত মেলি সে প্রেমেতে করে কেলি কেহ কেহ যায় সাঁতারিয়া ॥

*lāgiyā premera ḍheu bākī nā rahila keu pāpī tāpī calila bhāsiyā |*
*sakala bhakata meli se premete kare keli keha keha yāya sām̐tāriyā ||*

*Word for word:* lāgiyā premera ḍheu — the wave of prema striking; bākī nā rahila keu — no one was left aside; pāpī tāpī — sinners and sufferers; calila bhāsiyā — were carried away floating; sakala bhakata meli — all the devotees together; se premete kare keli — sport in that prema; keha keha yāya sām̐tāriyā — some go swimming

**14.2.** The wave of prema struck — no one was left aside: sinners and sufferers were carried off by the current;
all the devotees together sport in that prema, and some go swimming.

ডুবিল নদীয়াপুর ডুবে প্রেমে শান্তিপুর দোঁহে মিলি বাইছালি খেলায় ।
তা দেখি নিতাই হাসে সকলেই প্রেমে ভাসে বাসু ঘোষ হাবুডুবু খায় ॥

*ḍubila nadīyāpura ḍube preme śāntipura dom̐he mili bāichāli khelāya |*
*tā dekhi nitāi hāse sakalei preme bhāse bāsu ghoṣa hābuḍubu khāya ||*

*Word for word:* ḍubila nadīyāpura — Nadia went under; ḍube preme śāntipura — Shantipur sinks in prema; dom̐he mili — both together; bāichāli khelāya — play at boat-racing; tā dekhi nitāi hāse — seeing this, Nitai laughs; sakalei preme bhāse — all float in prema; bāsu ghoṣa hābuḍubu khāya — Vasu Ghosha flounders, gulping water

**14.3.** Nadia went under, Shantipur is sinking in prema — the two together have started a boat race;
seeing this, Nitai laughs; all float in prema, and Vasu Ghosha flounders, gulping water.[^15-31]

## 15. Kanu Dasa — "āota nityānanda adabhuta cām̐da…" (GPT1 pp. 431–432, no. 59)
*Praise of Nityananda: Nityananda comes — a wondrous moon with the enchanting gait of a dancer; His face and eyes are lotuses, His lips
brighter than the dawn, His teeth pearls; with the nectar of His words He sprinkles those scorched by worldly existence, with the rays of
the name "Hare Krishna" He dispels the darkness of bad desires; around Him are His companions like stars. Raga kalyana.*[^15-32]

আওত নিত্যানন্দ অদভুত চাঁদ ।
সহজ গমন নটন গতি সুন্দর ত্রিভুবন জন মোহন ছাঁদ ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*āota nityānanda adabhuta cām̐da |*
*sahaja gamana naṭana gati sundara tribhubana jana mohana chām̐da || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* āota nityānanda — Nityananda comes; adabhuta cām̐da — a wondrous moon; sahaja gamana — natural gait; naṭana gati sundara — beautiful dancing step; tribhubana jana mohana chām̐da — a form enchanting the people of the three worlds

**15.1.** *(Refrain)* Nityananda comes — a wondrous moon:
natural is His gait, beautiful His dancing step — a form that enchants the people of the three worlds.

বয়ন নয়ন সুবিমল সুন্দর অম্বুজ মধুলিহ ভুজযুগ ভাঁতি ।
অরুণাধরদ্যুতি অরুণিহ শোভে অতি দশন মোতিকল পাঁতি ॥

*bayana nayana subimala sundara ambuja madhuliha bhujayuga bhām̐ti |*
*aruṇādharadyuti aruṇiha śobhe ati daśana motikala pām̐ti ||*

*Word for word:* bayana nayana — face and eyes; subimala sundara — pure and beautiful; ambuja — lotuses; madhuliha — bees; bhuja-yuga (= bhuru-yuga?) bhām̐ti — the shine of the pair of brows; aruṇādhara-dyuti — the lustre of red lips; aruṇi-ha śobhe ati — shines more than the dawn; daśana motikala pām̐ti — teeth a string of pearls

**15.2.** His face and eyes are pure, beautiful lotuses, and over them, like bees, the pair of brows;
the lustre of His red lips is brighter than the dawn, His teeth a string of pearls.[^15-33]

ভবতাপিত জন সিঞ্চহ সকরুণ বচন পীযূষ-রস ধারে ।
হরেকৃষ্ণ নাম কিরণে নাশই সব দুর্বাসনা আঁধিয়ারে ॥

*bhabatāpita jana siñcaha sakaruṇa bacana pīyūṣa-rasa dhāre |*
*harekṛṣṇa nāma kiraṇe nāśai saba durvāsanā ām̐dhiyāre ||*

*Word for word:* bhabatāpita jana — those scorched by worldly existence; siñcaha sakaruṇa — He mercifully sprinkles; bacana pīyūṣa-rasa dhāre — with streams of the nectar of His words; harekṛṣṇa nāma kiraṇe — with the rays of the name "Hare Krishna"; nāśai saba — destroys all; durvāsanā ām̐dhiyāre — the darkness of bad desires

**15.3.** Those scorched by the heat of worldly existence He mercifully sprinkles with streams of the nectar of His words;
with the rays of the name "Hare Krishna" He destroys all the darkness of bad desires.

চৌদিকে সঙ্গী রঙ্গী উড়ু মণ্ডল নিশি দিশি চাঁদ পরকাশে ।
শ্রীজাহ্নবাবল্লভ শ্রীপাদপল্লব আশে শ্রীকানু দাস ভাষে ॥

*caudike saṅgī raṅgī uṛu maṇḍala niśi diśi cām̐da parakāśe |*
*śrījāhnabāballabha śrīpādapallaba āśe śrīkānu dāsa bhāṣe ||*

*Word for word:* caudike saṅgī raṅgī — around, merry companions; uḍu-maṇḍala — a host of stars; niśi diśi — night and day; cām̐da parakāśe — the moon shines; śrī-jāhnabā-ballabha — of Sri Jahnava-vallabha (Nityananda); śrī-pāda-pallava — the feet tender as shoots; āśe — hoping for; śrī-kānu dāsa bhāṣe — speaks Sri Kanu Dasa

**15.4.** Around Him are His merry companions, like a host of stars: night and day this moon shines.
Hoping for the feet, tender as young shoots, of Sri Jahnava-vallabha, speaks Sri Kanu Dasa.[^15-34]

[^15-28]: PK — vol. 3, 10th pallava ("nānābidha biraha"), at the beginning of the cycle "atha dibyonmādasya daśa daśāḥ | tatra śrīgauracandraḥ" (a
gaura-chandrika to the ten states of Radha in divine madness), mark "॥১৬॥১৮৬৭॥," raga suhini, checked against the scan (PDF p. 135, printed
p. 124); GPT1 — p. 281, section on bhavavesha, no. 12 (suhini), scan PDF p. 540; GPT2 — sec. 4.3, no. 12. The pada is not in BR, KGC or PS; it was
missing from the catalogue (new row CD-008). Chaitanyadasa, according to Majumdar, is probably a contemporary of the branch of Gadadhara
(chapters 4–7); B.
[^15-29]: The Lord's state is the divine madness of prema in separation from Krishna, not a worldly illness or grief: He rubs His face against
the walls of the Gambhira (CC Antya 19); in the deepest swoon of prema His breath stops (cf. CC Antya 14, 17). "Why does life not leave me"
is the sorrow of a devotee who sees the Lord's suffering in separation. The heavenly Ganga (Mandakini) flowing down the golden mountain
Sumeru is an image of the tears streaming down Gaura's golden body. PK MSS: "uṭhe" — kha; "durabale" — cha; "bhome" — cha.
[^15-30]: GPT1 — p. 424, section on Nityananda, no. 32 (sindhura), checked against the scan (PDF p. 683); GPT2 — sec. 6.1, no. 32. The pada is not in
PK, BR, KGC or PS; it was missing from the catalogue (new row VG-178). Colloquial words (bāichāli — boat race, hābuḍubu khāya — "flounders,
gulping water") point to a late origin; C. Nityananda's preaching in Gauda — CB Antya 5–6.
[^15-31]: The flood of prema that inundated the world is an image from CC Adi 7: Advaita called the Lord down, Nityananda spread prema all over
Gauda. Nadia (Navadvipa) is the Lord's place, Shantipur Advaita's. "Flounders" — the poet's humility: he cannot swim in this flood.

is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS (catalogue: KD-011). Kanu Thakura, the son of Purushottama, grew up in the care of Jahnava-devi ("Prema-vilasa") —
the signature "Sri Jahnava-vallabha" (Jahnava's husband, Nityananda) fits him; but the pada is known only from GPT; C.

eyes" is the usual image of brows. "A string of pearls": GPT1 "motikala," GPT2 "motiphala" ("pearl").

at the Lord's command, gave to everyone (CB Madhya 13).

# Chapter 16. Yadu: Two Gaura-padas from the *Padakalpataru* Found in the Full Check of PK

*This chapter is the result of a full check of all four volumes of the *Padakalpataru* (PK) by the signatures of the poets
contemporary with Mahaprabhu on Majumdar's list. Only three
gaura-padas turned out to be unknown to the catalogue and to translations 01–15, all signed "Yadu" (Yadunatha): two are translated
here, the third (PK 703) is in nagari-bhava and is deferred to the section of nagari-padas. The other results of the check are PK
numbers for padas previously known only from the *Gaura-pada-tarangini* (GPT), the *Bhakti-ratnakara* or the
*Kshanada-gita-chintamani* and already translated (YD-003 = PK 2512, YD-004 = PK 1976, AN-007 = PK 2328, AN-008 = PK 2337, BD-028 =
PK 2301, BD-041 = PK 635, KR-004 = PK 1464, VG-151 = PK 2668), and a correction: Balarama's pada "saba abatāra sāra…" (chapter 13,
no. 8) is PK 2201, bearing his signature in PK itself, not Lochana Dasa's pada PK 2203; the notes of those chapters have been
supplemented. Both padas of this chapter stand in the 20th pallava of PK ("Sri Gaurachandra — other descriptions") and are also in
GPT1 (p. 37, nos. 33–34): praise of the Gaura-avatara, before whom all living beings weep, and the love of Gaura and Gadadhara. The
text follows PK with the GPT variants; the Bengali original and the word-for-word translation are in the full version of the book.*

## 1. Yadu — "jalera jība kānde dekhiyā pratibimba…" (PK 2209; GPT1 p. 37, no. 34)
*Praise of the Gaura-avatara: at the sight of Gorachand all living beings weep — the creatures of the water seeing His reflection,
the beasts and birds in the forests; trees thrill, stones melt, the blind weep aloud hearing of Him, the wives of noble families
weep, the deaf and the helpless, infants leaving the breast; there will be no such incarnation again — He saved all, only the poet
is left out. Raga mangala.*[^16-1]

জলের জীব কান্দে দেখিয়া প্রতিবিম্ব কাননে কান্দয়ে পশু পাখী ।
তরুয়া পুলকিত পাষাণ দরবিত শুনিয়া অন্ধ কান্দে ডাকি ॥

*jalera jība kānde dekhiyā pratibimba kānane kāndaye paśu pākhī |*
*taruyā pulakita pāṣāṇa darabita śuniyā andha kānde ḍāki ||*

*Word for word:* jalera jība — the creatures of the water; kānde — weep; dekhiyā pratibimba — seeing [His] reflection; kānane — in the forest; kāndaye paśu pākhī — beasts and birds weep; taruyā pulakita — the trees thrill; pāṣāṇa darabita — the stones melt; śuniyā — hearing; andha kānde ḍāki — the blind weep, crying out

**1.1.** The creatures of the water weep, seeing His reflection; in the forests the beasts and birds weep;
the trees thrill, the stones melt, the blind, hearing of Him, weep and cry aloud.

অপরূপ গোরাচাঁদের দেহ ।
অসীম অনুভব এক মুখে কি কহব মনে যে মুখে না আইসে সেহ ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*aparūpa gorācām̐dera deha |*
*asīma anubhaba eka mukhe ki kahaba mane ye mukhe nā āise seha || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* aparūpa — wondrous; gorācām̐dera deha — the body of Gorachand; asīma anubhaba — boundless is what one feels; eka mukhe — with one mouth; ki kahaba — what shall I tell; mane ye — what is in the heart; mukhe nā āise seha — that does not come to the lips

**1.2.** *(Refrain)* Wondrous is the body of Gorachand!
Boundless is what one feels: how can one tell it with a single mouth? What is in the heart does not come to the lips.

কুলের কুল-বধূ ফুকরি সেহ কান্দে বধির জড় কান্দে ধান্দে ।
মায়ের স্তন ছাড়ি দুধের বালক না জানি কিবা লাগি কান্দে ॥

*kulera kula-badhū phukari seha kānde badhira jaṛa kānde dhānde |*
*māyera stana chāṛi dudhera bālaka nā jāni kibā lāgi kānde ||*

*Word for word:* kulera kula-badhū — the wives of noble families; phukari seha kānde — even they weep aloud; badhira jaṛa — the deaf and the helpless; kānde dhānde — weep in bewilderment; māyera stana chāṛi — leaving the mother's breast; dudhera bālaka — the suckling infant; nā jāni kibā lāgi kānde — weeps, no one knows why

**1.3.** The wives of noble families — even they weep aloud; the deaf and the helpless weep in bewilderment;
the infant, leaving its mother's breast, weeps — no one knows why.[^16-2]

এমন অবতার হবেক নাহি আর কেবল করুণার সিন্ধু ।
পতিত মূঢ় জড় অজড় উদ্ধারিল কেবল বঞ্চিত ভেল যদু ॥

*emana abatāra habeka nāhi āra kebala karuṇāra sindhu |*
*patita mūṛha jaṛa ajaṛa uddhārila kebala bañcita bhela yadu ||*

*Word for word:* emana abatāra — such an incarnation; habeka nāhi āra — there will be no more; kebala karuṇāra sindhu — an ocean of nothing but mercy; patita — the fallen; mūṛha — the foolish; jaṛa ajaṛa — the inanimate and the animate; uddhārila — He saved; kebala bañcita bhela yadu — only Yadu was left out

**1.4.** There will be no such incarnation again: He is an ocean of nothing but mercy.
The fallen, the foolish, the inanimate and the animate — He saved them all; only Yadu was left out.[^16-3]

## 2. Yadu — "gaura gadādhara duhum̐ tanu sundara…" (PK 2182; GPT1 p. 37, no. 33)
*Gaura and Gadadhara: both are beautiful and wondrously spread prema; when, rejoicing, they touch each other, nectar flows; hand in
hand, eye to eye — a sweetness beyond understanding; who, plunging into these feelings, will reach the bottom? Seeing them, people
forget body and mind. Raga kedara.*[^16-4]

গৌর গদাধর দুহুঁ তনু সুন্দর অপরূপ প্রেম বিথার ।
দুহুঁ দুহুঁ হরষে পরশে যব বিলসয়ে অমিয়া বরিখে অনিবার ॥

*gaura gadādhara duhum̐ tanu sundara aparūpa prema bithāra |*
*duhum̐ duhum̐ haraṣe paraśe yaba bilasaye amiyā barikhe anibāra ||*

*Word for word:* gaura gadādhara — Gaura and Gadadhara; duhum̐ tanu sundara — both beautiful in body; aparūpa prema bithāra — wondrously spreading prema; duhum̐ duhum̐ haraṣe — both rejoicing; paraśe yaba bilasaye — when they play, touching [each other]; amiyā barikhe anibāra — nectar pours without end

**2.1.** Gaura and Gadadhara — both are beautiful, wondrously spreading prema;
when, rejoicing, they touch each other in their play, nectar pours without end.[^16-5]

দেখ দেখ অপরূপ দুহুঁ জন-নেহ ।
কো অছু ভাব প্রেমময় চাতুরি নিমজিয়া পাওব থেহ ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*dekha dekha aparūpa duhum̐ jana-neha |*
*ko achu bhāba premamaya cāturi nimajiyā pāoba theha || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* dekha dekha — behold, behold; aparūpa — wondrous; duhum̐ jana-neha — the love of the two; ko — who; achu bhāba — [into] such feelings; premamaya cāturi — [into] an art full of prema; nimajiyā — plunging; pāoba theha — will reach the bottom

**2.2.** *(Refrain)* Behold, behold: wondrous is the love of these two!
Who, plunging into these feelings, into this art full of prema, will reach the bottom?

করে করে নয়নে নয়নে যোই মাধুরি সো সব কি বুঝব হাম ।
অপরূপ রূপ হেরি তনু চমকিত অখিল ভুবনে অনুপাম ॥

*kare kare nayane nayane yoi mādhuri so saba ki bujhaba hāma |*
*aparūpa rūpa heri tanu camakita akhila bhubane anupāma ||*

*Word for word:* kare kare — hand in hand; nayane nayane — eye to eye; yoi mādhuri — that sweetness; so saba — all that; ki bujhaba hāma — how could I understand; aparūpa rūpa heri — seeing the wondrous beauty; tanu camakita — the body thrills; akhila bhubane anupāma — matchless in all the worlds

**2.3.** Hand in hand, eye to eye — the sweetness that is between them, how could I understand it?
Seeing their wondrous beauty, the body thrills: there is none like it in all the worlds.

অমিয়া-পুতলি কিয়ে রসময় মূরতি কিয়ে দুহুঁ প্রেম-আকার ।
হেরইতে জগ-জন তনু মন ভূলয়ে যদু কিয়ে পাওব পার ॥

*amiyā-putali kiye rasamaya mūrati kiye duhum̐ prema-ākāra |*
*heraite jaga-jana tanu mana bhūlaye yadu kiye pāoba pāra ||*

*Word for word:* amiyā-putali kiye — are they dolls of nectar; rasamaya mūrati — [or] embodiments of rasa; kiye duhum̐ prema-ākāra — or prema in two forms; heraite — seeing; jaga-jana — the people of the world; tanu mana bhūlaye — forget body and mind; yadu — Yadu; kiye pāoba pāra — will he find a limit

**2.4.** Are they dolls of nectar, or embodiments of rasa, or is it prema itself that has taken two forms?
Seeing them, the people of the world forget body and mind — will Yadu find a limit to it?[^16-6]

checked against the scan (PDF p. 272, printed p. 261); GPT1 — p. 37, section of praise of the Gaura-avatara, no. 34 (mangala), checked

families here are among all living beings: this is not the motif of townswomen captivated by Gaura's beauty (nagari-bhava) but a

"gaura-nagari" (Gaura as the nagara among the women of Nadia).

# Part II. Appendix: Padas Signed "Narahari" from the Gaura-pada-tarangini

---

# Chapter 17. Appendix. Padas signed "Narahari" from the Gaura-pada-tarangini — I: mangalacharana, Gaura's form, abhisheka, kirtana and dance, bhavavesha

## Introductory note to the appendix

*In the Gaura-pada-tarangini (GPT1 — 1st ed. by Jagadbandhu Bhadra, 1903; GPT2 — 2nd ed., 1934) more than three hundred padas
are signed with the name "Narahari" (narahari, "narahari dāsa", "dāsa narahari", "narahari-pahu"). Those also found in the
Padakalpataru (PK) were translated in the main part (chapters 1–6): they are padas of Narahari Sarakara, which Majumdar
examines as songs of an eyewitness. Here, as a separate appendix, are gathered the padas with the same signature known only
from the GPT (and from the Bhakti-ratnakara) — by decision, all are to be translated, with a caveat about attribution.*

*Narahari is the name of two poets. **Narahari Sarakara Thakura** of Shrikhanda was an associate of Mahaprabhu, the teacher
of Lochana Dasa, a singer of the Lord's bhavas in Navadvipa and Puri; according to the Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika (177), he is Madhumati, an intimate friend of
Radha in Vrindavana. **Narahari Chakravarti** (also called Ghanashyama Dasa), who lived in Vrindavana in the first half of the 18th
century, is the author of the Bhakti-ratnakara (BR), Narottama-vilasa, Gita-chandrodaya and other books; in the BR he inserted
many of his own songs signed "Narahari" or "Ghanashyama", mostly in Vrajabuli, and often put them in the mouths of the people
of Navadvipa while describing the holy places.*

*The signature alone does not tell whose a pada is. The index of poets in GPT2 divides the "Narahari" padas into three groups:
≈30 of Sarakara (taken from the journal Gauranga-madhuri, published in Shrikhanda), ≈171 of Chakravarti (those found in the
BR) and 112 of "Narahari Dasa", undistinguished. Majumdar accepts as Sarakara's only the padas preserved in PK and regards
padas known only from the GPT as unreliable; of the "Narahari" padas in the BR, by his analysis, only one belongs to Sarakara
(BR p. 924 = PK 2122, chapter 3, no. 1). Sarakara's marks, according to Majumdar, are a simple Bengali without Vrajabuli,
without heaped comparisons and alliterations, a correct metre, brevity; ornate Vrajabuli with chains of assonance is
Chakravarti's manner. But even the index groups are not beyond doubt: thus pada no. 128 of the section on Gaura's form stands
in the index on a page assigned to Sarakara, while in the BR it is put in the mouth of a woman of Nadia (below, no. 8).*

*Therefore each pada is marked in its heading: **"probably Sarakara"** — simple Bengali, absent from the BR, assigned by the
GPT2 index to Sarakara; **"probably Chakravarti"** — the pada is in the BR (usually the language too is Vrajabuli with
alliterations); **"not established"** — the arguments conflict or are lacking. In the lila database the padas "probably
Chakravarti" have authority B (the author is a recognized acharya, the author of the Bhakti-ratnakara; his authorship is established by his
works), the padas "probably Sarakara" and "not established" have authority C; no pada of the appendix has authority D (doubtful
authenticity). Chakravarti's padas are a late (18th-century) poetic elaboration of the lilas by a recognized acharya: not the testimony of an
eyewitness, but not a forgery either; they often follow the Chaitanya-bhagavata and the Chaitanya-charitamrita. Padas in nagari-bhava
(speech of townswomen in love with Gaura) are deferred to the
section of nagari padas; padas in which "Narahari" is merely mentioned among the associates while the signature is
another's are excluded.*
