*Chapter 17 is the first chapter of the appendix: three padas of mangalacharana (by the GPT2 index — Sarakara's), Gaura's form,
the abhisheka in Srivasa's house and arati, kirtana and dance in Navadvipa (a large cycle, almost all of it known also from
the BR), bhavavesha — the Lord in the mood of Shiva and in the mood of Krishna. The padas follow the order of the lilas. The
base text is GPT1 (tesseract recognition, doubtful places by the IA scan in.ernet.dli.2015.477854) collated with GPT2 and
the BR (eds. 1912 and 1960); variants are in the full version of the book. All the padas were also checked against Narahari Chakravarti's Gita-chandrodaya — none of them is there. The notes of the GPT editors are not reproduced.*

## 1. Narahari — "gaura-līlā daraśane icchā baṛa haya mane…" (GPT1 p. 11, no. 27)
*Mangalacharana: the poet, seeing Gaura-lila, wishes to write it down in his own tongue but does not know how; the one who will
write a book of it is not yet born; the lila of Gaura and Gadadhara, which melts stone, cannot be described even by Sarasvati
and Shiva — may at least the poet's few songs help someone to reveal the Lord's lila. Raga pahida. **Attribution: probably
Sarakara** — the GPT2 index assigns the pada to Sarakara; it is not in the BR; simple Bengali tripadi; the poet speaks as an
eyewitness, before books on Gaura had appeared.*[^17-1]

গৌরলীলা দরশনে ইচ্ছা বড় হয় মনে ভাষায় লিখিয়া সব রাখি ।
মুঞি ত অতি অধম লিখিতে না জানি ক্রম কেমন করিয়া তাহা লিখি ॥

*gauralīlā daraśane icchā baṛa haya mane bhāṣāya likhiyā saba rākhi |*
*muñi ta ati adhama likhite nā jāni krama kemana kariyā tāhā likhi ||*

*Word for word:* gaura-līlā daraśane — seeing Gaura's lila; icchā baṛa haya mane — a great wish arises in the heart; bhāṣāya — in the vernacular; likhiyā saba rākhi — to write down and keep it all; muñi ta ati adhama — but I am most lowly; likhite nā jāni krama — I do not know the order of writing; kemana kariyā tāhā likhi — how shall I write it

**1.1.** Seeing Gaura's lila, I greatly long in my heart to write it all down in our own tongue;
but I am most lowly, I do not know how to write in due order — how then shall I write it?[^17-2]

এ গ্রন্থ লিখিবে যে এখনো জন্মে নাই সে জন্মিতে বিলম্ব আছে বহু ।
ভাষায় রচনা হৈলে বুঝিবে লোক সকলে কবে বাঞ্ছা পূরাবেন পহু ॥

*e grantha likhibe ye ekhano janme nāi se janmite bilamba āche bahu |*
*bhāṣāya racanā haile bujhibe loka sakale kabe bāñchā pūrābena pahu ||*

*Word for word:* e grantha likhibe ye — he who will write this book; ekhano janme nāi se — he is not yet born; janmite bilamba āche bahu — there is long delay before his birth; bhāṣāya racanā haile — when it is composed in the vernacular; bujhibe loka sakale — all people will understand; kabe bāñchā pūrābena pahu — when will the Lord fulfil the wish

**1.2.** He who will write this book is not yet born — long yet is the delay before his birth;
when it is composed in our own tongue, all people will understand — when will the Lord fulfil my wish?[^17-3]

গৌর গদাধর-লীলা আদ্রব করয়ে শিলা কার সাধ্য করিবে বর্ণন ।
সারদা লিখেন যদি নিরন্তর নিরবধি আর সদাশিব পঞ্চানন ॥

*gaura gadādhara-līlā ādraba karaye śilā kāra sādhya karibe barṇana |*
*sāradā likhena yadi nirantara nirabadhi āra sadāśiba pañcānana ||*

*Word for word:* gaura gadādhara-līlā — the lila of Gaura and Gadadhara; ādraba karaye śilā — softens stone; kāra sādhya — who has the power; karibe barṇana — to describe; sāradā likhena yadi — if Sharada (Sarasvati) wrote; nirantara nirabadhi — ceaselessly, without end; āra sadāśiba pañcānana — and five-faced Sadashiva

**1.3.** The lila of Gaura and Gadadhara softens stone — who has the power to describe it?
Even if Sharada were to write ceaselessly, without end, and five-faced Sadashiva with her…[^17-4]

কিছু কিছু পদ লিখি যদি ইহা কেহ দেখি প্রকাশ করয়ে প্রভুলীলা ।
নরহরি পাবে সুখ ঘুচিবে মনের দুখ গ্রন্থ গানে দরবিবে শিলা ॥

*kichu kichu pada likhi yadi ihā keha dekhi prakāśa karaye prabhulīlā |*
*narahari pābe sukha ghucibe manera dukha grantha gāne darabibe śilā ||*

*Word for word:* kichu kichu pada likhi — the few songs I write; yadi ihā keha dekhi — if someone, seeing them; prakāśa karaye prabhu-līlā — reveals the Lord's lila; narahari pābe sukha — Narahari will find happiness; ghucibe manera dukha — the grief of the heart will go; grantha gāne — at the singing of the book; darabibe śilā — stones will melt

**1.4.** If, seeing the few songs I write, someone reveals to the world the Lord's lila —
Narahari will find happiness, the grief of his heart will go: at the singing of that book stones will melt.

## 2. Narahari Dasa — "braja-bhūma kari śūnya nadīyāya abatīrṇa…" (GPT1 pp. 11–12, no. 28)
*Mangalacharana: an address to Gaura, recognized as the Krishna of Vraja: having emptied Vraja, He has descended in Nadia; there
is no peacock feather, no yellow cloth, no flute, no curving pose — yet, since He has let Himself be seen, the mind will not be
deceived: this is that very Kanai of Vraja. Raga pahida. **Attribution: probably Sarakara** — GPT2 index (Sarakara); not in
the BR; simple Bengali tripadi.*[^17-5]

ব্রজভূম করি শূন্য নদীয়ায় অবতীর্ণ এতেক তোমার চতুরাল ।
দুঃখ দিয়া নিরন্তর বর্ণ করি ভাবান্তর পুনঃ বাঢ়াও বিরহ-জঞ্জাল ॥

*brajabhūma kari śūnya nadīyāya abatīrṇa eteka tomāra caturāla |*
*duḥkha diyā nirantara barṇa kari bhābāntara punaḥ bāṛhāo biraha-jañjāla ||*

*Word for word:* braja-bhūma kari śūnya — having emptied the land of Vraja; nadīyāya abatīrṇa — descended in Nadia; eteka tomāra caturāla — such is Your cunning; duḥkha diyā nirantara — giving ceaseless pain; barṇa kari bhābāntara — changing colour and bhava; punaḥ bāṛhāo — again You increase; biraha-jañjāla — the snares of separation

**2.1.** Having emptied the land of Vraja, You descended in Nadia — such is Your cunning!
Giving ceaseless pain, having changed colour and bhava, You again multiply the snares of separation.[^17-6]

নাহি শিখিপুচ্ছ-চূড়া নাই সেই পীতধড়া করে নাই সে মোহন বাঁশরি ।
যে বাঁশরি করি গান বধিলে গোপীর প্রাণ সে বাঁশরি কোথা গৌরহরি ॥

*nāhi śikhipuccha-cūṛā nāi sei pītadhaṛā kare nāi se mohana bām̐śari |*
*ye bām̐śari kari gāna badhile gopīra prāṇa se bām̐śari kothā gaurahari ||*

*Word for word:* nāhi śikhi-puccha-cūṛā — no crown of peacock feather; nāi sei pīta-dhaṛā — none of that yellow cloth; kare nāi se mohana bām̐śari — in the hand none of that enchanting flute; ye bām̐śari kari gāna — singing with which flute; badhile gopīra prāṇa — You slew the gopis' life; se bām̐śari kothā gaurahari — where is that flute, Gaurahari

**2.2.** There is no crown of peacock feather, none of that yellow cloth, in Your hand none of that enchanting flute —
that flute with whose song You stole the very life of the gopis: where is that flute, Gaurahari?

নাহি সে বাঁকা নয়ন এবে হেরি সুলোচন নাই সে ভঙ্গিমা বাঁকা নাই ।
যদি দিলে দরশন এ রূপে ভুলে না মন তুমি সেই ব্রজের কানাই ॥

*nāhi se bām̐kā nayana ebe heri sulocana nāi se bhaṅgimā bām̐kā nāi |*
*yadi dile daraśana e rūpe bhule nā mana tumi sei brajera kānāi ||*

*Word for word:* nāhi se bām̐kā nayana — none of those slanting eyes; ebe heri sulocana — now I see lovely eyes; nāi se bhaṅgimā — none of that curve (tribhanga); bām̐kā nāi — no bending; yadi dile daraśana — since You gave sight of Yourself; e rūpe bhule nā mana — the mind is not deceived by this form; tumi sei brajera kānāi — You are that Kanai of Vraja

**2.3.** None of those slanting eyes — now I see lovely eyes; none of that curve, none of that bending.
But since You have let Yourself be seen, the mind is not deceived by this form: You are that very Kanai of Vraja.[^17-7]

কহে নরহরি দাস যার নাই বিশ্বাস সে আসিয়া দেখুক নয়নে ।
সে দিনের যেই কথা বলিতে মরমে ব্যথা যে হইল উভয় মিলনে ॥

*kahe narahari dāsa yāra nāi biśvāsa se āsiyā dekhuka nayane |*
*se dinera yei kathā balite marame byathā ye haila ubhaya milane ||*

*Word for word:* kahe narahari dāsa — says Narahari Dasa; yāra nāi biśvāsa — who has no faith; se āsiyā dekhuka nayane — let him come and see with his eyes; se dinera yei kathā — what happened that day; balite marame byathā — to speak of it is pain in the heart; ye haila ubhaya milane — what took place at the meeting of the two

**2.4.** Says Narahari Dasa: whoever has no faith, let him come and see with his own eyes.
To speak of what happened that day at the meeting of the two is a pain in the heart.[^17-8]

## 3. Narahari — "rase tanu ḍharaḍhara gaura-kiśora-bara…" (GPT1 p. 12, no. 29)
*Mangalacharana: the Shyama of Dvapara is called Sri Krishna Chaitanya in Kali; within He is Shyama, without golden: to play with
Rai in the groves, out of love He became golden; the poet fears to speak of the hidden and cannot keep silent. Raga pahida.
**Attribution: probably Sarakara** — GPT2 index (Sarakara); not in the BR; simple Bengali tripadi.*[^17-9]

রসে তনু ঢরঢর গৌরকিশোরবর এবে নাম শ্রীকৃষ্ণচৈতন্য ।
সে সব নিগূঢ় কথা কহিতে অন্তরে ব্যথা ভক্তি বিনা নাহি জানে অন্য ॥

*rase tanu ḍharaḍhara gaurakiśorabara ebe nāma śrīkṛṣṇacaitanya |*
*se saba nigūṛha kathā kahite antare byathā bhakti binā nāhi jāne anya ||*

*Word for word:* rase tanu ḍharaḍhara — the body brimming with rasa; gaura-kiśora-bara — the best of youths, Gaura-kishora; ebe nāma śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya — now His name is Sri Krishna Chaitanya; se saba nigūṛha kathā — those hidden matters; kahite antare byathā — to tell them is pain in the heart; bhakti binā — without bhakti; nāhi jāne anya — no one else knows

**3.1.** His body brimming with rasa, the best of youths, Gaura-kishora — now His name is Sri Krishna Chaitanya.
To speak of these hidden things is a pain in the heart: without bhakti no one else will know them.

দ্বাপর যুগেতে শ্যাম কলিতে চৈতন্য নাম গর্গবাক্য ভাগবতে লিখি ।
চিতে করি অনুমান শ্যাম হৈল গৌরাঙ্গ রাধাকৃষ্ণ-তনু তার সাখী ॥

*dvāpara yugete śyāma kalite caitanya nāma gargabākya bhāgabate likhi |*
*cite kari anumāna śyāma haila gaurāṅga rādhākṛṣṇa-tanu tāra sākhī ||*

*Word for word:* dvāpara yugete śyāma — in the Dvapara age Shyama; kalite caitanya nāma — in Kali the name Chaitanya; garga-bākya bhāgabate likhi — Garga's words are written in the Bhagavata; cite kari anumāna — I ponder in my heart; śyāma haila gaurāṅga — Shyama became Gauranga; rādhā-kṛṣṇa-tanu — the body of Radha and Krishna; tāra sākhī — is witness to it

**3.2.** In the Dvapara age Shyama, in Kali the name Chaitanya — so are Garga's words written in the Bhagavata.
I ponder in my heart: Shyama has become Gauranga — the body of Radha and Krishna is its witness.[^17-10]

অন্তরেতে শ্যামতনু বাহিরে গৌরাঙ্গ তনু অদ্ভুত গৌরাঙ্গ-লীলা ।
রাই সঙ্গে খেলাইতে কুঞ্জবন বিলাসিতে অনুরাগে গৌরতনু হৈলা ॥

*antarete śyāmatanu bāhire gaurāṅga tanu adbhuta gaurāṅga-līlā |*
*rāi saṅge khelāite kuñjabana bilāsite anurāge gauratanu hailā ||*

*Word for word:* antarete śyāma-tanu — within the dark body; bāhire gaurāṅga tanu — without the golden body; adbhuta gaurāṅga-līlā — wondrous is Gauranga's lila; rāi saṅge khelāite — to play with Rai; kuñja-bana bilāsite — to enjoy the groves; anurāge — out of love; gaura-tanu hailā — became golden-bodied

**3.3.** Within, the dark body; without, the golden body — wondrous is Gauranga's lila!
To play with Rai, to enjoy the groves, out of love He took the golden body.[^17-11]

কহিবার কথা নয় কহিলে কি জানি হয় না কহিলে মনে বড় তাপ ।
মনে অনুমান করি গৌরাঙ্গ হৃদয়ে ধরি নরহরি করয়ে বিলাপ ॥

*kahibāra kathā naya kahile ki jāni haya nā kahile mane baṛa tāpa |*
*mane anumāna kari gaurāṅga hṛdaye dhari narahari karaye bilāpa ||*

*Word for word:* kahibāra kathā naya — it is not a thing to be told; kahile ki jāni haya — if told, who knows what may happen; nā kahile mane baṛa tāpa — if not told, great pain in the heart; mane anumāna kari — pondering in the mind; gaurāṅga hṛdaye dhari — holding Gauranga in the heart; narahari karaye bilāpa — Narahari laments

**3.4.** This is not a thing to be told — who knows what may come of telling it; yet not to tell is great pain in the heart.
Pondering in his mind, holding Gauranga in his heart, Narahari laments.

[^17-1]: GPT1 — p. 11, mangalacharana section, no. 27 (pahida), checked against the scan (PDF pp. 270–271); GPT2 — sec. 1.2, no. 27
(catalogue: NG-001). Not in PK, the BR, the Kshanada-gita-chintamani (KGC) or the Padamrita-samudra (PS). The index of poets of GPT2
assigns p. 8 (padas nos. 27–29) to Narahari Sarakara (from the journal Gauranga-madhuri); the language is simple Bengali tripadi
without Vrajabuli, which fits Majumdar's marks of Sarakara. But the pada is known only from the GPT; C.
[^17-2]: "In our own tongue" (bhāṣāya) — in Bengali, not in Sanskrit: the first books on the Lord (Murari Gupta, Kavi Karnapura) were
written in Sanskrit.
[^17-3]: If the pada is genuine, it was written in the Lord's lifetime or soon after, when there were as yet no Bengali books about
Gaura. Whom the poet awaits he does not say; Bengali poems on the Lord were written by Vrindavana Dasa (Chaitanya-bhagavata) and by
Lochana Dasa, a disciple of Narahari Sarakara, who calls him his Thakura (Chaitanya-mangala, Sutra-khanda, ch. 1, vv. 9, 61).
[^17-4]: Sharada — Sarasvati, goddess of speech; Sadashiva — Shiva, the five-faced (pañcānana). Gadadhara — Gadadhara Pandita, the
inseparable associate of the Lord (in Krishna-lila — Radha): "the lila of Gaura and Gadadhara" is a favourite theme of Narahari
Sarakara (cf. chapter 3, no. 1).
[^17-5]: GPT1 — pp. 11–12, no. 28 (pahida), checked against the scan (PDF p. 271); GPT2 — sec. 1.2, no. 28. The pada was not in the
catalogue (new row NG-236): the stage-1 catalogue missed it. Not in PK, BR, KGC, PS. GPT2 index — Sarakara (p. 8). C.
[^17-6]: "Having changed colour and bhava" (barṇa kari bhābāntara) — Krishna, who is dark, became golden, accepting the bhava of Radha
(CC Adi 1.5; ch. 4). The speaker is a resident of Vraja who has recognized Krishna in Gaura: "the snares of separation" are his
separation from Krishna, who has left Vraja for Nadia.
[^17-7]: "Curve" — tribhanga, the threefold bend of Krishna's body with the flute; "slanting eyes" — Krishna's sidelong glance. Kanai —
an endearing name of Krishna in Vraja. Cf. CC Madhya 8 (Ramananda Raya sees Krishna in the Lord).
[^17-8]: Who "the two" are the poet does not say; it is only clear that he speaks of a meeting in which the Lord revealed Himself as
Krishna to an associate who recognized Him.
[^17-9]: GPT1 — p. 12, no. 29 (pahida), checked against the scan (PDF p. 271); GPT2 — sec. 1.2, no. 29. The pada was not in the catalogue
(new row NG-237). Not in PK, BR, KGC, PS. GPT2 index — Sarakara (p. 8). C.
[^17-10]: Garga's words — Bhag. 10.8.13: in former ages Krishna had white, red and yellow colours, now He has become dark. The words "in
Kali the name Chaitanya" are not in Garga: this is the poet's interpretation; CC Adi 3.36–40 sees in the "yellow" (pīta) colour an
indication of the golden avatara of the Kali age. "The body of Radha and Krishna" — Gaura, Radha and Krishna united in one form
(CC Adi 1.5; 4.55–56).
[^17-11]: "Krishna within, Gaura without" — cf. Tattva-sandarbha, mangalacharana 2 (CC Adi 3.81). "Out of love" (anurāge) — Krishna,
wishing to taste Radha's love, took Her bhava and golden lustre (CC Adi 1.6; ch. 4); the golden colour is Her colour, not a
worldly passion.

## 4. Narahari — "nācata bhubana-mano-mohana…" (GPT1 p. 135, no. 70; BR)
*Gaura's form in the dance: His colour brighter than champaka, gold and lotus, His body in sandal paste and Chinese silk, His face
gentler than moons, His brows a row of bees, necklace and earrings swaying, curls scattering, His tendril-like hands playing,
His feet keeping the rhythm. Raga karnata. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave); Vrajabuli
with chains of comparisons.*[^17-12]

নাচত ভুবনমনোমোহন চম্পক কনক কঞ্জ জিনি বরণা ।
সুবলিত তনু মৃদু মলয়জ-রঞ্জিত পহিরণ চীন বসন ঘন কিরণা ॥

*nācata bhubanamanomohana campaka kanaka kañja jini baraṇā |*
*subalita tanu mṛdu malayaja-rañjita pahiraṇa cīna basana ghana kiraṇā ||*

*Word for word:* nācata — dances; bhubana-mano-mohana — the Enchanter of the minds of the world; campaka kanaka kañja jini baraṇā — whose colour surpasses champaka, gold and lotus; subalita tanu mṛdu — shapely tender body; malayaja-rañjita — anointed with sandal; pahiraṇa cīna basana — wearing Chinese silk; ghana kiraṇā — densely shining

**4.1.** He dances, the Enchanter of the minds of all the worlds — His colour surpassing champaka, gold and lotus;
His shapely, tender body anointed with sandal, He wears garments of Chinese silk, densely shining.

হিমকর-নিকর-নিন্দি মধুরানন হাসত মধুর সুধা যনু ঝরঈ ।
ভুরুযুগ ভৃঙ্গ-পাঁতি লস লোচন ডগমগ অরুণ-কিরণ-ভর হরঈ ॥

*himakara-nikara-nindi madhurānana hāsata madhura sudhā yanu jharaī |*
*bhuruyuga bhṛṅga-pām̐ti lasa locana ḍagamaga aruṇa-kiraṇa-bhara haraī ||*

*Word for word:* himakara-nikara-nindi — putting to shame hosts of moons; madhurānana — sweet face; hāsata madhura — smiles sweetly; sudhā yanu jharaī — as if nectar flows; bhuru-yuga bhṛṅga-pām̐ti — the brows a row of bees; lasa locana — the eyes shine; ḍagamaga — swaying; aruṇa-kiraṇa-bhara haraī — rob the dawn's rays of their weight

**4.2.** His sweet face puts to shame hosts of moons; sweetly He smiles — as if nectar were flowing;
His brows a row of bees; His eyes gleam and sway, robbing the dawn's rays of their power.[^17-13]

দোলত মণিময় হার হরত ধৃতি টলমল কুণ্ডল ঝলকত শ্রবণে ।
চাঁচর চিকুর-ভঙ্গি-ভার-ভরে বিলুলিত হালত তিমির-তার যনু পবনে ॥

*dolata maṇimaya hāra harata dhṛti ṭalamala kuṇḍala jhalakata śrabaṇe |*
*cām̐cara cikura-bhaṅgi-bhāra-bhare bilulita hālata timira-tāra yanu pabane ||*

*Word for word:* dolata maṇimaya hāra — the jewelled necklace sways; harata dhṛti — stealing composure; ṭalamala kuṇḍala — earrings tremble; jhalakata śrabaṇe — flashing at the ears; cām̐cara cikura-bhaṅgi-bhāra-bhare — under the weight of the curling locks; bilulita hālata — scattered, they sway; timira-tāra yanu pabane — like strands of darkness in the wind

**4.3.** The jewelled necklace sways, stealing all composure; the earrings tremble, flashing at His ears;
His curling locks, under their own weight, scatter and sway like strands of darkness in the wind.

অভিনয় ললিত কলিত কর-কিশলয়ে কত শত তাল ধরত পগ ধরণে ।
নরহরি পরম উলস যশ গায়ত শোভা বিপুল কৌনক বিবরণে ॥

*abhinaya lalita kalita kara-kiśalaye kata śata tāla dharata paga dharaṇe |*
*narahari parama ulasa yaśa gāyata śobhā bipula kaunaka bibaraṇe ||*

*Word for word:* abhinaya lalita — graceful play; kalita kara-kiśalaye — performed with tendril-like hands; kata śata tāla dharata — keeps hundreds of rhythms; paga dharaṇe — in placing His feet; narahari parama ulasa — Narahari in great delight; yaśa gāyata — sings the glory; śobhā bipula — the boundless beauty; kaunaka bibaraṇe — who can describe

**4.4.** In graceful play of His tendril-like hands, stepping on the earth, He keeps hundreds of rhythms;
Narahari, in great delight, sings His glory: who can describe this boundless beauty?

## 5. Narahari — "nadīyāra mājhāre nācaye gorācām̐da…" (GPT1 p. 135, no. 72; BR)
*Gaura's form, from face to feet: Gorachand dancing in the midst of Nadia is a snare for every heart; seeing Him, the young
wives lose their senses; His face is the autumn moon, His speech nectar, His eyes the abode of love, His brows shame Kama's bow,
His curls are twined with malati, on His brow a drop of sandal; garland, long arms, slender waist, feet before whose nails Kama
swoons — this is the Nagara of Gokula, the ocean of rasa. Raga kamoda. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the
BR (12th wave, among the songs of the people of Nadia).*[^17-14]

নদীয়ার মাঝারে নাচয়ে গোরাচাঁদ ।
অখিল জনার মন বান্ধিবার ফাঁদ ॥

*nadīyāra mājhāre nācaye gorācām̐da |*
*akhila janāra mana bāndhibāra phām̐da ||*

*Word for word:* nadīyāra mājhāre — in the midst of Nadia; nācaye gorācām̐da — Gorachand dances; akhila janāra mana — the hearts of all people; bāndhibāra phām̐da — a snare to bind

**5.1.** In the midst of Nadia dances Gorachand —
a snare to capture the hearts of all people.

কনক কেশর তনু অনুপম ছটা ।
দেখিতে মোহিত নব যুবতীর ঘটা ॥

*kanaka keśara tanu anupama chaṭā |*
*dekhite mohita naba yubatīra ghaṭā ||*

*Word for word:* kanaka keśara tanu — body like golden filaments; anupama chaṭā — peerless radiance; dekhite mohita — seeing Him are bewitched; naba yubatīra ghaṭā — crowds of young wives

**5.2.** His body like golden filaments, His radiance beyond compare;
seeing Him, crowds of young wives lose their senses.[^17-15]

শরদের চাঁদ কি মধুর মুখখানি ।
অমিয়ার ধারা বাণী তাপিয়া জুড়ানি ॥

*śaradera cām̐da ki madhura mukhakhāni |*
*amiyāra dhārā bāṇī tāpiyā juṛāni ||*

*Word for word:* śaradera cām̐da — the autumn moon; ki madhura mukha-khāni — how sweet the face; amiyāra dhārā bāṇī — speech a stream of nectar; tāpiyā juṛāni — cooling the afflicted

**5.3.** How sweet His face — the autumn moon!
His speech a stream of nectar, cooling the afflicted.

ঈষৎ মিশাল হাসি অধর উজ্জ্বল ।
দশন মুকুতাপাঁতি করে ঝলমল ॥

*īṣat miśāla hāsi adhara ujjvala |*
*daśana mukutāpām̐ti kare jhalamala ||*

*Word for word:* īṣat miśāla hāsi — mingled slightly with a smile; adhara ujjvala — the lips shine; daśana mukutā-pām̐ti — the teeth a row of pearls; kare jhalamala — flash

**5.4.** Slightly mingled with a smile, His lips shine;
the pearl-row of His teeth flashes.

নয়নযুগল অনুরাগের আলয় ।
চাহনিতে ভুবন-পরাণ হরি লয় ॥

*nayanayugala anurāgera ālaya |*
*cāhanite bhubana-parāṇa hari laya ||*

*Word for word:* nayana-yugala — the pair of eyes; anurāgera ālaya — abode of love; cāhanite — with a glance; bhubana-parāṇa — the life of the world; hari laya — steals away

**5.5.** His eyes are the abode of love;
with a glance He steals the life of the whole world.

কামের ধনুক-মদ ভাঙ্গিবার তরে ।
কেবা গঢ়াইল ভুরু কত রঙ্গ ধরে ॥

*kāmera dhanuka-mada bhāṅgibāra tare |*
*kebā gaṛhāila bhuru kata raṅga dhare ||*

*Word for word:* kāmera dhanuka-mada — the pride of Kama's bow; bhāṅgibāra tare — in order to break; kebā gaṛhāila bhuru — who fashioned the brows; kata raṅga dhare — so full of play

**5.6.** Who carved these brows — so full of play —
to break the pride of Kama's bow?

চাঁচর কেশের ঝুঁটা চমকিয়া বাঁকে ।
মালতী-বলিত অলি ফিরে ঝাঁকে ঝাঁকে ॥

*cām̐cara keśera jhum̐ṭā camakiyā bām̐ke |*
*mālatī-balita ali phire jhām̐ke jhām̐ke ||*

*Word for word:* cām̐cara keśera jhum̐ṭā — the knot of curling hair; camakiyā bām̐ke — flashing, bends aside; mālatī-balita — twined with malati; ali phire jhām̐ke jhām̐ke — bees circle in swarms

**5.7.** The knot of His curling hair, flashing, is bent aside;
around the malati twined in it, swarms of bees are circling.

কে ধরে ধৈরজ হেরি সুচারু কপাল ।
চন্দনের বিন্দু ইন্দু-গরবের কাল ॥

*ke dhare dhairaja heri sucāru kapāla |*
*candanera bindu indu-garabera kāla ||*

*Word for word:* ke dhare dhairaja — who keeps composure; heri sucāru kapāla — seeing the lovely brow; candanera bindu — the drop of sandal; indu-garabera kāla — death to the moon's pride

**5.8.** Who can keep composure, seeing that lovely brow?
The drop of sandal on it is death to the moon's pride.

ভুবনবিজয়ী মালা দোলয়ে হিয়ায় ।
বারেক নিরখি আঁখি সদাই ধিয়ায় ॥

*bhubanabijayī mālā dolaye hiyāya |*
*bāreka nirakhi ām̐khi sadāi dhiyāya ||*

*Word for word:* bhubana-bijayī mālā — the world-conquering garland; dolaye hiyāya — sways on the breast; bāreka nirakhi ām̐khi — the eye that has seen it once; sadāi dhiyāya — ever meditates on it

**5.9.** On His breast sways the garland that has conquered the world;
whoever has seen it once keeps his eyes on it and remembers it ever.

কিবা সে দীঘল ভুজযুগের বলনী ।
কত ভাতি ভঙ্গী সতীকুলের দলনী ॥

*kibā se dīghala bhujayugera balanī |*
*kata bhāti bhaṅgī satīkulera dalanī ||*

*Word for word:* kibā se dīghala bhuja-yugera balanī — how graceful the curve of the long arms; kata bhāti bhaṅgī — how many movements; satī-kulera dalanī — crushing (the steadfastness of) the chaste

**5.10.** How graceful the curve of His long arms!
How many movements in them — crushing the steadfastness of the chaste.

সরুয়া কাঁকালি কিবা মুঠেতে লুকায় ।
বিনি মূলে কিনে মন নয়ন জুড়ায় ॥

*saruyā kām̐kāli kibā muṭhete lukāya |*
*bini mūle kine mana nayana juṛāya ||*

*Word for word:* saruyā kām̐kāli — slender waist; kibā muṭhete lukāya — would hide in a fist; bini mūle kine mana — buys hearts without price; nayana juṛāya — refreshes the eyes

**5.11.** His slender waist — it would hide within a fist;
without price He buys hearts and refreshes the eyes.

চরণ-কমলতল অতি অনুপাম ।
নখর-নিকরে কত মূরছয়ে কাম ॥

*caraṇa-kamalatala ati anupāma |*
*nakhara-nikare kata mūrachaye kāma ||*

*Word for word:* caraṇa-kamala-tala — the soles of the lotus feet; ati anupāma — beyond compare; nakhara-nikare — before the host of nails; kata mūrachaye kāma — many a Kama swoons

**5.12.** The soles of His lotus feet are beyond compare;
before the radiance of His nails many a Kama swoons.[^17-16]

কহে নরহরি কি না জানে রঙ্গ তার ।
গোকুলনাগর ও রসের পাথার ॥

*kahe narahari ki nā jāne raṅga tāra |*
*gokulanāgara o rasera pāthāra ||*

*Word for word:* kahe narahari — says Narahari; ki nā jāne raṅga tāra — what play of His does He not know; gokula-nāgara — the Nagara of Gokula; o rasera pāthāra — that ocean of rasa

**5.13.** Says Narahari: what play does He not know! —
the Nagara of Gokula, that ocean of rasa.[^17-17]

## 6. Narahari — "suradhunī-tīre gaura naṭa-nāgara…" (GPT1 p. 136, no. 73; BR)
*Gaura's dance on the bank of the Suradhuni: Gaura, the graceful dancer, sports with His associates, captivating the eyes of the world;
His body outshines a golden mountain, His arms put to shame an elephant's trunk, again and again He cries "Hari, Hari!"; seeing
Gadadhara, He sheds tears like a cloud of the month of Shravana, and the earth trembles beneath His feet. Raga somaraga.
**Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave); Vrajabuli.*[^17-18]

সুরধুনীতীরে গৌর নটনাগর পরিকর সঙ্গে রঙ্গে বিহরে ।
নিরুপম বিবিধ নৃত্য নব মাধুরী নিখিল ভুবনজন-নয়ন হরে ॥

*suradhunītīre gaura naṭanāgara parikara saṅge raṅge bihare |*
*nirupama bibidha nṛtya naba mādhurī nikhila bhubanajana-nayana hare ||*

*Word for word:* suradhunī-tīre — on the bank of the Suradhuni (Ganga); gaura naṭa-nāgara — Gaura the graceful dancer; parikara saṅge raṅge bihare — sports with the associates; nirupama bibidha nṛtya — peerless varied dance; naba mādhurī — ever-new sweetness; nikhila bhubana-jana-nayana hare — steals the eyes of all the people of the world

**6.1.** On the bank of the Suradhuni, Gaura, the graceful dancer, sports together with His associates;
the peerless, many-sided dance, ever-new sweetness — steals the eyes of all the people of the world.

কনক-ধরাধর-গরবহারী তনু ঝলমল বিপুল পুলকনিকরে ।
কুঞ্জর-কর-মদ-হর ভুজ-ভঙ্গিম নিন্দই কত শত কুসুমশরে ॥

*kanaka-dharādhara-garabahārī tanu jhalamala bipula pulakanikare |*
*kuñjara-kara-mada-hara bhuja-bhaṅgima nindai kata śata kusumaśare ||*

*Word for word:* kanaka-dharādhara-garaba-hārī tanu — the body robbing a golden mountain of its pride; jhalamala — shines; bipula pulaka-nikare — with abundant thrills; kuñjara-kara-mada-hara — humbling an elephant's trunk; bhuja-bhaṅgima — the curve of the arms; nindaī kata śata kusumaśare — puts to shame hundreds of Kamas

**6.2.** His body, robbing a golden mountain of its pride, shines with abundant thrills;
the curve of His arms, which surpass an elephant's trunk, puts to shame hundreds of Kamas.[^17-19]

কুন্দ-দশন-দ্যুতি দমকত মঞ্জুল মিলিত সুহাস মধুর অধরে ।
ডগমগ বদন বদত ঘন হরি হরি শুনইতে কো আছু ধৈরজ ধরে ॥

*kunda-daśana-dyuti damakata mañjula milita suhāsa madhura adhare |*
*ḍagamaga badana badata ghana hari hari śunaite ko āchu dhairaja dhare ||*

*Word for word:* kunda-daśana-dyuti — the lustre of the kunda-like teeth; damakata mañjula — flashes lovely; milita suhāsa madhura adhare — in a soft smile on the sweet lips; ḍagamaga badana — the face sways; badata ghana hari hari — says ceaselessly "Hari, Hari"; śunaite ko āchu dhairaja dhare — who, hearing it, keeps composure

**6.3.** His teeth flash, lovely — the lustre of kunda flowers — in a soft smile on His sweet lips;
His face sways, His lips cry ceaselessly "Hari, Hari!" — who, hearing it, can keep composure?

উমড়ই হৃদয় গদাধরে হেরইতে শাঙন-ঘন সম নয়ন ঝরে ।
নরহরি ভণত ধরণী করু টলমল সুললিত চঞ্চল চরণ-ভরে ॥

*umaṛai hṛdaya gadādhare heraite śāṅana-ghana sama nayana jhare |*
*narahari bhaṇata dharaṇī karu ṭalamala sulalita cañcala caraṇa-bhare ||*

*Word for word:* umaḍaī hṛdaya — the heart overflows; gadādhare heraite — on seeing Gadadhara; śām̐ṅana-ghana sama — like a cloud of Shravana; nayana jhare — the eyes pour; narahari bhaṇata — says Narahari; dharaṇī karu ṭalamala — the earth trembles; sulalita cañcala caraṇa-bhare — under the weight of the lovely restless feet

**6.4.** His heart overflows when He sees Gadadhara: His eyes pour tears like a cloud in the month of Shravana;
says Narahari: the earth trembles under the weight of His lovely, light feet.[^17-20]

## 7. Narahari — "biharata surasarita-tīra…" (GPT1 pp. 151–152, no. 119; BR)
*Gaura's form on the bank of the Ganga, from face to feet: youthful, He sports by the river; His colour outshines lightning, gold
and kunkuma, His face is a snare for the eyes of young wives, His curls dark clouds, His brows serpents; broad chest, slender
waist, lotus feet about which bee-devotees hover; a cloud of mercy, He ever showers the nectar of prema — only foolish Narahari it
does not touch. Raga nataraga. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave); Vrajabuli with strings of
comparisons.*[^17-21]

বিহরত সুরসরিত-তীর গৌর তরুণ বয়স থির তড়িত-কনক-কুঙ্কুম-মদ-মর্দন তনুকাঁতি ।
মদন-কদন বদনচন্দ্র নিখিল-তরুণী-নয়ান-ফন্দ হসত লসত দশনবৃন্দ কুন্দকুসুমপাঁতি ॥

*biharata surasarita-tīra gaura taruṇa bayasa thira taṛita-kanaka-kuṅkuma-mada-mardana tanukām̐ti |*
*madana-kadana badanacandra nikhila-taruṇī-nayāna-phanda hasata lasata daśanabṛnda kundakusumapām̐ti ||*

*Word for word:* biharata surasarita-tīra — strolls by the bank of the heavenly river; gaura taruṇa bayasa thira — Gaura, young, of unchanging youth; taṛita-kanaka-kuṅkuma-mada-mardana — crushing the pride of lightning, gold and kunkuma; tanu-kām̐ti — the lustre of the body; madana-kadana badana-candra — the moon-face tormenting Madana; nikhila-taruṇī-nayāna-phanda — a snare for the eyes of all young wives; hasata lasata daśana-bṛnda — smiling, the teeth gleam; kunda-kusuma-pām̐ti — a row of kunda flowers

**7.1.** By the bank of the heavenly river strolls Gaura — young, in unchanging youth: the lustre of His body crushes the pride of
lightning, gold and kunkuma; His moon-face torments Madana, a snare for the eyes of all young wives; in His smile His teeth gleam —
a row of kunda flowers.

অঞ্জন-ঘন-পুঞ্জ-বরণ কুঞ্চিত কচ ধৈরজ-হরণ বেশ বিমল অলকাকুল রাজত অনুপাম ।
ভাল-তিলক ঝলকত অতি ভাঙ-ভুজগ মঞ্জুল গতি চঞ্চল দিঠে অঞ্চল রসরঞ্জিত ছবিধাম ॥

*añjana-ghana-puñja-baraṇa kuñcita kaca dhairaja-haraṇa beśa bimala alakākula rājata anupāma |*
*bhāla-tilaka jhalakata ati bhāṅa-bhujaga mañjula gati cañcala diṭhe añcala rasarañjita chabidhāma ||*

*Word for word:* añjana-ghana-puñja-baraṇa — the colour of dense collyrium; kuñcita kaca — curling locks; dhairaja-haraṇa — stealing composure; beśa bimala — pure attire; alakākula rājata anupāma — the scattered tresses shine peerless; bhāla-tilaka jhalakata ati — the tilaka on the brow flashes brightly; bhām̐ṅa-bhujaga mañjula gati — the brows, serpents of graceful motion; cañcala diṭhe añcala — the corners of the restless eyes; rasa-rañjita chabidhāma — tinged with rasa, an abode of beauty

**7.2.** The colour of dense collyrium, His curling locks steal composure; peerless shine His pure attire and scattered tresses;
the tilaka on His brow flashes brightly, His brows are gracefully gliding serpents; the corners of His restless eyes, tinged with
rasa, are an abode of beauty.[^17-22]

কুণ্ডল শ্রুতি গণ্ড কলিত কণ্ঠহি বনমাল বলিত বাহু বিপুল বলয়া কর কোমল বলিহারি ।
পরিসর বর বক্ষ অতুল নাশত কত কুলবধূকুল ললিত কটি সুকৃশ কেশরী-গরব-খরবকারী ॥

*kuṇḍala śruti gaṇḍa kalita kaṇṭhahi banamāla balita bāhu bipula balayā kara komala balihāri |*
*parisara bara bakṣa atula nāśata kata kulabadhūkula lalita kaṭi sukṛśa keśarī-garaba-kharabakārī ||*

*Word for word:* kuṇḍala śruti gaṇḍa kalita — the earrings at the ears touch the cheeks; kaṇṭhahi banamāla balita — on the neck the forest garland; bāhu bipula — long arms; balayā kara komala — bracelets, tender palms; balihāri — I give my life for them; parisara bara bakṣa atula — broad, peerless chest; nāśata kata kulabadhū-kula — destroys (the steadfastness of) many noble wives; lalita kaṭi sukṛśa — graceful slender waist; keśarī-garaba-kharabakārī — humbling the pride of the lion

**7.3.** Earrings touch His cheeks, on His neck the forest garland; long arms, bracelets, tender palms — I give my life for them!
His broad, peerless chest destroys the steadfastness of many a noble wife; His graceful, slender waist humbles the pride of the
lion.

ডগমগ ভুজ জানু তরুণ অরুণাবলী কিরণ চরণ কমল মধুর সৌরভভরে ভকত-ভ্রমর ভোর ।
করুণা-ঘন ভুবনবিদিত প্রেম অমিয়া বরষত নিত নরহরি মতিমন্দ কবহুঁ পরশত নাহি থোর ॥

*ḍagamaga bhuja jānu taruṇa aruṇābalī kiraṇa caraṇa kamala madhura saurabhabhare bhakata-bhramara bhora |*
*karuṇā-ghana bhubanabidita prema amiyā baraṣata nita narahari matimanda kabahum̐ paraśata nāhi thora ||*

*Word for word:* ḍagamaga bhuja — swaying arms; jānu taruṇa — youthful knees; aruṇābalī kiraṇa caraṇa — the feet rays of the red dawn; kamala madhura saurabha-bhare — by the sweet fragrance of the lotuses; bhakata-bhramara bhora — the bee-devotees are intoxicated; karuṇā-ghana — cloud of mercy; bhubana-bidita — famed in the world; prema amiyā baraṣata nita — ever showers the nectar of prema; narahari matimanda — foolish Narahari; kabahum̐ paraśata nāhi thora — is never touched even a little

**7.4.** His arms sway, His knees are youthful; His feet are rays of the red dawn; to the sweet fragrance of these lotuses cling the
bee-devotees, intoxicated; a cloud of mercy, famed in the world, He ever showers the nectar of prema — only foolish Narahari is not
touched by a single drop.[^17-23]

## 8. Narahari — "ki jāni ki bhābe bhābita antara…" (GPT1 p. 154, no. 128; BR)
*Gaura's form with Gadadhara: absorbed in an unknown bhava, His eyes reddened, He holds Gadadhara's hand and says something — as
if honeyed; His lips a bandhuli flower, His teeth lightning, His smile pours nectar; He dances in the guise of a nagara, the thief
of the hearts of the women of Nadia — this is Gora, the Enchanter of Gokula. Raga vallari. **Attribution: not established
(more likely Chakravarti)** — the GPT2 index assigns the page to Sarakara, but the pada is in the BR, where it is sung by a woman
of Nadia.*[^17-24]

কি জানি কি ভাবে ভাবিত অন্তর অরুণ যুগল আঁখি ।
গদাধর-করে ধরি কি কহয়ে না জানি কি মধু মাখি ॥

*ki jāni ki bhābe bhābita antara aruṇa yugala ām̐khi |*
*gadādhara-kare dhari ki kahaye nā jāni ki madhu mākhi ||*

*Word for word:* ki jāni ki bhābe — who knows by what bhava; bhābita antara — the heart is absorbed; aruṇa yugala ām̐khi — both eyes are red; gadādhara-kare dhari — holding Gadadhara's hand; ki kahaye nā jāni — what He says I do not know; ki madhu mākhi — as if steeped in honey

**8.1.** Who knows by what bhava His heart is seized — both eyes are reddened;
holding Gadadhara's hand, what He says I do not know — as if steeped in honey.[^17-25]

অধর বান্ধুলি ফুল সুললিত দামিনী দশন-ছটা ।
হাসির মিশালে ঢালে সুধারাশি বদনচাঁদের ঘটা ॥

*adhara bāndhuli phula sulalita dāminī daśana-chaṭā |*
*hāsira miśāle ḍhāle sudhārāśi badanacām̐dera ghaṭā ||*

*Word for word:* adhara bāndhuli phula sulalita — the lips a tender bandhuli flower; dāminī daśana-chaṭā — the teeth a flash of lightning; hāsira miśāle — mingled with the smile; ḍhāle sudhā-rāśi — pours a sea of nectar; badana-cām̐dera ghaṭā — the splendour of the moon-face

**8.2.** His lips a tender bandhuli flower, His teeth a flash of lightning;
mingled with His smile pours a sea of nectar — the splendour of His moon-face.

নাগরালি-কাচে নাচয়ে নদীয়া-নাগরী-পরাণ-চোরা ।
নরহরি কহে তুমি কি না জান গোকুলমোহন গোরা ॥

*nāgarāli-kāce nācaye nadīyā-nāgarī-parāṇa-corā |*
*narahari kahe tumi ki nā jāna gokulamohana gorā ||*

*Word for word:* nāgarāli-kāce — in the guise of a nagara; nācaye — dances; nadīyā-nāgarī-parāṇa-corā — the thief of the hearts of Nadia's women; narahari kahe — says Narahari; tumi ki nā jāna — do you not know; gokula-mohana gorā — Gora is the Enchanter of Gokula

**8.3.** In the guise of a nagara dances the Thief of the hearts of Nadia's women;
says Narahari: do you not know? Gora is the Enchanter of Gokula.[^17-26]

[^17-12]: GPT1 — p. 135, section on Gaura's form (3.1), no. 70 (karnata); GPT2 — sec. 3.1, no. 70. The pada was not in the catalogue (new
row NG-238). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, pp. 835–836; ed. 1960, vv. 1861–1864), right after a pada signed "Ghanashyama" and before the
pada "nācata gaura puruba rase bhora" (below, no. 13). Not in PK, KGC, PS. The GPT2 index assigns p. 92 to Chakravarti. B.
[^17-13]: "Robbing the dawn's rays of their power" (aruṇa-kiraṇa-bhara haraī) — the eyes, reddened by prema, outshine the dawn.
[^17-14]: GPT1 — p. 135, no. 72 (kamoda); GPT2 — sec. 3.1, no. 72 (catalogue: NG-072). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 907; ed. 1960,
vv. 2830–2842), among the songs which Narahari Chakravarti puts in the mouths of the people of Nadia remembering the Lord. Not in PK,
KGC, PS. B.
[^17-15]: "The young wives lose their senses" (5.2), "crushing the steadfastness of the chaste" (5.10), "the Nagara of Gokula" (5.13) —
the motif of the townswomen captivated by Gaura's beauty: the language of nagari-bhava (Gaura as nagara); in the BR the pada is in
fact put in the mouth of a woman of Nadia. We translate faithfully to the author. Vrindavana Dasa stresses that in this incarnation
the Lord never looked at another man's wife; worship of Gaura in the spirit of "gaura-nagari" is not accepted by the Gaudiya
tradition (Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja, Bhaktisiddhanta). The attraction here is an image of the all-attractiveness of
Bhagavan, not of a worldly feeling.
[^17-16]: Description "from face to feet" (nakha-shikha) is the usual genre for describing Krishna's form; "many a Kama" — Gaura is more
beautiful than countless gods of love (cf. Bhag. 10.32.2: Krishna is "the enchanter of Manmatha himself").
[^17-17]: "The Nagara of Gokula" — Krishna, the beloved of the gopis of Gokula: the poet recognizes Krishna in Gaura. "What play does
He not know" — the Lord is expert in every lila.
[^17-18]: GPT1 — p. 136, no. 73 (somaraga); GPT2 — sec. 3.1, no. 73. In the catalogue it stood as a pada of Nayanananda (NN-006; chapter
10 excluded it: the signature is "narahari bhaṇata"); here a new row NG-239. BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 911; ed. 1960, vv. 2881–2884):
Ishana shows Srinivasa the place on the bank of the Ganga where the Lord danced, and this song is cited. Not in PK, KGC, PS. B.
[^17-19]: "Natanagara" (naṭanāgara) — "skilled, graceful dancer": an epithet, not a motif of nagari-bhava. Kama (Kusumashara — "He whose
arrows are flowers") — the god of love: the Lord's beauty is above Kama's.
[^17-20]: Gadadhara Pandita is Radha in Krishna-lila (Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika 147–153): at the sight of him Krishna's love for Radha awakens
in the Lord. Shravana — a month of the rainy season (July–August).
[^17-21]: GPT1 — pp. 151–152, section on Gaura's form, no. 119 (nataraga); GPT2 — sec. 3.1, no. 119. In the catalogue this pada stood by
mistake under the first line of the preceding one, no. 118 (NG-073 "āhā mari gorā-rūpera ki diba tulanā" — signed by Vasu, "bāsu
kahe"); the first line is corrected. BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 890; ed. 1960, vv. 2630–2633). The GPT2 index assigns p. 103 to
Chakravarti. Not in PK, KGC, PS. B.
[^17-22]: "Brows — serpents" (bhāṅa-bhujaga) — the thin, curving brows are likened to gliding snakes; "abode of beauty" (chabidhāma).
[^17-23]: "Destroys the steadfastness of many a noble wife" (7.3) — the same motif of the townswomen as in no. 5 (see note 15). The last
words differ among the witnesses (GPT1 "mati mandakababha", GPT2 "mati manda karaha", BR "mati mandaka bahu"); the sense is "only foolish
Narahari is not touched (by the nectar) at all": the poet's usual self-abasement.
[^17-24]: GPT1 — p. 154, no. 128 (vallari); GPT2 — sec. 3.1, no. 128 (catalogue: NG-074). The GPT2 index assigns p. 104 to Sarakara (this
page has two padas signed Narahari — nos. 128 and 129); but no. 128 is in the BR (12th wave; ed. 1912, p. 909; ed. 1960, vv.
2858–2861): Chakravarti cites it as the song of a certain woman of Nadia ("kācit — ballarī") and opens it with an address to a friend:
"Friend! What a wondrous form! The body thrilled, peerless — like a new king Madana." The two attributions conflict; by the BR,
Chakravarti is more likely. Not in PK, KGC, PS. C. The neighbouring no. 129 (address to women friends, the wish "to keep Him in the
heart") is nagari-bhava and is deferred.
[^17-25]: Gadadhara — see note 20. Cf. PK 2122 of Narahari Sarakara (chapter 3, no. 1): the Lord in the mood of Krishna embraces Gadadhara.
[^17-26]: "Nagara, the thief of the hearts of Nadia's women" — the motif of the townswomen (see note 15). The address "do you not know"
is to the listeners; in the BR, to the speaker's friend.

## 9. Narahari — "āju abhiṣeka sukhera abadhi…" (GPT1 pp. 241–242, no. 14; BR)
*The abhisheka in Srivasa's house: Gaura, the treasury of virtues, sits on the throne; His curls stream down His back like the
Yamuna down a golden mountain; Nityananda and Advaita recite the abhisheka mantras, Srivasa and others pour fragrant water from
pitchers on the Lord's head; Jagadisha, Vasudeva, Narayana, Mukunda, Madhava sing, Govinda and Govindananda play the mridanga,
Vakreshvara dances; the invisible gods shower flowers, the devoted wives cry "Jaya!". Raga suhai or mayura. **Attribution:
probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave, account of the abhisheka).*[^17-27]

আজু অভিষেক সুখের অবধি বৈসে সিংহাসনে গোরা গুণনিধি
নিরুপম শোভা ভঙ্গিমাতে কেউ ধৈরজ না ধরে ধরণীতলে ।

*āju abhiṣeka sukhera abadhi baise siṃhāsane gorā guṇanidhi*
*nirupama śobhā bhaṅgimāte keu dhairaja nā dhare dharaṇītale |*

*Word for word:* āju abhiṣeka — today the abhisheka; sukhera abadhi — the limit of happiness; baise siṃhāsane — sits on the throne; gorā guṇa-nidhi — Gora, treasury of virtues; nirupama śobhā bhaṅgimāte — in the peerless beauty of His bearing; keu dhairaja nā dhare — no one keeps composure; dharaṇī-tale — on earth

**9.1.** Today is the abhisheka — the very limit of happiness: on the throne sits Gora, the treasury of virtues;
peerless is the beauty of His bearing — no one on earth can keep composure.

চিকণ চাঁচর কেশ শিরে শোহে লোটায়ে এ পীঠে ছটা মন মোহে
হেম-ধরাধর-শিখরেতে যেন যমুনা-প্রবাহ বহয়ে ভালে ॥

*cikaṇa cām̐cara keśa śire śohe loṭāye e pīṭhe chaṭā mana mohe*
*hema-dharādhara-śikharete yena yamunā-prabāha bahaye bhāle ||*

*Word for word:* cikaṇa cām̐cara keśa — smooth curling locks; śire śohe — adorn the head; loṭāye e pīṭhe — stream down the back; chaṭā mana mohe — the lustre charms the mind; hema-dharādhara-śikharete yena — as if on the peak of a golden mountain; yamunā-prabāha bahaye bhāle — the stream of the Yamuna flows

**9.2.** Smooth curling locks adorn His head and stream down His back — their lustre charms the mind,
as if on the peak of a golden mountain the stream of the Yamuna were flowing.[^17-28]

নিরমল অঙ্গ ঝলমল করে কত শত মনমথ-মদ হরে
কেবা না বিভোল হয় হাসিমাখা মুখশশী-পানে বারেক চাঞা ।

*niramala aṅga jhalamala kare kata śata manamatha-mada hare*
*kebā nā bibhola haya hāsimākhā mukhaśaśī-pāne bāreka cāñā |*

*Word for word:* niramala aṅga — the pure body; jhalamala kare — shines; kata śata manamatha-mada hare — robs hundreds of Kamas of their pride; kebā nā bibhola haya — who would not be overwhelmed; hāsi-mākhā mukha-śaśī-pāne — at the moon-face steeped in smiles; bāreka cāñā — glancing once

**9.3.** His pure body shines, robbing hundreds of Kamas of their pride;
who would not lose himself, glancing but once at His moon-face steeped in smiles?

অভিষেক-মন্ত্র পড়ি বারে বারে নিত্যানন্দাদ্বৈত উল্লাস অন্তরে
শ্রীবাসাদি পহুঁ-শিরে সুবাসিত জল ঢালে করে কলসি লৈয়া ॥

*abhiṣeka-mantra paṛi bāre bāre nityānandādvaita ullāsa antare*
*śrībāsādi pahum̐-śire subāsita jala ḍhāle kare kalasi laiyā ||*

*Word for word:* abhiṣeka-mantra paṛi bāre bāre — reciting the abhisheka mantras again and again; nityānanda-advaita ullāsa antare — Nityananda and Advaita rejoice at heart; śrībāsa-ādi — Srivasa and others; pahum̐-śire — on the Lord's head; subāsita jala ḍhāle — pour fragrant water; kare kalasi laiyā — taking pitchers in hand

**9.4.** Again and again reciting the abhisheka mantras, Nityananda and Advaita rejoice at heart;
Srivasa and the others, pitchers in hand, pour fragrant water on the Lord's head.

জগদীশ বাসুদেব নারায়ণ মুকুন্দ মাধব গানে বিচক্ষণ
শ্রুতি জাতি স্বরভেদ নানা তানে গায় অভিষেক অমিঞা-পারা ।

*jagadīśa bāsudeba nārāyaṇa mukunda mādhaba gāne bicakṣaṇa*
*śruti jāti svarabheda nānā tāne gāya abhiṣeka amiñā-pārā |*

*Word for word:* jagadīśa bāsudeba nārāyaṇa mukunda mādhaba — Jagadisha, Vasudeva, Narayana, Mukunda, Madhava; gāne bicakṣaṇa — skilled in song; śruti jāti svara-bheda — by shruti, jati and distinctions of svara; nānā tāne — in various strains; gāya abhiṣeka — sing the abhisheka; amiñā-pārā — like nectar

**9.5.** Jagadisha, Vasudeva, Narayana, Mukunda, Madhava — skilled in singing —
in various strains, by shruti, jati and svara, sing the song of the abhisheka, like nectar.[^17-29]

গোবিন্দ গোবিন্দানন্দ খোল বায় ধা ধা ধিক ধিক ধেকা না না তায়
নাচে বক্রেশ্বর সুমধুর ছাঁদে কারু নেত্রে বহে আনন্দধারা ॥

*gobinda gobindānanda khola bāya dhā dhā dhika dhika dhekā nā nā tāya*
*nāce bakreśvara sumadhura chām̐de kāru netre bahe ānandadhārā ||*

*Word for word:* gobinda gobindānanda khola bāya — Govinda and Govindananda play the khol; dhā dhā dhika dhika dhekā nā nā tāya — "dha-dha, dhik-dhik, dheka, na-na" it sounds; nāce bakreśvara — Vakreshvara dances; sumadhura chām̐de — in a sweet rhythm; kāru netre bahe ānanda-dhārā — from some eyes streams of bliss flow

**9.6.** Govinda and Govindananda play the khol: "dha-dha, dhik-dhik, dheka, na-na" it sounds;
Vakreshvara dances in a sweet rhythm; from the eyes of some flow streams of bliss.[^17-30]

সুরগণ গণ সহ অলক্ষিত অভিষেক-সুখে হৈয়া বিমোহিত
বরষে কুসুম থরে থরে করে জয় জয় ধ্বনি পুলক-অঙ্গে ।

*suragaṇa gaṇa saha alakṣita abhiṣeka-sukhe haiyā bimohita*
*baraṣe kusuma thare thare kare jaya jaya dhvani pulaka-aṅge |*

*Word for word:* sura-gaṇa gaṇa saha — the gods with their retinues; alakṣita — unseen; abhiṣeka-sukhe haiyā bimohita — enchanted by the joy of the abhisheka; baraṣe kusuma thare thare — shower flowers layer upon layer; kare jaya jaya dhvani — cry "jaya, jaya"; pulaka-aṅge — with thrilling bodies

**9.7.** The gods with their retinues, unseen, enchanted by the joy of the abhisheka,
shower flowers layer upon layer, cry "Jaya, jaya!", their bodies thrilling.

পতিব্রতা নারীগণ ঘন ঘন দেই জয়কার অতি রসায়ন
মঙ্গল রীতি কি নব নব নরহরি হেরি হিয়া উথলে রঙ্গে ॥

*patibratā nārīgaṇa ghana ghana dei jayakāra ati rasāyana*
*maṅgala rīti ki naba naba narahari heri hiyā uthale raṅge ||*

*Word for word:* patibratā nārī-gaṇa — the wives devoted to their husbands; ghana ghana — again and again; dei jayakāra — cry "jaya"; ati rasāyana — most delightful; maṅgala rīti ki naba naba — what ever-new auspicious rites; narahari heri — Narahari, seeing; hiyā uthale raṅge — the heart surges with joy

**9.8.** The wives devoted to their husbands again and again cry "Jaya!" — how delightful!
What ever-new auspicious rites! Seeing them, Narahari feels his heart surge with joy.[^17-31]

## 10. Narahari — "ki ānanda śrībāsa-bhabane…" (GPT1 p. 242, no. 15; BR)
*The abhisheka in Srivasa's house: the Lord is seated on a golden throne, mantras are recited and water is poured on His head from
pitchers; the women raise the auspicious cry "ulu-ulu", instruments resound, all sing songs of the abhisheka; the gods, beholding the
abhisheka, dance; the poet offers himself to the Lord, before whose face Madana swoons. Raga dhanashi. **Attribution: probably
Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave, right after the preceding one).*[^17-32]

কি আনন্দ শ্রীবাসভবনে ।
করয়ে প্রভুর অভিষেক প্রিয়গণে ॥

*ki ānanda śrībāsabhabane |*
*karaye prabhura abhiṣeka priyagaṇe ||*

*Word for word:* ki ānanda — what bliss; śrībāsa-bhabane — in Srivasa's house; karaye prabhura abhiṣeka — perform the Lord's abhisheka; priya-gaṇe — the beloved associates

**10.1.** What bliss in Srivasa's house!
The beloved associates perform the Lord's abhisheka.

স্বর্ণসিংহাসনে বসাইয়া ।
আনে সুবাসিত জল উলসিত হৈয়া ॥

*svarṇasiṃhāsane basāiyā |*
*āne subāsita jala ulasita haiyā ||*

*Word for word:* svarṇa-siṃhāsane basāiyā — seating Him on a golden throne; āne subāsita jala — they bring fragrant water; ulasita haiyā — rejoicing

**10.2.** Seating Him on a golden throne,
they bring fragrant water, rejoicing.

অভিষেক-মন্ত্র পাঠ করি ।
প্রভুর মস্তকে জল ঢালে ঘট ভরি ॥

*abhiṣeka-mantra pāṭha kari |*
*prabhura mastake jala ḍhāle ghaṭa bhari ||*

*Word for word:* abhiṣeka-mantra pāṭha kari — reciting the abhisheka mantras; prabhura mastake — on the Lord's head; jala ḍhāle — pour water; ghaṭa bhari — from brimming pitchers

**10.3.** Having recited the abhisheka mantras,
they pour water on the Lord's head from brimming pitchers.

উলুলুলু দেই নারীগণ ।
বাজে নানা বাদ্যধ্বনি ভেদয়ে গগন ॥

*ulululu dei nārīgaṇa |*
*bāje nānā bādyadhvani bhedaye gagana ||*

*Word for word:* ulululu dei nārī-gaṇa — the women raise the cry "ulu-ulu"; bāje nānā bādya-dhvani — various instruments resound; bhedaye gagana — piercing the sky

**10.4.** The women raise the cry "ulu-ulu",
various instruments resound, piercing the sky.[^17-33]

অভিষেক-গীত সবে গায় ।
ভাসয়ে নিয়ত নেত্র আনন্দধারায় ॥

*abhiṣeka-gīta sabe gāya |*
*bhāsaye niyata netra ānandadhārāya ||*

*Word for word:* abhiṣeka-gīta sabe gāya — all sing the songs of the abhisheka; bhāsaye niyata netra — the eyes are ceaselessly flooded; ānanda-dhārāya — with streams of bliss

**10.5.** All sing songs of the abhisheka;
their eyes ceaselessly shed streams of bliss.

দেবগণ জয় জয় দিয়া ।
নাচে কত সাধে অভিষেক নিরখিয়া ॥

*debagaṇa jaya jaya diyā |*
*nāce kata sādhe abhiṣeka nirakhiyā ||*

*Word for word:* deba-gaṇa jaya jaya diyā — the gods, crying "jaya, jaya"; nāce kata sādhe — dance with what delight; abhiṣeka nirakhiyā — beholding the abhisheka

**10.6.** The gods, crying "Jaya, jaya!",
dance with what delight, beholding the abhisheka!

অভিষেক-শোভা মনোহর ।
ঝলমল করয়ে কোমল কলেবর ॥

*abhiṣeka-śobhā manohara |*
*jhalamala karaye komala kalebara ||*

*Word for word:* abhiṣeka-śobhā manohara — enchanting is the beauty of the abhisheka; jhalamala karaye — shines; komala kalebara — the tender body

**10.7.** Enchanting is the beauty of the abhisheka:
His tender body shines.

নরহরি আপনা নিছয়ে ।
সুধাময় বদনে মদন মূরছয়ে ॥

*narahari āpanā nichaye |*
*sudhāmaya badane madana mūrachaye ||*

*Word for word:* narahari āpanā nichaye — Narahari offers himself (the nichhani rite); sudhāmaya badane — before the nectarean face; madana mūrachaye — Madana swoons

**10.8.** Narahari offers himself to Him;
before His nectarean face Madana swoons.[^17-34]

## 11. Narahari — "śrī-śacī māyere āge kari…" (GPT1 p. 242, no. 16)
*The abhisheka: the women of Nadia, row upon row, follow Shachi to Srivasa's house to see Gora's abhisheka; the devotees pour Suradhuni
water on His head, wipe Him, dress Him in dry silk; Shachi puts sandal, gorochana and perfume on His forehead; the women raise the cry
"ulu-ulu", the khol, the kartals and the ramshinga horn resound. Raga suhai. **Attribution: not established** — the pada is not in
the BR; simple Bengali tripadi; the GPT2 index assigns the page to Chakravarti (because of the neighbouring pada).*[^17-35]

শ্রীশচী মায়েরে আগে করি যত নদীয়ানারী চলে কাতারে কাতারে ।
শ্রীবাস পণ্ডিত-গেহে উপনীত গোরা-অভিষেক দেখিবার তরে ॥

*śrīśacī māyere āge kari yata nadīyānārī cale kātāre kātāre |*
*śrībāsa paṇḍita-gehe upanīta gorā-abhiṣeka dekhibāra tare ||*

*Word for word:* śrī-śacī māyere āge kari — putting Mother Shachi in front; yata nadīyā-nārī — all the women of Nadia; cale kātāre kātāre — walk in rows upon rows; śrībāsa paṇḍita-gehe upanīta — arrive at the house of Srivasa Pandita; gorā-abhiṣeka dekhibāra tare — to see Gora's abhisheka

**11.1.** Letting Mother Shachi go before them, all the women of Nadia walk in rows upon rows;
they come to the house of Srivasa Pandita to see Gora's abhisheka.

গোরা-অভিষেক অপরূপ লীলা কেহ হেন কভু না দেখে নয়নে ।
সুরধুনী-বারি ঘট ভরি গোরা-শিরে ঢালে যত ভকতগণে ॥

*gorā-abhiṣeka aparūpa līlā keha hena kabhu nā dekhe nayane |*
*suradhunī-bāri ghaṭa bhari gorā-śire ḍhāle yata bhakatagaṇe ||*

*Word for word:* gorā-abhiṣeka aparūpa līlā — Gora's abhisheka is a wondrous lila; keha hena kabhu nā dekhe nayane — no one has ever seen the like with his eyes; suradhunī-bāri ghaṭa bhari — filling pitchers with water of the Suradhuni (Ganga); gorā-śire ḍhāle — pour on Gora's head; yata bhakata-gaṇe — all the devotees

**11.2.** Gora's abhisheka is a wondrous lila: no one has ever seen the like with his own eyes;
filling pitchers with Suradhuni water, all the devotees pour it on Gora's head.

গাত্র মুছাইয়া নেতের অঞ্চলে শুষ্ক পট্টবাস পরিতে দিল ।
ললাটে চন্দন গোরোচনা চুয়া শচী মাতা মনসাধে পরাইল ॥

*gātra muchāiyā netera añcale śuṣka paṭṭabāsa parite dila |*
*lalāṭe candana gorocanā cuyā śacī mātā manasādhe parāila ||*

*Word for word:* gātra muchāiyā — wiping the body; netera añcale — with the edge of a silk cloth; śuṣka paṭṭa-bāsa parite dila — gave dry silk garments to wear; lalāṭe candana gorocanā cuyā — on the brow sandal, gorochana and chua; śacī mātā mana-sādhe parāila — Mother Shachi lovingly applied

**11.3.** Wiping His body with the edge of a silk cloth, they gave Him dry silk garments to wear;
on His brow Mother Shachi lovingly placed sandal, gorochana and the perfume chua.[^17-36]

হুলুলুলু ধ্বনি দেয় নারীগণে গৌরাঙ্গের জয় হয় চারিভিতে ।
খোল করতাল বাজে রামশিঙ্গা নরহরি হেরে হরষিতে ॥

*hulululu dhvani deya nārīgaṇe gaurāṅgera jaya haya cāribhite |*
*khola karatāla bāje rāmaśiṅgā narahari here haraṣite ||*

*Word for word:* hulululu dhvani deya nārī-gaṇe — the women raise the cry "ulu-ulu"; gaurāṅgera jaya haya cāri-bhite — "glory to Gauranga" on all sides; khola karatāla bāje rāmaśiṅgā — khol, kartals and ramshinga resound; narahari here haraṣite — Narahari looks on, rejoicing

**11.4.** The women raise the cry "ulu-ulu", on all sides sounds "Glory to Gauranga!";
khol, kartals and ramshinga resound — Narahari looks on, rejoicing at heart.

## 12. Narahari — "jaya jaya ārati gaura-kiśora…" (GPT1 p. 244, no. 21; BR)
*Gaura's arati: young Gaura shines on the throne like a golden mountain; Advaita, seized by prema, performs arati gazing at His Lord;
on the right Nityananda, on the left Gadadhara, someone holds a parasol over the Lord, Srivasa throws flowers, Narahari tirelessly
waves the chamara, Shuklambara anoints Him with sandal, Murari cries "Jaya!", Madhava, Vasu Ghosha, Purushottama, Vijaya, Mukunda
sing, instruments resound, Vakreshvara dances; the gods in the sky, Shiva and Brahma weep with love. Raga gauri. **Attribution:
probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave); Vrajabuli; signature "narahari-pahu".*[^17-37]

জয় জয় আরতি গৌরকিশোর ।
লসত সিংহাসনে জনু কনকাচল ডগমগ জগত-যুবতী-চিতচোর ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*jaya jaya ārati gaurakiśora |*
*lasata siṃhāsane janu kanakācala ḍagamaga jagata-yubatī-citacora || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* jaya jaya ārati — glory, glory to the arati; gaura-kiśora — of young Gaura; lasata siṃhāsane — He shines on the throne; janu kanakācala — like a golden mountain; ḍagamaga — swaying; jagata-yubatī-cita-cora — thief of the hearts of the world's young women

**12.1.** *(Refrain)* Glory, glory to the arati of Gaura-kishora!
He shines on the throne like a golden mountain — the swaying Thief of the hearts of the young women of the world.[^17-38]

শ্রীঅদ্বৈত প্রেমভরে গরগর আরতি করু নিজ নাথে নেহারি ।
মণিগণ-জড়িত সুকনক-থারি-পর দমকত দীপ দুরিত-তমোহারী ॥

*śrīadvaita premabhare garagara ārati karu nija nāthe nehāri |*
*maṇigaṇa-jaṛita sukanaka-thāri-para damakata dīpa durita-tamohārī ||*

*Word for word:* śrī-advaita prema-bhare garagara — Sri Advaita, overwhelmed with prema; ārati karu — performs arati; nija nāthe nehāri — gazing at His own Lord; maṇigaṇa-jaṛita sukanaka-thāri-para — on a fine golden tray set with gems; damakata dīpa — the lamps flash; durita-tamohārī — destroying the darkness of sins

**12.2.** Sri Advaita, seized by prema, performs arati, gazing at His own Lord;
on a golden tray studded with gems the lamps flash, destroying the darkness of sins.[^17-39]

দক্ষিণভাগে ভাতি রীত অদ্ভুত নিত্যানন্দ রসভোর ।
বামে গদাধর সরস ভঙ্গী তহি কোউ ধরত নব ছত্র উজোর ॥

*dakṣiṇabhāge bhāti rīta adbhuta nityānanda rasabhora |*
*bāme gadādhara sarasa bhaṅgī tahi kou dharata naba chatra ujora ||*

*Word for word:* dakṣiṇa-bhāge — on the right; bhāti rīta adbhuta — a wondrous beauty; nityānanda rasa-bhora — Nityananda absorbed in rasa; bāme gadādhara — on the left Gadadhara; sarasa bhaṅgī — in a graceful pose; tahi kou dharata — there someone holds; naba chatra ujora — a shining new parasol

**12.3.** On the right, a wondrous beauty: Nityananda, absorbed in rasa;
on the left, Gadadhara in a graceful pose; someone holds a shining new parasol.

শ্রীনিবাস বর যত কুসুমাঞ্জলি চামর করু নরহরি অনিবার ।
শুক্লাম্বর বর চরচত চন্দন গুপ্ত মুরারি করত জয়কার ॥

*śrīnibāsa bara yata kusumāñjali cāmara karu narahari anibāra |*
*śuklāmbara bara caracata candana gupta murāri karata jayakāra ||*

*Word for word:* śrīnibāsa bara — the best Srinivasa; yata kusumāñjali — (offers) handfuls of flowers; cāmara karu narahari anibāra — Narahari tirelessly waves the chamara; śuklāmbara bara — the best Shuklambara; caracata candana — anoints with sandal; gupta murāri karata jayakāra — Murari Gupta cries "jaya"

**12.4.** The best Srinivasa throws handfuls of flowers, Narahari tirelessly waves the chamara;
the best Shuklambara anoints Him with sandal, Murari Gupta cries "Jaya!".[^17-40]

মাধব বাসু ঘোষ পুরুষোত্তম বিজয় মুকুন্দ আদি গুণী ভূপ ।
গায়ত মধুর রাগ শ্রুতি মূরছনা গ্রাম সপ্তস্বর ভেদ অনুপ ॥

*mādhaba bāsu ghoṣa puruṣottama bijaya mukunda ādi guṇī bhūpa |*
*gāyata madhura rāga śruti mūrachanā grāma saptasvara bheda anupa ||*

*Word for word:* mādhaba bāsu ghoṣa puruṣottama bijaya mukunda ādi — Madhava, Vasu Ghosha, Purushottama, Vijaya, Mukunda and others; guṇī bhūpa — masters of the art; gāyata madhura — sing sweetly; rāga śruti mūrachanā grāma saptasvara — ragas, shrutis, murchhanas, gramas, the seven svaras; bheda anupa — with peerless distinctions

**12.5.** Madhava, Vasu Ghosha, Purushottama, Vijaya, Mukunda and other masters of the art
sing sweetly, with peerless distinctions of ragas, shrutis, murchhanas, gramas and the seven svaras.

বাজত মুরজ মৃদঙ্গ চঙ্গড়ক বীণ নিশান বেণু চলু ওর ।
ঘন ঘন ঘণ্টা ঝমকত ঝাঁঝরি ঝন্‌ নন ঝাঁঝ গরজে ঘন ঘোর ॥

*bājata muraja mṛdaṅga caṅgaṛaka bīṇa niśāna beṇu calu ora |*
*ghana ghana ghaṇṭā jhamakata jhām̐jhari jhan nana jhām̐jha garaje ghana ghora ||*

*Word for word:* bājata muraja mṛdaṅga caṅgaṛaka bīṇa niśāna beṇu — muraja, mridanga, changadaka, vina, nishana, flutes sound; calu ora — without end; ghana ghana ghaṇṭā — bells again and again; jhamakata jhām̐jhari — jhanjharis clash; jhan nana jhām̐jha garaje ghana ghora — cymbals thunder deeply

**12.6.** Muraja, mridanga, changadaka, vina, nishana, bamboo flutes sound without end;
again and again bells ring, jhanjharis clash, cymbals thunder deeply.[^17-41]

নাচত পরম হরষ বক্রেশ্বর সরস ভাতি গতি নটক সুঠার ।
উঘটত ধিকট ধিকট ধিধি কট তক থৈ থৈ থৈতি বিবিধ পরকার ॥

*nācata parama haraṣa bakreśvara sarasa bhāti gati naṭaka suṭhāra |*
*ughaṭata dhikaṭa dhikaṭa dhidhi kaṭa taka thai thai thaiti bibidha parakāra ||*

*Word for word:* nācata parama haraṣa bakreśvara — Vakreshvara dances in great joy; sarasa bhāti gati naṭaka suṭhāra — with graceful, skilful movements of a dancer; ughaṭata — calls out; dhikaṭa dhikaṭa dhidhi kaṭa taka thai thai thaiti — rhythm syllables; bibidha parakāra — in various ways

**12.7.** Vakreshvara dances in great joy — with graceful, skilful movements of a dancer;
he calls out "dhikat, dhikat, dhidhi kat, tak thai thai" — in various ways.

বিবশ পূরব রসে রসিক গদাধর শ্রীধর গৌরীদাস হরিদাস ।
কো বিরচব সব ভকত মত্ত অতি নিরখি গৌরমুখ মধুরিম হাস ॥

*bibaśa pūraba rase rasika gadādhara śrīdhara gaurīdāsa haridāsa |*
*ko biracaba saba bhakata matta ati nirakhi gauramukha madhurima hāsa ||*

*Word for word:* bibaśa pūraba rase — beside himself in the rasa of the former (lila); rasika gadādhara — the rasika Gadadhara; śrīdhara gaurīdāsa haridāsa — Shridhara, Gauridasa, Haridasa; ko biracaba saba — who will describe them all; bhakata matta ati — the devotees are beside themselves; nirakhi gaura-mukha madhurima hāsa — seeing the sweet smile on Gaura's face

**12.8.** In the bhava of the former lila, the rasika Gadadhara is beside himself; Shridhara, Gauridasa, Haridasa —
who can describe them all? — the devotees are beyond themselves, seeing the sweet smile on Gaura's face.[^17-42]

সুরগণ গগনে মগন গণ সহ সুরপতি কত যতনে করত পরিহার ।
পার্বতীপতি চতুরানন পুলকিত ঝর ঝর নয়নে ঝরত জলধার ॥

*suragaṇa gagane magana gaṇa saha surapati kata yatane karata parihāra |*
*pārvatīpati caturānana pulakita jhara jhara nayane jharata jaladhāra ||*

*Word for word:* sura-gaṇa gagane magana gaṇa saha — the gods in the sky are immersed with their retinues; surapati kata yatane karata parihāra — Indra with much effort keeps aloof (hidden); pārvatī-pati caturānana pulakita — the Lord of Parvati and the Four-faced thrill; jhara jhara nayane jharata jala-dhāra — streams of tears pour from their eyes

**12.9.** In the sky the gods with their retinues are immersed in bliss; the lord of the gods with effort keeps himself hidden;
the Lord of Parvati and the Four-faced thrill, streams of tears pour from their eyes.[^17-43]

ত্রিভুবনে উলস শেষ যশ বরণত স্তুতি করু মুনি নব নাম উচারি ।
নরহরি-পহুঁ ব্রজভূষণ রসময় নদীয়াপুর-পরমানন্দকারী ॥

*tribhubane ulasa śeṣa yaśa baraṇata stuti karu muni naba nāma ucāri |*
*narahari-pahum̐ brajabhūṣaṇa rasamaya nadīyāpura-paramānandakārī ||*

*Word for word:* tribhubane ulasa — joyfully in the three worlds; śeṣa yaśa baraṇata — Shesha recounts the glory; stuti karu muni — the munis praise; naba nāma ucāri — uttering new names; narahari-pahum̐ — Narahari's Lord; braja-bhūṣaṇa rasamaya — ornament of Vraja, full of rasa; nadīyāpura-paramānanda-kārī — bestower of supreme bliss on Nadia

**12.10.** Ananta-Shesha in the three worlds joyfully recounts His glory, the munis praise Him, uttering new names;
the poet Narahari's Lord — the ornament of Vraja, full of rasa, bestower of supreme bliss on Nadia.[^17-44]

[^17-27]: GPT1 — pp. 241–242, section on abhisheka and adhivasa (4.1), no. 14 ("suhai or mayura"); GPT2 — sec. 4.1, no. 14. The pada was
not in the catalogue (new row NG-240). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 893; ed. 1960, vv. 2662–2665): Narahari Chakravarti tells of the
abhisheka in Srivasa's house and cites first the pada of Vasu Ghosha PK 1536 (chapter 1, no. 2), then this one and the next. GPT2
index — Chakravarti (p. 152, no. 14). Not in PK, KGC, PS. B. The abhisheka in Srivasa's house — CB Madhya 9 (mahaprakasha).
[^17-28]: The Yamuna, a dark river, down a golden mountain — the dark curls down the Lord's golden back.
[^17-29]: Jagadisha (Pandita), Vasudeva (Ghosha or Datta), Narayana, Mukunda (Datta), Madhava (Ghosha) — kirtana singers of Navadvipa.
Shruti, jati, svara — terms of musical theory: microtones, classes of melodies, notes.
[^17-30]: Govinda (Ghosha) and Govindananda — kirtana singers; "dha-dha, dhik-dhik…" — rhythm syllables of the mridanga (khol).
[^17-31]: "The wives devoted to their husbands" (patibratā nārīgaṇa) — the women present at the abhisheka, as in the pada of Vasu Ghosha PK
1537 (chapter 1, no. 3); "jaya" and the cry "ulu" are auspicious acclamations.
[^17-32]: GPT1 — p. 242, no. 15 (dhanashi); GPT2 — sec. 4.1, no. 15 (in the catalogue NG-136, wrongly in the "nagari-bhava" section: it is
the abhisheka, sec. 4.1). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 894; ed. 1960, vv. 2666–2673), right after the preceding; then Ishana tells
Srinivasa about Srivasa's maidservant Duhkhi, whom the Lord named Sukhi (CB Madhya 9). Not in PK, KGC, PS. B.
[^17-33]: "Ulu-ulu" (ulululu) — the auspicious cry of Bengali women at rites.
[^17-34]: "Offers himself" (āpanā nichaye) — Bengali nichhani: the rite of waving something around the beloved and offering oneself for his
welfare; a sign of selfless love. Madana (Kama) swoons before the Lord's beauty.
[^17-35]: GPT1 — p. 242, no. 16 (suhai); GPT2 — sec. 4.1, no. 16 (in the catalogue NG-137, wrongly in the "nagari-bhava" section). Not in
BR, PK, KGC, PS. The GPT2 index assigns p. 153 to Chakravarti — probably because of pada no. 15 on that page (no. 10). C.
[^17-36]: Gorochana — a yellow pigment for tilaka; chua (cuyā) — a fragrant resin, perfume. Shachi herself adorns her Son after the
bathing — cf. CB Madhya 9.
[^17-37]: GPT1 — p. 244, no. 21 (gauri); GPT2 — sec. 4.1, no. 21 (in the catalogue PA-005, wrongly as a pada of Paramananda; excluded in
chapter 11). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, pp. 846–847; ed. 1960, vv. 2018–2027): Ishana shows Srinivasa the place in Navadvipa where
Gadadhara adorned the Lord with flowers and the associates performed arati to Him. GPT2 index — Chakravarti. Not in PK, KGC, PS. B.
[^17-38]: "Thief of the hearts of the young women of the world" — an epithet of Krishna applied to Gaura: the same motif as in no. 5 (note
15).
[^17-39]: "His own Lord" (nija nātha) — Advaita worships Gaura as the Lord whom He called down by His prayers (CC Adi 3).
[^17-40]: Srinivasa — Srivasa Pandita; Narahari with the chamara — Narahari Sarakara, the Lord's associate already in Navadvipa (cf. PK 2128, chapter 4, no. 4);
Shuklambara — Shuklambara Brahmachari; Murari Gupta.
[^17-41]: Muraja, mridanga, changadaka — drums; nishana — kettledrum or horn; jhanjhari — small cymbals.
[^17-42]: "In the bhava of the former lila" (pūraba rase) — Gadadhara, in Krishna-lila Radha (Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika 147–153). Shridhara —
the seller of plantain leaves (CB Madhya 9); Gauridasa — Gauridasa Pandita; Haridasa — Haridasa Thakura.
[^17-43]: The lord of the gods (surapati) — Indra; the Lord of Parvati — Shiva; the Four-faced — Brahma. "With effort keeps himself hidden" (yatane karata
parihāra) — the gods are present invisibly.
[^17-44]: "The poet Narahari's Lord" (narahari-pahu, lit. "Narahari-Lord") — the Lord whom Narahari serves (cf. "nayanānanda-pahu" — "the Lord of
Nayanananda", chapter 10): Chakravarti's usual form of signature. "Bestower of supreme bliss on Nadia" (nadīyāpura-paramānanda-kārī) — in
the catalogue the word "paramānanda" was taken for the signature of the poet Paramananda.

## 13. Narahari — "nācata gaura puraba-rase bhora…" (GPT1 p. 261, no. 44; BR)
*Kirtana in Navadvipa: Gaura dances, absorbed in the rasa of the former lila; His smile dispels the darkness of sin, the earth trembles
at His step; He roars like a lion, and the Kali age flees in fear; the associates sing, khol and kartals resound, the whole world is
intoxicated. Raga somaraga. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave); Vrajabuli. With this pada begins
the large cycle "Gaura's dance" of the GPT (sec. 4.2), almost all of which is known also from the BR.*[^17-45]

নাচত গৌর পুরব-রসে ভোর ।
কনক-ধরাধর-গরব-বিভঞ্জন ঝলকত অঙ্গ অতনু-চিতচোর ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*nācata gaura puraba-rase bhora |*
*kanaka-dharādhara-garaba-bibhañjana jhalakata aṅga atanu-citacora || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* nācata gaura — Gaura dances; puraba-rase bhora — absorbed in the rasa of the former (lila); kanaka-dharādhara-garaba-bibhañjana — crushing the pride of a golden mountain; jhalakata aṅga — the body flashes; atanu-cita-cora — thief of the heart of the bodiless (Kama)

**13.1.** *(Refrain)* Gaura dances, absorbed in the rasa of the former lila;
His body flashes, crushing the pride of a golden mountain — it steals the heart even of bodiless Kama.[^17-46]

হাসত মৃদু মৃদু বদন-চাঁদ-ছবি নাশত ঘোর কলুষ-আঁধিয়ার ।
ধরইতে তাল তরল পদপঙ্কজ কম্পই ধরণী সহই নাহি ভার ॥

*hāsata mṛdu mṛdu badana-cām̐da-chabi nāśata ghora kaluṣa-ām̐dhiyāra |*
*dharaite tāla tarala padapaṅkaja kampai dharaṇī sahai nāhi bhāra ||*

*Word for word:* hāsata mṛdu mṛdu — smiles softly; badana-cām̐da-chabi — the beauty of the moon-face; nāśata ghora kaluṣa-ām̐dhiyāra — destroys the dense darkness of sin; dharaite tāla — keeping the rhythm; tarala pada-paṅkaja — the light lotus feet; kampaī dharaṇī — the earth trembles; sahaī nāhi bhāra — cannot bear the weight

**13.2.** Softly He smiles — the beauty of His moon-face destroys the dense darkness of sin;
keeping the rhythm, His light lotus feet step — and the earth trembles, unable to bear their weight.

তরুণ অরুণ-যুগ লোচন ডগমগ অবিরল বিপুল পুলককুল সাজি ।
গরজত সঘন সিংহ জিনি বিক্রম বলী কলিকাল বিপুল ভয়ে ভাজি ॥

*taruṇa aruṇa-yuga locana ḍagamaga abirala bipula pulakakula sāji |*
*garajata saghana siṃha jini bikrama balī kalikāla bipula bhaye bhāji ||*

*Word for word:* taruṇa aruṇa-yuga locana — the two eyes a young dawn; ḍagamaga — swaying; abirala bipula pulaka-kula sāji — adorned with constant abundant thrills; garajata saghana — roars again and again; siṃha jini bikrama — with might surpassing a lion; balī kalikāla — the mighty Kali age; bipula bhaye bhāji — flees in great fear

**13.3.** His two eyes are the young dawn, swaying; He is adorned with constant, abundant thrills;
again and again He roars with a might surpassing a lion's — and the mighty Kali age flees in great fear.[^17-47]

ভেদত গগন গানে প্রিয় পরিকর বায়ত খোল ললিত করতাল ।
মাতল অখিল লোক ভণ নরহরি ভুবন ভরল যশ বিশদ বিশাল ॥

*bhedata gagana gāne priya parikara bāyata khola lalita karatāla |*
*mātala akhila loka bhaṇa narahari bhubana bharala yaśa biśada biśāla ||*

*Word for word:* bhedata gagana — pierces the sky; gāne priya parikara — with the song of the dear associates; bāyata khola lalita karatāla — khol and graceful kartals play; mātala akhila loka — the whole world is intoxicated; bhaṇa narahari — says Narahari; bhubana bharala — has filled the world; yaśa biśada biśāla — pure, boundless fame

**13.4.** The song of the dear associates pierces the sky, khol and graceful kartals play;
the whole world is intoxicated, says Narahari — His pure, boundless fame has filled the universe.

## 14. Narahari — "nṛtyata gauracandra janarañjana…" (GPT1 p. 262, no. 45; BR)
*The dance of Gaura and Nityananda: both are golden mountains, Their glance steals Kama's pride, Their speech flows with nectar; the
associates sing, the mardala sounds, the gods on the paths of the sky shower flowers, the world is full of the cry "Jaya!". Raga
deshapala. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave); Vrajabuli.*[^17-48]

নৃত্যত গৌরচন্দ্র জনরঞ্জন নিত্যানন্দ বিপদ-ভয়-ভঞ্জন কঞ্জ-নয়ন জিতি নব নব খঞ্জন চাহনি মনমথ-গরব হরে ।
ঝলকত দুহুঁ তনু কনক-ধরাধর নটন ঘটন পগ ধরত ধরণী পর হাস মিলিত মুখ লসত সুধাকর উচরি বচন জনু অমিয় ঝরে ॥

*nṛtyata gauracandra janarañjana nityānanda bipada-bhaya-bhañjana kañja-nayana jiti naba naba khañjana cāhani manamatha-garaba hare |*
*jhalakata duhum̐ tanu kanaka-dharādhara naṭana ghaṭana paga dharata dharaṇī para hāsa milita mukha lasata sudhākara ucari bacana janu amiya jhare ||*

*Word for word:* nṛtyata gauracandra jana-rañjana — dances Gaurachandra, delight of the people; nityānanda bipada-bhaya-bhañjana — Nityananda, destroyer of the fear of calamity; kañja-nayana jiti naba naba khañjana — lotus eyes surpassing ever-new khanjanas; cāhani manamatha-garaba hare — the glance steals Kama's pride; jhalakata duhum̐ tanu kanaka-dharādhara — both bodies flash, golden mountains; naṭana ghaṭana paga dharata dharaṇī para — in the dance the feet strike the earth; hāsa milita mukha lasata sudhākara — faces mingled with smiles shine like moons; ucari bacana janu amiya jhare — when they speak, it is as if nectar flowed

**14.1.** Gaurachandra, the delight of the people, and Nityananda, the destroyer of the fear of calamity, dance: Their lotus eyes surpass
ever-new khanjana birds, Their glance steals Kama's pride; both bodies flash — golden mountains; in the dance Their feet strike the
earth; Their faces, mingled with smiles, shine like moons; when They speak, it is as if nectar were flowing.[^17-49]

শোভা নিরুপম ভণত না আয়ত বেষ্টিত পরিকর গুণগণ গায়ত মধুর মধুর মৃদু মর্দল বায়ত ধাধা ধিগি ধিগি ধিকট ধিলঙ্গ ।
গণ সহ সুরগণ গগন-পন্থ-গত ঘন ঘন সরস কুসুমবর বরষত জয় জয় জয় ধ্বনি ভুবন বিয়াপত নরহরি কহব কি প্রেম-তরঙ্গ ॥

*śobhā nirupama bhaṇata nā āyata beṣṭita parikara guṇagaṇa gāyata madhura madhura mṛdu mardala bāyata dhādhā dhigi dhigi dhikaṭa dhilaṅga |*
*gaṇa saha suragaṇa gagana-pantha-gata ghana ghana sarasa kusumabara baraṣata jaya jaya jaya dhvani bhubana biyāpata narahari kahaba ki prema-taraṅga ||*

*Word for word:* śobhā nirupama — peerless beauty; bhaṇata nā āyata — cannot be told; beṣṭita parikara — surrounding, the associates; guṇa-gaṇa gāyata — sing the virtues; madhura madhura mṛdu mardala bāyata — sweetly, softly the mardala plays; dhādhā dhigi dhigi dhikaṭa dhilaṅga — rhythm syllables; gaṇa saha sura-gaṇa — the gods with their retinues; gagana-pantha-gata — on the paths of the sky; ghana ghana sarasa kusuma-bara baraṣata — again and again shower choice flowers; jaya jaya jaya dhvani bhubana biyāpata — the cry "jaya" fills the world; narahari kahaba ki prema-taraṅga — what can Narahari say of the waves of prema

**14.2.** Peerless is this beauty — it cannot be told; surrounding Them, the associates sing Their virtues; sweetly, sweetly, softly the
mardala plays: "dha-dha, dhigi-dhigi, dhikat, dhilanga"; the gods with their retinues on the paths of the sky again and again shower
choice flowers; the cry "Jaya, jaya, jaya" fills the world — what can Narahari say of the waves of prema?

## 15. Narahari — "āju ki ānanda saṅkīrtane…" (GPT1 p. 262, no. 46; BR)
*The sankirtana of Gaura and Nityananda: all are beside themselves with prema, from everyone's eyes rivers of tears flow, some fall on
one another, others roar, tremble, embrace one another and cannot let go, take the dust of one another's feet and roll on the ground;
Lord and servants are all alike in this. Raga kamoda. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave); simple
Bengali tripadi.*[^17-50]

আজু কি আনন্দ সংকীর্তনে ।
নাচে গৌর নিত্যানন্দ পরম আনন্দকন্দ প্রিয় পারিষদবৃন্দ সনে ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*āju ki ānanda saṃkīrtane |*
*nāce gaura nityānanda parama ānandakanda priya pāriṣadabṛnda sane || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* āju ki ānanda saṅkīrtane — what bliss today in the sankirtana; nāce gaura nityānanda — Gaura and Nityananda dance; parama ānanda-kanda — the root of supreme bliss; priya pāriṣada-bṛnda sane — with the dear associates

**15.1.** *(Refrain)* What bliss today in the sankirtana!
Gaura and Nityananda dance — the root of supreme bliss — together with Their dear associates.

নাচে বোলে ভাল ভাল বাজে খোল করতাল সবে মহা বিহ্বল প্রেমায় ।
নদীর প্রবাহ-পারা সবার নয়নে ধারা কেহ কেহ পড়ে কারু গায় ॥

*nāce bole bhāla bhāla bāje khola karatāla sabe mahā bihvala premāya |*
*nadīra prabāha-pārā sabāra nayane dhārā keha keha paṛe kāru gāya ||*

*Word for word:* nāce bole bhāla bhāla — dancing, they cry "well done, well done"; bāje khola karatāla — khol and kartals resound; sabe mahā bihvala premāya — all are beside themselves with prema; nadīra prabāha-pārā — like the current of a river; sabāra nayane dhārā — streams from everyone's eyes; keha keha paṛe kāru gāya — some fall on one another

**15.2.** Dancing, they cry: "Well done, well done!"; khol and kartals resound — all are beside themselves with prema;
from everyone's eyes pour streams like the current of a river; some fall upon one another.

কেহ বা পুলকভরে হুঙ্কার গর্জন করে কাঁপে কেহ থির হৈতে নারে ।
কেহ কারু পানে চাঞা দুই বাহু পসারিয়া কোলে করি ছাড়িতে না পারে ॥

*keha bā pulakabhare huṅkāra garjana kare kām̐pe keha thira haite nāre |*
*keha kāru pāne cāñā dui bāhu pasāriyā kole kari chāṛite nā pāre ||*

*Word for word:* keha vā pulaka-bhare — someone, thrilling; huṅkāra garjana kare — roars and shouts; kām̐pe keha — someone trembles; thira haite nāre — cannot stand steady; keha kāru pāne cāñā — someone, looking at another; dui bāhu pasāriyā — spreading both arms; kole kari chāṛite nā pāre — embraces and cannot let go

**15.3.** Someone, thrilling, roars and shouts aloud; someone trembles, unable to stand steady;
someone, looking at another, opens his arms, embraces him — and cannot let him go.

কেহ কারু পায় ধরে পদধূলি লয় শিরে কেহ ভূমে পড়ি গড়ি যায় ।
প্রভু ভৃত্য এক রীতি দেখি নরহরি অতি আনন্দে প্রভুর গুণ গায় ॥

*keha kāru pāya dhare padadhūli laya śire keha bhūme paṛi gaṛi yāya |*
*prabhu bhṛtya eka rīti dekhi narahari ati ānande prabhura guṇa gāya ||*

*Word for word:* keha kāru pāya dhare — someone seizes another's feet; pada-dhūli laya śire — puts the dust of the feet on his head; keha bhūme paṛi gaṛi yāya — someone falls to the ground and rolls; prabhu bhṛtya eka rīti — Lord and servants in one state; dekhi narahari ati ānande — seeing this, Narahari in great bliss; prabhura guṇa gāya — sings the Lord's virtues

**15.4.** Someone seizes another's feet and puts the dust of his feet on his head; someone, falling to the ground, rolls in the dust;
Lord and servants are in one state: seeing this, Narahari in great bliss sings the virtues of the Lord.[^17-51]

## 16. Narahari — "nācata gaurāṅga-cām̐da bibhora bhābete…" (GPT1 p. 262, no. 47)
*Gauranga dances, seized by bhava; in the same bhava, on His left, Gadadhara dances; Nitai follows behind so that His golden body may
not fall to the ground; the Lord embraces the fallen. Raga pathamanjari. **Attribution: not established** — the pada is not in the BR
(the GPT2 index, however, assigns its page to Chakravarti); simple Bengali payar.*[^17-52]

নাচত গৌরাঙ্গচাঁদ বিভোর ভাবেতে ।
সেই ভাবে গদাধর নাচয়ে বামেতে ॥

*nācata gaurāṅgacām̐da bibhora bhābete |*
*sei bhābe gadādhara nācaye bāmete ||*

*Word for word:* nācata gaurāṅga-cām̐da — Gaurangachand dances; bibhora bhābete — seized by bhava; sei bhābe gadādhara — in the same bhava Gadadhara; nācaye bāmete — dances on the left

**16.1.** Gaurangachand dances, seized by bhava;
in the same bhava on His left dances Gadadhara.

ভাদর-সোণার অঙ্গ ভূমে পড়ে পাছে ।
তাই সে নিতাইচাঁদ ফিরে পাছে পাছে ॥

*bhādara-soṇāra aṅga bhūme paṛe pāche |*
*tāi se nitāicām̐da phire pāche pāche ||*

*Word for word:* bhādara-soṇāra aṅga — the body of pure gold; bhūme paṛe pāche — lest it fall to the ground; tāi se nitāicām̐da — that is why Nitaichand; phire pāche pāche — keeps close behind

**16.2.** Lest His body of pure gold should fall to the ground,
Nitaichand keeps following close behind Him.[^17-53]

নাচে রে গৌরাঙ্গ আমার হেলিয়া দুলিয়া ।
বাজে খোল করতাল তাধিয়া তাধিয়া ॥

*nāce re gaurāṅga āmāra heliyā duliyā |*
*bāje khola karatāla tādhiyā tādhiyā ||*

*Word for word:* nāce re gaurāṅga āmāra — my Gauranga dances; heliyā duliyā — swaying, rocking; bāje khola karatāla — khol and kartals sound; tādhiyā tādhiyā — "ta-dhiya, ta-dhiya"

**16.3.** My Gauranga dances, swaying, rocking;
khol and kartals sound: "ta-dhiya, ta-dhiya".

দুরগত পতিত ধরিয়া করু কোর ।
পামর এ নরহরি ও না রসে ভোর ॥

*duragata patita dhariyā karu kora |*
*pāmara e narahari o nā rase bhora ||*

*Word for word:* duragata patita — the fallen who have gone astray; dhariyā karu kora — He seizes and embraces; pāmara e narahari — only sinful Narahari; o nā rase bhora — is not immersed in that rasa

**16.4.** He seizes and embraces the fallen who have gone astray —
only sinful Narahari is not immersed in this rasa.

## 17. Narahari — "nācata gauracandra guṇadhāma…" (GPT1 p. 263, no. 49; BR)
