*Gaura's dance: the radiance of His body outshines a golden mountain and lightning; His smile steals composure, earrings tremble, curls
are decked with flowers, a garland on His chest, His arms in new play, His feet keeping the rhythm; the associates sing, khol and khamak
resound. Raga bangala. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave); Vrajabuli.*[^17-54]

নাচত গৌরচন্দ্র গুণধাম ।
ঝলকত অঙ্গ-কিরণ মনরঞ্জন কনক-মেরু দূরে দামিনী-দাম ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*nācata gauracandra guṇadhāma |*
*jhalakata aṅga-kiraṇa manarañjana kanaka-meru dūre dāminī-dāma || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* nācata gauracandra guṇadhāma — Gaurachandra dances, abode of virtues; jhalakata aṅga-kiraṇa — the radiance of the body flashes; mana-rañjana — charming the heart; kanaka-meru dūre — (casting) far away golden Meru; dāminī-dāma — and garlands of lightning

**17.1.** *(Refrain)* Gaurachandra dances, the abode of virtues;
the radiance of His body flashes, charming the heart — it casts far away both golden Meru and garlands of lightning.

বন্ধুর বদন মদন-মদ-মরদন মধুরিম হাস যুবতী-ধৃতি-হারী ।
শ্রুতি জিতি তরুণ-অরুণ মণিকুণ্ডল টলমল নয়নযুগল ছবি ভারি ॥

*bandhura badana madana-mada-maradana madhurima hāsa yubatī-dhṛti-hārī |*
*śruti jiti taruṇa-aruṇa maṇikuṇḍala ṭalamala nayanayugala chabi bhāri ||*

*Word for word:* bandhura badana — the lovely face; madana-mada-maradana — crushing Madana's pride; madhurima hāsa — the sweet smile; yubatī-dhṛti-hārī — stealing the composure of young wives; śruti jiti taruṇa-aruṇa maṇi-kuṇḍala — at the ears jewelled earrings surpassing the young dawn; ṭalamala nayana-yugala — both eyes sway; chabi bhāri — great is their beauty

**17.2.** His lovely face crushes Madana's pride; His sweet smile steals the composure of young wives;
at His ears tremble jewelled earrings surpassing the young dawn; both His eyes sway — how beautiful they are![^17-55]

চাঁচর চিকণ কেশ কুসুমাঞ্চিত চপল চারু উরে মণ্ডিত মাল ।
অভিনব বাহুভঙ্গী ভর নিরুপম ধরত চরণতলে সুললিত তাল ॥

*cām̐cara cikaṇa keśa kusumāñcita capala cāru ure maṇḍita māla |*
*abhinaba bāhubhaṅgī bhara nirupama dharata caraṇatale sulalita tāla ||*

*Word for word:* cām̐cara cikaṇa keśa — smooth curling locks; kusumāñcita — decked with flowers; capala cāru ure maṇḍita māla — on the restless lovely chest an adorning garland; abhinaba bāhu-bhaṅgī bhara nirupama — in the peerless, ever-new play of the arms; dharata caraṇa-tale sulalita tāla — the feet keep a graceful rhythm

**17.3.** His smooth curling locks are decked with flowers; on His restless, lovely chest — a garland;
in the peerless, ever-new play of His arms His feet keep a graceful rhythm.

পহুঁ চলু পাশ লসত প্রিয় পরিকর গায়ত মধুর রাগ রস মাতি ।
উলসিত সকল ভুবন ভণ নরহরি বায়ত খোল খমক বহু ভাঁতি ॥

*pahum̐ calu pāśa lasata priya parikara gāyata madhura rāga rasa māti |*
*ulasita sakala bhubana bhaṇa narahari bāyata khola khamaka bahu bhām̐ti ||*

*Word for word:* pahum̐ calu — the Lord moves; pāśa lasata priya parikara — beside Him shine the dear associates; gāyata madhura rāga — sing sweet ragas; rasa māti — intoxicated with rasa; ulasita sakala bhubana — the whole world rejoices; bhaṇa narahari — says Narahari; bāyata khola khamaka bahu bhām̐ti — khol and khamak sound in many ways

**17.4.** The Lord moves, beside Him shine the dear associates, singing sweet ragas, intoxicated with rasa;
the whole world rejoices, says Narahari; khol and khamak sound in every manner.

## 18. Narahari — "nācata gauracandra naṭabhūpa…" (GPT1 p. 263, no. 50; BR)
*The dance of Gaura, king of dancers: a form crushing the pride of a hundred thousand Kamas; He roars in bhava, spreads His arms,
smiles, His face is the autumn moon; the devotees sing, outdoing the kinnaras, the ocean of prema has flooded the earth — only
Narahari it does not touch. Raga belavali. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave); Vrajabuli.*[^17-56]

নাচত গৌরচন্দ্র নটভূপ ।
মনমথ-লাখ-গরব-ভর-ভঞ্জন অখিল-ভুবনজন-রঞ্জন রূপ ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*nācata gauracandra naṭabhūpa |*
*manamatha-lākha-garaba-bhara-bhañjana akhila-bhubanajana-rañjana rūpa || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* nācata gauracandra naṭa-bhūpa — Gaurachandra dances, king of dancers; manamatha-lākha-garaba-bhara-bhañjana — crushing the pride of a hundred thousand Kamas; akhila-bhubana-jana-rañjana rūpa — a form delighting the people of all the worlds

**18.1.** *(Refrain)* Gaurachandra dances, the king of dancers:
a form crushing the pride of a hundred thousand Kamas — the delight of the people of all the worlds.

অবিরত অতুল ভাবভরে গর গর গরজত অতি অদভুত রুচিকারী ।
মঙ্গলময় পদ ধরত ধরণী পর করত ভঙ্গী ভুজযুগল পসারি ॥

*abirata atula bhābabhare gara gara garajata ati adabhuta rucikārī |*
*maṅgalamaya pada dharata dharaṇī para karata bhaṅgī bhujayugala pasāri ||*

*Word for word:* abirata atula bhāba-bhare gara gara — ceaselessly seized by peerless bhava; garajata ati adabhuta rucikārī — roars wondrously, beautifully; maṅgalamaya pada dharata dharaṇī para — sets the auspicious feet on the earth; karata bhaṅgī bhuja-yugala pasāri — moves with both arms outspread

**18.2.** Ceaselessly seized by peerless bhava, He roars — wondrously, beautifully;
He sets His auspicious feet on the earth, moves with both arms outspread.

হাসত মধুর অধর মৃদু লাবণি শরদ-চাঁদ জিনি বদন-বিলাস ।
টলমল অরুণ কমলদল-লোচন কৌনে করয় কত রস পরকাশ ॥

*hāsata madhura adhara mṛdu lābaṇi śarada-cām̐da jini badana-bilāsa |*
*ṭalamala aruṇa kamaladala-locana kaune karaya kata rasa parakāśa ||*

*Word for word:* hāsata madhura — smiles sweetly; adhara mṛdu lābaṇi — the lips soft and lovely; śarada-cām̐da jini badana-bilāsa — the play of the face surpasses the autumn moon; ṭalamala aruṇa kamala-dala-locana — the eyes, red lotus petals, sway; kaune karaya kata rasa parakāśa — who can tell how much rasa He reveals

**18.3.** Sweetly He smiles, His lips soft and lovely, the play of His face surpasses the autumn moon;
His eyes, petals of a red lotus, sway: who can tell how much rasa He reveals?

গায়ত মধুর ভকতগণ নব নব কিন্নর-নিকর দরপ করু চূর ।
উথলল প্রেমসিন্ধু মহী ভাসল নরহরি কুমতি পরশ রহু দূর ॥

*gāyata madhura bhakatagaṇa naba naba kinnara-nikara darapa karu cūra |*
*uthalala premasindhu mahī bhāsala narahari kumati paraśa rahu dūra ||*

*Word for word:* gāyata madhura bhakata-gaṇa naba naba — the devotees sing sweetly ever-new (songs); kinnara-nikara darapa karu cūra — crush the pride of the host of kinnaras; uthalala prema-sindhu — the ocean of prema surged; mahī bhāsala — flooded the earth; narahari kumati — foolish Narahari; paraśa rahu dūra — remained far from its touch

**18.4.** Sweetly the devotees sing ever-new songs, crushing the pride of the host of kinnaras;
the ocean of prema has surged and flooded the earth — only foolish Narahari it has not touched.[^17-57]

## 19. Narahari — "nācata dvija-kula-candra gaurahari…" (GPT1 p. 264, no. 52; BR)
*The dance of Gaurahari, moon of the brahmana line: auspicious feet, absorption in the bhava of the former lila, body thrilling, curls
like a cloud on a golden mountain, a garland of malati, His face a snare of Kama; the associates sing, the world sinks in an ocean of
happiness. Raga nata. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave); Vrajabuli.*[^17-58]

নাচত দ্বিজকুলচন্দ্র গৌরহরি ।
মঙ্গলময় ভয়-হরণ চরণযুগ ধরত ধরণী পর পরম ভঙ্গী করি ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*nācata dvijakulacandra gaurahari |*
*maṅgalamaya bhaya-haraṇa caraṇayuga dharata dharaṇī para parama bhaṅgī kari || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* nācata dvija-kula-candra gaurahari — Gaurahari dances, moon of the twice-born line; maṅgalamaya bhaya-haraṇa caraṇa-yuga — the auspicious fear-removing feet; dharata dharaṇī para — He sets on the earth; parama bhaṅgī kari — in wondrous poses

**19.1.** *(Refrain)* Gaurahari dances, the moon of the twice-born line;
His auspicious, fear-removing feet He sets on the earth, assuming wondrous poses.

অবিরত পূরব-ভাবভরে গর গর অবিরল পুলক-কদম্ব-বলিত তনু ।
চাঁচর চিকুর-ভার রুচি সুচিকণ কনক-ধরাধর-শিখরে মেঘ জনু ॥

*abirata pūraba-bhābabhare gara gara abirala pulaka-kadamba-balita tanu |*
*cām̐cara cikura-bhāra ruci sucikaṇa kanaka-dharādhara-śikhare megha janu ||*

*Word for word:* abirata pūraba-bhāba-bhare gara gara — ceaselessly seized by the bhava of the former (lila); abirala pulaka-kadamba-balita tanu — the body covered with thrills like kadamba flowers; cām̐cara cikura-bhāra — heavy curling locks; ruci sucikaṇa — glossy and smooth; kanaka-dharādhara-śikhare megha janu — like a cloud on the peak of a golden mountain

**19.2.** Ceaselessly seized by the bhava of the former lila, His body is covered with thrills, as if with kadamba flowers;
His smooth, glossy curling locks — like a cloud on the peak of a golden mountain.[^17-59]

মালতী-কুসুম-মাল অতি মণ্ডিত চপল চারু উরে লম্বিত ঝলমল ।
মনমথ-ফাঁদ বদন মনরঞ্জন অরুণ কঞ্জযুগ লোচন টলমল ॥

*mālatī-kusuma-māla ati maṇḍita capala cāru ure lambita jhalamala |*
*manamatha-phām̐da badana manarañjana aruṇa kañjayuga locana ṭalamala ||*

*Word for word:* mālatī-kusuma-māla ati maṇḍita — a garland of malati flowers, wondrously arrayed; capala cāru ure lambita jhalamala — hangs swaying on the restless lovely chest; manamatha-phām̐da badana — the face, Kama's snare; mana-rañjana — delight of the heart; aruṇa kañja-yuga locana ṭalamala — the eyes, a pair of red lotuses, sway

**19.3.** A garland of malati flowers, wondrously arrayed, sways, hanging on His restless, lovely chest;
His face is Kama's snare, the delight of the heart; His eyes sway — a pair of red lotuses.

নিরুপম নটন নিরখি প্রিয় পরিকর গায়ত মধুর মধুর রস বরষত ।
অখিল লোক সুখসায়রে নিমগন নরহরি কুমতি দূরে নাহি পরশত ॥

*nirupama naṭana nirakhi priya parikara gāyata madhura madhura rasa baraṣata |*
*akhila loka sukhasāyare nimagana narahari kumati dūre nāhi paraśata ||*

*Word for word:* nirupama naṭana nirakhi — seeing the peerless dance; priya parikara gāyata madhura — the dear associates sing sweetly; madhura rasa baraṣata — showering sweet rasa; akhila loka sukha-sāyare nimagana — the whole world sinks in an ocean of happiness; narahari kumati dūre — foolish Narahari, far off; nāhi paraśata — is not touched

**19.4.** Seeing the peerless dance, the dear associates sing sweetly, showering rasa;
the whole world sinks in an ocean of happiness — only foolish Narahari stays far off, untouched.

## 20. Narahari — "nācata gaura nikhila-naṭa-paṇḍita…" (GPT1 p. 264, no. 53; BR)
*The dance of Gaura, most skilled of dancers: the radiance of His body, outshining the sun, lights up all directions; He roars like a
lion, and the elephant Kali trembles; leaps and stamping feet shake the earth; the associates sing, the sound of the khol reaches the
sky; the wicked, trembling, seek refuge at His feet. Raga ghantarava. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR
(12th wave); Vrajabuli.*[^17-60]

নাচত গৌর নিখিল-নট-পণ্ডিত নিরুপম ভঙ্গী মদন-মদ হরঈ ।
প্রচুর চণ্ডকর-দর-পরিভঞ্জন অঙ্গ-কিরণে দিগবিদিগ উজরঈ ॥

*nācata gaura nikhila-naṭa-paṇḍita nirupama bhaṅgī madana-mada haraī |*
*pracura caṇḍakara-dara-paribhañjana aṅga-kiraṇe digabidiga ujaraī ||*

*Word for word:* nācata gaura — Gaura dances; nikhila-naṭa-paṇḍita — most skilled of all dancers; nirupama bhaṅgī — with peerless movements; madana-mada haraī — takes away Madana's pride; pracura caṇḍakara-dara-paribhañjana — crushing the pride of the blazing sun; aṅga-kiraṇe — with the radiance of the body; digvidiga ujaraī — lights up all the quarters

**20.1.** Gaura dances, the most skilled of all dancers; with peerless movements He takes away Madana's pride;
crushing the pride of the blazing sun, with the radiance of His body He lights up all the quarters.

উনমত অতুল সিংহ জিনি গরজন শুনইতে বলী কলি-বারণ ডরঈ ।
ঘন ঘন লম্ফ ললিত গতি চঞ্চল চরণঘাতে ক্ষিতি টলমল করঈ ॥

*unamata atula siṃha jini garajana śunaite balī kali-bāraṇa ḍaraī |*
*ghana ghana lampha lalita gati cañcala caraṇaghāte kṣiti ṭalamala karaī ||*

*Word for word:* unamata atula — intoxicated, peerless; siṃha jini garajana — a roar surpassing a lion's; śunaite — on hearing it; balī kali-bāraṇa ḍaraī — the mighty elephant Kali trembles; ghana ghana lampha — again and again leaps; lalita gati cañcala — graceful restless gait; caraṇa-ghāte kṣiti ṭalamala karaī — at the strokes of the feet the earth shakes

**20.2.** Intoxicated, He roars beyond compare, stronger than a lion — hearing it, the mighty elephant Kali trembles;
again and again leaps, a graceful, restless gait — at the strokes of His feet the earth shakes.[^17-61]

কিন্নর-গরব খরব করু পরিকর গায়ত উলসে অমিয় রব ঝরঈ ।
বায়ত বহুবিধ খোল খমক ধুনি পরশত গগন কৌন ধৃতি ধরঈ ॥

*kinnara-garaba kharaba karu parikara gāyata ulase amiya raba jharaī |*
*bāyata bahubidha khola khamaka dhuni paraśata gagana kauna dhṛti dharaī ||*

*Word for word:* kinnara-garaba kharaba karu parikara — the associates crush the pride of the kinnaras; gāyata ulase — sing in jubilation; amiya raba jharaī — a nectarean sound flows; bāyata bahu-bidha khola khamaka dhuni — the sound of many khols and khamaks; paraśata gagana — touches the sky; kauna dhṛti dharaī — who can keep composure

**20.3.** The associates crush the pride of the kinnaras, singing in jubilation — a nectarean sound flows;
many khols and khamaks play, the sound touches the sky — who can keep composure?

অতুল প্রতাপ কাঁপি দুরজনগণ লেয়ই শরণ চরণতলে পড়ঈ ।
নরহরি-পহুঁক কীরিতি রহু জগভরি পরম দুলহ ধন নিয়ত বিতরঈ ॥

*atula pratāpa kām̐pi durajanagaṇa leyai śaraṇa caraṇatale paṛaī |*
*narahari-pahum̐ka kīriti rahu jagabhari parama dulaha dhana niyata bitaraī ||*

*Word for word:* atula pratāpa — before the peerless might; kām̐pi durajana-gaṇa — trembling, the wicked; leyaī śaraṇa — take refuge; caraṇa-tale paṛaī — fall at the feet; narahari-pahum̐ka kīriti — the fame of Narahari's Lord; rahu jaga-bhari — fills the world; parama dulaha dhana — the highest, rarest treasure; niyata bitaraī — ceaselessly gives away

**20.4.** Before His peerless might the wicked tremble, seek refuge, fall at His feet;
the fame of the poet Narahari's Lord fills the world: ceaselessly He gives away the highest, rarest treasure.[^17-62]

[^17-45]: GPT1 — p. 261, section on dance and kirtana (4.2), no. 44 (somaraga); GPT2 — sec. 4.2, no. 44. The pada was not in the catalogue
(new row NG-241). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 836; ed. 1960, vv. 1865–1868), right after the pada "nācata bhubana-mano-mohana" (no.
4). Not in PK, KGC, PS. B.
[^17-46]: "The rasa of the former lila" (puraba-rasa) — the bhava of Krishna-lila, which the Lord experiences in kirtana. "Bodiless" (atanu) —
Kama, burnt by Shiva.
[^17-47]: The Lord's roar in kirtana — cf. CB Madhya 23 (nagara-kirtana); the Kali age fleeing before the sankirtana is a frequent image.
[^17-48]: GPT1 — p. 262, no. 45 (deshapala); GPT2 — sec. 4.2, no. 45 (catalogue: NG-140). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 839; ed. 1960,
vv. ≈1905–1908). GPT2 index — Chakravarti (p. 167, no. 45). Not in PK, KGC, PS. B.
[^17-49]: Khanjana — the wagtail, a bird with restless eyes, a usual comparison for eyes. "Destroyer of the fear of calamity" — an epithet
of Nityananda.
[^17-50]: GPT1 — p. 262, no. 46 (kamoda); GPT2 — sec. 4.2, no. 46 (catalogue: NG-141). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 839; ed. 1960,
vv. 1909–1912), right after the preceding. GPT2 index — Chakravarti (p. 167, no. 46). The language is simple Bengali tripadi, without
Vrajabuli; by language alone the pada could be Sarakara's, but it is in the BR. Not in PK, KGC, PS. B.
[^17-51]: "Lord and servants are in one state" (prabhu bhṛtya eka rīti) — in the ecstasy of kirtana the Lord and the devotees are equally
seized by prema. Cf. CB Madhya 8 (the night kirtanas in Srivasa's house).
[^17-52]: GPT1 — p. 262, no. 47 (pathamanjari), checked against the scan (PDF p. 521); GPT2 — sec. 4.2, no. 47 (catalogue: NG-142). Not in
BR, PK, KGC, PS. The GPT2 index assigns p. 167 (padas nos. 45–47) to Chakravarti, but only nos. 45 and 46 were found in the BR. Simple
Bengali payar; C ("not established").
[^17-53]: "Pure gold" — GPT1 "bhādara soṇāra" (the reading is unclear in the scan), GPT2 "bhādra sonāra"; the sense is "golden body".
Nityananda follows the dancing Lord to catch Him should He fall in ecstasy — cf. CC Madhya 13 (Ratha-yatra).
[^17-54]: GPT1 — p. 263, no. 49 (bangala); GPT2 — sec. 4.2, no. 49 (catalogue: NG-143). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 841; ed. 1960,
vv. 1941–1944): "here, right by the house, is the lovely place where the Lord was beside Himself in sankirtana". Before it in the GPT
stands no. 48, signed "Ghanashyama Dasa" (not included in the appendix). Not in PK, KGC, PS. B.
[^17-55]: "Steals the composure of young wives" — the motif of the townswomen (note 15).
[^17-56]: GPT1 — p. 263, no. 50 (belavali); GPT2 — sec. 4.2, no. 50 (catalogue: NG-144). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 842; ed. 1960,
vv. 1945–1948). Not in PK, KGC, PS. B.
[^17-57]: Kinnaras — celestial singers. "Only Narahari it has not touched" — the poet's usual self-abasement (cf. no. 7.4).
[^17-58]: GPT1 — p. 264, no. 52 (nata); GPT2 — sec. 4.2, no. 52 (catalogue: NG-145). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 882; ed. 1960,
vv. 2560–2563), right after a pada signed "Ghanashyama" ("nācata gaura bhābabhare garagara", in the GPT no. 51). Not in PK, KGC, PS. B.
[^17-59]: Kadamba flowers are round and covered with filaments; hairs standing on end in ecstasy are compared to them. "A cloud on a golden
mountain" — dark curls above the golden brow.
[^17-60]: GPT1 — p. 264, no. 53 (ghantarava); GPT2 — sec. 4.2, no. 53. The pada was not in the catalogue (new row NG-242). BR — 12th wave
(ed. 1912, p. 883; ed. 1960, vv. 2564–2567), right after the preceding. Not in PK, KGC, PS. B.
[^17-61]: "The elephant Kali" (kali-bāraṇa) — the Kali age, like a mad elephant tamed by the lion Gaura (cf. "gaurasiṃha" in no. 24).
[^17-62]: "The poet Narahari's Lord" (narahari-pahum̐ka) — see note 44. "The wicked… seek refuge" — the conversion of sinners, like Jagai and Madhai
(no. 22).

## 21. Narahari — "suradhunī-tīra parama niramala thala…" (GPT1 p. 265, no. 54; BR)
*Gaura's dance on the bank of the Suradhuni: at a pure place by the river the generous devotees rejoice, sing nectarean songs, play
instruments; Gaura-kishora dances anointed with sandal, His face outshines autumn moons, His necklace flashes, His anklets tinkle.
Raga biragupta. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave); Vrajabuli.*[^17-63]

সুরধুনীতীর পরম নিরমল থল তহি উলসিত সব ভকত উদার ।
গায়ত কত কত গীত অমিয়ময় বায়ত বাদ্য বিবিধ পরকার ॥

*suradhunītīra parama niramala thala tahi ulasita saba bhakata udāra |*
*gāyata kata kata gīta amiyamaya bāyata bādya bibidha parakāra ||*

*Word for word:* suradhunī-tīra — the bank of the Suradhuni (Ganga); parama niramala thala — a most pure place; tahi ulasita saba bhakata udāra — there all the generous devotees rejoice; gāyata kata kata gīta amiyamaya — sing many nectarean songs; bāyata bādya bibidha parakāra — play instruments of many kinds

**21.1.** The bank of the Suradhuni is a most pure place; there all the generous devotees rejoice,
sing many nectarean songs, play instruments of every kind.

নাচত গুণমণি গৌরকিশোর ।
চন্দন-চরচিত রুচির অঙ্গ অতি অপরূপ রূপ রমণী-মনচোর ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*nācata guṇamaṇi gaurakiśora |*
*candana-caracita rucira aṅga ati aparūpa rūpa ramaṇī-manacora || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* nācata guṇamaṇi gaura-kiśora — Gaura-kishora dances, jewel of virtues; candana-caracita — anointed with sandal; rucira aṅga ati — the lovely body; aparūpa rūpa — a wondrous form; ramaṇī-mana-cora — stealing the hearts of women

**21.2.** *(Refrain)* Gaura-kishora dances, the jewel of virtues;
His lovely body is anointed with sandal — a wondrous form, stealing the hearts of women.[^17-64]

অমল কমলদল লোচন ডগমগ ভাঙ-ভঙ্গী নব অলকা-বিলাস ।
শরদ-নিশাকর-নিকর-নিন্দি মুখ কোটি-মদন-মদ-মরদন হাস ॥

*amala kamaladala locana ḍagamaga bhāṅa-bhaṅgī naba alakā-bilāsa |*
*śarada-niśākara-nikara-nindi mukha koṭi-madana-mada-maradana hāsa ||*

*Word for word:* amala kamala-dala locana ḍagamaga — the eyes, petals of a pure lotus, sway; bhām̐ṅa-bhaṅgī — the play of the brows; naba alakā-bilāsa — the new charm of the locks; śarada-niśākara-nikara-nindi mukha — a face shaming hosts of autumn moons; koṭi-madana-mada-maradana hāsa — a smile crushing the pride of millions of Madanas

**21.3.** His eyes, petals of a pure lotus, sway; the play of His brows, the new charm of His locks;
His face shames hosts of autumn moons, His smile crushes the pride of millions of Madanas.

চঞ্চল ললিত বিশাল বক্ষোপরি ঝলকত জিনি দামিনী মণিহার ।
নরহরি-পহুঁ পগ ধরত তাল যব তব কি মধুর রব নূপুর-ঝনকার ॥

*cañcala lalita biśāla bakṣopari jhalakata jini dāminī maṇihāra |*
*narahari-pahum̐ paga dharata tāla yaba taba ki madhura raba nūpura-jhanakāra ||*

*Word for word:* cañcala lalita biśāla bakṣopari — on the restless lovely broad chest; jhalakata jini dāminī maṇihāra — the jewelled necklace flashes, outshining lightning; narahari-pahum̐ — Narahari's Lord; paga dharata tāla yaba — when He keeps the rhythm with His feet; taba ki madhura raba nūpura-jhanakāra — how sweetly the anklets tinkle

**21.4.** On His restless, lovely, broad chest flashes a jewelled necklace, outshining lightning;
when the poet Narahari's Lord keeps the rhythm with His feet — how sweetly the anklets tinkle!

## 22. Narahari — "āju ki ānanda nadīyā-nagare…" (GPT1 p. 265, no. 55; BR)
*After the deliverance of Jagai and Madhai: the men and women of Nadia run to see the brothers and talk among themselves: they shine
like the sun — where has their sinful body gone? The brothers, in bhava, weep, tremble, roll in the dust, cannot take their eyes off
Gora's face, bathe Nitai's feet with tears, take the dust of the feet of Advaita, Gadadhara, Srivasa, and, holding straw between
their teeth, with arms raised, beg the Lord and His associates for mercy. Raga gurjari. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the
pada is in the BR (12th wave, the account of Jagai and Madhai).*[^17-65]

আজু কি আনন্দ নদীয়ানগরে জগাই মাধাই দোঁহে দেখিবারে ধায় চারিদিকে কি নারী পুরুষ পরস্পর কহে কত না কথা ।
কেহ কহে অতি বিরলেতে রৈয়া এ দেখ দেখ দুহুঁ পানে চাইয়া সুরুজের সম তেজ এবে ভেল সে পাপশরীর গেল বা কোথা ॥

*āju ki ānanda nadīyānagare jagāi mādhāi dom̐he dekhibāre dhāya cāridike ki nārī puruṣa paraspara kahe kata nā kathā |*
*keha kahe ati biralete raiyā e dekha dekha duhum̐ pāne cāiyā surujera sama teja ebe bhela se pāpaśarīra gela bā kothā ||*

*Word for word:* āju ki ānanda nadīyā-nagare — what bliss today in the town of Nadia; jagāi mādhāi dom̐he dekhibāre — to see Jagai and Madhai; dhāya cāridike ki nārī puruṣa — women and men run from all sides; paraspara kahe kata nā kathā — talk with one another; keha kahe ati biralete raiyā — someone says, standing apart; e dekha dekha duhum̐ pāne cāiyā — look, look at the two; surujera sama teja ebe bhela — now they shine like the sun; se pāpa-śarīra gela vā kothā — where has that sinful body gone

**22.1.** What bliss today in the town of Nadia! To see Jagai and Madhai, women and men run from every side and talk with one
another.
Someone says, standing apart: "Look, look at the two of them! Now they shine like the sun — where has that sinful body gone?"

কেহ কহে আহা মরি মরি মরি ভাবে গর গর বৈসে বেরি বেরি কাঁদি উঠে ছুটে আঁখি-বারিধারা নিবারিতে নারে না ধরে ধৃতি ।
কেহ কহে হেন দেখ নিরুপম পুলকিত তনু কাঁপে ঘন ঘন ধূলায় ধূসর ধরণীতে পড়ি গড়ি যায় কিছু নাহিক স্মৃতি ॥

*keha kahe āhā mari mari mari bhābe gara gara baise beri beri kām̐di uṭhe chuṭe ām̐khi-bāridhārā nibārite nāre nā dhare dhṛti |*
*keha kahe hena dekha nirupama pulakita tanu kām̐pe ghana ghana dhūlāya dhūsara dharaṇīte paṛi gaṛi yāya kichu nāhika smṛti ||*

*Word for word:* keha kahe āhā mari mari mari — someone says: ah, ah; bhābe gara gara — seized by bhava; baise beri beri — keep sitting down; kām̐di uṭhe — burst into tears; chuṭe ām̐khi-bāri-dhārā — streams rush from the eyes; nibārite nāre — they cannot check them; nā dhare dhṛti — have no composure; keha kahe hena dekha nirupama — someone: look, an unheard-of thing; pulakita tanu kām̐pe ghana ghana — the bodies thrill and tremble constantly; dhūlāya dhūsara — grey with dust; dharaṇīte paṛi gaṛi yāya — fall to the ground and roll; kichu nāhika smṛti — remembering nothing

**22.2.** Someone says: "Ah, ah! Seized by bhava, they keep sitting down, bursting into tears — streams rush from their eyes, they
cannot check them, they are beside themselves."
Someone says: "Look, an unheard-of thing: their bodies thrill and constantly tremble; grey with dust, they fall to the ground and
roll, remembering nothing."[^17-66]

কেহ কহে কিবা গোরা-মুখশশী পানে চাহে জানি কত সুখে ভাসি হাসি-সুধাপানে উনমত হৈয়া লোটাইয়া পড়ে চরণতলে ।
কেহ কহে দেখ নিতাইচাঁদেরে চাহি হিয়া মাঝে কত খেদ করে দুখানি চরণ পরশিয়া করে করে অভিষেক আঁখের জলে ॥

*keha kahe kibā gorā-mukhaśaśī pāne cāhe jāni kata sukhe bhāsi hāsi-sudhāpāne unamata haiyā loṭāiyā paṛe caraṇatale |*
*keha kahe dekha nitāicām̐dere cāhi hiyā mājhe kata kheda kare dukhāni caraṇa paraśiyā kare kare abhiṣeka ām̐khera jale ||*

*Word for word:* keha kahe kibā gorā-mukha-śaśī pāne cāhe — someone: how they gaze at Gora's moon-face; jāni kata sukhe bhāsi — as though floating in great happiness; hāsi-sudhā-pāne unamata haiyā — drunk with the nectar of His smile; loṭāiyā paṛe caraṇa-tale — they fall rolling at His feet; keha kahe dekha nitāicām̐dere cāhi — someone: look, gazing at Nitaichand; hiyā mājhe kata kheda kare — how they lament in their hearts; dukhāni caraṇa paraśiyā kare — touching His two feet with their hands; kare abhiṣeka ām̐khera jale — bathe them (perform abhisheka) with tears

**22.3.** Someone says: "How they gaze at Gora's moon-face — as though floating in some great happiness! Drunk with the nectar of His
smile, they fall and roll at His feet."
Someone says: "Look, gazing at Nitaichand, how bitterly they repent in their hearts: touching His two feet, they bathe them —
perform abhisheka — with their tears."[^17-67]

কেহ কেহ দেখ অদ্বৈত তপসী গদাধর শ্রীবাসাদি পাশে বসি অতুল উলসে ফুলি ফুলি ফিরে লইয়া সবার চরণধূলি ।
কেহ কেহ দুহুঁ কাতর-অন্তরে এক ভিতে রহি দন্তে তৃণ ধরে নরহরি-পহুঁ পরিকর সহ কর কৃপা কহে দু বাহু তুলি ॥

*keha keha dekha advaita tapasī gadādhara śrībāsādi pāśe basi atula ulase phuli phuli phire laiyā sabāra caraṇadhūli |*
*keha keha duhum̐ kātara-antare eka bhite rahi dante tṛṇa dhare narahari-pahum̐ parikara saha kara kṛpā kahe du bāhu tuli ||*

*Word for word:* keha keha dekha — others: look; advaita tapasī gadādhara śrībāsa-ādi pāśe basi — sitting beside the ascetic Advaita, Gadadhara, Srivasa and others; atula ulase phuli phuli phire — they wander, swelling with peerless joy; laiyā sabāra caraṇa-dhūli — taking the dust of everyone's feet; keha keha duhum̐ kātara-antare — others: the two, broken-hearted; eka bhite rahi — standing aside; dante tṛṇa dhare — hold straw between their teeth; narahari-pahum̐ parikara saha — to Narahari's Lord with His associates; kara kṛpā kahe — say "have mercy"; du bāhu tuli — raising both arms

**22.4.** Others say: "Look, they sit beside the ascetic Advaita, beside Gadadhara, Srivasa and the others, they wander about, full of
peerless joy, and take the dust of everyone's feet."
Others: "There the two, with broken hearts, stand aside with straw between their teeth and, raising their arms, say to the poet
Narahari's Lord and His associates: 'Have mercy!'"[^17-68]

## 23. Narahari — "nācata gaura naṭana-paṇḍita-bara…" (GPT1 pp. 265–266, no. 56; BR)
*The dance of Gaura, best of skilled dancers: His body outshines kunkuma and lightning, His smile pours nectar, His glance crushes the
pride of Madanas; raising His arms He cries "Hari, Hari!"; the associates sing, instruments resound; He gives the world the treasure of
prema — only Narahari is left out. Raga meghamallara. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave);
Vrajabuli.*[^17-69]

নাচত গৌর নটন-পণ্ডিতবর ।
কুঙ্কুম-দামিনী-দাম-দমন তনু মণ্ডিত নিরুপম বিপুল পুলকভর ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*nācata gaura naṭana-paṇḍitabara |*
*kuṅkuma-dāminī-dāma-damana tanu maṇḍita nirupama bipula pulakabhara || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* nācata gaura naṭana-paṇḍita-bara — Gaura dances, best of skilled dancers; kuṅkuma-dāminī-dāma-damana tanu — a body shaming kunkuma and garlands of lightning; maṇḍita nirupama bipula pulaka-bhara — adorned with peerless abundant thrills

**23.1.** *(Refrain)* Gaura dances, the best of skilled dancers;
His body, shaming kunkuma and garlands of lightning, is adorned with peerless, abundant thrills.

অরুণ অধর মৃদু চাঁদবদন লস দশন কুন্দ লহু হাস অমিয় ঝর ।
নয়নকঞ্জ জনরঞ্জন রসময় চাহনি কত শত মদন-গরব-হর ॥

*aruṇa adhara mṛdu cām̐dabadana lasa daśana kunda lahu hāsa amiya jhara |*
*nayanakañja janarañjana rasamaya cāhani kata śata madana-garaba-hara ||*

*Word for word:* aruṇa adhara — red lips; mṛdu cām̐da-badana lasa — the tender moon-face shines; daśana kunda — teeth like kunda flowers; lahu hāsa amiya jhara — a light smile pours nectar; nayana-kañja jana-rañjana rasamaya — the lotus eyes, delight of the people, full of rasa; cāhani kata śata madana-garaba-hara — the glance crushes the pride of hundreds of Madanas

**23.2.** Red lips, the tender moon-face shining, teeth like kunda flowers, a light smile pouring nectar;
His lotus eyes, the delight of the people, are full of rasa; His glance crushes the pride of hundreds of Madanas.

কনক-মৃণাল-নিন্দি ভুজযুগ তুলি বোলত হরি হরি অন্তর গর গর ।
মঙ্গলময় কোমল সুললিত পদ বিবিধ ভঙ্গী সঞে ধরয়ে ধরণীপর ॥

*kanaka-mṛṇāla-nindi bhujayuga tuli bolata hari hari antara gara gara |*
*maṅgalamaya komala sulalita pada bibidha bhaṅgī sañe dharaye dharaṇīpara ||*

*Word for word:* kanaka-mṛṇāla-nindi bhuja-yuga tuli — raising arms that shame golden lotus stalks; bolata hari hari — cries "Hari, Hari"; antara gara gara — the heart overflowing; maṅgalamaya komala sulalita pada — auspicious, tender, graceful feet; bibidha bhaṅgī sañe — with manifold movements; dharaye dharaṇī-para — sets on the earth

**23.3.** Raising His arms, which put to shame golden lotus stalks, He cries "Hari, Hari!" — His heart overflowing;
His auspicious, tender, graceful feet He sets on the earth in manifold movements.

বাজত ঝাঁঝ সুখমক খোল কত গায়ত মধুর মধুর সুর-পরিকর ।
বিতরত প্রেমরতন-ধন জগভরি বঞ্চিত কুমতি এ নরহরি পামর ॥

*bājata jhām̐jha sukhamaka khola kata gāyata madhura madhura sura-parikara |*
*bitarata premaratana-dhana jagabhari bañcita kumati e narahari pāmara ||*

*Word for word:* bājata jhām̐jha — small cymbals sound; sukhamaka khola kata — khamaks, many khols; gāyata madhura madhura sura-parikara — the associates sing sweetly, sweetly; bitarata prema-ratana-dhana jaga-bhari — He gives away the treasure, the jewel of prema, throughout the world; bañcita kumati e narahari pāmara — only foolish, sinful Narahari is left out

**23.4.** Small cymbals, khamaks, many khols sound; the associates sing sweetly, sweetly;
He gives away throughout the world the treasure, the jewel of prema — only foolish, sinful Narahari is left out.

## 24. Narahari — "bali-kali-matta-mataṅgaja-maradana…" (GPT1 p. 266, no. 57; BR)
*The lion Gaura, crusher of the mad elephant Kali, dances in Nadia; the world is full of the cry "Jaya!", people run from all sides, the
associates sing, drums thunder, the earth trembles; giving prema, the Lord embraces the sinners. Raga devakiri. **Attribution:
probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave); Vrajabuli.*[^17-70]

বলি-কলি-মত্ত-মতঙ্গজ-মরদন গৌরসিংহ নাচত নদীয়ায় ।
জয় জয় রব সব ভুবন বিয়াপিত নিখিল লোক মিলি চৌদিকে ধায় ॥

*bali-kali-matta-mataṅgaja-maradana gaurasiṃha nācata nadīyāya |*
*jaya jaya raba saba bhubana biyāpita nikhila loka mili caudike dhāya ||*

*Word for word:* bali-kali-matta-mataṅgaja-maradana — crusher of the mighty mad elephant Kali; gaura-siṃha nācata nadīyāya — the lion Gaura dances in Nadia; jaya jaya raba saba bhubana biyāpita — the cry "jaya" fills the whole world; nikhila loka mili caudike dhāya — people gather and run from all sides

**24.1.** The crusher of the mighty mad elephant Kali, the lion Gaura, dances in Nadia;
the cry "Jaya, jaya!" fills the whole world, from everywhere people gather and come running.

গায়ত পরম প্রবল প্রিয় পরিকর কিন্নর-দুরগম তাল-তরঙ্গ ।
বাজত মুরজ মৃদঙ্গ দ্রিমিকি দ্রিমি দ্রিমি দ্রিমিকট ধিকট ধিলঙ্গ ॥

*gāyata parama prabala priya parikara kinnara-duragama tāla-taraṅga |*
*bājata muraja mṛdaṅga drimiki drimi drimi drimikaṭa dhikaṭa dhilaṅga ||*

*Word for word:* gāyata parama prabala priya parikara — the dear associates sing mightily and beautifully; kinnara-duragama tāla-taraṅga — waves of rhythm beyond the kinnaras; bājata muraja mṛdaṅga — muraja and mridanga thunder; drimiki drimi drimi drimikaṭa dhikaṭa dhilaṅga — rhythm syllables

**24.2.** The dear associates sing mightily and beautifully — waves of rhythms beyond even the kinnaras;
muraja and mridanga thunder: "drimiki drimi drimi, drimikat, dhikat, dhilanga".[^17-71]

কম্পই ধরণী ধরত পদপঙ্কজ ডগমগি অঙ্গভঙ্গী অনুপাম ।
লোচন তরুণ অরুণ রুচি গঞ্জই চাহনি চারু চমকে কত কাম ॥

*kampai dharaṇī dharata padapaṅkaja ḍagamagi aṅgabhaṅgī anupāma |*
*locana taruṇa aruṇa ruci gañjai cāhani cāru camake kata kāma ||*

*Word for word:* kampaī dharaṇī — the earth trembles; dharata pada-paṅkaja — as He sets down His lotus feet; ḍagamagi aṅga-bhaṅgī anupāma — peerless are the swaying movements of the body; locana taruṇa aruṇa ruci gañjaī — the eyes surpass the young dawn in beauty; cāhani cāru — at the lovely glance; camake kata kāma — many a Kama starts

**24.3.** The earth trembles as He sets down His lotus feet; peerless are the swaying movements of His body;
His eyes surpass the young dawn in beauty; at His lovely glance many a Kama starts.

শশধর-নিকর-নিন্দি মুখ মধুরিম হাসত লহু লহু অমিঞা উগারি ।
প্রেম বিতরি নরহরি-পহুঁ পামরে করই কোরে ভুজযুগ পসারি ॥

*śaśadhara-nikara-nindi mukha madhurima hāsata lahu lahu amiñā ugāri |*
*prema bitari narahari-pahum̐ pāmare karai kore bhujayuga pasāri ||*

*Word for word:* śaśadhara-nikara-nindi mukha madhurima — the sweetness of the face shames hosts of moons; hāsata lahu lahu — smiles gently; amiñā ugāri — pouring out nectar; prema bitari — giving prema; narahari-pahum̐ — Narahari's Lord; pāmare karaī kore — embraces the sinners; bhuja-yuga pasāri — spreading His arms

**24.4.** The sweetness of His face shames hosts of moons; He smiles gently, pouring out nectar;
giving prema, the poet Narahari's Lord, spreading His arms, embraces the sinners.

## 25. Narahari — "nācata gaura naṭana-janarañjana…" (GPT1 p. 266, no. 58; BR)
*Gaura's dance: hearing of the former love, He thrills and trembles; His eyes are full of tears, like pearls; seeing Gadadhara, He
embraces him again and speaks of the secret of His heart, unable to restrain Himself; the ocean of prema surges, the sinners float in
happiness — only Narahari it does not touch. Raga bhupali. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave);
Vrajabuli.*[^17-72]

নাচত গৌর নটন-জনরঞ্জন নিখিল-মদন-মদ-ভঞ্জন অঙ্গ ।
পুলকিত ললিত কম্প ঘন উনমত শুনইতে পূরুব-পীরিতি-পরসঙ্গ ॥

*nācata gaura naṭana-janarañjana nikhila-madana-mada-bhañjana aṅga |*
*pulakita lalita kampa ghana unamata śunaite pūruba-pīriti-parasaṅga ||*

*Word for word:* nācata gaura naṭana-jana-rañjana — Gaura dances, delighting the people by His dance; nikhila-madana-mada-bhañjana aṅga — a body crushing the pride of all Madanas; pulakita — thrilling; lalita kampa — gracefully trembling; ghana unamata — again and again beside Himself; śunaite pūruba-pīriti-parasaṅga — hearing the story of the former love

**25.1.** Gaura dances, delighting the people by His dance; His body crushes the pride of all the Madanas;
He thrills, gracefully trembling, again and again beside Himself, hearing the story of the former love.[^17-73]

লোচন অরুণ কমলদল ছল ছল জল ঝলকত জনু মোতিমদাম ।
হসইতে দশন বিজুরী সম চমকত ঢর ঢর মধুর অধর অনুপাম ॥

*locana aruṇa kamaladala chala chala jala jhalakata janu motimadāma |*
*hasaite daśana bijurī sama camakata ḍhara ḍhara madhura adhara anupāma ||*

*Word for word:* locana aruṇa kamala-dala chala chala — the eyes, red lotus petals, brim with tears; jala jhalakata janu motima-dāma — the moisture flashes like strings of pearls; hasaite daśana bijurī sama camakata — when He laughs, the teeth flash like lightning; ḍhara ḍhara madhura adhara anupāma — peerless are the soft sweet lips

**25.2.** His eyes, petals of a red lotus, are brimming with tears; the moisture flashes like strings of pearls;
when He laughs, His teeth flash like lightning — peerless are His soft, sweet lips.

কুঞ্জর-করবর-গরব-বিমোচন মঞ্জু বিপুল ভুজযুগল পসারি ।
নিরখি গদাধরে করই কোরে পুনঃ ভণই মরম ধৃতি ধরই না পারি ॥

*kuñjara-karabara-garaba-bimocana mañju bipula bhujayugala pasāri |*
*nirakhi gadādhare karai kore punaḥ bhaṇai marama dhṛti dharai nā pāri ||*

*Word for word:* kuñjara-karabara-garaba-bimocana — taking away the pride of an elephant's trunk; mañju bipula bhuja-yugala pasāri — spreading His lovely long arms; nirakhi gadādhare — seeing Gadadhara; karaī kore punaḥ — embraces him again; bhaṇaī marama — speaks of His heart; dhṛti dharaī nā pāri — cannot keep composure

**25.3.** Spreading His lovely long arms, which take away the pride of an elephant's trunk,
He sees Gadadhara, embraces him again, speaks of what lies in His heart — and cannot restrain Himself.[^17-74]

উথলই প্রেম-পয়োনিধি নিরুপম প্রবল তরঙ্গ রঙ্গ উপজায় ।
পামর পতিত দুখিত সুখে ভাসই নরহরি পাপী পরশ নহ তায় ॥

*uthalai prema-payonidhi nirupama prabala taraṅga raṅga upajāya |*
*pāmara patita dukhita sukhe bhāsai narahari pāpī paraśa naha tāya ||*

*Word for word:* uthalaī prema-payonidhi nirupama — the peerless ocean of prema surges; prabala taraṅga raṅga upajāya — raising mighty playful waves; pāmara patita dukhita sukhe bhāsaī — the sinful, fallen, afflicted float in happiness; narahari pāpī paraśa naha tāya — only sinful Narahari it does not touch

**25.4.** The peerless ocean of prema surges, raising mighty, playful waves;
the sinful, the fallen, the afflicted float in happiness — only sinful Narahari it does not touch.

## 26. Narahari — "nācata gaura parama-sukha-sadanā…" (GPT1 pp. 266–267, no. 59; BR)
*The dance of Gaura, abode of supreme happiness: His thrilling body crushes Madana's pride, His glance is full of compassion, His
smile steals the heart, His gait is like a royal elephant's; with faltering voice He cries "Hari, Hari!", gives away the treasure of
prema, fulfilling the desires of all — only the poet is left out. Raga natanarayana. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada
is in the BR (12th wave); Vrajabuli.*[^17-75]

নাচত গৌর পরম-সুখ-সদনা ।
অবিরল বিপুল পুলককুল ঝলমল সুললিত অঙ্গ মদন-মদ-কদনা ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*nācata gaura parama-sukha-sadanā |*
*abirala bipula pulakakula jhalamala sulalita aṅga madana-mada-kadanā || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* nācata gaura parama-sukha-sadanā — Gaura dances, abode of supreme happiness; abirala bipula pulaka-kula jhalamala — shining with constant abundant thrills; sulalita aṅga — the graceful body; madana-mada-kadanā — tormenting Madana, crushing his pride

**26.1.** *(Refrain)* Gaura dances, the abode of supreme happiness;
shining with constant, abundant thrills, His graceful body torments Madana, crushing his pride.

টলমল অমল কমলদল-লোচন চাহনি করুণ অরুণ-রুচি রুচিরে ।
নিরসি শরদশশী হসিত লপন লস দশন সুচিকণ হর চিত অচিরে ॥

*ṭalamala amala kamaladala-locana cāhani karuṇa aruṇa-ruci rucire |*
*nirasi śaradaśaśī hasita lapana lasa daśana sucikaṇa hara cita acire ||*

*Word for word:* ṭalamala amala kamala-dala-locana — the eyes, petals of a pure lotus, sway; cāhani karuṇa — the glance compassionate; aruṇa-ruci rucire — lovely with the beauty of dawn; nirasi śarada-śaśī — spurning the autumn moon; hasita lapana lasa — the face shines with a smile; daśana sucikaṇa — gleaming teeth; hara cita acire — instantly steal the heart

**26.2.** His eyes, petals of a pure lotus, sway; His glance, full of compassion, is lovely with the beauty of dawn;
His face, spurning the autumn moon, shines with a smile; His gleaming teeth instantly steal the heart.

গজবর-গরব-হরণ-গতি নব নব ধরইতে চরণ ধরণী অতি মুদিতা ।
গদ গদ হৃদয় বদত ঘন হরি হরি নিরুপম ভাব-বিভব-ভর উদিতা ॥

*gajabara-garaba-haraṇa-gati naba naba dharaite caraṇa dharaṇī ati muditā |*
*gada gada hṛdaya badata ghana hari hari nirupama bhāba-bibhaba-bhara uditā ||*

*Word for word:* gajabara-garaba-haraṇa-gati naba naba — an ever-new gait taking away the pride of a royal elephant; dharaite caraṇa — as He steps; dharaṇī ati muditā — the earth rejoices; gada gada hṛdaya — the heart overflowing, voice faltering; badata ghana hari hari — ceaselessly cries "Hari, Hari"; nirupama bhāba-bibhaba-bhara uditā — a peerless wealth of bhava has risen

**26.3.** His gait, ever new, takes away the pride of a royal elephant; as He steps, the earth rejoices;
His heart overflowing, His voice faltering, He ceaselessly cries "Hari, Hari!" — a peerless wealth of bhava has risen in Him.

উনমত অতুল রতনধন-বিতরণে হরল বিপদ যশ ভরল এ ভুবনে ।
পূরিল সকল-মনোরথ ইথে বঞ্চিত নরহরি বিফল জনম ধিক জীবনে ॥

*unamata atula ratanadhana-bitaraṇe harala bipada yaśa bharala e bhubane |*
*pūrila sakala-manoratha ithe bañcita narahari biphala janama dhika jībane ||*

*Word for word:* unamata — intoxicated; atula ratana-dhana-bitaraṇe — giving away the peerless treasure; harala bipada — removed misfortunes; yaśa bharala e bhubane — His fame filled this world; pūrila sakala-manoratha — fulfilled everyone's desires; ithe bañcita narahari — only Narahari is left out; biphala janama — vain is his birth; dhika jībane — shame on his life

**26.4.** Intoxicated, giving away the peerless treasure, He has removed misfortunes; His fame has filled this world;
He has fulfilled the desires of all — only Narahari is left out: vain is his birth, shame on his life![^17-76]

## 27. Narahari — "nācata śacī-tanaya gaura…" (GPT1 p. 267, no. 60; BR)
*The dance of Gaura, the son of Shachi: His sweetness charms the mind, His body thrills, His smile pours nectar, His anklets ring in
rhythm, Kama is ashamed before His movements; the world sings His virtues and sinks in happiness — only Narahari burns in the forest
fire of worldly existence. Raga nata. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave); Vrajabuli.*[^17-77]

নাচত শচীতনয় গৌর মাধুরী মন মোহে ।
কনকাচল-দলন দেহে পুলকাবলী শোহে ॥

*nācata śacītanaya gaura mādhurī mana mohe |*
*kanakācala-dalana dehe pulakābalī śohe ||*

*Word for word:* nācata śacī-tanaya gaura — Gaura, the son of Shachi, dances; mādhurī mana mohe — His sweetness charms the mind; kanakācala-dalana dehe — on the body that crushes a golden mountain; pulakābalī śohe — rows of thrills shine

**27.1.** Gaura, the son of Shachi, dances — His sweetness charms the mind;
on His body, which crushes a golden mountain, rows of thrills are shining.

ঝলমল বিধুবদন অমিয় বরষত মৃদুহাসে ।
চঞ্চল নয়নাঞ্চলে কত কত রস পরকাশে ॥

*jhalamala bidhubadana amiya baraṣata mṛduhāse |*
*cañcala nayanāñcale kata kata rasa parakāśe ||*

*Word for word:* jhalamala bidhu-badana — the moon-face gleams; amiya baraṣata mṛdu-hāse — pouring nectar in a gentle smile; cañcala nayanāñcale — with the corners of the restless eyes; kata kata rasa parakāśe — reveals so much rasa

**27.2.** His moon-face gleams, pouring nectar in a gentle smile;
with the corners of His restless eyes He reveals so much rasa!

পদতলে ধরু তাল ঝনন নূপুর ঘন বাজে ।
অভিনব বহু ভঙ্গী নিরখি মনমথ মরু লাজে ॥

*padatale dharu tāla jhanana nūpura ghana bāje |*
*abhinaba bahu bhaṅgī nirakhi manamatha maru lāje ||*

*Word for word:* pada-tale dharu tāla — with His feet He keeps the rhythm; jhanana nūpura ghana bāje — the anklets ring resoundingly; abhinaba bahu bhaṅgī nirakhi — seeing many new movements; manamatha maru lāje — Kama dies of shame

**27.3.** With His feet He keeps the rhythm, the anklets ring out resoundingly;
seeing His many new movements, Kama dies of shame.

গায়ত গুণ জগজন নিমগন সুখ-পরবাহে ।
বঞ্চিত নরহরি দীনহীন দহে ভব-দব-দাহে ॥

*gāyata guṇa jagajana nimagana sukha-parabāhe |*
*bañcita narahari dīnahīna dahe bhaba-daba-dāhe ||*

*Word for word:* gāyata guṇa jaga-jana — the people of the world sing the virtues; nimagana sukha-parabāhe — sink in a stream of happiness; bañcita narahari dīnahīna — only deprived, lowly Narahari; dahe bhaba-daba-dāhe — burns in the forest fire of worldly existence

**27.4.** The people of the world sing His virtues, sinking in a stream of happiness;
only deprived, lowly Narahari burns in the forest fire of worldly existence.[^17-78]

[^17-63]: GPT1 — p. 265, no. 54 ("beragupta"); GPT2 — sec. 4.2, no. 54 (catalogue: NG-146). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 891; ed. 1960,
vv. 2634–2637), right after the pada "biharata surasarita-tīra" (no. 7). Not in PK, KGC, PS. B.
[^17-64]: "Stealing the hearts of women" (ramaṇī-manacora) — an epithet of Krishna; the motif of the townswomen (note 15).
[^17-65]: GPT1 — p. 265, no. 55 (gurjari); GPT2 — sec. 4.2, no. 55. In the catalogue the first line of this pada merged with another, a
wedding pada (NG-030: GPT2 2.3, no. 11 "ki ānanda nadīyā-nagare" — on Nimai's wedding); here a new row NG-243. BR — 12th wave (ed.
1912, p. 898; ed. 1960, vv. ≈2725–2732), in the account of Jagai and Madhai. GPT2 index — Chakravarti (p. 169, no. 55). Not in PK, KGC,
PS. B. The deliverance of Jagai and Madhai — CB Madhya 13; CC Adi 17.
[^17-66]: "Their bodies thrill… roll" — signs of prema (sattvika-bhavas) awakened in the former evildoers.
[^17-67]: Madhai wounded Nityananda by throwing a shard of an earthen pot at Him (CB Madhya 13); the brothers' repentance before Nityananda —
CB Madhya 13–15 (Madhai builds a ghat on the Ganga and bows down to everyone).
[^17-68]: "Straw between the teeth" (dante tṛṇa) — a sign of humility and of begging forgiveness. "The poet Narahari's Lord" — see note 44.
[^17-69]: GPT1 — pp. 265–266, no. 56 (meghamallara); GPT2 — sec. 4.2, no. 56 (catalogue: NG-147). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 901; ed.
1960, vv. 2765–2768). Not in PK, KGC, PS. B.
[^17-70]: GPT1 — p. 266, no. 57 (debakiri); GPT2 — sec. 4.2, no. 57. The pada was not in the catalogue (new row NG-244; BD-007 referred to it
as "BR p. 901 — a pada of Narahari"). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 901; ed. 1960, vv. ≈2761–2764), before the preceding one. Not in PK,
KGC, PS. B.
[^17-71]: Rhythm syllables of the drum; "beyond even the kinnaras" (kinnara-duragama) — the celestial singers. The reading "drimiki drimi drimi"
follows GPT1 and GPT2 (the recognition is faulty).
[^17-72]: GPT1 — p. 266, no. 58 (bhupali); GPT2 — sec. 4.2, no. 58. The pada was not in the catalogue (new row NG-245). BR — 12th wave
(ed. 1912, p. 902; ed. 1960, vv. 2769–2772). Not in PK, KGC, PS. B.
[^17-73]: "The story of the former love" (pūruba-pīriti-parasaṅga) — the account of the love of Radha and Krishna in Vraja: hearing it, the
Lord enters into bhava.
[^17-74]: Gadadhara is Radha in Krishna-lila (note 20). The Lord's feelings for Gadadhara are the prema of Krishna-lila, not a worldly
attachment.
[^17-75]: GPT1 — pp. 266–267, no. 59 (natanarayana); GPT2 — sec. 4.2, no. 59 (catalogue: NG-148). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 902; ed.
1960, vv. 2773–2776). Not in PK, KGC, PS. B.
[^17-76]: "Has removed misfortunes" (harala bipada) — freed the living beings from the calamities of worldly existence. The poet's self-reproach
is the usual ending of the padas of this cycle.
[^17-77]: GPT1 — p. 267, no. 60 (nata; in GPT2 unnumbered, after no. 59); GPT2 — sec. 4.2, after no. 59. The pada was not in the
catalogue (new row NG-246). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 903; ed. 1960, vv. 2779–2782). Not in PK, KGC, PS. B.
[^17-78]: "The forest fire of worldly existence" (bhaba-daba-dāha) — the image of samsara as a burning forest (cf. Vishvanatha Chakravarti's Sri
Gurvashtaka, 1: "saṃsāra-dābānala…").

## 28. Narahari — "āju śaṅkara-carita śuni…" (GPT1 pp. 283–284, no. 22; BR)
*The Lord in the mood of Shiva: hearing a song of Shankara's deeds, the son of Shachi became Shankara — a radiance brighter than the
silver mountain, a body smeared with ashes, a horn in His hand, the damaru sounding, three eyes, serpents for ornaments and clothes,
matted locks on His head. Raga malavashri. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave, the account of the
singer of Shiva); Vrajabuli.*[^17-79]

আজু শঙ্করচরিত শুনি শচীতনয় শঙ্কর ভেল ।
রজত-গিরি জিনি জ্যোতি ডগমগ জগত-ধৃতি হরি নেল ॥

*āju śaṅkaracarita śuni śacītanaya śaṅkara bhela |*
*rajata-giri jini jyoti ḍagamaga jagata-dhṛti hari nela ||*

*Word for word:* āju śaṅkara-carita śuni — today, hearing of Shankara's deeds; śacī-tanaya śaṅkara bhela — the son of Shachi became Shankara; rajata-giri jini — surpassing the silver mountain; jyoti ḍagamaga — the radiance sways; jagata-dhṛti hari nela — has stolen the composure of the world

**28.1.** Today, hearing of Shankara's deeds, the son of Shachi became Shankara;
His radiance sways, surpassing the silver mountain — He has stolen the composure of the world.[^17-80]

ভসম-ভূষিত অঙ্গ-ভঙ্গিম অনঙ্গ-মদ-ভর-হারী ।
রুচির কর গহি শৃঙ্গ বায়ত ডমরু-রব রুচিকারী ॥

*bhasama-bhūṣita aṅga-bhaṅgima anaṅga-mada-bhara-hārī |*
*rucira kara gahi śṛṅga bāyata ḍamaru-raba rucikārī ||*

*Word for word:* bhasama-bhūṣita — adorned with ashes; aṅga-bhaṅgima — the graceful body; anaṅga-mada-bhara-hārī — taking away Ananga's pride; rucira kara gahi — holding in the lovely hand; śṛṅga bāyata — blows the horn; ḍamaru-raba rucikārī — the sound of the damaru delights

**28.2.** His body, adorned with ashes, is graceful — it takes away Ananga's pride;
in His lovely hand He holds a horn and blows it; charmingly the damaru sounds.

লোল ললিত ত্রিলোচনাঞ্চল লসত বয়ন-ময়ঙ্ক ।
গণ্ডমণ্ডল বিমল মৃদুতর ভালে ভুরুযুগ বঙ্ক ॥

*lola lalita trilocanāñcala lasata bayana-mayaṅka |*
*gaṇḍamaṇḍala bimala mṛdutara bhāle bhuruyuga baṅka ||*

*Word for word:* lola lalita trilocanāñcala — restless, lovely are the corners of the three eyes; lasata bayana-mayaṅka — the moon-face shines; gaṇḍa-maṇḍala bimala mṛdutara — the cheeks pure and tender; bhāle bhuru-yuga baṅka — on the brow the eyebrows curve

**28.3.** Restless and lovely are the corners of His three eyes, His moon-face shines;
pure and tender are His cheeks, on His brow the eyebrows curve.

বিপুল পন্নগ-ভূষণাম্বর চরম পরম উজোর ।
শিরসি মঞ্জু জটা লটপট-ভর পেখি নরহরি ভোর ॥

*bipula pannaga-bhūṣaṇāmbara carama parama ujora |*
*śirasi mañju jaṭā laṭapaṭa-bhara pekhi narahari bhora ||*

*Word for word:* bipula pannaga-bhūṣaṇāmbara — huge serpents for ornaments and garments; carama parama ujora — the hide shines brightly; śirasi mañju jaṭā laṭapaṭa-bhara — on the head lovely tangled heavy matted locks; pekhi narahari bhora — seeing this, Narahari is beside himself

**28.4.** Huge serpents are His ornaments and garments, the hide shines brightly;
on His head lovely, tangled, heavy matted locks — seeing this, Narahari is beside himself.[^17-81]

## 29. Narahari Dasa — "ki bhābe gaurāṅga mora bhābita thāke…" (GPT1 p. 292, no. 52)
*The Lord in the mood of Krishna: seized by bhava, He calls "Radha!", the Ganga reminds Him of the Yamuna, a flower garden — of
Vrindavana; with His companions He plays, standing in the threefold bend and asking for the flute; taking Gadadhara for Radha, He
says something unknown to him and does not take His eyes off his face; Gadadhara, understanding the bhava, stands at His left. Raga
mallara. **Attribution: probably Sarakara** — the GPT2 index assigns the page to Sarakara; not in the BR; simple Bengali payar; the
content is close to Sarakara's pada PK 2122.*[^17-82]

কি ভাবে গৌরাঙ্গ মোর ভাবিত থাকে ।
ক্ষণে ক্ষণে ভাবাবেশে রাধা বলি ডাকে ॥

*ki bhābe gaurāṅga mora bhābita thāke |*
*kṣaṇe kṣaṇe bhābābeśe rādhā bali ḍāke ||*

*Word for word:* ki bhābe — by what bhava; gaurāṅga mora — my Gauranga; bhābita thāke — is seized; kṣaṇe kṣaṇe — again and again; bhābābeśe — in bhava; rādhā bali ḍāke — calls "Radha"

**29.1.** By what bhava is my Gauranga seized?
Again and again, in bhava, He calls: "Radha!"

যমুনারে পড়ে মনে ভাগীরথী হেরি ।
ফুলবনে বৃন্দাবন ভাবে মনে করি ॥

*yamunāre paṛe mane bhāgīrathī heri |*
*phulabane bṛndābana bhābe mane kari ||*

*Word for word:* yamunāre paṛe mane — He remembers the Yamuna; bhāgīrathī heri — seeing the Bhagirathi; phula-bane — a flower garden; bṛndābana bhābe mane kari — He takes in His heart for Vrindavana

**29.2.** Seeing the Bhagirathi, He remembers the Yamuna;
a flowering garden He takes in His heart for Vrindavana.[^17-83]

সহচর সঙ্গে পহুঁ করে কত রঙ্গ ।
মুরলী মুরলী কহে হইয়া ত্রিভঙ্গ ॥

*sahacara saṅge pahum̐ kare kata raṅga |*
*muralī muralī kahe haiyā tribhaṅga ||*

*Word for word:* sahacara saṅge — with His companions; pahum̐ kare kata raṅga — the Lord begins so many games; muralī muralī kahe — says "the flute, the flute"; haiyā tribhaṅga — standing in the threefold bend

**29.3.** With His companions the Lord begins so many games;
standing in the threefold bend, He says: "The flute, the flute!"[^17-84]

রাধা-ভাবে গদাধরে কি জানি কি কহে ।
অনিমিখে পণ্ডিতের মুখপানে চাহে ॥

*rādhā-bhābe gadādhare ki jāni ki kahe |*
*animikhe paṇḍitera mukhapāne cāhe ||*

*Word for word:* rādhā-bhābe gadādhare — taking Gadadhara for Radha; ki jāni ki kahe — who knows what He says; animikhe — without blinking; paṇḍitera mukha-pāne cāhe — gazes at the Pandita's face

**29.4.** Taking Gadadhara for Radha, who knows what He says to him;
without blinking He gazes at the Pandita's face.

ভাব বুঝি গদাধর রহে বাম পাশে ।
না বুঝয়ে ইহ রস নরহরি দাসে ॥

*bhāba bujhi gadādhara rahe bāma pāśe |*
*nā bujhaye iha rasa narahari dāse ||*

*Word for word:* bhāba bujhi — understanding the bhava; gadādhara rahe bāma pāśe — Gadadhara stands at the left; nā bujhaye iha rasa — does not comprehend this rasa; narahari dāse — Narahari Dasa

**29.5.** Understanding the bhava, Gadadhara stands at His left;
this rasa Narahari Dasa does not comprehend.[^17-85]

[^17-79]: GPT1 — pp. 283–284, section on bhavavesha (4.3), no. 22 (malavashri); GPT2 — sec. 4.3, no. 22 (catalogue: NG-153). BR — 12th
wave (ed. 1912, p. 834; ed. 1960, vv. 1841–1844): Ishana tells Srinivasa that here a singer of Shiva sang and danced, playing the
damaru, and the Lord, in the mood of Maheshvara, crying "I am Mahesha!", climbed onto his shoulders (a retelling of CB Madhya 8). GPT2
index — Chakravarti. Not in PK, KGC, PS. B. Before it in the GPT (no. 21) stands a pada signed Narahari about the Lord in the mood of
Balarama (for the next chapter).
[^17-80]: The mood of Shiva is one of the moods the Lord displayed in Navadvipa (CB Madhya 8; cf. the moods of Varaha, Nrisimha, Balarama):
the Lord is the source of all His manifestations, and Shiva is His partial manifestation and the greatest of Vaishnavas (Bhag.
12.13.16; Brahma-samhita 5.45). This is not God turning into a demigod: hearing of His devotee, the Lord takes on his form and mood.
The silver mountain — Kailasa.
[^17-81]: Shiva's attributes: ashes, the horn (shringa) and the small drum damaru, the third eye, serpents, a hide (of tiger or elephant),
matted hair (jata).
[^17-82]: GPT1 — p. 292, no. 52 (mallara; the recognition is incomplete, text from GPT1 and GPT2); GPT2 — sec. 4.3, no. 52. The pada was
not in the catalogue (new row NG-247). Not in BR, PK, KGC, PS. The GPT2 index assigns pp. 187–188 to Sarakara (here stand no. 51 = PK
853, a pada of Sarakara, and this one). The content repeats the motifs of Sarakara's pada PK 2122 (chapter 3, no. 1; Majumdar places
it in the Navadvipa lila): the Ganga seems the Yamuna, a garden Vrindavana, the Lord is in the mood of Krishna with Gadadhara as Radha. C.
[^17-83]: Bhagirathi — the Ganga. Cf. Rupa Gosvami, Chaitanyashtaka (Stava-mala) 1.6 and CC Antya 14–15 — in Puri the sea seems to the Lord
the Yamuna, and the groves Vrindavana.
[^17-84]: The threefold bend (tribhaṅga) — Krishna's pose with the flute. Here the Lord is in the mood of Krishna, not of Radha.
[^17-85]: Gadadhara is Radha in Krishna-lila (note 20): understanding the Lord's bhava, he stands at the left, where Radha stands beside
Krishna. This is the prema of Vraja, not a worldly feeling. "Does not comprehend" — the poet's humility.

---

# Chapter 18. Appendix. Padas signed "Narahari" from the Gaura-pada-tarangini — II: kirtana and dance (conclusion), bhavavesha, the festivals of the year, prarthanas

*Continuation of the appendix (the introductory note on the two Naraharis, on the arguments for attribution and on the marks in the
headings is in ch. 17). Chapter 18: the end of the cycle of kirtana and dance in Navadvipa (GPT, section 4.2), two padas on the
Lord's bhavas (the bhava of Balarama; the Lord in the bhava of Radha waiting for Krishna), the festivals of the year — the "twelve-month
lila" (GPT, section 5.1: the swing-jhulana, Janmashtami and Nanda-utsava, Radhashtami, the remembrance of the rasa-lila, spring and
Holi) and two prarthanas. Before translation the "Narahari" signatures in these sections were checked throughout in GPT1 (tesseract
recognition): the catalogue had missed several more padas. The base text is GPT1 (doubtful places from the scan), collated with GPT2 and
with the Bhakti-ratnakara (eds. 1912 and 1960; almost all padas of the chapter are in its 12th wave); PK, KGC, PS and the
Gita-chandrodaya have been checked. Padas signed "Ghanashyama" (the same Narahari Chakravarti) are not included in the appendix. The
notes of the GPT editors are not reproduced.*

## 1. Narahari — "kibā khola karatāla bāje…" (GPT1 p. 267, no. 61; BR)
*Kirtana: the khol and karatalas sound, the associates stand around; they sing the sweet lila at which wood and stone melt; Gaura
dances, and no one knows by what bhava He is seized; His body thrills, streams of tears flow from His eyes; He embraces the fallen and
gives the treasure of prema to everyone — only the poet is left out. Raga nata. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is
in the BR (12th wave); short payar with Vrajabuli forms.*[^18-1]

কিবা খোল করতাল বাজে ।
চারি পাশে পরিকর সাজে ॥

*kibā khola karatāla bāje |*
*cāri pāśe parikara sāje ||*

*Word for word:* kibā khola karatāla bāje — how the khol and karatalas sound; cāri pāśe — on all four sides; parikara sāje — the associates are adorned

**1.1.** How the khol and karatalas resound!
All around stand the adorned associates.

আজু গায়ত মধুর লীলা ।
শুনি দরবয়ে দারুশিলা ॥

*āju gāyata madhura līlā |*
*śuni darabaye dāruśilā ||*

*Word for word:* āju gāyata — today they sing; madhura līlā — the sweet lila; śuni — hearing; darabaye — melt; dāru-śilā — wood and stone

**1.2.** Today they sing the sweet lila —
hearing it, wood and stone melt.

রঙ্গে নাচয়ে সুন্দর গোরা ।
কেবা জানে কিবা ভাবে ভোরা ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*raṅge nācaye sundara gorā |*
*kebā jāne kibā bhābe bhorā || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* raṅge nācaye — joyfully dances; sundara gorā — beautiful Gora; kebā jāne — who knows; kibā bhābe bhorā — by what bhava He is overwhelmed

**1.3.** *(Refrain)* Joyfully the beautiful Gora dances —
who knows by what bhava He is seized?

নব পুলক-বলিত তনু ।
শোহে কনক-পনস জনু ॥

*naba pulaka-balita tanu |*
*śohe kanaka-panasa janu ||*

*Word for word:* naba pulaka-balita tanu — the body covered with fresh thrills; śohe — shines; kanaka-panasa janu — like a golden jackfruit

**1.4.** His body is covered with fresh thrills —
as if a golden jackfruit were shining.[^18-2]

সুরসরিত-প্রবাহ পারা ।
দুটী নয়নে বহয়ে ধারা ॥

*surasarita-prabāha pārā |*
*duṭī nayane bahaye dhārā ||*

*Word for word:* sura-sarita-prabāha pārā — like the current of the celestial river (Ganga); duṭī nayane — from both eyes; bahaye dhārā — streams flow

**1.5.** Like the current of the celestial river,
streams flow from both His eyes.[^18-3]

ঘন ঘন ভুজযুগ তুলি ।
গরজয়ে হরি হরি বলি ॥

*ghana ghana bhujayuga tuli |*
*garajaye hari hari bali ||*

*Word for word:* ghana ghana — again and again; bhuja-yuga tuli — raising both arms; garajaye — He thunders; hari hari bali — saying "Hari, Hari"

**1.6.** Again and again raising both arms,
He thunders: "Hari, Hari!"

অতি পতিত পামরে হেরি ।
ধরি কোরে করে বেরি বেরি ॥

*ati patita pāmare heri |*
*dhari kore kare beri beri ||*

*Word for word:* ati patita pāmare heri — seeing the most fallen and sinful; dhari kore kare — He takes them into His embrace; beri beri — again and again

**1.7.** Seeing the most fallen and sinful,
again and again He clasps them in His embrace.

প্রেমধন দেই জনে জনে ।
ছাড়ি একা নরহরি দীনে ॥

*premadhana dei jane jane |*
*chāṛi ekā narahari dīne ||*

*Word for word:* prema-dhana dei — gives the treasure of prema; jane jane — to each person; chāṛi — leaving out; ekā narahari dīne — the one wretched Narahari

**1.8.** To each and every one He gives the treasure of prema,
passing over only one wretched Narahari.[^18-4]

[^18-1]: GPT1 — p. 267, no. 61 (nata); GPT2 — sec. 4.2, no. 61 (catalogue: NG-249). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 903; ed. 1960,
vv. 2783–2790): Ishana, showing Srinivasa Navadvipa, quotes it at the house of Sanjaya, "dear to the Lord", where Vishvambhara
danced, right after the pada "nācata śacītanaya gaura" (chapter 17, no. 27). The GPT2 index assigns the page to Chakravarti. Not in
PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. The Lord's dancing in kirtana in Navadvipa — CB Madhya 8, 23; CC Adi 17.
[^18-2]: Thrills (pulaka) are one of the sattvika-bhavas, signs of prema: the hairs stand up like the spikes on the rind of a jackfruit
(panasa).
[^18-3]: "The celestial river" (surasarit) is the Ganga.
[^18-4]: Self-reproach is the usual ending of the padas of this cycle (cf. chapter 17, nos. 13–27): the poet regards himself as the only
one passed over by the mercy given to all.

## 2. Narahari — "bhubanamohana gorācām̐da…" (GPT1 p. 268, no. 63; BR)
*Dancing in prema: Gorachand, enchanter of the world, dances weeping, cries "Hari!", embraces the fallen, floods everyone with His
rasa, throws Himself on the ground and rolls in the dust; seeing this, all living beings weep. Raga varadi or dhanashi. **Attribution:
probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave), though its language is a simple Bengali payar.*[^18-5]

ভুবনমোহন গোরাচাঁদ ।
অখিল লোকের মনোফাঁদ ॥

*bhubanamohana gorācām̐da |*
*akhila lokera manophām̐da ||*

*Word for word:* bhubana-mohana — enchanter of the world; gorā-cām̐da — Gorachand (Gora the moon); akhila lokera — of all people; mano-phām̐da — the snare of hearts

**2.1.** Gorachand, the enchanter of the world —
a net that snares the hearts of all people.[^18-6]

নাচে পহু প্রেমের আবেশে ।
অরুণ-নয়ন জলে ভাসে ॥

*nāce pahu premera ābeśe |*
*aruṇa-nayana jale bhāse ||*

*Word for word:* nāce pahu — the Lord dances; premera ābeśe — absorbed in prema; aruṇa-nayana — reddened eyes; jale bhāse — swim in tears

**2.2.** The Lord dances, seized by prema;
His reddened eyes swim in tears.

ভুজ তুলি হরি হরি বোলে ।
পতিতে ধরিয়া করে কোলে ॥

*bhuja tuli hari hari bole |*
*patite dhariyā kare kole ||*

*Word for word:* bhuja tuli — raising His arms; hari hari bole — cries "Hari, Hari"; patite dhariyā — seizing the fallen; kare kole — takes them to His breast

**2.3.** Raising His arms, He cries: "Hari, Hari!" —
and, seizing the fallen, clasps them to His breast.

নিজ রসে সভায় ভাসায় ।
চারি পাশে পারিষদ গায় ॥

*nija rase sabhāya bhāsāya |*
*cāri pāśe pāriṣada gāya ||*

*Word for word:* nija rase — with His own rasa; sabhāya bhāsāya — floods everyone; cāri pāśe — all around; pāriṣada gāya — the associates sing

**2.4.** With His own rasa He floods everyone;
all around His associates sing.

সুকোমল অঙ্গ আছাড়িয়া ।
গড়ি যায় ধুলায় পড়িয়া ॥

*sukomala aṅga āchāṛiyā |*
*gaṛi yāya dhulāya paṛiyā ||*

*Word for word:* sukomala aṅga — His most tender body; āchāṛiyā — flinging down; gaṛi yāya — He rolls; dhulāya paṛiyā — falling into the dust

**2.5.** Flinging His most tender body to the ground,
He falls and rolls in the dust.

দেখিয়া সকল জীব কাঁদে ।
নরহরি হিয়া নাহি বাঁধে ॥

*dekhiyā sakala jība kām̐de |*
*narahari hiyā nāhi bām̐dhe ||*

*Word for word:* dekhiyā — seeing this; sakala jība kām̐de — all living beings weep; narahari hiyā — Narahari's heart; nāhi bām̐dhe — cannot hold firm

**2.6.** Seeing this, all living beings weep;
Narahari's heart finds no rest.

[^18-5]: GPT1 — p. 268, no. 63 (varadi or dhanashi); GPT2 — sec. 4.2, no. 63 (catalogue: NG-149). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 904; ed.
1960, vv. 2795–2800), at the same place, the house of Sanjaya; after the pada — "under this tree the Lord stayed a while and went on
by the road to the Ganga". Not in PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^18-6]: Marginal variants of GPT1: "purifier of the world" instead of "enchanter of the world", "of all living beings" instead of "of
all people". These are the readings of the second occurrence of the same pada in the BR: Narahari Chakravarti quotes it twice — at the
house of Sanjaya (vv. 2795–2800) and at the house of Srivasa (ed. 1960, v. 3397 ff., "bhubanapābana gorācām̐da | akhila jībera mana-phām̐da").

## 3. Narahari — "nācata gaurakiśora. suradhunītīre ujora…" (GPT1 p. 268, no. 65; BR)
*Dancing on the bank of the Suradhuni: young Gaura with hundreds of associates, making no distinction between His own and others, gives
away the treasure of prema, weeps in a peerless bhava and, speaking in a faltering voice, takes Gadadhara by the hand. Raga dhanashi.
**Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave); short payar with Vrajabuli forms.*[^18-7]

নাচত গৌরকিশোর ।
সুরধুনীতীরে উজোর ॥

*nācata gaurakiśora |*
*suradhunītīre ujora ||*

*Word for word:* nācata — dances; gaura-kiśora — young Gaura; suradhunī-tīre — on the bank of the Suradhuni (Ganga); ujora — shining, illumining

**3.1.** Young Gaura dances,
illumining the bank of the Suradhuni.

কত শত পরিকর সঙ্গ ।
কীর্তনে অতুলিত অঙ্গ ॥

*kata śata parikara saṅga |*
*kīrtane atulita aṅga ||*

*Word for word:* kata śata parikara saṅga — with Him hundreds of associates; kīrtane — in the kirtana; atulita aṅga — peerless limbs (movements)

**3.2.** With Him are hundreds of associates;
in the kirtana His movements are peerless.[^18-8]

নিজ পর কাছু না জান ।
প্রেমরতন করু দান ॥

*nija para kāchu nā jāna |*
*premaratana karu dāna ||*

*Word for word:* nija para — own and others; kāchu nā jāna — He does not distinguish at all; prema-ratana — the jewel of prema; karu dāna — He gives away

**3.3.** Making no distinction between His own and others,
He gives away the treasure of prema.

নিরুপম ভাবে বিভোর ।
অরুণ-নয়নে ঝরে লোর ॥

*nirupama bhābe bibhora |*
*aruṇa-nayane jhare lora ||*

*Word for word:* nirupama bhābe — in a peerless bhava; bibhora — absorbed; aruṇa-nayane — from the reddened eyes; jhare lora — tears flow

**3.4.** Immersed in a peerless bhava,
He sheds tears from His reddened eyes.

কহি কত গদ গদ বাণী ।
ধরই গদাধর-পাণি ॥

*kahi kata gada gada bāṇī |*
*dharai gadādhara-pāṇi ||*

*Word for word:* kahi kata — uttering so many; gada gada bāṇī — words in a faltering voice; dharai — He takes; gadādhara-pāṇi — Gadadhara's hand

**3.5.** Uttering so many words in a faltering voice,
He takes Gadadhara by the hand.[^18-9]

ঘন ঘন কাঁপয়ে অঙ্গ ।
নরহরি কি বুঝব রঙ্গ ॥

*ghana ghana kām̐paye aṅga |*
*narahari ki bujhaba raṅga ||*

*Word for word:* ghana ghana — again and again; kām̐paye aṅga — the body trembles; narahari — Narahari; ki bujhaba raṅga — what will he understand of this play

**3.6.** Again and again His body trembles —
what can Narahari grasp of this play?

[^18-7]: GPT1 — p. 268, no. 65 (dhanashi); GPT2 — sec. 4.2, no. 65 (catalogue: NG-250). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 912; ed. 1960,
vv. 2889–2894): Ishana shows the bank of the Ganga where the Lord danced with His associates and quotes several padas in a row
(including the next one, no. 4); after them — "having spread the good fortune of the Ganga, the Lord went home this way with His
associates". Not in PK, KGC, PS. The Gita-chandrodaya (ed. 1948, no. 30) has a pada with the same opening ("heranu gaurakiśora |
suradhanītīre ujora"), but it is a different song — signed by Kavishekhara Raya and with a different text after the first couplet; the
common opening is probably a current formula. B.
[^18-8]: The BR reads: "in the kirtana — peerless play" (raṅga instead of aṅga).
[^18-9]: Gadadhara Pandita is Radha in Krishna-lila (cf. chapter 17, note 20): in the dance the Lord turns to him in the bhava of
Krishna-lila. This is the prema of Vraja, not worldly attachment.

## 4. Narahari Dasa — "gaura suradhunītīre nācata…" (GPT1 p. 268, no. 66; BR)
*Dancing on the bank of the Suradhuni: Gaura's body takes away the pride of a golden mountain, His locks are adorned with flowers, at the
sight of His arms and breast Kama loses his peace; He walks with the gait of a king of elephants, from His lotus eyes flow as it were
two Gangas, the earth rejoices at the rhythm of His feet. Raga gauri. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR
(12th wave); Vrajabuli with chains of assonance.*[^18-10]

গৌর সুরধুনীতীরে নাচত সুঘড় পরিকর সঙ্গ ।
হেম-ভূধর-গৌরব-ভর-হর পরম মধুরিম অঙ্গ ॥

*gaura suradhunītīre nācata sughaṛa parikara saṅga |*
*hema-bhūdhara-gauraba-bhara-hara parama madhurima aṅga ||*

*Word for word:* gaura suradhunī-tīre nācata — Gaura dances on the bank of the Suradhuni (Ganga); sughaṛa parikara saṅga — with skilful associates; hema-bhūdhara-gauraba-bhara-hara — removing the pride of a golden mountain; parama madhurima aṅga — a body of supreme sweetness

**4.1.** Gaura dances on the bank of the Suradhuni with His skilful associates;
His body, full of supreme sweetness, takes away the pride of a golden mountain.

অতুল কুন্তল বলিত কেতকী কুন্দ কুসুম সুরঙ্গ ।
বাহু বলনি বিশাল বক্ষ বিলোকি বিকল অনঙ্গ ॥

*atula kuntala balita ketakī kunda kusuma suraṅga |*
*bāhu balani biśāla bakṣa biloki bikala anaṅga ||*

*Word for word:* atula kuntala — peerless locks; balita ketakī kunda kusuma suraṅga — adorned with ketaki, kunda and bright flowers; bāhu balani — the curve of the arms; biśāla bakṣa — the broad chest; biloki — seeing; bikala anaṅga — Ananga (Kama) is agitated

**4.2.** His peerless locks are adorned with ketaki, kunda jasmine and bright flowers;
seeing the curve of His arms and His broad chest, Ananga loses his peace.[^18-11]

ভাবে গরগর গমন গজপতি গঞ্জি গরজে অভঙ্গ ।
কঞ্জ-লোচনে লোর ঢরকত প্রকট জনু যুগ গঙ্গ ॥

*bhābe garagara gamana gajapati gañji garaje abhaṅga |*
*kañja-locane lora ḍharakata prakaṭa janu yuga gaṅga ||*

*Word for word:* bhābe garagara — overwhelmed by bhava; gamana gajapati gañji — with a gait that shames the king of elephants; garaje abhaṅga — He thunders unceasingly; kañja-locane — from the lotus eyes; lora ḍharakata — tears roll; prakaṭa janu yuga gaṅga — as if two Gangas appeared

**4.3.** Seized by bhava, He steps, putting to shame the king of elephants, and thunders unceasingly;
tears roll from His lotus eyes — as if two Gangas had appeared.

তরল পদতলে তাল ধরইতে ধরণী অধিক উমঙ্গ ।
দাস নরহরি করত জয় জয় কার কি কহব রঙ্গ ॥

*tarala padatale tāla dharaite dharaṇī adhika umaṅga |*
*dāsa narahari karata jaya jaya kāra ki kahaba raṅga ||*

*Word for word:* tarala pada-tale — with the unsteady soles; tāla dharaite — as He keeps the rhythm; dharaṇī adhika umaṅga — the earth rejoices exceedingly; dāsa narahari — Narahari Dasa; karata jaya jaya kāra — cries "glory, glory"; ki kahaba raṅga — what shall I say of the play

**4.4.** When His unsteady feet keep the rhythm, the earth rejoices beyond measure;
Narahari Dasa cries: "Glory, glory!" — what can be said of this play?

[^18-10]: GPT1 — p. 268, no. 66 (gauri, gauraṛī); GPT2 — sec. 4.2, no. 66 (catalogue: NG-251). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 912; ed. 1960,
vv. 2895–2898), right after the preceding pada, at the Ganga. The GPT1 recognition of this pada is faulty; the readings are restored
from GPT2 and the BR (see the full version of the book). Not in PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^18-11]: Ananga ("the Bodiless") is Kama, the god of love: the Lord's beauty surpasses Kama's (a usual image of the gaura-padas). Ketaki
and kunda are flowers.

## 5. Narahari Dasa — "bali-kalidamana śamanabhayabhañjana…" (GPT1 p. 269, no. 67; BR)
*The son of Shachi dancing in the midst of the kirtana: subduer of Kali and of the fear of death, skilful giver of prema, more
beautiful than a golden mountain; at the rhythm of His feet the earth sways, He spreads His arms, smiles, and seeing Gadadhara's face
loses His composure; His eyes reveal the former play of Vraja. Raga belavali. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in
the BR (12th wave); Vrajabuli.*[^18-12]

বলি-কলিদমন শমনভয়ভঞ্জন নিখিল-ভুবন-জনরঞ্জনকারী ।
দুলহ প্রেমধন-বিতরণ-পণ্ডিত সুরতরুনিকর-গরব-ভরহারী ॥

*bali-kalidamana śamanabhayabhañjana nikhila-bhubana-janarañjanakārī |*
*dulaha premadhana-bitaraṇa-paṇḍita suratarunikara-garaba-bharahārī ||*

*Word for word:* bali-kali-damana — subduer of mighty Kali; śamana-bhaya-bhañjana — destroyer of the fear of Yama; nikhila-bhubana-jana-rañjana-kārī — giving joy to the people of all worlds; dulaha prema-dhana-bitaraṇa-paṇḍita — skilled in distributing the rare treasure of prema; sura-taru-nikara-garaba-bhara-hārī — removing the pride of all the wish-fulfilling trees

**5.1.** Subduer of mighty Kali, dispeller of the fear of Yama, giver of joy to the people of all the worlds,
skilled in giving away the rare treasure of prema, taking away the pride of all the wish-fulfilling trees —[^18-13]

নাচত শচীসুত কীর্তন মাঝ ।
কনক-ধরাধর নিন্দি রুচির তনু বিলসত জনু নব মনমথরাজ ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*nācata śacīsuta kīrtana mājha |*
*kanaka-dharādhara nindi rucira tanu bilasata janu naba manamatharāja || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* nācata śacī-suta — the son of Shachi dances; kīrtana mājha — in the midst of the kirtana; kanaka-dharādhara nindi — surpassing a golden mountain; rucira tanu — the lovely body; bilasata — shines; janu naba manamatha-rāja — like a new king Manmatha

**5.2.** *(Refrain)* the son of Shachi dances in the midst of the kirtana;
His body, lovelier than a golden mountain, shines like a new king Manmatha.

পদতল-তালে ধরণী করু টলমল ললিত ভঙ্গী ভুজ রহত পসারি ।
হাসত মৃদু মৃদু অধর কম্প অতি অথির গদাধর-বদন নেহারি ॥

*padatala-tāle dharaṇī karu ṭalamala lalita bhaṅgī bhuja rahata pasāri |*
*hāsata mṛdu mṛdu adhara kampa ati athira gadādhara-badana nehāri ||*

*Word for word:* pada-tala-tāle — at the rhythm of the feet; dharaṇī karu ṭalamala — the earth sways; lalita bhaṅgī — gracefully bending; bhuja rahata pasāri — He keeps His arms spread; hāsata mṛdu mṛdu — smiling gently; adhara kampa ati — the lips tremble much; athira — unsteady; gadādhara-badana nehāri — on seeing Gadadhara's face

**5.3.** At the rhythm of His feet the earth sways; gracefully bending, He spreads His arms;
smiling gently, His lips tremble — and seeing Gadadhara's face, He loses His composure.

ডগমগ নয়ন-কমল ঘন ঘূরত নিরুপম পূরব রঙ্গ পরকাশ ।
উলসিত পরম চতুর পরিকরগণ ইহ রসে বঞ্চিত নরহরি দাস ॥

*ḍagamaga nayana-kamala ghana ghūrata nirupama pūraba raṅga parakāśa |*
*ulasita parama catura parikaragaṇa iha rase bañcita narahari dāsa ||*

*Word for word:* ḍagamaga nayana-kamala — the lotus eyes sway; ghana ghūrata — turn again and again; nirupama pūraba raṅga parakāśa — revealing the peerless former play; ulasita — rejoice; parama catura parikara-gaṇa — the most skilful associates; iha rase bañcita — deprived of this rasa; narahari dāsa — Narahari Dasa

**5.4.** His lotus eyes sway, turning again and again, revealing the peerless former play;
the skilful associates rejoice — only Narahari Dasa is deprived of this rasa.[^18-14]

[^18-12]: GPT1 — p. 269, no. 67 (belavali); GPT2 — sec. 4.2, no. 67 (catalogue: NG-150). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 921; ed. 1960,
vv. 3018–3021): "here Gaurachandra, with joy in His heart, danced in sankirtana in a wondrous bhava". Not in PK, KGC, PS or the
Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^18-13]: "Subduer of mighty Kali" — the Lord who conquers the age of Kali by sankirtana; "the fear of Yama" — the fear of death and its
consequences. The wish-fulfilling tree (sura-taru, kalpa-vriksha) grants only what is asked for, but the Lord gives prema beyond asking.
[^18-14]: "The former play" (pūraba raṅga) is Krishna's lila in Vraja, which the Lord remembers in the dance. Gadadhara is Radha in
Krishna-lila (note 9).

## 6. Narahari — "āju gorā nagarakīrtane…" (GPT1 p. 269, no. 68; BR)
*The night-time city kirtana: adorned Gora walks with His associates, dances, pours down a rain of prema; gods disguised as men shower
flowers, the townspeople run and sing, fools hearing the lion's roar expect disaster; hundreds of thousands of lamps are burning, the
whole world is intoxicated. Raga kamoda. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave, the account of the
night kirtana); Bengali payar.*[^18-15]

আজু গোরা নগরকীর্তনে ।
সাজিয়া চলয়ে প্রিয় পরিকর সনে ॥

*āju gorā nagarakīrtane |*
*sājiyā calaye priya parikara sane ||*

*Word for word:* āju — today; gorā nagara-kīrtane — Gora is in the city kirtana; sājiyā calaye — dressed up, He goes; priya parikara sane — with His dear associates

**6.1.** Today Gora is in the city kirtana:
having dressed Himself, He goes with His dear associates.

অঙ্গের সুবেশ ভাল শোহে ।
নাচে নানা ভঙ্গীতে ভুবন-মন মোহে ॥

*aṅgera subeśa bhāla śohe |*
*nāce nānā bhaṅgīte bhubana-mana mohe ||*

*Word for word:* aṅgera subeśa — the fine attire on His body; bhāla śohe — shines beautifully; nāce nānā bhaṅgīte — He dances in many ways; bhubana-mana mohe — charms the heart of the world

**6.2.** Beautifully shines the attire on His body;
He dances in every manner, charming the hearts of the world.

প্রেম বরিষয়ে অনিবার ।
বহয়ে আনন্দ-নদী নদীয়া মাঝার ॥

*prema bariṣaye anibāra |*
*bahaye ānanda-nadī nadīyā mājhāra ||*

*Word for word:* prema bariṣaye anibāra — He rains prema ceaselessly; bahaye ānanda-nadī — a river of bliss flows; nadīyā mājhāra — in the midst of Nadia

**6.3.** Ceaselessly He pours down a rain of prema;
in the midst of Nadia flows a river of bliss.

দেবগণ মিশাই মানুষে ।
বরিষে কুসুম কত মনের হরিষে ॥

*debagaṇa miśāi mānuṣe |*
*bariṣe kusuma kata manera hariṣe ||*

*Word for word:* deba-gaṇa miśāi mānuṣe — the gods, mingling with men; bariṣe kusuma kata — shower so many flowers; manera hariṣe — with joy in their hearts

**6.4.** The gods, mingling with men,
shower flowers with joy in their hearts.[^18-16]

নগরিয়া লোক সব ধায় ।
মনের মানসে গোরাচাঁদ-গুণ গায় ॥

*nagariyā loka saba dhāya |*
*manera mānase gorācām̐da-guṇa gāya ||*

*Word for word:* nagariyā loka saba dhāya — all the townspeople run; manera mānase — in the depths of the heart; gorācām̐da-guṇa gāya — sing the virtues of Gorachand

**6.5.** All the townspeople run;
in the depths of their hearts they sing the virtues of Gorachand.

মূঢ়গণ শুনি সিংহনাদ ।
হইয়া বিরস মন গণয়ে প্রমাদ ॥

*mūṛhagaṇa śuni siṃhanāda |*
*haiyā birasa mana gaṇaye pramāda ||*

*Word for word:* mūṛha-gaṇa — fools; śuni siṃha-nāda — hearing the lion's roar; haiyā birasa mana — becoming sullen at heart; gaṇaye pramāda — reckon on disaster

**6.6.** Fools, hearing the lion's roar,
grow sullen and expect disaster.[^18-17]

লাখে লাখে দীপ জ্বলে ভাল ।
উপমা কি অবনী গগন করে আলো ॥

*lākhe lākhe dīpa jvale bhāla |*
*upamā ki abanī gagana kare ālo ||*

*Word for word:* lākhe lākhe dīpa — lamps by hundreds of thousands; jvale bhāla — burn brightly; upamā ki — what comparison; abanī gagana kare ālo — they light up earth and sky

**6.7.** Hundreds of thousands of lamps are burning —
what comparison is there? Earth and sky are lit up.

নরহরি কহিতে কি জানে ।
মাতিল জগত কেউ ধৈরজ না মানে ॥

*narahari kahite ki jāne |*
*mātila jagata keu dhairaja nā māne ||*

*Word for word:* narahari kahite ki jāne — what does Narahari know how to say; mātila jagata — the world is intoxicated; keu dhairaja nā māne — no one keeps composure

**6.8.** What does Narahari know how to tell?
The world is intoxicated — no one can keep his composure.

[^18-15]: GPT1 — p. 269, no. 68 (kamoda); GPT2 — sec. 4.2, no. 68 (catalogue: NG-151). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 927; ed. 1960,
vv. 3104–3111): Ishana tells of the night kirtana, when the Lord went through the streets of Navadvipa by the light of hundreds of
