thousands of lamps, while "the foolish pashandis took it for a calamity" (v. 3103). Not in PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. The
night procession with kirtana through Navadvipa (to the Kazi's house) — CB Madhya 23; CC Adi 17.
[^18-16]: According to the CB (Madhya 23), gods who had taken human form were also in the procession.
[^18-17]: "The lion's roar" (siṃhanāda) is the loud singing of Hari's names. "Fools" are the opponents of kirtana (pashandis), who expected
the noise to bring down the ruler's wrath.

## 7. Narahari — "śacīra dulāla gorā nāce…" (GPT1 pp. 269–270, no. 69; BR)
*The dance of the son of Shachi: Gora offers to anyone the treasure unattainable for the gods; seeing the fallen, He cannot restrain
Himself, waves of bhava rise in Him; His face and breast are bathed in tears; devotees intoxicated with prema circle around, no one can
keep his composure. Raga kamoda. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave); Bengali payar.*[^18-18]

শচীর দুলাল গোরা নাচে ।
দেবের দুর্লভ ধন যারে তারে যাচে ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*śacīra dulāla gorā nāce |*
*debera durlabha dhana yāre tāre yāce || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* śacīra dulāla gorā nāce — Gora, Shachi's darling, dances; debera durlabha dhana — the treasure rare for the gods; yāre tāre yāce — He offers to anyone

**7.1.** *(Refrain)* Gora, the darling son of Shachi, dances:
the treasure unattainable for the gods He offers to whoever comes.

পতিতেরে হেরিয়া ধরিতে নারে অঙ্গ ।
ক্ষণে ক্ষণে উঠে কত ভাবের তরঙ্গ ॥

*patitere heriyā dharite nāre aṅga |*
*kṣaṇe kṣaṇe uṭhe kata bhābera taraṅga ||*

*Word for word:* patitere heriyā — seeing the fallen; dharite nāre aṅga — He cannot hold His body still; kṣaṇe kṣaṇe — moment by moment; uṭhe kata bhābera taraṅga — so many waves of bhava rise

**7.2.** Seeing the fallen, He cannot restrain Himself;
again and again waves of bhava rise in Him.

ঝলমল করয়ে কনক জিনি আভা ।
বিপুল পুলকাবলী বলিত কি শোভা ॥

*jhalamala karaye kanaka jini ābhā |*
*bipula pulakābalī balita ki śobhā ||*

*Word for word:* jhalamala karaye — flashes; kanaka jini ābhā — a radiance surpassing gold; bipula pulakābalī balita — covered with abundant thrills; ki śobhā — what beauty

**7.3.** A radiance surpassing gold flashes;
how beautiful He is, covered with abundant thrills!

ভাসয়ে শ্রীমুখ বুক নয়নের জলে ।
দুটী বাহু তুলিয়া সঘনে হরি বোলে ॥

*bhāsaye śrīmukha buka nayanera jale |*
*duṭī bāhu tuliyā saghane hari bole ||*

*Word for word:* bhāsaye śrī-mukha buka — the holy face and breast are bathed; nayanera jale — in the tears of the eyes; duṭī bāhu tuliyā — raising both arms; saghane hari bole — cries "Hari" again and again

**7.4.** His holy face and breast are bathed in tears;
raising both arms, He cries again and again: "Hari!"

উনমত ভকত ফিরয়ে চারি পাশে ।
জয় জয় কলরব এ ভূমি আকাশে ॥

*unamata bhakata phiraye cāri pāśe |*
*jaya jaya kalaraba e bhūmi ākāśe ||*

*Word for word:* unamata bhakata — intoxicated devotees; phiraye cāri pāśe — move all around; jaya jaya kalaraba — the clamour of "glory, glory"; e bhūmi ākāśe — on earth and in the sky

**7.5.** All around move devotees intoxicated with prema;
cries of "Glory, glory!" fill earth and sky.

পহু পানে হেরি কেহ ধৈরজ না বাঁধে ।
নরহরি ও রাঙ্গা চরণে পড়ি কাঁদে ॥

*pahu pāne heri keha dhairaja nā bām̐dhe |*
*narahari o rāṅgā caraṇe paṛi kām̐de ||*

*Word for word:* pahu pāne heri — looking at the Lord; keha dhairaja nā bām̐dhe — no one keeps composure; narahari — Narahari; o rāṅgā caraṇe paṛi kām̐de — falls at those red feet and weeps

**7.6.** Looking at the Lord, no one can keep his composure;
Narahari, fallen at His reddish feet, weeps.

[^18-18]: GPT1 — pp. 269–270, no. 69 (kamoda); GPT2 — sec. 4.2, no. 69 (catalogue: NG-152). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 948; ed. 1960,
vv. 3381–3386): at the house of Srivasa — "how Gaura plays in Navadvipa even Brahma cannot fathom; the fortunate will see the
dances, kirtana, bhavas and mercy of this place" (vv. 3379–3380). Not in PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.

## 8. Narahari — "nāce gorā guṇamaṇi…" (GPT1 p. 270, no. 70; BR)
*The dance of Gora, mine of prema, among His associates — like a golden moon among the stars; His body more tender than a shirisha
flower, a smile on His red lips; seeing the fallen, He weeps, and as it were the Suradhuni flows from His eyes; the khol and karatalas
sound, all are intoxicated — only the poet is left out. Raga kamoda. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR
(12th wave); Bengali tripadi.*[^18-19]

নাচে গোরা গুণমণি কেবল প্রেমের খনি প্রিয় পরিকর চারি পাশ ।
শোভা অপরূপ যেন উডুগণ মাঝে যেন কনক-চন্দ্রমা পরকাশ ॥

*nāce gorā guṇamaṇi kebala premera khani priya parikara cāri pāśa |*
*śobhā aparūpa yena uḍugaṇa mājhe yena kanaka-candramā parakāśa ||*

*Word for word:* nāce gorā guṇamaṇi — Gora, the jewel of virtues, dances; kebala premera khani — a very mine of prema; priya parikara cāri pāśa — dear associates all around; śobhā aparūpa — wondrous beauty; yena uḍugaṇa mājhe — as if among the stars; kanaka-candramā parakāśa — a golden moon appeared

**8.1.** Gora dances, the jewel of virtues, a very mine of prema, His dear associates around Him;
a wondrous beauty — as if a golden moon had risen among the stars.

শিরীষ-কুসুম জিনি সুকোমল তনুখানি পুলক-বলিত মনোহর ।
প্রফুল্ল কমল দূরে বদনে মদন ঝুরে হাসি-মাখা অরুণ অধর ॥

*śirīṣa-kusuma jini sukomala tanukhāni pulaka-balita manohara |*
*praphulla kamala dūre badane madana jhure hāsi-mākhā aruṇa adhara ||*

*Word for word:* śirīṣa-kusuma jini — surpassing the shirisha flower; sukomala tanu-khāni — the most tender body; pulaka-balita manohara — lovely, covered with thrills; praphulla kamala dūre — the full-blown lotus far behind; badane madana jhure — Madana weeps before the face; hāsi-mākhā aruṇa adhara — red lips anointed with a smile

**8.2.** His body, more tender than a shirisha flower, is lovely, covered with thrills;
the full-blown lotus is left far behind, Madana weeps before His face; a smile is on His red lips.[^18-20]

কত না ভঙ্গিমা করি ভুজ তুলি বোলে হরি বরিষে অমিয়া অনিবার ।
অতি সকরুণ হিয়া পতিতেরে নিরখিয়া আঁখি বহে সুরধুনী-ধার ॥

*kata nā bhaṅgimā kari bhuja tuli bole hari bariṣe amiyā anibāra |*
*ati sakaruṇa hiyā patitere nirakhiyā ām̐khi bahe suradhunī-dhāra ||*

*Word for word:* kata nā bhaṅgimā kari — striking so many poses; bhuja tuli bole hari — raising His arms, cries "Hari"; bariṣe amiyā anibāra — rains nectar ceaselessly; ati sakaruṇa hiyā — a heart full of compassion; patitere nirakhiyā — seeing the fallen; ām̐khi bahe suradhunī-dhāra — from the eyes flows a Ganga-stream

**8.3.** Striking so many poses, He raises His arms and cries "Hari!" — ceaselessly He rains nectar;
His heart is full of compassion: seeing the fallen He weeps, and from His eyes flows a stream like the Suradhuni.

বাজে খোল করতাল চলন চালনি ভাল দেখি কেবা না হয় মোহিত ।
না রহিল দুখ শোক মাতিল সকল লোক নরহরি এ সুখে বঞ্চিত ॥

*bāje khola karatāla calana cālani bhāla dekhi kebā nā haya mohita |*
*nā rahila dukha śoka mātila sakala loka narahari e sukhe bañcita ||*

*Word for word:* bāje khola karatāla — khol and karatalas sound; calana cālani bhāla — lovely is the gait; dekhi kebā nā haya mohita — who, seeing, is not enchanted; nā rahila dukha śoka — no grief or sorrow remained; mātila sakala loka — all the people are intoxicated; narahari e sukhe bañcita — Narahari is deprived of this joy

**8.4.** The khol and karatalas sound, lovely is His gait — who, seeing this, would not be enchanted?
No grief or sorrow remains, all the people are intoxicated — only Narahari is deprived of this joy.

[^18-19]: GPT1 — p. 270, no. 70 (kamoda); GPT2 — sec. 4.2, no. 70 (catalogue: NG-252). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 949; ed. 1960,
vv. 3387–3390), right after the preceding pada, at the house of Srivasa. Not in PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^18-20]: The shirisha is a tree with very delicate flowers (an image of tenderness). Madana (Kama) "weeps" seeing that the Lord's face is
more beautiful than his own.

## 9. Narahari — "nācata naṭabara gaurakiśora…" (GPT1 p. 270, no. 72; BR)
*Young Gaura, the best of dancers, enchants the world with new movements: the radiance of His body is peerless, a garland of forest
flowers sways on His neck, His moon-face pours nectar which the chakora-devotees drink; He sings the names of Hari, and all weep — only
the poet's heart does not melt. Raga suhai. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave); Vrajabuli.*[^18-21]

নাচত নটবর গৌরকিশোর ।
অভিনব ভঙ্গী ভুবন করু ভোর ॥

*nācata naṭabara gaurakiśora |*
*abhinaba bhaṅgī bhubana karu bhora ||*

*Word for word:* nācata naṭabara — the best of dancers dances; gaura-kiśora — young Gaura; abhinaba bhaṅgī — with new movements; bhubana karu bhora — sends the world into rapture

**9.1.** Young Gaura dances, the best of dancers;
with new movements He sends the world into rapture.

ঝলমল অঙ্গ-কিরণ অনুপাম ।
হেরইতে মূরছত কত কত কাম ॥

*jhalamala aṅga-kiraṇa anupāma |*
*heraite mūrachata kata kata kāma ||*

*Word for word:* jhalamala — flashes; aṅga-kiraṇa anupāma — the peerless radiance of the body; heraite — on seeing; mūrachata kata kata kāma — countless Kamas swoon

**9.2.** The peerless radiance of His body flashes;
seeing it, countless Kamas swoon.

টলমল লোচনযুগল বিশাল ।
দোলত কণ্ঠে বলিত বনমাল ॥

*ṭalamala locanayugala biśāla |*
*dolata kaṇṭhe balita banamāla ||*

*Word for word:* ṭalamala — sway; locana-yugala biśāla — the two large eyes; dolata kaṇṭhe — swings on the neck; balita banamāla — the garland of forest flowers

**9.3.** His large eyes sway;
on His neck swings a garland of forest flowers.

ঝরত অমিয় বিধুবদন উজোর ।
পীবই নয়ন ভরি ভকত-চকোর ॥

*jharata amiya bidhubadana ujora |*
*pībai nayana bhari bhakata-cakora ||*

*Word for word:* jharata amiya — pours nectar; bidhu-badana ujora — the radiant moon-face; pībai nayana bhari — drink to the full with their eyes; bhakata-cakora — the chakora-devotees

**9.4.** His radiant moon-face pours down nectar —
the chakora-devotees drink it to the full with their eyes.[^18-22]

ঘন ঘন বোলয়ে মধুর হরিনাম ।
শুনইতে কো ন রোয়ই অবিরাম ॥

*ghana ghana bolaye madhura harināma |*
*śunaite ko na royai abirāma ||*

*Word for word:* ghana ghana bolaye — again and again utters; madhura hari-nāma — the sweet name of Hari; śunaite — on hearing; ko na royai abirāma — who does not weep without end

**9.5.** Again and again He utters the sweet name of Hari —
who, hearing it, does not weep without end?

পামর পতিত প্রেমরসে মাতি ।
না দরবে কঠিন এ নরহরি-ছাতি ॥

*pāmara patita premarase māti |*
*nā darabe kaṭhina e narahari-chāti ||*

*Word for word:* pāmara patita — the sinful and fallen; prema-rase māti — intoxicated with the rasa of prema; nā darabe — does not melt; kaṭhina e narahari-chāti — this hard breast of Narahari

**9.6.** The sinful and the fallen are intoxicated with the rasa of prema —
only Narahari's hard breast does not melt.

[^18-21]: GPT1 — p. 270, no. 72 (suhai); GPT2 — sec. 4.2, no. 72. The pada was not in the catalogue — **new row NG-254** (the signature
sweep had matched it to another pada). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 952; ed. 1960, vv. 3430–3435), right after a pada of Vasu
Ramananda (GPT1 no. 73), before the account of Advaita's dance in the house of Srivasa. The GPT2 index assigns the pages of this
place to Chakravarti. Not in PK (PK 2065 "nācata naṭabara gaura kiśora" is a different pada, by Balarama Dasa), KGC, PS or the
Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^18-22]: The chakora is a bird which, by poetic tradition, feeds on moonlight: the devotees "drink with their eyes" the beauty of the
Lord's face.

## 10. Narahari — "prabhu biśvambhara priya parikara…" (GPT1 p. 283, no. 21; BR)
*The Lord's dream of Balarama: Vishvambhara tells His associates that at night He saw a beautiful chariot with a palm-tree banner arrive
here; a tall man with an earring in one ear, a pitcher in His hand, dressed in blue and with a blue cloth on His head, swaying, looked
around and asked for Him by name again and again — Haladhara must have come; having said this, the Lord was absorbed in the bhava of
Balarama. Raga kamoda. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave) and is set in the account of
Nityananda's arrival in Navadvipa; Bengali tripadi.*[^18-23]

প্রভু বিশ্বম্ভর প্রিয় পরিকর প্রতি কহে শুন স্বপন-কথা ।
কিবা সে নির্মিত অতি সুশোভিত তালধ্বজ রথ আইল এথা ॥

*prabhu biśvambhara priya parikara prati kahe śuna svapana-kathā |*
*kibā se nirmita ati suśobhita tāladhvaja ratha āila ethā ||*

*Word for word:* prabhu biśvambhara — Lord Vishvambhara; priya parikara prati kahe — says to His dear associates; śuna svapana-kathā — hear the account of a dream; kibā se nirmita — how wondrously made; ati suśobhita — beautifully adorned; tāla-dhvaja ratha — a chariot with a palm-tree banner; āila ethā — came here

**10.1.** Lord Vishvambhara says to His dear associates: "Listen to what I saw in a dream.
What a wondrously made, beautifully adorned chariot with a palm-tree banner has come here!

দেখিনু সুন্দর দীর্ঘ কলেবর পুরুষ এক কি উপমা তাহে ।
এক কর্ণে কিবা কুণ্ডল সে গ্রীবা কিবা মুখশশী ভুবন মোহে ॥

*dekhinu sundara dīrgha kalebara puruṣa eka ki upamā tāhe |*
*eka karṇe kibā kuṇḍala se grībā kibā mukhaśaśī bhubana mohe ||*

*Word for word:* dekhinu sundara — I saw a handsome; dīrgha kalebara puruṣa eka — tall-bodied man; ki upamā tāhe — what comparison for him; eka karṇe kibā kuṇḍala — what an earring in one ear; se grībā — what a neck; kibā mukha-śaśī — what a moon-face; bhubana mohe — enchants the world

**10.2.** I saw a handsome man of tall stature — what can He be compared with?
In one ear an earring, and what a neck! His moon-face enchants the world.

কালকুম্ভ হাতে নীল বস্ত্র মাথে নীলবাস পরিধান সুছাঁদে ।
চৌদিকে নেহালে হেলি দুলি চলে সে ভঙ্গীতে কেবা ধৈরজ বাঁধে ॥

*kālakumbha hāte nīla bastra māthe nīlabāsa paridhāna suchām̐de |*
*caudike nehāle heli duli cale se bhaṅgīte kebā dhairaja bām̐dhe ||*

*Word for word:* kāla-kumbha hāte — a dark pitcher in hand; nīla bastra māthe — a blue cloth on the head; nīla-bāsa paridhāna suchām̐de — fittingly dressed in blue; caudike nehāle — he looked on all sides; heli duli cale — walked swaying; se bhaṅgīte — at that gait; kebā dhairaja bām̐dhe — who keeps composure

**10.3.** A dark pitcher in His hand, a blue cloth on His head, and He was fittingly dressed in blue;
He looked about on all sides and walked swaying — who, seeing that gait, could keep his composure?

মোর নাম ধরি পুছে বেরি বেরি বুঝি হলধর গমন কৈলা ।
এত কহি নরহরি-প্রভু বর বলরাম-ভাবে বিভোল হৈলা ॥

*mora nāma dhari puche beri beri bujhi haladhara gamana kailā |*
*eta kahi narahari-prabhu bara balarāma-bhābe bibhola hailā ||*

*Word for word:* mora nāma dhari — calling My name; puche beri beri — he asked again and again; bujhi haladhara gamana kailā — surely Haladhara has come; eta kahi — having said this; narahari-prabhu bara — Narahari's excellent Lord; balarāma-bhābe bibhola hailā — was absorbed in the bhava of Balarama

**10.4.** Calling My name, He asked for Me again and again — Haladhara must have come."
Having said this, Narahari's Lord was absorbed in the bhava of Balarama.[^18-24]

[^18-23]: GPT1 — p. 283, sec. 4.3 (bhavavesha), no. 21 (kamoda); GPT2 — sec. 4.3, no. 21 (catalogue: NG-253). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912,
p. 826; ed. 1960, vv. 1731–1734): Nityananda came to Navadvipa and stayed with Nandana Acharya; the Lord, knowing this, in the temple of
Vishnu where He worshipped Vishnu and where the Vaishnavas gathered, "told here the dream of that night"; after the pada Srivasa and
others, seeing the Lord in this bhava, offer prayers, and Haridasa and Srivasa are sent to search for Nityananda (vv. 1735–1738). The
GPT2 index assigns this page to Chakravarti. Not in PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. The dream and the bhava of Balarama — CB
Madhya 3; cf. Murari 2.14 (the bhava of Balarama).
[^18-24]: The palm-tree banner (tala-dhvaja), blue garments, an earring in one ear are marks of Balarama (Haladhara, "Bearer of the
plough"); the one who has come is Nityananda, the Balarama of Gaura-lila, whom the Lord recognises before meeting Him. "Narahari's Lord"
(narahari-prabhu) is the Lord whom the poet serves (cf. chapter 17, note 44). The bhava of Balarama is one of the bhavas the Lord revealed
in Navadvipa: a manifestation of His own fullness, not a transformation into another.

## 11. Narahari — "pālaṅka upare gaurāṅga sundara…" (GPT1 p. 306, no. 23)
*The Lord in the bhava of Radha waiting for Krishna (vasaka-sajja): beautiful Gauranga sits sadly on the couch; He has decked the bed
with flowers because Shyama promised to come, but the night is almost over — where is the dark moon? Kala has not come — how much longer
to bear the burning of love? "I will break off love with cruel Shyama!" Raga dhanashi. **Attribution: not established** — the pada is
not in the BR; the GPT2 index assigns the page to "Narahari Dasa" (undistinguished); simple Bengali tripadi, like the neighbouring pada
of Sarakara PK 307 (GPT1 no. 22), which it follows in content.*[^18-25]

পালঙ্ক উপরে গৌরাঙ্গ সুন্দর বসিয়া বিরস মনে ।
রাধার ভাবেতে ভাবিত অন্তর বাসক-সজ্জার ভাণে ॥

*pālaṅka upare gaurāṅga sundara basiyā birasa mane |*
*rādhāra bhābete bhābita antara bāsaka-sajjāra bhāṇe ||*

*Word for word:* pālaṅka upare — on the couch; gaurāṅga sundara — beautiful Gauranga; basiyā birasa mane — sits with a sad heart; rādhāra bhābete — by the bhava of Radha; bhābita antara — the heart absorbed; bāsaka-sajjāra bhāṇe — showing (the state of) vasaka-sajja

**11.1.** On the couch beautiful Gauranga sits in sadness:
His heart is seized by the bhava of Radha — He shows the state of vasaka-sajja.[^18-26]

কহে শ্যাম বঁধু আসিবে বলিয়া শেজ সাজাইনু ফুলে ।
গতপ্রায় নিশি কোথা কালশশী রজনী গেল বিফলে ॥

*kahe śyāma bam̐dhu āsibe baliyā śeja sājāinu phule |*
*gataprāya niśi kothā kālaśaśī rajanī gela biphale ||*

*Word for word:* kahe — He says; śyāma bam̐dhu āsibe baliyā — because the dark friend said He would come; śeja sājāinu phule — I decked the bed with flowers; gataprāya niśi — the night is almost gone; kothā kāla-śaśī — where is the dark moon; rajanī gela biphale — the night has passed in vain

**11.2.** He says: "My dark friend said He would come — and I decked the bed with flowers;
the night is almost gone — where is He, the dark moon? The night has passed in vain.

না আসিল কালা আর প্রেমজ্বালা কত বা সহিবে প্রাণে ।
কহে নরহরি ভাঙ্গিব পিরীতি সে শ্যাম নিঠুর সনে ॥

*nā āsila kālā āra premajvālā kata bā sahibe prāṇe |*
*kahe narahari bhāṅgiba pirīti se śyāma niṭhura sane ||*

*Word for word:* nā āsila kālā — Kala (the Dark One) has not come; āra prema-jvālā — and the burning of love; kata vā sahibe prāṇe — how much more will the heart bear; kahe narahari — says Narahari; bhāṅgiba pirīti — I will break off the love; se śyāma niṭhura sane — with that cruel Shyama

**11.3.** Kala has not come — how much longer will the heart bear the burning of love?"
Narahari conveys: "I will break off love with that cruel Shyama!"[^18-27]

[^18-25]: GPT1 — p. 306, sec. 4.5 (abhisara, rasodgara, utkanthita), no. 23 (dhanashi); GPT2 — sec. 4.5, no. 23 (the catalogue did not know
this pada — **new row NG-255**; the signature sweep had matched it to another pada). Before it (no. 22) stands Narahari Sarakara's pada
"kī lāgiyā mora gaurasundara basiyā gṛhera mājhe" (PK 307, chapter 3, no. 3) on the same theme. Not in BR, PK, KGC, PS or the
Gita-chandrodaya. C.
[^18-26]: Vasaka-sajja is the heroine who has adorned herself and the bed and waits for her beloved (one of the eight states of the heroine
in alankara-shastra; Rupa Gosvami, Ujjvala-nilamani). The Lord, Krishna Himself, appeared in order to taste Radha's love for Him (CC Adi
4), and lives through Her waiting and separation. This is pure prema, not worldly passion: Radha's bhava is the highest manifestation of
the hladini-shakti.
[^18-27]: Anger at Krishna (mana) is one of the expressions of Radha's prema, in which love only grows stronger; the words "I will break off
love" are not a cooling but the voice of wounded love. PK 307 has a similar ending (chapter 3, no. 3). The pronoun "I" is the Lord's
speech in Radha's bhava, which the poet conveys.

## 12. Narahari — "jhulata rasamaya gaurakiśora…" (GPT1 p. 324, no. 10; BR)
*Jhulana: on the bank of the Suradhuni, under a lofty tree, a peerless swing has been made; the skilful associates gently swing young
Gaura, sing and play; the people of Nadia leave their homes and run to see His smiling face, the gods shower flowers, and Narahari
cannot count the virtues of the Lord of his life. Raga mallara or imana. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR
(12th wave, the beginning of the account of jhulana); Vrajabuli.*[^18-28]

ঝুলত রসময় গৌরকিশোর ।
সুরধুনীতীর তুঙ্গ তরুতলহি বিরচিত নিরুপম ললিত হিন্দোর ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*jhulata rasamaya gaurakiśora |*
*suradhunītīra tuṅga tarutalahi biracita nirupama lalita hindora || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* jhulata — swings; rasamaya gaura-kiśora — young Gaura, full of rasa; suradhunī-tīra — on the bank of the Suradhuni (Ganga); tuṅga taru-talahi — under a lofty tree; biracita — is made; nirupama lalita hindora — a peerless charming swing

**12.1.** *(Refrain)* Young Gaura, full of rasa, is swinging;
on the bank of the Suradhuni, under a lofty tree, a peerless, charming swing has been made.

পরিকর সুঘড় ঝুলায়ত লহু লহু গায়ত সরস তান রসে মাতি ।
উচরত রুচির বচন ধিক ধিক ধিনি বায়ত মধুর যন্ত্র কত ভাঁতি ॥

*parikara sughaṛa jhulāyata lahu lahu gāyata sarasa tāna rase māti |*
*ucarata rucira bacana dhika dhika dhini bāyata madhura yantra kata bhām̐ti ||*

*Word for word:* parikara sughaṛa — skilful associates; jhulāyata lahu lahu — gently swing Him; gāyata sarasa tāna rase māti — sing, rapt in the rasa of sweet melodies; ucarata rucira bacana — utter charming words; dhika dhika dhini — "dhik-dhik-dhini"; bāyata madhura yantra kata bhām̐ti — play sweet instruments of many kinds

**12.2.** The skilful associates gently swing Him and sing, rapt in the rasa of the melodies;
they utter a sweet "dhik-dhik-dhini" and play on so many sweet-sounding instruments.[^18-29]

নদীয়াপুর-নরনারী-নিকর ঘর তেজি চলত ধৃতি ধরই না পারি ।
লোচন চপল নিমিখ নাহি সঞ্চরু হাস-মিলিত বিধুবদন নেহারি ॥

*nadīyāpura-naranārī-nikara ghara teji calata dhṛti dharai nā pāri |*
*locana capala nimikha nāhi sañcaru hāsa-milita bidhubadana nehāri ||*

*Word for word:* nadīyāpura-nara-nārī-nikara — crowds of the men and women of Nadia; ghara teji calata — leaving their homes, they go; dhṛti dharai nā pāri — unable to restrain themselves; locana capala — eager eyes; nimikha nāhi sañcaru — do not blink; hāsa-milita bidhu-badana nehāri — gazing at the moon-face lit with a smile

**12.3.** Crowds of the men and women of Nadia leave their homes and come, unable to restrain themselves;
their eyes, unblinking, gaze at His moon-face lit with a smile.

সুরগণ গগনে মগন গণ সহ বরষত কুসুম করত জয়কারি ।
নরহরি-প্রাণনাথ-গুণে উনমত ভণত নিয়ত গুণ গণই না পারি ॥

*suragaṇa gagane magana gaṇa saha baraṣata kusuma karata jayakāri |*
*narahari-prāṇanātha-guṇe unamata bhaṇata niyata guṇa gaṇai nā pāri ||*

*Word for word:* sura-gaṇa gagane — the gods in the sky; magana gaṇa saha — immersed, with their companions; baraṣata kusuma — shower flowers; karata jayakāri — cry "Glory"; narahari-prāṇa-nātha-guṇe unamata — intoxicated by the virtues of the Lord of Narahari's life; bhaṇata niyata — he speaks constantly; guṇa gaṇai nā pāri — cannot count the virtues

**12.4.** The gods in the sky, immersed in bliss, with their companions shower flowers and cry "Glory!";
Narahari, intoxicated by the virtues of the Lord of his life, speaks of them without end — and cannot count them.[^18-30]

[^18-28]: GPT1 — p. 324, sec. 5.1 (the "twelve-month lila"), no. 10 (mallara or imana; in the recognition the number is distorted —
"১৪"); GPT2 — sec. 5.1, no. 10. In the catalogue — row NS-016 (with a wrong reference to PK 2106, a pada of Nayanananda); a Narahari
pada, known only from the GPT and the BR, now assigned to the appendix (new row NG-256). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 938; ed. 1960,
vv. 3263–3266): "by Gaurachandra's will the six seasons are always embodied in Nadia; to delight the rainy season, here the Lord swings
on a swing" (vv. 3261–3262). The GPT2 index assigns these pages to Chakravarti. Not in PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
Jhulana-yatra is the swing festival in the month of Shravana (July–August).
[^18-29]: "Dhik-dhik-dhini" are rhythmic syllables (bol) chanted to the drum.
[^18-30]: "The Lord of Narahari's life" (narahari-prāṇanātha) is Lord Gaura (cf. note 24).

## 13. Narahari — "āju suradhunītīre gorārāya…" (GPT1 p. 324, no. 11; BR)
*Jhulana: Gora Raya swings on the bank of the Suradhuni, looking at Gadadhara's face, and in His joy cannot sit still; all sing of the
former swinging, and everyone runs to see. Raga mallara. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave); short
Bengali payar.*[^18-31]

আজু সুরধুনীতীরে গোরারায় ।
ঝুলে কত না ভঙ্গীতে ঝুলনায় ॥

*āju suradhunītīre gorārāya |*
*jhule kata nā bhaṅgīte jhulanāya ||*

*Word for word:* āju — today; suradhunī-tīre — on the bank of the Suradhuni (Ganga); gorā-rāya — Gora Raya; jhule — swings; kata nā bhaṅgīte — in how many ways; jhulanāya — on the swing

**13.1.** Today on the bank of the Suradhuni Gora Raya
swings on the swing — in how many ways!

প্রিয় গদাধর-মুখ পানে চাঞা ।
রঙ্গে রহিতে নারয়ে থির হৈঞা ॥

*priya gadādhara-mukha pāne cāñā |*
*raṅge rahite nāraye thira haiñā ||*

*Word for word:* priya gadādhara-mukha pāne cāñā — looking at dear Gadadhara's face; raṅge — in His joy; rahite nāraye thira haiñā — cannot remain still

**13.2.** Looking at the face of dear Gadadhara,
in His joy He cannot sit still.[^18-32]

সবে পূরব ঝুলন-লীলা গায় ।
শোভা দেখিতে কেবা বা নাই ধায় ॥

*sabe pūraba jhulana-līlā gāya |*
*śobhā dekhite kebā bā nāi dhāya ||*

*Word for word:* sabe — all; pūraba jhulana-līlā gāya — sing of the former lila of the swing; śobhā dekhite — to see the beauty; kebā vā nāi dhāya — who does not run

**13.3.** All sing of the former lila of the swing;
who does not run to see this beauty?

নরহরি-প্রাণনাথে আঁখি দিয়া ।
কেহ কহে কত সুখী ঘরে গিয়া ॥

*narahari-prāṇanāthe ām̐khi diyā |*
*keha kahe kata sukhī ghare giyā ||*

*Word for word:* narahari-prāṇa-nāthe — on the Lord of Narahari's life; ām̐khi diyā — fixing the eyes; keha kahe — some tell; kata sukhī — how happy; ghare giyā — having gone home

**13.4.** Fixing their eyes on the Lord of Narahari's life,
some, returning home, tell how happy they are.[^18-33]

[^18-31]: GPT1 — p. 324, no. 11 (mallara); GPT2 — sec. 5.1, no. 11 (catalogue: NG-158). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 939; ed. 1960, vv.
3267–3270), right after the preceding one. Not in PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^18-32]: "The former lila of the swing" is the jhulana of Radha and Krishna in Vraja; the Lord remembers it with Gadadhara, who in
Krishna-lila is Radha (note 9).
[^18-33]: So in GPT2 ("kata sukhī"); the GPT1 recognition has "kata sakhī" ("tells her friend"); in the BR the line is damaged. The next pada of
the GPT (no. 12, "jhulata jhulata sundara rasamaya gorā…", also signed by Narahari and also in the BR) is the speech of a townswoman who
has resolved to forget her shame before her family for Gaura's sake — nagari-bhava; it is assigned to the section of nagari padas (new
catalogue row NG-257).

## 14. Narahari — "āju gorā suradhunītīre. jhule kibā lalita hindore…" (GPT1 p. 325, no. 13; BR)
*Jhulana in the rainy season: Gora swings on a charming swing by the Suradhuni, His form flashes like lightning in the dark clouds, the
thunder of the mridanga is like a storm, the peahens dance, Nadia rejoices, creepers and trees thrill; Narahari, looking at the Lord's
face, gently rocks the swing. Raga mallara. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave); short Bengali
payar.*[^18-34]

আজু গোরা সুরধুনীতীরে ।
ঝুলে কিবা ললিত হিন্দোরে ॥

*āju gorā suradhunītīre |*
*jhule kibā lalita hindore ||*

*Word for word:* āju gorā — today Gora; suradhunī-tīre — on the bank of the Suradhuni (Ganga); jhule — swings; kibā lalita hindore — on a charming swing

**14.1.** Today Gora on the bank of the Suradhuni
swings on a charming swing.

কিবা সে বরষা ঋতু তায় ।
অন্ধকারে মেঘের ঘটায় ॥

*kibā se baraṣā ṛtu tāya |*
*andhakāre meghera ghaṭāya ||*

*Word for word:* kibā se baraṣā ṛtu tāya — and what a rainy season it is; andhakāre — darkness; meghera ghaṭāya — from the mass of clouds

**14.2.** And what a rainy season it is!
Darkness from the gathered clouds.

গোরারূপ চমকে বিজুরী ।
জগতের প্রাণ করে চুরি ॥

*gorārūpa camake bijurī |*
*jagatera prāṇa kare curi ||*

*Word for word:* gorā-rūpa — Gora's form; camake bijurī — flashes like lightning; jagatera prāṇa kare curi — steals the life of the world

**14.3.** Gora's form flashes like lightning,
stealing the life of the world.

পারিষদ সুমধুর গায় ।
যেন কত সুধা বরিষায় ॥

*pāriṣada sumadhura gāya |*
*yena kata sudhā bariṣāya ||*

*Word for word:* pāriṣada sumadhura gāya — the associates sing sweetly; yena kata sudhā bariṣāya — as if raining so much nectar

**14.4.** Sweetly the associates sing —
as if pouring down so much nectar.

বাজয়ে মৃদঙ্গ গরজনি ।
নাচে শিখিকুলের রমণী ॥

*bājaye mṛdaṅga garajani |*
*nāce śikhikulera ramaṇī ||*

*Word for word:* bājaye mṛdaṅga — the mridanga sounds; garajani — like thunder; nāce śikhi-kulera ramaṇī — the peahens dance

**14.5.** The mridanga resounds like thunder —
the peahens dance.[^18-35]

নদীয়ানগর উলসিত ।
লতাতরুকুল পুলকিত ॥

*nadīyānagara ulasita |*
*latātarukula pulakita ||*

*Word for word:* nadīyā-nagara ulasita — the town of Nadia rejoices; latā-taru-kula pulakita — the creepers and trees thrill

**14.6.** The town of Nadia rejoices,
creepers and trees are covered with thrills.

সব লোক ধায় দেখিবারে ।
কেহ কত মনোরথ করে ॥

*saba loka dhāya dekhibāre |*
*keha kata manoratha kare ||*

*Word for word:* saba loka dhāya dekhibāre — all run to see; keha kata manoratha kare — each forms so many desires

**14.7.** All run to see,
and each has so many desires.

নরহরি পহু-মুখ হেরি ।
ঝুলায় ঝুলনা ধীরি ধীরি ॥

*narahari pahu-mukha heri |*
*jhulāya jhulanā dhīri dhīri ||*

*Word for word:* narahari — Narahari; pahu-mukha heri — looking at the Lord's face; jhulāya jhulanā — rocks the swing; dhīri dhīri — gently, gently

**14.8.** Narahari, looking at the Lord's face,
gently, gently rocks the swing.[^18-36]

[^18-34]: GPT1 — p. 325, no. 13 (mallara); GPT2 — sec. 5.1, no. 13 (catalogue: NG-159). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 940; ed. 1960, vv.
3275–3282), after pada no. 12 (nagari). Not in PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^18-35]: Images of the rainy season: Gaura is the lightning, the thunder of the drum the storm; peacocks (here peahens) dance on hearing
thunder.
[^18-36]: Narahari Sarakara is an associate of the Lord who served Him in Navadvipa (in the pada on the arati he waves the chamara —
chapter 17, no. 12); Chakravarti, describing the Navadvipa lila, often speaks in the person of Narahari the associate.

## 15. Narahari — "gorā pahu dole hindolete…" (GPT1 p. 325, no. 14; BR)
*After the jhulana: the Lord swings, looking at Gadadhara's face, His golden body thrills; the rejoicing associates take Him down from
the swing and seat Him under a kadamba tree; Nityananda weeps with prema, Advaita roars; Srivasa and others lovingly bring delicacies;
Gora Raya feeds everyone, and Narahari partakes of the remnants. Raga kamoda. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the
BR (12th wave); short Bengali payar.*[^18-37]

গোরা পহু দোলে হিন্দোলেতে ।
কত সুখ সে ভাব ভাবিতে ॥

*gorā pahu dole hindolete |*
*kata sukha se bhāba bhābite ||*

*Word for word:* gorā pahu — Lord Gora; dole hindolete — swings on the swing; kata sukha — how much happiness; se bhāba bhābite — in contemplating that bhava

**15.1.** Lord Gora swings on the swing —
how much happiness in the bhava He remembers!

গদাধর-মুখ পানে চায় ।
পুলক ভরয়ে হেম-গায় ॥

*gadādhara-mukha pāne cāya |*
*pulaka bharaye hema-gāya ||*

*Word for word:* gadādhara-mukha pāne cāya — looks at Gadadhara's face; pulaka bharaye — thrills fill; hema-gāya — the golden body

**15.2.** He looks at Gadadhara's face,
thrills fill His golden body.

পারিষদ উলসিত চিতে ।
নামাইয়া হিন্দোলা হৈতে ॥

*pāriṣada ulasita cite |*
*nāmāiyā hindolā haite ||*

*Word for word:* pāriṣada ulasita cite — the associates, rejoicing at heart; nāmāiyā hindolā haite — taking Him down from the swing

**15.3.** The associates, rejoicing at heart,
take Him down from the swing,

বসাইতে নীপতরু-মূলে ।
নিতাই ভাসয়ে প্রেমজলে ॥

*basāite nīpataru-mūle |*
*nitāi bhāsaye premajale ||*

*Word for word:* basāite — to seat Him; nīpa-taru-mūle — at the roots of the kadamba tree; nitāi bhāsaye prema-jale — Nitai swims in tears of prema

**15.4.** to seat Him at the roots of a kadamba;
Nitai swims in tears of prema.

অদ্বৈত করয়ে হুহুঙ্কার ।
বাড়ে মহা সুখের পাথার ॥

*advaita karaye huhuṅkāra |*
*bāṛe mahā sukhera pāthāra ||*

*Word for word:* advaita karaye huhuṅkāra — Advaita gives a thunderous roar; bāṛe mahā sukhera pāthāra — the vast ocean of happiness swells

**15.5.** Advaita gives a thunderous roar —
a boundless ocean of happiness swells.

শ্রীবাসাদি যতন করিয়া ।
দিল নানা দ্রব্য সাজাইয়া ॥

*śrībāsādi yatana kariyā |*
*dila nānā drabya sājāiyā ||*

*Word for word:* śrībāsa-ādi — Srivasa and others; yatana kariyā — with care; dila nānā drabya sājāiyā — set out and offered all kinds of foods

**15.6.** Srivasa and the others with care
bring and set out all kinds of delicacies.

সভার পরাণ গোরারায় ।
ভুঞ্জিব কি সভারে ভুঞ্জায় ॥

*sabhāra parāṇa gorārāya |*
*bhuñjiba ki sabhāre bhuñjāya ||*

*Word for word:* sabhāra parāṇa gorā-rāya — Gora Raya, the life of all; bhuñjiba ki — will He eat (Himself); sabhāre bhuñjāya — He feeds all

**15.7.** Gora Raya is the life of all; will He eat Himself? —
He feeds everyone.

যে কৌতুক কহিতে কি পারি ।
অবশেষ ভুঞ্জে নরহরি ॥

*ye kautuka kahite ki pāri |*
*abaśeṣa bhuñje narahari ||*

*Word for word:* ye kautuka — this joy; kahite ki pāri — can I describe; abaśeṣa bhuñje narahari — Narahari partakes of the remnants

**15.8.** Can this joy be described?
Narahari partakes of the remnants.[^18-38]

[^18-37]: GPT1 — p. 325, no. 14 (kamoda); GPT2 — sec. 5.1, no. 14 (catalogue: NG-160). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 940; ed. 1960, vv.
3283–3290), the last pada of the account of jhulana. Not in PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. The next GPT pada signed Narahari
(no. 16, "āju racita naba ratana-hindora") is PK 1559 (catalogue: NG-161 = NS-032), already translated (chapter 4).
[^18-38]: The last couplet is restored from GPT2 and the BR ("abaśeṣa bhuñje narahari"; distorted in the GPT1 recognition). The remnants of the
Lord's food (mahaprasada) are the highest mercy for a servant (cf. CC Antya 16).

## 16. Narahari — "gorā mora gokulera śaśī…" (GPT1 p. 327, no. 20; BR)
*Janmashtami and Nanda-utsava in the house of Srivasa: Gora, smiling, announces "Today is Krishna's birth!" and dances in a cowherd's
dress; Nitai with a staff, Gauridasa, Ramai and Sundara with carrying-poles, Srivasa and Advaita scatter turmeric and yoghurt, Mukunda and
Madhava sing, the women perform auspicious rites — the house of Srivasa has become the house of Nanda. Raga kamoda. **Attribution:
probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave, the account of the festival of Krishna's birth); Bengali payar.*[^18-39]

গোরা মোর গোকুলের শশী ।
কৃষ্ণের জনম আজি কহে হাসি হাসি ॥

*gorā mora gokulera śaśī |*
*kṛṣṇera janama āji kahe hāsi hāsi ||*

*Word for word:* gorā mora — my Gora; gokulera śaśī — the moon of Gokula; kṛṣṇera janama āji — today is Krishna's birth; kahe hāsi hāsi — He says, smiling

**16.1.** My Gora is the moon of Gokula;
smiling, He says: "Today is Krishna's birth!"

আবেশে থির হইতে নারে ।
ধরি গোপবেশ নাচে উল্লাস-অন্তরে ॥

*ābeśe thira haite nāre |*
*dhari gopabeśa nāce ullāsa-antare ||*

*Word for word:* ābeśe — in His absorption; thira haite nāre — cannot be still; dhari gopa-beśa — putting on a cowherd's dress; nāce ullāsa-antare — dances with joy in His heart

**16.2.** Seized by bhava, He cannot remain still:
putting on a cowherd's dress, He dances with joy in His heart.

নিতাই গোপের বেশ ধরি ।
হাতে লৈঞা লগুড় নাচয়ে ভঙ্গী করি ॥

*nitāi gopera beśa dhari |*
*hāte laiñā laguṛa nācaye bhaṅgī kari ||*

*Word for word:* nitāi gopera beśa dhari — Nitai, wearing a cowherd's dress; hāte laiñā laguṛa — taking a staff in hand; nācaye bhaṅgī kari — dances, striking poses

**16.3.** Nitai, dressed as a cowherd,
with a staff in His hand dances, bending in every way.

গৌরীদাস রামাই সুন্দর ।
নাচে গোপবেশে কাঁধে ভার মনোহর ॥

*gaurīdāsa rāmāi sundara |*
*nāce gopabeśe kām̐dhe bhāra manohara ||*

*Word for word:* gaurī-dāsa rāmāi sundara — Gauridasa, Ramai and Sundara; nāce gopa-beśe — dance in cowherd dress; kām̐dhe bhāra manohara — with lovely carrying-poles on their shoulders

**16.4.** Gauridasa, Ramai and Sundara
dance in cowherd dress, with lovely carrying-poles on their shoulders.[^18-40]

শ্রীবাস অদ্বৈত গোপবেশে ।
ছড়ায় হলদি দধি মনের হরিষে ॥

*śrībāsa advaita gopabeśe |*
*chaṛāya haladi dadhi manera hariṣe ||*

*Word for word:* śrībāsa advaita gopa-beśe — Srivasa and Advaita in cowherd dress; chaṛāya haladi dadhi — scatter turmeric and yoghurt; manera hariṣe — with joy in their hearts

**16.5.** Srivasa and Advaita in cowherd dress
scatter turmeric and yoghurt with joy in their hearts.

কেহ কেহ নানা বাদ্য বায় ।
মুকুন্দ মাধব সে জনমলীলা গায় ॥

*keha keha nānā bādya bāya |*
*mukunda mādhaba se janamalīlā gāya ||*

*Word for word:* keha keha — some; nānā bādya bāya — play various instruments; mukunda mādhaba — Mukunda and Madhava; se janama-līlā gāya — sing that lila of the birth

**16.6.** Some play on various instruments;
Mukunda and Madhava sing of the lila of the birth.

করে সুমঙ্গল নারীগণ ।
শ্রীবাস-আলয় যেন নন্দের ভবন ॥

*kare sumaṅgala nārīgaṇa |*
*śrībāsa-ālaya yena nandera bhabana ||*

*Word for word:* kare sumaṅgala nārī-gaṇa — the women perform auspicious rites; śrībāsa-ālaya — Srivasa's house; yena nandera bhabana — is like Nanda's house

**16.7.** The women perform auspicious rites;
the house of Srivasa is like the house of Nanda.[^18-41]

জয়ধ্বনি করি বারে বারে ।
ধায় লোক ধৈরজ ধরিতে কেহ নারে ॥

*jayadhvani kari bāre bāre |*
*dhāya loka dhairaja dharite keha nāre ||*

*Word for word:* jaya-dhvani kari bāre bāre — crying "glory" again and again; dhāya loka — people run; dhairaja dharite keha nāre — no one can keep composure

**16.8.** Again and again cries of "Glory!" ring out;
people run, and no one can keep his composure.

কত সাধে দেখে আঁখি ভরি ।
শোভায় ভুবন ভুলে ভণে নরহরি ॥

*kata sādhe dekhe ām̐khi bhari |*
*śobhāya bhubana bhule bhaṇe narahari ||*

*Word for word:* kata sādhe — with what longing; dekhe ām̐khi bhari — they look, filling their eyes; śobhāya bhubana bhule — by the beauty the world is lost in forgetfulness; bhaṇe narahari — says Narahari

**16.9.** With what longing they gaze, filling their eyes!
This beauty makes the world forget everything, says Narahari.

[^18-39]: GPT1 — p. 327, sec. 5.1 (subsection "janma-līlā"), no. 20 (kamoda); GPT2 — sec. 5.1, no. 20 (catalogue: NG-162). BR — 12th wave
(ed. 1912, pp. 930–931; ed. 1960, vv. 3160–3168). According to the BR account (vv. 3148–3159), one day in the house of Srivasa the Lord
said, laughing: "Tomorrow is Krishna's birthday"; Srivasa and the others prepared everything, at night they performed Krishna's
abhisheka and spent the night in sankirtana; in the morning the Lord and His associates put on cowherd dress (Nityananda was the most
skilful at it), with pots of yoghurt and butter on carrying-poles they entered Srivasa's courtyard, Srivasa and Advaita scattered
yoghurt and turmeric — "the house of Srivasa became like the house of Nanda". Not in PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
Nanda-utsava is the festival on the day after Janmashtami (Krishna's birth, Bhadra krishna-ashtami): the cowherds of Vraja in their joy
drenched one another with milk, yoghurt and butter (Bhag. 10.5). Cf. CC Madhya 15 — Nanda-utsava in Puri, where the Lord also
appears in cowherd dress.
[^18-40]: Ramai is probably Abhirama (Ramadasa), Sundara is Sundarananda: both among the twelve "cowherd boys" (gopalas) of Nityananda;
Gauridasa Pandita is Subala in Krishna-lila. In this lila they reveal their eternal bhava of cowherd friends.
[^18-41]: Auspicious rites (maṅgala) — the "ulu-ulu" cry, lamps and so on, with which women greet the birth of a child; Nanda is Krishna's
foster-father in Vraja.

## 17. Narahari — "gokulera śaśī gorā guṇarāśi…" (GPT1 pp. 327–328, no. 21; BR)
*Nanda-utsava: on the day of His former birth Gora dances in cowherd dress; Nitai dances with Ramai and Sundara, Advaita pours a pot of
yoghurt on His head, Srivasa and others sprinkle turmeric on Advaita, Shankara and Murari dance with carrying-poles, Mukunda and others
sing. Raga dhanashi. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave); Bengali tripadi.*[^18-42]

গোকুলের শশী গোরা গুণরাশি পূরুব-জনম-দিনে ।
কত না উলাসে নাচে গোপবেশে সে ভাব-আবেশ-মনে ॥

*gokulera śaśī gorā guṇarāśi pūruba-janama-dine |*
*kata nā ulāse nāce gopabeśe se bhāba-ābeśa-mane ||*

*Word for word:* gokulera śaśī — the moon of Gokula; gorā guṇarāśi — Gora, treasury of virtues; pūruba-janama-dine — on the day of the former birth; kata nā ulāse — with what joy; nāce gopa-beśe — dances in cowherd dress; se bhāba-ābeśa-mane — with a mind absorbed in that bhava

**17.1.** The moon of Gokula, Gora, a treasury of virtues — on the day of His former birth
with what joy He dances in cowherd dress, His heart seized by that bhava!

নিতাই আনন্দে নাচে গোপছন্দে রামাই সুন্দর সাথে ।
অদ্বৈত ধাইয়া দধিভাণ্ড লৈয়া ঢালয়ে নিতাই-মাথে ॥

*nitāi ānande nāce gopachande rāmāi sundara sāthe |*
*advaita dhāiyā dadhibhāṇḍa laiyā ḍhālaye nitāi-māthe ||*

*Word for word:* nitāi ānande nāce — Nitai dances in bliss; gopa-chande — in cowherd fashion; rāmāi sundara sāthe — with Ramai and Sundara; advaita dhāiyā — Advaita, running up; dadhi-bhāṇḍa laiyā — taking a pot of yoghurt; ḍhālaye nitāi-māthe — pours it on Nitai's head

**17.2.** Nitai in bliss dances in cowherd fashion together with Ramai and Sundara;
Advaita, running up with a pot of yoghurt, pours it on Nitai's head.

শ্রীবাসাদি রঙ্গে অদ্বৈতের অঙ্গে হরিদ্রা সিঞ্চিয়া হাসে ।
শঙ্কর মুরারি কাঁধে ভার করি নাচয়ে গোপের বেশে ॥

*śrībāsādi raṅge advaitera aṅge haridrā siñciyā hāse |*
*śaṅkara murāri kām̐dhe bhāra kari nācaye gopera beśe ||*

*Word for word:* śrībāsa-ādi raṅge — Srivasa and others, playfully; advaitera aṅge — on Advaita's body; haridrā siñciyā hāse — sprinkle turmeric and laugh; śaṅkara murāri — Shankara and Murari; kām̐dhe bhāra kari — with poles on their shoulders; nācaye gopera beśe — dance in cowherd dress

**17.3.** Srivasa and the others playfully sprinkle turmeric on Advaita and laugh;
Shankara and Murari, carrying-poles on their shoulders, dance in cowherd dress.

মুকুন্দাদি গায় নানা বাদ্য বায় হেরি গোরা-মুখ-ইন্দু ।
নরহরি ভালে ভণে তিলে তিলে উথলে আনন্দ-সিন্ধু ॥

*mukundādi gāya nānā bādya bāya heri gorā-mukha-indu |*
*narahari bhāle bhaṇe tile tile uthale ānanda-sindhu ||*

*Word for word:* mukunda-ādi gāya — Mukunda and others sing; nānā bādya bāya — play various instruments; heri gorā-mukha-indu — gazing at the moon of Gora's face; narahari bhāle bhaṇe — Narahari sings well; tile tile — moment by moment; uthale ānanda-sindhu — the ocean of bliss swells

**17.4.** Mukunda and the others sing and play various instruments, gazing at the moon of Gora's face;
Narahari sings well: moment by moment the ocean of bliss swells.

[^18-42]: GPT1 — pp. 327–328, no. 21 (dhanashi); GPT2 — sec. 5.1, no. 21 (catalogue: NG-163). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 931; ed. 1960,
vv. 3169–3172), right after the preceding one. Not in PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. Shankara is Shankara Pandita, brother of
Damodara Pandita; Murari is Murari Gupta.

## 18. Narahari Dasa — "gauraguṇamaṇi barajaśaśadhara…" (GPT1 p. 328, no. 22; BR)
*Nanda-utsava: on the day of Krishna's birth, the eighth of Bhadra, Gaura is with His associates in the house of Srivasa; like the
cowherds of Vraja all put on turbans, flowers, bracelets; with carrying-poles and staffs they dance in a courtyard covered with mud of
turmeric, yoghurt and butter, crying "hi-hi!"; Nitai sprinkles turmeric on the Lord, Advaita smears Nitai's face with butter, they roll
in the mud; the gods shower flowers, people run from all sides. Raga mayura. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the
BR (12th wave); Vrajabuli with long chains of assonance.*[^18-43]

গৌরগুণমণি বরজ-শশধর পূরুব-প্রকট সু-অটমী ভাদর আদরই প্রিয়বৃন্দ সহ শিরিবাস-ভবনে বিরাজয়ে ।
বাঁধি নটপটি পাগ মৃদুতর কুসুম-পল্লব ধরত শির-পর বলয় কর কটি-বসন নব ব্রজ-গোপ-সম সব সাজয়ে ॥

*gauraguṇamaṇi baraja-śaśadhara pūruba-prakaṭa su-aṭamī bhādara ādarai priyabṛnda saha śiribāsa-bhabane birājaye |*
*bām̐dhi naṭapaṭi pāga mṛdutara kusuma-pallaba dharata śira-para balaya kara kaṭi-basana naba braja-gopa-sama saba sājaye ||*

*Word for word:* gaura-guṇamaṇi — Gaura, the jewel of virtues; baraja-śaśadhara — the moon of Vraja; pūruba-prakaṭa su-aṭamī bhādara — on the eighth of Bhadra, when He appeared before; ādarai priya-bṛnda saha — lovingly, with His dear associates; śiribāsa-bhabane birājaye — abides in Srivasa's house; bām̐dhi naṭapaṭi pāga mṛdutara — tying soft jaunty turbans; kusuma-pallava dharata śira-para — putting flowers and leaves on their heads; balaya kara — bracelets on the hands; kaṭi-basana naba — new waistcloths; braja-gopa-sama saba sājaye — all dress like the cowherds of Vraja

**18.1.** Gaura, the jewel of virtues, the moon of Vraja — on the eighth day of Bhadra, when He appeared before — lovingly abides with
His associates in the house of Srivasa;
tying soft, jaunty turbans, adorning their heads with flowers and leaves, putting on bracelets and new waistcloths, all dress like
the cowherds of Vraja.

ভাণ্ড দধিযুত চিত্র বাঁহুক কাঁধে করু করে লগুড় কাহুক ভঙ্গী সঞে চলি হলদি-দধি-ঘৃত-পঙ্ক অঙ্গনে শোহয়ে ।
হি হি শবদ উচারি ঘন ঘন বিপুল পুলকিত তরল তনু-মন করত সুললিত নৃত্য নিরুপম নিখিল ভুবন বিমোহয়ে ॥

*bhāṇḍa dadhiyuta citra bām̐huka kām̐dhe karu kare laguṛa kāhuka bhaṅgī sañe cali haladi-dadhi-ghṛta-paṅka aṅgane śohaye |*
*hi hi śabada ucāri ghana ghana bipula pulakita tarala tanu-mana karata sulalita nṛtya nirupama nikhila bhubana bimohaye ||*

*Word for word:* bhāṇḍa dadhi-yuta — pots with yoghurt; citra bām̐huka — painted carrying-poles; kām̐dhe karu — some on their shoulders; kare laguṛa kāhuka — some with staffs in hand; bhaṅgī sañe cali — walking gracefully; haladi-dadhi-ghṛta-paṅka aṅgane śohaye — shine in the courtyard with mud of turmeric, yoghurt and butter; hi hi śabada ucāri ghana ghana — crying "hi-hi" again and again; bipula pulakita — with abundant thrills; tarala tanu-mana — stirred in body and mind; karata sulalita nṛtya nirupama — dance with peerless grace; nikhila bhubana bimohaye — enchanting the whole world

**18.2.** Some carry on their shoulders painted poles with pots of yoghurt, others have staffs in their hands; stepping gracefully,
they shine in the courtyard, where there is a mud of turmeric, yoghurt and butter;
crying "hi-hi!" without end, covered with thrills, stirred in body and mind, they dance with peerless grace, enchanting the whole
world.[^18-44]

হাসি হরষে নিতাই কহি কত হলদি দধি পহু-অঙ্গে ছিরকত তুরিতে তহি অদ্বৈত নবনী নিতাই-বদনে বিলেপয়ে ।
ধরল প্রবল নিতাই কৌতুকে ভারি কর্দমে যাত গড়ি সুখে লপটি ঝট অদ্বৈত নটত তহি গগনে ভুজ বিক্ষেপয়ে ॥

*hāsi haraṣe nitāi kahi kata haladi dadhi pahu-aṅge chirakata turite tahi advaita nabanī nitāi-badane bilepaye |*
*dharala prabala nitāi kautuke bhāri kardame yāta gaṛi sukhe lapaṭi jhaṭa advaita naṭata tahi gagane bhuja bikṣepaye ||*

*Word for word:* hāsi haraṣe — laughing with joy; nitāi kahi kata — Nitai, saying so much; haladi dadhi pahu-aṅge chirakata — sprinkles turmeric and yoghurt on the Lord's body; turite tahi — at once; advaita nabanī nitāi-badane bilepaye — Advaita smears fresh butter on Nitai's face; dharala prabala nitāi kautuke — mighty Nitai playfully seizes (Him); bhāri kardame yāta gaṛi sukhe — they roll happily in the thick mud; lapaṭi jhaṭa — all smeared, at once; advaita naṭata tahi — Advaita dances there; gagane bhuja bikṣepaye — flinging his arms to the sky

**18.3.** Laughing with joy, Nitai says so many things and sprinkles turmeric and yoghurt on the Lord's body; at once Advaita smears
fresh butter on Nitai's face;
mighty Nitai playfully seizes Him, and they roll with delight in the thick mud; all smeared, Advaita dances there at once, flinging
His arms to the sky.

বাসুদেব মুকুন্দ মাধব আদি গায়ত জনম-উৎসব ধা ধি ধিকি তক ধিনি নি নি বহু বাদ্য বাদক বায়ই ।
দেবগণ ঘন কুসুম বরষত দাস নরহরি নাথে নিরখত কোই ধরই ন ধিরজ ভর নরনারী চহুদিশ ধায়ই ॥

*bāsudeba mukunda mādhaba ādi gāyata janama-utsaba dhā dhi dhiki taka dhini ni ni bahu bādya bādaka bāyai |*
*debagaṇa ghana kusuma baraṣata dāsa narahari nāthe nirakhata koi dharai na dhiraja bhara naranārī cahudiśa dhāyai ||*

*Word for word:* bāsudeba mukunda mādhaba ādi — Vasudeva, Mukunda, Madhava and others; gāyata janama-utsaba — sing of the festival of the birth; dhā dhi dhiki taka dhini ni ni — rhythmic syllables; bahu bādya bādaka bāyai — musicians play many instruments; deba-gaṇa ghana kusuma baraṣata — the gods shower flowers profusely; dāsa narahari nāthe nirakhata — Narahari Dasa gazes at his Lord; koi dharai na dhiraja — no one keeps composure; bhara nara-nārī cahu-diśa dhāyai — men and women run from all sides

**18.4.** Vasudeva, Mukunda, Madhava and others sing of the festival of the birth; the musicians play many instruments: "dha-dhi-
dhiki-taka-dhini-ni-ni";
the gods shower flowers, Narahari Dasa gazes at his Lord; no one can keep his composure — men and women run from all sides.

[^18-43]: GPT1 — p. 328, no. 22 (mayura); GPT2 — sec. 5.1, no. 22. The pada was not in the catalogue — **new row NG-258**. BR — 12th wave
(ed. 1912, pp. 931–932; ed. 1960, vv. 3173–3176), right after the preceding one. Not in PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. The
eighth day of the dark half of Bhadra (August–September) is Janmashtami; "before" — in Krishna-lila.
[^18-44]: "Hi-hi!" is the cowherds' cry. The playful romp of Nityananda and Advaita in the mud of yoghurt and turmeric is a game of the
Nanda-utsava, in which the Lord's associates reveal the bhava of the cowherd boys of Vraja (cf. CC Madhya 15).

## 19. Narahari — "āju gorācām̐da gaṇasaha gopabeśe…" (GPT1 p. 328, no. 23; BR)
*Radhashtami in the house of Pundarika Vidyanidhi: Gorachand with His associates in cowherd dress, smiling, looks at Gadadhara and
weeps with bliss; Mukunda, Madhava and Vasu sing of Radhika's birth, the Lord dances, the earth sways; Gauridasa with a carrying-pole,
Vidyanidhi scatters butter, turmeric, milk and yoghurt; men and women run to see; Narahari dances crying "Glory!". Raga kamoda.
**Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave, the account of Radhashtami); Bengali payar.*[^18-45]

আজু গোরাচাঁদ গণসহ গোপবেশে ।
তিলে তিলে অধিক বিভোল সে না রসে ॥

*āju gorācām̐da gaṇasaha gopabeśe |*
*tile tile adhika bibhola se nā rase ||*

*Word for word:* āju gorācām̐da — today Gorachand; gaṇa-saha gopa-beśe — with His associates in cowherd dress; tile tile adhika bibhola — moment by moment more absorbed; se nā rase — in that rasa

**19.1.** Today Gorachand with His associates in cowherd dress
moment by moment sinks deeper into that rasa.

হাসে লহু লহু চাহে গদাধর-পানে ।
বহয়ে আনন্দ-বারিধারা দু-নয়নে ॥

*hāse lahu lahu cāhe gadādhara-pāne |*
*bahaye ānanda-bāridhārā du-nayane ||*

*Word for word:* hāse lahu lahu — smiles gently; cāhe gadādhara-pāne — looks at Gadadhara; bahaye ānanda-bāri-dhārā — streams of tears of bliss flow; du-nayane — from both eyes

**19.2.** Gently smiling, He looks at Gadadhara;
streams of tears of bliss flow from both His eyes.[^18-46]

মুকুন্দ মাধব বাসু উল্লাস-হিয়ায় ।
রাধিকা-জনম-চরিত সবে গায় ॥

*mukunda mādhaba bāsu ullāsa-hiyāya |*
*rādhikā-janama-carita sabe gāya ||*

*Word for word:* mukunda mādhaba bāsu — Mukunda, Madhava and Vasu; ullāsa-hiyāya — with joy in their hearts; rādhikā-janama-carita — of Radhika's birth; sabe gāya — all sing

**19.3.** Mukunda, Madhava and Vasu, with joy in their hearts —
all sing of the birth of Radhika.

বাজে খোল করতাল ভুবন-মঙ্গল ।
নাচে পহু ধরণী করয়ে টলমল ॥

*bāje khola karatāla bhubana-maṅgala |*
*nāce pahu dharaṇī karaye ṭalamala ||*

*Word for word:* bāje khola karatāla — khol and karatalas sound; bhubana-maṅgala — auspicious for the world; nāce pahu — the Lord dances; dharaṇī karaye ṭalamala — the earth sways

**19.4.** The khol and karatalas sound, auspicious for the world;
the Lord dances — the earth sways.

গৌরীদাস আদি নাচে ভার করি কাঁধে ।
দেখিতে গোপবেশ কেবা থির বাঁধে ॥

*gaurīdāsa ādi nāce bhāra kari kām̐dhe |*
*dekhite gopabeśa kebā thira bām̐dhe ||*

*Word for word:* gaurīdāsa ādi — Gauridasa and others; nāce bhāra kari kām̐dhe — dance with poles on their shoulders; dekhite gopa-beśa — seeing the cowherd dress; kebā thira bām̐dhe — who can stay calm

**19.5.** Gauridasa and others dance with carrying-poles on their shoulders;
seeing this cowherd dress, who can stay calm?

কত সাধে নাচে পুণ্ডরীক বিদ্যানিধি ।
ছড়াইয়া নবনী হলদি দুধ দধি ॥

*kata sādhe nāce puṇḍarīka bidyānidhi |*
*chaṛāiyā nabanī haladi dudha dadhi ||*

*Word for word:* kata sādhe — with what fervour; nāce puṇḍarīka bidyānidhi — Pundarika Vidyanidhi dances; chaṛāiyā nabanī haladi dudha dadhi — scattering butter, turmeric, milk and yoghurt

**19.6.** With what fervour Pundarika Vidyanidhi dances,
scattering butter, turmeric, milk and yoghurt!

নিতাই অদ্বৈত শ্রীবাসাদি রঙ্গ দেখি ।
ভাসে সুখ-সমুদ্রে ফিরাতে নারে আঁখি ॥

*nitāi advaita śrībāsādi raṅga dekhi |*
*bhāse sukha-samudre phirāte nāre ām̐khi ||*

*Word for word:* nitāi advaita śrībāsa-ādi — Nitai, Advaita, Srivasa and others; raṅga dekhi — seeing the play; bhāse sukha-samudre — float in an ocean of happiness; phirāte nāre ām̐khi — cannot turn their eyes away

**19.7.** Nitai, Advaita, Srivasa and the others, seeing this play,
float in an ocean of happiness and cannot take their eyes away.

কি নারী পুরুষ ধায় এ রঙ্গ দেখিতে ।
দাঁড়াইয়া অঙ্গনে চাহয়ে চারি ভিতে ॥

*ki nārī puruṣa dhāya e raṅga dekhite |*
*dām̐ṛāiyā aṅgane cāhaye cāri bhite ||*

*Word for word:* ki nārī puruṣa — women and men alike; dhāya e raṅga dekhite — run to see this play; dām̐ṛāiyā aṅgane — standing in the courtyard; cāhaye cāri bhite — look on all sides

**19.8.** Men and women run to see this play;
standing in the courtyard, they look in all directions.

দেখি গোরারূপের মাধুরী অনুপাম ।
কেহ কহে নাচে এ কি কনকের কাম ॥

*dekhi gorārūpera mādhurī anupāma |*
*keha kahe nāce e ki kanakera kāma ||*

*Word for word:* dekhi gorā-rūpera mādhurī anupāma — seeing the peerless sweetness of Gora's form; keha kahe — some say; nāce e ki kanakera kāma — is it a golden Kama dancing

**19.9.** Seeing the peerless sweetness of Gora's form,
some say: "Is it not a golden Kama dancing?"[^18-47]

দেবগণ নাচয়ে কুসুমবৃষ্টি করি ।
জয় জয় দিয়া রঙ্গে নাচে নরহরি ॥

*debagaṇa nācaye kusumabṛṣṭi kari |*
*jaya jaya diyā raṅge nāce narahari ||*

*Word for word:* deba-gaṇa nācaye — the gods dance; kusuma-bṛṣṭi kari — showering flowers; jaya jaya diyā — crying "glory, glory"; raṅge nāce narahari — Narahari dances joyfully

**19.10.** The gods dance, showering flowers;
joyfully Narahari dances with cries of "Glory, glory!"

[^18-45]: GPT1 — p. 328, no. 23 (kamoda); GPT2 — sec. 5.1, no. 23 (catalogue: NG-234, formerly NS-017; there and in the sweep the
signature is "nāce narahari"). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, pp. 932–933; ed. 1960, vv. 3183–3192): one day the Lord, laughing, said to Pundarika
Vidyanidhi: "Tomorrow at your house is the festival of the birth of Sri Radhika"; Vidyanidhi prepared everything, and the next day the
Lord came to him with His associates, and an abhisheka in honour of Radhika's birth was performed there (vv. 3177–3182). Not in PK, KGC,
PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. Radhashtami is the eighth day of the bright half of Bhadra, the day of Sri Radha's appearance. Pundarika
Vidyanidhi is an associate of the Lord, in Krishna-lila Vrishabhanu, Radha's father (Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika 54), hence the festival
is held at his house.
[^18-46]: Gadadhara is the Radha of Krishna-lila (note 9): on Radha's birthday the Lord looks at him with bliss.
[^18-47]: "A golden Kama" is an image of the Lord's beauty (cf. note 11); among the onlookers are both men and women — this is not the
nagari motif.

## 20. Narahari Dasa — "rādhikā-janama-utsabe mātiche…" (GPT1 p. 329, no. 25)
*Radhashtami: Gora rejoices at the festival of Radhika's birth, and with Him in cowherd dress dance His associates skilled in dancing;
the madal, khol, cymbals, karatalas, khamaka, ramashinga, gopi-yantra and khanjari resound; Mukunda and others sing, the boys take up the
melody; the sound of conches and the cowherds' call mingle with it — and the poet sings together with all. Raga dhanashi. **Attribution:
not established** — the pada is not in the BR; the language is late Bengali (present continuous forms: mātiche, bājiche, miśiche, gāiche)
with heaped-up onomatopoeia; probably a comparatively late pada.*[^18-48]

রাধিকা-জনম-উৎসবে মাতিছে শচীর দুলাল গোরা রঙ্গিয়া ।
গোপবেশ ধরি নাচে তার সাথে নটন-পণ্ডিত সুঘড় সঙ্গিয়া ॥

*rādhikā-janama-utsabe mātiche śacīra dulāla gorā raṅgiyā |*
*gopabeśa dhari nāce tāra sāthe naṭana-paṇḍita sughaṛa saṅgiyā ||*

*Word for word:* rādhikā-janama-utsabe — at the festival of Radhika's birth; mātiche — is rapt; śacīra dulāla gorā raṅgiyā — joyful Gora, Shachi's darling; gopa-beśa dhari — wearing cowherd dress; nāce tāra sāthe — dance with Him; naṭana-paṇḍita sughaṛa saṅgiyā — the associates, skilled masters of dance

**20.1.** At the festival of Radhika's birth Gora, Shachi's darling, full of joy, is rapt;
putting on cowherd dress, His associates skilled in dancing dance with Him.

বাজিছে মাদল তাদৃম্ তাদৃম্ ধিক ধিন্না তালে বাজিছে খোল ।
ঝনানা ঝনান্ ঝাঁঝরির বোল বাজে করতাল করি ঘোর রোল ॥

*bājiche mādala tādṛm tādṛm dhika dhinnā tāle bājiche khola |*
*jhanānā jhanān jhām̐jharira bola bāje karatāla kari ghora rola ||*

*Word for word:* bājiche mādala — the madal booms; tādṛm tādṛm — "tadrim, tadrim"; dhika dhinnā tāle — to the beat "dhika-dhinna"; bājiche khola — the khol sounds; jhanānā jhanān — "jhanana-jhanan"; jhām̐jharira bola — the clash of the cymbals; bāje karatāla — the karatalas sound; kari ghora rola — with a loud din

**20.2.** The madal booms: "tadrim, tadrim", to the beat "dhika-dhinna" the khol sounds;
"jhanana-jhanan" — the clash of cymbals, the karatalas sound with a loud din.[^18-49]

গাব গাব গাব খমক গমকে ভেউ ভেউ ভোঁ ভোঁ রামশিঙ্গা বাজে ।
ডিম্ ডিম্ ডিম্ গোপীযন্ত্র বাজে তাকৃতা তাধিন্ খঞ্জরি বাজে ॥

*gāba gāba gāba khamaka gamake bheu bheu bhom̐ bhom̐ rāmaśiṅgā bāje |*
*ḍim ḍim ḍim gopīyantra bāje tākṛtā tādhin khañjari bāje ||*

*Word for word:* gāba gāba gāba — "gab-gab-gab"; khamaka gamake — the khamaka resounds; bheu bheu bhom̐ bhom̐ — "bheu-bheu, bhon-bhon"; rāmaśiṅgā bāje — the ramashinga blares; ḍim ḍim ḍim — "dim-dim-dim"; gopīyantra bāje — the gopi-yantra sounds; tākṛtā tādhin — "takrita-tadhin"; khañjari bāje — the khanjari sounds

**20.3.** "Gab-gab-gab" — the khamaka resounds, "bheu-bheu, bhon-bhon" — the ramashinga blares;
"dim-dim-dim" — the gopi-yantra sounds, "takrita-tadhin" — the khanjari tambourine.

খরজে গায়ত মুকুন্দাদি সব পঞ্চমে বালক ধরয়ে তান ।
রহি রহি রহি উঠে তিন গ্রামে সপ্তস্বর সঙ্গে মূর্ছনা মান ॥

*kharaje gāyata mukundādi saba pañcame bālaka dharaye tāna |*
*rahi rahi rahi uṭhe tina grāme saptasvara saṅge mūrchanā māna ||*

*Word for word:* kharaje gāyata — sing on the low notes; mukunda-ādi saba — Mukunda and all others; pañcame bālaka dharaye tāna — the boys take the melody on the fifth; rahi rahi rahi — again and again; uṭhe tina grāme — rises in three registers; sapta-svara saṅge mūrchanā māna — the seven notes with the murchhanas

**20.4.** Mukunda and all the others sing on the low notes, the boys take the melody on the fifth;
again and again in three registers the seven notes rise with all the murchhanas.[^18-50]

শঙ্খ কাংস্য রব তা সহ মিশিছে তা সহ মিশিছে আবাবা ধ্বনি ।
তা সহ গাইছে দাস নরহরি বলিহারি যাই গোরার নিছনি ॥

*śaṅkha kāṃsya raba tā saha miśiche tā saha miśiche ābābā dhvani |*
*tā saha gāiche dāsa narahari balihāri yāi gorāra nichani ||*

*Word for word:* śaṅkha kāṃsya raba — the sound of conches and gongs; tā saha miśiche — mingles with it; ābābā dhvani — the cowherds' call "aba-aba"; tā saha gāiche — with it sings; dāsa narahari — Narahari Dasa; balihāri yāi — I offer myself; gorāra nichani — as a sacrifice for Gora

**20.5.** With this mingles the boom of conches and gongs, mingles the cowherds' call "aba-aba";
together with all sings Narahari Dasa: "I offer myself in sacrifice for Gora!"[^18-51]

[^18-48]: GPT1 — p. 329, no. 25 (dhanashi; text checked against the scan, PDF p. 588); GPT2 — sec. 5.1, no. 25 (catalogue: NG-164). Before
it (no. 24) stands a pada on the same festival signed "Ghanashyama" (it is also in the BR; not included in the appendix). This pada is
not in BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. C.
[^18-49]: The madal is a large drum; the khol is the clay drum of kirtana; cymbals (jhām̐jhari) and karatalas are small brass cymbals.
[^18-50]: The khamaka is a one-stringed plucked instrument; the ramashinga a curved horn; the gopi-yantra a one-stringed instrument of
wandering singers; the khanjari a tambourine. The low notes are shadja (kharaja); the fifth is panchama; three registers (gramas), seven
notes (svaras), murchhanas — concepts of Indian music theory.
[^18-51]: "Ava-aba" (ābābā) is the cry of cowherds calling the cows (cf. the padas on taking out the cows: "ābā ābā rabe"). "I offer myself
in sacrifice" (balihāri yāi… nichani) is an expression of utmost devotion.

## 21. Narahari — "sarasa suradhunī-pulina-bana…" (GPT1 p. 334, no. 43; BR)
*Remembrance of the rasa-lila: seeing the grove on the sandy bank of the Suradhuni, young Gaura remembers the former play of the rasa and is
absorbed in bliss; His face eclipses the moon, He dances in the threefold bend to the sweet thunder of the mridanga, the associates sing of
the rasa of the rasa dance, and Narahari's heart overflows. Raga shri. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th
wave, the account of the rasa-lila in Navadvipa); Vrajabuli.*[^18-52]

সরস সুরধুনী-পুলিন-বন অবলোকি গৌরকিশোর ।
পূরুব রাসবিলাস সোঙরি উলাসে ভৈ গেল ভোর ॥

*sarasa suradhunī-pulina-bana abaloki gaurakiśora |*
*pūruba rāsabilāsa soṅari ulāse bhai gela bhora ||*

*Word for word:* sarasa suradhunī-pulina-bana — the grove on the lovely sandy bank of the Suradhuni (Ganga); abaloki — seeing; gaura-kiśora — young Gaura; pūruba rāsa-bilāsa — the former play of the rasa; soṅari — remembering; ulāse bhai gela bhora — became absorbed in joy

**21.1.** Seeing the grove on the lovely sandy bank of the Suradhuni, young Gaura
remembered the former play of the rasa — and was absorbed in joy.[^18-53]

মদন-মদভর-হরণ তনু জনু দমকে দামিনী-দাম ।
বদন-বিধু বিধু-কদন মাধুরী অমিয়া ঝরে অবিরাম ॥

*madana-madabhara-haraṇa tanu janu damake dāminī-dāma |*
*badana-bidhu bidhu-kadana mādhurī amiyā jhare abirāma ||*

*Word for word:* madana-mada-bhara-haraṇa tanu — the body that takes away Madana's pride; janu damake dāminī-dāma — flashes like a garland of lightning; badana-bidhu — the moon-face; bidhu-kadana — tormenting the moon; mādhurī amiyā jhare abirāma — its sweetness pours nectar without end

**21.2.** His body, which takes away Madana's pride, flashes like a garland of lightning;
the sweetness of His moon-face, which eclipses the moon, pours down nectar without end.

আজু নিরুপম নটন ঘটইতে হোত ললিত ত্রিভঙ্গ ।
দ্রিমিকি দ্রিমি দ্রিমি দ্রিম্ বাজত মধুর মধুর মৃদঙ্গ ॥

*āju nirupama naṭana ghaṭaite hota lalita tribhaṅga |*
*drimiki drimi drimi drim bājata madhura madhura mṛdaṅga ||*

*Word for word:* āju — today; nirupama naṭana ghaṭaite — performing a peerless dance; hota lalita tribhaṅga — He takes a charming threefold bend; drimiki drimi drimi drim — drum syllables; bājata madhura madhura mṛdaṅga — the mridanga sounds sweetly, sweetly

**21.3.** Today, performing a peerless dance, He stands in a charming threefold bend;
"drimiki-drimi-drimi-drim" — sweetly, sweetly the mridanga sounds.

সুঘড় পরিকরবৃন্দ গায়ত রাসরস মুদ মাতি ।
দেব-দুলহ সে বিপুল কৌতুকে উথলে নরহরি-ছাতি ॥

*sughaṛa parikarabṛnda gāyata rāsarasa muda māti |*
*deba-dulaha se bipula kautuke uthale narahari-chāti ||*

*Word for word:* sughaṛa parikara-bṛnda — the skilful associates; gāyata rāsa-rasa — sing of the rasa of the rasa dance; muda māti — rapt in joy; deba-dulaha — rare for the gods; se bipula kautuke — at that great wonder; uthale narahari-chāti — Narahari's breast overflows

**21.4.** The skilful associates sing, rapt in the joy of the rasa of the rasa dance;
at this wondrous play, rare even for the gods, Narahari's breast overflows.

[^18-52]: GPT1 — p. 334, sec. 5.1 (subsection "rasa and maharasa"), no. 43 (shri); GPT2 — sec. 5.1, no. 43. The pada was not in the
catalogue — **new row NG-259**. BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 941; ed. 1960, vv. 3297–3300): "here Gaurachandra revealed great bliss,
remembering the former rasa of the rasa dance" (v. 3291), after a pada of Vasu Ghosha on the same subject. The GPT2 index assigns these
pages to Chakravarti. Not in PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. The next GPT pada (no. 44, "kī madhura madhuniśā" — the rasa of
Balarama revealed by Nityananda; in the catalogue wrongly VG-048, Vasu Ghosha) is also signed Narahari and also in the BR; as a pada about
Nityananda it is translated in chapter 24, no. 13 (new row NG-260).
[^18-53]: The rasa-lila is Krishna's circle dance with the gopis on an autumn night in Vrindavana (Bhag. 10.29–33), the summit of the lila
of love. The Lord, remembering it on the bank of the Ganga, experiences it as Krishna Himself; this is the pure prema of Vraja, not
worldly passion (Bhag. 10.33.39: one who hears of the rasa is freed from lust).

## 22. Narahari — "basanta samaya suśobhita…" (GPT1 p. 338, no. 55; BR)
*Spring in Nadia: the trees and creepers blossom, the cuckoos call, the bees hum, the southern breeze blows; Gora, the Nagara of Gokula,
plays with His associates on the bank of the Suradhuni: Mukunda and Madhava sing, all throw flower-pollen phagu at one another, Nitai,
Advaita, Gadadhara and Srivasa play phagu; the gods cannot keep their composure. Raga basanta. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** —
the pada is in the BR (12th wave, the account of the spring games); Bengali payar.*[^18-54]

বসন্ত সময় সুশোভিত ।
নদীয়ার কিবা তরু লতা প্রফুল্লিত ॥

*basanta samaya suśobhita |*
*nadīyāra kibā taru latā praphullita ||*

*Word for word:* basanta samaya — the springtime; suśobhita — is beautiful; nadīyāra kibā taru latā — how the trees and creepers of Nadia; praphullita — are in bloom

**22.1.** Beautiful is the springtime:
how the trees and creepers of Nadia blossom!

কুহরে কোকিল অনিবার ।
ভ্রময়ে ভ্রমরপুঞ্জ করয়ে গুঞ্জার ॥

*kuhare kokila anibāra |*
*bhramaye bhramarapuñja karaye guñjāra ||*

*Word for word:* kuhare kokila anibāra — the cuckoos call ceaselessly; bhramaye bhramara-puñja — swarms of bees roam; karaye guñjāra — and hum

**22.2.** Ceaselessly the cuckoos call,
swarms of bees roam about and hum.

বহে মন্দ মলয় সমীর ।
উথলয়ে হিয়া কেহ হৈতে নারে থির ॥

*bahe manda malaya samīra |*
*uthalaye hiyā keha haite nāre thira ||*

*Word for word:* bahe manda malaya samīra — the gentle southern breeze blows; uthalaye hiyā — the heart overflows; keha haite nāre thira — no one can remain still

**22.3.** A gentle southern breeze blows;
the heart overflows — no one can remain still.

গোকুলনাগর গোরা রঙ্গে ।
সুরধুনীতীরে বিহরয় গণ সঙ্গে ॥

*gokulanāgara gorā raṅge |*
*suradhunītīre biharaya gaṇa saṅge ||*

*Word for word:* gokula-nāgara gorā — Gora, the Nagara of Gokula; raṅge — joyfully; suradhunī-tīre — on the bank of the Suradhuni (Ganga); biharaya gaṇa saṅge — plays with His associates

**22.4.** Gora, the Nagara of Gokula, joyfully
plays with His associates on the bank of the Suradhuni.[^18-55]

মুকুন্দ মাধব আদি গায় ।
মৃদঙ্গ মন্দিরা নানা যন্ত্র সভে বায় ॥

*mukunda mādhaba ādi gāya |*
*mṛdaṅga mandirā nānā yantra sabhe bāya ||*

*Word for word:* mukunda mādhaba ādi gāya — Mukunda, Madhava and others sing; mṛdaṅga mandirā nānā yantra — the mridanga, the mandira and many instruments; sabhe bāya — all play

**22.5.** Mukunda, Madhava and others sing,
all play the mridanga, the mandira and many instruments.

পুষ্পের পরাগ ফাগু লৈয়া ।
হাসে মন্দ মন্দ কেহ গোরা-গায়ে দিয়া ॥

*puṣpera parāga phāgu laiyā |*
*hāse manda manda keha gorā-gāye diyā ||*

*Word for word:* puṣpera parāga phāgu laiyā — taking flower-pollen as phagu; hāse manda manda — laughs softly; keha — someone; gorā-gāye diyā — throwing it on Gora's body

**22.6.** Taking flower-pollen for phagu,
someone, softly laughing, throws it on Gora's body.[^18-56]

কেহ কেহ নাচে নানা ছাঁদে ।
সভার উপরে ফাগু ফেলে গোরাচাঁদে ॥

*keha keha nāce nānā chām̐de |*
*sabhāra upare phāgu phele gorācām̐de ||*

*Word for word:* keha keha nāce — some dance; nānā chām̐de — in various styles; sabhāra upare — over everyone; phāgu phele gorācām̐de — Gorachand throws phagu

**22.7.** Some dance in various ways;
Gorachand throws phagu over everyone.

নিতাই অদ্বৈত গদাধর ।
শ্রীবাসাদি ফাগুখেলা খেলে পরস্পর ॥

*nitāi advaita gadādhara |*
*śrībāsādi phāgukhelā khele paraspara ||*

*Word for word:* nitāi advaita gadādhara — Nitai, Advaita, Gadadhara; śrībāsa-ādi — Srivasa and others; phāgu-khelā khele paraspara — play phagu with one another

**22.8.** Nitai, Advaita, Gadadhara,
Srivasa and others play phagu with one another.

দেখি এ না অদ্ভুত বিহার ।
দেবগণ নারয়ে ধৈরজ ধরিবার ॥

*dekhi e nā adbhuta bihāra |*
*debagaṇa nāraye dhairaja dharibāra ||*

*Word for word:* dekhi e nā adbhuta bihāra — seeing this wondrous play; deba-gaṇa nāraye — the gods cannot; dhairaja dharibāra — keep their composure

**22.9.** Seeing this wondrous play,
the gods cannot keep their composure.

কেবা না করয়ে জয়ধ্বনি ।
নরহরি ভণে সুখে ভরল অবনী ॥

*kebā nā karaye jayadhvani |*
*narahari bhaṇe sukhe bharala abanī ||*

*Word for word:* kebā nā karaye jaya-dhvani — who does not cry "glory"; narahari bhaṇe — says Narahari; sukhe bharala abanī — the earth is filled with happiness

**22.10.** Who does not cry "Glory!"?
Narahari says: the earth is filled with happiness.

[^18-54]: GPT1 — p. 338, no. 55 (basanta); GPT2 — sec. 5.1, no. 55 (catalogue: NG-166). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, pp. 941–942; ed. 1960, vv.
3303–3312): "Gaurachandra plays in spring with His associates; here the wondrous phagu games began" (vv. 3301–3302). Not in PK, KGC, PS
or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^18-55]: "The Nagara of Gokula" (gokulanāgara) is an epithet of Krishna, the "skilful lover" of Vraja; here it indicates that Gaura is Krishna
Himself, not the nagari motif (cf. chapter 17, note 15).
[^18-56]: Phagu (phāgu) is the red powder (abir) people throw on one another at the spring festival of Holi (Dola-yatra, phalguna-purnima);
here flower-pollen is used instead.

## 23. Narahari — "phāgu khelata gaurakiśora…" (GPT1 p. 338, no. 56; BR)
*The phagu game: young Gaura in special attire, the radiance of His body eclipses lightning; with a golden syringe in hand He squirts
saffron water, the associates toss abir, and sky and earth turn red; the associates dance fearlessly, sing of the lilas of Vraja, and
cry "Ho-ho, Hari!" Raga basanta. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave); Vrajabuli.*[^18-57]

ফাগু খেলত গৌরকিশোর ।
বনি বেশ বিশেষ উজোর ॥

*phāgu khelata gaurakiśora |*
*bani beśa biśeṣa ujora ||*

*Word for word:* phāgu khelata — plays phagu; gaura-kiśora — young Gaura; bani beśa biśeṣa ujora — in special, radiant attire

**23.1.** Young Gaura plays phagu,
in special, radiant attire.

তনুরুচি জিনি দামিনী-দাম ।
তহি মূরছত কত শত কাম ॥

*tanuruci jini dāminī-dāma |*
*tahi mūrachata kata śata kāma ||*

*Word for word:* tanu-ruci — the radiance of the body; jini dāminī-dāma — surpassing a garland of lightning; tahi mūrachata — at it swoon; kata śata kāma — hundreds of Kamas

**23.2.** The radiance of His body surpasses a garland of lightning —
at the sight of it hundreds of Kamas swoon.

গহি কর কাঞ্চন-পিচকারী ।
বর বরষত কেশর-বারি ॥

*gahi kara kāñcana-picakārī |*
*bara baraṣata keśara-bāri ||*

*Word for word:* gahi kara kāñcana-picakārī — taking a golden syringe in hand; bara baraṣata keśara-bāri — He showers saffron water abundantly

**23.3.** Taking a golden syringe in His hand,
He squirts saffron water.

ঘন উড়ায়ত আবির গুলাল ।
সুরপুর পরশত মহী লাল ॥

*ghana uṛāyata ābira gulāla |*
*surapura paraśata mahī lāla ||*

*Word for word:* ghana uṛāyata ābira gulāla — they toss abir and gulal again and again; surapura paraśata — it touches the abode of the gods; mahī lāla — the earth is red

**23.4.** Without end they toss abir and gulal —
both the sky and the earth turn red.[^18-58]

লখি পহুক বয়ন-ময়ঙ্ক ।
পরিকরগণ নটত নিশঙ্ক ॥

*lakhi pahuka bayana-mayaṅka |*
*parikaragaṇa naṭata niśaṅka ||*

*Word for word:* lakhi pahuka bayana-mayaṅka — seeing the moon of the Lord's face; parikara-gaṇa naṭata niśaṅka — the associates dance without fear

**23.5.** Seeing the moon of the Lord's face,
the associates dance without fear.

মিলি গায়ত বরজ-বিহার ।
ধরু ধৈরজ ধরই ন পার ॥

*mili gāyata baraja-bihāra |*
*dharu dhairaja dharai na pāra ||*

*Word for word:* mili gāyata — together they sing; baraja-bihāra — of the lilas of Vraja; dharu dhairaja — composure; dharai na pāra — no one can keep

**23.6.** Together they sing of the lilas of Vraja;
no one can keep his composure.

বহু বায়ত যন্ত্র রসাল ।
উঘটত ধিকি ধিকি তক তাল ॥

*bahu bāyata yantra rasāla |*
*ughaṭata dhiki dhiki taka tāla ||*

*Word for word:* bahu bāyata yantra rasāla — they play many sweet instruments; ughaṭata — beat out; dhiki dhiki taka tāla — the rhythm "dhiki-dhiki-taka"

**23.7.** They play on many sweet-sounding instruments,
beating the rhythm "dhiki-dhiki-taka".

কহি হো হো হরি বিভোর ।
নরহরি কি ভণব মতি থোর ॥

*kahi ho ho hari bibhora |*
*narahari ki bhaṇaba mati thora ||*

*Word for word:* kahi ho ho hari — crying "Ho-ho, Hari"; bibhora — beside themselves; narahari ki bhaṇaba — what will Narahari say; mati thora — his mind is small

**23.8.** Crying "Ho-ho, Hari!", all are beside themselves;
what can Narahari, whose mind is so small, say?

[^18-57]: GPT1 — p. 338, no. 56 (basanta); GPT2 — sec. 5.1, no. 56 (catalogue: NG-167, its first line not recognised in the catalogue). BR —
12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 942; ed. 1960, vv. 3313–3320), right after the preceding one. Not in PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. The
next GPT pada (no. 57, "phāguyā khelata gaurakiśora") is signed "Ghanashyama" and is not included in the appendix.
[^18-58]: Abir and gulal are the red and pink powders of the spring festival; saffron water (keshara-vari) is coloured water with which people
drench one another.

## 24. Narahari — "gaura gokula-nāha naṭabara…" (GPT1 p. 339, no. 58; BR)
*A spring game on the bank of the Suradhuni: Gaura, the Lord of Gokula, best of dancers, with His associates dressed in every possible way;
His body eclipses a golden mountain, His face the moon; syringe in hand He tosses phagu; the associates cry "Hori!"; a cloud of gulal hides
the sun, the sky glows red; musk and saffron are poured on Nitai's head, Advaita frowns and claps His hands; the mridangas thunder. Raga
basanta. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave); Vrajabuli with long chains of assonance.*[^18-59]

গৌর গোকুল-নাহ নটবর বেশ বিরচি অশেষ পরিকর সঙ্গে সুরধুনীতীরে বিহরে বসন্ত-ঋতু-মুদ-বর্ধন ।
কনক-পর্বত-খর্বকৃত তনু-কিরণ মঞ্জু মনোজময় জনু ঝরত অমিয় সুহাস ঝলকত বদন বিধু-মদ-মর্দনা ॥

*gaura gokula-nāha naṭabara beśa biraci aśeṣa parikara saṅge suradhunītīre bihare basanta-ṛtu-muda-bardhana |*
*kanaka-parvata-kharvakṛta tanu-kiraṇa mañju manojamaya janu jharata amiya suhāsa jhalakata badana bidhu-mada-mardanā ||*

*Word for word:* gaura gokula-nāha naṭabara — Gaura, Lord of Gokula, best of dancers; beśa biraci aśeṣa parikara saṅge — with associates dressed in every way; suradhunī-tīre bihare — plays on the bank of the Suradhuni (Ganga); basanta-ṛtu-muda-bardhana — increasing the joy of spring; kanaka-parvata-kharvakṛta — humbling a golden mountain; tanu-kiraṇa — the radiance of His body; mañju manojamaya janu — lovely, as if made of Kama; jharata amiya suhāsa — a gentle smile pouring nectar; jhalakata — flashes; badana bidhu-mada-mardana — a face that crushes the moon's pride

**24.1.** Gaura, the Lord of Gokula, best of dancers, with His associates dressed in every way, plays on the bank of the Suradhuni,
increasing the joy of spring;
the radiance of His body humbles a golden mountain, lovely as Kama incarnate; a gentle smile pouring nectar flashes, His face crushes the
pride of the moon.

কঞ্জ-লোচন-যুগল সুললিত বঙ্ক চাহনি চপল অতুলিত ভঙ্গী সঞে পিচকারী গহি ফাগু ফেট ভরত উড়ায়ই ।
লসত চহুদিশ সুঘড় প্রিয়গণ সাজি অতিশয় মগন ঘন ঘন হোরি কহি কহি পেখি পহু-মুখ কো না নয়ন জুড়ায়ই ॥

*kañja-locana-yugala sulalita baṅka cāhani capala atulita bhaṅgī sañe picakārī gahi phāgu pheṭa bharata uṛāyai |*
*lasata cahudiśa sughaṛa priyagaṇa sāji atiśaya magana ghana ghana hori kahi kahi pekhi pahu-mukha ko nā nayana juṛāyai ||*

*Word for word:* kañja-locana-yugala sulalita — the pair of lotus eyes is charming; baṅka cāhani capala atulita — the sidelong glance restless and peerless; bhaṅgī sañe picakārī gahi — gracefully taking the syringe; phāgu pheṭa bharata uṛāyai — tosses phagu by handfuls; lasata cahudiśa sughaṛa priya-gaṇa — all around shine the skilful associates; sāji atiśaya magana ghana ghana — adorned, deeply immersed; hori kahi kahi — crying "Hori"; pekhi pahu-mukha — seeing the Lord's face; ko nā nayana juṛāyai — whose eyes are not soothed

**24.2.** His pair of lotus eyes is charming, His sidelong glance restless and peerless; gracefully taking the syringe, He tosses phagu
by handfuls;
around Him shine the skilful associates, adorned, immersed in bliss, and crying "Hori!" they look at the Lord's face — whose eyes would
not be soothed?[^18-60]

পরশ-পরবশ মাতি খেলত গগন-পন্থহি গুলাল মেলত ঝাঁপি দিনকর-কিরণ অম্বর অরুণ অতিশয় শোহয়ে ।
দলিত মৃগমদ-পঙ্ক কেশর ডারি হরষে নিতাই-শির-পর ভ্রুকুটি করি করতালিকা রচি অদ্বৈত জন-মন মোহয়ে ॥

*paraśa-parabaśa māti khelata gagana-panthahi gulāla melata jhām̐pi dinakara-kiraṇa ambara aruṇa atiśaya śohaye |*
*dalita mṛgamada-paṅka keśara ḍāri haraṣe nitāi-śira-para bhrukuṭi kari karatālikā raci advaita jana-mana mohaye ||*

*Word for word:* paraśa-parabaśa māti khelata — intoxicated by touch they play; gagana-panthahi gulāla melata — they fill the sky's path with gulal; jhām̐pi dinakara-kiraṇa — hiding the rays of the sun; ambara aruṇa atiśaya śohaye — the sky glows deep red; dalita mṛgamada-paṅka keśara — crushed musk paste and saffron; ḍāri haraṣe nitāi-śira-para — joyfully poured on Nitai's head; bhrukuṭi kari — knitting his brows; karatālikā raci — clapping his hands; advaita jana-mana mohaye — Advaita charms people's hearts

**24.3.** Intoxicated by touch they play, filling the path of the sky with gulal; hiding the rays of the sun, the sky glows red;
crushed paste of musk and saffron they joyfully pour on Nitai's head, while Advaita, knitting His brows and clapping His hands, charms
people's hearts.[^18-61]

নটন-পটু নট উঘটি থুঙ্গুট থেতা তক তক থোদি দ্রিমিকট দা দ্রিমিকি দ্রিমি দ্রিমিকি মুরজ মৃদঙ্গ বাদক বায়ই ।
ভণত নরহরি বলিত শ্রুতি স্বর গান করু গতিবৃন্দ সুমধুর ধিরজ পরিহরি নিখিল সুর-নর-নারী কৌতুকে ধায়ই ॥

*naṭana-paṭu naṭa ughaṭi thuṅguṭa thetā taka taka thodi drimikaṭa dā drimiki drimi drimiki muraja mṛdaṅga bādaka bāyai |*
