*bhaṇata narahari balita śruti svara gāna karu gatibṛnda sumadhura dhiraja parihari nikhila sura-nara-nārī kautuke dhāyai ||*

*Word for word:* naṭana-paṭu naṭa — skilful dancers (dance); ughaṭi — beating out; thuṅguṭa thetā taka taka thodi drimikaṭa dā drimiki drimi drimiki — drum syllables; muraja mṛdaṅga bādaka bāyai — the drummers play muraja and mridanga; bhaṇata narahari — says Narahari; balita śruti svara — keeping the shrutis and svaras; gāna karu gati-bṛnda sumadhura — the singers sing most sweetly; dhiraja parihari — abandoning composure; nikhila sura-nara-nārī — all gods, men and women; kautuke dhāyai — run eagerly

**24.4.** Skilful dancers dance, the drummers beat the mridanga and muraja: "thungut-theta-taka-taka-thodi-drimikat-da-drimiki-
drimi";
Narahari says: most sweetly the singers sing, keeping the shrutis and svaras — and all the gods, men and women, forgetting their
composure, run to see.

[^18-59]: GPT1 — p. 339, no. 58 (basanta); GPT2 — sec. 5.1, no. 58 (catalogue: NG-168). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 944; ed. 1960, vv.
3339–3342). Not in PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^18-60]: "Hori" (hori) is the cry of the Holi festival.
[^18-61]: Advaita's frowning is play: the elder associate "gets angry" to make everyone laugh (cf. no. 18).

## 25. Narahari — "suradhunītīre taruṇa taru-ballarī…" (GPT1 pp. 340–341, no. 63; BR)
*A spring dance: on the bank of the Suradhuni young trees and creepers in new leaves and flowers, the bees hum, intoxicated by the scent,
cuckoos and parrots flit around; there young Gaura dances, anointed with saffron, musk and sandal, red with phagu; the associates sing,
the gods cry "Glory!", Narahari plays the mridanga. Raga dhanashi or basanta. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the
BR (12th wave, in the cycle of the dance); Vrajabuli.*[^18-62]

সুরধুনীতীরে তরুণ তরু-বল্লরী পল্লব নব নব কুসুম-বিকাশ ।
পরিমলে মুগধ মধুপকুল কূজত কোকিল কীর ফিরত চহু পাশ ॥

*suradhunītīre taruṇa taru-ballarī pallaba naba naba kusuma-bikāśa |*
*parimale mugadha madhupakula kūjata kokila kīra phirata cahu pāśa ||*

*Word for word:* suradhunī-tīre — on the bank of the Suradhuni (Ganga); taruṇa taru-ballarī — young trees and creepers; pallava naba naba — ever new leaves; kusuma-bikāśa — flowers opening; parimale mugadha — enchanted by fragrance; madhupa-kula kūjata — swarms of bees hum; kokila kīra phirata cahu pāśa — cuckoos and parrots flit all around

**25.1.** On the bank of the Suradhuni are young trees and creepers — ever new leaves, flowers opening;
intoxicated by the fragrance, swarms of bees hum, cuckoos and parrots flit all around.

নাচত তহি নট গৌরকিশোর ।
কেশর মৃগমদ চন্দন-চরচিত ফাগু অরুণ তনু অধিক উজোর ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*nācata tahi naṭa gaurakiśora |*
*keśara mṛgamada candana-caracita phāgu aruṇa tanu adhika ujora || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* nācata tahi — there dances; naṭa gaura-kiśora — young Gaura, the dancer; keśara mṛgamada candana-caracita — anointed with saffron, musk and sandal; phāgu aruṇa tanu — the body red with phagu; adhika ujora — shines all the more

**25.2.** *(Refrain)* There young Gaura, the best of dancers, dances;
anointed with saffron, musk and sandal, His body, red with phagu, shines all the more.

নিরুপম বেশ বসন মণিভূষণ ঝলকত চারু চপল বনমাল ।
অভিনব ভঙ্গী ভুবন-মনমোহন ঘন ঘন ধরত চরণতলে তাল ॥

*nirupama beśa basana maṇibhūṣaṇa jhalakata cāru capala banamāla |*
*abhinaba bhaṅgī bhubana-manamohana ghana ghana dharata caraṇatale tāla ||*

*Word for word:* nirupama beśa basana maṇi-bhūṣaṇa — peerless attire, garments, jewelled ornaments; jhalakata cāru capala banamāla — the lovely garland of forest flowers sways; abhinaba bhaṅgī — with new movements; bhubana-mana-mohana — charming the hearts of the world; ghana ghana dharata caraṇa-tale tāla — again and again He beats time with His feet

**25.3.** Peerless attire, garments, jewelled ornaments; His garland of forest flowers sways charmingly;
with new movements that charm the hearts of the world, again and again He beats the rhythm with His feet.

গায়ত পরম মধুর পরিকরগণ নিরখি বদনশশী উলস অভঙ্গ ।
সুরগণ গগনে মগন ভণ জয় জয় বায়ত নরহরি মধুর মৃদঙ্গ ॥

*gāyata parama madhura parikaragaṇa nirakhi badanaśaśī ulasa abhaṅga |*
*suragaṇa gagane magana bhaṇa jaya jaya bāyata narahari madhura mṛdaṅga ||*

*Word for word:* gāyata parama madhura parikara-gaṇa — the associates sing most sweetly; nirakhi badana-śaśī — gazing at the moon of His face; ulasa abhaṅga — rejoicing without end; sura-gaṇa gagane magana — the gods in the sky, immersed; bhaṇa jaya jaya — cry "glory, glory"; bāyata narahari madhura mṛdaṅga — Narahari plays the sweet mridanga

**25.4.** Most sweetly the associates sing, gazing at the moon of His face, rejoicing without end;
the gods in the sky, immersed in bliss, cry "Glory, glory!", Narahari plays the sweet-sounding mridanga.

[^18-62]: GPT1 — pp. 340–341, no. 63 (dhanashi or basanta); GPT2 — sec. 5.1, no. 63 (catalogue: NG-169; in the GPT2 recognition the number is
"৬৬"). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, pp. 891–892; ed. 1960, vv. 2638–2641): in the BR this and the next pada stand in the cycle of the dance on
the bank of the Ganga, right after the pada "suradhunītīra parama niramala thala" (chapter 17, no. 21); after them — "having played on the
bank of the Ganga, the Lord went home this way" (v. 2650). Not in PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.

## 26. Narahari — "āju suradhunītīre sundara gaura nṛtye bibhora…" (GPT1 p. 342, no. 67; BR)
*A spring dance, a description of His form: beautiful Gaura, absorbed in dance on the bank of the Suradhuni, sprinkled with drops of phagu and
sandal; tilaka, locks, earrings, lotus eyes, smile, arms, broad chest, a garland of malati, a belt with bells, anklets; the associates sing
raga basanta, the people of Nadia run to see; "blessed is the age of Kali: in it the Lord of Gokula plays". Raga basanta. **Attribution:
probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave); Vrajabuli.*[^18-63]

আজু সুরধুনীতীরে সুন্দর গৌর নৃত্যে বিভোর ।
ফাগুবিন্দু সুগন্ধি চন্দন-চর্চিত অঙ্গ উজোর ॥

*āju suradhunītīre sundara gaura nṛtye bibhora |*
*phāgubindu sugandhi candana-carcita aṅga ujora ||*

*Word for word:* āju suradhunī-tīre — today on the bank of the Suradhuni (Ganga); sundara gaura — beautiful Gaura; nṛtye bibhora — is absorbed in dance; phāgu-bindu — with drops of phagu; sugandhi candana-carcita — anointed with fragrant sandal; aṅga ujora — the body shines

**26.1.** Today on the bank of the Suradhuni beautiful Gaura is absorbed in dance;
His body, sprinkled with drops of phagu and fragrant sandal, shines.

ভাল ঝলকত তিলক অতুলিত ললিত কুন্তল-ভার ।
শ্রবণ-কুণ্ডল গণ্ড-মণ্ডিত ভাঙ-ভঙ্গী অপার ॥

*bhāla jhalakata tilaka atulita lalita kuntala-bhāra |*
*śrabaṇa-kuṇḍala gaṇḍa-maṇḍita bhāṅa-bhaṅgī apāra ||*

*Word for word:* bhāla jhalakata tilaka atulita — on the forehead flashes a peerless tilaka; lalita kuntala-bhāra — lovely the weight of the locks; śrabaṇa-kuṇḍala gaṇḍa-maṇḍita — earrings adorn the cheeks; bhāṅga-bhaṅgī apāra — the arch of the brows is boundless

**26.2.** On His forehead a peerless tilaka flashes, lovely is the weight of His locks;
the earrings in His ears adorn His cheeks, the arch of His brows is boundless.

লোল লোচন কঞ্জ মঞ্জু ময়ঙ্ক জিতি মুখজ্যোতি ।
অরুণ অধর সুহাস মৃদু মৃদু দন্ত নিন্দই মোতি ॥

*lola locana kañja mañju mayaṅka jiti mukhajyoti |*
*aruṇa adhara suhāsa mṛdu mṛdu danta nindai moti ||*

*Word for word:* lola locana — restless eyes; kañja mañju — lovely lotuses; mayaṅka jiti mukha-jyoti — the radiance of the face conquers the moon; aruṇa adhara — red lips; suhāsa mṛdu mṛdu — a gentle, gentle smile; danta nindai moti — the teeth put pearls to shame

**26.3.** His restless eyes are lovely lotuses, the radiance of His face conquers the moon;
His red lips with a gentle, gentle smile, His teeth put pearls to shame.

বাহু কনক-মৃণাল মনমথ-মথন বক্ষ বিশাল ।
চারু রচিত বিচিত্র চঞ্চল কণ্ঠে মালতী-মাল ॥

*bāhu kanaka-mṛṇāla manamatha-mathana bakṣa biśāla |*
*cāru racita bicitra cañcala kaṇṭhe mālatī-māla ||*

*Word for word:* bāhu kanaka-mṛṇāla — the arms are golden lotus stalks; manamatha-mathana bakṣa biśāla — the broad chest that crushes Manmatha; cāru racita bicitra cañcala — lovely, artfully made, swaying; kaṇṭhe mālatī-māla — a malati garland on the neck

**26.4.** His arms are golden lotus stalks, His broad chest crushes Manmatha;
on His neck a lovely, skilfully woven, swaying garland of malati.

ক্ষীণ কটিতট জটিত কিঙ্কিণী পহিরে বসন সুচারু ।
চরণ-নূপুর রণিত নিরুপম সব মদ সকল শিঙ্গার ॥

*kṣīṇa kaṭitaṭa jaṭita kiṅkiṇī pahire basana sucāru |*
*caraṇa-nūpura raṇita nirupama saba mada sakala śiṅgāra ||*

*Word for word:* kṣīṇa kaṭi-taṭa — on the slender waist; jaṭita kiṅkiṇī — a belt set with bells; pahire basana sucāru — He wears beautiful garments; caraṇa-nūpura raṇita nirupama — the anklets jingle peerlessly; saba mada sakala śiṅgāra — all the attire intoxicates

**26.5.** On His slender waist a belt with bells, He wears beautiful garments;
peerlessly His anklets jingle — all His attire intoxicates.

হেরি অপরূপ রূপ পরিকর মগন গুণ নহু অন্ত ।
ঝাঁঝ মুরজ মৃদঙ্গ বায়ই গায় রাগ বসন্ত ॥

*heri aparūpa rūpa parikara magana guṇa nahu anta |*
*jhām̐jha muraja mṛdaṅga bāyai gāya rāga basanta ||*

*Word for word:* heri aparūpa rūpa — seeing the wondrous beauty; parikara magana — the associates are immersed; guṇa nahu anta — in virtues without end; jhām̐jha muraja mṛdaṅga bāyai — cymbals, muraja and mridanga play; gāya rāga basanta — they sing raga basanta

**26.6.** Seeing the wondrous beauty, the associates are immersed in His virtues, which have no end;
cymbals, muraja and mridanga play, they sing raga basanta.

শুনত সুরগণ গগনমণ্ডলে ধিরজ ধরই ন পারি ।
ধাই ধাই চলু চহু ওর নব নদীয়ানগর-নরনারী ॥

*śunata suragaṇa gaganamaṇḍale dhiraja dharai na pāri |*
*dhāi dhāi calu cahu ora naba nadīyānagara-naranārī ||*

*Word for word:* śunata sura-gaṇa — hearing, the gods; gagana-maṇḍale — in the heavens; dhiraja dharai na pāri — cannot keep composure; dhāi dhāi calu cahu ora — run from all sides; naba nadīyā-nagara-nara-nārī — the men and women of the young town of Nadia

**26.7.** Hearing it, the gods in the heavens cannot keep their composure;
from all sides run the men and women of the young town of Nadia.

হোত জয় জয় কার জগ ভরি উমড়ি প্রেম-প্রবাহ ।
ভণত নরহরি ধন্য কলিযুগে বিলসে গোকুল-নাহ ॥

*hota jaya jaya kāra jaga bhari umaṛi prema-prabāha |*
*bhaṇata narahari dhanya kaliyuge bilase gokula-nāha ||*

*Word for word:* hota jaya jaya kāra — cries of "glory" resound; jaga bhari — filling the world; umaṛi prema-prabāha — a stream of prema overflows; bhaṇata narahari — says Narahari; dhanya kali-yuge — blessed is the age of Kali; bilase gokula-nāha — (in it) the Lord of Gokula plays

**26.8.** Throughout the world cries of "Glory!" resound, a stream of prema overflows;
Narahari says: blessed is the age of Kali — in it the Lord of Gokula plays.[^18-64]

[^18-63]: GPT1 — p. 342, no. 67 (basanta); GPT2 — sec. 5.1, no. 67 (catalogue: NG-170); the GPT2 index assigns this pada (p. 220, no. 67) to
Chakravarti. BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 892; ed. 1960, vv. 2642–2649), right after the preceding one. Not in PK, KGC, PS or the
Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^18-64]: "Blessed is the age of Kali" — because in it the Lord appeared, giving prema through sankirtana (cf. Bhag. 11.5.36: "the wise
value the age of Kali, in which everything is attained by sankirtana").

## 27. Narahari Dasa — "gaurāṅgacām̐da hera nayanera koṇe…" (GPT1 p. 488, no. 3; PK 116)
*Prarthana: the poet has taken refuge at the cool feet of Gauranga, he has no one but the Lord; he begs Nityananda for mercy: before,
They saved sinners and gave away prema — let Them now show the world the deliverance of the most sinful; with a straw between his teeth
he asks Gauranga and Nitai not to leave him without hope. Raga kedara. **Attribution: not established** — the pada is in PK, but without
a signature (the last couplet with Narahari's name is not there); the GPT2 index assigns the page to "Narahari Dasa" (undistinguished);
not in the BR; simple Bengali payar.*[^18-65]

গৌরাঙ্গচাঁদ হের নয়নের কোণে ।
শরণ লইনু তোমার শীতল চরণে ॥

*gaurāṅgacām̐da hera nayanera koṇe |*
*śaraṇa lainu tomāra śītala caraṇe ||*

*Word for word:* gaurāṅga-cām̐da — Gaurangachand; hera nayanera koṇe — look from the corner of Your eye; śaraṇa lainu — I have taken refuge; tomāra śītala caraṇe — at Your cool feet

**27.1.** Gaurangachand, look at me at least from the corner of Your eye:
I have taken refuge at Your cool feet.

দিয়াছি তোমারে দায় আমার কেহ নাই ।
তুমি দয়া না করিলে যাব কার ঠাঁই ॥

*diyāchi tomāre dāya āmāra keha nāi |*
*tumi dayā nā karile yāba kāra ṭhām̐i ||*

*Word for word:* diyāchi tomāre dāya — I have laid the burden on You; āmāra keha nāi — I have no one; tumi dayā nā karile — if You show no mercy; yāba kāra ṭhām̐i — to whom shall I go

**27.2.** I have laid my burden on You — I have no one;
if You show no mercy, to whom shall I go?

প্রভু নিত্যানন্দ করহ করুণা ।
কাতর হইয়া ডাকে দীনহীন জনা ॥

*prabhu nityānanda karaha karuṇā |*
*kātara haiyā ḍāke dīnahīna janā ||*

*Word for word:* prabhu nityānanda — Lord Nityananda; karaha karuṇā — show compassion; kātara haiyā — in distress; ḍāke dīna-hīna janā — a lowly, wretched man calls

**27.3.** Lord Nityananda, show compassion:
in distress a lowly, wretched man calls You.

পূর্বে পাপী তরাইলে এবে না তরাও ।
পাপিষ্ঠ উদ্ধার এবার জগতে দেখাও ॥

*pūrve pāpī tarāile ebe nā tarāo |*
*pāpiṣṭha uddhāra ebāra jagate dekhāo ||*

*Word for word:* pūrve pāpī tarāile — before You saved sinners; ebe nā tarāo — now You do not save; pāpiṣṭha uddhāra — the deliverance of the most sinful; ebāra jagate dekhāo — now show the world

**27.4.** Before, You saved sinners — and now You do not save?
Show the world now the deliverance of the most sinful!

তোমার কৃপা না পাইয়া বেড়াই কাঁদিয়া ।
পূর্বে দিয়াছ প্রেম জগতে যাচিয়া ॥

*tomāra kṛpā nā pāiyā beṛāi kām̐diyā |*
*pūrve diyācha prema jagate yāciyā ||*

*Word for word:* tomāra kṛpā nā pāiyā — not having received Your mercy; beṛāi kām̐diyā — I wander weeping; pūrve diyācha prema — before You gave prema; jagate yāciyā — offering it unasked to the world

**27.5.** Not having received Your mercy, I wander weeping;
yet before You gave away prema, Yourself offering it to the world.[^18-66]

সে করুণা প্রকাশিয়া উদ্ধারহ মোরে ।
শুনিয়াছি দয়ার ঠাকুর দেখুক সংসারে ॥

*se karuṇā prakāśiyā uddhāraha more |*
*śuniyāchi dayāra ṭhākura dekhuka saṃsāre ||*

*Word for word:* se karuṇā prakāśiyā — revealing that mercy; uddhāraha more — deliver me; śuniyāchi — I have heard; dayāra ṭhākura — (You are) the merciful Lord; dekhuka saṃsāre — let the world see

**27.6.** Reveal that mercy and deliver me:
I have heard that You are the merciful Lord — let the world see it.

গৌরাঙ্গ নিতাই মোরে না কর নৈরাশ ।
দন্তে তৃণ ধরি কহে নরহরি দাস ॥

*gaurāṅga nitāi more nā kara nairāśa |*
*dante tṛṇa dhari kahe narahari dāsa ||*

*Word for word:* gaurāṅga nitāi — Gauranga, Nitai; more nā kara nairāśa — do not leave me hopeless; dante tṛṇa dhari — holding a straw between the teeth; kahe narahari dāsa — says Narahari Dasa

**27.7.** Gauranga, Nitai, do not leave me without hope! —
with a straw between his teeth says Narahari Dasa.[^18-67]

[^18-65]: GPT1 — p. 488, sec. "the devotee's dainya and prarthana", no. 3 (kedara); GPT2 — sec. 7, no. 3 (catalogue: NG-235, formerly
NS-023). The pada is in PK: vol. 1, PK 116 (the concluding "prayer" of the 5th pallava, "anya prārthanā") — without a signature and
without the last couplet; the readings of the PK manuscripts are in the full version of the book. Who added the couplet with Narahari's name is unknown.
Not in BR, KGC, PS, the Gaura-charita-chintamani or the Gita-chandrodaya. C.
[^18-66]: Cf. CC Adi 7: the Lord and Nityananda give away prema indiscriminately, "without asking who is worthy".
[^18-67]: "A straw between the teeth" is a sign of humility and supplication (cf. chapter 17, note 68).

## 28. Narahari — "mari mari ogo nadīyā mājhe…" (GPT1 p. 494, no. 30)
*Golden Navadvipa: a wondrous beauty in the midst of Nadia — the house of Shachi captivates the world, around it are rows of golden
palaces, in the golden courtyards golden men and women; trees, creepers, beasts and birds have become golden, the Ganga flows as a golden
stream, the sky and the whole world have become golden — so great is the power of the beauty of the poet's Lord. Raga "as one likes"
(yatharaga). **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in Narahari Chakravarti's Gaura-charita-chintamani (where it is put in the
mouth of a woman of Nadia); not in the BR; Bengali payar with repetitions.*[^18-68]

মরি মরি ওগো নদীয়া মাঝে কিবা অপরূপ শোভা ।
না জানিয়ে কেবা গঠিল শচীর ভবন ভুবনলোভা ॥

*mari mari ogo nadīyā mājhe kibā aparūpa śobhā |*
*nā jāniye kebā gaṭhila śacīra bhabana bhubanalobhā ||*

*Word for word:* mari mari — ah, ah; ogo — O people; nadīyā mājhe — in the midst of Nadia; kibā aparūpa śobhā — what wondrous beauty; nā jāniye — I do not know; kebā gaṭhila — who built; śacīra bhabana — the house of Shachi; bhubana-lobhā — captivating the world

**28.1.** Ah, ah, people! What a wondrous beauty in the midst of Nadia!
I do not know who built the house of Shachi, which captivates the world.

ঝলমল করে চারিদিকে নব কনক-মন্দির-সারি ।
কনক-অঙ্গনে বিলসয়ে কত কনক-পুরুষ-নারী ॥

*jhalamala kare cāridike naba kanaka-mandira-sāri |*
*kanaka-aṅgane bilasaye kata kanaka-puruṣa-nārī ||*

*Word for word:* jhalamala kare cāridike — shine all around; naba kanaka-mandira-sāri — rows of new golden palaces; kanaka-aṅgane — in the golden courtyards; bilasaye kata — so many play; kanaka-puruṣa-nārī — golden men and women

**28.2.** All around shine rows of new golden palaces;
in the golden courtyards play so many golden men and women.

আর অপরূপ দেখ কনকের নদীয়ানগর হৈল ।
কনকের তরু কদম্ব কনক-লতায় সাজিছে ভাল ॥

*āra aparūpa dekha kanakera nadīyānagara haila |*
*kanakera taru kadamba kanaka-latāya sājiche bhāla ||*

*Word for word:* āra aparūpa dekha — and another wonder, look; kanakera nadīyā-nagara haila — the town of Nadia has become golden; kanakera taru kadamba — golden kadamba trees; kanaka-latāya sājiche bhāla — are finely adorned with golden creepers

**28.3.** And another wonder — look: the whole town of Nadia has become golden;
golden kadamba trees are adorned with golden creepers.

কনকের পশুপক্ষী যত কীট পতঙ্গ কনক-পারা ।
শ্বেতবর্ণ কেবা হরিল জাহ্নবী হইলা কনকধারা ॥

*kanakera paśupakṣī yata kīṭa pataṅga kanaka-pārā |*
*śvetabarṇa kebā harila jāhnabī hailā kanakadhārā ||*

*Word for word:* kanakera paśu-pakṣī yata — all the beasts and birds are golden; kīṭa pataṅga kanaka-pārā — insects and moths like gold; śveta-barṇa kebā harila — who stole the white colour; jāhnabī hailā kanaka-dhārā — the Jahnavi became a golden stream

**28.4.** All the beasts and birds, all the insects and moths are like gold;
who has stolen the whiteness? The Jahnavi has become a golden stream.[^18-69]

কনক গগন হৈল ই কি হের জগত কনক-মত ।
তাহে বুঝি এই নরহরি-পহু-রূপের প্রতাপ এত ॥

*kanaka gagana haila i ki hera jagata kanaka-mata |*
*tāhe bujhi ei narahari-pahu-rūpera pratāpa eta ||*

*Word for word:* kanaka gagana haila — the sky became golden; i ki — what is this; hera jagata kanaka-mata — look, the world is like gold; tāhe bujhi — therein, it seems; ei narahari-pahu-rūpera pratāpa eta — so great is the power of the beauty of Narahari's Lord

**28.5.** The sky has become golden — what is this? Look: the whole world is like gold —
so great, it seems, is the power of the beauty of the poet Narahari's Lord.[^18-70]

[^18-68]: GPT1 — p. 494, sec. "the devotee's dainya and prarthana", no. 30 (yatharaga; checked against the scan, PDF p. 753); GPT2 — sec. 7,
no. 30. The pada was not in the catalogue — **new row NG-261** (the catalogue made from the GPT2 recognition had missed it). The pada is
in Narahari Chakravarti's Gaura-charita-chintamani (ed. Haridasa Dasa, 1947; recognition in
the OCR text) with the heading "kācicca" ("a certain [woman sings]"), right after a pada about
the townswomen of Nadia. Not in BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. Chakravarti's framing is the speech of a woman of Nadia (the
motif of the townswomen, cf. chapter 17, note 15); the pada itself speaks only of the Lord's beauty transforming His abode — we translate
faithfully to the author.
[^18-69]: The Jahnavi is the Ganga. The white waters of the Ganga have become golden from Gaura's radiance.
[^18-70]: "The poet Narahari's Lord" (narahari-pahu) — see note 24. Navadvipa is a spiritual abode (dhama), non-different from Vrindavana (cf. the
next GPT pada, no. 31: "where Krishna is, there is Vraja"); the gold is an image of Gaura's radiance, which it reflects.

# Chapter 19. Appendix. Padas signed "Narahari" from the Gaura-pada-tarangini — III: the childhood pastimes of Nimai

*Continuation of the appendix (the introductory note on the two Naraharis, on the arguments for attribution and on the marks in the
headings is in ch. 17). Chapter 19: padas on the Lord's childhood from the "Balya-lila" section of the GPT (2.2). First come three
padas which Narahari Chakravarti quotes in the Bhakti-ratnakara while showing the house of Jagannatha Mishra (the first feeding with
rice, Nimai in His father's arms, the first steps); then a large cycle in which the old men and elderly women of Navadvipa, coming at
dawn to the house of Shachi, gaze at Gaura, bless Him and recall His childhood pranks. Almost the whole of this cycle is found in the
Gaura-charita-chintamani of Narahari Chakravarti (chapters 5 and 6 of the "morning pastimes": the love of the old men and the love of the
women in vatsalya) — a strong argument for Chakravarti; two padas (nos. 24 and 27) have not been found in any witness. The index of poets of GPT2
assigns the padas of the section to Chakravarti (those found in the BR) or to an undistinguished "Narahari Dasa" (the GCC padas); none to Sarakara. According to
Majumdar, the padas on the birth and childhood of Nimai are late: Narahari Sarakara, who lived in Shrikhanda, did not see the Lord's
childhood, and the "Narahari" padas known only from the GPT are unreliable for attribution. Before translation the "Narahari" signatures
in sections 2.1–2.2 were checked throughout in GPT1 (tesseract recognition): the catalogue had missed 14 padas of this section (13 of
them in this chapter). The base text is GPT1 (doubtful places from the scan), collated with GPT2, the BR (eds. 1912 and 1960) and the
Gaura-charita-chintamani (ed. 1947); PK, KGC, PS and the Gita-chandrodaya have been checked. The childhood games of the Lord are the lila
of Bhagavan, not an ordinary childhood (note 2). The notes of the GPT editors are not reproduced.*

## 1. Narahari — "nadīyāra nārī puruṣa…" (GPT1 p. 65, no. 10; BR)
*The first feeding with rice: the men and women of Nadia gather with gifts; the Child sits on Nilambara's lap in new ornaments;
tasting grains of sweet rice, He smiles; all praise Shachi and Jagannatha. Raga kamoda. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the
pada is in the BR (12th wave); tripadi with chains of chiming sounds.*[^19-1]

নদীয়ার নারী পুরুষ, সুকৃতি মানি, মনে মহা আনন্দিত হৈয়া ।
নিমাইর অন্নপ্রাশনে, সকলে আইসেন, নানা সামগ্রী লৈঞা ॥

*nadīyāra nārī puruṣa, sukṛti māni, mane mahā ānandita haiyā |*
*nimāira annaprāśane, sakale āisena, nānā sāmagrī laiñā ||*

*Word for word:* nadīyāra nārī puruṣa — the women and men of Nadia; sukṛti māni — deeming [it] the fruit of pious deeds; mane mahā ānandita haiyā — greatly rejoicing at heart; nimāira anna-prāśane — at Nimai's first feeding with rice; sakale āisena — all come; nānā sāmagrī laiñā — bringing various gifts

**1.1.** The men and women of Nadia, counting it the reward of their pious deeds, in great joy
gather for Nimai's first feeding with rice — each bringing various gifts.[^19-2]

শচীসুতশোভা, দেখে আঁখি ভরি, নীলাম্বর ভাগ্যমন্তের কোলে ।
নব নব আভরণময়, কটীতটে পট্টধটী, অঞ্চল দোলে ॥

*śacīsutaśobhā, dekhe ām̐khi bhari, nīlāmbara bhāgyamantera kole |*
*naba naba ābharaṇamaya, kaṭītaṭe paṭṭadhaṭī, añcala dole ||*

*Word for word:* śacī-suta-śobhā — the beauty of Shachi's son; dekhe ām̐khi bhari — they see to their eyes' fill; nīlāmbara bhāgyamantera kole — on the lap of fortunate Nilambara; naba naba ābharaṇa-maya — all in ever-new ornaments; kaṭī-taṭe paṭṭa-dhaṭī — a silk cloth on the hips; añcala dole — the hem sways

**1.2.** They gaze their fill at the beauty of Shachi's son on the lap of fortunate Nilambara:[^19-3]
all in ever-new ornaments, a silk cloth about His hips, the hem of His garment swaying.

হেমসরসীজ জিনি তনুখানি, মুখে কি উপমা চাঁদের ঘটা ।
মিষ্ট-অন্নকণিকা, গ্রহণে কিবা অদ্ভুত, মৃদু হাসির ছটা ॥

*hemasarasīja jini tanukhāni, mukhe ki upamā cām̐dera ghaṭā |*
*miṣṭa-annakaṇikā, grahaṇe kibā adbhuta, mṛdu hāsira chaṭā ||*

*Word for word:* hema-sarasīja jini — surpassing a golden lotus; tanukhāni — the body; mukhe ki upamā — what comparison for the face; cām̐dera ghaṭā — the splendour of the moon; miṣṭa-anna-kaṇikā grahaṇe — on taking grains of sweet rice; kibā adbhuta — how wondrous; mṛdu hāsira chaṭā — the flash of a gentle smile

**1.3.** His body surpasses a golden lotus, and His face — what can compare? — the splendour of the moon;
how wondrously, tasting grains of sweet rice, He flashes a gentle smile!

এহেন উৎসবে, কেবা ধরে ধৃতি, কহিতে কৌতুক না আইসে মুখে ।
সবে শচী জগন্নাথে প্রশংসয়ে, নরহরি হিয়া উথলে সুখে ॥

*ehena utsabe, kebā dhare dhṛti, kahite kautuka nā āise mukhe |*
*sabe śacī jagannāthe praśaṃsaye, narahari hiyā uthale sukhe ||*

*Word for word:* ehena utsabe — at such a festival; kebā dhare dhṛti — who keeps composure; kahite kautuka nā āise mukhe — the joy does not come to the mouth to be told; sabe — all; śacī jagannāthe praśaṃsaye — praise Shachi and Jagannatha; narahari hiyā uthale sukhe — Narahari's heart overflows with happiness

**1.4.** At such a festival who can keep his composure? The joy cannot be put into words.
All praise Shachi and Jagannatha — Narahari's heart overflows with happiness.

[^19-1]: GPT1 — p. 65, section 2.2 ("Balya-lila"), no. 10 (kamoda; checked against the scan, PDF p. 324); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 10. The
catalogue did not know it (new row NG-262). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 768; ed. 1960, vv. 956–959): Ishana, showing Srinivasa the
house of Jagannatha Mishra, says that here at six months the Lord was given His first rice and named, and quotes the pada. Not in PK,
KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. The first feeding with rice (annaprashana) — CB Adi 4; CC Adi 14;
Murari 1.6.
[^19-2]: The childhood games of the Lord are not an ordinary childhood but the lila of Bhagavan (balya-lila): by His own will He appears
as an infant and a child for the sake of His eternal associates who love Him in vatsalya (parental love). Shachi and Jagannatha Mishra
are His eternal parents (in Krishna-lila, Yashoda and Nanda, CC Adi 13); their love, like the love of the people of Navadvipa, is pure
prema, not worldly attachment. So the whole Gaudiya tradition (Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja, Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati)
understands Gaura's childhood games, and so they are to be understood in all the padas of this chapter.
[^19-3]: Nilambara Chakravarti — the Lord's maternal grandfather (CC Adi 13).

## 2. Narahari — "jagannātha miśra mahāsukhe…" (GPT1 p. 65, no. 11; BR)
*Jagannatha Mishra fondles his son; Nimai climbs down from his lap and crawls about the courtyard, looking back; Shachi calls Him into
her arms — "dust will stick to You"; He climbs up to her, smiling. Raga tudi. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in
the BR (12th wave).*[^19-4]

জগন্নাথ মিশ্র মহাসুখে ।
পুত্র কোলে করি চুম্ব দেয় চাঁদমুখে ॥

*jagannātha miśra mahāsukhe |*
*putra kole kari cumba deya cām̐damukhe ||*

*Word for word:* jagannātha miśra mahā-sukhe — Jagannatha Mishra in great happiness; putra kole kari — taking his son on his lap; cumba deya cām̐da-mukhe — kisses the moonlike face

**2.1.** Jagannatha Mishra in great happiness
takes his son on his lap and kisses the moonlike face.

শিরে কেশভূষণ সাজায় ।
আগুলি চালিতে স্নেহ উথলে হিয়ায় ॥

*śire keśabhūṣaṇa sājāya |*
*āguli cālite sneha uthale hiyāya ||*

*Word for word:* śire keśa-bhūṣaṇa sājāya — adorns the hair on His head; āguli cālite — running his fingers [through it]; sneha uthale hiyāya — love overflows in his heart

**2.2.** The father adorns the hair on His little head —
running his fingers through it, his heart overflows with love.

নিমাই বাপের কোল হৈতে ।
ভঙ্গী করি নাময়ে অঙ্গনে বেড়াইতে ॥

*nimāi bāpera kola haite |*
*bhaṅgī kari nāmaye aṅgane beṛāite ||*

*Word for word:* nimāi bāpera kola haite — Nimai from His father's lap; bhaṅgī kari — gracefully; nāmaye — climbs down; aṅgane beṛāite — to roam about the courtyard

**2.3.** From His father's lap Nimai
gracefully gets down to roam about the courtyard.

হামাগুড়ি বেড়ায় অঙ্গনে ।
সোণার নূপুর বাজে সুচারু চরণে ॥

*hāmāguṛi beṛāya aṅgane |*
*soṇāra nūpura bāje sucāru caraṇe ||*

*Word for word:* hāmāguṛi beṛāya aṅgane — crawls on all fours about the courtyard; soṇāra nūpura bāje — golden nupuras ring; sucāru caraṇe — on the lovely feet

**2.4.** On all fours He crawls about the courtyard;
golden nupuras ring on His lovely feet.[^19-5]

চলিতে হেরই উলটিয়া ।
চলনমাধুরী মিশ্র দেখে দাঁড়াইয়া ॥

*calite herai ulaṭiyā |*
*calanamādhurī miśra dekhe dām̐ṛāiyā ||*

*Word for word:* calite — while moving; heraï ulaṭiyā — looks back; calana-mādhurī — the sweetness of His movement; miśra dekhe dām̐ṛāiyā — Mishra stands and watches

**2.5.** As He crawls, He looks back;
Mishra stands watching the sweetness of His movements.

সমুখে আসিয়া কহে মায় ।
কোলে চড়সিয়া বাপ ধূলি লাগে গায় ॥

*samukhe āsiyā kahe māya |*
*kole caṛasiyā bāpa dhūli lāge gāya ||*

*Word for word:* samukhe āsiyā — coming before [Him]; kahe māya — the mother says; kole caṛasiyā — come up onto my lap; bāpa — darling (lit. "father", an endearment); dhūli lāge gāya — dust sticks to the body

**2.6.** His mother comes before Him and says:
"Come up into my arms, darling — dust is sticking to Your body."

জননীর হাতে হাত দিয়া ।
কোলে উঠে লহু লহু হাসিয়া হাসিয়া ॥

*jananīra hāte hāta diyā |*
*kole uṭhe lahu lahu hāsiyā hāsiyā ||*

*Word for word:* jananīra hāte hāta diyā — putting His hand in His mother's hand; kole uṭhe — climbs onto her lap; lahu lahu — slowly; hāsiyā hāsiyā — smiling and smiling

**2.7.** Putting His little hand in His mother's hand,
He climbs onto her lap, smiling and smiling.

দুগ্ধবিন্দু সম দন্তজ্যোতি ।
হাসিতে প্রকাশ তায় কেবা ধরে ধৃতি ॥

*dugdhabindu sama dantajyoti |*
*hāsite prakāśa tāya kebā dhare dhṛti ||*

*Word for word:* dugdha-bindu sama — like drops of milk; danta-jyoti — the shine of His teeth; hāsite prakāśa tāya — when it shows in His smile; kebā dhare dhṛti — who keeps composure

**2.8.** His little teeth shine like drops of milk;
when they show in His smile — who can keep his composure?

দুটী আঁখে যার পানে চায় ।
তারে নিরন্তর সুখ-সমুদ্রে ভাসায় ॥

*duṭī ām̐khe yāra pāne cāya |*
*tāre nirantara sukha-samudre bhāsāya ||*

*Word for word:* duṭī ām̐khe — with both eyes; yāra pāne cāya — at whom He looks; tāre — him; nirantara — ceaselessly; sukha-samudre bhāsāya — makes float in an ocean of happiness

**2.9.** Whomever He looks at with both eyes,
him He immerses for ever in an ocean of happiness.

জননীর কোলে ভাল শোহে ।
নরহরি নিছনি ভুবন-মন-মোহে ॥

*jananīra kole bhāla śohe |*
*narahari nichani bhubana-mana-mohe ||*

*Word for word:* jananīra kole — on His mother's lap; bhāla śohe — shines beautifully; narahari nichani — Narahari offers himself (the nichhani rite); bhubana-mana-mohe — to the Enchanter of the world's heart

**2.10.** Beautifully He shines on His mother's lap;
Narahari offers himself to the Enchanter of the world's heart.[^19-6]

[^19-4]: GPT1 — p. 65, no. 11 (tudi; scan, PDF p. 324); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 11 (catalogue: NG-006). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 769;
ed. 1960, vv. 970–979): Ishana shows the courtyard where the Lord crawled on His knees (jānu-caṃkramaṇa), quotes the pada of Vasu Ghosha
"ek mukhe ki kahiba" (GPT no. 2, chapter 12) and after it this one. Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the
Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. Cf. Murari 1.6; CC Adi 14.
[^19-5]: Nupuras — ankle bells.
[^19-6]: "Offers himself" (nichani) — Bengali nichhani: the rite of waving something around the beloved and offering oneself for his welfare
(cf. chapter 17, note 34). The signature of this cycle is usually "Narahari offers himself…" or "Narahari's life is Nimai".

## 3. Narahari — "śacī ṭhākurāṇī cāru chām̐de…" (GPT1 p. 65, no. 12; BR)
*The first steps: Shachi teaches Gora to walk, holding out her finger; He stands up, takes two or four steps, lets go of the finger
and falls; His mother takes Him in her arms and nurses Him. Raga tudi. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR
(12th wave).*[^19-7]

শচী ঠাকুরাণী চারু ছাঁদে ।
হাটন শিখায় গোরাচাঁদে ॥

*śacī ṭhākurāṇī cāru chām̐de |*
*hāṭana śikhāya gorācām̐de ||*

*Word for word:* śacī ṭhākurāṇī — Shachi Thakurani; cāru chām̐de — in a lovely way, tenderly; hāṭana śikhāya — teaches walking; gorācām̐de — Gorachand

**3.1.** Shachi Thakurani tenderly
teaches Gorachand to walk.

মৃদু মৃদু কহেন হাসিয়া ।
ধর মোর অঙ্গুলি আসিয়া ॥

*mṛdu mṛdu kahena hāsiyā |*
*dhara mora aṅguli āsiyā ||*

*Word for word:* mṛdu mṛdu kahena hāsiyā — very gently she says, smiling; dhara mora aṅguli āsiyā — come and take hold of my finger

**3.2.** Very gently she says, smiling:
"Come, take hold of my finger."

শুনি সুখে নদীয়ার শশী ।
মায়ের অঙ্গুলি ধরে হাসি ॥

*śuni sukhe nadīyāra śaśī |*
*māyera aṅguli dhare hāsi ||*

*Word for word:* śuni — hearing; sukhe — joyfully; nadīyāra śaśī — the Moon of Nadia; māyera aṅguli dhare — takes hold of His mother's finger; hāsi — smiling

**3.3.** Hearing this, the Moon of Nadia joyfully
takes hold of His mother's finger with a smile.

ধীরে ধীরে উঠিয়া দাঁড়ায় ।
দুই চারি পদ চলি যায় ॥

*dhīre dhīre uṭhiyā dām̐ṛāya |*
*dui cāri pada cali yāya ||*

*Word for word:* dhīre dhīre — slowly, slowly; uṭhiyā dām̐ṛāya — rises and stands; dui cāri pada — two or four steps; cali yāya — He walks

**3.4.** Slowly, slowly He rises and stands up,
and takes two or four steps.

ছাড়িয়া অঙ্গুলি পড়ে ভূমে ।
শচী কোলে লৈঞা মুখ চুমে ॥

*chāṛiyā aṅguli paṛe bhūme |*
*śacī kole laiñā mukha cume ||*

*Word for word:* chāṛiyā aṅguli — letting go of the finger; paṛe bhūme — falls to the ground; śacī kole laiñā — Shachi, taking Him on her lap; mukha cume — kisses His face

**3.5.** Letting go of the finger, He falls to the ground;
Shachi takes Him in her arms and kisses His little face.

কোলে চড়ি চরণ দোলায় ।
বাজয়ে নূপুর রাঙ্গা পায় ॥

*kole caṛi caraṇa dolāya |*
*bājaye nūpura rāṅgā pāya ||*

*Word for word:* kole caṛi — climbing onto her lap; caraṇa dolāya — swings His feet; bājaye nūpura — the nupuras ring; rāṅgā pāya — on the reddish feet

**3.6.** Climbing onto her lap, He swings His little feet,
and the nupuras ring on His reddish soles.

আঙ্গুলে কচালি স্তন পীয়ে ।
নাহি যে উপমা তায় দিয়ে ॥

*āṅgule kacāli stana pīye |*
*nāhi ye upamā tāya diye ||*

*Word for word:* āṅgule kacāli — fingering with His little fingers; stana pīye — drinks at the breast; nāhi ye upamā — there is no comparison; tāya diye — to give for it

**3.7.** Fingering with His little hand, He drinks at the breast —
there is no comparison for it.

চারিদিকে চাহে ভঙ্গী করি ।
তাহাতে নিছনি নরহরি ॥

*cāridike cāhe bhaṅgī kari |*
*tāhāte nichani narahari ||*

*Word for word:* cāridike cāhe — looks about on all sides; bhaṅgī kari — with charming gestures; tāhāte — for that; nichani narahari — Narahari offers himself

**3.8.** He looks about on all sides with charming gestures —
Narahari offers himself for this.

[^19-7]: GPT1 — p. 65, no. 12 (tudi; scan, PDF p. 324); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 12. The catalogue did not know it (new row NG-263). BR — 12th
wave (ed. 1912, pp. 770–771; ed. 1960, vv. 990–997, "todi"): Ishana says that here in the courtyard the Lord took His first steps,
quotes a verse from Murari's Shri-Krishna-Chaitanya-carita (part 1: "walking with His reddish feet, He took from the earth the fever
of separation") and the pada. Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. The first steps — Murari 1.6;
CB Adi 4; cf. the pada of Vasu Ghosha "māyera aṅguli dhari" (chapter 12).

## 4. Narahari — "gaura-badana sukha-sadana sudhāmaya…" (GPT1 p. 66, no. 15; GCC)
*The old men of Navadvipa gaze at Gaura's face: each offers himself for Him; trembling, in tears, leaning on one another, they say:
who created Mishra's son, who has stolen our hearing, mind and eyes? A moment without Him is like a kalpa; people tease us as madmen, we
have forgotten all order in eating and sleeping, home has grown hateful, we have no love for our own sons. Yatharaga. **Attribution:
probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in his Gaura-charita-chintamani; Vrajabuli with chains of chiming sounds.*[^19-8]

গৌরবদন সুখসদন সুধাময় ঘন ঘন বৃদ্ধ পুরুষগণ হেরি ।
কত কত জনম সফল মানি নিজ নিজ তনু তনু নিছনি করত কত বেরি ॥

*gaurabadana sukhasadana sudhāmaya ghana ghana bṛddha puruṣagaṇa heri |*
*kata kata janama saphala māni nija nija tanu tanu nichani karata kata beri ||*

*Word for word:* gaura-badana — Gaura's face; sukha-sadana — abode of happiness; sudhāmaya — full of nectar; ghana ghana — again and again; bṛddha puruṣa-gaṇa heri — the old men, gazing; kata kata janama saphala māni — deeming many births fruitful; nija nija tanu tanu nichani karata — each offers his whole body for Him; kata beri — many times

**4.1.** Again and again the old men gaze at the face of Gaura — the abode of happiness, full of nectar;
counting many of their births crowned with fruit, each again and again offers his whole self for Him.

টলমল করু নয়নে জল ছল ছল বিপুল পুলক কুলে মণ্ডিত গাত ।
কাহুক করে কর করি অবলম্বন কোই কহত মৃদু মধুরিম বাত ॥

*ṭalamala karu nayane jala chala chala bipula pulaka kule maṇḍita gāta |*
*kāhuka kare kara kari abalambana koi kahata mṛdu madhurima bāta ||*

*Word for word:* ṭalamala karu — they totter; nayane jala chala chala — tears brim in the eyes; bipula pulaka kule maṇḍita gāta — the body adorned with abundant thrills; kāhuka kare kara kari abalambana — leaning on another's hand; koi kahata — someone says; mṛdu madhurima bāta — soft, sweet words

**4.2.** They totter, their eyes brimming with tears, their bodies covered with abundant thrills;
leaning on another's hand, someone speaks soft, sweet words:

মিশ্রতনয়ে কহ কো নিরমায়ল হরণ শ্রবণ মন লোচন মোর ।
পলক না হেরি কল্প সম লাগত অথির করই ধৃতি রহই ন থোর ॥

*miśratanaye kaha ko niramāyala haraṇa śrabaṇa mana locana mora |*
*palaka nā heri kalpa sama lāgata athira karai dhṛti rahai na thora ||*

*Word for word:* miśra-tanaye — Mishra's son; kaha — tell; ko niramāyala — who fashioned; haraṇa śrabaṇa mana locana mora — who has stolen my hearing, mind and eyes; palaka nā heri — not seeing for a moment; kalpa sama lāgata — it seems like a kalpa; athira karaï — it unsettles [me]; dhṛti rahaï na thora — not a little steadiness remains

**4.3.** "Tell me, who fashioned Mishra's son, who has stolen my hearing, my mind and my eyes?
A moment when I do not see Him is like a kalpa; I am thrown into turmoil, and not a drop of steadiness remains.[^19-9]

অনুখন সঙ্গ ভ্রমণে বহু সুখ ইথে পাগল বলি সবে করে পরিহাস ।
সোসব বচন শ্রবণ-পথে আওত পাওত মন পুনঃ অধিক উলাস ॥

*anukhana saṅga bhramaṇe bahu sukha ithe pāgala bali sabe kare parihāsa |*
*sosaba bacana śrabaṇa-pathe āota pāota mana punaḥ adhika ulāsa ||*

*Word for word:* anukhana — always; saṅga bhramaṇe — in going about with [Him]; bahu sukha — great happiness; ithe — for this; pāgala bali — calling [us] mad; sabe kare parihāsa — all mock; so saba bacana — those words; śrabaṇa-pathe āota — when they reach the ears; pāota mana punaḥ adhika ulāsa — the mind gets yet more joy

**4.4.** It is boundless happiness to follow Him everywhere; for this everyone laughs at us, calling us madmen;
but as soon as those words reach our ears, the heart rejoices all the more.

ভোজন গমন শয়ন বচন ক্রমে স্মৃতি নহু সকল হোই বিপরীত ।
গৃহপরিপাটী নিপট কূটময় আপন তনয়ে করহু নহু প্রীত ॥

*bhojana gamana śayana bacana krame smṛti nahu sakala hoi biparīta |*
*gṛhaparipāṭī nipaṭa kūṭamaya āpana tanaye karahu nahu prīta ||*

*Word for word:* bhojana gamana śayana bacana — eating, walking, sleeping, speaking; krame smṛti nahu — no memory of order; sakala hoi biparīta — everything turns upside down; gṛha-paripāṭī — the household routine; nipaṭa kūṭa-maya — utterly a snare; āpana tanaye — to our own sons; karahu nahu prīta — we bear no love

**4.5.** Eating, walking, sleeping, speaking — all order is forgotten, everything goes topsy-turvy;
the household routine is nothing but a burden, and we have no love for our own sons."[^19-10]

ঐছে বাণী ভণি বিরাম মগন পুন অন্তরে করত অভিলাষ ।
গর গর পরম-স্নেহভর ভণব কি মূর্খ-শিরোমণি নরহরি দাস ॥

*aiche bāṇī bhaṇi birāma magana puna antare karata abhilāṣa |*
*gara gara parama-snehabhara bhaṇaba ki mūrkha-śiromaṇi narahari dāsa ||*

*Word for word:* aiche bāṇī bhaṇi — speaking such words; birāma magana — they fall silent, absorbed; puna antare karata abhilāṣa — again they cherish desires within; gara gara — overflowing; parama-sneha-bhara — weight of supreme love; bhaṇaba ki — what can describe; mūrkha-śiromaṇi narahari dāsa — Narahari Dasa, crest-jewel of fools

**4.6.** Having spoken thus, they fall silent, absorbed within, and again cherish desires in their hearts.
How can I, Narahari Dasa, the crest-jewel of fools, describe their overflowing supreme love?

[^19-8]: GPT1 — pp. 66–67, no. 15 (yatharaga; scan, PDF pp. 325–326); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 15 (catalogue: NG-007). Gaura-charita-chintamani
(GCC) — chapter 5 ("morning pastimes": the love of the old men), pada 8, the last song of the chapter. In the GCC this whole cycle is
framed by Gaura's morning in Navadvipa: at dawn He sits in the courtyard of Shachi's house among His associates, and the people of the
town gather to gaze at Him; therefore many padas of the cycle speak of Gaura no longer as an infant, and the childhood pranks in them are
recollections. Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. Cf. the love of the people of Navadvipa for Nimai — CB Adi 6–7.
[^19-9]: A kalpa is a day of Brahma, an immeasurably long time; cf. the gopis' complaint about the blinking of the eyelids that hinders
them from seeing Krishna (Bhag. 10.31.15).
[^19-10]: Cf. Parikshit's question why the people of Vraja loved Krishna more than their own sons (Bhag. 10.14.49–57) — Krishna is the Soul
of all souls. Chakravarti transfers this to the people of Navadvipa.

## 5. Narahari — "rajanī prabhāta teji nija gṛha…" (GPT1 p. 67, no. 16; GCC)
*At dawn the old men, leaning on their sticks, come to Shachi's courtyard and cannot take their eyes off Gaura; each prays for Him: to
the Creator for long life, to Vishnu for grace and universal love, to Shiva for fame and freedom from misfortune, to Sarasvati for
invincible learning, to Bhagavati that they may always see Nimai. Raga vibhasa. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in
the GCC; Vrajabuli.*[^19-11]

রজনী প্রভাত তেজি নিজ গৃহ বৃদ্ধ বৃদ্ধ বর পুরুষগণে ।
সুরুচির শচী-অঙ্গনে সবে উপনীত উপজত কত কত রঙ্গ মনে ॥

*rajanī prabhāta teji nija gṛha bṛddha bṛddha bara puruṣagaṇe |*
*surucira śacī-aṅgane sabe upanīta upajata kata kata raṅga mane ||*

*Word for word:* rajanī prabhāta — at the end of the night; teji nija gṛha — leaving their homes; bṛddha bṛddha bara puruṣa-gaṇe — the venerable old men; surucira śacī-aṅgane — to Shachi's lovely courtyard; sabe upanīta — all arrive; upajata kata kata raṅga mane — joy upon joy arises in their hearts

**5.1.** At the end of the night, leaving their homes, the venerable old men
all come to the lovely courtyard of Shachi, and in their hearts joy upon joy arises.

ঠাট রহত কর লগুড়কৃতাশ্রয় ঘন ঘন নিরখত গৌরতনু ।
চির দিবসান্তর অতি যতনহি বক্ষে রতন বহু মিলল জনু ॥

*ṭhāṭa rahata kara laguṛakṛtāśraya ghana ghana nirakhata gauratanu |*
*cira dibasāntara ati yatanahi bakṣe ratana bahu milala janu ||*

*Word for word:* ṭhāṭa rahata — they stand; kara laguṛa-kṛtāśraya — leaning on the stick in hand; ghana ghana nirakhata gaura-tanu — again and again gaze at Gaura's body; cira dibasāntara — after long days; ati yatanahi — with great toil; bakṣe ratana bahu milala janu — as if they had found a jewel for the breast

**5.2.** They stand leaning on their sticks and again and again gaze at Gaura's body,
as if after long days, with great toil, they had found a jewel for their hearts.

স্নেহ-সুবিবশ কোই কহে বিহি প্রতি পূরণ কর মনরথ সগরে ।
মদধিক হউ পরমায়ু সতত রহ সুন্দর ইহ নদীয়ানগরে ॥

*sneha-subibaśa koi kahe bihi prati pūraṇa kara manaratha sagare |*
*madadhika hau paramāyu satata raha sundara iha nadīyānagare ||*

*Word for word:* sneha-subibaśa — overcome by love; koi kahe bihi prati — someone says to the Creator; pūraṇa kara manaratha sagare — fulfil all wishes; madadhika hau paramāyu — may [His] life be longer than mine; satata raha sundara iha nadīyā-nagare — may He always stay, beautiful, in this town of Nadia

**5.3.** One, overcome by love, says to the Creator: "Fulfil all His wishes;
may He live longer than I, may He, the beautiful one, always live in this town of Nadia."[^19-12]

কোই কহত করজোড়ি বিষ্ণু প্রতি করহ কটাক্ষ মিশ্রতনয়ে ।
কাহুক নহু বহিরঙ্গ সকলে করু প্রীতি নিরত জনু গুণ ভণয়ে ॥

*koi kahata karajoṛi biṣṇu prati karaha kaṭākṣa miśratanaye |*
*kāhuka nahu bahiraṅga sakale karu prīti nirata janu guṇa bhaṇaye ||*

*Word for word:* koi kahata karajoṛi biṣṇu prati — another, with joined palms, says to Vishnu; karaha kaṭākṣa miśra-tanaye — cast a glance on Mishra's son; kāhuka nahu bahiraṅga — may He be a stranger to no one; sakale karu prīti — may all love [Him]; nirata — ceaselessly; janu guṇa bhaṇaye — may they sing [His] virtues

**5.4.** Another, with joined palms, says to Vishnu: "Cast a gracious glance on the son of Mishra;
may He be a stranger to no one, may all love Him and ceaselessly sing His virtues."

কোই কহত কৈলাসনাথ প্রতি বৃদ্ধি করহ প্রতি অঙ্গ ছটা ।
জগ ভরি রহুক কীর্তি হউ সম্পদ দূর করু দুর্জয় অশুভ ঘটা ॥

*koi kahata kailāsanātha prati bṛddhi karaha prati aṅga chaṭā |*
*jaga bhari rahuka kīrti hau sampada dūra karu durjaya aśubha ghaṭā ||*

*Word for word:* koi kahata kailāsa-nātha prati — another says to the Lord of Kailasa; bṛddhi karaha prati aṅga chaṭā — increase the radiance of each limb; jaga bhari rahuka kīrti — may [His] fame fill the world; hau sampada — may there be plenty; dūra karu durjaya aśubha ghaṭā — drive away the hosts of invincible misfortunes

**5.5.** Another says to the Lord of Kailasa: "Increase the radiance of each of His limbs;
may His fame fill the world, may there be plenty; ward off the hosts of invincible misfortunes."

কোই কহত সরস্বতী প্রতি পণ্ডিত করহ অজয় জনু ন হই কদা ।
কোই কহত ভগবতী প্রতি নরহরি প্রাণ নিমাইক নিরখে সদা ॥

*koi kahata sarasvatī prati paṇḍita karaha ajaya janu na hai kadā |*
*koi kahata bhagabatī prati narahari prāṇa nimāika nirakhe sadā ||*

*Word for word:* koi kahata sarasvatī prati — another says to Sarasvati; paṇḍita karaha — make [Him] a pandit; ajaya — invincible; janu na hoi kadā — that He may never [be defeated]; koi kahata bhagabatī prati — another says to Bhagavati; narahari prāṇa nimāika — Nimai, Narahari's life; nirakhe sadā — may [we] always behold

**5.6.** Another says to Sarasvati: "Make Him a pandit, invincible, so that He may never know defeat";
another says to Bhagavati: "May we always see Nimai — the life of Narahari."

[^19-11]: GPT1 — p. 67, no. 16 (vibhasa; scan, PDF p. 326); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 16 (catalogue: NG-008). GCC — chapter 5, pada 6; in the
GCC it is followed by a short stanza (rasika-chandas) with the same signature — "thus all the old men ceaselessly bless Him…" — which is
not in the GPT. Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^19-12]: The old men pray to Brahma (the Creator), Vishnu, Shiva (the Lord of Kailasa), Sarasvati and Bhagavati (the goddess Durga) for
Gaura's welfare — this is how vatsalya, parental love, shows itself: in it the devotee forgets the Lord's majesty and, seeing Him as in
need of protection, entreats all the gods on His behalf (cf. the cowherds of Vraja and Yashoda entrusting Krishna to the protection of
the gods, Bhag. 10.6, 10.7). The sweetness (madhurya) of this love, by the will of yogamaya, hides from them the majesty (aishvarya) of
the Lord; this is not independent worship of the demigods, and the Lord, of course, needs no one's protection. Bhagavati here is an
epithet of the goddess, not of Bhagavan.

## 6. Narahari — "gaura-sneha-bhare gara gara gāta…" (GPT1 p. 67, no. 17; GCC)
*At the end of the night the old men, overflowing with love for Gaura, tell their households about Him; unable to live without His
darshan, they gather all their strength, rise from their beds and, trembling, sticks in hand, go to Him. Raga dhanashi. **Attribution:
probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC; Vrajabuli.*[^19-13]

গৌরস্নেহভরে গর গর গাত ।
মুদিত বৃদ্ধগণ নিশি পরভাত ॥

*gaurasnehabhare gara gara gāta |*
*mudita bṛddhagaṇa niśi parabhāta ||*

*Word for word:* gaura-sneha-bhare — with the weight of love for Gaura; gara gara gāta — their bodies overflowing; mudita bṛddha-gaṇa — the old men rejoice; niśi parabhāta — at the end of the night

**6.1.** Their bodies overflowing with love for Gaura,
the old men rejoice at the end of the night.

নিজ নিজ পরিজন কহল বিশেষ ।
শুনইতে সো সব উলস অশেষ ॥

*nija nija parijana kahala biśeṣa |*
*śunaite so saba ulasa aśeṣa ||*

*Word for word:* nija nija parijana — each to his own household; kahala biśeṣa — told in detail; śunaite — on hearing; so saba — all that; ulasa aśeṣa — they rejoice endlessly

**6.2.** Each told his household everything in detail;
hearing it all, they rejoice without end.

গৌরদরশ বিনু রহই না পারি ।
তেজল শেজ বাঁধল বল ভারী ॥

*gauradaraśa binu rahai nā pāri |*
*tejala śeja bām̐dhala bala bhārī ||*

*Word for word:* gaura-daraśa binu — without the darshan of Gaura; rahaï nā pāri — unable to stay; tejala śeja — they left their beds; bām̐dhala bala bhārī — gathering great strength

**6.3.** Unable to stay without the darshan of Gaura,
they left their beds, gathering all their strength.

করই লগুড় কর কাঁপই অঙ্গ ।
নিরখত নরহরি নিরুপম রঙ্গ ॥

*karai laguṛa kara kām̐pai aṅga |*
*nirakhata narahari nirupama raṅga ||*

*Word for word:* karaï laguṛa kara — staff in hand; kām̐paï aṅga — the body trembles; nirakhata narahari — Narahari beholds; nirupama raṅga — a matchless spectacle

**6.4.** Sticks in hand, bodies trembling —
Narahari watches this matchless spectacle.

[^19-13]: GPT1 — p. 67, no. 17 (dhanashi; scan, PDF p. 326); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 17 (catalogue: NG-009). GCC — chapter 5, pada 5
(yatharaga). GPT1 has "tejala śeṣe" ("left… at last"), the GCC "tejala śeja" ("left their beds"); the GCC reading is adopted. Not in the BR,
PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.

## 7. Narahari — "śuna mora bāṇī nā jāni ki habe…" (GPT1 p. 67, no. 18; GCC)
*An old man says to his household: "I have grown utterly decrepit, and Nimai is our life and all our wealth; I always want to see Him,
but have no strength to walk. Worship the gods, give gifts to brahmanas, send Him presents that please Him; go with Narahari to Shachi,
teach her auspicious rites and make Nimai swear to give up His obstinacy." Raga suhai. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada
is in the GCC.*[^19-14]

শুন মোর বাণী না জানি কি হবে হইনু নিপট বুড়া ।
আমাদের প্রাণধন সরবস নিমাই পরাণ-জুড়া ॥

*śuna mora bāṇī nā jāni ki habe hainu nipaṭa buṛā |*
*āmādera prāṇadhana sarabasa nimāi parāṇa-juṛā ||*

*Word for word:* śuna mora bāṇī — hear my words; nā jāni ki habe — I do not know what will be; hainu nipaṭa buṛā — I have become utterly old; āmādera prāṇa-dhana — our treasure of life; sarabasa — all our wealth; nimāi — Nimai; parāṇa-juṛā — the solace of the soul

**7.1.** "Listen to what I say: I do not know what will be — I have grown utterly decrepit.
Our treasure of life, all our wealth, is Nimai, the solace of the soul.

ওহে সদাই দেখিতে সাধ ।
চলিতে শকতি নাই তেঁই দুঃখ বিধাতা করিলে বাদ ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*ohe sadāi dekhite sādha |*
*calite śakati nāi tem̐i duḥkha bidhātā karile bāda || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* ohe — ah; sadāi dekhite sādha — I always long to see; calite śakati nāi — I have no strength to walk; tem̐i duḥkha — hence the grief; bidhātā karile bāda — Providence has turned hostile

**7.2.** *(Refrain)* Ah, I always long to see Him!
But I have no strength to walk — that is my grief: Providence has turned against me.

পূজহ দেবতা, দ্বিজে দেহ দান, চিন্তহ সদাই হিত ।
নানা উপহার পাঠাহ যতনে যাহাতে তাহার প্রীত ॥

*pūjaha debatā, dvije deha dāna, cintaha sadāi hita |*
*nānā upahāra pāṭhāha yatane yāhāte tāhāra prīta ||*

*Word for word:* pūjaha debatā — worship the gods; dvije deha dāna — give gifts to the brahmanas; cintaha sadāi hita — always think of [His] welfare; nānā upahāra pāṭhāha yatane — carefully send various presents; yāhāte tāhāra prīta — whatever pleases Him

**7.3.** Worship the gods, give gifts to the brahmanas, always think of His welfare;
carefully send Him various presents — whatever pleases Him.

নরহরি সহ যাইয়া শচীরে শিখাহ মঙ্গলক্রিয়া ।
নিমাইর বড় বিষম আঁখুটি ঘুচাবে শপথ দিয়া ॥

*narahari saha yāiyā śacīre śikhāha maṅgalakriyā |*
*nimāira baṛa biṣama ām̐khuṭi ghucābe śapatha diyā ||*

*Word for word:* narahari saha yāiyā — going with Narahari; śacīre śikhāha maṅgala-kriyā — teach Shachi auspicious rites; nimāira baṛa biṣama ām̐khuṭi — Nimai's dreadful obstinacy; ghucābe śapatha diyā — make Him drop it by an oath

**7.4.** Go with Narahari and teach Shachi auspicious rites;
let Nimai swear to give up His dreadful obstinacy."[^19-15]

[^19-14]: GPT1 — p. 67, no. 18 (suhai; scan, PDF p. 326); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 18. The catalogue did not know it (new row NG-264). GCC —
chapter 5, pada 4 (yatharaga). Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^19-15]: The poet introduces himself into the lila as one of the people of Navadvipa ("go with Narahari") — a frequent device of
Chakravarti in the GCC. "Obstinacy" (ām̐khuṭi) — Nimai's childish whims, of which the following padas tell (cf. CB Adi 6: the neighbours'
complaints to Jagannatha Mishra).

## 8. Narahari — "niśi parabhāta samaye yerūpa ānanda śacīra ghare…" (GPT1 p. 68, no. 19; GCC)
*The joy in Shachi's house at dawn cannot be told even by a thousand mouths through hundreds of yugas: Gaurachand, who gives happiness
to His own, has spread in the courtyard a net that enchants the world; people leave their beds, come running, drown in the ocean of His
beauty and cannot go home. Raga vibhasa. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC.*[^19-16]

নিশি পরভাত সময়ে যেরূপ আনন্দ শচীর ঘরে ।
শত শত যুগে সহস্র বদনে কিঞ্চিৎ বর্ণিতে নারে ॥

*niśi parabhāta samaye yerūpa ānanda śacīra ghare |*
*śata śata yuge sahasra badane kiñcit barṇite nāre ||*

*Word for word:* niśi parabhāta samaye — at the hour when night ends; yerūpa ānanda śacīra ghare — the joy that is in Shachi's house; śata śata yuge — in hundreds of yugas; sahasra badane — with a thousand mouths; kiñcit barṇite nāre — one cannot describe even a little

**8.1.** What joy there is in Shachi's house at the end of the night —
not even in hundreds of yugas could a thousand mouths describe a fraction of it![^19-17]

নিজ জনে সুখ দিতে কত রঙ্গ জানয়ে গৌরচাঁদ ।
বুঝিবা আঙ্গিনা মাঝেতে ফাঁদিল ভুবনমোহন ফাঁদ ॥

*nija jane sukha dite kata raṅga jānaye gauracām̐da |*
*bujhibā āṅginā mājhete phām̐dila bhubanamohana phām̐da ||*

*Word for word:* nija jane sukha dite — to give happiness to His own; kata raṅga jānaye gauracām̐da — how many games Gaurachand knows; bujhibā — it seems; āṅginā mājhete — in the middle of the courtyard; phām̐dila bhubana-mohana phām̐da — He has spread a world-enchanting net

**8.2.** How many games Gaurachand knows to give happiness to His own!
It seems that in the middle of the courtyard He has spread a net that enchants the world.

শেজ তেজি ধাঞা ধাঞা যত জন আইসে আনন্দ করে ।
সে শোভা-সায়রে ডুবে পুন ফিরে যাইতে নারয়ে ঘরে ॥

*śeja teji dhāñā dhāñā yata jana āise ānanda kare |*
*se śobhā-sāyare ḍube puna phire yāite nāraye ghare ||*

*Word for word:* śeja teji — leaving their beds; dhāñā dhāñā — running, running; yata jana āise — all the people come; ānanda kare — rejoicing; se śobhā-sāyare ḍube — they drown in that ocean of beauty; puna phire yāite nāraye ghare — cannot go back home

**8.3.** Leaving their beds, running and running, everyone gathers, rejoicing;
drowned in the ocean of that beauty, they can no longer return home.

অতি অপরূপ প্রীতি অনুক্ষণ উপজে সবার মনে ।
ও রাঙ্গা চরণে সঁপে তনু মন দাস নরহরি ভণে ॥

*ati aparūpa prīti anukṣaṇa upaje sabāra mane |*
*o rāṅgā caraṇe sam̐pe tanu mana dāsa narahari bhaṇe ||*

*Word for word:* ati aparūpa prīti — a wondrous love; anukṣaṇa upaje sabāra mane — ceaselessly arises in all hearts; o rāṅgā caraṇe — to those reddish feet; sām̐pe tanu mana — they surrender body and mind; dāsa narahari bhaṇe — says Narahari Dasa

**8.4.** A wondrous love ceaselessly arises in everyone's heart;
they give body and mind to those reddish feet, says Narahari Dasa.

[^19-16]: GPT1 — p. 68, no. 19 (vibhasa; scan, PDF p. 327); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 19. The catalogue did not know it (new row NG-265). GCC —
the first pada of chapter 7, which is devoted to the townswomen of Navadvipa (nāgarī) seized by love for Gaura; the pada itself speaks
only of the joy of all who come at dawn to Shachi's house, without the nagari motif, and in the GPT it stands in the section on
childhood — therefore it is translated here. In Chakravarti's frame it belongs to the motif of the townswomen (cf. chapter 17, note 15):
worship of Gaura in the spirit of "gaura-nagari" is not accepted by the Gaudiya tradition (Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja,
Bhaktisiddhanta). Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^19-17]: "A thousand mouths" — an allusion to the thousand-headed Ananta-Shesha, who eternally sings of the Lord and finds no end to His
qualities.

## 9. Narahari — "āhā mari mari gaurāṅgacām̐dera carite…" (GPT1 p. 68, no. 20; GCC)
*The people of Nadia cannot live through the night without Gaura: in sleep they see only Him and at dawn they wake with His name;
matchless are their old men and women; Gora, overflowing with tenderness, speaks sweet words with these old kinsfolk. Raga vibhasa.
**Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC.*[^19-18]

আহা মরি মরি গৌরাঙ্গচাঁদের চরিতে কেবা না ঝুরে ।
নদীয়া-নিবাসী নিশি অদরশে পরাণ ধরিতে নারে ॥

*āhā mari mari gaurāṅgacām̐dera carite kebā nā jhure |*
*nadīyā-nibāsī niśi adaraśe parāṇa dharite nāre ||*

*Word for word:* āhā mari mari — ah, ah; gaurāṅga-cām̐dera carite — for the deeds of Gaurangachand; kebā nā jhure — who does not pine; nadīyā-nibāsī — the people of Nadia; niśi adaraśe — not seeing [Him] at night; parāṇa dharite nāre — cannot keep their life

**9.1.** Ah, who does not pine for the deeds of Gaurangachand!
The people of Nadia cannot live through the night without seeing Him.

শুতিয়া স্বপনে, আন নাহি জানে, মানে সরবস গোরা ।
রজনীপ্রভাতে গোরা গোরা বলি জাগিয়া সে রসে ভোরা ॥

*śutiyā svapane, āna nāhi jāne, māne sarabasa gorā |*
*rajanīprabhāte gorā gorā bali jāgiyā se rase bhorā ||*

*Word for word:* śutiyā — lying down; svapane — in dreams; āna nāhi jāne — they know nothing else; māne sarabasa gorā — they deem Gora their all; rajanī-prabhāte — at daybreak; gorā gorā bali jāgiyā — waking up crying "Gora, Gora"; se rase bhorā — absorbed in that rasa

**9.2.** Lying down, in their dreams they know nothing else: Gora is all their wealth;
at dawn they wake crying "Gora, Gora!", absorbed in that rasa.

বৃদ্ধ বৃদ্ধ যত পুরুষ প্রকৃতি উপমা নাহিক কারু ।
কত না যতনে কেবা সিরজিল স্বভাব চরিত চারু ॥

*bṛddha bṛddha yata puruṣa prakṛti upamā nāhika kāru |*
*kata nā yatane kebā sirajila svabhāba carita cāru ||*

*Word for word:* bṛddha bṛddha yata puruṣa prakṛti — all the old men and women; upamā nāhika kāru — none can compare with them; kata nā yatane — with what care; kebā sirajila — who created; svabhāba carita cāru — their lovely nature and conduct

**9.3.** There is no one to equal all these old men and women;
who with such care created their beautiful nature and conduct?

নরহরি পহুঁ নিছনি সে সব বৃদ্ধ পরিজন পাশে ।
গোরা স্নেহভরে গর গর কিছু কহে সুমধুর ভাষে ॥

*narahari pahum̐ nichani se saba bṛddha parijana pāśe |*
*gorā snehabhare gara gara kichu kahe sumadhura bhāṣe ||*

*Word for word:* narahari pahum̐ nichani — Narahari offers himself to [his] Lord; se saba bṛddha parijana pāśe — near all those old kinsfolk; gorā sneha-bhare gara gara — Gora, overflowing with tenderness; kichu kahe — says something; sumadhura bhāṣe — in sweet words

**9.4.** Narahari offers himself to his Lord: among all these old kinsfolk
Gora, overflowing with tenderness, says something to them in sweet words.

[^19-18]: GPT1 — p. 68, no. 20 (vibhasa; scan, PDF p. 327); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 20 (catalogue: NG-010, wrongly as no. 10). GCC — chapter
5, pada 1; the chapter opens with the heading "Again in the morning — the excellence of the old men's love". Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or
the Gita-chandrodaya. B.

## 10. Narahari — "śuna he sumati ati nirajane…" (GPT1 p. 68, no. 21; GCC)
*One old man tells another in secret: "It seems the Son of the Lord of Vraja has appeared here: there is no one in Nadia who does not
pine for His qualities; Srivasa, Murari and the others do not live without His darshan; the ascetic Advaita of Shantipur is constantly
here and tells everyone of His sweet qualities. Make Gorachand the necklace of your throat." Raga vibhasa. **Attribution: probably
Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC.*[^19-19]

শুন হে সুমতি অতি নিরজনে কহিয়ে গুপত কথা ।
বরজে বরজ-পতি-সুত বুঝি প্রকট হইল এথা ॥

*śuna he sumati ati nirajane kahiye gupata kathā |*
*baraje baraja-pati-suta bujhi prakaṭa haila ethā ||*

*Word for word:* śuna he sumati — listen, wise one; ati nirajane — in great privacy; kahiye gupata kathā — I tell a secret; baraje — in Vraja; baraja-pati-suta — the Son of the Lord of Vraja; bujhi — it seems; prakaṭa haila ethā — has appeared here

**10.1.** "Listen, wise one, in great secrecy I tell you a hidden thing:
it seems that the Son of the Lord of Vraja, who was in Vraja, has appeared here.[^19-20]

নদীয়ানগরে হেন নাহি কেহ না ঝুরে উহার গুণে ।
শ্রীবাস মুরারি আদি যত তারা না জীয়ে দরশ বিনে ॥

*nadīyānagare hena nāhi keha nā jhure uhāra guṇe |*
*śrībāsa murāri ādi yata tārā nā jīye daraśa bine ||*

*Word for word:* nadīyā-nagare — in the town of Nadia; hena nāhi keha — there is no one; nā jhure uhāra guṇe — who does not pine for His qualities; śrībāsa murāri ādi yata — Srivasa, Murari and all the rest; tārā nā jīye daraśa bine — they do not live without seeing Him

**10.2.** There is no one in the town of Nadia who does not pine for His qualities;
Srivasa, Murari and all the others do not live without His darshan.

শান্তিপুরবাসী অদ্বৈত-তপসী সতত এথায় রহে ।
কিবা সে মধুর গুণ যারে তারে কত না যতনে কহে ॥

*śāntipurabāsī advaita-tapasī satata ethāya rahe |*
*kibā se madhura guṇa yāre tāre kata nā yatane kahe ||*

*Word for word:* śāntipura-bāsī — the resident of Shantipur; advaita-tapasī — the ascetic Advaita; satata ethāya rahe — stays here constantly; kibā se madhura guṇa — what sweet qualities; yāre tāre — to anyone; kata nā yatane kahe — with what zeal He tells

**10.3.** The resident of Shantipur, the ascetic Advaita, is constantly here,
and with what zeal He tells of His sweet qualities to whomever He meets!

আহা মরি মরি হেন অপরূপ বালক হবে কি আর ।
নরহরি সরবস গোরাচাঁদে করহ গলার হার ॥

*āhā mari mari hena aparūpa bālaka habe ki āra |*
*narahari sarabasa gorācām̐de karaha galāra hāra ||*

*Word for word:* āhā mari mari — ah, ah; hena aparūpa bālaka — such a wondrous boy; habe ki āra — will there be another; narahari sarabasa — Narahari's all; gorācām̐de — Gorachand; karaha galāra hāra — make the necklace of your throat

**10.4.** Ah, will there ever be another such wondrous youth?
Make Gorachand, Narahari's all, the necklace of your throat."

[^19-19]: GPT1 — p. 68, no. 21 (vibhasa; scan, PDF p. 327); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 21 (catalogue: NG-011). GCC — chapter 5, pada 2, marked
"someone says" (kopyāha); the address there is "listen, O worthy one, O wise one" (śuna ohe sati he sumati), that is, apparently to his
wife. Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. Srivasa, Murari and Advaita, "who do not live without His darshan", are a
sign of the GCC frame (Gaura's morning among His associates in Navadvipa after His return from Gaya); the "youth" here is the young
Gaura.
[^19-20]: The old man guesses the truth: Sri Gauranga is Krishna Himself, the Son of Nanda, the Lord of Vraja (CC Adi 1–4); "secret" — because in this incarnation
the Lord hides His divinity (the "concealed" avatara of the Kali-yuga, Bhag. 7.9.38).

## 11. Narahari — "śuna ohe sati nadīyā basati…" (GPT1 p. 68, no. 22; GCC)
*Another old man says to his wife: "Not in vain have I lived in Nadia — in my old age Providence has been merciful: I have gazed my fill
at Nimai; a moment without Him, and my soul weeps. Worship the gods, make vows for His welfare, reward the astrologers; go with Narahari
to Shachi's house and perform auspicious rites." Raga vibhasa. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC.*[^19-21]

শুন ওহে সতি নদীয়া বসতি সফল হইল মোর ।
এ বুড়া বয়সে বিহি সকরুণ সুখের নাহিক ওর ॥

*śuna ohe sati nadīyā basati saphala haila mora |*
*e buṛā bayase bihi sakaruṇa sukhera nāhika ora ||*

*Word for word:* śuna ohe sati — listen, good wife; nadīyā basati — dwelling in Nadia; saphala haila mora — mine has borne fruit; e buṛā bayase — in this old age; bihi sakaruṇa — Providence is merciful; sukhera nāhika ora — no end to happiness

**11.1.** "Listen, good wife: my life in Nadia has been crowned with fruit;
in my old age Providence has been merciful — there is no end to my happiness.

এ দুটী নয়ানভরি নিরখিল শচীর নিমাইচাঁদে ।
তিল আধ তাঁরে না দেখি বিষম সদাই পরাণ কাঁদে ॥

*e duṭī nayānabhari nirakhila śacīra nimāicām̐de |*
*tila ādha tām̐re nā dekhi biṣama sadāi parāṇa kām̐de ||*

*Word for word:* e duṭī nayāna-bhari — with these two eyes to the full; nirakhila — I have gazed; śacīra nimāicām̐de — at Shachi's Nimaichand; tila ādha — for half a moment; tām̐re nā dekhi — not seeing Him; biṣama sadāi parāṇa kām̐de — my soul always weeps bitterly

**11.2.** With these two eyes I have gazed my fill at Nimaichand, the son of Shachi;
not seeing Him for half a moment, my soul always weeps bitterly.

বালাই লইয়া মরি যেন হেন না দেখি না শুনি আর ।
বিবিধ বিধানে দেব আরাধিয়া মানাবে মঙ্গল তার ॥

*bālāi laiyā mari yena hena nā dekhi nā śuni āra |*
*bibidha bidhāne deba ārādhiyā mānābe maṅgala tāra ||*

*Word for word:* bālāi laiyā mari — may I die taking [His] misfortunes; yena hena nā dekhi nā śuni āra — never have I seen or heard of such another; bibidha bidhāne — by various rites; deba ārādhiyā — worshipping the gods; mānābe maṅgala tāra — make vows for His welfare

**11.3.** May I die taking His misfortunes upon myself: I have never seen or heard of anyone like Him;[^19-22]
worship the gods with various rites and make vows for His welfare.

অনেক যতনে দিবে ধন গ্রহ পূজিব দৈবজ্ঞগণে ।
শচীর মন্দিরে করহ মঙ্গল যাহ নরহরি সনে ॥

*aneka yatane dibe dhana graha pūjiba daibajñagaṇe |*
*śacīra mandire karaha maṅgala yāha narahari sane ||*

*Word for word:* aneka yatane — with great care; dibe dhana daibajña-gaṇe — you will give wealth to the astrologers; graha pūjiba — we shall propitiate the planets; śacīra mandire — in Shachi's house; karaha maṅgala — perform auspicious rites; yāha narahari sane — go with Narahari

**11.4.** Generously reward the astrologers so as to propitiate the planets;
go with Narahari to Shachi's house and perform auspicious rites there."

[^19-21]: GPT1 — pp. 68–69, no. 22 (vibhasa; scan, PDF pp. 327–328); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 22. The catalogue did not know it (new row
NG-266). GCC — chapter 5, pada 3, marked "and another [says]" (kopi ca). Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. On the
prayers to the gods for the Lord see note 12.
[^19-22]: "To die taking His misfortunes upon oneself" (bālāi laiyā mari) — a Bengali expression of tender love: "may all His troubles fall
on me".

## 12. Narahari — "āju śubhakṣaṇe pohāila niśi…" (GPT1 p. 69, no. 23; GCC)
*An auspicious dawn: the people of Nadia run to Shachi's house to see Gaurangachand; Gora sits in the middle of the courtyard,
surrounded by His associates like the moon by the stars; all have forgotten themselves and cannot take their eyes off His face. Raga
vibhasa. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC.*[^19-23]

আজু শুভক্ষণে পোহাইল নিশি ।
আনন্দে মগন নদীয়াবাসী ॥

*āju śubhakṣaṇe pohāila niśi |*
*ānande magana nadīyābāsī ||*

*Word for word:* āju śubhakṣaṇe — today at an auspicious moment; pohāila niśi — the night has ended; ānande magana — immersed in bliss; nadīyā-bāsī — the people of Nadia

**12.1.** Today at an auspicious hour the night has ended;
the people of Nadia are immersed in bliss.

দেখিতে গৌরাঙ্গচাঁদেরে স্নেহে ।
ধাঞা আইসে সব শচীর গেহে ॥

*dekhite gaurāṅgacām̐dere snehe |*
*dhāñā āise saba śacīra gehe ||*

*Word for word:* dekhite — to see; gaurāṅga-cām̐dere — Gaurangachand; snehe — with love; dhāñā āise saba — all come running; śacīra gehe — to Shachi's house

**12.2.** To see Gaurangachand with love,
all come running to Shachi's house.

আঙ্গিনার মাঝে বিলসে গোরা ।
জগজন মন নয়নচোরা ॥

*āṅgināra mājhe bilase gorā |*
*jagajana mana nayanacorā ||*

*Word for word:* āṅginār mājhe — in the middle of the courtyard; bilase gorā — Gora shines; jaga-jana mana nayana-corā — the stealer of the hearts and eyes of the world

**12.3.** In the middle of the courtyard Gora is shining,
the stealer of the hearts and eyes of all the world.

পরিকর শোভে সকল দিশে ।
উডু মধি বিধু উপমা কি সে ॥

*parikara śobhe sakala diśe |*
*uḍu madhi bidhu upamā ki se ||*

*Word for word:* parikara śobhe sakala diśe — the associates shine on all sides; uḍu madhi bidhu — the moon among the stars; upamā ki se — what comparison is that

**12.4.** On all sides His associates shine —
He among them like the moon among the stars; but what is that comparison!

কিছু স্মৃতি নাই কাহার মনে ।
সবাকার আঁখি ও মুখপানে ॥

*kichu smṛti nāi kāhāra mane |*
*sabākāra ām̐khi o mukhapāne ||*

*Word for word:* kichu smṛti nāi kāhāra mane — no one has any memory in mind; sabākāra ām̐khi — the eyes of all; o mukha-pāne — toward that face

**12.5.** No one remembers anything —
everyone's eyes are fixed on that face.

নরহরি এক মুখে কি কবে ।
নিজ নিজ রসে উলসে সবে ॥

*narahari eka mukhe ki kabe |*
*nija nija rase ulase sabe ||*

*Word for word:* narahari eka mukhe ki kabe — what will Narahari tell with one mouth; nija nija rase — each in his own rasa; ulase sabe — all rejoice

**12.6.** What can Narahari tell with only one mouth?
Each rejoices in his own rasa.

[^19-23]: GPT1 — p. 69, no. 23 (vibhasa; scan, PDF p. 328); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 23 (catalogue: NG-012, wrongly as no. 13). GCC — the first
pada of chapter 6, devoted to the love of the women in vatsalya ("morning pastimes": the love of the elderly women). Not in the BR, PK,
KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.

## 13. Narahari — "advaita-gharaṇī sītā ṭhākurāṇī…" (GPT1 p. 69, no. 24; GCC)
*Sita Thakurani, Advaita's wife, gazes unblinking at Gaura's smile; remembering His new deeds, she becomes as she was before, weeps,
carefully instructs Shachi, blesses and praises. Yatharaga. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC.*[^19-24]

অদ্বৈতঘরণী সীতা ঠাকুরাণী কেবল রসের রাশি ।
অনিমিখ আঁখে, নিরিখে সুন্দর, গৌরমুখের হাসি ॥

*advaitagharaṇī sītā ṭhākurāṇī kebala rasera rāśi |*
*animikha ām̐khe, nirikhe sundara, gauramukhera hāsi ||*

*Word for word:* advaita-gharaṇī — Advaita's wife; sītā ṭhākurāṇī — Sita Thakurani; kebala rasera rāśi — wholly a mass of rasa; animikha ām̐khe — with unblinking eyes; nirikhe — gazes; sundara gaura-mukhera hāsi — at the beautiful smile of Gaura's face

**13.1.** Advaita's wife, Sita Thakurani — the very embodiment of rasa —
with unblinking eyes gazes at the beautiful smile on Gaura's face.

ও নব চরিত ভাবিতে ভাবিতে, হইলা পূরব পারা ।
ধৈরজ ধরিতে নারয়ে যুগল নয়নে বহয়ে ধারা ॥

*o naba carita bhābite bhābite, hailā pūraba pārā |*
*dhairaja dharite nāraye yugala nayane bahaye dhārā ||*

*Word for word:* o naba carita — those new deeds; bhābite bhābite — thinking and thinking; hailā pūraba pārā — she became as before; dhairaja dharite nāraye — she cannot keep her composure; yugala nayane bahaye dhārā — streams flow from both eyes

**13.2.** Thinking and thinking of His new deeds, she became just as she was before;[^19-25]
unable to restrain herself — streams of tears flow from both her eyes.

কত কত কথা উপজয়ে চিতে স্নেহেতে আতুর মতি ।
যতন করিয়া করে উপদেশ সেরূপ শচীর প্রতি ॥

*kata kata kathā upajaye cite snehete ātura mati |*
*yatana kariyā kare upadeśa serūpa śacīra prati ||*

*Word for word:* kata kata kathā upajaye cite — so many words arise in her heart; snehete ātura mati — her mind faint with tenderness; yatana kariyā — with care; kare upadeśa serūpa — gives such instructions; śacīra prati — to Shachi

**13.3.** So many words arise in her heart, her mind is faint with tenderness;
and with care she gives Shachi instructions on what to do.

অশেষ আশীষ দিয়া প্রশংসয়ে সুখের নাহিক পার ।
নরহরি কহে এ সব চরিত বুঝিতে শকতি কার ॥

*aśeṣa āśīṣa diyā praśaṃsaye sukhera nāhika pāra |*
*narahari kahe e saba carita bujhite śakati kāra ||*

*Word for word:* aśeṣa āśīṣa diyā — giving endless blessings; praśaṃsaye — she praises; sukhera nāhika pāra — no limit to happiness; narahari kahe — Narahari says; e saba carita — all these deeds; bujhite śakati kāra — who has the power to understand

**13.4.** Blessing without end, she praises [Him] — there is no limit to her happiness.
Narahari says: who has the power to understand all these deeds?

[^19-24]: GPT1 — p. 69, no. 24 (yatharaga; scan, PDF p. 328); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 24. The catalogue did not know it (new row NG-267). GCC — chapter 6, pada 2. Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the
Gita-chandrodaya. B. Sita Thakurani — the wife of Advaita Acharya; according to CC Adi 13, she came with gifts to bless the newborn
Lord.
[^19-25]: "As before" (pūraba pārā) — apparently as in the days of His appearance, when she first came to the Child (CC Adi 13); another
reading is possible — as in the former (Krishna-)lila.

## 14. Narahari — "śrībāsa-banitā ati sucaritā…" (GPT1 p. 69, no. 25; GCC)
*Srivasa's wife, tenderness incarnate, chaste and modest, her face covered with the hem of her cloth, stands beside Sita and gazes at
Gaura, who sits in the middle of the courtyard among His dear associates; Malini floats in the ocean of His beauty. Raga vibhasa.
**Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC.*[^19-26]

শ্রীবাসবনিতা অতি সুচরিতা স্নেহের মূরতি যেন ।
সতত লজ্জিতা সতী পতিব্রতা জগতে নাহিক হেন ॥

*śrībāsabanitā ati sucaritā snehera mūrati yena |*
*satata lajjitā satī patibratā jagate nāhika hena ||*

*Word for word:* śrībāsa-banitā — Srivasa's wife; ati sucaritā — most virtuous; snehera mūrati yena — like tenderness embodied; satata lajjitā — ever modest; satī patibratā — chaste, devoted to her husband; jagate nāhika hena — there is none like her in the world

**14.1.** Srivasa's wife, virtuous, like tenderness itself in bodily form,
always modest, chaste, devoted to her husband — there is none like her in the world.

প্রফুল্লিত তনু অনুপম আধ বসন ঝাঁপিয়া মুখে ।
সীতার সমীপে দাঁড়াইয়া ঘন নিরিখে মনের সুখে ॥

*praphullita tanu anupama ādha basana jhām̐piyā mukhe |*
*sītāra samīpe dām̐ṛāiyā ghana nirikhe manera sukhe ||*

*Word for word:* praphullita tanu anupama — her matchless body blossoming; ādha basana jhām̐piyā mukhe — half covering her face with her cloth; sītāra samīpe dām̐ṛāiyā — standing near Sita; ghana nirikhe — gazes intently; manera sukhe — with joy at heart

**14.2.** Her whole matchless body has blossomed with joy; half covering her face with the hem of her cloth,
she stands beside Sita and cannot take her eyes off [Him], rejoicing at heart.

আঙ্গিনার মাঝে প্রিয় পরিকর বেষ্টিত বসিয়া গোরা ।
সুন্দর-বদনচাঁদ ঝলকয়ে গাখানি সোণার পারা ॥

*āṅgināra mājhe priya parikara beṣṭita basiyā gorā |*
*sundara-badanacām̐da jhalakaye gākhāni soṇāra pārā ||*

*Word for word:* āṅginār mājhe — in the middle of the courtyard; priya parikara beṣṭita — surrounded by dear associates; basiyā gorā — Gora sits; sundara-badana-cām̐da jhalakaye — the beautiful moonlike face flashes; gākhāni soṇāra pārā — the body like gold

**14.3.** In the middle of the courtyard, surrounded by His dear associates, sits Gora;
His beautiful moonlike face flashes, and His body is like gold.

নব নব সব কি কব মাল্যানি সে শোভা-সায়রে ভাসে ।
অপরূপ প্রেমবালাই লইয়া মরু নরহরি দাসে ॥

*naba naba saba ki kaba mālyāni se śobhā-sāyare bhāse |*
*aparūpa premabālāi laiyā maru narahari dāse ||*

*Word for word:* naba naba saba — all the ever-new [wonders]; ki kaba — what shall I say; mālyāni — Malini; se śobhā-sāyare bhāse — floats in that ocean of beauty; aparūpa prema-bālāi laiyā — taking on the misfortunes of this wondrous love; maru narahari dāse — may Narahari Dasa die

**14.4.** What can I say of all these ever-new [wonders]? Malini floats in the ocean of that beauty.[^19-27]
May Narahari Dasa die warding off misfortune from this wondrous love!

[^19-26]: GPT1 — pp. 69–70, no. 25 (vibhasa; scan, PDF pp. 328–329); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 25 (catalogue: NG-013, wrongly as no. 15). GCC —
chapter 6, pada 3 (the editor of the GCC marked the name "mālyānī" with a question mark). Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the
Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^19-27]: Malini (mālyāni = mālinī) — the wife of Srivasa Pandita, in Krishna-lila the nurse Ambika (Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika); in Navadvipa she
cared for the Lord with motherly love.

## 15. Narahari — "rajanī-prabhāte śacīdebī cite…" (GPT1 p. 70, no. 26; GCC)
*At dawn Shachi, weeping with joy, clasps Sita's feet and begs: "Be gracious to Nimai, bless Him with a long life; this child is the
apple of my eye; let Him stay at home and give up His restlessness; after Vishvarupa He is my life — let there be no separation."
Yatharaga. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC.*[^19-28]

রজনীপ্রভাতে শচীদেবী চিতে আনন্দের নাহি ওর ।
ও মুখ নিরখি নারে সম্বরিতে নয়ানে বহয়ে লোর ॥

*rajanīprabhāte śacīdebī cite ānandera nāhi ora |*
*o mukha nirakhi nāre sambarite nayāne bahaye lora ||*

*Word for word:* rajanī-prabhāte — at dawn; śacīdebī cite — in Shachi-devi's heart; ānandera nāhi ora — there is no end of joy; o mukha nirakhi — gazing at that face; nāre sambarite — she cannot restrain herself; nayāne bahaye lora — tears flow from her eyes

**15.1.** At dawn there is no end to the joy in the heart of Shachi-devi;
gazing at that face, she cannot restrain herself — tears flow from her eyes.

সীতার চরণে ধরিয়া যতনে কহয়ে মধুর বাণী ।
কেবল ভরসা তোমাদের ওগো ভাল মন্দ নাহি জানি ॥

*sītāra caraṇe dhariyā yatane kahaye madhura bāṇī |*
*kebala bharasā tomādera ogo bhāla manda nāhi jāni ||*

*Word for word:* sītāra caraṇe dhariyā — clasping Sita's feet; yatane — earnestly; kahaye madhura bāṇī — speaks sweet words; kebala bharasā tomādera — my only hope is in you; ogo — O [revered one]; bhāla manda nāhi jāni — I know not good from bad

**15.2.** Clasping Sita's feet, she earnestly speaks sweet words:
"All my hope is in you, O revered one: I do not know what is good and what is bad.

আপন জানিয়া নিমাইচাঁদেরে সতত প্রসন্ন হবা ।
চির আয়ু হৈঞা সুখে থাকে যেন এইসে আশীষ দিবা ॥

*āpana jāniyā nimāicām̐dere satata prasanna habā |*
*cira āyu haiñā sukhe thāke yena eise āśīṣa dibā ||*
