*Word for word:* āpana jāniyā — regarding as your own; nimāicām̐dere — to Nimaichand; satata prasanna habā — be always gracious; cira āyu haiñā — living long; sukhe thāke yena — that He may live happily; eise āśīṣa dibā — give this very blessing

**15.3.** Regarding Nimaichand as your own, be always gracious to Him;
give such a blessing that He may live long and happily.

কেহ নাহি মোর কত নিবেদিব এ শিশু আঁখির তারা ।
এই করো যেন ঘরে থাকে সদা ঘুচায়ে চঞ্চল ধারা ॥

*keha nāhi mora kata nibediba e śiśu ām̐khira tārā |*
*ei karo yena ghare thāke sadā ghucāye cañcala dhārā ||*

*Word for word:* keha nāhi mora — I have no one; kata nibediba — what more shall I beg; e śiśu ām̐khira tārā — this child is the pupil of my eye; ei karo — do this; yena ghare thāke sadā — that He always stay at home; ghucāye cañcala dhārā — giving up restless ways

**15.4.** I have no one — what more shall I ask? — this child is the apple of my eye;
make it so that He always stays at home, giving up His restless ways.

আর বলি বিশ্বরূপ মোর এই নিমাই জীবন প্রাণ ।
তিল আধ যেন না হয় বিচ্ছেদ এই বর দিবে দান ॥

*āra bali biśvarūpa mora ei nimāi jībana prāṇa |*
*tila ādha yena nā haya biccheda ei bara dibe dāna ||*

*Word for word:* āra bali — and I say more; biśvarūpa — Vishvarupa [is gone]; mora ei nimāi — this Nimai of mine; jībana prāṇa — is my life and soul; tila ādha — for half a moment; yena nā haya biccheda — that there be no separation; ei bara dibe dāna — grant this boon

**15.5.** And I say more: [Vishvarupa is gone] — now this Nimai is my life and soul;
give me this boon: that there be not half a moment of separation."[^19-29]

এইরূপ কত কহিয়া তুরিতে করায় মঙ্গল নীত ।
নরহরি এক মুখে কি কহিবে অতুল মায়ের প্রীত ॥

*eirūpa kata kahiyā turite karāya maṅgala nīta |*
*narahari eka mukhe ki kahibe atula māyera prīta ||*

*Word for word:* eirūpa kata kahiyā — saying much like this; turite — quickly; karāya maṅgala nīta — she has auspicious rites performed; narahari eka mukhe ki kahibe — what will Narahari tell with one mouth; atula māyera prīta — of the mother's incomparable love

**15.6.** Having said much more like this, she quickly performs auspicious rites.
What can Narahari tell with one mouth of the incomparable love of the mother?

[^19-28]: GPT1 — p. 70, no. 26 (yatharaga; scan, PDF p. 329); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 26. The catalogue did not know it (new row NG-268). GCC —
chapter 6, pada 4 (GCC scan, p. 60). Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. Shachi's fear that her younger son too will
leave home like Vishvarupa — CB Adi 7.
[^19-29]: Vishvarupa, the Lord's elder brother, took sannyasa and left home (CB Adi 7; CC Adi 15). In the GCC the line reads differently:
"…Vishvarupa — this is my Nitai, my life and soul" (nitāi instead of nimāi) — Shachi sees her elder son in Nityananda (cf. Shachi's
dream of her two sons, Krishna and Balarama — CB Madhya 8; cf. GPT no. 40, where Nitai loves Nimai as Balarama loved Krishna).
Translated according to the GPT.

## 16. Narahari — "śacīra ālaya ālo haiyāche…" (GPT1 p. 70, no. 27; GCC)
*The elderly women of Navadvipa stand in Shachi's courtyard and gaze at Nimai; each prays for Him: one gives Him all her merit, others
will worship Shiva, the Ganga, Chandi, Lakshmi — that He may live long, not leave Nadia, never go abroad to earn money, and be rich;
their love for Him is stronger than for their own sons; "may we see this boy in Nadia birth after birth". Yatharaga. **Attribution:
probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC.*[^19-30]

শচীর আলয় আলো হইয়াছে কি কব সুখের কথা ।
বৃদ্ধানারীগণ মনের হরিষে দাঁড়ায়ে দেখেন তথা ॥

*śacīra ālaya ālo haiyāche ki kaba sukhera kathā |*
*bṛddhānārīgaṇa manera hariṣe dām̐ṛāye dekhena tathā ||*

*Word for word:* śacīra ālaya ālo haiyāche — Shachi's house has become radiant; ki kaba sukhera kathā — what can I say of the happiness; bṛddhā-nārī-gaṇa — the elderly women; manera hariṣe — with joy of heart; dām̐ṛāye dekhena tathā — stand there and gaze

**16.1.** Shachi's house is full of light — what can I say of such happiness!
The elderly women stand there and gaze, rejoicing at heart.

কেহ বলে ওগো কুলের প্রদীপ নিমাই গুণের রাশি ।
আমাদের আঁখি সফল করিতে প্রকট হৈয়াছে আসি ॥

*keha bale ogo kulera pradīpa nimāi guṇera rāśi |*
*āmādera ām̐khi saphala karite prakaṭa haiyāche āsi ||*

*Word for word:* keha bale — one says; ogo — ah; kulera pradīpa — lamp of the family; nimāi guṇera rāśi — Nimai, a treasury of virtues; āmādera ām̐khi saphala karite — to make our eyes fruitful; prakaṭa haiyāche āsi — has come and appeared

**16.2.** One says: "Ah, the lamp of the family, Nimai, the treasury of virtues,
has come and appeared to make our eyes fruitful."

কেহ বলে ওগো শচীর তনয় সতত কুশলে রহু ।
মোর পুণ্য যত দিলাম ইহারে এড়াউক কণ্টক বহু ॥

*keha bale ogo śacīra tanaya satata kuśale rahu |*
*mora puṇya yata dilāma ihāre eṛāuka kaṇṭaka bahu ||*

*Word for word:* keha bale — another says; śacīra tanaya — Shachi's son; satata kuśale rahu — may He always be well; mora puṇya yata — all my merit; dilāma ihāre — I have given to Him; eṛāuka kaṇṭaka bahu — may He escape many thorns

**16.3.** Another says: "Ah, may Shachi's son always be well!
I have given Him all my merit — may He escape many thorns."

কেহ বলে ওগো ইহার লাগিয়া পূজিব কৈলাসরাজে ।
চির আয়ু হৈঞা এইরূপে যেন রহয়ে নদীয়া মাঝে ॥

*keha bale ogo ihāra lāgiyā pūjiba kailāsarāje |*
*cira āyu haiñā eirūpe yena rahaye nadīyā mājhe ||*

*Word for word:* ihāra lāgiyā — for His sake; pūjiba kailāsa-rāje — I shall worship the Lord of Kailasa; cira āyu haiñā — living long; eirūpe yena rahaye nadīyā mājhe — that He may stay like this in Nadia

**16.4.** Another says: "Ah, for His sake I shall worship the Lord of Kailasa,
that He may live long and stay like this in Nadia."

কেহ বলে ওগো নিতি নিতি গঙ্গা পূজিয়া মাগিব বর ।
নিজজন লৈয়া শচীর দুলাল আনন্দে করুক ঘর ॥

*keha bale ogo niti niti gaṅgā pūjiyā māgiba bara |*
*nijajana laiyā śacīra dulāla ānande karuka ghara ||*

*Word for word:* niti niti — daily; gaṅgā pūjiyā — worshipping the Ganga; māgiba bara — I shall ask a boon; nija-jana laiyā — with His own people; śacīra dulāla — Shachi's darling; ānande karuka ghara — may He joyfully keep house

**16.5.** Another says: "Ah, every day I shall worship the Ganga and ask for a boon:
may Shachi's darling live joyfully in His own home with His own people."[^19-31]

কেহ বলে চণ্ডী পূজিয়া মাগিব মনেতে যে আছে মেন ।
ধন উপার্জন লাগিয়া বিদেশে না যায় কখন যেন ॥

*keha bale caṇḍī pūjiyā māgiba manete ye āche mena |*
*dhana upārjana lāgiyā bideśe nā yāya kakhana yena ||*

*Word for word:* caṇḍī pūjiyā — worshipping Chandi; māgiba — I shall ask; manete ye āche mena — what is in my heart; dhana upārjana lāgiyā — to earn money; bideśe nā yāya kakhana yena — that He may never go abroad

**16.6.** Another says: "Worshipping Chandi, I shall ask for what is in my heart:
may He never go abroad to earn money."

কেহ বলে ওগো লক্ষ্মী পূজি আমি আছয়ে কারণ তার ।
অনায়াসে ইহ হবে মহাধনী কভু না ঠেকিবে ভার ॥

*keha bale ogo lakṣmī pūji āmi āchaye kāraṇa tāra |*
*anāyāse iha habe mahādhanī kabhu nā ṭhekibe bhāra ||*

*Word for word:* lakṣmī pūji āmi — I worship Lakshmi; āchaye kāraṇa tāra — there is a reason for it; anāyāse iha habe mahādhanī — that He may effortlessly become very rich; kabhu nā ṭhekibe bhāra — never will He be hard pressed

**16.7.** Another says: "Ah, I worship Lakshmi, and there is a reason for it:
may He become very rich without effort and never know want."

কেহ বলে ওগো আর শুন কিছু না বুঝি মনের গতি ।
নিজ সুত হৈতে শতগুণ স্নেহ উপজে ইহার প্রতি ॥

*keha bale ogo āra śuna kichu nā bujhi manera gati |*
*nija suta haite śataguṇa sneha upaje ihāra prati ||*

*Word for word:* āra śuna — listen to this too; kichu nā bujhi manera gati — I do not understand the working of my heart; nija suta haite śata-guṇa sneha — love a hundred times more than for my own son; upaje ihāra prati — arises for Him

**16.8.** Another says: "Ah, and listen to this too — I do not understand what goes on in my heart:
a love arises for Him a hundred times stronger than for my own son."

কেহ বলে ওগো ঘর তেয়াগিয়া আসিয়া ইহার তরে ।
তিলেক ছাড়িয়া যাইতে না জানি পরাণ কেমন করে ॥

*keha bale ogo ghara teyāgiyā āsiyā ihāra tare |*
*tileka chāṛiyā yāite nā jāni parāṇa kemana kare ||*

*Word for word:* ghara teyāgiyā — leaving home; āsiyā ihāra tare — I come for His sake; tileka chāṛiyā yāite — to go away even for a moment; nā jāni parāṇa kemana kare — I know not what my soul goes through

**16.9.** Another says: "Ah, I leave my house and come here for His sake —
and I do not know how my soul endures it when I must leave even for a moment."

কেহ বলে ওগো শচী ভাগ্যবতী অনেক সুকৃতি কৈল ।
তেঁই সবাকার প্রাণধন এই নদীয়াচাঁদেরে পাইল ॥

*keha bale ogo śacī bhāgyabatī aneka sukṛti kaila |*
*tem̐i sabākāra prāṇadhana ei nadīyācām̐dere pāila ||*

*Word for word:* śacī bhāgyabatī — fortunate Shachi; aneka sukṛti kaila — performed many pious deeds; tem̐i — therefore; sabākāra prāṇa-dhana — the treasure of life of all; ei nadīyā-cām̐dere pāila — she obtained this Moon of Nadia

**16.10.** Another says: "Ah, fortunate Shachi performed many pious deeds —
that is why she obtained this Moon of Nadia, the treasure of life for all."

কেহ বলে ওগো যে বল সে বল বিধিরে এতেক চাই ।
জনমে জনমে এ বালক যেন নৈদায় দেখিতে পাই ॥

*keha bale ogo ye bala se bala bidhire eteka cāi |*
*janame janame e bālaka yena naidāya dekhite pāi ||*

*Word for word:* ye bala se bala — say what you will; bidhire eteka cāi — I ask only this of the Creator; janame janame — birth after birth; e bālaka yena naidāya dekhite pāi — that I may see this boy in Nadia

**16.11.** Another says: "Ah, say what you will, I ask only this of the Creator:
that birth after birth I may see this boy in Nadia."

এইরূপে কত প্রেমের আবেশে কহয়ে নাহিক ওর ।
নরহরি কহে এ সবার স্নেহ কহি কি শকতি মোর ॥

*eirūpe kata premera ābeśe kahaye nāhika ora |*
*narahari kahe e sabāra sneha kahi ki śakati mora ||*

*Word for word:* eirūpe kata premera ābeśe — thus in the rapture of love; kahaye nāhika ora — they speak without end; narahari kahe — Narahari says; e sabāra sneha — the love of them all; kahi ki śakati mora — have I the power to tell

**16.12.** Thus, seized by love, they speak without end.
Narahari says: have I the power to tell of the love of them all?

[^19-30]: GPT1 — pp. 70–71, no. 27 (yatharaga; scan, PDF pp. 329–330); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 27. The catalogue did not know it (new row
NG-269). GCC — chapter 6, pada 5. Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. On the prayers to the gods for the Lord — note 12:
this is vatsalya, not independent worship of the demigods; Chandi is the goddess Durga. Lakshmi, to whom the woman prays, is in
Gaura-lila His eternal consort Herself (Lakshmipriya).
[^19-31]: An unwitting sadness which the poet puts into these wishes: the Lord would later go "abroad" — to East Bengal (CB Adi 14; CC Adi 16) — and
would take sannyasa, leaving home (CB Madhya 26–28).

## 17. Narahari — "āju ki ānanda śrīśacī-bhabane…" (GPT1 p. 71, no. 28; GCC)
*Dawn in Shachi's house: Vishvambhara sits among His dear associates and gives happiness to each in his own bhava; the old men and women,
faint with tenderness, weep as they gaze at His face and tell one another of His deeds. Yatharaga. **Attribution: probably
Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC.*[^19-32]

আজু কি আনন্দ শ্রীশচীভবনে রজনীপ্রভাতকালে ।
প্রিয়পরিকর মাঝে বিশ্বম্ভর বিলসে ভঙ্গীমা ভালে ॥

*āju ki ānanda śrīśacībhabane rajanīprabhātakāle |*
*priyaparikara mājhe biśvambhara bilase bhaṅgīmā bhāle ||*

*Word for word:* āju ki ānanda — what joy today; śrī-śacī-bhabane — in Sri Shachi's house; rajanī-prabhāta-kāle — at the end of the night; priya-parikara mājhe — among dear associates; biśvambhara bilase — Vishvambhara shines; bhaṅgīmā bhāle — in a charming pose

**17.1.** What joy there is today in the house of Sri Shachi at the end of the night!
Among His dear associates Vishvambhara shines in a charming pose.

যার যেই ভাব সেভাবে ভাবিত সবারে করয়ে সুখী ।
ভুবনমোহন গুণমণি হেন সুঘড় কভু না দেখি ॥

*yāra yei bhāba sebhābe bhābita sabāre karaye sukhī |*
*bhubanamohana guṇamaṇi hena sughaṛa kabhu nā dekhi ||*

*Word for word:* yāra yei bhāba — whatever one's bhava; se bhābe bhābita — in that bhava [He is] absorbed; sabāre karaye sukhī — He makes everyone happy; bhubana-mohana — enchanting the world; guṇa-maṇi — jewel of qualities; hena sughaṛa — such an artist; kabhu nā dekhi — I have never seen

**17.2.** Whatever one's bhava, in that bhava He responds, and He makes everyone happy;[^19-33]
never have I seen such an artist, a jewel of qualities, enchanting the world.

বৃদ্ধ বৃদ্ধনারী যত অতিশয় আতুর স্নেহের ভরে ।
ও মুখচন্দ্রমা হেরি হেরি কেহ ধৈরজ ধরিতে নারে ॥

*bṛddha bṛddhanārī yata atiśaya ātura snehera bhare |*
*o mukhacandramā heri heri keha dhairaja dharite nāre ||*

*Word for word:* bṛddha bṛddha-nārī yata — all the old men and old women; atiśaya ātura snehera bhare — are faint under the weight of tenderness; o mukha-candramā heri heri — gazing and gazing at that moonlike face; keha dhairaja dharite nāre — no one can keep composure

**17.3.** All the old men and women are faint under the weight of tenderness;
gazing and gazing at that moonlike face, no one can keep his composure.

নয়নেতে বারি বহে অনিবার মরম আনন্দমনে ।
নরহরি প্রাণ গৌরাঙ্গ চরিত পুনঃ পরস্পর ভণে ॥

*nayanete bāri bahe anibāra marama ānandamane |*
*narahari prāṇa gaurāṅga carita punaḥ paraspara bhaṇe ||*

*Word for word:* nayanete bāri bahe anibāra — tears flow unceasingly from the eyes; marama ānanda-mane — with bliss deep in the heart; narahari prāṇa — the life of Narahari; gaurāṅga carita — the deeds of Gauranga; punaḥ paraspara bhaṇe — again they tell one another

**17.4.** Tears flow unceasingly from their eyes, bliss is in the depths of their hearts;
and again they tell one another the deeds of Gauranga, the life of Narahari.

[^19-32]: GPT1 — p. 71, no. 28 (yatharaga; scan, PDF p. 330); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 28 (catalogue: NG-014). GCC — chapter 6, pada 6 ("bṛddha
naranārī"). Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^19-33]: Cf. Bhagavad-gita 4.11: "As they surrender to Me, so I reciprocate with them" — the Lord responds to each in his own rasa.

## 18. Narahari — "nadīyāra ati puṇyabatī patibratā-gaṇera…" (GPT1 p. 71, no. 29; BR)
*The pious married women of Nadia think more of Shachi's son than of their own sons: as soon as the night ends, they go to Him with trays
of gifts, see Him playing on His mother's lap, take Him in their arms and forget themselves. Raga vibhasa. **Attribution: probably
Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave).*[^19-34]

নদীয়ার অতি পুণ্যবতী পতিব্রতাগণের কি মনের গতি ।
নিজপুত্রে মন, নাই অনুক্ষণ, ভণে শচীসুতচরিত রীতি ॥

*nadīyāra ati puṇyabatī patibratāgaṇera ki manera gati |*
*nijaputre mana, nāi anukṣaṇa, bhaṇe śacīsutacarita rīti ||*

*Word for word:* nadīyāra ati puṇyabatī — of the most pious [women] of Nadia; patibratā-gaṇera — of those devoted to their husbands; ki manera gati — what a disposition of heart; nija-putre mana nāi — their mind is not on their own sons; anukṣaṇa — ceaselessly; bhaṇe śacī-suta-carita rīti — they speak of the deeds and ways of Shachi's son

**18.1.** What a disposition of heart the pious women of Nadia, devoted to their husbands, have!
Their thoughts are not on their own sons — ceaselessly they speak of the deeds and ways of Shachi's son.

নিশি শেষ দেখি, শয়ন উপেখি, তিল আধ নাহি ধৈরজ বাঁধে ।
নানা দ্রব্যে থারি, ভরি সারি সারি, লৈয়া চলে দিতে নদীয়াচাঁদে ॥

*niśi śeṣa dekhi, śayana upekhi, tila ādha nāhi dhairaja bām̐dhe |*
*nānā drabye thāri, bhari sāri sāri, laiyā cale dite nadīyācām̐de ||*

*Word for word:* niśi śeṣa dekhi — seeing the end of night; śayana upekhi — neglecting their beds; tila ādha nāhi dhairaja bām̐dhe — they cannot hold back for half a moment; nānā drabye thāri bhari — filling trays with various things; sāri sāri — in rows; laiyā cale dite nadīyā-cām̐de — they carry them to give to the Moon of Nadia

**18.2.** Seeing that the night is ending, they disregard their beds — they cannot hold back even for half a moment;
filling trays with various delicacies, in rows they carry them to the Moon of Nadia.

শচীর গৃহেতে, প্রবেশিতে চিতে, উথলয়ে কত কৌতুক সিন্ধু ।
দেখয়ে সকলে, জননীর কোলে, খেলে বসি গোরা গোকুল-ইন্দু ॥

*śacīra gṛhete, prabeśite cite, uthalaye kata kautuka sindhu |*
*dekhaye sakale, jananīra kole, khele basi gorā gokula-indu ||*

*Word for word:* śacīra gṛhete prabeśite — on entering Shachi's house; cite uthalaye kata kautuka sindhu — an ocean of joy surges in their hearts; dekhaye sakale — all see; jananīra kole — on the mother's lap; khele basi — sits playing; gorā gokula-indu — Gora, the Moon of Gokula

**18.3.** As soon as they enter Shachi's house, an ocean of joy surges in their hearts;
they all see: on His mother's lap sits Gora, the Moon of Gokula, playing.

জুড়ায় নয়ান, নারীগণপ্রাণ, পাইয়া কোলে করি পাসরে দেহা ।
কহে নরহরি, আহা মরি মরি, কিবা সিরজিল এ হেন লেহা ॥

*juṛāya nayāna, nārīgaṇaprāṇa, pāiyā kole kari pāsare dehā |*
*kahe narahari, āhā mari mari, kibā sirajila e hena lehā ||*

*Word for word:* juṛāya nayāna — the eyes are soothed; nārī-gaṇa-prāṇa — the women's souls; pāiyā kole kari — taking [Him] in their arms; pāsare dehā — they forget the body; kahe narahari — Narahari says; āhā mari mari — ah, ah; kibā sirajila e hena lehā — how was such love created

**18.4.** Their eyes are soothed, and the women's souls — taking Him in their arms, they forget their bodies.
Narahari says: ah, ah, how beautifully this love was fashioned!

[^19-34]: GPT1 — p. 71, no. 29 (vibhasa; scan, PDF p. 330); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 29. The catalogue did not know it (new row NG-270). BR —
12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 771; ed. 1960, vv. 1000–1003): Ishana says that the women of Navadvipa used to come here at dawn to see
Gaurachandra, and quotes the pada (immediately after no. 3). Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the GCC. B. This is love in
vatsalya (the women are mothers, the Lord an infant in Shachi's arms), not the nagari motif.

## 19. Narahari — "śuna śuna prāṇasakhi tomāre baliye go…" (GPT1 p. 72, no. 30; GCC)
*A woman of Navadvipa says to her friend: "Blessed is life in Nadia: in Treta there was Kaushalya, in Dvapara Yashoda, in Kali fortunate
Shachi; blessed is Jagannatha Mishra; Shachi is like the Mother of the world: who else could have borne so many childish pranks? Some god
has shown mercy — now Nimai has become good, but He was a dreadful scamp." Yatharaga. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada
is in the GCC.*[^19-35]

শুন শুন প্রাণসখি তোমারে বলিয়ে গো ধন্য এই নদীয়া বসতি ।
ত্রেতায় কৌশল্যা দেবী দ্বাপরে যশোদা গো কলিযুগে শচী ভাগ্যবতী ॥

*śuna śuna prāṇasakhi tomāre baliye go dhanya ei nadīyā basati |*
*tretāya kauśalyā debī dvāpare yaśodā go kaliyuge śacī bhāgyabatī ||*

*Word for word:* śuna śuna prāṇa-sakhi — listen, listen, dear friend; tomāre baliye go — I tell you; dhanya ei nadīyā basati — blessed is living in this Nadia; tretāya kauśalyā debī — in Treta, queen Kaushalya; dvāpare yaśodā — in Dvapara, Yashoda; kali-yuge śacī bhāgyabatī — in the Kali-yuga, fortunate Shachi

**19.1.** "Listen, listen, dear friend, I tell you: blessed is life in this Nadia!
In the Treta-yuga there was queen Kaushalya, in the Dvapara Yashoda, and in the Kali-yuga fortunate Shachi.[^19-36]

ধন্য জগন্নাথ মিশ্র জগতে বিদিত গো যার সুপুণ্যের সীমা নাই ।
তার এ গৃহিণী পতিব্রতা স্নেহবতী গো যার হেন তনয় নিমাই ॥

*dhanya jagannātha miśra jagate bidita go yāra supuṇyera sīmā nāi |*
*tāra e gṛhiṇī patibratā snehabatī go yāra hena tanaya nimāi ||*

*Word for word:* dhanya jagannātha miśra — blessed is Jagannatha Mishra; jagate bidita — known to the world; yāra supuṇyera sīmā nāi — whose holy merit has no limit; tāra e gṛhiṇī — and his wife; patibratā snehabatī — devoted to her husband, full of tenderness; yāra hena tanaya nimāi — who has such a son, Nimai

**19.2.** Blessed is Jagannatha Mishra, known to all the world — there is no limit to his holy merit;
and his wife, devoted to her husband and full of tenderness — she who has such a son, Nimai.

জগতজননী মেন ইহারে বলিয়ে গো এরূপ স্বভাব আছে কার ।
শিশু-উপদ্রব এত সহিতে কে পারে গো জগতে উপমা নাহি যার ॥

*jagatajananī mena ihāre baliye go erūpa svabhāba āche kāra |*
*śiśu-upadraba eta sahite ke pāre go jagate upamā nāhi yāra ||*

*Word for word:* jagata-jananī mena — as the Mother of the world (মেন = যেন); ihāre baliye — I would call her; erūpa svabhāba āche kāra — who else has such a nature; śiśu-upadraba eta — so many childish pranks; sahite ke pāre — who could bear; jagate upamā nāhi yāra — who has no equal in the world

**19.3.** Truly I would call her the Mother of the world: who else has such a nature?
Who could bear so many childish pranks? There is none like her in the world.

না জানিয়ে কোন দেব অনুগ্রহ কৈল গো তেঁইসে হইল এবে ভাল ।
নহিলে এ নরহরি পরাণ নিমাই গো বড়ই বিষম ক্ষেপা ছিল ॥

*nā jāniye kona deba anugraha kaila go tem̐ise haila ebe bhāla |*
*nahile e narahari parāṇa nimāi go baṛai biṣama kṣepā chila ||*

*Word for word:* nā jāniye — I do not know; kona deba anugraha kaila — what god showed mercy; tem̐ise haila ebe bhāla — that is why it is good now; nahile — otherwise; e narahari parāṇa nimāi — this Nimai, Narahari's life; baṛai biṣama kṣepā chila — was a dreadful scamp

**19.4.** I do not know what god has shown mercy — that is why all is well now;
otherwise, you know, Nimai, the life of Narahari, was a dreadful scamp."

[^19-35]: GPT1 — p. 72, no. 30 (yatharaga; scan, PDF p. 331); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 30. The catalogue did not know it (new row NG-271; the
first line in catalogue row NG-015 had mixed it with no. 31). GCC — chapter 6, pada 7, marked "a certain [woman] says" (kācidāha). Not in
the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. The words "now all is well, but He was a scamp" show the GCC frame: the women recall the
childhood of Gaura, who is already a youth (cf. note 8).
[^19-36]: Kaushalya — the mother of Rama; Yashoda — the mother of Krishna in Vraja; Shachi — the mother of Gaura in the Kali-yuga.
Chakravarti places her in the line of the Lord's eternal mothers.

## 20. Narahari — "nimāicām̐dera kathā tomāre baliye go…" (GPT1 p. 72, no. 31; GCC)
*Another recalls: "Nimai is the chief of scamps: born on the full moon of Phalguna during an eclipse, He cried wildly and would not take
the breast; only the great ascetic of Shantipur, who knows the nature of this child, by some trick got Him to suck. I do not fear what
people say: from His very birth He has been a great scamp." Yatharaga. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the
GCC.*[^19-37]

নিমাইচাঁদের কথা তোমারে বলিয়ে গো নিমাই ক্ষেপার শিরোমণি ।
এমন আঁখুটি আর কোথাও না দেখি গো ধন্য মেন জনক জননী ॥

*nimāicām̐dera kathā tomāre baliye go nimāi kṣepāra śiromaṇi |*
*emana ām̐khuṭi āra kothāo nā dekhi go dhanya mena janaka jananī ||*

*Word for word:* nimāicām̐dera kathā — about Nimaichand; tomāre baliye — I tell you; nimāi kṣepāra śiromaṇi — Nimai is the crown of scamps; emana ām̐khuṭi — such obstinacy; āra kothāo nā dekhi — I have seen nowhere else; dhanya mena janaka jananī — truly blessed are the father and mother

**20.1.** "I'll tell you about Nimaichand: Nimai is the chief of scamps;
such obstinacy I have never seen anywhere else — truly blessed are His father and mother!

ফাল্গুন-পূর্ণিমা তিথি গ্রহণের কালে গো জন্মিয়া কাঁদয়ে অতিশয় ।
অনেক যতনে শিশু স্তন নাহি পীয়ে গো দেখিয়া সবারে লাগে ভয় ॥

*phālguna-pūrṇimā tithi grahaṇera kāle go janmiyā kām̐daye atiśaya |*
*aneka yatane śiśu stana nāhi pīye go dekhiyā sabāre lāge bhaya ||*

*Word for word:* phālguna-pūrṇimā tithi — on the full-moon day of Phalguna; grahaṇera kāle — at the time of the eclipse; janmiyā — having been born; kām̐daye atiśaya — He cries wildly; aneka yatane — despite great efforts; śiśu stana nāhi pīye — the child does not suck the breast; dekhiyā sabāre lāge bhaya — seeing it, all are frightened

**20.2.** On the full moon of Phalguna, at the time of the eclipse, having been born, He cried wildly;[^19-38]
however they tried, the child would not take the breast; seeing this, everyone was frightened.

শান্তিপুরবাসী মহাতপস্বী গোসাঞী গো জানয়ে যে বালকের রীতি ।
না জানি কেমন ছলে স্তন পীয়াইল গো সবার হইল স্থিরমতি ॥

*śāntipurabāsī mahātapasvī gosāñī go jānaye ye bālakera rīti |*
*nā jāni kemana chale stana pīyāila go sabāra haila sthiramati ||*

*Word for word:* śāntipura-bāsī — the resident of Shantipur; mahā-tapasvī gosāñī — the great ascetic Gosani; jānaye ye bālakera rīti — who knows the nature of this child; nā jāni kemana chale — I know not by what trick; stana pīyāila — made [Him] suck the breast; sabāra haila sthira-mati — all became calm

**20.3.** The resident of Shantipur, the great ascetic Gosani, who knows the nature of this child —
I do not know by what trick He got Him to suck the breast — and everyone calmed down.[^19-39]

কেউ কিছু বলে মোর মনে নাই ভয় গো মো এই বিচার কনু চিতে ।
নরহরি প্রাণধন ক্ষেপা বড়ই হবে গো তাহার আরম্ভ জন্ম হৈতে ॥

*keu kichu bale mora mane nāi bhaya go mo ei bicāra kanu cite |*
*narahari prāṇadhana kṣepā baṛai habe go tāhāra ārambha janma haite ||*

*Word for word:* keu kichu bale — whatever anyone says; mora mane nāi bhaya — I have no fear; mo ei bicāra kanu cite — I have judged so in my heart; narahari prāṇa-dhana — Narahari's treasure of life; kṣepā baṛai habe — will be a great scamp; tāhāra ārambha janma haite — it began from birth

**20.4.** Let them say what they like — I am not afraid, I have judged it so in my heart:
the treasure of Narahari's life will be a great scamp — it began from His very birth."

[^19-37]: GPT1 — p. 72, no. 31 (yatharaga; scan, PDF p. 331); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 31 (catalogue: NG-015). GCC — chapter 6, pada 8, marked
"and another [says]" (anyā ca). Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^19-38]: "Having been born" — the author's word; the Lord is not born as conditioned souls are: by His own will He appears from the womb of
Shachi, as Krishna from the womb of Devaki (Bhag. 10.3; CC Adi 13). His appearance on the full moon of the month of Phalguna during a
lunar eclipse, when everyone was chanting the name of Hari — CC Adi 13; CB Adi 3.
[^19-39]: "The great ascetic of Shantipur" — Advaita Acharya. According to the Advaita-prakasha, the newborn would not take the breast until
He heard the holy name; in Chakravarti, Advaita calms the Child "by some means". The Infant's crying stilled by the name of Hari — CC Adi
13, 14; CB Adi 4.

## 21. Narahari — "parāṇa nimāi mora khepā baṛa baṭe go…" (GPT1 p. 72, no. 32; GCC)
*A woman recalls: little Nimai, all covered in dust, was crawling about the courtyard, called His mother, climbed into her arms and
suddenly burst into inconsolable sobs, struggled, and no one could calm Him; one woman in despair clapped her hands and said "Hari" — and
at once He fell silent, laughed and hugged her neck; all sang "Hari, Hari", and He, not yet able to stand, danced holding His mother's
hand. Yatharaga. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC.*[^19-40]

পরাণ নিমাই মোর খেপা বড় বটে গো একদিন দেখিনু নয়ানে ।
ধূলায় ধূসর তনু কিবা অপরূপ গো হামাগুড়ি ফিরয়ে অঙ্গনে ॥

*parāṇa nimāi mora khepā baṛa baṭe go ekadina dekhinu nayāne |*
*dhūlāya dhūsara tanu kibā aparūpa go hāmāguṛi phiraye aṅgane ||*

*Word for word:* parāṇa nimāi mora — Nimai, my life; khepā baṛa baṭe — is indeed a great scamp; ekadina dekhinu nayāne — one day I saw with my eyes; dhūlāya dhūsara tanu — a body grey with dust; kibā aparūpa — how wondrous; hāmāguṛi phiraye aṅgane — He crawled about the courtyard

**21.1.** "Nimai, my life, is a great scamp, it's true: one day I saw with my own eyes:
His wondrous little body all grey with dust, He was crawling on all fours about the courtyard.

সুচাঁদবদনে হাসি মা বলিয়া ডাকে গো অমনি আইল শচী ধাইয়া ।
কোলেতে চড়িয়া অতি কাঁদিয়া বিকল গো তা দেখি বিদরে যেন হিয়া ॥

*sucām̐dabadane hāsi mā baliyā ḍāke go amani āila śacī dhāiyā |*
*kolete caṛiyā ati kām̐diyā bikala go tā dekhi bidare yena hiyā ||*

*Word for word:* sucām̐da-badane hāsi — smiling with His lovely moon-face; mā baliyā ḍāke — He calls "Mama"; amani āila śacī dhāiyā — at once Shachi came running; kolete caṛiyā — climbing into her arms; ati kām̐diyā bikala — He sobbed inconsolably; tā dekhi bidare yena hiyā — seeing it, the heart seemed to break

**21.2.** With a smile on His beautiful moonlike face He called: 'Mama!' — and at once Shachi came running;
having climbed into her arms, He suddenly burst into inconsolable sobs — seeing it, one's heart broke.

কত যত্ন করে তবু প্রবোধ না মানে গো অঙ্গ আছাড়ায় বারে বারে ।
কি হৈল কি হৈল বলি কাঁদে পুণ্যবতী গো কেহ স্থির হইতে না পারে ॥

*kata yatna kare tabu prabodha nā māne go aṅga āchāṛāya bāre bāre |*
*ki haila ki haila bali kām̐de puṇyabatī go keha sthira haite nā pāre ||*

*Word for word:* kata yatna kare — however she tries; tabu prabodha nā māne — still He will not be soothed; aṅga āchāṛāya bāre bāre — He flings His body about again and again; ki haila ki haila bali — saying "what happened, what happened?"; kām̐de puṇyabatī — the pious lady weeps; keha sthira haite nā pāre — no one can stay calm

**21.3.** However she tried, He would not be soothed — again and again He threw Himself about;
'What has happened, what has happened?' — the pious lady wept; no one could stay calm.

হেনই সময়ে এক নারী অতি খেদে গো হাতে তালি দিয়া বোলে হরি ।
তা শুনি চঞ্চল শিশু ক্রন্দন সম্বরি গো হাসয়ে তাহার গলা ধরি ॥

*henai samaye eka nārī ati khede go hāte tāli diyā bole hari |*
*tā śuni cañcala śiśu krandana sambari go hāsaye tāhāra galā dhari ||*

*Word for word:* henai samaye — just then; eka nārī ati khede — a woman in great distress; hāte tāli diyā bole hari — clapping her hands says "Hari"; tā śuni — hearing that; cañcala śiśu — the restless child; krandana sambari — checking His crying; hāsaye tāhāra galā dhari — laughs, hugging her neck

**21.4.** Just then a woman in despair clapped her hands and said: 'Hari!'
Hearing this, the restless child stopped crying and, laughing, hugged her neck.

সবাই হরষ হৈয়া হরি হরি বলে গো নিমাই নামিয়া কোলে হৈতে ।
দাঁড়াইতে নারে তবু নাচয়ে কৌতুকে গো হাত দিয়া জননীর হাতে ॥

*sabāi haraṣa haiyā hari hari bale go nimāi nāmiyā kole haite |*
*dām̐ṛāite nāre tabu nācaye kautuke go hāta diyā jananīra hāte ||*

*Word for word:* sabāi haraṣa haiyā — all, rejoicing; hari hari bale — say "Hari, Hari"; nimāi nāmiyā kole haite — Nimai, climbing down from her arms; dām̐ṛāite nāre — cannot stand; tabu nācaye kautuke — yet dances merrily; hāta diyā jananīra hāte — His hand in His mother's hand

**21.5.** All rejoiced and sang: 'Hari, Hari!' — and Nimai climbed down from her arms;
He could not yet stand, but, holding His mother's hand, He danced merrily.

কি লাগি কাঁদিল কেউ বুঝিতে নারিল গো সবাই ভাবয়ে মনে মনে ।
নরহরি পরাণ নিমাই এইরূপে গো খেপামি করিতে ভাল জানে ॥

*ki lāgi kām̐dila keu bujhite nārila go sabāi bhābaye mane mane |*
*narahari parāṇa nimāi eirūpe go khepāmi karite bhāla jāne ||*

*Word for word:* ki lāgi kām̐dila — why He cried; keu bujhite nārila — no one could understand; sabāi bhābaye mane mane — all wonder to themselves; narahari parāṇa nimāi — Nimai, the life of Narahari; eirūpe — in this way; khepāmi karite bhāla jāne — knows well how to play pranks

**21.6.** Why He had cried, no one understood — everyone just wondered to themselves.
That is how Nimai, the life of Narahari, knows how to play His pranks."[^19-41]

[^19-40]: GPT1 — pp. 72–73, no. 32 (yatharaga; scan, PDF pp. 331–332); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 32 (catalogue: NG-016). GCC — chapter 6, pada 9.
Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. The same pada is printed in the GPT a second time — p. 76, no. 42, raga vibhasa
(catalogue: NG-023), in a shortened and altered form: without the episode of the name of Hari (lines 21.3b–21.4a are merged into one:
"however she tried, He would not be soothed — laughing, He hugged her neck"), with an added line "all the townspeople were enchanted,
seeing that wondrous form" and the ending "…knows how to play"; the variants are in the VAR, and it is not translated separately. The
Infant's crying stilled by the name of Hari — CC Adi 14; CB Adi 4 (the Lord cries, and the women, clapping their hands, sing "Hari").
[^19-41]: "Play His pranks" (khepāmi) — on the lips of those who love Him this is an affectionate word; the meaning of the lila, according to
the CB and CC: the Lord cries so that everyone will sing the name of Hari.

## 22. Narahari — "nimāi cañcala khepā kichui nā māne go…" (GPT1 p. 73, no. 33; GCC)
*A woman recalls: holding the hem of His mother's cloth, the little one was walking about the courtyard, saw His shadow and began to play
with it, and there lay a snake — He lay down on its terrible hood; all ran up in horror, the snake tried to slip away, and He caught it
again; Shachi carried Him off in her arms; then a bird flew by — "Catch it for Me!" — and He wept bitterly until He Himself forgot it.
Yatharaga. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC.*[^19-42]

নিমাই চঞ্চল খেপা কিছুই না মানে গো শুন এক দিবসের কথা ।
মায়ের অঞ্চলে ধরি ফিরয়ে অঙ্গনে গো আপনার ছায়া দেখি তথা ॥

*nimāi cañcala khepā kichui nā māne go śuna eka dibasera kathā |*
*māyera añcale dhari phiraye aṅgane go āpanāra chāyā dekhi tathā ||*

*Word for word:* nimāi cañcala khepā — Nimai is restless and a scamp; kichui nā māne — heeds nothing; śuna eka dibasera kathā — hear what happened one day; māyera añcale dhari — holding His mother's hem; phiraye aṅgane — He walks about the courtyard; āpanāra chāyā dekhi tathā — He sees His own shadow there

**22.1.** "Nimai is restless and a scamp, He heeds nothing; listen to what happened one day:
holding the hem of His mother's cloth, He was walking about the courtyard — and saw His own shadow there.

ছাড়িয়া অঞ্চল ছায়া-সহিত খেলায় গো তাহাতে আছিল এক ফণী ।
তাহার দারুণ ফণে শয়ন করিয়া গো কি আনন্দ কিছুই না জানি ॥

*chāṛiyā añcala chāyā-sahita khelāya go tāhāte āchila eka phaṇī |*
*tāhāra dāruṇa phaṇe śayana kariyā go ki ānanda kichui nā jāni ||*

*Word for word:* chāṛiyā añcala — letting go of the hem; chāyā-sahita khelāya — He plays with the shadow; tāhāte āchila eka phaṇī — there was a snake there; tāhāra dāruṇa phaṇe — on its terrible hood; śayana kariyā — lying down; ki ānanda — what bliss; kichui nā jāni — He knows nothing [of fear]

**22.2.** Letting go of the hem, He began to play with His shadow, and there was a snake;
lying down on its terrible hood — what bliss! — He feared nothing at all.[^19-43]

হায় হায় করি সবে ধাইয়া আইসে গো পলাইতে নাগ পুনঃ ধরে ।
কাঁপয়ে সকলে শচী ব্যাকুল হইয়া গো যতনে ধরিয়া কোলে করে ॥

*hāya hāya kari sabe dhāiyā āise go palāite nāga punaḥ dhare |*
*kām̐paye sakale śacī byākula haiyā go yatane dhariyā kole kare ||*

*Word for word:* hāya hāya kari — crying "alas, alas"; sabe dhāiyā āise — all come running; palāite nāga punaḥ dhare — as the snake flees, He catches it again; kām̐paye sakale — all tremble; śacī byākula haiyā — Shachi in distress; yatane dhariyā kole kare — carefully takes Him in her arms

**22.3.** Crying 'Alas, alas!' all came running; the snake tried to slip away, and He caught it again;
everyone trembled, and Shachi in distress carefully took Him up in her arms.

হেনই সময়ে এক পাখী উড়ি যায় গো কিবা সে ভঙ্গীতে তাই হেরি ।
দে মোরে ধরিয়া ইহা বলি বারে বারে গো কাঁদয়ে মায়ের গলা ধরি ॥

*henai samaye eka pākhī uṛi yāya go kibā se bhaṅgīte tāi heri |*
*de more dhariyā ihā bali bāre bāre go kām̐daye māyera galā dhari ||*

*Word for word:* henai samaye — just then; eka pākhī uṛi yāya — a bird flies by; kibā se bhaṅgīte tāi heri — how charmingly He looks at it; de more dhariyā ihā — catch it for Me; bali bāre bāre — saying again and again; kām̐daye māyera galā dhari — He weeps, His arms around His mother's neck

**22.4.** Just then a bird flew past — how charmingly He looked at it!
'Catch it for Me!' He said again and again, and wept, His arms around His mother's neck.

নীলমণি হার পারা ধারা দু-নয়নে গো ঘুচিল সে কাজরের রেখা ।
ও চাঁদবদনখানি মলিন হইল গো তাহা কিয়ে আঁখে যায় দেখা ॥

*nīlamaṇi hāra pārā dhārā du-nayane go ghucila se kājarera rekhā |*
*o cām̐dabadanakhāni malina haila go tāhā kiye ām̐khe yāya dekhā ||*

*Word for word:* nīlamaṇi hāra pārā — like a sapphire necklace; dhārā du-nayane — streams from both eyes; ghucila se kājarera rekhā — the line of kohl was washed away; o cām̐da-badana-khāni — that moonlike little face; malina haila — grew dim; tāhā kiye ām̐khe yāya dekhā — can one bear to look at it

**22.5.** From His eyes, two streams like a necklace of sapphires: the kohl was washed away;
that moonlike little face grew dim — can one bear to look at it?

কেউ কিছু কয় কারু কথায় না ভুলে গো প্রাণ ফাটে ক্রন্দন শুনিয়া ।
নরহরি প্রাণ শিশু আপনি ভুলিল গো তেঁই যে সুস্থির হৈল হিয়া ॥

*keu kichu kaya kāru kathāya nā bhule go prāṇa phāṭe krandana śuniyā |*
*narahari prāṇa śiśu āpani bhulila go tem̐i ye susthira haila hiyā ||*

*Word for word:* keu kichu kaya — whatever anyone says; kāru kathāya nā bhule — He is not won over by anyone's words; prāṇa phāṭe krandana śuniyā — the heart breaks hearing His crying; narahari prāṇa śiśu — the child, Narahari's life; āpani bhulila — forgot by Himself; tem̐i ye susthira haila hiyā — and so His heart became calm

**22.6.** Whatever anyone said — He would not yield to anyone's words; one's heart broke hearing His crying;
and then the child, the life of Narahari, forgot it Himself, and His heart grew calm."

[^19-42]: GPT1 — p. 73, no. 33 (yatharaga; scan, PDF p. 332); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 33. The catalogue did not know it (new row NG-272). GCC —
chapter 6, pada 10. Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^19-43]: The snake in the courtyard of Mishra's house, on whose coils the crawling Infant lay down — CB Adi 4; BR 12 (ed. 1960, vv. 982–983):
"that is why Ananta-deva passed along this road". It is Ananta-Shesha, the Lord's couch, come to serve Him; that is why the Child knows no
fear.

## 23. Narahari — "soṇāra nimāi mora parāṇa-putali go…" (GPT1 p. 73, no. 34; GCC)
*A woman recalls: if Nimai is not given what He wants — there is trouble; once, holding His mother's hem, He cried and begged for butter
and rolled in the dust; Shachi brought butter from somewhere, He ate it and said: "I am a cowherd's son, nothing but this pleases Me";
when they laughingly asked Him: "Which cowherd's, then?" — He ran away, and Shachi said in embarrassment: "Well, well." Yatharaga.
**Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC.*[^19-44]

সোণার নিমাই মোর পরাণ-পুতলি গো হেন খেলা আছে কি জগতে ।
যখন যা চায় তাহা না দিলে বিষম গো কেহ না পারয়ে প্রবোধিতে ॥

*soṇāra nimāi mora parāṇa-putali go hena khelā āche ki jagate |*
*yakhana yā cāya tāhā nā dile biṣama go keha nā pāraye prabodhite ||*

*Word for word:* soṇāra nimāi mora — my golden Nimai; parāṇa-putali — the doll of my soul; hena khelā āche ki jagate — are there such games in the world; yakhana yā cāya — whatever He wants; tāhā nā dile biṣama — if not given, there is trouble; keha nā pāraye prabodhite — no one can soothe Him

**23.1.** "Golden Nimai, the doll of my soul — are there such games anywhere in the world!
Whatever He wants — if it is not given, there is trouble: no one can soothe Him.

একদিন নিমাই নবনী দে বলিয়া গো মায়ের আঁচলে ধরি কাঁদে ।
প্রবোধিতে অধিক ধূলায় গড়ি যায় গো তিলেক ধৈরজ নাহি বাঁধে ॥

*ekadina nimāi nabanī de baliyā go māyera ām̐cale dhari kām̐de |*
*prabodhite adhika dhūlāya gaṛi yāya go tileka dhairaja nāhi bām̐dhe ||*

*Word for word:* ekadina nimāi — one day Nimai; nabanī de baliyā — saying "give Me butter"; māyera ām̐cale dhari kām̐de — cries holding His mother's hem; prabodhite adhika — the more they soothe; dhūlāya gaṛi yāya — He rolls in the dust; tileka dhairaja nāhi bām̐dhe — He does not calm down for a moment

**23.2.** One day Nimai, holding the hem of His mother's cloth, was crying: 'Give Me butter!'
The more they tried to soothe Him, the more He rolled in the dust — He could not calm down for a moment.

না জানিয়ে কোথা হৈতে নবনী আনিয়া গো নিমাইর করেতে দিল মায় ।
নবনী খাইয়া বোলে মো গোপতনয় গো ইহা বিনু কিছু নাহি ভায় ॥

*nā jāniye kothā haite nabanī āniyā go nimāira karete dila māya |*
*nabanī khāiyā bole mo gopatanaya go ihā binu kichu nāhi bhāya ||*

*Word for word:* nā jāniye — I do not know; kothā haite nabanī āniyā — bringing butter from where; nimāira karete dila māya — the mother put it in Nimai's hands; nabanī khāiyā bole — having eaten the butter, He says; mo gopa-tanaya — I am a cowherd's son; ihā binu kichu nāhi bhāya — nothing but this pleases Me

**23.3.** I do not know where His mother brought butter from, but she put it in Nimai's hands;
having eaten the butter, He says: 'I am a cowherd's son; nothing but this pleases Me.'[^19-45]

চাহি মুখ পানে মোরা হাসিয়া পুছিনু গো তুমি কোন্ গোপের ছাওয়াল ।
নরহরি প্রাণশিশু শুনি পলাইল গো লাজে শচী বলে ভাল ভাল ॥

*cāhi mukha pāne morā hāsiyā puchinu go tumi kon gopera chāoyāla |*
*narahari prāṇaśiśu śuni palāila go lāje śacī bale bhāla bhāla ||*

*Word for word:* cāhi mukha pāne — looking into His face; morā hāsiyā puchinu — we laughingly asked; tumi kon gopera chāoyāla — which cowherd's boy are You; narahari prāṇa-śiśu — the child, Narahari's life; śuni palāila — hearing, ran away; lāje śacī bale bhāla bhāla — Shachi in embarrassment says "well, well"

**23.4.** Looking into His face, we laughed and asked: 'Which cowherd's little son are You, then?'
Hearing this, the child — the life of Narahari — ran away, and Shachi said in embarrassment: 'Well, well!'"

[^19-44]: GPT1 — p. 73, no. 34 (yatharaga; scan, PDF p. 332); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 34 (catalogue: NG-017). GCC — chapter 6, pada 11. Not in
the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^19-45]: The Lord lets slip the truth about Himself: He is Krishna, the son of the cowherd Nanda, who loves butter (cf. no. 10 and note 20).
Shachi is embarrassed: a brahmana's son calls himself the son of a cowherd; by the will of yogamaya her motherly love does not let her
reflect on these words.

## 24. Narahari — "ekadina nirjane nimāi ghare bule go…" (GPT1 p. 73, no. 35)
*Three wonders of childhood: Shachi sees in the house footprints with the marks of a flag, a vajra and a goad — Mishra says these are the
footprints of their household Deity Gopala; another day Shachi hears the sound of a flute and the name "Radha" pouring from Nimai's
mouth; a third time two thieves carry Nimai off for His ornaments, but, deluded, return to Shachi's house, leave Him and flee. Yatharaga.
**Attribution: not established** — the pada is neither in the GCC (although it stands in the middle of its cycle) nor in the BR or other
witnesses; the metre is uneven, the refrain "go" is placed carelessly — perhaps a later imitation of the cycle.*[^19-46]

একদিন নির্জনে নিমাই ঘরে বুলে গো আশ্চর্য্য চরণচিহ্ন দেখি ।
অতি সঙ্গোপনে শচী দেখায় চরণচিহ্ন মিশ্র পুরন্দরে ঘরে ডাকি ॥

*ekadina nirjane nimāi ghare bule go āścaryya caraṇacihna dekhi |*
*ati saṅgopane śacī dekhāya caraṇacihna miśra purandare ghare ḍāki ||*

*Word for word:* ekadina nirjane — one day, alone; nimāi ghare bule — [when] Nimai roamed about the house; āścarya caraṇa-cihna dekhi — seeing wondrous footprints; ati saṅgopane — very secretly; śacī dekhāya caraṇa-cihna — Shachi shows the footprints; miśra purandare ghare ḍāki — calling Mishra Purandara into the house

**24.1.** One day, when Nimai was wandering alone about the house, Shachi saw wondrous footprints;
very secretly, calling Mishra Purandara into the house, she shows him these footprints.

মিশ্র পদচিহ্নে দেখি ধ্বজবজ্রাঙ্কুশ আদি মিশ্রবর ভাবে মনে মনে ।
গোপালবিগ্রহ গৃহে তারি পদচিহ্ন ইহা শচীরে বলেন সঙ্গোপনে ॥

*miśra padacihne dekhi dhvajabajrāṅkuśa ādi miśrabara bhābe mane mane |*
*gopālabigraha gṛhe tāri padacihna ihā śacīre balena saṅgopane ||*

*Word for word:* miśra pada-cihne dekhi — Mishra sees in the footprints; dhvaja-bajrāṅkuśa ādi — flag, vajra, goad and other [marks]; miśra-bara bhābe mane mane — the best of the Mishras ponders within; gopāla-bigraha gṛhe — the Deity Gopala in the house; tāri pada-cihna ihā — these are His footprints; śacīre balena saṅgopane — he says to Shachi secretly

**24.2.** Mishra sees in the footprints a flag, a vajra, a goad and other marks; the best of the Mishras ponders within himself
and secretly says to Shachi: "These are the footprints of our household Deity Gopala."[^19-47]

আর দিন শচী শুনে নিমাইর মুখ হৈতে বাহির হইছে বংশীরব ।
রাধা রাধা শব্দ তাতে নিরখি এহেন রঙ্গ শচী ভয়ে হইল নীরব ॥

*āra dina śacī śune nimāira mukha haite bāhira haiche baṃśīraba |*
*rādhā rādhā śabda tāte nirakhi ehena raṅga śacī bhaye haila nīraba ||*

*Word for word:* āra dina — another day; śacī śune — Shachi hears; nimāira mukha haite bāhira haiche baṃśī-raba — the sound of a flute coming out of Nimai's mouth; rādhā rādhā śabda tāte — and in it the words "Radha, Radha"; nirakhi ehena raṅga — seeing such play; śacī bhaye haila nīraba — Shachi fell silent from fear

**24.3.** Another day Shachi hears: from Nimai's mouth pours the sound of a flute,
and in it the words "Radha, Radha"; seeing such play, Shachi fell silent from fear.[^19-48]

আর দিন ভূষণের লোভে দুই চোর গো নিমাইরে করিল হরণ ।
নিমাই নিমাই বলি ফুকরিয়া শচী কাঁদে চারিভিতে হয় অন্বেষণ ॥

*āra dina bhūṣaṇera lobhe dui cora go nimāire karila haraṇa |*
*nimāi nimāi bali phukariyā śacī kām̐de cāribhite haya anveṣaṇa ||*

*Word for word:* āra dina — another day; bhūṣaṇera lobhe — out of greed for ornaments; dui cora — two thieves; nimāire karila haraṇa — abducted Nimai; nimāi nimāi bali phukariyā — crying aloud "Nimai, Nimai"; śacī kām̐de — Shachi weeps; cāribhite haya anveṣaṇa — there is a search on all sides

**24.4.** Another day two thieves, coveting His ornaments, carried Nimai off;
"Nimai, Nimai!" Shachi calls aloud and weeps; they search for Him everywhere.

এদিকে কি ভুলে ভুলি আপনার ঘর ভাবি দুই চোর শচীগৃহে ফিরি ।
কান্ধে হৈতে শিশুরে ভূতলে নামাইয়া গো পলাইয়া গেল ত্বরা করি ॥

*edike ki bhule bhuli āpanāra ghara bhābi dui cora śacīgṛhe phiri |*
*kāndhe haite śiśure bhūtale nāmāiyā go palāiyā gela tvarā kari ||*

*Word for word:* edike — meanwhile; ki bhule bhuli — bewildered by some illusion; āpanāra ghara bhābi — thinking it their own house; dui cora śacī-gṛhe phiri — the two thieves, returning to Shachi's house; kāndhe haite śiśure bhūtale nāmāiyā — setting the child down from their shoulders onto the ground; palāiyā gela tvarā kari — ran away in haste

**24.5.** Meanwhile the two thieves, bewildered by some illusion, taking Shachi's house for their own, came back there,
set the child down from their shoulders onto the ground and hastily ran away.[^19-49]

হারাধন পাঞা পুন সকলে হরিষ গো অর্থ কিছু বুঝিতে নারিল ।
চোরের দুর্দ্দশা দেখি মুচকি মুচকি গো নরহরি হাসিতে লাগিল ॥

*hārādhana pāñā puna sakale hariṣa go artha kichu bujhite nārila |*
*corera durddaśā dekhi mucaki mucaki go narahari hāsite lāgila ||*

*Word for word:* hārā-dhana pāñā puna — regaining the lost treasure; sakale hariṣa — all rejoiced; artha kichu bujhite nārila — could not understand anything of it; corera durdaśā dekhi — seeing the plight of the thieves; mucaki mucaki — slyly; narahari hāsite lāgila — Narahari began to smile

**24.6.** Having regained their lost treasure, all rejoiced, but could understand nothing;
seeing the plight of the thieves, Narahari began to smile slyly.

[^19-46]: GPT1 — pp. 73–74, no. 35 (yatharaga; scan, PDF pp. 332–333); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 35. The catalogue did not know it (new row
NG-273). It is not in the GCC: in chapter 6 the pada "soṇāra nimāi" (no. 23) is followed immediately by "śunaye nimāira kathā" (no. 25). Not in
the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. C. The pada retells all three episodes closely following the Chaitanya-bhagavata (Adi 4–5).
[^19-47]: Footprints with the marks of a flag (dhvaja), a vajra (thunderbolt) and a goad (ankusha) — the marks on the soles of Bhagavan. In CB
Adi 4, Jagannatha Mishra and Shachi, seeing these footprints, decided that their household Bala-Gopala had walked about the house, and
worshipped Him.
[^19-48]: The sound of the flute and the name of Radha in the child's mouth are signs that Gaura is Krishna Himself and His heart is full of
Radha; Shachi, out of motherly love, is frightened, without reflecting on her son's majesty. This episode is not in the CB.
[^19-49]: "Bewildered by an illusion" (ki bhule bhuli) — according to CB Adi 4, the thieves were confused by the Lord's power (vishnu-maya)
and, wandering, came back to the house of Jagannatha Mishra. The Lord Himself is not subject to it: it is His energy, which He directs for
the sake of His lila.

## 25. Narahari — "śunaye nimāira kathā ekadina sukhe go…" (GPT1 p. 74, no. 36; GCC)
*Shachi, so that Nimai may become calmer, worships a god with offerings; Nimai runs up from somewhere, eats the offering and laughingly
says: "I am the God of gods, why do you not worship Me?" Shachi chases Him in fear, afraid that something may happen to her son, and He,
sitting on His father's lap, complains: "Mother won't give Me anything to eat"; the father rejoices. Yatharaga. **Attribution: probably
Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC.*[^19-50]

শুনয়ে নিমাইর কথা একদিন সুখে গো নানা দ্রব্য লৈয়া শচী মায় ।
নিমাই চঞ্চল ভাল হবে এই হেতু গো যতনে পূজয়ে দেবতায় ॥

*śunaye nimāira kathā ekadina sukhe go nānā drabya laiyā śacī māya |*
*nimāi cañcala bhāla habe ei hetu go yatane pūjaye debatāya ||*

*Word for word:* śunaye nimāira kathā — hear about Nimai; ekadina sukhe — one day joyfully; nānā drabya laiyā śacī māya — Shachi-ma with various offerings; nimāi cañcala bhāla habe — that restless Nimai may become good; ei hetu — for this reason; yatane pūjaye debatāya — diligently worships a deity

**25.1.** Listen to this about Nimai: one day Shachi-ma joyfully, with various offerings,
so that restless Nimai might become good, was diligently worshipping a deity.

হেনই সময়ে কোথা হইতে আসিয়া গো না দেখিতে নৈবেদ্য খাইয়া ।
হাসিয়া বলয়ে মুই দেবের দেবতা গো মোরে না পূজহ কি লাগিয়া ॥

*henai samaye kothā haite āsiyā go nā dekhite naibedya khāiyā |*
*hāsiyā balaye mui debera debatā go more nā pūjaha ki lāgiyā ||*

*Word for word:* henai samaye — just then; kothā haite āsiyā — coming from somewhere; nā dekhite — unseen; naibedya khāiyā — eating the offering; hāsiyā balaye — laughingly says; mui debera debatā — I am the God of gods; more nā pūjaha ki lāgiyā — why do you not worship Me

**25.2.** Just then He, running in from somewhere — no one even noticed — ate the offering
and, laughing, says: "I am the God of gods; why do you not worship Me?"[^19-51]

হায় হায় করি শচী দাবাড়িয়া যায় গো মনেতে পাইয়া বড় ভয় ।
ব্যাকুল হইয়া চিতে বিচার করয়ে গো পাছে বা নিমাইর কিছু হয় ॥

*hāya hāya kari śacī dābāṛiyā yāya go manete pāiyā baṛa bhaya |*
*byākula haiyā cite bicāra karaye go pāche bā nimāira kichu haya ||*

*Word for word:* hāya hāya kari — crying "alas, alas"; śacī dābāṛiyā yāya — Shachi chases [Him]; manete pāiyā baṛa bhaya — with great fear in her heart; byākula haiyā cite bicāra karaye — in distress she thinks; pāche vā nimāira kichu haya — lest something happen to Nimai

**25.3.** Crying "Alas, alas!" Shachi chases Him, a great fear in her heart;
in distress she thinks: "What if something happens to Nimai!"

হেথা শিশু মিশ্রের কোলেতে বসি কয় গো মা মোরে না দেন খাইতে ।
নরহরি-পরাণ নিমাইর কথা শুনি গো বাপের আনন্দ বড় চিতে ॥

*hethā śiśu miśrera kolete basi kaya go mā more nā dena khāite |*
*narahari-parāṇa nimāira kathā śuni go bāpera ānanda baṛa cite ||*

*Word for word:* hethā — meanwhile; śiśu miśrera kolete basi — the child, sitting on Mishra's lap; kaya — says; mā more nā dena khāite — Mother won't give Me anything to eat; narahari-parāṇa nimāira kathā śuni — hearing the words of Nimai, Narahari's life; bāpera ānanda baṛa cite — great joy in the father's heart

**25.4.** And meanwhile the child, sitting on Mishra's lap, says: "Mother won't give Me anything to eat."
Hearing the words of Nimai, the life of Narahari, the father feels great joy in his heart.

[^19-50]: GPT1 — p. 74, no. 36 (yatharaga; scan, PDF p. 333); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 36 (catalogue: NG-018). GCC — chapter 6, pada 12. Not in
the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^19-51]: Cf. Lochana Dasa: Nimai eats the offering to the goddess Shashthi and tells His mother that worship of Him, like watering the root,
satisfies all the gods (Chaitanya-mangala, Adi-khanda; Bhag. 4.31.14). The Lord is the God of gods, and all the demigods are His
servants; here He reveals this in jest, and Shachi out of love fears only for Him.

## 26. Narahari — "e mora nimāicām̐da khāite cāhile go…" (GPT1 p. 74, no. 37; GCC)
*A woman tells: let Nimai ask for food and you delay a moment — in anger He smashes the house and spoils everything; scold Him — it gets
twice as bad; He fears neither father nor mother, the neighbours cannot restrain Him, He fears only Vishvarupa; He roams Nadia alone,
gets into other people's houses and everywhere makes the children cry. Yatharaga. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in
the GCC.*[^19-52]

এ মোর নিমাইচাঁদ খাইতে চাহিলে গো তিলেক বিলম্ব যদি হয় ।
ঘর দ্বার ভাঙ্গিয়া ফেলায় মহাক্রোধে গো করয়ে অনেক অপচয় ॥

*e mora nimāicām̐da khāite cāhile go tileka bilamba yadi haya |*
*ghara dvāra bhāṅgiyā phelāya mahākrodhe go karaye aneka apacaya ||*

*Word for word:* e mora nimāicām̐da — this Nimaichand of mine; khāite cāhile — if He asks for food; tileka bilamba yadi haya — if there is a moment's delay; ghara dvāra bhāṅgiyā phelāya — He smashes house and doors; mahā-krodhe — in great anger; karaye aneka apacaya — causes much waste

**26.1.** "This Nimaichand of mine — if He asks for food and you delay even a moment,
in great anger He smashes the house and the doors, spoils and scatters everything.

যদি কিছু বলে তবে দ্বিগুণ বাড়য় গো না ডরায় এ বাপ মায়েরে ।
এ পাড়াপড়সী কেউ নিবারিতে নারে গো একা বিশ্বরূপে ভয় করে ॥

*yadi kichu bale tabe dviguṇa bāṛaya go nā ḍarāya e bāpa māyere |*
*e pāṛāpaṛasī keu nibārite nāre go ekā biśvarūpe bhaya kare ||*

*Word for word:* yadi kichu bale — if anyone says something; tabe dviguṇa bāṛaya — then it doubles; nā ḍarāya e bāpa māyere — He fears neither father nor mother; e pāṛā-paṛasī keu — none of the neighbours; nibārite nāre — can restrain Him; ekā biśvarūpe bhaya kare — He fears only Vishvarupa

**26.2.** Say anything to Him — He plays up twice as much; He fears neither father nor mother;
none of the neighbours can restrain Him — He fears only Vishvarupa.[^19-53]

এমন বালক আর কোথাও না দেখি গো একাকী ফিরয়ে নদীয়াতে ।
অলখিতে যার তার ঘরে প্রবেশিয়া গো নানা কর্ম্ম করয়ে হেলাতে ॥

*emana bālaka āra kothāo nā dekhi go ekākī phiraye nadīyāte |*
*alakhite yāra tāra ghare prabeśiyā go nānā karmma karaye helāte ||*

*Word for word:* emana bālaka — such a boy; āra kothāo nā dekhi — I have seen nowhere else; ekākī phiraye nadīyāte — He wanders alone through Nadia; alakhite — unnoticed; yāra tāra ghare prabeśiyā — entering anyone's house; nānā karma karaye helāte — playfully does all sorts of things

**26.3.** I have never seen such a boy anywhere: He wanders alone through Nadia,
slips unnoticed into anybody's house and playfully gets up to all sorts of things.

যেখানে সেখানে শিশুগণেরে কাঁদায় গো কি বলিব তা সবার মায় ।
নরহরি প্রাণ বিশ্বম্ভরের চরিতে গো কেবা না ডরায় নদীয়ায় ॥

*yekhāne sekhāne śiśugaṇere kām̐dāya go ki baliba tā sabāra māya |*
*narahari prāṇa biśvambharera carite go kebā nā ḍarāya nadīyāya ||*

*Word for word:* yekhāne sekhāne — here and there; śiśu-gaṇere kām̐dāya — He makes the children cry; ki baliba tā sabāra māya — what will their mothers say; narahari prāṇa — the life of Narahari; biśvambharera carite — at the doings of Vishvambhara; kebā nā ḍarāya nadīyāya — who in Nadia is not afraid

**26.4.** Wherever He goes, He makes the children cry — what can their mothers say?
At the doings of Vishvambhara, the life of Narahari, who in Nadia does not tremble?"

the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. Nimai's childhood pranks in Navadvipa and the neighbours' complaints — CB Adi 6; CC Adi 14.

## 27. Narahari — "ekadina nimāi prabeśi gṛhamājhe go…" (GPT1 p. 74, no. 38)
*Nimai mixed together in the house rice, dal, salt, oil, yogurt, milk, butter and ghee; His mother ran after Him with a stick, and He sat
down on a heap of discarded pots; "Fie, get down, it is impure!" — "How can a pot in which bhoga was cooked for Vishnu be impure? The
impurity is in your mind"; the astonished mother bathed Him and took Him in her arms: "This child is not a child, but Hari of
Vaikuntha." Yatharaga. **Attribution: not established** — the pada is neither in the GCC (although it stands in the middle of its
cycle) nor in the BR or other witnesses; the metre is uneven, the refrain "go" drops out — perhaps a later imitation.*[^19-54]

একদিন নিমাই প্রবেশি গৃহমাঝে গো করিল দুরন্তপনা কত ।
মিশাইল একসঙ্গে চাউল দাইল নুন তৈল দধি দুগ্ধ নবনীত ঘৃত ॥

*ekadina nimāi prabeśi gṛhamājhe go karila durantapanā kata |*
*miśāila ekasaṅge cāula dāila nuna taila dadhi dugdha nabanīta ghṛta ||*

*Word for word:* ekadina nimāi — one day Nimai; prabeśi gṛha-mājhe — entering the house; karila durantapanā kata — made much mischief; miśāila eka-saṅge — mixed together; cāula dāila nuna taila — rice, dal, salt, oil; dadhi dugdha nabanīta ghṛta — yogurt, milk, butter and ghee

**27.1.** One day Nimai got into the house and made a great deal of mischief:
He mixed together rice, dal, salt, oil, yogurt, milk, butter and ghee.

নিমাইর দৌরাত্ম্য সহিতে না পারিয়া মায় লগুড় লইয়া এক হাতে ।
নিমাইর পাছে পাছে ধাইয়া চলিল শিশু দৌড়াইল মায়ের অগ্রেতে ॥

*nimāira daurātmya sahite nā pāriyā māya laguṛa laiyā eka hāte |*
*nimāira pāche pāche dhāiyā calila śiśu dauṛāila māyera agrete ||*

*Word for word:* nimāira daurātmya — Nimai's wildness; sahite nā pāriyā — unable to bear; māya laguṛa laiyā eka hāte — the mother, a stick in one hand; nimāira pāche pāche dhāiyā calila — ran after Nimai; śiśu dauṛāila māyera agrete — the child raced ahead of His mother

**27.2.** Unable to bear His wildness, His mother, a stick in one hand,
ran after Nimai, and the child raced ahead of her.

উচ্ছিষ্ট হাঁড়ীর রাশি যেইখানে ছিল গো নিমাই বসিল তারোপরে ।
শচী কহে ছি ছি বাপ অশুচি তেজিয়া আয় স্নান করি নিব তোরে ঘরে ॥

*ucchiṣṭa hām̐ṛīra rāśi yeikhāne chila go nimāi basila tāropare |*
*śacī kahe chi chi bāpa aśuci tejiyā āya snāna kari niba tore ghare ||*

*Word for word:* ucchiṣṭa hām̐ṛīra rāśi — the heap of discarded pots; yeikhāne chila — where it lay; nimāi basila tāropare — Nimai sat on it; śacī kahe — Shachi says; chi chi bāpa — fie, fie, my son; aśuci tejiyā āya — leave the impurity and come; snāna kari niba tore ghare — I'll bathe You and take You home

**27.3.** Where a heap of discarded pots lay, there Nimai sat down on top;
Shachi says: "Fie, fie, my son, leave that impurity, come here — I'll bathe You and take You home."[^19-55]

শিশু কহে যে হাঁড়ীতে বিষ্ণুর রাঁধিলে ভোগ সে হাঁড়ী অশুচি কি প্রকারে ।
অশুচি তোমার মনে আমি দেখি শুচি সব বল মা অশুচি কি সংসারে ॥

*śiśu kahe ye hām̐ṛīte biṣṇura rām̐dhile bhoga se hām̐ṛī aśuci ki prakāre |*
*aśuci tomāra mane āmi dekhi śuci saba bala mā aśuci ki saṃsāre ||*

*Word for word:* śiśu kahe — the child says; ye hām̐ṛīte — in which pot; biṣṇura rām̐dhile bhoga — bhoga was cooked for Vishnu; se hām̐ṛī aśuci ki prakāre — how can that pot be impure; aśuci tomāra mane — the impurity is in your mind; āmi dekhi śuci saba — I see everything as pure; bala mā — tell Me, Mother; aśuci ki saṃsāre — what in the world is impure

**27.4.** The child replies: "A pot in which bhoga was cooked for Vishnu — how can it be impure?
The impurity is in your mind; I see everything as pure; tell Me, Mother, what in the world is impure?"[^19-56]

শিশুমুখে তত্ত্বকথা শুনিয়া অবাক্ মাতা স্নান করাইয়া লয় কোলে ।
এ শিশু ত শিশু নয় বৈকুণ্ঠবিহারী হরি পুত্র তব নরহরি বোলে ॥

*śiśumukhe tattvakathā śuniyā abāk mātā snāna karāiyā laya kole |*
*e śiśu ta śiśu naya baikuṇṭhabihārī hari putra taba narahari bole ||*

*Word for word:* śiśu-mukhe tattva-kathā śuniyā — hearing words of truth from the child's mouth; abāk mātā — the amazed mother; snāna karāiyā laya kole — bathes Him and takes Him in her arms; e śiśu ta śiśu naya — this child is no child; baikuṇṭha-bihārī hari — Hari who sports in Vaikuntha; putra taba — your son; narahari bole — says Narahari

**27.5.** Hearing words of truth from the child's mouth, the mother was amazed, bathed Him and took Him in her arms.
"This child is no child: your son is Hari who dwells in Vaikuntha," says Narahari.

there the pada "e mora nimāicām̐da" (no. 26) is followed immediately by "nimāicām̐dera e carita" (no. 28). Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the
Gita-chandrodaya. C.
[^19-55]: Earthen pots in which food had once been cooked were thrown away as ritually impure; cf. CB Adi 6, CC Adi 14.
[^19-56]: Cf. CC Adi 14 (the Lord, sitting on the discarded pots, answers His mother; Krishnadasa Kaviraja explains that in these words He
playfully speaks like Dattatreya) and CB Adi 6; Murari 1.6. The meaning is not that the distinction between pure and impure is altogether
illusory: the Lord is Vishnu Himself, everything connected with service to Him is pure, and He Himself is defiled by nothing.

## 28. Narahari — "nimāicām̐dera e carita kata kaba go…" (GPT1 p. 75, no. 39; GCC)
*At bathing time on the bank of the Suradhuni Nimai gives neither men nor women any peace and quarrels with those carrying offerings to the
gods; but when they complain of Him to Shachi and Mishra, He is virtue itself; all marvel: as Kanu was in the house of Nanda, so is He in
the house of Shachi — it must be He. Yatharaga. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC.*[^19-57]

নিমাইচাঁদের এ চরিত কত কব গো স্নানকালে সুরধুনী-তীরে ।
কি নারী পুরুষ কেউ স্থির হৈতে নারে গো তথা মহা উপদ্রব করে ॥

*nimāicām̐dera e carita kata kaba go snānakāle suradhunī-tīre |*
*ki nārī puruṣa keu sthira haite nāre go tathā mahā upadraba kare ||*

*Word for word:* nimāicām̐dera e carita — these doings of Nimaichand; kata kaba — how much can I tell; snāna-kāle — at bathing time; suradhunī-tīre — on the bank of the Suradhuni (Ganga); ki nārī puruṣa — whether women or men; keu sthira haite nāre — no one can be at peace; tathā mahā upadraba kare — there He wreaks great havoc

**28.1.** "How much can I tell of such doings of Nimaichand! At bathing time on the bank of the Suradhuni
neither women nor men can find any peace — such havoc He wreaks there.

নানা উপহার অতি যতনে লইয়া গো দেবতা পূজিতে যেবা যায় ।
তা সনে কলহ যত লেখা নাই তার গো কিবা বা না করে নদীয়ায় ॥

*nānā upahāra ati yatane laiyā go debatā pūjite yebā yāya |*
*tā sane kalaha yata lekhā nāi tāra go kibā bā nā kare nadīyāya ||*

*Word for word:* nānā upahāra — various offerings; ati yatane laiyā — carrying with great care; debatā pūjite yebā yāya — whoever goes to worship a deity; tā sane kalaha yata — the quarrels with them; lekhā nāi tāra — are beyond counting; kibā vā nā kare nadīyāya — what does He not do in Nadia

**28.2.** Whoever goes with offerings, carefully carrying them to worship a deity —
with all of them He quarrels without number: what does He not do in Nadia!

যদি কেউ কভু শচী-মিশ্রেরে জানায় গো তখন কি বা সে সাধুরীতি ।
সবাকার মনে অতি কৌতুক বাড়য় গো দেখিলে না রহে বুদ্ধিগতি ॥

*yadi keu kabhu śacī-miśrere jānāya go takhana ki bā se sādhurīti |*
*sabākāra mane ati kautuka bāṛaya go dekhile nā rahe buddhigati ||*

*Word for word:* yadi keu kabhu — if anyone ever; śacī-miśrere jānāya — complains to Shachi and Mishra; takhana ki vā se sādhu-rīti — then what good manners [He shows]; sabākāra mane — in everyone's mind; ati kautuka bāṛaya — merriment grows; dekhile nā rahe buddhi-gati — on seeing [Him], one's wits fail

**28.3.** But if someone complains to Shachi and Mishra — then what good manners He has!
Everyone's merriment grows: seeing Him, one loses one's wits.[^19-58]

যেরূপ নন্দের ঘরে কানুর ধামালি গো সেরূপ দেখিয়ে শচী ঘরে ।
নরহরি প্রাণ নিমাই এই বুঝি সেই গো নহিলে এরূপ কেবা করে ॥

*yerūpa nandera ghare kānura dhāmāli go serūpa dekhiye śacī ghare |*
*narahari prāṇa nimāi ei bujhi sei go nahile erūpa kebā kare ||*

*Word for word:* yerūpa nandera ghare — as in Nanda's house; kānura dhāmāli — Kanu's pranks; serūpa dekhiye śacī ghare — so I see in Shachi's house; narahari prāṇa nimāi — Nimai, the life of Narahari; ei bujhi sei — must be that very one; nahile erūpa kebā kare — otherwise who would act like this

**28.4.** Such as were the pranks of Kanu in the house of Nanda, such I see in the house of Shachi;
Nimai, the life of Narahari — it must be He Himself: otherwise who would act like this?"[^19-59]

chapter 6, pada 14. Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. Nimai's pranks on the ghats of the Ganga, the complaints of the

# Chapter 20. Appendix. Padas signed "Narahari" from the Gaura-pada-tarangini — IV: the appearance of Gaura, the end of childhood, the samskaras and the betrothal

*Continuation of the appendix (the introductory note on the two Naraharis, on the arguments for attribution and on the marks in the
headings is in ch. 17). Chapter 20: a pada surveying Gaura's lila from the section "aishvarya and madhurya" (GPT 1.3); padas on the
appearance of the Lord (section 2.1); the last padas of the section "Balya-lila" (2.2); the beginning of the section "Karnavedha and the
wedding" (2.3) — the first tonsure and ear-piercing, the upanayana, the first meeting with Lakshmipriya by the Ganga, the news of the
wedding and the adhivasa (the wedding day follows in the next chapter). Almost all the padas of the chapter are quoted by Narahari
Chakravarti in the 12th wave of the Bhakti-ratnakara, where Ishana shows Srinivasa the house of Jagannatha Mishra and tells what happened
there (two are in Chakravarti's Gaura-charita-chintamani); one pada (no. 12) has not been found in any witness. According to Majumdar, the
padas on the birth and childhood of Nimai known under the name "Narahari" are late: Narahari Sarakara did not see the Lord's childhood.
Before translation the "Narahari" signatures in sections 1.3 and 2.1–2.3 were checked throughout in GPT1: the catalogue had missed five more
padas of section 2.3 (here nos. 13 and 15, new rows NG-280, 281; NG-282…284 follow in the next chapter). The base text is GPT1 (doubtful places from the scan), collated with GPT2, the
BR (eds. 1912 and 1960) and the Gaura-charita-chintamani (ed. 1947); PK, KGC, PS and the Gita-chandrodaya have been checked. On the "birth" of
the Lord see note 4; on the childhood games as lila, note 2 of chapter 19; on the samskaras, note 26. The notes of the GPT editors are not
reproduced.*

## 1. Narahari — "śacīsuta gaurahari…" (GPT1 p. 26, section 1.3, no. 2; BR)
*A survey of the lila: the son of Shachi appeared in Navadvipa and revealed sankirtana; He took sannyasa, remained in Nilachala and,
intoxicated with Radhika's love, intoxicated the world with it; His associates are beside themselves with prema; the treasure unattainable
even for the gods He gave to the world. Raga kamoda. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave).*[^20-1]

শচীসুত গৌরহরি, নবদ্বীপে অবতরি, করিলেন বিবিধ বিলাস ।
সঙ্গে লৈয়া প্রিয়গণ, প্রকাশিয়া সংকীর্ত্তন, বাঢ়াইলা সবার উল্লাস ॥

*śacīsuta gaurahari, nabadvīpe abatari, karilena bibidha bilāsa |*
*saṅge laiyā priyagaṇa, prakāśiyā saṃkīrttana, bāṛhāilā sabāra ullāsa ||*

*Word for word:* śacī-suta gaurahari — Shachi's son Gaurahari; nabadvīpe abatari — descending in Navadvipa; karilena bibidha bilāsa — displayed manifold pastimes; saṅge laiyā priyagaṇa — taking His dear ones with Him; prakāśiyā saṅkīrtana — revealing sankirtana; bāṛhāilā sabāra ullāsa — increased the joy of all

**1.1.** The son of Shachi, Gaurahari, having descended in Navadvipa, displayed manifold pastimes:
together with His dear associates He revealed sankirtana and increased the joy of all.

কিবা সে সন্ন্যাস বেশে, ভ্রমি প্রভু দেশে দেশে, নীলাচলে আসিয়া রহিলা ।
রাধিকার প্রেমে মাতি, না জানি দিবারাতি, সে প্রেমে জগত মাতাইলা ॥

*kibā se sannyāsa beśe, bhrami prabhu deśe deśe, nīlācale āsiyā rahilā |*
*rādhikāra preme māti, nā jāni dibārāti, se preme jagata mātāilā ||*

*Word for word:* kibā se sannyāsa beśe — and then in the dress of a sannyasi; bhrami prabhu deśe deśe — the Lord wandering from land to land; nīlācale āsiyā rahilā — came to Nilachala and remained; rādhikāra preme māti — intoxicated with Radhika's love; nā jāni dibārāti — knowing neither day nor night; se preme jagata mātāilā — intoxicated the world with that love

**1.2.** And then, in the dress of a sannyasi, the Lord wandered from land to land and, coming to Nilachala, remained there;
intoxicated with Radhika's love, knowing neither day nor night, He intoxicated the whole world with that love.[^20-2]

নিত্যানন্দ বলরাম, অদ্বৈত গুণের ধাম, গদাধর শ্রীবাসাদি যত ।
দেখি সে অদ্ভুত রীতি, কেহ না ধরয়ে ধৃতি, প্রেমায় বিহ্বল অবিরত ॥

*nityānanda balarāma, advaita guṇera dhāma, gadādhara śrībāsādi yata |*
*dekhi se adbhuta rīti, keha nā dharaye dhṛti, premāya bihvala abirata ||*

*Word for word:* nityānanda balarāma — Nityananda who is Balarama; advaita guṇera dhāma — Advaita, abode of virtues; gadādhara śrībāsādi yata — Gadadhara, Srivasa and all the rest; dekhi se adbhuta rīti — seeing that wondrous way; keha nā dharaye dhṛti — no one keeps composure; premāya bihvala abirata — ceaselessly overwhelmed with prema

**1.3.** Nityananda who is Balarama, Advaita the abode of virtues, Gadadhara, Srivasa and all the rest,
seeing this wondrous way, cannot keep their composure — ceaselessly overwhelmed with prema.

দেবের দুর্ল্লভ রত্ন, মিলাইলা করি যত্ন, কৃপার বালাই লৈয়া মরি ।
কৈলা কলিযুগ ধন্য, প্রভু কৃষ্ণচৈতন্য, যশ গায় দাস নরহরি ॥

*debera durllabha ratna, milāilā kari yatna, kṛpāra bālāi laiyā mari |*
*kailā kaliyuga dhanya, prabhu kṛṣṇacaitanya, yaśa gāya dāsa narahari ||*

*Word for word:* debera durlabha ratna — the treasure hard to obtain even for the gods; milāilā kari yatna — bestowed with effort; kṛpāra bālāi laiyā mari — may I die taking on myself all ill [threatening such] mercy; kailā kali-yuga dhanya — made the age of Kali blessed; prabhu kṛṣṇa-caitanya — the Lord Krishna-Chaitanya; yaśa gāya dāsa narahari — Narahari Dasa sings the glory

**1.4.** The treasure unattainable even for the gods He has, with effort, bestowed [on us] — may I die warding off all ill from such mercy!
The Lord Krishna-Chaitanya has blessed the age of Kali — Narahari Dasa sings His glory.

[^20-1]: GPT1 — p. 26, section 1.3 ("aishvarya and madhurya of the Gaura-avatara"), no. 2 (kamoda; scan, PDF p. 285); GPT2 — section 1.3, no. 2
(catalogue: NG-003). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 914; ed. 1960, vv. 3605–3608): Ishana, having told Srinivasa of the Lord's departure from
Navadvipa to Puri, quotes this pada as a brief survey of His whole lila. Variant: the BR has "bilāilā" — "distributed", the GPT "milāilā" —
"procured, bestowed". Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B.
[^20-2]: In Puri the Lord is absorbed in the bhava of Radha longing for Krishna: it was to taste Her love that He appeared (CC Adi 4; Antya 14–20).
Nityananda is Balarama Himself (1.3; CC Adi 5).

## 2. Narahari — "phālguna-pūrṇimā śubhakṣaṇe…" (GPT1 p. 59, section 2.1, no. 19; BR)
*In the auspicious hour of the full moon of Phalguna Shachi, having given birth to a son, cannot gaze at Him enough; Jagannatha Mishra,
hearing the news, floats in an ocean of happiness and performs the rites; the Ganga and the Earth forget their sorrows; with the rising
of Gaurachandra the darkness of sin departs. Raga vasanta. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave).*[^20-3]

ফাল্গুন-পূর্ণিমা শুভক্ষণে । পুত্র প্রসবিয়া শচী চাহে পুত্রপানে ॥

*phālguna-pūrṇimā śubhakṣaṇe | putra prasabiyā śacī cāhe putrapāne ||*

*Word for word:* phālguna-pūrṇimā śubha-kṣaṇe — in the auspicious hour of the Phalguna full moon; putra prasabiyā śacī — Shachi, having borne a son; cāhe putra-pāne — gazes at the son

**2.1.** In the auspicious hour of the full moon of Phalguna Shachi, having given birth to a son, cannot take her eyes from Him.[^20-4]

তিলে তিলে কত উঠে চিতে । কনকনবনী ভ্রমে নারে পরশিতে ॥

*tile tile kata uṭhe cite | kanakanabanī bhrame nāre paraśite ||*

*Word for word:* tile tile — at every moment; kata uṭhe cite — how much rises in the heart; kanaka-nabanī bhrame — as if [He were] golden fresh butter; nāre paraśite — cannot touch

**2.2.** How many feelings rise in her heart at every moment! As if He were golden fresh butter, she dares not touch Him.

কত না যতনে কোলে করে । পুত্রের জনম জানাইয়া মিশ্রবরে ॥

*kata nā yatane kole kare | putrera janama jānāiyā miśrabare ||*

*Word for word:* kata nā yatane — with what care; kole kare — takes on her lap; putrera janama jānāiyā — making known the son's birth; miśra-bare — to the best of the Mishras

**2.3.** With what care she takes Him on her lap and sends word of the son's birth to the best of the Mishras.

জগন্নাথ বিপ্রশিরোমণি । ভাসে সুখসমুদ্রে পুত্রের জন্ম শুনি ॥

*jagannātha bipraśiromaṇi | bhāse sukhasamudre putrera janma śuni ||*

*Word for word:* jagannātha bipra-śiromaṇi — Jagannatha, crown of brahmanas; bhāse sukha-samudre — floats in an ocean of happiness; putrera janma śuni — hearing of the son's birth

**2.4.** Jagannatha, the crown of brahmanas, hearing of the birth of his son, floats in an ocean of happiness.

কত সাধে চলয়ে ধাইয়া । না ধরে ধৈরজ চাঁদমুখ নিরখিয়া ॥

*kata sādhe calaye dhāiyā | nā dhare dhairaja cām̐damukha nirakhiyā ||*

*Word for word:* kata sādhe — with what eagerness; calaye dhāiyā — goes running; nā dhare dhairaja — cannot keep composure; cām̐da-mukha nirakhiyā — beholding the moonlike face

**2.5.** With what joy he hastens [to the son] — and, seeing the moonlike face, cannot contain himself.

লইয়া আপন প্রিয়গণে । করয়ে মঙ্গল কর্ম্ম পুত্রের কল্যাণে ॥

*laiyā āpana priyagaṇe | karaye maṅgala karmma putrera kalyāṇe ||*

*Word for word:* laiyā āpana priyagaṇe — gathering his dear ones; karaye maṅgala karma — performs auspicious rites; putrera kalyāṇe — for the son's welfare

**2.6.** Gathering his dear ones, he performs auspicious rites for the welfare of the son.

চতুর্দ্দিকে জয় জয়ধ্বনি । সবে কহে ধন্য ধন্য জনক জননী ॥

*caturddike jaya jayadhvani | sabe kahe dhanya dhanya janaka jananī ||*

*Word for word:* caturdike — on all sides; jaya jaya-dhvani — cries of "jaya, jaya"; sabe kahe — all say; dhanya dhanya janaka jananī — blessed, blessed are father and mother

**2.7.** On all sides sounds "jaya, jaya"; all say: "Blessed, blessed are the father and the mother!"

সবার অন্তরে বাঢ়ে সুখ । সুরধুনী ধরণী বিসরে সব দুখ ॥

*sabāra antare bāṛhe sukha | suradhunī dharaṇī bisare saba dukha ||*

*Word for word:* sabāra antare — in everyone's heart; bāṛhe sukha — happiness grows; suradhunī dharaṇī — the Suradhuni (Ganga) and the Earth; bisare saba dukha — forget all sorrow

**2.8.** Happiness grows in everyone's heart; the Suradhuni and the Earth forget all their sorrows.[^20-5]

দশদিক্ হইল উজ্জ্বল । পশুপক্ষী বৃক্ষলতা প্রফুল্ল সকল ॥

*daśadik haila ujjvala | paśupakṣī bṛkṣalatā praphulla sakala ||*

*Word for word:* daśa-dik haila ujjvala — the ten directions became bright; paśu-pakṣī bṛkṣa-latā — beasts, birds, trees, creepers; praphulla sakala — all blossomed

**2.9.** All ten directions have become bright; beasts, birds, trees and creepers — all have blossomed.

নরহরি কি কহিবে আর । গৌরচন্দ্রোদয়ে গেল পাপ-অন্ধকার ॥

*narahari ki kahibe āra | gauracandrodaye gela pāpa-andhakāra ||*

*Word for word:* narahari ki kahibe āra — what more will Narahari say; gauracandrodaye — at the rising of Gaurachandra; gela pāpa-andhakāra — the darkness of sin went away

**2.10.** What more can Narahari say? With the rising of Gaurachandra the darkness of sin has gone.

[^20-3]: GPT1 — p. 59, section 2.1 ("the appearance"), no. 19 (vasanta; scan, PDF p. 318); GPT2 — section 2.1, no. 19. The catalogue did not know it
(new row NG-276). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 764; ed. 1960, vv. 907–916): Ishana, showing Srinivasa the place of the Lord's appearance in
the house of Jagannatha Mishra, quotes padas of Vasu Ghosha and Vrindavana Dasa on the birth and then — in a row — this one and the next four
(nos. 3–5; between them a pada signed by Ghanashyama, GPT 2.1 no. 23, outside the appendix) and no. 6. Variant in the last line: the BR has
"the darkness of suffering" (tāpa), the GPT "the darkness of sin" (pāpa). Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B.
The GPT1 footnotes to lines 2.8–2.9 (editor's notes) are not reproduced.
[^20-4]: The poet speaks in the language of the lila: "gave birth to a son", "birth". But the Lord is not born as a conditioned soul is, by karma and
in a material body: He appears (avirbhava) by His own will in His eternal form — as Krishna appeared before Devaki (Bhag. 10.3; Gita 4.6, 4.9;
CC Adi 13–14). So the appearance of the Lord is understood by Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja and Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati; so too are all the
padas on the "birth" in this chapter to be understood.
[^20-5]: The Suradhuni ("the river of the gods") is the Ganga. The poet says that with the appearance of the Lord both the Ganga and the Earth,
burdened with the sins of the age of Kali, forgot their sorrows: on the banks of the Ganga He will perform His pastimes, and the sins of the world
will depart.

## 3. Narahari — "phālguna-pūrṇimā maṅgalera sīmā…" (GPT1 pp. 59–60, no. 20; BR)
*The full moon of Phalguna: the Moon of Gokula has appeared, in every house of Nadia there is an ocean of joy; Shachi with her son on her lap
in the birth-chamber; in the darkness of the eclipse crowds run to see the Child and forget themselves. Raga not stated (in the BR —
dhanashi). **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^20-6]

ফাল্গুন-পূর্ণিমা, মঙ্গলের সীমা, প্রকট গোকুল-ইন্দু ।
নদীয়ানগরে, প্রতি ঘরে ঘরে, উথলে আনন্দসিন্ধু ॥

*phālguna-pūrṇimā, maṅgalera sīmā, prakaṭa gokula-indu |*
*nadīyānagare, prati ghare ghare, uthale ānandasindhu ||*

*Word for word:* phālguna-pūrṇimā — the Phalguna full moon; maṅgalera sīmā — the summit of blessings; prakaṭa gokula-indu — the Moon of Gokula has appeared; nadīyā-nagare — in the town of Nadia; prati ghare ghare — in every house; uthale ānanda-sindhu — an ocean of joy surges

**3.1.** The full moon of Phalguna — the summit of all blessings: the Moon of Gokula has appeared!
In the town of Nadia, in every house, an ocean of joy surges.

কিবা কৌতুক পরস্পরে ।
শচীদেবী ভালে, পুত্র লৈয়া কোলে, বিলসে সূতিকাঘরে ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*kibā kautuka paraspare |*
*śacīdebī bhāle, putra laiyā kole, bilase sūtikāghare || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* kibā kautuka paraspare — what merriment among them; śacī-debī bhāle — Shachi-devi splendidly; putra laiyā kole — taking her son on her lap; bilase sūtikā-ghare — shines in the birth-chamber

**3.2.** What merriment among them all!
Shachi-devi, taking her son on her lap, shines in the birth-chamber.

বালকে দেখিতে, ধায় চারিভিতে, কেহ না ধরয়ে ধৃতি ।
গ্রহণান্ধকারে, কে চিনে কাহারে, অসংখ্য লোকের গতি ॥

*bālake dekhite, dhāya cāribhite, keha nā dharaye dhṛti |*
*grahaṇāndhakāre, ke cine kāhāre, asaṃkhya lokera gati ||*

*Word for word:* bālake dekhite — to see the Child; dhāya cāri-bhite — they run from all sides; keha nā dharaye dhṛti — no one restrains himself; grahaṇa-andhakāre — in the darkness of the eclipse; ke cine kāhāre — who knows whom; asaṃkhya lokera gati — the coming of countless people

**3.3.** To see the Child they run from all sides — no one can restrain himself;
in the darkness of the eclipse who can tell who is who? There is no counting the people coming.[^20-7]

বালক-মাধুরী, দেখি আঁখি ভরি, পাসরে আপন দেহা ।
নরহরি কয়, শচীর তনয়, প্রকাশে কি নব লেহা ॥

*bālaka-mādhurī, dekhi ām̐khi bhari, pāsare āpana dehā |*
*narahari kaya, śacīra tanaya, prakāśe ki naba lehā ||*
