*Word for word:* bālaka-mādhurī — the Child's sweetness; dekhi ām̐khi bhari — seeing to their eyes' fill; pāsare āpana dehā — they forget their own bodies; narahari kaya — Narahari says; śacīra tanaya — Shachi's son; prakāśe ki naba lehā — reveals what new love

**3.4.** Gazing their fill at the sweetness of the Child, they forget their own bodies.
Narahari says: the son of Shachi reveals some new love!

[^20-6]: GPT1 — pp. 59–60, no. 20 (no raga; scan, PDF pp. 318–319); GPT2 — section 2.1, no. 20. The catalogue did not know it (new row NG-277). BR —
12th wave (ed. 1912, pp. 764–765; ed. 1960, vv. 917–920, "punardhānaśī"). Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B.
Line 3.2 is the refrain (dhru).
[^20-7]: The Lord appeared in the evening of the full moon of Phalguna, during a lunar eclipse, when by custom everyone was bathing in the Ganga and
repeating the name of Hari (CC Adi 13; CB Adi 2–3; Murari 1.5). "The Moon of Gokula" is Krishna: Gaura is Krishna Himself, the Lord of Gokula.

## 4. Narahari — "parama śubha śacīgarbhe…" (GPT1 p. 60, no. 21; BR)
*Gaura, the Lord of Gokula, in the womb of Shachi; the gods praise Him; on the night of the full moon, when Rahu had swallowed the moon, the
Lord appeared, having first revealed His name; those entering Mishra's house, seeing the Child, lose their senses; the pride of Kali is
crushed. Raga kamoda. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR; Vrajabuli.*[^20-8]

পরম শুভ শচীগর্ভে বিলসত গৌর গোকুল নাহ ।
করই স্তুতিনতি দেবগণ ঘন, ভবনে ভরই উছাহ ॥

*parama śubha śacīgarbhe bilasata gaura gokula nāha |*
*karai stutinati debagaṇa ghana, bhabane bharai uchāha ||*

*Word for word:* parama śubha — in the supremely auspicious [hour]; śacī-garbhe bilasata — abides in Shachi's womb; gaura gokula nāha — Gaura, the Lord of Gokula; karaï stuti-nati debagaṇa ghana — the gods again and again praise and bow; bhabane bharaï uchāha — jubilation fills the house

**4.1.** In the womb of Shachi, in the supremely auspicious hour, abides Gaura — the Lord of Gokula;
again and again the gods offer praises and bow down; the house brims with jubilation.

শুভগ ফাল্গুন-পূর্ণিমানিশি শশী উদয়ে রাহু গরাসি ।
ঐছে সময়ে প্রকাশে পহুঁ নিজ নাম পহিলে প্রকাশি ॥

*śubhaga phālguna-pūrṇimāniśi śaśī udaye rāhu garāsi |*
*aiche samaye prakāśe pahum̐ nija nāma pahile prakāśi ||*

*Word for word:* śubhaga phālguna-pūrṇimā-niśi — on the auspicious night of the Phalguna full moon; śaśī udaye rāhu garāsi — Rahu swallowing the rising moon; aiche samaye — at such a time; prakāśe pahum̐ — the Lord appeared; nija nāma pahile prakāśi — having first revealed His own name

**4.2.** On the auspicious night of the Phalguna full moon, when Rahu had swallowed the rising moon —
at such an hour the Lord appeared, having first revealed His name.[^20-9]

হোত জয় জয়কার জগভরি ধিরজ ধরত ন কোই ।
মিশ্রভবনে প্রবেশি শিশু, অবলোকি উনমত হোই ॥

*hota jaya jayakāra jagabhari dhiraja dharata na koi |*
*miśrabhabane prabeśi śiśu, abaloki unamata hoi ||*

*Word for word:* hota jaya jayakāra jaga-bhari — "jaya, jaya" sounds through the world; dhiraja dharata na koi — no one keeps composure; miśra-bhabane prabeśi — entering Mishra's house; śiśu abaloki — beholding the Child; unamata hoi — they go mad [with joy]

**4.3.** "Jaya, jaya" resounds through the whole world, no one can restrain himself;
those entering Mishra's house, beholding the Child, go mad with happiness.

বিবিধ মঙ্গল, রচই নব নব, সব মনোরথ পূর ।
ভণত নরহরি, বিপুলবলী কলি গরবভরে ভেল চূর ॥

*bibidha maṅgala, racai naba naba, saba manoratha pūra |*
*bhaṇata narahari, bipulabalī kali garababhare bhela cūra ||*

*Word for word:* bibidha maṅgala racaï naba naba — they perform various auspicious rites, ever new; saba manoratha pūra — all desires are fulfilled; bhaṇata narahari — Narahari says; bipula-balī kali — mighty Kali; garaba-bhare bhela cūra — his pride is crushed

**4.4.** They perform various auspicious rites, ever new; all desires are fulfilled.
Narahari says: the pride of mighty Kali is crushed.

[^20-8]: GPT1 — p. 60, no. 21 (kamoda; scan, PDF p. 319); GPT2 — section 2.1, no. 21. The catalogue did not know it (new row NG-278). BR — 12th wave
(ed. 1912, p. 765; ed. 1960, vv. 921–924). Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. "In the womb of Shachi" —
on the appearance of the Lord see note 4.
[^20-9]: During the eclipse all the people of Nadia, bathing, were repeating "Hari, Hari" — thus the Lord, before appearing, made the whole world sing
His name (CC Adi 13). Rahu — according to the Puranas, the demon who swallows the moon at an eclipse.

## 5. Narahari — "jaya jaya jaya maṅgalaraba…" (GPT1 pp. 60–61, no. 22; BR)
*The night of the Phalguna full moon: from the womb of Shachi Gaura, the delight of Vraja, has appeared; His body flashes like steady
lightning; the gods shower flowers, the kinnaras sing, the heavenly dancers dance; it is spring, the Malaya breeze blows, the waters of the
Ganga surge; the poet is beside himself with the festivity in Mishra's house. Raga vasanta. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada
is in the BR; ornate Vrajabuli with rhythmic syllables.*[^20-10]

জয় জয় জয় মঙ্গলরব, ফাল্গুন-পূর্ণিমানিশি নব শোভিত,
শচীগর্ভে প্রকট গৌরবরজ রঞ্জনা ।
ঝলকত বর বালকতনু, কুঙ্কুম থির দামিনী জনু,
চমকত মুখচন্দ মধুর ধৈরজ ভর ভঞ্জনা ॥

*jaya jaya jaya maṅgalaraba, phālguna-pūrṇimāniśi naba śobhita,*
*śacīgarbhe prakaṭa gaurabaraja rañjanā |*
*jhalakata bara bālakatanu, kuṅkuma thira dāminī janu,*
*camakata mukhacanda madhura dhairaja bhara bhañjanā ||*

*Word for word:* jaya jaya jaya maṅgala-raba — the auspicious cries "jaya, jaya, jaya"; phālguna-pūrṇimā-niśi naba śobhita — the night of the Phalguna full moon shines anew; śacī-garbhe prakaṭa — appeared from Shachi's womb; gaura baraja-rañjanā — Gaura, the delight of Vraja; jhalakata bara bālaka-tanu — the lovely body of the Child flashes; kuṅkuma thira dāminī janu — like steady lightning the colour of kunkuma; camakata mukha-canda — the moonlike face gleams; madhura dhairaja-bhara bhañjanā — sweetly shattering all composure

**5.1.** "Jaya, jaya, jaya!" — auspicious cries; the night of the Phalguna full moon shines anew:
from the womb of Shachi Gaura has appeared — the delight of Vraja.
The lovely body of the Child flashes — like steady lightning the colour of kunkuma;
His moonlike face gleams, sweetly shattering all composure.

পহুঁ প্রকাশ নিরখত, ঘনগণ সহ সুরগণ গগনে বরষত,
কুসুমাবলী বিপুল পুলক ভরল অঙ্গহী ।
করত কত মনোরথ চিত, চঞ্চল ভণি চারু চরিত,
লোচন জলছল কত ছবি পায়ত বহু রঙ্গহী ॥

*pahum̐ prakāśa nirakhata, ghanagaṇa saha suragaṇa gagane baraṣata,*
*kusumābalī bipula pulaka bharala aṅgahī |*
*karata kata manoratha cita, cañcala bhaṇi cāru carita,*
*locana jalachala kata chabi pāyata bahu raṅgahī ||*

*Word for word:* pahum̐ prakāśa nirakhata — seeing the Lord's appearance; ghana-gaṇa saha sura-gaṇa gagane baraṣata — the gods with hosts of clouds shower from the sky; kusumābalī — garlands of flowers; bipula pulaka bharala aṅgahī — bodies filled with great thrills; karata kata manoratha cita — how many longings in their hearts; cañcala bhaṇi cāru carita — excitedly telling the lovely deeds; locana jala-chala — through the tears in their eyes; kata chabi pāyata bahu raṅgahī — how many images they behold, with much delight

**5.2.** Seeing the Lord's appearance, the gods with hosts of clouds shower from the sky
garlands of flowers; their bodies are filled with great thrills.
How many longings in their hearts! Excitedly they sing of His lovely deeds;
through the tears that flood their eyes, how many images they behold, in what rapture!

গায়ত কিন্নর সুধঙ্গ, বায়ত মৃদুতর মৃদঙ্গ,
ধাধিকি ধিকিতা ধিক্ ধিক্ ধিক্কটতক্ ধিন্নানা ।
নৃত্যত সুর নর্ত্তকীচয়, বিবিধ ভাতি করু অভিনয়,
উঘটতত কথৈ থৈ থৈ তি অই অই অতেন্নানা ॥

*gāyata kinnara sudhaṅga, bāyata mṛdutara mṛdaṅga,*
*dhādhiki dhikitā dhik dhik dhikkaṭatak dhinnānā |*
*nṛtyata sura narttakīcaya, bibidha bhāti karu abhinaya,*
*ughaṭatata kathai thai thai ti ai ai atennānā ||*

*Word for word:* gāyata kinnara sudhaṅga — the kinnaras sing with a sweet sound; bāyata mṛdutara mṛdaṅga — the mridanga plays softly; dhā-dhiki… — mridanga syllables; nṛtyata sura-nartakī-caya — the heavenly dancers dance; bibidha bhāti karu abhinaya — enact performances of every kind; ughaṭatata kathai… — dance counting

**5.3.** The kinnaras sing to a sweet sound, the mridanga softly plays:
"dhā-dhiki dhikitā dhik dhik dhikkaṭak dhinnānā";
the heavenly dancers dance, enacting performances of every kind:
"uṭṭata kathai thai thai ti ai ai atennānā".[^20-11]

নির্ম্মল দশদিশ উজোর, মলয়ানিল বহত থোর,
পিককুল কুহু কত বসন্ত ঋতুপতি সর সায়এ ।
উছলত সুর-সরিত-বারি, নদীয়া মহি মুদ বিথারি,
মিশ্রভবন কৌতুকে নরহরি হিয় উনমতায়এ ॥

*nirmmala daśadiśa ujora, malayānila bahata thora,*
*pikakula kuhu kata basanta ṛtupati sara sāyae |*
*uchalata sura-sarita-bāri, nadīyā mahi muda bithāri,*
*miśrabhabana kautuke narahari hiya unamatāyae ||*

*Word for word:* nirmala daśadiśa ujora — pure and bright are the ten directions; malayānila bahata thora — the Malaya breeze blows gently; pika-kula kuhu — the cuckoos sound "kuhu"; basanta ṛtupati sara sāyae — spring, king of seasons, is full of sweetness; uchalata sura-sarita-bāri — the waters of the river of the gods surge; nadīyā mahi muda bithāri — spreading joy over the land of Nadia; miśra-bhabana kautuke — at the festivity in Mishra's house; narahari hiya unamatāyae — Narahari's heart is beside itself

**5.4.** Pure and bright are all ten directions, gently blows the breeze from the Malaya hills,
the flocks of cuckoos sound "kuhu" — spring, the king of seasons, is full of sweetness.
The waters of the river of the gods surge, joy spreads over the land of Nadia;
at the festivity in Mishra's house Narahari's heart is beside itself.

[^20-10]: GPT1 — pp. 60–61, no. 22 (vasanta; scan, PDF pp. 319–320); GPT2 — section 2.1, no. 22. The catalogue did not know it (new row NG-279). BR —
12th wave (ed. 1912, pp. 765–766; ed. 1960, vv. 925–928). Line 5.3: GPT1 has "nṛtyasura", the BR "nṛtyata sura" ("the heavenly ones dance") — translated
after the BR; 5.4: GPT1 and GPT2 have "miśrabhubana", the BR "miśrabhabana" ("Mishra's house") — translated after the BR. Not in PK, KGC, PS, the
Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B.
[^20-11]: Kinnaras — heavenly singers. The syllables "dhā-dhiki…", "thai thai…" imitate the strokes of the mridanga and the dancers' counting (as in the
dance padas, chapters 17–18).

## 6. Narahari — "bhubanamanocorā gokulapati gorā…" (GPT1 pp. 61–62, no. 24; BR)
*The birth festival: the women of Nadia come with trays of gifts, and with them, mingling with the humans, the wives of the gods; Sita-devi and
Malini perform auspicious rites; the cowherd men and women, after their former nature, scatter curd in the courtyard and dance; the gods in
the guise of cowherds dance with them; in Mishra's house is the custom of Nanda's house. Raga vasanta or tori. **Attribution: probably
Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^20-12]

ভুবনমনোচোরা, গোকুলপতি গোরা, চাঁদের জনম কি শুভক্ষণে ।
দেখিয়া পুত্রমুখ, শচীর যত সুখ, তাহা কি কহিবার পারে আনে ॥

*bhubanamanocorā, gokulapati gorā, cām̐dera janama ki śubhakṣaṇe |*
*dekhiyā putramukha, śacīra yata sukha, tāhā ki kahibāra pāre āne ||*

*Word for word:* bhubana-mano-corā — stealer of the world's hearts; gokula-pati gorā-cām̐dera janama — the birth of Gorachand, Lord of Gokula; ki śubha-kṣaṇe — in what an auspicious hour; dekhiyā putra-mukha — seeing her son's face; śacīra yata sukha — all the happiness of Shachi; tāhā ki kahibāra pāre āne — can anyone else tell it

**6.1.** The Stealer of the world's hearts, the Lord of Gokula, Gorachand — in what an auspicious hour was He born!
How much happiness Shachi had when she saw her son's face — who else could tell it?

নদীয়াপুরনারী, আইসে সারি সারি, লইয়া থারি ভরি দ্রব্য বহু ।
সুসজ্জে সুরপ্রিয়া, মানুষে মিশাইয়া, বালকে নিরখিয়া থির নহু ॥

*nadīyāpuranārī, āise sāri sāri, laiyā thāri bhari drabya bahu |*
*susajje surapriyā, mānuṣe miśāiyā, bālake nirakhiyā thira nahu ||*

*Word for word:* nadīyā-pura-nārī — the women of the town of Nadia; āise sāri sāri — come in rows; laiyā thāri bhari drabya bahu — bringing trays full of many gifts; susajje sura-priyā — the richly adorned wives of the gods; mānuṣe miśāiyā — mingling with the humans; bālake nirakhiyā thira nahu — gazing at the Child are not steady

**6.2.** The women of the town of Nadia come in rows, bringing trays full of all kinds of gifts;
and, richly adorned, the wives of the gods, mingling with the humans, cannot gaze at the Child enough.

শ্রীসীতাদেবী আসি, সূতিকাগৃহে পশি, দেখিয়া শিশু উলসিত হিয়া ।
মালিনী আদি সঙ্গে, ভাসায়ে নানা রঙ্গে, করয় কত না মঙ্গলক্রিয়া ॥

*śrīsītādebī āsi, sūtikāgṛhe paśi, dekhiyā śiśu ulasita hiyā |*
*mālinī ādi saṅge, bhāsāye nānā raṅge, karaya kata nā maṅgalakriyā ||*

*Word for word:* śrī-sītā-debī āsi — Sri Sita-devi coming; sūtikā-gṛhe paśi — entering the birth-chamber; dekhiyā śiśu ulasita hiyā — her heart rejoices seeing the Child; mālinī ādi saṅge — with Malini and others; bhāsāye nānā raṅge — floating in merriment of many kinds; karaya kata nā maṅgala-kriyā — performs many auspicious rites

**6.3.** Sri Sita-devi came and, entering the birth-chamber, rejoices at heart seeing the Child;
together with Malini and others, floating in merriment, she performs many auspicious rites.[^20-13]

গোয়ালিনী বা কত, গোয়ালা শত শত, লইয়া দধি আসে চারু সাজে ।
সবে বিহ্বল-চিতে, পূর্ব্ব স্বভাবেতে, ছড়ায় দধি আঙ্গিনার মাঝে ॥

*goyālinī bā kata, goyālā śata śata, laiyā dadhi āse cāru sāje |*
*sabe bihvala-cite, pūrvva svabhābete, chaṛāya dadhi āṅgināra mājhe ||*

*Word for word:* goyālinī vā kata — how many cowherd women; goyālā śata śata — hundreds of cowherd men; laiyā dadhi āse cāru sāje — come in lovely attire bringing curd; sabe bihvala-cite — all with overwhelmed hearts; pūrva svabhābete — after their former nature; chaṛāya dadhi āṅgināra mājhe — scatter curd in the middle of the courtyard

**6.4.** How many cowherd women, hundreds of cowherd men come in lovely attire, bringing curd;
all, their hearts overwhelmed, after their former nature scatter curd in the middle of the courtyard.

রচিয়া করতালি, হাসিয়া নাচে ভালি, তা দেখি দেবে গোপবেশধারী ।
নাচয়ে আঙ্গিনাতে, কে বা না নাচে তাতে, সঘনে জয় জয়ধ্বনি করি ॥

*raciyā karatāli, hāsiyā nāce bhāli, tā dekhi debe gopabeśadhārī |*
*nācaye āṅgināte, ke bā nā nāce tāte, saghane jaya jayadhvani kari ||*

*Word for word:* raciyā karatāli — clapping their hands; hāsiyā nāce bhāli — laughing they dance splendidly; tā dekhi — seeing that; debe gopa-beśa-dhārī — the gods in the guise of cowherds; nācaye āṅgināte — dance in the courtyard; ke vā nā nāce tāte — who does not dance there; saghane jaya jaya-dhvani kari — repeatedly crying "jaya, jaya"

**6.5.** Clapping their hands, laughing, they dance splendidly; seeing this, the gods, taking the guise of cowherds,
dance in the courtyard — who does not dance there? — again and again crying "jaya, jaya".[^20-14]

বাজয়ে বাদ্য হেন, কৌতুক নাহি যেন, মিশ্রালয়ে সে নন্দালয়ের রীতি ।
নরহরি কি কব, প্রভু জন্মোৎসব, উৎসাহে কারু কিছু নাহি স্মৃতি ॥

*bājaye bādya hena, kautuka nāhi yena, miśrālaye se nandālayera rīti |*
*narahari ki kaba, prabhu janmotsaba, utsāhe kāru kichu nāhi smṛti ||*

*Word for word:* bājaye bādya hena — so the instruments sound; kautuka nāhi yena — there is no such festivity [elsewhere]; miśrālaye se nandālayera rīti — in Mishra's house the custom of Nanda's house; narahari ki kaba — what shall Narahari say; prabhu janmotsaba — the Lord's birth festival; utsāhe kāru kichu nāhi smṛti — in the jubilation no one remembers anything

**6.6.** So the instruments sound, such festivity is nowhere else: in Mishra's house is the custom of Nanda's house.
What can Narahari say? At the festival of the Lord's birth, for jubilation no one remembers anything.

[^20-12]: GPT1 — pp. 61–62, no. 24 (vasanta or tori; scan, PDF pp. 320–321); GPT2 — section 2.1, no. 24 (catalogue: NG-004). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912,
pp. ≈765–766; ed. 1960, vv. 937–942, "punarvvasanta—toṛī"), immediately after a pada of Ghanashyama (GPT 2.1 no. 23). Not in PK, KGC, PS, the
Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. Signature "narahari ki kaba" (6.6).
[^20-13]: Sita Thakurani, Advaita's wife, came to bless the newborn and brought gifts (CC Adi 13); Malini is Srivasa's wife (note 27 of chapter 19).
[^20-14]: As at the festival of Krishna's birth in Nanda's house the cowherds scattered curd, milk and butter and danced (Bhag. 10.5), so here: the
cowherds of Navadvipa act "after their former nature" (pūrvva svabhābete), that is, as the cowherds of Vraja. Cf. CB Adi 3 (the gods in human
guise come to see the Child).

## 7. Narahari — "nimāicām̐dera kathā ati aparūpa go…" (GPT1 p. 75, section 2.2, no. 40; GCC)
*One of the elderly women of Navadvipa about Nimai: where have His pranks gone — now He is grave, the pandits respect Him, the Vaishnavas are
inseparable from Him; Nitai loves Him as Balai loved Krishna; Shachi is the very Queen of Vraja, Nimai and Nitai are the two stars of her eyes.
Yatharaga. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC.*[^20-15]

নিমাইচাঁদের কথা অতি অপরূপ গো এবে এ প্রসন্ন কুলদেবা ।
সে সব চঞ্চল ধারা কোথায় বা গেল গো এমন সুধীর আছে কেবা ॥

*nimāicām̐dera kathā ati aparūpa go ebe e prasanna kuladebā |*
*se saba cañcala dhārā kothāya bā gela go emana sudhīra āche kebā ||*

*Word for word:* nimāi-cām̐dera kathā — the ways of Nimaichand; ati aparūpa go — are most wondrous; ebe e prasanna kula-debā — now He is a gracious family deity; se saba cañcala dhārā — all those restless ways; kothāya vā gela go — where have they gone; emana sudhīra āche kebā — who is as grave

**7.1.** "Wondrous are the ways of Nimaichand: now He is like a gracious deity of our family!
Where have all those pranks gone? Who else is as grave as He?

নদীয়ানিবাসী আর যতেক পণ্ডিত গো কেবা বা সমিহ নাহি করে ।
শ্রীবাস মুরারি আদি যতেক বৈষ্ণব গো কেহ সঙ্গ ছাড়িতে না পারে ॥

*nadīyānibāsī āra yateka paṇḍita go kebā bā samiha nāhi kare |*
*śrībāsa murāri ādi yateka baiṣṇaba go keha saṅga chāṛite nā pāre ||*

*Word for word:* nadīyā-nibāsī āra yateka paṇḍita go — all the pandits dwelling in Nadia; kebā vā samiha nāhi kare — who does not revere [Him]; śrībāsa murāri ādi yateka baiṣṇaba go — Srivasa, Murari and all the Vaishnavas; keha saṅga chāṛite nā pāre — none can leave His company

**7.2.** All the pandits living in Nadia — which of them does not respect Him?
Srivasa, Murari and all the Vaishnavas — none can bear to part from Him.

এ মোর নিতাই প্রাণসম স্নেহ করে গো কৃষ্ণ যেন করিল বলাই ।
বুঝি বা হেথায় তাহা প্রকট হইল গো এমন কোথাও দেখি নাই ॥

*e mora nitāi prāṇasama sneha kare go kṛṣṇa yena karila balāi |*
*bujhi bā hethāya tāhā prakaṭa haila go emana kothāo dekhi nāi ||*

*Word for word:* e mora nitāi — and my Nitai; prāṇa-sama sneha kare go — loves [Him] like life; kṛṣṇa yena karila balāi — as Balai [loved] Krishna; bujhi vā hethāya tāhā prakaṭa haila go — it seems that has appeared here; emana kothāo dekhi nāi — nowhere have I seen the like

**7.3.** And my Nitai loves Him like His own life — as Balai loved Krishna;
it seems that very thing has appeared here again: nowhere have I seen the like.[^20-16]

ধন্য পুণ্যবতী শচী জগতের মাঝে গো বুঝি এই সেই ব্রজেশ্বরী ।
নিমাই নিতাই দুটী নয়নের তারা গো এ প্রেম নিছনি নরহরি ॥

*dhanya puṇyabatī śacī jagatera mājhe go bujhi ei sei brajeśvarī |*
*nimāi nitāi duṭī nayanera tārā go e prema nichani narahari ||*

*Word for word:* dhanya puṇyabatī śacī jagatera mājhe go — blessed in the world is virtuous Shachi; bujhi ei sei brajeśvarī — it seems she is that Queen of Vraja; nimāi nitāi duṭī nayanera tārā go — Nimai and Nitai are the two stars of her eyes; e prema nichani narahari — Narahari offers himself to this love

**7.4.** Blessed in this world is virtuous Shachi — it seems she is that very Queen of Vraja;
Nimai and Nitai are the two stars of her eyes." Narahari offers himself to this love.

[^20-15]: GPT1 — p. 75, section 2.2, no. 40 (yatharaga; scan, PDF p. 334); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 40 (catalogue: NG-021; in the GPT2 recognition the
number was read as "70"). GCC — chapter 6, pada 15 (ed. 1947, printed pp. 65–66). Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. The pada
continues the GCC cycle in which the people of Navadvipa come at dawn to Shachi's house and gaze at Gaura, returned from Gaya (chapter 19,
nos. 4–28): "now" (ebe) is the time after Gaya, when Nityananda is already in Navadvipa and Srivasa and Murari are inseparable from the Lord. In
line 7.3 the GCC has "kṛṣṇe yena karila balāi" ("as Balai [loved] Krishna"); the GPT "kṛṣṇa yena…", with the same sense.
[^20-16]: Nityananda is Balarama, Krishna's elder brother in Vraja; Shachi is Yashoda (CC Adi 13; Adi 5). Shachi loved Nityananda as a son; cf. her
dream in which Nimai and Nitai appear as Krishna and Balarama (CB, Madhya-khanda). "My Nitai" — the affectionate words of an elderly woman.

## 8. Narahari — "nadīyāra yata bṛddhanārīgaṇe…" (GPT1 pp. 75–76, no. 41; GCC)
*The elderly women of Nadia speak thus to one another, gaze at Gauranga's face, count themselves fortunate and bless Him. Yatharaga.
**Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC (the last pada of its 6th chapter).*[^20-17]

নদীয়ার যত বৃদ্ধনারীগণে । এরূপ পরস্পর সবে ভণে ॥

*nadīyāra yata bṛddhanārīgaṇe | erūpa paraspara sabe bhaṇe ||*

*Word for word:* nadīyāra yata bṛddha-nārī-gaṇe — all the elderly women of Nadia; erūpa paraspara sabe bhaṇe — all speak thus to one another

**8.1.** Thus all the elderly women of Nadia speak to one another.

কিবা অপরূপ সবাকার রীতি । কি দিব উপমা অতি স্নেহবতী ॥

*kibā aparūpa sabākāra rīti | ki diba upamā ati snehabatī ||*

*Word for word:* kibā aparūpa sabākāra rīti — how wondrous is the way of them all; ki diba upamā — what comparison can I give; ati snehabatī — [they are] full of tenderness

**8.2.** How wondrous is the way of them all! With what to compare it? They are full of tenderness.

গৌরাঙ্গচাঁদের চাঁদমুখ পানে । চাঞা চাঞা আপনাকে ধন্য মানে ॥

*gaurāṅgacām̐dera cām̐damukha pāne | cāñā cāñā āpanāke dhanya māne ||*

*Word for word:* gaurāṅga-cām̐dera cām̐da-mukha pāne — at the moonlike face of Gaurangachand; cāñā cāñā — gazing and gazing; āpanāke dhanya māne — count themselves fortunate

**8.3.** Again and again gazing at the moonlike face of Gaurangachand, they count themselves fortunate.

কত বা আশীষ করে বারে বারে । নরহরি শুনি সে সুখে সাঁতারে ॥

*kata bā āśīṣa kare bāre bāre | narahari śuni se sukhe sām̐tāre ||*

*Word for word:* kata vā āśīṣa kare bāre bāre — how many blessings they give again and again; narahari śuni — Narahari, hearing; se sukhe sām̐tāre — swims in that happiness

**8.4.** How many times they bless Him, again and again! Narahari, hearing this, swims in happiness.

[^20-17]: GPT1 — pp. 75–76, no. 41 (yatharaga; scan, PDF pp. 334–335); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 41 (catalogue: NG-022). GCC — chapter 6, pada 16
(printed p. 66): with it Chakravarti closes the chapter on the love of the women of Navadvipa in vatsalya. Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the
Gita-chandrodaya. B. The next one in GPT1, no. 42, is an abridged doublet of no. 21 of chapter 19 (NG-023) and is not translated.

## 9. Narahari — "nāco āre bāpa biśvambhara…" (GPT1 p. 76, no. 43; BR)
*The virtuous women, clapping their hands and saying "Hari-bol", coax little Vishvambhara to dance, promising butter and cream; He, looking at
His mother, dances crying "Hari-bol"; the courtyard shines with His golden body. Raga tudi. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is
in the BR.*[^20-18]

নাচো আরে বাপ বিশ্বম্ভর । কর ভরি খাইতে দিব ননী ক্ষীর সর ॥

*nāco āre bāpa biśvambhara | kara bhari khāite diba nanī kṣīra sara ||*

*Word for word:* nāco āre bāpa biśvambhara — dance, dear Vishvambhara; kara bhari khāite diba — we will give handfuls to eat; nanī kṣīra sara — of butter, thickened milk, cream

**9.1.** "Dance, dear Vishvambhara! We will give You handfuls of butter, thickened milk and cream!"

পতিব্রতাগণ চারিপাশে । কহে কত নিমাইচাঁদেরে মৃদুভাষে ॥

*patibratāgaṇa cāripāśe | kahe kata nimāicām̐dere mṛdubhāṣe ||*

*Word for word:* patibratā-gaṇa cāri-pāśe — the chaste wives all around; kahe kata nimāi-cām̐dere mṛdu-bhāṣe — say much to Nimaichand in gentle words

**9.2.** The virtuous wives around say this tenderly to Nimaichand.

হরি হরিবোল বলি বলি । সবে মিলি সঘনে রচয়ে করতালি ॥

*hari haribola bali bali | sabe mili saghane racaye karatāli ||*

*Word for word:* hari haribola bali bali — saying again and again "Hari, Hari-bol"; sabe mili saghane racaye karatāli — all together clap their hands repeatedly

**9.3.** Saying "Hari, Hari-bol", all together clap their hands again and again.

চাহি গোরা জননীর পানে । হরিবোল বলি নাচে বিবিধ বন্ধানে ॥

*cāhi gorā jananīra pāne | haribola bali nāce bibidha bandhāne ||*

*Word for word:* cāhi gorā jananīra pāne — Gora, looking at His mother; haribola bali — saying "Hari-bol"; nāce bibidha bandhāne — dances in various styles

**9.4.** Gora, looking at His mother, dances in various ways crying "Hari-bol".[^20-19]

কিবা চাঁদমুখে মৃদু হাসি । ভুলায় ভুবন ঢালে সুধা রাশি রাশি ॥

*kibā cām̐damukhe mṛdu hāsi | bhulāya bhubana ḍhāle sudhā rāśi rāśi ||*

*Word for word:* kibā cām̐da-mukhe mṛdu hāsi — what a gentle smile on the moonlike face; bhulāya bhubana — enchants the world; ḍhāle sudhā rāśi rāśi — pours out nectar in heaps

**9.5.** What a gentle smile on the moonlike face! It enchants the world, pouring out nectar in streams.

নয়ন চাহনি চারু ছাঁদে । ভুজের ভঙ্গিমা দেখি কেবা স্থির বাঁধে ॥

*nayana cāhani cāru chām̐de | bhujera bhaṅgimā dekhi kebā sthira bām̐dhe ||*

*Word for word:* nayana cāhani cāru chām̐de — the glance of the eyes is lovely; bhujera bhaṅgimā dekhi — seeing the curves of the arms; kebā sthira bām̐dhe — who keeps steady

**9.6.** Lovely is the glance of His eyes; seeing the curves of His arms, who can stay calm?

কি মধুর মধুর কিরণে । ঝলকে অঙ্গন হেম-অঙ্গের কিরণে ॥

*ki madhura madhura kiraṇe | jhalake aṅgana hema-aṅgera kiraṇe ||*

*Word for word:* ki madhura madhura kiraṇe — what sweet, sweet radiance; jhalake aṅgana — the courtyard gleams; hema-aṅgera kiraṇe — with the rays of the golden body

**9.7.** What a sweet, sweet radiance! The courtyard gleams with the rays of His golden body.

কিঙ্কিণী নূপুর বাজে ভালে । নরহরি নিছনি চরণতল-তালে ॥

*kiṅkiṇī nūpura bāje bhāle | narahari nichani caraṇatala-tāle ||*

*Word for word:* kiṅkiṇī nūpura bāje bhāle — the waist-bells and anklets jingle sweetly; narahari nichani — Narahari offers himself; caraṇa-tala-tāle — to the rhythm of the soles of His feet

**9.8.** Sweetly the belt of bells and the anklets jingle; Narahari offers himself to the rhythm of His feet.

[^20-18]: GPT1 — p. 76, no. 43 (tudi; scan, PDF p. 335); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 43 (catalogue: NG-024). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 772; ed. 1960,
vv. 1005–1012): "here is Nimai's wondrous dance: the women, clapping their hands, make Him dance" (v. 1004). In GPT1 the first word is "nāce"
(a misprint?), in the BR "nāco" ("dance!"); translated after the BR. In 9.7 GPT1 has "hena aṅgera", the BR "hema-aṅgera" ("golden body") — after the
BR. Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B.
[^20-19]: Cf. CB Adi 4: when the Child cried, the women clapped their hands and sang "Hari", and He, quieted, danced — thus from infancy the Lord made
everyone sing the holy name (cf. no. 21 of chapter 19).

## 10. Narahari — "āre mora soṇāra nimāi…" (GPT1 pp. 76–77, no. 44; BR)
*Shachi begs Nimai to play at home and not to roam about other people's courtyards: let the children come to Him, she will give Him
whatever He wants; when He goes off with a band of rascals, her heart is not at rest. Raga dhanashi. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** —
the pada is in the BR.*[^20-20]

আরে মোর সোণার নিমাই ।
আপনার ঘর ছাড়ি, না যাবে পরের বাড়ী, বসিয়া খেলাবে এই ঠাঁই ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*āre mora soṇāra nimāi |*
*āpanāra ghara chāṛi, nā yābe parera bāṛī, basiyā khelābe ei ṭhām̐i || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* āre mora soṇāra nimāi — ah, my golden Nimai; āpanāra ghara chāṛi — leaving Your own house; nā yābe parera bāṛī — do not go to others' houses; basiyā khelābe ei ṭhām̐i — sit and play in this place

**10.1.** "Ah, my golden Nimai!
Do not leave Your own house for other people's courtyards — sit and play here.

শিশুগণ খেলাইতে, আসিবে তোমার সাতে, এথাই রাখিবে তা সবারে ।
যখন যে চাও তুমি, তাহা আনি দিব আমি, কিসের অভাব মোর ঘরে ॥

*śiśugaṇa khelāite, āsibe tomāra sāte, ethāi rākhibe tā sabāre |*
*yakhana ye cāo tumi, tāhā āni diba āmi, kisera abhāba mora ghare ||*

*Word for word:* śiśugaṇa khelāite — the children, to play; āsibe tomāra sāte — will come to You; ethāi rākhibe tā sabāre — keep them all here; yakhana ye cāo tumi — whatever You want; tāhā āni diba āmi — I will bring it; kisera abhāba mora ghare — what is lacking in my house

**10.2.** The children will come to play with You — keep them all right here.
Whatever You want, I will bring You: what is lacking in my house?

যদি কেহ কিছু কয়, তারে দেখাইও ভয়, বাপের নিষেধ জানাইয়া ।
চঞ্চল-বালকমেলে, বাড়ীর বাহির গেলে, মায়ে কি ধরিতে পারে হিয়া ॥

*yadi keha kichu kaya, tāre dekhāio bhaya, bāpera niṣedha jānāiyā |*
*cañcala-bālakamele, bāṛīra bāhira gele, māye ki dharite pāre hiyā ||*

*Word for word:* yadi keha kichu kaya — if anyone says anything [calls You]; tāre dekhāio bhaya — show him that You are afraid; bāpera niṣedha jānāiyā — telling of Your father's prohibition; cañcala-bālaka-mele — with a band of restless boys; bāṛīra bāhira gele — when You go out of the house; māye ki dharite pāre hiyā — can a mother hold her heart

**10.3.** If anyone calls You — say You are afraid: Your father forbids it.
When You go out of the house with a band of rascals — can a mother keep hold of her heart?

তিলেক আঁখের আড়ে, পরাণ না রহে ধড়ে, নরহরি জানে মোর দুখ ।
মায়ের বচন ধর, ঘরে বসি খেলা কর, সদা যেন দেখি চাঁদমুখ ॥

*tileka ām̐khera āṛe, parāṇa nā rahe dhaṛe, narahari jāne mora dukha |*
*māyera bacana dhara, ghare basi khelā kara, sadā yena dekhi cām̐damukha ||*

*Word for word:* tileka ām̐khera āṛe — out of sight for a moment; parāṇa nā rahe dhaṛe — life does not stay in the body; narahari jāne mora dukha — Narahari knows my grief; māyera bacana dhara — heed Your mother's word; ghare basi khelā kara — play sitting at home; sadā yena dekhi cām̐da-mukha — that I may always see the moonlike face

**10.4.** If You are out of my sight for a moment, my life will not stay in my body; Narahari knows my pain.
Heed Your mother, play at home — so that I may always see Your moonlike face."[^20-21]

[^20-20]: GPT1 — pp. 76–77, no. 44 (dhanashi; scan, PDF pp. 335–336); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 44 (catalogue: NG-025). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 772;
ed. 1960, vv. 1014–1017): "here the mother, beside herself with tenderness, spoke to Nimai, looking at His face" (v. 1013). Not in PK, KGC, PS, the
Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. Line 10.1 is the refrain (dhru) with the first line of the stanza.
[^20-21]: The mother's fear for the Child is vatsalya, the pure love of the Lord's eternal mother (note 2 of chapter 19), like Yashoda's anxiety for
Krishna.

## 11. Narahari — "raṅge nācaye śacīra bālā…" (GPT1 p. 77, no. 45; BR)
*Shachi's child dances merrily in the courtyard, grey with dust, clapping His hands and saying "Hari"; His mother gives Him cream; He whirls
round, the hem of His dhoti trails on the ground, the bells and anklets jingle. Raga kamoda. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada
is in the BR.*[^20-22]

রঙ্গে নাচয়ে শচীর বালা । রূপে করয়ে ভুবন আলা ॥

*raṅge nācaye śacīra bālā | rūpe karaye bhubana ālā ||*

*Word for word:* raṅge nācaye śacīra bālā — Shachi's child dances merrily; rūpe karaye bhubana ālā — lights up the world with His beauty

**11.1.** Merrily dances Shachi's child, lighting up the world with His beauty.

জিনি হেম-সরসিজ তনু । ধূলি ধূসর পরাগ জনু ॥

*jini hema-sarasija tanu | dhūli dhūsara parāga janu ||*

*Word for word:* jini hema-sarasija tanu — a body surpassing the golden lotus; dhūli dhūsara — grey with dust; parāga janu — as if with pollen

**11.2.** His body surpasses a golden lotus; grey with dust — as if with flower pollen.

বেশ ভূষণ শোভয়ে ভাল । হরি বলি দেই করতাল ॥

*beśa bhūṣaṇa śobhaye bhāla | hari bali dei karatāla ||*

*Word for word:* beśa bhūṣaṇa śobhaye bhāla — dress and ornaments shine beautifully; hari bali dei karatāla — saying "Hari", He claps His hands

**11.3.** Lovely shine His dress and ornaments; saying "Hari", He claps His hands.

মৃদু হাসয়ে মধুর ছাঁদে । তাহে কেবা ধৈরজ বাঁধে ॥

*mṛdu hāsaye madhura chām̐de | tāhe kebā dhairaja bām̐dhe ||*

*Word for word:* mṛdu hāsaye madhura chām̐de — smiles gently in a sweet manner; tāhe kebā dhairaja bām̐dhe — who then keeps composure

**11.4.** He smiles gently, sweetly and gracefully — who can keep his composure then?

চারিদিকে কি কৌতুকে চায় । কর ভরি সর দেয়ত মায় ॥

*cāridike ki kautuke cāya | kara bhari sara deyata māya ||*

*Word for word:* cāri-dike ki kautuke cāya — how merrily He looks around; kara bhari sara deyata māya — His mother gives handfuls of cream

**11.5.** How merrily He looks around on all sides! His mother gives Him handfuls of cream.

ভঙ্গী করি ঘন ঘন ঘুমে । ধটী অঞ্চল লোটায় ভূমে ॥

*bhaṅgī kari ghana ghana ghume | dhaṭī añcala loṭāya bhūme ||*

*Word for word:* bhaṅgī kari — striking poses; ghana ghana ghume — whirls again and again; dhaṭī añcala loṭāya bhūme — the hem of the dhoti trails on the ground

**11.6.** Striking poses, He whirls round again and again; the hem of His dhoti trails on the ground.

কটি কিঙ্কিণী সুচারু ছটা । তায় ঝিনি-নি শবদ ছটা ॥

*kaṭi kiṅkiṇī sucāru chaṭā | tāya jhini-ni śabada chaṭā ||*

*Word for word:* kaṭi kiṅkiṇī sucāru chaṭā — the waist-bells flash lovely; tāya jhini-ni śabada chaṭā — from them a ringing "jhini-ni"

**11.7.** Lovely flashes the belt of bells; from it a ringing "jhini-ni".

বাজে ঝুনুনু নূপুর পায় । নরহরি সে নিছনি তায় ॥

*bāje jhununu nūpura pāya | narahari se nichani tāya ||*

*Word for word:* bāje jhununu nūpura pāya — the anklets jingle "jhunu-nu" on His feet; narahari se nichani tāya — Narahari offers himself to them

**11.8.** On His feet the anklets jingle "jhunu-nu"; Narahari offers himself to them.

[^20-22]: GPT1 — p. 77, no. 45 (kamoda; scan, PDF p. 336); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 45 (catalogue: NG-026). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 775; ed. 1960,
vv. 1049–1056), immediately after Vasu Ghosha's padas on Nimai's dance in the courtyard (PK 1151, 1161 — chapter 7). Not in PK (under Narahari's
signature), KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. "Whirls" (ghume) — Vrajabuli, cf. Hindi "ghūmnā".

## 12. Narahari — "āji āṅginā para nadīyā bālaka saṅge…" (GPT1 p. 77, no. 46)
*Shachi's child plays in the courtyard with the boys of Nadia — like the moon among the stars; Shachi, beside herself with joy, kisses Him,
wipes His sweat and fans Him; beside them stands the poet with a chamara. Raga mangala. **Attribution: not established** — the pada is in
neither the BR nor the GCC nor any other witness; Vrajabuli; in the signature the poet himself serves in the lila (note 24).*[^20-23]

আজি আঙ্গিনা পর, নদীয়া বালক সঙ্গে, রঙ্গে খেলত শচী বালা ।
নখত-নিকর মাঝে, এক শশী রাজে, করত দিক উজলা ॥

*āji āṅginā para, nadīyā bālaka saṅge, raṅge khelata śacī bālā |*
*nakhata-nikara mājhe, eka śaśī rāje, karata dika ujalā ||*

*Word for word:* āji āṅginā para — today in the courtyard; nadīyā bālaka saṅge — with the boys of Nadia; raṅge khelata śacī bālā — Shachi's child plays merrily; nakhata-nikara mājhe — amid a host of stars; eka śaśī rāje — a single moon shines; karata dika ujalā — lighting up the directions

**12.1.** Today in the courtyard, with the boys of Nadia, Shachi's child plays merrily —
as if amid a host of stars a single moon shines, lighting up all directions.

বিবিধ খেলনা, লেই সকল মিলি, খেলত বিবিধ খেলা ।
সবহু বদনে, হাস বিকশিত, জনু এক সঙ্গে বহু পদমক মেলা ॥

*bibidha khelanā, lei sakala mili, khelata bibidha khelā |*
*sabahu badane, hāsa bikaśita, janu eka saṅge bahu padamaka melā ||*

*Word for word:* bibidha khelanā lei — taking various toys; sakala mili — all together; khelata bibidha khelā — play various games; sabahu badane hāsa bikaśita — smiles blossom on every face; janu eka saṅge bahu padamaka melā — as if many lotuses opened at once

**12.2.** Taking various toys, all together they play various games;
smiles blossom on every face — as if a multitude of lotuses had opened at once.

সো খেলা দরশনে, গর গর অন্তর, আনন্দে শচী উতরোল ।
দণ্ডে শতবেরি, চুমে বদনচাঁদ, বিশ্বম্ভরে করি কোল ॥

*so khelā daraśane, gara gara antara, ānande śacī utarola |*
*daṇḍe śataberi, cume badanacām̐da, biśvambhare kari kola ||*

*Word for word:* so khelā daraśane — seeing that play; gara gara antara — with overflowing heart; ānande śacī utarola — Shachi is beside herself with joy; daṇḍe śata-beri — a hundred times in a moment; cume badana-cām̐da — kisses the moonlike face; biśvambhare kari kola — taking Vishvambhara in her arms

**12.3.** Watching this play, Shachi, her heart overflowing, is beside herself with joy;
a hundred times in a moment, taking Vishvambhara in her arms, she kisses His moonlike face.

বসন-অঞ্চলে শ্রমজল মুছি, শ্রীঅঙ্গে করত বাতাস ।
করে চামর লেই, পাশে ঠারি রহ, পামর নরহরি দাস ॥

*basana-añcale śramajala muchi, śrīaṅge karata bātāsa |*
*kare cāmara lei, pāśe ṭhāri raha, pāmara narahari dāsa ||*

*Word for word:* basana-añcale — with the hem of her garment; śrama-jala muchi — wiping the sweat; śrī-aṅge karata bātāsa — fans the holy body; kare cāmara lei — taking a chamara in hand; pāśe ṭhāri raha — stands by the side; pāmara narahari dāsa — the wretched Narahari Dasa

**12.4.** With the hem of her garment she wipes away His sweat and fans His holy body;
and beside them, chamara in hand, stands the wretched Narahari Dasa.[^20-24]

[^20-23]: GPT1 — p. 77, no. 46 (mangala; scan, PDF p. 336); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 46 (catalogue: NG-275). Not in the BR, GCC, PK, KGC, PS or the
Gita-chandrodaya. C. The following padas of the section in GPT1 — nos. 47–48 signed "Murari" (Majumdar considers them doubtful), no. 49 without
Narahari's signature, no. 50 by Lochana Dasa — are not part of the appendix.
[^20-24]: The poet places himself in the lila as a servant fanning the Lord with a chamara (a yak-tail whisk) — an image of inner service (manasi-seva)
in meditation on the lila, usual for later Vaishnava poets; it is not a claim to have witnessed the Lord's childhood.

## 13. Narahari — "āju ki ānandamaya…" (GPT1 p. 79, section 2.3, no. 1; BR)
*Nimai's chudakarana (first tonsure): Shachi's house is full of people; Mishra, having adorned his son, performs the rites according to the
Vedas and custom; the barber, having done his work, ties a yellow thread at the ears; the women rejoice, the brahmanas recite the Vedas, the
bards compose praises. Raga dhanashi. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^20-25]

আজু কি আনন্দময়, লোকগতি অতিশয়, শোভাময় শচীর ভবনে ।
সবার পরাণ জুড়া, নিমাইচাঁদের চূড়া, কর্ম্ম কি অপূর্ব্ব শুভক্ষণে ॥

*āju ki ānandamaya, lokagati atiśaya, śobhāmaya śacīra bhabane |*
*sabāra parāṇa juṛā, nimāicām̐dera cūṛā, karmma ki apūrvva śubhakṣaṇe ||*

*Word for word:* āju ki ānanda-maya — how joyful today; loka-gati atiśaya — people throng; śobhāmaya śacīra bhabane — to Shachi's shining house; sabāra parāṇa juṛā — delighting everyone's heart; nimāi-cām̐dera cūṛā-karma — Nimaichand's tonsure rite; ki apūrva śubha-kṣaṇe — in what a wondrous auspicious hour

**13.1.** How joyful today! People throng to the shining house of Shachi:
a delight for all — in what a wondrous, auspicious hour Nimaichand's chudakarana is performed!

দিব্য বস্ত্র অলঙ্কারে, সাজাইয়া বিশ্বম্ভরে, বসাইয়া দিব্যাসনপরি ।
যে বেদবিহিত আর, লোকরীতি যে প্রকার, তাহা মিশ্র করে যত্ন করি ॥

*dibya bastra alaṅkāre, sājāiyā biśvambhare, basāiyā dibyāsanapari |*
*ye bedabihita āra, lokarīti ye prakāra, tāhā miśra kare yatna kari ||*

*Word for word:* dibya bastra alaṅkāre — in divine clothes and ornaments; sājāiyā biśvambhare — adorning Vishvambhara; basāiyā dibyāsana-pari — seating Him on a divine seat; ye beda-bihita āra — what the Vedas enjoin and; loka-rīti ye prakāra — whatever custom requires; tāhā miśra kare yatna kari — Mishra carefully performs it

**13.2.** Having dressed Vishvambhara in divine clothes and ornaments and seated Him on a divine seat,
Mishra carefully performs all that the Vedas enjoin and custom requires.[^20-26]

আসিয়া নাপিত আর্য্য, সাধিয়া সে নিজ কার্য্য, কর্ণমূলে পীত সূত্র দিতে ।
নারীগণ যজকারে, কে না জয়ধ্বনি করে, ব্যাপিল মঙ্গল পৃথিবীতে ॥

*āsiyā nāpita āryya, sādhiyā se nija kāryya, karṇamūle pīta sūtra dite |*
*nārīgaṇa yajakāre, ke nā jayadhvani kare, byāpila maṅgala pṛthibīte ||*

*Word for word:* āsiyā nāpita ārya — the worthy barber coming; sādhiyā se nija kārya — doing his work; karṇa-mūle pīta sūtra dite — tying a yellow thread at the root of the ears; nārī-gaṇa yajakāre — the women with jubilant cries; ke nā jaya-dhvani kare — who does not cry "jaya"; byāpila maṅgala pṛthibīte — auspiciousness spread over the earth

**13.3.** The worthy barber came and, having done his work, tied a yellow thread at the root of the ears;
the women raise jubilant cries — who does not cry "jaya"? Auspiciousness spread over the earth.[^20-27]

বিপ্রে করে বেদপাঠ, বর্ণয়ে কবিত্ব ভাট, বাদক বিবিধ বাদ্য বায় ।
নাচয়ে নর্ত্তক যত, নরহরি কবে কত, গায়কে নির্ম্মল যশ গায় ॥

*bipre kare bedapāṭha, barṇaye kabitva bhāṭa, bādaka bibidha bādya bāya |*
*nācaye narttaka yata, narahari kabe kata, gāyake nirmmala yaśa gāya ||*

*Word for word:* bipre kare beda-pāṭha — the brahmanas recite the Vedas; barṇaye kabitva bhāṭa — the bards compose verses; bādaka bibidha bādya bāya — the musicians play various instruments; nācaye nartaka yata — all the dancers dance; narahari kabe kata — how much will Narahari tell; gāyake nirmala yaśa gāya — the singers sing the pure glory

**13.4.** The brahmanas recite the Vedas, the bards compose verses of praise, the musicians play various instruments;
all the dancers dance, the singers sing His pure glory — how much can Narahari tell?

[^20-25]: GPT1 — p. 79, section 2.3 ("Karnavedha and the wedding"), no. 1 (dhanashi; scan, PDF p. 338); GPT2 — section 2.3, no. 1. The catalogue did not
know it (new row NG-280). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 781; ed. 1960, vv. 1156–1159): "here Mishra Purandara said to Shachi: Vishvambhara has
reached the age for the chudakarana — and both, as the Vedas enjoin, performed the chudakarana of their son" (vv. 1154–1155). Line 13.1: GPT1 has
"nimāicām̐dera cūṛā, karmma ki apūrvva śubhakṣaṇe", the BR "cūṛā-karmmādi apūrvva śubhakṣaṇe" — in sense the same: chuda-karma. Not in PK, KGC, PS, the
Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B.
[^20-26]: The samskaras are the purificatory rites of a brahmana's life (chudakarana, karnavedha, upanayana and others). The Lord, Himself the goal of
the Vedas, needs no purification: He accepts the samskaras following His lila in the form of a brahmana's son and setting an example for people.
So Chakravarti too understands it: right after this pada the BR says that the Lord, full of consciousness and bliss, performs His lila like a human
being — and the barber, before piercing His ears, saw that the holes were already there, but by the Lord's will told no one (vv. 1160–1161).
[^20-27]: The yellow thread at the root of the ears is the mark for the ear-piercing (karnavedha), which was performed together with the chudakarana;
hence the title of the GPT section "Karnavedha and the wedding". The women's jubilant cries (jayakāra, ulu) are an auspicious custom at Bengali
family festivals.

## 14. Narahari — "āju nirupama gauracandra-cūṛā…" (GPT1 p. 79, no. 2; BR)
*The same chudakarana: the wives of Navadvipa cry "ulu-lu" in jubilation, the brahmanas chant the Vedas, the sutas, magadhas and bandins
compose tales, the musicians and dancers beat the rhythm; Mishra gives gifts to the supplicants, the gods in the sky cry "jaya". Raga
belavali. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR; ornate Vrajabuli with rhythmic syllables.*[^20-28]

আজু নিরুপম গৌরচন্দ্র-চূড়া, বেদবিহিত মঙ্গল লোক ভীড় ভবনে ।
শ্রীনবদ্বীপ-বধূবৃন্দ, রীতি অতুল উলু লু লু লু লু লু দেত কি উলাস শ্রবণে ॥

*āju nirupama gauracandra-cūṛā, bedabihita maṅgala loka bhīṛa bhabane |*
*śrīnabadvīpa-badhūbṛnda, rīti atula ulu lu lu lu lu lu deta ki ulāsa śrabaṇe ||*

*Word for word:* āju nirupama gauracandra-cūṛā — today the incomparable tonsure of Gaurachandra; beda-bihita — as the Vedas enjoin; maṅgala — auspicious celebration; loka bhīṛa bhabane — the house is crowded with people; śrī-nabadvīpa-badhū-bṛnda — the wives of Sri Navadvipa; rīti atula — by an incomparable custom; ulu lu lu… deta — cry "ulu-lu-lu"; ki ulāsa śrabaṇe — what joy for the ear

**14.1.** Today is the incomparable chudakarana of Gaurachandra as the Vedas enjoin: an auspicious celebration, the house is full of people;
the wives of Sri Navadvipa, by an incomparable custom, cry "ulu-lu-lu-lu-lu-lu" — what a joy for the ear!

ভূসুর-সমাজ ভ্রাজত ভূরি ভঙ্গি বেদধ্বনি সুমধুর হৃদ মোদ ভরঈ ।
সূত মাগধ বন্দী রচয়ে নব চরিতচয়, শ্রবণপথ-গত জগত-চিত্ত হরঈ ॥

*bhūsura-samāja bhrājata bhūri bhaṅgi bedadhvani sumadhura hṛda moda bharaī |*
*sūta māgadha bandī racaye naba caritacaya, śrabaṇapatha-gata jagata-citta haraī ||*

*Word for word:* bhūsura-samāja bhrājata — the assembly of brahmanas shines; bhūri bhaṅgi beda-dhvani — the Vedas resound in many modes; sumadhura hṛda moda bharaï — sweetly filling hearts with delight; sūta māgadha bandī — the sutas, magadhas, bandins; racaye naba carita-caya — compose new tales of His deeds; śrabaṇa-patha-gata — reaching the ear; jagata-citta haraï — they steal the heart of the world

**14.2.** The assembly of brahmanas shines; in many modes the Vedas resound, sweetly filling hearts with delight;
the sutas, magadhas and bandins compose new tales of His deeds — reaching the ear, they steal the heart of the world.[^20-29]

বাদক মৃদঙ্গাদি-বাদ্য প্রভেদ ভণি ধাধা ধিলঙ্গ ধিকিতক ধিন্নিনা ।
গায়ত সুছন্দ গুণিগণ নটত নট্ট উঘটত তত্তথৈ থৈ তি অই তিন্নিনা ॥

*bādaka mṛdaṅgādi-bādya prabheda bhaṇi dhādhā dhilaṅga dhikitaka dhinninā |*
*gāyata suchanda guṇigaṇa naṭata naṭṭa ughaṭata tattathai thai ti ai tinninā ||*

*Word for word:* bādaka mṛdaṅgādi-bādya prabheda bhaṇi — the musicians on mridangas etc. play in many modes; dhā-dhā… — mridanga syllables; gāyata suchanda guṇi-gaṇa — skilled singers sing in fine metres; naṭata naṭṭa — the dancers dance; ughaṭata tattathai… — beating out the dance count

**14.3.** The musicians on mridangas and other instruments play in many modes: "dhā-dhā dhilaṅga dhikitaka dhinninā";
skilled singers sing in well-measured metres, the dancers dance beating out: "tattathai thai ti ai tinninā".

পুলক-কুল-বলিত উৎসাহময় মিশ্রবর বিতরি বহু দ্রব্য যাচক সকলে তোষঈ ।
নরহরি কি ভণব শোভা ভূরি নিরখি সুরগণ মগন গগনে জয় জয় সঘনে ঘোষঈ ॥

*pulaka-kula-balita utsāhamaya miśrabara bitari bahu drabya yācaka sakale toṣaī |*
*narahari ki bhaṇaba śobhā bhūri nirakhi suragaṇa magana gagane jaya jaya saghane ghoṣaī ||*

*Word for word:* pulaka-kula-balita — covered with thrills; utsāha-maya miśra-bara — the jubilant Mishra; bitari bahu drabya — distributing many gifts; yācaka sakale toṣaï — satisfies all the supplicants; narahari ki bhaṇaba — what shall Narahari say; śobhā bhūri nirakhi — beholding the great splendour; sura-gaṇa magana — the gods are immersed; gagane jaya jaya saghane ghoṣaï — loudly cry "jaya, jaya" in the sky

**14.4.** Thrilling all over, the jubilant Mishra, distributing many gifts, satisfies all the supplicants.
What can Narahari say? The gods, gazing at this great splendour, beside themselves, loudly cry "jaya, jaya" in the sky.

[^20-28]: GPT1 — p. 79, no. 2 (belavali; scan, PDF p. 338); GPT2 — section 2.3, no. 2 (catalogue: NG-027). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 782; ed. 1960,
vv. 1163–1166), immediately after the account of the pierced ears (note 26). Variants: 14.1 GPT1 "de’", BR "deta"; 14.2 GPT1 "śrabaṇa pakṣagata", BR
"śrabaṇapatha-gata" ("reaching the ear") — translated after the BR; 14.3 GPT1 "prabheda bhabi", BR "prabheda bhaṇi". Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the
Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. In the GPT1 signature the first letter of the name is cut off by the edge of the page ("…rahari").
[^20-29]: Sutas, magadhas and bandins — court bards, singers of genealogies and panegyrists.

## 15. Narahari — "ki ānanda nadīyānagare…" (GPT1 pp. 79–80, no. 3; BR)
*The upanayana: all over Nadia the news that Shachi's son will receive the sacred thread; everyone hastens with gifts; Mishra gives his son the
thread; Gaura in red cloth, with staff and bag, begs alms, and the heavenly women, mingling with the humans, and His associates give Him alms.
Raga kamoda. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^20-30]

কি আনন্দ নদীয়ানগরে ।
শ্রীশচীদেবীর পুত্র, ধরিবেন যজ্ঞসূত্র, এই কথা প্রতি ঘরে ঘরে ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*ki ānanda nadīyānagare |*
*śrīśacīdebīra putra, dharibena yajñasūtra, ei kathā prati ghare ghare || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* ki ānanda nadīyā-nagare — what joy in the town of Nadia; śrī-śacī-debīra putra — the son of Sri Shachi-devi; dharibena yajña-sūtra — will receive the sacred thread; ei kathā prati ghare ghare — this news in every house

**15.1.** What joy in the town of Nadia!
"The son of Sri Shachi-devi will receive the sacred thread!" — this news is in every house.

স্নেহেতে বিহ্বল হৈঞা, কেবা না চলয়ে ধাঞা, নানাদ্রব্য লঞা মিশ্রালয়ে ।
নিরুপম মিশ্রালয়, লোকভীড় অতিশয়, সে শোভায় কেবা না ভুলয়ে ॥

*snehete bihvala haiñā, kebā nā calaye dhāñā, nānādrabya lañā miśrālaye |*
*nirupama miśrālaya, lokabhīṛa atiśaya, se śobhāya kebā nā bhulaye ||*

*Word for word:* snehete bihvala haiñā — overwhelmed with tenderness; kebā nā calaye dhāñā — who does not hasten; nānā-drabya lañā miśrālaye — with various gifts to Mishra's house; nirupama miśrālaya — Mishra's incomparable house; loka-bhīṛa atiśaya — is very crowded; se śobhāya kebā nā bhulaye — whom does that splendour not enchant

**15.2.** Who, beside himself with tenderness, does not hasten to Mishra's house with various gifts?
Mishra's incomparable house is full of people — whom will this splendour not enchant?

মিশ্র মহা হর্ষ হঞা, করে বেদমত ক্রিয়া, যজ্ঞসূত্র দেই গোরাচাঁদে ।
গৌরমূর্ত্তি মনোহর, পরিধান রক্তাম্বর, হাতে দিব্য দণ্ড ঝুলি কাঁধে ॥

*miśra mahā harṣa hañā, kare bedamata kriyā, yajñasūtra dei gorācām̐de |*
*gauramūrtti manohara, paridhāna raktāmbara, hāte dibya daṇḍa jhuli kām̐dhe ||*

*Word for word:* miśra mahā harṣa hañā — Mishra in great joy; kare beda-mata kriyā — performs the rites by the Vedas; yajña-sūtra dei gorācām̐de — gives Gorachand the sacred thread; gaura-mūrti manohara — the golden form is lovely; paridhāna raktāmbara — wearing a red cloth; hāte dibya daṇḍa — a divine staff in hand; jhuli kām̐dhe — a bag on the shoulder

**15.3.** Mishra, in great joy, performs the rites according to the Vedas and gives Gorachand the sacred thread;
lovely is the golden form: He wears a red cloth, in His hand a divine staff, on His shoulder a bag.[^20-31]

প্রভু ভিক্ষা করে রঙ্গে, দেখি দেবনারী সঙ্গে, মানুষে মিশায় ভিক্ষা দিতে ।
প্রভুপ্রিয়গণ যারা, কত না কৌতুকে তারা, ভিক্ষা দেই প্রভুর ঝুলিতে ॥

*prabhu bhikṣā kare raṅge, dekhi debanārī saṅge, mānuṣe miśāya bhikṣā dite |*
*prabhupriyagaṇa yārā, kata nā kautuke tārā, bhikṣā dei prabhura jhulite ||*

*Word for word:* prabhu bhikṣā kare raṅge — the Lord merrily begs alms; dekhi debanārī saṅge — seeing it, the heavenly women; mānuṣe miśāya bhikṣā dite — mingle with the humans to give alms; prabhu-priya-gaṇa yārā — the Lord's dear associates; kata nā kautuke tārā — with what merriment they; bhikṣā dei prabhura jhulite — put alms into the Lord's bag

**15.4.** The Lord merrily begs alms; seeing this, the heavenly women, mingling with the humans, give to Him;
and the Lord's dear associates — with what merriment they put alms into His bag!

মঙ্গল বিধান যত, কে তাহা কহিবে কত, কিবা স্ত্রীগণের যজকার ।
বিপ্রে বেদধ্বনি করে, শুনি কে ধৈরজ ধরে, ভাটগণে কহে কায়বার ॥

*maṅgala bidhāna yata, ke tāhā kahibe kata, kibā strīgaṇera yajakāra |*
*bipre bedadhvani kare, śuni ke dhairaja dhare, bhāṭagaṇe kahe kāyabāra ||*

*Word for word:* maṅgala bidhāna yata — all the auspicious rites; ke tāhā kahibe kata — who can tell them; kibā strī-gaṇera yajakāra — and the jubilant cries of the women; bipre beda-dhvani kare — the brahmanas chant the Vedas; śuni ke dhairaja dhare — who hearing keeps composure; bhāṭa-gaṇe kahe kāyabāra — the bards recite panegyrics

**15.5.** Who can recount all the auspicious rites, all the jubilant cries of the women?
The brahmanas chant the Vedas — who, hearing them, can keep his composure? The bards recite verses of praise.

জয় জয় কলরব, ব্যাপিল সে দিশা সব, নৃত্যগীত বাদ্য নানা ভাতি ।
দাস নরহরি ভণে, যাচক উচিত দানে, ভণয়ে সুযশ সুখে মাতি ॥

*jaya jaya kalaraba, byāpila se diśā saba, nṛtyagīta bādya nānā bhāti |*
*dāsa narahari bhaṇe, yācaka ucita dāne, bhaṇaye suyaśa sukhe māti ||*

*Word for word:* jaya jaya kalaraba — the cries "jaya, jaya"; byāpila se diśā saba — spread in all directions; nṛtya-gīta bādya nānā bhāti — dance, song, music of every kind; dāsa narahari bhaṇe — Narahari Dasa says; yācaka ucita dāne — the supplicants with fitting gifts; bhaṇaye suyaśa sukhe māti — sing the glory, intoxicated with happiness

**15.6.** Cries of "jaya, jaya" spread in all directions; dancing, singing, music of every kind.
Narahari Dasa says: the supplicants, having received fitting gifts, intoxicated with happiness, sing His glory.

[^20-30]: GPT1 — pp. 79–80, no. 3 (kamoda; scan, PDF pp. 338–339); GPT2 — section 2.3, no. 3. The catalogue did not know it (new row NG-281; formerly its
first line was confused with the wedding pada no. 11 "ki ānanda nadīyā-nagare | nimāira bibāhakathā…", NG-030). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, pp. 783;
ed. 1960, vv. 1173–1178): "here Jagannatha Mishra resolved to give his son the sacred thread, fixed the day, called the relatives" (vv. 1170–1172).
The next pada of GPT1, no. 4 (the upanayana: the Lord in the form of Vamana begs alms), is signed by Ghanashyama (outside the appendix); it is also
in the BR (vv. 1179–1192). Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B.
[^20-31]: The red cloth, the staff and the alms-bag are the dress of a brahmachari at the upanayana; he begs his first alms from his relatives. The Lord,
Bhagavan Himself, accepts the sacred thread not out of need but following the lila (note 26). According to CB Adi 8, when He put on the thread, He
was seen as Vamana-deva (cf. Ghanashyama's pada no. 4, note 30). The heavenly women mingling with the humans are the same image as in no. 6.

## 16. Narahari — "gaurasundara parama śubhakṣaṇe…" (GPT1 p. 80, no. 5; BR)
*Gaurasundara in an auspicious hour receives the sacred thread; Shachi and Mishra perform the rites; the women rejoice, the bards praise, the
singers sing, the dancers dance; the gods are beside themselves at this lila. Raga suhai. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is
in the BR; Vrajabuli.*[^20-32]

গৌরসুন্দর পরম শুভক্ষণে ধরল যজ্ঞোপবীত ।
বেদবিহিত ক্রিয়ানিপুণ, শচী মিশ্র নিরুপম রীত ॥

*gaurasundara parama śubhakṣaṇe dharala yajñopabīta |*
*bedabihita kriyānipuṇa, śacī miśra nirupama rīta ||*

*Word for word:* gaurasundara parama śubha-kṣaṇe — Gaurasundara in the supremely auspicious hour; dharala yajñopabīta — received the sacred thread; beda-bihita kriyā-nipuṇa — skilled in the rites the Vedas enjoin; śacī miśra — Shachi and Mishra; nirupama rīta — in incomparable order

**16.1.** In the supremely auspicious hour Gaurasundara has received the sacred thread;
Shachi and Mishra, skilled in the rites the Vedas enjoin, perform them in incomparable order.

বিবিধ মঙ্গল হোত কুলবধূ উলু লু লু লু লু লু দেত ।
ভাটগণ ভণ সুযশ শুভ শোভা সুদিঠি ভরি লেত ॥

*bibidha maṅgala hota kulabadhū ulu lu lu lu lu lu deta |*
*bhāṭagaṇa bhaṇa suyaśa śubha śobhā sudiṭhi bhari leta ||*

*Word for word:* bibidha maṅgala hota — various auspicious rites take place; kula-badhū ulu lu lu… deta — the noble wives cry "ulu-lu-lu"; bhāṭa-gaṇa bhaṇa suyaśa śubha — the bards proclaim the auspicious glory; śobhā sudiṭhi bhari leta — drink in the beauty with their eyes

**16.2.** Various auspicious rites are performed; the noble wives cry "ulu-lu-lu-lu-lu-lu";
the bards proclaim His auspicious glory and drink in this beauty with their eyes.

গান করু নবতাল গুণী মুরজাদি বায়ত সুরঙ্গ ।
নৃত্য কৃত নর্ত্তক উঘটি ঘন ধাধি ধিকধ ধিলঙ্গ ॥

*gāna karu nabatāla guṇī murajādi bāyata suraṅga |*
*nṛtya kṛta narttaka ughaṭi ghana dhādhi dhikadha dhilaṅga ||*

*Word for word:* gāna karu naba-tāla guṇī — skilled singers sing in new metres; murajādi bāyata suraṅga — murajas and other drums sound merrily; nṛtya kṛta nartaka — the dancers dance; ughaṭi ghana — often beating out; dhā-dhi… — syllables

**16.3.** Skilled singers sing in new metres, merrily sound the murajas and other drums;
the dancers dance, often beating out: "dhā-dhi dhikadha dhilaṅga".

দেবগণ-মন মগন অতিশয় নিরখি ললিত বিলাস ।
ভুবন ভরি জয় জয়ধ্বনি, নিছনি নরহরি দাস ॥

*debagaṇa-mana magana atiśaya nirakhi lalita bilāsa |*
*bhubana bhari jaya jayadhvani, nichani narahari dāsa ||*

*Word for word:* debagaṇa-mana magana atiśaya — the gods' hearts are wholly immersed; nirakhi lalita bilāsa — beholding the charming lila; bhubana bhari jaya jaya-dhvani — "jaya, jaya" fills the world; nichani narahari dāsa — Narahari Dasa offers himself

**16.4.** The hearts of the gods are wholly immersed in bliss at the sight of this charming lila;
"jaya, jaya" resounds through the whole world — Narahari Dasa offers himself [to Him].

[^20-32]: GPT1 — p. 80, no. 5 (suhai; scan, PDF pp. 339–340); GPT2 — section 2.3, no. 5 (catalogue: NG-028). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 784; ed. 1960,
vv. 1193–1196), immediately after Ghanashyama's pada; then the BR tells how Mishra took his son to study with Gangadasa Pandita (vv. 1197–1200). The
following padas of the section in GPT1 — nos. 6–8 signed by Lochana, no. 9 by "Trilochana" (wedding padas, partly in nagari-bhava) — are not part of the appendix. Not in
PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B.

## 17. Narahari — "ballabhaduhitā lakṣmī sucaritā…" (GPT1 p. 83, no. 10; BR)
*The first meeting by the Ganga: Lakshmi, Vallabha's daughter, goes with her friends to bathe and, seeing Gaurangachand, cannot restrain
her hidden love; Gora, recognising His beloved, looks at her; their glances secretly meet, and He goes home smiling. Raga kamoda.
**Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^20-33]

বল্লভদুহিতা লক্ষ্মী সুচরিতা সখীতে বেষ্টিত হৈয়া ।
স্নান করিবারে চলে গঙ্গাতীরে চকিত চৌদিকে চাইয়া ॥

*ballabhaduhitā lakṣmī sucaritā sakhīte beṣṭita haiyā |*
*snāna karibāre cale gaṅgātīre cakita caudike cāiyā ||*

*Word for word:* ballabha-duhitā lakṣmī sucaritā — Vallabha's daughter, virtuous Lakshmi; sakhīte beṣṭita haiyā — surrounded by her friends; snāna karibāre — to bathe; cale gaṅgā-tīre — goes to the bank of the Ganga; cakita caudike cāiyā — glancing timidly around

**17.1.** Vallabha's daughter, virtuous Lakshmi, surrounded by her friends,
goes to the bank of the Ganga to bathe, timidly glancing around.

গৌরাঙ্গচাঁদেরে দেখি কিছু দূরে উথলে নিগূঢ় লেহা ।
সে রূপমাধুরী সুধা পান করি ধরিতে না রহে থেহা ॥

*gaurāṅgacām̐dere dekhi kichu dūre uthale nigūṛha lehā |*
*se rūpamādhurī sudhā pāna kari dharite nā rahe thehā ||*

*Word for word:* gaurāṅga-cām̐dere dekhi kichu dūre — seeing Gaurangachand a little way off; uthale nigūṛha lehā — a hidden love surges; se rūpa-mādhurī sudhā pāna kari — drinking the nectar of the sweetness of that form; dharite nā rahe thehā — she cannot keep her composure

**17.2.** Seeing Gaurangachand a little way off, she feels a hidden love surge up;
drinking the nectar of the sweetness of that form, she cannot keep her composure.

গোরা গুণমণি নিজপ্রিয়া চিনি চাহয়ে লক্ষ্মীর পানে ।
জিনি কাঁচা সোণা লক্ষ্মীতনু জেনা প্রবেশে মরম খানে ॥

*gorā guṇamaṇi nijapriyā cini cāhaye lakṣmīra pāne |*
*jini kām̐cā soṇā lakṣmītanu jenā prabeśe marama khāne ||*

*Word for word:* gorā guṇamaṇi — Gora, the jewel of virtues; nija-priyā cini — recognising His own beloved; cāhaye lakṣmīra pāne — looks at Lakshmi; jini kām̐cā soṇā — surpassing pure gold; lakṣmī-tanu jenā — Lakshmi's form, as it were; prabeśe marama khāne — enters the depth of His heart

**17.3.** Gora, the jewel of virtues, recognising His beloved, looks at Lakshmi;
her form, surpassing pure gold, seems to enter His very heart.[^20-34]

দোঁহে দিঠি কোণে মিলে সুসন্ধানে আনে না জানিতে পারে ।
নরহরি পহুঁ হাসি লহু লহু আনন্দে চলিল ঘরে ॥

*dom̐he diṭhi koṇe mile susandhāne āne nā jānite pāre |*
*narahari pahum̐ hāsi lahu lahu ānande calila ghare ||*

*Word for word:* dom̐he diṭhi koṇe mile — the two glances meet from the corners of the eyes; susandhāne — skilfully, secretly; āne nā jānite pāre — no one else can know; narahari pahum̐ — Narahari's Lord; hāsi lahu lahu — smiling softly; ānande calila ghare — went home in joy

**17.4.** The glances of the two meet secretly from the corners of their eyes — so that no one else notices;
Narahari's Lord, smiling softly, went home in joy.

[^20-33]: GPT1 — p. 83, no. 10 (kamoda; scan, PDF p. 342); GPT2 — section 2.3, no. 10 (catalogue: NG-029). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 787; ed. 1960,
vv. 1232–1235): "one day Shachi thought of her son's marriage; His boyhood was ending, His youth beginning… to increase His mother's joy, the Lord
wished to marry; He went along this road to the Ganga, and Lakshmi-devi, the Lord's beloved, came to bathe; their meeting is described by the wise"
(vv. 1226–1231). Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. The meeting by the Ganga — CB Adi 10; Murari 1.9.
[^20-34]: Lakshmipriya is the eternal consort of the Lord, Lakshmi Herself (CB Adi 10; CC Adi 14–15); that is why He "recognises His beloved". Their
love is not a worldly attraction but the eternal relation of the Lord and His energy. "Narahari's Lord" (narahari pahum̐) is a habitual turn of
Chakravarti's signature (note 44 of chapter 17).

## 18. Narahari — "ki ānanda nadīyā-nagare nimāira bibāhakathā…" (GPT1 p. 83, no. 11; BR)
*In every house of Nadia they talk of Nimai's wedding; all long to see it; the bards, dancers and musicians, astrologers, gardeners with
garlands, hundreds of poor supplicants come running; the poet longs to see the wedding with his own eyes. Raga dhanashi. **Attribution:
probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^20-35]

কি আনন্দ নদীয়া-নগরে । নিমাইর বিবাহকথা প্রতি ঘরে ঘরে ॥

*ki ānanda nadīyā-nagare | nimāira bibāhakathā prati ghare ghare ||*

*Word for word:* ki ānanda nadīyā-nagare — what joy in the town of Nadia; nimāira bibāha-kathā — talk of Nimai's wedding; prati ghare ghare — in every house

**18.1.** What joy in the town of Nadia! In every house there is talk of Nimai's wedding.

কি নারী পুরুষ নদীয়ার । বিবাহ দেখিতে হিয়া উথলে সবার ॥

*ki nārī puruṣa nadīyāra | bibāha dekhite hiyā uthale sabāra ||*

*Word for word:* ki nārī puruṣa nadīyāra — both women and men of Nadia; bibāha dekhite — to see the wedding; hiyā uthale sabāra — the hearts of all surge

**18.2.** The men and women of Nadia — the hearts of all are eager to see the wedding.

ভাটগণ চলয়ে ধাইয়া । পাইব অনেক ধন মনে বিচারিয়া ॥

*bhāṭagaṇa calaye dhāiyā | pāiba aneka dhana mane bicāriyā ||*

*Word for word:* bhāṭa-gaṇa calaye dhāiyā — the bards come running; pāiba aneka dhana — "we shall get much wealth"; mane bicāriyā — reckoning in their minds

**18.3.** The bards come running, reckoning they will get much wealth.

নর্ত্তক বাদক আদি যত । করে ধাওয়া ধাই কত করি মনোরথ ॥

*narttaka bādaka ādi yata | kare dhāoyā dhāi kata kari manoratha ||*

*Word for word:* nartaka bādaka ādi yata — dancers, musicians and all the rest; kare dhāoyā dhāi — hasten vying with one another; kata kari manoratha — with how many hopes

**18.4.** The dancers, the musicians and the rest — all hasten, vying with one another, with what hopes!

চলয়ে গণকগণ ধাঞা । করাইব বিবাহ অপূর্ব্ব লগ্ন পাঞা ॥

*calaye gaṇakagaṇa dhāñā | karāiba bibāha apūrvva lagna pāñā ||*

*Word for word:* calaye gaṇaka-gaṇa dhāñā — the astrologers hasten; karāiba bibāha — "we shall have the wedding performed"; apūrva lagna pāñā — finding an incomparable auspicious hour

**18.5.** The astrologers hasten: "We shall fix an incomparable auspicious hour for the wedding!"

মালীগণ চলয়ে উল্লাসে । নানা পুষ্পহার লঞা শ্রীশচী-আবাসে ॥

*mālīgaṇa calaye ullāse | nānā puṣpahāra lañā śrīśacī-ābāse ||*

*Word for word:* mālī-gaṇa calaye ullāse — the gardeners go joyfully; nānā puṣpa-hāra lañā — with various flower garlands; śrī-śacī-ābāse — to the house of Sri Shachi

**18.6.** Joyfully the gardeners go with various garlands of flowers to the house of Sri Shachi.

এক মুখে কহিবে কে কত । দরিদ্র যাচক তারা চলে শত শত ॥

*eka mukhe kahibe ke kata | daridra yācaka tārā cale śata śata ||*

*Word for word:* eka mukhe kahibe ke kata — who with one mouth can tell how many; daridra yācaka tārā — the poor supplicants; cale śata śata — come by the hundred

**18.7.** Who with one mouth can tell how many they are? The poor supplicants come by the hundred.

নরহরি-মনে এই আশ । দেখিব দু-আঁখি ভরি বিবাহ বিলাস ॥

*narahari-mane ei āśa | dekhiba du-ām̐khi bhari bibāha bilāsa ||*

*Word for word:* narahari-mane ei āśa — in Narahari's heart this hope; dekhiba du-ām̐khi bhari — to see to the full with both eyes; bibāha bilāsa — the wedding festivity

**18.8.** In Narahari's heart is one hope: to see the wedding festivity to the full with both eyes.

[^20-35]: GPT1 — p. 83, no. 11 (dhanashi; scan, PDF p. 342); GPT2 — section 2.3, no. 11 (catalogue: the wedding part of row NG-030; see note 30). BR —
12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 788; ed. 1960, vv. ≈1245–1252): after the account of Vanamali Acharya's matchmaking and of the wedding day (vv. 1237–1240).
Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. The matchmaking and the marriage with Lakshmipriya — CB Adi 10; CC Adi 15;
Murari 1.9.

## 19. Narahari — "nadīyāra nababadhū saba biralete kahe…" (GPT1 p. 83, no. 12; BR)
*The young wives of Nadia, apart by themselves, rejoice at the coming wedding: fortunate are Vallabha Acharya and his wife, who gain such a
son-in-law; fortunate is Lakshmi, who gains a husband more beautiful than Kama; Vanamali has made a good match; today is the adhivasa — time to
dress up. Raga dhanashi. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^20-36]

নদীয়ার নববধূ সব বিরলেতে কহে মধুর হাসি ।
ধন্য মোরা যেন দেখিব এহেন বিবাহ সে সুখ-সায়রে ভাসি ॥

*nadīyāra nababadhū saba biralete kahe madhura hāsi |*
*dhanya morā yena dekhiba ehena bibāha se sukha-sāyare bhāsi ||*

*Word for word:* nadīyāra nababadhū saba — all the young wives of Nadia; biralete kahe madhura hāsi — apart by themselves speak with sweet smiles; dhanya morā yena dekhiba — how blessed we are that we shall see; ehena bibāha — such a wedding; se sukha-sāyare bhāsi — floating in that ocean of bliss

**19.1.** The young wives of Nadia, apart by themselves, speak with sweet smiles:
"How fortunate we are that we shall see such a wedding, floating in an ocean of bliss!"

কেহ কহে আর্য্য বল্লভ আচার্য্য ভার্য্যা তার পতিব্রতা সুরীতি ।
হেন লয় চিতে পূরব-পুণ্যেতে পাবে এ জামাতা দুর্ল্লভ অতি ॥

*keha kahe āryya ballabha ācāryya bhāryyā tāra patibratā surīti |*
*hena laya cite pūraba-puṇyete pābe e jāmātā durllabha ati ||*

*Word for word:* keha kahe — one says; ārya ballabha ācārya — the worthy Vallabha Acharya; bhāryā tāra patibratā surīti — his wife, devoted to her husband, virtuous; hena laya cite — so I think; pūraba-puṇyete — through former pious deeds; pābe e jāmātā durlabha ati — they will gain this most rare son-in-law

**19.2.** One says: "The worthy Vallabha Acharya and his wife, devoted to her husband and virtuous —
I think it is for their former pious deeds that they gain so rare a son-in-law."

কেহ কহে ধন্যা বল্লভের কন্যা লক্ষ্মী রূপবতী লখিমী যেন ।
হেন ভাগ্যবতী কে আছে এমতি পাবে পতি জিনি মদন মেন ॥

*keha kahe dhanyā ballabhera kanyā lakṣmī rūpabatī lakhimī yena |*
*hena bhāgyabatī ke āche emati pābe pati jini madana mena ||*

*Word for word:* keha kahe dhanyā ballabhera kanyā — another says: blessed is Vallabha's daughter; lakṣmī rūpabatī — beautiful Lakshmi; lakhimī yena — like Lakshmi herself; hena bhāgyabatī ke āche emati — who else is so fortunate; pābe pati — she will gain a husband; jini madana mena — surpassing Madana (mena = yena, "as it were")

**19.3.** Another says: "Blessed is Vallabha's daughter, the beautiful Lakshmi — like Lakshmi herself;
who else is so fortunate? She will gain a husband who surpasses Madana!"

কেহ কয় ভালি কৈলে ঘটকালি বনমালী কত আনন্দ পাঞা ।
অধিবাস আজি চল চল সাজি নরহরি আসি গেলেন কৈঞা ॥

*keha kaya bhāli kaile ghaṭakāli banamālī kata ānanda pāñā |*
*adhibāsa āji cala cala sāji narahari āsi gelena kaiñā ||*

*Word for word:* keha kaya — yet another says; bhāli kaile ghaṭakāli banamālī — Vanamali made a fine match; kata ānanda pāñā — gaining how much joy; adhibāsa āji — today is the adhivasa; cala cala sāji — come, let us dress up; narahari āsi gelena kaiñā — Narahari came and told [us]

**19.4.** Yet another says: "Vanamali has made a fine match — how much joy he has had!
Today is the adhivasa — come, let us dress up: Narahari came and told us."[^20-37]

[^20-36]: GPT1 — p. 83, no. 12 (dhanashi; scan, PDF p. 342); GPT2 — section 2.3, no. 12 (catalogue: NG-031). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 788; ed. 1960,
vv. 1253–1256; the 1960 editor's heading: "the adhivasa of Nimai's wedding"). Line 19.1: GPT1 has "dhanya mora mena", the BR "dhanya morā yena" — translated
after the BR. Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B.
[^20-37]: Vanamali Acharya is the matchmaker who arranged the Lord's first marriage (CB Adi 10). The adhivasa is the pre-wedding rite on the eve of the
wedding (scents, garlands, blessings). The young wives' talk is joy at the wedding, not nagari-bhava; "surpassing Madana" is the usual praise of
a bridegroom's beauty. Here too the poet places himself in the lila — as the messenger calling the women to the adhivasa (cf. note 24).

## 20. Narahari — "śrīśacī-ālaya ati śobhāmaya…" (GPT1 pp. 83–84, no. 13; BR)
*The women of noble families, telling themselves that today is Gora's adhivasa, dress up and go in rows, lighting up the streets of Nadia, to
Shachi, bow to her and, seeing the Lord in the courtyard, comfort their hearts. Raga dhanashi. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the
pada is in the BR.*[^20-38]

শ্রীশচী-আলয়, অতি শোভাময়, উথলিবে তাহে আনন্দ-সিন্ধু ।
অধিবাস আজি, বিলসিব সাজি, সুখময় গোরা গোকুল-ইন্দু ॥

*śrīśacī-ālaya, ati śobhāmaya, uthalibe tāhe ānanda-sindhu |*
*adhibāsa āji, bilasiba sāji, sukhamaya gorā gokula-indu ||*

*Word for word:* śrī-śacī-ālaya ati śobhāmaya — the house of Sri Shachi is all aglow; uthalibe tāhe ānanda-sindhu — an ocean of joy will surge there; adhibāsa āji — today is the adhivasa; bilasiba sāji — adorned, He will shine; sukhamaya gorā gokula-indu — the blissful Gora, the Moon of Gokula

**20.1.** "The house of Sri Shachi is all aglow, in it an ocean of joy surges:
today is the adhivasa — adorned, the blissful Gora, the Moon of Gokula, will shine."

এত কহি চিতে, নারে স্থির হৈতে, চাহি চারিভিতে কুলের বালা ।
উপমা কি মেন, ঘর হৈতে যেন, বাইর হলো চারু চাঁদের মালা ॥

*eta kahi cite, nāre sthira haite, cāhi cāribhite kulera bālā |*
*upamā ki mena, ghara haite yena, bāira halo cāru cām̐dera mālā ||*

*Word for word:* eta kahi cite — saying this in their hearts; nāre sthira haite — unable to keep still; cāhi cāri-bhite — looking around on all sides; kulera bālā — the maidens of noble families; upamā ki mena — what comparison (mena = yena); ghara haite yena — as if from the houses; bāira halo cāru cām̐dera mālā — lovely garlands of moons came out

**20.2.** Saying this to themselves, unable to keep still, glancing around on all sides, the maidens of noble families —
with what to compare it? — as if lovely garlands of moons had come out of the houses.

বিচিত্র বসন, শোহে আভরণ, প্রতি অঙ্গে বেশ বিন্যাস ভাল ।
নানা ভঙ্গী করি, চলে সারি সারি, নদীয়ার পথ করি আলো ॥

*bicitra basana, śohe ābharaṇa, prati aṅge beśa binyāsa bhāla |*
*nānā bhaṅgī kari, cale sāri sāri, nadīyāra patha kari ālo ||*

*Word for word:* bicitra basana — many-coloured clothes; śohe ābharaṇa — ornaments shine; prati aṅge beśa binyāsa bhāla — every limb finely adorned; nānā bhaṅgī kari — striking various poses; cale sāri sāri — they go in rows; nadīyāra patha kari ālo — lighting up the streets of Nadia

**20.3.** Their many-coloured clothes and ornaments shine, every limb is adorned;
striking various poses, they go in rows, lighting up the streets of Nadia.

কত অভিলাষে, গিয়া আই পাশে, প্রণমিতে কত আদরে আই ।
নরহরি নাথে, পাঞা আঙ্গিনাতে, জুড়াইল হিয়া সে মুখ চাই ॥

*kata abhilāṣe, giyā āi pāśe, praṇamite kata ādare āi |*
*narahari nāthe, pāñā āṅgināte, juṛāila hiyā se mukha cāi ||*

*Word for word:* kata abhilāṣe — with what longing; giyā āi pāśe — going to Ai; praṇamite kata ādare āi — bowing to Ai with what reverence; narahari nāthe — Narahari's Lord; pāñā āṅgināte — finding in the courtyard; juṛāila hiyā — comforted their hearts; se mukha cāi — gazing at that face

**20.4.** With what longing they come to Ai, with what reverence they bow to her!
And finding Narahari's Lord in the courtyard, they comfort their hearts gazing at that face.[^20-39]

[^20-38]: GPT1 — pp. 83–84, no. 13 (dhanashi; scan, PDF pp. 342–343); GPT2 — section 2.3, no. 13 (catalogue: NG-032). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 789;
ed. 1960, vv. 1257–1260). Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. The pada continues the previous one: the young
wives go to the adhivasa.
[^20-39]: Ai ("mother") is Shachi. The women who "comfort their hearts gazing at the face" of the Lord are an image of the all-attractiveness of
Bhagavan at His festival: they have come to bow to the mother and bless the bridegroom; this is not nagari-bhava. Worship of Gaura in the spirit
of "gaura-nagari" is not accepted by the Gaudiya tradition (Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja, Bhaktisiddhanta) (cf. note 15 of chapter 17).

## 21. Narahari — "śobhāmaya śacīra aṅgane…" (GPT1 p. 84, no. 14; BR)
*Nimai's adhivasa: the brahmanas chant the Vedas, the relatives offer scents and garlands, Gora in the assembly surpasses myriads of Kamas;
Vallabha Acharya, having performed the rite, goes home; Shachi with the married women performs the auspicious rites; humans and gods together.
Raga kamoda. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^20-40]

শোভাময় শচীর অঙ্গনে । চতুর্দ্দিকে বেদধ্বনি করে বিপ্রগণে ॥

*śobhāmaya śacīra aṅgane | caturddike bedadhvani kare bipragaṇe ||*

*Word for word:* śobhāmaya śacīra aṅgane — in Shachi's shining courtyard; caturdike beda-dhvani kare bipra-gaṇe — on all sides the brahmanas chant the Vedas

**21.1.** In Shachi's shining courtyard on all sides the brahmanas chant the Vedas.

আজু কি আনন্দ পরকাশ । শুভক্ষণে নিমাইচাঁদের অধিবাস ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*āju ki ānanda parakāśa | śubhakṣaṇe nimāicām̐dera adhibāsa || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* āju ki ānanda parakāśa — what joy has appeared today; śubha-kṣaṇe — in an auspicious hour; nimāi-cām̐dera adhibāsa — the adhivasa of Nimaichand

**21.2.** What joy has appeared today! In an auspicious hour — the adhivasa of Nimaichand.

গন্ধমাল্য দেই আপ্তগণে । দিশা আলো করে গোরা অঙ্গের কিরণে ॥

*gandhamālya dei āptagaṇe | diśā ālo kare gorā aṅgera kiraṇe ||*

*Word for word:* gandha-mālya dei āpta-gaṇe — the relatives offer scents and garlands; diśā ālo kare — lights up the directions; gorā aṅgera kiraṇe — the radiance of Gora's body

**21.3.** The relatives offer scents and garlands; the radiance of Gora's body lights up all directions.

সভামধ্যে গোরা দ্বিজমণি । বিলসয়ে কত না অর্ব্বুদ কাম জিনি ॥

*sabhāmadhye gorā dvijamaṇi | bilasaye kata nā arvvuda kāma jini ||*

*Word for word:* sabhā-madhye — in the midst of the assembly; gorā dvija-maṇi — Gora, the jewel of brahmanas; bilasaye — shines; kata nā arvuda kāma jini — surpassing myriads of Kamas

**21.4.** In the midst of the assembly Gora, the jewel of brahmanas, shines, surpassing myriads of Kamas.

বারেক যে চায় গোরা পানে । না ধরে ধৈরজ সে আপনা নাহি জানে ॥

*bāreka ye cāya gorā pāne | nā dhare dhairaja se āpanā nāhi jāne ||*

*Word for word:* bāreka ye cāya gorā pāne — whoever looks once at Gora; nā dhare dhairaja — loses composure; se āpanā nāhi jāne — knows himself no more

**21.5.** Whoever looks even once at Gora loses his composure and forgets himself.

যেজন আইল অধিবাসে । গন্ধ-চন্দনাদি দিয়া সবে পরিতোষে ॥

*yejana āila adhibāse | gandha-candanādi diyā sabe paritoṣe ||*

*Word for word:* yejana āila adhibāse — whoever came to the adhivasa; gandha-candanādi diyā — giving scents, sandal and the like; sabe paritoṣe — all are satisfied

**21.6.** All who have come to the adhivasa are given scents, sandal paste and the like.

বিধিমতে করি অধিবাস । বল্লভ আচার্য্য গেলা আপন আবাস ॥

*bidhimate kari adhibāsa | ballabha ācāryya gelā āpana ābāsa ||*

*Word for word:* bidhi-mate kari adhibāsa — having performed the adhivasa by the rules; ballabha ācārya gelā āpana ābāsa — Vallabha Acharya went to his own home

**21.7.** Having performed the adhivasa according to the rules, Vallabha Acharya went to his own home.[^20-41]

কহিতে সুখের অন্ত নাই । আইহো শুইহো লঞা শুভ কর্ম্ম করে আই ॥

*kahite sukhera anta nāi | āiho śuiho lañā śubha karmma kare āi ||*

*Word for word:* kahite sukhera anta nāi — there is no end to the happiness to tell; āiho śuiho lañā — with the married women; śubha karma kare āi — Ai performs the auspicious rites

**21.8.** There is no end to the happiness, it cannot be told: with the married women Ai performs the auspicious rites.

নারীগণে দেই যজকার । ভাটগণে করয়ে মঙ্গল কায়বার ॥

*nārīgaṇe dei yajakāra | bhāṭagaṇe karaye maṅgala kāyabāra ||*

*Word for word:* nārī-gaṇe dei yajakāra — the women raise jubilant cries; bhāṭa-gaṇe karaye maṅgala kāyabāra — the bards recite auspicious panegyrics

**21.9.** The women raise jubilant cries, the bards recite auspicious verses of praise.

নৃত্য গীত বাদ্য নানা ভাতি । উপমা দিবার নাই কাহার শকতি ॥

*nṛtya gīta bādya nānā bhāti | upamā dibāra nāi kāhāra śakati ||*

*Word for word:* nṛtya gīta bādya nānā bhāti — dance, song, music of every kind; upamā dibāra nāi kāhāra śakati — no one has the power to give a comparison

**21.10.** Dancing, singing, music of every kind — no one has the power to find a comparison for it.

কেবা না বলয়ে ভাল ভাল । জগভরি জয় জয় শবদ রসাল ॥

*kebā nā balaye bhāla bhāla | jagabhari jaya jaya śabada rasāla ||*

*Word for word:* kebā nā balaye bhāla bhāla — who does not say "good, good"; jaga-bhari — filling the world; jaya jaya śabada rasāla — sweet cries of "jaya, jaya"

**21.11.** Who does not say there: "Good, good!"? Through the whole world — sweet cries of "jaya, jaya".

মানুষে মিশায়ে দেবগণে । দেখি অধিবাসরঙ্গ নরহরি ভণে ॥

*mānuṣe miśāye debagaṇe | dekhi adhibāsaraṅga narahari bhaṇe ||*

*Word for word:* mānuṣe miśāye deba-gaṇe — the gods mingling with the humans; dekhi adhibāsa-raṅga — watch the merriment of the adhivasa; narahari bhaṇe — says Narahari

**21.12.** The gods, mingling with the humans, watch the merriment of the adhivasa — says Narahari.

[^20-40]: GPT1 — p. 84, no. 14 (kamoda; scan, PDF p. 343); GPT2 — section 2.3, no. 14 (catalogue: NG-033). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, pp. 789–790; ed. 1960,
vv. 1261–1272). Variants: 21.3 GPT1 "ambagaṇe", BR "āptagaṇe" ("the relatives") — after the BR; 21.8 in GPT1 the end of the line is cut off ("kare a…"),

performs the bride's adhivasa (next pada). "The married women" (āiho śuiho) are wives whose husbands are living: only they perform the auspicious
wedding rites.
