receiving scents and a garland, rejoices, while around her, invisible, throng the heavenly women; music and the women's cries. Raga dhanashi.
**Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^20-42]

আজু স্নেহেতে বিহ্বল হৈয়া ।
বল্লভ আচার্য্য, অধিবাসকার্য্য, করে আত্মবিপ্রবর্গেরে লইয়া ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*āju snehete bihvala haiyā |*
*ballabha ācāryya, adhibāsakāryya, kare ātmabiprabargere laiyā || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* āju snehete bihvala haiyā — today, overwhelmed with tenderness; ballabha ācārya — Vallabha Acharya; adhibāsa-kārya kare — performs the rite of adhivasa; ātma-bipra-bargere laiyā — with his brahmana kinsmen

**22.1.** Today, beside himself with tenderness,
Vallabha Acharya with his brahmana kinsmen performs the rite of adhivasa.

কত সাধে মায়, লখিমী কন্যায়, পরাইয়া বাস ভূষণ ভালি ।
সুচারু অঙ্গনে, দিব্য সিংহাসনে, বসাইয়া সুখে ভাসয়ে আলী ॥

*kata sādhe māya, lakhimī kanyāya, parāiyā bāsa bhūṣaṇa bhāli |*
*sucāru aṅgane, dibya siṃhāsane, basāiyā sukhe bhāsaye ālī ||*

*Word for word:* kata sādhe māya — with what love the mother; lakhimī kanyāya — her daughter Lakshmi; parāiyā bāsa bhūṣaṇa bhāli — dressing in lovely clothes and ornaments; sucāru aṅgane — in the beautiful courtyard; dibya siṃhāsane basāiyā — seating on a divine throne; sukhe bhāsaye ālī — the friends float in happiness

**22.2.** With what love the mother, having dressed her daughter Lakshmi in lovely clothes and ornaments,
seats her on a divine throne in the middle of the beautiful courtyard — and her friends float in happiness.

শুভক্ষণে দিতে গন্ধমালা, চিতে উলসিত বাড়ে অঙ্গের ছটা ।
থির নহে চিত, দেখে অলখিত, চারিভিতে দেবরমণী ঘটা ॥

*śubhakṣaṇe dite gandhamālā, cite ulasita bāṛe aṅgera chaṭā |*
*thira nahe cita, dekhe alakhita, cāribhite debaramaṇī ghaṭā ||*

*Word for word:* śubha-kṣaṇe dite gandha-mālā — when in the auspicious hour scents and a garland are given; cite ulasita — joy in the heart; bāṛe aṅgera chaṭā — the radiance of her form grows; thira nahe cita — hearts are not steady; dekhe alakhita — they gaze unseen; cāri-bhite deba-ramaṇī ghaṭā — around her hosts of heavenly women

**22.3.** When in the auspicious hour scents and a garland are offered to her, her heart rejoices and her form shines brighter;
hearts know no rest: around, invisible, throng hosts of heavenly women, gazing.[^20-43]

শঙ্খ ঘণ্টা আদি বাদ্য নানাবিধি, নৃত্য গীত শুভ ভাটেতে ভণে ।
নারী যজকারে, ধৃতি ধরিবারে, নারে নরহরি নিছনি মেনে ॥

*śaṅkha ghaṇṭā ādi bādya nānābidhi, nṛtya gīta śubha bhāṭete bhaṇe |*

*Word for word:* śaṅkha ghaṇṭā ādi bādya nānā-bidhi — conches, bells and various instruments; nṛtya gīta — dance, song; śubha bhāṭete bhaṇe — the bards proclaim auspicious words; nārī yajakāre — at the women's jubilant cries; dhṛti dharibāre nāre narahari — Narahari cannot keep composure; nichani mene — offering himself

**22.4.** Conches, bells and various instruments, dancing, singing; the bards proclaim auspicious words;

# Chapter 21. Appendix. Padas signed "Narahari" from the Gaura-pada-tarangini — V: the wedding with Lakshmipriya and the beginning of the second wedding

*Continuation of the appendix (the introductory note on the two Naraharis, on the arguments for attribution and on the marks in the
headings is in ch. 17). Chapter 21: the end of GPT section 2.3 "Karnavedha and the wedding" — the wedding day with Lakshmipriya (the
morning after the adhivasa, the water rite, the bath and dressing of the bridegroom, the procession, the wedding in the house of Vallabha
Acharya, the bridal chamber, the return home) and life with Lakshmipriya; the beginning of section 2.4 "The second marriage" — the news of
the wedding with Vishnupriya, the women of Nadia with Shachi, the adhivasa of bridegroom and bride, the morning of the wedding day (the bath
and dressing of the bridegroom; the procession and the wedding itself follow in the next chapter). Narahari Chakravarti quotes almost all
the padas of the chapter one after another in the 12th wave of the Bhakti-ratnakara, where Ishana shows Srinivasa the house of Jagannatha
Mishra (two padas of section 2.4 are also in Chakravarti's Gaura-charita-chintamani); one (no. 13) has not been found in any witness. Before
translation the "Narahari" signatures in sections 2.3–2.4 (GPT1 pp. 84–100) were checked throughout, in the OCR and on the scan: the
catalogue had missed two padas of section 2.4 (nos. 18 and 23, new rows NG-285, 286). From section 2.4, up to the adhivasa and the morning
of the wedding, the following are not translated: nos. 4 and 11 — signed Ghanashyama (outside the appendix); nos. 2, 3 and 7 — padas in
nagari-bhava (a young wife's dream in which Gaura invites her to the wedding and embraces her; the "anuraga" of the women for Gaura; women
who give Him "life and youth") — assigned to the section of nagari padas. The base text is GPT1 (doubtful places from the scan), collated
with GPT2, the BR (eds. 1912 and 1960) and the Gaura-charita-chintamani (ed. 1947); PK, KGC, PS and the Gita-chandrodaya have been checked. On
Lakshmipriya and Vishnupriya as the eternal energies of the Lord and on the wedding rites as lila see notes 2 and 30; on the motif of the
women of Nadia, note 5. The notes of the GPT editors are not reproduced.*

## 1. Narahari — "adhibāsa niśi pohāile…" (GPT1 p. 85, section 2.3, no. 16; BR)
*The wedding day: the night of the adhivasa is over; Nimai, surrounded by brahmanas, performs the Vedic rites; crowds, music, songs, the
praises of the bhatas, the women's cries of joy; everyone rejoices at the women's rites. Raga kamoda. **Attribution: probably
Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave).*[^21-1]

অধিবাস নিশি পোহাইলে । বিবাহের কার্য্য যত করয়ে সকলে ॥

*adhibāsa niśi pohāile | bibāhera kāryya yata karaye sakale ||*

*Word for word:* adhibāsa niśi pohāile — when the night of the adhivasa had passed; bibāhera kāryya yata — all the wedding tasks; karaye sakale — everyone performs

**1.1.** When the night of the adhivasa had passed, everyone set about the wedding tasks.

বিপ্রগণে হইয়া বেষ্টিত । নিমাই করেন ক্রিয়া যে বেদবিহিত ॥

*bipragaṇe haiyā beṣṭita | nimāi karena kriyā ye bedabihita ||*

*Word for word:* bipragaṇe haiyā beṣṭita — surrounded by brahmanas; nimāi karena kriyā — Nimai performs the rites; ye beda-bihita — which are enjoined by the Vedas

**1.2.** Surrounded by brahmanas, Nimai performs the rites enjoined by the Vedas.[^21-2]

লোক ভীড় কহিলে না হয় । লেহ দেহ বাক্য কোলাহল অতিশয় ॥

*loka bhīṛa kahile nā haya | leha deha bākya kolāhala atiśaya ||*

*Word for word:* loka bhīṛa — the crowd of people; kahile nā haya — cannot be told; leha deha bākya — the cries "take! give!"; kolāhala atiśaya — the clamour is immense

**1.3.** The crowds cannot be described: the clamour of "take! give!" is immense.

বাজে নানা বাদ্য নিরন্তর । গায়কগণেতে গান করে পূর্ব্বাপর ॥

*bāje nānā bādya nirantara | gāyakagaṇete gāna kare pūrvvāpara ||*

*Word for word:* bāje nānā bādya nirantara — instruments of every kind play without pause; gāyaka-gaṇete gāna kare — the singers sing; pūrvvāpara — one [song] after another

**1.4.** Instruments of every kind play without pause; the singers sing song after song.

ভাটগণে পড়ে কায়বার । নারীগণে দেই সুমধুর যজকার ॥

*bhāṭagaṇe paṛe kāyabāra | nārīgaṇe dei sumadhura yajakāra ||*

*Word for word:* bhāṭa-gaṇe paṛe kāyabāra — the bhatas recite verses of praise; nārī-gaṇe dei — the women raise; sumadhura yajakāra — sweet cries of joy

**1.5.** The bhatas recite verses of praise; the women raise sweet cries of joy.

সবার উল্লাস স্ত্রী-আচারে । নরহরি ভাসে সেনা সুখের সায়রে ॥

*sabāra ullāsa strī-ācāre | narahari bhāse senā sukhera sāyare ||*

*Word for word:* sabāra ullāsa — all rejoice; strī-ācāre — at the women's rites; narahari bhāse — Narahari floats; senā sukhera sāyare — in that ocean of happiness

**1.6.** All rejoice at the women's rites; Narahari floats in that ocean of happiness.[^21-3]

[^21-1]: GPT1 — p. 85, section 2.3 ("karnavedha and the wedding"), no. 16 (kamoda; scan, PDF p. 344); GPT2 — section 2.3, no. 16 (catalogue: NG-282).
BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, pp. 790–791; ed. 1960, vv. 1277–1282), straight after the adhivasa of the bride (no. 22 of chapter 20); then the BR gives
the padas nos. 2–12 of this chapter in sequence. Variants: 1.4 GPT1 "pūrvvāpara" ("one after another"), BR "manohara" ("enchantingly"); 1.6 GPT1
"sāyare", BR "pāthāre" (both "in the ocean"). Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. The wedding with
Lakshmipriya — CB Adi 10; CC Adi 15; Murari 1.9–1.10.
[^21-2]: Lakshmipriya is the eternal consort of the Lord, Lakshmi Herself (CB Adi 10; CC Adi 14–15); the Lord's wedding is not a worldly event but His
lila with His own energy. The Lord, the goal of all the Vedas, is bound by nothing enjoined; He accepts the wedding rites in keeping with the
lila and for the joy of His mother and His associates — as Krishna did in Dvaraka. So are all the padas of this chapter on the Lord's
"marriage" to be understood.
[^21-3]: The women's rites (strī-ācāra) are the wedding customs performed by married women in addition to the Vedic rites (the cries of "ulu-lu", the
water rite, the anointing of the bridegroom, etc.). Here too the poet places himself in the lila as a witness and participant (cf. note 24 of
chapter 20).

## 2. Narahari — "kulabadhūgaṇa ulasita mana…" (GPT1 p. 85, no. 17; BR)
*The wives of noble families dress to go for the water of the wedding bath; looking at Gora's face, they cry "ulu-lu"; they go, talking among
themselves; anklets ring, music plays; having performed the water rite, they enter the house. Raga kamoda. **Attribution: probably
Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^21-4]

কুলবধূগণ উলসিত মন পানি-সহিবারে সাজয়ে রঙ্গে ।
গোরা-মুখশশী হেরি হেরি হাসি উলু লুলু দেই পুলক অঙ্গে ॥

*kulabadhūgaṇa ulasita mana pāni-sahibāre sājaye raṅge |*
*gorā-mukhaśaśī heri heri hāsi ulu lulu dei pulaka aṅge ||*

*Word for word:* kulabadhū-gaṇa — the wives of noble families; ulasita mana — their hearts rejoicing; pāni-sahibāre — for the water [rite]; sājaye raṅge — gaily dress; gorā-mukha-śaśī — Gora's moonlike face; heri heri — gazing again and again; hāsi — smiling; ulu lulu dei — cry "ulu-lu"; pulaka aṅge — a thrill in the body

**2.1.** The wives of noble families, their hearts rejoicing, gaily dress to go for the water;
gazing again and again at Gora's moonlike face, they smile and cry "ulu-lu", and a thrill runs through their bodies.

চলে ঘরে হৈতে কত উঠে চিতে গৌর-বিধু-অঙ্গ-সৌরভে মাতি ।
অথির অন্তর ভাবে গর গর আঁখি কোণে ভঙ্গী কত না ভাঁতি ॥

*cale ghare haite kata uṭhe cite gaura-bidhu-aṅga-saurabhe māti |*
*athira antara bhābe gara gara ām̐khi koṇe bhaṅgī kata nā bhām̐ti ||*

*Word for word:* cale ghare haite — they come out of their houses; kata uṭhe cite — how much rises in the heart; gaura-bidhu-aṅga-saurabhe māti — intoxicated by the fragrance of the Gaura-moon's body; athira antara — the heart unsteady; bhābe gara gara — brimming with feeling; ām̐khi koṇe — from the corners of the eyes; bhaṅgī kata nā bhām̐ti — how many kinds of glances

**2.2.** They come out of their houses — how many feelings rise in their hearts! — intoxicated by the fragrance of the body of the Gaura-moon;
their hearts know no rest, brimming with feeling; from the corners of their eyes — how many different glances!

পরস্পর কত কহে অবেকত কে না নিছে তনু রঙ্গিণী রীতে ।
বাসভূষা বেশে ধৈরজ বিনাশে কে পারে সে শোভা উপমা দিতে ॥

*paraspara kata kahe abekata ke nā niche tanu raṅgiṇī rīte |*
*bāsabhūṣā beśe dhairaja bināśe ke pāre se śobhā upamā dite ||*

*Word for word:* paraspara kata kahe — how much they say to one another; abekata — of the unmanifest (what cannot be told); ke nā niche tanu — who does not offer herself [for Him] (nichhani); raṅgiṇī rīte — playfully (lit. "in the manner of a playful woman"); bāsa-bhūṣā beśe — with dress, ornaments and attire; dhairaja bināśe — they destroy composure; ke pāre se śobhā upamā dite — who can compare that beauty

**2.3.** How much they say to one another of what cannot be told! Which of them, playful, does not offer herself for Him?
With their dress, ornaments and attire they shatter all composure — who could find a likeness for that beauty?

নূপুর কিঙ্কিণী নানা বাদ্যধ্বনি কি মধুর কহি না আসে মুখে ।
পানিসায়ি শেষে ভবনে প্রবেশে নরহরি হিয়া উথলে সুখে ॥

*nūpura kiṅkiṇī nānā bādyadhvani ki madhura kahi nā āse mukhe |*
*pānisāyi śeṣe bhabane prabeśe narahari hiyā uthale sukhe ||*

*Word for word:* nūpura kiṅkiṇī — anklets and girdles of bells; nānā bādya-dhvani — the sound of many instruments; ki madhura — how sweet; kahi nā āse mukhe — words cannot tell; pāni-sāyi śeṣe — at the end of the water rite; bhabane prabeśe — they enter the house; narahari hiyā uthale sukhe — Narahari's heart overflows with joy

**2.4.** Anklets, girdles of bells, the sounds of many instruments — how sweet, words cannot tell!
Having completed the water rite, they enter the house — and Narahari's heart overflows with joy.[^21-5]

[^21-4]: GPT1 — p. 85, no. 17 (kamoda; scan, PDF p. 344); GPT2 — section 2.3, no. 17 (catalogue: NG-035). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 791; ed. 1960,
vv. 1283–1286). Variant: 2.1 GPT1 "pāni-sahibāre", BR "pāni sāibāre" — "to perform the water rite" (translated by the sense of both readings).
Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. "Pani-sai" (jala sādhā) is a wedding custom: married women go with music
to the Ganga and draw water for the bath of the bridegroom (or bride).
[^21-5]: The poet describes the delight of the women of Nadia at the Lord's wedding in words close to the motif of the townswomen (nagaris) enamoured
of Gaura. We translate faithfully to the author; but the Gaudiya tradition (Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja, Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati)
does not accept the worship of Gaura in the mood of "Gaura-nagari": Gaura is Krishna Himself in the mood and lustre of Radha; He came to taste Her
love, not to enjoy as a nagara. The Lord's attractiveness for the people of Navadvipa is the quality of Bhagavan, who attracts all; it is not
worldly passion. The same holds for the other padas of the chapter about the women of Nadia (cf. note 39 of chapter 20).

## 3. Narahari — "kibā śrīśacī-bhabana mājhe…" (GPT1 p. 85, no. 18; BR)
*The wedding bath of the bridegroom: amid auspicious cries the women loosen His locks and braid them again, oiling them, rub Him with
turmeric and perfumes; He is bathed with Ganga water, and the poet playfully dries Him with a towel. Raga kamoda. **Attribution: probably
Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^21-6]

কিবা শ্রীশচী-ভবন মাঝে । বিবিধ মঙ্গল কলরবে সবে ভ্রময়ে বিবাহ কাজে ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*kibā śrīśacī-bhabana mājhe | bibidha maṅgala kalarabe sabe bhramaye bibāha kāje || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* kibā — what [bustle]; śrī-śacī-bhabana mājhe — in the house of Sri Shachi; bibidha maṅgala kalarabe — amid manifold auspicious cries; sabe bhramaye — all move about; bibāha kāje — on the wedding tasks

**3.1.** What [bustle] in the house of Sri Shachi! Amid manifold auspicious cries all are busy with the wedding tasks.

সে যে গোরা গোকুলের ইন্দু । বিবাহ-বিহিত স্নানে অতিশয় উথলে আনন্দ-সিন্ধু ॥

*se ye gorā gokulera indu | bibāha-bihita snāne atiśaya uthale ānanda-sindhu ||*

*Word for word:* se ye gorā — for Gora; gokulera indu — is the Moon of Gokula; bibāha-bihita snāne — at the bath enjoined for the wedding; atiśaya — beyond measure; uthale ānanda-sindhu — the ocean of joy surges

**3.2.** For Gora is the Moon of Gokula: at the bath enjoined before the wedding the ocean of joy surges beyond measure.

কুলবধূ সুমধুর ছাঁদে । সুচারু কুন্তলে তৈল দিব বলে বারে বারে আউলাঞা বাঁধে ॥

*kulabadhū sumadhura chām̐de | sucāru kuntale taila diba bale bāre bāre āulāñā bām̐dhe ||*

*Word for word:* kulabadhū — the wives of noble families; sumadhura chām̐de — sweetly and gracefully; sucāru kuntale — into the lovely locks; taila diba bale — saying "let us put in oil"; bāre bāre — again and again; āulāñā bām̐dhe — loosen and braid them

**3.3.** The wives of noble families, sweetly and gracefully, saying, "Let us oil His lovely locks," loosen and braid them again and again.

কেহ হলদি মাখায় গায় । হলদি মলিন হেরি হাসে সবে পরাণ নিছয়ে তায় ॥

*keha haladi mākhāya gāya | haladi malina heri hāse sabe parāṇa nichaye tāya ||*

*Word for word:* keha haladi mākhāya gāya — one rubs [His] body with turmeric; haladi malina heri — seeing the turmeric grow dim; hāse sabe — all laugh; parāṇa nichaye tāya — they give their lives for Him (the nimchhani rite)

**3.4.** One rubs His body with turmeric; seeing the turmeric grow dim, all laugh and give their lives for Him.[^21-7]

কেহ গন্ধদ্রব্য দেই অঙ্গে । সে না অঙ্গ-গন্ধে গন্ধমদ হরে উপমা দিব কি সঙ্গে ॥

*keha gandhadrabya dei aṅge | se nā aṅga-gandhe gandhamada hare upamā diba ki saṅge ||*

*Word for word:* keha gandha-drabya dei aṅge — one puts perfumes on His body; se nā aṅga-gandhe — the fragrance of that body; gandha-mada hare — takes away the pride of perfumes; upamā diba ki saṅge — with what shall I compare it

**3.5.** One anoints His body with perfumes — but the fragrance of that body robs the perfumes of their pride: with what to compare it?

অভিষেক কৈল গঙ্গাজলে । নরহরি পানি-তোলা লইয়া তনু পোছয়ে কৌতুক ছলে ॥

*abhiṣeka kaila gaṅgājale | narahari pāni-tolā laiyā tanu pochaye kautuka chale ||*

*Word for word:* abhiṣeka kaila gaṅgājale — they bathed [Him] with Ganga water; narahari — Narahari; pāni-tolā laiyā — taking a towel; tanu pochaye — dries the body; kautuka chale — as if in play

**3.6.** They bathed Him with Ganga water; Narahari, taking a towel, dries His body as if in play.

[^21-6]: GPT1 — p. 85, no. 18 (kamoda; scan, PDF p. 344); GPT2 — section 2.3, no. 18 (catalogue: NG-036). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 791; ed. 1960,
vv. 1287–1292). Variants: 3.2 GPT1 "sthāne" ("in the place"), BR "snāne" ("at the bath") — following the BR; 3.5 GPT1 "upamā diba ki saṅge", BR-1912
"ke dibe upamā aṅge". Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. Line 3.1 is the refrain (dhru).
[^21-7]: Grown dim beside the golden radiance of the Lord's body. "Give their lives" (parāṇa nichaye) refers to the rite of nimchhani: out of love one
waves something (in poetry — one's very life) around the beloved to ward off misfortune. The playful care of the women who perform the wedding
rites (anointing the bridegroom with turmeric and oil) is festive merriment, not nagari-bhava.

## 4. Narahari — "āju kata nā ānanda mane…" (GPT1 p. 86, no. 19; BR)
*His friends dress the bridegroom: they anoint Him with sandal, draw the tilaka, adorn His curls with a garland of malati, put on earrings,
necklace, bracelets and rings and a golden chain on His waist; the poet, having clothed Him in a red-bordered cloth, beholds His beauty.
Raga kamoda. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^21-8]

আজু কত না আনন্দ মনে । বসিয়া আসনে বিশ্বম্ভর-বেশ রচয়ে বয়স্যগণে ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*āju kata nā ānanda mane | basiyā āsane biśvambhara-beśa racaye bayasyagaṇe || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* āju kata nā ānanda mane — how much joy in the heart today; basiyā āsane — seated on a seat; biśvambhara-beśa — Vishvambhara's attire; racaye bayasya-gaṇe — His friends arrange

**4.1.** How much joy in the heart today! Seating Vishvambhara on a seat, His friends dress Him.

গন্ধ চন্দন চরচে গায় । বিরচয়ে চারু ললাটে তিলক কেবা না ভুলয় তায় ॥

*gandha candana carace gāya | biracaye cāru lalāṭe tilaka kebā nā bhulaya tāya ||*

*Word for word:* gandha candana — fragrant sandal paste; carace gāya — they smear on the body; biracaye cāru lalāṭe tilaka — they draw a lovely tilaka on the forehead; kebā nā bhulaya tāya — whom would it not enchant

**4.2.** They anoint His body with fragrant sandal paste and draw a lovely tilaka on His forehead — whom would it not enchant?

বাঁধি চাঁচর চিকুর ভালে । মনের উল্লাসে মধুর ছাঁদে বেড়য়ে মালতী মালে ॥

*bām̐dhi cām̐cara cikura bhāle | manera ullāse madhura chām̐de beṛaye mālatī māle ||*

*Word for word:* bām̐dhi cām̐cara cikura bhāle — gathering the curling locks on the brow; manera ullāse — in gladness of heart; madhura chām̐de — sweetly and gracefully; beṛaye mālatī māle — they wind them with a garland of malati

**4.3.** Gathering the curling locks above His brow, in gladness of heart, sweetly and gracefully they wind them with a garland of malati.

কাণে কুণ্ডল অর্পণ করে । ঝলকয়ে গণ্ডতটে গণ্ডযুগ দর্পণ দরপ হরে ॥

*kāṇe kuṇḍala arpaṇa kare | jhalakaye gaṇḍataṭe gaṇḍayuga darpaṇa darapa hare ||*

*Word for word:* kāṇe kuṇḍala arpaṇa kare — they put earrings in His ears; jhalakaye gaṇḍa-taṭe — they flash by the cheeks; gaṇḍa-yuga — the two cheeks; darpaṇa darapa hare — rob mirrors of their pride

**4.4.** They put earrings in His ears — they flash beside His cheeks, and His cheeks rob mirrors of their pride.

গলে দেই মণিময় হার । পরিসর বুকে দোলে সুললিত কে দিবে উপমা তার ॥

*gale dei maṇimaya hāra | parisara buke dole sulalita ke dibe upamā tāra ||*

*Word for word:* gale dei maṇimaya hāra — they put a jewelled necklace on His neck; parisara buke — on the broad chest; dole sulalita — it sways charmingly; ke dibe upamā tāra — who will find its likeness

**4.5.** They put a necklace of jewels on His neck; it sways charmingly on His broad chest — who can find a likeness for it?

বাহু অঙ্গদ বলয়া করে । অঙ্গুলে অঙ্গুরি সোঁপি মুখপানে চাহি না ধৈরজ ধরে ॥

*bāhu aṅgada balayā kare | aṅgule aṅguri som̐pi mukhapāne cāhi nā dhairaja dhare ||*

*Word for word:* bāhu aṅgada — armlets on the arms; balayā kare — bracelets on the hands; aṅgule aṅguri som̐pi — putting rings on the fingers; mukha-pāne cāhi — looking at the face; nā dhairaja dhare — they cannot keep composure

**4.6.** On His arms armlets and bracelets, on His fingers they put rings — and, looking at His face, they cannot keep their composure.

সিংহ জিনি মাজাখানি ক্ষীণ । সোণার শিকলি সাজাইতে আঁখি হইল নিমিষহীন ॥

*siṃha jini mājākhāni kṣīṇa | soṇāra śikali sājāite ām̐khi haila nimiṣahīna ||*

*Word for word:* siṃha jini — surpassing a lion's; mājākhāni kṣīṇa — the waist is slender; soṇāra śikali sājāite — adorning it with a golden chain; ām̐khi haila nimiṣa-hīna — the eyes became unblinking

**4.7.** His waist is slender, slenderer than a lion's; as they adorn it with a golden chain, their eyes cease to blink.

বেশ-বিন্যাস ভুবন-লোভা । রক্তপ্রান্ত বাস পরাইয়া নরহরি নিরখয়ে শোভা ॥

*beśa-binyāsa bhubana-lobhā | raktaprānta bāsa parāiyā narahari nirakhaye śobhā ||*

*Word for word:* beśa-binyāsa — the array of attire; bhubana-lobhā — tempting the world; raktaprānta bāsa parāiyā — clothing Him in a red-bordered cloth; narahari nirakhaye śobhā — Narahari beholds the beauty

**4.8.** An array that tempts the world! Having clothed Him in a red-bordered cloth, Narahari beholds His beauty.[^21-9]

[^21-8]: GPT1 — p. 86, no. 19 (kamoda; scan, PDF p. 345); GPT2 — section 2.3, no. 19 (catalogue: NG-037). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, pp. 791–792; ed. 1960,
vv. 1293–1300). Variant: 4.6 GPT1 "cāhilā dhairaja dhare" ("having looked, they kept composure"?), BR "cāhi nā dhairaya dhare" — translated following the BR. Not
in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. Line 4.1 is the refrain (dhru).
[^21-9]: Vishvambhara ("He who sustains the universe") is the name given to the Lord at His naming (CB Adi 4). The red-bordered cloth is the
bridegroom's wedding garment. Here too the poet takes part in the lila, clothing the Lord (cf. 3.6).

## 5. Narahari — "beśa banāiyā sahacare…" (GPT1 pp. 86–87, no. 20; BR)
*His friends, having dressed Nimai, give Him a golden mirror; even the gods cannot take their eyes off Him; Shachi and her friends perform
auspicious rites; the young wives look on from afar; bowing to His mother, Gaura sets out for the wedding amid Vedic chanting and music.
Raga kamoda. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^21-10]

বেশ বনাইয়া সহচরে । শশী সম সুবর্ণ দর্পণ দেই করে ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*beśa banāiyā sahacare | śaśī sama subarṇa darpaṇa dei kare || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* beśa banāiyā — having dressed [Him]; sahacare — His friends; śaśī sama — like the moon; subarṇa darpaṇa — a golden mirror; dei kare — put into His hand

**5.1.** Having dressed [Him], His friends put into His hand a golden mirror like the moon.

নিমাই চাঁদের বেশ দেখি । আনের কি দেবেও ফিরাইতে নারে আঁখি ॥

*nimāi cām̐dera beśa dekhi | ānera ki debeo phirāite nāre ām̐khi ||*

*Word for word:* nimāi cām̐dera beśa dekhi — seeing the attire of Nimaichand; ānera ki — what of others; debeo — even the gods; phirāite nāre ām̐khi — cannot turn away their eyes

**5.2.** Seeing the attire of Nimaichand — what to speak of others? — even the gods cannot turn their eyes away.

নিজ সখী সহ শচী আই । করয়ে মঙ্গল কত পুত্রমুখ চাই ॥

*nija sakhī saha śacī āi | karaye maṅgala kata putramukha cāi ||*

*Word for word:* nija sakhī saha — with her own friends; śacī āi — mother Shachi; karaye maṅgala kata — performs many auspicious rites; putra-mukha cāi — gazing at her son's face

**5.3.** Mother Shachi with her friends performs many auspicious rites, gazing at her son's face.

নব বধূগণ দূরে রৈয়া । না ধরে ধৈরজ গোরাচাঁদ পানে চাঞা ॥

*naba badhūgaṇa dūre raiyā | nā dhare dhairaja gorācām̐da pāne cāñā ||*

*Word for word:* naba badhū-gaṇa — the young wives; dūre raiyā — standing at a distance; nā dhare dhairaja — cannot keep composure; gorācām̐da pāne cāñā — looking at Gorachand

**5.4.** The young wives, standing at a distance, cannot keep their composure as they look at Gorachand.

উলু লুলু দেয় নারীগণে । বিবাহ বিনোদ কথা ভরিল ভুবনে ॥

*ulu lulu deya nārīgaṇe | bibāha binoda kathā bharila bhubane ||*

*Word for word:* ulu lulu deya nārī-gaṇe — the women cry "ulu-lu"; bibāha binoda kathā — the tale of the joyful wedding; bharila bhubane — filled the world

**5.5.** The women cry "ulu-lu"; the news of the joyful wedding has filled the world.

প্রণমিয়া জননীর পায় । বিবাহ করিতে যাত্রা করে গৌর রায় ॥

*praṇamiyā jananīra pāya | bibāha karite yātrā kare gaura rāya ||*

*Word for word:* praṇamiyā jananīra pāya — bowing at His mother's feet; bibāha karite — to be married; yātrā kare — sets out; gaura rāya — Gaura Raya

**5.6.** Bowing at His mother's feet, Gaura Raya sets out to be married.[^21-11]

বেদ ধ্বনি করে বিপ্রগণে । বাজে নানা বাদ্য শব্দ ভেদয়ে গগনে ॥

*beda dhvani kare bipragaṇe | bāje nānā bādya śabda bhedaye gagane ||*

*Word for word:* beda dhvani kare bipragaṇe — the brahmanas chant the Vedas; bāje nānā bādya — many instruments resound; śabda bhedaye gagane — the sound pierces the sky

**5.7.** The brahmanas chant the Vedas; instruments of many kinds resound — the sound pierces the sky.

কৌতুক কহিতে কেবা পারে । নরহরি সাঁতারয়ে সে সুখ পাথারে ॥

*kautuka kahite kebā pāre | narahari sām̐tāraye se sukha pāthāre ||*

*Word for word:* kautuka kahite kebā pāre — who can tell of the merriment; narahari sām̐tāraye — Narahari swims; se sukha pāthāre — in that ocean of happiness

**5.8.** Who can tell of this merriment? Narahari swims in that ocean of happiness.

[^21-10]: GPT1 — pp. 86–87, no. 20 (kamoda; scan, PDF pp. 345–346); GPT2 — section 2.3, no. 20. The catalogue did not know it (new row NG-283, chapter 20).
BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 792; ed. 1960, vv. 1301–1308; the 1960 editor's heading before the next pada: "the wedding of Sri Nimai"). Variant: 5.6 BR
"gaurarāya" — the same. Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. Line 5.1 is the refrain (dhru).
[^21-11]: The Lord bows to His mother, setting an example of respect for one's parents. On the young wives (5.4) see note 5.

## 6. Narahari — "āju godhūli samaya śubhakṣaṇa…" (GPT1 p. 87, no. 21; BR)
*The wedding procession: at the auspicious hour of dusk Gaura in wedding attire mounts the palanquin and, surrounded by brahmanas, moves
slowly to Vallabha's house; praises, dances, songs, a sea of music; the gods gaze unblinking from the sky and descend unseen to earth;
crowds, hundreds of lamps, moonlight; the Earth, the Ganga, beasts and birds rejoice. Raga bhupali. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** —
the pada is in the BR; ornate Vrajabuli.*[^21-12]

আজু গোধূলি সময় শুভক্ষণ গৌর গুণমণি ভুবনমোহন বেশ বিরচিত বিবাহ-বিহিত সুমৃদুল তনু ছবি ছলকায় ।
কোটি মনমথ-গরব-ভঞ্জন কঞ্জদিঠি জন-হৃদয়-রঞ্জন চাহি দিশ চহু হাসি লহু লহু চঢ়ত চৌদল ঝলকায় ॥

*āju godhūli samaya śubhakṣaṇa gaura guṇamaṇi bhubanamohana beśa biracita bibāha-bihita sumṛdula tanu chabi chalakāya |*
*koṭi manamatha-garaba-bhañjana kañjadiṭhi jana-hṛdaya-rañjana cāhi diśa cahu hāsi lahu lahu caṛhata caudala jhalakāya ||*

*Word for word:* āju godhūli samaya śubhakṣaṇa — today at the auspicious hour of dusk; gaura guṇamaṇi — Gaura, the jewel of virtues; bhubana-mohana — enchanter of the world; beśa biracita bibāha-bihita — in the attire enjoined for a wedding; sumṛdula tanu chabi chalakāya — the beauty of His tender body brims over; koṭi manamatha-garaba-bhañjana — crusher of the pride of millions of Kamas; kañja-diṭhi — lotus-eyed; jana-hṛdaya-rañjana — delighting people's hearts; cāhi diśa cahu — looking in the four directions; hāsi lahu lahu — smiling softly; caṛhata caudala — mounts the palanquin; jhalakāya — shining

**6.1.** Today, at the auspicious hour of dusk, Gaura — the jewel of virtues, enchanter of the world — is in the attire enjoined for a wedding,
and the beauty of His tender body seems to brim over;
crushing the pride of millions of Kamas, lotus-eyed, delighting people's hearts, glancing in all four directions with a soft smile, He mounts
the palanquin, shining.[^21-13]

চলত বল্লভ-ভবন ভূসুর বেঢ়ি গতি অতি মন্দ সুমধুর বন্দীগণ ভূরি মঙ্গল ভণ ভুবন ভরু জয় জয় ধ্বনি ।
নটত নটগণ উঘটি থৈ তত থোঙ্গ থোঙ্গিন গান রত কত বিরচি রুচির চরিত্র স্বর সাঞ সরস রস বরষত গুণী ॥

*calata ballabha-bhabana bhūsura beṛhi gati ati manda sumadhura bandīgaṇa bhūri maṅgala bhaṇa bhubana bharu jaya jaya dhvani |*
*naṭata naṭagaṇa ughaṭi thai tata thoṅga thoṅgina gāna rata kata biraci rucira caritra svara sāña sarasa rasa baraṣata guṇī ||*

*Word for word:* calata ballabha-bhabana — He moves towards Vallabha's house; bhūsura beṛhi — surrounded by brahmanas; gati ati manda sumadhura — the gait very slow and sweet; bandīgaṇa bhūri maṅgala bhaṇa — the bards proclaim abundant blessings; bhubana bharu jaya jaya dhvani — cries of "jaya, jaya" fill the world; naṭata naṭagaṇa — the dancers dance; ughaṭi thai tata — beating out "thai-tata"; thoṅga thoṅgina gāna rata kata — how many are absorbed in song to "thonga-thongina"; biraci rucira caritra — composing lovely [songs of His] deeds; svara sāñja — tuning the mode; sarasa rasa baraṣata guṇī — the artists rain down sweet rasa

**6.2.** Surrounded by brahmanas He moves towards Vallabha's house — His gait very slow and sweet; the bards proclaim abundant blessings, the
world is filled with cries of "jaya, jaya";
dancers dance, beating out "thai-tata", how many singers are absorbed in song to "thonga-thongina"; composing lovely [songs on His] deeds,
tuning the mode, the artists rain down sweet rasa.

বাদ্য কত কত ভাঁতি বায়ত বাদ্য পাঠ অভঙ্গ ভায়ত সুঘর বাদক-বৃন্দ বাদ্য-সমুদ্র মথি জনু সন্তরে ।
গগনে সুরগণ মগন অতিশয় সঘনে অনিমিখ নয়নে নিরখয় বিপুল পুলক অলক্ষ ক্ষিতি উতরত কি কৌতুক অন্তরে ॥

*bādya kata kata bhām̐ti bāyata bādya pāṭha abhaṅga bhāyata sughara bādaka-bṛnda bādya-samudra mathi janu santare |*
*gagane suragaṇa magana atiśaya saghane animikha nayane nirakhaya bipula pulaka alakṣa kṣiti utarata ki kautuka antare ||*

*Word for word:* bādya kata kata bhām̐ti bāyata — how many instruments play in every manner; bādya pāṭha abhaṅga bhāyata — the rhythmic syllables sound unbroken; sughara bādaka-bṛnda — skilled musicians; bādya-samudra mathi — churning the ocean of music; janu santare — as if swim; gagane suragaṇa — in the sky the gods; magana atiśaya — utterly absorbed; saghane animikha nayane nirakhaya — gaze steadily with unblinking eyes; bipula pulaka — with great thrill; alakṣa kṣiti utarata — descend unseen to earth; ki kautuka antare — what delight within

**6.3.** How many instruments play in every manner, the rhythmic syllables sound without a break; skilled musicians, as if churning the ocean of
music, swim in it;
in the sky the gods are utterly absorbed — they gaze steadily with unblinking eyes; thrilling all over they descend unseen to earth — what
delight in their hearts!

নারী পুরুষ অসংখ্য ধায়ত প্রসর পথ নিরুপম সুহায়ত দীপ শত শত উজোর যামিনীনাথ-কর পরকাশই ।
ধরণী অধিক উছাহে প্রফুল্লিত জাহ্নবী-জল ভেল উছলিত দাস নরহরি কহব কিয়ে পশু পাখী সব সুখে ভাসই ॥

*nārī puruṣa asaṃkhya dhāyata prasara patha nirupama suhāyata dīpa śata śata ujora yāminīnātha-kara parakāśai |*
*dharaṇī adhika uchāhe praphullita jāhnabī-jala bhela uchalita dāsa narahari kahaba kiye paśu pākhī saba sukhe bhāsai ||*

*Word for word:* nārī puruṣa asaṃkhya dhāyata — countless men and women run; prasara patha nirupama suhāyata — the broad road is incomparably lovely; dīpa śata śata ujora — hundreds upon hundreds of lamps blaze; yāminī-nātha-kara parakāśai — the rays of the lord of night (the moon) shine; dharaṇī adhika uchāhe praphullita — the Earth has blossomed in great joy; jāhnabī-jala bhela uchalita — the waters of the Jahnavi surge; dāsa narahari kahaba kiye — what will the servant Narahari say; paśu pākhī saba sukhe bhāsai — beasts and birds all float in happiness

**6.4.** Countless men and women run; the broad road is incomparably beautiful; hundreds upon hundreds of lamps blaze, the moon, lord of the
night, sheds its light;
the Earth has blossomed in great joy, the waters of the Jahnavi surge; what can the servant Narahari say? — beasts and birds all float in
happiness.

[^21-12]: GPT1 — p. 87, no. 21 (bhupali; scan, PDF p. 346); GPT2 — section 2.3, no. 21 (catalogue: NG-038). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, pp. 792–793; ed. 1960,
vv. 1309–1312). Variants: 6.1 GPT1 "chalakāya", "jhalakāya", BR "chalakaye", "jhalakaye"; 6.2 GPT1 "bandīgaṇa, bhuri maṅgalabhaṇa", BR "bandigaṇa bhaṇa bhuri maṅgala"; 6.3 GPT1
"janu", BR "yanu" (both "as if"). Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. The syllables "thai-tata",
"thonga-thongina" imitate the dancers' counting and the strokes of the drums (cf. note 11 of chapter 20).
[^21-13]: Dusk (godhūli, "the hour of cow-dust", when the herds return home) is an auspicious hour for a wedding. The palanquin (caudola) is the litter
on which the bridegroom is carried to the bride's house. The wedding with Lakshmipriya takes place in the house of her father, Vallabha
Acharya (CB Adi 10).

## 7. Narahari — "gorācām̐dera bibāha dekhibāre…" (GPT1 pp. 87–88, no. 22; BR)
*The young wives of Nadia, in fine dress and ornaments, their bells ringing, hurry to see Gorachand's wedding; they talk among themselves,
smiling under their veils; their glances dart in all directions; seeing the poet's Lord enter Vallabha's house, they are beside themselves
with joy. Raga bhupali. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^21-14]

গোরাচাঁদের বিবাহ দেখিবারে । কত না মনের সাধে ধায় নদীয়ার নববধূগণ ধৈরজ ধরিতে কেউ নারে ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*gorācām̐dera bibāha dekhibāre | kata nā manera sādhe dhāya nadīyāra nababadhūgaṇa dhairaja dharite keu nāre || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* gorācām̐dera bibāha dekhibāre — to see Gorachand's wedding; kata nā manera sādhe — with what longing of heart; dhāya — run; nadīyāra nababadhū-gaṇa — the young wives of Nadia; dhairaja dharite keu nāre — none can keep composure

**7.1.** To see Gorachand's wedding, with what longing the young wives of Nadia run — not one can keep her composure!

নিরুপম বেশবাস ভূষণে ভূষিত তনু ঝলমল করে সে ভঙ্গিমা শোহে ভালো ।
চলিতে বাজয়ে কটি-কিঙ্কিণী নূপুর পদে সুমধুর গমন করয় পথ আলো ॥

*nirupama beśabāsa bhūṣaṇe bhūṣita tanu jhalamala kare se bhaṅgimā śohe bhālo |*
*calite bājaye kaṭi-kiṅkiṇī nūpura pade sumadhura gamana karaya patha ālo ||*

*Word for word:* nirupama beśa-bāsa — incomparable attire and garments; bhūṣaṇe bhūṣita tanu — bodies adorned with ornaments; jhalamala kare — glitters; se bhaṅgimā śohe bhālo — that charm shines beautifully; calite bājaye — as they walk there ring; kaṭi-kiṅkiṇī — the bells of their girdles; nūpura pade — the anklets on their feet; sumadhura gamana — with sweet gait; karaya patha ālo — they light up the road

**7.2.** Incomparable attire and garments, bodies adorned with ornaments — their charm glitters and shines;
as they walk, the bells of their girdles and the anklets on their feet ring; with their sweet gait they light up the road.

সে রস-আবেশে পরস্পর কত কয় কিবা সুললিত বেসর দোলয়ে নাসামূলে ।
ঘুঙটে আবৃত মঞ্জুমুখে মৃদু মৃদু হাসি হাসি-ছটা ঘটায় কেবা বা নাহি ভুলে ॥

*se rasa-ābeśe paraspara kata kaya kibā sulalita besara dolaye nāsāmūle |*
*ghuṅaṭe ābṛta mañjumukhe mṛdu mṛdu hāsi hāsi-chaṭā ghaṭāya kebā bā nāhi bhule ||*

*Word for word:* se rasa-ābeśe — absorbed in that feeling; paraspara kata kaya — how much they say to one another; kibā sulalita — how charmingly; besara dolaye nāsāmūle — the nose-rings sway at the nostrils; ghuṅaṭe ābṛta mañju-mukhe — on lovely faces hidden by veils; mṛdu mṛdu hāsi — a soft, soft smile; hāsi-chaṭā ghaṭāya — by the radiance of the smile; kebā vā nāhi bhule — who is not enchanted

**7.3.** Absorbed in that feeling, how much they say to one another — how charmingly! — the rings at their nostrils sway;
on their lovely faces hidden by veils, a soft, soft smile; whom would the radiance of that smile not enchant?

অঞ্জনে রঞ্জিত মনোরঞ্জন খঞ্জনপাখী জিনি মঞ্জু নয়ন-চাহনি চারি ভিতে ।
নরহরি-পরাণনাথেরে নিরখিয়া হিয়া উথলয়ে বল্লভ-ভবন প্রবেশিতে ॥

*añjane rañjita manorañjana khañjanapākhī jini mañju nayana-cāhani cāri bhite |*
*narahari-parāṇanāthere nirakhiyā hiyā uthalaye ballabha-bhabana prabeśite ||*

*Word for word:* añjane rañjita — darkened with collyrium; mano-rañjana — delighting the heart; khañjana-pākhī jini — surpassing the khanjana bird; mañju nayana-cāhani — lovely glances of the eyes; cāri bhite — on every side; narahari-parāṇa-nāthere nirakhiyā — seeing Narahari's Lord of life; hiyā uthalaye — the heart overflows; ballabha-bhabana prabeśite — as He enters Vallabha's house

**7.4.** Darkened with collyrium, delighting the heart, surpassing the khanjana bird, their lovely glances [dart] on every side;
and, seeing Narahari's Lord of life entering Vallabha's house, they are beside themselves with joy.[^21-15]

[^21-14]: GPT1 — pp. 87–88, no. 22 (bhupali; scan, PDF pp. 346–347); GPT2 — section 2.3, no. 22 (catalogue: NG-039). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 793; ed.
1960, vv. 1313–1316). Variants: 7.4 GPT1 "uthalaye", BR-1960 "ulaye" (OCR?); 7.3 GPT1 "beśara", BR "besara" (the same word, "nose-ring"). Not in PK, KGC, PS,
the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. Line 7.1 is the refrain (dhru).
[^21-15]: The khanjana is the wagtail, in Indian poetry an image of lively, restless eyes. "Narahari's Lord of life" (narahari parāṇanātha) is the poet's Lord, a
turn of the signature (like "Narahari's Lord", note 34 of chapter 20); the young wives' joy is festive delight at the wedding (see note 5).

## 8. Narahari — "ballabha-bhabane gorā rāya…" (GPT1 pp. 88–89, no. 23; BR)
*The wedding in Vallabha's house: Vishvambhara stands on a little board under the wedding canopy; the bride's mother with the married women
welcomes the bridegroom, circling Him seven times with seven lamps; Vallabha Acharya brings his daughter, seats her on a throne and by the
rite gives Lakshmi to the son of Shachi; Vedic chanting, cries of joy, music; from their celestial chariots the gods invisibly shower the
wedding with flowers. Raga kamoda. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^21-16]

বল্লভ-ভবনে গোরা রায় । বল্লভ মিশ্রের মহা আনন্দ বাঢ়ায় ॥

*ballabha-bhabane gorā rāya | ballabha miśrera mahā ānanda bāṛhāya ||*

*Word for word:* ballabha-bhabane — in Vallabha's house; gorā rāya — Gora Raya; ballabha miśrera — of Vallabha Mishra; mahā ānanda bāṛhāya — increases the great joy

**8.1.** Gora Raya in Vallabha's house increases the great joy of Vallabha Mishra.

বল্লভ হইয়া উল্লসিত । করায় মঙ্গল কার্য্য বিবাহ-বিহিত ॥

*ballabha haiyā ullasita | karāya maṅgala kāryya bibāha-bihita ||*

*Word for word:* ballabha haiyā ullasita — Vallabha, rejoicing; karāya maṅgala kāryya — has the auspicious rites performed; bibāha-bihita — enjoined for a wedding

**8.2.** Vallabha, rejoicing, has the auspicious rites enjoined for a wedding performed.

বিশ্বম্ভর হরষ হিয়ায় । দাঁড়াইলা পিড়ির উপরে ছোড়লায় ॥

*biśvambhara haraṣa hiyāya | dām̐ṛāilā piṛira upare choṛalāya ||*

*Word for word:* biśvambhara — Vishvambhara; haraṣa hiyāya — with a glad heart; dām̐ṛāilā — stood; piṛira upare — on the little board; choṛalāya — at the place of the rite under the canopy

**8.3.** Vishvambhara, His heart glad, stood on the little board under the wedding canopy.[^21-17]

অঙ্গের ভঙ্গীতে প্রাণ হরে । রূপের ছটায় দশদিক আলো করে ॥

*aṅgera bhaṅgīte prāṇa hare | rūpera chaṭāya daśadika ālo kare ||*

*Word for word:* aṅgera bhaṅgīte — by the movements of His body; prāṇa hare — He steals life; rūpera chaṭāya — by the radiance of His form; daśa-dik ālo kare — lights up the ten directions

**8.4.** The movements of His body steal one's life; the radiance of His form lights up the ten directions.

চাঁদমুখে উপমা কি দিতে । অমিয়া-গরব নাশে ঈষৎ হাসিতে ॥

*cām̐damukhe upamā ki dite | amiyā-garaba nāśe īṣat hāsite ||*

*Word for word:* cām̐da-mukhe — to the moonlike face; upamā ki dite — what comparison to give; amiyā-garaba nāśe — destroys the pride of nectar; īṣat hāsite — with a slight smile

**8.5.** To what shall His moonlike face be compared? With a slight smile it destroys the pride of nectar.

নয়ন চাহনি চারু ছাঁদে । যার পানে চায় সে ধৈরজ নাহি বাঁধে ॥

*nayana cāhani cāru chām̐de | yāra pāne cāya se dhairaja nāhi bām̐dhe ||*

*Word for word:* nayana cāhani — the glance of His eyes; cāru chām̐de — is lovely; yāra pāne cāya — whomever He looks at; se dhairaja nāhi bām̐dhe — cannot hold his composure

**8.6.** The glance of His eyes is lovely: whomever He looks at cannot hold his composure.

মকর-কুণ্ডল শ্রুতিমূলে । চাঁচর কেশের বেশে কে বা নাহি ভুলে ॥

*makara-kuṇḍala śrutimūle | cām̐cara keśera beśe ke bā nāhi bhule ||*

*Word for word:* makara-kuṇḍala — makara-shaped earrings; śruti-mūle — at the roots of the ears; cām̐cara keśera beśe — by the arrangement of the curling hair; ke vā nāhi bhule — who is not enchanted

**8.7.** At the roots of His ears, makara-shaped earrings; whom would the arrangement of His curling hair not enchant?

অঙ্গদ বলয় ভাল সাজে । শোভা দেখি কত না মদন মরে লাজে ॥

*aṅgada balaya bhāla sāje | śobhā dekhi kata nā madana mare lāje ||*

*Word for word:* aṅgada balaya — armlets and bracelets; bhāla sāje — sit beautifully; śobhā dekhi — seeing the beauty; kata nā madana mare lāje — how many Madanas die of shame

**8.8.** Armlets and bracelets sit beautifully; seeing that beauty, how many Madanas die of shame!

এহেন বরেরে উরুথিতে । কন্যার জননী চলে আয়োগণ সাতে ॥

*ehena barere uruthite | kanyāra jananī cale āyogaṇa sāte ||*

*Word for word:* e-hena barere — such a bridegroom; urukhite — to welcome (the rite of receiving the bridegroom); kanyāra jananī — the bride's mother; cale āyo-gaṇa sāte — goes with the married women

**8.9.** To welcome such a bridegroom, the bride's mother comes out with the married women.

সে শোভা কহিতে কেবা পারে । সপ্তদীপ হাতে সপ্তপ্রদক্ষিণ করে ॥

*se śobhā kahite kebā pāre | saptadīpa hāte saptapradakṣiṇa kare ||*

*Word for word:* se śobhā kahite kebā pāre — who can describe that beauty; sapta-dīpa hāte — with seven lamps in hand; sapta-pradakṣiṇa kare — she circles seven times

**8.10.** Who can describe that beauty? With seven lamps in her hands she circles Him seven times.

পরম অদ্ভুত স্ত্রী-আচার । বর উরথিয়া ঘরে গমন সবার ॥

*parama adbhuta strī-ācāra | bara urathiyā ghare gamana sabāra ||*

*Word for word:* parama adbhuta strī-ācāra — wondrous are the women's rites; bara urathiyā — having welcomed the bridegroom; ghare gamana sabāra — all go into the house

**8.11.** Wondrous are the women's rites! Having welcomed the bridegroom, all go into the house.

বল্লভ আচার্য্য ভাগ্যবান্ । আনাইলা কন্যায় করিতে কন্যাদান ॥

*ballabha ācāryya bhāgyabān | ānāilā kanyāya karite kanyādāna ||*

*Word for word:* ballabha ācāryya bhāgyabān — fortunate Vallabha Acharya; ānāilā kanyāya — had his daughter brought; karite kanyā-dāna — to perform the kanya-dana

**8.12.** Fortunate Vallabha Acharya had his daughter brought to perform the kanya-dana — the giving of the daughter.

বসাইলা দিব্য সিংহাসনে । হইল উজ্জ্বল মহা অঙ্গের কিরণে ॥

*basāilā dibya siṃhāsane | haila ujjvala mahā aṅgera kiraṇe ||*

*Word for word:* basāilā dibya siṃhāsane — they seated her on a divine throne; haila ujjvala mahā — it shone brightly; aṅgera kiraṇe — with the radiance of her body

**8.13.** They seated her on a divine throne — and it shone with the radiance of her body.

অতি সুকোমল তনুখানি । হাসিমাখা বদন পূর্ণিমাচাঁদ জিনি ॥

*ati sukomala tanukhāni | hāsimākhā badana pūrṇimācām̐da jini ||*

*Word for word:* ati sukomala tanu-khāni — her body is very tender; hāsi-mākhā badana — her smiling face; pūrṇimā-cām̐da jini — surpasses the full moon

**8.14.** Her body is so tender, her smiling face surpasses the full moon.

পরিধেয় বিচিত্র বসন । ঝলমল করে নানা রত্ন-আভরণ ॥

*paridheya bicitra basana | jhalamala kare nānā ratna-ābharaṇa ||*

*Word for word:* paridheya bicitra basana — her garments are many-coloured; jhalamala kare — glitter; nānā ratna-ābharaṇa — ornaments of many jewels

**8.15.** She wears many-coloured garments; ornaments of many jewels glitter.

হেন কন্যা বিবিধ বিধানে । করিল প্রদান মিশ্র শচীর নন্দনে ॥

*hena kanyā bibidha bidhāne | karila pradāna miśra śacīra nandane ||*

*Word for word:* hena kanyā — such a daughter; bibidha bidhāne — with every prescribed rite; karila pradāna miśra — Mishra gave; śacīra nandane — to the son of Shachi

**8.16.** Such a daughter, with every prescribed rite, Mishra gave to the son of Shachi.[^21-18]

বিপ্রগণে করে বেদধ্বনি । উলু লু লু দেই যত কুলের কামিনী ॥

*bipragaṇe kare bedadhvani | ulu lu lu dei yata kulera kāminī ||*

*Word for word:* bipragaṇe kare beda-dhvani — the brahmanas chant the Vedas; ulu lu lu dei — cry "ulu-lu"; yata kulera kāminī — all the women of noble families

**8.17.** The brahmanas chant the Vedas; all the women of noble families cry "ulu-lu".

বাজে বাদ্য বিবিধ প্রকার । নাচয়ে নর্ত্তক ভাট পড়ে কায়বার ॥

*bāje bādya bibidha prakāra | nācaye narttaka bhāṭa paṛe kāyabāra ||*

*Word for word:* bāje bādya bibidha prakāra — instruments of every kind resound; nācaye narttaka — the dancers dance; bhāṭa paṛe kāyabāra — the bhatas recite verses of praise

**8.18.** Instruments of every kind resound, dancers dance, the bhatas recite verses of praise.

দেবগণ বিমানে চড়িয়া । বরিষে কুসুম অলখিতে জয় দিয়া ॥

*debagaṇa bimāne caṛiyā | bariṣe kusuma alakhite jaya diyā ||*

*Word for word:* deba-gaṇa bimāne caṛiyā — the gods, mounting celestial chariots; bariṣe kusuma — shower flowers; alakhite — invisibly; jaya diyā — crying "jaya"

**8.19.** The gods, mounting their celestial chariots, invisibly shower flowers, crying "jaya!".

ভুবন ব্যাপিল মহাসুখে । নরহরি কত না কহিব এক মুখে ॥

*bhubana byāpila mahāsukhe | narahari kata nā kahiba eka mukhe ||*

*Word for word:* bhubana byāpila mahāsukhe — great happiness pervaded the world; narahari kata nā kahiba — how much can Narahari tell; eka mukhe — with one mouth

**8.20.** Great happiness has spread through the world — how can Narahari tell of it with one mouth?

[^21-16]: GPT1 — pp. 88–89, no. 23 (kamoda; scan, PDF pp. 347–348); GPT2 — section 2.3, no. 23 (catalogue: NG-040). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, pp. 794–795; ed.
1960, vv. 1317–1336). Variants: 8.3 GPT1 "sarasa hiyāya" ("with a heart full of rasa"), BR "haraṣa hiyāya" ("with a glad heart"); 8.9 GPT1 "āyogaṇa sāte", BR
"āigaṇa sāthe" (the same: married women); 8.17 GPT1 "kulera kāminī", BR "kulera ramaṇī"; 8.18 BR "rāyabāra". The GPT1 editor's notes on 8.3 and 8.9 are not
reproduced. Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B.
[^21-17]: The piri (piṛi) is a low wooden board on which the bridegroom stands or sits during the rite; choṛalā is the place of the wedding rite under the
canopy.
[^21-18]: Kanya-dana is the central rite of a Hindu wedding: the father gives his daughter to the bridegroom. The Lord's wedding with Lakshmipriya —
CB Adi 10; CC Adi 15. Lakshmipriya is Lakshmi Herself, the eternal energy of the Lord; the marriage is His lila (note 2).

## 9. Narahari — "gorā guṇamaṇi prāṇapriyā saha…" (GPT1 p. 89, no. 24; BR)
*The bridal chamber: Gora is in the chamber with His beloved; the women keep coming in and going out, joke, give Him betel to put into
Lakshmi's mouth, themselves offer Him betel, braid and loosen His hair, seat Lakshmi on His lap. Raga bhupali. **Attribution: probably
Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^21-19]

গোরা গুণমণি প্রাণপ্রিয়া সহ বিলসয়ে সে যে বাসর ঘরে ।
কুলবধূগণ ঘন ঘন করু গতাগতি কত কৌতুক ভরে ॥

*gorā guṇamaṇi prāṇapriyā saha bilasaye se ye bāsara ghare |*
*kulabadhūgaṇa ghana ghana karu gatāgati kata kautuka bhare ||*

*Word for word:* gorā guṇamaṇi — Gora, the jewel of virtues; prāṇa-priyā saha — with His beloved, dear as life; bilasaye se ye bāsara ghare — passes the time in the bridal chamber; kulabadhū-gaṇa — the wives of noble families; ghana ghana karu gatāgati — keep coming and going; kata kautuka bhare — full of merriment

**9.1.** Gora, the jewel of virtues, with His beloved, dear as life, passes the time in the bridal chamber;
the wives of noble families keep coming in and going out, full of merriment.

কেহ নানা ছল করি পরিহাস করে হাসি হাসি মনের সুখে ।
কেহ গোরা-কর-কমলে তাম্বূল দিয়া কহে দেহ লক্ষ্মীর মুখে ॥

*keha nānā chala kari parihāsa kare hāsi hāsi manera sukhe |*
*keha gorā-kara-kamale tāmbūla diyā kahe deha lakṣmīra mukhe ||*

*Word for word:* keha nānā chala kari — some, inventing various pretexts; parihāsa kare — tease; hāsi hāsi manera sukhe — laughing for the joy of their hearts; keha gorā-kara-kamale tāmbūla diyā — another, putting betel in Gora's lotus hand; kahe deha lakṣmīra mukhe — says, "put it into Lakshmi's mouth"

**9.2.** Some, inventing various pretexts, tease and laugh, laugh for the joy of their hearts;
another, placing betel in Gora's lotus hand, says, "Put it into Lakshmi's mouth!"

কেহ গোরা-বিধুবদনে তাম্বূল দিতে দিতে বহু বাঢ়য়ে প্রীতি ।
কেহ পরশের সাধে বাঁধে কেশ আউলাইতে নারে ধরিতে ধৃতি ॥

*keha gorā-bidhubadane tāmbūla dite dite bahu bāṛhaye prīti |*
*keha paraśera sādhe bām̐dhe keśa āulāite nāre dharite dhṛti ||*

*Word for word:* keha gorā-bidhu-badane — one to Gora's moonlike mouth; tāmbūla dite dite — offering betel; bahu bāṛhaye prīti — affection grows greatly; keha paraśera sādhe — another, longing to touch; bām̐dhe keśa — braids His hair; āulāite — loosening it; nāre dharite dhṛti — cannot contain herself

**9.3.** One offers betel to Gora's moonlike mouth — and her affection grows and grows;
another, longing to touch Him, braids His hair — and, loosening it, cannot contain herself.

কেহ বিশ্বম্ভর-কোলে লখিমীরে বসাইয়া চারু ভঙ্গীতে চাহে ।
ভণে নরহরি বাসরে যে রস উথলয়ে নাহি উপমা তাহে ॥

*keha biśvambhara-kole lakhimīre basāiyā cāru bhaṅgīte cāhe |*
*bhaṇe narahari bāsare ye rasa uthalaye nāhi upamā tāhe ||*

*Word for word:* keha biśvambhara-kole — another on Vishvambhara's lap; lakhimīre basāiyā — seating Lakshmi; cāru bhaṅgīte cāhe — looks with a charming manner; bhaṇe narahari — says Narahari; bāsare ye rasa uthalaye — the rasa that surges in the bridal chamber; nāhi upamā tāhe — has no comparison

**9.4.** Yet another, seating Lakshmi on Vishvambhara's lap, looks at them with a charming smile;
says Narahari: the rasa that surges in the bridal chamber has no comparison.[^21-20]

[^21-19]: GPT1 — p. 89, no. 24 (bhupali; scan, PDF p. 348); GPT2 — section 2.3, no. 24 (catalogue: NG-041). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 795; ed. 1960, vv.
1337–1340). Variant: 9.1 GPT1 "śoja" (misprint), BR "se ye" — following the BR. Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B.
[^21-20]: Vasara (bāsara) is the first night after the wedding, which the couple spend in the chamber while the women of the bride's house keep them awake
joking with the bridegroom — a custom of the Bengali wedding. The women's jokes at the wedding are ritual merriment, not nagari-bhava;
Lakshmipriya is the eternal energy of the Lord (note 2), and the whole scene is the Lord's lila with His energy, not worldly love.

## 10. Narahari — "gorācām̐dera bibāha paradine…" (GPT1 p. 89, no. 25; BR)
*At dawn after the wedding the women run together to admire bride and bridegroom; Vallabha's fortunate wife rejoices; generous Vallabha
Mishra does everything for his son-in-law; Gaurahari, having performed the wedding rites, is glad; the gods praise Vallabha. Raga todi.
**Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^21-21]

গোরাচাঁদের বিবাহ পরদিনে । কত আনন্দ উথলে তায় রজনী বিহানে ॥

*gorācām̐dera bibāha paradine | kata ānanda uthale tāya rajanī bihāne ||*

*Word for word:* gorācām̐dera bibāha paradine — the day after Gorachand's wedding; kata ānanda uthale tāya — how much joy surges then; rajanī bihāne — at daybreak

**10.1.** The day after Gorachand's wedding, at daybreak — how much joy surges up!

কুলবধূগণ চারিদিকে ধায় । দেখি বর-কন্যা-শোভা সবে নয়ন জুড়ায় ॥

*kulabadhūgaṇa cāridike dhāya | dekhi bara-kanyā-śobhā sabe nayana juṛāya ||*

*Word for word:* kulabadhū-gaṇa cāridike dhāya — the wives of noble families run from every side; dekhi bara-kanyā-śobhā — seeing the beauty of bridegroom and bride; sabe nayana juṛāya — all delight their eyes

**10.2.** The wives of noble families run together from every side; seeing the beauty of bride and bridegroom, all delight their eyes.

কিবা বল্লভ-ঘরণী ভাগ্যবতী । পাইয়া জামাতারত্ন না জানয়ে আছে কতি ॥

*kibā ballabha-gharaṇī bhāgyabatī | pāiyā jāmātāratna nā jānaye āche kati ||*

*Word for word:* kibā ballabha-gharaṇī bhāgyabatī — how fortunate is Vallabha's wife; pāiyā jāmātā-ratna — having gained a jewel of a son-in-law; nā jānaye āche kati — does not know where she is

**10.3.** How fortunate is Vallabha's wife! Having gained a jewel of a son-in-law, she does not know where she is.

মিশ্র বল্লভ উদার অতিশয় । নিজ জামাতা-মঙ্গল-হেতু কিবা না করয় ॥

*miśra ballabha udāra atiśaya | nija jāmātā-maṅgala-hetu kibā nā karaya ||*

*Word for word:* miśra ballabha — Mishra Vallabha; udāra atiśaya — is generous beyond measure; nija jāmātā-maṅgala-hetu — for the good of his son-in-law; kibā nā karaya — what does he not do

**10.4.** Mishra Vallabha is generous beyond measure: what does he not do for the good of his son-in-law!

ভালে বল্লভ-জামাতা গৌরহরি । হর্ষ হইলেন বিবাহ-বিহিত কর্ম্ম করি ॥

*bhāle ballabha-jāmātā gaurahari | harṣa hailena bibāha-bihita karmma kari ||*

*Word for word:* bhāle — and so; ballabha-jāmātā gaurahari — Vallabha's son-in-law Gaurahari; harṣa hailena — became joyful; bibāha-bihita karmma kari — having performed the wedding rites

**10.5.** And Vallabha's son-in-law, Gaurahari, having performed the wedding rites, is filled with joy.

কৈল কার্য্য সমাধান সুবিধানে । নরহরি কহে বল্লভে প্রশংসে দেবগণে ॥

*kaila kāryya samādhāna subidhāne | narahari kahe ballabhe praśaṃse debagaṇe ||*

*Word for word:* kaila kāryya samādhāna — completed the tasks; subidhāne — properly; narahari kahe — says Narahari; ballabhe praśaṃse debagaṇe — the gods praise Vallabha

**10.6.** All has been completed as is proper; says Narahari: the gods praise Vallabha.

[^21-21]: GPT1 — p. 89, no. 25 (todi; scan, PDF p. 348); GPT2 — section 2.3, no. 25 (catalogue: NG-042). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, pp. 795–796; ed. 1960, vv.
1341–1346; the catalogue and the chapter plan took it for "GPT only" — the search by witnesses missed it because of garbled OCR; it was found by
reading the BR straight through). Variant: 10.3 GPT1 "jāmātāratna", BR "jāmātā-ratana" (the same). Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or
the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B.

## 11. Narahari — "gaura gokulacandra calu nija gehe…" (GPT1 p. 89, no. 26; BR)
*At dawn Gaura sets out for His home; Vallabha in private speaks lovingly to Him of Lakshmi; the women on the road weep, Lakshmi's friends
know that her Lord is departing; conches, kettledrums, dancing, songs, Vedic chanting, praises — the world is full of cries of "jaya". Raga
todi. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR; Vrajabuli.*[^21-22]

গৌর গোকুলচন্দ্র চলু নিজ গেহে নিশি পরভাত ।
বিরলে বল্লভ স্নেহে কহি কত কহল লখিমীক বাত ॥

*gaura gokulacandra calu nija gehe niśi parabhāta |*
*birale ballabha snehe kahi kata kahala lakhimīka bāta ||*

*Word for word:* gaura gokula-candra — Gaura, the Moon of Gokula; calu nija gehe — set out for His home; niśi parabhāta — when night turned to dawn; birale ballabha — in private Vallabha; snehe kahi kata — tenderly saying much; kahala lakhimīka bāta — spoke of Lakshmi

**11.1.** When the night gave way to dawn, Gaura, the Moon of Gokula, set out for His own home;
in private Vallabha tenderly said much to Him — he spoke of Lakshmi.

হেরি পথ যত নারী ধৈরজ না ধরই ঝরই নয়ান ।
লখিমী-সহচরী জানে লখিমীক নাথ করব পয়ান ॥

*heri patha yata nārī dhairaja nā dharai jharai nayāna |*
*lakhimī-sahacarī jāne lakhimīka nātha karaba payāna ||*

*Word for word:* heri patha — looking at the road; yata nārī — all the women; dhairaja nā dharai — cannot restrain themselves; jharai nayāna — tears stream from the eyes; lakhimī-sahacarī — Lakshmi's friends; jāne — know; lakhimīka nātha — Lakshmi's Lord; karaba payāna — will depart

**11.2.** Looking at the road, all the women cannot restrain themselves — tears stream from their eyes:
Lakshmi's friends know that Lakshmi's Lord is departing.[^21-23]

শঙ্খ দুন্দুভি ভেরী বাজত বাদ্য বিবিধ প্রকার ।
নটত নর্ত্তকবৃন্দ গায়ত গীত গুণী অনিবার ॥

*śaṅkha dundubhi bherī bājata bādya bibidha prakāra |*
*naṭata narttakabṛnda gāyata gīta guṇī anibāra ||*

*Word for word:* śaṅkha dundubhi bherī bājata — conches, kettledrums and great drums sound; bādya bibidha prakāra — instruments of every kind; naṭata narttaka-bṛnda — troupes of dancers dance; gāyata gīta guṇī anibāra — skilled singers sing songs without end

**11.3.** Conches, kettledrums and great drums sound, instruments of every kind;
troupes of dancers dance, skilled singers sing songs without end.

বেদ উচরত বিপ্রগণ গুণ বন্দী করু পরকাশ ।
ভুবন ভরি জয় জয় কি নরহরি ভবন পহুঁক বিলাস ॥

*beda ucarata bipragaṇa guṇa bandī karu parakāśa |*
*bhubana bhari jaya jaya ki narahari bhabana pahum̐ka bilāsa ||*

*Word for word:* beda ucarata bipragaṇa — the brahmanas chant the Vedas; guṇa bandī karu parakāśa — the bards proclaim [His] virtues; bhubana bhari jaya jaya — the world full of "jaya, jaya"; ki — what; narahari bhabana pahum̐ka bilāsa — the pastime of Narahari's Lord [going] home

**11.4.** The brahmanas chant the Vedas, the bards proclaim His virtues;
the whole world is full of cries of "jaya, jaya" — what a pastime of Narahari's Lord [returning] home!

[^21-22]: GPT1 — p. 89, no. 26 (todi; scan, PDF p. 348); GPT2 — section 2.3, no. 26 (catalogue: NG-043). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 796; ed. 1960, vv.
1347–1350). Variants: 11.1 GPT1 "kahala lakhimī ki bāta", BR "kahala lakhimika bāta" ("spoke of Lakshmi") — following the BR; 11.2 GPT1 "karaba payāna" ("will depart"),
BR "kayala payāna" ("departed"). Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B.
[^21-23]: By custom the bride leaves her father's house after the wedding for her husband's house; the father entrusts his daughter to his son-in-law,
and her friends lament the parting.

## 12. Narahari — "bibāha kariyā biśvambhara…" (GPT1 p. 90, no. 27; BR)
*Vishvambhara returns home with His young wife; the married women perform auspicious rites; Shachi, taking her daughter-in-law on her lap,
blesses her with paddy and durva grass and gazes again and again at the faces of her son and daughter-in-law; the Lord gladdens everyone
with sweet words and fulfils the wishes of the bhatas, dancers and musicians. Raga kamoda. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada
is in the BR.*[^21-24]

বিবাহ করিয়া বিশ্বম্ভর । শ্বশুরালয় হৈতে আইল নিজঘর ॥

*bibāha kariyā biśvambhara | śvaśurālaya haite āila nijaghara ||*

*Word for word:* bibāha kariyā biśvambhara — having married, Vishvambhara; śvaśurālaya haite — from His father-in-law's house; āila nija-ghara — came to His own home

**12.1.** Having married, Vishvambhara returned from His father-in-law's house to His own home.

যে আনন্দ কহিতে না পারি । করয় মঙ্গল যত পতিব্রতা নারী ॥

*ye ānanda kahite nā pāri | karaya maṅgala yata patibratā nārī ||*

*Word for word:* ye ānanda — that joy; kahite nā pāri — I cannot describe; karaya maṅgala — perform the auspicious rites; yata patibratā nārī — all the women devoted to their husbands

**12.2.** That joy I cannot describe: the women devoted to their husbands perform all the auspicious rites.

শচী পুত্রবধূ কোলে লৈয়া । কৈল আশীর্ব্বাদ বহু ধান্য দূর্ব্বা দিয়া ॥

*śacī putrabadhū kole laiyā | kaila āśīrvvāda bahu dhānya dūrvvā diyā ||*

*Word for word:* śacī putrabadhū kole laiyā — Shachi, taking her daughter-in-law on her lap; kaila āśīrvvāda — blessed her; bahu dhānya dūrvvā diyā — with abundant paddy and durva grass

**12.3.** Shachi, taking her daughter-in-law on her lap, blessed her, [showering her] abundantly with paddy and durva grass.[^21-25]

শ্রীশচী সুখের নাহি পার । পুত্রমুখ বধূমুখ দেখে কত বার ॥

*śrīśacī sukhera nāhi pāra | putramukha badhūmukha dekhe kata bāra ||*

*Word for word:* śrī-śacī sukhera nāhi pāra — there is no limit to Sri Shachi's happiness; putra-mukha badhū-mukha — her son's face, her daughter-in-law's face; dekhe kata bāra — how many times she looks

**12.4.** There is no limit to Sri Shachi's happiness: how many times she looks at her son's face and her daughter-in-law's face!

লক্ষ্মী-বিশ্বম্ভর-শোভা দেখি । কেহ ফিরাইতে নারে অনিমিখ আঁখি ॥

*lakṣmī-biśvambhara-śobhā dekhi | keha phirāite nāre animikha ām̐khi ||*

*Word for word:* lakṣmī-biśvambhara-śobhā dekhi — seeing the beauty of Lakshmi and Vishvambhara; keha phirāite nāre — no one can turn away; animikha ām̐khi — their unblinking eyes

**12.5.** Seeing the beauty of Lakshmi and Vishvambhara, no one can turn away their unblinking eyes.

ভুবনমোহন গোরা রায় । সুমধুর ভাষে পরিতোষয় সবায় ॥

*bhubanamohana gorā rāya | sumadhura bhāṣe paritoṣaya sabāya ||*

*Word for word:* bhubana-mohana gorā rāya — Gora Raya, enchanter of the world; sumadhura bhāṣe — with sweet words; paritoṣaya sabāya — gladdens everyone

**12.6.** Gora Raya, enchanter of the world, gladdens everyone with sweet words.

ভাট নট বাদকাদি যত । করিলেন পূর্ণ সকলের মনোরথ ॥

*bhāṭa naṭa bādakādi yata | karilena pūrṇa sakalera manoratha ||*

*Word for word:* bhāṭa naṭa bādakādi yata — bhatas, dancers, musicians and all the rest; karilena pūrṇa — He fulfilled; sakalera manoratha — the wishes of all

**12.7.** For the bhatas, dancers, musicians and all the rest He fulfilled every wish.

নরহরি কহে উভরায় । দেখি যেন এহেন কৌতুক নদীয়ায় ॥

*narahari kahe ubharāya | dekhi yena ehena kautuka nadīyāya ||*

*Word for word:* narahari kahe ubharāya — Narahari cries aloud; dekhi yena — may I see; e-hena kautuka nadīyāya — such merriment in Nadia

**12.8.** Narahari cries aloud: "Oh, that I might see such merriment in Nadia!"

[^21-24]: GPT1 — p. 90, no. 27 (kamoda; scan, PDF p. 349); GPT2 — section 2.3, no. 27 (catalogue: NG-044). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 796; ed. 1960, vv.
1351–1358). Variant: 12.4 GPT1 "śrīśacī sukhera nāhi pāra… dekhe kata bāra", BR "śrīśacī-snehera nāi pāra… cumbe kata bāra" ("there is no limit to Shachi's
tenderness… how many times she kisses"). In the BR, straight after the pada, Ishana tells Srinivasa: "I saw this wedding merriment with my own eyes"
(v. 1359) — whereas the signature of the pada voices the poet's wish to see such merriment (12.8): so might speak a poet who had not seen the
wedding — one more argument for Chakravarti. Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B.
[^21-25]: Paddy and durva grass (dhānya dūrvvā) are auspicious gifts with which a newly married couple is blessed.

## 13. Narahari — "lakṣmī prāya lakṣmī ṭhākurāṇī…" (GPT1 p. 90, no. 28)
*Life with Lakshmipriya: Lakshmi serves her mother-in-law and her husband day and night; Nimai Pandita teaches countless students who come
from every side — as if Brihaspati were teaching in Nadia; a pupil of Gangadasa, He poses such tricky questions that no one can answer; in
the evening He enjoys learning with His students by the Ganga; His fame spreads in every direction. Raga kamoda. **Attribution: not
established** — GPT only; by its place in the cycle and its closeness to the BR narrative, rather Chakravarti.*[^21-26]

লক্ষ্মী প্রায় লক্ষ্মী ঠাকুরাণী । শাশুড়ীর সেবা করে দিবস রজনী ॥

*lakṣmī prāya lakṣmī ṭhākurāṇī | śāśuṛīra sebā kare dibasa rajanī ||*

*Word for word:* lakṣmī prāya — like Lakshmi; lakṣmī ṭhākurāṇī — Lakshmi Thakurani; śāśuṛīra sebā kare — serves her mother-in-law; dibasa rajanī — day and night

**13.1.** Lakshmi Thakurani, like Lakshmi Herself, serves her mother-in-law day and night.

পতিপ্রতি অচলা ভকতি । পতিসেবা করে দিন রাতি ॥

*patiprati acalā bhakati | patisebā kare dina rāti ||*

*Word for word:* pati-prati — towards her husband; acalā bhakati — unwavering devotion; pati-sebā kare — she serves her husband; dina rāti — day and night

**13.2.** To her husband — unwavering devotion: she serves her husband day and night.

পাঠ দেয় নিমাই পণ্ডিত । পড়ুয়া অসংখ্য আসে হৈতে চারিভিত ॥

*pāṭha deya nimāi paṇḍita | paṛuyā asaṃkhya āse haite cāribhita ||*

*Word for word:* pāṭha deya nimāi paṇḍita — Nimai Pandita gives lessons; paṛuyā asaṃkhya — countless students; āse haite cāribhita — come from every side

**13.3.** Nimai Pandita gives lessons; countless students come from every side.

হেন শিক্ষা কোথাও না পায় । বৃহস্পতি পাঠ যেন দেয় নদীয়ায় ॥

*hena śikṣā kothāo nā pāya | bṛhaspati pāṭha yena deya nadīyāya ||*

*Word for word:* hena śikṣā — such learning; kothāo nā pāya — is found nowhere; bṛhaspati — Brihaspati; pāṭha yena deya — as if giving lessons; nadīyāya — in Nadia

**13.4.** Such learning is to be found nowhere — as if Brihaspati were giving lessons in Nadia.

গঙ্গাদাস-শিষ্য বিশ্বম্ভর । সর্ব্ববিদ্যা-বিশারদ সে বিদ্যাসাগর ॥

*gaṅgādāsa-śiṣya biśvambhara | sarvvabidyā-biśārada se bidyāsāgara ||*

*Word for word:* gaṅgādāsa-śiṣya biśvambhara — Vishvambhara, pupil of Gangadasa; sarvva-bidyā-biśārada — versed in every science; se bidyā-sāgara — He is an ocean of learning

**13.5.** Vishvambhara, pupil of Gangadasa, versed in every science, is an ocean of learning.

হেন ফাঁকি করেন নিমাই । যাহার উত্তর দিতে কারো সাধ্য নাই ॥

*hena phām̐ki karena nimāi | yāhāra uttara dite kāro sādhya nāi ||*

*Word for word:* hena phām̐ki karena nimāi — Nimai poses such tricky questions; yāhāra uttara dite — to answer which; kāro sādhya nāi — no one is able

**13.6.** Nimai poses such tricky questions that no one is able to answer them.[^21-27]

সন্ধ্যাকালে শিষ্যগণ লৈঞা । বিদ্যার বিলাস করে গঙ্গাতীরে যাঞা ॥

*sandhyākāle śiṣyagaṇa laiñā | bidyāra bilāsa kare gaṅgātīre yāñā ||*

*Word for word:* sandhyā-kāle — in the evening; śiṣya-gaṇa laiñā — taking His students; bidyāra bilāsa kare — delights in learning; gaṅgā-tīre yāñā — going to the bank of the Ganga

**13.7.** In the evening, taking His students, He goes to the bank of the Ganga and delights in learning.

চারিদিগে নিমাইর যশ । নরহরি আনন্দেতে হইল অবশ ॥

*cāridige nimāira yaśa | narahari ānandete haila abaśa ||*

*Word for word:* cāridige nimāira yaśa — in every direction the fame of Nimai; narahari ānandete — Narahari, in bliss; haila abaśa — is beside himself

**13.8.** In every direction — the fame of Nimai; Narahari is beside himself with bliss.

[^21-26]: GPT1 — p. 90, no. 28 (kamoda; scan, PDF p. 349; in the OCR the signature is garbled — "narahabri"); GPT2 — section 2.3, no. 28. The catalogue made
from the OCR of GPT2 did not know it (new row NG-284, chapter 20). Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani;
but in the BR, straight after the cycle of wedding padas (no. 12), Ishana says the same in prose: Lakshmi serves Ai, her Lord is absorbed with
His students in the rasa of learning, all the scholars of Nadia honour Vishvambhara (ed. 1960, vv. 1360–1364). C. Line 13.2 is metrically
incomplete in GPT1. Nimai Pandita teaches — CC Adi 16. After it GPT1 (nos. 29–35) gives the Lord's
learning, the journey to East Bengal and Lakshmipriya's departure — padas of Vrindavana Dasa, Lochana and Govinda Ghosha (no Narahari
signatures; the pada of Govinda Ghosha is PK 1597, chapter 1, no. 1).
[^21-27]: "Like Lakshmi" is a turn of praise; according to the CB and CC Lakshmipriya is Lakshmi Herself (note 2). Brihaspati is the preceptor of
the gods. Tricky questions (phām̐ki) are knotty problems of grammar and logic with which students and pandits in the schools of Navadvipa tested
one another.

## 14. Narahari — "nadīyā-nagare haila dhvani…" (GPT1 p. 93, section 2.4, no. 1; BR)
*Section "The second marriage". The news spreads through Nadia: Gora is marrying again — Sanatana Mishra is giving Him his daughter Vishnupriya,
peerless in beauty and virtue; tomorrow is the adhivasa; the women cannot wait for morning to go to Shachi's for the water rite. Raga kamoda.
**Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^21-28][^21-29]

নদীয়া-নগরে হৈল ধ্বনি । করিব বিবাহ পুনঃ গোরা গুণমণি ॥

*nadīyā-nagare haila dhvani | kariba bibāha punaḥ gorā guṇamaṇi ||*

*Word for word:* nadīyā-nagare — through the town of Nadia; haila dhvani — the news rang out; kariba bibāha punaḥ — will marry again; gorā guṇamaṇi — Gora, the jewel of virtues

**14.1.** Through the town of Nadia the news rang out: "Gora, the jewel of virtues, is marrying again!

সনাতন মিশ্র ভাগ্যবান । করিবেন নিমাইচাঁদেরে কন্যাদান ॥

*sanātana miśra bhāgyabāna | karibena nimāicām̐dere kanyādāna ||*

*Word for word:* sanātana miśra bhāgyabāna — fortunate Sanatana Mishra; karibena nimāi-cām̐dere kanyā-dāna — will give his daughter to Nimaichand

**14.2.** Fortunate Sanatana Mishra will give his daughter to Nimaichand.

বিষ্ণুপ্রিয়া নাম সে কন্যার । রূপে গুণে ভুবনে তুলনা নাহি তার ॥

*biṣṇupriyā nāma se kanyāra | rūpe guṇe bhubane tulanā nāhi tāra ||*

*Word for word:* biṣṇupriyā nāma — the name Vishnupriya; se kanyāra — of that maiden; rūpe guṇe — in beauty and virtue; bhubane tulanā nāhi tāra — she has no equal in the world

**14.3.** The maiden's name is Vishnupriya — in beauty and virtue she has no equal in the world.[^21-30]

কালি হবে শুভ অধিবাস । দেখিব নয়ন ভরি বিবাহ বিলাস ॥

*kāli habe śubha adhibāsa | dekhiba nayana bhari bibāha bilāsa ||*

*Word for word:* kāli habe śubha adhibāsa — tomorrow will be the auspicious adhivasa; dekhiba nayana bhari — we shall see to our eyes' content; bibāha bilāsa — the wedding festivities

**14.4.** Tomorrow will be the auspicious adhivasa — we shall see the wedding festivities to our eyes' content.

কতক্ষণে নিশি পোহাইব । শ্রীশচী-ভবনে পাণি সাইতে যাইব ॥

*katakṣaṇe niśi pohāiba | śrīśacī-bhabane pāṇi sāite yāiba ||*

*Word for word:* kata-kṣaṇe niśi pohāiba — how soon will the night be over; śrī-śacī-bhabane — to Sri Shachi's house; pāṇi sāite yāiba — we shall go for the water rite

**14.5.** How soon will the night be over? Let us go to Sri Shachi's house for the water rite!"

নরহরি কহে হেন বাসি । তো সভার অনুরাগে পোহাইল নিশি ॥

*narahari kahe hena bāsi | to sabhāra anurāge pohāila niśi ||*

*Word for word:* narahari kahe — Narahari says; hena bāsi — I think so; to sabhāra anurāge — through the eagerness of you all; pohāila niśi — the night has passed

**14.6.** Narahari says: "I think it was your eagerness that brought the night to an end."

[^21-28]: Before section 2.4, a brief note on the lila. While the Lord was travelling in East Bengal, Lakshmipriya left this world: according to the
CB and CC, the "snake of separation" from the Lord bit her, and she departed with her mind fixed on His feet; on His return the Lord consoled His
mother with instruction on the transience of everything worldly (CB Adi 14; CC Adi 16; Murari 1.11–1.12). Lakshmipriya is the eternal energy of
the Lord; her departure, too, is lila. In GPT1 the departure of Lakshmipriya is the subject of padas by Lochana and Govinda Ghosha (2.3, nos.
32–35; no Narahari signatures). Then Shachi, wishing to marry her son again, through the matchmaker Kashinatha arranges His marriage with
Vishnupriya, the daughter of Sanatana Mishra (CB Adi 15; Murari 1.13–1.14). In the BR this account is in the 12th wave (ed. 1960, vv. 1372–1396):
according to Chakravarti, Shachi herself noticed Vishnupriya at a ghat of the Ganga, the match was arranged by Kashinatha Pandita, and the
expenses of a wedding "like a prince's" were taken on by Buddhimanta Khan and Mukunda Sanjaya.
[^21-29]: GPT1 — p. 93, section 2.4 ("the second marriage"), no. 1 (kamoda; scan, PDF p. 352); GPT2 — section 2.4, no. 1 (catalogue: NG-045). BR — 12th wave
(ed. 1912, p. 799; ed. 1960, vv. ≈1397–1402: the first line falls on a part lost in the OCR), straight after the account of the match; then the BR
gives in sequence the padas of section 2.4 nos. 2–16 (nos. 15–24 of this chapter and nos. 2–4, 7, 11, not translated here). Not in PK, KGC, PS, the
Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B.
[^21-30]: Vishnupriya is the eternal consort of the Lord, His own Bhu-shakti (the energy of the Earth); like Lakshmipriya (note 2), she is not a worldly
wife but His own energy, and the wedding with her is the Lord's lila.

## 15. Narahari — "yubatī-yūtha mati gati ati adabhuta…" (GPT1 p. 94, no. 5; BR; GCC)
*The morning of the adhivasa: lines of young women who have come to Shachi's house bow down at her feet like young golden creepers weighed
down with flowers; they stretch out their hands to take the dust of her feet and, covering their faces with the ends of their veils, smile
softly. Raga belavali. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR and in the Gaura-charita-chintamani; Vrajabuli.*[^21-31]

যুবতী-যূথ মতি গতি অতি অদভুত করত প্রণাম ভঙ্গী রুচিকারী ।
নয়ত সুতনু জনু কনকলতা নব কুসুম-সমূহ-ভার-গত ভারী ॥

*yubatī-yūtha mati gati ati adabhuta karata praṇāma bhaṅgī rucikārī |*
*nayata sutanu janu kanakalatā naba kusuma-samūha-bhāra-gata bhārī ||*

*Word for word:* yubatī-yūtha — lines of young women; mati gati ati adabhuta — wondrous their thoughts and gait; karata praṇāma — bow down; bhaṅgī rucikārī — charmingly; nayata sutanu — the slender ones bend; janu kanaka-latā naba — like young golden creepers; kusuma-samūha-bhāra-gata bhārī — weighed down by clusters of flowers

**15.1.** Lines of young women — wondrous their thoughts and their gait — bow down charmingly;
slender, they bend like young golden creepers under the weight of clusters of flowers.

সুরুচির চরণ-উপান্ত ধরত শির শিথিল শিরোরুহ অসিত সুকাঁতি ।
ভূমি পতিত জনু বিজুরী-পুঞ্জ সহ সজল জলদ থির-চর তছু ভাঁতি ॥

*surucira caraṇa-upānta dharata śira śithila śiroruha asita sukām̐ti |*
*bhūmi patita janu bijurī-puñja saha sajala jalada thira-cara tachu bhām̐ti ||*

*Word for word:* surucira caraṇa-upānta — at the edge of the lovely feet; dharata śira — they lay their heads; śithila śiroruha — loosened hair; asita sukām̐ti — dark and lustrous; bhūmi patita — fallen to the earth; janu bijurī-puñja saha — as if with a swarm of lightnings; sajala jalada — a rain-cloud; thira-cara — still and moving; tachu bhām̐ti — such is their look

**15.2.** At the edge of [Shachi's] lovely feet they lay their heads — their dark, lustrous hair loosened;
they look like a rain-cloud fallen to the earth with a swarm of motionless lightnings.

লঘু লঘু কর-পল্লব করু প্রেরণ দুর্লভ রেণু-গ্রহণে চিত চাহ ।
ঝলকত নখ মরিযাদ হেতু জনু ভেটত মণিগণ অনুপ উছাহ ॥

*laghu laghu kara-pallaba karu preraṇa durlabha reṇu-grahaṇe cita cāha |*
*jhalakata nakha mariyāda hetu janu bheṭata maṇigaṇa anupa uchāha ||*

*Word for word:* laghu laghu — gently, gently; kara-pallava karu preraṇa — they stretch out their palms tender as shoots; durlabha reṇu-grahaṇe — to take the rare dust; cita cāha — the heart longs; jhalakata nakha — the nails flash; mariyāda hetu janu — as if out of reverence; bheṭata maṇi-gaṇa — jewels come to pay homage; anupa uchāha — with peerless zeal

**15.3.** Gently, gently they stretch out their palms, tender as shoots, longing to take the rare dust [of her feet];
their nails flash — as if jewels had come in reverence to pay homage with peerless zeal.

অম্বুজ-বদনে ঝাঁপি বসনাঞ্চল হাসত মৃদু মৃদু কিরণ প্রকাশ ।
নব মকরন্দ ছানি জনু যতনহি সিঞ্চত ঘন ভণ নরহরি দাস ॥

*ambuja-badane jhām̐pi basanāñcala hāsata mṛdu mṛdu kiraṇa prakāśa |*
*naba makaranda chāni janu yatanahi siñcata ghana bhaṇa narahari dāsa ||*

*Word for word:* ambuja-badane — the lotus faces; jhām̐pi basanāñcala — covering with the end of the veil; hāsata mṛdu mṛdu — they smile softly, softly; kiraṇa prakāśa — radiance spreads; naba makaranda chāni — straining fresh nectar; janu yatanahi — as if carefully; siñcata ghana — they sprinkle abundantly; bhaṇa narahari dāsa — says Narahari Dasa

**15.4.** Covering their lotus faces with the ends of their veils, they smile softly, softly, and radiance spreads around —
as if, carefully straining fresh nectar, they sprinkle it abundantly, says Narahari Dasa.[^21-32]

[^21-31]: GPT1 — p. 94, no. 5 (belavali; scan, PDF p. 353); GPT2 — section 2.4, no. 5 (catalogue: NG-048). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, pp. 800–801; ed. 1960, vv.
1415–1418). GCC — ch. 9 ("the desires of the nagaris of Navadvipa", morning), pada 19: there it stands among padas on the townswomen-nagaris, while
in the BR and GPT it is among the wedding padas. Variants: 15.2 GPT1 and BR "śithila saroruha" ("a loosened lotus"), GCC "śithila śiroruha" ("loosened hair") —
translated following the GCC; GPT1 "kira caratachu", BR "thira-cara tachu" — following the BR; 15.4 GPT1 "siñcita ghanabhaṇa", BR and GCC "siñcata ghana bhaṇa". Not in PK, KGC,
PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. The preceding GPT pada (no. 4, signed Ghanashyama; outside the appendix) describes how these women come to Ai
(Shachi) and strew her feet with champaka buds; the next (no. 16) how Shachi blesses them.
[^21-32]: Subtle Vrajabuli similes: the women bowing in dark garments with loosened hair are a cloud, their golden bodies the lightnings; their nails
are jewels come to bow at her feet; their smile is strained nectar. On the motif of the women of Nadia see note 5.

## 16. Narahari — "śacī jagata-jananī jana-nītabida…" (GPT1 p. 95, no. 6; BR; GCC)
*Shachi, mother of the world, lovingly receives the young wives, asks each about her welfare and blesses her, placing a hand on her head; they
answer with a smile: "Having seen these auspicious feet, how could misfortune remain with us?" — and stand with joined palms; Shachi's eyes
fill with tears of tenderness. Raga todi. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR and in the Gaura-charita-chintamani.*[^21-33]

শচী জগত-জননী জন-নীতবিদ বিদিত সুচারু-চরিত-রীতি ।
নিজ প্রাণের অধিক বধূসম মান সবাকারে করে পরম প্রীতি ॥

*śacī jagata-jananī jana-nītabida bidita sucāru-carita-rīti |*
*nija prāṇera adhika badhūsama māna sabākāre kare parama prīti ||*

*Word for word:* śacī jagata-jananī — Shachi, mother of the world; jana-nītabida — who knows how to treat people; bidita sucāru-carita-rīti — renowned for her lovely ways; nija prāṇera adhika — dearer than her own life; badhū-sama māna — regarding them as daughters-in-law; sabākāre kare parama prīti — shows the greatest love to all

**16.1.** Shachi — mother of the world, who knows how to treat people, renowned for her lovely ways —
regarding all as her daughters-in-law, dearer than her own life, shows them all the greatest love.

প্রতি জনে জনে পুছি মঙ্গল শিরেতে কর ধরি করে আশীষ বহু ।
সদা বাঢ়ুক সম্পদ পতি আদি সব চিরঞ্জীবী হৈয়া কুশলে রহু ॥

*prati jane jane puchi maṅgala śirete kara dhari kare āśīṣa bahu |*
