*sadā bāṛhuka sampada pati ādi saba cirañjībī haiyā kuśale rahu ||*

*Word for word:* prati jane jane puchi maṅgala — asking each about her welfare; śirete kara dhari — placing a hand on the head; kare āśīṣa bahu — blesses abundantly; sadā bāṛhuka sampada — may your fortune ever grow; pati ādi saba — husbands and all your kin; ciranjībī haiyā kuśale rahu — may they live long and prosper

**16.2.** Asking each one about her welfare, she places a hand on her head and blesses her abundantly:
"May your fortune ever grow; may your husbands and all your kin live long and prosper!"

ইহা শুনি বধূগণ মনে মনে হাসি সুখে ভাসি কহে মধুর কথা ।
ওগো এ শুভ চরণ দরশনে বলো কি লাগি অশুভ রহিব এথা ॥

*ihā śuni badhūgaṇa mane mane hāsi sukhe bhāsi kahe madhura kathā |*
*ogo e śubha caraṇa daraśane balo ki lāgi aśubha rahiba ethā ||*

*Word for word:* ihā śuni badhū-gaṇa — hearing this, the young wives; mane mane hāsi — smiling inwardly; sukhe bhāsi — floating in happiness; kahe madhura kathā — speak sweet words; ogo — oh; e śubha caraṇa daraśane — having seen these auspicious feet; bolo — tell us; ki lāgi aśubha rahiba ethā — why should misfortune remain here

**16.3.** Hearing this, the young wives smile inwardly and, floating in happiness, speak sweet words:
"Oh, tell us — having seen these auspicious feet, why should any misfortune stay here?"

অতি সঙ্কুচিত চিতে কিঞ্চিৎ কহি করজোড়ি সদা দাঁড়াঞা রহে ।
নরহরি-প্রাণপতি-মাতা তা দেখিয়া আঁখি ছল ছল বিবশ স্নেহে ॥

*ati saṅkucita cite kiñcit kahi karajoṛi sadā dām̐ṛāñā rahe |*
*narahari-prāṇapati-mātā tā dekhiyā ām̐khi chala chala bibaśa snehe ||*

*Word for word:* ati saṅkucita cite — with very shy hearts; kiñcit kahi — saying a little; kara-joṛi — with joined palms; sadā dām̐ṛāñā rahe — they stand on; narahari-prāṇapati-mātā — the mother of Narahari's Lord of life; tā dekhiyā — seeing this; ām̐khi chala chala — eyes brimming with tears; bibaśa snehe — overcome with tenderness

**16.4.** Having shyly said a little, they stand on with joined palms;
the mother of Narahari's Lord of life, seeing this, is overcome with tenderness — her eyes brim with tears.[^21-34]

[^21-33]: GPT1 — p. 95, no. 6 (todi; scan, PDF p. 354); GPT2 — section 2.4, no. 6 (catalogue: NG-049). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 801; ed. 1960, vv. 1419–1422).
GCC — ch. 9, pada 21 (there "jananī-tattvabida", "kara yuṛi nikaṭe dām̐ṛāyā rahe" — "they stand near with joined palms"). Variant: 16.3 GPT1 "āgā", BR and GCC
"ogo" — following the BR. Not in PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^21-34]: Shachi is the Lord's mother, His eternal associate in vatsalya-rasa; blessing the wives of Nadia, she wishes them worldly welfare, as befits a
mother in the lila — and they reply that after the darshan of her feet no misfortune can remain: that is the highest good.

## 17. Narahari — "gorā-rase bhāsi hāsi hāsi lahu lahu…" (GPT1 pp. 95–96, no. 8; BR)
*The water rite on the day of the adhivasa: at Shachi's bidding the women of noble families, young and mature, dress and go in lines for the
water with auspicious articles, lotuses and trays; girdles and anklets ring, musicians go in front; celestial women invisibly mingle with them;
returning, they distribute oil and turmeric and perform the women's rites. Raga not specified ("yatha-raga"). **Attribution: probably
Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^21-35]

গোরা-রসে ভাসি হাসি হাসি লহু লহু । কুলবতী-কুল উলসিত বহু ॥

*gorā-rase bhāsi hāsi hāsi lahu lahu | kulabatī-kula ulasita bahu ||*

*Word for word:* gorā-rase bhāsi — floating in Gora's rasa; hāsi hāsi lahu lahu — smiling softly, softly; kulabatī-kula — the women of noble families; ulasita bahu — rejoice greatly

**17.1.** Floating in Gora's rasa, smiling softly, softly, the women of noble families rejoice.

পাণি সাইবারে সাজে শচীদেবী-আদেশেতে কিবা কৌতুক চিতে ।
নব্য মধ্য পূর্ণা যৌবনা সুন্দরী যূথে যূথে গতি অতি সুমাধুরী ।
চঞ্চল চারু দৃগঞ্চল চাহনি ভঙ্গী নানা নাহি উপমা দিতে ॥

*pāṇi sāibāre sāje śacīdebī-ādeśete kibā kautuka cite |*
*nabya madhya pūrṇā yaubanā sundarī yūthe yūthe gati ati sumādhurī |*
*cañcala cāru dṛgañcala cāhani bhaṅgī nānā nāhi upamā dite ||*

*Word for word:* pāṇi sāibāre sāje — they dress for the water rite; śacīdebī-ādeśete — at Shachi-devi's bidding; kibā kautuka cite — what merriment in their hearts; nabya madhya pūrṇā yaubanā sundarī — beauties in early, middle and full youth; yūthe yūthe — in lines; gati ati sumādhurī — their gait so sweet; cañcala cāru dṛgañcala cāhani — restless lovely sidelong glances; bhaṅgī nānā — manifold graces; nāhi upamā dite — no comparison can be given

**17.2.** At the bidding of Shachi-devi they dress for the water rite — what merriment in their hearts!
Beauties in early, middle and full youth, in lines, their gait so sweet;
restless their lovely sidelong glances, manifold their graces — there is no comparison for them.

পরিধেয় কত ভাঁতি সুবসন প্রতি অঙ্গে হেম-মণি-আভরণ ঝলকয় মুখে ঘুঙট অতুল সুললিত বেণী পীঠেতে দোলে ।
কারু কারু করে শুভময় দ্রব্য কারু কারু করে সরসীজ নব্য কারু শিরে ডালা আলা করে পট্টবাসে সে আবৃত শোভয়ে ভালে ॥

*paridheya kata bhām̐ti subasana prati aṅge hema-maṇi-ābharaṇa jhalakaya mukhe ghuṅaṭa atula sulalita beṇī pīṭhete dole |*
*kāru kāru kare śubhamaya drabya kāru kāru kare sarasīja nabya kāru śire ḍālā ālā kare paṭṭabāse se ābṛta śobhaye bhāle ||*

*Word for word:* paridheya kata bhām̐ti subasana — garments of many kinds; prati aṅge hema-maṇi-ābharaṇa — on every limb ornaments of gold and jewels; jhalakaya mukhe ghuṅaṭa — veils gleam on the faces; atula sulalita beṇī pīṭhete dole — peerlessly lovely braids sway on the backs; kāru kāru kare śubhamaya drabya — some carry auspicious articles; sarasīja nabya — fresh lotuses; kāru śire ḍālā ālā kare — on the heads of others trays shine; paṭṭabāse se ābṛta śobhaye bhāle — beautifully covered with silk

**17.3.** They wear garments of many kinds, on every limb ornaments of gold and jewels;
veils gleam on their faces, peerlessly lovely braids sway on their backs;
some carry auspicious articles in their hands, some fresh lotuses,
on the heads of others trays shine, beautifully covered with silk.

চলিতেই বাজে কটিতে কিঙ্কিণী ঝণি ঝিনি ঝণি ঝিনিনি নি নি নি চরণে নূপুর রুনু ঝুনু রুনু ঝুনু ঝু ঝু রবে রঞ্জয়ে শ্রুতি ।
আগে আগে চলে বাদক আনন্দে বাজায়য়ে বাদ্য সুমধুর ছন্দে ধাধা ধিং নিং নিং ধো ধিকি ধিকতাধেন্না নানা বাদ্যে হরয়ে ধৃতি ॥

*calitei bāje kaṭite kiṅkiṇī jhaṇi jhini jhaṇi jhinini ni ni ni caraṇe nūpura runu jhunu runu jhunu jhu jhu rabe rañjaye śruti |*
*āge āge cale bādaka ānande bājāyaye bādya sumadhura chande dhādhā dhiṃ niṃ niṃ dho dhiki dhikatādhennā nānā bādye haraye dhṛti ||*

*Word for word:* calitei bāje kaṭite kiṅkiṇī — as they walk the bells on their girdles ring; jhaṇi jhini… — sound-words; caraṇe nūpura runu jhunu — anklets on the feet "runu-jhunu"; rabe rañjaye śruti — delight the ear with their sound; āge āge cale bādaka ānande — in front the musicians walk joyfully; bājāyaye bādya sumadhura chande — play instruments in sweet rhythms; dhādhā dhiṃ… — drum syllables; nānā bādye haraye dhṛti — with many instruments steal composure

**17.4.** As they walk, the bells on their girdles ring — "jhani-jhini, jhani-jhinini ni-ni-ni",
the anklets on their feet — "runu-jhunu, runu-jhunu jhu-jhu" — delighting the ear with their sound;
in front the musicians walk joyfully, playing sweet rhythms —
"dha-dha dhing ning ning dho dhiki dhikatadhenna": with many instruments they steal away composure.

অলখিত সুরনারীগণ রঙ্গে মিশাইয়া নদীয়ার বধূ-সঙ্গে পাণি সাই সবে প্রবেশে ভবনে ধনি ধনি ধনি কেবা না কহে ।
তৈল হরিদ্রাদি বিলাইয়া যত স্ত্রী-আচার তাহা কে কহিবে কত সে সুখ-পাথারে কে না সাঁতারয়ে নরহরি পহুঁ নিছনি তাহে ॥

*alakhita suranārīgaṇa raṅge miśāiyā nadīyāra badhū-saṅge pāṇi sāi sabe prabeśe bhabane dhani dhani dhani kebā nā kahe |*
*taila haridrādi bilāiyā yata strī-ācāra tāhā ke kahibe kata se sukha-pāthāre ke nā sām̐tāraye narahari pahum̐ nichani tāhe ||*

*Word for word:* alakhita suranārī-gaṇa — invisible celestial women; raṅge miśāiyā — merrily mingling; nadīyāra badhū-saṅge — with the wives of Nadia; pāṇi sāi — having done the water rite; sabe prabeśe bhabane — all enter the house; dhani dhani dhani — "blessed!"; kebā nā kahe — who does not say; taila haridrādi bilāiyā — distributing oil, turmeric and the rest; yata strī-ācāra — all the women's rites; tāhā ke kahibe kata — who can tell them; se sukha-pāthāre — in that ocean of happiness; ke nā sām̐tāraye — who does not swim; narahari pahum̐ nichani tāhe — Narahari gives himself to the Lord in this

**17.5.** Invisible celestial women have merrily mingled with the wives of Nadia;
having performed the water rite, all enter the house — who does not say "Blessed, blessed, blessed!"?
They distribute oil, turmeric and the rest — who can tell all the women's rites?
Who does not swim in that ocean of happiness? Narahari gives himself to the Lord in this [joy].[^21-36]

[^21-35]: GPT1 — pp. 95–96, no. 8 ("yathārāga"; scan, PDF pp. 354–355); GPT2 — section 2.4, no. 8 (catalogue: NG-051). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 802; ed. 1960, vv.
1429–1432). Variants: 17.4 GPT1 "bālaka" ("boys"), BR "bādaka" ("musicians") — following the BR; the bells in the BR "rini jhini rini jhinini"; 17.5 GPT1 "bhubane"
("into the world"), BR "bhabane" ("into the house") — following the BR; GPT1 "narahari pahum̐ nichani tāhe", BR "narahari bahu nichani tāhe" ("Narahari again and again gives
himself for that"). Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. Line 17.1 is the opening couplet. The chapter plan had
provisionally assigned this pada to the nagari section ("floating in Gora's rasa"); in substance it describes the wedding water rite (cf. no. 2), and
it is translated here — with the caveat of note 5.
[^21-36]: "Floating in Gora's rasa" — in joy over the Lord whose wedding is being celebrated; on the motif of the women of Nadia see note 5. The celestial
women come invisibly to take part in the Lord's wedding (cf. no. 21).

## 18. Narahari — "śacīdebī ulasita haiñā…" (GPT1 p. 96, no. 9; BR)
*Shachi with the married women goes to the Ganga and worships her with flowers and sandal — and the Suradhuni surges, holding in her heart the feet
of Shachi's son; then she worships Shashthi — and Shashthi, rejoicing, praises her own good fortune; the women return home; at home Shachi
performs the auspicious rites. Raga not specified. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^21-37]

শচীদেবী উলসিত হৈঞা । গঙ্গা পূজিবারে যায় গঙ্গাতীরে আয়ো সুয়োগণ সঙ্গেতে লৈঞা ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*śacīdebī ulasita haiñā | gaṅgā pūjibāre yāya gaṅgātīre āyo suyogaṇa saṅgete laiñā || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* śacīdebī ulasita haiñā — Shachi-devi, rejoicing; gaṅgā pūjibāre — to worship the Ganga; yāya gaṅgā-tīre — goes to the bank of the Ganga; āyo suyo-gaṇa — the married women; saṅgete laiñā — taking with her

**18.1.** Shachi-devi, rejoicing, goes to the bank of the Ganga to worship the Ganga, taking the married women with her.

নানা পুষ্প গন্ধ চন্দনাদি দিয়া পূজে জাহ্নবীরে যতন করি ।
উছলয়ে সুরধুনী অনিবার শচীসুত-পদ হৃদয়ে ধরি ॥

*nānā puṣpa gandha candanādi diyā pūje jāhnabīre yatana kari |*
*uchalaye suradhunī anibāra śacīsuta-pada hṛdaye dhari ||*

*Word for word:* nānā puṣpa gandha candanādi diyā — with various flowers, perfumes and sandal; pūje jāhnabīre yatana kari — carefully worships the Jahnavi; uchalaye suradhunī anibāra — the Suradhuni surges unceasingly; śacīsuta-pada hṛdaye dhari — holding in her heart the feet of Shachi's son

**18.2.** With various flowers, perfumes and sandal paste she carefully worships the Jahnavi;
and the Suradhuni surges unceasingly, holding in her heart the feet of Shachi's son.[^21-38]

বাজে বাদ্য ভালে ষষ্ঠী-থলে চলে পূজে ষষ্ঠী কত সামগ্রী দিয়া ।
ষষ্ঠী সুখে ভাসি প্রশংসে আপনা গোরাচাঁদ-গুণে উথলে হিয়া ॥

*bāje bādya bhāle ṣaṣṭhī-thale cale pūje ṣaṣṭhī kata sāmagrī diyā |*
*ṣaṣṭhī sukhe bhāsi praśaṃse āpanā gorācām̐da-guṇe uthale hiyā ||*

*Word for word:* bāje bādya bhāle — instruments play beautifully; ṣaṣṭhī-thale cale — she goes to the place of Shashthi; pūje ṣaṣṭhī kata sāmagrī diyā — worships Shashthi with many offerings; ṣaṣṭhī sukhe bhāsi — Shashthi, floating in happiness; praśaṃse āpanā — praises her own fortune; gorācām̐da-guṇe uthale hiyā — her heart overflows with Gorachand's virtues

**18.3.** Instruments play beautifully; she goes to the place of Shashthi and worships Shashthi with many offerings;
Shashthi, floating in happiness, praises her own good fortune — her heart overflows with the virtues of Gorachand.

কত সাধে বধূগণ গৃহে গতি অতি উল্লাস সে সবার চিতে ।
আসি নিজ ঘরে করে শুভ ক্রিয়া নরহরি নারে তুলনা দিতে ॥

*kata sādhe badhūgaṇa gṛhe gati ati ullāsa se sabāra cite |*
*āsi nija ghare kare śubha kriyā narahari nāre tulanā dite ||*

*Word for word:* kata sādhe badhū-gaṇa gṛhe gati — with what longing the wives go home; ati ullāsa se sabāra cite — great rejoicing in all their hearts; āsi nija ghare — coming home; kare śubha kriyā — performs the auspicious rites; narahari nāre tulanā dite — Narahari cannot find a comparison

**18.4.** With what longing the wives go home — how great the rejoicing in all their hearts!
Returning home, [Shachi] performs the auspicious rites — Narahari cannot find a comparison.

[^21-37]: GPT1 — p. 96, no. 9 ("yathārāga"; scan, PDF p. 355; in the OCR the number is garbled — "“ma pada"); GPT2 — section 2.4, no. 9. **The catalogue did not
know it** (new row NG-285). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 803; ed. 1960, vv. 1433–1436). Variants: 18.1 GPT1 "āyo suyogaṇa", BR "āiha-suihagaṇa" (the same:
married women); 18.4 GPT1 "badhūgaṇa", BR "bandhugaṇa" ("kinsfolk"). Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. Line 18.1 is the
refrain (dhru).
[^21-38]: The Ganga flows from the feet of the Lord (Bhag. 5.17), so, says the poet, she "holds in her heart" Gaura's feet. Shashthi is the goddess who
protects children; the worship of the Ganga and of Shashthi before a son's wedding is a custom of Bengali mothers, and Shachi follows it in the
lila. The Gaudiya tradition does not worship the demigods for separate ends; and the poet shows that the Ganga and Shashthi themselves rejoice as
servants of the Lord.

## 19. Narahari — "gorā-bidhu adhibāsa-sukhe…" (GPT1 p. 96, no. 10; BR)
*The bridegroom's adhivasa: everyone hurries into the house; Gora's dear ones skilfully perform the rites and distribute garlands and sandal; in
the midst of the assembly the son of Shachi shines like Indra among the gods; Sanatana Mishra with his people brings gifts, touches Him with
perfume and cannot take his eyes from His face; Vedic chanting, cries of joy, praises, music. Raga not specified. **Attribution: probably
Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^21-39]

গোরা-বিধু অধিবাস-সুখে কে না বৈসে প্রবেশিয়া ভবন মাঝে ।
গোরা-প্রিয়গণ নিত নব নব নিপুণতা অধিবাসের কাজে ॥

*gorā-bidhu adhibāsa-sukhe ke nā baise prabeśiyā bhabana mājhe |*
*gorā-priyagaṇa nita naba naba nipuṇatā adhibāsera kāje ||*

*Word for word:* gorā-bidhu adhibāsa-sukhe — in the joy of the Gora-moon's adhivasa; ke nā baise — who would not sit; prabeśiyā bhabana mājhe — entering the house; gorā-priya-gaṇa — Gora's dear ones; nita naba naba nipuṇatā — ever new skill; adhibāsera kāje — in the rites of the adhivasa

**19.1.** Who, in the joy of the Gora-moon's adhivasa, would not enter the house and sit down?
Gora's dear ones show ever new skill in the rites of the adhivasa.

মালা চন্দনাদি দেই জনে জনে সে অতি কৌতুক কে কত কবে ।
সভা মধ্যে বিলসয়ে শচীসুত যেন পুরন্দর বেষ্টিত দেবে ॥

*mālā candanādi dei jane jane se ati kautuka ke kata kabe |*
*sabhā madhye bilasaye śacīsuta yena purandara beṣṭita debe ||*

*Word for word:* mālā candanādi dei jane jane — they give garlands, sandal and the rest to each; se ati kautuka — that great merriment; ke kata kabe — who can tell; sabhā madhye — in the midst of the assembly; bilasaye śacīsuta — the son of Shachi shines; yena purandara beṣṭita debe — like Purandara surrounded by the gods

**19.2.** To each they give garlands, sandal paste and the rest — who can tell of that great merriment?
In the midst of the assembly the son of Shachi shines — like Purandara surrounded by the gods.

মিশ্র সনাতন গণ সহ শুভক্ষণে আসি নানা সামগ্রী লৈয়া ।
ছোঁয়াইয়া গন্ধ গোরা-মুখ পানে অনিমিষ আঁখে রহয়ে চাহিয়া ॥

*miśra sanātana gaṇa saha śubhakṣaṇe āsi nānā sāmagrī laiyā |*
*chom̐yāiyā gandha gorā-mukha pāne animiṣa ām̐khe rahaye cāhiyā ||*

*Word for word:* miśra sanātana gaṇa saha — Mishra Sanatana with his people; śubha-kṣaṇe āsi — coming at the auspicious moment; nānā sāmagrī laiyā — with various gifts; chom̐yāiyā gandha — touching with perfume; gorā-mukha pāne — at Gora's face; animiṣa ām̐khe rahaye cāhiyā — keeps gazing with unblinking eyes

**19.3.** Mishra Sanatana with his people came at the auspicious moment with various gifts;
touching [Him] with perfume, he gazes with unblinking eyes at Gora's face.[^21-40]

বিপ্র বেদধ্বনি করে নারী যজকার চারু রঙ্গ ভাটেতে ভণে ।
গায় নরহরি অধিবাস-রস বায় নানা বাদ্য বাদকগণে ॥

*bipra bedadhvani kare nārī yajakāra cāru raṅga bhāṭete bhaṇe |*
*gāya narahari adhibāsa-rasa bāya nānā bādya bādakagaṇe ||*

*Word for word:* bipra beda-dhvani kare — the brahmanas chant the Vedas; nārī yajakāra — the women raise cries of joy; cāru raṅga bhāṭete bhaṇe — the bhatas recite lovely praises; gāya narahari adhibāsa-rasa — Narahari sings the rasa of the adhivasa; bāya nānā bādya bādaka-gaṇe — the musicians play many instruments

**19.4.** The brahmanas chant the Vedas, the women raise cries of joy, the bhatas recite lovely praises;
Narahari sings the rasa of the adhivasa, the musicians play on many instruments.

[^21-39]: GPT1 — p. 96, no. 10 ("yathārāga"; scan, PDF p. 355); GPT2 — section 2.4, no. 10 (catalogue: NG-052). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, pp. 803–804; ed. 1960, vv.
1437–1440). Variants: 19.1 GPT1 "bhūbana mājhe" ("into the world"), BR "bhabana-mājhe" ("into the house") — following the BR; GPT1 "gorā priyāgaṇa" ("Gora's
beloveds"), BR "gorā-priyagaṇa" ("Gora's dear ones") — following the BR; 19.2 GPT1 "ke kata kare", BR "ke kata kabe" ("who can tell") — following the BR. Not in PK,
KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B.
[^21-40]: Purandara is Indra, king of the gods. Sanatana Mishra is Vishnupriya's father, the "Raja-pandita" of Navadvipa (CB Adi 15); by custom the
bride's father comes to the bridegroom's house and performs his adhivasa, touching him with perfume (cf. no. 21 of chapter 20).

## 20. Narahari — "miśra sanātana harṣa mane…" (GPT1 pp. 97–98, no. 12; BR)
*The bride's adhivasa in the house of Sanatana Mishra: brahmanas bring from Ai's house all that is needed for the rite, the noble brahmanas of
Nadia gather in the house of the Raja-pandita; Mishra's wife and her friends perform auspicious rites; Vishnupriya, glancing shyly around,
comes out and sits on a throne in the midst of the assembly — her beauty eclipses the moon; all touch her with perfume and bless her. Raga not
specified. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^21-41]

মিশ্র সনাতন হর্ষ মনে । করয়ে কন্যার অধিবাস শুভক্ষণে ॥

*miśra sanātana harṣa mane | karaye kanyāra adhibāsa śubhakṣaṇe ||*

*Word for word:* miśra sanātana — Mishra Sanatana; harṣa mane — with a glad heart; karaye kanyāra adhibāsa — performs his daughter's adhivasa; śubha-kṣaṇe — at the auspicious moment

**20.1.** Mishra Sanatana, his heart glad, at the auspicious moment performs his daughter's adhivasa.

বিপ্রগণ আই-গৃহ হৈতে । অধিবাস-সজ্জ লৈঞা আইলা তুরিতে ॥

*bipragaṇa āi-gṛha haite | adhibāsa-sajja laiñā āilā turite ||*

*Word for word:* bipragaṇa āi-gṛha haite — brahmanas from Ai's house; adhibāsa-sajja laiñā — bringing the things for the adhivasa; āilā turite — came in haste

**20.2.** Brahmanas from Ai's house came in haste, bringing everything needed for the adhivasa.

নদীয়ার ব্রাহ্মণ সজ্জন । রাজপণ্ডিতের ঘরে সবার গমন ॥

*nadīyāra brāhmaṇa sajjana | rājapaṇḍitera ghare sabāra gamana ||*

*Word for word:* nadīyāra brāhmaṇa sajjana — the brahmanas and worthy people of Nadia; rāja-paṇḍitera ghare — to the house of the Raja-pandita; sabāra gamana — all go

**20.3.** The brahmanas and worthy people of Nadia — all go to the house of the Raja-pandita.

মিশ্র মহা আদর করিয়া । বসান সবারে মালাচন্দনাদি দিয়া ॥

*miśra mahā ādara kariyā | basāna sabāre mālācandanādi diyā ||*

*Word for word:* miśra mahā ādara kariyā — Mishra with great respect; basāna sabāre — seats everyone; mālā-candanādi diyā — presenting garlands, sandal and the rest

**20.4.** Mishra with great respect seats everyone, presenting garlands, sandal and the rest.

কি অপূর্ব্ব সুষমা অঙ্গনে । বৈসয়ে সকলে চারু মণ্ডল-বন্ধানে ॥

*ki apūrvva suṣamā aṅgane | baisaye sakale cāru maṇḍala-bandhāne ||*

*Word for word:* ki apūrvva suṣamā aṅgane — what wondrous beauty in the courtyard; baisaye sakale — all sit; cāru maṇḍala-bandhāne — arranged in a lovely circle

**20.5.** What wondrous beauty in the courtyard! All sit arranged in a lovely circle.

সখী সহ মিশ্রের ঘরণী । করয় মঙ্গল যত কহিতে না জানি ॥

*sakhī saha miśrera gharaṇī | karaya maṅgala yata kahite nā jāni ||*

*Word for word:* sakhī saha miśrera gharaṇī — Mishra's wife with her friends; karaya maṅgala yata — performs so many auspicious rites; kahite nā jāni — that I cannot tell

**20.6.** Mishra's wife with her friends performs so many auspicious rites that I cannot tell them.

চকিত চাহিয়া চারি ভিতে । বিষ্ণুপ্রিয়া বাহির হইল ঘর হৈতে ॥

*cakita cāhiyā cāri bhite | biṣṇupriyā bāhira haila ghara haite ||*

*Word for word:* cakita cāhiyā cāri bhite — glancing shyly on every side; biṣṇupriyā — Vishnupriya; bāhira haila ghara haite — came out of the house

**20.7.** Glancing shyly on every side, Vishnupriya came out of the house.

সভা মধ্যে বৈসে সিংহাসনে । অনিমিষ আঁখে শোভা দেখে সর্ব্বজনে ॥

*sabhā madhye baise siṃhāsane | animiṣa ām̐khe śobhā dekhe sarvvajane ||*

*Word for word:* sabhā madhye — in the midst of the assembly; baise siṃhāsane — sits on a throne; animiṣa ām̐khe — with unblinking eyes; śobhā dekhe sarvvajane — everyone gazes at her beauty

**20.8.** In the midst of the assembly she sits on a throne — everyone gazes at her beauty with unblinking eyes.

বসন ভূষণ সাজে ভালো । প্রতি অঙ্গ-ছটায় ভুবন করে আলো ॥

*basana bhūṣaṇa sāje bhālo | prati aṅga-chaṭāya bhubana kare ālo ||*

*Word for word:* basana bhūṣaṇa sāje bhālo — her garments and ornaments become her well; prati aṅga-chaṭāya — with the radiance of every limb; bhubana kare ālo — lights up the world

**20.9.** Her garments and ornaments become her well; with the radiance of every limb she lights up the world.

উপমা কি কনক-বিজুরী । চাঁদের গরব হরে মুখের মাধুরী ॥

*upamā ki kanaka-bijurī | cām̐dera garaba hare mukhera mādhurī ||*

*Word for word:* upamā ki — what comparison; kanaka-bijurī — gold, lightning; cām̐dera garaba hare — steals the moon's pride; mukhera mādhurī — the sweetness of her face

**20.10.** To what shall she be compared — to gold, to lightning? The sweetness of her face steals the moon's pride.

যত শোভা কে কহিতে পারে । ছোঁয়াইয়া গন্ধ সবে আশীর্ব্বাদ করে ॥

*yata śobhā ke kahite pāre | chom̐yāiyā gandha sabe āśīrvvāda kare ||*

*Word for word:* yata śobhā — all the beauty; ke kahite pāre — who can describe; chom̐yāiyā gandha — touching with perfume; sabe āśīrvvāda kare — all bless her

**20.11.** Who can describe all that beauty? Touching her with perfume, all bless her.

নারীগণে দেই জয়কার । বিপ্রগণে বেদধ্বনি করে অনিবার ॥

*nārīgaṇe dei jayakāra | bipragaṇe bedadhvani kare anibāra ||*

*Word for word:* nārī-gaṇe dei jayakāra — the women raise cries of joy; bipragaṇe beda-dhvani kare — the brahmanas chant the Vedas; anibāra — without pause

**20.12.** The women raise cries of joy, the brahmanas chant the Vedas without pause.

ভাটগণে ভণে সুচরিত । বাজে নানা বাদ্য গুণীজনে গায় গীত ॥

*bhāṭagaṇe bhaṇe sucarita | bāje nānā bādya guṇījane gāya gīta ||*

*Word for word:* bhāṭa-gaṇe bhaṇe sucarita — the bhatas praise auspicious deeds; bāje nānā bādya — many instruments sound; guṇījane gāya gīta — skilled singers sing songs

**20.13.** The bhatas praise auspicious deeds, many instruments sound, skilled singers sing songs.

কত না কৌতুক মিশ্র-ঘরে । নরহরি ভাসে সে না সুখের সায়রে ॥

*kata nā kautuka miśra-ghare | narahari bhāse se nā sukhera sāyare ||*

*Word for word:* kata nā kautuka miśra-ghare — how much merriment in Mishra's house; narahari bhāse — Narahari floats; se nā sukhera sāyare — in that ocean of happiness

**20.14.** How much merriment in Mishra's house! Narahari floats in that ocean of happiness.[^21-42]

[^21-41]: GPT1 — pp. 97–98, no. 12 ("yathārāga"; scan, PDF pp. 356–357); GPT2 — section 2.4, no. 12 (catalogue: NG-053). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 805; ed. 1960, vv.
1445–1458). Variants: 20.13 GPT1 "sucarita", "guṇījane", BR "svacarita", "guṇigaṇe" — minor. Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B.
Before it in the GPT (no. 11) stands an ornate pada on the bridegroom's adhivasa signed Ghanashyama ("ghanaśyāma hiyā"; = BR vv. 1441–1444) — outside the
appendix.
[^21-42]: The Raja-pandita is Sanatana Mishra, the court scholar (CB Adi 15; note 40). Vishnupriya is the eternal energy of the Lord (note 30); as at
Lakshmipriya's adhivasa (no. 22 of chapter 20), all the people of Nadia come to bless her.

## 21. Narahari — "adhibāsa dibasera pare…" (GPT1 p. 98, no. 13; BR)
*The wedding day: through Nadia rings "today is Nimai's wedding"; to see it there come invisibly Shiva with Parvati, Ananta with his
associates, the residents of Vaikuntha, Brahma with his consort, Indra with Shachi, the gods, the celestial women, gandharvas and kinnaras,
the heavenly dancers, the divine sages; the Yamuna and the Ganga surge; the brahmanas of Nadia gather in Nimai's house; Gaurahari, having
performed the wedding rites, sits in joy. Raga not specified. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^21-43]

অধিবাস-দিবসের পরে । বাঢ়য়ে আনন্দ নব নদীয়া-নগরে ॥

*adhibāsa-dibasera pare | bāṛhaye ānanda naba nadīyā-nagare ||*

*Word for word:* adhibāsa-dibasera pare — on the day after the adhivasa; bāṛhaye ānanda — joy grows; naba nadīyā-nagare — in the new town of Nadia

**21.1.** On the day after the adhivasa, joy grows in the new town of Nadia.

চারিদিকে ফিরে লোক ধাঞা । নিমাইর বিবাহ আজি এই কথা কৈঞা ॥

*cāridike phire loka dhāñā | nimāira bibāha āji ei kathā kaiñā ||*

*Word for word:* cāridike phire loka dhāñā — everywhere people run about; nimāira bibāha āji — "today is Nimai's wedding"; ei kathā kaiñā — saying these words

**21.2.** Everywhere people run about, saying: "Today is Nimai's wedding!"

ভুবন ভরিয়া জয় জয় । বিবাহ দেখিতে সাধ কার বা না হয় ॥

*bhubana bhariyā jaya jaya | bibāha dekhite sādha kāra bā nā haya ||*

*Word for word:* bhubana bhariyā jaya jaya — the world full of "jaya, jaya"; bibāha dekhite sādha — the longing to see the wedding; kāra vā nā haya — who would not have

**21.3.** The world is full of cries of "jaya, jaya" — who would not long to see the wedding?

শিব সুখে পার্ব্বতী সহিতে । ছাড়িয়া কৈলাস আসে বিবাহ দেখিতে ॥

*śiba sukhe pārvvatī sahite | chāṛiyā kailāsa āse bibāha dekhite ||*

*Word for word:* śiba sukhe — Shiva in joy; pārvvatī sahite — with Parvati; chāṛiyā kailāsa — leaving Kailasa; āse bibāha dekhite — comes to see the wedding

**21.4.** Shiva in joy, with Parvati, leaving Kailasa, comes to see the wedding.

অনন্ত আপনগণ লৈঞা । বিবাহ দেখিতে রহে অলক্ষিত হৈঞা ॥

*ananta āpanagaṇa laiñā | bibāha dekhite rahe alakṣita haiñā ||*

*Word for word:* ananta — Ananta; āpana-gaṇa laiñā — with his own associates; bibāha dekhite — to see the wedding; rahe alakṣita haiñā — remains unseen

**21.5.** Ananta with his own associates remains here unseen to behold the wedding.

বৈকুণ্ঠের যত পরিকর । বিবাহ দেখিব বলি অধীর অন্তর ॥

*baikuṇṭhera yata parikara | bibāha dekhiba bali adhīra antara ||*

*Word for word:* baikuṇṭhera yata parikara — all the residents of Vaikuntha; bibāha dekhiba bali — saying "we shall see the wedding"; adhīra antara — are restless at heart

**21.6.** All the residents of Vaikuntha, saying "we shall see the wedding", are restless at heart.

চতুর্ম্মুখ নিজপ্রিয়া সনে । দেখিতে বিবাহ কত সাধ ক্ষণে ক্ষণে ॥

*caturmmukha nijapriyā sane | dekhite bibāha kata sādha kṣaṇe kṣaṇe ||*

*Word for word:* caturmmukha — the four-faced (Brahma); nija-priyā sane — with his consort; dekhite bibāha — to see the wedding; kata sādha kṣaṇe kṣaṇe — how he longs every moment

**21.7.** The four-faced [Brahma] with his consort longs every moment to see the wedding.

সুরপতি শচী সঙ্গে লৈঞা । বিবাহ দেখিতে সাজে মহা হর্ষ হৈঞা ॥

*surapati śacī saṅge laiñā | bibāha dekhite sāje mahā harṣa haiñā ||*

*Word for word:* surapati — the lord of the gods (Indra); śacī saṅge laiñā — taking Shachi with him; bibāha dekhite sāje — dresses to see the wedding; mahā harṣa haiñā — in great joy

**21.8.** The lord of the gods, taking Shachi with him, dresses in great joy to see the wedding.[^21-44]

উৎসাহে ভণয়ে দেবগণে । দেখিব বিবাহ রহি প্রভুর ভবনে ॥

*utsāhe bhaṇaye debagaṇe | dekhiba bibāha rahi prabhura bhabane ||*

*Word for word:* utsāhe bhaṇaye debagaṇe — the gods say with zeal; dekhiba bibāha — we shall see the wedding; rahi prabhura bhabane — staying in the Lord's house

**21.9.** The gods say with zeal: "We shall see the wedding, staying in the Lord's house!"

দেবনারী বিচারিল চিতে । মাতিব বিবাহে নদীয়ার বধূ সাতে ॥

*debanārī bicārila cite | mātiba bibāhe nadīyāra badhū sāte ||*

*Word for word:* deba-nārī bicārila cite — the celestial women resolved in their hearts; mātiba bibāhe — we shall make merry at the wedding; nadīyāra badhū sāte — together with the wives of Nadia

**21.10.** The celestial women have resolved: "We shall make merry at the wedding together with the wives of Nadia!"

গন্ধর্ব্ব কিন্নর করে মনে । গীত বাদ্যে মিশিব বিবাহে গুণী সনে ॥

*gandharvva kinnara kare mane | gīta bādye miśiba bibāhe guṇī sane ||*

*Word for word:* gandharvva kinnara kare mane — the gandharvas and kinnaras think; gīta bādye — in song and music; miśiba bibāhe — we shall join at the wedding; guṇī sane — with the artists

**21.11.** The gandharvas and kinnaras think: "We shall join the artists in song and music at the wedding!"

ইন্দ্রের নর্ত্তকীগণ কহে । নদীয়া-নর্ত্তকী-সহ সাজিব বিবাহে ॥

*indrera narttakīgaṇa kahe | nadīyā-narttakī-saha sājiba bibāhe ||*

*Word for word:* indrera narttakī-gaṇa kahe — Indra's dancers say; nadīyā-narttakī-saha — together with the dancers of Nadia; sājiba bibāhe — we shall dress for the wedding

**21.12.** Indra's dancers say: "We shall dress for the wedding together with the dancers of Nadia!"

দেবঋষি উলসিত চিতে । কত অভিলাষ করে বিবাহ দেখিতে ॥

*debaṛṣi ulasita cite | kata abhilāṣa kare bibāha dekhite ||*

*Word for word:* deba-ṛṣi — the divine sages; ulasita cite — rejoicing at heart; kata abhilāṣa kare — how much they long; bibāha dekhite — to see the wedding

**21.13.** The divine sages, rejoicing at heart, long so much to see the wedding!

উথলয়ে যমুনা জাহ্নবী । বিবাহ-কৌতুক-রসে প্রফুল্ল পৃথিবী ॥

*uthalaye yamunā jāhnabī | bibāha-kautuka-rase praphulla pṛthibī ||*

*Word for word:* uthalaye yamunā jāhnabī — the Yamuna and the Jahnavi surge; bibāha-kautuka-rase — in the delight of the wedding festivities; praphulla pṛthibī — the Earth rejoices

**21.14.** The Yamuna and the Jahnavi surge; the Earth rejoices in the delight of the wedding festivities.

ব্রাহ্মণ সজ্জন নদীয়ার । বিবাহে নিমাইর গৃহে গমন সবার ॥

*brāhmaṇa sajjana nadīyāra | bibāhe nimāira gṛhe gamana sabāra ||*

*Word for word:* brāhmaṇa sajjana nadīyāra — the brahmanas and worthy people of Nadia; bibāhe nimāira gṛhe — to the wedding at Nimai's house; gamana sabāra — all go

**21.15.** The brahmanas and worthy people of Nadia — all go to the wedding at Nimai's house.

শচীর নন্দন গৌরহরি । বৈসে সুখে বিবাহ-বিহিত কর্ম্ম করি ॥

*śacīra nandana gaurahari | baise sukhe bibāha-bihita karmma kari ||*

*Word for word:* śacīra nandana gaurahari — the son of Shachi, Gaurahari; baise sukhe — sits in joy; bibāha-bihita karmma kari — having performed the rites enjoined for the wedding

**21.16.** The son of Shachi, Gaurahari, having performed the rites enjoined for the wedding, sits [among them] in joy.

প্রভু-মুখচন্দ্র নিরখিয়া । কহে কত কেউ না ধরিতে পারে হিয়া ॥

*prabhu-mukhacandra nirakhiyā | kahe kata keu nā dharite pāre hiyā ||*

*Word for word:* prabhu-mukha-candra nirakhiyā — gazing at the Lord's moonlike face; kahe kata — how much they say; keu nā dharite pāre hiyā — no one can master his heart

**21.17.** Gazing at the Lord's moonlike face, how much they say — no one can master his heart.

উপজে মঙ্গল যত যত । এক মুখে নরহরি কহিবে তা কত ॥

*upaje maṅgala yata yata | eka mukhe narahari kahibe tā kata ||*

*Word for word:* upaje maṅgala yata yata — how much auspiciousness arises; eka mukhe — with one mouth; narahari kahibe tā kata — how much can Narahari tell of it

**21.18.** How much auspiciousness arises here! How can Narahari tell of it with one mouth?

[^21-43]: GPT1 — p. 98, no. 13 ("yathārāga"; scan, PDF p. 357); GPT2 — section 2.4, no. 13 (catalogue: NG-054). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 806; ed. 1960, vv. 1459–1476;
two lines, 1469–1470, fall on a part lost in the 1960 OCR; the 1960 editor's heading — "the wedding of Sri Nimai"). Variants: 21.13 BR "debṛṣi"; 21.15
BR-1960 "brāhmaṇī(?)" — OCR. Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B.
[^21-44]: "The lord of the gods" is Indra; Shachi here is his consort (not the Lord's mother). Ananta is Ananta-Shesha, the thousand-headed servant of the
Lord. All the demigods and the residents of Vaikuntha themselves come to the Lord's wedding as His servants — thus the poet shows that Gaura is the
Supreme Lord Himself.

## 22. Narahari — "gorā rasamaya sukhera ālaya…" (GPT1 p. 98, no. 14; BR)
*The bridegroom's wedding bath (before the second wedding): the women, crying "ulu-lu", gaze at His face; some tremble, others anoint Him with
perfumes and turmeric, rub oil into His curls, bathe Him with Ganga water, dry Him with a towel and clothe Him in a dry red-bordered cloth. Raga
not specified. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^21-45]

গোরা রসময় সুখের আলয় বিলসে বিবাহ-বিহিত স্নানে ।
কুলবধূ-কুল উলু উলু দিয়া চাহে চারু চাঁদ-মুখের পানে ॥

*gorā rasamaya sukhera ālaya bilase bibāha-bihita snāne |*
*kulabadhū-kula ulu ulu diyā cāhe cāru cām̐da-mukhera pāne ||*

*Word for word:* gorā rasamaya — Gora, full of rasa; sukhera ālaya — the abode of joy; bilase bibāha-bihita snāne — takes the bath enjoined for the wedding; kulabadhū-kula — the wives of noble families; ulu ulu diyā — crying "ulu-ulu"; cāhe cāru cām̐da-mukhera pāne — gaze at the lovely moonlike face

**22.1.** Gora, full of rasa, abode of joy, takes the bath enjoined before the wedding;
the wives of noble families, crying "ulu-lu", gaze at His lovely moonlike face.

কেহ কেহ সে না অঙ্গের বাতাসে কাঁপে ঘন ঘন বিজুরী জিতি ।
কেহ পরশের সাধে গন্ধ-হরিদ্রাদি মাখাইতে না ধরে ধৃতি ॥

*keha keha se nā aṅgera bātāse kām̐pe ghana ghana bijurī jiti |*
*keha paraśera sādhe gandha-haridrādi mākhāite nā dhare dhṛti ||*

*Word for word:* keha keha — some; se nā aṅgera bātāse — at the breeze from that body; kām̐pe ghana ghana — tremble again and again; bijurī jiti — outdoing lightning; keha paraśera sādhe — others, longing to touch; gandha-haridrādi mākhāite — anointing with perfumes, turmeric and the rest; nā dhare dhṛti — cannot master themselves

**22.2.** Some, at the breeze coming from that body, tremble again and again — more than lightning;
others, longing to touch Him, cannot master themselves as they anoint Him with perfumes, turmeric and the rest.

কেহ সুললিত কুন্তলেতে তৈল দিতে কত রঙ্গ উপজে চিতে ।
কেহ অভিষেক করে গঙ্গাজলে ভঙ্গী নানা নাহি উপমা দিতে ॥

*keha sulalita kuntalete taila dite kata raṅga upaje cite |*
*keha abhiṣeka kare gaṅgājale bhaṅgī nānā nāhi upamā dite ||*

*Word for word:* keha sulalita kuntalete — one into the lovely curls; taila dite — rubbing oil; kata raṅga upaje cite — how much merriment rises in the heart; keha abhiṣeka kare gaṅgājale — another bathes Him with Ganga water; bhaṅgī nānā — manifold movements; nāhi upamā dite — beyond compare

**22.3.** One, rubbing oil into His lovely curls, feels so much merriment rise in her heart;
another bathes Him with Ganga water — manifold her movements, beyond compare.

কেহ আধ হাসি ভাসে রসে তনু পোছে পাণি-তোলা লইয়া হাতে ।
রক্তপ্রান্ত শুষ্ক বাস পিন্ধায় এ নরহরি অতি কৌতুক তাতে ॥

*keha ādha hāsi bhāse rase tanu poche pāṇi-tolā laiyā hāte |*
*raktaprānta śuṣka bāsa pindhāya e narahari ati kautuka tāte ||*

*Word for word:* keha ādha hāsi — another, half-smiling; bhāse rase — floating in rasa; tanu poche — dries the body; pāṇi-tolā laiyā hāte — taking a towel in hand; raktaprānta śuṣka bāsa pindhāya — they clothe Him in a dry red-bordered cloth; e narahari ati kautuka tāte — Narahari is in great merriment over it

**22.4.** Yet another, half-smiling, floating in rasa, dries His body, taking a towel in her hands;
they clothe Him in a dry red-bordered cloth — Narahari is in great merriment over it.[^21-46]

[^21-45]: GPT1 — p. 98, no. 14 ("yathārāga"; scan, PDF p. 357); GPT2 — section 2.4, no. 14 (catalogue: NG-055; the catalogue's first line "(gāra samaya…" is a garbling of
"gorā rasamaya"). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, pp. 806–807; ed. 1960, vv. 1477–1480). Variant: 22.4 GPT1 "pidhāya e", BR "pim̐dhā-ae" (the same: "they clothe").
Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. Cf. the bath before the first wedding (no. 3).
[^21-46]: The trembling and the "longing to touch" of the women who perform the bridegroom's bath are an image of the Lord's all-attractive beauty,
conveyed in a lyrical manner; this is a wedding rite and merriment, not nagari-bhava (see note 5).

## 23. Narahari — "ki ānanda śacīra bhabane…" (GPT1 p. 99, no. 15; BR)
*After the bath Gaurahari sits on a wondrous throne; the married women perform auspicious rites; His dear ones come, cannot take their eyes off
Him, and joyfully dress Him for the wedding. Raga not specified. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^21-47]

কি আনন্দ শচীর ভবনে । করয়ে মঙ্গল কর্ম্ম আইহ সুইহ গণে ॥

*ki ānanda śacīra bhabane | karaye maṅgala karmma āiha suiha gaṇe ||*

*Word for word:* ki ānanda śacīra bhabane — what joy in Shachi's house; karaye maṅgala karmma — perform the auspicious rites; āiha suiha gaṇe — the married women

**23.1.** What joy in Shachi's house! The married women perform the auspicious rites.

বিবাহ-বিহিত স্নান করি । বৈসেন অপূর্ব্ব সিংহাসনে গৌরহরি ॥

*bibāha-bihita snāna kari | baisena apūrvva siṃhāsane gaurahari ||*

*Word for word:* bibāha-bihita snāna kari — having taken the bath enjoined for the wedding; baisena apūrvva siṃhāsane — sits on a wondrous throne; gaurahari — Gaurahari

**23.2.** Having taken the bath enjoined before the wedding, Gaurahari sits on a wondrous throne.

রূপের ছটায় মন মোহে । চাঁচর চিকণ কেশ পীঠে ভাল শোহে ॥

*rūpera chaṭāya mana mohe | cām̐cara cikaṇa keśa pīṭhe bhāla śohe ||*

*Word for word:* rūpera chaṭāya — the radiance of His form; mana mohe — enchants the mind; cām̐cara cikaṇa keśa — curling glossy hair; pīṭhe bhāla śohe — falls beautifully down His back

**23.3.** The radiance of His form enchants the mind; His curling, glossy hair falls beautifully down His back.

গোরা-পাশে আসে প্রিয়গণ । বারেক চাহিয়া নারে ফিরাতে নয়ন ॥

*gorā-pāśe āse priyagaṇa | bāreka cāhiyā nāre phirāte nayana ||*

*Word for word:* gorā-pāśe āse priya-gaṇa — His dear ones come to Gora's side; bāreka cāhiyā — having looked once; nāre phirāte nayana — cannot turn their eyes away

**23.4.** His dear ones come to Gora's side — having looked once, they cannot turn their eyes away.

কত না আনন্দে সবে মাতি । বিবাহ-বিহিত বেশ রচে নানা ভাঁতি ॥

*kata nā ānande sabe māti | bibāha-bihita beśa race nānā bhām̐ti ||*

*Word for word:* kata nā ānande sabe māti — all, intoxicated with great joy; bibāha-bihita beśa — the attire enjoined for the wedding; race nānā bhām̐ti — arrange in various ways

**23.5.** Intoxicated with great joy, all array Him in various ways in His wedding attire.

কহিতে কি জানে নরহরি । নিরুপম বেশের বালাই লৈয়া মরি ॥

*kahite ki jāne narahari | nirupama beśera bālāi laiyā mari ||*

*Word for word:* kahite ki jāne narahari — what can Narahari say; nirupama beśera — of this peerless attire; bālāi laiyā mari — let me die taking on myself the misfortunes

**23.6.** What can Narahari say? Let me die taking on myself the misfortunes of this peerless attire![^21-48]

[^21-47]: GPT1 — p. 99, no. 15 ("yathārāga"; scan, PDF p. 358); GPT2 — section 2.4, no. 15. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-286). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912,
p. 807; ed. 1960, vv. 1481–1486). Variants: 23.1 BR "ki ānanda śacī-bhabane"; 23.4 BR "priyagaṇa… nāre phirāite nayana". Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya
or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B.
[^21-48]: "Taking on myself the misfortunes" (bālāi laiyā mari) is a homely formula of love: may every misfortune that threatens the beloved fall on me
(cf. note 7).

## 24. Narahari — "nadīyāra śaśī rasika-śekhara…" (GPT1 p. 99, no. 16; BR)
*The bridegroom's wedding attire: the Moon of Nadia in auspicious wedding array — His body anointed, a crescent-shaped sandal tilaka on His
forehead, a crown of flowers on His head, His eyes lined with collyrium, makara earrings in His ears; paddy and durva tied with thread, a golden
mirror in His right hand. Raga not specified. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^21-49]

নদীয়ার শশী রসিক-শেখর শোভে ভাল শুভ-বিবাহ-বেশে ।
চর্চ্চিতাঙ্গ চারু চন্দন-তিলক অর্দ্ধচন্দ্রাকৃতি ললাটদেশে ॥

*nadīyāra śaśī rasika-śekhara śobhe bhāla śubha-bibāha-beśe |*
*carccitāṅga cāru candana-tilaka arddhacandrākṛti lalāṭadeśe ||*

*Word for word:* nadīyāra śaśī — the Moon of Nadia; rasika-śekhara — crown of the connoisseurs of rasa; śobhe bhāla śubha-bibāha-beśe — shines beautifully in auspicious wedding attire; carccitāṅga — His body anointed; cāru candana-tilaka — a lovely sandal tilaka; arddha-candrākṛti — shaped like a half-moon; lalāṭa-deśe — on the forehead

**24.1.** The Moon of Nadia, crown of the connoisseurs of rasa, shines beautifully in auspicious wedding attire;
His body anointed, on His forehead a lovely sandal tilaka shaped like a half-moon.

নানা পুষ্পময় বিচিত্র মুকুট শিরে সে না ছাঁদে কে নাহি ভুলে ।
আঁখে কাজরের রেখা নব কুলবতী-সতীগণে না রাখে কুলে ॥

*nānā puṣpamaya bicitra mukuṭa śire se nā chām̐de ke nāhi bhule |*
*ām̐khe kājarera rekhā naba kulabatī-satīgaṇe nā rākhe kule ||*

*Word for word:* nānā puṣpamaya bicitra mukuṭa śire — on His head a wondrous crown of many flowers; se nā chām̐de — by its arrangement; ke nāhi bhule — whom would it not enchant; ām̐khe kājarera rekhā — the line of collyrium at His eyes; naba kulabatī-satī-gaṇe — the young chaste wives of noble families; nā rākhe kule — does not keep within the bounds of their families

**24.2.** On His head a wondrous crown of many flowers: whom would its arrangement not enchant?
The line of collyrium at His eyes does not let the young chaste wives of noble families stay within the bounds of their families.[^21-50]

শ্রুতিমূলে মণি-মকর-কুণ্ডল ঝলকয়ে কিবা গণ্ডের ছটা ।
সুমধুর হাসিমাখা মুখখানি নিছনি পূর্ণিম-চাঁদের ঘটা ॥

*śrutimūle maṇi-makara-kuṇḍala jhalakaye kibā gaṇḍera chaṭā |*
*sumadhura hāsimākhā mukhakhāni nichani pūrṇima-cām̐dera ghaṭā ||*

*Word for word:* śruti-mūle — at the roots of the ears; maṇi-makara-kuṇḍala — jewelled makara earrings; jhalakaye kibā gaṇḍera chaṭā — how the radiance of the cheeks flashes; sumadhura hāsi-mākhā mukha-khāni — to the sweetly smiling face; nichani — offer themselves; pūrṇima-cām̐dera ghaṭā — hosts of full moons

**24.3.** At the roots of His ears jewelled makara earrings; how the radiance of His cheeks flashes!
To His sweetly smiling face hosts of full moons offer themselves.

সূত্রে বাঁধা ধান্য দূর্ব্বাদি সুন্দর হেম-দরপণ দক্ষিণ করে ।
নরহরি ভণে ভূষণে ভূষিত প্রতি অঙ্গ হেরি কে ধৃতি ধরে ॥

*sūtre bām̐dhā dhānya dūrvvādi sundara hema-darapaṇa dakṣiṇa kare |*
*narahari bhaṇe bhūṣaṇe bhūṣita prati aṅga heri ke dhṛti dhare ||*

*Word for word:* sūtre bām̐dhā — tied with thread; dhānya dūrvvādi — paddy, durva and the rest; sundara hema-darapaṇa — a beautiful golden mirror; dakṣiṇa kare — in the right hand; narahari bhaṇe — says Narahari; bhūṣaṇe bhūṣita prati aṅga heri — seeing every limb adorned with ornaments; ke dhṛti dhare — who can keep composure

**24.4.** Paddy, durva and the rest tied with thread, and a beautiful golden mirror in His right hand;
says Narahari: seeing every limb adorned with ornaments, who can keep his composure?

[^21-49]: GPT1 — p. 99, no. 16 ("yathārāga"; scan, PDF p. 358); GPT2 — section 2.4, no. 16 (catalogue: NG-056). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 807; ed. 1960, vv. 1487–1490).
Variants: 24.4 GPT1 "dakṣiṇa dakṣiṇa kare" (the word repeated), BR "dakṣiṇa kare" — following the BR; 24.3 GPT1 "purṇima-cām̐dera", BR "pūrṇimā-cāndera". Not in PK, KGC,
PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. Next in GPT1 (no. 17 — signed Ghanashyama; no. 18 onwards — Narahari) and in the BR comes the
wedding procession to the house of Sanatana Mishra and the wedding (chapter 22).
[^21-50]: The praise of the bridegroom's beauty is expressed in a conventional turn of love poetry (a beauty before which women "do not stay within the
bounds of their families" is a familiar formula about Krishna); the poet speaks of the Lord's all-attractive beauty. Translated faithfully to the
author; on the position of the tradition see note 5.

---

# Chapter 22. Appendix. Padas signed "Narahari" from the Gaura-pada-tarangini — VI: the wedding with Vishnupriya; the beginning of the ashtakaliya

*Continuation of the appendix (the introductory note on the two Naraharis, on the arguments for attribution and on the marks in the
headings is in ch. 17). Chapter 22: the end of GPT section 2.4 "The second marriage" — the wedding procession to the house of Sanatana
Mishra, the reception of the bridegroom, the wedding, the gods and celestial women at the wedding, the bridal chamber (vasara), the morning
after the wedding and the Lord's return home with Vishnupriya (nos. 1–16; GPT 2.4 nos. 18–20, 22–34); the beginning of section 5.2
"Ashtakaliya" — the songs of Gaura's awakening at the end of the night (nos. 17–26; GPT 5.2 nos. 1–10). Narahari Chakravarti quotes all the
wedding padas of the chapter one after another in the 12th wave of the Bhakti-ratnakara (Ishana shows Srinivasa the house of Jagannatha
Mishra), and all the awakening songs in his Gaura-charita-chintamani (kiranas 2–3: the last part of the night and the awakening). Before
translation the signatures in these sections were checked throughout, in the OCR and on the scan; the Bhakti-ratnakara (ed. 1960, vv.
1491–1626) was read continuously. Not translated: 2.4 no. 17 — signed Ghanashyama (outside the appendix); no. 21 — a pada in nagari-bhava
(assigned to the section of nagari padas); nos. 35–38 — without the Narahari signature: an extract from Lochana Dasa's Chaitanya-mangala
(no. 38 is signed "dāsa trilocana"; translated with Lochana, *Chaitanya-mangala*, Adi-khanda, part 14, vv. ≈146–178); nos. 39–40 — Vrindavana Dasa (= CB Adi 15).
The base text is GPT1 (doubtful places from the scan), collated with GPT2, the BR (eds. 1912 and 1960) and the Gaura-charita-chintamani (ed.
1947); PK, KGC, PS and the Gita-chandrodaya have been checked. On Vishnupriya and the wedding rites as lila see note 2; on the motif of the
women of Nadia, note 5; on the ashtakaliya as eternal lila, note 36. The notes of the GPT editors are not reproduced.*

## 1. Narahari — "gaura rasika-śekharabara…" (GPT1 p. 100, section 2.4, no. 18; BR)
*The wedding procession: Gaura, surrounded by brahmanas, sets out for the wedding in a palanquin; instruments of the four kinds sound;
invisible celestial dancers dance together with earthly ones, the gandharvas sing with the singers; Ananta, Brahma, Shiva, Indra, Ganesha,
Parvati float in an ocean of joy; horses, elephants, guards, jesters, hundreds of banners; having gone round Nadia and paused on the bank of
the Suradhuni, the procession approaches Mishra's house. Raga not stated. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR; ornate
Vrajabuli.*[^22-1]

গৌর রসিক-শেখরবর, বেষ্টিত প্রিয় বিপ্রনিকর, হরষিত সুবিবাহ করব, ইথে চলু চঢ়ি চৌদোলে ।
তত ঘন আনদ্ধ শুষির, বাদ্য চতুর্ব্বিধ সুরুচির, বাজত বহু ভাঁতি শবদ ভরল গগন-মণ্ডলে ॥

*gaura rasika-śekharabara, beṣṭita priya bipranikara, haraṣita subibāha karaba, ithe calu caṛhi caudole |*
*tata ghana ānaddha śuṣira, bādya caturvvidha surucira, bājata bahu bhām̐ti śabada bharala gagana-maṇḍale ||*

*Word for word:* gaura — Gaura; rasika-śekhara-bara — best of the crowns of the connoisseurs of rasa; beṣṭita priya bipra-nikara — surrounded by a host of dear brahmanas; haraṣita — joyful; subibāha karaba — I shall celebrate an auspicious wedding; ithe — with this [intent]; calu caṛhi caudole — set out, mounting the palanquin; tata — strings; ghana — metal (cymbals, gongs); ānaddha — skin-covered (drums); śuṣira — winds; bādya caturvvidha surucira — splendid instruments of four kinds; bājata bahu bhām̐ti — sound in many manners; śabada bharala gagana-maṇḍale — the sound filled the vault of the sky

**1.1.** Gaura, best of the crowns of the connoisseurs of rasa, surrounded by His dear brahmanas — "joyfully I shall celebrate an auspicious
wedding!" — sets out, mounting the palanquin;
strings, metal, drums and winds — splendid instruments of the four kinds — sound in many manners: the sound has filled the vault of the sky.[^22-2]

সর্ব্ব বাদ্য শোভন নব, মর্দ্দল মুদবর্দ্ধন রব, ধো ধো ধিগি তগ ধিলঙ্গ, ধা ধা নি নি নিধিয়া ।
অলখিত সুর-নর্ত্তকীগণ, নর্ত্তকী সহ লাস্য সঘন, ভণ তক তক থৈ থৈ থৈ, আই অতি নি নি নি তিয়া ॥

*sarvva bādya śobhana naba, marddala mudabarddhana raba, dho dho dhigi taga dhilaṅga, dhā dhā ni ni nidhiyā |*
*alakhita sura-narttakīgaṇa, narttakī saha lāsya saghana, bhaṇa taka taka thai thai thai, āi ati ni ni ni tiyā ||*

*Word for word:* sarvva bādya śobhana naba — all the instruments splendid and new; marddala — the mardala (drum); muda-barddhana raba — a sound increasing joy; dho dho dhigi taga dhilaṅga, dhā dhā ni ni nidhiyā — onomatopoeia of the drum-strokes; alakhita — invisible; sura-narttakī-gaṇa — the celestial dancers; narttakī saha — together with the [earthly] dancers; lāsya saghana — dance the lasya without pause; bhaṇa taka taka thai thai thai, āi ati ni ni ni tiyā — the dance-count

**1.2.** All the instruments are splendid and new; the boom of the mardala increases the joy: "dho-dho dhigi taga dhilanga, dha-dha ni-ni
nidhiya";
invisible, the celestial dancers together with the [earthly] dancers dance the lasya without pause: "bhana taka-taka thai-thai-thai, ai ati
ni-ni-ni tiya".

গায়কগণে মিলি উলসিত, গায়ত গন্ধর্ব্ব ললিত, শ্রুতি সুমধুর গ্রামাদি বিবিধে কৌতুক পরকাশয়ে ।
দশশত মুখ বিহি মহেশ, গণ সহ সুরপতি গণেশ, গিরিজাদিক ধৃতি কি ধরব সুখ-সায়রে ভাসয়ে ॥

*gāyakagaṇe mili ulasita, gāyata gandharvva lalita, śruti sumadhura grāmādi bibidhe kautuka parakāśaye |*
*daśaśata mukha bihi maheśa, gaṇa saha surapati gaṇeśa, girijādika dhṛti ki dharaba sukha-sāyare bhāsaye ||*

*Word for word:* gāyaka-gaṇe mili — together with the singers; ulasita — rejoicing; gāyata gandharvva lalita — the gandharvas sing sweetly; śruti — the shrutis (intervals); sumadhura grāmādi — sweet gramas and the rest; bibidhe — in many ways; kautuka parakāśaye — display their delight; daśa-śata mukha — the Thousand-mouthed [Ananta]; bihi — Brahma; maheśa — Shiva; gaṇa saha surapati — the lord of the gods [Indra] with his retinue; gaṇeśa — Ganesha; girijādika — Girija (Parvati) and others; dhṛti ki dharaba — how could they keep composure?; sukha-sāyare bhāsaye — float in an ocean of joy

**1.3.** Together with the singers, rejoicing, the gandharvas sing sweetly; shrutis, sweet gramas and the rest — in every manner they
display their delight;
the Thousand-mouthed One, Brahma, Mahesha, the lord of the gods with his retinue, Ganesha, Girija and others — how could they keep their
composure? — float in an ocean of joy.[^22-3]

হয় গজ বহু অস্ত্রধারী, প্রকটত গুণ হাস্যকারী, লসত শত পতাকাদিক ভীড়ে পথ রোকঈ ।
নদীয়াপুর ভরমি ভরমি, সুরধুনী-তীরে বিরমি বিরমি, মিশ্রগৃহ সমীপ নরহরি শোভা অবলোকঈ ॥

*haya gaja bahu astradhārī, prakaṭata guṇa hāsyakārī, lasata śata patākādika bhīṛe patha rokaī |*
*nadīyāpura bharami bharami, suradhunī-tīre birami birami, miśragṛha samīpa narahari śobhā abalokaī ||*

*Word for word:* haya — horses; gaja — elephants; bahu astra-dhārī — many armed men; prakaṭata guṇa hāsya-kārī — the jesters display their skill; lasata śata patākādika — hundreds of banners and the like shine; bhīṛe patha rokaī — the crowd blocks the road; nadīyā-pura bharami bharami — going round the town of Nadia; suradhunī-tīre birami birami — pausing again and again on the bank of the Suradhuni (Ganga); miśra-gṛha samīpa — near Mishra's house; narahari śobhā abalokaī — Narahari beholds the splendour

**1.4.** Horses, elephants, many armed men; jesters display their arts; hundreds of banners and the like shine — the crowd blocks the road;
going round the town of Nadia, pausing again and again on the bank of the Suradhuni — near Mishra's house Narahari beholds this
splendour.

[^22-1]: GPT1 — p. 100, section 2.4 ("the second marriage"), no. 18 ("yathārāga"; scan, PDF p. 359); GPT2 — section 2.4, no. 18 (catalogue: NG-057). BR — 12th wave
(ed. 1912, pp. 809–810; ed. 1960, vv. 1495–1498), immediately after pada no. 17 on the same procession signed by Ghanashyama ("ghana ghanaśyāma hiya umatāaī";
= BR vv. 1491–1494 — outside the appendix); after it the BR gives all the wedding padas of this chapter one after another (vv. 1499–1614), then prose:
Vishnupriya's service to her mother-in-law and the Lord's journey to Gaya (vv. 1615–1625). Variants: 1.1 GPT1 "surata cira" (misprint?), BR "surucira" —
following the BR; 1.3 BR "surapati" — the same. Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. The wedding with Vishnupriya —
CB Adi 15; CC Adi 16; Murari 1.14.
[^22-2]: Vishnupriya is the eternal consort of the Lord, His own Bhu-shakti (the energy of the Earth); she is not a worldly wife but His own
energy, and the wedding with her is the Lord's lila (note 30 of chapter 21). The Lord is bound by nothing that is enjoined; He accepts the
wedding rites following the lila, for the joy of His mother and His associates (note 2 of chapter 21). So are all the padas of the chapter
about the Lord's "marrying" to be understood. The instruments "of the four kinds" (tata ghana ānaddha śuṣira) — strings, metal (cymbals, gongs),
skin-covered (drums) and winds — are the classical division of Indian music.
[^22-3]: As in the pada on the wedding day (no. 21 of chapter 21), the demigods gather at the Lord's wedding: Ananta-Shesha ("the Thousand-mouthed
One"), Brahma, Shiva (Mahesha), Indra ("the lord of the gods"), Ganesha, Parvati (Girija); invisible to men, they come to serve their Lord
and to behold His lila. The gandharvas are the celestial singers; shrutis and gramas are the intervals and scales of Indian music; lasya is
the tender, "feminine" kind of dance.

## 2. Narahari — "gorācām̐dera bibāha dekhibāre…" (GPT1 p. 100, no. 19; BR)
*The wives of noble families, with great longing, adorn themselves to see Gorachand's wedding: collyrium, braids with golden clasps,
sindura and sandal, necklaces, flowers in their ears, silk saris; with stately gait they go to the wedding, and on seeing the poet's Lord
they whisper. Raga not stated. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^22-4]

গোরাচাঁদের বিবাহ দেখিবারে ।
কত না মনের সাধে, সাজয়ে কুলের বধূ, ধৈরজ ধরিতে কেউ নারে ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*gorācām̐dera bibāha dekhibāre |*
*kata nā manera sādhe, sājaye kulera badhū, dhairaja dharite keu nāre || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* gorācām̐dera bibāha dekhibāre — to see Gorachand's wedding; kata nā manera sādhe — with what longing of heart; sājaye kulera badhū — the wives of noble families adorn themselves; dhairaja dharite keu nāre — no one can keep her composure

**2.1.** To see Gorachand's wedding, with what longing the wives of noble families adorn themselves — not one can keep her composure!

রসের আবেশে আঁখে, অঞ্জন রঞ্জয় কিবা, বঙ্কিম চাহনি বঙ্ক ভুরু ।
চিকণ চিকুর বেণী, পীঠেতে লোটায় কিবা, কনক-নির্ম্মিত ঝাঁপা চারু ॥

*rasera ābeśe ām̐khe, añjana rañjaya kibā, baṅkima cāhani baṅka bhuru |*
*cikaṇa cikura beṇī, pīṭhete loṭāya kibā, kanaka-nirmmita jhām̐pā cāru ||*

*Word for word:* rasera ābeśe — absorbed in rasa; ām̐khe añjana rañjaya kibā — how charmingly they line their eyes with collyrium; baṅkima cāhani — sidelong glances; baṅka bhuru — arched brows; cikaṇa cikura beṇī — smooth braids; pīṭhete loṭāya kibā — how they fall down the back; kanaka-nirmmita jhām̐pā cāru — lovely golden clasps

**2.2.** Absorbed in rasa, how charmingly they line their eyes with collyrium — sidelong glances, arched brows;
smooth braids fall down their backs — how lovely the golden clasps!

কপালে সিন্দুর-বিন্দু, চন্দন শোভয়ে কিবা, ঝলমল করে আভরণে ।
মণি-মুকুতার মালা, গলায় দোলয়ে কিবা, গন্ধরাজ চাঁপা দেই কাণে ॥

*kapāle sindura-bindu, candana śobhaye kibā, jhalamala kare ābharaṇe |*
*maṇi-mukutāra mālā, galāya dolaye kibā, gandharāja cām̐pā dei kāṇe ||*

*Word for word:* kapāle sindura-bindu — a dot of sindura on the forehead; candana śobhaye kibā — how beautifully the sandal shines; jhalamala kare ābharaṇe — the ornaments glitter; maṇi-mukutāra mālā — necklaces of gems and pearls; galāya dolaye kibā — how they sway on the neck; gandharāja cām̐pā — gandharaja and champaka flowers; dei kāṇe — they put in their ears

**2.3.** On the forehead a dot of sindura, how beautifully the sandal shines! Their ornaments glitter;
on their necks sway necklaces of gems and pearls; in their ears they put gandharaja and champaka flowers.

পরিয়া পাটের শাড়ী, ছাড়িয়া ভবন কিবা, চলি যায় গজেন্দ্র-গমনে ।
নরহরি-নাথে নিরখিয়া হিয়া উথলয়ে, কেউ কিছু কহে কারু কাণে ॥

*pariyā pāṭera śāṛī, chāṛiyā bhabana kibā, cali yāya gajendra-gamane |*
*narahari-nāthe nirakhiyā hiyā uthalaye, keu kichu kahe kāru kāṇe ||*

*Word for word:* pariyā pāṭera śāṛī — putting on silk saris; chāṛiyā bhabana — leaving their homes; cali yāya gajendra-gamane — they go with the gait of a royal elephant; narahari-nāthe nirakhiyā — seeing the Lord of Narahari; hiyā uthalaye — the heart overflows; keu kichu kahe kāru kāṇe — one whispers something in another's ear

**2.4.** Putting on silk saris, leaving their homes, they walk with a stately gait like that of a royal elephant;
seeing Narahari's Lord — the heart overflows — one whispers something into another's ear.[^22-5]

[^22-4]: GPT1 — p. 100, no. 19 (scan, PDF p. 359); GPT2 — section 2.4, no. 19 (catalogue: NG-058). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 810; ed. 1960, vv. 1499–1502).
Variant: in 2.3 the BR has the second half-lines interchanged ("…gandharāja cām̐pā dei kāṇe" in the first line, "…jhalamala kare ābharaṇe" in the second). Not in PK,
KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. Line 2.1 is the refrain (dhru). The first line is the same as that of the pada on the
first wedding (2.3 no. 22, no. 7 of chapter 21), but the text is different.
[^22-5]: The poet describes the delight of the women of Nadia at the Lord's wedding in words close to the motif of the townswomen (nagaris)
enamoured of Gaura. We translate faithfully to the author; but the Gaudiya tradition (Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja,
Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati) does not accept the worship of Gaura in the mood of "Gaura-nagari": Gaura is Krishna Himself in the mood and
lustre of Radha; He came to taste Her love, not to enjoy as a nagara. The Lord's attractiveness for the people of Navadvipa is the quality
of Bhagavan, who attracts all; it is not worldly passion. The same holds for the other padas of the chapter about the women of Nadia (nos.
3, 11, 12; cf. note 5 of chapter 21). GPT pada no. 21 ("āhā mari ki madhura rīti": the "nagaris of Nadia" dream of being "with Gora day and night" and of
touching His golden body in the bridal chamber; = BR vv. 1507–1510) is openly in nagari-bhava and is assigned to the section of nagari padas.

## 3. Narahari — "sai ai dekha nadīyāra cām̐de…" (GPT1 p. 101, no. 20; BR)
*A woman says to her friend: look at the Moon of Nadia — hundreds of Kamadevas, offering themselves for His beauty, fall weeping at His
feet; His glance, His face, His smile; who has arranged this wedding attire — the crown, the curls, the yellow thread and durva, the golden
mirror? Raga not stated. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^22-6]

সই অই দেখ নদীয়ার চাঁদে ।
ভুবনমোহন ও না রূপের নিছনি লৈঞা, কত শত মদন চরণে পড়ি কাঁদে ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*sai ai dekha nadīyāra cām̐de |*
*bhubanamohana o nā rūpera nichani laiñā, kata śata madana caraṇe paṛi kām̐de || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* sai — friend; ai dekha nadīyāra cām̐de — look, there is the Moon of Nadia; bhubana-mohana — world-enchanting; o nā rūpera nichani laiñā — offering themselves for that beauty; kata śata madana — hundreds upon hundreds of Madanas; caraṇe paṛi kām̐de — fall at His feet and weep

**3.1.** Friend, look — there is the Moon of Nadia! Offering themselves for His world-enchanting beauty, hundreds upon hundreds of Madanas
fall weeping at His feet.

রসে ডুবু ডুবু দুটী নয়ান-চাহনি, বিধি সিরজিল যুবতী বধিতে হেন বাসি ।
বদন-চাঁদের শোভা, চাঁদের গরব হরে, হাসি মিশে অমিয়া বরষে রাশি রাশি ॥

*rase ḍubu ḍubu duṭī nayāna-cāhani, bidhi sirajila yubatī badhite hena bāsi |*
*badana-cām̐dera śobhā, cām̐dera garaba hare, hāsi miśe amiyā baraṣe rāśi rāśi ||*

*Word for word:* rase ḍubu ḍubu — drowning in rasa; duṭī nayāna-cāhani — the glance of the two eyes; bidhi sirajila — the Creator made; yubatī badhite — to slay young women; hena bāsi — so I think; badana-cām̐dera śobhā — the beauty of the moon-face; cām̐dera garaba hare — takes away the moon's pride; hāsi miśe — mingled with the smile; amiyā baraṣe rāśi rāśi — nectar pours down in heaps

**3.2.** The glance of His two eyes, drowning in rasa — I think the Creator made it to slay young women;
the beauty of His moon-face takes away the moon's pride; mingled with His smile, nectar pours down in streams.[^22-7]

আহা মরি মরি যেন কত না মনের সাধে, কেবা বনাইল এ না বিবাহের বেশ ।
পরম উজ্জ্বল অতি বিচিত্র মুকুট মাথে, ঝাঁপিয়াছে চিকণ চাঁচর চারু কেশ ॥

*āhā mari mari yena kata nā manera sādhe, kebā banāila e nā bibāhera beśa |*
*parama ujjvala ati bicitra mukuṭa māthe, jhām̐piyāche cikaṇa cām̐cara cāru keśa ||*

*Word for word:* āhā mari mari — ah, I die, I die; yena kata nā manera sādhe — as if with what longing of heart; kebā banāila — who has arranged; e nā bibāhera beśa — this wedding attire; parama ujjvala ati bicitra mukuṭa māthe — on His head a wondrous, dazzlingly bright crown; jhām̐piyāche — have covered; cikaṇa cām̐cara cāru keśa — smooth, curling, lovely locks

**3.3.** Ah, I die, I die! With what longing of heart has someone arranged this wedding attire!
On His head a wondrous, dazzlingly bright crown, covered by His smooth, curling, lovely locks.

মঙ্গল-বিহিত পীতসূতা দূর্ব্বাদল করে, নিরুপম কনক-দর্পণ ভাল শোহে ।
পরিধেয় বসন ভূষণ সুমধুর, প্রতি অঙ্গের ভঙ্গীতে নরহরি-মন মোহে ॥

*maṅgala-bihita pītasūtā dūrvvādala kare, nirupama kanaka-darpaṇa bhāla śohe |*
*paridheya basana bhūṣaṇa sumadhura, prati aṅgera bhaṅgīte narahari-mana mohe ||*

*Word for word:* maṅgala-bihita — enjoined for the auspicious rite; pīta-sūtā — the yellow thread; dūrvvā-dala kare — blades of durva in the hand; nirupama kanaka-darpaṇa — the incomparable golden mirror; bhāla śohe — shines beautifully; paridheya basana bhūṣaṇa sumadhura — the garments and ornaments are sweet; prati aṅgera bhaṅgīte — by the grace of every limb; narahari-mana mohe — enchants Narahari's mind

**3.4.** In His hand the yellow thread and the blades of durva enjoined for the auspicious rite; the incomparable golden mirror shines
beautifully;
His garments and ornaments are sweet; by the grace of every limb [He] enchants Narahari's mind.

[^22-6]: GPT1 — p. 101, no. 20 (scan, PDF p. 360); GPT2 — section 2.4, no. 20 (catalogue: NG-059). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 810; ed. 1960, vv. 1503–1506).
The variants are minor (3.1 GPT1 "laiñā", BR "laiyā"; 3.3 GPT1 "enā", BR "e nā"). Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B.
Line 3.1 is the refrain. The next pada in the GPT and the BR (no. 21) is in nagari-bhava (note 5).
[^22-7]: "Made it to slay young women" is a conventional formula of love poetry about Krishna's beauty; here it speaks of the all-attractive
beauty of the Lord (see note 5). Madana is Kamadeva, the god of love; hundreds of Madanas "offer themselves" (nichani — give themselves as a
ransom) for His beauty: it surpasses the beauty of Kamadeva himself.

## 4. Narahari — "sanātana miśrera bhabane…" (GPT1 pp. 101–102, no. 22; BR)
*The reception of the bridegroom in the house of Sanatana Mishra: music sounds; Sanatana with his kin comes out to meet Him; the
bridegroom shines in the palanquin; around Him brahmanas and worthy men, a countless crowd; the blind, holding others' hands, stand
where Gaurachandra is, the lame come out on the road, the infirm totter along with sticks; all sing Gora's glories; children and old men
dance; hundreds of lamps burn; Mishra, embracing his son-in-law, brings Him into the house, seats Him on a wondrous seat, showers Him
with flowers and performs the reception of the bridegroom. Raga not stated. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^22-8]

সনাতন মিশ্রের ভবনে । যে মঙ্গল-ক্রিয়া তা কহিতে কেবা জানে ॥

*sanātana miśrera bhabane | ye maṅgala-kriyā tā kahite kebā jāne ||*

*Word for word:* sanātana miśrera bhabane — in the house of Sanatana Mishra; ye maṅgala-kriyā — what auspicious rites; tā kahite kebā jāne — who knows how to tell them

**4.1.** What auspicious rites are performed in the house of Sanatana Mishra — who could describe them?

বাজে নানা বাদ্য শোভাময় । উথলে আনন্দ-কোলাহল অতিশয় ॥

*bāje nānā bādya śobhāmaya | uthale ānanda-kolāhala atiśaya ||*

*Word for word:* bāje nānā bādya śobhāmaya — all kinds of splendid instruments sound; uthale ānanda-kolāhala atiśaya — an immense joyful clamour surges up

**4.2.** All kinds of splendid instruments sound; an immense joyful clamour surges up.

বন্ধুগণ সনে সনাতন । আগুসরি আসে নিতে জামাতা-রতন ॥

*bandhugaṇa sane sanātana | āgusari āse nite jāmātā-ratana ||*

*Word for word:* bandhu-gaṇa sane sanātana — Sanatana with his kin; āgusari āse — comes forward; nite jāmātā-ratana — to receive his jewel of a son-in-law

**4.3.** Sanatana with his kin comes forward to receive his jewel of a son-in-law.

জামাতা কি মনোহর সাজে । ঝলমল করে দিব্য চতুর্দ্দোল মাঝে ॥

*jāmātā ki manohara sāje | jhalamala kare dibya caturddola mājhe ||*

*Word for word:* jāmātā ki manohara sāje — how captivating the son-in-law's attire; jhalamala kare — He shines; dibya caturddola mājhe — in the midst of the wondrous palanquin

**4.4.** How captivating the son-in-law's attire! He shines in the midst of the wondrous palanquin.

চতুর্দ্দিকে ব্রাহ্মণ সজ্জন । অসংখ্য লোকের ভীড়ে না যায় গণন ॥

*caturddike brāhmaṇa sajjana | asaṃkhya lokera bhīṛe nā yāya gaṇana ||*

*Word for word:* caturddike — on all sides; brāhmaṇa sajjana — brahmanas and worthy men; asaṃkhya lokera bhīṛe — in the crowd of countless people; nā yāya gaṇana — there is no counting

**4.5.** On all sides brahmanas and worthy men; the crowd of countless people cannot be counted.

কারু হাতে হাত দিয়া অন্ধ । দাঁড়াইয়া রহয়ে যেদিকে গৌরচন্দ্র ॥

*kāru hāte hāta diyā andha | dām̐ṛāiyā rahaye yedike gauracandra ||*

*Word for word:* kāru hāte hāta diyā — holding another's hand; andha — the blind; dām̐ṛāiyā rahaye — stand; yedike gauracandra — on the side where Gaurachandra is

**4.6.** The blind, holding others' hands, stand on the side where Gaurachandra is.[^22-9]

পঙ্গুগণ রাজপথে আসি । দেখয়ে মনের সাধে গোরা-রূপরাশি ॥

*paṅgugaṇa rājapathe āsi | dekhaye manera sādhe gorā-rūparāśi ||*

*Word for word:* paṅgu-gaṇa rājapathe āsi — the lame, coming out on the main road; dekhaye manera sādhe — gaze to their heart's content; gorā-rūpa-rāśi — at Gora's wealth of beauty

**4.7.** The lame come out on the main road and gaze to their heart's content at Gora's beauty.

যেবা কেউ চলিতে না পারে । ধরিয়া লগুড় পথে আইসে ধীরে ধীরে ॥

*yebā keu calite nā pāre | dhariyā laguṛa pathe āise dhīre dhīre ||*

*Word for word:* yebā keu calite nā pāre — whoever cannot walk; dhariyā laguṛa — holding a stick; pathe āise dhīre dhīre — comes slowly along the road

**4.8.** Whoever cannot walk comes slowly along the road, leaning on a stick.

কেবা নাহি গোরাগুণ গায় । না জানয়ে কত সুখ বাঢ়য়ে হিয়ায় ॥

*kebā nāhi gorāguṇa gāya | nā jānaye kata sukha bāṛhaye hiyāya ||*

*Word for word:* kebā nāhi gorā-guṇa gāya — who does not sing Gora's glories; nā jānaye — they do not know; kata sukha bāṛhaye hiyāya — how much happiness grows in the heart

**4.9.** Who does not sing Gora's glories! They do not know how happiness grows in their hearts.

নানা বাদ্য বাজে নানা ছাঁদে । নাচে বালবৃদ্ধ কেউ থির নাহি বাঁধে ॥

*nānā bādya bāje nānā chām̐de | nāce bālabṛddha keu thira nāhi bām̐dhe ||*

*Word for word:* nānā bādya bāje nānā chām̐de — various instruments sound in various manners; nāce bāla-bṛddha — children and old men dance; keu thira nāhi bām̐dhe — no one keeps still

**4.10.** Various instruments sound in various manners; children and old men dance — no one can stand still.

কত শত মহাদীপ জ্বলে । ধরণী ছাইল আলো গগন-মণ্ডলে ॥

*kata śata mahādīpa jvale | dharaṇī chāila ālo gagana-maṇḍale ||*

*Word for word:* kata śata mahā-dīpa jvale — hundreds of great lamps burn; dharaṇī chāila ālo gagana-maṇḍale — light has covered the earth and the vault of the sky

**4.11.** Hundreds of great lamps burn; the light has filled the earth and the vault of the sky.

কেহ কুন রঙ্গ প্রকাশয় । ব্যাপয়ে সকল মহীতলে যাহা হয় ॥

*keha kuna raṅga prakāśaya | byāpaye sakala mahītale yāhā haya ||*

*Word for word:* keha kuna raṅga prakāśaya — someone displays some entertainment; byāpaye sakala mahī-tale — spreads over the whole earth; yāhā haya — whatever happens

**4.12.** Someone displays some entertainment — and all that happens there spreads over the whole earth.

মিশ্র মহা উল্লসিত মনে । জামাতা লইয়া কোলে প্রবেশে ভবনে ॥

*miśra mahā ullasita mane | jāmātā laiyā kole prabeśe bhabane ||*

*Word for word:* miśra mahā ullasita mane — Mishra, greatly rejoicing at heart; jāmātā laiyā kole — taking his son-in-law in his embrace; prabeśe bhabane — enters the house

**4.13.** Mishra, greatly rejoicing, embracing his son-in-law, enters the house.

অপূর্ব্ব আসনে বসাইয়া । করে পুষ্পবৃষ্টি চাঁদমুখ-পানে চাঞা ॥

*apūrvva āsane basāiyā | kare puṣpabṛṣṭi cām̐damukha-pāne cāñā ||*

*Word for word:* apūrvva āsane basāiyā — seating [Him] on a wondrous seat; kare puṣpa-bṛṣṭi — he showers flowers; cām̐da-mukha-pāne cāñā — looking at the moon-face

**4.14.** Seating [Him] on a wondrous seat, he showers [Him] with flowers, gazing at His moon-face.

জয় জয়ধ্বনি অনিবার । বাদাবাদি বায় বাদ্য বাদক দোঁহার ॥

*jaya jayadhvani anibāra | bādābādi bāya bādya bādaka dom̐hāra ||*

*Word for word:* jaya jaya-dhvani anibāra — cries of "jaya, jaya" without pause; bādābādi — in rivalry; bāya bādya — play the instruments; bādaka dom̐hāra — the musicians of both sides

**4.15.** Cries of "jaya, jaya" sound without pause; the musicians of both sides play their instruments in rivalry.

মিশ্র করে জামাতা-বরণ । নরহরি তাহা দেখি জুড়ায় নয়ন ॥

*miśra kare jāmātā-baraṇa | narahari tāhā dekhi juṛāya nayana ||*

*Word for word:* miśra kare jāmātā-baraṇa — Mishra performs the reception of his son-in-law; narahari tāhā dekhi — Narahari, seeing it; juṛāya nayana — refreshes his eyes

**4.16.** Mishra performs the reception of his son-in-law; Narahari, seeing it, refreshes his eyes.

[^22-8]: GPT1 — pp. 101–102, no. 22 (scan, PDF pp. 360–361); GPT2 — section 2.4, no. 22 (catalogue: NG-061; the number in the catalogue is garbled — "no. 2").
BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, pp. 811–812; ed. 1960, vv. 1511–1526). Variants: 4.12 GPT1 "kula-raṅga", BR "kuna raṅga" ("some entertainment") — following the BR;
others are minor. Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. The reception of the bridegroom in Sanatana's house — CB
Adi 15; in Lochana — *Chaitanya-mangala*, Adi-khanda, part 14, vv. 146–147.
[^22-9]: The blind, the lame, the infirm — an image by which the poet shows that the Lord draws all to Himself without distinction. "The
reception" (baraṇa) is the honouring of the bridegroom by the bride's father: water for washing the feet, arghya, clothes, ornaments, a garland
(in Lochana, vv. 146–147, 153). "Of both sides" (dom̐hāra) — the musicians of the bridegroom and of the bride.

## 5. Narahari — "nadīyāra śaśī bilasaye cāru…" (GPT1 p. 102, no. 23; BR)
*The bridegroom under the wedding canopy: Vishnupriya's mother, under various pretexts, looks at Him again and again, her feet not
touching the ground; with the married women skilled in auspicious rites she places rice and durva on His head, blesses Him, circles Him
seven times with a lamp and, going into the house, looks back at the poet's Lord and cannot take even half a step. Raga not stated.
**Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^22-10]

নদীয়ার শশী বিলসয়ে চারু, ছোঁড়লাতে কিবা মধুর ছাঁদে ।
কনক নবনী জিনি তনু নব, ভঙ্গিমাতে কেবা ধৈরজ বাঁধে ॥

*nadīyāra śaśī bilasaye cāru, chom̐ṛalāte kibā madhura chām̐de |*
*kanaka nabanī jini tanu naba, bhaṅgimāte kebā dhairaja bām̐dhe ||*

*Word for word:* nadīyāra śaśī — the Moon of Nadia; bilasaye cāru — shines charmingly; chom̐ṛalāte — under the wedding canopy; kibā madhura chām̐de — in what sweet array; kanaka nabanī jini — surpassing gold and fresh butter; tanu naba — His youthful body; bhaṅgimāte — at His bearing; kebā dhairaja bām̐dhe — who keeps composure

**5.1.** The Moon of Nadia shines charmingly under the wedding canopy — how sweet His array!
His youthful body surpasses gold and fresh butter — seeing His bearing, who could keep composure?

বারে বারে বিষ্ণুপ্রিয়ার জননী, অনিমিখ আঁখে নিরখে ছলে ।
কত না আনন্দে উথলয়ে হিয়া, না পরশে পদ ধরণীতলে ॥

*bāre bāre biṣṇupriyāra jananī, animikha ām̐khe nirakhe chale |*
*kata nā ānande uthalaye hiyā, nā paraśe pada dharaṇītale ||*

*Word for word:* bāre bāre — again and again; biṣṇupriyāra jananī — Vishnupriya's mother; animikha ām̐khe — with unblinking eyes; nirakhe chale — gazes under pretexts; kata nā ānande — with what joy; uthalaye hiyā — the heart overflows; nā paraśe pada dharaṇī-tale — her feet do not touch the ground

**5.2.** Again and again Vishnupriya's mother, under various pretexts, gazes [at Him] with unblinking eyes;
with what joy her heart overflows — her feet do not touch the ground!

আইহ সুঁইহ সহ সুবেশে আইসে, মঙ্গল-বিধানে নিপুণা অতি ।
ধান্য দূর্ব্বাদল সুললিত মাথে, দেই আশীর্ব্বাদ অতুল রীতি ॥

*āiha sum̐iha saha subeśe āise, maṅgala-bidhāne nipuṇā ati |*
*dhānya dūrvvādala sulalita māthe, dei āśīrvvāda atula rīti ||*

*Word for word:* āiha suiha saha — with the married women; subeśe āise — finely dressed, she comes; maṅgala-bidhāne nipuṇā ati — very skilled in auspicious rites; dhānya dūrvvā-dala — rice and durva; sulalita māthe — on the lovely head; dei āśīrvvāda — gives blessings; atula rīti — in a matchless way

**5.3.** Finely dressed, she comes with the married women, very skilled in auspicious rites;
on His lovely head she places rice and durva and blesses Him in a matchless way.

হাতে দীপ সপ্ত প্রদক্ষিণ করে, বরে উরথিয়া যাইতে ঘরে ।
নরহরি-নাথে চাহে পালটি না চলে পদ আধ স্নেহের ভরে ॥

*hāte dīpa sapta pradakṣiṇa kare, bare urathiyā yāite ghare |*
*narahari-nāthe cāhe pālaṭi nā cale pada ādha snehera bhare ||*

*Word for word:* hāte dīpa — lamp in hand; sapta pradakṣiṇa kare — circles seven times; bare urathiyā — having performed the reception of the bridegroom; yāite ghare — going into the house; narahari-nāthe cāhe pālaṭi — looks back at the Lord of Narahari; nā cale pada ādha — cannot move even half a step; snehera bhare — under the weight of tenderness

**5.4.** Lamp in hand she circles [Him] seven times; having performed the reception of the bridegroom, she goes into the house,
but, looking back at the Lord of Narahari, under the weight of tenderness she cannot take even half a step.[^22-11]

[^22-10]: GPT1 — p. 102, no. 23 (scan, PDF p. 361); GPT2 — section 2.4, no. 23 (catalogue: NG-062). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 812; ed. 1960, vv. 1527–1530).
Variant: 5.4 GPT1 "cāhe pālaṭi nā cale pada ādha" ("looks back — cannot take even half a step"), BR "cāhe pālaṭiyā, cale pada ādha" ("looking back, takes half a
step") — following GPT1. The signature is garbled in the GPT1 OCR ("narahabi"), so the signature-checking script misses the pada (chapter 21). Not in PK,
KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B.
[^22-11]: The wedding canopy (chom̐ṛalā) is the place of the rites in the courtyard of the bride's house. The reception of the bridegroom (bare urathiyā)
is performed by the bride's mother and the married women: rice and durva on the head, a lamp, the sevenfold circling (in Lochana, vv.
149–152). The tenderness of the mother-in-law for the Lord is parental love, which He accepts from His associates.

## 6. Narahari — "sanātana miśrera gharaṇī…" (GPT1 pp. 102–103, no. 24; BR)
*The wedding: Sanatana's wife adorns her daughter; at Mishra's bidding Vishnupriya is brought out and seated on a throne under the canopy;
Vishnupriya first, offering a garland, gives herself to the Lord's feet; Gaura with a smile puts a garland round her neck; They shower each
other with flowers; Sanatana performs the kanya-dana, placing his daughter's hand in Vishvambhara's, and gives the dowry; at the end the
homa is performed. Raga not stated. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^22-12]

সনাতন মিশ্রের ঘরণী । করে লোকাচার যত কহিতে না জানি ॥

*sanātana miśrera gharaṇī | kare lokācāra yata kahite nā jāni ||*

*Word for word:* sanātana miśrera gharaṇī — the wife of Sanatana Mishra; kare lokācāra yata — performs so many customary rites; kahite nā jāni — I cannot tell them

**6.1.** The wife of Sanatana Mishra performs so many customary rites — I cannot even tell them.

সাঁতারয়ে সুখের পাথারে । কন্যায় ভূষিত করে নানা অলঙ্কারে ॥

*sām̐tāraye sukhera pāthāre | kanyāya bhūṣita kare nānā alaṅkāre ||*

*Word for word:* sām̐tāraye sukhera pāthāre — she swims in an ocean of happiness; kanyāya bhūṣita kare — adorns her daughter; nānā alaṅkāre — with many ornaments

**6.2.** She swims in an ocean of happiness, adorning her daughter with many ornaments.

দেখি বিষ্ণুপ্রিয়ার সুবেশ । বাঢ়য়ে সবার মনে উল্লাস অশেষ ॥

*dekhi biṣṇupriyāra subeśa | bāṛhaye sabāra mane ullāsa aśeṣa ||*

*Word for word:* dekhi biṣṇupriyāra subeśa — seeing Vishnupriya's beautiful attire; bāṛhaye sabāra mane — grows in everyone's heart; ullāsa aśeṣa — boundless joy

**6.3.** Seeing Vishnupriya's beautiful attire, joy grows boundlessly in everyone's heart.

মিশ্র মহাশয় শুভক্ষণে । কন্যায় আনিতে নিদেশিল প্রিয়গণে ॥

*miśra mahāśaya śubhakṣaṇe | kanyāya ānite nideśila priyagaṇe ||*

*Word for word:* miśra mahāśaya — the venerable Mishra; śubha-kṣaṇe — at the auspicious moment; kanyāya ānite — to bring his daughter; nideśila priya-gaṇe — told his dear ones

**6.4.** The venerable Mishra at the auspicious moment told his dear ones to bring his daughter.

মিশ্রের ভবন মনোহর । ঝলমল করয়ে অঙ্গন পরিসর ॥

*miśrera bhabana manohara | jhalamala karaye aṅgana parisara ||*

*Word for word:* miśrera bhabana manohara — Mishra's house is captivating; jhalamala karaye — glitters; aṅgana parisara — the spacious courtyard

**6.5.** Mishra's house is captivating; the spacious courtyard glitters.

ছোঁড়লা শোভয়ে সেইখানে । আনিলেন কন্যা বসাইয়া সিংহাসনে ॥

*chom̐ṛalā śobhaye seikhāne | ānilena kanyā basāiyā siṃhāsane ||*
