*Word for word:* chom̐ṛalā śobhaye seikhāne — there the wedding canopy is beautiful; ānilena kanyā — they brought the daughter; basāiyā siṃhāsane — and seated her on a throne

**6.6.** There the wedding canopy is beautiful; they brought the daughter and seated her on a throne.

যে কিছু আছয়ে লোকাচার । তাহাও করেন তাহে কৌতুক অপার ॥

*ye kichu āchaye lokācāra | tāhāo karena tāhe kautuka apāra ||*

*Word for word:* ye kichu āchaye lokācāra — whatever customary rites there are; tāhāo karena — these too are performed; tāhe kautuka apāra — and in this is boundless merriment

**6.7.** All the rites there are by custom are also performed — and in this is boundless merriment.

প্রথমেই দেবী বিষ্ণুপ্রিয়া । আত্মসমর্পিল প্রভু-পদে মালা দিয়া ॥

*prathamei debī biṣṇupriyā | ātmasamarpila prabhu-pade mālā diyā ||*

*Word for word:* prathamei debī biṣṇupriyā — first the goddess Vishnupriya; ātma-samarpila — gave herself; prabhu-pade — to the Lord's feet; mālā diyā — offering a garland

**6.8.** First the goddess Vishnupriya, offering a garland, gave herself to the Lord's feet.[^22-13]

ঈষৎ হাসিয়া গোরারায় । দিল পুষ্পমালা বিষ্ণুপ্রিয়ার গলায় ॥

*īṣat hāsiyā gorārāya | dila puṣpamālā biṣṇupriyāra galāya ||*

*Word for word:* īṣat hāsiyā gorārāya — smiling slightly, Gora Raya; dila puṣpa-mālā — put a garland of flowers; biṣṇupriyāra galāya — round Vishnupriya's neck

**6.9.** Smiling slightly, Gaura Raya put a garland of flowers round Vishnupriya's neck.

পুষ্প ফেলাফেলি দুইজনে । দোঁহার মনের কথা দোঁহে ভাল জানে ॥

*puṣpa phelāpheli duijane | dom̐hāra manera kathā dom̐he bhāla jāne ||*

*Word for word:* puṣpa phelāpheli duijane — the two shower each other with flowers; dom̐hāra manera kathā — what is in each one's heart; dom̐he bhāla jāne — both know well

**6.10.** The two shower each other with flowers; each knows well what is in the other's heart.

তিলে তিলে বাঢ়য়ে আনন্দ । বিষ্ণুপ্রিয়া-সহ বিলসয়ে গৌরচন্দ্র ॥

*tile tile bāṛhaye ānanda | biṣṇupriyā-saha bilasaye gauracandra ||*

*Word for word:* tile tile — moment by moment; bāṛhaye ānanda — joy grows; biṣṇupriyā-saha — together with Vishnupriya; bilasaye gauracandra — Gaurachandra rejoices

**6.11.** Moment by moment the joy grows: Gaurachandra rejoices together with Vishnupriya.

কি নব শোভার নাহি পার । চারিদিকে নারীগণ দেয় জয়কার ॥

*ki naba śobhāra nāhi pāra | cāridike nārīgaṇa deya jayakāra ||*

*Word for word:* ki naba śobhāra nāhi pāra — what new beauty without end; cāridike nārī-gaṇa — on all sides the women; deya jaya-kāra — raise cries of "jaya"

**6.12.** What new beauty without end! On all sides the women raise cries of "jaya".

করে কোলাহল সর্ব্বজন । বাজে নানা বাদ্য ধ্বনি ভেদয়ে গগন ॥

*kare kolāhala sarvvajana | bāje nānā bādya dhvani bhedaye gagana ||*

*Word for word:* kare kolāhala sarvvajana — everyone makes a clamour; bāje nānā bādya — various instruments sound; dhvani bhedaye gagana — the sound pierces the sky

**6.13.** Everyone makes a clamour; various instruments sound — the sound pierces the sky.

সনাতন মিশ্র ভাগ্যবান । বসিলেন উল্লাসে করিতে কন্যাদান ॥

*sanātana miśra bhāgyabāna | basilena ullāse karite kanyādāna ||*

*Word for word:* sanātana miśra bhāgyabān — the blessed Sanatana Mishra; basilena ullāse — joyfully sat down; karite kanyā-dāna — to perform the kanya-dana

**6.14.** The blessed Sanatana Mishra joyfully sat down to perform the kanya-dana.

বেদাদিবিহিত ক্রিয়া করি । সমর্পিল কন্যা বিশ্বম্ভর-করে ধরি ॥

*bedādibihita kriyā kari | samarpila kanyā biśvambhara-kare dhari ||*

*Word for word:* bedādi-bihita kriyā kari — having performed the rites enjoined by the Vedas and the rest; samarpila kanyā — he gave his daughter; biśvambhara-kare dhari — placing [her hand] in Vishvambhara's hand

**6.15.** Having performed the rites enjoined by the Vedas and the rest, he gave his daughter, placing her hand in Vishvambhara's.

দিলেন যৌতুক সুখে ভাসি । দিব্য ধেনু ধন ভূমি শয্যা দাস দাসী ॥

*dilena yautuka sukhe bhāsi | dibya dhenu dhana bhūmi śayyā dāsa dāsī ||*

*Word for word:* dilena yautuka — he gave the dowry; sukhe bhāsi — floating in happiness; dibya dhenu — splendid cows; dhana — wealth; bhūmi — land; śayyā — a bed; dāsa dāsī — menservants and maidservants

**6.16.** Floating in happiness, he gave the dowry: splendid cows, wealth, land, a bed, menservants and maidservants.

সর্ব্বশেষে হোমকর্ম্ম করে । বিশ্বম্ভর-বামে বসাইয়া দুহিতারে ॥

*sarvvaśeṣe homakarmma kare | biśvambhara-bāme basāiyā duhitāre ||*

*Word for word:* sarvva-śeṣe — at the very end; homa-karmma kare — the homa is performed; biśvambhara-bāme — at Vishvambhara's left; basāiyā duhitāre — seating the daughter

**6.17.** At the very end the homa is performed: the daughter is seated at Vishvambhara's left.

কি অদ্ভুত দোঁহার মাধুরী । কহিতে কি ? দোঁহার নিছনি নরহরি ॥

*ki adbhuta dom̐hāra mādhurī | kahite ki ? dom̐hāra nichani narahari ||*

*Word for word:* ki adbhuta dom̐hāra mādhurī — how wondrous the sweetness of the two; kahite ki — what is there to say; dom̐hāra nichani narahari — Narahari gives himself for the two of Them

**6.18.** How wondrous the sweetness of the two of Them! What can one say? Narahari gives himself for Them both.[^22-14]

[^22-12]: GPT1 — pp. 102–103, no. 24 (scan, PDF pp. 361–362); GPT2 — section 2.4, no. 24 (catalogue: NG-063). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, pp. 812–813; ed. 1960,
vv. 1531–1548). The variants are minor (6.10 GPT1 "kelākeli", BR "phelāpheli" — the same "shower each other"). Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya
or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. The wedding — CB Adi 15; in Lochana — vv. 155–160.
[^22-13]: Vishnupriya is the eternal energy of the Lord (note 2); offering the garland, she "gives herself" to the Lord (ātmasamarpaṇa) — not a worldly
bride but His shakti, eternally serving Him. The exchange of garlands and flowers is a wedding custom; "each knows what is in the other's
heart" — the inseparability of the Lord and His energy.
[^22-14]: Kanya-dana is the "gift of the daughter" by her father; the homa is the fire sacrifice; the bride is seated at the bridegroom's left.
The Lord accepts these rites following the lila (note 2). "Gives himself for Them" (nichani) is a formula of love and devotion (cf. note 7).

## 7. Narahari — "dekhi pahum̐ka bibāha mādhurī…" (GPT1 p. 103, no. 25; BR)
*The gods at the wedding: seeing the sweetness of the Lord's wedding, Shesha, Shiva, Brahma, Indra, Ganapati and others thrill; the
chariots of the gods block the path of the sky; invisible, telling one another of His deeds, the gods shower the wedding with flowers and
praise the good fortune of the brahmana Sanatana; the poet longs to be intoxicated with that joy. Raga not stated. **Attribution: probably
Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR; Vrajabuli.*[^22-15]

দেখি পহুঁক বিবাহ-মাধুরী কোই ধরই না থেহ ।
শেষ শিব বিহি ইন্দ্র গণপতি আদি পুলকিত দেহ ॥

*dekhi pahum̐ka bibāha-mādhurī koi dharai nā theha |*
*śeṣa śiba bihi indra gaṇapati ādi pulakita deha ||*

*Word for word:* dekhi — seeing; pahum̐ka bibāha-mādhurī — the sweetness of the Lord's wedding; koi dharai nā theha — no one keeps steady; śeṣa — Shesha; śiba — Shiva; bihi — Brahma; indra — Indra; gaṇapati ādi — Ganapati and others; pulakita deha — their bodies thrill

**7.1.** Seeing the sweetness of the Lord's wedding, no one can stay steady:
Shesha, Shiva, Brahma, Indra, Ganapati and the others — their whole bodies thrill.

ভীড় অতিশয় গগন-পথ বহু রোকি দেব-বিমান ।
হোত জয় জয় শবদ সুমধুর ভঙ্গী ভণই ন জান ॥

*bhīṛa atiśaya gagana-patha bahu roki deba-bimāna |*
*hota jaya jaya śabada sumadhura bhaṅgī bhaṇai na jāna ||*

*Word for word:* bhīṛa atiśaya — the crowd is immense; gagana-patha — the path of the sky; bahu roki deba-bimāna — many chariots of the gods have blocked; hota jaya jaya śabada sumadhura — sweet cries of "jaya, jaya" sound; bhaṅgī bhaṇai na jāna — the manner cannot be told

**7.2.** The crowd is immense: many chariots of the gods have blocked the path of the sky;
sweet cries of "jaya, jaya" sound — how it was cannot be told.

ভূরি কৌতুক পরস্পর বর সরস চরিত উচারি ।
করত কুসুম-সুবৃষ্টি অলখিত ললিত রঙ্গ বিথারি ॥

*bhūri kautuka paraspara bara sarasa carita ucāri |*
*karata kusuma-subṛṣṭi alakhita lalita raṅga bithāri ||*

*Word for word:* bhūri kautuka — in great delight; paraspara — to one another; bara sarasa carita ucāri — telling of the excellent deeds full of rasa; karata kusuma-subṛṣṭi — they pour a fine rain of flowers; alakhita — invisible; lalita raṅga bithāri — spreading lovely merriment

**7.3.** In great delight, telling one another of [the Lord's] wondrous deeds, full of rasa,
invisible, they pour down a rain of flowers, spreading lovely merriment.

দ্বিজ সনাতন ভাগভর পরশংসি পরম বিথোর ।
দাস নরহরি আশ ইহ সুখে মাতব কি মতি মোর ॥

*dvija sanātana bhāgabhara paraśaṃsi parama bithora |*
*dāsa narahari āśa iha sukhe mātaba ki mati mora ||*

*Word for word:* dvija sanātana — of the brahmana Sanatana; bhāga-bhara — the great good fortune; paraśaṃsi — praising; parama bithora — utterly enraptured; dāsa narahari āśa — the hope of the servant Narahari; iha sukhe mātaba ki mati mora — will my mind be intoxicated with this joy

**7.4.** Praising the great good fortune of the brahmana Sanatana, they are utterly enraptured;
the hope of the servant Narahari: will my mind become intoxicated with this joy?[^22-16]

[^22-15]: GPT1 — p. 103, no. 25 (scan, PDF p. 362); GPT2 — section 2.4, no. 25 (catalogue: NG-064). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 813; ed. 1960, vv. 1549–1552).
Variants: 7.3 BR "alakṣita" ("invisible") — the same; 7.4 GPT1 "bhāgabhara", BR "bhāga bhara" — the same. Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the
Gaura-charita-chintamani. B.
[^22-16]: The demigods are the Lord's servants: invisibly they come to behold His lila and to serve it (note 3). Sanatana Mishra's good fortune
is that the Lord Himself has accepted his daughter. Shesha is Ananta; Ganapati is Ganesha.

## 8. Narahari — "deba-ramaṇībṛnda biraci beśa…" (GPT1 p. 103, no. 26; BR)
*The celestial women at the wedding: adorned, with flashing bangles, their countless hosts roam the path of the sky and deem their eyes
rewarded at seeing Gaura's wedding; praising Mishra's house, they thrill; with full eyes they drink in the form of the Lord and His beloved
and give their lives for Them. Raga not stated. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR; Vrajabuli.*[^22-17]

দেব-রমণীবৃন্দ বিরচি বেশ বিবিধ ভাঁতি ।
বাজত থর মাহি অতুল ঝলকে কম্বুক কাঁতি ॥

*deba-ramaṇībṛnda biraci beśa bibidha bhām̐ti |*
*bājata thara māhi atula jhalake kambuka kām̐ti ||*

*Word for word:* deba-ramaṇī-bṛnda — the hosts of celestial women; biraci beśa bibidha bhām̐ti — adorned in various ways; bājata — [their ornaments] ring; thara māhi — (unclear: "in rows"?); atula jhalake — flashes matchlessly; kambuka kām̐ti — the lustre of conch-shell bangles

**8.1.** The hosts of celestial women have adorned themselves in various ways;
[their ornaments] ring, the lustre of their conch-shell bangles flashes matchlessly.

ভ্রমত গগন-পথ অগণিত যূথ হিয় উৎসাহ ।
মানত দিঠি সফল নিরখি গৌরবর-বিবাহ ॥

*bhramata gagana-patha agaṇita yūtha hiya utsāha |*
*mānata diṭhi saphala nirakhi gaurabara-bibāha ||*

*Word for word:* bhramata gagana-patha — they roam the path of the sky; agaṇita yūtha — countless hosts; hiya utsāha — with eagerness in their hearts; mānata diṭhi saphala — deem their eyes rewarded; nirakhi gaurabara-bibāha — seeing the wedding of the beautiful Gaura

**8.2.** Countless hosts roam the path of the sky, eagerness in their hearts;
they deem their eyes rewarded, seeing the wedding of the beautiful Gaura.

মিশ্র-ভবন রীত রুচির উচরি পুলক-গাত ।
নব নব অভিলাষ করহ ধৃতি ধরই ন জাত ॥

*miśra-bhabana rīta rucira ucari pulaka-gāta |*
*naba naba abhilāṣa karaha dhṛti dharai na jāta ||*

*Word for word:* miśra-bhabana rīta rucira — the lovely custom of Mishra's house; ucari — praising; pulaka-gāta — thrilling all over; naba naba abhilāṣa karaha — they form ever new desires; dhṛti dharai na jāta — composure cannot be kept

**8.3.** Praising the lovely custom of Mishra's house, they thrill all over;
new and ever new desires arise in them — composure cannot be kept.

নিরুপম পহুঁ প্রেয়সী-ছবি লোচন ভরি নেত ।
নরহরি কত ভাখব সভে প্রাণ নিছনি দেত ॥

*nirupama pahum̐ preyasī-chabi locana bhari neta |*
*narahari kata bhākhaba sabhe prāṇa nichani deta ||*

*Word for word:* nirupama pahum̐ — of the incomparable Lord; preyasī-chabi — and the form of His beloved; locana bhari neta — they take in with full eyes; narahari kata bhākhaba — how much can Narahari say; sabhe prāṇa nichani deta — all give their lives for Them

**8.4.** With full eyes they drink in the form of the incomparable Lord and His beloved;
how much can Narahari say? — all give their lives for Them.[^22-18]

[^22-17]: GPT1 — p. 103, no. 26 (scan, PDF p. 362); GPT2 — section 2.4, no. 26 (catalogue: NG-065). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, pp. 813–814; ed. 1960, vv. 1553–1556).
Variants: 8.2 GPT1 "mānata diṭhi sakala nirakhi gaurabara nibāha", BR "saphala", "bibāha" — following the BR; 8.1 "bājata thara māhi" (BR 1912 "bājata thara, nāhi atula") — the
sense is unclear, the translation conjectural. Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B.
[^22-18]: The celestial women, like the demigods, come to behold the Lord's lila and to serve Him (cf. no. 21 of chapter 21: "we shall make merry
at the wedding together with the wives of Nadia"). "His beloved" (preyasī) is Vishnupriya, the eternal energy of the Lord (note 2). "They give
their lives" (prāṇa nichani deta) is a formula of love and devotion (note 7).

## 9. Narahari — "āhā mari mari suranārīgaṇa…" (GPT1 p. 103, no. 27; BR)
*The celestial women, watching the wedding of the Moon of Nadia, talk among themselves: Sanatana Mishra is beside himself with joy at
having given his daughter to Krishna; seating his daughter at his son-in-law's left he performs the homa but cannot take his eyes from His
face; Mishra's wife is as if maddened in the wedding bustle and, gazing at the poet's Lord, does not feel the ground under her feet. Raga
not stated. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^22-19]

আহা মরি মরি সুরনারীগণ, নদীয়া-চাঁদের বিবাহ দেখি ।
সে শোভা-সায়রে সাঁতারিয়া সভে, তিরপিত করে তৃষিত আঁখি ॥

*āhā mari mari suranārīgaṇa, nadīyā-cām̐dera bibāha dekhi |*
*se śobhā-sāyare sām̐tāriyā sabhe, tirapita kare tṛṣita ām̐khi ||*

*Word for word:* āhā mari mari — ah, I die; sura-nārī-gaṇa — the celestial women; nadīyā-cām̐dera bibāha dekhi — seeing the wedding of the Moon of Nadia; se śobhā-sāyare sām̐tāriyā sabhe — all swimming in that ocean of beauty; tirapita kare tṛṣita ām̐khi — sate their thirsting eyes

**9.1.** Ah, I die! The celestial women, seeing the wedding of the Moon of Nadia,
all swim in that ocean of beauty and sate their thirsting eyes.

কেহ কারু প্রতি কহে দেখ মিশ্র-সনাতন সুখে না ধরে হিয়া ।
কৃষ্ণে কন্যাদান করি কত সাধে কহে কত নানা যৌতুক দিয়া ॥

*keha kāru prati kahe dekha miśra-sanātana sukhe nā dhare hiyā |*
*kṛṣṇe kanyādāna kari kata sādhe kahe kata nānā yautuka diyā ||*

*Word for word:* keha kāru prati kahe — one says to another; dekha — look; miśra-sanātana sukhe nā dhare hiyā — Mishra Sanatana's heart cannot contain the joy; kṛṣṇe kanyā-dāna kari — having given his daughter to Krishna; kata sādhe — with what longing; kahe kata — how much he says; nānā yautuka diyā — giving gifts of every kind

**9.2.** One says to another: "Look — Mishra Sanatana's heart cannot contain his joy!
With what longing he has given his daughter to Krishna — how much he says, how many gifts of every kind he gives!"[^22-20]

কেহ কহে জামাতার বামে কন্যা, বসাইয়া ধন্য আপনা মানে ।
করে হোমক্রিয়া তাহে নাহি মন চাহি রহে চাঁদমুখের পানে ॥

*keha kahe jāmātāra bāme kanyā, basāiyā dhanya āpanā māne |*
*kare homakriyā tāhe nāhi mana cāhi rahe cām̐damukhera pāne ||*

*Word for word:* keha kahe — another says; jāmātāra bāme kanyā basāiyā — seating his daughter at his son-in-law's left; dhanya āpanā māne — he deems himself blessed; kare homa-kriyā — he performs the homa; tāhe nāhi mana — his mind is not on it; cāhi rahe cām̐da-mukhera pāne — he keeps gazing at the moon-face

**9.3.** Another says: "Seating his daughter at his son-in-law's left, he deems himself blessed;
he performs the homa, but his mind is not on it — he keeps gazing at the moon-face".

কেহ কহে দেখ মিশ্রের ঘরণী উনমত পারা বিবাহ-ধূমে ।
নরহরি-নাথে দেখে কত ছলে, উলসিত পদ না পড়ে ভূমে ॥

*keha kahe dekha miśrera gharaṇī unamata pārā bibāha-dhūme |*
*narahari-nāthe dekhe kata chale, ulasita pada nā paṛe bhūme ||*

*Word for word:* keha kahe dekha — yet another says: look; miśrera gharaṇī — Mishra's wife; unamata pārā — as if maddened; bibāha-dhūme — in the wedding bustle; narahari-nāthe dekhe kata chale — gazes at the Lord of Narahari under many pretexts; ulasita — delighted; pada nā paṛe bhūme — her feet do not touch the ground

**9.4.** Yet another says: "Look — Mishra's wife is as if maddened in the wedding bustle;
under various pretexts she gazes at the Lord of Narahari, and in her delight her feet do not touch the ground".

[^22-19]: GPT1 — p. 103, no. 27 (scan, PDF p. 362); GPT2 — section 2.4, no. 27. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-287). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912,
p. 814; ed. 1960, vv. 1557–1560). The variants are minor (9.2 BR 1960 "kaṣe" — an OCR distortion of "kṛṣṇe"). Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya
or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B.
[^22-20]: "Has given his daughter to Krishna" — the celestial women call Gaura Krishna outright: He is Krishna Himself, and Vishnupriya is His
eternal energy (note 2).

## 10. Narahari — "deba debaramaṇī ullāse…" (GPT1 p. 104, no. 28; BR)
*Gods and celestial women talk softly of the wedding: fortunate are the people of Nadia; the brahmanas who have beautiful daughters
lament that they could not give a daughter to such a bridegroom; all praise Sanatana Mishra; he completes the homa; the women raise their
cries; Vishnupriya and Gorachand are led to the bridal chamber. Raga not stated. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in
the BR.*[^22-21]

দেব দেবরমণী উল্লাসে । বিবাহ-প্রসঙ্গ সবে কহে মৃদুভাষে ॥

*deba debaramaṇī ullāse | bibāha-prasaṅga sabe kahe mṛdubhāṣe ||*

*Word for word:* deba — the gods; deba-ramaṇī — the celestial women; ullāse — rejoicing; bibāha-prasaṅga — talk of the wedding; sabe kahe mṛdu-bhāṣe — all speak in soft voices

**10.1.** The gods and the celestial women, rejoicing, all talk of the wedding in soft voices:

ভাগ্যবন্ত লোক নদীয়ার । হইল বিবাহ দেখি উল্লাস সভার ॥

*bhāgyabanta loka nadīyāra | haila bibāha dekhi ullāsa sabhāra ||*

*Word for word:* bhāgyabanta loka nadīyāra — fortunate are the people of Nadia; haila bibāha — the wedding has taken place; dekhi ullāsa sabhāra — seeing it, all rejoice

**10.2.** "Fortunate are the people of Nadia! The wedding has taken place — seeing it, all rejoice".

রূপবতী কন্যা যার ঘরে । সে সকল বিপ্র মনে মহাখেদ করে ॥

*rūpabatī kanyā yāra ghare | se sakala bipra mane mahākheda kare ||*

*Word for word:* rūpabatī kanyā yāra ghare — who have a beautiful daughter at home; se sakala bipra — all those brahmanas; mane mahākheda kare — grieve bitterly at heart

**10.3.** All the brahmanas who have a beautiful daughter at home grieve bitterly at heart:

এহেন বরেরে কন্যা দিতে । না পারিলুঁ হেন সুখ নাহিক ভাগ্যেতে ॥

*ehena barere kanyā dite | nā pārilum̐ hena sukha nāhika bhāgyete ||*

*Word for word:* ehena barere — to such a bridegroom; kanyā dite nā pārilum̐ — we could not give a daughter; hena sukha nāhika bhāgyete — such happiness is not in our fate

**10.4.** "We could not give a daughter to such a bridegroom — such happiness is not in our fate!"

এইমত কেহ কত কয় । সকলেই সনাতন মিশ্রে প্রশংসয় ॥

*eimata keha kata kaya | sakalei sanātana miśre praśaṃsaya ||*

*Word for word:* ei-mata keha kata kaya — thus they say this and that; sakalei sanātana miśre praśaṃsaya — all praise Sanatana Mishra

**10.5.** So one says one thing, another another; all praise Sanatana Mishra.

সনাতন মিশ্র ভাগ্যবান । হোমকর্ম্ম আদি সব কৈল সমাধান ॥

*sanātana miśra bhāgyabāna | homakarmma ādi saba kaila samādhāna ||*

*Word for word:* sanātana miśra bhāgyabān — the blessed Sanatana Mishra; homa-karmma ādi saba — the homa and all the rest; kaila samādhāna — completed

**10.6.** The blessed Sanatana Mishra completed the homa and all the rest.

কন্যা-জামাতায় নিরখিয়া । তিলে তিলে বাঢ়ে সুখ উথলয়ে হিয়া ॥

*kanyā-jāmātāya nirakhiyā | tile tile bāṛhe sukha uthalaye hiyā ||*

*Word for word:* kanyā-jāmātāya nirakhiyā — gazing at his daughter and son-in-law; tile tile bāṛhe sukha — moment by moment happiness grows; uthalaye hiyā — the heart overflows

**10.7.** Gazing at his daughter and son-in-law, he feels his happiness grow moment by moment and his heart overflow.

কহিতে কে জানে লোকাচার । ঘন ঘন নারীগণ দেই জয়কার ॥

*kahite ke jāne lokācāra | ghana ghana nārīgaṇa dei jayakāra ||*

*Word for word:* kahite ke jāne lokācāra — who knows how to tell of the customs; ghana ghana — again and again; nārī-gaṇa dei jaya-kāra — the women raise cries of "jaya"

**10.8.** Who could tell of the wedding customs? Again and again the women raise cries of "jaya".

বিষ্ণুপ্রিয়া দেবী গোরাচাঁদে । লইতে বাসর-ঘরে কেবা থির বাঁধে ॥

*biṣṇupriyā debī gorācām̐de | laite bāsara-ghare kebā thira bām̐dhe ||*

*Word for word:* biṣṇupriyā debī gorācām̐de — the goddess Vishnupriya and Gorachand; laite bāsara-ghare — leading to the bridal chamber; kebā thira bām̐dhe — who stays calm

**10.9.** Who can stay calm as the goddess Vishnupriya and Gorachand are led to the bridal chamber?

নরহরি-পহুঁ গোরারায় । চলে বাসর-ঘরে কত কৌতুক হিয়ায় ॥

*narahari-pahum̐ gorārāya | cale bāsara-ghare kata kautuka hiyāya ||*

*Word for word:* narahari-pahum̐ — the Lord of Narahari; gorārāya — Gora Raya; cale bāsara-ghare — goes to the bridal chamber; kata kautuka hiyāya — with such delight in His heart

**10.10.** The Lord of Narahari, Gaura Raya, goes to the bridal chamber with such delight in His heart![^22-22]

[^22-21]: GPT1 — p. 104, no. 28 (scan, PDF p. 363); GPT2 — section 2.4, no. 28 (catalogue: NG-066; GPT2 has "dekha deba ramaṇī" — "look: the celestial women…").
BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, pp. 814–815; ed. 1960, vv. 1561–1570). Variants: 10.4 GPT1 "nā pārāli", BR "nā pārilum̐" — following the BR. Not in PK, KGC, PS,
the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B.
[^22-22]: The bridal chamber (bāsara-ghara) is the room where the newly-weds spend the first night; by custom the women of the house gather there,
sing and joke with the bridegroom (nos. 11–12). The brahmanas' lament is praise of the bridegroom: such a son-in-law is not to be found again.

## 11. Narahari — "nadīyā-binoda gorā…" (GPT1 p. 104, no. 29; BR)
*The bridal chamber: Gora, the delight of Nadia, enters the bridal chamber; the wives of noble families seat Vishvambhara with Vishnupriya
and gaze unblinkingly at His face; one, wishing to touch Him, anoints Him with sandal, another sets a casket of betel before Him, a third
leans towards Him in jest, yet another offers Him a handful of flowers. Raga not stated. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada
is in the BR.*[^22-23]

নদীয়া-বিনোদ গোরা ।
প্রবেশে বাসর-ঘরে নব নব তরুণীগণের পরাণ-চোরা ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*nadīyā-binoda gorā |*
*prabeśe bāsara-ghare naba naba taruṇīgaṇera parāṇa-corā || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* nadīyā-binoda gorā — Gora, the delight of Nadia; prabeśe bāsara-ghare — enters the bridal chamber; naba naba taruṇī-gaṇera — of ever new young women; parāṇa-corā — stealer of the life

**11.1.** Gora, the delight of Nadia, stealer of the lives of ever new young women, enters the bridal chamber.

কুলবধূগণ মনের উল্লাসে বিশ্বম্ভর বিষ্ণুপ্রিয়ায় লৈয়া ।
সুমধুর ছাঁদে বসায় বাসরে অনিমিখ আঁখে ও মুখ চাঞা ॥

*kulabadhūgaṇa manera ullāse biśvambhara biṣṇupriyāya laiyā |*
*sumadhura chām̐de basāya bāsare animikha ām̐khe o mukha cāñā ||*

*Word for word:* kulabadhū-gaṇa — the wives of noble families; manera ullāse — with joy at heart; biśvambhara biṣṇupriyāya laiyā — taking Vishvambhara and Vishnupriya; sumadhura chām̐de — sweetly, in due manner; basāya bāsare — seat [Them] in the bridal chamber; animikha ām̐khe — with unblinking eyes; o mukha cāñā — gazing at that face

**11.2.** The wives of noble families, joy in their hearts, taking Vishvambhara and Vishnupriya,
sweetly, by custom, seat [Them] in the bridal chamber and gaze with unblinking eyes at that face.

কেহ পরশের সাধে হাসি হাসি সুগন্ধি চন্দন মাখায় অঙ্গে ।
কেহ সাজাইয়া তাম্বূল-বীটিকা সম্পুট সম্মুখে রাখয়ে রঙ্গে ॥

*keha paraśera sādhe hāsi hāsi sugandhi candana mākhāya aṅge |*
*keha sājāiyā tāmbūla-bīṭikā sampuṭa sammukhe rākhaye raṅge ||*

*Word for word:* keha paraśera sādhe — one, wishing to touch; hāsi hāsi — smiling; sugandhi candana mākhāya aṅge — anoints His body with fragrant sandal; keha sājāiyā tāmbūla-bīṭikā — another, having prepared rolls of betel; sampuṭa sammukhe rākhaye raṅge — merrily sets the casket before [Him]

**11.3.** One, wishing to touch [Him], smilingly anoints His body with fragrant sandal;
another, having prepared rolls of betel, merrily sets the casket before Him.

কেহ করে কত কৌতুক-ছলেতে ঢলি পড়ি গায় পুলক হিয়া ।
নরহরি-নাথ আগে রহে কেহ ভঙ্গীতে কুসুম-অঞ্জলি দিয়া ॥

*keha kare kata kautuka-chalete ḍhali paṛi gāya pulaka hiyā |*
*narahari-nātha āge rahe keha bhaṅgīte kusuma-añjali diyā ||*

*Word for word:* keha — yet another; kautuka-chalete — on the pretext of a jest; ḍhali paṛi gāya — leans towards [His] body; pulaka hiyā — her heart thrilling; narahari-nātha āge rahe keha — another stands before the Lord of Narahari; bhaṅgīte — gracefully; kusuma-añjali diyā — offering a handful of flowers

**11.4.** Yet another, on the pretext of a jest, leans towards Him, her heart thrilling;
and another stands before the Lord of Narahari and gracefully offers a handful of flowers.[^22-24]

[^22-23]: GPT1 — p. 104, no. 29 (scan, PDF p. 363); GPT2 — section 2.4, no. 29. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-288). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912,
p. 815; ed. 1960, vv. 1571–1574). The variants are minor (11.2 BR "chande" for "chām̐de"; 11.4 BR "ḍhali’ paṛe gāya"). Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya
or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. Line 11.1 is the refrain.
[^22-24]: In the bridal chamber, by custom, the married women of the house joke merrily with the bridegroom, treat Him to betel and anoint Him
with sandal; the poet describes these wedding jests — this is not nagari-bhava, though the words ("stealer of the lives of young women",
"wishing to touch") are close to its language. We translate faithfully to the author; for the position of the tradition see note 5. The
Lord's attractiveness is the quality of Bhagavan, who attracts all; and what the women do here is service to Him: sandal, betel, flowers.

## 12. Narahari — "bāsara gharete gorārāya. rūpe koṭi madana mātāya…" (GPT1 p. 104, no. 30; BR)
*In the bridal chamber: by His beauty Gaura Raya intoxicates millions of Kamadevas; the wives of noble families cannot take their eyes
from His moon-face and whisper with their veils drawn together; one covers the thrill of her body with her cloth, another trembles in the
rapture of rasa, yet another, unable to master her heart, offers her life at His reddish feet; the poet longs to see these pastimes. Raga
not stated. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^22-25]

বাসর-ঘরেতে গোরারায় । রূপে কোটি মদন মাতায় ॥

*bāsara-gharete gorārāya | rūpe koṭi madana mātāya ||*

*Word for word:* bāsara-gharete gorārāya — in the bridal chamber Gora Raya; rūpe — by His beauty; koṭi madana mātāya — intoxicates millions of Madanas

**12.1.** In the bridal chamber Gaura Raya by His beauty intoxicates millions of Madanas.

কুলবধূগণ মনোসুখে । সোঁপয়ে নয়ন চাঁদমুখে ॥

*kulabadhūgaṇa manosukhe | som̐paye nayana cām̐damukhe ||*

*Word for word:* kulabadhū-gaṇa — the wives of noble families; manosukhe — with joy at heart; som̐paye nayana — give their eyes; cām̐da-mukhe — to the moon-face

**12.2.** The wives of noble families, joy in their hearts, give their eyes to His moon-face.

ঘুঙটে ঘুঙট কেহ দিয়া । কহে কিবা ঈষৎ হাসিয়া ॥

*ghuṅaṭe ghuṅaṭa keha diyā | kahe kibā īṣat hāsiyā ||*

*Word for word:* ghuṅaṭe ghuṅaṭa keha diyā — one, putting her veil to another's veil; kahe kibā — says something; īṣat hāsiyā — smiling slightly

**12.3.** One, drawing her veil close to another's, says something, smiling slightly.

পুলকে ভরয় সব গা । ঝাঁপয়ে বসন দিয়া তা ॥

*pulake bharaya saba gā | jhām̐paye basana diyā tā ||*

*Word for word:* pulake bharaya saba gā — all their bodies are full of thrill; jhām̐paye basana diyā tā — they cover it with their cloth

**12.4.** All their bodies are full of thrill — they cover it with their cloth.

কেউ দাঁড়াইয়া কারু পাশে । কাঁপে সে না রসের আবেশে ॥

*keu dām̐ṛāiyā kāru pāśe | kām̐pe se nā rasera ābeśe ||*

*Word for word:* keu dām̐ṛāiyā kāru pāśe — one, standing beside another; kām̐pe — trembles; se nā rasera ābeśe — in that rapture of rasa

**12.5.** One, standing beside another, trembles in the rapture of rasa.

কেহ অতি অথির হিয়ায় । নিছয়ে জীবন রাঙ্গা পায় ॥

*keha ati athira hiyāya | nichaye jībana rāṅgā pāya ||*

*Word for word:* keha ati athira hiyāya — another, her heart very restless; nichaye jībana — offers her life; rāṅgā pāya — at the reddish feet

**12.6.** Another, her heart without rest, offers her life at His reddish feet.[^22-26]

বাসর-ঘরেতে রঙ্গ যত । তাহা কেবা কহিবেক কত ॥

*bāsara-gharete raṅga yata | tāhā kebā kahibeka kata ||*

*Word for word:* bāsara-gharete raṅga yata — all the merriment in the bridal chamber; tāhā kebā kahibeka kata — who could tell so much of it

**12.7.** How much merriment in the bridal chamber — who could tell so much?

নরহরি-মনে বড় আশ । দেখিব কি এ সব বিলাস ॥

*narahari-mane baṛa āśa | dekhiba ki e saba bilāsa ||*

*Word for word:* narahari-mane baṛa āśa — a great hope in Narahari's heart; dekhiba ki e saba bilāsa — shall I see all these pastimes

**12.8.** A great hope is in Narahari's heart: shall I see all these pastimes?

[^22-25]: GPT1 — p. 104, no. 30 (scan, PDF p. 363); GPT2 — section 2.4, no. 30. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-289; the row NG-067 with the
same first line "bāsara gharete gorārāya" is no. 31, no. 13 here). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, pp. 815–816; ed. 1960, vv. 1575–1582). Variants: 12.6 "rāṅgā pāya"
in GPT1 and BR 1912 (the BR 1960 OCR has "rādhā pāya", a distortion); 12.8 GPT1 "narahari mane baṛa āśa", BR "narahari-mane ei āśa". Not in PK, KGC, PS, the
Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B.
[^22-26]: "Offers her life at His feet" (nichaye jībana rāṅgā pāya) is an image of devotion to the Lord. The thrill and the "rapture of rasa" of the women
in the bridal chamber are delight in the Lord's all-attractive beauty; we translate faithfully to the author, for the position of the
tradition see note 5.

## 13. Narahari — "bāsara gharete gorārāya. biṣṇupriyā saha…" (GPT1 p. 105, no. 31; BR)
*The morning after the wedding: Gaura Raya spends the night with Vishnupriya in the bridal chamber; Sanatana and his kin are enraptured;
at dawn the Lord performs the kushandika and asks Sanatana to let Him go home; Sanatana, restraining himself, places his daughter's hand in
Vishvambhara's; the Lord bows to the venerable people, and they bless Him with rice and durva; Mishra's wife cannot master herself; amid
Vedic chanting, the women's cries and music all perform the auspicious rites for the journey. Raga not stated. **Attribution: probably
Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^22-27]

বাসর-ঘরেতে গোরারায় । বিষ্ণুপ্রিয়া-সহ সুখে রজনী গোঙায় ॥

*bāsara-gharete gorārāya | biṣṇupriyā-saha sukhe rajanī goṅāya ||*

*Word for word:* bāsara-gharete gorārāya — in the bridal chamber Gora Raya; biṣṇupriyā-saha — with Vishnupriya; sukhe rajanī goṅāya — happily spends the night

**13.1.** In the bridal chamber Gaura Raya happily spends the night with Vishnupriya.

কহিতে কৌতুক নাহি ওর । গোষ্ঠী-সহ সনাতন আনন্দে বিভোর ॥

*kahite kautuka nāhi ora | goṣṭhī-saha sanātana ānande bibhora ||*

*Word for word:* kahite kautuka nāhi ora — the merriment has no end in the telling; goṣṭhī-saha sanātana — Sanatana with his kin; ānande bibhora — enraptured with joy

**13.2.** The merriment is endless — it cannot be told; Sanatana with his kin is enraptured with joy.

রজনী-প্রভাতে গৌরহরি । হৈলা হর্ষ কুশণ্ডিকা আদি কর্ম্ম করি ॥

*rajanī-prabhāte gaurahari | hailā harṣa kuśaṇḍikā ādi karmma kari ||*

*Word for word:* rajanī-prabhāte — at the dawn of the night; gaurahari — Gaurahari; hailā harṣa — was filled with joy; kuśaṇḍikā ādi karmma kari — having performed the kushandika and other rites

**13.3.** At dawn Gaurahari, having performed the kushandika and the other rites, was filled with joy.[^22-28]

গমন করিব নিজালয়ে । সনাতন মিশ্র মহাশয়ে নিবেদয়ে ॥

*gamana kariba nijālaye | sanātana miśra mahāśaye nibedaye ||*

*Word for word:* gamana kariba nijālaye — "I shall go to My home"; sanātana miśra mahāśaye — to the venerable Sanatana Mishra; nibedaye — He says

**13.4.** "I shall go to My home," He says to the venerable Sanatana Mishra.

সনাতন জামাতা-রতনে । করিতে বিদায় ধৈর্য্য ধরয়ে যতনে ॥

*sanātana jāmātā-ratane | karite bidāya dhairyya dharaye yatane ||*

*Word for word:* sanātana — Sanatana; jāmātā-ratane karite bidāya — sending off his jewel of a son-in-law; dhairyya dharaye yatane — keeps his composure with effort

**13.5.** Sanatana, sending off his jewel of a son-in-law, keeps his composure with difficulty.

কন্যায় কত না প্রবোধিয়া । দিল বিশ্বম্ভর-কর ধরি সমর্পিয়া ॥

*kanyāya kata nā prabodhiyā | dila biśvambhara-kara dhari samarpiyā ||*

*Word for word:* kanyāya kata nā prabodhiyā — how much he consoled his daughter; dila — he gave [her]; biśvambhara-kara dhari samarpiyā — placing [her hand] in Vishvambhara's hand

**13.6.** How much he consoled his daughter — and gave her, placing her hand in Vishvambhara's.

গৌরহরি গমন-সময়ে । মান্যগণে পরম উল্লাসে প্রণময়ে ॥

*gaurahari gamana-samaye | mānyagaṇe parama ullāse praṇamaye ||*

*Word for word:* gaurahari gamana-samaye — Gaurahari, at the time of setting out; mānya-gaṇe — to the venerable people; parama ullāse praṇamaye — bows in great joy

**13.7.** Gaurahari, setting out, bows in great joy to the venerable people.

কহিতে কি সে সভার সাধ । ধান্য দূর্ব্বা দিয়া শিরে করে আশীর্ব্বাদ ॥

*kahite ki se sabhāra sādha | dhānya dūrvvā diyā śire kare āśīrvvāda ||*

*Word for word:* kahite ki se sabhāra sādha — what can be said of the longing of all; dhānya dūrvvā diyā śire — placing rice and durva on His head; kare āśīrvvāda — they bless

**13.8.** What can be said of the longing of them all? With rice and durva on His head they bless [Him].

মিশ্র-প্রিয়া কন্যা-জামাতারে । বিদায় করিতে ধৈর্য্য ধরিতে না পারে ॥

*miśra-priyā kanyā-jāmātāre | bidāya karite dhairyya dharite nā pāre ||*

*Word for word:* miśra-priyā — Mishra's wife; kanyā-jāmātāre bidāya karite — sending off her daughter and son-in-law; dhairyya dharite nā pāre — cannot keep her composure

**13.9.** Mishra's wife, sending off her daughter and son-in-law, cannot keep her composure.

গোরা গৃহে গমন করিতে । বিপ্রগণ বেদধ্বনি করে চারিভিতে ॥

*gorā gṛhe gamana karite | bipragaṇa bedadhvani kare cāribhite ||*

*Word for word:* gorā gṛhe gamana karite — as Gora sets out for home; bipra-gaṇa — the brahmanas; beda-dhvani kare cāri-bhite — chant the Vedas on all sides

**13.10.** As Gora sets out for home, the brahmanas chant the Vedas on all sides.

নারীগণ দেয় জয়কার । নানা বাদ্য বাজে ভাটে পড়ে কায়বার ॥

*nārīgaṇa deya jayakāra | nānā bādya bāje bhāṭe paṛe kāyabāra ||*

*Word for word:* nārī-gaṇa deya jaya-kāra — the women raise cries of "jaya"; nānā bādya bāje — various instruments sound; bhāṭe paṛe kāyabāra — the bhatas recite praises

**13.11.** The women raise cries of "jaya"; various instruments sound, the bhatas recite praises.

নরহরি-নাথে নিরখিয়া । গমন-উচিত সভে করে শুভক্রিয়া ॥

*narahari-nāthe nirakhiyā | gamana-ucita sabhe kare śubhakriyā ||*

*Word for word:* narahari-nāthe nirakhiyā — gazing at the Lord of Narahari; gamana-ucita — proper for a departure; sabhe kare śubha-kriyā — all perform auspicious rites

**13.12.** Gazing at the Lord of Narahari, all perform the auspicious rites proper for a departure.

[^22-27]: GPT1 — p. 105, no. 31 (scan, PDF p. 364); GPT2 — section 2.4, no. 31 (catalogue: NG-067). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 816; ed. 1960, vv. 1583–1594).
Variants: 13.8 GPT1 "karite ki se bhāra sādha", BR "kahite ki se sabhāra sādha" — following the BR; 13.11 GPT1 "kāyabāra", BR "rāyabāra" (the same — a song of
praise). Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. The morning after the wedding and the departure — CB Adi 15; in
Lochana — vv. 166–174.
[^22-28]: The kushandika is the rite at the sacred fire on the day after the wedding, which completes it. The Lord, the Goal of all rites,
performs them following the lila (note 2), and bows to His elders, setting an example of respect.

## 14. Narahari — "baraja-bhūṣaṇa gaura-bidhubara…" (GPT1 p. 105, no. 32; BR)
*The return home: Gaura, the ornament of Vraja, after the wedding rides home in the palanquin with His beloved; countless men and women
watch and say to one another: "This is Lakshmi and the Lord of Lakshmi!"; the praises of the bhatas, Vedic chanting, music, dancing,
singing such that the does come out of the forest; at the hour of cow-dust, having paused on the bank of the Suradhuni, He comes home. Raga
not stated. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR; ornate Vrajabuli.*[^22-29]

বরজ-ভূষণ গৌর-বিধুবর, করি বিবাহ বিনোদ-গতিপর, প্রেয়সী সহ চলই নিজ ঘর, পরম অদ্ভুত শোহয়ে ।
চঢ়ল চৌদোল মাহি ঝলকত, রূপ-অমিয়-প্রবাহ উছলত, বলিত নয়ন শিঙ্গার অনুপম, নিখিল জনমন মোহয়ে ॥

*baraja-bhūṣaṇa gaura-bidhubara, kari bibāha binoda-gatipara, preyasī saha calai nija ghara, parama adbhuta śohaye |*
*caṛhala caudola māhi jhalakata, rūpa-amiya-prabāha uchalata, balita nayana śiṅgāra anupama, nikhila janamana mohaye ||*

*Word for word:* baraja-bhūṣaṇa — the ornament of Vraja; gaura-bidhubara — the beautiful moon Gaura; kari bibāha — having celebrated the wedding; binoda-gatipara — with playful gait; preyasī saha — with His beloved; calai nija ghara — goes to His home; parama adbhuta śohaye — shines most wondrously; caṛhala caudola māhi — mounted on the palanquin; jhalakata — flashes; rūpa-amiya-prabāha uchalata — the stream of the nectar of beauty overflows; balita nayana — eyes adorned; śiṅgāra anupama — incomparable array; nikhila janamana mohaye — enchants the minds of all people

**14.1.** The ornament of Vraja, the beautiful moon — Gaura, having celebrated the wedding, with playful gait
goes with His beloved to His home — His splendour is wondrous beyond words;
mounted on the palanquin He flashes; the stream of the nectar of His beauty overflows;
His eyes adorned, His array incomparable — He enchants the minds of all people.

হোত জয় জয় শব্দ অবিরত, নারী পুরুখ অসংখ্য নিরখত, পরস্পর ভণ লখিমী লখিমীক-নাথ দুহুঁ বিলসত জনু ।
বন্দীগণ মন মোদ অতিশয়, উচরিত নব নব চরিত মধুময়, ভূরি ভূসুর করত ঘন ঘন বেদধ্বনি পুলকিত তনু ॥

*hota jaya jaya śabda abirata, nārī purukha asaṃkhya nirakhata, paraspara bhaṇa lakhimī lakhimīka-nātha duhum̐ bilasata janu |*
*bandīgaṇa mana moda atiśaya, ucarita naba naba carita madhumaya, bhūri bhūsura karata ghana ghana bedadhvani pulakita tanu ||*

*Word for word:* hota jaya jaya śabda abirata — cries of "jaya, jaya" sound without pause; nārī purukha asaṃkhya nirakhata — countless men and women watch; paraspara bhaṇa — say to one another; lakhimī lakhimīka-nātha — Lakshmi and the Lord of Lakshmi; duhum̐ bilasata janu — as if the two shine; bandīgaṇa mana moda atiśaya — the singers of praises in great joy; ucarita naba naba carita madhumaya — proclaim ever new sweet deeds; bhūri bhūsura — many brahmanas; karata ghana ghana beda-dhvani — chant the Vedas again and again; pulakita tanu — their bodies thrill

**14.2.** Cries of "jaya, jaya" sound without pause; countless men and women watch
and say to one another: "It is as if Lakshmi and the Lord of Lakshmi — the two of Them — were shining!";[^22-30]
the singers of praises in great joy proclaim ever new sweet deeds;
many brahmanas chant the Vedas again and again — and their bodies thrill.

বাদ্য বহুবিধ মুরজ মরদল, ত্রিসরি কুণ্ডলী পটহ পুষ্কল, কু কুনু নু নুনু সুধা বিবিধ বায়ত মধুর বাদক-ঘটা ।
নটত নর্ত্তকী নর্ত্তকাবলী, উঘটি তাধিক ধিকিতা ধিনি, নিধি ধেন্না ধিকি তক তাল ধরু, পগ-ভঙ্গী চমকত তনু-ছটা ॥

*bādya bahubidha muraja maradala, trisari kuṇḍalī paṭaha puṣkala, ku kunu nu nunu sudhā bibidha bāyata madhura bādaka-ghaṭā |*
*naṭata narttakī narttakābalī, ughaṭi tādhika dhikitā dhini, nidhi dhennā dhiki taka tāla dharu, paga-bhaṅgī camakata tanu-chaṭā ||*

*Word for word:* bādya bahubidha — many kinds of instruments; muraja maradala — muraja, mardala; trisari kuṇḍalī paṭaha — trisari, kundali, pataha; puṣkala — abundantly; ku kunu nu nunu sudhā — onomatopoeia; bibidha bāyata — play in various manners; madhura bādaka-ghaṭā — throngs of musicians, sweetly; naṭata narttakī narttakābalī — the dancing girls and lines of dancers dance; ughaṭi — beating out; tādhika dhikitā dhini nidhi dhennā dhiki taka — the dance-count; tāla dharu — keeping time; paga-bhaṅgī — movements of the feet; camakata tanu-chaṭā — the lustre of their bodies flashes

**14.3.** Many instruments — muraja, mardala, trisari, kundali, pataha — sound abundantly:
"ku-ku nu-nu nu-nu"; throngs of musicians play sweetly in various manners;
the dancing girls and lines of dancers dance, beating out "ta-dhika dhikita dhini,
ni-dhi dhenna dhiki taka", keeping time; the movements of their feet — the lustre of their bodies flashes.

জাতি শ্রুতি স্বর-গ্রাম মূরছন, তান নব নব নব আলাপন, শুনত কানন ত্যজি মৃগ, গুণীবৃন্দ নিকটহি ধায়এ ।
ভবন চহুঁ দিশ বিপুল কলকল, দাস নরহরি হৃদয় উছলল, সময় গোধূলি ললিত সুরধুনী-তীরে বিরমি ঘরে আয়এ ॥

*jāti śruti svara-grāma mūrachana, tāna naba naba naba ālāpana, śunata kānana tyaji mṛga, guṇībṛnda nikaṭahi dhāyae |*
*bhabana cahum̐ diśa bipula kalakala, dāsa narahari hṛdaya uchalala, samaya godhūli lalita suradhunī-tīre birami ghare āyae ||*

*Word for word:* jāti śruti svara-grāma mūrachana — jati, shruti, svaras, gramas, murcchanas; tāna — tanas; naba naba naba ālāpana — ever new alapas; śunata — hearing; kānana tyaji mṛga — the does leave the forest; guṇī-bṛnda nikaṭahi dhāyae — run to the skilled musicians; bhabana cahum̐ diśa — all around the house; bipula kalakala — a great clamour; dāsa narahari hṛdaya uchalala — the heart of the servant Narahari overflowed; samaya godhūli — at the hour of cow-dust; lalita suradhunī-tīre birami — pausing on the lovely bank of the Suradhuni (Ganga); ghare āyae — comes home

**14.4.** Jati, shruti, svaras, gramas, murcchanas, tanas — ever new alapas;
hearing them, the does leave the forest and run to the skilled musicians;
all around the house a great clamour; the heart of the servant Narahari overflowed:
at the hour of cow-dust, having paused on the lovely bank of the Suradhuni, [the Lord] comes home.

[^22-29]: GPT1 — p. 105, no. 32 (scan, PDF p. 364); GPT2 — section 2.4, no. 32 (catalogue: NG-068). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, pp. 816–817; ed. 1960, vv. 1595–1598).
Variants: 14.2 GPT1 "ucarita naba naba carita madhumaya", BR "ucari naba naba carita rasamaya" — the sense is the same; the onomatopoeic syllables in 14.3 differ among the
witnesses (GPT1 "ku kunu nu nunu sudhā", BR 1912 "kuku nunu nunu, mu dhā"). Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. Jati,
shruti, svara, grama, murcchana, tana, alapa are terms of Indian music (modes, intervals, notes, scales, transitions, runs, preludes).
[^22-30]: "Lakshmi and the Lord of Lakshmi" — in the newly-weds the people of Nadia recognise Lakshmi and Narayana: Vishnupriya is the eternal
energy of the Lord (note 2), Gaura is the Lord Himself; "the ornament of Vraja" (baraja-bhūṣaṇa) is Krishna. Cf. CB Adi 15 (= GPT 2.4 no. 39, Vrindavana
Dasa): on the way back some say this is Hara and Gauri, others — Kamala and Sri Hari.

## 15. Narahari — "gorācām̐da bibāha kariyā…" (GPT1 p. 106, no. 33; BR)
*The welcome at home: Gorachand, having married, returns home in joy; the invisible gods strew the way with flowers; someone hurries to
tell Shachi of the wedding; hearing the music, Shachi, beside herself with joy, comes out of the house, circles the newly-weds with
countless offerings and casts them away, kisses her son's moon-face and leads her son and daughter-in-law into the house; Vishvambhara with
Vishnupriya sit on the throne; the women raise cries of "ulu-lu", the bhatas recite praises, the brahmanas chant the Vedas. Raga not
stated. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^22-31]

গোরাচাঁদ বিবাহ করিয়া । আইসেন ঘরে অতি উলসিত হৈয়া ॥

*gorācām̐da bibāha kariyā | āisena ghare ati ulasita haiyā ||*

*Word for word:* gorācām̐da bibāha kariyā — Gorachand, having married; āisena ghare — comes home; ati ulasita haiyā — in great joy

**15.1.** Gorachand, having celebrated the wedding, comes home in great joy.

অলখিত হৈয়া দেবগণ । করয়ে সকল পথে পুষ্প-বরিষণ ॥

*alakhita haiyā debagaṇa | karaye sakala pathe puṣpa-bariṣaṇa ||*

*Word for word:* alakhita haiyā deba-gaṇa — the gods, invisible; karaye sakala pathe puṣpa-bariṣaṇa — shower flowers along the whole way

**15.2.** The invisible gods shower flowers along the whole way.

সুখের পাথার নদীয়ায় । বিবাহ-প্রসঙ্গ কেউ কহে শচীমায় ॥

*sukhera pāthāra nadīyāya | bibāha-prasaṅga keu kahe śacīmāya ||*

*Word for word:* sukhera pāthāra nadīyāya — an ocean of happiness in Nadia; bibāha-prasaṅga — of the wedding; keu kahe śacī-māya — someone tells Mother Shachi

**15.3.** An ocean of happiness in Nadia! Someone tells Mother Shachi of the wedding.

শুনি মহাবাদ্য-কোলাহল । শচীদেবী হইলেন আনন্দে বিহ্বল ॥

*śuni mahābādya-kolāhala | śacīdebī hailena ānande bihvala ||*

*Word for word:* śuni mahā-bādya-kolāhala — hearing the clamour of the great music; śacī-debī — Shachidevi; hailena ānande bihvala — became overwhelmed with joy

**15.4.** Hearing the clamour of the great music, Shachidevi is beside herself with joy.

বাড়ীর বাহির শচী আই । নিছিয়া ফেলয়ে যত দ্রব্য লেখা নাই ॥

*bāṛīra bāhira śacī āi | nichiyā phelaye yata drabya lekhā nāi ||*

*Word for word:* bāṛīra bāhira — out of the house; śacī āi — Mother Shachi; nichiyā phelaye — circling, casts away; yata drabya lekhā nāi — countless offerings

**15.5.** Mother Shachi [comes] out of the house; circling [the newly-weds], she casts away countless offerings.[^22-32]

স্নেহে চাঁদ-বদন চুম্বিয়া । প্রবেশে ভবনে পুত্রবধূ পুত্রে লৈয়া ॥

*snehe cām̐da-badana cumbiyā | prabeśe bhabane putrabadhū putre laiyā ||*

*Word for word:* snehe — tenderly; cām̐da-badana cumbiyā — kissing the moon-face; prabeśe bhabane — enters the house; putra-badhū putre laiyā — leading her daughter-in-law and son

**15.6.** Tenderly kissing the moon-face, she enters the house, leading her son and her daughter-in-law.

বিষ্ণুপ্রিয়া-সহ বিশ্বম্ভর । বৈসে সিংহাসনে দেখে যত পরিকর ॥

*biṣṇupriyā-saha biśvambhara | baise siṃhāsane dekhe yata parikara ||*

*Word for word:* biṣṇupriyā-saha biśvambhara — Vishvambhara with Vishnupriya; baise siṃhāsane — sit on the throne; dekhe yata parikara — all the associates gaze

**15.7.** Vishvambhara with Vishnupriya sit on the throne; all the associates gaze at Them.

উলু লুলু দেই নারীগণ । হইল মঙ্গলময় সকল ভবন ॥

*ulu lulu dei nārīgaṇa | haila maṅgalamaya sakala bhabana ||*

*Word for word:* ulu lulu dei nārī-gaṇa — the women raise cries of "ulu-lu"; haila maṅgalamaya — became filled with blessing; sakala bhabana — the whole house

**15.8.** The women raise cries of "ulu-lu"; the whole house became filled with blessing.

ভাটগণে পড়ে কায়বার । বিপ্রগণ বেদধ্বনি করে অনিবার ॥

*bhāṭagaṇe paṛe kāyabāra | bipragaṇa bedadhvani kare anibāra ||*

*Word for word:* bhāṭa-gaṇe paṛe kāyabāra — the bhatas recite praises; bipra-gaṇa beda-dhvani kare anibāra — the brahmanas chant the Vedas without pause

**15.9.** The bhatas recite praises; the brahmanas chant the Vedas without pause.

নানা বাদ্য বায় সবে সুখে । নরহরি কত বা কহিব একমুখে ॥

*nānā bādya bāya sabe sukhe | narahari kata bā kahiba ekamukhe ||*

*Word for word:* nānā bādya bāya sabe sukhe — all joyfully play various instruments; narahari kata vā kahiba eka-mukhe — how much can Narahari tell with one mouth

**15.10.** All joyfully play various instruments. How much can Narahari tell with a single mouth?

[^22-31]: GPT1 — p. 106, no. 33 (scan, PDF p. 365); GPT2 — section 2.4, no. 33 (catalogue: NG-069). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, pp. 817–818; ed. 1960, vv. 1599–1610).
Variants: between 15.4 and 15.5 the BR has two couplets more: "Mother Shachi outside the house waits with the chaste wives, watching the road.
Gora with all comes slowly and at the door descends from the palanquin. Seeing her son and daughter-in-law, mother…" (vv. 1603–1605); in GPT1
these lines are compressed into the single couplet 15.5 — the translation follows GPT1. 15.8 BR "sakala bhubana" ("the whole world"). Not in PK, KGC,
PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B.
[^22-32]: "Circling, she casts away" (nichiyā phelaye) — the custom of nirmanchhana: the mother circles the newly-weds with offerings and casts them
away, warding off all evil (in Lochana, vv. 175–178). Shachi is the mother of the Lord, eternally abiding in parental love for Him. Shachi
welcomes her son and daughter-in-law — CB Adi 15.

## 16. Narahari — "gorā guṇamaṇi sughaṛa-śekhara…" (GPT1 p. 106, no. 34; BR)
*The Lord gives gifts and sends off the guests: to the bhatas, dancers, singers, musicians, beggars and brahmanas He gives clothes,
ornaments and wealth, fulfilling their desires, and satisfies all with kind words; all go home singing the glories of Gaurahari; Shachi
honours each of the women. Raga not stated. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR; Vrajabuli.*[^22-33]

গোরা গুণমণি সুঘড়-শেখর পরম মুদিত হিয়ায় ।
লোক বহুত বিবাহে আকুল তাহে দেয়ই বিদায় ॥

*gorā guṇamaṇi sughaṛa-śekhara parama mudita hiyāya |*
*loka bahuta bibāhe ākula tāhe deyai bidāya ||*

*Word for word:* gorā guṇamaṇi — Gora, the jewel of virtues; sughaṛa-śekhara — crown of the skilful; parama mudita hiyāya — in great joy of heart; loka bahuta — many people; bibāhe ākula — eager for the wedding; tāhe deyai bidāya — He sends them off with gifts

**16.1.** Gora, the jewel of virtues, the crown of the skilful, in great joy of heart
sends off [with gifts] the many people who came to the wedding in excitement.

ভাট নট গীতজ্ঞ বাদক ভিক্ষু ভূসুর ভূরি ।
দেত সবে বহু বস্ত্র ভূষণ ধন মনোরথ পূরি ॥

*bhāṭa naṭa gītajña bādaka bhikṣu bhūsura bhūri |*
*deta sabe bahu bastra bhūṣaṇa dhana manoratha pūri ||*

*Word for word:* bhāṭa naṭa gītajña bādaka — to bhatas, dancers, connoisseurs of song, musicians; bhikṣu — beggars; bhūsura bhūri — many brahmanas; deta sabe — He gives to all; bahu bastra bhūṣaṇa dhana — many clothes, ornaments, riches; manoratha pūri — fulfilling desires

**16.2.** To the bhatas, dancers, connoisseurs of song, musicians, beggars and the many brahmanas
He gives to all many clothes, ornaments and riches, fulfilling their desires.

অতিহি সুমধুর বচনে সুনিপুণ পরিতোষ করই সভায় ।
চলল নিজ নিজ গেহে সবে মিলি গৌরহরি-যশ গায় ॥

*atihi sumadhura bacane sunipuṇa paritoṣa karai sabhāya |*
*calala nija nija gehe sabe mili gaurahari-yaśa gāya ||*

*Word for word:* atihi sumadhura bacane — with most sweet words; sunipuṇa — skilfully; paritoṣa karai sabhāya — satisfies everyone; calala nija nija gehe — went to their own homes; sabe mili — all together; gaurahari-yaśa gāya — singing the glories of Gaurahari

**16.3.** With most sweet words He skilfully satisfies everyone;
all together go to their homes, singing the glories of Gaurahari.

শ্রীশচী সব নারী জনে জনে কয়ল কত সম্মান ।
ভণত নরহরি সো সকল সুখে গেহে কয়ল পয়ান ॥

*śrīśacī saba nārī jane jane kayala kata sammāna |*
*bhaṇata narahari so sakala sukhe gehe kayala payāna ||*

*Word for word:* śrī-śacī — Sri Shachi; saba nārī jane jane — to each of the women; kayala kata sammāna — showed so much honour; bhaṇata narahari — says Narahari; so sakala sukhe — they all in happiness; gehe kayala payāna — set out for home

**16.4.** Sri Shachi showed so much honour to each of the women;
says Narahari: they all went home in happiness.[^22-34]

[^22-33]: GPT1 — p. 106, no. 34 (scan, PDF p. 365); GPT2 — section 2.4, no. 34 (catalogue: NG-070). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 818; ed. 1960, vv. 1611–1614).
Variants: 16.1 GPT1 "bibāhe ātula", BR "bibāhe ākula" — following the BR; 16.2 GPT1 "manorama puri", BR "manoratha pūri" ("fulfilling desires") — following
the BR. Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. Next in the BR comes prose on Vishnupriya's service to her
mother-in-law and on the Lord's journey to Gaya (vv. 1615–1625); in the GPT — nos. 35–38 (an extract from Lochana's Chaitanya-mangala) and nos. 39–40
(Vrindavana Dasa) — outside the appendix (introductory note).
[^22-34]: To send off with gifts (bidāya) all who came to the wedding and served at it is the custom; the Lord is a generous host, Shachi the
mistress of the house. In the chronology of the biographies the Lord's journey to Gaya follows (CB Adi 17; CC Adi 17).

## 17. Narahari — "jāgaha jana-mana-cora caturabara…" (GPT1 p. 343, section 5.2, no. 1; GCC)
*Ashtakaliya, the songs of awakening at the end of the night: "Awake, Stealer of hearts, jewel of Radha's heart! The night is over. You
who, hearing of the deeds of Vraja, find no taste in food or sleep, who hold sankirtana dearer than life — what sleep has overcome You?"
Raga not stated. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC; Vrajabuli.*[^22-35]

জাগহ জন-মন-চোর চতুরবর সুন্দর নদীয়া-নগর-বিহারী ।
রাধা রমণী-শিরোমণি রসবতী তাকর হৃদয়-রতন-রুচিকারী ॥

*jāgaha jana-mana-cora caturabara sundara nadīyā-nagara-bihārī |*
*rādhā ramaṇī-śiromaṇi rasabatī tākara hṛdaya-ratana-rucikārī ||*

*Word for word:* jāgaha — awake; jana-mana-cora — Stealer of people's hearts; catura-bara — best of the clever; sundara — beautiful; nadīyā-nagara-bihārī — who sports in the town of Nadia; rādhā — of Radha; ramaṇī-śiromaṇi — crown of women; rasabatī — full of rasa; tākara hṛdaya-ratana — the jewel of Her heart; rucikārī — shining with [Her] light (lit. "illumining")

**17.1.** Awake, Stealer of people's hearts, best of the clever, beautiful One who sports in the town of Nadia, —
jewel of the heart of Radha, crown of women, full of rasa — You who shine with Her light![^22-36]

কি কহব পুন পুন নিশি ভেল ভোর ।
কৈছন অলস কিছুই নাহি সমুঝিয়ে হৃদয়ে সন্দেহ রহত বহু মোর ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*ki kahaba puna puna niśi bhela bhora |*
*kaichana alasa kichui nāhi samujhiye hṛdaye sandeha rahata bahu mora || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* ki kahaba — what shall I say; puna puna — again and again; niśi bhela bhora — the night is over; kaichana alasa — what languor is this; kichui nāhi samujhiye — I understand nothing; hṛdaye sandeha rahata bahu mora — much doubt remains in my heart

**17.2.** What shall I say? Again and again [I tell You]: the night is over!
What languor is this? I understand nothing — there is much doubt in my heart.

ব্রজপুর-চারু-চরিত-গুণ শুনইতে ভোজন শয়ন করহি নাহি ভায় ।
ভণইতে দিবস রজনী বহি যাওয়ে তাহে কৈছে অব ঘুম শোহায় ॥

*brajapura-cāru-carita-guṇa śunaite bhojana śayana karahi nāhi bhāya |*
*bhaṇaite dibasa rajanī bahi yāoye tāhe kaiche aba ghuma śohāya ||*

*Word for word:* brajapura-cāru-carita-guṇa — the virtues of the lovely deeds of Vraja; śunaite — hearing; bhojana śayana — food and sleep; karahi nāhi bhāya — You find no taste in; bhaṇaite — telling; dibasa rajanī bahi yāoye — days and nights pass; tāhe kaiche aba ghuma śohāya — how then is sleep pleasing now

**17.3.** Hearing of the virtues of the lovely deeds of Vraja, You find no taste in food or sleep;
telling of them, You pass days and nights — how then is sleep pleasing to You now?

প্রাণ-অধিক করি মানহ অনুখন নিরুপম সংকীর্ত্তন সুখকন্দ ।
তা বিনু পলক কল্প সম অনুভব ইথে নরহরি চিতে লাগয়ে ধন্দ ॥

*prāṇa-adhika kari mānaha anukhana nirupama saṃkīrttana sukhakanda |*
*tā binu palaka kalpa sama anubhaba ithe narahari cite lāgaye dhanda ||*

*Word for word:* prāṇa-adhika kari mānaha — You hold dearer than life; anukhana — every moment; nirupama saṅkīrttana — the incomparable sankirtana; sukha-kanda — root of joy; tā binu — without it; palaka kalpa sama anubhaba — a moment feels like a kalpa; ithe — at this; narahari cite lāgaye dhanda — Narahari's heart is perplexed

**17.4.** Every moment You hold dearer than life the incomparable sankirtana, the root of joy;
without it a moment seems to You a kalpa — and so Narahari's heart is perplexed.[^22-37]

[^22-35]: GPT1 — p. 343, section 5.2 "Ashtakaliya" (dvitīya ucchvāsa — aṣṭakālīyalīlā), no. 1 ("yathārāga"; scan, PDF p. 602); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 1 (catalogue:
NG-171). GCC — kirana 2 (the last part of the night: "the pastimes on the bed"), pada 23. All the awakening songs GPT 5.2 nos. 1–10 are in the
GCC, but in a different order: in kirana 2 as padas 14 (no. 10) and 16–23 (nos. 6, 7, 8, 9, 4, 5, 2, 1), in kirana 3 ("the awakening") as pada 8
(no. 3); between them the GCC says that these songs were sung by a clever parrot (kīra), raised by the Lord's servant, together with Narahari
(pada 15), and that the sleeping Gaura, absorbed in rasa, heard a little of them (pada 24). The variants are minor (17.1 GCC "jana-mana-cora"). Not
in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. Cf. Gaura's awakening in Vasu Ghosha (GPT 5.2 no. 11; chapter 12, no. 6).
[^22-36]: Ashtakaliya, "the eight parts of the day": songs of the Lord's eternal pastimes in Navadvipa by the hours of day and night, on the
model of the ashtakaliya of Radha and Krishna in Vraja; it is eternal lila, which devotees remember in their service, not the routine of an
ordinary day. The Lord's sleep is not the sleep of a conditioned soul under the sway of maya: in the GCC Gaura's night is "the pastimes on
the bed", absorption in the pastimes of Vraja (cf. 17.3; no. 18: "as before"); His associates wake Him (in the GCC a parrot, as in Vraja
Vrinda's parrots wake Radha and Krishna), and in their joking reproaches to the "sluggard" is their love. "Jewel of Radha's heart… You who
shine with Her light" (tākara hṛdaya-ratana-rucikārī, lit. "who illumines the jewel of Her heart") — Gaura is Krishna Himself, the jewel of Radha's
heart, appearing in Her mood and lustre (CC Adi 1.5).
[^22-37]: Sankirtana is the congregational singing of the holy names, for which the Lord appeared (CC Adi 3); a kalpa is a day of Brahma, an
image of endlessly long time.

## 18. Narahari — "uṭha uṭha āji eki adbhuta ghuma…" (GPT1 pp. 343–344, no. 2; GCC)
*A joking reproach to the sleeping Gaura: "Get up! What strange sleep is this? People laugh at You; were it now as before, You would run
away Yourself for shame; it is well that Your Gadadhara, Narahari and the others are asleep too and the old fears are gone — otherwise
they would have run away, leaving You; sleep with them, but if it gets late, do not blame Narahari afterwards". Raga not stated.
**Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC.*[^22-38]

উঠ উঠ আজি একি অদ্ভুত ঘুম ঘুমায়াছ চতুর ওহে ।
এরূপ কখন না দেখিয়ে তুয়া রীতি আর কত বুঝাব তোহে ॥

*uṭha uṭha āji eki adbhuta ghuma ghumāyācha catura ohe |*
*erūpa kakhana nā dekhiye tuyā rīti āra kata bujhāba tohe ||*

*Word for word:* uṭha uṭha — get up, get up; āji — today; eki adbhuta ghuma ghumāyācha — what wondrous sleep You sleep; catura ohe — O clever One; e-rūpa kakhana nā dekhiye — never have I seen such; tuyā rīti — Your habit; āra kata bujhāba tohe — how much more must I coax You

**18.1.** Get up, get up! What wondrous sleep are You sleeping today, O clever One!
Never have I seen such a habit in You — how much longer must I coax You?

এ সময়ে এত অলসে কি সুখ আনে হাসি করে তোমার কাজে ।
পূর্ব্বের মত হইলে এখন জাগাতে না হৈত পলাইতে লাজে ॥

*e samaye eta alase ki sukha āne hāsi kare tomāra kāje |*
*pūrvvera mata haile ekhana jāgāte nā haita palāite lāje ||*

*Word for word:* e samaye — at this hour; eta alase ki sukha — what joy in such languor; āne hāsi kare tomāra kāje — others laugh at Your doings; pūrvvera mata haile ekhana — were it now as before; jāgāte nā haita — there would be no need to wake [You]; palāite lāje — [You would] run away for shame

**18.2.** What joy is there in such languor at this hour? Others laugh at Your doings.
Were it now as before, You would not need waking: You would run away for shame.[^22-39]

তেমতি তোমার গদাধর নরহরি আদি সব আছয়ে শুঞা ।
সে সকল ভয় নাহি তেঞি ভালো নহিলে পলাইত তোমারে থুঞা ॥

*temati tomāra gadādhara narahari ādi saba āchaye śuñā |*
*se sakala bhaya nāhi teñi bhālo nahile palāita tomāre thuñā ||*

*Word for word:* temati — likewise; tomāra gadādhara narahari ādi saba — Your Gadadhara, Narahari and all the others; āchaye śuñā — are lying asleep; se sakala bhaya nāhi — those fears are not there; teñi bhālo — so it is well; nahile palāita tomāre thuñā — otherwise they would have fled, leaving You

**18.3.** Likewise Your Gadadhara, Narahari and all the others are lying asleep;
those fears are gone too — so it is well; otherwise they would have run away, leaving You.

কি বলিব নিজ প্রিয়গণে লৈয়া শুয়ে থাক ইথে কিসের যাবে ।
বেলাধিক হৈলে নরহরি প্রতি পাছে কিছু দোষ দিতে না পাবে ॥

*ki baliba nija priyagaṇe laiyā śuye thāka ithe kisera yābe |*
*belādhika haile narahari prati pāche kichu doṣa dite nā pābe ||*

*Word for word:* ki baliba — what shall I say; nija priya-gaṇe laiyā — with Your dear ones; śuye thāka — lie [there]; ithe kisera yābe — what will You lose by it; belādhika haile — if it gets late; narahari prati — on Narahari; pāche kichu doṣa dite nā pābe — afterwards You cannot lay any blame

**18.4.** What shall I say? Lie with Your dear ones — what do You lose by it?
But if it gets very late — do not blame Narahari afterwards.

[^22-38]: GPT1 — pp. 343–344, no. 2 (scan, PDF pp. 602–603); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 2 (catalogue: NG-172). GCC — kirana 2, pada 22. The variants are minor
(18.3 GCC "śuyā", "thuyā"; 18.4 GCC "śuyā thāka"). Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^22-39]: "As before" — a hint at the eternal lila of Vraja: at the end of the night Krishna and the gopis hurriedly leave the kunja, afraid of
being seen by the elders. Gadadhara, according to Kavi Karnapura's Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika, is the manifestation of Radha in Gaura's lila;
Narahari Sarakara is Madhumati, Radha's friend. In Navadvipa "those fears are gone" — so the associates sleep beside the Lord. The joking
reproaches are the associates' love, not censure (note 36).

## 19. Narahari — "śuna śuna ohe kichu nā bujhiye…" (GPT1 p. 344, no. 3; GCC)
*At Gaura's bedside: the night is over, yet He, the enchanter of the world, sleeps, absorbed in who knows what rasa; Gadadhara, his eyes on
His face, sits at His feet and smilingly presses them; Narahari floats in an ocean of joy, gazing at Gauranga, and whispers something into
Gadadhara's ear; others, intoxicated with Gaura-rasa, doze; someone insists that the Lord be woken. Raga lalita. **Attribution: probably
Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC.*[^22-40]

শুন শুন ওহে কিছু না বুঝিয়ে কি রসে হৈয়াছ ভোরা ।
নিশি ভোর তমু ঘুমাঞা রৈয়াছ ভুবনমোহন গোরা ॥

*śuna śuna ohe kichu nā bujhiye ki rase haiyācha bhorā |*
*niśi bhora tamu ghumāñā raiyācha bhubanamohana gorā ||*

*Word for word:* śuna śuna ohe — listen, listen; kichu nā bujhiye — I cannot understand; ki rase haiyācha bhorā — in what rasa He is lost; niśi bhora — the night is over; tamu — still (?); ghumāñā raiyācha — He keeps sleeping; bhubana-mohana gorā — Gora, the enchanter of the world

**19.1.** Listen, listen! I cannot understand — in what rasa is He lost?
The night is over, and still Gora, the enchanter of the world, sleeps.

আর দেখ গদাধর আঁখি দিয়ে গৌরাঙ্গচাঁদের মুখে ।
চরণ-নিকটে বসি হাসি হাসি চরণ চাপয়ে সুখে ॥

*āra dekha gadādhara ām̐khi diye gaurāṅgacām̐dera mukhe |*
*caraṇa-nikaṭe basi hāsi hāsi caraṇa cāpaye sukhe ||*

*Word for word:* āra dekha gadādhara — and look at Gadadhara; ām̐khi diye gaurāṅgacām̐dera mukhe — his eyes fixed on the face of Gaurangachand; caraṇa-nikaṭe basi — sitting at the feet; hāsi hāsi — smiling; caraṇa cāpaye sukhe — joyfully presses the feet

**19.2.** And look at Gadadhara: his eyes fixed on the face of Gaurangachand,
he sits at His feet and, smiling, joyfully presses His feet.

নরহরি সুখ-সায়রেতে ভাসে চাহিয়া গৌরাঙ্গ-পানে ।
অপরূপ ভঙ্গী করি কিবা কথা কহে গদাধর-কাণে ॥

*narahari sukha-sāyarete bhāse cāhiyā gaurāṅga-pāne |*
*aparūpa bhaṅgī kari kibā kathā kahe gadādhara-kāṇe ||*

*Word for word:* narahari sukha-sāyarete bhāse — Narahari floats in an ocean of joy; cāhiyā gaurāṅga-pāne — gazing at Gauranga; aparūpa bhaṅgī kari — with wondrous grace; kibā kathā kahe gadādhara-kāṇe — whispers something into Gadadhara's ear

**19.3.** Narahari floats in an ocean of joy, gazing at Gauranga;
with wondrous grace he whispers something into Gadadhara's ear.

কেহ কেহ ঢুলি পড়ে গোরা-রসে মাতিয়া হৈয়াছে ধন্দ ।
নরহরি-প্রাণনাথে জাগাইতে কেহ করে অনুবন্ধ ॥

*keha keha ḍhuli paṛe gorā-rase mātiyā haiyāche dhanda |*
*narahari-prāṇanāthe jāgāite keha kare anubandha ||*

*Word for word:* keha keha — some; ḍhuli paṛe — nod in drowsiness; gorā-rase mātiyā — intoxicated with Gora-rasa; haiyāche dhanda — are confused; narahari-prāṇanāthe jāgāite — to wake the Lord of Narahari's life; keha kare anubandha — someone insists

**19.4.** Others, intoxicated with Gaura-rasa, nod in drowsiness, their senses confused;
and someone insists that the Lord of Narahari's life be woken.[^22-41]

[^22-40]: GPT1 — p. 344, no. 3 ("lalita"; scan, PDF p. 603); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 3 (catalogue: NG-173). GCC — kirana 3 ("the awakening"), pada 8 (introduced
there with the words "and someone [says]", kopi ca). Variants: 19.1 "tamu" in both GPT1 and GCC — probably "tabu" ("still"); 19.2 GCC "ām̐khi diyā". Not in
the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^22-41]: Here Narahari is a participant in the lila at the Lord's bedside beside Gadadhara; if the pada belongs to Chakravarti, this is
Narahari Sarakara, the Lord's associate (introductory note in ch. 17; cf. note 39). Gadadhara pressing the Lord's feet is an image of his
eternal service.

## 20. Narahari — "jāga jāga ohe gauraśaśī…" (GPT1 p. 344, no. 4; GCC)
*"Awake, Gaura-moon: the night is over; Your associates, leaving their homes, have gathered in the courtyard like chakoras without the
moon; leave Your bed, show Yourself, sate their thirsting eyes, speak but a word, embrace them and take away their sorrow". Raga not
stated. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC.*[^22-42]

জাগ জাগ ওহে গৌরশশী, কত ঘুম যাও পোহাইল নিশি ।
গৃহ পরিহরি তুয়া পরিকর তুরিতে আঙ্গিনা বেঢ়ল আসি ॥

*jāga jāga ohe gauraśaśī, kata ghuma yāo pohāila niśi |*
*gṛha parihari tuyā parikara turite āṅginā beṛhala āsi ||*

*Word for word:* jāga jāga ohe gauraśaśī — awake, awake, O Gaura-moon; kata ghuma yāo — how long You sleep; pohāila niśi — the night is over; gṛha parihari — leaving their homes; tuyā parikara — Your associates; turite — quickly; āṅginā beṛhala āsi — have come and filled the courtyard

**20.1.** Awake, awake, O Gaura-moon! How long You sleep — the night is over.
Leaving their homes, Your associates have hurried here and filled the courtyard.

এ সভার সম কাহু না দেখি, চাঁদ বিনা জনু চকোর পাখী ।
তাহে শীঘ্র শেজ তেজি দেখা দিয়া তিরপিত কর তৃষিত আঁখি ॥

*e sabhāra sama kāhu nā dekhi, cām̐da binā janu cakora pākhī |*
*tāhe śīghra śeja teji dekhā diyā tirapita kara tṛṣita ām̐khi ||*

*Word for word:* e sabhāra sama kāhu nā dekhi — I see none like them; cām̐da binā janu cakora pākhī — like chakora birds without the moon; tāhe — so; śīghra śeja teji — quickly leaving the bed; dekhā diyā — showing Yourself; tirapita kara tṛṣita ām̐khi — sate their thirsting eyes

**20.2.** I have seen none like them: they are like chakora birds without the moon;
so leave Your bed quickly, show Yourself and sate their thirsting eyes.

কি কহব চারু চরিত-কথা, নীরব হইয়া আছয়ে হেথা ।
সুধামাখা মৃদু বচন বারেক শুনাঞা ঘুচাহ হিয়ার বেথা ॥

*ki kahaba cāru carita-kathā, nīraba haiyā āchaye hethā |*
*sudhāmākhā mṛdu bacana bāreka śunāñā ghucāha hiyāra bethā ||*

*Word for word:* ki kahaba — what shall I say; cāru carita-kathā — the lovely talks of [Your] deeds; nīraba haiyā āchaye hethā — have fallen silent here; sudhā-mākhā mṛdu bacana — soft words steeped in nectar; bāreka śunāñā — letting them hear once; ghucāha hiyāra bethā — remove the pain of their hearts

**20.3.** What shall I say? The lovely talks of [Your] deeds have fallen silent here — all stand mute;
let them hear but once Your soft words steeped in nectar — take away the pain of their hearts.

চারি পাশে চাহে চঞ্চল মতি অতিশয় ক্ষীণ বুঝিনু রীতি ।
আলিঙ্গন দিয়া দেহ-দুঃখ দূর কর নরহরি-পরাণপতি ॥

*cāri pāśe cāhe cañcala mati atiśaya kṣīṇa bujhinu rīti |*
*āliṅgana diyā deha-duḥkha dūra kara narahari-parāṇapati ||*

*Word for word:* cāri pāśe cāhe — they look all around; cañcala mati — their minds restless; atiśaya kṣīṇa — utterly exhausted; bujhinu rīti — I have understood their state; āliṅgana diyā — giving an embrace; deha-duḥkha dūra kara — drive away the suffering of the body; narahari-parāṇapati — O Lord of Narahari's life

**20.4.** They look around on all sides, their hearts restless; I have understood — they are utterly exhausted;
embrace them and drive away the suffering of their bodies, O Lord of Narahari's life![^22-43]

[^22-42]: GPT1 — p. 344, no. 4 ("yathārāga"; scan, PDF p. 603); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 4 (catalogue: NG-174). GCC — kirana 2, pada 20. The variants are minor
(20.2 GCC "yena cakora pākhi"; 20.4 GCC "atiśaya khiṇa"). Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^22-43]: The chakora is a bird which, according to poetic tradition, feeds only on moonlight; an image of devotees who live by beholding the
Lord. The Lord's embrace is His mercy to His associates.

## 21. Narahari — "pohāila niśi pāila parāṇa…" (GPT1 pp. 344–345, no. 5; GCC)
*"The night is over — all have come back to life; thinking of Your deeds, no one can attend to household work, and all have hurried to You,
yet You do not wake. The brahmanas of Nadia go to the Suradhuni and laugh: 'Look, Nimai Pandita is still asleep!' Get up and perform Your
morning duties, or ill fame will spread about You and Narahari will be ashamed". Raga not stated. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** —
the pada is in the GCC.*[^22-44]

পোহাইল নিশি পাইল পরাণ পরস্পর নারী-পুরুষগণে ।
তুয়া সুচরিত-চয় চারু চিন্তি গৃহকর্ম্ম কারু নাহিক মনে ॥

*pohāila niśi pāila parāṇa paraspara nārī-puruṣagaṇe |*
*tuyā sucarita-caya cāru cinti gṛhakarmma kāru nāhika mane ||*

*Word for word:* pohāila niśi — the night is over; pāila parāṇa — have regained life; paraspara nārī-puruṣa-gaṇe — all the men and women; tuyā sucarita-caya cāru cinti — thinking of the multitude of Your lovely deeds; gṛha-karmma kāru nāhika mane — no one has a mind for household work

**21.1.** The night is over — and all the men and women have as it were regained their lives;
thinking of Your many lovely deeds, no one can attend to household work.

অতি ত্বরা করি তিরপিত হৈতে আইল সকলে তোমার কাছে ।
না জাগহ তুমি এ বড় বিষম না জানি কি সুখ ঘুমেতে আছে ॥

*ati tvarā kari tirapita haite āila sakale tomāra kāche |*
*nā jāgaha tumi e baṛa biṣama nā jāni ki sukha ghumete āche ||*

*Word for word:* ati tvarā kari — in great haste; tirapita haite — to be sated; āila sakale tomāra kāche — all have come to You; nā jāgaha tumi — You do not wake; e baṛa biṣama — this is a great trouble; nā jāni ki sukha ghumete āche — I do not know what joy is in sleep

**21.2.** In great haste all have come to You, to sate themselves [with seeing You];
yet You do not wake — what a trouble! I do not know what joy there is in this sleep.

নদীয়ার যত দ্বিজ নিজকাজে সুরধুনী-তীরে চলিলা ধাঞা ।
তারা পরস্পর করে হাসি দেখ নিমাই পণ্ডিত রৈয়াছে শুঞা ॥

*nadīyāra yata dvija nijakāje suradhunī-tīre calilā dhāñā |*
*tārā paraspara kare hāsi dekha nimāi paṇḍita raiyāche śuñā ||*

*Word for word:* nadīyāra yata dvija — all the brahmanas of Nadia; nija-kāje — about their business; suradhunī-tīre calilā dhāñā — hurried to the bank of the Suradhuni (Ganga); tārā paraspara kare hāsi — laugh among themselves; dekha — look; nimāi paṇḍita raiyāche śuñā — Nimai Pandita is still lying asleep

**21.3.** All the brahmanas of Nadia, about their business, have hurried to the bank of the Suradhuni;
they laugh among themselves: "Look, Nimai Pandita is still lying asleep!"

তাহে বলি শেজ তেজি প্রাতঃক্রিয়া কর ওহে গোরা গুণের মণি ।
নহে তুয়া অপযশ সবে গাবে পাবে লাজ নরহরি তা শুনি ॥

*tāhe bali śeja teji prātaḥkriyā kara ohe gorā guṇera maṇi |*
*nahe tuyā apayaśa sabe gābe pābe lāja narahari tā śuni ||*

*Word for word:* tāhe bali — so I say; śeja teji — leaving the bed; prātaḥ-kriyā kara — perform the morning duties; ohe gorā guṇera maṇi — O Gora, jewel of virtues; nahe — otherwise; tuyā apayaśa sabe gābe — all will spread ill fame about You; pābe lāja narahari tā śuni — Narahari will be ashamed on hearing it

**21.4.** So, I say, leave Your bed and perform Your morning duties, O Gora, jewel of virtues,
or else all will spread ill fame about You — and hearing it, Narahari will be ashamed.[^22-45]

[^22-44]: GPT1 — pp. 344–345, no. 5 ("yathārāga"; scan, PDF pp. 603–604; the number is garbled in the OCR — "৫ pda", and the signature-checking script misses the
pada); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 5. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-290). GCC — kirana 2, pada 21. Variants: 21.2 GPT1 "nā jānaha tumi" ("You
do not know"), GCC "nā jāgaha tumi" ("You do not wake") — following the GCC; 21.2 GCC "ati tvarātvari". Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^22-45]: "Nimai Pandita" is the Lord's name in the time of His scholarship; the brahmanas go to the Ganga for the morning bath. The joking
threat of "ill fame" is the love of the one who wakes Him (note 36): the eternal lila of Navadvipa includes these pastimes of the Lord in
the guise of a young scholar and householder.

## 22. Narahari — "jāgaha jagajībana naba nadīyāpuracām̐da he…" (GPT1 p. 345, no. 6; GCC)
*A hymn of awakening in solemn Vrajabuli: "Awake, Life of the world, new Moon of Nadia!" — with a chain of epithets: auspicious king
Kamadeva, form the colour of gorochana, full of rasa, teeth like jasmine, eyes a snare for glances and hearts, crusher of Kama, golden lotus
in the lake of the devotees' hearts, clad in cloud-coloured garments, King of dancers, He whose feet, dispelling the fear of worldly
existence, are worshipped by the gods; "today, seeing Your sleep, I am perplexed". Raga bhairava. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** —
the pada is in the GCC; Vrajabuli.*[^22-46]

জাগহ জগজীবন নব নদীয়াপুরচাঁদ হে ।
মঙ্গলময় মদন-ভূপ, গোরোচনা-রুচির রূপ,
রসময় রস-বিবশ রসিকভূষণ রসকন্দ হে ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*jāgaha jagajībana naba nadīyāpuracām̐da he |*
*maṅgalamaya madana-bhūpa, gorocanā-rucira rūpa,*
*rasamaya rasa-bibaśa rasikabhūṣaṇa rasakanda he || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* jāgaha — awake; jaga-jībana — Life of the world; naba nadīyā-pura-cām̐da he — O new Moon of the town of Nadia; maṅgalamaya madana-bhūpa — auspicious king Kamadeva; gorocanā-rucira rūpa — a form lovely as gorochana; rasamaya — full of rasa; rasa-bibaśa — overwhelmed by rasa; rasika-bhūṣaṇa — ornament of the connoisseurs of rasa; rasa-kanda — root of rasa

**22.1.** Awake, Life of the world, new Moon of the town of Nadia!
Auspicious king Kamadeva, Your form is lovely as gorochana;
full of rasa, overwhelmed by rasa, ornament of the connoisseurs of rasa, root of rasa!

সুন্দর বর কুন্দরদন, রঙ্গদ মৃদু মঞ্জু বদন,
চারু চপল লোচন জন-লোচন-মন-ফন্দ হে ॥

*sundara bara kundaradana, raṅgada mṛdu mañju badana,*
*cāru capala locana jana-locana-mana-phanda he ||*

*Word for word:* sundara bara — beautiful; kunda-radana — with teeth like jasmine; raṅgada — joy-giving; mṛdu mañju badana — a soft lovely face; cāru capala locana — lovely restless eyes; jana-locana-mana-phanda — a snare for the eyes and hearts of people

**22.2.** Beautiful One, with teeth like jasmine flowers, with a soft, lovely, joy-giving face,
with lovely, restless eyes — a snare for the eyes and hearts of people!

বন্ধুর উর মধুর দাম, চঞ্চল-ললনাভিরাম,
ধৃতিভরহর ধৈর্য্যধাম কাম-দলত শন্দ হে ॥

*bandhura ura madhura dāma, cañcala-lalanābhirāma,*
*dhṛtibharahara dhairyyadhāma kāma-dalata śanda he ||*

*Word for word:* bandhura ura — a lovely chest; madhura dāma — a sweet garland; cañcala-lalanābhirāma — delight of trembling women; dhṛti-bhara-hara — stealing composure; dhairyya-dhāma — abode of steadiness; kāma-dalata — crushing Kama; śanda — (unclear)

**22.3.** On Your beautiful chest a sweet garland; You are the delight of trembling women,
stealing their composure, Yourself the abode of steadiness, crusher of Kama!

শোভাকর কুটিল কেশ, নিরুপম ধৃত ললিত বেশ,
ভক্তহৃদয়-সরসি হেম-সরসিজ-কৃত-ছন্দ হে ।
সিংহগ্রীব বিমল কর্ণ, তিলকিত চন্দন সুবর্ণ,
মেঘাম্বরধর নটেন্দ্র নন্দিত-প্রিয়বৃন্দ হে ॥

*śobhākara kuṭila keśa, nirupama dhṛta lalita beśa,*
*bhaktahṛdaya-sarasi hema-sarasija-kṛta-chanda he |*
*siṃhagrība bimala karṇa, tilakita candana subarṇa,*
*meghāmbaradhara naṭendra nandita-priyabṛnda he ||*

*Word for word:* śobhākara kuṭila keśa — beautiful curling hair; nirupama dhṛta lalita beśa — an incomparable graceful attire; bhakta-hṛdaya-sarasi — in the lake of the devotees' hearts; hema-sarasija — a golden lotus; kṛta-chanda — having made its home; siṃha-grība — with a lion's neck; bimala karṇa — pure ears; tilakita candana subarṇa — marked with a tilaka of golden sandal; meghāmbara-dhara — wearing cloud-coloured garments; naṭendra — King of dancers; nandita-priya-bṛnda — delighting His dear ones

**22.4.** Beautiful curling hair, an incomparable graceful attire,
a golden lotus that has made its home in the lake of the devotees' hearts!
Neck like a lion's, pure ears, a tilaka of golden sandal,
clad in cloud-coloured garments, King of dancers, delighting His dear ones!

গুণমণি-মন্দির মনোজ্ঞ, গতিজিত-কুঞ্জর কৃতজ্ঞ,
ভবভয়ভর-ভঞ্জন-পদ বৃন্দারক-বন্দ্য হে ।
নরহরি-প্রিয় হিয়াকি বাত, কি কহব কছু কহি ন জাত,
আজু তোহারি শয়ন হেরি লাগত মোহে ধন্দ হে ॥

*guṇamaṇi-mandira manojña, gatijita-kuñjara kṛtajña,*
*bhababhayabhara-bhañjana-pada bṛndāraka-bandya he |*
*narahari-priya hiyāki bāta, ki kahaba kachu kahi na jāta,*
*āju tohāri śayana heri lāgata mohe dhanda he ||*

*Word for word:* guṇamaṇi-mandira — temple of jewel-like virtues; manojña — captivating; gati-jita-kuñjara — whose gait surpasses the elephant; kṛtajña — grateful; bhaba-bhaya-bhara-bhañjana-pada — whose feet shatter the burden of the fear of worldly existence; bṛndāraka-bandya — worshipped by the gods; narahari-priya — dear One of Narahari; hiyāki bāta — the matter of the heart; ki kahaba kichu kahi na jāta — what shall I say, nothing can be told; āju tohāri śayana heri — seeing Your sleep today; lāgata mohe dhanda — perplexity seizes me

**22.5.** Temple of jewel-like virtues, captivating, with a gait surpassing the elephant's, grateful,
He whose feet, which shatter the burden of the fear of worldly existence, are worshipped by the gods!
Dear One of Narahari, what can I say of what is in my heart? — nothing can be expressed:
today, seeing Your sleep, I am perplexed.[^22-47]

[^22-46]: GPT1 — p. 345, no. 6 ("bhairaba"; scan, PDF p. 604); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 6. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-291). GCC — kirana 2, pada 16
("rāga bhairaba"). Variants: 22.1 GCC "nadīyāpuracanda"; 22.3 "kāma-dalata śanda" — the last word is unclear (also in the GCC), translated by the sense; 22.4 GPT1
"bhabhaktahṛdaya" (misprint). Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. Lines 22.1 are the refrain (dhru).
[^22-47]: "Worshipped by the gods" (bṛndāraka-bandya), "dispelling the fear of worldly existence" are epithets of the Supreme Lord; "crusher of Kama" —
