His beauty surpasses that of the god of love, and remembrance of Him destroys lust. The attraction of women to the Lord (22.3) is the
quality of Bhagavan, who attracts all (note 5). Gorochana is a bright yellow pigment; "King of dancers" (naṭendra) is the Lord dancing in
kirtana.

## 23. Narahari — "tejaha śayana gaura guṇadhāma…" (GPT1 p. 345, no. 7; GCC)
*Dawn: "Leave Your bed, Gaura, abode of virtues: the moon has paled, the watches of the night are gone; the East, forgetting everything, has
put on red out of love; the night-lotus has closed, and the bees fly to the opened day-lotus; the chakravaki rejoices with her mate;
seeing these pastimes, Narahari laughs". Raga not stated. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC.*[^22-48]

তেজহ শয়ন গৌর গুণধাম । চাঁদ মলিন গত যামিনী যাম ॥

*tejaha śayana gaura guṇadhāma | cām̐da malina gata yāminī yāma ||*

*Word for word:* tejaha śayana — leave Your bed; gaura guṇa-dhāma — Gaura, abode of virtues; cām̐da malina — the moon has paled; gata yāminī yāma — the watches of the night are gone

**23.1.** Leave Your bed, Gaura, abode of virtues! The moon has paled, the watches of the night are gone.

পুরুব দিশা সখি সব ভুলি গেল । অনুরাগহি রক্তাম্বরি ভেল ॥

*puruba diśā sakhi saba bhuli gela | anurāgahi raktāmbari bhela ||*

*Word for word:* puruba diśā — the East; sakhi — the [night's] companion; saba bhuli gela — has forgotten everything; anurāgahi — out of love (also "out of redness"); raktāmbari bhela — has put on red

**23.2.** The East — the [night's] companion — has forgotten everything and out of love has put on red.

মুদিত কুমুদ তহি মধুপ-নিবাস । বিকশিত কমল চলত তছু পাশ ॥

*mudita kumuda tahi madhupa-nibāsa | bikaśita kamala calata tachu pāśa ||*

*Word for word:* mudita kumuda — the night-lotus has closed; tahi madhupa-nibāsa — in which the bees dwelt; bikaśita kamala — the opened day-lotus; calata tachu pāśa — they go to it

**23.3.** The night-lotus where the bees lived has closed — and they fly to the opened day-lotus.

চক্রবাকী উলসিত পতি-সঙ্গ । নরহরি হেরি হসত বহু রঙ্গ ॥

*cakrabākī ulasita pati-saṅga | narahari heri hasata bahu raṅga ||*

*Word for word:* cakrabākī — the chakravaki; ulasita — rejoices; pati-saṅga — with her mate; narahari heri — Narahari, seeing; hasata — laughs; bahu raṅga — so much merriment

**23.4.** The chakravaki rejoices, united with her mate; Narahari, seeing so much merriment, laughs.[^22-49]

[^22-48]: GPT1 — p. 345, no. 7 ("yathārāga"; scan, PDF p. 604); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 7. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-292). GCC — kirana 2, pada 17
("punaryathārāga"). Variants: 23.1 GPT1 "gata yāminī yāma" (the last word is distorted in the GCC); 23.2 GCC "anurāga hi". Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the
Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^22-49]: Images of dawn in Indian poetry: the night-lotus (kumuda) closes, the day-lotus (kamala) opens; the chakravaka birds, separated for
the night according to legend, are united in the morning. "The East, which out of love has put on red" is the dawn; "anuraga" means both
"love" and "redness".

## 24. Narahari — "niśigata śaśī darapa dūre…" (GPT1 p. 345, no. 8; GCC)
*"The night is over — the moon's pride is far away, the chakora is in great sorrow; the stars, ashamed at their husband's humiliation,
have hidden in the forest of the sky; the people of Nadia are awake — so leave Your bed, Gora; if You do not believe me, ask Narahari".
Raga not stated. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC.*[^22-50]

নিশিগত শশী দরপ দূরে । অতিশয় দুঃখে চকোর ফিরে ॥

*niśigata śaśī darapa dūre | atiśaya duḥkhe cakora phire ||*

*Word for word:* niśi-gata — the night is gone; śaśī darapa dūre — the moon's pride is far away; atiśaya duḥkhe — in great sorrow; cakora phire — the chakora flutters about

**24.1.** The night is over — the moon's pride is far away; in great sorrow the chakora flutters about.

পতি বিড়ম্বিত লজ্জিত মনে । লুকাইল তারা গগন-বনে ॥

*pati biṛambita lajjita mane | lukāila tārā gagana-bane ||*

*Word for word:* pati biṛambita — [seeing] their husband humiliated; lajjita mane — ashamed at heart; lukāila tārā — the stars hid; gagana-bane — in the forest of the sky

**24.2.** Ashamed at their husband's humiliation, the stars have hidden in the forest of the sky.

নদীয়ার লোক জাগিল ত্বরা । তেঞি বলি শেজ তেজহ গোরা ॥

*nadīyāra loka jāgila tvarā | teñi bali śeja tejaha gorā ||*

*Word for word:* nadīyāra loka jāgila tvarā — the people of Nadia are already awake; teñi bali — so I say; śeja tejaha gorā — leave Your bed, Gora

**24.3.** The people of Nadia are already awake — so, I say, leave Your bed, Gora.

মোরে না প্রত্যয় করহ যদি । তবে পুছহ নরহরির প্রতি ॥

*more nā pratyaya karaha yadi | tabe puchaha naraharira prati ||*

*Word for word:* more nā pratyaya karaha yadi — if You do not believe me; tabe puchaha naraharira prati — then ask Narahari

**24.4.** If You do not believe me — then ask Narahari.[^22-51]

[^22-50]: GPT1 — p. 345, no. 8 ("yathārāga"; scan, PDF p. 604); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 8 (catalogue: NG-175). GCC — kirana 2, pada 18. Variants: 24.2 GPT1 "pati
biṛambita", GCC "gati-biṛambana" ("seeing the [moon's] humiliation"). Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^22-51]: The moon is the "husband" of the stars (nakshatras) in Indian legend. "Ask Narahari" — in the GCC these songs are sung by a parrot
(note 35), who appeals to Narahari as a witness; in the GPT the line reads as the poet's signature.

## 25. Narahari — "jāga jāga ohe jībana gorā…" (GPT1 p. 346, no. 9; GCC)
*"Awake, Gora, my life, stealer of hearts and eyes! You are still asleep at dawn, while the neighbours are awake and chuckling; the people
of Nadia praise You and run to Your house — are You not ashamed? Tell me, what do You do at night? The peacocks, the bees, the chakoras
pine without You; get up, come out into the courtyard — otherwise Narahari's fault will not be washed away". Raga not stated.
**Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC.*[^22-52]

জাগ জাগ ওহে জীবন গোরা, জগজন-মন-নয়ন-চোরা, না জানিয়ে কিসে হইয়া ভোরা, ঘুমাঞা রয়েছ বিয়ান বেলে ।
আঁখি খুলি দেখ পোহাইল নিশি, জাগিল এ সব পড়স-বাসী, তেজি দুখ সুখ-সায়রে ভাসি, হাসি করে তারা কতেক ছলে ॥

*jāga jāga ohe jībana gorā, jagajana-mana-nayana-corā, nā jāniye kise haiyā bhorā, ghumāñā rayecha biyāna bele |*
*ām̐khi khuli dekha pohāila niśi, jāgila e saba paṛasa-bāsī, teji dukha sukha-sāyare bhāsi, hāsi kare tārā kateka chale ||*

*Word for word:* jāga jāga ohe jībana gorā — awake, awake, O Gora, my life; jagajana-mana-nayana-corā — stealer of the hearts and eyes of the world's people; nā jāniye kise haiyā bhorā — I do not know in what You are lost; ghumāñā rayecha biyāna bele — You keep sleeping at dawn; ām̐khi khuli dekha — open Your eyes and look; pohāila niśi — the night is over; jāgila e saba paṛasa-bāsī — all these neighbours have woken; teji dukha — casting off sorrow; sukha-sāyare bhāsi — floating in an ocean of joy; hāsi kare tārā kateka chale — they chuckle in many ways

**25.1.** Awake, awake, O Gora, my life, stealer of the hearts and eyes of the people of the world!
I do not know in what You are lost, that You are still asleep at dawn;
open Your eyes, look: the night is over, all these neighbours are awake;
casting off sorrow, floating in an ocean of joy, they chuckle in every way.

আর বলি এই নদীয়াপুরে, কত রূপে সভে প্রশংসা করে, ধাইয়া আইসে তারা তোমার ঘরে, ইথে কিছু লাজ না বাস মনে ।
এ কি বিপরীত অলস ধর, প্রভাত হইলে উঠিতে নার, বল দেখি রাতে কি কাজ কর, সুঘর হইয়া এমন কেনে ॥

*āra bali ei nadīyāpure, kata rūpe sabhe praśaṃsā kare, dhāiyā āise tārā tomāra ghare, ithe kichu lāja nā bāsa mane |*
*e ki biparīta alasa dhara, prabhāta haile uṭhite nāra, bala dekhi rāte ki kāja kara, sughara haiyā emana kene ||*

*Word for word:* āra bali — and I say more; ei nadīyā-pure — in this town of Nadia; kata rūpe sabhe praśaṃsā kare — all praise [You] in many ways; dhāiyā āise tārā tomāra ghare — they run to Your house; ithe kichu lāja nā bāsa mane — do You feel no shame at this; e ki biparīta alasa dhara — what strange languor You keep; prabhāta haile uṭhite nāra — at dawn You cannot rise; bala dekhi — tell me; rāte ki kāja kara — what do You do at night; sughara haiyā emana kene — being so clever, why like this

**25.2.** And I say more: in this town of Nadia all praise [You] in various ways
and run to Your house — are You not ashamed at all?
What strange languor You keep: dawn has come, and You cannot get up!
Tell me, what do You do at night? You are so clever — why then like this?[^22-53]

ময়ূর ময়ূরী পৃথক্ আছে, কেহ না আইসে কাহার কাছে, বিরস হইয়া রৈয়াছে গাছে, তুমি না দেখিলে না নাচে তাহারা ।
ভ্রমরা ভ্রমরী রুচির কুঞ্জে, ভুলি না বৈসয়ে কুসুম-পুঞ্জে, কারে শুনাইব বলি না গুঞ্জে, ফিরয়ে বিপিনে ব্যাকুল-পারা ॥

*mayūra mayūrī pṛthak āche, keha nā āise kāhāra kāche, birasa haiyā raiyāche gāche, tumi nā dekhile nā nāce tāhārā |*
*bhramarā bhramarī rucira kuñje, bhuli nā baisaye kusuma-puñje, kāre śunāiba bali nā guñje, phiraye bipine byākula-pārā ||*

*Word for word:* mayūra mayūrī pṛthak āche — the peacock and the peahen are apart; keha nā āise kāhāra kāche — neither comes near the other; birasa haiyā raiyāche gāche — dejected they stay in the trees; tumi nā dekhile nā nāce tāhārā — not seeing You they do not dance; bhramarā bhramarī rucira kuñje — the bee and his mate in the lovely kunja; bhuli nā baisaye kusuma-puñje — forgetting, they do not alight on the clusters of flowers; kāre śunāiba bali nā guñje — saying "for whom shall we sing?" they do not hum; phiraye bipine byākula-pārā — they roam the forest as if distraught

**25.3.** The peacock and the peahen are apart: neither comes near the other;
dejected, they sit in the trees — not seeing You, they do not dance.
The bee and his mate in the lovely kunja, forgetting all, do not alight on the clusters of flowers;
"For whom should we hum?" — saying so, they do not hum and roam the forest as if distraught.

চকোর ও মুখশশীর ছাঁদে, রত হৈয়া ছিল গগন-চাঁদে, সে হৈল ম্লান এ পড়িয়া ধান্দে, কান্দে অতি দুখে বলে কি হবে ।
তারে সুখী কর সুখের রাশি, উঠি আঙ্গিনাতে দাঁড়াহ আসি, নহিলে বিষম মনেতে বাসি, নরহরি-দোষ ধুলে না যাবে ॥

*cakora o mukhaśaśīra chām̐de, rata haiyā chila gagana-cām̐de, se haila mlāna e paṛiyā dhānde, kānde ati dukhe bale ki habe |*
*tāre sukhī kara sukhera rāśi, uṭhi āṅgināte dām̐ṛāha āsi, nahile biṣama manete bāsi, narahari-doṣa dhule nā yābe ||*

*Word for word:* cakora — the chakora; o mukha-śaśīra chām̐de — in the likeness of that moon-face; rata haiyā chila gagana-cām̐de — had been devoted to the moon in the sky; se haila mlāna — it has paled; e paṛiyā dhānde — he, falling into confusion; kānde ati dukhe — weeps in great sorrow; bale ki habe — saying "what will become [of me]?"; tāre sukhī kara — make him happy; sukhera rāśi — O treasure of joy; uṭhi āṅgināte dām̐ṛāha āsi — rise, come and stand in the courtyard; nahile biṣama manete bāsi — otherwise I feel it will be grievous; narahari-doṣa dhule nā yābe — Narahari's fault will not be washed away

**25.4.** The chakora, seeing in it the likeness of Your moon-face, was devoted to the moon in the sky;
it has paled — and he, bewildered, weeps in great sorrow: "What will become of me?"
Make him happy, O treasure of joy: get up, come out and stand in the courtyard,
or else, I feel, there will be trouble — then Narahari's fault will not be washed away.

[^22-52]: GPT1 — p. 346, no. 9 ("yathārāga"; scan, PDF p. 605); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 9. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-293; by the opening "jāga jāga
ohe" the checking script matched it with NG-174). GCC — kirana 2, pada 19. Variants: 25.1 GPT1 "paṛabāsī", GCC "paṛasa-bāsī" ("neighbours") — following the
GCC; others minor. Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^22-53]: "What do You do at night?" is the joking reproach of one who loves; the Lord's nights pass in kirtana and in absorption in the
pastimes of Vraja (17.3; note 36). The peacocks, bees and chakora are the nature of Navadvipa, which, like the nature of Vraja, lives by
love for the Lord.

## 26. Narahari — "āju rajanīśeṣa samaya sukha-samāja sāje…" (GPT1 pp. 346–347, no. 10; GCC)
*Navadvipa before dawn: at the end of the night a feast of joy gathers — melodies rare even for the kinnaras, the songs of parrots, the fifth
note of the cuckoos; in the blossoming kunjas the bees hum as if instruments were playing; the peacocks dance and the celestial dancers are
ashamed; swans and cranes call, doves coo; the breeze stirs the leaves, dew on the grass is like tears of joy: incomparable is the town of
Nadia on earth. Raga bhairava. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC; Vrajabuli.*[^22-54]

আজু রজনীশেষ সময় সুখ-সমাঝ সাজে ।
কিন্নরকুল দুলহ তান, কীরনিকর করত গান,
কোকিলকুল কলিত ললিত পঞ্চম সুর রাজে ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*āju rajanīśeṣa samaya sukha-samājha sāje |*
*kinnarakula dulaha tāna, kīranikara karata gāna,*
*kokilakula kalita lalita pañcama sura rāje || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* āju rajanī-śeṣa samaya — today, at the end of the night; sukha-samājha sāje — a feast of joy gathers; kinnara-kula dulaha tāna — melodies rare even for the kinnaras; kīra-nikara karata gāna — flocks of parrots sing songs; kokila-kula kalita lalita — the lovely sweet [song] of the cuckoos; pañcama sura rāje — the fifth note resounds

**26.1.** Today, at the end of the night, a feast of joy gathers:
melodies rare even for the race of kinnaras — flocks of parrots sing songs,
the lovely, sweet fifth note of the cuckoos resounds.

বিকশিত নব কুসুম-কুঞ্জ, তহি মধুকর-পুঞ্জ-পুঞ্জ,
গুঞ্জত অতি মঞ্জুল জনু মধুর যন্ত্র বাজে ।
ষড়জ যুগ গমক সুঢঙ্গ উঘটত ধিধি কিটি ধিলঙ্গ,
নৃত্যতি শিখী নিরখত সুর-নর্ত্তকীগণ লাজে ॥

*bikaśita naba kusuma-kuñja, tahi madhukara-puñja-puñja,*
*guñjata ati mañjula janu madhura yantra bāje |*
*ṣaṛaja yuga gamaka suḍhaṅga ughaṭata dhidhi kiṭi dhilaṅga,*
*nṛtyati śikhī nirakhata sura-narttakīgaṇa lāje ||*

*Word for word:* bikaśita naba kusuma-kuñja — new flowering kunjas have opened; tahi madhukara-puñja-puñja — there swarms upon swarms of bees; guñjata ati mañjula — hum most charmingly; janu madhura yantra bāje — as if sweet instruments were playing; ṣaṛaja yuga gamaka suḍhaṅga — shadja and pairs of gamakas, lovely trills; ughaṭata dhidhi kiṭi dhilaṅga — "dhi-dhi kiti dhilanga"; nṛtyati śikhī — the peacocks dance; nirakhata sura-narttakī-gaṇa lāje — seeing them, the celestial dancers are ashamed

**26.2.** New flowering kunjas have opened — there swarms upon swarms of bees
hum so wondrously, as if sweet instruments were playing;
shadja and pairs of gamakas, lovely trills — "dhi-dhi kiti dhilanga";
the peacocks dance — seeing them, the celestial dancers are ashamed.

হংস করত সাধু ধ্বনি, ক্রৌঞ্চ ধৈর্য্য তেজত শুনি,
অঙ্কুরছল পুলক বল্লীন্দ্র ভূমি নমিতায়ে ।
অদ্ভুত উহ প্রেমে মাতি, লসত শত কপোত-পাঁতি,
ঘুঘু ইতি শব্দ-ছন্দ হুঙ্কৃতি ঘন গাজে ॥

*haṃsa karata sādhu dhvani, krauñca dhairyya tejata śuni,*
*aṅkurachala pulaka ballīndra bhūmi namitāye |*
*adbhuta uha preme māti, lasata śata kapota-pām̐ti,*
*ghughu iti śabda-chanda huṅkṛti ghana gāje ||*

*Word for word:* haṃsa karata sādhu dhvani — the swans raise auspicious calls; krauñca dhairyya tejata śuni — the cranes, hearing them, lose composure; aṅkura-chala pulaka — thrill in the guise of sprouts; ballīndra bhūmi namitāye — the earth bows under the creepers (?); adbhuta uha preme māti — wondrously drunk with love; lasata śata kapota-pām̐ti — hundreds of flocks of doves shine; ghughu iti śabda-chanda — "ghu-ghu" is their cooing; huṅkṛti ghana gāje — rolling sounds resound

**26.3.** The swans raise auspicious calls; the cranes, hearing them, lose their composure;
the earth, as if thrilling in the guise of sprouts, bows beneath the creepers;
wondrously drunk with love, hundreds of flocks of doves shine;
"ghu-ghu" is their cooing, rolling sounds resound.

পবন মিশ শিঙ্গার হার, ধূনত পল্লব রীঝ অপার,
কুসুম মিশ প্রবাল মোতি রীঝ দেত ভ্রাজে ।
যবস ওস-বিন্দু পড়ত, জনু আনন্দ-অশ্রু ঝরত,
নরহরি ভণ অনুপম নদীয়াপুর মহী মাঝে ॥

*pabana miśa śiṅgāra hāra, dhūnata pallaba rījha apāra,*
*kusuma miśa prabāla moti rījha deta bhrāje |*
*yabasa osa-bindu paṛata, janu ānanda-aśru jharata,*
*narahari bhaṇa anupama nadīyāpura mahī mājhe ||*

*Word for word:* pabana miśa śiṅgāra hāra — the breeze, as if offering adornment; dhūnata pallava — stirs the leaves; rījha apāra — in boundless delight; kusuma miśa — in the guise of flowers; prabāla moti — coral and pearls; rījha deta bhrāje — radiantly bestows; yabasa osa-bindu paṛata — dew-drops fall on the grass; janu ānanda-aśru jharata — as if tears of joy were flowing; narahari bhaṇa — says Narahari; anupama nadīyāpura mahī mājhe — incomparable is the town of Nadia on earth

**26.4.** The breeze, as if offering adornment, stirs the leaves in boundless delight;
in the guise of flowers it radiantly bestows coral and pearls;
drops of dew fall on the grass — as if tears of joy were flowing;
says Narahari: incomparable is the town of Nadia on earth.[^22-55]

[^22-54]: GPT1 — pp. 346–347, no. 10 ("bhairaba"; scan, PDF pp. 605–606); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 10. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-294). GCC — kirana 2,
pada 14 ("bhairaba rāga"; in the GCC the first of the awakening songs). Variants: 26.1 GPT1 "sukha samājha sāje", GPT2 "sukha samāja sāje"; the places in 26.3
("aṅkurachala pulaka ballīndra bhūmi namitāye", GCC "… ballīnrara bhūmi nadi tām̐je") and 26.4 ("pabana miśa śiṅgāra hāra", GCC "pabana niśa siṅgāra hara") are unclear in all
witnesses — the translation is conjectural. Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. Further in GPT 5.2: no. 11 — Vasu Ghosha (chapter 12,
no. 6), no. 12 — Jagannatha Dasa, nos. 13–14 — Radhamohana, no. 15 — signed by Uddhava Dasa (the catalogue wrongly listed it under Narahari: NG-176),
no. 16 onwards — Narahari and others (chapter 23).
[^22-55]: The nature of Navadvipa at dawn serves the Lord: the birds sing, the dew is tears of joy; so too in Krishna's ashtakaliya the nature
of Vrindavana awakens together with Him. Navadvipa-dhama is no worldly place; according to Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati it is non-different
from Vrindavana. Shadja is the first note of the scale, gamakas are ornaments of the sound.

# Chapter 23. Appendix. Padas signed "Narahari" from the Gaura-pada-tarangini — VII: the ashtakaliya (the last part of the night, morning, day, evening)

*Continuation of the appendix (the introductory note on the two Naraharis, on the arguments for attribution and on the marks in the
headings is in ch. 17). Chapter 23: the continuation of GPT section 5.2 "Ashtakaliya" (GPT1 pp. 348–362, nos. 16–51): the Lord's words
in sleep at the end of the night and His awakening; the morning in Shachi's house among the companions; the pastimes of the day — the Lord
playfully takes away the companions' clothes, the meal on the bank of the Ganga; the walk through Navadvipa — old men, old women, the blind,
the lame, the dandies and the merchants gaze at Him; the companions' longing at night as they wait for the dawn; two "table-of-contents"
padas of the ashtakaliya (the eight parts of Gaura's day and night); the evening kirtanas — the Lord's dance in the guise of Rukmini and the
dance in Srivasa's courtyard. The signatures in the section were checked throughout, in the OCR and on the scan; the Gaura-charita-chintamani
(GCC, kiranas 1–4) and the 12th wave of the Bhakti-ratnakara (BR) were read continuously at the relevant places. Not translated (outside
the appendix): nos. 17, 52, 54 — signed Ghanashyama; no. 18 — Yadunatha Dasa (translated in chapter 13, no. 16); nos. 24, 25, 30, 32, 53 — Vasu
Ghosha (no. 24 — chapter 12, no. 7; no. 25 = PK 1108 — chapter 5; no. 32 — chapter 5; no. 53 = PK 656 — chapter 9; no. 30 — the festival in the
house of Narahari Thakura at Shrikhanda, signed Vasu); nos. 29, 41 — Narottama Dasa; no. 31 — Madhava (= PK 2638); nos. 33, 46 — Radhamohana; no. 44 —
without the Narahari signature (= PK vol. 4); no. 45 — Vaishnava Dasa; no. 39 — a pada in nagari-bhava (assigned to the section of nagari padas).
The padas on Gaura's night sleep (nos. 55–63, 65) go to the next chapter. The base text is GPT1 (doubtful places by the scan), collated with
GPT2, the GCC (ed. 1947) and the BR (eds. 1912 and 1960); the PK, KGC, PS and the Gita-chandrodaya were checked. On the ashtakaliya as eternal
lila and on the Lord's sleep see note 36 of chapter 22; on the motif of the women of Nadia, note 7. The notes of the GPT editors are not
reproduced.*

## 1. Narahari — "alasa abaśa pahum̐ rasika-śiromaṇi…" (GPT1 pp. 348–349, section 5.2, no. 16; GCC)
*The last part of the night: the Lord, in the languor of half-sleep, speaks as in a dream words full of rasa: without the sight of
Radharamana His life is burning; calling by name Gauridasa, Haridasa, Dhananjaya and dozens of companions, He asks them to sing of the deeds
of the people of Vraja to quench the burning of His heart; in humility He says that enemies have subdued Him and He has taken a body in
vain, and prays to be, birth after birth, a servant of the feet of the Lord of the gopis; having said this, He grows still again in sleep.
Raga not stated. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC; Vrajabuli.*[^23-1]

রাধারমণ-দরশ-রস-বিরহিত জর জর জীউ জীউ জরি যাত ॥

**1.1.** Languid and overcome, my Lord, the crown of the relishers of rasa, speaks as in a dream words full of rasa:
"Bereft of the rasa of seeing Radharamana, My life is wasting — My life is burning away.[^23-2]

নরহরি ধন্দ ন বরণে শকত কছু সুরগণ-দুলহ সুচরিত অনুপ ॥

[^23-1]: GPT1 — pp. 348–349, section 5.2 "Ashtakaliya", no. 16 ("yathārāga"; scan, PDF pp. 607–608); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 16 (p. ≈224). **The catalogue did
not know it** (new row NG-295). GCC — kirana 2 ("the pastimes on the bed" in the last part of the night), pada 25: after the awakening songs sung by
the parrot (padas 14–23; chapter 22, nos. 17–26, note 35), the GCC says that Gaura, absorbed in rasa, heard a little of them (pada 24) — and the Lord
speaks these words in His sleep. Variants: 1.1 GCC "rasamaya bāta" ("words full of rasa"; GPT "rasa rasa bāta"); 1.6 GCC "maramaka bāta", "hom̐yalu"; 1.7 GCC "jaga" for
"jani". The name "Shrinidhi" stands twice in the list in all witnesses. Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. On the ashtakaliya and
the Lord's sleep see note 36 of chapter 22.
[^23-2]: Radharamana, "the beloved of Radha", is Krishna: the Lord, Krishna Himself appearing in the mood of Radha, longs for Krishna as Radha longs
for Him. The list names the Lord's companions in Navadvipa, mostly known from the biographies: Gauridasa Pandita (in the GCC "gauri"), Haridasa
Thakura, Dhananjaya, Sanjaya, Vijaya Dasa, Mukunda Datta, Murari Gupta, Shridhara, Vakreshvara Pandita, Satyaraja Khan, Garuda Pandita, Nandana
Acharya, Chandrashekhara Acharya, Shuklambara Brahmachari, Nakula Brahmachari, Vanamali and others.
[^23-3]: The words of 1.6–1.7 are the Lord's humility (dainya) in the mood of a devotee: He, the Supreme Lord, is subject neither to maya nor to the
"enemies" (lust, anger and the rest), but, relishing the mood of a bhakta, speaks of Himself as a fallen soul — cf. His words "there is not a
trace of love for Krishna in Me" (CC Madhya 2.42), the prayer "birth after birth, causeless devotion to You" (Shikshashtaka, CC Antya 20.29) and
the verse "a servant of the servant of the servant of the lotus feet of the Lord of the gopis" (CC Madhya 13.80). The reading "prema bharāti" (GCC
"premabharāti") is unclear; understood as "prema-bhrānti", "the bewilderment of prema".

## 2. Narahari — "śuti rahum̐ sundara gaurakiśora…" (GPT1 pp. 349–350, no. 19; GCC)
*Dawn: the beautiful young Gaura is still asleep; the companions read prose and verse, sing songs about Him to instruments, compose verses,
loudly recite the names, weep in humility; the cows low, calling their calves — and the Lord, hearing them, wakes, stretches, yawns, leaves
the chamber and asks for the hobbling rope, calling Gauridasa and the others by their former names. Raga not stated. **Attribution: probably
Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC; Vrajabuli.*[^23-4]

শুতি রহুঁ সুন্দর গৌরকিশোর ।
দিনকর পূরুব দিশাগত গতি পর জাগত জন যামিনী ভেল ভোর ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*śuti rahum̐ sundara gaurakiśora |*
*dinakara pūruba diśāgata gati para jāgata jana yāminī bhela bhora || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* śuti rahum̐ — still lies; sundara gaura-kiśora — the beautiful young Gaura; dinakara — the sun; pūruba diśāgata gati para — on its way toward the east; jāgata jana — people wake; yāminī bhela bhora — the night is over

**2.1.** The beautiful young Gaura still lies [asleep].
The sun is already on its way to the east, people are waking — the night is over.

কোই যন্ত্রকুল মিলিত সুগাওত পহুঁক প্রীতি-চরিতময় গীত ॥

**2.2.** Someone reads the sweetest prose and verse, wholly absorbed in it — a wondrous thing!
Someone, to the sound of many instruments, beautifully sings songs of the Lord's loving deeds.

কোই রুচির রচনা করু নিয়মিত উচরত নাম উচ্চ করি কোয় ।
কোই দৈন্যহত মাতি ভক্তিরসে শরদ ঘটা পটতর নাহি হোয় ॥

*koi rucira racanā karu niyamita ucarata nāma ucca kari koya |*
*koi dainyahata māti bhaktirase śarada ghaṭā paṭatara nāhi hoya ||*

*Word for word:* koi — someone; rucira racanā karu — composes lovely verses; niyamita — by vow; ucarata nāma ucca kari — loudly recites the names; dainya-hata — struck down by humility; māti bhakti-rase — drunk with the rasa of bhakti; śarada ghaṭā — an autumn downpour (?); paṭantara nāhi hoya — does not compare

তাকর শবদ শুনত অতি তুরিতহি শেজ উপরি পহুঁ বৈঠল জাগি ॥

মন্দির তেজি চলত চিত চঞ্চল মাগত ঘন ঘন ছাঁদন-ডোর ॥

*puna kara moṛi cāru karayuge yuga locana jhām̐pi jimbhāyata thora |*

*Word for word:* puna — then; kara moṛi — stretching; cāru karayuge — with His lovely palms; yuga locana jhām̐pi — covering both eyes; jimbhāyata thora — yawned a little; mandira teji — leaving the chamber; calata — goes; cita cañcala — with an eager heart; māgata ghana ghana — asks again and again; chām̐dana-ḍora — the hobbling rope

**2.5.** Then He stretched, covered both eyes with His lovely palms, yawned a little,
left the chamber and goes with an eager heart, asking again and again for the hobbling rope.[^23-5]

নিরখি গৌরীদাসাদিক জনে জনে পূরুব নাম লই বদত উলাস ।
নরহরি ভণ সুচরিত্র চিত্র ইহ ঘুম ঘোর কি এ প্রেমবিলাস ॥

*nirakhi gaurīdāsādika jane jane pūruba nāma lai badata ulāsa |*

**2.6.** Seeing Gauridasa and the others, He joyfully calls each by his former name.

[^23-4]: GPT1 — pp. 349–350, no. 19 ("yathārāga"; scan, PDF pp. 608–609); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 19, pp. 224–225 (catalogue: NG-177). GCC — kirana 3 ("the
awakening"), pada 10. Variants: 2.2 GCC "kou" for "koi" (and so on); 2.3 GCC "śabda ghaṭāpaṭatara nāhi hoya" for "śarada ghaṭā paṭatara…" — the end of the line is
unclear in both readings, the translation is tentative ("not even the roar of autumn clouds compares with it" by the GCC); 2.4 GPT1 "rata sapiyā ana" —
a misprint, corrected by the GCC "batasa piyāana" ("to give milk to the calves"); 2.5 GCC "puna tanu moṛi" ("stretched His body"). Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS
or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^23-5]: The hobbling rope (chām̐dana-ḍora) is used to tie a cow's hind legs at milking. Woken by the lowing of the cows, the Lord is in the mood of a
cowherd boy of Vraja: He hurries to the cows and calls the companions by their "former names", their names in Krishna's lila (thus Gauridasa
Pandita is Subala, Krishna's friend, according to Kavi Karnapura's Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika). Here too the Lord's sleep is absorption in the
lilas of Vraja (note 36 of chapter 22).

## 3. Narahari — "pekhaha gauracandra aparūpa…" (GPT1 p. 350, no. 20; GCC)
*Morning: Gaurachandra, still drowsy, sits on a jewelled seat; the radiance of His body fills the three worlds and rises in the hearts of His
own; His smile is lovelier than a forest of lotuses, His sleepy eyes are reddish; jasmine flowers fall from His loosened hair like stars to
the earth. Raga not stated. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC; Vrajabuli.*[^23-6]

পেখহ গৌরচন্দ্র অপরূপ ।
ঝলমল ললিত সুরতন পীঠ পরি বিলসত নিরুপম মনমথ-ভূপ ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*pekhaha gauracandra aparūpa |*
*jhalamala lalita suratana pīṭha pari bilasata nirupama manamatha-bhūpa || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* pekhaha — behold; gauracandra aparūpa — the wondrous Gaurachandra; jhalamala — gleaming; lalita — lovely; suratana pīṭha pari — on a seat of jewels; bilasata — sits resplendent; nirupama — incomparable; manamatha-bhūpa — king Kamadeva

**3.1.** Behold the wondrous Gaurachandra!
On a gleaming lovely seat of jewels sits the incomparable king Kamadeva.

সুরগিরি-শিখর-দরপ-হর বরতনু তেজ প্রবল ত্রিভুবন ভরি পূর ।
নিজজন-হৃদয় উদয় করু অবিরত রবি শশী কোটি গরব করু চূর ॥

*suragiri-śikhara-darapa-hara baratanu teja prabala tribhubana bhari pūra |*
*nijajana-hṛdaya udaya karu abirata rabi śaśī koṭi garaba karu cūra ||*

*Word for word:* suragiri-śikhara — of the peaks of the mountain of the gods; darapa-hara — crushing the pride; baratanu — beautiful body; teja prabala — mighty radiance; tribhubana bhari pūra — has filled the three worlds; nijajana-hṛdaya — in the hearts of His own; udaya karu abirata — rises ceaselessly; rabi śaśī koṭi — of millions of suns and moons; garaba karu cūra — crushes the pride

**3.2.** His beautiful body crushes the pride of the peaks of the mountain of the gods; His mighty radiance has filled the three worlds;
ceaselessly rising in the hearts of His own, He crushes the pride of millions of suns and moons.

মৃদু মৃদু হাস মিলিত মুখ মঞ্জুল বিকসিত কঞ্জ-বিপিন নহ তুল ।
ঘুম ঘোরে ঢুলু ঢুলত অরুণ দিঠি নাশত যুবতী-লাজ-ভয়-কুল ॥

*mṛdu mṛdu hāsa milita mukha mañjula bikasita kañja-bipina naha tula |*
*ghuma ghore ḍhulu ḍhulata aruṇa diṭhi nāśata yubatī-lāja-bhaya-kula ||*

*Word for word:* mṛdu mṛdu hāsa milita — with a gentle smile; mukha mañjula — the lovely face; bikasita kañja-bipina — a forest of blossoming lotuses; naha tula — is no match; ghuma ghore — in deep drowsiness; ḍhulu ḍhulata — droop; aruṇa diṭhi — reddish eyes; nāśata — destroy; yubatī-lāja-bhaya-kula — the shame, fear and family honour of young women

**3.3.** His lovely face with its gentle smile — a forest of blossoming lotuses is no match for it;
His reddish eyes droop in deep drowsiness — and destroy the shame, fear and family honour of young women.[^23-7]

শিথিল কেশ তহিঁ গিরত কুন্দ জনু গগন তেজি উড়ু পড়ু খিতি মাহি ।
কো কবি রচব ভঙ্গী অতি অদ্ভুত নরহরি নিরমঞ্ছন বহু তাহি ॥

*śithila keśa tahim̐ girata kunda janu gagana teji uṛu paṛu khiti māhi |*
*ko kabi racaba bhaṅgī ati adbhuta narahari niramañchana bahu tāhi ||*

*Word for word:* śithila keśa tahim̐ — from the loosened hair; girata kunda — jasmine flowers fall; janu — as if; gagana teji — leaving the sky; uḍu paṛu khiti māhi — stars fall to the earth; ko kabi racaba — what poet will describe; bhaṅgī ati adbhuta — the wondrous pose; narahari niramañchana bahu tāhi — Narahari again and again offers himself for it

**3.4.** From His loosened hair fall jasmine flowers — as if stars, leaving the sky, were falling to the earth.
What poet will describe this wondrous pose? Narahari again and again offers himself for it.

[^23-6]: GPT1 — p. 350, no. 20 ("yathārāga"; scan, PDF p. 609); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 20 (catalogue: NG-178). GCC — kirana 3, pada 12 (before it the GCC has
pada 11 "guṇamaṇi gauracandra dvijarāja", which is not in the GPT: Gaura comes out of the chamber and sits on the seat). Variants: 3.1 GPT1 "bilapita" (a
misprint), GCC "bilasata"; 3.3 GCC "nāśata yubati-lāja-bhaya-kula". Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. "The mountain of the gods" is
Sumeru, the golden mountain; "king Kamadeva" (manamatha-bhūpa) — an image of beauty surpassing that of the god of love.
[^23-7]: The line repeats a common formula of love poetry about the all-attractive beauty of Krishna. We translate faithfully to the author; but
the Gaudiya tradition (Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja, Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati) does not accept the worship of Gaura in the mood of
"Gaura-nagari": Gaura is Krishna Himself in the mood and lustre of Radha; He came to taste Her love, not to enjoy as a nagara. The Lord's
attractiveness for the people of Navadvipa is the quality of Bhagavan, who attracts all; it is not worldly passion. The same holds for the other
places of the chapter speaking of the young women of Nadia (no. 22, v. 22.2). GPT pada no. 39 ("nadīyāra śaśī raṅge rājapathe": a young woman "has drowned in
the rasa of Narahari's Lord and given up shame and family"; = BR 12, vv. 2380–2383) is in nagari-bhava and is set aside for the section of nagari
padas. "Offers himself for it" (niramañchana) — the rite of "warding off" (nirmanchhana): the lover waves something around the beloved and gives it
(or himself) away for him, averting misfortune.

## 4. Narahari — "śrīśacībhabane adhika sukha āja…" (GPT1 p. 350, no. 21; GCC)
*Morning in Shachi's house: Gaura sits on a seat, around Him circle upon circle of companions, like gods around Sumeru; someone, leaning on
another's hand, stands still as a painting; someone's cloth is slipping; someone, startled, has run from his bed with sleepy eyes — all
drink, like bees, the honey of His face. Raga lalita. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC; Vrajabuli.*[^23-8]

শ্রীশচীভবনে অধিক সুখ আজ ।
অনুপম পাদপীঠ পরি বিলসত সুন্দর গৌরচন্দ্র দ্বিজরাজ ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*śrīśacībhabane adhika sukha āja |*
*anupama pādapīṭha pari bilasata sundara gauracandra dvijarāja || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* śrī-śacī-bhabane — in the house of Sri Shachi; adhika sukha āja — great joy today; anupama pādapīṭha pari — on an incomparable seat; bilasata — sits resplendent; sundara gauracandra — the beautiful Gaurachandra; dvijarāja — king of the twice-born

**4.1.** Great joy today in the house of Sri Shachi:
on an incomparable seat sits the beautiful Gaurachandra, king of the twice-born.

পহুঁ চহুদিশ প্রিয়-পরিকর-মণ্ডল-মণ্ডলী অতি অপরূপ রুচিকারী ।
জনু সুমেরু গিরি বেষ্টিত সুরগণ শোভা শেষ বরণে নাহি পারি ॥

*pahum̐ cahudiśa priya-parikara-maṇḍala-maṇḍalī ati aparūpa rucikārī |*
*janu sumeru giri beṣṭita suragaṇa śobhā śeṣa baraṇe nāhi pāri ||*

*Word for word:* pahum̐ cahudiśa — around the Lord; priya-parikara-maṇḍala-maṇḍalī — circle upon circle of dear companions; ati aparūpa rucikārī — wondrously beautiful; janu — as if; sumeru giri beṣṭita suragaṇa — the gods surrounding Mount Sumeru; śobhā — the beauty; śeṣa baraṇe nāhi pāri — even Shesha cannot describe

**4.2.** Around the Lord — circle upon circle of dear companions, wondrously beautiful,
like the gods surrounding Mount Sumeru: even Shesha cannot describe this beauty.

কাহুক করে কর করি অবলম্বন চিত্রক পুতরি সদৃশ রহু কোয় ।
কাহুক বসন খসত নাহি সম্বরু কৈছন ভাবন অনুভব হোয় ॥

*kāhuka kare kara kari abalambana citraka putari sadṛśa rahu koya |*
*kāhuka basana khasata nāhi sambaru kaichana bhābana anubhaba hoya ||*

*Word for word:* kāhuka kare kara kari abalambana — leaning his hand on another's hand; citraka putari sadṛśa — like a painted doll; rahu koya — someone stands still; kāhuka basana khasata — someone's cloth slips; nāhi sambaru — he does not set it right; kaichana bhābana anubhaba hoya — what feeling he experiences

**4.3.** Someone, leaning his hand on another's hand, stands still like a painted doll;
someone's cloth is slipping, and he does not set it right — what feeling is he experiencing?

কোই সচকিত শেজ তেজি উপনীত ঘুম ঘোরে ঢুলু ঢুলুই নয়ান ।
নরহরি ভণ উহ মুখ-পঙ্কজ-মধুপানে মত্ত মধুকর অনুমান ॥

*koi sacakita śeja teji upanīta ghuma ghore ḍhulu ḍhului nayāna |*
*narahari bhaṇa uha mukha-paṅkaja-madhupāne matta madhukara anumāna ||*

*Word for word:* koi sacakita — someone, startled; śeja teji upanīta — has left his bed and come; ghuma ghore — in deep drowsiness; ḍhulu ḍhului nayāna — his eyes droop; narahari bhaṇa — Narahari says; uha — they; mukha-paṅkaja-madhu-pāne matta — drunk on the honey of the lotus-face; madhukara anumāna — like bees

**4.4.** Someone, startled, has left his bed and come — his eyes still drooping in deep drowsiness.
Narahari says: they are like bees drunk on the honey of this lotus-face.

[^23-8]: GPT1 — p. 350, no. 21 ("lalita"; scan, PDF p. 609); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 21. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-296). GCC — kirana 4
("the Lord surrounded by devotees"), pada 2 (pada 1 of kirana 4 is a list of companions signed Ghanashyama). Variants: 4.3 GCC "kaichana bhāba na
anubhaba hoya" ("what feeling — it cannot be grasped"); 4.4 GCC "mukha paṅkaja-madhupāne". Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. Shesha
(Ananta) is the thousand-mouthed serpent who eternally sings the Lord's glories.

## 5. Narahari — "āju ānanda parabhāta śacī-aṅganahi…" (GPT1 p. 350, no. 22; GCC)
*A joyful morning in Shachi's courtyard: the companions come and go, sing, dance, whisper and laugh, embrace and bow to one another, ask
whether the night passed well, call one another blessed; someone recites verses, someone with a sigh takes a blade of grass between his
teeth; the companions are countless — like a surging ocean of joy. Raga not stated. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in
the GCC; Vrajabuli.*[^23-9]

আজু আনন্দ পরভাত শচী-অঙ্গনহি ভঙ্গ নহু নেহ নবরঙ্গ বহু ভাঁতি রে ।
কোই আওত যাত কোই গাওত ললিত রাগ অদ্ভুত নিরত ফিরত রস মাতি রে ॥

*āju ānanda parabhāta śacī-aṅganahi bhaṅga nahu neha nabaraṅga bahu bhām̐ti re |*
*koi āota yāta koi gāota lalita rāga adbhuta nirata phirata rasa māti re ||*

*Word for word:* āju — today; ānanda parabhāta — a joyful morning; śacī-aṅganahi — in Shachi's courtyard; bhaṅga nahu neha — unending love; nabaraṅga bahu bhām̐ti — new delights of every kind; koi āota yāta — someone comes and goes; koi gāota lalita rāga — someone sings a lovely raga; adbhuta nirata — dances wondrously; phirata rasa māti — wanders drunk with rasa

**5.1.** Today a joyful morning in Shachi's courtyard — unending love, new delights of every kind!
Someone comes and goes, someone sings a lovely raga, dances wondrously, wanders drunk with rasa.

কোই কাহুক কর্ণ লাগি বহু বচন মৃদু পড়ত হসি হসি তনু ন যাত ধরণে ।
কোই কাহুক পকারি করত আলিঙ্গনহি কোই পরণাম করু কাহু চরণে ॥

*koi kāhuka karṇa lāgi bahu bacana mṛdu paṛata hasi hasi tanu na yāta dharaṇe |*
*koi kāhuka pakāri karata āliṅganahi koi paraṇāma karu kāhu caraṇe ||*

*Word for word:* koi kāhuka karṇa lāgi — someone, at another's ear; bahu bacana mṛdu — softly many words; paṛata hasi hasi — laughing, collapses; tanu na yāta dharaṇe — unable to stand; koi kāhuka pakāri — someone, calling another; karata āliṅgana-hi — embraces; koi paraṇāma karu kāhu caraṇe — someone bows at someone's feet

**5.2.** Someone, putting his lips to another's ear, softly says many words — and, laughing, collapses, unable to stand;
someone calls another and embraces him; someone bows down at someone's feet.

কোই কাহুক পুছত রজনী-মঙ্গল কোই কহত অব মঙ্গল সু পহুঁক দরশে ।
কোই কাহুক কহত ধন্য তুহুঁ ধন্য তুহুঁ দুখ মিটব তব অঙ্গ-পবন-পরশে ॥

*koi kāhuka puchata rajanī-maṅgala koi kahata aba maṅgala su pahum̐ka daraśe |*
*koi kāhuka kahata dhanya tuhum̐ dhanya tuhum̐ dukha miṭaba taba aṅga-pabana-paraśe ||*

*Word for word:* koi kāhuka puchata — someone asks another; rajanī-maṅgala — whether the night passed well; koi kahata — someone says; aba maṅgala — now all is well; su pahum̐ka daraśe — from seeing the Lord; dhanya tuhum̐ — blessed are you; dukha miṭaba — sorrow will go; taba aṅga-pabana-paraśe — at the touch of the breeze from your body

**5.3.** Someone asks another whether the night passed well; someone says: "Now all is well — from seeing the Lord";
someone says to another: "Blessed are you, blessed! Sorrow will go at the mere touch of the breeze from your body."

কোই নর পদ্য-গদ্যাদি উচ্চার করু কোই ফুৎকারি তৃণ ধরত রদনে ।
পরিকর অসংখ্য অতি জনু সুখ উথলল সিন্ধু নরহরি কি রচব ইহ এক বদনে ॥

*koi nara padya-gadyādi uccāra karu koi phutkāri tṛṇa dharata radane |*
*parikara asaṃkhya ati janu sukha uthalala sindhu narahari ki racaba iha eka badane ||*

*Word for word:* koi nara — someone; padya-gadyādi uccāra karu — recites verses and prose; koi phutkāri — someone with a sigh; tṛṇa dharata radane — takes a blade of grass between his teeth; parikara asaṃkhya ati — the companions are countless; janu sukha uthalala sindhu — as if an ocean of joy had surged; narahari ki racaba — how can Narahari describe; iha eka badane — this with one mouth

**5.4.** Someone recites verses and prose; someone with a sigh takes a blade of grass between his teeth;
the companions are countless — as if an ocean of joy had surged: how can Narahari describe it with one mouth?[^23-10]

[^23-9]: GPT1 — p. 350, no. 22 ("yathārāga"; scan, PDF p. 609); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 22 (catalogue: NG-179). GCC — kirana 4, pada 3 (the search through
the witnesses missed it because of the garbled OCR; found by reading the GCC continuously). Variants: 5.1 GCC "bhaṅga hu neha" (OCR unclear); 5.2 GCC
"kahu bacana"; 5.4 GCC "kutakāri" (OCR). Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^23-10]: A blade of grass between the teeth is a sign of humility: so one begs for mercy in Bengal. The Lord's companions honour one another
("blessed are you!") — for each of them is His eternal intimate.

## 6. Narahari — "ki kahaba ājuka aparūpa raṅga…" (GPT1 p. 351, no. 23; GCC)
*The courtyard of Shachi's house: Gaurahari and the companions are like a host of moons in a clear starless sky, which will dispel the
darkness of the threefold miseries; like an arena of mighty wrestlers, who will overcome the asuras averse to the Lord's feet; like a field
of blossoming wish-fulfilling trees giving priceless fruits — no one will be left without. Raga not stated. **Attribution: probably
Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC; Vrajabuli.*[^23-11]

কি কহব আজুক অপরূপ রঙ্গ ।
পরিসর অঙ্গন মধ্য গৌরহরি প্রিয় পরিকরগণ লসত অভঙ্গ ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*ki kahaba ājuka aparūpa raṅga |*
*parisara aṅgana madhya gaurahari priya parikaragaṇa lasata abhaṅga || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* ki kahaba — what shall I say; ājuka aparūpa raṅga — of today's wondrous delight; parisara aṅgana madhya — in the midst of the spacious courtyard; gaurahari priya parikaragaṇa — Gaurahari and His dear companions; lasata — shine; abhaṅga — inseparably

**6.1.** What shall I say of today's wondrous delight!
In the midst of the spacious courtyard shine Gaurahari and His dear companions, inseparable from Him.

উড়ুগণ বিহীন বিমল কিয়ে উড়ুপতিবৃন্দ বিমল পরকাশ ।
জগত তাপত্রয় ঘোর কঠিনতম তম নিশ্চয় বুঝি করব বিনাশ ॥

*uṛugaṇa bihīna bimala kiye uṛupatibṛnda bimala parakāśa |*
*jagata tāpatraya ghora kaṭhinatama tama niścaya bujhi karaba bināśa ||*

*Word for word:* uḍugaṇa bihīna — without stars; bimala — in the clear [sky]; kiye — is it; uṛupati-bṛnda — a host of moons; bimala parakāśa — shining brightly; jagata tāpatraya — of the world's threefold miseries; ghora kaṭhinatama tama — the dreadful densest darkness; niścaya bujhi — surely; karaba bināśa — will destroy

**6.2.** Is it a host of moons shining brightly in the clear starless [sky]?
Surely they will destroy the dreadful, densest darkness of the world's threefold miseries.

ভব-ভয়-ভর-হর রঙ্গভূমি কিয়ে প্রবল মল্লকুল ললিত সমাজ ।
পহু-পদ-বিমুখ অসুর অতি দুর্জয় জয় করি বুঝি সাধব নিজকাজ ॥

*bhaba-bhaya-bhara-hara raṅgabhūmi kiye prabala mallakula lalita samāja |*
*pahu-pada-bimukha asura ati durjaya jaya kari bujhi sādhaba nijakāja ||*

*Word for word:* bhaba-bhaya-bhara-hara — removing the burden of the fear of worldly existence; raṅgabhūmi kiye — is it an arena; prabala mallakula — of mighty wrestlers; lalita samāja — a lovely assembly; pahu-pada-bimukha — averse to the Lord's feet; asura ati durjaya — invincible asuras; jaya kari — having overcome; bujhi sādhaba nija-kāja — will surely accomplish their work

**6.3.** Is it an arena that removes the burden of the fear of worldly existence — a lovely assembly of mighty wrestlers?
Having overcome the invincible asuras averse to the Lord's feet, they will surely accomplish their work.

বাধ করি রহিত বিহিত খেত কিয়ে প্রকট কলপতরু প্রফুল্লিত হোই ।
বিতরব অতুল অমূল ফল নরহরি ভণ বুঝি বঞ্চিত না রহব কোই ॥

*bādha kari rahita bihita kheta kiye prakaṭa kalapataru praphullita hoi |*
*bitaraba atula amūla phala narahari bhaṇa bujhi bañcita nā rahaba koi ||*

*Word for word:* bādha kari rahita — free of obstacles; bihita kheta — on a prepared field; kiye — is it; prakaṭa kalapataru — wish-fulfilling trees have appeared; praphullita hoi — blossoming; bitaraba atula amūla phala — will give away incomparable priceless fruits; narahari bhaṇa — Narahari says; bujhi bañcita nā rahaba koi — surely no one will be left without

**6.4.** Is it a field free of every obstacle, where wish-fulfilling trees have appeared and blossomed?
They will give away incomparable, priceless fruits; Narahari says: surely no one will be left without.

[^23-11]: GPT1 — p. 351, no. 23 ("yathārāga"; scan, PDF p. 610); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 23 (catalogue: NG-180). GCC — kirana 4, pada 4. Variants: 6.2 GCC
"uḍugaṇa-bihīna bimala ākāśa kiye…" (the GPT lacks the word "ākāśa", "sky"; supplied in brackets); 6.4 GCC "phire" for "kiye" (OCR). Not in the BR,
PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. The threefold miseries are those from one's own body and mind, from other beings and from the forces of
nature. "The asuras averse to the Lord's feet" — the godlessness of the age of Kali; the companions are warriors of sankirtana who conquer it with
the holy name; "the wish-fulfilling trees" — the companions who give everyone the fruit of prema (cf. CC Adi 9: the Lord is the gardener and the
tree of prema).

## 7. Narahari — "gorācām̐dera kibā e līlā…" (GPT1 p. 351, no. 26; BR)
*The Lord in the mood of His former lila: as in Vraja He stole the gopis' clothes, so now, glancing at His dear companions, He playfully takes
away their clothes and then, His purpose fulfilled, gives them all back. Raga shri. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the
BR; plain Bengali.*[^23-12]

গোরাচাঁদের কিবা এ লীলা ।
পূরুবে গোপিকা-চীর হরে এবে সে ভাবে বিভোল হৈলা ॥

*gorācām̐dera kibā e līlā |*
*pūrube gopikā-cīra hare ebe se bhābe bibhola hailā ||*

*Word for word:* gorācām̐dera — of Gorachand; kibā e līlā — what a lila; pūrube — once; gopikā-cīra hare — stole the gopis' clothes; ebe — now; se bhābe — in that mood; bibhola hailā — became lost

**7.1.** What a lila of Gorachand!
Once He stole the gopis' clothes — now He is lost in that mood.

চাহি প্রিয় পরিকর পানে ।
ভঙ্গী করি চীর হরে সে সভার কেবা এ মরম জানে ॥

*cāhi priya parikara pāne |*
*bhaṅgī kari cīra hare se sabhāra kebā e marama jāne ||*

*Word for word:* cāhi — glancing; priya parikara pāne — at the dear companions; bhaṅgī kari — playfully; cīra hare se sabhāra — takes away their clothes; kebā e marama jāne — who knows the secret of this

**7.2.** Glancing at His dear companions,
He playfully takes away their clothes — who knows the secret of this?[^23-13]

যেন হৈল সকল সেই ।
সুখের অবধি সাধি নিজকাজ সবারে বসন দেই ॥

*yena haila sakala sei |*
*sukhera abadhi sādhi nijakāja sabāre basana dei ||*

*Word for word:* yena haila sakala sei — as if all had become as then; sukhera abadhi — [reaching] the limit of joy; sādhi nija-kāja — fulfilling His purpose; sabāre basana dei — gives everyone their clothes

**7.3.** As if everything had become as it was then;
having reached the limit of joy and fulfilled His purpose, He gives everyone back their clothes.

দেখি দাস নরহরি ভণে ।
ভুবনের মাঝে কে না উনমত এ চারু চরিত গানে ॥

*dekhi dāsa narahari bhaṇe |*
*bhubanera mājhe ke nā unamata e cāru carita gāne ||*

*Word for word:* dekhi — seeing; dāsa narahari bhaṇe — Narahari Dasa says; bhubanera mājhe — in the world; ke nā unamata — who would not go mad; e cāru carita gāne — singing this lovely deed

**7.4.** Seeing this, Narahari Dasa says:
who in the world would not go mad singing this lovely deed?

[^23-12]: GPT1 — p. 351, no. 26 ("śrīrāga"; scan, PDF p. 610); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 26 (catalogue: NG-181). BR 12 (ed. 1912, p. 946; ed. 1960, vv. 3358–3361):
Ishana shows Srinivasa the place where "Gaurachandra manifested His former lila — He stole the clothes of the devotees" (v. 3355), and quotes Murari
Gupta's verses about it (in our translation, Murari 2.10.16–17: "at the beginning of the night" the Lord pulled the clothes off His servants, filled
with bhava, and gave them back a moment later). Variants: 7.1 GPT1 "gārācām̐dera" (a misprint), GPT1 and GPT2 "bibhola hailā", BR "bihvala hailā"; 7.3 BR "yena
haila sakali sei". Not in the PK, KGC, PS, GCC or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^23-13]: The stealing of the clothes (cīra-haraṇa) is Krishna's pastime in Vraja (Bhag. 10.22): by carrying off the clothes of the bathing gopis He
fulfilled their vow and desire and removed the last barrier between them and Himself; it is a play of pure prema, not a worldly prank. Here the
Lord repeats it with the devotees in whom the mood of the gopis has awakened (cf. Murari 2.10.15–17) — this is the "secret" of the lila the poet
has in mind.

## 8. Narahari — "suradhunītīre kata raṅge…" (GPT1 pp. 351–352, no. 27; BR)
*Midday on the bank of the Suradhuni: Srivasa and Murari have food brought; Advaita seats everyone in a circle on palasha leaves; Nitai, forgetting
Himself, feeds Gora sweets, Advaita gives Nitai a drink, Nitai puts sweets into Advaita's mouth; the companions merrily feed one another and
snatch food from one another's leaves, and drink the water of the Suradhuni; Narahari carefully gathers the remnants. Raga saranga. **Attribution:
probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^23-14]

সুরধুনীতীরে কত রঙ্গে ।
বিহরয়ে গৌর প্রিয়-পারিষদ সঙ্গে ॥

*suradhunītīre kata raṅge |*
*biharaye gaura priya-pāriṣada saṅge ||*

*Word for word:* suradhunī-tīre — on the bank of the Suradhuni (Ganga); kata raṅge — in many delights; biharaye gaura — Gaura wanders; priya-pāriṣada saṅge — with His dear companions

**8.1.** On the bank of the Suradhuni, in many delights,
Gaura wanders with His dear companions.

হইল প্রহর দুই দিবা ।
সে সময় না জানি প্রভুর মনে কিবা ॥

*haila prahara dui dibā |*
*se samaya nā jāni prabhura mane kibā ||*

*Word for word:* haila prahara dui dibā — two praharas of the day passed; se samaya — at that time; nā jāni — I do not know; prabhura mane kibā — what was in the Lord's mind

**8.2.** Two praharas of the day have passed —
who knows what was then in the Lord's mind?

শ্রীবাস মুরারি সেই বেলে ।
আনাইল বিবিধ সামগ্রী ভরি থালে ॥

*śrībāsa murāri sei bele |*
*ānāila bibidha sāmagrī bhari thāle ||*

*Word for word:* śrībāsa murāri — Srivasa and Murari; sei bele — at that hour; ānāila — had brought; bibidha sāmagrī — all kinds of food; bhari thāle — on full platters

**8.3.** At that hour Srivasa and Murari
had all kinds of food brought on platters.

উলসিত নদীয়ার শশী ।
চাহে সীতানাথ পানে লহু লহু হাসি ॥

*ulasita nadīyāra śaśī |*
*cāhe sītānātha pāne lahu lahu hāsi ||*

*Word for word:* ulasita — rejoices; nadīyāra śaśī — the Moon of Nadia; cāhe — gazes; sītānātha pāne — at the Lord of Sita; lahu lahu hāsi — with a gentle smile

**8.4.** The Moon of Nadia rejoices,
gazing with a gentle smile at the Lord of Sita.

অদ্বৈত পরমানন্দ মনে ।
বসাইলা সবে কিবা মণ্ডলিবন্ধানে ॥

*advaita paramānanda mane |*
*basāilā sabe kibā maṇḍalibandhāne ||*

*Word for word:* advaita — Advaita; paramānanda mane — with great joy in His heart; basāilā sabe — seated everyone; kibā — how lovely; maṇḍali-bandhāne — in a circle

**8.5.** Advaita, with great joy in His heart,
seated everyone — how lovely! — in a circle.

পাতিয়া পলাশ পাত তায় ।
বিবিধ সামগ্রী পরিবেশয়ে সভায় ॥

*pātiyā palāśa pāta tāya |*
*bibidha sāmagrī paribeśaye sabhāya ||*

*Word for word:* pātiyā palāśa pāta tāya — spreading palasha leaves there; bibidha sāmagrī — all kinds of dishes; paribeśaye sabhāya — serves to everyone

**8.6.** Spreading palasha leaves there,
He serves everyone all kinds of dishes.

অনুমতি পাইয়া ভোজনে ।
সভে এক দিঠে চায় গোরা-মুখপানে ॥

*anumati pāiyā bhojane |*
*sabhe eka diṭhe cāya gorā-mukhapāne ||*

*Word for word:* anumati pāiyā bhojane — given leave to eat; sabhe — all; eka diṭhe — steadily; cāya gorā-mukha-pāne — gaze at Gora's face

**8.7.** Given leave to eat,
all gaze steadily at Gora's face.

নিতাই ধরিতে নারে থেহা ।
উমড়য় হিয়ায় কে জানে কিবা লেহা ॥

*nitāi dharite nāre thehā |*
*umaṛaya hiyāya ke jāne kibā lehā ||*

*Word for word:* nitāi — Nitai; dharite nāre thehā — cannot contain Himself; umaṛaya hiyāya — surges in His heart; ke jāne — who can fathom; kibā lehā — what love

**8.8.** Nitai cannot contain Himself:
love surges in His heart — who can fathom it?

ক্ষীর সর নবনীত ছানা ।
গোরার বদনে দিয়া পাসরে আপনা ॥

*kṣīra sara nabanīta chānā |*
*gorāra badane diyā pāsare āpanā ||*

*Word for word:* kṣīra — sweet rice (thickened milk); sara — cream; nabanīta — fresh butter; chānā — curd cheese; gorāra badane diyā — putting into Gora's mouth; pāsare āpanā — forgets Himself

**8.9.** Sweet rice, cream, fresh butter, curd cheese
He puts into Gora's mouth and forgets Himself.

অদ্বৈত লইয়া নিজ করে ।
পিয়াইল ছানাপানা নিতাইচাঁদেরে ॥

*advaita laiyā nija kare |*
*piyāila chānāpānā nitāicām̐dere ||*

*Word for word:* advaita laiyā nija kare — Advaita with His own hand; piyāila — gives to drink; chānāpānā — a curd drink; nitāicām̐dere — to Nitaichand

**8.10.** Advaita with His own hand
gives Nitaichand a curd drink.

নিতাই সুন্দর মহাবলী ।
মোদকাদি অদ্বৈত-বদনে দিল তুলি ॥

*nitāi sundara mahābalī |*
*modakādi advaita-badane dila tuli ||*

*Word for word:* nitāi sundara — lovely Nitai; mahābalī — the mighty; modakādi — sweet balls and the like; advaita-badane dila tuli — puts into Advaita's mouth

**8.11.** Lovely Nitai, the mighty,
puts sweet balls into Advaita's mouth.

ও না তনু পুলকে ভরিল ।
পরিকর মাঝে কি কৌতুক উপজিল ॥

*o nā tanu pulake bharila |*
*parikara mājhe ki kautuka upajila ||*

*Word for word:* o nā tanu — their bodies (?); pulake bharila — were filled with rapture; parikara mājhe — among the companions; ki kautuka upajila — what merriment arose

**8.12.** Their bodies thrilled with rapture —
what merriment arose among the companions!

কেহ খায় কারু মুখে দিয়া ।
কেহ লেন কারু পত্র হইতে কাড়িয়া ॥

*keha khāya kāru mukhe diyā |*
*keha lena kāru patra haite kāṛiyā ||*

*Word for word:* keha khāya — someone eats; kāru mukhe diyā — putting into another's mouth; keha lena — someone takes; kāru patra haite kāṛiyā — snatching from another's leaf

**8.13.** Someone eats after first putting food into another's mouth,
someone snatches [food] from another's leaf.

মিঠাই অনেক পরকার ।
খাইতে সভার সুখ বাড়িল অপার ॥

*miṭhāi aneka parakāra |*
*khāite sabhāra sukha bāṛila apāra ||*

*Word for word:* miṭhāi aneka parakāra — sweets of many kinds; khāite — in eating; sabhāra sukha bāṛila apāra — everyone's joy grew boundless

**8.14.** There are sweets of many kinds —
eating them, everyone's joy grew boundless.

অঞ্জলি অঞ্জলি ভরি ভরি ।
পীয়ে সভে সুশীতল সুরধুনী-বারি ॥

*añjali añjali bhari bhari |*
*pīye sabhe suśītala suradhunī-bāri ||*

*Word for word:* añjali añjali bhari bhari — handful after brimming handful; pīye sabhe — all drink; suśītala suradhunī-bāri — the cool water of the Suradhuni (Ganga)

**8.15.** Handful after brimming handful
all drink the cool water of the Suradhuni.

পত্র শেষ যে কিছু রহিল ।
দাস নরহরি তা যতন করি নিল ॥

*patra śeṣa ye kichu rahila |*
*dāsa narahari tā yatana kari nila ||*

*Word for word:* patra śeṣa — the remnants on the leaves; ye kichu rahila — whatever was left; dāsa narahari — Narahari Dasa; tā yatana kari nila — carefully gathered

**8.16.** Whatever was left on the leaves
Narahari Dasa carefully gathered.[^23-15]

[^23-14]: GPT1 — pp. 351–352, no. 27 ("sāraṅga"; scan, PDF pp. 610–611); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 27 (catalogue: NG-182). BR 12 (ed. 1912, pp. 937–938; ed. 1960,
vv. 3241–3256): Ishana shows Srinivasa the bank of the Ganga where "the Lord with His companions holds a vana-bhojana" (a meal in the open, v. 3240).
Variants: 8.3 BR-1960 "prabāsa murāri" (OCR; GPT1 on the scan "śrībāsa murāri"); 8.8 BR "kibā mehā" for "kibā lehā"; 8.9 BR "kṣīra sara nabanīta chenā"; 8.10 BR
"chenā pānā". Not in the PK, KGC, PS, GCC or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. Two praharas are half the daylight (a prahara is a quarter of the day): in the
ashtakaliya this is midday, the time of Gaura's pastimes on the bank of the Ganga (below, no. 18, v. 18.4).
[^23-15]: The meal of the Lord and His companions is prasada; the remnants from the leaves of the Lord and His eternal companions are mahaprasada,
precious to a devotee: so the poet gathers them "carefully" (cf. CC Antya 16 on the glory of the remnants of the Vaishnavas' meals). Srivasa,
Murari, Advaita ("the Lord of Sita"), Nitai (Nityananda) are the Lord's closest companions in Navadvipa. The curd drink (chānā-pānā) is curd cheese
mashed with water and sugar.

## 9. Narahari — "āju gorā parikara saṅge…" (GPT1 p. 352, no. 28; BR)
*After the meal Gora wanders with His companions along the bank of the Suradhuni; standing in the shade of a tall tree, He says something sweet
and gazes at the Suradhuni, takes Gadai by the hand and gently smiles. Raga saranga. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the
BR.*[^23-16]

আজু গোরা পরিকর সঙ্গে ।
ভোজন কৌতুক সারি সুরধুনীতীরেতে ভ্রময়ে রঙ্গে ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*āju gorā parikara saṅge |*
*bhojana kautuka sāri suradhunītīrete bhramaye raṅge || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* āju — today; gorā parikara saṅge — Gora with His companions; bhojana kautuka sāri — having finished the merry meal; suradhunī-tīrete — along the bank of the Suradhuni (Ganga); bhramaye raṅge — joyfully wanders

**9.1.** Today Gora with His companions,
having finished the merry meal, joyfully wanders along the bank of the Suradhuni.

রহি অতি উচ্চ তরু-ছায় ।
কহি কি মধুর বাণী ঘন ঘন সুরধুনী পানে চায় ॥

*rahi ati ucca taru-chāya |*
*kahi ki madhura bāṇī ghana ghana suradhunī pāne cāya ||*

*Word for word:* rahi — standing; ati ucca taru-chāya — in the shade of a very tall tree; kahi ki madhura bāṇī — saying something sweet; ghana ghana — again and again; suradhunī pāne cāya — gazes at the Suradhuni (Ganga)

**9.2.** Standing in the shade of a very tall tree,
saying something sweet, He gazes again and again at the Suradhuni.

ধীরে ধরিয়া গদাই-করে ।
লহু লহু হাসে কি সুধা বরষে তাহা কে ধৈরজ ধরে ॥

*dhīre dhariyā gadāi-kare |*
*lahu lahu hāse ki sudhā baraṣe tāhā ke dhairaja dhare ||*

*Word for word:* dhīre — gently; dhariyā gadāi-kare — taking Gadai by the hand; lahu lahu hāse — softly smiles; ki sudhā baraṣe — what nectar pours; tāhā ke dhairaja dhare — who could keep composure at that

**9.3.** Gently taking Gadai by the hand,
He softly smiles — what nectar pours forth! Who could keep his composure?

আহা মরি কি মধুর রীত ।
নরহরি ভণে মনে অভিলাষ এ রসে মজুক চিত ॥

*āhā mari ki madhura rīta |*
*narahari bhaṇe mane abhilāṣa e rase majuka cita ||*

*Word for word:* āhā mari — ah; ki madhura rīta — how sweet this is; narahari bhaṇe — Narahari says; mane abhilāṣa — the desire in my heart; e rase — in this rasa; majuka cita — may my mind drown

**9.4.** Ah, how sweet this is!
Narahari says: the desire in my heart — may my mind drown in this rasa.

[^23-16]: GPT1 — p. 352, no. 28 ("sāraṅga"; scan, PDF p. 611); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 28. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-297). BR 12 (ed. 1912,
p. 938; ed. 1960, vv. 3257–3260) — immediately after no. 8. Variants: 9.2 GPT1 "rahi ati uccatara chāya", BR "rahi ati ucca taruchāya" (the BR reading is
adopted); 9.3 BR "dhariyā gadādhara-kare", "dhairaya dhare"; 9.4 BR "manuka cita" (OCR). Not in the PK, KGC, PS, GCC or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. Gadai is Gadadhara
Pandita (on him see note 39 of chapter 22).

## 10. Narahari — "gaura bidhubara barajamohana…" (GPT1 p. 354, no. 34; BR)
*The walk through Nadia (the afternoon part of the ashtakaliya): countless old men come out onto the road and gaze at Gaura with joy — "who
created this beautifully formed Ananga? How could we hide Him forever in the casket of the heart?" — and bless Him without end. Raga kamoda.
**Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR; Vrajabuli.*[^23-17]

গৌর বিধুবর বরজমোহন ভ্রমণ করু নদীয়ায় ।
বৃদ্ধ পুরুষ অসংখ্য পথগত নিরখে হরিষ হিয়ায় ॥

*gaura bidhubara barajamohana bhramaṇa karu nadīyāya |*
*bṛddha puruṣa asaṃkhya pathagata nirakhe hariṣa hiyāya ||*

*Word for word:* gaura bidhubara — Gaura, the best of moons; barajamohana — the Enchanter of Vraja; bhramaṇa karu nadīyāya — walks through Nadia; bṛddha puruṣa asaṃkhya — countless old men; pathagata — come out onto the road; nirakhe — gaze; hariṣa hiyāya — with joy in their hearts

**10.1.** Gaura, the best of moons, the Enchanter of Vraja, walks through Nadia;
countless old men who have come out onto the road gaze at Him with joy in their hearts.

কেউ কহে কিয়ে অনঙ্গ সুগঠন কোনে সিরজন কেল ।
ঐছে অপরূপ রূপক বহুল নয়নগোচর ভেল ॥

*keu kahe kiye anaṅga sugaṭhana kone sirajana kela |*
*aiche aparūpa rūpaka bahula nayanagocara bhela ||*

*Word for word:* keu kahe — someone says; kiye — what is this; anaṅga sugaṭhana — a beautifully formed Ananga; kone sirajana kela — who created; aiche aparūpa — such wondrous; rūpaka bahula — abundance of beauty; nayanagocara bhela — has come before the eyes

**10.2.** Someone says: "What is this — a beautifully formed Ananga? Who created Him?
Such a wondrous abundance of beauty has come before our eyes!"

কোই কহ কিয়ে নেহ ঘটই কি কহব কহই না যায় ।
হৃদয়-সম্পুটে ধরয় অনুক্ষণ কহ কি করব উপায় ॥

*koi kaha kiye neha ghaṭai ki kahaba kahai nā yāya |*
*hṛdaya-sampuṭe dharaya anukṣaṇa kaha ki karaba upāya ||*

*Word for word:* koi kaha — someone says; kiye neha ghaṭai — what love is born; ki kahaba — what can I say; kahai nā yāya — it cannot be told; hṛdaya-sampuṭe — in the casket of the heart; dharaya anukṣaṇa — to keep always; kaha ki karaba upāya — tell me, what means is there

**10.3.** Someone says: "What love is born — it cannot be put into words;
how could we keep Him always in the casket of the heart — tell me, what means is there?"

কোই কত কত ভাঁতি ভণত অনিবার আশীষ দেত ।
দাস নরহরি পহুঁক মাধুরী নিয়ত দিঠি ভরি লেত ॥

*koi kata kata bhām̐ti bhaṇata anibāra āśīṣa deta |*
*dāsa narahari pahum̐ka mādhurī niyata diṭhi bhari leta ||*

*Word for word:* koi — someone; kata kata bhām̐ti bhaṇata — speaking in every way; anibāra āśīṣa deta — gives blessings without end; dāsa narahari — Narahari Dasa; pahum̐ka mādhurī — the Lord's sweetness; niyata — ceaselessly; diṭhi bhari leta — drinks in with his eyes

**10.4.** Someone in every way gives blessings without end;
Narahari Dasa ceaselessly drinks in the Lord's sweetness with his eyes.[^23-18]

[^23-17]: GPT1 — p. 354, no. 34 ("kāmoda"; scan, PDF p. 613); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 34 (catalogue: NG-183, "in the BR"). BR 12 (ed. 1912, p. 868; ed. 1960, vv.
2358–2361): Ishana tells Srinivasa that the Lord, "to dispel the sorrow of the Vaishnavas and to make Himself known", walked through Nadia in beautiful
attire, and men and women, seeing Him, spoke to one another (vv. 2353–2357); then follow in a row nos. 10–14 and GPT pada no. 39 (vv. 2358–2383).
Variants: 10.3 BR "dharaba anukṣaṇa" ("I shall keep"; GPT "dharaya"); 10.4 BR "nirata diṭhi bhari leta" (GPT "niyata"). Not in the PK, KGC, PS, GCC or the
Gita-chandrodaya. B. In the ashtakaliya the walk through the town is the fifth part of the day, in the afternoon (no. 18, v. 18.5; no. 19, v. 19.6).
[^23-18]: Ananga ("the bodiless") is Kamadeva, the god of love: the Lord's beauty surpasses his. "The Enchanter of Vraja" (barajamohana): Gaura is Krishna,
who enchants Vraja. The old men, seeing Gaura, bless Him as the cowherds of Vraja blessed the young Krishna — their love is parental (vatsalya).

## 11. Narahari — "āju ki ānanda nadīyāya…" (GPT1 pp. 354–355, no. 35; BR)
*Old women stand in rows by the road and gaze at Shachi's darling: "He is not human!"; "blessed is Shachi, whom this Moon-faced One calls
mother"; "may He walk through Nadia like this and never leave it"; "may He always be well — let us take His misfortunes on ourselves". Raga
kamoda. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^23-19]

আজু কি আনন্দ নদীয়ায় ।
পথে কত বৃদ্ধা নারী দাঁড়াইয়া সারি সারি শচীর দুলাল পানে চায় ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*āju ki ānanda nadīyāya |*
*pathe kata bṛddhā nārī dām̐ṛāiyā sāri sāri śacīra dulāla pāne cāya || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* āju ki ānanda nadīyāya — what joy today in Nadia; pathe — by the road; kata bṛddhā nārī — how many old women; dām̐ṛāiyā sāri sāri — standing in rows; śacīra dulāla pāne cāya — gaze at Shachi's darling

**11.1.** What joy today in Nadia!
How many old women, standing in rows by the road, gaze at Shachi's darling!

কেহ কারু প্রতি কয় এ কভু মানুষ নয় বুঝিলাম চিতে বিচারিয়া ।
এমন বালক যেন না দেখি না শুনি হেন ভারতভূমেতে জনমিয়া ॥

*keha kāru prati kaya e kabhu mānuṣa naya bujhilāma cite bicāriyā |*
*emana bālaka yena nā dekhi nā śuni hena bhāratabhūmete janamiyā ||*

*Word for word:* keha kāru prati kaya — one says to another; e kabhu mānuṣa naya — He is not human; bujhilāma cite bicāriyā — I have understood, having thought it over; emana bālaka — such a youth; nā dekhi nā śuni — I have never seen or heard; bhārata-bhūmete janamiyā — since being born in the land of Bharata

**11.2.** One says to another: "He is not human — I have understood it, having thought it over;
such a youth I have never seen or heard of since I was born in the land of Bharata."

কেহ পুন পুন ভণে কি বলিব এত দিনে হইল সকল দুঃখ নাশ ।
কেহ কহে মনে যাহা কহিতে নারিয়ে তাহা ধন্য এই নদীয়ার বাস ॥

*keha puna puna bhaṇe ki baliba eta dine haila sakala duḥkha nāśa |*
*keha kahe mane yāhā kahite nāriye tāhā dhanya ei nadīyāra bāsa ||*

*Word for word:* keha puna puna bhaṇe — another says again and again; ki baliba — what can I say; eta dine — after so many days; haila sakala duḥkha nāśa — all sorrows have ended; mane yāhā — what is in my heart; kahite nāriye tāhā — I cannot express; dhanya ei nadīyāra bāsa — blessed is life in this Nadia

**11.3.** Another says again and again: "What can I say? Now, after so many days, all sorrows have come to an end."
A third says: "What is in my heart I cannot express; blessed is life in this Nadia!"

কেহ কহে শচী ধন্য করিলে যতেক পুণ্য কহিতে না জানি স্নেহ তার ।
এ চাঁদবদনে যাকে সদা মা বলিয়া ডাকে হেন ভাগ্য আছে আর কার ॥

*keha kahe śacī dhanya karile yateka puṇya kahite nā jāni sneha tāra |*
*e cām̐dabadane yāke sadā mā baliyā ḍāke hena bhāgya āche āra kāra ||*

*Word for word:* śacī dhanya — blessed is Shachi; karile yateka puṇya — how many pious deeds she has done; kahite nā jāni sneha tāra — her love cannot be told; e cām̐dabadane — this Moon-faced One; yāke sadā mā baliyā ḍāke — whom He always calls mother; hena bhāgya āche āra kāra — who else has such fortune

**11.4.** One says: "Blessed is Shachi! How many pious deeds she has done — and her love cannot be told:
this Moon-faced One always calls her 'mother' — who else has such fortune?"

কেহ কহে এই মতে বেড়াউক নদীয়াতে সকল প্রকৃতি সঙ্গে লৈয়া ।
কেহ কহে মনে হেন সোণার নিমাই যেন কখন না ছাড়য়ে নদীয়া ॥

*keha kahe ei mate beṛāuka nadīyāte sakala prakṛti saṅge laiyā |*
*keha kahe mane hena soṇāra nimāi yena kakhana nā chāṛaye nadīyā ||*

*Word for word:* ei mate — like this; beṛāuka nadīyāte — may He go about Nadia; sakala prakṛti saṅge laiyā — with all the people; mane hena — in my heart is this; sonāra nimāi — golden Nimai; yena kakhana nā chāṛaye nadīyā — that He may never leave Nadia

**11.5.** One says: "May He go about Nadia like this with all the people";
another says: "I have one thing in my heart — that golden Nimai may never leave Nadia."

কেহ কহে নদীয়াতে সদা রহ কুশলেতে বিধিরে প্রার্থনা এই করি ।
নরহরি-প্রাণ গোরা কেবল আঁখের তারা ইহার বালাই লইয়া মরি ॥

*keha kahe nadīyāte sadā raha kuśalete bidhire prārthanā ei kari |*
*narahari-prāṇa gorā kebala ām̐khera tārā ihāra bālāi laiyā mari ||*

*Word for word:* nadīyāte sadā raha kuśalete — may He always live in Nadia in well-being; bidhire prārthanā ei kari — this I pray to the Creator; narahari-prāṇa gorā — Gora, Narahari's life; kebala ām̐khera tārā — the very pupil of the eye; ihāra bālāi laiyā mari — may I die taking His misfortunes upon myself

**11.6.** One says: "I pray to the Creator for this alone — that He may always live in Nadia in well-being."
Gora is Narahari's life, the very pupil of the eye; may I die taking His misfortunes upon myself![^23-20]

[^23-19]: GPT1 — pp. 354–355, no. 35 ("kāmoda"; scan, PDF pp. 613–614); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 35. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-298). BR 12 (ed.
1912, pp. 868–869; ed. 1960, vv. 2362–2367) — immediately after no. 10. Variants: 11.4 BR "karila kateka puṇya"; 11.5 GPT1 and GPT2 "sakala prakṛti saṅge laiyā"
("with all the people"), BR "sakala sukṛti-saṅge laiyā" ("with all the pious"); 11.6 BR "narahari-prāṇa gorā, kebala ām̐khera tārā, ihāra bālāi laiyā mari". Not in
the PK, KGC, PS, GCC or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^23-20]: "He is not human": the women of Nadia perceive Bhagavan in Gaura. "May I die taking His misfortunes upon myself" (bālāi laiyā mari) is a Bengali
formula of motherly love. The last line apparently continues the women's speech, with the poet's signature inside it ("Gora is Narahari's life").

## 12. Narahari — "gaurāṅga-gamana śuni andhagaṇa…" (GPT1 p. 355, no. 36; BR)
*The blind, hearing that Gauranga is coming, step outside; having gained eyes, they gaze and gaze: "The Creator made us blind to give us great
bliss — so that we should see nothing else; whoever has not seen this beauty is blind though he has eyes; Narahari is witness: I have given
these eyes to golden Nimai." Raga bhupali. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^23-21]

গৌরাঙ্গ-গমন শুনি অন্ধগণ বাহিরে বাড়ায় পা ।
চাহে ঘন ঘন পাইয়া নয়ন উলসে ভরয়ে গা ॥

*gaurāṅga-gamana śuni andhagaṇa bāhire bāṛāya pā |*
*cāhe ghana ghana pāiyā nayana ulase bharaye gā ||*

*Word for word:* gaurāṅga-gamana śuni — hearing that Gauranga is coming; andhagaṇa — the blind; bāhire bāṛāya pā — step outside; cāhe ghana ghana — gaze and gaze; pāiyā nayana — having gained eyes; ulase bharaye gā — their bodies fill with rapture

**12.1.** Hearing that Gauranga is coming, the blind step outside;
having gained eyes, they gaze and gaze, and their bodies are full of rapture.

কেহ কারু করে ধরি কহে ধীরে আজু সে সফল হৈল ।
দিতে মহানন্দ বিধি কৈল অন্ধ আনে না দেখিতে দিল ॥

*keha kāru kare dhari kahe dhīre āju se saphala haila |*
*dite mahānanda bidhi kaila andha āne nā dekhite dila ||*

*Word for word:* keha kāru kare dhari — one, taking another by the hand; kahe dhīre — softly says; āju se saphala haila — today it has borne fruit; dite mahānanda — to give great bliss; bidhi kaila andha — the Creator made [us] blind; āne nā dekhite dila — did not let [us] see anything else

**12.2.** One, taking another by the hand, softly says: "Today [our blindness] has borne fruit:
to give us great bliss the Creator made us blind — He did not let us see anything else.

এ রূপ অমিয়া পিয়া এ না হিয়া কি করে না যায় জানা ।
হেন রূপ যেহ না দেখিল সেহ নয়ন থাকিতে কাণা ॥

*e rūpa amiyā piyā e nā hiyā ki kare nā yāya jānā |*
*hena rūpa yeha nā dekhila seha nayana thākite kāṇā ||*

*Word for word:* e rūpa amiyā — the nectar of this beauty; piyā e nā hiyā — this heart drinks; ki kare — what it does; nā yāya jānā — cannot be known; hena rūpa yeha nā dekhila — whoever has not seen such beauty; seha — he; nayana thākite kāṇā — is blind though he has eyes

**12.3.** The heart drinks the nectar of this beauty — what happens to it cannot be known;
whoever has not seen such beauty is blind, though he has eyes.

সদা দেখিবারে ধায় বারে বারে আঁখি না ধৈরজ বাঁধে ।
নরহরি সাখী সঁপিলুঁ এ আঁখি সোণার নিমাইচাঁদে ॥

*sadā dekhibāre dhāya bāre bāre ām̐khi nā dhairaja bām̐dhe |*
*narahari sākhī sam̐pilum̐ e ām̐khi soṇāra nimāicām̐de ||*

*Word for word:* sadā dekhibāre — to see always; dhāya bāre bāre — run again and again; ām̐khi nā dhairaja bām̐dhe — the eyes know no restraint; narahari sākhī — Narahari is witness; sam̐pilum̐ e ām̐khi — I have given these eyes; soṇāra nimāicām̐de — to golden Nimaichand

**12.4.** Again and again [the eyes] run to see Him and know no restraint;
Narahari is witness: I have given these eyes to golden Nimaichand."[^23-22]

[^23-21]: GPT1 — p. 355, no. 36 ("bhūpālī"; scan, PDF p. 614); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 36. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-299). BR 12 (ed. 1912,
p. 869; ed. 1960, vv. 2368–2371). Variants: 12.2 BR "bidhi kaile andha"; 12.3 BR "e rūpa amiyā, piyā e nā hiyā" (understood accordingly: "the heart drinks the
nectar of this beauty"); 12.4 BR "ām̐khi nā dhairya bām̐dhe", "som̐pilu". Not in the PK, KGC, PS, GCC or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^23-22]: "Having gained eyes" (pāiyā nayana): the blind receive sight at the sight of the Lord, and the only meaning of sight for them is to see Him; the
miracle here is a sign of mercy, and still more an image: truly sighted is only one who sees the Lord (12.3).

## 13. Narahari — "nadīyā bhramaye gorā guṇamaṇi…" (GPT1 p. 355, no. 37; BR)
*The lame, hearing that Gora is walking through Nadia, come out onto the road and cannot take their eyes off His face: "Now I understand,
merciful Creator, why You made me lame: if I were not lame, I would have gone off on business to distant lands and died there without
knowing Him; let me remain lame, so as always to see Narahari's Lord in Nadia." Raga todi. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada
is in the BR.*[^23-23]

নদীয়া ভ্রময়ে গোরা গুণমণি শুনি পঙ্গু পথে গিয়া ।
অনিমিষ আঁখি সে মুখ নিরখি আনন্দে উথলে হিয়া ॥

*nadīyā bhramaye gorā guṇamaṇi śuni paṅgu pathe giyā |*
*animiṣa ām̐khi se mukha nirakhi ānande uthale hiyā ||*

*Word for word:* nadīyā bhramaye — walks through Nadia; gorā guṇamaṇi — Gora, the jewel of virtues; śuni — hearing; paṅgu pathe giyā — the lame went onto the road; animiṣa ām̐khi — with unblinking eyes; se mukha nirakhi — gazing at that face; ānande uthale hiyā — the heart overflows with joy

**13.1.** Hearing that Gora, the jewel of virtues, is walking through Nadia, the lame went out onto the road;
gazing with unblinking eyes at that face, their hearts overflow with joy.

কেহ কহে শুন বিধি সকরুণ এবে সে বুঝিনু মনে ।
যে লাগিয়া পঙ্গু করিলে সে ফল ফলালে এতেক দিনে ॥

*keha kahe śuna bidhi sakaruṇa ebe se bujhinu mane |*
*ye lāgiyā paṅgu karile se phala phalāle eteka dine ||*

*Word for word:* keha kahe — one says; śuna bidhi sakaruṇa — listen, merciful Creator; ebe se bujhinu mane — now I have understood; ye lāgiyā paṅgu karile — for which You made [me] lame; se phala phalāle — that fruit You have brought forth; eteka dine — after so many days

**13.2.** One says: "Listen, merciful Creator, now I have understood:
the purpose for which You made me lame — that fruit You have brought forth now, after so many days.

পঙ্গু না হইলে গৃহ-কাজ-ছলে যাইতাম দূর দেশ ।
না জানিয়া তথা মরণ হইলে দুঃখের নহিত শেষ ॥

*paṅgu nā haile gṛha-kāja-chale yāitāma dūra deśa |*
*nā jāniyā tathā maraṇa haile duḥkhera nahita śeṣa ||*

*Word for word:* paṅgu nā haile — if I were not lame; gṛha-kāja-chale — on household business; yāitāma dūra deśa — I would go to distant lands; nā jāniyā — without knowing; tathā maraṇa haile — had I died there; duḥkhera nahita śeṣa — there would be no end of sorrow

**13.3.** If I were not lame, I would have gone to distant lands on household business;
had I died there without knowing [of Him], there would have been no end to my sorrow.

পঙ্গু হৈয়া যেন থাকি মেন হেন বিধিরে প্রার্থনা করি ।
নরহরি-নাথে সদা নদীয়াতে দেখি এ নয়ন ভরি ॥

*paṅgu haiyā yena thāki mena hena bidhire prārthanā kari |*
*narahari-nāthe sadā nadīyāte dekhi e nayana bhari ||*

*Word for word:* paṅgu haiyā — lame; yena thāki mena (= yena) hena — that I may remain like this; bidhire prārthanā kari — I pray to the Creator; narahari-nāthe — Narahari's Lord; sadā nadīyāte — always in Nadia; dekhi e nayana bhari — to see to my eyes' content

**13.4.** I pray to the Creator: let me remain lame like this —
so as always to see in Nadia Narahari's Lord to my eyes' content."

[^23-23]: GPT1 — p. 355, no. 37 ("tuṛi"; scan, PDF p. 614; the number is garbled in the OCR — "৩| pada"); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 37 (catalogue: NG-184). BR 12 (ed.
1912, pp. 869–870; ed. 1960, vv. 2372–2375). Variants: 13.2 GPT1 "ye lāgiyā paṅgu, karile saphala, phalāle eteka dine", BR "ye lāgiyā paṅgu karile se phala, phalā'le
eteka dine" (the sense is the same; translated by the BR); 13.3 BR "nā jāniye tathā". Not in the PK, KGC, PS, GCC or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. So in nos. 12–13:
every circumstance of life gains meaning if it leads to the Lord.

## 14. Narahari — "bhubanamohana gorā guṇamaṇi…" (GPT1 p. 356, no. 38; BR)
*Gora walks along the royal road, and hundreds of Kamadevas swoon at His feet; people run from all sides and give Him body, mind and life;
the young dandies of Nadia, glancing at Him, lose their foppish pride, and the connoisseurs of elegance become like fireflies before the
moon. Raga kamoda. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^23-24]

ভুবনমোহন গোরা গুণমণি রাজপথে কত ভঙ্গীতে চলে ।
কত কত শত মদন মূরছি লোটায়ে চরণ-কমল-তলে ॥

*bhubanamohana gorā guṇamaṇi rājapathe kata bhaṅgīte cale |*
*kata kata śata madana mūrachi loṭāye caraṇa-kamala-tale ||*

*Word for word:* bhubanamohana — enchanter of the world; gorā guṇamaṇi — Gora, the jewel of virtues; rājapathe — along the royal road; kata bhaṅgīte cale — walks with countless graces; kata kata śata madana — hundreds upon hundreds of Kamadevas; mūrachi — swooning; loṭāye caraṇa-kamala-tale — roll at His lotus feet

**14.1.** Gora, enchanter of the world, the jewel of virtues, walks along the royal road with countless graces;
hundreds upon hundreds of Kamadevas, swooning, roll at His lotus feet.

চারি দিকে লোক করে ধাওয়া ধাই অতুল শোভায় মোহিত হৈয়া ।
তনু মন প্রাণ কেবা না নিছয়ে পরস্পর চারু চরিত কৈয়া ॥

*cāri dike loka kare dhāoyā dhāi atula śobhāya mohita haiyā |*
*tanu mana prāṇa kebā nā nichaye paraspara cāru carita kaiyā ||*

*Word for word:* cāri dike loka — people on all sides; kare dhāoyā dhāi — run headlong; atula śobhāya mohita haiyā — enchanted by incomparable beauty; tanu mana prāṇa — body, mind and life; kebā nā nichaye — who does not offer; paraspara cāru carita kaiyā — telling one another of His lovely deeds

**14.2.** From all sides people come running, enchanted by His incomparable beauty;
who does not offer [Him] body, mind and life, telling one another of His lovely deeds?

নদীয়ানগরে নাগরালি বেশে ফিরয়ে নবীন নাগর যত ।
গোরাচাঁদ পানে চাহি তা সবার নাগর-গরব হইল হত ॥

*nadīyānagare nāgarāli beśe phiraye nabīna nāgara yata |*
*gorācām̐da pāne cāhi tā sabāra nāgara-garaba haila hata ||*

*Word for word:* nadīyā-nagare — in the town of Nadia; nāgarāli beśe — in fashionable dress; phiraye — stroll about; nabīna nāgara yata — all the young dandies; gorācām̐da pāne cāhi — glancing at Gorachand; tā sabāra — their; nāgara-garaba haila hata — foppish pride was destroyed

**14.3.** All the young dandies who stroll about the town of Nadia in fashionable dress —
glancing at Gorachand, they lost their foppish pride.

জগতের মাঝে প্রবীণতা অতি রসিকতামোদে বিভোর যারা ।
নরহরি ভণে খদ্যোত যেমন বিধু আগে হৈল তেমন তারা ॥

*jagatera mājhe prabīṇatā ati rasikatāmode bibhora yārā |*
*narahari bhaṇe khadyota yemana bidhu āge haila temana tārā ||*

*Word for word:* jagatera mājhe — in the world; prabīṇatā ati — most refined; rasikatāmode bibhora yārā — those drunk with the delight of elegance; narahari bhaṇe — Narahari says; khadyota yemana — like fireflies; bidhu āge — before the moon; haila temana tārā — they became

**14.4.** Those who in the world pass for refined and are drunk with the delight of elegance —
says Narahari — have become like fireflies before the moon.[^23-25]

[^23-24]: GPT1 — p. 356, no. 38 ("kāmoda"; scan, PDF p. 615); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 38 (catalogue: NG-185, "in the BR"). BR 12 (ed. 1912, p. 870; ed. 1960, vv.
