2376–2379). Variants: 14.4 GPT1 and GPT2 "khadyota yemana, kichu āge haila temana tārā" — "kichu" is clearly an error; the BR reading "bidhu āge" ("before the moon")
is adopted; 14.2 BR "kebā nāhi nichaye". Not in the PK, KGC, PS, GCC or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. The next GPT pada (no. 39; BR vv. 2380–2383) is in
nagari-bhava (note 7).
[^23-25]: "Dandies" (nabīna nāgara) are the fops of the town, men; there is no nagari-bhava here: the Lord's beauty humbles the pride of those who prided
themselves on their beauty and refinement.

## 15. Narahari — "nagarabhramaṇe bāhira haiyā…" (GPT1 p. 356, no. 40)
*Walking through the town, Gora goes into the houses of merchants; they joyfully give Him their goods. "I am a poor brahmana pandita," says
Gauranga, "how shall I pay?" — "Pay when You can, and if You cannot — no matter; since You were born we have lived happily; bless us and give
us the dust of Your feet." Raga dhanashi. **Attribution: not established** — the pada is known only from the GPT; plain Bengali.*[^23-26]

নগরভ্রমণে বাহির হইয়া নানা ব্যবসায়ী গৃহে যান গোরা ।
ব্যবসায়িগণ নানা দ্রব্য আনি দেয় তাঁরে হৈয়া আনন্দে ভোরা ॥

*nagarabhramaṇe bāhira haiyā nānā byabasāyī gṛhe yāna gorā |*
*byabasāyigaṇa nānā drabya āni deya tām̐re haiyā ānande bhorā ||*

*Word for word:* nagara-bhramaṇe bāhira haiyā — going out for a walk through the town; nānā byabasāyī gṛhe yāna gorā — Gora goes into the houses of various merchants; byabasāyigaṇa — the merchants; nānā drabya āni — bringing all kinds of goods; deya tām̐re — give to Him; haiyā ānande bhorā — beside themselves with joy

**15.1.** Going out for a walk through the town, Gora goes into the houses of various merchants;
the merchants, beside themselves with joy, bring all kinds of goods and give them to Him.

কহেন গৌরাঙ্গ ব্রাহ্মণ পণ্ডিত আমি হই ওহে দরিদ্র অতি ।
যে সব সামগ্রী দিতেছ তোমরা তার মূল্য মুই পাইব কতি ॥

*kahena gaurāṅga brāhmaṇa paṇḍita āmi hai ohe daridra ati |*
*ye saba sāmagrī ditecha tomarā tāra mūlya mui pāiba kati ||*

*Word for word:* kahena gaurāṅga — Gauranga says; brāhmaṇa paṇḍita āmi hai — I am a brahmana pandita; ohe — friends; daridra ati — very poor; ye saba sāmagrī diteccha tomarā — all the things you are giving; tāra mūlya — their price; mui pāiba kati — where shall I get

**15.2.** Gauranga says: "I am a brahmana pandita, friends, and very poor;
where shall I get the price for all these things you are giving?"

ব্যবসায়িগণ কহয়ে এ সব দয়া করি তুমি করহ গ্রহণ ।
যখন পারিবে মূল্য দিহ তুমি না পারিলে মোরা নাহি চাহি পণ ॥

*byabasāyigaṇa kahaye e saba dayā kari tumi karaha grahaṇa |*
*yakhana pāribe mūlya diha tumi nā pārile morā nāhi cāhi paṇa ||*

*Word for word:* byabasāyigaṇa kahaye — the merchants say; e saba — all this; dayā kari tumi karaha grahaṇa — be kind and accept; yakhana pāribe — when You can; mūlya diha tumi — You will pay; nā pārile — if You cannot; morā nāhi cāhi paṇa — we ask no payment

**15.3.** The merchants say: "Be kind and accept all this;
when You can, You will pay, and if You cannot, we do not ask for payment.

যে হইতে তুমি জনম লভিলা স্ত্রী পুত্র লইয়া আছি মোরা সুখে ।
কর শুভ দৃষ্টি কর আশীর্বাদ দেও পদধূলি শিরেতে বুকে ॥

*ye haite tumi janama labhilā strī putra laiyā āchi morā sukhe |*
*kara śubha dṛṣṭi kara āśīrvāda deo padadhūli śirete buke ||*

*Word for word:* ye haite tumi janama labhilā — since You were born; strī putra laiyā — with wives and sons; āchi morā sukhe — we live happily; kara śubha dṛṣṭi — cast an auspicious glance; kara āśīrvāda — bless; deo padadhūli — give the dust of Your feet; śirete buke — on our heads and breasts

**15.4.** Since You were born we have lived happily with our wives and sons;
cast an auspicious glance on us, bless us, give us the dust of Your feet for our heads and breasts."

তা সবার বাক্যে সন্তুষ্ট হইয়া গৃহেতে চলিলা নদীয়াশশী ।
কহে নরহরি ধন্য ব্যবসায়ী ধন্য ধন্য সব নদীয়াবাসী ॥

*tā sabāra bākye santuṣṭa haiyā gṛhete calilā nadīyāśaśī |*
*kahe narahari dhanya byabasāyī dhanya dhanya saba nadīyābāsī ||*

*Word for word:* tā sabāra bākye — by their words; santuṣṭa haiyā — pleased; gṛhete calilā — went home; nadīyāśaśī — the Moon of Nadia; kahe narahari — Narahari says; dhanya byabasāyī — blessed are the merchants; dhanya dhanya saba nadīyābāsī — blessed are all the people of Nadia

**15.5.** Pleased with their words, the Moon of Nadia went home.
Narahari says: blessed are the merchants, blessed, blessed are all the people of Nadia![^23-27]

[^23-26]: GPT1 — p. 356, no. 40 ("dhānaśī"; scan, PDF p. 615); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 40. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-300). Not in the BR, GCC, PK,
KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya; plain Bengali without Vrajabuli — according to Majumdar, rather a sign of Sarakara, but the pada exists only in the GPT, and
the story is common to the biographies; "not established", C.
[^23-27]: Cf. the account in the Chaitanya-bhagavata (Adi-khanda) of how Nimai Pandita went round the shops of Navadvipa — the weaver, the cowherd, the
sellers of perfumes, flowers and betel — and the merchants joyfully gave Him their goods, saying "You will pay later". The Lord calls Himself "a poor
brahmana" in the lila of a brahmana scholar; the merchants feel that their happiness comes from Him.

## 16. Narahari — "mari mari gauragaṇera carita…" (GPT1 p. 357, no. 42; GCC)
*Night: Gaura's companions know nothing but Him even in sleep; separated from Him for the time of sleep, they look at the sky — is the dawn
near? — and listen for the cries of peacocks and cuckoos. Raga not stated. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the
GCC.*[^23-28]

মরি মরি গৌরগণের চরিত বুঝিতে শকতি কার ।
শয়নে স্বপনে গৌরাঙ্গ বিহনে কিছু না জানয়ে আর ॥

*mari mari gauragaṇera carita bujhite śakati kāra |*
*śayane svapane gaurāṅga bihane kichu nā jānaye āra ||*

*Word for word:* mari mari — ah; gauragaṇera carita — the ways of Gaura's companions; bujhite śakati kāra — who has the power to understand; śayane svapane — in sleep and in dreams; gaurāṅga bihane — apart from Gauranga; kichu nā jānaye āra — they know nothing else

**16.1.** Ah! Who has the power to understand the ways of Gaura's companions?
In sleep and in dreams they know nothing but Gauranga.

ও চাঁদমুখের মৃদু মৃদু হাসি অমিয়া গরব নাশে ।
তিল আধ তাহা না দেখি কলপ অলপ করিয়া বাসে ॥

*o cām̐damukhera mṛdu mṛdu hāsi amiyā garaba nāśe |*
*tila ādha tāhā nā dekhi kalapa alapa kariyā bāse ||*

*Word for word:* o cām̐damukhera — of that moon-face; mṛdu mṛdu hāsi — the gentle smile; amiyā garaba nāśe — crushes the pride of nectar; tila ādha — even half a moment; tāhā nā dekhi — not seeing it; kalapa alapa kariyā bāse — they feel the little [while] as a kalpa

**16.2.** The gentle smile of that moon-face crushes the pride of nectar;
not seeing it even for half a moment, they feel that little while as a kalpa.

কি কব সে সব শয়ন-বিচ্ছেদে অধিক আকুল মনে ।
কতক্ষণে নিশি পোহাইব বলি চাহয়ে গগন পানে ॥

*ki kaba se saba śayana-bicchede adhika ākula mane |*
*katakṣaṇe niśi pohāiba bali cāhaye gagana pāne ||*

*Word for word:* ki kaba — what shall I say; se saba — of them; śayana-bicchede — in the separation of sleep; adhika ākula mane — in great agitation of heart; katakṣaṇe niśi pohāiba — how soon will the night end; bali — saying; cāhaye gagana pāne — they look at the sky

**16.3.** What shall I say of them! Separated [from Him] for the time of sleep, they are in great agitation:
"How soon will the night end?" they say, and look at the sky.

ময়ূর কপোত কোকিলাদি নাদ শুনিতে পাতয়ে কাণ ।
নরহরি কহে প্রভাত-উপায় চিন্তিতে ব্যাকুল প্রাণ ॥

*mayūra kapota kokilādi nāda śunite pātaye kāṇa |*
*narahari kahe prabhāta-upāya cintite byākula prāṇa ||*

*Word for word:* mayūra kapota kokilādi nāda — the cries of peacocks, doves, cuckoos; śunite pātaye kāṇa — they listen for; narahari kahe — Narahari says; prabhāta-upāya cintite — thinking how to bring the dawn; byākula prāṇa — anxious at heart

**16.4.** They listen for the cries of peacocks, doves, cuckoos;
Narahari says: anxiously they think how to bring the dawn nearer.[^23-29]

[^23-28]: GPT1 — p. 357, no. 42 ("yathārāga"; scan, PDF p. 616); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 42 (catalogue: NG-187). GCC — kirana 2 (nishanta, the last part of the night),
pada 2: immediately after pada 1 (= GPT 5.2 no. 63, Navadvipa at night: the companions sleep around the Lord's chamber; that pada goes to the next chapter).
Variants: 16.1 GCC "kichu nā jāne āra"; 16.3 GCC "ki kaba se saba śayana bicchede". Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^23-29]: The companions' separation from the Lord for the time of sleep is also a lila of love: cf. the gopis of Vraja, for whom a moment without
Krishna is like a yuga. The cry of the birds is the sign of dawn; in Krishna's ashtakaliya the birds of Vrinda likewise wake Radha and Krishna.

## 17. Narahari — "ko baraṇaba parikaragaṇa-leha…" (GPT1 p. 357, no. 43; GCC)
*The end of the night: the companions tremble, dreaming of seeing Gaura rise from His bed, drinking the nectar of His words and touching His
feet to drive away the sorrow of their hearts; their hearts long like the chataka waiting for the cloud. Raga not stated. **Attribution:
probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC; Vrajabuli.*[^23-30]

কো বরণব পরিকরগণ-লেহ ।
নিরখি নিতান্ত নিশান্ত সুমন্তর অন্তররহিত অতি পুলকিত দেহ ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*ko baraṇaba parikaragaṇa-leha |*
*nirakhi nitānta niśānta sumantara antararahita ati pulakita deha || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* ko baraṇaba — who can describe; parikaragaṇa-leha — the love of the companions; nirakhi — seeing; nitānta niśānta sumantara — that the end of the night is very near; antara-rahita — unceasingly; ati pulakita deha — their bodies thrill

**17.1.** Who can describe the love of the companions?
Seeing that the end of the night is very near, their bodies thrill unceasingly.

সাহস করি কত করত মনোরথ যাত রজনী অব হোত বিহান ।
গৌর-সুশয়নোত্থান-ভঙ্গি নব নিরখি করব ইহ তৃপত নয়ান ॥

*sāhasa kari kata karata manoratha yāta rajanī aba hota bihāna |*
*gaura-suśayanotthāna-bhaṅgi naba nirakhi karaba iha tṛpata nayāna ||*

*Word for word:* sāhasa kari — taking courage; kata karata manoratha — they build up hopes; yāta rajanī — the night is going; aba hota bihāna — now morning comes; gaura-suśayanotthāna-bhaṅgi naba — the new grace of Gaura rising from His bed; nirakhi — seeing; karaba iha tṛpata nayāna — we shall satisfy these eyes

**17.2.** Taking courage, they build up their hopes: "The night is going, now the morning comes;
seeing the new grace of Gaura rising from His lovely bed, we shall satisfy these eyes.

মৃদু মৃদু হসিত বদনে বচনামৃত শ্রবণে চমক ভরি পিয়ব ভূরি ।
করযুগে যুগপদ পরশি প্রচুরতর অন্তরখেদ করব অবদূরি ॥

*mṛdu mṛdu hasita badane bacanāmṛta śrabaṇe camaka bhari piyaba bhūri |*
*karayuge yugapada paraśi pracuratara antarakheda karaba abadūri ||*

*Word for word:* mṛdu mṛdu hasita badane — from the gently smiling lips; bacanāmṛta — the nectar of words; śrabaṇe — with the ears; camaka bhari — trembling; piyaba bhūri — we shall drink our fill; karayuge — with our hands; yuga-pada paraśi — touching both feet; pracuratara antara-kheda — the heavy sorrow of the heart; karaba abadūri — we shall drive far away

**17.3.** The nectar of words from His gently smiling lips we shall drink our fill with our ears, trembling;
touching His feet with our hands, we shall drive the sorrow of the heart far away."

ঐছে আশ কত উপজত হিয় মধি অধিক মগন গুণগণ করি গান ।
নরহরি ভণ ঘন-চাতক-সম চিত উৎকণ্ঠিত (নাহি) সমুঝত অনিদান ॥

*aiche āśa kata upajata hiya madhi adhika magana guṇagaṇa kari gāna |*
*narahari bhaṇa ghana-cātaka-sama cita utkaṇṭhita (nāhi) samujhata anidāna ||*

*Word for word:* aiche āśa kata — so many hopes; upajata hiya madhi — arise in the heart; adhika magana — they sink deeper; guṇagaṇa kari gāna — singing His virtues; narahari bhaṇa — Narahari says; ghana-cātaka-sama cita — the heart like a chataka [awaiting] the cloud; utkaṇṭhita — longs; (nāhi) samujhata anidāna — not knowing why

**17.4.** So many hopes arise in the heart — they sink still deeper, singing His virtues.
Narahari says: the heart, like the chataka [awaiting] the cloud, longs — and does not itself know why.

[^23-30]: GPT1 — p. 357, no. 43 ("yathārāga"; scan, PDF p. 616); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 43 (catalogue: NG-188). GCC — kirana 2, pada 3. Variants: 17.1 GCC "nirakhi niśānta
niśānta-sumantara" (OCR); 17.3 GCC "śrabaṇa camaka bhari piyaba bhūri"; 17.4 GCC, like the GPT, "utkaṇṭhita (nāhi) samujhata anidāna" — the word "nāhi" is in brackets in both
editions (an editor's supplement?); the sense is tentative. Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. The chataka is a bird that, according to
tradition, drinks only rainwater from the cloud — an image of the devotee who waits for the Lord alone.

## 18. Narahari — "niśi abaśeṣe lasata nadīyāśaśī…" (GPT1 pp. 358–359, no. 47; BR)
*A "table of contents" of the ashtakaliya in Vrajabuli — the eight parts of Gaura's day and night: at the end of the night, sleep in His
chamber; in the morning, bathing in the Suradhuni, the meal and a short rest; in the forenoon, pastimes in the companions' houses; at midday,
pastimes on the bank of the Suradhuni; in the afternoon, the walk through Nadia; at dusk, the return home to Shachi; at pradosha, the house of
Srivasa; at night, sankirtana and sleep again. Raga not stated (in the BR — shri). **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in
the BR; Vrajabuli.*[^23-31]

নিশি অবশেষে লসত নদীয়াশশী শয়ন সেজে নিজ মন্দির মাহি ।
ঝলমল অঙ্গ-কিরণ জন-রঞ্জন মনমথ-মথন-ভঙ্গী সম নাহি ॥

*niśi abaśeṣe lasata nadīyāśaśī śayana seje nija mandira māhi |*
*jhalamala aṅga-kiraṇa jana-rañjana manamatha-mathana-bhaṅgī sama nāhi ||*

*Word for word:* niśi abaśeṣe — at the end of the night; lasata nadīyāśaśī — the Moon of Nadia rests; śayana seje — on the bed; nija mandira māhi — in His chamber; jhalamala aṅga-kiraṇa — the rays of His body sparkle; jana-rañjana — delighting people; manamatha-mathana-bhaṅgī — grace that crushes Kamadeva; sama nāhi — has no equal

**18.1.** At the end of the night the Moon of Nadia rests on the bed in His chamber;
the rays of His body sparkle, delighting people — there is no equal to His grace, which crushes Kamadeva.

প্রাতঃ সময়ে সুক্রিয়ারত সুরধুনী অবগাহ করু পরম উলাস ।
গণ সহ বিবিধ ভাঁতি করি ভোজন পলছন শয়ন সেবই সব দাস ॥

*prātaḥ samaye sukriyārata suradhunī abagāha karu parama ulāsa |*
*gaṇa saha bibidha bhām̐ti kari bhojana palachana śayana sebai saba dāsa ||*

*Word for word:* prātaḥ samaye — in the morning; sukriyā-rata — performing auspicious rites; suradhunī abagāha karu — bathes in the Suradhuni (Ganga); parama ulāsa — with great joy; gaṇa saha — with His companions; bibidha bhām̐ti kari bhojana — having eaten many kinds of food; palachana śayana — lies down for a moment; sebai saba dāsa — all the servants serve

**18.2.** In the morning, performing the auspicious rites, He bathes in the Suradhuni with great joy;
having eaten all kinds of food with His companions, He lies down for a moment — all the servants serve Him.

পূর্বাহ্নে পরিতোষ করই সবে ধরি নব বেশ নিকসে চিতচোর ।
পরিকর সহ পরিকর-গৃহে বিলসত বুঝব কি প্রেম কি গতি নাহি ওর ॥

*pūrvāhne paritoṣa karai sabe dhari naba beśa nikase citacora |*
*parikara saha parikara-gṛhe bilasata bujhaba ki prema ki gati nāhi ora ||*

*Word for word:* pūrvāhne — in the forenoon; paritoṣa karai sabe — having gladdened everyone; dhari naba beśa — in new attire; nikase citacora — the Stealer of hearts goes out; parikara saha — with His companions; parikara-gṛhe bilasata — sports in the companions' houses; bujhaba ki prema — how to understand what love; ki gati nāhi ora — its ways have no end

**18.3.** In the forenoon, having gladdened everyone, the Stealer of hearts goes out in new attire;
with His companions He sports in the companions' houses — how to understand what this love is? There is no end to its ways.

ধন্য সময় মধ্যাহ্নে সরসি-বন-রাজী সুশীতল সুরধুনী-তীর ।
বিবিধ কেলি তহিঁ কো কবি বরণব নিরখত সুরগণ হোত অধীর ॥

*dhanya samaya madhyāhne sarasi-bana-rājī suśītala suradhunī-tīra |*
*bibidha keli tahim̐ ko kabi baraṇaba nirakhata suragaṇa hota adhīra ||*

*Word for word:* dhanya samaya madhyāhne — blessed is the time of midday; sarasi-bana-rājī — lakes and groves; suśītala suradhunī-tīra — the cool bank of the Suradhuni (Ganga); bibidha keli tahim̐ — many pastimes there; ko kabi baraṇaba — what poet will describe; nirakhata suragaṇa hota adhīra — the gods, watching, lose composure

**18.4.** Blessed is the time of midday: lakes, groves, the cool bank of the Suradhuni;
what poet will describe the many pastimes there? The gods, watching, lose their composure.

অতি অপরূপ অপরাহ্ন সময়ে নদীয়া মধি ভ্রমণ করয়ে গণ সঙ্গ ।
শোভা ভুবনবিজয়ী রস-বাদর নিরখি নগর-নরনারী উমঙ্গ ॥

*ati aparūpa aparāhna samaye nadīyā madhi bhramaṇa karaye gaṇa saṅga |*
*śobhā bhubanabijayī rasa-bādara nirakhi nagara-naranārī umaṅga ||*

*Word for word:* ati aparūpa — wondrous; aparāhna samaye — in the afternoon; nadīyā madhi bhramaṇa karaye — walks through Nadia; gaṇa saṅga — with His companions; śobhā bhubana-bijayī — beauty conquering the world; rasa-bādara — a downpour of rasa; nirakhi — seeing; nagara-naranārī umaṅga — the men and women of the town are in rapture

**18.5.** Wondrous is the time of afternoon: He walks with His companions through Nadia;
the beauty conquers the world, a downpour of rasa pours — seeing it, the men and women of the town are in rapture.

সাঁজ সময়ে নিজভবন গমন করু শ্রীশচীদেবী মুদিত মুখ হেরি ।
অদ্ভুত রঙ্গ প্রকট পহুঁ দরশনে কত শত লোক আয়ত কত বেরি ॥

*sām̐ja samaye nijabhabana gamana karu śrīśacīdebī mudita mukha heri |*
*adbhuta raṅga prakaṭa pahum̐ daraśane kata śata loka āyata kata beri ||*

*Word for word:* sām̐ja samaye — at dusk; nijabhabana gamana karu — goes home; śrī-śacīdebī mudita — Sri Shachidevi rejoices; mukha heri — seeing His face; adbhuta raṅga prakaṭa — a wondrous joy appears; pahum̐ daraśane — to see the Lord; kata śata loka āyata kata beri — hundreds of people come again and again

**18.6.** At dusk He goes home — Sri Shachidevi rejoices, looking at His face;
a wondrous joy: hundreds of people come again and again to see the Lord.

সময় প্রদোষহি তুষি জননী-মন প্রিয় শ্রীবাস-মন্দিরে উপনীত ।
অধিক উছাহ ভকতগণ তহিঁ পহুঁ রচই সুবেশ মধুরতর রীত ॥

*samaya pradoṣahi tuṣi jananī-mana priya śrībāsa-mandire upanīta |*
*adhika uchāha bhakatagaṇa tahim̐ pahum̐ racai subeśa madhuratara rīta ||*

*Word for word:* samaya pradoṣahi — at the time of pradosha; tuṣi jananī-mana — gladdening His mother's heart; priya śrībāsa-mandire upanīta — comes to the house of dear Srivasa; adhika uchāha bhakatagaṇa tahim̐ — there the devotees are in great enthusiasm; pahum̐ racai subeśa — the Lord puts on beautiful attire; madhuratara rīta — the sweetest custom

**18.7.** At the time of pradosha, having gladdened His mother's heart, He comes to the house of dear Srivasa;
there the devotees are in great enthusiasm, and the Lord puts on beautiful attire — the sweetest custom.

বিমল নিশার সময়ে সংকীর্তনে মাতি মুদিত হিয় কৌতুক জোর ।
গণ সহ পুন নিজভবনে শুতই নরহরি-পহুঁ রসময় গৌরকিশোর ॥

*bimala niśāra samaye saṃkīrtane māti mudita hiya kautuka jora |*
*gaṇa saha puna nijabhabane śutai narahari-pahum̐ rasamaya gaurakiśora ||*

*Word for word:* bimala niśāra samaye — at night, in the clear hours; saṅkīrtane māti — drunk with sankirtana; mudita hiya — with a joyful heart; kautuka jora — in boisterous delight; gaṇa saha puna — again with His companions; nijabhabane śutai — lies down in His own house; narahari-pahum̐ — Narahari's Lord; rasamaya gaura-kiśora — the young Gaura full of rasa

**18.8.** At night, in the clear hours, drunk with sankirtana, with a joyful heart, in boisterous delight —
and again with His companions He lies down in His own house, Narahari's Lord, the young Gaura full of rasa.[^23-32]

[^23-31]: GPT1 — pp. 358–359, no. 47 ("yathārāga"; scan, PDF pp. 617–618); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 47 (catalogue: NG-189, "in the BR"). BR 12 (ed. 1912, p. 947; ed. 1960,
vv. 3371–3378, "śrīrāga"): Ishana tells Srinivasa that the wise remember Chaitanya's eternal lila by the eight parts of the day, quotes the Sanskrit verses of
"the ancients" (vv. 3366–3370: nishanta — sleep in His house; morning — rising, bathing, the meal; forenoon — the devotees' houses; midday — pastimes on the
bank of the Ganga; afternoon — the walk through Navadvipa; dusk — the return home; pradosha — the house of Srivasa; night — the festival of sankirtana) and
then this pada, which retells them. Variants: 18.1 BR "śayana seje", "manorañjana"; 18.2 BR "abagāhana kara", "gala-chana śayana" (GPT "palachana śayana" — understood as "pala-kṣaṇa", "for a
moment"); 18.3 BR "premaka gati naha ora"; 18.7 BR "pahu rāi subeśa" (OCR). Not in the PK, KGC, PS, GCC or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^23-32]: Gaura's ashtakaliya follows the model of the ashtakaliya of Radha and Krishna (the eight parts of the day in Vraja); it is eternal lila,
which devotees remember in their service (note 36 of chapter 22). The chapter follows these parts: sleep and awakening (nos. 1–6), midday at the
Ganga (nos. 7–9), the walk through Nadia (nos. 10–15), night (nos. 16–17), kirtana in the houses of Srivasa and Chandrashekhara (nos. 20–22).

## 19. Narahari — "niśiśeṣe gorā ghumera ābeśe…" (GPT1 p. 359, no. 48; GCC)
*The same "table of contents" of the ashtakaliya in plain Bengali: sleep at the end of the night; in the morning, Gaura in the courtyard
among His companions; bathing in the Suradhuni, the meal and rest; in the forenoon, in the houses of Shuklambara and other devotees; at midday,
in a flower garden; in the afternoon, the walk through Nadia; in the evening, at home, worship of the Deity to please His mother; at
pradosha, the house of Srivasa; at night, sankirtana and sleep. Raga todi. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the
GCC.*[^23-33]

নিশিশেষে গোরা ঘুমের আবেশে শয়ন পালঙ্কোপরে ।
হেন জন নাহি বারেক সে শোভা হেরিয়া পরাণ ধরে ॥

*niśiśeṣe gorā ghumera ābeśe śayana pālaṅkopare |*
*hena jana nāhi bāreka se śobhā heriyā parāṇa dhare ||*

*Word for word:* niśiśeṣe — at the end of the night; gorā — Gora; ghumera ābeśe — absorbed in sleep; śayana pālaṅkopare — lies on the bed; hena jana nāhi — there is no one; bāreka se śobhā heriyā — who, seeing that beauty even once; parāṇa dhare — could keep hold of his heart

**19.1.** At the end of the night Gora, absorbed in sleep, lies on the bed;
there is no one who, seeing that beauty even once, could keep hold of his heart.

প্রভাতে জাগিয়া নিজ পরিকর-বেষ্টিত অঙ্গনে বসি ।
জগজন-মন হেলাতে হরিয়া হিয়াতে থাকয়ে পশি ॥

*prabhāte jāgiyā nija parikara-beṣṭita aṅgane basi |*
*jagajana-mana helāte hariyā hiyāte thākaye paśi ||*

*Word for word:* prabhāte jāgiyā — in the morning, having woken; nija parikara-beṣṭita — surrounded by His companions; aṅgane basi — sits in the courtyard; jagajana-mana — the hearts of the people of the world; helāte hariyā — playfully stealing; hiyāte thākaye paśi — enters the hearts and dwells there

**19.2.** In the morning, having woken, He sits in the courtyard surrounded by His companions;
playfully stealing the hearts of the people of the world, He enters them and dwells there.

দন্তধাবনাদি সারি সুরধুনী-সিনান আনন্দাবেশে ।
নিজগৃহে গণ সহিত ভোজন কৌতুক শয়ন শেষে ॥

*dantadhābanādi sāri suradhunī-sināna ānandābeśe |*
*nijagṛhe gaṇa sahita bhojana kautuka śayana śeṣe ||*

*Word for word:* dantadhābanādi sāri — having cleaned His teeth and so on; suradhunī-sināna — the bath in the Suradhuni (Ganga); ānandābeśe — in joyful rapture; nijagṛhe — in His own house; gaṇa sahita bhojana kautuka — the merry meal with His companions; śayana śeṣe — then rest

**19.3.** Having cleaned His teeth and so on — the bath in the Suradhuni in joyful rapture;
in His own house — the merry meal with His companions, and then rest.

পূর্বাহ্ন সময়ে শুক্লাম্বর আদি ভকতগণের ঘরে ।
প্রেমের আবেশে অবশ হইয়া বিবিধ বিলাস করে ॥

*pūrvāhna samaye śuklāmbara ādi bhakatagaṇera ghare |*
*premera ābeśe abaśa haiyā bibidha bilāsa kare ||*

*Word for word:* pūrvāhna samaye — in the forenoon; śuklāmbara ādi bhakatagaṇera ghare — in the houses of Shuklambara and other devotees; premera ābeśe — in the rapture of prema; abaśa haiyā — overcome; bibidha bilāsa kare — sports in many ways

**19.4.** In the forenoon — in the houses of Shuklambara and other devotees:
overcome by the rapture of prema, He sports in many ways.

মধ্যাহ্ন কালেতে অতি মনোহর পুষ্পের উদ্যান মাঝে ।
কত কত রঙ্গ-তরঙ্গে বিভোর সঙ্গে পারিষদ সাজে ॥

*madhyāhna kālete ati manohara puṣpera udyāna mājhe |*
*kata kata raṅga-taraṅge bibhora saṅge pāriṣada sāje ||*

*Word for word:* madhyāhna kālete — at midday; ati manohara puṣpera udyāna mājhe — in a most charming flower garden; kata kata raṅga-taraṅge bibhora — drunk with the waves of countless delights; saṅge pāriṣada sāje — with His companions in their finery

**19.5.** At midday — in a most charming flower garden:
with His companions in their finery, drunk with the waves of countless delights.

অপরাহ্ন সময়ে ধরিয়া ভুবনমোহন বেশ ।
নদীয়ানগরে ভ্রমণ-বিনোদ শোভার নাহিক শেষ ॥

*aparāhna samaye dhariyā bhubanamohana beśa |*
*nadīyānagare bhramaṇa-binoda śobhāra nāhika śeṣa ||*

*Word for word:* aparāhna samaye — in the afternoon; dhariyā bhubanamohana beśa — putting on attire that enchants the world; nadīyānagare — through the town of Nadia; bhramaṇa-binoda — the pleasure-walk; śobhāra nāhika śeṣa — there is no end to the beauty

**19.6.** In the afternoon, putting on attire that enchants the world —
the pleasure-walk through the town of Nadia: there is no end to the beauty.

সন্ধ্যাকালে নিজ ভবনে গমন অতি অপরূপ রীত ।
দেব-বন্দনাদি করিয়া যতনে যাহাতে মায়ের প্রীত ॥

*sandhyākāle nija bhabane gamana ati aparūpa rīta |*
*deba-bandanādi kariyā yatane yāhāte māyera prīta ||*

*Word for word:* sandhyā-kāle — in the evening; nija bhabane gamana — the return home; ati aparūpa rīta — wondrous in every way; deba-bandanādi — worship of the Deity and so on; kariyā yatane — doing diligently; yāhāte māyera prīta — what pleases His mother

**19.7.** In the evening — the return home, wondrous in every way:
He diligently worships the Deity and so on — what pleases His mother.

প্রদোষে শ্রীবাস-মন্দিরে প্রবেশ অধিক উলাস হিয়া ।
তথা প্রিয়গণ-মন-অনুরূপ করয়ে অদ্ভুত ক্রিয়া ॥

*pradoṣe śrībāsa-mandire prabeśa adhika ulāsa hiyā |*
*tathā priyagaṇa-mana-anurūpa karaye adbhuta kriyā ||*

*Word for word:* pradoṣe — at pradosha; śrībāsa-mandire prabeśa — into the house of Srivasa; adhika ulāsa hiyā — with great joy in His heart; tathā — there; priyagaṇa-mana-anurūpa — as the hearts of His dear companions desire; karaye adbhuta kriyā — performs wondrous deeds

**19.8.** At pradosha — into the house of Srivasa, with great joy in His heart:
there He performs wondrous deeds, as the hearts of His dear companions desire.

নিশায় সকল পরিকর সহ সংকীর্তন করি ।
পুনঃ নিজগৃহে শয়ন আনন্দে ভণে দাস নরহরি ॥

*niśāya sakala parikara saha saṃkīrtana kari |*
*punaḥ nijagṛhe śayana ānande bhaṇe dāsa narahari ||*

*Word for word:* niśāya — at night; sakala parikara saha — with all His companions; saṅkīrtana kari — performing sankirtana; punaḥ nijagṛhe — again in His own house; śayana ānande — blissful rest; bhaṇe dāsa narahari — says Narahari Dasa

**19.9.** At night — sankirtana with all His companions;
and again in His own house blissful rest, says Narahari Dasa.[^23-34]

[^23-33]: GPT1 — p. 359, no. 48 ("tuṛī"; scan, PDF p. 618); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 48 (catalogue: NG-190). GCC — kirana 1 (mangalacarana), pada 61, "rāga toṛī": before it
the GCC says that Narahari arranged the eight parts of the day (dawn, morning, forenoon, midday, afternoon, evening, pradosha, night) following "the view of
the crest-jewel of poets, a devotee of Gaura" (pada 59), and gives it as the "summary" (sūtra) of the ashtakaliya, which it then unfolds kirana by kirana.
Variants: 19.3 GCC "suradhuni sināna"; 19.6 GPT1 and GPT2 "bhramaṇa bibāda" — an error, corrected by the GCC "bhramaṇa-binoda"; 19.7 GCC "kariye yatane"; 19.9 GCC "parikarasaha sukhe
saṃkīrtana kari", "nijagṛhe". Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^23-34]: "Worships the Deity" (deba-bandanā): the worship of the household Deity of Vishnu in Shachi's house; the Lord, Krishna Himself, in the lila of a
brahmana householder performs the duties of a devotee and pleases His mother. Shuklambara Brahmachari is a companion of the Lord at whose place the
Lord ate the rice he had begged (CB, Madhya-khanda).

## 20. Narahari — "bhubanamohana gaura naṭabara…" (GPT1 p. 360, no. 49; BR)
*The evening kirtana: Gaura, the best of dancers, today dances in the guise of Rukmini — a description of the attire and beauty from the hair
to the feet: many-coloured silks, a jewelled band, earrings, collyrium, a nose-pendant, a necklace, conch bangles, a golden girdle with
bells, ankle-bells. Raga shankarabharana. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR; Vrajabuli.*[^23-35]

ভুবনমোহন গৌর নটবর বরজমোহন রসিকশেখর
আজু রুক্মিণী-বেশে করু নব নৃত্য নিরুপম ভ্রাজয়ে ।
অঙ্গরুচি জিনি কনক-দরপণ করত ঝলমল ললিত চিকণ
রুচির পরম বিচিত্র পহিরণ বিবিধ অংশুক সাজয়ে ॥

*bhubanamohana gaura naṭabara barajamohana rasikaśekhara*
*āju rukmiṇī-beśe karu naba nṛtya nirupama bhrājaye |*
*aṅgaruci jini kanaka-darapaṇa karata jhalamala lalita cikaṇa*
*rucira parama bicitra pahiraṇa bibidha aṃśuka sājaye ||*

*Word for word:* bhubanamohana — enchanter of the world; gaura naṭabara — Gaura, the best of dancers; barajamohana — the Enchanter of Vraja; rasikaśekhara — crown of the relishers of rasa; āju rukmiṇī-beśe — today in the guise of Rukmini; karu naba nṛtya — dances a new dance; nirupama bhrājaye — shines incomparably; aṅga-ruci — the lustre of His body; jini kanaka-darapaṇa — surpassing a golden mirror; karata jhalamala — sparkles; lalita cikaṇa — lovely, tender; rucira parama bicitra pahiraṇa — beautiful, wondrously many-coloured dress; bibidha aṃśuka sājaye — arrayed in various silks

**20.1.** Gaura, enchanter of the world, the best of dancers, the Enchanter of Vraja, crown of the relishers of rasa,
today dances a new dance in the guise of Rukmini — He shines incomparably;
the lustre of His body surpasses a golden mirror — He sparkles, lovely and tender;
His beautiful, wondrously many-coloured dress — He is arrayed in various silks.

চিকুরচয় কমনীয় বন্ধন ঘোরি মৃগমদ চিত্রচন্দন
সরস লসত ললাট-তট মণি-বন্ধনী মন মোহয়ে ।
কর্ণভূষণ তরল মৃদুতর গণ্ডযুগ জনু ভ্রমর ভুরুবর
কঞ্জলোচন মঞ্জু অঞ্জন-রঞ্জিতাধিক শোহয়ে ॥

*cikuracaya kamanīya bandhana ghori mṛgamada citracandana*
*sarasa lasata lalāṭa-taṭa maṇi-bandhanī mana mohaye |*
*karṇabhūṣaṇa tarala mṛdutara gaṇḍayuga janu bhramara bhurubara*
*kañjalocana mañju añjana-rañjitādhika śohaye ||*

*Word for word:* cikuracaya kamanīya bandhana — the locks charmingly arranged; ghori mṛgamada — ground musk; citra-candana — patterned sandal paste; sarasa lasata lalāṭa-taṭa — shine freshly on the forehead; maṇi-bandhanī — the jewelled band; mana mohaye — captivates the mind; karṇabhūṣaṇa tarala — the earrings sway; mṛdutara gaṇḍayuga — at the tender cheeks; janu bhramara bhurubara — the lovely brows like bees; kañjalocana — lotus eyes; mañju añjana-rañjita — with charming collyrium; adhika śohaye — lovelier still

**20.2.** The locks of His hair are charmingly arranged; ground musk and patterned sandal paste
shine freshly on His forehead; the jewelled band captivates the mind;
the earrings sway at His tender cheeks; His lovely brows are like bees;
His lotus eyes with charming collyrium are lovelier still.[^23-36]

বিম্বফলমিব বন্ধুরাধর নাসিকা শুক-চঞ্চু বেশর-
বলিত বয়ন-ময়ঙ্ক দশন কুন্দ-মদ-ভর-ভঞ্জন ।
কম্বু-অঙ্কিত বক্ষ মৃদুতর হার-রতন অনঙ্গ-ধৃতি-হর
শঙ্খ সরু কর কঙ্কণাঙ্গুলি অঙ্গুরী জনু রঞ্জন ॥

*bimbaphalamiba bandhurādhara nāsikā śuka-cañcu beśara-*
*balita bayana-mayaṅka daśana kunda-mada-bhara-bhañjana |*
*kambu-aṅkita bakṣa mṛdutara hāra-ratana anaṅga-dhṛti-hara*
*śaṅkha saru kara kaṅkaṇāṅguli aṅgurī janu rañjana ||*

*Word for word:* bimbaphalam iba — like the bimba fruit; bandhurādhara — the lovely lips; nāsikā śuka-cañcu — the nose like a parrot's beak; beśara-balita — with a pendant; bayana-mayaṅka — the face a moon; daśana — the teeth; kunda-mada-bhara-bhañjana — crushing the pride of jasmine; kambu-aṅkita — marked like a conch [the neck]; bakṣa mṛdutara — the tender breast; hāra-ratana — the jewelled necklace; anaṅga-dhṛti-hara — stealing Ananga's composure; śaṅkha — conch bangles; saru kara — on slender hands; kaṅkaṇāṅguli aṅgurī — rings on the fingers; janu rañjana — like a delight

**20.3.** His lips are like the bimba fruit; His nose is like a parrot's beak, with a pendant;
His face is the moon; His teeth crush the pride of jasmine;
His neck has three lines like a conch, His breast is tender; the jewelled necklace steals Ananga's composure;
on His slender hands are conch bangles, on His fingers rings, a delight [to the eye].

অতুল উদর সুঠাম রস ঝরু নবীন কেশরি-গৌরব দূর করু
ক্ষীণ মধ্য সুমধুর মাধুরী কনক কিঙ্কিণী রাজয়ে ।
ভঙ্গী সঞে পদ ধরণী ধরু যব অতিহি কোমল হোত ক্ষিতি তব
নিছুই নরহরি-জীবন ঘন মঞ্জীর ঝননন বাজয়ে ॥

*atula udara suṭhāma rasa jharu nabīna keśari-gauraba dūra karu*
*kṣīṇa madhya sumadhura mādhurī kanaka kiṅkiṇī rājaye |*
*bhaṅgī sañe pada dharaṇī dharu yaba atihi komala hota kṣiti taba*
*nichui narahari-jībana ghana mañjīra jhananana bājaye ||*

*Word for word:* atula udara suṭhāma — the incomparable shapely belly; rasa jharu — pours out rasa; nabīna keśari-gauraba dūra karu — shames the pride of a young lion; kṣīṇa madhya — the slender middle; sumadhura mādhurī — of the sweetest charm; kanaka kiṅkiṇī rājaye — a golden girdle with bells shines; bhaṅgī sañe — gracefully; pada dharaṇī dharu yaba — when He steps on the earth; atihi komala hota kṣiti taba — the earth becomes very soft; nichui — offers [for Him]; narahari-jībana — Narahari's life; ghana — loudly; mañjīra jhanana bājaye — the ankle-bells ring

**20.4.** His incomparable shapely belly pours out rasa, [His waist] shames the pride of a young lion;
His slender middle of the sweetest charm — a golden girdle with bells shines;
when He gracefully steps on the earth — the earth becomes very soft;
Narahari offers his life for Him; the ankle-bells ring out jhanana.

[^23-35]: GPT1 — p. 360, no. 49 ("śaṅkarābharaṇa"; scan, PDF p. 619); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 49 (catalogue: NG-191). BR 12 (ed. 1912, pp. 913–914; ed. 1960, vv. 2913–2916,
"rāga śaṅkarābharaṇa"): in the house of Chandrashekhara Acharya, Sadashiva and Buddhimanta Khan prepare costumes; the Lord is to dance in the guise of Lakshmi and
others; Shachi comes with her daughter-in-law to watch; Mukunda begins the kirtana; "the Lord became Rukmini — no one could recognise Him" (vv. 2903–2912);
after the pada the BR says that the Lord is the embodiment of all His energies: He dances now in the guise of Parvati, now in the guise of Lakshmi (vv.
2917–2918). Variants: 20.1 BR "barajabhūṣaṇa" ("ornament of Vraja"), "aṅgaruci jini' kanaka darapaṇa"; 20.2 GPT1 "sarasa lasata lalāṭa taṭa maṇi, bandhanā mana mohaye" — divided by the BR
"lalāṭa-taṭa maṇi-bandhanī"; 20.3 GPT1 "daśana mukunda madabharabhañjana", BR "daśana sukunda madabhara tathanā" (OCR) — understood as "daśana kunda-mada-bhara-bhañjana" ("the teeth crush the pride
of jasmine"); 20.4 BR "bhaṅgi saṅge", "nichai". Not in the PK, KGC, PS, GCC or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^23-36]: The Lord's dance in the guise of Rukmini (and of Lakshmi, Adya-shakti) in the house of Chandrashekhara is described by Vrindavana Dasa (CB Madhya
18): there the Lord appears in the form of His own energy, and the devotees see in Him the Mother of the universe. The Lord is the source of all
energies; the form of Rukmini, queen of Dvaraka, is a manifestation of His own shakti, not a worldly disguise; the description of beauty "from the hair
to the feet" is the traditional praise (nakha-shikha) of the Lord's form.

## 21. Narahari — "āju śubha ārambha kīrtane…" (GPT1 pp. 360–361, no. 50; BR)
*The night kirtana in Srivasa's courtyard: Gaurasundara in a joyful dance among His companions; His feet keep time, and the earth trembles;
on the left Gadadhara, on the right Nitai, in front the intoxicated Advaita; Vasudeva, Srivasa, Vijaya, Vakreshvara, Mukunda and others sing,
Rama, Govinda and Garuda play the mardala; the world is full of cries of "jaya!". Raga mayura. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada
is in the BR; Vrajabuli.*[^23-37]

আজু শুভ আরম্ভ কীর্তনে গৌরসুন্দর মুদিত নর্তনে
সুঘর পরিকর মধ্য মধুর শ্রীবাস-অঙ্গনে শোহয়ে ।
কনক-কেশর-গরব-গঞ্জন মঞ্জু তনুরুচি অতনু-রঞ্জন
কঞ্জলোচন চপল চহুদিশ চাহি জনমন মোহয়ে ॥

*āju śubha ārambha kīrtane gaurasundara mudita nartane*
*sughara parikara madhya madhura śrībāsa-aṅgane śohaye |*
*kanaka-keśara-garaba-gañjana mañju tanuruci atanu-rañjana*
*kañjalocana capala cahudiśa cāhi janamana mohaye ||*

*Word for word:* āju śubha ārambha kīrtane — today the auspicious beginning of the kirtana; gaurasundara mudita nartane — Gaurasundara in a joyful dance; sughara parikara madhya — among His skilful companions; madhura śrībāsa-aṅgane śohaye — shines sweetly in Srivasa's courtyard; kanaka-keśara-garaba-gañjana — shaming the pride of golden filaments; mañju tanuruci — the lovely lustre of His body; atanu-rañjana — delighting Kamadeva; kañjalocana capala cahudiśa cāhi — lotus eyes glancing restlessly in all directions; janamana mohaye — captivate people's hearts

**21.1.** Today is the auspicious beginning of the kirtana: Gaurasundara in a joyful dance
shines sweetly among His skilful companions in the courtyard of Srivasa;
the lovely lustre of His body shames the pride of golden filaments [of the lotus] and delights Kamadeva;
His lotus eyes glance restlessly in all directions and captivate people's hearts.

নটন-গতি অতি তরুণ পদতল তাল ধরইতে ধরণী টলমল
করই হস্তক ত্রস্ত কলিত সুললিত কর-কিশলয়-ছটা ।
দশন মোতিম-পাঁতি নিরসত হাস লহু লহু অমিয়া বরষত
সরস লসত সুবদন-মাধুরী জিতই শারদ-শশী-ঘটা ॥

*naṭana-gati ati taruṇa padatala tāla dharaite dharaṇī ṭalamala*
*karai hastaka trasta kalita sulalita kara-kiśalaya-chaṭā |*
*daśana motima-pām̐ti nirasata hāsa lahu lahu amiyā baraṣata*
*sarasa lasata subadana-mādhurī jitai śārada-śaśī-ghaṭā ||*

*Word for word:* naṭana-gati — dancing; ati taruṇa padatala — with the tenderest feet; tāla dharaite — keeping time; dharaṇī ṭalamala — the earth trembles; karai hastaka — makes hastaka gestures; trasta kalita sulalita — quivering and graceful; kara-kiśalaya-chaṭā — the radiance of hands like young shoots; daśana motima-pām̐ti nirasata — the teeth outshine a string of pearls; hāsa lahu lahu amiyā baraṣata — the soft smile pours nectar; sarasa lasata subadana-mādhurī — the fresh sweetness of the lovely face; jitai śārada-śaśī-ghaṭā — conquers a host of autumn moons

**21.2.** Dancing, with the tenderest feet He keeps time — and the earth trembles;
He makes the hastaka gestures, quivering and graceful — the radiance of His hands like young shoots;
His teeth outshine a string of pearls; His soft smile pours nectar;
the fresh sweetness of His lovely face conquers a host of autumn moons.

চিকণ চাঁচর চিকুর-বন্ধন চারু রচিত সুতিলক চন্দন
ভূরি ভূষণ ঝলকে অঙ্গ বিভঙ্গী ভণত না আয়য়ে ।
বামে পহুঁ পণ্ডিত গদাধর দক্ষিণেতে নিতাই সুন্দর
সম্মুখে শ্রীঅদ্বৈত উনমত পেখি সুরগণ ধায়য়ে ॥

*cikaṇa cām̐cara cikura-bandhana cāru racita sutilaka candana*
*bhūri bhūṣaṇa jhalake aṅga bibhaṅgī bhaṇata nā āyaye |*
*bāme pahum̐ paṇḍita gadādhara dakṣiṇete nitāi sundara*
*sammukhe śrīadvaita unamata pekhi suragaṇa dhāyaye ||*

*Word for word:* cikaṇa cām̐cara cikura-bandhana — the glossy curling hair bound up; cāru racita sutilaka candana — tilaka and sandal paste charmingly applied; bhūri bhūṣaṇa jhalake aṅga — a wealth of ornaments sparkles on His body; bibhaṅgī bhaṇata nā āyaye — His bends cannot be described; bāme pahum̐ — on the Lord's left; paṇḍita gadādhara — Gadadhara Pandita; dakṣiṇete nitāi sundara — on the right lovely Nitai; sammukhe śrī-advaita unamata — in front the intoxicated Sri Advaita; pekhi suragaṇa dhāyaye — seeing, the gods come running

**21.3.** His glossy curling hair is bound up, the tilaka and sandal paste are charmingly applied;
a wealth of ornaments sparkles on His body — His graceful bends cannot be described;
on the Lord's left is Gadadhara Pandita, on His right lovely Nitai,
in front the intoxicated Sri Advaita; seeing this, the gods come running.

বাসুদেব শ্রীবাস নন্দন বিজয় বক্রেশ্বর নারায়ণ
গোপীনাথ মুকুন্দ মাধব গায়ত এ অদ্ভুত গুণী ।
রাম বামে গোবিন্দ গরুড় আদিক বায় মর্দল ধিকতা তাধিক
ধিনি নি নি নি নি নি ভণত নরহরি ভুবন ভরু জয় জয় ধুনি ॥

*bāsudeba śrībāsa nandana bijaya bakreśvara nārāyaṇa*
*gopīnātha mukunda mādhaba gāyata e adbhuta guṇī |*
*rāma bāme gobinda garuṛa ādika bāya mardala dhikatā tādhika*
*dhini ni ni ni ni ni bhaṇata narahari bhubana bharu jaya jaya dhuni ||*

*Word for word:* bāsudeba śrībāsa nandana — Vasudeva, Srivasa, Nandana; bijaya bakreśvara nārāyaṇa — Vijaya, Vakreshvara, Narayana; gopīnātha mukunda mādhaba — Gopinatha, Mukunda, Madhava; gāyata — sing; e adbhuta guṇī — these wondrous masters; rāma — Rama; bāme — on the left; gobinda garuṛa ādika — Govinda, Garuda and others; bāya mardala — play the mardala; dhikatā tādhika dhini ni ni — drum syllables; bhaṇata narahari — says Narahari; bhubana bharu jaya jaya dhuni — the world is filled with cries of "jaya, jaya"

**21.4.** Vasudeva, Srivasa, Nandana, Vijaya, Vakreshvara, Narayana,
Gopinatha, Mukunda, Madhava — these wondrous masters sing;
Rama, and on the left Govinda, Garuda and others play the mardala: "dhikata tadhika,
dhini-ni-ni-ni-ni-ni," says Narahari; the world is filled with cries of "jaya, jaya!"[^23-38]

[^23-37]: GPT1 — pp. 360–361, no. 50 ("māyūra"; scan, PDF pp. 619–620); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 50 (catalogue: NG-192 — with the wrong number "no. 57"). BR 12 (ed. 1912,
pp. 885–886; ed. 1960, vv. 2568–2571, "punaḥ — māyūra"): in a series of padas on the kirtana in Srivasa's house. Variants: 21.1 GPT1 "mudita nartabane" (a misprint);
21.3 GPT1 "sanathukhe" (a misprint; on the scan "sammukhe"); 21.4 GPT1 "ghāsudeba" (a misprint), BR-1960 "bāsudeba, prabāsa, nakhana…" (OCR garbled), "rāma bāme garuṛa, gobinda ādi
bāye, mardala dhiki tā tā dhik". Not in the PK, KGC, PS, GCC or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^23-38]: Srivasa's courtyard (Srivasa-angana) is the place of the Lord's night kirtanas in Navadvipa (CB Madhya-khanda; CC Adi 17). The singers and
musicians are the Lord's companions: Vasudeva (Datta or Ghosha), Srivasa, Nandana Acharya, Vijaya Dasa, Vakreshvara Pandita, Narayana, Gopinatha,
Mukunda Datta, Madhava (Ghosha), Rama (Shrirama, Srivasa's brother?), Govinda, Garuda Pandita; "dhikatā tādhika, dhini-ni-ni…" are drum syllables
(bol).

## 22. Narahari — "nācata śacītanaya gaurasundara…" (GPT1 p. 361, no. 51; BR)
*Gaura's dance in the kirtana: the mridangas sound, He sings in a sweet voice; His form from the hair to the feet — flowers in His hair,
earrings, tilaka, brows like bees, a face outshining the moons, His smile, arms like an elephant's trunk, a broad chest with a garland, a slender
waist; His feet shame the morning sun. Raga ashavari. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR; Vrajabuli.*[^23-39]

নাচত শচীতনয় গৌরসুন্দর মনমোহনা ।
বাজত কত কত মৃদঙ্গ উঘটত ধিধিকট ধিলঙ্গ
গায়ত সুর মধুর অঙ্গভঙ্গী পরম শোহনা ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*nācata śacītanaya gaurasundara manamohanā |*
*bājata kata kata mṛdaṅga ughaṭata dhidhikaṭa dhilaṅga*
*gāyata sura madhura aṅgabhaṅgī parama śohanā || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* nācata — dances; śacītanaya — the son of Shachi; gaurasundara — beautiful Gaura; manamohanā — enchanter of hearts; bājata kata kata mṛdaṅga — many mridangas sound; ughaṭata — beating out; dhidhikaṭa dhilaṅga — "dhi-dhikat dhilang"; gāyata sura madhura — sings in a sweet voice; aṅga-bhaṅgī parama śohanā — the bends of His body are wondrously lovely

**22.1.** The son of Shachi dances, beautiful Gaura, enchanter of hearts!
Many mridangas sound, beating out "dhi-dhikat dhilang";
He sings in a sweet voice — the bends of His body are wondrously lovely.

নিরুপম রস উলস আজ বিলসত প্রিয় ভকত-মাঝ
ঝলকত অতি ললিত সাজ যুবতী-ধীরজ-মোচনা ।
কুসুমাঞ্চিত চারু চিকুর কুণ্ডল শ্রুতি গণ্ড মুকুর
ভালতিলক মঞ্জুল ভুরু ভৃঙ্গ কমললোচনা ॥

*nirupama rasa ulasa āja bilasata priya bhakata-mājha*
*jhalakata ati lalita sāja yubatī-dhīraja-mocanā |*
*kusumāñcita cāru cikura kuṇḍala śruti gaṇḍa mukura*
*bhālatilaka mañjula bhuru bhṛṅga kamalalocanā ||*

*Word for word:* nirupama rasa ulasa āja — today an incomparable rasa rejoices; bilasata priya bhakata-mājha — sports among His dear devotees; jhalakata ati lalita sāja — the lovely attire sparkles; yubatī-dhīraja-mocanā — robbing young women of composure; kusumāñcita cāru cikura — beautiful hair adorned with flowers; kuṇḍala śruti — earrings in the ears; gaṇḍa mukura — cheeks like mirrors; bhāla-tilaka — tilaka on the forehead; mañjula bhuru bhṛṅga — lovely brows like bees; kamalalocanā — lotus-eyed

**22.2.** Today an incomparable rasa rejoices: He sports among His dear devotees;
His lovely attire sparkles, robbing young women of their composure;
His beautiful hair is adorned with flowers, earrings in His ears, His cheeks are mirrors,
tilaka on His forehead, His lovely brows are bees above His lotus eyes.

নাসাপুট মোদ-সদন ইন্দুনিকর-নিন্দি বদন
মন্দ মন্দ হসনি কুন্দ-দশন মধুর বোলনা ।
কণ্ঠ মদন-মদভর-হর ভুজযুগ জিনি কুঞ্জরকর
কক্ষ মৃদু বিশাল বক্ষ মাল অতুল দোলনা ॥

*nāsāpuṭa moda-sadana indunikara-nindi badana*
*manda manda hasani kunda-daśana madhura bolanā |*
*kaṇṭha madana-madabhara-hara bhujayuga jini kuñjarakara*
*kakṣa mṛdu biśāla bakṣa māla atula dolanā ||*

*Word for word:* nāsāpuṭa moda-sadana — the nostrils, abode of fragrance; indu-nikara-nindi badana — the face shaming a host of moons; manda manda hasani — the soft smile; kunda-daśana — teeth like jasmine; madhura bolanā — sweet speech; kaṇṭha madana-madabhara-hara — the neck stealing Madana's pride; bhujayuga jini kuñjarakara — arms surpassing an elephant's trunk; kakṣa mṛdu — soft armpits; biśāla bakṣa — a broad chest; māla atula dolanā — an incomparable garland swaying

**22.3.** His nostrils are the abode of fragrance; His face shames a host of moons;
His soft smile, His teeth are jasmine, His speech sweet;
His neck steals Madana's pride; His arms surpass an elephant's trunk;
soft armpits, a broad chest — on it sways an incomparable garland.

নাভি ত্রিবলী-বলিত ভাঁতি লোমাবলী ভুজগ-পাঁতি
রসনা-যুত কৃশ কটি নব কেশরি-মদ-ভঞ্জনা ।
পহিরে বর বসন বেশ উরু বরণি না শকত শেষ
নরহরি-পহুঁ পদতলে করু তরুণারুণ-গঞ্জনা ॥

*nābhi tribalī-balita bhām̐ti lomābalī bhujaga-pām̐ti*
*rasanā-yuta kṛśa kaṭi naba keśari-mada-bhañjanā |*
*pahire bara basana beśa uru baraṇi nā śakata śeṣa*
*narahari-pahum̐ padatale karu taruṇāruṇa-gañjanā ||*

*Word for word:* nābhi tribalī-balita bhām̐ti — the navel shining with three folds; lomābalī bhujaga-pām̐ti — the line of hair like a little snake; rasanā-yuta kṛśa kaṭi — the slender waist with its girdle; naba keśari-mada-bhañjanā — crushing the pride of a young lion; pahire bara basana beśa — clad in beautiful garments; uru baraṇi nā śakata śeṣa — even Shesha cannot describe the thighs; narahari-pahum̐ padatale — the feet of Narahari's Lord; karu taruṇa-aruṇa-gañjanā — shame the young morning sun

**22.4.** His navel shines with three folds, the line of hair is like a little snake;
His slender waist with its girdle crushes the pride of a young lion;
He is clad in beautiful garments; even Shesha cannot describe His thighs;
the feet of Narahari's Lord shame the young morning sun.

[^23-39]: GPT1 — p. 361, no. 51 ("āśābarī"; scan, PDF p. 620); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 51. The catalogue listed it under Vasu Ghosha (VG-057, "5.3 no. 51"), but the
signature is "narahari pahum̐ padatale…": **new row NG-301**, VG-057 corrected. BR 12 (ed. 1912, p. 890; ed. 1960, vv. 2624–2627, "punaḥ — āśābarī"): in the same series of
kirtana padas (preceded by a pada of Govinda Dasa). Variants: 22.1 BR "bhaṅgi parama śohana"; 22.2 BR "yubati-dhiraya-mocanā"; 22.3 GPT1 "kakṣa mṛdu bilāsa bakṣa", BR "kakṣa
mṛdu, biśāla bakṣa" (the BR reading is adopted); 22.4 BR "pahire bara basanabeśa", "taruṇāruṇe gañjanā". Not in the PK, KGC, PS, GCC or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. "Robbing
young women of their composure" is the same formula as in no. 3 (note 7).

---

# Chapter 24. Appendix. Padas signed "Narahari" from the Gaura-pada-tarangini — VIII: Gaura's night sleep; Nityananda

*Continuation of the appendix (the introductory note on the two Naraharis, on the arguments for attribution and on the marks in the headings
is in ch. 17). Chapter 24: the end of GPT section 5.2 "Ashtakaliya" — the songs on Gaura's night sleep (GPT1 pp. 362–365, nos. 55–63, 65: the
companions gaze at the sleeping Lord and do not dare to wake Him), then section 6.1 "Nityananda" (GPT1 pp. 414–439) — all padas signed Narahari
(nos. 10, 26, 64–69, 71–78, 80, 81: the advent at Ekachakra, the first meeting with the Lord, the coming to Gauda, Panihati, Khardaha, the wedding,
praises), with the addition of the pada on Balarama's rasa manifested by Nityananda (section 5.1, no. 44). The signatures in both sections were
checked throughout, in the OCR and on the scan; the Gaura-charita-chintamani (GCC, kiranas 2–4) and the 12th wave of the Bhakti-ratnakara (BR) were
read continuously at the relevant places. Not translated (outside the appendix): 5.2 nos. 54, 64 and 6.1 nos. 6, 11, 19, 70, 79 — signed Ghanashyama;
the other padas of section 6.1 are by other poets (Atmarama, Govinda Dasa, Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa, Lochana, Jnanadasa, Vasu Ghosha, Balarama
Dasa, Kanu Dasa, Raya Ananta and others; some were translated earlier). The base text is GPT1 (doubtful places by the scan), collated with GPT2, the
GCC (ed. 1947), the BR (eds. 1912 and 1960) and the Gita-chandrodaya; the PK, KGC and PS were checked. On the ashtakaliya as eternal lila and on the
Lord's sleep see note 36 of chapter 22. The notes of the GPT editors are not reproduced.*

## 1. Narahari — "ko baraṇaba bara gaura uttāna śayana…" (GPT1 p. 362, section 5.2, no. 55; GCC)
*The end of the night: Gaura sleeps on His back; the poet describes His form — the shining limbs, the face outshining autumn moons, the
earrings, lips, teeth, the necklaces on His chest, the folded hands: as if even in sleep He were pleading with an offended beloved. Raga not
specified ("yathārāga"). **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC; Vrajabuli.*[^24-1]

কো বরণব বর গৌর উত্তান শয়ন শোভা সুখকারী ।
ঝলকত অঙ্গ সুবলিত ললিত থির দামিনী-পুঞ্জ-পুঞ্জ-মদহারী ॥

*ko baraṇaba bara gaura uttāna śayana śobhā sukhakārī |*
*jhalakata aṅga subalita lalita thira dāminī-puñja-puñja-madahārī ||*

*Word for word:* ko — who; baraṇaba — will describe; bara gaura — fair Gaura; uttāna śayana — lying on His back; śobhā — beauty; sukhakārī — delightful; jhalakata — shine; aṅga — limbs; subalita — shapely; lalita — graceful; thira dāminī — steady lightning; puñja-puñja — of hosts; mada-hārī — robbing of pride

**1.1.** Who can describe the delightful beauty of fair Gaura sleeping on His back?
His shapely, graceful limbs shine, robbing hosts of steady lightning of their pride.

শরদ-সুধাকর-নিকর বিনির্জিত যুবতী-বিজয় মুখ মধুরিম জ্যোতি ।
শ্রুতি অতি বিমল গণ্ড মণ্ডিত নব কুণ্ডল অতুল জড়িত মণি মোতি ॥

*śarada-sudhākara-nikara binirjita yubatī-bijaya mukha madhurima jyoti |*
*śruti ati bimala gaṇḍa maṇḍita naba kuṇḍala atula jaṛita maṇi moti ||*

*Word for word:* śarada-sudhākara-nikara — hosts of autumn moons; binirjita — defeated; yubatī-bijaya — conquering young maidens; mukha — of the face; madhurima jyoti — sweet light; śruti — ears; ati bimala gaṇḍa — clear cheeks; maṇḍita — adorned; naba kuṇḍala — with new earrings; atula — matchless; jaṛita maṇi moti — set with gems and pearls

**1.2.** The sweet light of His face, which conquers young maidens, defeats hosts of autumn moons;
His ears and clear cheeks are adorned with new earrings, matchless, set with gems and pearls.

বিম্ব অরুণ-কর-কদন বদন-ছদ কিঞ্চিদ মিলন রুচির রুচিপূর ।
বিকসত দন্তকিরণ সিত সুন্দর তারকবৃন্দ কুন্দ রহু দূর ॥

*bimba aruṇa-kara-kadana badana-chada kiñcida milana rucira rucipūra |*
*bikasata dantakiraṇa sita sundara tārakabṛnda kunda rahu dūra ||*

*Word for word:* bimba — the bimba fruit; aruṇa-kara — the rays of dawn; kadana — putting to shame; badana-chada — lips; kiñcida milana — slightly closed; rucira — lovely; ruci-pūra — full of radiance; bikasata — gleams; danta-kiraṇa — the light of the teeth; sita sundara — white, beautiful; tāraka-bṛnda — stars; kunda — jasmine; rahu dūra — stay far away

**1.3.** His lips, putting to shame the bimba fruit and the rays of dawn, are slightly closed, lovely, full of radiance;
the white, beautiful light of His teeth gleams — the stars and the jasmine stay far behind.

প্রসর বক্ষ পরি হার প্রচুর তহি কর করযুক্ত লসত অনিবার ।
নরহরি ভণ অনুভব ন হোত বুঝি মানিনী নিকট করত পরিহার ॥

*prasara bakṣa pari hāra pracura tahi kara karayukta lasata anibāra |*
*narahari bhaṇa anubhaba na hota bujhi māninī nikaṭa karata parihāra ||*

*Word for word:* prasara bakṣa pari — on the broad chest; hāra pracura — many necklaces; tahi — there; kara kara-yukta — hands joined palm to palm; lasata anibāra — rest unmoving; narahari bhaṇa — Narahari says; anubhaba na hota — cannot be grasped; bujhi — surely; māninī nikaṭa — before an offended beloved; karata parihāra — pleads

**1.4.** On His broad chest are many necklaces, and on it His hands, joined palm to palm, rest unmoving.
Narahari says: this cannot be grasped — surely He is pleading before an offended beloved.[^24-2]

[^24-1]: GPT1 — p. 362, section 5.2 "Ashtakaliya", no. 55 ("yathārāga"; scan, PDF p. 621); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 55, p. ≈233–234 (catalogue: NG-193,
"5.3" — wrongly). GCC — kirana 2 (the "pastimes on the couch" in the last part of the night), pada 18: before it Gadadhara, waking first, serves the
Lord's feet, and He turns onto His back (padas 15–16); then comes a pada of Ghanashyama (GPT no. 54) and this one. Readings: 1.1 GCC "bara gaura
sarasa uttāna śayana"; "dāminī-puñja" ("of lightning") — GPT1 and GPT2 "yāminī puñja" ("of nights"), a misprint; the GCC reading is adopted; 1.4 GCC
"anubhaba na hota" (GPT "anubhava nohata"). Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS, Gita-chandrodaya. B. On the ashtakaliya and on the Lord's sleep see note 36
of chapter 22.
[^24-2]: The Lord's sleep is not the sleep of a conditioned soul: He is absorbed in the lilas of Vraja and, in the mood of Krishna, pleads in sleep
with Radha who is in mana (offended pride) — the folded hands betray His inner mood (cf. in the same kirana of the GCC, pada 13: in sleep Gaura calls
upon "the crown of beautiful women" to wake). "Which conquers young maidens" is a stock formula of the lyric on Krishna's all-attractive beauty (cf.
note 7 of chapter 23); here it refers to Gaura as Krishna Himself.

## 2. Narahari — "ki kahaba gaura śayana anupāma…" (GPT1 pp. 362–363, no. 56; GCC)
*Gaura's matchless sleep: His limbs shine like Kama embodied; His body is soft as fresh butter — it seems to melt on the couch; His
breathing gently lifts His belly, as the Malaya wind stirs the waves of a river on Sumeru. The poet prays that the Lord may so rest on the
couch of his heart. Raga lalita. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC; Vrajabuli.*[^24-3]

কি কহব গৌর শয়ন অনুপাম ।
সুবলিত অঙ্গ অঙ্গ ঝলকত জনু বিলসিত সোই মূরতিময় কাম ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*ki kahaba gaura śayana anupāma |*
*subalita aṅga aṅga jhalakata janu bilasita soi mūratimaya kāma || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* ki kahaba — what shall I say; gaura śayana — of Gaura's sleep; anupāma — matchless; subalita aṅga aṅga — each shapely limb; jhalakata — shines; janu — as if; bilasita — displayed his play; soi — himself; muratimaya kāma — Kama in visible form

**2.1.** What shall I say of Gaura's matchless sleep!
Each of His shapely limbs shines — as if Kama himself, in visible form, were displaying his play here.

কনক-ক্ষীরোদদধি মন্থন নব নবনী-পিণ্ডসম কোমল কায় ।
অতি অপরূপ ইহ তপনতাপ বিনু শেজ উপরি জনু জাত মিলায় ॥

*kanaka-kṣīrodadadhi manthana naba nabanī-piṇḍasama komala kāya |*
*ati aparūpa iha tapanatāpa binu śeja upari janu jāta milāya ||*

*Word for word:* kanaka-kṣīroda-dadhi — a golden ocean of milk; manthana — churned from; naba nabanī-piṇḍa-sama — like a lump of fresh butter; komala kāya — soft body; ati aparūpa iha — wonder of wonders; tapana-tāpa binu — without the sun's heat; śeja upari — on the couch; janu — as if; jāta milāya — melts away

**2.2.** His body is soft as a lump of fresh butter churned from a golden ocean of milk;
and, wonder of wonders, without the sun's heat it seems to melt upon the couch.

অলসে অবশ মৃদু চলত নিশাসহি উচ নীচ হোয়ত উদর উজোর ।
মলয় পবন জনু পরশ সুমেরুসু সরিত তরঙ্গ বহত বহু থোর ॥

*alase abaśa mṛdu calata niśāsahi uca nīca hoyata udara ujora |*
*malaya pabana janu paraśa sumerusu sarita taraṅga bahata bahu thora ||*

*Word for word:* alase — in languor; abaśa — limp; mṛdu calata niśāsahi — breathing softly; uca nīca hoyata — rises and falls; udara ujora — the radiant belly; malaya pabana — the Malaya wind; janu — as if; paraśa — touching; sumerusu — Sumeru; sarita taraṅga — the river's waves; bahata — drives; bahu thora — gentle, small

**2.3.** Languid, limp, He breathes softly, and His radiant belly rises and falls —
as if the Malaya wind, touching Sumeru, drove the quiet waves of its river.

বচনক দূর বিরচব কৌন পুনি নিরখত নয়ন তৃপিত নহি হোয় ।
নরহরি ভণ মঝু হৃদয়-তল্প কব বিলসব ঐছে দেয়ব সুখ মোয় ॥

*bacanaka dūra biracaba kauna puni nirakhata nayana tṛpita nahi hoya |*
*narahari bhaṇa majhu hṛdaya-talpa kaba bilasaba aiche deyaba sukha moya ||*

*Word for word:* bacanaka dūra — beyond words; biracaba kauna — who will compose; puni — and; nirakhata nayana — the eyes, gazing; tṛpita nahi hoya — are not sated; narahari bhaṇa — Narahari says; majhu hṛdaya-talpa — on the couch of my heart; kaba — when; bilasaba aiche — will so recline; deyaba sukha moya — will give me joy

**2.4.** Words cannot convey it — who could compose it? However long one looks, the eyes are never sated.
Narahari says: when will He so recline on the couch of my heart and give me joy?[^24-4]

[^24-3]: GPT1 — pp. 362–363, no. 56 ("lalita"; scan, PDF pp. 621–622); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 56, p. ≈234 (catalogue: NG-194). GCC — kirana 2, pada 7
("lalita rāga"; preceded by a description of the chamber and the couch). Readings: 2.2 GCC "kṣīrododadhi" ("ocean of milk"; GPT "kṣīroda dadhi"); 2.4 GCC
"biracaba" (GPT1 "viracana"). Under line 2.3 GPT1 has an editor's note on the reading "bilāse" (not reproduced). Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS. B.
[^24-4]: The comparison with Kama (Manmatha) is a common image of the poetry on Krishna; but Krishna is "the Manmatha of Manmatha himself", who
enchants even the god of love (Bhag. 10.32.2), and Gaura's beauty is not mundane: the poet prays not for anything sensual but that the Lord may
reign in his heart. Sumeru is the golden mountain — an image of Gaura's golden body.

## 3. Narahari — "ki kaba analpa talpa jhalakata ati…" (GPT1 p. 363, no. 57; GCC)
*Gaura's couch: spacious, spotless as autumn, fashioned by Kama himself; the white pillows are like blocks of Kailasa and the stilled
waves of the Ganga; heaps of flowers, a painted canopy of moonbeams, a silver frame set with gold and gems. Raga lalita. **Attribution:
probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC; Vrajabuli (the text is obscure in places).*[^24-5]

কি কব অনল্প তল্প ঝলকত অতি শরদ কাল সম বিরহিত মলিনা ।
সুরপতি-স্বপন-অগোচর অপরূপ রচিত মনোজ্ঞ মনোভব বলিনা ॥

*ki kaba analpa talpa jhalakata ati śarada kāla sama birahita malinā |*
*surapati-svapana-agocara aparūpa racita manojña manobhaba balinā ||*

*Word for word:* ki kaba — what shall I say; analpa talpa — the spacious couch; jhalakata ati — shines beyond measure; śarada kāla sama — like the autumn season; birahita malinā — free of stain; surapati-svapana-agocara — beyond the dreams of the king of the gods; aparūpa — wondrous; racita — fashioned; manojña — charming; manobhaba balinā — by mighty Manobhava (Kama)

**3.1.** What shall I say! The spacious couch shines beyond measure, spotless as the autumn season;
wondrous, beyond even the dreams of the king of the gods, a charming work of mighty Manobhava.

আলস-ধর জন-লালস-কর বর বালিস বিলসত জগত অদৃশ রে ।
হরগিরি-খণ্ড অখণ্ড সদ্য দধি-পিণ্ড গঙ্গ-থির-তরঙ্গ সদৃশ রে ॥

*ālasa-dhara jana-lālasa-kara bara bālisa bilasata jagata adṛśa re |*
*haragiri-khaṇḍa akhaṇḍa sadya dadhi-piṇḍa gaṅga-thira-taraṅga sadṛśa re ||*

*Word for word:* ālasa-dhara — full of languor; jana-lālasa-kara — awakening desire in people; bara bālisa — lovely pillows; bilasata — shine; jagata adṛśa — unlike anything in the world; haragiri-khaṇḍa — blocks of Hara's mountain; akhaṇḍa — whole; sadya dadhi-piṇḍa — lumps of fresh curd; gaṅga-thira-taraṅga — the stilled waves of the Ganga; sadṛśa — like

**3.2.** Lovely pillows, full of languor and awakening desire, shine — there is nothing like them in the world:
like blocks of Hara's mountain, whole lumps of fresh curd, the stilled waves of the Ganga.

তহি বন্ধুরে করবীর কুন্দ কেতকী কনকাব্জ জাতী কৃতনয়না ।
তনু অব যব সব সুমনগণ ঝটিত অনুভব ন হোই গৌরহরি-শয়না ॥

*tahi bandhure karabīra kunda ketakī kanakābja jātī kṛtanayanā |*
*tanu aba yaba saba sumanagaṇa jhaṭita anubhaba na hoi gaurahari-śayanā ||*

*Word for word:* tahi — on it; bandhure — in heaps; karabīra, kunda, ketakī — karavira, kunda, ketaki; kanakābja — golden lotuses; jātī — jasmine; kṛta-nayanā — arranged (?); tanu — tender; aba yaba saba sumanagaṇa — when all the flowers; jhaṭita — are strewn (?); anubhaba na hoi — one cannot tell; gaurahari-śayanā — that it is Gaurahari's couch

**3.3.** On it, in heaps — karavira, kunda, ketaki, golden lotuses, jasmine;
and when all their tender flowers are strewn, one can no longer tell that this is Gaurahari's couch.

বুঝি শশী-কর-পটে বিরচি চিত্র বিহি মন্দির দেবে দেওল বহু যতনে ।
নরহরি ভণব সুমতি উরথিত ইহ রজত-চতুষ্কি জটিত হেম রতনে ॥

*bujhi śaśī-kara-paṭe biraci citra bihi mandira debe deola bahu yatane |*
*narahari bhaṇaba sumati urathita iha rajata-catuṣki jaṭita hema ratane ||*

*Word for word:* bujhi — as if; śaśī-kara-paṭe — on a cloth of moonbeams; biraci citra — painting pictures; bihi — the Creator; mandira — into the chamber; debe — of the Lord (?); deola — brought; bahu yatane — with great care; narahari bhaṇaba — Narahari will say; sumati urathita — rises beautifully (?); iha — this; rajata-catuṣki — a silver frame; jaṭita hema ratane — studded with gold and gems

**3.4.** It is as if the Creator painted pictures on a cloth of moonbeams and with great care brought it into the Lord's chamber;
Narahari will say: this couch rises on a silver frame studded with gold and gems.[^24-6]

[^24-5]: GPT1 — p. 363, no. 57 ("lalita"; scan, PDF p. 622); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 57, p. ≈234 (catalogue: NG-195). GCC — kirana 2, pada 8 ("yathārāga";
right after no. 56). Readings: 3.2 GCC "ālasa-dhara jana lālasa-kara bara bālisa" (GPT "ālasa dhara jala lālasa karabara bālisa"; translated after the
GCC: "… awakening desire in people"); 3.3 GCC "bandhuṇa", "kṛta nayana", "sumanagaṇa" (GPT "bandhure", "kṛtanayanā", "samana gana"); 3.4 GCC "deyala",
"bhaṇaba sumati" (the sense of "sumati urathita" is unclear; taken as "rises beautifully"). Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS. B.
[^24-6]: Manobhava ("born of the mind") is Kama: the Lord's couch is the matchless furnishing of His eternal chamber; yet even in this sumptuous picture
"Gaura-Hari" is Krishna Himself, not a worldly prince. Hara's mountain is Kailasa, the white abode of Shiva; curd and the waves of the Ganga are
images of whiteness.

## 4. Narahari — "mari mari gaura-mūrati aparūpa…" (GPT1 p. 363, no. 58; GCC)
*One of the companions, looking at the sleeping Lord: wondrous is Gaura's form; alas that I have only two eyes; I keep this treasure in my
heart; every morning I see Him, but I have never seen such sleep — shall I wake Him today? Raga vibhasa. **Attribution: probably
Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC; Vrajabuli.*[^24-7]

মরি মরি গৌর-মূরতি অপরূপ । ভুবন-বিমোহন মনমথ-ভূপ ॥

*mari mari gaura-mūrati aparūpa | bhubana-bimohana manamatha-bhūpa ||*

*Word for word:* mari mari — ah, ah; gaura-mūrati — Gaura's form; aparūpa — wondrous; bhubana-bimohana — enchanter of the world; manamatha-bhūpa — king Manmatha

**4.1.** Ah, ah! Wondrous is Gaura's form — the enchanter of the world, king Manmatha.

কি করব অগণিত নয়ন না ভেল । দারুণ দৈব দরশে দুখ দেল ॥

*ki karaba agaṇita nayana nā bhela | dāruṇa daiba daraśe dukha dela ||*

*Word for word:* ki karaba — what can I do; agaṇita nayana — countless eyes; nā bhela — were not given; dāruṇa daiba — cruel fate; daraśe — in letting me see; dukha dela — gave grief

**4.2.** What can I do — I was not given countless eyes! Cruel fate, letting me see Him, gave me grief as well.

রাখি হৃদয় ভরি ইহ অভিলাষ । অমূল রতন সম না করি প্রকাশ ॥

*rākhi hṛdaya bhari iha abhilāṣa | amūla ratana sama nā kari prakāśa ||*

*Word for word:* rākhi — I keep; hṛdaya bhari — filling the heart; iha abhilāṣa — this longing; amūla ratana sama — like a priceless jewel; nā kari prakāśa — I do not reveal

**4.3.** I keep this longing, filling my heart with it; like a priceless jewel I reveal it to no one.

কৌনে গঢ়ল তনু-বলনি সুঠাম । মঝু সরবস এ জগতে অনুপাম ॥

*kaune gaṛhala tanu-balani suṭhāma | majhu sarabasa e jagate anupāma ||*

*Word for word:* kaune gaṛhala — who sculpted; tanu-balani — the body, the frame; suṭhāma — graceful; majhu sarabasa — all my wealth; e jagate anupāma — matchless in this world

**4.4.** Who sculpted His body, this graceful frame? It is all my wealth, matchless in the world.

অনুদিন রজনীশেষে হাম পেখি । ঐছন শয়ন কবহুঁ নাহি দেখি ॥

*anudina rajanīśeṣe hāma pekhi | aichana śayana kabahum̐ nāhi dekhi ||*

*Word for word:* anudina — every day; rajanī-śeṣe — at the end of the night; hāma pekhi — I see; aichana śayana — such sleep; kabahum̐ nāhi dekhi — I have never seen

**4.5.** Every day at the end of the night I see Him, but such sleep I have never seen.

তাহে বুঝলুঁ নব ঘুম বিরাজ । নরহরি ইথে কি জাগাওব আজ ॥

*tāhe bujhalum̐ naba ghuma birāja | narahari ithe ki jāgāoba āja ||*

*Word for word:* tāhe — therefore; bujhalum̐ — I understand; naba ghuma — a new sleep; birāja — reigns; narahari — Narahari; ithe — then; ki jāgāoba — shall I wake; āja — now

**4.6.** So I understand: a new, unheard-of sleep reigns. Narahari: shall I wake Him now?[^24-8]

[^24-7]: GPT1 — p. 363, no. 58 ("bibhāsa"; scan, PDF p. 622); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 58, p. ≈234 (catalogue: NG-196). GCC — kirana 3 ("the awakening"), pada 4
("ko 'pi ca — bibhāṣa rāgeṇa", "and another [said] in raga vibhasa"): after a pada describing the sleeper (3.3) the GCC puts padas 4–7 into the
mouths of various companions who have come to the Lord's chamber at dawn. The readings differ insignificantly (4.5 GCC "kavahi"). Not in the BR, PK,
KGC, PS. B.
[^24-8]: "King Manmatha" — cf. note 4. Hiding one's love (4.3) is a mark of mature prema: the devotee does not display his feeling. "A new sleep":
the Lord is absorbed in lila more deeply than usual; the companion hesitates to wake Him, not daring to interrupt His bliss.

## 5. Narahari — "dhani dhani āju rajanī dhani lekhi…" (GPT1 p. 363, no. 59; GCC)
*Another companion: blessed is this night! The Lord, greedy for sankirtana, did not close His eyes at night, speaking of Vraja in His former
mood — and now He has sunk into a matchless sleep and speaks nectarean words in it; it is already dawn, and He does not wake. Raga bhairava.
**Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC; Vrajabuli.*[^24-9]

ধনি ধনি আজু রজনী ধনি লেখি ।
সংকীর্তন-রস-লম্পট পহুঁ কর ঐছন শয়ন কবহিঁ নাহি দেখি ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*dhani dhani āju rajanī dhani lekhi |*
*saṃkīrtana-rasa-lampaṭa pahum̐ kara aichana śayana kabahim̐ nāhi dekhi || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* dhani dhani — blessed, blessed; āju rajanī — this night; dhani lekhi — I count blessed; saṅkīrtana-rasa-lampaṭa — greedy for the rasa of sankirtana; pahum̐ kara — of the Lord; aichana śayana — such sleep; kabahim̐ nāhi dekhi — I have never seen

**5.1.** Blessed, blessed — I count this night blessed!
Such sleep of the Lord, greedy for the rasa of sankirtana, I have never seen.

যো নিজ পূরুব ভাব-ভরে উনমত অনুক্ষণ ভণই সুব্রজপুর-বাত ।
লোচন পলক অলপ নাহি লাগত যামিনী জাগি করত পরভাত ॥

*yo nija pūruba bhāba-bhare unamata anukṣaṇa bhaṇai subrajapura-bāta |*
*locana palaka alapa nāhi lāgata yāminī jāgi karata parabhāta ||*

*Word for word:* yo — he who; nija pūruba bhāba-bhare — by His own former bhava; unamata — maddened; anukṣaṇa — ceaselessly; bhaṇai — speaks; subrajapura-bāta — of lovely Vraja; locana palaka — the eyelids; alapa nāhi lāgata — do not close even for a moment; yāminī jāgi — waking through the night; karata parabhāta — meets the dawn

**5.2.** He who, maddened by His own former bhava, ceaselessly speaks of lovely Vraja —
whose eyelids do not close even for a moment, who stays awake all night and so meets the dawn —

সো অব অতুল নিঁদ গত অতিশয় জাগব কিয়ে অরু অধিক বিলাস ।
অদ্ভুত ঘুমক রীত স্বপন সম অমিয় সদৃশ করু বচন প্রকাশ ॥

*so aba atula nim̐da gata atiśaya jāgaba kiye aru adhika bilāsa |*
*adbhuta ghumaka rīta svapana sama amiya sadṛśa karu bacana prakāśa ||*

*Word for word:* so — He; aba — now; atula nim̐da — into matchless sleep; gata atiśaya — has sunk deeply; jāgaba kiye — will He wake; aru adhika bilāsa — or is it a greater play; adbhuta ghumaka rīta — wondrous is the way of sleep; svapana sama — as in a dream; amiya sadṛśa — like nectar; karu bacana prakāśa — utters words

**5.3.** He has now sunk into a matchless, deep sleep: will He wake — or is this a still greater play?
Wondrous is the way of His sleep: as if in a dream, He utters words like nectar.

নিশি চলি যাও প্রাত ভেল উপনীত তবহি ন জাগত নদীয়া-বিহারী ।
বুঝবি কি নরহরি-নাথ-চরিত ইহ ঘুমক ভাগব বলি নাহি পারি ॥

*niśi cali yāo prāta bhela upanīta tabahi na jāgata nadīyā-bihārī |*
*bujhabi ki narahari-nātha-carita iha ghumaka bhāgaba bali nāhi pāri ||*

*Word for word:* niśi cali yāo — the night has gone; prāta bhela upanīta — morning has come; tabahi na jāgata — still does not wake; nadīyā-bihārī — He who sports in Nadia; bujhabi ki — how can one grasp; narahari-nātha-carita iha — this deed of Narahari's Lord; ghumaka bhāgaba — whether the sleep will break; bali nāhi pāri — I cannot say

**5.4.** The night has gone, the morning has come — and He who sports in Nadia still does not wake.
How can one grasp this deed of Narahari's Lord? I cannot even say whether this sleep will break.[^24-10]

[^24-9]: GPT1 — p. 363, no. 59 ("bhairava"; scan, PDF p. 622); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 59, p. ≈234 (catalogue: NG-197). GCC — kirana 3, pada 5 ("ko 'pi ca —
bhairaba rāga"). Readings: 5.3 GPT1 and GPT2 "adbhuta ghuma karīta" — a wrong word division; the GCC reading "ghumaka rīta" ("the way of sleep") is
adopted; 5.4 GCC "bujhaba". Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS. B.
[^24-10]: "Former bhava" is the mood of Vraja: the Lord, Krishna Himself, in the mood of Radha and the gopis, does not sleep at night, speaking of Vraja
and of Krishna (cf. CC Antya 14–19: the Lord's nights in the Gambhira). The word "maddened" (unamata) refers to the madness of prema, not to anything
mundane. His sleep too is lila, "a still greater play": in sleep He utters words full of the rasa of Vraja (cf. no. 1 of chapter 23).

## 6. Narahari — "pekhaha aparūpa pahum̐ka bilāsa…" (GPT1 pp. 363–364, no. 60; GCC)
*Another companion: behold the Lord's wondrous sleep! He whose radiance is not revealed even in the hearts of the gods shines in this
chamber brighter than suns; sages perform sacrifices for ages to imagine Him on the couch of their hearts — and here He is easily
reached; it is not the praises of Brahma and Shiva that please the Lord but the words of the parrot in its cage — the custom of Vraja
returns. Raga lalita. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC; Vrajabuli.*[^24-11]

পেখহ অপরূপ পহুঁক বিলাস ।
শয়ন সুছন্দ অমন্দ মধুর উপজাওত তনু-মন-নয়ন-উলাস ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*pekhaha aparūpa pahum̐ka bilāsa |*
*śayana suchanda amanda madhura upajāota tanu-mana-nayana-ulāsa || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* pekhaha — behold; aparūpa — the wondrous; pahum̐ka bilāsa — play of the Lord; śayana — sleep; suchanda — lovely; amanda — boundless; madhura — sweet; upajāota — gives rise to; tanu-mana-nayana-ulāsa — joy of body, mind and eyes

**6.1.** Behold the wondrous play of the Lord!
His sleep — lovely, boundless, sweet — gives rise to the joy of body, mind and eyes.

যাকর তনুরুচি কিঞ্চিৎ সুরহিয়ে নহ পরকাশ যতন কত ভাঁতি ।
সো রুচিপুঞ্জ সুকৃতি ইহ মন্দির-মাঝ ঝলকে জিনি দিনকর-পাঁতি ॥

*yākara tanuruci kiñcit surahiye naha parakāśa yatana kata bhām̐ti |*
*so rucipuñja sukṛti iha mandira-mājha jhalake jini dinakara-pām̐ti ||*

*Word for word:* yākara tanu-ruci — whose bodily radiance; kiñcit — even a glimpse; sura-hiye — in the hearts of the gods; naha parakāśa — is not revealed; yatana kata bhām̐ti — however many efforts; so ruci-puñja — that mass of radiance; sukṛti — by good fortune; iha mandira-mājha — in this chamber; jhalake — shines; jini dinakara-pām̐ti — outdoing rows of suns

**6.2.** He, a glimpse of whose bodily radiance is not revealed in the hearts of the gods, however great their effort —
that mass of radiance, by good fortune, shines in this chamber, outdoing rows of suns.

মুনিগণ-হৃদয়-সুতলপে কলপয়িতে করু কত কলপ কলপ ভরি যাগ ।
তাকর দুলভ সুলভ এ তলপ পরিকলপন কবি কি রচব অছু ভাগ ॥

*munigaṇa-hṛdaya-sutalape kalapayite karu kata kalapa kalapa bhari yāga |*
*tākara dulabha sulabha e talapa parikalapana kabi ki racaba achu bhāga ||*

*Word for word:* munigaṇa-hṛdaya-sutalape — on the fine couch of the sages' hearts; kalapayite — to imagine; karu kata kalapa kalapa bhari yāga — perform sacrifices kalpa after kalpa; tākara dulabha — hard for them to reach; sulabha — easily found; e talapa — on this couch; parikalapana — the description; kabi ki racaba — what poet can compose; achu bhāga — its good fortune

**6.3.** To imagine Him on the fine couch of their hearts, sages perform sacrifices kalpa after kalpa —
and on this couch He, so hard for them to reach, is easily found: what poet can describe this couch's good fortune?

বিহি ভব বচনে হরষ নহ অব নব পিঞ্জরে শুক বহু ভণ শুনি প্রীত ।
নরহরি-নাথ গুপত কত করব সুপ্রকট হোত উহ পূরবক রীত ॥

*bihi bhaba bacane haraṣa naha aba naba piñjare śuka bahu bhaṇa śuni prīta |*
*narahari-nātha gupata kata karaba suprakaṭa hota uha pūrabaka rīta ||*

*Word for word:* bihi bhaba bacane — in the words of Brahma and Shiva; haraṣa naha — no joy; aba — now; naba piñjare śuka — the parrot in the new cage; bahu bhaṇa — speaks much; śuni prīta — hearing, pleased; narahari-nātha — the poet Narahari's Lord; gupata kata karaba — how long will He stay hidden; suprakaṭa hota — plainly shows itself; uha pūrabaka rīta — that former custom

**6.4.** The words of Brahma and Shiva do not gladden Him now — yet He listens with love to the parrot in its new cage, chattering on.
How long will the poet Narahari's Lord stay hidden? His former custom is plainly showing itself.[^24-12]

[^24-11]: GPT1 — pp. 363–364, no. 60 ("lalita"; scan, PDF pp. 622–623); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 60, p. 235. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-302). GCC —
kirana 3, pada 6 ("ko 'pi ca — rāga lalita"). Readings: 6.2 GPT1 "suruci puñja sukṛti iha mandira mājha" — GCC and GPT2 "so rucipuñja" (adopted); 6.4 GCC
"suprakaṭa". Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS. B.
[^24-12]: Brahma and Shiva glorify the Lord with hymns, but the confidential lila is open not to them but to the companions of Navadvipa. The parrot is the
one who, according to the GCC, was reared by a servant of the Lord and sings the awakening songs at dawn (chapter 22, note 35): in Vraja Vrinda's
parrots wake Radha and Krishna — the "former custom" of Vraja reveals itself in Navadvipa. The sages "imagine" the Lord on the couch of the heart —
an image of meditation: what is not reached by yoga is revealed in love.

## 7. Narahari — "hera cāñā dekha rajanī pāne…" (GPT1 p. 364, no. 61; GCC)
*Another companion: look — who ever knew such sleep? The pose of the hands and feet, the eyes, the moon-face, the smile that seems to drip
nectar; one cannot tell whether He sleeps or wakes; it will be hard to wake Him. Raga vibhasa. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** —
the pada is in the GCC.*[^24-13]

হের চাঞা দেখ রজনী পানে । এরূপ শয়ন কেবা বা জানে ॥

*hera cāñā dekha rajanī pāne | erūpa śayana kebā bā jāne ||*

*Word for word:* hera — here; cāñā dekha — look, see; rajanī pāne — at the night; erūpa śayana — such sleep; kebā vā jāne — who ever knew

**7.1.** Here, look, see this night: who ever knew such sleep?

কিবা করপদ-ভঙ্গিমাখানি । ঘুমে কি এরূপ কভু না জানি ॥

*kibā karapada-bhaṅgimākhāni | ghume ki erūpa kabhu nā jāni ||*

*Word for word:* kibā — how lovely; karapada-bhaṅgimā-khāni — the pose of hands and feet; ghume — in sleep; ki erūpa — can it be so; kabhu nā jāni — I never knew

**7.2.** How beautifully His hands and feet lie! I never knew that sleep could be like this.

লোচন সুভাঁতি ভঙ্গিমা তাহে । অলসে এমতি হইবে কাহে ॥

*locana subhām̐ti bhaṅgimā tāhe | alase emati haibe kāhe ||*

*Word for word:* locana — the eyes; subhām̐ti bhaṅgimā — charmingly closed; tāhe — and then; alase — in languor; emati haibe kāhe — how can it be like this

**7.3.** And the eyes — so charmingly closed: how can languor be like this?

মুখ-শশিশোভা অধিক হেন । মৃদু হাসি সুধা খসিছে যেন ॥

*mukha-śaśiśobhā adhika hena | mṛdu hāsi sudhā khasiche yena ||*

*Word for word:* mukha-śaśi-śobhā — the beauty of the moon-face; adhika hena — greater still; mṛdu hāsi — from the gentle smile; sudhā khasiche yena — as if nectar dripped

**7.4.** The beauty of His moon-face is greater still: as if nectar dripped from His gentle smile.

নিঁদ অনিঁদ না চিনিতে পারি । মনে যাহা তাহা কহিতে না পারি ॥

*nim̐da anim̐da nā cinite pāri | mane yāhā tāhā kahite nā pāri ||*

*Word for word:* nim̐da anim̐da — sleep or no sleep; nā cinite pāri — I cannot tell; mane yāhā — what is in the heart; tāhā kahite nā pāri — I cannot utter

**7.5.** I cannot tell whether He sleeps or not; what is in my heart I cannot utter.

নরহরি ইথে কত বা কবে । বুঝি জাগাইতে বিষম হবে ॥

*narahari ithe kata bā kabe | bujhi jāgāite biṣama habe ||*

*Word for word:* narahari — Narahari; ithe — of this; kata vā kabe — how much can say; bujhi — it seems; jāgāite — to wake; biṣama habe — will be hard

**7.6.** How much can Narahari say of it? It seems it will be hard to wake Him.[^24-14]

[^24-13]: GPT1 — p. 364, no. 61 ("bibhāsa"; scan, PDF p. 623); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 61, p. 235 (catalogue: NG-198). GCC — kirana 3, pada 7 ("ko 'pi ca — rāga
lalita"; the GCC edition notes that the Agartala manuscript lacks this pada). Readings: 7.1 GCC "hera cāya dekha gaurāṅga pāne" ("look at Gauranga";
GPT "rajanī pāne", "at the night"); 7.2 GCC "kara-pada-bhaṅgimā", "kabhu"; 7.3 GCC "subhagati"; 7.5 GCC "kahite nāri". Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS. B.
[^24-14]: The Lord's sleep cannot be told from waking: it is not the unconsciousness of a conditioned soul but absorption in lila (cf. 5.3: "or is this a
still greater play?").

## 8. Narahari — "gorācām̐dera rajanī śayana…" (GPT1 p. 364, no. 62; GCC)
*The companions gaze at the sleeping Gorachand, and their eyes are refreshed; joyful, they banter with one another and again and again
admire His sleep. Raga vibhasa. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC.*[^24-15]

গোরাচাঁদের রজনী-শয়ন । হেরি হেরি সভে জুড়ায় নয়ন ॥

*gorācām̐dera rajanī-śayana | heri heri sabhe juṛāya nayana ||*

*Word for word:* gorācām̐dera — of Gorachand; rajanī-śayana — night sleep; heri heri — gazing and gazing; sabhe — all; juṛāya nayana — refresh their eyes

**8.1.** Gorachand's night sleep: gazing and gazing at it, everyone's eyes find rest.

পরস্পর অতি আনন্দ হৃদয় । কত ভাঁতি কথা কৌতুকে কহয় ॥

*paraspara ati ānanda hṛdaya | kata bhām̐ti kathā kautuke kahaya ||*
