*Word for word:* paraspara — to one another; ati ānanda hṛdaya — the heart full of joy; kata bhām̐ti kathā — many things; kautuke kahaya — they tell playfully

**8.2.** Each one's heart is full of joy, and playfully they tell one another many things.

তাহা কি রচিতে পারে কবিজন । অনুপম গৌরাঙ্গের গুণগণ ॥

*tāhā ki racite pāre kabijana | anupama gaurāṅgera guṇagaṇa ||*

*Word for word:* tāhā — that; ki racite pāre — can describe; kabijana — a poet; anupama — matchless; gaurāṅgera guṇagaṇa — the virtues of Gauranga

**8.3.** Can a poet describe it — the matchless virtues of Gauranga?

পুন পুন নিরিখয়ে আঁখি ভরি । নরহরি-পহুঁ-শয়ন-মাধুরী ॥

*puna puna nirikhaye ām̐khi bhari | narahari-pahum̐-śayana-mādhurī ||*

*Word for word:* puna puna — again and again; nirikhaye — they gaze; ām̐khi bhari — with full eyes; narahari-pahum̐ — the poet Narahari's Lord; śayana-mādhurī — the sweetness of sleep

**8.4.** Again and again, with full eyes, they gaze at the sweetness of the sleep of the poet Narahari's Lord.[^24-16]

[^24-15]: GPT1 — p. 364, no. 62 ("bibhāsa"; scan, PDF p. 623); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 62, p. 235 (catalogue: NG-199). GCC — kirana 3, pada 9 ("yathārāga"; before it,
pada 8: Gadadhara sits at the Lord's feet and presses them, while Narahari "floats in an ocean of happiness"). Readings: 8.1 GCC "gaurāṅga cāndera rajani-śayana";
8.2 GCC "ati ānanda hṛdaya". The search of the witnesses had missed it (distorted OCR of the GCC); found by reading the GCC continuously. Not in the BR, PK,
KGC, PS. B.
[^24-16]: "Playfully they tell" — the companions' loving talk about the Lord; it too is part of His lila (cf. chapter 23, no. 5: the companions honour one
another).

## 9. Narahari — "kibā se niśira śobhā…" (GPT1 pp. 364–365, no. 63; GCC)
*Night in Nadia: the moon has washed the town, the trees blossom, a cool wind blows, all the inhabitants sleep in bliss; around the Lord's
chamber are His dear companions, some asleep, some awake; others have gone home at His bidding and pine. The poet prays to be near at this
hour. Raga bhairava. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC (it opens the nishanta-lila).*[^24-17]

কিবা সে নিশির শোভা শুভরাশি পূরা সে নদীয়াপুর ।
রজনীকর-রজক নিজ করে করিল মলিনতা দূর ॥

*kibā se niśira śobhā śubharāśi pūrā se nadīyāpura |*
*rajanīkara-rajaka nija kare karila malinatā dūra ||*

*Word for word:* kibā — how lovely; se niśira śobhā — the beauty of that night; śubha-rāśi — a heap of blessings; pūrā — filling; se nadīyāpura — that town of Nadia; rajanīkara-rajaka — the moon, a washerman; nija kare — with his own hands; karila malinatā dūra — washed away all darkness (dirt)

**9.1.** How lovely is that night — a heap of blessings filling the town of Nadia!
The moon, a washerman, with his own hands has washed all darkness from it.

বিচিত্র তরুণ তরুলতা মুনিমোহন-মাধুরী লসে ।
প্রফুল্লিত নবকুসুমে ভ্রমর ভ্রময়ে মধুর আশে ॥

*bicitra taruṇa tarulatā munimohana-mādhurī lase |*
*praphullita nabakusume bhramara bhramaye madhura āśe ||*

*Word for word:* bicitra — wondrous; taruṇa tarulatā — young trees and creepers; munimohana-mādhurī — with a sweetness enchanting sages; lase — shine; praphullita nabakusume — over the freshly opened flowers; bhramara — bees; bhramaye — roam; madhura āśe — in hope of honey

**9.2.** Wondrous young trees and creepers shine with a sweetness that enchants sages;
over the freshly opened flowers bees roam in hope of honey.

শীতল পবন মন্দ মন্দ বহে উগারে সুগন্ধরাশি ।
পরম আনন্দে ঘুমায়ে রয়েছে সকল নদীয়াবাসী ॥

*śītala pabana manda manda bahe ugāre sugandharāśi |*
*parama ānande ghumāye rayeche sakala nadīyābāsī ||*

*Word for word:* śītala pabana — a cool breeze; manda manda bahe — blows softly, softly; ugāre sugandha-rāśi — breathing waves of fragrance; parama ānande — in supreme bliss; ghumāye rayeche — lie asleep; sakala nadīyābāsī — all the inhabitants of Nadia

**9.3.** Softly, softly a cool breeze blows, breathing waves of fragrance;
in supreme bliss all the inhabitants of Nadia lie asleep.

গভীর আলয় সদা সুখময় শোভার নাহিক পার ।
ত্রিজগত মাঝে দেখিনু কোথাহ উপমা নাহিক যার ॥

*gabhīra ālaya sadā sukhamaya śobhāra nāhika pāra |*
*trijagata mājhe dekhinu kothāha upamā nāhika yāra ||*

*Word for word:* gabhīra ālaya — the deep house; sadā sukhamaya — ever full of happiness; śobhāra nāhika pāra — its beauty has no bounds; trijagata mājhe — in the three worlds; dekhinu kothāha — I have seen anywhere; upamā nāhika yāra — nothing to compare with it

**9.4.** The deep house [of the Lord], ever full of happiness — its beauty has no bounds;
in all three worlds I have seen nothing to compare with it.

পহুঁর মন্দিরে বেড়িয়া সকল প্রিয় পরিকর স্থিতি ।
কেহ শুঞা কেহ জাগিয়া রয়েছে কে বুঝে এ সব প্রীতি ॥

*pahum̐ra mandire beṛiyā sakala priya parikara sthiti |*
*keha śuñā keha jāgiyā rayeche ke bujhe e saba prīti ||*

*Word for word:* pahum̐ra mandire — the Lord's chamber; beṛiyā — surrounding; sakala priya parikara — all the dear companions; sthiti — have taken their places; keha śuñā — some asleep; keha jāgiyā rayeche — some lie awake; ke bujhe — who can fathom; e saba prīti — such love

**9.5.** Around the Lord's chamber all His dear companions have taken their places;
some sleep, some lie awake — who can fathom such love?

আজ্ঞা-অনুসারে কেহ নিজ ঘরে কাতরে শুতিয়া আছে ।
নরহরি হেন দশা হবে কবে সে সময় রহিব কাছে ॥

*ājñā-anusāre keha nija ghare kātare śutiyā āche |*
*narahari hena daśā habe kabe se samaya rahiba kāche ||*

*Word for word:* ājñā-anusāre — at His bidding; keha — some; nija ghare — in their own homes; kātare — pining; śutiyā āche — lie; narahari — Narahari; hena daśā — such a state; habe kabe — when will it be; se samaya — at that hour; rahiba kāche — I shall be near

**9.6.** And others, at His bidding, lie in their own homes, pining;
Narahari: when will it be so for me — when shall I too be near at that hour?[^24-18]

[^24-17]: GPT1 — pp. 364–365, no. 63 ("bhairava"; scan, PDF pp. 623–624); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 63, p. 235 (catalogue: NG-200). GCC — kirana 2, pada 1 ("rāga bhairaba"):
the first pada of the description of the ashtakaliya ("first, nishanta", the end of the night), right after the "table of contents" in kirana 1 (cf. chapter
23, no. 19). Readings: 9.1 GCC has, at the words "purā se", an editor's mark of a reading "bāsa" (sense: "abode"); 9.2 GCC "praphullita naba kusume bhramara
bhramaye madhura āśe" ("bees roam" — the subject missing in the GPT is restored after the GCC); 9.5 GCC "keha śuñā keha jāgiyā rayeche". Not in the BR, PK,
KGC, PS. B.
[^24-18]: The moon as a "washerman" washing away darkness is a familiar image of moonlight. The pining of the companions sent home is a lila of separation
(cf. chapter 23, nos. 16–17). The poet's wish "to be near at that hour" is a prayer for eternal service to the Lord in His nitya-lila.

## 10. Narahari — "ratana mandira madhi śuti gora sundara…" (GPT1 p. 365, no. 65)
*The Lord sleeps in a chamber of jewels, surrounded by His companions, like the moon among the stars; at the end of the night the
companions sing auspicious songs, as court singers wake a prince; the Lord leaves sleep and sits up on the couch to listen. Raga turi.
**Attribution: not established** — only in the GPT; Vrajabuli.*[^24-19]

রতন-মন্দির মধি শুতি গোর সুন্দর ভুঞ্জই শয়ন-বিলাস ।
প্রিয় পরিকর-সমূহ শুতি রহ পিয় পহুঁক চহু পাশ ॥

*ratana-mandira madhi śuti gora sundara bhuñjai śayana-bilāsa |*
*priya parikara-samūha śuti raha piya pahum̐ka cahu pāśa ||*

*Word for word:* ratana-mandira madhi — in the chamber of jewels; śuti — sleeps; gora sundara — fair Gora; bhuñjai — enjoying; śayana-bilāsa — the play of sleep; priya parikara-samūha — the host of dear companions; śuti raha — sleeps; piya pahum̐ka — of the beloved Lord; cahu pāśa — all around

**10.1.** In the chamber of jewels fair Gora sleeps, enjoying the play of sleep;
the host of dear companions sleeps all around the beloved Lord.

প্রসর গগন মধি তারকাবলী-বেষ্টিত জনু শশধর ।
সো অদভুত শোভা কো কবি বরণনে শকতিধর ॥

*prasara gagana madhi tārakābalī-beṣṭita janu śaśadhara |*
*so adabhuta śobhā ko kabi baraṇane śakatidhara ||*

*Word for word:* prasara gagana madhi — in the wide sky; tārakābalī-beṣṭita — encircled by rows of stars; janu śaśadhara — like the moon; so adabhuta śobhā — that wondrous beauty; ko kabi — what poet; baraṇane śakatidhara — has the power to describe

**10.2.** As in the wide sky the moon, encircled by rows of stars —
what poet has the power to describe that wondrous beauty?

যামিনী-অবসান পেখি পরিকর গাওত মঙ্গল গান ।
জনু নৃপ-কোঙর নিঁদ ভাঙ্গাইতে বৈতালিক মাগধ ধরু তান ॥

*yāminī-abasāna pekhi parikara gāota maṅgala gāna |*
*janu nṛpa-koṅara nim̐da bhāṅgāite baitālika māgadha dharu tāna ||*

*Word for word:* yāminī-abasāna — the end of the night; pekhi — seeing; parikara — the companions; gāota maṅgala gāna — sing auspicious songs; janu — as; nṛpa-koṅara — a prince's; nim̐da bhāṅgāite — to break the sleep; baitālika māgadha — court singers and bards; dharu tāna — strike up a tune

**10.3.** Seeing that the night is ending, the companions sing auspicious songs —
as court singers and bards strike up a tune to break a prince's sleep.

নিঁদ পরিহরি বৈঠল শেজ পরি শুনব নদীয়া-বিহারী ।
মুগধ নরহরি মুগধল অতিশয় সো আনন্দ নেহারি ॥

*nim̐da parihari baiṭhala śeja pari śunaba nadīyā-bihārī |*
*mugadha narahari mugadhala atiśaya so ānanda nehāri ||*

*Word for word:* nim̐da parihari — leaving sleep; baiṭhala śeja pari — sat up on the couch; śunaba — to listen; nadīyā-bihārī — He who sports in Nadia; mugadha narahari — enchanted Narahari; mugadhala atiśaya — is enchanted beyond measure; so ānanda nehāri — beholding that joy

**10.4.** Leaving sleep, He who sports in Nadia sat up on the couch to listen;
enchanted Narahari is enchanted beyond measure, beholding that joy.[^24-20]

[^24-19]: GPT1 — p. 365, no. 65 ("tuṛī"; scan, PDF p. 624; the last pada of section 5.2); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 65, p. ≈235–236. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row
NG-303). Not found in any witness (GCC, BR, PK, KGC, PS, Gita-chandrodaya). The GPT1 OCR is badly distorted ("batana mandira maṇi śuṇaṭha … bhugcai
śanabilāsa"); the text follows the scan. Before it, no. 64 is a pada of Ghanashyama on the Lord's chamber (= GCC 2.10). "Not established", C.
[^24-20]: Vaitalikas and magadhas are court singers and bards who woke kings with songs and praises. The Lord's awakening by His companions' songs is the
beginning of the morning lila (cf. the awakening songs, chapter 22, nos. 17–26). The companions sleep "around" the Lord, as in 9.5.

## 11. Narahari — "āhā mari āju ki ānanda…" (GPT1 p. 417, section 6.1, no. 10; BR)
*Nityananda's advent at Ekachakra, in the house of Hadai Pandita: the parents' joy; Advaita in Shantipura roars and dances: "I have brought
Balavira!"; the gods shower flowers; the Ojha gives gifts; blessed are the land of Radha and the bright thirteenth night of the month of
Magha. Raga kamoda. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^24-21]

আহা মরি আজু কি আনন্দ ।
কিবা একচক্রাপুরে হারাই-পণ্ডিতের ঘরে অবতীর্ণ হৈলা নিত্যানন্দ ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*āhā mari āju ki ānanda |*
*kibā ekacakrāpure hārāi-paṇḍitera ghare abatīrṇa hailā nityānanda || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* āhā mari — ah; āju — today; ki ānanda — what joy; kibā — lo; ekacakrāpure — in Ekachakrapura; hārāi-paṇḍitera ghare — in the house of Hadai Pandita; abatīrṇa hailā — descended; nityānanda — Nityananda

**11.1.** Ah, what joy today!
In Ekachakrapura, in the house of Hadai Pandita, Nityananda has descended!

অতি সুকোমল তনু হেম নবনীত জনু শোভায় ভুবন বিমোহিত ।
চন্দ্রমুখ নিরখিয়া উল্লাসে না ধরে হিয়া পদ্মাবতী হারাই পণ্ডিত ॥

*ati sukomala tanu hema nabanīta janu śobhāya bhubana bimohita |*
*candramukha nirakhiyā ullāse nā dhare hiyā padmābatī hārāi paṇḍita ||*

*Word for word:* ati sukomala tanu — a most tender body; hema nabanīta janu — like golden fresh butter; śobhāya — by His beauty; bhubana bimohita — the world is enchanted; candramukha nirakhiyā — gazing at the moon-face; ullāse nā dhare hiyā — cannot contain their delight; padmābatī hārāi paṇḍita — Padmavati and Hadai Pandita

**11.2.** His body is most tender, like fresh golden butter; by His beauty the world is enchanted.
Gazing at His moon-face, Padmavati and Hadai Pandita cannot contain their delight.

শ্রীঅদ্বৈত শান্তিপুরে গর্জয়ে আনন্দ-ভরে তিলেক হইতে নারে থির ।
নাচে পহুঁ ঊর্ধ্ববাহে কাঁখতালি দিয়া কহে আনিলুঁ আনিলুঁ বলবীর ॥

*śrīadvaita śāntipure garjaye ānanda-bhare tileka haite nāre thira |*
*nāce pahum̐ ūrdhvabāhe kām̐khatāli diyā kahe ānilum̐ ānilum̐ balabīra ||*

*Word for word:* śrī-advaita śāntipure — Sri Advaita in Shantipura; garjaye — roars; ānanda-bhare — in a flood of joy; tileka — for a moment; haite nāre thira — cannot be still; nāce pahum̐ — the Lord dances; ūrdhvabāhe — with arms raised; kām̐khatāli diyā — slapping His sides; kahe — says; ānilu ānilu — I have brought, I have brought; balabīra — Balavira

**11.3.** Sri Advaita in Shantipura roars in a flood of joy and cannot be still for a moment;
He dances with arms raised, slaps His sides and says: "I have brought, I have brought Balavira!"

ব্রহ্মা আদি দেবগণ করে পুষ্প বরিষণ জয় জয় ধ্বনি অনিবার ।
গন্ধর্ব কিন্নর যত বায় বাদ্য শত শত গায় গুণ সুখের পাথার ॥

*brahmā ādi debagaṇa kare puṣpa bariṣaṇa jaya jaya dhvani anibāra |*
*gandharva kinnara yata bāya bādya śata śata gāya guṇa sukhera pāthāra ||*

*Word for word:* brahmā ādi debagaṇa — Brahma and the other gods; kare puṣpa bariṣaṇa — shower flowers; jaya jaya dhvani anibāra — "jaya, jaya" resounds without end; gandharva kinnara yata — all the gandharvas and kinnaras; bāya bādya śata śata — play hundreds of instruments; gāya guṇa — sing His glory; sukhera pāthāra — an ocean of happiness

**11.4.** Brahma and the other gods shower Him with flowers; "Jaya, jaya!" resounds without end;
all the gandharvas and kinnaras play hundreds of instruments and sing His glory — an ocean of happiness.

ওঝা মহাভাগ্যবান পুত্রের কল্যাণে দান করে যত লেখা নাই দিতে ।
কত না কৌতুক লঞা লোক সব আসে ধাঞা মহাভীড় গৃহে প্রবেশিতে ॥

*ojhā mahābhāgyabāna putrera kalyāṇe dāna kare yata lekhā nāi dite |*
*kata nā kautuka lañā loka saba āse dhāñā mahābhīṛa gṛhe prabeśite ||*

*Word for word:* ojhā — the Ojha; mahā-bhāgyabāna — most fortunate; putrera kalyāṇe — for his son's welfare; dāna kare yata — gives so many gifts; lekhā nāi dite — beyond counting; kata nā kautuka lañā — in what merriment; loka saba āse dhāñā — all the people come running; mahā-bhīṛa — a great crowd; gṛhe prabeśite — to enter the house

**11.5.** The Ojha, most fortunate, for his son's welfare gives away gifts beyond counting;
in what merriment the people come running — the house is too crowded to enter!

ধন্য রাঢ়-মহী আর ধন্য সে নক্ষত্র বার ধন্য মাঘ-শুক্লা ত্রয়োদশী ।
নরহরি কহে ভাল ধন্য ধন্য কলিকাল প্রকটে খণ্ডিল দুঃখরাশি ॥

*dhanya rāṛha-mahī āra dhanya se nakṣatra bāra dhanya māgha-śuklā trayodaśī |*
*narahari kahe bhāla dhanya dhanya kalikāla prakaṭe khaṇḍila duḥkharāśi ||*

*Word for word:* dhanya — blessed; rāṛha-mahī — the land of Radha; āra — and; dhanya se nakṣatra bāra — blessed that nakshatra and that day; dhanya māgha-śuklā trayodaśī — blessed the bright thirteenth of Magha; narahari kahe — Narahari says; bhāla — well done; dhanya dhanya kalikāla — blessed, blessed the age of Kali; prakaṭe — by His appearance; khaṇḍila duḥkha-rāśi — destroyed the heaps of sorrow

**11.6.** Blessed is the land of Radha, blessed that nakshatra and that day, blessed the bright thirteenth night of Magha!
Narahari says: well done! Blessed, blessed is the age of Kali — by His appearance He has destroyed the heaps of sorrow.[^24-22]

[^24-21]: GPT1 — p. 417, section 6.1 "Nityananda", no. 10 ("kāmoda"; scan, PDF p. 676); GPT2 — section 6.1, no. 10, p. ≈273 (catalogue: NG-202, "in the BR"). BR 12 (ed. 1912,
pp. 824–825; ed. 1960, vv. 1711–1716): Narahari Chakravarti, showing Srinivasa the places of Navadvipa, tells of Nityananda, His parents and the day of His
advent — the bright thirteenth night of Magha (a Sanskrit verse, v. 1709) — and introduces the pada with the words "this joy the wise have described in many
ways"; then follows a pada of Ghanashyama (GPT no. 11). Readings: 11.2 BR "putramukha nirakhiyā" ("gazing at their son's face"; GPT "candra mukha"), "hāṛāi"
(GPT "hārāi"); 11.5 BR "yautuka laiyā" ("bringing gifts"; GPT "kautuka lañā", "in merriment"). Not in the PK, KGC, PS, GCC. B.
[^24-22]: Nityananda is Balarama Himself, the first expansion of Krishna (CC Adi 5); therefore Advaita, foreseeing His advent, cries: "I have brought Balavira"
("the hero Bala", Balarama) — just as He called Gaura into the world. Ojha is Hadai Pandita's family title. On Nityananda's childhood at Ekachakra — CB Adi 9.
The land of Radha (Rāṛha) is the region of Bengal west of the Ganga where Ekachakra lies.

## 12. Narahari — "bhābe gara gara nitāi sundara…" (GPT1 p. 422, no. 26; BR)
*The first meeting in Navadvipa: seeing Gorachand's radiance, Nityananda enters ecstasy — roaring, rolling on the ground, sighs, laughter,
leaps, trembling; at last He grows still in Vishvambhara's embrace; the Lord, holding Him in His lap, weeps; Srivasa and the others weep.
Raga mayura. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^24-23]

ভাবে গর গর নিতাই সুন্দর হেরি গোরাচাঁদের ছটা ।
কত উঠে চিতে নারে থির হৈতে প্রতি অঙ্গে নব পুলক-ঘটা ॥

*bhābe gara gara nitāi sundara heri gorācām̐dera chaṭā |*
*kata uṭhe cite nāre thira haite prati aṅge naba pulaka-ghaṭā ||*

*Word for word:* bhābe gara gara — overflowing with bhava; nitāi sundara — beautiful Nitai; heri — seeing; gorācām̐dera chaṭā — Gorachand's radiance; kata uṭhe cite — how much wells up in the heart; nāre thira haite — cannot stand still; prati aṅge — on every limb; naba pulaka-ghaṭā — new waves of thrill

**12.1.** Overflowing with bhava, beautiful Nitai, seeing Gorachand's radiance —
how much wells up in His heart! He cannot stand still; on every limb new waves of thrill.

কিবা উনমাদ ক্ষণে সিংহনাদ ক্ষণে লোটে ধরাতলে ।
ক্ষণে দীর্ঘশ্বাস ক্ষণে মহাহাস খসে বাস ভাসে আঁখের জলে ॥

*kibā unamāda kṣaṇe siṃhanāda kṣaṇe loṭe dharātale |*
*kṣaṇe dīrghaśvāsa kṣaṇe mahāhāsa khase bāsa bhāse ām̐khera jale ||*

*Word for word:* kibā unamāda — what madness; kṣaṇe siṃhanāda — now a lion's roar; kṣaṇe loṭe dharātale — now He rolls on the ground; kṣaṇe dīrghaśvāsa — now long sighs; kṣaṇe mahāhāsa — now loud laughter; khase bāsa — His cloth slips; bhāse ām̐khera jale — floats in tears

**12.2.** What madness! Now a lion's roar, now He rolls on the ground;
now long sighs, now loud laughter; His cloth slips off, He floats in tears.

ক্ষণে জোড় লম্ফ ক্ষণে দেহে কম্প খেনে যায় কেহ ধরিতে নারে ।
ক্ষণে কিবা কৈয়া রহে থির হৈয়া সামাইয়া বিশ্বম্ভরের কোরে ॥

*kṣaṇe joṛa lampha kṣaṇe dehe kampa khene yāya keha dharite nāre |*
*kṣaṇe kibā kaiyā rahe thira haiyā sāmāiyā biśvambharera kore ||*

*Word for word:* kṣaṇe joṛa lampha — now leap after leap; kṣaṇe dehe kampa — now trembling of the body; khene yāya — now He runs; keha dharite nāre — no one can hold Him; kṣaṇe kibā kaiyā — now, saying something; rahe thira haiyā — grows still; sāmāiyā — sinking; biśvambharera kore — into Vishvambhara's embrace

**12.3.** Now leap after leap, now His whole body trembles; now He runs — no one can hold Him;
now, saying something, He grows still and sinks into Vishvambhara's embrace.

নিত্যানন্দে কোলে লৈয়া নেত্রজলে ভাসে কিবা প্রভু প্রেমের রীতি ।
কহে নরহরি শ্রীবাসাদি চারি- পাশে কাঁদে কেহ না ধরে ধৃতি ॥

*nityānande kole laiyā netrajale bhāse kibā prabhu premera rīti |*
*kahe narahari śrībāsādi cāri- pāśe kām̐de keha nā dhare dhṛti ||*

*Word for word:* nityānande kole laiyā — taking Nityananda in His lap; netrajale bhāse — floats in tears; kibā — what; prabhu — the Lord; premera rīti — the way of love; kahe narahari — Narahari says; śrībāsādi — Srivasa and the others; cāri-pāśe — all around; kām̐de — weep; keha nā dhare dhṛti — no one keeps composure

**12.4.** Taking Nityananda in His lap, the Lord floats in tears — such is the way of love!
Narahari says: Srivasa and the others around weep; no one can keep composure.[^24-24]

[^24-23]: GPT1 — p. 422, no. 26 ("māyura"; scan, PDF p. 681); GPT2 — section 6.1, no. 26. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-304; the catalogue row NG-203 had
by mistake given the first line of no. 64). BR 12 (ed. 1912, p. 874; ed. 1960, vv. 2437–2440): Nityananda has come secretly to Nadia; the Lord with the devotees
goes to Him in Nandana Acharya's house; at the Lord's sign Srivasa recites the verse on Krishna entering Vrindavana (Bhag. 10.21.5) — "hearing the verse on
Krishna, Nityananda entered the bhava that everyone sings of". Readings: 12.1 BR "gorā-mukhacāndera chaṭā" ("the radiance of Gora's moon-face"); 12.2 BR
"loṭāyaye dharaṇītale". The Navadvipa-parikrama is the same as the BR. Not in the PK, KGC, PS, GCC. B.
[^24-24]: The Lord's first meeting with Nityananda in Nandana Acharya's house — CB Madhya 3; CC Adi 17. Nityananda's "madness" (unmāda) is the madness of prema: the
ecstasy of Balarama hearing of His younger brother Krishna — not a worldly derangement. Vishvambhara is the Lord's name in Navadvipa.

## 13. Narahari — "ki madhura madhuniśā…" (GPT1 p. 335, section 5.1, no. 44; BR)
*A moonlit spring night by the Ganga, which is like the Yamuna; remembering His former pastimes, Nityananda trembles; seeing this,
Gaurasundara enters ecstasy; all sing of Balarama's rasa; gods and men dance; through all the world — "Jaya, Nityananda, son of Rohini!"
Raga kedara. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^24-25]

কি মধুর মধুনিশা চাঁদে আলো কৈল দিশা বহে মন্দ মলয়-সমীর ।
জাহ্নবী যমুনা প্রায় নির্মল পুলিন তায় কুহকে কোকিল শিখি কীর ॥

*ki madhura madhuniśā cām̐de ālo kaila diśā bahe manda malaya-samīra |*
*jāhnabī yamunā prāya nirmala pulina tāya kuhake kokila śikhi kīra ||*

*Word for word:* ki madhura madhuniśā — what a sweet spring night; cām̐de — the moon; ālo kaila diśā — has lit the quarters; bahe manda malaya-samīra — a gentle Malaya breeze blows; jāhnabī — the Jahnavi (Ganga); yamunā prāya — like the Yamuna; nirmala pulina tāya — its banks are pure; kuhake — call; kokila śikhi kīra — cuckoos, peacocks, parrots

**13.1.** What a sweet spring night! The moon has lit the quarters, a gentle Malaya breeze blows;
the Jahnavi is like the Yamuna, its banks are pure; cuckoos, peacocks and parrots call.

আজু কি কৌতুকে নদীয়াতে ।
সোঙরি পুরুব রঙ্গ নিতাই পুলক-অঙ্গ তিলেক নারয়ে থির হৈতে ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*āju ki kautuke nadīyāte |*
*soṅari puruba raṅga nitāi pulaka-aṅga tileka nāraye thira haite || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* āju — today; ki kautuke — what festivity; nadīyāte — in Nadia; soṅari — remembering; puruba raṅga — His former play; nitāi — Nitai; pulaka-aṅga — thrills all over; tileka — for a moment; nāraye thira haite — cannot be still

**13.2.** What festivity today in Nadia!
Remembering His former play, Nitai thrills all over and cannot be still for a moment.

দেখিয়া নিতাইর রীতি শ্রীগৌরসুন্দর অতি প্রেমাবেশে অবশ হইলা ।
কেহ না ধৈরজ বাঁধে গায় সবে নানা ছাঁদে বলাইচাঁদের রাসলীলা ॥

*dekhiyā nitāira rīti śrīgaurasundara ati premābeśe abaśa hailā |*
*keha nā dhairaja bām̐dhe gāya sabe nānā chām̐de balāicām̐dera rāsalīlā ||*

*Word for word:* dekhiyā — seeing; nitāira rīti — Nitai's ways; śrī-gaurasundara — Sri Gaurasundara; ati premābeśe — in great love; abaśa hailā — is overcome; keha nā dhairaja bām̐dhe — no one keeps composure; gāya sabe nānā chām̐de — all sing in many tunes; balāicām̐dera rāsa-līlā — of Balaichand's rasa-lila

**13.3.** Seeing Nitai's ways, Sri Gaurasundara, in great love, is overcome;
no one can keep composure — all sing in many tunes of Balaichand's rasa-lila.

দেবতা মানুষে মিলি নাচে বাহু তুলি তুলি নানা বাদ্য বায় অনিবার ।
দাস নরহরি কয় জগ ভরি জয় জয় নিত্যানন্দ রোহিণীকুমার ॥

*debatā mānuṣe mili nāce bāhu tuli tuli nānā bādya bāya anibāra |*
*dāsa narahari kaya jaga bhari jaya jaya nityānanda rohiṇīkumāra ||*

*Word for word:* debatā mānuṣe mili — gods and men together; nāce bāhu tuli tuli — dance with arms raised; nānā bādya bāya anibāra — many instruments play without end; dāsa narahari kaya — Narahari Dasa says; jaga bhari — through all the world; jaya jaya — jaya, jaya; nityānanda rohiṇīkumāra — Nityananda, son of Rohini

**13.4.** Gods and men dance together with arms raised; many instruments play without end;
Narahari Dasa says: through all the world — "Jaya, jaya Nityananda, son of Rohini!"[^24-26]

[^24-25]: GPT1 — p. 335, section 5.1 ("festivals of the year"), no. 44 ("kedāra"; scan, PDF p. 594); GPT2 — section 5.1, no. 44, p. ≈214. The catalogue had assigned it
to Vasu Ghosha (VG-048); the signature is "dāsa narahari kaya" (NG-260). BR 12 (ed. 1912, p. 945; ed. 1960, vv. 3351–3354): "once here Nityananda-Haladhara,
rejoicing in the rasa of His former rasa-lila…" — among the places of Navadvipa, after a pada on Holi; then follows the account of the stealing of the
companions' clothes (cf. chapter 23, no. 7). Readings: 13.1 BR "kuhure kokila"; 13.2 BR "āju ki kautuka nadīyāte"; 13.3 BR "gāya sabhe nānā chām̐de". Not in the
PK, KGC, PS, GCC. B.
[^24-26]: Balarama's rasa — Bhag. 10.65: coming to Vraja, Balarama spent the moonlit nights of two spring months with the gopis on the bank of the Yamuna
(madhu-madhava); this is His own eternal lila, not a worldly one. Nityananda, Balarama Himself, remembers it by the Ganga, and Gaura, Krishna Himself,
seeing His elder brother's bhava, is Himself overcome. "Sweet night" (madhuniśā) is a night of the month of Madhu (spring).

## 14. Narahari — "gorāpreme gara gara nitāi āmāra…" (GPT1 p. 433, no. 64; BR, Gita-chandrodaya)
*Nityananda comes to Gauda: overflowing with love for Gaura, He weeps, thrills, walks with an elephant's gait, embraces the fallen and makes
them repeat "Hari!". Raga dhanashi. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR and in the Gita-chandrodaya.*[^24-27]

গোরাপ্রেমে গর গর নিতাই আমার । অরুণ-নয়নে বহে সুরধুনী-ধার ॥

*gorāpreme gara gara nitāi āmāra | aruṇa-nayane bahe suradhunī-dhāra ||*

*Word for word:* gorāpreme — with love for Gora; gara gara — overflowing; nitāi āmāra — my Nitai; aruṇa-nayane — from His crimson eyes; bahe — flows; suradhunī-dhāra — a stream like the Suradhuni (Ganga)

**14.1.** My Nitai, overflowing with love for Gora!
From His crimson eyes flows a stream like the Suradhuni.

বিপুল পুলকাবলী শোহে পহুঁ-গায় । গজেন্দ্রগমনে হেলি দুলি চলি যায় ॥

*bipula pulakābalī śohe pahum̐-gāya | gajendragamane heli duli cali yāya ||*

*Word for word:* bipula pulakābalī — waves of thrill; śohe — shine; pahum̐-gāya — on the Lord's body; gajendra-gamane — with the gait of a lordly elephant; heli duli — swaying; cali yāya — He goes

**14.2.** Waves of thrill shine on the Lord's body;
with the gait of a lordly elephant He goes, swaying.

পতিতেরে নিরখিয়া দু-বাহু পসারি । কোলে করি সঘনে বোলয় হরি হরি ॥

*patitere nirakhiyā du-bāhu pasāri | kole kari saghane bolaya hari hari ||*

*Word for word:* patitere nirakhiyā — seeing the fallen; du-bāhu pasāri — spreads both arms; kole kari — embraces them; saghane bolaya — makes them say again and again; hari hari — Hari, Hari

**14.3.** Seeing the fallen, He spreads both arms,
embraces them and makes them say again and again: "Hari, Hari!"

এমন দয়ার নিধি কে হইবে আর । নরহরি অধম তারিতে অবতার ॥

*emana dayāra nidhi ke haibe āra | narahari adhama tārite abatāra ||*

*Word for word:* emana dayāra nidhi — such an ocean of mercy; ke haibe āra — who else will be; narahari — Narahari; adhama tārite — to deliver the fallen; abatāra — descended

**14.4.** Who else will be such an ocean of mercy?
Narahari: He descended to deliver the fallen.[^24-28]

[^24-27]: GPT1 — p. 433, no. 64 ("dhānaśī"; scan, PDF p. 692); GPT2 — section 6.1, no. 64, p. ≈286 (catalogue: NG-203 — with a garbled first line). BR 12 (ed. 1912, p. 967;
ed. 1960, vv. 3632–3635): the Lord sends Nityananda from Puri to Gauda (CB Antya 5 is quoted there); Nityananda, passing through Utkala, comes to Gauda —
"everywhere the word spread: Nityananda Raya has come, intoxicated with prema", — and people run to see Him. Gita-chandrodaya (ed. 1948), section on
Nityananda, pada 2. Readings: 14.2 BR and Gita-chandrodaya "śobhe hema gāya" ("on His golden body"; GPT "śohe pahum̐ gāya"); 14.3 BR "kroṛe kari", "bolāya"; 14.4:
see note 28. Not in the PK, KGC, PS, GCC. B.
[^24-28]: 14.4 in the GPT and BR-1960 reads "narahari adhama tārite abatāra"; BR-1912 has "narahari-adhama" ("to deliver fallen Narahari"), the Gita-chandrodaya
"adhama tāriteo" ("to deliver even fallen Narahari"): the poet counts himself among the fallen. "An elephant's gait", "swaying" — the majestic gait of
Nityananda, intoxicated with prema for Gaura (not with worldly drink).

## 15. Narahari — "prabhu nityānanda rāma…" (GPT1 p. 433, no. 65; BR)
*Nityananda's life in brief: birth from Padmavati, twelve years of play at Ekachakra; leaving home with a sannyasi; twenty years of pilgrimage;
coming to Nadia, where He cast away His staff and water-pot; the journey with the Lord to Puri and the Lord's broken staff; the return to
Gauda by the Lord's order and the giving of prema to all. Raga kamoda. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^24-29]

প্রভু নিত্যানন্দ রাম রূপে গুণে অনুপাম পদ্মাবতী-গর্ভে জনমিলা ।
নিজগণ লৈয়া সঙ্গে দ্বাদশ বৎসর রঙ্গে শ্রীএকচক্রায় বিলসিলা ॥

*prabhu nityānanda rāma rūpe guṇe anupāma padmābatī-garbhe janamilā |*
*nijagaṇa laiyā saṅge dvādaśa batsara raṅge śrīekacakrāya bilasilā ||*

*Word for word:* prabhu nityānanda rāma — Lord Nityananda-Rama; rūpe guṇe anupāma — matchless in beauty and virtues; padmābatī-garbhe — from Padmavati's womb; janamilā — was born; nijagaṇa laiyā saṅge — with His companions; dvādaśa batsara — for twelve years; raṅge — joyfully; śrī-ekacakrāya — in Sri Ekachakra; bilasilā — played

**15.1.** Lord Nityananda-Rama, matchless in beauty and virtues, was born from Padmavati's womb;
with His companions He played joyfully for twelve years in Sri Ekachakra.

গোরা অবতীর্ণ হৈলে সন্ন্যাসীর সঙ্গছলে বাহির হইলা ঘর হৈতে ।
তীর্থ পর্যটন করে বিংশতি বর্ষের পরে আনন্দে আইলা নদীয়াতে ॥

*gorā abatīrṇa haile sannyāsīra saṅgachale bāhira hailā ghara haite |*
*tīrtha paryaṭana kare biṃśati barṣera pare ānande āilā nadīyāte ||*

*Word for word:* gorā abatīrṇa haile — when Gora had appeared; sannyāsīra saṅga-chale — on the pretext of a sannyasi's company; bāhira hailā ghara haite — left home; tīrtha paryaṭana kare — wandered among the holy places; biṃśati barṣera pare — after twenty years; ānande āilā nadīyāte — joyfully came to Nadia

**15.2.** When Gora had appeared, He left home on the pretext of a sannyasi's company;
He wandered among the holy places and after twenty years joyfully came to Nadia.

পাঞা প্রাণ গোরাচাঁদে পড়ি সে প্রেমের ফাঁদে দণ্ড কমণ্ডলু ফেলে দূরে ।
সদা মাতি সংকীর্তনে ক্ষেত্রে চলে প্রভু সনে প্রভু-দণ্ড তিনখণ্ড করে ॥

*pāñā prāṇa gorācām̐de paṛi se premera phām̐de daṇḍa kamaṇḍalu phele dūre |*
*sadā māti saṃkīrtane kṣetre cale prabhu sane prabhu-daṇḍa tinakhaṇḍa kare ||*

*Word for word:* pāñā prāṇa gorācām̐de — finding Gorachand, His life; paṛi se premera phām̐de — caught in that net of love; daṇḍa kamaṇḍalu — staff and water-pot; phele dūre — cast far away; sadā māti saṅkīrtane — ever intoxicated with sankirtana; kṣetre cale prabhu sane — went with the Lord to Kshetra; prabhu-daṇḍa tinakhaṇḍa kare — broke the Lord's staff into three pieces

**15.3.** Finding Gorachand, His very life, caught in that net of love, He cast His staff and water-pot far away;
ever intoxicated with sankirtana, He went with the Lord to Kshetra and broke the Lord's staff into three pieces.

প্রভুর আদেশ-মতে গৌড়ে আসি ক্ষেত্র হৈতে প্রভু-মনোহিত কর্ম কৈলা ।
দাস নরহরি-গতি বসু-জাহ্নবার পতি যারে তারে প্রেম বিলাইলা ॥

*prabhura ādeśa-mate gauṛe āsi kṣetra haite prabhu-manohita karma kailā |*
*dāsa narahari-gati basu-jāhnabāra pati yāre tāre prema bilāilā ||*

*Word for word:* prabhura ādeśa-mate — by the Lord's order; gauṛe āsi kṣetra haite — coming from Kshetra to Gauda; prabhu-manohita karma kailā — did the work dear to the Lord's heart; dāsa narahari-gati — the refuge of Narahari Dasa; basu-jāhnabāra pati — the Husband of Vasudha and Jahnava; yāre tāre — to everyone; prema bilāilā — gave prema

**15.4.** By the Lord's order He came from Kshetra to Gauda and did the work dear to the Lord's heart;
the refuge of Narahari Dasa, the Husband of Vasudha and Jahnava, gave prema to everyone He met.[^24-30]

[^24-29]: GPT1 — p. 433, no. 65 ("kāmoda"; scan, PDF p. 692); GPT2 — section 6.1, no. 65. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-305). BR 12 (ed. 1912, p. 996; ed. 1960,
vv. 4018–4021): after the account of the wedding and of Nityananda's life in Khardaha — "the poets glorify the virtues of Padmavati's son in many ways"; then
follow the padas on Advaita. Readings: 15.2 BR "tīrtha-paryaṭana ka're"; 15.4 BR "basu-jāhnabāra pati" (GPT "basu jāhnabāra pati"). The Navadvipa-parikrama is the
same as the BR. Not in the PK, KGC, PS, GCC. B.
[^24-30]: Childhood at Ekachakra and the departure with a sannyasi — CB Adi 9; Nityananda broke the Lord's staff on the way to Puri (CC Madhya 5; CB Antya 2); He was
sent by the Lord to preach in Gauda — CB Antya 5. The numbers ("twelve", "twenty" years) follow the poet's account. "Was born from Padmavati's womb" (15.1) is the author's word: Nityananda, Balarama Himself, appears by His own will (cf. 11.1: "has descended"; on the Lord's "birth" see note 4 of chapter 20). On the caveat about Nityananda's marriage —
no. 20.

## 16. Narahari — "kṛṣṇera agraja rāma rohiṇīnandana…" (GPT1 pp. 433–434, no. 66; BR)
*Praise of Nityananda: He is Balarama, Krishna's elder brother, the Lord of Varuni and Revati; now He is Nitai, Chaitanya's elder brother, the
Husband of Vasudha and Jahnava; His form, dance, tears, mercy to the fallen; the poet laments that he did not serve Him. Raga kamoda.
**Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^24-31]

কৃষ্ণের অগ্রজ রাম রোহিণীনন্দন । বারুণী রেবতী দুই প্রিয়া প্রাণধন ॥

*kṛṣṇera agraja rāma rohiṇīnandana | bāruṇī rebatī dui priyā prāṇadhana ||*

*Word for word:* kṛṣṇera agraja — Krishna's elder brother; rāma — Rama; rohiṇī-nandana — son of Rohini; bāruṇī rebatī — Varuni and Revati; dui priyā — of the two beloveds; prāṇa-dhana — the treasure of life

**16.1.** Rama, Krishna's elder brother, the son of Rohini —
the treasure of the lives of His two beloveds, Varuni and Revati —

ধন্য কলিযুগে সেই নিতাই সুন্দর । চৈতন্য-অগ্রজ পদ্মাবতীর কোঙর ॥

*dhanya kaliyuge sei nitāi sundara | caitanya-agraja padmābatīra koṅara ||*

*Word for word:* dhanya kaliyuge — blessed in the age of Kali; sei nitāi sundara — He, beautiful Nitai; caitanya-agraja — Chaitanya's elder brother; padmābatīra koṅara — Padmavati's son

**16.2.** blessed in the age of Kali is He, beautiful Nitai,
Chaitanya's elder brother, Padmavati's son.

বসুধা-জাহ্নবা-প্রাণ-পতি প্রেমময় । নিজগুণে প্রভু জীবে হইলা সদয় ॥

*basudhā-jāhnabā-prāṇa-pati premamaya | nijaguṇe prabhu jībe hailā sadaya ||*

*Word for word:* basudhā-jāhnabā-prāṇa-pati — the Lord of the lives of Vasudha and Jahnava; premamaya — loving; nijaguṇe — by His own goodness; prabhu — the Lord; jībe — to the living beings; hailā sadaya — became merciful

**16.3.** The loving Lord of the lives of Vasudha and Jahnava
by His own goodness became merciful to the living beings.

গোরাপ্রেমে মত্ত দিবানিশি নাহি জানে । পবিত্র করিল মহী প্রেমামৃতদানে ॥

*gorāpreme matta dibāniśi nāhi jāne | pabitra karila mahī premāmṛtadāne ||*

*Word for word:* gorāpreme matta — intoxicated with love for Gora; dibāniśi nāhi jāne — knows neither day nor night; pabitra karila mahī — sanctified the earth; premāmṛta-dāne — by giving the nectar of prema

**16.4.** Intoxicated with love for Gora, He knows neither day nor night;
He sanctified the earth by giving the nectar of prema.

গোরা-অনুরাগে সে অরুণ তনুখানি । ঝলমল করয়ে তপত হেম জিনি ॥

*gorā-anurāge se aruṇa tanukhāni | jhalamala karaye tapata hema jini ||*

*Word for word:* gorā-anurāge — with love for Gora; se aruṇa tanukhāni — His crimson body; jhalamala karaye — shines; tapata hema jini — outdoing molten gold

**16.5.** With love for Gora His crimson body
shines, outdoing molten gold.

শ্রবণে কুণ্ডল দোলে মুনি-মনোলোভা । আজানুলম্বিত ভুজ নিরুপম শোভা ॥

*śrabaṇe kuṇḍala dole muni-manolobhā | ājānulambita bhuja nirupama śobhā ||*

*Word for word:* śrabaṇe kuṇḍala dole — earrings sway in His ears; muni-manolobhā — captivating the minds of sages; ājānulambita bhuja — arms reaching to the knees; nirupama śobhā — matchless beauty

**16.6.** Earrings sway in His ears, captivating the minds of sages;
His arms reach to His knees — matchless beauty.

পরিসর বুক দেখি কেবা নাহি ভুলে । সতী কুলবতী তিলাঞ্জলি দেয় কুলে ॥

*parisara buka dekhi kebā nāhi bhule | satī kulabatī tilāñjali deya kule ||*

*Word for word:* parisara buka dekhi — seeing the broad chest; kebā nāhi bhule — who would not forget himself; satī kulabatī — chaste wives of noble families; tilāñjali deya kule — give up their kin (lit. "offer the family the water of funeral rites")

**16.7.** Who would not forget himself, seeing His broad chest?
Chaste wives of noble families give up their kin for Him.

ও চাঁদবদনে সদা বোলে গোরা গোরা । বুক মুখ বাহিয়া নয়নে বহে লোরা ॥

*o cām̐dabadane sadā bole gorā gorā | buka mukha bāhiyā nayane bahe lorā ||*

*Word for word:* o cām̐dabadane — from that moon-face; sadā bole — always says; gorā gorā — Gora, Gora; buka mukha bāhiyā — down chest and face; nayane bahe lorā — tears flow from the eyes

**16.8.** From His moon-face never cease the words "Gora, Gora!" —
and tears from His eyes run down His face and chest.

প্রিয় পরিকরগণ সহ সে আবেশে । সংকীর্তন-সুখের সায়রে সভে ভাসে ॥

*priya parikaragaṇa saha se ābeśe | saṃkīrtana-sukhera sāyare sabhe bhāse ||*

*Word for word:* priya parikaragaṇa saha — with the dear companions; se ābeśe — in that rapture; saṅkīrtana-sukhera sāyare — in the ocean of the joy of sankirtana; sabhe bhāse — all float

**16.9.** With His dear companions, in that same rapture,
all float in the ocean of the joy of sankirtana.

ভুবনমোহন ছাঁদে নাচে গুণনিধি । দেবের দুর্লভ সব শোভার অবধি ॥

*bhubanamohana chām̐de nāce guṇanidhi | debera durlabha saba śobhāra abadhi ||*

*Word for word:* bhubanamohana chām̐de — in a world-enchanting way; nāce guṇanidhi — the treasure of virtues dances; debera durlabha — unattainable even for the gods; saba śobhāra abadhi — the limit of all beauty

**16.10.** The treasure of virtues dances so as to enchant the world —
the utmost limit of beauty, unattainable even for the gods.

চাহিতে নিতাইচাঁদে কেবা থির পায় । পাষাণ সমান হিয়া সেহ গলি যায় ॥

*cāhite nitāicām̐de kebā thira pāya | pāṣāṇa samāna hiyā seha gali yāya ||*

*Word for word:* cāhite nitāicām̐de — looking at Nitaichand; kebā thira pāya — who can stay steady; pāṣāṇa samāna hiyā — a heart like stone; seha gali yāya — even that melts

**16.11.** Who, looking at Nitaichand, can stay steady?
Even a heart of stone melts.

পাতকী পতিতে করুণার নাহি পার । হেন পহুঁ না ভজিল নরহরি ছার ॥

*pātakī patite karuṇāra nāhi pāra | hena pahum̐ nā bhajila narahari chāra ||*

*Word for word:* pātakī patite — to sinners and the fallen; karuṇāra nāhi pāra — mercy is boundless; hena pahum̐ — such a Lord; nā bhajila — did not serve; narahari chāra — wretched Narahari

**16.12.** To sinners and the fallen His mercy is boundless —
such a Lord wretched Narahari did not serve![^24-32]

[^24-31]: GPT1 — pp. 433–434, no. 66 ("kāmoda"; scan, PDF pp. 692–693); GPT2 — section 6.1, no. 66, p. ≈286 (catalogue: NG-204, "in the BR"). BR 12 (ed. 1912, pp. 994–995;
ed. 1960, vv. 3997–4008): after the wedding and a quotation from the Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika on Vasudha and Jahnava — "the poets sing the deeds of Nityananda,
the Saviour of the fallen". Readings: 16.2 BR "padmābatīra kumāra"; 16.7 BR "satī kulabatī tilāñjali dei kule". The Navadvipa-parikrama is the same as the BR. Not in
the PK, KGC, PS, GCC. B.
[^24-32]: Varuni and Revati are Balarama's consorts; Vasudha and Jahnava are their incarnations (Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika, quoted in BR 12, v. 3992). "Give up their
kin" (16.7; lit. "offer their family the water of funeral rites") is the same formula as that used of the gopis who left everything for Krishna: it speaks of the
all-attractive spiritual beauty of Nityananda-Balarama, which frees the soul from worldly bonds, not of a worldly attraction (on Balarama's own rasa with the
gopis — Bhag. 10.65; see no. 13). Nityananda is Balarama Himself, the original spiritual master (CC Adi 5).

## 17. Narahari — "āhā mari ki nitāira śobhā…" (GPT1 p. 434, no. 67; BR)
*Panihati, the house of Raghava Pandita: Nityananda dances in sankirtana with arms raised, calls "Gora!", floats in tears of bliss and gives
the poor the treasure of prema. Raga gandhara. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^24-33]

আহা মরি কি নিতাইর শোভা ।
কত না ভঙ্গীতে নাচে ভুজ তুলি অখিল-ভুবন-লোভা ॥

*āhā mari ki nitāira śobhā |*
*kata nā bhaṅgīte nāce bhuja tuli akhila-bhubana-lobhā ||*

*Word for word:* āhā mari — ah; ki nitāira śobhā — what beauty of Nitai; kata nā bhaṅgīte — in how many wondrous ways; nāce — He dances; bhuja tuli — raising His arms; akhila-bhubana-lobhā — enticing the whole world

**17.1.** Ah, what beauty of Nitai!
How wondrously He dances with arms raised — enticing the whole world!

ঘন ঘন গোরা বলে ।
হেম-ধরাধর তনু অনুখন ভাসয়ে আনন্দ-জলে ॥

*ghana ghana gorā bale |*
*hema-dharādhara tanu anukhana bhāsaye ānanda-jale ||*

*Word for word:* ghana ghana — again and again; gorā bale — calls "Gora"; hema-dharādhara tanu — His body, a golden mountain; anukhana — ever; bhāsaye ānanda-jale — floats in tears of bliss

**17.2.** Again and again He calls: "Gora!" —
and His body, a golden mountain, ever floats in tears of bliss.

করুণায় উমড়য়ে হিয়া ।
দীনহীন জনে করে মহাধনী প্রেমচিন্তামণি দিয়া ॥

*karuṇāya umaṛaye hiyā |*
*dīnahīna jane kare mahādhanī premacintāmaṇi diyā ||*

*Word for word:* karuṇāya — with compassion; umaṛaye hiyā — the heart overflows; dīnahīna jane — the poor and lowly; kare mahādhanī — makes rich; prema-cintāmaṇi diyā — giving the wish-fulfilling gem of prema

**17.3.** His heart overflows with compassion:
He makes the poor and lowly rich, giving them the gem of prema.

কিবা ভাবে মন্দ মন্দ হাসে ।
নরহরি কহে কুলবতী সতী ধৈরজ ধরম নাশে ॥

*kibā bhābe manda manda hāse |*
*narahari kahe kulabatī satī dhairaja dharama nāśe ||*

*Word for word:* kibā bhābe — with what feeling; manda manda hāse — gently smiles; narahari kahe — Narahari says; kulabatī satī — chaste wives; dhairaja dharama nāśe — robs of composure and rules

**17.4.** With what feeling He gently smiles!
Narahari says: [that smile] robs chaste wives of their composure and their rules.[^24-34]

[^24-33]: GPT1 — p. 434, no. 67 ("gāndhāra"; scan, PDF p. 693); GPT2 — section 6.1, no. 67. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-306). BR 12 (ed. 1912, p. 968; ed. 1960,
vv. 3649–3652): "first Nityananda with His companions came to Panihati… who can describe the singing and dancing in the house of Raghava Pandita!" Readings:
17.3 GPT1 "kare mahādhvani" ("raises a great cry") — BR "kare mahādhanī" ("makes [them] rich"; adopted); 17.4 BR "dhairaya-dharama nāśe". The
Navadvipa-parikrama is the same as the BR. Not in the PK, KGC, PS, GCC. B.
[^24-34]: Panihati and the kirtana in Raghava's house — CB Antya 5. On the formula of 17.4 see note 32: it is an image of Nityananda's all-attractive spiritual
beauty, which frees from worldly bonds, not of worldly temptation.

## 18. Narahari — "kibā nācai nitāicām̐da…" (GPT1 p. 434, no. 68; BR)
*The same place: Nitaichand's dance among His companions; He calls "Gora!", the poor run to Him, feeling the breeze of His mercy; all drown in
prema, Kali's pride retreats. Raga dhanashi. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^24-35]

কিবা নাচই নিতাইচাঁদ ।
ঝলমল তনু অনুপম-শোভা অখিল-লোচন-ফাঁদ ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*kibā nācai nitāicām̐da |*
*jhalamala tanu anupama-śobhā akhila-locana-phām̐da || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* kibā — how; nācai — dances; nitāicām̐da — Nitaichand; jhalamala tanu — the body shines; anupama-śobhā — with matchless beauty; akhila-locana-phām̐da — a snare for all eyes

**18.1.** How Nitaichand dances!
His body shines with matchless beauty — a snare for all eyes.

কি নব ভঙ্গীতে চাহে চারি ভিতে না জানি কি রঙ্গে ভোরা ।
আজানুলম্বিত ভুজযুগ তুলি সঘনে বোলয়ে গোরা ॥

*ki naba bhaṅgīte cāhe cāri bhite nā jāni ki raṅge bhorā |*
*ājānulambita bhujayuga tuli saghane bolaye gorā ||*

*Word for word:* ki naba bhaṅgīte — with what new movements; cāhe cāri bhite — looks about; nā jāni — who knows; ki raṅge bhorā — in what joy He is lost; ājānulambita — reaching to the knees; bhujayuga tuli — raising both arms; saghane bolaye gorā — calls "Gora" again and again

**18.2.** With what new movements He looks about — who knows in what joy He is!
Raising His arms that reach to His knees, He calls again and again: "Gora!"

কীর্তনবিলাস- রসে ভাসে সদা প্রিয় পারিষদ লৈয়া ।
দীনহীন জন ধায় চারিপাশে করুণা-বাতাস পাইয়া ॥

*kīrtanabilāsa- rase bhāse sadā priya pāriṣada laiyā |*
*dīnahīna jana dhāya cāripāśe karuṇā-bātāsa pāiyā ||*

*Word for word:* kīrtana-bilāsa-rase — in the rasa of the play of kirtana; bhāse sadā — ever floats; priya pāriṣada laiyā — with His dear companions; dīnahīna jana — the poor and lowly; dhāya cāripāśe — run from all sides; karuṇā-bātāsa pāiyā — feeling the breeze of mercy

**18.3.** He ever floats in the rasa of kirtana with His dear companions;
the poor and lowly run to Him from all sides, feeling the breeze of His mercy.

মাতিল সকলে ভাসে প্রেমজলে কলির দরপ দূরে ।
নরহরি-পহুঁ-গুণ গণি গণি কেবা না জগতে ঝুরে ॥

*mātila sakale bhāse premajale kalira darapa dūre |*
*narahari-pahum̐-guṇa gaṇi gaṇi kebā nā jagate jhure ||*

*Word for word:* mātila sakale — all are maddened; bhāse premajale — float in the waters of prema; kalira darapa dūre — Kali's pride is far away; narahari-pahum̐-guṇa — the virtues of the poet Narahari's Lord; gaṇi gaṇi — counting; kebā nā jagate jhure — who in the world would not shed tears

**18.4.** All are maddened, floating in the waters of prema; Kali's pride has gone far away;
counting the virtues of the poet Narahari's Lord, who in the world would not shed tears?[^24-36]

[^24-35]: GPT1 — p. 434, no. 68 ("dhānaśī"; scan, PDF p. 693); GPT2 — section 6.1, no. 68, p. ≈287 (catalogue: NG-205). BR 12 (ed. 1912, p. 968; ed. 1960, vv. 3653–3656; "punaḥ
dhānaśī", right after no. 67). Readings: 18.1 BR "kibā nācaye nitāicām̐da"; 18.2 BR "nā jāni ki raṅge bhorā". Not in the PK, KGC, PS, GCC. B.
[^24-36]: "Maddened" (mātila) — with prema. The poet Narahari's Lord here is Nityananda.

## 19. Narahari — "āju ānande nitāicām̐de…" (GPT1 pp. 434–435, no. 69; BR)
*Nityananda's abhisheka at Panihati: He is seated on a throne, Damodara bathes Him with fragrant Ganga water to mantras; the gods,
mingling with men, look on; Narahari brings a dry cloth and anoints Him with sandal. Raga ashavari. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** —
the pada is in the BR.*[^24-37]

আজু আনন্দে নিতাইচাঁদে ।
শোভাময় সিংহাসনে বসাইয়া কেহ না ধৈরজ বাঁধে ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*āju ānande nitāicām̐de |*
*śobhāmaya siṃhāsane basāiyā keha nā dhairaja bām̐dhe || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* āju ānande — today in joy; nitāicām̐de — Nitaichand; śobhāmaya siṃhāsane — on a beautiful throne; basāiyā — having seated; keha nā dhairaja bām̐dhe — no one can contain his delight

**19.1.** Today, in joy, having seated Nitaichand
on a beautiful throne — no one can contain his delight.

সুবাসিত গঙ্গাজল লৈয়া ।
পড়ি মন্ত্র মাথে ঢালে জল দামোদর হরষিত হৈয়া ॥

*subāsita gaṅgājala laiyā |*
*paṛi mantra māthe ḍhāle jala dāmodara haraṣita haiyā ||*

*Word for word:* subāsita gaṅgā-jala laiyā — taking fragrant Ganga water; paṛi mantra — reciting mantras; māthe ḍhāle jala — pours the water on His head; dāmodara — Damodara; haraṣita haiyā — joyfully

**19.2.** Taking fragrant Ganga water
and reciting mantras, Damodara joyfully pours it over His head.

জয় জয় ধ্বনি করি ।
মানুষে মিশাঞা সুরগণে শোভা নিরখে নয়ান ভরি ॥

*jaya jaya dhvani kari |*
*mānuṣe miśāñā suragaṇe śobhā nirakhe nayāna bhari ||*

*Word for word:* jaya jaya dhvani kari — with cries of "jaya, jaya"; mānuṣe miśāñā — mingling with men; suragaṇe — the gods; śobhā nirakhe — gaze at the beauty; nayāna bhari — with full eyes

**19.3.** With cries of "Jaya, jaya!"
the gods, mingling with men, gaze at His beauty with full eyes.

কেহ গায় অভিষেক-রঙ্গে ।
পাইয়া শুষ্কবাস নরহরি চন্দন দেই সে অঙ্গে ॥

*keha gāya abhiṣeka-raṅge |*
*pāiyā śuṣkabāsa narahari candana dei se aṅge ||*

*Word for word:* keha gāya — some sing; abhiṣeka-raṅge — rejoicing in the abhisheka; pāiyā śuṣkabāsa — bringing a dry cloth; narahari — Narahari; candana dei — applies sandal; se aṅge — to His body

**19.4.** Some sing, rejoicing in the abhisheka;
Narahari brings a dry cloth and anoints His body with sandal.[^24-38]

[^24-37]: GPT1 — pp. 434–435, no. 69 ("āśābarī"; scan, PDF pp. 693–694); GPT2 — section 6.1, no. 69. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-307). BR 12 (ed. 1912, p. 969;
ed. 1960, vv. 3658–3661): "there the abhisheka of Sri Nityananda was performed…"; then prose: Nityananda is seated on a couch and garlanded, Raghava holds
the umbrella; Nityananda asks for a kadamba garland, and kadamba flowers are found on a lemon tree (vv. 3662–3665). Readings: 19.4 GPT "pāiyā śuṣkabāsa narahari,
candana dei se aṅge" — BR "parāiyā śuṣka bāsa narahari, candana dei se raṅge" ("having dressed [Him] in a dry cloth… anoints with sandal in joy"). Not in the PK, KGC,
PS, GCC. B.
[^24-38]: The abhisheka and the kadamba miracle in Raghava's house — CB Antya 5. Who the Damodara performing the bath is cannot be established from this text
alone. "Narahari" in 19.4 is a participant in the event; if the pada belongs to Narahari Chakravarti, this is not a signature but a mention of a companion
(probably Narahari Sarakara), and the pada has no signature. The gods "mingle with men" — they come to the festival unrecognized (cf. no. 20).

## 20. Narahari — "basudhā jāhnabā debī śobhābadhi…" (GPT1 p. 435, no. 71; BR)
*The adhivasa of the brides — Vasudha and Jahnava, the daughters of Suryadasa Pandita: the brahmanas bless them, placing rice and durva grass
on their heads; their mother is beside herself with joy; the women friends perform auspicious rites; the heavenly women watch unseen. Raga
bhupali. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^24-39]

বসুধা জাহ্নবা দেবী শোভাবধি অধিবাস-ভূষা-ভূষিত তনু ।
ঝলমল করে চারু রুচিছটা তড়িত কুঙ্কুম কেতকী জনু ॥

*basudhā jāhnabā debī śobhābadhi adhibāsa-bhūṣā-bhūṣita tanu |*
*jhalamala kare cāru rucichaṭā taṛita kuṅkuma ketakī janu ||*

*Word for word:* basudhā jāhnabā debī — Vasudha and Jahnava Devi; śobhābadhi — the utmost of beauty; adhibāsa-bhūṣā-bhūṣita tanu — bodies adorned with the adhivasa ornaments; jhalamala kare — shines; cāru rucichaṭā — lovely radiance; taṛita kuṅkuma ketakī janu — like lightning, kunkuma and ketaki

**20.1.** Vasudha and Jahnava Devi, the utmost of beauty — their bodies adorned with the ornaments of the adhivasa;
their lovely radiance shines like lightning, kunkuma and ketaki.

চারিপাশে বিপ্রগণ ধন্য মানে চাহি কন্যাপানে হরষ-হিয়া ।
বেদধ্বনি করি করে আশীর্বাদ ধান্য দূর্বা দুঁহু-মস্তকে দিয়া ॥

*cāripāśe bipragaṇa dhanya māne cāhi kanyāpāne haraṣa-hiyā |*
*bedadhvani kari kare āśīrvāda dhānya dūrvā dum̐hu-mastake diyā ||*

*Word for word:* cāripāśe — around; bipragaṇa — the brahmanas; dhanya māne — count themselves fortunate; cāhi kanyā-pāne — looking at the brides; haraṣa-hiyā — with joyful hearts; beda-dhvani kari — reciting the Vedas; kare āśīrvāda — bless; dhānya dūrvā — rice and durva grass; dum̐hu-mastake diyā — placing on the heads of both

**20.2.** Around them the brahmanas count themselves fortunate, looking joyfully at the brides;
reciting the Vedas, they bless them, placing rice and durva grass on the heads of both.

পণ্ডিত-ঘরণী ধরণীতে পদ না ধরয় হিয়া ধৈরজ বাঁধে ।
বিবিধ মঙ্গল করু সখীকুল উলু লুলু দেই কত না সাধে ॥

*paṇḍita-gharaṇī dharaṇīte pada nā dharaya hiyā dhairaja bām̐dhe |*
*bibidha maṅgala karu sakhīkula ulu lulu dei kata nā sādhe ||*

*Word for word:* paṇḍita-gharaṇī — the pandita's wife; dharaṇīte pada nā dharaya — does not feel the ground beneath her feet; hiyā dhairaja bām̐dhe — barely restrains her heart; bibidha maṅgala — every kind of auspicious rite; karu sakhīkula — the women friends perform; ulu lulu dei — cry "ulu-lulu"; kata nā sādhe — how eagerly

**20.3.** The pandita's wife hardly feels the ground beneath her feet, barely restrains her heart;
the women friends perform every kind of auspicious rite and how eagerly they cry "ulu-lulu"!

শঙ্খ ঘণ্টা আদি বাদ্য বাজে বহু কোলাহল নাহি তুলনা দিতে ।
ভণে নরহরি সুরনারী অলখিত দেখে কত কৌতুক চিতে ॥

*śaṅkha ghaṇṭā ādi bādya bāje bahu kolāhala nāhi tulanā dite |*
*bhaṇe narahari suranārī alakhita dekhe kata kautuka cite ||*

*Word for word:* śaṅkha ghaṇṭā ādi — conches, bells and the rest; bādya bāje bahu — many instruments sound; kolāhala — the din; nāhi tulanā dite — beyond compare; bhaṇe narahari — Narahari says; suranārī — the heavenly women; alakhita — unseen; dekhe — watch; kata kautuka cite — with great delight in their hearts

**20.4.** Conches, bells and many instruments sound — there is no din to compare with it;
Narahari says: the heavenly women, unseen, watch it with great delight in their hearts.[^24-40]

[^24-39]: GPT1 — p. 435, no. 71 ("bhūpālī"; scan, PDF p. 694); GPT2 — section 6.1, no. 71, p. ≈288. The catalogue (NG-207) had run its first line together with the first line of
no. 73 ("basudhā jāhnabā debī śobhābadhi bhubanapābana nitāi mora"); no. 73 is the new row NG-309. BR 12 (ed. 1912, pp. 991–992; ed. 1960, vv. 3965–3968): after the
bridegroom's adhivasa at Badagachhi in Krishnadasa's house (vv. 3948–3956; there a pada of Ghanashyama, GPT no. 70), Suryadasa at Saligrama performs the adhivasa
of his daughters — "although he had seen his daughters' glory in a dream, he was still overcome by a father's tenderness". Readings: 20.1 BR "taṛita-kuṅkuma ketakī
yanu"; 20.3 BR "karu sakhīkula". Not in the PK, KGC, PS, GCC. B.
[^24-40]: Nityananda's wedding is His lila, not a worldly event: Nityananda, Balarama Himself, is not subject to worldly bonds, and Vasudha and Jahnava are
incarnations of His eternal consorts Varuni and Revati (note 32); Jahnava Devi later became one of the foremost teachers of the Gaudiya Vaishnavas. The
adhivasa is the pre-wedding consecration; "ulu-lulu" is the jubilant cry of Bengali women. The pandita's wife is the brides' mother, Suryadasa's wife.

## 21. Narahari — "koṭi manamatha-garababhara-hara…" (GPT1 pp. 435–436, no. 72; BR)
*The wedding procession: Nitai-Haladhara in wedding attire rides in a new palanquin; brahmanas and bards praise Him, the people run to look;
singers, dancers and musicians; torches turn night into day; the gods unseen shower flowers. Raga deshapala. **Attribution: probably
Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR; Vrajabuli.*[^24-41]

কোটি মনমথ-গরবভর-হর পরম সুঘর নিতাই হলধর
করত গমন চড়ি নব চৌদোলে ছবি ছল ছলকয়ে ।
বেশ বিরচি বিবাহ-মত কত ভাঁতি ভূষণ অঙ্গে বিলসত
ললিত লোচন-কঞ্জ মুখ মৃদুহাস মঞ্জুল ঝলকয়ে ॥

*koṭi manamatha-garababhara-hara parama sughara nitāi haladhara*
*karata gamana caṛi naba caudole chabi chala chalakaye |*
*beśa biraci bibāha-mata kata bhām̐ti bhūṣaṇa aṅge bilasata*
*lalita locana-kañja mukha mṛduhāsa mañjula jhalakaye ||*

*Word for word:* koṭi manamatha-garababhara-hara — crusher of the pride of millions of Kamadevas; parama sughara — most handsome; nitāi haladhara — Nitai-Haladhara; karata gamana — goes; caṛi naba caudole — riding in a new palanquin; chabi chala chalakaye — His beauty brims over; beśa biraci bibāha-mata — in wedding attire; kata bhām̐ti bhūṣaṇa — ornaments of many kinds; aṅge bilasata — shine on His body; lalita locana-kañja — lovely lotus-eyes; mukha mṛduhāsa mañjula jhalakaye — a charming gentle smile shines on His face

**21.1.** Crusher of the pride of millions of Kamadevas, most handsome Nitai-Haladhara
rides in a new palanquin, His beauty brimming over;
in wedding attire, with ornaments of many kinds on His body,
with lovely lotus-eyes, a charming gentle smile on His shining face.

রূপ পীবইতে মত্ত অতিশয় করত ভূসুরবৃন্দ জয় জয়
বন্দীগণ-মন মোদিত ঘন ঘন বিমল যশ পরকাশয়ে ।
তেজি নিজ নিজ গেহ ধায়ত নারীপুরুষ ন থেহ পায়ত
নিরখি রহুঁ চহু ওর নিমিখন-দরশরস-সুখে ভাসয়ে ॥

*rūpa pībaite matta atiśaya karata bhūsurabṛnda jaya jaya*
*bandīgaṇa-mana modita ghana ghana bimala yaśa parakāśaye |*
*teji nija nija geha dhāyata nārīpuruṣa na theha pāyata*
*nirakhi rahum̐ cahu ora nimikhana-daraśarasa-sukhe bhāsaye ||*

*Word for word:* rūpa pībaite — drinking His beauty; matta atiśaya — greatly intoxicated; karata bhūsurabṛnda jaya jaya — the brahmanas cry "jaya, jaya"; bandīgaṇa-mana modita — the bards rejoice; ghana ghana — again and again; bimala yaśa parakāśaye — proclaim His spotless fame; teji nija nija geha — leaving their homes; dhāyata nārīpuruṣa — men and women run; na theha pāyata — finding no rest; nirakhi rahum̐ cahu ora — gaze from all sides; nimikhana — unblinking; daraśa-rasa-sukhe bhāsaye — float in the bliss of beholding

**21.2.** Intoxicated by drinking His beauty, the brahmanas cry "Jaya, jaya";
the bards rejoice and again and again proclaim His spotless fame;
leaving their homes, men and women run, finding no rest,
and, unblinking, gaze at Him from all sides, floating in the bliss of beholding.

গান করু গুণী তাল-শ্রুতি-সুর রাগ মূরছন গ্রাম-সুমধুর
নটত নর্তক উঘটিত কতক থৈতা থৈ থৈ নিনি নি না ।
বাদ্য বাদক বাওয়ে বহুতর তাল প্রকট না হোত পটতর
থোঙ্ক না না না না খুঙ্গ খুঙ্কট ধোধিলঙ্গ ধিকি ধিকি নিনা ॥

*gāna karu guṇī tāla-śruti-sura rāga mūrachana grāma-sumadhura*
*naṭata nartaka ughaṭita kataka thaitā thai thai nini ni nā |*
*bādya bādaka bāoye bahutara tāla prakaṭa nā hota paṭatara*
*thoṅka nā nā nā nā khuṅga khuṅkaṭa dhodhilaṅga dhiki dhiki ninā ||*

*Word for word:* gāna karu guṇī — skilled singers sing; tāla-śruti-sura — keeping tala, shruti and svara; rāga mūrachana grāma-sumadhura — sweet ragas with murchhanas and gramas; naṭata nartaka — dancers dance; ughaṭita — beating out; kataka thaitā thai thai nini ni nā — (dance syllables); bādya bādaka bāoye bahutara — musicians play many instruments; tāla prakaṭa nā hota paṭatara — their skill has no equal; thoṅka nā nā nā nā khuṅga khuṅkaṭa dhodhilaṅga dhiki dhiki ninā — (drum syllables)

**21.3.** Skilled singers sing, keeping tala, shruti and svara, the sweet ragas with their murchhanas and gramas;
dancers dance, beating out: "kataka thaita thai-thai nini ni na";
musicians play many instruments — their skill has no equal:
"thongka na na na na khunga khungkata dhodhilanga dhiki-dhiki nina".

দীপ-দমকে অসংখ্য ক্ষিতি-পর দিবস সব ভেল রজনী উজোর
বিপুল-কলকলধ্বনি-নিরত সব লোক গতি-পথ শোহয়ে ।
গগনগত লখি দেব অলখিত সরস বরখত কুসুম পুলকিত
দাস নরহরি-পহুঁক অতুল বিলাস জন-মন মোহয়ে ॥

*dīpa-damake asaṃkhya kṣiti-para dibasa saba bhela rajanī ujora*
*bipula-kalakaladhvani-nirata saba loka gati-patha śohaye |*
*gaganagata lakhi deba alakhita sarasa barakhata kusuma pulakita*
*dāsa narahari-pahum̐ka atula bilāsa jana-mana mohaye ||*

*Word for word:* dīpa-damake — by the glare of torches; asaṃkhya kṣiti-para — countless on the earth; dibasa saba bhela rajanī ujora — the night became bright as day; bipula-kalakaladhvani-nirata — amid a great din; saba loka gati-patha śohaye — all the people fill the roads; gaganagata lakhi — seeing from the sky; deba alakhita — the gods unseen; sarasa barakhata kusuma — shower flowers lavishly; pulakita — thrilled; dāsa narahari-pahum̐ka — of the Lord of Narahari Dasa; atula bilāsa — the matchless play; jana-mana mohaye — enchants people's minds

**21.4.** By the glare of countless torches on the earth the night became bright as day;
amid a great din all the people fill the roads;
seeing from the sky, the gods unseen, thrilled with joy, shower flowers lavishly;
the matchless play of the Lord of Narahari Dasa enchants people's minds.[^24-42]

[^24-41]: GPT1 — pp. 435–436, no. 72 ("deśapāla"; scan, PDF pp. 694–695; the heading is garbled in the OCR — "৭২ parda"); GPT2 — section 6.1, no. 72. **The catalogue did not know it**
(new row NG-308). BR 12 (ed. 1912, p. 993; ed. 1960, vv. 3973–3976): "at dusk the Lord set out from Badagachhi to Saligrama for the wedding; instruments sounded…";
then follows the wedding in Suryadasa's house ("according to the custom of the world and the shastras Suryadasa gave Nityananda his two daughters", v. 3983).
Readings: 21.2 GPT1 (scan) "karata bhūsurabṛnda jaya jaya" (OCR "tṛṣabṛnda"), BR "bhūmsurabṛnda"; 21.4 BR "dibasa sama bhela rajanī ujora", "saptalokagati patha
śohaye" (GPT "divasa sava", "sava loka gati-patha"). The onomatopoeic syllables of drums and dance (21.3) differ among the witnesses; given after GPT1. Not in the PK,
KGC, PS, GCC. B.
[^24-42]: Tala is rhythm, shruti and svara are microtones and tones, murchhana and grama are the modes of classical music. Haladhara ("bearer of the plough") is a
name of Balarama. On Nityananda's wedding see note 40.

## 22. Narahari — "bhubanapābana nitāi mora…" (GPT1 p. 436, no. 73; BR)
*Nityananda goes to the house of Gadadhara Dasa: He calls "Gora!", walks like an intoxicated elephant, with a malati garland on His chest;
whomever He glances at even once He plunges into the ocean of prema; the poet laments that he did not serve Him. Raga dhanashi.
**Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^24-43]

ভুবনপাবন নিতাই মোর । না জানি কি ভাবে সদাই ভোর ॥

*bhubanapābana nitāi mora | nā jāni ki bhābe sadāi bhora ||*

*Word for word:* bhubanapābana — purifier of the world; nitāi mora — my Nitai; nā jāni — who knows; ki bhābe — in what bhava; sadāi bhora — ever absorbed

**22.1.** My Nitai, the purifier of the world —
who knows in what bhava He is, ever absorbed in it!

গোরা গোরা বলি দু-বাহু তুলি । মত্তগজ যেন চলয়ে ঢুলি ॥

*gorā gorā bali du-bāhu tuli | mattagaja yena calaye ḍhuli ||*

*Word for word:* gorā gorā bali — calling "Gora, Gora"; du-bāhu tuli — raises both arms; mattagaja yena — like an intoxicated elephant; calaye ḍhuli — goes swaying

**22.2.** Calling "Gora, Gora!", He raises both arms
and goes swaying like an intoxicated elephant.

কণ্ঠে ঝলমল মালতী-মালা । পরিসর বুকে করয়ে খেলা ॥

*kaṇṭhe jhalamala mālatī-mālā | parisara buke karaye khelā ||*

*Word for word:* kaṇṭhe — on the neck; jhalamala — glitters; mālatī-mālā — a malati garland; parisara buke — on the broad chest; karaye khelā — plays

**22.3.** On His neck a malati garland glitters,
playing upon His broad chest.

সুললিত-মুখে মধুর হাসি । চাঁদে ঢালে যেন অমিঞা-রাশি ॥

*sulalita-mukhe madhura hāsi | cām̐de ḍhāle yena amiñā-rāśi ||*

*Word for word:* sulalita-mukhe — on the lovely face; madhura hāsi — a sweet smile; cām̐de ḍhāle yena — as if the moon pours; amiñā-rāśi — heaps of nectar

**22.4.** On His lovely face — a sweet smile,
as if the moon were pouring out heaps of nectar.

টলমল জলজারুণ আঁখি । সে চাহনি চারু করুণা মাখি ॥

*ṭalamala jalajāruṇa ām̐khi | se cāhani cāru karuṇā mākhi ||*

*Word for word:* ṭalamala — brimming; jalajāruṇa ām̐khi — eyes red as lotuses; se cāhani — that glance; cāru karuṇā mākhi — suffused with lovely compassion

**22.5.** His eyes, red as lotuses, brim with tears;
that glance is suffused with lovely compassion.

বারেক সে আঁখে দেখয়ে যারে । প্রেমের পাথারে ভাসায় তারে ॥

*bāreka se ām̐khe dekhaye yāre | premera pāthāre bhāsāya tāre ||*

*Word for word:* bāreka — even once; se ām̐khe — with those eyes; dekhaye yāre — whomever He looks at; premera pāthāre — in the ocean of prema; bhāsāya tāre — He sets afloat

**22.6.** Whomever He looks at even once with those eyes,
He plunges into the ocean of prema.

দীনহীন দুঃখী কিছু না বাছে । হেন প্রেমদাতা কে আর আছে ॥

*dīnahīna duḥkhī kichu nā bāche | hena premadātā ke āra āche ||*

*Word for word:* dīnahīna duḥkhī — the poor, lowly, wretched; kichu nā bāche — He rejects no one; hena premadātā — such a giver of prema; ke āra āche — who else is there

**22.7.** The poor, the lowly, the wretched — He rejects no one:
who else gives prema like this?

নরহরি হেন প্রভু না ভজি । বিষয়-বিষেতে রহিল মজি ॥

*narahari hena prabhu nā bhaji | biṣaya-biṣete rahila maji ||*

*Word for word:* narahari — Narahari; hena prabhu — such a Lord; nā bhaji — not serving; biṣaya-biṣete — in the poison of sense objects; rahila maji — stayed drowning

**22.8.** Narahari did not serve such a Lord —
and stayed drowning in the poison of sense objects.[^24-44]

[^24-43]: GPT1 — p. 436, no. 73 ("dhānaśī"; scan, PDF p. 695); GPT2 — section 6.1, no. 73. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-309; see note 39). BR 12 (ed. 1912, p. 970;
ed. 1960, vv. 3680–3687): "having stayed at Panihati, He set out for Navadvipa to see Ai (Shachi); the Purifier of the world with His companions, absorbed in bhava,
goes to the house of Gadadhara Dasa"; then follows Gadadhara Dasa's mercy to the kazi of that village (v. 3689). Readings: 22.8 GPT1 "biṣayabiśeṣe rahila maji" — BR
"biṣaya-biṣete rahila maji'" ("drowning in the poison of sense objects"; adopted). Not in the PK, KGC, PS, GCC. B.
[^24-44]: "Like an intoxicated elephant" is an image of the majestic gait of Nityananda, intoxicated with prema for Gaura, not with worldly drink. Gadadhara Dasa
is a companion of Nityananda; on his house and the kazi — CB Antya-khanda.

## 23. Narahari — "nitāi guṇanidhi śobhāra abadhi…" (GPT1 pp. 436–437, no. 74; BR)
*Khardaha: Nityananda's beauty, outshining the morning sun; He walks swaying like an elephant, calling "Gora!", with tears of bliss; gods and
men run to touch His feet, and the age of Kali trembles before His might. Raga dhanashi. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is
in the BR.*[^24-45]

নিতাই গুণনিধি শোভার অবধি কি সুধায় বিধি গড়িল সাধে ।
প্রভাতের ভানু জিনি তনুছটা হেরিয়া কেমন ধৈরজ বাঁধে ॥

*nitāi guṇanidhi śobhāra abadhi ki sudhāya bidhi gaṛila sādhe |*
*prabhātera bhānu jini tanuchaṭā heriyā kemana dhairaja bām̐dhe ||*

*Word for word:* nitāi — Nitai; guṇanidhi — treasure of virtues; śobhāra abadhi — the utmost of beauty; ki sudhāya — from what nectar; bidhi gaṛila sādhe — the Creator lovingly fashioned; prabhātera bhānu jini — outshining the morning sun; tanuchaṭā — the radiance of the body; heriyā — seeing; kemana dhairaja bām̐dhe — how can one keep composure

**23.1.** Nitai — treasure of virtues, the utmost of beauty: from what nectar did the Creator so lovingly fashion Him!
The radiance of His body outshines the morning sun — seeing it, who could keep composure?

আজানুলম্বিত ভুজ ভুজঙ্গম ভঙ্গী নিরুপম রঙ্গেতে ভাসি ।
বদন শরদবিধু-ঘটা ঘন বরিষয়ে সুধা ঈষৎ হাসি ॥

*ājānulambita bhuja bhujaṅgama bhaṅgī nirupama raṅgete bhāsi |*
*badana śaradabidhu-ghaṭā ghana bariṣaye sudhā īṣat hāsi ||*

*Word for word:* ājānulambita — reaching to the knees; bhuja bhujaṅgama — arms like serpents; bhaṅgī nirupama — matchless movements; raṅgete bhāsi — floating in joy; badana — the face; śaradabidhu-ghaṭā ghana — a host of autumn moons; bariṣaye sudhā — sheds nectar; īṣat hāsi — with a slight smile

**23.2.** His arms reach to His knees like serpents; His matchless movements float in joy;
His face — a host of autumn moons — sheds nectar with a slight smile.

গোরা গোরা বলি গর গর হিয়া হেলি দুলি চলে কুঞ্জর-পারা ।
টলমল জলজারুণ-লোচনে ঝর ঝর ঝরে আনন্দধারা ॥

*gorā gorā bali gara gara hiyā heli duli cale kuñjara-pārā |*
*ṭalamala jalajāruṇa-locane jhara jhara jhare ānandadhārā ||*

*Word for word:* gorā gorā bali — calling "Gora, Gora"; gara gara hiyā — His heart overflowing; heli duli — swaying; cale kuñjara-pārā — goes like an elephant; ṭalamala — trembling; jalajāruṇa-locane — from eyes red as lotuses; jhara jhara jhare — pour down; ānanda-dhārā — streams of bliss

**23.3.** Calling "Gora, Gora!", His heart overflowing, He goes swaying like an elephant;
from His trembling eyes, red as lotuses, streams of bliss pour down.

সুর-নরগণ ধায় চারিপাশে সে দুলহ পদ পরশ-আশে ।
দাস নরহরি পহুঁ-পরতাপে বলী কলিকাল কাঁপয়ে ত্রাসে ॥

*sura-naragaṇa dhāya cāripāśe se dulaha pada paraśa-āśe |*
*dāsa narahari pahum̐-paratāpe balī kalikāla kām̐paye trāse ||*

*Word for word:* sura-naragaṇa — gods and men; dhāya cāripāśe — run from all sides; se dulaha pada — those rarest feet; paraśa-āśe — in the hope of touching; dāsa narahari — Narahari Dasa; pahum̐-paratāpe — before the Lord's might; balī kalikāla — the mighty age of Kali; kām̐paye trāse — trembles with fear

**23.4.** Gods and men run to Him from all sides in the hope of touching those rarest feet;
Narahari Dasa: before the Lord's might the mighty age of Kali trembles with fear.[^24-46]

[^24-45]: GPT1 — pp. 436–437, no. 74 ("dhānaśī"; scan, PDF pp. 695–696); GPT2 — section 6.1, no. 74. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-310). BR 12 (ed. 1912, pp. 971–972;
ed. 1960, vv. 3698–3701): "Lord Nityananda came to Khardaha, surrounded by His companions; in the middle, Nityananda, enchanting Kamadeva"; before it is a pada of
Vrindavana Dasa ("bande prabhu nityānanda", GPT 6.1 no. 5). Readings: 23.1 BR "gaṛhila sādhe", "prabhātera bhānu jini' tanuchaṭā"; 23.3 BR "hili' duli' cale kuñjara-pārā". Not
in the PK, KGC, PS, GCC. B.
[^24-46]: Nityananda in Khardaha — CB Antya 5. The age of Kali "trembles": with Nityananda's coming the power of Kali recedes, and the holy name and prema flood Gauda.

## 24. Narahari — "nitāi karuṇānidhi…" (GPT1 p. 437, no. 75; BR)
*Khardaha: Nityananda dances with His companions, making the poor rich in prema; He knows neither day nor night, weeps calling "Gora!", is
covered with dust; all weep hearing of His virtues — only Narahari is far away. Raga kamoda. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada
is in the BR.*[^24-47]

নিতাই করুণানিধি । আনি মিলাইল বিধি ॥

*nitāi karuṇānidhi | āni milāila bidhi ||*

*Word for word:* nitāi — Nitai; karuṇānidhi — ocean of mercy; āni — bringing; milāila — has united [with us]; bidhi — Providence

**24.1.** Nitai — an ocean of mercy: Providence has brought Him to us.

দীনহীন দুখী জনে । ধনী কৈল প্রেমধনে ॥

*dīnahīna dukhī jane | dhanī kaila premadhane ||*

*Word for word:* dīnahīna dukhī jane — the poor, lowly and wretched; dhanī kaila — made rich; premadhane — with the wealth of prema

**24.2.** The poor, the lowly and the wretched He made rich, giving them the wealth of prema.

প্রিয় পরিকর সঙ্গে । নাচিয়া বুলয় রঙ্গে ॥

*priya parikara saṅge | nāciyā bulaya raṅge ||*

*Word for word:* priya parikara saṅge — with the dear companions; nāciyā bulaya — goes about dancing; raṅge — joyfully

**24.3.** With His dear companions He goes about, joyfully dancing.

না জানি কি প্রেমে মাতি । না জানে দিবস রাতি ॥

*nā jāni ki preme māti | nā jāne dibasa rāti ||*

*Word for word:* nā jāni — who knows; ki preme māti — with what prema intoxicated; nā jāne — He knows not; dibasa rāti — day or night

**24.4.** Who knows with what prema He is intoxicated: He knows neither day nor night.

গোরা গোরা বলি কাঁদে । তিলে না ধৈরজ বাঁধে ॥

*gorā gorā bali kām̐de | tile nā dhairaja bām̐dhe ||*

*Word for word:* gorā gorā bali — calling "Gora, Gora"; kām̐de — He weeps; tile — for a moment; nā dhairaja bām̐dhe — cannot restrain Himself

**24.5.** Calling "Gora, Gora!", He weeps; not for a moment can He restrain Himself.

ধূলি-ধূসরিত দেহা । তা হেরি কে ধরে থেহা ॥

*dhūli-dhūsarita dehā | tā heri ke dhare thehā ||*

*Word for word:* dhūli-dhūsarita dehā — the body grey with dust; tā heri — seeing that; ke dhare thehā — who can stay steady

**24.6.** His body is grey with dust — seeing this, who can stay steady?

গুণে কেবা নাহি ঝুরে । একা নরহরি দূরে ॥

*guṇe kebā nāhi jhure | ekā narahari dūre ||*

*Word for word:* guṇe — over His virtues; kebā nāhi jhure — who does not weep; ekā narahari — Narahari alone; dūre — is far away

**24.7.** Who does not weep over His virtues? Narahari alone is far away.[^24-48]

[^24-47]: GPT1 — p. 437, no. 75 ("kāmoda"; scan, PDF p. 696); GPT2 — section 6.1, no. 75, p. ≈288 (catalogue: NG-208, "in the BR"). BR 12 (ed. 1912, p. 972; ed. 1960, vv. 3706–3711):
"coming to Khardaha, the Lord with His people — in the temple-house of Purandara Pandita… dances and distributes the rarest treasure". Readings: 24.1 BR "āni'
bilāyala bidhi" ("Providence brought and distributed [Him]"); couplet 24.5 is absent from the BR. Not in the PK, KGC, PS, GCC. B.
[^24-48]: "Only Narahari is far away" — the poet's humility (cf. 16.12, 22.8). Purandara Pandita is a companion of Nityananda.

## 25. Narahari — "gorāpreme mātiyā nitāi…" (GPT1 p. 437, no. 76; BR)
*The same place: intoxicated with love for Gaura, Nityananda dances, falls into the arms of the fallen, weeps, thrills; Kamadeva swoons at
His beauty; the poet drowns in the beauty of His feet. Raga dhanashi. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^24-49]

গোরাপ্রেমে মাতিয়া নিতাই । জগত মাতায় সকরুণ দিঠে চাই ॥

*gorāpreme mātiyā nitāi | jagata mātāya sakaruṇa diṭhe cāi ||*

*Word for word:* gorāpreme mātiyā — intoxicated with love for Gora; nitāi — Nitai; jagata mātāya — intoxicates the world; sakaruṇa diṭhe cāi — looking with compassionate eyes

**25.1.** Intoxicated with love for Gora, Nitai
intoxicates the world, looking at it with compassionate eyes.

নাচয়ে আজানু বাহু তুলি । পতিতের কোলেতে পড়য়ে ঢুলি ঢুলি ॥

*nācaye ājānu bāhu tuli | patitera kolete paṛaye ḍhuli ḍhuli ||*

*Word for word:* nācaye — dances; ājānu bāhu tuli — raising His arms that reach to the knees; patitera kolete — into the embrace of the fallen; paṛaye ḍhuli ḍhuli — falls, swaying

**25.2.** He dances, raising His arms that reach to His knees,
and, swaying, falls into the embrace of the fallen.

কত সুখে হিয়া না উথলে । মুখ বুক ভাসি যায় নয়নের জলে ॥

*kata sukhe hiyā nā uthale | mukha buka bhāsi yāya nayanera jale ||*

*Word for word:* kata sukhe — with what happiness; hiyā nā uthale — how the heart overflows; mukha buka — face and chest; bhāsi yāya — are washed; nayanera jale — by the tears of the eyes

**25.3.** How His heart overflows with happiness!
Face and chest are washed by the tears from His eyes.

প্রতি অঙ্গে পুলকের ঘটা । মদন মূরছি পড়ে দেখি রূপছটা ॥

*prati aṅge pulakera ghaṭā | madana mūrachi paṛe dekhi rūpachaṭā ||*

*Word for word:* prati aṅge — on every limb; pulakera ghaṭā — waves of thrill; madana mūrachi paṛe — Madana swoons; dekhi rūpachaṭā — seeing the radiance of His form

**25.4.** On every limb — waves of thrill;
Madana swoons, seeing the radiance of His form.

সুচাঁদবদনে মৃদু হাসি । কহিতে মধুর কথা ঢালে সুধারাশি ॥

*sucām̐dabadane mṛdu hāsi | kahite madhura kathā ḍhāle sudhārāśi ||*

*Word for word:* sucām̐da-badane — on the lovely moon-face; mṛdu hāsi — a gentle smile; kahite madhura kathā — speaking sweet words; ḍhāle sudhārāśi — pours out heaps of nectar

**25.5.** On His lovely moon-face, a gentle smile;
speaking sweet words, He pours out heaps of nectar.

কি নব ভঙ্গিমা রাঙ্গা পায় । নরহরি-পরাণ মজিল যেন তায় ॥

*ki naba bhaṅgimā rāṅgā pāya | narahari-parāṇa majila yena tāya ||*

*Word for word:* ki naba bhaṅgimā — what new grace; rāṅgā pāya — in the crimson feet; narahari-parāṇa — Narahari's life; majila — has drowned; yena — as it were; tāya — in it

**25.6.** What new grace in His crimson feet!
Narahari's life has, as it were, drowned in it.[^24-50]

[^24-49]: GPT1 — p. 437, no. 76 ("dhānaśī"; scan, PDF p. 696); GPT2 — section 6.1, no. 76. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-311). BR 12 (ed. 1912, p. 972; ed. 1960, vv. 3712–3717;
"punaḥ dhānaśī", right after no. 75). Readings: 25.6 GPT1 (scan) "narahari-parāṇa majila mene tāya" — BR "yena tāya" (adopted). Not in the PK, KGC, PS, GCC. B.
[^24-50]: "Intoxicated", "intoxicates" — with prema for Gaura; Nityananda gives the world the same intoxication of love for the Lord. Madana is Kamadeva: his beauty
pales before Nityananda's spiritual beauty.

## 26. Narahari — "bhubane jaya jaya nitāi dayāmaya…" (GPT1 p. 437, no. 77; BR)
*The same place: merciful Nitai removes the fear of the round of births and maddens the fallen with prema; He dances calling "Gaurahari!",
falls in the dust; the whole world, seeing Him, forgets its sorrow. Raga gurjari. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in
the BR.*[^24-51]

ভুবনে জয় জয় নিতাই দয়াময় হরয়ে ভবভয় নিজগুণে ।
অধম দুরগত তাহারে উনমত করই অবিরত প্রেমদানে ॥

*bhubane jaya jaya nitāi dayāmaya haraye bhababhaya nijaguṇe |*
*adhama duragata tāhāre unamata karai abirata premadāne ||*

*Word for word:* bhubane jaya jaya — through the world "jaya, jaya"; nitāi dayāmaya — merciful Nitai; haraye bhababhaya — removes the fear of samsara; nijaguṇe — by His goodness; adhama duragata — the low and wretched; tāhāre unamata — them into ecstasy; karai abirata — ceaselessly brings; premadāne — by the gift of prema

**26.1.** Through all the world — "Jaya, jaya!": merciful Nitai by His goodness removes the fear of samsara;
the low and wretched He ceaselessly maddens with the gift of prema.

গৌরহরি বলি নাচয়ে বাহু তুলি পড়য়ে ঢুলি ঢুলি ক্ষিতিতলে ।
কোমল কলেবর কি হেম-ধরাধর সে ধূলি-ধূসর শোহে ভালে ॥

*gaurahari bali nācaye bāhu tuli paṛaye ḍhuli ḍhuli kṣititale |*
*komala kalebara ki hema-dharādhara se dhūli-dhūsara śohe bhāle ||*

*Word for word:* gaurahari bali — calling "Gaurahari"; nācaye bāhu tuli — dances with arms raised; paṛaye ḍhuli ḍhuli kṣititale — falls swaying to the ground; komala kalebara — the tender body; ki hema-dharādhara — or a golden mountain; se dhūli-dhūsara — grey with that dust; śohe bhāle — shines beautifully

**26.2.** Calling "Gaurahari!", He dances with arms raised and, swaying, falls to the ground;
His tender body — or a golden mountain? — is covered with dust, and how beautiful it is in it!

জিনি কমলদল নয়ন টলমল সঘনে ছল ছল জলধারা ।
বদনে মৃদু হাসি ঢালয়ে সুধারাশি কলুষ-তমনাশী শশী পারা ॥

*jini kamaladala nayana ṭalamala saghane chala chala jaladhārā |*
*badane mṛdu hāsi ḍhālaye sudhārāśi kaluṣa-tamanāśī śaśī pārā ||*

*Word for word:* jini kamaladala — surpassing lotus petals; nayana ṭalamala — eyes brimming; saghane chala chala — again and again; jaladhārā — streams of tears; badane mṛdu hāsi — a gentle smile on the face; ḍhālaye sudhārāśi — pours heaps of nectar; kaluṣa-tamanāśī — dispelling the darkness of sin; śaśī pārā — like the moon

**26.3.** His eyes, surpassing lotus petals, brim with tears, and again and again the streams flow;
on His face a gentle smile pours out heaps of nectar — a moon dispelling the darkness of sin.

কি ভাবে গর গর কাঁপয়ে থর থর রঙ্গ কি কব নরহরি দাসে ।
অখিল চরাচর নিরখি পহুঁ বর ভুলল দুঃখভর সুখে ভাসে ॥

*ki bhābe gara gara kām̐paye thara thara raṅga ki kaba narahari dāse |*
*akhila carācara nirakhi pahum̐ bara bhulala duḥkhabhara sukhe bhāse ||*

*Word for word:* ki bhābe gara gara — in what bhava overflowing; kām̐paye thara thara — trembles all over; raṅga ki kaba — how can describe this play; narahari dāse — Narahari Dasa; akhila carācara — all moving and unmoving beings; nirakhi pahum̐ bara — seeing the excellent Lord; bhulala duḥkhabhara — forgot the burden of sorrow; sukhe bhāse — float in happiness

**26.4.** In what bhava He overflows, trembling all over — how can Narahari Dasa describe this play?
All moving and unmoving beings, seeing the excellent Lord, have forgotten the burden of sorrow and float in happiness.[^24-52]

[^24-51]: GPT1 — p. 437, no. 77 ("gujari"; scan, PDF p. 696); GPT2 — section 6.1, no. 77. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-312). BR 12 (ed. 1912, pp. 972–973; ed. 1960,
vv. 3718–3721; "punaḥ gurjarī"); after it Nityananda leaves Khardaha for Saptagrama, for Uddharana Datta. Readings: 26.2 BR "gaurahari buli'"; 26.3 BR "kaluṣa tama nāśi'
śaśī-pārā". Not in the PK, KGC, PS, GCC. B.
[^24-52]: "Maddens" (unamata) — with the gift of prema, not with worldly madness. Nityananda removes the fear of samsara: His mercy as the original guru opens the
way to Gaura (cf. no. 28).

## 27. Narahari — "nityānanda haraṣa hiyā māha…" (GPT1 pp. 437–438, no. 78; GCC)
