*Morning in Shachi's house, the Lord among the companions: Nityananda, gazing at His younger brother, plunges into the ocean of His beauty
and thinks: "Before, I saw the wondrous dark body — but Gaura's golden body captivates me still more; this secret rasa cannot be fathomed";
He prays never to be separated from Him and longs for a body made all of eyes. Raga velavali. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the
pada is in the GCC; Vrajabuli.*[^24-53]

নিত্যানন্দ হরষ হিয়া মাহ ।
অনুজ নিহারি বিসারি সকল উহ শোভা-সায়রে করু অবগাহ ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*nityānanda haraṣa hiyā māha |*
*anuja nihāri bisāri sakala uha śobhā-sāyare karu abagāha || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* nityānanda — Nityananda; haraṣa hiyā māha — joy in the heart; anuja nihāri — gazing at His younger brother; bisāri sakala — forgetting everything; uha śobhā-sāyare — into that ocean of beauty; karu abagāha — plunges

**27.1.** Joy in Nityananda's heart:
gazing at His younger brother, forgetting everything, He plunges into that ocean of beauty.

মনহি বিচার করত হাম পুরুবহি পেখনু অপরূপ শ্যামর দেহ ।
তদধিক চিত হরি লেত গৌরতনু কি বুঝব অতএ গূঢ় রস এহ ॥

*manahi bicāra karata hāma purubahi pekhanu aparūpa śyāmara deha |*
*tadadhika cita hari leta gauratanu ki bujhaba atae gūṛha rasa eha ||*

*Word for word:* manahi bicāra karata — reflects in His mind; hāma purubahi — I before; pekhanu — saw; aparūpa śyāmara deha — the wondrous dark body; tadadhika — more than that; cita hari leta — steals the heart; gauratanu — Gaura's body; ki bujhaba — how can I fathom; atae — therefore; gūṛha rasa eha — this secret rasa

**27.2.** In His mind He reflects: "Before, I saw the wondrous dark body;
but Gaura's body steals my heart still more — how can I fathom this secret rasa?

এ অতি দুলহ অবহুঁ কোই ভাঁতিক করি প্রসন্ন বরণে অব মাগি ।
কবহু ন ইহ বিচ্ছেদ সতত মম লোচনযুগে জনু রহে ইহ লাগি ॥

*e ati dulaha abahum̐ koi bhām̐tika kari prasanna baraṇe aba māgi |*
*kabahu na iha biccheda satata mama locanayuge janu rahe iha lāgi ||*

*Word for word:* e ati dulaha — this is the rarest; abahum̐ — now; koi bhām̐tika — somehow; kari prasanna — propitiating; baraṇe aba māgi — I will ask for a boon; kabahu na iha biccheda — may there never be separation; satata — always; mama locanayuge — to my two eyes; janu rahe iha lāgi — may He stay fixed

**27.3.** This is the rarest treasure — now, somehow propitiating [the Creator], I will ask him for a boon:
may there never be separation — may He stay fixed forever before my eyes."

ঐছে আশ কত উপজত অন্তরে প্রেমক-গতি অতুল অপার ।
চাহত বিহিক নয়নময় তনু পুন আতুর নরহরি-পহুঁ অনিবার ॥

*aiche āśa kata upajata antare premaka-gati atula apāra |*
*cāhata bihika nayanamaya tanu puna ātura narahari-pahum̐ anibāra ||*

*Word for word:* aiche āśa kata — such hopes; upajata antare — arise in the heart; premaka-gati — the way of prema; atula apāra — matchless and boundless; cāhata — asks; bihika — of the Creator; nayanamaya tanu — a body made of eyes; puna — again; ātura — longing; narahari-pahum̐ — the poet Narahari's Lord; anibāra — ceaselessly

**27.4.** Such hopes arise in His heart — the way of prema is matchless and boundless;
again and again, in longing, the poet Narahari's Lord asks the Creator for a body made all of eyes.[^24-54]

[^24-53]: GPT1 — pp. 437–438, no. 78 ("belābalī"; scan, PDF pp. 696–697); GPT2 — section 6.1, no. 78. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-313). GCC — kirana 4 ("the Lord among
the devotees", morning in Shachi's courtyard), pada 8 ("belābalī"); before it (pada 7) is a pada of Ghanashyama on Nityananda gazing at Gaura's face amid the companions.
Readings: 27.1 GCC "nityānanda harṣa hiya māha", "anuja nihāri bisāri sakala"; 27.4 GCC "premaka gati". Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS. B.
[^24-54]: Nityananda is Balarama: "before" (in Vraja) He saw dark Krishna, and now Krishna has appeared as golden Gaura — in the mood and radiance of Radha (CC Adi 1.5),
and this "secret rasa" captivates Him even more. The prayer for a "body of eyes" is like the gopis' complaint against the Creator who made eyelids (Bhag. 10.31.15):
Nityananda, the Lord Himself, relishes the mood of a loving servant and brother. The poet Narahari's Lord here is Nityananda.

## 28. Narahari — "aparūpa pahum̐ka prema balihāri…" (GPT1 p. 438, no. 80; GCC)
*The same place: Nityananda, rapt in prema, cannot stand steady; Abhirama hastens up and gives Him his shoulder, and Nityananda, gazing at
Gaura's moon-face, laughs; the poet: whoever hopes to attain Gaura's feet bypassing Nitai is the one fool in all three worlds. Raga veloyara. **Attribution:
probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC; Vrajabuli.*[^24-55]

অপরূপ পহুঁক প্রেম বলিহারি ।
গর গর অন্তর তরল অঙ্গ-গতি অথির চরণ ধৃতি ধরণ না পারি ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*aparūpa pahum̐ka prema balihāri |*
*gara gara antara tarala aṅga-gati athira caraṇa dhṛti dharaṇa nā pāri || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* aparūpa — wondrous; pahum̐ka prema — the Lord's prema; balihāri — I give myself for it; gara gara antara — the heart overflowing; tarala aṅga-gati — unsteady movements; athira caraṇa — unsteady feet; dhṛti dharaṇa nā pāri — cannot keep composure

**28.1.** Wondrous is the Lord's prema — I give myself for it!
His heart overflowing, His movements wavering, His feet unsteady — He cannot restrain Himself.

দূরহি দূর অবলোকি তুরিত গতি আওল নিয়ড়ে সুঘড় অভিরাম ।
অধিক অবশ বশ নাহি বসন পরি তাকর কন্ধে ধরল কর বাম ॥

*dūrahi dūra abaloki turita gati āola niyaṛe sughaṛa abhirāma |*
*adhika abaśa baśa nāhi basana pari tākara kandhe dharala kara bāma ||*

*Word for word:* dūrahi dūra abaloki — seeing from afar; turita gati — with swift steps; āola niyaṛe — came near; sughaṛa abhirāma — handsome Abhirama; adhika abaśa — utterly beside Himself; baśa nāhi basana — not in control of His cloth; pari tākara kandhe — on his shoulder; dharala kara bāma — laid His left hand

**28.2.** Seeing [this] from afar, handsome Abhirama came up to Him with swift steps;
[Nitai], utterly beside Himself, not even in control of His cloth, laid His left hand on his shoulder.

গৌরক মুখচন্দ নিরখি ঘন হাসত মৃদু মৃদু অধর উজোর ।
অনুপম ভঙ্গী ভূরি শোভা শেষ শারদ বরণে শকত নাহি থোর ॥

*gauraka mukhacanda nirakhi ghana hāsata mṛdu mṛdu adhara ujora |*
*anupama bhaṅgī bhūri śobhā śeṣa śārada baraṇe śakata nāhi thora ||*

*Word for word:* gauraka mukhacanda — Gaura's moon-face; nirakhi — gazing at; ghana hāsata — laughs again and again; mṛdu mṛdu — softly, softly; adhara ujora — His lips shining; anupama bhaṅgī — of the matchless movements; bhūri śobhā — the great beauty; śeṣa śārada — Shesha and Sharada; baraṇe śakata nāhi thora — cannot describe even a little

**28.3.** Gazing at Gaura's moon-face, He laughs again and again — softly, softly, His lips shining;
not even a little of the beauty of His matchless movements could Shesha or Sharada describe.

ইহ নিতাই বিনু গৌর-বিমল-পদপদ্ম পাওব বলি যো করু আশ ।
সো ত্রিজগত মধি মুরুখ এক সব বিফল নিচয় ভণ নরহরি দাস ॥

*iha nitāi binu gaura-bimala-padapadma pāoba bali yo karu āśa |*
*so trijagata madhi murukha eka saba biphala nicaya bhaṇa narahari dāsa ||*

*Word for word:* iha nitāi binu — bypassing this Nitai; gaura-bimala-padapadma — Gaura's pure lotus feet; pāoba — I shall attain; bali yo karu āśa — whoever hopes; so trijagata madhi — he in the three worlds; murukha eka — is the one fool; saba biphala — all is in vain; nicaya — surely; bhaṇa narahari dāsa — says Narahari Dasa

**28.4.** Whoever, bypassing Nitai, hopes to attain Gaura's pure lotus feet
is the one fool in all three worlds: all his efforts are in vain, — says Narahari Dasa.[^24-56]

[^24-55]: GPT1 — p. 438, no. 80 ("beloyāra"; scan, PDF p. 697); GPT2 — section 6.1, no. 80. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-314). GCC — kirana 4, pada 10 ("beloyāra"); before
it is a pada of Ghanashyama (GPT no. 79) on Nityananda intoxicated with His brother's bhava. Readings: 28.1 GCC "aparūpa prema balihārī" (without "pahum̐ka"); 28.2 GCC
"abaloki", "āola niyaṛe", "basana pari tām̐kara kandhe"; 28.3 GCC "gauracandra-mukhacanda", "śobhā śeṣa śārada baraṇa śakata nāhi thora" — "śeṣa" adopted after the GCC (GPT
"śobhā śubha śāradabaraṇa"). Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS. B.
[^24-56]: "Handsome Abhirama" (sughaṛa abhirāma) is Abhirama (Ramadasa) Thakura, a companion of Nityananda, one of the twelve gopalas; Nityananda leans on him in
other padas of the section as well (cf. 6.1 no. 2: "calling 'brother Abhirama!'"). It can also be taken as an epithet — "the handsome, charming [Nitai] came up [to
Gaura] and laid His hand on His shoulder"; the first reading is more natural. Shesha is the thousand-headed serpent who sings the Lord's glories with all his mouths; Sharada is Sarasvati, the goddess of speech. 28.4 is the central
thought of the tradition: Nityananda is the original spiritual master (CC Adi 5), and Gaura's mercy is attained only by His mercy; cf. Narottama Dasa's song
"nitāi-pada-kamala" ("without Nitai one cannot attain Radha and Krishna").

## 29. Narahari — "bilase nitāicām̐da rasabhūpa…" (GPT1 pp. 438–439, no. 81; GCC)
*Nityananda's form from head to foot: a body the colour of gold with kunkuma and dawn, softer than shirisha flowers, its fragrance filling
the quarters; the smile, teeth, eyes, brows, tilaka, earrings, arms, chest, navel, slender waist, blue silk garments, crimson feet; the poet
prays that the radiance of Nitai's toenails may dispel the darkness of his heart. Raga veloyara. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** —
the pada is in the GCC; Vrajabuli.*[^24-57]

বিলসে নিতাইচাঁদ রসভূপ ।
অরুণ-মিলিত-কনকাচল-কুঙ্কুমপুঞ্জ-গঞ্জি জগ-বঞ্চন রূপ ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*bilase nitāicām̐da rasabhūpa |*
*aruṇa-milita-kanakācala-kuṅkumapuñja-gañji jaga-bañcana rūpa || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* bilase — shines; nitāicām̐da — Nitaichand; rasabhūpa — king of rasa; aruṇa-milita — with the dawn; kanakācala — on a golden mountain; kuṅkuma-puñja — a heap of kunkuma; gañji — outdoing; jaga-bañcana rūpa — a form enchanting (lit. "deceiving") the world

**29.1.** Nitaichand, king of rasa, shines!
His form, outdoing a heap of kunkuma with the dawn upon a golden mountain, enchants the world.

ঝলমল অঙ্গ-বলনি অতি অদভুত কোমল শিরীষ-কুসুম বহুদূর ।
কুলবতী যুবতী ধরমভয়-ভঞ্জন তনু-সৌরভ দশ দিশ ভরি পূর ॥

*jhalamala aṅga-balani ati adabhuta komala śirīṣa-kusuma bahudūra |*
*kulabatī yubatī dharamabhaya-bhañjana tanu-saurabha daśa diśa bhari pūra ||*

*Word for word:* jhalamala — shining; aṅga-balani — the radiance of the limbs; ati adabhuta — most wondrous; komala — soft; śirīṣa-kusuma bahu-dūra — far softer than a shirisha flower; kulabatī yubatī — of chaste maidens; dharama-bhaya-bhañjana — shattering the fear for their rules; tanu-saurabha — the fragrance of the body; daśa diśa bhari pūra — fills the ten directions

**29.2.** The radiance of His limbs is wondrous; He is far softer than a shirisha flower;
the fragrance of His body, which shatters chaste maidens' fear for their rules, fills the ten directions.

মধুরিম অধরে মধুর মৃদুহাসি বরিষে সুধা বিধুবদন উজোর ।
মোতিমদাম-দমন-দ্যুতি দশনক বসন সুরুচির চিবুক চিতচোর ॥

*madhurima adhare madhura mṛduhāsi bariṣe sudhā bidhubadana ujora |*
*motimadāma-damana-dyuti daśanaka basana surucira cibuka citacora ||*

*Word for word:* madhurima adhare — sweetness on the lips; madhura mṛduhāsi — a sweet gentle smile; bariṣe sudhā — pours nectar; bidhubadana ujora — the bright moon-face; motimadāma-damana-dyuti — a radiance humbling strings of pearls; daśanaka — of the teeth; basana surucira — the lips are lovely; cibuka citacora — the chin steals hearts

**29.3.** Sweetness on His lips, a sweet gentle smile — His bright moon-face pours nectar;
the gleam of His teeth humbles strings of pearls, His lips are lovely, His chin steals hearts.

বিমল বিশাল কমলদল-লোচন ডগমগ রঙ্গে ভঙ্গী কত ভাঁতি ।
বন্ধুর ভুরুবর বক্র অতনু-ধনু নিন্দই ভুজগ-ভৃঙ্গকুল-পাঁতি ॥

*bimala biśāla kamaladala-locana ḍagamaga raṅge bhaṅgī kata bhām̐ti |*

**29.4.** Pure, large eyes like lotus petals glisten in joy, full of countless movements;
His curved fine brows — Ananga's bow — put to shame serpents and rows of bees.

তিলকিত ভাল চপল শ্রুতিকুণ্ডল নাসা গরুড়-চঞ্চু রুচিকারী ।
সুগঠন গণ্ড গীম গরবিত গুরু ভুজযুগ দ্বিরদ-শুণ্ড-মদহারী ॥

*tilakita bhāla capala śrutikuṇḍala nāsā garuṛa-cañcu rucikārī |*
*sugaṭhana gaṇḍa gīma garabita guru bhujayuga dvirada-śuṇḍa-madahārī ||*

*Word for word:* tilakita bhāla — the forehead with tilaka; capala śruti-kuṇḍala — earrings swaying in the ears; nāsā — the nose; garuṛa-cañcu — like Garuda's beak; rucikārī — lovely; sugaṭhana gaṇḍa — finely sculpted cheeks; gīma garabita — a proud neck; guru bhujayuga — mighty arms; dvirada-śuṇḍa-madahārī — stealing the pride of an elephant's trunk

**29.5.** Tilaka on His forehead, earrings swaying in His ears, His nose like Garuda's beak, lovely;

ত্রিভুবনবিজয় বক্ষ বর পরিসর কঠিন কপাট কি পটতর হোয় ।
নাভি সরসি শৈবাল লোম লস ত্রিবলি ত্রিবেণী কো ধরু ধৃতি জোয় ॥

*tribhubanabijaya bakṣa bara parisara kaṭhina kapāṭa ki paṭatara hoya |*

*Word for word:* tribhubana-bijaya — conqueror of the three worlds; bakṣa bara parisara — the chest, fine and broad; kaṭhina kapāṭa — hard as a gate; ki paṭatara hoya — what can compare; nābhi sarasi — the navel a lake; śaibāla loma lasa — the line of hair its weed; tribali tribeṇī — the three folds, the Triveni; ko dharu dhṛti joya — who keeps composure, gazing

**29.6.** His chest, conqueror of the three worlds, broad and fine — hard as a gate: what can compare?
His navel a lake, the line of hair its weed, the three folds — the Triveni: who can keep composure?

ধৈরজ ধরি কো সিরজিল সুন্দর কেশরী-গরব-খরব কটি ক্ষীণ ।
জন-মন-নয়ন লোভায়ত অপরূপ পহিরণ নীলবসন অতি চীন ॥

*dhairaja dhari ko sirajila sundara keśarī-garaba-kharaba kaṭi kṣīṇa |*

*Word for word:* dhairaja dhari — keeping patience; ko sirajila sundara — who created this beauty; keśarī-garaba-kharaba — humbling the lion's pride; kaṭi kṣīṇa — the slender waist; jana-mana-nayana lobhāyata — entice the minds and eyes of people; aparūpa pahiraṇa — wondrous garments; nīlabasana — blue; ati cīna — of the finest silk

**29.7.** Who, keeping patience, created this beauty? His slender waist humbles the lion's pride;

পীন জঙ্ঘযুগ মৃদুল সুশোভিত গুরু উরু পর্ব সুখদ পরকাশ ।
রাতুল চরণ চারু নখকিরণ এ নরহরি-হৃদয়ক তম করু নাশ ॥

*pīna jaṅghayuga mṛdula suśobhita guru uru parva sukhada parakāśa |*
*rātula caraṇa cāru nakhakiraṇa e narahari-hṛdayaka tama karu nāśa ||*

*Word for word:* pīna jaṅghayuga — full shanks; mṛdula suśobhita — soft and graceful; guru uru parva — mighty thighs and knees; sukhada parakāśa — give joy; rātula caraṇa — crimson feet; cāru nakha-kiraṇa — the lovely radiance of the toenails; e narahari-hṛdayaka — of this Narahari's heart; tama karu nāśa — may they dispel the darkness

**29.8.** His full shanks are soft and graceful, His mighty thighs and knees give joy;
crimson feet, the lovely radiance of the toenails — may they dispel the darkness of this Narahari's heart![^24-58]

[^24-57]: GPT1 — pp. 438–439, no. 81 ("beloyāra"; scan, PDF pp. 697–698; the last pada of section 6.1); GPT2 — section 6.1, no. 81. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-315).
GCC — kirana 4, pada 11 ("beloyāra"; right after no. 80); next (pada 12) is a pada on Advaita's joy (GPT 6.2 no. 5 — no. 1 of chapter 25). Readings: 29.1 GCC
"aruṇamilita-kanakācala-kuṅkumapuñja gañji jaga-bañcana rūpa" ("upon a golden mountain" — after the GCC; GPT "kala-kāñcana", "pure gold"); 29.2 GCC
"kulabatī-yubatī-dharama-bhaya-bhañjana"; 29.8 GCC "e narahari hṛdayaka tama karu nāśa". Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS. B.
[^24-58]: A description of the form "from head to foot" (cf. no. 22 of chapter 23) is a devotional contemplation of the Lord. Blue garments are Balarama's
(Nilambara, "clad in blue"). "Shatters chaste maidens' fear for their rules" (29.2) is the same formula as in 16.7 and 17.4 (see note 32): the Lord's spiritual
beauty, which frees from worldly bonds. Ananga is Kamadeva; the Triveni is the confluence of three rivers at Prayaga; the shirisha is a flower that is the
very type of softness. "Enchants the world" — lit. "deceives the world" (jaga-bañcana): under the guise of an avadhuta Balarama Himself is hidden.

# Chapter 25. Appendix. Padas signed "Narahari" from the Gaura-pada-tarangini — IX: Advaita

*Continuation of the appendix (the introductory note on the two Naraharis, on the arguments for attribution and on the marks in the headings
is in ch. 17). Chapter 25: GPT section 6.2 "Advaita" (GPT1 pp. 439–449) — all fourteen padas signed Narahari (nos. 5–7, 9–11, 13, 15–18, 20, 21, 24):
Advaita among Gaura's companions in the morning at Navadvipa, His form, His thundering calls and His dancing in the kirtana of Gaura's glories, a
survey of His life, a praise, and His advent at Navagram. The signatures of the section were checked throughout, in the OCR and on the scan; the 12th
wave of the Bhakti-ratnakara (BR) at the relevant places, the Gaura-charita-chintamani (GCC, kirana 4) and the section on Advaita in the
Gita-chandrodaya were read continuously. Not translated (outside the appendix): nos. 8, 12, 14, 19, 22, 23 — signed Ghanashyama; no. 4 — no
signature (it ends "the Lord Sankarshana wanders behind them from door to door"); the other padas of the section are by other poets (Vrindavana Dasa,
Lochana, Shyamadasa, Vaishnava Dasa, Kanu, Trilochana, Gokulananda, Balarama Dasa). The base text is GPT1 (doubtful places by the scan), collated
with GPT2, the GCC (ed. 1947), the BR (eds. 1912 and 1960) and the Gita-chandrodaya; the PK, KGC and PS were checked. Advaita Acharya is Maha-Vishnu
Himself and Sadashiva, non-different from Hari (CC Adi 6; the Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika, 11, 76, also calls Him Sadashiva); as with Gaura and
Nityananda, the pronouns referring to Him are capitalized. The notes of the GPT editors are not reproduced.*

## 1. Narahari — "rajanī prabhāta prabhākara sama…" (GPT1 p. 440, section 6.2, no. 5; GCC)
*Morning among the companions: seeing the rising of Gaura's moon-face, Advaita, shining like the sun, beats His armpits in jubilation, walks to
and fro more intoxicated than the king of elephants; His smile is a rain of jasmine; tears flow from His eyes like strings of pearls. Raga beloyara.
**Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC; Vrajabuli.*[^25-1]

রজনী প্রভাত প্রভাকর সম অদ্বৈত মহাশয় পরম উলাস ।
করত কক্ষযুগ-বাদ্য নিরন্তর নিরখি গৌর-মুখচন্দ্র প্রকাশ ॥

*rajanī prabhāta prabhākara sama advaita mahāśaya parama ulāsa |*
*karata kakṣayuga-bādya nirantara nirakhi gaura-mukhacandra prakāśa ||*

*Word for word:* rajanī prabhāta — the night has turned to dawn; prabhākara sama — like the sun; advaita mahāśaya — Advaita Mahashaya; parama ulāsa — in supreme delight; karata — makes; kakṣayuga-bādya — the beating of both armpits; nirantara — ceaselessly; nirakhi — seeing; gaura-mukhacandra — of Gaura's moon-face; prakāśa — the rising

**1.1.** The night has turned to dawn — and Advaita Mahashaya, like the sun, in supreme delight,
ceaselessly beats His armpits, seeing the rising of Gaura's moon-face.

তুন্দিল দেহ দিশা-জয়কৃত অতি শোভিত তহি নব পুলক বিরাজ ।
ইতি উতি করত গতাগতি অদভুত অধিক মত্ত জিতি কুঞ্জররাজ ॥

*tundila deha diśā-jayakṛta ati śobhita tahi naba pulaka birāja |*
*iti uti karata gatāgati adabhuta adhika matta jiti kuñjararāja ||*

*Word for word:* tundila deha — the portly body; diśā-jaya-kṛta — that has conquered the quarters; ati śobhita — is most beautiful; tahi — on it; naba pulaka birāja — fresh horripilation shines; iti uti — here and there; karata gatāgati — He goes to and fro; adabhuta — wondrously; adhika matta — more intoxicated; jiti — surpassing; kuñjara-rāja — the king of elephants

**1.2.** His portly body, which has conquered the quarters, is most beautiful, and on it shines fresh horripilation;
wondrously He walks to and fro, more intoxicated than the king of elephants.

লহু লহু হসত লসত দশনাবলী শ্বেত কিরণ নিকসত অনিবার ।
অপরূপ কুন্দকুসুম চহুঁ দিশ বুঝি বরষত সুঘর লোভ রিঝ আর ॥

*lahu lahu hasata lasata daśanābalī śveta kiraṇa nikasata anibāra |*
*aparūpa kundakusuma cahum̐ diśa bujhi baraṣata sughara lobha rijha āra ||*

*Word for word:* lahu lahu hasata — He laughs softly; lasata daśanābalī — the rows of teeth gleam; śveta kiraṇa — white rays; nikasata anibāra — issue ceaselessly; aparūpa — wondrous; kunda-kusuma — jasmine flowers; cahum̐ diśa — in all directions; bujhi — as if; baraṣata — rain down; sughara — the connoisseurs; lobha — longing; rijha — delight; āra — and more

**1.3.** He laughs softly — His rows of teeth gleam, white rays issue ceaselessly,
as if wondrous jasmine flowers were raining down on every side, — and the connoisseurs of beauty are filled with longing and delight.

টলমল নয়নযুগল জল ছলছল চরত চারু বারণ নাহি মানি ।
মুকুতাদাম সদৃশ করু ঝলমল নরহরি পহুঁক পরাভব জানি ॥

*ṭalamala nayanayugala jala chalachala carata cāru bāraṇa nāhi māni |*
*mukutādāma sadṛśa karu jhalamala narahari pahum̐ka parābhaba jāni ||*

*Word for word:* ṭalamala — tremble; nayana-yugala — both eyes; jala chalachala — brimming with tears; carata cāru — flow beautifully; bāraṇa nāhi māni — heeding no restraint; mukutādāma sadṛśa — like strings of pearls; karu jhalamala — glitter; narahari — Narahari; pahum̐ka — of the Lord; parābhaba — the victory over [them]; jāni — knows

**1.4.** His eyes tremble, brimming with tears, and the tears flow beautifully, heeding no restraint,
glittering like strings of pearls, — and Narahari sees the pearls put to shame by the Lord.[^25-2]

[^25-1]: GPT1 — p. 440, section 6.2 "Advaita", no. 5 ("beloyāra"; scan, PDF p. 699); GPT2 — section 6.2, no. 5. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-316).
GCC — kirana 4 ("the Lord among His devotees": in the morning, after waking, the companions gather round Gaura, and the poet describes each of them —
Nityananda, padas 7–11, Advaita, padas 12–15, Gadadhara, 16–17, Narahari Sarakara, 18, Srivasa, 19, and others), pada 12 ("punaḥ beloyāra"; right after
the pada on Nityananda's form — no. 29 of chapter 24). Readings: 1.1 "nirakhi" ("seeing") — from the GCC, the word has dropped out in the GPT (the line is
short of the metre); 1.4 GCC "calata" ("flow"; GPT "carata"). Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS, Gita-chandrodaya. B. Note 57 of chapter 24 wrongly calls this
pada no. 4 (corrected).
[^25-2]: Beating the armpits (kakṣa-bādya) is a gesture of jubilation and challenge, as of a wrestler or a hero (cf. below, 9.3 and 11.2: He slaps His
arms, and Kali trembles at Advaita's roar). "Portly body": in the lila Advaita is the elder, venerable in years (cf. "the old man", buṛā, in other poets
of the same section); "which has conquered the quarters" — by its radiance and might. Advaita's tears and laughter are the ecstasy of love for Gaura,
whom He Himself called into the world. The last words (pahum̐ka parābhaba jāni, lit. "knows the defeat by the Lord") may also be understood otherwise:
"Narahari owns himself defeated by the Lord's beauty".

## 2. Narahari — "sītāpati atiśaya sukhe bhora…" (GPT1 p. 441, no. 6; GCC)
*Advaita, the Lord of Sita, is absorbed in happiness and reflects with a smile: Gaura's beauty has left Madana no trace of pride; the three worlds,
having drunk this intoxicating nectar, have forgotten everything and made Shachi's son the essence of their life; the word "sorrow" has vanished;
the sin of Kali with its retinue is cowed. Raga not specified ("yathārāga"). **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC;
Vrajabuli.*[^25-3]

সীতাপতি অতিশয় সুখে ভোর ।
মনহি বিচার করত মৃদু হসি হসি ঐছে মদন-মদ ন রহল থোর ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*sītāpati atiśaya sukhe bhora |*
*manahi bicāra karata mṛdu hasi hasi aiche madana-mada na rahala thora || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* sītāpati — the Lord of Sita; atiśaya sukhe bhora — absorbed in boundless happiness; manahi — in His mind; bicāra karata — reflects; mṛdu hasi hasi — smiling gently; aiche — thus; madana-mada — of Madana's pride; na rahala thora — not a little remained

**2.1.** The Lord of Sita is absorbed in boundless happiness.
Smiling gently, He reflects in His mind: "Thus not a little of Madana's pride is left!"

অতি অপরূপ ইহ গৌরবরণ বর মাদক অমৃত অলপ করি পান ।
মাতল ত্রিজগত সকল বিসারল সার করল শচীতনয় পরাণ ॥

*ati aparūpa iha gaurabaraṇa bara mādaka amṛta alapa kari pāna |*
*mātala trijagata sakala bisārala sāra karala śacītanaya parāṇa ||*

*Word for word:* ati aparūpa — most wondrous; iha — this; gaura-baraṇa bara — excellent golden complexion; mādaka amṛta — intoxicating nectar; alapa kari pāna — drinking a little; mātala trijagata — the three worlds became intoxicated; sakala bisārala — forgot everything; sāra karala — made the essence; śacī-tanaya — Shachi's son; parāṇa — of their life

**2.2.** How wondrous is this excellent golden complexion — an intoxicating nectar: drinking only a little of it,
the three worlds became intoxicated, forgot everything and made Shachi's son the essence of their life.

জনমন-প্রবল তাপ তম হারণ করুণালয় সুপারিষদ চন্দ ।
দুঃখ শবদ মহি হোত শ্রবণগত ভবন ভুবন মধি অধিক আনন্দ ॥

*janamana-prabala tāpa tama hāraṇa karuṇālaya supāriṣada canda |*
*duḥkha śabada mahi hota śrabaṇagata bhabana bhubana madhi adhika ānanda ||*

*Word for word:* janamana — of people's hearts; prabala tāpa — the fierce burning; tama — the darkness; hāraṇa — removing; karuṇālaya — abode of compassion; supāriṣada — with fine companions; canda — the moon; duḥkha śabada — the word "sorrow"; mahi — on earth; hota śrabaṇa-gata — has gone from hearing; bhabana bhubana madhi — in homes and in the worlds; adhika ānanda — great bliss

**2.3.** The Moon with His fine companions, the abode of compassion, takes away the fierce burning and the darkness of people's hearts;
the word "sorrow" has gone from hearing on earth, in homes and in all the worlds there is great bliss.

মিটল হরষ বিপরীত ভেল অব পরিকর সহ কুণ্ঠিত কলিপাপ ।
হরি হরি কো অধিকার হীন করু নরহরি ভণ পহুঁ তব পরতাপ ॥

*miṭala haraṣa biparīta bhela aba parikara saha kuṇṭhita kalipāpa |*
*hari hari ko adhikāra hīna karu narahari bhaṇa pahum̐ taba paratāpa ||*

*Word for word:* miṭala haraṣa — the joy ended; biparīta bhela — everything turned the other way; aba — now; parikara saha — with its retinue; kuṇṭhita — cowed; kali-pāpa — the sin of Kali; hari hari — Hari, Hari; ko — whom; adhikāra hīna karu — has it not stripped of power; narahari bhaṇa — Narahari says; pahum̐ — O Lord; taba paratāpa — Your might

**2.4.** [Kali's] joy has ended, everything has turned the other way: now the sin of Kali with all its retinue is cowed.
Hari, Hari! Whom has it not stripped of power, — says Narahari, — Your might, O Lord![^25-4]

[^25-3]: GPT1 — p. 441, no. 6 ("yathārāga"; scan, PDF p. 700); GPT2 — section 6.2, no. 6. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-317). GCC — kirana 4,
pada 13 ("yathārāga"). Readings: 2.1 "bicāra" ("reflects") — from the GCC (GPT1 and GPT2 misprint "bicā"); 2.3 GCC "bharala bhubanamadhi adhika ānanda"
("great bliss filled the worlds"; GPT "bhavana bhuvana madhi"). Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS, Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^25-4]: Madana (Kamadeva) is the god of love; "Madana's pride" is put to shame by the spiritual beauty of Gaura — Krishna Himself, Madana-mohana,
"the enchanter of Madana": this is praise of the Lord's all-attractive beauty, not of worldly attraction. "The Moon" is Gaura (Gaurachandra) with His
companions. Kali is the personified age of quarrel; his "joy" is his power over people, which the advent of the Lord and of His name destroys.

## 3. Narahari — "acyuta-janaka janāśraya jagamadhi…" (GPT1 p. 441, no. 7; GCC)
*The Father of Achyuta, stirred by longings, with a pauper's greed takes Gaura, still in His night attire, through His eyes into His heart,
worships Him with the flowers of His bhavas, dances unnoticed crying "Jaya!" and repeats: "I have won!"; Narahari, Haridasa and the others watch
Him in unspeakable happiness. Raga not specified. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC; Vrajabuli.*[^25-5]

অচ্যুত-জনক জনাশ্রয় জগমধি বিদিত উদার দীন-দুঃখহারী ।
করতহি কত কত মনহি মনোরথ অধীর হোত পুন রহত সম্ভারী ॥

*acyuta-janaka janāśraya jagamadhi bidita udāra dīna-duḥkhahārī |*
*karatahi kata kata manahi manoratha adhīra hota puna rahata sambhārī ||*

*Word for word:* acyuta-janaka — the Father of Achyuta; janāśraya — the shelter of people; jagamadhi bidita — renowned in the world; udāra — generous; dīna-duḥkha-hārī — remover of the sorrow of the lowly; karatahi — He forms; kata kata — so many; manahi — in His mind; manoratha — longings; adhīra hota — loses composure; puna — again; rahata sambhārī — restrains Himself

**3.1.** The Father of Achyuta, shelter of people, renowned in the world, generous, remover of the sorrow of the lowly,
forms so many longings in His mind — now He loses composure, now again restrains Himself.

প্রবল লোভ রঙ্ক সম নিঃশঙ্কহি রজনীক বেশ সহিত দ্বিজরাজ ।
লোচন পন্থে লেই বহু যতনহি বৈঠায়ল হিয়-আসন মাঝ ॥

*prabala lobha raṅka sama niḥśaṅkahi rajanīka beśa sahita dvijarāja |*
*locana panthe lei bahu yatanahi baiṭhāyala hiya-āsana mājha ||*

*Word for word:* prabala lobha — with fierce greed; raṅka sama — like a pauper; niḥśaṅkahi — without hesitation; rajanīka beśa sahita — in His night attire; dvijarāja — the king of the twice-born (the moon); locana-panthe — by the path of the eyes; lei — taking; bahu yatanahi — with great care; baiṭhāyala — seated; hiya-āsana mājha — on the throne of His heart

**3.2.** With the unbounded greed of a pauper, without hesitation, the King of the twice-born — still in His night attire —
He took in by the path of the eyes and with great care seated on the throne of His heart.

ভাব-কদম্ব-কুসুম দেই পূজত তনু মন নিরমঞ্ছন করু তায় ।
জয় জয় শবদ উচরি অলখিত মৃদু নাচত জন মন লেত চোরায় ॥

*bhāba-kadamba-kusuma dei pūjata tanu mana niramañchana karu tāya |*
*jaya jaya śabada ucari alakhita mṛdu nācata jana mana leta corāya ||*

*Word for word:* bhāba-kadamba-kusuma — kadamba flowers of bhava; dei — offering; pūjata — He worships; tanu mana — body and mind; niramañchana karu tāya — offers to Him in nirmanchana; jaya jaya śabada uccari — crying "jaya, jaya"; alakhita — unnoticed; mṛdu nācata — dances gently; jana mana — people's hearts; leta corāya — steals away

**3.3.** He worships Him, offering kadamba flowers — His bhavas, and offers body and mind to Him in nirmanchana;
crying "Jaya, jaya!", unnoticed, He dances gently — and steals away people's hearts.

খণে খণে জিতলুঁ জিতলুঁ বলি প্রফুল্লিত আপহি আপ দরশরস ভোর ।
অনুপম ভঙ্গী নিরখি নরহরি হরিদাস আদি সুখ কো করু ওর ॥

*khaṇe khaṇe jitalum̐ jitalum̐ bali praphullita āpahi āpa daraśarasa bhora |*
*anupama bhaṅgī nirakhi narahari haridāsa ādi sukha ko karu ora ||*

*Word for word:* khaṇe khaṇe — again and again; jitalum̐ jitalum̐ bali — saying "I have won, I have won"; praphullita — blossoming; āpahi āpa — by Himself; daraśa-rasa bhora — absorbed in the rasa of beholding; anupama bhaṅgī — the matchless gestures; nirakhi — seeing; narahari haridāsa ādi — Narahari, Haridasa and the others; sukha — of the happiness; ko karu ora — who can find the end

**3.4.** Again and again He says: "I have won, I have won!" — and blossoms, absorbed by Himself in the rasa of beholding.
Seeing this matchless play, Narahari, Haridasa and the others — who can measure their happiness?[^25-6]

[^25-5]: GPT1 — p. 441, no. 7 ("yathārāga"; scan, PDF p. 700); GPT2 — section 6.2, no. 7 (catalogue: NG-210). GCC — kirana 4, pada 14 ("yathārāga"); next
(pada 15) comes Ghanashyama's pada on Advaita's form (GPT no. 8). Readings: 3.2 "raṅka sama" ("like a pauper") and "rajanīka beśa" ("night attire";
cf. in the same kirana, pada 16: the Lord in the morning "in His night dress") — from the GCC; the GPT "bakṣa sama", "rajanī kareṇa" make no sense;
3.4 GCC "ko kahu ora" ("who can tell"). Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS, Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^25-6]: Achyuta is Achyutananda, Advaita's son, "the beloved of Krishna-Chaitanya" (Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika, 87); the name also means "the
Infallible" (Krishna). The King of the twice-born (dvijarāja) is both the moon and the king of brahmanas: Gaura. Nirmanchana is the rite of circular
offering (as in arati), a sign of self-surrender. "I have won!": Advaita triumphs — His worship has been fulfilled, the Lord whom He called has
appeared (cf. in the same GPT section Lochana's pada no. 30: "jitilum̐ jitilum̐… jība nistārite habe gaura abatāra"). In the last line the name
"Narahari" is both the poet's signature and, probably, the name of one of the onlookers: in the same kirana of the GCC, the pada after those on
Advaita and Gadadhara (pada 18) praises Narahari Sarakara among the Lord's companions; Haridasa is Haridasa Thakura.

## 4. Narahari — "śrī-advaitacandra bhūpa mora…" (GPT1 p. 442, no. 9; BR; GCd)
*Advaita's form in love for Gaura: tears from His reddened eyes, a radiance shaming hosts of suns, a gait surpassing the elephant's, a smile;
His roar robs the lion of its pride — Kali trembles, the wicked flee; the ocean of compassion overflows and the fallen float in the rasa of bhakti.
Raga kamoda or belavali. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR and the Gita-chandrodaya; Vrajabuli.*[^25-7]

শ্রীঅদ্বৈতচন্দ্র ভূপ মোর ।
গৌরপ্রেমভরে গর গর অন্তর অবিরত অরুণ-নয়ানে ঝরে লোর ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*śrīadvaitacandra bhūpa mora |*
*gaurapremabhare gara gara antara abirata aruṇa-nayāne jhare lora || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* śrī-advaitacandra — Sri Advaitachandra; bhūpa mora — my sovereign; gaura-prema-bhare — with the weight of love for Gaura; gara gara antara — His heart overflowing; abirata — ceaselessly; aruṇa-nayāne — from His reddened eyes; jhare lora — tears stream

**4.1.** Sri Advaitachandra is my sovereign!
His heart overflows with love for Gaura, tears stream ceaselessly from His reddened eyes.

পুলকিত ললিত অঙ্গ ঝলমল কত দিনকর-নিকর নিন্দি বর জ্যোতি ।
কুঞ্জরগমন দমন মনোরঞ্জন হসত সুলসত দশন জনু মোতি ॥

*pulakita lalita aṅga jhalamala kata dinakara-nikara nindi bara jyoti |*
*kuñjaragamana damana manorañjana hasata sulasata daśana janu moti ||*

*Word for word:* pulakita — thrilled with horripilation; lalita aṅga — graceful limbs; jhalamala — shine; kata — how; dinakara-nikara — hosts of suns; nindi — putting to shame; bara jyoti — with excellent light; kuñjara-gamana damana — surpassing the elephant's gait; manorañjana — delighting the heart; hasata — He laughs; sulasata daśana — His teeth gleam; janu moti — like pearls

**4.2.** His graceful limbs, thrilling with horripilation, shine with an excellent light that puts to shame hosts of suns;
His gait, the delight of the heart, surpasses the elephant's; He laughs — and His teeth gleam like pearls.

সিংহগরবহর গরজত ঘন ঘন কম্পিত কলি দূরে দুরজন গেল ।
প্রবল প্রতাপে তাপত্রয় কুণ্ঠিত জগজন পরম হরিষহিয়া ভেল ॥

*siṃhagarabahara garajata ghana ghana kampita kali dūre durajana gela |*
*prabala pratāpe tāpatraya kuṇṭhita jagajana parama hariṣahiyā bhela ||*

*Word for word:* siṃha-garaba-hara — robbing the lion of its pride; garajata ghana ghana — He roars again and again; kampita kali — Kali trembles; dūre durajana gela — the wicked have fled far; prabala pratāpe — by His mighty power; tāpatraya — the threefold miseries; kuṇṭhita — are subdued; jagajana — the people of the world; parama hariṣa-hiyā bhela — became supremely glad at heart

**4.3.** Robbing the lion of its pride, He roars again and again — Kali trembles, the wicked flee far away;
by His mighty power the threefold miseries are subdued, and the hearts of the people are filled with supreme gladness.

করুণা-জলধি উমড়ি চহুঁ দিশ পামর পতিত ভকতিরসে ভাসি ।
নরহরি কুমতি কি বুঝব রঙ্গ নব গৌরচরিত গুণ ভুবনে প্রকাশি ॥

*karuṇā-jaladhi umaṛi cahum̐ diśa pāmara patita bhakatirase bhāsi |*
*narahari kumati ki bujhaba raṅga naba gauracarita guṇa bhubane prakāśi ||*

*Word for word:* karuṇā-jaladhi — the ocean of compassion; umaṛi — overflowing; cahum̐ diśa — in all directions; pāmara patita — the base and fallen; bhakati-rase bhāsi — float in the rasa of bhakti; narahari kumati — foolish Narahari; ki bujhaba raṅga — what will he understand of this play; naba gaura-carita guṇa — the new deeds and qualities of Gaura; bhubane prakāśi — revealing to the world

**4.4.** The ocean of compassion has overflowed in all directions — the base and the fallen float in the rasa of bhakti.
What will foolish Narahari understand of this play? He has revealed to the world the new deeds and qualities of Gaura.[^25-8]

[^25-7]: GPT1 — p. 442, no. 9 ("kāmoda vā belābalī"; scan, PDF p. 701); GPT2 — section 6.2, no. 9. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-318). BR 12
(ed. 1912, p. 977; ed. 1960, vv. 3767–3770, "belābalī"): Nityananda, preaching in Gauda, stays at Saptagrama with Uddharana Datta and is about to go to
Shantipura, to Advaita's house; Ishana, telling Srinivasa of this, describes Advaita's glory ("Advaita Acharya lives in Shantipura… He who brought Shri
Krishna-Chaitanya into the world", vv. 3753–3754) and quotes one after another padas on Advaita: Narahari (vv. 3755–3760, "śrīgaura-abhinna tanu advaita āmāra" —
not in the GPT), Lochana (GPT no. 2), "Advaitachandra with His companions ever floats on the waves of the ocean of love for Gora" (v. 3766) — and this
pada; then come nos. 11, 12, 14 (Ghanashyama), 15, 16, 17, 18, 19 (Ghanashyama), 20 (nos. 6, 8–12 of this chapter). Gita-chandrodaya — the section "atha
śrī-advaitacandrasya", pada 2 (there also nos. 14, 2, 11, 12, 17, 21). The Navadvipa-parikrama is the same as the BR. Readings: 4.1 BR and GCd "pahu mora"
("my Lord"); 4.2 BR and GCd "kuñjaradamana gamana" ("a gait shaming the elephant"; GPT "kuñjaragamana damana"); 4.4 BR and GCd "umaṛi calu cahu diśa"
("overflowing, flowed in all directions"). Not in the PK, KGC, PS, GCC. B.
[^25-8]: Advaita's roar (huṅkāra) is the thundering calls with which, worshipping with Ganga water and tulasi leaves, He called the Lord down (CC Adi 3);
here it is a jubilant roar from which Kali flees. "The threefold miseries" — those caused by one's own body and mind, by other beings and by nature.
"He has revealed Gaura's deeds to the world": Advaita was the first to proclaim and glorify Gaura as the Lord.

## 5. Narahari — "śrī-advaita guṇamaṇi sakala rasera khani…" (GPT1 p. 442, no. 10; BR)
*Advaita's life in one pada: birth from Nabha at Navagram, removal to Shantipura, pilgrimage after His parents' passing, marriage to Sita and the
austerities by which He brought Krishna and Haladhara; kirtana in Nadia, service to the Lord as sannyasi in His own house, journeys to Nilachala.
Raga kamoda. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^25-9]

শ্রীঅদ্বৈত গুণমণি সকল রসের খনি নাভাগর্ভে জনম লভিলা ।
জন্ম নবগ্রাম বঙ্গে তথা বিলসিয়া রঙ্গে কিছু দিনে শান্তিপুরে আইলা ॥

*śrīadvaita guṇamaṇi sakala rasera khani nābhāgarbhe janama labhilā |*
*janma nabagrāma baṅge tathā bilasiyā raṅge kichu dine śāntipure āilā ||*

*Word for word:* śrī-advaita — Sri Advaita; guṇamaṇi — the jewel of virtues; sakala rasera khani — the mine of all rasas; nābhā-garbhe — from Nabha's womb; janama labhilā — took birth; janma — born; nabagrāma baṅge — in Navagram, in Vanga; tathā bilasiyā raṅge — playing there joyfully; kichu dine — after some time; śāntipure āilā — came to Shantipura

**5.1.** Sri Advaita, the jewel of virtues, the mine of all rasas, took birth from Nabha's womb;
He was born at Navagram, in Vanga, played there joyfully, and after some time came to Shantipura.

পিতা মাতা অদর্শনে গিয়া তীর্থপর্যটনে আসিয়া রহিলা শান্তিপুরে ।
হৈয়া শ্রীসীতার পতি কত তপ করি নিতি আনিলেন কৃষ্ণ হলধরে ॥

*pitā mātā adarśane giyā tīrthaparyaṭane āsiyā rahilā śāntipure |*
*haiyā śrīsītāra pati kata tapa kari niti ānilena kṛṣṇa haladhare ||*

*Word for word:* pitā mātā adarśane — when father and mother passed from sight; giyā tīrtha-paryaṭane — going on pilgrimage to holy places; āsiyā rahilā śāntipure — returning, He settled in Shantipura; haiyā śrī-sītāra pati — becoming the husband of Sri Sita; kata tapa kari niti — performing so many austerities daily; ānilena — He brought; kṛṣṇa haladhare — Krishna and Haladhara

**5.2.** When His father and mother passed from sight, He went on pilgrimage to the holy places, and returning, settled in Shantipura;
becoming the husband of Sri Sita, day after day He performed so many austerities — and brought [into the world] Krishna and Haladhara.

নদীয়া বিহার দেখি সদা জুড়াইলা আঁখি নাচিলা কীর্তনে নানা ছাঁদে ।
আপনার ঘরে পাঞা সেবিলা আনন্দ হৈয়া ন্যাসী-শিরোমণি গোরাচাঁদে ॥

*nadīyā bihāra dekhi sadā juṛāilā ām̐khi nācilā kīrtane nānā chām̐de |*
*āpanāra ghare pāñā sebilā ānanda haiyā nyāsī-śiromaṇi gorācām̐de ||*

*Word for word:* nadīyā bihāra dekhi — seeing the pastimes in Nadia; sadā juṛāilā ām̐khi — ever refreshed His eyes; nācilā kīrtane — danced in kirtana; nānā chām̐de — in many ways; āpanāra ghare pāñā — receiving in His own house; sebilā ānanda haiyā — served joyfully; nyāsī-śiromaṇi — the crown of sannyasis; gorācām̐de — Gorachand

**5.3.** Seeing the pastimes in Nadia, He ever refreshed His eyes and danced in kirtana in many ways;
receiving Gorachand, the crown of sannyasis, in His own house, He served Him joyfully.

নীলাচলে পহুঁ স্থিতি তথা কৈলা গতাগতি সবে মাতাইলা গোরা গুণে ।
দাস নরহরি কয় শ্রীঅদ্বৈত দয়াময় এ যশ ঘোষয়ে ত্রিভুবনে ॥

*nīlācale pahum̐ sthiti tathā kailā gatāgati sabe mātāilā gorā guṇe |*
*dāsa narahari kaya śrīadvaita dayāmaya e yaśa ghoṣaye tribhubane ||*

*Word for word:* nīlācale pahum̐ sthiti — when the Lord stayed at Nilachala; tathā kailā gatāgati — He went there and back; sabe mātāilā — intoxicated everyone; gorā guṇe — with Gora's glories; dāsa narahari kaya — Narahari Dasa says; śrī-advaita dayāmaya — Sri Advaita is merciful; e yaśa — this fame; ghoṣaye tribhubane — the three worlds proclaim

**5.4.** When the Lord stayed at Nilachala, He went there and back and intoxicated everyone with Gora's glories.
Narahari Dasa says: Sri Advaita is merciful — the three worlds proclaim this fame.[^25-10]

[^25-9]: GPT1 — p. 442, no. 10 ("kāmoda"; scan, PDF p. 701); GPT2 — section 6.2, no. 10 (catalogue: NG-211). BR 12 (ed. 1912, pp. 996–997; ed. 1960,
vv. 4024–4027, "kāmoda"): right after the pada surveying Nityananda's life (6.1 no. 65, no. 15 of chapter 24) Ishana tells Srinivasa: "Sri Advaita with His
companions is ceaselessly absorbed in singing Gaura's deeds, now in Shantipura, now in Nadia; who does not sing the glory of Nabha's Son?" (vv.
4022–4023). Readings: 5.1 "bilasiyā" — from the BR (GPT "bilāsiyā"); 5.4 BR "prabhu-sthiti" ("the Lord's stay"). Not in the PK, KGC, PS, GCC,
Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^25-10]: Navagram is Advaita's birthplace in Vanga (East Bengal), near Shrihatta (Sylhet); His father is Kuvera Pandita (Kuvera Mishra), His mother Nabha
(in the Advaita-prakasha, Labha; BR 12, vv. 1751–1758). Sri Sita is Advaita's wife, according to the Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika (86) Yogamaya. "Austerities"
(tapa) are His worship and His prayers for the Lord's descent (CC Adi 3); "Krishna and Haladhara" are Gaura and Nityananda. The Lord after sannyasa in
Advaita's house at Shantipura — CC Madhya 3; Advaita's yearly journeys to Puri with the Bengali devotees — CC Madhya 11 ff.

## 6. Narahari — "śāntipurapati parama sundara…" (GPT1 p. 442, no. 11; BR; GCd)
*The Lord of Shantipura in the intoxication of bhava: He roars, subduing Kali's arrogance, trembles at the name "Gaurahari" and falls into the arms of
His companions, rolls in the dust, streams pour from His lotus eyes like the rains of Shravana; seeing the wretched, He spreads mercy through the world.
Raga kamoda. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR and the Gita-chandrodaya; Vrajabuli.*[^25-11]

শান্তিপুরপতি পরম সুন্দর চরিত বর লীলা যাত ।
ভাবভরে অতি মত্ত অনুখন বিপুল পুলকিত গাত ॥

*śāntipurapati parama sundara carita bara līlā yāta |*
*bhābabhare ati matta anukhana bipula pulakita gāta ||*

*Word for word:* śāntipura-pati — the Lord of Shantipura; parama sundara — most beautiful; carita bara līlā yāta — whose deeds are excellent lila; bhāba-bhare — with the weight of bhava; ati matta — deeply intoxicated; anukhana — constantly; bipula pulakita gāta — His body thrilling all over

**6.1.** The Lord of Shantipura, most beautiful, — whose deeds are an excellent lila, —
is constantly intoxicated with the weight of bhava, His body thrilling all over.

প্রবল কলিমদ দমন ঘন ঘন ঘোর গরজি বিভোর ।
গৌরহরি হরি ভণত কম্পই গিরত সহচর কোর ॥

*prabala kalimada damana ghana ghana ghora garaji bibhora |*
*gaurahari hari bhaṇata kampai girata sahacara kora ||*

*Word for word:* prabala kali-mada — the mighty arrogance of Kali; damana — subduing; ghana ghana — again and again; ghora garaji — roaring terribly; bibhora — beside Himself; gaurahari hari bhaṇata — crying "Gaurahari! Hari!"; kampai — He trembles; girata — falls; sahacara kora — into the arms of His companions

**6.2.** Subduing the mighty arrogance of Kali, again and again He roars terribly, beside Himself;
crying "Gaurahari! Hari!", He trembles and falls into the arms of His companions.

অবনী ঘন গড়ি যাত নিরুপম ধূলিধূসর দেহ ।
কঞ্জলোচন ঝরই ঝর ঝর জনু স শাঙন মেহ ॥

*abanī ghana gaṛi yāta nirupama dhūlidhūsara deha |*
*kañjalocana jharai jhara jhara janu sa śāṅana meha ||*

*Word for word:* abanī ghana gaṛi yāta — He rolls on the ground again and again; nirupama — incomparable; dhūli-dhūsara deha — His body grey with dust; kañja-locana — the lotus eyes; jharai jhara jhara — pour down in streams; janu — like; sa śāṅana meha — the rain-cloud of Shravana

**6.3.** Again and again He rolls on the ground, incomparable, His body grey with dust;
from His lotus eyes streams pour down like the rain-clouds of Shravana.

দীন দুখিত নেহারি করু করুণা ভুবনে পরচার ।
দাস নরহরি পহুঁক বলি বলিহারি পরম উদার ॥

*dīna dukhita nehāri karu karuṇā bhubane paracāra |*
*dāsa narahari pahum̐ka bali balihāri parama udāra ||*

*Word for word:* dīna dukhita nehāri — seeing the lowly and the sorrowful; karu karuṇā — He shows mercy; bhubane paracāra — spreads it through the world; dāsa narahari — Narahari Dasa; pahum̐ka bali balihāri — offers himself to the Lord; parama udāra — supremely generous

**6.4.** Seeing the lowly and the sorrowful, He shows mercy and spreads it through the world.
Narahari Dasa offers himself to the Lord: how supremely generous He is![^25-12]

[^25-11]: GPT1 — p. 442, no. 11 ("kāmoda"; scan, PDF p. 701); GPT2 — section 6.2, no. 11. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-319). BR 12 (ed. 1912,
p. 977; ed. 1960, vv. 3771–3774, "punaḥ — kāmoda"; right after no. 9, see note 7); Gita-chandrodaya — the section on Advaita, pada 4. Readings: 6.1 GCd
"carita baraṇi na yāta" ("His deeds cannot be described"); 6.3 "kañjalocana" ("lotus eyes") — from the BR and GCd (GPT misprint "kuñja locana"); GCd
"aparūpa dhūlidhūsarita deha". Not in the PK, KGC, PS, GCC. B.
[^25-12]: Shravana (śāṅana) is the month of the rainy season (July–August). "Gaurahari" is the Lord's name: Advaita, Himself non-different from Hari, repeats
Gaura's name in ecstasy. "Offers himself" (balihāri) — lit. "sacrifices himself", an exclamation of admiration and devotion.

## 7. Narahari — "jaya deba deba maheśvara rūpa…" (GPT1 p. 443, no. 13; GPT only)
*Praise of Advaita, the form of Maheshvara, the king of the rasa of lila: by His call Gauranga was manifested, for His sake Gaura's lila unfolded;
He was born as Kuvera's son on the bright seventh day of the month of Magha. Raga dhanashi. **Attribution: not established** — found in no witness
(it stands among padas that are in the BR; the GPT2 index wrongly assigns it to Ghanashyama).*[^25-13]

জয় দেব দেব মহেশ্বর রূপ । অদ্বৈত আচার্য লীলারস ভূপ ॥

*jaya deba deba maheśvara rūpa | advaita ācārya līlārasa bhūpa ||*

*Word for word:* jaya — glory; deba deba — of the God of gods; maheśvara rūpa — to the form of Maheshvara; advaita ācārya — to Advaita Acharya; līlārasa bhūpa — the king of the rasa of lila

**7.1.** Glory to Him who is the form of Maheshvara, the God of gods, —
to Advaita Acharya, the king of the rasa of lila!

যার হুহুঙ্কারে গৌরাঙ্গ প্রকাশ । যার লাগি গৌর-লীলাবিকাশ ॥

*yāra huhuṅkāre gaurāṅga prakāśa | yāra lāgi gaura-līlābikāśa ||*

*Word for word:* yāra — by whose; huhuṅkāre — thundering calls; gaurāṅga prakāśa — Gauranga was manifested; yāra lāgi — for whose sake; gaura-līlā-bikāśa — Gaura's lila unfolded

**7.2.** By His thundering calls Gauranga was manifested,
for His sake Gaura's lila unfolded.

শুক্লা সপ্তমীতে শুভ মাঘ মাসে । জনমিলা যেহ কুবের ঔরসে ॥

*śuklā saptamīte śubha māgha māse | janamilā yeha kubera aurase ||*

*Word for word:* śuklā saptamīte — on the bright seventh lunar day; śubha māgha māse — in the auspicious month of Magha; janamilā — was born; yeha — He who; kubera aurase — as Kuvera's son

**7.3.** In the auspicious month of Magha, on the bright seventh lunar day,
He was born — as Kuvera's son.

নাভানন্দন শ্রীমদদ্বৈত পহুঁ । দাস নরহরি পদে মতি রহু ॥

*nābhānandana śrīmadadvaita pahum̐ | dāsa narahari pade mati rahu ||*

*Word for word:* nābhā-nandana — the son of Nabha; śrīmad-advaita pahum̐ — the Lord Sri Advaita; dāsa narahari — of Narahari Dasa; pade — at His feet; mati rahu — may the mind remain

**7.4.** The son of Nabha, the Lord Sri Advaita, —
may the mind of Narahari Dasa remain at His feet![^25-14]

[^25-13]: GPT1 — p. 443, no. 13 ("dhānaśī"; scan, PDF p. 702); GPT2 — section 6.2, no. 13 (catalogue: NG-212). In the GPT2 index of first lines "jaya debadeba maheśvara rūpa"
stands under Ghanashyama's name, but in the text of both editions the signature is "dāsa narahari". Readings: 7.3 GPT2 "kubera rase" (a letter has dropped out:
GPT1 "aurase", "as the son"). Not in the BR (eds. 1912, 1913, 1960), GCC, Gita-chandrodaya, Navadvipa-parikrama, PK, KGC, PS. C.
[^25-14]: "Maheshvara, the God of gods" is Sadashiva: Advaita is Maha-Vishnu Himself (CC Adi 6), and the Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika (11, 76) calls Him Sadashiva.
The Sadashiva of Gaudiya theology is not the demigod Shiva who governs the mode of ignorance, but an eternal form of the Lord, non-different from Vishnu;
that is why Advaita is called "non-dual" — non-different from Hari. Kuvera is Kuvera Pandita, Advaita's father, according to the Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika
(81) Kubera, the friend of Mahadeva; Nabha is Advaita's mother. The bright seventh lunar day of the month of Magha is the day of Advaita's advent
(Advaita-saptami); likewise in Ghanashyama (GPT no. 23) and in no. 14.

## 8. Narahari — "ki bhābe bibhora mora advaita gosāñi re…" (GPT1 p. 443, no. 15; BR)
*Advaita is lost in bhava: tears, a sweet smile, the constant call "Gora! Gora!"; a body more tender than the shirisha flower, His shikha fluttering in
the wind, a garland of malati on His neck; stretching out His long arms, He embraces the fallen and gives everyone the treasure of prema, rare even for
Brahma. Raga gurjari. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^25-15]

কি ভাবে বিভোর মোর অদ্বৈত গোসাঞি রে ও দুটী নয়ানে বহে লোরা ।
মধুর মধুর হাসি ও চাঁদবদনে রে সঘনে বলয়ে গোরা গোরা ॥

*ki bhābe bibhora mora advaita gosāñi re o duṭī nayāne bahe lorā |*
*madhura madhura hāsi o cām̐dabadane re saghane balaye gorā gorā ||*

*Word for word:* ki bhābe — in what bhava; bibhora — lost; mora advaita gosāñi — my Advaita Gosani; o duṭī nayāne — from those two eyes; bahe lorā — tears flow; madhura madhura hāsi — a sweet, sweet smile; o cām̐da-badane — on that moon-face; saghane balaye — again and again He calls; gorā gorā — "Gora! Gora!"

**8.1.** In what bhava is my Advaita Gosani lost! Tears flow from His eyes;
on His moon-face is a sweet, sweet smile, and again and again He calls: "Gora! Gora!"

শিরীষ কুসুম জিনি তনু অনুপাম রে বিপুল পুলক তাহে শোহে ।
কি ছার কুঞ্জরগতি অতিশয় শোভা রে ভঙ্গীতে ভুবনমন মোহে ॥

*śirīṣa kusuma jini tanu anupāma re bipula pulaka tāhe śohe |*
*ki chāra kuñjaragati atiśaya śobhā re bhaṅgīte bhubanamana mohe ||*

*Word for word:* śirīṣa kusuma jini — surpassing the shirisha flower; tanu anupāma — the matchless body; bipula pulaka — abundant horripilation; tāhe śohe — shines on it; ki chāra kuñjara-gati — what is the elephant's gait; atiśaya śobhā — before such beauty; bhaṅgīte — by His movements; bhubana-mana mohe — He enchants the hearts of the world

**8.2.** His matchless body is more tender than the shirisha flower, and abundant horripilation shines on it;
what is the elephant's gait before such beauty! By His movements He enchants the hearts of the world.

শিরেতে সুন্দর শিখা পবনে উড়ায় রে মালতীর মালা গলে দোলে ।
আজানুলম্বিত দুটী বাহু পসারিয়া রে পতিতে ধরিয়া করে কোলে ॥

*śirete sundara śikhā pabane uṛāya re mālatīra mālā gale dole |*
*ājānulambita duṭī bāhu pasāriyā re patite dhariyā kare kole ||*

*Word for word:* śirete — on the head; sundara śikhā — the beautiful shikha; pabane uṛāya — flutters in the wind; mālatīra mālā — the garland of malati; gale dole — sways on the neck; ājānu-lambita — reaching to the knees; duṭī bāhu pasāriyā — stretching out both arms; patite dhariyā — seizing the fallen; kare kole — embraces them

**8.3.** On His head the beautiful shikha flutters in the wind, a garland of malati sways on His neck;
stretching out His arms, which reach to His knees, He seizes the fallen and embraces them.

ব্রহ্মার দুর্লভ প্রেম ভকতি রতন রে জনে জনে যাচে কত রূপে ।
নরহরি হেন কৃপাময় প্রভু পাঞা রে না ভজি মজিল ভবকূপে ॥

*brahmāra durlabha prema bhakati ratana re jane jane yāce kata rūpe |*
*narahari hena kṛpāmaya prabhu pāñā re nā bhaji majila bhabakūpe ||*

*Word for word:* brahmāra durlabha — rare even for Brahma; prema bhakati ratana — the jewel of prema and bhakti; jane jane — to each person; yāce — He offers unasked; kata rūpe — in so many ways; narahari — Narahari; hena kṛpāmaya prabhu pāñā — having found such a merciful Lord; nā bhaji — not serving Him; majila bhabakūpe — sank in the well of worldly existence

**8.4.** The treasure of prema and bhakti, rare even for Brahma, He Himself offers to everyone in so many ways;
and Narahari, having found so merciful a Lord, did not serve Him — and sank in the well of worldly existence.[^25-16]

[^25-15]: GPT1 — p. 443, no. 15 ("gujjarī"; scan, PDF p. 702); GPT2 — section 6.2, no. 15 (catalogue: NG-213). BR 12 (ed. 1912, pp. 978–979; ed. 1960, vv. 3782–3785,
"punaḥ gurjarī"; after Ghanashyama's pada no. 14); next Ishana says: "Sita's Lord, Advaita Gosani, is absorbed in dancing and kirtana — now in His own house,
now in the houses of His companions, now on the bank of the Ganga" (vv. 3786–3789) — and quotes no. 16. Readings: 8.3 BR "patita dhariyā"; 8.4 BR "pahu pāyā
re nā bhaji majinu bhabakūpe" ("not serving, I sank"). Not in the PK, KGC, PS, GCC, Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^25-16]: The shikha is the lock of hair on the crown, the sign of a Vaishnava brahmana. "Rare even for Brahma": the prema given away by Gaura and His
companions surpasses all that the demigods attain. The poet's self-abasement in the signature ("did not serve… sank") is the usual ending of a pada: a
humble Vaishnava considers himself deprived of what is given to all.

## 9. Narahari — "nācaye advaita premarāśi…" (GPT1 pp. 443–444, no. 16; BR)
*Advaita dances, singing of Gora: He begs the Creator for thousands of mouths, slaps His arms like a wrestler — Kali trembles and knows not where to
flee; the companions sing of Gorachand's deeds, khol and karatalas resound, even the noble wives weep; the world is full of His fame. Raga dhanashi.
**Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^25-17]

নাচয়ে অদ্বৈত প্রেমরাশি । গোরাগুণ-গরবে না জানে দিবানিশি ॥

*nācaye advaita premarāśi | gorāguṇa-garabe nā jāne dibāniśi ||*

*Word for word:* nācaye advaita — Advaita dances; prema-rāśi — a mass of prema; gorā-guṇa-garabe — proud of Gora's glories; nā jāne dibā-niśi — knows neither day nor night

**9.1.** Advaita dances — prema itself;
proud of Gora's glories, He knows neither day nor night.

গোরা গোরা বলিতে কি সুখ । বিহরে মাগয়ে কত লাখ লাখ মুখ ॥

*gorā gorā balite ki sukha | bihare māgaye kata lākha lākha mukha ||*

*Word for word:* gorā gorā balite — in saying "Gora! Gora!"; ki sukha — what happiness; bihare — of the Creator; māgaye — He begs; kata lākha lākha mukha — hundreds of thousands of mouths

**9.2.** What happiness it is to say "Gora! Gora!" —
He begs the Creator for hundreds of thousands of mouths.

গোরা বলি মারে মালসাট । ভয়ে কাঁপে কলি পলাইতে নাহি বাট ॥

*gorā bali māre mālasāṭa | bhaye kām̐pe kali palāite nāhi bāṭa ||*

*Word for word:* gorā bali — crying "Gora!"; māre mālasāṭa — slaps His arms like a wrestler; bhaye kām̐pe kali — Kali trembles with fear; palāite nāhi bāṭa — there is no way to flee

**9.3.** Crying "Gora!", He slaps His arms like a wrestler —
Kali trembles with fear, and there is no way for him to flee.

গোরা নামে কি ভাব হিয়ায় । পুলক-বলিত তনু সঘন দোলায় ॥

*gorā nāme ki bhāba hiyāya | pulaka-balita tanu saghana dolāya ||*

*Word for word:* gorā nāme — at the name of Gora; ki bhāba hiyāya — what bhava in His heart; pulaka-balita tanu — His body covered with horripilation; saghana dolāya — sways again and again

**9.4.** What bhava is in His heart at the name of Gora!
His body, thrilling with horripilation, sways again and again.

পরিকর সেনা রসে মাতি । গায় গোরাচাঁদের চরিত কত ভাতি ॥

*parikara senā rase māti | gāya gorācām̐dera carita kata bhāti ||*

*Word for word:* parikara senā — the companions, His army; rase māti — intoxicated with rasa; gāya — sing; gorācām̐dera carita — of Gorachand's deeds; kata bhāti — in many ways

**9.5.** His companions — His army — intoxicated with this rasa,
sing in many ways of Gorachand's deeds.

কিবা খোল করতাল ধ্বনি । কুলের বৌহারি কাঁদে সে শবদ শুনি ॥

*kibā khola karatāla dhvani | kulera bauhāri kām̐de se śabada śuni ||*

*Word for word:* kibā — how; khola karatāla dhvani — the sound of khol and karatalas; kulera bauhāri — the daughters-in-law of noble families; kām̐de — weep; se śabada śuni — hearing that sound

**9.6.** How the khol and the karatalas resound!
Even the wives of noble families weep, hearing that sound.

ভুবন ভরিল ওনা যশে । দীনহীন পতিত পামর প্রেমে ভাসে ॥

*bhubana bharila onā yaśe | dīnahīna patita pāmara preme bhāse ||*

*Word for word:* bhubana bharila — the world was filled; onā yaśe — with His fame; dīna-hīna — the wretched; patita pāmara — the fallen and the base; preme bhāse — float in prema

**9.7.** The world is filled with His fame;
the wretched, the fallen, the base float in prema.

নরহরি জীবনে কি সুখ । হেন দয়াময় পহুঁ-চরণে বিমুখ ॥

*narahari jībane ki sukha | hena dayāmaya pahum̐-caraṇe bimukha ||*

*Word for word:* narahari — Narahari; jībane ki sukha — what happiness in life; hena dayāmaya pahum̐-caraṇe — from the feet of so merciful a Lord; bimukha — turned away

**9.8.** What happiness is there in Narahari's life?
He has turned away from the feet of so merciful a Lord.[^25-18]

[^25-17]: GPT1 — pp. 443–444, no. 16 ("dhānaśī"; scan, PDF pp. 702–703); GPT2 — section 6.2, no. 16 (catalogue: NG-214). BR 12 (ed. 1912, p. 979; ed. 1960,
vv. 3790–3797, "gīte — yathā dhānaśī"; see note 15). Readings: 9.2 BR "bihire" ("of the Creator"; GPT "vihare"); 9.5 "senā" ("army") — from the BR (the GPT
splits it "se nā"); 9.8 "jībane" — from the BR (GPT "jībana"). Not in the PK, KGC, PS, GCC, Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^25-18]: "Slaps His arms" (mālasāṭa) is a wrestler's challenge before a bout: singing of Gaura, Advaita as it were challenges Kali to battle. "Even the noble
wives weep": their hearts melt at the kirtana; these are tears of devotion, not of worldly feeling.

## 10. Narahari — "dekha mora advaita guṇanidhi…" (GPT1 p. 444, no. 17; BR; GCd)
*Advaita's form, as if fashioned of nectar: its radiance surpasses gold, ketaki and kunkuma; His moon-face gleams as He calls "Gora, Gora!"; He
dances with raised arms, embraces the fallen and gives away the priceless treasure. Raga kamoda. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is
in the BR and the Gita-chandrodaya.*[^25-19]

দেখ মোর অদ্বৈত গুণনিধি ।
না জানিয়ে কত সাধে সুধা দিয়া এ তনু গঠিল বিধি ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*dekha mora advaita guṇanidhi |*
*nā jāniye kata sādhe sudhā diyā e tanu gaṭhila bidhi || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* dekha — behold; mora advaita — my Advaita; guṇanidhi — the treasury of virtues; nā jāniye — I do not know; kata sādhe — with what longing; sudhā diyā — with nectar; e tanu — this body; gaṭhila bidhi — the Creator fashioned

**10.1.** Behold: my Advaita is a treasury of virtues!
I do not know with what love the Creator fashioned this body of nectar.

কনক কেতকী কুঙ্কুম জিনি সুচারু রূপের ছটা ।
গর গর গোরা-প্রেমে অতিশয় শোভয়ে পুলক ঘটা ॥

*kanaka ketakī kuṅkuma jini sucāru rūpera chaṭā |*
*gara gara gorā-preme atiśaya śobhaye pulaka ghaṭā ||*

*Word for word:* kanaka ketakī kuṅkuma jini — surpassing gold, ketaki and kunkuma; sucāru rūpera chaṭā — the radiance of His lovely form; gara gara — overflowing; gorā-preme — with love for Gora; atiśaya śobhaye — is wondrously adorned; pulaka ghaṭā — with a wealth of horripilation

**10.2.** The radiance of His lovely form surpasses gold, ketaki and kunkuma;
overflowing with love for Gora, He is wondrously adorned with a wealth of horripilation.

নিরুপম বিধুবদন ঝলকে ঘন গোরা গোরা গোরা বুলি ।
দুনয়নে ধারা বহে অবিরত নাচয়ে দুবাহু তুলি ॥

*nirupama bidhubadana jhalake ghana gorā gorā gorā buli |*
*dunayane dhārā bahe abirata nācaye dubāhu tuli ||*

*Word for word:* nirupama bidhu-badana — the matchless moon-face; jhalake — gleams; ghana — again and again; gorā gorā gorā buli — crying "Gora, Gora, Gora!"; du-nayane — from both eyes; dhārā bahe abirata — streams flow ceaselessly; nācaye — He dances; du-bāhu tuli — raising both arms

**10.3.** His matchless moon-face gleams as again and again He cries: "Gora, Gora, Gora!";
streams flow ceaselessly from both His eyes, He dances with both arms raised.

পতিত পামরে ধরি করে কোরে অমূল রতন যাচে ।
নরহরি পহুঁ বিনে কি এমন দয়ালু ভুবনে আছে ॥

*patita pāmare dhari kare kore amūla ratana yāce |*
*narahari pahum̐ bine ki emana dayālu bhubane āche ||*

*Word for word:* patita pāmare dhari — seizing the fallen and the base; kare kore — He embraces them; amūla ratana yāce — offers the priceless jewel unasked; narahari pahum̐ bine — apart from Narahari's Lord; ki emana dayālu — is there anyone so merciful; bhubane āche — in the world

**10.4.** Seizing the fallen and the base, He embraces them and Himself offers the priceless jewel;
is there anyone in the world so merciful, apart from Narahari's Lord?[^25-20]

[^25-19]: GPT1 — p. 444, no. 17 ("kāmoda"; scan, PDF p. 703); GPT2 — section 6.2, no. 17 (catalogue: NG-215). BR 12 (ed. 1912, p. 980; ed. 1960, vv. 3798–3801,
"punaḥ — kāmoda"; right after no. 16); Gita-chandrodaya — the section on Advaita, pada 6. Readings: 10.1 BR "e deha gaṭhala bidhi", GCd "guṇera nidhi",
"e deha gaṛala bidhi"; 10.4 BR and GCd "amūlya ratana". Not in the PK, KGC, PS, GCC. B.
[^25-20]: "The Creator fashioned the body of nectar" is a poetic formula of admiration for beauty: Advaita's body, like the Lord's, is eternal and
spiritual, not created by Brahma. Ketaki is the golden pandanus flower; kunkuma is saffron. "Narahari's Lord" (narahari-pahum̐) is the Lord whom the poet
serves (cf. note 44 of chapter 17): here, Advaita.

## 11. Narahari — "dekha advaita guṇera maṇi…" (GPT1 p. 444, no. 18; BR)
*Advaita gives away the treasure of bhakti and makes the world rich: He dances with the name of Gora, slapping His armpits; streams of bliss from His
eyes, His body gleaming like gold; around Him the companions singing to khol and karatalas; the wretched are maddened with prema. Raga ashavari.
**Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^25-21]

দেখ অদ্বৈত গুণের মণি ।
ভকতি রতন করি বিতরণ জগতে করয়ে ধনী ॥

*dekha advaita guṇera maṇi |*
*bhakati ratana kari bitaraṇa jagate karaye dhanī ||*

*Word for word:* dekha — behold; advaita — Advaita; guṇera maṇi — the jewel of virtues; bhakati ratana — the jewel of bhakti; kari bitaraṇa — distributing; jagate — the world; karaye dhanī — makes rich

**11.1.** Behold: Advaita is the jewel of virtues!
Distributing the treasure of bhakti, He makes the world rich.

কিবা ভাবে পুলকিত হিয়া ।
গোরা গোরা বুলি নাচে ভুজ তুলি ঘন কাঁখতালি দিয়া ॥

*kibā bhābe pulakita hiyā |*
*gorā gorā buli nāce bhuja tuli ghana kām̐khatāli diyā ||*

*Word for word:* kibā bhābe — in what bhava; pulakita hiyā — His heart thrills; gorā gorā buli — crying "Gora, Gora!"; nāce — He dances; bhuja tuli — raising His arms; ghana — again and again; kām̐khatāli diyā — slapping His armpits

**11.2.** In what bhava His heart thrills!
Crying "Gora, Gora!", He dances with raised arms and again and again slaps His armpits.

দুটী নয়নে আনন্দধারা ।
পুলক-বলিত তনু সুললিত ঝলকে কনক পারা ॥

*duṭī nayane ānandadhārā |*
*pulaka-balita tanu sulalita jhalake kanaka pārā ||*

*Word for word:* duṭī nayane — from both eyes; ānanda-dhārā — streams of bliss; pulaka-balita tanu — the body covered with horripilation; sulalita — lovely; jhalake — gleams; kanaka pārā — like gold

**11.3.** From both His eyes — streams of bliss;
His lovely body, covered with horripilation, gleams like gold.

মুখে ঝরয়ে অমিয়ারাশি ।
কি নব ভঙ্গীতে চাহে চারি ভিতে মধুর মধুর হাসি ॥

*mukhe jharaye amiyārāśi |*
*ki naba bhaṅgīte cāhe cāri bhite madhura madhura hāsi ||*

*Word for word:* mukhe — from His mouth; jharaye — pours; amiyā-rāśi — a mass of nectar; ki naba bhaṅgīte — with what new grace; cāhe cāri bhite — He looks on all sides; madhura madhura hāsi — smiling sweetly, sweetly

**11.4.** From His mouth pours a mass of nectar;
with what new grace He looks on all sides, smiling sweetly, sweetly!

পহুঁ বেড়ি পরিকর সাজে ।
মধুর সুস্বরে গায় ধীরে ধীরে খোল করতাল বাজে ॥

*pahum̐ beṛi parikara sāje |*
*madhura susvare gāya dhīre dhīre khola karatāla bāje ||*

*Word for word:* pahum̐ beṛi — surrounding the Lord; parikara sāje — the companions are arrayed; madhura susvare — with sweet voices; gāya dhīre dhīre — sing slowly; khola karatāla bāje — khol and karatalas resound

**11.5.** Around the Lord the companions are arrayed;
with sweet voices they sing slowly, khol and karatalas resound.

তাহা শুনি কে ধৈরজ বাঁধে ।
দীন হীন যত তারা উনমত নরহরি পড়ু ধাঁদে ॥

*tāhā śuni ke dhairaja bām̐dhe |*
*dīna hīna yata tārā unamata narahari paṛu dhām̐de ||*

*Word for word:* tāhā śuni — hearing that; ke dhairaja bām̐dhe — who can keep composure; dīna hīna yata — all the lowly and wretched; tārā unamata — they are maddened; narahari — Narahari; paṛu dhām̐de — falls into bewilderment

**11.6.** Who, hearing this, can keep his composure?
All the lowly and the wretched are maddened [with prema], and Narahari is lost in bewilderment.[^25-22]

[^25-21]: GPT1 — p. 444, no. 18 ("āśābarī"; scan, PDF p. 703); GPT2 — section 6.2, no. 18 (catalogue: NG-216). BR 12 (ed. 1912, p. 980; ed. 1960, vv. 3802–3807,
"punaḥ — āśābarī"; right after no. 17). Readings: 11.1 BR "jagat karaye dhanī"; 11.3 BR "subalita" ("shapely"); 11.6 BR "narahari paṛu phām̐de" ("Narahari is
caught in the snare" [of prema]). Not in the PK, KGC, PS, GCC, Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^25-22]: The pada is built of short refrain lines and long lines (a couplet is one unit). "Maddened" — the madness of prema, not worldly derangement. "Lost
in bewilderment" (paṛu dhām̐de) is a humble ending: the poet cannot fathom this play (in the BR, "caught in the snare", i.e. captivated by it).

## 12. Narahari — "advaita guṇamaṇi abanī karu dhanī…" (GPT1 p. 445, no. 20; BR)
*Advaita with His dear companions dances in the kirtana of Gora's glories: a radiance stealing Madana's pride, a body more tender than the shirisha,
tilaka, a garland of malati, the sacred thread; He whirls with raised arms, loudly cries "Gaurahari!" — and the fallen poet, seeing His merciful glance,
weeps. Raga tori (todi). **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^25-23]

অদ্বৈত গুণমণি অবনী করু ধনী ভকতিধন ঘন বিতরণে ।
সঙ্গেতে প্রিয়গণ আনন্দে নিমগন নাচয়ে গোরাগুণ কীরতনে ॥

*advaita guṇamaṇi abanī karu dhanī bhakatidhana ghana bitaraṇe |*
*saṅgete priyagaṇa ānande nimagana nācaye gorāguṇa kīratane ||*

*Word for word:* advaita guṇamaṇi — Advaita, the jewel of virtues; abanī karu dhanī — makes the earth rich; bhakati-dhana ghana bitaraṇe — lavishly distributing the wealth of bhakti; saṅgete priyagaṇa — with Him His dear ones; ānande nimagana — immersed in bliss; nācaye — dances; gorā-guṇa kīratane — in the kirtana of Gora's glories

**12.1.** Advaita, the jewel of virtues, lavishly distributing the wealth of bhakti, makes the earth rich;
with Him are His dear companions; immersed in bliss, He dances in the kirtana of Gora's glories.

কি নব ভঙ্গিভরে মদন-মদ হরে ঝলকে নিরুপম রুচি ছটা ।
শিরীষ ফুল জিনি মৃদুল তনুখানি তাহে বিপুল পুলকের ঘটা ॥

*ki naba bhaṅgibhare madana-mada hare jhalake nirupama ruci chaṭā |*
*śirīṣa phula jini mṛdula tanukhāni tāhe bipula pulakera ghaṭā ||*

*Word for word:* ki naba bhaṅgi-bhare — with what new grace; madana-mada hare — stealing Madana's pride; jhalake — gleams; nirupama ruci chaṭā — matchless radiance; śirīṣa phula jini — surpassing the shirisha flower; mṛdula tanukhāni — the tender body; tāhe — on it; bipula pulakera ghaṭā — a wealth of horripilation

**12.2.** With what new grace! — stealing Madana's pride, a matchless radiance gleams;
His tender body is softer than the shirisha flower, and on it is a wealth of horripilation.

তিলক শোভে ভালে মালতীমালা গলে দোলয়ে যজ্ঞসূত্র নেত্রলোভা ।
অতুল ভুজ তুলি ফিরয়ে হেলি দুলি চরণ চারু চালনি কি শোভা ॥

*tilaka śobhe bhāle mālatīmālā gale dolaye yajñasūtra netralobhā |*
*atula bhuja tuli phiraye heli duli caraṇa cāru cālani ki śobhā ||*

*Word for word:* tilaka śobhe bhāle — tilaka shines on the forehead; mālatī-mālā gale — a malati garland on the neck; dolaye yajñasūtra — the sacred thread sways; netra-lobhā — enticing the eyes; atula bhuja tuli — raising His matchless arms; phiraye heli duli — He turns, swaying; caraṇa cāru cālani — the lovely movements of His feet; ki śobhā — what beauty

**12.3.** Tilaka shines on His forehead, a garland of malati on His neck, the sacred thread sways, enticing the eyes;
raising His matchless arms, He whirls, swaying, — how lovely are the movements of His feet!

সঘনে গৌরহরি বোলয়ে উচ্চ করি ঝরয়ে সুধা জনু মুখচাঁদে ।
করুণ চাহনিতে কে পারে থির হৈতে পতিত নরহরি হেরি কাঁদে ॥

*saghane gaurahari bolaye ucca kari jharaye sudhā janu mukhacām̐de |*
*karuṇa cāhanite ke pāre thira haite patita narahari heri kām̐de ||*

*Word for word:* saghane — again and again; gaurahari bolaye — He cries "Gaurahari!"; ucca kari — loudly; jharaye sudhā — nectar flows; janu — as if; mukha-cām̐de — from His moon-face; karuṇa cāhanite — before His merciful glance; ke pāre thira haite — who can stay composed; patita narahari — fallen Narahari; heri kām̐de — weeps, beholding

**12.4.** Again and again He loudly cries "Gaurahari!" — as if nectar flowed from His moon-face;
who can stay composed before His merciful glance? Fallen Narahari, beholding Him, weeps.[^25-24]

[^25-23]: GPT1 — p. 445, no. 20 ("ṭori"; scan, PDF p. 704); GPT2 — section 6.2, no. 20. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-320; the signature-sweep
script took "gaurahari" in 12.4 for the signature — the signature here is "narahari" in the same line). BR 12 (ed. 1912, p. 981; ed. 1960, vv. 3812–3815, "punaḥ —
toṛī"; after Ghanashyama's pada no. 19); next comes the account of Nityananda's coming to Advaita: "Advaita Acharya, the merciful, plays in bhava with His
dear companions in His own house… He dances with raised arms, crying 'Nitai, Nitai!' — and at that moment Nityananda-Haladhara came from Saptagrama to
Advaita's house" (vv. 3816–3821). Readings: 12.1 BR "kiritane"; 12.4 "janu" ("as if") — from the BR (GPT "jāni"). Not in the PK, KGC, PS, GCC,
Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^25-24]: The sacred thread (yajñasūtra): Advaita is a brahmana; the malati garland and tilaka are the marks of a Vaishnava. Madana is the god of love: his
"pride" is put to shame by spiritual beauty (cf. note 4).

## 13. Narahari — "sītānātha mora advaitacām̐da…" (GPT1 p. 445, no. 21; BR; GCd)
*Praise of Advaita: by His call Gora was manifested; He is an ocean of compassion, the friend of the fallen, a second Creator in the three worlds, the giver
of sankirtana; whoever would float in the rasa of the Vraja lila, let him worship the Father of Achyuta. Raga dhanashi. **Attribution: probably
Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR and the Gita-chandrodaya.*[^25-25]

সীতানাথ মোর অদ্বৈতচাঁদ । প্রেমময় মহা মোহন ফাঁদ ॥

*sītānātha mora advaitacām̐da | premamaya mahā mohana phām̐da ||*

*Word for word:* sītānātha — the Lord of Sita; mora advaitacām̐da — my Advaitachandra; premamaya — full of prema; mahā mohana phām̐da — a great enchanting snare

**13.1.** My Advaitachandra, the Lord of Sita, —
full of prema, a great enchanting snare!

যাহার হুঙ্কারে প্রকট গোরা । নিত্যানন্দ সহ আনন্দে ভোরা ॥

*yāhāra huṅkāre prakaṭa gorā | nityānanda saha ānande bhorā ||*

*Word for word:* yāhāra huṅkāre — by whose roar; prakaṭa gorā — Gora was manifested; nityānanda saha — with Nityananda; ānande bhorā — absorbed in bliss

**13.2.** By His roar Gora was manifested;
with Nityananda He is absorbed in bliss.

অনুপম গুণ করুণা-সিন্ধু । পতিত অধম জনার বন্ধু ॥

*anupama guṇa karuṇā-sindhu | patita adhama janāra bandhu ||*

*Word for word:* anupama guṇa — matchless in virtues; karuṇā-sindhu — an ocean of compassion; patita adhama janāra bandhu — the friend of fallen and lowly people

**13.3.** Matchless are His virtues, He is an ocean of compassion,
the friend of fallen and lowly people.

ত্রিজগত মাঝে দ্বিতীয় ধাতা । সংকীর্তন ধন দুলহ দাতা ॥

*trijagata mājhe dvitīya dhātā | saṃkīrtana dhana dulaha dātā ||*

*Word for word:* trijagata mājhe — in the three worlds; dvitīya dhātā — a second Creator; saṃkīrtana dhana — of the wealth of sankirtana; dulaha — rare; dātā — the giver

**13.4.** In the three worlds He is a second Creator,
the giver of the rare wealth of sankirtana.

ব্রজলীলারসে ভাসিবে যে । অচ্যুতজনকে ভজুক সে ॥

*brajalīlārase bhāsibe ye | acyutajanake bhajuka se ||*

*Word for word:* braja-līlā-rase — in the rasa of the Vraja lila; bhāsibe ye — whoever would float; acyuta-janake — the Father of Achyuta; bhajuka se — let him worship

**13.5.** Whoever would float in the rasa of the Vraja lila,
let him worship the Father of Achyuta.

নরহরি পহুঁ যে নাহি ভজে । সেই অভাগিয়া ভুবন মাঝে ॥

*narahari pahum̐ ye nāhi bhaje | sei abhāgiyā bhubana mājhe ||*

*Word for word:* narahari pahum̐ — Narahari's Lord; ye nāhi bhaje — whoever does not worship; sei abhāgiyā — he is unfortunate; bhubana mājhe — in the world

**13.6.** Whoever does not worship Narahari's Lord —
he is the most unfortunate in the world.[^25-26]

[^25-25]: GPT1 — p. 445, no. 21 ("dhānaśī"; scan, PDF p. 704); GPT2 — section 6.2, no. 21. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-321). BR 12 (ed. 1912, p. 984;
ed. 1960, vv. 3853–3858, "gīte — yathā dhānaśī"): Nityananda, after staying with Advaita, comes to Navadvipa to Shachi, and then "from Shantipura came
Advaita Gosani and is always in bliss with Nityananda" (v. 3852); after the pada — "Nityananda and Advaita play in the joy of sankirtana together with
Srivasa, Murari and others" (v. 3859). Gita-chandrodaya — the section on Advaita, pada 7 (the last; "suhai"; some lines have dropped out in the OCR).
Readings: 13.3 BR "janera bandhu"; GCd 13.2 "yāra huṅkāre". Not in the PK, KGC, PS, GCC. B.
[^25-26]: "Enchanting snare" (mohana phām̐da): Advaita captivates hearts with prema. "A second Creator": Advaita as Maha-Vishnu is the original cause of
creation (CC Adi 6), as Brahma is its executor. "The Father of Achyuta" is Advaita, the Father of Achyutananda (cf. note 6); but "Achyuta" is also a name of
Krishna: service to Advaita leads into the rasa of the Vraja lila. "Narahari's Lord" is the Lord whom the poet serves (cf. note 20).

## 14. Narahari — "māgha saptamī śuklapakṣa…" (GPT1 p. 446, no. 24; BR)
*The advent of Advaita: on the bright seventh day of the month of Magha the beautiful Lord Advaita appeared and drove away Kali's arrogance; people run to
Kuvera's house and hail the child; bards, singers, musicians and dancers celebrate. Raga bhupali. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in
the BR; Vrajabuli.*[^25-27]

মাঘ সপ্তমী শুক্লপক্ষ শুভক্ষণ ক্ষণ ভূরী ।
প্রকট প্রভু অদ্বৈত সুন্দর কয়ল কলিমদ দূরি ॥

*māgha saptamī śuklapakṣa śubhakṣaṇa kṣaṇa bhūrī |*
*prakaṭa prabhu advaita sundara kayala kalimada dūri ||*

*Word for word:* māgha saptamī — in Magha, on the seventh day; śukla-pakṣa — of the bright fortnight; śubhakṣaṇa kṣaṇa bhūrī — at a most auspicious moment; prakaṭa prabhu — the Lord, appearing; advaita sundara — beautiful Advaita; kayala kalimada dūri — drove away Kali's arrogance

**14.1.** In the month of Magha, in the bright fortnight, on the seventh day, at a most auspicious moment,
the beautiful Lord Advaita appeared and drove away Kali's arrogance.

ধাই চলু সব লোক পৈঠি কুবেরভবন মাঝার ।
বিপুল পুলক নিরখি বালক দেত জয় জয় কার ॥

*dhāi calu saba loka paiṭhi kuberabhabana mājhāra |*
*bipula pulaka nirakhi bālaka deta jaya jaya kāra ||*

*Word for word:* dhāi calu saba loka — all the people ran; paiṭhi — entering; kubera-bhabana mājhāra — into Kuvera's house; bipula pulaka — with great thrill; nirakhi bālaka — gazing at the child; deta jaya jaya kāra — raise cries of "jaya, jaya"

**14.2.** All the people ran and entered Kuvera's house;
gazing at the child with great thrill, they cry: "Jaya, jaya!"

ভাটগণ ঘন ভণত যশ গায়ত গুণী মুদমাতি ।
সুঘড় বাদকবৃন্দ বায়ত বাদ্য কত কত ভাঁতি ॥

*bhāṭagaṇa ghana bhaṇata yaśa gāyata guṇī mudamāti |*
*sughaṛa bādakabṛnda bāyata bādya kata kata bhām̐ti ||*

*Word for word:* bhāṭagaṇa — the bards; ghana bhaṇata yaśa — loudly proclaim His fame; gāyata guṇī — skilled singers sing; muda-māti — intoxicated with joy; sughaṛa bādaka-bṛnda — skilful musicians; bāyata bādya — play instruments; kata kata bhām̐ti — in many ways

**14.3.** The bards loudly proclaim His fame, skilled singers sing, intoxicated with joy;
skilful musicians play their instruments in many ways.

করত নর্তক নৃত্য উঘটত থৈতা তক তক থোন ।
দাস নরহরি পহুঁক জনম বিলস বরণব কোন ॥

*karata nartaka nṛtya ughaṭata thaitā taka taka thona |*
*dāsa narahari pahum̐ka janama bilasa baraṇaba kona ||*

*Word for word:* karata nartaka nṛtya — the dancers dance; ughaṭata — sounding the rhythm; thaitā taka taka thona — "thaita taka taka thona"; dāsa narahari — Narahari Dasa; pahum̐ka janama — of the Lord's birth; bilasa — the festivity; baraṇaba kona — who can describe

**14.4.** The dancers dance, sounding the rhythm: "thaita taka taka thona".
Narahari Dasa: who can describe the festivity of the Lord's advent?[^25-28]

[^25-27]: GPT1 — p. 446, no. 24 ("bhūpālī"; scan, PDF p. 705); GPT2 — section 6.2, no. 24. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-322). BR 12 (ed. 1912, p. 829;
ed. 1960, vv. 1763–1766, "punaḥ — bhūpālī"): Ishana, showing Srinivasa the places of Navadvipa, tells how the Lord sent Rama Pandita to Shantipura for
Advaita, and from there turns to Advaita's family: His father is Kuvera Pandita (a quotation from the Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika on Kubera, v. 1755), His mother
Nabha; in their old age Advaitachandra was born to them at Navagram (vv. 1751–1758); then comes Ghanashyama's pada on the advent (GPT no. 23, vv. 1759–1762)
and this one; after it — "at Advaita's birth all loudly sang the names of Krishna and Govinda", His childhood, the move to Shantipura, His marriage (v. 1767
ff.). Readings: 14.1 BR "prakaṭi'" ("appearing"); 14.2 BR "biloki" ("seeing"); 14.4 BR "janama-bilāsa". The Navadvipa-parikrama is the same as the BR. Not in
the PK, KGC, PS, GCC, Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^25-28]: Advaita's advent took place at Navagram (Shrihatta), in the house of Kuvera Pandita and Nabha (cf. notes 10, 14); according to the
Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika (81–85) Kubera received from Sadashiva the boon: "in another birth I shall become your son". The Lord's appearance is not subject
to the laws of karma: it is a descent, not the birth of a conditioned soul (cf. Bhagavad-gita 4.6–9). "Thaita taka taka thona" are rhythm syllables (bol) of
the dance.

# Chapter 26. Appendix. Padas signed "Narahari" from the Gaura-pada-tarangini — X: companions and followers
