*Continuation and conclusion of the appendix (the introductory note on the two Naraharis, on the arguments for attribution and on the marks in
the headings is in ch. 17). Chapter 26: GPT section 6.3 "Companions" (GPT1 pp. 451–489) — all eighteen padas signed Narahari (nos. 2, 4, 7, 8,
42–44, 49, 55, 58, 61, 62, 68, 69, 71, 72, 77, 83), and also one pada on the sannyasa found in the continuous check of signatures in sections 3.x,
4.x and 5.3–7 (GPT1 5.3, no. 7). The first padas of the section are about Gaura's companions (Gadadhara Pandita, Srivasa, Gadadhara Dasa, the circle
of companions); then come padas about the followers of later generations: Shyamananda, the poet Jnanadasa, Srinivasa Acharya, Narottama,
Ramachandra and Govinda Kaviraja and their disciples. Such padas are marked in the heading "late layer: on the followers": they are not
Gaura-lila in the narrow sense but praises of the acharyas of the tradition through whom Gaura's mercy reached the following generations. The
signatures of the section were checked throughout, in the OCR and on the scan; the 14th and 15th waves of the Bhakti-ratnakara (BR) and its
conclusion, and the Gaura-charita-chintamani (GCC, kiranas 1 and 4), were read continuously at the relevant places. Not translated (outside the
appendix): nos. 15, 41, 48, 54, 63, 82 — signed Ghanashyama; no. 13 — signed Papiya Shekhara (about Narahari Sarakara; the catalogue had
counted it as Narahari's); no. 70 — signed Vallabha; no. 6 — no signature; the other padas of the section are by other poets. Pages 462–463 of
GPT1 (no. 27, end, to no. 30) are missing from the scan: these padas were checked in GPT2 — signed Madho and Radhavallabha. The base text is
GPT1 (by the scan), collated with GPT2, the BR (eds. 1912, 1960 and 2006) and the GCC (ed. 1947); the PK, KGC, PS, Gita-chandrodaya and
Narottama-vilasa were checked. Pronouns referring to Gaura, Nityananda and Advaita are capitalized, those referring to the companions and
followers are not. The notes of the GPT editors are not reproduced. At the end — a concluding note to the whole appendix.*

## 1. Narahari — "dhanya dhanya bali mena…" (GPT1 pp. 452–453, section 6.3, no. 2)
*The birth of Gadadhara Pandita: on the new-moon day of the month of Vaishakha, in the house of Madhava Mishra in Nadia, Gadadhara, Gauranga's
beloved, was born; Madhava and Ratnavati are beside themselves with joy, the people of Nadia praise their fortune, the brahmanas' wives bless
the infant, placing rice and durva grass on his head; the poet asks to sing Gadai's qualities birth after birth. Raga pahida. **Attribution: not
established** — GPT only; plain Bengali tripadi; the GPT2 index does not assign it to Sarakara.*[^26-1]

ধন্য ধন্য বলি মেন, চারি যুগ মধ্যে হেন, কলির ভাগ্যে সীমা নাই ।
সুন্দর নদীয়া পুরে, মাধব মিশ্রের ঘরে, কি অদ্ভুত আনন্দ বাধাই ॥

*dhanya dhanya bali mena, cāri yuga madhye hena, kalira bhāgye sīmā nāi |*
*sundara nadīyā pure, mādhaba miśrera ghare, ki adbhuta ānanda bādhāi ||*

*Word for word:* dhanya dhanya — glory, glory; bali — saying; mena (= yena) — as it were (here a particle; taken as "[all] say"); cāri yuga madhye — in the four yugas; hena — such; kalira bhāgye — to the fortune of Kali; sīmā nāi — there is no limit; sundara nadīyā pure — in the beautiful town of Nadia; mādhaba miśrera ghare — in the house of Madhava Mishra; ki adbhuta — what wondrous; ānanda bādhāi — rejoicing, festivity

**1.1.** "Glory, glory!" all say: in all four yugas there was nothing like it — the fortune of Kali knows no limit:
in beautiful Nadia, in the house of Madhava Mishra — what wondrous rejoicing!

বৈশাখের কুহু দিনে, জনমিলা শুভক্ষণে, গৌরাঙ্গের প্রিয় গদাধর ।
শ্রীমাধব রত্নাবতী, পুত্রমুখ দেখি অতি, উল্লাসে অধৈর্য্য নিরন্তর ॥

*baiśākhera kuhu dine, janamilā śubhakṣaṇe, gaurāṅgera priya gadādhara |*
*śrīmādhaba ratnābatī, putramukha dekhi ati, ullāse adhairyya nirantara ||*

*Word for word:* baiśākhera kuhu dine — on the new-moon day of Vaishakha; janamilā — was born; śubhakṣaṇe — at an auspicious moment; gaurāṅgera priya — Gauranga's beloved; gadādhara — Gadadhara; śrī-mādhaba ratnābatī — Sri Madhava and Ratnavati; putramukha dekhi — seeing their son's face; ati ullāse — in great joy; adhairya nirantara — ceaselessly beside themselves

**1.2.** On the new-moon day of Vaishakha, at an auspicious moment, Gadadhara, Gauranga's beloved, was born.
Sri Madhava and Ratnavati, seeing their son's face, are beside themselves with joy.

কিবা গদাধরশোভা, সভার নয়নলোভা, যেন কত আনন্দের ধাম ।
ঝলমল করে বর্ণ, জিনিয়া সে শুদ্ধ স্বর্ণ, সর্ব্বাঙ্গ সুন্দর অনুপাম ॥

*kibā gadādharaśobhā, sabhāra nayanalobhā, yena kata ānandera dhāma |*
*jhalamala kare barṇa, jiniyā se śuddha svarṇa, sarvvāṅga sundara anupāma ||*

*Word for word:* kibā — what; gadādhara-śobhā — Gadadhara's beauty; sabhāra nayana-lobhā — the delight of everyone's eyes; yena — as if; kata ānandera dhāma — the abode of every joy; jhalamala kare barṇa — his colour shines; jiniyā — surpassing; se śuddha svarṇa — pure gold; sarvāṅga sundara — his whole body beautiful; anupāma — incomparable

**1.3.** What beauty Gadadhara has — a delight to the eyes of all, as if the abode of every joy!
The colour of his skin shines, surpassing pure gold; his whole body is beautiful, incomparable.

যত নদীয়ার লোক, পাসরিয়া দুঃখ শোক, পরস্পর কহে কুতূহলে ।
মাধবের কিবা ভাগ্য, হৈল যেন রত্ন লভ্য, না জানি কতেক পুণ্যফলে ॥

*yata nadīyāra loka, pāsariyā duḥkha śoka, paraspara kahe kutūhale |*
*mādhabera kibā bhāgya, haila yena ratna labhya, nā jāni kateka puṇyaphale ||*

*Word for word:* yata nadīyāra loka — all the people of Nadia; pāsariyā — forgetting; duḥkha śoka — grief and sorrow; paraspara kahe — say to one another; kutūhale — with delight; mādhabera kibā bhāgya — how fortunate Madhava is; haila yena ratna labhya — as if he gained a jewel; nā jāni — we do not know; kateka puṇya-phale — as the fruit of what merits

**1.4.** All the people of Nadia, forgetting grief and sorrow, say to one another with delight:
"How fortunate Madhava is — as if he had gained a jewel! We do not know for what merits!"

বিপ্রপত্নীগণ আসি, আনন্দ-সাগরে ভাসি, রত্নাবতী মায়ে প্রশংসিয়া ।
দেখিয়া সোণার সুতে, ধান দূর্ব্বা দিয়া মাথে, আশীর্ব্বাদ করে হর্ষ হৈয়া ॥

*biprapatnīgaṇa āsi, ānanda-sāgare bhāsi, ratnābatī māye praśaṃsiyā |*
*dekhiyā soṇāra sute, dhāna dūrvvā diyā māthe, āśīrvvāda kare harṣa haiyā ||*

*Word for word:* bipra-patnī-gaṇa āsi — the brahmanas' wives, coming; ānanda-sāgare bhāsi — floating in an ocean of bliss; ratnābatī māye — mother Ratnavati; praśaṃsiyā — praising; dekhiyā soṇāra sute — seeing the golden son; dhāna dūrvā diyā māthe — placing rice and durva on his head; āśīrvāda kare — bless; harṣa haiyā — rejoicing

**1.5.** The wives of the brahmanas come, floating in an ocean of bliss, praise mother Ratnavati,
and, gazing on the golden son, place rice and durva grass on his head and joyfully bless him.

গদাধরপ্রভাবেতে, বিবিধ মঙ্গল যাতে, বন্দীগণ করে ধাওয়া ধাই ।
নরহরি কহে যেন, জনমে জনমে হেন, গদাইচাঁদের গুণ গাই ॥

*gadādharaprabhābete, bibidha maṅgala yāte, bandīgaṇa kare dhāoyā dhāi |*
*narahari kahe yena, janame janame hena, gadāicām̐dera guṇa gāi ||*

*Word for word:* gadādhara-prabhābete — by Gadadhara's power; bibidha maṅgala — all kinds of auspicious [rites]; yāte — [take place]; bandī-gaṇa — the bards; kare dhāoyā dhāi — hasten one after another; narahari kahe — Narahari says; yena — may it be that; janame janame — birth after birth; hena — thus; gadāicām̐dera guṇa gāi — I sing the qualities of Gadaichand

**1.6.** By Gadadhara's power all kinds of auspicious rites are performed; the bards hasten one after another [with praises].
Narahari says: "O that birth after birth I might sing Gadaichand's qualities just so!"[^26-2]

[^26-1]: GPT1 — pp. 452–453, section 6.3 "Companions" (parikara), no. 2 ("pahida"; scan, PDF pp. 711–712); GPT2 — section 6.3, no. 2 (NG-217). Not found in
the BR, GCC, Gita-chandrodaya, PK, KGC or PS. The reading in 1.1 "bali mena" (so in GPT1 and GPT2) is unclear; understood as "[all] say". C.
[^26-2]: Gadadhara Pandita — son of Madhava Mishra and Ratnavati of Navadvipa, inseparable companion of Mahaprabhu; according to the
Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika (147–153) he is Sri Radha Herself, "the Lakshmi of Gaura's love". "The new moon of Vaishakha" (kuhu — the new moon) is
the day of his appearance, as also in the Prema-vilasa (bilasa 22). The appearance of the Lord's eternal companion is not a birth under karma:
he descends together with the Lord. Rice and durva grass on the head — a Bengali rite of blessing a newborn. Gadai, Gadaichand — affectionate
names of Gadadhara.

## 2. Narahari — "gadādhara parama sughara rasadhāma…" (GPT1 p. 453, no. 4; GCC)
*Gadadhara among the companions in the morning: his fair body captivates Kama; the smile of his lotus face is nectar; his speech eclipses the
mantra that enchants the world; remembering his former pastimes he loses his composure; the poet smiles, seeing the hidden become manifest. Raga
not specified ("yatharaga"). **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC; Vrajabuli.*[^26-3]

গদাধর পরম সুঘর রসধাম ।
রুচির গৌর তনু তনুরুচি রুচিকর তছু নিরমঞ্ছন করু কত কাম ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*gadādhara parama sughara rasadhāma |*
*rucira gaura tanu tanuruci rucikara tachu niramañchana karu kata kāma || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* gadādhara — Gadadhara; parama sughara — supreme elegance; rasa-dhāma — abode of rasa; rucira gaura tanu — the beautiful fair body; tanu-ruci rucikara — captivating in its lustre; tachu — his; niramañchana karu — offer themselves in expiation; kata kāma — how many Kamadevas

**2.1.** Gadadhara is supreme elegance, an abode of rasa:
to his beautiful fair body, captivating in its lustre, how many Kamadevas offer themselves in expiation!

ও মুখকমল কমলবনবিজিত সুচারু মকরন্দ সদৃশ মৃদুহাস ।
ঘন ঘন নয়ন-চষক ভরি ভরি পরি পীয়ত হিয় মধি অধিক উলাস ॥

*o mukhakamala kamalabanabijita sucāru makaranda sadṛśa mṛduhāsa |*
*ghana ghana nayana-caṣaka bhari bhari pari pīyata hiya madhi adhika ulāsa ||*

*Word for word:* o mukha-kamala — that lotus face; kamalabana-bijita — that has conquered a forest of lotuses; sucāru makaranda sadṛśa — like lovely flower-nectar; mṛduhāsa — the gentle smile; ghana ghana — again and again; nayana-caṣaka — the cups of the eyes; bhari bhari pari — filling to the brim; pīyata — drinks; hiya madhi — in the heart; adhika ulāsa — great delight

**2.2.** That lotus face, which has conquered a whole forest of lotuses; his gentle smile — like lovely flower-nectar;
again and again, filling the cups of his eyes, he drinks — and in his heart there is great delight.

ও মৃদু মধুর বচন রচনা নব নিন্দিত জগবশীকরণ-সুমন্ত্র ।
শুনত লুব্ধ শ্রুতি শ্রুতিবাঞ্ছিত বহু বিসরিত বেদশ্রবণ শ্রুতিতন্ত্র ॥

*o mṛdu madhura bacana racanā naba nindita jagabaśīkaraṇa-sumantra |*
*śunata lubdha śruti śrutibāñchita bahu bisarita bedaśrabaṇa śrutitantra ||*

*Word for word:* o mṛdu madhura bacana — that soft, sweet speech; racanā naba — ever new in its composition; nindita — eclipsing; jaga-baśīkaraṇa-sumantra — the excellent mantra that enchants the world; śunata — hearing; lubdha śruti — the greedy ears; śruti-bāñchita — coveted by the Vedas; bahu bisarita — utterly forget; beda-śrabaṇa — the hearing of the Vedas; śruti-tantra — the shrutis and tantras

**2.3.** His soft, sweet speech, ever new, eclipses the mantra that enchants the world;
hearing it, greedy ears — coveted even by the Vedas — forget the hearing of Vedas and tantras.

পূরব চরিত চিত চিন্তি অথির ধৃতি গতি বিরহিত অতিশয় সুখে ভাসি ।
দূরে রহু হেম প্রেম নিরুপম বর নরহরি গুপত বেকত হেরি হাসি ॥

*pūraba carita cita cinti athira dhṛti gati birahita atiśaya sukhe bhāsi |*
*dūre rahu hema prema nirupama bara narahari gupata bekata heri hāsi ||*

*Word for word:* pūraba carita — former pastimes; cita cinti — remembering in the heart; athira — unsteady; dhṛti gati birahita — bereft of composure and motion; atiśaya sukhe bhāsi — floating in boundless happiness; dūre rahu hema — away with gold; prema nirupama bara — peerless, excellent [is his] prema; narahari — Narahari; gupata bekata heri — seeing the hidden made manifest; hāsi — smiles

**2.4.** Remembering in his heart his former pastimes, he loses steadiness, is bereft of motion and floats in boundless happiness.
Away with gold! — so peerless is his prema; Narahari, seeing the hidden become manifest, smiles.[^26-4]

[^26-3]: GPT1 — p. 453, no. 4 ("yatharaga"; scan, PDF p. 712); GPT2 — section 6.3, no. 4 (NG-218). GCC — kirana 4 ("The Lord in the circle of devotees":
in the morning the companions gather around Gaura, and the poet describes each of them), pada 17 ("yatharaga"; before it, pada 16 — also on
Gadadhara, signed Narahari, not in the GPT; after it — Ghanashyama's pada on Narahari Sarakara = GPT no. 15). The variants are insignificant (in the
OCR of the GCC the lines of 2.3 are distorted). Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^26-4]: "How many Kamadevas offer themselves" (niramañchana — a rite of waving something around a beloved and giving it away in expiation) — an
image of beauty before which the god of love fades. "Former pastimes" — the lila of Vraja: according to the Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika (147–153)
Gadadhara Pandita is Sri Radha; in Gaura-lila he hides this bhava, but in ecstasy it shows through — this is "the hidden become manifest".
"Away with gold" — neither the gold of his skin nor anything else compares with his prema. The subject in 2.2 (who "drinks") is not named:
Gadadhara drinks Gaura's beauty with his eyes (so in the context of the GCC), or the onlookers drink the nectar of his smile.

## 3. Narahari — "ājuka sukha kachu baraṇe na jāta…" (GPT1 p. 454, no. 7; GCC)
*Srivasa among the companions: seeing the Lord's play, he smiles softly; from love his body sways, his hairs stand on end as if he wore a
jacket of kadamba flowers; he trembles like a creeper in the wind, repeats "Friend of the lowly!", sings, dances, weeps. Raga not specified
("yatharaga"). **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC; Vrajabuli.*[^26-5]

আজুক সুখ কছু বরণে ন জাত ।
রসিক সুধীর সুঘর শ্রীবাস পহুঁ রঙ্গ হেরি মৃদু মৃদু মুসিকাত ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*ājuka sukha kachu baraṇe na jāta |*
*rasika sudhīra sughara śrībāsa pahum̐ raṅga heri mṛdu mṛdu musikāta || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* ājuka sukha — today's happiness; kachu baraṇe na jāta — cannot at all be described; rasika — knower of rasa; sudhīra — wise; sughara — elegant; śrībāsa — Srivasa; pahum̐ raṅga heri — seeing the Lord's play; mṛdu mṛdu musikāta — smiles very softly

**3.1.** Today's happiness cannot be described in words:
Srivasa — knower of rasa, wise and elegant — seeing the Lord's play, smiles very softly.

সুবলিত দেহ নেহভরে টলমল ললিত ভঙ্গী নিরুপম ছবি ভারী ।
অবিরল পুলক কদম্ব লসত জনু পহিরল কঞ্চু পরম রুচিকারী ॥

*subalita deha nehabhare ṭalamala lalita bhaṅgī nirupama chabi bhārī |*
*abirala pulaka kadamba lasata janu pahirala kañcu parama rucikārī ||*

*Word for word:* subalita deha — the stately body; nehabhare ṭalamala — sways with love; lalita bhaṅgī — graceful bearing; nirupama chabi bhārī — incomparable great beauty; abirala pulaka — the dense thrill of hairs; kadamba lasata — shines [like] kadamba; janu — as if; pahirala kañcu — he had put on a jacket; parama rucikārī — most beautiful

**3.2.** His stately body sways with love; graceful is his bearing, incomparable his wondrous beauty;
his thickly risen hairs shine as if he had put on a most beautiful jacket of kadamba flowers.

বাতাতুর লতিকা সম কম্প ন শকত সম্ভারি বিবশ রসপূর ।
দীনবন্ধু কত বদত নিরন্তর অন্তর তরল রহল ধৃতি দূর ॥

*bātātura latikā sama kampa na śakata sambhāri bibaśa rasapūra |*
*dīnabandhu kata badata nirantara antara tarala rahala dhṛti dūra ||*

*Word for word:* bātātura latikā sama — like a creeper tormented by the wind; kampa — he trembles; na śakata sambhāri — cannot master [himself]; bibaśa rasa-pūra — helpless in the flood of rasa; dīnabandhu — "Friend of the lowly"; kata badata nirantara — repeats ceaselessly; antara tarala — his heart melts; rahala dhṛti dūra — steadiness has gone far away

**3.3.** He trembles like a creeper in the wind and cannot master himself, helpless in the flood of rasa;
ceaselessly he repeats: "Friend of the lowly!" — his heart melts, and steadiness has left him.

সুন্দর গুণগণ গাওত লঘু লঘু নাচত নয়নে বহত জলধার ।
নরহরি ভণ অনুভব ন হোত হিয় উপজত কত কত ভাব বিকার ॥

*sundara guṇagaṇa gāota laghu laghu nācata nayane bahata jaladhāra |*
*narahari bhaṇa anubhaba na hota hiya upajata kata kata bhāba bikāra ||*

*Word for word:* sundara guṇagaṇa gāota — he sings the beautiful qualities; laghu laghu nācata — lightly dances; nayane bahata jaladhāra — streams of tears flow from his eyes; narahari bhaṇa — says Narahari; anubhaba na hota — one cannot fathom; hiya upajata — arise in the heart; kata kata bhāba-bikāra — how many stirrings of bhava

**3.4.** He sings the beautiful qualities [of the Lord], lightly dances, streams of tears flow from his eyes.
Narahari says: one cannot fathom how many stirrings of bhava arise in his heart.[^26-6]

[^26-5]: GPT1 — p. 454, no. 7 ("yatharaga"; scan, PDF p. 713); GPT2 — section 6.3, no. 7. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-323). GCC — kirana 4,
pada 19 ("yatharaga"). Variants: 3.3 "dīnabandhu" by the GCC and the GPT1 scan (GPT1 OCR — "bīṇa bandhu"). Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or
Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^26-6]: Srivasa Pandita — in his house the Lord held the nightly sankirtana; according to the Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika (90) he is Narada Muni.
"A jacket of kadamba flowers" — the thrill of the hairs (pulaka), like the knobbly kadamba flower. "Friend of the lowly" (dīnabandhu) — an
address to the Lord.

## 4. Narahari — "sundara sughara gadādhara dāsa…" (GPT1 p. 454, no. 8; GCC)
*Gadadhara Dasa beside Gaura — like a moon beside the moon; his tender body eclipses the champaka flower; his eyes are languid; former bhavas
arise ceaselessly in his heart, and however much he hides them, he cannot. Raga not specified ("yatharaga"). **Attribution: probably
Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC; Vrajabuli.*[^26-7]

সুন্দর সুঘর গদাধর দাস ।
গুণমণি গৌরসমীপ বিলসত জনু চন্দ নিকট হি চন্দ পরকাশ ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*sundara sughara gadādhara dāsa |*
*guṇamaṇi gaurasamīpa bilasata janu canda nikaṭa hi canda parakāśa || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* sundara sughara — beautiful, elegant; gadādhara dāsa — Gadadhara Dasa; guṇamaṇi gaura-samīpa — beside Gaura, the jewel of qualities; bilasata — shines; janu — as if; canda nikaṭa hi — beside the moon; canda parakāśa — a moon had risen

**4.1.** Beautiful, elegant is Gadadhara Dasa:
beside Gaura, the jewel of qualities, he shines as if beside the moon another moon had risen.

মৃদুতর দেহ নেহময় মধুরিম মাধুরী করু চম্পক-মদ-খীন ।
ধৃতিভর-ভঞ্জনকারী ভঙ্গী ভুব রঞ্জন কঞ্জ-চরণ গতিহীন ॥

*mṛdutara deha nehamaya madhurima mādhurī karu campaka-mada-khīna |*
*dhṛtibhara-bhañjanakārī bhaṅgī bhuba rañjana kañja-caraṇa gatihīna ||*

*Word for word:* mṛdutara deha — the most tender body; nehamaya — full of love; madhurima mādhurī — sweet charm; karu campaka-mada-khīna — robs the champaka of its pride; dhṛti-bhara-bhañjanakārī — shattering composure; bhaṅgī — bearing; bhuba rañjana — the brows enchant; kañja-caraṇa — lotus feet; gatihīna — motionless

**4.2.** His most tender body is full of love, his sweet charm robs the champaka flower of its pride;
his bearing shatters composure, the movement of his brows enchants, his lotus feet cannot take a step.

আলস যুত যুগ নেত্র রুচিরতর তরল কিঞ্চিদপি নিমিখ বিভঙ্গ ।
নিরমল গণ্ডযুগল ঝল ঝলকত ললিত হাস সহ অধর সুরঙ্গ ॥

*ālasa yuta yuga netra ruciratara tarala kiñcidapi nimikha bibhaṅga |*
*niramala gaṇḍayugala jhala jhalakata lalita hāsa saha adhara suraṅga ||*

*Word for word:* ālasa yuta — languid; yuga netra — both eyes; ruciratara — lovelier than lovely; tarala — tremulous; kiñcidapi nimikha bibhaṅga — barely blinking; niramala gaṇḍa-yugala — clear cheeks; jhala jhalakata — gleam; lalita hāsa saha — with a charming smile; adhara suraṅga — red lips

**4.3.** Both his eyes are languid and lovelier than lovely, tremulous, barely blinking;
his clear cheeks gleam, on his red lips — a charming smile.

অনুভব ন হোই নিরন্তর অন্তর উপজত পূরব ভাব বহু ভাঁতি ।
গুপত করত কত যতন ন গোপন নরহরি হেরি হসত সুখে মাতি ॥

*anubhaba na hoi nirantara antara upajata pūraba bhāba bahu bhām̐ti |*
*gupata karata kata yatana na gopana narahari heri hasata sukhe māti ||*

*Word for word:* anubhaba na hoi — unfathomable; nirantara antara upajata — ceaselessly arise in the heart; pūraba bhāba — former bhavas; bahu bhām̐ti — in many ways; gupata karata — he hides; kata yatana — however he tries; na gopana — they are not hidden; narahari heri — Narahari, looking; hasata sukhe māti — laughs, intoxicated with happiness

**4.4.** Unfathomable: in his heart former bhavas ceaselessly arise — in every way;
however he tries to hide them — they cannot be hidden; Narahari, looking at him, laughs, intoxicated with happiness.[^26-8]

[^26-7]: GPT1 — p. 454, no. 8 ("yatharaga"; scan, PDF p. 713); GPT2 — section 6.3, no. 8 (NG-219; the signature in GPT1 is "narahari", distorted in the
OCR — "nabrahari"). GCC — kirana 4, pada 20 ("yatharaga"). Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^26-8]: Gadadhara Dasa — a companion of Gaura and Nityananda (later lived in Ariadaha, cf. chapter 24, no. 22); according to the
Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika (154–155) — Chandrakanti, a manifestation of Radha's radiance, and in him also Purnananda, the beloved of Balarama.
"Former bhavas" — his eternal service in Vraja. "Like a moon beside the moon" — both are fair: Gauranga and His companion.

## 5. Narahari — "o mora parāṇa-bandhu śyāmānanda…" (GPT1 p. 469, no. 42; BR)
*Late layer: on the followers. The life of Shyamananda: he left home and came to Ambika to Hridaya Chaitanya, who accepted him as a disciple and
entrusted him to Nitai and Chaitanya; receiving at his departure the garland of permission, he came alone to Vrindavana, at Radha-kunda received
the mercy of Raghunatha Dasa, from Jiva Gosvami fatherly love; he studied the books and, at the Gosvamis' command, returned through Gauda and Ambika
to Utkala, and there intoxicated even the godless with Gaura's name. Raga kamoda. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR
(15th wave, "the song of Shyamananda's life").*[^26-9]

ও মোর পরাণ-বন্ধু, শ্যামানন্দ সুখসিন্ধু, সদাই বিহ্বল গোরাগুণে ।
গৃহ পরিহরি দূরে, আনন্দে অম্বিকাপুরে, আইলেন প্রভুর ভবনে ॥

*o mora parāṇa-bandhu, śyāmānanda sukhasindhu, sadāi bihvala gorāguṇe |*
*gṛha parihari dūre, ānande ambikāpure, āilena prabhura bhabane ||*

*Word for word:* o mora parāṇa-bandhu — O my dear friend; śyāmānanda — Shyamananda; sukha-sindhu — ocean of happiness; sadāi bihvala — ever intoxicated; gorā-guṇe — with Gora's qualities; gṛha parihari dūre — leaving home far behind; ānande — joyfully; ambikāpure — to Ambikapur; āilena prabhura bhabane — came to his master's house

**5.1.** O my dear friend Shyamananda, ocean of happiness, ever intoxicated with the qualities of Gora!
Leaving his home far behind, he came joyfully to Ambikapur, to the house of his master.

হৃদয়চৈতন্য দেখি, অঝোরে ঝরয়ে আঁখি, ভূমিতে পড়য়ে লোটাইয়া ।
শিরে ধরি সে চরণ, করি আত্মসমর্পণ, একচিতে রহে দাঁড়াইয়া ॥

*hṛdayacaitanya dekhi, ajhore jharaye ām̐khi, bhūmite paṛaye loṭāiyā |*
*śire dhari se caraṇa, kari ātmasamarpaṇa, ekacite rahe dām̐ṛāiyā ||*

*Word for word:* hṛdaya-caitanya dekhi — seeing Hridaya Chaitanya; ajhore jharaye ām̐khi — his eyes weep unrestrainedly; bhūmite paṛaye loṭāiyā — falls rolling on the ground; śire dhari se caraṇa — taking those feet on his head; kari ātmasamarpaṇa — surrendering himself; ekacite — single-mindedly; rahe dām̐ṛāiyā — stands

**5.2.** Seeing Hridaya Chaitanya, he weeps unrestrainedly and falls, rolling on the ground;
taking his feet on his head, surrendering himself, he stands with his whole heart fixed on him.

দেখি শ্যামানন্দ রীত, ঠাকুর করিয়া প্রীত, নিকটে রাখিয়া শিষ্য কৈল ।
করি অনুগ্রহ অতি, শিখাইয়া ভক্তিরীতি, নিতাই চৈতন্যে সমর্পিল ॥

*dekhi śyāmānanda rīta, ṭhākura kariyā prīta, nikaṭe rākhiyā śiṣya kaila |*
*kari anugraha ati, śikhāiyā bhaktirīti, nitāi caitanye samarpila ||*

*Word for word:* dekhi śyāmānanda-rīta — seeing Shyamananda's nature; ṭhākura kariyā prīta — the Thakura, growing fond; nikaṭe rākhiyā — keeping him near; śiṣya kaila — made him a disciple; kari anugraha ati — showing great mercy; śikhāiyā bhakti-rīti — teaching the way of bhakti; nitāi caitanye samarpila — entrusted him to Nitai and Chaitanya

**5.3.** Seeing Shyamananda's nature, the Thakura grew fond of him, kept him near and made him a disciple;
showing him great mercy and teaching him the way of bhakti, he entrusted him to Nitai and Chaitanya.

কতক দিবস পরে, পাঠাইতে ব্রজপুরে, শ্যামানন্দ ব্যাকুল হইলা ।
প্রভু নিতাই চৈতন্য, শ্যামানন্দে কৈলা ধন্য, যাত্রাকালে আজ্ঞা মালা দিলা ॥

*kataka dibasa pare, pāṭhāite brajapure, śyāmānanda byākula hailā |*
*prabhu nitāi caitanya, śyāmānande kailā dhanya, yātrākāle ājñā mālā dilā ||*

*Word for word:* kataka dibasa pare — after some days; pāṭhāite brajapure — [longing] to be sent to Vraja; śyāmānanda byākula hailā — Shyamananda grew restless; prabhu nitāi caitanya — the Lords Nitai and Chaitanya; śyāmānande kailā dhanya — blessed Shyamananda; yātrākāle — at the time of departure; ājñā mālā dilā — gave the garland of permission

**5.4.** After some days Shyamananda grew restless with longing — to be sent to Vraja;
the Lords Nitai and Chaitanya blessed Shyamananda: at the time of departure he was given the garland of permission.

শ্যামানন্দ পথে চলে, ভাসয়ে আঁখের জলে, সোঙরিয়া প্রভুর গুণগণ ।
একাকী কতক দিনে, প্রবেশিলা বৃন্দাবনে, বহু তীর্থ করিয়া ভ্রমণ ॥

*śyāmānanda pathe cale, bhāsaye ām̐khera jale, soṅariyā prabhura guṇagaṇa |*
*ekākī kataka dine, prabeśilā bṛndābane, bahu tīrtha kariyā bhramaṇa ||*

*Word for word:* śyāmānanda pathe cale — Shyamananda goes on his way; bhāsaye ām̐khera jale — drowned in tears; soṅariyā — remembering; prabhura guṇagaṇa — his master's qualities; ekākī — alone; kataka dine — after some days; prabeśilā bṛndābane — entered Vrindavana; bahu tīrtha kariyā bhramaṇa — having visited many holy places

**5.5.** Shyamananda goes on his way, drowned in tears, remembering his master's qualities;
alone, after some days, having visited many holy places, he entered Vrindavana.

দেখিয়া শ্রীবৃন্দারণ্য, আপনা মানয়ে ধন্য, আনন্দে ধরিতে নারে থেহা ।
সিক্ত হৈয়া নেত্রজলে, লোটায় ধরণীতলে, বিপুল পুলকময় দেহা ॥

*dekhiyā śrībṛndāraṇya, āpanā mānaye dhanya, ānande dharite nāre thehā |*
*sikta haiyā netrajale, loṭāya dharaṇītale, bipula pulakamaya dehā ||*

*Word for word:* dekhiyā śrī-bṛndāraṇya — seeing Sri Vrindaranya; āpanā mānaye dhanya — counted himself blessed; ānande dharite nāre thehā — could not contain himself for joy; sikta haiyā netrajale — bathed in tears; loṭāya dharaṇītale — rolls on the ground; bipula pulakamaya dehā — his body full of thrills

**5.6.** Seeing Sri Vrindaranya, he counted himself blessed and could not contain his bliss;
bathed in tears, he rolls on the ground, his whole body thrilling.

গিয়া গিরি গোবর্দ্ধনে, কৈল যা আছিল মনে, শ্রীরাধাকুণ্ডের তটে আসি ।
প্রেমায় বিহ্বল হৈলা, দেখি অনুগ্রহ কৈলা, শ্রীদাস গোসাঁই গুণরাশি ॥

*giyā giri gobarddhane, kaila yā āchila mane, śrīrādhākuṇḍera taṭe āsi |*
*premāya bihvala hailā, dekhi anugraha kailā, śrīdāsa gosām̐i guṇarāśi ||*

*Word for word:* giyā giri gobardhane — going to Mount Govardhana; kaila yā āchila mane — he did what was in his heart; śrī-rādhākuṇḍera taṭe āsi — coming to the bank of Sri Radha-kunda; premāya bihvala hailā — was overwhelmed with prema; dekhi — seeing [this]; anugraha kailā — showed mercy; śrī-dāsa gosām̐i — Sri Dasa Gosani; guṇarāśi — a treasury of virtues

**5.7.** Going to Mount Govardhana, he did what was in his heart; coming to the bank of Sri Radha-kunda,
he was overwhelmed with prema — seeing this, Sri Dasa Gosani, a treasury of virtues, showed him mercy.

শ্রীজীব নিকটে গেলা, নিজ পরিচয় দিলা, তেঁহ কৃপা কৈলা বাৎসল্যেতে ।
যেবা মনোরথ ছিল, তাহা যেন পূর্ণ হৈল, হৃদয়চৈতন্য-কৃপা হৈতে ॥

*śrījība nikaṭe gelā, nija paricaya dilā, tem̐ha kṛpā kailā bātsalyete |*
*yebā manoratha chila, tāhā yena pūrṇa haila, hṛdayacaitanya-kṛpā haite ||*

*Word for word:* śrī-jība nikaṭe gelā — went to Sri Jiva; nija paricaya dilā — told who he was; tem̐ha kṛpā kailā — he showed mercy; bātsalyete — with fatherly love; yebā manoratha chila — whatever he had longed for; tāhā yena pūrṇa haila — was as if fulfilled; hṛdaya-caitanya-kṛpā haite — by the mercy of Hridaya Chaitanya

**5.8.** He went to Sri Jiva and told who he was; Jiva showed him mercy with fatherly love.
Whatever he had longed for was as if fulfilled — by the mercy of Hridaya Chaitanya.

ভ্রমিলা দ্বাদশ বন, কৈলা গ্রন্থ অধ্যয়ন, হৈলা অতি নিপুণ সেবায় ।
শ্রীগৌড় অম্বিকা হৈয়া, রহিলা উৎকলে গিয়া, শ্রীগোস্বামিগণের আজ্ঞায় ॥

*bhramilā dvādaśa bana, kailā grantha adhyayana, hailā ati nipuṇa sebāya |*
*śrīgauṛa ambikā haiyā, rahilā utkale giyā, śrīgosvāmigaṇera ājñāya ||*

*Word for word:* bhramilā dvādaśa bana — wandered through the twelve forests; kailā grantha adhyayana — studied the books; hailā ati nipuṇa sebāya — became most skilled in service; śrī-gauṛa ambikā haiyā — by way of Sri Gauda and Ambika; rahilā utkale giyā — went and settled in Utkala; śrī-gosvāmigaṇera ājñāya — at the command of the Gosvamis

**5.9.** He wandered through the twelve forests, studied the books, became most skilled in service;
by way of Sri Gauda and Ambika he went and settled in Utkala — at the command of the Gosvamis.

পাষণ্ডী অসুরগণে, মাতাইল গোরাগুণে, কারে বা না কৈলা ভক্তিদান ।
অধম আনন্দে ভাসে, শ্যামানন্দ-কৃপালেশে, কেবা না পাইল পরিত্রাণ ॥

*pāṣaṇḍī asuragaṇe, mātāila gorāguṇe, kāre bā nā kailā bhaktidāna |*
*adhama ānande bhāse, śyāmānanda-kṛpāleśe, kebā nā pāila paritrāṇa ||*

*Word for word:* pāṣaṇḍī asura-gaṇe — the godless and the asuras; mātāila gorā-guṇe — he intoxicated with Gora's qualities; kāre vā nā kailā bhakti-dāna — to whom did he not give bhakti; adhama ānande bhāse — the fallen float in bliss; śyāmānanda-kṛpāleśe — by a particle of Shyamananda's mercy; kebā nā pāila paritrāṇa — who did not gain deliverance

**5.10.** The godless and the asuras he intoxicated with Gora's qualities — to whom did he not give bhakti!
The fallen float in bliss — who did not gain deliverance by a particle of Shyamananda's mercy?

কে জানিবে তার তত্ত্ব, সদা সংকীর্ত্তনে মত্ত, অবনীতে বিদিত মহিমা ।
নিজ পরিকর সঙ্গে, বিলসে পরম রঙ্গে, উৎকলে সুখের নাহি সীমা ॥

*ke jānibe tāra tattva, sadā saṃkīrttane matta, abanīte bidita mahimā |*
*nija parikara saṅge, bilase parama raṅge, utkale sukhera nāhi sīmā ||*

*Word for word:* ke jānibe tāra tattva — who will know his true nature; sadā saṅkīrtane matta — ever intoxicated with sankirtana; abanīte bidita mahimā — his greatness is famed on earth; nija parikara saṅge — with his own companions; bilase parama raṅge — sports with great delight; utkale sukhera nāhi sīmā — in Utkala happiness has no bounds

**5.11.** Who will understand his true nature? Ever intoxicated with sankirtana, he is famed on earth for his greatness;
with his companions he sports joyfully — in Utkala happiness knows no bounds.

যে বারেক দেখে তারে, সে ধৃতি ধরিতে নারে, কিবা সে মূরতি মনোহর ।
নরহরি কহে কভু, রসিকানন্দের প্রভু, হবে কি এ নয়নগোচর ॥

*ye bāreka dekhe tāre, se dhṛti dharite nāre, kibā se mūrati manohara |*
*narahari kahe kabhu, rasikānandera prabhu, habe ki e nayanagocara ||*

*Word for word:* ye bāreka dekhe tāre — whoever sees him once; se dhṛti dharite nāre — cannot keep composure; kibā se mūrati manohara — how enchanting is that form; narahari kahe — Narahari says; kabhu — ever; rasikānandera prabhu — the master of Rasikananda; habe ki — will he be; e nayana-gocara — visible to these eyes

**5.12.** Whoever sees him even once cannot keep his composure — how enchanting is his form!
Narahari says: "Will the master of Rasikananda ever appear before these eyes?"[^26-10]

[^26-9]: GPT1 — p. 469, no. 42 ("kamoda"; scan, PDF p. 726); GPT2 — section 6.3, no. 42 (NG-221). BR 15 (ed. 1912, pp. 1059–1060; ed. 1960, 15.93–104, "the
song of the life of Srila Shyamananda Prabhu — in song, kamoda"): after the account of Rasikananda and Ghanashyama's pada about him (GPT no. 48) —
"who is not charmed by Shyamananda's qualities? All sing of his life in various ways" (15.92), then this pada and the next (GPT no. 43). Variants:
5.2 BR "eka bhite rahe dām̐ṛāiyā" ("stands to one side"; GPT "ekacite" — "single-mindedly"); 5.6 BR "ānande dharite nāre thehā"; the rest
orthographic. Not in the GCC, PK, KGC, PS or Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^26-10]: Shyamananda (in his youth Duhkhi Krishnadasa) — a disciple of Hridaya Chaitanya (himself a disciple of Gauridasa Pandita) of Ambika-Kalna;
together with Srinivasa and Narottama he studied under Jiva Gosvami and returned to Gauda with the Gosvamis' books; he preached in Utkala
(Orissa). In Ambika are the Gaura-Nitai Deities of Gauridasa Pandita: the "garland of permission" (ājñāmālā) is a garland from the Deity as a sign
of leave; hence in 5.4 it is "the Lords Nitai and Chaitanya", not only the teacher, who release Shyamananda (cf. the Prema-vilasa, vilasa 12).
"Sri Dasa Gosani" — Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami at Radha-kunda. "The twelve forests" — the forests of Vraja. "The master of Rasikananda" — Shyamananda,
guru of Rasikananda (Murari), his chief disciple in Utkala. The poet's wish to "see" Shyamananda is a prayer for darshan in the heart (the poet
lived later).

## 6. Narahari — "jaya śrīla duḥkhī kṛṣṇadāsa…" (GPT1 p. 470, no. 43; BR)
*Late layer: on the followers. Praise of Duhkhi Krishnadasa: his mind is a bee at the lotus feet of Hridaya Chaitanya; in Vrindavana, in a grove,
he found Radha's anklet and became known as Shyamananda; he flooded Utkala, where there was not a particle of bhakti, with Gaura's prema; the
poet praises his mercy. Raga suhai. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (15th wave, right after the preceding one).*[^26-11]

জয় শ্রীল দুঃখী কৃষ্ণদাস গুণ কহিতে শকতি কার ।
হৃদয়চৈতন্য পদাম্বুজে সদা চিত-মধুকর যার ॥

*jaya śrīla duḥkhī kṛṣṇadāsa guṇa kahite śakati kāra |*
*hṛdayacaitanya padāmbuje sadā cita-madhukara yāra ||*

*Word for word:* jaya — glory; śrīla duḥkhī kṛṣṇadāsa — to Srila Duhkhi Krishnadasa; guṇa kahite — to tell the qualities; śakati kāra — who has the power; hṛdaya-caitanya padāmbuje — at the lotus feet of Hridaya Chaitanya; sadā — ever; cita-madhukara yāra — whose mind is a bee

**6.1.** Glory to Srila Duhkhi Krishnadasa! Who has the power to tell his qualities?
His mind-bee is ever at the lotus feet of Hridaya Chaitanya.

বৃন্দাবনে নব নিকুঞ্জে রাইর নূপুর পাইল যে ।
শ্যামানন্দ নাম বিদিত তথায় চরিত বুঝিবে কে ॥

*bṛndābane naba nikuñje rāira nūpura pāila ye |*
*śyāmānanda nāma bidita tathāya carita bujhibe ke ||*

*Word for word:* bṛndābane — in Vrindavana; naba nikuñje — in a new grove; rāira nūpura — Rai's anklet; pāila ye — he who found; śyāmānanda nāma — the name Shyamananda; bidita tathāya — became known there; carita bujhibe ke — who will understand his life

**6.2.** In Vrindavana, in a new grove, he found the anklet of Rai;
there he became known as Shyamananda — who will understand his life?

মহামূঢ়মতি উৎকলেতে যার না ছিল ভকতিলেশ ।
গৌরপ্রেমরসে ভাসাইল সব সফল করিল দেশ ॥

*mahāmūṛhamati utkalete yāra nā chila bhakatileśa |*
*gaurapremarase bhāsāila saba saphala karila deśa ||*

*Word for word:* mahā-mūṛha-mati — utterly darkened in mind; utkalete — in Utkala; yāra nā chila — who had not; bhakati-leśa — a trace of bhakti; gaura-prema-rase — with the rasa of Gaura's prema; bhāsāila saba — he flooded all; saphala karila deśa — made the land blessed

**6.3.** In Utkala, where people utterly darkened in mind had not a trace of bhakti,
he flooded everyone with the rasa of Gaura's prema and made the land blessed.

পরমদুঃখে দুঃখী শ্যামানন্দ মোর রসিকানন্দের প্রভু ।
কি কব করুণা যেহো নরহরি দীনে না ছাড়য়ে কভু ॥

*paramaduḥkhe duḥkhī śyāmānanda mora rasikānandera prabhu |*
*ki kaba karuṇā yeho narahari dīne nā chāṛaye kabhu ||*

*Word for word:* parama-duḥkhe duḥkhī — sorrowing at great sorrow; śyāmānanda mora — my Shyamananda; rasikānandera prabhu — the master of Rasikananda; ki kaba karuṇā — how can I tell his mercy; yeho — he who; narahari dīne — lowly Narahari; nā chāṛaye kabhu — never abandons

**6.4.** My Shyamananda, "the Sorrowful" — sorrowing at the great sorrow [of others], the master of Rasikananda —
how can I tell his mercy? He never abandons lowly Narahari.[^26-12]

[^26-11]: GPT1 — p. 470, no. 43 ("suhai"; scan, PDF p. 727); GPT2 — section 6.3, no. 43. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-324). BR 15 (ed. 1912,
p. 1060; ed. 1960, 15.105–108, "again — suhai"). Variants: 6.1 BR "śrīduḥkhinī kṛṣṇadāsa" (so in the OCR of the 1960 ed.; GPT "duḥkhī"). Not in the
GCC, PK, KGC, PS or Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^26-12]: According to tradition, Duhkhi Krishnadasa, sweeping a grove in Vrindavana, found Sri Radha's anklet (nupura) and received Her mercy; from then
on he was called Shyamananda, and the tilaka of his line is in the form of a foot (Prema-vilasa, vilasa 12; event "Radha's nupura…"). "Duhkhi"
("sorrowful") is his former name; the poet plays on it: Shyamananda grieves at the suffering of fallen souls. Rai — Sri Radha.

## 7. Narahari — "śrī-bīrabhūmete dhāma…" (GPT1 p. 470, no. 44)
*Late layer: on the followers. Praise of the poet Jnanadasa: born in the village of Kandra in Birbhum, renounced from childhood, he received
initiation from Jahnava; in Kandra to this day a three-day festival is held in his honour at the full moon; his names are "Madana-mangala" and
"Manohara"; he went to the festival at Kheturi with Baba Aul; he is the sun among poets, equal to Chandidasa. Raga kamoda. **Attribution: not
established** — GPT only; plain Bengali tripadi; the pada speaks of events after the passing of Narahari Sarakara and of a festival held "to this
day", i.e. it was written much later (not Sarakara; possibly not Chakravarti either).*[^26-13]

শ্রীবীরভূমেতে ধাম, কাঁদড়া মাঁদড়া গ্রাম, তথায় জন্মিলা জ্ঞানদাস ।
অকুমার বৈরাগ্যেতে, রত বাল্যকাল হৈতে, দীক্ষা লৈলা জাহ্নবার পাশ ॥

*śrībīrabhūmete dhāma, kām̐daṛā mām̐daṛā grāma, tathāya janmilā jñānadāsa |*
*akumāra bairāgyete, rata bālyakāla haite, dīkṣā lailā jāhnabāra pāśa ||*

*Word for word:* śrī-bīrabhūmete dhāma — abode in Sri Birbhum; kām̐daṛā mām̐daṛā grāma — the village Kandra-Mandra; tathāya janmilā jñānadāsa — there Jnanadasa was born; akumāra bairāgyete — in renunciation from youth (unmarried); rata bālyakāla haite — devoted from childhood; dīkṣā lailā jāhnabāra pāśa — took initiation from Jahnava

**7.1.** His abode is in Sri Birbhum, the village of Kandra-Mandra: there Jnanadasa was born.
Renounced from his youth, devoted [to God] from childhood, he received initiation from Jahnava.

অদ্যাপি কাঁদড়া গ্রামে, জ্ঞানদাস কবি নামে, পূর্ণিমায় হয় মহামেলা ।
তিনদিন মহোৎসব, আসেন মহান্ত সব, হয় তাহাদের লীলাখেলা ॥

*adyāpi kām̐daṛā grāme, jñānadāsa kabi nāme, pūrṇimāya haya mahāmelā |*
*tinadina mahotsaba, āsena mahānta saba, haya tāhādera līlākhelā ||*

*Word for word:* adyāpi — to this day; kām̐daṛā grāme — in the village of Kandra; jñānadāsa kabi nāme — in the name of the poet Jnanadasa; pūrṇimāya — at the full moon; haya mahāmelā — a great fair is held; tina dina mahotsaba — three days of festival; āsena mahānta saba — all the mahantas come; haya tāhādera līlākhelā — there are their games and merriment

**7.2.** To this day in the village of Kandra, in the name of the poet Jnanadasa, a great fair is held at the full moon;
three days of festival — all the mahantas come, and there are their games and merriment.

মদনমঙ্গল নাম, রূপে গুণে অনুপাম, আর এক উপাধি মনোহর ।
খেতুরীর মহোৎসবে, জ্ঞানদাস গেলা যবে, বাবা আউল ছিল সহচর ॥

*madanamaṅgala nāma, rūpe guṇe anupāma, āra eka upādhi manohara |*
*kheturīra mahotsabe, jñānadāsa gelā yabe, bābā āula chila sahacara ||*

*Word for word:* madanamaṅgala nāma — the name "Madana-mangala"; rūpe guṇe anupāma — peerless in beauty and virtue; āra eka upādhi manohara — and another title, "Manohara"; kheturīra mahotsabe — to the great festival at Kheturi; jñānadāsa gelā yabe — when Jnanadasa went; bābā āula chila sahacara — Baba Aul was his companion

**7.3.** His name is "Madana-mangala", peerless in beauty and virtue, and another title — "Manohara";
when Jnanadasa went to the great festival at Kheturi, Baba Aul was his companion.

কবিকুলে যেন রবি, চণ্ডীদাস তুল্য কবি, জ্ঞানদাস বিদিত ভুবনে ।
যার পদ সুধাসার, যেন অমৃতের ধার, নরহরি দাস ইহা ভণে ॥

*kabikule yena rabi, caṇḍīdāsa tulya kabi, jñānadāsa bidita bhubane |*
*yāra pada sudhāsāra, yena amṛtera dhāra, narahari dāsa ihā bhaṇe ||*

*Word for word:* kabikule yena rabi — like the sun in the race of poets; caṇḍīdāsa tulya kabi — a poet equal to Chandidasa; jñānadāsa bidita bhubane — Jnanadasa is known to the world; yāra pada sudhāsāra — whose padas are the essence of nectar; yena amṛtera dhāra — like a stream of amrita; narahari dāsa ihā bhaṇe — so sings Narahari Dasa

**7.4.** He is like the sun in the race of poets, a poet equal to Chandidasa; Jnanadasa is known to the whole world.
His padas are the essence of nectar, like a stream of amrita — so sings Narahari Dasa.[^26-14]

[^26-13]: GPT1 — p. 470, no. 44 ("kamoda"; scan, PDF p. 727); GPT2 — section 6.3, no. 44. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-325). Not found in
the BR, GCC, Gita-chandrodaya, Narottama-vilasa, PK, KGC or PS. The BR (14.180) calls Kandra the village "of Sri Mangala Jnanadasa"
(śrīmaṅgala jñānadāsera ālaya) — the same title "Mangala" as in the pada. C.
[^26-14]: Jnanadasa — one of the greatest Vaishnava poets of the 16th century, a disciple of Jahnava Devi (Nityananda's consort); a participant in the great
festival at Kheturi (the Prema-vilasa, vilasa 19, names him among those who came there from Nityananda's branch). Chandidasa — a poet of the age
before Chaitanya, whose songs Mahaprabhu loved to hear (CC Madhya 2). Who "Baba Aul" is cannot be determined from the pada itself. The pada is a
praise of a poet, not Gaura-lila; included as a pada on the followers (coordinator's decision).

## 8. Narahari — "jaya jaya harirāma ācāryabarya…" (GPT1 pp. 471–472, no. 49; BR, GCC)
*Late layer: on the followers. Praise of Harirama Acharya, disciple of Ramachandra Kaviraja: his life is wondrous and steals hearts; the fame of his
victory over the Lord's opponents has spread through the world; he is ever intoxicated with Gaura's prema, greedy for the rasa of sankirtana,
skilled in serving the Vaishnavas; his exposition of the Bhagavata pours nectar; his life is the Deity Sri Krishna Raya. Raga purabi.
**Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (15th wave) and in the GCC (kirana 1).*[^26-15]

জয় জয় হরিরাম আচার্য্যবর্য্য আশ্চর্য্য চরিত চিতহারী ।
গুণগণ বিশদ বিপদমদমর্দ্দন মধুর মূরতি মুদবর্দ্ধনকারী ॥

*jaya jaya harirāma ācāryyabaryya āścaryya carita citahārī |*
*guṇagaṇa biśada bipadamadamarddana madhura mūrati mudabarddhanakārī ||*

*Word for word:* jaya jaya — glory, glory; harirāma ācārya-barya — to Harirama, best of acharyas; āścarya carita — wondrous life; citahārī — stealing hearts; guṇagaṇa biśada — pure virtues; bipada-mada-mardana — crushing the pride of calamities; madhura mūrati — sweet form; muda-bardhanakārī — increasing joy

**8.1.** Glory, glory to Harirama, best of acharyas, whose wondrous life steals hearts!
His virtues are pure, he crushes the pride of calamities, his form is sweet and increases joy.

পহুঁপদ-বিমুখ অসুর-দুর্জ্জয়-জয়কারক কীর্ত্তি জগত প্রচার ।
পরম সুধীর ধীরধৃতিহারক করুণাময় মতি অতিহুঁ উদার ॥

*pahum̐pada-bimukha asura-durjjaya-jayakāraka kīrtti jagata pracāra |*
*parama sudhīra dhīradhṛtihāraka karuṇāmaya mati atihum̐ udāra ||*

*Word for word:* pahum̐-pada-bimukha — turned away from the Lord's feet; asura-durjaya — invincible asuras; jaya-kāraka — conquering; kīrti jagata pracāra — fame spread through the world; parama sudhīra — supremely wise and firm; dhīra-dhṛti-hāraka — stealing the composure of the steady; karuṇāmaya mati — compassionate mind; atihum̐ udāra — boundlessly generous

**8.2.** The fame of his victories over the invincible asuras, turned away from the Lord's feet, has spread through the world;
he is wise and firm, he steals the firmness [of others], his mind is full of compassion, he is boundlessly generous.

অনুখন গৌরপ্রেমভরে উনমত মত্ত করীন্দ্র নিন্দি গতি জোর ।
সংকীর্ত্তনরস লম্পট পটু বৈষ্ণব-সেবা-সুখ কো কহুঁ ওর ॥

*anukhana gaurapremabhare unamata matta karīndra nindi gati jora |*
*saṃkīrttanarasa lampaṭa paṭu baiṣṇaba-sebā-sukha ko kahum̐ ora ||*

*Word for word:* anukhana — ever; gaura-prema-bhare unamata — intoxicated with the weight of Gaura's prema; matta karīndra nindi — surpassing an intoxicated king of elephants; gati jora — mighty gait; saṅkīrtana-rasa lampaṭa — greedy for the rasa of sankirtana; paṭu — skilled; baiṣṇaba-sebā — in serving the Vaishnavas; sukha ko kahum̐ ora — who can tell the bounds of his happiness

**8.3.** Ever intoxicated with the weight of Gaura's prema, he walks more mightily than an intoxicated king of elephants;
he is greedy for the rasa of sankirtana, skilled in serving the Vaishnavas — who can describe his happiness?

শ্রীমদ্ভাগবতাদিক গ্রন্থকথন অনুপম বরষত অমৃতধার ।
শ্রীশ্রীকৃষ্ণ রায় যজ্জীবন ভণব কি নরহরি মহিমা অপার ॥

*śrīmadbhāgabatādika granthakathana anupama baraṣata amṛtadhāra |*
*śrīśrīkṛṣṇa rāya yajjībana bhaṇaba ki narahari mahimā apāra ||*

*Word for word:* śrīmad-bhāgabatādika — of the Srimad-Bhagavata and others; grantha-kathana — exposition of the books; anupama — incomparable; baraṣata amṛta-dhāra — pours a stream of nectar; śrī-śrī-kṛṣṇa-rāya — Sri Sri Krishna Raya; yaj-jībana — whose life; bhaṇaba ki narahari — how can Narahari tell; mahimā apāra — the boundless greatness

**8.4.** His expositions of the Srimad-Bhagavata and other books pour an incomparable stream of nectar;
Sri Sri Krishna Raya is his very life. How can Narahari describe his boundless greatness?[^26-16]

[^26-15]: GPT1 — pp. 471–472, no. 49 ("purabi"; scan, PDF pp. 728–729); GPT2 — section 6.3, no. 49 (NG-222). BR 15 (ed. 1912, p. 1061; ed. 1960, 15.117–120;
"in song, pauravi"): "Srinivasa Acharya's dearest disciple is Ramachandra Kaviraja; Ramachandra's disciple is Harirama Acharya, whose deeds are
wondrous; distributing Sri Krishna Chaitanya's prema-bhakti he destroys the stain of souls… poets sing his life" (15.113–116), then the pada; after
it — the pada on Ramakrishna Acharya (GPT no. 72). GCC — kirana 1 (in a row of vandana-padas to the companions and followers), pada 23 (between the
padas on Ramachandra Kaviraja — GPT no. 69 — and on Ramakrishna — no. 72). Variants: 8.1 BR "śrīharirāma ācāryabarya" (with "śrī"), "madhura
murati"; 8.3 BR the same; in the OCR of the GCC the lines are distorted. Not in the PK, KGC, PS or Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^26-16]: Harirama Acharya and his brother Ramakrishna — brahmana scholars converted by Ramachandra Kaviraja and Narottama at the river Padmavati
(Prema-vilasa, vilasa 14): Harirama became Ramachandra's disciple, Ramakrishna Narottama's. "The asuras turned away from the Lord's feet" — the
opponents of bhakti, defeated in debate. "Steals the firmness" (dhīra-dhṛti-hāraka) — with his prema he robs even the steady of their composure.
Sri Krishna Raya — the Deity he served.

## 9. Narahari — "jaya jaya śrīnibāsa ācārya…" (GPT1 pp. 473–474, no. 55; BR)
*Late layer: on the followers. Praise of Srinivasa Acharya: the life of the people of the world, refuge of the fallen, his body like a champaka
flower, beloved companion of Gaurachandra; Narottama is his life; he tastes the nectar of the pastimes of the Divine Couple; Ramachandra Kaviraja
is the servant of his feet; he planted on earth a new wish-fulfilling tree of bhakti. Raga belabali. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the
pada is in the BR (14th wave, Srinivasa at Budhari).*[^26-17]

জয় জয় শ্রীনিবাস আচার্য্য জগতজন-জীবন পরম রসিক গুণধাম ।
পামর অগতি পতিত গতিদায়ক দীনবন্ধু বর চরিত ললাম ॥

*jaya jaya śrīnibāsa ācāryya jagatajana-jībana parama rasika guṇadhāma |*
*pāmara agati patita gatidāyaka dīnabandhu bara carita lalāma ||*

*Word for word:* jaya jaya — glory, glory; śrīnibāsa ācārya — to Srinivasa Acharya; jagata-jana-jībana — the life of the people of the world; parama rasika — supreme knower of rasa; guṇadhāma — abode of virtues; pāmara agati patita — the wretched, helpless, fallen; gatidāyaka — giver of refuge; dīnabandhu — friend of the lowly; bara carita lalāma — ornament of noble deeds

**9.1.** Glory, glory to Srinivasa Acharya, life of all the people of the world, supreme knower of rasa, abode of virtues!
Refuge of the wretched, the helpless and the fallen, friend of the lowly, ornament of noble deeds.

সুললিত ভাব ভূষণে অতি ভূষিত চম্পক শোণ কুসুম সম দেহ ।
নিরুপম গৌরচন্দ্র প্রিয় পরিকর যাহে হেরি হিয় না বাঁধয়ে থেহ ॥

*sulalita bhāba bhūṣaṇe ati bhūṣita campaka śoṇa kusuma sama deha |*
*nirupama gauracandra priya parikara yāhe heri hiya nā bām̐dhaye theha ||*

*Word for word:* sulalita bhāba bhūṣaṇe — with the lovely ornaments of bhavas; ati bhūṣita — beautifully adorned; campaka śoṇa kusuma sama deha — body like a champaka flower, golden-red; nirupama — peerless; gauracandra priya parikara — beloved companion of Gaurachandra; yāhe heri — seeing whom; hiya nā bām̐dhaye theha — the heart cannot hold its composure

**9.2.** He is beautifully adorned with the wondrous ornaments of bhavas, his body like a champaka flower, golden-red;
the peerless beloved companion of Gaurachandra — seeing him, the heart cannot keep its composure.

ভুবন-সুবিদিত প্রেমরস-বাদর সুখদ নরোত্তম পহুঁ যছু প্রাণ ।
নিরবধি যুগল কেলি অমিঞা পীবি মাতি বিলসে কি রচব কবি আন ॥

*bhubana-subidita premarasa-bādara sukhada narottama pahum̐ yachu prāṇa |*
*nirabadhi yugala keli amiñā pībi māti bilase ki racaba kabi āna ||*

*Word for word:* bhubana-subidita — famed in the world; prema-rasa-bādara — a cloud of the rasa of prema; sukhada narottama — blissful Narottama; pahum̐ yachu prāṇa — his master and life; nirabadhi — ceaselessly; yugala keli amiñā pībi — drinking the nectar of the Divine Couple's pastimes; māti bilase — rejoices intoxicated; ki racaba kabi āna — what more can a poet compose

**9.3.** Famed in the world, a cloud raining the rasa of prema — blissful Narottama, his master and life;
ceaselessly drinking the nectar of the Divine Couple's pastimes, he rejoices in intoxication — what more can a poet compose?

মরি মরি যাক চরণকিঙ্কর করুণাময় রামচন্দ্র কবিরাজ ।
কহব কি এ নব ভকতিকলপতরু নরহরি লাগি রোপল মহী মাঝ ॥

*mari mari yāka caraṇakiṅkara karuṇāmaya rāmacandra kabirāja |*
*kahaba ki e naba bhakatikalapataru narahari lāgi ropala mahī mājha ||*

*Word for word:* mari mari — ah, ah; yāka caraṇa-kiṅkara — the servant of whose feet; karuṇāmaya rāmacandra kabirāja — merciful Ramachandra Kaviraja; kahaba ki — what can I say; e naba bhakati-kalapataru — this new wish-fulfilling tree of bhakti; narahari lāgi — for Narahari's sake; ropala mahī mājha — planted on the earth

**9.4.** Ah, ah! — the servant of his feet is merciful Ramachandra Kaviraja.
What can I say? — this new wish-fulfilling tree of bhakti he planted on earth for Narahari's sake.[^26-18]

[^26-17]: GPT1 — pp. 473–474, no. 55 ("belabali"; scan, PDF pp. 730–731); GPT2 — section 6.3, no. 55. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-326). BR 14
(ed. 1912, pp. ≈1037–1038; ed. 1960, 14.78–81, "again — belabali"): Srinivasa with his disciples comes to the village of Budhari, Narottama comes
there from Kheturi; "all, seeing the Acharya's beauty, lose their composure — who does not sing of his form and virtues?" (14.73), then
Ghanashyama's pada (GPT no. 54), this pada and the pada on Narottama (GPT no. 61); afterwards — the festival at Boraquli. Variants: 9.1 BR "jaya
śrīnibāsa ācārya jagata-jana-jībana" (one "jaya"); 9.2 BR "campaka śoṇa kusumasama deha"; 9.4 BR "ki kahaba — ki e naba bhakatikalpataru" — same
sense. Not in the GCC, PK, KGC, PS or Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^26-18]: Srinivasa Acharya — a disciple of Gopala Bhatta Gosvami who, together with Narottama and Shyamananda, brought the Gosvamis' books from
Vrindavana to Gauda; the tradition sees in him a manifestation of Sri Chaitanya's prema (so also in the next pada, 10.1). "The pastimes of the
Divine Couple" (yugala keli) — the lila of Radha and Krishna. "For Narahari's sake" — that is, for the poet and fallen souls like him: a humble
ending. Here Narottama is called Srinivasa's "master and life" — an image of their inseparable friendship ("one life in two bodies", 12.4).

## 10. Narahari — "o mora jībana prāṇa…" (GPT1 pp. 474–475, no. 58; BR)
*Late layer: on the followers. The life of Srinivasa Acharya: learned from his youth and devoted to Chaitanya's feet; Sri Chaitanya with Nitai in
a dream bids him go to Vrindavana — through him the books of Rupa and Sanatana will be distributed; in Mathura he learns of the passing of Rupa
and Sanatana and faints; they appear to him in a dream and bid him surrender to Gopala Bhatta; Jiva receives him, Gopala Bhatta initiates him; he
meets Narottama, goes round Vraja with him and, receiving Govinda's garland of command, distributes the Gosvamis' books in Gauda. Raga kamoda.
**Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (14th wave, "the song of Srinivasa Acharya's life").*[^26-19]

ও মোর জীবন প্রাণ, পরম করুণাবান্, আচার্য্য ঠাকুর শ্রীনিবাস ।
জিনিয়া কাঞ্চনদেহ, জগতে বিদিত যেহ, শ্রীচৈতন্য প্রেমের প্রকাশ ॥

*o mora jībana prāṇa, parama karuṇābān, ācāryya ṭhākura śrīnibāsa |*
*jiniyā kāñcanadeha, jagate bidita yeha, śrīcaitanya premera prakāśa ||*

*Word for word:* o mora jībana prāṇa — O my life and soul; parama karuṇābān — supremely merciful; ācārya ṭhākura śrīnibāsa — Acharya Thakura Srinivasa; jiniyā kāñcana-deha — his body surpassing gold; jagate bidita yeha — he who is known to the world; śrī-caitanya premera prakāśa — as the manifestation of Sri Chaitanya's prema

**10.1.** O my life and soul, supremely merciful — Acharya Thakura Srinivasa!
His body surpasses gold; he is known to the world as the manifestation of Sri Chaitanya's prema.

চৈতন্যের প্রিয় যত, করে স্নেহ অবিরত, কহিতে কি জানি গুণগণ ।
অলপ বয়স হৈতে, বিদ্যায় নিপুণ চিতে, চিন্তে সদা চৈতন্যচরণ ॥

*caitanyera priya yata, kare sneha abirata, kahite ki jāni guṇagaṇa |*
*alapa bayasa haite, bidyāya nipuṇa cite, cinte sadā caitanyacaraṇa ||*

*Word for word:* caitanyera priya yata — all who are dear to Chaitanya; kare sneha abirata — love [him] ceaselessly; kahite ki jāni guṇagaṇa — how can I tell his virtues; alapa bayasa haite — from his early years; bidyāya nipuṇa — skilled in learning; cite cinte sadā — always meditated in his heart; caitanya-caraṇa — on Chaitanya's feet

**10.2.** All who are dear to Chaitanya love him ceaselessly — how can I tell his virtues?
Skilled in learning from his early years, he always meditated on Chaitanya's feet.

একদিন রাত্রিশেষে, শ্রীচৈতন্য স্নেহাবেশে, নিতাইচাঁদেরে সঙ্গে লৈয়া ।
শ্রীনিবাস পাশে আসি, স্বপ্নচ্ছলে হাসি হাসি, কহে শ্রীনিবাস মুখ চাঞা ॥

*ekadina rātriśeṣe, śrīcaitanya snehābeśe, nitāicām̐dere saṅge laiyā |*
*śrīnibāsa pāśe āsi, svapnacchale hāsi hāsi, kahe śrīnibāsa mukha cāñā ||*

*Word for word:* ekadina rātriśeṣe — one day at the end of the night; śrī-caitanya snehābeśe — Sri Chaitanya, full of love; nitāicām̐dere saṅge laiyā — taking Nitaichand with Him; śrīnibāsa pāśe āsi — coming to Srinivasa; svapnacchale — in a dream; hāsi hāsi — smiling; kahe — says; śrīnibāsa mukha cāñā — looking into Srinivasa's face

**10.3.** One day, at the end of the night, Sri Chaitanya, full of love, taking Nitaichand with Him,
came to Srinivasa and in a dream, smiling, spoke, looking into his face:

যাবে শীঘ্র বৃন্দাবন, তথা রূপ সনাতন, রচিল বিচিত্র গ্রন্থগণ ।
বিতরিব তোমা দ্বারে, এত কহি বারে বারে, নিত্যানন্দে কৈল সমর্পণ ॥

*yābe śīghra bṛndābana, tathā rūpa sanātana, racila bicitra granthagaṇa |*
*bitariba tomā dvāre, eta kahi bāre bāre, nityānande kaila samarpaṇa ||*

*Word for word:* yābe śīghra bṛndābana — go quickly to Vrindavana; tathā rūpa sanātana — there Rupa and Sanatana; racila bicitra granthagaṇa — have written wonderful books; bitariba tomā dvāre — I shall distribute through you; eta kahi bāre bāre — saying this again and again; nityānande kaila samarpaṇa — He entrusted [him] to Nityananda

**10.4.** "Go quickly to Vrindavana: there Rupa and Sanatana have written wonderful books —
through you I shall distribute them." Saying this, again and again He entrusted him to Nityananda.

হেন কালে স্বপ্নভঙ্গ, ধরিতে নারয় অঙ্গ, শ্রীনিবাস ব্যাকুল হইলা ।
নীলাচল গৌড়দেশে, ভ্রমিয়া সে প্রেমাবেশে, বৃন্দাবন গমন করিলা ॥

*hena kāle svapnabhaṅga, dharite nāraya aṅga, śrīnibāsa byākula hailā |*
*nīlācala gauṛadeśe, bhramiyā se premābeśe, bṛndābana gamana karilā ||*

*Word for word:* hena kāle — then; svapna-bhaṅga — the dream broke; dharite nāraya aṅga — could not contain himself; śrīnibāsa byākula hailā — Srinivasa was filled with longing; nīlācala gauṛadeśe — through Nilachala and Gauda; bhramiyā — wandering; se premābeśe — in the ecstasy of love; bṛndābana gamana karilā — set out for Vrindavana

**10.5.** Then the dream broke — Srinivasa could not contain himself and was filled with longing;
having wandered in the ecstasy of love through Nilachala and Gauda, he set out for Vrindavana.

কত অভিলাষ মনে, উলাসে অলপদিনে, মথুরানগরে প্রবেশিল ।
শ্রীরূপ শ্রীসনাতন, এ দুঁহার অদর্শন, শুনি তথা মূর্চ্ছিত হইল ॥

*kata abhilāṣa mane, ulāse alapadine, mathurānagare prabeśila |*
*śrīrūpa śrīsanātana, e dum̐hāra adarśana, śuni tathā mūrcchita haila ||*

*Word for word:* kata abhilāṣa mane — with great hopes in his heart; ulāse — rejoicing; alapa dine — in a few days; mathurā-nagare prabeśila — reached the city of Mathura; śrī-rūpa śrī-sanātana — Sri Rupa and Sri Sanatana; e dum̐hāra adarśana — the disappearance of these two; śuni tathā — hearing there; mūrcchita haila — fainted

**10.6.** With great hopes, rejoicing, in a few days he reached the city of Mathura;
there, hearing of the disappearance of Sri Rupa and Sri Sanatana, he fainted.

কাঁদয়ে চেতন পাঞা, কহে ভূমে লোটাইয়া, হাহা প্রভু রূপ সনাতন ।
কি লাগি বঞ্চিত কৈলা, না বুঝি এসব খেলা, কি লাগিয়া রাখিলা জীবন ॥

*kām̐daye cetana pāñā, kahe bhūme loṭāiyā, hāhā prabhu rūpa sanātana |*
*ki lāgi bañcita kailā, nā bujhi esaba khelā, ki lāgiyā rākhilā jībana ||*

*Word for word:* kām̐daye cetana pāñā — coming to, he weeps; kahe bhūme loṭāiyā — says, rolling on the ground; hāhā prabhu rūpa sanātana — alas, my masters Rupa and Sanatana; ki lāgi bañcita kailā — why did you deprive [me]; nā bujhi e saba khelā — I do not understand this play; ki lāgiyā rākhilā jībana — why did you keep me alive

**10.7.** Coming to, he weeps and, rolling on the ground, says: "Alas, alas, my masters Rupa and Sanatana!
Why have you deprived me? I do not understand this play! Why have you kept me alive?"

ঐছে খেদযুক্ত মন, জানি রূপ সনাতন, স্বপ্নচ্ছলে আসি প্রেমাবেশে ।
শ্রীনিবাস কোলে লৈয়া, নেত্রবারি নিবারিয়া, কহে অতি সুমধুর ভাষে ॥

*aiche khedayukta mana, jāni rūpa sanātana, svapnacchale āsi premābeśe |*
*śrīnibāsa kole laiyā, netrabāri nibāriyā, kahe ati sumadhura bhāṣe ||*

*Word for word:* aiche kheda-yukta mana — such a grief-stricken mind; jāni — knowing; rūpa sanātana — Rupa and Sanatana; svapnacchale āsi — coming in a dream; premābeśe — in the ecstasy of love; śrīnibāsa kole laiyā — taking Srinivasa on their laps; netrabāri nibāriyā — wiping his tears; kahe ati sumadhura bhāṣe — say in the sweetest words

**10.8.** Knowing his grief-stricken mind, Rupa and Sanatana in the ecstasy of love came to him in a dream,
took Srinivasa on their laps, wiped away his tears and said in the sweetest words:

শীঘ্র গিয়া বৃন্দাবন, কর আত্মসমর্পণ, শ্রীগোপাল ভট্টের চরণে ।
না ভাবিবে কোন দুখ, পাইবে পরম সুখ, ঐছে দেখা দিব দুই জনে ॥

*śīghra giyā bṛndābana, kara ātmasamarpaṇa, śrīgopāla bhaṭṭera caraṇe |*
*nā bhābibe kona dukha, pāibe parama sukha, aiche dekhā diba dui jane ||*

*Word for word:* śīghra giyā bṛndābana — going quickly to Vrindavana; kara ātmasamarpaṇa — surrender yourself; śrī-gopāla bhaṭṭera caraṇe — at the feet of Sri Gopala Bhatta; nā bhābibe kona dukha — do not think of any sorrow; pāibe parama sukha — you will attain the highest happiness; aiche dekhā diba dui jane — thus we two will appear

**10.9.** "Go quickly to Vrindavana and surrender at the feet of Sri Gopala Bhatta;
do not think of any sorrow — you will attain the highest happiness; thus we two will appear to you."

এত কহি অদর্শন, হৈল রূপ সনাতন, শ্রীনিবাস প্রভাতে উঠিয়া ।
প্রবেশয়ে বৃন্দাবনে, প্রেমধারা দুনয়নে, বৃন্দাবনশোভা নিরখিয়া ॥

*eta kahi adarśana, haila rūpa sanātana, śrīnibāsa prabhāte uṭhiyā |*
*prabeśaye bṛndābane, premadhārā dunayane, bṛndābanaśobhā nirakhiyā ||*

*Word for word:* eta kahi — saying this; adarśana haila — vanished; rūpa sanātana — Rupa and Sanatana; śrīnibāsa prabhāte uṭhiyā — Srinivasa, rising at dawn; prabeśaye bṛndābane — enters Vrindavana; premadhārā dunayane — streams of prema from both eyes; bṛndābana-śobhā nirakhiyā — gazing at the beauty of Vrindavana

**10.10.** Saying this, Rupa and Sanatana vanished; Srinivasa, rising at dawn,
entered Vrindavana — streams of prema from both eyes — gazing at the beauty of Vrindavana.

শ্রীজীব শ্রীশ্রীনিবাসে, পাইয়া আনন্দাবেশে, গোস্বামিগণেরে মিলাইল ।
শ্রীরূপের স্বপ্নাদেশে, অতি স্নেহে শ্রীনিবাসে, শ্রীগোপালভট্ট শিষ্য কৈল ॥

*śrījība śrīśrīnibāse, pāiyā ānandābeśe, gosvāmigaṇere milāila |*
*śrīrūpera svapnādeśe, ati snehe śrīnibāse, śrīgopālabhaṭṭa śiṣya kaila ||*

*Word for word:* śrī-jība — Sri Jiva; śrī-śrīnibāse pāiyā — having found Sri Srinivasa; ānandābeśe — in bliss; gosvāmigaṇere milāila — introduced [him] to the Gosvamis; śrī-rūpera svapnādeśe — by Sri Rupa's command in a dream; ati snehe — with great love; śrīnibāse — Srinivasa; śrī-gopāla-bhaṭṭa śiṣya kaila — Sri Gopala Bhatta made his disciple

**10.11.** Sri Jiva, having found Sri Srinivasa, in bliss introduced him to the Gosvamis;
by Sri Rupa's command in a dream, Sri Gopala Bhatta with great love made Srinivasa his disciple.

শ্রীজীব গোস্বামীর যত, স্নেহ কে কহিবে কত, করাইলা শাস্ত্রে বিচক্ষণ ।
শ্রীবাস আনন্দ মনে, প্রিয় নরোত্তম সনে, কিছু দিনে হইলা মিলন ॥

*śrījība gosvāmīra yata, sneha ke kahibe kata, karāilā śāstre bicakṣaṇa |*
*śrībāsa ānanda mane, priya narottama sane, kichu dine hailā milana ||*

*Word for word:* śrī-jība gosvāmīra yata sneha — how much Sri Jiva Gosvami loved; ke kahibe kata — who can tell; karāilā śāstre bicakṣaṇa — made [him] learned in the shastras; śrībāsa — Srinivasa (shortened); ānanda mane — joyful at heart; priya narottama sane — with dear Narottama; kichu dine hailā milana — after some days met

**10.12.** Who can tell how much Sri Jiva Gosvami loved him! He made him learned in the shastras;
and Srinivasa, joyful at heart, after some days met dear Narottama.

নরোত্তমে লৈয়া সঙ্গে, ব্রজে ভ্রমিলেন রঙ্গে, গোবিন্দের আজ্ঞামালা পাঞা ।
গোস্বামীর গ্রন্থগণ, করিলেন বিতরণ, শ্রীগৌড়মণ্ডলে স্থির হৈয়া ॥

*narottame laiyā saṅge, braje bhramilena raṅge, gobindera ājñāmālā pāñā |*
*gosvāmīra granthagaṇa, karilena bitaraṇa, śrīgauṛamaṇḍale sthira haiyā ||*

*Word for word:* narottame laiyā saṅge — taking Narottama with him; braje bhramilena raṅge — joyfully went round Vraja; gobindera ājñāmālā pāñā — receiving Govinda's garland of command; gosvāmīra granthagaṇa — the Gosvamis' books; karilena bitaraṇa — distributed; śrī-gauṛa-maṇḍale sthira haiyā — settling in Sri Gauda-mandala

**10.13.** Taking Narottama with him, he joyfully went round Vraja and, receiving Govinda's garland of command,
distributed the Gosvamis' books, settling in Sri Gauda-mandala.

গৌর প্রেমসুধাপানে, সদা মত্ত সংকীর্ত্তনে, জগতে ঘোষয়ে যশ যার ।
কহে নরহরি দীনে, উদ্ধারে আপন গুণে, এমন দয়াল নাহি আর ॥

*gaura premasudhāpāne, sadā matta saṃkīrttane, jagate ghoṣaye yaśa yāra |*
*kahe narahari dīne, uddhāre āpana guṇe, emana dayāla nāhi āra ||*

*Word for word:* gaura prema-sudhā-pāne — drinking the nectar of Gaura's prema; sadā matta saṅkīrtane — ever intoxicated with sankirtana; jagate ghoṣaye yaśa yāra — whose fame resounds in the world; kahe narahari dīne — says lowly Narahari; uddhāre āpana guṇe — he saves by his own goodness; emana dayāla nāhi āra — there is no other so merciful

**10.14.** Drinking the nectar of Gaura's prema, ever intoxicated with sankirtana, he is famed in the world.
Lowly Narahari says: "He saves [the fallen] by his own goodness — there is no one so merciful."[^26-20]

[^26-19]: GPT1 — pp. 474–475, no. 58 ("kamoda"; scan, PDF pp. 731–732); GPT2 — section 6.3, no. 58. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-327). BR 14
(ed. 1912, pp. ≈1048–1049; ed. 1960, 14.195–208, "the song of the life of Sri Srinivasa Acharya — in song, kamoda"): after the festival at Boraquli,
Srinivasa with his disciples at Yajigrama spends his days in discussing the shastras and in sankirtana; "who does not sing of the Acharya's life?"
(14.194), then this pada and Govindadasa's pada (GPT no. 57). Variants: 10.4 in the OCR of BR-1960 the stanza is longer ("parama karuṇābān",
"śrīnibāse kole laiyā" — probably an OCR fault: these words come from 10.1 and 10.8); 10.12 BR "śrībāsa ānandamane … kichu dine haila milana"; the
rest orthographic. Not in the GCC, PK, KGC, PS or Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^26-20]: The pada retells the beginning of Srinivasa's life just as the prose account of the BR and the Prema-vilasa do (the appearance of Rupa and
Sanatana in a dream — vilasa 6): the dream in which Mahaprabhu entrusts Srinivasa to Nityananda and sends him to Vrindavana; the news of Rupa's and
Sanatana's passing in Mathura; their appearance in a dream; initiation from Gopala Bhatta; study under Jiva; the meeting with Narottama; the garland
from the Deity Govinda as the command to take the books to Gauda. "Srinivasa" in 10.12 is called "śrībāsa" — a shortening of the name for the metre
(not Srivasa Pandita). A dream in which the Lord and His associates appear is not a play of imagination but their mercy (svapna-darshana).

## 11. Narahari — "jaya jaya śrīnarottama parama udāra…" (GPT1 p. 476, no. 61; BR)
*Late layer: on the followers. The form of Narottama: he delights the world, shines like a golden lotus, as if ceaselessly pouring nectar; his body
thrills, a smile is on his face, his eyes are full of compassion, his speech enchants; tilaka, tulasi-mala, blue garments; his cool, tender feet
shine in the poet's heart. Raga belabali. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (14th wave, Budhari).*[^26-21]

জয় জয় শ্রীনরোত্তম পরম উদার ।
জগজনরঞ্জন কনক কঞ্জরুচি জনু মকরন্দ বরিখে অনিবার ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*jaya jaya śrīnarottama parama udāra |*
*jagajanarañjana kanaka kañjaruci janu makaranda barikhe anibāra || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* jaya jaya — glory, glory; śrī-narottama — to Sri Narottama; parama udāra — boundlessly generous; jaga-jana-rañjana — delighting the people of the world; kanaka-kañja-ruci — shining like a golden lotus; janu — as if; makaranda barikhe anibāra — ceaselessly pouring nectar

**11.1.** Glory, glory to Sri Narottama, boundlessly generous!
He delights the people of the world, shines like a golden lotus — as if ceaselessly pouring nectar.

ঝলমল বিপুল পুলক কুল মণ্ডিত নিরুপম বদনে নিরত মৃদু হাস ।
টলমল নয়ন করুণ রসরঞ্জিত হরই শ্রবণ মন বচন বিলাস ॥

*jhalamala bipula pulaka kula maṇḍita nirupama badane nirata mṛdu hāsa |*
*ṭalamala nayana karuṇa rasarañjita harai śrabaṇa mana bacana bilāsa ||*

*Word for word:* jhalamala — gleaming; bipula pulaka-kula maṇḍita — adorned with an abundant thrill of hairs; nirupama badane — on the peerless face; nirata mṛdu hāsa — an unfailing gentle smile; ṭalamala nayana — quivering eyes; karuṇa-rasa-rañjita — tinged with the rasa of compassion; haraī śrabaṇa mana — steals ear and mind; bacana-bilāsa — the play of speech

**11.2.** An abundant thrill of the hairs gleams, on his peerless face — an unfailing gentle smile;
his eyes quiver, tinged with the rasa of compassion; the play of his speech steals ear and mind.

নিরুপম তিলক ললাট মধুরতর তুলসী মাল কুলকণ্ঠ উজোর ।
সুবলনি বাহু ললিত কর পল্লব পরিসর উর উপমা নহ থোর ॥

*nirupama tilaka lalāṭa madhuratara tulasī māla kulakaṇṭha ujora |*
*subalani bāhu lalita kara pallaba parisara ura upamā naha thora ||*

*Word for word:* nirupama tilaka — peerless tilaka; lalāṭa madhuratara — most charming brow; tulasī māla kula — necklaces of tulasi; kaṇṭha ujora — the neck shines; subalani bāhu — beautifully formed arms; lalita kara pallava — tender hand-shoots; parisara ura — broad chest; upamā naha thora — no comparison for it

**11.3.** A peerless tilaka on a most charming brow, his neck shines with a necklace of tulasi;
his arms are beautifully formed, his hands tender shoots, his broad chest — there is no comparison for it.

কটিতট ক্ষীণ নীল নব অম্বর পীন প্রবর উরু গঢ়ল সুঠার ।
কোমল চরণ যুগল অতি শীতল বিলসত নরহরি হৃদয় মাঝার ॥

*kaṭitaṭa kṣīṇa nīla naba ambara pīna prabara uru gaṛhala suṭhāra |*
*komala caraṇa yugala ati śītala bilasata narahari hṛdaya mājhāra ||*

*Word for word:* kaṭitaṭa kṣīṇa — slender waist; nīla naba ambara — new blue garments; pīna prabara uru — full strong thighs; gaṛhala suṭhāra — beautifully sculpted; komala caraṇa yugala — both tender feet; ati śītala — most cool; bilasata — shine; narahari hṛdaya mājhāra — in Narahari's heart

**11.4.** A slender waist, new blue garments, full strong thighs as if sculpted;
his tender feet, both most cool, shine in Narahari's heart.[^26-22]

[^26-21]: GPT1 — p. 476, no. 61 ("belabali"; scan, PDF p. 733); GPT2 — section 6.3, no. 61. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-328). BR 14 (ed. 1912,
p. ≈1038; ed. 1960, 14.83–86, "in song, belabali"): at Budhari "the beauty of Sri Narottama intoxicates all; who does not sing of his form and
virtues?" (14.82), then this pada; after it — "the circle of Vaishnavas is beautiful, the radiance of all is like the sun" and the departure for
Boraquli (14.87–89). Variants: 11.4 BR "pīna prabara uru gaṛhala sāra" (GPT "suṭhāra"); the rest orthographic. Not in the GCC, PK, KGC, PS or
Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^26-22]: Narottama Dasa Thakura (Thakura Mahashaya) — son of Raja Krishnananda Datta of Kheturi, a disciple of Lokanatha Gosvami, author of the
Prema-bhakti-candrika and the Prarthana, a great kirtaniya. The description of the form "from head to foot" (nakha-shikha) is a usual genre of songs
about saints; here it is contemplation of a Vaishnava's form, not worldly admiration. "Shine in the heart" — the poet meditates on Narottama's feet as
his refuge.

## 12. Narahari — "o mora karuṇāmaya, śrīṭhākura mahāśaya…" (GPT1 pp. 476–477, no. 62; BR)
*Late layer: on the followers. The life of Narottama: young, he left royal pleasures and went to Vraja, received initiation from Lokanatha, became
friends with Srinivasa — "one life in two bodies"; returning to Gauda, he visited Navadvipa and Nilachala; at Kheturi he serves six Deities; in his
sankirtana the fortunate saw Gaurachandra dancing with Advaita, Nityananda and the companions; the poet longs to roll in the dust in tears with
Narottama's name. Raga kamoda. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (14th wave, "the song of Narottama's life").*[^26-23]

ও মোর করুণাময়, শ্রীঠাকুর মহাশয়, নরোত্তম প্রেমের মূরতি ।
কিবা সে কোমল তনু, শিরীষ কুসুম জনু, জিনিয়া কনক দেহজ্যোতি ॥

*o mora karuṇāmaya, śrīṭhākura mahāśaya, narottama premera mūrati |*
*kibā se komala tanu, śirīṣa kusuma janu, jiniyā kanaka dehajyoti ||*

*Word for word:* o mora karuṇāmaya — O my merciful; śrī-ṭhākura mahāśaya — Sri Thakura Mahashaya; narottama — Narottama; premera mūrati — embodiment of prema; kibā se komala tanu — how tender his body; śirīṣa kusuma janu — like a shirisha flower; jiniyā kanaka — surpassing gold; deha-jyoti — the radiance of his body

**12.1.** O my merciful Sri Thakura Mahashaya, Narottama — embodiment of prema!
How tender his body — like a shirisha flower; its radiance surpasses gold.

অল্প বয়স তায়, কোন সুখ নাহি ভায়, গোরাগুণ শুনি সদা ঝুরে ।
রাজ্যভোগ তেয়াগিয়া, অতি লালায়িত হৈয়া, গমন করিলা ব্রজপুরে ॥

*alpa bayasa tāya, kona sukha nāhi bhāya, gorāguṇa śuni sadā jhure |*
*rājyabhoga teyāgiyā, ati lālāyita haiyā, gamana karilā brajapure ||*

*Word for word:* alpa bayasa tāya — even in his youth; kona sukha nāhi bhāya — no pleasure pleased him; gorā-guṇa śuni — hearing Gora's qualities; sadā jhure — always weeps; rājya-bhoga teyāgiyā — abandoning royal enjoyments; ati lālāyita haiyā — filled with ardent longing; gamana karilā brajapure — went to Vraja

**12.2.** Even in his youth no pleasures pleased him: hearing of Gora's qualities he always wept;
abandoning royal enjoyments, filled with ardent longing, he went to Vraja.

প্রবেশিয়া বৃন্দাবনে, পরম আনন্দমনে, লোকনাথে আত্ম সমর্পিল ।
কৃপা করি লোকনাথ, করিলেন আত্মসাথ, রাধাকৃষ্ণ মন্ত্রদীক্ষা দিল ॥

*prabeśiyā bṛndābane, parama ānandamane, lokanāthe ātma samarpila |*
*kṛpā kari lokanātha, karilena ātmasātha, rādhākṛṣṇa mantradīkṣā dila ||*

*Word for word:* prabeśiyā bṛndābane — entering Vrindavana; parama ānanda-mane — with great joy in his heart; lokanāthe ātma samarpila — surrendered to Lokanatha; kṛpā kari lokanātha — Lokanatha, in mercy; karilena ātmasātha — accepted him as his own; rādhā-kṛṣṇa mantra-dīkṣā dila — gave initiation into the mantra of Radha and Krishna

**12.3.** Entering Vrindavana, with great joy in his heart, he surrendered to Lokanatha;
Lokanatha in his mercy accepted him as his own and gave him initiation into the mantra of Radha and Krishna.

নরোত্তম-চেষ্টা দেখি, বৃন্দাবনে সবে সুখী, প্রাণের সমান করে স্নেহ ।
শ্রীনিবাসাচার্য্য সনে, যে মর্ম্ম তা কেবা জানে, প্রাণ এক ভিন্নমাত্র দেহ ॥

*narottama-ceṣṭā dekhi, bṛndābane sabe sukhī, prāṇera samāna kare sneha |*
*śrīnibāsācāryya sane, ye marmma tā kebā jāne, prāṇa eka bhinnamātra deha ||*

*Word for word:* narottama-ceṣṭā dekhi — seeing Narottama's endeavours; bṛndābane sabe sukhī — all in Vrindavana rejoice; prāṇera samāna kare sneha — love him as their life; śrīnibāsācārya sane — with Srinivasa Acharya; ye marma — what intimacy of heart; tā kebā jāne — who knows; prāṇa eka — one life; bhinna-mātra deha — only the bodies differ

**12.4.** Seeing Narottama's endeavours, all in Vrindavana rejoiced and loved him as their own life;
what was in his heart with Srinivasa Acharya — who knows? One life — only the bodies are different.

শ্রীরাধাবিনোদ দেখি, সদায় জুড়ায় আঁখি, প্রভু লোকনাথ-সেবারত ।
ভক্তিশাস্ত্র-অধ্যয়নে, মহানন্দ বাড়ে মনে, পূর্ণ হৈল অভিলাষ যত ॥

*śrīrādhābinoda dekhi, sadāya juṛāya ām̐khi, prabhu lokanātha-sebārata |*
*bhaktiśāstra-adhyayane, mahānanda bāṛe mane, pūrṇa haila abhilāṣa yata ||*

*Word for word:* śrī-rādhābinoda dekhi — beholding Sri Radha-Vinoda; sadāya juṛāya ām̐khi — always delights his eyes; prabhu lokanātha-sebā-rata — devoted to the service of his master Lokanatha; bhakti-śāstra-adhyayane — in studying the books on bhakti; mahānanda bāṛe mane — great joy grows in his heart; pūrṇa haila abhilāṣa yata — all his desires were fulfilled

**12.5.** Beholding Sri Radha-Vinoda, he always delighted his eyes, devoted to the service of his master Lokanatha;
in studying the books on bhakti his joy grew, and all his desires were fulfilled.

প্রভু অনুমতি মতে, শ্রীব্রজমণ্ডল হৈতে, শ্রীগৌড়মণ্ডলে প্রবেশিলা ।
প্রভু অনুগ্রহ বলে, নবদ্বীপ নীলাচলে, ভক্তগৃহে ভ্রমণ করিলা ॥

*prabhu anumati mate, śrībrajamaṇḍala haite, śrīgauṛamaṇḍale prabeśilā |*
*prabhu anugraha bale, nabadvīpa nīlācale, bhaktagṛhe bhramaṇa karilā ||*

*Word for word:* prabhu anumati mate — with his master's permission; śrī-brajamaṇḍala haite — from Sri Vraja-mandala; śrī-gauṛamaṇḍale prabeśilā — came to Sri Gauda-mandala; prabhu anugraha bale — by the power of his master's mercy; nabadvīpa nīlācale — in Navadvipa and Nilachala; bhakta-gṛhe bhramaṇa karilā — visited the homes of devotees

**12.6.** With his master's permission he came from Sri Vraja-mandala to Sri Gauda-mandala;
by the power of his master's mercy he visited the homes of devotees in Navadvipa and Nilachala.

কিবা সে মধুর রীতি, খেতুরী গ্রামেতে স্থিতি, সেবে গৌর শ্রীরাধারমণে ।
শ্রীবল্লভীকান্ত নাম, রাধাকান্ত রসধাম, রাধাকৃষ্ণ শ্রীব্রজমোহনে ॥

*kibā se madhura rīti, kheturī grāmete sthiti, sebe gaura śrīrādhāramaṇe |*
*śrīballabhīkānta nāma, rādhākānta rasadhāma, rādhākṛṣṇa śrībrajamohane ||*

*Word for word:* kibā se madhura rīti — how sweet his way; kheturī grāmete sthiti — living in the village of Kheturi; sebe gaura — serves Gaura; śrī-rādhāramaṇe — Sri Radha-Ramana; śrī-ballabhīkānta nāma — the one named Sri Vallavikanta; rādhākānta rasadhāma — Radha-Kanta, the abode of rasa; rādhākṛṣṇa — Radha-Krishna; śrī-brajamohane — Sri Vraja-Mohana

**12.7.** How sweet is his way: living in the village of Kheturi, he serves Gaura and Sri Radha-Ramana,
the one named Sri Vallavikanta, Radha-Kanta — the abode of rasa, Radha-Krishna and Sri Vraja-Mohana.

এ ছয় বিগ্রহ যেন, সাক্ষাত বিহরে হেন, শোভা দেখি কেবা নাহি ভুলে ।
প্রিয় রামচন্দ্র সঙ্গে, নরোত্তম মহারঙ্গে, ভাসে প্রেমরসের হিল্লোলে ॥

*e chaya bigraha yena, sākṣāta bihare hena, śobhā dekhi kebā nāhi bhule |*
*priya rāmacandra saṅge, narottama mahāraṅge, bhāse premarasera hillole ||*

*Word for word:* e chaya bigraha — these six Deities; yena sākṣāta bihare hena — as if sporting visibly; śobhā dekhi — seeing the beauty; kebā nāhi bhule — who would not lose himself; priya rāmacandra saṅge — with dear Ramachandra; narottama mahāraṅge — Narottama in great joy; bhāse prema-rasera hillole — floats on the waves of the rasa of prema

**12.8.** These six Deities seem to sport there visibly — who, seeing their beauty, would not lose himself?
With dear Ramachandra, Narottama in great joy floats on the waves of the rasa of prema.

নরোত্তম গুণ যত, কে তাহা কহিবে কত, প্রেমবৃষ্টি যার সংকীর্ত্তনে ।
শ্রীঅদ্বৈত নিত্যানন্দ, গণ সহ গৌরচন্দ্র, নাচয়ে দেখিল ভাগ্যবানে ॥

*narottama guṇa yata, ke tāhā kahibe kata, premabṛṣṭi yāra saṃkīrttane |*
*śrīadvaita nityānanda, gaṇa saha gauracandra, nācaye dekhila bhāgyabāne ||*

*Word for word:* narottama guṇa yata — all Narottama's virtues; ke tāhā kahibe kata — who can tell; prema-bṛṣṭi yāra saṅkīrtane — in whose sankirtana rains prema; śrī-advaita nityānanda — Sri Advaita and Nityananda; gaṇa saha gauracandra — Gaurachandra with the companions; nācaye — dance; dekhila bhāgyabāne — the fortunate saw

**12.9.** Who can tell all the virtues of Narottama, whose sankirtana rained down prema?
The fortunate saw Sri Advaita, Nityananda and Gaurachandra with the companions dancing in it.

গৌরগণ প্রিয় অতি, নরোত্তম মহামতি, বৈষ্ণবসেবনে যার ধ্বনি ।
কি অদ্ভুত দয়াবান, কারে বা না করে দান, নির্ম্মল ভকতি চিন্তামণি ॥

*gauragaṇa priya ati, narottama mahāmati, baiṣṇabasebane yāra dhvani |*
*ki adbhuta dayābāna, kāre bā nā kare dāna, nirmmala bhakati cintāmaṇi ||*

*Word for word:* gauragaṇa priya ati — exceedingly dear to Gaura's companions; narottama mahāmati — great-minded Narottama; baiṣṇaba-sebane yāra dhvani — whose fame is in serving the Vaishnavas; ki adbhuta dayābān — how wondrously merciful; kāre vā nā kare dāna — to whom does he not give; nirmala bhakati cintāmaṇi — pure bhakti, the chintamani gem

**12.10.** Exceedingly dear to Gaura's companions, great-minded Narottama — the fame of his service to the Vaishnavas resounds;
how wondrously merciful he is — to whom does he not give pure bhakti, the chintamani gem!

পাষণ্ডী অসুরগণে, মাতাইলা গোরাগুণে, বিহ্বল হইয়া প্রেমাবেশে ।
অলৌকিক ক্রিয়া যার, হেন কি হইবে আর, সে না যশ ঘোষে দেশে দেশে ॥

*pāṣaṇḍī asuragaṇe, mātāilā gorāguṇe, bihvala haiyā premābeśe |*
*alaukika kriyā yāra, hena ki haibe āra, se nā yaśa ghoṣe deśe deśe ||*

*Word for word:* pāṣaṇḍī asura-gaṇe — the godless and the asuras; mātāilā gorā-guṇe — he intoxicated with Gora's qualities; bihvala haiyā premābeśe — himself overwhelmed in the ecstasy of love; alaukika kriyā yāra — whose deeds are not of this world; hena ki haibe āra — will there be another such; se nā yaśa ghoṣe deśe deśe — does not his fame resound everywhere

**12.11.** The godless and the asuras he intoxicated with Gora's qualities, he himself overwhelmed in the ecstasy of love;
