his deeds are not of this world — will there be another such? Where does his fame not resound!

কহে নরহরি হীন, হবে কি এমন দিন, নরোত্তম পদে বিকাইব ।
সঘনে দুবাহু তুলি, প্রভু নরোত্তম বলি, কাঁদিয়া ধূলায় লোটাইব ॥

*kahe narahari hīna, habe ki emana dina, narottama pade bikāiba |*
*saghane dubāhu tuli, prabhu narottama bali, kām̐diyā dhūlāya loṭāiba ||*

*Word for word:* kahe narahari hīna — says worthless Narahari; habe ki emana dina — will such a day come; narottama pade bikāiba — I will sell myself at Narottama's feet; saghane dubāhu tuli — again and again raising both arms; prabhu narottama bali — crying "Master Narottama"; kām̐diyā dhūlāya loṭāiba — weeping, I will roll in the dust

**12.12.** Worthless Narahari says: "Will such a day come when I sell myself at Narottama's feet
and, again and again raising both arms, crying 'Master Narottama!', roll weeping in the dust?"[^26-24]

[^26-23]: GPT1 — pp. 476–477, no. 62 ("kamoda"; scan, PDF pp. 733–734); GPT2 — section 6.3, no. 62. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-329). BR 14
(ed. 1912, pp. ≈1050–1051; ed. 1960, 14.215–226, "the song of the life of Sri Thakura Mahashaya — in song, kamoda"): after the songs on Srinivasa's life
— "Thakura Mahashaya, dear to the Acharya — who does not sing of his life full of prema?" (14.214); after the pada — Ghanashyama's pada (GPT no. 63) and
the end of the wave. Variants: 12.2 BR "ati lālasita haiyā"; 12.10 BR "baiṣṇabasebane yā'ra dhvani"; the rest orthographic. Not in the GCC, PK, KGC,
PS or Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^26-24]: The pada retells Narottama's life as the Prema-vilasa and the BR do: leaving home for Vrindavana, secret service to Lokanatha and initiation,
friendship with Srinivasa, the return, the pilgrimage to Navadvipa and Puri, the six Deities of Kheturi (Gauranga, Vallavikanta, Vraja-Mohana,
Radha-Kanta, Radha-Ramana and Sri Krishna — in the poet "Radha-Krishna"), the great festival at Kheturi, where Mahaprabhu with His associates appeared
in the kirtana (Prema-vilasa, vilasa 19). Sri Radha-Vinoda (12.5) — Lokanatha Gosvami's Deity in Vrindavana. The Lord's appearance in Narottama's
kirtana is not an imagined vision: the Lord eternally abides in the sankirtana of His pure devotees.

## 13. Narahari — "rāmacandra kabirāja…" (GPT1 p. 479, no. 68)
*Late layer: on the followers. Govinda Kaviraja: younger brother of Ramachandra Kaviraja, son of Chiranjiva Sena, disciple of Srinivasa, a poet;
the brothers were born in Teliya-Budhari in a family of great Shaktas but, leaving the faith of their fathers, became Vaishnavas: during Govinda's
grave illness Katyayani bade him from the sky to worship Govinda's feet; his maternal grandfather was the poet Damodara of Shrikhanda; from him
Govinda inherited his poetic gift. Raga mangala. **Attribution: not established** — GPT only; plain Bengali tripadi; about events after the passing
of Narahari Sarakara (not Sarakara).*[^26-25]

রামচন্দ্র কবিরাজ, বিখ্যাত ধরণী মাঝ, তাহার কনিষ্ঠ শ্রীগোবিন্দ ।
চিরঞ্জীবসেন-সুত, কবিরাজ নামে খ্যাত, শ্রীনিবাস শিষ্য কবিচন্দ ॥

*rāmacandra kabirāja, bikhyāta dharaṇī mājha, tāhāra kaniṣṭha śrīgobinda |*
*cirañjībasena-suta, kabirāja nāme khyāta, śrīnibāsa śiṣya kabicanda ||*

*Word for word:* rāmacandra kabirāja — Ramachandra Kaviraja; bikhyāta dharaṇī mājha — famed on earth; tāhāra kaniṣṭha śrīgobinda — his younger brother is Sri Govinda; cirañjībasena-suta — son of Chiranjiva Sena; kabirāja nāme khyāta — known by the name "Kaviraja"; śrīnibāsa śiṣya — disciple of Srinivasa; kabicanda — a moon among poets

**13.1.** Ramachandra Kaviraja is famed on earth; his younger brother is Sri Govinda,
son of Chiranjiva Sena, known by the name "Kaviraja", disciple of Srinivasa, a moon among poets.

তেলিয়াবুধরি গ্রামে, জন্মিলেন শুভক্ষণে, মহাশাক্তবংশে দুই ভাই ।
পরে পিতৃধর্ম্মত্যাগী, ঘোরতর পীড়া লাগি, বৈষ্ণব হইলা দোঁহে তাই ॥

*teliyābudhari grāme, janmilena śubhakṣaṇe, mahāśāktabaṃśe dui bhāi |*
*pare pitṛdharmmatyāgī, ghoratara pīṛā lāgi, baiṣṇaba hailā dom̐he tāi ||*

*Word for word:* teliyābudhari grāme — in the village of Teliya-Budhari; janmilena śubhakṣaṇe — were born at an auspicious moment; mahāśākta-baṁśe — in a family of great Shaktas; dui bhāi — two brothers; pare — later; pitṛdharma-tyāgī — leaving the faith of their fathers; ghoratara pīṛā lāgi — because of a grave illness; baiṣṇaba hailā dom̐he tāi — both became Vaishnavas

**13.2.** In the village of Teliya-Budhari, at an auspicious moment, the two brothers were born in a family of great Shaktas;
later, leaving the faith of their fathers because of a grave illness, both became Vaishnavas.

হইল আকাশবাণী, কহিলেন কাত্যায়নী, গোবিন্দ গোবিন্দপদ ভজ ।
বিপত্তে মধুসূদন, বিনে নাহি অন্য জন, সার কর তাঁর পদরজ ॥

*haila ākāśabāṇī, kahilena kātyāyanī, gobinda gobindapada bhaja |*
*bipatte madhusūdana, bine nāhi anya jana, sāra kara tām̐ra padaraja ||*

*Word for word:* haila ākāśabāṇī — a voice resounded from the sky; kahilena kātyāyanī — Katyayani said; gobinda — Govinda; gobinda-pada bhaja — worship Govinda's feet; bipatte — in calamity; madhusūdana bine — but for Madhusudana; nāhi anya jana — there is no one; sāra kara — make your essence; tām̐ra pada-raja — the dust of His feet

**13.3.** A voice resounded from the sky — Katyayani said: "Govinda, worship the feet of Govinda!
In calamity there is no one but Madhusudana: make the dust of His feet your essence."

শ্রীখণ্ডের দামোদর, কবিকুলে শ্রেষ্ঠতর, গোবিন্দের হন মাতামহ ।
সুরগুরু সঙ্গে যার, তুলনায় বারে বার, লোকে যশ গায় অহরহ ॥

*śrīkhaṇḍera dāmodara, kabikule śreṣṭhatara, gobindera hana mātāmaha |*
*suraguru saṅge yāra, tulanāya bāre bāra, loke yaśa gāya aharaha ||*

*Word for word:* śrīkhaṇḍera dāmodara — Damodara of Shrikhanda; kabikule śreṣṭhatara — best in the race of poets; gobindera hana mātāmaha — is Govinda's maternal grandfather; suraguru saṅge yāra — with the preceptor of the gods, whose; tulanāya bāre bāra — comparison again and again; loke yaśa gāya aharaha — people sing his fame ceaselessly

**13.4.** Damodara of Shrikhanda, the best in the race of poets, is Govinda's maternal grandfather;
again and again even the preceptor of the gods is compared with him, and people ceaselessly sing his fame.

বুঝি মাতামহ হৈতে, কবিকীর্ত্তি বিধিমতে, পাইলা গোবিন্দ কবিরাজ ।
কহে দীন নরহরি, তাই ধন্য ধন্য করি, গায় গুণ পণ্ডিতসমাজ ॥

*bujhi mātāmaha haite, kabikīrtti bidhimate, pāilā gobinda kabirāja |*
*kahe dīna narahari, tāi dhanya dhanya kari, gāya guṇa paṇḍitasamāja ||*

*Word for word:* bujhi — evidently; mātāmaha haite — from his maternal grandfather; kabikīrti — poetic fame; bidhimate — duly; pāilā gobinda kabirāja — Govinda Kaviraja obtained; kahe dīna narahari — says lowly Narahari; tāi — therefore; dhanya dhanya kari — crying "blessed, blessed"; gāya guṇa paṇḍita-samāja — the assembly of pandits sings [his] virtues

**13.5.** Evidently from his maternal grandfather Govinda Kaviraja duly obtained his poetic fame.
Lowly Narahari says: therefore the assembly of pandits, crying "Blessed, blessed!", sings his virtues.[^26-26]

[^26-25]: GPT1 — p. 479, no. 68 ("mangala"; scan, PDF p. 736); GPT2 — section 6.3, no. 68 (NG-223: the catalogue, from the OCR of GPT2, gave as the first
line a fragment "…ṭabaṣjara hā phoche bhāi" — line 13.2; the first line is "rāmacandra kabirāja bikhyāta dharaṇī mājha"). Not found in the BR, GCC,
Gita-chandrodaya, Narottama-vilasa, PK, KGC or PS. In GPT1 an editor's note with quotations from other books stands under the pada (not reproduced). C.
[^26-26]: Govinda Kaviraja (Govindadasa) — one of the greatest pada-poets, younger brother of Ramachandra Kaviraja; both were disciples of Srinivasa
Acharya (Prema-vilasa, vilasa 14: the Goddess bids Govinda remember Govinda). **Fidelity to the author:** the pada calls the brothers' family "a family
of great Shaktas" and their conversion "leaving the faith of their fathers"; yet their father Chiranjiva Sena of Khanda was an associate of
Mahaprabhu — the Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika (209) calls Chiranjiva and Sulochana of Khanda exalted by association with Narahari, with Gauranga as their
only refuge. What the author means the pada does not explain; the translation renders the text as it stands. Katyayani (Durga) here is a maidservant
of the Lord who directs to Him (cf. Brahma-samhita 5.44: Durga is the energy carrying out the Lord's will); bhakti is not worship of her but surrender
to Govinda's feet, which she herself enjoins. "The preceptor of the gods" (suraguru) — Brihaspati: Damodara is compared with him in learning and
poetry.

## 14. Narahari — "jaya jaya rāmacandra kabirāja…" (GPT1 pp. 479–480, no. 69; GCC)
*Late layer: on the followers. Praise of Ramachandra Kaviraja and of Srinivasa Acharya's circle: Ramachandra is always absorbed in the Name,
immersed in serving Srinivasa's feet, inseparable from Narottama; then the poet praises other disciples and associates of the Acharya — Govinda
Kaviraja, Karnapura, Nrisimha, Bhagavan, Gokula, Vallavikanta, Gopiramana, Shyamadasa Chakravarti, Ramacharana, Vyasa, Govinda, Shridasa, Gokula
Chakravarti, Rupa Ghataka, Radhavallabha Mandala and King Vira Hambira — and asks to be kept at their feet as a servant. Raga pathamanjari.
**Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC (kirana 1); Vrajabuli.*[^26-27]

জয় জয় রামচন্দ্র কবিরাজ ।
সুললিত রীত নামরত নিরবধি মগন আনন্দ মহোদধি মাঝ ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*jaya jaya rāmacandra kabirāja |*
*sulalita rīta nāmarata nirabadhi magana ānanda mahodadhi mājha || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* jaya jaya — glory, glory; rāmacandra kabirāja — to Ramachandra Kaviraja; sulalita rīta — beautiful way; nāma-rata nirabadhi — ceaselessly devoted to the Name; magana — immersed; ānanda mahodadhi mājha — in an ocean of great bliss

**14.1.** Glory, glory to Ramachandra Kaviraja!
Beautiful is his way, ceaselessly devoted to the Name, immersed in an ocean of great bliss.

শ্রীশ্রীনিবাস আচার্য্যবর্য্য-যুগচরণ-কঞ্জরজ-ভজন বিভোর ।
তছু গুণ চরিত অমৃত নিত পান সুপ্রেম অতুল তুলনা নহু থোর ॥

*śrīśrīnibāsa ācāryyabaryya-yugacaraṇa-kañjaraja-bhajana bibhora |*
*tachu guṇa carita amṛta nita pāna suprema atula tulanā nahu thora ||*

*Word for word:* śrī-śrīnibāsa ācāryabarya — of Sri Srinivasa, best of acharyas; yuga-caraṇa-kañja-raja — the dust of both lotus feet; bhajana bibhora — absorbed in serving; tachu guṇa carita amṛta — the nectar of his virtues and life; nita pāna — always drinks; suprema atula — peerless prema; tulanā nahu thora — not the least comparison

**14.2.** He is absorbed in serving the dust of the lotus feet of Sri Sri Srinivasa, best of acharyas;
ceaselessly he drinks the nectar of his virtues and life — peerless is his prema, there is not the least comparison for it.

রসময় শ্রীমদ্ভাগবতাদিক গ্রন্থ পঠন অনুভব নহ মর্ম্ম ।
শ্রীল নরোত্তম সঙ্গ সতত অতি প্রীতি বিদিত অদভুত সব কর্ম্ম ॥

*rasamaya śrīmadbhāgabatādika grantha paṭhana anubhaba naha marmma |*
*śrīla narottama saṅga satata ati prīti bidita adabhuta saba karmma ||*

*Word for word:* rasamaya — full of rasa; śrīmad-bhāgabatādika grantha — the Srimad-Bhagavata and other books; paṭhana — reading; anubhaba naha marma — the depth of realization not fathomable; śrīla narottama saṅga — the company of Srila Narottama; satata ati prīti — unfailing great friendship; bidita — known; adabhuta saba karma — all deeds wondrous

**14.3.** He reads the Srimad-Bhagavata and other books full of rasa — the depth of his realization cannot be fathomed;
unfailing is his friendship with Srila Narottama, known to all, and wondrous are all his deeds.

শ্রীগোবিন্দ কবীন্দ্র কৃপানিধি ধীর মহামন গৌরচরিত্র ।
নির্ম্মল প্রেমপ্রচার চারু গুণ যাক কার্য্য করু ভুবন পবিত্র ॥

*śrīgobinda kabīndra kṛpānidhi dhīra mahāmana gauracaritra |*
*nirmmala premapracāra cāru guṇa yāka kāryya karu bhubana pabitra ||*

*Word for word:* śrīgobinda kabīndra — Sri Govinda, king of poets; kṛpānidhi — ocean of mercy; dhīra — steady; mahāmana — great-souled; gaura-caritra — [who sang] Gaura's life; nirmala prema-pracāra — preaching of pure prema; cāru guṇa — beautiful virtue; yāka kārya — whose work; karu bhubana pabitra — purifies the world

**14.4.** Sri Govinda, king of poets, ocean of mercy, steady, great-souled, [who sang] the life of Gaura,
whose work — the beautiful preaching of pure prema — purifies the world;

কর্ণপুর পরিপূর্ণ প্রেমরস রসিক অনন্য হরষ দিন রাতি ।
সুঘড় নৃসিংহ সিংহ সম বিক্রম ভাব প্রবল অবিরত বহু মাতি ॥

*karṇapura paripūrṇa premarasa rasika ananya haraṣa dina rāti |*
*sughaṛa nṛsiṃha siṃha sama bikrama bhāba prabala abirata bahu māti ||*

*Word for word:* karṇapura — Karnapura; paripūrṇa prema-rasa — filled with the rasa of prema; rasika — knower of rasa; ananya haraṣa dina rāti — day and night in joy alone; sughaṛa nṛsiṃha — graceful Nrisimha; siṃha sama bikrama — in might like a lion; bhāba prabala — with intense bhava; abirata bahu māti — ceaselessly intoxicated

**14.5.** Karnapura, filled with the rasa of prema, a knower of rasa, day and night filled with joy alone;
graceful Nrisimha, in might like a lion, ceaselessly intoxicated with intense bhava;

শ্রীভগবান্ ভাব ভর ভূষিত চতুর-শিরোমণি চরিত গভীর ।
গুণমণি গোকুল গৌরচন্দ্র-গুণকীর্ত্তনে অনুখন হোত অথির ॥

*śrībhagabān bhāba bhara bhūṣita catura-śiromaṇi carita gabhīra |*
*guṇamaṇi gokula gauracandra-guṇakīrttane anukhana hota athira ||*

*Word for word:* śrī-bhagabān — Sri Bhagavan; bhāba bhara bhūṣita — adorned with abundant bhava; catura-śiromaṇi — crest-jewel of the expert; carita gabhīra — deep in character; guṇamaṇi gokula — Gokula, jewel of virtues; gauracandra-guṇa-kīrtane — in the kirtana of Gaurachandra's virtues; anukhana hota athira — every time loses composure

**14.6.** Sri Bhagavan, adorned with an abundance of bhava, crest-jewel of the expert, deep in character;
Gokula, a jewel of virtues, losing his composure every time in the kirtana of Gaurachandra's qualities;

শ্রীবল্লভীকান্ত করুণার্ণব ভক্তিপ্রচারক অধিক উদার ।
গোপীরমণ নৃত্যগীতপ্রিয় পূজ্য প্রচণ্ড প্রতাপ অপার ॥

*śrīballabhīkānta karuṇārṇaba bhaktipracāraka adhika udāra |*
*gopīramaṇa nṛtyagītapriya pūjya pracaṇḍa pratāpa apāra ||*

*Word for word:* śrī-ballabhīkānta — Sri Vallavikanta; karuṇārṇaba — ocean of compassion; bhakti-pracāraka — preacher of bhakti; adhika udāra — boundlessly generous; gopīramaṇa — Gopiramana; nṛtya-gīta-priya — fond of dance and song; pūjya — worthy of honour; pracaṇḍa pratāpa apāra — boundless might

**14.7.** Sri Vallavikanta, ocean of compassion, preacher of bhakti, boundlessly generous;
Gopiramana, fond of dance and song, worthy of honour, boundless in his might;

দ্বিজকুল উজ্জ্বলকারী চক্রবর্ত্তী শ্রীশ্যামদাসাখ্য কৃপাল ।
কো সমুঝব তছু চরিত সুধাময় ত্রিভুবন বিদিত সুকীর্ত্তিবিশাল ॥

*dvijakula ujjvalakārī cakrabarttī śrīśyāmadāsākhya kṛpāla |*
*ko samujhaba tachu carita sudhāmaya tribhubana bidita sukīrttibiśāla ||*

*Word for word:* dvijakula ujjvalakārī — illumining the brahmana race; cakrabartī — Chakravarti; śrī-śyāmadāsākhya — named Sri Shyamadasa; kṛpāla — merciful; ko samujhaba — who will understand; tachu carita sudhāmaya — his nectarean life; tribhubana bidita — known to the three worlds; sukīrti biśāla — great fame

**14.8.** the merciful Chakravarti named Sri Shyamadasa, who illumines the brahmana race —
who will understand his nectarean life? His great fame is known to the three worlds;

রামচরণ চিতচোর চতুরবর পণ্ডিত পরম কৃপার্ণব ধীর ।
গৌর নিতাই নাম শুনইতে যছু ঝর ঝর নয়নযুগলে ঝরু নীর ॥

*rāmacaraṇa citacora caturabara paṇḍita parama kṛpārṇaba dhīra |*
*gaura nitāi nāma śunaite yachu jhara jhara nayanayugale jharu nīra ||*

*Word for word:* rāmacaraṇa — Ramacharana; citacora — stealer of hearts; caturabara — best of the wise; paṇḍita — pandita; parama kṛpārṇaba — great ocean of mercy; dhīra — steady; gaura nitāi nāma śunaite — on hearing the names of Gaura and Nitai; yachu — whose; jhara jhara — in streams; nayana-yugale jharu nīra — tears pour from both eyes

**14.9.** Ramacharana, stealer of hearts, best of the wise, a pandita, an ocean of mercy, steady,
from whose two eyes, as soon as he hears the names of Gaura and Nitai, streams of tears pour down;

শ্রীমদ্ব্যাস বিদিত বিদগধ অতি সঘনে জপতহি সুমধুর হরিনাম ।
রোয়ত খনে খনে কম্প পুলক তনু লোটত ক্ষিতি নহি হোত বিরাম ॥

*śrīmadvyāsa bidita bidagadha ati saghane japatahi sumadhura harināma |*
*royata khane khane kampa pulaka tanu loṭata kṣiti nahi hota birāma ||*

*Word for word:* śrīmad-byāsa — Srimad Vyasa; bidita — famed; bidagadha ati — most refined; saghane japatahi — repeats again and again; sumadhura harināma — Hari's sweetest name; royata khane khane — weeps every moment; kampa pulaka tanu — body trembling and thrilling; loṭata kṣiti — rolls on the ground; nahi hota birāma — without respite

**14.10.** Srimad Vyasa, famed, most refined, again and again repeating Hari's sweetest name —
he weeps every moment, his body trembles and thrills, and he rolls on the ground without respite;

শ্রীগোবিন্দ গৌরগুণ লম্পট ভাসত প্রেমসমুদ্র মাঝার ।
শ্রীশ্রীদাস রসিক-জন-জীবন দীনবন্ধু-যশ বিশদ বিথার ॥

*śrīgobinda gauraguṇa lampaṭa bhāsata premasamudra mājhāra |*
*śrīśrīdāsa rasika-jana-jībana dīnabandhu-yaśa biśada bithāra ||*

*Word for word:* śrī-gobinda — Sri Govinda; gaura-guṇa lampaṭa — greedy for Gaura's virtues; bhāsata prema-samudra mājhāra — floats in the ocean of prema; śrī-śrī-dāsa — Sri Sri Dasa; rasika-jana-jībana — the life of the knowers of rasa; dīnabandhu-yaśa — the fame of the Friend of the lowly; biśada bithāra — pure, spreads

**14.11.** Sri Govinda, greedy for Gaura's virtues, floating in the ocean of prema;
Sri Sri Dasa, the life of the knowers of rasa, spreading the pure fame of the Friend of the lowly;

গোকুল-চক্রবর্ত্তী গুণসাগর কি কহব জগভরি মহিমা প্রকাশ ।
শ্রীমদ্রূপ ঘটক ঘটনাকৃত নিত্যচিত্ত মতি যুগল বিলাস ॥

*gokula-cakrabarttī guṇasāgara ki kahaba jagabhari mahimā prakāśa |*
*śrīmadrūpa ghaṭaka ghaṭanākṛta nityacitta mati yugala bilāsa ||*

*Word for word:* gokula-cakrabartī — Gokula Chakravarti; guṇa-sāgara — ocean of virtues; ki kahaba — how can I tell; jagabhari mahimā prakāśa — greatness manifest to the whole world; śrīmad-rūpa ghaṭaka — Srimad Rupa Ghataka; ghaṭanākṛta — "arranger of meetings"; nitya citta mati — mind ever; yugala bilāsa — in the pastimes of the Divine Couple

**14.12.** Gokula Chakravarti, ocean of virtues — how can I tell his greatness, manifest to the whole world?
Srimad Rupa Ghataka, "the arranger of meetings", whose mind is ever in the pastimes of the Divine Couple;

শ্রীরাধাবল্লভ মণ্ডল মহী মণ্ডিত গুণ আনন্দ স্বরূপ ।
পরিকর সহিত গৌর যছু সরবস পরম উদার ভকতিরসভূপ ॥

*śrīrādhāballabha maṇḍala mahī maṇḍita guṇa ānanda svarūpa |*
*parikara sahita gaura yachu sarabasa parama udāra bhakatirasabhūpa ||*

*Word for word:* śrī-rādhāballabha maṇḍala — Sri Radhavallabha Mandala; mahī maṇḍita — adorning the earth; guṇa ānanda svarūpa — embodiment of the bliss of virtues; parikara sahita gaura — Gaura with His companions; yachu sarabasa — whose whole wealth; parama udāra — great-souled; bhakati-rasa-bhūpa — king of the rasa of bhakti

**14.13.** Sri Radhavallabha Mandala, adorning the earth, embodiment of the bliss of virtues,
whose whole wealth is Gaura with His companions, great-souled, a king of the rasa of bhakti;

নৃপতি বীর হাম্বীর বীরবর করি দুঃখ দূর পূরই অভিলাষ ।
কাতর উর নরহরি সুপুকারত চরণ নিকট রাখহ করি দাস ॥

*nṛpati bīra hāmbīra bīrabara kari duḥkha dūra pūrai abhilāṣa |*
*kātara ura narahari supukārata caraṇa nikaṭa rākhaha kari dāsa ||*

*Word for word:* nṛpati bīra hāmbīra — King Vira Hambira; bīrabara — best of heroes; kari duḥkha dūra — dispelling sorrow; pūraī abhilāṣa — fulfilling desires; kātara ura — broken-hearted; narahari supukārata — Narahari cries aloud; caraṇa nikaṭa — near the feet; rākhaha kari dāsa — keep [me] as a servant

**14.14.** King Vira Hambira, best of heroes, who dispels sorrow and fulfils desires —
Narahari, broken-hearted, cries aloud: "Keep me near your feet as a servant!"[^26-28]

[^26-27]: GPT1 — pp. 479–480, no. 69 ("pathamanjari"; scan, PDF pp. 736–737); GPT2 — section 6.3, no. 69. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-330). GCC —
kirana 1, pada 22 ("raga pathamanjari"): in the row of vandana-padas with which the poet at the beginning of the book praises Gaura's companions and the
followers (padas 13–26; before it — Ghanashyama's pada on Srinivasa and others, after it — padas on Harirama, Ramakrishna and Ganganarayana = GPT nos.
49, 72, 71). The variants in the OCR of the GCC are insignificant ("anubhaba nahu marma", "śrīgobinda kabīndra kṛpānidhi mahāmana gauracaritra" —
without "dhīra"). Not in the BR (as a separate pada), PK, KGC, PS or Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^26-28]: All those named are disciples and associates of Srinivasa Acharya: Govinda Kaviraja — Ramachandra's brother (no. 13); Karnapura, Nrisimha,
Bhagavan — also "kavirajas" of his circle; Govinda (14.11) — probably Govinda Chakravarti of Boraquli, "Bhavuka Chakravarti" (cf. no. 9 and the event
of the festival at Boraquli); Vira Hambira — the king of Vana-Vishnupura converted by Srinivasa after the theft of the Gosvamis' books. Some
identifications are uncertain: the pada gives only names. "Rupa Ghataka" is a pun: ghaṭaka is a surname (the caste of matchmakers) and "arranger of
meetings", i.e. one who in his mind serves the meetings of Radha and Krishna. "The depth of his realization cannot be fathomed" (14.3, anubhaba naha
marma) — possibly also "he grasps not the letter only but the essence" (the reading is ambiguous).

## 15. Narahari — "jaya jaya śrīgaṅgānārāyaṇa cakrabartī…" (GPT1 p. 481, no. 71; BR, GCC)
*Late layer: on the followers. Praise of Ganganarayana Chakravarti, a disciple of Narottama: steady and deep, beautiful in form, greedy for
sankirtana, skilled in dance, immersed in prema; he worships Narottama's feet, drinks the nectar of the Chaitanya-charitamrita; his life is the Deity
Sri Govinda; the poet cannot describe his wondrous ways. Raga belabali or gauri. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR
(15th wave) and in the GCC (kirana 1).*[^26-29]

জয় জয় শ্রীগঙ্গানারায়ণ চক্রবর্ত্তী অতি ধীর গভীর ।
ধৈরজহরণ বরণ বর মাধুরী নিরুপম মৃদুতর রুচির শরীর ॥

*jaya jaya śrīgaṅgānārāyaṇa cakrabarttī ati dhīra gabhīra |*
*dhairajaharaṇa baraṇa bara mādhurī nirupama mṛdutara rucira śarīra ||*

*Word for word:* jaya jaya — glory, glory; śrī-gaṅgānārāyaṇa cakrabartī — to Sri Ganganarayana Chakravarti; ati dhīra gabhīra — most steady and deep; dhairaja-haraṇa — stealing composure; baraṇa bara mādhurī — the charm of his lovely colour; nirupama mṛdutara rucira śarīra — an incomparably tender, beautiful body

**15.1.** Glory, glory to Sri Ganganarayana Chakravarti, most steady and deep!
His lovely colour steals composure, his body is incomparably tender and beautiful.

অবিরত সংকীর্ত্তনরস লম্পট ললিত নৃত্যরত প্রেমবিভোর ।
শ্রীল নরোত্তম চরণ-সরোরুহ-ভজনপরায়ণ ভুবন উজোর ॥

*abirata saṃkīrttanarasa lampaṭa lalita nṛtyarata premabibhora |*
*śrīla narottama caraṇa-saroruha-bhajanaparāyaṇa bhubana ujora ||*

*Word for word:* abirata — ceaselessly; saṅkīrtana-rasa lampaṭa — greedy for the rasa of sankirtana; lalita nṛtya-rata — devoted to graceful dance; prema-bibhora — enraptured with prema; śrīla narottama caraṇa-saroruha — the lotus feet of Srila Narottama; bhajana-parāyaṇa — devoted to worshipping; bhubana ujora — illumining the world

**15.2.** Ceaselessly greedy for the rasa of sankirtana, devoted to graceful dance, enraptured with prema;
devoted to the worship of Srila Narottama's lotus feet, he illumines the world.

শ্রীচৈতন্যচন্দ্র-চরিতামৃতপানে মগন মন সতত উদার ।
শ্রীগোবিন্দ মনোহর বিগ্রহ যজ্জীবন ধন প্রাণ আধার ॥

*śrīcaitanyacandra-caritāmṛtapāne magana mana satata udāra |*
*śrīgobinda manohara bigraha yajjībana dhana prāṇa ādhāra ||*

*Word for word:* śrī-caitanyacandra-caritāmṛta-pāne — in drinking the nectar of Sri Chaitanyachandra's deeds; magana mana — the mind immersed; satata udāra — ever generous; śrī-gobinda manohara bigraha — the enchanting Deity of Sri Govinda; yaj-jībana — whose life; dhana — wealth; prāṇa ādhāra — support of the soul

**15.3.** His mind is immersed in drinking the nectar of the deeds of Sri Chaitanyachandra, he is ever generous;
the enchanting Deity of Sri Govinda is his life, wealth and the support of his soul.

পরম দয়াল দীনজন-বান্ধব প্রবল প্রতাপ তাপতমহারী ।
বরণি না শকতি কি রীতি অতি অদভুত বিদিত দাস নরহরি সুখকারী ॥

*parama dayāla dīnajana-bāndhaba prabala pratāpa tāpatamahārī |*
*baraṇi nā śakati ki rīti ati adabhuta bidita dāsa narahari sukhakārī ||*

*Word for word:* parama dayāla — supremely merciful; dīnajana-bāndhaba — friend of the lowly; prabala pratāpa — great might; tāpa-tama-hārī — destroying the darkness of suffering; baraṇi nā śakati — I have no power to describe; ki rīti ati adabhuta — how wondrous [his] ways; bidita — known; dāsa narahari sukhakārī — the joy of Narahari Dasa

**15.4.** Supremely merciful, friend of the lowly, of great might, he destroys the darkness of suffering;
I have no power to describe his wondrous ways, known to all — he is the joy of Narahari Dasa.[^26-30]

[^26-29]: GPT1 — p. 481, no. 71 ("belabali or gauri"; scan, PDF p. 738); GPT2 — section 6.3, no. 71. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-331). BR 15 (ed. 1912,
p. ≈1062; ed. 1960, 15.131–134, "in song, gauri"): "Narottama's branch: Sri Thakura Narottama, the purifier of the fallen; his disciple — Chakravarti
Ganganarayana; very learned, refuting the doctrines of the godless, he manifests bhakti… poets sing his life" (15.128–130); after the pada — the end of
the 15th wave. GCC — kirana 1, pada 25 ("raga dhanashi"). Variants: 15.3 BR "śrīcaitanyacandracaritāmṛtapāne magana mana, satata udāra"; 15.4 BR
"baraṇi nā śakati kīriti ati adabhuta, bidita dāsa narahari-sukhakārī" ("his fame" instead of "his ways"). Not in the PK, KGC, PS or Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^26-30]: Ganganarayana Chakravarti — a kulina brahmana who became a disciple of Narottama (Prema-vilasa, vilasa 17); together with Ramakrishna Acharya
he, according to the BR, refuted the doctrines of the opponents of bhakti. "The nectar of the deeds of Sri Chaitanyachandra" (caitanyacandra-caritāmṛta)
is here probably also the Chaitanya-charitamrita of Krishnadasa Kaviraja itself, which Narottama's circle spread. Sri Govinda — the Deity whom
Ganganarayana served.

## 16. Narahari — "jaya jaya rāmakṛṣṇa ācārya…" (GPT1 p. 481, no. 72; BR, GCC)
*Late layer: on the followers. Praise of Ramakrishna Acharya, a disciple of Narottama: wise, generous, ever in bhava, greedy for kirtana; an ornament
of the brahmana race, crushing the pride of the evil-tongued; the chief servant of the Deity Sri Manmohana Raya; Narottama's feet are his whole
wealth. Raga gauri. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (15th wave) and in the GCC (kirana 1).*[^26-31]

জয় জয় রামকৃষ্ণ আচার্য্য সুধীর মহাশয় সুখদ উদার ।
ভাবাবেশে নিরন্তর কীর্ত্তন লম্পট অতিশয় সুঘড় প্রচার ॥

*jaya jaya rāmakṛṣṇa ācāryya sudhīra mahāśaya sukhada udāra |*
*bhābābeśe nirantara kīrttana lampaṭa atiśaya sughaṛa pracāra ||*

*Word for word:* jaya jaya — glory, glory; rāmakṛṣṇa ācārya — to Ramakrishna Acharya; sudhīra mahāśaya — the wise Mahashaya; sukhada udāra — giver of happiness, generous; bhābābeśe nirantara — ceaselessly absorbed in bhava; kīrtana lampaṭa — greedy for kirtana; atiśaya sughaṛa pracāra — supremely graceful preaching

**16.1.** Glory, glory to Ramakrishna Acharya, the wise Mahashaya, giver of happiness, generous!
Ceaselessly absorbed in bhava, greedy for kirtana — his preaching is supremely graceful.

সুখময় রসিকজন-মনরঞ্জন তাপপুঞ্জতম-ভঞ্জনকারী ।
দ্বিজকুল মণ্ডল গুণগণমণ্ডিত বড় দুর্ম্মুখ-মদহারী ॥

*sukhamaya rasikajana-manarañjana tāpapuñjatama-bhañjanakārī |*
*dvijakula maṇḍala guṇagaṇamaṇḍita baṛa durmmukha-madahārī ||*

*Word for word:* sukhamaya — blissful; rasikajana-mana-rañjana — delighting the hearts of the knowers of rasa; tāpa-puñja-tama-bhañjanakārī — dispelling the darkness of suffering; dvijakula maṇḍala — ornament of the brahmana race; guṇagaṇa-maṇḍita — adorned with virtues; baṛa durmukha-mada-hārī — crushing the pride of the evil-tongued

**16.2.** Blissful, delighting the hearts of the knowers of rasa, dispelling the darkness of suffering;
an ornament of the brahmana race, adorned with virtues, he crushes the pride of the evil-tongued.

শ্রীমন্মোহন রায় সুবিগ্রহ সেবা সতত নিযুক্ত প্রধান ।
অদ্ভুত রতি উলসিত দিবানিশি গৌরচন্দ্র চরিতামৃতপান ॥

*śrīmanmohana rāya subigraha sebā satata niyukta pradhāna |*
*adbhuta rati ulasita dibāniśi gauracandra caritāmṛtapāna ||*

*Word for word:* śrī-manmohana rāya — Sri Manmohana Raya; subigraha sebā — service of the beautiful Deity; satata niyukta pradhāna — ever appointed chief; adbhuta rati — wondrous attachment; ulasita dibāniśi — rejoicing day and night; gauracandra caritāmṛta-pāna — drinking the nectar of Gaurachandra's deeds

**16.3.** He is ever appointed chief in the service of the beautiful Deity of Sri Manmohana Raya;
wondrous is his attachment: rejoicing day and night, he drinks the nectar of Gaurachandra's deeds.

পরম দয়াল নরোত্তমপদযুগ যছু সর্ব্বস্ব ন জানত অন্য ।
কো সমুঝব উহ রীত রুচির যশ গায়ত নরহরি মানত ধন্য ॥

*parama dayāla narottamapadayuga yachu sarvvasva na jānata anya |*
*ko samujhaba uha rīta rucira yaśa gāyata narahari mānata dhanya ||*

*Word for word:* parama dayāla narottama-pada-yuga — the feet of supremely merciful Narottama; yachu sarvasva — his whole wealth; na jānata anya — knows nothing else; ko samujhaba — who will understand; uha rīta — his way; rucira yaśa gāyata — sings his beautiful fame; narahari mānata dhanya — Narahari counts himself fortunate

**16.4.** The feet of supremely merciful Narottama are his whole wealth, he knows nothing else;
who will understand his way? Narahari sings his beautiful fame and counts himself fortunate.[^26-32]

[^26-31]: GPT1 — p. 481, no. 72 ("gauri"; scan, PDF p. 738); GPT2 — section 6.3, no. 72 (NG-225; signature "narahari mānata dhanya" — Narahari; the next pada,
no. 73, is by Manohara Dasa). BR 15 (ed. 1912, pp. ≈1061–1062; ed. 1960, 15.124–127, "in song, gauri"): "Sri Narottama's disciple — Ramakrishna Acharya,
a great pandita… a refuter of godless doctrines, known everywhere" (15.121–123; lost in the OCR of the 1960 ed., the text — from the 1912 ed.), then the
pada, then — on Ganganarayana (GPT no. 71). GCC — kirana 1, pada 24 ("raga kamoda"). Variants: 16.2 BR "paṇḍitabara durmukha-madahārī" ("best of
panditas"; GPT "baṛa durmmukha-madahārī"); the rest orthographic. Not in the PK, KGC, PS or Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^26-32]: Ramakrishna Acharya — Harirama's brother (no. 8), a brahmana pandita who became a disciple of Narottama (Prema-vilasa, vilasa 14). Shri
Manmohana Raya — the Deity he served. "The evil-tongued" (durmukha) — the revilers of bhakti, defeated by him in debate.

## 17. Narahari — "ki kahaba parikara parama udāra…" (GPT1 p. 483, no. 77; GCC)
*The companions around Gaura in the morning: they ceaselessly drink the nectar of His face, lose their composure, are adorned with bhavas — thrill,
trembling, tears, a choked voice; one whirls, one repeats the Name, one laughs and dances; the poet longs to see this. Raga not specified
("yatharaga"). **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC; Vrajabuli.*[^26-33]

কি কহব পরিকর পরম উদার ।
নিরুপম গৌরবদন অমৃতাকর তাকর অমিয় পীয়ত অনিবার ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*ki kahaba parikara parama udāra |*
*nirupama gaurabadana amṛtākara tākara amiya pīyata anibāra || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* ki kahaba — how can I describe; parikara — the companions; parama udāra — boundlessly generous; nirupama gaura-badana — Gaura's peerless face; amṛtākara — a mine of nectar; tākara amiya — its nectar; pīyata anibāra — they drink ceaselessly

**17.1.** How can I describe the companions, boundlessly generous!
Gaura's peerless face is a mine of nectar, and they ceaselessly drink that nectar.

কত কত যতন করত ধৃতি ধরইতে অনুখন অথির বিবশ রসে মাতি ।
অপরূপ ভাব ভূরি ভূষণ বর ভূষিত শুভ শোভা বহু ভাঁতি ॥

*kata kata yatana karata dhṛti dharaite anukhana athira bibaśa rase māti |*
*aparūpa bhāba bhūri bhūṣaṇa bara bhūṣita śubha śobhā bahu bhām̐ti ||*

*Word for word:* kata kata yatana karata — however they try; dhṛti dharaite — to keep composure; anukhana athira — ever unsteady; bibaśa rase māti — helplessly intoxicated with rasa; aparūpa bhāba bhūri bhūṣaṇa bara — with abundant wondrous ornaments of bhava; bhūṣita — adorned; śubha śobhā bahu bhām̐ti — beautiful in every way

**17.2.** However they try to keep their composure — they are ever unsteady, helplessly intoxicated with rasa;
adorned with abundant, wondrous ornaments of bhava, they are beautiful in every way.

কাহুক পুলকিত গাত বাত নহি নিকসত গদ গদ কণ্ঠ সুচার ।
কাহুক কম্প কাঁপাওত জনম কাহুক নয়নে বহত জলধার ॥

*kāhuka pulakita gāta bāta nahi nikasata gada gada kaṇṭha sucāra |*
*kāhuka kampa kām̐pāota janama kāhuka nayane bahata jaladhāra ||*

*Word for word:* kāhuka pulakita gāta — one's body thrills; bāta nahi nikasata — no words come out; gada gada kaṇṭha sucāra — a choked sound from the lovely throat; kāhuka kampa — another's trembling; kām̐pāota janama — shakes his whole being (?); kāhuka nayane bahata jaladhāra — from another's eyes tears flow

**17.3.** One's body thrills, there are no words — from his lovely throat comes only a choked sound;
another is shaken through his whole being by trembling, from a third one's eyes pour streams of tears.

কোউ ফিরত ভুজ ভঙ্গী করু কোউ মধুরিম নাম উচরি বেরি বেরি ।
কোউ হসত মৃদু নাচত ঘন ঘন নরহরি সফল হোয়ব কব হেরি ॥

*kou phirata bhuja bhaṅgī karu kou madhurima nāma ucari beri beri |*
*kou hasata mṛdu nācata ghana ghana narahari saphala hoyaba kaba heri ||*

*Word for word:* kou phirata — one whirls; bhuja bhaṅgī karu — making gestures with his arms; kou madhurima nāma ucari — another utters the sweet Name; beri beri — again and again; kou hasata mṛdu — one laughs softly; nācata ghana ghana — dances again and again; narahari saphala hoyaba kaba heri — when will Narahari, seeing, be fulfilled

**17.4.** One whirls about, making gestures with his arms, another again and again utters the sweet Name;
one laughs softly and dances again and again — when will Narahari, seeing this, find his life fulfilled?[^26-34]

[^26-33]: GPT1 — p. 483, no. 77 ("yatharaga"; scan, PDF p. 740); GPT2 — section 6.3, no. 77 (NG-226). GCC — kirana 4, pada 21 ("yatharaga"), the last of the padas on
the companions around Gaura in the morning; after it — a couplet with the same signature: "thus all the companions gaze at the moon of Gaura's face,
their hearts in great joy, and they form various wishes" (pada 22) — and the colophon of the kirana ("The Lord in the circle of devotees"). Variants:
17.1 GCC "piyata"; 17.3 "kām̐pāota janama" (so in GPT1; understood as "the whole being"; the word is distorted in the OCR of the GCC). Not in the BR, PK,
KGC, PS or Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^26-34]: The sattvika-bhavas are listed — ecstatic manifestations of prema: thrill (pulaka), choked voice (svara-bhanga), trembling (kampa), tears (ashru).
"Find his life fulfilled" (saphala hoyaba) — the poet considers life fulfilled if he beholds this lila (in contemplation).

## 18. Narahari — "ei abhilāṣa mane…" (GPT1 pp. 484–485, no. 83; BR)
*The poet's prayer about Gaura's companions: intoxicated with His virtues, to wander day and night, to sing of Nitai with a thousand mouths, to honour
Advaita, to dance crying the names of Gadadhara, Narahari, Svarupa, Srivasa and others, to serve the feet of the Lord's parents and of His companions,
to glorify the Gosvamis of Vrindavana, to become "a dog at the door" of the kirtaniyas — and to wear the names of all the companions on his neck as a
necklace. Raga kamoda. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the concluding chapter of the BR (eds. 1960 and 2006), right before the
author's word about himself; among the companions it also names Narahari (Sarakara).*[^26-35]

এই অভিলাষ মনে, গৌরাঙ্গচাঁদের গুণে, মাতিয়া বেড়াই দিবানিশি ।
লক্ষ্মী বিষ্ণুপ্রিয়া সঙ্গ, নদীয়াবিহার রঙ্গ, সে সুখসায়রে যেন ভাসি ॥

*ei abhilāṣa mane, gaurāṅgacām̐dera guṇe, mātiyā beṛāi dibāniśi |*
*lakṣmī biṣṇupriyā saṅga, nadīyābihāra raṅga, se sukhasāyare yena bhāsi ||*

*Word for word:* ei abhilāṣa mane — this is the desire of my heart; gaurāṅgacām̐dera guṇe — by Gaurangachand's virtues; mātiyā beṛāi dibāniśi — intoxicated, to wander day and night; lakṣmī biṣṇupriyā saṅga — the company of Lakshmi and Vishnupriya; nadīyā-bihāra raṅga — the joy of the pastimes in Nadia; se sukha-sāyare yena bhāsi — as if floating in that ocean of happiness

**18.1.** This is the desire of my heart: intoxicated with the virtues of Gaurangachand, to wander day and night,
[remembering] His company with Lakshmi and Vishnupriya and His pastimes in Nadia — as if floating in that ocean of happiness.

লক্ষ মুখে ক্ষণে ক্ষণে, বসুধা জাহ্নবী সনে, নিতাইচাঁদের গুণ গাই ।
সীতা সহ সীতানাথে, সতত বন্দিয়া মাথে, তার যশে জগত ভাসাই ॥

*lakṣa mukhe kṣaṇe kṣaṇe, basudhā jāhnabī sane, nitāicām̐dera guṇa gāi |*
*sītā saha sītānāthe, satata bandiyā māthe, tāra yaśe jagata bhāsāi ||*

*Word for word:* lakṣa mukhe — with a hundred thousand mouths; kṣaṇe kṣaṇe — again and again; basudhā jāhnabī sane — with Vasudha and Jahnava; nitāicām̐dera guṇa gāi — I sing Nitaichand's virtues; sītā saha sītānāthe — Sitanatha with Sita; satata bandiyā māthe — ceaselessly bowing my head; tāra yaśe jagata bhāsāi — with His fame I flood the world

**18.2.** With a hundred thousand mouths again and again to sing the virtues of Nitaichand with Vasudha and Jahnava;
ceaselessly to bow my head to Sitanatha with Sita — and with His fame to flood the world.

গদাধর নরহরি, স্বরূপ ফুৎকার করি, নাচি সদা কাঁখতালি দিয়া ।
শ্রীনিবাস বনমালী, দাস গদাধর বলি, আনন্দে উমড়ে যেন হিয়া ॥

*gadādhara narahari, svarūpa phutkāra kari, nāci sadā kām̐khatāli diyā |*
*śrīnibāsa banamālī, dāsa gadādhara bali, ānande umaṛe yena hiyā ||*

*Word for word:* gadādhara narahari svarūpa — Gadadhara, Narahari, Svarupa; phutkāra kari — with jubilant cries; nāci sadā — ever to dance; kāṅkha-tāli diyā — slapping the armpits; śrīnibāsa banamālī dāsa gadādhara bali — crying "Srinivasa, Vanamali, Dasa Gadadhara"; ānande umaṛe yena hiyā — that the heart may overflow with bliss

**18.3.** Gadadhara, Narahari, Svarupa — with jubilant cries ever to dance, slapping my armpits;
crying "Srinivasa! Vanamali! Dasa Gadadhara!" — so that my heart would overflow with bliss.

হরিদাস বক্রেশ্বর, রামানন্দ দামোদর, গৌরীদাস শ্রীরঘুনন্দন ।
মুরারি মুকুন্দ রাম, লৈয়া এ সভার নাম, নিরন্তর করিয়ে কীর্ত্তন ॥

*haridāsa bakreśvara, rāmānanda dāmodara, gaurīdāsa śrīraghunandana |*
*murāri mukunda rāma, laiyā e sabhāra nāma, nirantara kariye kīrttana ||*

*Word for word:* haridāsa bakreśvara — Haridasa, Vakreshvara; rāmānanda dāmodara — Ramananda, Damodara; gaurīdāsa śrīraghunandana — Gauridasa, Sri Raghunandana; murāri mukunda rāma — Murari, Mukunda, Rama; laiyā e sabhāra nāma — with all their names; nirantara kariye kīrtana — I ceaselessly perform kirtana

**18.4.** Haridasa, Vakreshvara, Ramananda, Damodara, Gauridasa, Sri Raghunandana,
Murari, Mukunda, Rama — with their names ceaselessly to perform kirtana.

শচী মিশ্র জগন্নাথ, প্রভুর জননী তাত, পদ্মাবতী হাড়াই পণ্ডিত ।
জগত বিদিত গুণে, এ সভার শ্রীচরণে, জনমে জনমে রহুঁ চিত ॥

*śacī miśra jagannātha, prabhura jananī tāta, padmābatī hāṛāi paṇḍita |*
*jagata bidita guṇe, e sabhāra śrīcaraṇe, janame janame rahum̐ cita ||*

*Word for word:* śacī miśra jagannātha — Shachi and Mishra Jagannatha; prabhura jananī tāta — the Lord's mother and father; padmābatī hāṛāi paṇḍita — Padmavati and Hadai Pandita; jagata bidita guṇe — known to the world for their virtues; e sabhāra śrīcaraṇe — at the feet of all these; janame janame rahum̐ cita — birth after birth may my mind abide

**18.5.** Shachi and Mishra Jagannatha — the Lord's mother and father, Padmavati, Hadai Pandita —
known to the world for their virtues: at their feet, birth after birth, may my mind abide.

শ্রীমাধব রত্নাবতী, মালতী মাধবী অতি, স্নেহবতী দময়ন্তী দেবী ।
শ্রীঅচ্যুতানন্দ কন্দ, দয়াময় বীরচন্দ্র, ও পদপঙ্কজ যেন সেবি ॥

*śrīmādhaba ratnābatī, mālatī mādhabī ati, snehabatī damayantī debī |*
*śrīacyutānanda kanda, dayāmaya bīracandra, o padapaṅkaja yena sebi ||*

*Word for word:* śrī-mādhaba ratnābatī — Sri Madhava and Ratnavati; mālatī mādhabī — Malati, Madhavi; ati snehabatī damayantī debī — loving Damayanti Devi; śrī-acyutānanda kanda — Sri Achyutananda, the root [of bliss]; dayāmaya bīracandra — merciful Virachandra; o padapaṅkaja yena sebi — may I serve those lotus feet

**18.6.** Sri Madhava and Ratnavati, Malati, Madhavi, loving Damayanti Devi,
Sri Achyutananda — the root of bliss, merciful Virachandra — may I serve their lotus feet.

শ্রীবল্লভ সনাতন, সদাশিব সুদর্শন, নন্দন বিজয় কাশীশ্বর ।
বিশ্বরূপ বুলি বুলি, ফিরি যেন ফুলি ফুলি, দেখিয়া পাষণ্ডী পাউক ডর ॥

*śrīballabha sanātana, sadāśiba sudarśana, nandana bijaya kāśīśvara |*
*biśvarūpa buli buli, phiri yena phuli phuli, dekhiyā pāṣaṇḍī pāuka ḍara ||*

*Word for word:* śrī-ballabha sanātana — Sri Vallabha, Sanatana; sadāśiba sudarśana — Sadashiva, Sudarshana; nandana bijaya kāśīśvara — Nandana, Vijaya, Kashishvara; biśvarūpa — Vishvarupa; buli buli — repeating [their names]; phiri yena phuli phuli — may I wander rejoicing; dekhiyā pāṣaṇḍī pāuka ḍara — that the godless, seeing, may fear

**18.7.** Sri Vallabha, Sanatana, Sadashiva, Sudarshana, Nandana, Vijaya, Kashishvara,
Vishvarupa — repeating their names, may I wander rejoicing, so that the godless, seeing me, take fright.

প্রিয় সনাতন রূপ, ভট্টযুগ রসকূপ, রঘুনাথ শ্রীজীব গভীর ।
এ নাম লইতে যেন, ধূলায় ধূসর যেন, হয় মোর এ পাপশরীর ॥

*priya sanātana rūpa, bhaṭṭayuga rasakūpa, raghunātha śrījība gabhīra |*
*e nāma laite yena, dhūlāya dhūsara yena, haya mora e pāpaśarīra ||*

*Word for word:* priya sanātana rūpa — dear Sanatana and Rupa; bhaṭṭa-yuga rasa-kūpa — the two Bhattas, wells of rasa; raghunātha śrījība gabhīra — Raghunatha and deep Sri Jiva; e nāma laite — taking these names; dhūlāya dhūsara yena — grey with dust; haya mora e pāpa-śarīra — may this sinful body of mine become

**18.8.** Dear Sanatana and Rupa, the two Bhattas — wells of rasa, Raghunatha and deep Sri Jiva —
repeating these names, may this sinful body of mine become grey with dust.

সুবুদ্ধি রাঘব সাথ, ভূগর্ভ শ্রীলোকনাথ, ব্রজে যারা ফিরে প্রেমরঙ্গে ।
এ নামে হউক রতি, দূরে যাউক দুষ্ট মতি, পুলক ব্যাপুক সব অঙ্গে ॥

*subuddhi rāghaba sātha, bhūgarbha śrīlokanātha, braje yārā phire premaraṅge |*
*e nāme hauka rati, dūre yāuka duṣṭa mati, pulaka byāpuka saba aṅge ||*

*Word for word:* subuddhi rāghaba sātha — Subuddhi with Raghava; bhūgarbha śrīlokanātha — Bhugarbha, Sri Lokanatha; braje yārā phire premaraṅge — who wander in Vraja in the joy of prema; e nāme hauka rati — may there be attachment to these names; dūre yāuka duṣṭa mati — may the evil mind go far away; pulaka byāpuka saba aṅge — may a thrill pervade the whole body

**18.9.** Subuddhi with Raghava, Bhugarbha, Sri Lokanatha, who wander in Vraja in the joy of prema —
may I have attachment to these names, may the evil mind go far away, may a thrill pervade my whole body.

গোবিন্দ মাধব হরি, শুক্লাম্বর ব্রহ্মচারী, বাসুঘোষ গৌর যার প্রাণ ।
এ সবার পরসাদে, ফিরি যেন সিংহনাদে, অভক্তে করিয়া তৃণজ্ঞান ॥

*gobinda mādhaba hari, śuklāmbara brahmacārī, bāsughoṣa gaura yāra prāṇa |*
*e sabāra parasāde, phiri yena siṃhanāde, abhakte kariyā tṛṇajñāna ||*

*Word for word:* gobinda mādhaba hari — Govinda, Madhava, Hari; śuklāmbara brahmacārī — Shuklambara Brahmachari; bāsughoṣa — Vasu Ghosha; gaura yāra prāṇa — whose life is Gaura; e sabāra parasāde — by the grace of all these; phiri yena siṃhanāde — may I wander with a lion's roar; abhakte kariyā tṛṇajñāna — counting non-devotees as straw

**18.10.** Govinda, Madhava, Hari, Shuklambara Brahmachari, Vasu Ghosha, whose life is Gaura —
by their grace may I wander with a lion's roar, not counting the non-devotees even as a straw.

কীর্ত্তনিয়া ষষ্ঠীবর, হরিদাস দ্বিজবর, খোলাবেচা শ্রীধর ঠাকুর ।
কংসারি বল্লভ আর, ধনঞ্জয় এ সভার, হই যেন নাচের কুকুর ॥

*kīrttaniyā ṣaṣṭhībara, haridāsa dvijabara, kholābecā śrīdhara ṭhākura |*
*kaṃsāri ballabha āra, dhanañjaya e sabhāra, hai yena nācera kukura ||*

*Word for word:* kīrtaniyā ṣaṣṭhībara — the kirtaniya Shashthivara; haridāsa dvijabara — Haridasa, best of brahmanas; kholābecā śrīdhara ṭhākura — Shridhara Thakura, seller of banana leaves; kaṃsāri ballabha āra dhanañjaya — Kamsari, Vallabha and Dhananjaya; e sabhāra — of all these; hai yena nācera kukura — may I become the dancing dog

**18.11.** The kirtaniya Shashthivara, Haridasa — the best of brahmanas, Shridhara Thakura, the seller of banana leaves,
Kamsari, Vallabha and Dhananjaya — may I become their dancing dog.

কবিচন্দ্র বিদ্যানিধি, শ্রীমধু পণ্ডিত আদি, গৌরপ্রিয় যত পরিবার ।
দাস নরহরি ভণে, এ নাম রতনগণে, গলায় পরিয়া করি হার ॥

*kabicandra bidyānidhi, śrīmadhu paṇḍita ādi, gaurapriya yata paribāra |*
*dāsa narahari bhaṇe, e nāma ratanagaṇe, galāya pariyā kari hāra ||*

*Word for word:* kabicandra bidyānidhi — Kavichandra, Vidyanidhi; śrīmadhu paṇḍita ādi — Sri Madhu Pandita and others; gaura-priya yata paribāra — all those dear to Gaura; dāsa narahari bhaṇe — sings Narahari Dasa; e nāma ratanagaṇe — of these jewel-names; galāya pariyā kari hāra — making a necklace, I put it on my neck

**18.12.** Kavichandra, Vidyanidhi, Sri Madhu Pandita and all the others dear to Gaura —
Narahari Dasa sings: of these jewel-names I will make a necklace and put it on my neck.[^26-36]

[^26-35]: GPT1 — pp. 484–485, no. 83 ("kamoda"; scan, PDF pp. 741–742); GPT2 — section 6.3, no. 83. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-332). BR — the
concluding chapter (a brief table of contents of the fifteen waves; ed. 1960 — 35–46, "in song, kamoda"; ed. 2006 — the same place): having listed the

PS or Gita-chandrodaya. B. This is the strongest argument for attribution in the whole section: the pada is part of the author's conclusion of the BR, and
"Narahari" in 18.3 is a companion of the Lord (Sarakara), whom the poet invokes like the others.

(18.11); Kavichandra, Pundarika Vidyanidhi, Madhu Pandita (18.12). "Not counting the non-devotees even as a straw" (abhakte kariyā tṛṇajñāna) — not to fear
the opponents of bhakti, not to despise living beings; "a dancing dog" — an image of utmost humility: a devoted servant dancing at his master's word.

## 19. Narahari — "gorācām̐da chāṛi yābe naidā…" (GPT1 pp. 367–368, section 5.3, no. 7; BR)
*Before the sannyasa: Gorachand will leave Nadia — and the Jahnavi grew still, the murtis of Shambhu, Bhagavati and Ganapati faded, the trees do not
blossom, the bees do not hum, the cuckoos have fallen silent, the peacocks do not dance, the birds weep, the cows and deer find no rest: the land of Nadia
cannot contain its grief. Raga ashabari or deshpal. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave); found in the
continuous check of signatures (supplement).*[^26-37]

গোরাচাঁদ ছাড়ি যাবে নৈদা ইথে, তরঙ্গরহিত জাহ্নবী ধারা ।
শম্ভু ভগবতী গণপতি মূর্ত্তি যত ছিল, হৈল মলিনপারা ॥

*gorācām̐da chāṛi yābe naidā ithe, taraṅgarahita jāhnabī dhārā |*
*śambhu bhagabatī gaṇapati mūrtti yata chila, haila malinapārā ||*

*Word for word:* gorācām̐da chāṛi yābe — Gorachand will leave; naidā — Nadia; ithe — therefore; taraṅga-rahita — without waves; jāhnabī dhārā — the stream of the Jahnavi; śambhu bhagabatī gaṇapati — Shambhu, Bhagavati, Ganapati; mūrti yata chila — all the murtis (Deities) there were; haila malina-pārā — became as if faded

**19.1.** Gorachand will leave Nadia — therefore the stream of the Jahnavi is left without waves;
the murtis of Shambhu, Bhagavati, Ganapati — all there were — seem to have faded.

তরুলতা ফুল পল্লবিত নহে, না বিকাশে পুষ্প সুগন্ধহীনা ।
তাহে না বৈসে না পিয়ে পুষ্পরস, না গুঞ্জে ভ্রমর ভ্রমরী দীনা ॥

*tarulatā phula pallabita nahe, nā bikāśe puṣpa sugandhahīnā |*
*tāhe nā baise nā piye puṣparasa, nā guñje bhramara bhramarī dīnā ||*

*Word for word:* tarulatā phula pallabita nahe — trees and creepers do not put forth flowers and leaves; nā bikāśe puṣpa — the flowers do not open; sugandha-hīnā — without fragrance; tāhe nā baise — do not alight on them; nā piye puṣpa-rasa — do not drink nectar; nā guñje — do not hum; bhramara bhramarī dīnā — the bee and his mate, downcast

**19.2.** The trees and creepers do not put forth leaves, the flowers do not open — without fragrance;
the bee and his mate do not alight on them, do not drink the nectar, do not hum — downcast.

পিককুল কলরব বিরহিত, না নাচে ময়ূর ময়ূরী সনে ।
সারী শুক নানা পাখী আঁখি ঝুরে, নারে উড়িবারে ব্যাকুল বনে ॥

*pikakula kalaraba birahita, nā nāce mayūra mayūrī sane |*
*sārī śuka nānā pākhī ām̐khi jhure, nāre uṛibāre byākula bane ||*

*Word for word:* pikakula kalaraba birahita — the flocks of cuckoos without song; nā nāce mayūra mayūrī sane — the peacock does not dance with the peahen; sārī śuka nānā pākhī — the shari, shuka and other birds; ām̐khi jhure — weep; nāre uṛibāre — cannot fly; byākula bane — distraught in the forest

**19.3.** The flocks of cuckoos have fallen silent, the peacock does not dance with the peahen;
the shari, the shuka and other birds weep — they cannot fly, they flutter about the forest.

ধেনুগণ হাম্বা রবে না ধায়য়ে, মৃগাদি পশু না ধরয়ে ধৃতি ।
ভণে নরহরি শোভা দূরে দুখ, সম্বরিতে নারে নদীয়া খিতি ॥

*dhenugaṇa hāmbā rabe nā dhāyaye, mṛgādi paśu nā dharaye dhṛti |*
*bhaṇe narahari śobhā dūre dukha, sambarite nāre nadīyā khiti ||*

*Word for word:* dhenugaṇa hāmbā rabe — the cows with lowing; nā dhāyaye — do not run; mṛgādi paśu — deer and other beasts; nā dharaye dhṛti — find no rest; bhaṇe narahari — Narahari says; śobhā dūre — beauty is gone; dukha sambarite nāre — cannot contain the grief; nadīyā khiti — the land of Nadia

**19.4.** The cows do not run lowing, the deer and other beasts find no rest.
Narahari says: beauty has gone, and the land of Nadia cannot contain its grief.[^26-38]

"bhaṇe narahari, śobhā dūre, dukha sambarite nāre nadīyā-khiti" — the same. The Navadvipa-parikrama is the same as the BR. Not in the GCC, PK, KGC, PS or
Gita-chandrodaya. B.

(Bhagavati) and Ganesha "fade" not because they are worshipped on a par with the Lord, but because the demigods too are His servants and grieve at His
departure. Shari and shuka — a pair of parrots (female and male), constant images of forest poetry.

## Concluding note to the appendix

*The appendix "Padas signed 'Narahari' from the Gaura-pada-tarangini" (chapters 17–26) is complete: **241 padas** have been translated — all the padas
signed Narahari known only from the GPT (with their witnesses — the Bhakti-ratnakara, the Gaura-charita-chintamani, the Gita-chandrodaya), except the padas
in nagari-bhava (they will form a separate section with an introductory note). Attribution as marked in the headings: **"probably Sarakara" — 4**
(mangalacharana and Gaura's form: plain Bengali, not in the BR, assigned to Sarakara by the GPT2 index; authority C); **"probably Chakravarti" — 221**
(almost all found in the Bhakti-ratnakara or in the Gaura-charita-chintamani of Narahari Chakravarti, and one stands in the author's
conclusion of the BR; authority B);
**"not established" — 16** (GPT only; among them several late padas, written apparently after both Naraharis; authority C); no pada of the
appendix has
authority D (doubtful authenticity). The result of the continuous check: the great majority of the "Narahari" padas known only from the GPT belong to Narahari Chakravarti (Ghanashyama
Dasa), an 18th-century author who wove his songs into his accounts of the holy places and of the Lord's associates; the legacy of Narahari Sarakara,
Mahaprabhu's companion, is above all the padas preserved in the Padakalpataru (the main part, chapters 1–6). Left outside the appendix: the padas in
nagari-bhava (a separate section), the padas signed Ghanashyama, prayers to the guru and praises of poets without Gaura-lila, padas in which Narahari is
only mentioned while the signature is another's, and one pada on Advaita known only from the BR (12th wave, vv. 3755–3760).*

# Part III. Nagari Padas

---

# Chapter 27. Nagari Padas — I: Vasu Ghosha (padas from the *Padakalpataru*)

## Introductory Note to the Section of Nagari Padas

*"Nagari" (nāgarī) means a townswoman, a woman of Nadia; "nagara" (nāgara) is a townsman, a gallant, and in the language of
Vaishnava poetry the beloved, the hero of the play of love (Krishna is so called: "Shyama-nagara," "rasika-nagara").
**Nagari-bhava** is the name given to the mood of padas in which the women of Nadia, having seen the young Gaura in the
street, at the bathing ghat on the Ganga, in kirtana, tell their friends of His beauty, lose their peace, forget home,
modesty and family, pine through the nights, see Him in dreams, and after His sannyasa lament the separation. In these
songs Gaura is "Gauranga-nagara," "the nagara of Nadia." The imagery is taken from the padas on Radha and Krishna —
purvaraga, anuraga, longing in expectation, disappointed waiting, telling a friend of the meeting; that is why in the
*Padakalpataru* (PK) such padas stand as gaura-chandrikas (preludes) to the corresponding sections on Radha — marked "the
words of the nagaris" (nāgarī ukti) — or are gathered into a separate pallava, "Gauranga's form: the words of the nagaris
and others."*

*Who sang in this mood. Tradition regards Narahari Sarakara of Shrikhanda and Vasu Ghosha as the first singers of
nagari-bhava (Majumdar remarks that Vasu calls Gaura "nagara" following Narahari); poets of the Shrikhanda school wrote in
the same spirit, among them Narahari's disciple Lochana Dasa; later such padas multiply — Nayanananda, Yadunandana, and many
songs signed "Narahari" in the *Gaura-pada-tarangini* (GPT), mostly by Narahari Chakravarti (18th century). Majumdar counts
about twenty padas of Vasu Ghosha in PK as nagari-bhava; padas known only from GPT he considers unreliable (among them are
even reworkings of padas on Krishna, ascribed to Vasu to give nagari-bhava an air of antiquity).*

*The position of the tradition. The Gaudiya Vaishnava tradition does not accept the worship of Gaura in the spirit of the
nagaris.*
- *Vrindavana Dasa in the *Chaitanya-bhagavata* (Adi-khanda), telling of the young Nimai, says that the Lord, who joked and
  played pranks with everyone, in this incarnation did not look at any woman even from the corner of His eye and would not
  even hear the word "woman"; therefore the wise, though every praise befits Him, do not glorify Him as "Gauranga-nagara,"
  but sing of Him according to His nature.*
- *Krishnadasa Kaviraja in the *Chaitanya-charitamrita* (Adi 1.5–6; Adi 4) reveals the secret of this incarnation: Gaura is
  Krishna Himself, who has taken the bhava and the luster of Radha in order to taste the greatness of Her love, the
  sweetness of Himself that She tastes, and Her happiness. He came to taste Radha's love — as Radha, in the mood of a
  devotee — and not to enjoy the love of women as a hero.*
- *Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati counts "gaura-nagari" among the apasampradayas — currents that have departed from the
  teaching of Mahaprabhu: worshipping Gaura as a nagara-lover transfers to His lila in Navadvipa what belongs to Krishna's
  Vraja-lila and distorts its meaning.*

*Gaura's attractiveness for all who saw Him is a quality of Bhagavan (so Krishna too is Madana-mohana, "the enchanter of the
god of love himself"); the biographers also write that the Lord's beauty robbed the people of Nadia of their peace. But the
Lord Himself in Navadvipa was a brahmana teacher, strict in conduct, then a devotee in Radha's bhava and a sannyasi; His
lilas are not worldly love.*

*Rules of the section. (1) The nagari padas are translated for the completeness of the corpus of padas on Gaura and as a
historical document — a witness to how He was sung of in the 16th–18th centuries; they are no basis for worshipping Gaura as
a nagara. (2) The translation is faithful to the author: the text is neither softened nor heightened; where the original
speaks of a glance and of beauty, it is so translated; where it speaks openly of attraction, it is translated exactly, with
a note. (3) The heading of each pada is marked "nagari-bhava"; the notes give a brief reference to this note instead of the
full caveat. (4) Pronouns referring to Gaura are capitalized; the nagaris' words about themselves are in lower case.*

*Chapter 27 contains the padas of Vasu Ghosha known from PK (the earliest and most reliable layer of nagari padas; Majumdar
includes them in his list of Vasu's padas), in the order of the lila: Gaura's form through the eyes of the townswomen, first
love and longing, a night of vain waiting, dreams and tales told to friends, the lament after the sannyasa. The text
follows PK, checked against the scans, with the manuscript variants from PK's apparatus and the *Gaura-pada-tarangini*
(GPT1 — 1st ed., 1903; GPT2 — 2nd ed., 1934); the Bengali original, variants and word-for-word translation are in the full version of the book.*

## 1. Vasu Ghosha — "sajanī ai dekha śacīra nandana…" (PK 2151)
*Nagari-bhava. Gaura's form: "Friend, look — there is Shachi's son!" Birds, beasts and trees weep hearing of His virtues,
noble wives cannot hold their hearts steady; giving to all the name unattainable even for Brahma, Gora has delivered the
world. In PK it stands in the pallava "Gaura's form." According to Majumdar, a pada of nagari-bhava. Raga varadi.*[^27-1]

সজনী ঐ দেখ শচীর নন্দন ।
যেবা জন দেখে তার স্থির নহে মন ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*sajanī ai dekha śacīra nandana |*
*yebā jana dekhe tāra sthira nahe mana || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* sajanī — friend; ai dekha — look, there; śacīra nandana — Shachi's son; yebā jana dekhe — whoever sees; tāra — his; sthira nahe mana — the mind (heart) is not at peace

**1.1.** *(Refrain)* Friend, look — there is Shachi's son:
whoever sees Him has no peace in his heart.

অসীম গুণের নিধি অপার মহিমা ।
এ তিন ভুবনে নাহি রূপে দিতে সীমা ॥

*asīma guṇera nidhi apāra mahimā |*
*e tina bhubane nāhi rūpe dite sīmā ||*

*Word for word:* asīma guṇera nidhi — treasury of boundless virtues; apāra mahimā — endless glory; e tina bhubane — in these three worlds; nāhi — there is none; rūpe dite sīmā — to set a limit to the beauty

**1.2.** A treasury of boundless virtues, His glory without end;
in the three worlds there is none who could set a limit to His beauty.

খগ মৃগ তরু লতা গুণ শুনি কান্দে ।
রূপে গুণে কুলবতী বুক নাহি বান্ধে ॥

*khaga mṛga taru latā guṇa śuni kānde |*
*rūpe guṇe kulabatī buka nāhi bāndhe ||*

*Word for word:* khaga mṛga taru latā — birds, beasts, trees, creepers; guṇa śuni kānde — weep hearing of the virtues; rūpe guṇe — by the beauty and virtues; kulabatī — noble wives; buka nāhi bāndhe — cannot bind the breast (hold the heart steady)

**1.3.** Birds, beasts, trees and creepers weep hearing of His virtues;
by His beauty and virtues noble wives cannot hold their hearts steady.[^27-2]

ব্রহ্মার দুর্লভ নাম জনে জনে দিয়া ।
বাসুদেব বলে গোরা লইল তরিয়া ॥

*brahmāra durlabha nāma jane jane diyā |*
*bāsudeba bale gorā laila tariyā ||*

*Word for word:* brahmāra durlabha nāma — the name unattainable for Brahma; jane jane diyā — giving to each person; bāsudeba bale — says Vasudeva; gorā — Gora; laila tariyā — has carried across (delivered)

**1.4.** The name unattainable even for Brahma He has given to everyone —
says Vasudeva — so Gora has carried [all across the ocean of births].[^27-3]

[^27-1]: Signature: "Vasudeva." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 249 (printed p. 238), 4th shakha, 18th pallava, section "atha
śrīgauracandrasya rūpa-barṇanaṃ" (description of Gaura's form), no. 43 (mark "॥৪৩॥২১৫১॥"); raga varadi; MS P-R-Sa no. 2258. GPT1 —
p. 117, no. 20 (raga varadi); GPT2 — sec. 3.1, no. 20 (catalogue: VG-183). Majumdar counts PK 2149–2155 among Vasu's nagari
padas. Here the nagari motif is only "noble wives" (1.3); the rest is praise of Gaura, the giver of the name. On nagari-bhava
see the introductory note to the section.
[^27-2]: "Noble wives" (kulabatī) are married women of worthy families who guard the honour of the family; "cannot hold their
hearts steady" (buka nāhi bāndhe, lit. "cannot bind the breast") — lose their peace. A common formula for describing
beauty, as in the padas on Krishna; cf. chapter 23, note 7.
[^27-3]: Hari's name, unattainable even for Brahma, Gaura gives to all without distinction — the main theme of the padas on
Him as the yuga-avatara (cf. chapter 9, no. 1). MS "gha" in 1.2: "i" for "e" ("these [three worlds]"), "rūpera" for
"rūpe" (same sense).

## 2. Vasu Ghosha — "sakhi he oi dekha gorā-kalebare…" (PK 2152)
*Nagari-bhava. Gora's form from head to foot: a face more beautiful than many moons, arms like an elephant's trunk, a
glance quicker than a wagtail, a sandal tilaka, garlands to the knees, a neck like a conch, a broad chest with necklaces,
reddish feet, jewel-like nails; "the Creator fashioned this form to be the ruin of young women." Raga kamoda.*[^27-4]

সখি হে ওই দেখ গোরা-কলেবরে ।
কত চাঁদ জিনি মুখ সুন্দর অধরে ॥

*sakhi he oi dekha gorā-kalebare |*
*kata cām̐da jini mukha sundara adhare ||*

*Word for word:* sakhi he — O friend; oi dekha — look, there; gorā-kalebare — Gora's form (body); kata cām̐da jini — surpassing many moons; mukha — the face; sundara adhare — with lovely lips

**2.1.** Friend, look — there is Gora's form:
His face more beautiful than many moons, His lips lovely.

করিবর-কর জিনি বাহু সুবলনি ।
খঞ্জন জিনিয়া গোরার নয়ন-চাহনি ॥

*karibara-kara jini bāhu subalani |*
*khañjana jiniyā gorāra nayana-cāhani ||*

*Word for word:* karibara-kara jini — surpassing the trunk of the best elephant; bāhu subalani — rounded arms; khañjana jiniyā — surpassing the wagtail; gorāra nayana-cāhani — the glance of Gora's eyes

**2.2.** His rounded arms surpass the trunk of the best of elephants;
the glance of Gora's eyes surpasses the wagtail.[^27-5]

চন্দন-তিলক সাজে সুচারু কপালে ।
আজানুলম্বিত চারু নব নব মালে ॥

*candana-tilaka sāje sucāru kapāle |*
*ājānulambita cāru naba naba māle ||*

*Word for word:* candana-tilaka — a tilaka of sandal; sāje — adorns; sucāru kapāle — on the lovely forehead; ājānulambita — hanging to the knees; cāru naba naba māle — wondrous, ever-fresh garlands

**2.3.** On His lovely forehead is a tilaka of sandal,
wondrous garlands, ever fresh, hang down to His knees.

কম্বু-কণ্ঠ পীন পরিসর হিয়া মাঝে ।
চন্দনে শোভিত কত রত্ন-হার সাজে ॥

*kambu-kaṇṭha pīna parisara hiyā mājhe |*
*candane śobhita kata ratna-hāra sāje ||*

*Word for word:* kambu-kaṇṭha — a neck like a conch; pīna parisara hiyā mājhe — on the mighty, broad chest; candane śobhita — shining with sandal; kata ratna-hāra sāje — many jewelled necklaces adorn

**2.4.** His neck is like a conch; on His broad and mighty chest,
anointed with sandal, are many jewelled necklaces.

রামরম্ভা জিনি উরু অরুণ চরণ ।
নখমণি জিনি ইন্দু পূর্ণ দরপণ ॥

*rāmarambhā jini uru aruṇa caraṇa |*
*nakhamaṇi jini indu pūrṇa darapaṇa ||*

*Word for word:* rāmarambhā jini uru — thighs surpassing plantain stems; aruṇa caraṇa — reddish feet; nakha-maṇi — jewel-like nails; jini indu pūrṇa darapaṇa — surpass the full moon and a mirror

**2.5.** His thighs are lovelier than plantain stems, His feet are reddish;
His jewel-like nails outshine the full moon and a mirror.

বাসুঘোষ বলে গোরা কোথা না আছিল ।
যুবতি বধিতে রূপ বিধি সিরজিল ॥

*bāsughoṣa bale gorā kothā nā āchila |*
*yubati badhite rūpa bidhi sirajila ||*

*Word for word:* bāsughoṣa bale — says Vasu Ghosha; gorā kothā nā āchila — where was Gora not (where has Gora come from?); yubati badhite — to slay young women; rūpa bidhi sirajila — the Creator fashioned the form

**2.6.** Says Vasu Ghosha: where has Gora come from?
The Creator fashioned this form to be the ruin of young women.[^27-6]

[^27-4]: Signature: "Vasu Ghosha." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 250 (printed p. 239), 18th pallava, no. 44 (mark "॥৪৪॥২১৫২॥"); raga kamoda;
MS P-R-Sa no. 2259. GPT1 — p. 117, no. 21 (raga kamoda); GPT2 — sec. 3.1, no. 21 (catalogue: VG-009). On nagari-bhava see the
introductory note to the section.
[^27-5]: The wagtail (khañjana) is an image of lively, quick eyes. MS "ka": "ai," P-R-Sa: "ai" (the same "there," 2.1).
[^27-6]: Lit. "where was Gora not?" — an exclamation of wonder: such a form had never been anywhere. "The ruin of young women"
is a formula of the poetics of beauty (as in the padas on Krishna, "the enchanter of the god of love himself"), not a
description of the Lord's deeds; cf. chapter 23, note 7. MSS "ka," "kha": "shines" (śobhe) for "adorns" (sāje, 2.3; so also
GPT1); "kha": "body" (aṅga, 2.4).

## 3. Vasu Ghosha — "dekha dekha sakhi gorā bara dvijamaṇiyā…" (PK 2153)
*Nagari-bhava. "Look, friend — Gora, the jewel of brahmanas!" With great patience the Creator made this peerless form: arms
to the knees, a hue brighter than gold — is it ketaki, a golden lotus, champaka or a gem? His speech pours nectar; millions
of moons offer themselves for His face; who, having seen Him, could walk away? Raga kanada.*[^27-7]

দেখ দেখ সখি গোরা বর দ্বিজমণিয়া ।
নিরুপম রূপ বিধি নিরমিল
কেমনে ধৈরজ ধরিয়া ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*dekha dekha sakhi gorā bara dvijamaṇiyā |*
*nirupama rūpa bidhi niramila*
*kemane dhairaja dhariyā || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* dekha dekha sakhi — look, look, friend; gorā bara dvijamaṇiyā — Gora, the finest jewel of the twice-born; nirupama rūpa — the peerless form; bidhi niramila — the Creator made; kemane dhairaja dhariyā — with what patience (lit. "how, holding patience")

**3.1.** *(Refrain)* Look, look, friend — Gora, the finest jewel of the twice-born!
With what patience
the Creator made this peerless form![^27-8]

আজানুলম্বিত সুবাহু-যুগল
বরণ কাঞ্চন জিনিয়া ।
কিয়ে সে কেতকী কনক-অম্বুজ
কিয়ে বা চম্পক মণিয়া ॥

*ājānulambita subāhu-yugala*
*baraṇa kāñcana jiniyā |*
*kiye se ketakī kanaka-ambuja*
*kiye bā campaka maṇiyā ||*

*Word for word:* ājānulambita — reaching to the knees; subāhu-yugala — the two lovely arms; baraṇa kāñcana jiniyā — a hue surpassing gold; kiye se ketakī — is it ketaki; kanaka-ambuja — a golden lotus; kiye vā campaka maṇiyā — or champaka, a gem

**3.2.** His two lovely arms reach to the knees,
the hue [of His body] outshines gold.
Is it ketaki, a golden lotus,
or champaka, or a gem?

কিয়ে গোরোচনা কুঙ্কুম-বরণ
জিনি অঙ্গ ঝলমলিয়া ।
মধুর বচনে অমিয়া বরিখে
ত্রিজগত-মন ভুলিয়া ॥

*kiye gorocanā kuṅkuma-baraṇa*
*jini aṅga jhalamaliyā |*
*madhura bacane amiyā barikhe*
*trijagata-mana bhuliyā ||*

*Word for word:* kiye gorocanā — is it gorochana; kuṅkuma-baraṇa — of kunkuma hue; jini — surpassing; aṅga jhalamaliyā — the body shines; madhura bacane — with sweet words; amiyā barikhe — pours nectar; tri-jagata-mana bhuliyā — enchanting the mind of the three worlds

**3.3.** Is its hue that of gorochana or kunkuma? —
no, the radiant body surpasses them.
With sweet words He pours down nectar,
and the mind of the three worlds is enchanted.[^27-9]

কত কোটি চাঁদ বদন নিছনি
নখ-চাঁদে পড়ে গলিয়া ।
বাসুঘোষে কহে গৌরাঙ্গ-বদন
কে দেখি আসিবে চলিয়া ॥

*kata koṭi cām̐da badana nichani*
*nakha-cām̐de paṛe galiyā |*
*bāsughoṣe kahe gaurāṅga-badana*
*ke dekhi āsibe caliyā ||*

*Word for word:* kata koṭi cām̐da — many millions of moons; badana nichani — offer themselves (nichani) for the face; nakha-cām̐de paṛe galiyā — melt, falling at the moons of the nails; bāsughoṣe kahe — says Vasu Ghosha; gaurāṅga-badana — Gauranga's face; ke dekhi āsibe caliyā — who, having seen, will walk away

**3.4.** Millions of moons offer themselves for His face
and melt, falling at the moons of His nails.[^27-10]
Says Vasu Ghosha: who, having seen Gauranga's face,
could walk away?

[^27-7]: Signature: "Vasu Ghosha." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 250 (printed p. 239), 18th pallava, no. 45 (mark "॥৪৫॥২১৫৩॥"); raga kanada;
MS P-R-Sa no. 2260 (the word "finest," bara, is absent from it). GPT1 — p. 122, no. 32 (raga kalyani); GPT2 — sec. 3.1,
no. 32 (catalogue: VG-127; row VG-126 has the same PK number). On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section.
[^27-8]: "Jewel of the twice-born" (dvijamaṇi) — the best of brahmanas. The words "kemane dhairaja dhariyā" can also be taken as
"how can one keep one's composure?"; following the structure of the sentence ("the Creator made… how, summoning patience")
we translate it as wonder at the Creator's painstaking work.
[^27-9]: Ketaki and champaka are golden flowers; gorochana is a yellow pigment, kunkuma is saffron: all these are customary
comparisons for Gaura's golden body.
[^27-10]: "Offer themselves" (nichani) — a rite in which something precious is waved around the beloved to ward off misfortune
and then given away (glossary): the moons are but a ransom for His face; "the moons of His nails" are His toenails, shining
like moons.

## 4. Vasu Ghosha — "o nā ke bala go sajani…" (PK 2154)
*Nagari-bhava. "Tell me, friend, who is this?" — a face lovelier than moons, a hue of gold and gem; the moon and the red
lotus hide in shame before His nails, palms and feet; at the beauty of His brows Madana throws away his bow; a sidelong
glance mixed with a smile strikes everyone; "beware — He has lit up the whole world." Raga (illegible in PK; in GPT1
varadi).*[^27-11]

ও না কে বল গো সজনি ।
কত চাঁদ জিনি সুন্দর মুখানি
বরণ কাঞ্চন মণি ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*o nā ke bala go sajani |*
*kata cām̐da jini sundara mukhāni*
*baraṇa kāñcana maṇi || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* o nā ke — who is that; bala go sajani — tell me, friend; kata cām̐da jini — surpassing many moons; sundara mukhāni — the lovely face; baraṇa kāñcana maṇi — the hue is gold and gem

**4.1.** *(Refrain)* Tell me, friend, who is this?
His lovely face is lovelier than many moons,
His hue is like gold and gem.

করি-কর জিনি বাহুর বলনি
আজানুলম্বিত সাজে ।
নখ কর পদ বিধু কোকনদ
হেরি লুকাইল লাজে ॥

*kari-kara jini bāhura balani*
*ājānulambita sāje |*
*nakha kara pada bidhu kokanada*
*heri lukāila lāje ||*

*Word for word:* kari-kara jini — surpassing an elephant's trunk; bāhura balani — the roundness of the arms; ājānulambita sāje — reaching to the knees, it is lovely; nakha kara pada — nails, palms, feet; bidhu kokanada — the moon and the red lotus; heri — seeing; lukāila lāje — hid in shame

**4.2.** The roundness of His arms surpasses an elephant's trunk,
reaching to His knees — how lovely they are!
The moon and the red lotus, seeing His nails, palms and feet,
have hidden themselves in shame.[^27-12]

ভাঙ-যুগ বর দেখিতে সুন্দর
মদনে তেজয়ে ধনু ।
তেরছ চাহিয়া হাসি মিশাইয়া
হানয়ে সভার তনু ॥

*bhāṅa-yuga bara dekhite sundara*
*madane tejaye dhanu |*
*teracha cāhiyā hāsi miśāiyā*
*hānaye sabhāra tanu ||*

*Word for word:* bhāṅa-yuga bara — the two fine arches of the brows; dekhite sundara — lovely to see; madane tejaye dhanu — Madana gives up his bow; terachha cāhiyā — glancing sidelong; hāsi miśāiyā — mixing in a smile; hānaye sabhāra tanu — strikes everyone (everyone's body)

**4.3.** The two arches of His brows are so lovely
that Madana throws away his bow;
He casts a sidelong glance, mixing it with a smile —
and strikes everyone.[^27-13]

কটিতে বসন অরুণ-বরণ
গলে দোলে বন-মালা ।
বাসুঘোষ ভণে হও সাবধানে
জগত কর্যাছে আলা ॥

*kaṭite basana aruṇa-baraṇa*
*gale dole bana-mālā |*
*bāsughoṣa bhaṇe hao sābadhāne*
*jagata karyāche ālā ||*

*Word for word:* kaṭite basana — at the waist a cloth; aruṇa-baraṇa — of the colour of dawn; gale dole bana-mālā — on the neck sways a garland of forest flowers; bāsughoṣa bhaṇe — says Vasu Ghosha; hao sābadhāne — beware; jagata karyāche ālā — He has lit up the world

**4.4.** At His waist is a cloth the colour of dawn,
on His neck sways a garland of forest flowers.
Says Vasu Ghosha: beware —
He has lit up the whole world!

[^27-11]: Signature: "Vasu Ghosha." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 250 (printed p. 239), 18th pallava, no. 46 (mark "॥৪৬॥২১৫৪॥"); MS P-R-Sa
no. 2261; the name of the raga is damaged in the scan. GPT1 — p. 122, no. 33 (raga varadi); GPT2 — sec. 3.1, no. 33
(catalogue: VG-010). On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section.
[^27-12]: Nails are compared to the moon, palms and feet to the red lotus (kokanada); here the compared is so beautiful that the
objects of comparison hide in shame. MSS "ka," "gha," "cha," P-R-Sa: "of the best elephant" (karibara); "kha": "the trunk of
the best elephant" (karibara-kara); "kha": "roundness" in the form subalani.
[^27-13]: Madana (Kamadeva) throws away his bow because Gaura's brows are a bow lovelier than his own; "strikes" (hānaye)
continues the same image: the glance is an arrow. Cf. note 6.

## 5. Vasu Ghosha — "dekhaha nāgara nadiyāra…" (PK 2155)
*Nagari-bhava. "Behold the nagara of Nadia!" — His gait is sweeter than the step of a royal elephant; bee-like devotees fly
to the fragrance of His lotus feet, and the whole world, drunk with honey, loses the directions; full of rasa, He smiles
slightly, and at the arrow from the corner of His eye millions of Kamadevas swoon; the world is full of cries of "Glory to
Gora!" Raga kamoda.*[^27-14]

দেখহ নাগর নদিয়ার ।
গজবর-গতি জিতি গমন সুমাধুরি
অপরূপ গোরা দ্বিজরায় ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*dekhaha nāgara nadiyāra |*
*gajabara-gati jiti gamana sumādhuri*
*aparūpa gorā dvijarāya || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* dekhaha — behold; nāgara nadiyāra — the nagara of Nadia; gajabara-gati jiti — surpassing the gait of the best of elephants; gamana sumādhuri — a sweet gait; aparūpa gorā — wondrous Gora; dvija-rāya — king of the twice-born

**5.1.** *(Refrain)* Behold the nagara of Nadia![^27-15]
His gait in sweetness has surpassed the step of the best of elephants —
wondrous Gora, king of the twice-born.

চরণ কমল যেন ভকত ভ্রমরগণ
পরিমলে চৌদিগে ধায় ।
মধু-মদে মাতল সব মহী-মণ্ডল
দিগ বিদিগ নাহি পায় ॥

*caraṇa kamala yena bhakata bhramaragaṇa*
*parimale caudige dhāya |*
*madhu-made mātala saba mahī-maṇḍala*
*diga bidiga nāhi pāya ||*

*Word for word:* caraṇa kamala yena — the feet like lotuses; bhakata bhramara-gaṇa — the devotees are bees; parimale caudige dhāya — run from all sides to the fragrance; madhu-made mātala — drunk with honey; saba mahī-maṇḍala — the whole circle of the earth; diga bidiga nāhi pāya — cannot find the directions

**5.2.** His feet are like lotuses, and the devotees, like bees,
fly from all sides to their fragrance;
drunk with honey, the whole circle of the earth
cannot tell the directions apart.

রস-ভরে গর গর অধর মনোহর
ঈষত হাসিয়া ঘন চায় ।
অপাঙ্গ-ইঙ্গিত বর নয়ান-কোণের শর
কত কোটি কাম মুরছায় ॥

*rasa-bhare gara gara adhara manohara*
*īṣata hāsiyā ghana cāya |*
*apāṅga-iṅgita bara nayāna-koṇera śara*
*kata koṭi kāma murachāya ||*

*Word for word:* rasa-bhare gara gara — brimming with rasa; adhara manohara — enchanting lips; īṣata hāsiyā — smiling slightly; ghana cāya — glances again and again; apāṅga-iṅgita bara — the fine sign from the corner of the eye; nayāna-koṇera śara — the arrow from the corner of the eyes; kata koṭi kāma murachāya — many millions of Kamadevas swoon

**5.3.** Brimming with rasa, with enchanting lips,
He smiles slightly and glances again and again;
a sign from the corner of His eye, an arrow from the corner of His eyes —
and millions of Kamadevas fall senseless.

আভরণ বহু মণি বসন অরুণ জিনি
বাজন-নূপুর রাঙ্গা পায় ।
জগ ভরি জয় ধ্বনি জয় গোরা দ্বিজমণি
বাসুদেব ঘোষে গুণ গায় ॥

*ābharaṇa bahu maṇi basana aruṇa jini*
*bājana-nūpura rāṅgā pāya |*
*jaga bhari jaya dhvani jaya gorā dvijamaṇi*
*bāsudeba ghoṣe guṇa gāya ||*

*Word for word:* ābharaṇa bahu maṇi — ornaments of many gems; basana aruṇa jini — a cloth outshining the dawn; bājana-nūpura — jingling ankle bells; rāṅgā pāya — on the reddish feet; jaga bhari jaya dhvani — the world is full of cries of "Jaya!"; jaya gorā dvijamaṇi — glory to Gora, the jewel of the twice-born; bāsudeba ghoṣe guṇa gāya — Vasudeva Ghosha sings of the virtues

**5.4.** His ornaments are many gems, His cloth outshines the dawn,
ankle bells jingle on His reddish feet.
The world is full of cries: "Glory to Gora, the jewel of the twice-born!" —
so sings of His virtues Vasudeva Ghosha.[^27-16]

[^27-14]: Signature: "Vasudeva Ghosha." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 251 (printed p. 240), 18th pallava, no. 47 (mark "॥৪৭॥২১৫৫॥"); raga
kamoda; MS P-R-Sa no. 2262. GPT1 — p. 122, no. 34 (raga kamoda; "nadīyāya" — "in Nadia"); GPT2 — sec. 3.1, no. 34 (catalogue:
VG-011). On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section.
[^27-15]: "Nagara" (nāgara) — a townsman, a gallant, in poetry the beloved hero; a word by which Krishna is glorified. Why the
tradition does not so call Gaura — see the introductory note. Here, apart from the name "nagara," the pada is a praise of the
Lord's form; the "bee-like devotees" at His feet and the Kamadevas losing consciousness are images of His divine
attractiveness.
[^27-16]: P-R-Sa: "slow" (sumanthara) for "sweet" (sumādhuri, 5.1). MS "ka" and GPT1: "the world's cry of victory" (jagata
bijaya) for "the world is full of cries" (jaga bhari jaya, 5.4).

## 6. Vasu Ghosha — "āre mora rasamaya gaurakiśora…" (PK 2211)
*Nagari-bhava. Praise of the young Gaura, full of rasa: in the three worlds there is no such nagara; noble wives are
enchanted by His beauty, trees thrill, stones melt, birds and beasts weep, the townswomen lose their peace; He stirs the
minds of gods and sages — Gora, the saviour of the fallen. In PK it stands in the pallava "Gaurachandra — another way."
Raga varadi.*[^27-17]

আরে মোর রসময় গৌরকিশোর ।
এ তিন ভুবনে নাহি এমন নাগর ॥

*āre mora rasamaya gaurakiśora |*
*e tina bhubane nāhi emana nāgara ||*

*Word for word:* āre mora — O my; rasamaya gaurakiśora — young Gaura, full of rasa; e tina bhubane — in these three worlds; nāhi emana nāgara — there is no such nagara

**6.1.** O my young Gaura, full of rasa!
In all three worlds there is no such nagara.

কুলবতী সতী রূপ দেখিয়া মোহিত ।
গুণ শুনি তরুলতা হয় পুলকিত ॥

*kulabatī satī rūpa dekhiyā mohita |*
*guṇa śuni tarulatā haya pulakita ||*

*Word for word:* kulabatī satī — chaste noble wives; rūpa dekhiyā mohita — are enchanted seeing the form; guṇa śuni — hearing of the virtues; tarulatā — trees and creepers; haya pulakita — thrill with joy

**6.2.** Chaste wives of noble families, seeing His beauty, are enchanted;
hearing of His virtues, trees and creepers thrill with joy.

শিলা তরু গলি যায় খগ মৃগ কান্দে ।
নগরের নাগরী বুক স্থির নাহি বান্ধে ॥

*śilā taru gali yāya khaga mṛga kānde |*
*nagarera nāgarī buka sthira nāhi bāndhe ||*

*Word for word:* śilā taru gali yāya — stones and trees melt; khaga mṛga kānde — birds and beasts weep; nagarera nāgarī — the townswomen of the town; buka sthira nāhi bāndhe — cannot keep the heart at rest

**6.3.** Stones and trees melt, birds and beasts weep;
the townswomen cannot keep their hearts at rest.

সুর-সিদ্ধ-মুনির মন করে উচাটন ।
বাসুঘোষ কহে গোরা পতিত-পাবন ॥

*sura-siddha-munira mana kare ucāṭana |*
*bāsughoṣa kahe gorā patita-pābana ||*

*Word for word:* sura-siddha-munira mana — the minds of gods, siddhas and sages; kare ucāṭana — He stirs; bāsughoṣa kahe — says Vasu Ghosha; gorā patita-pābana — Gora is the saviour of the fallen

**6.4.** He stirs the minds of gods, siddhas and sages.
Says Vasu Ghosha: Gora is the saviour of the fallen.[^27-18]

[^27-17]: Signature: "Vasu Ghosha." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 272 (printed p. 261), 20th pallava, no. 28 (mark "॥২৮॥২২১১॥"); raga varadi;
MS P-R-Sa no. 2319. The neighbouring pada of the same pallava is Vasu's PK 2210 (chapter 8, no. 2). GPT1 — p. 44, no. 58
(raga varadi); GPT2 — sec. 1.3 (catalogue: VG-132). Majumdar (1961 ed.) cites this pada as an example of Vasu calling Gaura
"nagara" following Narahari Sarakara. On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section.
[^27-18]: The pada joins nagari motifs (6.1, 6.3) with praise of the Lord before whom stones melt and gods and sages tremble —
Bhagavan, who saves the fallen.

## 7. Vasu Ghosha — "madanamohana gaurāṅga-badana…" (PK 2149)
*Nagari-bhava. A townswoman tells her friend: having seen Gauranga's face, which enchants Madana himself, she has lost
herself; this is the former dark Kanu become golden — otherwise how could He have stolen her heart? The young wives of
Nadia drown in love, in every house there is weeping; she will cast the rites of her family into the waters of the
Suradhuni and serve Gora. Raga tudi.*[^27-19]

মদনমোহন গৌরাঙ্গ-বদন
