রূপ হেরি কি না হৈল মোরে ।
সোণার বরণ তনু এই ছিল কালা কানু
নহিলে কি মন চুরি করে ॥

*madanamohana gaurāṅga-badana*
*rūpa heri ki nā haila more |*
*soṇāra baraṇa tanu ei chila kālā kānu*
*nahile ki mana curi kare ||*

*Word for word:* madana-mohana — enchanting Madana; gaurāṅga-badana — Gauranga's face; rūpa heri — seeing the form; ki nā haila more — what has not befallen me; soṇāra baraṇa tanu — a body the colour of gold; ei chila kālā kānu — this was dark Kanu; nahile — otherwise; ki mana curi kare — would He steal the heart

**7.1.** Gauranga's face enchants Madana himself:
having seen this form, what has not befallen me!
His body is the colour of gold — [yet once] this was dark Kanu;
otherwise would He have stolen [so] my heart?[^27-20]

রসের পরাণ যার কুল কি করিবে তার
নদীয়া নগরে হেন জনা ।
কি ছার দারুণ মতি মজিল যুবতী সতী
ঘরে ঘরে প্রেমের কান্দনা ॥

*rasera parāṇa yāra kula ki karibe tāra*
*nadīyā nagare hena janā |*
*ki chāra dāruṇa mati majila yubatī satī*
*ghare ghare premera kāndanā ||*

*Word for word:* rasera parāṇa yāra — whose life is rasa; kula ki karibe tāra — what will family do to her; nadīyā nagare — in the town of Nadia; hena janā — such a person; ki chāra dāruṇa mati — what a bitter, cruel lot; majila yubatī satī — the young chaste wives have drowned; ghare ghare premera kāndanā — in every house the weeping of love

**7.2.** To one whose life is rasa, what is family?
Such is [He] — in the town of Nadia!
What a bitter, cruel lot: the young chaste wives have drowned,
in every house there is the weeping of love.[^27-21]

নয়ন-কমল নব অরুণ পরাভব
ধারা বহে বুক বাহিয়া ।
আহা মরি মরি সই মরম তোমারে কই
জীব না গো গোরা না দেখিয়া ॥

*nayana-kamala naba aruṇa parābhaba*
*dhārā bahe buka bāhiyā |*
*āhā mari mari sai marama tomāre kai*
*jība nā go gorā nā dekhiyā ||*

*Word for word:* nayana-kamala — lotus eyes; naba aruṇa parābhaba — defeat the fresh dawn (are redder than it); dhārā bahe buka bāhiyā — streams run down the breast; āhā mari mari sai — ah, I die, I die, friend; marama tomāre kai — I tell you my heart; jība nā go — I will not live; gorā nā dekhiyā — without seeing Gora

**7.3.** [My] lotus eyes are redder than the fresh dawn,
streams [of tears] run down my breast.
Ah, I am dying, dying, friend — to you I open my heart:
I will not live without seeing Gora.

হিয়ায় প্রেমের শর তনু কৈল জর জর
প্রবোধ না মানে মোর প্রাণী ।
সুরধুনী-তীরে যাঞা ভাসাইব কুল-ক্রিয়া
ভজিব সে গোরা গুণমণি ॥

*hiyāya premera śara tanu kaila jara jara*
*prabodha nā māne mora prāṇī |*
*suradhunī-tīre yāñā bhāsāiba kula-kriyā*
*bhajiba se gorā guṇamaṇi ||*

*Word for word:* hiyāya premera śara — the arrow of love in the heart; tanu kaila jara jara — has wounded the body; prabodha nā māne — accepts no consolation; mora prāṇī — my soul; suradhunī-tīre yāñā — going to the bank of the Suradhuni; bhāsāiba kula-kriyā — I will float away the family's rites; bhajiba — I will serve; se gorā guṇa-maṇi — that Gora, the jewel of virtues

**7.4.** The arrow of love in my heart has wounded all my body,
my soul accepts no consolation.
I will go to the bank of the Suradhuni and cast my family's rites into its waters —
I will serve Gora, the jewel of virtues.[^27-22]

পূরবে শুনিনু যত সেই সব অভিমত
এবে ভেল কাল-তনু গোরা ।
বাসুদেব ঘোষের বাণী রসিক নাগর জানি
নহিলে কি গোপীর মন-চোরা ॥

*pūrabe śuninu yata sei saba abhimata*
*ebe bhela kāla-tanu gorā |*
*bāsudeba ghoṣera bāṇī rasika nāgara jāni*
*nahile ki gopīra mana-corā ||*

*Word for word:* pūrabe śuninu yata — all that I heard before; sei saba abhimata — all that is so (as held); ebe bhela — now has become; kāla-tanu gorā — the dark-bodied one — Gora (fair); bāsudeba ghoṣera bāṇī — the word of Vasudeva Ghosha; rasika nāgara jāni — know [Him] as the rasika-nagara; nahile — otherwise; ki gopīra mana-corā — would He be the stealer of the gopis' hearts

**7.5.** All that I heard before is just so:
[He who was] dark-bodied has now become Gora.
The word of Vasudeva Ghosha: know — He is the rasika-nagara;
otherwise would He be the stealer of the gopis' hearts?[^27-23]

[^27-19]: Signature: "Vasudeva Ghosha." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 249 (printed p. 238), 18th pallava, no. 41 (mark "॥৪১॥২১৪৯॥"); raga tudi;
MS P-R-Sa no. 2256. GPT1 — p. 160, no. 8 (raga tudi); GPT2 — sec. 3.2, no. 8 (catalogue: VG-013). A witness is the *Bhakti-ratnakara*, 12th wave (1913 ed., p. 910, scan PDF
p. 918): in the cycle of the words of the women of Nadia that Narahari Chakravarti cites while describing the places of Navadvipa (chapter 29,
note 1), with Vasudeva Ghosha's signature, raga deshapala, beginning with the words "rūpa heri…"; in 7.2 it reads "rahibe" (as MSS "kha," "cha").
On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section.
[^27-20]: Gaura is Krishna (Kanu) Himself, who has taken Radha's golden luster (CC Adi 1.5); the townswoman recognizes in Him the
"stealer of hearts" of Vraja. This affirmation of the identity of Gaura and Krishna is the main theological content of the
pada (cf. 7.5).
[^27-21]: The sense of 7.2: before such a Gaura the bonds of family are powerless. MS "ka": "will say" (kahibe), "kha," "cha":
"will remain" (rahibe) for "will do" (karibe). P-R-Sa: "down face and breast" (mukha buka, 7.3; so also GPT1); "that" (se) for
the particle "go" (7.3).
[^27-22]: "I will cast my family's rites into the waters" — I will abandon the duty and honour of my family: a nagari motif
(introductory note). The words of love and service (bhajiba) are spoken by a townswoman; the translation does not soften
them, nor does it add worldly shades.
[^27-23]: "The stealer of the gopis' hearts" is a name of Krishna; Vasu again bears witness: the golden Gaura is the same
Krishna. "Rasika-nagara" — the connoisseur and enjoyer of rasa; in Krishna-lila this is Krishna with the gopis. The tradition
does not accept the application of this name to Gaura (introductory note).

## 8. Vasu Ghosha — "ki kahaba aparūpa gaura kiśora…" (PK 2150)
*Nagari-bhava. "What can I say of the wondrous young Gaura?" — with a sign from the corner of His eye He has stolen her
life; His sidelong glance is a calamity: the ruin of the townswomen has risen in the town; she who sees Him cannot forget,
the noble wife leaves her home; love for Gora is a pain of the heart. Raga suhini.*[^27-24]

কি কহব অপরূপ গৌর কিশোর ।
অপাঙ্গ-ইঙ্গিতে প্রাণ হরি নিল মোর ॥

*ki kahaba aparūpa gaura kiśora |*
*apāṅga-iṅgite prāṇa hari nila mora ||*

*Word for word:* ki kahaba — what shall I say; aparūpa gaura kiśora — of the wondrous young Gaura; apāṅga-iṅgite — with a sign from the corner of the eye; prāṇa hari nila mora — has stolen my life

**8.1.** What can I say of the wondrous young Gaura?
With a sign from the corner of His eye He has stolen my life.

তেরছ চাহনি তার বড়ই জঞ্জাল ।
নগরে উদয় ভেল নাগরীর কাল ॥

*teracha cāhani tāra baṛai jañjāla |*
*nagare udaya bhela nāgarīra kāla ||*

*Word for word:* terachha cāhani tāra — His sidelong glance; baṛai jañjāla — a real calamity; nagare udaya bhela — has risen in the town; nāgarīra kāla — the doom of the townswomen

**8.2.** His sidelong glance is a real calamity:
the ruin of the townswomen has risen in the town.

যেবা ধনী দেখে তারে পাসরিতে নারে ।
কুল ছাড়ে কুলবতী নাহি রহে ঘরে ॥

*yebā dhanī dekhe tāre pāsarite nāre |*
*kula chāṛe kulabatī nāhi rahe ghare ||*

*Word for word:* yebā dhanī dekhe tāre — whatever woman sees Him; pāsarite nāre — cannot forget; kula chāṛe kulabatī — the noble wife leaves her family; nāhi rahe ghare — does not stay at home

**8.3.** Whatever woman sees Him cannot forget Him;
the noble wife leaves her family and does not stay at home.

বাসুদেব ঘোষ কহে শুন মোর কথা ।
গোরার পিরিতি খানি মরমের বেথা ॥

*bāsudeba ghoṣa kahe śuna mora kathā |*
*gorāra piriti khāni maramera bethā ||*

*Word for word:* bāsudeba ghoṣa kahe — says Vasudeva Ghosha; śuna mora kathā — listen to my words; gorāra piriti khāni — love for Gora; maramera bethā — a pain deep in the heart

**8.4.** Says Vasudeva Ghosha: listen to my words —
love for Gora is a pain deep in the heart.

[^27-24]: Signature: "Vasudeva Ghosha." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 249 (printed p. 238), 18th pallava, no. 42 (mark "॥৪২॥২১৫০॥"); raga
suhini; MS P-R-Sa no. 2257. GPT1 — p. 160, no. 9 (raga suhini); GPT2 — sec. 3.2, no. 9 (catalogue: VG-014). On nagari-bhava
see the introductory note to the section; "the ruin of the townswomen" is a formula of the power of beauty (cf. note 6).

## 9. Vasu Ghosha — "āra eka dina gaurāṅgasundara…" (PK 2169)
*Nagari-bhava. A townswoman tells: on another day she saw the beautiful Gauranga bathing at the ghat — a face lovelier than
millions of moons, lotus eyes, brows a bow, glances the arrows of Kama; drops of water on His curls like a string of pearls
in a cloud, on His body like pearls on gold; He wrung out His curls and put on a red cloth — "I cannot stay at home." In PK
it is Vasu's first pada in the pallava "Gauranga's form: the words of the nagaris and others." Raga varadi.*[^27-25]

আর এক দিন গৌরাঙ্গসুন্দর
নাহিতে দেখিলুঁ ঘাটে ।
কোটি চাঁদ জিনি বদন সুন্দর
দেখিয়া পরাণ ফাটে ॥

*āra eka dina gaurāṅgasundara*
*nāhite dekhilum̐ ghāṭe |*
*koṭi cām̐da jini badana sundara*
*dekhiyā parāṇa phāṭe ||*

*Word for word:* āra eka dina — on another day; gaurāṅga-sundara — the beautiful Gauranga; nāhite dekhilum̐ ghāṭe — I saw bathing at the ghat; koṭi cām̐da jini — surpassing millions of moons; badana sundara — the lovely face; dekhiyā parāṇa phāṭe — seeing it, the heart breaks

**9.1.** On another day I saw the beautiful Gauranga —
He was bathing at the ghat.
His face lovelier than millions of moons —
seeing it, the heart breaks.

অঙ্গ ঢল ঢল কনক-কষিল
অমল কমল-আঁখি ।
নয়ানের শর ভাঙ ধনুবর
বিন্ধয়ে কাম-ধানুকী ॥

*aṅga ḍhala ḍhala kanaka-kaṣila*
*amala kamala-ām̐khi |*
*nayānera śara bhāṅa dhanubara*
*bindhaye kāma-dhānukī ||*

*Word for word:* aṅga ḍhala ḍhala — the body tender and radiant; kanaka-kaṣila — like tested gold; amala kamala-ām̐khi — eyes pure lotuses; nayānera śara — the arrows of the eyes; bhāṅa dhanu-bara — the brows a fine bow; bindhaye kāma-dhānukī — the archer Kama pierces

**9.2.** His body tender and radiant like tested gold,
His eyes pure lotuses;
the glances are arrows, the arches of the brows a bow:
so the archer Kama strikes.[^27-26]

কুটিল কুন্তল তাহে বিন্দু জল
মেঘে মুকুতার দাম ।
জল-বিন্দু তনু হেমে মোতি জনু
হেরিয়া মুরছে কাম ॥

*kuṭila kuntala tāhe bindu jala*
*meghe mukutāra dāma |*
*jala-bindu tanu heme moti janu*
*heriyā murache kāma ||*

*Word for word:* kuṭila kuntala — curling locks; tāhe bindu jala — on them drops of water; meghe mukutāra dāma — a string of pearls in a cloud; jala-bindu tanu — drops on the body; heme moti janu — like pearls on gold; heriyā murache kāma — seeing it, Kama swoons

**9.3.** His curling locks, and on them drops of water:
like a string of pearls in a cloud;
the drops on His body are like pearls on gold;
seeing this, Kama swoons.

মোছে সব অঙ্গ নিঙ্গারি কুন্তল
অরুণ বসন পরে ।
বাসুঘোষে কয় হেন মনে লয়
রহিতে নারিব ঘরে ॥

*moche saba aṅga niṅgāri kuntala*
*aruṇa basana pare |*
*bāsughoṣe kaya hena mane laya*
*rahite nāriba ghare ||*

*Word for word:* mochhe saba aṅga — wipes the whole body; niṅgāri kuntala — wringing out the curls; aruṇa basana pare — puts on a red cloth; bāsughoṣe kaya — says Vasu Ghosha; hena mane laya — so it seems to me; rahite nāriba ghare — I cannot stay at home

**9.4.** He wipes His whole body, wrings out His curls,
puts on a red cloth.
Says Vasu Ghosha: so it seems to me —
I cannot stay at home.[^27-27]

[^27-25]: Signature: "Vasu Ghosha." PK: vol. 3, PDF pp. 257–258 (printed pp. 246–247), 19th pallava, section "atha śrīgaurāṅgasya
rūpa-barṇanaṃ nāgarīgaṇādyuktiḥ" (description of Gauranga's form: the words of the nagaris and others), no. 2 (mark "॥২॥২১৬৯॥");
raga varadi; MSS P-R-Sa no. 2276 and P-R no. 61. GPT1 — p. 160, no. 10 (raga varadi); GPT2 — sec. 3.2, no. 10 (catalogue:
VG-015). The beginning of 9.2 is illegible in the PK scan — restored from GPT1 ("aṅga ḍhala ḍhala"). On nagari-bhava see the
introductory note to the section.
[^27-26]: The Lord bathed in the Ganga daily — the *Chaitanya-bhagavata* too tells of His baths at the ghats of Navadvipa; here
it is only an occasion to describe His beauty. Kamadeva is "the archer" with flower arrows (cf. note 13).
[^27-27]: MSS "ka," "kha," "gha," "cha," P-R-Sa and GPT1: "she cannot stay at home" (nāribe). In MS P-R 9.3 differs: "a cloud
flows over it (the cloud of hair)" (bahe jaladhara), "as if" (yena), "pearls on all His limbs" (sakala aṅge mukutāra phala).

## 10. Vasu Ghosha — "eka dina ghāṭe jale giyāchilāma…" (PK 2171)
*Nagari-bhava. "One day I went to the ghat for water — and what beauty of Gora I saw!" A body like tested gold, the Lord
absorbed in the rasa of prema; a lovely face, signs from the corners of the eyes, a sandal tilaka — like the moon among the
stars; smiling, He speaks half-words; who, seeing such a nagara, can keep composure? Raga dhanashi.*[^27-28]

এক দিন ঘাটে জলে গিয়াছিলাম
কি রূপ দেখিলুঁ গোরা ।
কনক কষিল অঙ্গ নিরমল
প্রেম-রসে পহু ভোরা ॥

*eka dina ghāṭe jale giyāchilāma*
*ki rūpa dekhilum̐ gorā |*
*kanaka kaṣila aṅga niramala*
*prema-rase pahu bhorā ||*

*Word for word:* eka dina ghāṭe — one day to the ghat; jale giyāchilāma — I went for water; ki rūpa dekhilum̐ gorā — what beauty of Gora I saw; kanaka kaṣila — tested gold; aṅga niramala — the pure body; prema-rase pahu bhorā — the Lord absorbed in the rasa of prema

**10.1.** One day I went to the ghat for water —
what beauty of Gora I saw!
His pure body like tested gold;
the Lord was absorbed in the rasa of prema.

সুন্দর বদন মদনমোহন
অপাঙ্গ-ইঙ্গিত-ছটা ।
সুচারু কপোল চন্দন-তিলক
তারা সনে বিধু-ঘটা ॥

*sundara badana madanamohana*
*apāṅga-iṅgita-chaṭā |*
*sucāru kapola candana-tilaka*
*tārā sane bidhu-ghaṭā ||*

*Word for word:* sundara badana — the lovely face; madana-mohana — enchanting Madana; apāṅga-iṅgita-chaṭā — the radiance of signs from the corners of the eyes; sucāru kapola — fair cheeks; candana-tilaka — a sandal tilaka; tārā sane bidhu-ghaṭā — the moon with the stars

**10.2.** A lovely face, enchanting Madana,
the radiance of signs from the corners of His eyes;
fair cheeks, a sandal tilaka —
like the moon surrounded by stars.[^27-29]

মধুর অধরে ঈষত হাসিয়া
বলে আধ আধ বাণী ।
হাসিতে খসয়ে মণি মোতি-বর
দেখিতে ভুলয়ে প্রাণী ॥

*madhura adhare īṣata hāsiyā*
*bale ādha ādha bāṇī |*
*hāsite khasaye maṇi moti-bara*
*dekhite bhulaye prāṇī ||*

*Word for word:* madhura adhare — with sweet lips; īṣata hāsiyā — smiling slightly; bale ādha ādha bāṇī — speaks half-words; hāsite khasaye — with the smile there fall; maṇi moti-bara — gems and the finest pearls; dekhite bhulaye prāṇī — seeing it, a living being forgets itself

**10.3.** Smiling slightly with sweet lips,
He speaks half-words;
with His smile gems and the finest pearls seem to fall —
seeing this, every living being forgets itself.

বাসুঘোষে কহে এমন নাগর
দেখি কে ধৈরজ ধরে ।
ধন্য সে যুবতী ও রূপ দেখিয়া
কেমনে আছয়ে ঘরে ॥

*bāsughoṣe kahe emana nāgara*
*dekhi ke dhairaja dhare |*
*dhanya se yubatī o rūpa dekhiyā*
*kemane āchaye ghare ||*

*Word for word:* bāsughoṣe kahe — says Vasu Ghosha; emana nāgara dekhi — seeing such a nagara; ke dhairaja dhare — who keeps composure; dhanya se yubatī — remarkable (blessed) is that young woman; o rūpa dekhiyā — having seen that form; kemane āchaye ghare — how does she stay at home

**10.4.** Says Vasu Ghosha: who, seeing such a nagara,
can keep composure?
Remarkable is that young woman who, having seen this form,
can still stay at home![^27-30]

[^27-28]: Signature: "Vasu Ghosha." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 258 (printed p. 247), 19th pallava, no. 4 (mark "॥৪॥২১৭১॥"); raga dhanashi;
MS P-R-Sa no. 2279. Between PK 2169 and 2171 stands PK 2170, a pada of Nayanananda (chapter 28). GPT1 — pp. 160–161, no. 11
(raga dhanashi); GPT2 — sec. 3.2, no. 11 (catalogue: VG-016). On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section.
[^27-29]: GPT1: "on the fair forehead" (sucāru kapāle) for "fair cheeks" (sucāru kapola). "The Lord was absorbed in the rasa of
prema" (10.1) — Gaura in the mood of a devotee: the townswoman sees Him intoxicated with love of God.
[^27-30]: "Remarkable" (dhanya, lit. "blessed") — with bitter irony: it is impossible, having seen Him, to stay at home.

## 11. Vasu Ghosha — "yakhana dekhilum̐ gorācām̐de…" (PK 2172)
*Nagari-bhava. "As soon as I saw Gorachand — I fell into the snare of love": she gave Him body and soul, bade farewell to
fear for her family; without Gora she cannot live, Gauranga has become the treasure of her life. Raga
pathamanjari.*[^27-31]

যখন দেখিলুঁ গোরাচাঁদে ।
তখনি পড়িলুঁ প্রেম-ফাঁদে ॥

*yakhana dekhilum̐ gorācām̐de |*
*takhani paṛilum̐ prema-phām̐de ||*

*Word for word:* yakhana dekhilum̐ gorācām̐de — when I saw Gorachand; takhani paṛilum̐ prema-phām̐de — at once I fell into the snare of love

**11.1.** As soon as I saw Gorachand —
at once I fell into the snare of love.

তনু মন তাহারে সোঁপিলুঁ ।
কুল-ভয়ে তিলাঞ্জলি দিলুঁ ॥

*tanu mana tāhāre som̐pilum̐ |*
*kula-bhaye tilāñjali dilum̐ ||*

*Word for word:* tanu mana tāhāre som̐pilum̐ — body and mind I gave to Him; kula-bhaye — to fear for the family; tilāñjali dilum̐ — I gave tilanjali (bade farewell for ever)

**11.2.** Body and soul I gave to Him,
to fear for my family I bade farewell for ever.[^27-32]

গোরা বিনু না রহে জীবন ।
গৌরাঙ্গ হইল প্রাণ-ধন ॥

*gorā binu nā rahe jībana |*
*gaurāṅga haila prāṇa-dhana ||*

*Word for word:* gorā binu — without Gora; nā rahe jībana — life does not remain; gaurāṅga haila — Gauranga has become; prāṇa-dhana — the treasure of life

**11.3.** Without Gora I cannot live:
Gauranga has become the treasure of my life.

ধৈরজ না বান্ধে মোর মনে ।
বাসুদেব ঘোষ রস জানে ॥

*dhairaja nā bāndhe mora mane |*
*bāsudeba ghoṣa rasa jāne ||*

*Word for word:* dhairaja nā bāndhe — does not hold composure; mora mane — my mind; bāsudeba ghoṣa rasa jāne — Vasudeva Ghosha knows [this] rasa

**11.4.** My heart cannot hold its composure;
Vasudeva Ghosha knows this rasa.[^27-33]

[^27-31]: Signature: "Vasudeva Ghosha." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 258 (printed p. 247), 19th pallava, no. 5 (mark "॥৫॥২১৭২॥"); raga
pathamanjari; MSS P-R-Sa no. 2280 and P-R no. 14/24. GPT1 — p. 161, no. 12 (raga pathamanjari); GPT2 — sec. 3.2, no. 12
(catalogue: VG-017). On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section.
[^27-32]: Lit. "to fear for my family I gave tilanjali" — the libation of water with sesame offered for the dead: a sign of
final farewell. "I gave body and soul" — the words of a townswoman (a nagari motif; introductory note). MS P-R: "to
propriety" (śīle) for "to fear for my family" (kula-bhaye).
[^27-33]: MS P-R: "Gora is my very own" (gorā mora nija) for "Gauranga has become" (11.3); "without Gora I cannot live"
(jībana nā rahe gorā bine) for "cannot hold… composure" (11.4).

## 12. Vasu Ghosha — "gorā-rūpa dekhibāre mane kari sādha…" (PK 2173)
*Nagari-bhava. A townswoman longs to see Gora: love for Gaura is a great calamity; she knows neither day nor night, she
remembers Him ceaselessly; what spell has Gora cast with the arrows of His eyes? Her eyes shed tears without end. The raga
is the same as for the preceding pada (pathamanjari).*[^27-34]

গোরা-রূপ দেখিবারে মনে করি সাধ ।
গৌর-পিরিতি খানি বড় পরমাদ ॥

*gorā-rūpa dekhibāre mane kari sādha |*
*gaura-piriti khāni baṛa paramāda ||*

*Word for word:* gorā-rūpa dekhibāre — to see Gora's form; mane kari sādha — I long in my heart; gaura-piriti khāni — love for Gaura; baṛa paramāda — a great calamity

**12.1.** I long in my heart to see Gora's form;
love for Gaura is a great calamity.

কিবা নিশি কিবা দিশি কিছুই না জানি ।
অনুখণ পড়ে মনে গোরা গুণমণি ॥

*kibā niśi kibā diśi kichui nā jāni |*
*anukhaṇa paṛe mane gorā guṇamaṇi ||*

*Word for word:* kibā niśi kibā diśi — whether night or day; kichui nā jāni — I know nothing; anukhaṇa paṛe mane — ceaselessly comes to mind; gorā guṇa-maṇi — Gora, the jewel of virtues

**12.2.** Whether it is night or day, I know nothing;
ceaselessly I remember Gora, the jewel of virtues.

গোরা গোরা করি মোর কি হৈল অন্তরে ।
কিবা মন্ত্র কৈল গোরা নয়ানের শরে ॥

*gorā gorā kari mora ki haila antare |*
*kibā mantra kaila gorā nayānera śare ||*

*Word for word:* gorā gorā kari — repeating "Gora, Gora"; mora ki haila antare — what has happened in my heart; kibā mantra kaila gorā — what spell has Gora cast; nayānera śare — with the arrows of the eyes

**12.3.** Repeating "Gora, Gora," what has become of my heart?
What spell has Gora cast with the arrows of His eyes?

নিঝরে ঝরয়ে আঁখি প্রবোধ না মানে ।
বড় পরমাদ প্রেম বাসু ঘোষ গানে ॥

*nijhare jharaye ām̐khi prabodha nā māne |*
*baṛa paramāda prema bāsu ghoṣa gāne ||*

*Word for word:* nijhare jharaye ām̐khi — the eyes pour without end; prabodha nā māne — accept no consolation; baṛa paramāda prema — a great calamity is love; bāsu ghoṣa gāne — sings Vasu Ghosha

**12.4.** My eyes pour without ceasing and accept no consolation;
"a great calamity is love," sings Vasu Ghosha.

[^27-34]: Signature: "Vasu Ghosha." PK: vol. 3, PDF pp. 258–259 (printed pp. 247–248), 19th pallava, no. 6 (mark "॥৬॥২১৭৩॥");
"the same raga" (tathā rāga); MS P-R-Sa no. 2281 (it reads "form" (rūpakhāni) for "the jewel of virtues," 12.2). GPT1 —
p. 161, no. 13 ("yathārāga"); GPT2 — sec. 3.2, no. 13 (catalogue: VG-128 = VG-018). On nagari-bhava see the introductory
note to the section.

## 13. Vasu Ghosha — "gṛha-kāja kari tāhe thira nahe mana…" (PK 2175)
*Nagari-bhava. A townswoman cannot do her housework — her heart is restless: "Come, let us go and see Gora's moonlike
face!" She has bidden farewell to her family and her hopes, given up food and pastimes; without Gora she cannot live. The
same raga.*[^27-35]

গৃহ-কাজ করি তাহে থির নহে মন ।
চল দেখি গিয়া গোরার ও চাঁদ-বদন ॥

*gṛha-kāja kari tāhe thira nahe mana |*
*cala dekhi giyā gorāra o cām̐da-badana ||*

*Word for word:* gṛha-kāja kari — doing housework; tāhe — in it; thira nahe mana — the mind is not steady; cala dekhi giyā — come, let us go and see; gorāra o cām̐da-badana — that moonlike face of Gora

**13.1.** I do my housework — but my heart is restless:
come, let us go and see Gora's moonlike face!

কুলে দিলুঁ তিলাঞ্জলি ছাড়ি সব আশ ।
তেজিলুঁ সকল সুখ ভোজন-বিলাস ॥

*kule dilum̐ tilāñjali chāṛi saba āśa |*
*tejilum̐ sakala sukha bhojana-bilāsa ||*

*Word for word:* kule dilum̐ tilāñjali — I gave tilanjali to the family (bade it farewell for ever); chāṛi saba āśa — abandoning all hopes; tejilum̐ sakala sukha — I gave up all pleasures; bhojana-bilāsa — food and pastimes

**13.2.** To my family I bade farewell for ever, abandoning all hopes,
I gave up all pleasures — food and pastimes.

রজনী দিবস মোর মন ছনছন ।
বাসু কহে গোরা বিনু না রহে জীবন ॥

*rajanī dibasa mora mana chanachana |*
*bāsu kahe gorā binu nā rahe jībana ||*

*Word for word:* rajanī dibasa — night and day; mora mana chanachana — my heart is restless; bāsu kahe — says Vasu; gorā binu nā rahe jībana — without Gora life does not remain

**13.3.** Day and night my heart finds no rest.
Says Vasu: without Gora I cannot live.

[^27-35]: Signature: "Vasu." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 259 (printed p. 248), 19th pallava, no. 8 (mark "॥৮॥২১৭৫॥"); "the same raga";
MS P-R-Sa no. 2283. Before it stands PK 2174 by Lochana Dasa ("āra śunecha ālo sai gorā-bhābera kathā"; chapter 28). GPT1 —
p. 161, no. 14 (raga shri) — with an extra opening couplet: "āhā mari mari sai āhā mari mari, kikṣaṇe dekhilum̐ gorā
pāśarite nāri" ("Ah, I am dying, dying, friend! In what moment did I see Gora — I cannot forget"); GPT2 — sec. 3.2, no. 14.
In the catalogue the pada was listed twice: VG-019 (from GPT) and VG-129 (from PK). On nagari-bhava see the introductory
note to the section.

## 14. Vasu Ghosha — "cala dekhi giyā gorā ati manohare…" (PK 2176, nagari recension)
*Nagari-bhava. The same pada as PK 973 (chapter 9, no. 2), in PK's second recension — in the pallava of the nagaris'
words: "Come, let us go and see Gora!" — Gaura's form in Nadia; the ending differs: "I will go and give my youth for Him."
The same raga.*[^27-36]

চল দেখি গিয়া গোরা অতি মনোহরে ।
অপরূপ রূপ গোরা নদীয়া নগরে ॥

*cala dekhi giyā gorā ati manohare |*
*aparūpa rūpa gorā nadīyā nagare ||*

*Word for word:* cala dekhi giyā — come, let us go and see; gorā — Gora; ati manohare — exceedingly beautiful; aparūpa rūpa — the wondrous form; gorā — of Gora; nadīyā nagare — in the town of Nadia

**14.1.** Come, let us go and see Gora, beautiful beyond words:
wondrous is Gora's form in the town of Nadia!

ঢল ঢল কষিল কাঞ্চন জিনি অঙ্গ ।
কে দেখি ধৈরজ ধরে নয়ান-তরঙ্গ ॥

*ḍhala ḍhala kaṣila kāñcana jini aṅga |*
*ke dekhi dhairaja dhare nayāna-taraṅga ||*

*Word for word:* ḍhala ḍhala — tender and radiant; kaṣila kāñcana jini — surpassing tested gold; aṅga — the body; ke dekhi dhairaja dhare — who, seeing, keeps composure; nayāna-taraṅga — the waves of the eyes

**14.2.** His body, tender and radiant, outshines tested gold;
who, seeing the waves of His eyes, can keep his composure?

আজানুলম্বিত ভুজ কনকের স্তম্ভ ।
অরুণ বসন কটি বিপুল নিতম্ব ॥

*ājānulambita bhuja kanakera stambha |*
*aruṇa basana kaṭi bipula nitamba ||*

*Word for word:* ājānulambita bhuja — arms reaching to the knees; kanakera stambha — golden pillars; aruṇa basana kaṭi — a red cloth at the waist; bipula nitamba — broad hips

**14.3.** His arms reach to His knees like golden pillars,
a red cloth is at His waist, broad are His hips.

মালতীর মালা গলে আপাদ দোলনি ।
কহে বাসু দিব গিয়া যৌবন নিছনি ॥

*mālatīra mālā gale āpāda dolani |*
*kahe bāsu diba giyā yaubana nichani ||*

*Word for word:* mālatīra mālā gale — a garland of malati on the neck; āpāda dolani — swaying down to the feet; kahe bāsu — says Vasu; diba giyā — I will go and give; yaubana nichani — my youth as nichani (for Him)

**14.4.** A garland of malati sways on His neck down to His feet.
Says Vasu: I will go and give my youth for Him.[^27-37]

[^27-36]: Signature: "Vasu." PK: vol. 3, PDF pp. 259–260 (printed pp. 248–249), 19th pallava, no. 9 (mark "॥৯॥২১৭৬॥"); "the same
raga"; MS P-R-Sa no. 2284. GPT1 — p. 161, no. 15 (raga shri); GPT2 — sec. 3.2, no. 15 (catalogue: VG-096). Lines 14.1–14.3 are
identical with PK 973 and are translated as in chapter 9 (no. 2, notes 6–8). On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to
the section.
[^27-37]: "I will give… my youth" (diba giyā yaubana nichani) — the rite of nichani (note 10): the speaker gives for Him the
dearest thing she has; in the recension of PK 973 — "I will give my life." The signature is put into the mouth of a
townswoman (as in other padas of the section).

## 15. Vasu Ghosha — "niramala gorā tanu kaṣila kāñcana janu…" (PK 28)
*Nagari-bhava. A townswoman's first love: seeing Gora's body, pure as tested gold, she lost herself; the serpent of His brow
has bitten her heart; the arrows of His reddish eyes have left her without support — she is as if drowning in the
bottomless Ganga; "if you know a spell or a remedy, help me: for Gora's sake my life is leaving me." In PK it is the
gaura-chandrika to Radha's purvaraga, "the words of a nagari." Raga kamoda.*[^27-38]

নিরমল গোরা তনু কষিল কাঞ্চন জনু
হেরইতে ভৈ গেলুঁ ভোর ।
ভাঙ-ভুজঙ্গমে দংশল মঝু মন
অন্তর কাঁপয়ে মোর ॥

*niramala gorā tanu kaṣila kāñcana janu*
*heraite bhai gelum̐ bhora |*
*bhāṅa-bhujaṅgame daṃśala majhu mana*
*antara kām̐paye mora ||*

*Word for word:* niramala gorā tanu — Gora's pure body; kaṣila kāñcana janu — like tested gold; heraite — gazing; bhai gelum̐ bhora — I lost myself; bhāṅa-bhujaṅgame — the serpent of the brow; daṃśala majhu mana — has bitten my heart; antara kām̐paye mora — my inner self trembles

**15.1.** Gora's pure body is like tested gold;
gazing at it, I lost myself.
The serpent of His brow has bitten my heart —
everything within me trembles.

সজনি যব হাম পেখলুঁ গোরা ।
আকুল দীগ বিদিগ নাহি পাইয়ে
মদন-লালসে মন ভোরা ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*sajani yaba hāma pekhalum̐ gorā |*
*ākula dīga bidiga nāhi pāiye*
*madana-lālase mana bhorā || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* sajani — friend; yaba hāma pekhalum̐ gorā — since I saw Gora; ākula — distressed; dīga bidiga nāhi pāiye — I cannot find the directions; madana-lālase — by the longing of Madana; mana bhorā — the heart is overwhelmed

**15.2.** *(Refrain)* Friend, ever since I saw Gora,
in my distress I cannot tell the directions apart,
my heart is seized by the longing of Madana.[^27-39]

অরুণিত-নয়নে তেরছ অবলোকনে
বরিখে কুসুম-শর সাধে ।
জিবইতে জীবনে থেহ নাহি পায়লুঁ
ডুবলুঁ গঙ্গ অগাধে ॥

*aruṇita-nayane teracha abalokane*
*barikhe kusuma-śara sādhe |*
*jibaite jībane theha nāhi pāyalum̐*
*ḍubalum̐ gaṅga agādhe ||*

*Word for word:* aruṇita-nayane — with reddening eyes; terachha abalokane — with sidelong glances; barikhe kusuma-śara sādhe — rains flower arrows with delight; jibaite jībane — to go on living; theha nāhi pāyalum̐ — I found no support; ḍubalum̐ gaṅga agādhe — I drowned in the bottomless Ganga

**15.3.** With sidelong glances of His reddening eyes
He rains down flower arrows with delight.
How shall I live on? — I have found no support:
I have drowned in the bottomless Ganga.[^27-40]

মন্ত্র মহৌষধি তুহুঁ জানসি যদি
মঝু লাগি করবি উপায় ।
বাসুদেব ঘোষ কহে শুন শুন এ সখি
গোরা লাগি প্রাণ মোর যায় ॥

*mantra mahauṣadhi tuhum̐ jānasi yadi*
*majhu lāgi karabi upāya |*
*bāsudeba ghoṣa kahe śuna śuna e sakhi*
*gorā lāgi prāṇa mora yāya ||*

*Word for word:* mantra mahauṣadhi — a spell, a mighty remedy; tuhum̐ jānasi yadi — if you know; majhu lāgi karabi upāya — find a means for me; bāsudeba ghoṣa kahe — says Vasudeva Ghosha; śuna śuna e sakhi — listen, listen, friend; gorā lāgi prāṇa mora yāya — for Gora's sake my life is leaving

**15.4.** If you know a spell or a mighty remedy,
find a means for me.
Says Vasudeva Ghosha: listen, listen, friend —
for Gora's sake my life is leaving me.[^27-41]

[^27-38]: Signature: "Vasudeva Ghosha." PK: vol. 1, PDF p. 34 (printed p. 23), section "atha śrīrādhāyāḥ pūrvarāgaḥ | taducita
śrīgauracandra | nāgarī ukti" (Radha's purvaraga; the gaura-chandrika befitting it — the words of a nagari), no. 1 (mark
"॥১॥২৮॥"); raga kamoda; MS P-R-Sa no. 258. GPT1 — p. 163, no. 20 (raga kamoda); GPT2 — sec. 3.2 (catalogue: VG-023, "no. 27" —
the number is apparently garbled by the OCR). The earliest nagari pada of PK by number: Satishchandra Raya opens the whole
cycle of purvaraga with it. On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section.
[^27-39]: "My heart is seized by the longing of Madana" (madana-lālase mana bhorā) — the original names the attraction openly
(Madana is the god of love); we translate it exactly. This is the language of Radha's purvaraga, to which the pada serves as
a prelude; in Krishna-lila the "Madana" of such padas is Krishna Himself, Madana-mohana, and their love is not worldly. The
tradition does not accept the application of this language to Gaura (introductory note). P-R-Sa: "the intoxication of
Madana" (madanamadārase); the word "friend" is absent; "I found" (pāyalum̐) for "I cannot tell" (pāiye).
[^27-40]: "I have drowned in the bottomless Ganga" — an image of complete loss of self. MS "ka": "purified" (kaṣita) for
"tested" (15.1); "ka"–"cha": "I fell into oblivion" (paṛi gelum̐). P-R-Sa: "with reddish eyes" (aruṇa nayāne); "He has aimed a
cruel arrow" (baṛai biṣama śara sāndhi) for "rains down flower arrows"; "I will not hold my composure" (dhairaja nā bāndhaba)
for "I have found no support"; "into the bottomless Ganga" (gaṅgā agādhi).
[^27-41]: P-R-Sa: "do you" (so tuhum̐ karaha) for "find for me"; "beauty" (sundari) for "friend" (so also MS "kha"); "without
Gora my body perishes" (gorā binu mora tanu yāya).

## 16. Vasu Ghosha — "nirabadhi mora mane gorā-rūpa lāgiyāche…" (PK 777)
*Nagari-bhava. Gora's form does not leave the townswoman's heart: not seeing His face, her breast is breaking; she fears
neither husband nor elders and is ready to part with life for Gora's sake; she has abandoned all joys and her family —
nothing but Gora pleases her. In PK it is the gaura-chandrika to the section "anuraga: love for the form." Raga
suhai.*[^27-42]

নিরবধি মোর মনে গোরা-রূপ লাগিয়াছে
কহ সখী কি করি উপায় ।
না দেখিলে গোরা-মুখ বিদরিয়া যায় বুক
পরাণ বাহির হৈতে চায় ॥

*nirabadhi mora mane gorā-rūpa lāgiyāche*
*kaha sakhī ki kari upāya |*
*nā dekhile gorā-mukha bidariyā yāya buka*
*parāṇa bāhira haite cāya ||*

*Word for word:* nirabadhi mora mane — ceaselessly in my heart; gorā-rūpa lāgiyāche — Gora's form has fixed itself; kaha sakhī ki kari upāya — tell me, friend, what shall I do; nā dekhile gorā-mukha — not seeing Gora's face; bidariyā yāya buka — the breast breaks; parāṇa bāhira haite cāya — the soul wants to leave

**16.1.** Ceaselessly Gora's form stays in my heart —
tell me, friend, what shall I do?
Not seeing Gora's face, my breast is breaking,
my soul longs to leave my body.

কহ সখি কি বুদ্ধি করিব ।
গৃহপতি গুরুজন ভয় নাহি মোর মন
গোরা লাগি পরাণ তেজিব ॥

*kaha sakhi ki buddhi kariba |*
*gṛhapati gurujana bhaya nāhi mora mana*
*gorā lāgi parāṇa tejiba ||*

*Word for word:* kaha sakhi — tell me, friend; ki buddhi kariba — what plan shall I make; gṛhapati — the husband (master of the house); gurujana — the elders; bhaya nāhi mora mana — my heart does not fear; gorā lāgi — for Gora's sake; parāṇa tejiba — I will give up my life

**16.2.** Tell me, friend, what am I to do?
My heart does not fear my husband or my elders:
for Gora's sake I will give up my life.[^27-43]

সব সুখ তেয়াগিলুঁ কুলে তিলাঞ্জলি দিলুঁ
গোরা বিনু আন নাহি ভায় ।
নিঝরে ঝরয়ে আঁখি শুন হে মরমি সখি
বাসুঘোষ কি বলিবে তায় ॥

*saba sukha teyāgilum̐ kule tilāñjali dilum̐*
*gorā binu āna nāhi bhāya |*
*nijhare jharaye ām̐khi śuna he marami sakhi*
*bāsughoṣa ki balibe tāya ||*

*Word for word:* saba sukha teyāgilum̐ — I have abandoned all joys; kule tilāñjali dilum̐ — I gave tilanjali to the family; gorā binu āna nāhi bhāya — nothing but Gora pleases; nijhare jharaye ām̐khi — the eyes pour without end; śuna he marami sakhi — listen, friend of my heart; bāsughoṣa ki balibe tāya — what can Vasu Ghosha say to this

**16.3.** I have abandoned all joys, bidden my family farewell for ever;
nothing but Gora pleases me.
My eyes pour without end — listen, dear friend of my heart —
what can Vasu Ghosha say to this?

[^27-42]: Signature: "Vasu Ghosha." PK: vol. 2, PDF p. 120 (printed p. 107), 10th pallava, section "atha anurāgaḥ… ādau rūpānurāgo
yathā | tatra śrīmahāprabhuḥ" (anuraga; first, love for the form; here — on Mahaprabhu), no. 1 (mark "॥১॥৭৭৭॥"); raga suhai; MSS P-R-Sa
no. 1267 and P-R no. 14/1 (in P-R the raga is tudi). GPT1 — p. 162, no. 17 (raga suhai); GPT2 — sec. 3.2 (catalogue: VG-095). In GPT1 the same pada stands once more — sect. 3.2, no. 84 (pp. 188–189), with the signature "locana dāsa ki baliba tāya" — Lochana's (found in chapter 34; the signature is erroneous).
On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section.
[^27-43]: "My husband and my elders" (gṛhapati gurujana) — the speaker is married; readiness to disregard husband and elders is
the parakiya motif of the padas on the gopis, transferred to the townswomen of Nadia: precisely this transfer the
tradition rejects (introductory note). P-R: "does not hold" (nāhi laye) for "does not fear." MS P-R: "what shall I do, what
will become of me" (16.1); "ka," "kha," "gha," "cha," P-R-Sa: "form" (rūpa) for "face" (mukha, 16.1); P-R-Sa: "pour without
ceasing" (nijhure jhuraye), "of my heart" (marama) for "dear… of my heart" (16.3).

## 17. Vasu Ghosha — "gorā-rūpa lāgila nayane…" (PK 899)
*Nagari-bhava. Gora's form is imprinted on her eyes — night and day, awake and in dreams; wherever she looks she sees Him,
she wants to turn her gaze away and cannot; He is deep in her heart, and her heart cannot be restrained: "Gora is the
enchanter of women." In PK it is the gaura-chandrika to the section "anuraga — another way." Raga shri.*[^27-44]

গোরা-রূপ লাগিল নয়নে ।
কিবা নিশি কিবা দিশি শয়নে স্বপনে ॥

*gorā-rūpa lāgila nayane |*
*kibā niśi kibā diśi śayane svapane ||*

*Word for word:* gorā-rūpa lāgila nayane — Gora's form has fixed itself in my eyes; kibā niśi kibā diśi — whether night or day; śayane svapane — on the bed, in dreams

**17.1.** Gora's form is imprinted on my eyes —
whether by night or by day, on my bed or in dreams.

যে দিগে ফিরাই আঁখি সেই দিগে দেখি ।
পিছলিতে করি সাধ না পিছলে আঁখি ॥

*ye dige phirāi ām̐khi sei dige dekhi |*
*pichalite kari sādha nā pichale ām̐khi ||*

*Word for word:* ye dige phirāi ām̐khi — wherever I turn my eyes; sei dige dekhi — there I see; pichalite — to slip away (look away); kari sādha — I wish; nā pichale ām̐khi — the eyes do not slip away

**17.2.** Wherever I turn my eyes — there I see [Him];
I wish to look away — my eyes will not turn.

কি খেণে দেখিলাম গোরা কি না মোর হৈল ।
নিরবধি গোরা-রূপ মরমে লাগিল ॥

*ki kheṇe dekhilāma gorā ki nā mora haila |*
*nirabadhi gorā-rūpa marame lāgila ||*

*Word for word:* ki khene dekhilāma gorā — in what moment I saw Gora; ki nā mora haila — what has not befallen me; nirabadhi — ceaselessly; gorā-rūpa marame lāgila — Gora's form has fixed itself deep in my heart

**17.3.** In what moment did I see Gora — what has not befallen me!
Ceaselessly Gora's form is deep in my heart.

চিত নিবারিতে চাহি নহে নিবারণ ।
বাসুঘোষে বলে গোরা রমণী-মোহন ॥

*cita nibārite cāhi nahe nibāraṇa |*
*bāsughoṣe bale gorā ramaṇī-mohana ||*

*Word for word:* cita nibārite cāhi — I want to restrain the heart; nahe nibāraṇa — it is not restrained; bāsughoṣe bale — says Vasu Ghosha; gorā ramaṇī-mohana — Gora is the enchanter of women

**17.4.** I want to restrain my heart — it cannot be restrained.
Says Vasu Ghosha: Gora is the enchanter of women.[^27-45]

[^27-44]: Signature: "Vasu Ghosha." PK: vol. 2, PDF p. 171 (printed p. 158), section "atha anurāgaḥ prakārāntaraṃ yathā | tatra
śrīgauracandraḥ" (anuraga — another way; here — on Gaurachandra), no. 101 (mark "॥১০১॥৮৯৯॥"); raga shri; MSS P-R-Sa nos. 1390 and
1398, P-R no. 14/7. The pada stands in PK a second time — PK 916 (vol. 2, PDF p. 178; with a reference there to 899). GPT1 —
p. 162, no. 18 (raga shri); GPT2 — sec. 3.2, no. 18 (catalogue: VG-021). On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the
section.
[^27-45]: "The enchanter of women" (ramaṇī-mohana) — in a townswoman's mouth, praise of His beauty; cf. Madana-mohana, "the
enchanter of the god of love." MS P-R: "my gaze falls" (paṛaye diṭhi) for "I turn my eyes" (17.2); P-R-Sa: "the heart wishes"
(kare mana), P-R: "there is a wish" (kare sādha) for "I wish" (17.2); "ka": "in the eyes" (nayane), P-R: "has entered"
(paśila) for "is deep in my heart" (17.3).

## 18. Vasu Ghosha — "gorā-anurāge mora parāṇa kātare…" (PK 747)
*Nagari-bhava. "My soul languishes with love for Gora": her eyes are full of tears, repeating "Gora, Gora" she is as if
ill; she remembers Him ceaselessly, she does not know where to go; love for Gauranga is no easy thing: "the dharma of the
family will not stand." In PK it is the gaura-chandrika to the section "anuraga with reproaches." Raga suhai.*[^27-46]

গোরা-অনুরাগে মোর পরাণ কাতরে ।
নিরবধি ছল ছল আঁখি-জল ঝরে ॥

*gorā-anurāge mora parāṇa kātare |*
*nirabadhi chala chala ām̐khi-jala jhare ||*

*Word for word:* gorā-anurāge — from love for Gora; mora parāṇa kātare — my soul languishes; nirabadhi — ceaselessly; chala chala — brimming over; ām̐khi-jala jhare — tears fall from the eyes

**18.1.** With love for Gora my soul languishes;
ceaselessly, brimming over, my eyes shed tears.

গোরা গোরা করি মোর কি হৈল বিয়াধি ।
নিরবধি পড়ে মনে গোরা গুণনিধি ॥

*gorā gorā kari mora ki haila biyādhi |*
*nirabadhi paṛe mane gorā guṇanidhi ||*

*Word for word:* gorā gorā kari — repeating "Gora, Gora"; mora ki haila biyādhi — what malady has come upon me; nirabadhi paṛe mane — ceaselessly comes to mind; gorā guṇa-nidhi — Gora, the treasury of virtues

**18.2.** Repeating "Gora, Gora," what malady has seized me?
Ceaselessly I remember Gora, the treasury of virtues.

কি করিব কোথা যাব গোরা-অনুরাগে ।
অনুখণ গোরা-প্রেম হিয়ার মাঝে জাগে ॥

*ki kariba kothā yāba gorā-anurāge |*
*anukhaṇa gorā-prema hiyāra mājhe jāge ||*

*Word for word:* ki kariba kothā yāba — what shall I do, where shall I go; gorā-anurāge — with love for Gora; anukhaṇa — at every moment; gorā-prema — love for Gora; hiyāra mājhe jāge — awakens in the heart

**18.3.** What shall I do, where shall I go from this love for Gora?
At every moment love for Gora awakens in my heart.

গৌরাঙ্গ-পিরিতি খানি বড়ই বিষম ।
বাসু কহে নাহি রহে কুলের ধরম ॥

*gaurāṅga-piriti khāni baṛai biṣama |*
*bāsu kahe nāhi rahe kulera dharama ||*

*Word for word:* gaurāṅga-piriti khāni — love for Gauranga; baṛai biṣama — no easy (grievous) thing; bāsu kahe — says Vasu; nāhi rahe — will not remain; kulera dharama — the dharma of the family

**18.4.** Love for Gauranga is no easy thing:
says Vasu — the dharma of the family will not stand.[^27-47]

[^27-46]: Signature: "Vasu." PK: vol. 2, PDF p. 107 (printed p. 94), 8th pallava, section "atha ākṣepānurāgaḥ | śrīgauracandraḥ"
(anuraga with reproaches; gaura-chandrika), no. 1 (mark "॥১॥৭৪৭॥"); raga suhai; MS P-R-Sa no. 1236. GPT1 — p. 386, no. 12 (raga
suhai) — in the section "the lament of Shachi and Vishnupriya" after the sannyasa; GPT2 — sec. 5.4, no. 12 (catalogue:
VG-071). On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section.
[^27-47]: "The dharma of the family" (kulera dharama) — the duty and honour of the family; words of a townswoman, not of
Vishnupriya, though GPT places the pada among the laments after the sannyasa. GPT1: "my soul is breaking" (parāṇa bidare,
18.1). P-R-Sa: "weep" (jhure) for "shed" (18.1); MS "ka": "every moment" (anukṣaṇa, 18.3).

## 19. Vasu Ghosha — "e hena sundara beśa kene banāilum̐…" (PK 360)
*Nagari-bhava. A night of vain waiting: "Why did I adorn myself so? Gora's form I never saw"; the night passes in vain, the
Creator has mocked her; whose body will she now anoint with perfumes and sandal, to whom will she offer camphor and betel?
In PK it is the gaura-chandrika to the section on the utkanthita (the heroine pining in expectation). Raga mallar.*[^27-48]

এ হেন সুন্দর বেশ কেনে বনাইলুঁ ।
নিরুপম গোরা-রূপ দেখিতে নারিলুঁ ॥

*e hena sundara beśa kene banāilum̐ |*
*nirupama gorā-rūpa dekhite nārilum̐ ||*

*Word for word:* e hena sundara beśa — such a beautiful attire; kene banāilum̐ — why did I put on; nirupama gorā-rūpa — Gora's peerless form; dekhite nārilum̐ — I could not see

**19.1.** Why did I adorn myself so beautifully?
Gora's peerless form I never saw.

অকাজে রজনী যায় কিবা মোর হৈল ।
নিশ্চয়ে জানিলুঁ মোরে বিধি বিড়ম্বিল ॥

*akāje rajanī yāya kibā mora haila |*
*niścaye jānilum̐ more bidhi biṛambila ||*

*Word for word:* akāje rajanī yāya — the night passes in vain; kibā mora haila — what has become of me; niścaye jānilum̐ — I know for certain; more bidhi biṛambila — the Creator has mocked me

**19.2.** The night passes in vain — what has become of me?
Now I know for certain: the Creator has mocked me.[^27-49]

সুবাসিত গন্ধ আদি অগোর চন্দন ।
গোরা বিনু কার অঙ্গে করিব লেপন ॥

*subāsita gandha ādi agora candana |*
*gorā binu kāra aṅge kariba lepana ||*

*Word for word:* subāsita gandha ādi — perfumes and the like; agora candana — aguru, sandal; gorā binu — without Gora; kāra aṅge — whose body; kariba lepana — shall I anoint

**19.3.** Perfumes, aguru, sandal —
without Gora, whose body shall I anoint with them?

কর্পূর তাম্বুল গুয়া দিব কার মুখে ।
বাসুঘোষ কহে নিশি যায় বড় দুখে ॥

*karpūra tāmbula guyā diba kāra mukhe |*
*bāsughoṣa kahe niśi yāya baṛa dukhe ||*

*Word for word:* karpūra tāmbula guyā — camphor, betel, areca; diba kāra mukhe — into whose mouth shall I give; bāsughoṣa kahe — says Vasu Ghosha; niśi yāya baṛa dukhe — the night departs in great sorrow

**19.4.** Camphor, betel, areca — into whose mouth shall I give them?
Says Vasu Ghosha: the night departs in great sorrow.[^27-50]

[^27-48]: Signature: "Vasu Ghosha." PK: vol. 1, PDF p. 243 (printed p. 232), section "athotkaṇṭhitā | tatra śrīgauracandraḥ"
(utkanthita; gaura-chandrika), no. 9 (mark "॥৯॥৩৬০॥"); raga mallar; MS P-R-Sa no. 479. GPT1 — p. 303, no. 11 (raga mallar) — in
section 4.5 (the bhavas of the night); GPT2 — sec. 4.5, no. 11 (catalogue: VG-180; row VG-088 has the same PK number). On
nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section.
[^27-49]: "The Creator has mocked me" (bidhi biṛambila) — has deceived, thwarted my design. The Creator (bidhi) is Brahma, the
arbiter of fate; not the Lord. MS "gha": "did not obtain" (nā pāilum̐), "cha": (nā pālum̐) for "never saw" (19.1); P-R-Sa:
"today" (āji) for "me" (19.2).
[^27-50]: Camphor, betel and areca are the refreshment offered to a dear guest; the waiting and preparations are the image of
the utkanthita from the padas on Radha, transferred to a townswoman. MS "gha": "agaura" for "agora" (aguru, 19.3); "ka"–"ga":
"Gaura" (gaura) for "Gora" (19.3); P-R-Sa: "guvaka" (the same nut, 19.4).

## 20. Vasu Ghosha — "āju rajani hāma kaiche bañcaba re…" (PK 365)
*Nagari-bhava. Disappointed waiting: "How shall I pass this night? The king of dancers has turned away from me"; the hope
of new love has not been fulfilled, half a moment drags on like ages; for Gaura's sake she cast aside respect for her
elders — and the Creator has deprived her of this love; the fruit of prema He has scattered over the whole world, and she
is left without hope. In PK it is the gaura-chandrika to the section on the vipralabdha (the heroine disappointed in her
waiting). Raga kedara.*[^27-51]

আজু রজনি হাম কৈছে বঞ্চব রে
মোহে বিমুখ নট-রাজ ।
নব অনুরাগে আশ নাহি পূরল
বিফল ভেল সব কাজ ॥

*āju rajani hāma kaiche bañcaba re*
*mohe bimukha naṭa-rāja |*
*naba anurāge āśa nāhi pūrala*
*biphala bhela saba kāja ||*

*Word for word:* āju rajani — this night; hāma kaiche bañcaba re — how shall I pass; mohe bimukha naṭa-rāja — the king of dancers has turned away from me; naba anurāge — in new love; āśa nāhi pūrala — the hope was not fulfilled; biphala bhela saba kāja — all efforts became fruitless

**20.1.** How shall I pass this night? —
The king of dancers has turned away from me.
In new love my hope has not been fulfilled,
all my efforts have come to nothing.

সজনি কাহে বনায়লুঁ বেশ ।
আধ পলকে কত যুগ বহি যাওত
ভাবিতে পাঁজর ভেল শেষ ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*sajani kāhe banāyalum̐ beśa |*
*ādha palake kata yuga bahi yāota*
*bhābite pām̐jara bhela śeṣa || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* sajani — friend; kāhe banāyalum̐ beśa — why did I adorn myself; ādha palake — in half a moment; kata yuga bahi yāota — many yugas seem to pass; bhābite — in pining; pām̐jara bhela śeṣa — the ribs have come to an end (I have wasted to the ribs)

**20.2.** *(Refrain)* Friend, why did I adorn myself?
Half a moment drags on like ages;
pining [for Him] I have wasted to the ribs.[^27-52]

গুরুজন-গৌরব দূরহি ডারলুঁ
গৌর-প্রেমরস লাগি ।
দুর্লভ প্রেম মোহে বিহি বঞ্চল
মঝু ভালে দেয়ল আগি ॥

*gurujana-gauraba dūrahi ḍāralum̐*
*gaura-premarasa lāgi |*
*durlabha prema mohe bihi bañcala*
*majhu bhāle deyala āgi ||*

*Word for word:* gurujana-gauraba — respect for the elders; dūrahi ḍāralum̐ — I cast far away; gaura-prema-rasa lāgi — for the rasa of love for Gaura; durlabha prema — the rare love; mohe bihi bañcala — the Creator has denied me; majhu bhāle — on my forehead (fate); deyala āgi — has set fire

**20.3.** Respect for my elders I cast far away
for the sake of the rasa of love for Gaura.
The rare love the Creator has denied me —
he has set fire to my fate.[^27-53]

প্রেম-রতন-ফল জগ ভরি বিথারল
হাম তাহে ভেল নৈরাশ ।
নব অনুরাগ-ভরমে হাম ভূলল
বাসুঘোষ না পূরল আশ ॥

*prema-ratana-phala jaga bhari bithārala*
*hāma tāhe bhela nairāśa |*
*naba anurāga-bharame hāma bhūlala*
*bāsughoṣa nā pūrala āśa ||*

*Word for word:* prema-ratana-phala — the jewel-fruit of prema; jaga bhari bithārala — He scattered over the whole world; hāma tāhe bhela nairāśa — I was left without hope by it; naba anurāga-bharame — in the delusion of new love; hāma bhūlala — I went astray; bāsughoṣa nā pūrala āśa — Vasu Ghosha's hope was not fulfilled

**20.4.** The jewel-fruit of prema He has scattered over the whole world —
and I am left by it without hope;
deceived by new love, I have gone astray:
Vasu Ghosha's hope has not been fulfilled.[^27-54]

[^27-51]: Signature: "Vasu Ghosha." PK: vol. 1, PDF p. 247 (printed p. 236), section "atha bipralabdhā | tatra śrīgauracandraḥ"
(vipralabdha; gaura-chandrika), no. 14 (mark "॥১৪॥৩৬৫॥"); raga kedara; MSS P-R-Sa no. 493 and P-R no. 18/1. GPT1 — p. 303, no. 12
(raga kedara); GPT2 — sec. 4.5, no. 12 (catalogue: VG-181; row VG-089 has the same PK number). On nagari-bhava see the
introductory note to the section.
[^27-52]: The formula of separation — "half a moment is like many yugas": a moment without Him drags on endlessly (not the
reverse). "I have wasted to the ribs" (lit. "my ribs have come to an end") — I have wasted away with longing. MS P-R:
"looking at the road, I have wasted to the ribs" (patha heri pām̐jara śeṣa).
[^27-53]: "Respect for my elders I cast away" — a nagari motif (cf. note 43). The Creator (bidhi) is the arbiter of fate, not the
Lord. MS P-R: "he has put fire into my honeyed mouth" (deola madhu mukhe āgi); "ka"–"ga," "cha," P-R-Sa: "durlabhi," P-R:
"dulaha" (the same "rare").
[^27-54]: "The fruit of prema He has scattered over the whole world" — Gaura gives love of God to all; the townswoman complains
that she, who awaited Him otherwise, received nothing. In her own words — "the king of dancers has turned away from me"
(20.1) — what Vrindavana Dasa says is unwittingly recorded: the Lord did not turn His gaze to women (introductory note). MS
P-R: "over the world" (jagate) for "over the whole world," "fell" (paṛala) for "am left"; P-R-Sa: "by new love"
(anurāge); "ka"–"ga," "cha," P-R: "tulala" — a slip.
## 21. Vasu Ghosha — "ājuka premaka nāhika ora…" (PK 723)
*Nagari-bhava. A townswoman's dream: "Today's love has no limit — in a dream I lay in Gaura's embrace"; gazing at the Lord's
face she lost herself, tears flowed and washed down the collyrium, her tilaka grew wet, her adornment was effaced. In PK it
is the gaura-chandrika to the section "telling of the meeting — another way." Raga vibhasa.*[^27-55]

আজুক প্রেমক নাহিক ওর ।
স্বপনহি শুতলুঁ গৌরক কোর ॥

*ājuka premaka nāhika ora |*
*svapanahi śutalum̐ gauraka kora ||*

*Word for word:* ājuka premaka — of today's love; nāhika ora — there is no end; svapanahi — in a dream; śutalum̐ — I lay; gauraka kora — in Gaura's embrace (lap)

**21.1.** Today's love has no limit:
in a dream I lay in Gaura's embrace.[^27-56]

পহু-মুখ হেরইতে পড়লহি ভোর ।
ঢরকি ঢরকি বহে লোচনে লোর ॥

*pahu-mukha heraite paṛalahi bhora |*
*ḍharaki ḍharaki bahe locane lora ||*

*Word for word:* pahu-mukha heraite — gazing at the Lord's face; paṛalahi bhora — I lost myself; ḍharaki ḍharaki — rolling and rolling; bahe locane lora — tears flow from the eyes

**21.2.** Gazing at the Lord's face, I lost myself;
tears rolled and rolled from my eyes.

উচ-কুচ কাজরে হার উজোর ।
ভীগল তিলক বসন রুচি গোর ॥

*uca-kuca kājare hāra ujora |*
*bhīgala tilaka basana ruci gora ||*

*Word for word:* uca-kuca — the high breast; kājare — with collyrium; hāra ujora — the necklace bright; bhīgala tilaka — the tilaka is wet; basana — the cloth; ruci gora — a golden radiance (Gora's radiance)

**21.3.** On my high breast — collyrium [with tears], the necklace shines bright;
my tilaka is wet, on my cloth is a golden radiance.[^27-57]

মীটল অঙ্গ-বেশ রহু থোর ।
বাসুদেব ঘোষ কহে প্রেম আগোর ॥

*mīṭala aṅga-beśa rahu thora |*
*bāsudeba ghoṣa kahe prema āgora ||*

*Word for word:* mīṭala aṅga-beśa — the adornment of the body is effaced; rahu thora — little remains; bāsudeba ghoṣa kahe — says Vasudeva Ghosha; prema āgora — love brims over

**21.4.** The adornment of my body is effaced, little remains.
Says Vasudeva Ghosha: love brims over.[^27-58]

[^27-55]: Signature: "Vasudeva Ghosha." PK: vol. 2, PDF pp. 96–97 (printed pp. 83–84), section "atha rasodgāraḥ prakārāntaraṃ yathā |
śrīmahāprabhuḥ" (rasodgara — telling a friend of the meeting — another way; here — on Mahaprabhu), no. 60 (mark "॥৬০॥৭২৩॥"); raga
vibhasa; MS P-R-Sa no. 1197. GPT1 — p. 296, no. 13 (raga vibhasa); GPT2 — sec. 4.4, no. 13 (catalogue: VG-039; row VG-093 has
the same PK number). On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section.
[^27-56]: The pada describes a meeting in a dream (svapanahi) — this is sambhoga-nagari: a townswoman in Gaura's embrace. The
translation adds nothing beyond the original, but does not soften it either. Majumdar holds that padas on sambhoga with
Gaura known only from GPT were ascribed to Vasu later; this pada, however, stands in PK with his signature. The tradition
rejects such a portrayal of Gaura (introductory note). MSS "ka," "kha," "cha," P-R-Sa: "lay" (śutala) — the same.
[^27-57]: The tears have washed the collyrium (kājara) from her eyes down onto her breast. "A golden radiance" (ruci gora) — we
take it as the reflection of the golden Gaura; GPT1: "ruci mora" — "my attire (its lustre)."
[^27-58]: "Brims over" (āgora) — overflowing, measureless. MSS "ka," "kha," "gha," P-R-Sa: "much" (bahu) for "remains" (rahu);
P-R-Sa: "dark" (ghora) for "little" (thora); "in love" (preme).

## 22. Vasu Ghosha — "ki kahaba re sakhi rajanika bāta…" (PK 724)
*Nagari-bhava. A townswoman tells her friend of the night: she was sleeping beside her elders; at midnight, under the full
moon and the gentle Malaya breeze, love for Gaura overwhelmed her, and weeping she cried out: "Gaura, Gaura!"; the elders
woke and heard Gaura's name — then she raised the cry: "Thief, thief!" Raga dhanashi.*[^27-59]

কি কহব রে সখি রজনিক বাত ।
শুতিয়া আছিলুঁ হাম গুরুজন সাথ ॥

*ki kahaba re sakhi rajanika bāta |*
*śutiyā āchilum̐ hāma gurujana sātha ||*

*Word for word:* ki kahaba re sakhi — what shall I say, friend; rajanika bāta — of the night; śutiyā āchilum̐ hāma — I was sleeping; gurujana sātha — beside the elders

**22.1.** What shall I say, friend, of last night!
I was sleeping beside my elders.

আধ রজনি যব পূরল চন্দা ।
সুমলয় পবন বহয়ে অতি মন্দা ॥

*ādha rajani yaba pūrala candā |*
*sumalaya pabana bahaye ati mandā ||*

*Word for word:* ādha rajani — at midnight; yaba pūrala candā — when the moon was full; sumalaya pabana — the Malaya breeze; bahaye ati mandā — blows very gently

**22.2.** At midnight, when the moon was full,
very gently the breeze from Malaya was blowing.

গৌরক প্রেম ভরল মঝু দেহা ।
আকুল জিবন না বান্ধই থেহা ॥

*gauraka prema bharala majhu dehā |*
*ākula jibana nā bāndhai thehā ||*

*Word for word:* gauraka prema — love for Gaura; bharala majhu dehā — filled my body; ākula jibana — my life in distress; nā bāndhai thehā — finds no support

**22.3.** Love for Gaura filled my body;
my life in distress could find no support.

গৌর গৌর করি উঠলুঁ রোই ।
জাগল গুরুজন কহে পুন কোই ॥

*gaura gaura kari uṭhalum̐ roi |*
*jāgala gurujana kahe puna koi ||*

*Word for word:* gaura gaura kari — crying "Gaura, Gaura"; uṭhalum̐ roi — I rose weeping; jāgala gurujana — the elders woke; kahe puna koi — they say: "who is it again?"

**22.4.** Weeping "Gaura, Gaura!" I rose —
the elders woke: "Who is it again?"

গৌর নাম সভে শূনল কাণে ।
গুরুজন তবহিঁ করল চিতে আনে ॥

*gaura nāma sabhe śūnala kāṇe |*
*gurujana tabahim̐ karala cite āne ||*

*Word for word:* gaura nāma — Gaura's name; sabhe śunala kāṇe — all heard with their ears; gurujana tabahim̐ — the elders then; karala cite āne — took it otherwise (suspected)

**22.5.** Gaura's name they all heard with their own ears;
then the elders began to suspect.

চৌর চৌর করি উঠায়লুঁ ভাষ ।
বাসুদেব ঘোষ কহে ঐছে বিলাস ॥

*caura caura kari uṭhāyalum̐ bhāṣa |*
*bāsudeba ghoṣa kahe aiche bilāsa ||*

*Word for word:* caura caura kari — crying "thief, thief"; uṭhāyalum̐ bhāṣa — I raised the cry; bāsudeba ghoṣa kahe — says Vasudeva Ghosha; aiche bilāsa — such is the play

**22.6.** I raised the cry: "Thief, thief!" —
says Vasudeva Ghosha: such is the play![^27-60]

[^27-59]: Signature: "Vasudeva Ghosha." PK: vol. 2, PDF p. 97 (printed p. 84), the same section as PK 723, no. 61 (mark
"॥৬১॥৭২৪॥"); raga dhanashi; MS P-R-Sa no. 1198. GPT1 — p. 204, no. 114 (raga dhanashi); GPT2 — sec. 3.2, no. 114. **Catalogue
correction**: row VG-094 counted PK 724 as "Krishna-lila" and excluded it from translation; in fact the pada is about Gaura
(the name "Gaura" in 22.3–22.5) and stands in GPT among the nagari padas. It is not in Majumdar's list (he gives the
neighbouring PK 723). On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section.
[^27-60]: A play on words: "gaura" — "caura" ("thief"): to hide whose name she was calling, the townswoman turns "Gaura" into
"thief." In PK this pada is preceded by a pada of Jnanadasa on Radha (PK 722), where Radha likewise covers an involuntary
"Kanu, Kanu" with the word "Bhanu, Bhanu" (the sun): Vasu transfers a motif of Krishna-lila to the nagaris. MS P-R-Sa:
"canda," "manda" (22.2); "ka," "kha," "cha," P-R-Sa: "śunala" (22.5); "kha," "gha": "I rose" (uṭhalum̐), P-R-Sa: "rose"
(uṭhala) for "I raised the cry" (22.6).

## 23. Vasu Ghosha — "ki kahaba re sakhi ājuka bhāba…" (PK 249)
*Nagari-bhava. A townswoman tells her friend: she was alone, adorning herself and dressing her hair before the mirror — and at
that moment Gora, the king of dancers, appeared; her composure and her modesty gave way; at the sight of Him her body
thrilled, and He took her in His embrace. In PK it follows Radhamohana's gaura-chandrika to the section "telling of the
meeting — another way," under the heading "the words of the nagaris of Navadvipa befitting this rasa." Raga
vibhasa.*[^27-61]

কি কহব রে সখি আজুক ভাব ।
অযতনে মোহে হোয়ল বহু লাভ ॥

*ki kahaba re sakhi ājuka bhāba |*
*ayatane mohe hoyala bahu lābha ||*

*Word for word:* ki kahaba re sakhi — what shall I say, friend; ājuka bhāba — of today's (feeling); ayatane — without effort; mohe hoyala bahu lābha — a great fortune came to me

**23.1.** What shall I say, friend, of today!
Without any effort a great fortune has come to me.

একলি আছিলুঁ হাম বনাইতে বেশ ।
মুকুরে নিরখি মুখ বান্ধলুঁ কেশ ॥

*ekali āchilum̐ hāma banāite beśa |*
*mukure nirakhi mukha bāndhalum̐ keśa ||*

*Word for word:* ekali āchilum̐ hāma — I was alone; banāite beśa — adorning myself; mukure nirakhi mukha — looking at my face in the mirror; bāndhalum̐ keśa — I dressed my hair

**23.2.** I was alone, adorning myself;
looking in the mirror, I was dressing my hair.

তৈখনে মীলল গোরা নটরাজ ।
ধৈরজ ভাঙল কুলবতি লাজ ॥

*taikhane mīlala gorā naṭarāja |*
*dhairaja bhāṅala kulabati lāja ||*

*Word for word:* taikhane — at that moment; mīlala gorā naṭarāja — Gora, the king of dancers, appeared; dhairaja bhāṅgala — composure gave way; kulabati lāja — the modesty of a noble wife

**23.3.** At that moment Gora, the king of dancers, appeared:
the composure and modesty of a noble wife gave way.

দরশনে পুলকে পুরল তনু মোর ।
বাসুদেব ঘোষ কহে করলহি কোর ॥

*daraśane pulake purala tanu mora |*
*bāsudeba ghoṣa kahe karalahi kora ||*

*Word for word:* daraśane — at the sight; pulake pūrala tanu mora — my body was filled with thrills; bāsudeba ghoṣa kahe — says Vasudeva Ghosha; karalahi kora — [He] took into His embrace

**23.4.** At the sight [of Him] my body thrilled all over —
says Vasudeva Ghosha: He took [me] in His embrace.[^27-62]

[^27-61]: Signature: "Vasudeva Ghosha." PK: vol. 1, PDF pp. 178–179 (printed pp. 167–168), section "atha punaśca
rasodgāraprakārāntaramāha" — after the gaura-chandrika of Radhamohana Dasa (PK 248) — the subsection "tadrasocita-nabadvīpa-nāgarīṇāṃ uktiḥ"
(the words of the nagaris of Navadvipa befitting this rasa), no. 2 (mark "॥২॥২৪৯॥"); raga vibhasa; MS P-R no. 1364. GPT1 —
p. 203, no. 111 (raga vibhasa); GPT2 — sec. 3.2, no. 111 (catalogue: VG-026). On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the
section.
[^27-62]: The last line describes an embrace — sambhoga-nagari (cf. note 56); we translate it exactly. An important variant: in
MS P-R the couplet is different — "At the sight my body was filled with thrills; says Vasudeva: Gora is young and fresh"
(daraśe pūrala tanu pulakita mora, bāsudeba kahe gorā naola kiśora), without the embrace. MS P-R: "today with effort He gave
me fortune" (23.1), "I" (āmi), "there I dressed" (tahi bāndhala, 23.2), "fled" (bhāgala, 23.3); "ka," "kha": "dressed"
(bāndhala).

## 24. Vasu Ghosha — "hari hari gorā kothā gela…" (PK 1636)
*Nagari-bhava. A townswoman's lament after Gaura has gone: where has Gora gone? what cruel Creator sent this grief? Her heart
is wounded; she cannot weep aloud, like a thief's wife; she is a daughter of a noble family and does not leave the house, and
even in dreams she cannot see Him; to whom can she tell of His beauty and His pastimes? "Why does not a thunderbolt fall on
my head?" In PK it stands in the section "the lament of the devotees, and also of the nagaris of Navadvipa, in separation
from Gaurachandra." Raga suhai.*[^27-63]

হরি হরি গোরা কোথা গেল ।
কোন নিদারুণ বিধি এত দুখ দিল ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*hari hari gorā kothā gela |*
*kona nidāruṇa bidhi eta dukha dila || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* hari hari — Hari, Hari! (a cry of grief); gorā kothā gela — where has Gora gone; kona nidāruṇa bidhi — what pitiless Creator; eta dukha dila — has given such grief

**24.1.** *(Refrain)* Hari, Hari! Where has Gora gone?
What pitiless Creator has sent such grief?

হিয়া মোর জরজর পাঁজর ধসে ।
পরাণ গেল যদি পিরিতি কিসে ॥

*hiyā mora jarajara pām̐jara dhase |*
*parāṇa gela yadi piriti kise ||*

*Word for word:* hiyā mora jarajara — my heart is wounded; pām̐jara dhase — the ribs crumble; parāṇa gela yadi — if life has gone; piriti kise — in what then is love

**24.2.** My heart is wounded, my ribs are crumbling;
since life is leaving — what then is left of love?

ফুকারি কান্দিতে নারি চোরের রমণী ।
অনুক্ষণ পড়ে মনে গোরা-মুখখানি ॥

*phukāri kāndite nāri corera ramaṇī |*
*anukṣaṇa paṛe mane gorā-mukhakhāni ||*

*Word for word:* phukāri kāndite nāri — I cannot weep aloud; corera ramaṇī — a thief's wife; anukṣaṇa paṛe mane — every moment comes to mind; gorā-mukhakhāni — Gora's face

**24.3.** I cannot weep aloud — I am like a thief's wife;
every moment I remember Gora's face.[^27-64]

ঘরের বাহিরি নহি কুলের ঝি ।
স্বপনে না হয় দেখা করিব কি ॥

*gharera bāhiri nahi kulera jhi |*
*svapane nā haya dekhā kariba ki ||*

*Word for word:* gharera bāhiri nahi — I do not go out of the house; kulera jhi — a daughter of a noble family; svapane nā haya dekhā — even in dreams there is no meeting; kariba ki — what shall I do

**24.4.** I am a daughter of a noble family, I do not leave the house;
even in dreams I cannot see Him — what shall I do?

সে রূপ-মাধুরী লীলা কাহারে কহিব ।
গোরা পহুঁ বিনে মুঞি অনলে পশিব ॥

*se rūpa-mādhurī līlā kāhāre kahiba |*
*gorā pahum̐ bine muñi anale paśiba ||*

*Word for word:* se rūpa-mādhurī līlā — that sweet beauty and the pastimes; kāhāre kahiba — to whom shall I tell; gorā pahum̐ bine — without Gora, the Lord; muñi anale paśiba — I will enter the fire

**24.5.** To whom shall I tell of that sweet beauty and those pastimes?
Without Gora, my Lord, I will enter the fire.[^27-65]

গোরা বিনু প্রাণ রহে এহ বড় লাজ ।
বাসু কহে কেনে মুণ্ডে না পড়য়ে বাজ ॥

*gorā binu prāṇa rahe eha baṛa lāja |*
*bāsu kahe kene muṇḍe nā paṛaye bāja ||*

*Word for word:* gorā binu — without Gora; prāṇa rahe — life remains; eha baṛa lāja — this is a great shame; bāsu kahe — says Vasu; kene muṇḍe nā paṛaye bāja — why does no thunderbolt fall on my head

**24.6.** That life holds on without Gora — this is a great shame.
Says Vasu: why does not a thunderbolt fall on my head?

[^27-63]: Signature: "Vasu." PK: vol. 3, PDF pp. 37–38 (printed pp. 26–27), 4th shakha, section "atha śrīgauracandra-biraheṇa
bhaktagaṇasya tathā nabadvīpa-nāgarīṇāṃ bilāpo yathā" (the lament of the devotees, and also of the nagaris of Navadvipa, in separation from
Gaurachandra), no. 3 (mark "॥৩॥১৬৩৬॥"); raga suhai (P-R: sindhura); MSS P-R-Sa no. 859 and P-R no. 40/111. GPT1 — p. 388,
no. 19 (raga suhai) — in the section "the lament of Shachi and Vishnupriya"; GPT2 — sec. 5.4, no. 19 (catalogue: VG-076, where
this pada is separated from "gela gaura nā gela baliyā," GPT 5.4 no. 18 — GPT only). Separation after the sannyasa. On
nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section.
[^27-64]: A proverb: a thief's wife dare not mourn her husband aloud — her grief is secret. So the townswoman cannot weep openly
for Gaura. MSS "ka," "kha," P-R: "she cannot" (nāre) for "I cannot"; P-R: "form" (gorā-baraṇa) for "face" (24.3); for
"crumbling" P-R has khase ("falling away").
[^27-65]: "I will enter the fire" — a formula of despair in separation, as in the padas on Radha. MS P-R lacks couplets
24.4–24.5; "kha": "bine" (24.6); "ka": "ei," "kha," "gha," P-R-Sa, P-R: "iha" for "eha" (24.6); P-R: "fell" (paṛila, 24.6).

## 25. Vasu Ghosha — "kaha sakhi jibana-upāya…" (PK 1669)
*Nagari-bhava. A lament after Gaura has gone: "Tell me, friend, how shall I live? Gora, the king of dancers, has left [me]";
her body has wasted away, how many days can she live in separation? where can she go to see His face? what has the Creator
written on her forehead? to whom can she tell this grief? In PK it is the gaura-chandrika to the section on Radha's lament
in external consciousness; in GPT it stands among the laments of Shachi and Vishnupriya. Raga suhai.*[^27-66]

কহ সখি জিবন-উপায় ।
ছাড়ি গেল গোরা নট-রায় ॥

*kaha sakhi jibana-upāya |*
*chāṛi gela gorā naṭa-rāya ||*

*Word for word:* kaha sakhi — tell me, friend; jibana-upāya — a means to live; chāṛi gela — has left; gorā naṭa-rāya — Gora, the king of dancers

**25.1.** Tell me, friend, how shall I live?
Gora, the king of dancers, has left [me].

ভাবি ভাবি তনু ভেল ক্ষীণ ।
বিচ্ছেদে বাঁচিব কত দিন ॥

*bhābi bhābi tanu bhela kṣīṇa |*
*bicchede bām̐ciba kata dina ||*

*Word for word:* bhābi bhābi — pining and pining; tanu bhela kṣīṇa — the body has wasted away; bicchede bām̐ciba — shall I live in separation; kata dina — how many days

**25.2.** Pining [for Him], my body has wasted away;
how many days shall I live in separation?

নিরমল গৌরাঙ্গ-বদন ।
কোথা গেলে পাব দরশন ॥

*niramala gaurāṅga-badana |*
*kothā gele pāba daraśana ||*

*Word for word:* niramala gaurāṅga-badana — Gauranga's pure face; kothā gele — going where; pāba daraśana — shall I see (obtain darshan)

**25.3.** Gauranga's pure face —
where shall I go to see it?

কি বিহি লিখিল মোর ভালে ।
চিড়ি দেখি কি আছে কপালে ॥

*ki bihi likhila mora bhāle |*
*ciṛi dekhi ki āche kapāle ||*

*Word for word:* ki bihi likhila — what has the Creator written; mora bhāle — on my forehead; ciṛi dekhi — I will cut it open and see; ki āche kapāle — what is there on my brow (in my fate)

**25.4.** What has the Creator written on my forehead?
I will cut it open and see what is there on my brow![^27-67]

হিয়া জরজর অনুরাগে ।
এ দুখ কহিব কার আগে ॥

*hiyā jarajara anurāge |*
*e dukha kahiba kāra āge ||*

*Word for word:* hiyā jarajara — the heart is wounded; anurāge — by love; e dukha kahiba — this grief shall I tell; kāra āge — to whom (before whom)

**25.5.** My heart is wounded with love —
to whom shall I tell this grief?

কহ বাসু ঘোষ নিদান ।
গোরা বিনু না রহে পরাণ ॥

*kaha bāsu ghoṣa nidāna |*
*gorā binu nā rahe parāṇa ||*

*Word for word:* kaha bāsu ghoṣa — says Vasu Ghosha; nidāna — the end, the last word; gorā binu — without Gora; nā rahe parāṇa — life does not remain

**25.6.** Says Vasu Ghosha at the last:
without Gora life cannot be kept.[^27-68]

[^27-66]: Signature: "Vasu Ghosha." PK: vol. 3, PDF pp. 54–55 (printed pp. 43–44), section "atha kebalaṃ bāhya-daśāyāṃ bilāpo yathā |
tatra śrīgauracandraḥ" (lament in external consciousness; gaura-chandrika), no. 8 (mark "॥৮॥১৬৬৯॥"); raga suhai (P-R: pahida and
gandhara — the pada stands in it twice); MSS P-R-Sa no. 892 and P-R nos. 40/15, 43/12. GPT1 — p. 388, no. 20; GPT2 — sec. 5.4,
no. 20 (catalogue: VG-117). The pada does not name the speaker; GPT assigns it to Vishnupriya's lament, PK to the words of the
townswomen (according to Majumdar, nagari-bhava). Separation after the sannyasa. On nagari-bhava see the introductory note
to the section.
[^27-67]: According to popular belief, the Creator (bidhi) writes a person's fate on his forehead. The Creator is Brahma, not
the Lord.
[^27-68]: Lit. "says Vasu Ghosha the end (nidāna)": the last word, the verdict. GPT1: "kahe bāsu ghoṣa nidāna." MS P-R: "said
Vasu Ghosha" (bāsu ghoṣe kahila), "I will give up [life]" (tejiba) for "cannot be kept" (25.6); "ka," "cha," P-R-Sa:
"jībana" (25.1); P-R: "goes" (yāya, 25.1), "shedding tears" (jhuri jhuri) for "pining," "became" (haila, 25.2), "in this grief I
will pass" (e duḥkhe bañciba, 25.2), and instead of 25.3: "Shall I see again that pure moonlike face?" (puna ki pāiba
daraśana, niramala o cām̐nda-badana).

## Note to Chapter 27

*Vasu Ghosha in PK — 25 nagari padas (including PK 724, which the catalogue mistakenly regarded as Krishna-lila, and PK 2176 —
the nagari recension of PK 973). Of Majumdar's list, PK 2219 (a pada of Lochana Dasa signed "e dāsa locana gāya") and PK 2228
(already translated, chapter 4, no. 16) are not included. Vasu's nagari padas known only from GPT (VG-020, 022, 024, 025,
027–030, 032, 040, 168, 169, 182 and others), as well as the nagari padas of other poets in the same pallavas of PK
(Nayanananda — PK 2170, 2177; Lochana Dasa — PK 2174; Govinda Dasa — PK 2168 and others), are in chapter 28.*

---

# Chapter 28. Nagari Padas — II: Vasu Ghosha (padas from GPT), Nayanananda, Yadu, Murari, Balarama Dasa, Chandrashekhara, Lochana Dasa

*On what nagari-bhava is, the position of the tradition (Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja, Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati) and the rules of translation, see the introductory note to the section of nagari padas in chapter 27.*

## 1. Vasu Ghosha — "ki herinu ogo sai bidagadha-rāja…" (KGC 5.1; GPT1 p. 162, no. 16)
*Nagari-bhava (only in the address to a friend). "What have I seen, friend — the king of those versed in rasa!" Gaura is the
wish-fulfilling tree of the devotees in the midst of Navadvipa: its branches are love, its leaves anuraga, its flowers longing,
its fruit pure prema, from which rasa flows without end; the devotees, like birds and bees, taste it, the tree's shade nourishes
all — only the poet is deprived through his own fault. In KGC it is the gaura-chandrika to the 5th kshanada. Raga suhai-deshag.*[^28-1]

কি হেরিনু ওগো সই বিদগধ-রাজ ।
ভকত-কলপতরু নবদ্বীপ মাঝ ॥

*ki herinu ogo sai bidagadha-rāja |*
*bhakata-kalapataru nabadvīpa mājha ||*

*Word for word:* ki herinu — what have I seen; ogo sai — O friend; bidagadha-rāja — the king of the vidagdhas (those versed in rasa); bhakata-kalapataru — the wish-fulfilling tree of the devotees; nabadvīpa mājha — in the midst of Navadvipa

**1.1.** What have I seen, friend! — the king of those versed in rasa,
the wish-fulfilling tree of the devotees in the midst of Navadvipa.[^28-2]

পিরীতির শাখা সব অনুরাগ-পাতে ।
কুসুম আরতি তাহে জগত মোহিতে ॥

*pirītira śākhā saba anurāga-pāte |*
*kusuma ārati tāhe jagata mohite ||*

*Word for word:* pirītira śākhā saba — all its branches are love; anurāga-pāte — with leaves of anuraga; kusuma ārati — its flowers are longing (ārati); tāhe — on it; jagata mohite — to enchant the world

**1.2.** Its branches are love, its leaves are anuraga,
its flowers are longing, to enchant the world.

নিরমল প্রেম-ফল ফলে সর্বকাল ।
এক ফলে নব রস ঝরয়ে অপার ॥

*niramala prema-phala phale sarvakāla |*
*eka phale naba rasa jharaye apāra ||*

*Word for word:* niramala prema-phala — the pure fruit of prema; phale sarvakāla — ripens at all times; eka phale — from a single fruit; naba rasa — fresh (or: ninefold) rasa; jharaye apāra — flows without end

**1.3.** At all times the pure fruit of prema ripens on it;
from a single fruit ever-fresh rasa flows without end.[^28-3]

ভকত চাতক পিক শুক অলি হংস ।
নিরবধি বিলসয়ে রস পরশংস ॥

*bhakata cātaka pika śuka ali haṃsa |*
*nirabadhi bilasaye rasa paraśaṃsa ||*

*Word for word:* bhakata — the devotees; cātaka pika śuka ali haṃsa — chatakas, cuckoos, parrots, bees, swans; nirabadhi — ceaselessly; bilasaye — delight; rasa paraśaṃsa — praising the rasa

**1.4.** The devotees — chatakas, cuckoos, parrots, bees, swans —
ceaselessly delight in it, praising its rasa.

স্থির চর সুর নর যার ছায়া পোষে ।
বাসুদেব বঞ্চিত আপন কর্ম-দোষে ॥

*sthira cara sura nara yāra chāyā poṣe |*
*bāsudeba bañcita āpana karma-doṣe ||*

*Word for word:* sthira cara — the unmoving and the moving; sura nara — gods and men; yāra chāyā poṣe — whose shade nourishes; bāsudeba bañcita — Vasudeva is deprived; āpana karma-doṣe — through the fault of his own deeds

**1.5.** The unmoving and the moving, gods and men, are nourished by its shade —
only Vasudeva is deprived through the fault of his own deeds.[^28-4]

[^28-1]: Signature: "Vasudeva." KGC (Vishvanatha Chakravarti, late 17th c.; ed. 1925) — 5th kshanada ("krishna-panchami"), no. 1,
"śrīgauracandrasya" (gaura-chandrika), raga suhai-deshag, p. 34 (scan PDF p. 66). GPT1 — p. 162, no. 16 (raga suhai or desharaga;
scan PDF p. 421); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 16 (catalogue: VG-020). The pada is not in PK. The catalogue listed it as "GPT only";
the KGC witness was found in preparing this chapter (attribution to Vasu by KGC and GPT, A). In GPT the pada stands in the section
of nagari padas (3.2), but the nagari motif in it is only the address "friend": in substance it praises Gaura in the image of the
wish-fulfilling tree. On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^28-2]: "The king of those versed in rasa" (bidagadha-rāja): a vidagdha is a connoisseur, finely sensitive to rasa; so Krishna is
called. "Wish-fulfilling tree" (kalpataru) — an image known from CC (Adi 9: the Lord is both the gardener and the tree of prema itself,
giving its fruits to all). GPT1 notes a variant of the first line: "What shall I say, friend, of a wondrous thing!"
[^28-3]: "Ever-fresh rasa" (nava rasa) can also be understood as "ninefold rasa" (all rasas in one fruit). "Longing" (ārati) is eager
yearning, not the arati rite.
[^28-4]: Self-abasement in the signature is a usual device of Vaishnava poets (cf. "Vasudeva is deprived" in Vasu's padas — chapter 27).
Instead of this couplet GPT1 gives a variant: "the bee-devotees seek the wish-fulfilling tree [of His feet]; says Vasu: wondrous is
this on earth"; instead of 1.4b — "many bhavas arose, but the hope was not fulfilled." KGC: "its shade nourishes" (poṣe), GPT:
"enter its shade" (paise).

## 2. Vasu Ghosha — "āju mui ki dekhilum̐ gorā naṭarāya…" (GPT1 p. 164, no. 23; GCd, no. 12)
*Nagari-bhava. "What have I seen today — Gora, the king of dancers!" The Creator made Him, putting in so much rasa; His body
surpasses gold, His face a hundred moons, His eyes steal the hearts of women; on the bank of the Suradhuni Gorachand shines.
Raga dhanashi.*[^28-5]

আজু মুই কি দেখিলুঁ গোরা নটরায় ।
অসীম মহিমা গোরার কহনে না যায় ॥

*āju mui ki dekhilum̐ gorā naṭarāya |*
*asīma mahimā gorāra kahane nā yāya ||*

*Word for word:* āju — today; mui ki dekhilum̐ — what have I seen; gorā naṭarāya — Gora, the king of dancers; asīma mahimā gorāra — Gora's boundless glory; kahane nā yāya — cannot be told

**2.1.** What have I seen today — Gora, the king of dancers!
Gora's boundless glory cannot be told.

কেমনে গঢ়ল বিধি কত রস দিয়া ।
ঢল ঢল গোরা-তনু কাঞ্চন জিনিয়া ॥

*kemane gaṛhala bidhi kata rasa diyā |*
*ḍhala ḍhala gorā-tanu kāñcana jiniyā ||*

*Word for word:* kemane gaṛhala bidhi — how did the Creator fashion; kata rasa diyā — putting in so much rasa; ḍhala ḍhala — rippling, overflowing; gorā-tanu — Gora's body; kāñcana jiniyā — surpassing gold

**2.2.** How did the Creator fashion Him, putting in so much rasa!
Gora's body ripples with radiance, surpassing gold.

কত শত চাঁদ জিনি বদন-কমল ।
রমণীর চিত হরে নয়ন-যুগল ॥

*kata śata cām̐da jini badana-kamala |*
*ramaṇīra cita hare nayana-yugala ||*

*Word for word:* kata śata cām̐da jini — surpassing hundreds of moons; badana-kamala — the lotus face; ramaṇīra cita hare — steals the hearts of women; nayana-yugala — the pair of eyes

**2.3.** His lotus face is lovelier than hundreds of moons;
the pair of His eyes steals the hearts of women.[^28-6]

বাসুদেব ঘোষ কহে হইয়া বিভোর ।
সুরধুনী-তীরে গোরাচাঁদ উজোর ॥

*bāsudeba ghoṣa kahe haiyā bibhora |*
*suradhunī-tīre gorācām̐da ujora ||*

*Word for word:* bāsudeba ghoṣa kahe — says Vasudeva Ghosha; haiyā bibhora — lost [in rapture]; suradhunī-tīre — on the bank of the Suradhuni; gorācām̐da ujora — Gorachand shines

**2.4.** Says Vasudeva Ghosha, lost in rapture:
on the bank of the Suradhuni Gorachand shines.

[^28-5]: Signature: "Vasudeva Ghosha." GPT1 — p. 164, no. 23 (raga dhanashi; scan PDF p. 423); GPT2 — sect. 3.2 (in the same series,
after VG-025). The catalogue had no row for it (**new row**: VG-184). Witness: the *Gita-chandrodaya* of Narahari Chakravarti (GCd;
ed. 1948, p. 72, gaura-chandrikas to Radha's purvaraga, no. 12, raga suhai) — with the same signature; there it stands among
Vasu's nagari padas known from PK (PK 2169, 28, 2172, 899, 777 — chapter 27, nos. 9, 15, 11, 17, 16). The pada is not in PK or KGC; attribution to
Vasu by GPT and GCd (B). On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^28-6]: "Steal the hearts of women" is a formula of the poetics of beauty, as in the padas on Krishna (cf. chapter 27, note 6). GCd:
"how many moons," "ripples" (ḍharaḍhara), in 2.4 — "Gora has lit up the bank of the Suradhuni."

## 3. Vasu Ghosha — "āju mui ki pekhalum̐ gaurāṅga sundara…" (GPT1 p. 164, no. 24)
*Nagari-bhava. "What have I seen today — the beautiful Gauranga: in the three worlds there is no such nagara!" Noble wives are
enchanted by His form, trees thrill hearing of His virtues, stones melt, beasts and birds weep, the townswomen cannot hold their
hearts steady, gods, siddhas and sages are in turmoil: Gora is Madana-mohana. Raga dhanashi.*[^28-7]

আজু মুই কি পেখলুঁ গৌরাঙ্গ সুন্দর ।
এ তিন ভুবনে নাই এমন নাগর ॥

*āju mui ki pekhalum̐ gaurāṅga sundara |*
*e tina bhubane nāi emana nāgara ||*

*Word for word:* āju mui ki pekhalum̐ — what have I seen today; gaurāṅga sundara — the beautiful Gauranga; e tina bhubane — in these three worlds; nāi emana nāgara — there is no such nagara

**3.1.** What have I seen today — the beautiful Gauranga!
In these three worlds there is no such nagara.[^28-8]

কুলবতী সব রূপ দেখিয়া মোহিত ।
গুণ শুনি তরু-লতা হয় পুলকিত ॥

*kulabatī saba rūpa dekhiyā mohita |*
*guṇa śuni taru-latā haya pulakita ||*

*Word for word:* kulabatī saba — all the noble wives; rūpa dekhiyā mohita — are enchanted, seeing [His] form; guṇa śuni — hearing of [His] virtues; taru-latā — trees and creepers; haya pulakita — thrill

**3.2.** All the noble wives are enchanted, seeing His form;
trees and creepers thrill, hearing of His virtues.

শিলা গলি গলি বহে মৃগ পাখী কাঁদে ।
নগরের নাগরী সব বুক নাহি বাঁধে ॥

*śilā gali gali bahe mṛga pākhī kām̐de |*
*nagarera nāgarī saba buka nāhi bām̐dhe ||*

*Word for word:* śilā gali gali bahe — stones melt and flow; mṛga pākhī kām̐de — beasts and birds weep; nagarera nāgarī saba — all the women of the town; buka nāhi bām̐dhe — cannot hold their hearts steady

**3.3.** Stones melt and flow, beasts and birds weep;
all the women of the town cannot hold their hearts steady.

সুর-সিদ্ধ-মুনিগণের মন উচাটন ।
বাসুদেব কহে গোরা মদনমোহন ॥

*sura-siddha-munigaṇera mana ucāṭana |*
*bāsudeba kahe gorā madanamohana ||*

*Word for word:* sura-siddha-munigaṇera — of the gods, siddhas and sages; mana ucāṭana — the mind is in turmoil; bāsudeba kahe — says Vasudeva; gorā madanamohana — Gora is Madana-mohana

**3.4.** The gods, siddhas and sages are in turmoil of heart.
Says Vasudeva: Gora is Madana-mohana.[^28-9]

[^28-7]: Signature: "Vasudeva." GPT1 — p. 164, no. 24 (raga dhanashi; scan PDF p. 423); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 24 (catalogue: VG-182).
The pada is not in PK, KGC or GCd; attribution to Vasu by GPT only (C). It is close to Vasu's PK 2151 (chapter 27, no. 1: "birds,
beasts and trees weep hearing of His virtues; noble wives cannot hold their hearts steady"), but it is a different text. On
nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^28-8]: "Nagara" (nāgara) — townsman, gallant, in poetry the beloved (introductory note); so a townswoman speaks of the young Gaura.
