[^28-9]: Madana-mohana — "the enchanter of the god of love himself," a name of Krishna: the Lord's beauty conquers even Kamadeva.
"Cannot hold their hearts steady" (lit. "bind the breast") is a general formula of beauty (chapter 27, note 2). GPT1: "nagarī" — a
misprint for "nāgarī" (GPT2).

## 4. Vasu Ghosha — "sajani lo gorārūpa janu kām̐cā sonā…" (GPT1 pp. 162–163, no. 19)
*Nagari-bhava. "Friend, Gora's form is like pure gold: seeing it, a woman cannot stay at home." His form has fixed itself in
her eyes, wherever she looks there is Gora; He seems familiar, yet she cannot make out who He is. The poet answers: "Townswoman,
that is the stealer of the gopis' hearts!" Raga suhai.*[^28-10]

সজনি লো গোরারূপ জনু কাঁচা সোনা ।
দেখিতে নারীর মন ঘরেতে টিকে না ॥

*sajani lo gorārūpa janu kām̐cā sonā |*
*dekhite nārīra mana gharete ṭike nā ||*

*Word for word:* sajani lo — friend; gorārūpa — Gora's form; janu kām̐cā sonā — like pure (unworked) gold; dekhite — seeing [it]; nārīra mana — a woman's heart; gharete ṭike nā — does not stay at home

**4.1.** Friend, Gora's form is like pure gold:
seeing it, a woman cannot stay at home.

বাঁকা ভুরু বাঁকা নয়ন চাহনিতে যায় চেনা ।
ও রূপে মন দিলে সই কুলমান থাকে না ॥

*bām̐kā bhuru bām̐kā nayana cāhanite yāya cenā |*
*o rūpe mana dile sai kulamāna thāke nā ||*

*Word for word:* bām̐kā bhuru — curved brows; bām̐kā nayana — slanting eyes; cāhanite yāya cenā — by the glance one knows [Him]; o rūpe mana dile — if one gives one's heart to that form; sai — friend; kulamāna thāke nā — the family's honour does not remain

**4.2.** Curved brows, slanting eyes — by His glance you know Him;
give your heart to that form, friend, and no family honour remains.[^28-11]

নয়নে লেগেছে রূপ না যায় পাশরা ।
যেদিকে চাই দেখিতে পাই শুধুই সেই গোরা ॥

*nayane legeche rūpa nā yāya pāśarā |*
*yedike cāi dekhite pāi śudhui sei gorā ||*

*Word for word:* nayane legeche rūpa — the form has fixed itself in my eyes; nā yāya pāśarā — it cannot be forgotten; yedike cāi — wherever I look; dekhite pāi — I see; śudhui sei gorā — only that Gora

**4.3.** The form has fixed itself in my eyes — I cannot forget it:
wherever I look, I see only that Gora.

চিন চিন লাগে কিন্তু চিনতে না যায় পারা ।
বাসু কহে নাগরি ঐ গোপীর মনচোরা ॥

*cina cina lāge kintu cinate nā yāya pārā |*
*bāsu kahe nāgari ai gopīra manacorā ||*

*Word for word:* cina cina lāge — He seems familiar, so familiar; kintu cinate nā yāya pārā — but I cannot make out who He is; bāsu kahe — says Vasu; nāgari — O townswoman; ai gopīra manacorā — that is the stealer of the gopis' hearts

**4.4.** He seems familiar, so familiar, yet I cannot make out who He is.
Says Vasu: townswoman, that is the stealer of the gopis' hearts![^28-12]

[^28-10]: Signature: "Vasu." GPT1 — pp. 162–163, no. 19 (raga suhai; scan PDF pp. 421–422); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 19 (catalogue:
VG-022). The pada is not in PK, KGC, PS or GCd; attribution to Vasu by GPT only (C). The language is late and colloquial
("legeche," "cinate," "śudhui"), which, like the absence of early witnesses, tells against Vasu's authorship (cf. Majumdar's argument
on the unreliability of GPT — introductory note to the section). On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^28-11]: "No family honour remains" is a nagari motif (a woman ready to disregard her family's honour for Gaura), transferred from the
padas on Radha and Krishna; translated as in the original (introductory note, rule 2).
[^28-12]: The poet's answer reveals what the townswoman cannot grasp: Gora is Krishna Himself, "the stealer of the gopis' hearts," and
that is why He seems familiar to her. This is a tenet of gaura-tattva (Gaura is Krishna who has taken Radha's bhava and luster;
CC Adi 1.5); it does not make Gaura the hero of a love play in Navadvipa (introductory note). GPT2: "e" ("this") instead of "ai".

## 5. Vasu Ghosha — "nirabadhi gorārūpa dekhi…" (GPT1 p. 164, no. 25)
*Nagari-bhava. "Ceaselessly I see Gora's form — streams flow from my eyes": night and day the townswoman knows nothing, the jewel
of brahmanas has entered her inmost heart; not seeing Gorachand's face, she cannot hold on to life. Raga dhanashi.*[^28-13]

নিরবধি গোরারূপ দেখি ।
নিঝরে ঝরয়ে দুটী আঁখি ॥

*nirabadhi gorārūpa dekhi |*
*nijhare jharaye duṭī ām̐khi ||*

*Word for word:* nirabadhi — ceaselessly; gorārūpa dekhi — I see Gora's form; nijhare jharaye — stream like a waterfall; duṭī ām̐khi — both eyes

**5.1.** Ceaselessly I see Gora's form —
from both my eyes it streams like a waterfall.

কি কহব কি হবে উপায় ।
প্রাণ মোর ধরণে না যায় ॥

*ki kahaba ki habe upāya |*
*prāṇa mora dharaṇe nā yāya ||*

*Word for word:* ki kahaba — what shall I say; ki habe upāya — what will be the remedy; prāṇa mora — my life; dharaṇe nā yāya — cannot be held

**5.2.** What shall I say? Where is my remedy?
My life will not stay in me.

নিশি দিশি কিছুই না জানি ।
মরমে লাগিল দ্বিজমণি ॥

*niśi diśi kichui nā jāni |*
*marame lāgila dvijamaṇi ||*

*Word for word:* niśi diśi — night and day; kichui nā jāni — I know nothing; marame lāgila — has pierced my inmost heart; dvijamaṇi — the jewel of the twice-born

**5.3.** Night and day I know nothing:
the jewel of brahmanas has entered my inmost heart.[^28-14]

না দেখিয়া গোরাচাঁদ-মুখ ।
কহে বাসু বিদরয়ে বুক ॥

*nā dekhiyā gorācām̐da-mukha |*
*kahe bāsu bidaraye buka ||*

*Word for word:* nā dekhiyā — not seeing; gorācām̐da-mukha — Gorachand's face; kahe bāsu — says Vasu; bidaraye buka — the breast breaks

**5.4.** Not seeing Gorachand's face —
says Vasu — the breast breaks.

[^28-13]: Signature: "Vasu." GPT1 — p. 164, no. 25 (raga dhanashi; scan PDF p. 423); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, in the same series (the number
is unclear in the OCR). The catalogue had no row for it (**new row**: VG-185). The pada is not in PK, KGC or GCd; attribution to
Vasu by GPT only (C). On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^28-14]: "The jewel of brahmanas" (dvijamaṇi) — the young Gaura, best of brahmanas (cf. chapter 27, note 8).

## 6. Vasu Ghosha — "dekhiyā āyalum̐ gorācām̐de…" (GPT1 p. 164, no. 26)
*Nagari-bhava. "I have seen Gorachand — and since then my soul weeps": not seeing His moon-face, the townswoman finds no rest,
household work falls from her hands; Gauranga's glory has no limit. Raga dhanashi.*[^28-15]

দেখিয়া আয়লুঁ গোরাচাঁদে ।
সেই হৈতে প্রাণ মোর কাঁদে ॥

*dekhiyā āyalum̐ gorācām̐de |*
*sei haite prāṇa mora kām̐de ||*

*Word for word:* dekhiyā āyalum̐ — I came back having seen; gorācām̐de — Gorachand; sei haite — since then; prāṇa mora kām̐de — my soul weeps

**6.1.** I came back having seen Gorachand —
and since then my soul weeps.

মন মোর করে ছন ছন ।
না দেখিলে ও চাঁদ-বদন ॥

*mana mora kare chana chana |*
*nā dekhile o cām̐da-badana ||*

*Word for word:* mana mora — my heart; kare chana chana — is restless, finds no rest; nā dekhile — when I do not see; o cām̐da-badana — that moon-face

**6.2.** My heart is restless, finds no peace,
when I do not see that moon-face.

গৃহকাজে নাহি রহে চিত ।
না দেখিয়া গৌর-চরিত ॥

*gṛhakāje nāhi rahe cita |*
*nā dekhiyā gaura-carita ||*

*Word for word:* gṛhakāje — on household work; nāhi rahe cita — the mind does not stay; nā dekhiyā — not seeing; gaura-carita — Gaura's deeds

**6.3.** My mind will not stay on household work
when I do not see Gaura's deeds.

অনুপম গৌরাঙ্গ-মহিমা ।
বাসুদেব না পায়েন সীমা ॥

*anupama gaurāṅga-mahimā |*
*bāsudeba nā pāyena sīmā ||*

*Word for word:* anupama — matchless; gaurāṅga-mahimā — Gauranga's glory; bāsudeba — Vasudeva; nā pāyena sīmā — finds no limit

**6.4.** Matchless is Gauranga's glory:
Vasudeva finds no limit to it.[^28-16]

[^28-15]: Signature: "Vasudeva." GPT1 — p. 164, no. 26 (raga dhanashi; scan PDF p. 423); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, in the same series. The
catalogue had no row for it (**new row**: VG-186). The pada is not in PK, KGC or GCd; attribution to Vasu by GPT only (C). On
nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^28-16]: The last couplet passes from the townswoman's words to the poet's praise: Gaura's glory has no limit (cf. chapter 27, no. 1:
"in the three worlds there is none who could set a limit to His beauty").

## 7. Vasu Ghosha — "so bahuballabha gorā jagatera manacorā…" (GPT1 pp. 163–164, no. 22)
*Nagari-bhava. "Gora is beloved of many, He steals the hearts of all the world — why then should I want Him to be mine alone?
Yet whose heart can bear the sharing!" The townswoman gives family, honour, life and youth for the treasure that is Gora; without
Him she will enter the waters of the Suradhuni. Raga vibhasa.*[^28-17]

সো বহুবল্লভ গোরা জগতের মনচোরা
তবে কেন আমার করিতে চাই একা ।
হেন ধন অন্যে দিতে পারে বল কার চিতে
ভাগাভাগি নাহি যায় দেখা ॥

*so bahuballabha gorā jagatera manacorā*
*tabe kena āmāra karite cāi ekā |*
*hena dhana anye dite pāre bala kāra cite*
*bhāgābhāgi nāhi yāya dekhā ||*

*Word for word:* so bahuballabha gorā — He, Gora, beloved of many; jagatera manacorā — the stealer of the world's hearts; tabe kena — why then; āmāra karite cāi ekā — do I want to make Him mine alone; hena dhana — such a treasure; anye dite — to give to another; pāre bala kāra cite — say, whose heart can bear; bhāgābhāgi — sharing; nāhi yāya dekhā — cannot be borne to see

**7.1.** He is Gora, beloved of many, the stealer of all the world's hearts —
why then do I want Him to be mine alone?
But say, whose heart could give such a treasure to another?
The sharing is unbearable to see.[^28-18]

সজনি লো মনের মরম কই তোরে ।
না হেরি গৌরাঙ্গ-মুখ বিদরিয়া যায় বুক
কে চুরি করিল মনচোরে ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*sajani lo manera marama kai tore |*
*nā heri gaurāṅga-mukha bidariyā yāya buka*
*ke curi karila manacore || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* sajani lo — friend; manera marama — the secret of my heart; kai tore — I tell you; nā heri gaurāṅga-mukha — not seeing Gauranga's face; bidariyā yāya buka — the breast breaks; ke curi karila manacore — who has stolen the stealer of hearts

**7.2.** *(Refrain)* Friend, I will tell you my heart's secret:
not seeing Gauranga's face, I feel my breast breaking —
who has stolen the stealer of hearts?

লও কুল লও মান লও শীল লও প্রাণ
লও মোর জীবন যৌবন ।
দেও মোরে গোরানিধি যাহে চাহি নিরবধি
সেই মোর সরবস ধন ॥

*lao kula lao māna lao śīla lao prāṇa*
*lao mora jībana yaubana |*
*deo more gorānidhi yāhe cāhi nirabadhi*
*sei mora sarabasa dhana ||*

*Word for word:* lao kula — take my family; lao māna — take my honour; lao śīla — take my virtue; lao prāṇa — take my life; lao mora jībana yaubana — take my life and youth; deo more — give me; gorānidhi — the treasure, Gora; yāhe cāhi nirabadhi — whom I long for ceaselessly; sei mora sarabasa dhana — He is my whole wealth

**7.3.** Take my family, take my honour, take my virtue, take my life,
take my life and my youth —
give me the treasure, Gora, for whom I ceaselessly long:
He is my whole wealth.

ন তু সুরধুনী-নীরে পশিয়া তেজিব প্রাণ
পরাণের পরাণ মোর গোরা ।
বাসুদেব ঘোষে কয় সে ধন দিবার নয়
দণ্ডে দণ্ডে তিলে হই হারা ॥

*na tu suradhunī-nīre paśiyā tejiba prāṇa*
*parāṇera parāṇa mora gorā |*
*bāsudeba ghoṣe kaya se dhana dibāra naya*
*daṇḍe daṇḍe tile hai hārā ||*

*Word for word:* na tu — otherwise; suradhunī-nīre paśiyā — entering the waters of the Suradhuni; tejiba prāṇa — I will give up my life; parāṇera parāṇa mora gorā — Gora is the life of my life; bāsudeba ghoṣe kaya — says Vasudeva Ghosha; se dhana dibāra naya — that treasure is not to be given; daṇḍe daṇḍe tile — every moment, every instant; hai hārā — I am bereft [of it]

**7.4.** Or else I will enter the waters of the Suradhuni and give up my life:
Gora is the life of my life.
Says Vasudeva Ghosha: that treasure is not given away —
every moment, every instant I am bereft of it.[^28-19]

[^28-17]: Signature: "Vasudeva Ghosha." GPT1 — pp. 163–164, no. 22 (raga vibhasa; scan PDF pp. 422–423); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 22
(catalogue: VG-025). The pada is not in PK, KGC or GCd; attribution to Vasu by GPT only (C). On nagari-bhava see the introductory
note to the section (chapter 27).
[^28-18]: "Beloved of many" (bahuballabha) is an epithet of Krishna, the beloved of all the gopis; the jealousy of a heroine who will not
share her beloved is a motif of the padas on Radha, transferred to a townswoman of Nadia. That Gaura belongs to all (He gave prema to
the whole world) is true; but Gaura's love for the world is mercy, not the love play of a nagara (introductory note). GPT2: "You,
beloved of many, Gora" (to).
[^28-19]: The signature line is ambiguous: "that treasure is not given away" — the poet confirms that Gora cannot be yielded; "every
moment I am bereft" (hai hārā) we take as unceasing separation (cf. chapter 27, note 52); it can also be read "I lose myself."
"I will enter the waters of the Suradhuni," "take my family, honour…" are nagari formulas, translated as in the original.

## 8. Vasu Ghosha — "daṇḍe daṇḍe tile tile gorācām̐da nā dekhile…" (GPT1 p. 296, no. 14)
*Nagari-bhava. "If I do not see Gorachand every moment, I live as one dead": the townswoman wants to keep His golden form always in
her heart; not seeing Him for an instant, she loses her composure; she will set her family's honour adrift on the Suradhuni, burn
her shame and gaze her fill at Gauranga. Raga suhai.*[^28-20]

দণ্ডে দণ্ডে তিলে তিলে গোরাচাঁদ না দেখিলে
মরমে মরিয়া যেন থাকি ।
সাধ হয় নিরন্তর হেমকান্তি কলেবর
হিয়ার মাঝারে সদা রাখি ॥

*daṇḍe daṇḍe tile tile gorācām̐da nā dekhile*
*marame mariyā yena thāki |*
*sādha haya nirantara hemakānti kalebara*
*hiyāra mājhāre sadā rākhi ||*

*Word for word:* daṇḍe daṇḍe tile tile — every danda, every instant; gorācām̐da nā dekhile — if I do not see Gorachand; marame mariyā yena thāki — I live as though dead at heart; sādha haya nirantara — I constantly long; hemakānti kalebara — the golden-lustred form; hiyāra mājhāre sadā rākhi — to keep always within my heart

**8.1.** If every moment, every instant I do not see Gorachand,
I live as though dead at heart.
Ceaselessly I long to keep
His golden-lustred form within my heart.

পলকে না হেরি তায় পাঁজর ধসিয়া যায়
ধৈরজ ধরিতে নাহি পারি ।
অনুরাগের তুলি দিয়ে অন্তর বাহির হিয়ে
না জানি তার কত ধার ধারি ॥

*palake nā heri tāya pām̐jara dhasiyā yāya*
*dhairaja dharite nāhi pāri |*
*anurāgera tuli diye antara bāhira hiye*
*nā jāni tāra kata dhāra dhāri ||*

*Word for word:* palake nā heri tāya — not seeing Him for a moment; pām̐jara dhasiyā yāya — my ribs give way; dhairaja dharite nāhi pāri — I cannot keep my composure; anurāgera tuli diye — with the brush of anuraga; antara bāhira hiye — within and without the heart; nā jāni — I do not know; tāra kata dhāra dhāri — how much I owe Him

**8.2.** I do not see Him for a moment — my ribs give way,
I cannot keep my composure.
With the brush of anuraga my heart is painted within and without —
I do not know how much I owe Him.[^28-21]

সুরধুনীর নীরে যেয়ে কুল দিব ভাসাইয়ে
অনল জ্বালিয়া দিব লাজে ।
গৌরাঙ্গ সমুখে করি দেখিব নয়ন ভরি
বাসু নাহি চায় আন কাজে ॥

*suradhunīra nīre yeye kula diba bhāsāiye*
*anala jvāliyā diba lāje |*
*gaurāṅga samukhe kari dekhiba nayana bhari*
*bāsu nāhi cāya āna kāje ||*

*Word for word:* suradhunīra nīre yeye — going to the waters of the Suradhuni; kula diba bhāsāiye — I will set my family adrift; anala jvāliyā diba lāje — I will set fire to shame; gaurāṅga samukhe kari — placing Gauranga before me; dekhiba nayana bhari — I will gaze my fill; bāsu nāhi cāya āna kāje — Vasu wants no other work

**8.3.** I will go to the waters of the Suradhuni and set my family adrift,
I will set fire to my shame;
I will place Gauranga before me and gaze my fill —
Vasu wants no other work.[^28-22]

[^28-20]: Signature: "Vasu." GPT1 — p. 296, no. 14 (raga suhai; scan PDF p. 555), in the section of gaura-chandrikas to purvaraga and
anuraga (4.4); GPT2 — sect. 4.4, no. 14 (catalogue: VG-040). Not in PK, KGC or GCd. According to the catalogue, in the late
collection *Padamrita-madhuri* (vol. 1, pp. 469–470; an edition under copyright, its text is not used) the same pada bears the
signature of Murari Gupta and has an extra couplet: the attribution is disputed (C). On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to
the section (chapter 27).
[^28-21]: The line is obscure: "anurāgera tuli diye antara bāhira hiye, nā jāni tāra kata dhāra dhāri" — lit. "with the brush of anuraga —
the inside and outside of the heart; I do not know how much debt I hold to Him." We understand: love has coloured the whole heart,
and the townswoman does not know how to repay this gift. The translation is conjectural.
[^28-22]: "Set my family adrift," "set fire to my shame" are formulas of renouncing family honour for love (from the padas on Radha);
translated as in the original (introductory note, rule 2).

## 9. Vasu Ghosha — "āpana jāni banāyalum̐ beśa…" (GPT1 p. 305, no. 18)
*Nagari-bhava (vasaka-sajja — "she who has prepared for the meeting"). The townswoman, regarding Gaura as her own, adorns herself
for His coming: she binds her hair, puts on a sandal tilaka, a pearl necklace, draws designs in musk on her breast; love for Gaura
cannot be told. Raga dhanashi.*[^28-23]

আপন জানি বনায়লুঁ বেশ ।
বাঁধল যতনে উদাস করি কেশ ॥

*āpana jāni banāyalum̐ beśa |*
*bām̐dhala yatane udāsa kari keśa ||*

*Word for word:* āpana jāni — knowing [Him] as my own; banāyalum̐ beśa — I made my attire; bām̐dhala yatane — carefully bound; udāsa kari keśa — my hair in a loose knot

**9.1.** Regarding Him as my own, I dressed myself:
carefully I bound my hair in a loose knot.

চন্দন-তিলক দেয়ল মঝু ভাল ।
কণ্ঠে চঢ়ায়ল মোতিম মাল ॥

*candana-tilaka deyala majhu bhāla |*
*kaṇṭhe caṛhāyala motima māla ||*

*Word for word:* candana-tilaka deyala — put a sandal tilaka; majhu bhāla — on my forehead; kaṇṭhe caṛhāyala — put on my neck; motima māla — a pearl necklace

**9.2.** I put a sandal tilaka on my forehead,
I put a pearl necklace round my neck.

মৃগমদ-চিত্র কয়ল কুচ-মাঝ ।
অঙ্গহি অঙ্গ বনায়লুঁ সাজ ॥

*mṛgamada-citra kayala kuca-mājha |*
*aṅgahi aṅga banāyalum̐ sāja ||*

*Word for word:* mṛgamada-citra kayala — drew designs in musk; kuca-mājha — on the breast; aṅgahi aṅga — limb by limb; banāyalum̐ sāja — I adorned myself

**9.3.** I drew designs in musk on my breast,
I adorned myself all over, limb by limb.[^28-24]

গৌরক লেহ কহনে না যায় ।
বাসুদেব ঘোষে রস ওর নাহি পায় ॥

*gauraka leha kahane nā yāya |*
*bāsudeba ghoṣe rasa ora nāhi pāya ||*

*Word for word:* gauraka leha — love for Gaura; kahane nā yāya — cannot be told; bāsudeba ghoṣe — Vasudeva Ghosha; rasa ora nāhi pāya — finds no end to the rasa

**9.4.** Love for Gaura cannot be told:
Vasudeva Ghosha finds no end to this rasa.[^28-25]

[^28-23]: Signature: "Vasudeva Ghosha." GPT1 — p. 305, no. 18 (raga dhanashi; scan PDF p. 564), in the section of gaura-chandrikas to
abhisara, rasodgara and utkanthita (4.5), next to a pada on vasaka-sajja (no. 19); GPT2 — sect. 4.5, no. 18 (catalogue: VG-168). Not in PK, KGC or GCd; attribution to Vasu by GPT only (C). On
nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^28-24]: The adornment of the vasaka-sajja (the heroine who adorns herself for her beloved's coming) is a canon of the padas on
Radha; designs in musk on the breast (kuca) are part of that canon. Translated exactly, with nothing added. The Vrajabuli forms
"deyala," "caṛhāyala," "kayala" can also be 3rd person ("He put…"); but the pada is framed by "I dressed myself… I adorned myself"
(banāyalum̐), and it speaks of the heroine's own adornment.
[^28-25]: Lit. "Gaura's love (leha) cannot be told"; we understand it as the townswoman's love for Gaura. Gaura Himself, according to CC,
is in the bhava of Radha, tasting Her love; the tradition does not accept depicting Him as the beloved of the townswomen
(introductory note).

## 10. Vasu Ghosha — "niśi-parabhāte basi āṅgināte…" (GPT1 p. 163, no. 21)
*Nagari-bhava (khandita — "the deceived"). At daybreak the townswoman sits in the courtyard with a cheerless face: "Friend, who has
done this? Gora, the Creator's finest work — another has got Him!" She had prepared the bed, did not sleep all night, went out of
the door a hundred times; when Gauranga comes she will ask: in whose house did He spend the night? Raga vibhasa-dashakushi.*[^28-26]

নিশি-পরভাতে বসি আঙ্গিনাতে বিরস বদনখানি ।
গৌরাঙ্গচাঁদের হেন ব্যবহার এমতি কভু না জানি ॥

*niśi-parabhāte basi āṅgināte birasa badanakhāni |*
*gaurāṅgacām̐dera hena byabahāra emati kabhu nā jāni ||*

*Word for word:* niśi-parabhāte — at daybreak; basi āṅgināte — sitting in the courtyard; birasa badanakhāni — with a cheerless face; gaurāṅgacām̐dera — of Gaurangachand; hena byabahāra — such conduct; emati kabhu nā jāni — such I never knew

**10.1.** At daybreak I sit in the courtyard with a cheerless face:
such conduct from Gaurangachand I never knew.

সই এমতি করিল কে ।
গোরা গুণনিধি বিধির অবধি তাহারে পাইল সে ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*sai emati karila ke |*
*gorā guṇanidhi bidhira abadhi tāhāre pāila se || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* sai — friend; emati karila ke — who has done this; gorā guṇanidhi — Gora, the treasury of virtues; bidhira abadhi — the utmost of the Creator's work; tāhāre pāila se — she has got Him

**10.2.** *(Refrain)* Friend, who has done this?
Gora, the treasury of virtues, the utmost of the Creator's work — she has got Him.[^28-27]

কস্তূরি চন্দন করি বরিষণ গাঁথিয়া ফুলের মালা ।
বিচিত্র পালঙ্কে শেজ বিছাইনু শুইবে শচীর বালা ॥

*kastūri candana kari bariṣaṇa gām̐thiyā phulera mālā |*
*bicitra pālaṅke śeja bichāinu śuibe śacīra bālā ||*

*Word for word:* kastūri candana kari bariṣaṇa — sprinkling musk and sandal; gām̐thiyā phulera mālā — stringing garlands of flowers; bicitra pālaṅke — on a splendid couch; śeja bichāinu — I spread the bed; śuibe śacīra bālā — Shachi's boy will lie [here]

**10.3.** Sprinkling musk and sandal, stringing flower garlands,
I spread the bed on a splendid couch: here Shachi's boy will lie.

হেদে গো সজনি সকল রজনী জাগিয়া পোহাল বসি ।
তিলে তিনবার দণ্ডে শতবার মন্দির বাহিরে আসি ॥

*hede go sajani sakala rajanī jāgiyā pohāla basi |*
*tile tinabāra daṇḍe śatabāra mandira bāhire āsi ||*

*Word for word:* hede go sajani — ah, friend; sakala rajanī — the whole night; jāgiyā pohāla basi — I sat awake till dawn; tile tinabāra — three times an instant; daṇḍe śatabāra — a hundred times a danda; mandira bāhire āsi — I came out of the house

**10.4.** Ah, friend, the whole night I sat awake till dawn;
three times an instant, a hundred times a danda I went out of the house.

বাসু ঘোষ বলে গৌরাঙ্গ আইলে এখনি কহিব তাহে ।
হেথা না আয়ল রজনী বঞ্চল আছিল কাহার ঘরে ॥

*bāsu ghoṣa bale gaurāṅga āile ekhani kahiba tāhe |*
*hethā nā āyala rajanī bañcala āchila kāhāra ghare ||*

*Word for word:* bāsu ghoṣa bale — says Vasu Ghosha; gaurāṅga āile — when Gauranga comes; ekhani kahiba tāhe — I will ask Him at once; hethā nā āyala — He did not come here; rajanī bañcala — He spent the night; āchila kāhāra ghare — in whose house was He

**10.5.** Says Vasu Ghosha: when Gauranga comes I will ask Him at once:
"You did not come here — where did You spend the night, in whose house were You?"[^28-28]

[^28-26]: Signature: "Vasu Ghosha." GPT1 — p. 163, no. 21 (raga vibhasa-dashakushi; scan PDF p. 422); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 21
(catalogue: VG-024). The pada is not in PK, KGC or GCd; attribution to Vasu by GPT only (C). On nagari-bhava see the introductory
note to the section (chapter 27).
[^28-27]: "The utmost of the Creator's work" (bidhira abadhi) — the most perfect thing the Creator could make (a poetic formula; Gaura is not
created — He is the Lord Himself). "She has got Him" — another woman: the khandita heroine suspects a rival.
[^28-28]: The pada is wholly transferred from the canon of padas on Radha as khandita: Krishna has spent the night with another gopi and
comes at dawn bearing the marks of the meeting. Such a plot is inapplicable to Gaura: Vrindavana Dasa says plainly that in Navadvipa
the Lord did not look at women (CB, Adi-khanda; introductory note) — which is why the townswoman waits for Him all night in vain.
Translated faithfully to the author, but this is a poetic fiction of the late layer of GPT, not a lila; the tradition does not accept
such a depiction of Gaura (introductory note). Cf. the night of vain waiting in Vasu's padas from PK (chapter 27, nos. 19, 20).

## 11. Vasu Ghosha — "kena māna karinu lo sai…" (GPT1 p. 313, no. 20)
*Nagari-bhava (mana — offended pride and repentance). "Why did I take offence, friend? Where has Gora gone?" The townswoman herself
pushed Gaurahari away, and now reproaches her friends for not holding Him back: home and body are empty, Gaura has turned away. The
poet consoles her: the hope will be fulfilled. Raga suhai.*[^28-29]

কেন মান করিনু লো সই ।
গোরা গুণনিধি গেল কই ॥

*kena māna karinu lo sai |*
*gorā guṇanidhi gela kai ||*

*Word for word:* kena māna karinu — why did I sulk (keep mana); lo sai — friend; gorā guṇanidhi — Gora, the treasury of virtues; gela kai — where has He gone

**11.1.** Why did I take offence, friend?
Where has Gora, the treasury of virtues, gone?

তেজিলাম যদি বঁধুয়ায় ।
কেন প্রাণ নাহি বাহিরায় ॥

*tejilāma yadi bam̐dhuyāya |*
*kena prāṇa nāhi bāhirāya ||*

*Word for word:* tejilāma yadi — if I have abandoned; bam̐dhuyāya — my beloved; kena prāṇa nāhi bāhirāya — why does my life not depart

**11.2.** If I have abandoned my beloved,
why then does my life not leave me?

আমি ত তেজিনু গৌরহরি ।
তোরা কেনে না রাখিলি ধরি ॥

*āmi ta tejinu gaurahari |*
*torā kene nā rākhili dhari ||*

*Word for word:* āmi ta tejinu — I did abandon; gaurahari — Gaurahari; torā kene — why did you; nā rākhili dhari — not hold [Him] back

**11.3.** I did abandon Gaurahari —
but why did you not hold Him back?

এবে গেহ দেহ শূন ভেল ।
গৌর বৈমুখ ভৈ গেল ॥

*ebe geha deha śūna bhela |*
*gaura baimukha bhai gela ||*

*Word for word:* ebe — now; geha deha śūna bhela — home and body have become empty; gaura baimukha bhai gela — Gaura has turned away

**11.4.** Now home and body are both empty:
Gaura has turned away.

এবে কেন মিছা হা-হুতাশ ।
বাসু কহে পূরিবেক আশ ॥

*ebe kena michā hā-hutāśa |*
*bāsu kahe pūribeka āśa ||*

*Word for word:* ebe kena — why now; michā hā-hutāśa — vain sighing; bāsu kahe — says Vasu; pūribeka āśa — the hope will be fulfilled

**11.5.** Why now these vain sighs?
Says Vasu: the hope will be fulfilled.[^28-30]

[^28-29]: Signature: "Vasu." GPT1 — p. 313, no. 20 (raga suhai; scan PDF p. 572), in the section of gaura-chandrikas to khandita and
mana (4.6); GPT2 — sect. 4.6, no. 20 (catalogue: VG-169; the first line according to the scan is "kena māna karinu," not "karisa").
Not in PK, KGC or GCd; attribution to Vasu by GPT only (C). On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^28-30]: The motif of the kalahantarita — the heroine who in offended pride (mana) has pushed her beloved away and at once repents — is
taken from the padas on Radha and Krishna. "Beloved" (bam̐dhuyā) is a word of the same padas. "Gaura has turned away" (baimukha) — as in
Vasu's padas from PK (chapter 27, no. 20: "the king of dancers has turned away from me"), here what is unwittingly reflected is that
the Lord did not respond to such feelings (introductory note).

## 12. Vasu Ghosha — "śayana-mandire hāma śutiyā āchilā…" (GPT1 p. 203, no. 113)
*Nagari-bhava (a dream). "I was lying in my bedchamber, and tonight in a dream I saw Gauranga": since then her soul burns, Gora's
form stands before her day and night, her garment is soaked with tears, her body has lost its strength. Raga bhupala.*[^28-31]

শয়ন-মন্দিরে হাম শুতিয়া আছিলা ।
নিশির স্বপনে আজি গৌরাঙ্গ দেখিলা ॥

*śayana-mandire hāma śutiyā āchilā |*
*niśira svapane āji gaurāṅga dekhilā ||*

*Word for word:* śayana-mandire — in the bedchamber; hāma śutiyā āchilā — I was lying; niśira svapane — in a night dream; āji — today; gaurāṅga dekhilā — I saw Gauranga

**12.1.** I was lying in my bedchamber —
and tonight in a dream I saw Gauranga.

সেই হৈতে প্রাণ পোড়ে শুন গো সজনি ।
গোরারূপ মনে পড়ে দিবস রজনী ॥

*sei haite prāṇa poṛe śuna go sajani |*
*gorārūpa mane paṛe dibasa rajanī ||*

*Word for word:* sei haite — since then; prāṇa poṛe — my soul burns; śuna go sajani — listen, friend; gorārūpa mane paṛe — Gora's form comes to mind; dibasa rajanī — day and night

**12.2.** Since then my soul burns — listen, friend:
Gora's form comes to my mind day and night.

গোরা গোরা করি মোর কি হৈল অন্তরে ।
বসন তিতিল মোর নয়নের লোরে ॥

*gorā gorā kari mora ki haila antare |*
*basana titila mora nayanera lore ||*

*Word for word:* gorā gorā kari — crying "Gora, Gora"; mora ki haila antare — what has happened in my heart; basana titila mora — my garment is soaked; nayanera lore — with the tears of my eyes

**12.3.** I keep crying "Gora, Gora" — what has become of my heart!
My garment is soaked with my tears.

অলসে অবশ গা ধরণে না যায় ।
গোরা-ভাব মনে করি বাসু ঘোষ গায় ॥

*alase abaśa gā dharaṇe nā yāya |*
*gorā-bhāba mane kari bāsu ghoṣa gāya ||*

*Word for word:* alase abaśa gā — my body is languid and limp; dharaṇe nā yāya — cannot be held up; gorā-bhāba mane kari — recalling the feeling for Gora; bāsu ghoṣa gāya — Vasu Ghosha sings

**12.4.** My body is languid and limp, it will not hold up;
recalling this feeling for Gora, Vasu Ghosha sings.[^28-32]

[^28-31]: Signature: "Vasu Ghosha." GPT1 — p. 203, no. 113 (raga bhupala; scan PDF p. 462), among the padas on the townswomen's dreams
(nos. 111–115: Vasu's PK 249 and PK 724 — chapter 27, nos. 23, 22; VG-027, VG-029 — nos. 13, 14 of this chapter); GPT2 — sect. 3.2,
no. 113 (catalogue: VG-028). Not in PK, KGC or GCd; attribution to Vasu by GPT only (C). On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to
the section (chapter 27).
[^28-32]: "Feeling for Gora" (gorā-bhāba) can also be read as "Gora's bhava," i.e. the feeling He awakens. The verb forms "āchilā,"
"dekhilā" are Old Bengali first-person forms ("I was lying," "I saw").

## 13. Vasu Ghosha (according to Majumdar, not Vasu) — "niśi śeṣe chinu ghumera ghore…" (GPT1 p. 203, no. 112)
*Nagari-bhava (a dream; sambhoga). The townswoman relates: at the end of the night, deep in sleep, "Gaura the nagara" embraced and
kissed her; sleep broke, the nagara went away, and coming to her senses she left the bedchamber in shame. According to Majumdar, a
reworking of a well-known pada on Krishna, ascribed to Vasu. Raga vibhasa.*[^28-33]

নিশি শেষে ছিনু ঘুমের ঘোরে ।
গৌর-নাগর পরিরম্ভিল মোরে ॥

*niśi śeṣe chinu ghumera ghore |*
*gaura-nāgara parirambhila more ||*

*Word for word:* niśi śeṣe — at the end of the night; chinu ghumera ghore — I was deep in sleep; gaura-nāgara — Gaura the nagara; parirambhila more — embraced me

**13.1.** At the end of the night I was deep in sleep —
Gaura the nagara embraced me.

গণ্ডে কয়ল সোই চুম্বন দান ।
করল অধরে অধর-রস পান ॥

*gaṇḍe kayala soi cumbana dāna |*
*karala adhare adhara-rasa pāna ||*

*Word for word:* gaṇḍe — on the cheek; kayala soi cumbana dāna — He gave a kiss; karala adhare — with His lips He drank; adhara-rasa pāna — the nectar of the lips

**13.2.** He kissed me on the cheek,
with His lips He drank the nectar of my lips.[^28-34]

ভাঙ্গল নিদ নাগর চলি গেল ।
অচেতনে ছিনু চেতনা ভেল ॥

*bhāṅgala nida nāgara cali gela |*
*acetane chinu cetanā bhela ||*

*Word for word:* bhāṅgala nida — sleep broke; nāgara cali gela — the nagara went away; acetane chinu — I had been senseless; cetanā bhela — I came to my senses

**13.3.** Sleep broke, the nagara went away;
I had been senseless — and I came to my senses.

লাজে তেয়াগিনু শয়ন-গেহ ।
বাসু কহে তুয়া কপট লেহ ॥

*lāje teyāginu śayana-geha |*
*bāsu kahe tuyā kapaṭa leha ||*

*Word for word:* lāje — out of shame; teyāginu śayana-geha — I left the bedchamber; bāsu kahe — says Vasu; tuyā kapaṭa leha — your love is a deceit

**13.4.** Out of shame I left the bedchamber.
Says Vasu: your love is a deceit.[^28-35]

[^28-33]: Signature: "Vasu." GPT1 — p. 203, no. 112 (raga vibhasa; scan PDF p. 462); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 112 (p. 131; catalogue:
VG-027). Not in PK, KGC or GCd. **Majumdar** explicitly names this pada (from GPT2, p. 131) as a reworking of a well-known pada of
Krishna-lila, ascribed to Vasu to lend "antiquity" to sambhoga-nagari-bhava; because of such padas he considers GPT unreliable for
Vasu Ghosha and Narahari Sarakara. Hence the authority is **D** (a forgery according to Majumdar). On nagari-bhava see the
introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^28-34]: Sambhoga (a love meeting) with Gaura, and in such words, is what even Majumdar considers incompatible with the genuine padas
of the contemporaries (in Narahari Sarakara, by his criteria, "there is no sambhoga"), and the tradition rejects it as a distortion
(Vrindavana Dasa: in Navadvipa the Lord did not look at women; Bhaktisiddhanta: "gaura-nagari" is an apasampradaya; introductory
note). Translated exactly, with nothing added, for the completeness of the corpus; this is not a lila of the Lord but a late reworking
of a pada on Krishna.
[^28-35]: "Your love is a deceit" (tuyā kapaṭa leha): a reproach, apparently, to the "nagara" who left at dawn (in the original pada — to
Krishna); it can also be taken as the poet's words to the heroine.

## 14. Vasu Ghosha — "ājuka prema kahane nāhi yāya…" (GPT1 p. 204, no. 115)
*Nagari-bhava (telling of a meeting). "Today's love cannot be told": the townswoman lay on the bed she had spread — and heard the
jingling of anklets: Gauranga, the king of dancers, had come; she hid under her veil, and the skilful nagara searched for her with
His eyes; Gora found great joy. Raga dhanashi.*[^28-36]

আজুক প্রেম কহনে নাহি যায় ।
শুতি রহল হাম শেজ বিছায় ॥

*ājuka prema kahane nāhi yāya |*
*śuti rahala hāma śeja bichāya ||*

*Word for word:* ājuka prema — today's love; kahane nāhi yāya — cannot be told; śuti rahala hāma — I lay; śeja bichāya — having spread the bed

**14.1.** Today's love cannot be told:
I lay down, having spread the bed.

রুনু ঝুনু রুনু ঝুনু নূপুর পায় ।
পেখলুঁ গৌরাঙ্গ বর নটরায় ॥

*runu jhunu runu jhunu nūpura pāya |*
*pekhalum̐ gaurāṅga bara naṭarāya ||*

*Word for word:* runu jhunu runu jhunu — runu-jhunu (a jingling); nūpura pāya — anklets on the feet; pekhalum̐ — I saw; gaurāṅga bara naṭarāya — Gauranga, the finest king of dancers

**14.2.** Runu-jhunu, runu-jhunu — the anklets jingle on His feet:
I saw Gauranga, the finest king of dancers.

আঁচলে রাখনু আঁচল ছাপাই ।
বিদগধ নাগর চৌদিকে চাই ॥

*ām̐cale rākhanu ām̐cala chāpāi |*
*bidagadha nāgara caudike cāi ||*

*Word for word:* ām̐cale rākhanu — I kept myself under the end of my sari; ām̐cala chāpāi — covering [myself] with the veil; bidagadha nāgara — the skilful nagara; caudike cāi — looks about on all sides

**14.3.** I hid under the end of my sari, covering myself with the veil;
the skilful nagara looks about on all sides.

বহু সুখ পায়ল গোরা নটরায় ।
বাসুদেব কহে রস কহনে না যায় ॥

*bahu sukha pāyala gorā naṭarāya |*
*bāsudeba kahe rasa kahane nā yāya ||*

*Word for word:* bahu sukha pāyala — found great joy; gorā naṭarāya — Gora, the king of dancers; bāsudeba kahe — says Vasudeva; rasa kahane nā yāya — the rasa cannot be told

**14.4.** Great joy did Gora, the king of dancers, find.
Says Vasudeva: the rasa cannot be told.[^28-37]

[^28-36]: Signature: "Vasudeva." GPT1 — p. 204, no. 115 (raga dhanashi; scan PDF p. 463), among the padas on the townswomen's dreams
and meetings (nos. 111–115); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 115 (catalogue: VG-029). Not in PK, KGC or GCd; attribution to Vasu by GPT only (C).
On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^28-37]: The pada is a telling of a meeting (rasodgara), like Vasu's PK 249 (chapter 27, no. 23, note 61): the plot is taken from the
padas on Radha and Krishna. Majumdar considers the padas of sambhoga with Gaura known only from GPT to be later ascriptions; the
tradition rejects such a depiction of Gaura (introductory note; cf. note 34). Translated exactly, with nothing added. The Lord's
"joy" (sukha) is in truth the joy of prema and kirtana, not worldly love.

## 15. Vasu Ghosha — "gela gaura nā gela baliyā…" (GPT1 p. 388, no. 18)
*Nagari-bhava (by its place in the section; the speaker is probably Vishnupriya — then this is a lament of separation, not nagari-bhava). Lament after the sannyasa. "Gaura has gone without saying He was going — He has cast me, unfortunate, adrift on a shoreless sea":
cruel Fate did not let the tree grow, it broke the sprout; to whom has it given Gauranga? Who will bear the burden of youth — in the
fire of separation there is nothing left but to burn. The speaker is not named: in GPT the pada stands among Vishnupriya's laments.
Raga karuna.*[^28-38]

গেল গৌর না গেল বলিয়া ।
হাম অভাগিনী নারী অকূলে ভাসাইয়া ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*gela gaura nā gela baliyā |*
*hāma abhāginī nārī akūle bhāsāiyā || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* gela gaura — Gaura went away; nā gela baliyā — without saying "I am going"; hāma abhāginī nārī — me, an unfortunate woman; akūle bhāsāiyā — setting adrift on a shoreless [sea]

**15.1.** *(Refrain)* Gaura has gone without saying, "I am going" —
He has cast me, an unfortunate woman, adrift on a shoreless sea.

হায় রে দারুণ বিধি নিদয় নিঠুর ।
জন্মিতে না দিলি তরু ভাঙ্গিলি অঙ্কুর ॥

*hāya re dāruṇa bidhi nidaya niṭhura |*
*janmite nā dili taru bhāṅgili aṅkura ||*

*Word for word:* hāya re — alas; dāruṇa bidhi — cruel Fate (the Creator); nidaya niṭhura — pitiless, heartless; janmite nā dili taru — you did not let the tree grow; bhāṅgili aṅkura — you broke the sprout

**15.2.** Alas, cruel Fate, pitiless, heartless!
You did not let the tree grow — you broke the sprout.[^28-39]

হায় রে দারুণ বিধি কি বাদ সাধিলি ।
প্রাণের গৌরাঙ্গ আমার কারে নিয়া দিলি ॥

*hāya re dāruṇa bidhi ki bāda sādhili |*
*prāṇera gaurāṅga āmāra kāre niyā dili ||*

*Word for word:* ki bāda sādhili — what enmity have you wrought; prāṇera gaurāṅga āmāra — my Gauranga, my very life; kāre niyā dili — to whom have you given [Him]

**15.3.** Alas, cruel Fate, what enmity you have wrought!
To whom have you given my Gauranga, my very life?

আর কে সহিবে আমার যৌবনের ভার ।
বিরহ-অনলে পুড়ি হব ছারখার ॥

*āra ke sahibe āmāra yaubanera bhāra |*
*biraha-anale puṛi haba chārakhāra ||*

*Word for word:* āra ke sahibe — who now will bear; āmāra yaubanera bhāra — the burden of my youth; biraha-anale puṛi — burning in the fire of separation; haba chārakhāra — I shall be reduced to ashes

**15.4.** Who now will bear the burden of my youth?
Burning in the fire of separation, I shall be reduced to ashes.

বাসু ঘোষ কহে আর কারে দুঃখ কব ।
গোরাচাঁদ বিনা প্রাণ আর না রাখিব ॥

*bāsu ghoṣa kahe āra kāre duḥkha kaba |*
*gorācām̐da binā prāṇa āra nā rākhiba ||*

*Word for word:* bāsu ghoṣa kahe — says Vasu Ghosha; āra kāre duḥkha kaba — to whom else shall I tell my grief; gorācām̐da binā — without Gorachand; prāṇa āra nā rākhiba — I will keep my life no longer

**15.5.** Says Vasu Ghosha: to whom else shall I tell my grief?
Without Gorachand I will keep my life no longer.

[^28-38]: Signature: "Vasu Ghosha." GPT1 — p. 388, no. 18 (raga karuna; scan PDF p. 647), in the section of the laments of Shachi and
Vishnupriya (5.4), before Vasu's PK 1636 and PK 1669 (chapter 27, nos. 24, 25); GPT2 — sect. 5.4, no. 18. Not in PK, KGC or GCd;
attribution to Vasu by GPT only (C). In the catalogue its first line stood in row VG-076 together with PK 1636 (they are different
padas; see chapter 27, note 63); now it has a separate row, VG-187. The speaker is not named: by its place in GPT it may be
Vishnupriya (the words about the "burden of youth" and the "broken sprout" suit a young wife); by the catalogue (Majumdar's mark of
nagari-bhava in this series) a townswoman; therefore the pada is placed here, next to the nagaris' laments from PK. The speaker is probably Vishnupriya — then this is a lament of
separation, not nagari-bhava; the pada is left in the section by its place (coordinator's decision after the review of 27–30). On nagari-bhava
see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^28-39]: "Did not let the tree grow, broke the sprout" — an image of love (or of married life) cut off at its very beginning. Fate (bidhi)
is the arbiter of destiny, the Creator, not the Lord (cf. chapter 27, note 53). The Lord's going into sannyasa is His will and lila
(CB, CC), not the cruelty of fate: only the grief of those left behind speaks so.

## 16. Nayanananda — "premera sāgara nayana-kamala…" (PK 2170)
*Nagari-bhava. "What an auspicious moment — I have met the beloved of my life!" The townswoman saw Gora in enchanting attire: lotus
eyes, a moon-face, red garments, hands and feet redder than the lotus; He stands bent in three places; absorbed in bhava — Gora
within and without. In PK it stands in the pallava "Gauranga's form — the words of the nagaris." Raga bhatiyari.*[^28-40]

প্রেমের সাগর নয়ন-কমল নাচন খঞ্জন তারা ।
কিয়ে শুভক্ষণ সর্ব সুলক্ষণ ভেটলুঁ প্রাণ-পিয়ারা ॥

*premera sāgara nayana-kamala nācana khañjana tārā |*
*kiye śubhakṣaṇa sarva sulakṣaṇa bheṭalum̐ prāṇa-piyārā ||*

*Word for word:* premera sāgara — an ocean of love; nayana-kamala — lotus eyes; nācana khañjana tārā — the pupils dancing wagtails; kiye śubhakṣaṇa — what an auspicious moment; sarva sulakṣaṇa — all omens favourable; bheṭalum̐ — I met; prāṇa-piyārā — the beloved of my life

**16.1.** An ocean of love; lotus eyes, the pupils dancing wagtails:
what an auspicious moment, all omens favourable — I have met the beloved of my life![^28-41]

গোরা-রূপ দেখিলুঁ মোহন বেশে ।
যার অনুভব সেই সে জানয়ে না পায় আনে উদ্দেশে ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*gorā-rūpa dekhilum̐ mohana beśe |*
*yāra anubhaba sei se jānaye nā pāya āne uddeśe || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* gorā-rūpa dekhilum̐ — I saw Gora's form; mohana beśe — in enchanting attire; yāra anubhaba — whoever has experienced it; sei se jānaye — he alone knows; nā pāya āne uddeśe — others find no trace of it

**16.2.** *(Refrain)* I saw Gora's form in enchanting attire:
whoever has experienced it alone knows it, others find no trace of it.

রূপের সদন ও চাঁদ-বদন সরুয়া বসন রাঙ্গা ।
রাঙ্গা কর-পদ জিনি কোকনদ রহে অঙ্গ তিরিভঙ্গা ॥

*rūpera sadana o cām̐da-badana saruyā basana rāṅgā |*
*rāṅgā kara-pada jini kokanada rahe aṅga tiribhaṅgā ||*

*Word for word:* rūpera sadana — the abode of beauty; o cām̐da-badana — that moon-face; saruyā basana rāṅgā — fine red cloth; rāṅgā kara-pada — red hands and feet; jini kokanada — surpassing the red lotus; rahe aṅga tiribhaṅgā — He stands bent in three places

**16.3.** The abode of beauty — that moon-face, the fine red cloth;
red hands and feet surpass the red lotus; He stands bent in three places.[^28-42]

ভাবের আবেশে ভাবিনী-লালসে অন্তরে বাহিরে গোরা ।
এ নয়নানন্দ ভাবে অনুবন্ধ সতত ভাবে বিভোরা ॥

*bhābera ābeśe bhābinī-lālase antare bāhire gorā |*
*e nayanānanda bhābe anubandha satata bhābe bibhorā ||*

*Word for word:* bhābera ābeśe — absorbed in bhava; bhābinī-lālase — with the longing of the bhavini; antare bāhire gorā — Gora within and without; e nayanānanda — this Nayanananda; bhābe anubandha — bound by bhava; satata bhābe bibhorā — ever lost in bhava

**16.4.** Absorbed in bhava, with the longing of the bhavini — Gora within and without.
This Nayanananda, bound by bhava, is ever lost in bhava.[^28-43]

[^28-40]: Signature: "Nayanananda." PK: vol. 3, PDF pp. 257–258 (printed pp. 246–247), 4th shakha, 19th pallava, section "atha
śrīgaurāṅgasya rūpa-barṇanaṃ nāgarīgaṇādyuktiḥ" (Gauranga's form: the words of the nagaris and others), no. 3 (mark "॥৩॥২১৭০॥"),
between Vasu's padas PK 2169 and 2171 (chapter 27, nos. 9, 10); raga bhatiyari; MS P-R-Sa no. 2277. GPT1 — p. 165, no. 27 (raga
bhatiyari); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 25 (catalogue: NN-009 and NN-026 — one pada; the first line of NN-026 in the catalogue is wrong —
"kāmera pāṭe ratira bilāsa" is taken from the neighbouring PK 2168 of Govinda Dasa). Nayanananda (Nayana Mishra), nephew of Gadadhara
Pandita, is a contemporary according to Majumdar; the pada is in PK with his signature (A). On nagari-bhava see the introductory note
to the section (chapter 27).
[^28-41]: "The beloved of my life" (prāṇa-piyārā) — the townswoman's words; "I have met" (bheṭalum̐) — she saw Him in the street or in
kirtana. MSS "ka," "kha," "cha": "lotus face" (bayāna) instead of "lotus eyes"; "ka"–"cha": "eyes" (locana) instead of "dancing"
(so also GPT1).
[^28-42]: "Bent in three places" (tiribhaṅga, tribhanga) is the pose of Krishna with the flute: Gaura, remembering the lilas of Vraja,
takes Krishna's form (cf. Vasu's pada "soṅari puruba-līlā tribhaṅga hailā" from BR — chapter 1, no. 10). The townswoman sees in Him
Krishna's beauty.
[^28-43]: "With the longing of the bhavini" (bhābinī-lālase): bhavini, "the loving one," usually refers to Radha; it may mean that Gaura
is immersed in Radha's bhava (CC Adi 4), or it may be the longing of the heroine herself, who sees Gora "within and without." MSS
"ka"–"cha": "within, without" (antara bāhira).

## 17. Nayanananda — "sai cala dekhi giyā…" (PK 2177)
*Nagari-bhava. "Friend, let us go and see how wondrously charming Gora dances!" His form is adorned with love, yellow garments,
sandal, a forest garland round which bees swarm; absorbed in bhava He thrills all over, tears flow from His reddened eyes; the
townswoman longs to run and touch Him; the noble wives of Nadia have lost family and shame, but before people they dare not even
sigh. The poet advises: go to the bank of the Suradhuni — there you will see Gora. Raga shri.*[^28-44]

সই চল দেখি গিয়া ।
কেমন বন্ধানে নাচে গোরা বিনোদিয়া ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*sai cala dekhi giyā |*
*kemana bandhāne nāce gorā binodiyā || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* sai — friend; cala dekhi giyā — let us go and see; kemana bandhāne — with what artistry; nāce — dances; gorā binodiyā — charming Gora

**17.1.** *(Refrain)* Friend, let us go and see
how wondrously charming Gora dances!

পীত পিরিতিময় রূপের সাজনি ।
পীত বসন রাঙ্গা ডোরের দোলনি ॥

*pīta piritimaya rūpera sājani |*
*pīta basana rāṅgā ḍorera dolani ||*

*Word for word:* pīta — golden-yellow; piritimaya — all made of love; rūpera sājani — the adornment of His form; pīta basana — yellow garments; rāṅgā ḍorera dolani — the swaying of the red cord

**17.2.** Golden, all made of love — so is His form adorned;
yellow garments, the red cord swaying.[^28-45]

সর্বাঙ্গে চন্দন গলে নব বন-মালে ।
কত ফুলশর ধায় অলিকুল-জালে ॥

*sarvāṅge candana gale naba bana-māle |*
*kata phulaśara dhāya alikula-jāle ||*

*Word for word:* sarvāṅge candana — sandal on every limb; gale naba bana-māle — a fresh forest garland on the neck; kata phulaśara dhāya — how many flower-arrows fly; alikula-jāle — in swarms of bees

**17.3.** Sandal on every limb, a fresh forest garland on His neck;
how many flower-arrows fly — in swarms of bees![^28-46]

ভাবের আবেশে পুলকের নাহি ওর ।
অনুরাগে অরুণ নয়ানে বহে লোর ॥

*bhābera ābeśe pulakera nāhi ora |*
*anurāge aruṇa nayāne bahe lora ||*

*Word for word:* bhābera ābeśe — absorbed in bhava; pulakera nāhi ora — there is no end to His thrill; anurāge — with anuraga; aruṇa nayāne — from reddened eyes; bahe lora — tears flow

**17.4.** Absorbed in bhava, His thrill knows no end;
from eyes reddened with anuraga tears flow.

সাত পাঁচ করে প্রাণ ধরিতে নারি হিয়া ।
হেন মনে করে সাধ পরশি ধাইয়া ॥

*sāta pām̐ca kare prāṇa dharite nāri hiyā |*
*hena mane kare sādha paraśi dhāiyā ||*

*Word for word:* sāta pām̐ca kare prāṇa — my soul is tossed this way and that; dharite nāri hiyā — I cannot hold my heart; hena mane kare sādha — I so long; paraśi dhāiyā — to run and touch [Him]

**17.5.** My soul is tossed this way and that, I cannot hold my heart:
I so long to run up and touch Him.[^28-47]

নদীয়ার কুল-বধূর গেল কুল-লাজে ।
নিশ্বাস ছাড়িতে নাহি সভার সমাজে ॥

*nadīyāra kula-badhūra gela kula-lāje |*
*niśvāsa chāṛite nāhi sabhāra samāje ||*

*Word for word:* nadīyāra kula-badhūra — for the family wives of Nadia; gela kula-lāje — family and shame are gone; niśvāsa chāṛite nāhi — one cannot even sigh; sabhāra samāje — in the presence of everyone

**17.6.** The noble wives of Nadia have lost both family and shame —
but before everyone they dare not even sigh.

কহয়ে নয়নানন্দ আছয়ে উপায় ।
সুরধুনী-তীরে যাই দেখিবে গোরারায় ॥

*kahaye nayanānanda āchaye upāya |*
*suradhunī-tīre yāi dekhibe gorārāya ||*

*Word for word:* kahaye nayanānanda — says Nayanananda; āchaye upāya — there is a way; suradhunī-tīre yāi — go to the bank of the Suradhuni; dekhibe gorārāya — you will see Gora Raya

**17.7.** Says Nayanananda: there is a way —
go to the bank of the Suradhuni: there you will see Gora Raya.

[^28-44]: Signature: "Nayanananda." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 260 (printed p. 249), 19th pallava, no. 10 (mark "॥১০॥২১৭৭॥"); raga "tathā rāga"
(= shri, as for PK 2174); MS P-R-Sa no. 2285. GPT1 — p. 165, no. 28 (raga shri); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 28 (catalogue: NN-010).
Signature in PK — A. On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^28-45]: "Golden" (pīta, lit. "yellow"): Gaura's golden form; so also GPT1. The red cord (ḍora) is the dancer's waist-string.
[^28-46]: Bees flying to the garland are Kamadeva's "flower-arrows" (phulaśara): an image of beauty piercing hearts.
[^28-47]: The longing "to run up and touch" is a nagari motif; translated as in the original. Gaura Himself is here in kirtana, in the
ecstasy of prema (thrill, tears, 17.4); the townswomen are only onlookers (cf. Nayanananda's PK 2179 — chapter 10, no. 16).

## 18. Nayanananda (signature in GPT only) — "dekha jība aparūpa gaurāṅgacāndera mukha…" (PK 291; GPT1 p. 166, no. 31)
*Nagari-bhava (only in the GPT recension). Gaura's form. "Look, O souls — the wondrous face of Gaurangachand: how many streams flow from His eyes!"
Hearing of His virtues, stone turns to water, the parrot weeps in its cage, and a noble wife who loves Hari's name weeps over Him in
solitude. According to GPT, Gaura has conquered the world by the rasa of love, even yavanas and chandalas were delivered — only the
poet's doubt has not gone. Raga malar.*[^28-48]

দেখ জীব অপরূপ গৌরাঙ্গচান্দের মুখ
নয়নে বহয়ে কত ধারা ।
কুন্দ করবীর গাঁথিয়াছে থরে থর
গলে দোলে বিনোদিয়া মালা ॥

*dekha jība aparūpa gaurāṅgacāndera mukha*
*nayane bahaye kata dhārā |*
*kunda karabīra gām̐thiyāche thare thara*
*gale dole binodiyā mālā ||*

*Word for word:* dekha jība — look, O souls; aparūpa — wondrous; gaurāṅgacāndera mukha — Gaurangachand's face; nayane bahaye kata dhārā — how many streams flow from the eyes; kunda karabīra — kunda and karavira; gām̐thiyāche thare thara — strung row upon row; gale dole — swings on the neck; binodiyā mālā — a charming garland

**18.1.** Look, O souls — the wondrous face of Gaurangachand:
how many streams flow from His eyes!
Kunda and karavira strung row upon row —
a charming garland swings on His neck.[^28-49]

গৌরাঙ্গের গুণ শুনি পাষাণ হয়ে ত পানি
শুক কান্দে পিঞ্জর-ভিতরে ।
কুলের কুলবতী হরিনামে পীরিতি
বিরলে বসিয়া গুণে ঝুরে ॥

*gaurāṅgera guṇa śuni pāṣāṇa haye ta pāni*
*śuka kānde piñjara-bhitare |*
*kulera kulabatī harināme pīriti*
*birale basiyā guṇe jhure ||*

*Word for word:* gaurāṅgera guṇa śuni — hearing of Gauranga's virtues; pāṣāṇa haye ta pāni — stone becomes water; śuka kānde — the parrot weeps; piñjara-bhitare — in its cage; kulera kulabatī — the noble wife of a worthy family; harināme pīriti — with love for Hari's name; birale basiyā — sitting in solitude; guṇe jhure — weeps over His virtues

**18.2.** Hearing of Gauranga's virtues, stone turns to water,
the parrot weeps in its cage;
the noble wife of a worthy family, loving Hari's name,
sits in solitude and weeps over His virtues.

গৌরাঙ্গ-পীরিতি-রসে জগত করিল বশে
যবন চণ্ডাল তরি গেল ।
পামর নয়নানন্দ না ঘুচিল মনের সন্দ
মরমে রহল বড় শেল ॥

*gaurāṅga-pīriti-rase jagata karila baśe*
*yabana caṇḍāla tari gela |*
*pāmara nayanānanda nā ghucila manera sanda*
*marame rahala baṛa śela ||*

*Word for word:* gaurāṅga-pīriti-rase — by the rasa of love for Gauranga; jagata karila baśe — He brought the world under His sway; yabana caṇḍāla tari gela — even yavanas and chandalas were delivered; pāmara nayanānanda — of the wretched Nayanananda; nā ghucila manera sanda — the doubt of the mind did not go; marame rahala baṛa śela — a great spear remained in the heart

**18.3.** By the rasa of love for Gauranga He has conquered the world —
even yavanas and chandalas were delivered;
the wretched Nayanananda's doubt of mind has not gone —
a heavy spear remains in his heart.[^28-50]

[^28-48]: PK: vol. 1, PDF p. 202 (printed p. 191), 3rd pallava, section "kebala rūpānurāga" (rupanuraga — gaura-chandrikas), no. 4
(mark "॥৪॥২৯১॥"), right after PK 290 (= Nayanananda's PK 787, no. 19); raga malar; in PK only 18.1–18.2, without signature. GPT1 —
p. 166, no. 31 (raga malar; scan PDF p. 425) — with a third couplet and the signature "pāmara nayanānanda"; GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 31
(catalogue: NN-013, "GPT only"; the PK number was found in preparing this chapter). Text 18.1–18.2 follows PK, 18.3 GPT1.
Attribution to Nayanananda by GPT only (C). On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^28-49]: PK: "look, O souls" (dekha jība) — an address to all; GPT1: "look, friend" (dekha sai) — a townswoman's words. In the PK recension
there is no nagari motif at all, apart from the noble wife weeping over Gauranga (18.2) — and she loves Hari's name. GPT1: "a
garland that enchants the sages" (munimanoharā).
[^28-50]: "Yavanas and chandalas" — Muslims and outcastes: Gaura delivers all without distinction (cf. chapter 9, no. 1). "Doubt of
mind" and "a spear in the heart" are the poet's self-abasement (cf. note 4).

## 19. Nayanananda — "gaurāṅga-lābaṇya rūpe ki kahiba eka mukhe…" (PK 787 = PK 290)
*Nagari-bhava. "How can one mouth tell of Gauranga's lovely form!" His smile and glance leave her no life; the Creator fashioned Him
in the mould of beauty, and her heart is in turmoil. The heroine laments: the Creator made her a daughter of a family, she is not free;
family, shame and fear are gone, she burns in the fire of her heart, but can tell no one. The poet: "Listen, charming one — you are
caught in the snare of love for Gauranga." Raga dhanashi.*[^28-51]

গৌরাঙ্গ-লাবণ্য রূপে কি কহিব এক মুখে
আর তাহে ফুলের কাঁচনি ।
চাঁদ-মুখের হাসি জীব না গো হেন বাসি
আর তাহে ভাতিয়া চাহনি ॥

*gaurāṅga-lābaṇya rūpe ki kahiba eka mukhe*
*āra tāhe phulera kām̐cani |*
*cām̐da-mukhera hāsi jība nā go hena bāsi*
*āra tāhe bhātiyā cāhani ||*

*Word for word:* gaurāṅga-lābaṇya rūpe — of Gauranga's lovely form; ki kahiba eka mukhe — what can I say with one mouth; āra tāhe — and besides; phulera kām̐cani — the freshness of a flower (?); cām̐da-mukhera hāsi — the smile of the moon-face; jība nā go hena bāsi — I feel I shall not live; bhātiyā cāhani — the radiant glance

**19.1.** How can one mouth tell of Gauranga's lovely form —
and besides, the freshness of a flower!
The smile of the moon-face — I feel, friend, I shall not live —
and besides, the radiant glance![^28-52]

বিহি সে গঢ়ল রূপ ছান্দে ।
কেমন কেমন করে মন সব লাগে উচাটন
পরাণ-পুতলি মোর কান্দে ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*bihi se gaṛhala rūpa chānde |*
*kemana kemana kare mana saba lāge ucāṭana*
*parāṇa-putali mora kānde || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* bihi se gaṛhala — the Creator fashioned; rūpa chānde — in the mould of beauty; kemana kemana kare mana — my heart feels strange; saba lāge ucāṭana — everything unsettles me; parāṇa-putali mora kānde — the little doll of my soul weeps

**19.2.** *(Refrain)* In the mould of beauty the Creator fashioned Him!
My heart feels strange, everything unsettles me,
the little doll of my soul weeps.[^28-53]

বিধিরে বলিব কি করিলে কুলের ঝি
আর তাহে নহি স্বতন্তরি ।
গেল কুল লাজ ভয় পরাণ রহিবার নয়
মনের অনলে পুড়ে মরি ॥

*bidhire baliba ki karile kulera jhi*
*āra tāhe nahi svatantari |*
*gela kula lāja bhaya parāṇa rahibāra naya*
*manera anale puṛe mari ||*

*Word for word:* bidhire baliba ki — what shall I say to the Creator; karile kulera jhi — you made me a daughter of a family; āra tāhe nahi svatantari — and besides I am not free; gela kula lāja bhaya — gone are family, shame and fear; parāṇa rahibāra naya — life will not stay; manera anale puṛe mari — I burn and die in the fire of my heart

**19.3.** What shall I say to the Creator? He made me a daughter of a family,
and besides I am not free.
Gone are family, shame and fear; life will not stay —
I burn and perish in the fire of my heart.

কহিব কাহার আগে কহিলে পিরিতি ভাঙ্গে
চিত মোর ধৈরজ না বান্ধে ।
নয়নানন্দের বাণী শুন শুন বিনোদিনি
ঠেকিলা গৌরাঙ্গ-প্রেম-ফান্দে ॥

*kahiba kāhāra āge kahile piriti bhāṅge*
*cita mora dhairaja nā bāndhe |*
*nayanānandera bāṇī śuna śuna binodini*
*ṭhekilā gaurāṅga-prema-phānde ||*

*Word for word:* kahiba kāhāra āge — before whom shall I speak; kahile piriti bhāṅge — if told, love breaks; cita mora dhairaja nā bāndhe — my heart cannot keep its composure; nayanānandera bāṇī — the word of Nayanananda; śuna śuna binodini — listen, charming one; ṭhekilā gaurāṅga-prema-phānde — you are caught in the snare of love for Gauranga

**19.4.** To whom shall I tell it? Once told, love is broken;
my heart cannot keep its composure.
The word of Nayanananda: listen, listen, charming one —
you are caught in the snare of love for Gauranga.[^28-54]

[^28-51]: Signature: "Nayanananda." PK 787: vol. 2, PDF p. 124 (printed p. 111), 3rd shakha, 10th pallava, section "rūpānurāga"
(rupanuraga), "punashcha prakarantaram" — a gaura-chandrika of another kind, no. 11 (mark "॥১১॥৭৮৭॥"); raga dhanashi; MS P-R-Sa
no. 1277. The same pada is PK 290 (vol. 1, PDF pp. 201–202, printed pp. 190–191, 3rd pallava, "kebala rūpānurāga"; a duplicate with
minor variants). GPT1 — p. 166, no. 30 (raga dhanashi-dharatala); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 30 (catalogue: NN-012). Signature in PK — A.
On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^28-52]: "The freshness of a flower" (phulera kām̐cani) — the meaning of "kām̐cani" is uncertain (from kām̐cā, "fresh, young"?); MSS
"ka"–"cha" and GPT1: "kulera kām̐cani" (? "…of the family"). PK 290 and GPT1: "loving glance" (piriti-cāhani) instead of "radiant."
[^28-53]: "The little doll of my soul" (parāṇa-putali) — the inmost soul, the "pupil" of life. PK 290 and GPT1: "Friend, in what shapes
has the Creator fashioned Him!"
[^28-54]: "Charming one" (binodinī) is usually a name of Radha; here the poet addresses the heroine (her name is not given; pronouns in
lower case). MS "kha" and GPT1: "lady" (ṭhākurāṇī). In PK the pada stands as a gaura-chandrika to Radha's rupanuraga: its frame — a
love that cannot be revealed, "a daughter of a family," "not free" — is taken from the padas on Radha. MS P-R-Sa: "life will not go
out" (bāhirābāra), "in the fire of love" (prema anale).

## 20. Nayanananda — "kariba ki muñi kariba ki…" (PK 694)
*Nagari-bhava (a dream). "What shall I do? Secretly I am caught in love for Gauranga": in a dream Gorachand's face appeared to her —
long curling hair, eyes full of rasa; she, the daughter of a worthy family and the daughter-in-law of a worthy family, a faithful
wife, was lying in her husband's arms — and the waters of love for Gora swept all away. The poet: how will you now restrain your
heart? In PK, a gaura-chandrika to the section "telling of a meeting in a dream." Raga vibhasa.*[^28-55]

করিব কি মুঞি করিব কি ।
গোপতে গৌরাঙ্গের প্রেমে ঠেকিয়াছি ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*kariba ki muñi kariba ki |*
*gopate gaurāṅgera preme ṭhekiyāchi || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* kariba ki muñi — what shall I do; gopate — secretly; gaurāṅgera preme — in love for Gauranga; ṭhekiyāchi — I am caught

**20.1.** *(Refrain)* What shall I do, what shall I do?
Secretly I am caught in love for Gauranga.

দীঘল দীঘল চাঁচর কেশ রসাল দুটি আঁখি ।
রূপে গুণে প্রেমে তনু মাখা যেন দেখি ॥

*dīghala dīghala cām̐cara keśa rasāla duṭi ām̐khi |*
*rūpe guṇe preme tanu mākhā yena dekhi ||*

*Word for word:* dīghala dīghala cām̐cara keśa — long, long curling hair; rasāla duṭi ām̐khi — two eyes full of rasa; rūpe guṇe preme — with beauty, virtue and love; tanu mākhā yena dekhi — I see a body as if anointed

**20.2.** Long, long curling hair, two eyes full of rasa;
I see a body as if anointed with beauty, virtue and love.

আচম্বিতে আসিয়া ধরল মোর বুক ।
স্বপনে দেখিলুঁ হাম গোরাচাঁদের মুখ ॥

*ācambite āsiyā dharala mora buka |*
*svapane dekhilum̐ hāma gorācām̐dera mukha ||*

*Word for word:* ācambite — suddenly; āsiyā dharala mora buka — came and seized my breast; svapane dekhilum̐ hāma — in a dream I saw; gorācām̐dera mukha — Gorachand's face

**20.3.** Suddenly it came and seized my breast:
in a dream I saw Gorachand's face.[^28-56]

বাপের কুলের মুই কুলের ঝিয়ারী ।
শ্বশুর-কুলের মুঞি কুলের বৌহারী ॥

*bāpera kulera mui kulera jhiyārī |*
*śvaśura-kulera muñi kulera bauhārī ||*

*Word for word:* bāpera kulera — in my father's family; mui kulera jhiyārī — I am the daughter of the house; śvaśura-kulera — in my father-in-law's family; muñi kulera bauhārī — I am the daughter-in-law of the house

**20.4.** In my father's family I am the daughter of the house,
in my father-in-law's family I am the daughter-in-law of the house.

পতিব্রতা মুঞি সে আছিলুঁ পতির কোলে ।
সকল ভাসিয়া গেল গোরা-প্রেম-জলে ॥

*patibratā muñi se āchilum̐ patira kole |*
*sakala bhāsiyā gela gorā-prema-jale ||*

*Word for word:* patibratā muñi se — I, a faithful wife; āchilum̐ patira kole — was in my husband's arms; sakala bhāsiyā gela — all was swept away; gorā-prema-jale — by the waters of love for Gora

**20.5.** I, a faithful wife, was lying in my husband's arms —
and the waters of love for Gora swept all away.[^28-57]

কহয়ে নয়নানন্দ বুঝিলাম ইহা ।
কোন পরকারে এখন নিবারিবা হিয়া ॥

*kahaye nayanānanda bujhilāma ihā |*
*kona parakāre ekhana nibāribā hiyā ||*

*Word for word:* kahaye nayanānanda — says Nayanananda; bujhilāma ihā — I have understood this; kona parakāre — by what means; ekhana nibāribā hiyā — will you now restrain your heart

**20.6.** Says Nayanananda: I have understood this —
how will you now restrain your heart?

[^28-55]: Signature: "Nayanananda." PK: vol. 2, PDF p. 77 (printed p. 64), 3rd shakha, section "atha svapnarasodgāraḥ| śrīgauracandraḥ"
(gaura-chandrika to the telling of a meeting in a dream), no. 31 (mark "॥৩১॥৬৯৪॥"); raga vibhasa; MSS P-R-Sa no. 1169 and P-R
no. 10/39. GPT1 — pp. 165–166, no. 29 (raga vibhasa); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 29 (catalogue: NN-011). Signature in PK — A (MS P-R has
no signature). On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^28-56]: The subject is not named: "it came and seized my breast" we take as the sudden shock of the dream (in Bengali "buka dharā" —
"the heart is gripped"); it can also be read "[He] came and embraced me." MS P-R puts this couplet before the signature; MS P-R:
instead of 20.1b — "I have fallen into the bhava of Gaurangachand."
[^28-57]: The sharpest nagari motif in Nayanananda's padas: a married woman, "a faithful wife," gives herself in a dream to love for
Gaura. This is a transfer of the plot of the padas on Radha (the parakiya-rasa of Vraja) to a townswoman of Nadia; translated exactly,
with nothing added. The tradition rejects such a depiction of Gaura (introductory note). MS P-R: "swept away by tears" (nayanera jale).

## 21. Yadu — "kaha nā upāya sakhi kaha nā upāya…" (PK 703)
*Nagari-bhava. "Do tell me, friend, what to do: Gora Raya ceaselessly rises in my heart!" Love for Gorachand cannot be forgotten, yet
Fate has made her a noble wife; His sweet speech is a stream of nectar, His form steals the hearts of faithful wives; the poet: "I have
sold myself to love for Gora for this whole life." In PK, a gaura-chandrika to the section "anuraga in the telling of a meeting."
Raga suhai.*[^28-58]

কহ না উপায় সখি কহ না উপায় ।
নিরবধি হৃদয়ে জাগয়ে গোরা রায় ॥

*kaha nā upāya sakhi kaha nā upāya |*
*nirabadhi hṛdaye jāgaye gorā rāya ||*

*Word for word:* kaha nā upāya — do tell me a way; sakhi — friend; nirabadhi — ceaselessly; hṛdaye jāgaye — rises in my heart; gorā rāya — Gora Raya

**21.1.** Do tell me, friend, what to do, tell me what to do:
ceaselessly Gora Raya rises in my heart.

পাসরা না যায় গোরাচাঁদের পিরিতি ।
কি করিব বিধি সে করিল কুলবতী ॥

*pāsarā nā yāya gorācām̐dera piriti |*
*ki kariba bidhi se karila kulabatī ||*

*Word for word:* pāsarā nā yāya — cannot be forgotten; gorācām̐dera piriti — Gorachand's love; ki kariba — what can I do; bidhi se karila kulabatī — Fate made me a noble wife

**21.2.** Love for Gorachand cannot be forgotten —
what can I do? Fate has made me a noble wife.

কিবা সে মধুর বাণী অমিয়ার ধারা ।
কিবা সে মোহন রূপ সতী-মন-চোরা ॥

*kibā se madhura bāṇī amiyāra dhārā |*
*kibā se mohana rūpa satī-mana-corā ||*

*Word for word:* kibā se madhura bāṇī — what sweet speech; amiyāra dhārā — a stream of nectar; kibā se mohana rūpa — what an enchanting form; satī-mana-corā — stealing the hearts of chaste wives

**21.3.** What sweet speech — a stream of nectar!
What an enchanting form — it steals the hearts of faithful wives![^28-59]

যদু কহে কি কহিব গোরা-গুণ যত ।
বিকাইলুঁ গোরা-প্রেমে এ জনমের মত ॥

*yadu kahe ki kahiba gorā-guṇa yata |*
*bikāilum̐ gorā-preme e janamera mata ||*

*Word for word:* yadu kahe — says Yadu; ki kahiba — what can I say; gorā-guṇa yata — of all Gora's virtues; bikāilum̐ gorā-preme — I have sold myself to love for Gora; e janamera mata — for this whole life

**21.4.** Says Yadu: what can I say of all Gora's virtues?
I have sold myself to love for Gora for this whole life.[^28-60]

[^28-58]: Signature: "Yadu." PK: vol. 2, PDF p. 82 (printed p. 69), 3rd shakha, 6th pallava, section "rasodgārānurāgaḥ| prakārāntaraṃ|
tatra gauracandraḥ" (anuraga in the telling of a meeting — of another kind; here a gaura-chandrika), no. 40 (mark "॥৪০॥৭০৩॥"); raga
suhai; MS P-R-Sa no. 1176. Not found in GPT, KGC or BR (catalogue: YD-020; found in the full collation of PK, chapter 16, and
deferred to the nagari padas). The signature "yadu": Yadunatha Dasa (Kavichandra) or Yadunandana — not established (as with the
"Yadu" padas PK 2209, 2182 — chapter 16, note 1); C. On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^28-59]: "Noble wife" (kulabatī), "faithful wives" (satī) — a nagari motif (cf. chapter 27, note 2): Gaura's beauty is such that even the
chaste lose their peace — a formula as in the padas on Krishna. MS P-R-Sa: "sweet form" (madhura) instead of "enchanting."
[^28-60]: In the signature the poet speaks of himself: "I have sold myself to love for Gora" — no longer as a townswoman, but as a
devotee who has given himself to Gaura. MS "kha": "what can I say" (ki kahiba) instead of "what can I do" (21.2).

## 22. Yadu — "gorācām̐de dekhiyā ki hailum̐…" (PK 859; GPT1 p. 169, no. 38)
*Nagari-bhava (reproaching the elders). "What has become of me since I saw Gorachand! I am caught in the snare of secret love": at
home she cannot bear the torment from the elders, her mother-in-law always scolds her because, remembering Gora's form, she goes mad;
she cannot stay at home. The poet: "Leave Gora — He will not leave you." In PK, a gaura-chandrika to the section "reproaches to the
elders." Raga varadi.*[^28-61]

গোরাচাঁদে দেখিয়া কি হৈলুঁ ।
গোপত পিরিতি-ফাঁদে মুঞি সে ঠেকিলুঁ ॥

*gorācām̐de dekhiyā ki hailum̐ |*
*gopata piriti-phām̐de muñi se ṭhekilum̐ ||*

*Word for word:* gorācām̐de dekhiyā — having seen Gorachand; ki hailum̐ — what has become of me; gopata piriti-phām̐de — in the snare of secret love; muñi se ṭhekilum̐ — I have been caught

**22.1.** What has become of me since I saw Gorachand!
I have been caught in the snare of secret love.

ঘরে গুরুজন-জ্বালা সহিতে না পারি ।
অবলা করিল বিহি তাহে কুলনারী ॥

*ghare gurujana-jvālā sahite nā pāri |*
*abalā karila bihi tāhe kulanārī ||*

*Word for word:* ghare — at home; gurujana-jvālā — the torment from the elders; sahite nā pāri — I cannot bear; abalā karila bihi — the Creator made [me] a weak woman; tāhe kulanārī — and a family woman besides

**22.2.** At home I cannot bear the torment from the elders:
the Creator made me a weak woman, and a family woman besides.

গোরা-রূপ মনে হৈলে হইয়ে পাগলী ।
দেখিয়া শাশুড়ী মোর সদা পাড়ে গালি ॥

*gorā-rūpa mane haile haiye pāgalī |*
*dekhiyā śāśuṛī mora sadā pāṛe gāli ||*

*Word for word:* gorā-rūpa mane haile — when Gora's form comes to mind; haiye pāgalī — I go mad; dekhiyā — seeing [it]; śāśuṛī mora — my mother-in-law; sadā pāṛe gāli — always scolds

**22.3.** When Gora's form comes to mind, I go mad;
seeing it, my mother-in-law always scolds me.

রহিতে নারিলুঁ ঘরে কি করি উপায় ।
যদু কহে ছাড়িলে না ছাড়ে গোরারায় ॥

*rahite nārilum̐ ghare ki kari upāya |*
*yadu kahe chāṛile nā chāṛe gorārāya ||*

*Word for word:* rahite nārilum̐ ghare — I could not stay at home; ki kari upāya — what remedy can I find; yadu kahe — says Yadu; chāṛile nā chāṛe gorārāya — leave Him, and Gora Raya will not leave you

**22.4.** I could not stay at home — what am I to do?
Says Yadu: leave Gora Raya — He will not leave you.[^28-62]

[^28-61]: Signature: "Yadu." PK: vol. 2, PDF p. 153 (printed p. 140), 3rd shakha, section "gurugaṇādīn prati ākṣepo yathā|
śrīgauracandraḥ" (reproaches to the elders; gaura-chandrika), no. 61 (mark "॥৬১॥৮৫৯॥"); raga varadi; MS P-R-Sa no. 1349. GPT1 —
p. 169, no. 38 (raga varadi); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 38. **Catalogue correction**: row YD-014 listed the pada as "GPT only"; it is
PK 859 (found in preparing this chapter). The signature "Yadu" — who exactly is not established (cf. note 58); C. On nagari-bhava see
the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^28-62]: "Leave — He will not leave" (chāṛile nā chāṛe): even if she tries to forget Gora, He will not go out of her heart. MS P-R-Sa:
"cannot be left" (chāṛite) — "Gora Raya cannot be left"; GPT1: "I shall go mad" (haibe pāgalī). MSS "gha," P-R-Sa: "dei" instead of
"pāṛe" ("heaps abuse" — the same sense). The mother-in-law and the elders are figures of the padas on Radha (Jatila, Kutila); here
in the domestic life of Nadia.

## 23. Murari Gupta (signature in GPT only) — "sakhi he kena gorā niṭhurāi mohe…" (GPT1 p. 172, no. 48)
*Nagari-bhava. "Friend, why is Gora cruel to me? To the world He showed mercy, giving the shade of His feet — but me, unfortunate, He
has passed over." The woman who gave her life to love for Gaura finds no peace: had she known before, she would not have loved; what
joy is there in love if He does not look back? The poet answers: love for Gauranga burns; give up family honour, take shelter at His
feet — then you will attain Shachi's son. Raga suhai.*[^28-63]

সখি হে কেন গোরা নিঠুরাই মোহে ।
জগতে করিল দয়া দিয়া সেই পদছায়া
বঞ্চল এ অভাগিরে কহে ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*sakhi he kena gorā niṭhurāi mohe |*
*jagate karila dayā diyā sei padachāyā*
*bañcala e abhāgire kahe || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* sakhi he — O friend; kena gorā niṭhurāi mohe — why is Gora cruel to me; jagate karila dayā — He showed mercy to the world; diyā sei padachāyā — giving the shade of His feet; bañcala e abhāgire — He has passed over this unfortunate one; kahe — say (why?)

**23.1.** *(Refrain)* Friend, why is Gora cruel to me?
To the world He showed mercy, giving the shade of His feet —
but me, unfortunate, He has passed over: tell me, why?[^28-64]

গৌর-প্রেমে সঁপি প্রাণ জিউ করে আনচান
স্থির হৈয়া রইতে নারি ঘরে ।
আগে যদি জানিতাম পীরিতি না করিতাম
যাচিঞা না দিতু প্রাণ পরে ॥

*gaura-preme sam̐pi prāṇa jiu kare ānacāna*
*sthira haiyā raite nāri ghare |*
*āge yadi jānitāma pīriti nā karitāma*
*yāciñā nā ditu prāṇa pare ||*

*Word for word:* gaura-preme sam̐pi prāṇa — having given my life to love for Gaura; jiu kare ānacāna — my soul is restless; sthira haiyā raite nāri ghare — I cannot stay calmly at home; āge yadi jānitāma — had I known before; pīriti nā karitāma — I would not have loved; yāciñā nā ditu prāṇa pare — I would not have offered my life to another

**23.2.** I gave my life to love for Gaura — my soul is restless,
I cannot stay calmly at home.
Had I known before, I would not have loved,
I would not have offered my life to another of my own accord.

আমি ঝুরি যার তরে সে যদি না চায় ফিরে
এমন পীরিতে কিবা সুখ ।
চাতক সলিল চাহে বজর ক্ষেপিলে তাহে
যায় ফাটি যায় কিনা বুক ॥

*āmi jhuri yāra tare se yadi nā cāya phire*
*emana pīrite kibā sukha |*
*cātaka salila cāhe bajara kṣepile tāhe*
*yāya phāṭi yāya kinā buka ||*

*Word for word:* āmi jhuri yāra tare — He for whom I weep; se yadi nā cāya phire — if He does not turn to look; emana pīrite kibā sukha — what joy is there in such love; cātaka salila cāhe — the chataka begs for water; bajara kṣepile tāhe — if a thunderbolt is hurled at it; yāya phāṭi yāya kinā buka — will its breast not burst

**23.3.** He for whom I weep — if He does not turn to look,
what joy is there in such love?
The chataka begs the cloud for water — and if a thunderbolt is hurled at it,
will its breast not burst?[^28-65]

মুরারি গুপত কয় পীরিতি সহজ নয়
বিশেষে গৌরাঙ্গ-প্রেমের জ্বালা ।
কুলমান সব ছাড় চরণ আশ্রয় কর
তবে সে পাইবা শচীর বালা ॥

*murāri gupata kaya pīriti sahaja naya*
*biśeṣe gaurāṅga-premera jvālā |*
*kulamāna saba chāṛa caraṇa āśraya kara*
*tabe se pāibā śacīra bālā ||*

*Word for word:* murāri gupata kaya — says Murari Gupta; pīriti sahaja naya — love is no easy thing; biśeṣe gaurāṅga-premera jvālā — least of all the burning of love for Gauranga; kulamāna saba chāṛa — give up all family honour; caraṇa āśraya kara — take shelter at His feet; tabe se pāibā śacīra bālā — then you will attain Shachi's son

**23.4.** Says Murari Gupta: love is no easy thing,
least of all the burning of love for Gauranga.
Give up all family honour, take shelter at His feet —
then you will attain Shachi's son.[^28-66]

[^28-63]: Signature: "Murari Gupta." GPT1 — p. 172, no. 48 (raga suhai; scan PDF p. 431), right after PK 751 with the same signature
(GPT1 no. 47 — Radha's anuraga, without Gaura; catalogue: MU-002); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 48 (catalogue: MU-010). Not in PK, KGC or
BR. Majumdar considers most Bengali padas signed "Murari" doubtful (cf. chapter 13, nos. 11, 12); attribution by GPT only (C). On
nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^28-64]: "Tell me, why?" — we read "kahe" as "kāhe" ("why?", Vrajabuli); reading "kahe" ("says"), the sense is the same: the heroine
complains to her friend. "The shade of His feet" — shelter, the Lord's mercy to all.
[^28-65]: The chataka is a bird which, as the belief goes, drinks only rain water and waits for it from the cloud; if the cloud hurls
lightning instead of rain — an image of unrequited love from the padas on Radha. GPT1: "bāra" — a misprint for "yāra."
[^28-66]: The poet's counsel turns the nagari's complaint into an instruction on shelter: "give up family honour, take shelter at His
feet" — the path of surrender to Gaura (sharanagati), not of a love play. Some other padas of the section end in the same way (cf.
no. 21, note 60).

## 24. Dasa Murari — "eka dina mane ānanda bāṛhala…" (PK 2334)
*Nagari-bhava (the townswomen see Gaura and Nitai in the street). One day Nitai and Gaura, joyful and laughing, go alone to the
bazaar; the townswomen on their way to fetch water meet Them and cannot take their eyes off Gora: "It seems a dancer has come from
Gokula — let us go and see Him dance in the bazaar, let the water-fetching go hang!" Arm in arm the women fill both banks of the
Jahnavi. Raga dhanashi.*[^28-67]

এক দিন মনে আনন্দ বাঢ়ল নিতাই গৌর রায় ।
হাসিতে হাসিতে কেহ নাহি সাথে বাজারে চলিয়া যায় ॥

*eka dina mane ānanda bāṛhala nitāi gaura rāya |*
*hāsite hāsite keha nāhi sāthe bājāre caliyā yāya ||*

*Word for word:* eka dina — one day; mane ānanda bāṛhala — joy rose in Their hearts; nitāi gaura rāya — Nitai and Gaura Raya; hāsite hāsite — laughing; keha nāhi sāthe — with no one beside Them; bājāre caliyā yāya — go to the bazaar

**24.1.** One day, with joy in Their hearts, Nitai and Gaura Raya
go laughing to the bazaar — no one is with Them.

হেনই সময়ে যতেক নাগরী জল ভরিবারে যায় ।
পথে হৈল দেখা রূপের নাহি লেখা দিঠি পইল গোরা-গায় ॥

*henai samaye yateka nāgarī jala bharibāre yāya |*
*pathe haila dekhā rūpera nāhi lekhā diṭhi paila gorā-gāya ||*

*Word for word:* henai samaye — at that very time; yateka nāgarī — all the townswomen; jala bharibāre yāya — are going to fetch water; pathe haila dekhā — they met on the way; rūpera nāhi lekhā — the beauty is beyond description; diṭhi paila gorā-gāya — their eyes fell on Gora's person

**24.2.** At that very time all the townswomen were going for water;
they met on the way — the beauty is beyond description — their eyes fell on Gora.

কেহ বলে ইথে গোকুল হইতে নাটুয়া আইসাছে পারা ।
চল দেখিবারে নাচিবে বাজারে মরুক মরুক জল ভরা ॥

*keha bale ithe gokula haite nāṭuyā āisāche pārā |*
*cala dekhibāre nācibe bājāre maruka maruka jala bharā ||*

*Word for word:* keha bale — one says; ithe — here; gokula haite — from Gokula; nāṭuyā āisāche pārā — a dancer seems to have come; cala dekhibāre — let us go to see; nācibe bājāre — He will dance in the bazaar; maruka maruka jala bharā — let the water-fetching go hang

**24.3.** One says: "It seems a dancer has come here from Gokula!
Let us go and see — He will dance in the bazaar; let the water-fetching go hang!"[^28-68]

বাহে বাহে ছান্দা জাহ্নবী দু-কান্দা ভরিল যতেক নারী ।
হেরি গোরা পানে ভুলিল নয়ানে কহয়ে দাস মুরারি ॥

*bāhe bāhe chāndā jāhnabī du-kāndā bharila yateka nārī |*
*heri gorā pāne bhulila nayāne kahaye dāsa murāri ||*

*Word for word:* bāhe bāhe chāndā — arm linked in arm; jāhnabī du-kāndā — both banks of the Jahnavi; bharila yateka nārī — all the women filled; heri gorā pāne — gazing at Gora; bhulila nayāne — lost themselves through their eyes; kahaye dāsa murāri — says Dasa Murari

**24.4.** Arm in arm, all the women filled both banks of the Jahnavi;
gazing at Gora, they forgot themselves — says Dasa Murari.

[^28-67]: Signature: "dāsa murāri" (Dasa Murari). PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 316 (printed p. 305), 4th shakha, 23rd pallava, section
"śrīcaitanya-nityānandera rūpa-guṇa-barṇana" (the form and virtues of Chaitanya and Nityananda), no. 3 (mark "॥৩॥২৩৩৪॥"); raga
dhanashi; MS P-R-Sa no. 2408. GPT1 — p. 47, no. 71; GPT2 — sect. 1.3, no. 71 (catalogue: MU-005; in chapter 6 deferred to the nagari
padas). According to Majumdar, the signature "dāsa murāri" is not Murari Gupta; the author is not established (C). On nagari-bhava see
the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^28-68]: "A dancer from Gokula" — the townswomen, without knowing it, recognize Krishna in Gaura (cf. no. 4, note 12). Here the nagari
motif is mild: the women only crowd to see Gaura and Nitai; there is no love speech. MS P-R-Sa: "is coming" (āsiche); GPT1: "their eyes
filled [with tears]" (bharila nayāne) instead of "they forgot themselves" (24.4).

## 25. Balarama Dasa — "gaura-baraṇa maṇi-ābharaṇa nāṭuyā-mohana beśa…" (PK 2109)
*Nagari-bhava. Gaura's form — golden, in jewels, in the enchanting attire of a dancer: gazing at Him, the world forgot itself. "I am
dying, friend, seeing Gaura's figure: did not the Creator fashion, to slay young women, a Kama above Kama?" The townswomen lose their
composure and, disregarding their husbands, weep; the poet offers himself for the beauty of the nails of Gora's feet. In PK it opens the
pallava "Gaura's form." Raga mangala.*[^28-69]

গৌর-বরণ মণি-আভরণ নাটুয়া-মোহন বেশ ।
দেখিতে দেখিতে ভুবন ভুলল টলিল সকল দেশ ॥

*gaura-baraṇa maṇi-ābharaṇa nāṭuyā-mohana beśa |*
*dekhite dekhite bhubana bhulala ṭalila sakala deśa ||*

*Word for word:* gaura-baraṇa — golden complexion; maṇi-ābharaṇa — jewelled ornaments; nāṭuyā-mohana beśa — the enchanting attire of a dancer; dekhite dekhite — gazing and gazing; bhubana bhulala — the world was bewildered; ṭalila sakala deśa — the whole land swayed

**25.1.** Golden colour, jewelled ornaments, the enchanting attire of a dancer:
gazing and gazing, the world forgot itself, the whole land swayed.

মলুঁ মলুঁ সোই দেখিয়া গৌর-ঠাম ।
বধিতে যুবতী গঢ়ল কি বিধি কামের উপরে কাম ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*malum̐ malum̐ soi dekhiyā gaura-ṭhāma |*
*badhite yubatī gaṛhala ki bidhi kāmera upare kāma || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* malum̐ malum̐ — I am dying, dying; soi — friend; dekhiyā gaura-ṭhāma — seeing Gaura's figure; badhite yubatī — to slay young women; gaṛhala ki bidhi — did the Creator fashion; kāmera upare kāma — a Kama above Kama

**25.2.** *(Refrain)* I am dying, dying, friend, seeing Gaura's figure!
