*Word for word:* dhairaja dharama lāja kula-bhaya — composure, dharma, shame, fear for family; dila tilāñjali tāya — gave up for Him; gorā-sukhe sukha — in Gora's happiness their happiness; bāṛhaye satata — ever grows; dāsa narahari gāya — sings Narahari Dasa

**14.6.** Composure, dharma, shame, fear for their family — all they have given up for Him;
in Gora's happiness their happiness ever grows, sings Narahari Dasa.[^29-41]

[^29-40]: Signature: "Dasa Narahari" (dāsa narahari). GPT1 — p. 189, no. 86 ("yathārāga"; scan PDF p. 448); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 86 (catalogue: NG-080). Witness —
Narahari Chakravarti's *Gaura-charita-chintamani* (GCC; ed. 1947, p. 67): kirana 7 — "in the morning, the conversations among themselves of the
nagaris of Navadvipa, filled with that love", pada 2 (after an opening pada on the joy in Shachi's house at dawn). Kirana 7 of GCC is wholly a
"description of the nagaris of Navadvipa"; its padas form the greater part of section 3.2 of GPT (nos. 86–99, 124 and on; kiranas 8–11 — the dreams,
wishes and conversations of the townswomen) — a late (18th-century) poetic elaboration of the nagari motif by Narahari Chakravarti (B). Majumdar
says plainly that the long padas of GPT, uneven in metre, signed Narahari cannot be Sarakara's; the collation confirms it: they are padas of GCC.
Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^29-41]: "Their happiness lies in Gora's happiness" (gorā-sukhe sukha) is the mark of the gopis' love, which seeks only Krishna's happiness and not its
own (CC Adi 4: in the gopis' love there is not a trace of desire for their own enjoyment). Giving up "shame and family" is the same formula of the
supremacy of prema over worldly dharma (cf. note 28). The translation is faithful to the author; the tradition does not accept worship of Gaura in
the mood of the nagaris (introductory note, chapter 27).

## 15. Narahari — "mari mari hena nadīyā-nāgarīgaṇera…" (GPT1 pp. 189–190, no. 87; GCC 7.3)
*Nagari-bhava. The townswomen of Nadia spent the night in longing: some did not sleep, singing of Gorachand's deeds, others saw Him in a dream;
at dawn they come out of their houses on the pretext of work; skilled in stratagems, they do whatever pleases the elders and, with their leave,
go where they wish; they gather in a secluded place — the poet admires them. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC,
kirana 7, pada 3.*[^29-42]

মরি মরি, হেন নদীয়া-নাগরীগণের বালাই লৈয়া ।
আজুক রজনী গোঙাইলা সবে অধিক আতুর হৈয়া ॥

*mari mari, hena nadīyā-nāgarīgaṇera bālāi laiyā |*
*ājuka rajanī goṅāilā sabe adhika ātura haiyā ||*

*Word for word:* mari mari — ah, ah; hena nadīyā-nāgarīgaṇera — of such townswomen of Nadia; bālāi laiyā — taking their misfortunes on myself; ājuka rajanī — this night; goṅāilā sabe — they all spent; adhika ātura haiyā — in great longing

**15.1.** Ah, ah! — I take upon myself all the misfortunes of such townswomen of Nadia:
this night they all spent in great longing.[^29-43]

কেহ কেহ গোরাচাঁদের চরিত গাইয়া জাগিলা নিশি ।
কেহ কেহ সুখে শুতিয়া স্বপনে পাইলা গৌর-শশী ॥

*keha keha gorācām̐dera carita gāiyā jāgilā niśi |*
*keha keha sukhe śutiyā svapane pāilā gaura-śaśī ||*

*Word for word:* keha keha — some; gorācām̐dera carita gāiyā — singing of Gorachand's deeds; jāgilā niśi — stayed awake all night; sukhe śutiyā — sleeping sweetly; svapane pāilā gaura-śaśī — found the Moon Gaura in a dream

**15.2.** Some stayed awake all night, singing of Gorachand's deeds;
others, sleeping sweetly, found the Moon Gaura in a dream.

পুনঃ সে শয়ন ত্যজিয়া উঠিলা নিশি-পরভাত-কালে ।
এ-ঘর সে-ঘর হইতে বাহির হইলা কাজের ছলে ॥

*punaḥ se śayana tyajiyā uṭhilā niśi-parabhāta-kāle |*
*e-ghara se-ghara haite bāhira hailā kājera chale ||*

*Word for word:* punaḥ se śayana tyajiyā — again leaving their beds; uṭhilā niśi-parabhāta-kāle — rose at the end of the night; e-ghara se-ghara haite — from this house and that; bāhira hailā — came out; kājera chale — on the pretext of work

**15.3.** Leaving their beds again, they rose at the end of the night
and came out of this house and that, as if on some errand.

পরম চতুরা নাগরী-চরিত কিছু না বুঝিতে পারি ।
গুরুজন-সুখ যে কাজে, সে কাজ করয়ে যতন করি ॥

*parama caturā nāgarī-carita kichu nā bujhite pāri |*
*gurujana-sukha ye kāje, se kāja karaye yatana kari ||*

*Word for word:* parama caturā nāgarī-carita — the ways of the very clever townswomen; kichu nā bujhite pāri — I cannot understand at all; gurujana-sukha ye kāje — whatever work pleases the elders; se kāja karaye yatana kari — that work they do with care

**15.4.** The ways of these clever townswomen I cannot understand at all:
whatever work pleases the elders, that they do with care.

তা-সবার অনুমতি-মতে গতাগতি, কি কহিব আর ।
নিতি নিতি রীতি যেরূপে, সেরূপে সুখের নাহিক পার ॥

*tā-sabāra anumati-mate gatāgati, ki kahiba āra |*
*niti niti rīti yerūpe, serūpe sukhera nāhika pāra ||*

*Word for word:* tā-sabāra anumati-mate — with their leave; gatāgati — coming and going; ki kahiba āra — what more to say; niti niti rīti yerūpe — as the custom is day after day; serūpe sukhera nāhika pāra — so their happiness has no bounds

**15.5.** With the elders' leave they come and go — what more is there to say!
As their custom is day after day, so their happiness has no bounds.

অলখিত অতি নিভৃতে বসি যুবতী জগত-লোভা ।
ক্রমে ক্রমে সবে মিলে তথা, নরহরি নিরখয়ে শোভা ॥

*alakhita ati nibhṛte basi yubatī jagata-lobhā |*
*krame krame sabe mile tathā, narahari nirakhaye śobhā ||*

*Word for word:* alakhita — unseen; ati nibhṛte basi — sitting in a secluded place; yubatī jagata-lobhā — young women who captivate the world; krame krame sabe mile tathā — one by one all gather there; narahari nirakhaye śobhā — Narahari beholds the beauty

**15.6.** Unseen, in a secluded place, sit the young women who captivate the world;
one by one they all gather there — and Narahari admires them.

[^29-42]: Signature: "Narahari." GPT1 — pp. 189–190, no. 87 (scan PDF pp. 448–449); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 87 (catalogue: NG-081). GCC — kirana 7, pada 3 (ed. 1947,
pp. 67–68). GCC readings: "keha keha gorācāndera caritra gāiyā", "niśi parabhāta-kāle". B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section
(chapter 27).
[^29-43]: "I take upon myself their misfortunes" (bālāi laiyā) is a Bengali formula of admiring tenderness (lit. "taking their ills upon oneself"): the
poet blesses the townswomen.

## 16. Narahari — "ki kaba yubatī-janera yerūpa pīriti paraspare…" (GPT1 p. 190, no. 88; GCC 7.4)
*Nagari-bhava. The love of the young townswomen for one another is such that their bodies are different but their heart is one: one, laughing,
puts her arm round another's neck, another teases; "leave your pretence, tell us about yesterday — what stood in whose way, who saw Gaura the
jewel and how, how did you spend this night?" Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 7, pada 4.*[^29-44]

কি কব যুবতী-জনের যেরূপ পীরিতি পরস্পরে ।
তনু ভিন, মন এক, এ লেহ কে বুঝিতে শকতি ধরে ॥

*ki kaba yubatī-janera yerūpa pīriti paraspare |*
*tanu bhina, mana eka, e leha ke bujhite śakati dhare ||*

*Word for word:* ki kaba — what shall I say; yubatī-janera — of the young women; yerūpa pīriti paraspare — the love for one another; tanu bhina — bodies different; mana eka — heart one; e leha — this tenderness; ke bujhite śakati dhare — who has the power to understand

**16.1.** What shall I say of the love of these young women for one another?
Their bodies are different, their heart is one — who has the power to understand this tenderness?

কোন রসিকিনী হাসিয়া হাসিয়া ধরয়ে কাহার গলা ।
কেহ কারু প্রতি করে উপহাস করিয়া কতেক ছলা ॥

*kona rasikinī hāsiyā hāsiyā dharaye kāhāra galā |*
*keha kāru prati kare upahāsa kariyā kateka chalā ||*

*Word for word:* kona rasikinī — one full of rasa; hāsiyā hāsiyā — laughing and laughing; dharaye kāhāra galā — puts her arm round another's neck; keha kāru prati — one towards another; kare upahāsa — teases; kariyā kateka chalā — in a thousand ways

**16.2.** One, full of rasa, laughing and laughing, puts her arm round another's neck;
that one teases this one in a thousand ways.

কেহ কহে, তেজি কপট কহ গো, কালিকার কথা শুনি ।
কার বা কেমন বাধা, কে কিরূপে দেখিলা গৌরমণি ॥

*keha kahe, teji kapaṭa kaha go, kālikāra kathā śuni |*
*kāra bā kemana bādhā, ke kirūpe dekhilā gauramaṇi ||*

*Word for word:* keha kahe — another says; teji kapaṭa — leaving pretence; kaha go — tell us; kālikāra kathā śuni — let us hear about yesterday; kāra vā kemana bādhā — what stood in whose way; ke kirūpe dekhilā gauramaṇi — who saw Gaura the jewel, and how

**16.3.** Another says: "Leave your pretence, tell us — let us hear about yesterday:
what stood in whose way, who saw Gaura the jewel, and how?"

কেহ কহে, অগো, আজুক রজনী কিরূপে বঞ্চিলে বল ।
নরহরি কহে, এ সব কাহিনী বিস্তারি কহিলে ভাল ॥

*keha kahe, ago, ājuka rajanī kirūpe bañcile bala |*
*narahari kahe, e saba kāhinī bistāri kahile bhāla ||*

*Word for word:* keha kahe ago — another says: ah; ājuka rajanī — this night; kirūpe bañcile bala — tell how you spent; narahari kahe — Narahari says; e saba kāhinī — all these stories; bistāri kahile bhāla — it would be good to tell at length

**16.4.** Another says: "Ah, tell me how you spent this night!"
Narahari says: it would be good to tell all these stories at length.

[^29-44]: Signature: "Narahari." GPT1 — p. 190, no. 88 (scan PDF p. 449); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 88 (catalogue: NG-082). GCC — kirana 7, pada 4 (p. 68); GCC: "kare
parihāsa" (GPT1 "upahāsa"), "keha kahe ogo". The pada introduces the townswomen's stories that follow (nos. 17–21). B. Nagari-bhava — see the
introductory note to the section (chapter 27).

## 17. Narahari — "ki puchaha sakhi kālikāra kathā…" (GPT1 pp. 190–191, no. 89; GCC 7.5)
*Nagari-bhava. A townswoman's story: in the evening she was sitting beside her mother-in-law and sister-in-law when she heard that Gaura was
passing along their lane; she did not know what to do, tears flowed; the mother-in-law kindly asked what was wrong — "I feel unwell" — and let
her go and lie down; on the pretext of sleep she went out of the gate and gazed her fill at His face. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably
Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 7, pada 5.*[^29-45]

কি পুছহ সখি কালিকার কথা, কহিতে উপজে হাসি ।
লাজ তেয়াগিয়া বলিয়ে যেরূপে দেখিনু নদ্যার শশী ॥

*ki puchaha sakhi kālikāra kathā, kahite upaje hāsi |*
*lāja teyāgiyā baliye yerūpe dekhinu nadyāra śaśī ||*

*Word for word:* ki puchaha sakhi — why do you ask, friend; kālikāra kathā — about yesterday; kahite upaje hāsi — it makes me laugh to tell; lāja teyāgiyā — casting off shame; baliye yerūpe — I will tell how; dekhinu nadyāra śaśī — I saw the Moon of Nadia

**17.1.** "Why do you ask, friend, about yesterday? — it makes me laugh to tell it;
casting off shame, I will tell how I saw the Moon of Nadia.

দিবা অবসানে শাশুড়ী ননদ আর বা কতেক জনা ।
তা-সবার পাশে বসিয়া আছিনু জানাঞা সুজনপনা ॥

*dibā abasāne śāśuṛī nanada āra bā kateka janā |*
*tā-sabāra pāśe basiyā āchinu jānāñā sujanapanā ||*

*Word for word:* dibā abasāne — at the end of the day; śāśuṛī nanada — mother-in-law, sister-in-law; āra vā kateka janā — and several others; tā-sabāra pāśe basiyā āchinu — I was sitting beside them; jānāñā sujanapanā — showing my good conduct

**17.2.** At the end of the day my mother-in-law, my sister-in-law and several other women —
I was sitting beside them, showing how well-behaved I am.

হেনই সময়ে আমাদের পথে আইলা পরাণ-পতি ।
শুনিয়া চকিত চৌদিকে চাহিয়া হইনু অথির-মতি ॥

*henai samaye āmādera pathe āilā parāṇa-pati |*
*śuniyā cakita caudike cāhiyā hainu athira-mati ||*

*Word for word:* henai samaye — just then; āmādera pathe — along our lane; āilā parāṇa-pati — came the Lord of my life; śuniyā cakita — hearing, startled; caudike cāhiyā — looking all around; hainu athira-mati — my mind was thrown into confusion

**17.3.** Just then the Lord of my life came along our lane;
hearing it, I started, looked all around — my mind was thrown into confusion.[^29-46]

বিষম সঙ্কটে পড়িনু, বিচার কিছু না মনেতে ফুরে ।
আনচান করে প্রাণ, কি করিব, নিয়ত নয়ন ঝুরে ॥

*biṣama saṅkaṭe paṛinu, bicāra kichu nā manete phure |*
*ānacāna kare prāṇa, ki kariba, niyata nayana jhure ||*

*Word for word:* biṣama saṅkaṭe paṛinu — I fell into a terrible fix; bicāra kichu nā manete phure — no thought came to my mind; ānacāna kare prāṇa — my soul was restless; ki kariba — what to do; niyata nayana jhure — my eyes kept weeping

**17.4.** I fell into a terrible fix, nothing came to my mind;
my soul was restless — what to do? — my eyes kept shedding tears.

আমারে বিমনা দেখিয়া শাশুড়ী কহয়ে মধুর কথা ।
কি লাগিয়া বাছা এমন, না জানি হৈয়াছে কোন বা ব্যথা ॥

*āmāre bimanā dekhiyā śāśuṛī kahaye madhura kathā |*
*ki lāgiyā bāchā emana, nā jāni haiyāche kona bā byathā ||*

*Word for word:* āmāre bimanā dekhiyā — seeing me downcast; śāśuṛī kahaye madhura kathā — the mother-in-law speaks sweetly; ki lāgiyā bāchā emana — why are you like this, child; nā jāni — I do not know; haiyāche kona vā byathā — what pain you have

**17.5.** Seeing me downcast, my mother-in-law says sweetly:
'Why are you like this, child? I don't know what pain you have.'

এ বোল বলিতে বলিনু তাহারে, গা মোর কেমন করে ।
এতেক শুনিয়া অনুমতি দিল, শুতিয়া থাকহ ঘরে ॥

*e bola balite balinu tāhāre, gā mora kemana kare |*
*eteka śuniyā anumati dila, śutiyā thākaha ghare ||*

*Word for word:* e bola balite — at these words; balinu tāhāre — I told her; gā mora kemana kare — I feel somehow unwell; eteka śuniyā — hearing this; anumati dila — she gave leave; śutiyā thākaha ghare — lie down in the house

**17.6.** At these words I told her: 'I feel somehow unwell';
hearing this, she gave me leave: 'Go and lie down in the house.'

শয়নের ছলে তুরিতে বাড়ীর বাহিরে দাঁড়ানু গিয়া ।
ও মুখ-মাধুরী বারেক নিরখি জুড়ানু নয়ন হিয়া ॥

*śayanera chale turite bāṛīra bāhire dām̐ṛānu giyā |*
*o mukha-mādhurī bāreka nirakhi juṛānu nayana hiyā ||*

*Word for word:* śayanera chale — on the pretext of lying down; turite — at once; bāṛīra bāhire — outside the house; dām̐ṛānu giyā — I went and stood; o mukha-mādhurī — the sweetness of that face; bāreka nirakhi — seeing once; juṛānu nayana hiyā — I refreshed my eyes and heart

**17.7.** As if to lie down, I went out at once and stood outside the gate,
and, seeing once the sweetness of that face, refreshed my eyes and heart.

কেহ না লখিতে পারিল, আমার আনন্দে ভরিল দে ।
নরহরি কহে, রসিক জনার চাতুরী বুঝিবে কে ॥

*keha nā lakhite pārila, āmāra ānande bharila de |*
*narahari kahe, rasika janāra cāturī bujhibe ke ||*

*Word for word:* keha nā lakhite pārila — no one could notice; āmāra ānande bharila de — my body was filled with joy; narahari kahe — Narahari says; rasika janāra cāturī — the stratagems of those full of rasa; bujhibe ke — who will understand

**17.8.** No one could notice — my body was filled with joy."
Narahari says: the stratagems of those full of rasa — who can understand them?[^29-47]

[^29-45]: Signature: "Narahari." GPT1 — pp. 190–191, no. 89 (scan PDF pp. 449–450); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 89 (catalogue: NG-083). GCC — kirana 7, pada 5 ("kācidāha" —
"a certain one says", pp. 68–69). GCC readings: "dekhinu nadyāra śaśī" (GPT1 "dekhila"), "athira ati", "rasika janāra cāturī" (so also GPT1). B.
Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^29-46]: "The Lord of my life" (parāṇa-pati) is the heroine's word for Gaura, as the gopis in the padas speak of Krishna; the translation is faithful
to the author. The Lord Himself in this and the following padas only passes along the lane or stands with His companions at the ghat — He takes
no part in the townswomen's stratagems (cf. nos. 18, 20, 21).
[^29-47]: The heroine's ruse — deceiving her mother-in-law for the darshana of Gaura — and the poet's praise of "the stratagems of those full of rasa"
are rendered as in the original: this is a poetic convention of the padas on purvaraga (so the gopis deceive their elders for Krishna's sake).
The tradition does not accept worship of Gaura in the mood of the nagaris (introductory note, chapter 27), and the *Chaitanya-bhagavata* says
plainly that the Lord in Navadvipa did not look at women.

## 18. Narahari — "kālikāra kathā ki kaba sajani…" (GPT1 p. 191, no. 90; GCC 7.6)
*Nagari-bhava. Another townswoman's story: yesterday she was sitting alone and heard that Gaura was passing; she hurried — and He with His
companions flashed by like lightning; she returned home in fear of the elders; someone told her mother-in-law, who came running in anger; the
young wife swore she had not seen Him and touched her feet — and the mother-in-law believed her. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably
Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 7, pada 6.*[^29-48]

কালিকার কথা কি কব সজনি, কহিতে পরাণ কান্দে ।
দেখিয়া দেখিতে না পাইনু প্রাণ-জীবন নদ্যার চান্দে ॥

*kālikāra kathā ki kaba sajani, kahite parāṇa kānde |*
*dekhiyā dekhite nā pāinu prāṇa-jībana nadyāra cānde ||*

*Word for word:* kālikāra kathā — about yesterday; ki kaba sajani — what shall I say, friend; kahite parāṇa kānde — my soul weeps as I tell; dekhiyā dekhite nā pāinu — I saw and did not see; prāṇa-jībana — the life of my life; nadyāra cānde — the Moon of Nadia

**18.1.** "What shall I say of yesterday, friend? — my soul weeps as I tell it:
I saw and yet did not see the Moon of Nadia, the life of my life.

শুন সে কাহিনী, একাকিনী অতি বিরলে বসিয়া ছিনু ।
আচম্বিতে লোকগণ-মুখে গৌর-গমন শুনিতে পাইনু ॥

*śuna se kāhinī, ekākinī ati birale basiyā chinu |*
*ācambite lokagaṇa-mukhe gaura-gamana śunite pāinu ||*

*Word for word:* śuna se kāhinī — listen to the story; ekākinī — alone; ati birale basiyā chinu — I was sitting in complete solitude; ācambite — suddenly; lokagaṇa-mukhe — from people's lips; gaura-gamana śunite pāinu — I heard that Gaura was coming

**18.2.** Listen to how it was: I was sitting alone, in complete solitude;
suddenly I hear from people's lips: Gaura is coming.

তুরিতে যাইয়া দেখিনু সে নিজ প্রিয় পরিকর-সাথে ।
বিদ্যুতের মত চমকি চলিয়া গেলেন আপন পথে ॥

*turite yāiyā dekhinu se nija priya parikara-sāthe |*
*bidyutera mata camaki caliyā gelena āpana pathe ||*

*Word for word:* turite yāiyā — hurrying; dekhinu se — I saw Him; nija priya parikara-sāthe — with His dear companions; bidyutera mata camaki — flashing like lightning; caliyā gelena āpana pathe — He went on His way

**18.3.** I hurried — and saw Him with His dear companions;
flashing like lightning, He went on His way.

বিকল হইনু লাজ তেয়াগিয়া বারেক ও মুখ হেরি ।
গুরুজন-ডরে ঘরে তরাতরি আইনু পরাণে মরি ॥

*bikala hainu lāja teyāgiyā bāreka o mukha heri |*
*gurujana-ḍare ghare tarātari āinu parāṇe mari ||*

*Word for word:* bikala hainu — I was overcome; lāja teyāgiyā — casting off shame; bāreka o mukha heri — looking once at that face; gurujana-ḍare — in fear of the elders; ghare tarātari āinu — I hurried home; parāṇe mari — more dead than alive

**18.4.** I was overcome, casting off shame and looking once at that face;
in fear of the elders I hurried home, more dead than alive.

না জানিয়ে কেবা কহিয়া দিলেক সে কথা শাশুড়ী-পাশে ।
শুনি সে বিকট-বদনে মো-পানে ধাইয়া আইল রোষে ॥

*nā jāniye kebā kahiyā dileka se kathā śāśuṛī-pāśe |*
*śuni se bikaṭa-badane mo-pāne dhāiyā āila roṣe ||*

*Word for word:* nā jāniye — I do not know; kebā kahiyā dileka — who told; se kathā śāśuṛī-pāśe — it to my mother-in-law; śuni se — hearing it, she; bikaṭa-badane — with a distorted face; mo-pāne dhāiyā āila roṣe — came running at me in anger

**18.5.** I do not know who told my mother-in-law about it;
hearing it, she came running at me in anger, her face distorted.

কত কটু বাণী কহিল, তা শুনি ভয়েতে কাঁপিল গা ।
না দেখিয়ে বলি শপথ খাইয়া ছুঁইনু তাহার পা ॥

*kata kaṭu bāṇī kahila, tā śuni bhayete kām̐pila gā |*
*nā dekhiye bali śapatha khāiyā chum̐inu tāhāra pā ||*

*Word for word:* kata kaṭu bāṇī kahila — how many harsh words she said; tā śuni — hearing them; bhayete kām̐pila gā — I trembled with fear; nā dekhiye bali — saying "I did not see"; śapatha khāiyā — swearing an oath; chum̐inu tāhāra pā — I touched her feet

**18.6.** How many harsh words she said! — I trembled with fear;
I said, 'I did not see Him', swore an oath and touched her feet.

কত কত মিছা কহিয়া সুজন হনু, সে প্রত্যয় গেল ।
নরহরি কহে, ইথে দোষ ইহা না মান, এ নহে ভাল ॥

*kata kata michā kahiyā sujana hanu, se pratyaya gela |*
*narahari kahe, ithe doṣa ihā nā māna, e nahe bhāla ||*

*Word for word:* kata kata michā kahiyā — telling many untruths; sujana hanu — I came out good; se pratyaya gela — she believed; narahari kahe — Narahari says; ithe doṣa ihā nā māna — do not count this a fault; e nahe bhāla — that is not right

**18.7.** Telling many untruths, I came out good — she believed me."
Narahari says: do not count this a fault — to think so is not right.[^29-49]

[^29-48]: Signature: "Narahari." GPT1 — p. 191, no. 90 (scan PDF p. 450; the number is garbled in the recognized text); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 90 (catalogue: NG-084).
GCC — kirana 7, pada 6 (p. 69). GCC readings: "turite yāiyā dekhinu se nija priya parikara sāthe" (GPT1 without "priya"), "chum̐inu uhāra pā". B.
Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^29-49]: 18.7b (narahari kahe ithe doṣa ihā nā māna, e nahe bhāla) can be read in two ways: "do not count this a fault — to count it so is not good"
(the poet excuses the ruse for the sake of darshana) or "you do not count this a fault — but it is not good" (a gentle reproach). It is translated
by the first reading, more likely in the context of GCC, where the poet constantly praises the townswomen's "stratagems" (cf. 17.8, 20.16). The lie
and the oath are a poetic convention of the padas on purvaraga (cf. note 47).

## 19. Narahari — "nilaji haiyā bali ye sajani…" (GPT1 p. 191, no. 91; GCC 7.7)
*Nagari-bhava. A townswoman's story: her husband's aunt came to visit for the first time in a long while; she joyfully sat beside her, but then
heard that Gaura was passing; she wanted to go out of the door — but the aunt, suspecting nothing, held her back by the end of her sari, adjuring
her "by my head", and asked about household matters; her kindness seemed like poison; the young wife did not know how to break away. Raga
"yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 7, pada 7.*[^29-50]

নিলজি হইয়া বলি যে, সজনি, শুন হে আমার কথা ।
নিকরুণ বিধি গত দিন মোরে দিলেক দারুণ ব্যথা ॥

*nilaji haiyā bali ye, sajani, śuna he āmāra kathā |*
*nikaruṇa bidhi gata dina more dileka dāruṇa byathā ||*

*Word for word:* nilaji haiyā — casting off shame; bali ye — I tell; sajani — friend; śuna he āmāra kathā — listen to my story; nikaruṇa bidhi — the pitiless Creator; gata dina — yesterday; more dileka dāruṇa byathā — gave me cruel pain

**19.1.** "Casting off shame, I'll tell you, friend — listen to my story:
the pitiless Creator yesterday gave me cruel pain.

অনেক দিনের পরেতে মাসৈস আইলা আমার বাড়ী ।
মনের উলাসে তার পাশে গিয়া বসিনু সকল ছাড়ি ॥

*aneka dinera parete māsaisa āilā āmāra bāṛī |*
*manera ulāse tāra pāśe giyā basinu sakala chāṛi ||*

*Word for word:* aneka dinera parete — after many days; māsaisa āilā — my husband's aunt came; āmāra bāṛī — to my house; manera ulāse — with joy in my heart; tāra pāśe giyā basinu — I sat beside her; sakala chāṛi — leaving everything

**19.2.** For the first time in many days my husband's aunt came to my house;
with joy in my heart I sat beside her, leaving everything.[^29-51]

হেনই সময়ে গৌর-নাগরের গমন শুনিতে পাইনু ।
দুয়ার-বাহিরে যাইবার লাগি অধিক আতুর হৈনু ॥

*henai samaye gaura-nāgarera gamana śunite pāinu |*
*duyāra-bāhire yāibāra lāgi adhika ātura hainu ||*

*Word for word:* henai samaye — just then; gaura-nāgarera gamana — that the nagara Gaura was passing; śunite pāinu — I heard; duyāra-bāhire yāibāra lāgi — to go out of the door; adhika ātura hainu — I was all eagerness

**19.3.** And just then I hear: the nagara Gaura is passing;
I was all eagerness to go out of the door.

যদি বা উঠিতে মনে করি, ওগো, সে পুনঃ মো-পানে চাঞা ।
আঁচরে ধরিয়া বসায় যতনে মাথার শপথ দিয়া ॥

*yadi bā uṭhite mane kari, ogo, se punaḥ mo-pāne cāñā |*
*ām̐care dhariyā basāya yatane māthāra śapatha diyā ||*

*Word for word:* yadi vā uṭhite mane kari — if I think of getting up; ogo — ah; se punaḥ mo-pāne cāñā — she looks at me again; ām̐care dhariyā — catching the end of my sari; basāya yatane — kindly sits me down; māthāra śapatha diyā — adjuring by her head

**19.4.** As soon as I think of getting up — ah! — she looks at me again,
catches the end of my sari and kindly sits me down, adjuring me by her head.

এ সব কিছু না বুঝিয়ে তাহার কপট-রহিত চিত ।
কত কত মতে যতন করিয়া পুছয়ে ঘরের রীত ॥

*e saba kichu nā bujhiye tāhāra kapaṭa-rahita cita |*
*kata kata mate yatana kariyā puchaye gharera rīta ||*

*Word for word:* e saba kichu nā bujhiye — understanding nothing of this; tāhāra kapaṭa-rahita cita — her heart free of guile; kata kata mate — in every way; yatana kariyā — with care; puchaye gharera rīta — asks about household matters

**19.5.** Understanding nothing of this, with a heart free of all guile,
she asks in every way, with care, about household matters.

মোর প্রাণ আনচান করে, তাহা শুনিয়া না শুনি কাণে ।
কি কথা কহিতে কিবা কহি, ভাল মন্দ না থাকয়ে মনে ॥

*mora prāṇa ānacāna kare, tāhā śuniyā nā śuni kāṇe |*
*ki kathā kahite kibā kahi, bhāla manda nā thākaye mane ||*

*Word for word:* mora prāṇa ānacāna kare — my soul is restless; tāhā śuniyā nā śuni kāṇe — I listen and do not hear; ki kathā kahite kibā kahi — what is asked, what I say; bhāla manda nā thākaye mane — good or bad, I do not remember

**19.6.** My soul is restless — I listen to her and do not hear;
what is asked, what I answer — good or bad, I do not remember.

সে করে পীরিতি যথোচিত, মোরে লাগয়ে বিষের প্রায় ।
বাহিরে প্রকাশ না করি সঙ্কোচে, অন্তর দহিয়া যায় ॥

*se kare pīriti yathocita, more lāgaye biṣera prāya |*
*bāhire prakāśa nā kari saṅkoce, antara dahiyā yāya ||*

*Word for word:* se kare pīriti yathocita — she is affectionate as is proper; more lāgaye biṣera prāya — to me it is like poison; bāhire prakāśa nā kari — I do not show it outwardly; saṅkoce — out of awkwardness; antara dahiyā yāya — inside I am burning

**19.7.** She is affectionate with me, as is proper, and to me it is like poison;
out of awkwardness I do not show it, but inside I am burning.

বিষম সঙ্কট জানি, মনে হেন, শরীর ছাড়িয়া দি ।
নরহরি কহে, না জান চাতুরী, মাসৈসে ভুলাতে কি ॥

*biṣama saṅkaṭa jāni, mane hena, śarīra chāṛiyā di |*
*narahari kahe, nā jāna cāturī, māsaise bhulāte ki ||*

*Word for word:* biṣama saṅkaṭa jāni — seeing a terrible fix; mane hena — I thought; śarīra chāṛiyā di — let me give up my body; narahari kahe — Narahari says; nā jāna cāturī — don't you know stratagems; māsaise bhulāte ki — how to fool the aunt

**19.8.** Seeing a terrible fix, I thought — let my body leave me!"
Narahari says: don't you know any stratagems — how to fool the aunt?[^29-52]

[^29-50]: Signature: "Narahari." GPT1 — pp. 191–192, no. 91 (scan PDF pp. 450–451); GPT2 — sect. 3.2 (the number is not recognized in the GPT2 OCR). The catalogue of
stage 1 did not have this line (**new line**: NG-335). GCC — kirana 7, pada 7 (pp. 69–70); GCC readings: "nilaji haiyā baliye sajani śunaha āmāra kathā",
"mo'pāne cāya", "māthāra śapatha diyā". B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^29-51]: "The husband's aunt" (māsaisa, māsaśāśa) — the mother-in-law's sister, come on a visit. The plot is an obstacle to darshana: the same convention
as in nos. 17–18 (the elders prevent the heroine from seeing the beloved).
[^29-52]: The ending is a playful remark by the poet: "don't you know stratagems to get round your aunt?" Cf. 17.8 and notes 47, 49.

## 20. Narahari — "śuna go sajani suradhunī-ghāṭa haite…" (GPT1 pp. 192–193, no. 92; GCC 7.8)
*Nagari-bhava. A townswoman's story: returning alone from the ghat of the Suradhuni, she met the Moon of Nadia on the road; at the sight of His face
she forgot composure and shame — the pot fell and broke; someone told her sister-in-law, who came running in fury; the young wife wept so that the
sister-in-law's anger passed, and invented a story: the sister-in-law's friends abuse her at every corner, and she herself, unable to bear it,
broke the pot in anger; the sister-in-law, pleased, comforted her. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 7, pada 8.*[^29-53]

শুন গো সজনি, সুরধুনী-ঘাট হইতে আসিয়ে একা ।
নদীয়া-চাঁদের সহিত আমার পথেতে হইল দেখা ॥

*śuna go sajani, suradhunī-ghāṭa haite āsiye ekā |*
*nadīyā-cām̐dera sahita āmāra pathete haila dekhā ||*

*Word for word:* śuna go sajani — listen, friend; suradhunī-ghāṭa haite — from the ghat of the Suradhuni; āsiye ekā — I was coming alone; nadīyā-cām̐dera sahita — with the Moon of Nadia; āmāra pathete haila dekhā — I met on the road

**20.1.** "Listen, friend: I was coming alone from the ghat of the Suradhuni —
and on the road I met the Moon of Nadia.

কিবা অপরূপ মাধুরী, মধুর গমন কুঞ্জর জিনি ।
না জানিয়ে কেবা গড়িল কিরূপে পীরিতি-মূরতিখানি ॥

*kibā aparūpa mādhurī, madhura gamana kuñjara jini |*
*nā jāniye kebā gaṛila kirūpe pīriti-mūratikhāni ||*

*Word for word:* kibā aparūpa mādhurī — what wondrous sweetness; madhura gamana — a lovely gait; kuñjara jini — surpassing an elephant; nā jāniye — I do not know; kebā gaṛila kirūpe — who made, and how; pīriti-mūratikhāni — this image of love embodied

**20.2.** What wondrous sweetness! His gait is lovelier than an elephant's;
I do not know who made this image of love embodied, and how.

উপমা কি দিব, মনে হেন, নব বেশের সহিতে গোরা ।
হিয়ার মাঝারে রাখিয়ে অথবা করিয়ে আঁখির তারা ॥

*upamā ki diba, mane hena, naba beśera sahite gorā |*
*hiyāra mājhāre rākhiye athabā kariye ām̐khira tārā ||*

*Word for word:* upamā ki diba — what comparison shall I give; mane hena — I long; naba beśera sahite gorā — Gora in His new attire; hiyāra mājhāre rākhiye — to keep in my heart; athabā kariye ām̐khira tārā — or to make the pupil of my eyes

**20.3.** To what shall I compare Him? I long to take Gora in His new attire
and either hide Him in my heart or make Him the pupil of my eyes.

ও মুখ হেরিতে ধৈরজ ধরম সরম রহিল দূর ।
কাঁখের কলসি ভূমিতে পড়িয়া হইল শতেক চূর ॥

*o mukha herite dhairaja dharama sarama rahila dūra |*
*kām̐khera kalasi bhūmite paṛiyā haila śateka cūra ||*

*Word for word:* o mukha herite — looking at that face; dhairaja dharama sarama — composure, dharma, shame; rahila dūra — went far away; kām̐khera kalasi — the pot on my hip; bhūmite paṛiyā — falling to the ground; haila śateka cūra — broke into a hundred pieces

**20.4.** As I looked at that face, composure, dharma and shame went far away;
the pot fell from my hip to the ground and broke into a hundred pieces.[^29-54]

কি করিব, প্রাণ-পিয়ারে জীবন যৌবন সঁপিয়া সুখে ।
গুরুজন-ভয়ে ঘরেতে আসিয়ে বসিনু মনের দুখে ॥

*ki kariba, prāṇa-piyāre jībana yaubana sam̐piyā sukhe |*
*gurujana-bhaye gharete āsiye basinu manera dukhe ||*

*Word for word:* ki kariba — what could I do; prāṇa-piyāre — to the Beloved of my soul; jībana yaubana — life and youth; sam̐piyā sukhe — giving gladly; gurujana-bhaye — in fear of the elders; gharete āsiye — coming home; basinu manera dukhe — I sat with grief in my heart

**20.5.** What could I do? — having given my life and youth gladly to the Beloved of my soul,
in fear of the elders I came home and sat with grief in my heart.

কলসি-ভঞ্জন-কথা না জানি কে ননদে কহিয়া দিল ।
দাবানল-সম বিষম কোরধ-আবেশে ধাইয়া আইল ॥

*kalasi-bhañjana-kathā nā jāni ke nanade kahiyā dila |*
*dābānala-sama biṣama koradha-ābeśe dhāiyā āila ||*

*Word for word:* kalasi-bhañjana-kathā — the story of the broken pot; nā jāni ke — I do not know who; nanade kahiyā dila — told my sister-in-law; dābānala-sama — like a forest fire; biṣama koradha-ābeśe — in terrible anger; dhāiyā āila — she came rushing

**20.6.** I do not know who told my sister-in-law that the pot was broken;
in terrible anger, like a forest fire, she came rushing.

কিছু ছল নাহি চলয়ে তাহার বিকট স্বরূপ দেখি ।
দুটি হাত মাথে ধরিয়া অধিক কান্দিয়া ফুলানু আঁখি ॥

*kichu chala nāhi calaye tāhāra bikaṭa svarūpa dekhi |*
*duṭi hāta māthe dhariyā adhika kāndiyā phulānu ām̐khi ||*

*Word for word:* kichu chala nāhi calaye — no trick works; tāhāra bikaṭa svarūpa dekhi — seeing her fearsome look; duṭi hāta māthe dhariyā — clutching my head with both hands; adhika kāndiyā — weeping much; phulānu ām̐khi — I made my eyes swell

**20.7.** No trick would work, seeing her fearsome look —
I clutched my head with both hands and wept till my eyes were swollen.

বিপরীত মোর কান্দন নিরখি তাহার কোরধ গেল ।
স্থির হৈয়া পুনঃ পুছে বারে বারে, তাহে না উত্তর দিল ॥

*biparīta mora kāndana nirakhi tāhāra koradha gela |*
*sthira haiyā punaḥ puche bāre bāre, tāhe nā uttara dila ||*

*Word for word:* biparīta mora kāndana nirakhi — seeing my immoderate weeping; tāhāra koradha gela — her anger passed; sthira haiyā — growing calm; punaḥ puche bāre bāre — she asks again and again; tāhe nā uttara dila — no answer was given

**20.8.** Seeing my immoderate weeping, she let go of her anger;
calming down, she asks again and again — I gave no answer.

খানিক থাকিয়া মনেতে বিচার করিয়া ধরিয়া করে ।
ধীরে ধীরে কহে, কিসের লাগিয়া না বোল মরম মোরে ॥

*khānika thākiyā manete bicāra kariyā dhariyā kare |*
*dhīre dhīre kahe, kisera lāgiyā nā bola marama more ||*

*Word for word:* khānika thākiyā — after a little while; manete bicāra kariyā — thinking it over; dhariyā kare — taking my hand; dhīre dhīre kahe — says softly, softly; kisera lāgiyā — why; nā bola marama more — you do not tell me your heart

**20.9.** After a little while, having thought it over, she took my hand
and says softly, softly: 'Why don't you open your heart to me?'

অনেক যতনে গদগদ ভাষে তা-সনে কহিনু কথা ।
মনের দুখেতে কান্দিয়া, এ সব কি লাগি পুছহ বৃথা ॥

*aneka yatane gadagada bhāṣe tā-sane kahinu kathā |*
*manera dukhete kāndiyā, e saba ki lāgi puchaha bṛthā ||*

*Word for word:* aneka yatane — with great difficulty; gadagada bhāṣe — in a faltering voice; tā-sane kahinu kathā — I spoke to her; manera dukhete kāndiyā — weeping with grief in my heart; e saba ki lāgi — why all this; puchaha bṛthā — do you ask in vain

**20.10.** With difficulty, in a faltering voice, I told her,
weeping, with grief in my heart: 'Why do you ask in vain?[^29-55]

যা-সবারে তুমি প্রাণ-সম জান, সে করে দারুণ কাজ ।
ঘাটে মাঠে পথে নিন্দয়ে তোমারে, শুনিয়া পাইয়ে লাজ ॥

*yā-sabāre tumi prāṇa-sama jāna, se kare dāruṇa kāja |*
*ghāṭe māṭhe pathe nindaye tomāre, śuniyā pāiye lāja ||*

*Word for word:* yā-sabāre tumi prāṇa-sama jāna — those whom you hold dear as life; se kare dāruṇa kāja — they do terrible things; ghāṭe māṭhe pathe — at the ghat, in the field, on the road; nindaye tomāre — they slander you; śuniyā pāiye lāja — I was ashamed to hear

**20.11.** Those whom you hold dear as life do terrible things:
at the ghat, in the field, on the road they slander you — I was ashamed to hear it.

মনে করি, গলে কলসি বাঁধিয়া পশিব গঙ্গার জলে ।
তাহা না করিতে পারিয়ে, পাছে বা কলঙ্ক রটয়ে কুলে ॥

*mane kari, gale kalasi bām̐dhiyā paśiba gaṅgāra jale |*
*tāhā nā karite pāriye, pāche bā kalaṅka raṭaye kule ||*

*Word for word:* mane kari — I thought; gale kalasi bām̐dhiyā — tying the pot to my neck; paśiba gaṅgāra jale — I would enter the Ganga; tāhā nā karite pāriye — I could not do it; pāche vā kalaṅka raṭaye kule — lest an ill name spread about the family

**20.12.** I thought of tying the pot to my neck and throwing myself into the Ganga,
but could not — lest an ill name should spread about the family.

কি করিব আমি, তা-সবার সনে করিতে নারিয়ে দ্বন্দ্ব ।
যত অপযশ পাইল সে সব শুনিয়া হইনু ধন্দ ॥

*ki kariba āmi, tā-sabāra sane karite nāriye dvandva |*
*yata apayaśa pāila se saba śuniyā hainu dhanda ||*

*Word for word:* ki kariba āmi — what could I do; tā-sabāra sane — with them; karite nāriye dvandva — I cannot quarrel; yata apayaśa pāila — all the ill repute you have got; se saba śuniyā — hearing it all; hainu dhanda — I was bewildered

**20.13.** What could I do? I cannot quarrel with them;
all the ill they say of you — I heard it and was bewildered.

কাহারে করিব সাথী, সেথা কেহ না ছিল আমার সাথে ।
তা-সবার প্রতি কোরধ করিয়া কলসি ভাঙ্গিনু পথে ॥

*kāhāre kariba sāthī, sethā keha nā chila āmāra sāthe |*
*tā-sabāra prati koradha kariyā kalasi bhāṅginu pathe ||*

*Word for word:* kāhāre kariba sāthī — whom could I make a witness; sethā keha nā chila āmāra sāthe — no one was with me there; tā-sabāra prati — at them; koradha kariyā — in anger; kalasi bhāṅginu pathe — I broke the pot on the road

**20.14.** Whom could I call as a witness? No one was with me there;
in anger at them I broke the pot on the road.'

এত শুনি চিতে হরষিত অতি পীরিতি করিয়া মোরে ।
কত কত মতে বুঝাইয়া মুখ মুছিল আপন করে ॥

*eta śuni cite haraṣita ati pīriti kariyā more |*
*kata kata mate bujhāiyā mukha muchila āpana kare ||*

*Word for word:* eta śuni — hearing this; cite haraṣita ati — greatly delighted at heart; pīriti kariyā more — caressing me; kata kata mate bujhāiyā — comforting me in every way; mukha muchila āpana kare — wiped my face with her own hand

**20.15.** Hearing this, she was overjoyed, caressed me,
comforted me in every way and wiped my face with her own hand.

এইরূপে কালি বিষম সঙ্কট এড়ানু সাহস করি ।
নরহরি কহে, তুয়া চাতুরীর বালাই লইয়া মরি ॥

*eirūpe kāli biṣama saṅkaṭa eṛānu sāhasa kari |*
*narahari kahe, tuyā cāturīra bālāi laiyā mari ||*

*Word for word:* eirūpe — thus; kāli — yesterday; biṣama saṅkaṭa eṛānu — I escaped a terrible fix; sāhasa kari — boldly; narahari kahe — Narahari says; tuyā cāturīra — of your cleverness; bālāi laiyā mari — I take upon myself the ills

**20.16.** So yesterday I boldly escaped a terrible fix."
Narahari says: I take upon myself all the ills of your cleverness![^29-56]

[^29-53]: Signature: "Narahari." GPT1 — pp. 192–193, no. 92 (scan PDF pp. 451–452); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 92 (catalogue: NG-085). GCC — kirana 7, pada 8 (pp. 70–71); GCC
readings: "dhīre dhīre kahe kisera lāgiyā nā kaha marama more", "śuniyā pāiye lāja", "paśiye gaṅgāra jale", "mukha mochāla āpana kare". B.
Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^29-54]: "Broke into a hundred pieces" — the motif of the broken pot (cf. nos. 8, 12 and note 27). "Composure, dharma and shame went away" — see note 28.
[^29-55]: After 20.10 GPT1 (p. 192, at the bottom) has an extra half-line "ki karili taila phelāli, balaye śāśuṛī" ("'What have you done — you've spilt the
oil!' says the mother-in-law"), which is not in GCC and does not fit the story (it is the sister-in-law who speaks); probably an insertion or a
printer's error. It is not included in the translation.
[^29-56]: "I take upon myself all the ills" (bālāi laiyā mari) is a formula of admiration (cf. note 43): the poet delights in the heroine's resourcefulness.
The invented story about the sister-in-law's friends is the same convention of "stratagems" (note 47).

## 21. Narahari — "ki kaba sajani nanadera kathā…" (GPT1 pp. 193–194, no. 93; GCC 7.9)
*Nagari-bhava. A townswoman's story: her sister-in-law, who thought herself the only faithful wife in Nadia and would not let her speak to anyone,
yesterday went for water herself and on the road to the ghat saw Gora with His companions — and lost all composure: the pot fell, her hair came
loose, her clothes slipped; coming to herself, she in embarrassment begged her brother's wife to keep the secret and promised to help her in
everything; "I did not spread it — a noble person guards another's shame." Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 7,
pada 9.*[^29-57]

কি কব সজনি ননদের কথা, কহিতে উপজে হাসি ।
তেঁহ পতিব্রতা, তার লেখে সব অসতী নদীয়াবাসী ॥

*ki kaba sajani nanadera kathā, kahite upaje hāsi |*
*tem̐ha patibratā, tāra lekhe saba asatī nadīyābāsī ||*

*Word for word:* ki kaba sajani — what shall I say, friend; nanadera kathā — of my sister-in-law; kahite upaje hāsi — it is laughable to tell; teṃha patibratā — she is a faithful wife; tāra lekhe — by her reckoning; saba asatī nadīyābāsī — all the women of Nadia are unfaithful

**21.1.** "What shall I say of my sister-in-law, friend? — it is laughable to tell:
she is a faithful wife, and all the women of Nadia, by her reckoning, are unfaithful.

আর বিপরীত, কারু সনে কথা কহিতে না দেয় মোরে ।
সতত তর্জন করে, একা কোথা যাইতে নারিয়ে ডরে ॥

*āra biparīta, kāru sane kathā kahite nā deya more |*
*satata tarjana kare, ekā kothā yāite nāriye ḍare ||*

*Word for word:* āra biparīta — and worse; kāru sane kathā kahite — to speak with anyone; nā deya more — she does not let me; satata tarjana kare — she is forever scolding; ekā kothā yāite nāriye ḍare — I dare not go anywhere alone for fear

**21.2.** And worse: she will not let me say a word to anyone,
she is forever scolding — I dare not go anywhere alone for fear.

মনোদুখে দিন রজনী মরিয়ে শুনিয়া নিন্দন-ভাষ ।
বিধি-প্রতি করি প্রার্থনা, ইহার দরপ হউক নাশ ॥

*manodukhe dina rajanī mariye śuniyā nindana-bhāṣa |*
*bidhi-prati kari prārthanā, ihāra darapa hauka nāśa ||*

*Word for word:* manodukhe — with grief in my heart; dina rajanī mariye — day and night I was dying; śuniyā nindana-bhāṣa — hearing her abuse; bidhi-prati kari prārthanā — I prayed to the Creator; ihāra darapa hauka nāśa — let her pride be destroyed

**21.3.** With grief in my heart, day and night, I was dying, hearing her abuse;
I prayed to the Creator: let her pride be destroyed.

না জানিয়ে কোন গুণে নিবেদন শুনিল সদয় বিধি ।
মনেতে করিনু যাহা, তাহা যেন তুরিতে হইল সিধি ॥

*nā jāniye kona guṇe nibedana śunila sadaya bidhi |*
*manete karinu yāhā, tāhā yena turite haila sidhi ||*

*Word for word:* nā jāniye — I do not know; kona guṇe — for what merit; nibedana śunila — heard my plea; sadaya bidhi — the merciful Creator; manete karinu yāhā — what I had in mind; tāhā yena turite haila sidhi — that soon came true

**21.4.** I do not know for what merit the merciful Creator heard my plea:
what I had in mind soon came true.

শুন গো সে কথা, গত দিন তেঁহ চলিলা কলসি লঞা ।
তার পাছে পাছে চলিনু মো পুনি তার অনুমতি পাঞা ॥

*śuna go se kathā, gata dina tem̐ha calilā kalasi lañā |*
*tāra pāche pāche calinu mo puni tāra anumati pāñā ||*

*Word for word:* śuna go se kathā — listen to how it was; gata dina — yesterday; teṃha calilā kalasi lañā — she went, taking her pot; tāra pāche pāche calinu mo puni — and I followed behind her; tāra anumati pāñā — with her leave

**21.5.** Listen to how it was: yesterday she went off, taking her pot;
and I followed behind her, with her leave.

সুরধুনী-ঘাট যাইতে আমরা দুজনে যাই যে পথে ।
সেই পথে গোরা দাঁড়াঞা আছেন প্রিয়-পারিষদ-সাথে ॥

*suradhunī-ghāṭa yāite āmarā dujane yāi ye pathe |*
*sei pathe gorā dām̐ṛāñā āchena priya-pāriṣada-sāthe ||*

*Word for word:* suradhunī-ghāṭa yāite — going to the ghat of the Suradhuni; āmarā dujane yāi ye pathe — by the road we both go; sei pathe — on that road; gorā dām̐ṛāñā āchena — Gora is standing; priya-pāriṣada-sāthe — with His dear companions

**21.6.** On the road by which we both go to the ghat of the Suradhuni,
on that very road Gora stands with His dear companions.

ও-রূপ-মাধুরী হেরিয়া ননদী ধৈরজ ধরিতে নারে ।
হইল বিষম থরহরি তনু, কাঁপয়ে মদন-ভরে ॥

*o-rūpa-mādhurī heriyā nanadī dhairaja dharite nāre |*
*haila biṣama tharahari tanu, kām̐paye madana-bhare ||*

*Word for word:* o-rūpa-mādhurī heriyā — seeing the sweetness of that form; nanadī — my sister-in-law; dhairaja dharite nāre — cannot keep her composure; haila biṣama tharahari tanu — her body began to shake violently; kām̐paye madana-bhare — she trembles under Madana's onslaught

**21.7.** Seeing the sweetness of that form, my sister-in-law could not keep her composure:
she began to shake all over, trembling under Madana's onslaught.[^29-58]

কাঁখের কলস ভূমেতে পড়িল, আউলাইল মাথার কেশ ।
অঙ্গের বসন খসে অনায়াসে, স্মৃতির নাহিক লেশ ॥

*kām̐khera kalasa bhūmete paṛila, āulāila māthāra keśa |*
*aṅgera basana khase anāyāse, smṛtira nāhika leśa ||*

*Word for word:* kām̐khera kalasa — the pot on her hip; bhūmete paṛila — fell to the ground; āulāila māthāra keśa — her hair came loose; aṅgera basana khase anāyāse — her clothes slip from her body of themselves; smṛtira nāhika leśa — there is not a trace of memory

**21.8.** The pot fell from her hip to the ground, her hair came loose,
her clothes slip from her body of themselves — and there is not a trace of memory.

কতেক যতনে ধৈরজ ধরিল অধিক লজ্জিত হঞা ।
দুই করে ধরি ধীরে ধীরে কহে মোর মুখ-পানে চাঞা ॥

*kateka yatane dhairaja dharila adhika lajjita hañā |*
*dui kare dhari dhīre dhīre kahe mora mukha-pāne cāñā ||*

*Word for word:* kateka yatane — with difficulty; dhairaja dharila — she regained her composure; adhika lajjita hañā — greatly embarrassed; dui kare dhari — taking both my hands; dhīre dhīre kahe — says softly, softly; mora mukha-pāne cāñā — looking into my face

**21.9.** With difficulty she regained her composure, greatly embarrassed,
took me by both hands and says softly, softly, looking into my face:

নিশ্চয় জানিহ, গুণবতী বধূ, পরাণ-অধিক তুমি ।
কহিয়াছি কত, দোষ না লইবে, তোমার অধীন আমি ॥

*niścaya jāniha, guṇabatī badhū, parāṇa-adhika tumi |*
*kahiyāchi kata, doṣa nā laibe, tomāra adhīna āmi ||*

*Word for word:* niścaya jāniha — know for certain; guṇabatī badhū — virtuous brother's wife; parāṇa-adhika tumi — you are dearer than life; kahiyāchi kata — all I have said; doṣa nā laibe — do not hold it against me; tomāra adhīna āmi — I am in your power

**21.10.** 'Know for certain: you, my virtuous brother's wife, are dearer to me than life;
all I have said to you — do not hold it against me; I am in your power.

যখন যে কাজ কর, তাহা মোরে কবে নিঃসঙ্কোচ হঞা ।
প্রাণধন দিয়া সহায় করিব, বলয়ে শপথ খাঞা ॥

*yakhana ye kāja kara, tāhā more kabe niḥsaṅkoca hañā |*
*prāṇadhana diyā sahāya kariba, balaye śapatha khāñā ||*

*Word for word:* yakhana ye kāja kara — whatever you do; tāhā more kabe — tell me; niḥsaṅkoca hañā — without embarrassment; prāṇadhana diyā — even at the cost of my life; sahāya kariba — I will help; balaye śapatha khāñā — she says, swearing

**21.11.** Whatever you do — tell me without embarrassment;
I will help you, even at the cost of my life,' she swears.

আনে না কহিও সে সব কাহিনী, রাখিহ গোপন করি ।
ঠেকিনু এ রসে, কি কব, পাগলী করিলে গৌরহরি ॥

*āne nā kahio se saba kāhinī, rākhiha gopana kari |*
*ṭhekinu e rase, ki kaba, pāgalī karile gaurahari ||*

*Word for word:* āne nā kahio — tell no one; se saba kāhinī — all this; rākhiha gopana kari — keep it secret; ṭhekinu e rase — I have fallen into this rasa; ki kaba — what can I say; pāgalī karile gaurahari — Gaurahari has driven me mad

**21.12.** 'Only tell no one about this, keep it secret;
I have fallen into this rasa — what can I say? — Gaurahari has driven me mad!'

এইরূপ বহু কহিল, শুনিয়া বাড়িল অশেষ সুখ ।
পুরবের কথা বিচার করিতে উঠিল অনেক দুখ ॥

*eirūpa bahu kahila, śuniyā bāṛila aśeṣa sukha |*
*purabera kathā bicāra karite uṭhila aneka dukha ||*

*Word for word:* eirūpa bahu kahila — thus she said much; śuniyā bāṛila aśeṣa sukha — hearing it, my joy grew endlessly; purabera kathā bicāra karite — recalling what had gone before; uṭhila aneka dukha — much bitterness rose

**21.13.** Thus she said much — hearing it, my joy knew no bounds,
and remembering what had gone before, much bitterness rose in me.

মনেতে হইল, এ সকল কথা বেকত করিলে কাজ ।
নরহরি কহে, সাধু-রীতি যার, সে রাখে পরের লাজ ॥

*manete haila, e sakala kathā bekata karile kāja |*
*narahari kahe, sādhu-rīti yāra, se rākhe parera lāja ||*

*Word for word:* manete haila — I thought; e sakala kathā — all this; bekata karile kāja — what use in revealing; narahari kahe — Narahari says; sādhu-rīti yāra — one whose ways are noble; se rākhe parera lāja — guards another's shame

**21.14.** I thought: what is the use of spreading all this?"
Narahari says: one whose conduct is noble guards another's shame.[^29-59]

[^29-57]: Signature: "Narahari." GPT1 — pp. 193–194, no. 93 (scan PDF pp. 452–453); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 93 (catalogue: NG-086; "nadera" for "nanadera"). GCC — kirana 7,
pada 9 (pp. 71–72); GCC readings: "teṃha patibratā" (so also GPT1), "haila biṣama tharahari tanu" (GPT1 "narahari tanu" — a printer's error: a signature
is out of place here), "prāṇadhana diyā sahāya kariba balaye śapatha khā'yā". B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^29-58]: "Madana's onslaught" (madana-bhare) — attraction, of which the original speaks directly; translated precisely. 21.7–21.8 are signs of being
overwhelmed (trembling, the falling pot, loosened hair, slipping clothes, oblivion), usual in the padas about the gopis at the sight of Krishna
(cf. *Bhag.* 10.29 and note 79 of chapter 28). The tradition does not accept the image of Gaura as nagara (introductory note, chapter 27); the Lord
Himself here only stands with His companions by the road.
[^29-59]: The ending is a moral maxim of the poet: a noble person does not divulge another's disgrace. The translation is faithful to the author.

## Summary of chapter 29

*The chapter opens the nagari padas signed "Narahari" from section 3.2 of GPT. Before translating, section 3.2 of GPT1 (pp. 157–237, 180 padas) was
read through on the scan: 95 padas bear Narahari's signature, of which 32 were not in the catalogue (new lines NG-334…365); the witness of almost
all the long padas of this series is Narahari Chakravarti's *Gaura-charita-chintamani*, kiranas 7–11 ("the nagaris of Navadvipa"), which confirms
Majumdar's argument: the long padas of GPT with this signature are not Sarakara's. Translated: the cycle of the *Bhakti-ratnakara* (12th wave) —
the speeches of the "anuragavatis", the women of Nadia, by the tree on the bank of the Ganga (nos. 1–7: five padas of Yadunandana, a pada of Yadu
and a pada of Narahari Chakravarti; in them the townswomen see Gaura in the bhava of Krishna calling Radha and recognize in Him "the Moon of
Gokula"); the short padas of GPT1 3.2 nos. 39–45 in simple Bengali, which the GPT2 index assigns to Sarakara (nos. 8–13; "probably Sarakara" — C,
no. 43 — "not established"); the beginning of the 7th kirana of GCC — the townswomen's morning conversations and their stories of how, deceiving
their elders, they saw Gaura (nos. 14–21; "probably Chakravarti" — B). The padas of other poets of the section (nos. 49–60, Govinda Dasa, Jnanadasa)
were not translated; Lochana Dasa's padas (nos. 61–85, 116) are translated in chapters 28 and 34.*

---

# Chapter 30. Nagari Padas — IV: the "Narahari" padas of GPT (sect. 3.2, nos. 94–110, 120–123)

*On what nagari-bhava is, the position of the tradition (Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja, Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati) and the rules of translation, see the introductory note to the section of nagari padas in chapter 27; on the two poets named Narahari (Narahari Sarakara and Narahari Chakravarti) and on the attribution labels ("probably Sarakara", "probably Chakravarti", "not established"), see the introductory note to the "Narahari" appendix in chapter 17.*

## 1. Narahari — "śuna śuna ago parāṇa soi…" (GPT1 p. 194, no. 94; GCC 7.10)
*Nagari-bhava. A townswoman complains to her friend about her household: whenever she sighs and murmurs "Gora", her mother-in-law burns with
anger, her sister-in-law is like poison, the neighbours taunt her day and night, she lives like a bird in a cage; but yesterday the Creator took
pity — at the close of day Gaura passed along their street, and she secretly saw Him from the window: His face, brows, eyes, garland, gait; and
the pain of her heart only doubled. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 7, pada 10.*[^30-1]

শুন শুন অগো পরাণ সোই । বেথিত জানিয়া তোমারে কই ॥

*śuna śuna ago parāṇa soi | bethita jāniyā tomāre kai ||*

*Word for word:* śuna śuna ago — listen, listen; parāṇa soi — friend of my heart; bethita jāniyā — knowing you feel my pain; tomāre kai — I tell you

**1.1.** Listen, listen, friend of my heart: I know you feel my pain — so to you I will tell it.

দেশের বাহির ঘরের রীত । সে কথা কহিতে কাঁদয়ে চিত ॥

*deśera bāhira gharera rīta | se kathā kahite kām̐daye cita ||*

*Word for word:* deśera bāhira — beyond the custom of the land, unheard of; gharera rīta — the ways of the house; se kathā kahite — telling of it; kām̐daye cita — the heart weeps

**1.2.** The ways of our house are unheard of in the land: as I tell them, my heart weeps.

গোরা বলি যদি নিশ্বাস ছাড়ি । শুনিয়া কোরধে জ্বলয়ে বুড়ী ॥

*gorā bali yadi niśvāsa chāṛi | śuniyā koradhe jvalaye buṛī ||*

*Word for word:* gorā bali — saying "Gora"; yadi niśvāsa chāṛi — if I sigh; śuniyā — hearing; koradhe jvalaye — burns with anger; buṛī — the old woman (mother-in-law)

**1.3.** If only I sigh, murmuring "Gora", the old woman hears and burns with anger.

ননদী বিষম বিষের প্রায় । তার গুণে প্রাণ দহিয়া যায় ॥

*nanadī biṣama biṣera prāya | tāra guṇe prāṇa dahiyā yāya ||*

*Word for word:* nanadī — sister-in-law; biṣama biṣera prāya — like deadly poison; tāra guṇe — through her "virtues"; prāṇa dahiyā yāya — life burns away

**1.4.** My sister-in-law is like deadly poison: through her "virtues" my life is burnt away.

পড়সি কেবল কুলের কাঁটা । দিবস রজনী দেয় যে খোঁটা ॥

*paṛasi kebala kulera kām̐ṭā | dibasa rajanī deya ye khom̐ṭā ||*

*Word for word:* paṛasi — the neighbours; kebala — nothing but; kulera kām̐ṭā — thorns to the family's good name; dibasa rajanī — day and night; deya ye khom̐ṭā — they taunt

**1.5.** The neighbours are nothing but thorns to a good name: day and night they prick me with taunts.

কারে দিব অগো ইহার সাখী । ঘরে থাকি যেন পিঞ্জরে পাখী ॥

*kāre diba ago ihāra sākhī | ghare thāki yena piñjare pākhī ||*

*Word for word:* kāre diba ago — whom, friend, shall I give; ihāra sākhī — as witness to this; ghare thāki — I stay at home; yena piñjare pākhī — like a bird in a cage

**1.6.** Whom, friend, shall I call to witness this? I stay at home like a bird in a cage.

সে সব কাহিনী কি কব আর । কহিতে দুখের নাহিক পার ॥

*se saba kāhinī ki kaba āra | kahite dukhera nāhika pāra ||*

*Word for word:* se saba kāhinī — all those tales; ki kaba āra — what more shall I say; kahite — in the telling; dukhera nāhika pāra — there is no end to sorrow

**1.7.** What more shall I tell of all this? There is no end to my sorrow.

গতদিন বিধি সদয় মোরে । আকাশের চাঁদ দিলেক করে ॥

*gatadina bidhi sadaya more | ākāśera cām̐da dileka kare ||*

*Word for word:* gatadina — yesterday; bidhi sadaya more — the Creator was kind to me; ākāśera cām̐da — the moon of the sky; dileka kare — gave into my hand

**1.8.** But yesterday the Creator was kind to me — he put the moon of the sky into my hand.

দিবা অবসানে গৌররায় । আমাদের পথে চলিয়া যায় ॥

*dibā abasāne gaurarāya | āmādera pathe caliyā yāya ||*

*Word for word:* dibā abasāne — at the close of day; gaurarāya — Gaura Raya; āmādera pathe — along our street; caliyā yāya — goes walking

**1.9.** At the close of day Gaura Raya was walking along our street.

তরাতরি গিয়া গবাক্ষদ্বারে । অলখিত হৈয়া দেখিনু তারে ॥

*tarātari giyā gabākṣadvāre | alakhita haiyā dekhinu tāre ||*

*Word for word:* tarātari giyā — going in haste; gabākṣa-dvāre — to the window; alakhita haiyā — unseen; dekhinu tāre — I saw Him

**1.10.** Hurrying to the window, unseen, I saw Him.

কিবা সে মধুর বদনচাঁদ । তরুণীগণের হৃদয়ফাঁদ ॥

*kibā se madhura badanacām̐da | taruṇīgaṇera hṛdayaphām̐da ||*

*Word for word:* kibā se madhura — how sweet is that; badana-cām̐da — moon of a face; taruṇī-gaṇera — of young women; hṛdaya-phām̐da — a snare for hearts

**1.11.** How sweet is that moon of a face — a snare for the hearts of young women!

ভুরুযুগ বড় ভঙ্গিম ছাঁদে । কে আছে এমন ধৈরজ বাঁধে ॥

*bhuruyuga baṛa bhaṅgima chām̐de | ke āche emana dhairaja bām̐dhe ||*

*Word for word:* bhuruyuga — the pair of brows; baṛa bhaṅgima chām̐de — so gracefully curved; ke āche emana — who is there who; dhairaja bām̐dhe — can hold his composure

**1.12.** The curve of His brows is so graceful — who has the composure to bear it?

খঞ্জন জিনিয়া নয়ান নাচে । বুঝিনু তাহাতে কেহ না বাঁচে ॥

*khañjana jiniyā nayāna nāce | bujhinu tāhāte keha nā bām̐ce ||*

*Word for word:* khañjana jiniyā — outdoing wagtails; nayāna nāce — the eyes dance; bujhinu — I understood; tāhāte keha nā bām̐ce — from them no one escapes

**1.13.** His eyes, outdoing wagtails, dance — I understood: from them no one escapes.

গলায় দোলয়ে কুসুমদাম । তা হেরি মূরছে কতেক কাম ॥

*galāya dolaye kusumadāma | tā heri mūrache kateka kāma ||*

*Word for word:* galāya dolaye — sways at the throat; kusuma-dāma — a garland of flowers; tā heri — seeing it; mūrache kateka kāma — many a Kamadeva swoons

**1.14.** A garland of flowers sways at His throat — seeing it, many a Kamadeva swoons.[^30-2]

শোভা অপরূপ কি কব আর । ভুবনমোহন গমন তার ॥

*śobhā aparūpa ki kaba āra | bhubanamohana gamana tāra ||*

*Word for word:* śobhā aparūpa — wondrous beauty; ki kaba āra — what more shall I say; bhubana-mohana — enchanting the world; gamana tāra — His gait

**1.15.** What more shall I say of that wondrous beauty? His gait enchants the world.

তিলেক দেখিতে পাইনু সেথা । বাড়িল দ্বিগুণ হিয়ার ব্যথা ॥

*tileka dekhite pāinu sethā | bāṛila dviguṇa hiyāra byathā ||*

*Word for word:* tileka — for a moment; dekhite pāinu sethā — I could see Him there; bāṛila dviguṇa — grew twofold; hiyāra byathā — the pain of the heart

**1.16.** For only a moment could I see Him there — and the pain of my heart grew twofold.

নরহরি কহে দুখ না রবে । মনের মতন সকলি হবে ॥

*narahari kahe dukha nā rabe | manera matana sakali habe ||*

*Word for word:* narahari kahe — Narahari says; dukha nā rabe — sorrow will not remain; manera matana — as the heart wishes; sakali habe — all will come to pass

**1.17.** Narahari says: sorrow will not remain — all will come to pass as your heart desires.[^30-3]

[^30-1]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — p. 194, no. 94 (scan PDF p. 453); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 94 (catalogue: NG-336). GCC — kirana 7, pada 10 (ed. 1947,
p. 73; scan PDF p. 78). Nos. 94–99 of this chapter continue the 7th kirana of GCC — the townswomen of Navadvipa telling their friends in the morning
(beginning — chapter 29, nos. 14–21): GCC 7.10–7.12 = nos. 94–96, 7.14–7.16 = nos. 97–99; GCC 7.13 (how a townswoman remembered Gaura while cooking)
was not taken into GPT. GCC pp. 73–80 were checked against the scan (PDF pp. 78–85; re-OCRed with tesseract); pp. 81–88 (GCC 7.17–7.28) are missing
from the only available scan (see n. 18). GCC readings: "parāṇa sai" (so also GPT2), "deya e khom̐ṭā", "bhuruyuga bara bhaṅgima chānde". Metre — short payar (a couplet to a
line). B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^30-2]: "Many a Kamadeva swoons" (mūrache kateka kāma) — the usual praise in the padas of the Lord's beauty, surpassing that of the god of love
(cf. Krishna's name Madana-mohana, "He who enchants Madana himself").
[^30-3]: The poet's consolation is a convention of the purvaraga padas; in the GCC padas the fulfilment of the wish is a darshan of Gaura seen from
afar (cf. nos. 2–3 and 5).

## 2. Narahari — "ki baliba ago gharera kathā…" (GPT1 pp. 195–196, no. 95; GCC 7.11)
*Nagari-bhava. A townswoman's story: yesterday morning her mother-in-law went out, leaving her with her sister-in-law; the latter picked a quarrel
and went off in a huff to the neighbours; alone at the window, the townswoman saw Gaura passing and threw Him a withered kumuda bud; Gora, taking
it, said to the flower: "Do not grieve — the moon will rise"; at His glance she lost all strength; to her mother-in-law, on her return, she
complained of her sister-in-law and explained her agitation by fatigue and fear — and the mother-in-law comforted her and scolded the
sister-in-law. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 7, pada 11.*[^30-4]

কি বলিব অগো ঘরের কথা । সে সব শুনিলে পাইবে বেথা ॥

*ki baliba ago gharera kathā | se saba śunile pāibe bethā ||*

*Word for word:* ki baliba ago — what shall I say, friend; gharera kathā — of the house; se saba śunile — if you hear it all; pāibe bethā — you will feel pain

**2.1.** "What shall I say, friend, of what goes on in our house? If you hear it, it will pain you too.

কালি সুপ্রভাত হইল নিশি । বিরলে দেখিনু গৌরশশী ॥

*kāli suprabhāta haila niśi | birale dekhinu gauraśaśī ||*

*Word for word:* kāli — yesterday; suprabhāta haila niśi — the night became a bright morning; birale — in secret; dekhinu — I saw; gaura-śaśī — the Moon Gaura

**2.2.** Yesterday, as soon as night gave way to a bright morning, I secretly saw the Moon Gaura.

মরুক এখন লাজে কি করে । সে কাহিনী কিছু কহি তোমারে ॥

*maruka ekhana lāje ki kare | se kāhinī kichu kahi tomāre ||*

*Word for word:* maruka ekhana — let it perish now; lāje ki kare — what can shame do; se kāhinī kichu — something of that tale; kahi tomāre — I tell you

**2.3.** Perish shame now — what can it do to me? Something of it I will tell you.

আমারে রাখিয়া ননদী স্থানে । শাশুড়ী গেলেন সে পাড়া পানে ॥

*āmāre rākhiyā nanadī sthāne | śāśuṛī gelena se pāṛā pāne ||*

*Word for word:* āmāre rākhiyā — leaving me; nanadī sthāne — with my sister-in-law; śāśuṛī gelena — my mother-in-law went; se pāṛā pāne — towards that quarter

**2.4.** Leaving me with my sister-in-law, my mother-in-law went off to the other end of the village.

এথা ননদিনী করিল দ্বন্দ্ব । কহিল আমারে অনেক মন্দ ॥

*ethā nanadinī karila dvandva | kahila āmāre aneka manda ||*

*Word for word:* ethā — and here; nanadinī karila dvandva — my sister-in-law picked a quarrel; kahila āmāre — said to me; aneka manda — many bad things

**2.5.** And here my sister-in-law picked a quarrel and said many bad things to me,

নিজ জিত লাগি সকল ছাড়ি । রুষিয়া গেলেন পরের বাড়ী ॥

*nija jita lāgi sakala chāṛi | ruṣiyā gelena parera bāṛī ||*

*Word for word:* nija jita lāgi — to have her own way; sakala chāṛi — leaving everything; ruṣiyā gelena — went off in anger; parera bāṛī — to someone else's house

**2.6.** and, to have her own way, she dropped everything and went off in a huff to someone else's house.

একাকিনী মুই রহিনু ঘরে । বসিনু যাইয়া গবাক্ষদ্বারে ॥

*ekākinī mui rahinu ghare | basinu yāiyā gabākṣadvāre ||*

*Word for word:* ekākinī mui rahinu ghare — I stayed at home alone; basinu yāiyā — I went and sat; gabākṣa-dvāre — by the window

**2.7.** I stayed at home alone; I went and sat by the window.

গৌররূপগুণ ভাবিয়া মনে । চাহিয়া রহিনু পথের পানে ॥

*gaurarūpaguṇa bhābiyā mane | cāhiyā rahinu pathera pāne ||*

*Word for word:* gaura-rūpa-guṇa — Gaura's beauty and virtues; bhābiyā mane — thinking in my mind; cāhiyā rahinu — I kept gazing; pathera pāne — at the road

**2.8.** Thinking of Gaura's beauty and virtues, I kept my eyes on the road.

হেনই সময়ে গৌরাঙ্গসখা । আমাদের পথে দিলেন দেখা ॥

*henai samaye gaurāṅgasakhā | āmādera pathe dilena dekhā ||*

*Word for word:* henai samaye — at that very moment; gaurāṅga-sakhā — Gauranga, the dear friend; āmādera pathe — in our street; dilena dekhā — appeared

**2.9.** And at that very moment Gauranga, the dear friend, appeared in our street.

অলখিত লখি ও চাঁদমুখ । বিসরিনু কিছু হিয়ার দুখ ॥

*alakhita lakhi o cām̐damukha | bisarinu kichu hiyāra dukha ||*

*Word for word:* alakhita lakhi — gazing unseen; o cām̐da-mukha — at that moonlike face; bisarinu kichu — I forgot a little; hiyāra dukha — the sorrow of my heart

**2.10.** Gazing unseen at that moonlike face, I forgot a little of the sorrow of my heart.

তুরিতে মলিন কুমুদকলি । গবাক্ষের পথে দিলাম ফেলি ॥

*turite malina kumudakali | gabākṣera pathe dilāma pheli ||*

*Word for word:* turite — at once; malina kumuda-kali — a withered kumuda bud; gabākṣera pathe — through the window; dilāma pheli — I threw

**2.11.** At once I threw a withered kumuda bud through the window.

তা দেখিয়া গোরা চতুর অতি । করে লৈয়া কহে কুমুদ প্রতি ॥

*tā dekhiyā gorā catura ati | kare laiyā kahe kumuda prati ||*

*Word for word:* tā dekhiyā — seeing it; gorā catura ati — Gora, very quick-witted; kare laiyā — taking it in His hand; kahe kumuda prati — says to the kumuda

**2.12.** Seeing it, Gora — and He is very quick-witted — took it in His hand and says, speaking to the kumuda:

চিন্তা নাহি শশী উদয় হবে । দিনকর-তাপ দূরেতে যাবে ॥

*cintā nāhi śaśī udaya habe | dinakara-tāpa dūrete yābe ||*

*Word for word:* cintā nāhi — do not grieve; śaśī udaya habe — the moon will rise; dinakara-tāpa — the heat of the sun; dūrete yābe — will go far away

**2.13.** 'Do not grieve: the moon will rise, and the heat of the sun will go far away.'[^30-5]

এত কহি হাসি নয়ান কোণে । বারেক চাহিল আমার পানে ॥

*eta kahi hāsi nayāna koṇe | bāreka cāhila āmāra pāne ||*

*Word for word:* eta kahi — having said this; hāsi — smiling; nayāna koṇe — from the corner of His eye; bāreka cāhila — glanced once; āmāra pāne — towards me

**2.14.** Having said this, smiling, He glanced just once from the corner of His eye towards me.

অমনি অবশ হইল তনু । বিষম সাপেতে দংশিল জনু ॥

*amani abaśa haila tanu | biṣama sāpete daṃśila janu ||*

*Word for word:* amani — at once; abaśa haila tanu — the body lost its strength; biṣama sāpete — a deadly snake; daṃśila janu — as if had bitten

**2.15.** At once my body lost all strength, as if a deadly snake had bitten me.

যতনে ধৈরজ ধরিতে নারি । মনে হয় গিয়া পরশ করি ॥

*yatane dhairaja dharite nāri | mane haya giyā paraśa kari ||*

*Word for word:* yatane — try as I might; dhairaja dharite nāri — I cannot keep my composure; mane haya — I feel; giyā paraśa kari — to go and touch

**2.16.** Try as I might, I could not keep my composure: I longed to go and touch Him.[^30-6]

ঘন ঘন কাঁপি ঘামিল গা । উঠিয়া চলিতে না চলে পা ॥

*ghana ghana kām̐pi ghāmila gā | uṭhiyā calite nā cale pā ||*

*Word for word:* ghana ghana kām̐pi — trembling again and again; ghāmila gā — the body sweated; uṭhiyā calite — rising to walk; nā cale pā — the feet do not move

**2.17.** I tremble all over, my body sweats; I rise to walk — my feet will not move.

কি কহিব চিতে প্রবোধ দিয়া । রহিলাম অতি আতুর হৈয়া ॥

*ki kahiba cite prabodha diyā | rahilāma ati ātura haiyā ||*

*Word for word:* ki kahiba — what shall I say; cite prabodha diyā — trying to calm my heart; rahilāma — I remained; ati ātura haiyā — in great agitation

**2.18.** What shall I say? Trying to calm my heart, I remained in great agitation.

হেন কালে ঘরে শাশুড়ী আইলা । মোরে পুছে কেন এমন হৈলা ॥

*hena kāle ghare śāśuṛī āilā | more puche kena emana hailā ||*

*Word for word:* hena kāle — just then; ghare śāśuṛī āilā — my mother-in-law came home; more puche — asks me; kena emana hailā — why are you like this

**2.19.** Just then my mother-in-law came home and asks me: 'Why are you like this?'

মো অতি কাতরে কহিনু তারে । ননদী রহিতে না দিবে ঘরে ॥

*mo ati kātare kahinu tāre | nanadī rahite nā dibe ghare ||*

*Word for word:* mo ati kātare — I very piteously; kahinu tāre — told her; nanadī — my sister-in-law; rahite nā dibe ghare — will not let me live in the house

**2.20.** Very piteously I told her: 'My sister-in-law will not let me live in the house.

আপনি রহিলে কিছু না বলে । অনলের সম অন্তর জ্বলে ॥

*āpani rahile kichu nā bale | analera sama antara jvale ||*

*Word for word:* āpani rahile — when you yourself are here; kichu nā bale — she says nothing; analera sama — like fire; antara jvale — her heart burns

**2.21.** When you yourself are at home, she says nothing, but her heart burns like fire.

তুমি গেলা ঘর ছাড়িয়া সেথা । মো সনে কোন্দল করিল হেথা ॥

*tumi gelā ghara chāṛiyā sethā | mo sane kondala karila hethā ||*

*Word for word:* tumi gelā — you went; ghara chāṛiyā sethā — leaving the house, there; mo sane — with me; kondala karila hethā — she quarrelled here

**2.22.** You left the house to go there — and here she picked a quarrel with me.

সে কথা কহিতে নাহিক ওর । ইথে কিছু দোষ না ছিল মোর ॥

*se kathā kahite nāhika ora | ithe kichu doṣa nā chila mora ||*

*Word for word:* se kathā kahite — in telling of it; nāhika ora — there is no end; ithe — in this; kichu doṣa nā chila mora — there was no fault of mine

**2.23.** There is no end to the telling of it; and there was no fault of mine in it at all.

যদি মনে কোন সন্দেহ থাকে । তবে পুছ এই পড়সি লোকে ॥

*yadi mane kona sandeha thāke | tabe pucha ei paṛasi loke ||*

*Word for word:* yadi mane — if in your mind; kona sandeha thāke — there is any doubt; tabe pucha — then ask; ei paṛasi loke — these neighbours

**2.24.** If you have any doubt in your mind, ask the neighbours here.

কি কহিব একা রাখিয়া মোরে । ননদিয়া গেলা পরের ঘরে ॥

*ki kahiba ekā rākhiyā more | nanadiyā gelā parera ghare ||*

*Word for word:* ki kahiba — what shall I say; ekā rākhiyā more — leaving me alone; nanadiyā gelā — my sister-in-law went; parera ghare — to someone else's house

**2.25.** What shall I say! Leaving me alone, my sister-in-law went off to someone else's house —

তার বুদ্ধি যত ইহাতে জান । মো কেনে এমন সে কথা শুন ॥

*tāra buddhi yata ihāte jāna | mo kene emana se kathā śuna ||*

*Word for word:* tāra buddhi yata — how much sense she has; ihāte jāna — know from this; mo kene emana — why I am like this; se kathā śuna — hear that

**2.26.** judge from this how much sense she has. And why I am like this — listen:

একে একা ভয় হৃদয় মাঝ । আর তাহে ভাবি ঘরের কাজ ॥

*eke ekā bhaya hṛdaya mājha | āra tāhe bhābi gharera kāja ||*

*Word for word:* eke ekā — first, alone; bhaya hṛdaya mājha — fear in my heart; āra tāhe — and besides; bhābi gharera kāja — I thought of the housework

**2.27.** besides being afraid all alone, I was also thinking of the housework;

কি করি শ্রম অনেক হৈল । তাহাতেই ভ্রমি হইয়াছিল ॥

*ki kari śrama aneka haila | tāhātei bhrami haiyāchila ||*

*Word for word:* ki kari — whatever I did; śrama aneka haila — I grew very tired; tāhātei — from that; bhrami haiyāchila — my head was spinning

**2.28.** whatever I did, I grew very tired, and that is why my head was spinning.'

গদ গদ বাণী শুনিয়া স্নেহে । নিজ কর দিল আমার মাথে ॥

*gada gada bāṇī śuniyā snehe | nija kara dila āmāra māthe ||*

*Word for word:* gada gada bāṇī — faltering words; śuniyā snehe — hearing, tenderly; nija kara dila — she laid her own hand; āmāra māthe — on my head

**2.29.** Hearing my faltering words, my mother-in-law tenderly laid her hand on my head,

আপন বসনে পবন করি । বুঝাইল কত করেতে ধরি ॥

*āpana basane pabana kari | bujhāila kata karete dhari ||*

*Word for word:* āpana basane — with her own cloth; pabana kari — fanning; bujhāila kata — comforted me at length; karete dhari — holding my hands

**2.30.** fanned me with the end of her own cloth, took my hands and comforted me at length.

ননদে ডাকিয়া তর্জন কৈল । তা শুনিয়া মোর আনন্দ হৈল ॥

*nanade ḍākiyā tarjana kaila | tā śuniyā mora ānanda haila ||*

*Word for word:* nanade ḍākiyā — calling my sister-in-law; tarjana kaila — she scolded her; tā śuniyā — hearing that; mora ānanda haila — I was delighted

**2.31.** Calling my sister-in-law, she scolded her — and hearing that, I was delighted."

নরহরি কহে তুমি সে ধন্য । এরূপ চাতুরী জানে কে অন্য ॥

*narahari kahe tumi se dhanya | erūpa cāturī jāne ke anya ||*

*Word for word:* narahari kahe — Narahari says; tumi se dhanya — you are truly fortunate; erūpa cāturī — such tricks; jāne ke anya — who else knows

**2.32.** Narahari says: you are truly fortunate — who else knows such tricks?[^30-7]

[^30-4]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — pp. 195–196, no. 95 (scan PDF pp. 454–455); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 95 (catalogue: NG-087). GCC — kirana 7, pada 11
(pp. 73–75; scan PDF pp. 78–80). GCC readings: "henai samaye gaurāṅga ekā" (GPT1 "gaurāṅgasakhā"; the GCC reading, "Gauranga alone", rhymes better with
dekhā), "nija kara dila āmāri māthe". Short payar. On 2.13 GPT1 has an editor's footnote with an interpretation (not reproduced). B. Nagari-bhava —
see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^30-5]: The kumuda is the white night-lily: it opens at moonrise and closes under the sun; in poetry it is an image of the loving woman pining for
her moon-beloved. The withered bud thrown from the window is the townswoman's mute sign ("I wither without my moon"); Gora answers the flower, not
her: "the moon will rise, and the heat of the sun will go." The moon (śaśī, cām̐da) is a constant name of Gaura in the GCC padas ("the Moon of
Nadia"), so the answer is both consolation and a promise of darshan; translated literally, without interpretation.
[^30-6]: The longing "to go and touch" and the signs of agitation (loss of strength, trembling, sweat) are stated plainly in the original; translated
exactly. These are formulas of purvaraga shared with the padas on the gopis; the Lord merely passes along the street and answers the flower. The
tradition does not accept worship of Gaura in the nagari mood (introductory note, chapter 27).
[^30-7]: The deception of the mother-in-law (the complaint against the sister-in-law, "fatigue" instead of the true cause) and the poet's praise of
the "tricks" are rendered as in the original — a poetic convention of the purvaraga padas (cf. n. 47 of chapter 29).

## 3. Narahari — "śuna go sajani balie tore…" (GPT1 p. 196, no. 96; GCC 7.12)
*Nagari-bhava. A townswoman's story: putting on a new sari, she went alone to her brother's house and on the way met Gora; at His glance she lost
her composure and barely made it home; her mother-in-law, seeing tears in her eyes, asked what had happened — "I went out of the gate and saw a
terrible snake"; the frightened mother-in-law splashed water on her face. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 7,
pada 12.*[^30-8]

শুন গো সজনি বলিএ তোরে । না জানিএ কিবা হইল মোরে ॥

*śuna go sajani balie tore | nā jānie kibā haila more ||*

*Word for word:* śuna go sajani — listen, friend; balie tore — I tell you; nā jānie — I do not know; kibā haila more — what has happened to me

**3.1.** "Listen, friend, I will tell you: I do not know what has come over me.

তুরিতে পরিয়া নবীন সাড়ী । একাকী চলিনু ভাইয়ের বাড়ী ॥

*turite pariyā nabīna sāṛī | ekākī calinu bhāiyera bāṛī ||*

*Word for word:* turite pariyā — hastily putting on; nabīna sāṛī — a new sari; ekākī calinu — I went alone; bhāiyera bāṛī — to my brother's house

**3.2.** Hastily putting on a new sari, I set out alone for my brother's house.

পথে গোরা সনে হইল দেখা । কি কব রূপের নাহিক লেখা ॥

*pathe gorā sane haila dekhā | ki kaba rūpera nāhika lekhā ||*

*Word for word:* pathe — on the way; gorā sane haila dekhā — I met Gora; ki kaba — what shall I say; rūpera nāhika lekhā — there is no measure to His beauty

**3.3.** On the way I met Gora — what shall I say? There is no measure to His beauty.

বারেক চাহিয়া আমার পানে । না জানি কি কৈল নয়ন-কোণে ॥

*bāreka cāhiyā āmāra pāne | nā jāni ki kaila nayana-koṇe ||*

*Word for word:* bāreka cāhiyā — glancing just once; āmāra pāne — towards me; nā jāni — I do not know; ki kaila nayana-koṇe — what He did with the corner of His eye

**3.4.** He glanced just once towards me — and I do not know what He did with the corner of His eye:

ধৈরজ ধরম সরম যত । তা মেনে তখনি হইল হত ॥

*dhairaja dharama sarama yata | tā mene takhani haila hata ||*

*Word for word:* dhairaja — composure; dharama — dharma; sarama — modesty; yata — all there was; tā mene — it seems; takhani haila hata — perished at once

**3.5.** composure, dharma, modesty — all there was perished at that very moment.

কেমন কেমন করয়ে হিয়া । সম্বরিতে নারি প্রবোধ দিয়া ॥

*kemana kemana karaye hiyā | sambarite nāri prabodha diyā ||*

*Word for word:* kemana kemana karaye hiyā — my heart feels I know not how; sambarite nāri — I cannot restrain it; prabodha diyā — though I reason with it

**3.6.** My heart became I know not how — I reason with it and cannot calm it.

চলিতে অধীর না চলে পা । কাঁপিয়া কাঁপিয়া উঠয়ে গা ॥

*calite adhīra nā cale pā | kām̐piyā kām̐piyā uṭhaye gā ||*

*Word for word:* calite adhīra — agitated as I walk; nā cale pā — my feet will not move; kām̐piyā kām̐piyā uṭhaye gā — my body trembles and trembles

**3.7.** In agitation I walk — my feet will not move; my whole body trembles and trembles.

সঘনে অঙ্গের বসন খসে । এসব হেরিয়া সে পুনঃ হাসে ॥

*saghane aṅgera basana khase | esaba heriyā se punaḥ hāse ||*

*Word for word:* saghane — again and again; aṅgera basana khase — the cloth slips from the body; e saba heriyā — seeing all this; se punaḥ hāse — He in turn smiles

**3.8.** Again and again my clothes slip from my body — and He, seeing all this, smiles.[^30-9]

কি করিব গুরুজনের ডরে । ধরমে ধরমে আইনু ঘরে ॥

*ki kariba gurujanera ḍare | dharame dharame āinu ghare ||*

*Word for word:* ki kariba — what could I do; gurujanera ḍare — for fear of the elders; dharame dharame — somehow; āinu ghare — I came home

**3.9.** What could I do? For fear of the elders I somehow made my way home.

পুনঃ আনচান করয়ে তনু । সে গৌরসুন্দর দরশ বিনু ॥

*punaḥ ānacāna karaye tanu | se gaurasundara daraśa binu ||*

*Word for word:* punaḥ — again; ānacāna karaye tanu — the body languishes; se gaurasundara — of that beautiful Gaura; daraśa binu — without the sight

**3.10.** And there again my body languishes without the sight of that beautiful Gaura.

হেনই সময়ে শাশুড়ী আসি । পুছয়ে আমার নিকটে বসি ॥

*henai samaye śāśuṛī āsi | puchaye āmāra nikaṭe basi ||*

*Word for word:* henai samaye — at that very moment; śāśuṛī āsi — my mother-in-law, coming; puchaye — asks; āmāra nikaṭe basi — sitting beside me

**3.11.** Just at that moment my mother-in-law came, sat down beside me and asks:

আজু কি লাগিয়া এমন দেখি । জলে টলমল করয়ে আঁখি ॥

*āju ki lāgiyā emana dekhi | jale ṭalamala karaye ām̐khi ||*

*Word for word:* āju ki lāgiyā — why today; emana dekhi — do I see you like this; jale ṭalamala karaye ām̐khi — your eyes are brimming with tears

**3.12.** 'Why are you like this today? Your eyes are brimming with tears.

কাতর হইয়া কহিছ কথা । না জানি এ কিবা হয়েছে ব্যথা ॥

*kātara haiyā kahicha kathā | nā jāni e kibā hayeche byathā ||*

*Word for word:* kātara haiyā — piteously; kahicha kathā — you speak; nā jāni — I do not know; e kibā hayeche byathā — what pain this is

**3.13.** You speak so piteously — I do not know what pain has come to you.'

এতেক শুনিয়া কহিনু তারে । গিয়াছিনু মুই বাহির দ্বারে ॥

*eteka śuniyā kahinu tāre | giyāchinu mui bāhira dvāre ||*

*Word for word:* eteka śuniyā — hearing this; kahinu tāre — I told her; giyāchinu mui — I had gone; bāhira dvāre — out of the gate

**3.14.** Hearing this, I told her: 'I had gone out of the gate,

তথাতে দেখিনু বিষম সাপ । অন্তর কাঁপিল মিটিল দাপ ॥

*tathāte dekhinu biṣama sāpa | antara kām̐pila miṭila dāpa ||*

*Word for word:* tathāte — there; dekhinu biṣama sāpa — I saw a terrible snake; antara kām̐pila — my heart shook; miṭila dāpa — my courage was gone

**3.15.** and there I saw a terrible snake — my heart shook, all my courage was gone.

সে পুনঃ যাইয়া সাঁধাল খালে । মু বাঁচিনু তুয়া চরণবলে ॥

*se punaḥ yāiyā sām̐dhāla khāle | mu bām̐cinu tuyā caraṇabale ||*

*Word for word:* se punaḥ yāiyā — it then; sām̐dhāla khāle — slid into the ditch; mu bām̐cinu — I was saved; tuyā caraṇa-bale — by the power of your feet

**3.16.** Then it slid away into the ditch — I was saved by the power of your feet.'

ইহা শুনি অতি বিকল হৈলা । চোকে মুখে জল আপনি দিলা ॥

*ihā śuni ati bikala hailā | coke mukhe jala āpani dilā ||*

*Word for word:* ihā śuni — hearing this; ati bikala hailā — she grew very alarmed; coke mukhe — on eyes and face; jala āpani dilā — she herself splashed water

**3.17.** Hearing this, she grew very alarmed and herself splashed water on my eyes and face."[^30-10]

নরহরি কহে কিছু না মান । শাশুড়ী ভুলাতে তুমি সে জান ॥

*narahari kahe kichu nā māna | śāśuṛī bhulāte tumi se jāna ||*

*Word for word:* narahari kahe — Narahari says; kichu nā māna — you fear nothing; śāśuṛī bhulāte — how to fool your mother-in-law; tumi se jāna — you surely know

**3.18.** Narahari says: you fear nothing — you certainly know how to fool your mother-in-law!

[^30-8]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — p. 196, no. 96 (scan PDF p. 455); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 96 (catalogue: NG-088). GCC — kirana 7, pada 12 (p. 75; scan PDF
p. 80). GCC has two extra couplets: after 3.15 — "se punaḥ mo pāne āila dhāiyā | palāinu mui byākula haiyā ||" ("It rushed at me — I fled in
