alarm"), after 3.17 — "nija kara dhari āmāra śire | māne śibe kata manera ḍare ||" ("Laying her hand on my head, she in fear vowed many offerings to
Shiva"); the translation follows GPT1. Short payar. B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^30-9]: The slipping clothes are a sign of agitation, as in the padas on the gopis (cf. n. 58 of chapter 29); the original states it plainly, translated
exactly. The Lord's smile is the same as in no. 2 (2.14): He merely passes along the road. The tradition does not accept the image of Gaura as
nagara (introductory note, chapter 27).
[^30-10]: "A terrible snake" is an ambiguous answer: in no. 2 (2.15) Gaura's glance stung the townswoman "as if a deadly snake had bitten" her. The
deception of the mother-in-law and the poet's praise (3.18) are a poetic convention of the purvaraga padas (cf. n. 47 of chapter 29).

## 4. Narahari — "nanadī bicāra kariyā garabe…" (GPT1 pp. 196–197, no. 97; GCC 7.14)
*Nagari-bhava. A townswoman's story: her sister-in-law, having planned mischief, dressed up and went for water, leaving her alone at home; on the
road she met Gaura with His companions and, forgetting all her schemes, followed Him with the pot on her hip; the mother-in-law caught her so and
snatched away the pot — while the daughter-in-law meanwhile saw Gaura on her own road; the mother-in-law praised her, and the sister-in-law was
put to shame. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 7, pada 14 (second half).*[^30-11]

ননদী বিচার করিয়া গরবে পরিয়া নবীন সাড়ী ।
জল আনিবারে গেলেন আমারে ঘরেতে একাকী ছাড়ি ॥

*nanadī bicāra kariyā garabe pariyā nabīna sāṛī |*
*jala ānibāre gelena āmāre gharete ekākī chāṛi ||*

*Word for word:* nanadī — my sister-in-law; bicāra kariyā — having thought it out; garabe — proudly; pariyā nabīna sāṛī — putting on a new sari; jala ānibāre gelena — went to fetch water; āmāre gharete ekākī chāṛi — leaving me alone at home

**4.1.** "Having thought it all out, my sister-in-law proudly put on a new sari
and went to fetch water, leaving me alone at home.

মনের হরিষে অতি তরাতরি ননদী যে পথে যায় ।
সেই পথে নিজ পরিকর সনে আইসে গৌররায় ॥

*manera hariṣe ati tarātari nanadī ye pathe yāya |*
*sei pathe nija parikara sane āise gaurarāya ||*

*Word for word:* manera hariṣe — with a glad heart; ati tarātari — in great haste; nanadī ye pathe yāya — the road my sister-in-law takes; sei pathe — along that road; nija parikara sane — with His companions; āise gaurarāya — comes Gaura Raya

**4.2.** Gleeful, she hurried along her road —
and along that very road, with His companions, comes Gaura Raya.

ওরূপ-মাধুরী হেরি বারে বারে ননদী পাগলী হৈলা ।
মনের যতেক মনোরথ তাহা সকলি ভুলিয়া গেলা ॥

*orūpa-mādhurī heri bāre bāre nanadī pāgalī hailā |*
*manera yateka manoratha tāhā sakali bhuliyā gelā ||*

*Word for word:* o-rūpa-mādhurī heri — seeing the sweetness of that form; bāre bāre — again and again; nanadī pāgalī hailā — my sister-in-law went mad; manera yateka manoratha — all the schemes in her mind; tāhā sakali bhuliyā gelā — she forgot them all

**4.3.** Seeing the sweetness of that form, my sister-in-law quite lost her head:
all the schemes she had in mind she clean forgot.

সে পথে শাশুড়ী আসি নিরখিতে নিকটে দেখয়ে তারে ।
কলসী কাঁখেতে করিয়া গৌরাঙ্গচাঁদের পাছেতে ফিরে ॥

*se pathe śāśuṛī āsi nirakhite nikaṭe dekhaye tāre |*
*kalasī kām̐khete kariyā gaurāṅgacām̐dera pāchete phire ||*

*Word for word:* se pathe śāśuṛī āsi — the mother-in-law, coming that way; nirakhite — looking; nikaṭe dekhaye tāre — sees her close by; kalasī kām̐khete kariyā — with the pot on her hip; gaurāṅgacām̐dera pāchete phire — wanders behind Gaurangachand

**4.4.** Along that road came my mother-in-law — and, looking, sees her close by:
with the pot on her hip she is wandering after Gaurangachand.[^30-12]

ভাল ভাল বলি অধিক কোরধে কলসি কাড়িয়া নিল ।
কারে কি কহিবে ননদী অমনি মরমে মরিয়া গেল ॥

*bhāla bhāla bali adhika koradhe kalasi kāṛiyā nila |*
*kāre ki kahibe nanadī amani marame mariyā gela ||*

*Word for word:* bhāla bhāla bali — saying "very good"; adhika koradhe — in great anger; kalasi kāṛiyā nila — snatched away the pot; kāre ki kahibe — what and to whom could she say; nanadī — my sister-in-law; amani marame mariyā gela — at once died of shame

**4.5.** 'Very good, very good!' she said in great anger, and snatched away the pot;
what could my sister-in-law say, and to whom? — she wished the earth would swallow her.

এথা মুই প্রাণগৌরাঙ্গসুন্দরে আপন পথেতে পাঞা ।
হিয়ার বেদনা মিটাইনু মেন ও চাঁদবদন চাঞা ॥

*ethā mui prāṇagaurāṅgasundare āpana pathete pāñā |*
*hiyāra bedanā miṭāinu mena o cām̐dabadana cāñā ||*

*Word for word:* ethā mui — I meanwhile; prāṇa-gaurāṅga-sundare — beautiful Gauranga, my life; āpana pathete pāñā — finding on my own road; hiyāra bedanā miṭāinu — I eased the pain of my heart; mena (= yena) — as it were, truly (an emphatic particle); o cām̐da-badana cāñā — gazing at that moonlike face

**4.6.** And I meanwhile, meeting beautiful Gauranga, my life, on my own road,
eased the pain of my heart gazing at that moonlike face.

কতক্ষণে আসি শাশুড়ী অনেক প্রশংসা করয়ে মোরে ।
ননদের লাজ কি কহিব যেন থাকি না থাকয়ে ঘরে ॥

*katakṣaṇe āsi śāśuṛī aneka praśaṃsā karaye more |*
*nanadera lāja ki kahiba yena thāki nā thākaye ghare ||*

*Word for word:* katakṣaṇe — after a while; āsi śāśuṛī — the mother-in-law, coming; aneka praśaṃsā karaye more — praises me at length; nanadera lāja — my sister-in-law's shame; ki kahiba — what shall I say; yena thāki nā thākaye ghare — she is at home as if not there

**4.7.** A little later my mother-in-law came and praised me at length;
and what shall I say of my sister-in-law's shame — she is at home as if she were not there."

নরহরি কহে মূরখ হইলে কিছু না দেখিতে পায় ।
আপনার দোষ আঁচলে বাঁধিয়া পরকে দূষিতে চায় ॥

*narahari kahe mūrakha haile kichu nā dekhite pāya |*
*āpanāra doṣa ām̐cale bām̐dhiyā parake dūṣite cāya ||*

*Word for word:* narahari kahe — Narahari says; mūrakha haile — one who is a fool; kichu nā dekhite pāya — sees nothing; āpanāra doṣa — her own fault; ām̐cale bām̐dhiyā — tying in the end of her sari; parake dūṣite cāya — seeks to blame another

**4.8.** Narahari says: one who is a fool sees nothing:
tying her own fault in the end of her sari, she seeks to blame another.

[^30-11]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — pp. 196–197, no. 97 (scan PDF pp. 455–456); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 97 (catalogue: NG-089). GCC — kirana 7, pada 14
(pp. 77–79; scan PDF pp. 82–84). In GCC the pada is twice as long: GPT begins it from the middle (GCC "erūpa bicāra kariyā garabe" — "having thus
thought it out…"; GPT "nanadī bicāra kariyā"). In the omitted first half (13 couplets, pp. 77–78) the townswoman tells how her sister-in-law and
her friends plotted to disgrace her: she told the mother-in-law that the bride would bring shame on the house with "a brahmana's son" (a hint at
Gaura); the mother-in-law replied that she would believe it only when she saw it with her own eyes; then the sister-in-law resolved to leave the
bride alone, on her way to fetch water to send a young man she knew to the house, and then to call the neighbours and expose her. The translation
follows GPT1; the omitted part is not translated (the text is that of GPT), only retold here. GCC readings in the second half: "prāṇa-gaurāṅgasundare",
"praśaṃsā karaye more". B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^30-12]: The strict sister-in-law who forgets her schemes at the sight of Gaura is a recurrent motif of GCC (cf. chapter 29, no. 21): even the
townswomen's adversaries lose their composure on seeing Gaura. The Lord here merely walks along the road with His companions.

## 5. Narahari — "ki baliba sakhi kakhana saphala…" (GPT1 p. 197, no. 98; GCC 7.15)
*Nagari-bhava. A townswoman's story: her wish has never come true — the Creator has always put obstacles in the way; but yesterday, hearing that
Gaura was coming, she went up to the upper gallery and saw Him; the fragrance of His body reached her; Gora turned towards her — and just then her
mother-in-law called her; she went away, but the mother-in-law let her go for water. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** —
GCC, kirana 7, pada 15.*[^30-13]

কি বলিব সখি কখন সফল না হৈল মনের সাধা ।
দুখ ভুঞ্জাইতে বিধি নিকরুণ করিল অনেক বাধা ॥

*ki baliba sakhi kakhana saphala nā haila manera sādhā |*
*dukha bhuñjāite bidhi nikaruṇa karila aneka bādhā ||*

*Word for word:* ki baliba sakhi — what shall I say, friend; kakhana saphala nā haila — never came true; manera sādhā — the wish of my heart; dukha bhuñjāite — to make me suffer; bidhi nikaruṇa — the pitiless Creator; karila aneka bādhā — put many obstacles

**5.1.** "What shall I say, friend? Never has the wish of my heart come true:
to make me suffer, the pitiless Creator has put many obstacles in the way.

গতদিন মেন আমাদের পথে আইল পরাণপিয়া ।
লোক মুখে শুনি সাহসে উপর দালানে দাঁড়ানু গিয়া ॥

*gatadina mena āmādera pathe āila parāṇapiyā |*
*loka mukhe śuni sāhase upara dālāne dām̐ṛānu giyā ||*

*Word for word:* gatadina — yesterday; mena (= yena) — as it were, truly (an emphatic particle); āmādera pathe āila — came along our road; parāṇa-piyā — the Beloved of my life; loka mukhe śuni — hearing from people; sāhase — boldly; upara dālāne dām̐ṛānu giyā — I went and stood on the upper gallery

**5.2.** But yesterday, truly, along our road came the Beloved of my life;
hearing of it from people, I took courage, went up and stood on the upper gallery.[^30-14]

ওরূপমাধুরী হেরিয়া আমার মজিল যুগল আঁখি ।
মনেতে হইল নিকটে উড়িয়া যাইএ হইয়া পাখী ॥

*orūpamādhurī heriyā āmāra majila yugala ām̐khi |*
*manete haila nikaṭe uṛiyā yāie haiyā pākhī ||*

*Word for word:* o-rūpa-mādhurī heriyā — seeing the sweetness of that form; āmāra majila yugala ām̐khi — both my eyes were drowned; manete haila — I thought; nikaṭe uṛiyā yāie — to fly to Him; haiyā pākhī — becoming a bird

**5.3.** Seeing the sweetness of that form, both my eyes were drowned in it;
I thought: if only I could become a bird and fly to Him!

ললিত অঙ্গের সৌরভ আসিয়া নাসায় পশিল মোর ।
অধিক অধীর হইনু কি কব সুখের নাহিক ওর ॥

*lalita aṅgera saurabha āsiyā nāsāya paśila mora |*
*adhika adhīra hainu ki kaba sukhera nāhika ora ||*

*Word for word:* lalita aṅgera saurabha — the fragrance of the graceful body; āsiyā nāsāya paśila mora — came and entered my nostrils; adhika adhīra hainu — I lost all calm; ki kaba — what shall I say; sukhera nāhika ora — there was no end to joy

**5.4.** The fragrance of His graceful body came and entered my nostrils;
I lost all calm — what shall I say? There was no end to my joy.

গোরা মোর পানে ফিরিয়া চাহিল হেনই সময়ে বুড়ী ।
ঘন ঘন ডাকে কাঁপিল অন্তর আইনু সে সুখ ছাড়ি ॥

*gorā mora pāne phiriyā cāhila henai samaye buṛī |*
*ghana ghana ḍāke kām̐pila antara āinu se sukha chāṛi ||*

*Word for word:* gorā mora pāne phiriyā cāhila — Gora turned and looked towards me; henai samaye buṛī — at that very moment the old woman; ghana ghana ḍāke — keeps calling; kām̐pila antara — my heart shook; āinu se sukha chāṛi — I came away, leaving that joy

**5.5.** Gora turned and looked towards me — and at that very moment the old woman
keeps calling and calling me; my heart shook — I came away, leaving that joy.

অনুমতি দিল জলকে যাইতে ভাসিনু আনন্দ-জলে ।
নরহরি কহে এমন শাশুড়ী অনেক ভাগ্যেতে মিলে ॥

*anumati dila jalake yāite bhāsinu ānanda-jale |*
*narahari kahe emana śāśuṛī aneka bhāgyete mile ||*

*Word for word:* anumati dila — she gave leave; jalake yāite — to go for water; bhāsinu ānanda-jale — I floated on waters of joy; narahari kahe — Narahari says; emana śāśuṛī — such a mother-in-law; aneka bhāgyete mile — is found by great fortune

**5.6.** She gave me leave to go for water — I floated on waters of joy."
Narahari says: such a mother-in-law is found only by great good fortune.

[^30-13]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — p. 197, no. 98 (scan PDF p. 456); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 98 (catalogue: NG-337). GCC — kirana 7, pada 15 (pp. 79–80; scan
PDF pp. 84–85); GCC readings: "loka mukhe śuni sāhase upara-dālāne dām̐ṛānu giyā", "bhāgyete mile". In letting her daughter-in-law go for water (to the
Ganga), the mother-in-law unknowingly lets her see Gaura again — hence the poet's playful praise. B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the
section (chapter 27).
[^30-14]: "The Beloved of my life" (parāṇa-piyā) — the heroine's word for Gaura, as in the padas on the gopis for Krishna (cf. n. 46 of chapter 29);
the translation is faithful to the author.

## 6. Narahari — "sajani, kata nā kahiba āmāra dukhera kāhinī kathā…" (GPT1 p. 197, no. 99; GCC 7.16)
*Nagari-bhava. A townswoman's story: her mother-in-law, hearing that Gaura was coming, hurried home, bolted the door and sat in the courtyard on
guard; the daughter-in-law pressed her eyes to a tiny window and saw Gaura among His companions; with a look she let Him know how it was with her;
when the mother-in-law unbolted the door, the daughter-in-law was already sitting by the hearth. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably
Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 7, pada 16.*[^30-15]

সজনি, কত না কহিব আমার দুখের কাহিনী কথা ।
তাহে গতদিন সকরুণ বিধি ঘুচাইল কিঞ্চিৎ ব্যথা ॥

*sajani, kata nā kahiba āmāra dukhera kāhinī kathā |*
*tāhe gatadina sakaruṇa bidhi ghucāila kiñcit byathā ||*

*Word for word:* sajani — friend; kata nā kahiba — however much I tell; āmāra dukhera kāhinī kathā — the tale of my woes; tāhe gatadina — but yesterday; sakaruṇa bidhi — the merciful Creator; ghucāila kiñcit byathā — relieved my pain a little

**6.1.** "Friend, however much I tell, there is no end to my tale of woe;
but yesterday the merciful Creator relieved my pain a little.

আমাকে রন্ধনে রাখিয়া শাশুড়ী বাড়ীর বাহিরে ছিলা ।
গৌরগমন শুনিয়া তুরিতে আমার নিকটে আইলা ॥

*āmāke randhane rākhiyā śāśuṛī bāṛīra bāhire chilā |*
*gauragamana śuniyā turite āmāra nikaṭe āilā ||*

*Word for word:* āmāke randhane rākhiyā — leaving me at the cooking; śāśuṛī bāṛīra bāhire chilā — my mother-in-law was out of the house; gaura-gamana śuniyā — hearing that Gaura was coming; turite āmāra nikaṭe āilā — came back to me at once

**6.2.** Leaving me at the cooking, my mother-in-law had gone out of the house;
hearing that Gaura was coming, she came back to me at once.

আমাপানে পুনঃ চাহিয়া ঘরের দুয়ারে কপাট দিয়া ।
আঙ্গিনার মাঝে বসিয়া চকিত চৌদিকে রহিলা চাঞা ॥

*āmāpāne punaḥ cāhiyā gharera duyāre kapāṭa diyā |*
*āṅgināra mājhe basiyā cakita caudike rahilā cāñā ||*

*Word for word:* āmā pāne punaḥ cāhiyā — glancing at me once more; gharera duyāre kapāṭa diyā — bolting the door of the house; āṅgināra mājhe basiyā — sitting in the middle of the courtyard; cakita — warily; caudike rahilā cāñā — kept watching on every side

**6.3.** Glancing at me once more, she bolted the door of the house,
sat down in the middle of the courtyard and kept watching warily on every side.

এথা মোর প্রাণ আনচান করে কিছু না উপায় দেখি ।
অলপ গবাক্ষ আছিল তাহাতে সঁপিনু যুগল আঁখি ॥

*ethā mora prāṇa ānacāna kare kichu nā upāya dekhi |*
*alapa gabākṣa āchila tāhāte sam̐pinu yugala ām̐khi ||*

*Word for word:* ethā mora prāṇa ānacāna kare — here my heart is in turmoil; kichu nā upāya dekhi — I see no way out; alapa gabākṣa āchila — there was a tiny window; tāhāte sam̐pinu yugala ām̐khi — to it I gave both my eyes

**6.4.** And here my heart is in turmoil — I see no way out;
there was a tiny window — to it I pressed both my eyes.

পরিকর মাঝে রসিকশেখর কে বুঝে তাহার রীতি ।
অতি অলখিত চারি ভিতে চাহি চলয়ে কুঞ্জরগতি ॥

*parikara mājhe rasikaśekhara ke bujhe tāhāra rīti |*
*ati alakhita cāri bhite cāhi calaye kuñjaragati ||*

*Word for word:* parikara mājhe — among the companions; rasika-śekhara — the Crown of connoisseurs of rasa; ke bujhe tāhāra rīti — who can fathom His ways; ati alakhita — quite unobtrusively; cāri bhite cāhi — glancing on all sides; calaye kuñjara-gati — He walks with an elephant's gait

**6.5.** Among His companions — the Crown of connoisseurs of rasa; who can fathom His ways?
Glancing about quite unobtrusively, He walks with the gait of an elephant.

সেরূপ-মাধুরী বারেক নিরখি নয়ানে নয়ান দিয়া ।
আমার যেরূপ দশা তাহা যেন জানানু ইঙ্গিত পাঞা ॥

*serūpa-mādhurī bāreka nirakhi nayāne nayāna diyā |*
*āmāra yerūpa daśā tāhā yena jānānu iṅgita pāñā ||*

*Word for word:* se-rūpa-mādhurī — the sweetness of that form; bāreka nirakhi — beholding but once; nayāne nayāna diyā — meeting eyes with eyes; āmāra yerūpa daśā — what state I was in; tāhā yena jānānu — I as it were made known; iṅgita pāñā — catching the sign

**6.6.** Beholding but once the sweetness of that form, meeting His eyes with mine,
I, as if catching His sign, let Him know what state I was in.

মোর পাশে আসি ঈষৎ হাসিয়া বলিলা চতুরমণি ।
মো পুন রন্ধনে বসিনু কপাট খুলিল শাশুড়ী কাণী ॥

*mora pāśe āsi īṣat hāsiyā balilā caturamaṇi |*
*mo puna randhane basinu kapāṭa khulila śāśuṛī kāṇī ||*

*Word for word:* mora pāśe āsi — coming level with me; īṣat hāsiyā — smiling a little; balilā catura-maṇi — the Jewel of the clever spoke; mo puna randhane basinu — I sat down again at the cooking; kapāṭa khulila — unbolted the door; śāśuṛī kāṇī — my one-eyed mother-in-law

**6.7.** Coming level with me, the Jewel of the clever smiled a little and spoke;
and I sat down again at the cooking — and then my one-eyed mother-in-law unbolted the door.[^30-16]

তেরছ হইয়া বাম আঁখে মোরে দেখিয়া সুস্থির হৈল ।
নরহরি কহে ও আঁখি-আপদ গেলেই হইল ভাল ॥

*teracha haiyā bāma ām̐khe more dekhiyā susthira haila |*
*narahari kahe o ām̐khi-āpada gelei haila bhāla ||*

*Word for word:* terācha haiyā — squinting sideways; bāma ām̐khe — with the left eye; more dekhiyā — seeing me; susthira haila — was reassured; narahari kahe — Narahari says; o ām̐khi-āpada — that calamity of an eye; gelei haila bhāla — if it were gone, it would be well

**6.8.** Squinting sideways, she looked at me with her left eye and was reassured."
Narahari says: if that calamity of an eye were gone too, all would be well![^30-17]

[^30-15]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — p. 197, no. 99 (scan PDF p. 456); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 99 (catalogue: NG-090). GCC — kirana 7, pada 16 (p. 80; scan PDF
p. 85) — the last pada of GCC before the lacuna in the scan (pp. 81–88 are missing; the next surviving one is GCC 7.29 = GPT1 no. 124). GCC readings:
"āmāke randhane rākhiyā", "alapa gabākṣa āchila tāhāte sam̐pinu yugala ām̐khi", "calaye kuñjara-gati". B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the
section (chapter 27).
[^30-16]: "Crown of connoisseurs of rasa" (rasikaśekhara), "Jewel of the clever" (caturamaṇi), "the gait of an elephant" are epithets of Krishna
transferred by the poet to Gaura; what He said the pada does not tell. As in the other GCC padas, the Lord merely passes along the street among His
companions; all the rest takes place in the townswoman's heart.
[^30-17]: The poet's joke at the one-eyed (kāṇī) mother-in-law — literally "let that calamity of an eye be gone too, and it will be well"; translated
without softening.

## 7. Narahari — "ekadina āmi śāśuṛī nanadī basiyāchi āṅgināya…" (GPT1 p. 198, no. 100)
*Nagari-bhava. A townswoman's comic story: once she, her mother-in-law and her sister-in-law were sitting in the courtyard when Gauranga passed by;
the sister-in-law, gazing at Him, so forgot herself that her clothes fell from her; the daughter-in-law went to dress her — and forgot herself
the same way; the mother-in-law came to rebuke them — and the same befell her; coming to their senses, the mother-in-law told her daughter-in-law
to tell no one. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: not established** — GPT only; not in the surviving pages of GCC (it may have stood on the lost
pp. 81–88).*[^30-18]

একদিন আমি শাশুড়ী ননদী বসিয়াছি আঙ্গিনায় ।
খেরকীর পথে চাহিয়া দেখিনু যাইছে গৌরাঙ্গরায় ॥

*ekadina āmi śāśuṛī nanadī basiyāchi āṅgināya |*
*kherakīra pathe cāhiyā dekhinu yāiche gaurāṅgarāya ||*

*Word for word:* ekadina — one day; āmi śāśuṛī nanadī — I, my mother-in-law and sister-in-law; basiyāchi āṅgināya — were sitting in the courtyard; kherakīra pathe — through the back gate; cāhiyā dekhinu — I looked and saw; yāiche gaurāṅgarāya — Gauranga Raya is passing

**7.1.** "One day we — I, my mother-in-law and my sister-in-law — were sitting in the courtyard;
through the back gate I looked out and saw: Gauranga Raya is passing.

সুজনের মত ঘোমটা টানিয়া আমি রহিলাম বসি ।
পহিলা ননদী মদনে মাতিয়া দাঁড়াইল হাসি হাসি ॥

*sujanera mata ghomaṭā ṭāniyā āmi rahilāma basi |*
*pahilā nanadī madane mātiyā dām̐ṛāila hāsi hāsi ||*

*Word for word:* sujanera mata — as befits a modest woman; ghomaṭā ṭāniyā — drawing my veil; āmi rahilāma basi — I stayed seated; pahilā nanadī — first my sister-in-law; madane mātiyā — intoxicated by Madana; dām̐ṛāila hāsi hāsi — stood up, smiling and smiling

**7.2.** As befits a modest woman, I drew my veil and stayed seated;
but my sister-in-law, first of all, intoxicated by Madana, stood up, smiling and smiling.

গবাক্ষের পথে চাহিয়া চাহিয়া দেখিতে লাগিল গোরা ।
অঙ্গের বসন শিথিল দেখিয়া শাশুড়ী দিলেন তাড়া ॥

*gabākṣera pathe cāhiyā cāhiyā dekhite lāgila gorā |*
*aṅgera basana śithila dekhiyā śāśuṛī dilena tāṛā ||*

*Word for word:* gabākṣera pathe — through the window; cāhiyā cāhiyā — gazing and gazing; dekhite lāgila gorā — began to look at Gora; aṅgera basana śithila — the clothes on her body loose; dekhiyā — seeing; śāśuṛī dilena tāṛā — my mother-in-law shouted

**7.3.** Gazing and gazing through the window, she began to look at Gora;
seeing that her clothes had come loose, my mother-in-law shouted at her.

বিবশ ননদী গোরারূপ হেরি সে তাড়া না শুনিল ।
দেখিতে দেখিতে সর্বাঙ্গ উলঙ্গ বসন পড়িয়া গেল ॥

*bibaśa nanadī gorārūpa heri se tāṛā nā śunila |*
*dekhite dekhite sarvāṅga ulaṅga basana paṛiyā gela ||*

*Word for word:* bibaśa nanadī — the overpowered sister-in-law; gorārūpa heri — gazing at Gora's form; se tāṛā nā śunila — did not hear that shout; dekhite dekhite — as she gazed; sarvāṅga ulaṅga — quite naked; basana paṛiyā gela — her clothes fell

**7.4.** Overpowered, gazing at Gora's form, my sister-in-law did not hear that shout;
and as she gazed, her clothes fell from her — she was left quite naked.[^30-19]

তা দেখিয়া আমি হাসিতে হাসিতে বস্ত্র পরাইতে গেলাম ।
বস্ত্র পরাব কি গৌররূপ হেরি নিজেই উলঙ্গ হৈলাম ॥

*tā dekhiyā āmi hāsite hāsite bastra parāite gelāma |*
*bastra parāba ki gaurarūpa heri nijei ulaṅga hailāma ||*

*Word for word:* tā dekhiyā — seeing this; āmi hāsite hāsite — I, laughing and laughing; bastra parāite gelāma — went to dress her; bastra parāba ki — dress her, indeed; gaurarūpa heri — looking at Gaura's form; nijei ulaṅga hailāma — I myself became naked

**7.5.** Seeing this, I, laughing and laughing, went to dress her —
dress her, indeed! — looking at Gaura's form, I too was left naked.

দুঁহারে শাসিতে কোরধ করিয়া শাশুড়ী নিকটে গেল ।
বিধির কি কাজ গৌরাঙ্গ দেখিতে বুড়িও উলঙ্গ হৈল ॥

*dum̐hāre śāsite koradha kariyā śāśuṛī nikaṭe gela |*
*bidhira ki kāja gaurāṅga dekhite buṛio ulaṅga haila ||*

*Word for word:* dum̐hāre śāsite — to rebuke the two of us; koradha kariyā — in anger; śāśuṛī nikaṭe gela — my mother-in-law came over; bidhira ki kāja — what a deed of the Creator; gaurāṅga dekhite — looking at Gauranga; buṛio ulaṅga haila — the old woman too became naked

**7.6.** To rebuke the two of us, my mother-in-law came over in anger —
what a deed of the Creator! — looking at Gauranga, the old woman too became naked.

উলঙ্গ হইয়া তিনজন মোরা দেখিতে লাগিনু গোরা ।
দেখিতে দেখিতে আঁধল করিয়া চলি গেল আঁখিতারা ॥

*ulaṅga haiyā tinajana morā dekhite lāginu gorā |*
*dekhite dekhite ām̐dhala kariyā cali gela ām̐khitārā ||*

*Word for word:* ulaṅga haiyā — naked; tinajana morā — the three of us; dekhite lāginu gorā — gazed at Gora; dekhite dekhite — as we gazed; ām̐dhala kariyā — leaving us sightless; cali gela ām̐khi-tārā — the star of our eyes went away

**7.7.** Naked, the three of us gazed at Gora;
and as we gazed, He — the star of our eyes — went away, leaving us sightless.

তখন সম্বিত হইল তিনের মাঝে জিভ কাটি সবে ।
শাশুড়ী কহিলা আজুকার লাজ বধূ কারে না কহিবে ॥

*takhana sambita haila tinera mājhe jibha kāṭi sabe |*
*śāśuṛī kahilā ājukāra lāja badhū kāre nā kahibe ||*

*Word for word:* takhana sambita haila — then came to our senses; tinera mājhe — the three of us; jibha kāṭi sabe — all bit our tongues; śāśuṛī kahilā — my mother-in-law said; ājukāra lāja — today's disgrace; badhū kāre nā kahibe — daughter-in-law, tell no one

**7.8.** Then all three of us came to our senses and bit our tongues;
my mother-in-law said: 'Daughter-in-law, tell no one of today's disgrace.'"

নরহরি কহে কেবা কি কহিবে তিনের দশা সমান ।
চুপ করি থাক যতনেতে ঢাক চুল দিয়া কাটা কাণ ॥

*narahari kahe kebā ki kahibe tinera daśā samāna |*
*cupa kari thāka yatanete ḍhāka cula diyā kāṭā kāṇa ||*

*Word for word:* narahari kahe — Narahari says; kebā ki kahibe — who will say what; tinera daśā samāna — the plight of the three is the same; cupa kari thāka — keep quiet; yatanete ḍhāka — carefully cover; cula diyā kāṭā kāṇa — the cut-off ear with your hair

**7.9.** Narahari says: who will say what? — the plight of all three is the same:
keep quiet and carefully cover the cut-off ear with your hair.[^30-20]

[^30-18]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — p. 198, no. 100 (scan PDF pp. 456–457); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 100 (catalogue: NG-338). **No witnesses.** GPT1 nos. 86–99
and 124–180 stand in the same order as the padas of Narahari Chakravarti's *Gaura-charita-chintamani* (GCC 7.2–7.16 and 7.29 onwards), so nos. 100–110
and 120–123, absent from the OCR text of GCC, were checked against the scan of GCC (ed. 1947; IA gaurcharitra-chintamani, the only available copy):
the scan (a 200-page PDF) **lacks printed pp. 81–88** — after p. 80 (PDF 85; end of GCC 7.16 = no. 99) comes p. 89 at once (PDF 86; beginning of GCC
7.29 = no. 124), and PDF pp. 94–98 repeat pp. 89–93. The lost pages held GCC 7.17–7.28 — 12 padas; in GPT this place holds 15 padas signed Narahari
(nos. 100–110, 120–123; between them — padas of Vasu, Lochana, Jnanadasa and no. 119 = GCC, kirana 2). Eight pages of GCC hold about 95 couplets of
the long metre, and the 15 GPT padas about 113; so most of them probably come from GCC, but all 15 cannot have stood there, and which ones did
cannot be established from the available sources. BR, *Gita-chandrodaya*, PK, KGC, PS, *Narottama-vilasa* — none of these padas. Hence nos. 100–110
and 120–123 are labelled "not established" (C), with a note on their probable origin in GCC. In tone — a rather coarse joke — this pada stands
out among the GCC padas. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^30-19]: 7.2–7.6: "intoxicated by Madana" (madane mātiyā) and the nakedness of the three women are as in the original; translated exactly, without
additions. It is a hyperbole of self-forgetfulness (in the *Bhagavata* the gopis running to Krishna put their clothes and ornaments on wrongly —
*Bhag.* 10.29), carried here to the point of a joke; the Lord merely passes by the house. The *Chaitanya-bhagavata* says plainly that in Navadvipa
the Lord did not look at women, and the Gaudiya tradition does not accept worship of Gaura in the nagari mood (introductory note, chapter 27); such
padas are a monument of late poetry, not an image of the Lord.
[^30-20]: "To cover the cut-off ear with one's hair" (cula diyā kāṭā kāṇa ḍhākā) — a proverb: to hide one's disgrace.

## 8. Narahari — "ki kaba sajani āṅgināra mājhe…" (GPT1 p. 199, no. 101)
*Nagari-bhava. A townswoman's story: hearing that Gora was approaching their house, she hastily finished the housework so as to go and look — but
her mother-in-law, guessing, shouted at her, and she could not take a single step. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: not established** — GPT only
(see n. 18).*[^30-21]

কি কব সজনি আঙ্গিনার মাঝে বসিয়া আছিনু মোরা ।
শুনিনু বাড়ীর নিকটে আইলা শচীর দুলাল গোরা ॥

*ki kaba sajani āṅgināra mājhe basiyā āchinu morā |*
*śuninu bāṛīra nikaṭe āilā śacīra dulāla gorā ||*

*Word for word:* ki kaba sajani — what shall I say, friend; āṅgināra mājhe — in the middle of the courtyard; basiyā āchinu morā — we were sitting; śuninu — we heard; bāṛīra nikaṭe āilā — is coming near the house; śacīra dulāla gorā — Gora, Shachi's son

**8.1.** "What shall I say, friend? We were sitting in the middle of the courtyard —
and we heard: Gora, Shachi's son, is coming near our house.

সেথা যাইবার তরে তরাতরি সারিনু ঘরের কাজ ।
অধিক আতুর হইনু তখন কিছু না রহিল লাজ ॥

*sethā yāibāra tare tarātari sārinu gharera kāja |*
*adhika ātura hainu takhana kichu nā rahila lāja ||*

*Word for word:* sethā yāibāra tare — to go there; tarātari sārinu — I hastily finished; gharera kāja — the housework; adhika ātura hainu — I was very impatient; takhana — then; kichu nā rahila lāja — no shame remained

**8.2.** To go there, I hastily finished the housework;
I was so impatient that no shame was left in me.

বুঝিয়া শাশুড়ী দিলেক দাবুড়ি ভয়েতে কাঁপিল গা ।
মাথায় ভাঙ্গিয়া বজর পড়িল বাড়াতে নারিনু পা ॥

*bujhiyā śāśuṛī dileka dābuṛi bhayete kām̐pila gā |*
*māthāya bhāṅgiyā bajara paṛila bāṛāte nārinu pā ||*

*Word for word:* bujhiyā śāśuṛī — guessing, my mother-in-law; dileka dābuṛi — shouted at me; bhayete kām̐pila gā — my body trembled with fear; māthāya bhāṅgiyā bajara paṛila — a thunderbolt crashed on my head; bāṛāte nārinu pā — I could not take a step

**8.3.** Guessing it, my mother-in-law shouted at me — my body trembled with fear;
it was as if a thunderbolt crashed on my head — I could not take a step.

কাতর হইয়া অমনি রহিনু মুখে না সরল কথা ।
নরহরি কহে শাশুড়ী থাকিতে না যাবে হিয়ার ব্যথা ॥

*kātara haiyā amani rahinu mukhe nā sarala kathā |*
*narahari kahe śāśuṛī thākite nā yābe hiyāra byathā ||*

*Word for word:* kātara haiyā — stricken with grief; amani rahinu — so I remained; mukhe nā sarala kathā — no word left my lips; narahari kahe — Narahari says; śāśuṛī thākite — while there is a mother-in-law; nā yābe hiyāra byathā — the pain of the heart will not go

**8.4.** So I remained, stricken with grief — no word would leave my lips."
Narahari says: while there is a mother-in-law, the pain of the heart will not go.

[^30-21]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — p. 199, no. 101 (scan PDF p. 458); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 101 (catalogue: NG-339). No witnesses; probably from the lost
pages of GCC (pp. 81–88), but this cannot be established (n. 18). C. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).

## 9. Narahari — "śuna śuna sai kālikāra kathā ki āra baliba tore…" (GPT1 p. 199, no. 102)
*Nagari-bhava. A townswoman's story: yesterday her mother-in-law was instructing her in the dharma of a noble wife — when a wondrous sound of kirtana
arose; hearing the mridangas, the mother-in-law became as if mad, dropped her work and called her daughter-in-law to come along; to her excuses she
replied: "Look but once on that moonlike face — and your life will not be in vain." Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: not established** — GPT only
(see n. 18).*[^30-22]

শুন শুন সই কালিকার কথা কি আর বলিব তোরে ।
কুলবতী সতী ধরম শাশুড়ী শিখাতে বলিল মোরে ॥

*śuna śuna sai kālikāra kathā ki āra baliba tore |*
*kulabatī satī dharama śāśuṛī śikhāte balila more ||*

*Word for word:* śuna śuna sai — listen, listen, friend; kālikāra kathā — about yesterday; ki āra baliba tore — what more shall I tell you; kulabatī satī dharama — the dharma of a noble faithful wife; śāśuṛī śikhāte balila more — my mother-in-law set about teaching me

**9.1.** "Listen, listen, friend, about yesterday — what more shall I tell you?
My mother-in-law set about teaching me the dharma of a noble, faithful wife.

হেনই সময়ে অতি অপরূপ উঠিল কীর্তনধ্বনি ।
পাগলীর পারা হইলা শাশুড়ী খোলের শবদ শুনি ॥

*henai samaye ati aparūpa uṭhila kīrtanadhvani |*
*pāgalīra pārā hailā śāśuṛī kholera śabada śuni ||*

*Word for word:* henai samaye — at that very moment; ati aparūpa — wondrous; uṭhila kīrtana-dhvani — a sound of kirtana arose; pāgalīra pārā hailā śāśuṛī — my mother-in-law became as if mad; kholera śabada śuni — hearing the voice of the mridanga (khol)

**9.2.** And at that very moment a wondrous sound of kirtana arose —
hearing the voice of the mridanga, my mother-in-law became as if mad.

ত্যজি নিজকাজ তরাতরি সেথা যাইতে অথির পথে ।
আতুর হইয়া মোর প্রতি বলে চলহ আমার সাথে ॥

*tyaji nijakāja tarātari sethā yāite athira pathe |*
*ātura haiyā mora prati bale calaha āmāra sāthe ||*

*Word for word:* tyaji nija-kāja — dropping her own work; tarātari sethā yāite — hurrying to go there; athira pathe — restless on the way; ātura haiyā — impatiently; mora prati bale — says to me; calaha āmāra sāthe — come with me

**9.3.** Dropping her own work, hurrying there, unable to keep still on the way,
she says to me impatiently: 'Come with me!'

মো পুনঃ কহিনু গৃহকাজ সব পড়িয়া আছয়ে এথা ।
আর তাহে মুই কুলবধূ বলি কিরূপে যাইব সেথা ॥

*mo punaḥ kahinu gṛhakāja saba paṛiyā āchaye ethā |*
*āra tāhe mui kulabadhū bali kirūpe yāiba sethā ||*

*Word for word:* mo punaḥ kahinu — but I said; gṛhakāja saba — all the housework; paṛiyā āchaye ethā — lies here undone; āra tāhe — and besides; mui kulabadhū bali — I being a wife of a noble family; kirūpe yāiba sethā — how shall I go there

**9.4.** But I told her: 'All the housework is lying here undone;
and besides, I am a wife of a noble family — how can I go there?'

এতেক শুনিয়া কহে গৃহকাজ করিয়া নিতুই মর ।
বারেক ও চাঁদবদন নিরখি জনম সফল কর ॥

*eteka śuniyā kahe gṛhakāja kariyā nitui mara |*
*bāreka o cām̐dabadana nirakhi janama saphala kara ||*

*Word for word:* eteka śuniyā kahe — hearing this, she says; gṛhakāja kariyā — doing the housework; nitui mara — you die every day; bāreka — but once; o cām̐da-badana nirakhi — looking on that moonlike face; janama saphala kara — make your birth fruitful

**9.5.** Hearing this, she says: 'Doing the housework, you die every day;
look but once on that moonlike face — and make your birth fruitful.'

ইহা শুনি সুখে তুরিতে যাইয়া দেখিনু নয়ান ভরি ।
নরহরি কহে তুয়া শাশুড়ীর বালাই লইয়া মরি ॥

*ihā śuni sukhe turite yāiyā dekhinu nayāna bhari |*
*narahari kahe tuyā śāśuṛīra bālāi laiyā mari ||*

*Word for word:* ihā śuni — hearing this; sukhe turite yāiyā — joyfully hurrying; dekhinu nayāna bhari — I gazed to my eyes' content; narahari kahe — Narahari says; tuyā śāśuṛīra bālāi laiyā mari — I take upon myself the ills of your mother-in-law

**9.6.** Hearing this, I joyfully hurried there and gazed to my eyes' content."
Narahari says: I take upon myself all the ills of your mother-in-law![^30-23]

[^30-22]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — p. 199, no. 102 (scan PDF p. 458); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 102 (catalogue: NG-340). No witnesses; probably from the lost
pages of GCC (n. 18). C. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^30-23]: The strict mother-in-law whom the sound of Gaura's kirtana makes "mad" is an image of the power of sankirtana, which even the elders of
Nadia could not resist (cf. *Chaitanya-bhagavata*, Madhya-khanda: the whole town gathers for the Lord's kirtana). Her words "make your birth
fruitful" are a call to the darshan of the Lord; the poet's praise is a formula of fond admiration (bālāi laiyā, cf. n. 43 of chapter 29).

## 10. Narahari — "śuna śuna sai dibā abasāne…" (GPT1 pp. 199–200, no. 103)
*Nagari-bhava. A townswoman's story: at the close of day, hearing that Gaura was coming, she joyfully went out of the gate — and, as ill luck would
have it, ran into her father-in-law there; he heaped abuse on her and in anger threatened to leave Nadia; at these words her heart sank. The poet's
consolation: who can leave Nadia? Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: not established** — GPT only (see n. 18).*[^30-24]

শুন শুন সই দিবা অবসানে অধিক সানন্দ হৈয়া ।
গৌরগমন শুনিয়া বাহির দুয়ারে দাঁড়ানু গিয়া ॥

*śuna śuna sai dibā abasāne adhika sānanda haiyā |*
*gauragamana śuniyā bāhira duyāre dām̐ṛānu giyā ||*

*Word for word:* śuna śuna sai — listen, listen, friend; dibā abasāne — at the close of day; adhika sānanda haiyā — full of joy; gaura-gamana śuniyā — hearing that Gaura was coming; bāhira duyāre dām̐ṛānu giyā — I went and stood by the gate

**10.1.** "Listen, listen, friend: at the close of day, full of joy,
hearing that Gaura was coming, I went out and stood by the gate.

বিধি বিড়ম্বিল তথা সে শ্বশুর সহিত হইল দেখা ।
কহিল যতেক কটুবাণী ও গো নাহিক তাহার লেখা ॥

*bidhi biṛambila tathā se śvaśura sahita haila dekhā |*
*kahila yateka kaṭubāṇī o go nāhika tāhāra lekhā ||*

*Word for word:* bidhi biṛambila — the Creator mocked me; tathā — there; se śvaśura sahita haila dekhā — I ran into my father-in-law; kahila yateka kaṭu-bāṇī — all the harsh words he said; o go — friend; nāhika tāhāra lekhā — there is no counting them

**10.2.** The Creator mocked me: there I ran into my father-in-law;
how many harsh words he said to me, friend — there is no counting them.

অধিক কোরধে কহয়ে এখন ছাড়িব নদ্যার বাস ।
সে কথা শুনিয়া পরাণ উড়িল মিটিল সকল আশ ॥

*adhika koradhe kahaye ekhana chāṛiba nadyāra bāsa |*
*se kathā śuniyā parāṇa uṛila miṭila sakala āśa ||*

*Word for word:* adhika koradhe kahaye — in great anger he says; ekhana chāṛiba nadyāra bāsa — now I will leave my home in Nadia; se kathā śuniyā — hearing this; parāṇa uṛila — my heart stood still; miṭila sakala āśa — all hopes were gone

**10.3.** In great anger he says: 'I will leave Nadia and live elsewhere — this very day!'
Hearing this, my heart stood still — all my hopes were gone.

কাতর হইয়া রহিনু ব্যথিত কে আছে বুঝাতে পারে ।
নরহরি কহে কিসের ভাবনা নদ্যা কে ছাড়িতে পারে ॥

*kātara haiyā rahinu byathita ke āche bujhāte pāre |*
*narahari kahe kisera bhābanā nadyā ke chāṛite pāre ||*

*Word for word:* kātara haiyā rahinu — I remained stricken with grief; byathita — pained; ke āche bujhāte pāre — who could console me; narahari kahe — Narahari says; kisera bhābanā — why worry; nadyā ke chāṛite pāre — who is able to leave Nadia

**10.4.** So I remained, stricken with grief — who could console me?"
Narahari says: why worry? Who is able to leave Nadia?[^30-25]

[^30-24]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — pp. 199–200, no. 103 (scan PDF pp. 458–459); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 103 (catalogue: NG-341). No witnesses; probably from
the lost pages of GCC (n. 18). C. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^30-25]: The poet's consolation means: no one will leave Nadia, where Gaura is (cf. no. 13: the father-in-law, on seeing Gaura, himself dances with
arms upraised). Translated literally.

## 11. Narahari — "śuna śuna ago mane chila āśā…" (GPT1 p. 200, no. 104)
*Nagari-bhava. A townswoman's story: she had hoped to live in happiness, but the Creator settled her in a thicket of thorns: her father-in-law
coaches her kind mother-in-law — "Nimai's mridanga will soon sound to drive Nadia mad, and the young wives will run, heeding no one; go quickly and
bolt the door from outside"; how is she to see Him now? Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: not established** — GPT only (see n. 18).*[^30-26]

শুন শুন অগো মনে ছিল আশা রহিব পরম সুখে ।
কণ্টকের বনে বিহি বসাইল সতত মরি এ দুখে ॥

*śuna śuna ago mane chila āśā rahiba parama sukhe |*
*kaṇṭakera bane bihi basāila satata mari e dukhe ||*

*Word for word:* śuna śuna ago — listen, listen, friend; mane chila āśā — I had a hope; rahiba parama sukhe — to live in great happiness; kaṇṭakera bane — in a forest of thorns; bihi basāila — the Creator settled me; satata mari e dukhe — I am forever dying of this sorrow

**11.1.** "Listen, listen, friend: I had a hope — to live in great happiness,
but the Creator has settled me in a forest of thorns — I am forever dying of this sorrow.

আমার শ্বশুর গুণের ঠাকুর সে দেয় অধিক ব্যথা ।
শাশুড়ী মোর অতি সুজন তারে শিখায় কঠিন কথা ॥

*āmāra śvaśura guṇera ṭhākura se deya adhika byathā |*
*śāśuṛī mora ati sujana tāre śikhāya kaṭhina kathā ||*

*Word for word:* āmāra śvaśura — my father-in-law; guṇera ṭhākura — a "lord of virtues"; se deya adhika byathā — gives much pain; śāśuṛī mora ati sujana — my mother-in-law is very kind; tāre śikhāya kaṭhina kathā — he teaches her harsh words

**11.2.** My father-in-law — a 'lord of virtues' — gives me much pain;
my mother-in-law is very kind, but he teaches her harsh words.

নিভৃতে বসিয়া ধীরে ধীরে কহে ঘরেতে থাকত তুমি ।
সেখানে যাইয়া কাজ সমাধিয়ে তুরিতে আসিব আমি ॥

*nibhṛte basiyā dhīre dhīre kahe gharete thākata tumi |*
*sekhāne yāiyā kāja samādhiye turite āsiba āmi ||*

*Word for word:* nibhṛte basiyā — sitting in private; dhīre dhīre kahe — says softly; gharete thākata tumi — you stay at home; sekhāne yāiyā — going there; kāja samādhiye — settling the matter; turite āsiba āmi — I will come back quickly

**11.3.** Sitting in private, he says to her softly: 'You stay at home,
and I will go there, settle the matter and come back quickly.

নদীয়া পাগল করিতে এখনি বাজিবে নিমাইর খোল ।
বধূগণ যাবে ধাইয়া কেহ না মানিব কাহার বোল ॥

*nadīyā pāgala karite ekhani bājibe nimāira khola |*
*badhūgaṇa yābe dhāiyā keha nā māniba kāhāra bola ||*

*Word for word:* nadīyā pāgala karite — to drive Nadia mad; ekhani bājibe — will sound at once; nimāira khola — Nimai's mridanga (khol); badhūgaṇa yābe dhāiyā — the young wives will run; keha nā mānibe kāhāra bola — no one will heed anyone's word

**11.4.** Soon Nimai's mridanga will sound to drive Nadia mad —
the young wives will run there, no one will heed anyone.

তাহাতে বাড়ীর বাহিরে কপাট দেওল তুরিতে যাঞা ।
এইরূপ কত কহয়ে আমরা শুনিয়া লজ্জিত হৈঞা ॥

*tāhāte bāṛīra bāhire kapāṭa deola turite yāñā |*
*eirūpa kata kahaye āmarā śuniyā lajjita haiñā ||*

*Word for word:* tāhāte — so; bāṛīra bāhire kapāṭa deola — bolt the door of the house from outside; turite yāñā — going quickly; eirūpa kata kahaye — much of this kind he says; āmarā śuniyā — we, hearing; lajjita haiñā — are ashamed

**11.5.** So go quickly and bolt the door of the house from outside.'
Much of this kind he says, and we hear it — and we are ashamed.

ইহাতে কিরূপে দেখিব তাহারে বিষম হইল ঘর ।
নরহরি কহে যেজন চতুর তার কি ইহাতে ডর ॥

*ihāte kirūpe dekhiba tāhāre biṣama haila ghara |*
*narahari kahe yejana catura tāra ki ihāte ḍara ||*

*Word for word:* ihāte — in this; kirūpe dekhiba tāhāre — how shall I see Him; biṣama haila ghara — the house has become unbearable; narahari kahe — Narahari says; yejana catura — one who is clever; tāra ki ihāte ḍara — would that frighten her

**11.6.** How then am I to see Him? The house has become unbearable."
Narahari says: one who is clever — would that frighten her?[^30-27]

[^30-26]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — p. 200, no. 104 (scan PDF p. 459); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 104 (catalogue: NG-091). No witnesses; probably from the lost
pages of GCC (n. 18). C. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^30-27]: The father-in-law calls the Lord by His household name — "Nimai" (nimāi); his fear of the kirtana that "drives Nadia mad" is an admission
of the power of sankirtana (cf. nos. 9 and 13). The poet's consolation is the same convention of the purvaraga padas as the praise of the
townswomen's tricks (n. 7).

## 12. Narahari — "dukhera kāhinī ki kaba sajani…" (GPT1 pp. 200–201, no. 105)
*Nagari-bhava. A townswoman's story: she burns in the taunts of the neighbours; her friend knows about her mother-in-law and sister-in-law, while her
father-in-law — a hunchbacked old man who can hardly walk — prays to Shiva with offerings that the young wives may not leave the house; and when Gaura
begins kirtana, the old man, hearing the mridangas, looks about in alarm, abuses everyone and sets a guard at the gate. The poet: who will forbid going
by the back gate? Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: not established** — GPT only (see n. 18).*[^30-28]

দুখের কাহিনী কি কব সজনি আর না সহিতে পারি ।
পাড়া পড়সীর গঞ্জন-আনল তাহাতে পুড়িয়া মরি ॥

*dukhera kāhinī ki kaba sajani āra nā sahite pāri |*
*pāṛā paṛasīra gañjana-ānala tāhāte puṛiyā mari ||*

*Word for word:* dukhera kāhinī — the tale of woes; ki kaba sajani — what shall I tell, friend; āra nā sahite pāri — I can bear it no longer; pāṛā paṛasīra — of the neighbours; gañjana-ānala — the fire of taunts; tāhāte puṛiyā mari — I burn in it

**12.1.** "What shall I tell of my woes, friend? I can bear it no longer:
I burn in the fire of the neighbours' taunts.

শাশুড়ী ননদ যেরূপ আমারে তাহা কি না জান সই ।
শ্বশুরের গুণ কহিতে না হয় তখনি তোমারে কই ॥

*śāśuṛī nanada yerūpa āmāre tāhā ki nā jāna sai |*
*śvaśurera guṇa kahite nā haya takhani tomāre kai ||*

*Word for word:* śāśuṛī nanada — mother-in-law and sister-in-law; yerūpa āmāre — how they treat me; tāhā ki nā jāna sai — do you not know, friend; śvaśurera guṇa — the father-in-law's "virtues"; kahite nā haya — it is not fit to tell; takhani tomāre kai — yet I tell you

**12.2.** How my mother-in-law and sister-in-law treat me — do you not know, friend?
Of my father-in-law's 'virtues' it is not fit to speak — and yet I will tell you.

ঘরে বসি থাকে চলিতে শকতি নাহিক নিপট কুঁজা ।
নানা দ্রব্য লৈঞা বিবিধ বিধানে করয়ে শিবের পূজা ॥

*ghare basi thāke calite śakati nāhika nipaṭa kum̐jā |*
*nānā drabya laiñā bibidha bidhāne karaye śibera pūjā ||*

*Word for word:* ghare basi thāke — he sits at home; calite śakati nāhika — no strength to walk; nipaṭa kum̐jā — quite hunchbacked; nānā drabya laiñā — taking various things; bibidha bidhāne — in every manner; karaye śibera pūjā — performs puja to Shiva

**12.3.** He sits at home — he has no strength even to walk, quite bent double —
and, gathering all sorts of things, he performs puja to Shiva in every manner.

গলায় বসন দিয়া দুই কর যুড়িয়া মাগয়ে বর ।
থির হৈয়া রহে বধূগণ যেন তিলেক না ছাড়ে ঘর ॥

*galāya basana diyā dui kara yuṛiyā māgaye bara |*
*thira haiyā rahe badhūgaṇa yena tileka nā chāṛe ghara ||*

*Word for word:* galāya basana diyā — winding his cloth round his neck; dui kara yuṛiyā — joining both palms; māgaye bara — he begs a boon; thira haiyā rahe badhūgaṇa — may the young wives keep still; yena tileka nā chāṛe ghara — that they may not leave the house for a moment

**12.4.** With his cloth wound round his neck and both palms joined, he begs a boon:
'May the young wives keep still and not leave the house for a moment!'[^30-29]

এইরূপ কত প্রার্থনা করিয়া সাধয়ে আপন কাজ ।
আড়ালে থাকিয়া শুনিএ সে সব পাইয়া অধিক লাজ ॥

*eirūpa kata prārthanā kariyā sādhaye āpana kāja |*
*āṛāle thākiyā śunie se saba pāiyā adhika lāja ||*

*Word for word:* eirūpa kata prārthanā kariyā — making many such prayers; sādhaye āpana kāja — he gets his way; āṛāle thākiyā — standing behind the screen; śunie se saba — I hear all this; pāiyā adhika lāja — feeling deep shame

**12.5.** Thus, with many prayers, he gets his way;
and I, standing behind the screen, hear it all — and am deeply ashamed.

আর শুন যেই সময়ে কীর্তন করয়ে গুণের মণি ।
সে সময় বুড়া অতি সচকিত খোলের শবদ শুনি ॥

*āra śuna yei samaye kīrtana karaye guṇera maṇi |*
*se samaya buṛā ati sacakita kholera śabada śuni ||*

*Word for word:* āra śuna — listen further; yei samaye — whenever; kīrtana karaye — begins kirtana; guṇera maṇi — the Jewel of virtues; se samaya buṛā — then the old man; ati sacakita — is all alarm; kholera śabada śuni — hearing the voice of the mridanga

**12.6.** And listen further: whenever the Jewel of virtues begins kirtana,
the old man, hearing the voice of the mridanga, is all alarm;

ডাগর নয়ানে চাহে চারি পানে দেখিতে লাগয়ে ভয় ।
বিকট বদন করিয়া সবারে কঠোর বচন কয় ॥

*ḍāgara nayāne cāhe cāri pāne dekhite lāgaye bhaya |*
*bikaṭa badana kariyā sabāre kaṭhora bacana kaya ||*

*Word for word:* ḍāgara nayāne — with eyes wide open; cāhe cāri pāne — looks on every side; dekhite lāgaye bhaya — it is frightful to see; bikaṭa badana kariyā — twisting his face; sabāre kaṭhora bacana kaya — speaks harsh words to all

**12.7.** with eyes wide open he looks on every side — it is frightful to see —
and, twisting his face, speaks harsh words to everyone.

আমাদের গতি বুঝিয়া সে করে বাহির দুয়ারে থানা ।
নরহরি কহে খিড়কির পথে যাইতে কে করে মানা ॥

*āmādera gati bujhiyā se kare bāhira duyāre thānā |*
*narahari kahe khiṛakira pathe yāite ke kare mānā ||*

*Word for word:* āmādera gati bujhiyā — guessing our intentions; se kare bāhira duyāre thānā — he sets a guard at the gate; narahari kahe — Narahari says; khiṛakira pathe yāite — going by the back gate; ke kare mānā — who forbids

**12.8.** Guessing our intentions, he sets a guard at the gate."
Narahari says: but who forbids going by the back gate?

[^30-28]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — pp. 200–201, no. 105 (scan PDF pp. 459–460); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 105 (catalogue: NG-092). No witnesses; probably from
the lost pages of GCC (n. 18). C. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^30-29]: A cloth wound round the neck and joined palms are a gesture of abject supplication. The old man prays to Shiva for a worldly end — that his
daughters-in-law stay at home; the poet sets his prayer against Gaura's kirtana (12.6), but does not disparage the worship of Shiva.

## 13. Narahari — "śuna go sajani śvaśurera kichu caritra…" (GPT1 p. 201, no. 106)
*Nagari-bhava. A townswoman's story: her father-in-law instructed her at length and made her swear to guard the family's honour; but no sooner had
she sworn than the sound of the mridanga reached her — and she ran to where Gauranga was. The father-in-law chased her in a rage with a club — but,
glancing angrily at Gaurangachand, he could not take his eyes away, was caught in the net of prema, threw down the club and, raising his arms with
cries of "Hari, Hari!", broke into dance; afterwards he praised his daughter-in-law and himself begged her pardon. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution:
not established** — GPT only (see n. 18).*[^30-30]

শুন গো সজনি শ্বশুরের কিছু চরিত্র কহিয়ে তোরে ।
বিরলে অনেক বুঝাইয়া পুনঃ যতনে কহয়ে মোরে ॥

*śuna go sajani śvaśurera kichu caritra kahiye tore |*
*birale aneka bujhāiyā punaḥ yatane kahaye more ||*

*Word for word:* śuna go sajani — listen, friend; śvaśurera kichu caritra — something of my father-in-law's ways; kahiye tore — I tell you; birale aneka bujhāiyā — instructing me at length in private; punaḥ yatane kahaye more — then says to me earnestly

**13.1.** "Listen, friend, I will tell you something of my father-in-law's ways:
in private he instructed me at length, and then he says to me earnestly:

এক মোর বহু ভ্রম আর তুমি ভাল মানুষের ঝী ।
চরণ ছুঁইয়া বলহ দুদিগ রাখিব না হ'লে কি ॥

*eka mora bahu bhrama āra tumi bhāla mānuṣera jhī |*
*caraṇa chum̐iyā balaha dudiga rākhiba nā ha'le ki ||*

*Word for word:* eka mora bahu bhrama — one thing troubles me greatly (?); āra tumi bhāla mānuṣera jhī — and you are the daughter of good people; caraṇa chum̐iyā — touching my feet; balaha — swear; dudiga rākhiba — I will guard both families; nā ha'le ki — otherwise what

**13.2.** 'One thing troubles me greatly; and you are the daughter of good people:
touch my feet and swear that you will guard the honour of both families — otherwise what will become of us?'[^30-31]

এত শুনি কত শপথ খাইয়া ঘুচাইনু তার দ্বিধা ।
হেন কালে মোর শ্রবণে পশিল মৃদঙ্গ-শবদ-সুধা ॥

*eta śuni kata śapatha khāiyā ghucāinu tāra dvidhā |*
*hena kāle mora śrabaṇe paśila mṛdaṅga-śabada-sudhā ||*

*Word for word:* eta śuni — hearing this; kata śapatha khāiyā — swearing many oaths; ghucāinu tāra dvidhā — I dispelled his doubts; hena kāle — just then; mora śrabaṇe paśila — entered my ears; mṛdaṅga-śabada-sudhā — the nectar of the mridanga's sound

**13.3.** Hearing this, I swore many oaths and dispelled his doubts —
and just then the nectar of the mridanga's sound entered my ears.

অমনি ধাইয়া চলিনু যেখানে বিলসে গৌরাঙ্গরায় ।
মোর এ চরিত শুনিয়া শ্বশুর হইলা আনলপ্রায় ॥

*amani dhāiyā calinu yekhāne bilase gaurāṅgarāya |*
*mora e carita śuniyā śvaśura hailā ānalaprāya ||*

*Word for word:* amani dhāiyā calinu — at once I ran off; yekhāne bilase gaurāṅgarāya — to where Gauranga Raya disports Himself; mora e carita śuniyā — hearing of this deed of mine; śvaśura hailā ānalaprāya — my father-in-law became like fire

**13.4.** At once I ran off to where Gauranga Raya disports Himself;
learning of this deed of mine, my father-in-law became like fire.

মোর পাছে পাছে ধাইয়া আইলা বিষম লগুড় লৈয়া ।
কি করিব মোর পরাণ উড়িল শ্বশুরের পানে চাঞা ॥

*mora pāche pāche dhāiyā āilā biṣama laguṛa laiyā |*
*ki kariba mora parāṇa uṛila śvaśurera pāne cāñā ||*

*Word for word:* mora pāche pāche dhāiyā āilā — came running after me; biṣama laguṛa laiyā — seizing a fearsome club; ki kariba — what could I do; mora parāṇa uṛila — my heart stood still; śvaśurera pāne cāñā — looking at my father-in-law

**13.5.** He came running after me, seizing a fearsome club —
what could I do? — looking at my father-in-law, my heart stood still.

কোরধ-নয়ানে সে পুনঃ বারেক হেরিল গৌরাঙ্গচাঁদে ।
আঁখি ফিরাইতে নারিল অমনি পড়িল প্রেমের ফাঁদে ॥

*koradha-nayāne se punaḥ bāreka herila gaurāṅgacām̐de |*
*ām̐khi phirāite nārila amani paṛila premera phām̐de ||*

*Word for word:* koradha-nayāne — with angry eyes; se punaḥ bāreka herila — he glanced just once; gaurāṅgacām̐de — at Gaurangachand; ām̐khi phirāite nārila — could not turn his eyes away; amani paṛila premera phām̐de — at once fell into the net of prema

**13.6.** But with angry eyes he glanced just once at Gaurangachand —
and could not turn his eyes away: at once he fell into the net of prema.

পরম হরষ হইয়া হাতের লগুড় ফেলাঞা দিলা ।
হরি হরি বলি তুলিয়া দুবাহু নাচিয়া বিহ্বল হৈলা ॥

*parama haraṣa haiyā hātera laguṛa phelāñā dilā |*
*hari hari bali tuliyā dubāhu nāciyā bihvala hailā ||*

*Word for word:* parama haraṣa haiyā — in supreme joy; hātera laguṛa phelāñā dilā — flung away the club from his hand; hari hari bali — crying "Hari, Hari"; tuliyā dubāhu — raising both arms; nāciyā bihvala hailā — danced beside himself

**13.7.** In supreme joy he flung away the club from his hand
and, raising both arms and crying 'Hari, Hari!', he danced beside himself.

এইরূপ কত কৌতুক দেখিয়া মো পুনঃ চলিনু ঘরে ।
কতক্ষণে তেঁহ যাইয়া কতেক প্রশংসা করিল মোরে ॥

*eirūpa kata kautuka dekhiyā mo punaḥ calinu ghare |*
*katakṣaṇe tem̐ha yāiyā kateka praśaṃsā karila more ||*

*Word for word:* eirūpa kata kautuka dekhiyā — having seen many such wonders; mo punaḥ calinu ghare — I went back home; katakṣaṇe — after a while; teṃha yāiyā — he, coming; kateka praśaṃsā karila more — praised me at length

**13.8.** Having seen many such wonders, I went back home;
after a while he too came and praised me at length.

মোর করে ধরি আপনার দোষ কহিতে আতুর হৈলা ।
দেখি বেয়াকুল চরণ বন্দিনু তাহাতে আনন্দ পাইলা ॥

*mora kare dhari āpanāra doṣa kahite ātura hailā |*
*dekhi beyākula caraṇa bandinu tāhāte ānanda pāilā ||*

*Word for word:* mora kare dhari — taking my hand; āpanāra doṣa kahite — confessing his fault; ātura hailā — he grew anxious; dekhi beyākula — seeing him distressed; caraṇa bandinu — I bowed to his feet; tāhāte ānanda pāilā — that made him glad

**13.9.** Taking my hand, he anxiously began to confess his fault;
seeing him so distressed, I bowed to his feet — and that made him glad."

নরহরি কহে এতদিনে যেন সকল সঙ্কোচ গেল ।
তুয়া কৃপাবলে বুড়ার বিষম হৃদয় হইল ভাল ॥

*narahari kahe etadine yena sakala saṅkoca gela |*
*tuyā kṛpābale buṛāra biṣama hṛdaya haila bhāla ||*

*Word for word:* narahari kahe — Narahari says; etadine — at last; yena sakala saṅkoca gela — all awkwardness is gone; tuyā kṛpā-bale — by your grace; buṛāra biṣama hṛdaya — the old man's hard heart; haila bhāla — has become good

**13.10.** Narahari says: now at last all awkwardness is gone;
by your grace the old man's hard heart has become good.[^30-32]

[^30-30]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — p. 201, no. 106 (scan PDF p. 460); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 106 (catalogue: NG-093). No witnesses; probably from the lost
pages of GCC (n. 18). C. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^30-31]: 13.2: "one thing troubles me greatly" (eka mora bahu bhrama; so GPT1 and GPT2) — the sense of the opening words is unclear; "both families"
(dudiga) — the father's family and the husband's.
[^30-32]: 13.6–13.7: the father-in-law who rushes at his daughter-in-law with a club and, at the sight of Gaura, breaks into dance crying "Hari!" is an
image of the transforming power of the Lord's darshan and of sankirtana; cf. the conversion of the opponents of kirtana in the
*Chaitanya-bhagavata* (Madhya-khanda). "By your grace" (tuyā kṛpābale) — in the signatures of these padas the poet addresses the heroine; the words
can also be taken as addressed to Gaura.

## 14. Narahari — "rajanī dibasa kakhana svapane…" (GPT1 pp. 201–202, no. 107)
*Nagari-bhava. A townswoman's complaint: all her friends' hopes have been fulfilled, but she is "a wife in the corner": her mother-in-law abuses her
whenever she steps over the threshold, and to the ghat of the Suradhuni she is accompanied by her watchful sister-in-law, so that she dares not
even lift her veil. The poet advises her to outwit the wily one. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: not established** — GPT only (see n. 18).*[^30-33]

রজনী দিবস কখন স্বপনে না জানি সুখের লেশ ।
ভাবিতে ভাবিতে হিয়া জর জর শরীর হইল শেষ ॥

*rajanī dibasa kakhana svapane nā jāni sukhera leśa |*
*bhābite bhābite hiyā jara jara śarīra haila śeṣa ||*

*Word for word:* rajanī dibasa — night and day; kakhana svapane — even in dreams; nā jāni sukhera leśa — I know no trace of happiness; bhābite bhābite — with longing; hiyā jara jara — the heart is worn out; śarīra haila śeṣa — the body is wasted away

**14.1.** "Neither by day nor by night, nor even in dreams, do I know a trace of happiness;
my heart is worn out with longing, my body wasted away.

যদি বল আশা পূরিল সবার কি লাগি তোমার নহ ।
সে কথা কি কব করমের দোষে হৈয়াছি কোণের বহু ॥

*yadi bala āśā pūrila sabāra ki lāgi tomāra naha |*
*se kathā ki kaba karamera doṣe haiyāchi koṇera bahu ||*

*Word for word:* yadi bala — if you say; āśā pūrila sabāra — everyone's hopes were fulfilled; ki lāgi tomāra naha — why not yours; se kathā ki kaba — what shall I say; karamera doṣe — through the fault of karma; haiyāchi koṇera bahu — I have become a wife in the corner

**14.2.** You will say: everyone's hopes have been fulfilled — why not yours?
What shall I say? Through the fault of my karma I have become a wife who sits in the corner.

বাড়ীর বাহির যাইতে শাশুড়ী পাড়য়ে কতেক গালি ।
সতী অসতী পতিমতিহীন সে দেখে চোকের বালি ॥

*bāṛīra bāhira yāite śāśuṛī pāṛaye kateka gāli |*
*satī asatī patimatihīna se dekhe cokera bāli ||*

*Word for word:* bāṛīra bāhira yāite — if I step outside the house; śāśuṛī pāṛaye kateka gāli — my mother-in-law heaps abuse; satī asatī — faithful? unfaithful; pati-mati-hīna — no thought for your husband; se dekhe cokera bāli — she sees me as grit in her eye

**14.3.** If I step outside the house, my mother-in-law heaps abuse on me:
'Faithful? Unfaithful! No thought for your husband!' — I am a speck of grit in her eye.

যদি কোন দিন সুরধুনীঘাটে যাইয়া সিনান কালে ।
আনেরে না করে প্রতীত দারুণ ননদী সঙ্গেতে চলে ॥

*yadi kona dina suradhunīghāṭe yāiyā sināna kāle |*
*ānere nā kare pratīta dāruṇa nanadī saṅgete cale ||*

*Word for word:* yadi kona dina — if some day; suradhunī-ghāṭe yāiyā — going to the ghat of the Suradhuni; sināna kāle — at bathing time; ānere nā kare pratīta — trusting no one else; dāruṇa nanadī — the relentless sister-in-law; saṅgete cale — goes along with me

**14.4.** And if some day I go to the ghat of the Suradhuni to bathe —
trusting no one else, my relentless sister-in-law goes along with me.

কোন ছলে যদি কাহাকে বারেক দেখিতে বাসনা করি ।
বিকট দপটে কাঁপে তনু ঘন ঘুঙট ঘুচাইতে নারি ॥

*kona chale yadi kāhāke bāreka dekhite bāsanā kari |*
*bikaṭa dapaṭe kām̐pe tanu ghana ghuṅaṭa ghucāite nāri ||*

*Word for word:* kona chale — on some pretext; yadi kāhāke bāreka — if Someone just once; dekhite bāsanā kari — I wish to see; bikaṭa dapaṭe — at her fierceness; kām̐pe tanu — my body trembles; ghana ghuṅaṭa ghucāite nāri — I dare not lift the thick veil

**14.5.** If on some pretext I wish to see Someone just once,
at her fierceness my body trembles — I dare not lift my thick veil.

সে অতি চতুরা তার কাছে ছল করিতে লাগয়ে ডর ।
পরাণ কেমন করয়ে অমনি সিনাঞা আসিয়ে ঘর ॥

*se ati caturā tāra kāche chala karite lāgaye ḍara |*
*parāṇa kemana karaye amani sināñā āsiye ghara ||*

*Word for word:* se ati caturā — she is very cunning; tāra kāche chala karite — to play tricks before her; lāgaye ḍara — is frightening; parāṇa kemana karaye — my heart is ill at ease; amani sināñā āsiye ghara — so, having bathed, I come home

**14.6.** She is very cunning, and to play tricks before her is frightening;
my heart is ill at ease — so, having bathed, I come straight home."

নরহরি কহে তু বড় আজুলি ননদীরে কিবা ভয় ।
চোরের উপরে করি বাটপাড়ি চোকে ধূলা দিতে হয় ॥

*narahari kahe tu baṛa ājuli nanadīre kibā bhaya |*
*corera upare kari bāṭapāṛi coke dhūlā dite haya ||*

*Word for word:* narahari kahe — Narahari says; tu baṛa ājuli — you are a great simpleton; nanadīre kibā bhaya — why fear your sister-in-law; corera upare kari bāṭapāṛi — robbing the thief; coke dhūlā dite haya — one must throw dust in the eyes

**14.7.** Narahari says: you, little friend, are a simpleton — why fear your sister-in-law?
To rob a thief you must throw dust in his eyes.[^30-34]

[^30-33]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — pp. 201–202, no. 107 (scan PDF pp. 460–461); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 107 (catalogue: NG-094). No witnesses; probably from
the lost pages of GCC (n. 18). C. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^30-34]: "Someone" (kāhāke) — a bashful withholding of Gaura's name. "Little friend" (ājuli) — here, from the sense, "simpleton" (cf. n. 7 of
chapter 29: the exact meaning of the word is not established). "To rob a thief you must throw dust in his eyes" — a proverb (lit. "doing highway
robbery upon a thief, one must throw dust in his eyes"). The advice to outwit the elders is a poetic convention (n. 7).

## 15. Narahari — "ki kaba sajani manera bedana kalaṅke pūrila deśa…" (GPT1 p. 202, no. 108)
*Nagari-bhava. A townswoman's complaint: the whole neighbourhood is full of gossip about her, though she is in no way to blame — she has only heard
Gauranga's name from people, has never seen Him, and He does not know her; the neighbours sing of her "disgrace", for in youth every woman is to
blame. The poet does not believe her: there is no smoke without fire. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: not established** — GPT only (see n. 18).*[^30-35]

কি কব সজনি মনের বেদন কলঙ্কে পূরিল দেশ ।
যদিও আমার কোন পরকারে নাহি কিছু দোষলেশ ॥

*ki kaba sajani manera bedana kalaṅke pūrila deśa |*
*yadio āmāra kona parakāre nāhi kichu doṣaleśa ||*

*Word for word:* ki kaba sajani — what shall I say, friend; manera bedana — of the pain of my heart; kalaṅke pūrila deśa — the land is full of scandal; yadio āmāra — though in me; kona parakāre — in any way; nāhi kichu doṣa-leśa — there is not a trace of fault

**15.1.** "What shall I say, friend, of the pain of my heart? The whole neighbourhood is full of talk about me,
though I am in no way to blame — not a trace of fault.

গৌরাঙ্গ গৌরাঙ্গ শুনি লোক মুখে না জানি কিরূপ সে ।
আমি কুলবধূ গৃহকোণে থাকি আমারে না জানে কে ॥

*gaurāṅga gaurāṅga śuni loka mukhe nā jāni kirūpa se |*
*āmi kulabadhū gṛhakoṇe thāki āmāre nā jāne ke ||*

*Word for word:* gaurāṅga gaurāṅga śuni — I hear "Gauranga, Gauranga"; loka mukhe — from people's lips; nā jāni kirūpa se — I do not know what He is like; āmi kulabadhū — I am a wife of a noble family; gṛha-koṇe thāki — I stay in a corner of the house; āmāre nā jāne ke — who does not know me

**15.2.** 'Gauranga, Gauranga' — I hear from people's lips, but what He is like I do not know;
I am a wife of a noble family, I sit in a corner of the house — who does not know me?

গৌরাঙ্গসুন্দর কিরূপ কখন না দেখি নয়ানকোণে ।
শপথ খাইয়া নিবেদি তোমারে সে নাহি আমারে চিনে ॥

*gaurāṅgasundara kirūpa kakhana nā dekhi nayānakoṇe |*
*śapatha khāiyā nibedi tomāre se nāhi āmāre cine ||*

*Word for word:* gaurāṅgasundara kirūpa — what beautiful Gauranga is like; kakhana nā dekhi — I have never seen; nayāna-koṇe — from the corner of my eye; śapatha khāiyā — swearing; nibedi tomāre — I tell you; se nāhi āmāre cine — He does not know me

**15.3.** What beautiful Gauranga is like I have never seen, even from the corner of my eye;
I swear to you, I tell you truly: He does not even know me.

মরমে মরিয়া থাকিয়ে কখন না যাই পরের ঘরে ।
তথাপি এ পাড়া-পড়সী আমার কলঙ্ক গাইয়া মরে ॥

*marame mariyā thākiye kakhana nā yāi parera ghare |*
*tathāpi e pāṛā-paṛasī āmāra kalaṅka gāiyā mare ||*

*Word for word:* marame mariyā thākiye — I stay dying of shame; kakhana nā yāi parera ghare — I never go to others' houses; tathāpi — still; e pāṛā-paṛasī — these neighbours; āmāra kalaṅka gāiyā mare — wear themselves out singing of my disgrace

**15.4.** Dying of shame, I stay at home — I never go to other people's houses;
and still these neighbours of ours sing on and on of my disgrace.

মিছা অপবাদ শুনিতে শুনিতে জ্বলয়ে দ্বিগুণ আগি ।
কারে কি কহিব যুবক সময় কেবল দোষের ভাগী ॥

*michā apabāda śunite śunite jvalaye dviguṇa āgi |*
*kāre ki kahiba yubaka samaya kebala doṣera bhāgī ||*

*Word for word:* michā apabāda — empty slander; śunite śunite — hearing and hearing; jvalaye dviguṇa āgi — the fire burns twofold; kāre ki kahiba — what shall I say, and to whom; yubaka samaya — in youth; kebala doṣera bhāgī — one is only there to take the blame

**15.5.** Hearing and hearing empty slander, I burn twice over —
what can I say, and to whom? In youth one is just there to take the blame."

নরহরি কহে যে বল সে বল একথা কাণে না ধরে ।
কিছু না থাকিলে মিছামিছি কেহ কারে কি কহিতে পারে ॥

*narahari kahe ye bala se bala ekathā kāṇe nā dhare |*
*kichu nā thākile michāmichi keha kāre ki kahite pāre ||*

*Word for word:* narahari kahe — Narahari says; ye bala se bala — say what you will; ekathā kāṇe nā dhare — the ear does not hold it true; kichu nā thākile — if there were nothing; michāmichi — for no reason; keha kāre ki kahite pāre — could anyone speak of another

**15.6.** Narahari says: say what you will — the ear does not believe it:
if there were nothing, would anyone speak of another for no reason?[^30-36]

[^30-35]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — p. 202, no. 108 (scan PDF p. 461); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 108 (catalogue: NG-095). No witnesses; probably from the lost
pages of GCC (n. 18). The last couplet is repeated in no. 123 (no. 21). C. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^30-36]: The townswoman's denial and the poet's disbelief are a game: in the padas of this series the very gossip about the "disgrace" of loving Gaura
is a sign of that love (cf. no. 16: "the whole world has gone mad with love of Him — why should I be the one to blame?"). Translated as in the
original.

## 16. Narahari Dasa — "ramaṇīramaṇa bhubanamohana gaurāṅga-ratana sai…" (GPT1 pp. 202–203, no. 109)
*Nagari-bhava. A townswoman asks her friend: the whole world — children, old people, young men and women — has gone mad with love of Gauranga,
all float in joy seeing His dance and hearing the kirtana — why is she alone defamed? Better to drown herself than to live in Nadia; the poet: in
life and in death Gora will not forsake her. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: not established** — GPT only (see n. 18).*[^30-37]

রমণীরমণ ভুবনমোহন গৌরাঙ্গ-রতন সই ।
তাহার পীরিতে জগত মাতিল দোষী কেন আমি হই ॥

*ramaṇīramaṇa bhubanamohana gaurāṅga-ratana sai |*
*tāhāra pīrite jagata mātila doṣī kena āmi hai ||*

*Word for word:* ramaṇī-ramaṇa — the Delight of women; bhubana-mohana — the Enchanter of the world; gaurāṅga-ratana — Gauranga the jewel; sai — friend; tāhāra pīrite — with love of Him; jagata mātila — the world went mad; doṣī kena āmi hai — why am I to blame

**16.1.** "The Delight of women, the Enchanter of the world, Gauranga is a jewel, friend:
the whole world has gone mad with love of Him — why should I be the one to blame?[^30-38]

বালক বিরধ যুবক যুবতী গৌরাঙ্গ দেখিয়া ঝুরে ।
আমি কেন তবে একাকী কলঙ্কী বচন মুখে না স্ফুরে ॥

*bālaka biradha yubaka yubatī gaurāṅga dekhiyā jhure |*
*āmi kena tabe ekākī kalaṅkī bacana mukhe nā sphure ||*

*Word for word:* bālaka biradha — children, old people; yubaka yubatī — young men and women; gaurāṅga dekhiyā jhure — weep seeing Gauranga; āmi kena tabe ekākī kalaṅkī — why then am I alone disgraced; bacana mukhe nā sphure — words fail my lips

**16.2.** Children, old people, young men and young women weep at the sight of Gauranga —
why then am I alone disgraced? — words fail my lips.

জগত আনন্দ সেই গৌরচন্দ্র সবাই আনন্দে ভাসে ।
মোর নিরানন্দ চোকে ঝরে জল বুঝিবা করমদোষে ॥

*jagata ānanda sei gauracandra sabāi ānande bhāse |*
*mora nirānanda coke jhare jala bujhibā karamadoṣe ||*

*Word for word:* jagata ānanda — the joy of the world; sei gauracandra — that Gaurachandra; sabāi ānande bhāse — all float in joy; mora nirānanda coke — from my joyless eyes; jhare jala — tears stream; bujhibā karama-doṣe — no doubt through the fault of karma

**16.3.** That Gaurachandra is the joy of the world: everyone floats in joy;
but from my joyless eyes tears stream — through the fault of my karma, no doubt.

নর্তন কীর্তন যে দেখে যে শুনে সেই হয় মাতোয়ারা ।
কি ক্ষতি কাহার যদি দেখি শুনি আমি হই জ্ঞানহারা ॥

*nartana kīrtana ye dekhe ye śune sei haya mātoyārā |*
*ki kṣati kāhāra yadi dekhi śuni āmi hai jñānahārā ||*

*Word for word:* nartana kīrtana — the dancing and kirtana; ye dekhe ye śune — whoever sees, whoever hears; sei haya mātoyārā — becomes intoxicated; ki kṣati kāhāra — whom does it harm; yadi dekhi śuni — if, seeing and hearing; āmi hai jñānahārā — I lose my senses

**16.4.** Whoever sees His dancing, whoever hears His kirtana — becomes intoxicated;
whom does it harm if I too, seeing and hearing, lose my senses?

নদীয়াবসতি আর না করিব ডুবিয়া মরিব জলে ।
জীবনে মরণে না ছাড়িবে গোরা দাস নরহরি বোলে ॥

*nadīyābasati āra nā kariba ḍubiyā mariba jale |*
*jībane maraṇe nā chāṛibe gorā dāsa narahari bole ||*

*Word for word:* nadīyā-basati — dwelling in Nadia; āra nā kariba — I will no longer do; ḍubiyā mariba jale — I will drown in the water; jībane maraṇe — in life and in death; nā chāṛibe gorā — Gora will not forsake; dāsa narahari bole — says Narahari Dasa

**16.5.** I will live in Nadia no more — I will throw myself into the water and drown!"
In life and in death Gora will not forsake you, says Narahari Dasa.[^30-39]

[^30-37]: Signature — "Dasa Narahari" (dāsa narahari). GPT1 — pp. 202–203, no. 109 (misprinted "169"; scan PDF pp. 461–462); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 109 (catalogue:
NG-096). No witnesses; probably from the lost pages of GCC (n. 18). C. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^30-38]: "The Delight of women" (ramaṇīramaṇa) — an epithet of Krishna transferred to Gaura (cf. n. 16); translated faithfully to the author. The
pada itself speaks of the whole world's love for Gaura — children, old people, young men (16.2) — and of His kirtana (16.4): the townswoman is
not alone in her love.
[^30-39]: "I will throw myself into the water and drown" is the usual formula of a loving woman's despair in the padas, not an intention; the poet's
answer reverses it: Gora will not forsake the one who loves Him, either in life or in death.

## 17. Narahari — "bidhātāra mane nā jāni ki āche…" (GPT1 p. 203, no. 110)
*Nagari-bhava. A townswoman's complaint: yesterday she went to see Gorachand, and her husband, learning of it, heaped abuse on her; her
brother-in-law, unable to bear her distress, himself rebuked his brother. How then is the wish of her heart to be fulfilled? The poet: do not
grieve — folly will be destroyed. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: not established** — GPT only (see n. 18).*[^30-40]

বিধাতার মনে না জানি কি আছে মানুষ-জনম দিয়া ।
কি কব দারুণ দুখ-দাবানলে সতত দহিছে হিয়া ॥

*bidhātāra mane nā jāni ki āche mānuṣa-janama diyā |*
*ki kaba dāruṇa dukha-dābānale satata dahiche hiyā ||*

*Word for word:* bidhātāra mane — in the Creator's mind; nā jāni ki āche — I do not know what there is; mānuṣa-janama diyā — giving a human birth; ki kaba — what shall I say; dāruṇa dukha-dābānale — in a fierce wildfire of sorrow; satata dahiche hiyā — the heart is ever burning

**17.1.** "I do not know what the Creator had in mind when he gave me a human birth:
what shall I say? — in a fierce wildfire of sorrow my heart is ever burning.

প্রাণধন গোরাচাঁদেরে দেখিতে সেখানে গেছিনু কাইল ।
সে কথা শুনিয়া পতি মতিহীন দিলে কত শত গাইল ॥

*prāṇadhana gorācām̐dere dekhite sekhāne gechinu kāila |*
*se kathā śuniyā pati matihīna dile kata śata gāila ||*

*Word for word:* prāṇadhana gorācām̐dere — Gorachand, the treasure of my life; dekhite — to see; sekhāne gechinu kāila — I went there yesterday; se kathā śuniyā — hearing of it; pati matihīna — my senseless husband; dile kata śata gāila — gave hundreds of abuses

**17.2.** Yesterday I went there to see Gorachand, the treasure of my life;
hearing of it, my senseless husband heaped hundreds of abuses on me.

দেবর আছিল নিকটে সে মোর বিরস দেখিতে নারে ।
নিন্দা কুবচন শুনিয়া তখনি কত নিরসিল তাঁরে ॥

*debara āchila nikaṭe se mora birasa dekhite nāre |*
*nindā kubacana śuniyā takhani kata nirasila tām̐re ||*

*Word for word:* debara āchila nikaṭe — my husband's younger brother was near; se mora birasa dekhite nāre — he cannot bear to see me unhappy; nindā kubacana śuniyā — hearing the reproach and abuse; takhani kata nirasila tām̐re — at once rebuked him (his brother) soundly

**17.3.** My husband's younger brother was near — he cannot bear to see me unhappy;
hearing the reproach and the abuse, he at once rebuked his brother soundly.

বল বল অগো ইহাতে কেমনে পূরিবে মনের আশ ।
নরহরি কহে না ভাবিহ আর কুমতি হইবে নাশ ॥

*bala bala ago ihāte kemane pūribe manera āśa |*
*narahari kahe nā bhābiha āra kumati haibe nāśa ||*

*Word for word:* bala bala ago — tell me, tell me, friend; ihāte kemane — how then; pūribe manera āśa — will the wish of my heart be fulfilled; narahari kahe — Narahari says; nā bhābiha āra — grieve no more; kumati haibe nāśa — folly will be destroyed

**17.4.** Tell me, tell me, friend: how then will the wish of my heart be fulfilled?"
Narahari says: grieve no more — folly will be destroyed.[^30-41]

[^30-40]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — p. 203, no. 110 (scan PDF p. 462); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 110 (catalogue: NG-097). No witnesses; probably from the lost
pages of GCC (n. 18). C. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^30-41]: "The treasure of my life" (prāṇadhana) — the townswoman's word for Gaura (cf. n. 14). "Folly will be destroyed" (kumati haibe nāśa) — from the
sense of the pada, the folly of the husband who abuses his wife for taking darshan of Gaura: the poet promises not a meeting in defiance of the
husband but a change in the husband himself (cf. GCC 7.29 = GPT1 no. 124: "my husband is very good" — the husband himself praises Nimai and does
not forbid the wives to see Him). On the motif "disregarding their husbands" see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).

## 18. Narahari — "śuna śuna ogo parāṇa sajani kahie tomāra prati…" (GPT1 pp. 205–206, no. 120)
*Nagari-bhava. A townswoman's story: in her house she is loved — and yesterday she went with her husband's aunt to the house of Ai (Shachi); Ai
was very affectionate to her, but she did not see Gaurangachand, and her pain doubled; on the way back, envying Shachi's neighbours, she suddenly
saw Gora with His companions on her own road, lifted her veil a little — and lost her composure; the aunt too could not stand firm. Raga
"yatharaga". **Attribution: not established** — GPT only (see n. 18).*[^30-42]

শুন শুন ওগো পরাণ সজনি কহিএ তোমার প্রতি ।
শ্বশুর শাশুড়ী না জানি কি গুণে করয়ে অধিক প্রীতি ॥

*śuna śuna ogo parāṇa sajani kahie tomāra prati |*
*śvaśura śāśuṛī nā jāni ki guṇe karaye adhika prīti ||*

*Word for word:* śuna śuna ogo — listen, listen; parāṇa sajani — friend of my heart; kahie tomāra prati — I tell you; śvaśura śāśuṛī — father-in-law and mother-in-law; nā jāni ki guṇe — I know not for what virtues; karaye adhika prīti — love me very much

**18.1.** "Listen, listen, friend of my heart, to what I tell you:
my father-in-law and mother-in-law — I know not for what virtues — love me very much;

ননদী আমারে প্রাণসম জানে কখন না দেয় গাইল ।
তেঁই পিসেসের সনে গিয়াছিনু আইয়ের বাড়ীতে কাইল ॥

*nanadī āmāre prāṇasama jāne kakhana nā deya gāila |*
*tem̐i pisesera sane giyāchinu āiyera bāṛīte kāila ||*

*Word for word:* nanadī āmāre prāṇasama jāne — my sister-in-law holds me dear as life; kakhana nā deya gāila — never scolds; teṃi — therefore; pisesera sane — with my husband's aunt; giyāchinu āiyera bāṛīte kāila — I went yesterday to Ai's house

**18.2.** my sister-in-law holds me dear as life and never scolds me —
so yesterday I went with my husband's aunt to the house of Ai.[^30-43]

আই মোরে স্নেহ করিল অনেক কি কব সে সব কথা ।
গৌরাঙ্গচাঁদেরে না দেখি অন্তরে বাড়িল দ্বিগুণ ব্যথা ॥

*āi more sneha karila aneka ki kaba se saba kathā |*
*gaurāṅgacām̐dere nā dekhi antare bāṛila dviguṇa byathā ||*

*Word for word:* āi more sneha karila aneka — Ai was very affectionate to me; ki kaba se saba kathā — what need to tell it all; gaurāṅgacām̐dere nā dekhi — not seeing Gaurangachand; antare bāṛila dviguṇa byathā — the pain in my heart doubled

**18.3.** Ai was very affectionate to me — what need to tell it all!
But I did not see Gaurangachand — and the pain of my heart doubled.

খানিক থাকিয়া বিদায় হইয়া চলিনু মনের দুখে ।
দেখিলুঁ সে পাড়াবাসী বধূগণ আছয়ে পরমসুখে ॥

*khānika thākiyā bidāya haiyā calinu manera dukhe |*
*dekhilum̐ se pāṛābāsī badhūgaṇa āchaye paramasukhe ||*

*Word for word:* khānika thākiyā — staying a little; bidāya haiyā — taking leave; calinu manera dukhe — I set off, sad at heart; dekhilum̐ — I saw; se pāṛā-bāsī badhūgaṇa — the young wives of that quarter; āchaye parama-sukhe — are in great happiness

**18.4.** After staying a little while, I took my leave and set off, sad at heart,
and I saw that the young wives who live in that quarter are in great happiness.

মনেতে হইল যদি এ পাড়াতে হইত সবার বাস ।
তবে অনায়াসে সফল হইত যে ছিল মনেতে আশ ॥

*manete haila yadi e pāṛāte haita sabāra bāsa |*
*tabe anāyāse saphala haita ye chila manete āśa ||*

*Word for word:* manete haila — I thought; yadi e pāṛāte haita sabāra bāsa — if we all lived in this quarter; tabe anāyāse — then easily; saphala haita — would come true; ye chila manete āśa — the hope that was in my heart

**18.5.** I thought: if only we all lived in this quarter,
then the hope that was in my heart would easily come true.

তুরিত গমনে ঘর পানে ওগো যে পথে আসিএ মোরা ।
সেই পথে প্রিয় পরিকর সাথে দাঁড়ায়ে আছেন গোরা ॥

*turita gamane ghara pāne ogo ye pathe āsie morā |*
*sei pathe priya parikara sāthe dām̐ṛāye āchena gorā ||*

*Word for word:* turita gamane — with quick steps; ghara pāne — towards home; ogo — friend; ye pathe āsie morā — the road by which we go; sei pathe — on that road; priya parikara sāthe — with His dear companions; dām̐ṛāye āchena gorā — Gora stands

**18.6.** With quick steps I head for home, friend — and on the very road by which we go
Gora stands with His dear companions.

পিসৈস নিকটে সঙ্কটে পড়িনু মুখে না নিঃসরে বাণী ।
অলপ ঘুঙট ঘুচাঞা দেখিনু ও চাঁদবদন খানি ॥

*pisaisa nikaṭe saṅkaṭe paṛinu mukhe nā niḥsare bāṇī |*
*alapa ghuṅaṭa ghucāñā dekhinu o cām̐dabadana khāni ||*

*Word for word:* pisaisa nikaṭe — my husband's aunt beside me; saṅkaṭe paṛinu — I was in a fix; mukhe nā niḥsare bāṇī — no word left my lips; alapa ghuṅaṭa ghucāñā — lifting my veil a little; dekhinu o cām̐da-badana khāni — I saw that moonlike face

**18.7.** My husband's aunt beside me — I was in a fix: no word would leave my lips;
lifting my veil a little, I saw that moonlike face.

অঙ্গের বসন খসিয়া পড়য়ে কাঁপিয়া উঠয়ে গা ।
ধরমে ধরমে ধীর ধীর করি বাড়াইতে লাগিনু পা ॥

*aṅgera basana khasiyā paṛaye kām̐piyā uṭhaye gā |*
*dharame dharame dhīra dhīra kari bāṛāite lāginu pā ||*

*Word for word:* aṅgera basana khasiyā paṛaye — the clothes slip from the body; kām̐piyā uṭhaye gā — the body trembles; dharame dharame — somehow; dhīra dhīra kari — slowly, slowly; bāṛāite lāginu pā — I began to move my feet
