**18.8.** My clothes slip from my body, my whole body trembles;
somehow, slowly, slowly, I began to move my feet.

ফিরিয়া ফিরিয়া হেরিয়ে হৃদয় অধিক ব্যাকুল হৈল ।
লাজ কুলভয় ধরম কিছু না রহিবে নিশ্চয় কৈল ॥

*phiriyā phiriyā heriye hṛdaya adhika byākula haila |*
*lāja kulabhaya dharama kichu nā rahibe niścaya kaila ||*

*Word for word:* phiriyā phiriyā heriye — turning back and back I gaze; hṛdaya adhika byākula haila — my heart grew utterly bewildered; lāja kulabhaya dharama — shame, fear for the family, dharma; kichu nā rahibe — nothing will remain; niścaya kaila — it resolved for certain

**18.9.** Turning back and back I gazed — my heart grew utterly bewildered;
it resolved for certain: neither shame, nor fear for the family, nor dharma will remain.[^30-44]

সে পথে পিসৈস দাঁড়াইল হেরি ধরিতে নারয়ে থে ।
নরহরি কহে ওরূপ হেরিয়া না ভুলে এমন কে ॥

*se pathe pisaisa dām̐ṛāila heri dharite nāraye the |*
*narahari kahe orūpa heriyā nā bhule emana ke ||*

*Word for word:* se pathe — on that road; pisaisa dām̐ṛāila — my husband's aunt stopped; heri — seeing Him; dharite nāraye the — could not stand firm; narahari kahe — Narahari says; o-rūpa heriyā — seeing that form; nā bhule emana ke — who would not lose herself

**18.10.** On that road my husband's aunt stopped too: seeing Him, she could not stand firm."
Narahari says: seeing that form, who would not lose herself?

[^30-42]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — pp. 205–206, no. 120 (scan PDF pp. 464–465); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 120 (catalogue: NG-099). No witnesses; probably from
the lost pages of GCC (n. 18): in its structure (a visit with the husband's aunt to another quarter, a meeting with Gora on the way back) the pada
is close to GCC 7.30 = GPT1 no. 125 (with the aunt — to the house of Murari Gupta). C. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section
(chapter 27).
[^30-43]: "My husband's aunt" (pisesa, pisi-śāśuṛī — the father-in-law's sister). "Ai" (āi, "mother") — Shachi-devi: the townswoman had gone to the house
of the Lord's mother.
[^30-44]: 18.8–18.9: the slipping clothes, the trembling, the resolve to cast off "shame, fear for the family and dharma" are stated plainly in the
original (cf. n. 9, and n. 41 of chapter 29: the formula of the supremacy of prema over worldly dharma); the Lord merely stands with His
companions on the road. The tradition does not accept worship of Gaura in the nagari mood (introductory note, chapter 27).

## 19. Narahari — "ki baliba ogo nanada āmāra, kebala biṣera phala…" (GPT1 pp. 206–207, no. 121)
*Nagari-bhava. A townswoman's story: her sister-in-law is a veritable poison fruit, and no trick can be played before her; but she trusts the
friends and lets her brother's wife go to them at any time — and on this pretext she went yesterday to see Gaurangachand; there follows a
description of His form from head to foot. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: not established** — GPT only (see n. 18).*[^30-45]

কি বলিব ওগো ননদ আমার কেবল বিষের ফল ।
পরম চতুরা তার কাছে মোরা করিতে নারিএ ছল ॥

*ki baliba ogo nanada āmāra kebala biṣera phala |*
*parama caturā tāra kāche morā karite nārie chala ||*

*Word for word:* ki baliba ogo — what shall I say, friend; nanada āmāra — my sister-in-law; kebala biṣera phala — a veritable poison fruit; parama caturā — very cunning; tāra kāche — before her; morā karite nārie chala — we cannot play a trick

**19.1.** "What shall I say, friend? My sister-in-law is a veritable poison fruit:
she is very cunning — before her we cannot play any trick.

তোমাদের প্রতি অধিক বিশ্বাস কপট না যায় জানা ।
বিহান বিকাল রজনী এথাতে আসিতে না করে মানা ॥

*tomādera prati adhika biśvāsa kapaṭa nā yāya jānā |*
*bihāna bikāla rajanī ethāte āsite nā kare mānā ||*

*Word for word:* tomādera prati adhika biśvāsa — she trusts you very much; kapaṭa nā yāya jānā — the pretence cannot be seen through; bihāna bikāla rajanī — morning, evening, night; ethāte āsite — to come here; nā kare mānā — she does not forbid

**19.2.** But she trusts you very much — the pretence cannot be seen through:
morning, evening, night — she does not forbid me to come here.

এই ছলে যেন গিয়াছিনু কাইল দেখিতে গৌরাঙ্গচাঁদে ।
কে আছে এমন যুবতী তাহারে হেরিয়া ধৈরজ বাঁধে ॥

*ei chale yena giyāchinu kāila dekhite gaurāṅgacām̐de |*
*ke āche emana yubatī tāhāre heriyā dhairaja bām̐dhe ||*

*Word for word:* ei chale — on this pretext; yena giyāchinu kāila — I went yesterday; dekhite gaurāṅgacām̐de — to see Gaurangachand; ke āche emana yubatī — is there a young woman; tāhāre heriyā — who, seeing Him; dhairaja bām̐dhe — keeps her composure

**19.3.** On this pretext I went yesterday to see Gaurangachand:
is there a young woman who, seeing Him, could keep her composure?

কিবা সে পীঠের উপরে দুলিছে চাঁচর চিকুর ভার ।
কিবা সে কপালে অলকা তিলক কি দিব উপমা তার ॥

*kibā se pīṭhera upare duliche cām̐cara cikura bhāra |*
*kibā se kapāle alakā tilaka ki diba upamā tāra ||*

*Word for word:* kibā — how; se pīṭhera upare — upon His back; duliche — sways; cām̐cara cikura bhāra — the weight of curling locks; kibā se kapāle — how on His brow; alakā tilaka — curls and tilaka; ki diba upamā tāra — what comparison shall I give

**19.4.** How the weight of curling locks sways upon His back!
How lovely on His brow are the curls and the tilaka — to what shall I compare them?

কিবা সে ভুরুর ভঙ্গিমা চাহনি কিবা সে আঁখির ঠারা ।
কিবা সে মুখের হাসি অপরূপ বচন অমিঞা ধারা ॥

*kibā se bhurura bhaṅgimā cāhani kibā se ām̐khira ṭhārā |*
*kibā se mukhera hāsi aparūpa bacana amiñā dhārā ||*

*Word for word:* kibā se bhurura bhaṅgimā — how the brows curve; cāhani — the glance; kibā se ām̐khira ṭhārā — what a signal of the eyes; kibā se mukhera hāsi aparūpa — how wondrous the smile; bacana amiñā dhārā — speech a stream of nectar

**19.5.** How the brows curve, what a glance, what a signal of the eyes!
How wondrous the smile on His lips — His speech flows in a stream of nectar!

কিবা সে কাণের কুণ্ডল দোলনি কিবা সে গণ্ডের শোভা ।
কিবা সে নাসার মুকুতা কিবা সে রুচির চিবুক-আভা ॥

*kibā se kāṇera kuṇḍala dolani kibā se gaṇḍera śobhā |*
*kibā se nāsāra mukutā kibā se rucira cibuka-ābhā ||*

*Word for word:* kibā se kāṇera kuṇḍala dolani — how the earrings sway; kibā se gaṇḍera śobhā — how beautiful the cheeks; kibā se nāsāra mukutā — what a pearl in the nose; kibā se rucira cibuka-ābhā — what a radiance of the lovely chin

**19.6.** How the earrings sway in His ears, how beautiful His cheeks!
What a pearl in His nose, what a radiance of the lovely chin!

কিবা সে ভুজের বলনি কিবা সে গলায় ফুলের হারা ।
কিবা সে সরুয়া মাজাখানি উরু উলট-কদলী পারা ॥

*kibā se bhujera balani kibā se galāya phulera hārā |*
*kibā se saruyā mājākhāni uru ulaṭa-kadalī pārā ||*

*Word for word:* kibā se bhujera balani — what a curve of the arms; kibā se galāya phulera hārā — what a garland at the throat; kibā se saruyā mājākhāni — how slender the waist; uru ulaṭa-kadalī pārā — thighs like inverted plantain stems

**19.7.** What a curve of the arms, what a garland of flowers at His throat!
How slender the waist, and the thighs like inverted plantain stems!

কিবা সে সুচারু চরণ-নখর-কিরণে পরাণ হরে ।
নরহরি কহে ওরূপ হেরিয়া কিরূপে আইলা ঘরে ॥

*kibā se sucāru caraṇa-nakhara-kiraṇe parāṇa hare |*
*narahari kahe orūpa heriyā kirūpe āilā ghare ||*

*Word for word:* kibā se sucāru caraṇa-nakhara-kiraṇe — how with the radiance of the nails of the lovely feet; parāṇa hare — He steals the heart; narahari kahe — Narahari says; o-rūpa heriyā — seeing that form; kirūpe āilā ghare — how did you get home

**19.8.** How the radiance of the nails of His lovely feet steals away the heart!"
Narahari says: having seen that form, how did you ever get home?[^30-46]

[^30-45]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — pp. 206–207, no. 121 (scan PDF pp. 465–466); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 121 (catalogue: NG-100). No witnesses; probably from
the lost pages of GCC (n. 18). C. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^30-46]: 19.4–19.8 — a description of the Lord's form "from head to foot" (rupa-varnana) in the usual images of the padas on Krishna and Gaura (curling
locks down the back — Gaura before sannyasa; a slender waist, thighs like "inverted plantain stems", the radiance of the nails) — this is
contemplation of the Lord's beauty, not a worldly description. "A pearl in His nose" (nāsāra mukutā) — so in the original.

## 20. Narahari — "śuna śuna ogo parāṇa sajani nibedi tomāra āge…" (GPT1 p. 207, no. 122)
*Nagari-bhava. A townswoman's complaint: her sister-in-law is hard-hearted and knows nothing of another's pain; whenever she hears that Gauranga has
come to someone's house, she, on some pretext and unbeknown to the old woman, runs there herself — but forbids her brother's wife. The poet: such
is the way of sisters-in-law. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: not established** — GPT only (see n. 18).*[^30-47]

শুন শুন ওগো পরাণ সজনি নিবেদি তোমার আগে ।
দিবস রজনী ভাবিয়া মরিএ ঘর পর সম লাগে ॥

*śuna śuna ogo parāṇa sajani nibedi tomāra āge |*
*dibasa rajanī bhābiyā marie ghara para sama lāge ||*

*Word for word:* śuna śuna ogo — listen, listen; parāṇa sajani — friend of my heart; nibedi tomāra āge — I confide to you; dibasa rajanī — day and night; bhābiyā marie — I die with longing; ghara para sama lāge — my home feels like a stranger's

**20.1.** "Listen, listen, friend of my heart, to what I confide to you:
day and night I am dying with longing — my own home feels like a stranger's.

ননদী কঠিন সে কথা কি কব কহিতে বাসিএ দুখ ।
পরের বেদন কিছু না জান সে জানয়ে আপন সুখ ॥

*nanadī kaṭhina se kathā ki kaba kahite bāsie dukha |*
*parera bedana kichu nā jāna se jānaye āpana sukha ||*

*Word for word:* nanadī kaṭhina — my sister-in-law is hard; se kathā ki kaba — what shall I say of it; kahite bāsie dukha — it is bitter to tell; parera bedana — another's pain; kichu nā jāna se — she knows nothing of; jānaye āpana sukha — she knows only her own pleasure

**20.2.** My sister-in-law is hard — what shall I say of her? It is bitter even to tell:
of another's pain she knows nothing at all — she knows only her own pleasure.

যদি কার মুখে শুনয়ে গৌরাঙ্গ আইলা কাহার বাড়ী ।
তবে কত ছল করয়ে তাহা না বুঝয়ে ঘরের বুড়ী ॥

*yadi kāra mukhe śunaye gaurāṅga āilā kāhāra bāṛī |*
*tabe kata chala karaye tāhā nā bujhaye gharera buṛī ||*

*Word for word:* yadi kāra mukhe śunaye — if she hears from anyone; gaurāṅga āilā kāhāra bāṛī — that Gauranga has come to someone's house; tabe kata chala karaye — she plays so many tricks; tāhā nā bujhaye gharera buṛī — the old woman of the house does not see through them

**20.3.** If she hears from anyone that Gauranga has come to someone's house,
she thinks up so many tricks — and the old woman of the house does not see through them —

ধাঞা যায় তথা এ বড় বিষম আমারে করয়ে মানা ।
নরহরি কহে ইহাতে কি দোষ জানায় ননদ-পনা ॥

*dhāñā yāya tathā e baṛa biṣama āmāre karaye mānā |*
*narahari kahe ihāte ki doṣa jānāya nanada-panā ||*

*Word for word:* dhāñā yāya tathā — she runs off there; e baṛa biṣama — this is most unfair; āmāre karaye mānā — she forbids me; narahari kahe — Narahari says; ihāte ki doṣa — what is wrong in that; jānāya nanada-panā — she shows her sister-in-law's nature

**20.4.** and off she runs there, — but me, and this is the unfair part, she forbids!"
Narahari says: what is wrong in that? She is showing what a sister-in-law is.

[^30-47]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — p. 207, no. 122 (scan PDF p. 466); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 122 (catalogue: NG-101). No witnesses; probably from the lost
pages of GCC (n. 18). C. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).

## 21. Narahari — "sajani to sabe dekhe sukha pāi…" (GPT1 p. 207, no. 123)
*Nagari-bhava. A townswoman whose friends question her about yesterday laughs and denies it: such talk does not become her. The poet does not
believe her. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: not established** — GPT only (see n. 18).*[^30-48]

সজনি তো সবে দেখে সুখ পাই তেঁই সে এথায় আসি ।
কালিকার কথা পুছহ আমারে ইহাতে উপজে হাসি ॥

*sajani to sabe dekhe sukha pāi tem̐i se ethāya āsi |*
*kālikāra kathā puchaha āmāre ihāte upaje hāsi ||*

*Word for word:* sajani — friend; to sabe dekhe — seeing you all; sukha pāi — I am glad; teṃi se ethāya āsi — that is why I come here; kālikāra kathā puchaha āmāre — you ask me about yesterday; ihāte upaje hāsi — it is laughable

**21.1.** "Friend, seeing you all I am glad — that is why I come here;
and you ask me about yesterday — it is simply laughable!

বল বল দেখি কিরূপে আমারে সাজিবে এ সব কথা ।
জানিয়া শুনিয়া এরূপ বলহ ইহাতে পাইএ ব্যথা ॥

*bala bala dekhi kirūpe āmāre sājibe e saba kathā |*
*jāniyā śuniyā erūpa balaha ihāte pāie byathā ||*

*Word for word:* bala bala dekhi — tell me, tell me; kirūpe āmāre sājibe — how would befit me; e saba kathā — such talk; jāniyā śuniyā — knowing me; erūpa balaha — you say such things; ihāte pāie byathā — it pains me

**21.2.** Tell me, tell me: how would such talk befit me?
Knowing me, you say such things — it pains me."

নরহরি কহে যে বল সে বল এ কথা কাণে না ধরে ।
কিছু না থাকিলে মিছামিছি কেহ কারে কি কহিতে পারে ॥

*narahari kahe ye bala se bala e kathā kāṇe nā dhare |*
*kichu nā thākile michāmichi keha kāre ki kahite pāre ||*

*Word for word:* narahari kahe — Narahari says; ye bala se bala — say what you will; e kathā kāṇe nā dhare — the ear does not hold it true; kichu nā thākile — if there were nothing; michāmichi — for no reason; keha kāre ki kahite pāre — could anyone speak of another

**21.3.** Narahari says: say what you will — the ear does not believe it:
if there were nothing, would anyone speak of another for no reason?

[^30-48]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — p. 207, no. 123 (scan PDF p. 466); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 123 (catalogue: NG-342). No witnesses. A short pada (3 couplets);
the signature (21.3) repeats word for word the signature of no. 108 (no. 15, 15.6) — perhaps the answer of another townswoman in the same
conversation, or a fragment. In tone it continues no. 15 (denial and the poet's disbelief; see n. 36). C. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to
the section (chapter 27).

## Summary of chapter 30

*The chapter continues the padas signed "Narahari" from section 3.2 of GPT — the townswomen of Nadia telling their friends in the morning how,
despite the strictness of their mothers-in-law, sisters-in-law, fathers-in-law and husbands, they saw Gaura. Nos. 94–99 (nos. 1–6) were found in
Narahari Chakravarti's *Gaura-charita-chintamani* (kirana 7, padas 10–12, 14–16; "probably Chakravarti" — B; no. 97 in GPT is only the second half of
the GCC pada 7.14). Nos. 100–110 and 120–123 (nos. 7–21) stand in GPT in the place of GCC 7.17–7.28, but those pages (pp. 81–88) are lost in the
only available scan of GCC, and there are no other witnesses: they are labelled "not established" (C), with a note on their probable origin in GCC
(n. 18). In several padas the strict elders — a mother-in-law, a father-in-law, the husband's aunt — themselves lose their composure on hearing the
kirtana or seeing Gaura and become His devotees (nos. 9, 13, 18); the direct motifs of attraction and of deceiving the elders are rendered
exactly, with notes on the position of the tradition (introductory note, chapter 27).*

# Chapter 31. Nagari Padas — V: the "Narahari" padas of GPT (sect. 3.2, nos. 119, 124–145): the townswomen's dreams

*On what nagari-bhava is, the position of the tradition (Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja, Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati) and the rules of translation, see the introductory note to the section of nagari padas in chapter 27; on the two poets named Narahari (Narahari Sarakara and Narahari Chakravarti) and on the attribution labels ("probably Sarakara", "probably Chakravarti", "not established"), see the introductory note to the "Narahari" appendix in chapter 17.*

## 1. Narahari — "ghumaka-ghore bhora śacīnandana…" (GPT1 p. 205, no. 119; GCC 2.13)
*Gaura asleep. At the end of the night Shachi's son, deep in sleep, as if immersed in a sleep of long ago in the kunja, softly says: "Wake,
crown-jewel of women, beautiful one! Without the song of your words My hearing has no joy; open your eyes, give Me a smile; rise — I Myself will
adorn you." This is not a townswoman's speech: GPT placed the pada in the section of nagari padas, but in GCC it stands in the account of the
last part of the Lord's night. Raga lalita. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 2, pada 13.*[^31-1]

ঘুমক-ঘোরে ভোর শচীনন্দন কো সমুঝব তছু প্রেমবিলাস ।
পুরব-নিকুঞ্জে শয়নে জনু নিমগন বোলত ঐছন মধুর মৃদু ভাষ ॥

*ghumaka-ghore bhora śacīnandana ko samujhaba tachu premabilāsa |*
*puraba-nikuñje śayane janu nimagana bolata aichana madhura mṛdu bhāṣa ||*

*Word for word:* ghumaka-ghore bhora — overcome by deep sleep; śacīnandana — Shachi's son; ko samujhaba — who will fathom; tachu premabilāsa — His play of prema; puraba-nikuñje śayane — in sleep in the kunja of old; janu nimagana — as if immersed; bolata aichana — speaks thus; madhura mṛdu bhāṣa — in sweet soft words

**1.1.** Shachi's son, held by deep sleep — who can fathom His play of prema? — as if immersed in a sleep of long ago in the kunja, speaks thus, sweetly and softly:

জাগ জাগ রমণীশিরোমণি সুন্দরি কতহি ঘুমায়সি রজনীক শেষ ।
তব বচনামৃত-সঙ্গীত পান বিনু চঞ্চল শ্রবণ রহিত সুখলেশ ॥

*jāga jāga ramaṇīśiromaṇi sundari katahi ghumāyasi rajanīka śeṣa |*
*taba bacanāmṛta-saṅgīta pāna binu cañcala śrabaṇa rahita sukhaleśa ||*

*Word for word:* jāga jāga — wake, wake; ramaṇīśiromaṇi sundari — crown-jewel of women, beautiful one; katahi ghumāyasi — how long you sleep; rajanīka śeṣa — at the end of the night; taba bacanāmṛta-saṅgīta — the song of the nectar of your words; pāna binu — without drinking; cañcala śrabaṇa — restless hearing; rahita sukhaleśa — bereft of the least joy

**1.2.** "Wake, wake, crown-jewel of women, beautiful one — how long will you sleep at the end of the night? Without drinking the song of the nectar of your words, My restless hearing is bereft of the least joy.

মুদ্রিত ত্যজি তরল-নয়নাঞ্চলে ললিত ভঙ্গী করি মন মান ।
মম মন বন্ধ নিশঙ্ক কহই তোহে হাসি রভস মোহে দেহ দান ॥

*mudrita tyaji tarala-nayanāñcale lalita bhaṅgī kari mana māna |*
*mama mana bandha niśaṅka kahai tohe hāsi rabhasa mohe deha dāna ||*

*Word for word:* mudrita tyaji — leaving the closed (eyelids); tarala-nayanāñcale — with the tremulous corners of the eyes; lalita bhaṅgī kari — with a graceful movement; mana māna — honour (sense unclear; GCC "kara sammāna" — do honour); mama mana bandha — My heart is bound (GCC: in pledge); niśaṅka kahai — I say without fear; tohe hāsi — you, smiling; rabhasa mohe deha dāna — give Me joy

**1.3.** Leave your closed eyelids: with the tremulous corners of your eyes, with a graceful movement, do Me honour. My heart is bound — I say it without fear: smile and give Me joy.

মঝু অভিলাষ সমুঝি উঠি বৈঠহ নিজকরে বেশ বিরচব তোহারি ।
ইহ বিধি কহত নরহরি পহুঁ বহুরি নিগদত কখন বিশারি ॥

*majhu abhilāṣa samujhi uṭhi baiṭhaha nijakare beśa biracaba tohāri |*
*iha bidhi kahata narahari pahum̐ bahuri nigadata kakhana biśāri ||*

*Word for word:* majhu abhilāṣa samujhi — understanding My wish; uṭhi baiṭhaha — rise and sit up; nijakare — with My own hands; beśa biracaba tohāri — I will adorn you; iha bidhi kahata — thus He speaks; narahari pahum̐ — Narahari's Lord; bahuri nigadata — says again; kakhana biśāri — lost to Himself (lit. "forgetting when"; GCC: "forgetting what is said")

**1.4.** Understand My wish — rise and sit up: with My own hands I will adorn you." So speaks Narahari's Lord — and says it again, lost to Himself.[^31-2]

[^31-1]: Signature — "Narahari" (narahari pahum̐ — "Narahari's Lord", i.e. the poet's Lord). GPT1 — p. 205, no. 119 (raga lalita; scan PDF p. 464); GPT2 — sect. 3.2,
no. 119 (catalogue: NG-098). GCC — kirana 2, pada 13 (ed. 1947, p. 30; scan PDF p. 35), "lalita-rāga". The second kirana of GCC describes the last part
of the Lord's night: the bedchamber, the bees flying into the house, the birds that wake Him at dawn; in the next pada (GCC 2.14, not taken into GPT) these
words spoken in sleep are heard by Gadadhara Pandita, who wakes and then keeps watch by Gaura's bed (2.15–2.16). Thus in the author Gaura in sleep speaks
the words of Krishna waking Radha in the kunja at the end of the night (cf. the padas on the waking of Radha and Krishna, nishanta-lila): this is a
remembrance of Vraja, not nagari-bhava; on Gadadhara as the embodiment of Radha's bhava in Gaura-lila — GGD. The pada is in Vrajabuli (tachu, mohe, tohe,
majhu). B. The pada stands in the GPT section of nagari padas — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^31-2]: 1.2: "the song of the nectar of your words" (bacanāmṛta-saṅgīta) — so GPT1 and GPT2; GCC has "the nectar of your sigh" (sītkṛta, "sitkara" — a sigh from descriptions of a lovers'
meeting), a more explicit reading; the GPT text is translated. 1.3: "do Me honour" — after the GCC reading "kari kara sammāna" (GPT: "kari mana māna", sense
unclear); "My heart is bound" — GPT "mana mana bandha" (probably a misprint for GCC "mama mana bandhaka" — "My heart is in pledge [to you]"); "give Me joy"
(GPT "rabhasa") — GCC "give Me the jewel of a smile" (hāsi ratana). 1.4: "says it again, lost to Himself" (GPT "bahuri nigadata kakhana biśāri"; GCC "bahu
binigadata kathana bisāri" — "speaks much, forgetting what He says") — the sense of the last words is conjectural.

## 2. Narahari — "mora pati ati sujana sajani…" (GPT1 pp. 207–208, no. 124; GCC 7.29)
*Nagari-bhava. A townswoman tells her friend: yesterday her husband, alone with his father, said that Nimai Pandita has the power of God, has
mastered His senses, is righteous, merciful to wicked people and full of the joy of kirtana; therefore the young wives should not be forbidden
to see Him — His darshan destroys all that is inauspicious; as in Vraja Krishna was not recognised by the brahmanas but by their wives, so it is
here. Hearing this she rejoiced, and when Gaura passed along the street with Gadadhara, Nityananda and His companions, she went out and gazed
on Him to her heart's content: the other women were held back by their mothers-in-law, but no one held her back. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution:
probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 7, pada 29.*[^31-3]

মোর পতি অতি সুজন সজনি শুন লো তাহার রীতি ।
গতদিন তেঁই বিরলে বসিয়া কহয়ে পিতার প্রতি ॥

*mora pati ati sujana sajani śuna lo tāhāra rīti |*
*gatadina tem̐i birale basiyā kahaye pitāra prati ||*

*Word for word:* mora pati — my husband; ati sujana — a very good man; sajani — friend; śuna lo — do listen; tāhāra rīti — his ways; gatadina — yesterday; tem̐i — he; birale basiyā — sitting alone; kahaye pitāra prati — says to his father

**2.1.** "My husband, friend, is a very good man: listen to what he is like. Yesterday, sitting alone with his father, he said to him:

নদীয়া নগরে নিমাই পণ্ডিত ঈশ্বর-শকতি তার ।
কেবা সিরজিল না জানি এরূপ গুণের নাহিক পার ॥

*nadīyā nagare nimāi paṇḍita īśvara-śakati tāra |*
*kebā sirajila nā jāni erūpa guṇera nāhika pāra ||*

*Word for word:* nadīyā nagare — in the town of Nadia; nimāi paṇḍita — Nimai Pandita; īśvara-śakati tāra — in Him is the power of God; kebā sirajila — who created; nā jāni — I do not know; erūpa — such a one; guṇera nāhika pāra — no end to His virtues

**2.2.** 'In the town of Nadia is Nimai Pandita: in Him is the power of God. Who created such a wonder I do not know; there is no end to His virtues.

হেন জিতেন্দ্রিয় ধার্মিক কখন না দেখি আপন আঁখে ।
দুর্মতি-জনের প্রতি অতি দয়া ভাসয়ে কীর্তনসুখে ॥

*hena jitendriya dhārmika kakhana nā dekhi āpana ām̐khe |*
*durmati-janera prati ati dayā bhāsaye kīrtanasukhe ||*

*Word for word:* hena — such; jitendriya — master of the senses; dhārmika — righteous; kakhana nā dekhi — I have never seen; āpana ām̐khe — with my own eyes; durmati-janera prati — towards wicked people; ati dayā — great mercy; bhāsaye kīrtanasukhe — floats in the joy of kirtana

**2.3.** One so master of His senses and so righteous I have never seen with my own eyes. To wicked people He is boundlessly merciful; He floats in the joy of kirtana.

তাহে বলি নিজ বধূগণে কভু ভুলি না নিষেধ তুমি ।
তার দরশনে অশুভ বিনাশে নিশ্চয় জানিয়ে আমি ॥

*tāhe bali nija badhūgaṇe kabhu bhuli nā niṣedha tumi |*
*tāra daraśane aśubha bināśe niścaya jāniye āmi ||*

*Word for word:* tāhe bali — therefore I say; nija badhūgaṇe — your daughters-in-law; kabhu bhuli nā niṣedha tumi — never, even by oversight, forbid; tāra daraśane — by His darshan; aśubha bināśe — the inauspicious perishes; niścaya jāniye āmi — I know for certain

**2.4.** Therefore I say: never, not even by oversight, forbid your daughters-in-law [to go to Him]. I know for certain: by His darshan all that is inauspicious perishes.

ভাগ্যবতী সব বহু কি কহব অধিক কহিতে নারি ।
তাহে ধন্য এই নারী-জনমের বালাই লইয়া মরি ॥

*bhāgyabatī saba bahu ki kahaba adhika kahite nāri |*
*tāhe dhanya ei nārī-janamera bālāi laiyā mari ||*

*Word for word:* bhāgyabatī saba bahu — fortunate are all the young wives (bahu = vadhū); ki kahaba adhika — what more shall I say; kahite nāri — I cannot express it; tāhe dhanya — therefore blessed; ei nārī-janamera — this birth as a woman; bālāi laiyā mari — I take upon myself its ills

**2.5.** Fortunate are all our young wives — what more can I say? I cannot even express it. Therefore blessed is this birth as a woman — I take upon myself all its ills.

মিছা অভিমানে মাতি রাতি দিন রহিএ অন্ধের পারা ।
নদীয়ার মাঝে হেন অপরূপ চিনিতে নারিয়ে মোরা ॥

*michā abhimāne māti rāti dina rahie andhera pārā |*
*nadīyāra mājhe hena aparūpa cinite nāriye morā ||*

*Word for word:* michā abhimāne māti — drunk with false pride; rāti dina — night and day; rahie andhera pārā — we live like the blind; nadīyāra mājhe — in the midst of Nadia; hena aparūpa — such a Wonder; cinite nāriye morā — we cannot recognise

**2.6.** But we, drunk with false pride, live day and night like the blind: such a Wonder in the midst of Nadia — and we cannot recognise Him.

ব্রজে ব্রজনাথে দ্বিজে না জানিল পাইল দ্বিজের নারী ।
সেইরূপ এথা ইথে না সন্দেহ বুঝিনু বিচার করি ॥

*braje brajanāthe dvije nā jānila pāila dvijera nārī |*
*seirūpa ethā ithe nā sandeha bujhinu bicāra kari ||*

*Word for word:* braje — in Vraja; brajanāthe — the Lord of Vraja; dvije nā jānila — the brahmanas did not know; pāila dvijera nārī — the brahmanas' wives attained; seirūpa ethā — so it is here; ithe nā sandeha — no doubt in this; bujhinu bicāra kari — I have understood, reflecting

**2.7.** In Vraja the brahmanas did not know the Lord of Vraja — the brahmanas' wives attained Him. So it is here, there is no doubt of it — I have understood, having reflected.'[^31-4]

এইরূপ পিতাপুত্র দুঁহে কথা কহয়ে অনেক মতে ।
আড়ে থাকি তাহা শুনিয়া শুনিয়া হনু উলসিত চিতে ॥

*eirūpa pitāputra dum̐he kathā kahaye aneka mate |*
*āṛe thāki tāhā śuniyā śuniyā hanu ulasita cite ||*

*Word for word:* eirūpa — thus; pitā-putra dum̐he — father and son both; kathā kahaye aneka mate — talk in many ways; āṛe thāki — staying hidden; tāhā śuniyā śuniyā — listening and listening to it; hanu ulasita cite — I rejoiced in heart

**2.8.** So father and son talked long in many ways; hidden nearby, I listened and listened — and my heart rejoiced.

মনে হৈল হেন বেলে যদি গোরাচাঁদেরে দেখিতে পাতু ।
নয়নের কোণে এ সব কাহিনী তাহারে কহিয়ে দিতু ॥

*mane haila hena bele yadi gorācām̐dere dekhite pātu |*
*nayanera koṇe e saba kāhinī tāhāre kahiye ditu ||*

*Word for word:* mane haila — I thought; hena bele — at this hour; yadi gorācām̐dere dekhite pātu — if I could see Gorachand; nayanera koṇe — with the corners of my eyes; e saba kāhinī — all this story; tāhāre kahiye ditu — I would tell Him

**2.9.** I thought: if only I could see Gorachand right now — with the corners of my eyes I would tell Him all this.

এইকালে পাড়া পানে ঘন ঘন উঠিল আনন্দ-ধ্বনি ।
তরাতরি পথে দাঁড়াইনু গিয়া গৌরগমন জানি ॥

*eikāle pāṛā pāne ghana ghana uṭhila ānanda-dhvani |*
*tarātari pathe dām̐ṛāinu giyā gauragamana jāni ||*

*Word for word:* eikāle — at this time; pāṛā pāne — from the direction of our quarter; ghana ghana — again and again; uṭhila ānanda-dhvani — joyful cries rose; tarātari — in haste; pathe dām̐ṛāinu giyā — I went and stood by the road; gauragamana jāni — knowing Gaura was coming

**2.10.** Just then, from the direction of our quarter, joyful cries rose again and again; knowing that Gaura was coming, I hurried out and stood by the road.

দূরে থাকি আঁখি ভরি নিরখিনু কিবা অপরূপ শোভা ।
ঝলমল করে চারিদিকে হেম জিনিয়া অঙ্গের আভা ॥

*dūre thāki ām̐khi bhari nirakhinu kibā aparūpa śobhā |*
*jhalamala kare cāridike hema jiniyā aṅgera ābhā ||*

*Word for word:* dūre thāki — from afar; ām̐khi bhari — to my eyes' content; nirakhinu — I gazed; kibā aparūpa śobhā — what wondrous beauty; jhalamala kare — blazes; cāridike — in every direction; hema jiniyā — outshining gold; aṅgera ābhā — the radiance of His body

**2.11.** From afar I gazed my fill — what wondrous beauty! The radiance of His body, outshining gold, blazes in every direction.

তার বামে গদাধর নিত্যানন্দ দক্ষিণে আনন্দরাশি ।
চারিপাশে আর পরিকর তারা নিরখে ও মুখশশী ॥

*tāra bāme gadādhara nityānanda dakṣiṇe ānandarāśi |*
*cāripāśe āra parikara tārā nirakhe o mukhaśaśī ||*

*Word for word:* tāra bāme — on His left; gadādhara — Gadadhara; nityānanda dakṣiṇe — on His right Nityananda; ānandarāśi — bliss itself; cāripāśe — all around; āra parikara tārā — the other companions; nirakhe o mukhaśaśī — gaze at that moon of a face

**2.12.** On His left is Gadadhara, on His right Nityananda, bliss itself; all around are His other companions: all gaze at that moon of a face.

নিজগণ সঙ্গে রসিকশেখর আইসে রসের ভরে ।
সে চাহনি চারু হেরিয়া এমন কে আছে পরাণ ধরে ॥

*nijagaṇa saṅge rasikaśekhara āise rasera bhare |*
*se cāhani cāru heriyā emana ke āche parāṇa dhare ||*

*Word for word:* nijagaṇa saṅge — with His own companions; rasikaśekhara — the Crown of connoisseurs of rasa; āise rasera bhare — comes overflowing with rasa; se cāhani cāru heriyā — seeing that lovely glance; emana ke āche — who is there; parāṇa dhare — who keeps hold of her heart (lit. "life")

**2.13.** With His own companions the Crown of connoisseurs of rasa comes, overflowing with rasa; who, seeing that lovely glance, can keep hold of her heart?

হাসি হাসি কথা-ছলে সুধারাশি বরিখে নদ্যার চাঁদ ।
অঙ্গ-ভঙ্গী ভারি ভুলালে ভুবন যেন সে মদনফাঁদ ॥

*hāsi hāsi kathā-chale sudhārāśi barikhe nadyāra cām̐da |*
*aṅga-bhaṅgī bhāri bhulāle bhubana yena se madanaphām̐da ||*

*Word for word:* hāsi hāsi — smiling; kathā-chale — as if in talk; sudhārāśi barikhe — showers streams of nectar; nadyāra cām̐da — the Moon of Nadia; aṅga-bhaṅgī bhāri — the grace of His form; bhulāle bhubana — captivated the world; yena se madana-phām̐da — like the snare of Madana

**2.14.** Smiling, as if in conversation, the Moon of Nadia showers streams of nectar; the grace of His form has captivated the world — like the snare of Madana.

প্রাণনাথ গতি জানি পাড়াবাসী যুবতী আসিয়ে ধাঞা ।
তা সবার শাশুড়ী ননদী দারুণ নিবারি অনেক কৈঞা ॥

*prāṇanātha gati jāni pāṛābāsī yubatī āsiye dhāñā |*
*tā sabāra śāśuṛī nanadī dāruṇa nibāri aneka kaiñā ||*

*Word for word:* prāṇanātha gati jāni — knowing the Lord of their life was coming; pāṛābāsī yubatī — the young women of the quarter; āsiye dhāñā — came running; tā sabāra śāśuṛī nanadī — their mothers-in-law and sisters-in-law; dāruṇa — harsh; nibāri aneka kaiñā — held them back with many words

**2.15.** Knowing that the Lord of their life was coming, the young women of our quarter came running; their harsh mothers-in-law and sisters-in-law held them back with many words.[^31-5]

মোরে কেহ নাহি নিবারিল মুই পূরালু মনের সাধা ।
নরহরি কহে যার পতি অতি প্রসন্ন তার কি বাধা ॥

*more keha nāhi nibārila mui pūrālu manera sādhā |*
*narahari kahe yāra pati ati prasanna tāra ki bādhā ||*

*Word for word:* more keha nāhi nibārila — no one held me back; mui pūrālu manera sādhā — I fulfilled my heart's desire; narahari kahe — Narahari says; yāra pati ati prasanna — whose husband is very gracious; tāra ki bādhā — what obstacle has she

**2.16.** But no one held me back — I fulfilled my heart's desire." Narahari says: she whose husband is so gracious — what obstacles has she?

[^31-3]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — pp. 207–208, no. 124 (scan PDF pp. 466–467); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 124 (catalogue: NG-102). GCC — kirana 7, pada 29 (ed. 1947,
pp. 89–90; scan PDF pp. 86–87; the pada begins with the first line of p. 89 — directly after the lost pp. 81–88, see n. 18 of chapter 30). GPT nos. 124–126 are
the last padas of the 7th kirana of GCC (7.29–7.31). GCC readings: "seirūpa hethā", "hema jiniyā" (2.11; GPT1 and GPT2 "hena", a misprint; translated after
GCC), "āise dhāyā … nibāre aneka kaiyā" (2.15), "pāinu manera sādhā" (2.16). B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^31-4]: The husband's speech is praise of the Lord from the lips of a householder of Nadia: Nimai Pandita has "the power of God" (īśvara-śakati), has mastered the
senses (jitendriya), is merciful to the wicked — cf. in CB (Madhya) the deliverance of Jagai and Madhai and the words that the Lord's kirtana purifies even
sinners. 2.7 — the story of the wives of the sacrificing brahmanas (Bhag. 10.23): the brahmana priests did not recognise Krishna and refused Him food, while
their wives left everything, came to Him and received His mercy. So in this pada the rightness of the women who long to see Gaura is affirmed by a husband
in conversation with his father.
[^31-5]: "The Lord of their life" (prāṇanātha) — the townswoman's word for Gaura, as in the padas of the gopis about Krishna (cf. n. 14 of chapter 30); translated
faithfully to the author. The townswoman herself in this pada only gazes at Gaura from afar, standing by the road.

## 3. Narahari — "śuna śuna sai bidhi arasika…" (GPT1 pp. 208–209, no. 125; GCC 7.30)
*Nagari-bhava. A townswoman laments that the Creator has not settled any of Gaura's companions in her street — then He would come there too;
yesterday she went with her husband's aunt to the house of Murari Gupta, where the young wives were preparing sandal paste and garlands for
Gauranga's coming, but the aunt took her away; on the road, looking back, she saw Gaura with His companions — lips, smile, brows, sandal on His
brow, necklace, gait; then her husband's elder brother appeared with his students, but he too was looking at Gora, and she, covering her face,
slipped away. The poet teases her about her shame. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 7, pada 30.*[^31-6]

শুন শুন সই বিধি অরসিক বুঝিনু কাজের গতি ।
নহিলে এমন দুঃখ কি কারণে দিবেক দিবস রাতি ॥

*śuna śuna sai bidhi arasika bujhinu kājera gati |*
*nahile emana duḥkha ki kāraṇe dibeka dibasa rāti ||*

*Word for word:* śuna śuna sai — listen, listen, friend; bidhi arasika — the Creator has no taste for rasa; bujhinu kājera gati — I understood the course of his work; nahile — otherwise; emana duḥkha — such pain; ki kāraṇe — why; dibeka dibasa rāti — would he give day and night

**3.1.** "Listen, listen, friend: the Creator has no taste for rasa — I have understood how he goes about his work; otherwise why would he give me such pain day and night?

যদি গৌর-পরিকর মাঝে কারু বসতি করাইত এথা ।
তবে এ পাড়াতে নদীয়ার শশী আসিয়া ঘুচাইত ব্যথা ॥

*yadi gaura-parikara mājhe kāru basati karāita ethā |*
*tabe e pāṛāte nadīyāra śaśī āsiyā ghucāita byathā ||*

*Word for word:* yadi — if; gaura-parikara mājhe kāru — any of Gaura's companions; basati karāita ethā — had settled here; tabe — then; e pāṛāte — to this quarter; nadīyāra śaśī — the Moon of Nadia; āsiyā ghucāita byathā — would come and dispel the grief

**3.2.** Had he settled one of Gaura's companions here, then the Moon of Nadia would come to our street too and dispel our grief.

তাহে বলি ওগো কালিকার কথা গৃহেতে সকল ছাড়ি ।
মাসৈসের সনে গেলাম সে পাড়া মুরারি গুপ্তের বাড়ী ॥

*tāhe bali ogo kālikāra kathā gṛhete sakala chāṛi |*
*māsaisera sane gelāma se pāṛā murāri guptera bāṛī ||*

*Word for word:* tāhe bali ogo — so I tell you, friend; kālikāra kathā — about yesterday; gṛhete sakala chāṛi — leaving all the housework; māsaisera sane — with the husband's aunt; gelāma se pāṛā — I went to that quarter; murāri guptera bāṛī — to the house of Murari Gupta

**3.3.** That is why I tell you: yesterday, leaving all the housework, I went with my husband's aunt to that quarter — to the house of Murari Gupta.[^31-7]

তথা বধূগণ উলসিত অতি সুখের নাহিক পার ।
প্রাণপিয়া লাগি ঘষয়ে চন্দন গাঁথয়ে কুসুমহার ॥

*tathā badhūgaṇa ulasita ati sukhera nāhika pāra |*
*prāṇapiyā lāgi ghaṣaye candana gām̐thaye kusumahāra ||*

*Word for word:* tathā — there; badhūgaṇa — the young wives; ulasita ati — greatly rejoicing; sukhera nāhika pāra — no bounds to their joy; prāṇapiyā lāgi — for the Beloved of their life; ghaṣaye candana — grind sandal paste; gām̐thaye kusumahāra — string flower garlands

**3.4.** There the young wives were rejoicing — their happiness had no bounds: for the Beloved of their life they were grinding sandal paste and stringing garlands of flowers.

তা সবার মুখে শুনিতে পাইনু গৌরাঙ্গ আসিয়ে হেথা ।
কাজ সমাধিয়া আইল মাসৈস রহিতে না পাইনু তথা ॥

*tā sabāra mukhe śunite pāinu gaurāṅga āsiye hethā |*
*kāja samādhiyā āila māsaisa rahite nā pāinu tathā ||*

*Word for word:* tā sabāra mukhe — from their lips; śunite pāinu — I heard; gaurāṅga āsiye hethā — that Gauranga would come here; kāja samādhiyā — her business done; āila māsaisa — the aunt came; rahite nā pāinu tathā — I could not stay there

**3.5.** From them I heard that Gauranga would come there; but the aunt, her business done, set off home — and I could not stay.

ভাবিতে ভাবিতে কত দূরে আসি চাহিনু পথের পানে ।
নদীয়ার নব-যুবরাজ সাজি আইসে স্বগণ সনে ॥

*bhābite bhābite kata dūre āsi cāhinu pathera pāne |*
*nadīyāra naba-yubarāja sāji āise svagaṇa sane ||*

*Word for word:* bhābite bhābite — lost in thought; kata dūre āsi — having gone some way; cāhinu pathera pāne — I looked towards the road; nadīyāra naba-yubarāja — the young crown prince of Nadia; sāji — adorned; āise svagaṇa sane — comes with His companions

**3.6.** Lost in thought, having gone some way, I looked back at the road: the young crown prince of Nadia, finely dressed, was coming with His companions.

কিবা অপরূপ অধরের শোভা দশন মুকুতা ছটা ।
হাসি সুধারাশি বরিষয়ে মুখ শরদ-শশীর ঘটা ॥

*kibā aparūpa adharera śobhā daśana mukutā chaṭā |*
*hāsi sudhārāśi bariṣaye mukha śarada-śaśīra ghaṭā ||*

*Word for word:* kibā aparūpa — what wondrous; adharera śobhā — beauty of the lips; daśana mukutā chaṭā — the teeth a gleam of pearls; hāsi — the smile; sudhārāśi bariṣaye — showers streams of nectar; mukha — the face; śarada-śaśīra ghaṭā — the splendour of the autumn moon

**3.7.** What wondrous beauty of the lips! The teeth — a gleam of pearls; the smile showers streams of nectar; the face — the splendour of the autumn moon.

কিবা ভুরুভঙ্গী বঙ্কিম-লোচন-চাহনি অনেক ভাঁতি ।
কপালে চন্দন চারু হেরইতে মজায় যুবতী জাতি ॥

*kibā bhurubhaṅgī baṅkima-locana-cāhani aneka bhām̐ti |*
*kapāle candana cāru heraite majāya yubatī jāti ||*

*Word for word:* kibā bhurubhaṅgī — and the curve of the brows; baṅkima-locana-cāhani — the glances of curving eyes; aneka bhām̐ti — in many ways; kapāle candana cāru — lovely sandal on the brow; herite — at a look; majāya yubatī jāti — drowns the whole race of young women

**3.8.** And the curve of His brows, the glances of His curving eyes — in so many ways! The sandal on His brow is so lovely — at one look all young women are drowned.

গলে দোলে হেম মণিমালা আলা করয়ে ভুবন ভালে ।
মনোহর ছাঁদে গতি তাহা দেখি জগতে কে বা না ভুলে ॥

*gale dole hema maṇimālā ālā karaye bhubana bhāle |*
*manohara chām̐de gati tāhā dekhi jagate ke bā nā bhule ||*

*Word for word:* gale dole — sways at the throat; hema maṇimālā — a necklace of gold and gems; ālā karaye bhubana bhāle — brightly lights the world; manohara chām̐de gati — the gait so enchanting; tāhā dekhi — seeing it; jagate ke vā nā bhule — who in the world would not forget himself

**3.9.** At His throat sways a necklace of gold and gems, lighting up the world; His gait is so enchanting — who in the world, seeing it, would not forget himself?

সেরূপ-সায়রে সিনাইনু সুখে রহিয়া মাসৈস কাছে ।
ফিরিয়া দেখলু পড়ুয়ার সহ ভাসুর আইসে পাছে ॥

*serūpa-sāyare sināinu sukhe rahiyā māsaisa kāche |*
*phiriyā dekhalu paṛuyāra saha bhāsura āise pāche ||*

*Word for word:* serūpa-sāyare — in the ocean of that beauty; sināinu sukhe — I bathed in joy; rahiyā māsaisa kāche — staying by the aunt; phiriyā dekhalu — turning, I saw; paṛuyāra saha — with the students; bhāsura āise pāche — the husband's elder brother coming behind

**3.10.** In the ocean of that beauty I bathed in joy, standing by my husband's aunt; turning round, I saw: behind us, with his students, came my husband's elder brother.

ভাগ্য ভাল তেঁহ মোরে না দেখিল ছিল গোরা পানে চাঞা ।
ঘুঙটে মুখ ঢাকিয়া আঁখি সম্বরি চলিলুঁ যতনে ধাঞা ॥

*bhāgya bhāla tem̐ha more nā dekhila chila gorā pāne cāñā |*
*ghuṅaṭe mukha ḍhākiyā ām̐khi sambari calilum̐ yatane dhāñā ||*

*Word for word:* bhāgya bhāla — by good luck; tem̐ha more nā dekhila — he did not see me; chila gorā pāne cāñā — he was looking at Gora; ghuṅaṭe mukha ḍhākiyā — covering my face with the veil; ām̐khi sambari — restraining my eyes; calilum̐ yatane dhāñā — I carefully hurried away

**3.11.** By good luck he did not see me — he was looking at Gora; covering my face with my veil, lowering my eyes, I carefully hurried away."

নরহরি কহে ভাসুরে যে লাজ তাহা কি না জানি আমি ।
সে সকল কথা বেকত করিলে দেশে না থাকিবে তুমি ॥

*narahari kahe bhāsure ye lāja tāhā ki nā jāni āmi |*
*se sakala kathā bekata karile deśe nā thākibe tumi ||*

*Word for word:* narahari kahe — Narahari says; bhāsure ye lāja — the shame before the husband's elder brother; tāhā ki nā jāni āmi — do I not know it; se sakala kathā — all that; bekata karile — if made known; deśe nā thākibe tumi — you would not stay in the land

**3.12.** Narahari says: your shame before your husband's elder brother — do I not know it? Were I to tell it all, you could not stay in this land.[^31-8]

[^31-6]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — pp. 208–209, no. 125 (scan PDF pp. 467–468); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 125 (catalogue: NG-103). GCC — kirana 7, pada 30 (ed. 1947,
pp. 90–91; scan PDF pp. 87–88). It is followed in GCC by a short concluding stanza (7.31, metre "surata-surati": the townswomen, recalling the past day, each tell
their own) and the colophon of the 7th kirana: "the morning doings… the description of the doings of the nagaris of Navadvipa"; stanza 7.31 was not taken
into GPT. GCC readings: "prāṇapriyā" (3.4), "gaurāṅga āsibe hethā", "rahite nā pālum̐ tathā" (3.5), "daśana tāraka-chaṭā" — "the teeth — a gleam of stars"
(3.7), "majaye yubatī jāti" (3.8), "dekhilum̐" (3.10). B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^31-7]: Murari Gupta — a physician from Shrihatta, the Lord's companion from childhood, author of a Sanskrit life of Him (Murari's "Kadacha"; our translation);
his house in Navadvipa is one of the places of the Lord's kirtanas (CB, Madhya).
[^31-8]: "The husband's elder brother" (bhāsura) — before him a young wife by custom covers her face and does not show herself. He himself, walking with his
students (paṛuyā), was also "looking at Gora". The last line is the poet's joke: the whole street would know at whom she was gazing; translated as in the
original.

## 4. Narahari — "śuna śuna sai niśira kāhinī…" (GPT1 pp. 209–210, no. 126; GCC 8.2)
*Nagari-bhava; a dream. A townswoman tells her friend about the night: in the evening, thinking of Gaura, she went with her mother-in-law to
the house of Srivasa Pandita, where Gora sat among His companions and talked smilingly with Gadadhara; for fear of her mother-in-law she
could not stay and returned home, lay down without supper and fell asleep only late at night; in her dream she came again to Srivasa's house,
anointed Gora with sandal paste, put garlands on Him — and on some pretext He embraced her. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably
Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 8, pada 2.*[^31-9]

শুন শুন সই নিশির কাহিনী যতনে কহিয়ে তোরে ।
সাঁঝের বেলাতে কাজ সমাধিয়া বসিয়া আছিলুঁ ঘরে ॥

*śuna śuna sai niśira kāhinī yatane kahiye tore |*
*sām̐jhera belāte kāja samādhiyā basiyā āchilum̐ ghare ||*

*Word for word:* śuna śuna sai — listen, listen, friend; niśira kāhinī — the tale of the night; yatane kahiye tore — I will carefully tell you; sām̐jhera belāte — at dusk; kāja samādhiyā — the work done; basiyā āchilum̐ ghare — I was sitting at home

**4.1.** "Listen, listen, friend: what happened at night I will carefully tell you. At dusk, my work done, I was sitting at home.

গোরারূপগুণ ভাবিতে ভাবিতে না জানি কি হৈল মনে ।
শ্রীবাস পণ্ডিত ঠাকুরের বাড়ী গেলাম শাশুড়ী সনে ॥

*gorārūpaguṇa bhābite bhābite nā jāni ki haila mane |*
*śrībāsa paṇḍita ṭhākurera bāṛī gelāma śāśuṛī sane ||*

*Word for word:* gorārūpaguṇa — Gora's beauty and virtues; bhābite bhābite — thinking and thinking; nā jāni ki haila mane — I do not know what came over me; śrībāsa paṇḍita ṭhākurera bāṛī — to the house of Srivasa Pandita Thakura; gelāma śāśuṛī sane — I went with my mother-in-law

**4.2.** Thinking and thinking of Gora's beauty and virtues — I do not know what came over me — I went with my mother-in-law to the house of Srivasa Pandita Thakura.

তথা নিরুপম পরিকর মাঝে বসিয়া আছেন গোরা ।
কুলবতী সতী যুবতী জনের ধৈরজ-রতনচোরা ॥

*tathā nirupama parikara mājhe basiyā āchena gorā |*
*kulabatī satī yubatī janera dhairaja-ratanacorā ||*

*Word for word:* tathā — there; nirupama parikara mājhe — among peerless companions; basiyā āchena gorā — Gora is seated; kulabatī satī yubatī janera — of young women well-born and chaste; dhairaja-ratana-corā — the thief of the jewel of composure

**4.3.** There, among His peerless companions, Gora is seated — the thief of the precious composure of young women, well-born and chaste.

ঝলমল হেমতনু তাহে মাখা সুচারু চন্দনরাশি ।
সুমেরু পর্বত লেপিয়াছে জনু বাটিয়া শারদশশী ॥

*jhalamala hematanu tāhe mākhā sucāru candanarāśi |*
*sumeru parvata lepiyāche janu bāṭiyā śāradaśaśī ||*

*Word for word:* jhalamala — shining; hematanu — the golden body; tāhe mākhā — smeared on it; sucāru candanarāśi — lovely sandal paste; sumeru parvata — Mount Sumeru; lepiyāche janu — as if smeared; bāṭiyā śāradaśaśī — with the ground-up autumn moon

**4.4.** His golden body shines, anointed with lovely sandal paste — as if Mount Sumeru had been smeared with the ground-up autumn moon.

মালতীর মালা গলে দোলে যেন ভুবনমোহন ফাঁদ ।
কত কত শত মদন মূরছে নিরখি বদনছাঁদ ॥

*mālatīra mālā gale dole yena bhubanamohana phām̐da |*
*kata kata śata madana mūrache nirakhi badanachām̐da ||*

*Word for word:* mālatīra mālā — a garland of malati; gale dole — sways at the throat; yena bhubanamohana phām̐da — like a snare enchanting the world; kata kata śata madana — hundreds upon hundreds of Madanas; mūrache — swoon; nirakhi badanachām̐da — seeing the shape of His face

**4.5.** A garland of malati sways at His throat — like a snare enchanting the world; hundreds upon hundreds of Madanas swoon at the sight of the shape of His face.

হাসিয়া হাসিয়া গদাধর সনে কহয়ে মধুর কথা ।
বরষিয়া সুধা রাশি রাশি দূর করয়ে শ্রবণ-ব্যথা ॥

*hāsiyā hāsiyā gadādhara sane kahaye madhura kathā |*
*baraṣiyā sudhā rāśi rāśi dūra karaye śrabaṇa-byathā ||*

*Word for word:* hāsiyā hāsiyā — smiling; gadādhara sane — with Gadadhara; kahaye madhura kathā — speaks sweet words; baraṣiyā sudhā rāśi rāśi — showering nectar in streams; dūra karaye śrabaṇa-byathā — removes the ache of the ears

**4.6.** Smiling, He holds sweet converse with Gadadhara; showering nectar in streams, He soothes the ache of the ears.

মরি মরি যেন সে শোভা হেরিতে পরাণ কেমন করে ।
কি কব ক্ষণেক দুটী আঁখি ভরি দেখিতে না পালুঁ তারে ॥

*mari mari yena se śobhā herite parāṇa kemana kare |*
*ki kaba kṣaṇeka duṭī ām̐khi bhari dekhite nā pālum̐ tāre ||*

*Word for word:* mari mari — ah, ah (lit. "I die"); yena se śobhā herite — at the sight of such beauty; parāṇa kemana kare — what becomes of the heart; ki kaba — what shall I say; kṣaṇeka — for a moment; duṭī ām̐khi bhari — to the fill of both eyes; dekhite nā pālum̐ tāre — I could not see Him

**4.7.** Ah, ah! At the sight of such beauty, what becomes of the heart! What shall I say — not for one moment could I gaze my fill of Him with both my eyes.

মুই অভাগিনী কি করিব বিধি কৈল পরবশ নারী ।
শাশুড়ীর ভয়ে রহিতে নারিলুঁ আইনুঁ পরাণে মরি ॥

*mui abhāginī ki kariba bidhi kaila parabaśa nārī |*
*śāśuṛīra bhaye rahite nārilum̐ āinum̐ parāṇe mari ||*

*Word for word:* mui abhāginī — wretched me; ki kariba — what could I do; bidhi kaila parabaśa nārī — the Creator made woman dependent; śāśuṛīra bhaye — for fear of the mother-in-law; rahite nārilum̐ — I could not stay; āinum̐ parāṇe mari — I came home dying at heart

**4.8.** Wretched me, what could I do? The Creator made woman dependent. For fear of my mother-in-law I could not stay and came home, dying at heart.

মনের দুঃখেতে শুতিনুঁ ননদ সুধাইলে কলুঁ তারে ।
ক্ষুধা নাহি মোর মোরে না জাগাবে গা মোর কেমন করে ॥

*manera duḥkhete śutinum̐ nanada sudhāile kalum̐ tāre |*
*kṣudhā nāhi mora more nā jāgābe gā mora kemana kare ||*

*Word for word:* manera duḥkhete — in grief of heart; śutinum̐ — I lay down; nanada sudhāile — when my sister-in-law asked; kalum̐ tāre — I told her; kṣudhā nāhi mora — I am not hungry; more nā jāgābe — do not wake me; gā mora kemana kare — I feel somehow unwell (lit. "my body feels strange")

**4.9.** In grief I lay down; when my sister-in-law asked, I told her: 'I am not hungry, do not wake me — I feel somehow unwell.'

সে অতি সরলা ফিরি গেল মুই রহিলুঁ ব্যাকুলচিতে ।
তনু আনছান করে ওগো নিঁদ আইল অনেক রাতে ॥

*se ati saralā phiri gela mui rahilum̐ byākulacite |*
*tanu ānachāna kare ogo nim̐da āila aneka rāte ||*

*Word for word:* se ati saralā — she, a simple soul; phiri gela — went away; mui rahilum̐ byākulacite — I stayed distraught; tanu ānachāna kare — the body was restless; ogo — friend; nim̐da āila aneka rāte — sleep came late in the night

**4.10.** She, a simple soul, went away, and I lay there distraught; my body was restless, friend — sleep came only deep in the night.

স্বপনে শ্রীবাস ঠাকুরের বাড়ী যাইয়া দেখিলুঁ তায় ।
কত মন-সাধে সুগন্ধি চন্দন মাখাইলুঁ গোরা গায় ॥

*svapane śrībāsa ṭhākurera bāṛī yāiyā dekhilum̐ tāya |*
*kata mana-sādhe sugandhi candana mākhāilum̐ gorā gāya ||*

*Word for word:* svapane — in a dream; śrībāsa ṭhākurera bāṛī — to the house of Srivasa Thakura; yāiyā dekhilum̐ tāya — going there I saw Him; kata mana-sādhe — with all my heart's longing; sugandhi candana — fragrant sandal paste; mākhāilum̐ gorā gāya — I anointed Gora's body

**4.11.** In my dream I went to the house of Srivasa Thakura and saw Him; with all the longing of my heart I anointed Gora's body with fragrant sandal paste.

বিবিধ ফুলের নব নব মালা যতনে দিলাম গলে ।
নরহরি-প্রাণ রসিকশেখর আলিঙ্গন কৈল ছলে ॥

*bibidha phulera naba naba mālā yatane dilāma gale |*
*narahari-prāṇa rasikaśekhara āliṅgana kaila chale ||*

*Word for word:* bibidha phulera — of many flowers; naba naba mālā — fresh garland after garland; yatane dilāma gale — I carefully put on His neck; narahari-prāṇa — the life of Narahari; rasikaśekhara — the Crown of connoisseurs of rasa; āliṅgana kaila chale — on a pretext embraced

**4.12.** Carefully I put on His neck garland after fresh garland of many flowers; and the life of Narahari, the Crown of connoisseurs of rasa, on some pretext embraced [me]."[^31-10]

[^31-9]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — pp. 209–210, no. 126 (scan PDF pp. 468–469); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 126 (catalogue: NG-343). GCC — kirana 8, pada 2 (ed. 1947,
p. 92; scan PDF p. 89), "kācidāha — yathā[rāga]" ("one of them said"). The 8th kirana of GCC (colophon: "…the description of the tales of dreams") continues the
nagaris' "morning": it opens with pada 8.1 (raga vibhasa, not taken into GPT) — at dawn the friends gather, laughing, and each without shame tells her dream;
GPT nos. 126–144 are these tales. GCC readings: "basiyā āchilum̐", "gorā rūpa-guṇa", "śarada śaśī" (4.4), "bhubana-mohana-phānda", "badana-chānda" (4.5),
"mākhālum̐ gaura gāya" (4.11). B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^31-10]: The townswoman's dream (4.11–4.12): the embrace (āliṅgana) is a direct motif of sambhoga; translated exactly, adding nothing. The dream is her imagination:
the Lord in His lila did not touch women and in Navadvipa did not look at them (CB, Adi; introductory note, chapter 27), and the Gaudiya tradition does not
accept the worship of Gaura as a nagara ("gaura-nagari" is counted by Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati among the apasampradayas). Majumdar regards the long GPT padas
signed Narahari as late, not Sarakara's; these padas indeed belong to Narahari Chakravarti (18th c.). The signature merges with the townswoman's speech:
"the life of Narahari" (narahari-prāṇa) is an epithet of Gaura (cf. "Narahari's Lord"). Srivasa's house is the place of the Lord's night kirtanas (CB, Madhya;
there the doors were barred and outsiders not admitted) — here only the backdrop of the tale.

## 5. Narahari — "śuna śuna ohe parāṇa sajani…" (GPT1 pp. 210–211, no. 127; GCC 8.3)
*Nagari-bhava; a dream. A townswoman tells her dream: adorned, she sat in a kunja, pining; suddenly at the entrance there appeared a youth, a
kishora the colour of a rain-cloud — with a peacock feather on His crown, a flute at His lips, a pearl necklace; He came near, jested, beckoned
her with His glance; and as she watched, the Dark One became Gora; He sat beside her, she turned away in feigned anger, He begged forgiveness —
and the dream ends with their meeting. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 8, pada 3.*[^31-11]

শুন শুন ওহে পরাণ সজনি কহিয়ে তোমার ঠাঁই ।
আজুক যেরূপ স্বপন এমন কখন দেখিএ নাই ॥

*śuna śuna ohe parāṇa sajani kahiye tomāra ṭhām̐i |*
*ājuka yerūpa svapana emana kakhana dekhie nāi ||*

*Word for word:* śuna śuna ohe — listen, listen; parāṇa sajani — friend of my heart; kahiye tomāra ṭhām̐i — I tell you; ājuka yerūpa svapana — a dream such as tonight's; emana kakhana dekhie nāi — I have never seen

**5.1.** "Listen, listen, friend of my heart, to you I will tell it: a dream such as tonight's I have never seen.

নিকুঞ্জভবনে বসিয়া আছিলুঁ করিয়া বিবিধ বেশ ।
ভাবিতে ভাবিতে দেহ ক্ষীণ মোর না ছিল সুখের লেশ ॥

*nikuñjabhabane basiyā āchilum̐ kariyā bibidha beśa |*
*bhābite bhābite deha kṣīṇa mora nā chila sukhera leśa ||*

*Word for word:* nikuñjabhabane — in the kunja bower; basiyā āchilum̐ — I was sitting; kariyā bibidha beśa — adorned in every way; bhābite bhābite — thinking and thinking; deha kṣīṇa mora — my body wasted; nā chila sukhera leśa — there was no trace of joy

**5.2.** I was sitting in a kunja bower, adorned in every way; thinking and thinking, my body had wasted away, there was not a trace of joy in it.

চঞ্চল-নয়ানে চাহি চারি পানে না জানি কি হৈল মোরে ।
তথা আচম্বিতে দেখিলুঁ জনেক আইল বাহির দ্বারে ॥

*cañcala-nayāne cāhi cāri pāne nā jāni ki haila more |*
*tathā ācambite dekhilum̐ janeka āila bāhira dvāre ||*

*Word for word:* cañcala-nayāne — with restless eyes; cāhi cāri pāne — I look in all directions; nā jāni ki haila more — I do not know what befell me; tathā ācambite — then suddenly; dekhilum̐ janeka — I saw someone; āila bāhira dvāre — come to the outer door

**5.3.** With restless eyes I looked in every direction — I do not know what had come over me; and suddenly I saw: someone had come to the outer door.

কিবা অপরূপ বয়স কিশোর রসের মূরতি জনু ।
নাগর গরিমা কি কব তাহার মেঘের বরণ তনু ॥

*kibā aparūpa bayasa kiśora rasera mūrati janu |*
*nāgara garimā ki kaba tāhāra meghera baraṇa tanu ||*

*Word for word:* kibā aparūpa — what wondrous; bayasa kiśora — youthful age, kishora; rasera mūrati janu — as if rasa embodied; nāgara garimā — the majesty of the nagara; ki kaba tāhāra — what shall I say of Him; meghera baraṇa tanu — a body the colour of a cloud

**5.4.** What wondrous youth — a kishora, as if rasa itself in bodily form! What shall I say of the majesty of that nagara? His body is the colour of a rain-cloud.

অরুণ জিনিয়া করপদতল নখরনিচয় চাঁদ ।
অলকা তিলক ভালে শোভে যেন ভুবনমোহন ফাঁদ ॥

*aruṇa jiniyā karapadatala nakharanicaya cām̐da |*
*alakā tilaka bhāle śobhe yena bhubanamohana phām̐da ||*

*Word for word:* aruṇa jiniyā — outshining the dawn; karapadatala — palms and soles; nakharanicaya cām̐da — the nails a cluster of moons; alakā tilaka — curls and tilaka; bhāle śobhe — shine on the brow; yena bhubanamohana phām̐da — like a snare enchanting the world

**5.5.** His palms and soles outshine the dawn, His nails are a cluster of moons; the curls and the tilaka on His brow are lovely — like a snare enchanting the world.

চূড়ার টালনি চারু নিরুপম উড়য়ে ময়ূরপাখা ।
তাই সুকুসুম-সৌরভে ভ্রমর ভ্রময়ে নাহিক লেখা ॥

*cūṛāra ṭālani cāru nirupama uṛaye mayūrapākhā |*
*tāi sukusuma-saurabhe bhramara bhramaye nāhika lekhā ||*

*Word for word:* cūṛāra ṭālani — the tilt of the crown; cāru — graceful; nirupama — peerless; uṛaye mayūrapākhā — the peacock feather flutters; tāi — there; sukusuma-saurabhe — at the fragrance of fine flowers; bhramara bhramaye — bees hover; nāhika lekhā — beyond counting

**5.6.** His crown is gracefully tilted, a peerless peacock feather flutters; to the fragrance of its fine flowers bees come swarming — there is no counting them.

অধরের অধঃ ধরিয়া মুরলী রহিয়া রহিয়া পূরে ।
জগতের মাঝে কে আছে এমন শুনিয়া ধৈরজ ধরে ॥

*adharera adhaḥ dhariyā muralī rahiyā rahiyā pūre |*
*jagatera mājhe ke āche emana śuniyā dhairaja dhare ||*

*Word for word:* adharera adhaḥ dhariyā muralī — holding the flute to the lower lip; rahiyā rahiyā pūre — plays it again and again; jagatera mājhe — in the world; ke āche emana — who is there; śuniyā dhairaja dhare — who hearing keeps composure

**5.7.** Holding the flute to His lower lip, He plays it again and again: who in the world, hearing it, can keep composure?

গলায় দোথরি মুকুতার মালা সুরধুনীধারা প্রায় ।
চলিতে কিঙ্কিণী কটিতটে বাজে সুন্দর নূপুর পায় ॥

*galāya dothari mukutāra mālā suradhunīdhārā prāya |*
*calite kiṅkiṇī kaṭitaṭe bāje sundara nūpura pāya ||*

*Word for word:* galāya dothari mukutāra mālā — a double string of pearls at the neck; suradhunī-dhārā prāya — like the streams of the Suradhuni; calite — as He walks; kiṅkiṇī kaṭitaṭe bāje — the bell-belt tinkles on the hips; sundara nūpura pāya — lovely anklets on the feet

**5.8.** On His neck — a double string of pearls, like the streams of the Suradhuni; as He walks, the belt of bells on His hips tinkles, and lovely anklets on His feet.

ভুরুযুগবর ভঙ্গী করি মোর নিকটে আসিয়া সে ।
কত কত ছলে করে পরিহাস তাহা বা বুঝিবে কে ॥

*bhuruyugabara bhaṅgī kari mora nikaṭe āsiyā se |*
*kata kata chale kare parihāsa tāhā bā bujhibe ke ||*

*Word for word:* bhuruyugabara bhaṅgī kari — with a graceful play of the brows; mora nikaṭe āsiyā se — He came near me; kata kata chale — in so many ways; kare parihāsa — He jests; tāhā vā bujhibe ke — who will understand it

**5.9.** With a graceful play of His brows He came up to me — and in how many ways He jested: who could understand it?

হাসিয়া হাসিয়া আমাপানে চাঞা ঠারয়ে আঁখির কোণে ।
ঘুচয়ে ঘুঙট কপটে কি করে পরাণ সহিত টানে ॥

*hāsiyā hāsiyā āmāpāne cāñā ṭhāraye ām̐khira koṇe |*
*ghucaye ghuṅaṭa kapaṭe ki kare parāṇa sahita ṭāne ||*

*Word for word:* hāsiyā hāsiyā — smiling; āmāpāne cāñā — looking at me; ṭhāraye ām̐khira koṇe — signals with the corners of His eyes; ghucaye ghuṅaṭa — removes the veil; kapaṭe — by a trick; ki kare — what He does; parāṇa sahita ṭāne — draws my very life

**5.10.** Smiling, looking at me, He signals with the corners of His eyes; with a trick He lifts away my veil — what is He doing! — He draws my very life to Himself.

আর অপরূপ দেখিতে দেখিতে সে শ্যাম হৈল গোরা ।
কি দিব উপমা কত কত সতী যুবতী-পরাণচোরা ॥

*āra aparūpa dekhite dekhite se śyāma haila gorā |*
*ki diba upamā kata kata satī yubatī-parāṇacorā ||*

*Word for word:* āra aparūpa — another wonder; dekhite dekhite — as I watched; se śyāma haila gorā — that Dark One became Gora; ki diba upamā — what comparison can I give; kata kata satī yubatī-parāṇa-corā — the thief of the life of so many chaste young wives

**5.11.** And another wonder: as I watched, that Dark One became Gora. With what shall I compare Him — the thief of the life of so many chaste young wives?

ধীর ধীর করি নিকট আসিয়া বসিয়া আমার পাশে ।
মধুর মধুর বচনে তোষয়ে অঙ্গের পরশ-আশে ॥

*dhīra dhīra kari nikaṭa āsiyā basiyā āmāra pāśe |*
*madhura madhura bacane toṣaye aṅgera paraśa-āśe ||*

*Word for word:* dhīra dhīra kari — slowly, slowly; nikaṭa āsiyā — coming near; basiyā āmāra pāśe — sitting beside me; madhura madhura bacane — with sweet, sweet words; toṣaye — He soothes; aṅgera paraśa-āśe — longing to touch

**5.12.** Slowly, slowly He came near and sat beside me; with sweet, sweet words He soothes me, longing to touch.

মিছা ক্রোধে মুই মুখ ফিরাইলুঁ সুখের নাহিক ওর ।
ক্ষম অপরাধ বলিয়া সে পুনঃ আঁচরে ধরল মোর ॥

*michā krodhe mui mukha phirāilum̐ sukhera nāhika ora |*
*kṣama aparādha baliyā se punaḥ ām̐care dharala mora ||*

*Word for word:* michā krodhe — in feigned anger; mui mukha phirāilum̐ — I turned my face away; sukhera nāhika ora — yet my joy had no bounds; kṣama aparādha baliyā — saying "forgive the offence"; se punaḥ — He again; ām̐care dharala mora — caught the end of my sari

**5.13.** In feigned anger I turned my face away — yet my joy had no bounds; 'Forgive My offence,' He said, and again caught the end of my sari.

অঙ্গ পরশিতে অবশ হইয়া মজিলুঁ উহার সনে ।
নরহরি-প্রাণপতি সুরসিক কৈল যে আছিল মনে ॥

*aṅga paraśite abaśa haiyā majilum̐ uhāra sane |*
*narahari-prāṇapati surasika kaila ye āchila mane ||*

*Word for word:* aṅga paraśite — at the touch of His body; abaśa haiyā — growing helpless; majilum̐ uhāra sane — I was lost in Him; narahari-prāṇapati — the Lord of Narahari's life; surasika — the great Connoisseur of rasa; kaila ye āchila mane — did what was in His heart

**5.14.** At the touch of His body I grew helpless and was lost in Him." The Lord of Narahari's life, the great Connoisseur of rasa, did what was in His heart.[^31-12]

[^31-11]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — pp. 210–211, no. 127 (scan PDF pp. 469–470); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 127 (catalogue: NG-104; the catalogue line "aruṇa jiniyā…"
is from the middle of the pada). GCC — kirana 8, pada 3 (ed. 1947, pp. 93–94; scan PDF pp. 90–91), "anyā ca — yathārāga" ("and another"). GCC readings:
"dekhiye nāi" (5.1), "nakhara-nicaya cānda" (5.5), "uṛaye mayūra pākhā" (5.6; GPT1 and GPT2 "ubhaye", probably a misprint; translated after GCC), "muralī"
(5.7), "kaṭi taṭe", "sundara nūpura" (5.8), "majila uhāra sane" (5.14). B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^31-12]: The townswoman's dream (5.12–5.14): the longing to touch, the touch, and "was lost in Him" (majilum̐ uhāra sane) are a direct motif of sambhoga; translated
exactly, adding nothing and softening nothing. The dream is her imagination: the Lord in His lila did not touch women and in Navadvipa did not look at them
(CB, Adi; introductory note, chapter 27); the Gaudiya tradition does not accept the worship of Gaura as a nagara ("gaura-nagari" is counted by Bhaktisiddhanta
Sarasvati among the apasampradayas); according to Majumdar such GPT padas signed Narahari are late (here — Narahari Chakravarti, 18th c.). The Dark One
becoming Gora in the dream (5.11) is a poetic image of the identity of Gaura and Krishna (CC Adi 1.5; cf. the Lord's revealing of Shyamasundara to Ramananda
Raya — CC Madhya 8). "The Lord of Narahari's life" (narahari-prāṇapati) — a signature merged with the speech: Gaura is the Lord of the poet's life.

## 6. Narahari — "ājuka rajanī sukhamaya svapana…" (GPT1 pp. 211–212, no. 128; GCC 8.4)
*Nagari-bhava; a dream. A townswoman tells her friends a dream about themselves: adorned, they sat together and sang of Gaura for a watch of the night,
then sent a messenger to Gauranga; hearing of Him, they ran to the kunja; He seated them, jested, wounded them with His glance, embraced them. The
poet: why be ashamed to tell of yourself? Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 8, pada 4.*[^31-13]

আজুক রজনী সুখময় স্বপন দেখিনু সই ।
তোমরা পরমধন্যা জগমাঝে শুনহ সে কথা কই ॥

*ājuka rajanī sukhamaya svapana dekhinu sai |*
*tomarā paramadhanyā jagamājhe śunaha se kathā kai ||*

*Word for word:* ājuka rajanī — tonight; sukhamaya svapana — a blissful dream; dekhinu sai — I saw, friends; tomarā paramadhanyā — you are most fortunate; jagamājhe — in the world; śunaha se kathā kai — listen, I tell it

**6.1.** "Tonight I saw a blissful dream, friends: you are the most fortunate in the world; listen, I will tell it.

নিজ নিজ বেশ বিরচি চঞ্চল তোমরা বিরলে বসি ।
গোরাগুণ গান গাইয়া গাইয়া গোঙাইলা প্রহর নিশি ॥

*nija nija beśa biraci cañcala tomarā birale basi |*
*gorāguṇa gāna gāiyā gāiyā goṅāilā prahara niśi ||*

*Word for word:* nija nija beśa biraci — each adorning herself; cañcala — eager; tomarā birale basi — you sitting in seclusion; gorāguṇa gāna gāiyā gāiyā — singing and singing of Gora's virtues; goṅāilā prahara niśi — you passed a watch of the night

**6.2.** Each adorned in her own way, eager, you sat together in a secluded place; singing and singing songs of Gora's virtues, you passed a watch of the night.

সময় জানিয়া দূতী পাঠাইলা গোবিন্দ আছেন যথা ।
সে অতি তুরিতে যাইয়া গৌরাঙ্গে কহিল সকল কথা ॥

*samaya jāniyā dūtī pāṭhāilā gobinda āchena yathā |*
*se ati turite yāiyā gaurāṅge kahila sakala kathā ||*

*Word for word:* samaya jāniyā — knowing the time; dūtī pāṭhāilā — you sent a messenger; gobinda āchena yathā — to where Govinda is; se ati turite yāiyā — she going very quickly; gaurāṅge kahila sakala kathā — told Gauranga everything

**6.3.** Choosing the moment, you sent a messenger to where Govinda was; she went very quickly and told Gauranga everything.[^31-14]

পুন সে তুরিতে তোমাদের পাশে আইলা আতুর হৈয়া ।
প্রাণপ্রিয়-কথা তার মুখে শুনি চলিল সকলে ধাঞা ॥

*puna se turite tomādera pāśe āilā ātura haiyā |*
*prāṇapriya-kathā tāra mukhe śuni calila sakale dhāñā ||*

*Word for word:* puna se turite — she again quickly; tomādera pāśe āilā — came back to you; ātura haiyā — agitated; prāṇapriya-kathā — news of the Beloved of your life; tāra mukhe śuni — hearing from her lips; calila sakale dhāñā — all ran

**6.4.** Just as quickly she came back to you, herself agitated; hearing from her lips the news of the Beloved of your life, you all ran.

দূরে থাকি গোরারূপের মাধুরী হেরিয়া মোহিত হৈলা ।
নিকুঞ্জ-ভবনে প্রবেশিয়া প্রাণনাথের নিকট গেলা ॥

*dūre thāki gorārūpera mādhurī heriyā mohita hailā |*
*nikuñja-bhabane prabeśiyā prāṇanāthera nikaṭa gelā ||*

*Word for word:* dūre thāki — from afar; gorārūpera mādhurī — the sweetness of Gora's form; heriyā mohita hailā — seeing, you were enchanted; nikuñja-bhabane prabeśiyā — entering the kunja bower; prāṇanāthera nikaṭa gelā — you went up to the Lord of your life

**6.5.** From afar, seeing the sweetness of Gora's form, you were enchanted; entering the kunja bower, you came up to the Lord of your life.

সে অতি আদর করি বসাইল ধরিয়া সবার করে ।
হাসিয়া হাসিয়া কত পরিহাস করিলা পরস্পরে ॥

*se ati ādara kari basāila dhariyā sabāra kare |*
*hāsiyā hāsiyā kata parihāsa karilā paraspare ||*

*Word for word:* se ati ādara kari — He with great tenderness; basāila dhariyā sabāra kare — seated you, taking each by the hand; hāsiyā hāsiyā — smiling; kata parihāsa karilā — how many jests were made; paraspare — with one another

**6.6.** With great tenderness He seated you, taking each by the hand; smiling, how many jests He and you exchanged with one another!

গোরা সুচতুর নয়নের কোণে হানিল বিষম বাণ ।
তাহাতে বিবশ হইয়া রাখিতে নারিলা যৌবন মান ॥

*gorā sucatura nayanera koṇe hānila biṣama bāṇa |*
*tāhāte bibaśa haiyā rākhite nārilā yaubana māna ||*

*Word for word:* gorā sucatura — most clever Gora; nayanera koṇe — from the corners of His eyes; hānila biṣama bāṇa — shot a fearful arrow; tāhāte bibaśa haiyā — overcome by it; rākhite nārilā yaubana māna — you could not keep the pride of youth

**6.7.** Most clever Gora shot a fearful arrow from the corners of His eyes; by it you were overcome and could not keep the pride of youth.

তোমা সবাকার ভুরু-ভুজঙ্গমে সঘনে দংশন কৈল ।
নদীয়াচাঁদের যে ছিল ধৈরজ তা যেন তখনি গেল ॥

*tomā sabākāra bhuru-bhujaṅgame saghane daṃśana kaila |*
*nadīyācām̐dera ye chila dhairaja tā yena takhani gela ||*

*Word for word:* tomā sabākāra — of all of you; bhuru-bhujaṅgame — the serpents of the brows; saghane daṃśana kaila — bit again and again; nadīyācām̐dera — of the Moon of Nadia; ye chila dhairaja — the composure that was; tā yena takhani gela — seemed at once to go

**6.8.** The serpents of all your brows bit Him again and again — and the composure the Moon of Nadia had seemed at once to leave Him.

দুবাহু পসারি করে আলিঙ্গন অতুল উহার লেহ ।
সুবহু হরষে ঠারিনু বুঝিয়া অধিক মাতিল সেহ ॥

*dubāhu pasāri kare āliṅgana atula uhāra leha |*
*subahu haraṣe ṭhārinu bujhiyā adhika mātila seha ||*

*Word for word:* dubāhu pasāri — opening both arms; kare āliṅgana — He embraces; atula uhāra leha — peerless is His love; subahu haraṣe — in great joy; ṭhārinu — I made a sign (?); bujhiyā — understanding; adhika mātila seha — He (or "that love") grew more intoxicated

**6.9.** Opening both arms, He embraces — peerless is His love; in great joy I made a sign — and, understanding it, He grew still more intoxicated.

তোমাদের মনে যে ছিল সে সাধ পূরিল রসিকরাজ ।
নরহরি কহে নিজ কথা কেন কহিতে বাসহ লাজ ॥

*tomādera mane ye chila se sādha pūrila rasikarāja |*
*narahari kahe nija kathā kena kahite bāsaha lāja ||*

*Word for word:* tomādera mane — in your hearts; ye chila se sādha — the desire that was; pūrila rasikarāja — the King of connoisseurs of rasa fulfilled; narahari kahe — Narahari says; nija kathā — your own story; kena kahite bāsaha lāja — why are you ashamed to tell

**6.10.** The desire that was in your hearts the King of connoisseurs of rasa fulfilled." Narahari says: why are you ashamed to tell of yourself?[^31-15]

[^31-13]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — pp. 211–212, no. 128 (scan PDF pp. 470–471); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 128 (catalogue: NG-105). GCC — kirana 8, pada 4 (ed. 1947,
p. 94; scan PDF p. 91), "anyā ca — yathārāga". GCC readings: "sukhamaya saba svapana" (6.1), "gorā-guṇagaṇa … gom̐āilā" (6.2), "karilā paraspare" — "jested with
one another" (6.6; adopted in the main text: GPT1 and GPT2 "paraśa pare" — "touching", a misprint, as in 22.7), "tā yena takhani gela" (6.8; GPT1 and GPT2 "mena"), "tomādera mane ye chila tā yena karila rasikarāja" (6.10; the OCR is uncertain). B.
Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^31-14]: "To where Govinda was" (gobinda āchena yathā): the messenger speaks with Gauranga — Govinda here is apparently Krishna's name given to Gaura (cf. "the Moon
of Gokula", chapter 29); another understanding is also possible — the house of Govinda (Ghosha or another companion) where the Lord was. The messenger (dūtī)
is an image from the padas on Radha and Krishna.
[^31-15]: The dream (6.6–6.10): touches, embrace, the "composure leaving" the Moon of Nadia are direct motifs of sambhoga and attraction; translated exactly, adding
nothing and softening nothing. The dream is the townswoman's imagination, not the Lord's lila: the Lord did not touch women (CB, Adi); the tradition does not
accept gaura-nagari (n. 10 and the introductory note, chapter 27). 6.9: "I made a sign — and, understanding it, He grew still more intoxicated" (subahu haraṣe
ṭhārinu bujhiyā adhika mātila seha) — the sense of the line is unclear ("seha" may mean "he" or "that love"). The poet's signature (6.10) is a joke: under the
guise of a dream about her friends the teller is telling her own.

## 7. Narahari — "śuna śuna sai svapane dekhinu nikuñjakānane gorā…" (GPT1 p. 212, no. 129; GCC 8.5)
*Nagari-bhava; a dream. A friend tells the heroine her dream: Gora in a kunja grove was gazing at her path and weeping; learning from the friend
that she would come, He begged her to hasten; the heroine, adorned, came, and the King of connoisseurs of rasa embraced her; then on some
pretext she became manini — and He entreats her to relent; at this the teller woke. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** —
GCC, kirana 8, pada 5.*[^31-16]

শুন শুন সই স্বপনে দেখিনু নিকুঞ্জকাননে গোরা ।
তুয়া পথ পানে নিরখি কাতরে ঝরয়ে লোচনলোরা ॥

*śuna śuna sai svapane dekhinu nikuñjakānane gorā |*
*tuyā patha pāne nirakhi kātare jharaye locanalorā ||*

*Word for word:* śuna śuna sai — listen, listen, friend; svapane dekhinu — in a dream I saw; nikuñjakānane gorā — Gora in a kunja grove; tuyā patha pāne nirakhi — gazing at your path; kātare — in anguish; jharaye locanalorā — tears flow from His eyes

**7.1.** "Listen, listen, friend: in a dream I saw Gora in a kunja grove — gazing at your path, in anguish He was shedding tears.

মোর মুখে তুয়া গমন শুনিয়া কত না সাধিল মোরে ।
অতি তরাতরি হেরি তার দশা আসিয়া কহিনু তোরে ॥

*mora mukhe tuyā gamana śuniyā kata nā sādhila more |*
*ati tarātari heri tāra daśā āsiyā kahinu tore ||*

*Word for word:* mora mukhe — from my lips; tuyā gamana śuniyā — hearing of your coming; kata nā sādhila more — how He pleaded with me; ati tarātari — in great haste; heri tāra daśā — seeing His state; āsiyā kahinu tore — I came and told you

**7.2.** Hearing from me that you were coming, how He pleaded with me! Seeing His state, I came in haste and told you.

শুনিয়া উলসে বেশ বনাইয়া ভেটিলা নিকুঞ্জ মাঝ ।
দূরেতে আদরি ধরি করে কোরে করিল রসিকরাজ ॥

*śuniyā ulase beśa banāiyā bheṭilā nikuñja mājha |*
*dūrete ādari dhari kare kore karila rasikarāja ||*

*Word for word:* śuniyā — hearing; ulase beśa banāiyā — joyfully adorning yourself; bheṭilā nikuñja mājha — you met (Him) in the kunja; dūrete ādari — welcoming from afar; dhari kare — taking your hand; kore karila — took you in His embrace; rasikarāja — the King of connoisseurs of rasa

**7.3.** Hearing it, you joyfully adorned yourself and met Him in the kunja; welcoming you from afar, the King of connoisseurs of rasa took your hand and drew you into His embrace.

উপজিল কত কৌতুক ছলেতে মানিনী হইলা তুমি ।
নরহরি পহুঁ করয়ে মিনতি জাগি বিয়াকুল আমি ॥

*upajila kata kautuka chalete māninī hailā tumi |*
*narahari pahum̐ karaye minati jāgi biyākula āmi ||*

*Word for word:* upajila kata kautuka — how much jesting arose; chalete — on a pretext; māninī hailā tumi — you became manini; narahari pahum̐ — Narahari's Lord; karaye minati — entreats; jāgi biyākula āmi — I woke in distress

**7.4.** How much merry jesting there was! — and on some pretext you became manini. Narahari's Lord entreats you — and I woke in distress."[^31-17]

[^31-16]: Signature — "Narahari" (narahari pahum̐ — "Narahari's Lord"). GPT1 — p. 212, no. 129 (scan PDF p. 471); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 129 (catalogue: NG-344). GCC — kirana 8,
pada 5 (ed. 1947, p. 95; scan PDF p. 92), "anyā ca — yathārāga". GCC readings: "locana lorā" (7.1), "bheṭilā nikuñjamājha" (7.3), "māninī hailā tumi" (7.4). B.
Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^31-17]: The pada is built on the pattern of the padas on Radha and Krishna: the friend as messenger, the Beloved waiting in tears in the kunja, the meeting and
the heroine's mana (manini — "full of mana", the lover's pique). Gaura here — in a townswoman's dream — plays the part of Krishna; in His own lila He wept not
for the women of Nadia but for Krishna, in the bhava of Radha (CC Adi 4). The embrace (kore karila, 7.3) is a direct motif of sambhoga; translated exactly. The
dream is the townswoman's imagination; the Lord did not touch women (CB, Adi); the tradition does not accept gaura-nagari (n. 10 and the introductory note,
chapter 27).

## 8. Narahari — "śuna śuna ogo tomāre balie niśira svapanakathā…" (GPT1 pp. 212–213, no. 130; GCC 8.6)
*Nagari-bhava; a dream. In her dream a townswoman went to Srivasa's house, where the companions were singing to mridangas and karatalas and
Gaura was dancing among them; suddenly bhava seized Him — trembling, streams of tears; He fell and rolled on the ground like a golden lotus;
forgetting shame, she sobbed aloud and woke; the household ran to ask why she was weeping; falling asleep again, she saw that Gora had come to
her courtyard — she seated Him on a couch, fanned Him with the end of her sari, offered betel. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably
Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 8, pada 6.*[^31-18]

শুন শুন ওগো তোমারে বলিএ এ নিশির স্বপনকথা ।
শ্রীবাস পণ্ডিত ঠাকুরের বাড়ী গেলাম গৌরাঙ্গ যথা ॥

*śuna śuna ogo tomāre balie e niśira svapanakathā |*
*śrībāsa paṇḍita ṭhākurera bāṛī gelāma gaurāṅga yathā ||*

*Word for word:* śuna śuna ogo — listen, listen, friend; tomāre balie — I tell you; e niśira svapanakathā — this dream of the night; śrībāsa paṇḍita ṭhākurera bāṛī — to the house of Srivasa Pandita Thakura; gelāma gaurāṅga yathā — I went, where Gauranga was

**8.1.** "Listen, listen, friend, I will tell you the night's dream: I went to the house of Srivasa Pandita Thakura, where Gauranga was.

কিবা সে শ্রীবাস-অঙ্গনের শোভা দেখিয়া জুড়াল আঁখি ।
মনের হরিষে নিভৃতে দাঁড়ালুঁ ধৈরজে ধরম রাখি ॥

*kibā se śrībāsa-aṅganera śobhā dekhiyā juṛāla ām̐khi |*
*manera hariṣe nibhṛte dām̐ṛālum̐ dhairaje dharama rākhi ||*

*Word for word:* kibā se śrībāsa-aṅganera śobhā — how lovely Srivasa's courtyard; dekhiyā juṛāla ām̐khi — seeing it, my eyes were soothed; manera hariṣe — with joy at heart; nibhṛte dām̐ṛālum̐ — I stood in a secluded spot; dhairaje dharama rākhi — keeping composure and dharma

**8.2.** How lovely is Srivasa's courtyard — I saw it, and my eyes were soothed; with joy in my heart I stood in a secluded spot, keeping composure and dharma.

তথা পরিকরগণ মনসুখে খোল করতাল লৈয়া ।
গায়য়ে মধুর সুর সুধাময় অতি উনমত হৈয়া ॥

*tathā parikaragaṇa manasukhe khola karatāla laiyā |*
*gāyaye madhura sura sudhāmaya ati unamata haiyā ||*

*Word for word:* tathā — there; parikaragaṇa — the companions; manasukhe — happy at heart; khola karatāla laiyā — with mridangas (khol) and karatalas; gāyaye madhura sura sudhāmaya — sing sweet nectarean melodies; ati unamata haiyā — quite maddened

**8.3.** There the companions, happy at heart, with mridangas and karatalas, quite mad with joy, sing sweet, nectarean melodies.

সে মণ্ডলি মাঝে সাজে শচীসুত কিবা অদ্ভুত বেশ ।
নানাজাতি ফুলে রচিত রুচির চিক্কণ চাঁচর কেশ ॥

*se maṇḍali mājhe sāje śacīsuta kibā adbhuta beśa |*
*nānājāti phule racita rucira cikkaṇa cām̐cara keśa ||*

*Word for word:* se maṇḍali mājhe — in the midst of that circle; sāje śacīsuta — Shachi's son shines; kibā adbhuta beśa — what wondrous attire; nānājāti phule racita — adorned with flowers of every kind; rucira cikkaṇa cām̐cara keśa — lovely glossy curling hair

**8.4.** In the midst of that circle Shachi's son shines — what wondrous attire! His curling, glossy hair is adorned with lovely flowers of every kind.

শ্রুতিমূলে দোলে কুণ্ডল ললিত অতুল গণ্ডের ছটা ।
ভালে সুচন্দন বিন্দু বিন্দু যেন শারদ-শশীর ঘটা ॥

*śrutimūle dole kuṇḍala lalita atula gaṇḍera chaṭā |*
*bhāle sucandana bindu bindu yena śārada-śaśīra ghaṭā ||*

*Word for word:* śrutimūle dole — sway at the ears; kuṇḍala lalita — graceful earrings; atula gaṇḍera chaṭā — peerless glow of the cheeks; bhāle sucandana bindu bindu — on the brow drops of fine sandal; yena śārada-śaśīra ghaṭā — like the splendour of the autumn moon

**8.5.** At His ears graceful earrings sway, the glow of His cheeks is peerless; on His brow are drops of fine sandal paste, like the splendour of the autumn moon.

মৃদুতর পরিসর উরঃপরি তরল বিবিধ হার ।
পহিরণ নব ভূষণ লসয়ে কি দিব উপমা তার ॥

*mṛdutara parisara uraḥpari tarala bibidha hāra |*
*pahiraṇa naba bhūṣaṇa lasaye ki diba upamā tāra ||*

*Word for word:* mṛdutara — light as down (lit. "softest"); parisara uraḥpari — on the broad chest; tarala bibidha hāra — many necklaces swaying; pahiraṇa naba bhūṣaṇa — the new ornaments He wears; lasaye — shine; ki diba upamā tāra — what comparison can I give Him
