**8.6.** On His broad chest sway many necklaces, light as down; new ornaments shine on Him — with what shall I compare Him?

ভুজভঙ্গী করি নাচে সুচতুর চরণ চালনি চারু ।
হরি হরি বোল বলে তাহা শুনি ধৈরজ না রহে কারু ॥

*bhujabhaṅgī kari nāce sucatura caraṇa cālani cāru |*
*hari hari bola bale tāhā śuni dhairaja nā rahe kāru ||*

*Word for word:* bhujabhaṅgī kari — swaying His arms; nāce sucatura — the Most Clever One dances; caraṇa cālani cāru — with graceful steps; hari hari bola bale — cries "Hari, Hari!"; tāhā śuni — hearing it; dhairaja nā rahe kāru — no one keeps composure

**8.7.** Swaying His arms, the Most Clever One dances, stepping gracefully; "Hari, Hari!" He cries; hearing it, no one keeps composure.

না জানিয়ে তার কি ভাব উঠিল সঘনে কাঁপয়ে তনু ।
দুনয়নে ধারা বহে নিরন্তর নদীর প্রবাহ জনু ॥

*nā jāniye tāra ki bhāba uṭhila saghane kām̐paye tanu |*
*dunayane dhārā bahe nirantara nadīra prabāha janu ||*

*Word for word:* nā jāniye — I do not know; tāra ki bhāba uṭhila — what bhava rose in Him; saghane kām̐paye tanu — His body trembles again and again; dunayane dhārā bahe — streams flow from both eyes; nirantara — without cease; nadīra prabāha janu — like the current of a river

**8.8.** I do not know what bhava rose in Him: His body trembles again and again; from both eyes streams flow without cease — like the current of a river.

নিবিড় নিশ্বাস ছাড়ি বিয়াকুল ভূমিতে পড়িল সেহ ।
সোণার কমল সম গড়ি যায় ধরিতে নারয়ে কেহ ॥

*nibiṛa niśvāsa chāṛi biyākula bhūmite paṛila seha |*
*soṇāra kamala sama gaṛi yāya dharite nāraye keha ||*

*Word for word:* nibiṛa niśvāsa chāṛi — heaving a deep sigh; biyākula — agitated; bhūmite paṛila seha — He fell to the ground; soṇāra kamala sama — like a golden lotus; gaṛi yāya — He rolls; dharite nāraye keha — no one can hold Him

**8.9.** Heaving a deep sigh, in agitation He fell to the ground — He rolls like a golden lotus; no one can hold Him.

তাহা দেখি মোর কাঁপিল অন্তর লাজে তিলাঞ্জলি দিনু ।
কি হৈল কি হৈল বলি উচ্চ করি কাঁদিয়া বিকল হনু ॥

*tāhā dekhi mora kām̐pila antara lāje tilāñjali dinu |*
*ki haila ki haila bali ucca kari kām̐diyā bikala hanu ||*

*Word for word:* tāhā dekhi — seeing this; mora kām̐pila antara — my heart trembled; lāje tilāñjali dinu — I gave shame its last libation; ki haila ki haila bali — crying "what has happened?"; ucca kari kām̐diyā — weeping aloud; bikala hanu — I was beside myself

**8.10.** Seeing this, my heart trembled; I gave shame its last libation of water; "What has happened, what has happened?" I cried, and sobbed aloud, beside myself.[^31-19]

হেন কালে নিঁদ ভাঙ্গিল জাগিয়া বসিনু শয়ন যথা ।
কি কি বলি সবে ধাইয়া আইল পুছয়ে রোদন-কথা ॥

*hena kāle nim̐da bhāṅgila jāgiyā basinu śayana yathā |*
*ki ki bali sabe dhāiyā āila puchaye rodana-kathā ||*

*Word for word:* hena kāle — then; nim̐da bhāṅgila — sleep broke; jāgiyā basinu śayana yathā — waking, I sat up on the bed; ki ki bali — saying "what, what?"; sabe dhāiyā āila — all came running; puchaye rodana-kathā — they ask about the weeping

**8.11.** Then my sleep broke; waking, I sat up in bed; "What is it, what is it?" — everyone came running to ask why I wept.

কারে কি কহিব পুনঃ মনোদুখে ঘুমানু চাতকীপারা ।
ফিরিয়া স্বপন দেখিনু আমার অঙ্গনে আইলা গোরা ॥

*kāre ki kahiba punaḥ manodukhe ghumānu cātakīpārā |*
*phiriyā svapana dekhinu āmāra aṅgane āilā gorā ||*

*Word for word:* kāre ki kahiba — whom shall I tell what; punaḥ manodukhe — again with grief at heart; ghumānu cātakīpārā — I slept like a chataki bird; phiriyā svapana dekhinu — again I dreamed; āmāra aṅgane āilā gorā — Gora came to my courtyard

**8.12.** What could I tell anyone? With grief in my heart I fell asleep again, like a chataki bird; and again I dreamed: Gora had come to my courtyard.

আইস আইস বন্ধু বলিয়া তুরিতে বসানু পালঙ্কপরি ।
শ্রম জানি নিজ আঁচরে বাতাস করিনু যতন করি ॥

*āisa āisa bandhu baliyā turite basānu pālaṅkapari |*
*śrama jāni nija ām̐care bātāsa karinu yatana kari ||*

*Word for word:* āisa āisa bandhu baliyā — saying "come in, come in, friend"; turite basānu pālaṅkapari — quickly I seated Him on the couch; śrama jāni — knowing His fatigue; nija ām̐care — with the end of my sari; bātāsa karinu yatana kari — I carefully fanned Him

**8.13.** "Come in, come in, friend!" I said, and quickly seated Him on the couch; seeing He was tired, I carefully fanned Him with the end of my sari.

সাজাইয়া নব তাম্বূল সাজিয়া দিলাম সে চাঁদমুখে ।
নরহরি প্রাণনাথেরে লইয়া বসিনু মনের সুখে ॥

*sājāiyā naba tāmbūla sājiyā dilāma se cām̐damukhe |*
*narahari prāṇanāthere laiyā basinu manera sukhe ||*

*Word for word:* sājāiyā naba tāmbūla — preparing fresh betel; sājiyā dilāma se cām̐damukhe — I offered it to that moon-like face; narahari prāṇanāthere laiyā — with the Lord of Narahari's life; basinu manera sukhe — I sat, happy at heart (GCC: "lay down")

**8.14.** Preparing fresh betel, I offered it to that moon-like face; and with the Lord of Narahari's life I sat, happy at heart."[^31-20]

[^31-18]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — pp. 212–213, no. 130 (scan PDF pp. 471–472); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 130 (catalogue: NG-345). GCC — kirana 8, pada 6 (ed. 1947,
pp. 95–96; scan PDF pp. 92–93), "anyā ca — yathārāga". GCC readings: "gelāma gaura yathā" (8.1), "dām̐ṛāinu" (8.2), "nānā jāti" (8.4), "śarada śaśīra ghaṭā" (8.5),
"hainu" (8.10), "ghumāinu cātakī-pārā" (8.12), "tāmbūla hāsiyā dilāma" (8.14), "laiyā śutinu manera sukhe" (8.14; see n. 20). B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory
note to the section (chapter 27).
[^31-19]: 8.7–8.10 describe the Lord's ecstasy in kirtana at Srivasa's house (trembling, tears, falling to the ground — sattvika-bhavas; cf. CB, Madhya, on the kirtanas
in Srivasa's courtyard; CC Adi 17). "I gave shame its last libation of water" (lāje tilāñjali dinu; tilanjali — the offering of water with sesame to the dead) — a
saying: I abandoned shame for good. "Like a chataki bird" (8.12) — the chataka, by poetic tradition, drinks only rain-water from the clouds and ever waits for it:
an image of longing.
[^31-20]: 8.12–8.14 — the second dream: serving Gaura in her own house (couch, fan, betel). The GPT ending is "I sat" (basinu); GCC has "I lay down" (śutinu): the motif
of sambhoga is more direct; the GPT text is translated, the GCC reading is noted here. The dream is the townswoman's imagination; the Lord did not touch women
(CB, Adi); the tradition does not accept gaura-nagari (n. 10 and the introductory note, chapter 27).

## 9. Narahari — "śuna śuna ogo rajani-svapana…" (GPT1 pp. 213–214, no. 131; GCC 8.7)
*Nagari-bhava; a dream. First the townswoman dreams that the whole world has gone mad with the virtues of Gaurangachand, and even the wicked and
the slanderers have become His followers; falling asleep again, she sees: as Shyama held the rasa on the bank of the Yamuna, so Gora on the bank
of the Suradhuni has made an abode of rasa; the women of Nadia, casting off shame, go there in crowds; her husband bolts the door, but her
husband's brother's wife slyly opens it; she runs, sees Gaura Raya in a circle of young women amid music and song, dances — and He, laughing,
presses her to His breast. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 8, pada 7.*[^31-21]

শুন শুন ওগো রজনি-স্বপন কহিয়ে আছিয়ে মনে ।
জগতের লোক পাগল হইল গৌরাঙ্গচাঁদের গুণে ॥

*śuna śuna ogo rajani-svapana kahiye āchiye mane |*
*jagatera loka pāgala haila gaurāṅgacām̐dera guṇe ||*

*Word for word:* śuna śuna ogo — listen, listen, friend; rajani-svapana — the night's dream; kahiye — I tell; āchiye mane — that is in my heart; jagatera loka — the people of the world; pāgala haila — went mad; gaurāṅgacām̐dera guṇe — with the virtues of Gaurangachand

**9.1.** "Listen, listen, friend, I will tell the night's dream that is in my heart: the people of the whole world went mad with the virtues of Gaurangachand.

কুমতি কুটিল কপটী নিন্দুক আদি যত যত ছিল ।
ছাড়ি বিপরীত স্বভাব সকলে গৌর-অনুগত হৈল ॥

*kumati kuṭila kapaṭī ninduka ādi yata yata chila |*
*chāṛi biparīta svabhāba sakale gaura-anugata haila ||*

*Word for word:* kumati — the foolish; kuṭila — the crooked; kapaṭī — the deceitful; ninduka — slanderers; ādi yata yata chila — and all who were; chāṛi biparīta svabhāba — giving up their perverse nature; sakale — all; gaura-anugata haila — became followers of Gaura

**9.2.** All who were — the foolish, the crooked, the deceitful, the slanderers — giving up their perverse nature, became followers of Gaura.

এইরূপ কত দেখিতে দেখিতে বারেক জাগিনু সই ।
পুনঃ ঘুমাইতে আর অপরূপ দেখিনু সে সব কই ॥

*eirūpa kata dekhite dekhite bāreka jāginu sai |*
*punaḥ ghumāite āra aparūpa dekhinu se saba kai ||*

*Word for word:* eirūpa kata — this and much else; dekhite dekhite — seeing; bāreka jāginu sai — once I woke, friend; punaḥ ghumāite — falling asleep again; āra aparūpa dekhinu — I saw another wonder; se saba kai — I tell it all

**9.3.** Seeing this and much else, once I woke, friend; and when I fell asleep again, I saw another wonder — I will tell you all of it.

যমুনাপুলিনে রাস-বিলাসাদি যেরূপ করিল শ্যাম ।
সেইরূপ গোরা সুরধুনীতীরে রচিল রসের ধাম ॥

*yamunāpuline rāsa-bilāsādi yerūpa karila śyāma |*
*seirūpa gorā suradhunītīre racila rasera dhāma ||*

*Word for word:* yamunāpuline — on the bank of the Yamuna; rāsa-bilāsādi — the rasa and other pastimes; yerūpa karila śyāma — as Shyama held; seirūpa gorā — so Gora; suradhunītīre — on the bank of the Suradhuni; racila rasera dhāma — made an abode of rasa

**9.4.** As Shyama on the bank of the Yamuna held the rasa and other pastimes, so Gora on the bank of the Suradhuni made an abode of rasa.[^31-22]

লাজকুলভয় সব তেয়াগিয়া নদীয়া-নাগরী যত ।
মনোরথে চড়ি চলে যূথে যূথে এড়ায়ে কণ্টক শত ॥

*lājakulabhaya saba teyāgiyā nadīyā-nāgarī yata |*
*manorathe caṛi cale yūthe yūthe eṛāye kaṇṭaka śata ||*

*Word for word:* lājakulabhaya saba teyāgiyā — casting off shame and fear for family; nadīyā-nāgarī yata — all the nagaris of Nadia; manorathe caṛi — mounted on the chariot of desire; cale yūthe yūthe — go crowd after crowd; eṛāye kaṇṭaka śata — passing by hundreds of thorns

**9.5.** Casting off shame and fear for their families, all the nagaris of Nadia, mounted on the chariot of desire, go crowd after crowd, passing by hundreds of thorns.

গৃহকাজ ত্যজি মু বড় চঞ্চল তথা যাইবার তরে ।
আচম্বিতে পতি আসিয়া তুরিতে কপাট দিলেক ঘরে ॥

*gṛhakāja tyaji mu baṛa cañcala tathā yāibāra tare |*
*ācambite pati āsiyā turite kapāṭa dileka ghare ||*

*Word for word:* gṛhakāja tyaji — leaving the housework; mu baṛa cañcala — I in great eagerness; tathā yāibāra tare — to go there; ācambite pati āsiyā — suddenly my husband came; turite kapāṭa dileka ghare — quickly bolted the door of the house

**9.6.** Leaving the housework, I was in great eagerness to go there; suddenly my husband came and quickly bolted the door of the house.

পড়িনু সঙ্কটে কারে কি কহিব অধিক বিকল হৈনু ।
মনে হেন প্রাণ না রবে পিয়ারে পুনহুঁ দেখিতে পাইনু ॥

*paṛinu saṅkaṭe kāre ki kahiba adhika bikala hainu |*
*mane hena prāṇa nā rabe piyāre punahum̐ dekhite pāinu ||*

*Word for word:* paṛinu saṅkaṭe — I fell into a fix; kāre ki kahiba — whom shall I tell what; adhika bikala hainu — I lost all strength; mane hena — I thought; prāṇa nā rabe — life will not remain; piyāre punahum̐ dekhite pāinu — (unless) I see the Beloved again (lit. "I saw")

**9.7.** I was in a fix — whom could I tell what? — and lost all strength; I thought: I shall not live if I do not see the Beloved again.

সে সময়ে ছলে কপাট খুলিল চতুর আমার জা ।
ধরমে ধরমে ধীরে ধীরে গৃহ-বাহিরে বাড়ানু পা ॥

*se samaye chale kapāṭa khulila catura āmāra jā |*
*dharame dharame dhīre dhīre gṛha-bāhire bāṛānu pā ||*

*Word for word:* se samaye — at that moment; chale — on a pretext; kapāṭa khulila — unbolted the door; catura āmāra jā — my clever sister-in-law (husband's brother's wife); dharame dharame — carefully; dhīre dhīre — softly; gṛha-bāhire bāṛānu pā — I stepped outside

**9.8.** At that moment my clever sister-in-law, my husband's brother's wife, on some pretext unbolted the door; carefully, carefully, softly, softly I stepped outside.

প্রফুল্লিত হৈয়া ধাইনু কাহার পানে না পালটি আঁখি ।
লোহার পিঞ্জর হইতে যেমন পলায় নবীন পাখী ॥

*praphullita haiyā dhāinu kāhāra pāne nā pālaṭi ām̐khi |*
*lohāra piñjara haite yemana palāya nabīna pākhī ||*

*Word for word:* praphullita haiyā — blossoming with joy; dhāinu — I ran; kāhāra pāne nā pālaṭi ām̐khi — not turning my eyes to anyone; lohāra piñjara haite — from an iron cage; yemana palāya nabīna pākhī — as a young bird escapes

**9.9.** Blossoming with joy, I ran, looking back at no one — as a young bird escapes from an iron cage.

যাইয়া তুরিতে নয়ান ভরিয়া দেখিনু গৌররায় ।
যুবতীমণ্ডলি মাঝে সাজে ভাল কি দিব উপমা তায় ॥

*yāiyā turite nayāna bhariyā dekhinu gaurarāya |*
*yubatīmaṇḍali mājhe sāje bhāla ki diba upamā tāya ||*

*Word for word:* yāiyā turite — arriving quickly; nayāna bhariyā — to my eyes' fill; dekhinu gaurarāya — I saw Gaura Raya; yubatīmaṇḍali mājhe — in the circle of young women; sāje bhāla — shines finely; ki diba upamā tāya — what comparison can I give Him

**9.10.** Arriving quickly, I gazed my fill on Gaura Raya: in the midst of a circle of young women He shines — with what shall I compare Him?

নানাজাতি যন্ত্র বাজে চারিদিকে সুখের নাহিক পার ।
গাওয়ে মধুর সুরনারীগণ বরিষে অমিয় ধার ॥

*nānājāti yantra bāje cāridike sukhera nāhika pāra |*
*gāoye madhura suranārīgaṇa bariṣe amiya dhāra ||*

*Word for word:* nānājāti yantra — all kinds of instruments; bāje cāridike — sound on every side; sukhera nāhika pāra — no end of joy; gāoye madhura sura — sing sweet melodies; nārīgaṇa — the women (or suranārīgaṇa — celestial women); bariṣe amiya dhāra — shower streams of nectar

**9.11.** On every side all kinds of instruments sound — there is no end of joy; women sing sweet melodies, showering streams of nectar.

ও মুখ-কমল-মধুপানে মাতি মো পুনঃ নাচিনু সুখে ।
নরহরিনাথ তা দেখি হাসিয়া আমারে করিল বুকে ॥

*o mukha-kamala-madhupāne māti mo punaḥ nācinu sukhe |*
*naraharinātha tā dekhi hāsiyā āmāre karila buke ||*

*Word for word:* o mukha-kamala-madhupāne māti — drunk with the honey of that lotus face; mo punaḥ nācinu sukhe — I danced again in joy; naraharinātha — Narahari's Lord; tā dekhi hāsiyā — seeing it, laughing; āmāre karila buke — pressed me to His breast

**9.12.** Drunk with the honey of that lotus face, I danced again in joy; Narahari's Lord, seeing this, laughed and pressed me to His breast."[^31-23]

[^31-21]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — pp. 213–214, no. 131 (scan PDF pp. 472–473); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 131 (catalogue: NG-106; the catalogue line is from the middle
of the pada). GCC — kirana 8, pada 7 (ed. 1947, pp. 96–97; scan PDF pp. 93/101–102), "anyā ca — yathārāga". GCC readings: "kahi ye āchaye mane" (9.1), "lāja kula
bhaya guru teyāgiyā" — "casting off shame, family, fear of the elders" (9.5), "gṛha kāja tyaji mu baṛa cañcala" (9.6), "catura āmāra yā" (9.8), "nā pālaṭi dekhi"
(9.9), "yubatī-maṇḍalī" (9.10), "cāridige", "sura nārīgaṇa" (9.11). B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^31-22]: 9.2 — in the first dream — is what the biographies also tell: the Lord's mercy turned slanderers and sinners (CB, Madhya: Jagai and Madhai; CC Adi 17). 9.4–9.12 —
in the second dream — Gora's "rasa" on the bank of the Ganga on the pattern of Krishna's rasa-lila (Bhag. 10.29–33): this is precisely the "gaura-nagari" notion
that the Gaudiya tradition expressly rejects: Vrindavana Dasa says that the Lord in Navadvipa did not look at women (CB, Adi), His night pastimes in Navadvipa
are sankirtana with the devotees behind the barred doors of Srivasa's house (CB, Madhya), and the rasa-lila belongs to Vrindavana and Krishna; Bhaktisiddhanta
Sarasvati counts gaura-nagari among the apasampradayas (introductory note, chapter 27). The pada is translated faithfully to the author as a record of late
poetry, without softening.
[^31-23]: "My husband's brother's wife" (jā). Deceiving the husband and fleeing the house (9.6–9.9) is a motif of the padas on the gopis running to the call of the flute
(Bhag. 10.29); pressing to the breast (9.12) is a direct motif of sambhoga; translated exactly. The dream is the townswoman's imagination; the Lord did not touch
women (CB, Adi). "Women sing sweet melodies" (madhura sura-nārīgaṇa) may also be understood as "celestial women" (suranārī); GCC separates "sura" ("melody").

## 10. Narahari — "rajanī-svapana śuna go sajani…" (GPT1 p. 214, no. 132; GCC 8.8)
*Nagari-bhava; a dream. A townswoman, casting off shame, tells: in her dream Gora quietly entered her chamber, looking around, sat at the head
of her bed, touched her lips, jested, embraced her, weeping with joy — as if He had found a treasure He could not let go of even for a moment.
Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 8, pada 8.*[^31-24]

রজনী-স্বপন শুন গো সজনি বলি যে নিলজী হৈয়া ।
ধীরে ধীরে গোরা মন্দিরে প্রবেশে চকিত চৌদিকে চাঞা ॥

*rajanī-svapana śuna go sajani bali ye nilajī haiyā |*
*dhīre dhīre gorā mandire prabeśe cakita caudike cāñā ||*

*Word for word:* rajanī-svapana — the night's dream; śuna go sajani — listen, friend; bali ye nilajī haiyā — I tell it, shameless; dhīre dhīre — softly; gorā mandire prabeśe — Gora enters the chamber; cakita caudike cāñā — warily looking all around

**10.1.** "Listen to the night's dream, friend — I tell it, casting off shame: softly, softly Gora enters my chamber, warily looking all around.

হাসিয়া হাসিয়া বসিয়া বসিয়া আসিয়া শিথান পাশে ।
নিজকরে মোর অধর পরশি সুখের সায়রে ভাসে ॥

*hāsiyā hāsiyā basiyā basiyā āsiyā śithāna pāśe |*
*nijakare mora adhara paraśi sukhera sāyare bhāse ||*

*Word for word:* hāsiyā hāsiyā — smiling; basiyā basiyā — sitting; āsiyā śithāna pāśe — coming to the head of the bed; nijakare — with His own hand; mora adhara paraśi — touching my lips; sukhera sāyare bhāse — floats in an ocean of joy

**10.2.** Smiling, He sat, moving close to the head of my bed; with His own hand He touched my lips — and floats in an ocean of joy.

সুমধুর বাণী ভণে নানা জাতি মাতিয়া কৌতুক ছলে ।
ভুজে ভুজ দিয়া হিয়া মাঝে রাখি ভিজয়ে আঁখির জলে ॥

*sumadhura bāṇī bhaṇe nānā jāti mātiyā kautuka chale |*
*bhuje bhuja diyā hiyā mājhe rākhi bhijaye ām̐khira jale ||*

*Word for word:* sumadhura bāṇī bhaṇe — speaks the sweetest words; nānā jāti — in every way; mātiyā — intoxicated; kautuka chale — jesting; bhuje bhuja diyā — twining arms; hiyā mājhe rākhi — holding to the heart; bhijaye ām̐khira jale — bathes with the tears of the eyes

**10.3.** Intoxicated, jesting, He speaks the sweetest words in every way; twining His arms, holding [me] to His heart, He bathes [me] with the tears of His eyes.

আপনার মনে মানে পাইনু নিধি তিলেক ছাড়াতে ভার ।
নরহরি-প্রাণ-পিয়া পীরিতের মূরতি কি কব আর ॥

*āpanāra mane māne pāinu nidhi tileka chāṛāte bhāra |*
*narahari-prāṇa-piyā pīritera mūrati ki kaba āra ||*

*Word for word:* āpanāra mane māne — in His own heart He deems; pāinu nidhi — "I have found a treasure"; tileka chāṛāte bhāra — hard to let go even for a moment; narahari-prāṇa-piyā — the Beloved of Narahari's life; pīritera mūrati — love embodied; ki kaba āra — what more shall I say

**10.4.** In His own heart He deems He has found a treasure — it is hard for Him to let it go even for a moment." The Beloved of Narahari's life is love itself embodied; what more shall I say?[^31-25]

[^31-24]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — p. 214, no. 132 (scan PDF p. 473); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 132 (catalogue: NG-107). GCC — kirana 8, pada 8 (ed. 1947, p. 97; scan PDF
p. 102), "anyā ca — yathārāga". GCC readings: "caudige cāyā" (10.1), "śithāna-pāśe" (10.2), "pirītera mūrati" (10.4). B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the
section (chapter 27).
[^31-25]: The whole dream (10.1–10.4) is a direct motif of sambhoga: Gora enters the townswoman's chamber, touches her lips, embraces her; translated exactly, adding
nothing and softening nothing. This is the townswoman's imagination, not the Lord's lila: the Lord did not touch women and in Navadvipa did not look at them (CB,
Adi); the Gaudiya tradition does not accept the worship of Gaura as a nagara (Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati; introductory note, chapter 27); according to Majumdar
such GPT padas signed Narahari are late (here — Narahari Chakravarti). Gaura's tears (10.3) in His own lila are tears of prema for Krishna (CC Adi 4).

## 11. Narahari — "śuna śuna niśi-svapana sai…" (GPT1 p. 214, no. 133; GCC 8.9)
*Nagari-bhava; a dream, on the pattern of the khandita padas. In a dream at dawn the finely dressed Gaura came to the townswoman; she asked why He
had come and told Him to go where He had spent the night — the traces of a sleepless night cannot be hidden; He swore hundreds of oaths, pleaded
with her — and then the dream broke. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 8, pada 9.*[^31-26]

শুন শুন নিশি-স্বপন সই । লাজ তিয়াগিয়া তোমারে কই ॥

*śuna śuna niśi-svapana sai | lāja tiyāgiyā tomāre kai ||*

*Word for word:* śuna śuna — listen, listen; niśi-svapana — the night's dream; sai — friend; lāja tiyāgiyā — leaving shame aside; tomāre kai — I tell you

**11.1.** "Listen, listen, friend, to the night's dream — I tell it to you, leaving shame aside.

প্রভাত সময়ে সুচারু বেশে । আইলেন গৌর আমার পাশে ॥

*prabhāta samaye sucāru beśe | āilena gaura āmāra pāśe ||*

*Word for word:* prabhāta samaye — at dawn; sucāru beśe — in fine attire; āilena gaura — Gaura came; āmāra pāśe — to me

**11.2.** At dawn, in fine attire, Gaura came to me.

সে চন্দ্রবদন পানেতে চাঞা । বলিনু কি কাজে আইলে ধাঞা ॥

*se candrabadana pānete cāñā | balinu ki kāje āile dhāñā ||*

*Word for word:* se candrabadana pānete cāñā — looking at that moon-like face; balinu — I said; ki kāje āile dhāñā — why have You come running

**11.3.** Looking at that moon-like face, I said: 'Why have You come running?

সুখে গোঙাইলে রজনী যথা । তুরিত যাইয়া মিলহ তথা ॥

*sukhe goṅāile rajanī yathā | turita yāiyā milaha tathā ||*

*Word for word:* sukhe goṅāile rajanī yathā — where You happily spent the night; turita yāiyā — going quickly; milaha tathā — meet there

**11.4.** Where You happily spent the night — go there quickly and meet there.

গুপত না রহে বেকত রীতি । তা সহ জাগিয়া পোহালে রাতি ॥

*gupata nā rahe bekata rīti | tā saha jāgiyā pohāle rāti ||*

*Word for word:* gupata nā rahe — the hidden does not stay hidden; bekata rīti — the ways are plain; tā saha jāgiyā — staying awake with her; pohāle rāti — You passed the night

**11.5.** What is hidden does not stay hidden — it is all plain: with her You stayed awake, passing the night.'

শুনি কত শত শপথ করে । পরশের আশে সাধয়ে মোরে ॥

*śuni kata śata śapatha kare | paraśera āśe sādhaye more ||*

*Word for word:* śuni — hearing; kata śata śapatha kare — swears hundreds of oaths; paraśera āśe — longing to touch; sādhaye more — pleads with me

**11.6.** Hearing this, He swears hundreds of oaths — and, longing to touch, pleads with me.

হেন কালে নিঁদ ভাঙ্গিয়া গেল । নরহরি জানে যে দশা হৈল ॥

*hena kāle nim̐da bhāṅgiyā gela | narahari jāne ye daśā haila ||*

*Word for word:* hena kāle — then; nim̐da bhāṅgiyā gela — sleep broke; narahari jāne — Narahari knows; ye daśā haila — what state befell

**11.7.** Then the dream broke." Narahari knows what became of her.[^31-27]

[^31-26]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — p. 214, no. 133 (scan PDF p. 473); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 133 (catalogue: NG-346). GCC — kirana 8, pada 9 (ed. 1947, p. 98; scan PDF
p. 103), "anyā ca — yathārāga". Metre — short payar (a couplet to a line). Readings: 11.3 "balinu" — "I said" (so GPT2 and GCC; GPT1 "calinu" — "I went", probably a
misprint; translated after GPT2 and GCC); GCC: "prabhāta-samaye" (11.2), "se candrabadana-pānete cāyā" (11.3), "henakāle" (11.7). B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory
note to the section (chapter 27).
[^31-27]: The pada repeats the scheme of the khandita padas — the heroine to whom the Beloved comes at dawn bearing the traces of a night spent with another (in the
Krishna padas — with Chandravali); the reproach, the oaths and the longing to touch come from there. Transferring this image to Gaura is a convention of the nagari
padas, not the Lord's lila (n. 25; introductory note, chapter 27). "Narahari knows what became of her" — the poet's signature; translated as in the original.

## 12. Narahari — "śuna śuna ogo sajani rajanī-svapana…" (GPT1 pp. 214–215, no. 134; GCC 8.10)
*Nagari-bhava; a dream. In a dream the Moon of Nadia came to a townswoman's house; her harsh sister-in-law at the door accused her of a liaison
with a strange man and threatened to tell her brother in the morning; the townswoman feared not for herself — let them revile her — but that
wicked people would slander the Beloved and He would never again come to their street; she wept, repeating His name, and woke. Raga
"yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 8, pada 10.*[^31-28]

শুন শুন ওগো সজনি রজনী-স্বপন বলিয়ে তোরে ।
অনেক যতনে নদীয়ার শশী আসিয়া মিলিল ঘরে ॥

*śuna śuna ogo sajani rajanī-svapana baliye tore |*
*aneka yatane nadīyāra śaśī āsiyā milila ghare ||*

*Word for word:* śuna śuna ogo sajani — listen, listen, friend; rajanī-svapana baliye tore — I tell you the night's dream; aneka yatane — with great effort; nadīyāra śaśī — the Moon of Nadia; āsiyā milila ghare — came and met (me) in the house

**12.1.** "Listen, listen, friend, I will tell you the night's dream: with great effort the Moon of Nadia came and met me in the house.

হেন কালে মোর দারুণ ননদী দুয়ারে দাঁড়ায়া কয় ।
পর-পুরুষের সনে বিলসহ ইথে না বাসহ ভয় ॥

*hena kāle mora dāruṇa nanadī duyāre dām̐ṛāyā kaya |*
*para-puruṣera sane bilasaha ithe nā bāsaha bhaya ||*

*Word for word:* hena kāle — at that time; mora dāruṇa nanadī — my harsh sister-in-law; duyāre dām̐ṛāyā kaya — standing at the door says; para-puruṣera sane bilasaha — you dally with a strange man; ithe nā bāsaha bhaya — and feel no fear

**12.2.** Just then my harsh sister-in-law, standing at the door, says: 'You are dallying with a strange man and are not afraid!

ভাল ভাল ভাই আইলে প্রভাতে এসব জানাঞা তারে ।
আপনার লাজ লইয়া যাইব না রব এ পাপ-ঘরে ॥

*bhāla bhāla bhāi āile prabhāte esaba jānāñā tāre |*
*āpanāra lāja laiyā yāiba nā raba e pāpa-ghare ||*

*Word for word:* bhāla bhāla — very well; bhāi āile prabhāte — when my brother comes in the morning; esaba jānāñā tāre — I will tell him all this; āpanāra lāja laiyā yāiba — I will take my honour and go; nā raba e pāpa-ghare — I will not stay in this sinful house

**12.3.** Very well: in the morning my brother will come — I will tell him everything; and I will take my own honour and go — I will not stay in this sinful house.'

ইহা শুনি মনে বিচারিনু ভয় পাঞা পোহাইলে নিশি ।
না জানি পতি কি বিপরীত ক্রিয়া করিবে গৃহেতে আসি ॥

*ihā śuni mane bicārinu bhaya pāñā pohāile niśi |*
*nā jāni pati ki biparīta kriyā karibe gṛhete āsi ||*

*Word for word:* ihā śuni — hearing this; mane bicārinu — I thought; bhaya pāñā — in fear; pohāile niśi — when the night is over; nā jāni — I do not know; pati ki biparīta kriyā karibe — what harm my husband will do; gṛhete āsi — coming home

**12.4.** Hearing this, I thought in fear: when the night is over — I do not know what my husband will do when he comes home.

মোরে সবে কত গঞ্জনা করিবে তাহে না পাইব ব্যথা ।
পাপ লোক পাছে প্রাণ-পিয়ারে বা কহয়ে কলঙ্ককথা ॥

*more sabe kata gañjanā karibe tāhe nā pāiba byathā |*
*pāpa loka pāche prāṇa-piyāre bā kahaye kalaṅkakathā ||*

*Word for word:* more sabe kata gañjanā karibe — let all revile me as they will; tāhe nā pāiba byathā — that will not pain me; pāpa loka pāche — lest wicked people; prāṇa-piyāre vā kahaye kalaṅkakathā — speak slander of the Beloved of my life

**12.5.** Let everyone revile me as much as they like — that does not pain me; but what if wicked people should slander the Beloved of my life!

যদি বিহি ইহা বেকত করয় তবে ত বিষম হব ।
জনমের মত নদীয়া-চাঁদেরে আর না দেখিতে পাব ॥

*yadi bihi ihā bekata karaya tabe ta biṣama haba |*
*janamera mata nadīyā-cām̐dere āra nā dekhite pāba ||*

*Word for word:* yadi bihi ihā bekata karaya — if the Creator makes this known; tabe ta biṣama haba — then it will be dreadful; janamera mata — for life; nadīyā-cām̐dere — the Moon of Nadia; āra nā dekhite pāba — I shall see no more

**12.6.** If the Creator makes this known, then it will be dreadful: for the rest of my life I shall never again see the Moon of Nadia.

এ পাড়ার পানে না আসিবে কভু মোরে না করিব মনে ।
মুই অভাগিনী জানিনু নিশ্চয় নহিলে এমন কেনে ॥

*e pāṛāra pāne nā āsibe kabhu more nā kariba mane |*
*mui abhāginī jāninu niścaya nahile emana kene ||*

*Word for word:* e pāṛāra pāne — to this street; nā āsibe kabhu — He will never come; more nā kariba mane — will not think of me; mui abhāginī — wretched I; jāninu niścaya — know for certain; nahile emana kene — otherwise why should it be so

**12.7.** He will never come to our street, will never think of me; wretched as I am, I know it for certain — otherwise why should things be so?

এত বলি কাঁদি বেকুল হইনু সঘনে সে নাম লৈয়া ।
নরহরি জানে প্রাণ বাঁচাইনু তুরিতে চেতন পাইয়া ॥

*eta bali kām̐di bekula hainu saghane se nāma laiyā |*
*narahari jāne prāṇa bām̐cāinu turite cetana pāiyā ||*

*Word for word:* eta bali — saying this; kām̐di bekula hainu — I wept in distress; saghane se nāma laiyā — repeating His name again and again; narahari jāne — Narahari knows; prāṇa bām̐cāinu — I saved my life; turite cetana pāiyā — quickly regaining consciousness (waking)

**12.8.** Saying this, I sobbed in distress, repeating His name again and again. Narahari knows: I saved my life by waking up quickly."[^31-29]

[^31-28]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — pp. 214–215, no. 134 (scan PDF pp. 473–474); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 134 (catalogue: NG-347; in GPT2 no. 134 is printed after no. 135).
GCC — kirana 8, pada 10 (ed. 1947, p. 98; scan PDF p. 103), "anyā ca — yathārāga". GCC readings: "āsiyā sāmbhāila ghare" — "entered the house" (12.1), "para puruṣera sane
bilasaha, ithe nā bāsaha bhaya" (12.2), "bhaya pāyā pohāile niśi" (12.4), "prāṇe bām̐cāinu turite cetana pāyā" (12.8). B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to
the section (chapter 27).
[^31-29]: The sister-in-law's accusation ("you are dallying with a strange man", para-puruṣera sane bilasaha) is rendered exactly. The heart of the pada is 12.5–12.6: the
townswoman is ready to bear any abuse, so long as rumour does not touch Gaura and she is not deprived of His darshan. This is a dream, not an event (n. 10;
introductory note, chapter 27). The signature merges with the townswoman's speech ("Narahari knows: I saved…"); "waking up" — lit. "regaining consciousness"
(cetana pāiyā).

## 13. Narahari — "sajani rajanī-svapana śunaha…" (GPT1 pp. 215–216, no. 135; GCC 8.11)
*Nagari-bhava; a comic dream. To guard the townswoman, her sister-in-law slept on her bed; at night the Moon of Nadia came and by mistake sat on
the sister-in-law's couch and touched her chin; she woke crying "Thief!", chased Him, caught Him and brought Him back with abuse, but Gora looked
at her — and conquered her; then, not finding the townswoman, He left dejected; and the sister-in-law, with downcast face, confessed that she had
"fallen into the hands of a terrible thief" and begged her to keep silent. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 8,
pada 11.*[^31-30]

সজনি রজনী-স্বপন শুনহ এ বড় হাসির কথা ।
মোরে আগুলিতে শুতিলা ননদী আমার শয়ন যথা ॥

*sajani rajanī-svapana śunaha e baṛa hāsira kathā |*
*more āgulite śutilā nanadī āmāra śayana yathā ||*

*Word for word:* sajani — friend; rajanī-svapana śunaha — listen to the night's dream; e baṛa hāsira kathā — this is a great laugh; more āgulite — to guard me; śutilā nanadī — my sister-in-law lay down; āmāra śayana yathā — where my bed is

**13.1.** "Friend, listen to the night's dream — what a laugh! To guard me, my sister-in-law lay down where my bed is.

নদীয়ার শশী আসি প্রবেশিল অথির আনন্দ ভরে ।
আমার ভরমে বসিলা ননদিনীর পালঙ্ক উপরে ॥

*nadīyāra śaśī āsi prabeśila athira ānanda bhare |*
*āmāra bharame basilā nanadinīra pālaṅka upare ||*

*Word for word:* nadīyāra śaśī āsi — the Moon of Nadia came; prabeśila — entered; athira ānanda bhare — trembling with joy; āmāra bharame — mistaking her for me; basilā nanadinīra pālaṅka upare — sat on the sister-in-law's couch

**13.2.** The Moon of Nadia came, entered, trembling with joy — and, taking her for me, sat on my sister-in-law's couch.

ধীরে ধীরে করপল্লবে চিবুক পরশে হরিষ হৈয়া ।
ননদী চেতন পাইয়া উঠে ঘন চমকি চৌদিকে চাঞা ॥

*dhīre dhīre karapallabe cibuka paraśe hariṣa haiyā |*
*nanadī cetana pāiyā uṭhe ghana camaki caudike cāñā ||*

*Word for word:* dhīre dhīre — softly; karapallabe — with His tendril-hand; cibuka paraśe — touches the chin; hariṣa haiyā — in delight; nanadī cetana pāiyā — the sister-in-law awoke; uṭhe ghana camaki — starts up in alarm; caudike cāñā — looking all around

**13.3.** Softly, softly, in delight, He touched her chin with His tendril-like hand; my sister-in-law awoke, started up in alarm, looking all around.

মোরে কহে জাগ জাগহ তুরিতে ঘরে সামাইল চোরা ।
ইহা শুনি ভয়ে পালাইলা দূরে দাঁড়াঞা রহিলা গোরা ॥

*more kahe jāga jāgaha turite ghare sāmāila corā |*
*ihā śuni bhaye pālāilā dūre dām̐ṛāñā rahilā gorā ||*

*Word for word:* more kahe — she says to me; jāga jāgaha turite — wake up, wake up quickly; ghare sāmāila corā — a thief has got into the house; ihā śuni — hearing this; bhaye pālāilā — fled in fear; dūre dām̐ṛāñā rahilā gorā — Gora stood some way off

**13.4.** She says to me: 'Wake up, wake up, quick — a thief has got into the house!' Hearing this, Gora fled in fear and stood some way off.

তার পাছে পাছে দারুণ ননদী ধাইল ধমক দিয়া ।
কতদূর যাই পাইল পলাইতে নারিল পরাণ-পিয়া ॥

*tāra pāche pāche dāruṇa nanadī dhāila dhamaka diyā |*
*katadūra yāi pāila palāite nārila parāṇa-piyā ||*

*Word for word:* tāra pāche pāche — right behind Him; dāruṇa nanadī — the harsh sister-in-law; dhāila dhamaka diyā — ran with threats; katadūra yāi pāila — going a little way, caught Him; palāite nārila parāṇa-piyā — the Beloved of my life could not escape

**13.5.** The harsh sister-in-law ran after Him with threats; going a little way, she caught up — and the Beloved of my life could not escape.

যৌবন-গৌরবে মাতি অতিশয় ধরিয়া দুখানি করে ।
কত কটু বাণী কহি রহি রহি লইয়া আইসে ঘরে ॥

*yaubana-gaurabe māti atiśaya dhariyā dukhāni kare |*
*kata kaṭu bāṇī kahi rahi rahi laiyā āise ghare ||*

*Word for word:* yaubana-gaurabe māti — drunk with the pride of youth; atiśaya dhariyā dukhāni kare — seizing firmly by both hands; kata kaṭu bāṇī kahi — speaking many harsh words; rahi rahi — stopping again and again; laiyā āise ghare — brings Him into the house

**13.6.** Drunk with the pride of youth, she seized Him firmly by both hands — and, abusing Him in every way, stopping again and again, she leads Him into the house.

কিশোর বয়স রসময় গোরা চাহিয়া ননদী পানে ।
বাঁধি ভুজপাশে করি পরাজয় কৈল যে আছিল মনে ॥

*kiśora bayasa rasamaya gorā cāhiyā nanadī pāne |*
*bām̐dhi bhujapāśe kari parājaya kaila ye āchila mane ||*

*Word for word:* kiśora bayasa — youthful; rasamaya gorā — Gora full of rasa; cāhiyā nanadī pāne — looking at the sister-in-law; bām̐dhi bhujapāśe — binding in the noose of His arms; kari parājaya — conquering; kaila ye āchila mane — did what was in His heart

**13.7.** Youthful Gora, full of rasa, looked at my sister-in-law — bound her in the noose of His arms, conquered her, and did what was in His heart.[^31-31]

মোরে না দেখিতে পাঞা গুণমণি বিমন হইয়া গেলা ।
অবশ হইয়া ননদিনী পুনঃ আমার নিকট আইলা ॥

*more nā dekhite pāñā guṇamaṇi bimana haiyā gelā |*
*abaśa haiyā nanadinī punaḥ āmāra nikaṭa āilā ||*

*Word for word:* more nā dekhite pāñā — not finding me; guṇamaṇi — the Jewel of virtues; bimana haiyā gelā — went away dejected; abaśa haiyā — limp; nanadinī punaḥ — the sister-in-law again; āmāra nikaṭa āilā — came to me

**13.8.** Not finding me, the Jewel of virtues went away dejected; and my sister-in-law, all limp, came to me again.

চাহি তার পানে পুছিনু এবা কি আছহ হরিষচিতে ।
তেঁই অধোমুখে কহয়ে ঠেকিনু বিষম চোরের হাতে ॥

*cāhi tāra pāne puchinu ebā ki āchaha hariṣacite |*
*tem̐i adhomukhe kahaye ṭhekinu biṣama corera hāte ||*

*Word for word:* cāhi tāra pāne — looking at her; puchinu — I asked; ebā ki — what is this; āchaha hariṣacite — you are glad at heart; tem̐i adhomukhe — she with downcast face; kahaye — says; ṭhekinu biṣama corera hāte — I fell into the hands of a terrible thief

**13.9.** Looking at her, I asked: 'What is this — why are you so glad at heart?' She, with downcast face, says: 'I fell into the hands of a terrible thief.

রাখিব গোপনে নহে পরভাতে হইবে কলঙ্ক-ধূম ।
নরহরি সাথী তাহে আশ্বাসিতে ভাঙ্গিল আঁখির ঘুম ॥

*rākhiba gopane nahe parabhāte haibe kalaṅka-dhūma |*
*narahari sāthī tāhe āśvāsite bhāṅgila ām̐khira ghuma ||*

*Word for word:* rākhiba gopane — keep it secret; nahe — otherwise; parabhāte haibe kalaṅka-dhūma — in the morning the smoke of scandal will rise; narahari sāthī — Narahari the witness; tāhe āśvāsite — as (I began) to console her; bhāṅgila ām̐khira ghuma — sleep left (my) eyes

**13.10.** Keep it secret, or in the morning the smoke of scandal will rise.'" Narahari is the witness: as I began to console her, sleep left my eyes.[^31-32]

[^31-30]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — pp. 215–216, no. 135 (scan PDF pp. 474–475); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 135 (catalogue: NG-348). GCC — kirana 8, pada 11 (ed. 1947, p. 99;
scan PDF p. 104), "anyā ca — yathārāga". GCC readings: "prabeśila adhika madana-bhare" — "entered, overflowing with Madana" (13.2; GPT "athira ānanda bhare", "trembling
with joy"; the GPT text is translated), "basilena nanadinīra pālaṅka-pare" (13.2), "kara-pallave cibuka paraśe haraṣa haiyā" (13.3), "kata dūre yāi pāila, palāite
nārila parāṇapiyā" (13.5), "yaubana-garabe" (13.6), "tem̐ha adhomukhe" (13.9), "parabhāte haibe kalaṅka-dhūma" (13.10). B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to
the section (chapter 27).
[^31-31]: 13.7 is a direct motif of sambhoga (bound her in the noose of His arms, "conquered", "did what was in His heart" — kaila ye āchila mane); translated exactly,
adding nothing. The pada is a farce: the strict sister-in-law who guards the young wife is herself "conquered" by Gaura; this is the motif running through GCC (the
strict elders, on seeing Gaura, lose their severity; cf. nn. 12, 23 of chapter 30) carried to a coarse joke. Such a depiction of the Lord is precisely what the
Gaudiya tradition rejects: the Lord did not touch women and in Navadvipa did not look at them (CB, Adi); the worship of Gaura as a nagara is an apasampradaya
(Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati; introductory note, chapter 27). This is a townswoman's dream told for laughter (13.1: "what a laugh!").
[^31-32]: "The smoke of scandal" (kalaṅka-dhūma) — evil rumour. The signature is "Narahari the witness" (narahari sāthī): the poet brings himself into the dream as a
witness; the last words
(āśvāsite bhāṅgila ām̐khira ghuma — "as [I] began to console her, sleep left the eyes") are understood thus: the teller herself consoles her sister-in-law and at once
wakes up (cf. the ending of 12.8: "I saved my life by waking up quickly"); the subject is not named in the original, and the reading "as he began to console her" is also possible.

## 14. Narahari — "svapanera kathā śuna go sajani…" (GPT1 pp. 216–217, no. 136; GCC 8.12)
*Nagari-bhava; a comic dream. In a dream the Beloved entered the townswoman's house wrapped in a blanket, so that her sister-in-law would not
recognise Him; she seated Him on a couch and threw off His blanket — and His face shone like the moon from behind the clouds; her mother-in-law
asked what the light in the house was, and the townswoman answered that it was Chandra, the moon god, who had appeared, pleased with her vow, and
asked the mother-in-law to name a boon; she wished everyone wealth, long life and well-being; returning, the townswoman wiped her Beloved's body
with the end of her sari, He embraced her — and then she woke. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 8, pada 12.*[^31-33]

স্বপনের কথা শুন গো সজনি পরাণ-রসিকরায় ।
অলখিত ঘরে প্রবেশিল কালি কম্বল উড়িয়া গায় ॥

*svapanera kathā śuna go sajani parāṇa-rasikarāya |*
*alakhita ghare prabeśila kāli kambala uṛiyā gāya ||*

*Word for word:* svapanera kathā — about the dream; śuna go sajani — listen, friend; parāṇa-rasikarāya — the Connoisseur of rasa, the Beloved of my life; alakhita — unseen; ghare prabeśila — entered the house; kāli — yesterday; kambala uṛiyā gāya — wrapped in a blanket

**14.1.** "Listen to the dream, friend: yesterday the Connoisseur of rasa, the Beloved of my life, entered the house unseen, wrapped in a blanket.

তাহা দেখি মৃদু হাসিয়া পুছিনু এ সাজ সাজিলে কেনে ।
পিয়া কহে তুয়া ননদিনী কালি পাছে বা আমারে চিনে ॥

*tāhā dekhi mṛdu hāsiyā puchinu e sāja sājile kene |*
*piyā kahe tuyā nanadinī kāli pāche bā āmāre cine ||*

*Word for word:* tāhā dekhi — seeing it; mṛdu hāsiyā — laughing softly; puchinu — I asked; e sāja sājile kene — why have You dressed like this; piyā kahe — the Beloved says; tuyā nanadinī — your sister-in-law; kāli pāche vā āmāre cine — lest later (tomorrow) she recognise Me

**14.2.** Seeing this, I laughed softly and asked: 'Why have You dressed up like this?' The Beloved says: 'In case your sister-in-law should recognise Me later [tomorrow].'[^31-34]

এইরূপ কত কহিল তা শুনি বসন ঝাঁপিয়া মুখে ।
সুরুচির করে ধরি প্রাণনাথে পালঙ্কে বসানু সুখে ॥

*eirūpa kata kahila tā śuni basana jhām̐piyā mukhe |*
*surucira kare dhari prāṇanāthe pālaṅke basānu sukhe ||*

*Word for word:* eirūpa kata kahila — much like this He said; tā śuni — hearing it; basana jhām̐piyā mukhe — covering my face with my cloth; surucira kare dhari — taking by the lovely hand; prāṇanāthe — the Lord of my life; pālaṅke basānu sukhe — I joyfully seated on the couch

**14.3.** Much like this He said; hearing it, I covered my face with the end of my cloth, took the Lord of my life by His lovely hand and joyfully seated Him on the couch.

সে সময়ে মুখ-মাধুরী অধিক কি কব মনেতে বাসি ।
কালিন্দীর জলে প্রফুল্লিত যেন কনক-কমলরাশি ॥

*se samaye mukha-mādhurī adhika ki kaba manete bāsi |*
*kālindīra jale praphullita yena kanaka-kamalarāśi ||*

*Word for word:* se samaye — at that moment; mukha-mādhurī adhika — the sweetness of the face was great; ki kaba manete bāsi — what shall I say of what I felt; kālindīra jale — in the waters of the Kalindi; praphullita yena — as if blossomed; kanaka-kamalarāśi — a mass of golden lotuses

**14.4.** What sweetness His face had at that moment — what can I say of what was in my heart? As if a mass of golden lotuses had blossomed in the waters of the Kalindi.

তাহা হেরি ধরি ধৃতি সে কম্বল খসাঞা ফেলিনু মেন ।
শরদের শশী ঘনঘটা হৈতে বাহির হইল যেন ॥

*tāhā heri dhari dhṛti se kambala khasāñā phelinu mena |*
*śaradera śaśī ghanaghaṭā haite bāhira haila yena ||*

*Word for word:* tāhā heri — seeing this; dhari dhṛti — taking heart; se kambala khasāñā phelinu — I threw off that blanket; mena (= yena) — as if; śaradera śaśī — the autumn moon; ghana-ghaṭā haite bāhira haila yena — came out from behind thick clouds

**14.5.** Seeing this, I took heart and threw off that blanket from Him — as if the autumn moon had come out from behind thick clouds.

হেনই সময়ে শাশুড়ী পুছয়ে ঘরেতে কিসের আলো ।
তাহা শুনি তনু কাঁপিল অমনি পরাণ উড়িয়া গেল ॥

*henai samaye śāśuṛī puchaye gharete kisera ālo |*
*tāhā śuni tanu kām̐pila amani parāṇa uṛiyā gela ||*

*Word for word:* henai samaye — at that very moment; śāśuṛī puchaye — the mother-in-law asks; gharete kisera ālo — what light is in the house; tāhā śuni — hearing this; tanu kām̐pila — my body trembled; amani parāṇa uṛiyā gela — my soul simply flew away

**14.6.** At that very moment my mother-in-law asks: 'What is that light in the house?' Hearing this, my whole body trembled — my soul simply flew away.

তরাতরি গিয়া দাঁড়াঞা দুয়ারে চাহিয়া সভয়মনে ।
সাহসে চাতুরী বচন কহিতে লাগিনু তাঁহার সনে ॥

*tarātari giyā dām̐ṛāñā duyāre cāhiyā sabhayamane |*
*sāhase cāturī bacana kahite lāginu tām̐hāra sane ||*

*Word for word:* tarātari giyā — going out in haste; dām̐ṛāñā duyāre — standing at the door; cāhiyā sabhayamane — looking with fear at heart; sāhase — with courage; cāturī bacana kahite lāginu — I began to speak cunning words; tām̐hāra sane — with her

**14.7.** Hurrying out, I stood at the door, looking with fear in my heart, and, taking courage, began to speak cunningly with her:

চন্দ্রব্রত মোর নিয়ম জানহ করিয়ে যতন পাইয়া ।
কৃপা করি তেঁই দেখা দিল আজি পূজায় প্রসন্ন হৈয়া ॥

*candrabrata mora niyama jānaha kariye yatana pāiyā |*
*kṛpā kari tem̐i dekhā dila āji pūjāya prasanna haiyā ||*

*Word for word:* candrabrata mora niyama — my vow to Chandra; jānaha — you know; kariye yatana pāiyā — I keep it with care; kṛpā kari — by grace; tem̐i dekhā dila āji — he appeared today; pūjāya prasanna haiyā — pleased with the worship

**14.8.** 'You know my vow to Chandra — I keep it with care; so by his grace he has appeared today, pleased with my worship.

বর দিতে চান কি বর মাগিব কিছু না জানিয়ে আমি ।
আপনি যে কহ তাহা লেই তাহে এথা না আসিও তুমি ॥

*bara dite cāna ki bara māgiba kichu nā jāniye āmi |*
*āpani ye kaha tāhā lei tāhe ethā nā āsio tumi ||*

*Word for word:* bara dite cāna — he wishes to give a boon; ki bara māgiba — what boon shall I ask; kichu nā jāniye āmi — I do not know; āpani ye kaha — what you say; tāhā lei — that I take; tāhe ethā nā āsio tumi — only do not come here

**14.9.** He wishes to give a boon — but what boon to ask I do not know; whatever you say, that I will take; only do not come in here yourself.'

ইহা শুনি ধীরে ধীরে কহে কত যতনে আনন্দ পাইয়া ।
সম্পদ্ আয়ু বৃদ্ধি শুভ সবার এতেক লেয়হ চাহিয়া ॥

*ihā śuni dhīre dhīre kahe kata yatane ānanda pāiyā |*
*sampad āyu bṛddhi śubha sabāra eteka leyaha cāhiyā ||*

*Word for word:* ihā śuni — hearing this; dhīre dhīre kahe — softly says; kata yatane — with great earnestness; ānanda pāiyā — delighted; sampad āyu bṛddhi śubha — wealth, long life, prosperity, well-being; sabāra — for all; eteka leyaha cāhiyā — ask for all this

**14.10.** Hearing this, softly, softly, delighted, she says with great earnestness: 'Ask for wealth, long life, prosperity and well-being for all — all of this.'

ইহা শুনি শীঘ্র ঘরে সামাইল অতি আনন্দবেশে ।
বসন-অঞ্চলে অঙ্গ মুছাইনু বসিয়া পিয়ার পাশে ॥

*ihā śuni śīghra ghare sāmāila ati ānandabeśe |*
*basana-añcale aṅga muchāinu basiyā piyāra pāśe ||*

*Word for word:* ihā śuni — hearing this; śīghra ghare sāmāila — quickly went into the house; ati ānandabeśe — in great joy; basana-añcale — with the end of my sari; aṅga muchāinu — I wiped His body; basiyā piyāra pāśe — sitting by the Beloved

**14.11.** Hearing this, I quickly went into the house in great joy; sitting by my Beloved, I wiped His body with the end of my sari.

নরহরি-প্রাণনাথ মোরে কত আদরে করিল কোলে ।
হেন কালে নিঁদ ভাঙ্গিল বিচ্ছেদে ভাসিনু আঁখির জলে ॥

*narahari-prāṇanātha more kata ādare karila kole |*
*hena kāle nim̐da bhāṅgila bicchede bhāsinu ām̐khira jale ||*

*Word for word:* narahari-prāṇanātha — the Lord of Narahari's life; more kata ādare — me with great tenderness; karila kole — took in His embrace; hena kāle — then; nim̐da bhāṅgila — sleep broke; bicchede — in separation; bhāsinu ām̐khira jale — I was drowned in tears

**14.12.** The Lord of Narahari's life with great tenderness took me in His embrace; then my sleep broke — and in separation I was drowned in tears."[^31-35]

[^31-33]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — pp. 216–217, no. 136 (scan PDF pp. 475–476); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 136 (catalogue: NG-108). GCC — kirana 8, pada 12 (ed. 1947, pp. 99–100;
scan PDF pp. 104–105), "anyā ca — yathārāga". GCC readings: "parāṇa rasika rāya" (14.1), "kanaka-kamala-rāśi" (14.4), "khasāyā phelinu mena" (14.5; "mena" — so also GPT1,
= "yena"), "tem̐ho dekhā dila" (14.8), "ethā nā āsiha tumi" (14.9), "āyubṛddhi śubha sabāra eteka leha cāyā" (14.10), "bhāsinu ām̐khira jale" (14.12). B. Nagari-bhava —
see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^31-34]: Bengali kāli means both "yesterday" and "tomorrow": in 14.1 — "yesterday" (the night being told of), in 14.2 — "tomorrow", "later". The blanket (kambala) under which Gaura hides the radiance of His body, and the
"light in the house" (14.6), play on the image of Gaura as the moon: the townswoman passes Him off as Chandra, the moon god — and this is true in a poetic sense: He is "the
Moon of Nadia". The deceiving of the mother-in-law is rendered as in the original (cf. n. 7 of chapter 30).
[^31-35]: The embrace (14.12) is a motif of sambhoga, translated exactly; the dream breaks off, and the townswoman is left in separation. The dream is her imagination; the Lord
did not touch women (CB, Adi); the tradition does not accept gaura-nagari (n. 10 and the introductory note, chapter 27).

## 15. Narahari — "śuna śuna ogo baliye tomāre svapane nadyāra śaśī…" (GPT1 p. 217, no. 137; GCC 8.13)
*Nagari-bhava; a dream. In a dream the Moon of Nadia sat beside the townswoman and asked her to adorn Him with her own hands; she oiled and
decked His hair with flowers, drew sandal on His brow, put on earrings, a pearl in His nose, bracelets, necklaces, a belt of bells and anklets —
and then woke before she had gazed her fill. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 8, pada 13.*[^31-36]

শুন শুন ওগো বলিয়ে তোমারে স্বপনে নদ্যার শশী ।
হাসি মোর পাশে আসিয়া বসিলা যেন হেমাম্বুজরাশি ॥

*śuna śuna ogo baliye tomāre svapane nadyāra śaśī |*
*hāsi mora pāśe āsiyā basilā yena hemāmbujarāśi ||*

*Word for word:* śuna śuna ogo — listen, listen, friend; baliye tomāre — I tell you; svapane — in a dream; nadyāra śaśī — the Moon of Nadia; hāsi — smiling; mora pāśe āsiyā basilā — came and sat beside me; yena hemāmbujarāśi — like a mass of golden lotuses

**15.1.** "Listen, listen, friend, I will tell you: in a dream the Moon of Nadia, smiling, came and sat beside me — like a mass of golden lotuses.

মোরে কহে আজু নিজকরে মোর বেশ বনাঅহ তুমি ।
শুনি সে চাতুরী-বচন যে সুখ তাহা কি কহিব আমি ॥

*more kahe āju nijakare mora beśa banāaha tumi |*
*śuni se cāturī-bacana ye sukha tāhā ki kahiba āmi ||*

*Word for word:* more kahe — He says to me; āju — today; nijakare — with your own hands; mora beśa banāaha tumi — you adorn Me; śuni se cāturī-bacana — hearing those clever words; ye sukha — what joy; tāhā ki kahiba āmi — how shall I tell it

**15.2.** He says to me: 'Today adorn Me with your own hands.' Hearing those clever words — what joy I felt, how can I tell?

বাড়িল কৌতুক নদীয়ার নব-যুবতী ভুলয়ে চুলে ।
নানা গন্ধতৈল দিয়া নানা ছাঁদে বাঁধিনু সাজায়ে ফুলে ॥

*bāṛila kautuka nadīyāra naba-yubatī bhulaye cule |*
*nānā gandhataila diyā nānā chām̐de bām̐dhinu sājāye phule ||*

*Word for word:* bāṛila kautuka — merriment grew; nadīyāra naba-yubatī bhulaye cule — the hair that enchants the young women of Nadia; nānā gandhataila diyā — with many fragrant oils; nānā chām̐de bām̐dhinu — I dressed it in many styles; sājāye phule — decking it with flowers

**15.3.** The merriment grew: His hair — the young women of Nadia are mad for it — I anointed with many fragrant oils, dressed in many styles and decked with flowers.

ললাটে রচিনু রুচির চন্দন বিন্দু সুচন্দ্রের প্রায় ।
শ্রুতিমূলে দিনু কুণ্ডল ঝলকে ভানু কি উপমা তায় ॥

*lalāṭe racinu rucira candana bindu sucandrera prāya |*
*śrutimūle dinu kuṇḍala jhalake bhānu ki upamā tāya ||*

*Word for word:* lalāṭe racinu — on the brow I drew; rucira candana bindu — lovely drops of sandal; sucandrera prāya — like bright moons; śrutimūle dinu kuṇḍala — I fixed earrings at the ears; jhalake bhānu — they flash like the sun; ki upamā tāya — what comparison for them

**15.4.** On His brow I drew lovely drops of sandal, like bright moons; at His ears I fixed earrings — they flash like the sun; with what can I compare them?

হাসিমাখা মুখ কমল মুছাঞা দেখি ভুরু ভৃঙ্গপাঁতি ।
আঁখে আঁখি দিয়া নাসায় মুকুতা পরানু আনন্দে মাতি ॥

*hāsimākhā mukha kamala muchāñā dekhi bhuru bhṛṅgapām̐ti |*
*ām̐khe ām̐khi diyā nāsāya mukutā parānu ānande māti ||*

*Word for word:* hāsimākhā mukha kamala — the smiling lotus face; muchāñā — wiping; dekhi bhuru bhṛṅgapām̐ti — I see the brows, a row of bees; ām̐khe ām̐khi diyā — looking into His eyes; nāsāya mukutā parānu — I set a pearl in His nose; ānande māti — drunk with joy

**15.5.** Wiping the smiling lotus of His face, I saw His brows — like a row of bees; looking into His eyes, drunk with joy, I set a pearl in His nose.

সুললিত ভুজ গজশুণ্ড জিনি ধৈরজ ধরম হরে ।
তাহে নানা ভূষা দিয়া পুনঃ সাধে বলয়া সঁপিনু করে ॥

*sulalita bhuja gajaśuṇḍa jini dhairaja dharama hare |*
*tāhe nānā bhūṣā diyā punaḥ sādhe balayā sam̐pinu kare ||*

*Word for word:* sulalita bhuja — lovely arms; gajaśuṇḍa jini — outdoing an elephant's trunk; dhairaja dharama hare — steal composure and dharma; tāhe nānā bhūṣā diyā — putting many ornaments on them; punaḥ sādhe — and lovingly; balayā sam̐pinu kare — I put bracelets on the wrists

**15.6.** His lovely arms, outdoing an elephant's trunk, steal away composure and dharma; on them I put many ornaments and lovingly bracelets on His wrists.

পরিসর উরে হার সাজাইনু অতুল উদর-শোভা ।
কিঙ্কিণী কটিতটে পিন্ধাইনু লসয়ে জানুর আভা ॥

*parisara ure hāra sājāinu atula udara-śobhā |*
*kiṅkiṇī kaṭitaṭe pindhāinu lasaye jānura ābhā ||*

*Word for word:* parisara ure — on the broad chest; hāra sājāinu — I arranged necklaces; atula udara-śobhā — peerless the beauty of the waist; kiṅkiṇī kaṭitaṭe pindhāinu — I put a bell-belt on the hips; lasaye jānura ābhā — the knees shine

**15.7.** On His broad chest I arranged necklaces — peerless is the beauty of His waist; on His hips I put a belt of bells — His knees shine.

নরহরি প্রিয়-চরণে নূপুর পরানু যতন করি ।
হেন কালে নিঁদ ভাঙ্গিল দেখিতে না পানু নয়ন ভরি ॥

*narahari priya-caraṇe nūpura parānu yatana kari |*
*hena kāle nim̐da bhāṅgila dekhite nā pānu nayana bhari ||*

*Word for word:* narahari priya-caraṇe — on the feet of Narahari's Beloved; nūpura parānu — I put anklets; yatana kari — carefully; hena kāle — then; nim̐da bhāṅgila — sleep broke; dekhite nā pānu nayana bhari — I could not see Him to my eyes' fill

**15.8.** On the feet of Narahari's Beloved I carefully put anklets; then my sleep broke — and I could not gaze my fill of Him."[^31-37]

[^31-36]: Signature — "Narahari" (narahari priya — "Narahari's Beloved"). GPT1 — p. 217, no. 137 (scan PDF p. 476); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 137 (catalogue: NG-109). GCC — kirana 8,
pada 13 (ed. 1947, pp. 100–101; scan PDF pp. 105–106), "anyā ca — yathārāga". GCC readings: "naba yubatī bhule ye cule" (15.3), "bām̐kā chānde bāndhinu" — "tied it
aslant" (15.3), "candanabindu" (15.4), "bhṛṅga-pām̐ti" (15.5), "gaja-śuṇḍa" (15.6), "henakāle nim̐da bhāṅgila" (15.8). B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the
section (chapter 27).
[^31-37]: The heroine adorning the Beloved with her own hands (beśa racanā) is a motif of the padas on Radha adorning Krishna; the nose-pearl (gajamuktā), the belt of
bells and the anklets are Krishna's ornaments in the padas. In Gaura-lila the Lord was adorned and anointed by His companions (cf. Gaura's abhisheka and adornment
at Srivasa's — CB, Madhya; chapter 14); here the service is transferred into a townswoman's dream. There is no motif of sambhoga in the pada.

## 16. Narahari — "śuna śuna ogo parāṇa-sai…" (GPT1 pp. 217–218, no. 138; GCC 8.14)
*Nagari-bhava; a dream. A townswoman tells her friends without shame: in her dream Gora embraced and kissed her; she teased Him about the traces
of kajal, kumkum and sindur on His face, but then her harsh sister-in-law sat down at the door — the Beloved hid, and she woke; falling asleep
again, she saw Him adorning her — putting sindur in her parting, braiding her hair, putting on a bodice and a nose ornament — and laying her on
His breast. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 8, pada 14.*[^31-38]

শুন শুন ওগো পরাণ-সই ।
তোমা সবার পাশে নিলজি হইয়া নিশির স্বপন কই ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*śuna śuna ogo parāṇa-sai |*
*tomā sabāra pāśe nilaji haiyā niśira svapana kai || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* śuna śuna ogo — listen, listen; parāṇa-sai — dear friends; tomā sabāra pāśe — before all of you; nilaji haiyā — casting off shame; niśira svapana kai — I tell the night's dream

**16.1.** *(Refrain)* "Listen, listen, dear friends: before all of you, casting off shame, I will tell the night's dream.

হাসি হাসি সুখে ভাসি সে রঙ্গিয়া কত না আদরে মোরে ।
দুবাহু পসারি করি কত ভঙ্গী তুরিতে করয়ে কোরে ॥

*hāsi hāsi sukhe bhāsi se raṅgiyā kata nā ādare more |*
*dubāhu pasāri kari kata bhaṅgī turite karaye kore ||*

*Word for word:* hāsi hāsi — smiling; sukhe bhāsi — floating in joy; se raṅgiyā — that Playful One; kata nā ādare more — how tenderly to me; dubāhu pasāri — opening both arms; kari kata bhaṅgī — in every way; turite karaye kore — quickly takes into His embrace

**16.2.** Smiling, floating in joy, how tender that Playful One is with me! Opening both arms, in every way, He quickly takes me in His embrace.

থির হৈতে নারে থর থর তনু কাঁপয়ে বিজুরী ভাঁতি ।
লুবধ মধুপ সম মধু মুখ চুম্বয় আনন্দে মাতি ॥

*thira haite nāre thara thara tanu kām̐paye bijurī bhām̐ti |*
*lubadha madhupa sama madhu mukha cumbaya ānande māti ||*

*Word for word:* thira haite nāre — cannot be still; thara thara tanu kām̐paye — the body quivers and trembles; bijurī bhām̐ti — like lightning; lubadha madhupa sama — like a greedy bee; madhu mukha cumbaya — kisses the honeyed face; ānande māti — drunk with joy

**16.3.** He cannot be still — His body quivers, trembles like lightning; like a greedy bee, drunk with joy, He kisses the honeyed face.

সে চাঁদবদন কাজর কুঙ্কুম সিন্দূরে সুচারু সাজ ।
তাহারে করিনু পরিহাস শুনি বন্ধুয়া পাইল লাজ ॥

*se cām̐dabadana kājara kuṅkuma sindūre sucāru sāja |*
*tāhāre karinu parihāsa śuni bandhuyā pāila lāja ||*

*Word for word:* se cām̐dabadana — that moon-like face; kājara kuṅkuma sindūre — with kajal, kumkum and sindur; sucāru sāja — prettily adorned; tāhāre karinu parihāsa — I teased Him; śuni bandhuyā pāila lāja — hearing, my Friend was abashed

**16.4.** That moon-like face was prettily adorned with kajal, kumkum and sindur; seeing this, I teased Him — hearing it, my Friend was abashed.[^31-39]

মনসাধে পুনঃ সে চাঁদবদন মুছাইয়া ঈষৎ হাসি ।
হেন কালে মোর দুয়ারে দারুণ ননদী বৈঠিল আসি ॥

*manasādhe punaḥ se cām̐dabadana muchāiyā īṣat hāsi |*
*hena kāle mora duyāre dāruṇa nanadī baiṭhila āsi ||*

*Word for word:* manasādhe — lovingly; punaḥ se cām̐dabadana muchāiyā — wiping that moon face again; īṣat hāsi — smiling a little; hena kāle — just then; mora duyāre — at my door; dāruṇa nanadī baiṭhila āsi — the harsh sister-in-law came and sat

**16.5.** Lovingly, smiling a little, I wiped that moon-like face again; and just then my harsh sister-in-law came and sat down at my door.

উড়িল পরাণ কি করিব প্রাণবন্ধুয়া লুকালো ডরে ।
হেন কালে নিঁদ ভাঙ্গিল জাগিয়া হিয়া ধক ধক করে ॥

*uṛila parāṇa ki kariba prāṇabandhuyā lukālo ḍare |*
*hena kāle nim̐da bhāṅgila jāgiyā hiyā dhaka dhaka kare ||*

*Word for word:* uṛila parāṇa — my soul flew; ki kariba — what could I do; prāṇabandhuyā lukālo ḍare — the Friend of my life hid in fear; hena kāle nim̐da bhāṅgila — then sleep broke; jāgiyā — waking; hiyā dhaka dhaka kare — the heart pounds

**16.6.** My soul flew away — what could I do? The Friend of my life hid in fear; then my sleep broke — waking, I feel my heart pounding.

পুনঃ ঘুমাইতে সে নবনাগর রচয়ে আমার বেশ ।
সিঁথির সিন্দুর সাজায়ে কত সে যতনে বাঁধিয়া কেশ ॥

*punaḥ ghumāite se nabanāgara racaye āmāra beśa |*
*sim̐thira sindura sājāye kata se yatane bām̐dhiyā keśa ||*

*Word for word:* punaḥ ghumāite — when I slept again; se nabanāgara — that young Nagara; racaye āmāra beśa — adorns me; sim̐thira sindura sājāye — puts sindur in the parting; kata se yatane bām̐dhiyā keśa — with what care braiding the hair

**16.7.** When I fell asleep again, that young Nagara is adorning me: He puts sindur in my parting and with what care He braids my hair!

উরজে কাঁচলি দিতে মু কহিনু কাঁচলি পরাহ কেনে ।
পিয়া কহে হাসি পুরুষের বেশ নাহি কি তোমার মনে ॥

*uraje kām̐cali dite mu kahinu kām̐cali parāha kene |*
*piyā kahe hāsi puruṣera beśa nāhi ki tomāra mane ||*

*Word for word:* uraje kām̐cali dite — when putting a bodice on the breast; mu kahinu — I said; kām̐cali parāha kene — why do You put on a bodice; piyā kahe hāsi — the Beloved laughing says; puruṣera beśa — the man's attire; nāhi ki tomāra mane — do you not remember

**16.8.** When He began to put a bodice on my breast, I said: 'Why are You putting a bodice on me?' The Beloved, laughing, says: 'And the man's attire — do you not remember it?'

আর কি বলিব নাসায় বেশর দিতে সুচঞ্চল হৈয়া ।
অমনি শুতয়ে মোরে পরিসর বুকের উপরে লৈয়া ॥

*āra ki baliba nāsāya beśara dite sucañcala haiyā |*
*amani śutaye more parisara bukera upare laiyā ||*

*Word for word:* āra ki baliba — what more shall I say; nāsāya beśara dite — setting a nose ornament; sucañcala haiyā — eagerly; amani śutaye more — at once lays me; parisara bukera upare laiyā — on His broad chest

**16.9.** What more shall I say? Eagerly setting an ornament in my nose, He at once lays me on His broad chest.

কত ভাঁতি রসকাহিনী কহয়ে অমিঞা ঢালয়ে যেন ।
নরহরিনাথ পীরিতি মূরতি যুবতীমোহন মেন ॥

*kata bhām̐ti rasakāhinī kahaye amiñā ḍhālaye yena |*
*naraharinātha pīriti mūrati yubatīmohana mena ||*

*Word for word:* kata bhām̐ti — in every way; rasakāhinī kahaye — tells tales of rasa; amiñā ḍhālaye yena — as if pouring nectar; naraharinātha — Narahari's Lord; pīriti mūrati — love embodied; yubatīmohana mena (= yena) — the Enchanter of young women

**16.10.** In every way He tells tales of rasa — as if pouring nectar." Narahari's Lord is love embodied, the Enchanter of young women.[^31-40]

[^31-38]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — pp. 217–218, no. 138 (scan PDF pp. 476–477); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 138 (catalogue: NG-110). GCC — kirana 8, pada 14 (ed. 1947, pp. 101–102;
scan PDF pp. 106–107), "anyā ca — yathārāga". The first stanza is a refrain (dhru; so GPT1). GCC readings: "nilajī haiyā" (16.1), "cumbaye madane māti" — "drunk with
Madana" (16.3; GPT "ānande māti", "drunk with joy"; the GPT text is translated), "kājara kuṅkuma sindūre", "tā heri karinu parihāsa" (16.4; see n. 39), "mochāiye" (16.5),
"uroje kām̐cali dite mo kahinu kām̐culi parāha kene" (16.8). B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^31-39]: 16.4 is translated after GCC "kājara kuṅkuma sindūre sucāru sāja" (kajal, kumkum, sindur on the Beloved's face — traces of the embrace, a motif of the Krishna
padas); GPT1 and GPT2 "kātare kusuma sindure" ("in agitation — with flowers and sindur") is apparently a corruption.
[^31-40]: The embrace, the kiss (cumbaya), "lays me on His chest" are direct motifs of sambhoga; translated exactly, adding nothing. The dream is the townswoman's imagination:
the Lord did not touch women and in Navadvipa did not look at them (CB, Adi); the Gaudiya tradition does not accept gaura-nagari (Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati; introductory
note, chapter 27). 16.7–16.9 is the reverse motif: the Beloved adorns the heroine (cf. no. 15); the answer "And the man's attire…" (16.8) is not fully clear — probably a
joke about an earlier change of dress (in the padas on Radha and Krishna — the exchange of attire). "The Enchanter of young women" (yubatīmohana mena; "mena" = "yena",
so also GCC).

## 17. Narahari — "ki kaba svapane kata parihāsa kare go…" (GPT1 p. 218, no. 139; GCC 8.15)
*Nagari-bhava; a dream. A townswoman tells how in her dream Gora jested with her, embraced her, trembling, and spoke of rasa; the poet: "How
shameless is Narahari's Beloved — the thief of the dharma and vows of young wives!" Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC,
kirana 8, pada 15.*[^31-41]

কি কব স্বপনে কত পরিহাস করে গো রসিকশেখর মোর গোরা ।
কিবা সে নয়ান বাঁকা চাহনি বিষম গো জীবন-যৌবনধন-চোরা ॥

*ki kaba svapane kata parihāsa kare go rasikaśekhara mora gorā |*
*kibā se nayāna bām̐kā cāhani biṣama go jībana-yaubanadhana-corā ||*

*Word for word:* ki kaba — what shall I say; svapane — in the dream; kata parihāsa kare — how He jests; go — (address); rasikaśekhara mora gorā — my Gora, the Crown of connoisseurs of rasa; kibā se nayāna — and those eyes; bām̐kā cāhani biṣama — fearful curving glances; jībana-yaubanadhana-corā — stealing the treasure of life and youth

**17.1.** "What shall I say! In the dream how He jests, my Gora, the Crown of connoisseurs of rasa! And what eyes He has — fearful are the curving glances that steal the treasure of life and youth.

মধুর মধুর হাসি ভাসি কত সুখে গো মুখে মুখ দিয়া করে কোলে ।
পুলকিত অঙ্গ অতি মদন-তরঙ্গে গো কত না রসের কথা তোলে ॥

*madhura madhura hāsi bhāsi kata sukhe go mukhe mukha diyā kare kole |*
*pulakita aṅga ati madana-taraṅge go kata nā rasera kathā tole ||*

*Word for word:* madhura madhura hāsi — smiling sweetly, sweetly; bhāsi kata sukhe — floating in joy; mukhe mukha diyā — putting face to face; kare kole — takes into His embrace; pulakita aṅga — the body thrills; ati madana-taraṅge — in the waves of Madana; kata nā rasera kathā tole — how many words of rasa He raises

**17.2.** Smiling sweetly, sweetly, floating in joy, He puts His face to my face and takes me in His embrace; His body thrills in the waves of Madana — how many words of rasa He brings up!

সাধে সাধে নাসার বেশর দোলাইয়া গো না জানি কি রসে হয় ভোর ।
নরহরি-প্রাণপিয় কি নিলজ গো যুবতী-ধরম-ব্রত-চোর ॥

*sādhe sādhe nāsāra beśara dolāiyā go nā jāni ki rase haya bhora |*
*narahari-prāṇapiya ki nilaja go yubatī-dharama-brata-cora ||*

*Word for word:* sādhe sādhe — lovingly; nāsāra beśara dolāiyā — swinging the nose ornament; nā jāni ki rase haya bhora — I know not by what rasa He is enraptured; narahari-prāṇapiya — the Beloved of Narahari's life; ki nilaja — how shameless; yubatī-dharama-brata-cora — the thief of the dharma and vows of young wives

**17.3.** Lovingly swinging the ornament in my nose, He is — I know not by what rasa — enraptured." How shameless is the Beloved of Narahari's life — the thief of the dharma and vows of young wives![^31-42]

[^31-41]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — p. 218, no. 139 (scan PDF p. 477); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 139 (catalogue: NG-111). GCC — kirana 8, pada 15 (ed. 1947, p. 102; scan PDF
p. 107), "anyā ca — yathārāga". Metre — a long line with the address "go" in the middle. In GCC the pada is a line longer: in place of GPT's last line there are two
lines with more explicit details of the dream and the signature "narahari-prāṇa-priya nilaja emana go, yubatī-barata kare bhaṅga" ("so shameless is the Beloved of
Narahari's life — He breaks the vows of young wives"); GPT omits them and they are not translated here. GCC readings: "nayana" (17.1), "mukhe mukha diyā" (17.2). B.
Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^31-42]: The embrace, "puts His face to my face", "His body thrills in the waves of Madana" (madana-taraṅge) are direct motifs of sambhoga and attraction; translated exactly,
adding nothing and softening nothing. "Shameless… thief of the dharma and vows of young wives" is reproach-as-praise, usual in the padas on Krishna (cf. "the stealer of
clothes", "the breaker of dharma"); transferring it to Gaura is a convention of the nagari padas which the tradition rejects: the Lord did not touch women (CB, Adi; n. 10
and the introductory note, chapter 27).

## 18. Narahari — "svapane bandhuyā mora pālaṅke basila go…" (GPT1 p. 218, no. 140; GCC 8.16)
*Nagari-bhava; a dream. In a dream the Beloved sat on her couch, called her dearer than life, embraced her, offered her betel, touched her lips;
the poet: Narahari's Beloved is the only one who enchants young women. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 8,
pada 16.*[^31-43]

স্বপনে বন্ধুয়া মোর পালঙ্কে বসিল গো বারেক চাহিনু আঁখি কোণে ।
পীরিতি মূরতি গোরা কত আদরিয়া গো আপনা অধীন করি মানে ॥

*svapane bandhuyā mora pālaṅke basila go bāreka cāhinu ām̐khi koṇe |*
*pīriti mūrati gorā kata ādariyā go āpanā adhīna kari māne ||*

*Word for word:* svapane — in the dream; bandhuyā mora — my Friend; pālaṅke basila — sat on the couch; bāreka cāhinu ām̐khi koṇe — once I glanced from the corner of my eye; pīriti mūrati gorā — Gora, love embodied; kata ādariyā — so tenderly; āpanā adhīna kari māne — deems Himself in my power

**18.1.** "In the dream my Friend sat on the couch, and once I glanced at Him from the corner of my eye; Gora, love embodied, with such tenderness deems Himself in my power.

সে চাঁদবদনে মোরে বারে বারে কয় গো পরাণ অধিক মোর তুমি ।
ইহা বলি কোলেতে করিয়া সুখে ভাসে গো লাজেতে মরিয়া যাই আমি ॥

*se cām̐dabadane more bāre bāre kaya go parāṇa adhika mora tumi |*
*ihā bali kolete kariyā sukhe bhāse go lājete mariyā yāi āmi ||*

*Word for word:* se cām̐dabadane — with those moon-like lips; more bāre bāre kaya — tells me again and again; parāṇa adhika mora tumi — you are dearer to Me than life; ihā bali — saying this; kolete kariyā — embracing; sukhe bhāse — floats in joy; lājete mariyā yāi āmi — I die of shame

**18.2.** With His moon-like lips He tells me again and again: 'You are dearer to Me than life'; saying this, He embraces me and floats in joy, while I die of shame.

সাজায়ে তাম্বূল মোর বদনে সঁপিয়া গো হরষে বিভোর হঞা চায় ।
সে করপল্লবে পুনঃ অধর পরশি গো পরাণ নিছিয়া দেয় তায় ॥

*sājāye tāmbūla mora badane sam̐piyā go haraṣe bibhora hañā cāya |*
*se karapallabe punaḥ adhara paraśi go parāṇa nichiyā deya tāya ||*

*Word for word:* sājāye tāmbūla — preparing betel; mora badane sam̐piyā — putting it in my mouth; haraṣe bibhora hañā cāya — gazes, beside Himself with joy; se karapallabe — with that tendril-hand; punaḥ adhara paraśi — then touching the lips; parāṇa nichiyā deya tāya — offers His life for them (nichani)

**18.3.** Preparing betel, He puts it into my mouth and gazes, beside Himself with joy; then with His tendril-like hand He touches my lips — and offers His life for them.

মধুর মধুর হাসি অমিয়া বরষে গো কিবা বা সে সুরসিকপনা ।
নরহরি-প্রাণপিয়া হিয়ার পুতলি গো যুবতী মোহিতে একজনা ॥

*madhura madhura hāsi amiyā baraṣe go kibā bā se surasikapanā |*
*narahari-prāṇapiyā hiyāra putali go yubatī mohite ekajanā ||*

*Word for word:* madhura madhura hāsi — smiling sweetly, sweetly; amiyā baraṣe — showers nectar; kibā vā se surasikapanā — what art of a connoisseur of rasa; narahari-prāṇapiyā — the Beloved of Narahari's life; hiyāra putali — the darling (doll) of the heart; yubatī mohite ekajanā — the One who enchants young women

**18.4.** Smiling sweetly, sweetly, He showers nectar — what art of a connoisseur of rasa!" The Beloved of Narahari's life, the darling of the heart, is the One who enchants young women.[^31-44]

[^31-43]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — p. 218, no. 140 (scan PDF p. 477); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 140 (catalogue: NG-112). GCC — kirana 8, pada 16 (ed. 1947, pp. 102–103; scan PDF
pp. 107–108), "anyā ca — yathārāga". GCC readings: "ām̐khi-koṇe" (18.1), "madane bibhora hayā cāya" — "gazes, drunk with Madana" (18.3; GPT "haraṣe bibhora", "beside Himself with
joy"; the GPT text is translated), "bariṣe" (18.4), "narahari-prāṇa-priyā … eka janā" (18.4). B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^31-44]: The embrace and the touching of the lips are direct motifs of sambhoga; translated exactly. "Offers His life for them" (parāṇa nichiyā deya tāya) — the rite of
nichani: giving oneself in exchange "for" the beloved (cf. the glossary). "The darling of the heart" (hiyāra putali, lit. "the doll of the heart") — an endearment.
The dream is the townswoman's imagination; the Lord did not touch women (CB, Adi); the tradition does not accept gaura-nagari (n. 10 and the introductory note,
chapter 27).

## 19. Narahari — "śunaye svapana āmā pāne cāñā cāñā go…" (GPT1 pp. 218–219, no. 141; GCC 8.17)
*Nagari-bhava; a dream. In a dream Gora, gazing at the townswoman, sat down beside her, lifted away her veil, touched her chin, gazed at her face,
embraced her; the poet: where did Narahari's Beloved learn so many plays of rasa? Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC,
kirana 8, pada 17.*[^31-45]

শুনয়ে স্বপন আমা পানে চাঞা চাঞা গো যুবতীপরাণচোরা গোরা ।
জিনিয়া খঞ্জন যুগনয়ন নাচায় গো না জানি কি রসে হৈয়া ভোরা ॥

*śunaye svapana āmā pāne cāñā cāñā go yubatīparāṇacorā gorā |*
*jiniyā khañjana yuganayana nācāya go nā jāni ki rase haiyā bhorā ||*

*Word for word:* śunaye svapana — listen to the dream; āmā pāne cāñā cāñā — gazing and gazing at me; go — (address); yubatīparāṇa-corā gorā — Gora, the thief of the life of young women; jiniyā khañjana — outdoing wagtails; yuganayana nācāya — plays His pair of eyes; nā jāni ki rase haiyā bhorā — enraptured by I know not what rasa

**19.1.** "Listen to the dream: gazing and gazing at me, Gora, the thief of the life of young women, plays His pair of eyes that outdo the wagtails — enraptured by I know not what rasa.

হাসিয়া হাসিয়া আসি নিকটে বসিয়া গো ঘুঙট ঘুচায় নিজকরে ।
আহা মরি মরি বলি চিবুক পরশি গো বদন নেহারে বারে বারে ॥

*hāsiyā hāsiyā āsi nikaṭe basiyā go ghuṅaṭa ghucāya nijakare |*
*āhā mari mari bali cibuka paraśi go badana nehāre bāre bāre ||*

*Word for word:* hāsiyā hāsiyā — smiling; āsi nikaṭe basiyā — coming and sitting near; ghuṅaṭa ghucāya nijakare — lifts away the veil with His own hand; āhā mari mari bali — saying "ah, ah!"; cibuka paraśi — touching the chin; badana nehāre bāre bāre — gazes at the face again and again

**19.2.** Smiling, He came, sat beside me and with His own hand lifts away my veil; 'Ah, ah!' He says, touching my chin, and gazes at my face again and again.

কিবা সে পীরিতি তার মনে এই হয় গো গলায় পরিয়া করি-হার ।
অঙ্গে অঙ্গে পরশিতে কত রঙ্গ বাড়ে গো নবীন মদন সাথী তার ॥

*kibā se pīriti tāra mane ei haya go galāya pariyā kari-hāra |*
*aṅge aṅge paraśite kata raṅga bāṛe go nabīna madana sāthī tāra ||*

*Word for word:* kibā se pīriti — what love; tāra mane ei haya — this is in His mind; galāya pariyā kari-hāra — to wear (me) at His neck as a necklace; aṅge aṅge paraśite — when body touches body; kata raṅga bāṛe — how the play increases; nabīna madana sāthī tāra — young Madana is His companion

**19.3.** What love! — in His mind there is one thing: to wear me at His neck like a necklace; when body touches body, how the play increases — young Madana is His companion.

অধরে অধর দিতে যত রসিকতা গো কি কব না শুনি কভু কাণে ।
নরহরি প্রাণপিয়া কোথায় শিখিল গো এত না রসের কথা জানে ॥

*adhare adhara dite yata rasikatā go ki kaba nā śuni kabhu kāṇe |*
*narahari prāṇapiyā kothāya śikhila go eta nā rasera kathā jāne ||*

*Word for word:* adhare adhara dite — laying lips to lips; yata rasikatā — how much art; ki kaba — what shall I say; nā śuni kabhu kāṇe — never heard of; narahari prāṇapiyā — the Beloved of Narahari's life; kothāya śikhila — where did He learn; eta nā rasera kathā jāne — He knows so much of rasa

**19.4.** How much art there is in His laying lips to lips — what shall I say? I have never heard of such a thing." Where did the Beloved of Narahari's life learn it — He knows so much of rasa?[^31-46]

[^31-45]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — pp. 218–219, no. 141 (scan PDF pp. 477–478); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 141 (catalogue: NG-113; there wrongly "no. 111"). GCC — kirana 8, pada 17
(ed. 1947, p. 103; scan PDF p. 108), "kācicca — yathārāga". GCC readings: "cāyā cāyā go yubatī-parāṇa-corā gorā", "jiniyā khañjana yuga nayana nācāya go" (19.1), "badana
nehāre bāre bāre" (19.2), "galāya paraye kari hāra", "nabīna madana sāthī tāra" (19.3), "kothāya śikhila go eta vā rasera kathā jāne" (19.4). B. Nagari-bhava — see the
introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^31-46]: The touches, the embrace ("to wear me at His neck like a necklace"), the kiss (adhare adhara) are direct motifs of sambhoga; translated exactly, adding nothing and
softening nothing. The dream is the townswoman's imagination; the Lord did not touch women and in Navadvipa did not look at them (CB, Adi); the Gaudiya tradition does
not accept gaura-nagari (Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati; introductory note, chapter 27); according to Majumdar such GPT padas are late (here — Narahari Chakravarti).

## 20. Narahari — "ogo sai rasera bhramara mora gorā…" (GPT1 p. 219, no. 142; GCC 8.18)
*Nagari-bhava; a dream. "My Gora is a bee of rasa, the stealer of the honey of the lotus faces of young women": in the dream He sat beside her,
spoke nectarean words, touched her chin, laid His lips to hers, embraced her. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC,
kirana 8, pada 18.*[^31-47]

ওগো সই রসের ভ্রমর মোর গোরা ।
কে জানে মরম নব নবযুবতীর গো বদনকমল-মধুচোরা ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*ogo sai rasera bhramara mora gorā |*
*ke jāne marama naba nabayubatīra go badanakamala-madhucorā || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* ogo sai — friend; rasera bhramara mora gorā — my Gora is a bee of rasa; ke jāne marama — who knows the secret heart; naba nabayubatīra — of young women; badanakamala-madhucorā — the stealer of the honey of lotus faces

**20.1.** *(Refrain)* Friend, my Gora is a bee of rasa: who knows the secret heart of young women? — He is the stealer of the honey of their lotus faces.

স্বপনে আসিয়া মোর নিকটে বসিয়া হাসিয়া হাসিয়া কথা কয় ।
না জানি কেমন সে অমিয় রস ঢালে গো ঘুচায় শ্রবণমনোব্যথা ॥

*svapane āsiyā mora nikaṭe basiyā hāsiyā hāsiyā kathā kaya |*
*nā jāni kemana se amiya rasa ḍhāle go ghucāya śrabaṇamanobyathā ||*

*Word for word:* svapane āsiyā — coming in the dream; mora nikaṭe basiyā — sitting near me; hāsiyā hāsiyā kathā kaya — smiling, He talks; nā jāni kemana — I know not what; se amiya rasa ḍhāle — nectar of rasa He pours; ghucāya śrabaṇa-mano-byathā — removes the ache of ears and heart

**20.2.** "In the dream He came, sat beside me and, smiling, talks with me; I know not what nectar of rasa He pours — and the ache of ears and heart is gone.

কত না আদরে মোর চিবুক পরশি গো কিবা সে ভঙ্গিমা করে ছলে ।
অধরে অধর রাখি আঁখি না পালটে গো বদন ঝাঁপয়ে করতলে ॥

*kata nā ādare mora cibuka paraśi go kibā se bhaṅgimā kare chale |*
*adhare adhara rākhi ām̐khi nā pālaṭe go badana jhām̐paye karatale ||*

*Word for word:* kata nā ādare — with what tenderness; mora cibuka paraśi — touching my chin; kibā se bhaṅgimā kare chale — what grace in His wiles; adhare adhara rākhi — laying lips to lips; ām̐khi nā pālaṭe — does not turn His eyes away; badana jhām̐paye karatale — covers the face with His palm

**20.3.** With what tenderness He touches my chin — what grace in His wiles! Laying lips to lips, He does not turn His eyes away and covers my face with His palm.

হিয়ায় ধরয়ে হিয়া কি আর বলিব গো সঘনে কাঁপয়ে হেমদেহা ।
নরহরি পরাণবন্ধুয়া কিবা জানে গো সুখের পাথার তার লেহা ॥

*hiyāya dharaye hiyā ki āra baliba go saghane kām̐paye hemadehā |*
*narahari parāṇabandhuyā kibā jāne go sukhera pāthāra tāra lehā ||*

*Word for word:* hiyāya dharaye hiyā — holds heart to heart; ki āra baliba — what more shall I say; saghane kām̐paye hemadehā — the golden body trembles again and again; narahari parāṇa-bandhuyā — the Friend of Narahari's life; kibā jāne — what He knows; sukhera pāthāra tāra lehā — His love is an ocean of joy

**20.4.** He holds heart to heart — what more shall I say? — and His golden body trembles again and again." What does the Friend of Narahari's life know! — His love is an ocean of joy.[^31-48]

[^31-47]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — p. 219, no. 142 (scan PDF p. 478); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 142 (catalogue: NG-114). GCC — kirana 8, pada 18 (ed. 1947, p. 103; scan PDF
p. 108), "anyā ca — yathārāga". The first stanza is a refrain (dhru). GCC readings: "naba naba yubatīra go, badana-kamala-madhucorā" (20.1), "śrabaṇa-mana-byathā" (20.2),
"uroja jhām̐paye karatale" (20.3; GPT "vadana", "the face"; GCC is more explicit; the GPT text is translated), "narahari-parāṇabam̐dhuyā kibā jāne go, sukhera pāthāra
tāra lehā" (20.4). B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
