[^31-48]: "A bee of rasa" (rasera bhramara) is an image of Krishna in the padas (Madhukara); transferring it to Gaura is a convention of the nagari padas. The kiss and the
embrace (20.3–20.4) are direct motifs of sambhoga; translated exactly. The dream is the townswoman's imagination; the Lord did not touch women (CB, Adi); the tradition
does not accept gaura-nagari (n. 10 and the introductory note, chapter 27).

## 21. Narahari — "svapanera kathā kahite kahite uṭhila premera ḍheu…" (GPT1 pp. 219–220, no. 143; GCC 8.19)
*Nagari-bhava. As the townswomen told their dreams, a wave of prema rose: one laments that the Creator made her a woman for sorrow — she can never
gaze her fill on Gorachand; another is ready to rid herself by cunning of the fear of the elders; a third — to leave home for Gaurasundara; one
complains of the wicked tongues of Nadia, another wishes her name to be linked by rumour with Shachi's son; one calls them to go to Him at once;
and the last one's left eye twitches — a good omen, says the poet. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 8,
pada 19.*[^31-49]

স্বপনের কথা কহিতে কহিতে উঠিল প্রেমের ঢেউ ।
অতি অনুপম প্রীতি রীতি ধৃতি ধরিতে নারয়ে কেউ ॥

*svapanera kathā kahite kahite uṭhila premera ḍheu |*
*ati anupama prīti rīti dhṛti dharite nāraye keu ||*

*Word for word:* svapanera kathā kahite kahite — as they told their dreams; uṭhila premera ḍheu — a wave of prema rose; ati anupama prīti rīti — so peerless their love; dhṛti dharite nāraye keu — none can keep composure

**21.1.** As they told their dreams, a wave of prema rose: their love is so peerless that none of them can keep composure.

কেহ বলে ওগো দুখ ভুঞ্জাইতে বিধাতা করিল নারী ।
হেন গোরাচাঁদে কখন দেখিতে না পানু নয়ন ভরি ॥

*keha bale ogo dukha bhuñjāite bidhātā karila nārī |*
*hena gorācām̐de kakhana dekhite nā pānu nayana bhari ||*

*Word for word:* keha bale ogo — one says: oh; dukha bhuñjāite — to suffer sorrow; bidhātā karila nārī — the Creator made me a woman; hena gorācām̐de — such a Gorachand; kakhana dekhite nā pānu nayana bhari — never could I see Him to my eyes' fill

**21.2.** One says: "Oh, the Creator made me a woman to suffer sorrow: never can I gaze my fill on such a Gorachand!"

কেহ বলে ওগো রমণী হইলে না পূরে মনের আশ ।
বিবিধ চাতুরি করি ঘুচাইব এ গুরুজনের ত্রাস ॥

*keha bale ogo ramaṇī haile nā pūre manera āśa |*
*bibidha cāturi kari ghucāiba e gurujanera trāsa ||*

*Word for word:* keha bale ogo — another says: oh; ramaṇī haile — being a woman; nā pūre manera āśa — the heart's desire is not fulfilled; bibidha cāturi kari — with all kinds of cunning; ghucāiba e gurujanera trāsa — I will rid myself of this fear of the elders

**21.3.** Another says: "Oh, born a woman, one cannot fulfil the heart's desire; with all kinds of cunning I will rid myself of this fear of the elders."

কেহ বলে মরুক এ গুরুজনের করিব কিসের ডর ।
প্রাণধন গৌরসুন্দর লাগিয়া নিশ্চয় তেজিব ঘর ॥

*keha bale maruka e gurujanera kariba kisera ḍara |*
*prāṇadhana gaurasundara lāgiyā niścaya tejiba ghara ||*

*Word for word:* keha bale — a third says; maruka e gurujanera — let these elders perish; kariba kisera ḍara — what shall I fear; prāṇadhana gaurasundara lāgiyā — for the treasure of my life, Gaurasundara; niścaya tejiba ghara — I will surely leave home

**21.4.** A third says: "Let these elders perish — what have I to fear? For the treasure of my life, Gaurasundara, I will surely leave my home."[^31-50]

কেহ বলে ওগো নদীয়ার লোক বড়ই বিষম হয় ।
প্রাণনাথে কভু না দেখি তথাপি কত কুবচন কয় ॥

*keha bale ogo nadīyāra loka baṛai biṣama haya |*
*prāṇanāthe kabhu nā dekhi tathāpi kata kubacana kaya ||*

*Word for word:* keha bale ogo — one says: oh; nadīyāra loka — the people of Nadia; baṛai biṣama haya — are very wicked; prāṇanāthe kabhu nā dekhi — I have never seen the Lord of my life; tathāpi kata kubacana kaya — still they say so many evil things

**21.5.** One says: "Oh, the people of Nadia are very wicked: I have never even seen the Lord of my life, and still they say so many evil things."

কেহ বলে ওগো নদীয়ানগরে হইবে কলঙ্ককথা ।
তাহা না মানিয়া পিয়া হিয়া মাঝে রাখিয়া ঘুচাব ব্যথা ॥

*keha bale ogo nadīyānagare haibe kalaṅkakathā |*
*tāhā nā māniyā piyā hiyā mājhe rākhiyā ghucāba byathā ||*

*Word for word:* keha bale ogo — another says: oh; nadīyānagare — in the town of Nadia; haibe kalaṅkakathā — there will be scandal; tāhā nā māniyā — heedless of it; piyā hiyā mājhe rākhiyā — keeping the Beloved in my heart; ghucāba byathā — I will soothe the pain

**21.6.** Another says: "Oh, there will be talk throughout the town of Nadia; heedless of it, I will keep the Beloved in my heart and soothe my pain."

কেহ বলে ওগো দিবস রজনী এই যে বাসনা মনে ।
মোর পরিবাদ হউক নিশ্চয় শ্রীশচীনন্দন সনে ॥

*keha bale ogo dibasa rajanī ei ye bāsanā mane |*
*mora paribāda hauka niścaya śrīśacīnandana sane ||*

*Word for word:* keha bale ogo — yet another says: oh; dibasa rajanī — day and night; ei ye bāsanā mane — this desire in my heart; mora paribāda hauka niścaya — let my name surely be slandered; śrīśacīnandana sane — together with Sri Shachinandana

**21.7.** Yet another says: "Oh, day and night there is one desire in my heart: let my name surely be slandered together with Sri Shachinandana!"

কেহ বলে ওগো যে বল সে বল আর না রহিতে পারি ।
তা বিনু পরাণ আনছান করে বল কি উপায় করি ॥

*keha bale ogo ye bala se bala āra nā rahite pāri |*
*tā binu parāṇa ānachāna kare bala ki upāya kari ||*

*Word for word:* keha bale ogo — one says: oh; ye bala se bala — say what you will; āra nā rahite pāri — I can bear it no longer; tā binu — without Him; parāṇa ānachāna kare — my soul is restless; bala ki upāya kari — tell me, what shall I do

**21.8.** One says: "Oh, say what you will — I can bear it no longer: without Him my soul is restless; tell me, what shall I do?"

কেহ বলে ওগো এ কুললাজের কপালে আগুনি দিয়া ।
চল চল প্রাণপতিরে তুরিতে মিলিব এখনি গিয়া ॥

*keha bale ogo e kulalājera kapāle āguni diyā |*
*cala cala prāṇapatire turite miliba ekhani giyā ||*

*Word for word:* keha bale ogo — another says: oh; e kulalājera kapāle āguni diyā — throwing fire on the brow of this family shame; cala cala — come, come; prāṇapatire turite miliba ekhani giyā — let us quickly go and meet the Lord of our life now

**21.9.** Another says: "Oh, let us throw fire on the brow of this family shame — come, come quickly, let us go and meet the Lord of our life right now!"

কেহ বলে দেখ একি হৈল ওগো নাচয়ে এ বাম-আঁখি ।
নরহরি কহে ভাব কি লাগিয়া এসব শুভের সাখী ॥

*keha bale dekha eki haila ogo nācaye e bāma-ām̐khi |*
*narahari kahe bhāba ki lāgiyā esaba śubhera sākhī ||*

*Word for word:* keha bale — yet another says; dekha eki haila ogo — look, what is this; nācaye e bāma-ām̐khi — my left eye twitches; narahari kahe — Narahari says; bhāba ki lāgiyā — why worry; esaba śubhera sākhī — all these are witnesses of good fortune

**21.10.** Yet another says: "Look, what is happening to me? — my left eye is twitching!" Narahari says: why worry? — all these are witnesses of good fortune.[^31-51]

[^31-49]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — pp. 219–220, no. 143 (scan PDF pp. 478–479); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 143 (catalogue: NG-349). GCC — kirana 8, pada 19 (ed. 1947, pp. 103–104;
scan PDF pp. 108–109), "yathārāga". GCC readings: "nārī haile nā pūre manera āśa" (21.3), "keha bale ogo maruka e gurujanere kisera ḍara" (21.4), "tāhā nā māniye … ghucāba
bethā" (21.6), "śrīśacīnandana-sane" (21.7), "e kula-lājera kapāle āguni diyā", "miliba ekhana giyā" (21.9), "bhāba ki lāgiye" (21.10). B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory
note to the section (chapter 27).
[^31-50]: The resolve to leave home and disregard the elders (21.3–21.4, 21.9) is a motif of the gopis leaving husbands and homes for Krishna (Bhag. 10.29); the original speaks
plainly — translated exactly. The Gaudiya tradition does not accept the worship of Gaura in the mood of the nagaris (introductory note, chapter 27).
[^31-51]: 21.7: "let my name be slandered together with Shachinandana" (mora paribāda hauka… śrīśacīnandana sane) — as in the padas of the gopis, for whom the rumour of their
love for Krishna is an ornament (kalanka-bhushana). 21.9: "throw fire on the brow" (kapāle āguni diyā) — a curse: "damn it". 21.10: the twitching of a woman's left eye
is a good omen (for a man — the right); the poet's reply: "why worry (bhāba ki lāgiyā)? — all these are witnesses of good fortune" (the sense is conjectural).

## 22. Narahari — "rajanīprabhāte aneka maṅgala…" (GPT1 p. 220, no. 144; GCC 8.20)
*Nagari-bhava. At dawn the townswomen, seeing many good omens, forgot a little the pain of their hearts; each tells whom she worships in order
to attain Gauranga: one — Ganga-devi, another — Gauri, a third — the Sun, a fourth vows to honour Old Shiva if today she sees the Beloved
without hindrance. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 8, pada 20.*[^31-52]

রজনীপ্রভাতে অনেক মঙ্গল দেখিয়া যুবতীগণে ।
বিসরিল কিছু হিয়ার বেদনা আনন্দ বাড়িল মনে ॥

*rajanīprabhāte aneka maṅgala dekhiyā yubatīgaṇe |*
*bisarila kichu hiyāra bedanā ānanda bāṛila mane ||*

*Word for word:* rajanī-prabhāte — at the dawn of the night; aneka maṅgala dekhiyā — seeing many good omens; yubatīgaṇe — the young women; bisarila kichu hiyāra bedanā — forgot a little the heart's pain; ānanda bāṛila mane — joy grew in their minds

**22.1.** At the dawn of the night the young women, seeing many good omens, forgot a little the pain of their hearts, and joy grew in their minds.

কেহ বলে ওগো বুঝিলাম আজি প্রসন্ন হইল বিধি ।
যেবা অভিলাষ আছয়ে সভার সে সব হইবে সিধি ॥

*keha bale ogo bujhilāma āji prasanna haila bidhi |*
*yebā abhilāṣa āchaye sabhāra se saba haibe sidhi ||*

*Word for word:* keha bale ogo — one says: oh; bujhilāma āji — I understood: today; prasanna haila bidhi — the Creator has been gracious; yebā abhilāṣa āchaye sabhāra — whatever desire anyone has; se saba haibe sidhi — all will be fulfilled

**22.2.** One says: "Oh, I have understood: today the Creator has been gracious; whatever desire anyone has — all will be fulfilled."

কেহ বলে ওগো নিতি নিতি এই জাহ্নবী পূজিয়ে আমি ।
তার বরে প্রাণনাথেরে পাইব নিশ্চয় জানিহ তুমি ॥

*keha bale ogo niti niti ei jāhnabī pūjiye āmi |*
*tāra bare prāṇanāthere pāiba niścaya jāniha tumi ||*

*Word for word:* keha bale ogo — another says: oh; niti niti — every day; ei jāhnabī pūjiye āmi — I worship this Jahnavi; tāra bare — by her boon; prāṇanāthere pāiba niścaya — I will surely attain the Lord of my life; jāniha tumi — know it

**22.3.** Another says: "Oh, every day I worship this Jahnavi: by her boon I will surely attain the Lord of my life — know it."

কেহ বলে ওগো অনেক যতনে গৌরী আরাধিয়ে নিতি ।
তেঁই দুখ দূর করিব মিলায়ে গৌরাঙ্গ পরাণপতি ॥

*keha bale ogo aneka yatane gaurī ārādhiye niti |*
*tem̐i dukha dūra kariba milāye gaurāṅga parāṇapati ||*

*Word for word:* keha bale ogo — a third says: oh; aneka yatane — with great care; gaurī ārādhiye niti — I worship Gauri every day; tem̐i — so; dukha dūra kariba — I will end my sorrow; milāye gaurāṅga parāṇapati — meeting Gauranga, the Lord of my life

**22.4.** A third says: "Oh, with great care I worship Gauri every day: so I will end my sorrow, meeting Gauranga, the Lord of my life."

কেহ বলে ওগো ভানু আরাধনা করিয়ে বিবিধ মতে ।
তাঁর কৃপাবরে জুড়াইব হিয়া চিন্তা না করিহ চিতে ॥

*keha bale ogo bhānu ārādhanā kariye bibidha mate |*
*tām̐ra kṛpābare juṛāiba hiyā cintā nā kariha cite ||*

*Word for word:* keha bale ogo — yet another says: oh; bhānu ārādhanā kariye — I worship the Sun; bibidha mate — in many ways; tām̐ra kṛpābare — by his grace and boon; juṛāiba hiyā — I will soothe my heart; cintā nā kariha cite — do not worry

**22.5.** Yet another says: "Oh, I worship the Sun in many ways: by his grace and boon I will soothe my heart — do not worry."

কেহ বলে যদি অবিরোধে আজু দেখিএ পরাণপিয়া ।
তবে বুড়াশিবে পূজিব যতনে নানা উপহার দিয়া ॥

*keha bale yadi abirodhe āju dekhie parāṇapiyā |*
*tabe buṛāśibe pūjiba yatane nānā upahāra diyā ||*

*Word for word:* keha bale — one says; yadi abirodhe — if without hindrance; āju dekhie parāṇapiyā — today I see the Beloved of my life; tabe buṛāśibe pūjiba yatane — then I will worship Old Shiva with care; nānā upahāra diyā — offering many gifts

**22.6.** One says: "If today I see the Beloved of my life without hindrance — then I will worship Old Shiva with care, offering many gifts."[^31-53]

কেহ বলে মোর মনে লয় হেন এখনি মিলিব তারে ।
এইরূপ কত প্রেমের আবেশে কহয়ে পরস্পরে ॥

*keha bale mora mane laya hena ekhani miliba tāre |*
*eirūpa kata premera ābeśe kahaye paraspare ||*

*Word for word:* keha bale — another says; mora mane laya hena — I feel; ekhani miliba tāre — I shall meet Him right now; eirūpa kata — thus and much more; premera ābeśe — in the rapture of prema; kahaye paraspare — they talk with one another

**22.7.** Another says: "I feel I shall meet Him right now." Thus, in the rapture of prema, they talk with one another.

শ্রীগৌরসুন্দর-দরশনহেতু সবার চঞ্চল হিয়া ।
নরহরি কহে মরি মরি হেন প্রেমের বালাই লৈয়া ॥

*śrīgaurasundara-daraśanahetu sabāra cañcala hiyā |*
*narahari kahe mari mari hena premera bālāi laiyā ||*

*Word for word:* śrīgaurasundara-daraśana-hetu — for the darshan of Sri Gaurasundara; sabāra cañcala hiyā — all hearts tremble; narahari kahe — Narahari says; mari mari — ah, ah; hena premera bālāi laiyā — I take upon myself the ills of such prema

**22.8.** All their hearts are trembling — if only they could see Sri Gaurasundara. Narahari says: ah, ah! — I take upon myself all the ills of such prema.

[^31-52]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — p. 220, no. 144 (scan PDF p. 479); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 144 (catalogue: NG-115). GCC — kirana 8, pada 20 (ed. 1947, pp. 104–105; scan PDF
pp. 109–110), "yathārāga". It is followed in GCC by the short pada 8.21 (in tripadi metre: the nagaris know only Gora, He is their life and wealth; the poet prays that
the doings of the nagaris may always appear in his heart; not taken into GPT) and the colophon of the 8th kirana: "…the description of the tales of dreams". GCC
readings: "sabāra" (22.2), "jāhnabī", "tāra bare" (22.3), "tem̐ha dukha dūra kariba miliyā" (22.4), "tām̐ra kṛpābale" (22.5), "dekhiye" (22.6), "kahaye paraspare" (22.7;
GPT1 "paraśa pare" — a misprint; translated after GCC). B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^31-53]: Jahnavi — the Ganga; Gauri — Parvati; Bhanu — the Sun (Surya); "Old Shiva" (buṛā śiba, Vura-Shiva) — a revered murti of Shiva in Navadvipa. The girls and wives of
Nadia worship the demigods, praying to meet Gaura — as the gopis of Vraja worshipped Katyayani, praying for Krishna as their husband (Bhag. 10.22): the aim of their vows
is the Lord; translated as in the original.

## 23. Narahari — "rajanī prabhāte āju naba naba nāgarī yata…" (GPT1 pp. 220–221, no. 145; GCC 9.1)
*Nagari-bhava. At dawn the young nagaris, longing to see Gaura, devise stratagems — one plans tricks, another laughingly rejects them, a third
considers her mother-in-law's temper; and she, pleased by an astrologer's good words, had slept with the door unbarred and, waking at daybreak,
came to the young wives: "What are you doing here, children?" — "We are learning the tale of Lakshmi for the Lakshmi-puja," answers one; and the
mother-in-law praises them. The poet: there is nothing in the world but the desire for wealth. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably
Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 9, pada 1.*[^31-54]

রজনী প্রভাতে আজু নব নব নাগরী যত ।
প্রাণপ্রিয় গৌরদরশন-আশে রচয়ে যুকতি কত ॥

*rajanī prabhāte āju naba naba nāgarī yata |*
*prāṇapriya gauradaraśana-āśe racaye yukati kata ||*

*Word for word:* rajanī prabhāte āju — at daybreak today; naba naba nāgarī yata — all the young nagaris; prāṇapriya gauradaraśana-āśe — hoping to see Gaura, dear to their life; racaye yukati kata — devise so many stratagems

**23.1.** At daybreak today all the young nagaris, in the hope of seeing Gaura, dear to their life, devise so many stratagems!

পরম চতুরা রসিকিনী সব রস-সায়রেতে ভাসি ।
কেহ নানা ছল যোজনা করয়ে কেহ বা খণ্ডয়ে হাসি ॥

*parama caturā rasikinī saba rasa-sāyarete bhāsi |*
*keha nānā chala yojanā karaye keha bā khaṇḍaye hāsi ||*

*Word for word:* parama caturā — most clever; rasikinī saba — all versed in rasa; rasa-sāyarete bhāsi — floating in an ocean of rasa; keha nānā chala yojanā karaye — one plans all kinds of tricks; keha vā khaṇḍaye hāsi — another laughingly rejects them

**23.2.** All of them are most clever, versed in rasa, floating in an ocean of rasa: one plans all kinds of tricks, another laughingly rejects them.

কেহ নানা শঙ্কা নিবারিয়া চিতে চিন্তয়ে শাশুড়ীরীত ।
এথা তার শুভ দৈবজ্ঞবচনে হৈয়াছে অধিক প্রীত ॥

*keha nānā śaṅkā nibāriyā cite cintaye śāśuṛīrīta |*
*ethā tāra śubha daibajñabacane haiyāche adhika prīta ||*

*Word for word:* keha nānā śaṅkā nibāriyā cite — a third, setting aside many fears; cintaye śāśuṛīrīta — considers her mother-in-law's temper; ethā — meanwhile; tāra — she (the mother-in-law); śubha daibajñabacane — by an astrologer's good words; haiyāche adhika prīta — is greatly pleased

**23.3.** A third, setting aside many fears, considers her mother-in-law's temper; and she, meanwhile, is greatly pleased by an astrologer's good words.

মনের সুখেতে শুতিয়াছে বুড়ী ঘরের কপাট খুলি ।
চমকি চমকি উঠে ক্ষণে ক্ষণে রজনী পোহালো বলি ॥

*manera sukhete śutiyāche buṛī gharera kapāṭa khuli |*
*camaki camaki uṭhe kṣaṇe kṣaṇe rajanī pohālo bali ||*

*Word for word:* manera sukhete — in her contentment; śutiyāche buṛī — the old woman had slept; gharera kapāṭa khuli — with the door of the house unbarred; camaki camaki uṭhe — starting, she jumps up; kṣaṇe kṣaṇe — again and again; rajanī pohālo bali — saying "the night is over!"

**23.4.** In her contentment the old woman had slept with the door of the house unbarred; starting up again and again, she jumped up: "The night is over!"

জাগিয়া দেখয়ে পূরব দিশাতে অরুণ উদয় হৈলা ।
শয়ন ত্যজিয়া তরাতরি বধূগণের নিকটে আইলা ॥

*jāgiyā dekhaye pūraba diśāte aruṇa udaya hailā |*
*śayana tyajiyā tarātari badhūgaṇera nikaṭe āilā ||*

*Word for word:* jāgiyā dekhaye — waking, she sees; pūraba diśāte — in the east; aruṇa udaya hailā — the dawn has risen; śayana tyajiyā — leaving her bed; tarātari — in haste; badhūgaṇera nikaṭe āilā — she came to the young wives

**23.5.** Waking, she sees: in the east the dawn has risen; hastily leaving her bed, she came to her daughters-in-law.

মধুরবচনে পুছে বাছা সব কি কর বসিয়া এথা ।
কেহ বলে ওগো লক্ষ্মীপূজা লাগি শিখিয়ে লক্ষ্মীর কথা ॥

*madhurabacane puche bāchā saba ki kara basiyā ethā |*
*keha bale ogo lakṣmīpūjā lāgi śikhiye lakṣmīra kathā ||*

*Word for word:* madhurabacane puche — sweetly asks; bāchā saba — children; ki kara basiyā ethā — what are you sitting here doing; keha bale ogo — one says: oh; lakṣmīpūjā lāgi — for the Lakshmi-puja; śikhiye lakṣmīra kathā — we are learning the tale of Lakshmi

**23.6.** Sweetly she asks: "Children, what are you sitting here doing?" One says: "Oh, for the Lakshmi-puja we are learning the tale of Lakshmi."

এতেক শুনিয়া ভাল ভাল বলি প্রশংসে কতেক বার ।
নরহরি কহে ধনের বাসনা জগতে নাহিক আর ॥

*eteka śuniyā bhāla bhāla bali praśaṃse kateka bāra |*
*narahari kahe dhanera bāsanā jagate nāhika āra ||*

*Word for word:* eteka śuniyā — hearing this; bhāla bhāla bali — saying "good, good"; praśaṃse kateka bāra — praises many times; narahari kahe — Narahari says; dhanera bāsanā — the desire for wealth; jagate nāhika āra — there is nothing else in the world

**23.7.** Hearing this, saying "good, good", she praised them many times. Narahari says: in the world there is nothing but the desire for wealth.[^31-55]

[^31-54]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — pp. 220–221, no. 145 (scan PDF pp. 479–480); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 145 (catalogue: NG-116). GCC — kirana 9, pada 1 (ed. 1947, pp. 105–106;
scan PDF pp. 110–111), without a raga mark; the 9th kirana opens with the heading "Again in the morning — of the goings of the nagaris of Navadvipa, their desires, darshan
and the rest". GCC readings: "prāṇapriya gaura daraśana āse" (23.1), "keha vā khaṇḍaye hāsi" (23.2), "śubha daibajña bacane haiyāche adhika prīta" (23.3), "rajanī pohāila
bali" (23.4), "nāhika kāra" — "who has it not?" (23.7). The next GPT pada (no. 146 = GCC 9.2) — the mother-in-law's account of that very astrologer, who told her to send
the young wives to Shachi-devi — opens chapter 32. B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^31-55]: The Lakshmi-puja (worship of the goddess of prosperity) and "the tale of Lakshmi" (lakṣmīra kathā, "Lakshmi-katha" — a ritual story read by women at the puja) are
the pretext with which the young wives reassure their mother-in-law; the deceiving of the elders is rendered as in the original (cf. n. 7 of chapter 30). The signature is
the poet's smile: the mother-in-law, hearing of Lakshmi, that is, of wealth, is at once content; GCC has "who in the world has no desire for wealth?".

## Summary of chapter 31

*The chapter continues the padas signed "Narahari" from section 3.2 of GPT. All 23 padas were found in Narahari Chakravarti's "Gaura-charita-chintamani"
and checked against its scan ("probably Chakravarti" — B): no. 119 (no. 1) = GCC 2.13 — Gaura in sleep speaks the words of Krishna waking Radha (not
nagari-bhava; GPT placed it in the section of nagari padas); nos. 124–125 (nos. 2–3) = GCC 7.29–7.30 — the end of the townswomen's morning tales (the
husband praising Nimai Pandita; the house of Murari Gupta); nos. 126–144 (nos. 4–22) = GCC 8.2–8.20 — the 8th kirana, "the tales of dreams": at dawn the
townswomen tell their friends their dreams of Gaura and then speak of their love and of good omens; no. 145 (no. 23) = GCC 9.1 — the beginning of the 9th
kirana. Dreams with a direct motif of sambhoga (embrace, kiss, "He did what was in His heart") are translated exactly, without additions and without
softening, each with a note: the dream is the townswoman's imagination, the Lord in His lila did not touch women and in Navadvipa did not look at them (CB,
Adi), the Gaudiya tradition does not accept the worship of Gaura as a nagara (introductory note, chapter 27). Where GCC is more explicit than GPT ("drunk with
Madana", "lay down" instead of "sat", the extra lines in no. 17), the GPT text is translated and the GCC reading noted.*
