# Chapter 32. Nagari Padas — VI: the "Narahari" padas of GPT (sect. 3.2, nos. 146–168): the townswomen's daydreams and the talk of the heavenly women

*On what nagari-bhava is, the position of the tradition (Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja, Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati) and the rules of translation, see the introductory note to the section of nagari padas in chapter 27; on the two poets named Narahari (Narahari Sarakara and Narahari Chakravarti) and on the attribution labels ("probably Sarakara", "probably Chakravarti", "not established"), see the introductory note to the "Narahari" appendix in chapter 17.*

## 1. Narahari — "śuna śuna badhū eta dine bidhi…" (GPT1 pp. 221–222, no. 146; GCC 9.2)
*Nagari-bhava (a mother-in-law's speech). An elderly woman tells her daughters-in-law: yesterday an astrologer came to their house who knows what is in
everyone's mind; when she asked how good fortune might come, he told her to honour Shachi-devi, Nimaichand's mother: the dust of her feet removes the
threefold miseries, whoever sees her face at dawn knows no sorrow, and whoever reviles her is destroyed by the goddess Ugrachanda; so every morning she
should send her daughters-in-law to her house. The mother-in-law hurries the young wives off to Shachi — and they, covering their faces, make a show of
pleading their household work. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 9, pada 2.*[^32-1]

শুন শুন বধূ এত দিনে বিধি প্রসন্ন হইল মোরে ।
গত দিন দিন-প্রহর সময়ে দৈবজ্ঞ আইল ঘরে ॥

*śuna śuna badhū eta dine bidhi prasanna haila more |*
*gata dina dina-prahara samaye daibajña āila ghare ||*

*Word for word:* śuna śuna badhū — listen, listen, daughters-in-law; eta dine — at last (lit. "after so many days"); bidhi prasanna haila more — the Creator has become gracious to me; gata dina — yesterday; dina-prahara samaye — at the time of the day-watch (prahara — a "watch" of the day); daibajña āila ghare — an astrologer came to the house

**1.1.** "Listen, listen, daughters-in-law: at last the Creator has become gracious to me! Yesterday, at the time of the day-watch, an astrologer came to our house.

কি কহিব তার গুণগণ মেন এমন না দেখি এথা ।
যেবা যা পুছয়ে তাহা কহে সব জানয়ে মনের কথা ॥

*ki kahiba tāra guṇagaṇa mena emana nā dekhi ethā |*
*yebā yā puchaye tāhā kahe saba jānaye manera kathā ||*

*Word for word:* ki kahiba — what shall I say; tāra guṇagaṇa — of his virtues; mena (= yena) — as it were; emana nā dekhi ethā — such a one I have not seen here; yebā yā puchaye — whatever anyone asks; tāhā kahe saba — he tells it all; jānaye manera kathā — he knows what is in the mind

**1.2.** What shall I say of his virtues — such a one, truly, I have never seen here: whatever anyone asks, he tells it all — he knows what is in a person's mind.

কিরূপে মঙ্গল হবে বলি মুই ধরিনু তাহার পা ।
আমারে আতুর দেখি কহে কিছু চিন্তা না করিহ মা ॥

*kirūpe maṅgala habe bali mui dharinu tāhāra pā |*
*āmāre ātura dekhi kahe kichu cintā nā kariha mā ||*

*Word for word:* kirūpe maṅgala habe — how will good come; bali — saying; mui dharinu tāhāra pā — I clasped his feet; āmāre ātura dekhi — seeing me anxious; kahe — he says; kichu cintā nā kariha — do not worry at all; mā — mother

**1.3.** 'How will good fortune come?' I said, and clasped his feet. Seeing my anxiety, he says: 'Do not worry at all, mother.

তোমাদের গ্রামে শচীদেবী বৈসে না জান মহিমা তাঁর ।
পরম পূজিতা জগতের মাঝে বিদিত চরিত যাঁর ॥

*tomādera grāme śacīdebī baise nā jāna mahimā tām̐ra |*
*parama pūjitā jagatera mājhe bidita carita yām̐ra ||*

*Word for word:* tomādera grāme — in your village; śacīdebī baise — lives Shachi-devi; nā jāna mahimā tām̐ra — do you not know her greatness; parama pūjitā — supremely honoured; jagatera mājhe — in the world; bidita carita yām̐ra — whose deeds are renowned

**1.4.** In your village lives Shachi-devi — do you not know her greatness? She is supremely honoured in the world; her deeds are known to all.

অতি সুলভ তাঁর পদরজ যে জন ধরএ শিরে ।
ধনজন হবে এ কি বড় কথা তুরিতে ত্রিতাপ হরে ॥

*ati sulabha tām̐ra padaraja ye jana dharae śire |*
*dhanajana habe e ki baṛa kathā turite tritāpa hare ||*

*Word for word:* ati sulabha — very easily had; tām̐ra padaraja — the dust of her feet; ye jana dharae śire — whoever places on the head; dhanajana habe — wealth and kin will come; e ki baṛa kathā — is that anything great; turite — swiftly; tritāpa hare — it removes the threefold miseries

**1.5.** Very easily had is the dust of her feet: whoever places it on his head will have wealth and kin — but what is great in that! — at once it removes the threefold miseries.

রজনীপ্রভাতে উঠিয়া যে জন দেখয়ে তাঁহার মুখ ।
জনমে জনমে সে সুখে ভাসয়ে কভু না জানয়ে দুখ ॥

*rajanīprabhāte uṭhiyā ye jana dekhaye tām̐hāra mukha |*
*janame janame se sukhe bhāsaye kabhu nā jānaye dukha ||*

*Word for word:* rajanīprabhāte uṭhiyā — rising at dawn; ye jana dekhaye tām̐hāra mukha — whoever sees her face; janame janame — birth after birth; se sukhe bhāsaye — floats in happiness; kabhu nā jānaye dukha — never knows sorrow

**1.6.** Whoever rises at dawn and sees her face floats in happiness birth after birth and never knows sorrow.

শচীমায়ে যেবা নিন্দয়ে সে দুখ-আনলে পুড়িয়া মরে ।
নিশ্চয় জানিহ উগ্রচণ্ডা দেবী তাহারে সংহার করে ॥

*śacīmāye yebā nindaye se dukha-ānale puṛiyā mare |*
*niścaya jāniha ugracaṇḍā debī tāhāre saṃhāra kare ||*

*Word for word:* śacīmāye yebā nindaye — whoever reviles Mother Shachi; se — he; dukha-ānale puṛiyā mare — burns to death in the fire of sorrow; niścaya jāniha — know for certain; ugracaṇḍā debī — the goddess Ugrachanda; tāhāre saṃhāra kare — destroys him

**1.7.** Whoever reviles Mother Shachi burns to death in the fire of sorrow; know for certain: the goddess Ugrachanda destroys him.

তাহে উপদেশ দিয়া বধূগণে মনের কপট ছাড়ি ।
নিশি পরভাতে যতনে পাঠাবে শ্রীশচীদেবীর বাড়ী ॥

*tāhe upadeśa diyā badhūgaṇe manera kapaṭa chāṛi |*
*niśi parabhāte yatane pāṭhābe śrīśacīdebīra bāṛī ||*

*Word for word:* tāhe — therefore; upadeśa diyā badhūgaṇe — instructing your daughters-in-law; manera kapaṭa chāṛi — giving up all guile of heart; niśi parabhāte — at the break of night; yatane pāṭhābe — send them with care; śrī-śacīdebīra bāṛī — to the house of Sri Shachi-devi

**1.8.** Therefore, instructing your daughters-in-law and giving up all guile of heart, send them with care at daybreak to the house of Sri Shachi-devi.

তেঁহ কৃপা করি করিবে আশীষ পূরিবে মনের আশ ।
বাড়িবে সম্পদ সদা সুখ বহু বিপদ হইবে নাশ ॥

*tem̐ha kṛpā kari karibe āśīṣa pūribe manera āśa |*
*bāṛibe sampada sadā sukha bahu bipada haibe nāśa ||*

*Word for word:* tem̐ha kṛpā kari — she, being gracious; karibe āśīṣa — will bless; pūribe manera āśa — the heart's wish will be fulfilled; bāṛibe sampada — prosperity will grow; sadā sukha bahu — always much happiness; bipada haibe nāśa — misfortunes will be destroyed

**1.9.** She will be gracious and bless them — and the heart's wish will be fulfilled: prosperity will grow, there will always be much happiness, misfortunes will be destroyed.

পরদুঃখে দুঃখী নিতান্ত জানিহ নিমাইচাঁদের মায় ।
এইরূপ কত কহি অন্য বাড়ী গেলেন দৈবজ্ঞরায় ॥

*paraduḥkhe duḥkhī nitānta jāniha nimāicām̐dera māya |*
*eirūpa kata kahi anya bāṛī gelena daibajñarāya ||*

*Word for word:* paraduḥkhe duḥkhī — grieved by others' grief; nitānta jāniha — know for sure; nimāicām̐dera māya — Nimaichand's mother; eirūpa kata kahi — saying much like this; anya bāṛī gelena — went on to another house; daibajñarāya — the worthy astrologer

**1.10.** Know for sure: Nimaichand's mother grieves at others' grief.' Saying much like this, the worthy astrologer went on to another house.[^32-2]

এ সকল কথা শুনিয়া আমার বড়ই আনন্দ হৈল ।
মনে অনুভব কৈনু হেন যেন সব অমঙ্গল গেল ॥

*e sakala kathā śuniyā āmāra baṛai ānanda haila |*
*mane anubhaba kainu hena yena saba amaṅgala gela ||*

*Word for word:* e sakala kathā śuniyā — hearing all this; āmāra baṛai ānanda haila — I became very glad; mane anubhaba kainu — I felt in my heart; hena yena — as if; saba amaṅgala gela — all ill fortune had gone

**1.11.** Hearing all this I was very glad: I felt in my heart as if all ill fortune had gone.

তাহাতে তোমরা যাও শীঘ্র করি সে হয় আমার ঘর ।
দিদি বলি মোরে আদর করে সে কভু না জানয়ে পর ॥

*tāhāte tomarā yāo śīghra kari se haya āmāra ghara |*
*didi bali more ādara kare se kabhu nā jānaye para ||*

*Word for word:* tāhāte — so; tomarā yāo śīghra kari — go quickly; se haya āmāra ghara — she is my own (lit. "she is my house"); didi bali — calling me "elder sister"; more ādara kare — treats me fondly; se kabhu nā jānaye para — she never regards anyone as a stranger

**1.12.** So go quickly: she is my own — she calls me 'elder sister', treats me fondly, and never regards anyone as a stranger.

তথা গিয়া তাঁরে প্রণাম করিয়া কহিয়ে বিনয়-বাণী ।
তাঁহার কৃপায় হবে সব সুখ ইহা ত নিশ্চয় জানি ॥

*tathā giyā tām̐re praṇāma kariyā kahiye binaya-bāṇī |*
*tām̐hāra kṛpāya habe saba sukha ihā ta niścaya jāni ||*

*Word for word:* tathā giyā — going there; tām̐re praṇāma kariyā — bowing to her; kahiye binaya-bāṇī — speak humble words; tām̐hāra kṛpāya — by her grace; habe saba sukha — all happiness will come; ihā ta niścaya jāni — this I know for certain

**1.13.** When you get there, bow to her and speak humble words: by her grace all happiness will come — this I know for certain.

তোমা সবা প্রতি তেঁহ কহিবেন এ বেলা থাকহ এথা ।
তাহে কোন ছলে আসিবে সকালে আমি যে যাইব সেথা ॥

*tomā sabā prati tem̐ha kahibena e belā thākaha ethā |*
*tāhe kona chale āsibe sakāle āmi ye yāiba sethā ||*

*Word for word:* tomā sabā prati — to you all; tem̐ha kahibena — she will say; e belā thākaha ethā — stay here this morning; tāhe — then; kona chale — on some pretext; āsibe sakāle — come back early; āmi ye yāiba sethā — for I myself shall go there

**1.14.** She will say to you all: 'Stay here this morning,' — then come back early on some pretext: for I myself shall be going there."

শাশুড়ীর অতি আতুর বচন শুনিয়া অধিক সুখে ।
আদর লাগিয়া ধীরে ধীরে কহে বসন ঝাঁপিয়া মুখে ॥

*śāśuṛīra ati ātura bacana śuniyā adhika sukhe |*
*ādara lāgiyā dhīre dhīre kahe basana jhām̐piyā mukhe ||*

*Word for word:* śāśuṛīra ati ātura bacana — the mother-in-law's most eager words; śuniyā adhika sukhe — hearing with great joy; ādara lāgiyā — to be coaxed; dhīre dhīre kahe — [one] says softly; basana jhām̐piyā mukhe — covering her face with her cloth

**1.15.** Hearing the mother-in-law's most eager words, [the young wives] are overjoyed; and, to be coaxed a little more, one says very softly, covering her face with her cloth:

প্রভাত সময়ে কেমনে ছাড়িয়া যাইব ঘরের কাজ ।
নরহরি কহে আসিয়া করিবা এখন না সহে ব্যাজ ॥

*prabhāta samaye kemane chāṛiyā yāiba gharera kāja |*
*narahari kahe āsiyā karibā ekhana nā sahe byāja ||*

*Word for word:* prabhāta samaye — at the time of dawn; kemane chāṛiyā yāiba — how can we go, leaving; gharera kāja — the household work; narahari kahe — Narahari says; āsiyā kariba — you will come back and do it; ekhana nā sahe byāja — now there must be no delay

**1.16.** "How can we go in the morning, leaving the household work?" Narahari says: "You will come back and do it; now there must be no delay."[^32-3]

[^32-1]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — pp. 221–222, no. 146 (scan PDF pp. 480–481); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 146 (catalogue: NG-117). GCC — kirana 9, pada 2 (ed. 1947,
pp. 106–107; scan PDF pp. 111–112), "bṛddhāha — yathārāga" ("the old woman said"). The ninth kirana of GCC ("Again in the morning — the outings of the nagaris of Navadvipa,
their wishes, their darshan and so on"; it opens with GCC 9.1, no. 23 of chapter 31) tells how the mothers-in-law themselves send their daughters-in-law to Shachi-devi;
GPT omits GCC 9.3–9.5 — the mother-in-law coaxes the young wives again, they dress, bow to her and set out (9.3), the joyful procession of the young women (9.4, Vrajabuli,
raga lalita) and the first of their "wishes" — to bow to Shachi and steal a glance at Gauranga (9.5). Before 9.5 the author has a Sanskrit rubric, "their wishes
(manoratha) he relates in order": the following padas (nos. 2–12 of this chapter) are these wishes. GCC readings: "parama ānanda" (1.11), "yāha śīghra kari" (1.12),
"āsiyā karibe" (1.16). B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^32-2]: The astrologer's speech is a praise of Shachi-devi, the Lord's mother: so the Vaishnava biographies too honour her (CB, Adi and Madhya — Shachi as the mother of the
Lord, worthy of the whole world's reverence). The "threefold miseries" (tritāpa) — those caused by one's own body and mind, by other beings and by the forces of nature.
Ugrachanda (ugracaṇḍā) is a fierce form of Durga (Chandi); the threat to those who revile Shachi is the village astrologer's word, rendered as in the original. The
promise "will have wealth and kin — but what is great in that" (1.5) the poet puts in the astrologer's mouth so that the mother-in-law, mindful of prosperity, will
gladly let the young wives go (cf. the end of no. 23 of chapter 31: "there is nothing in the world but the craving for wealth").
[^32-3]: 1.15–1.16: the young wives, longing to see Gaura, make a show of pleading their household work "to be coaxed" — the poet's smile; rendered as in the original.
The last line can be understood either as the mother-in-law's answer or as the poet's own word ("Narahari says…"); it is left as in the original.

## 2. Narahari — "sakhīsaha sukhe śrīśacīdebīra…" (GPT1 p. 222, no. 147; GCC 9.6)
*Nagari-bhava; a daydream. On the way to Shachi's house a townswoman dreams: she will stand with her friend in Shachi-devi's courtyard and steal a
glance at Gaura; He will answer with a sly look — and she will have neither composure nor dharma left, she will tremble at Madana's arrow and strain
to embrace Gaurangachand, but her friend will hold her back by the end of her sari; the others will laugh, she will be abashed and turn away, covering
her face — and Gaura will smile. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 9, pada 6.*[^32-4]

সখীসহ সুখে শ্রীশচীদেবীর অঙ্গনে দাঁড়াব গিয়া ।
অলখিতে তাঁরে বারেক নিরখি জুড়াব নয়ন হিয়া ॥

*sakhīsaha sukhe śrīśacīdebīra aṅgane dām̐ṛāba giyā |*
*alakhite tām̐re bāreka nirakhi juṛāba nayana hiyā ||*

*Word for word:* sakhīsaha sukhe — gladly, with my friend; śrī-śacīdebīra aṅgane — in the courtyard of Sri Shachi-devi; dām̐ṛāba giyā — I shall go and stand; alakhite — unnoticed; tām̐re bāreka nirakhi — glancing at Him once; juṛāba nayana hiyā — I shall cool my eyes and heart

**2.1.** "Gladly, with my friend, I shall go and stand in the courtyard of Sri Shachi-devi; unnoticed, I shall glance at Him once — and cool my eyes and heart.

সে পুনঃ মো পানে চাহিবে তাহার বিষম আঁখির ঠারে ।
ধৈরজ ধরম কিছু না থাকিবে কাঁপিব মদনশরে ॥

*se punaḥ mo pāne cāhibe tāhāra biṣama ām̐khira ṭhāre |*
*dhairaja dharama kichu nā thākibe kām̐piba madanaśare ||*

*Word for word:* se punaḥ — He in turn; mo pāne cāhibe — will look at me; tāhāra biṣama ām̐khira ṭhāre — with the sly signal of His eyes; dhairaja dharama — composure and dharma; kichu nā thākibe — nothing will remain; kām̐piba madanaśare — I shall tremble at Madana's arrow

**2.2.** He in turn will look at me — with the sly signal of His eyes; I shall have neither composure nor dharma left — I shall tremble at Madana's arrow.

ঘামেতে তিতিবে তনু ঘন ঘন আউলাবে মাথার কেশ ।
খসিবে বসন বারে বারে আর না রবে লাজের লেশ ॥

*ghāmete titibe tanu ghana ghana āulābe māthāra keśa |*
*khasibe basana bāre bāre āra nā rabe lājera leśa ||*

*Word for word:* ghāmete titibe tanu — my body will be wet with sweat; ghana ghana — again and again; āulābe māthāra keśa — my hair will come loose; khasibe basana bāre bāre — my cloth will slip again and again; āra nā rabe lājera leśa — not a trace of shame will remain

**2.3.** My body will be wet with sweat, my hair will keep coming loose; my cloth will slip again and again — not a trace of shame will remain.

গৌরাঙ্গচাঁদেরে আলিঙ্গন দিতে অধিক উদ্যত হব ।
আঁচরে ধরিয়া রাখিবেক সখী তাহার কথায় রব ॥

*gaurāṅgacām̐dere āliṅgana dite adhika udyata haba |*
*ām̐care dhariyā rākhibeka sakhī tāhāra kathāya raba ||*

*Word for word:* gaurāṅgacām̐dere — Gaurangachand; āliṅgana dite — to embrace; adhika udyata haba — I shall be all too eager; ām̐care dhariyā — seizing the end of my sari; rākhibeka sakhī — my friend will hold me back; tāhāra kathāya raba — I shall heed her word

**2.4.** I shall be all too eager to embrace Gaurangachand — my friend will hold me back by the end of my sari; I shall heed her word.

মোরে এইরূপ হেরি আনে আনে করিব কতেক হাসি ।
সে সব বুঝিয়া থির হব চিতে কিঞ্চিৎ সঙ্কোচ বাসি ॥

*more eirūpa heri āne āne kariba kateka hāsi |*
*se saba bujhiyā thira haba cite kiñcit saṅkoca bāsi ||*

*Word for word:* more eirūpa heri — seeing me so; āne āne — the others among themselves; kariba kateka hāsi — will laugh a good deal; se saba bujhiyā — understanding all that; thira haba cite — I shall grow calm at heart; kiñcit saṅkoca bāsi — feeling a little abashed

**2.5.** Seeing me so, the others will laugh a good deal among themselves; understanding all that, I shall grow calm at heart, a little abashed.

বিমুখী হইয়া দাঁড়াইব পুনঃ বসন ঝাঁপিয়া মুখে ।
নরহরি-প্রাণনাথে তাহা দেখি হাসিবে মনের সুখে ॥

*bimukhī haiyā dām̐ṛāiba punaḥ basana jhām̐piyā mukhe |*
*narahari-prāṇanāthe tāhā dekhi hāsibe manera sukhe ||*

*Word for word:* bimukhī haiyā — turning away; dām̐ṛāiba punaḥ — I shall stand again; basana jhām̐piyā mukhe — covering my face with my cloth; narahari-prāṇanāthe — the Lord of Narahari's life; tāhā dekhi — seeing this; hāsibe manera sukhe — will smile with joy of heart

**2.6.** Turning away, I shall stand again, covering my face with my cloth; the Lord of Narahari's life, seeing this, will smile with joy of heart."[^32-5]

[^32-4]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — p. 222, no. 147 (scan PDF p. 481); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 147 (catalogue: NG-118). GCC — kirana 9, pada 6 (ed. 1947, p. 109; scan
PDF p. 114), "kācicca — yathārāga" ("and another [said]"). This is the second of the "wishes" (manoratha) of the townswomen on their way to Shachi's house (note 1):
all the padas nos. 2–12 are in the future tense ("I shall stand", "I shall glance", "He will say"), i.e. not an account of what happened but what each one pictures to
herself on the way. GCC reading: "kām̐piba madana-bhare" — "I shall tremble under Madana's weight" (2.2). B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section
(chapter 27).
[^32-5]: 2.2–2.4: "I shall tremble at Madana's arrow", "neither composure nor dharma left", the slipping cloth, the urge to embrace Gaurangachand — a direct motif of
attraction; rendered exactly, adding nothing and softening nothing. It is the townswoman's daydream, her imagination: in the pada itself she is held back, and Gaura
only smiles. According to the biographies, in Navadvipa the Lord did not look at women or touch them (CB, Adi); the Gaudiya tradition does not accept the worship of
Gaura as a nagara (introductory note, chapter 27; Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati counts "gaura-nagari" among the apasampradayas). The padas of this cycle belong to
Narahari Chakravarti (18th c.); Majumdar regards the long GPT padas signed Narahari as late, not Sarakara's.

## 3. Narahari — "saiyera samīpe dām̐ṛāiba punaḥ…" (GPT1 pp. 222–223, no. 148; GCC 9.7)
*Nagari-bhava; a daydream (feigned mana). A townswoman dreams: at her friend's sign she will stand beside her, turned away from Gaura; unable to see
her face, He will be troubled and with the corner of His eye will ask her friend: "Why such anger? Forgive — one's own are not blamed; tell her to lift
her veil just once." The friend will entreat her, she in feigned anger will go and stand far off; Gauranga will be bathed in tears, the friend will
clasp her feet — and then, smiling, she will lift her veil and glance sidelong, giving Him supreme joy. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably
Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 9, pada 7.*[^32-6]

সইয়ের সমীপে দাঁড়াইব পুনঃ সইয়ের ইঙ্গিত পাইয়া ।
গৌরনাগরের পানে না হেরিব রহিব বিমুখী হৈয়া ॥

*saiyera samīpe dām̐ṛāiba punaḥ saiyera iṅgita pāiyā |*
*gauranāgarera pāne nā heriba rahiba bimukhī haiyā ||*

*Word for word:* saiyera samīpe — beside my friend; dām̐ṛāiba punaḥ — I shall stand again; saiyera iṅgita pāiyā — at my friend's sign; gaura-nāgarera pāne — at Gaura the nagara; nā heriba — I shall not look; rahiba bimukhī haiyā — I shall stay turned away

**3.1.** "At my friend's sign I shall stand beside her again; I shall not look at Gaura the nagara — I shall stay turned away.

মোর মুখ নিরখিতে না পাইয়া অধিক ব্যাকুল হবে ।
অলখিত মোর সখী প্রতি হেরি নয়ন-কোণেতে কবে ॥

*mora mukha nirakhite nā pāiyā adhika byākula habe |*
*alakhita mora sakhī prati heri nayana-koṇete kabe ||*

*Word for word:* mora mukha nirakhite nā pāiyā — unable to see my face; adhika byākula habe — [He] will be much troubled; alakhita — unnoticed; mora sakhī prati heri — looking at my friend; nayana-koṇete kabe — will say with the corner of His eye

**3.2.** Unable to see my face, He will be much troubled; glancing unnoticed at my friend, He will say to her with the corner of His eye:

কিছু না বুঝিয়ে কি লাগিয়া এত হৈয়াছে দারুণ রোষ ।
ক্ষমা করহ আপন জনের কেহ ত না লয় দোষ ॥

*kichu nā bujhiye ki lāgiyā eta haiyāche dāruṇa roṣa |*
*kṣamā karaha āpana janera keha ta nā laya doṣa ||*

*Word for word:* kichu nā bujhiye — I do not understand at all; ki lāgiyā — why; eta haiyāche dāruṇa roṣa — there is such cruel anger; kṣamā karaha — forgive; āpana janera — one's own; keha ta nā laya doṣa — no one holds it against

**3.3.** 'I do not understand at all: why such cruel anger? Forgive — no one holds it against one's own.

বারেক ঘুঙট ঘুচাইতে বল আমার শপথ দিয়া ।
ও মুখমাধুরী নিরখিয়া মোর জুড়াক নয়ন হিয়া ॥

*bāreka ghuṅaṭa ghucāite bala āmāra śapatha diyā |*
*o mukhamādhurī nirakhiyā mora juṛāka nayana hiyā ||*

*Word for word:* bāreka ghuṅaṭa ghucāite bala — tell her to lift her veil just once; āmāra śapatha diyā — adjuring her by Me; o mukhamādhurī nirakhiyā — beholding the sweetness of that face; mora juṛāka nayana hiyā — let My eyes and heart be cooled

**3.4.** Tell her to lift her veil just once, adjuring her by Me: let My eyes and heart be cooled by beholding the sweetness of that face.'

এতেক বুঝিয়া সখী মোরে পুনঃ কহিবে বিনয় করি ।
মুখের বসন ঘুচায়ে দাঁড়াহ দেখুক গৌরহরি ॥

*eteka bujhiyā sakhī more punaḥ kahibe binaya kari |*
*mukhera basana ghucāye dām̐ṛāha dekhuka gaurahari ||*

*Word for word:* eteka bujhiyā — understanding this; sakhī more punaḥ kahibe — my friend will say to me; binaya kari — entreating; mukhera basana ghucāye — removing the cloth from your face; dām̐ṛāha — stand; dekhuka gaurahari — let Gaurahari see

**3.5.** Understanding this, my friend will entreat me: 'Take the cloth from your face and stand there — let Gaurahari see.'

এ কথা শুনি না শুনিব সে পুনঃ ঘুচাবে আপন করে ।
তাহে নিবারিয়া অধিক কোরধে দাঁড়াব যাইয়া দূরে ॥

*e kathā śuni nā śuniba se punaḥ ghucābe āpana kare |*
*tāhe nibāriyā adhika koradhe dām̐ṛāba yāiyā dūre ||*

*Word for word:* e kathā śuni — hearing this; nā śuniba — I shall not hear; se punaḥ ghucābe — she then will lift it; āpana kare — with her own hand; tāhe nibāriyā — stopping her; adhika koradhe — in great anger; dām̐ṛāba yāiyā dūre — I shall go and stand far off

**3.6.** Hearing this, I shall pretend not to hear; then she will lift it with her own hand — but I shall stop her and in great anger go and stand far off.

ইহা নিরখিয়া নয়নের জলে ভাসিবে গৌরাঙ্গ রায় ।
তাহা দেখি সখী আতুর হইয়া ধরিবে আমার পায় ॥

*ihā nirakhiyā nayanera jale bhāsibe gaurāṅga rāya |*
*tāhā dekhi sakhī ātura haiyā dharibe āmāra pāya ||*

*Word for word:* ihā nirakhiyā — seeing this; nayanera jale bhāsibe — will be bathed in tears; gaurāṅga rāya — Gauranga Raya; tāhā dekhi — seeing that; sakhī ātura haiyā — my friend, distressed; dharibe āmāra pāya — will clasp my feet

**3.7.** Seeing this, Gauranga Raya will be bathed in tears; seeing that, my friend, distressed, will clasp my feet.

তখন হাসিয়া ঘুঙট ঘুচাঞা তেরছ নয়নে চাব ।
নরহরি-প্রাণপতি বন্ধুয়ারে পরম আনন্দ দিব ॥

*takhana hāsiyā ghuṅaṭa ghucāñā teracha nayane cāba |*
*narahari-prāṇapati bandhuyāre parama ānanda diba ||*

*Word for word:* takhana hāsiyā — then, smiling; ghuṅaṭa ghucāñā — lifting my veil; terachha nayane cāba — I shall glance sidelong; narahari-prāṇapati — the Lord of Narahari's life; bandhuyāre — to the Friend; parama ānanda diba — I shall give supreme joy

**3.8.** Then, smiling, I shall lift my veil and glance sidelong — I shall give the Lord of Narahari's life, the Friend, supreme joy."[^32-7]

[^32-6]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — pp. 222–223, no. 148 (scan PDF pp. 481–482); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 148 (catalogue: NG-119). GCC — kirana 9, pada 7 (ed. 1947,
pp. 109–110; scan PDF pp. 114–115). GCC readings: "keha nā laoye doṣa" (3.3), "juṛāuka nayāna hiyā" (3.4), "terachha nayāne raba" — "I shall remain [standing],
glancing sidelong" (3.8). B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^32-7]: Feigned anger (mana) and entreaty through a friend are motifs of the padas on Radha's mana, transferred to a townswoman's daydream; Gauranga's tears (3.7) and
His plea (3.3–3.4) are what she imagines; rendered as in the original. "Friend" (bandhuyā) and "the Lord of Narahari's life" are the townswoman's words and the
poet's signature about Gaura (cf. note 5 of chapter 31).

## 4. Narahari — "gaura nāgara rasera sāgara…" (GPT1 p. 223, no. 149; GCC 9.8)
*Nagari-bhava; a daydream. A townswoman dreams: looking at Gaura the nagara, the ocean of rasa, she will smile and talk with her friend about rasa;
seeing her wondrous grace, He will float in joy; she will signal to Him with a curved glance, bite her lip and draw her veil, and with the aim of her
brows steal away His composure; the King of connoisseurs of rasa will long to embrace her — and Narahari will restrain Him, reminding Him of what
people would say. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 9, pada 8.*[^32-8]

গৌর নাগর রসের সাগর হেরিয়া তাহার পানে ।
মুচকি হাসিয়া রসের কাহিনী কহিব সইয়ের সনে ॥

*gaura nāgara rasera sāgara heriyā tāhāra pāne |*
*mucaki hāsiyā rasera kāhinī kahiba saiyera sane ||*

*Word for word:* gaura nāgara — Gaura the nagara; rasera sāgara — the ocean of rasa; heriyā tāhāra pāne — looking at Him; mucaki hāsiyā — with a faint smile; rasera kāhinī — tales of rasa; kahiba saiyera sane — I shall tell my friend

**4.1.** "Looking at Gaura the nagara, the ocean of rasa, with a faint smile I shall tell my friend tales of rasa.

মোর অপরূপ ভঙ্গী নিরখিয়া সে পুনঃ ভাসিবে সুখে ।
ঈষৎ ঈষৎ হাসিয়া হাসিয়া ঠারিব বঙ্কিম আঁখে ॥

*mora aparūpa bhaṅgī nirakhiyā se punaḥ bhāsibe sukhe |*
*īṣat īṣat hāsiyā hāsiyā ṭhāriba baṅkima ām̐khe ||*

*Word for word:* mora aparūpa bhaṅgī — my wondrous grace; nirakhiyā — seeing; se punaḥ bhāsibe sukhe — He will float in joy; īṣat īṣat hāsiyā hāsiyā — smiling ever so slightly; ṭhāriba baṅkima ām̐khe — I shall signal with a curved glance

**4.2.** Seeing my wondrous grace, He will float in joy; smiling ever so slightly, I shall signal to Him with a curved glance.

তাহা বুঝি মুই দশনে অধর দাবিয়া ঘুঙট দিব ।
অলখিতে ভুরু-সন্ধানে বন্ধুর ধৈরজ হরিয়া নিব ॥

*tāhā bujhi mui daśane adhara dābiyā ghuṅaṭa diba |*
*alakhite bhuru-sandhāne bandhura dhairaja hariyā niba ||*

*Word for word:* tāhā bujhi — understanding that; mui — I; daśane adhara dābiyā — biting my lip; ghuṅaṭa diba — I shall draw my veil; alakhite — unnoticed; bhuru-sandhāne — by the aim of my brows; bandhura dhairaja hariyā niba — I shall steal away the Friend's composure

**4.3.** Understanding that, I shall bite my lip and draw my veil; unnoticed, by the aim of my brows, I shall steal away the Friend's composure.

মোরে আলিঙ্গন করিতে আতুর হইবে রসিকরাজ ।
নরহরি তাহে যতনে রাখিবে বুঝায়ে লোকের লাজ ॥

*more āliṅgana karite ātura haibe rasikarāja |*
*narahari tāhe yatane rākhibe bujhāye lokera lāja ||*

*Word for word:* more āliṅgana karite — to embrace me; ātura haibe — will long; rasikarāja — the King of connoisseurs of rasa; narahari tāhe — Narahari then; yatane rākhibe — will carefully restrain [Him]; bujhāye lokera lāja — reminding Him of what people would say (lit. "of shame before people")

**4.4.** The King of connoisseurs of rasa will long to embrace me — and Narahari will carefully restrain Him, reminding Him of what people would say."[^32-9]

[^32-8]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — p. 223, no. 149 (scan PDF p. 482); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 149 (catalogue: NG-120). GCC — kirana 9, pada 8 (ed. 1947, p. 110;
scan PDF p. 115). GCC readings: "alakhita bhuru-sandhāne" (4.3), "bujhāyā" (4.4). B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^32-9]: 4.4: Gaura longing for the townswoman's embrace is again her imagination (cf. note 5); rendered exactly. The poet places himself in the heroine's daydream as
the Lord's companion who restrains Him by "shame before people" (lokera lāja). According to the biographies, the Lord in Navadvipa was strict and did not look at
women (CB, Adi; cf. nos. 19–20 of this chapter, where Narahari's own heroines say the same).

## 5. Narahari — "saiyera nikaṭe dām̐ṛāba ghuṅaṭe…" (GPT1 p. 223, no. 150; GCC 9.12)
*Nagari-bhava; a daydream. A townswoman dreams: she will stand beside her friend with half her face veiled and steal glances; when the Friend looks
at her with a half-smile, she will look away; out of shyness He will lower His eyes — and then from the corner of her eye she will look at the moon of
His face; He will not be able to meet her eyes, and she will keep gazing. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 9,
pada 12.*[^32-10]

সইয়ের নিকটে দাঁড়াব ঘুঙটে ঝাঁপিয়া বদন আধ ।
অলপ অলপ চাহি অলখিত পুরাব মনের সাধ ॥

*saiyera nikaṭe dām̐ṛāba ghuṅaṭe jhām̐piyā badana ādha |*
*alapa alapa cāhi alakhita purāba manera sādha ||*

*Word for word:* saiyera nikaṭe dām̐ṛāba — I shall stand near my friend; ghuṅaṭe jhām̐piyā badana ādha — half my face covered by my veil; alapa alapa cāhi — glancing little by little; alakhita — unnoticed; purāba manera sādha — I shall fulfil my heart's desire

**5.1.** "I shall stand near my friend, half my face covered by my veil; glancing little by little, unnoticed, I shall fulfil my heart's desire.

বন্ধুয়া যখন আধ আধ হাসি চাহিবে আমার পানে ।
বুঝিয়া তখনি আঁখি ফিরাইয়া হেরিয়া রহিব আনে ॥

*bandhuyā yakhana ādha ādha hāsi cāhibe āmāra pāne |*
*bujhiyā takhani ām̐khi phirāiyā heriyā rahiba āne ||*

*Word for word:* bandhuyā yakhana — when the Friend; ādha ādha hāsi — with a half-smile; cāhibe āmāra pāne — will look at me; bujhiyā takhani — understanding, at once; ām̐khi phirāiyā — turning my eyes away; heriyā rahiba āne — I shall keep looking elsewhere

**5.2.** When the Friend looks at me with a half-smile, I shall understand, at once turn my eyes away and keep looking elsewhere.

প্রাণপিয়া লাজে লোচন সঙ্কোচ করিবে মধুর ছাঁদে ।
তাহা হেরি পুনঃ আড়-নয়নেতে হেরিব বদনচাঁদে ॥

*prāṇapiyā lāje locana saṅkoca karibe madhura chām̐de |*
*tāhā heri punaḥ āṛa-nayanete heriba badanacām̐de ||*

*Word for word:* prāṇapiyā — the Beloved of my life; lāje — out of shyness; locana saṅkoca karibe — will lower His eyes; madhura chām̐de — in a charming way; tāhā heri — seeing that; punaḥ āṛa-nayanete — again from the corner of my eye; heriba badanacām̐de — I shall look at the moon of His face

**5.3.** The Beloved of my life, out of shyness, will charmingly lower His eyes; seeing that, I shall again look from the corner of my eye at the moon of His face.

আঁখে আঁখি দিতে না পারে চঞ্চল তা হেরি রহিব চাঞা ।
নরহরি পহুঁ ভাসিবেন সুখে নয়নে নয়ন দিয়া ॥

*ām̐khe ām̐khi dite nā pāre cañcala tā heri rahiba cāñā |*
*narahari pahum̐ bhāsibena sukhe nayane nayana diyā ||*

*Word for word:* ām̐khe ām̐khi dite nā pāre — cannot meet my eyes; cañcala — the Restless One; tā heri — seeing that; rahiba cāñā — I shall keep gazing; narahari pahum̐ — Narahari's Lord; bhāsibena sukhe — will float in joy; nayane nayana diyā — eyes meeting eyes

**5.4.** The Restless One will not be able to meet my eyes — and I, seeing that, shall keep gazing." Narahari's Lord will float in joy as eyes meet eyes.

[^32-10]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — p. 223, no. 150 (scan PDF p. 482); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 150 (catalogue: NG-350). GCC — kirana 9, pada 12 (ed. 1947, pp. 112–113;
scan PDF pp. 117–118), "anyā ca — yathārāga" ("and another"). In GCC this pada comes after GCC 9.11 (= no. 153, no. 8 of this chapter); the compiler of GPT moved it.
"The Restless One" (cañcala, 5.4) refers to Gaura. The last line (signature) is the poet's word; it can also be read as continuing the townswoman's daydream ("…will
float in joy, His eyes meeting [mine]"). B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).

## 6. Narahari — "āi more bahu yatana karibe…" (GPT1 p. 224, no. 151; GCC 9.9)
*Nagari-bhava; a daydream. A townswoman dreams: Ai (Shachi) will be kind to her, but she will not stay by Ai — she will stand behind her friend and
gaze her fill at Gaura while remaining unseen; He will grow anxious and ask her friend with a sign of the eyes: "Where is your companion?"; the friend
will draw her forward and lift her veil; the Crown of connoisseurs of rasa will say with the corner of His eye: "Where did you learn these tricks? How
shall I live without seeing you?" — and Narahari will make peace between them. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC,
kirana 9, pada 9.*[^32-11]

আই মোরে বহু যতন করিবে, না রব আইয়ের কাছে ।
অতি অলখিত হইয়া দাঁড়াব আপন সইয়ের পাছে ॥

*āi more bahu yatana karibe, nā raba āiyera kāche |*
*ati alakhita haiyā dām̐ṛāba āpana saiyera pāche ||*

*Word for word:* āi — Ai (Shachi); more bahu yatana karibe — will be very kind to me; nā raba āiyera kāche — [but] I shall not stay by Ai; ati alakhita haiyā — quite unnoticed; dām̐ṛāba āpana saiyera pāche — I shall stand behind my friend

**6.1.** "Ai will be very kind to me — but I shall not stay by Ai: quite unnoticed, I shall stand behind my friend.

পরমানন্দিত হইয়া মিটাব অনেক দিনের ক্ষুধা ।
নয়ানচকোরে পান করাব সে বদনচাঁদের সুধা ॥

*paramānandita haiyā miṭāba aneka dinera kṣudhā |*
*nayānacakore pāna karāba se badanacām̐dera sudhā ||*

*Word for word:* paramānandita haiyā — supremely joyful; miṭāba aneka dinera kṣudhā — I shall still the hunger of many days; nayāna-cakore — to the chakora birds of my eyes; pāna karāba — I shall give to drink; se badanacām̐dera sudhā — the nectar of that moon of a face

**6.2.** Supremely joyful, I shall still the hunger of many days: I shall give the chakora birds of my eyes the nectar of that moon of a face to drink.

আমি ত দেখিব আঁখি ভরি তেঁহ মোরে না দেখিতে পাবে ।
আতুর হইয়া মোর সখী প্রতি নয়ান-ইঙ্গিতে কবে ॥

*āmi ta dekhiba ām̐khi bhari tem̐ha more nā dekhite pābe |*
*ātura haiyā mora sakhī prati nayāna-iṅgite kabe ||*

*Word for word:* āmi ta dekhiba ām̐khi bhari — I shall look my fill; tem̐ha more nā dekhite pābe — but He will not be able to see me; ātura haiyā — anxious; mora sakhī prati — to my friend; nayāna-iṅgite kabe — will say by a sign of the eyes

**6.3.** I shall look my fill, but He will not be able to see me; growing anxious, He will say to my friend by a sign of the eyes:

একাকিনী তুমি আইলে তোমার সঙ্গিনী রহিল কোথা ।
তুয়া দুইজনে একত্র না দেখি অন্তরে পাইনু ব্যথা ॥

*ekākinī tumi āile tomāra saṅginī rahila kothā |*
*tuyā duijane ekatra nā dekhi antare pāinu byathā ||*

*Word for word:* ekākinī tumi āile — you have come alone; tomāra saṅginī rahila kothā — where has your companion stayed; tuyā duijane — you two; ekatra nā dekhi — not seeing together; antare pāinu byathā — I am pained at heart

**6.4.** 'You have come alone — where has your companion stayed? Not seeing you two together, I am pained at heart.'

ইহা বুঝি সখী ধরি করে মোরে আপন সম্মুখে নিব ।
মিছা ক্রোধ করি ঈষৎ হাসিয়া আমি না আগেতে যাব ॥

*ihā bujhi sakhī dhari kare more āpana sammukhe niba |*
*michā krodha kari īṣat hāsiyā āmi nā āgete yāba ||*

*Word for word:* ihā bujhi — understanding this; sakhī dhari kare more — my friend, taking me by the hand; āpana sammukhe niba — will draw me in front of her; michā krodha kari — feigning anger; īṣat hāsiyā — smiling slightly; āmi nā āgete yāba — I shall not go forward

**6.5.** Understanding this, my friend will take me by the hand and draw me in front of her; feigning anger, smiling slightly, I shall not go forward.

তথাপি আমার সখী আপনার সম্মুখে রাখিবে ধরি ।
নিজ করে মোর ঘুঙট ঘুচাবে কত পরিহাস করি ॥

*tathāpi āmāra sakhī āpanāra sammukhe rākhibe dhari |*
*nija kare mora ghuṅaṭa ghucābe kata parihāsa kari ||*

*Word for word:* tathāpi — even so; āmāra sakhī — my friend; āpanāra sammukhe rākhibe dhari — will hold me in front of her; nija kare — with her own hand; mora ghuṅaṭa ghucābe — will lift my veil; kata parihāsa kari — teasing me no end

**6.6.** Even so my friend will hold me in front of her and with her own hand lift my veil, teasing me no end.

নয়ন-ইঙ্গিতে বঁধু প্রতি কবে দেখহ আপন জনে ।
আমা পানে চাঞা রসিকশেখর কহিবে নয়ানকোণে ॥

*nayana-iṅgite bam̐dhu prati kabe dekhaha āpana jane |*
*āmā pāne cāñā rasikaśekhara kahibe nayānakoṇe ||*

*Word for word:* nayana-iṅgite — by a sign of the eyes; bam̐dhu prati kabe — will say to the Friend; dekhaha āpana jane — look at Your own; āmā pāne cāñā — looking at me; rasikaśekhara — the Crown of connoisseurs of rasa; kahibe nayānakoṇe — will say with the corner of His eye

**6.7.** By a sign of the eyes she will say to the Friend: 'Look at Your own,' — and the Crown of connoisseurs of rasa, looking at me, will say with the corner of His eye:

ভাল ভাল ওহে এসব চাতুরি কোথাতে শিখিলে তুমি ।
বল বল দেখি তোমা না দেখিয়া কিরূপে বাঁচিব আমি ॥

*bhāla bhāla ohe esaba cāturi kothāte śikhile tumi |*
*bala bala dekhi tomā nā dekhiyā kirūpe bām̐ciba āmi ||*

*Word for word:* bhāla bhāla ohe — well, well, you; esaba cāturi — these tricks; kothāte śikhile tumi — where did you learn; bala bala dekhi — tell Me now; tomā nā dekhiyā — without seeing you; kirūpe bām̐ciba āmi — how shall I live

**6.8.** 'Well, well! Where did you learn these tricks? Tell Me now: how shall I live without seeing you?'

এইরূপ বহু জানাবে বুঝিয়া মানিব আপন দোষ ।
রসিকশেখর গোরা মোর প্রতি তথাপি করিব রোষ ॥

*eirūpa bahu jānābe bujhiyā māniba āpana doṣa |*
*rasikaśekhara gorā mora prati tathāpi kariba roṣa ||*

*Word for word:* eirūpa bahu jānābe — He will convey much like this; bujhiyā — understanding; māniba āpana doṣa — I shall own my fault; rasikaśekhara gorā — the Crown of connoisseurs of rasa, Gora; mora prati — with me; tathāpi kariba roṣa — will still be cross (the sense of the line is unclear)

**6.9.** He will convey much like this; understanding, I shall own my fault — and yet the Crown of connoisseurs of rasa, Gora, will still be cross with me.

নরহরি তাহে মানাব আনিয়া দেখাব গলার হার ।
ঈষৎ হাসিয়া কহেন এরূপ কভু না করিহ আর ॥

*narahari tāhe mānāba āniyā dekhāba galāra hāra |*
*īṣat hāsiyā kahena erūpa kabhu nā kariha āra ||*

*Word for word:* narahari tāhe mānāba — Narahari will then make it up; āniyā — bringing [me]; dekhāba galāra hāra — will show the necklace on the neck (whose is unclear); īṣat hāsiyā kahena — [He], smiling slightly, says; erūpa kabhu nā kariha āra — never do so again

**6.10.** Then Narahari will make it up: he will bring [me], show the necklace on the neck — and [He], smiling slightly, will say: 'Never do so again.'"[^32-12]

[^32-11]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — p. 224, no. 151 (scan PDF p. 483); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 151 (catalogue: NG-351). GCC — kirana 9, pada 9 (ed. 1947, pp. 110–111;
scan PDF pp. 115–116). In GCC the second line of couplet 6.6 is omitted: in its place the edition has a row of asterisks (a mark of omission); otherwise there are minor
differences ("parama ānanda haiyā", 6.2; "antare pāiye byathā", 6.4; "bandhu prati", 6.7). B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^32-12]: Ai ("mother") is Shachi-devi (cf. note 1); the townswoman dreams of being received kindly by Shachi. The silent conversation of the eyes (6.3–6.8) is what she
imagines (cf. note 5). 6.9–6.10 are understood conjecturally: who is "cross" and whose necklace Narahari will "show" (perhaps as a token of reconciliation) is not
clear from the text; GCC has "will make it up, yielding, will show the necklace on the neck" (mānāba māniyā dekhābe). The verb forms in -ba (niba, kariba) are used
here by the poet for the third person as well (the friend, Gora), for the sake of rhyme.

## 7. Narahari — "gaurāṅgacām̐dera pāne nirakhite…" (GPT1 pp. 224–225, no. 152; GCC 9.10)
*Nagari-bhava; a daydream. A townswoman dreams: gazing at Gaurangachand she will fall into a daze, be overcome, and her earring will roll on the
ground; she will hastily cover herself with her sari-end — and the jingle of her bangles will delight Him; with a glance He will ask: "Remove the cloth
— let Me see your hair"; her friend will tell her to turn away, and then herself throw the cloth off her head; Gora, enraptured, will gaze without
blinking, while she, abashed, will pull up her veil, scold her friend as "shameless" and step aside — to Gauranga's delight. Raga "yatharaga".
**Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 9, pada 10.*[^32-13]

গৌরাঙ্গচাঁদের পানে নিরখিতে পড়িব বিষম ভোলে ।
হইব অবশ খসিবে কুণ্ডল লোটাবে ধরণীতলে ॥

*gaurāṅgacām̐dera pāne nirakhite paṛiba biṣama bhole |*
*haiba abaśa khasibe kuṇḍala loṭābe dharaṇītale ||*

*Word for word:* gaurāṅgacām̐dera pāne nirakhite — gazing at Gaurangachand; paṛiba biṣama bhole — I shall fall into a deep daze; haiba abaśa — I shall be overcome; khasibe kuṇḍala — an earring will slip; loṭābe dharaṇītale — it will roll on the ground

**7.1.** "Gazing at Gaurangachand, I shall fall into a deep daze: I shall be overcome, an earring will slip and roll on the ground.

তুরিতে অঞ্চলে ঝাঁপিব তাহাতে হাতের চালনি হবে ।
ঝনঝন কর-কঙ্কণ-শবদ শুনি সে আনন্দ পাবে ॥

*turite añcale jhām̐piba tāhāte hātera cālani habe |*
*jhanajhana kara-kaṅkaṇa-śabada śuni se ānanda pābe ||*

*Word for word:* turite añcale jhām̐piba — I shall quickly cover myself with my sari-end; tāhāte — with that; hātera cālani habe — my hand will move; jhanajhana — jingling; kara-kaṅkaṇa-śabada — the sound of the bangles on my wrist; śuni — hearing; se ānanda pābe — He will be delighted

**7.2.** I shall quickly cover myself with my sari-end — with that my hand will move: hearing the jingle of the bangles on my wrist, He will be delighted.

তেরছ-নয়ানকোণেতে জানাব গৌরাঙ্গ ভুবনলোভা ।
বারেক বসন ঘুচাও নিরখি কিরূপ কেশের শোভা ॥

*teracha-nayānakoṇete jānāba gaurāṅga bhubanalobhā |*
*bāreka basana ghucāo nirakhi kirūpa keśera śobhā ||*

*Word for word:* terachha-nayānakoṇete — with the corner of a sidelong glance; jānāba — will convey; gaurāṅga bhubanalobhā — Gauranga, the allure of the world; bāreka basana ghucāo — remove the cloth for a moment; nirakhi — let Me see; kirūpa keśera śobhā — how beautiful the hair is

**7.3.** With the corner of a sidelong glance Gauranga, the allure of the world, will convey: 'Remove the cloth for a moment — let Me see how beautiful your hair is.'

ইহা বুঝি মুই ঈষৎ হাসিয়া ঘুঙটে ঢাকিব মুখ ।
লজ্জিত দেখিয়া সখী প্রতি পুনঃ জানাবে পাইয়া সুখ ॥

*ihā bujhi mui īṣat hāsiyā ghuṅaṭe ḍhākiba mukha |*
*lajjita dekhiyā sakhī prati punaḥ jānābe pāiyā sukha ||*

*Word for word:* ihā bujhi — understanding this; mui īṣat hāsiyā — I, smiling slightly; ghuṅaṭe ḍhākiba mukha — shall cover my face with my veil; lajjita dekhiyā — seeing me shy; sakhī prati punaḥ jānābe — He will again convey to my friend; pāiyā sukha — delighted

**7.4.** Understanding this, I shall smile slightly and cover my face with my veil; seeing me shy, He will be delighted and again convey something to my friend.

সখী সুচতুরা আমারে কহিবে দাঁড়াহ বিমুখ হৈয়া ।
নহিলে অধিক অথির হইবা গৌরাঙ্গ পানেতে চাঞা ॥

*sakhī sucaturā āmāre kahibe dām̐ṛāha bimukha haiyā |*
*nahile adhika athira haibā gaurāṅga pānete cāñā ||*

*Word for word:* sakhī sucaturā — my clever friend; āmāre kahibe — will say to me; dām̐ṛāha bimukha haiyā — stand turned away; nahile — otherwise; adhika athira haibā — you will lose all calm; gaurāṅga pānete cāñā — looking at Gauranga

**7.5.** My clever friend will say to me: 'Stand turned away — otherwise, looking at Gauranga, you will lose all calm.'

এতেক বচনে গোরাপানে পিছু করিয়া দাঁড়াব ভুলি ।
নিজকরে সখী শীঘ্র মোর শিরে বসন দিবেক ফেলি ॥

*eteka bacane gorāpāne pichu kariyā dām̐ṛāba bhuli |*
*nijakare sakhī śīghra mora śire basana dibeka pheli ||*

*Word for word:* eteka bacane — at these words; gorā-pāne pichu kariyā — turning my back to Gora; dām̐ṛāba bhuli — I shall stand, forgetting myself; nijakare — with her own hand; sakhī śīghra — my friend quickly; mora śire basana dibeka pheli — will throw off the cloth from my head

**7.6.** At these words I shall forget myself and stand with my back to Gora — and my friend with her own hand will quickly throw the cloth off my head.

সে সময়ে গোরা রসের আবেশে অধিক অবশ হৈয়া ।
কিছু না থাকিবে স্মৃতি অনিমিখ-নয়নে রহিব চাঞা ॥

*se samaye gorā rasera ābeśe adhika abaśa haiyā |*
*kichu nā thākibe smṛti animikha-nayane rahiba cāñā ||*

*Word for word:* se samaye — at that moment; gorā — Gora; rasera ābeśe — rapt in rasa; adhika abaśa haiyā — quite overcome; kichu nā thākibe smṛti — He will remember nothing; animikha-nayane — with unblinking eyes; rahiba cāñā — will keep gazing

**7.7.** At that moment Gora, rapt in rasa, quite overcome, will remember nothing — He will keep gazing with unblinking eyes.

মুই অতি সঙ্কোচে তরাতরি মাথে বসন দিব যে তুলি ।
বাহিরে কোরধ করিয়া সইয়েতে ভর্ৎসিব নিলজী বলি ॥

*mui ati saṅkoce tarātari māthe basana diba ye tuli |*
*bāhire koradha kariyā saiyete bhartsiba nilajī bali ||*

*Word for word:* mui ati saṅkoce — I, much abashed; tarātari — hastily; māthe basana diba ye tuli — shall pull the cloth up over my head; bāhire koradha kariyā — with outward anger; saiyete bhartsiba — I shall scold my friend; nilajī bali — calling her shameless

**7.8.** I, much abashed, shall hastily pull the cloth up over my head and, with outward anger, scold my friend, calling her shameless.

সখীর সমীপ হইতে কিঞ্চিত দূরেতে দাঁড়াব গিয়া ।
নিজ দোষ মানি টানিয়া রাখিবে মাথার শপথ দিয়া ॥

*sakhīra samīpa haite kiñcita dūrete dām̐ṛāba giyā |*
*nija doṣa māni ṭāniyā rākhibe māthāra śapatha diyā ||*

*Word for word:* sakhīra samīpa haite — from my friend's side; kiñcita dūrete — a little way off; dām̐ṛāba giyā — I shall go and stand; nija doṣa māni — owning her fault; ṭāniyā rākhibe — she will draw me back and hold me; māthāra śapatha diyā — swearing by my head

**7.9.** I shall go and stand a little way off from my friend — and she, owning her fault, will draw me back and hold me, swearing by my head.

আমার এ রঙ্গ হেরি পুনঃ রঙ্গে ভাসিবে গৌরাঙ্গ রঙ্গী ।
মনের মানসে হাসিবেক নরহরি বন্ধুয়ার সঙ্গী ॥

*āmāra e raṅga heri punaḥ raṅge bhāsibe gaurāṅga raṅgī |*
*manera mānase hāsibeka narahari bandhuyāra saṅgī ||*

*Word for word:* āmāra e raṅga heri — seeing this play of mine; punaḥ raṅge bhāsibe — will again float in merriment; gaurāṅga raṅgī — Gauranga, lover of play; manera mānase — in the depths of his heart; hāsibeka — will laugh; narahari bandhuyāra saṅgī — Narahari, the Friend's companion

**7.10.** Seeing this play of mine, Gauranga, lover of play, will again float in merriment," — and in the depths of his heart Narahari, the Friend's companion, will laugh.[^32-14]

[^32-13]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — pp. 224–225, no. 152 (scan PDF pp. 483–484); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 152 (catalogue: NG-121). GCC — kirana 9, pada 10 (ed. 1947,
pp. 111–112; scan PDF pp. 116–117). Two places in GPT1 are corrected after GCC (noted in VAR): 7.2 "jhām̐piba" ("I shall cover myself"; GPT1 "kām̐pila" — "trembled",
a misprint) and 7.6 "pichu kariyā" ("turning my back"; GPT1 "kichu kariyā"). B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^32-14]: Gora, enraptured and oblivious at the sight of the townswoman's uncovered head (7.7), is her daydream, as in all the padas of this cycle (note 5); rendered
exactly. A married woman's uncovered head before a strange man was by custom immodest; hence "shameless" (7.8) and the heroine's feigned indignation.

## 8. Narahari — "gaurāṅgacām̐dere nirakhi sakhīre…" (GPT1 p. 225, no. 153; GCC 9.11)
*Nagari-bhava; a daydream. A townswoman dreams: gazing at Gaurangachand and signalling to her friend, she will smile sweetly and talk with her;
swaying her head, she will loosen her hair-knot, her nose-pendant and earrings will swing; the nagara will say with a glance that He cannot see the
ornament on her back — and she, on some pretext, will lift the cloth and show it to Him; at once the Connoisseur of rasa will be overcome. Raga
"yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 9, pada 11.*[^32-15]

গৌরাঙ্গচাঁদেরে নিরখি সখীরে ঠারিয়া তেরছ-আঁখে ।
মধুর মধুর হাসিয়া মধুর-কাহিনী কহিব সুখে ॥

*gaurāṅgacām̐dere nirakhi sakhīre ṭhāriyā teracha-ām̐khe |*
*madhura madhura hāsiyā madhura-kāhinī kahiba sukhe ||*

*Word for word:* gaurāṅgacām̐dere nirakhi — gazing at Gaurangachand; sakhīre ṭhāriyā — signalling to my friend; terachha-ām̐khe — with a sidelong glance; madhura madhura hāsiyā — smiling sweetly, sweetly; madhura-kāhinī — sweet talk; kahiba sukhe — I shall happily tell

**8.1.** "Gazing at Gaurangachand, signalling to my friend with a sidelong glance, smiling sweetly, sweetly, I shall happily make sweet talk.

রসভরে শির চালন করিতে আউলাবে চুলের খোঁপা ।
মধুর মধুর দুলিবে নাসার বেশর কাণের চাঁপা ॥

*rasabhare śira cālana karite āulābe culera khom̐pā |*
*madhura madhura dulibe nāsāra beśara kāṇera cām̐pā ||*

*Word for word:* rasabhare — rapt in rasa; śira cālana karite — as I sway my head; āulābe culera khom̐pā — my hair-knot will come loose; madhura madhura dulibe — will sweetly swing; nāsāra beśara — the nose-pendant; kāṇera cām̐pā — the champaka ear-ornaments

**8.2.** Rapt in rasa, swaying my head, I shall loosen my hair-knot; sweetly, sweetly will swing my nose-pendant and my champaka ear-ornaments.

পিঠের উপর ঝাঁপার দোলনি তাহা না দেখিতে পাবে ।
নয়ানের কোণে ঠারিয়া নাগর ঈষৎ হাসিতে কবে ॥

*piṭhera upara jhām̐pāra dolani tāhā nā dekhite pābe |*
*nayānera koṇe ṭhāriyā nāgara īṣat hāsite kabe ||*

*Word for word:* piṭhera upara — on my back; jhām̐pāra dolani — the swinging of the jhapa (a braid-ornament); tāhā nā dekhite pābe — that He will not be able to see; nayānera koṇe ṭhāriyā — signalling with the corner of His eye; nāgara — the nagara; īṣat hāsite kabe — will say with a slight smile

**8.3.** The swinging of the jhapa on my back He will not be able to see — and the nagara, signalling with the corner of His eye, will say [so] with a slight smile.

কোন ছলে বাম-করেতে বসন তুলিয়া দেখাব তায় ।
অমনি অবশ হবে নরহরি-পরাণ রসিক রায় ॥

*kona chale bāma-karete basana tuliyā dekhāba tāya |*
*amani abaśa habe narahari-parāṇa rasika rāya ||*

*Word for word:* kona chale — on some pretext; bāma-karete — with my left hand; basana tuliyā — lifting the cloth; dekhāba tāya — I shall show it to Him; amani abaśa habe — at once will be overcome; narahari-parāṇa rasika rāya — the Connoisseur of rasa, the life of Narahari

**8.4.** On some pretext I shall lift the cloth with my left hand and show it to Him — at once the Connoisseur of rasa, the life of Narahari, will be overcome."[^32-16]

[^32-15]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — p. 225, no. 153 (scan PDF p. 484); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 153 (catalogue: NG-352). GCC — kirana 9, pada 11 (ed. 1947, p. 112;
scan PDF p. 117). GCC readings: "piṭhera upare" (8.3), "kona chalete" (8.4); 8.2 "kāṇera cām̐pā" follows GCC (in GPT1 the word is hard to read, GPT2 "ṭāpā"). B.
Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^32-16]: Beśara — a nose-pendant; cām̐pā — earrings shaped like the champaka flower; jhām̐pā — an ornament braided into the hair and hanging down the back. Lifting the
cloth to show it is a coquetry the townswoman pictures to herself (cf. note 5); rendered as in the original.

## 9. Narahari — "āiyera aṅgane yatane dām̐ṛāba…" (GPT1 pp. 225–226, no. 154; GCC 9.13)
*Nagari-bhava; a daydream. A townswoman dreams: in Ai's courtyard she will stand holding her friend's hand; Gora, the Jewel of virtues, will ask
her by a sign of the eyes to uncover her face; abashed, she will turn away, but her clever friend, with feigned alarm, will lift the cloth from her
face; the Connoisseur of rasa, covering His face, will smile — and Narahari Dasa, seeing that smile, will thrill. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution:
probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 9, pada 13.*[^32-17]

আইয়ের অঙ্গনে যতনে দাঁড়াব ধরিয়া সইয়ের করে ।
গোরা গুণমণি মো পানে চাহিয়া কহিবে আঁখির ঠারে ॥

*āiyera aṅgane yatane dām̐ṛāba dhariyā saiyera kare |*
*gorā guṇamaṇi mo pāne cāhiyā kahibe ām̐khira ṭhāre ||*

*Word for word:* āiyera aṅgane — in Ai's courtyard; yatane dām̐ṛāba — I shall carefully stand; dhariyā saiyera kare — holding my friend's hand; gorā guṇamaṇi — Gora, the Jewel of virtues; mo pāne cāhiyā — looking at me; kahibe ām̐khira ṭhāre — will say by a sign of the eyes

**9.1.** "In Ai's courtyard I shall carefully stand, holding my friend's hand; Gora, the Jewel of virtues, looking at me, will say by a sign of the eyes:

মুখের বসন বারেক ঘুচাঞা ঘুচাহ মনের দুখ ।
এ কথা বুঝিয়া লজ্জিত হইয়া অমনি ফিরাব মুখ ॥

*mukhera basana bāreka ghucāñā ghucāha manera dukha |*
*e kathā bujhiyā lajjita haiyā amani phirāba mukha ||*

*Word for word:* mukhera basana — the cloth over your face; bāreka ghucāñā — lifting just once; ghucāha manera dukha — dispel [My] heart's grief; e kathā bujhiyā — understanding this; lajjita haiyā — abashed; amani phirāba mukha — I shall at once turn my face away

**9.2.** 'Lift the cloth from your face just once — dispel My heart's grief.' Understanding this, I shall be abashed and at once turn my face away.

সখী মোর অতি চতুরা বুঝিয়া পসারি আপন কর ।
ইকি ইকি বলি মুখের বসন ঘুচাবে দেখাঞা ডর ॥

*sakhī mora ati caturā bujhiyā pasāri āpana kara |*
*iki iki bali mukhera basana ghucābe dekhāñā ḍara ||*

*Word for word:* sakhī mora ati caturā — my friend is very clever; bujhiyā — understanding; pasāri āpana kara — stretching out her hand; iki iki bali — crying "what's this, what's this"; mukhera basana ghucābe — will lift the cloth from my face; dekhāñā ḍara — making a show of alarm

**9.3.** My friend is very clever: understanding [Him], she will stretch out her hand and, crying 'What's this, what's this?', with a show of alarm will lift the cloth from my face.

ইহা দেখি মুখ বসনে ঝাঁপিয়া হাসিবে রসিকরায় ।
দাস নরহরি সে হাসি দেখিয়া হবে পুলকিত-কায় ॥

*ihā dekhi mukha basane jhām̐piyā hāsibe rasikarāya |*
*dāsa narahari se hāsi dekhiyā habe pulakita-kāya ||*

*Word for word:* ihā dekhi — seeing this; mukha basane jhām̐piyā — covering His face with His cloth; hāsibe rasikarāya — the Connoisseur of rasa will smile; dāsa narahari — Narahari Dasa; se hāsi dekhiyā — seeing that smile; habe pulakita-kāya — will thrill with gooseflesh

**9.4.** Seeing this, the Connoisseur of rasa, covering His face with His cloth, will smile" — and Narahari Dasa, seeing that smile, will thrill with gooseflesh.[^32-18]

[^32-17]: Signature — "Narahari Dasa" (dāsa narahari). GPT1 — pp. 225–226, no. 154 (scan PDF pp. 484–485); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 154 (catalogue: NG-122). GCC — kirana 9,
pada 13 (ed. 1947, p. 113; scan PDF p. 118), without a raga rubric. B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^32-18]: In GCC this pada is more explicit: in 9.2 and 9.3 the cloth is not over the face but over the breast, and the last line is different — "[He] will be
tormented by Madana; Narahari will calm Him"; the signature "Narahari Dasa" is only in GPT. The GPT text (the base text) is translated; the GCC readings are in
VAR. In GPT too this is a townswoman's daydream (cf. note 5): the Lord Himself did not look at women in Navadvipa (CB, Adi), and the tradition does not accept such
notions of Him (introductory note, chapter 27).

## 10. Narahari — "saiyera samīpe dām̐ṛāba nāgara…" (GPT1 p. 226, no. 155; GCC 9.14)
*Nagari-bhava; a daydream. A townswoman dreams: she will stand beside her friend, and the nagara will not look at her but only exchange smiling
signs with her friend; understanding nothing, she will ask: "What are you laughing at?" — "The fault is yours: the nagara wants to see your dear
face, and you are cross"; then she will speak by a sign and smile — and Gora will lose all composure. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably
Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 9, pada 14.*[^32-19]

সইয়ের সমীপে দাঁড়াব নাগর না চাবে আমার পানে ।
হাসিয়া হাসিয়া সুখে ঠারাঠারি করিবে সইয়ের সনে ॥

*saiyera samīpe dām̐ṛāba nāgara nā cābe āmāra pāne |*
*hāsiyā hāsiyā sukhe ṭhārāṭhāri karibe saiyera sane ||*

*Word for word:* saiyera samīpe dām̐ṛāba — I shall stand beside my friend; nāgara nā cābe āmāra pāne — the nagara will not look at me; hāsiyā hāsiyā — smiling and smiling; sukhe — happily; ṭhārāṭhāri karibe — He will exchange signs; saiyera sane — with my friend

**10.1.** "I shall stand beside my friend — and the nagara will not look at me: smiling and smiling, happily, He will exchange signs with my friend.

কিছু না বুঝিতে পারিয়া পুছিব ধরিয়া সইয়ের করে ।
কি দোষ আমার দেখিয়া তোমরা হাসহ পরসপরে ॥

*kichu nā bujhite pāriyā puchiba dhariyā saiyera kare |*
*ki doṣa āmāra dekhiyā tomarā hāsaha parasapare ||*

*Word for word:* kichu nā bujhite pāriyā — understanding nothing; puchiba dhariyā saiyera kare — I shall ask, taking my friend's hand; ki doṣa āmāra dekhiyā — seeing what fault of mine; tomarā hāsaha parasapare — do you laugh with each other

**10.2.** Understanding nothing, I shall take my friend's hand and ask: 'Seeing what fault of mine do you laugh with each other?'

এতেক শুনিয়া কহিবেন সখী আছয়ে তোমার দোষ ।
মুখানি দেখিতে চাহয়ে নাগর তাহাতে করহ রোষ ॥

*eteka śuniyā kahibena sakhī āchaye tomāra doṣa |*
*mukhāni dekhite cāhaye nāgara tāhāte karaha roṣa ||*

*Word for word:* eteka śuniyā — hearing this; kahibena sakhī — my friend will say; āchaye tomāra doṣa — the fault is yours; mukhāni dekhite cāhaye nāgara — the nagara wants to see your dear face; tāhāte karaha roṣa — and you are cross at that

**10.3.** Hearing this, my friend will say: 'The fault is yours: the nagara wants to see your dear face, and you are cross at that.'

ইহা শুনি কব সঙ্কেত করিয়া হাসিব অমিয় পারা ।
নরহরি থির করিতে নারিবে অধীর হইবে গোরা ॥

*ihā śuni kaba saṅketa kariyā hāsiba amiya pārā |*
*narahari thira karite nāribe adhīra haibe gorā ||*

*Word for word:* ihā śuni — hearing this; kaba saṅketa kariyā — I shall speak by a sign; hāsiba amiya pārā — I shall smile like nectar; narahari thira karite nāribe — Narahari will not be able to calm [Him]; adhīra haibe gorā — Gora will lose all composure

**10.4.** Hearing this, I shall speak [to Him] by a sign and smile like nectar," — Narahari will not be able to calm Him: Gora will lose all composure.

[^32-19]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — p. 226, no. 155 (scan PDF p. 485); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 155 (catalogue: NG-353). GCC — kirana 9, pada 14 (ed. 1947, p. 113; scan
PDF p. 118). In GCC 10.3 is more explicit: "the nagara wants to embrace [you]" (āliṅgana dite) instead of "wants to see your dear face"; the GPT text is translated
(cf. note 18). B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).

## 11. Narahari — "gaurāṅgacām̐dera hāsimākhā mukha…" (GPT1 p. 226, no. 156; GCC 9.15)
*Nagari-bhava; a daydream (reproach). A townswoman dreams: seeing Gaurangachand's smiling face, she will put her cloth round her neck, join her palms
and say to Him with a glance: "Why do You play false? Not once do You show Yourself on the road! The Creator made me a woman — hence the grief, or else
I would be with You"; He will be abashed and swear with the corner of His eye: "I will surely come." Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably
Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 9, pada 15.*[^32-20]

গৌরাঙ্গচাঁদের হাসিমাখা মুখ দেখিয়া রসের ভরে ।
গলায় বসন দিয়া করজোড়ি কহিব আঁখির ঠারে ॥

*gaurāṅgacām̐dera hāsimākhā mukha dekhiyā rasera bhare |*
*galāya basana diyā karajoṛi kahiba ām̐khira ṭhāre ||*

*Word for word:* gaurāṅgacām̐dera hāsimākhā mukha — Gaurangachand's smile-anointed face; dekhiyā — seeing; rasera bhare — rapt in rasa; galāya basana diyā — putting my cloth round my neck; karajoṛi — with joined palms; kahiba ām̐khira ṭhāre — I shall say by a sign of the eyes

**11.1.** "Seeing Gaurangachand's smile-anointed face, rapt in rasa, putting my cloth round my neck and joining my palms, I shall say by a sign of the eyes:

ভাল ভাল ওহে রসিকশেখর কি লাগি কপট কর ।
না জানিয়ে ইহা কোথায় শিখিলা এত বা ভাঁড়াতে পার ॥

*bhāla bhāla ohe rasikaśekhara ki lāgi kapaṭa kara |*
*nā jāniye ihā kothāya śikhilā eta bā bhām̐ṛāte pāra ||*

*Word for word:* bhāla bhāla ohe — well, well; rasikaśekhara — Crown of connoisseurs of rasa; ki lāgi kapaṭa kara — why do You play false; nā jāniye — I do not know; ihā kothāya śikhilā — where You learned this; eta vā bhām̐ṛāte pāra — that You can deceive so well

**11.2.** 'Well, well, Crown of connoisseurs of rasa, why do You play false? I do not know where You learned it — You can deceive so well!

আর কিবা হবে বারেক আসিয়া দেখাটি না দেহ পথে ।
বিধাতা করিলে নারী তেঁই দুখ নহিলে রহিতু সাথে ॥

*āra kibā habe bāreka āsiyā dekhāṭi nā deha pathe |*
*bidhātā karile nārī tem̐i dukha nahile rahitu sāthe ||*

*Word for word:* āra kibā habe — what more is there to say; bāreka āsiyā — coming just once; dekhāṭi nā deha pathe — You do not show Yourself on the road; bidhātā karila nārī — the Creator made [me] a woman; tem̐i dukha — hence the grief; nahile rahitu sāthe — otherwise I would stay with You

**11.3.** What more is there to say — not once do You come and show Yourself on the road. The Creator made me a woman — hence the grief; otherwise I would stay with You.'

এতেক শুনিয়া নরহরি-প্রাণবন্ধুয়া লজ্জিত হবে ।
অবশ্য যাইব বলিয়া নয়ন-কোণেতে শপথ খাবে ॥

*eteka śuniyā narahari-prāṇabandhuyā lajjita habe |*
*abaśya yāiba baliyā nayana-koṇete śapatha khābe ||*

*Word for word:* eteka śuniyā — hearing this; narahari-prāṇabandhuyā — the Friend of Narahari's life; lajjita habe — will be abashed; abaśya yāiba baliyā — saying "I will surely come"; nayana-koṇete śapatha khābe — will swear with the corner of His eye

**11.4.** Hearing this, the Friend of Narahari's life will be abashed and, saying 'I will surely come', will swear with the corner of His eye."[^32-21]

[^32-20]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — p. 226, no. 156 (scan PDF p. 485); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 156 (catalogue: NG-354). GCC — kirana 9, pada 15 (ed. 1947, p. 114; scan
PDF p. 119). GCC readings: "kara yuṛi" (11.1), "bhāla ohe", "śikhile" (11.2). B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^32-21]: A cloth put round the neck and joined palms are a sign of humble supplication. 11.3: "otherwise I would stay with You" — the townswoman envies the Lord's
companions, who are always with Him (in kirtana, on His walks through Nadia; CB, Madhya) — something a woman cannot have. Gaura's promise "I will come" is her
daydream (cf. note 5).

## 12. Narahari — "sakhīra samāje rahiyā bāreka…" (GPT1 pp. 226–227, no. 157; GCC 9.16)
*Nagari-bhava; a daydream (reproach). A townswoman dreams: standing among her friends, with a sorrowful face she will say to the nagara with the
corner of her eye: "You do not know the heart of love: You roam every street, I alone am left out; because of You the elders who loved me more than
life regard me as poison, and those I laughed at laugh at me; if You were gracious to me I would count this disgrace as nothing; but You are pitiless
— why this anger?" And He, joining His palms, will answer with a glance: "Perish My nature, I am full of faults — but I know one thing: you are dearer
to Me than life." Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 9, pada 16.*[^32-22]

সখীর সমাজে রহিয়া বারেক চাহিয়া ও মুখপানে ।
বিরস-বদন হইয়া নাগরে কহিব নয়ানকোণে ॥

*sakhīra samāje rahiyā bāreka cāhiyā o mukhapāne |*
*birasa-badana haiyā nāgare kahiba nayānakoṇe ||*

*Word for word:* sakhīra samāje rahiyā — staying among my friends; bāreka cāhiyā o mukhapāne — glancing once at that face; birasa-badana haiyā — with a sorrowful face; nāgare kahiba — I shall say to the nagara; nayānakoṇe — with the corner of my eye

**12.1.** "Staying among my friends, glancing once at that face, with a sorrowful face I shall say to the nagara with the corner of my eye:

ভাল ভাল ওহে পীরিতি-মরম কখন না জান তুমি ।
এ পাড়া সে পাড়া বেড়াইতে পার কেবল বঞ্চিত আমি ॥

*bhāla bhāla ohe pīriti-marama kakhana nā jāna tumi |*
*e pāṛā se pāṛā beṛāite pāra kebala bañcita āmi ||*

*Word for word:* bhāla bhāla ohe — well, well, You; pīriti-marama — the heart of love; kakhana nā jāna tumi — You have never known; e pāṛā se pāṛā — this quarter and that; beṛāite pāra — You can wander; kebala bañcita āmi — only I am left out

**12.2.** 'Well, well, You: the heart of love You have never known! This quarter and that You can wander — only I am left out.

তুমি ত রসিকশেখর সতত আনন্দে থাকহ ভোর ।
মুই অভাগিনী তোমার লাগিয়া কিবা না হৈয়াছে মোর ॥

*tumi ta rasikaśekhara satata ānande thākaha bhora |*
*mui abhāginī tomāra lāgiyā kibā nā haiyāche mora ||*

*Word for word:* tumi ta rasikaśekhara — You, the Crown of connoisseurs of rasa; satata ānande thākaha bhora — always stay lost in joy; mui abhāginī — I, unfortunate; tomāra lāgiyā — on Your account; kibā nā haiyāche mora — what has not befallen me

**12.3.** You, the Crown of connoisseurs of rasa, always stay lost in joy — while to me, unfortunate, what has not befallen me on Your account!

গুরুজন প্রাণ অধিক বাসিত তারা বিষসম বাসে ।
যারে দেখি হাসি করিতু এখন সে মোরে দেখিয়া হাসে ॥

*gurujana prāṇa adhika bāsita tārā biṣasama bāse |*
*yāre dekhi hāsi karitu ekhana se more dekhiyā hāse ||*

*Word for word:* gurujana — the elders; prāṇa adhika bāsita — loved [me] more than life; tārā biṣasama bāse — they now regard [me] as poison; yāre dekhi hāsi karitu — those I used to laugh at; ekhana se more dekhiyā hāse — now laugh when they see me

**12.4.** The elders who loved me more than life regard me as poison; those I used to laugh at now laugh when they see me.

ইহাতেও যদি আপন জানিয়া প্রসন্ন থাকিতা তুমি ।
তবে এসকল কলঙ্ক তৃণের অধিক গণিতু আমি ॥

*ihāteo yadi āpana jāniyā prasanna thākitā tumi |*
*tabe esakala kalaṅka tṛṇera adhika gaṇitu āmi ||*

*Word for word:* ihāteo — even so; yadi āpana jāniyā — if, knowing [me] as Your own; prasanna thākitā tumi — You were pleased with me; tabe — then; esakala kalaṅka — all this disgrace; tṛṇera adhika gaṇitu āmi — I would count as no more than a straw (lit. "would count more than grass"?)

**12.5.** If even so You knew me as Your own and were gracious to me, I would count all this disgrace as no more than a straw.

একে এ দিবস রজনী দারুণ জ্বালা না শরীরে সয় ।
আর তাহে তুমি নিদয় ইহাতে কিরূপে পরাণ রয় ॥

*eke e dibasa rajanī dāruṇa jvālā nā śarīre saya |*
*āra tāhe tumi nidaya ihāte kirūpe parāṇa raya ||*

*Word for word:* eke — as it is; e dibasa rajanī — day and night; dāruṇa jvālā — a cruel burning; nā śarīre saya — the body cannot bear; āra tāhe — and on top of that; tumi nidaya — You are pitiless; ihāte kirūpe parāṇa raya — how can life remain in this

**12.6.** As it is, day and night there is a cruel burning — the body cannot bear it; and on top of that You are pitiless — how can life remain?

তাহে মোর মন সন্দেহ ঘুচাও কি লাগি হৈয়াছে রোষ ।
এরূপ তোমার স্বভাব অথবা পাঞাছ কোন বা দোষ ॥

*tāhe mora mana sandeha ghucāo ki lāgi haiyāche roṣa |*
*erūpa tomāra svabhāba athabā pāñācha kona bā doṣa ||*

*Word for word:* tāhe — so; mora mana sandeha ghucāo — dispel my heart's doubt; ki lāgi haiyāche roṣa — why this anger; erūpa tomāra svabhāba — is this Your nature; athabā pāñācha kona vā doṣa — or have You found some fault [in me]

**12.7.** So dispel the doubt in my heart: why this anger? Is this Your nature — or have You found some fault in me?'

এতেক বুঝিয়া রসাবেশ হৈয়া চাহিয়া আমার পানে ।
অলখিত করযুগল যুড়িয়া কহিবে নয়নকোণে ॥

*eteka bujhiyā rasābeśa haiyā cāhiyā āmāra pāne |*
*alakhita karayugala yuṛiyā kahibe nayanakoṇe ||*

*Word for word:* eteka bujhiyā — understanding this; rasābeśa haiyā — rapt in rasa; cāhiyā āmāra pāne — looking at me; alakhita — unnoticed; karayugala yuṛiyā — joining His palms; kahibe nayanakoṇe — will say with the corner of His eye

**12.8.** Understanding this, He, rapt in rasa, looking at me, will unnoticed join His palms and say with the corner of His eye:

মরুক আমার স্বভাব সকল দোষেতে দূষিত আমি ।
অনুখন মনে জানিয়ে কেবল পরাণ অধিক তুমি ॥

*maruka āmāra svabhāba sakala doṣete dūṣita āmi |*
*anukhana mane jāniye kebala parāṇa adhika tumi ||*

*Word for word:* maruka āmāra svabhāba — perish My nature; sakala doṣete dūṣita āmi — I am stained with every fault; anukhana mane jāniye — ever in My heart I know; kebala — only this; parāṇa adhika tumi — you are dearer to Me than life

**12.9.** 'Perish My nature, I am stained with every fault; but ever in My heart I know one thing: you are dearer to Me than life.'

ইহা বুঝি মুই মুচকি হাসিয়া ঠারিব সইয়ের প্রতি ।
নরহরি-পিয়া হিয়া থির হবে দেখিয়া হরষ অতি ॥

*ihā bujhi mui mucaki hāsiyā ṭhāriba saiyera prati |*
*narahari-piyā hiyā thira habe dekhiyā haraṣa ati ||*

*Word for word:* ihā bujhi — understanding this; mui mucaki hāsiyā — I, with a faint smile; ṭhāriba saiyera prati — shall signal to my friend; narahari-piyā — the Beloved of Narahari; hiyā thira habe — will be calmed at heart; dekhiyā haraṣa ati — seeing [my] great joy

**12.10.** Understanding this, I shall smile faintly and signal to my friend" — and the heart of Narahari's Beloved will be calmed, seeing [her] great joy.[^32-23]

[^32-22]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — pp. 226–227, no. 157 (scan PDF pp. 485–486); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 157 (catalogue: NG-123). GCC — kirana 9, pada 16 (ed. 1947,
pp. 114–115; scan PDF pp. 119–120). 12.8 follows GCC and GPT2 "eteka bujhiyā" (GPT1 "eketa", a misprint). This is the last "wish" taken into GPT. In GCC the ninth kirana
continues with padas that are not in GPT (9.17–9.23): the townswomen come to Shachi's house and bow to her (9.18 — a Vrajabuli pada signed "Ghanashyama", another name
of Narahari Chakravarti); Shachi, the mother of the world, receives them as her own daughters-in-law and blesses them — "may your prosperity grow, may your husbands
and all your family live long" (9.21); the kirana ends with the poet's prayer for devotion to the feet of the nagaris of Nadia (9.23). B. Nagari-bhava — see the
introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^32-23]: The townswoman's reproaches (12.2–12.7) are motifs of the padas on Radha in separation and after a quarrel (kalahantarita); Gaura's answer (12.9) is what she
pictures to herself (cf. note 5); rendered exactly. 12.2: "You roam this quarter and that" — Nimai's walks through Nadia with His students and companions (CB, Adi
and Madhya). 12.5: "as no more than a straw" — by sense (lit. "would count more than a blade of grass"; the grass-blade is the usual image of the worthless).

## 13. Narahari — "śuna śuna ogo prāṇasama tumi…" (GPT1 p. 227, no. 158; GCC 10.10)
*Nagari-bhava (the heavenly women's talk). One says to her friend in her ear: "You judged rightly — the same came to my mind: today something is
strange with Him, I have never seen Him so overcome in the rapture of rasa; who has stolen Gaurangachand's heart? He is indeed a nagara — one can tell
by His doings, but I am ashamed to say it outright." Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 10, pada 10.*[^32-24]

শুন শুন ওগো প্রাণসম তুমি কহিয়ে তোমার কাণে ।
তুমি যে বিচার করিয়াছ তাহা হৈয়াছে আমার মনে ॥

*śuna śuna ogo prāṇasama tumi kahiye tomāra kāṇe |*
*tumi ye bicāra kariyācha tāhā haiyāche āmāra mane ||*

*Word for word:* śuna śuna ogo — listen, listen; prāṇasama tumi — you, dear to me as life; kahiye tomāra kāṇe — I tell you in your ear; tumi ye bicāra kariyācha — what you have judged; tāhā haiyāche āmāra mane — has come to my mind too

**13.1.** "Listen, listen, you who are dear to me as life — I tell you in your ear: what you have judged has come to my mind too.

কেমন কেমন লাগে আজু যেন দেখহ চতুর তুমি ।
রসের আবেশে অবশ এমন কভু না দেখিয়ে আমি ॥

*kemana kemana lāge āju yena dekhaha catura tumi |*
*rasera ābeśe abaśa emana kabhu nā dekhiye āmi ||*

*Word for word:* kemana kemana lāge āju — today something seems strange; yena dekhaha — as you see; catura tumi — you, shrewd one; rasera ābeśe abaśa — overcome in the rapture of rasa; emana kabhu nā dekhiye āmi — I have never seen [Him] so

**13.2.** Today something is strange — you see it yourself, shrewd one: I have never seen Him so overcome in the rapture of rasa.

যদি কোন দিন দেখিয়ে তথাপি কিছু না লখিতে পারি ।
বল বল দেখি গৌরাঙ্গচাঁদের মন কে করিল চুরি ॥

*yadi kona dina dekhiye tathāpi kichu nā lakhite pāri |*
*bala bala dekhi gaurāṅgacām̐dera mana ke karila curi ||*

*Word for word:* yadi kona dina dekhiye — even if I saw it some day; tathāpi kichu nā lakhite pāri — still I could make nothing out; bala bala dekhi — tell me now; gaurāṅgacām̐dera mana — Gaurangachand's heart; ke karila curi — who has stolen

**13.3.** And even if I saw it some day, still I could make nothing out. Tell me now: who has stolen Gaurangachand's heart?

নরহরি-চাঁদ নাগর বটেন বুঝিতে পারিএ কাজে ।
তবু দড় করি কার কাছে ইহা কহিতে নারিএ লাজে ॥

*narahari-cām̐da nāgara baṭena bujhite pārie kāje |*
*tabu daṛa kari kāra kāche ihā kahite nārie lāje ||*

*Word for word:* narahari-cām̐da — Narahari's moon; nāgara baṭena — is indeed a nagara; bujhite pārie kāje — I can tell by His doings; tabu — yet; daṛa kari — firmly; kāra kāche ihā — to anyone this; kahite nārie lāje — I cannot say for shame

**13.4.** Narahari's moon is indeed a nagara — I can tell by His doings; and yet for shame I cannot say it outright to anyone."[^32-25]

[^32-24]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — p. 227, no. 158 (scan PDF p. 486); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 158 (catalogue: NG-124). GCC — kirana 10, pada 10 (ed. 1947, pp. 121–122;
scan PDF pp. 126–127). **Who is speaking.** The tenth kirana of GCC is headed "Again in the morning — the various amusements of the heavenly women (debaramaṇī), eager
for the rasa of His darshan": the wives of the gods look down from the sky on Nadia and on Gaura (10.1–10.2), praise the nagaris of Nadia and lament that they live not
in Nadia but in the city of the gods (10.3–10.9); GCC 10.10–10.24 (GPT nos. 158–168, nos. 13–23 of this chapter) are their conversation and dispute about Gaura. In
GPT these padas stand without the introduction and read as a conversation of townswomen; that the speakers are celestials can be seen in the GPT text itself: "you,
connoisseurs of rasa in the city of the gods" (17.3), "in the city of the gods a false rumour has arisen" (20.1). Section 3.2 of GPT omits GCC 10.1–10.9 (of these, 10.7–10.9 stand in other sections of GPT — p. 494, no. 30 and sect. 3.1, nos. 129–130; see chapter 33), 10.11 (one woman's explicit
guess as to where Gaura spent the night), 10.18, 10.20 and 10.23 (short links). B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^32-25]: Gaura "overcome in the rapture of rasa" in the morning is how the celestial women interpret His state (GCC 10.9 describes His morning appearance: tousled curls,
garland); for Krishnadasa Kaviraja and Vrindavana Dasa the Lord's rapture is prema for Krishna in the bhava of Radha (CC, Adi 4; CB, Madhya), not a nagara's love. The
heroines' guesses are rendered as in the original; their "He is indeed a nagara" is the very notion the tradition does not accept (introductory note, chapter 27).

## 14. Narahari — "ki baliba ogo anubhabi bhāla…" (GPT1 pp. 227–228, no. 159; GCC 10.12)
*Nagari-bhava (the heavenly women's talk). Another answers: "You judged rightly: I know all His play as a nagara, only I am shy to tell it — it is
laughable to watch how He behaves: He thinks Himself the king of the clever, imagines that everything of His is secret — His descent, His gait, His
dance, His love with the nagaris of Nadia — and covers the sun's rays with His hand. Before one who is cleverer than the clever no cleverness holds —
whom then does He fear?" Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 10, pada 12.*[^32-26]

কি বলিব ওগো অনুভবি ভাল নিশ্চয় করিলা তুমি ।
গৌরাঙ্গচাঁদের নাগরালি যত সকলি জানিএ আমি ॥

*ki baliba ogo anubhabi bhāla niścaya karilā tumi |*
*gaurāṅgacām̐dera nāgarāli yata sakali jānie āmi ||*

*Word for word:* ki baliba ogo — what shall I say; anubhabi — perceiving; bhāla niścaya karilā tumi — you judged rightly; gaurāṅgacām̐dera nāgarāli yata — all Gaurangachand's ways as a nagara; sakali jānie āmi — I know them all

**14.1.** "What shall I say? You judged rightly: all Gaurangachand's ways as a nagara I know.

তোমা সবা পাশে সেসব কাহিনী কহিতে সঙ্কোচ বাসি ।
তাহে গৌরাঙ্গের চরিত হেরিয়া অন্তরে উপজে হাসি ॥

*tomā sabā pāśe sesaba kāhinī kahite saṅkoca bāsi |*
*tāhe gaurāṅgera carita heriyā antare upaje hāsi ||*

*Word for word:* tomā sabā pāśe — before you all; sesaba kāhinī kahite — to tell those tales; saṅkoca bāsi — I feel shy; tāhe — and yet; gaurāṅgera carita heriyā — seeing Gauranga's conduct; antare upaje hāsi — laughter rises within me

**14.2.** Before you all I am shy to tell those tales — and yet, watching Gauranga's conduct, laughter rises within me.

ইহোঁ আপনাকে সতত বাসয়ে আমি সে চতুররাজ ।
গুপত আমার অবতার আর গুপত সকল কাজ ॥

*ihom̐ āpanāke satata bāsaye āmi se caturarāja |*
*gupata āmāra abatāra āra gupata sakala kāja ||*

*Word for word:* ihom̐ — He; āpanāke satata bāsaye — always thinks of Himself; āmi se caturarāja — "I am the king of the clever"; gupata āmāra abatāra — "secret is My descent"; āra gupata sakala kāja — "and secret all My deeds"

**14.3.** He always thinks of Himself: 'I am the king of the clever: secret is My descent, and secret all My deeds;

গুপত চলন বোলন গুপত গুপত নটন ভঙ্গ ।
গুপত নদীয়ানাগরীর সনে গুপত পীরিতি রঙ্গ ॥

*gupata calana bolana gupata gupata naṭana bhaṅga |*
*gupata nadīyānāgarīra sane gupata pīriti raṅga ||*

*Word for word:* gupata calana — secret the gait; bolana gupata — secret the speech; gupata naṭana bhaṅga — secret the poses of the dance; gupata nadīyānāgarīra sane — secret with the nagaris of Nadia; gupata pīriti raṅga — secret the play of love

**14.4.** secret the gait, secret the speech, secret the poses of the dance; in secret with the nagaris of Nadia — secret the play of love.

গুপত করিয়া নাগরালি ইহা কেহ না লখিতে পারে ।
এইরূপ বহু মনে দিনকর-কিরণ ঝাঁপয়ে করে ॥

*gupata kariyā nāgarāli ihā keha nā lakhite pāre |*
*eirūpa bahu mane dinakara-kiraṇa jhām̐paye kare ||*

*Word for word:* gupata kariyā nāgarāli — playing the nagara in secret; ihā keha nā lakhite pāre — no one can perceive it; eirūpa bahu mane — thinking much like this; dinakara-kiraṇa — the sun's rays; jhām̐paye kare — He covers with His hand

**14.5.** I play the nagara in secret — no one can perceive it,' — thinking much like this, He covers the sun's rays with His hand.

চতুর উপরে চতুর যে জন তাহে কি চাতুরি রয় ।
ইহা না বুঝিয়া নরহরি-পহুঁ কাহারে করয় ভয় ॥

*catura upare catura ye jana tāhe ki cāturi raya |*
*ihā nā bujhiyā narahari-pahum̐ kāhāre karaya bhaya ||*

*Word for word:* catura upare catura ye jana — one who is cleverer than the clever; tāhe ki cāturi raya — before such a one what cleverness remains; ihā nā bujhiyā — not understanding this; narahari-pahum̐ — Narahari's Lord; kāhāre karaya bhaya — whom does He fear

**14.6.** Before one who is cleverer than the clever, what cleverness remains? Not understanding this, Narahari's Lord — whom does He fear?"[^32-27]
