pp. 122–123; scan PDF pp. 127–128). Between GPT nos. 158 and 159 GCC has pada 10.11, not taken into GPT (note 24). 14.2 "before you all" follows GPT2 and GCC "pāśe"
(GPT1 reads "pāche"). B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^32-27]: "Secret is My descent" (14.3) — in the tradition Gaura is indeed a "hidden" avatara: in the Kali age the Lord comes concealing His divinity (*Bhag.* 7.9.38:
*channaḥ kalau*; CC, Madhya 6), and conceals it in order to taste Radha's prema (CC, Adi 4). The heroine, however, transfers this "secret" to a love for the nagaris of
Nadia; that is the notion of gaura-nagari, which the tradition does not accept (introductory note, chapter 27); rendered as in the original. "Covers the sun's rays with
His hand" (14.5) is a proverb for the vain concealment of the obvious.

## 15. Narahari — "gaurāṅgacām̐dera eirūpa saba…" (GPT1 p. 228, no. 160; GCC 10.13)
*Nagari-bhava (the heavenly women's talk). A third defends secrecy: "Do not grieve: with Gaurangachand all is so; in the open there is sorrow, in
secret greater joy; even people who get a little wealth hide it more carefully than life; love is the supreme jewel and must be hidden, and a
connoisseur of rasa is ashamed if it becomes known; Narahari's Lord is the crown of the adroit, and so He sports in secret." Raga "yatharaga".
**Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 10, pada 13.*[^32-28]

গৌরাঙ্গচাঁদের এইরূপ সব ইথে না বাসিহ দুখ ।
বেকত বিষয়ে বিষাদ ঘটয়ে গুপতে অধিক সুখ ॥

*gaurāṅgacām̐dera eirūpa saba ithe nā bāsiha dukha |*
*bekata biṣaye biṣāda ghaṭaye gupate adhika sukha ||*

*Word for word:* gaurāṅgacām̐dera eirūpa saba — with Gaurangachand all is so; ithe nā bāsiha dukha — do not grieve at this; bekata biṣaye — in what is open; biṣāda ghaṭaye — sorrow arises; gupate adhika sukha — in secret there is greater joy

**15.1.** "With Gaurangachand all is so — do not grieve at this: in what is open sorrow arises, in secret there is greater joy.

পরাণ অধিক গুপত করয়ে পাইয়া অলপ ধনে ।
যদি বল ইহা অসম্ভব তাতে দেখহ জগত-জনে ॥

*parāṇa adhika gupata karaye pāiyā alapa dhane |*
*yadi bala ihā asambhaba tāte dekhaha jagata-jane ||*

*Word for word:* parāṇa adhika — more than life; gupata karaye — they hide; pāiyā alapa dhane — on getting a little wealth; yadi bala ihā asambhaba — if you say this is impossible; tāte dekhaha jagata-jane — look at the people of the world

**15.2.** On getting even a little wealth, people hide it more carefully than life; if you say this is impossible — look at the people of the world.

পীরিতি পরম রতন ইহারে গুপত করিলে কাজ ।
বেকত হইলে রসিক জনার অন্তরে উপজে লাজ ॥

*pīriti parama ratana ihāre gupata karile kāja |*
*bekata haile rasika janāra antare upaje lāja ||*

*Word for word:* pīriti parama ratana — love is the supreme jewel; ihāre gupata karile kāja — it must be kept hidden; bekata haile — if it becomes known; rasika janāra — in a connoisseur of rasa; antare upaje lāja — shame arises in the heart

**15.3.** Love is the supreme jewel: it must be kept hidden; if it becomes known, shame arises in the heart of a connoisseur of rasa.

নরহরি-পহুঁ সুঘড়শেখর জানে কি এমন জনা ।
গুপত-বিহার করে অবিরত জানায় সুঘড়পনা ॥

*narahari-pahum̐ sughaṛaśekhara jāne ki emana janā |*
*gupata-bihāra kare abirata jānāya sughaṛapanā ||*

*Word for word:* narahari-pahum̐ — Narahari's Lord; sughaṛaśekhara — the crown of the adroit; jāne ki emana janā — does anyone know such a one; gupata-bihāra kare abirata — He sports in secret unceasingly; jānāya sughaṛapanā — showing His adroitness

**15.4.** Narahari's Lord is the crown of the adroit: does anyone know His like? Unceasingly He sports in secret, showing His adroitness."

[^32-28]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — p. 228, no. 160 (scan PDF p. 487); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 160 (catalogue: NG-355). GCC — kirana 10, pada 13 (ed. 1947, p. 123; scan
PDF p. 128), "anyā ca — yathārāga". The argument that love must be hidden is a commonplace of the poetics of rasa (cf. the answer in no. 16: "love never stays hidden");
on Gaura's "secret play" see note 27. B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).

## 16. Narahari — "ye bala se bala pīriti gupata…" (GPT1 p. 228, no. 161; GCC 10.14)
*Nagari-bhava (the heavenly women's talk). Yet another objects: "Love never stays hidden — its nature is to be seen; He behaves like the sun. Gora,
Shachi's darling, is the thief of the composure of all the young wives of good family in Nadia: whoever wants to keep her dharma He enchants with a
glance; night and day He sports with the young nagaris and pines for them." Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana
10, pada 14.*[^32-29]

যে বল সে বল পীরিতি গুপত করিতে অধিক ভার ।
পীরিতি গুপত না থাকে কখন বেকত স্বভাব তার ॥

*ye bala se bala pīriti gupata karite adhika bhāra |*
*pīriti gupata nā thāke kakhana bekata svabhāba tāra ||*

*Word for word:* ye bala se bala — say what you will; pīriti gupata karite adhika bhāra — to hide love is a heavy burden; pīriti gupata nā thāke kakhana — love never stays hidden; bekata svabhāba tāra — its nature is to be seen

**16.1.** "Say what you will: to hide love is a heavy burden; love never stays hidden — its nature is to be seen.

দিনকর সম করে আচরণ ইহা কি গুপত মানি ।
গুপত গুপত তোমরা জানহ আমি ত বেকত জানি ॥

*dinakara sama kare ācaraṇa ihā ki gupata māni |*
*gupata gupata tomarā jānaha āmi ta bekata jāni ||*

*Word for word:* dinakara sama — like the sun; kare ācaraṇa — He behaves; ihā ki gupata māni — can I take this as secret; gupata gupata tomarā jānaha — you think it secret; āmi ta bekata jāni — but I know it is open

**16.2.** He behaves like the sun — can I take that as secret? You think it secret, but I know it is open.

নদীয়ানগরে রসিকশেখর শচীর দুলাল গোরা ।
যত কুলবতী যুবতী সবার ধৈরজ-রতন-চোরা ॥

*nadīyānagare rasikaśekhara śacīra dulāla gorā |*
*yata kulabatī yubatī sabāra dhairaja-ratana-corā ||*

*Word for word:* nadīyānagare — in the town of Nadia; rasikaśekhara — the Crown of connoisseurs of rasa; śacīra dulāla gorā — Gora, Shachi's darling; yata kulabatī yubatī sabāra — of all the young wives of good family; dhairaja-ratana-corā — the thief of the jewel of composure

**16.3.** In the town of Nadia the Crown of connoisseurs of rasa, Gora, Shachi's darling, is the thief of the jewel of composure of all the young wives of good family.

জগতের মাঝে দেখিনু এমন নাগর কোথাও নাই ।
নিশ্চয় জানিহ কেহ এড়াইতে না রহে ইহার ঠাঁই ॥

*jagatera mājhe dekhinu emana nāgara kothāo nāi |*
*niścaya jāniha keha eṛāite nā rahe ihāra ṭhām̐i ||*

*Word for word:* jagatera mājhe — in all the world; dekhinu — I have seen; emana nāgara kothāo nāi — there is no such nagara anywhere; niścaya jāniha — know for certain; keha eṛāite nā rahe — no one remains safe; ihāra ṭhām̐i — from Him

**16.4.** In all the world, as far as I have seen, there is no such nagara anywhere; know for certain: no one remains safe from Him.

যদি কোন ধনী ধৈরজ ধরিয়া ধরম রাখিতে চায় ।
বিষম নয়ান কোণে নিরখিয়া মোহিত করয় তায় ॥

*yadi kona dhanī dhairaja dhariyā dharama rākhite cāya |*
*biṣama nayāna koṇe nirakhiyā mohita karaya tāya ||*

*Word for word:* yadi kona dhanī — if some fair one; dhairaja dhariyā — holding to her composure; dharama rākhite cāya — wants to keep her dharma; biṣama nayāna koṇe nirakhiyā — glancing with the sly corner of His eye; mohita karaya tāya — He enchants her

**16.5.** If some fair one, holding to her composure, wants to keep her dharma, — He, glancing with the sly corner of His eye, enchants her.

নিশিদিন নবনাগরী সহিত অশেষ বিলাস করে ।
নরহরি-নাথ নাগরী-বল্লভ নাগরী লাগিয়া ঝুরে ॥

*niśidina nabanāgarī sahita aśeṣa bilāsa kare |*
*narahari-nātha nāgarī-ballabha nāgarī lāgiyā jhure ||*

*Word for word:* niśidina — night and day; nabanāgarī sahita — with the young nagaris; aśeṣa bilāsa kare — He sports without end; narahari-nātha — Narahari's Lord; nāgarī-ballabha — the beloved of the nagaris; nāgarī lāgiyā jhure — pines for the nagaris

**16.6.** Night and day He sports without end with the young nagaris; Narahari's Lord, the beloved of the nagaris, pines for the nagaris."[^32-30]

[^32-29]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — p. 228, no. 161 (scan PDF p. 487); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 161 (catalogue: NG-356). GCC — kirana 10, pada 14 (ed. 1947, pp. 123–124;
scan PDF pp. 128–129), "anyā ca — yathārāga". B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^32-30]: 16.5–16.6: "He enchants her who wants to keep her dharma", "night and day He sports with the young nagaris" — this is the notion of gaura-nagari in its direct form;
rendered exactly, without softening. The Gaudiya tradition rejects it: according to Vrindavana Dasa, in this avatara the Lord did not look at women and allowed no jesting
with them (CB, Adi), and Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati counts "gaura-nagari" among the apasampradayas (introductory note, chapter 27). In Narahari Chakravarti's own work
these words are at once answered by other heroines, who describe the Lord's strictness (nos. 19–20 of this chapter).

## 17. Narahari — "śuna śuna ogo niścaya balie…" (GPT1 pp. 228–229, no. 162; GCC 10.15)
*Nagari-bhava (the heavenly women's talk). The next says: "We are quite simple: we cannot understand the play of a nagara that Gora performs in
Nadia; we know Him only by His outward nobility, and what is within Him cannot be known; blessed are you, connoisseurs of rasa in the city of the gods —
who but you could understand it? At last the darkness has lifted: Narahari's Lord has appeared in the world subject to young women." Raga
"yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 10, pada 15.*[^32-31]

শুন শুন ওগো নিশ্চয় বলিএ অধিক অবোধ মোরা ।
বুঝিতে নারিএ হেন নাগরালি নদ্যাতে করয়ে গোরা ॥

*śuna śuna ogo niścaya balie adhika abodha morā |*
*bujhite nārie hena nāgarāli nadyāte karaye gorā ||*

*Word for word:* śuna śuna ogo — listen, listen; niścaya balie — I say for certain; adhika abodha morā — we are quite simple; bujhite nārie — we cannot understand; hena nāgarāli — such play of a nagara; nadyāte karaye gorā — Gora performs in Nadia

**17.1.** "Listen, listen: I say for certain — we are quite simple: we cannot understand such play of a nagara as Gora performs in Nadia.

বাহিরে যেরূপ দেখিএ ইহার পরম উদারপনা ।
সেইরূপ মোরা জানিএ অন্তরে কি আছে না যায় জানা ॥

*bāhire yerūpa dekhie ihāra parama udārapanā |*
*seirūpa morā jānie antare ki āche nā yāya jānā ||*

*Word for word:* bāhire yerūpa dekhie — as we see outwardly; ihāra parama udārapanā — His supreme nobility; seirūpa morā jānie — so we know Him; antare ki āche — what is within; nā yāya jānā — cannot be known

**17.2.** As we see His supreme nobility outwardly, so we know Him; what is within cannot be known.

ধন্য ধন্য যেন তোমরা পরম রসিকিনী সুরপুরে ।
এ সব বিহার তোমা সবা বিনা আনে কি বুঝিতে পারে ॥

*dhanya dhanya yena tomarā parama rasikinī surapure |*
*e saba bihāra tomā sabā binā āne ki bujhite pāre ||*

*Word for word:* dhanya dhanya — blessed, blessed; yena tomarā — you indeed; parama rasikinī — the foremost connoisseurs of rasa; surapure — in the city of the gods; e saba bihāra — these sports; tomā sabā binā — but for you; āne ki bujhite pāre — can others understand

**17.3.** Blessed indeed are you, the foremost connoisseurs of rasa in the city of the gods: who but you can understand these sports?

যে হৌক সে হৌক এত দিনে যেন মনের আঁধার গেল ।
নরহরি-পহুঁ যুবতী-অধীন জগতে প্রকট হৈল ॥

*ye hauka se hauka eta dine yena manera ām̐dhāra gela |*
*narahari-pahum̐ yubatī-adhīna jagate prakaṭa haila ||*

*Word for word:* ye hauka se hauka — be that as it may; eta dine — at last; yena manera ām̐dhāra gela — as if the darkness of the mind has gone; narahari-pahum̐ — Narahari's Lord; yubatī-adhīna — subject to young women; jagate prakaṭa haila — has appeared in the world

**17.4.** Be that as it may, at last the darkness of my mind seems to have gone: Narahari's Lord has appeared in the world subject to young women."[^32-32]

[^32-31]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — pp. 228–229, no. 162 (scan PDF pp. 487–488); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 162 (catalogue: NG-357). GCC — kirana 10, pada 15 (ed. 1947,
p. 124; scan PDF p. 129). The GPT1 OCR of 17.1 is garbled; the text follows the GPT1 scan, GPT2 and GCC. B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section
(chapter 27).
[^32-32]: The tone of the pada seems mocking: the speaker appears to agree with the "connoisseurs of rasa in the city of the gods" (17.3 — a direct indication that the
disputants are celestials, note 24), but her "subject to young women" (yubatī-adhīna, 17.4) sounds like a challenge. "Subject to His devotees" is the Lord's word about Himself
(*Bhag.* 9.4.63), and of the gopis — 10.32.22; the transfer of this to Gaura as a nagara the tradition does not accept (introductory note, chapter 27). Rendered as in the original.

## 18. Narahari — "gorācām̐dera nāgarāli yata…" (GPT1 p. 229, no. 163; GCC 10.16)
*A link (short payar). All speak in many ways of Gorachand's play as a nagara, as if nectar were flowing; hearing this, a woman of another group comes
and boldly addresses them all. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 10, pada 16.*[^32-33]

গোরাচাঁদের নাগরালি যত । কহয়ে সকলে কত কত মত ॥

*gorācām̐dera nāgarāli yata | kahaye sakale kata kata mata ||*

*Word for word:* gorācām̐dera nāgarāli yata — of all Gorachand's play as a nagara; kahaye sakale — all of them speak; kata kata mata — in so many ways

**18.1.** Of all Gorachand's play as a nagara they all speak — in so many ways.

যেন বরিষয়ে অমিয়ার ধার । না জানি কি সুখ অন্তরে সবার ॥

*yena bariṣaye amiyāra dhāra | nā jāni ki sukha antare sabāra ||*

*Word for word:* yena bariṣaye — as if raining down; amiyāra dhāra — a stream of nectar; nā jāni — I do not know; ki sukha antare sabāra — what joy is in all their hearts

**18.2.** As if a stream of nectar were raining down: I do not know what joy is in all their hearts.

আর এক নব যূথের রমণী । আইলেন তথা শুনিয়া এ বাণী ॥

*āra eka naba yūthera ramaṇī | āilena tathā śuniyā e bāṇī ||*

*Word for word:* āra eka — another; naba yūthera ramaṇī — woman of a new group; āilena tathā — came there; śuniyā e bāṇī — hearing these words

**18.3.** Another — a woman of a new group — came there, hearing these words.

নরহরি তার রীতি না জানয়ে । এ সবার প্রতি সাহসে ভণয়ে ॥

*narahari tāra rīti nā jānaye | e sabāra prati sāhase bhaṇaye ||*

*Word for word:* narahari tāra rīti nā jānaye — Narahari does not know her ways; e sabāra prati — to all of them; sāhase bhaṇaye — she boldly speaks

**18.4.** Narahari does not know her ways: she boldly speaks to them all.

[^32-33]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — p. 229, no. 163 (scan PDF p. 488); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 163 (catalogue: NG-126). GCC — kirana 10, pada 16 (ed. 1947, p. 124; scan PDF
p. 129). Short payar: a couplet is one line. The newcomer's speech is the next pada (no. 19). B. The pada stands in the GPT section of nagari padas — see the introductory
note to the section (chapter 27).

## 19. Narahari — "ki baliba ogo tomādera prati…" (GPT1 p. 229, no. 164; GCC 10.17)
*An answer: praise of the Lord's strictness (by content — not nagari-bhava). The newcomer says: "I am bewildered: why do you revile the Moon of Nadia?
He is the lamp of Jagannatha Mishra's family, the conqueror of the digvijayi, the pandits of Nadia submit to Him, He is ever on the path of dharma; He does
not listen to talk of women and never, even by mistake, looks at the faces of others' wives; if, while bathing in the Ganga, a woman's cloth touches Him,
He at once performs expiation and still cannot regain His peace. To slander Him wilfully is an aparadha; Narahari is witness: never say such things."
Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 10, pada 17.*[^32-34]

কি বলিব ওগো তোমাদের প্রতি মুই সে পড়িনু ধন্দে ।
কি লাগিয়া এত নিন্দহ এমন সুজন নদ্যার চান্দে ॥

*ki baliba ogo tomādera prati mui se paṛinu dhande |*
*ki lāgiyā eta nindaha emana sujana nadyāra cānde ||*

*Word for word:* ki baliba ogo — what shall I say; tomādera prati — to you; mui se paṛinu dhande — I am quite bewildered; ki lāgiyā eta nindaha — why do you revile so; emana sujana — so good a person; nadyāra cānde — the Moon of Nadia

**19.1.** "What shall I say to you? I am quite bewildered: why do you so revile so good a person — the Moon of Nadia?

পরম পণ্ডিত জগন্নাথ মিশ্র কেবা না জানয়ে তায় ।
তাঁর নিরমল কুলের প্রদীপ জগতে যাহারে গায় ॥

*parama paṇḍita jagannātha miśra kebā nā jānaye tāya |*
*tām̐ra niramala kulera pradīpa jagate yāhāre gāya ||*

*Word for word:* parama paṇḍita — a great scholar; jagannātha miśra — Jagannatha Mishra; kebā nā jānaye tāya — who does not know him; tām̐ra niramala kulera pradīpa — the lamp of his pure family; jagate yāhāre gāya — whom the world extols

**19.2.** Who does not know the great scholar Jagannatha Mishra? The world extols Him as the lamp of his pure family.

যে দিগ্বিজয়ী-জয়ী নদীয়ার পণ্ডিত অধীন যাঁর ।
সদা ধর্মপথে রত বেদাদিক বিনা না জানয়ে আর ॥

*ye digvijayī-jayī nadīyāra paṇḍita adhīna yām̐ra |*
*sadā dharmapathe rata bedādika binā nā jānaye āra ||*

*Word for word:* ye digvijayī-jayī — the conqueror of the digvijayi; nadīyāra paṇḍita adhīna yām̐ra — to whom the pandits of Nadia submit; sadā dharmapathe rata — ever devoted to the path of dharma; bedādika binā — but for the Vedas and the like; nā jānaye āra — knows nothing else

**19.3.** He conquered the digvijayi, the pandits of Nadia submit to Him; He is ever devoted to the path of dharma and knows nothing but the Vedas and the like.

প্রকৃতি-প্রসঙ্গ কভু না শুনয়ে শুনিতে বাসয়ে দুখ ।
ভুলিয়া কখন না দেখয়ে পর-রমণীগণের মুখ ॥

*prakṛti-prasaṅga kabhu nā śunaye śunite bāsaye dukha |*
*bhuliyā kakhana nā dekhaye para-ramaṇīgaṇera mukha ||*

*Word for word:* prakṛti-prasaṅga — talk about women; kabhu nā śunaye — He never listens to; śunite bāsaye dukha — it pains Him to hear; bhuliyā kakhana — never, even by mistake; nā dekhaye — does He look at; para-ramaṇīgaṇera mukha — the faces of others' wives

**19.4.** He never listens to talk of women — it pains Him to hear it; never, even by mistake, does He look at the faces of others' wives.

যদি কভু সুরধুনী-স্নানে নারী-বসন ঠেকয়ে গায় ।
তখনি উচিত করে পরাচিত তবু না সম্বিত পায় ॥

*yadi kabhu suradhunī-snāne nārī-basana ṭhekaye gāya |*
*takhani ucita kare parācita tabu nā sambita pāya ||*

*Word for word:* yadi kabhu — if ever; suradhunī-snāne — while bathing in the Suradhuni; nārī-basana ṭhekaye gāya — a woman's cloth touches His body; takhani — at once; ucita kare parācita — He performs the due expiation (prayashchitta); tabu nā sambita pāya — and still cannot regain His peace

**19.5.** If ever, while He bathes in the Suradhuni, a woman's cloth touches His body, He at once performs the due expiation and still cannot regain His peace.

তাহে সাধ করি মিছা অপবাদ দিলে অপরাধ হবে ।
নরহরি সাখী শিখাই সবারে একথা কভু না কবে ॥

*tāhe sādha kari michā apabāda dile aparādha habe |*
*narahari sākhī śikhāi sabāre ekathā kabhu nā kabe ||*

*Word for word:* tāhe — Him; sādha kari — wilfully; michā apabāda dile — slandering falsely; aparādha habe — there will be an offence (aparadha); narahari sākhī — Narahari is witness; śikhāi sabāre — I teach you all; ekathā kabhu nā kabe — never say this

**19.6.** To slander Him falsely and wilfully would be an aparadha. Narahari is witness: I teach you all — never say this."[^32-35]

[^32-34]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — p. 229, no. 164 (scan PDF p. 488); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 164 (catalogue: NG-358; first line "paṛinu dhande", as in GPT1). GCC — kirana 10,
pada 17 (ed. 1947, pp. 124–125; scan PDF pp. 129–130). The pada stands in the GPT section of nagari padas, but by content it is an answer to the notion of gaura-nagari;
in GCC it is the speech of a celestial woman "of a new group" (no. 18; note 24). B. The pada stands in the GPT section of nagari padas — see the introductory note to
the section (chapter 27).
[^32-35]: Here Gaura is described just as in the biographies: His learning and the victory over the digvijayi (Keshava Kashmiri; CB, Adi; CC, Adi 16), His strictness
towards women (CB, Adi: in this avatara the Lord did not look at women and allowed no jesting with them; cf. note 30). The detail of the expiation (prāyaścitta,
parācita) after an accidental touch of a woman's cloth while bathing is the author's own; it is not in the biographies known to us. "Aparadha" is an offence — here,
slander of the Lord. The signature "Narahari is witness": the poet himself testifies to the Lord's purity.

## 20. Narahari — "hera āisa ogo o saba sahite…" (GPT1 pp. 229–230, no. 165; GCC 10.19)
*An answer: praise of the Lord's strictness (by content — not nagari-bhava). Another takes her friend by the hand: "Come here — why quarrel with them?
In the city of the gods a false tale has arisen; do not be troubled. Only the guilty revile the faultless. Shachi's son out of modesty does not raise His
face — far from looking at anyone; He does not touch even the shadow of other women — how could there be a touching of bodies? He does not go to the
Ganga ghat where young women throng — He bathes at a secluded pond or at home, trembling for fear of disgrace. Let no one revile Narahari's Lord any more."
Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 10, pada 19.*[^32-36]

হের আইস ওগো ও সব সহিতে কি লাগি করিছ দ্বন্দ ।
সুরপুরে মিছা প্রপঞ্চ ঘটিল ইথে না বাসহ ধন্দ ॥

*hera āisa ogo o saba sahite ki lāgi karicha dvanda |*
*surapure michā prapañca ghaṭila ithe nā bāsaha dhanda ||*

*Word for word:* hera āisa ogo — come over here; o saba sahite — with those; ki lāgi karicha dvanda — why do you quarrel; surapure — in the city of the gods; michā prapañca ghaṭila — a false tale has arisen; ithe nā bāsaha dhanda — do not be troubled by it

**20.1.** "Come over here: why do you quarrel with those? In the city of the gods a false tale has arisen — do not be troubled by it.

যত সদাচার সব গেল দূরে কেহ না কাহুক মানে ।
এ বড় বিষম কিসে কিবা হয় তাহা না কিছুই জানে ॥

*yata sadācāra saba gela dūre keha nā kāhuka māne |*
*e baṛa biṣama kise kibā haya tāhā nā kichui jāne ||*

*Word for word:* yata sadācāra — all good conduct; saba gela dūre — has gone far away; keha nā kāhuka māne — no one respects anyone; e baṛa biṣama — this is a grave thing; kise kibā haya — what comes of what; tāhā nā kichui jāne — of that they know nothing

**20.2.** All good conduct has gone far away, no one respects anyone; this is a grave thing: what comes of what, of that they know nothing.

দোষযুক্ত জনে দূষিতে নিষেধ একথা সকলে কয় ।
দোষহীন জনে যে দূষে অবশ্য সে দোষী জগতে হয় ॥

*doṣayukta jane dūṣite niṣedha ekathā sakale kaya |*
*doṣahīna jane ye dūṣe abaśya se doṣī jagate haya ||*

*Word for word:* doṣayukta jane — one who has faults; dūṣite niṣedha — it is forbidden to censure; ekathā sakale kaya — all say this; doṣahīna jane — one who is faultless; ye dūṣe — whoever censures; abaśya se doṣī jagate haya — surely he is the guilty one in the world

**20.3.** To censure one who has faults is forbidden — all say this; and whoever censures the faultless is surely the guilty one in the world.

পরম সুজন শচীসুত ইহা বিদিত ভুবন মাঝে ।
কারু পানে কভু চাহিবে থাকুক বদন না তোলে লাজে ॥

*parama sujana śacīsuta ihā bidita bhubana mājhe |*
*kāru pāne kabhu cāhibe thākuka badana nā tole lāje ||*

*Word for word:* parama sujana śacīsuta — Shachi's son is the best of men; ihā bidita bhubana mājhe — this is known throughout the world; kāru pāne kabhu cāhibe thākuka — far from ever looking at anyone; badana nā tole lāje — out of modesty He does not raise His face

**20.4.** Shachi's son is the best of men — this is known throughout the world: far from ever looking at anyone, out of modesty He does not raise His face.

কখন যে পর-প্রকৃতিগণের ছায়া না পরশে পায় ।
না বুঝিয়ে কিছু অঙ্গ-পরশাদি কিরূপে সম্ভবে তায় ॥

*kakhana ye para-prakṛtigaṇera chāyā nā paraśe pāya |*
*nā bujhiye kichu aṅga-paraśādi kirūpe sambhabe tāya ||*

*Word for word:* kakhana ye — He who never; para-prakṛtigaṇera chāyā — the shadow of other women; nā paraśe pāya — touches with His foot; nā bujhiye kichu — I cannot understand at all; aṅga-paraśādi — touching of bodies and the like; kirūpe sambhabe tāya — how it could be possible for Him

**20.5.** He who never touches even the shadow of other women with His foot — I cannot understand at all: how could a touching of bodies and the like be possible for Him?

সুরধুনীঘাটে যুবতীর ঘটা জানি না যায়েন তথা ।
সরোবরে গিয়া করয়ে সিনান দেখয়ে নিভৃত যথা ॥

*suradhunīghāṭe yubatīra ghaṭā jāni nā yāyena tathā |*
*sarobare giyā karaye sināna dekhaye nibhṛta yathā ||*

*Word for word:* suradhunīghāṭe — at the ghat of the Suradhuni; yubatīra ghaṭā — a throng of young women; jāni — knowing; nā yāyena tathā — He does not go there; sarobare giyā — going to a pond; karaye sināna — He bathes; dekhaye nibhṛta yathā — where He sees a secluded spot

**20.6.** Knowing that a throng of young women is at the ghat of the Suradhuni, He does not go there: He goes to a pond and bathes where He sees a secluded spot;

নহে নিজ ঘরে সারে ক্রিয়া হিয়া কাঁপয়ে কলঙ্ক-ডরে ।
মহাজিতেন্দ্রিয় প্রিয় সবাকার কেবা না প্রশংসা করে ॥

*nahe nija ghare sāre kriyā hiyā kām̐paye kalaṅka-ḍare |*
*mahājitendriya priya sabākāra kebā nā praśaṃsā kare ||*

*Word for word:* nahe — or else; nija ghare sāre kriyā — He performs [His bath] (lit. "the rite") at home; hiyā kām̐paye kalaṅka-ḍare — His heart trembles for fear of disgrace; mahājitendriya — the great master of the senses; priya sabākāra — dear to all; kebā nā praśaṃsā kare — who does not praise Him

**20.7.** or else He performs His bath at home: His heart trembles for fear of disgrace. The great master of the senses, dear to all — who does not praise Him?

হায় হায় হেন জনে হেন কথা কহয়ে কিরূপ করি ।
অনুপম যার যশ-রসায়ন রৈয়াছে জগত ভরি ॥

*hāya hāya hena jane hena kathā kahaye kirūpa kari |*
*anupama yāra yaśa-rasāyana raiyāche jagata bhari ||*

*Word for word:* hāya hāya — alas, alas; hena jane hena kathā — such words of such a one; kahaye kirūpa kari — how can one say; anupama yāra yaśa-rasāyana — whose peerless elixir of fame; raiyāche jagata bhari — has filled the world

**20.8.** Alas, alas! How can one say such words of Him whose peerless fame, like an elixir, has filled the world?

তাহে হেন কথা কে যাবে প্রতীত ইহাতে বাসিএ লাজ ।
সুজন জানে কি সুজন নিন্দয়ে কুজন জনের কাজ ॥

*tāhe hena kathā ke yābe pratīta ihāte bāsie lāja |*
*sujana jāne ki sujana nindaye kujana janera kāja ||*

*Word for word:* tāhe — of Him; hena kathā — such words; ke yābe pratīta — who will believe; ihāte bāsie lāja — I feel ashamed at this; sujana jāne ki — does a good person know how; sujana nindaye — to revile a good one; kujana janera kāja — it is the work of wicked people

**20.9.** Who will believe such words of Him? I feel ashamed at this. Does a good person know how to revile a good one? It is the work of wicked people.

তথাপি বলিএ সহবাসী জানি মানিবে বচন-সার ।
ভুলিয়া কখন নরহরি-নাথে কেহ না নিন্দিহ আর ॥

*tathāpi balie sahabāsī jāni mānibe bacana-sāra |*
*bhuliyā kakhana narahari-nāthe keha nā nindiha āra ||*

*Word for word:* tathāpi balie — still I say; sahabāsī jāni — knowing you as neighbours; mānibe bacana-sāra — accept the essence of [my] words; bhuliyā kakhana — never, even by mistake; narahari-nāthe — Narahari's Lord; keha nā nindiha āra — let no one revile any more

**20.10.** Still I say, knowing you as neighbours: accept the essence of my words — let no one, even by mistake, revile Narahari's Lord any more."[^32-37]

[^32-36]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — pp. 229–230, no. 165 (scan PDF pp. 488–489); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 165 (catalogue: NG-127). GCC — kirana 10, pada 19 (ed. 1947,
pp. 125–126; scan PDF pp. 130–131); it is preceded by the short pada 10.18 (not in GPT): another woman, fearless, takes her friend by the hand and speaks to her. GCC
readings: "dekhibe thākuka" (20.4), "sujana jane ki sujane nindaye" (20.9). 20.7 "kriyā" follows GCC (GPT1 reads "krīṛā", "play" — probably a misprint). B. The pada
stands in the GPT section of nagari padas — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^32-37]: "In the city of the gods a false tale has arisen" (20.1) is a direct indication that the dispute is among celestial women (note 24). The description of the Lord
(20.4–20.7) is the same as in the biographies: according to CB (Adi), in this avatara the Lord did not look at other men's wives; the detail of bathing in a secluded
place is the author's own. The words "let no one revile the Lord", in the mouth of Narahari Chakravarti's heroine, coincide with the position of the tradition, which
rejects gaura-nagari (introductory note, chapter 27).

## 21. Narahari — "bhāla bhāla ogo esaba kathāte…" (GPT1 pp. 230–231, no. 166; GCC 10.21)
*Nagari-bhava (a mocking answer). The disputants laugh: "We are not afraid: as virtuous as you are, so is your Gora — ah, He knows nothing, a muni among
sages, He never goes into other people's houses! So many such virtues He has — and how many within He does not show; only young women's glances know them;
but your eyes, like those of some birds, do not see the moon of the night: how should others know that Narahari's Lord is a snare that enchants women?"
Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 10, pada 21.*[^32-38]

ভাল ভাল ওগো এসব কথাতে ভয় না বাসিএ মোরা ।
যেরূপ সুজন তুমি সেইরূপ সুজন তোমার গোরা ॥

*bhāla bhāla ogo esaba kathāte bhaya nā bāsie morā |*
*yerūpa sujana tumi seirūpa sujana tomāra gorā ||*

*Word for word:* bhāla bhāla ogo — well, well, dear; esaba kathāte — at such words; bhaya nā bāsie morā — we are not afraid; yerūpa sujana tumi — as virtuous as you are; seirūpa sujana tomāra gorā — so virtuous is your Gora

**21.1.** "Well, well, dear: we are not afraid of such words. As virtuous as you are — so virtuous is your Gora!

আহা মরি মরি কিছু না জানয়ে না দেখি এমন জনা ।
অতি জিতেন্দ্রিয় মুনীন্দ্র-সদৃশ বিদিত ধার্মিকপনা ॥

*āhā mari mari kichu nā jānaye nā dekhi emana janā |*
*ati jitendriya munīndra-sadṛśa bidita dhārmikapanā ||*

*Word for word:* āhā mari mari — ah, ah; kichu nā jānaye — He knows nothing; nā dekhi emana janā — I have never seen such a one; ati jitendriya — utterly master of the senses; munīndra-sadṛśa — like the king of sages; bidita dhārmikapanā — renowned [His] righteousness

**21.2.** Ah, ah! He knows nothing at all — I have never seen such a one! Utterly master of the senses, like the king of sages — His righteousness is renowned!

প্রকৃতি-প্রসঙ্গ না শুনে এ যশঃ প্রসিদ্ধ জগত মাঝে ।
নিজ গৃহ ছাড়ি কারু বাড়ী কভু না যান কোনই কাজে ॥

*prakṛti-prasaṅga nā śune e yaśaḥ prasiddha jagata mājhe |*
*nija gṛha chāṛi kāru bāṛī kabhu nā yāna konai kāje ||*

*Word for word:* prakṛti-prasaṅga nā śune — He does not listen to talk of women; e yaśaḥ prasiddha jagata mājhe — this fame is known in the world; nija gṛha chāṛi — leaving His own house; kāru bāṛī kabhu — to anyone's house ever; nā yāna konai kāje — He never goes on any business

**21.3.** He does not listen to talk of women — this fame is known in the world; He never leaves His own house to go into anyone's house on any business!

এইরূপ বহু গুণ অনুপম তুমি বা কহিবা কত ।
বাহিরে প্রকট না করয়ে আর অন্তরে আছয়ে যত ॥

*eirūpa bahu guṇa anupama tumi bā kahibā kata |*
*bāhire prakaṭa nā karaye āra antare āchaye yata ||*

*Word for word:* eirūpa bahu guṇa anupama — so many such peerless virtues; tumi vā kahibā kata — how many will you tell; bāhire prakaṭa nā karaye — He does not show outwardly; āra antare āchaye yata — and as many as there are within

**21.4.** So many such peerless virtues He has — how many of them will you tell? And as many as there are within — those He does not show outwardly.

তাহে বলি শুন সে গুণ জানিতে আনের শকতি নয় ।
কেবল এ নব যুবতী-কটাক্ষ-ছটায়ে প্রকট হয় ॥

*tāhe bali śuna se guṇa jānite ānera śakati naya |*
*kebala e naba yubatī-kaṭākṣa-chaṭāye prakaṭa haya ||*

*Word for word:* tāhe bali śuna — so I say, listen; se guṇa jānite — to know those virtues; ānera śakati naya — others have no power; kebala — only; e naba yubatī-kaṭākṣa-chaṭāye — in the flash of these young women's glances; prakaṭa haya — they appear

**21.5.** So I say, listen: others have no power to know those virtues — they appear only in the flash of these young women's glances.

তোমাদের আঁখি পাখী-সম দেখি না দেখে রজনী-চাঁদ ।
আনে কি জানিবে নরহরি-নাথ রমণীমোহন-ফাঁদ ॥

*tomādera ām̐khi pākhī-sama dekhi nā dekhe rajanī-cām̐da |*
*āne ki jānibe narahari-nātha ramaṇīmohana-phām̐da ||*

*Word for word:* tomādera ām̐khi — your eyes; pākhī-sama dekhi — I see, like [some] birds'; nā dekhe rajanī-cām̐da — do not see the moon of the night; āne ki jānibe — how should others know; narahari-nātha — [that] Narahari's Lord; ramaṇīmohana-phām̐da — is a snare that enchants women

**21.6.** Your eyes, I see, like those of [some] birds, do not see the moon of the night: how should others know that Narahari's Lord is a snare that enchants women?"[^32-39]

[^32-38]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — pp. 230–231, no. 166 (scan PDF pp. 489–490); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 166 (catalogue: NG-359). GCC — kirana 10, pada 21 (ed. 1947,
pp. 126–127; scan PDF pp. 131–132); it is preceded by the short pada 10.20 (not in GPT): "these merry ones, hearing the admonition, laughed to themselves and answered
slyly". 21.3 "nā yāna" follows GCC (GPT1 "nā jāna"). B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^32-39]: The whole pada mocks the defender: the praise of the Lord's strictness (21.2–21.3) is repeated with derision; rendered as in the original, keeping the mocking
tone. "Do not see the moon of the night" (21.6) apparently refers to birds that sleep at night: the defender supposedly does not know the "night" side of Gaura's
life — and that is the very notion of gaura-nagari, which the tradition does not accept (introductory note, chapter 27; cf. notes 30, 35).

## 22. Narahari — "hera āisa prāṇa sajani ihāte…" (GPT1 p. 231, no. 167; GCC 10.22)
*Nagari-bhava (the dispute). The mocker's friend says to her: "Leave it — you hold these secret talks of rasa with her in vain: she is simple and does not
walk this path; one who delights in the formless will not like form. Ask her instead: if He is so master of His senses, why does He take on the guise of
a nagara in the midst of Nadia, why do women lose their shame at the fragrance of His body, why does He, seeing a man's face and mistaking it for a woman's,
fall in a swoon, why does He dance in the assembly of the virtuous taking a woman's name and repeat 'woman' in His mind, why does He gather so many young
women in His house? Let her answer." Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 10, pada 22.*[^32-40]

হের আইস প্রাণ সজনি ইহাতে সুখ না উপজে মনে ।
এ সব নিগূঢ় রসকথা বৃথা কহিছ উহার সনে ॥

*hera āisa prāṇa sajani ihāte sukha nā upaje mane |*
*e saba nigūṛha rasakathā bṛthā kahicha uhāra sane ||*

*Word for word:* hera āisa — come over here; prāṇa sajani — dear friend; ihāte sukha nā upaje mane — this brings no joy to the heart; e saba nigūṛha rasakathā — these secret talks of rasa; bṛthā kahicha — you hold in vain; uhāra sane — with her

**22.1.** "Come over here, dear friend: this brings no joy to the heart — in vain you hold these secret talks of rasa with her.

রসিকিনী বিনা বুঝিতে পারে কি রসিক জনের হিয়া ।
তাহে এহ অতি সরলা কখন না চলে এ পথ দিয়া ॥

*rasikinī binā bujhite pāre ki rasika janera hiyā |*
*tāhe eha ati saralā kakhana nā cale e patha diyā ||*

*Word for word:* rasikinī binā — but a woman versed in rasa; bujhite pāre ki — can anyone understand; rasika janera hiyā — the heart of a rasika; tāhe — and she; eha ati saralā — is very simple; kakhana nā cale e patha diyā — never walks this path

**22.2.** Who but a woman versed in rasa can understand the heart of a rasika? And she is very simple — she never walks this path.

যত তত তুমি বুঝাহ তাহাতে নাহিক উহার দায় ।
নিরাকারে যার আরতি তারে কি আকার কখন ভায় ॥

*yata tata tumi bujhāha tāhāte nāhika uhāra dāya |*
*nirākāre yāra ārati tāre ki ākāra kakhana bhāya ||*

*Word for word:* yata tata tumi bujhāha — however much you explain; tāhāte nāhika uhāra dāya — she has no concern with it; nirākāre yāra ārati — one whose delight is in the formless; tāre ki ākāra kakhana bhāya — will form ever please her

**22.3.** However much you explain, she has no concern with it: one whose delight is in the formless — will form ever please her?

যদি অকপটে কখন করয়ে দুলহ তোদের সঙ্গ ।
তবে সে বুঝিতে পারিবে নদীয়াচাঁদের যেরূপ রঙ্গ ॥

*yadi akapaṭe kakhana karaye dulaha todera saṅga |*
*tabe se bujhite pāribe nadīyācām̐dera yerūpa raṅga ||*

*Word for word:* yadi akapaṭe kakhana — if ever sincerely; karaye dulaha todera saṅga — she keeps your rare company; tabe se bujhite pāribe — then she will understand; nadīyācām̐dera yerūpa raṅga — what the play of the Moon of Nadia is

**22.4.** If ever she sincerely keeps your rare company, then she will understand what the play of the Moon of Nadia is.

এ সকল কথা থাকুক এখন বারেক সুধাহ তারে ।
অতি জিতেন্দ্রিয় হইয়া কেমন এরূপ বিলাস করে ॥

*e sakala kathā thākuka ekhana bāreka sudhāha tāre |*
*ati jitendriya haiyā kemana erūpa bilāsa kare ||*

*Word for word:* e sakala kathā thākuka ekhana — let all this be now; bāreka sudhāha tāre — ask her just once; ati jitendriya haiyā — being so much master of His senses; kemana erūpa bilāsa kare — how does He sport like this

**22.5.** Let all this be now; ask her just once: being so much master of His senses, how does He sport like this?

যে জন কিছু না জানে যার নাহি কোনই সুখের লেশ ।
সে কেনে নদীয়ানগরের মাঝে ধরে নাগরালি বেশ ॥

*ye jana kichu nā jāne yāra nāhi konai sukhera leśa |*
*se kene nadīyānagarera mājhe dhare nāgarāli beśa ||*

*Word for word:* ye jana kichu nā jāne — He who knows nothing [of this]; yāra nāhi konai sukhera leśa — in whom is no trace of [worldly] pleasure; se kene — why does He; nadīyānagarera mājhe — in the midst of the town of Nadia; dhare nāgarāli beśa — take on the guise of a nagara

**22.6.** He who knows nothing [of this], in whom is no trace of pleasure — why does He take on the guise of a nagara in the midst of the town of Nadia?

ইহা কোনখানে না শুনি উদার জনের কি হেন কাজ ।
অঙ্গের সৌরভে নারী-ভ্রমরীর ভাঙ্গয়ে ভরম লাজ ॥

*ihā konakhāne nā śuni udāra janera ki hena kāja |*
*aṅgera saurabhe nārī-bhramarīra bhāṅgaye bharama lāja ||*

*Word for word:* ihā konakhāne nā śuni — nowhere have I heard of this; udāra janera ki hena kāja — is this the deed of a noble person; aṅgera saurabhe — with the fragrance of His body; nārī-bhramarīra — of the women-bees; bhāṅgaye bharama lāja — He breaks their reserve and shame

**22.7.** Nowhere have I heard of this: is this the deed of a noble person? With the fragrance of His body He breaks the reserve and shame of the women-bees.

অতি ধীর যেহ তার কি এ ক্রিয়া কিরূপে মনেতে ভায় ।
পুরুষ বদন হেরি নারী মুখ ভরমে মুরছা যায় ॥

*ati dhīra yeha tāra ki e kriyā kirūpe manete bhāya |*
*puruṣa badana heri nārī mukha bharame murachā yāya ||*

*Word for word:* ati dhīra yeha — He who is so grave; tāra ki e kriyā — are such deeds His; kirūpe manete bhāya — how do they please His mind; puruṣa badana heri — seeing a man's face; nārī mukha bharame — mistaking it for a woman's face; murachā yāya — He falls in a swoon

**22.8.** He who is so grave — are such deeds His, how do they please His mind? Seeing a man's face and mistaking it for a woman's face, He falls in a swoon.

এ বড় বিষম বহু লাজ যার তার কি এমন কাম ।
সতের সমাজে নাচে অবিরত লইয়া নারীর নাম ॥

*e baṛa biṣama bahu lāja yāra tāra ki emana kāma |*
*satera samāje nāce abirata laiyā nārīra nāma ||*

*Word for word:* e baṛa biṣama — this is very strange; bahu lāja yāra — one who has so much modesty; tāra ki emana kāma — is such desire His; satera samāje — in the assembly of the virtuous; nāce abirata — He dances unceasingly; laiyā nārīra nāma — taking a woman's name

**22.9.** This is very strange: one who has so much modesty — is such desire His? In the assembly of the virtuous He dances unceasingly, taking a woman's name.

প্রকৃতি-প্রসঙ্গ যেজন কখন না শুনে আপন কাণে ।
সে জন কেমন করিয়া সতত প্রকৃতি জপয়ে মনে ॥

*prakṛti-prasaṅga yejana kakhana nā śune āpana kāṇe |*
*se jana kemana kariyā satata prakṛti japaye mane ||*

*Word for word:* prakṛti-prasaṅga — talk of women; yejana kakhana nā śune āpana kāṇe — He who never hears with His own ears; se jana kemana kariyā — how is it that He; satata prakṛti japaye mane — constantly repeats "prakriti" (woman) in His mind

**22.10.** He who never hears talk of women with His own ears — how is it that He constantly repeats "woman" in His mind?

যেহ জগতের মাঝে অতিশয় অনন্য-ধার্মিক বড় ।
সে নিজ ভবনে কি কারণে এত যুবতী করয়ে জড় ॥

*yeha jagatera mājhe atiśaya ananya-dhārmika baṛa |*
*se nija bhabane ki kāraṇe eta yubatī karaye jaṛa ||*

*Word for word:* yeha jagatera mājhe — He who in the world; atiśaya ananya-dhārmika baṛa — is righteous as no one else; se nija bhabane — in His own house; ki kāraṇe — for what reason; eta yubatī karaye jaṛa — gathers so many young women

**22.11.** He who in the world is righteous as no one else — for what reason does He gather so many young women in His own house?

নরহরি-পহুঁ এই রীতি ইথে বলহ উত্তর দিতে ।
হেন জনে হেন প্রত্যয় কিরূপে হৈয়াছে উদারচিতে ॥

*narahari-pahum̐ ei rīti ithe balaha uttara dite |*
*hena jane hena pratyaya kirūpe haiyāche udāracite ||*

*Word for word:* narahari-pahum̐ — of Narahari's Lord; ei rīti — such are the ways; ithe balaha uttara dite — tell her to answer this; hena jane hena pratyaya — such faith in such a one; kirūpe haiyāche udāracite — how has it arisen in a generous heart

**22.12.** Such are the ways of Narahari's Lord: tell her to answer this — how has such faith in such a one arisen in a generous heart?"[^32-41]

[^32-40]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — p. 231, no. 167 (scan PDF p. 490); in the GPT1 OCR line 22.7b is missing, but it is in the scan. GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 167 (catalogue:
NG-360). GCC — kirana 10, pada 22 (ed. 1947, pp. 127–128; scan PDF pp. 132–133), "asyāḥ svapakṣāha — yathārāga" ("one of her own side said"). GCC readings: "dhare
nāgariṇī beśa" — "takes on the guise of a nagarini (a woman)" (22.6), "uhāra cite" — "in her heart" (22.12). B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section
(chapter 27).
[^32-41]: The disputant's rhetorical questions reinterpret features of the Lord's lila known from the biographies in the spirit of gaura-nagari: dancing in kirtana "with a
woman's name" (22.9) — cf. the episode when the Lord repeated "gopi, gopi" (CC, Adi 17); "the guise of a nagarini" in the GCC reading (22.6) — perhaps an allusion to the
drama in Chandrashekhara's house, where the Lord appeared in a woman's form (CB, Madhya 18); "repeats 'woman' in His mind" (22.10) and the swoons (22.8) — His absorption
in the bhava of the gopis and of Radha; "gathers young women in His house" (22.11) — the visits of the young wives to Shachi-devi (nos. 1–12). According to Krishnadasa
Kaviraja, all this is Radha's prema for Krishna, which the Lord tastes (CC, Adi 4), not a nagara's love; the tradition does not accept the disputant's interpretation
(introductory note, chapter 27). "One whose delight is in the formless" (22.3) is a gibe: the defender's strict view of the Lord is likened to worship of the impersonal
(nirākāra). Rendered as in the original.

## 23. Narahari — "śuna śuna ogo sakala bujhinu…" (GPT1 pp. 231–233, no. 168; GCC 10.24)
*Nagari-bhava (the end of the dispute). Yet another, skilled in speech, says: "She is not at fault — you dispute in vain. Do not be sad, good and fair one:
you say Gora does not look at others' women — how can I believe it, when the nagara's play in Nadia is beyond counting and I have seen it myself? And if
you ask how this is possible in this descent — no one gives up his nature: this son of Shachi is the son of Yashoda; for the gopis' sake He herded cows and
lifted the hill, was subject to them, sought their touch, clasped a friend's feet to end a gopi's mana, carried [a gopi] on His shoulders, and their scolding
was sweeter to Him than the hymns of the Vedas; how would He give up such a nature?" Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC,
kirana 10, pada 24.*[^32-42]

শুন শুন ওগো সকল বুঝিনু ইহার নাহিক দোষ ।
বিচার করিতে তোমা সবা প্রতি হইছে আমার রোষ ॥

*śuna śuna ogo sakala bujhinu ihāra nāhika doṣa |*
*bicāra karite tomā sabā prati haiche āmāra roṣa ||*

*Word for word:* śuna śuna ogo — listen, listen; sakala bujhinu — I have understood everything; ihāra nāhika doṣa — she is not at fault; bicāra karite — for your disputing; tomā sabā prati — with you all; haiche āmāra roṣa — I am angry

**23.1.** "Listen, listen: I have understood everything — she is not at fault; it is with you all that I am angry, for your disputing.

যদি না বুঝিয়া কেহ কিছু কহে তাহে কি করিএ হাসি ।
যেরূপে বুঝিতে পারয়ে সেরূপ বুঝালে সুবুদ্ধি বাসি ॥

*yadi nā bujhiyā keha kichu kahe tāhe ki karie hāsi |*
*yerūpe bujhite pāraye serūpa bujhāle subuddhi bāsi ||*

*Word for word:* yadi nā bujhiyā — if without understanding; keha kichu kahe — someone says something; tāhe ki karie hāsi — should one laugh at that; yerūpe bujhite pāraye — in the way she can understand; serūpa bujhāle — to explain so; subuddhi bāsi — I would think wise

**23.2.** If someone says something without understanding — should one laugh at that? To explain in the way she can understand — that I would think wise.

এহ সুচরিত আহা মরি হেন জানে না বুঝাইতে জান ।
থাকহ নীরব হইয়া এখন আমি যে কহি তা শুন ॥

*eha sucarita āhā mari hena jāne nā bujhāite jāna |*
*thākaha nīraba haiyā ekhana āmi ye kahi tā śuna ||*

*Word for word:* eha sucarita — she is of good conduct; āhā mari — ah; hena jāne — such a one; nā bujhāite jāna — you do not know how to make understand; thākaha nīraba haiyā ekhana — be silent now; āmi ye kahi tā śuna — listen to what I say

**23.3.** She is of good conduct; ah, such a one you do not know how to bring round. Be silent now and listen to what I say.

হের আইস ওহে সুজন সুন্দরি মনে না বাসিহ দুখ ।
তোমার বচন শুনি মোর মনে হৈয়াছে পরম সুখ ॥

*hera āisa ohe sujana sundari mane nā bāsiha dukha |*
*tomāra bacana śuni mora mane haiyāche parama sukha ||*

*Word for word:* hera āisa ohe — come over here; sujana sundari — good and fair one; mane nā bāsiha dukha — do not be sad; tomāra bacana śuni — hearing your words; mora mane haiyāche parama sukha — my heart is overjoyed

**23.4.** Come over here, good and fair one, do not be sad: hearing your words, my heart is overjoyed.

তুমি বল গোরা পর-প্রকৃতি না দেখে নয়ানকোণে ।
এ সকল কথা কিরূপে প্রত্যয় হইবে আমার মনে ॥

*tumi bala gorā para-prakṛti nā dekhe nayānakoṇe |*
*e sakala kathā kirūpe pratyaya haibe āmāra mane ||*

*Word for word:* tumi bala — you say; gorā para-prakṛti — [that] Gora at others' women; nā dekhe nayānakoṇe — does not look even from the corner of His eye; e sakala kathā — all this; kirūpe pratyaya haibe āmāra mane — how can I believe it

**23.5.** You say that Gora does not look at others' women even from the corner of His eye — how can I believe all this?

যেরূপ প্রশংসা কর তার যদি কিঞ্চিত দেখিতে পাই ।
নিশ্চয় বলিয়া শপথ খাইয়া তথাপি প্রত্যয় যাই ॥

*yerūpa praśaṃsā kara tāra yadi kiñcita dekhite pāi |*
*niścaya baliyā śapatha khāiyā tathāpi pratyaya yāi ||*

*Word for word:* yerūpa praśaṃsā kara — what you praise; tāra yadi kiñcita dekhite pāi — if I could see even a little of it; niścaya baliyā — saying "certainly"; śapatha khāiyā — swearing an oath; tathāpi pratyaya yāi — then I would come to believe

**23.6.** If I could see even a little of what you praise — then, swearing an oath and saying 'certainly', I would come to believe.

নদীয়ানগরে নাগরালি যত নাহিক তাহার লেখা ।
আনের কথাতে যে হৌক সে হউক ইহা ত আমার দেখা ॥

*nadīyānagare nāgarāli yata nāhika tāhāra lekhā |*
*ānera kathāte ye hauka se hauka ihā ta āmāra dekhā ||*

*Word for word:* nadīyānagare — in the town of Nadia; nāgarāli yata — the nagara's play; nāhika tāhāra lekhā — is beyond counting; ānera kathāte — by others' words; ye hauka se hauka — be it as it may; ihā ta āmāra dekhā — this I have seen myself

**23.7.** In the town of Nadia the nagara's play is beyond counting; be it as it may with others' words — this I have seen myself.

যদি বল এই অবতারে ইহা সম্ভব কিরূপে হয় ।
আছয়ে তাহার কারণ প্রসিদ্ধ সকল লোকেতে কয় ॥

*yadi bala ei abatāre ihā sambhaba kirūpe haya |*
*āchaye tāhāra kāraṇa prasiddha sakala lokete kaya ||*

*Word for word:* yadi bala — if you say; ei abatāre — in this descent; ihā sambhaba kirūpe haya — how is this possible; āchaye tāhāra kāraṇa prasiddha — there is a well-known reason for it; sakala lokete kaya — all people speak of it

**23.8.** If you say: how is this possible in this descent? — there is a well-known reason for it; all people speak of it.

যার যে স্বভাব থাকে তাহা কেহ কভু না ছাড়িতে পারে ।
স্বভাবানুরূপ করে ক্রিয়া কারু নিষেধে কিছু না করে ॥

*yāra ye svabhāba thāke tāhā keha kabhu nā chāṛite pāre |*
*svabhābānurūpa kare kriyā kāru niṣedhe kichu nā kare ||*

*Word for word:* yāra ye svabhāba thāke — whatever nature one has; tāhā keha kabhu nā chāṛite pāre — no one can ever abandon it; svabhābānurūpa kare kriyā — one acts according to one's nature; kāru niṣedhe kichu nā kare — no one's prohibition avails

**23.9.** Whatever nature one has, no one can ever abandon it: one acts according to one's nature, and no one's prohibition avails.

যদি মনে কর এরূপ ইহার স্বভাব কোথাও না দেখি ।
তাহাতে তোমারে নিবেদিএ শুন ইহাতে জগত সাখী ॥

*yadi mane kara erūpa ihāra svabhāba kothāo nā dekhi |*
*tāhāte tomāre nibedie śuna ihāte jagata sākhī ||*

*Word for word:* yadi mane kara — if you think; erūpa ihāra svabhāba — such a nature of His; kothāo nā dekhi — is seen nowhere; tāhāte tomāre nibedie — to that I tell you; śuna — listen; ihāte jagata sākhī — the world is witness to it

**23.10.** If you think such a nature of His is seen nowhere — to that I tell you, listen: the world is witness to it.

এই শচীসুত যশোদানন্দন তাহা কি না জান তুমি ।
বৃন্দাবনে যত নিগূঢ় বিলাস তাহা কি জানাব আমি ॥

*ei śacīsuta yaśodānandana tāhā ki nā jāna tumi |*
*bṛndābane yata nigūṛha bilāsa tāhā ki jānāba āmi ||*

*Word for word:* ei śacīsuta — this son of Shachi; yaśodānandana — is the son of Yashoda; tāhā ki nā jāna tumi — do you not know that; bṛndābane yata nigūṛha bilāsa — all the secret pastimes in Vrindavana; tāhā ki jānāba āmi — need I tell you of them

**23.11.** This son of Shachi is the son of Yashoda: do you not know that? Need I tell you of all the secret pastimes in Vrindavana?

গোপিকার লাগি গোচারণ গিরিধারণ আদিক যত ।
গোপিকা সহিত যেখানে যে লীলা তাহা বা কহিব কত ॥

*gopikāra lāgi gocāraṇa giridhāraṇa ādika yata |*
*gopikā sahita yekhāne ye līlā tāhā bā kahiba kata ||*

*Word for word:* gopikāra lāgi — for the gopis' sake; gocāraṇa — the herding of cows; giridhāraṇa ādika yata — the lifting of the hill and all else; gopikā sahita — with the gopis; yekhāne ye līlā — whatever lila, wherever; tāhā vā kahiba kata — how much of it shall I tell

**23.12.** For the gopis' sake — the herding of cows, the lifting of the hill and all else; how much shall I tell of the lilas with the gopis, whatever and wherever they were!

তা সবার অতি অধীন তিলেক না দেখি কলপ বাসে ।
কত ছল করি ফিরে অনুখন অঙ্গের পরশ-আশে ॥

*tā sabāra ati adhīna tileka nā dekhi kalapa bāse |*
*kata chala kari phire anukhana aṅgera paraśa-āśe ||*

*Word for word:* tā sabāra ati adhīna — utterly subject to them all; tileka nā dekhi — not seeing [them] for a moment; kalapa bāse — feels it an aeon; kata chala kari — with so many pretexts; phire anukhana — He goes about constantly; aṅgera paraśa-āśe — hoping for the touch of [their] bodies

**23.13.** Utterly subject to them all, not seeing them for a moment He feels it an aeon; with so many pretexts He goes about constantly, hoping for the touch of their bodies!

মানবতী কেহ মান করি কানু-পানে না ফিরিয়া চায় ।
তার মান-অবসানের কারণে ধরেন সখীর পায় ॥

*mānabatī keha māna kari kānu-pāne nā phiriyā cāya |*
*tāra māna-abasānera kāraṇe dharena sakhīra pāya ||*

*Word for word:* mānabatī keha — if some [gopi] in mana; māna kari — being offended; kānu-pāne nā phiriyā cāya — will not turn to look at Kanu; tāra māna-abasānera kāraṇe — to end her mana; dharena sakhīra pāya — He clasps [her] friend's feet

**23.14.** If some [gopi] in mana, being offended, will not turn to look at Kanu, — to end her mana He clasps her friend's feet.

কান্ধেতে করিয়া বহে আপনার পরম সৌভাগ্য মানি ।
বেদস্তুতি হৈতে পরম আনন্দ শুনিয়া ভর্ৎসন-বাণী ॥

*kāndhete kariyā bahe āpanāra parama saubhāgya māni |*
*bedastuti haite parama ānanda śuniyā bhartsana-bāṇī ||*

*Word for word:* kāndhete kariyā bahe — He carries [her] on His shoulders; āpanāra parama saubhāgya māni — deeming it His supreme good fortune; bedastuti haite — more than from the hymns of the Vedas; parama ānanda — supreme joy; śuniyā bhartsana-bāṇī — hearing [their] scolding words

**23.15.** He carries [her] on His shoulders, deeming it His supreme good fortune; hearing their scolding words gives Him more joy than the hymns of the Vedas.

যুবতী লাগিয়া জগতে বিষম কলঙ্ক না গণে যেহ ।
বল বল দেখি এরূপ স্বভাব কিরূপে ছাড়িব তেঁহ ॥

*yubatī lāgiyā jagate biṣama kalaṅka nā gaṇe yeha |*
*bala bala dekhi erūpa svabhāba kirūpe chāṛiba tem̐ha ||*

*Word for word:* yubatī lāgiyā — for the sake of young women; jagate biṣama kalaṅka — grave disgrace in the world; nā gaṇe yeha — He who does not mind; bala bala dekhi — tell me now; erūpa svabhāba — such a nature; kirūpe chāṛiba tem̐ha — how would He give up

**23.16.** He who for the sake of young women does not mind grave disgrace in the world — tell me now: how would He give up such a nature?

ইহাতে নিশ্চয় জানিহ তোমরা বিচার করিয়া চিতে ।
স্বভাবে করয়ে এ সকল ক্রিয়া বুঝিবা আপনা হৈতে ॥

*ihāte niścaya jāniha tomarā bicāra kariyā cite |*
*svabhābe karaye e sakala kriyā bujhibā āpanā haite ||*

*Word for word:* ihāte niścaya jāniha tomarā — know this for certain; bicāra kariyā cite — reflecting in your hearts; svabhābe karaye e sakala kriyā — by His nature He does all this; bujhibā āpanā haite — you will understand of yourselves

**23.17.** Know this for certain, reflecting in your hearts: by His nature He does all this — you will understand of yourselves.

নরহরি-পহুঁ রসিকশেখর উপমা নাহিক যার ।
এ সব চরিত কেবা নাহি জানে ইথে কি সন্দেহ আর ॥

*narahari-pahum̐ rasikaśekhara upamā nāhika yāra |*
*e saba carita kebā nāhi jāne ithe ki sandeha āra ||*

*Word for word:* narahari-pahum̐ — Narahari's Lord; rasikaśekhara — the Crown of connoisseurs of rasa; upamā nāhika yāra — who has no equal; e saba carita — these deeds; kebā nāhi jāne — who does not know; ithe ki sandeha āra — what further doubt is there

**23.18.** Narahari's Lord is the Crown of connoisseurs of rasa, who has no equal: who does not know these deeds? What further doubt is there?"[^32-43]

[^32-42]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — pp. 231–233, no. 168 (scan PDF pp. 490–492); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 168 (catalogue: NG-361). GCC — kirana 10, pada 24 (ed. 1947,
pp. 128–129; scan PDF pp. 133–134); it is preceded by the short pada 10.23 (not in GPT): the mockers said much, the defender was abashed, and then another, skilled
in speech, looked at her own group and spoke sweetly. 23.13 "adhīna" ("subject") follows GCC (GPT1 "adhika"). The next GPT pada (no. 169 = GCC 10.25, "brajapure
rasabilāsa biśeṣa…") is in chapter 33. B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^32-43]: "This son of Shachi is the son of Yashoda" (23.11): that Gaura is Krishna Himself is the foundation of Gaudiya theology (CC, Adi 1–4; CB). But the heroine's
conclusion — "a nature cannot be given up, so in Nadia too He plays the nagara" — the tradition does not accept: according to Krishnadasa Kaviraja, Krishna comes as
Gaura in order to taste Radha's love — in her bhava and complexion, as a devotee, not as an enjoyer (CC, Adi 4); therefore Vrindavana Dasa and Krishnadasa Kaviraja do
not portray Gaura as a nagara, and Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati regards gaura-nagari as a deviation (introductory note, chapter 27). Rendered as in the original.
23.12–23.15 are motifs of Vraja-lila: the lifting of Govardhana, the gopis' mana, the gopi who asked to be carried on His shoulders (*Bhag.* 10.30.37–38); "the beloved's
scolding is sweeter than the hymns of the Vedas" — cf. Krishna's words in CC, Adi 4.26. "Kalpa" (kalapa, 23.13) — an aeon.

## Summary of chapter 32

*The chapter continues the padas signed "Narahari" from section 3.2 of GPT. All 23 padas have been found in Narahari Chakravarti's "Gaura-charita-chintamani" and
checked against its scan ("probably Chakravarti" — B). No. 146 (no. 1) = GCC 9.2 — a mother-in-law, on an astrologer's word, sends her daughters-in-law to
Shachi-devi. Nos. 147–157 (nos. 2–12) = GCC 9.6–9.16 — the "wishes" (manoratha) of the townswomen on the way to Shachi's house, all in the future tense: to steal a
glance at Gaura, feigned mana, a silent conversation of the eyes, reproaches; in GCC no. 150 comes after no. 153 (9.12). Nos. 158–168 (nos. 13–23) = GCC 10.10–10.24 —
according to GCC this is the conversation and dispute of heavenly women (debaramaṇī) looking down on Nadia from the sky: some speak of the "secret play of the nagara",
others (nos. 19–20) answer with a description of the Lord's strictness — He does not look at women, does not listen to talk of them, bathes in a secluded place — and
call slander of Him an aparadha; the dispute ends with mockery and the argument "Shachi's son is Yashoda's son, a nature cannot be given up" (nos. 21–23). Section 3.2 of GPT omits GCC
9.3–9.5, 9.17–9.23, 10.1–10.9, 10.11, 10.18, 10.20, 10.23 (some of them — 9.18–9.19, 9.21–9.22, 10.7–10.9 — stand in other sections of GPT, see the concluding note of chapter 33). Where GCC is more explicit than GPT (no. 9 — "the cloth over the breast" instead of "the cloth over the face";
no. 10 — "wants to embrace" instead of "wants to see your dear face"; no. 2 — "under Madana's weight"), the GPT text is translated and the GCC reading is noted in VAR
and in a note. The motifs of attraction in the townswomen's daydreams and the talk of the "nagara" are rendered exactly, without softening, with notes on the position
of the tradition (notes 5, 25, 27, 30, 41, 43).*

# Chapter 33. Nagari Padas — VII: the "Narahari" padas of GPT (sect. 3.2, nos. 169–180; sects. 2.4, 3.1, 5.1, 5.2): the quarrels of the heavenly women, the townswomen's words at the Lord's wedding; concluding note

*On what nagari-bhava is, the position of the tradition (Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja, Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati) and the rules of translation, see the introductory note to the section of nagari padas in chapter 27; on the two poets named Narahari (Narahari Sarakara and Narahari Chakravarti) and on the attribution labels ("probably Sarakara", "probably Chakravarti", "not established"), see the introductory note to the "Narahari" appendix in chapter 17.*

## 1. Narahari — "brajapure rasabilāsa biśeṣa…" (GPT1 p. 233, no. 169; GCC 10.25)
*Nagari-bhava (the heavenly women's talk). The heavenly woman who closed the dispute (chapter 32, no. 23) tells her friend in confidence: who can
tell the special plays of rasa in Vraja? Yet He is the very same, and with all the same dear companions He ever sports in Nadia, absorbed in singing of
His own virtues; first giving His own the nectar of His beauty to drink, He made them as if mad, and the young noble wives, bidding farewell to family
and shame, made Gora their very essence. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 10, pada 25.*[^33-1]

ব্রজপুরে রসবিলাস বিশেষ সে সকল কেবা কহিতে পারে ।
গুপতে রাখিহ দিহ চিত যাহা কহিয়া আপনা জানিয়া তোরে ॥

*brajapure rasabilāsa biśeṣa se sakala kebā kahite pāre |*
*gupate rākhiha diha cita yāhā kahiyā āpanā jāniyā tore ||*

*Word for word:* brajapure — in the city of Vraja; rasabilāsa biśeṣa — the special plays of rasa; se sakala kebā kahite pāre — who can tell them all; gupate rākhiha — keep it secret; diha cita — attend (lit. "give the mind"); yāhā kahiyā — to what I shall say; āpanā jāniyā tore — counting you as my own

**1.1.** "The special plays of rasa in the city of Vraja — who can tell them all? Keep it secret; attend to what I tell you, counting you as my own.

এই সেই সেই এই সেই সব প্রিয়পরিকর সঙ্গেতে লৈয়া ।
বিহরয়ে সদা নদীয়ানগরে নিজ গুণগানে মগন হৈয়া ॥

*ei sei sei ei sei saba priyaparikara saṅgete laiyā |*
*biharaye sadā nadīyānagare nija guṇagāne magana haiyā ||*

*Word for word:* ei sei sei ei — this is He, He is this; sei saba priya-parikara — all the same dear companions; saṅgete laiyā — taking along; biharaye sadā — ever sports; nadīyā-nagare — in the city of Nadia; nija guṇagāne — in singing of His own virtues; magana haiyā — absorbed

**1.2.** This is He, and He is this: taking with Him all the same dear companions, He ever sports in the city of Nadia, absorbed in singing of His own virtues.

অপরূপ রূপমাধুরী অমিয়া পিয়াইয়া আগে আপন জনে ।
উনমত মত মতি গতি করু তাহে তারা কেহ কিছু না গণে ॥

*aparūpa rūpamādhurī amiyā piyāiyā āge āpana jane |*
*unamata mata mati gati karu tāhe tārā keha kichu nā gaṇe ||*

*Word for word:* aparūpa rūpa-mādhurī amiyā — the nectar of the wondrous sweetness of form; piyāiyā āge — first giving to drink; āpana jane — to His own; unamata mata — as if mad; mati gati karu — made their minds and steps; tāhe tārā keha kichu nā gaṇe — and they count nothing

**1.3.** First giving His own the nectar of the wondrous sweetness of His form to drink, He made their minds and their steps as if mad — and they count nothing else.

নব নব কুলবতী কুল কুল-কলঙ্ক লাজে তিলাঞ্জলি দিয়া ।
নরহরি সাথী সার কৈল সবে সুখময় গোরা পরাণপিয়া ॥

*naba naba kulabatī kula kula-kalaṅka lāje tilāñjali diyā |*
*narahari sāthī sāra kaila sabe sukhamaya gorā parāṇapiyā ||*

*Word for word:* naba naba kulabatī — ever new noble wives; kula kula-kalaṅka lāje — to family, family disgrace and shame; tilāñjali diyā — giving the last libation; narahari sāthī — Narahari the witness; sāra kaila sabe — all made their essence; sukhamaya gorā — Gora full of joy; parāṇapiyā — the Beloved of their life

**1.4.** Ever new noble wives, giving the last libation to family, to the family's disgrace and to shame, have all made their essence Gora, full of joy, the Beloved of their life — Narahari is witness to it."[^33-2]

[^33-1]: Signature — "Narahari" (narahari sāthī — "Narahari the witness", cf. chapter 31, 13.10). GPT1 — p. 233, no. 169 (scan PDF p. 492); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 169 (catalogue: NG-128).
GCC — kirana 10, pada 25 (ed. 1947, p. 130; scan PDF p. 135), "yathārāga". **Who speaks.** The tenth kirana of GCC is the morning talk of the heavenly women (debaramaṇī)
looking down on Nadia from the sky (chapter 32, note 24); padas 10.25–10.26 (nos. 1–2 of this chapter) close their talk: one tells another "in confidence", and the other asks
to be taught how to come and live in Nadia. GCC readings: "gupate rākhiyā dio cita yāhā kahiye āpana jāniyā tore" ("keeping it secret, attend…"), "nija guṇagaṇe"
("absorbed in His own virtues"). B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^33-2]: "This is He, and He is this; with all the same companions" (1.2): that Gaura is Krishna Himself and that Krishna's companions came with Him to Navadvipa is the
teaching of the tradition (CC, Adi 1 and 3–4; Kavi Karnapura's "Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika" names who among Gaura's companions was whom in Vraja). But the gopis in
Gaura-lila are not townswomen of Nadia in love with Gaura: the Lord Himself came in Radha's bhava to taste Her love (CC, Adi 4), and therefore the Gaudiya tradition
does not accept the speaker's conclusion — that "the young wives of Nadia made Gora, as a nagara, their essence" (introductory note, chapter 27). Rendered as in the
original. "Absorbed in singing of His own virtues" — cf. CB, Madhya (the Lord in bhavavesha sings of Himself). "To give the last libation" (tilāñjali) — to abandon for good.

## 2. Narahari — "gaurāṅgacām̐dera sucāru carita…" (GPT1 p. 233, no. 170; GCC 10.26)
*Nagari-bhava (the heavenly women's talk). The listener, hearing of Gaurangachand's lovely deeds, is filled with joy and cannot hold back tears of
love; joining her palms, she asks to be taught how she might once come to live in Nadia and be a companion of its young playful women, keep Narahari's
Beloved in her heart and be rid of the cruel barrier. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 10, pada 26.*[^33-3]

গৌরাঙ্গচাঁদের সুচারু চরিত শুনি শুনি ধনী পরমসুখী ।
ধৈরজ ধরিতে নারে বারে বারে প্রেমনীরে ভরে যুগল আঁখি ॥

*gaurāṅgacām̐dera sucāru carita śuni śuni dhanī paramasukhī |*
*dhairaja dharite nāre bāre bāre premanīre bhare yugala ām̐khi ||*

*Word for word:* gaurāṅgacām̐dera sucāru carita — of Gaurangachand's lovely deeds; śuni śuni — hearing and hearing; dhanī parama-sukhī — the fair one, filled with joy; dhairaja dharite nāre — cannot hold her composure; bāre bāre — again and again; prema-nīre bhare yugala ām̐khi — both eyes fill with tears of love

**2.1.** Hearing and hearing of Gaurangachand's lovely deeds, the fair one was filled with joy; she cannot hold her composure — again and again both eyes fill with tears of love.

যুড়ি করে কর করিয়া প্রণাম কহে পুনঃ মৃদু মধুর কথা ।
নিজ জন জানি এত দিনে যেন ঘুচাইলে সব হিয়ার ব্যথা ॥

*yuṛi kare kara kariyā praṇāma kahe punaḥ mṛdu madhura kathā |*
*nija jana jāni eta dine yena ghucāile saba hiyāra byathā ||*

*Word for word:* yuṛi kare kara — joining hand to hand; kariyā praṇāma — bowing; kahe punaḥ mṛdu madhura kathā — again speaks soft, sweet words; nija jana jāni — counting me your own; eta dine — at last; yena — as it were; ghucāile saba hiyāra byathā — you have removed all the pain of the heart

**2.2.** Joining her palms and bowing, she again speaks soft, sweet words: "Counting me as your own, at last you have, as it were, taken all the pain from my heart.

নিবেদিয়ে এই নদীয়ানগরে বারেক বসতি কিরূপে পাব ।
আর নব নব রঙ্গিণীগণের সঙ্গিনী হইয়া কিরূপে রব ॥

*nibediye ei nadīyānagare bāreka basati kirūpe pāba |*
*āra naba naba raṅgiṇīgaṇera saṅginī haiyā kirūpe raba ||*

*Word for word:* nibediye — I pray; ei nadīyā-nagare — in this city of Nadia; bāreka basati kirūpe pāba — how might I once find a dwelling; āra — and; naba naba raṅgiṇīgaṇa — of the ever new playful beauties; saṅginī haiyā — becoming a companion; kirūpe raba — how might I live

**2.3.** I pray: how might I once dwell in this city of Nadia? And how might I live as a companion of these ever new playful beauties?

নরহরি-প্রাণপিয়া হিয়া মাঝে রাখিয়া ঘুচাব দারুণ বাধা ।
কহ কহ ওগো উপায় কিরূপে সফল হবে এ সকল সাধা ॥

*narahari-prāṇapiyā hiyā mājhe rākhiyā ghucāba dāruṇa bādhā |*
*kaha kaha ogo upāya kirūpe saphala habe e sakala sādhā ||*

*Word for word:* narahari-prāṇapiyā — the Beloved of Narahari's life; hiyā mājhe rākhiyā — keeping within the heart; ghucāba dāruṇa bādhā — I shall remove the cruel barrier; kaha kaha ogo — tell, tell; upāya kirūpe — by what means; saphala habe — will be fulfilled; e sakala sādhā — all these wishes

**2.4.** Keeping the Beloved of Narahari's life within my heart, I shall be rid of the cruel barrier. Tell me, tell me: by what means will all these wishes be fulfilled?"

[^33-3]: Signature — "Narahari" (narahari prāṇapiyā — "the Beloved of Narahari's life", glossary). GPT1 — p. 233, no. 170 (scan PDF p. 492); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 170
(catalogue: NG-362). GCC — kirana 10, pada 26 (ed. 1947, p. 130; scan PDF p. 135). 2.4 "be fulfilled" follows GPT2 and GCC "saphala" (GPT1 "sakala", a misprint); "barrier" —
GPT1 and GCC "bādhā" (GPT2 "dhām̐dhā", "bewilderment"). The wish of heavenly beings to be born where the Lord reveals His lila is a commonplace of the hagiographies (CB,
Adi: the gods long to be born in Navadvipa to share in the Lord's sankirtana); the "cruel barrier" is that one living in the city of the gods cannot come to Nadia. The
closing pada of the kirana (GCC 10.27) is not in GPT: the fair one told her friend all she had asked, and the heavenly women, trembling and winking at one another,
gave themselves to merry play, gazing at Narahari's Lord; the colophon: "the description of the play of the heavenly women filled with love for Him". B. Nagari-bhava —
see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).

## 3. Narahari — "surapura mājhe basati kariyā…" (GPT1 pp. 233–234, no. 171; GCC 11.4)
*An answer: defence of the chastity of the women of Nadia (the heavenly women's talk; by content not nagari-bhava). The opening of the eleventh
kirana of GCC — "the love-quarrels of the heavenly women". A heavenly woman who has just arrived angrily rebukes her friends: living in the city of the
gods, they have grown proud and slander the women of Nadia; what they describe happens only with the young wives of Vraja, while the wives of Nadia are
faithful to their husbands, do not see another man's face even in a dream, revere their elders; whoever sings of others' disgrace is disgraced. Raga
"yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 11, pada 4.*[^33-4]

সুরপুর মাঝে বসতি করিয়া এত অহঙ্কার করিছ কেনে ।
নদীয়ার নারীগণে পরিবাদ দিতে ভয় কিছু না হয় মনে ॥

*surapura mājhe basati kariyā eta ahaṅkāra karicha kene |*
*nadīyāra nārīgaṇe paribāda dite bhaya kichu nā haya mane ||*

*Word for word:* surapura mājhe basati kariyā — dwelling in the city of the gods; eta ahaṅkāra karicha kene — why such pride; nadīyāra nārīgaṇe — the women of Nadia; paribāda dite — to slander; bhaya kichu nā haya mane — you feel no fear at heart

**3.1.** "Living in the city of the gods, why have you grown so proud? You feel no fear at heart in slandering the women of Nadia!

হায় হায় হেন বিপরীত বাণী শুনিয়া কি আমি সহিতে পারি ।
না জানিয়ে তোমা সবার কি দোষ করিলে এ সব নদ্যার নারী ॥

*hāya hāya hena biparīta bāṇī śuniyā ki āmi sahite pāri |*
*nā jāniye tomā sabāra ki doṣa karile e saba nadyāra nārī ||*

*Word for word:* hāya hāya — alas, alas; hena biparīta bāṇī śuniyā — hearing such perverse words; ki āmi sahite pāri — can I bear it; nā jāniye — I do not know; tomā sabāra ki doṣa karile — what wrong they did to you all; e saba nadyāra nārī — these women of Nadia

**3.2.** Alas, alas! Hearing such perverse words, how can I bear it? I do not know what wrong these women of Nadia have done to you all.

নিজ নিজ রীতিমত জান আনে না জান আনের মরম কথা ।
না বুঝহ কিছু কিসে কিবা হয় তেঁই বলি দেহ ধরিলে বৃথা ॥

*nija nija rītimata jāna āne nā jāna ānera marama kathā |*
*nā bujhaha kichu kise kibā haya tem̐i bali deha dharile bṛthā ||*

*Word for word:* nija nija rītimata — by your own ways; jāna āne — you judge others; nā jāna ānera marama kathā — you do not know others' heart; nā bujhaha kichu — you understand nothing; kise kibā haya — what comes of what; tem̐i bali — so I say; deha dharile bṛthā — in vain you bear a body

**3.3.** You judge others by your own ways and do not know the secret of others' hearts; you understand nothing — what comes of what; so I say: in vain do you bear a body.

যেরূপ কহ সে সম্ভব কেবল ব্রজপুরে নব রমণীগণে ।
নদীয়ার যত যুবতী অতি সুপতিব্রতা জানে জগত জনে ॥

*yerūpa kaha se sambhaba kebala brajapure naba ramaṇīgaṇe |*
*nadīyāra yata yubatī ati supatibratā jāne jagata jane ||*

*Word for word:* yerūpa kaha — what you describe; se sambhaba kebala — is possible only; brajapure naba ramaṇīgaṇe — with the young wives in the city of Vraja; nadīyāra yata yubatī — all the young wives of Nadia; ati supatibratā — most faithful to their husbands; jāne jagata jane — the people of the world know

**3.4.** What you describe is possible only with the young wives in the city of Vraja; but all the young wives of Nadia are the most faithful of the faithful — the whole world knows it.

পরপতি মুখ না দেখে স্বপনে না চলে কভু কুপথ দিয়া ।
না জানে চাতুরি কপট শঠতা সতত সবার সরল হিয়া ॥

*parapati mukha nā dekhe svapane nā cale kabhu kupatha diyā |*
*nā jāne cāturi kapaṭa śaṭhatā satata sabāra sarala hiyā ||*

*Word for word:* parapati mukha — another husband's face; nā dekhe svapane — they do not see even in a dream; nā cale kabhu kupatha diyā — never walk an evil road; nā jāne cāturi kapaṭa śaṭhatā — know no tricks, deceit, guile; satata sabāra sarala hiyā — the hearts of all ever simple

**3.5.** They do not see another husband's face even in a dream, never walk an evil road; they know no tricks, no deceit, no guile — all of them always simple of heart.

ধৈর্য্যবতী কার্য্যে বিচক্ষণা চারু প্রবৃত্তি পরম ধরম পথে ।
অতুলিত কুল লাজ ভয় কভু ভুলি না বৈসয়ে কুজন সাথে ॥

*dhairyyabatī kāryye bicakṣaṇā cāru prabṛtti parama dharama pathe |*
*atulita kula lāja bhaya kabhu bhuli nā baisaye kujana sāthe ||*

*Word for word:* dhairyabatī — steadfast; kārye bicakṣaṇā — skilful in work; cāru prabṛtti — of lovely conduct; parama dharama pathe — on the highest path of dharma; atulita kula lāja bhaya — the matchless family shame and fear; kabhu bhuli — ever, forgetting; nā baisaye kujana sāthe — they do not sit with a bad man

**3.6.** Steadfast, skilful in their work, of lovely conduct — always on the highest path of dharma; mindful of the matchless shame of family and of fear, never, forgetting themselves, do they sit with a bad man.

গুরুজন প্রাণসম বাসে সবে শুভ রাশি গুণ গণিতে নারি ।
মোর মনে এই এ সবারে সদা আঁখি মাঝে রাখি যতন করি ॥

*gurujana prāṇasama bāse sabe śubha rāśi guṇa gaṇite nāri |*
*mora mane ei e sabāre sadā ām̐khi mājhe rākhi yatana kari ||*

*Word for word:* gurujana prāṇasama bāse sabe — all love their elders as life; śubha rāśi guṇa gaṇite nāri — their host of good virtues I cannot count; mora mane ei — in my heart this; e sabāre sadā — them all always; ām̐khi mājhe rākhi — to keep in my eyes; yatana kari — with care

**3.7.** They all love their elders as their life; their auspicious virtues cannot be counted. In my heart there is one thing: always to keep them with care in my eyes.

তাহে কহি সহবাসী জানি বাণী মানিবে নিশ্চয় না কহি আনে ।
পরের কলঙ্ক গায় যেই সেই কলঙ্কী এ নরহরি তা জানে ॥

*tāhe kahi sahabāsī jāni bāṇī mānibe niścaya nā kahi āne |*
*parera kalaṅka gāya yei sei kalaṅkī e narahari tā jāne ||*

*Word for word:* tāhe kahi — so I say; sahabāsī jāni — knowing you are neighbours; bāṇī mānibe niścaya — you will surely accept the words; nā kahi āne — I say nothing else; parera kalaṅka gāya yei — whoever sings another's disgrace; sei kalaṅkī — is disgraced; e narahari tā jāne — this Narahari knows

**3.8.** So I tell you: knowing that you are my neighbours, you will surely accept these words — I say nothing else. Whoever sings of another's disgrace is herself disgraced: this Narahari knows."[^33-5]

[^33-4]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — pp. 233–234, no. 171 (scan PDF pp. 492–493); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 171 (catalogue: NG-129). GCC — kirana 11, pada 4 (ed. 1947, pp. 132–133;
scan PDF pp. 137–138), "yathārāga". **Who speaks.** The eleventh kirana of GCC is headed "Again in the morning — the love-quarrels and so on of the heavenly women"; its
opening is not in GPT: from the sky the heavenly women drink the nectar of Gaura's form as He plays in Shachi's courtyard and argue — some say that the nagaris of
Nadia "have gone mad for the Beloved" and will bring disgrace on themselves, others answer that the wives of Vraja did the same (GCC 11.1); a short pada on the heavenly
women's rapture (11.2); praise of the love of Nadia's young wives — and then "a heavenly woman arrived and, waving her hand, said angrily to all" (11.3). GCC readings:
"nā jāniyā" (3.2), "tem̐i bali" (3.3). B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27); this pada answers it.
[^33-5]: The defender sets Vraja against Nadia: a love that takes no account of husbands and of talk "is possible only with the young wives of Vraja" (3.4), while the women
of Nadia are faithful wives. Gaudiya theology agrees: the parakiya-rasa of the gopis belongs to Vraja (CC, Adi 4), and in Navadvipa the Lord did not accept the worship
of women as a nagara (CB, Adi). The pada is therefore by content not nagari-bhava (like nos. 19–20 of chapter 32); in the heavenly women's dispute, however, her words
will be mocked (nos. 4–10). "Neighbours" (sahabāsī, 3.8) — those who live with her in the city of the gods.

## 4. Narahari — "bhāla bhāla ihā śikhāte habe nā…" (GPT1 p. 234, no. 172; GCC 11.6)
*Nagari-bhava (the heavenly women's quarrel). A mocker answers the defender: they need no teaching — as if they did not know: on earth only the
wives of Nadia are faithful, and in the city of the gods only she; they themselves, forever singing of others' disgrace, will be disgraced, but will not
make her a sharer; how can so clever a woman live among the unchaste? Let her go to Nadia with her dharma and her shame and live among the chaste.
Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 11, pada 6.*[^33-6]

ভাল ভাল ইহা শিখাতে হবে না এ সকল কথা না জানি এ আমি ।
অবনীতে নৈদা নারী পতিব্রতা সুরপুর মাঝে কেবল তুমি ॥

*bhāla bhāla ihā śikhāte habe nā e sakala kathā nā jāni e āmi |*
*abanīte naidā nārī patibratā surapura mājhe kebala tumi ||*

*Word for word:* bhāla bhāla — well, well; ihā śikhāte habe nā — no need to teach this; e sakala kathā nā jāni e āmi — as if I did not know all this; abanīte — on earth; naidā nārī patibratā — the wives of Nadia are faithful; surapura mājhe kebala tumi — in the city of the gods only you

**4.1.** "Well, well! No need to teach us this — as if I did not know it all! On earth only the wives of Nadia are faithful to their husbands, and in the city of the gods only you!

অনুখন পর কলঙ্ক গাইয়া কলঙ্কিনী মোরা সকলে হব ।
ইহা চিন্তা তুমি না করিহ তোমা ইহার ভাগী করিতে না যাব ॥

*anukhana para kalaṅka gāiyā kalaṅkinī morā sakale haba |*
*ihā cintā tumi nā kariha tomā ihāra bhāgī karite nā yāba ||*

*Word for word:* anukhana para kalaṅka gāiyā — ever singing others' disgrace; kalaṅkinī morā sakale haba — we shall all be disgraced; ihā cintā tumi nā kariha — do not you worry about this; tomā ihāra bhāgī karite nā yāba — we shall not make you a sharer in it

**4.2.** We, ever singing of others' disgrace, shall all be disgraced — do not you worry about that: we shall not make you a sharer in it.

তাহে তুমি অতি চতুরা রমণী একা সুরপুরে কিরূপে রবে ।
অসতীর সহ বসতি করিলে অনায়াসে তুমি অসতী হবে ॥

*tāhe tumi ati caturā ramaṇī ekā surapure kirūpe rabe |*
*asatīra saha basati karile anāyāse tumi asatī habe ||*

*Word for word:* tāhe — besides; tumi ati caturā ramaṇī — you, the cleverest woman; ekā surapure kirūpe rabe — how will you live alone in the city of the gods; asatīra saha basati karile — dwelling with the unchaste; anāyāse tumi asatī habe — you will easily become unchaste

**4.3.** Besides, how will you, the cleverest of women, live alone in the city of the gods? Living with the unchaste, you will easily become unchaste yourself.

তাই বলি এই নদীয়ানগরে যাহ নিজ ধর্ম্ম লজ্জাদি লৈয়া ।
নরহরি ইথে সুখী সদা সাবধানে থাক সতী সংহতি হৈয়া ॥

*tāi bali ei nadīyānagare yāha nija dharmma lajjādi laiyā |*
*narahari ithe sukhī sadā sābadhāne thāka satī saṃhati haiyā ||*

*Word for word:* tāi bali — so I say; ei nadīyā-nagare yāha — go to this city of Nadia; nija dharma lajjādi laiyā — taking your dharma, shame and the rest; narahari ithe sukhī — Narahari is glad of it; sadā sābadhāne thāka — be always careful; satī saṃhati haiyā — in the company of the chaste

**4.4.** So I say: go to this city of Nadia, taking your dharma, your shame and the rest. Narahari is glad of it: be always careful, living among the chaste."

[^33-6]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — p. 234, no. 172 (scan PDF p. 493); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 172 (catalogue: NG-363). GCC — kirana 11, pada 6 (ed. 1947, p. 133; scan PDF p. 138);
before it, the short pada 11.5 (not in GPT): hearing this, a heavenly woman versed in rasa laughed inwardly with her own group, exchanged signs with them and spoke.
