The tone of the pada is mocking — rendered as in the original. B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).

## 5. Narahari — "hera āisa ogo patibratā saha…" (GPT1 p. 234, no. 173; GCC 11.7)
*Nagari-bhava (the heavenly women's quarrel). Another calls her friend: why talk with a "faithful wife"? Joy is among equals; not all heavenly women
are adroit — as the owl does not see the sun; the secret stories of Nadia's young wives she will not reveal for shame; but our Gora — beautiful, good —
speaks to no one with raised face, is always careful on the path of dharma, knows nothing of such things — and such a Lord of Narahari they bewitched
with signs from the corners of their eyes. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 11, pada 7.*[^33-7]

হের আইস ওগো পতিব্রতা সহ কি লাগি কহিব এ সকল কথা ।
সমানে সমানে সুখ উপজয় অসমান সনে বাড়য়ে ব্যথা ॥

*hera āisa ogo patibratā saha ki lāgi kahiba e sakala kathā |*
*samāne samāne sukha upajaya asamāna sane bāṛaye byathā ||*

*Word for word:* hera āisa ogo — come here, friend; patibratā saha — with a "faithful wife"; ki lāgi kahiba e sakala kathā — why say all this; samāne samāne — among equals; sukha upajaya — joy arises; asamāna sane — with unequals; bāṛaye byathā — pain grows

**5.1.** "Come here, friend: why say all this to a 'faithful wife'? Among equals joy arises; with unequals pain grows.

সুরনারী হৈলে সবে কি সুঘড় ইহা কখন না করিহ মনে ।
ভানুকর যৈছে না হেরে উলুক এরূপ জানিহ অনেক জনে ॥

*suranārī haile sabe ki sughaṛa ihā kakhana nā kariha mane |*
*bhānukara yaiche nā here uluka erūpa jāniha aneka jane ||*

*Word for word:* suranārī haile — being heavenly women; sabe ki sughaṛa — are all adroit; ihā kakhana nā kariha mane — never think so; bhānukara yaiche nā here ulūka — as the owl does not see the sun's rays; erūpa jāniha aneka jane — know many to be so

**5.2.** Being born heavenly women — are all of us then adroit? Never think so: as the owl does not see the sun — so, know, are many.

নদীয়ার যত যুবতী নবীনা প্রবীণা কে সম ভুবন মাঝে ।
তা সবার অতি গুপত কাহিনী বেকত করিতে নারিএ লাজে ॥

*nadīyāra yata yubatī nabīnā prabīṇā ke sama bhubana mājhe |*
*tā sabāra ati gupata kāhinī bekata karite nārie lāje ||*

*Word for word:* nadīyāra yata yubatī — the young wives of Nadia; nabīnā prabīṇā — the young and the experienced; ke sama bhubana mājhe — who equals them in the world; tā sabāra ati gupata kāhinī — their most secret stories; bekata karite nārie lāje — I cannot reveal for shame

**5.3.** The young wives of Nadia — the young and the experienced — who equals them in the world? Their secret stories I cannot reveal for shame.

এই দেখ দেখ আমাদের প্রাণজীবন সুন্দর সুজন গোরা ।
মুখ তুলি কথা না কহে কাহুরে অপরূপ রীতি পরম ভোরা ॥

*ei dekha dekha āmādera prāṇajībana sundara sujana gorā |*
*mukha tuli kathā nā kahe kāhure aparūpa rīti parama bhorā ||*

*Word for word:* ei dekha dekha — look, look here; āmādera prāṇajībana — the life of our life; sundara sujana gorā — beautiful, good Gora; mukha tuli kathā nā kahe kāhure — speaks to no one with raised face; aparūpa rīti — wondrous way; parama bhorā — wholly absorbed

**5.4.** Look, look here: our Gora, the life of our life, beautiful and good, speaks to no one with raised face; wondrous is His way, He is wholly absorbed within.

ধরম-পথেতে সদা সাবধান কি কব এসব কিছু না জানে ।
হেন নরহরিনাথে ভুলাইল ঠারাঠারি করি আঁখির কোণে ॥

*dharama-pathete sadā sābadhāna ki kaba esaba kichu nā jāne |*
*hena naraharināthe bhulāila ṭhārāṭhāri kari ām̐khira koṇe ||*

*Word for word:* dharama-pathete sadā sābadhāna — ever careful on the path of dharma; ki kaba — what shall I say; esaba kichu nā jāne — He knows nothing of this; hena naraharināthe — such a Lord of Narahari; bhulāila — they bewitched; ṭhārāṭhāri kari ām̐khira koṇe — signalling with the corners of their eyes

**5.5.** Always careful on the path of dharma — what shall I say! — He knows nothing of all this. And such a Lord of Narahari they bewitched, signalling from the corners of their eyes."[^33-8]

[^33-7]: Signature — "Narahari" (naraharinātha — "Narahari's Lord"). GPT1 — p. 234, no. 173 (scan PDF p. 493); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 173 (catalogue: NG-130; the catalogue's "paratatratā" is an
OCR error for "patibratā"). GCC — kirana 11, pada 7 (ed. 1947, p. 134; scan PDF p. 139), "anyā ca — yathārāga" ("and another"). 5.1 in GCC "ki lāgi kahicha" — "why are you
saying all this to a faithful wife". "The owl does not see the sun" (5.2) — a proverb for blindness to the obvious. B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the
section (chapter 27).
[^33-8]: The Lord's portrait in 5.4–5.5 is the same as in the hagiographies: He speaks to no one with raised face and is "always careful on the path of dharma" (CB, Adi: in this
incarnation the Lord did not look at women and allowed no jesting with them; cf. nos. 19–20 of chapter 32). The words "they bewitched Him" are the speaker's slander of
the women of Nadia, rendered as in the original; the tradition's answer — introductory note (chapter 27).

## 6. Narahari — "ki baliba ogo nadīyāra naba…" (GPT1 p. 235, no. 174; GCC 11.8)
*Nagari-bhava (the heavenly women's quarrel). Another: the young wives of Nadia do not reveal their secrets, are always gracious outwardly, well-behaved
before mother-in-law and sister-in-law, yet gain their ends so that no one notices, and secretly try to win the Moon of Nadia; she herself saw how they
bewitched Him — and there was no one to restrain the women: Narahari was not with Gauranga. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** —
GCC, kirana 11, pada 8.*[^33-9]

কি বলিব ওগো নদীয়ার নব-যুবতীগণের যেরূপ রীতি ।
অন্তরের কথা না করে বেকত বাহিরেতে সদা উদার অতি ॥

*ki baliba ogo nadīyāra naba-yubatīgaṇera yerūpa rīti |*
*antarera kathā nā kare bekata bāhirete sadā udāra ati ||*

*Word for word:* ki baliba ogo — what shall I say, friend; nadīyāra naba-yubatīgaṇera yerūpa rīti — the ways of the young wives of Nadia; antarera kathā nā kare bekata — they do not reveal what is within; bāhirete sadā udāra ati — outwardly always most gracious

**6.1.** "What shall I say, friend, of the ways of the young wives of Nadia! They do not reveal what is within, but outwardly they are always most gracious.

শাশুড়ী ননদ তা সবার পাশে থাকয়ে সতত সুজন হৈয়া ।
যে বিষয়ে সবে প্রশংসয়ে তাহা করয়ে অনেক যতন পাইয়া ॥

*śāśuṛī nanada tā sabāra pāśe thākaye satata sujana haiyā |*
*ye biṣaye sabe praśaṃsaye tāhā karaye aneka yatana pāiyā ||*

*Word for word:* śāśuṛī nanada tā sabāra pāśe — before mother-in-law and sister-in-law; thākaye satata sujana haiyā — they always behave well; ye biṣaye sabe praśaṃsaye — whatever everyone praises; tāhā karaye aneka yatana pāiyā — that they do with great care

**6.2.** Before mother-in-law and sister-in-law they always behave well; whatever everyone praises, that they do with great care.

কত কত মতে সাধে নিজ কাজ কেহ কোনদিন লখিতে নারে ।
নদীয়ার চাঁদে অধীন করিতে অধিক গুপত হইয়া ফিরে ॥

*kata kata mate sādhe nija kāja keha konadina lakhite nāre |*
*nadīyāra cām̐de adhīna karite adhika gupata haiyā phire ||*

*Word for word:* kata kata mate — in many ways; sādhe nija kāja — they gain their ends; keha kona dina lakhite nāre — no one can ever notice; nadīyāra cām̐de adhīna karite — to win the Moon of Nadia; adhika gupata haiyā phire — they go about most secretly

**6.3.** In many ways they gain their ends — no one can ever notice; to win the Moon of Nadia they go about most secretly.

আপনার আঁখে দেখিনু সেদিন কত ভঙ্গী করি মোহিত কৈল ।
কেবা নিবারিবে নারীগণে নরহরি গৌরাঙ্গের সঙ্গে না ছিল ॥

*āpanāra ām̐khe dekhinu sedina kata bhaṅgī kari mohita kaila |*
*kebā nibāribe nārīgaṇe narahari gaurāṅgera saṅge nā chila ||*

*Word for word:* āpanāra ām̐khe dekhinu sedina — with my own eyes I saw that day; kata bhaṅgī kari — with so many graceful poses; mohita kaila — they bewitched; kebā nibāribe nārīgaṇe — who would restrain the women; narahari gaurāṅgera saṅge nā chila — Narahari was not with Gauranga

**6.4.** With my own eyes I saw that day how, with so many graceful poses, they bewitched [Him]. Who would restrain the women? Narahari was not with Gauranga."

[^33-9]: Signature — "Narahari", merged with the speech (6.4). GPT1 — p. 235, no. 174 (scan PDF p. 494); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 174 (catalogue: NG-131). GCC — kirana 11, pada 8 (ed. 1947,
p. 134; scan PDF p. 139), "anyā ca — yathārāga". "Narahari was not with Gauranga": in GCC the poet usually accompanies the Lord and leads Him away from what is improper
(GCC 11.11, 11.14 — see notes 18 and 19); here the speaker seems to explain why this time "there was no one to restrain the women". As in no. 5, the words about
"bewitching" are the speaker's surmise; in the following padas (nos. 7–8) the mockers themselves describe how the Lord turns away and leaves. B. Nagari-bhava — see the
introductory note to the section (chapter 27).

## 7. Narahari — "nadīyāte kata kata e kautuka…" (GPT1 p. 235, no. 175; GCC 11.9)
*Nagari-bhava (the heavenly women's quarrel). The next one confirms it mockingly: she knows well how "faithful" these young chaste ones are: the other
day, standing under a young kadamba, she saw Gora walking alone in the late afternoon toward Murari Gupta's quarter; the "faithful wives" were coming
along with a fearsome mother-in-law and sister-in-law — and yet, finding Gorachand on a near path, they contrived to stand in His way, signalled to Him
and did not keep the end of the sari over the breast; and Narahari's Lord, lowering His face in shame, stepped aside. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution:
probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 11, pada 9.*[^33-10]

নদীয়াতে কত কত এ কৌতুক তাহে তাহা কত কহিবে তুমি ।
যেরূপ এ যত যুবতী সতী সুপতিব্রতা তাহা জানিএ আমি ॥

*nadīyāte kata kata e kautuka tāhe tāhā kata kahibe tumi |*
*yerūpa e yata yubatī satī supatibratā tāhā jānie āmi ||*

*Word for word:* nadīyāte kata kata e kautuka — how many such pranks in Nadia; tāhe tāhā kata kahibe tumi — how many will you tell; yerūpa e yata yubatī satī supatibratā — how faithful all these young chaste ones are; tāhā jānie āmi — that I know

**7.1.** "How many such pranks there are in Nadia — how many will you tell! And how 'faithful to their husbands' all these young chaste ones are — that I know.

সে দিবস নিজ আঁখে নিরখিনু রহিয়া নবীন কদম্বতলে ।
মুরারিগুপ্তের পাড়াপানে গোরা একা চলি যায় বিকাল বেলে ॥

*se dibasa nija ām̐khe nirakhinu rahiyā nabīna kadambatale |*
*murāriguptera pāṛāpāne gorā ekā cali yāya bikāla bele ||*

*Word for word:* se dibasa — that day; nija ām̐khe nirakhinu — I saw with my own eyes; rahiyā nabīna kadamba-tale — standing under a young kadamba; murāri-guptera pāṛā-pāne — toward Murari Gupta's quarter; gorā ekā cali yāya — Gora goes alone; bikāla bele — in the late afternoon

**7.2.** That day I saw with my own eyes, standing under a young kadamba: Gora was walking alone in the late afternoon toward Murari Gupta's quarter.

সে সময় পতিব্রতাগণ আসে বিষম শাশুড়ী ননদ সাথে ।
তবু সে দাঁড়ায় ভঙ্গী করি ছলে গোরাচাঁদে পাঞা নিকট পথে ॥

*se samaya patibratāgaṇa āse biṣama śāśuṛī nanada sāthe |*
*tabu se dām̐ṛāya bhaṅgī kari chale gorācām̐de pāñā nikaṭa pathe ||*

*Word for word:* se samaya — at that hour; patibratāgaṇa āse — the "faithful wives" come; biṣama śāśuṛī nanada sāthe — with a fearsome mother-in-law and sister-in-law; tabu se dām̐ṛāya — still they stand; bhaṅgī kari chale — swaying, on a pretext; gorācām̐de pāñā nikaṭa pathe — finding Gorachand on a near path

**7.3.** At that hour the 'faithful wives' were coming with a fearsome mother-in-law and sister-in-law — and still, finding Gorachand on a near path, they stood there on a pretext, swaying their bodies.

ঠারি বারে বারে তারে ভুলাইয়া আধ পটাঞ্চল না রাখি উরে ।
নরহরিনাথ লাজে অধোমুখ একভিত হৈয়া রহয়ে দূরে ॥

*ṭhāri bāre bāre tāre bhulāiyā ādha paṭāñcala nā rākhi ure |*
*naraharinātha lāje adhomukha ekabhita haiyā rahaye dūre ||*

*Word for word:* ṭhāri bāre bāre — signalling again and again; tāre bhulāiyā — beguiling Him; ādha paṭāñcala nā rākhi ure — not keeping even half the sari's end on the breast; naraharinātha — Narahari's Lord; lāje adhomukha — face lowered in shame; ekabhita haiyā — stepping aside; rahaye dūre — stays far off

**7.4.** Signalling to Him again and again, luring Him, not keeping even half the end of the sari over the breast… And Narahari's Lord, lowering His face in shame, stepped aside and stood far off."[^33-11]

[^33-10]: Signature — "Narahari" (naraharinātha). GPT1 — p. 235, no. 175 (scan PDF p. 494); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 175 (catalogue: NG-364). GCC — kirana 11, pada 9 (ed. 1947, pp. 134–135;
scan PDF pp. 139–140), "anyā ca — yathārāga". GCC readings: "jāniye āmi" (7.1), "murārī-guptera" (7.2), "pāyā" (7.3), "lubhāiye" (7.4, "luring"; GPT1 "bhulāiyā", "beguiling"),
"eka bhita hayā". Murari Gupta's quarter (pāṛā) — Murari's house in Navadvipa, which the Lord visited (CB, Madhya; cf. chapter 31, no. 3). B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory
note to the section (chapter 27).
[^33-11]: 7.3–7.4 — an open motif of enticement; rendered exactly, without softening. The Lord's response, described by the mocker herself — He lowers His face in shame and
moves away (7.4) — is the same as in the hagiographies: in Navadvipa the Lord did not look at women and avoided their company (CB, Adi). The speaker's words about
"faithful wives" are mockery; the tradition accepts neither this slander nor the worship of Gaura as a nagara (introductory note, chapter 27).

## 8. Narahari — "ki kahiba ogo e sakala kathā…" (GPT1 p. 235, no. 176; GCC 11.10)
*Nagari-bhava (the heavenly women's quarrel). Another: it is shameful even to speak of it — the beautiful Moon of Nadia ever trembles before young women;
once Gora walked alone with an elephant's gait, looking at no one — and the "faithful wives" stood on His path and shot unseen sharp arrows from the
corners of their eyes; one, holding a pomegranate, said: "To whom shall I give this wondrous fruit?", another: "He whose body is like new gold will take
it Himself, unasked"; Narahari's Lord, holding His composure, finished His errand in shame and quickly went home. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution:
probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 11, pada 10.*[^33-12]

কি কহিব ওগো এ সকল কথা কহিতে অধিক সঙ্কোচ বাসি ।
যুবতীর ভয়ে কাঁপয়ে সতত সুজন সুন্দর নৈদার শশী ॥

*ki kahiba ogo e sakala kathā kahite adhika saṅkoca bāsi |*
*yubatīra bhaye kām̐paye satata sujana sundara naidāra śaśī ||*

*Word for word:* ki kahiba ogo — what shall I say, friend; e sakala kathā kahite — to speak of these things; adhika saṅkoca bāsi — I feel great shame; yubatīra bhaye — for fear of young women; kām̐paye satata — ever trembles; sujana sundara — good and beautiful; naidāra śaśī — the Moon of Nadia

**8.1.** "What shall I say, friend: it is most shameful even to speak of these things. Before young women the good and beautiful Moon of Nadia ever trembles.

না জানি সে দিন কিবা কাজে একা চলিলা কুঞ্জর-গমনে গোরা ।
কারুপানে নাহি নিরখে বারেক অতিশয় মৃদু পরম ভোরা ॥

*nā jāni se dina kibā kāje ekā calilā kuñjara-gamane gorā |*
*kārupāne nāhi nirakhe bāreka atiśaya mṛdu parama bhorā ||*

*Word for word:* nā jāni — I do not know; se dina kibā kāje — on what errand that day; ekā calilā kuñjara-gamane gorā — Gora went alone with an elephant's gait; kāru-pāne nāhi nirakhe bāreka — did not look at anyone even once; atiśaya mṛdu — most gentle; parama bhorā — wholly absorbed

**8.2.** I do not know on what errand that day Gora went alone with an elephant's gait; He did not look at anyone even once — most gentle, wholly absorbed within.

সেই পথে পতিব্রতা নারীগণে রহিয়া চাহয়ে গৌরাঙ্গপানে ।
অলখিত খরতর শর পুনঃ হানয়ে চঞ্চল নয়ন-কোণে ॥

*sei pathe patibratā nārīgaṇe rahiyā cāhaye gaurāṅgapāne |*
*alakhita kharatara śara punaḥ hānaye cañcala nayana-koṇe ||*

*Word for word:* sei pathe — on that road; patibratā nārīgaṇe — the "faithful wives"; rahiyā cāhaye gaurāṅga-pāne — standing, gaze at Gauranga; alakhita kharatara śara — unseen sharp arrows; punaḥ hānaye — again they shoot; cañcala nayana-koṇe — from restless corners of the eyes

**8.3.** On that road the 'faithful wives' stood looking at Gauranga — again and again they shot unseen sharp arrows from the restless corners of their eyes.

কেহ সুদাড়িম্ব ফল লৈয়া করে কহে এ অপূর্ব্ব কাহারে দিব ।
কেহ কহে নব হেমতনু যাঁর অযাচিত তেঁহ আপনি নিব ॥

*keha sudāṛimba phala laiyā kare kahe e apūrvva kāhāre diba |*
*keha kahe naba hematanu yām̐ra ayācita tem̐ha āpani niba ||*

*Word for word:* keha sudāṛimba phala laiyā kare — one, holding a fine pomegranate in hand; kahe — says; e apūrva kāhāre diba — to whom shall I give this wondrous (fruit); keha kahe — another says; naba hema-tanu yām̐ra — whose body is new gold; ayācita tem̐ha āpani niba — He will take it Himself, unasked

**8.4.** One, holding a fine pomegranate in her hand, says: 'To whom shall I give this wondrous [fruit]?' Another says: 'He whose body is like new gold will take it Himself, unasked.'

এইরূপ বাণী ভণে আনে আনে তাহা শুনি থির কেবা বা রহে ।
নরহরি পহুঁ ধৃতি ধরি লাজে কাজ সারি শীঘ্র গেলেন গৃহে ॥

*eirūpa bāṇī bhaṇe āne āne tāhā śuni thira kebā bā rahe |*
*narahari pahum̐ dhṛti dhari lāje kāja sāri śīghra gelena gṛhe ||*

*Word for word:* eirūpa bāṇī bhaṇe āne āne — such words they spoke to one another; tāhā śuni — hearing it; thira kebā vā rahe — who would stay calm; narahari pahum̐ — Narahari's Lord; dhṛti dhari — holding His composure; lāje — in shame; kāja sāri — finishing the errand; śīghra gelena gṛhe — quickly went home

**8.5.** Such words they spoke to one another; who, hearing them, would stay calm? Narahari's Lord, holding His composure, in shame quickly finished His errand and went home."[^33-13]

"no. 175" is an error, corrected at the collation of chapter 29). GCC — kirana 11, pada 10 (ed. 1947, p. 135; scan PDF p. 140), "anyā ca — yathārāga". In GCC, after 8.3 there is one

"Ever trembles before young women" (8.1), "did not look at anyone" (8.2), "in shame quickly went home" (8.5) — again the Lord's strictness, as in the hagiographies (CB, Adi;
notes 8 and 11). The mocker tells it to show the "nature" of the women of Nadia; rendered as in the original.

## 9. Narahari — "ki baliba iha sabāre nirakhi…" (GPT1 p. 236, no. 177; GCC 11.15)
*Nagari-bhava (the heavenly women's quarrel). The mocker goes on: the fame of the ways of Nadia's wives has filled the world — mothers-in-law, sisters-in-law,
husbands always scold them and every day fervently pray to Old Shiva, fearing disgrace; they keep them at home, do not let them on the road, let them go to
the Suradhuni only with a sister-in-law; the neighbour-women restrain them unceasingly, no one trusts them in anything; hearing such reproach, Narahari dies of
shame every day. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 11, pada 15.*[^33-14]

কি বলিব ইহ সবারে নিরখি কহিল কত কি সহিতে পারি ।
নদীয়ার নারীগণের যে রীত রহিয়াছে তাহা জগত ভরি ॥

*ki baliba iha sabāre nirakhi kahila kata ki sahite pāri |*
*nadīyāra nārīgaṇera ye rīta rahiyāche tāhā jagata bhari ||*

*Word for word:* ki baliba — what shall I say; iha sabāre nirakhi — looking at them all; kahila kata — how much she said; ki sahite pāri — can one bear it; nadīyāra nārīgaṇera ye rīta — what the ways of the women of Nadia are; rahiyāche tāhā jagata bhari — it fills the whole world

**9.1.** "What shall I say! How much she said, looking at them — can one bear it? What the ways of the women of Nadia are — the whole world is full of it:

যা সবারে সদা শাশুড়ী ননদ পতি আদি সব পাড়য়ে গালি ।
প্রতিদিন বুড়াশিবে পূজে কত আদরে কলঙ্ক হইবে বলি ॥

*yā sabāre sadā śāśuṛī nanada pati ādi saba pāṛaye gāli |*
*pratidina buṛāśibe pūje kata ādare kalaṅka haibe bali ||*

*Word for word:* yā sabāre — whom all; sadā — always; śāśuṛī nanada pati ādi saba — mother-in-law, sister-in-law, husband and the rest; pāṛaye gāli — scold; pratidina — every day; buṛā-śibe pūje kata ādare — worship Old Shiva with great fervour; kalaṅka haibe bali — saying "there will be disgrace"

**9.2.** mother-in-law, sister-in-law, husband and the rest always scold them all; every day they pray with great fervour to Old Shiva — 'there will be disgrace!'

অনুখন ঘরে রাখয়ে যতনে বাহির হইতে না দেয় পথে ।
যদি সুরধুনী সিনাইতে চাহে তবে সে ননদী চলয়ে সাথে ॥

*anukhana ghare rākhaye yatane bāhira haite nā deya pathe |*
*yadi suradhunī sināite cāhe tabe se nanadī calaye sāthe ||*

*Word for word:* anukhana ghare rākhaye yatane — they constantly keep them carefully at home; bāhira haite nā deya pathe — do not let them out on the road; yadi suradhunī sināite cāhe — if one wants to bathe in the Suradhuni; tabe se nanadī calaye sāthe — the sister-in-law goes with her

**9.3.** They always keep them carefully at home, do not let them go out on the road; and if one wants to bathe in the Suradhuni — the sister-in-law goes with her.

পড়সিনী অনিবার নিবারয়ে কেহ না প্রত্যয় করয় কাজে ।
আর কব কি সে গঞ্জনা শুনিয়া নরহরি নিতি মরয়ে লাজে ॥

*paṛasinī anibāra nibāraye keha nā pratyaya karaya kāje |*

*Word for word:* paṛasinī anibāra nibāraye — the neighbour-women restrain unceasingly; keha nā pratyaya karaya kāje — no one trusts them in any matter; āra kaba ki — what more shall I say; se gañjanā śuniyā — hearing that reproach; narahari niti maraye lāje — Narahari dies of shame daily

**9.4.** The neighbour-women restrain them unceasingly; no one trusts them in any matter. What more shall I say? Hearing that reproach, Narahari dies of shame every day."

[^33-14]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — p. 236, no. 177 (scan PDF p. 495); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 177 (catalogue: NG-133). GCC — kirana 11, pada 15 (ed. 1947, p. 138; scan PDF p. 143),

(or the women themselves) fervently worship Old Shiva (buṛāśiba, a revered murti of Shiva in Navadvipa; chapter 31, note 53), fearing that "there will be disgrace". 9.4 "Narahari

## 10. Narahari — "surapure kebā nā jāne nadīyā…" (GPT1 p. 236, no. 178; GCC 11.17)
*Nagari-bhava (the heavenly women's quarrel). The defender, frightened, has fallen silent (GCC 11.16); then a playful one, glancing at her own group, says:
in the city of the gods everyone knows the ways of the nagaris of Nadia — why be vainly angry with her? What she said is secret; and taking her hand and
praising her, she goes on gently: the ways of Nadia's young wives are past counting; no one looks at the bracelet on her own hand in a mirror — here is the
jewel in Ai's house: if she came on the astrologer's word, why does she stare unblinking at Gora, playing with her brows, tremble, let her clothes and
ornaments slip, break into gooseflesh and sweat? Narahari's Lord is the husband of them all. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** —
GCC, kirana 11, pada 17.*[^33-15]

সুরপুরে কেবা না জানে নদীয়া-নাগরীগণের যেরূপ রীতি ।
তাহাতে এরূপ বৃথা ক্রোধ কেন করিছ তোমরা ইহার প্রতি ॥

*surapure kebā nā jāne nadīyā-nāgarīgaṇera yerūpa rīti |*
*tāhāte erūpa bṛthā krodha kena karicha tomarā ihāra prati ||*

*Word for word:* surapure kebā nā jāne — who in the city of the gods does not know; nadīyā-nāgarīgaṇera yerūpa rīti — what the ways of the nagaris of Nadia are; tāhāte — then; erūpa bṛthā krodha — such vain anger; kena karicha tomarā ihāra prati — why do you bear it toward her

**10.1.** "In the city of the gods who does not know what the ways of the nagaris of Nadia are? Why then are you so vainly angry with her?

কি বলিব ইহ যে কিছু কহিল সে অতি গূঢ় তা কেহ না জানে ।
ধৈরজ ধরিয়া থাকহ সকলে আমি যে কহি তা শুন যতনে ॥

*ki baliba iha ye kichu kahila se ati gūṛha tā keha nā jāne |*
*dhairaja dhariyā thākaha sakale āmi ye kahi tā śuna yatane ||*

*Word for word:* ki baliba — what shall I say; iha ye kichu kahila — what she said; se ati gūṛha — is most secret; tā keha nā jāne — no one knows it; dhairaja dhariyā thākaha sakale — have patience, all; āmi ye kahi — what I say; tā śuna yatane — listen to it with care

**10.2.** What shall I say: what she said is most secret; no one knows it. Have patience, all of you, and listen with care to what I say."

এইরূপ নিজগণে নিরখিয়া ধরিয়া তুরিতে তাহার করে ।
কত কত মতে প্রশংসা করিয়া কহে মৃদু মৃদু রসের ভরে ॥

*eirūpa nijagaṇe nirakhiyā dhariyā turite tāhāra kare |*
*kata kata mate praśaṃsā kariyā kahe mṛdu mṛdu rasera bhare ||*

*Word for word:* eirūpa — thus; nijagaṇe nirakhiyā — glancing at her own group; dhariyā turite tāhāra kare — quickly taking her hand; kata kata mate praśaṃsā kariyā — praising her in many ways; kahe mṛdu mṛdu — speaks very softly; rasera bhare — full of rasa

**10.3.** So, glancing at her own group, she quickly took her hand, praised her in many words and speaks very softly, full of rasa:

নদীয়ার যত যুবতী তাদের ভঙ্গী কেবা কত কহিতে পারে ।
কত দিন কত কৌতুক আপন আঁখে দেখি তাহা না কহি কারে ॥

*nadīyāra yata yubatī tādera bhaṅgī kebā kata kahite pāre |*

*Word for word:* nadīyāra yata yubatī — the young wives of Nadia; tādera bhaṅgī — their ways; kebā kata kahite pāre — who can tell how many; kata dina kata kautuka — many days, many pranks; āpana ām̐khe dekhi — seeing with my own eyes; tāhā nā kahi kāre — I tell no one

**10.4.** "The ways of the young wives of Nadia — who can tell how many? Many days I have seen many pranks with my own eyes — and I tell no one.

সে কথা থাকুক কেহ নিজ কর-কঙ্কণ না দেখে দর্পণ দিয়া ।
এই দেখ আই ভবনের মণি প্রাতঃকালে আইল কি লাগি ধাঞা ॥

*se kathā thākuka keha nija kara-kaṅkaṇa nā dekhe darpaṇa diyā |*
*ei dekha āi bhabanera maṇi prātaḥkāle āila ki lāgi dhāñā ||*

*Word for word:* se kathā thākuka — let that be; keha nija kara-kaṅkaṇa nā dekhe darpaṇa diyā — no one looks at the bracelet on her own hand with a mirror; ei dekha — look here; āi bhabanera maṇi — the jewel in Ai's house; prātaḥkāle āila ki lāgi dhāñā — why did she come running in the morning

**10.5.** Let that be; no one looks at the bracelet on her own hand in a mirror: look here — the jewel in Ai's house: why has she come running in the morning?

যদি বল শুভ দৈবজ্ঞবচনে নিজ কাজে আইলা আইয়ের কাছে ।
তবে কেন অনিমিখ আঁখে গোরাপানে ভ্রূ নাচাঞা চাহিয়া আছে ॥

*yadi bala śubha daibajñabacane nija kāje āilā āiyera kāche |*
*tabe kena animikha ām̐khe gorāpāne bhrū nācāñā cāhiyā āche ||*

*Word for word:* yadi bala — if you say; śubha daibajña-bacane — on the auspicious word of the astrologer; nija kāje āilā āiyera kāche — she came to Ai on her own business; tabe kena — then why; animikha ām̐khe — with unblinking eyes; gorā-pāne — at Gora; bhrū nācāñā — making her brows dance; cāhiyā āche — is gazing

**10.6.** If you say: on the auspicious word of the astrologer she came to Ai on her own business — then why, playing with her brows, does she gaze unblinking at Gora?

আর ঘন ঘন কাঁপে তনু বাস ভূষণ খসিছে চুলের খোঁপা ।
পুলকের ঘটা ঘরম চুইছে সঘনে দুলিছে কাণের চাঁপা ॥

*āra ghana ghana kām̐pe tanu bāsa bhūṣaṇa khasiche culera khom̐pā |*
*pulakera ghaṭā gharama cuiche saghane duliche kāṇera cām̐pā ||*

*Word for word:* āra ghana ghana kām̐pe tanu — and the body trembles again and again; bāsa bhūṣaṇa khasiche — clothes and ornaments slip; culera khom̐pā — the knot of hair (comes loose); pulakera ghaṭā — a mass of gooseflesh; gharama cuiche — sweat trickles; saghane duliche kāṇera cām̐pā — the champa-earrings sway again and again

**10.7.** And her body trembles again and again, her clothes and ornaments slip, the knot of her hair comes loose; she is all gooseflesh, sweat trickles, her champa-earrings sway again and again.

এ কাজ কে করে বল বল ইহা কারু বা প্রত্যয় না হবে কেনে ।
নরহরিপহুঁ পতি সবাকার ইথে না সন্দেহ করিহ মনে ॥

*e kāja ke kare bala bala ihā kāru bā pratyaya nā habe kene |*
*naraharipahum̐ pati sabākāra ithe nā sandeha kariha mane ||*

*Word for word:* e kāja ke kare — who does such things; bala bala — say, say; ihā kāru vā pratyaya nā habe kene — why should anyone not believe it; naraharipahum̐ — Narahari's Lord; pati sabākāra — the husband (lord) of all; ithe nā sandeha kariha mane — have no doubt of this

**10.8.** Who does such things — say, say? Why should anyone not believe it? Narahari's Lord is the husband of them all: have no doubt of this."[^33-16]

[^33-15]: Signature — "Narahari" (naraharipahum̐). GPT1 — p. 236, no. 178 (scan PDF p. 495); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 178 (catalogue: NG-134). GCC — kirana 11, pada 17 (ed. 1947, p. 139; scan
PDF p. 144), "yathārāga"; before it, the short pada 11.16 (not in GPT): the playful heavenly women said so much that the fair one took fright and could not utter a word; seeing this,
a playful one, unable to contain her glee, glanced at her group and spoke slyly. 10.5 — GPT1 and GPT2 "āi bhabanera maṇi" ("the jewel in Ai's house"), GCC "āi-bhabane ramaṇī"
("the woman in Ai's house"); GPT rendered. "No one looks at the bracelet on her hand in a mirror" — a proverb: the obvious needs no proof. The astrologer who sends the daughters-in-law
to Shachi — chapter 32, no. 1 (GCC 9.2). B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^33-16]: "Narahari's Lord is the husband of them all" (naraharipahum̐ pati sabākāra, 10.8): pati — "husband", "lord". In Vaishnava theology Krishna is the Lord and the sole enjoyer
(CC, Adi 5), but on the heroine's lips the word means "the beloved husband of the nagaris of Nadia" — this is the gaura-nagari notion in its plain form, which the tradition does
not accept: Gaura came in Radha's bhava as a devotee, not as the enjoyer (CC, Adi 4; introductory note, chapter 27). Rendered exactly. The signs the heroine lists (trembling,
gooseflesh, sweat, 10.7) are the sattvika-bhavas, the marks of love in the poetics of rasa. The kirana closes with padas not in GPT: the fair one, hearing these words, let go of
her doubts, and the one versed in rasa took her into her circle; all the heavenly women, gazing at Gaurahari playing in Shachi's courtyard among His devotees, cast off shame
and began to sing of His deeds (GCC 11.18); the closing stanza is the poet's prayer: "Lord full of rasa, with Your companions keep me in Nadia" (11.19).

## 11. Narahari — "śuna śuna ei kālikāra kathā…" (GPT1 pp. 236–237, no. 179; GCC 11.14, first part)
*Nagari-bhava (a heavenly woman's story). One, "casting off shame", tells her friend what happened yesterday: many young women joyfully took counsel — one
urges going at once with pitchers for water, for the Moon of Nadia will come to the ghat on the Suradhuni; others advise dressing up, adorning the hair with
flowers, rubbing the face with kunkuma, lining the eyes, putting on necklaces like a snare, ringing anklets and a belled girdle — so that Gora may lose His
composure. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 11, pada 14 (first half).*[^33-17]

শুন শুন এই কালিকার কথা কহি এ তোমারে নিলজী হৈয়া ।
অনেক যুবতী অতিশয় সুখে করয়ে যুকতি যতন পাঞা ॥

*śuna śuna ei kālikāra kathā kahi e tomāre nilajī haiyā |*
*aneka yubatī atiśaya sukhe karaye yukati yatana pāñā ||*

*Word for word:* śuna śuna — listen, listen; ei kālikāra kathā — what happened yesterday; kahi e tomāre — I shall tell you; nilajī haiyā — casting off shame; aneka yubatī — many young women; atiśaya sukhe — with the greatest joy; karaye yukati — took counsel; yatana pāñā — eagerly

**11.1.** "Listen, listen: I shall tell you what happened yesterday, casting off shame. Many young women, with the greatest joy, eagerly took counsel.

কেহ কহে ওগো না কর বিলম্ব কলসি লইয়া জলকে চল ।
নদীয়ার শশী সুরধুনীঘাটে আসিবে আসিতে সময় হৈল ॥

*keha kahe ogo nā kara bilamba kalasi laiyā jalake cala |*
*nadīyāra śaśī suradhunīghāṭe āsibe āsite samaya haila ||*

*Word for word:* keha kahe — one says; ogo nā kara bilamba — oh, do not delay; kalasi laiyā jalake cala — take your pitcher, let us go for water; nadīyāra śaśī — the Moon of Nadia; suradhunī-ghāṭe āsibe — will come to the Suradhuni ghat; āsite samaya haila — it is time for Him to come

**11.2.** One says: 'Oh, do not delay, take your pitcher — let us go for water: the Moon of Nadia will come to the ghat on the Suradhuni — it is time for Him to come.'

কেহ কহে কেন এরূপে যাইব বেশ বিরচহ বিবিধ ভাঁতি ।
যার ছটালেশে সে নব-কিশোর যেন তিলআধ না ধরে ধৃতি ॥

*keha kahe kena erūpe yāiba beśa biracaha bibidha bhām̐ti |*
*yāra chaṭāleśe se naba-kiśora yena tilaādha nā dhare dhṛti ||*

*Word for word:* keha kahe — another says; kena erūpe yāiba — why go like this; beśa biracaha bibidha bhām̐ti — dress in many ways; yāra chaṭāleśe — by a spark of whose radiance; se naba-kiśora — the young Kishora; yena tila-ādha nā dhare dhṛti — that He keeps not even half a sesame of composure

**11.3.** Another says: 'Why go like this? Dress yourselves in every way — so that by a spark of that radiance the young Kishora cannot keep His composure even by half a sesame seed.'

কেহ কহে কেশ-বেণী বনাইয়া বিবিধ কুসুম সাজাও শিরে ।
যার সুগন্ধিতে যেন জিতেন্দ্রিয় বারেক নাসা না ফিরাতে পারে ॥

*keha kahe keśa-beṇī banāiyā bibidha kusuma sājāo śire |*
*yāra sugandhite yena jitendriya bāreka nāsā nā phirāte pāre ||*

*Word for word:* keha kahe — another says; keśa-beṇī banāiyā — braiding the hair; bibidha kusuma sājāo śire — adorn the head with many flowers; yāra sugandhite — by whose fragrance; yena jitendriya — so that even the conqueror of the senses; bāreka nāsā nā phirāte pāre — cannot once turn away His face (lit. "nose")

**11.4.** Another says: 'Braid your hair, adorn your heads with many flowers — so that by their fragrance even the One who has conquered the senses cannot turn His face away.'

কেহ কহে মুখ মাজহ কুঙ্কুমে কাজরে উজোর করহ আঁখি ।
যেন গৌরাঙ্গের নয়ন ভুলায়ে সুললিত নব-ভঙ্গিমা দেখি ॥

*keha kahe mukha mājaha kuṅkume kājare ujora karaha ām̐khi |*
*yena gaurāṅgera nayana bhulāye sulalita naba-bhaṅgimā dekhi ||*

*Word for word:* keha kahe — another says; mukha mājaha kuṅkume — rub the face with kunkuma; kājare ujora karaha ām̐khi — brighten the eyes with kajal; yena gaurāṅgera nayana bhulāye — so that Gauranga's eyes are enchanted; sulalita naba-bhaṅgimā dekhi — seeing the charming new graces

**11.5.** Another says: 'Rub your faces with kunkuma, line your eyes brightly with kajal — so that Gauranga's eyes are enchanted, seeing the charming new graces.'

কেহ কহে নানা মণিময়-মালা গলে পর চারু ফাঁদের পারা ।
যেন অনায়াসে বন্দী হয় ইথে নদীয়ার শশী সুন্দর গোরা ॥

*keha kahe nānā maṇimaya-mālā gale para cāru phām̐dera pārā |*
*yena anāyāse bandī haya ithe nadīyāra śaśī sundara gorā ||*

*Word for word:* keha kahe — another says; nānā maṇimaya-mālā gale para — put on necklaces of many jewels; cāru phām̐dera pārā — like a lovely snare; yena anāyāse bandī haya ithe — so that in it is easily caught; nadīyāra śaśī sundara gorā — the Moon of Nadia, beautiful Gora

**11.6.** Another says: 'Put on necklaces of many jewels, like a lovely snare — so that in it the Moon of Nadia, beautiful Gora, may easily be caught.'

কেহ কহে মণি নূপুর-কিঙ্কিণী মুখরিত দেখি পরহ আনি ।
যেন নরহরিনাথ-শ্রুতিযুগ মুগধে মধুর শবদ শুনি ॥

*keha kahe maṇi nūpura-kiṅkiṇī mukharita dekhi paraha āni |*
*yena naraharinātha-śrutiyuga mugadhe madhura śabada śuni ||*

*Word for word:* keha kahe — another says; maṇi nūpura-kiṅkiṇī — jewelled anklets and belled girdle; mukharita dekhi paraha āni — choose ringing ones, bring and wear; yena naraharinātha-śrutiyuga — so that the ears of Narahari's Lord; mugadhe — are charmed; madhura śabada śuni — hearing the sweet sound

**11.7.** Another says: 'Bring and put on ringing anklets and a jewelled, belled girdle — so that the ears of Narahari's Lord are charmed, hearing the sweet sound.'"[^33-18]

[^33-17]: Signature — "Narahari" (naraharinātha, 11.7). GPT1 — pp. 236–237, no. 179 (scan PDF pp. 495–496); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 179 (catalogue: NG-135; the catalogue line is from the middle
of the pada). GCC — kirana 11, pada 14 (ed. 1947, pp. 137–138; scan PDF pp. 142–143), "anyā ca — yathārāga". **GPT has split one pada of GCC into two** (nos. 179 and 180, nos. 11–12 of
this chapter); the last couplet of no. 179 in GCC reads "yena gaura-śrutiyuga mugadhaye madhura madhura śabada śuni" ("so that Gaura's ears are charmed…"): the poet's name
("naraharinātha") stands here only in GPT, and this "signature" is the compiler's work. GCC readings: "kahiye tomāre nilaji haiyā", "yugati yatana pāyā" (11.1), "ghāṭa āsiba"
(11.2), "sājāha śire", "phirāite" (11.4), "ujara" (11.5). B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^33-18]: "The One who has conquered the senses" (jitendriya, 11.4) is Gaura Himself: even the speakers acknowledge the restraint they hope to shake. Before this pada GCC has three
padas not taken into GPT (the most outspoken of the kirana): the jests and improper antics of women at the Ganga ghat in the Lord's presence — and Narahari, seeing the
impropriety, hurries to finish the bath and leads Gauranga home (GCC 11.11); the Lord, abashed at their words, covers His face with the end of His cloth (11.12); hearing their
gossip, the Lord in fear, returning home, performs expiation (prayashchitta, 11.13). The author of GCC himself thus always shows the Lord strict and untouched (cf. CB, Adi).

## 12. Narahari — "nānā kathā kahi āne āne sabe…" (GPT1 p. 237, no. 180; GCC 11.14, conclusion)
*Nagari-bhava (a heavenly woman's story, concluded). Dressed up, the women with pitchers on their hips come out of their houses and go to the Suradhuni,
holding hands and talking of rasa; on the way they see Gaura — but He, a great pandita, walks with bowed head, keeping His composure; suspecting something
amiss, He looked back once — and they showered Him with the arrows of their glances; the Jewel of virtues, abashed, thought of disgrace; the nagaris, keeping
His form in their hearts, worshipped Him with love. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 11, pada 14 (second half; the last
couplet differs in GPT).*[^33-19]

নানা কথা কহি আনে আনে সবে সাজিলেন সাজ উলস হৈয়া ।
প্রতি জনে জনে দরপণে মুখ নিরখয়ে ত্বরা তাম্বূল খাঞা ॥

*nānā kathā kahi āne āne sabe sājilena sāja ulasa haiyā |*
*prati jane jane darapaṇe mukha nirakhaye tvarā tāmbūla khāñā ||*

*Word for word:* nānā kathā kahi āne āne — saying much to one another; sabe sājilena sāja — all dressed themselves; ulasa haiyā — eagerly; prati jane jane — each one; darapaṇe mukha nirakhaye — looks at her face in a mirror; tvarā tāmbūla khāñā — hastily chewing betel

**12.1.** Having said much to one another, all eagerly dressed themselves; each looks at her face in a mirror, hastily chewing betel.

বিচিত্র বসন পরি সবে অতি চঞ্চল কলসি লইয়া কাঁখে ।
এ ঘর সে ঘর হইতে বাহির হইল কত না মনের সুখে ॥

*bicitra basana pari sabe ati cañcala kalasi laiyā kām̐khe |*
*e ghara se ghara haite bāhira haila kata nā manera sukhe ||*

*Word for word:* bicitra basana pari — putting on bright clothes; sabe ati cañcala — all very lively; kalasi laiyā kām̐khe — with pitchers on their hips; e ghara se ghara haite — from this house and that; bāhira haila — came out; kata nā manera sukhe — with what joy of heart

**12.2.** Putting on bright clothes, all very lively, pitchers on their hips — from this house and that they came out, with what joy of heart!

হাসিয়া হাসিয়া সমবয়ঃ সব রসিয়া সে পতিব্রতার ঘটা ।
সুরধুনী-তীর আলো করি চলে কিবা অপরূপ রূপের ছটা ॥

*hāsiyā hāsiyā samabayaḥ saba rasiyā se patibratāra ghaṭā |*
*suradhunī-tīra ālo kari cale kibā aparūpa rūpera chaṭā ||*

*Word for word:* hāsiyā hāsiyā — laughing and laughing; samabayaḥ saba — all of an age; rasiyā — full of rasa; se patibratāra ghaṭā — that throng of "faithful wives"; suradhunī-tīra ālo kari cale — go, lighting up the Suradhuni bank; kibā aparūpa rūpera chaṭā — what wondrous radiance of beauty

**12.3.** Laughing and laughing, the girls of an age — all that throng of "faithful wives", full of rasa — go, lighting up the bank of the Suradhuni: what wondrous radiance of beauty!

রসের আবেশে কর ধরাধরি ঈষৎ ঈষৎ ভঙ্গীতে চাঞা ।
কত ছলে রস-কাহিনী কহয়ে পথমাঝে গৌর দরশ পাঞা ॥

*rasera ābeśe kara dharādhari īṣat īṣat bhaṅgīte cāñā |*
*kata chale rasa-kāhinī kahaye pathamājhe gaura daraśa pāñā ||*

*Word for word:* rasera ābeśe — in the rapture of rasa; kara dharādhari — holding hands; īṣat īṣat bhaṅgīte cāñā — glancing with slight graces; kata chale rasa-kāhinī kahaye — telling tales of rasa in many ways; patha-mājhe gaura daraśa pāñā — on the path catching sight of Gaura

**12.4.** In the rapture of rasa, holding hands, glancing with slight graces, telling tales of rasa in many ways — on the path they caught sight of Gaura.

তাহে গৌরবর পরম পণ্ডিত নতশিরে রহে ধৈরজ ধরি ।
অতি বিপরীত ক্রিয়া অনুমানি বারেক চাহিল তা পানে ফিরি ॥

*tāhe gaurabara parama paṇḍita nataśire rahe dhairaja dhari |*
*ati biparīta kriyā anumāni bāreka cāhila tā pāne phiri ||*

*Word for word:* tāhe — then; gaurabara — Gaura the best; parama paṇḍita — a great pandita; nataśire rahe — goes with bowed head; dhairaja dhari — keeping composure; ati biparīta kriyā anumāni — suspecting most improper conduct; bāreka cāhila tā pāne phiri — once looked back at them

**12.5.** But Gaura, the best of all, a great pandita, walked with bowed head, keeping His composure; suspecting something most improper, He looked back at them only once.

সে সময় সব সঘন কটাক্ষ-বাণ বরিষয়ে নয়ান-কোণে ।
অমনি লজ্জিত গুণমণি পুনঃ কলঙ্কের ভয় ভাবয়ে মনে ॥

*se samaya saba saghana kaṭākṣa-bāṇa bariṣaye nayāna-koṇe |*
*amani lajjita guṇamaṇi punaḥ kalaṅkera bhaya bhābaye mane ||*

*Word for word:* se samaya — at that moment; saba — all; saghana kaṭākṣa-bāṇa bariṣaye — shower thick arrows of glances; nayāna-koṇe — from the corners of the eyes; amani lajjita — at once abashed; guṇa-maṇi — the Jewel of virtues; punaḥ kalaṅkera bhaya bhābaye mane — again thinks with fear of disgrace

**12.6.** At that moment they all showered Him thickly with the arrows of glances from the corners of their eyes; and at once, abashed, the Jewel of virtues again thought with fear of disgrace.

নাগরী সকলে গৌরাঙ্গ-মূরতি হিয়ায় রাখিয়া প্রেমে পূজিল ।
নরহরি কহে নদীয়া-নগরে নাগরী নাগর মিলন হৈল ॥

*nāgarī sakale gaurāṅga-mūrati hiyāya rākhiyā preme pūjila |*
*narahari kahe nadīyā-nagare nāgarī nāgara milana haila ||*

*Word for word:* nāgarī sakale — all the nagaris; gaurāṅga-mūrati hiyāya rākhiyā — keeping Gauranga's form in the heart; preme pūjila — worshipped with love; narahari kahe — Narahari says; nadīyā-nagare — in the city of Nadia; nāgarī nāgara milana haila — the meeting of the nagaris and the nagara came to pass

**12.7.** All the nagaris, keeping Gauranga's form in their hearts, worshipped Him with love. Narahari says: in the city of Nadia the meeting of the nagaris and the nagara came to pass.[^33-20]

[^33-19]: Signature — "Narahari" (only in GPT, see note 20). GPT1 — p. 237, no. 180 (scan PDF p. 496); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 180 (catalogue: NG-365). GCC — the second half of pada 11.14
(ed. 1947, p. 138; scan PDF p. 143), without a heading of its own; its first line in GCC is "eirūpa kata kahi āne āne sājilena sabe ulasa haiyā" ("Having said so much…"; in GPT
"nānā kathā kahi…"). 12.3 "full of rasa" follows GCC "rasiyā" (GPT1 and GPT2 "basiyā", "sitting" — a misprint); 12.5 GPT1 "rahe" ("remains", "goes"). GCC readings: "cāyā", "pāyā",
"īṣata" (12.4), "bhaye bhābaye" (12.6). B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^33-20]: **The last couplet of GPT (12.7) is different in GCC**: "What happened — what shall I say! Only Narahari was with Gauranga: that is why propriety and honour were kept; otherwise
there would have been trouble on the road" (ye haila tāhā ki kaba kebala narahari chila gaurāṅga-sāthe, tem̐i se sarama bharama rahila, nahile biṣama haita pathe). Here GPT — the
only time in the section — does not soften GCC but heightens it: in place of the words that the companion preserved propriety stands the formula "the meeting of the nagaris and
the nagara". GPT's text is translated, the GCC reading is in VAR. The "meeting" in the pada itself is only a glance on the road and the worship of the Lord's form in the heart; the
Lord walks with bowed head and fears disgrace (12.5–12.6), as in the hagiographies (CB, Adi). The notion of Gaura as a nagara meeting with nagaris is not accepted by the
tradition (introductory note, chapter 27).

## 13. Narahari — "niśi parabhāte nibhṛta nikete…" (GPT1 pp. 93–94, sect. 2.4, no. 2; BR)
*Nagari-bhava (a dream). The marriage with Vishnupriya, the morning of the adhivasa day. At dawn, in a secluded house, young wives make merry; one, full of
rasa, tells her friends a dream: the young Moon of Nadia, glancing at her sidelong, smilingly invited her to come in the morning for the water rite at His
wedding, and then, taking her hand, embraced her again and again; the fragrance of His body is on her still; today is the adhivasa — quickly dress and go to
meet Narahari's Lord. Raga todi. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in BR (twelfth wave).*[^33-21]

নিশি পরভাতে নিভৃত নিকেতে কুলবধূকুল বিলসে রঙ্গে ।
কেহ কারু প্রতি কহে ইতি উতি সৌরভ ভরল অলস অঙ্গে ॥

*niśi parabhāte nibhṛta nikete kulabadhūkula bilase raṅge |*
*keha kāru prati kahe iti uti saurabha bharala alasa aṅge ||*

*Word for word:* niśi parabhāte — at the close of night; nibhṛta nikete — in a secluded house; kulabadhūkula — a throng of young wives; bilase raṅge — makes merry; keha kāru prati kahe iti uti — one says this and that to another; saurabha bharala alasa aṅge — fragrance has filled the languid body

**13.1.** At the close of night, in a secluded house, a throng of young wives makes merry; one says this and that to another: fragrance has filled [her] languid body.

শুনি রসাবেশে ভণে নিশি শেষে স্বপনে সে নব-নদীয়া-বিধু ।
তেরছ নয়ানে চাহি আমা পানে হাসি মিশে যেন বরিষে মধু ॥

*śuni rasābeśe bhaṇe niśi śeṣe svapane se naba-nadīyā-bidhu |*
*teracha nayāne cāhi āmā pāne hāsi miśe yena bariṣe madhu ||*

*Word for word:* śuni — hearing; rasābeśe — full of rasa; bhaṇe — she says; niśi śeṣe — at night's end; svapane — in a dream; se naba-nadīyā-bidhu — that young Moon of Nadia; terachha nayāne — sidelong; cāhi āmā pāne — glancing at me; hāsi miśe — mixed with a smile; yena bariṣe madhu — as if raining honey

**13.2.** Hearing it, she, full of rasa, says: "At the close of night, in a dream, that young Moon of Nadia, glancing at me sidelong — as if raining honey mixed with a smile —

ধীরে ধীরে কহে মোর এ বিবাহে জল সাইবারে আইবে প্রাতে ।
এত কহি করে ধরি বারে বারে আলিঙ্গিয়ে কত কৌতুক তাতে ॥

*dhīre dhīre kahe mora e bibāhe jala sāibāre āibe prāte |*
*eta kahi kare dhari bāre bāre āliṅgiye kata kautuka tāte ||*

*Word for word:* dhīre dhīre kahe — very softly says; mora e bibāhe — at this wedding of Mine; jala sāibāre — for the water rite; āibe prāte — come in the morning; eta kahi — saying this; kare dhari — taking my hand; bāre bāre āliṅgiye — embraces again and again; kata kautuka tāte — what a jest in that

**13.3.** says very softly: 'At My wedding come in the morning for the water rite.' Saying this, He takes my hand and embraces me again and again — what a jest in that!

সে তনু-সৌরভ পরশে এ সব তো সবে কহিয়ে নিলজী হৈয়া ।
অধিবাস আজি বেগে চল সাজি নরহরিনাথে মিলহ গিয়া ॥

*se tanu-saurabha paraśe e saba to sabe kahiye nilajī haiyā |*
*adhibāsa āji bege cala sāji naraharināthe milaha giyā ||*

*Word for word:* se tanu-saurabha paraśe — from the touch of that body's fragrance; e saba — all this; to sabe kahiye — I tell you; nilajī haiyā — casting off shame; adhibāsa āji — today is the adhivasa; bege cala sāji — quickly dress and go; naraharināthe milaha giyā — go and meet Narahari's Lord

**13.4.** All this is from the touch of that body's fragrance; I tell you, casting off shame. Today is the adhivasa — quickly dress and go to meet Narahari's Lord."[^33-22]

[^33-21]: Signature — "Narahari" (naraharinātha). GPT1 — pp. 93–94, sect. 2.4 ("the second marriage"), no. 2 (todi; scan PDF pp. 352–353); GPT2 — sect. 2.4, no. 2 (catalogue: NG-046). BR — twelfth
wave (ed. 1912, p. 799; ed. 1960, vv. 1403–1406), "punaśca — toṛī", in the series of wedding songs that Narahari Chakravarti gives when Ishana shows Srinivasa the house of Jagannatha
Mishra (cf. chapter 21, note 29, and the opening of chapter 22); the preceding pada (GPT 2.4 no. 1 — chapter 21, no. 14) is the night before the adhivasa, when the women of Nadia
wait for morning to go to Shachi for the water rite. The pada is not in GCC. BR readings: "iki ati" (13.1), "svapane se saba nadīyā-bidhu" (BR-1960; 13.2), "hāsi-miṣe" ("as if under
cover of a smile"), "āliṅgaye" (13.3). The water rite (jala sāi) — a wedding rite of married women (chapter 21, note 3). B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section
(chapter 27).
[^33-22]: The young wife's dream with an embrace (13.3) is the motif of sambhoga in a dream, as in the eighth kirana of GCC (chapter 31); rendered exactly. It is the heroine's imagining:
in His lila the Lord did not touch women and in Navadvipa did not look at them (CB, Adi), and His wedding with Vishnupriya — His eternal consort, the Lord's Bhu-shakti (chapter 21,
note 30) — is told by Vrindavana Dasa without any nagari motif (CB, Adi 15). The Gaudiya tradition does not accept the worship of Gaura in the nagari mood (introductory note,
chapter 27).

## 14. Narahari — "gaura baraja-kiśora bara…" (GPT1 p. 94, sect. 2.4, no. 3; BR)
*Nagari-bhava (anuraga). The same morning: ever new women, full of anuraga for Gaura, the best of the youths of Vraja, tremble; they hastily dress, line
their eyes, rub their faces with kunkuma, bow to their elders, who gladly let them go to Shachi's house; countless throngs hurry along the road. Vrajabuli.
Raga todi. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in BR (twelfth wave).*[^33-23]

গৌর বরজ-কিশোর বর অনুরাগে নব নব নারী ।
বিপুল পুলকিত গাত গরগর ধিরজ ধরই না পারি ॥

*gaura baraja-kiśora bara anurāge naba naba nārī |*
*bipula pulakita gāta garagara dhiraja dharai nā pāri ||*

*Word for word:* gaura — Gaura; baraja-kiśora bara — the best of the youths of Vraja; anurāge — with anuraga; naba naba nārī — ever new women; bipula pulakita gāta — bodies thrilling with gooseflesh; garagara — overwhelmed; dhiraja dharai nā pāri — cannot keep their composure

**14.1.** Gaura is the best of the youths of Vraja; with anuraga for Him come ever new women: their bodies thrill with gooseflesh, they are overwhelmed and cannot keep their composure.

বেগি বিরচি সুবেশ কাজরে আঁজি কঞ্জ-নয়ান ।
মুকুর কর গহি পেখি কুঙ্কুম সে মাজি মঞ্জু বয়ান ॥

*begi biraci subeśa kājare ām̐ji kañja-nayāna |*
*mukura kara gahi pekhi kuṅkuma se māji mañju bayāna ||*

*Word for word:* begi biraci subeśa — quickly making fine attire; kājare ām̐ji kañja-nayāna — lining the lotus eyes with kajal; mukura kara gahi — taking mirrors in hand; pekhi — looking; kuṅkuma se māji — rubbing with kunkuma; mañju bayāna — the lovely faces

**14.2.** Quickly dressing in fine attire, lining their lotus eyes with kajal, taking mirrors in hand and looking into them, they rubbed their lovely faces with kunkuma.

গমন সময় বিচারি গুরুজন চরণ বন্দন কেল ।
শ্রীশচী-গৃহ-গমনে সো সব উলসে অনুমতি দেল ॥

*gamana samaya bicāri gurujana caraṇa bandana kela |*
*śrīśacī-gṛha-gamane so saba ulase anumati dela ||*

*Word for word:* gamana samaya bicāri — judging it time to go; gurujana caraṇa bandana kela — bowed at the feet of the elders; śrī-śacī-gṛha-gamane — for going to Sri Shachi's house; so saba — they all (the elders); ulase anumati dela — gladly gave leave

**14.3.** Judging it time to go, they bowed at the feet of their elders — and these gladly gave them leave to go to the house of Sri Shachi.

পরশ পররস বরষে ঘন ঘন ভবন তেজি তুরন্ত ।
ভণত নরহরি পন্থগত কত যূথ গণই ন অন্ত ॥

*paraśa pararasa baraṣe ghana ghana bhabana teji turanta |*
*bhaṇata narahari panthagata kata yūtha gaṇai na anta ||*

*Word for word:* paraśa pararasa — the rasa of touch (sense unclear); baraṣe ghana ghana — pours like rain again and again; bhabana teji turanta — hastily leaving the houses; bhaṇata narahari — says Narahari; panthagata kata — how many on the path; yūtha gaṇai na anta — the throngs cannot be counted

**14.4.** Again and again the rasa of touch pours down like rain; hastily leaving their houses — says Narahari — how many on the path! The throngs cannot be counted.[^33-24]

[^33-23]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — p. 94, sect. 2.4, no. 3 (todi; scan PDF p. 353); GPT2 — sect. 2.4, no. 3 (catalogue: NG-047). BR — twelfth wave (ed. 1912, p. 800; ed. 1960, vv. 1407–1410),
"punaśca — toṛī". The pada is not in GCC. 14.2 "ām̐ji" ("lining"; GPT1 "āji", without candrabindu); BR readings: "aṅgarāge" (BR-1960, 14.1 — "in unguents"; GPT and BR-1912 "anurāge"),
"kuṅkumame" (14.2). The following padas of GPT (nos. 4–6 — the women's procession to Shachi, their bow, Shachi's blessing) were translated in chapter 21 (nos. 15–16; no. 4 bears the
signature of Ghanashyama, outside the corpus). B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^33-24]: "The best of the youths of Vraja" (baraja-kiśora-bara, 14.1): that Gaura is Krishna Himself, the youth of Vraja, is the teaching of the tradition (CC, Adi 1–4); the women's anuraga
for Him is rendered as the author has it. Here the elders themselves let the young wives go — to the wedding rite at Shachi's house (14.3); the motif of deceiving the elders
(chapters 29–30) is absent. 14.4 "paraśa pararasa baraṣe ghana ghana" — the sense of the line is unclear (the same in all witnesses; perhaps "a thrill as if from a touch"); rendered literally.

## 15. Narahari — "naba nadīyā-nāgarī gori bhori baya thori…" (GPT1 p. 95, sect. 2.4, no. 7; BR; GCC 9.22)
*Nagari-bhava. In Shachi's house the young nagaris of Nadia secretly gaze at the Beloved and tremble at Madana's arrow: one thinks she has become shameless,
another cannot hold back a smile, a third speaks of love, half covered by her veil; others make signs, wipe their friends' faces, whisper aside; so all the noble
chaste wives were immersed in the ocean of the rasa of prema for Gaura and gave the Lord of their life their life, their soul and their youth. Raga "yatharaga".
**Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in BR (twelfth wave) and in GCC (kirana 9, pada 22).*[^33-25]

নব নদীয়া-নাগরী গোরি ভোরি বয় থোরি কি চরিত বুঝিব আনে ।
অতি অলখিত পিয়া পানে চাহি হিয়া থরহরি কাঁপে মদন-বাণে ॥

*naba nadīyā-nāgarī gori bhori baya thori ki carita bujhiba āne |*
*ati alakhita piyā pāne cāhi hiyā tharahari kām̐pe madana-bāṇe ||*

*Word for word:* naba nadīyā-nāgarī — the young nagaris of Nadia; gori — fair; bhori — enraptured; baya thori — young in years; ki carita bujhiba āne — who else could understand their ways; ati alakhita — quite unnoticed; piyā pāne cāhi — gazing at the Beloved; hiyā tharahari kām̐pe — the heart trembles; madana-bāṇe — at Madana's arrow

**15.1.** The young nagaris of Nadia — fair, enraptured, young in years — who else could understand their ways? Gazing quite unnoticed at the Beloved, their hearts tremble at Madana's arrow.

কেহ ভাবি মনে মনে ভণে আজু বুঝি নিলজ হইনু সবার পাশে ।
কেহ কারুপ্রতি ঠারি নারে সম্বরিতে অমনি ঈষৎ ঈষৎ হাসে ॥

*keha bhābi mane mane bhaṇe āju bujhi nilaja hainu sabāra pāśe |*
*keha kāruprati ṭhāri nāre sambarite amani īṣat īṣat hāse ||*

*Word for word:* keha bhābi mane mane bhaṇe — one, thinking to herself, says; āju bujhi — today, it seems; nilaja hainu sabāra pāśe — I have become shameless before all; keha kāru prati ṭhāri — another, signalling to a friend; nāre sambarite — cannot restrain herself; amani īṣat īṣat hāse — at once smiles a little

**15.2.** One, thinking to herself, says: "Today, it seems, I have become shameless before all." Another, signalling to a friend, cannot restrain herself — and at once smiles a little.

কেহ কারু করে ধরি ধীরে ধীরে সাধে অধিক আনন্দে উমড়ে হিয়া ।
কেহ কারু প্রতি কহে পীরিতি-কাহিনী অলপ ঘুঙটে ঘুঙট দিয়া ॥

*keha kāru kare dhari dhīre dhīre sādhe adhika ānande umaṛe hiyā |*
*keha kāru prati kahe pīriti-kāhinī alapa ghuṅaṭe ghuṅaṭa diyā ||*

*Word for word:* keha kāru kare dhari — one, taking a friend's hand; dhīre dhīre sādhe — softly pleads; adhika ānande umaṛe hiyā — the heart overflows with great joy; keha kāru prati kahe pīriti-kāhinī — another tells a friend of love; alapa ghuṅaṭe ghuṅaṭa diyā — half covering herself with the veil

**15.3.** One, taking a friend's hand, softly pleads — great joy overflows her heart; another tells a friend of love, half covering herself with her veil.

কেহ কারু প্রতি করে করেতে সঙ্কেত কত কত কথা উপজে মনে ।
কেহ কারু মতি থির করে কত ভয় দেখাইয়া চারু নয়ান-কোণে ॥

*keha kāru prati kare karete saṅketa kata kata kathā upaje mane |*
*keha kāru mati thira kare kata bhaya dekhāiyā cāru nayāna-koṇe ||*

*Word for word:* keha kāru prati kare karete saṅketa — one makes signs to a friend, hand in hand; kata kata kathā upaje mane — how many words arise in the mind; keha kāru mati thira kare — another steadies a friend's mind; kata bhaya dekhāiyā — threatening in every way; cāru nayāna-koṇe — with the lovely corner of the eye

**15.4.** One makes signs to a friend, hand in hand — how many words arise in the mind! Another, threatening in every way with the lovely corner of her eye, keeps her friend in her senses.

কেহ নিজ ধৈর্য্য জানাইতে কারু মুখ মুছে পটাঞ্চল যতনে লৈঞা ।
কেহ করি কাণাকাণি জানি বিপরীত এক ভিতে থাকে গুপত হৈঞা ॥

*keha nija dhairyya jānāite kāru mukha muche paṭāñcala yatane laiñā |*
*keha kari kāṇākāṇi jāni biparīta eka bhite thāke gupata haiñā ||*

*Word for word:* keha nija dhairya jānāite — one, to show her composure; kāru mukha muche — wipes a friend's face; paṭāñcala yatane laiñā — carefully taking the sari's end; keha kari kāṇākāṇi — another, whispering ear to ear; jāni biparīta — knowing it improper; eka bhite thāke gupata haiñā — stands hidden aside

**15.5.** One, to show her own composure, carefully wipes a friend's face with the end of her sari; another, after a whisper in the ear, knowing it improper, stands hidden aside.

এইরূপে যত কুলবতী সতী গৌর-প্রেম-রসার্ণবে সবে মগন হৈলা ।
নরহরি কি কহিব প্রাণনাথে প্রাণ জীবন যৌবন সঁপিয়া দিলা ॥

*eirūpe yata kulabatī satī gaura-prema-rasārṇabe sabe magana hailā |*
*narahari ki kahiba prāṇanāthe prāṇa jībana yaubana sam̐piyā dilā ||*

*Word for word:* eirūpe yata kulabatī satī — thus all the noble chaste wives; gaura-prema-rasārṇabe — in the ocean of the rasa of prema for Gaura; sabe magana hailā — were all immersed; narahari ki kahiba — what shall Narahari say; prāṇanāthe — to the Lord of their life; prāṇa jībana yaubana — life, soul and youth; sam̐piyā dilā — they gave over

**15.6.** So all the noble chaste wives were immersed in the ocean of the rasa of prema for Gaura. What shall Narahari say: to the Lord of their life they gave their life, their soul and their youth.[^33-26]

[^33-25]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — p. 95, sect. 2.4, no. 7 ("yathārāga"; scan PDF p. 354); GPT2 — sect. 2.4, no. 7 (catalogue: NG-050). BR — twelfth wave (ed. 1912, pp. 801–802; ed. 1960,
vv. 1423–1428), "yathā — rāga", after Shachi's blessing (GPT 2.4 no. 6 = chapter 21, no. 16). GCC — kirana 9, pada 22 (ed. 1947, pp. 116–117; scan PDF pp. 121–122): there it is a morning at
Shachi's house in the ninth kirana ("the wishes of the nagaris of Navadvipa"), after Shachi has blessed the townswomen (GCC 9.21); after it comes the closing pada of the kirana with
the poet's prayer for devotion to the feet of the nagaris of Nadia (9.23; chapter 32, note 22). The series GPT 2.4 nos. 4–7 = GCC 9.18, 9.19, 9.21, 9.22 stands both in BR and in GCC: Chakravarti
placed the same padas both in BR's wedding narrative and in the morning scenes of GCC. GCC readings: "gori bibhori" (15.1), "madana-bāṇe", "umaṛe", "ogo" and others; "gaura-premarasārṇabe"
(15.6). B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^33-26]: "Tremble at Madana's arrow" (15.1), "gave the Lord of their life their life, their soul and their youth" (15.6) — the nagari motif in its plain form; rendered exactly. According to
Krishnadasa Kaviraja, prema is the desire for Krishna's happiness, not one's own (CC, Adi 4); in the hagiographies the women of Navadvipa honour Gaura and Shachi as devotees (CB, Adi),
and the tradition does not accept the worship of Gaura as a nagara (introductory note, chapter 27). "Chaste wives" (kulabatī satī) — so the poet calls them here and in GCC.

## 16. Narahari — "āhā mari ki madhura rīti…" (GPT1 p. 101, sect. 2.4, no. 21; BR)
*Nagari-bhava; wishes (manoratha). At the wedding: the nagaris of Nadia, gazing at Gorachand, lose their composure; one whispers: "What is family shame to
me — day and night I shall be with Gora, I shall hold Him to my breast"; another: "Rapt in that rasa, I shall watch the wedding and, slipping on a pretext into
the chamber (in BR: the bridal chamber), touch the golden body"; with such wishes, together with Narahari, they enter the house of Sanatana Mishra. Raga
"yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in BR (twelfth wave).*[^33-27]

আহা মরি কি মধুর রীতি ।
নদীয়া-নাগরী গোরাচাঁদে হেরি ধরিতে না রয়ে ধৃতি ॥ ধ্রু ॥

*āhā mari ki madhura rīti |*
*nadīyā-nāgarī gorācām̐de heri dharite nā raye dhṛti || dhru ||*

*Word for word:* āhā mari — ah; ki madhura rīti — how sweet the ways; nadīyā-nāgarī — the nagaris of Nadia; gorācām̐de heri — gazing at Gorachand; dharite nā raye dhṛti — cannot keep their composure; dhru — refrain

**16.1.** Ah, how sweet these ways! The nagaris of Nadia, gazing at Gorachand, cannot keep their composure. *(Refrain)*

কেহ ধীরি ধীরি কেহ ভঙ্গী করি কি কাজ কুলের লাজে ।
নিশিদিশি গোরাসহ বিলসিব রাখিব বুকের মাঝে ॥

*keha dhīri dhīri keha bhaṅgī kari ki kāja kulera lāje |*
*niśidiśi gorāsaha bilasiba rākhiba bukera mājhe ||*

*Word for word:* keha dhīri dhīri — one very softly; keha bhaṅgī kari — another, swaying; ki kāja kulera lāje — what is family shame to us; niśi-diśi — night and day; gorā-saha bilasiba — I shall play with Gora; rākhiba bukera mājhe — I shall hold Him to my breast

**16.2.** One very softly, another swaying her body: "What is family shame to us? Day and night I shall play with Gora, I shall hold Him to my breast."

কেহ কহে এবে সে রসে মাতিয়া দেখিব বিবাহ-রঙ্গ ।
সামায়া রসের ঘরে ছল করি ছুঁইব সোণার অঙ্গ ॥

*keha kahe ebe se rase mātiyā dekhiba bibāha-raṅga |*
*sāmāyā rasera ghare chala kari chum̐iba soṇāra aṅga ||*

*Word for word:* keha kahe — another says; ebe se rase mātiyā — now, rapt in that rasa; dekhiba bibāha-raṅga — I shall watch the wedding festivity; sāmāyā — slipping in; rasera ghare — into the chamber of rasa; chala kari — on a pretext; chum̐iba soṇāra aṅga — I shall touch the golden body

**16.3.** Another says: "Now, rapt in that rasa, I shall watch the wedding festivity; slipping on a pretext into the chamber of rasa, I shall touch the golden body."

এইমত কত মনোরথ তাহা কহিতে না আইসে মুখে ।
নরহরি সহ সনাতনমিশ্র-ভবনে প্রবেশে সুখে ॥

*eimata kata manoratha tāhā kahite nā āise mukhe |*
*narahari saha sanātanamiśra-bhabane prabeśe sukhe ||*

*Word for word:* eimata kata manoratha — so many such wishes; tāhā kahite nā āise mukhe — they cannot even be spoken; narahari saha — together with Narahari; sanātana-miśra-bhabane — into the house of Sanatana Mishra; prabeśe sukhe — joyfully enter

**16.4.** So many such wishes — they cannot even be spoken! Together with Narahari they joyfully enter the house of Sanatana Mishra.[^33-28]

[^33-27]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — p. 101, sect. 2.4, no. 21 ("yathārāga"; scan PDF p. 360; the catalogue's "no. 20" was corrected in chapter 22); GPT2 — sect. 2.4, no. 21 (catalogue: NG-060). BR —
twelfth wave (ed. 1912, pp. 810–811; ed. 1960, vv. 1507–1510), "punaḥ yathā — rāga", between the padas on the Lord's wedding form (GPT 2.4 no. 20 — chapter 22, no. 3) and on the procession to
Sanatana Mishra's house (no. 22 — chapter 22, no. 4). The pada is not in GCC. BR readings: "keho dhīri dhīri, kahe bhaṅgi kari" (16.2: "one very softly says, swaying her body"), "rākhi' bukera mājhe";
"sāmā'yā bāsara-ghare" (16.3: "slipping into the bridal chamber" — more outspoken than GPT "rasera ghare"). B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^33-28]: The townswomen's wishes (16.2–16.3) — "to play with Gora day and night", "to touch the golden body" — are the nagari motif in its plain form; rendered exactly; where BR is more outspoken
than GPT ("the bridal chamber"), GPT is translated. At the Lord's wedding with Vishnupriya, His eternal consort (chapter 21, note 30), Vrindavana Dasa describes the joy of the people of Nadia
without the nagari motif (CB, Adi 15); the tradition does not accept the worship of Gaura as a nagara (introductory note, chapter 27). "Together with Narahari" (16.4) — the poet places himself
among those in the procession.

## 17. Narahari — "dekha dekha ago bhubanamohana gaurāṅgarūpera chaṭā…" (GPT1 p. 155, sect. 3.1, no. 129; GCC 10.8)
*Nagari-bhava (the heavenly women's talk): praise of His form. One of the heavenly women calls her friends to look at the radiance of Gauranga's form: is it
lightning that has left the cloud and flashed upon the earth? a heap of golden lotus buds, of ground gorochana? fresh kunkuma on the breasts of the young
wives of Vraja, a champaka garland on the necks of the nagaris of Navadvipa? One longs to keep Him always in the heart; the eyes are never sated. Raga
"yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 10, pada 8.*[^33-29]

দেখ দেখ অগো ভুবনমোহন গৌরাঙ্গরূপের ছটা ।
কিয়ে ধরাধর তেজিয়া ধরণী উপরে বিজুরী ঘটা ॥

*dekha dekha ago bhubanamohana gaurāṅgarūpera chaṭā |*
*kiye dharādhara tejiyā dharaṇī upare bijurī ghaṭā ||*

*Word for word:* dekha dekha ago — look, look, friends; bhubanamohana — world-enchanting; gaurāṅgarūpera chaṭā — the radiance of Gauranga's form; kiye — is it; dharādhara tejiyā — leaving the cloud (GPT lit. "mountain"); dharaṇī upare — above the earth; bijurī ghaṭā — a flash of lightning

**17.1.** "Look, look, friends: the radiance of the form of Gauranga, who enchants the world! Is it lightning that has left the cloud and flashed above the earth?

কিয়ে নিরমল মঞ্জুর কনক-কমল-কলিকা-রাশি ।
কিয়ে অতিশয় মর্দ্দিত বিমল চারু গোরোচনা-রাশি ॥

*kiye niramala mañjura kanaka-kamala-kalikā-rāśi |*
*kiye atiśaya marddita bimala cāru gorocanā-rāśi ||*

*Word for word:* kiye — is it; niramala mañjura — pure, lovely; kanaka-kamala-kalikā-rāśi — a heap of golden lotus buds; atiśaya marddita — finely ground; bimala cāru — pure, beautiful; gorocanā-rāśi — a heap of gorochana

**17.2.** Is it a heap of pure, lovely buds of the golden lotus? Is it a heap of finely ground, pure, beautiful gorochana?

কিয়ে ব্রজ-নব-যুবতী-কুচের নবীন কুঙ্কুম ভার ।
কিয়ে নবদ্বীপ-নাগরীগণের গলার চম্পকহার ॥

*kiye braja-naba-yubatī-kucera nabīna kuṅkuma bhāra |*
*kiye nabadvīpa-nāgarīgaṇera galāra campakahāra ||*

*Word for word:* kiye — is it; braja-naba-yubatī-kucera — on the breasts of the young wives of Vraja; nabīna kuṅkuma bhāra — fresh kunkuma (lit. "load of kunkuma"); nabadvīpa-nāgarīgaṇera — of the nagaris of Navadvipa; galāra campaka-hāra — the champaka garland on the neck

**17.3.** Is it fresh kunkuma on the breasts of the young wives of Vraja? Is it a champaka garland on the necks of the nagaris of Navadvipa?

মনে হয় হেন সতত ইহারে হিয়ার মাঝারে রাখি ।
নিরখিতে আঁখি নহে তিরপিত ইথে নরহরি সাথী ॥

*mane haya hena satata ihāre hiyāra mājhāre rākhi |*
*nirakhite ām̐khi nahe tirapita ithe narahari sāthī ||*

*Word for word:* mane haya hena — one longs; satata ihāre — always Him; hiyāra mājhāre rākhi — to keep deep in the heart; nirakhite ām̐khi nahe tirapita — the eyes are not sated with gazing; ithe narahari sāthī — Narahari is witness to it

**17.4.** One longs to keep Him always deep within the heart; the eyes are never sated with gazing — Narahari is witness to it."[^33-30]

[^33-29]: Signature — "Narahari" (ithe narahari sāthī — "Narahari is witness to it"). GPT1 — p. 155, sect. 3.1 ("form"), no. 129 (scan PDF p. 414); GPT2 — sect. 3.1, no. 129 (catalogue: NG-248).
**A witness found** (the catalogue had: "not in BR, GPT2 index — Sarakara; nagari, later"): GCC — kirana 10, pada 8 (ed. 1947, p. 121; scan PDF p. 126), "kācicca — yathārāga" ("and a
certain [heavenly woman]"): it is one of the morning speeches of the heavenly women that open the tenth kirana (chapter 32, note 24); after it come GCC 10.9 (no. 18 of this chapter) and
10.10 (GPT no. 158 — chapter 32, no. 13). GPT placed both padas at the end of section 3.1 ("Gaura's form"), before the section of nagari padas. GCC readings: "ogo" (17.1), "dhārādhara"
("cloud"; GPT1 "dharādhara" — "mountain" — rendered "cloud" by sense and after GCC: lightning leaves the cloud), "niramala sundara kanaka kamala-kalikā-rāśi" (17.2), "nabayubatī-kucera"
(17.3). B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^33-30]: The comparisons for Gaura's golden colour (lightning, golden lotus, gorochana, kunkuma, champaka) are usual in the padas; kunkuma from the gopis' breasts is the paint left on Krishna's
body after embraces — an image of Vraja-lila. Gaura is golden because He took Radha's colour (CC, Adi 4; CC, Adi 1.5); "to keep Him in the heart" is the wish of the speaking heavenly woman;
the tradition does not accept the worship of Gaura as a nagara (introductory note, chapter 27).

## 18. Narahari — "dekha dekha ago gaurāṅgacām̐dera bhubanamohana beśa…" (GPT1 p. 155, sect. 3.1, no. 130; GCC 10.9)
*Nagari-bhava (the heavenly women's talk): His morning form. Another calls them to look at the world-enchanting form of Gaurangachand: dishevelled curls
wreathed with kunda buds; on His brow a tilaka of kunkuma and sandal — as if the moon had risen in a golden sky; the earrings flash; "He will steal dharma,
modesty and honour"; a garland that enchants young women; "what play this is — I cannot understand". Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** —
GCC, kirana 10, pada 9.*[^33-31]

দেখ দেখ অগো গৌরাঙ্গচাঁদের ভুবনমোহন বেশ ।
আউলায়া পড়িছে কুন্দকলি-বেড়া সুচারু চাঁচর কেশ ॥

## 19. Narahari — "jhulata jhulata sundara rasamaya gorā…" (GPT1 pp. 324–325, sect. 5.1, no. 12; BR)
*Nagari-bhava (only at the end: a townswoman's speech); jhulana. Gora, full of rasa, swings on the swing on the bank of the Suradhuni, gazing at Gadadhara's face; His
companions, smiling, push the swing and sing; a townswoman says: who, seeing it, could turn her eyes away; I swear — now all family shame will go: I shall go
to the bank of the Suradhuni and look but once at Narahari's Lord. Raga mallar or beloyar. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in BR (twelfth wave).*[^33-33]

*Word for word:* jhulata jhulata — swinging, swinging; sundara rasamaya gorā — beautiful Gora, full of rasa; aparūpa raṅge mātiyā — rapt in wondrous play; go — o (refrain exclamation); heri heri gadādhara-mukha — gazing and gazing at Gadadhara's face; ām̐khi bhaṅgī kare — makes signs with the eyes; kata bhām̐tiyā — in every way

সুরচিত চারু হিন্দোল ঝুলায় না জানি কি সুখে ভাসিয়া গো ॥

## 20. Narahari — "nadīyāra śaśī raṅge rājapathe…" (GPT1 p. 356, sect. 5.2, no. 39; BR)
*Nagari-bhava; ashtakaliya (a walk through the town). The Moon of Nadia, at play, walks along the royal road, swaying, His heart thrilling; the young women,
unnoticed, restless, long to cast at Him even half a glance; one says to her friend: Gora's form is a heap of nectar — lips bright with betel, a gentle smile, a
garland of rangana, a glance that enchants the world, curls, a sandal tilaka, arms reaching to the knees, a broad chest — "I have drowned in the rasa of Narahari's
Lord and bidden farewell to shame and family". Raga dhanashi. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in BR (twelfth wave).*[^33-35]

নদীয়ার শশী রঙ্গে রাজপথে হেলি দুলি চলে পুলক হিয়া ।
অলখিত যত যুবতী অথির সাধে আধ দিঠি সে অঙ্গে দিবা ॥

*nadīyāra śaśī raṅge rājapathe heli duli cale pulaka hiyā |*
*alakhita yata yubatī athira sādhe ādha diṭhi se aṅge dibā ||*

*Word for word:* nadīyāra śaśī — the Moon of Nadia; raṅge rājapathe — at play, on the royal road; heli duli cale — walks swaying; pulaka hiyā — the heart thrilling; alakhita yata yubatī — the young women, unnoticed; athira — restless; sādhe ādha diṭhi se aṅge dibā — long to cast even half a glance on Him

**20.1.** The Moon of Nadia, at play, walks along the royal road, swaying, His heart thrilling; the young women, unnoticed, restless, long to cast at Him even half a glance.

কেহ কহে দেখ দেখ সখি এই গোরারূপ কিয়ে অমিয়ারাশি ।
তাম্বূলের রাগে অধর উজ্জ্বল তাহে কিবা মন্দ মধুর হাসি ॥

*keha kahe dekha dekha sakhi ei gorārūpa kiye amiyārāśi |*

*Word for word:* keha kahe — one says; dekha dekha sakhi — look, look, friend; ei gorārūpa kiye amiyā-rāśi — is not Gora's form a heap of nectar; tāmbūlera rāge — with the colour of betel; adhara ujjvala — the lips shine; tāhe kibā manda madhura hāsi — and on them what a gentle, sweet smile

চাঁচর চিকুরচয় চারু কিবা কপালে চন্দন তিলক শোহে ॥

*raṅgaṇa phulera mālā dole kibā ām̐khera bhaṅgīte bhubana mohe |*

## Summary of chapter 33

*The chapter completes the padas signed "Narahari" in nagari-bhava. All 20 padas are "probably Chakravarti" (B). GPT1 3.2 nos. 169–180 (nos. 1–12) = GCC 10.25–10.26 and
the eleventh kirana of the "Gaura-charita-chintamani" ("the love-quarrels of the heavenly women"): 11.4, 11.6–11.10, 11.15, 11.17 and 11.14 — GPT rearranged the padas (no. 177 =
11.15, no. 178 = 11.17) and split 11.14 into two (nos. 179–180). The speakers are heavenly women looking down on Nadia from the sky: one defends the chastity of the women of Nadia
(no. 3 — by content not nagari-bhava), the others mock her, tell of the townswomen's "pranks" and call Narahari's Lord "the husband of them all" (no. 10) — yet they themselves
describe the Lord as strict: He does not raise His face, turns away, hurries home in shame (nos. 5, 7, 8, 12). GPT padas outside section 3.2: 2.4 nos. 2, 3, 7, 21 (nos. 13–16) — the
women of Nadia at the Lord's wedding with Vishnupriya (a dream with an embrace, setting out for Shachi's house, "Madana's arrow", wishes to touch His body; all in the twelfth
wave of the "Bhakti-ratnakara", no. 7 also in GCC 9.22); 3.1 nos. 129–130 (nos. 17–18) — found in GCC (10.8–10.9, the heavenly women's words on Gaura's morning appearance;
no. 130 was not in the catalogue — new line NG-366; for no. 129, NG-248, "Sarakara?, no witnesses" is replaced by B); 5.1 no. 12 (no. 19, jhulana) and 5.2 no. 39 (no. 20, a walk
through the town) — in BR. Where GCC or BR is more outspoken than GPT (no. 8 — an extra couplet in GCC; no. 16 — BR's "bridal chamber"), GPT is translated; the only place
where GPT is more outspoken than GCC is the last couplet of no. 12 ("the meeting of the nagaris and the nagara" instead of GCC's words that Narahari preserved propriety;
note 20). The open motifs of attraction and sambhoga (nos. 7, 10, 13, 15, 16) are rendered exactly, with notes on the tradition's position.*

## Concluding note on the "Narahari" nagari padas (chapters 29–33)

*1. **How many.** In the section of nagari padas, 102 padas signed "Narahari" from the "Gaura-pada-tarangini" have been translated: chapter 29 — 15 (Narahari Chakravarti's
pada NG-079 from the cycle of the twelfth wave of the "Bhakti-ratnakara"; GPT1 3.2 nos. 39, 40, 42–45; nos. 86–93), chapter 30 — 21 (nos. 94–110, 120–123), chapter 31 — 23 (nos. 119,
124–145), chapter 32 — 23 (nos. 146–168), chapter 33 — 20 (nos. 169–180; 2.4 nos. 2, 3, 7, 21; 3.1 nos. 129–130; 5.1 no. 12; 5.2 no. 39). Of the 95 padas signed Narahari in section
3.2 of GPT, 94 are translated here — all except no. 41 (= PK 103 of Narahari Sarakara, translated in the main part, chapter 3); the other 8 are nagari padas from sections 2.4,
3.1, 5.1, 5.2. No. 119 (Gaura in sleep speaks Krishna's words) is by content not nagari-bhava, as are the rebuttals within the heavenly women's dispute (chapter 32, nos. 19–20;
chapter 33, no. 3).*

*2. **Attribution.** "Probably Chakravarti" (B) — 81 padas: 75 are found in Narahari Chakravarti's "Gaura-charita-chintamani" (GCC, ed. 1947) — padas 2.13; 7.2–7.12, 7.14–7.16,
7.29–7.30; 8.2–8.20; 9.1–9.2, 9.6–9.16, 9.22; 10.8–10.10, 10.12–10.17, 10.19, 10.21–10.22, 10.24–10.26; 11.4, 11.6–11.10, 11.14 (two padas in GPT), 11.15, 11.17 — and 6 occur only in the
"Bhakti-ratnakara" (NG-079; 2.4 nos. 2, 3, 21; 5.1 no. 12; 5.2 no. 39). "Not established" or "probably Sarakara" (C) — 21 padas: six short padas GPT1 3.2 nos. 39, 40, 42–45 in plain Bengali
(the GPT2 index assigns them to Sarakara; there are no other witnesses; no. 43 — "not established") and fifteen padas nos. 100–110, 120–123, which stand in GPT in the place of the
lost pages of the only available scan of GCC (pp. 81–88 = GCC 7.17–7.28; apparently also from GCC). Not one "Narahari" nagari pada of GPT is confirmed by PK or by other early
collections as a song of Narahari Sarakara, the Lord's companion; almost all of them are Narahari Chakravarti's poetic elaboration of the nagari motif (first half of the
18th century). The collation confirms Majumdar's argument: the long padas of GPT with this signature do not belong to Sarakara.*

*3. **The composition of GCC 7–11 in GPT.** Kiranas 7–11 of the "Gaura-charita-chintamani" describe morning in Navadvipa: the townswomen of Nadia talk of Gaura and of how,
deceiving their strict elders, they saw Him (kirana 7), tell their dreams (8), go to Shachi's house and dream of meeting Him (9); then the heavenly women look down on Nadia
from the sky — praise its nagaris, argue about Gaura (10) and quarrel among themselves (11). These five kiranas have 121 padas (12 of them on the lost pages of the scan);
the compiler of GPT took at least 78 and distributed them among his sections:
— kirana 7: 7.1 — in sect. 2.2 (GPT1 p. 68, no. 19; chapter 19); 7.2–7.12, 7.14–7.16 = 3.2 nos. 86–99 (no. 97 is only the second half of 7.14); 7.29–7.30 = nos. 124–125; not taken:
7.13 and the closing 7.31; 7.17–7.28 are lost in the scan (in their place — nos. 100–110, 120–123);
— kirana 8: 8.2–8.20 = nos. 126–144; not taken: the opening 8.1 and the closing 8.21;
— kirana 9: 9.1–9.2 = nos. 145–146; 9.6–9.16 = nos. 147–157 (9.12 = no. 150 stands earlier in GPT); 9.18–9.19, 9.21–9.22 — in sect. 2.4 ("the second marriage", nos. 4–7: where they
also stand in BR's wedding narrative); not taken: 9.3–9.5, 9.17, 9.20 and the closing prayer 9.23;
— kirana 10: 10.7 — GPT1 p. 494, no. 30 (chapter 18, no. 28); 10.8–10.9 — in sect. 3.1, "form" (nos. 129–130); 10.10, 10.12–10.17, 10.19, 10.21–10.22, 10.24–10.26 = 3.2 nos. 158–170;
not taken: the opening 10.1–10.6, 10.11, 10.18, 10.20, 10.23 and the closing 10.27;
— kirana 11: 11.4, 11.6–11.10, 11.14, 11.15, 11.17 = nos. 171–180 (in a different order; 11.14 split into nos. 179–180); not taken: the opening 11.1–11.3, the links 11.5, 11.16, the
padas 11.11–11.13 and the close 11.18–11.19. Besides these, GCC 2.13 (Gaura's words in sleep) stands in GPT 3.2 (no. 119).*

*4. **Who speaks.** In GCC the padas of kiranas 7–9 are the words of the townswomen of Nadia (and of a mother-in-law who sends her daughters-in-law to Shachi, 9.2); the padas
of kiranas 10–11 are the words of heavenly women (debaramaṇī), who only watch Nadia from the sky and long to be born there. In GPT the openings, colophons and links of
the kiranas are left out, and all the padas of section 3.2 read as the words of townswomen; but traces remain in the GPT text itself — "you, connoisseurs of rasa in the city of
the gods", "in the city of the gods a rumour has arisen", "living in the city of the gods, why have you grown so proud", "how will you live alone in the city of the gods" (chapter
32, nos. 17, 20; chapter 33, nos. 3, 4, 10). Therefore 25 padas of GPT (3.2 nos. 158–180 and 3.1 nos. 129–130) are translated with the label "the heavenly women's talk".*

*5. **Where GPT softens GCC.** The compiler of GPT did not take the most outspoken padas (10.11 — one heavenly woman's guess at where Gaura spent the night; 11.11–11.13 —
the antics of women at the ghat and on the road), left out single lines (8.15; the couplet in 11.10 about a shadow touching Gora's body) and replaced single words (8.6 "lay
