down" → "sat"; 8.11, 8.14, 8.16 — mentions of Madana, e.g. 8.14 "rapt with Madana" → "rapt with joy"; 8.18 — "breast"; 9.6 — "under Madana's weight"; 9.13 "the cloth over
the breast" → "the cloth over the face"; 9.14 "wants to embrace" → "wants to see your dear face"). Throughout, GPT's text is translated and the GCC reading is noted in VAR
and in the notes. The reverse case occurs once: the last couplet of no. 180 (chapter 33, no. 12), where in place of GCC's words that Narahari, being with Gauranga, preserved
propriety stands the formula "in Nadia the meeting of the nagaris and the nagara came to pass"; the compiler's work is also the signature "Narahari" at the end of no. 179,
where GCC has no poet's name.*

*6. **Conclusion.** The "Narahari" nagari padas of GPT are not songs of a contemporary of the Lord but a late (18th-century) poetic elaboration of the nagari motif, carried over
from the "Gaura-charita-chintamani" and the "Bhakti-ratnakara" into an anthology of the early 20th century, abridged and without the author's frame. Within that frame
Narahari Chakravarti himself never shows Gaura responding to the women's attraction: the Lord passes by without raising His face, turns away, hurries home, performs
expiation, and His companion leads Him away (GCC 11.11–11.14; chapter 32, nos. 19–20; chapter 33, nos. 5, 7, 8, 12); the wishes and dreams are the heroines' imagining, and in
kiranas 10–11 it is even a dispute of heavenly women about what they have not seen. Everything is translated faithfully to the author — without worldly vocabulary beyond
the original and without softening — with notes on the tradition's position: Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja and Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati do not accept the
worship of Gaura in the mood of "gaura-nagari"; Gaura is Krishna Himself in Radha's bhava and radiance, tasting Her love as a devotee, not as the enjoyer (introductory note,
chapter 27). What remains of the section is the padas of Lochana Dasa from GPT 3.2 (nos. 61–85, 116; chapter 34) and the concluding note to the whole section of nagari padas.*

---

# Chapter 34. Nagari Padas — VIII: Lochana Dasa (22 padas from GPT, sect. 3.2, nos. 62–85, 116); concluding note to the section of nagari padas

*On what nagari-bhava is, the position of the tradition (Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja, Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati) and the rules of translation, see the introductory note to the section of nagari padas in chapter 27.*

*Chapter 34 is the last of the section of nagari padas: the padas signed by Lochana Dasa in section 3.2 of the *Gaura-pada-tarangini* (GPT). There are 26
of them: nos. 61–85 (GPT1 pp. 177–189, scan PDF pp. 436–448, in one continuous block) and no. 116 (p. 204, PDF p. 463). All have been checked against the
scan of GPT1 (text and signatures), against GPT2 (same numbering, same text), the *Padakalpataru* (PK), the *Padamrita-samudra*, the
*Kshanada-gita-chintamani*, Lochana's *Chaitanya-mangala* (our translation) and the anthologies of the early twentieth century. Four
padas are not translated anew here: **no. 61** "nadīyā-nāgarī sāri sāri sāri…" = PK 2178 and **no. 66** "āra śunecha ālo sai…" = PK 2174 were translated
in chapter 28 (nos. 28 and 27); **no. 80** "ānanda nadīyāpure ṭalamala premabhare…" = PK 2088 is a passage of the *Chaitanya-mangala* itself
(Madhya-khanda: the Lord in kirtana, raga sindhura, with the refrain "The town of Nadia rejoices…"; our translation — *Chaitanya-mangala*, Madhya-khanda, part 4, vv. 110–118;
GPT gives vv. 110–114 and 118, without vv. 115–117), in content a praise of the Lord in kirtana, not nagari-bhava; **no. 84** "nirabadhi gorārūpa mane
jāgiyāche go…" = PK 777, signed by **Vasu Ghosha** (translated in chapter 27, no. 16): in GPT1 the same pada also stands as no. 17 with Vasu's
signature, so Lochana's signature in no. 84 contradicts both PK and GPT itself. The remaining 22 padas are translated below (nos. 1–22).*

*Lochana Dasa (c. 1520 — ?) is the author of the *Chaitanya-mangala*, a disciple of Narahari Sarakara Thakura of Shrikhanda, a younger contemporary of
the Lord's associates; he himself did not see the Lord. The nagari motif is present in the *Chaitanya-mangala* too (the women of Nadia, forgetting
shame, hurry to look at Gaura — see our translation, *Chaitanya-mangala*, Adi-khanda, part 1, note 9; *Chaitanya-mangala*, Adi-khanda, part 10, notes 5–6); Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati,
publishing the *Chaitanya-mangala* (1922), refuses in his preface to ascribe to it "the doctrine of gaura-nagari" (the translator's preface to our translation of the *Chaitanya-mangala*). The padas
of this chapter are of two kinds: (1) padas in the literary language of the padas, in payar and tripadi metre (nos. 1–4, 15–17, 21); (2) padas in
colloquial Bengali, in short rhymed feet, with colloquial forms ("dekhalāma", "halo", "ka're") and kirtana singers' insertions in brackets (nos. 5–14,
18–20, 22) — in the manner of the playful songs traditionally connected with Lochana's name (dhāmālī, "dhamali"). The padas of the second kind are
known only from GPT (two of them — nos. 16, 17 — are also in the anthology *Prachina-vaishnava-padavali*, 1922, with Lochana's signature); their
language was probably renewed in oral transmission. None of the 22 padas is in PK or in the *Chaitanya-mangala*; Lochana's signature does not
compete with any other (except in no. 84, excluded above). The attribution rests only on the signature in GPT: Lochana is a recognized
author, but these padas have no independent witnesses (PVP, 1922, is a late anthology), hence C ("attribution by GPT only"; cf. Lochana's padas from
PK in chapter 28 — B). Where a pada builds on someone else's lines (no. 5 begins with two couplets of Jnanadasa's pada PK 748), this is noted.*

*The translation is faithful to the author, without worldly vocabulary beyond the original and without softening: where a townswoman speaks of
attraction, embraces, a dream, it is translated exactly, with a note on the position of the tradition. The Bengali text, variants and word-for-word
translation are in the full version of the book. At the end — the summary of the chapter and the concluding note to the whole section of nagari padas (chapters 27–34).*

## 1. Lochana Dasa — "gaurāṅga-taraṅge nayana majila…" (GPT1 pp. 177–178, no. 62)
*Nagari-bhava. The townswoman's eyes have drowned in the waves of Gauranga: she is ready to take disgrace upon herself and leave home; all her
household work betrays her — she knows nothing but Gora, in anyone she meets she sees Gauranga; lying with her husband, she imagines Gaurahari coming
and taking her to Himself. Raga pahida.*[^34-1]

গৌরাঙ্গ-তরঙ্গে নয়ন মজিল কিবা সে করিব সার ।
কলঙ্কের ডালি মাথায় ধরিয়া ঘরে না রহিব আর ॥

*gaurāṅga-taraṅge nayana majila kibā se kariba sāra |*
*kalaṅkera ḍāli māthāya dhariyā ghare nā rahiba āra ||*

*Word for word:* gaurāṅga-taraṅge — in the waves of Gauranga; nayana majila — the eyes have drowned; kibā se kariba sāra — what shall I make my all; kalaṅkera ḍāli — the basket of disgrace; māthāya dhariyā — holding on the head; ghare nā rahiba āra — I will stay at home no more

**1.1.** In the waves of Gauranga my eyes have drowned — what now shall I choose?
Lifting the basket of disgrace onto my head, I will stay at home no more.

সই এবে সে করিব কি ।
গৌরাঙ্গচাঁদের নিছনি লইয়া গৃহে সমাধান দি ॥

*sai ebe se kariba ki |*
*gaurāṅgacām̐dera nichani laiyā gṛhe samādhāna di ||*

*Word for word:* sai — friend; ebe se kariba ki — what am I to do now; gaurāṅgacām̐dera nichani laiyā — giving myself away (nichani) for Gaurangachand; gṛhe samādhāna di — I make an end of the house

**1.2.** *(Refrain)* Friend, what am I to do now?
Giving myself away for Gaurangachand, I will make an end of the house.[^34-2]

গৃহধর্ম্ম যত হইল বেকত গোরা বিনা নাহি জানি ।
আনেরে দেখিয়া ভরমে ভুলিয়া গৌরাঙ্গ বলি যে আমি ॥

*gṛhadharmma yata haila bekata gorā binā nāhi jāni |*
*ānere dekhiyā bharame bhuliyā gaurāṅga bali ye āmi ||*

*Word for word:* gṛha-dharmma yata — all the household duties; haila bekata — it became manifest; gorā binā nāhi jāni — I know nothing but Gora; ānere dekhiyā — seeing another; bharame bhuliyā — mistaken in confusion; gaurāṅga bali ye āmi — I say "Gauranga"

**1.3.** All my household work — it is plain to everyone now: I know nothing but Gora;
seeing another, mistaking him in my confusion, I say: "Gauranga!"

পতির সহিতে শুতিয়া থাকিতে গৌরাঙ্গ জাগয়ে মনে ।
আসি তরাতরি প্রাণ গৌরহরি পতিরে ফেলাঞা ভূমে ॥

*patira sahite śutiyā thākite gaurāṅga jāgaye mane |*
*āsi tarātari prāṇa gaurahari patire phelāñā bhūme ||*

*Word for word:* patira sahite — with the husband; śutiyā thākite — while lying; gaurāṅga jāgaye mane — Gauranga awakens in the heart; āsi tarātari — coming in haste; prāṇa gaurahari — Gaurahari, [my] life; patire phelāñā bhūme — throwing the husband to the ground

**1.4.** When I lie with my husband, Gauranga awakens in my heart:
Gaurahari, my life, comes in haste and throws my husband down on the ground;

আমারে লইয়া করে উরপরে বদনে বদন দিয়া ।
আবেশে গৌরাঙ্গ সুধা উগারয়ে প্রতি অঙ্গে পড়ে বাইঞা ॥

*āmāre laiyā kare urapare badane badana diyā |*
*ābeśe gaurāṅga sudhā ugāraye prati aṅge paṛe bāiñā ||*

*Word for word:* āmāre laiyā — taking me; kare ura-pare — places on the breast; badane badana diyā — pressing face to face; ābeśe gaurāṅga — Gauranga in ecstasy; sudhā ugāraye — pours out nectar; prati aṅge paṛe bāiñā — it flows down over every limb

**1.5.** He takes me, places me on His breast, presses face to face;
in ecstasy Gauranga pours out nectar — it flows down over every limb.[^34-3]

গৌরাঙ্গ-রতন করিয়া যতন মোড়াঞা লইব কোলে ।
তিলাঞ্জলি দিয়া সকলি ভাসানু এ দাস লোচন বলে ॥

*gaurāṅga-ratana kariyā yatana moṛāñā laiba kole |*
*tilāñjali diyā sakali bhāsānu e dāsa locana bale ||*

*Word for word:* gaurāṅga-ratana — Gauranga the jewel; kariyā yatana — carefully; moṛāñā laiba kole — I will enfold in my arms; tilāñjali diyā — bidding farewell for ever; sakali bhāsānu — I let everything float away; e dāsa locana bale — says this servant Lochana

**1.6.** Gauranga, the jewel, I will carefully enfold in my arms;
bidding farewell to all, I have let everything float away, — says this servant Lochana.[^34-4]

[^34-1]: Signature: "e dāsa locana" ("this servant Lochana"). GPT1 — pp. 177–178, no. 62 (raga pahida; scan PDF pp. 436–437); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 62
(same text). The pada is not in PK, the *Padamrita-samudra*, KGC or the *Chaitanya-mangala*; no other witnesses have been found. On Lochana Dasa see
chapter 28, note 75, and the note at the beginning of this chapter: a disciple of Narahari Sarakara, a younger contemporary of the Lord's associates;
attribution by GPT only — C. On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^34-2]: "Lifting the basket of disgrace onto my head" (kalaṅkera ḍāli māthāya dhariyā) — a saying: to take ill fame upon oneself openly. "Giving myself
away for Gaurangachand" (nichani laiyā) — the nichhani rite (chapter 27, note 10). "I will make an end of the house" (gṛhe samādhāna di) — lit. "I will
give the house its conclusion."
[^34-3]: The scene in 1.4–1.5 is the speaker's imagination: "Gauranga awakens in my heart," and she goes on to picture what He would do. It is translated
as in the original, without softening. This is precisely the notion of Gaura as the lover of the townswomen ("gaura-nagari") which the Gaudiya
tradition rejects: according to the *Chaitanya-bhagavata* (Adi-khanda), the Lord in this incarnation did not look at any woman; Srila Bhaktisiddhanta
Sarasvati counts "gaura-nagari" among the apasampradayas (introductory note). According to Majumdar, nagari padas known only from GPT are an
unreliable and late layer. "Pours out nectar" (sudhā ugāraye) is an image of sweetness common in padas on Krishna.
[^34-4]: "Bidding farewell to all" (tilāñjali diyā) — lit. "giving the farewell handful of water with sesame" (as to the dead): leaving for ever. "I have
let float away" (bhāsānu) is in the past tense, while "I will enfold" (laiba) is in the future; so in the original.

## 2. Lochana Dasa — "śuna śuna sai āra kichu kai…" (GPT1 p. 178, no. 63)
*Nagari-bhava. "Listen, friend: Gauranga is not a man!" Ever since the townswoman saw the moon of His face, her eyes have drowned in the ocean of
beauty; at the ghat and in the field she sees Gora, the colour of a golden filament; sitting among the elders, she remembers His face; giving herself
away for Him, she will leave everything. Raga kamoda.*[^34-5]

শুন শুন সই আর কিছু কই গৌরাঙ্গ মানুষ নয় ।
ভুবন মাঝারে শচীর কুমারে উপমা কিসে বা হয় ॥

*śuna śuna sai āra kichu kai gaurāṅga mānuṣa naya |*
*bhubana mājhāre śacīra kumāre upamā kise bā haya ||*

*Word for word:* śuna śuna sai — listen, listen, friend; āra kichu kai — I tell you more; gaurāṅga mānuṣa naya — Gauranga is not a man; bhubana mājhāre — in the world; śacīra kumāre — for the son of Shachi; upamā kise vā haya — what comparison can there be

**2.1.** Listen, listen, friend, I will tell you more: Gauranga is not a man!
In all the world, to what can the son of Shachi be compared?[^34-6]

ছাড়িতে না পারি যে অবধি হেরি গৌরাঙ্গবদনচাঁদ ।
সে রূপসায়রে নয়ান ডুবিল লাগিল পীরিতি ফাঁদ ॥

*chāṛite nā pāri ye abadhi heri gaurāṅgabadanacām̐da |*
*se rūpasāyare nayāna ḍubila lāgila pīriti phām̐da ||*

*Word for word:* chāṛite nā pāri — I cannot leave; ye abadhi heri — since I saw; gaurāṅga-badana-cām̐da — the moon of Gauranga's face; se rūpa-sāyare — in that ocean of beauty; nayāna ḍubila — the eyes drowned; lāgila pīriti phām̐da — the noose of love caught

**2.2.** Since I saw the moon of Gauranga's face, I cannot turn away [from it]:
in that ocean of beauty my eyes have drowned, the noose of love has tightened.

ঘাটে মাঠে যাই হেরি গো সদাই কনক-কেশর গোরা ।
কুলের বিচার ধরম আচার সকলি করিল ছাড়া ॥

*ghāṭe māṭhe yāi heri go sadāi kanaka-keśara gorā |*
*kulera bicāra dharama ācāra sakali karila chāṛā ||*

*Word for word:* ghāṭe māṭhe yāi — I go to the ghat, to the field; heri go sadāi — I see all the time; kanaka-keśara gorā — Gora, the golden filament; kulera bicāra — the honour (judgement) of family; dharama ācāra — dharma and custom; sakali karila chāṛā — He made me give it all up

**2.3.** Whether I go to the ghat or the field — I see Gora all the time, the golden filament;
the honour of family, dharma and custom — all this He has made me leave.[^34-7]

থাকি গুরু মাঝে হেরি গো নয়নে বয়ান পড়িছে মনে ।
নিবারিতে চাই নাহি নিবারণ বিকল করিল প্রাণে ॥

*thāki guru mājhe heri go nayane bayāna paṛiche mane |*
*nibārite cāi nāhi nibāraṇa bikala karila prāṇe ||*

*Word for word:* thāki guru mājhe — I stay among the elders; heri go nayane — I see with the eyes; bayāna paṛiche mane — the face comes to mind; nibārite cāi — I want to hold back; nāhi nibāraṇa — there is no holding back; bikala karila prāṇe — He has troubled the soul

**2.4.** Sitting among the elders, I see Him with my eyes, His face comes to my mind;
I try to hold myself back — I cannot: He has thrown my soul into turmoil.

গৌরাঙ্গচাঁদের নিছনি লইয়া সকলি ছাড়িয়া দিব ।
লোচনের মনে হয় রাত্রি দিনে হিয়ার মাঝারে থোব ॥

*gaurāṅgacām̐dera nichani laiyā sakali chāṛiyā diba |*
*locanera mane haya rātri dine hiyāra mājhāre thoba ||*

*Word for word:* gaurāṅgacām̐dera nichani laiyā — giving myself away for Gaurangachand; sakali chāṛiyā diba — I will leave everything; locanera mane haya — it is on Lochana's mind; rātri dine — night and day; hiyāra mājhāre thoba — I will place [Him] in the heart

**2.5.** Giving myself away for Gaurangachand, I will leave everything.
On Lochana's mind night and day: "I will place Him in my heart."

[^34-5]: Signature: "on Lochana's mind" (locanera mane). GPT1 — p. 178, no. 63 (raga kamoda; scan PDF p. 437); GPT2 — 3.2, no. 63 (same text). No other
witnesses; attribution by GPT only — C. On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^34-6]: "Gauranga is not a man" — a praise that agrees with the teaching: Gaura is Bhagavan Himself (CC Adi 1–4); the townswoman says it out of
amazement at His beauty.
[^34-7]: "Golden filament" (kanaka-keśara) — the colour of Gora's body is compared to the golden filaments (keshara) of a flower. Leaving "the honour of
family, dharma and custom" is a motif of the padas on the gopis (*Bhag.* 10.29) transferred to the townswomen of Nadia; it is this transfer that the
tradition rejects (introductory note; cf. chapter 27, note 43).

## 3. Lochana Dasa — "hiyāra mājhāre gaurāṅga rākhiyā…" (GPT1 p. 178, no. 64)
*Nagari-bhava (only in the address to a friend). Having placed Gauranga in her heart, the townswoman will sit in solitude and look at the moon of His
face; she has heard that He who was formerly in Gokula, in Nanda's house, has now appeared in Navadvipa, in Shachi's house. Raga kamoda.*[^34-8]

হিয়ার মাঝারে গৌরাঙ্গ রাখিয়া বিরলে বসিয়া রব ।
মনের সাধে ও মুখচাঁদে নয়নে নয়নে থোব ॥

*hiyāra mājhāre gaurāṅga rākhiyā birale basiyā raba |*
*manera sādhe o mukhacām̐de nayane nayane thoba ||*

*Word for word:* hiyāra mājhāre — in the heart; gaurāṅga rākhiyā — placing Gauranga; birale basiyā raba — I will sit in solitude; manera sādhe — to my heart's content; o mukha-cām̐de — that moon of a face; nayane nayane thoba — I will keep before my eyes

**3.1.** Having placed Gauranga in my heart, I will sit in solitude;
to my heart's content I will keep that moon of a face before my eyes.

শুনেছি পূরবে গোকুলনগরে নন্দের মন্দিরে যে ।
নবদ্বীপ আসি হৈলা পরকাশি শচীর মন্দিরে সে ॥

*śunechi pūrabe gokulanagare nandera mandire ye |*
*nabadvīpa āsi hailā parakāśi śacīra mandire se ||*

*Word for word:* śunechi — I have heard; pūrabe — formerly; gokula-nagare — in Gokula; nandera mandire ye — He who [was] in Nanda's house; nabadvīpa āsi — coming to Navadvipa; hailā parakāśi — revealed Himself; śacīra mandire se — He, in Shachi's house

**3.2.** I have heard: He who formerly [was] in Gokula, in the house of Nanda, —
He has come to Navadvipa and revealed Himself in the house of Shachi.[^34-9]

লোচনের বাণী শুন গো সজনি কি আর বলিব তোরে ।
হেরিয়া বদন ভুলে গেল মন পাসরিতে নারি তারে ॥

*locanera bāṇī śuna go sajani ki āra baliba tore |*
*heriyā badana bhule gela mana pāsarite nāri tāre ||*

*Word for word:* locanera bāṇī — the word of Lochana; śuna go sajani — listen, friend; ki āra baliba tore — what more shall I tell you; heriyā badana — seeing the face; bhule gela mana — the mind forgot itself; pāsarite nāri tāre — I cannot forget Him

**3.3.** The word of Lochana: listen, friend, what more shall I tell you?
I saw the face — and the mind forgot itself: I cannot forget Him.

[^34-8]: Signature: "the word of Lochana" (locanera bāṇī). GPT1 — p. 178, no. 64 (raga kamoda; scan PDF p. 437); GPT2 — 3.2, no. 64 (same text). No other
witnesses; attribution by GPT only — C. The nagari motif is only in the address "friend": in substance this is a praise of Gaura and contemplation of Him in the heart. On
nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^34-9]: Gaura is the same Krishna, the son of Nanda, who has appeared in Shachi's house (CC Adi 1–4); in Lochana this thought runs through the whole
*Chaitanya-mangala*.

## 4. Lochana Dasa — "gaurāṅgabadane harila cetane…" (GPT1 p. 178, no. 65)
*Nagari-bhava. Gauranga's face has stolen the townswoman's reason: she wants to forget — she cannot. Refrain: "Gora has entered the heart; the
townswomen of Nadia have gone mad — I have understood it by myself." Seeing Gauranga's feet, a noble wife leaves her husband; whether it is righteous
or not — it is shameful even to say. Raga kamoda.*[^34-10]

গৌরাঙ্গবদনে হরিল চেতনে বড় পরমাদ দেখি ।
পাসরিতে চাই পাসরা না যায় উপায় বল গো সখি ॥

*gaurāṅgabadane harila cetane baṛa paramāda dekhi |*
*pāsarite cāi pāsarā nā yāya upāya bala go sakhi ||*

*Word for word:* gaurāṅga-badane — Gauranga's face; harila cetane — stole the reason; baṛa paramāda dekhi — I see a great calamity; pāsarite cāi — I want to forget; pāsarā nā yāya — it cannot be forgotten; upāya bala go sakhi — tell me a way, friend

**4.1.** Gauranga's face has stolen my reason — I see a great calamity has come;
I want to forget — I cannot forget; tell me, friend, what am I to do?

গোরা পশিল হিয়ার মাঝে ।
নদীয়া-নাগরী হইল পাগলী বুঝিনু আপন কাজে ॥

*gorā paśila hiyāra mājhe |*
*nadīyā-nāgarī haila pāgalī bujhinu āpana kāje ||*

*Word for word:* gorā paśila hiyāra mājhe — Gora entered the heart; nadīyā-nāgarī — the townswomen of Nadia; haila pāgalī — went mad; bujhinu āpana kāje — I understood by my own case

**4.2.** *(Refrain)* Gora has entered the heart.
The townswomen of Nadia have gone mad — I have understood it by myself.

যখন দেখিনু গৌরাঙ্গচরণ তখনি হরিল মন ।
কুলবতী সতী যুবতী যেজন ত্যজে নিজ পতিধন ॥

*yakhana dekhinu gaurāṅgacaraṇa takhani harila mana |*
*kulabatī satī yubatī yejana tyaje nija patidhana ||*

*Word for word:* yakhana dekhinu — when I saw; gaurāṅga-caraṇa — Gauranga's feet; takhani harila mana — at once He stole the mind; kulabatī satī yubatī yejana — whatever young noble faithful wife; tyaje nija pati-dhana — leaves her own treasure, the husband

**4.3.** As soon as I saw Gauranga's feet, He at once stole my mind;
a young noble faithful wife, whoever she may be, leaves her treasure — her husband.[^34-11]

না জানি ধরমে কি জানি করমে কহিতে বাসি হে লাজ ।
লোচনদাসের মন বেয়াকুল এবে সে বুঝিল কাজ ॥

*nā jāni dharame ki jāni karame kahite bāsi he lāja |*
*locanadāsera mana beyākula ebe se bujhila kāja ||*

*Word for word:* nā jāni dharame — I do not know if by dharma; ki jāni karame — or by karma; kahite bāsi he lāja — I am ashamed to say; locana-dāsera mana beyākula — Lochana Dasa's mind is troubled; ebe se bujhila kāja — now he has understood the matter

**4.4.** I do not know whether by dharma or by karma — I am ashamed even to say;
Lochana Dasa is troubled in soul: now he too has understood what it is.

[^34-10]: Signature: "Lochana Dasa." GPT1 — p. 178, no. 65 (raga kamoda; refrain marked "dhru"; scan PDF p. 437); GPT2 — 3.2, no. 65 (same text). No other
witnesses; attribution by GPT only — C. On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^34-11]: "Leaves her treasure — her husband" (tyaje nija patidhana) is the parakiya motif of the padas on the gopis transferred to the noble wives of
Nadia (see note 7); translated exactly. "Whether by dharma or by karma" (4.4) — i.e., one cannot tell whether it is righteous or sinful. In 4.4b the poet
speaks of himself in the third person: he too has "understood by himself" the power of Gaura's form (cf. the refrain).

## 5. Lochana Dasa — "(gaurera) rūpa lāgi ām̐khi jhore…" (GPT1 pp. 179–180, no. 67)
*Nagari-bhava. The townswoman's eyes weep for Gaura's form, each of her limbs for each of His; why did she go to the Suradhuni, why did she look at
Gaura — He pierced her with the arrows of His eyes; her eyes want to go and look, her mind wants to become His maidservant; her mind slipped on the
slippery ghat of the ocean of His beauty. She will cut open her breast and hide Him there together with her life. Raga "yatharaga".*[^34-12]

(গৌরের) রূপ লাগি আঁখি ঝোরে গুণে মন ভোর ।
প্রতি অঙ্গ লাগি কাঁদে প্রতি অঙ্গ মোর ॥

*(gaurera) rūpa lāgi ām̐khi jhore guṇe mana bhora |*
*prati aṅga lāgi kām̐de prati aṅga mora ||*

*Word for word:* (gaurera) — (of Gaura); rūpa lāgi — for the form; ām̐khi jhore — the eyes weep; guṇe mana bhora — the mind is enraptured by the virtues; prati aṅga lāgi — for each limb; kām̐de prati aṅga mora — each of my limbs weeps

**5.1.** For the form (of Gaura) my eyes weep, my mind is enraptured by His virtues;
for each [of His] limbs each of my limbs weeps.

হিয়ার পরশ লাগি হিয়া মোর কাঁদে ।
পরাণ পুতলী মোর হিয়া নাহি বাঁধে ॥

*hiyāra paraśa lāgi hiyā mora kām̐de |*
*parāṇa putalī mora hiyā nāhi bām̐dhe ||*

*Word for word:* hiyāra paraśa lāgi — for the touch of the breast; hiyā mora kām̐de — my breast weeps; parāṇa putalī mora — the darling doll of my soul; hiyā nāhi bām̐dhe — the heart cannot hold

**5.2.** For the touch of [His] breast my breast weeps;
my heart cannot hold the darling doll of my soul.[^34-13]

আমি কেন সুরধুনী গেলাম (গেলাম ! গেলাম !!) ।
কেন গৌররূপে নয়ন দিলাম ॥

*āmi kena suradhunī gelāma (gelāma ! gelāma !!) |*
*kena gaurarūpe nayana dilāma ||*

*Word for word:* āmi kena suradhunī gelāma — why did I go to the Suradhuni; (gelāma gelāma) — (I went! I went!); kena gaura-rūpe nayana dilāma — why did I turn my eyes to Gaura's form

**5.3.** Why did I go to the Suradhuni (I went! I went!!),
why did I turn my eyes to the form of Gaura?

আমি কেনই চাইলাম গৌরপানে ।
(গৌর) আমায় হান্‌লে দুটী নয়ন-বাণে ॥

*āmi kenai cāilāma gaurapāne |*
*(gaura) āmāya hānle duṭī nayana-bāṇe ||*

*Word for word:* āmi kenai cāilāma gaura-pāne — why ever did I look at Gaura; (gaura) — (Gaura); āmāya hānle — pierced me; duṭī nayana-bāṇe — with the two arrows of His eyes

**5.4.** Why ever did I look at Gaura?
(Gaura) pierced me with the two arrows of His eyes.

আমার নয়ন বোলে ওরূপ দেখে আসি ।
আমার মন বলে তার হৈগা দাসী ॥

*āmāra nayana bole orūpa dekhe āsi |*
*āmāra mana bale tāra haigā dāsī ||*

*Word for word:* āmāra nayana bole — my eyes say; o-rūpa dekhe āsi — let us go and see that form; āmāra mana bale — my mind says; tāra haigā dāsī — I will become His maidservant

**5.5.** My eyes say: "Let us go and look at that form";
my mind says: "I will become His maidservant."

করে নয়ন-পথে আনাগোনা ।
আমার পাঁজর কেটে করল খানা ॥

*kare nayana-pathe ānāgonā |*
*āmāra pām̐jara keṭe karala khānā ||*

*Word for word:* kare nayana-pathe ānāgonā — He comes and goes by the path of the eyes; āmāra pām̐jara keṭe — cutting through my ribs; karala khānā — made a dwelling (or: cut to pieces)

**5.6.** He comes and goes by the path of the eyes;
He has cut through my ribs and made Himself a dwelling [there].[^34-14]

গৌররূপ-সাগরের পিছল ঘাটে ।
আমার মন গিয়া তায় পড়ল ছুটে ॥

*gaurarūpa-sāgarera pichala ghāṭe |*
*āmāra mana giyā tāya paṛala chuṭe ||*

*Word for word:* gaura-rūpa-sāgarera — of the ocean of Gaura's form; pichala ghāṭe — at the slippery ghat; āmāra mana giyā tāya — my mind, going there; paṛala chuṭe — slipped and fell

**5.7.** At the slippery ghat of the ocean that is Gaura's form
my mind went down, slipped and fell.

একে গৌররূপ তায় পীরিত মাখা ।
(তাতে আবার) ঈষৎ হাসি নয়ন বাঁকা ॥

*eke gaurarūpa tāya pīrita mākhā |*
*(tāte ābāra) īṣat hāsi nayana bām̐kā ||*

*Word for word:* eke gaura-rūpa — as if Gaura's form were not enough; tāya pīrita mākhā — it is steeped in love besides; (tāte ābāra) — (and on top of that); īṣat hāsi — a slight smile; nayana bām̐kā — a sidelong glance

**5.8.** As if Gaura's form were not enough — it is steeped in love besides,
(and on top of that) a slight smile and a sidelong glance.

(গৌরের) যত রূপ তত বেশ ।
ও ! সে ! ভাজিতে পাঁজর শেষ ॥

*(gaurera) yata rūpa tata beśa |*
*o ! se ! bhājite pām̐jara śeṣa ||*

*Word for word:* (gaurera) — (Gaura has); yata rūpa tata beśa — as many forms as adornments; o se — oh, He; bhājite — scorching (lit. frying); pām̐jara śeṣa — the ribs are spent

**5.9.** (Gaura has) as many forms as He has adornments;
oh! He! — He scorches me till my ribs are spent.[^34-15]

(গৌরের) রূপ লাগি আঁখি ঝোরে ।
গুণে মনোভোর করে ॥

*(gaurera) rūpa lāgi ām̐khi jhore |*
*guṇe manobhora kare ||*

*Word for word:* (gaurera) rūpa lāgi — for the form (of Gaura); ām̐khi jhore — the eyes weep; guṇe mano-bhora kare — the virtues enrapture the mind

**5.10.** For the form (of Gaura) my eyes weep;
His virtues intoxicate my mind.

(গৌররূপ) তিল আধ পাসরিতে নারি ।
কি খনে (গৌরাঙ্গরূপ) হিয়ার মাঝে ধরি ॥

*(gaurarūpa) tila ādha pāsarite nāri |*
*ki khane (gaurāṅgarūpa) hiyāra mājhe dhari ||*

*Word for word:* (gaura-rūpa) — (Gaura's form); tila ādha pāsarite nāri — I cannot forget for half a moment; ki khane — in what an hour; (gaurāṅga-rūpa) — (Gauranga's form); hiyāra mājhe dhari — I placed in my heart

**5.11.** Not for a moment can I forget (Gaura's form);
in what an hour did I place (Gauranga's form) in my heart!

এ বুক চিরিয়া রাখি পরাণেরই সঙ্গ ।
মনে হোলে বাহির ক'রে দেখি মুখচন্দ ॥

*e buka ciriyā rākhi parāṇerai saṅga |*
*mane hole bāhira ka're dekhi mukhacanda ||*

*Word for word:* e buka ciriyā rākhi — I will cut open this breast and keep [Him]; parāṇerai saṅga — together with my very life; mane hole — when I wish; bāhira ka're dekhi — I take Him out and look; mukha-canda — the moon of the face

**5.12.** I will cut open this breast and hide [Him] there together with my very life;
when I wish, I will take Him out and look at the moon of His face.[^34-16]

গৌররূপ হেরি সবার অন্তর উল্লাস ।
আনন্দ হৃদয়ে কহে এ লোচন দাস ॥

*gaurarūpa heri sabāra antara ullāsa |*
*ānanda hṛdaye kahe e locana dāsa ||*

*Word for word:* gaura-rūpa heri — seeing Gaura's form; sabāra antara ullāsa — everyone's heart rejoices; ānanda hṛdaye — with joy in the heart; kahe e locana dāsa — says this Lochana Dasa

**5.13.** At the sight of Gaura's form everyone's heart rejoices;
with joy in his heart says this Lochana Dasa.

[^34-12]: Signature: "e locana dāsa." GPT1 — pp. 179–180, no. 67 (raga "yatharaga"; scan PDF pp. 438–439); GPT2 — 3.2, no. 67 (same text). The first
two couplets (5.1–5.2) are the beginning of Jnanadasa's pada PK 748 "rūpa lāgi ām̐khi jhure guṇe mana bhora…" (PK vol. 2, 8th pallava, signature
"jñāna"; also in the *Padamrita-samudra*), where Radha weeps for Shyama; here "(gaurera)" — "of Gaura" — is added, and the whole pada is turned to
Gaura; from then on it is colloquial Bengali. Developing the opening lines of a well-known pada is a usual practice of kirtaniyas; the pada is a
composite, and its attribution to Lochana rests only on the signature in GPT (C). On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^34-13]: The words in brackets — "(gaurera)", "(gaura)", "(gelāma! gelāma!!)", "(tāte ābāra)", "(gaurarūpa)", "(gaurāṅgarūpa)" — are insertions of
the kirtana singers (akhar), as GPT prints them; they are translated in brackets. "The darling doll of my soul" (parāṇa putalī) — what is dearest;
PK 748 has here "parāṇa pirīti lāgi," while "parāṇa-putalī mora" is the reading of MS P-R-Sa in the PK apparatus: GPT follows it.
[^34-14]: "Made a dwelling" (karala khānā): khānā is "house, dwelling" (Pers. khana) or "pieces" ("cut to pieces"); both readings are possible.
[^34-15]: "Scorches" (bhājite) — lit. "frying"; the sense of the line is unclear, the translation is conjectural.
[^34-16]: The wish to keep the Lord's form in the heart for ever; "to cut open the breast" is a hyperbole of love poetry, known also from padas on Radha.

## 6. Lochana Dasa — "uṣaḥkāle sakhī mile jala bharite yāya…" (GPT1 pp. 180–181, no. 68)
*Nagari-bhava. At dawn a young wife goes with her friends for water and meets Gora with His friends on the road; having filled her pitcher, she stands
as if stunned and gazes: who is this — a god of rasa? Brows, eyes, nose, teeth, the colour of His body, arms, necklace, white cloth, ringing anklets;
the nagara of beauty has risen — and the mind of "the nagari Lochana" is swept away. Raga "yatharaga".*[^34-17]

উষঃকালে সখী মিলে জল ভরিতে যায় ।
সঙ্গে সখা পথে দেখা হলো গোরারায় ॥

*uṣaḥkāle sakhī mile jala bharite yāya |*
*saṅge sakhā pathe dekhā halo gorārāya ||*

*Word for word:* uṣaḥkāle — at dawn; sakhī mile — together with friends; jala bharite yāya — she goes to fetch water; saṅge sakhā — with [His] friends; pathe dekhā halo — on the road there was a meeting; gorārāya — Gora-raya

**6.1.** At dawn, together with her friends, she goes to fetch water;
on the road — a meeting: Gora-raya with His friends.

মরমে মরি কলসি ভরি তুলে নিলাম কাঁখে ।
থাকিত পারা চৌউর হারা বঁধু দাঁড়ায়ে দেখে ॥

*marame mari kalasi bhari tule nilāma kām̐khe |*
*thākita pārā cauura hārā bam̐dhu dām̐ṛāye dekhe ||*

*Word for word:* marame mari — dying at heart; kalasi bhari — filling the pitcher; tule nilāma kām̐khe — I lifted it onto my hip; thākita pārā — as if stunned; cauura hārā — beside herself (?); bam̐dhu (= badhū) — the young wife; dām̐ṛāye dekhe — stands and gazes

**6.2.** Dying at heart, I filled the pitcher and lifted it onto my hip;
the young wife stands as if stunned, beside herself, and gazes.[^34-18]

ওবা কে রসের দে রূপের সীমা নাই ।
কোন বিধি রসের নিধি কৈল এক ঠাঁই ॥

*obā ke rasera de rūpera sīmā nāi |*
*kona bidhi rasera nidhi kaila eka ṭhām̐i ||*

*Word for word:* obā ke — who is this; rasera de — a god (?) of rasa; rūpera sīmā nāi — there is no limit to the beauty; kona bidhi — what creator; rasera nidhi — the treasure of rasa; kaila eka ṭhām̐i — gathered in one place

**6.3.** "Who is this — a god of rasa? there is no limit to His beauty;
what creator has gathered the treasure of rasa in one place?

যুগ্মভুরু কামের গুরু ছাড়ছে ফুলের বাণ ।
কেমন কালি ধরে তুলি ক'রেছে নির্ম্মাণ ॥

*yugmabhuru kāmera guru chāṛache phulera bāṇa |*
*kemana kāli dhare tuli ka'reche nirmmāṇa ||*

*Word for word:* yugma-bhuru — the pair of brows; kāmera guru — the teacher of Kama; chāṛche phulera bāṇa — shoots flower-arrows; kemana kāli — with what ink; dhare tuli — holding a brush; kareche nirmmāṇa — they were made

**6.4.** The pair of brows — the teacher of Kama — shoots flower-arrows;
with what ink, with what brush were they made?

আঁখির তল নিরমল নীল-কমলের দল ।
অরুণতা দুটী পাতা ক'রছে ছলছল্ ॥

*ām̐khira tala niramala nīla-kamalera dala |*
*aruṇatā duṭī pātā ka'rache chalachal ||*

*Word for word:* ām̐khira tala — the depths of the eyes; niramala — spotless; nīla-kamalera dala — petals of a blue lotus; aruṇatā duṭī pātā — two reddish lids; karche chalachala — glisten moist

**6.5.** The depths of the eyes are spotless petals of a blue lotus;
the two lids, reddish, glisten moist.

তিলফুল কিসে তুল এমনি নাসার শোভা ।
কুঁদে কাটি পরিপাটী কিবা দন্তের আভা ॥

*tilaphula kise tula emani nāsāra śobhā |*
*kum̐de kāṭi paripāṭī kibā dantera ābhā ||*

*Word for word:* tila-phula — a sesame flower; kise tula — how could it compare; emani nāsāra śobhā — such is the beauty of the nose; kum̐de kāṭi — turned on a lathe; paripāṭī — even; kibā dantera ābhā — what a lustre of teeth

**6.6.** A sesame flower — how could it compare? such is the beauty of the nose;
turned on a lathe, even — what a lustre of teeth!

হিঙ্গুল ভালে হরিতালে নবনী দিল ভেঁজে ।
কাঁচা সোণা চাঁদখানা রসান দিল মেজে ॥

*hiṅgula bhāle haritāle nabanī dila bhem̐je |*
*kām̐cā soṇā cām̐dakhānā rasāna dila meje ||*

*Word for word:* hiṅgula bhāle haritāle — vermilion and orpiment; nabanī dila bhem̐je — kneaded with fresh butter; kām̐cā soṇā — pure gold; cām̐dakhānā — the moon; rasāna dila meje — laid on and burnished

**6.7.** Vermilion and orpiment were kneaded with fresh butter;
pure gold, the moon — laid on and burnished.

আল্‌তা তুলি দুধে গুলি কর দিয়াছে ছেনে ।
চাঁদকে আনি ছানি ছানি তায় বসালে জেনে ॥

*āltā tuli dudhe guli kara diyāche chene |*
*cām̐dake āni chāni chāni tāya basāle jene ||*

*Word for word:* āltā tuli — taking lac-dye; dudhe guli — dissolving in milk; kara diyāche chene — they moulded the hands; cām̐dake āni — bringing the moon; chāni chāni — sifting and sifting; tāya basāle jene — skilfully set it there

**6.8.** Dissolving lac-dye in milk, they moulded the hands;
they brought the moon, sifted it and sifted it — and skilfully set it there.[^34-19]

গলে হার শোভে তার কিবা বাহুর ভাতি ।
গগন হতে জল তুলতে নামল সোণার হাতী ॥

*gale hāra śobhe tāra kibā bāhura bhāti |*
*gagana hate jala tulate nāmala soṇāra hātī ||*

*Word for word:* gale hāra — a necklace on the neck; śobhe tāra — shines on Him; kibā bāhura bhāti — what a splendour of the arms; gagana hate — from the sky; jala tulte — to draw water; nāmala soṇāra hātī — a golden elephant came down

**6.9.** On His neck a necklace — how it shines! and what a splendour of arms! —
as if a golden elephant had come down from the sky to draw water.

কটি আঁটি পরিপাটী ধবল বসন সাজে ।
সুললিত ভুবনজিত পায়ে নূপুর বাজে ॥

*kaṭi ām̐ṭi paripāṭī dhabala basana sāje |*
*sulalita bhubanajita pāye nūpura bāje ||*

*Word for word:* kaṭi ām̐ṭi — girt at the waist; paripāṭī — neatly; dhabala basana sāje — the white cloth adorns; sulalita — graceful; bhubana-jita — conquering the world; pāye nūpura bāje — anklets ring on the feet

**6.10.** Neatly girt, the white cloth adorns Him;
graceful, conquering the world, the anklets ring on His feet.

রূপের নাগর রসের সাগর উদয় হলো এসে ।
নাগরী লোচনের মন তাইতে গেলো ভেসে ॥

*rūpera nāgara rasera sāgara udaya halo ese |*
*nāgarī locanera mana tāite gelo bhese ||*

*Word for word:* rūpera nāgara — the nagara of beauty; rasera sāgara — the ocean of rasa; udaya halo ese — has come and risen; nāgarī locanera mana — the mind of the nagari Lochana; tāite gelo bhese — by this was swept away

**6.11.** The nagara of beauty, the ocean of rasa, has come and risen [like the sun];
by this the mind of the nagari Lochana has been swept away."[^34-20]

[^34-17]: Signature: "the nagari Lochana." GPT1 — pp. 180–181, no. 68 (raga "yatharaga"; scan PDF pp. 439–440); GPT2 — 3.2, no. 68 (same text). No other
witnesses; attribution by GPT only — C. The pada begins as a narrative in the third person ("goes") and passes into the first ("I filled"); so in the original. On nagari-bhava
see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^34-18]: "The young wife" — GPT1 has "bam̐dhu" (usually "beloved, friend"); from the sense (stupor, bewilderment) it apparently stands here for badhū,
"young wife": the speaker about herself. "Beside herself" (cauura hārā) — the meaning is conjectural. "Friends" (sakhā) — the Lord's associates.
[^34-19]: 6.3–6.10 describe the form from the brows to the feet, as in padas on Krishna: the brows are "the teacher of Kama" (they teach him to shoot), the
colour of the body is a mixture of vermilion, orpiment and butter burnished like pure gold; "the moon sifted and set" in the hands is apparently the
nails (cf. "the moons of the nails"). "A god of rasa" (rasera de) is conjectural (de = deba).
[^34-20]: "The nagari Lochana": the poet calls himself a townswoman — he sings in the bhava of a nagari, putting himself in the heroine's place. The
tradition does not accept such worship of Gaura (introductory note). "The nagara of beauty" is an epithet of Gaura in nagari-bhava (ibid.).

## 7. Lochana Dasa — "śacīra gorā kāmera koṛā…" (GPT1 p. 181, no. 69)
*Nagari-bhava. The townswoman saw Gora at the ghat: curly hair, a garland of malati round His forehead; it is distasteful even to compare pure gold
with Him. She cannot explain it to her friend: she saw Him on the way to bathe and cannot take her eyes away; the secret has stayed in her heart; awake
and asleep Gaura is in her heart. Raga "yatharaga".*[^34-21]

শচীর গোরা কামের কোড়া দেখলাম ঘাটের কূলে ।
চাঁচর চুলে বেড়িয়া ভালে নব-মালতীর মালে ॥

*śacīra gorā kāmera koṛā dekhalāma ghāṭera kūle |*
*cām̐cara cule beṛiyā bhāle naba-mālatīra māle ||*

*Word for word:* śacīra gorā — Shachi's Gora; kāmera koṛā — the whip (or shoot?) of Kama; dekhlāma ghāṭera kūle — I saw on the bank at the ghat; cām̐cara cule — with curly hair; beṛiyā bhāle — encircling the forehead; naba-mālatīra māle — a garland of fresh malati

**7.1.** Shachi's Gora — the whip of Kama — I saw on the bank by the ghat:
curly hair, round the forehead a garland of fresh malati.

কাঁচা সোণা লাগে ঘৃণা রূপের তুলনা দিতে ।
(এমন) চিতচোরা মনোহরা নাইকো অবনীতে ॥

*kām̐cā soṇā lāge ghṛṇā rūpera tulanā dite |*
*(emana) citacorā manoharā nāiko abanīte ||*

*Word for word:* kām̐cā soṇā — pure gold; lāge ghṛṇā — it is distasteful; rūpera tulanā dite — to compare with the beauty; (emana) — (such); cita-corā — a thief of hearts; manoharā — a charmer of minds; nāiko abanīte — there is not on earth

**7.2.** Pure gold — it is distasteful even to compare it with His beauty;
(such) a thief of hearts, a charmer of minds, is not on earth.

কি আর বলিছ গো সই (তোমায়) বুঝাব কি ।
(ছাদে) স্নানে যেতে সখীর সাথে গৌর দেখেছি ॥

*ki āra balicha go sai (tomāya) bujhāba ki |*
*(chāde) snāne yete sakhīra sāthe gaura dekhechi ||*

*Word for word:* ki āra balicha go sai — what more are you saying, friend; (tomāya) — (to you); bujhāba ki — how shall I explain; (chāde) — (on the roof?); snāne yete — going to bathe; sakhīra sāthe — with friends; gaura dekhechi — I saw Gaura

**7.3.** What more are you saying, friend — how shall I explain (to you)?
(From the roof?) — going to bathe with my friends, I saw Gaura.

(সে) রূপ দেখি দুটী আঁখি ফিরাইতে নারি ।
পুনঃ তারে দেখবার তরে কতো সাধ করি ॥

*(se) rūpa dekhi duṭī ām̐khi phirāite nāri |*
*punaḥ tāre dekhabāra tare kato sādha kari ||*

*Word for word:* (se) rūpa dekhi — seeing (that) form; duṭī ām̐khi phirāite nāri — I cannot turn my two eyes away; punaḥ tāre — Him again; dekhvāra tare — in order to see; kato sādha kari — how I long

**7.4.** Seeing (that) form, I cannot turn my two eyes away;
how I long to see Him again!

কি আর বলিছ গো সই তুমি ত আছ ভাল ।
আমার মরমের কথা মরমেই রহিল ॥

*ki āra balicha go sai tumi ta ācha bhāla |*
*āmāra maramera kathā maramei rahila ||*

*Word for word:* ki āra balicha go sai — what more are you saying, friend; tumi ta ācha bhāla — you are well off; āmāra maramera kathā — my heart's secret; maramei rahila — has stayed in the heart

**7.5.** What more are you saying, friend — you are well off;
but my heart's secret has stayed in my heart.

জাগিতে ঘুমাইতে সদা গৌর জাগে মনে ।
লোচন বলে যে দেখেছে সেই সে উহা জানে ॥

*jāgite ghumāite sadā gaura jāge mane |*
*locana bale ye dekheche sei se uhā jāne ||*

*Word for word:* jāgite ghumāite — awake and asleep; sadā gaura jāge mane — Gaura is ever in the heart; locana bale — says Lochana; ye dekheche — whoever has seen; sei se uhā jāne — he knows it

**7.6.** Awake or asleep, Gaura is always in my heart;
says Lochana: whoever has seen, he knows it.

[^34-21]: Signature: "Lochana." GPT1 — p. 181, no. 69 (raga "yatharaga"; scan PDF p. 440); GPT2 — 3.2, no. 69 (same text). No other witnesses;
attribution by GPT only — C. "The whip
of Kama" (kāmera koṛā) is an unclear image: "whip," or, reading kom̐ṛā, "shoot"; in sense — the One stronger than Kama (cf. "Madana-mohana,"
introductory note). The insertion "(chāde)" in 7.3 — "on the roof" (?): the sense is unclear. On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section
(chapter 27).

## 8. Lochana Dasa — "eka nāgarī bale didi nāite yakhana yāi…" (GPT1 pp. 181–182, no. 70)
*Nagari-bhava. A townswoman tells how, going to bathe, she put back her veil and saw Gaura; she ran home, but her eyes stayed with Him; her body
trembles; the ghat shines with His body, young women crowd; with the rope of anuraga He pulls her soul. She playfully warns her friend: look — and
you are lost; if you would keep the family honour, stay at home. Raga "yatharaga".*[^34-22]

এক নাগরী বলে দিদি নাইতে যখন যাই ।
ঘোম্‌টা খুলে বদন তুলে দেখেছিলাম তাই ॥

*eka nāgarī bale didi nāite yakhana yāi |*
*ghomṭā khule badana tule dekhechilāma tāi ||*

*Word for word:* eka nāgarī bale — one nagari says; didi — sister; nāite yakhana yāi — when I went to bathe; ghomṭā khule — putting back the veil; badana tule — raising the face; dekhechilāma tāi — I saw that

**8.1.** One nagari says: "Sister, when I went to bathe,
I put back my veil, raised my face — and saw Him.

রূপ দেখে চম্‌কে উঠে ঘরকে এলাম ধেয়ে ।
দুটী নয়ন বাঁধা রইল গৌরপানে চেয়ে ॥

*rūpa dekhe camke uṭhe gharake elāma dheye |*
*duṭī nayana bām̐dhā raila gaurapāne ceye ||*

*Word for word:* rūpa dekhe — seeing the form; camke uṭhe — starting; gharake elāma dheye — I ran home; duṭī nayana bām̐dhā raila — the two eyes stayed tied; gaura-pāne ceye — gazing at Gaura

**8.2.** Seeing the form, I started — and ran home;
but my two eyes stayed tied — gazing at Gaura.

গা থর থর করে আমার অঙ্গ সকল কাঁপে ।
নাসার নোলক ঝলক দিয়ে মনের ভিতর ঝাঁপে ॥

*gā thara thara kare āmāra aṅga sakala kām̐pe |*
*nāsāra nolaka jhalaka diye manera bhitara jhām̐pe ||*

*Word for word:* gā thara thara kare āmāra — my body trembles; aṅga sakala kām̐pe — all limbs shake; nāsāra nolaka — the pendant in the nose; jhalaka diye — flashing; manera bhitara jhām̐pe — leaps into the heart

**8.3.** My body trembles, all my limbs shake;
the pendant in the nose, flashing, leaps into my very heart.[^34-23]

জলের ঘাট আলো ক'রেছে গৌর-অঙ্গের ছটা ।
রূপ দেখিতে হুড় পড়েছে নব যুবতীর ঘটা ॥

*jalera ghāṭa ālo ka'reche gaura-aṅgera chaṭā |*
*rūpa dekhite huṛa paṛeche naba yubatīra ghaṭā ||*

*Word for word:* jalera ghāṭa — the bathing ghat; ālo kareche — has been lit; gaura-aṅgera chaṭā — by the radiance of Gaura's body; rūpa dekhite — to see the form; huṛa paṛeche — there is a throng; naba yubatīra ghaṭā — crowds of young women

**8.4.** The ghat is lit by the radiance of Gaura's body;
to see His beauty, crowds of young women throng.

সাধ কৈরে দেখতে গেলাম এমন কেবা জানে ।
অনুরাগের ডুরি দিয়ে প্রাণকে ধৈরে টানে ॥

*sādha kaire dekhate gelāma emana kebā jāne |*
*anurāgera ḍuri diye prāṇake dhaire ṭāne ||*

*Word for word:* sādha kaire — out of fancy; dekhte gelāma — I went to see; emana kebā jāne — who knew it would be so; anurāgera ḍuri diye — with the rope of anuraga; prāṇake dhaire ṭāne — He seizes and pulls the soul

**8.5.** I went to look out of curiosity — who knew it would be like this?
With the rope of anuraga He pulls my soul.

উড়ু উড়ু করে প্রাণ রইতে নারি ঘরে ।
গৌরচাঁদকে না দেখিলে প্রাণ সে কেমন করে ॥

*uṛu uṛu kare prāṇa raite nāri ghare |*
*gauracām̐dake nā dekhile prāṇa se kemana kare ||*

*Word for word:* uṛu uṛu kare prāṇa — the soul longs to fly away; raite nāri ghare — I cannot stay at home; gauracām̐dake nā dekhile — not seeing Gaurachand; prāṇa se kemana kare — how the soul is

**8.6.** My soul longs to fly away, I cannot stay at home;
not seeing Gaurachand, I do not know what is happening to my soul.

চাইলে নয়ন বাঁধা রবে মনচোরা তার রূপ ।
হাস্যবয়ান রাঙ্গা নয়ান এই না রসের কূপ ॥

*cāile nayana bām̐dhā rabe manacorā tāra rūpa |*
*hāsyabayāna rāṅgā nayāna ei nā rasera kūpa ||*

*Word for word:* cāile — if you look; nayana bām̐dhā rabe — the eyes will stay tied; mana-corā tāra rūpa — His form steals the heart; hāsya-bayāna — the smiling face; rāṅgā nayāna — reddish eyes; ei nā rasera kūpa — here it is, the well of rasa

**8.7.** Look — and your eyes will stay tied: His form steals the heart;
the smiling face, the reddish eyes — here it is, the well of rasa!

চাইলে মেনে মরবি ক্ষেপি কুল সে রবে নাই ।
কুলশীল রাখ্‌বি যদি থাক্‌গা বিরল ঠাঁই ॥

*cāile mene marabi kṣepi kula se rabe nāi |*
*kulaśīla rākhvi yadi thākgā birala ṭhām̐i ||*

*Word for word:* cāile — if you look; mene — mind you (= surely); marvi kṣepi — you will die gone mad; kula se rabe nāi — the family will not survive; kulaśīla rākhvi yadi — if you would keep family and good conduct; thākgā birala ṭhām̐i — stay in a secluded place

**8.8.** Look — mind you, you will die gone mad, your family honour will not survive;
if you would keep family and good conduct — stay in a secluded place.

কুল খোওয়াবি বউরি হবি লাগ্‌বে রসের ঢেউ ।
লোচন বলে রসিক হ'লে বুঝতে পারে কেউ ॥

*kula khooyābi bauri habi lāgve rasera ḍheu |*
*locana bale rasika ha'le bujhate pāre keu ||*

*Word for word:* kula khoyābi — you will lose the family; bauri habi — you will go crazy; lāgve rasera ḍheu — the wave of rasa will strike; locana bale — says Lochana; rasika ha'le — if one knows rasa; bujhte pāre keu — someone can understand

**8.9.** You will lose your family, you will go crazy, the wave of rasa will strike."
Says Lochana: only one who knows rasa can understand this.[^34-24]

[^34-22]: Signature: "Lochana." GPT1 — pp. 181–182, no. 70 (raga "yatharaga"; scan PDF pp. 440–441); GPT2 — 3.2, no. 70 (same text). No other witnesses;
attribution by GPT only — C. Lines 8.3 and 8.5b recur almost word for word in no. 13 (no. 75, 13.4b, 13.6) — lines common to these songs. On nagari-bhava see the introductory
note to the section (chapter 27).
[^34-23]: "The pendant in the nose" (nāsāra nolaka) is apparently Gaura's ornament (cf. no. 13, 13.3, 13.6: "a pendant swings in the nose… at Gora's
laughter"); in padas on Krishna — the pearl (veshara) in His nose. Translated as in the original.
[^34-24]: 8.7–8.9 are a playful "warning" to the friend: so great is the power of the Lord's form. "Crazy" (bauri = bāurī). The motif of "losing the
family" — see note 7.

## 9. Lochana Dasa — "gorārūpa rasera kūpa sahajei eta…" (GPT1 p. 182, no. 71)
*Nagari-bhava. Gora's form is a well of rasa just by itself — and if He were to use His art, what then! Should He arrange His curls, a noble wife
could not keep her family honour; should He glance sidelong, should He ask — who could withstand? Rati herself, leaving Kama, worships Gora's feet.
The poet: "Now I have made Gora my all." Raga "yatharaga".*[^34-25]

গোরারূপ রসের কূপ সহজেই এত ।
করে কলা রসের ছলা তবে হয় কত ॥

*gorārūpa rasera kūpa sahajei eta |*
*kare kalā rasera chalā tabe haya kata ||*

*Word for word:* gorārūpa — Gora's form; rasera kūpa — a well of rasa; sahajei eta — is so much by itself; kare kalā — [if] He uses His art; rasera chalā — the wiles of rasa; tabe haya kata — how much then

**9.1.** Gora's form — a well of rasa — is so much just by itself;
and if He uses His art, the wiles of rasa, — what will it be then!

যদি বাঁধে বিনোদছাঁদে চাঁচর চিকণ চুল ।
তবে সতী কুলবতী রাখতে নারে কুল ॥

*yadi bām̐dhe binodachām̐de cām̐cara cikaṇa cula |*
*tabe satī kulabatī rākhate nāre kula ||*

*Word for word:* yadi bām̐dhe — if He binds; binoda-chām̐de — gracefully; cām̐cara cikaṇa cula — the soft curling hair; tabe satī kulabatī — then the faithful noble wife; rākhte nāre kula — cannot keep the family honour

**9.2.** If He gracefully arranges His soft curling hair,
then a faithful, noble wife cannot keep her family honour.

যাঁরে দেখে নয়ন বাঁকে তার কি রহে মান ।
যদি যাচে তবে কি বাঁচে রসবতীর প্রাণ ॥

*yām̐re dekhe nayana bām̐ke tāra ki rahe māna |*
*yadi yāce tabe ki bām̐ce rasabatīra prāṇa ||*

*Word for word:* yām̐re dekhe nayana bām̐ke — whom He looks at sidelong; tāra ki rahe māna — will her pride remain; yadi yāce — if He asks; tabe ki bām̐ce — would it survive; rasabatīra prāṇa — the life of the rasavati

**9.3.** Whomever He glances at sidelong — will her pride remain?
and if He should ask — would the rasavati survive?[^34-26]

গলায় মালা বাহু দোলা দিয়ে চলে যায় ।
কামের রতি ছাড়ি পতি ভজে গোরার পায় ॥

*galāya mālā bāhu dolā diye cale yāya |*
*kāmera rati chāṛi pati bhaje gorāra pāya ||*

*Word for word:* galāya mālā — with a garland on the neck; bāhu dolā diye — swinging the arms; cale yāya — He passes by; kāmera rati — Kama's Rati; chāṛi pati — leaving the husband; bhaje gorāra pāya — worships Gora's feet

**9.4.** With a garland on His neck, swinging His arms, He passes by —
Rati herself, Kama's wife, leaving her husband, worships Gora's feet.[^34-27]

বুক ভরা গোরা মোরা দেখ্‌লে ভরে বুক ।
কোলে হেন করি যেন সুখের উপর সুখ ॥

*buka bharā gorā morā dekhle bhare buka |*
*kole hena kari yena sukhera upara sukha ||*

*Word for word:* buka bharā — filling the breast; gorā morā — our Gora; dekhle bhare buka — seeing Him, the breast fills; kole hena kari yena — as if I held Him in my arms; sukhera upara sukha — joy upon joy

**9.5.** Our Gora fills the breast: look — and the breast is full;
as if one held Him in one's arms — joy upon joy.

হাসির ধারা সুধাপারা শীতল করা প্রাণ ।
রসবশ (সর্ব্বস্ব) সরবস সাধের স্বরূপখান ॥

*hāsira dhārā sudhāpārā śītala karā prāṇa |*
*rasabaśa (sarvvasva) sarabasa sādhera svarūpakhāna ||*

*Word for word:* hāsira dhārā — the stream of the smile; sudhā-pārā — like nectar; śītala karā prāṇa — cooling the soul; rasa-baśa — subject to rasa; (sarvvasva) — (everything); sarabasa — all my wealth; sādhera svarūpa-khāna — the form of my longing

**9.6.** The stream of His smile, like nectar, cools the soul;
subject to rasa, He is (everything) all my wealth, the form of my longing.[^34-28]

শুন প্রাণ-প্রিয়সখি কি কহিবো আর ।
লোচন বলে এবার আমি গোরা করেছি সার ॥

*śuna prāṇa-priyasakhi ki kahibo āra |*
*locana bale ebāra āmi gorā karechi sāra ||*

*Word for word:* śuna prāṇa-priya-sakhi — listen, friend dear to my heart; ki kahibo āra — what more shall I say; locana bale — says Lochana; ebāra āmi — now I; gorā karechi sāra — have made Gora my all

**9.7.** Listen, friend dear to my heart, what more shall I say?
Says Lochana: now I have made Gora my all.

[^34-25]: Signature: "Lochana." GPT1 — p. 182, no. 71 (raga "yatharaga"; scan PDF p. 441); GPT2 — 3.2, no. 71 (same text). No other witnesses;
attribution by GPT only — C. Couplets
9.1–9.4 recur almost word for word in no. 20 (no. 83, 20.4–20.6, 20.8) — lines common to these songs. On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the
section (chapter 27).
[^34-26]: 9.2–9.3 are all in the conditional ("if"): the townswoman pictures what would happen if Gora wished to charm. Translated exactly. According to CB
(Adi-khanda), the Lord in Navadvipa did not look at women; the notion of Him as a nagara seeking the townswomen's love is rejected by the tradition
(note 3; introductory note). "Rasavati" (rasabatī) — "she who is full of rasa," the heroine.
[^34-27]: Rati is the wife of Kama, the god of love: even she would leave her husband for Gora — a hyperbole of a beauty surpassing Kama himself (cf.
Krishna's epithet "Madana-mohana," "the charmer of the god of love").
[^34-28]: "(sarvvasva)" is the GPT compiler's gloss on saravasa ("all one's wealth"); translated in brackets. "Subject to rasa" (rasabaśa) — in GPT1 joined
to "all my wealth"; it may also be understood of the speaker herself: "overcome by rasa."

## 10. Lochana Dasa — "gaura-ratana ka're yatana rākhaba hiyāra mājhe…" (GPT1 pp. 182–183, no. 72)
*Nagari-bhava. The townswoman will carefully keep the jewel Gaura in her heart, put on ornaments of His colour, write "Gaura" on her body with
gorochana, walk proudly along the road repeating "Gaura," tear up her family by the roots and give shame to the fire; Gaurachand has set the snares of
rasa in every house. Raga "yatharaga".*[^34-29]

গৌর-রতন ক'রে যতন রাখব হিয়ার মাঝে ।
গৌর-বরণ ভূষণ পরবো যেখানে যেমন সাজে ॥

*gaura-ratana ka're yatana rākhaba hiyāra mājhe |*
*gaura-baraṇa bhūṣaṇa parabo yekhāne yemana sāje ||*

*Word for word:* gaura-ratana — the jewel Gaura; ka're yatana — carefully; rākhaba hiyāra mājhe — I will keep in the heart; gaura-baraṇa bhūṣaṇa parabo — I will wear ornaments of Gaura's colour; yekhāne yemana sāje — whichever suits where

**10.1.** The jewel Gaura I will carefully keep in my heart;
I will put on ornaments of Gaura's colour — whichever suits where.

গৌরবরণ ফুলের ঝাঁপায় লোটন বাঁধবো চুলে ।
গৌর বৈলে গৌরব কৈরে পথে যাব চ'লে ॥

*gaurabaraṇa phulera jhām̐pāya loṭana bām̐dhabo cule |*
*gaura baile gauraba kaire pathe yāba ca'le ||*

*Word for word:* gaura-baraṇa phulera jhām̐pāya — with golden flowers in the jhapa; loṭana bām̐dhvo cule — I will tie the hair in a knot; gaura baile — saying "Gaura"; gauraba kaire — with pride; pathe yāba ca'le — I will walk along the road

**10.2.** With golden flowers in my jhapa I will tie my hair in a knot;
saying "Gaura," I will walk along the road with pride.[^34-30]

গৌরবরণ গোরোচনায় গৌর লিখবো গায় ।
গৌর বৈলে রূপ যৌবন সমর্পিবো পায় ॥

*gaurabaraṇa gorocanāya gaura likhabo gāya |*
*gaura baile rūpa yaubana samarpibo pāya ||*

*Word for word:* gaura-baraṇa gorocanāya — with golden gorochana; gaura likhvo gāya — I will write "Gaura" on the body; gaura baile — saying "Gaura"; rūpa yaubana — beauty and youth; samarpibo pāya — I will offer at the feet

**10.3.** With golden gorochana I will write "Gaura" on my body;
saying "Gaura," I will lay my beauty and youth at [His] feet.

কুলের মূল উপাড়িয়ে ভাসাব গঙ্গার জলে ।
লাজের মুখে আগুন দিয়া বেড়াবো গৌর ব'লে ॥

*kulera mūla upāṛiye bhāsāba gaṅgāra jale |*
*lājera mukhe āguna diyā beṛābo gaura ba'le ||*

*Word for word:* kulera mūla upāṛiye — tearing up the family by the roots; bhāsāba gaṅgāra jale — I will float it on the waters of the Ganga; lājera mukhe āguna diyā — giving shame to the funeral fire (lit. putting fire to the face of shame); beṛābo gaura va'le — I will go about saying "Gaura"

**10.4.** Tearing up my family by the roots, I will float it away on the waters of the Ganga;
giving shame to the funeral fire, I will go about saying "Gaura."

গৌরচাঁদ রসের ফাঁদ পেতেছে ঘরে ঘরে ।
সতী পতি ছাড়ি দেহ দিতে সাধ করে ॥

*gauracām̐da rasera phām̐da peteche ghare ghare |*
*satī pati chāṛi deha dite sādha kare ||*

*Word for word:* gauracām̐da — Gaurachand; rasera phām̐da — the snare of rasa; peteche ghare ghare — has set in every house; satī — the faithful wife; pati chāṛi — leaving the husband; deha dite sādha kare — longs to give her body

**10.5.** Gaurachand has set the snares of rasa in every house:
the faithful wife, leaving her husband, longs to give [Him] her body.[^34-31]

(তোমরা) কিছুই বলো রূপসাগরে সকলি গেল ভেসে ।
লোচন বলে কুতূহলে দেখবে বৈসে বৈসে ॥

*(tomarā) kichui balo rūpasāgare sakali gela bhese |*
*locana bale kutūhale dekhabe baise baise ||*

*Word for word:* (tomarā) — (you); kichui balo — say anything; rūpa-sāgare — in the ocean of beauty; sakali gela bhese — everything has floated away; locana bale kutūhale — says Lochana with delight; dekhve baise baise — sit and wait, you will see

**10.6.** (You) say what you like — in the ocean of beauty everything has floated away.
Says Lochana with delight: sit and wait — you will see.

[^34-29]: Signature: "Lochana." GPT1 — pp. 182–183, no. 72 (raga "yatharaga"; scan PDF pp. 441–442); GPT2 — 3.2, no. 72 (same text). No other witnesses;
attribution by GPT only — C.
On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^34-30]: A play on gaura — gaurava ("Gaura" — "pride"): "saying 'Gaura,' with pride" (cf. chapter 28, note 74). "Jhapa" (jhām̐pā) is an ornament of the
braids; "knot" (loṭana) — a loosely tied bun. Gorochana is a yellow pigment used for tilaka; "to write the name on the body" — as Vaishnavas write the
names of the Lord with sandal paste.
[^34-31]: "Longs to give [Him] her body" (deha dite sādha kare) is a direct motif of attraction, translated exactly. This is the very notion of
"gaura-nagari" which the tradition rejects (note 3; introductory note). "Giving shame to the funeral fire" (10.4; lājera mukhe āguna diyā) — lit.
"putting fire to the face of shame," as to the dead.

## 11. Lochana Dasa — "nayane nayana diye ki guṇa karila priye…" (GPT1 p. 183, no. 73)
*Nagari-bhava (a dream). Refrain: "What spell has the Beloved cast with a single glance!" A townswoman tells in tears: she had long wished to drink
the nectar of His lips and, pining, lay down at night; at midnight she dreamed that Gora was on her breast, embracing and kissing her; waking at
dawn, she reproaches the creator and cannot stay at home. The poet: do not weep — go into your own house, hold Gorachand in your heart. Raga
"yatharaga".*[^34-32]

নয়নে নয়ন দিয়ে । কি গুণ করিল প্রিয়ে ॥
(ওঝা-রাজ গুণীর শিরোমণি ॥)

*nayane nayana diye | ki guṇa karila priye ||*
*(ojhā-rāja guṇīra śiromaṇi ||)*

*Word for word:* nayane nayana diye — eye to eye; ki guṇa karila priye — what a spell the Beloved cast; (ojhā-rāja — king of exorcists; guṇīra śiromaṇi — crest-jewel of sorcerers)

**11.1.** *(Refrain)* Eye to eye — what a spell the Beloved has cast!
(King of exorcists, crest-jewel of sorcerers!)

দুটি আঁখি ছল্‌ছলায়ে এক নাগরী বলে ।
গৌরলেহের কি বা জানি রসে অঙ্গ ঢলে ॥

*duṭi ām̐khi chalchalāye eka nāgarī bale |*
*gauralehera ki bā jāni rase aṅga ḍhale ||*

*Word for word:* duṭi ām̐khi chalchalāye — with brimming eyes; eka nāgarī bale — one nagari says; gaura-lehera ki vā jāni — what do I know of Gaura's love; rase aṅga ḍhale — the body melts with rasa

**11.2.** With tears in her eyes one nagari says:
"What do I know of Gaura's love? — my body melts with rasa.

অনেক দিনের সাধ ছিল মোর অধররস পীতে ।
মনের দুখে ভাব্‌না ক'রে শুয়েছিলাম রেতে ॥

*aneka dinera sādha chila mora adhararasa pīte |*
*manera dukhe bhābnā ka're śuyechilāma rete ||*

*Word for word:* aneka dinera sādha chila mora — for many days I had the wish; adhara-rasa pīte — to drink the nectar of the lips; manera dukhe — with sorrow at heart; bhābnā ka're — brooding; śuyechilāma rete — I lay down at night

**11.3.** For many days I had the wish to drink the nectar of [His] lips;
with sorrow in my heart, brooding, I lay down at night.

যখন আমি মাঝ-নিশিতে ঘুমে হ'য়েছি ভোরা ।
তখন আমি দেখ্‌ছি যেন বুকের উপর গোরা ॥

*yakhana āmi mājha-niśite ghume ha'yechi bhorā |*
*takhana āmi dekhchi yena bukera upara gorā ||*

*Word for word:* yakhana āmi mājh-niśite — when I at midnight; ghume ha'yechi bhorā — was lost in sleep; takhana āmi dekhchi yena — then I see as if; bukera upara gorā — Gora on my breast

**11.4.** When at midnight I was lost in sleep,
then I see — as if Gora were upon my breast.[^34-33]

নবকিশোর গাখানি তার কাঁচা ননী হেন ।
ভুজলতায় বেঁধে কথা কয় ছেড়ে দিব কেন ॥

*nabakiśora gākhāni tāra kām̐cā nanī hena |*
*bhujalatāya bem̐dhe kathā kaya cheṛe diba kena ||*

*Word for word:* naba-kiśora — a fresh youth; gākhāni tāra — His body; kām̐cā nanī hena — like fresh butter; bhuja-latāya bem̐dhe — binding with creeper-arms; kathā kaya — He says; cheṛe diba kena — why should I let [you] go

**11.5.** A fresh youth, His body like fresh butter;
binding me with His creeper-arms, He says: 'Why should I let you go?'

হেন মতে মন ডুবিয়ে ঠেক্‌লাম সুখের দুখে ।
বদন ঢলে অধর-রস পড়লো আমার মুখে ॥

*hena mate mana ḍubiye ṭheklāma sukhera dukhe |*
*badana ḍhale adhara-rasa paṛalo āmāra mukhe ||*

*Word for word:* hena mate — thus; mana ḍubiye — immersing the heart; ṭheklāma sukhera dukhe — I was caught in a sweet torment; badana ḍhale — the face bent down; adhara-rasa — the nectar of the lips; paṛlo āmāra mukhe — fell into my mouth

**11.6.** Thus, my heart immersed, I was caught in a sweet torment:
His face bent down — the nectar of His lips fell into my mouth.

অধররস খেয়ে তাপিত প্রাণ যে শীতল হলো ।
বিলাসান্তে সময় মতে নিশি পোহাইলো ॥

*adhararasa kheye tāpita prāṇa ye śītala halo |*
*bilāsānte samaya mate niśi pohāilo ||*

*Word for word:* adhara-rasa kheye — having tasted the nectar of the lips; tāpita prāṇa ye śītala halo — the burning soul grew cool; bilāsānte — after the play; samaya mate — in due time; niśi pohāilo — the night came to an end

**11.7.** I tasted the nectar of His lips — and my thirsting soul grew cool;
after the play, in due time, the night came to an end.

হায় হায় হায় বলি উঠ্‌লাম চমকিয়ে ।
হায় রে বিধি রসের নিধি নিলি কেন দিয়ে ॥

*hāya hāya hāya bali uṭhlāma camakiye |*
*hāya re bidhi rasera nidhi nili kena diye ||*

*Word for word:* hāya hāya hāya bali — crying "alas, alas, alas"; uṭhlāma camakiye — I started up; hāya re bidhi — ah, creator; rasera nidhi — the treasure of rasa; nili kena diye — why did you give and take it away

**11.8.** 'Alas, alas, alas!' I cried and started up:
'Ah, creator, the treasure of rasa — why did you give it and take it away?'

প্রাণ ছন্‌ছন্‌ করে আমার মন ছন্‌ছন্‌ করে ।
আধ-কপালে মাথার বিষে রৈতে নারি ঘরে ॥

*prāṇa chanchan kare āmāra mana chanchan kare |*
*ādha-kapāle māthāra biṣe raite nāri ghare ||*

*Word for word:* prāṇa chan-chan kare āmāra — my soul aches; mana chan-chan kare — my heart aches; ādha-kapāle — half the head; māthāra biṣe — with the pain in the head; raite nāri ghare — I cannot stay at home

**11.9.** My soul aches, my heart aches,
half my head is throbbing — I cannot stay at home."

লোচন বলে কাঁদছিস্‌ কেনে ঢোক্‌ আপনার ঘর ।
হিয়ার মাঝে গোরাচাঁদে মন ডুবায়ে ধর ॥

*locana bale kām̐dachis kene ḍhok āpanāra ghara |*
*hiyāra mājhe gorācām̐de mana ḍubāye dhara ||*

*Word for word:* locana bale — says Lochana; kām̐dchis kene — why are you weeping; ḍhok āpanāra ghara — go into your own house; hiyāra mājhe — in the heart; gorācām̐de — Gorachand; mana ḍubāye dhara — hold, immersing the mind

**11.10.** Says Lochana: "Why are you weeping? Go into your own house:
deep in your heart hold Gorachand, immersing your mind in Him."[^34-34]

[^34-32]: Signature: "Lochana." GPT1 — p. 183, no. 73 (raga "yatharaga"; refrain marked "dhru" in brackets; scan PDF p. 442); GPT2 — 3.2, no. 73 (same
text). No other witnesses; attribution by GPT only — C. "Spell" (guṇa) — the sorcery of an exorcist (ojhā): Gaura's glance as a charm. On nagari-bhava
see the introductory note
to the section (chapter 27).
[^34-33]: 11.4–11.7 are a dream with a direct motif of sambhoga (embrace, kiss, "play"); translated exactly, without softening. The dream is the
townswoman's imagination, not an event of the lila; the Lord in His lila did not touch women and in Navadvipa did not look at them (CB, Adi-khanda);
the tradition does not accept "gaura-nagari" (Bhaktisiddhanta; introductory note); according to Majumdar, such padas of GPT are a late layer. GPT1
gives under the line a variant to 11.4b: "I look — on my breast is Gora, Shachi's darling."
[^34-34]: "Go into your own house" (ḍhoka āpanāra ghara) — the poet answers the heroine: do not weep over the dream, but turn inward and hold Gora in
your heart. The same ending in no. 13 (13.13), a similar one in no. 20 (20.10).

## 12. Lochana Dasa — "hem̐i go hem̐i go gorā kene nā yāya pāsarā…" (GPT1 pp. 183–184, no. 74)
*Nagari-bhava. The townswoman cannot forget Gora: the secret came out within a couple of days; in sleep He is on her heart, even in her husband's
arms; going to bathe, she remembers Him and falls on the spot. The poet jokes: "Go and tell why your foot slipped!" Raga "yatharaga".*[^34-35]

হেঁই গো হেঁই গো গোরা কেনে না যায় পাসরা ।
গোরারূপে মন মজিলো বাউল হৈল পারা ॥

*hem̐i go hem̐i go gorā kene nā yāya pāsarā |*
*gorārūpe mana majilo bāula haila pārā ||*

*Word for word:* hem̐i go hem̐i go — hey, hey; gorā kene nā yāya pāsarā — why can Gora not be forgotten; gorārūpe — in Gora's form; mana majilo — the mind is swallowed; bāula haila pārā — I became as if mad

**12.1.** Hey, hey! why can Gora not be forgotten?
Gora's form has swallowed my mind — I have become as if mad.

নয়নে লাগিল গোরা কি করিব সই ।
গুপত কথা ব্যক্ত হলো দিন দুই চার বৈ ॥

*nayane lāgila gorā ki kariba sai |*
*gupata kathā byakta halo dina dui cāra bai ||*

*Word for word:* nayane lāgila gorā — Gora lodged in the eyes; ki kariba sai — what shall I do, friend; gupata kathā — the secret; byakta halo — came out; dina dui cāra bai — within no more than two or four days

**12.2.** Gora has lodged in my eyes — what am I to do, friend?
The secret has come out — not even two or four days have passed.

শয়নে স্বপনে গোরা হিয়ার উপরে ।
নিজপতি কোরে থাকি কি আর বলো মোরে ॥

*śayane svapane gorā hiyāra upare |*
*nijapati kore thāki ki āra balo more ||*

*Word for word:* śayane svapane — in sleep and in dreams; gorā hiyāra upare — Gora upon the heart; nija-pati kore thāki — I lie in my own husband's arms; ki āra balo more — what more will you tell me

**12.3.** In sleep and in dreams Gora is upon my heart;
even lying in my own husband's arms — what more will you tell me?[^34-36]

তৈল খুরি লৈয়া যদি সিনান্‌ বারে যাই ।
গোরারূপ মনে পড়ে পড়ি সেই ঠাঁই ॥

*taila khuri laiyā yadi sinān bāre yāi |*
*gorārūpa mane paṛe paṛi sei ṭhām̐i ||*

*Word for word:* taila khuri laiyā — taking a cup of oil; yadi sinān bāre yāi — if I go to bathe; gorārūpa mane paṛe — Gora's form comes to mind; paṛi sei ṭhām̐i — I fall right there

**12.4.** If, taking a cup of oil, I go to bathe —
Gora's form comes to mind, and I fall right there.

গা থর্‌ থর্‌ অঙ্গ কাঁপে কিছু বলতে নারি ॥

*gā thar thar aṅga kām̐pe kichu balate nāri ||*

*Word for word:* gā thar thar — the body trembles; aṅga kām̐pe — the limbs shake; kichu balte nāri — I cannot say anything

**12.5.** My body trembles, my limbs shake — I cannot say anything.[^34-37]

নিশি দিশি হিয়ায় জাগে কি বল্‌ব তা বলে ।
লোচন বলে বল্‌গা কেনে পা গ্যালো পিছলে ॥

*niśi diśi hiyāya jāge ki balva tā bale |*
*locana bale balgā kene pā gyālo pichale ||*

*Word for word:* niśi diśi — night and day; hiyāya jāge — He wakes in the heart; ki balva tā bale — what shall I say of it; locana bale — says Lochana; balgā — go and tell; kene pā gyālo pichle — why your foot slipped

**12.6.** Night and day He wakes in my heart — what shall I say of it?
Says Lochana: "Go and tell why your foot has slipped!"

[^34-35]: Signature: "Lochana." GPT1 — pp. 183–184, no. 74 (raga "yatharaga"; scan PDF pp. 442–443); GPT2 — 3.2, no. 74 (same text). No other witnesses;
attribution by GPT only — C.
"Mad" (bāula) — lit. "baul," possessed, "beside oneself." On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^34-36]: Gora is on her heart "even in her own husband's arms" — the parakiya motif transferred to the townswomen (notes 7, 11).
[^34-37]: In GPT1 and GPT2 this is a single line (with the mark ॥); its pair has apparently dropped out. "Your foot has slipped" (12.6) — the poet's joke:
the heroine has "stumbled," losing her head over Gora.

## 13. Lochana Dasa — "eka nāgarī hese bale śunago marama sai…" (GPT1 pp. 184–185, no. 75)
*Nagari-bhava. One townswoman, laughing, tells her intimate friend: they have never seen such a "man of rasa" — the pendant swings, at His laughter
one cannot be still; she went to look by chance — and He pulls her heart with the rope of anuraga; from under her veil she saw the dancer of rasa go
dancing through the bazaar of Nadia. Another answers: I will go to another land — shut the doors of this one, go to the "inner village"; a jewel
must be kept secret. The poet: go into your own house, hold Gorachand in your heart. Raga "yatharaga".*[^34-38]

এক নাগরী হেসে বলে শুন্‌গো মরম সই ।
মরম্‌ জানিস্‌ রসিক বটিস্‌ তেঁই সে তোরে কই ॥

*eka nāgarī hese bale śungo marama sai |*
*maram jānis rasika baṭis tem̐i se tore kai ||*

*Word for word:* eka nāgarī hese bale — one nagari, laughing, says; śungo marama sai — listen, intimate friend; maram jānis — you know what is hidden; rasika baṭis — you know rasa; tem̐i se tore kai — that is why I tell you

**13.1.** One nagari, laughing, says: "Listen, my intimate friend:
you know what is hidden, you know rasa — that is why I tell you.

তো বিনে গো রসের কথা কইবো কার ঠাঁই ।
এমন রসের মানুষ মোরা কভু দেখি নাই ॥

*to bine go rasera kathā kaibo kāra ṭhām̐i |*
*emana rasera mānuṣa morā kabhu dekhi nāi ||*

*Word for word:* to bine go — besides you; rasera kathā — of rasa; kaibo kāra ṭhām̐i — to whom shall I speak; emana rasera mānuṣa — such a man of rasa; morā kabhu dekhi nāi — we have never seen

**13.2.** Besides you, to whom should I speak of rasa?
Such a man of rasa as our [Gora] we have never seen.

কিবা জলদ্‌ ঝলক মতি নাশায় নোলক দোলে ।
স্থির হৈতে নারি গোরার হাসির হিল্লোলে ॥

*kibā jalad jhalaka mati nāśāya nolaka dole |*
*sthira haite nāri gorāra hāsira hillole ||*

*Word for word:* kibā jalad — how it burns (?); jhalaka mati — the pearl flashes; nāśāya nolaka dole — the pendant swings in the nose; sthira haite nāri — I cannot be still; gorāra hāsira hillole — for the waves of Gora's laughter

**13.3.** How it burns, how it flashes, the pearl — a pendant swings in the nose;
I cannot be still for the waves of Gora's laughter.

হঠাৎকারে দেখ্‌তে গেলাম এমন কে তা জানে ।
অনুরাগের ডুরি দিয়ে মনকে ধৈরে টানে ॥

*haṭhātkāre dekhte gelāma emana ke tā jāne |*
*anurāgera ḍuri diye manake dhaire ṭāne ||*

*Word for word:* haṭhātkāre — by chance; dekhte gelāma — I went to look; emana ke tā jāne — who knew it would be so; anurāgera ḍuri diye — with the rope of anuraga; manake dhaire ṭāne — He seizes and pulls the heart

**13.4.** By chance I went to look — who knew it would be like this?
With the rope of anuraga He has seized my heart and pulls it.

অঙ্গঘটা রূপের ছটা পথে চলে যায় ।
গৌররূপের ঠমক দেখে চমক্‌ লাগে গায় ॥

*aṅgaghaṭā rūpera chaṭā pathe cale yāya |*
*gaurarūpera ṭhamaka dekhe camak lāge gāya ||*

*Word for word:* aṅga-ghaṭā — the form; rūpera chaṭā — the radiance of beauty; pathe cale yāya — goes along the road; gaura-rūpera ṭhamaka dekhe — seeing the grace of Gaura's form; camak lāge gāya — the body starts

**13.5.** The form, the radiance of beauty — He goes along the road;
at the sight of the grace of Gaura's form my whole body starts.

গা থর্‌ থর্‌ করে মোর অঙ্গ সকল কাঁপে ।
নাসার নোলক রূপের ছটা হিয়ার মাঝে ঝাঁপে ॥

*gā thar thar kare mora aṅga sakala kām̐pe |*
*nāsāra nolaka rūpera chaṭā hiyāra mājhe jhām̐pe ||*

*Word for word:* gā thar thar kare mora — my body trembles; aṅga sakala kām̐pe — all limbs shake; nāsāra nolaka — the pendant in the nose; rūpera chaṭā — the radiance of beauty; hiyāra mājhe jhām̐pe — leap into the heart

**13.6.** My body trembles, all my limbs shake;
the pendant in the nose, the radiance of beauty leap into my very heart.

আড় নয়নে ঘোমটা দিয়া দেখেছিলাম চেয়ে ।
রসের নেটো নেচে যায় নদের বাজার দিয়ে ॥

*āṛa nayane ghomaṭā diyā dekhechilāma ceye |*
*rasera neṭo nece yāya nadera bājāra diye ||*

*Word for word:* āṛa nayane — sidelong; ghomṭā diyā — from under the veil; dekhechilāma ceye — I looked; rasera neṭo — the dancer of rasa; nece yāya — goes dancing; nadera bājāra diye — through the bazaar of Nadia

**13.7.** Sidelong, from under my veil, I looked at Him:
the dancer of rasa goes dancing through the bazaar of Nadia.

তোরা খুব্‌ খুব্‌ রসে ডুব্‌ ডুব্‌ রসকাঙ্গালি মোরা ।
রসের ডালি রসে পেলি নবকিশোর গোরা ॥

*torā khub khub rase ḍub ḍub rasakāṅgāli morā |*
*rasera ḍāli rase peli nabakiśora gorā ||*

*Word for word:* torā khub khub — you, deep, deep; rase ḍub ḍub — sunk in rasa; rasa-kāṅgāli morā — we are beggars of rasa; rasera ḍāli — the basket of rasa; rase peli — you have gained in rasa; naba-kiśora gorā — young Gora

**13.8.** You are deep, deep sunk in rasa, while we are beggars of rasa;
you have gained in rasa the basket of rasa — young Gora!"[^34-39]

আর এক নাগরী বলে এদেশে না রবো ।
রসের মালা গলায় দিয়ে দেশান্তরি হবো ॥

*āra eka nāgarī bale edeśe nā rabo |*
*rasera mālā galāya diye deśāntari habo ||*

*Word for word:* āra eka nāgarī bale — another nagari says; edeśe nā rabo — I will not stay in this land; rasera mālā galāya diye — putting the garland of rasa on the neck; deśāntari habo — I will go to another land

**13.9.** Another nagari says: "I will not stay in this land;
putting the garland of rasa on my neck, I will go to another land.

এদেশে তো কপাট দিলে সে দেশ তো পাই ।
বাহির গাঁয়ে কাম নাই চলো ভিতর গাঁয়ে যাই ॥

*edeśe to kapāṭa dile se deśa to pāi |*
*bāhira gām̐ye kāma nāi calo bhitara gām̐ye yāi ||*

*Word for word:* edeśe to kapāṭa dile — shutting the doors of this land; se deśa to pāi — I gain that land; bāhira gām̐ye kāma nāi — there is nothing to do in the outer village; calo bhitara gām̐ye yāi — let us go to the inner village

**13.10.** Shut the doors of this land — and I gain that land:
there is nothing to do in the outer village — let us go to the inner village.

সাপের মণি বার্‌ করিলে হারাই যদি মণি ।
মণি হারাইলে তবে না বাঁচয়ে ফণী ॥

*sāpera maṇi bār karile hārāi yadi maṇi |*
*maṇi hārāile tabe nā bām̐caye phaṇī ||*

*Word for word:* sāpera maṇi — the snake's jewel; bār karile — if taken out; hārāi yadi maṇi — the jewel may be lost; maṇi hārāile tabe — if the jewel is lost; nā bām̐caye phaṇī — the snake does not live

**13.11.** The jewel of a snake — if you take it out, you may lose the jewel;
and if the snake loses its jewel, it does not live.

যতন করে রতন রাখা বাহির করা নয় ।
প্রাণের ধনকে বার্‌ করিলে চৌকি দিতে হয় ॥

*yatana kare ratana rākhā bāhira karā naya |*
*prāṇera dhanake bār karile cauki dite haya ||*

*Word for word:* yatana kare ratana rākhā — a jewel is kept carefully; bāhira karā naya — not brought out; prāṇera dhanake — the treasure of the soul; bār karile — if you bring out; cauki dite haya — you must stand guard

**13.12.** A jewel must be kept carefully, not brought out;
if you bring out the treasure of your soul, you will have to stand guard."[^34-40]

লোচন বলে ভাবিস্‌ কেন ঢোক আপনার ঘর ।
হিয়ার মাঝে গোরাচাঁদে মন ডুবায়ে ধর ॥

*locana bale bhābis kena ḍhoka āpanāra ghara |*
*hiyāra mājhe gorācām̐de mana ḍubāye dhara ||*

*Word for word:* locana bale — says Lochana; bhābis kena — why are you brooding; ḍhoka āpanāra ghara — go into your own house; hiyāra mājhe — in the heart; gorācām̐de — Gorachand; mana ḍubāye dhara — hold, immersing the mind

**13.13.** Says Lochana: "Why are you brooding? Go into your own house:
deep in your heart hold Gorachand, immersing your mind in Him."

[^34-38]: Signature: "Lochana." GPT1 — pp. 184–185, no. 75 (raga "yatharaga"; scan PDF pp. 443–444); GPT2 — 3.2, no. 75 (same text). No other witnesses;
attribution by GPT only — C. Lines 13.4b and 13.6 occur almost word for word in no. 8 (8.5b, 8.3), the ending 13.13 in no. 11 (11.10). On nagari-bhava
see the introductory note to
the section (chapter 27).
[^34-39]: In 13.8 the townswoman apparently envies her friends who have seen Gora more closely: "you" are rich in rasa, "we" are its beggars; the sense of
the couplet is conjectural. "The dancer of rasa" (rasera neṭo) is Gaura in kirtana.
[^34-40]: 13.10–13.12 are images of hidden devotion: the "outer" and the "inner village," the snake's jewel (by popular belief a snake dies without its
jewel), a treasure kept secret: love for Gaura is held in the heart, not displayed; the ending agrees with this (13.13; cf. no. 11, 11.10). Translated
as in the original.

## 14. Lochana Dasa — "āmāra gaurāṅga nāce hemakiraṇiyā…" (GPT1 p. 185, no. 76)
*Nagari-bhava (only in the frame). Gauranga dances, shining like gold — the juice of prema drips from the golden tree; His gestures, the curve of His
waist, His smile; crowds of young women throng to see Him; the flood of prema flows, even Madana loses his head. Raga "yatharaga".*[^34-41]

আমার গৌরাঙ্গ নাচে হেমকিরণিয়া ।
হেমের গাছে প্রেমের রস পড়ছে চুয়াইয়া ॥

*āmāra gaurāṅga nāce hemakiraṇiyā |*
*hemera gāche premera rasa paṛache cuyāiyā ||*

*Word for word:* āmāra gaurāṅga nāce — my Gauranga dances; hema-kiraṇiyā — shining with golden rays; hemera gāche — from the golden tree; premera rasa — the juice of prema; paṛche cuyāiyā — falls drop by drop

**14.1.** My Gauranga dances, shining with golden rays;
from the golden tree, drop by drop, the juice of prema falls.

ঠার ঠম্‌কা কাঁকাল বাঁকা মধুরমাখা হাসি ।
রূপ দেখিতে জাতিকুল হারাই হারাই বাসি ॥

*ṭhāra ṭhamkā kām̐kāla bām̐kā madhuramākhā hāsi |*
*rūpa dekhite jātikula hārāi hārāi bāsi ||*

*Word for word:* ṭhāra ṭhamkā — gestures and graceful poses; kām̐kāla bām̐kā — the curved waist; madhura-mākhā hāsi — a smile steeped in sweetness; rūpa dekhite — looking at the form; jāti-kula — caste and family; hārāi hārāi bāsi — I feel I am about to lose

**14.2.** Gestures, graceful poses, the curved waist, a smile steeped in sweetness;
looking at the form, I feel I am about to lose caste and family.

অদ্ভুত নাটের ঠাম গোরা-অঙ্গের ছটা ।
রূপ দেখিতে হুড় পড়েছে নব-যুবতীর ঘটা ॥

*adbhuta nāṭera ṭhāma gorā-aṅgera chaṭā |*
*rūpa dekhite huṛa paṛeche naba-yubatīra ghaṭā ||*

*Word for word:* adbhuta nāṭera ṭhāma — the wondrous bearing of the dance; gorā-aṅgera chaṭā — the radiance of Gora's body; rūpa dekhite — to see the form; huṛa paṛeche — there is a throng; naba-yubatīra ghaṭā — crowds of young women

**14.3.** The wondrous bearing of the dance, the radiance of Gora's body;
to see His form, crowds of young women throng.

মন মজিল কুল ডুবিল বৈছে প্রেমের বান্‌ ।
লোচন বলে মদন ভোলে আর কি আছে আন্‌ ॥

*mana majila kula ḍubila baiche premera bān |*
*locana bale madana bhole āra ki āche ān ||*

*Word for word:* mana majila — the mind is absorbed; kula ḍubila — the family is drowned; baiche premera bān — the flood of prema flows; locana bale — says Lochana; madana bhole — Madana loses his head; āra ki āche ān — what more is there

**14.4.** The mind is absorbed, the family drowned — the flood of prema flows;
says Lochana: even Madana loses his head — what more is there to say?[^34-42]

[^34-41]: Signature: "Lochana." GPT1 — p. 185, no. 76 (raga "yatharaga"; scan PDF p. 444); GPT2 — 3.2, no. 76 (same text). No other witnesses; attribution by GPT only — C. In
substance a praise of Gaura's dance in kirtana; the nagari motif is in the frame (caste and family, the crowd of young women). Line 14.3b coincides with
8.4b. On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^34-42]: "The flood of prema" is the Lord's kirtana that flooded Nadia (CB, Madhya-khanda); "even Madana loses his head" — cf. the epithet
