"Madana-mohana" (note 27).

## 15. Lochana Dasa — "kibā se lābaṇya rūpa bayase utthāna…" (GPT1 p. 185, no. 77)
*Nagari-bhava. The townswoman describes Gauranga's form: the hair, the brows — Kama's bow, the eyes; whether she dives into water or closes her eyes,
she still sees Him; she would spread her breast over all Nadia for Gauranga to dance and walk on; let them call her "disgraced by Gaura." At the end
the poet looks on from outside: Gaurachand walks through Nadia, and the townswomen's eyes, like bees, drink the honey of His face. Raga
"yatharaga".*[^34-43]

কিবা সে লাবণ্য রূপ বয়সে উত্থান ।
চাহিতে গৌরাঙ্গ পানে পিছলে নয়ান ॥

*kibā se lābaṇya rūpa bayase utthāna |*
*cāhite gaurāṅga pāne pichale nayāna ||*

*Word for word:* kibā se lābaṇya rūpa — what loveliness, beauty; bayase utthāna — youth in its rising; cāhite gaurāṅga pāne — looking at Gauranga; pichale nayāna — the eyes slip

**15.1.** What loveliness, what beauty, youth in its very rising!
When one looks at Gauranga, the eyes slip.

প্রতি অঙ্গ নিরুপম কি দিব তুলনা ।
হিয়ার আরতি মাত্র করিয়ে যোটনা ॥

*prati aṅga nirupama ki diba tulanā |*
*hiyāra ārati mātra kariye yoṭanā ||*

*Word for word:* prati aṅga nirupama — each limb is matchless; ki diba tulanā — what comparison shall I give; hiyāra ārati mātra — only the heart's longing; kariye yoṭanā — I gather together

**15.2.** Each limb is matchless — to what shall I compare it?
I only gather together my heart's longing.

কেশের লাবণ্য দেখে না রহে পরাণ ।
ভুরু-ধনু কামের উন্নত নাসা বাণ ॥

*keśera lābaṇya dekhe nā rahe parāṇa |*
*bhuru-dhanu kāmera unnata nāsā bāṇa ||*

*Word for word:* keśera lābaṇya dekhe — seeing the loveliness of the hair; nā rahe parāṇa — the soul cannot hold; bhuru-dhanu kāmera — the brows, Kama's bow; unnata nāsā bāṇa — the high nose, the arrow

**15.3.** Seeing the loveliness of the hair, the soul cannot hold;
the brows are Kama's bow, the high nose — the arrow.

লোল দীঘল আঁখি যার পানে চায় ।
না দিয়ে নিছনি কুল কেবা ঘরে যায় ॥

*lola dīghala ām̐khi yāra pāne cāya |*
*nā diye nichani kula kebā ghare yāya ||*

*Word for word:* lola dīghala ām̐khi — the moving long eyes; yāra pāne cāya — whomever they look at; nā diye nichani kula — without giving the family away for Him; kebā ghare yāya — who goes home

**15.4.** Whomever those moving, long eyes look at —
who goes home without giving her family away for Him?

জলের ভিতর ডুবি তবু দেখি গোরা ।
ত্রিভুবন মগ্ন গোরা চাঁদ হৈল পারা ॥

*jalera bhitara ḍubi tabu dekhi gorā |*
*tribhubana magna gorā cām̐da haila pārā ||*

*Word for word:* jalera bhitara ḍubi — I dive into the water; tabu dekhi gorā — still I see Gora; tribhubana magna — the three worlds are immersed; gorā cām̐da haila pārā — Gora has become like the moon

**15.5.** If I dive into the water, still I see Gora;
the three worlds are immersed [in Him] — Gora has become like the moon.[^34-44]

চিতের আকুতে যদি মুদি দুটি আঁখি ।
হিয়ার মাঝারে তবু গৌররূপ দেখি ॥

*citera ākute yadi mudi duṭi ām̐khi |*
*hiyāra mājhāre tabu gaurarūpa dekhi ||*

*Word for word:* citera ākute — in the heart's longing; yadi mudi duṭi ām̐khi — if I close both eyes; hiyāra mājhāre — deep in the heart; tabu gaura-rūpa dekhi — still I see Gaura's form

**15.6.** If in my heart's longing I close both eyes —
still deep in my heart I see Gaura's form.

করিশুণ্ড জিনি কিয়ে বাহুর হেলা দোলা ।
হিয়ার দোলনে দোলে মালতীর মালা ॥

*kariśuṇḍa jini kiye bāhura helā dolā |*
*hiyāra dolane dole mālatīra mālā ||*

*Word for word:* kari-śuṇḍa jini — surpassing an elephant's trunk; kiye bāhura helā dolā — how the arms sway; hiyāra dolane — on the heaving chest; dole mālatīra mālā — the malati garland swings

**15.7.** Surpassing an elephant's trunk — how the arms sway!
On the heaving chest the malati garland swings.

মনে করি নৈদে যুড়ি এ বুক বিছাই ।
তাহার উপরে আমি গৌরাঙ্গ নাচাই ॥

*mane kari naide yuṛi e buka bichāi |*
*tāhāra upare āmi gaurāṅga nācāi ||*

*Word for word:* mane kari — I think; naide yuṛi — over all Nadia; e buka bichāi — I will spread this breast; tāhāra upare — upon it; āmi gaurāṅga nācāi — I will make Gauranga dance

**15.8.** I think: I will spread this breast of mine over all Nadia
and on it make Gauranga dance.

মনে করি নৈদে যুড়ি হোক মোর হিয়া ।
বেড়ান গৌরাঙ্গ তাতে পদ পসারিয়া ॥

*mane kari naide yuṛi hoka mora hiyā |*
*beṛāna gaurāṅga tāte pada pasāriyā ||*

*Word for word:* mane kari — I think; naide yuṛi hoka mora hiyā — let my heart cover all Nadia; beṛāna gaurāṅga tāte — may Gauranga walk upon it; pada pasāriyā — stepping out

**15.9.** I think: let my heart cover all Nadia,
and Gauranga walk upon it, stepping out.[^34-45]

বলুক বলুক সকল লোকে গৌরকলঙ্কিনী ।
ধিক্‌ যারা কুল রাখে কুলের কামিনী ॥

*baluka baluka sakala loke gaurakalaṅkinī |*
*dhik yārā kula rākhe kulera kāminī ||*

*Word for word:* baluka baluka sakala loke — let, let all the people call; gaura-kalaṅkinī — "disgraced by Gaura"; dhik yārā kula rākhe — shame on those who keep the family honour; kulera kāminī — the wives of noble families

**15.10.** Let them, let all the people call me "disgraced by Gaura";
shame on those wives of noble families who keep their family honour!

নদীয়ানগরে গৌরচাঁদ চলে যায় ।
চঞ্চল নয়ন করি দুই দিকে চায় ॥

*nadīyānagare gauracām̐da cale yāya |*
*cañcala nayana kari dui dike cāya ||*

*Word for word:* nadīyā-nagare — through the town of Nadia; gauracām̐da cale yāya — Gaurachand goes; cañcala nayana kari — with moving eyes; dui dike cāya — looks to both sides

**15.11.** Through the town of Nadia Gaurachand goes,
with moving eyes He looks to both sides.

নাগরীদের নেত্র যেন ভ্রমরার পাঁতি ।
গৌর-মুখ-পদ্মমধু পিউ মাতি মাতি ॥

*nāgarīdera netra yena bhramarāra pām̐ti |*
*gaura-mukha-padmamadhu piu māti māti ||*

*Word for word:* nāgarīdera netra — the townswomen's eyes; yena bhramarāra pām̐ti — like rows of bees; gaura-mukha-padma-madhu — the honey of the lotus of Gaura's face; piu māti māti — drink, drunk and drunker

**15.12.** The townswomen's eyes are like rows of bees:
they drink the honey of the lotus of Gaura's face, drunk and drunker.

পদ্মমধু পানে তাদের দেখিয়া উল্লাস ।
গৌরগুণ গায় সুখে এ লোচন দাস ॥

*padmamadhu pāne tādera dekhiyā ullāsa |*
*gauraguṇa gāya sukhe e locana dāsa ||*

*Word for word:* padma-madhu pāne — in drinking the lotus honey; tādera dekhiyā ullāsa — seeing their delight; gaura-guṇa gāya sukhe — joyfully sings of Gaura's virtues; e locana dāsa — this Lochana Dasa

**15.13.** Seeing their delight as they drink the lotus honey,
this Lochana Dasa joyfully sings of Gaura's virtues.[^34-46]

[^34-43]: Signature: "e locana dāsa." GPT1 — p. 185, no. 77 (raga "yatharaga"; payar metre, a couplet to a line; scan PDF p. 444); GPT2 — 3.2, no. 77 (same
text). No other witnesses; attribution by GPT only — C. On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^34-44]: The moon, whose light floods all the three worlds and is reflected in any water — that is why the townswoman sees Gora even in the water; the
interpretation is conjectural.
[^34-45]: 15.8–15.9 — the wish that the Lord's feet should tread on one's heart: a mood of service known from the song of the gopis (*Bhag.* 10.31).
"Disgraced by Gaura" (gaurakalaṅkinī, 15.10) is modelled on "disgraced by Krishna" (kṛṣṇakalaṅkinī), as Radha is called; on the transfer of the parakiya
motif see note 7.
[^34-46]: 15.11 "He looks to both sides" is the poet's image; according to CB (Adi-khanda) the Lord in Navadvipa did not look at women (note 3). The last
three couplets are the poet's view from outside: he sees the townswomen's delight and sings of it, as he sings of Gaura's virtues.

## 16. Lochana Dasa — "ehena sundara gorā kothā vā āchila go…" (GPT1 p. 186, no. 78)
*Nagari-bhava (only in the frame). Where was such a beautiful Gora before, who brought Him to Nadia? In bhava He has gone limp, His eyes are moist with
prema; the creator made Him from the treasure of bliss. The dancer of Gokula, Kanu, was bent and crooked of heart — Radha's love straightened Him: He
it is who now sports in Nadia. Raga "yatharaga".*[^34-47]

এহেন সুন্দর গোরা কোথা বা আছিল গো
কে আনিল নদীয়ানগরে ।
নিরখিতে গৌররূপ হৃদয়ে পশিল গো
তনু কাঁপে পুলকের ভরে ॥

*ehena sundara gorā kothā bā āchila go*
*ke ānila nadīyānagare |*
*nirakhite gaurarūpa hṛdaye paśila go*
*tanu kām̐pe pulakera bhare ||*

*Word for word:* ehena sundara gorā — such a beautiful Gora; kothā vā āchila go — where was He before, o; ke ānila nadīyā-nagare — who brought Him to the town of Nadia; nirakhite gaura-rūpa — as I looked at Gaura's form; hṛdaye paśila go — He entered the heart, o; tanu kām̐pe pulakera bhare — the body trembles, filled with thrill

**16.1.** Where was such a beautiful Gora before, o,
who brought Him to the town of Nadia?
As soon as I looked at Gaura's form, He entered my heart, o;
my body trembles, filled with thrill.

ভাবের আবেশে ও লা এলায়ে পড়েছে গো
প্রেমে ছল ছল্‌ দুটি আঁখি ।
দেখিতে দেখিতে আমার হেন মনে হয় গো
পরাণ পুতলি করি রাখি ॥

*bhābera ābeśe o lā elāye paṛeche go*
*preme chala chal duṭi ām̐khi |*
*dekhite dekhite āmāra hena mane haya go*
*parāṇa putali kari rākhi ||*

*Word for word:* bhābera ābeśe — in the rapture of bhava; o lā — friend (address); elāye paṛeche go — He has gone limp, o; preme chala chal duṭi ām̐khi — the two eyes glisten moist with prema; dekhite dekhite — looking and looking; āmāra hena mane haya go — it seems to me, o; parāṇa putali kari rākhi — I would make Him the darling doll of my soul and keep Him

**16.2.** In the rapture of bhava, friend, He has gone all limp, o,
His eyes glisten moist with prema;
I look and look — and it seems to me, o:
I would make Him the darling doll of my soul and keep Him.

বিধি কি আনন্দ নিধি মথি নিরমিল গো
কিবা সে গড়িল কারিকরে ।
পীরিতি কুঁদের কুঁদে উহারে কুঁদিল গো
(উহার) নয়ান কুঁদিল কামশরে ॥

*bidhi ki ānanda nidhi mathi niramila go*
*kibā se gaṛila kārikare |*
*pīriti kum̐dera kum̐de uhāre kum̐dila go*
*(uhāra) nayāna kum̐dila kāmaśare ||*

*Word for word:* bidhi ki — did the creator; ānanda nidhi mathi — churning the treasure of bliss; niramila go — make Him, o; kibā se gaṛila kārikare — what a craftsman shaped Him; pīriti kum̐dera kum̐de — on the lathe of love; uhāre kum̐dila go — turned Him, o; (uhāra) nayāna kum̐dila kāmaśare — turned (His) eyes with Kama's arrows

**16.3.** Did the creator churn the treasure of bliss to make Him, o?
what a craftsman it was who shaped Him!
On the lathe of love he turned Him, o,
and turned (His) eyes with Kama's arrows.

গোকুল-নেটোর কাণ বঙ্কিম আছিল গো
কালিয়ে কুটিল যার হিয়া ।
রাধার পীরিতি উহায় সমান করেছে গো
সেই এই বিহরে নদীয়া ॥

*gokula-neṭora kāṇa baṅkima āchila go*
*kāliye kuṭila yāra hiyā |*
*rādhāra pīriti uhāya samāna kareche go*
*sei ei bihare nadīyā ||*

*Word for word:* gokula-neṭora kāṇa — Kanu, the dancer of Gokula; baṅkima āchila go — was bent, o; kāliye kuṭila yāra hiyā — dark and crooked of heart; rādhāra pīriti — Radha's love; uhāya samāna kareche go — has made Him straight, o; sei ei bihare nadīyā — that same One sports in Nadia

**16.4.** The dancer of Gokula, Kanu, was bent, o,
dark and crooked was He at heart;
Radha's love has made Him straight, o, —
He it is who now sports in Nadia.[^34-48]

মনের মরম কথা কাহারে কহিব গো
চিত যেন চুরি কৈল চোরে ।
লোচন পিয়াসে মরে ওরূপ দেখিয়া গো
বিধাতা বঞ্চিত ভেল মোরে ॥

*manera marama kathā kāhāre kahiba go*
*cita yena curi kaila core |*
*locana piyāse mare orūpa dekhiyā go*
*bidhātā bañcita bhela more ||*

*Word for word:* manera marama kathā — the secret of the heart; kāhāre kahiba go — to whom shall I tell it, o; cita yena curi kaila core — as if a thief stole the heart; locana piyāse mare — Lochana dies of thirst; o-rūpa dekhiyā go — seeing that form, o; bidhātā bañcita bhela more — the creator has cheated me

**16.5.** The secret of my heart — to whom shall I tell it, o?
as if a thief had stolen my heart;
Lochana dies of thirst, seeing that form, o:
the creator has cheated me.

[^34-47]: Signature: "Lochana." GPT1 — p. 186, no. 78 (raga "yatharaga"; tripadi; scan PDF p. 445); GPT2 — 3.2, no. 78 (same text). The pada is also in the *Padamrita-sindhu (Prachina-vaishnava-padavali)*, vol. 1 (collection of Chandranatha Bandyopadhyaya, publ. 1922; hereafter PVP), p. 114, with the same
signature and with an extra stanza after 16.4 (see note 48); PVP is a late anthology, not an independent witness; attribution by GPT only — C. "O"
(go) at the ends of the half-lines is a refrain exclamation. On nagari-bhava see the
introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^34-48]: Stanza 16.4 is the heart of the pada: Gaura is the same Krishna, the "bent" (tribhanga) and "crooked" Kanu of Gokula, whom Radha's love has made
"straight": He has taken Radha's bhava (CC Adi 4). PVP: "Kanu, Nanda's son, was bent in Gokula… by Rai's love He was tamed" (damana karila), followed by
an extra stanza: "Thinking of Radha's form, Gora became a golden body; formerly this turned into a gift of prema; whose heart does not drown in His
deeds — shame on him!" "The darling doll of my soul" (16.2) — what is dearest (note 13).

## 17. Lochana Dasa — "śāradacandrikā svarṇa dhik campakera barṇa…" (GPT1 p. 186, no. 79)
*A praise of Gaura's form (in content not nagari-bhava: the nagari motif is only the address "friend"). Neither gold nor moonlight, nor champaka, nor
precious stones, nor lightning compare with Gora: all these are forms of the world of prakriti, while He is the king of rasa beyond the world; He can
be compared only with Himself. As a bird flies in the sky as far as its strength allows, so the poet sings of Him. Raga "yatharaga".*[^34-49]

শারদচন্দ্রিকা স্বর্ণ ধিক্‌ চম্পকের বর্ণ
শোণ-কুসুম গোরোচনা ।
হরিতাল সে কোন ছার বিকার সে মৃত্তিকার
সে কি গোরারূপের তুলনা ॥

*śāradacandrikā svarṇa dhik campakera barṇa*
*śoṇa-kusuma gorocanā |*
*haritāla se kona chāra bikāra se mṛttikāra*
*se ki gorārūpera tulanā ||*

*Word for word:* śārada-candrikā — autumn moonlight; svarṇa — gold; dhik campakera barṇa — shame on the champaka's colour; śoṇa-kusuma — the red shona flower; gorocanā — gorochana; haritāla se kona chāra — orpiment, what a trifle; bikāra se mṛttikāra — a modification of clay; se ki gorārūpera tulanā — can it compare with Gora's form

**17.1.** Autumn moonlight, gold — shame on the colour of the champaka, on the red shona flower, on gorochana!
Orpiment — what a trifle, a modification of clay — can it compare with Gora's form?

ধিক্‌ চন্দ্রকান্তমণি তার বর্ণ কিসে গণি
ফণি-মণি সৌদামিনী আর ।
ও সব প্রপঞ্চরূপ অপ্রপঞ্চরসভূপ
তুলনা কি দিব আমি তার ॥

*dhik candrakāntamaṇi tāra barṇa kise gaṇi*
*phaṇi-maṇi saudāminī āra |*
*o saba prapañcarūpa aprapañcarasabhūpa*
*tulanā ki diba āmi tāra ||*

*Word for word:* dhik candrakānta-maṇi — shame on the moonstone; tāra barṇa kise gaṇi — how should its colour be reckoned; phaṇi-maṇi — the serpent's jewel; saudāminī āra — and lightning; o saba prapañca-rūpa — all these are forms of the world of prakriti; aprapañca-rasa-bhūpa — the king of rasa beyond prakriti; tulanā ki diba āmi tāra — what comparison shall I give Him

**17.2.** Shame on the moonstone — how should its colour be reckoned? — on the serpent's jewel and on lightning!
All these are forms of the world of prakriti; He is the king of rasa beyond prakriti: to what shall I compare Him?[^34-50]

যত দেখ বর্ণন অনুসারে উদ্দীপন
গৌররূপ বর্ণন কে করে ।
জান না যে সেই গোরা ধরারূপে অঙ্গধরা
দরশে ধৈরজ দূর করে ॥

*yata dekha barṇana anusāre uddīpana*
*gaurarūpa barṇana ke kare |*
*jāna nā ye sei gorā dharārūpe aṅgadharā*
*daraśe dhairaja dūra kare ||*

*Word for word:* yata dekha barṇana — all the descriptions you see; anusāre uddīpana — are uddipana by likeness; gaura-rūpa barṇana ke kare — who can describe Gaura's form; jāna nā ye — do you not know; sei gorā — that very Gora; dharā-rūpe aṅga-dharā — taking a body in earthly form; daraśe dhairaja dūra kare — drives away steadfastness by His sight

**17.3.** All the descriptions you see are only uddipana by likeness: who can describe Gaura's form?
Do you not know: that very Gora, taking a body in earthly form, drives away steadfastness by His mere sight?

শুন ওগো প্রাণ সই জগতে তুলনা কই
তবে সে তুলনা দিব কিসে ।
জগতে তুলনা নাই যাঁর তুলনা তাঁর ঠাঁই
অমিয়া মিশাব কেন বিষে ॥

*śuna ogo prāṇa sai jagate tulanā kai*
*tabe se tulanā diba kise |*
*jagate tulanā nāi yām̐ra tulanā tām̐ra ṭhām̐i*
*amiyā miśāba kena biṣe ||*

*Word for word:* śuna ogo prāṇa sai — listen, o dear friend; jagate tulanā kai — where in the world is a comparison; tabe se tulanā diba kise — to what then shall I compare; jagate tulanā nāi — there is no comparison in the world; yām̐ra tulanā tām̐ra ṭhām̐i — whose comparison is in Himself; amiyā miśāba kena biṣe — why mix nectar with poison

**17.4.** Listen, o dear friend: where in the world is a comparison? to what then shall I compare Him?
There is no comparison in the world; He who is comparable only to Himself — why mix nectar with poison?

কেবা তার গুণ গায় গুণের কে ওর পায়
কেবা করে রূপনিরূপণ ।
রূপ নিরূপিতে নারে গুণ কে কহিতে পারে
ভাবিয়া বাউল হৈল মন ॥

*kebā tāra guṇa gāya guṇera ke ora pāya*
*kebā kare rūpanirūpaṇa |*
*rūpa nirūpite nāre guṇa ke kahite pāre*
*bhābiyā bāula haila mana ||*

*Word for word:* kebā tāra guṇa gāya — who sings His virtues; guṇera ke ora pāya — who finds the end of the virtues; kebā kare rūpa-nirūpaṇa — who can describe the form; rūpa nirūpite nāre — the form cannot be described; guṇa ke kahite pāre — who can tell the virtues; bhābiyā bāula haila mana — thinking, the mind has gone mad

**17.5.** Who can sing His virtues, who can find their end, who can describe His form?
The form cannot be described, who can tell the virtues? — thinking of this, the mind has gone mad.

পক্ষী যেন আকাশের কিছুই না পায় টের
যত দূর শক্তি উড়ি যায় ।
সেইরূপ গৌরাঙ্গের রূপের না পায় টের
অনুসারে এ লোচন গায় ॥

*pakṣī yena ākāśera kichui nā pāya ṭera*
*yata dūra śakti uṛi yāya |*
*seirūpa gaurāṅgera rūpera nā pāya ṭera*
*anusāre e locana gāya ||*

*Word for word:* pakṣī yena ākāśera — as a bird of the sky; kichui nā pāya ṭera — learns nothing; yata dūra śakti uṛi yāya — flies as far as its strength allows; sei-rūpa gaurāṅgera — just so of Gauranga; rūpera nā pāya ṭera — of the beauty one cannot know; anusāre e locana gāya — as far as he is able this Lochana sings

**17.6.** As a bird in the sky learns nothing [of its end], flying as far as its strength allows,
so of Gauranga's beauty [the end] cannot be known: as far as he is able, this Lochana sings.[^34-51]

[^34-49]: Signature: "e locana." GPT1 — p. 186, no. 79 (raga "yatharaga"; tripadi; scan PDF p. 445); GPT2 — 3.2, no. 79 (same text). The pada is also in PVP (vol. 1, pp. c. 122–123; see note 47), with Lochana's signature: the stanzas in a different order, with variants and with an extra opening stanza
("The colour of Gaurangachand surpasses the gold of the Jambu river — so the great describe it; since my birth I have nowhere seen the gold of the
Jambu: in my heart is the vision of Gauranga"); PVP is a late anthology, not an independent witness; attribution by GPT only — C. In the GPT section of nagari padas the pada stands because of the address to a friend; on
nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^34-50]: "Forms of the world of prakriti" (prapañcarūpa): everything poets compare with belongs to the material world (prapancha); Gaura is "the king of
rasa beyond prakriti" (aprapañcarasabhūpa): His form is not material. The thought agrees with the teaching: the Lord's body is eternity, knowledge and
bliss (CC Adi 4 and elsewhere). Shona is a red flower; gorochana and orpiment are yellow pigments; "the serpent's jewel" is the gem in a snake's hood
(cf. note 40).
[^34-51]: "Uddipana" (uddīpana) — in the teaching on rasa, the "kindling" causes of feeling: the poets' comparisons only kindle feeling, they do not
describe Him. "Taking a body in earthly form" (dharārūpe aṅgadharā) — the interpretation is conjectural. "As far as he is able" (anusāre) — as a bird
flies in the boundless sky as far as its strength allows.

## 18. Lochana Dasa — "(hem̐i go hem̐i go) sai tore birala peye kai…" (GPT1 p. 187, no. 81)
*Nagari-bhava (a dream). Finding her friend alone, the townswoman tells her dream: Shachi's Gora, with a garland of malati and a thin sacred thread,
came up smiling, put a garland on her neck, wiped her face with His cloth, took her hand — as her heart had wished; Gora's love is like gold, it cannot
be forgotten. Raga "yatharaga".*[^34-52]

(হেঁই গো হেঁই গো) সই তোরে বিরল পেয়ে কই ।
স্বপনে শচীর গোরা দেখিলাম শুই ॥

*(hem̐i go hem̐i go) sai tore birala peye kai |*
*svapane śacīra gorā dekhilāma śui ||*

*Word for word:* (hem̐i go hem̐i go) — (hey, hey); sai tore birala peye kai — friend, finding you alone, I tell you; svapane — in a dream; śacīra gorā — Shachi's Gora; dekhilāma śui — lying asleep, I saw

**18.1.** (Hey, hey!) Friend, finding you alone, I will tell you:
lying asleep, I saw Shachi's Gora in a dream.

গলা আলা মালতীমালা সরু পৈতা কাঁধে ।
অমিয়া পারা কত ধারা বইছে মুখচাঁদে ॥

*galā ālā mālatīmālā saru paitā kām̐dhe |*
*amiyā pārā kata dhārā baiche mukhacām̐de ||*

*Word for word:* galā ālā mālatī-mālā — a malati garland lights up the neck; saru paitā kām̐dhe — a thin sacred thread on the shoulder; amiyā pārā — like nectar; kata dhārā baiche — how many streams flow; mukha-cām̐de — over the moon of the face

**18.2.** A malati garland lights up His neck, a thin sacred thread on His shoulder;
how many streams, like nectar, flow over the moon of His face!

হাসি হাসি কাছে আসি গলায় দেয় মালা ।
তার কাজ কৈতে লাজ কত জানে ছলা ॥

*hāsi hāsi kāche āsi galāya deya mālā |*
*tāra kāja kaite lāja kata jāne chalā ||*

*Word for word:* hāsi hāsi kāche āsi — smiling, coming near; galāya deya mālā — He puts a garland on the neck; tāra kāja kaite lāja — I am ashamed to tell what He did; kata jāne chalā — how many wiles He knows

**18.3.** Smiling, He comes near and puts a garland on my neck;
what He did, I am ashamed to tell: how many wiles He knows!

আপনবাসে মুখানি মোছে চেয়ে থাকে পুন ।
হাতে ধরে আদর কৈবে মনের মত যেন ॥

*āpanabāse mukhāni moche ceye thāke puna |*
*hāte dhare ādara kaibe manera mata yena ||*

*Word for word:* āpana-bāse — with His own cloth; mukhāni moche — wipes the face; ceye thāke puna — and gazes again; hāte dhare — taking the hand; ādara kaibe — He caresses; manera mata yena — just as the heart desired

**18.4.** With His own cloth He wipes my face and gazes again;
taking my hand, He caresses me — just as my heart desired.[^34-53]

গোরাপ্রেম যেন হেম পাসরিতে নারি ।
লোচন বলে বস্‌ বিরলে আয় দুখে মরি ॥

*gorāprema yena hema pāsarite nāri |*
*locana bale bas birale āya dukhe mari ||*

*Word for word:* gorā-prema yena hema — Gora's love is like gold; pāsarite nāri — I cannot forget it; locana bale — says Lochana; bas birale — sit in solitude; āya dukhe mari — come here, I die of grief

**18.5.** Gora's love is like gold: I cannot forget it.
Says Lochana: "Sit in solitude — come here, I die of grief."

[^34-52]: Signature: "Lochana." GPT1 — p. 187, no. 81 (raga "yatharaga"; scan PDF p. 446); GPT2 — 3.2, no. 81 (same text). No other witnesses; attribution by GPT only — C. "(Hey,
hey!)" is an insertion in brackets (cf. no. 12, 12.1). The sacred thread — Gaura as a young brahmana, before the sannyasa. On nagari-bhava see the
introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^34-53]: 18.3–18.4 are a dream with the motif of sambhoga (a garland on the neck — the sign of being chosen, "what He did, I am ashamed to tell,"
caresses); translated exactly. The dream is the townswoman's imagination; see note 33. 18.5b — the sense is conjectural: the poet apparently shares the
heroine's longing.

## 19. Lochana Dasa — "hera āya go manera kathā birala peye kai…" (GPT1 p. 187, no. 82)
*Nagari-bhava. The townswoman calls her friend: in the late afternoon she went to see Shachi's son — a moon anointed with sandal, a sandal mark on the
forehead, a snare for the heart; out of shame she held herself back, but, seeing His long eyes, she could not come away. Raga "yatharaga".*[^34-54]

হের আয় গো মনের কথা বিরল পেয়ে কই ।
শচীর রায় বিকাল বেলায় দেখে এলাম সই ॥

*hera āya go manera kathā birala peye kai |*
*śacīra rāya bikāla belāya dekhe elāma sai ||*

*Word for word:* hera āya go — come here; manera kathā — what is on my heart; birala peye kai — finding you alone I tell; śacīra rāya — Shachi's Raya (son); bikāla belāya — in the late afternoon; dekhe elāma sai — I went and saw, friend

**19.1.** Come here, friend — finding you alone, I will tell what is on my heart:
in the late afternoon I went to see the son of Shachi, friend.

চন্দন মাখা চাঁদে ও সই ! চন্দন মাখা চাঁদে ।
কপালে চন্দনফোঁটা মন বাঁধিবার ফাঁদে ॥

*candana mākhā cām̐de o sai ! candana mākhā cām̐de |*
*kapāle candanaphom̐ṭā mana bām̐dhibāra phām̐de ||*

*Word for word:* candana mākhā cām̐de — a moon anointed with sandal; o sai — o friend; kapāle candana-phom̐ṭā — the sandal mark on the forehead; mana bām̐dhibāra phām̐de — a snare to catch the heart

**19.2.** A moon anointed with sandal, o friend! A moon anointed with sandal:
the sandal mark on His forehead — a snare to catch the heart.

ভরম সরম করি অম্‌নি আপনা সম্বরি ।
দীঘল আঁখি দেখে সখি আর কি আস্‌তে পারি ॥

*bharama sarama kari amni āpanā sambari |*
*dīghala ām̐khi dekhe sakhi āra ki āste pāri ||*

*Word for word:* bharama sarama kari — out of decorum and shame; amni āpanā sambari — I at once held myself back; dīghala ām̐khi dekhe — seeing the long eyes; sakhi — friend; āra ki āste pāri — could I come away

**19.3.** Out of decorum and shame I at once held myself back;
but, seeing those long eyes, friend, — could I come away?

গৌররূপ দেখে হৃদে হইয়া উল্লাস ।
আনন্দ-হৃদয়ে কহে এ লোচন দাস ॥

*gaurarūpa dekhe hṛde haiyā ullāsa |*
*ānanda-hṛdaye kahe e locana dāsa ||*

*Word for word:* gaura-rūpa dekhe — seeing Gaura's form; hṛde haiyā ullāsa — the heart rejoices; ānanda-hṛdaye — with joy in the heart; kahe e locana dāsa — says this Lochana Dasa

**19.4.** At the sight of Gaura's form the heart rejoices;
with joy in his heart says this Lochana Dasa.

[^34-54]: Signature: "e locana dāsa." GPT1 — p. 187, no. 82 (raga "yatharaga"; scan PDF p. 446); GPT2 — 3.2, no. 82 (same text). No other witnesses; attribution by GPT only — C.
"The son of Shachi" (śacīra rāya) — lit. "Shachi's Raya." The ending 19.4 nearly coincides with 5.13. On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the
section (chapter 27).

## 20. Lochana Dasa — "mukha jhalamala badana-kamala dīghala ām̐khi duṭi…" (GPT1 p. 188, no. 83)
*Nagari-bhava. The townswoman describes Gaura: the radiant lotus face, the long eyes, the reddish soles; walking, swaying, He leans on His friends;
once He glanced at her from the corner of His eye — and the doe of her heart was caught in the snare of His brows. Then come couplets shared with
no. 9; others seek Him by austerity through many births, while she keeps Him in her heart. The poet: hold the nagara Gora captive in your heart. Raga
"yatharaga".*[^34-55]

মুখ ঝলমল বদন-কমল দীঘল আঁখি দুটি ।
দেখে লাজে মনঃখেদে খঞ্জন কোটি কোটি ॥

*mukha jhalamala badana-kamala dīghala ām̐khi duṭi |*
*dekhe lāje manaḥkhede khañjana koṭi koṭi ||*

*Word for word:* mukha jhalamala — a radiant face; badana-kamala — a lotus face; dīghala ām̐khi duṭi — two long eyes; dekhe lāje manaḥkhede — seeing, in shame and sorrow; khañjana koṭi koṭi — millions of wagtails

**20.1.** A radiant face, a lotus face, two long eyes;
seeing them, millions of wagtails are in shame and sorrow.

চরণতলে অরুণ খেলে কমল শোভে তায় ।
চ'লে চ'লে ঢ'লে ঢ'লে পড়ছে সখার গায় ॥

*caraṇatale aruṇa khele kamala śobhe tāya |*
*ca'le ca'le ḍha'le ḍha'le paṛache sakhāra gāya ||*

*Word for word:* caraṇa-tale — on the soles; aruṇa khele — the dawn plays; kamala śobhe tāya — lotuses shine there; ca'le ca'le — walking, walking; ḍha'le ḍha'le — swaying, swaying; paṛche sakhāra gāya — He leans on His friends

**20.2.** On His soles the dawn plays, lotuses shine on them;
walking, walking, swaying, swaying, He leans on His friends.[^34-56]

আমা পানে নয়নকোণে চাইল একবার ।
মন-হরিণী বাঁধা গেল ভুরুপাশে তার ॥

*āmā pāne nayanakoṇe cāila ekabāra |*
*mana-hariṇī bām̐dhā gela bhurupāśe tāra ||*

*Word for word:* āmā pāne — at me; nayana-koṇe — from the corner of the eye; cāila ekabāra — He glanced once; mana-hariṇī — the doe of the heart; bām̐dhā gela — was caught; bhuru-pāśe tāra — in the snare of His brows

**20.3.** From the corner of His eye He once glanced at me —
the doe of my heart was caught in the snare of His brows.

গৌররূপ রসের কূপ সহজেই এত ।
করলে কলা রসের ছলা তবে হয় কত ॥

*gaurarūpa rasera kūpa sahajei eta |*
*karale kalā rasera chalā tabe haya kata ||*

*Word for word:* gaura-rūpa — Gaura's form; rasera kūpa — a well of rasa; sahajei eta — is so much by itself; karle kalā — if He uses His art; rasera chalā — the wiles of rasa; tabe haya kata — how much then

**20.4.** Gaura's form — a well of rasa — is so much just by itself;
if He uses His art, the wiles of rasa, — what will it be then!

যদি বাঁধে বিনোদছাঁদে চাঁচর চিকণ চুল ।
তবে সতী কুলবতী রাখতে নারে কুল ॥

*yadi bām̐dhe binodachām̐de cām̐cara cikaṇa cula |*
*tabe satī kulabatī rākhate nāre kula ||*

*Word for word:* yadi bām̐dhe binoda-chām̐de — if He gracefully binds; cām̐cara cikaṇa cula — the soft curling hair; tabe satī kulabatī — then the faithful noble wife; rākhte nāre kula — cannot keep the family honour

**20.5.** If He gracefully arranges His soft curling hair,
then a faithful, noble wife cannot keep her family honour.

যারে ডাকে নয়ন বাঁকে তার কি রহে মান ।
যদি যাচে তবে কি বাঁচে রসবতীর প্রাণ ॥

*yāre ḍāke nayana bām̐ke tāra ki rahe māna |*
*yadi yāce tabe ki bām̐ce rasabatīra prāṇa ||*

*Word for word:* yāre ḍāke — whom He calls; nayana bām̐ke — with a sidelong glance; tāra ki rahe māna — will her pride remain; yadi yāce — if He asks; tabe ki bām̐ce — would it survive; rasabatīra prāṇa — the life of the rasavati

**20.6.** Whomever He calls with a sidelong glance — will her pride remain?
and if He should ask — would the rasavati survive?

যদি হাসে কতই আসে রাশি রাশি হীরে ।
নয়ন মন প্রাণধন কে নিবি আয় ফিরে ॥

*yadi hāse katai āse rāśi rāśi hīre |*
*nayana mana prāṇadhana ke nibi āya phire ||*

*Word for word:* yadi hāse — if He smiles; katai āse — how many appear; rāśi rāśi hīre — heaps of diamonds; nayana mana prāṇadhana — eyes, mind, the treasure of the soul; ke nibi — who will take; āya phire — come back

**20.7.** If He smiles — what heaps of diamonds appear!
Eyes, mind, the treasure of the soul — who will take them back? come!

গলায় মালা বাহু দোলা দিয়া চ'লে যায় ।
কামের রতি ছেড়ে পতি ভজে গোরার পায় ॥

*galāya mālā bāhu dolā diyā ca'le yāya |*
*kāmera rati cheṛe pati bhaje gorāra pāya ||*

*Word for word:* galāya mālā — with a garland on the neck; bāhu dolā diyā — swinging the arms; ca'le yāya — He passes by; kāmera rati — Kama's Rati; cheṛe pati — leaving her husband; bhaje gorāra pāya — worships Gora's feet

**20.8.** With a garland on His neck, swinging His arms, He passes by —
Rati herself, Kama's wife, leaving her husband, worships Gora's feet.

কঠোর তপ করে জপ কত জন্ম ফিরে ।
হিয়ায় থুয়ে পরাণ দিয়ে দেখি নয়ন ভরে ॥

*kaṭhora tapa kare japa kata janma phire |*
*hiyāya thuye parāṇa diye dekhi nayana bhare ||*

*Word for word:* kaṭhora tapa — harsh austerity; kare japa — they practise japa; kata janma phire — wandering through many births; hiyāya thuye — keeping in the heart; parāṇa diye — giving my life; dekhi nayana bhare — I gaze to my eyes' fill

**20.9.** [Others] practise harsh austerity and japa, wandering birth after birth;
but I, keeping [Him] in my heart, giving my life, gaze at Him to my fill.

লোচন বলে ভাবিস্‌ কেন থাক আপনার ঘর ।
হিয়ার মাঝে গোরা নাগর আটক ক'রে ধর ॥

*locana bale bhābis kena thāka āpanāra ghara |*
*hiyāra mājhe gorā nāgara āṭaka ka're dhara ||*

*Word for word:* locana bale — says Lochana; bhābis kena — why are you brooding; thāka āpanāra ghara — stay in your own house; hiyāra mājhe — deep in the heart; gorā nāgara — the nagara Gora; āṭaka ka're dhara — hold captive

**20.10.** Says Lochana: "Why are you brooding? Stay in your own house:
deep in your heart hold the nagara Gora captive."[^34-57]

[^34-55]: Signature: "Lochana." GPT1 — p. 188, no. 83 (raga "yatharaga"; scan PDF p. 447); GPT2 — 3.2, no. 83 (same text). No other witnesses;
attribution by GPT only — C. 20.4–20.6,
20.8 = no. 9, 9.1–9.4 (in 20.6 "whom He calls," yāre ḍāke, instead of "whom He looks at," yām̐re dekhe); on the motifs of these couplets see notes 26–27.
On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^34-56]: Gaura, swaying in bhava, leans on His associates — as in the descriptions of His kirtana (CB, Madhya-khanda). "He glanced at me" (20.3) is how it
seems to the heroine; according to CB (Adi-khanda) the Lord did not look at women (note 3). The wagtail (khañjana) is an image of restless eyes.
[^34-57]: 20.9 contrasts austerity and love: others seek Him by harsh feats through many births, while she has found Him by keeping Him in her heart. 20.10
is the same turn inward as in nos. 11 and 13 (11.10, 13.13); "the nagara Gora" is an epithet of nagari-bhava (introductory note). 20.7b — the sense is
conjectural.

## 21. Lochana Dasa — "nabadvīpanāgarī āgari gorārase…" (GPT1 p. 189, no. 85)
*Nagari-bhava. A townswoman of Navadvipa, foremost in the rasa of Gora, floats in tears of prema as she speaks of Gauranga; in her ears, eyes and
mind — Gora; she writes His name on her body with gorochana and performs puja to Him in her mind: tears are the abhisheka, love the naivedya, words the
betel, the radiance of her body the lamp, the jingling of her bangles the bell; her anuraga grows day by day. The poet: at last the thorn of knowledge
is gone. Raga "yatharaga".*[^34-58]

নবদ্বীপনাগরী আগরি গোরারসে ।
কহিতে গৌরাঙ্গকথা প্রেমজলে ভাসে ॥

*nabadvīpanāgarī āgari gorārase |*
*kahite gaurāṅgakathā premajale bhāse ||*

*Word for word:* nabadvīpa-nāgarī — a townswoman of Navadvipa; āgari gorā-rase — foremost in the rasa of Gora; kahite gaurāṅga-kathā — speaking of Gauranga; prema-jale bhāse — floats in tears of prema

**21.1.** A townswoman of Navadvipa, foremost in the rasa of Gora,
speaking of Gauranga, floats in tears of prema.

ভাবভরে ভাবিনী পুলকভরে ভোরা ।
শ্রবণে নয়নে মনে গোরা গোরা গোরা ॥

*bhābabhare bhābinī pulakabhare bhorā |*
*śrabaṇe nayane mane gorā gorā gorā ||*

*Word for word:* bhāba-bhare — overflowing with bhava; bhābinī — the loving one; pulaka-bhare bhorā — beside herself with thrill; śrabaṇe nayane mane — in ears, eyes, mind; gorā gorā gorā — Gora, Gora, Gora

**21.2.** Overflowing with bhava, the loving one is beside herself with thrill:
in her ears, in her eyes, in her mind — Gora, Gora, Gora.

গোরা-রূপগুণ-অবতংস পরে কাণে ।
দিবানিশি গোরা বিনা আর নাহি জানে ॥

*gorā-rūpaguṇa-abataṃsa pare kāṇe |*
*dibāniśi gorā binā āra nāhi jāne ||*

*Word for word:* gorā-rūpa-guṇa-abataṃsa — Gora's form and virtues as ear-ornaments; pare kāṇe — she wears in her ears; dibā-niśi — day and night; gorā binā āra nāhi jāne — she knows nothing but Gora

**21.3.** Gora's form and virtues she wears as ornaments in her ears;
day and night she knows nothing but Gora.

গোরোচনা নিবিড় করিয়া মাখে গায় ।
যতন করিয়া গোরানাম লেখে তায় ॥

*gorocanā nibiṛa kariyā mākhe gāya |*
*yatana kariyā gorānāma lekhe tāya ||*

*Word for word:* gorocanā nibiṛa kariyā — thickly with gorochana; mākhe gāya — she anoints the body; yatana kariyā — carefully; gorānāma lekhe tāya — writes Gora's name on it

**21.4.** She thickly anoints her body with gorochana
and carefully writes Gora's name on it.

গোরোচনা হরিদ্রার পুতলী করিয়া ।
পূজয়ে চক্ষের জলে প্রাণফুল দিয়া ॥

*gorocanā haridrāra putalī kariyā |*
*pūjaye cakṣera jale prāṇaphula diyā ||*

*Word for word:* gorocanā haridrāra — of gorochana and turmeric; putalī kariyā — making a little figure; pūjaye cakṣera jale — she worships with the water of her eyes; prāṇaphula diyā — offering the flower of her life

**21.5.** Making a little figure of gorochana and turmeric,
she worships it with the water of her eyes, offering the flower of her life.

প্রেমনেত্রে প্রেমজল ঝোরে দুনয়নে ।
তায় অভিসিঞ্চে গোরার রাঙ্গা দু-চরণে ॥

*premanetre premajala jhore dunayane |*
*tāya abhisiñce gorāra rāṅgā du-caraṇe ||*

*Word for word:* prema-netre — from loving eyes; prema-jala jhore dunayane — tears of prema stream from both eyes; tāya abhisiñce — with them she performs the abhisheka; gorāra rāṅgā du-caraṇe — of Gora's two reddish feet

**21.6.** From her loving eyes tears of prema stream —
with them she performs the abhisheka of Gora's reddish feet.

পীরিতি নৈবেদ্য তাহে বচন তাম্বূল ।
পরিচর্য্যা করে ভাব সময় অনুকূল ॥

*pīriti naibedya tāhe bacana tāmbūla |*
*paricaryyā kare bhāba samaya anukūla ||*

*Word for word:* pīriti naibedya — love is the naivedya; tāhe bacana tāmbūla — and words the betel; paricaryyā kare — she serves; bhāba samaya anukūla — with the bhava fitting the hour

**21.7.** Love is her naivedya, her words the betel;
she serves with the bhava fitting the hour.

অঙ্গকান্তি প্রদীপে করয়ে আরাত্রিকে ।
কঙ্কণশবদে ঘণ্টা আনন্দ অধিকে ॥

*aṅgakānti pradīpe karaye ārātrike |*
*kaṅkaṇaśabade ghaṇṭā ānanda adhike ||*

*Word for word:* aṅga-kānti pradīpe — with the radiance of the body as the lamp; karaye ārātrike — she performs arati; kaṅkaṇa-śabade ghaṇṭā — the jingling of bangles is the bell; ānanda adhike — joy ever greater

**21.8.** With the radiance of her body as the lamp she performs arati;
the jingling of her bangles is the bell; her joy grows ever greater.

অঙ্গগন্ধ ধূপ ধূনা বহে অনুরাগে ।
পূজা করি দরশ-পরশরস মাগে ॥

*aṅgagandha dhūpa dhūnā bahe anurāge |*
*pūjā kari daraśa-paraśarasa māge ||*

*Word for word:* aṅga-gandha — the fragrance of the body; dhūpa dhūnā — incense and fragrant smoke; bahe anurāge — rises in anuraga; pūjā kari — having done the puja; daraśa-paraśa-rasa māge — she begs for the rasa of seeing and touching

**21.9.** The fragrance of her body — incense and fragrant smoke — rises in anuraga;
having done the puja, she begs for the rasa of seeing and touching [Him].[^34-59]

দিনে দিনে অনুরাগ বাড়িতে লাগিল ।
লোচন বলে এত দিনে জ্ঞানশেল গেল ॥

*dine dine anurāga bāṛite lāgila |*
*locana bale eta dine jñānaśela gela ||*

*Word for word:* dine dine — day by day; anurāga bāṛite lāgila — anuraga grew; locana bale — says Lochana; eta dine — at last; jñāna-śela gela — the thorn of knowledge is gone

**21.10.** Day by day her anuraga grew;
says Lochana: at last the thorn of knowledge is gone.[^34-60]

[^34-58]: Signature: "Lochana." GPT1 — p. 189, no. 85 (raga "yatharaga"; payar metre, a couplet to a line; scan PDF p. 448); GPT2 — 3.2, no. 85 (same text). No
other witnesses; attribution by GPT only — C. On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^34-59]: 21.5–21.9 are a mental puja (manasa-puja): all the articles of worship come from the feelings and body of the loving one: tears are the water of
the abhisheka, love the naivedya, words the betel, the radiance of the body the arati lamp, the jingling of bangles the bell, the fragrance of the body
the incense. The little figure of gorochana and turmeric (putalī) is an image of Gaura made by herself; translated as in the original. The request "to
see and to touch" (daraśa-paraśarasa) is a motif of nagari-bhava (introductory note).
[^34-60]: "The thorn of knowledge" (jñānaśela) — knowledge (jnana) that obstructs love like a splinter; as anuraga grows it goes away — the thought of
the superiority of bhakti over jnana (cf. CC Madhya 19 — pure bhakti, "not covered by knowledge and karma").

## 22. Lochana Dasa — "gorāpade sudhāhrade mana ḍubāye thāki…" (GPT1 p. 204, no. 116)
*A praise of Gaura (the nagari motif is only in the address "mother"). The poet keeps his mind immersed in Gora's feet as in a lake of nectar; refrain:
"Such a Gora, rapt in rasa, I have never seen anywhere." In the midst of Nadia He has come in the guise of a devotee, covered with Radha's form;
steady, calm, self-controlled — meditate on Gora in your heart. Raga suhai.*[^34-61]

গোরাপদে সুধাহ্রদে মন ডুবায়ে থাকি ।
কপাট খুলে নয়ান মেলে গোরাচাঁদে দেখি ॥

*gorāpade sudhāhrade mana ḍubāye thāki |*
*kapāṭa khule nayāna mele gorācām̐de dekhi ||*

*Word for word:* gorāpade — in Gora's feet; sudhā-hrade — in the lake of nectar; mana ḍubāye thāki — I keep the mind immersed; kapāṭa khule — opening the doors; nayāna mele — opening the eyes; gorācām̐de dekhi — I gaze at Gorachand

**22.1.** In Gora's feet, a lake of nectar, I keep my mind immersed;
opening the doors, opening my eyes, I gaze at Gorachand.

আই গো মাই ।
এমন গোরা রসে ভোরা কোথাও দেখি নাই ॥

*āi go māi |*
*emana gorā rase bhorā kothāo dekhi nāi ||*

*Word for word:* āi go māi — ah, mother; emana gorā — such a Gora; rase bhorā — rapt in rasa; kothāo dekhi nāi — I have never seen anywhere

**22.2.** *(Refrain)* Ah, mother!
Such a Gora, rapt in rasa, I have never seen anywhere.

নৈদে মাঝে ভক্ত সাজে আইল রসের বেশে ।
রাধারূপে মাখা গোরা ভাল ভুলাচ্ছে রসে ॥

*naide mājhe bhakta sāje āila rasera beśe |*
*rādhārūpe mākhā gorā bhāla bhulācche rase ||*

*Word for word:* naide mājhe — in the midst of Nadia; bhakta sāje — in the guise of a devotee; āila rasera beśe — He came in the dress of rasa; rādhā-rūpe mākhā gorā — Gora covered with Radha's form; bhāla bhulācche rase — how He enchants with rasa

**22.3.** In the midst of Nadia, in the guise of a devotee, He has come in the dress of rasa;
Gora, covered with Radha's form — how He enchants with rasa![^34-62]

রূপের ছটা বিজুরী বাটা রূপে ভুবন ভোলে ।
গোরারূপ ভুবন-ভূপ পাশরা যে নারে ॥

*rūpera chaṭā bijurī bāṭā rūpe bhubana bhole |*
*gorārūpa bhubana-bhūpa pāśarā ye nāre ||*

*Word for word:* rūpera chaṭā — the radiance of beauty; bijurī bāṭā — like ground lightning; rūpe bhubana bhole — the form enchants the world; gorārūpa bhubana-bhūpa — Gora's form, the king of the world; pāśarā ye nāre — cannot be forgotten

**22.4.** The radiance of His beauty is like ground lightning; His form enchants the world;
Gora's form is the king of the world: no one can forget it.

ধীর শান্ত রসে দান্ত হেরলে নয়ন কোণে ।
লোচন বলে কুতূহলে গোরা ভাব মনে ॥

*dhīra śānta rase dānta herale nayana koṇe |*
*locana bale kutūhale gorā bhāba mane ||*

*Word for word:* dhīra śānta — steady, calm; rase dānta — self-controlled in rasa; herale nayana koṇe — if you see Him from the corner of the eye; locana bale kutūhale — says Lochana with joy; gorā bhāba mane — meditate on Gora in the mind

**22.5.** Steady, calm, self-controlled even in rasa — if you see Him even from the corner of your eye…
Says Lochana with joy: meditate on Gora in your heart.[^34-63]

[^34-61]: Signature: "Lochana." GPT1 — p. 204, no. 116 (raga suhai; refrain marked "dhru"; scan PDF p. 463), among the padas of Vasu Ghosha (nos. 111–115) and
before the padas of Jnanadasa (nos. 117–118); GPT2 — 3.2, no. 116 (same text). No other witnesses; attribution by GPT only — C. "Ah, mother!" (āi go māi) is an exclamation in
women's speech (chapter 29, glossary). On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^34-62]: "In the guise of a devotee" (bhakta sāje) and "covered with Radha's form" (rādhārūpe mākhā) are an exact formula of the teaching: Gaura is
Krishna, who has taken the form of a devotee and the bhava and radiance of Radha (CC Adi 1.5; Adi 4). "The dress of rasa" — His form as the one who
tastes rasa.
[^34-63]: "Steady, calm, self-controlled" (dhīra śānta dānta) — so the tradition too sees Gaura (CB, Adi-khanda, on the Lord's strictness). "Ground
lightning" (bijurī bāṭā) — the interpretation is conjectural. "Opening the doors" (22.1) — cf. the "inner village" of no. 13 (13.10).

## Summary of Chapter 34

*Chapter 34 completes the nagari padas of Lochana Dasa: of the 26 padas with his signature in section 3.2 of GPT, 22 are translated here (nos. 62–65,
67–79, 81–83, 85, 116; records pad-0735…0756); nos. 61 and 66 (= PK 2178, 2174) were translated in chapter 28; no. 80 (= PK 2088) is a passage of the
*Chaitanya-mangala* (Madhya-khanda, part 4, vv. 110–118), no. 84 (= PK 777) is a pada of Vasu Ghosha (chapter 27, no. 16; in GPT1 it
stands twice — as no. 17 with Vasu's signature and as no. 84 with Lochana's). All 22 padas are known only from GPT (nos. 16, 17 also from PVP, 1922, with
the same signature); all are C: attribution by GPT only (the signature of a recognized author, but without independent witnesses; PVP, 1922, is a late
anthology); no. 5 begins with two couplets of Jnanadasa's pada PK 748. In content: the purvaraga and anuraga of the townswomen (nos. 1–2, 4–10, 12–13, 15, 19–21); an imagined meeting and dreams with the
motif of sambhoga (no. 1 — a fancy beside her husband; nos. 11, 18 — dreams); praise of Gaura's form and dance, where the nagari motif is only in the
frame or the address (nos. 3, 14, 16) or absent in content (nos. 17, 22). Separate notes on attraction and sambhoga — 3, 26, 31, 33, 53; on the motif
of "leaving family and husband" — 7, 11, 36, 45; on the Lord's looking at women — 26, 46, 56. Many of Lochana's padas end with a turn inward — "go into
your own house, hold Gora in your heart" (nos. 11, 13, 20; cf. nos. 3, 22), and in several the teaching is voiced directly: Gaura is the same Krishna,
"straightened" by Radha's love (16.4); His form is beyond prakriti (17.2); He has come in the guise of a devotee, covered with Radha's form (22.3).
Doubtful places: the meaning of a number of colloquial words (5.6, 5.9, 6.2, 6.3, 7.1, 7.3, 13.8, 15.5, 18.5, 20.7, 22.4) — translated conjecturally,
with notes; line 12.5 has no pair (lost in GPT).*

## Concluding Note to the Section of Nagari Padas (Chapters 27–34)

*1. **How many and whose.** The section contains 183 padas in eight chapters: Vasu Ghosha — 40 (chapter 27 — 25 padas from PK; chapter 28 — 15 padas
known from GPT); Nayanananda — 5; Yadunandana — 6 (the cycle of the 12th wave of the *Bhakti-ratnakara*, chapter 29; one signed "Yadu"); Yadu — 2;
Murari — 2 (Murari Gupta by the GPT signature and Dasa Murari); Balarama Dasa — 1; Chandrashekhara — 1; Lochana Dasa — 24 (two padas from PK in
chapter 28 and 22 from GPT in chapter 34); "Narahari" — 102 (chapters 29–33; nearly all by Narahari Chakravarti; their concluding note is at the end of
chapter 33).*

*2. **Attribution** (scale — see the preface). **A — 30**: 26 padas of Vasu Ghosha (25 from PK and one confirmed by the *Kshanada-gita-chintamani*) and 4
padas of Nayanananda from PK. **B — 90**: "probably Chakravarti" — 81 (75 found in the *Gaura-charita-chintamani*, 6 only in the
*Bhakti-ratnakara*), Yadunandana — 6, Lochana Dasa — 2 (padas from PK, chapter 28), Vasu — 1 (GPT and the *Gita-chandrodaya*). **C — 62**: Lochana Dasa —
22 (chapter 34: signature only in GPT, without independent witnesses — "attribution by GPT only"), "Narahari" — 21 (padas only from GPT;
some stand in place of the lost pages of GCC), Vasu — 12 (GPT only), Nayanananda — 1, Yadu — 2, Murari — 2, Balarama — 1, Chandrashekhara — 1.
**D — 1** (a pada signed Vasu, according to Majumdar a reworking of a pada on Krishna; chapter 28, no. 13). The earliest and most reliable layer is the
padas of Vasu Ghosha and Nayanananda from the *Padakalpataru*; the rest is a poetic development of the nagari motif: Lochana Dasa (a disciple of
Narahari Sarakara), Yadunandana (a disciple of Gadadhara Dasa) and, most of all, Narahari Chakravarti (first half of the eighteenth century).*

*3. **Who speaks.** In the great majority of padas the townswomen of Nadia speak — to a friend, to themselves, to the elders; in 25 "Narahari" padas
(GPT 3.2 nos. 158–180 and 3.1 nos. 129–130 = GCC, kiranas 10–11) heavenly women speak, who only look at Nadia from the sky; in a few, the poet himself,
putting himself in a townswoman's place ("the nagari Lochana," 34/6.11) or looking on from outside (34/15.11–15.13). Not nagari-bhava in content — 6
padas: Gaura's words in sleep in the words of Krishna (31/1), the heavenly women's replies praising the Lord's strictness (32/19–20, 33/3), Lochana's
praise of Gaura's form (34/17, 22); in a number of other padas the nagari motif is only the address "friend" or the frame (28/1, 34/3, 14, 16 and
others). Three padas are laments after the Lord's sannyasa (in 28/15 the speaker is probably Vishnupriya — then it is a lament of separation, not nagari-bhava), four are the women's words at His wedding.*

*4. **What the corpus shows.** The nagari padas speak of Gaura in the language of purvaraga and anuraga from the padas on Radha and the gopis: deceiving
the elders, "leaving family and husband," dreams of a meeting. The later the layer, the more outspoken the motif: in Vasu Ghosha (PK) it is mostly
admiration and longing; in the "Narahari" padas from GCC and in Lochana's colloquial padas — dreams with embraces and direct words of attraction. Yet
even in them Gaura in the lila itself does not respond to attraction: He passes by, dances in kirtana, leans on His associates; the "meeting" happens
only in the heroine's dream and fancy; in Narahari Chakravarti the Lord turns away and hurries off, and Lochana ends many padas with a call to "go into
your own house" and keep Gora in the heart and voices the teaching directly (34/16.4, 17.2, 22.3).*

*5. **The position of the tradition** (briefly). The Gaudiya Vaishnava tradition does not accept the worship of Gaura in the mood of the nagaris.
Vrindavana Dasa (*Chaitanya-bhagavata*, Adi-khanda) testifies that the Lord in this incarnation did not look at any woman and that the wise do not
glorify Him as "Gauranga-nagara"; Krishnadasa Kaviraja (*Chaitanya-charitamrita*, Adi 1.5–6; Adi 4) reveals that Gaura is Krishna Himself in the bhava
and radiance of Radha, who came to taste Her love as a devotee, not as an enjoying hero; Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati counts "gaura-nagari" among
the apasampradayas — and, publishing Lochana's *Chaitanya-mangala*, refuses to ascribe this doctrine to it. The nagari padas have been translated for
the completeness of the corpus of padas on Gaura and as a historical document — faithfully to the author, without worldly vocabulary beyond the
original and without softening, with notes on the position of the tradition; they are not a basis for worshipping Gaura as a nagara (introductory
note, chapter 27).*
